heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the Aboriginal Communal Fishing Licences Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: aboriginal organization includes an Indian band, an Indian band council, a tribal council and an organization that represents a territorially based aboriginal community; (organisation autochtone)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: licence means a communal licence issued under subsection 4(1); (permis)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Minister means, in respect of

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) fisheries for the fish and species of fish described in subsection 3(1) of the Quebec Fishery Regulations, 1990, in the waters referred to in that subsection, the Minister responsible in the Province of Quebec for the application of An Act respecting the conservation and development of wildlife, R.S.Q., c. C-61.1,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a.1) fisheries in the non-tidal waters of Ontario, the Minister of Natural Resources for Ontario; and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) any other fishery, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans. (ministre)

heading: Application
paragraph: 3 (1) These Regulations apply in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) fisheries in Canadian fisheries waters in and adjacent to Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and the Northwest Territories;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) fisheries in the tidal waters in and adjacent to Manitoba;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) fisheries in tidal waters in and adjacent to the Yukon Territory and fisheries in the Yukon Territory for fish of an anadromous stock of chum salmon, coho salmon, chinook salmon, pink salmon, sockeye salmon, rainbow trout, the family Coregonidae (whitefish and cisco) or Arctic char; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) fisheries in the waters of the Areas enumerated and described in Schedule II to the Pacific Fishery Management Area Regulations and salmon fisheries in British Columbia.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) These Regulations do not apply in respect of national parks.

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: 4 (1) The Minister may issue a communal licence to an aboriginal organization to carry on fishing and related activities.

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (2) The Minister may designate, in the licence,

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (a) the persons who may fish under the authority of the licence, and

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (b) the vessels that may be used to fish under the authority of the licence.

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (3) If the Minister does not designate the persons who may fish under the authority of the licence, the aboriginal organization may designate, in writing, those persons.

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (4) If the Minister does not designate the vessels that may be used to fish under the authority of the licence, the aboriginal organization may designate, in writing, those vessels.

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: 5 (1) For the proper management and control of fisheries and the conservation and protection of fish, the Minister may specify in a licence any condition respecting any of the matters set out in paragraphs 22(1)(b) to (z.1) of the Fishery (General) Regulations and any condition respecting any of the following matters, without restricting the generality of the foregoing:

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (a) the species and quantities of fish that are permitted to be taken or transported;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (b) the method by which and when the licence holder is to notify the Minister of designations, the documents that constitute proof of designation, when, under what circumstances and to whom proof of designation must be produced, the documents or information that designated persons and vessels must carry when carrying on fishing and related activities, and when, under what circumstances and to whom the documents or information must be produced;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (c) the method to be used to mark and identify vessels and fishing gear;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (d) the locations and times at which landing of fish is permitted;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (e) the method to be used for the landing of fish and the methods by which the quantity of the fish is to be determined;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (f) the information that a designated person or the master of a designated vessel is to report to the Minister or a person specified by the licence holder, prior to commencement of fishing, with respect to where and when fishing will be carried on, including the method by which, the times at which and the person to whom the report is to be made;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (g) the locations and times of inspections of the contents of the hold and the procedure to be used in conducting those inspections;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (h) the maximum number of persons or vessels that may be designated to carry on fishing and related activities;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (i) the maximum number of designated persons who may fish at any one time;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (j) the type, size and quantity of fishing gear that may be used by a designated person;

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (k) the circumstances under which fish are to be marked for scientific or administrative purposes; and

heading: Communal Licences
paragraph: (l) the disposition of fish caught under the authority of the licence.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 7 No person carrying on fishing or any related activity under the authority of a licence shall contravene or fail to comply with any condition of the licence.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 8 No person other than a designated person may fish under the authority of a licence.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 9 (1) No person who is authorized to fish under the authority of a licence shall fish for or catch and retain any species of fish in any area of the waters referred to in subsection 3(1) during the close time beginning on December 29 and ending on December 31.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) The close time established by subsection (1) is considered to be fixed separately and individually with respect to any species of fish found in any of the waters referred to in subsection 3(1).

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "additional residence" means a residence on a parcel of agricultural land, other than the principal residence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "administrative region" means an administrative region established under section 4.1;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agreement in principle" means a non-binding agreement, negotiated among a first nation government, the Province and Canada in accordance with a process facilitated by the British Columbia Treaty Commission, established under section 3 of the Treaty Commission Act, that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) has been approved by each party in accordance with the approval process provided in the agreement in principle, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) contemplates that legislative authority over all or part of the proposed settlement lands described in the agreement in principle will, under a final agreement or a governance agreement and an enactment of the Province or Canada, be provided to the first nation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agricultural land" means land that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is included in the agricultural land reserve under section 15 (1.1), 17 (3.1) or 45 (1) of this Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) was included under a former Act as agricultural land or land in an agricultural land reserve,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: unless the land has been excluded from the agricultural land reserve under this Act or from an agricultural land reserve under a former Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agricultural land reserve" means the total of all agricultural land in British Columbia;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "alter" means the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) to alter the exterior of a structure so as to increase its size;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) to move or alter the exterior walls or edges of a structure so as to change its siting;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "approving officer" means an approving officer as defined in the Land Title Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authority" means an agent of the government, a public body or a public officer with whom the commission has an agreement under section 26 (1) (b) or 38;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "chief executive officer" means the person appointed under section 8 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commission" means the Provincial Agricultural Land Commission established under section 4;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "construct" means the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) to build a new structure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) to place on land a new structure that is fully or partially pre-fabricated;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) to replace a structure, 75% or more of which has been substantially damaged or destroyed;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "enactment of the Province or Canada" includes an enactment as defined in the Interpretation Act (Canada);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "exclusion application" means an application for exclusion made under section 29 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "executive committee" means the executive committee of the commission established under section 10;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "farm use"

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) means an occupation or use of agricultural land for

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  farming land, plants, mushrooms, truffles or animals,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a farm operation as defined in the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  a purpose designated as a farm use by regulation, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) does not include a residential use or a soil or fill use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fill" means any material brought onto agricultural land other than materials exempted by regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "first nation government" means,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to settlement lands, other than treaty lands, the governing body that has legislative authority in relation to those settlement lands,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a.1) in relation to treaty lands, the treaty first nation, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to proposed settlement lands, an aboriginal governing body that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the first nation, in relation to which an agreement in principle applying to those lands has been entered into, has organized and established within its traditional territory in British Columbia, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  has been mandated by the members of that first nation to enter into treaty negotiations on their behalf in accordance with a process facilitated by the British Columbia Treaty Commission, established under section 3 of the Treaty Commission Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "former Act" means the Agricultural Land Reserve Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 10, or the Land Reserve Commission Act, S.B.C. 1999, c. 14;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "law", in relation to a first nation government described in paragraph (a) or  (a.1) of the definition of "first nation government", means a law enacted by the first nation government under

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a treaty and land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a governance agreement among the Province, Canada and the first nation, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) an enactment of the Province or Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local government" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to land within a municipality, the municipal council,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to land within an electoral area but not within a local trust area under the Islands Trust Act, the board of the regional district, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in relation to land within a local trust area under the Islands Trust Act, the local trust committee or the executive committee acting as a local trust committee for that area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "non-adhering residential use" means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an additional residence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a principal residence having a total floor area that is more than 500 m2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a use of a residential structure that contravenes the regulations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "non-farm use" means a use of agricultural land other than a farm use, a residential use or a soil or fill use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "notice to suspend negotiations" means a notice to suspend negotiations sent by one party to an agreement in principle to the other parties;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "official" means the chief executive officer and any employee of the commission or a person who is designated by name or title by the chief executive officer to be an official;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "owner", subject to subsection (2), means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to land, other than treaty lands, registered in the records of the land title office, the person registered in those records as the fee simple owner of the land,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to settlement lands,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  if an agreement under this Act between a first nation government and the commission defines "owner" for the purposes of the application of this Act to the settlement lands of the first nation, a person described by that definition, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  otherwise, the first nation government,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in relation to land that is vested, under an enactment, in a municipality, a regional district or a local trust committee, the municipality, regional district or local trust committee, as applicable, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) in relation to Crown land, the government;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "panel" means a panel established under section 11;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "parcel" means land that is the subject of a single indefeasible title under the Land Title Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "person" includes a first nation government;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "principal residence" means the residence permitted under section 20.1 (1) (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "proposed settlement lands" means land described in an agreement in principle as the land that will become, in whole or in part,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the treaty lands of the first nation under a final agreement, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the settlement lands of the first nation under a governance agreement among the Province, Canada and the first nation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "residential structure" means a structure used, during all or part of the year and whether fully or partially, as

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a residence,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if prescribed, accommodation, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) if prescribed, in relation to a residence or accommodation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "residential use"

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) means a use of agricultural land for a residential structure, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) does not include a farm use or a soil or fill use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "settlement lands" means land, other than land located within a reserve as defined in the Indian Act (Canada), that is subject to the legislative authority of a first nation under

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a treaty and land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a governance agreement among the Province, Canada and the first nation, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) an enactment of the Province or Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "soil" includes the entire mantle of unconsolidated material above bedrock other than minerals as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "soil or fill use"

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) means the removal of soil from, or the placement of fill on, agricultural land, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) does not include a farm use or a residential use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "use or subdivision application" means an application for permission made under any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) section 20 (2) for a non-farm use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) section 20.1 (2) (a) for a non-adhering residential use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) section 20.3 (5) for a soil or fill use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) section 21 (2) for subdivision.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of an inclusion application under section 17 (3), a use or subdivision application or an exclusion application in relation to proposed settlement lands, the first nation government may apply as if it were the owner of those lands from the date that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an agreement in principle in relation to those lands is approved by each party to it in accordance with the agreement in principle, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if a notice to suspend negotiations has earlier taken effect, an agreement among the parties to the agreement in principle to resume negotiations takes effect,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: until the earlier of the following dates:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the date an enactment of the Province or Canada establishes all or part of the proposed settlement lands as settlement lands;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the date that a notice to suspend negotiations takes effect.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (3) For the period that a first nation government is authorized to make an application in relation to proposed settlement lands, the owner of that land may not make an application.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: 2		  (1) This Act and the regulations are not subject to any other enactment, whenever enacted, except the Interpretation Act, the Environment and Land Use Act and the Environmental Management Act and as provided in this Act.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (1.1) Despite subsection (1) and section 3, if a regulation under the Water Sustainability Act requires that the commission consider a water sustainability plan in making decisions in relation to an area that is subject to the water sustainability plan, the commission must comply with the regulation.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (1.2) Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to the Haida Nation Recognition Act and, despite section 3 of this Act, the Haida Nation Recognition Act prevails to the extent of any conflict or inconsistency with this Act.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (2) Despite section 14 (2) of the Interpretation Act, this Act binds the government.

heading: Power under other Acts
paragraph: 3		  A minister or an agent of the government must not exercise a power granted under another enactment except in accordance with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Commission established
paragraph:
4
		  The Provincial Agricultural Land Commission is established as a corporation consisting of the members appointed under section 5.

heading: Administrative regions
paragraph:
4.1
		  The following administrative regions are established, consisting of the geographic areas of British Columbia as set out in the Schedule:

heading: Administrative regions
paragraph: (a) the Interior Administrative Region;

heading: Administrative regions
paragraph: (b) the Island Administrative Region;

heading: Administrative regions
paragraph: (c) the Kootenay Administrative Region;

heading: Administrative regions
paragraph: (d) the North Administrative Region;

heading: Administrative regions
paragraph: (e) the Okanagan Administrative Region;

heading: Administrative regions
paragraph: (f) the South Coast Administrative Region.

heading: Commission members
paragraph:
5
		  (1) The commission consists of at least 11 members appointed under this section as follows:

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (a) the Lieutenant Governor in Council must appoint the chair;

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (b) the minister must appoint the other members after consulting with the chair;

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (c) appointments must be made using a merit-based process to select individuals who are knowledgeable in matters relating to agriculture, land use planning, local government or first nation government;

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (d) members must be residents of administrative regions, with at least one but no more than 3 members, other than the chair, representing each region;

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (e) if more than one member represents the same administrative region, each member must be a resident of a different regional district incorporated under the Local Government Act.

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (2) The chair may appoint one or more vice chairs from the persons appointed under subsection (1) (b).

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (3) If a member, other than the chair, ceases to be a resident of the administrative region in which the member was a resident at the time of appointment, the member's appointment expires on the date on which the member's residency ceases.

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (4) If there is no member, other than the chair, who is a resident of a particular administrative region, the minister must within 90 days appoint a resident of that administrative region as a member in accordance with subsection (1).

heading: Commission members
paragraph: (5) The members are the board of directors of the commission.

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: 5.1		  The following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the commission:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (a) Part 1 [Interpretation and Application];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (b) Part 2 [Appointments];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (c) Part 3 [Clustering];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (d) section 26 (6) [decision of majority decision of panel];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (d.1) section 30 [tribunal duties];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (e) section 44 [tribunal without jurisdiction over constitutional questions];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (f) section 46.3 [tribunal without jurisdiction to apply the Human Rights Code];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (g) Part 8 [Immunities];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (h) section 59.1 [surveys];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (i) section 59.2 [reporting];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to commission generally
paragraph: (j) section 60 (1) (g) to (i) and (2) [power to make regulations].

heading: Purposes of the commission
paragraph: 6		  (1) The following are the purposes of the commission:

heading: Purposes of the commission
paragraph: (a) to preserve the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Purposes of the commission
paragraph: (b) to encourage farming of land within the agricultural land reserve in collaboration with other communities of interest;

heading: Purposes of the commission
paragraph: (c) to encourage local governments, first nations, the government and its agents to enable and accommodate farm use of land within the agricultural land reserve and uses compatible with agriculture in their plans, bylaws and policies.

heading: Purposes of the commission
paragraph: (2) The commission, to fulfill its purposes under subsection (1), must give priority to protecting and enhancing all of the following in exercising its powers and performing its duties under this Act:

heading: Purposes of the commission
paragraph: (a) the size, integrity and continuity of the land base of the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Purposes of the commission
paragraph: (b) the use of the agricultural land reserve for farm use.

heading: Commission as agent of the government
paragraph:
7
		  The commission is an agent of the government.

heading: Staff of the commission
paragraph:
8
		  (1) On consultation with the chair of the commission, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may appoint, during pleasure, a chief executive officer of the commission, establish the terms of the appointment and set the remuneration of the chief executive officer.

heading: Staff of the commission
paragraph: (2) The commission may determine the duties of the chief executive officer.

heading: Staff of the commission
paragraph: (3) The chief executive officer may appoint other officers and employees necessary for the operations of the commission, determine their duties and set their remuneration.

heading: Staff of the commission
paragraph: (4) The Public Service Act and the Public Service Labour Relations Act apply to the commission and its officers and employees other than the chief executive officer, except that the references to the agency head and a deputy minister in section 22 of the Public Service Act are to be read as references to the chief executive officer.

heading: Staff of the commission
paragraph: (5) The chief executive officer may retain consultants considered advisable and may set their remuneration.

heading: Operation of the commission
paragraph: 9		  The commission may pass resolutions and bylaws it considers necessary or advisable for the management and conduct of its affairs, the exercise of its powers and the performance of its duties.

heading: Executive committee
paragraph:
10
		  (1) An executive committee of the commission is established, comprising the chair of the commission and the vice chairs.

heading: Executive committee
paragraph: (2) The chair of the commission is the chair of the executive committee.

heading: Executive committee
paragraph: (3) The commission may delegate to the executive committee any of its powers or duties.

heading: Executive committee
paragraph: (4) In relation to a matter delegated by the commission to the executive committee,

heading: Executive committee
paragraph: (a) the executive committee has all the powers and duties of the commission, and

heading: Executive committee
paragraph: (b) a decision of the executive committee is for all purposes a decision of the commission.

heading: Establishment of panels
paragraph:
11
		  (1) The chair of the commission may establish panels consisting of 2 or more members of the commission.

heading: Establishment of panels
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of establishing panels, the chair may consider administrative regions, expertise of panel members, the type of application under consideration and any other criteria the chair may determine.

heading: Establishment of panels
paragraph: (3) The chair may designate a member of the commission to chair a panel.

heading: Establishment of panels
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act, the commission, a panel and the executive committee may rely on advice, information or findings from any panel.

heading: What panels may do
paragraph:
11.1
		  (1) The chair of the commission may refer to a panel any of the following:

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (2), a power or duty of the commission under this Act;

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (b) without limiting paragraph (a), the reconsideration of a decision for the purposes of section 33;

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (c) the provision of advice, information or findings to the commission, the executive committee or another panel.

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (2) The chair must not refer to a panel any of the following:

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (a) the power to determine an application

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (i)  that may be of provincial importance,

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (ii)  that raises an issue that is novel or is otherwise of general importance for the administration of the Act, or

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (iii)  if the determination may substantively affect more than one administrative region;

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (b) an application

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (i)  for which the power to decide has been delegated under section 26, or

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (ii)  that the chief executive officer may approve under section 27;

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (c) a reconsideration under section 33.1 of a decision made by a panel.

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (3) In relation to an application or other matter referred to a panel,

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (a) the panel has all the powers and duties of the commission, and

heading: What panels may do
paragraph: (b) a decision made by the panel is for all purposes a decision of the commission.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph:
12
		  (1) The financial year end of the commission is March 31 and the Minister of Finance is the fiscal agent of the commission.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the Business Corporations Act does not apply to the commission.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by order, may declare that specified provisions of the Business Corporations Act apply to the commission.

heading: Completion of proceedings
paragraph:
14
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a member of the commission may take up and carry on to completion any proceeding commenced but not completed before the member's appointment.

heading: Completion of proceedings
paragraph: (2) A member of the commission who was not present at a meeting to determine an application or other matter may vote on the application or matter only if a summary of the meeting is given to the member before the vote.

heading: Inclusion of land in agricultural land reserve by the commission
paragraph:
15
		  (1) For the purposes of section 6, the commission may designate land, including Crown land, as agricultural land if the commission is satisfied that the land is suitable for farm use.

heading: Inclusion of land in agricultural land reserve by the commission
paragraph: (1.1) Land designated as agricultural land under subsection (1) is included, on designation, in the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Inclusion of land in agricultural land reserve by the commission
paragraph: (2) If the final agreement of a treaty first nation provides that the treaty lands of the treaty first nation may not be designated as agricultural land without the consent of the treaty first nation, the commission may not exercise the authority under subsection (1) in relation to those treaty lands without the consent of the treaty first nation.

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph:
17
		  (1) Subject to subsection (1.1), if the commission considers that an approval under this subsection carries out the intent of this Act, the commission may approve the inclusion in the agricultural land reserve

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (a) on the commission's own initiative, of any land,

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (b) on application of a local government, of land within the local government's jurisdiction, and

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (c) on application of a first nation government, of land within the first nation's settlement lands.

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (1.1) If section 15 (2) applies in relation to treaty lands, an approval under subsection (1) (a) of this section in respect of those treaty lands may be made only with the consent of the treaty first nation.

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (2) For a matter under subsection (1), a public hearing must be held in the manner, and after giving the notice, required by the regulations, by

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (a) the commission, if the commission is acting on its own initiative,

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (b) the local government before making an application, and

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (c) the first nation government before making an application.

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (3) On application by an owner of land, the commission may designate all or part of the land described in the application as land within the agricultural land reserve if the commission considers that the designation carries out the intent of this Act.

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (3.1) Land designated as land within the agricultural land reserve under subsection (3) is included, on designation, in the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (4) A decision of the commission granting an application under subsection (3) in relation to proposed settlement lands may not be made effective unless and until those lands are established, in whole or in part, as settlement lands.

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (5) Unless a decision granting an application under subsection (3) first becomes effective under subsection (4), the decision expires on the earlier of the following dates:

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (a) the date the decision expires according to its terms;

heading: Inclusion applications
paragraph: (b) the date that a notice to suspend negotiations takes effect.

heading: Agricultural land to remain in reserve unless excluded
paragraph:
17.1
		  Agricultural land may be removed from the agricultural land reserve only by exclusion under section 29.1 (2) (b), 30 (1) (a) or 45 (1).

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph:
18
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: "approving body" means one or more of the following:

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (a) a local government, a first nation government or an authority;

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (b) a board or other agency established by a local government, a first nation government or an authority;

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (c) a person or agency that enters into an agreement under the Local Services Act;

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: "permitted non-farm use" means a non-farm use that is permitted under section 25 or 45 or the regulations.

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (2) An approving body may approve or permit a non-farm use of agricultural land only if the non-farm use is a permitted non-farm use.

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (3) An approving body may approve or permit a building or structure to be constructed or altered on agricultural land only if the building or structure

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (a) is not a residential structure and will be used for a farm use or permitted non-farm use,

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (b) is a principal residence and

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (i)  is of a size and is sited in accordance with section 20.1 (1), or

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (ii)  is permitted under section 25 or 45 or the regulations,

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (c) is an additional residence and is permitted under section 25 or 45 or the regulations, or

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (d) is a residential structure other than a residence and

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (i)  is of a size and is sited in accordance with the regulations or as permitted under an application made in accordance with the regulations, and

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (ii)  will be used as permitted under section 25 or 45 or the regulations.

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (4) An approving body may approve or permit a soil or fill use of agricultural land only if the soil or fill use is permitted under section 20.3, 25 or 45.

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (5) The following persons may not approve a subdivision of land that would cause agricultural land to be subdivided unless the subdivision is permitted under section 25 or 45 or the regulations:

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (a) an approving officer under the Land Title Act, the Local Government Act or the Strata Property Act;

heading: Restrictions on approving land uses and subdivision
paragraph: (b) a person who exercises the powers of an approving officer under any other Act.

heading: Notice of statutory right of way
paragraph: 18.1		  (1) In this section, "statutory right of way" means a statutory right of way as described in section 218 of the Land Title Act that extends fully or partially over land within the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Notice of statutory right of way
paragraph: (2) Before applying to register a charge granting or otherwise creating a statutory right of way, the applicant must give notice, in the prescribed form and manner, to the commission.

heading: Notice of statutory right of way
paragraph: (3) A Registrar of Titles must not register a charge granting or otherwise creating a statutory right of way unless the application to register the charge is accompanied by proof, given in the prescribed form and manner, that notice has been given as required under subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Registration restrictions
paragraph: 19		  (1) In this section, "plan" means the following:

heading: Registration restrictions
paragraph: (a) a subdivision plan, reference plan, explanatory plan or other plan showing subdivision of land;

heading: Registration restrictions
paragraph: (b) a statutory right of way plan allowed under section 114 of the Land Title Act.

heading: Registration restrictions
paragraph: (2) Unless the subdivision of agricultural land is permitted under this Act, a Registrar of Titles must not, under the Land Title Act or the Strata Property Act, do either of the following things if it would cause the subdivision of agricultural land:

heading: Registration restrictions
paragraph: (a) accept an application for the deposit of a plan;

heading: Registration restrictions
paragraph: (b) permit a new parcel of land to be created by a metes and bounds description or an abbreviated description.

heading: Non-farm use of land within agricultural land reserve
paragraph: 20		  (1) A person must not use agricultural land for a non-farm use unless permitted under section 25 or 45 or the regulations.

heading: Non-farm use of land within agricultural land reserve
paragraph: (2) A person may apply to the commission for permission under section 25 for a non-farm use of agricultural land if the person

heading: Non-farm use of land within agricultural land reserve
paragraph: (a) is an owner of the agricultural land, or

heading: Non-farm use of land within agricultural land reserve
paragraph: (b) has a right of entry, granted under an enactment, to the agricultural land.

heading: Residential use of agricultural land
paragraph:
20.1
		  (1) Unless permitted under section 20.2, 25 or 45 or the regulations, an owner of agricultural land who constructs, alters or uses a residential structure on the agricultural land must comply with all of the following:

heading: Residential use of agricultural land
paragraph: (a) the agricultural land may have no more than one residence per parcel;

heading: Residential use of agricultural land
paragraph: (b) the total floor area of a principal residence must be 500 m2 or less;

heading: Residential use of agricultural land
paragraph: (c) the residential structure must be sized, sited and used, in accordance with all applicable regulations.

heading: Residential use of agricultural land
paragraph: (2) An owner may apply

heading: Residential use of agricultural land
paragraph: (a) to the commission for permission under section 25 for a non-adhering residential use, or

heading: Residential use of agricultural land
paragraph: (b) in the manner set out in the regulations for a variation of or exemption from a regulation with respect to size or siting.

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph:
20.2
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: "as designed" means as stated or shown in

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (a) a design, proposal or other plan approved under or accepted in support of an authorization, or

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (b) a design or plan finalized, before the date this section comes into force, by an architect or engineer or, if none, the designer of the residence, if no authorizations are needed to construct or alter the residence;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: "authorization" means a permit or other authorization, issued under an enactment, to construct or alter a residence;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: "pre-existing residential structure" means a residential structure that exists on agricultural land on the date this section comes into force, and

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (a) is an additional residence for which all required authorizations to construct or alter the residence were granted,

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (b) is a principal residence having a total floor area of more than 500 m2, or

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (c) is of a size or is sited in contravention of a regulation;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: "unfinished pre-existing residence" means a residence to which all of the conditions in paragraphs (a) and (b), and either paragraph (c) or paragraph (d), apply:

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (a) the residence, if completed as designed, will be an additional residence or have a total floor area of more than 500 m2;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (b) from the date construction or alteration of the residence began until completion, the construction or alteration

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (i)  is carried out in accordance with all applicable authorizations and enactments, and

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (ii)  continues without interruption, other than work stoppages considered reasonable in the building industry;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (c) in the case of a residence that, on completion, will be an additional residence,

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (i)  all required authorizations to construct or alter the residence were granted, and

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (ii)  construction of the foundation of the residence, or alteration of the residence, had substantially begun

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: before the date this section comes into force;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (d) in the case of a residence that, on completion, will be a primary residence, either

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (i)  all required authorizations to construct or alter the residence were granted before the date this section comes into force and construction of the foundation of the residence, or alteration of the residence, substantially begins on or before November 5, 2019, or

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (ii)  if no authorizations to construct or alter the residence are required, construction of the foundation of the residence, or alteration of the residence, had substantially begun before the date this section comes into force.

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (2) Despite section 20.1 (1), an owner of agricultural land may, on or after the date this section comes into force, do one or more of the following:

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (a) complete construction or alteration of an unfinished pre-existing residence that

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (i)  is a principal residence, but only if, on completion, the total floor area is as designed or less, or

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (ii)  is an additional residence, and

heading: Pre-existing residential structures
paragraph: (b) alter a pre-existing residential structure, but only if, on completion, the alteration will lead to no further contravention of the Act or regulations.

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph:
20.3
		  (1) A person must not remove soil from or place fill on agricultural land unless one of the following applies:

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (a) the removal or placement is permitted under section 25 or 45 and the removal or placement is done in accordance with the permission;

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (b) the removal or placement is permitted under the regulations and the removal or placement is done in accordance with the regulations;

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (c) the person

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (i)  is an owner of the agricultural land, or has a right of entry, granted under an enactment, to the agricultural land,

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (ii)  first submits to the chief executive officer the prescribed fee and notice of the person's intent, in the form and manner required by the chief executive officer, and

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (iii)  receives approval under subsection (2) (b) and removes the soil or places the fill in accordance with the approval, or is a person to whom subsection (4) applies.

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (2) If the chief executive officer receives the fee and notice submitted under subsection (1) (c) (ii), the chief executive officer must do one or more of the following:

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (a) request further information from the person who gave the notice;

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (b) approve, in writing, the removal of soil or the placement of fill

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (i)  as set out in the notice, or

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (ii)  subject to limits and conditions;

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (c) order, in writing, the person to stop or not engage in removing soil or placing fill unless permitted under section 25 or 45.

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (3) If a person fails to comply with subsection (1) (c) (ii), the chief executive officer may do one or both of the following:

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (a) order, in writing, the person to comply with subsection (1) (c) (ii);

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (b) take the action described in subsection (2) (c).

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (4) If the chief executive officer does not take an action described in subsection (2) within 60 days after receiving the fee and notice submitted under subsection (1) (c) (ii) or the information requested under subsection (2) (a), the person may remove soil from or place fill on the agricultural land as described in the notice.

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (5) A person may apply to the commission for permission under section 25 for a soil or fill use of agricultural land

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (a) if the person is an owner of the agricultural land, or has a right of entry, granted under an enactment, to the agricultural land, and

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (b) whether or not a fee and notice have been submitted under subsection (1) (c) (ii) of this section or the chief executive officer has taken an action described in subsection (2) (b) (ii) or (c).

heading: Soil or fill use
paragraph: (6) The chief executive officer may delegate, in writing, the powers and duties of the chief executive officer under this section to an employee of the commission.

heading: Subdivision of agricultural land
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A person must not subdivide agricultural land unless permitted under section 25 or 45 or the regulations.

heading: Subdivision of agricultural land
paragraph: (2) An owner of agricultural land may apply to the commission for permission under section 25 to subdivide agricultural land.

heading: Covenants
paragraph:
22
		  (1) The commission may enter into a covenant under the Land Title Act with an owner of agricultural land.

heading: Covenants
paragraph: (2) A covenant that restricts or prohibits the use of agricultural land for farm purposes has no effect until approved by the commission.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: 23		  (1) Restrictions on the use of agricultural land do not apply to land that, on December 21, 1972, was, by separate certificate of title issued under the Land Registry Act, R.S.B.C. 1960, c. 208, less than 2 acres in area.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (2) The restrictions on the use of agricultural land do not apply to land lawfully used for a non-farm use, established and carried on continuously for at least 6 months immediately before December 21, 1972, unless and until

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a) the use is changed, other than to farm use, without the permission of the commission,

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a.1) the use is discontinued for a continuous period of 6 months,

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (b) an enactment made after December 21, 1972, prohibits the use, or

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (c) permission for the use granted under an enactment is withdrawn or expires.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, the exception in subsection (2) applies only to the land that was actually being used for a non-farm use and not to the entire parcel on which that use was being carried on.

heading: Preservation of rights
paragraph:
24
		  Despite sections 2 and 3, if Crown land continued as agricultural land under this Act has been leased by the government, or sold by agreement for sale by the government and not transferred to the purchaser before December 21, 1972, and on that date was being used for a non-farm use, and not in contravention of the terms of the lease or agreement, that use may continue until termination of the lease or issue of title to the purchaser under the agreement for sale.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph:
25
		  (1) On receiving a use or subdivision application,

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (a) the commission, if required by the regulations, must reject the application, or

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (b) if paragraph (a) of this subsection does not apply, the commission may, subject to subsection (1.1),

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (i)  refuse permission for the use or subdivision applied for,

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (ii)  grant permission, with or without limits or conditions, for the use or subdivision applied for, or

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (iii)  grant permission for an alternative use or subdivision, with or without limits or conditions, as applicable.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (1.1) In making a determination under subsection (1) (b) with respect to an application for a non-adhering residential use, the commission

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (a) must consider the prescribed criteria, if any, and

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (b) must not grant permission for an additional residence unless the additional residence is necessary for a farm use.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (3) An application referred to in subsection (1), except such an application from a first nation government, may not proceed unless authorized by a resolution of the local government if, on the date the application is made, the application

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (a) applies to land that is zoned by bylaw to permit farm use, or

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (b) requires, in order to proceed, an amendment to an official settlement plan, an official community plan, an official development plan or a zoning bylaw.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (3.1) An application referred to in subsection (1) in relation to settlement lands may not proceed unless authorized by a law of the first nation government of the first nation that has legislative authority over the settlement lands.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (4) In deciding an application referred to in subsection (1), the commission may meet with the applicant or may make a decision on the basis of written representations only.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (4.1) A decision of the commission under subsection (1) (b) (ii) or (iii) in relation to proposed settlement lands may not be made effective unless and until

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (a) those lands are established, in whole or in part, as settlement lands, and

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (b) the first nation government in relation to those settlement lands enacts a law approving the commission's decision and provides a certified copy of the law to the commission.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (4.2) Unless a decision under subsection (1) (b) (ii) or (iii) first becomes effective under subsection (4.1), the decision expires on the earlier of the following dates:

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (a) the date the decision expires according to its terms;

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (b) the date that a notice to suspend negotiations takes effect.

heading: Applications by owner
paragraph: (5) The commission must deliver its written decision to the owner.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph:
26
		  (1) The commission may enter into an agreement with any of the following to enable a first nation government or an authority to exercise some or all of the commission's power to decide use or subdivision applications:

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (a) a first nation government, for applications made in respect of settlement lands within the jurisdiction of the first nation government;

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (b) an agent of the government, a public officer or a public body other than a local government, for applications made in respect of land within the jurisdiction of the authority, if the agent, officer or body is prescribed by regulation.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (2) An agreement under subsection (1) between the commission and an authority may exempt a non-farm use in a specified area within the jurisdiction of the authority from the requirement of an application on the condition that the authority conducts audits and reports to the commission as required by the agreement.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (3) If an agreement is entered into under subsection (1), the first nation government or authority must, with respect to an application covered by the agreement,

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (a) consider each application in the prescribed manner, and

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (b) advise the commission in the prescribed manner of each application received and of the decision made on each application.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (4) A decision made under this section must be made as follows:

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (a) in the case of a decision of a first nation government, by a law of the first nation government;

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (b) in the case of a decision of an authority, by a resolution of the governing body of the authority.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (5) If, by an agreement entered into under subsection (1) of this section, the commission delegates its power to decide applications under section 25 to a first nation government or an authority,

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (a) section 6 applies to the first nation government or the authority for the purposes of deciding use or subdivision applications, and

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (b) the decision of the first nation government or the authority is a decision of the commission for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (6) If an authority has the power to decide an application under an agreement entered into under subsection (1), an application that would otherwise be required to be submitted to a local government or first nation government under section 34.1 (1) must be made directly to the authority.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (7) If a first nation government or an authority has the power to decide an application under an agreement entered into under subsection (1),

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (a) the first nation government or authority may retain the entire fee payable under section 34 with respect to the application,

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (a.1) section 35.1 applies to the applicant with respect to the application, except that a reference to the commission in that section must be read as a reference to the first nation government or authority, and

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (b) sections 39 to 45 apply to the application as if the application were before the commission.

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (8) If the commission enters into an agreement under subsection (1) (c) with a first nation government in relation to settlement lands, that agreement or another agreement under this Act must include a definition of "owner" for the purposes of paragraph (b) (i) of the definition of "owner" in section 1 (1).

heading: Delegation of powers respecting applications
paragraph: (9) The Financial Administration Act does not apply in relation to a fee collected under this section.

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: 27		  (1) The commission, by resolution, may establish criteria under which the following may be approved by the chief executive officer:

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: (a) specified types of use or subdivision applications or exclusion applications;

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: (b) applications with respect to specified regions of British Columbia.

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: (2) The commission must put the criteria established under subsection (1) in writing and make them available for inspection during ordinary business hours.

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: (3) An application that meets the criteria established under subsection (1) may be approved by the chief executive officer on the terms that the chief executive officer may impose.

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: (4) If the chief executive officer considers that the application does not meet the criteria specified under subsection (1) or for any other reason does not wish to approve the application under subsection (3), the application must be referred to the commission for a decision.

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: (5) An approval of an application by the chief executive officer under subsection (3) is a decision of the commission for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Chief executive officer may approve some applications
paragraph: (6) The chief executive officer may not exercise a power that has been delegated to a first nation government or an authority by an agreement entered into under section 26.

heading: Application of sections 18 and 20 to 21 limited to agricultural land
paragraph:
28
		  For greater certainty, if a parcel of land is not wholly within the agricultural land reserve, sections 18 (1) to (4) and 20 to 21 apply only to that portion of the parcel that is agricultural land.

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph:
29
		  (1) A person may apply to the commission to have land excluded from the agricultural land reserve if the person is

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (a) the owner of the land and is

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (i)  the Province, a first nation government or a local government, or

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (ii)  a prescribed public body,

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (b) a local government, and the land is within the local government's jurisdiction, or

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (c) a first nation government, and the land is within the first nation's settlement lands.

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3),

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (a) an applicant must give notice, in the prescribed form and manner and before making the application, of the application and of a public hearing respecting that application, and

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (b) the public hearing must be held in the prescribed manner.

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (3) On request of an applicant described in subsection (1) (a), the commission may waive one or more of the requirements of subsection (2).

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (4) An application made by an applicant described in subsection (1) (a) may not proceed unless authorized as follows:

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (a) by a resolution of a local government if the application is made by a person other than a first nation government and, on the date the application is made, the application

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (i)  applies to land within the local government's jurisdiction that is zoned by bylaw to permit farm use, or

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (ii)  requires, in order to proceed, an amendment to an official settlement plan, official community plan, official development plan or zoning bylaw of the local government;

heading: Exclusion applications
paragraph: (b) by a law of a first nation government if the application applies to settlement lands over which the first nation has legislative authority.

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph:
29.1
		  (1) In this section, "decision respecting proposed settlement lands" means a decision of the commission made under subsection (2) (b) or (c) of this section on receiving an application under section 29

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (a) by an applicant described in subsection (1) (a) of that section, and

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (b) in relation to proposed settlement lands.

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application under section 29, the commission may do one of the following:

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (a) refuse permission to have land excluded from the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (b) grant permission, with or without limits or conditions, to have land excluded from the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (c) permit, with or without limits or conditions, a non-farm use, non-adhering residential use, soil or fill use or subdivision of land.

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (3) A decision respecting proposed settlement lands is not effective unless and until

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (a) those lands are established, in whole or in part, as settlement lands, and

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (b) the first nation government that has jurisdiction over those settlement lands enacts a law approving the commission's decision and provides a certified copy of the law to the commission.

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (4) Unless a decision respecting proposed settlement lands first becomes effective under subsection (3), the decision expires on the earlier of the following dates:

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (a) the date the decision expires according to its terms;

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (b) the date a notice to suspend negotiations takes effect.

heading: Decision on exclusion applications
paragraph: (5) The commission must deliver its written decision to the applicant.

heading: Exclusion by the commission
paragraph:
30
		  (1) On the commission's own initiative, the commission may do one of the following, with or without limits or conditions, as applicable:

heading: Exclusion by the commission
paragraph: (a) exclude land from the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Exclusion by the commission
paragraph: (b) permit a non-farm use, non-adhering residential use, soil or fill use or subdivision of land.

heading: Exclusion by the commission
paragraph: (2) Before taking action under subsection (1),

heading: Exclusion by the commission
paragraph: (a) the commission must give notice as required by the regulations of the commission's intentions and of a public hearing respecting those intentions, and

heading: Exclusion by the commission
paragraph: (b) the public hearing must be held in the prescribed manner.

heading: Exclusion by the commission
paragraph: (3) If the commission takes an action under subsection (1), it must deliver written notice of the action to the owner of the land.

heading: Effect of permission
paragraph:
31
		  It is a condition of a permission granted under section 25 (1) (b) (ii) or (iii), 29.1 (2) (b) or 30 (1) (b) that the person to whom permission was granted must comply with the applicable Acts, regulations, bylaws of the local government, laws of the first nation government, and decisions and orders of any person or body having jurisdiction over the land under an enactment.

heading: Boundaries to be amended
paragraph:
32
		  If land is excluded from the agricultural land reserve under this Act, the commission must do both of the following:

heading: Boundaries to be amended
paragraph: (a) amend the boundaries of the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Boundaries to be amended
paragraph: (b) notify the Registrar of Titles and the appropriate local government or first nation government.

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph:
33
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: "decision" means a decision made under this Act with respect to an application;

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: "decision maker" means the following, as applicable:

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (a) the commission, in relation to a decision made by the commission;

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (b) a panel, in relation to a decision made by the panel;

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (c) a first nation government or an authority, in relation to a decision made by the first nation government or the authority under an agreement entered into under section 26 (1).

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (2) On the written request of a person affected by a decision, or on a decision maker's own initiative, the decision maker may reconsider the decision maker's decision, and may confirm, reverse or vary the decision, if

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (b) no previous request has been made, if reconsideration is on request and not on the decision maker's own initiative, and

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (c) the decision maker determines that

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (i)  evidence has become available that was not available at the time of the original decision and could not have been available had the person affected by the decision exercised due diligence, or

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (ii)  all or part of the original decision was based on incorrect or false information.

heading: Reconsideration of decisions
paragraph: (3) The decision maker must give notice of an intention to reconsider a decision to any person that the decision maker considers is affected by the reconsideration.

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph:
33.1
		  (1) The chair of the commission may, in writing, direct the executive committee to reconsider a decision made by a panel respecting an application or other matter referred to the panel by the chair of the commission or a panel's reconsideration of a decision under section 33 (2), if

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (a) the chair considers that the decision or the reconsideration of the decision

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (i)  may not fulfill the purposes of the commission as set out in section 6 (1), or

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (ii)  fails to give priority to the matters referred to in section 6 (2), and

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (b) the chair makes the direction to the executive committee within 60 days of the decision being made.

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (2) If the chair of the commission directs the executive committee to reconsider a decision under subsection (1), the chair must give notice of the reconsideration to any person that the chair considers is affected by the reconsideration.

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (3) If the chair of the commission directs the executive committee to reconsider a decision under subsection (1), the executive committee must confirm, reverse or vary the decision.

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (3), the executive committee has all the powers and duties of the commission.

heading: Reconsideration of decisions of panel
paragraph: (5) A decision by the executive committee under subsection (3) is for all purposes a decision of the commission.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph:
34
		  (1) This section applies to the following types of applications:

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (a) an application made by a first nation government as the owner of proposed settlement lands, other than an inclusion application under section 17;

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (b) an exclusion application made by a person referred to in section 29 (1) (b) or (c);

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (c) an application for which review would be required under section 34.1, but the application is made by the local government or first nation government that would be responsible for the review;

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (d) an application for a specific type of use prescribed by regulation as an application that must be filed directly with the commission;

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (e) an application made under section 58.3 (1) (e), unless a regulation made under that section provides otherwise.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (2) A person may make an application described in subsection (1) by submitting the application and paying the prescribed application fee to the commission.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (3) In respect of an application described in subsection (1) (d), the commission

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (a) may request comments and information from the local government or first nation government for the area in which the land described in the application is located, and

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (b) if a request is made under paragraph (a) of this subsection, pay a prescribed portion of the fee received under subsection (2) to the local government or first nation government.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review not required
paragraph: (4) A local government or first nation government that is paid a fee under subsection (3) (b) may retain the fee, and the Financial Administration Act does not apply in relation to that fee.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: 34.1		  (1) A person may make an application to which section 34 does not apply by submitting the application and paying the prescribed application fee, if any, to the following, as applicable:

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (a) the municipality, if the land described in the application is in a municipality;

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (b) the regional district, if the land described in the application is in a regional district but not in a municipality or a local trust area;

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (c) the Islands Trust, if the land described in the application is within a local trust area under the Islands Trust Act;

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (d) the first nation government, if the land described in the application is in the settlement lands of a first nation.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (2) A local government or first nation government that receives an application must review the application and do one of the following:

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (a) forward to the commission

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (i)  the application, and

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (ii)  the comments and recommendations of the local government or first nation government respecting the application;

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (b) notify the applicant that the application will not be forwarded to the commission if

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (i)  the application is refused, or

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (ii)  the application may not, under this Act, proceed unless authorized by a resolution of the local government or a law of the first nation government and the required resolution or law is refused.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (3) If a local government or first nation government forwards an application under subsection (2) (a) to the commission, the applicant must pay the prescribed application fee, if any, to the commission.

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (4) The application fee that must be paid under subsection (3) is in addition to the application fee, if any, paid under subsection (1).

heading: Application procedure if local government or first nation government review required
paragraph: (5) A local government or first nation government that collects a fee under subsection (1) may retain the fee, and the Financial Administration Act does not apply in relation to that fee.

heading: Waiver of application fees
paragraph: 35		  (1) The commission may waive an application fee payable under section 34 (2) or 34.1 (3) if the commission considers that a case of hardship exists.

heading: Waiver of application fees
paragraph: (2) A designated local government officer or an official designated for this purpose by a first nation government may waive an application fee payable under section 34.1 (1) if the designated officer or official considers that a case of hardship exists.

heading: Waiver of application fees
paragraph: (3) The Financial Administration Act does not apply in relation to the waiver of a fee under this section.

heading: Information and fees respecting terms
paragraph: 35.1		  If, on making a decision under section 25 (1) (b) (ii) or (iii) or 29.1 (2) (b) or (c), the commission imposes one or more limits or conditions, the person who made the application resulting in the decision must submit to the commission the following:

heading: Information and fees respecting terms
paragraph: (a) the prescribed information and fees, if any;

heading: Information and fees respecting terms
