paragraph: (b) any other information requested by the commission, in the form and manner specified by the commission.

heading: Notice of applications
paragraph:
36
		  (1) A person who makes an application to which section 34 or 34.1 applies must, in the prescribed circumstances,

heading: Notice of applications
paragraph: (a) give notice of the application in accordance with the regulations, and

heading: Notice of applications
paragraph: (b) provide evidence, satisfactory to the commission, that the applicant has complied with the notice requirements of the regulations.

heading: Notice of applications
paragraph: (2) A decision of the commission with respect to an application is not invalidated merely because the applicant fails to comply with the notice requirements of the regulations, if the applicant made reasonable efforts to comply with those requirements.

heading: No compensation for inclusion in agricultural land reserve
paragraph:
37
		  Land is deemed not to be taken or injuriously affected by its inclusion in the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Agreements
paragraph:
38
		  For the purposes of this Act, the commission may enter into agreements with the government, a local government, a first nation government, Canada or an authority.

heading: Definition of "board" in sections 40 to 45
paragraph:
39
		  (1) In sections 40 to 45, "board" means a commissioner appointed as a study commission under the Public Inquiry Act for the purpose of inquiring into a matter described in section 40 of this Act.

heading: Definition of "board" in sections 40 to 45
paragraph: (2) The board has the powers set out in sections 22 and 23 of the Public Inquiry Act.

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: 40		  (1) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it to be in the Provincial interest, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may by order refer to the board, for the purpose of a public hearing described in section 43, any of the following matters before the commission at the time of the order:

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (a) an inclusion application under section 17 (1) or (3);

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (b) a use or subdivision application;

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (b.1) an exclusion application;

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (c) if land is being considered by the commission on its own initiative, the issues relating to

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (i)  approval and designation under section 17 (1),

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (ii)  an exclusion under section 30 (1) (a), or

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (iii)  a permission granted under section 30 (1) (b);

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (d) a reconsideration under section 33 of a decision of the commission made in respect of a matter referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c) of this subsection.

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must specify written terms of reference for the purpose of a public hearing by the board pertaining to a matter referred to the board under this section.

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (3) In determining whether it is in the Provincial interest to refer a matter to the board under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council must take into account

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (a) the preservation of agricultural land as a scarce and important asset,

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (b) the potential long term consequences of failing to preserve agricultural land, and

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (c) the province-wide context of the matter.

heading: Reference of a matter to the board
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make an order under subsection (1) on the Lieutenant Governor in Council's own initiative or at the request of a local government, a first nation government or the commission.

heading: Suspension of matters pending a decision under section 40
paragraph:
41
		  (1) For the purpose of giving the Lieutenant Governor in Council time to consider whether an order under section 40 is warranted, the minister may order that the matter be suspended for a period, to be specified in the order, that is not longer than 90 days.

heading: Suspension of matters pending a decision under section 40
paragraph: (2) An order of the minister under subsection (1) has effect and is binding on the commission, and on any parties to a proceeding relating to a matter that is the subject of the order, until the expiry of the period specified in the order.

heading: Effect of an order under section 40
paragraph:
42
		  (1) On the date of an order under section 40 referring a matter to the board, the commission's powers and duties under this Act in relation to the matter are transferred to the Lieutenant Governor in Council to the extent necessary to enable the Lieutenant Governor in Council to act in accordance with section 45.

heading: Effect of an order under section 40
paragraph: (2) An order under section 40 is final and binding.

heading: Effect of an order under section 40
paragraph: (3) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council makes an order under section 40 referring a matter to the board, the commission must, within 14 days of the date of the order,

heading: Effect of an order under section 40
paragraph: (a) prepare a written report with respect to the matter, and

heading: Effect of an order under section 40
paragraph: (b) submit the report to the board for the purpose of assisting the board in conducting a public hearing under section 43 in respect of the matter.

heading: Public hearing
paragraph:
43
		  (1) On receiving the written terms of reference specified in conjunction with an order under section 40, the board must

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (a) prepare a discussion paper with respect to the matter that is the subject of the order, and

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (b) make the paper available to the public before holding a public hearing under this section.

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (2) The discussion paper prepared under subsection (1) (a) must include the written report that the commission submitted to the board under section 42 (3) (b).

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of providing the report and recommendations required under section 44, the board must conduct a public hearing to evaluate the probable agricultural, environmental, heritage, economic, cultural and social effects of any of the following if it is a matter that was before the commission at the time the order under section 40 made the referral:

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (a) an approval and a designation under section 17 (1);

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (b) a designation under section 17 (3);

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (c) a refusal under section 29.1 (2) (a);

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (c.1) an exclusion under section 29.1 (2) (b) or 30 (1) (a);

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (d) a permission granted under section 29.1 (2) (c);

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (e) a decision under section 33 to confirm, reverse or vary a decision referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d) of this subsection.

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (4) The public hearing held under subsection (3) must be conducted in accordance with the terms of reference specified in conjunction with the order made under section 40.

heading: Public hearing
paragraph: (5) The board must hold at least one public hearing with respect to the matter in each administrative region.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph:
44
		  (1) On conclusion of the public hearing under section 43, the board must submit to the Lieutenant Governor in Council

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (a) a written report in accordance with the terms of reference specified in conjunction with the order made under section 40, and

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (b) a summary of the evidence received and submissions made in the course of any public hearing held in accordance with the terms of reference.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (2) The report referred to in subsection (1) must include the board's recommendations to the Lieutenant Governor in Council for action under section 45.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (3) In making the recommendations referred to in subsection (2), the board must give weight to the following values in descending order of priority:

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (a) agricultural values;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (b) environmental and heritage values, but only if

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (i)  those values cannot be replaced or relocated to land other than agricultural land, or

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (ii)  giving weight to those values results in no net loss to the agricultural capabilities of the area;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (c) economic, cultural and social values.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (4) The board must provide a copy of its report to the commission at the same time that the report is submitted to the Lieutenant Governor in Council under subsection (1).

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (5) The commission may submit to the Lieutenant Governor in Council written comments on the report, but it must do so within 30 days of receiving a copy of the report under subsection (4).

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (6) Within 10 days after submitting its report under subsection (1), the board must publish the report in the prescribed manner.

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council's decision
paragraph:
45
		  (1) On receiving the board's report under section 44 (1) and the commission's comments, if any, under section 44 (5), the Lieutenant Governor in Council, by order, may decide the outcome of the matter that is the subject of the order under section 40 by

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (a) granting or refusing to grant the approval, designation, exclusion or permission applied for, in the case of a matter described in section 40 (1) (a), (b) or (b.1),

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (b) making or deciding not to make the approval, designation, exclusion or permission that was under consideration by the commission on its own initiative, in the case of a matter described in section 40 (1) (c), or

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (c) confirming, reversing or varying a decision referred to in section 40 (1) (d).

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council's decision
paragraph:
(2) 
          Section 44 (3) applies to a decision made under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may attach conditions to an order made under this section.

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (4) An order made under this section is final and binding.

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph:
46
		  (1) In this section, "bylaw" means

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (a) a bylaw, made by a local government, that adopts a regional growth strategy, an official settlement plan, an official community plan, an official development plan or a zoning bylaw,

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (b) any other bylaw respecting land use in a local government's jurisdiction made by a local government under any other enactment, and

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (c) a law of a first nation government respecting land use within the first nation's settlement lands.

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (2) A local government in respect of its bylaws and a first nation government in respect of its laws must ensure consistency with this Act, the regulations and the orders of the commission.

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), nothing in this Act affects or impairs the validity of a local government bylaw or a first nation government law relating to the use of land in the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (4) A local government bylaw or a first nation government law that is inconsistent with this Act, the regulations or an order of the commission has, to the extent of the inconsistency, no force or effect.

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (5) Without limiting subsection (4), a local government bylaw or a first nation government law is deemed to be inconsistent with this Act if it

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (a) allows a use of land in the agricultural land reserve that is not permitted under this Act, or

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (b) contemplates a use of land that would impair or impede the intent of this Act, the regulations or an order of the commission, whether or not that use requires the adoption of any further bylaw or law, the giving of any consent or approval or the making of any order.

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (6) A local government bylaw or a first nation government law that provides restrictions on farm use, residential use or soil or fill use of land in the agricultural land reserve additional to those provided under this Act is not, for that reason alone, inconsistent with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Conflict with bylaws
paragraph: (7) This section applies only to local government bylaws or first nation government laws made after August 26, 1994.

heading: Consolidated revenue fund
paragraph:
47
		  The commission must pay as soon as practicable all money received by it, other than money received under an appropriation under a Supply Act, into the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Bonding or other security
paragraph:
48
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council, the commission, a local government, a first nation government or an authority may require that an applicant under this Act whose application has been approved on terms, in order to ensure compliance with the terms, post security in the form of insurance, a bond or another prescribed form of security.

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
49
		  (1) For the purposes of administering this Act or of ensuring compliance with this Act, the regulations or an order of the commission, a member of the commission or an official may do one or more of the following:

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) enter any land, other than a dwelling house;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) make any surveys, analyses, inspections, examinations or soil tests that are necessary to determine any of the following:

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (i)  the current use of the land;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (ii)  the suitability of the land for farm use;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (iii)  the potential effects that the proposed changes to the use of the land may have on agricultural land;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) remove soil samples for the purposes of conducting the analyses and tests referred to in paragraph (b);

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (d) make any inspection of records, things or activities reasonably related to the purpose of the inspection;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (e) make copies of any records or documents reasonably related to the purpose of the inspection;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (f) make an order requiring a person to produce for the member or official a record or thing in the person's possession or control.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (2) A person who hinders, obstructs, impedes or otherwise interferes with a person exercising a power under subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (3) If a member of the commission or an official exercises a power under subsection (1), the commission may order the person in respect of whom the power was exercised to pay to the commission fees related to the exercise of the power, as prescribed in the regulations.

heading: Stop work order
paragraph:
50
		  If an official considers that a person is contravening or is about to contravene a provision of this Act or the regulations, the official, in accordance with the regulations, may order that

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (a) the contravention cease,

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (b) the contravention cease to the extent specified by the order, or

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (c) the person not take any action that would result in a contravention.

heading: Power to rescind or vary orders
paragraph:
51
		  The chief executive officer may rescind or vary any determination, decision or order made by the chief executive officer or an official under section 50, 52 or 54

heading: Power to rescind or vary orders
paragraph: (a) on new information being provided to the chief executive officer,

heading: Power to rescind or vary orders
paragraph: (b) if the chief executive officer determines that there were insufficient grounds for making the determination, decision or order, or

heading: Power to rescind or vary orders
paragraph: (c) if the chief executive officer considers that it would be in the best interests of the administration of this Act.

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph:
52
		  (1) If the chief executive officer determines that a person has contravened this Act, the regulations or an order of the commission, the chief executive officer, in accordance with the regulations, may order the person to remedy the contravention by

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph: (a) carrying out a requirement of this Act or the regulations that the person has failed to carry out, or

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph: (b) repairing or mitigating damage caused to agricultural land by the contravention, including the removal of buildings or structures.

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to comply with an order under subsection (1), the chief executive officer, in accordance with the regulations, may do one or more of the following:

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph: (a) in a written notice given to the person, restrict or prohibit the person from carrying out the work referred to in the order;

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph: (b) require the person to provide the security that the chief executive officer considers necessary and realize on that security;

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph: (c) carry out all necessary work.

heading: Determinations and remediation orders
paragraph: (3) A person referred to in subsection (2) is liable to the commission for costs incurred by the commission under this section.

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph:
52.1
		  (1) If the chief executive officer makes a remediation order under section 52 (1) in respect of agricultural land, the chief executive officer may file in the land title office a written notice containing

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (a) a description of the agricultural land sufficient for the Registrar of Titles to identify the agricultural land in the records of the land title office, and

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (b) a statement that

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (i)  an order has been issued under this Act that affects the agricultural land,

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (ii)  further information about the order may be inspected at the offices of the commission, and

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (iii)  any person who acquires an interest in the agricultural land before the order ceases to have effect is subject to the order.

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (2) If a notice is filed under subsection (1) and on payment of all applicable fees imposed under the Land Title Act, the Registrar of Titles must make a note of the filing against the title to the land that is affected by the notice.

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (3) In the event of any omission, mistake or misfeasance by the Registrar of Titles or the staff of the Registrar of Titles in relation to the making of a note of a filing, or the registration of a transfer or other disposition under this section,

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (a) neither the Registrar of Titles, nor the government nor the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia is liable vicariously, and

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (b) neither the assurance fund nor the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia, as a nominal defendant, is liable under Part 19.1 [Land Title and Survey Authority Assurance Fund] of the Land Title Act.

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (4) If a note is made under subsection (2) of this section, the order made under section 52 (1) and, if applicable, any variation of it are binding on all persons who acquire an interest in the agricultural land that is the subject of the order.

heading: Notice of remediation orders in land title office
paragraph: (5) The authority under this section is in addition to any other action that the chief executive officer or the commission is authorized to take under this Act in respect of a contravention of this Act, the regulations or an order of the commission or chief executive officer.

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: 52.2		  (1) In this section:

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: "affected person" means an owner of land with respect to which a remediation order note has been made;

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: "cancellation notice" means a notice directing the cancellation of a remediation order note;

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: "remediation order" means an order made under section 52 (1);

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: "remediation order note" means a note made under section 52.1 (2).

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (2) If a remediation order is reversed on appeal,

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (a) the chief executive officer must deliver a cancellation notice to the Registrar of Titles, and

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (3) The chief executive officer may deliver a cancellation notice to the Registrar of Titles if the chief executive officer

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (a) is satisfied that a remediation order has been or cannot be substantially complied with, and

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (4) An affected person may apply to the chief executive officer to have a remediation order note cancelled by giving to the chief executive officer all of the following:

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (a) an application made in the form and manner required by the chief executive officer;

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (b) evidence satisfactory to the chief executive officer that the remediation order has been or cannot be substantially complied with.

heading: Cancellation of remediation order note
paragraph: (6) On receiving a cancellation notice and cancellation fee, if any, the Registrar of Titles must cancel the remediation order note referred to in the notice.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph:
53
		  (1) The commission may apply to the Supreme Court for an order under subsection (2) if the commission considers

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (a) that a person is not complying, or has not complied, with a determination, a decision or an order under section 49 (1) (f), 50, 52 or 54 (1),

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (b) that a person is not complying with an order of the commission, or

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (c) that a present or future activity or use of agricultural land may contravene this Act, the regulations, an order of the commission or a determination, a decision or an order under section 50, 52 or 54 (1).

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (2) On application by the commission under this section, the Supreme Court may make one or more of the following kinds of orders:

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (a) directing the person to comply with the determination, decision or order;

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (b) directing the person to cease violating the determination, decision or order;

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (c) restraining the person from violating the determination, decision or order;

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (d) if the person is a corporation, directing the directors and officers of the corporation to cause the corporation to comply with an order under this section.

heading: Penalties levied by chief executive officer
paragraph:
54
		  (1) The chief executive officer, in accordance with the regulations, may levy a penalty up to the prescribed amount against a person who contravenes this Act, the regulations or the orders of the commission.

heading: Penalties levied by chief executive officer
paragraph: (2) The time limit for levying a penalty against a person under subsection (1) is 3 years after the facts on which the penalty is based first came to the knowledge of the chief executive officer.

heading: Appeal
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A person who is the subject of a determination, a decision, an order or a penalty under section 50, 52 or 54 (1) may appeal the determination, decision, order or penalty to the commission by serving the commission with a notice of appeal.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (2) On an appeal under this section, the commission may

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (a) confirm, vary or reverse the determination, decision, order or penalty, or

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (b) refer the matter, with or without directions, back to the person who made the initial determination, decision or order.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (3) The commission must give notice of an appeal to any person the commission considers is affected by the appeal.

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to appeals
paragraph:
55.01
		  For the purposes of an appeal under section 55, the following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the commission:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to appeals
paragraph: (a) Part 4 [Practice and Procedure], except the following:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to appeals
paragraph: (i)  section 16 [consent orders];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to appeals
paragraph: (ii)  section 22 [notice of appeal (inclusive of prescribed fee)];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to appeals
paragraph: (iii)  section 26 (1) to (5) and (7) to (9) [organization of tribunal, except decision of majority is decision of panel];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act to appeals
paragraph: (iv)  section 27 [staff of tribunal];

heading: Land use regulations

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph:
3
		  (1) A subdivision of agricultural land is permitted for the purposes of the Act if

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (a) an approving officer determines that the subdivision is of a type referred to in subsection (2), and

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (b) the approving officer

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (i)  indicates the approval by endorsing on the plan of subdivision a certificate in the form required by the commission, and

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (ii)  submits to the commission a copy of the endorsed plan.

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (2) The following types of subdivision are permitted for the purposes of subsection (1) (a):

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (a) a subdivision that does one or more of the following:

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (i)  consolidates 2 or more parcels into a single parcel by eliminating common lot lines;

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (ii)  establishes a legal boundary along the boundary of the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (iii)  resolves a building encroachment on a property line, if no additional parcels are created;

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (b) a subdivision for which all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (i)  the agricultural land to be subdivided involves not more than 4 parcels, each of which is a minimum of 1 ha;

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (ii)  on subdivision, there would be no increase in the number of parcels and no parcel would be less than 1 ha;

heading: Subdivision permitted on determination by approving officer
paragraph: (iii)  the subdivision would allow for boundary adjustments that, in the opinion of the approving officer, will enhance farming on the agricultural land or permit better use of structures used for farming.

paragraph: (b) a fee as follows:

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (i)  $450 in the case of an application described in section 34 (1) (a), (c) or (e) of the Act that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use;

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (ii)  $750 in the case of an application described in section 34 (1) (a), (b), (c) or (e) of the Act other than one that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use;

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (iii)  $1 500 in the case of an application made under section 34 (1) (d) of the Act.

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) and (4) of this section, an applicant may make an application to which section 34.1 [local government or first nation government review required] of the Act applies by submitting to the applicable body under that section

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (a) an application in the form and manner required by the commission, and

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (b) a fee as follows:

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (i)  in the case of an application that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use,

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (A) $450 for the purposes of section 34.1 (1) of the Act, and

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (B) if applicable, an additional $450 for the purposes of section 34.1 (3) of the Act;

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of an application other than one that is made for the purposes of section 20.1 (2) (a) of the Act in respect of a non-adhering residential use,

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (A) $750 for the purposes of section 34.1 (1) of the Act, and

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (B) if applicable, an additional $750 for the purposes of section 34.1 (3) of the Act.

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (3) If a fee has already been submitted under section 20.3 (1) (c) (ii) [soil or fill use] of the Act in respect of an application, the fee payable under subsection (1) or (2) (b) (ii) of this section is reduced by $150.

heading: Applications and application fees
paragraph: (4) Applicants are exempt from paying application fees in respect of applications to include land in the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Payment by commission for comments or information
paragraph:
7
		  The commission may pay $200 to each local government or first nation government from which the commission requests comments or information under section 34 (3) [local government or first nation government review not required] of the Act.

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A local government or first nation government that receives an application under section 34.1 [application procedure if local government or first nation government review required] of the Act must, in accordance with this section, forward to the commission

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (a) the application, and

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (b) the comments and recommendations of the local government or first nation government in respect of the application.

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (2) The application, comments and recommendations must be forwarded within the following period after the local government or first nation government receives the application:

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (a) 90 days, if a public information meeting is held under section 19 (b) [public hearing and public information meeting];

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (b) 60 days, if paragraph (a) does not apply.

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (3) The comments and recommendations must be in a form acceptable to the commission and address all of the following that apply:

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (a) in the case of an exclusion application made by a public body applicant,

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (i)  whether the notice required under section 17 (a) [exclusion applications by public body applicants] of this regulation has been given,

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (ii)  whether the resolution or law required under section 29 (4) [exclusion applications] of the Act has been made, and

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (iii)  any responses the local government or first nation government received

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (A) under section 18 [responses to exclusion applications], and

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (B) through a public information meeting held under section 19 (b), if any;

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (b) in the case of a use or subdivision application, whether

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (i)  the resolution, if required under section 25 (3) [applications by owner] of the Act, has been made, or

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (ii)  the law required under section 25 (3.1) of the Act has been made.

heading: Local or first nation government review
paragraph: (4) The comments and recommendations may include any other information the local government or first nation government wants the commission to consider concerning the application.

heading: Procedures at meetings and public hearings
paragraph:
9
		  (1) The commission, a local government, a first nation government or a public body applicant that holds a meeting, public information meeting or a public hearing with respect to an application may, without limiting any other powers of the commission, local government, first nation government or public body applicant,

heading: Procedures at meetings and public hearings
paragraph: (a) designate the date, time and place for the meeting or public hearing, and

heading: Procedures at meetings and public hearings
paragraph: (b) adjourn the meeting or public hearing.

heading: Procedures at meetings and public hearings
paragraph: (2) The commission, a local government, a first nation government or a public body applicant holding a public hearing

heading: Procedures at meetings and public hearings
paragraph: (a) must give all persons present an opportunity to be heard on matters related to the proposal or application that is the subject of the public hearing, and

heading: Procedures at meetings and public hearings
paragraph: (b) may, without further notice, allow a proposal or application that is the subject of the public hearing to be amended to accommodate representations made at that public hearing.

heading: Procedures at meetings and public hearings
paragraph: (3) A member of the commission, a local government or a first nation government who was not present at a public hearing may vote on the proposal or application that was the subject of the public hearing if an oral or written report of the public hearing has been given to the member.

heading: Notice of action
paragraph:
10
		  (1) Without limiting any other requirement under the Act, the commission must give written notice to each applicable person referred to in subsection (2) if the commission does any of the following, whether on the commission's own initiative or on determination of an application:

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (a) includes, or refuses to include, land in the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (b) excludes, or refuses to exclude, agricultural land from the agricultural land reserve;

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (c) grants, or refuses to grant, permission for a use or subdivision;

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (d) reverses or varies a decision on reconsideration under the Act.

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (2) The persons who must receive notice are the following:

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (a) the applicant;

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (b) the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the land that is the subject of the action.

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph:
11
		  (1) An applicant must pay a fee in accordance with this section if

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (a) the commission, on granting an application, imposes a term or condition on the applicant, and

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (b) the effect of the term or condition is to cause an official to engage in an activity described in this section.

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (2) At the time that the term or condition is imposed, an applicant must pay a fee as follows:

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (a) $350 for each site inspection an official must conduct, unless subsection (3) applies;

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (b) $150 for each of the following that an official must administer, process, prepare, review, execute, file or register, other than in the context of an application:

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (i)  a contract or similar legal instrument, report, survey, map or a form of security;

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (ii)  a record that must be approved, filed or registered under an enactment;

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (iii)  a plan within the meaning of section 19 [registration restrictions] of the Act or a covenant, including related records necessary for deposit of the plan or covenant with a Registrar of Titles.

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (3) On the annual date set by the commission, an applicant must pay a fee as follows for each year or part of a year that an official monitors activities conducted on agricultural land:

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (a) $500 for agricultural land surveyed as being less than 0.8 ha;

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (b) $1 000 for agricultural land surveyed as being between 0.8 ha and 4 ha;

heading: Fees if action of official required
paragraph: (c) $2 000 for agricultural land surveyed as being more than 4 ha.

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph:
12
		  (1) The commission must publish the following information in respect of each application:

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (a) the date on which the application was received;

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (b) in general terms, the intent of the application;

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (c) the name of the applicant;

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (d) the dates on which the commission began and completed its review of the application;

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (e) the commission's determination and the reasons for it.

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1),

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (a) publication must be on a website maintained by or on behalf of the commission, and

heading: Publishing the status of applications
paragraph: (b) published information must be kept current.

heading: Proposals by commission
paragraph:
13
		  If the commission is proposing on the commission's own initiative to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve, the commission must do all of the following:

heading: Proposals by commission
paragraph: (a) give notice of the proposal not less than 3 days and not more than 10 days before the date of the public hearing;

heading: Proposals by commission
paragraph: (b) give a copy of the proposal and supporting material to each local government or first nation government whose interests, the commission believes, will be affected by the application;

heading: Proposals by commission
paragraph: (c) post a sign, in a form and manner acceptable to the commission, on the land that is the subject of the application.

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph:
14
		  (1) If a local or first nation government applicant is applying to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve, the applicant must do all of the following:

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (a) give notice of the application not less than 3 days and not more than 10 days before the date of the public hearing;

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (b) give a copy of the application to the following:

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (i)  if the land that is the subject of the application is adjacent to an area over which a different local government or first nation government has jurisdiction, that different local government or first nation government;

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (ii)  each local government or first nation government whose interests, the local or first nation government applicant believes, will be affected by the application;

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (c) include with the application

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (i)  a report of the public hearing and any additional public comments, and

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (ii)  any other supporting material the commission may require;

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (d) post a sign, in a form and manner acceptable to the commission, on the land that is the subject of the application.

heading: Applications by local or first nation government applicants
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1) (b), a local or first nation government applicant is not required to give a copy of an application to a first nation government referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of "first nation government" in section 1 of the Act.

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph:
15
		  (1) A notice of a public hearing must be given in accordance with this section by

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (a) the commission, in respect of a proposal on the commissions' own initiative to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve, and

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (b) a local or first nation government applicant, in respect of an application by the applicant to include land in, or exclude agricultural land from, the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (2) The notice must do all of the following:

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (a) state the general intent of the proposal or application;

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (b) identify the land affected, whether by using the legal description or by describing the land generally;

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (c) state the date, time and place of the public hearing;

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (d) state when and where a copy of the proposal or application may be inspected.

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (3) The notice must be published as follows:

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (a) publication must be in at least 2 issues of a newspaper within the meaning of the Community Charter;

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (b) the newspaper must be circulated in the municipality, regional district or settlement lands within which the land that is the subject of the proposal or application is located;

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (c) the last publication must be circulated not less than 3 days and not more than 10 days before the date of the public hearing.

heading: Notice of public hearing
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3) of this section, if the requirements of that subsection are not practical, the commission or local or first nation government applicant, as applicable, may give notice in the same manner as a council may give notice under section 94 (4) and (5) of the Community Charter.

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: 16		  (1) An applicant to exclude agricultural land from the agricultural land reserve is a public body applicant if the applicant is the owner of the agricultural land and is

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (a) the Province, a local government or a first nation government, or

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (b) a person or body listed in subsection (2).

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (2) The following are prescribed for the purposes of section 29 (1) (a) (ii) [exclusion applications] of the Act:

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (a) a regional health board designated under section 4 (1) of the Health Authorities Act;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (b) an educational body within the meaning of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (c) an improvement district within the meaning of the Local Government Act;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (d) BC Transportation Financing Authority;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (e) British Columbia Housing Management Commission;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (f) British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (g) South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (h) British Columbia Transit Corporation;

heading: Public body applicants
paragraph: (i) Columbia Power Corporation.

heading: Exclusion applications by public body applicants
paragraph: 17		  If a public body applicant is applying to exclude agricultural land from the agricultural land reserve, the public body applicant must do all of the following:

heading: Exclusion applications by public body applicants
paragraph: (a) give notice of the application not less than 3 days and not more than 10 days before the date of the public hearing;

heading: Exclusion applications by public body applicants
paragraph: (b) give a copy of the application to any local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over land that shares a common boundary with the agricultural land that is the subject of the application;

heading: Exclusion applications by public body applicants
paragraph: (c) include with the application a copy of the notice required under paragraph (a);

heading: Exclusion applications by public body applicants
paragraph: (d) post a sign, in a form and manner acceptable to the commission, on the land that is the subject of the application.

heading: Responses to exclusion applications
paragraph:
18
		  (1) If a public body applicant receives a response to a notice given under section 17 (a) [exclusion applications by public body applicants], the applicant must promptly forward the response to the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application.

heading: Responses to exclusion applications
paragraph: (2) A local government or first nation government that receives a copy of an application under section 17 (b) may respond to the application by giving comments and recommendations to the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application.

heading: Public hearing and public information meeting
paragraph:
19
		  If a public body applicant is applying to exclude agricultural land from the agricultural land reserve,

heading: Public hearing and public information meeting
paragraph: (a) the applicant must give notice of a public hearing in accordance with section 15 (2) to (4) [notice of public hearing] as if the applicant were a local or first nation government applicant, and

heading: Public hearing and public information meeting
paragraph: (b) the commission, or the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application, may, in addition to the public hearing, hold a public information meeting with respect to that application.

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph:
20
		  (1) The commission must do all of the following:

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (a) hold a meeting to determine an exclusion application;

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (b) not more than 30 days before the meeting, give written notice of the meeting to

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (i)  the applicant,

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (ii)  the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application, and

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (iii)  if the commission considers it advisable, each owner of agricultural land that shares a common boundary with, or is separated by a public road right of way from, the agricultural land that is the subject of the application;

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (c) before the meeting, give notice to the applicant of the following:

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (i)  the information, if any, related to the application that will be considered at the meeting;

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (ii)  any new information that becomes available.

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (2) At the meeting, the commission may do one or more of the following:

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (a) hear representations from the applicant;

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (b) accept written submissions or any other form of evidence, whether or not it would be admissible as evidence in a court of law;

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (c) hear representations, evidence and opinions the commission considers relevant of

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (i)  any person present or represented at the meeting, and

heading: Commission meeting
paragraph: (ii)  the local government or first nation government that has jurisdiction over the agricultural land that is the subject of the application.

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph:
21
		  (1) This section applies if

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (a) evidence is presented at a meeting of the commission held to determine an exclusion application, and

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (b) a statement or summary of that evidence has not been given to the applicant before the meeting.

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (2) If the applicant is present at the meeting, the commission may

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (a) hear further representations in respect of the evidence, or

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (b) adjourn the meeting to enable the applicant to answer the evidence.

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (3) If the applicant is not present at the meeting, the commission must notify the applicant personally or by registered or electronic mail of

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (a) the evidence, and

heading: Evidence presented at meeting
paragraph: (b) the date by which the additional evidence may be answered.

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph:
22
		  (1) For the purposes of section 34 (1) (d) [local government or first nation government review not required] of the Act, an application for any of the following uses must, unless the use is permitted under the Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation, be filed directly with the commission:

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (a) construction for the purpose of widening an existing road right of way;

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (b) construction of a road within an existing right of way;

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (c) construction of any of the following:

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (i)  a new road, railway or recreational trail;

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (ii)  a new forest service road under the Forest Act;

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (iii)  a utility corridor use;

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (iv)  a sewer or water line other than for ancillary utility connections;

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (d) a new use of an existing right of way for a recreational trail.

heading: Transportation and utility use applications
paragraph: (2) If the applicant is not the owner of the agricultural land that is the subject of the application, the applicant must give notice of the application to the owner within the period stated by the commission.

heading: Fill placement applications
paragraph: 23		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the commission must reject an application for permission to place fill on agricultural land if the fill to be placed includes any of the materials referred to in section 36 [prohibited fill] of the Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation.

heading: Fill placement applications
paragraph: (2) The commission may grant an application to use recycled concrete aggregate and recycled asphalt pavement within the meaning of section 36 of the Agricultural Land Reserve Use Regulation as fill on agricultural land for any of the following purposes:

heading: Fill placement applications
paragraph: (a) constructing, maintaining or widening a road;

heading: Fill placement applications
paragraph: (b) constructing or maintaining a parking area.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
24
		  In sections 25 [residency information] and 26 [determining residency in administrative region], "director" means the director of the office of the government that is responsible for the recruitment and recommendation of candidates for appointments to all Crown corporations, agencies, boards and commissions.

heading: Residency information
paragraph:
25
		  (1) A person is a resident of an administrative region if the person

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (a) is a citizen or permanent resident of Canada,

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (b) resides in the administrative region, and

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (c) intends to return to the administrative region when absent.

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (2) A person seeking to be appointed as a member of the commission must do all of the following:

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (a) identify to the director, in writing,

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (i)  the administrative region of which the person is a resident, and

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (ii)  either the regional district in which the person is a resident or, if the person resides in the area referred to in section 4 (b) of the Schedule to the Act, that area;

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (b) provide supporting evidence for the purpose of subsection (1).

heading: Residency information
paragraph: (3) The director may request additional supporting evidence to that provided under subsection (2) (b).

heading: Determining residency in administrative region
paragraph:
26
		  (1) If the director is satisfied that a person seeking to be appointed as a member of the commission is a resident of the administrative region identified by the person under section 25 (2) (a) (i) [residency information], the director must provide confirmation of that fact and the information provided under that section to

heading: Determining residency in administrative region
paragraph: (a) the Lieutenant Governor in Council, in the case of a person seeking to be appointed as chair of the commission, and

heading: Determining residency in administrative region
paragraph: (b) the minister, in any other case of a person seeking to be appointed as a member of the commission.

heading: Determining residency in administrative region
paragraph: (2) Confirmation by the director that a person is a resident of an administrative region must be in writing and is final and binding.

heading: Mapping of agricultural land reserve boundaries
paragraph:
27
		  The commission must ensure that

heading: Mapping of agricultural land reserve boundaries
paragraph: (a) the agricultural land reserve boundary is represented on maps using technology, standards and security procedures the commission considers appropriate, and

heading: Mapping of agricultural land reserve boundaries
paragraph: (b) a map referred to in paragraph (a) is updated as soon as reasonably practicable after becoming aware that the agricultural land reserve boundary is not accurately represented on the map.

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph:
28
		  The commission must submit to the minister reports as follows:

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: (a) before June 30 of each year, an annual report that includes information respecting the financial operation of the commission and a financial statement

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: (i)  showing the commission's financial operations for the 2 preceding financial years, and

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: (ii)  prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and the accounting policies and practices established by Treasury Board;

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: (b) on request of the minister, a report that includes the following information with respect to the period specified by the minister:

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: (i)  information specified by the minister respecting the administration of the Act by the commission and the expenditure of the budget allocated to the commission;

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: (ii)  information respecting expenditures in relation to specific budget allocations.

heading: Publishing reports
paragraph:
29
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2) of this section, the commission must publish on a website maintained by or on behalf of the commission a report submitted under

heading: Publishing reports
paragraph: (a) section 44 [report and recommendations respecting matters referred to the board] of the Act, and

heading: Publishing reports
paragraph: (b) section 28 [reports to minister] of this regulation, no earlier than 60 days and not later than 90 days after submitting the report.

heading: Publishing reports
paragraph: (2) The minister may direct the commission not to publish any part of a report that, in the opinion of the minister, contains information that would be protected from disclosure under Division 2 of Part 2 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, whether the information relates to the commission or to the government.

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: 30		  (1) The chief executive officer must consider all of the following before levying a penalty against a person for contravening the Act, the regulations or an order of the commission:

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (a) the gravity and magnitude of the contravention;

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (b) whether the contravention was deliberate, repeated or continuous;

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (c) whether there has been any contravention of a similar nature by the person;

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (d) whether the person derived an economic benefit from the contravention;

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (e) the person's cooperativeness and efforts to correct the contravention;

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (f) the degree to which the contravention detrimentally affected or impaired the agricultural capability of agricultural land or its suitability for farming.

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (2) The maximum penalty which the chief executive officer may levy is as follows:

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (a) for any single contravention, $100 000;

heading: Penalties for contraventions
paragraph: (b) for a subsequent contravention, double the amount of the penalty levied for the first contravention.

heading: Notice of action
paragraph:
31
		  (1) In this section, "action" means a determination or an order made, or a penalty levied, under section 50 [stop work order], 52 [determinations and remediation orders] or 54 (1) [penalties levied by chief executive officer] of the Act.

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (2) An official who takes an action must give notice of the action to the person against whom it is taken.

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (3) If the chief executive officer levies a penalty against a person for contravening the Act, the regulations or an order of the commission, the chief executive officer must set out all of the following in the notice:

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (a) the nature of the contravention;

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (b) the amount of the penalty;

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (c) the date by which the penalty must be paid;

heading: Notice of action
paragraph: (d) a description of the person's right to appeal the penalty.

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph:
32
		  (1) An official who is required to give notice under section 31 (2) [notice of action] must give the notice by one or more of the following means:

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (a) personally;

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (b) by registered mail sent to the person's last known address;

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (c) by electronic mail sent to the person's last known electronic mail address;

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (d) by posting the notice at a conspicuous location on the agricultural land that is the subject of the notice.

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (2) Notice is deemed to have been received by the person who is the subject of the notice as follows:

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (a) if sent in accordance with subsection (1) (b), on the 14th day after deposit with Canada Post unless the person actually received the notice before that day;

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (b) if sent in accordance with subsection (1) (c), as follows:

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (i)  as provided for under section 18 (2) of the Electronic Transactions Act;

heading: Giving a notice of action
paragraph: (ii)  despite subparagraph (i), no later than 96 hours after the notice was sent.

heading: Service and receipt of notice and records generally
paragraph: 33		  Except as otherwise set out in this regulation,

heading: Service and receipt of notice and records generally
paragraph: (a) if the commission is required to give a notice under the Act, the commission may determine the form and manner of giving the notice, and

heading: Service and receipt of notice and records generally
paragraph: (b) if a person other than the commission is required to give a notice under the Act, the person must do so in a form and manner acceptable to the commission.

heading: Notice of statutory right of way
paragraph:
34
		  (1) For the purposes of section 18.1 (3) [notice of statutory right of way] of the Act, the form issued by the commission to the applicant under subsection (2) of this section, confirming that the commission received notice in accordance with section 18.1 (2) of the Act, is proof that notice has been given as required under that section.

heading: Notice of statutory right of way
paragraph: (2) The commission

heading: Notice of statutory right of way
paragraph: (a) must, if it received notice in accordance with section 18.1 (2) of the Act, issue a form confirming that fact, and

heading: Notice of statutory right of way
paragraph: (b) may issue the form electronically or otherwise.

heading: Fee if notice of intent to remove soil or place fill
paragraph:
35
		  A person who submits to the chief executive officer a notice of intent to remove soil or place fill on agricultural land must pay a fee of $150.

heading: Delegation to British Columbia Energy Regulator
paragraph:
36
		  The commissioner appointed under the Energy Resource Activities Act is prescribed as a public officer for the purposes of section 26 (1) (b) [delegation of powers respecting applications] of the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Agricultural Land Commission Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agri-tourism activity" means an activity referred to in section 12 [agri-tourism];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "compost" means a product that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a stabilized earthy matter having the properties and structure of humus,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) beneficial to plant growth when used as a soil amendment,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) produced by composting, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) derived only from organic matter;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "controlled environment structure" means a structure that provides a controlled environment intended to intensify crop production, including, without limitation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a vertical farming system,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a rotating tray system, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any other structure that minimizes the use of land, controls the use of light, air, water or nutrients or relies in whole or in part on automation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but not including

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a greenhouse,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a structure for mushroom production, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) a structure described in section 8 (1) (b) or (2) that is used for producing cannabis in accordance with section 8;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "farm product" means a commodity that is produced from a farm use but does not include water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "gathering for an event" means a gathering of people on agricultural land for the purpose of attending

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a wedding, other than a wedding to which paragraph (c) (ii) applies,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a music festival, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) an event, other than

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  an event held for the purpose of an agri-tourism activity, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the celebration, by residents of the agricultural land and those persons whom they invite, of a family event for which no fee or other charge is payable in connection with the event by invitees;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "soil amendment" means compost, fertilizer, manure, mulch and soil conditioners.

heading: Other laws not ousted
paragraph: 2		  For the purpose of section 2 (1) of the Act, a person who engages in a use of agricultural land that is permitted under this regulation is not relieved from complying with

heading: Other laws not ousted
paragraph: (a) any other enactment that may apply, or

heading: Other laws not ousted
paragraph: (b) a decision of a responsible authority that may apply.

heading: If farming extends over multiple parcels
paragraph:
3
		  Unless a contrary intention appears, a reference to a use of agricultural land includes all of the agricultural land on which a single farm operation is conducted, regardless of

heading: If farming extends over multiple parcels
paragraph: (a) whether activities are conducted over one parcel or multiple parcels, or

heading: If farming extends over multiple parcels
paragraph: (b) whether, in the case of multiple parcels, the parcels are adjacent.

heading: Controlled environment structures
paragraph:
3.1
		  The use of agricultural land to construct, maintain or operate a controlled environment structure is designated as a farm use.

heading: Farm uses that may not be prohibited
paragraph:
4
		  The farm uses referred to in this Division may not be prohibited

heading: Farm uses that may not be prohibited
paragraph: (a) by a local government enactment except a bylaw under section 552 [farming area bylaws] of the Local Government Act, or

heading: Farm uses that may not be prohibited
paragraph: (b) by a first nation government law, if the activity is conducted on settlement lands.

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: 5		  (1) Subject to any limits and conditions set out in this Division, the use of agricultural land to construct, maintain or operate any of the following is designated as a farm use and may not be prohibited as described in section 4:

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (a) a structure, other than a residential structure, that is necessary for a farm use;

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (b) a driveway or utility that is necessary for a farm use.

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, subsection (1) (a) includes all of the following:

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (a) a greenhouse;

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (b) a structure for use in an intensive livestock operation or for mushroom production;

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (c) an aquaculture facility.

heading: Land development works
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for conducting land development works may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if the works are required for farm uses conducted on the agricultural land on which the works are conducted.

heading: Land development works
paragraph: (2) Without limiting paragraph (b) of the definition of "farm operation" in section 1 of the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act, land development works include all of the following:

heading: Land development works
paragraph: (a) levelling and berming agricultural land;

heading: Land development works
paragraph: (b) constructing reservoirs;

heading: Land development works
paragraph: (c) constructing works ancillary to clearing, draining, irrigating, levelling or berming agricultural land and to constructing reservoirs.

heading: Soil testing, biosolids and soil amendments
paragraph: 7		  (1) Soil sampling conducted on agricultural land, including testing of the soil samples, may not be prohibited as described in section 4.

heading: Soil testing, biosolids and soil amendments
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for storing and applying biosolids and soil amendments, other than compost, may not be prohibited as described in section 4.

heading: Soil testing, biosolids and soil amendments
paragraph: (3) The use of agricultural land for producing, storing and applying compost may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if, in the case of

heading: Soil testing, biosolids and soil amendments
paragraph: (a) compost classified as Class A compost under the Organic Matter Recycling Regulation, all of the compost produced, stored and applied is used on the agricultural land on which it was produced, or

heading: Soil testing, biosolids and soil amendments
paragraph: (b) any other compost, the compost is from agricultural by-products that were produced for a farm use.

heading: Cannabis
paragraph:
8
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for producing cannabis lawfully may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if the cannabis is produced

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (a) outdoors in a field, or

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (b) inside a structure that, subject to subsection (2), has a base consisting entirely of soil.

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for producing cannabis lawfully may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if the cannabis is produced inside a structure that meets both of the following conditions:

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (a) the structure was, before July 13, 2018,

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (i)  constructed for the purpose of growing crops inside it, including but not limited to producing cannabis lawfully, or

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (ii)  under construction for the purpose referred to in subparagraph (i), if that construction

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (A) was being conducted in accordance with all applicable authorizations and enactments, and

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (B) continues without interruption from the date it began until the date the structure is completed, other than work stoppages considered reasonable in the building industry;

heading: Cannabis
paragraph: (b) the structure has not been altered since July 13, 2018 to increase the size of its base or to change the material used as its base.

heading: Horse facilities
paragraph:
9
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for commercial horse riding, training and boarding may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Horse facilities
paragraph: (a) facilities for horse riding do not include a racetrack that is or must be licensed by the British Columbia Racing Commission;

heading: Horse facilities
paragraph: (b) no more than 40 horses are boarded on the agricultural land.

heading: Horse facilities
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for non-commercial horse riding, training and boarding is designated as a farm use and may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if both of the conditions referred to in subsection (1) of this section are met.

heading: Forestry
paragraph:
10
		  The following uses of agricultural land are designated as farm uses and may not be prohibited as described in section 4:

heading: Forestry
paragraph: (a) deliberately retaining, introducing and mixing trees or other plants in crop or animal production systems to provide an economic return, commonly referred to as "agroforestry";

heading: Forestry
paragraph: (b) producing botanical forest products;

heading: Forestry
paragraph: (c) producing and harvesting timber, including engaging in silviculture and forest protection activities.

heading: Farm products
paragraph:
11
		  (1) In this section, "association" has the same meaning as in the Cooperative Association Act.

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for storing, packing, preparing and processing farm products is designated as a farm use and may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if at least 50% of the farm product is

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (a) produced either on that agricultural land or by an association to which the owner of the agricultural land belongs, or

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (b) feed required for farm use on that agricultural land.

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (3) The use of agricultural land for conducting farm retail sales is designated as a farm use and may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (a) all of the farm products offered for sale are produced on that agricultural land, or

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (b) the area used for all retail sales meets both of the following conditions:

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (i)  the total area, both indoors and outdoors, does not exceed 300 m2;

heading: Farm products
paragraph: (ii)  at least 50% of that area is limited to the sale of farm products produced either on that agricultural land or by an association to which the owner of the agricultural land belongs.

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: 11.1		  (1) In this section:

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: "farm product rule" means a requirement imposed under section 11 (2) respecting the proportion of farm product stored, packaged, prepared or processed;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: "specified facility" means a facility, in existence on the first day of the temporary exception period, for storing, packing, preparing or processing fruit all or most of which is specified fruit;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: "specified fruit" means any of the following:

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (a) apples;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (b) apricots;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (c) cherries;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (d) nectarines;
