heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (e) peaches;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (f) pears;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (g) prune plums;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (h) table grapes;

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: "temporary exception period" means the period that

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (a) begins on the date on which this section comes into force, and

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (b) ends on March 31, 2026.

heading: Farm products - temporary exception for specified fruits
paragraph: (2) Despite section 11 (2), the farm product rule does not apply with respect to the storing, packing, preparing or processing of specified fruit at a specified facility during the temporary exception period.

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph:
12
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for conducting an agri-tourism activity described in subsection (2) of this section is designated as a farm use and may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (a) the activity is conducted on agricultural land that is classified as a farm under the Assessment Act;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (b) members of the public are ordinarily invited to the activity, whether or not a fee or other charge is payable;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (c) no permanent facilities are constructed or erected in connection with the activity.

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (2) The following are agri-tourism activities for the purposes of subsection (1):

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (a) an agricultural heritage exhibit displayed on the agricultural land;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (b) a tour of the agricultural land, an educational activity or demonstration in respect of all or part of the farm operation conducted on that agricultural land, and activities ancillary to any of these;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (c) cart, sleigh and tractor rides on the agricultural land;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (d) subject to section 9 [horse facilities], activities that promote or market livestock raised or kept on the agricultural land, whether or not the activity also involves livestock raised or kept elsewhere, including shows, cattle driving and petting zoos;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (e) dog trials held on the agricultural land;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (f) harvest festivals and other seasonal events held on the agricultural land for the purpose of promoting or marketing farm products produced on that agricultural land;

heading: Agri-tourism
paragraph: (g) corn mazes prepared using corn produced on the agricultural land on which the activity is taking place.

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: 13		  (1) In this section:

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: "alcohol product" means beer, cider, spirits, mead or wine;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: "alcohol production facility" means a brewery, cidery, distillery, meadery or winery;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: "ancillary use" means the following activities conducted at an alcohol production facility:

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (a) processing, storing and retail sales of an alcohol product produced by the alcohol production facility;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (b) operating a food and beverage service lounge, if the area of the lounge does not exceed 125 m2 indoors and 125 m2 outdoors;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (c) selling an alcoholic beverage other than one produced by the alcohol production facility, if the alcoholic beverage is intended to be consumed immediately and is sold

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (i)  as a single serving in a lounge referred to in paragraph (b), or

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (ii)  in a service area under a special event area endorsement endorsed on the licence issued under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act for the alcohol production facility;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (d) conducting a cooking class, if the class is held in a food premises within the meaning of the Food Premises Regulation that has been constructed, and is being operated, in compliance with that regulation;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (e) gathering for an event, if the event is held only in the lounge referred to in paragraph (b) or the special event area under a special event area endorsement referred to in paragraph (c), and, for this purpose, section 17 [gathering for an event] does not apply;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: "brewery", "cidery", "distillery", "meadery" and "winery" mean a brewery, cidery, distillery, meadery or winery, as applicable, that is licensed under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act to produce beer, cider, spirits, mead or wine;

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: "primary farm product" means the farm product that is the primary ingredient used in a fermentation process to make an alcohol product.

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for constructing, maintaining and operating an alcohol production facility and the use of the facility for ancillary uses are designated as farm uses and may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (a) at least 50% of the primary farm product used to make the alcohol product produced each year is harvested from the agricultural land on which the alcohol production facility is located, or

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (b) the agricultural land on which the alcohol production facility is located is more than 2 ha in area and at least 50% of the primary farm product used to make the alcohol product produced each year is

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (i)  harvested from that agricultural land, or

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (ii)  both harvested from that agricultural land and received from a farm operation located in British Columbia that provides that primary farm product to the alcohol production facility under a contract having a term of at least 3 years.

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), the use of agricultural land for maintaining and operating a winery or cidery and ancillary uses is designated as a farm use and may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (a) the winery or cidery

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (i)  is the subject of a licence under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act to produce wine or cider, issued on or before June 15, 2015, or

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (ii)  is the subject of a letter of eligibility to produce wine or cider, given in respect of a licensing application made under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act and received during the period that begins June 15, 2014 and ends June 15, 2015, and

heading: Alcohol production
paragraph: (b) the production of wine or cider by the winery or cidery would be designated as a farm use under section 2 (2) (b) of the Agricultural Land Reserve Use, Subdivision and Procedure Regulation as it read on June 14, 2015.

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: 13.01		  (1) In this section:

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: "primary farm product rule" means a requirement respecting the proportion of primary farm product used to make an alcohol product imposed under

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: (a) section 13 (2) of this regulation, or

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: (b) section 2 (2) (b) of the Agricultural Land Reserve Use, Subdivision and Procedure Regulation as it read on June 14, 2015;

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: "temporary exception period" means the period that

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: (a) begins on the date on which this section comes into force, and

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: (b) ends on March 31, 2026.

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: (2) Despite section 13, primary farm product rules do not apply with respect to either of the following:

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: (a) the processing by a winery of wine made from grapes or grape products acquired by the winery during the temporary exception period, if processing begins during that period;

heading: Temporary exception for wine made from grapes
paragraph: (b) the continued processing, and the storage and sale, of wine to which paragraph (a) applies.

heading: Controlled environment structures
paragraph:
13.1
		  The use of agricultural land to construct, maintain or operate a controlled environment structure may not be prohibited as described in section 4 if

heading: Controlled environment structures
paragraph: (a) the structure that is being constructed, maintained or operated as a controlled environment structure was constructed or was under construction before August 31, 2022, and

heading: Controlled environment structures
paragraph: (b) the structure is constructed in accordance with all applicable authorizations and enactments.

heading: Permitted non-farm uses that may not be prohibited
paragraph:
14
		  The non-farm uses permitted under this Division may not be prohibited

heading: Permitted non-farm uses that may not be prohibited
paragraph: (a) by a local government enactment, or

heading: Permitted non-farm uses that may not be prohibited
paragraph: (b) by a first nation government law, if the activity is conducted on settlement lands.

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph:
15
		  Subject to any limits and conditions set out in this Division, the use of agricultural land to construct, maintain or operate any of the following is permitted and may not be prohibited as described in section 14:

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (a) a structure, other than a residential structure, that is necessary for a non-farm use permitted under this Division;

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (b) a driveway or utility that is necessary for a non-farm use permitted under this Division.

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph:
16
		  The following uses of agricultural land are permitted and may not be prohibited as described in section 14:

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (a) a park established or continued under the Park Act or the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act;

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (b) an ecological reserve established or continued under the Ecological Reserve Act or the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act;

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (c) a wildlife management area designated under the Wildlife Act;

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (d) a reserve established under section 15 of the Land Act for recreational use;

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (e) a recreation site established under section 56 of the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (f) an area established by order under section 7 (1) of the Environment and Land Use Act to protect the environment or restrict land or resource use within the area.

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: 17		  The use of agricultural land for the purpose of gathering for an event is permitted and may not be prohibited as described in section 14 if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (a) the event is conducted on agricultural land that is classified as a farm under the Assessment Act;

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (b) no permanent facilities are constructed or erected in connection with the event;

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (c) parking for those attending the event

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (i)  is available on that agricultural land,

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (ii)  occurs only in connection with that event, and

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (iii)  does not interfere with the productivity of that agricultural land;

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (d) no more than 150 people, excluding residents of the agricultural land and employees of the farm operation conducted on that agricultural land, are gathered on that agricultural land at one time for the purpose of attending the event;

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (e) the event is of no more than 24 hours in duration;

heading: Gathering for an event
paragraph: (f) no more than 10 gatherings for an event of any type occur on that agricultural land within a single calendar year.

heading: Roads
paragraph: 18		  The use of agricultural land for any of the following purposes is permitted and may not be prohibited as described in section 14:

heading: Roads
paragraph: (a) constructing and upgrading roads within a dedicated right of way that has a constructed road bed for vehicular access and use;

heading: Roads
paragraph: (b) upgrading an existing road that has vehicular access and use and that is declared to be a highway under section 42 of the Transportation Act;

heading: Roads
paragraph: (c) widening an existing constructed road within a right of way

heading: Roads
paragraph: (i)  to ease one curve, or

heading: Roads
paragraph: (ii)  if the right of way width is 24 m or less, for safety or maintenance purposes or for drainage or flood control works;

heading: Roads
paragraph: (d) declaring as a forest service road an existing road under the Forest Act or a new road in a managed forest;

heading: Roads
paragraph: (e) increasing the width of a forest service road within a right of way by up to 4 m if the right of way width is

heading: Roads
paragraph: (i)  30 m or less, if the forest service road is located on Crown land, or

heading: Roads
paragraph: (ii)  20 m or less, in any other case;

heading: Roads
paragraph: (f) constructing and upgrading a road, and conducting related works, for the purpose of realigning Highway 29 between Hudson's Hope and Charlie Lake, to the extent necessary to

heading: Roads
paragraph: (i)  construct the dam and hydroelectric generating station on the Peace River known as the Site C Clean Energy Project, and

heading: Roads
paragraph: (ii)  address potential adverse effects on the highway arising from the operation of the dam and generating station referred to in subparagraph (i).

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: 19		  The use of agricultural land for any of the following purposes is permitted and may not be prohibited as described in section 14:

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (a) collecting surface water for farm use or domestic use, water well drilling, connection of water lines and access to water well sites;

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (b) surveying, exploring and prospecting for gravel or minerals if all cuts, trenches and similar alterations are restored to the natural ground level on completing the surveying, exploring or prospecting;

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (c) constructing, upgrading and operating a railway on an existing railbed within a dedicated right of way;

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (d) widening an existing railbed within a right of way if the right of way width is 30.5 m or less.

heading: Permitted non-farm uses that may be prohibited
paragraph:
20
		  The non-farm uses permitted under this Division may be prohibited

heading: Permitted non-farm uses that may be prohibited
paragraph: (a) by a local government enactment, or

heading: Permitted non-farm uses that may be prohibited
paragraph: (b) by a first nation government law, if the activity is conducted on settlement lands.

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph:
21
		  Subject to any limits and conditions set out in this Division, the use of agricultural land to construct, maintain or operate any of the following is permitted but may be prohibited as described in section 20:

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (a) a structure, other than a residential structure, that is necessary for a non-farm use permitted under this Division;

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (b) a driveway or utility that is necessary for a non-farm use permitted under this Division.

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph:
22
		  (1) The following uses of agricultural land are permitted but may be prohibited as described in section 20:

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (a) an open land park established by a local government or a first nation government, other than an aboriginal governing body referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of "first nation government" in the Act, for biodiversity conservation, passive recreation, heritage, wildlife or scenery viewing purposes;

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (b) converting non-forested land to forested land on parcels less than 20 ha, other than for a farm use as described in section 10 [forestry].

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for biodiversity conservation, passive recreation, heritage, wildlife and scenery viewing purposes, other than in a park referred to in subsection (1) (a), is permitted, but may be prohibited as described in section 20, if both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (a) the area occupied by any associated structures does not exceed 100 m2 for each parcel;

heading: Parks and similar areas
paragraph: (b) the purpose does not include the creation of a wetland intended to manage urban runoff or waste.

heading: Keeping animals
paragraph:
23
		  The following uses of agricultural land are permitted but may be prohibited as described in section 20:

heading: Keeping animals
paragraph: (a) pet breeding and boarding;

heading: Keeping animals
paragraph: (b) sheltering and caring for surrendered, abandoned or seized livestock;

heading: Keeping animals
paragraph: (c) providing a refuge for wildlife within the meaning of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Home occupation use
paragraph: 24		  (1) The use of agricultural land for a commercial or similar use within a structure is permitted, but may be prohibited as described in section 20, if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Home occupation use
paragraph: (a) the structure is accessory to and located on the same parcel as a residence;

heading: Home occupation use
paragraph: (b) the structure occupies an area that does not exceed

heading: Home occupation use
paragraph: (i)  the limit specified in an applicable local government enactment or first nation government law, or

heading: Home occupation use
paragraph: (ii)  if subparagraph (i) does not apply, 100 m2.

heading: Home occupation use
paragraph: (2) The conditions set out in subsection (1) do not apply to a type of use referred to in any other provision of this regulation.

heading: Infrastructure
paragraph:
25
		  The following uses of agricultural land are permitted but may be prohibited as described in section 20:

heading: Infrastructure
paragraph: (a) constructing, maintaining and operating force mains, trunk sewers, gas pipelines and water lines within an existing dedicated right of way;

heading: Infrastructure
paragraph: (b) constructing, maintaining and operating, for the purpose of drainage or irrigation or to combat the threat of flooding,

heading: Infrastructure
paragraph: (i)  dikes and related pumphouses, and

heading: Infrastructure
paragraph: (ii)  ancillary works, including access roads and facilities.

heading: Aggregate removal
paragraph:
26
		  The use of agricultural land for the purpose of removing aggregate is permitted, but may be prohibited as described in section 20, if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Aggregate removal
paragraph: (a) the total volume of aggregate removed from any single parcel is less than 500 m3;

heading: Aggregate removal
paragraph: (b) regardless of the volume of aggregate removed, the disturbed area is rehabilitated in accordance with good agricultural practice as soon as reasonably practicable after

heading: Aggregate removal
paragraph: (i)  aggregate removal is complete, if the aggregate is removed as part of a single continuous operation, or

heading: Aggregate removal
paragraph: (ii)  each stage of aggregate removal is complete, if subparagraph (i) does not apply;

heading: Aggregate removal
paragraph: (c) the cultivable surface layer of soil is salvaged, stored on the parcel and available for rehabilitation in accordance with paragraph (b).

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph:
27
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for producing and developing biological products used in integrated pest management programs is permitted, but may be prohibited as described in section 20, if the area occupied by all structures used for the production or development does not exceed 300 m2 for each parcel.

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for producing, storing and applying compost classified as Class A compost under the Organic Matter Recycling Regulation is permitted, but may be prohibited as described in section 20, if at least 50% but less than 100% of the compost produced, stored and applied is used on the agricultural land on which it was produced.

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (3) The use of agricultural land for operating a temporary sawmill is permitted, but may be prohibited as described in section 20, if at least 50% of the volume of milled timber is harvested from the agricultural land on which the sawmill is located.

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (4) The use of agricultural land for education and conducting research respecting a farm use or permitted non-farm use is permitted, but may be prohibited as described in section 20, if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (a) the area occupied by any structures necessary for conducting education or research does not exceed 100 m2 for each parcel;

heading: Other permitted non-farm uses
paragraph: (b) the agricultural land is not used for a school within the meaning of the School Act.

heading: Section 20.1 (1) (a) and (b) of Act applies
paragraph: 28		  A person who engages in a residential use that is permitted under this Part is not relieved from complying with section 20.1 (1) (a) or (b) of the Act, except as provided under Division 2 [Additional Residences] of this regulation.

heading: Prescribed residential structures
paragraph:
29
		  (1) A structure used, whether permanently or temporarily, to provide or in connection with providing accommodation as described in this Part is prescribed as a residential structure for the purposes of the Act.

heading: Prescribed residential structures
paragraph: (2) A vehicle used, whether permanently or temporarily, to provide or in connection with providing accommodation as described in this Part is prescribed as a residential structure for the purposes of this Part.

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph:
30
		  Subject to any limits and conditions set out in this Part, the use of agricultural land to construct, maintain or operate any of the following is permitted:

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (a) a structure, other than a residential structure, that is necessary for a residential use permitted under this Part;

heading: Necessary structures and ancillary services
paragraph: (b) a driveway or utility necessary for a residential use permitted under this Part.

heading: Secondary suites
paragraph:
31
		  The use of agricultural land for a secondary suite is permitted if there is one suite only, located in the principal residence.

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph:
33
		  (1) In this section, "sleeping unit" means the following:

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph: (a) a bedroom or other area used for sleeping located in a residence, cabin or other structure;

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph: (b) a vehicle, trailer, tent or other structure located on a campsite, field or other area.

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for providing accommodation in relation to an agri-tourism activity is permitted if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph: (a) the accommodation is located on agricultural land that is classified as a farm under the Assessment Act;

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph: (b) the total developed area for structures, landscaping and access for the accommodation is less than 5% of any parcel;

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph: (c) the accommodation is limited to 10 sleeping units in total, including bedrooms under section 34 [tourist accommodation];

heading: Agri-tourism accommodation
paragraph: (d) accommodation is provided on a seasonal or short-term basis only.

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: 34		  (1) In this section, "bedroom" means a bedroom or other area used for sleeping in a residence.

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (2) The use of agricultural land for providing accommodation for tourists is permitted in a principal residence that is not a pre-existing residential structure if both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (a) the accommodation is limited to 4 bedrooms in total;

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (b) accommodation is provided on a short-term basis only.

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (3) The use of agricultural land for providing accommodation for tourists is permitted in a principal residence that is a pre-existing residential structure if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (a) on the date this section comes into force, the number of bedrooms complies with section 3 (1) (d) of the Agricultural Land Reserve Use, Subdivision and Procedure Regulation, as it read immediately before this section came into force;

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (b) the number of bedrooms is not changed after the date this section comes into force unless

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (i)  permitted under section 25 or 45 of the Act, or

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (ii)  the number of bedrooms is not increased by the change;

heading: Tourist accommodation
paragraph: (c) accommodation is provided on a short-term basis only.

heading: Pre-existing residential structures constructed before February 22, 2019
paragraph:
34.1
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for an additional residence that is a pre-existing residential structure is permitted if

heading: Pre-existing residential structures constructed before February 22, 2019
paragraph: (a) the residence is constructed in accordance with all applicable enactments, and

heading: Pre-existing residential structures constructed before February 22, 2019
paragraph: (b) on February 22, 2019, the size, siting and use of the residence complied with section 3 (1) (b) (ii) or (b.1) (ii) or (iii) of the Agricultural Land Reserve Use, Subdivision and Procedure Regulation, B.C. Reg. 171/2002, as it read on February 21, 2019.

heading: Pre-existing residential structures constructed before February 22, 2019
paragraph: (2) The size and siting of a residence permitted under this section must not be altered unless one of the following applies:

heading: Pre-existing residential structures constructed before February 22, 2019
paragraph: (a) the alteration is permitted under section 25 or 45 of the Act;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures constructed before February 22, 2019
paragraph: (b) in the case of a manufactured home, the alteration does not increase the size of the manufactured home;

heading: Pre-existing residential structures constructed before February 22, 2019
paragraph: (c) in the case of residence that is not a manufactured home, the alteration does not increase the total area occupied by all residences and other residential structures, roads and service lines, and all agricultural land between them.

heading: Manufactured homes constructed between July 4, 2019 and December 31, 2021
paragraph:
34.2
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for an additional residence that is a manufactured home and that is not a pre-existing residential structure is permitted if

heading: Manufactured homes constructed between July 4, 2019 and December 31, 2021
paragraph: (a) the residence is constructed in accordance with all applicable enactments, and

heading: Manufactured homes constructed between July 4, 2019 and December 31, 2021
paragraph: (b) on December 31, 2021, all conditions with respect to the residence imposed under section 32 (3), as it read on December 30, 2021, were met.

heading: Manufactured homes constructed between July 4, 2019 and December 31, 2021
paragraph: (2) The size and siting of a residence permitted under this section must not be altered unless permitted under section 25 or 45 of the Act.

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph:
34.3
		  (1) The use of agricultural land for an additional residence for which construction begins after December 30, 2021 is permitted on a parcel if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (a) at the time that construction begins, the parcel has located on it only one residence, whether or not a secondary suite is located in the residence as permitted under section 31;

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (b) neither residence will be attached to, nor be part of, the other residence;

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (c) one of the following applies to the residences, as constructed:

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (i)  if the parcel is 40 ha or less, there will be

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (A) one residence, the total floor area of which is 500 m2 or less, and

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (B) one residence, the total floor area of which is 90 m2 or less;

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (ii)  if the parcel is more than 40 ha, there will be

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (A) one residence, the total floor area of which is any size permitted under the Act, and

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (B) one residence, the total floor area of which is 186 m2 or less.

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (2) The size of a residence permitted under this section must not be altered unless one of the following applies:

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (a) the alteration is permitted under section 25 or 45 of the Act;

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (b) the alteration does not increase the size of the residence beyond the size permitted under subsection (1) (c).

heading: Additional residences constructed after December 30, 2021
paragraph: (3) Nothing in this section prevents the granting of permission, under section 25 or 45 of the Act, for additional residences to be constructed after the additional residence permitted under this section.

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph:
35
		  Subject to section 36 [prohibited fill], the removal of soil from, or the placement of fill on, agricultural land for one or more of the following purposes is permitted if all applicable conditions are met:

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (a) constructing or maintaining a structure for farm use or for a principal residence if both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (i)  the total area from which soil is removed or on which fill is placed is 1 000 m2 or less;

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (ii)  if the area from which the soil is removed or on which the fill is placed is in a floodplain, the resulting elevation level is consistent with the minimum elevation level established under all applicable local government enactments and first nation government laws, if any, respecting flood protection in the floodplain;

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (b) constructing or maintaining berms for producing cranberries, if any fill placed on the area is

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (i)  no higher than 2 m above the natural grade, and

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (ii)  no wider than 10 m at the base;

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (c) constructing or maintaining flood protection dikes, drainage, irrigation and livestock watering works for farm use, if the total annual volume of soil removed or fill placed is 320 m3/16 ha or less;

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (d) maintaining an existing farm road, if the total annual volume of soil removed or fill placed is equal to or less than the ratio of 50 m3 of soil or fill to 100 m of existing road length;

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (e) using clean sand as a top-dress for berry production, if the total annual volume of soil removed or fill placed is 100 m3/ha or less;

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (f) applying soil amendments, if incorporated into the soil to a depth of 30 cm or less;

heading: Permitted soil or fill uses
paragraph: (g) conducting soil research and testing, if the soil removed or fill placed is limited to the amount necessary for the research or testing.

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph:
36
		  (1) Except as permitted under subsection (2), the following must not be used as fill on agricultural land:

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (a) construction or demolition waste, including masonry rubble, concrete, cement, rebar, drywall and wood waste;

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (b) asphalt;

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (c) glass;

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (d) synthetic polymers;

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (e) treated wood;

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (f) unchipped lumber.

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (2) Recycled concrete aggregate and recycled asphalt pavement may be used as fill on agricultural land for the purpose of maintaining an existing farm road as described in section 35 (d).

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), "recycled concrete aggregate" and "recycled asphalt pavement" mean concrete and asphalt that

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (a) have been recovered from a demolition process,

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (b) have been crushed to a particle size

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (i)  that may pass through a 1.905 cm screen, in the case of recycled concrete aggregate, or

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (ii)  of 1.905 cm3 or smaller, in the case of recycled asphalt pavement, and

heading: Prohibited fill
paragraph: (c) do not include, or are not combined with, metal, plastic, rubber, wood, glass, paper, organic materials or other contaminants.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Professional Governance Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "limited licence agrologist" means an individual who is registered with the regulatory body as a limited license agrologist in accordance with the bylaws of the regulatory body;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "practice of agrology", subject to subsection (2), means the provision of any of the following advice or services:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) advice or services that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  are based on agricultural or natural sciences or agricultural or resource economics, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  relate to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (A) cultivation, production, improvement, processing, marketing or management of aquatic or terrestrial plants or animals,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (B) classification, management, use, conservation, protection or enhancement of aquatic, terrestrial or atmospheric ecosystems that are affected by, sustain or have the potential to sustain the cultivation or production of aquatic or terrestrial plants or animals, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (C) restoration, reclamation or remediation of aquatic, terrestrial or atmospheric ecosystems;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) advice or services that are ancillary to those described in paragraph (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protective purposes" means the safety, health and welfare of the public, including the protection of the environment and the promotion of health and safety in the workplace.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) The practice of agrology does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the provision of advice or services within the reserved practice of a registrant of another regulatory body, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a normal farm practice, as defined in the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act, by a person on the person's land.

heading: Regulated practice
paragraph: 2		  For the purposes of the definition of "regulated practice" in section 2 [definitions in respect of the British Columbia Institute of Agrologists] of Schedule 1 of the Act, the practice of agrology is prescribed.

heading: Reserved title
paragraph:
3
		  For the purposes of section 51 (1) (a) [reserved titles] of the Act, the following titles are reserved for exclusive use by registrants:

heading: Reserved title
paragraph: (a) "professional agrologist";

heading: Reserved title
paragraph: (b) "articling agrologist";

heading: Reserved title
paragraph: (c) "technical agrologist";

heading: Reserved title
paragraph: (d) "articling technical agrologist";

heading: Reserved title
paragraph: (e) "limited licence agrologist".

heading: Reserved practice
paragraph:
4
		  (1) For the purposes of section 51 (1) (b) [reserved practice] of the Act, the practice of agrology described in paragraph (a) (ii) of the definition of "practice of agrology" in section 1 (1) of this regulation is a reserved practice that may only be carried out by or under the supervision of a registrant, if the practice relates to providing advice or another service that, having regard to the protective purposes, requires the experience or technical knowledge of an agrologist or limited licence agrologist.

heading: Reserved practice
paragraph: (2) In the case of advice or services described in paragraph (a) (ii) (C) of the definition of "practice of agrology", the reserved practice is limited to the advice or services relating to the state or quality of soil, water or air, for an agrology purpose.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "Act" means the Wildlife Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "annual angling licence" means an angling licence issued for a term of not more than 12 months ending March 31;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "Class I water" means one of the classified waters listed under the heading Class I Coastal Waters (anadromous) or Class I Inland Waters (non-anadromous) in Schedule A;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "Class II water" means one of the classified waters listed under the heading Class II Coastal Waters (anadromous) or Class II Inland Waters (non-anadromous) in Schedule A;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "classified water" means a water or group of waters that is an item in column 1 of Schedule A;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "classified waters angling licence" means an angling licence, issued under section 2.01, that permits angling in a classified water;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "conservation surcharge" means a surcharge assessed for the purposes of Part 3 of the Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "guided classified water angler" means a person who, in respect of a classified water, is a client of an angling guide who is authorized under the Act to guide for fish on the classified water;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "licence year" means a period of 12 months beginning on April 1 in each year and ending on March 31 in the following year;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "management plan" means a plan for managing guiding for fish and angling referred to in section 52 (3) of the Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "non-guided non-resident" means a non-resident who is not a guided classified water angler, but does not include a non-guided non-resident alien;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "non-guided non-resident alien" means a non-resident alien who is not a guided classified water angler;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "Shuswap Lake" means the waters of Mara Lake and Shuswap Lake including Seymour, Anstey and Salmon arms, Little Shuswap Lake, and that portion of South Thompson River (Little River) between Shuswap Lake and Little Shuswap Lake.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) A classified water may be referred to in this regulation or on a classified waters angling licence by the term, if any, set out in brackets following the description of the classified water in column 1 of Schedule A.

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: 2		  For the purposes of section 12 (a) (ii) of the Act, a person must be the holder of an angling licence bearing a conservation surcharge stamp affixed to the licence that permits angling in relation to that affixed stamp, and pay the applicable fee and conservation surcharge set out in Schedule C, as follows:

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (a) for waters not listed in Schedule A, a conservation surcharge stamp affixed to the front of an angling licence in the box labelled "Steelhead" permits angling for or retaining steelhead in those unclassified waters;

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (a.1) for classified waters listed in column 1 of Schedule A, a conservation surcharge stamp affixed to the front of an angling licence, in the box labelled "Steelhead",

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (i)  is required for angling in those classified waters during the period set out opposite in column 5, and

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (ii)  permits angling for or retaining steelhead in those classified waters;

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (b) a conservation surcharge stamp affixed to the front of an angling licence in the box labelled "Kootenay Rainbow Trout" permits the retention of up to 5 rainbow trout that measure more than 50 cm from the tip of the nose to the fork of the tail that are caught in Kootenay Lake east of a line between fishing boundary signs on opposite shores at Balfour Point and Proctor Lighthouse;

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (c) a conservation surcharge stamp affixed to the front of an angling licence in the box labelled "Non-tidal Salmon" permits the retention of salmon that are caught in non-tidal waters of the Province, including not more than 10 adult chinook salmon;

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (e) a conservation surcharge stamp affixed to the front of an angling licence in the box labelled "Shuswap Rainbow Trout" permits the retention of up to 5 rainbow trout that measure more than 50 cm from the tip of the nose to the fork in the tail that are caught in Shuswap Lake;

heading: Conservation surcharge stamps
paragraph: (f) a conservation surcharge stamp affixed to the front of an angling licence in the box labelled "Shuswap Char" permits the retention of up to 5 char that measure more than 60 cm from the tip of the nose to the fork in the tail that are caught in Shuswap Lake.

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph:
2.001
		  (1) For the purpose of section 12 (a) of the Act, in order to angle for white sturgeon in waters open to such angling, a person must be the holder of both

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph: (a) a basic angling licence, and

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph: (b) a white sturgeon conservation licence,

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph: and have paid the applicable fee and conservation surcharges set out in Schedule C.

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph: (2) The white sturgeon conservation licence referred to in subsection (1) permits a resident, non-resident or non-resident alien angler, who possesses a basic angling licence for the same period, to angle for white sturgeon on an annual, 8-day, or one-day basis, depending on the conservation surcharges paid and the date or dates listed on the licence at the time of purchase, as follows:

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph: (a) an annual licence is valid from April 1 or the date of purchase (whichever is later) through March 31;

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph: (b) an 8-day licence is valid only on the period of 8 consecutive days listed on the licence;

heading: White sturgeon conservation licence
paragraph: (c) a one-day licence is valid only from 12:00 a.m. to 11:59 p.m. on the date specified on the licence.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph:
2.01
		  (1) Subject to subsections (9) and (10) of this section and sections 4, 4.1 and 18, for the purpose of section 12 (a) of the Act, a person who angles in a classified water during a period specified in column 4 of Schedule A for the classified water must be the holder of both

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (a) a basic angling licence, and

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (b) a classified waters angling licence that permits angling in that classified water at the time the angling takes place.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (2) A classified waters angling licence permits a resident to angle in all classified waters during the term of the licence.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (3) A classified waters angling licence permits a non-resident or a non-resident alien to angle only

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (a) in a classified water specified on the licence, and

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (b) on a date that is specified on the licence at the time the licence is issued.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3) and subject to subsection (5), a non-guided non-resident alien must not angle in a classified water or part of a classified water that is an item in column 1 of Schedule A.1 during the day or days of the week or the period of time specified in column 2 of Schedule A.1 for the water.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (5) The prohibition in subsection (4) applies only during the period specified in column 3 of Schedule A.1 for the water.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (6) Subject to section 2.02, a classified waters angling licence may be issued to a person who pays the applicable fee and conservation surcharge set out in Schedule C.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (8) A classified waters angling licence issued to a non-resident or a non-resident alien is invalid if it specifies a period that is longer than 8 consecutive days.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (9) An angling guide, or an assistant angling guide employed by the angling guide, need not be the holder of a classified waters angling licence while guiding for fish a client of the angling guide on a classified water.

heading: Classified waters angling licence
paragraph: (10) A person who angles on the Atnarko River/Bella Coola River classified water is not required to be the holder of a classified waters angling licence.

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph:
2.02
		  (1) The director may establish one or both of the following for a classified water for a calendar year:

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (a) the maximum number of classified waters angling licences or angler days to be allocated to non-guided non-residents;

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (b) the maximum number of classified waters angling licences or angler days to be allocated to non-guided non-resident aliens.

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (2) In making a decision under subsection (1), the director must have regard to the management plan for the classified water.

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (3) Upon setting a maximum number of classified waters angling licences or angler days for non-guided non-residents or non-guided non-resident aliens under subsection (1), the director must specify whether the licences or days will be allocated by a lottery or a booking system.

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (4) If the director decides to allocate licences or days by a lottery, the director must inform applicants about the lottery to be conducted as follows:

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (a) before the lottery takes place, by means of a press release or other publication, giving

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (i)  the time and place of the lottery,

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (ii)  the manner of making an application, and

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (iii)  other relevant information about the conduct of the lottery;

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (b) after the lottery, by giving

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (i)  the results of the lottery, and

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (ii)  the names of the officials of the ministry who were present and conducting the lottery.

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (5) If the director decides to allocate licences or days by a booking system, the licences or days must be allocated in the order in which the director receives completed applications.

heading: Allocating classified waters angling licences to non-guided non-residents and non-guided non-resident aliens
paragraph: (6) The director may delegate the director's powers and duties under this section to another person.

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph:
3
		  (1) For the purpose of section 1 of the Act and regulations under the Act, "guide for fish" does not include a class of persons who operate

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (a) an aircraft or motor vehicle used for commercial purposes

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (i)  on a government regulated schedule,

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  between a commercial fishing camp, lodge or resort and any other place which is not an angling site,

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (iii)  to transport persons travelling primarily for a non-recreational purpose, or

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (iv)  to transport anglers to or from an angling site where such transportation is not a significant part of their transportation business and this transportation is not promoted by any person as a service to anglers,

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (b) a fishing school

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (i)  on waters for a period of less than 8 days in a calendar year,

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  considered by the regional manager not to be in conflict with the management plan for the waters, and

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (iii)  for which a permit is issued under subsection (3).

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (a) (iv) does not apply to a person who transports an angler to 2 or more angling sites during a 24 hour period.

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (3) A regional manager may issue a permit for the operation of a fishing school on waters in the region to a person who

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (a) is associated with a recognized educational institution, or

heading: Angling guide exemptions
paragraph: (b) derives part of the person's income from work related to angling.

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph:
4
		  For the purpose of section 12 of the Act, a person is exempt who

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph: (a) angles in waters on premises operated under a licence or permit for breeding, holding or rearing fish under this Act or the Fisheries Act,

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph: (b) is a resident under 16 years of age,

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph: (c) is under 16 years of age, not a resident and is accompanied by a person 16 years or older who holds an angling licence and other licences required by regulation, and fish caught and kept by the younger person are included as part of the daily catch and possession limit of that older person, or

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph: (e) angles in any of the following waters while holding a sport fishing licence under the Yukon Territory Fishery Regulations (Canada):

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph: (i)  Bennett Lake;

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  Laidlaw Lake;

heading: Angler exemptions
paragraph: (iii)  Morley Lake;

paragraph: 4.1		  (1) An individual who is ordinarily resident in Canada is exempt from section 12 of the Act during the weekend in June in which Father's Day occurs, and the Friday immediately preceding that weekend, while angling in non-tidal water that is not a classified water.

heading: Family fishing exemption
paragraph: (2) The exemption of an individual under subsection (1) is on condition that the individual not retain fish caught while exempt of a species for which a conservation surcharge stamp is required for retention.

5

6

heading: Waters reserved for young or disabled anglers
paragraph:
6.1
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Waters reserved for young or disabled anglers
paragraph: "authorized angler" means a person who is

heading: Waters reserved for young or disabled anglers

heading: Waters reserved for young or disabled anglers
paragraph: (b) a disabled resident;

heading: Waters reserved for young or disabled anglers
paragraph: "companion" means a person, other than an authorized angler, who accompanies and attends an authorized angler.

heading: Waters reserved for young or disabled anglers

heading: Qualifications for an angling guide licence
paragraph:
9
		  (1) A person who is an angling guide must have public liability insurance, in an amount of not less than $2 million, that is

heading: Qualifications for an angling guide licence
paragraph: (a) applicable to the person's angling guide business, and

heading: Qualifications for an angling guide licence
paragraph: (b) in effect during the period for which the angling guide will operate.

heading: Qualifications for an angling guide licence
paragraph: (2) A person under 19 years of age is not eligible for an angling guide licence.

heading: Qualifications for an angling guide licence
paragraph: (3) An applicant for an angling guide licence or assistant angling guide licence is required to satisfy the regional manager that, with respect to angling in the region where the applicant intends to guide for fish, the applicant has a working knowledge of the Act and regulations and the Fisheries Act (Canada) and its regulations.

heading: Application for an angling guide licence
paragraph: 10		  (1) For each region of the Province in which an applicant for an angling guide licence proposes to guide for fish, the applicant must complete and submit an application in a manner satisfactory to the regional manager

heading: Application for an angling guide licence
paragraph: (a) by May 31 where the waters and terms and conditions covered by the application are the same as those in the licence for the preceding year, or

heading: Application for an angling guide licence
paragraph: (b) by January 15 where paragraph (a) does not apply.

heading: Application for an angling guide licence
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), the regional manager may consider applications submitted after the dates specified in subsection (1) (a) or (b) where the operating plan of the applicant is consistent with the management practices of the water or area and a $50 payment is received to help defray the cost of processing the late application.

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph:
11
		  (1) Subsections (1.1) to (2) apply with respect to angler day quota for classified waters.

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (1.1) Subject to subsection (1.2), a regional manager may allocate angler day quota to an angling guide by issuing a certificate to the angling guide only if

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (a) a management plan applies to the classified water for which angler day quota is to be issued,

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (b) the allocation is in accordance with

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (i)  the management plan, and

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (ii)  the requirements of this section, and

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (c) the period for which the angler day quota is allocated is 20 years or less.

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (1.2) A regional manager must use one of the following processes for allocating angler day quota for classified waters:

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (a) a process that requires an angling guide to bid for angler day quota for one or more classified waters by sealed tender or auction;

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (b) a process that requires an angling guide to submit a written proposal for the use of angler day quota;

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (c) a process that requires an angling guide to submit a sealed tender referred to in paragraph (a), together with a written proposal, as referred to in paragraph (b).

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (2) A regional manager may renew or extend the period for which angler day quota is allocated to an angling guide, if

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (a) the angling guide submits to the regional manager an application, in the form required by the regional manager, for renewal of the angler day quota, and

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (b) at least 1/2 of the term of the existing angler day quota has elapsed.

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (3) A regional manager must not, in respect of a classified water for which the regional manager is responsible,

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (a) issue angling guide licences for the licence year in excess of the number specified in column 2 of Schedule A for the classified water, or

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (b) allocate total angler day quota for a period specified in column 4 of Schedule A for the classified water in excess of the number of days specified for that period in column 3 of Schedule A.

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (4) A regional manager may exempt a class of angler from the application of subsection (3) (b) in respect of a water in a region specified by the regional manager in the exemption.

heading: Allocation of angler day quota
paragraph: (5) The regional manager may allocate angler day quota for the Bulkley River additional guiding zone classified water only to a single person who is the holder of an angling guide licence for the Bulkley River classified water.

heading: Adjustments to allocated angler day quota
paragraph:
11.1
		  If a number specified in column 3 of Schedule A for a classified water is revised downward so that the number of angler days in the existing total allocation of angler day quota in a period specified in column 4 of Schedule A for the classified water exceeds the maximum allowable specified in column 3 of Schedule A for that period, the regional manager who is responsible for the classified water must adjust the allocation of angler day quota

heading: Adjustments to allocated angler day quota
paragraph: (a) by any method agreed upon by the regional manager and all of the affected angling guides, or

heading: Adjustments to allocated angler day quota
paragraph: (b) by applying the following:

heading: Adjustments to allocated angler day quota
paragraph: (i)  first, by reducing any unused angler day quota that is part of an existing allocation;

heading: Adjustments to allocated angler day quota
paragraph: (ii)  secondly, if needed, by subtracting the remaining excess angler days from each angling guide according to the percentage of angler days each angling guide retained after the adjustment under subparagraph (i).

heading: Cancellation, suspension or variation of angler day quota
paragraph:
11.2
		  Subject to section 11.3, a regional manager may cancel, suspend or vary angler day quota held by a person if the person

heading: Cancellation, suspension or variation of angler day quota
paragraph: (a) fails to use substantially all of the person's angler day quota, without reasonable excuse, or

heading: Cancellation, suspension or variation of angler day quota
paragraph: (b) contravenes the Act or this regulation.

heading: Hearing
paragraph:
11.3
		  (1) A regional manager may cancel, suspend or vary angler day quota under section 11.2 only after holding a hearing.

heading: Hearing
paragraph: (2) The regional manager must give reasonable notice of the time and place for the hearing to the person who holds the angler day quota that is to be considered at the hearing.

heading: Fees for angler day quota
paragraph:
11.4
		  (1) A person who holds angler day quota must pay annually, for each day of angler day quota held, the applicable fee and conservation surcharge set out in Schedule C.1.

heading: Fees for angler day quota
paragraph: (2) A person referred to in subsection (1) must pay

heading: Fees for angler day quota
paragraph: (a) 45% of the amount required under that subsection

heading: Fees for angler day quota
paragraph: (i)  on the date of application for an angling guide licence, if the person applies on or before May 30 for an angling guide licence for the first time or for an angling guide licence that has different terms and conditions from the immediately prior licence held by that person, or

heading: Fees for angler day quota
paragraph: (ii)  by May 31, in all other cases, and

heading: Fees for angler day quota
paragraph: (b) the remainder of the amount required by September 30.

heading: Angling guide fees
paragraph:
12
		  (1) The successful applicant for a licence to guide for fish must pay the applicable fee as follows:

heading: Angling guide fees
paragraph: (a) for an angling guide: $400 plus a conservation surcharge of $50;

heading: Angling guide fees
paragraph: (b) for an assistant angling guide: $130 plus a conservation surcharge of $20;

heading: Angling guide fees
paragraph: (c) for an increase in angler day quota through transfer from another angling guide: $300.

paragraph:
13
		  (1) The conditions of an angling guide licence are that the holder

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (b) report to the regional manager on or before the date specified in the licence,

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (i)  the number of resident, non-resident and non-resident alien angler days guided for fish,

paragraph: (ii)  the species, number and location of fish caught by each class of person the holder or the holder's assistant angling guides have guided for fish, and

paragraph: (d) use substantially all of the holder's angler day quota or have a reasonable excuse for failing to do so.

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (1.1) It is a condition of an angling guide licence that permits guiding for fish on a water that is an item in column 1 of Schedule C.2 that the angling guide must not, on any day during the period specified in column 2 of Schedule C.2 for that item, guide for fish on that water, or permit an assistant angling guide employed by the angling guide to guide for fish on that water,

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (a) a group that has more than 3 anglers, or

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (2) It is a condition of an angling guide licence and of an assistant angling guide licence that the angling guide or assistant angling guide not accompany or assist a non-resident or non-resident alien angling on classified waters unless

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (a) the non-resident or non-resident alien is included in the angler day quota of an angling guide, or

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (b) the holder of the licence has obtained the prior written approval of the regional manager to so accompany or assist.

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (3) If a regional manager issues an angling guide licence to an angling guide who holds angler day quota for a classified water, the regional manager may attach conditions to the angling guide licence in respect of the classified water that

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (a) limit

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (i)  the period of time during which,

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (iii)  the area in which

heading: Conditions of licence

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (b) limit the species for which the angling guide may guide for fish, and

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (c) require, in addition to the requirements of subsection (1) (b) (ii), that the angling guide report

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (i)  the size and sex of fish caught by the angling guide's guided classified water anglers, and

heading: Conditions of licence
paragraph: (ii)  the name and classified waters angling licence number of each guided classified water angler who has taken fish from the classified water.

heading: Requirement to report
paragraph:
13.1
		  Without limiting section 13 (1) (b), an angling guide who is authorized under the Act to guide for fish in a classified water must submit a report described in that section to the regional manager within 30 days after receiving a notice from the regional manager requesting the report.

heading: Sale of fish prohibited
paragraph:
14
		  (1) No person shall sell, barter or attempt to sell or barter fish caught by angling in the non-tidal waters of the Province.

heading: Sale of fish prohibited
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who is the operator of premises licensed under the Fisheries Act to culture fish if it is those fish that are to be sold or bartered.

heading: Fish roe
paragraph: 15		  (1) No person shall possess salmon roe or trout roe in an amount greater than 1 kg unless

heading: Fish roe
paragraph: (a) the roe was obtained from a commercial source that lawfully obtained that roe, or

heading: Fish roe
paragraph: (b) the person also has in the person's lawful possession fresh dressed salmon or trout, as the case may be, that was capable at the time it was caught of providing a quantity of roe exceeding 1 kg.

heading: Fish roe
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to roe a person possesses at the person's private residence or in circumstances to which the laws of the Province do not apply.

heading: Dressing or packing of fish

16

paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to the dressing or packing of fish

paragraph: (a) by a person at that person's private residence, or

heading: Dressing or packing of fish

heading: Catch record
paragraph:
17
		  A person who catches and retains any of the following fish shall immediately record, in ink, in the space provided on the back of the basic angling licence, the year, month, day and region in which the fish was caught:

heading: Catch record

heading: Catch record
paragraph: (b) a rainbow trout that measures more than 50 cm from the tip of the nose to the fork of the tail from Kootenay Lake east of a line between fishing boundary signs on opposite shores at Balfour Point and Proctor Lighthouse;

heading: Catch record
paragraph: (e) a rainbow trout that measures more than 50 cm from the tip of the nose to the fork in the tail from Shuswap Lake;

heading: Catch record
paragraph: (f) a char that measures more than 60 cm from the tip of the nose to the fork in the tail from Shuswap Lake.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "affected",

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to an animal, means an animal that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  is or is likely suffering from a notifiable or reportable disease, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  has been or has likely been exposed to a notifiable or reportable disease,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: regardless of whether the animal suffers, or exhibits any sign of suffering, any adverse effect from the notifiable or reportable disease, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to an animal product or byproduct, means an animal product or byproduct that came from, or may have come from, an animal referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "animal" means, subject to the regulations,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a species of the animal kingdom, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any organism prescribed as an animal;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "animal byproduct" means prescribed material, taken from the body of an animal, that is not intended to be used for human consumption;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "animal health" means the health of a population or subpopulation of animals, and includes the preservation of a population or subpopulation of animals that is at risk of being exposed to or affected by a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "animal product" means prescribed material, taken from the body of an animal, that is intended to be used for human consumption;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "animal product or byproduct" means an animal product, an animal byproduct or both, as applicable;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "chief veterinarian" means the person appointed under section 68 [chief veterinarian] as the chief veterinarian for British Columbia;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "contact information" means information sufficient to contact a person, including the person's home, business and email addresses, and telephone number;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "control zone" means the area described in an order made under section 36 [deemed control zones] or in a regulation made under section 94 [regulations respecting disease prevention and control];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "diagnostic examination" includes, for the purposes of determining the presence or identity of a notifiable or reportable disease,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) collecting bodily fluids and substances for examination,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) diagnostic imaging examinations,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) skin testing, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) physical examinations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environmental toxin" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a chemical, a toxic substance or another deleterious substance, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a thing that contains a chemical, a toxic substance or another deleterious substance;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "exposed" means to have been

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in contact with, or near, an animal or an animal product or byproduct affected by a notifiable or reportable disease, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in a place in which a notifiable or reportable disease is or is likely present,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: in such a manner as to be at risk of being affected by the notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "facility" includes a laboratory;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "infestation" means infestation by an organism;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "inspector" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the chief veterinarian, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person appointed or retained as an inspector under section 71 [appointment of inspectors], subject to any limits or conditions of the appointment or retainer;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "laboratory" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a veterinary diagnostic or research laboratory,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a medical or clinical diagnostic laboratory,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a medical research laboratory,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a laboratory that tests environmental samples, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a laboratory, or a laboratory within a class of laboratories, designated by order of the minister as a laboratory for the purposes of this Act and the regulations made under it;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licence" means a licence issued under section 11 [licences and permits];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "notifiable and reportable disease" or "notifiable or reportable disease" means a notifiable disease, a reportable disease or both, as applicable;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "notifiable disease" means an environmental toxin, infestation, syndrome or transmissible disease that is prescribed as a notifiable disease for the purpose of implementing monitoring measures

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) to determine its presence, identity, nature, effects or spread,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) to avoid barriers to trade, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) for other reasons in the public interest;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "operator" means a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) engages in a regulated activity, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) assists, directs, supervises or employs a person referred to in paragraph (a) for the purpose of engaging in the regulated activity;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permit" means a permit issued under section 11;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "person responsible", in relation to an animal or a thing, includes a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) owns the animal or thing,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has custody or control of the animal or thing, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is an operator in relation to the animal or thing;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "personal information" means recorded information about an identifiable individual;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "preventive measures" means preventive measures as described in section 5 (2) [preventive measures];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "private dwelling" means a place, or part of a place, used exclusively for residential purposes;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "quarantine zone" means the area described in an order made under section 27 [quarantine zone orders];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "registration" means a registration granted under section 12 [registrations];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regulated activity" means an activity that is prescribed as a regulated activity;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "reportable disease" means an environmental toxin, infestation, syndrome or transmissible disease that is prescribed as a reportable disease for the purpose of implementing preventive, control or eradication measures

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) to safeguard animal health,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) to safeguard public health in relation to environmental toxins, infestations, syndromes or transmissible diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) to avoid barriers to trade, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) for other reasons in the public interest;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "surveillance zone" means the area described in an order made under section 28 [surveillance zone orders];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "syndrome" means a condition that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is characterized by or associated with a group of signs, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has an adverse effect on animal health;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "traceability system" means a system designed to track the location or transport of one or more of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) animals;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) animal products or byproducts;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) prescribed things in relation to animals, or animal products or byproducts;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transmissible disease" means a disease that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is caused by an infectious agent or its toxic products, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) may be transmitted in any manner and at any distance through an animal, a person, a thing, the environment or any other means;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "vary", in relation to an order, a licence, a permit or a registration, includes to vary existing terms or conditions of, and to attach new terms or conditions to, the order, licence, permit or registration;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "vehicle" means a device, whether self-propelled or propelled by other means, designed to transport people, animals or things on, under or over land, including by rail, or in or on water, and includes machinery, equipment or an apparatus mounted on or attached to the device;
