heading: Definitions
paragraph: "veterinarian" means an individual who is authorized to practise veterinary medicine under the Veterinarians Act.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2		  (1) Unless a contrary intention is expressed, a reference in this Act or a regulation made under it to

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) a building or structure includes part of the building or structure, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) a place includes part of the place, any natural or artificial feature on or in the place and any building or structure located on the place.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Act and the regulations made under it, a condition, situation or thing is caused by a person or another thing if the person or other thing

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) contributes beyond a minimal extent to the happening or existence of the condition, situation or thing, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) directly or indirectly causes the condition, situation or thing.

heading: Must not cause disease
paragraph:
3
		  A person responsible for an animal must not, in keeping or dealing with animals or in engaging in a regulated activity, act in a manner that the person knows, or ought to know,

heading: Must not cause disease
paragraph: (a) may cause conditions that contribute to

heading: Must not cause disease
paragraph: (i)  the presence of a notifiable or reportable disease,

heading: Must not cause disease
paragraph: (ii)  the transmission or spread of a notifiable or reportable disease between animals, or

heading: Must not cause disease
paragraph: (iii)  the transmission of disease from animals to humans, or

heading: Must not cause disease
paragraph: (b) may interfere with the prevention, control or eradication of a notifiable or reportable disease.

heading: Duty to train and equip
paragraph:
4
		  (1) In this section, "employee" includes a person providing services, in relation to an animal,

heading: Duty to train and equip
paragraph: (a) under contract, or

heading: Duty to train and equip
paragraph: (b) under the direction or supervision of the person responsible for the animal, whether or not for a fee.

heading: Duty to train and equip
paragraph: (2) A person responsible for an animal must ensure that the person's employees are adequately trained and sufficiently equipped to

heading: Duty to train and equip
paragraph: (a) prevent, to the extent reasonably possible, the presence, transmission or spread of notifiable and reportable diseases, and

heading: Duty to train and equip
paragraph: (b) respond to notifiable and reportable diseases.

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A person responsible for an animal must

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (a) take prescribed preventive measures, and

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (b) take preventive measures consistent with reasonable and generally accepted practices of animal management.

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (2) Without limitation, preventive measures include the following:

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (a) administering a treatment, vaccination or medication;

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (b) washing with or applying a substance, or having a substance injected or inserted;

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (c) applying disinfection and decontamination measures;

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (d) using a type of equipment or implementing a process, or removing or altering equipment or processes;

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (e) any measure set out in the regulations;

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (f) any measure required by an inspector for the purpose of

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (i)  preventing notifiable or reportable diseases in animals,

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (ii)  preventing the transmission or spread of notifiable or reportable diseases between animals,

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (iii)  preventing the transmission of diseases from animals to humans, or

heading: Preventive measures
paragraph: (iv)  promoting animal health.

heading: Must comply with veterinary advice
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A person responsible for an animal who is informed by a veterinarian that the animal is or may be affected by a notifiable or reportable disease must comply with the instructions of the veterinarian, including instructions respecting diagnostic examinations and preventive measures.

heading: Must comply with veterinary advice
paragraph: (2) If, in the opinion of a veterinarian, a person who receives information under subsection (1) is not complying with instructions given under that subsection, the veterinarian must report the non-compliance to the chief veterinarian in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Must not keep or deal with affected animals
paragraph:
7
		  (1) Except with the permission and in accordance with the instructions of an inspector, a person must not keep or deal with, in British Columbia, an animal that

heading: Must not keep or deal with affected animals
paragraph: (a) was imported into British Columbia, and

heading: Must not keep or deal with affected animals
paragraph: (b) the person knows, or ought to know, is affected by a notifiable or reportable disease.

heading: Must not keep or deal with affected animals
paragraph: (2) An inspector may conduct an inspection under Division 1 [Inspections] of Part 4 for the purposes of subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Must not slaughter, destroy or dispose of affected or harmful things
paragraph:
8
		  A person must not slaughter, destroy or dispose of any of the following except with the permission and in accordance with the instructions of an inspector, or in accordance with the regulations:

heading: Must not slaughter, destroy or dispose of affected or harmful things
paragraph: (a) an animal or an animal product or byproduct the person knows to be, or has reason to believe may be, affected by a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Must not slaughter, destroy or dispose of affected or harmful things
paragraph: (b) an animal the person knows has been, or has reason to believe may have been, administered medication, if the medication's withdrawal period, as indicated on the medication's packaging, has not yet expired;

heading: Must not slaughter, destroy or dispose of affected or harmful things
paragraph: (c) an animal or an animal product or byproduct the person knows has been, or has reason to believe may have been, exposed to an environmental toxin that may be harmful to human health or the environment, regardless of whether the environmental toxin has been prescribed as a notifiable or reportable disease.

heading: Disease control orders
paragraph:
9
		  If a person has reason to believe that

heading: Disease control orders
paragraph: (a) the person is entering or is about to enter a quarantine zone, a surveillance zone or a control zone, or

heading: Disease control orders
paragraph: (b) an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing is subject to a quarantine zone order made under section 27 [quarantine zone orders],

heading: Disease control orders
paragraph: the person must comply with all applicable prohibitions, limits or requirements imposed under an order or a regulation that applies to the quarantine zone, surveillance zone, control zone, animal, animal product or byproduct, or thing.

heading: Duties of operators
paragraph:
10
		  (1) In this section, "employee" includes a person providing services, in relation to an animal or an animal product or byproduct,

heading: Duties of operators
paragraph: (a) under contract, or

heading: Duties of operators
paragraph: (b) under the direction or supervision of the person responsible for the animal or for the animal product or byproduct, whether or not for a fee.

heading: Duties of operators
paragraph: (2) An operator who engages in a regulated activity must comply with any requirement or duty set out in a regulation respecting the regulated activity.

heading: Duties of operators
paragraph: (3) An operator must ensure that the operator's employees are adequately trained and sufficiently equipped to comply with any requirement or duty set out in a regulation respecting a regulated activity in which the employees are engaged.

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph:
11
		  (1) If a person is required by regulation to have a licence or permit to engage in a regulated activity, the person may apply for the licence or permit by submitting to the chief veterinarian, in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian,

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (a) an application, and

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (b) the prescribed records and fees, if any.

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application for a licence or permit under subsection (1), the chief veterinarian may do one or more of the following:

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (a) request, in writing, from the applicant or from a person referred to by the applicant further information, samples, proof of a fact, records or any other thing necessary to evaluate the application;

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (b) conduct an inspection under Division 1 [Inspections] of Part 4;

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (c) refer the application for review and comment to a veterinarian, a public officer, an employee of a local government or a person having special expertise;

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (d) issue a temporary licence or permit with or without terms or conditions, valid for a period of no more than 3 months;

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (e) issue the licence or permit with or without terms or conditions;

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (f) reject the application, providing to the applicant, in writing, the reason for the rejection.

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (3) An operator who has a licence or permit may request a variation of the licence or permit by

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (a) submitting to the chief veterinarian

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (i)  an application in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian, and

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (ii)  the prescribed records and fees, if any, and

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (b) providing to the chief veterinarian information, samples, proof of a fact, records or any other thing necessary to evaluate the application.

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (4) On receiving an application under subsection (3), the chief veterinarian may do the following:

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (a) exercise any of the powers set out in subsection (2) (a) to (c) and (f);

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (b) vary the licence or permit.

heading: Licences and permits
paragraph: (5) A licence or permit is not transferable.

heading: Registrations
paragraph:
12
		  (1) If a person is required by regulation to be registered to engage in a regulated activity, the person may apply to register by submitting to the chief veterinarian, in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian,

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (a) registration information, and

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (b) the prescribed records and fees, if any.

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (2) On receiving a registration form under subsection (1) of this section, the chief veterinarian may do one or more of the following:

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (a) do anything under section 11 (2) (a), (b) or (c) [licences and permits] as if the registration were an application for a licence or permit;

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (b) grant the registration by issuing a producer number;

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (c) refuse to grant the registration, providing to the person, in writing,

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (i)  the reason for the refusal, and

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (ii)  if applicable, notice of the terms and conditions the person would need to meet for a registration to be granted.

heading: Registrations
paragraph: (3) A producer number issued under subsection (2) (b) is not transferable.

heading: Certification programs
paragraph:
13
		  If a certification program is prescribed for the purposes of a regulated activity,

heading: Certification programs
paragraph: (a) a person must not hold themselves out as being certified unless the person is certified in accordance with the regulations, and

heading: Certification programs
paragraph: (b) a person who is certified must meet all prescribed standards.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph:
14
		  (1) In this section, "administrative action" means

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (a) to suspend, cancel or vary an operator's licence or permit, or

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (b) to suspend or cancel an operator's registration.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (2) In addition to any other action that may be taken under this Act, the chief veterinarian may take an administrative action if the operator

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (a) has contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations made under it,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (b) has contravened an order made under this Act,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (c) has contravened a term or condition of the operator's licence or permit,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (d) is carrying out a regulated activity in a manner that may endanger

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans, or

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (e) has abandoned a regulated activity.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (3) Before taking an administrative action, the chief veterinarian must provide to the operator

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (a) a written notice stating

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (i)  the administrative action the chief veterinarian proposes to take,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (ii)  the reason for taking the proposed administrative action,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (iii)  the date the proposed administrative action is to take effect, and

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (iv)  the manner in which the operator may respond to the proposed administrative action, and

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (b) a reasonable opportunity to respond, in writing, to the proposed administrative action.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (4) After providing the operator with a reasonable opportunity to respond in accordance with the manner set out in the notice provided under subsection (3) (a), the chief veterinarian may do one or both of the following:

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (a) delay the date the administrative action is to take effect or suspend the administrative action, if satisfied that the delay or suspension would not be detrimental to

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (b) after considering the operator's response, if any, and any supporting records or written submissions of the operator,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (i)  take the proposed administrative action,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (ii)  take a different administrative action, or

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (iii)  rescind the notice and take no administrative action.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (5) The chief veterinarian must provide written reasons for a decision made under subsection (4) (b) (i) or (ii).

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph:
15
		  (1) In this section, "decision" means a decision of the chief veterinarian to

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (a) reject an application for a licence or permit, or an application to vary a licence or permit,

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (b) refuse to grant a registration,

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (c) issue a licence or permit subject to terms and conditions,

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (d) suspend, cancel or vary a licence or permit, or

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (e) suspend or cancel a registration.

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (2) On receiving notice of a decision, a person may request the chief veterinarian to reconsider the decision by submitting to the chief veterinarian, within 30 days after receiving the notice, a request in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian.

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (3) After considering a request for reconsideration, the chief veterinarian may take, as applicable, one or more of the actions described in section 11 (2) or (4) (b), 12 (2) or 14 (4).

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (4) The chief veterinarian must provide written reasons for an action taken under subsection (3) of this section, and a person may not request further reconsideration.

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: (5) If the chief veterinarian is unable or unavailable to reconsider a decision, a person acting for the chief veterinarian may act under this section in respect of the decision as if that person had made the decision.

heading: Protected information
paragraph:
16
		  (1) Except as permitted under section 17 [duty to keep information confidential] or 18 [personal information], a person described in section 17 (1) or 18 (1) must refuse to disclose the following:

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (a) information that would identify a person responsible for an animal or for an animal product or byproduct;

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (b) information that would identify an animal or an animal product or byproduct that is located at or in a specific place or on or in a specific vehicle;

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (c) information that would identify a specific place at which an animal or an animal product or byproduct is located;

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (d) information that would reveal that a notifiable or reportable disease is or may be present in a specific place or on or in a specific vehicle;

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (e) information that would reveal that an animal or an animal product or byproduct affected by a notifiable or reportable disease is

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (i)  located at or in a specific place or on or in a specific vehicle, or

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (ii)  owned, or in the custody or control of, an identifiable person or body, or that an identifiable person or body is an operator in relation to the animal or the animal product or byproduct;

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (f) information that is derived from a sample taken under this Act or that is submitted to the ministry of the minister or a laboratory identified in an order of the minister.

heading: Protected information
paragraph: (2) Despite the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, a person who would otherwise be required under that Act to disclose information described in subsection (1) of this section is not required to disclose the information except as required under section 25 of that Act.

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: 17		  (1) In this section, "person engaged in the administration of this Act" includes the following persons:

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (a) each employee and former employee of the ministry of the minister;

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (b) each inspector and former inspector;

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (c) any person engaged or previously engaged in the administration of this Act;

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (d) a person responsible for administering a laboratory identified for the purposes of section 16 (1) (f) [protected information];

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (e) each employee and former employee of a laboratory identified for the purposes of section 16 (1) (f).

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (2) A person engaged in the administration of this Act must keep confidential the information described in section 16 (1) that comes to the person's knowledge in the course of that person's employment or duties, and must not communicate any of those matters except as follows:

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (a) to administer this Act or another enactment or a program administered by the minister;

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (b) to make a report that the person is required to make under this Act;

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (c) to disclose, in accordance with the regulations, prescribed information contained in a traceability system;

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (d) to disclose prescribed information in respect of an order made under this Act;

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (e) to publish or disclose information that, in the opinion of the minister, must be published or disclosed in the public interest.

heading: Duty to keep information confidential
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, information may be disclosed outside British Columbia for the purposes of subsection (2) regardless of whether there is a threat to animal health or public health, or to an animal's health or a person's health, in British Columbia.

heading: Personal information
paragraph:
18
		  (1) A person may collect, use or disclose personal information under this Act for one or more of the purposes listed in subsection (2) if the person is one of the following:

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (a) an employee of the ministry of the minister;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (b) an inspector;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (c) currently engaged in the administration of this Act;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (d) responsible for administering a laboratory identified for the purposes of section 16 (1) (f) [protected information];

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (e) an employee of a laboratory identified for the purposes of section 16 (1) (f);

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (f) a prescribed person.

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (2) The purposes referred to in subsection (1) are as follows:

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (a) to identify a person who may have been exposed to an affected animal or an affected animal product or byproduct;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (b) to identify a person who was, is or is expected to be a person responsible for an affected animal or for an affected animal product or byproduct;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (c) to identify a person who is or may be engaged in a regulated activity;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (d) to determine the presence of, identify, prevent, control or eradicate a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (e) to notify a person or body responsible for animal health or public health, including public officers responsible for animal health or public health in other jurisdictions, that an order has been made under Division 2 [General Disease Control Orders] or 3 [Temporary Disease Control Orders] of Part 4, and of the contents of the order;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (f) to engage in animal health program planning, delivery, evaluation and monitoring, including

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (i)  compilation of statistical information, and

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (ii)  animal health surveillance;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (g) to conduct or facilitate research into animal health management and animal disease control;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (h) to assess and address threats to animal health;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (i) to assess and address threats to public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (j) to implement and maintain a traceability system;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (k) to monitor compliance with this Act and the regulations made under it;

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (l) without limiting any other purpose listed in this subsection, if necessary for the effective operation of a provision of this Act or a regulation made under it.

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, personal information may be disclosed outside British Columbia for the purposes of subsection (2) regardless of whether there is a threat to animal health or public health, or to an animal's health or a person's health, in British Columbia.

heading: Personal information
paragraph: (4) A person listed in subsection (1) must not collect, use or disclose personal information except as permitted under this Act or another enactment.

heading: Duty to keep records
paragraph:
19
		  A person responsible for an animal or for an animal product or byproduct, and a prescribed person, must

heading: Duty to keep records
paragraph: (a) keep, in accordance with the regulations, the prescribed records, and

heading: Duty to keep records
paragraph: (b) produce those records on the request of an inspector within the time requested.

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph:
20
		  (1) This section applies to each of the following persons who becomes aware of a matter referred to in subsection (2):

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (a) a person responsible for an animal or for an animal product or byproduct;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (b) an inspector, a veterinarian and a person responsible for administering a laboratory, acting in the course of the inspector's, the veterinarian's or the person's duties.

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (2) A person to whom this section applies must report, in accordance with subsection (3), the following matters:

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (a) that an animal is affected by or has been exposed to a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (b) that an animal has died, or may have died, as a result of a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (c) that an animal

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (i)  is exhibiting signs of illness that are unusual in nature, or

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (ii)  has died of an illness that is unusual in nature;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (d) that an animal product or byproduct

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (i)  is or may be affected by a notifiable or reportable disease, or

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (ii)  came from, or may have come from, an animal described in paragraph (c) of this subsection.

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (3) A person to whom this section applies must promptly report to the chief veterinarian the following information, to the extent of the person's knowledge:

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (a) the identity and contact information, if known, of a person responsible for the animal or for the animal product or byproduct;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (b) if the information described in paragraph (a) is unavailable, or if there is no person responsible for the animal or for the animal product or byproduct,

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (i)  the last known location of the animal or the animal product or byproduct, and

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (ii)  information that would assist in identifying the animal or the animal product or byproduct;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (c) the identity or nature of the notifiable or reportable disease, or illness, including any signs;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (d) if a diagnostic examination or other examination was done, the type of examination and the results;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (e) any preventive measures taken;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (f) any prescribed information;

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (g) any other relevant information requested by the chief veterinarian.

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (4) A person to whom this section applies must

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (a) make records and take samples as prescribed, and

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: (b) take other prescribed actions.

heading: Mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting
paragraph:
21
		  (1) The chief veterinarian may, on the chief veterinarian's own initiative or on receiving a report under this Division, order a person responsible for administering a laboratory, or another person, to perform a diagnostic examination and make a report of findings if the chief veterinarian reasonably believes it is necessary to do one or more of the following:

heading: Mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting
paragraph: (a) determine the identity or presence of a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting
paragraph: (b) monitor the incidence and nature of

heading: Mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting
paragraph: (i)  a notifiable or reportable disease, or

heading: Mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting
paragraph: (ii)  signs of illness that are unusual in nature;

heading: Mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting
paragraph: (c) control or eradicate a notifiable or reportable disease.

heading: Mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting
paragraph: (2) A person subject to an order under this section must comply with the order.

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph:
22
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: "traceability program" means a program established and maintained, or designated, under subsection (2) (b);

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: "traceable animal" means an animal that is subject to a traceability system;

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: "traceable item" means an animal product or byproduct, or a prescribed thing in relation to an animal product or byproduct, that is subject to a traceability system.

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (2) The minister may, for the purposes of this Act, establish and maintain, or designate, one or more of the following:

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (a) traceability systems;

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (b) programs that, in the opinion of the minister,

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (i)  facilitate the effectiveness of a traceability system, or

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (ii)  are an integral part of a traceability system.

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (3) A program may be designated under subsection (2) (b) whether

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (a) the program is established or maintained by a public or private body, including, without limitation, the government of another jurisdiction and a voluntary association, or

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (b) the traceability system to which the program relates, or is intended to relate, has not yet been established or designated.

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (4) A person who is responsible for a traceable animal or for a traceable item, or for a place, vehicle or thing that is subject to a traceability program, must do all of the following if and as required by a regulation made under section 96 (3):

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (a) obtain a unique identifier for the traceable animal, traceable item, place, vehicle or thing;

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (b) attach the identifier or notice of the identifier to the corresponding traceable animal, traceable item, place, vehicle or thing;

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (c) make records respecting the traceable animal, traceable item, place, vehicle or thing and, if applicable, take samples;

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (d) report to the minister or a prescribed person all prescribed information respecting

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (i)  the traceable animal, traceable item, place, vehicle or thing,

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (ii)  places, vehicles or things used in connection with a traceable animal or traceable item, even if those places, vehicles or things are not themselves subject to a traceability program, and

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (iii)  the transport or other movement of a traceable animal or traceable item, including the means of transport or movement and the destination;

heading: Traceability systems
paragraph: (e) take other prescribed actions.

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph:
23
		  (1) Subject to section 25 [entering to inspect] and subsection (2) of this section, an inspector may do one or more of the following:

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (a) stop a person who the inspector reasonably believes is a person responsible for an animal or for an animal product or byproduct;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (b) stop a vehicle if the inspector has reason to believe that an animal or an animal product or byproduct affected by a notifiable or reportable disease is present or has been kept in the vehicle;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (c) enter and inspect a vehicle or place if the inspector has reason to believe that an animal or an animal product or byproduct is present or has been kept in the vehicle or place.

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (2) An action may be taken under subsection (1) for one or more of the following purposes only:

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (a) if there is reason to believe that a notifiable or reportable disease may be present, to determine

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (i)  the presence of a notifiable or reportable disease, or

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (ii)  whether there is otherwise a significant risk to animal health, or to public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (b) if a report is made under section 20 [mandatory reporting] or 21 [mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting], to confirm the information provided in the report or to obtain further information;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (c) to determine whether

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (i)  a licence or permit should be issued, or a registration should be granted, or

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (ii)  a term or condition of a licence or permit, or of an order made under this Act, should be varied or rescinded;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (d) to monitor animal health within a quarantine zone, surveillance zone or control zone in relation to the notifiable or reportable disease for which the order or regulation establishing the zone was made;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (e) to monitor or confirm compliance with

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (i)  a provision of this Act or a regulation made under it,

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (ii)  an order made under this Act, or

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (iii)  a term or condition of a licence or permit;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (f) to determine whether an order made under this Act should be varied or terminated;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (g) if an inspector has the power to monitor or confirm compliance with a provision of another enactment, including an enactment of Canada, to monitor or confirm compliance with that provision;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (h) for any purpose for which an inspection by an inspector is expressly authorized under this or any other enactment, including an enactment of Canada;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (i) for a prescribed purpose.

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph:
24
		  (1) An inspector may do one or more of the following for the purposes of an inspection:

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (a) pass through a place to reach a vehicle or place that is to be the subject of an inspection;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (b) be accompanied or assisted by a person who has special, expert or professional knowledge of a matter relevant to the inspection;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (c) require a person to produce, including assembling animals and opening cages or containers, relevant records or things in the person's possession or control;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (d) inspect, copy or remove relevant records or things;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (e) make records in respect of a person, place or thing;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (f) require a person to stop engaging in an activity, or stop the operation of a thing;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (g) require a person whom the inspector reasonably believes to have relevant information to answer questions and otherwise provide that information;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (h) take samples and perform analyses and tests;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (i) conduct a post-mortem examination of an animal and, for this purpose,

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (i)  exhume a dead animal, and

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (ii)  transport or require the transport of the animal to the place where the post-mortem examination will be conducted;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (j) require that a place or thing not be altered or disturbed for a reasonable period of time;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (k) require a person to operate a thing, carry out a procedure or demonstrate a relevant skill, as directed by the inspector;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (l) attach to an animal or an animal product or byproduct an identifying mark or tag that permits identification of the animal or the animal product or byproduct as having been inspected;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (m) make an order that is necessary for the purpose of exercising a power of inspection, including ordering a person found in a vehicle or place under inspection to assist in the inspection.

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (2) If an inspector removes records or things under subsection (1) (d), the inspector must do both of the following:

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (a) provide a receipt for the records or things to the person from whom they were taken;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (b) subject to a power under this or any other enactment to order a thing destroyed, promptly return the records or things

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (i)  when the records or things have served the purposes for which the records or things were taken, or

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (ii)  if a proceeding is taken under this or any other enactment as a result of an inspection, and the records or things are relevant to the proceeding, no later than 3 months after the conclusion of the proceeding.

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph:
25
		  (1) An inspector may conduct an inspection at any reasonable hour.

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (2) Before entering a place, an inspector must

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (a) take reasonable steps to notify the owner or occupier of the place of the date and time that the inspector will be entering, and

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (b) if the place is a private dwelling, obtain either the consent of the owner or occupier or a warrant to enter.

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2) (a), an inspector may conduct an inspection without providing notice in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (a) the thing to be inspected is on display in a public place;

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (b) providing notice would not be reasonably possible or practicable in the circumstances;

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (c) in the case of a regulated activity, providing notice might frustrate the purposes of the inspection.

heading: Voluntary inspections
paragraph:
26
		  (1) A person responsible for an animal or for an animal product or byproduct, or for a thing related to an animal or an animal product or byproduct, may request an inspection of the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing.

heading: Voluntary inspections
paragraph: (2) A request under this section must be

heading: Voluntary inspections
paragraph: (a) made in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian, and

heading: Voluntary inspections
paragraph: (b) accompanied by payment of the prescribed fee, if any.

heading: Voluntary inspections
paragraph: (3) Section 23 (2) [when inspections may be made] does not apply to an inspection made under this section.

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph:
27
		  (1) If the chief veterinarian reasonably believes, based on the results of a diagnostic examination, that a reportable disease is present, the chief veterinarian may make an order establishing a quarantine zone on an area described in the order.

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (2) A quarantine zone order must describe

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (a) the reportable disease that gave rise to the order, and

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (b) the species of animal, the types of animal products or byproducts, or the types of things that are the subject of the order.

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (3) A quarantine zone order may include any terms and conditions the chief veterinarian considers necessary to minimize the risk of the reportable disease being transmitted or spread, including one or more of the following:

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (a) prohibiting, limiting or imposing requirements in respect of

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (i)  the movement of persons into, from or within the quarantine zone,

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (ii)  the possession of animals, animal products or byproducts, or things within the quarantine zone,

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (iii)  the transport of animals, animal products or byproducts, or things into, from or within the quarantine zone, and

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (iv)  dealing with quarantined animals, animal products or byproducts, or things;

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (b) requiring the isolation and segregation of quarantined animals;

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (c) requiring a person to take specific preventive measures within the quarantine zone or in respect of quarantined animals, animal products or byproducts, or things;

heading: Quarantine zone orders
paragraph: (d) requiring a person to make specified records and reports in respect of the quarantine zone or the location and condition of quarantined animals, animal products or byproducts, or things.

heading: Surveillance zone orders
paragraph:
28
		  (1) The chief veterinarian may make an order establishing a surveillance zone around a quarantine zone.

heading: Surveillance zone orders
paragraph: (2) A surveillance zone order must

heading: Surveillance zone orders
paragraph: (a) identify the quarantine zone order made under section 27 [quarantine zone orders] and the reportable disease to which the quarantine zone order relates, and

heading: Surveillance zone orders
paragraph: (b) describe the area of the surveillance zone.

heading: Surveillance zone orders
paragraph: (3) A surveillance zone order may include any terms and conditions the chief veterinarian considers necessary to do one or both of the following:

heading: Surveillance zone orders
paragraph: (a) monitor the surveillance zone for the presence of the reportable disease that is or is likely present within the quarantine zone, including requiring a person to make specified records and reports;

heading: Surveillance zone orders
paragraph: (b) prevent the transmission into the surveillance zone of the reportable disease that is or is likely present within the quarantine zone.

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph:
29
		  (1) An order may be made under section 30 [seizure orders] only if the chief veterinarian

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (a) reasonably believes that one or both of the circumstances referred to in subsection (2) of this section may exist,

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (b) reasonably believes that

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (i)  an operator has contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations or an order made under it, or a term or condition of the operator's licence or permit, and

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (ii)  a failure to comply with the provision, order, term or condition may result in a significant risk that an animal or an animal product or byproduct may become affected, or

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (c) reasonably believes that a former operator has abandoned an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing, and the animal, animal product or byproduct, or thing

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (i)  is an animal, animal product or byproduct, or thing described in subsection (2) of this section,

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (ii)  may endanger animal health, or

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (iii)  may endanger public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans.

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 30 (4), an order may be made under section 31 [slaughter or destruction orders] only if one or both of the following circumstances exist:

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (a) an animal or an animal product or byproduct is affected by a reportable disease;

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (b) a thing has been exposed to an animal or an animal product or byproduct affected by a reportable disease and the chief veterinarian reasonably believes that preventive measures would be inadequate to protect

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans.

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph:
30
		  (1) Subject to section 29 [reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction], the chief veterinarian may make an order to seize one or more of the following:

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (a) an animal;

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (b) an animal product or byproduct;

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (c) a thing in relation to an animal or an animal product or byproduct.

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (2) On making a seizure under this section, the chief veterinarian may

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (a) return the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing to a person responsible for it, with or without an order imposing conditions on the return, or

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (b) dispose of the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing, including by sale.

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (3) If an action is taken under subsection (2) (b),

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (a) each person responsible for the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing ceases to have any rights and interests in the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing, and

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (b) if the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing is disposed of to another person, all rights and interests in the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing vest in the person to whom it is disposed of.

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (4) If an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing was seized in the circumstances set out in section 29 (1) (c), a disposition under subsection (2) (b) of this section by slaughter or destruction may be made

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (a) regardless of whether either of the circumstances set out in section 29 (2) exists, and

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (b) without the need to make a further order under section 31 [slaughter or destruction orders].

heading: Seizure orders
paragraph: (5) Nothing in section 29 prevents a person who acquires an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing, disposed of under subsection (2) (b) of this section, from slaughtering or destroying the animal, animal product or byproduct, or thing, regardless of the reason for which the animal, animal product or byproduct, or thing was seized.

heading: Slaughter or destruction orders
paragraph:
31
		  Subject to section 29 [reason for seizure, slaughter or destruction], the chief veterinarian may order the slaughter of an animal, or the destruction of an animal product or byproduct, or a thing, and, for this purpose, may order that

heading: Slaughter or destruction orders
paragraph: (a) the slaughter or destruction be carried out by a specified person, or under the supervision or instructions of a specified person,

heading: Slaughter or destruction orders
paragraph: (b) the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing be transported to a specified place for the purpose of destruction, and

heading: Slaughter or destruction orders
paragraph: (c) the slaughter or destruction, and subsequent disposal, be carried out in accordance with specified procedures.

heading: General orders may be included
paragraph:
32
		  Despite section 39 [when general orders may be made], if the chief veterinarian considers it necessary or advisable for the purposes of an order made under this Division, the chief veterinarian may include in the order any order that may be made under section 40 [power to do anything reasonably necessary] or 41 [general orders].

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A person subject to an order made under this Division is responsible for all costs incurred to comply with the order and all costs or losses incurred as a result of the order, including, without limitation,

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph: (a) costs of keeping or transporting an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing,

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph: (b) costs of taking preventive measures,

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph: (c) costs of examination and sampling incurred to determine the presence or identity, or continued presence, of a reportable disease, and

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph: (d) market or other economic losses sustained

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph: (i)  while animals, animal products or byproducts, or things were the subject of the order, or

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph: (ii)  due to the slaughter of an animal or the destruction of an animal product or byproduct or a thing.

heading: Costs due to orders
paragraph: (2) Without limiting section 55 [recovery of costs], that section applies to costs incurred by an inspector as described in subsection (1) (a), (b) or (c) of this section.

heading: Compensation
paragraph:
34
		  (1) A person has no right of action as a result of an order made under this Division and must not commence or maintain proceedings

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (a) to claim damages or compensation of any kind from the government, or

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (b) to obtain a declaration that damages or compensation is payable by the government.

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph:
35
		  (1) This section applies if the minister reasonably believes that

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (a) either

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (i)  an environmental toxin, an infestation or a transmissible disease is present in an area, or

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (ii)  a significant number of animals within an area are exhibiting signs of illness that are unusual in nature, or have died of an illness that is unusual in nature,

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (b) the matter described in paragraph (a) may be a significant risk to

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans, and

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (c) the matter described in paragraph (a) is not an environmental toxin, infestation or transmissible disease, or evidence of a syndrome, that is prescribed as either a notifiable disease or a reportable disease.

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (2) In the circumstances set out in subsection (1), the minister may order that, for the purposes of one or more provisions of this Act or the regulations made under it,

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (a) the environmental toxin, infestation or transmissible disease is deemed, or

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (b) a condition that is characterized by or associated with a group of signs or an illness as described in subsection (1) (a) (ii) is deemed

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: as being prescribed as either a notifiable disease or a reportable disease.

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (3) If the minister makes an order under subsection (2),

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (a) the provisions identified in the order apply in respect of the matter described in subsection (1) (a) as if it were prescribed as either a notifiable disease or a reportable disease, as applicable, and

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (b) the minister may include in the order any prohibition, requirement, limit or condition necessary to

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (i)  determine the presence and identity of, and monitor, the deemed notifiable or reportable disease, and

heading: Deemed diseases
paragraph: (ii)  prevent, control or eradicate the deemed notifiable or reportable disease.

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph:
36
		  (1) If the minister reasonably believes that it is necessary for one or both of the following purposes, the minister may make an order deeming an area described in the order to be a temporary control zone:

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (a) preventing a notifiable or reportable disease from entering British Columbia;

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (b) establishing or protecting an area that is free of a notifiable or reportable disease that is present elsewhere in British Columbia.

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (2) A control zone order must describe

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (a) the notifiable or reportable disease that gave rise to the order, and

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (b) the species of animal, the types of animal products or byproducts, or the types of things that are the subject of the order.

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (3) A control zone order may include any terms and conditions the minister considers necessary for a purpose set out in subsection (1), including one or more of the following:

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (a) prohibiting, limiting or imposing requirements in respect of the movement of persons into or within the control zone;

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (b) prohibiting, limiting or imposing requirements in respect of the possession or transport of animals, animal products or byproducts, or things into or within the control zone;

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (c) requiring a person to take specific preventive measures within the control zone;

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (d) requiring a person to make specified records and reports in respect of

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (i)  the control zone, or

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (ii)  the condition of animals, or animal products or byproducts, within the control zone;

heading: Deemed control zones
paragraph: (e) requiring proof, in the form and manner satisfactory to the minister, that an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing is not affected by the notifiable or reportable disease that is the subject of the control zone.

heading: Publication of temporary orders
paragraph:
37
		  An order made under this Division

heading: Publication of temporary orders
paragraph: (a) must be published in the Gazette or in any other prescribed manner, and

heading: Publication of temporary orders
paragraph: (b) takes effect on the date it is made, regardless of when publication occurs.

heading: End of temporary orders
paragraph:
38
		  An order made under this Division ceases to have effect 42 days after it is made and must not be extended past that period.

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph:
39
		  (1) An inspector may make an order under this Division only if the inspector reasonably believes that

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (a) an animal is or may be affected by, or is at risk of being exposed to an animal affected by, a notifiable or reportable disease,

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (b) an animal product or byproduct is or may be affected by a notifiable or reportable disease,

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (c) a condition, a thing or an activity presents a significant risk of causing a threat to

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans, or

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (d) a person has contravened

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (i)  a provision of this Act, or a regulation or an order made under it, or

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (ii)  a term or condition of the person's licence or permit.

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, an inspector may make an order under this Division even if the person subject to the order is complying with all terms and conditions of a licence or permit issued under this or any other enactment.

heading: When general orders may be made
paragraph: (3) An order may be made based on a diagnostic examination, the circumstances or health history of an animal, or the history of an animal product or byproduct, even if the animal or the animal product or byproduct has been examined and the examination did not reveal the presence of a notifiable or reportable disease.

heading: Power to do anything reasonably necessary
paragraph:
40
		  If the circumstances described in section 39 [when general orders may be made] apply, an inspector may order a person to do anything that the inspector reasonably believes is necessary for one or more of the following purposes:

heading: Power to do anything reasonably necessary
paragraph: (a) to determine the presence of a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Power to do anything reasonably necessary
paragraph: (b) to identify, prevent, control or eradicate a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Power to do anything reasonably necessary
paragraph: (c) to bring the person into compliance with this Act or a regulation made under it, or a term or condition of that person's licence or permit.

heading: General orders
paragraph:
41
		  Without limiting section 40 [power to do anything reasonably necessary], an inspector may order a person to do one or more of the following:

heading: General orders
paragraph: (a) keep an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing in a specified place;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (b) prevent an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing from

heading: General orders
paragraph: (i)  being transported to or from a place,

heading: General orders
paragraph: (ii)  being unloaded from a vehicle, or

heading: General orders
paragraph: (iii)  entering a specified place;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (c) prevent persons or animals from being exposed to an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (d) provide to the inspector or a specified person information, records, samples or other things relevant to an animal's possible exposure to a notifiable or reportable disease, including information respecting

heading: General orders
paragraph: (i)  persons who and animals that may have been exposed to the animal,

heading: General orders
paragraph: (ii)  animal products or byproducts that may have come from the animal, and

heading: General orders
paragraph: (iii)  a thing that may have been used in relation to the animal;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (e) have an animal placed under the supervision or care of a specified person;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (f) have an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing examined by a specified person or under the supervision or instructions of a specified person, including

heading: General orders
paragraph: (i)  transporting the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing to a specified place for the purpose of examination, and

heading: General orders
paragraph: (ii)  having the animal, the animal product or byproduct, or the thing examined before a particular date or according to a schedule;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (g) take preventive measures, including

heading: General orders
paragraph: (i)  complying with preventive measures set out in the order, specified by a veterinarian or both, as applicable,

heading: General orders
paragraph: (ii)  transporting an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing to a specified place for the purpose of preventive measures, and

heading: General orders
paragraph: (iii)  beginning preventive measures before a particular date and continuing until a particular date or event;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (h) do specific work in respect of a place, including removing or altering things found in the place and altering or locking the place to restrict or prevent entry to the place;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (i) not deal with or dispose of an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing, or do so only in accordance with a specified procedure;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (j) stop operating, or not operate, a thing;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (k) to protect the health of animals or of persons who may be exposed to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans,

heading: General orders
paragraph: (i)  wear a type of clothing or personal protective equipment, or change, remove or alter clothing or personal protective equipment, or

heading: General orders
paragraph: (ii)  use a type of equipment or implement a process, or remove equipment or alter equipment or processes;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (l) attach an identifying mark or tag to an animal, an animal product or byproduct, or a thing;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (m) provide evidence of complying with the order, including

heading: General orders
paragraph: (i)  getting specified evidence of compliance from a veterinarian or specified person, and

heading: General orders
paragraph: (ii)  providing to an inspector any relevant record;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (n) make or keep a specific record;

heading: General orders
paragraph: (o) take a prescribed action.

heading: Application of this Division
paragraph:
42
		  This Division applies in respect of an order made under Division 2 [General Disease Control Orders] or 4 [General Orders] of this Part.

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph:
43
		  Any of the following persons may be the subject of an order:

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (a) a person responsible for an animal that is or may be affected by, or at risk of being exposed to an animal affected by, a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (b) a person responsible for an animal product or byproduct that is or may be affected by a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (c) a person who has custody or control of a condition, thing or activity that presents a significant risk of causing a threat to

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (d) a person who has contravened

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (i)  a provision of this Act or a regulation or an order made under it, or

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (ii)  a term or condition of the person's licence or permit;

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (e) the owner or occupier of a place where

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (i)  an animal, animal product or byproduct, condition, thing or activity described in paragraph (a), (b) or (c) is located, or

heading: Who may be the subject of an order
paragraph: (ii)  an activity is occurring that is not in compliance with this Act or a regulation or an order made under it, or a term or condition of a licence or permit.

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph:
44
		  (1) An order must be made in writing and describe all of the following:

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (a) who must comply with the order;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (b) what must be done or not done, and any conditions, including, if applicable, the date by which something must be done;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (c) the date on which, or the circumstances under which, the order is to terminate, if the date or circumstances are known;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (d) subject to the regulations, information sufficient to enable a person to contact the person who made the order;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (e) how the person subject to the order may have the order reconsidered;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (f) any prescribed matter.

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (2) Two or more orders may be combined in a single written notice.

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (3) An order may be made in respect of a class of persons or things.

heading: Instructions to another person
paragraph:
45
		  (1) If an inspector orders an animal or an animal product or byproduct to undergo a diagnostic examination, the inspector must include with the order an instruction to the examiner to provide a copy of the results of the examination to the person responsible for the animal or for the animal product or byproduct.

heading: Instructions to another person
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) may

heading: Instructions to another person
paragraph: (a) authorize the examiner to provide recommendations to the person subject to the order, and

heading: Instructions to another person
paragraph: (b) instruct the examiner to provide to the inspector

heading: Instructions to another person
paragraph: (i)  a copy of the results of the examination, and

heading: Instructions to another person
paragraph: (ii)  a report respecting the examiner's recommendations and the compliance, by the person subject to the order, with the examiner's recommendations.

heading: Instructions to another person
paragraph: (3) An examiner given instructions under subsection (2) (b) must comply with the instructions.

heading: Service of orders
paragraph:
46
		  An order must be served in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph:
47
		  (1) An inspector who makes an order may vary or terminate the order, at any time, on the inspector's own initiative.

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, a person subject to an order may request the inspector who made the order to

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (a) reassess the relevant circumstances,

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (b) assess the extent to which the order has been complied with, and

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (c) determine whether the order continues to be necessary to protect

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans.

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (3) A request under subsection (2) must be made in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian.

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (4) On receiving a request under subsection (2), the inspector who made the order may, based on the matters referred to in that subsection,

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (a) confirm or vary the order, or

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (b) terminate the order.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph:
48
		  (1) A person subject to an order made under this Part may request the person who made the order to reconsider the order if

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (a) the person subject to the order has additional relevant information that was not reasonably available at the time the order was made, and

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (b) less than 20 days has passed since the order was made.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (2) A request for reconsideration must be made in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (3) After considering a request for reconsideration, the inspector who made the order may do one or more of the following:

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (a) reject the request on the basis that the information submitted in support of the request is not relevant or was reasonably available at the time the order was made;

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (b) delay the date the order is to take effect or suspend the order, if satisfied that the delay or suspension would not be detrimental to

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (c) confirm, vary or rescind the order.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (4) The inspector who made the order must provide written reasons for a decision to reject the request under subsection (3) (a) or to confirm or vary the order under subsection (3) (c), and a person may not request further reconsideration.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (5) An order is not suspended during the period of reconsideration unless the inspector who made the order agrees, in writing, to suspend it.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of this section,

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (a) if a class of persons is subject to an order, a request for reconsideration may be made by one person on behalf of the class, and

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (b) if multiple orders are made in respect of a class of persons, or that address related matters or issues, the inspector who made the orders may reconsider the orders separately or together.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (7) If the inspector is unable or unavailable to reconsider an order the inspector made, a person designated by the chief veterinarian may act under this section in respect of the order as if the designated person had made the order.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph:
49
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person subject to an order made under section 40 [power to do anything reasonably necessary] or 41 [general orders] may request a review of the order under this section.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (2) This section does not apply to an order made under section 40 or 41 if the order is made in the circumstances described in section 32 [general orders may be included].

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (3) A request for a review may be made,

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (a) in the case of an order made by the chief veterinarian, to the minister, or

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (b) in the case of an order made by an inspector, to the chief veterinarian.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (4) A request for a review

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (a) must be made in the form and manner required by the chief veterinarian, and

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (b) may be made only if less than 20 days has passed since

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (i)  the order was made, if reconsideration is not available under section 48 (1) [reconsideration of orders], or

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (ii)  an action was taken under section 48 (3).

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (5) A review must be based on the record.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (6) After considering a request for a review, a reviewer may do one or more of the following:

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (a) delay the date the order is to take effect or suspend the order, if satisfied that the delay or suspension would not be detrimental to

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (b) confirm, vary or rescind the order;

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (c) refer the matter back to the person who made the order, with or without directions.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (7) A reviewer must provide written reasons for an action taken under subsection (6) (b) or (c), and a person may not request further review of an order.

heading: Termination of orders
paragraph:
50
		  An order ceases to have effect on the date or in the circumstances stated in the order, or if no date or circumstances are stated, as follows:

heading: Termination of orders
paragraph: (a) if an order is served by posting the order, or notice of the order, in or on a place, on the date the order or notice is removed from the place by the minister or the inspector who made the order, or by a person acting under the direction of either of them;

heading: Termination of orders
paragraph: (b) if an order is served by publishing the order, or notice of the order, on the date the inspector who made the order publishes a notice that the order has been terminated;

heading: Termination of orders
paragraph: (c) if an order is made under section 41 (m) [general orders], on the date the person subject to the order provides evidence of compliance as required by the order;

heading: Termination of orders
paragraph: (d) in any other case, on the date the inspector who made the order provides notice by any means to the person subject to the order that the order is terminated.

heading: Application of this Division
paragraph:
51
		  This Division applies in respect of an order made under this Part.

heading: Duty to comply with orders
paragraph:
52
		  A person named or described in an order must comply with the order.

heading: Postings and identification
paragraph:
53
		  (1) If the minister or an inspector, or a person acting under the direction of either of them, posts an order or a notice under this Act, a person other than the minister or an inspector, or a person acting under the direction of either of them, must not remove, deface or alter the posted order or notice.

heading: Postings and identification
paragraph: (2) If the minister or an inspector requires that an animal or an animal product or byproduct have an identifying mark or tag, a person other than the minister or an inspector, or a person acting with the permission of either of them, must not remove, deface or alter the identifying mark or tag.

heading: Entering to take action
paragraph:
54
		  (1) If an inspector believes that a person is inadequately complying with, or has inadequately complied with, an order, the inspector may take action to fulfill the requirements of the order, including authorizing a person to carry out work on behalf of the inspector.

heading: Entering to take action
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies whether or not the inspector was the person who made the order.

heading: Entering to take action
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), an inspector or a person acting on behalf of an inspector may enter on or into a place for the purpose of taking an action under subsection (1).

heading: Entering to take action
paragraph: (4) Section 25 [entering to inspect] applies to entry under subsection (3) of this section as if the inspector, or the person acting on behalf of the inspector, were conducting an inspection of the place.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph:
55
		  (1) If an inspector does work or contracts for work to be done under section 54 [entering to take action], the inspector may, by filing a certificate in the prescribed form in the Supreme Court, recover reasonable costs for the work from the person subject to the order in relation to which the work was done.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (2) A certificate must be filed within 2 years of the work being done.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (3) A certificate must be signed by the inspector or the chief veterinarian, and it must include all of the following information:

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (a) the details of the order referred to in subsection (1), including the date the order was made;

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (b) the total amount owing;

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (c) the name of the person subject to the order referred to in subsection (1);

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (d) the date, and the manner in which, the costs were incurred.

heading: Recovery of costs
