paragraph: (4) Subject to the regulations, a certificate has the same effect, and proceedings may be taken on it, as if the certificate were a judgment of the Supreme Court for the recovery of a debt in the amount stated against the person who was subject to the order referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (5) A certificate is

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (a) admissible in any proceedings to recover the certified debt without proof of the signature or official position of the person appearing to have signed the certificate, and

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (b) proof of the certified facts.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (6) A copy of the filed certificate must be served in the prescribed manner on the person who was subject to the order referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (7) A person who has been served with a copy of the filed certificate under subsection (6) may, within 30 days of being served, request the Supreme Court to review, in accordance with the regulations, the amount owing.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (8) After reviewing the amount owing, the Supreme Court may rescind or modify the certificate if satisfied that the amount owing is not reasonable.

heading: Warrants
paragraph:
56
		  (1) Without notice to any person, an inspector may apply, in the manner set out in the regulations, to a justice of the peace for an order under this section.

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (2) A justice of the peace may issue a warrant in the prescribed form authorizing an inspector, or a person acting on behalf of an inspector, to enter and search a place, including a private dwelling, and take any necessary action if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation that doing so is necessary for the purposes of

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (a) taking an action authorized under this Act, or

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (b) determining whether an action authorized under this Act should be taken.

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (3) If an inspector believes that it would be impracticable to appear personally before a justice of the peace to apply for a warrant under this section, the inspector may submit an information on oath by telephone or other means of telecommunication and, for this purpose, section 22 of the Offence Act applies.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: 57		  (1) Without notice to any person, an inspector may apply, in the manner set out in the regulations, to a judge of the Supreme Court for an order under this section.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (2) A judge of the Supreme Court may grant an injunction restraining a person from contravening, or requiring a person to comply with,

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (a) a provision of this Act or a regulation or an order made under it, or

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (b) a term or condition of the person's licence or permit,

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation that there has been or will be a contravention of this Act, the regulations, the order, the licence or the permit.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (3) A judge of the Supreme Court may order a person to do or refrain from doing those things the judge considers necessary if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation that the person is interfering with or obstructing, or will likely interfere with or obstruct, a person who is exercising powers or performing duties under this Act.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (4) A judge of the Supreme Court may grant an interim injunction or order until the outcome of an application commenced under this section.

heading: Emergency defined
paragraph:
58
		  In this Part, "emergency" means an emergency declared under section 59 [conditions to be met before this Part applies].

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph:
59
		  (1) The chief veterinarian may declare that an emergency exists in one or more areas of British Columbia if the chief veterinarian reasonably believes that at least 2 of the following criteria exist:

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (a) the presence, or suspected presence, of a reportable disease in the area could have a serious impact on

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (i)  animal health, or

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (ii)  public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (b) there is an immediate and significant risk of a reportable disease being transmitted into, or spread in, the area;

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (c) the incidence of a reportable disease in the area is unusual or unexpected;

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (d) there is a significant risk of travel or trade restrictions as a result of the presence, or suspected presence, of a reportable disease in the area.

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (2) If an emergency is declared, a person must not exercise powers under this Part unless the person reasonably believes that

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (a) the action is immediately necessary to address a matter referred to in subsection (1), and

heading: Conditions to be met before this Part applies
paragraph: (b) compliance with this Act, other than this Part, or a regulation made under this Act would hinder that person from acting in a manner that would avoid or mitigate an immediate and significant harm or loss that may reasonably result from a matter referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Part applies despite other enactments
paragraph:
60
		  During an emergency, this Part applies despite any provision of this or any other enactment, including,

heading: Part applies despite other enactments
paragraph: (a) in respect of the collection, use or disclosure of personal information, the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act and the Personal Information Protection Act, and

heading: Part applies despite other enactments
paragraph: (b) in respect of a specific person or thing, a provision that would impose a specific duty, limit or procedural requirement,

heading: Part applies despite other enactments
paragraph: to the extent there is any inconsistency or conflict with the provision or other enactment.

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: 61		  (1) An inspector may, in an emergency, do one or more of the following:

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (a) act in a shorter or longer time period than is otherwise required;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (b) not provide a notice that is otherwise required;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (c) do orally what must otherwise be done in writing;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (d) suspend or vary a licence, permit or registration, and do so without approval of the chief veterinarian or providing an opportunity to

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (i)  respond to the action under section 14 (3) (b) [taking administrative action], or

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (ii)  have the action reconsidered under section 15 [reconsideration];

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (e) specify in an order a facility that does not meet the standards or qualifications established under section 69 (g) [general powers of chief veterinarian], unless an order under that section states that the order applies in an emergency;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (f) omit from an order things that are otherwise required;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (g) serve an order in any manner;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (h) not reassess, reconsider or review an order under section 47 [variation and reassessment of orders], 48 [reconsideration of orders] or 49 [review of orders], as applicable;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (i) conduct an inspection at any time, with or without a warrant, including of a private dwelling;

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (j) collect, use or disclose information, including personal information,

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (i)  that could not otherwise be collected, used or disclosed, or

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (ii)  in a form or manner other than the form or manner required.

heading: General emergency powers
paragraph: (2) An order that may be made under this Part may be made in respect of a class of persons or things and may make different requirements for different persons or things, or classes of persons or things, or for different geographic areas.

heading: Emergency inspectors and veterinarians
paragraph:
62
		  Despite section 71 [appointment of inspectors] of this Act and section 46 of the Veterinarians Act, the chief veterinarian may, in an emergency, make an order designating a person to exercise the powers or perform the duties of an inspector or a veterinarian for the purposes of this Act, and that person may exercise a power or perform a duty of an inspector or a veterinarian under this Act in accordance with the terms of the designation for the period of the emergency.

heading: Emergency powers respecting reporting
paragraph: 63		  (1) The chief veterinarian may, in an emergency, order that any matter in relation to the reportable disease referred to in section 59 [conditions to be met before this Part applies] be reported under this section.

heading: Emergency powers respecting reporting
paragraph: (2) If an order is made under this section, a person required by the order to make a report must promptly report, to the extent of the person's knowledge, to an inspector the information required by the order.

heading: Emergency powers respecting reporting
paragraph: (3) If a person is required to make a report under this Act, the chief veterinarian may, in an emergency, order the person exempt from the requirement, or vary the requirement.

heading: Emergency powers to make regulations
paragraph:
64
		  The minister may, in an emergency, make regulations as follows:

heading: Emergency powers to make regulations
paragraph: (a) exempting a person, place or thing from a provision of this Act or the regulations made under it;

heading: Emergency powers to make regulations
paragraph: (b) modifying a requirement of this Act or the regulations made under it;

heading: Emergency powers to make regulations
paragraph: (c) authorizing the chief veterinarian to make an exemption or modify a requirement as described in paragraphs (a) and (b);

heading: Emergency powers to make regulations
paragraph: (d) applying or modifying a regulation made under section 97 (4) (b) or (c) [regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement] for the purposes of applications to the court.

heading: When authority to act under this Part ends
paragraph:
65
		  Unless otherwise expressed, the authority to act under this Part ends when the chief veterinarian provides notice that the emergency has passed.

heading: Duties when authority to act ends
paragraph:
66
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), if a person exercises a power under this Part, the person must, as soon as reasonably practicable after the person's authority ends under section 65 [when authority to act under this Part ends], take any reasonable action to do the following:

heading: Duties when authority to act ends
paragraph: (a) unless it would serve no reasonable purpose, do a thing that the person would otherwise have been required to do under this Act if this Part did not apply;

heading: Duties when authority to act ends
paragraph: (b) in the case of a power exercised in respect of a person under section 61 [general emergency powers], provide to the person written reasons for exercising the power;

heading: Duties when authority to act ends
paragraph: (c) rescind an order that was made under this Part and give notice of the rescission to persons subject to the order, or, if necessary to protect animal health or to protect public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans,

heading: Duties when authority to act ends
paragraph: (i)  reissue the order in accordance with sections 44 [contents of orders] and 46 [service of orders], and

heading: Duties when authority to act ends
paragraph: (ii)  provide to persons subject to the order the right to reconsideration, reassessment or review available under sections 15 [reconsideration], 47 [variation and reassessment of orders], 48 [reconsideration of orders] and 49 [review of orders], as applicable;

heading: Duties when authority to act ends
paragraph: (2) In respect of powers exercised under this Part by a person designated as an inspector under section 62 [emergency inspectors or veterinarians], the chief veterinarian may require a person appointed or retained as an inspector under section 71 [appointment of inspectors] to take one or more actions referred to in subsection (1) of this section on behalf of a person designated under section 62.

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph:
67
		  (1) The minister may establish programs and engage in planning in respect of animal health promotion and protection.

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (2) The minister may enter into agreements with any person or body, including the government of another jurisdiction, for one or more of the following purposes:

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (a) to administer this Act;

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (b) to exercise powers or perform duties in relation to animal health under an enactment of another jurisdiction;

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (c) to engage in animal health program planning, delivery, evaluation and monitoring;

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (d) to exchange information, including personal information,

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (i)  under an agreement referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c),

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (ii)  for the purposes of a traceability system, or

heading: Role and general powers of minister
paragraph: (iii)  if necessary for the protection of animal health and public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans.

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph:
68
		  (1) The minister may appoint as the chief veterinarian a person who is

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (a) an employee within the ministry of the minister, and

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (b) a veterinarian.

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (2) The chief veterinarian is the senior animal health official for British Columbia.

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (3) The chief veterinarian must advise the minister on

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (a) animal health issues, including animal health promotion and protection,

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (b) legislation, policies and practices respecting those issues, and

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (c) any matter arising from the exercise of the chief veterinarian's powers or the performance of the chief veterinarian's duties under this or any other enactment.

heading: Chief veterinarian
paragraph: (4) If the minister appoints a deputy or person to act for the chief veterinarian, the appointed person must meet the requirements of subsection (1).

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph:
69
		  In addition to any other power of the chief veterinarian under this Act, the chief veterinarian may do one or more of the following:

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph: (a) establish training and qualifications for inspectors, including requiring ongoing training;

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph: (b) establish standards of practice for inspectors in relation to the exercise of their powers and the performance of their duties under this or any other enactment;

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph: (c) establish procedures for the conduct of an inspection requested under section 26 [voluntary inspections];

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph: (d) establish procedures for the disinfection of persons and equipment during and after an inspection;

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph: (e) issue instructions to inspectors in relation to preventive measures generally;

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph: (f) issue instructions to inspectors for the purposes of fulfilling their duties under Part 5 [Emergency Powers];

heading: General powers of chief veterinarian
paragraph: (g) set standards and qualifications that facilities must meet for the purposes of the examination or testing of, or the analysis of samples from, animals, animal products or byproducts, or things related to any of these, under this Act.

heading: Delegation by chief veterinarian
paragraph:
70
		  The chief veterinarian may, in writing, delegate to a person or class of persons any of the chief veterinarian's powers or duties under this Act, except the following:

heading: Delegation by chief veterinarian
paragraph: (a) a power to further delegate the power or duty;

heading: Delegation by chief veterinarian
paragraph: (b) a duty to advise the minister under section 68 (3) [chief veterinarian].

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph:
71
		  (1) Subject to subsection (6), the chief veterinarian may appoint employees within a ministry of the government as inspectors under this Act and, for this purpose, may

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (a) name a specific person, or

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (b) provide that a person holding a specified title or position is an inspector.

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (2) The chief veterinarian may, in an appointment under subsection (1),

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (a) limit the person's powers and duties as an inspector

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (i)  to a geographic area, and

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (ii)  to a class of animals or a class of animal products or byproducts, and

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (b) require the person to hold specified credentials as a condition of the appointment.

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1) but subject to subsection (6), the chief veterinarian may retain persons as necessary to be inspectors and, for this purpose, delegate to those persons any power or duty of an inspector.

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (4) A person retained under subsection (3) may be remunerated in accordance with the prescribed fees for being an inspector.

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (5) The Public Service Act does not apply to a person retained under subsection (3).

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (6) A person must not be appointed or retained as an inspector unless the person

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (a) is a veterinarian, or

heading: Appointment of inspectors
paragraph: (b) has, in the opinion of the chief veterinarian, sufficient training, knowledge, skills and experience to exercise the powers and perform the duties of an inspector.

heading: Compliance by inspectors
paragraph: 72		  An inspector must comply with all applicable standards and procedures established, and instructions issued, under section 69 [general powers of chief veterinarian].

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph:
73
		  (1) An inspector may call on the assistance of a peace officer for the purpose of taking an action authorized under this or any other enactment, including, without limitation, either of the following purposes:

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph: (a) making or enforcing an order or carrying out an inspection;

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph: (b) assisting a person to comply with or to carry out an order of the inspector.

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph: (2) A peace officer called on under this section may take any action that is necessary for a purpose described in subsection (1) and may use such force as is reasonably required for that purpose.

heading: Immunity from legal proceedings
paragraph:
74
		  No legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against the minister, an inspector or a person acting under the order or direction of either of them, because of anything done or omitted

heading: Immunity from legal proceedings
paragraph: (a) in the exercise or intended exercise of a power under this or any other enactment, or

heading: Immunity from legal proceedings
paragraph: (b) in the performance or intended performance of a duty under this or any other enactment.

heading: Immunity for persons required to act
paragraph:
75
		  (1) No legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against a veterinarian, a person responsible for administering a laboratory, or another person who, under this Act,

heading: Immunity for persons required to act
paragraph: (a) makes a report that the person is required to make, or

heading: Immunity for persons required to act
paragraph: (b) takes another action that the person is required to take.

heading: Immunity for persons required to act
paragraph: (2) No legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against an employer of a person described in subsection (1).

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph:
76
		  (1) In this section, "adverse action" means an action that would adversely affect, or that threatens to adversely affect, the personal, financial or other interests of a person, or a relative, dependent, friend, or business or other close associate of the person, and includes any prescribed action.

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (2) A person must not take an adverse action against another person because the other person, acting in good faith, does any of the following:

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (a) makes a report or takes another action under this Act;

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (b) assists in, or provides information during, an inspection or a proceeding under this Act;

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (c) complies with, or assists in carrying out, an order made under this Act;

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (d) refuses to take an action that is or may be a contravention of this Act or a regulation made under it;

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (e) discloses to an inspector that a person has contravened or is about to contravene this Act or a regulation made under it.

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (3) Nothing in this section prevents an inspector from taking enforcement action in respect of a violation or contravention of

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (a) this Act or a regulation or an order made under it, or

heading: Protection against adverse actions
paragraph: (b) a term or condition of a licence or permit.

heading: Test results as evidence
paragraph:
77
		  For the purposes of a proceeding under this Act, a report or certificate from

heading: Test results as evidence
paragraph: (a) a laboratory, or

heading: Test results as evidence
paragraph: (b) a facility specified in an order made under this Act

heading: Test results as evidence
paragraph: stating the result or interpretation of a test or an analysis made in the laboratory or facility is evidence of the facts stated in the report or certificate.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph:
78
		  (1) If a person is authorized by regulation to impose an administrative penalty, the person may impose an administrative penalty in the amount permitted by the regulations if satisfied on a balance of probabilities that another person has done any of the following:

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of this Act or a regulation made under it;

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with an order made under this Act;

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) failed to comply with a term or condition of that other person's licence or permit.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) An administrative penalty may be imposed by serving notice of the administrative penalty in the prescribed manner.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) If a person is subject to an administrative penalty, the person must do one of the following within the prescribed time:

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) pay the administrative penalty;

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) dispute the administrative penalty in accordance with the regulations, including disputing the amount of the administrative penalty on any ground permitted by the regulations;

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) agree, in writing, with the person who imposed the administrative penalty to do one or more things, including paying a reduced administrative penalty, that the person who imposed the administrative penalty reasonably believes would

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (i)  be sufficient for the protection of animal health and public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans, and

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (ii)  if applicable, bring the person into compliance with this Act, the regulations or an order made under it, or a term or condition of the person's licence or permit.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) If an administrative penalty is disputed or made the subject of an agreement under subsection (3) (c), the person subject to the administrative penalty must pay the administrative penalty or any part of it that remains outstanding

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) under the terms of the agreement,

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) on receiving notice, following a dispute, that the person remains subject to all or part of the administrative penalty, or

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) on receiving notice that the person failed to meet the terms of the agreement to the satisfaction of the person who imposed the administrative penalty.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (5) If a corporation contravenes this Act or a regulation made under it, or fails to comply with an order made under this Act or a term or condition of a licence or permit, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure to comply is also liable under this section even though the corporation is liable for or pays an administrative penalty.

heading: Person not to be charged with both administrative penalty and offence
paragraph:
79
		  (1) A person subject to an administrative penalty must not be prosecuted for an offence in respect of the same incident that gave rise to the administrative penalty.

heading: Person not to be charged with both administrative penalty and offence
paragraph: (2) A person prosecuted for an offence must not be subject to an administrative penalty in respect of the same incident that gave rise to the prosecution.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
80
		  (1) An administrative penalty under this Act may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required, the person who imposed the administrative penalty may file a certificate with a court that has jurisdiction and, on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) must be in the prescribed form, be signed by the person who imposed the administrative penalty and contain

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the administrative penalty,

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) the contravention or failure in relation to which the administrative penalty is imposed, and

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the administrative penalty.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) All administrative penalties received under this Division must be paid into the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
81
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of the following provisions commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) section 5 (2) [fails to take preventive measures];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) section 6 (1) [fails to comply with veterinary advice];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) section 9 [fails to comply with disease control order];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) section 19 [fails to keep or produce records];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (e) section 20 (2), (3) or (4) [fails to make reports and records, take samples or do other required things];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (f) section 45 (3) [fails to comply with instructions];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (g) section 52 [fails to comply with order];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (h) section 53 [removes, defaces or alters a notice, mark or tag];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (i) section 63 (2) [fails to make a report in an emergency];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (j) section 76 (2) [takes an adverse action against a person].

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes any of the following provisions commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) section 3 [causes disease or its transmission or spread, or interferes with disease prevention, control or eradication];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) section 4 (2) [fails to train or equip employees];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) section 7 [keeps or deals with affected animals];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) section 8 [slaughters, destroys or disposes of affected or harmful things];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (e) section 10 (2) or (3) [fails to comply with regulations or to train or equip employees];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (f) section 17 (2) [fails to keep information confidential];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (g) section 18 (4) [collects, uses or discloses personal information without authorization];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (h) section 22 (4) [fails to do a required thing in respect of a traceability system].

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) A person who does either of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) knowingly provides false or misleading information to a person who is exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act, or a person acting under the order or direction of that person;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) wilfully interferes with, or obstructs, a person who is exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act, or a person acting under the order or direction of that person.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (4) A person who commits an offence under this Act may be liable for the offence whether or not an order is made under this Act in respect of the matter.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (5) A proceeding for an offence under this Act may not be commenced in any court more than 2 years after the facts on which the proceeding is based first come to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Offence by corporation or employee
paragraph:
82
		  (1) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence whether or not the corporation is convicted.

heading: Offence by corporation or employee
paragraph: (2) If an employee commits an offence under this Act, an employer who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence whether or not the employee is identified or convicted.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph:
83
		  (1) In this section, "order" means an order that may be made under this Act by an inspector or the court.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: (2) If a person commits an offence under this Act and continues to commit the offence, separate penalties may be imposed in respect of the offence for each day the original offence continues.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: (3) If a person commits an offence under this Act and an order is made in respect of the matter that is the subject of the offence, but the offence continues after the date by which the order is to be complied with,

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: (a) subsection (2) applies from the date by which the order is to be complied with, and

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: (b) the person may be prosecuted both for the original offence and for the additional offence of contravening the order.

heading: Offence Act application
paragraph:
84
		  Sections 4 and 5 of the Offence Act do not apply in respect of this Act or the regulations made under it.

heading: Defences
paragraph: 85		  A person must not be convicted of an offence under this Act if the person proves that the person

heading: Defences
paragraph: (a) exercised due diligence by taking all reasonable steps to avoid committing the offence,

heading: Defences
paragraph: (b) reasonably believed in the existence of facts that, if true, would establish that the person did not contravene this Act or a regulation made under it,

heading: Defences
paragraph: (c) relied on information or an instruction provided to the person by another person who was exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act, if the first person had no reason to believe that the information may have been false or the instruction may have been unauthorized, or

heading: Defences
paragraph: (d) acted under the order of another person who was exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act, if the first person had no reason to believe that the order may have been unauthorized under this Act or any other enactment.

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph:
86
		  (1) Before imposing a sentence, a sentencing judge may request a joint submission from the offender and the prosecutor setting out any agreement on

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (a) the circumstances that should be considered by the sentencing judge as either mitigating or aggravating the offence, and

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (b) the penalty to be imposed.

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (2) In determining the appropriate sentence, the sentencing judge must consider, in accordance with the regulations, circumstances that aggravate or mitigate the offence.

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (3) In determining the appropriate sentence, a sentencing judge must do the following:

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (a) consider the purposes of sentencing set out in section 87 [purposes of sentencing];

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (b) to give effect to those purposes,

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (i)  first, consider as a penalty one or more of the orders that may be made under section 88 [alternative penalties],

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (ii)  second, consider whether an order should be made under section 89 [no animal order], and

heading: Determining sentence
paragraph: (iii)  third, consider whether a fine or incarceration under section 90 [fines and incarceration] is also necessary.

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph:
87
		  (1) In imposing a sentence, a sentencing judge may impose one or more penalties that, in order, achieve the following:

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (a) first,

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (i)  if harm was caused, remedy the harm or compensate a person who remedied or suffered the harm, including the government, or

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (ii)  if no harm was caused, acknowledge the potential harm or further the regulatory objective underlying the provision that was contravened;

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (b) second, if the offence was committed in relation to a regulated activity or other activity that the offender is reasonably likely to continue to engage in, rehabilitate the offender.

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (2) In addition to a penalty imposed under subsection (1), a sentencing judge may impose one or more penalties under subsection (3) or (4), or both, unless it would be disproportionate to the offence, given the offender, the nature of the offence and the total of the penalties imposed under this section.

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (3) A sentencing judge may impose a penalty for the purpose of achieving general deterrence if the sentencing judge reasonably believes that the additional penalty would have a deterrent effect, including because

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (a) the penalty imposed under subsection (1) is inadequate to address the circumstances related to the offence, or

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (b) the nature of the penalty may

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (i)  assist others similarly situated to the offender to avoid committing a similar offence, or

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (ii)  educate others similarly situated to the offender respecting the seriousness of the offence.

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (4) A sentencing judge may impose a penalty for the purpose of punishing the offender if

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (a) the offender committed the offence knowingly or deliberately, or was reckless as to the commission of the offence, or

heading: Purposes of sentencing
paragraph: (b) sufficient aggravating circumstances exist that the offender should be punished for the offence.

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph:
88
		  (1) To give effect to the purposes of sentencing as set out in section 87 [purposes of sentencing], a sentencing judge may order a person convicted of an offence under this Act to do one or more of the following:

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (a) do a thing, or not do a thing, as set out in a joint submission under section 86 (1) [determining sentence];

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (b) take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or stop the transmission or spread, caused by the commission of the offence, of a notifiable or reportable disease;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (c) pay a person an amount of money as compensation, in whole or in part, for the cost of a remedial or preventive action taken by or on behalf of the person as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (d) perform community service for a period of up to 3 years;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (e) not do any act or engage in any activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence or the commission of a similar offence under this Act;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (f) comply with any conditions that the court considers appropriate for preventing the person from continuing or repeating the offence or committing a similar offence under this Act;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (g) submit to the minister or an inspector information respecting the activities of the person that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances, for a period of up to 3 years;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (h) if the person is a corporation, designate a senior official within the corporation as the person responsible for monitoring compliance with this Act or the regulations or an order made under it, or the terms or conditions of a licence or permit held by the corporation under this Act;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (i) develop guidelines or standards in respect of a matter, implement a process or do another thing, for the purposes of preventing the person from continuing or repeating the offence, or committing a similar offence;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (j) make available, either free of charge or for a fee, to another person or class of persons guidelines or standards developed under paragraph (i) of this subsection, in any manner and under any conditions the court considers appropriate, for up to 3 years from the date by which the guidelines or standards must be developed;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (k) publish, in any manner the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence and any other information the court considers appropriate;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (l) post a bond for an amount of money the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with a prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (m) submit to inspections, submit samples or analyses, or do any other thing necessary to permit an inspector or other person specified by the court to monitor compliance, for a period of up to 3 years, with an order made under this section.

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1) (j), the court may set or limit the amount of the fee or put conditions on the charging of the fee.

heading: Alternative penalties
paragraph: (3) A person who contravenes an order under this section or section 91 [variation of orders imposed at sentencing] commits an offence and is liable to the penalties provided for the offence in relation to which the order was made.

heading: No animal order
paragraph:
89
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, a sentencing judge may, in addition to a penalty imposed under section 88 [alternative penalties], prohibit the person from owning or having custody or control of an animal.

heading: No animal order
paragraph: (2) If a sentencing judge makes an order under subsection (1), the judge may

heading: No animal order
paragraph: (a) limit the order to a period of time specified by the judge, and

heading: No animal order
paragraph: (b) make the order on any terms the judge considers appropriate.

heading: Fines and incarceration
paragraph:
90
		  (1) In addition to a penalty imposed under section 88 [alternative penalties], a person who commits an offence listed in

heading: Fines and incarceration
paragraph: (a) section 81 (1) [offences] is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $25 000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or to both, or

heading: Fines and incarceration
paragraph: (b) section 81 (2) or (3) is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $75 000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years, or to both.

heading: Fines and incarceration
paragraph: (2) In determining the fine to be imposed on conviction, a sentencing judge must consider the means and ability of the offender to pay the fine, and, if the sentencing judge believes that the offender is unable to pay the amount of the fine that the sentencing judge would otherwise impose, the sentencing judge may impose a fine in a lesser amount that the sentencing judge considers appropriate.

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph:
91
		  (1) An application for variation of an order made under section 88 [alternative penalties] may be made to the court that made the order by

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (a) an inspector, or

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (b) the person subject to the order.

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (2) Before hearing an application for variation, the court may order the applicant to provide notice of the application in accordance with the directions of the court.

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (3) On an application for variation, if the court considers variation appropriate because the circumstances have changed, the court may make an order to do one or more of the following:

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (a) change the original order or conditions specified in it;

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (b) relieve the person subject to the original order absolutely or partially from compliance with all or part of that order;

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (c) reduce the period for which the original order is to remain in effect;

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (d) extend, for not longer than one year, the period for which the original order is to remain in effect.

heading: Variation of orders imposed at sentencing
paragraph: (4) If an application for variation has been heard by a court, no other application for variation may be made in respect of the order except with leave of the court.

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph:
92
		  (1) If a person fails to comply with an order referred to in section 88 (1) (k) [alternative penalties], the chief veterinarian may publish the facts and information referred to in the order, including any personal information contained in the order, and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (2) If

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (a) an order under section 88 directs a person to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose, or

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (b) the chief veterinarian incurs publication costs under subsection (1) of this section,

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: the amount and any interest payable on that amount constitute a debt due to the government and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (3) Except as set out in subsection (2), every penalty imposed under this Division may be recovered by proceedings under the Offence Act.

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: 93		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting terms as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (a) prescribing organisms as animals;

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (b) prescribing animals to which this Act does not apply;

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (c) prescribing material as an animal product or byproduct;

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (d) for the purposes of the definition of "regulated activity", prescribing trades, businesses and activities, whether or not the activities are commercial in nature, that

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (i)  involve keeping or dealing with animals, or animal products or byproducts,

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (ii)  may have an impact on animal health,

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (iii)  may cause or contribute to, or otherwise be associated with, the transmission or spread of a notifiable or reportable disease between animals, or

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (iv)  may cause or contribute to, or otherwise be associated with, the transmission of diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans;

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (e) prescribing actions for the purposes of section 76 (1) [protection against adverse actions];

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (f) respecting what it means to keep or deal with an animal for the purposes of this Act or a regulation made under it.

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing environmental toxins, infestations, syndromes or transmissible diseases as either notifiable diseases or reportable diseases and, for this purpose, may do the following:

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (a) provide the name or other common description of organisms and animals;

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (b) provide the name or other common description of a disease, chemical, toxic substance or other deleterious substance, thing, organism or condition;

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (c) provide the names or other common descriptions of

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (i)  one or more infectious agents or syndromes associated with infection by a disease,

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (ii)  contamination by a chemical, toxic substance or other deleterious substance or thing, or

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (iii)  infestation by an organism;

heading: Regulations respecting terms
paragraph: (d) describe the signs or indicators of the presence of an environmental toxin, an infestation, a syndrome or a transmissible disease.

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph:
94
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the prevention, control and eradication of notifiable and reportable diseases as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (a) respecting reports of non-compliance under section 6 [must comply with veterinary advice];

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (b) respecting the circumstances in which a person must take preventive measures;

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (c) respecting the prevention of the presence, transmission or spread of notifiable and reportable diseases, including providing for particular preventive measures for particular purposes;

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (d) placing restrictions or prohibitions on persons who have not taken preventive measures, including restrictions or prohibitions on the disposition of animals, or animal products or byproducts;

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (e) respecting the disposition of animals, and animal products or byproducts, for the purposes of section 8 [must not slaughter, destroy or dispose of affected or harmful things], including setting limits and conditions on disposition;

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (f) respecting facilities, equipment, management, sanitation, operation and maintenance in relation to activities in respect of keeping or dealing with animals, or animal products or byproducts, whether or not the activity is prescribed as a regulated activity;

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (g) respecting the transportation of animals, and animal products or byproducts;

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (h) respecting the establishment and maintenance of animal health programs.

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations establishing control zones for a purpose described in section 36 (1) [deemed control zones] in respect of a notifiable or reportable disease.

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (3) In a regulation made under subsection (2) of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council must do the things described in section 36 (2) and may do one or more of the things described in section 36 (3).

heading: Regulations respecting disease prevention and control
paragraph: (4) Despite section 38 [end of temporary orders], if a regulation made under subsection (2) of this section establishes a control zone over an area that is subject to an order made under section 36, the order ceases to have effect on the date the regulation is effective.

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph:
95
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting operators and regulated activities as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (a) prohibiting matters in respect of regulated activities, and restricting or putting conditions on the performance of a regulated activity;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (b) respecting the monitoring of regulated activities for conditions that may cause or contribute to the transmission or spread of notifiable and reportable diseases, including requiring a program of self-monitoring;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (c) respecting training and qualifications for operators and employees, including

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (i)  requiring ongoing training, and

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (ii)  setting examinations and charging fees for taking examinations;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (d) respecting information that must be provided by an operator to the government and the public about an animal or an animal product or byproduct for which the operator is responsible;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (e) respecting standards that must be met in respect of an animal product or byproduct for which the operator is responsible.

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting licences, permits and registrations as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (a) requiring licences, permits or registration to engage in regulated activities, including requiring registration of the place at which a regulated activity is to be engaged in;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (b) respecting applications and renewals;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (c) prescribing factors that may or must be considered in determining whether to issue a licence or permit or to grant a registration;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (d) respecting conditions that may be attached to a licence or permit;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (e) prescribing fees for applications, registrations, changes and renewals, and prescribing different fees based on the type of regulated activity and the number or type of animals for which an operator is responsible;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (f) requiring operators to have and provide evidence of financial security as a condition of a licence or permit, or to have a registration granted, and respecting the type and amount of security;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (g) respecting bonding;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (h) respecting service and deemed receipt of a notice for the purposes of section 14 [taking administrative action];

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (i) respecting actions operators must take during a suspension or cancellation of a licence or permit, or after cancellation of a licence, permit or registration, in relation to their premises or animals.

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (a) limiting the number of animals for which operators may be responsible;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (b) designating areas of British Columbia for one or more purposes in relation to the management of populations or subpopulations of animals;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (c) prohibiting or putting limits or conditions on species, races, strains or ages of animals

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (i)  for which operators may be responsible, or

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (ii)  that may be kept or dealt with in an area designated under paragraph (b);

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (d) prohibiting or putting limits or conditions on keeping or dealing with animal products or byproducts, or equipment related to a regulated activity, in an area designated under paragraph (b);

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (e) prescribing periods for the purposes of section 76 of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting certification programs as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (a) prescribing certification programs;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (b) respecting applications and fees for certification;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (c) respecting the training and qualifications an operator must have to be certified;

heading: Regulations respecting operators and regulated activities
paragraph: (d) respecting standards that a certified operator must meet.

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: 96		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the following:

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (a) the making and keeping of records, and the making of reports, by persons referred to in section 19 [duty to keep records];

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (b) prescribing additional persons for the purposes of section 19;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (c) respecting fees that may be charged in relation to the taking or analysis of samples, whether or not the taking or analysis of samples is

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (i)  required under section 20 [mandatory reporting] or 21 [mandatory diagnostic examination and reporting], or

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (ii)  done during the course of an inspection.

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of sections 20 and 21 as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (a) prescribing additional persons who may collect, use and disclose information under this Act;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (b) respecting the making of reports, including

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (i)  the form of a report and the manner of making the report,

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (ii)  information, in addition to anything described in this Act, that must be reported, and

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (iii)  records or analyses that must accompany a report;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (c) respecting actions that must be taken on the making of a report, including requiring monitoring, making records and taking samples;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (d) respecting conditions under which a person may be exempted from a requirement to make a report under this Act.

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of section 22 [traceability systems] as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (a) prescribing traceability systems and traceability programs in respect of which section 22 (4) applies;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (b) prescribing things that are traceable items for the purposes of the definition of "traceable item" in section 22 (1);

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (c) respecting unique identifiers, including respecting fees for the issuance of unique identifiers and their replacement;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (d) respecting the making of reports, including

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (i)  prescribing persons to whom reports must be made or persons who must receive a copy of a report,

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (ii)  the form of a report and the manner of making the report,

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (iii)  information, in addition to anything described in this Act, that must be reported, and

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (iv)  records or analyses that must accompany a report;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (e) respecting actions that must be taken, including taking samples, by a person subject to section 22 (4);

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (f) without limiting paragraphs (d) and (e) of this subsection and despite section 20 (1), respecting circumstances in which a person responsible for a place, vehicle or thing that is subject to a traceability program must make a report under that section even if the person is not responsible for an animal or for an animal product or byproduct;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (g) prohibiting or putting conditions on the distribution or disposition of animals, animal products or byproducts, or things subject to a traceability system or traceability program;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (h) respecting audits of traceability systems and traceability programs;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (i) respecting the types of, the linking and disclosure of, and access to information kept in respect of a traceability system or traceability program, including for the purposes of an enactment of British Columbia or Canada in relation to animal health, public health in relation to diseases that are or may be transmissible from animals to humans, or emergency planning;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (j) respecting the participation by British Columbia in extrajurisdictional traceability systems or extrajurisdictional traceability programs;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (k) authorizing the collection, use and disclosure of information contained in the assessment roll, as that term is defined in the Assessment Act, for the purposes of a traceability system or traceability program;

heading: Regulations respecting reporting
paragraph: (l) despite section 22 (4), permitting, with or without conditions, a person responsible for a class of traceable animals or traceable items, or for a class of places, vehicles or things that are subject to a traceability program, to meet a requirement under this Act in respect of a group of traceable animals, traceable items, places, vehicles or things rather than in respect of each traceable animal, traceable item, place, vehicle or thing.

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
paragraph: 97		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting inspectors and inspections as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
paragraph: (a) authorizing further purposes for which an inspection may be made;

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
paragraph: (b) respecting fees for the conduct of inspections under section 26 [voluntary inspections];

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
paragraph: (c) respecting the remuneration of persons retained as inspectors under section 71 (3) [appointment of inspectors].

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting orders made under this Act as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
paragraph: (a) respecting actions that an inspector may by order require for the purposes of section 41 (n) [general orders];

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
paragraph: (b) respecting the contents of an order for the purposes of section 44 [contents of orders];

heading: Regulations respecting inspections, orders and enforcement
