heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "antisapstain chemical" means chlorophenol, 2-(thiocyanomethylthio) benzothiazole (TCMTB), copper-8-quinolinolate (Cu-8), 3-iodo-2-propynyl butyl carbamate (IPBC) and didecyldimethyl ammonium chloride (DDAC);

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "chlorophenol" means the sum of chlorophenols plus chlorophenates as reported by a laboratory testing method approved by a director;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "curb" means a raised edge or curbing which would confine all liquids dropping within the enclosure formed by it and the surface on which it sits;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "effluent" includes precipitation runoff;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph:
"fixed roof" means a roof which is designed and constructed to
            prevent the entry of precipitation and to be a maintenance free structure for a period of not less than 10 years, but does not include a structure which utilizes tarpaulins or similar materials;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "impervious" means not allowing entrance or passage of antisapstain chemicals;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph:
"isolated" means set apart from other operations in an
          enclosure away from any high traffic areas that can, under normal circumstances, prevent
          the entry of unauthorized persons.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this regulation effluent is toxic if the effluent at 100% concentration kills 50% or more of rainbow trout within 96 hours when tested in accordance with procedures approved by a director.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph:
2
		  A person shall not introduce into the environment

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (a) an effluent that contains antisapstain chemicals from

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (i)  sawmills, lumber export terminals and other facilities that, for the purpose of preventing sapstain growth, apply antisapstain chemicals or have during the 12 months immediately preceding the introduction of the effluent applied antisapstain chemicals, or

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (ii)  storage areas for lumber treated with antisapstain chemicals, not including storage yards at facilities which only store lumber for the purpose of retail sale directly to the public,

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (b) emissions to the air from antisapstain chemical spray booth vents, or

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (c) emissions to the air consisting of combustion products of antisapstain chemicals and their byproducts

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: unless the person

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (d) meets the requirements under sections 4 to 12 where the person used or uses chlorophenol, TCMTB, DDAC, IPBC or Cu-8, and

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (e) complies with a monitoring program, if any, established by a director that allows the director to determine

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (i)  the concentration of antisapstain chemical in effluents,

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (ii)  the toxicity of the effluents, or

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (iii)  the rate of antisapstain chemical emissions to the air from antisapstain chemical spray booths.

heading: Exemption
paragraph:
3
		  A person to whom section 2 applies is exempt from section 6 of the Environmental Management Act in respect of the introduction into the environment of an effluent or emission referred to in section 2 (a) to (c) if the person meets the requirements of section 2 (d) and (e).

heading: Storm sewer design
paragraph: 4		  (1) A storm sewer serving a storage area referred to in section 2 (a) (ii) or any antisapstain treatment area of any facility referred to in section 2 (a) shall receive only precipitation and runoff from the storage area, treatment area or both, including roof drainage from structures which shelter the storage areas and treatment areas, and shall convey it to a sampling point downstream of the storage area and treatment area.

heading: Storm sewer design
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), the storm sewer may receive and convey additional liquids downstream of the sampling point.

heading: Quality of effluent including stormwater
paragraph: (3) The concentration of an individual antisapstain chemical in effluent shall not exceed 6 µg/l chlorophenol, 6 µg/l TCMTB, 15 µg/l Cu-8, 120 µg/l IPBC or 700 µg/l DDAC.

heading: Quality of effluent including stormwater
paragraph: (4) The effluents from operations described in section 2 (a) shall not be toxic.

heading: Quality of effluent including stormwater
paragraph: (5) Sampling to determine a concentration of any individual antisapstain chemical in effluent under subsection (3) shall occur at the sampling point referred to in section 4.

heading: Quality of effluent including stormwater
paragraph: (6) Sampling referred to in subsection (4) and the analysis of the samples shall be conducted using sampling and analytical methods approved by a director.

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical storage and mix facilities
paragraph:
6
		  (1) An antisapstain concentrated chemical storage system, concentrate feed system, mix system and working solution storage tanks

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical storage and mix facilities
paragraph: (a) shall be located in an isolated area within a building, and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical storage and mix facilities
paragraph: (b) shall have doors that provide access to the area and that shall be kept locked except when a person is present for work related purposes.

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical storage and mix facilities
paragraph: (2) A spill containment system shall be maintained for the isolated area under subsection (1) and the spill system shall be impervious and of sufficient size to contain at least 120% of the volume of the largest tank in the isolated area.

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph:
7
		  (1) An antisapstain chemical dip tank shall

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (a) be impervious,

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (b) if it is an above ground tank, be located in an impervious containment area which has

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (i)  a sloped floor, and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (ii)  a curb that is of sufficient height to enable the containment area to hold at least 120% of the largest chemical dip tank volume, and that prevents entry of surface runoff,

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph:
(c) if it is not an above ground tank, be a double wall containment tank constructed
            with

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (i)  both walls impervious, and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (ii)  a means for determining if there is leakage of the chemicals into the area between the walls,

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (d) have an associated impervious primary drip area that provides 30 minutes minimum dripping time for treated wood immediately following the treatment and that prevents entry to the dip tank of surface runoff and precipitation,

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (e) have a system for recycling all drippings from the containment area referred to in paragraphs (b) and (c) and from the impervious drip area referred to in paragraph (d) back to the dip tank, and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (f) be constructed so as to prevent a motorized vehicle of a type that can reasonably be expected to operate near the dip tank from driving in or through the dip tank.

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical dip tank systems
paragraph: (2) The containment area referred to in subsection (1) (b), the tank referred to in subsection (1) (c) and the primary drip area referred to in subsection (1) (d) shall be provided with a fixed roof and with guard rails or equivalent to provide vehicle impact protection.

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph:
8
		  (1) An antisapstain chemical spray booth system shall have

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (a) a collection tray that is impervious and that facilitates recycling for re-use of all oversprayed antisapstain chemicals,

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (b) under both the spray box and collection tray, a containment area that

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (i)  consists of a floor and curb,

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (ii)  is impervious, and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (iii)  has the capacity to contain all drippings for subsequent recycling or for disposal in accordance with the provisions of the Hazardous Waste Regulation (B.C. Reg. 63/88), and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (c) a primary drip area that

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (i)  provides 30 minutes minimum drying time for treated wood immediately following treatment,

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (ii)  has a fixed roof, and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (iii)  has a system for recycling all drippings for re-use.

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph:
(2) Emissions to the air from antisapstain chemical application spray
          booths

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (a) shall be treated by a demister or an alternative approved by a director and then

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (i)  shall be vented directly to the atmosphere by a stack, the top of which shall be at least 10 metres above the ground and 5 metres above the highest point of the roof of the building which houses the antisapstain chemical spray booth, or

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (ii)  all or part of the treated emission shall be recirculated back to the spray booth, and

heading: Design of antisapstain chemical spray booth systems
paragraph: (b) shall not be combined with any pneumatic stream that conveys chips, sawdust, planer shavings, hog fuel or any other wood residue.

heading: Demister purge
paragraph:
9
		  Where a director has issued a directive to minimize the quantity of antisapstain chemicals introduced to the environment by effluent purged from a demister referred to in section 8 (2) (a), the effluent shall be handled, treated and disposed of in accordance with the directive.

heading:
Antisapstain chemical spray booth atmospheric emission
        quality
paragraph:
10
		  The rate of emissions to the air from an antisapstain chemical spray booth stack referred to in section 8 (2) (a) shall not exceed

heading:
Antisapstain chemical spray booth atmospheric emission
        quality
paragraph: (a) 7.0 mg per second chlorophenol,

heading:
Antisapstain chemical spray booth atmospheric emission
        quality
paragraph: (b) 7.0 mg per second TCMTB,

heading:
Antisapstain chemical spray booth atmospheric emission
        quality
paragraph: (c) 7.0 mg per second Cu-8,

heading:
Antisapstain chemical spray booth atmospheric emission
        quality
paragraph: (d) 7.0 mg per second DDAC, or

heading:
Antisapstain chemical spray booth atmospheric emission
        quality
paragraph: (e) 7.0 mg per second IPBC

heading:
Antisapstain chemical spray booth atmospheric emission
        quality
paragraph: as determined by sampling and analytical methods approved by a director.

heading: Management of sludges and wood residue
paragraph:
11
		  (1) Sludges that qualify as hazardous waste and that have originated from antisapstain chemical dip tanks and spray system filtering or screening processes shall not be incinerated, buried or otherwise disposed of or introduced into the environment unless all provisions of the Hazardous Waste Regulation are satisfied.

heading: Management of sludges and wood residue
paragraph: (2) Trim ends, broken lumber, chips, sawdust, planer shavings and other wood residue resulting from processing and handling of wood following its treatment with antisapstain chemicals

heading: Management of sludges and wood residue
paragraph: (a) shall not be provided to a person for use as mulch or for burning in a residential fireplace, stove or other burning device other than an incinerator permitted under paragraph (b),

heading: Management of sludges and wood residue
paragraph: (b) shall be incinerated only in a hog fuel burning incinerator, or other incineration device, that is designed

heading: Management of sludges and wood residue
paragraph: (i)  to burn the wood residue at a minimum combustion temperature of 900°C, and

heading: Management of sludges and wood residue
paragraph: (ii)  for gases in the combustion zone to have a minimum residence time of one second, and

heading: Management of sludges and wood residue
paragraph: (c) if the antisapstain chemical is a chlorophenol, shall not be provided to a person for the purpose of supplying digesters in pulp manufacturing processes.

heading: Design of treated wood storage areas
paragraph:
12
		  Lumber treated with antisapstain chemicals and not otherwise protected from contact with precipitation shall be stored in an area that has a floor and a curb that are impervious to the treatment chemicals or that are constructed of asphalt that is maintained in good condition.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Professional Governance Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "applied biology limited licensee" means an individual who is registered with the regulatory body as an applied biology limited licensee in accordance with the bylaws of the regulatory body;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "biological science" includes botany, zoology, ecology, biochemistry and microbiology;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "biology objective" means the restoration, retention or enhancement of, or the mitigation of impacts on, the receiving environment, and the living organisms, habitats or processes within ecosystems in relation to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) conservation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) protection, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) wild terrestrial or aquatic species management;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "impact" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the harming or removal of living organisms, including by gathering, collecting, hunting or angling,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the effect of a contaminant or other circumstances affecting the environment, including light or noise, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the damage or loss of a habitat;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "practice of applied biology", subject to subsection (2), means the provision of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) advice or services that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  are based on biological sciences, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  relate to aquatic or terrestrial ecosystems or the living organisms, habitats or processes of those ecosystems, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) advice or services that are ancillary to those described in paragraph (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Fisheries Act. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aquaculture means the cultivation of fish. (aquaculture)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aquaculture licence means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a lease or licence issued or granted by the Minister under section 7 or 58 of the Act, or its regulations, for the purpose of aquaculture;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a lease granted by the government of a province under subsection 59(1) of the Act for the cultivation of oysters;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a provincial licence or authorization for the operation of an aquaculture facility. (permis d'aquaculture)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: barren substrate means benthic substrate on which there are no visible organisms. (substrat sterile)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: biochemical oxygen demanding matter means any organic matter that contributes to the consumption of oxygen that is dissolved in water or sediment. (matiere exercant une demande biochimique en oxygene)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Monitoring Standard means the Aquaculture Monitoring Standard, as amended from time to time, that is produced by the Minister and maintained on the Department of Fisheries and Oceans website. (Norme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: soft bottom means a benthic substrate that consists of loose particles such as clay, mud, marl, sand, pebbles, gravel, shells or small stones.  (fond meuble)

heading: Specified substances
paragraph: 2 For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(c) of the Act, the following classes of substances deposited in the operation of an aquaculture facility are specified to be deleterious substances:

heading: Specified substances
paragraph: (a) drugs whose sale is permitted or otherwise authorized, or whose importation is not prohibited, under the Food and Drugs Act;

heading: Specified substances
paragraph: (b) pest control products that are registered, or whose use is authorized, under the Pest Control Products Act; and

heading: Specified substances
paragraph: (c) biochemical oxygen demanding matter.

heading: Conditions applicable to deposits
paragraph: 3 An owner or operator of an aquaculture facility may, subject to the conditions set out in sections 4 to 14, deposit a deleterious substance specified in section 2 in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act.

heading: Aquaculture facility
paragraph: 4 The deleterious substance must be deposited in the operation of the aquaculture facility and the facility must be operated under an aquaculture licence.

heading: Drugs
paragraph: 5 In the case of a deposit of a drug,

heading: Drugs
paragraph: (a) if by or under an Act of Parliament the drug may only be sold under a prescription, it must be prescribed by a person who is duly authorized to practise veterinary medicine

heading: Drugs
paragraph: (i) under the laws of the province in which the aquaculture facility is located, or

heading: Drugs
paragraph: (ii) under the laws of any province, if the aquaculture facility is not located in a province;

heading: Drugs
paragraph: (b) the owner or operator of the facility must take measures to minimize the risk of an accidental deposit of the drug; and

heading: Drugs
paragraph: (c) if the drug is deposited to control a pest as defined in the Pest Control Products Act, the owner or operator must consider, before depositing the drug, whether there are alternatives to the deposit of that drug and make a record of that consideration.

heading: Pest control products
paragraph: 6 In the case of a deposit of a pest control product,

heading: Pest control products
paragraph: (a) if the pest control product is registered, the owner or operator of the aquaculture facility must use it in compliance with any conditions specified under the Pest Control Products Act, including any conditions relating to the place where it may be used and the quantity and concentration that may be used;

heading: Pest control products
paragraph: (b) if the pest control product is not registered, it must be authorized to be used by the owner or the operator under subsection 21(5) or 41(1) of the Pest Control Products Act or have been exempted from registration by a regulation made under paragraph 67(1)(z.4) of that Act;

heading: Pest control products
paragraph: (c) the owner or the operator must consider, before depositing the pest control product, whether there are alternatives to the deposit of that pest control product and make a record of that consideration; and

heading: Pest control products
paragraph: (d) the owner or the operator must notify the Minister, at least 72 hours before the deposit, of the product name of the pest control product and the time, date and geographic coordinates of the deposit.

heading: Measures to reduce detriment
paragraph: 7 (1) The owner or the operator of the aquaculture facility must, in depositing a deleterious substance referred to in paragraph 2(a) or (b), take reasonable measures to minimize detriment to fish and fish habitat outside the facility, having regard to

heading: Measures to reduce detriment
paragraph: (a) the cost and effectiveness of the available measures;

heading: Measures to reduce detriment
paragraph: (b) the degree and nature of the detriment that may result from the deposit; and

heading: Measures to reduce detriment
paragraph: (c) the physical characteristics of the facility and the type of aquaculture that is engaged in.

heading: Feces and unconsumed feed
paragraph: (2) In the case of an aquaculture facility that cultivates finfish and that is operated under an aquaculture licence that permits a standing biomass of more than 2.5 t or an annual production of more than 5 t, the owner or operator of the facility must take reasonable measures to minimize the deposit of fish feces and unconsumed feed, having regard to the factors set out in paragraphs (1)(a) to (c).

heading: Information required before depositing
paragraph: 8 (1) In the case of an aquaculture facility located in tidal waters for the cultivation of finfish that commences operations after the day on which these Regulations come into force, the owner or operator of the facility must submit the following information to the Minister at least 300 days before making a first deposit of a deleterious substance in the operation of the facility:

heading: Information required before depositing
paragraph: (a) the predicted contours of the footprint of the biochemical oxygen demanding matter that will be deposited by the facility, calculated in accordance with the Monitoring Standard;

heading: Information required before depositing
paragraph: (b) a survey conducted in accordance with the Monitoring Standard that identifies the fish and fish habitat on the seabed that is leased for the operations of the facility and in the water column above the seabed;

heading: Information required before depositing
paragraph: (c) the bathymetry of the seabed that is leased for the operations of the facility, measured in accordance with the Monitoring Standard; and

heading: Information required before depositing
paragraph: (d) in the case of a facility located over a soft bottom, the additional information that is specified in the Monitoring Standard concerning the seabed that is leased for the operations of the facility.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if an aquaculture facility commences operations during the 300 days after the day on which these Regulations come into force, the owner or operator of the facility must provide the information referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) to (d) within 30 days after the day on which the operations were commenced.

heading: Monitoring Standard
paragraph: (3) The studies undertaken to obtain the information referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) to (d) must be conducted in accordance with the Monitoring Standard.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (4) Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to an acquaculture facility whose aquaculture licence, if issued or granted, permits a maximum standing biomass of 2.5 t or less or a maximum annual production of 5 t or less.

heading: Applications affecting contours of footprint
paragraph: 9 (1) If the owner or operator of an aquaculture facility located in tidal waters that cultivates finfish makes an application under federal or provincial law that, if approved, would authorize any activity that is likely to increase the predicted contours of the footprint of the biochemical oxygen demanding matter deposited by the facility, the owner or the operator must conduct the studies necessary to obtain the information referred to in paragraphs 8(1)(a) to (d) and submit the information to the Minister within 30 days after the day on which the application was made.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to an acquaculture facility whose aquaculture licence, if amended, permits a maximum standing biomass of 2.5 t or less or a maximum annual production of 5 t or less.

heading: Substrate sampling and restocking
paragraph: 10 (1) In the case of an aquaculture facility that is located over a soft bottom and cultivates finfish in tidal waters in or adjacent to Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, British Columbia, Prince Edward Island or Newfoundland and Labrador, the owner or operator of the facility

heading: Substrate sampling and restocking
paragraph: (a) must take samples of the benthic substrate in the manner and at the times and locations specified in the Monitoring Standard and determine the concentration of free sulfide in the samples in accordance with that Standard;

heading: Substrate sampling and restocking
paragraph: (b) must take additional samples of the benthic substrate, in the manner and at the times and locations specified in the Monitoring Standard, if

heading: Substrate sampling and restocking
paragraph: (i) in the case of a facility located in tidal waters in or adjacent to Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island or Newfoundland and Labrador, the mean concentration of free sulfide as calculated at the locations specified in the Monitoring Standard exceeds 3000 µM, and

heading: Substrate sampling and restocking
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a facility located in tidal waters in or adjacent to British Columbia, the mean concentration of free sulfide as calculated at 30 m and 125 m from the structure that contains the cultivated fish exceeds 1300 µM and 700 µM, respectively; and

heading: Substrate sampling and restocking
paragraph: (c) must not restock the facility if the concentrations of free sulfide exceed the applicable concentration limits set out in paragraph (b).

heading: Visual monitoring instead of sampling
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of an acquaculture facility must conduct visual monitoring in accordance with section 11 instead of the sampling described in subsection (1) if the owner or the operator cannot obtain, from each of the locations specified in the Monitoring Standard, benthic substrate samples that

heading: Visual monitoring instead of sampling
paragraph: (a) contain substrate to a depth of at least 5 cm; and

heading: Visual monitoring instead of sampling
paragraph: (b) have a volume of at least 15 ml and undisturbed sediment-water interface.

heading: Visual monitoring of substrate
paragraph: 11 (1) This section applies to aquaculture facilities that cultivate finfish in the waters referred to in subsection 10(1) but

heading: Visual monitoring of substrate
paragraph: (a) are not located over a soft bottom; or

heading: Visual monitoring of substrate
paragraph: (b) are located over a soft bottom in respect of which subsection 10(2) applies.

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of a facility referred to in subsection (1)

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (a) must conduct visual monitoring of the benthic substrate in the manner and at the times and locations specified in the Monitoring Standard;

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (b) must not, if the facility is located in tidal waters in or adjacent to Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island or Newfoundland and Labrador, restock the facility if the visual monitoring shows the presence of Beggiatoa species or similar bacteria, marine worms or barren substrate in more than 70% of the locations specified in the Monitoring Standard; and

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (c) must not, if the facility is located in tidal waters in or adjacent to British Columbia, restock the facility if visual monitoring shows that Beggiatoa species or similar bacteria or marine worms cover

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (i) 10% or more of any four segments of substrate specified in the Monitoring Standard that are within 100 m to 124 m from the fish containment structure, or

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (ii) 10% or more of

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (A) the two contiguous segments of substrate specified in the Monitoring Standard that are within 116 m to 124 m from the fish containment structure, and

heading: Monitoring and restocking
paragraph: (B) the two or more contiguous segments of substrate specified in the Monitoring Standard that are within 124 m to 140 m from the fish containment structure.

heading: Notification of Minister
paragraph: 12 (1) The owner or operator of an aquaculture facility that cultivates finfish that is located in tidal waters in or adjacent to Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island or Newfoundland and Labrador must notify the Minister if the following occurs:

heading: Notification of Minister
paragraph: (a) the concentration limits set out in subparagraph 10(1)(b)(i) are exceeded; or

heading: Notification of Minister
paragraph: (b) Beggiatoa species or similar bacteria, marine worms or barren substrate are present to the extent referred to in paragraph 11(2)(b).

heading: Notification - British Columbia facilities
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of an aquaculture facility that cultivates finfish that is located in tidal waters in or adjacent to British Columbia must notify the Minister if the following occurs:

heading: Notification - British Columbia facilities
paragraph: (a) the concentration limits set out in subparagraph 10(1)(b)(ii) are exceeded; or

heading: Notification - British Columbia facilities
paragraph: (b) Beggiatoa species or similar bacteria or marine worms are present to the extent referred to in paragraph 11(2)(c).

heading: Time for notification
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of an acquaculture facility that cultivates finfish that is located in tidal waters must notify the Minister within 14 days after the day on which the samples of the substrate were taken or the visual monitoring conducted, as the case may be.

heading: Fish morbidity or mortality
paragraph: 13 (1) If fish morbidity or mortality outside the aquaculture facility is observed from any part of the facility within 96 hours after the deposit of any drug or pest control product referred to in paragraph 2(a) or (b), the owner or operator of the facility must immediately notify a fishery officer of

heading: Fish morbidity or mortality
paragraph: (a) the name of the facility and its operator;

heading: Fish morbidity or mortality
paragraph: (b) the geographic coordinates of the fish observed;

heading: Fish morbidity or mortality
paragraph: (c) the estimated number and, if known, species of the fish observed; and

heading: Fish morbidity or mortality
paragraph: (d) the product name of the drug or pest control product deposited and the date of the deposit.

heading: Minister's directions
paragraph: (2) If the owner or operator of an acquaculture facility is directed by the Minister to undertake measures under subsection 36(6) of the Act, and the Minister advises the owner or the operator that the direction is related to a notification made by them under subsection (1), the owner or the operator must cease depositing the drug or pest control product referred to in subsection (1) until they have complied with the Minister's directions.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: 14 The owner or operator of an acquaculture facility must submit an annual report to the Minister, and retain a copy of it, in accordance with section 16.

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: 15 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 35(2)(a) of the Act,

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (a) the following works, undertakings and activities are prescribed:

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (i) the installation, operation, maintenance or removal of an aquaculture facility, and

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (ii) measures to control biofouling or the presence of fish pathogens or pests in the aquaculture facility; and

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (b) the following conditions are prescribed for the carrying on of those works, undertakings and activities:

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (i) the aquaculture facility is operated under an aquaculture licence,

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (ii) the owner or operator of the facility takes reasonable measures to mitigate the risk of serious harm to fish outside the facility that are part of a commercial, recreational or Aboriginal fishery, having regard to

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (A) the effectiveness of the available measures,

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (B) the degree of serious harm that may result from the carrying on of the works, undertakings and activities, and

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (C) the physical characteristics of the facility and the type of aquaculture that is engaged in at the facility, and

heading: Prescribed works, undertakings, activities and conditions
paragraph: (iii) the owner or operator submits an annual report to the Minister in accordance with section 16.

heading: Exception - deleterious substances
paragraph: (2) The deposit of deleterious substances is not prescribed for the purpose of paragraph (1)(a).

heading: Exception - Pacific Aquaculture Regulations
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to any work, undertaking or activity carried on in any waters or place referred to in section 2 of the Pacific Aquaculture Regulations.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: 16 (1) An annual report must be submitted in a form acceptable to the Minister and contain the following information in respect of the operation of the aquaculture facility during the calendar year:

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) for each deposit of a drug or pest control product during the year,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (i) the product name of the drug or pest control product or the common chemical names of its active ingredients,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (ii) the purpose of the deposit,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (iii) the date, quantity and geographic coordinates of the deposit, and

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (iv) the record of consideration of alternatives referred to in paragraph 5(c) or 6(c);

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) a description of any measures taken under paragraph 5(b), section 7 and subparagraph 15(1)(b)(ii);

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (c) in the case of a facility referred to in section 10,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (i) the concentrations of free sulfide referred to in subsection 10(1), or

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (ii) if visual monitoring is required under subsection 10(2), the visual monitoring data collected; and

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (d) if a fishery officer was notified of fish morbidity or mortality in accordance with subsection 13(1), the information provided to the officer.

heading: Due date of report
paragraph: (2) An annual report must be submitted to the Minister on or before April 1 of the year following the year that is the subject of the report.

heading: Copy of report to be retained
paragraph: (3) An owner or operator of an aquaculture facility must retain a copy of the annual report in the facility for a period of two years after the day on which it is submitted to the Minister.

heading: Information prior to coming into force
paragraph: (4) For greater certainty, an owner or operator of an aquaculture facility is not required to include information in an annual report in respect of any period before the day on which these Regulations come into force.

heading: Paragraph 35(2)(a) of Act
paragraph: 17 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 35(2)(a) of the Act, the disposal of fish by the President of the Canadian Food Inspection Agency for the purposes of fish pathogen or pest control and the Health of Animals Act is prescribed.

heading: Deposit of deleterious substance
paragraph: (2) The President of the Canadian Food Inspection Agency may, for the purposes of fish pathogen or pest control and the Health of Animals Act, deposit a deleterious substance referred to in paragraph 2(a) or (b) in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act.

heading: Registration
paragraph: 18 These Regulations come into force on the day on which they are registered.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Fisheries Act. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aquatic invasive species means a species set out in Part 2 or 3 of the schedule. (espece aquatique envahissante)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: indigenous, in respect of an aquatic species, means that the species originated naturally in a particular region or body of water. (indigene)

heading: List of aquatic invasive species
paragraph: 2 For the purpose of subsection 43(3) of the Act, the list of aquatic invasive species is the list set out in Parts 2 and 3 of the schedule.

heading: Estimate of costs
paragraph: 3 Before publishing proposed regulations made under subsection 43(3) of the Act, the Minister must provide the President of the Treasury Board with an estimate of the costs of their implementation.

heading: Designation of species
paragraph: 4 A reference in these Regulations to an aquatic invasive species or family of aquatic invasive species by its common name as set out in column 1 in Part 2 or 3 of the schedule is to be read as a reference to the scientific name of that species or family of species that is set out in column 2.

heading: Inconsistency with other regulations
paragraph: 5 In the event of an inconsistency between these Regulations and any other regulations made under the Act, these Regulations prevail to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Prohibition against importation
paragraph: 6 It is prohibited for any person to import members of a species set out in Part 2 of the schedule, including any genetic material capable of propagating the species, into the applicable area set out in column 4 of that Part, unless the member is in the condition, if any, set out in column 3.

heading: Prohibition against possession
paragraph: 7 It is prohibited for any person to possess members of a species set out in Part 2 of the schedule, including any genetic material capable of propagating the species, within the applicable area set out in column 5 of that Part, unless the member is in the condition, if any, set out in column 3.

heading: Prohibition against transportation
paragraph: 8 It is prohibited for any person to transport members of a species set out in Part 2 of the schedule, including any genetic material capable of propagating the species, within the applicable area set out in column 6 of that Part, unless the member is in the condition, if any, set out in column 3.

heading: Prohibition against release
paragraph: 9 It is prohibited for any person to release, or engage in any activity that may lead to the release of, members of a species set out in Part 2 of the schedule, including any genetic material capable of propagating the species, into a body of water frequented by fish within the applicable area set out in column 7 of that Part, unless the member is in the condition, if any, set out in column 3.

heading: Prohibition against introduction of non-indigenous species
paragraph: 10 It is prohibited for any person to introduce an aquatic species into a particular region or body of water frequented by fish where it is not indigenous unless authorized to do so under federal or provincial law.

heading: Exemption for certain persons
paragraph: 11 Sections 6 to 9 do not apply to fishery officers or fishery guardians carrying out their duties under these Regulations or to any other person acting under their direction.

heading: Exemption for emergencies
paragraph: 12 Sections 6 to 10 do not apply to persons operating any vehicles, vessels or aircraft engaged in emergency, search and rescue or firefighting operations.

heading: Exemption for authorized purposes
paragraph: 13 (1) If the purpose of the importation, possession, transportation or release of members of a species set out in Part 2 of the schedule is for scientific, educational or aquatic invasive species control purposes, sections 6 to 9 do not apply

heading: Exemption for authorized purposes
paragraph: (a) to employees or any other person acting under the direction of

heading: Exemption for authorized purposes
paragraph: (i) an educational institution,

heading: Exemption for authorized purposes
paragraph: (ii) a research facility,

heading: Exemption for authorized purposes
paragraph: (iii) a zoo or aquarium, or

heading: Exemption for authorized purposes
paragraph: (iv) a federal or provincial department with a mandate to manage or control aquatic invasive species; and

heading: Exemption for authorized purposes
paragraph: (b) to persons engaged in the activities authorized under subsection 19(3).

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (2) The employees or persons exempted under subparagraphs (1)(a)(i) to (iii) must hold the applicable permits, licences and authorizations issued under the following provisions:

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (a) section 6.1 of the Manitoba Fishery Regulations, 1987;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (b) section 19 of the Quebec Fishery Regulations, 1990;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (c) sections 52 and 56 of the Fishery (General) Regulations;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (d) subsection 9(3) of the Saskatchewan Fishery Regulations, 1995;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (e) subsection 6(2) of the Ontario Fishery Regulations, 2007;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (f) sections 34.1 and 34.2 of Fish Licensing of Ontario, O. Reg. 664/98;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (g) subsection 3(1) of the Fishing Licensing Regulation of Manitoba, Man. Reg. 124/97;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (h) section 3 of the Freshwater Fish Regulation of British Columbia, B.C. Reg. 261/83;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (i) subsection 88(3) and section 88.1 of The Fisheries Regulations of Saskatchewan, R.R.S. c. F-16.1 Reg. 1;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (j) subsection 12(1) of the Fisheries (Alberta) Act of Alberta, R.S.A. 2000, c. F-16;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (k) section 86 of the Wild Life Regulations of Newfoundland and Labrador, C.N.L.R. 1156/96;

heading: Permit, licence or authorization required
paragraph: (l) all applicable provisions in regulations made under the Canada National Parks Act.

heading: Exemption for licence holder
paragraph: 14 Section 7 does not apply to a person holding a fishing licence who has caught a member of a species set out in Part 2 of the schedule if that person takes immediate measures to destroy the member in a manner that ensures that it and any genetic material capable of propagating the species cannot survive.

heading: Exemption - certain diploid grass carp
paragraph: 15 (1) Section 7 does not apply, in respect of the possession of diploid grass carp, to persons employed by the Aquaculture Centre of Excellence at Lethbridge College and Alberta Agriculture and Rural Development, or persons under their direction, if they hold a fish research licence issued under subsection 12(1) of the Fisheries (Alberta) Act of Alberta and if the diploid grass carp are possessed for the purpose of culturing triploid grass carp.

heading: Exemption - triploid grass carp
paragraph: (2) Sections 7 and 8 do not apply, in respect of the possession and transportation of triploid grass carp, to persons holding a cultured fish licence issued under subsection 12(1) of the Fisheries (Alberta) Act of Alberta.

heading: Exemption for holder of cultured fish licence
paragraph: 16 Section 9 does not apply to persons holding a cultured fish licence issued under subsection 12(1) of the Fisheries (Alberta) Act of Alberta in respect of the release of grass carp - that have been confirmed as triploid grass carp - for the purpose of vegetation control, in a body of water on privately owned land that is isolated from other bodies of water in a manner that ensures that the grass carp will not adversely affect - in any other body of water - other fish, fish habitat or the use of fish.

heading: Exemption if otherwise regulated

paragraph: (2) A person must give all reasonable assistance requested by the fishery officer or the fishery guardian to enable them to carry out the measures set out in subsection (1) and must provide any information requested by them that is relevant to the measures if the person

paragraph: (3) If a direction given under subsection (1) requires a person to be in possession of or to transport a member of a species set out in Part 2 of the schedule, that person is exempted from sections 7 and 8 to the extent necessary to fulfill the requirements of the direction.

paragraph: (c) in the case of a non-emergency situation in which the measure or direction may have a significant impact on activities under the jurisdiction of a department or agency of the Government of Canada or the government of any province or municipality, the Minister, the fishery officer or the fishery guardian has notified that department, agency or government.

paragraph: (a) an estimate of the total assessed value of each property class in the municipality, the treaty lands of the treaty first nation or Nisga'a Lands, as applicable, and
