paragraph: (b) for each property class specified for the purpose of this section by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, estimates of the distribution of value changes that have occurred in the property class in the municipality, the treaty lands or Nisga'a Lands, as applicable, since the previous revised assessment roll and the completion of any supplementary roll.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph:
3
		  (1) On or before December 31 of each year, the assessor must

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (a) complete a new assessment roll containing a list of each property that is in a municipality, the treaty lands of a treaty first nation, Nisga'a Lands or another rural area and that is liable to assessment, and

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (2.2), deliver an assessment notice to each person named in the assessment roll.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (2) Subject to this Act, an assessment roll completed under subsection (1) is the assessment roll for the purpose of taxation during the calendar year following completion of that roll.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (2.1) In relation to property in the treaty lands of a treaty first nation or Nisga'a Lands, an assessment roll completed under subsection (1) is the assessment roll

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (a) for the purpose of taxation, during the calendar year following completion of that roll,

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (i)  by the treaty first nation, if the treaty first nation has adopted this Act and the regulations, in their entirety and as amended from time to time, for the purposes of valuing and classifying interests in real property within its treaty lands, or

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (ii)  by the Nisga'a Lisims Government, if the Nisga'a Lisims Government has adopted this Act and the regulations, in their entirety and as amended from time to time, for the purposes of valuing and classifying interests in real property within Nisga'a Lands, and

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of requisitioning the treaty first nation or Nisga'a Nation during that calendar year.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (2.2) The requirement in subsection (1) (b) to deliver an assessment notice to each person named in the assessment roll does not apply in relation to an assessment roll prepared for the purpose of requisitioning a treaty first nation or the Nisga'a Nation.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (3) The assessment roll and assessment notice must be in the form and contain the information specified by regulations made under the Assessment Authority Act.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (4) When completing an assessment roll, the assessor must use the information contained in the records of the land title office as those records stood on November 30 of the year in which the assessment roll is completed.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (5) In the case of a parcel of land for which a land title office description is not available, the assessor must use the best description available to the assessor.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (6) The assessor must exercise reasonable care in obtaining and setting down the address of an owner, and must more particularly adopt the following alternatives in the order named:

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (a) the address known to the assessor;

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (b) the address as it appears in the application for registration or otherwise in the land title office.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (7) If the address of the owner is not known to the assessor and is not recorded in the land title office, the assessor must,

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (a) in the case of a city, town or village municipality, set down the address of the owner as the main post office, and

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (b) in the case of a district municipality, the treaty lands of a treaty first nation, Nisga'a Lands or another rural area, set down the address of an owner as the post office located nearest the land in question.

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (8) An assessment notice required under subsection (1) (b) to be delivered must be delivered to the person named in the assessment roll

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (a) by mail at the address on the assessment roll, or

heading: Completion of assessment roll
paragraph: (b) by electronic transmission, if the person provides authorization under section 65.1 (1) (a), using the email address provided under section 65.1 (2).

heading: Request for copy of assessment notice
paragraph: 4		  (1) A holder of a registered charge may, at any time, give notice, with full particulars of the nature, extent, and duration of the charge, to the assessor and request copies of all assessment and tax notices issued during the duration of the charge.

heading: Request for copy of assessment notice
paragraph: (2) The assessor to whom a notice and request is given under subsection (1) must enter the holder's name and address on the assessment roll.

heading: Request for copy of assessment notice
paragraph: (3) The fee required under section 6 (5) does not apply in respect of a request under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Splitting and grouping of parcels
paragraph:
5
		  (1) Without limiting subsection (2), if a building or other improvement extends over more than one parcel of land, those parcels, if contiguous, may be treated by the assessor as one parcel and assessed accordingly.

heading: Splitting and grouping of parcels
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 20.2, parcels of land and parts of parcels of land may be treated by the assessor as one parcel and assessed accordingly.

heading: Assessment notice
paragraph:
6
		  (1) Any number of parcels of land assessed in the name of the same owner may be included in one assessment notice.

heading: Assessment notice
paragraph: (2) If several parcels of land are assessed in the name of the same owner at the same value, the assessment notice is sufficient if it clearly identifies the property assessed, setting it out as a block, parts of a block or as a series of lots, without giving in full the description of each parcel as it appears in the assessment roll.

heading: Assessment notice
paragraph: (3) Despite section 3, if property is wholly exempt from taxation, the assessor need not deliver an assessment notice in respect of that property.

heading: Assessment notice
paragraph: (5) An assessor must provide, to any person who requests it and pays the prescribed fee, the information contained in the current assessment notice delivered by the assessor under section 3.

heading: Assessment notice
paragraph: (6) In subsection (7), "lessee" means a lessee holding property under a lease or sublease, other than a registered lease or registered sublease, for a term of one year or more.

heading: Assessment notice
paragraph: (7) After receiving an assessment notice for a property included in a class specified for the purpose of this subsection by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the owner of the property must, on request by a lessee of all or part of the property, promptly deliver a copy of the notice to the lessee.

heading: Providing assessment rolls
paragraph: (2) The assessor must provide the following, as soon as they become available, to the appropriate municipality, regional district or treaty first nation and to the Nisga'a Nation:

heading: Providing assessment rolls
paragraph: (a) the assessment roll completed under section 3;

heading: Providing assessment rolls
paragraph: (b) the revised assessment roll;

heading: Providing assessment rolls
paragraph: (c) an amendment to the assessment roll ordered or directed under section 63 or 65 (10).

heading: Providing assessment rolls
paragraph: (3) Despite section 69 (1), the assessment rolls and amendments referred to in subsection (2) of this section must be provided to the appropriate municipality, regional district or treaty first nation, and to the Nisga'a Nation, free of charge.

heading: Assessment roll available for inspection
paragraph:
8
		  (1) An assessor must maintain the assessment roll for the geographic area assigned to that assessor by the board of directors of the assessment authority.

heading: Assessment roll available for inspection
paragraph: (2) The assessment roll referred to in subsection (1) must be

heading: Assessment roll available for inspection
paragraph: (a) available for public inspection during regular business hours at the office of that assessor, and

heading: Assessment roll available for inspection
paragraph: (b) in the format and presented in the manner prescribed by regulation.

heading: Certification
paragraph:
9
		  Upon completion of an assessment roll, the assessor must certify in writing that the assessment roll was completed in accordance with the requirements of this Act.

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph:
10
		  (1) In accordance with section 34, the assessor must notify a review panel of all errors or omissions in the assessment roll completed under section 3, except those errors or omissions corrected under subsection (2).

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (2) Before March 16 of the year following the completion of the assessment roll under section 3, the assessor may amend an individual entry in the completed assessment roll to correct an error or omission, with the consent of

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (a) the owner of the affected property, and

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (b) the complainant, if the complainant is not the owner of the affected property.

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1), the assessor must give notice to the review panel in respect of any of the following circumstances:

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (a) because of a change of ownership that occurs after November 30 and before the following January 1 and that is recorded in the records of the land title office before that January 1,

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (i)  land or improvements or both that were not previously liable to taxation become liable to taxation, or

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (ii)  land or improvements or both that were previously liable to taxation cease to be liable to taxation;

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (b) after October 31 and before the following January 1, a manufactured home is moved to a new location, substantially damaged or destroyed;

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (c) after October 31 and before the following January 1, a manufactured home is placed on land that has been assessed or the home is purchased by the owner of land that has been assessed;

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (c.1) improvements, other than a manufactured home, that are assessable under this Act

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (i)  are substantially damaged or destroyed after October 31 and before the following January 1, and

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (ii)  cannot reasonably be repaired or replaced before the following January 1;

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (d) after November 30 and before the following January 1, land or improvements or both are transferred to or from the British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority and the transfer is recorded in the records of the land title office before that January 1;

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (e) land or improvements or both that are owned by the British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority are held or occupied by another person, whose interest begins or ends after November 30 and before the following January 1;

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (f) land or improvements or both that are owned by the British Columbia Railway Company or by its subsidiary are held or occupied by another person, whose interest begins or ends after November 30 and before the following January 1;

heading: Errors and omissions in completed assessment roll
paragraph: (g) land or improvements or both that are referred to in section 26, 27 or 28 are held or occupied by a person other than the owner of the fee simple, and the interest of the holder or occupier begins or ends after November 30 and before the following January 1.

heading: Validity as confirmed by review panel
paragraph:
11
		  The revised assessment roll is, unless changed or amended under section 12, 63 or 65 (10),

heading: Validity as confirmed by review panel
paragraph: (a) valid and binding on all parties concerned, despite

heading: Validity as confirmed by review panel
paragraph: (i)  any omission, defect or error committed in, or with respect to, that assessment roll,

heading: Validity as confirmed by review panel
paragraph: (ii)  any defect, error or misstatement in any notice required, or

heading: Validity as confirmed by review panel
paragraph: (iii)  the omission to deliver the notice, and

heading: Validity as confirmed by review panel
paragraph: (b) for all purposes, the assessment roll of the municipality, treaty lands of the treaty first nation, Nisga'a Lands or other rural area, as applicable, until the next revised assessment roll.

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (2) If, after the completion of an assessment roll, the assessor finds that any property or any thing liable to assessment

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (a) was liable to assessment for the current year, but has not been assessed on the current roll, or

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (b) has been assessed for less than the amount for which it was liable to assessment,

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: the assessor must assess the property or thing on a supplementary roll, or further supplementary roll, subject to the conditions of assessment governing the current assessment roll on which the property or thing should have been assessed.

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (3) If, after the completion of an assessment roll, the assessor finds that any property or any thing liable to assessment

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (a) was liable to assessment for a previous year, but has not been assessed on the roll for that year, or

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (b) has been assessed in a previous year for less than the amount for which it was liable to assessment,

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: the assessor must assess the property or thing on a supplementary roll or further supplementary roll for that year, subject to the conditions of assessment governing the assessment roll on which the property or thing should have been assessed, but only if the failure to assess the property or thing, or the assessment for less than it was liable to be assessed, is attributable to

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (c) an owner's failure to disclose,

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (d) an owner's concealment of particulars relating to assessable property,

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (e) a person's failure to make a return, or

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (f) a person's making of an incorrect return,

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: required under this or any other Act.

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (4) Despite sections 10, 11 and 42, and in addition to supplementary assessments under subsections (2) and (3), the assessor may, at any time before December 31 of the year following completion of the assessment roll under section 3, correct errors and omissions in a completed assessment roll by means of entries in a supplementary assessment roll.

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (5) The assessor must not make a change or amendment that would be contrary to an amendment in the assessment roll ordered or directed by the board under section 63 or 65 (10).

heading: Supplementary roll
paragraph: (6) Nothing in subsection (2), (4) or (5) authorizes the preparation of a supplementary roll, or the correction of a roll, for the purpose of changing or updating an assessment roll later than 12 months after that assessment roll is completed.

heading: Provisions applicable to supplementary assessment roll
paragraph:
13
		  (1) The duties imposed on the assessor with respect to the annual assessment roll and the provisions of this Act relating to assessment rolls, so far as they are applicable, apply to supplementary assessment rolls.

heading: Provisions applicable to supplementary assessment roll
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a notice of complaint under section 33 in respect of a supplementary assessment roll, the assessor must

heading: Provisions applicable to supplementary assessment roll
paragraph: (a) record receipt of the notice, and

heading: Provisions applicable to supplementary assessment roll
paragraph: (b) if the complaint is not resolved under section 10 (2), ensure the complaint is brought before a review panel at the next sitting of review panels.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
13.1
		  In this Part, "authorized person" means any of the following:

heading: Definition
paragraph: (a) the assessor;

heading: Definition
paragraph: (b) an appraiser;

heading: Definition
paragraph: (c) any other employee of the assessment authority who is authorized by the assessment authority.

heading: Inspections and assessment powers
paragraph:
14
		  An authorized person may, for any purposes relating to assessment, enter into or on and inspect land and improvements.

heading: Return of information
paragraph: (2) At any time, an authorized person may by written notice require a person who owns, occupies or disposes of property to provide to the authorized person, within 21 days of the date on which the notice is sent or a longer period specified in the notice, information for any purpose related to the administration of this Act.

heading: Return of information
paragraph: (3) A person who does not provide information as required by notice under subsection (2) commits an offence.

heading: Return of information
paragraph: (4) An authorized person is not bound by the information provided, but may, if the authorized person has reason to doubt its accuracy, assess the property in the manner and for the amount the authorized person believes to be correct.

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph:
16
		  (1) An authorized person may enter on any premises and may examine any property

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (a) to determine an assessment of land and improvements, in respect of which the authorized person thinks a person may be liable to assessment, or

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (b) to confirm an assessment.

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (2) An authorized person must be given access to, and may examine and take copies of and extracts from, the books, accounts, vouchers, documents and appraisals of the person referred to in subsection (1), who must, on request, furnish every facility and assistance required for the entry and examination.

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (3) An authorized person, a member of a review panel, a member of the board or any other person who has custody or control of information or records obtained or created under this Act must not disclose the information or records to any other person except

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (a) in the course of administering this Act or performing functions under it,

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (b) in proceedings before a review panel, the board or a court of law,

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (c) in accordance with subsection (4), or

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (d) in accordance with a regulation under subsection (6).

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (4) An authorized person may disclose to the agent of a property owner confidential information relating to the property if the disclosure has been authorized in the prescribed form by the owner or, if a form has not been prescribed for the property class, authorized in writing by the owner.

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (5) An agent must not use information disclosed under subsection (4) except for the purposes authorized by the owner in the form or writing referred to in that subsection.

heading: Power to examine property and accounts
paragraph: (6) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the disclosure of information obtained or created under this Act, including, without limitation, information respecting the declared value, financing and physical characteristics of property.

heading: Assessor to be advised of sales, etc.
paragraph:
17
		  (1) If land of the Crown or treaty lands have been leased, granted or sold, the minister of the relevant ministry, or the representative designated by the treaty first nation by notice in writing to the assessment authority, as the case may be, must immediately advise the assessor of the assessment area in which the land is located, the name and address of the lessee, grantee or purchaser, the legal description, consideration and other details of the transfer.

heading: Assessor to be advised of sales, etc.
paragraph: (2) All public officers and officers and employees of Crown corporations and agencies, and individuals occupying similar positions with a treaty first nation or a public institution of a treaty first nation, must, on the written request of an authorized person, provide without fee all information as may be requested to complete assessments under this Act.

heading: Valuation and status dates
paragraph:
18
		  (1) For the purpose of determining the actual value of property for an assessment roll, the valuation date is July 1 of the year during which the assessment roll is completed.

heading: Valuation and status dates
paragraph: (2) The actual value of property for an assessment roll is to be determined as if on the valuation date

heading: Valuation and status dates
paragraph: (a) the property and all other properties were in the physical condition that they are in on October 31 following the valuation date, and

heading: Valuation and status dates
paragraph: (b) the permitted use of the property and of all other properties were the same as on October 31 following the valuation date.

heading: Valuation and status dates
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) (a) does not apply to property referred to in section 10 (3) (b), (c) or (c.1).

heading: Valuation and status dates
paragraph: (4) The actual value of property referred to in section 10 (3) (b), (c) or (c.1) for an assessment roll is to be determined as if on the valuation date the property was in the physical condition that it is in on December 31 following the valuation date.

heading: Property assessment
paragraph:
18.1
		  All land and improvements in British Columbia are liable to assessment under this Act unless exempted from assessment under this or another enactment.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph:
19
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: "accommodation unit" means a unit that is rented or offered for rent as overnight accommodation for periods of less than 28 days for at least the prescribed percentage of the 12-month period ending June 30 of the year previous to the taxation year for which the assessment roll is completed;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: "actual value" means the market value of the fee simple interest in land and improvements;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: "eligible residential property" means a parcel of land on which there are improvements if

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) the parcel does not exceed 2.03 ha in area, and

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) the improvements are designed to accommodate and are used only to accommodate no more than 3 families;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: "leasehold accommodation property" means a parcel of land or contiguous parcels of land on which there are buildings that

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) collectively include at least a prescribed number of leasehold units, and

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) do not consist of any strata lots;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: "leasehold unit" means an accommodation unit

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) that is leased for a term of at least a prescribed number of years, and

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) for which the lease is registered in the land title office;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: "strata accommodation property" means a strata lot in respect of which the following requirements are met:

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) the strata lot is in a strata plan that, with or without contiguous strata plans, includes 20 or more strata lots;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) the strata lot is rented or offered for rent as overnight accommodation for periods of less than 28 days for at least the prescribed percentage of the 12-month period ending June 30 of the year previous to the taxation year for which the assessment roll is completed.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (1.1) For the purposes of the definitions of "accommodation unit" and "strata accommodation property", an accommodation unit or a strata lot is not rented or offered for rent as overnight accommodation if the accommodation unit or strata lot is used or available for parking, storage or similar purposes or for commercial purposes other than overnight accommodation.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (2) The assessor must determine the actual value of land and improvements and must enter the actual value of the land and improvements in the assessment roll.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (3) In determining actual value, the assessor may, except where this Act has a different requirement, give consideration to the following:

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) present use;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) location;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (c) original cost;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (d) replacement cost;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (e) revenue or rental value;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (f) selling price of the land and improvements and comparable land and improvements;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (g) economic and functional obsolescence;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (h) any other circumstances affecting the value of the land and improvements.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (4) Without limiting the application of subsections (1) to (3), if an industrial or commercial undertaking, a business or a public utility enterprise is carried on, the land and improvements used by it must be valued as the property of a going concern.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (5) If the land and improvements are to be assessed under section 26, 27 or 28, the assessor must include in the factors that the assessor considers under subsection (3), any restriction placed on the use of the land and improvements by the owner of the fee.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (6) The duration of the interest of a holder or occupier of land and improvements referred to in subsection (5), or the right of the owner of the fee to terminate that interest, is not a restriction within the meaning of that subsection.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (7) In determining actual value, the assessor must give consideration to any terms or conditions contained, as applicable,

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) in a covenant registered under section 219 of the Land Title Act,

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) in a covenant or similar instrument registered under a law of a treaty first nation in the land registry office of the treaty first nation, or

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (c) in a covenant or similar instrument registered under a Nisga'a law in a Nisga'a land registry.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (7.1) Despite any provision of this Act, if a natural area exemption certificate under Part 7.1 of the Islands Trust Act applies to a parcel, the actual value of the parcel is deemed to be what it would be if

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) the protection covenant to which the natural area exemption certificate relates did not apply, and

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) no natural area exemption certificate was in effect.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (8) Despite any requirement of this section respecting actual value, if the assessor receives, on or before January 31 in any year, from the owner and occupier of eligible residential property, a notice in the form prescribed by the assessment authority that the owner and occupier owned and occupied the eligible residential property as the owner and occupier's principal place of residence during the entire 10 year period ending on the preceding October 31, the actual value of the eligible residential property, for the purpose of the assessment roll for the calendar year following that October 31, must be determined taking into consideration only the actual use of the land and improvements that comprise the eligible residential property and not taking into consideration any other use to which the land or improvements could be put.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (9) If eligible residential property is the subject of a notice referred to in subsection (8) and the eligible residential property is, during the lifetime of the owner and occupier, or by will or on an intestacy, transferred to the spouse of the owner and occupier, the notice continues to be a valid notice for the purposes of subsection (8), and the spouse to whom the property is transferred is deemed to have owned and occupied the eligible residential property as that spouse's principal place of residence for the period referred to in subsection (8) and may in subsequent years give the notice referred to in subsection (8) on that basis.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (10) Despite any requirement of this section respecting actual value, the actual value of land and improvements must be determined by taking into consideration the terms and conditions of any heritage protection of the property if, on October 31 following the valuation date under section 18, land and improvements, or a portion of the land and improvements, is

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) designated under section 9 of the Heritage Conservation Act,

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) designated under section 611 of the Local Government Act or section 593 of the Vancouver Charter,

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (c) included under section 614 (3) (b) of the Local Government Act in a schedule to an official community plan,

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (d) treaty lands designated under a law of the treaty first nation enacted for the purpose of conserving and protecting heritage sites and heritage objects, or

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (e) Nisga'a Lands designated under a Nisga'a law enacted for the purpose of conserving and protecting heritage sites and heritage objects.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (11) Despite this or any other Act, the assessor, unless ordered by the board of directors of the assessment authority, need not, in respect of land and improvements that are exempt from taxation,

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) assess the land and improvements, or

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) prepare an annual assessment roll.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (12) Despite this or any other Act, improvements designed, constructed or installed to provide emergency protection for persons or domestic animals in the event of an emergency within the meaning of the Emergency and Disaster Management Act are exempt from assessment.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (13) Land and improvements must be assessed at their actual value.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (14) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must prescribe classes of property for the purpose of administering property taxes and must define the types or uses of land or improvements, or both, to be included in each property class.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (14.01) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council prescribes supportive housing property as a class of property under subsection (14), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, designate eligible supportive housing property as included in the supportive housing property class for a taxation year rather than defining the types or uses of land or improvements to be included in that property class.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (14.02) A designation under subsection (14.01)

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) is to be by assessment roll number, and

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) applies to the property that is identified by the assessment roll number and that is used for the provision of supportive housing or for purposes ancillary to the provision of supportive housing.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (14.03) Subject to subsection (14.04), in order to be effective for a taxation year, a regulation under subsection (14.01) must be in force on or before October 31 in the preceding year.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (14.04) If eligible supportive housing property

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) is included on a supplementary roll under section 26 (5) (a), and

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (b) is designated under subsection (14.01) of this section,

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: the designation, regardless of when the regulation under subsection (14.01) comes into force, is effective for that portion of the taxation year on and after the date that the assessor made the entry on the supplementary roll.

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (14.1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a) prescribing a percentage for the purposes of the definition of "strata accommodation property";

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a.1) for the purposes of the definition of "accommodation unit", prescribing a percentage;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a.2) for the purposes of the definition of "leasehold accommodation property", prescribing a number of leasehold units;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment
paragraph: (a.3) for the purposes of the definition of "leasehold unit", prescribing a number of years;

heading: Valuation for purposes of assessment

paragraph: 19.1		  (1) Despite the regulations under section 19, the assessor must classify a strata lot as being in the class 1 property class if

heading: Continued classification of strata lot in class 1

heading: Classification of treaty lands or Nisga'a Lands in supportive housing class
paragraph:

heading: Classification of treaty lands or Nisga'a Lands in supportive housing class

heading: Classification of treaty lands or Nisga'a Lands in supportive housing class

heading: Classification of treaty lands or Nisga'a Lands in supportive housing class

heading: Classification of treaty lands or Nisga'a Lands in supportive housing class
paragraph: (b) the property is used for the provision of supportive housing or for purposes ancillary to the provision of supportive housing;

heading: Classification of treaty lands or Nisga'a Lands in supportive housing class

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph:
20
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: "cost of industrial improvement" means the cost of replacing an existing industrial improvement with an improvement that

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) has the same area and volume as the existing industrial improvement,

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) serves the same function that the existing industrial improvement was designed for or, if the existing industrial improvement is no longer used for that function, serves the same function that the existing industrial improvement now serves, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (c) is constructed using current, generally accepted construction techniques and materials for the type of improvement being constructed;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: "eligible major industry property" means land and improvements that comprise property of the class described in subsection (3), or a portion of land and improvements that comprise that property, the actual value of which is directly affected by a local government's adoption of an official community plan under the Local Government Act;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: "industrial improvement", subject to subsection (2), means an improvement that is part of a plant, whether or not the plant can be operated as a going concern or is temporarily or permanently unprofitable, if the plant is designed and built for the purpose of one or more of the following:

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) mining, extracting, beneficiating or milling of metallic or non-metallic ore;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) mining, breaking, washing, grading or beneficiating of coal;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (c) producing of aluminum;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (d) smelting or refining of metal from ore or ore concentrate;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (e) producing, manufacturing, processing or refining of petroleum or natural gas;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (f) manufacturing of lumber or other sawmill and planing mill products;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (g) manufacturing of wood veneer, plywood, particle board, wafer board, hardboard and similar products;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (h) manufacturing of gypsum board;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (i) manufacturing of pulp, paper or linerboard;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (j) manufacturing of chemicals;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (k) manufacturing of chemical fertilizer;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (l) manufacturing of synthetic resins or the compounding of synthetic resins into moulding compounds;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (m) manufacturing of cement;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (n) manufacturing of insulation;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (o) manufacturing sheet glass or glass bottles;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (p) building, refitting or repairing ships;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (q) loading cargo onto sea-going ships or barges, and associated cargo storage and loading facilities, including grain elevators;

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: "relevant year", in relation to eligible major industry property, means the year in which the official community plan described in the definition of "eligible major industry property" was adopted in respect of the property.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may exempt from the definition of "industrial improvement" improvements in a plant or class of plant that has less than a prescribed capacity and may prescribe different capacities for different types of plants.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (3) Despite section 19, there is continued a class of properties consisting of

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) land used in conjunction with the operation of industrial improvements, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) industrial improvements.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (4) The actual value of properties to which this section applies is

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) the actual value of the land as determined under section 19 or 20.3, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) the cost of industrial improvements less depreciation that is at a rate and applied in a manner prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, and the Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe different rates and different manners of application of depreciation for individual properties or classes or types of properties.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of the definition of "cost of industrial improvement" in subsection (1), subject to the prior approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the assessment authority by order may establish or adopt by reference manuals establishing rates, formulas, rules or principles for the calculation of the cost of replacing an existing industrial improvement described in that definition.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (5.1) Copies, in print or electronic format, of the manuals established or adopted under subsection (5) must be

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) kept at the offices of the assessment authority, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) made available for public inspection at those offices during normal office hours.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (6) If, for the year 2000 and subsequent taxation years, in the opinion of the Lieutenant Governor in Council the assessed values for a class of plant are substantially different in a taxation year than they were in the previous taxation year, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, order that the changes in assessed values be phased in by the assessment authority as directed in the regulation.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of subsection (6), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations specifying classes of plants for which changes in assessed values are to be phased in over a period of up to 3 years and for that purpose may make regulations

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) prescribing the manner in which the changes in assessed values are to be phased in, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) prescribing different rates and different periods of time for the phasing in of changes in assessed values for different classes of plants.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (8) Despite sections 18 (2) and 19 respecting actual value, but subject to subsections (9) and (12) of this section, if the assessor receives, on or before December 31 in the relevant year, from the owner and occupier of eligible major industry property, a notice in the form prescribed by the assessment authority that, during the 2 taxation years following the relevant year, the owner and occupier intends

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) to operate the industrial improvements on the eligible major industry property as a going concern, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) to use the eligible major industry property for the same purpose and at an equivalent or greater level of production as at the time the notice is given,

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: the actual value of the eligible major industry property, for the purpose of the assessment roll for the 2 taxation years following the relevant year, must be determined by taking into consideration only the actual use of the land and improvements that comprise the eligible major industry property and not taking into consideration any other use to which the land or improvements could be put.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (9) If, after completing an assessment roll for a taxation year referred to in subsection (8), the assessor determines that, at any time before December 31 in that year, the operation or use of eligible major industry property for which notice was given under that subsection is not consistent with the operation or use described in the notice, the assessor must

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) determine the actual value of the eligible major industry property in accordance with subsection (4), and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) reassess the eligible major industry property by means of an entry on a supplementary assessment roll.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (10) If, on or before October 31 in the later of the 2 taxation years referred to in subsection (8), the assessor receives, from the owner and occupier of eligible major industry property for which notice was given under that subsection, a notice in the form prescribed by the assessment authority that, during one or more subsequent taxation years, the owner and occupier intends

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) to operate the industrial improvements on the eligible major industry property as a going concern, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) to use the eligible major industry property for the same purpose and at an equivalent or greater level of production as at the time notice was given under subsection (8),

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: the Lieutenant Governor in Council, by order made on or before December 31 in the later of the 2 taxation years referred to in subsection (8), may extend the application of that subsection to the eligible major industry property for one or more subsequent taxation years, as specified in the order.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (11) If an order is made under subsection (10) in respect of eligible major industry property for a taxation year,

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (a) despite sections 18 (2) and 19 respecting actual value, but subject to paragraph (b) of this subsection, the actual value of the eligible major industry property for the purpose of the assessment roll for the taxation year must be determined in accordance with subsection (8) of this section, and

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (b) subsection (9) applies in relation to the eligible major industry property for the taxation year.

heading: Major industry valuation
paragraph: (12) Notice may be provided under subsection (8) or (10) only once in relation to an eligible major industry property.

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: 20.1		  (1) In this section:

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: "dam" means any structure designed and built to control or store water flowing in a water course for the purposes of, or for purposes ancillary to, generating electricity;

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: "power plant" means any structure designed and built to

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (a) contain boilers, turbines or compressors for the purposes of, or for purposes ancillary to, generating electricity, or

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (b) support, contain or have affixed to it components that convert sunlight into electricity, either directly or indirectly, if the primary purpose of the structure is for use in the business of generating electricity;

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: "substation" means a facility at which electric current is switched, transformed or converted

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (a) at a dam or a power plant,

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (b) between a power plant and a transmission system, or

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (c) between a transmission system and a distribution network.

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (2) This section applies to properties where there is a dam, power plant or substation, other than properties to which section 20 applies.

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (3) Despite any other section of this Act, the actual value of a property to which this section applies is

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (a) the actual value of the land as determined under section 19 or 20.3, and

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (b) the cost of

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (i)  the dams, power plants and substations on the property, and

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (ii)  any other improvements on the property, except those exempted under subsection (4.1),

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: determined in accordance with the manuals described in subsection (4) of this section, less depreciation determined in accordance with the rates and applied in the manner prescribed under subsection (4.1) of this section.

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this section, subject to the prior approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the assessment authority by order may establish or adopt by reference manuals establishing rates, formulas, rules or principles for the calculation of cost.

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (4.1) For the purposes of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (a) excluding from the definition of "improvements" any category or type of thing used in the generation of electricity at a power plant, and

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (b) prescribing depreciation rates and principles for the application of depreciation.

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (5) Orders under subsection (4) and regulations under subsection (4.1) (b) may be different for individual properties or properties with different categories of dams, power plants and substations.

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (6) Copies, in print or electronic format, of the manuals established or adopted by order under subsection (4) must be

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (a) kept at the offices of the assessment authority, and

heading: Special valuation rules for dams, power plants and substations
paragraph: (b) made available for public inspection at those offices during normal office hours.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph:
20.2
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: "designated ski hill property" means eligible property that is designated under subsection (4) (a);

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: "eligible property" means land identified by a specific assessment roll number, and any improvements on that land, if the following apply to the property:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (a) in the case of land on which there are improvements, all the improvements are recreational improvements;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (b) in the case of land on which there are no improvements, the land is necessarily incidental to the provision of recreational activities on a ski hill;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: "recreational improvements" means improvements used to provide recreational activities on a ski hill, including

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (a) lifts, tows, day-use facilities, parking facilities, trails, snowmaking piping, surfaced pathways, service roads or other facilities or works, and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (b) utilities that support the facilities or works referred to in paragraph (a) and that are not assessed as property in class 2 under the Prescribed Classes of Property Regulation.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (2) The actual value of designated ski hill property is the actual value as determined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of entry on the assessment roll, the actual value by classification of land and improvements that are designated ski hill property is the actual value of the designated ski hill property apportioned to the land and improvements in each property class in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (a) designating eligible property as ski hill property;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (b) establishing rates, formulas, rules or principles for determining the actual value of designated ski hill property;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (c) respecting the apportionment of the actual value of designated ski hill property between property classes and between land and improvements for the purposes of entry on the assessment roll.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (5) A designation under subsection (4) (a)

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (a) is to be by assessment roll number, and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (b) applies to the land identified by the assessment roll number and to all improvements on that land, whether the improvements were on the land at the date of designation or added later.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (6) In order to be effective for a taxation year, a regulation under subsection (4) (a) must be in force on or before October 31 in the preceding year.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (7) Without limiting subsection (4) (b), regulations made under that subsection may do one or more of the following:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (a) determine actual value based in whole or in part on revenue relating to the designated ski hill property;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (b) treat designated ski hill properties as one designated ski hill property for the purposes of determining actual value and provide for the apportionment of the actual value between the designated ski hill properties;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (c) in determining actual value, provide for adjustments in respect of fluctuating revenues or actual value over a specified period.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (8) In making regulations under this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may do one or both of the following:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (a) define classes of designated ski hill properties;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated ski hill property
paragraph: (b) make different regulations for different designated ski hill properties or for different classes defined under paragraph (a).

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph:
20.3
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: "designated port land" means land that

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (a) is designated under subsection (3) (a), and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (b) is assessed as property in the class referred to in section 20 (3);

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: "eligible port land" means land identified by a specific assessment roll number if the following apply to that land and the improvements on that land:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (a) the land is located next to a navigable waterway;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (b) the land and the improvements on that land are assessed, in whole or in part, as property in the class referred to in section 20 (3);

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (c) the land and improvements on that land

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (i)  include one or more improvements that are assessed as property in the class referred to in section 20 (3) by reason of being industrial improvements within the meaning of paragraph (q) [sea-going cargo loading and storage] of the definition of "industrial improvement" in section 20 (1), or

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land

paragraph: (e) the improvements referred to in paragraph (c) (i) are not primarily used or held for the purpose of the transport of products from an industrial production or processing facility that is on the land or is near that land, or for purposes that are ancillary to that transport.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (2) The actual value of designated port land is the actual value as determined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (a) designating land that is eligible port land on the date of designation;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (b) prescribing the actual value of designated port land;

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (c) establishing rates, formulas, rules or principles for determining the actual value of designated port land.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (4) A designation under subsection (3) (a)

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (a) is to be by assessment roll number as at a date specified in the regulation, and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (b) applies to the land that

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (i)  is identified by the assessment roll number, and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (ii)  is assessed as property in the class referred to in section 20 (3).

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (6) Despite section 74 (5), if land

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (a) is included on a supplementary roll under section 26 (5) (a), and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (b) is designated under subsection (3) (a) of this section,

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: the designation, regardless of when the regulation under subsection (3) (a) comes into force, is effective for that portion of the taxation year on and after the date that the assessor made the entry on the supplementary roll.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (6.1) Despite section 74 (5), if

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (a) an entry is made on a supplementary roll under section 26 (5) (b) with respect to land that is designated under subsection (3) (a) of this section, and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (b) the Lieutenant Governor in Council rescinds the designation,

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: the rescission, regardless of when the regulation rescinding the designation comes into force, is effective for that portion of the taxation year on and after the date that the assessor made the entry on the supplementary roll.

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (7) Without limiting subsection (3) (c), in making regulations under that subsection, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide for

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (a) the use of a consumer price index published by Statistics Canada under the Statistics Act (Canada), and

heading: Special valuation rules for designated port land
paragraph: (b) any matters respecting the use of a consumer price index.

heading: Special valuation rules for supportive housing property
paragraph: 20.4		  (1) Despite any other section of this Act, the actual value of a property in the supportive housing property class is the actual value otherwise determined under this Act reduced by an amount established by the Lieutenant Governor in Council by regulation.

heading: Special valuation rules for supportive housing property
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Special valuation rules for supportive housing property
paragraph: (a) establishing the amount for the purposes of subsection (1);

heading: Special valuation rules for supportive housing property
paragraph: (b) establishing rates, formulas, rules or principles for determining the amount for the purposes of subsection (1);

heading: Special valuation rules for supportive housing property
paragraph: (c) respecting the apportionment of the actual value of property in the supportive housing property class between land and improvements for the purposes of entry on the assessment roll.

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph:
20.5
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: "designated restricted-use property" means eligible property that is designated under subsection (4) (a);

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (a) that is used by an eligible person, and

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (b) that is either

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (i)  to be assessed under section 26, 27 or 28, or

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (2) The actual value of designated restricted-use property is the actual value as determined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of entry on the assessment roll, the actual value by classification of land and improvements that are designated restricted-use property is the actual value of the designated restricted-use property apportioned to the land and improvements in each property class in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (a) designating eligible property as restricted-use property;

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (d) establishing rates, formulas, rules or principles for determining the actual value of designated restricted-use property;

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (e) respecting the apportionment of the actual value of designated restricted-use property between property classes and between land and improvements for the purposes of entry on the assessment roll.

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (5) A designation under subsection (4) (a)

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (a) is to be by assessment roll number, and

paragraph: (b) applies to the property identified by the assessment roll number.

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (6) Despite section 74 (5), if property

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (a) is included on a supplementary roll under section 26 (5) (a), and

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (b) is designated under subsection (4) (a) of this section,

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
paragraph: (a) an entry is made on a supplementary roll under section 26 (5) (b) with respect to property that is designated under subsection (4) (a) of this section, and

paragraph: (8) Without limiting subsection (4) (c) or (d), regulations made under that subsection may do one or both of the following:

heading: Special valuation rules for restricted-use property
