heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: 21		  (1) The actual value of the following must be determined using rates prescribed by the assessment authority:

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) the pole lines, metallic or fibre optic cables, towers, poles, wires, transformers, conduits and mains of a telecommunications, trolley coach, bus or electrical power corporation, but not including substations;

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) the track in place of a railway corporation, whether the track is on a public highway or on a privately owned right of way;

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (c) the pipe lines of a pipe line corporation for the transportation of petroleum, petroleum products or natural gas, including valves, cleanouts, fastenings, and appurtenances located on the right of way, but not including distribution pipelines, pumping equipment, compressor equipment, storage tanks and buildings;

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (d) the right of way for pole lines, cables, towers, poles, wires, transformers, conduits, mains and pipe lines referred to in paragraphs (a) and  (c);

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (e) the right of way for track referred to in paragraph (b).

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (2) In prescribing rates respecting improvements referred to in subsection (1) (a) to (c), the assessment authority

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) must base the rates on the average current cost of the existing improvements,

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) may, within the rates, make an allowance for physical depreciation,

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b.1) may, within the rates, make an allowance for a decline in the cost of constructing or installing a similar improvement of the same or similar functional utility,

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (c) may express the rates in terms of an amount

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (i)  per customer served by the improvements, or

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (ii)  per kilometre of the improvements that may vary according to

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (A) the size of the improvements,

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (B) the capacity of the improvements,

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (C) the type of use or extent of use of the improvements, or

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (D) the location of the improvements, and

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (d) may prescribe different rates or a reduction in rates for improvements that should, in the opinion of the assessment authority, be valued differently from other improvements of the same type by reason of

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (i)  lack of use for a period specified in the regulation,

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of railway track in place, use at less than its annual rated capacity, or

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (iii)  other special circumstances that are specified in the regulation and relate to the construction or installation of the improvements.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2):

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: "average current cost" means the cost to construct or install the existing improvements

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) including all materials, labour, overhead and indirect costs, and

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) assuming the improvements were to be constructed or installed

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (i)  on July 1 in the year previous to the year in which the assessment roll is prepared, and

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (ii)  at a location that has average construction and installation difficulty;

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: "functional utility" means the ability of an improvement to meet market standards.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (4) In prescribing rates respecting the right of way referred to in subsection (1) (d) and (e), the assessment authority must base the rates on the criteria prescribed under section 74 (2) (f).

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (4.1) If, in the opinion of the assessment authority, the rate prescribed for the purposes of subsection (1) is substantially different in a taxation year than it was in the previous taxation year, the assessment authority, by regulation, may order that the rate change be phased in as directed in the regulation.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (4.2) For the purposes of subsection (4.1), the assessment authority may make regulations specifying types of improvements or rights of way for which rate changes are to be phased in over a period of up to 5 years and for that purpose may make regulations

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) prescribing the manner in which the rate changes are to be phased in, and

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) prescribing different rates and periods of time for the phasing in of rate changes for different types of improvements or rights of way.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (5) The rates prescribed by the assessment authority are subject to appeal to the board by notice filed with the board and the assessment authority before February 1 following delivery of the assessment notice.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (6) An appeal under subsection (5) of rates prescribed in respect of improvements referred to in subsection (1) (a) to (c) must be made, heard and decided only on the ground that the assessment authority did not prescribe the rates in accordance with one or more of subsection (2) (a), (b) or (b.1).

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (7) The notice of appeal filed with the board must be accompanied by the prescribed fee.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (8) For the purposes of an appeal under this section, sections 50 (4) (b) to (g) and (5), 52 (2), 55 and 59 to 62 and Part 7 apply with all necessary changes.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (9) If, on an appeal referred to in subsection (6), the board decides that the assessment authority did not prescribe the rates in accordance with one or both of paragraphs (a) and (b) of subsection (2), the board must

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) refer the rates back to the assessment authority for the purpose of prescribing new rates under subsection (10), and

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) advise the assessment authority of its reasons.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (10) If rates prescribed under subsection (1) (a), (b) or (c) are referred back to the assessment authority by the board, the assessment authority may prescribe new rates to replace those rates within

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) 3 months after the date on which the board referred the rates back to the assessment authority, or

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) a period of time longer than 3 months that the board, on application by the assessment authority, may direct.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (11) Rates prescribed under subsection (1) (a), (b) or (c) that are referred back to the assessment authority by the board remain in full force until

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) new rates are prescribed under subsection (10), or

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) the time for prescribing new rates under subsection (10) has expired,

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: whichever is earlier.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (12) Rates prescribed under subsection (10)

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) apply for the purposes of assessment and taxation for the taxation years to which the rates they are replacing applied, and

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) may, within one month after the date on which they were prescribed, be appealed as if they were rates prescribed under subsection (1).

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (13) For the purposes of subsection (1) (d), "right of way" does not include

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (a) land of which the corporation referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (c) is not the owner within the meaning of this Act, and

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (b) land that the corporation referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (c) leases to a lessee.

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (14) For the purposes of subsection (1) (e), "right of way" means land that meets the criteria prescribed under section 74 (2) (e).

heading: Valuation for certain purposes not actual value
paragraph: (15) For the purpose of applying subsection (1) (b), the "track in place of a railway corporation" includes all structures, erections and things, other than any buildings, bridges, trestles, viaducts, overpasses and similar things, coal bunkers, corrals, stand pipes, fuel oil storage tanks, oil fuelling equipment, water tanks, station houses, engine houses, roundhouses, turntables, docks, wharves, freight sheds, weigh scales, repair and cleaning shops and equipment, boiler houses, offices, sand towers and equipment, pavement, platforms, yard fencing and lighting, powerhouses, transmission stations or substations, and the separate equipment for each of them, that are necessary for the operation of the railway.

heading: Special rules for railway property
paragraph:
22
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Special rules for railway property
paragraph: (a) excluding from the definition of "improvements" bridges, trestles, viaducts, overpasses and similar things that carry track in place of a railway corporation;

heading: Special rules for railway property
paragraph: (b) prescribing adjustment factors for property of a railway corporation;

heading: Special rules for railway property
paragraph: (c) prescribing, for the purposes of section 21 (1) (e), in relation to a specified jurisdiction or authority to or for which taxes are to be paid, or a specified class of those jurisdictions and authorities, criteria for land that is to be dealt with as right of way that differ from the criteria prescribed under section 74 (2) (e).

heading: Special rules for railway property
paragraph: (2) Regulations under this section may be different for one or more of the following:

paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation under this section only after the minister has consulted with representatives of the Union of British Columbia Municipalities respecting the proposed regulation.

paragraph: (5) For the 1996 taxation year, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation under this section only in relation to taxes under the School Act.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: 23		  (0.1) In this section:

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: "owner's dwelling" means the dwelling referred to in subsection (3.1) (a) (iii);

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: "retire" means retire from being actively involved in the day-to-day activities on a farm;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: "retired farmer" means an individual

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (a) who, at all times during a prescribed period or periods of time,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (i)  occupied, as the individual's principal residence, a dwelling that was owned by the individual or the individual's spouse and was located on land that was

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (A) owned by the individual or the individual's spouse,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (B) used for the dwelling, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (C) classified as a farm, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (ii)  was actively involved in the day-to-day activities on land that was

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (A) owned by the individual or the individual's spouse,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (B) classified as a farm, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (C) part of the parcel or adjacent to the parcel on which the dwelling was located, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (b) who has retired.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (1) An owner of land who wants all or part of the land classified as a farm must apply to the assessor using the application form, and following the procedure, prescribed by the assessment authority.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (2) Subject to this Act, the assessor must classify as a farm any land, or any part of a parcel of land, that meets the standards prescribed under subsection (3).

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must prescribe standards for classification of land as a farm.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (3.1) Despite this Act and any regulations made under this Act except a regulation made under subsection (3.2), the assessor must, on receipt of an application from an owner of land in respect of a taxation year, classify the land as a farm for the taxation year if the following requirements are met:

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (a) when the application is made, the owner

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (i)  is

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (A) a retired farmer,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (B) the spouse of a retired farmer, or

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (C) a person who was the spouse of a retired farmer at the time of the retired farmer's death,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (ii)  has reached the prescribed age, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (iii)  owns a dwelling on the land and occupies the dwelling as the owner's principal residence;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (b) if the owner is a person referred to in paragraph (a) (i) (B) or (C), the owner meets the prescribed requirements, if any;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (c) when the application is made, the land is used for the owner's dwelling;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (d) when the retired farmer retired,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (i)  the retired farmer or the retired farmer's spouse owned the owner's dwelling,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (ii)  the owner occupied the owner's dwelling as the owner's principal residence,

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (iii)  the land was classified as a farm, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (iv)  the retired farmer met the prescribed requirements, if any;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (e) the land is in the agricultural land reserve, within the meaning of the Agricultural Land Commission Act, on October 31 of the year preceding the taxation year in respect of which the application is made;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (f) the owner's dwelling is located

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (i)  on a parcel of land that, under subsection (2), is classified in whole or in part as a farm for the taxation year in respect of which the application is made, or

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (ii)  on a parcel of land adjacent to a parcel of land

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (A) that is owned by the owner or the owner's spouse, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (B) that, under subsection (2), is classified in whole or in part as a farm for the taxation year in respect of which the application is made;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (g) the application is

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (i)  in the form prescribed by the assessment authority, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (ii)  received by the assessor on or before October 31 of the year preceding the taxation year in respect of which the application is made;

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (h) the requirements, if any, prescribed by regulation.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (3.2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting classification of land as a farm under subsection (3.1), including, without limitation, for the purposes of subsections (0.1) and  (3.1).

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (3.3) In making regulations under subsection (3.2), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make different regulations for different classes of persons, classes of land, classes of places or classes of things.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (4) Land classified as a farm must, while so classified, be valued at its actual value as a farm, without regard to its value for other purposes.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (5) The actual value of improvements on a farm must be determined under section 19.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (6) If land classified as a farm ceases to meet the standards for that classification merely because the farm is reduced in area as a result of a portion being expropriated for a public purpose, the land continues to be classified as a farm until it no longer meets the standards in some other respect.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of valuing a farm under subsection (4), the assessment authority must prescribe land value schedules for use by assessors in determining the actual value of the land as a farm without regard to its value for other purposes.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (8) In subsections (9) and (10), "assessed value" means assessed value before exemptions.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (9) If the assessed value determined under section 19 (13) for any year of land classified as a farm exceeds the assessed value for the preceding year by more than 10%, its assessed value for that year is the total of

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (a) 110% of the assessed value for the preceding year, and

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (b) 25% of the difference between the assessed value determined under section 19 (13) for that year and 110% of the assessed value for the preceding year.

heading: Classification of land as a farm
paragraph: (10) If an obvious error or omission occurred in the preparation of the assessed value in the preceding year, the assessed value under subsection (9) must be determined as though the error or omission had not occurred.

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: 24		  (1) In this section:

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: "council" means the Private Managed Forest Land Council established under section 4 of the Private Managed Forest Land Act;

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: "managed forest land" means land, other than farm land,

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (a) that is being used for the production and harvesting of timber,

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (b) that is managed in accordance with

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (i)  the Private Managed Forest Land Act and the regulations under that Act, or

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (ii)  the Forest and Range Practices Act,

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (c) in respect of which

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (i)  there is a management commitment under section 17 of the Private Managed Forest Land Act, or

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (ii)  a management plan has been approved under the Forest Act,

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (d) with respect to paragraphs (b) (i) and (c) (i), for which the assessor

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (i)  receives notification from the council under section 17 (4) of the Private Managed Forest Land Act, and

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (ii)  has not received notification from the council under section 31 (1) or (2) (b) of the Private Managed Forest Land Act, and

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (e) that meets other requirements prescribed by regulation of the assessment authority for classification of land as managed forest land under this Act.

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (2) The assessor must classify as managed forest land any land that meets the requirements set out in the definition of "managed forest land".

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (3) The assessor must declassify all or part of a parcel of land as managed forest land if the assessor is

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (a) notified by September 30 of the year in which the assessment roll is completed,

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (i)  under section 31 (1) of the Private Managed Forest Land Act that the owner or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the owner has contravened or is contravening a provision of that Act or the regulations made under it, or

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (ii)  under section 31 (2) (b) of the Private Managed Forest Land Act that the owner has withdrawn the owner's management commitment, or

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (b) not satisfied, on September 30 of the year in which the assessment roll is completed, that the land meets all requirements to be classified as managed forest land.

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (4) The actual value of managed forest land is the total of

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (a) the value that the land has for the purpose of growing and harvesting trees, but without taking into account the existence on the land of any trees, and

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (b) a value for cut timber determined in accordance with subsection (8).

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (5) Despite subsection (4), if land is classified as managed forest land but its classification changes before the value of timber cut on the land is added to the value of the land for assessment purposes,

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (a) the value of the cut timber must be added to the value of the land, and

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (b) the cut timber must be assessed as if the land were still managed forest land.

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (6) The actual value of managed forest land must be determined on the basis of its topography, accessibility, soil quality, parcel size and location.

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (7) For the purpose of valuing managed forest land, the assessment authority must prescribe land value schedules for use by assessors in determining the actual value of the land.

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (8) The value of cut timber referred to in subsection (5) (b) must be determined by the assessor as follows:

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (a) for the purpose of taxation during an odd numbered year, the value must be determined on the basis of

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (i)  the scale of that timber under the Forest Act during the last odd numbered year before that taxation year, and

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (ii)  schedules of timber values prescribed by the assessment authority under subsection (9);

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of taxation during an even numbered year, the value must be determined on the basis of

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (i)  the scale of that timber under the Forest Act during the last even numbered year before that taxation year, and

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (ii)  schedules of timber values prescribed by the assessment authority under subsection (9).

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (9) The assessment authority must prescribe schedules of timber values based on the following factors:

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (a) the species and grade of logs;

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (b) the locality in which the timber is cut;

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (c) in relation to timber cut from a coastal area as defined in the regulations, the average price for logs in the year of cutting determined on the basis of the value reported for the Vancouver log market and the distance from Howe Sound of the parcel on which the cutting occurred;

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (d) in relation to timber cut from an interior area as defined in the regulations, the average price for logs, delivered to the nearest sawmill, in the year of cutting determined on the basis of the selling prices of timber products, the costs of milling and the distance from the nearest sawmill of the parcel on which the cutting occurred.

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (10) An owner of managed forest land must submit to the assessment authority the following information respecting the forest land:

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (a) the volume of timber scaled under the Forest Act;

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (b) other matters prescribed by regulation of the assessment authority;

heading: Classification and valuation of forest land
paragraph: (c) other information that the assessment authority may require that is not inconsistent with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: 24.1		  (1) In this section:

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: "forest management objectives" means forest management objectives established by law of a treaty first nation that address the following matters:

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (a) conservation of soil;

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (b) water quality;

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (c) protection of fish habitat;

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (d) critical wildlife habitat;

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (e) reforestation of areas where timber has been harvested;

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: "forest management plan" means a plan that contains information about the proposed use of land within the treaty lands of a treaty first nation for the production and harvesting of timber, including, without limitation, the strategies that will be used to attain the forest management objectives of the treaty first nation during and following the production and harvesting of timber;

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: "treaty first nation managed forest land" means land, other than farm land, within the treaty lands of a treaty first nation

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (a) that is being used for the production and harvesting of timber,

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (b) that is managed in accordance with the treaty first nation's laws respecting forest management,

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (c) in respect of which a forest management plan has been approved under the laws of the treaty first nation, and

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (d) in respect of which the assessor receives a recommendation under subsection (2).

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (2) If a treaty first nation has, under its law, approved a forest management plan for an area of land within its treaty lands, the treaty first nation may recommend to the assessor that the area of land be classified as managed forest land.

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (3) The assessor must classify as managed forest land any land within the treaty lands of a treaty first nation that meets the criteria set out in the definition of "treaty first nation managed forest land".

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (4) After classifying land under subsection (3), the assessor must notify the treaty first nation and the owner of the land.

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (5) The assessor must declassify as managed forest land all or part of a parcel of land within the treaty lands of a treaty first nation if the assessor is

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (a) notified by the treaty first nation, by September 30 of the year in which the assessment roll is completed,

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (i)  that the owner or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the owner has contravened or is contravening a provision of the treaty first nation's law respecting management of forest land, or

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (ii)  the owner has withdrawn the owner's forest management plan, or

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (b) not satisfied, on September 30 of the year in which the assessment roll is completed, that the land meets all criteria set out in the definition of "treaty first nation managed forest land".

heading: Classification and valuation of treaty first nation managed forest land
paragraph: (6) Section 24 (4) to (10) applies for the purpose of determining the actual value of managed forest land classified under subsection (3) of this section.

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph:
24.2
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: "forest management plan" means a plan that contains information about the proposed use of land within Nisga'a Lands for the production and harvesting of timber, including, without limitation, the strategies that will be used to attain the Nisga'a forest management objectives during and following the production and harvesting of timber;

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: "Nisga'a forest management objectives" means forest management objectives established by Nisga'a law that address the following matters:

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (a) conservation of soil;

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (b) water quality;

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (c) protection of fish habitat;

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (d) critical wildlife habitat;

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (e) reforestation of areas where timber has been harvested;

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: "Nisga'a managed forest land" means land, other than farm land, within the Nisga'a Lands

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (a) that is being used for the production and harvesting of timber,

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (b) that is managed in accordance with the Nisga'a laws respecting forest management,

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (c) in respect of which a forest management plan has been approved under the Nisga'a laws, and

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (d) in respect of which the assessor receives a recommendation under subsection (2).

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (2) If the Nisga'a Nation has, under Nisga'a law, approved a forest management plan for an area of land within the Nisga'a Lands, the Nisga'a Nation may recommend to the assessor that the area of land be classified as managed forest land.

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (3) The assessor must classify as managed forest land any land that meets the criteria set out in the definition of "Nisga'a managed forest land".

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (4) After classifying land under subsection (3), the assessor must notify the Nisga'a Nation and the owner of the land.

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (5) The assessor must declassify as managed forest land all or part of a parcel of land within the Nisga'a Lands if the assessor is

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (a) notified by the Nisga'a Nation, by September 30 of the year in which the assessment roll is completed,

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (i)  that the owner or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the owner has contravened or is contravening a provision of a Nisga'a law respecting management of forest land, or

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (ii)  the owner has withdrawn the owner's forest management plan, or

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (b) not satisfied, on September 30 of the year in which the assessment roll is completed, that the land meets all criteria set out in the definition of "Nisga'a managed forest land".

heading: Classification and valuation of Nisga'a managed forest land
paragraph: (6) Section 24 (4) to (10) applies for the purpose of determining the actual value of managed forest land classified under subsection (3) of this section.

heading: Occupiers of railway land
paragraph:
25
		  (1) If any parcel liable to assessment is railway land and part of it is leased, that part must be treated under this Act as a separate parcel and a separate entry made on the assessment roll in respect of the land or improvements or both.

heading: Occupiers of railway land
paragraph: (2) If part of a parcel of railway land is treated as a separate parcel under subsection (1), the remainder of the parcel must be treated under this Act as a separate parcel and a separate entry made on the assessment roll in respect of the land or improvements or both.

heading: Occupiers of railway land
paragraph: (3) The actual value of land or improvements, or both, referred to in subsection (1) or (2) must be determined under section 19.

heading: Occupiers of railway land
paragraph: (4) If the whole of any parcel of railway land liable to assessment is leased or a part of a parcel is assessed under subsection (1), the owner or lessee may give notice, with full particulars of the duration of the lease, to the assessor and request that copies of all assessment and tax notices issued during the duration of the lease be sent to the lessee.

heading: Occupiers of railway land
paragraph: (5) After receiving a notice under subsection (4), the assessor must enter the name and address of the lessee on the assessment roll.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph:
26
		  (1) Land, the fee of which is in the Crown, or in some person on behalf of the Crown, that is held or occupied otherwise than by, or on behalf of, the Crown, is, with the improvements on it, to be assessed in accordance with this section.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph: (2) The land referred to in subsection (1) with the improvements on it must be entered in the assessment roll in the name of the holder or occupier, whose interest must be valued at the actual value of the land and improvements determined under this Part.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph: (3) This section applies, with the necessary changes and so far as it is applicable, to improvements owned by, leased to, held, or occupied by some person other than the Crown, located on land the fee of which is in the Crown, or in some person on behalf of the Crown.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph: (4) This section applies, with the necessary changes and so far as it is applicable, if land is held in trust for a tribe or band of Indians and occupied, in other than an official capacity, by a person who is not an Indian.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph: (5) As soon as the assessor determines that

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph: (a) land is held or occupied, or

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph: (b) land ceases to be held or occupied

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph: in the manner referred to in subsection (1), the assessor must make an entry on a supplementary roll.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the Crown
paragraph:
(6) 
            Subsection (5) does not apply in respect of land in a rural area.

heading: Assessment of exempt land held by occupier
paragraph:
27
		  (1) Land, the fee simple of which is held by or on behalf of a person who is exempted from taxation under an Act, and which is held or occupied otherwise than by or on behalf of that person, is, with its improvements, to be assessed in accordance with this section.

heading: Assessment of exempt land held by occupier
paragraph: (2) The land and improvements referred to in subsection (1) must be entered in the assessment roll in the name of the holder or occupier, whose interest must be valued at the actual value of the land and improvements determined under this Part.

heading: Assessment of exempt land held by occupier
paragraph: (3) This section applies to improvements owned by, leased to, held or occupied otherwise than by, or on behalf of, a person exempted from taxation by an Act, located on land the fee simple of which is held by or on behalf of a person exempted from taxation by any Act.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the municipality
paragraph:
28
		  (1) Land, the fee of which is in the municipality, held or occupied otherwise than by, or on behalf of, the municipality, is, with the improvements on it, to be assessed in accordance with this section.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the municipality
paragraph: (2) The land referred to in subsection (1) with the improvements on it must be entered in the assessment roll in the name of the holder or occupier, whose interest must be valued at the actual value of the land and improvements determined under this Part.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the municipality
paragraph: (3) This section applies, with the necessary changes and so far as it is applicable, to improvements owned by, leased to, held, or occupied by some person other than the municipality, located on land the fee of which is in the municipality, or in some person on behalf of the municipality.

heading: Assessment of land the fee of which is in the municipality
paragraph: (4) This section does not apply to any land or improvements that were exempted from taxation by the municipality under the terms of a lease agreement entered into before July 1, 1957.

heading: Joint interests
paragraph:
29
		  If land or improvements or both are held or occupied in the manner referred to in section 26, 27 or 28 by 2 or more persons and there is no paramount occupier, the land or improvements or both must be assessed in the names of those persons jointly.

heading: Assessment of an improvement on land under other ownership
paragraph:
30
		  (1) Any structure, aqueduct, pipe line, tunnel, bridge, dam, reservoir, road, storage tank, transformer, substation, pole lines, cables, towers, poles, wires, transmission equipment or other improvement that extends over, under or through land may be separately assessed to the person owning, leasing, maintaining, operating or using it, even though the land may be owned by some other person.

heading: Assessment of an improvement on land under other ownership
paragraph: (2) Each individual residential building located on a land cooperative or multi dwelling leased parcel, as those terms are defined in the Home Owner Grant Act, must be separately assessed.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: 31		  (1) The minister must appoint property assessment review panels, each comprised of 3 members, to review and consider

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (a) the annual assessments of land and improvements in British Columbia, and

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (b) in accordance with the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority Act, parking site rolls as that term is defined in section 131 of that Act.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (2) The minister must appoint and designate one member of each panel as the chair of the panel, after a merit-based process, to hold office for an initial term of 3 to 5 years.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (3) The minister may appoint members of a panel, other than the chair, after a merit-based process, to hold office for an initial term of 2 to 4 years.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (4) A member may be reappointed by the minister as a member or chair of a panel for additional terms of up to 5 years.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (5) A member of a review panel must faithfully, honestly and impartially perform the member's duties and must not, except in the proper performance of those duties, disclose to any person any information obtained as a member.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (6) If a member is absent or incapacitated for an extended period of time or expects to be absent for an extended period of time, the minister may appoint another person, who would otherwise be qualified for appointment as a member, to replace the member until the member returns to full duty or the member's term expires, whichever comes first.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (6.1) The appointment of a person to replace a member under subsection (6) is not affected by the member returning to less than full duty.

heading: Appointment of property assessment review panels
paragraph: (7) Sections 1, 4, 6 to 8, 10, 18, 40 (1) to (4), 44, 46.3, 48, 49, 55, 56 and 61 of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to a review panel.

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: 32		  (1) Subject to the requirements in section 33, a person may make a complaint against an individual entry in an assessment roll on any of the following grounds:

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (a) there is an error or omission respecting the name of a person in the assessment roll;

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (b) there is an error or omission respecting land or improvements, or both land and improvements, in the assessment roll;

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (c) land or improvements, or both land and improvements, are not assessed at actual value;

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (d) land or improvements, or both land and improvements, have been improperly classified;

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (e) an exemption has been improperly allowed or disallowed.

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (2) Subject to the requirements in section 33, the Minister of Finance or the assessment authority may make a complaint against all or any part of the completed assessment roll, based on any of the grounds specified in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (3) Subject to the requirements in section 33, a local government may make a complaint against all or any part of the completed assessment roll relating to property in the municipality or regional district, as the case may be, based on any of the grounds specified in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (3.1) Subject to the requirements in section 33, a treaty first nation may make a complaint against all or any part of the completed assessment roll relating to its treaty lands, based on any of the grounds specified in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (3.2) Subject to the requirements in section 33, the Nisga'a Nation may make a complaint against all or any part of the completed assessment roll relating to Nisga'a Lands, based on any of the grounds specified in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (4) Subject to the requirements in section 33, an assessor may make a complaint against all or any part of the assessment roll completed by the assessor, based on any of the grounds specified in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Complaints respecting completed assessment roll
paragraph: (5) Without limiting subsections (2) to (4), complaints under those subsections may be in respect of a class, category or type of property or interest in land or improvements, or both land and improvements.

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A person who wishes to make a complaint under section 32 must file notice of the complaint with the assessor responsible for the assessment that is the subject of the complaint.

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (2) The notice of complaint must be filed with the assessor no later than January 31 of the year following the year in which the assessment roll is completed under section 3 or changed or amended under section 12, as the case may be.

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (3) The notice of complaint must

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (a) clearly identify the property in respect of which the complaint is made,

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (b) include the full name of the complainant and a telephone number at which the complainant may be contacted during regular business hours,

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (c) indicate whether or not the complainant is the owner of the property to which the complaint relates,

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (d) if the complainant has an agent to act on the complainant's behalf in respect of the complaint, include the full name of the agent and a telephone number at which the agent may be contacted during regular business hours,

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (e) include an address for delivery of any notices in respect of the complaint,

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (f) state the grounds on which the complaint is based under section 32 (1), and

heading: Notice of complaint
paragraph: (g) include any other prescribed information.

heading: Assessor recommendations
paragraph:
34
		  Before March 16 of each year, an assessor must, for the purpose of correcting an error or omission under section 10  that is not corrected with the consent of the owner of the affected property, recommend to a review panel changes to the assessment roll completed by the assessor.

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph:
35
		  (1) If a complaint is received under section 33 (1) and is not resolved under section 10 (2), the assessor must

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (a) set a time for a hearing of the complaint by a review panel before March 16,

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (b) deliver notice of the hearing to the complainant's address for delivery, and

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (c) if the complainant is not the owner of the property in respect of which the complaint is made, deliver notice of the hearing to each owner of that property.

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1) (c), if the complaint is made under section 32 (2), (3), (3.1), (3.2) or (4), the requirement set out in subsection (1) (c) of this section is satisfied by publication of notice of the hearing in 2 current issues of a newspaper circulating in the municipality, the treaty lands of the treaty first nation, Nisga'a Lands or the other rural area, in which the property that is the subject of the complaint is located.

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (3) An assessor is not required to deliver notice of the hearing to the owner of a property affected by a recommendation for change under section 34 if

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (b) the recommendation

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (i)  results in a decrease in the assessed value of the property,

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (ii)  does not change the classification of the property, and

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (iii)  does not result in the removal of an exemption.

heading: Notice of hearing
paragraph: (6) A notice under this section must include a statement that the recipient may file written submissions instead of appearing at the hearing.

heading: Daily schedule
paragraph:
36
		  (1) The daily schedule of matters for review and consideration by a review panel, as set by the assessor, must be posted at the place where the review panel is to meet.

heading: Daily schedule
paragraph: (2) The review panel must proceed to deal with complaints and assessor recommendations in accordance with that schedule, unless the review panel considers a change in the schedule necessary and desirable in the circumstances.

heading: Notice of withdrawal
paragraph:
37
		  (1) A complainant may apply to withdraw a complaint made under section 33 by filing with the assessor a notice of withdrawal.

heading: Notice of withdrawal
paragraph: (2) The review panel may summarily dismiss the complaint referred to in subsection (1) on consent of the assessor.

heading: Notice of withdrawal
paragraph: (3) No appeal lies under section 50 (1) in respect of summary dismissal of a complaint under subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph:
38
		  (1) A review panel may review and consider the assessment roll and the individual entries made in it to ensure accuracy and that assessments are at actual value applied in a consistent manner in the municipality, treaty lands of the treaty first nation, Nisga'a Lands or other rural area.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), a review panel

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (a) may investigate the assessment roll and the individual entries made in it, whether or not the investigation is based on a complaint or an assessor recommendation,

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (b) must adjudicate the matters set for its consideration under section 36,

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (c) when considering whether land or improvements are assessed at actual value, must consider the total assessed value of the land and improvements together, and

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (d) may direct amendments to be made to the assessment roll, subject to the requirements of subsections (4) to (6).

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2) (b), the review panel may

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (a) refuse to adjudicate a matter set for its consideration if the notice of complaint was not filed in accordance with section 33 (2), and

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (b) summarily dismiss a matter set for its consideration if a notice of withdrawal is filed in accordance with section 37.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (4) A review panel must before March 16 complete

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (a) any investigation referred to in subsection (2) (a), and

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (b) adjudication of the matters set for its consideration under section 36.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (5) If the review panel intends to direct that an amendment be made that is not based on a complaint or on an assessor recommendation and the amendment would

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (a) increase the assessed value of the property,

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (b) change the classification of the property, or

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (c) result in the removal of an exemption,

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: the review panel must order the assessor to set a hearing in respect of the proposed amendment, giving the owner of the affected property an opportunity to make submissions.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of subsection (5), the assessor must, at least 5 days before the hearing, deliver to the owner of the affected property a notice of the hearing and the notice must include

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (a) particulars of the proposed amendment, and

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (b) a statement that the owner may file written submissions instead of appearing at the hearing.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (7) The chair of the review panel may

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (a) determine the procedures to be followed at proceedings of the review panel,

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (b) administer an oath or solemn affirmation to a person or witness before the person's or witness's evidence is taken, and

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (c) for the purposes of section 36 (2), but subject to the requirement of subsection (4), adjourn the hearings from day to day or from time to time and from place to place within the geographic area of the review panel's jurisdiction.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (8) The chair of the review panel must make a record of a summary dismissal under section 37, a refusal to adjudicate a matter under section 38 (3) (a) and any decision made in relation to an investigation, adjudication or direction by the review panel.

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (9) The chair of the review panel must provide the assessor with information necessary to

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (a) amend the assessment roll in accordance with a decision referred to in subsection (8), and

heading: Duties and powers of review panels
paragraph: (b) provide sufficient notice under section 41 (1).

heading: Power to compel witnesses and order disclosure
paragraph:
39
		  (1) At any time before or during a hearing, but before its decision, a review panel may make an order requiring a person

heading: Power to compel witnesses and order disclosure
paragraph: (a) to attend an oral or electronic hearing to give evidence on oath or affirmation or in any other manner that is admissible and relevant to an issue in an application, or

heading: Power to compel witnesses and order disclosure
paragraph: (b) to produce for the review panel or a party a document or other thing in the person's possession or control, as specified by the review panel, that is admissible and relevant to an issue in an application.

heading: Power to compel witnesses and order disclosure
paragraph: (2) A review panel may apply to the court for an order

heading: Power to compel witnesses and order disclosure
paragraph: (a) directing a person to comply with an order made by the review panel under subsection (1), or

heading: Power to compel witnesses and order disclosure
paragraph: (b) directing any directors and officers of a person to cause the person to comply with an order made by the review panel under subsection (1).

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph:
40
		  In a hearing before the review panel, the burden of proof is

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: (a) on the complainant, or

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: (b) if the matter concerns an assessor recommendation under section 34, on the assessor.

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph:
41
		  (1) Before April 7 following the sitting of the review panel, the assessor must deliver notice of the decision made by the review panel, or of its refusal to adjudicate the complaint made, to

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (a) the owner of the property to which the decision relates, and

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (b) the complainant, if the complainant is not the owner.

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (1.1) Before April 7, the assessor must deliver notice of the amendment made by the assessor under section 10 (2) to

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (a) the owner of the property to which the amendment relates, and

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (b) the complainant, if the amendment resolved a complaint and the complainant is not the owner.

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (2) Notice under subsection (1) or (1.1) must include

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (a) a statement that the decision or amendment may be appealed to the board in accordance with section 50, and

heading: Notice of decisions and corrections
paragraph: (b) information on the procedures to be followed for initiating the appeal.

heading: Amendment of assessment roll
paragraph:
42
		  (1) The assessor must ensure that all amendments are made to the assessment roll in accordance with the directions of the review panel under section 38 (2) (d).

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph:
43
		  (1) The property assessment appeal board is continued consisting of at least 6 members appointed after a merit-based process as follows:

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (a) one member appointed and designated by the Lieutenant Governor in Council as the chair;

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (b) one or more members appointed and designated by the Lieutenant Governor in Council as vice chairs after consultation with the chair;

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (c) other members appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council after consultation with the chair.

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (2) The board has jurisdiction to determine

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (a) appeals brought under section 50,

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (b) appeals from the rates prescribed by the assessment authority under section 21,

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (c) complaints referred to the board for its determination under the regulations, and

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (d) appeals brought under section 23 of the Forest Land Reserve Act.

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (4) The chair is the chief executive officer of the board.

heading: Property assessment appeal board
paragraph: (8) A member of the board must faithfully, honestly and impartially perform the member's duties and must not, except in the proper performance of those duties, disclose to any person any information obtained as a member.

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: 43.1		  The following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the property assessment appeal board:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a) Part 1 [Interpretation and Application];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a.1) Part 2 [Appointments];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b) Part 3 [Clustering];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b.1) section 11 [general power to make rules respecting practice and procedure];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (c) section 13 [practice directives tribunal may make];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (c.1) section 14 [general power to make orders];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (d) section 15 [interim orders];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (d.1) section 16 [consent orders];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (e) section 17 (2) [order of tribunal may include terms of settlement];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (e.1) section 18 [failure of party to comply with tribunal orders and rules];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (f) section 19 [service of notice or documents];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (f.1) section 20 [when failure to serve does not invalidate proceeding];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (g) section 28 [facilitated settlement];
