heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: 44		  (1) The chair of the board may organize the board into panels, each comprised of one or more members.

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (2) If the chair organizes a panel comprised of more than one member, the chair must designate one of those members as chair of the panel.

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (3) The members of the board may sit

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (a) as a board, or

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (b) as a panel of the board,

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: and 2 or more panels may sit at the same time.

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (4) If members of the board sit as a panel,

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (a) the panel has the jurisdiction of, and may exercise and perform the powers and duties of, the board, and

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (b) an order, decision or action of the panel is an order, decision or action of the board.

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (5) The decision of a majority of the members of a panel of the board is a decision of the board and, in the case of a tie, the decision of the chair of the panel governs.

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (6) If a member of a panel is unable for any reason to complete the member's duties, the remaining members of that panel may, with consent of the chair of the board, continue to hear and determine the matter, and the vacancy does not invalidate the proceeding.

heading: Organization of the board
paragraph: (8) If the panel is a single member and that member is unable for any reason to complete the member's duties, with the consent of all parties to the application the chair of the board may organize a new panel to continue to hear and determine the matter on terms agreed to by the parties, and the vacancy does not invalidate the proceeding.

heading: Staff of the board
paragraph:
45
		  (1) The chair of the board may appoint, in accordance with the Public Service Act, employees necessary to enable the board to perform its duties.

heading: Staff of the board
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of the application of the Public Service Act to subsection (1) of this section, the chair is deemed to be a deputy minister.

heading: Staff of the board
paragraph: (3) The chair of the board may retain consultants, investigators, expert witnesses or other persons as may be necessary for the board to discharge its functions under this Act and may establish their remuneration and other terms and conditions of their retainers.

heading: Staff of the board
paragraph: (4) The Public Service Act does not apply to a person retained under subsection (3) of this section.

heading: General board powers
paragraph: (2) Members of the board may, in the performance of their duties,

heading: General board powers
paragraph: (a) enter on and inspect any land or improvement,

heading: General board powers
paragraph: (b) require the production of any record, and

heading: General board powers
paragraph: (c) administer oaths, solemn affirmations or declarations.

heading: General board powers
paragraph: (3) The chair may in writing delegate the powers of the board under subsection (2) (a) and (b) to a person designated by the chair.

heading: General board powers
paragraph: (4) The board may at any time require the assessment authority to provide any information or record, obtained or created under this Act, that is in the custody or control of the assessment authority, including, without limitation, a revised assessment roll and any information respecting an assessment dealt with by a review panel.

heading: General board powers
paragraph: (5) Despite section 69 (1), the information or record referred to in subsection (4) of this section must be provided to the board free of charge and in the form and manner required by the board.

heading: Board records
paragraph:
48
		  A record purporting to be a record of an order or decision of the board is admissible in all courts of British Columbia, without proof of appointment, authority or signature and is evidence of the record.

heading: Report
paragraph:
49
		  (1) In accordance with a regulation made under section 74 (2) (g) (iv), the board must annually and at other times it considers appropriate, report to the minister on its activities under this Act.

heading: Report
paragraph: (2) The minister must promptly lay the board's annual report before the Legislative Assembly if it is in session and, if the Legislative Assembly is not in session when the report is submitted, within 15 days after the beginning of the next session.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
49.1
		  In this Part, except in section 57, "appeal under this Part" includes an application for leave to appeal under section 50 (1.1).

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph:
50
		  (1) Subject to the requirements of subsections (2) to (4), a person may appeal to the board if the person is dissatisfied

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (a) with a decision of a review panel,

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (b) with an omission or refusal of the review panel to adjudicate a complaint made under section 33 (1), or

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (c) with an amendment to the assessment roll under section 10 (2).

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (1.1) Subject to the requirements of subsections (2) to (4.2), an owner may, with leave of the board, appeal to the board if the owner failed to file a notice of complaint in respect of the owner's property within the time required under section 33 (2).

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (2) The appeal must be based on one or more of the grounds referred to in section 32 (1).

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (3) A notice of appeal under this section and the prescribed appeal fee must be filed with the board on or before April 30 following the sitting of the review panel.

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (4) The notice of appeal must

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (a) clearly identify the property in respect of which the appeal is made,

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (b) include the full name of the appellant and a telephone number at which the appellant may be contacted during regular business hours,

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (c) indicate whether or not the appellant is the owner of the property to which the appeal relates,

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (d) if the appellant has an agent to act on the appellant's behalf in respect of the appeal, include the full name of the agent and a telephone number at which the agent may be contacted during regular business hours,

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (e) include an address for delivery of any notices in respect of the appeal,

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (f) state the grounds on which the appeal is based, and

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (g) include any other prescribed information.

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (4.1) In addition to the requirements under subsection (4), a notice of appeal for an appeal under subsection (1.1) must state the reasons why leave should be granted under subsection (4.3).

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (4.2) All evidence on which the owner relies in support of the reasons why leave should be granted must be filed with the notice of appeal.

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (4.3) The board may grant leave to appeal under subsection (1.1) if the board is satisfied that the owner's failure to file a notice of complaint within the time required under section 33 (2) was due to circumstances beyond the owner's control.

heading: Appeals to board
paragraph: (5) If a notice of appeal is deficient or if the prescribed appeal fee is outstanding, the chair of the board may in the chair's discretion allow a reasonable period of time within which the notice may be perfected or the fee is to be paid.

heading: Copies of appeal to persons
paragraph:
51
		  If the board receives a notice of appeal in accordance with section 50, the board must promptly provide a copy of the notice to each of the following who is not the appellant:

heading: Copies of appeal to persons
paragraph: (a) the owner of the property;

heading: Copies of appeal to persons
paragraph: (b) the assessor;

heading: Copies of appeal to persons
paragraph: (c) if the property is located in a municipality, a regional district or the treaty lands of a treaty first nation, the municipality, regional district or treaty first nation, as applicable;

heading: Copies of appeal to persons
paragraph: (c.1) if the property is located in Nisga'a Lands, the Nisga'a Nation;

heading: Copies of appeal to persons
paragraph: (d) the chief executive officer of the assessment authority;

heading: Copies of appeal to persons
paragraph: (e) the complainant before the review panel, if that person is not a person specified in paragraphs (a) to (d).

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph:
52
		  (1) The following persons are parties to an appeal under this Part:

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (a) the appellant;

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (b) the owner of the property, if not the appellant;

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (c) the complainant at the review panel, if not the owner or appellant;

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (d) the assessor.

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (2) The board may direct that any other person who may be affected by the appeal may be added as a party to the appeal, including, without limitation,

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (a) a local government or treaty first nation in respect of which the property is located,

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (a.1) if the property is located in Nisga'a Lands, the Nisga'a Nation, or

heading: Parties to an appeal
paragraph: (b) the government.

heading: Means of hearing appeals and notice of hearings
paragraph:
55
		  (1) In a proceeding, the board may hold any combination of written, electronic and oral hearings.

heading: Means of hearing appeals and notice of hearings
paragraph: (2) The chair of the board must give notice of a hearing under subsection (1) to all parties and intervenors.

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph:
57
		  (1) In an appeal under this Part, the board

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (a) may reopen the whole question of the property's assessment to ensure accuracy and that assessments are at actual value applied in a consistent manner in the municipality, treaty lands of the treaty first nation, Nisga'a Lands or other rural area, and

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (b) when considering whether land or improvements are assessed at actual value, must consider the total assessed value of the land and improvements together.

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (2) Nothing in subsection (1) (a) empowers the board to determine an assessment of a property other than the property that is the subject of the appeal, except to the extent permitted under subsection (3).

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (3) If the property referred to in subsection (1) includes a building or other improvement that extends over one or more contiguous parcels of land that actually abut that property but the other parcels were not originally the subject of the appeal, the board may, if the board considers it necessary to accurately determine the assessment of the property referred to in subsection (1), include those parcels in its determinations.

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (4) The board may order the assessment authority to reassess at actual value land and improvements in all or part of a municipality, the treaty lands of a treaty first nation, Nisga'a Lands or other rural area, whether or not they are the subject of the appeal, if the board finds

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (a) that the assessments in the municipality, treaty lands, Nisga'a Lands or other rural area, or in part of any of them, are above their actual value, or

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (b) that the assessment appealed against is at actual value but that the assessments of similar land and improvements in the municipality, treaty lands, Nisga'a Lands or other rural area, or in part of any of them, are below their actual value.

heading: Powers and duties of board in an appeal
paragraph: (5) Despite section 12 (6), the assessor must enter any reassessments ordered under subsection (4) of this section on a supplementary assessment roll.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph:
59
		  (1) The board or a party to an appeal under this Part may apply to the Supreme Court for an order

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (a) directing a person to comply with an order or decision of the board under this Part, and

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (b) directing any directors and officers of the person to cause the person to comply with an order or decision of the board under this Part.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph:
(2) 
            Subsection (1) is in addition to and not instead of any other remedy or course of action that may be available to the board or a party under this Act or otherwise available by law.

heading: Costs
paragraph:
60
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, the board may order that a party to an appeal under this Part or an intervenor pay another party or intervenor or the board any or all of the actual costs in respect of the appeal.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) has, after filing in the court registry, the same effect as an order of the Supreme Court for the recovery of a debt in the amount stated in the order against the person named in it, and all proceedings may be taken as if it were an order of the court.

heading: Decision of board
paragraph:
61
		  (1) The board must issue a decision at the earliest opportunity after hearing an appeal under this Part.

heading: Notice of board decision
paragraph:
62
		  (1) The board must deliver a notice of its decision on an appeal under this Part to

heading: Notice of board decision
paragraph: (a) the parties to the appeal and any intervenors, and

heading: Notice of board decision
paragraph: (b) the chief executive officer of the assessment authority.

heading: Notice of board decision
paragraph: (2) Notice under subsection (1) must include

heading: Notice of board decision
paragraph: (a) the board's decision,

heading: Notice of board decision
paragraph: (b) a statement that the decision may be appealed to the Supreme Court on a question of law, and

heading: Notice of board decision
paragraph: (c) information on the procedures to be followed for such an appeal.

heading: Amending the roll to reflect board decisions
paragraph:
63
		  (1) On receipt of notice of the board's decision under section 62, the assessor must

heading: Amending the roll to reflect board decisions
paragraph: (a) ensure that all amendments ordered to be made in the assessment roll by the board are made promptly, and

heading: Amending the roll to reflect board decisions
paragraph: (b) ensure that a copy of the notice is available for public inspection during regular business hours.

heading: Amending the roll to reflect board decisions
paragraph: (2) If there is a conflict between the revised assessment roll and an amendment made under this section, the amendment prevails.

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph:
64
		  (1) At any stage of a proceeding before it, the board, on its own initiative or at the request of one or more of the persons affected by the appeal, may refer a question of law in the proceeding to the Supreme Court in the form of a stated case.

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (1.1) If the question of law that is referred under subsection (1) is a constitutional question, the party who raises the question must give notice in compliance with section 8 of the Constitutional Question Act.

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (2) The stated case must be in writing and filed with the court registry, and must include a statement of the facts and all evidence material to the stated case.

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (3) The board must

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (a) suspend the proceeding as it relates to the stated case and reserve its decision until the opinion of the Supreme Court has been given, and

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (b) decide the appeal in accordance with the opinion.

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (4) The stated case must be brought on for hearing within one month from the date on which it is filed under subsection (2).

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), the court must hear and determine the stated case and within 2 months give its decision.

heading: Reference on question of law to Supreme Court
paragraph: (6) The court may send the stated case back to the board for amendment and the board must promptly amend and return the stated case for the opinion of the court.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: 65		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person affected by a decision of the board on appeal, including a local government, a treaty first nation, the government, the Nisga'a Nation or the assessment authority, may require the board to refer the decision to the Supreme Court for appeal on a question of law alone in the form of a stated case.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (2) Within 21 days after receiving the decision referred to in subsection (1), the person must deliver to the board a written request to refer the decision to the Supreme Court, and include in the request the question of law to be referred.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (3) On receipt of the request under subsection (2), the board must promptly provide written notice of the request to

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (a) the parties to the appeal from which the reference is requested and any intervenors, and

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (b) the chief executive officer of the assessment authority.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (4) Within 21 days after receiving the request under subsection (2), the board must file the stated case with the court registry, including the decision on appeal, a statement of the facts and all evidence material to the stated case.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (5) The stated case must be brought on for hearing within one month from the date on which it is filed under subsection (4).

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (6) Subject to subsection (7), the court must hear and determine the stated case and within 2 months give its decision.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (7) The court may send the stated case back to the board for amendment and the board must promptly amend and return the stated case for the opinion of the court.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (8) The costs of, and incidental to, a stated case under this section are at the discretion of the court.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (9) An appeal on a question of law lies from a decision of the Supreme Court to the Court of Appeal with leave of a justice of the Court of Appeal.

heading: Appeal of board decision on question of law
paragraph: (10) The board must direct the assessor to make any amendment to the assessment roll necessary to give effect to a decision made by the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal under this section.

heading: Authorization for electronic transmission of notices
paragraph:
65.1
		  (1) A person may,

heading: Authorization for electronic transmission of notices
paragraph: (a) if the assessment authority provides for electronic transmission, authorize, in writing, the assessment authority to electronically transmit a notice under this Act to the person, and

heading: Authorization for electronic transmission of notices
paragraph: (b) at any time, in writing, withdraw the authorization provided under paragraph (a).

heading: Authorization for electronic transmission of notices
paragraph: (2) If a person provides an authorization under subsection (1) (a), the person must provide to the assessment authority an email address for the purposes of electronic transmission.

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph:
66
		  (0.1) In this section, "net taxable value", in relation to land and improvements in the treaty lands of a treaty first nation or Nisga'a Lands, means the net taxable value of the land and improvements determined for regional hospital district purposes as if this Act, the Hospital District Act and the Taxation (Rural Area) Act apply for the purposes of the assessment and taxation of those lands and improvements.

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (1) The assessment authority must provide assessment information to the government for purposes of determining tax liability, collecting a tax or, if applicable, requisitioning under the Speculation and Vacancy Tax Act, the Police Act, the School Act and the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, as follows:

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (a) before February 1 in each year, information from or respecting the completed assessment roll on December 31 of the previous year;

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (b) before March 26 in each year, information from or respecting the assessment roll as amended by the review panels in that year;

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (c) when it becomes available, information from or respecting an assessment roll as it is amended or changed under section 10, 12, 42, 63 or 65 (10).

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (1.1) On request of the government, the assessment authority must provide assessment inventory and valuation information to the government for purposes of determining a school tax refund under section 131.1 of the School Act.

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (2) Despite section 69 (1), information under subsection (1) or (1.1) of this section must be provided to the government free of charge and in the form and manner required by the Minister of Finance.

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (3) Before April 15 in each year, the assessment authority must provide free of charge to regional hospital district boards information setting out the current year net taxable value of all land and improvements in each member municipality, the treaty lands of each treaty first nation and the other rural area, in the district, on both the completed and the revised assessment rolls, for the purpose of requisitioning and raising funds under the Hospital District Act.

heading: Assessment authority to provide information to the government
paragraph: (4) In the case of the North West Regional Hospital District, in addition to the information provided under subsection (3), the assessment authority must provide free of charge the net taxable value of all land and improvements in Nisga'a Lands.

heading: Open hearings
paragraph: 67		  Except for an order that may be made in relation to a prehearing conference, a hearing under this Act must be open to the public.

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph:
68
		  (1) On application by an owner, the assessment authority may omit or obscure the owner's name, address or other information about the owner that would ordinarily be included in an assessment roll if, in the opinion of the assessment authority, the inclusion of the name, address or other information could reasonably be expected to threaten the safety or mental or physical health of the owner or a member of the owner's household.

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (2) Names of individuals must be deleted from

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (a) an assessment roll other than an assessment roll that is

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (i)  supplied under subsection (4),

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (ii)  available for public inspection under section 8, or

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (iii)  accessible through the B.C. OnLine information service or through another electronic information service used by the assessment authority, and

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (b) other prescribed records that are obtained or created under this Act.

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of tracing unauthorized use of information, the assessment authority may have fictitious or false entries or information included in an assessment roll or other record related to an assessor's valuations under Part 2 or 3, that is available for public inspection under this Act or may otherwise be disclosed in accordance with a regulation under section 16 (6).

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph:
(4) 
            Subsections (1) and (3) do not apply to an assessment roll or record that is supplied

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (a) to a person or for a purpose specified in section 33 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act,

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (b) to any of the following:

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (i)  the government;

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (ii)  a municipality, regional district or treaty first nation;

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (ii.1)  the Nisga'a Nation;

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (iii)  a prescribed entity with taxing authority under an enactment of British Columbia or Canada, or

heading: Protection of privacy in assessment roll and records
paragraph: (c) to the board.

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: 69		  (1) Subject to the requirements of this section and section 68 and any prescribed limits on the fees that may be charged, if this Act, or a regulation under this Act, requires or authorizes the disclosure or public inspection or other use of or access to a record, including an assessment roll, a person may obtain a copy of the record or assessment roll on payment of any fee that may be set for the copy by the assessment authority or by the chair of the board, as the case may be.

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (2) A person must not, directly or indirectly, use the assessment roll or information contained in the assessment roll or a record referred to in subsection (1) as follows:

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (a) to obtain names, addresses or telephone numbers for solicitation purposes, whether the solicitations are made by telephone, mail or any other means;

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (b) to harass an individual;

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (c) for other uses or purposes specified by regulation.

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (3) A person who wishes to inspect or obtain a copy of a record referred to in subsection (1) may be required to complete a declaration in the prescribed form

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (a) specifying the purpose for which the information is to be used, and

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (b) certifying that the information contained in the record will not be used in a manner prohibited under subsection (2).

heading: Use of and access to information in records
paragraph: (4) A person who contravenes subsection (2) commits an offence.

heading: Offences in relation to false or misleading information
paragraph:
70
		  (1) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences in relation to false or misleading information
paragraph: (a) provides false or misleading information when required under this Act to provide information;

heading: Offences in relation to false or misleading information
paragraph: (b) makes a false or misleading statement or declaration when required under this Act to make a statement or declaration.

heading: Offences in relation to false or misleading information
paragraph: (2) A person is not guilty of an offence under this section if the person establishes that, at the time the information was given or the statement or declaration was made, the person did not know that it was false or misleading and exercised reasonable care and diligence in providing the information or making the statement or declaration.

heading: Fines and penalties for offences
paragraph:
71
		  (1) A person who commits an offence under section 15 (3), 69 (4) or 70 (1) is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $10 000 or imprisonment for a term not longer than 2 years, or both.

heading: Fines and penalties for offences
paragraph: (2) If a person is convicted of an offence under section 69 (4) or 70 (1) and the court is satisfied that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any monetary benefits or that monetary benefits accrued to the person, the court may order the person to pay a fine equal to the court's estimation of the amount of those monetary benefits.

heading: Fines and penalties for offences
paragraph: (3) A fine under subsection (2) is in addition to and not in place of the fine or punishment that may be imposed under subsection (1) and is not limited to the maximum fine prescribed under subsection (1).

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
72
		  Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Act prevails
paragraph: 73		  If there is a conflict between this Act and any other Act, this Act prevails.

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph:
74
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (a) defining any expression used and not defined in this Act;

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (b) prescribing capacity for the purposes of section 1 (2) (l) and different capacities may be prescribed for different categories or types of vessels referred to in that section;

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (c) exempting classes of interest in land or improvements, or both, from assessment under section 26, 27, 28 or 29;

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (d) excluding from the definition of "improvements" any category or type of thing included in that definition by section 1 (2);

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (e) prescribing criteria for determining the land that is considered for the purposes of section 21 to be right of way for the track in place of a railway corporation;

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (f) prescribing criteria to be applied by the assessment authority in prescribing rates under section 21 (1) (d) and (e), including different criteria for different categories of right of way;

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws
paragraph: (g) respecting

heading: Power to make regulations and bylaws

heading: Definition of Act
paragraph: 1 In these Regulations, Act means the Fisheries Act.

heading: Required information and documents
paragraph: 2 (1) The Minister may, on application, issue the authorization referred to in paragraph 34.4(2)(b) or 35(2)(b) of the Act. The application must be made to the Minister in writing and include

heading: Required information and documents
paragraph: (a) the information and documents set out in Schedule 1; and

heading: Required information and documents
paragraph: (b) an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a recognized Canadian financial institution, or another equivalent financial guarantee, including a performance bond, to cover the costs of implementing the plan referred to in section 16 of Schedule 1.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Paragraph (1)(b) does not apply if the applicant is Her Majesty in right of Canada, Her Majesty in right of a province or the government of a territory.

heading: Required information - emergency situation
paragraph: 3 Only the information set out in Schedule 2 must be provided to the Minister in support of an application in respect of a work, undertaking or activity that needs to be carried on without delay in response to the following situations:

heading: Required information - emergency situation
paragraph: (a) a matter of national security;

heading: Required information - emergency situation
paragraph: (b) a national emergency for which special temporary measures are taken under the Emergencies Act; or

heading: Required information - emergency situation
paragraph: (c) an emergency that poses a risk to public health or safety, the environment or property.

heading: Application
paragraph: 4 (1) This section applies to applications referred to in section 2.

heading: Confirmation of receipt
paragraph: (2) The Minister must, on receipt of an application, send to the applicant a confirmation of receipt that indicates the date of receipt.

heading: 60-day time limit
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (6) and (8), the Minister must, within a period of 60 days beginning on the day on which the application is received, notify the applicant in writing that the application is complete, incomplete or inadequate. If the application is incomplete or inadequate, the notification must specify the information or documents to be provided.

heading: Subsection (3) applies again
paragraph: (4) The Minister must, on receipt of any information or documents set out in the notification, send to the applicant a confirmation of receipt that indicates the date of receipt. Subsection (3) applies again to the application, except that the period begins on the date indicated in the confirmation of receipt.

heading: Minister's decision
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsections (6) and (8), the Minister must, within a period of 90 days beginning on the date of the notification informing the applicant that their application is complete, either issue an authorization or notify the applicant in writing of the refusal to do so.

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (6) The time limit referred to in subsection (3) or (5) ceases to apply if

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (a) the applicant proposes amendments to their application;

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (b) the applicant requests in writing that the processing of the application be suspended;

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (c) circumstances require that information or documents other than those referred to in subsection 2(1) be obtained or that amendments to the information or documents submitted by the applicant be made before an authorization can be issued or a notification of refusal can be given;

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (d) consultation is required before an authorization can be issued or a notification of refusal can be given; or

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (e) an Act of Parliament, a regulation made under an Act of Parliament or a land claims agreement provides that a decision be made or that conditions be met before an authorization can be issued or a notification of refusal can be given.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (7) If a time limit ceases to apply, the Minister must notify the applicant in writing and, if it ceases to apply for a reason set out in any of paragraphs (6)(c), (d) and (e), inform the applicant of the reason and, if applicable, the information or documents that must be submitted.

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (8) The time limit referred to in subsection (3) or (5) starts over as soon as all of the following conditions have been met:

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (a) all information or documents in support of the proposed amendments have been received, in the case referred to in paragraph (6)(a);

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (b) the Minister receives a request in writing that the processing of the application be resumed, in the case referred to in paragraph 6(b);

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (c) the information or documents referred to in paragraph (6)(c) have been obtained or amended;

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (d) the consultation referred to in paragraph (6)(d) has been conducted;

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (e) the decision has been made or the conditions have been met, in the case referred to in paragraph (6)(e).

heading: Notice
paragraph: (9) The Minister must notify the applicant in writing of the day on which the time limit referred to in subsection (3) or (5) starts over.

heading: Request for amendment
paragraph: 5 The holder of any authorization may request that the authorization be amended. The request must be submitted to the Minister in writing and include

heading: Request for amendment
paragraph: (a) the file numbers indicated on the original authorization;

heading: Request for amendment
paragraph: (b) a description of the amendment;

heading: Request for amendment
paragraph: (c) the updated information and documents set out in Schedule 1 or 2 that are necessary to support the request; and

heading: Request for amendment
paragraph: (d) a detailed description of the likely effects of the amendment on fish and fish habitat, if not otherwise submitted under paragraph (c).

heading: Request for suspension
paragraph: 6 The holder of any authorization may request that the authorization be suspended in whole or in part. The request must be submitted to the Minister in writing and include

heading: Request for suspension
paragraph: (a) the file numbers indicated on the original authorization;

heading: Request for suspension
paragraph: (b) the period of suspension requested, if any;

heading: Request for suspension
paragraph: (c) the reason for requesting the suspension; and

heading: Request for suspension
paragraph: (d) a detailed description of the likely effects of the suspension on fish and fish habitat.

heading: Request for cancellation
paragraph: 7 The holder of any authorization may request that the authorization be cancelled. The request must be submitted to the Minister in writing and include

heading: Request for cancellation
paragraph: (a) the file numbers indicated on the original authorization;

heading: Request for cancellation
paragraph: (b) the requested cancellation date;

heading: Request for cancellation
paragraph: (c) the reason for requesting the cancellation; and

heading: Request for cancellation
paragraph: (d) a detailed description of the likely effects of the cancellation on fish and fish habitat.

heading: Confirmation of receipt
paragraph: 8 (1) The Minister must, on receipt of a request referred to in sections 5 to 7, send to the authorization holder a confirmation of receipt that indicates the date of receipt.

heading: 60-day time limit
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (5) and (7), the Minister must, within a period of 60 days beginning on the day on which the request is received, notify the authorization holder in writing that the request is complete, incomplete or inadequate. If the request is incomplete or inadequate, the notification must specify the information or documents to be provided.

heading: Subsection (2) applies again
paragraph: (3) The Minister must, on receipt of any information or documents set out in the notification, send to the authorization holder a confirmation of receipt that indicates the date of receipt. Subsection (2) applies again to the request, except that the period begins on the date indicated in the confirmation of receipt.

heading: Minister's decision
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsections (5) and (7), the Minister must, within a period of 90 days beginning on the date of the notification informing the authorization holder that their request is complete, either amend, suspend or cancel the authorization or notify the authorization holder in writing of the refusal to do so.

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (5) The time limit referred to in subsection (2) or (4) ceases to apply if

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (a) the authorization holder proposes amendments to the request to amend, suspend or cancel;

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (b) the authorization holder requests in writing that the processing of the request be suspended;

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (c) circumstances require that information or documents other than those referred to in sections 5 to 7 be obtained or that amendments to the information or documents submitted by the authorization holder be made before the Minister amends, suspends or cancels the authorization;

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (d) consultation is required before the authorization can be amended, suspended or cancelled; or

heading: Time limit ceases to apply
paragraph: (e) an Act of Parliament, a regulation made under an Act of Parliament or a land claims agreement provides that a decision be made or that conditions be met before the authorization can be amended, suspended or cancelled.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (6) If the time limit ceases to apply, the Minister must notify the authorization holder in writing and, if it ceases to apply for a reason set out in any of paragraphs (5)(c), (d) and (e), inform the authorization holder of the reason and, if applicable, the information or documents that must be submitted.

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (7) The time limit referred to in subsection (2) or (4) starts over as soon as all of the following conditions have been met:

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (a) all information or documents in support of the proposed amendments have been received, in the case referred to in paragraph (5)(a);

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (b) the Minister receives a request in writing that the processing of the request be resumed, in the case referred to in paragraph 5(b);

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (c) the information or documents referred to in paragraph (5)(c) have been obtained or amended;

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (d) the consultation referred to in paragraph (5)(d) has been conducted;

heading: Time limit starts over
paragraph: (e) the decision has been made or the conditions have been met, in the case referred to in paragraph (5)(e).

heading: Notice
paragraph: (8) The Minister must notify the authorization holder in writing of the day on which the time limit referred to in subsection (2) or (4) starts over.

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation by Minister
paragraph: 9 (1) The Minister may, on the Minister's own initiative, amend or suspend, in whole or in part, or cancel any authorization if

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation by Minister
paragraph: (a) the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the conditions established by the Minister in the authorization have not been or will not be met;

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation by Minister
paragraph: (b) the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the authorization was obtained by fraudulent or improper means or by the misrepresentation of a material fact;

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation by Minister
paragraph: (c) the Minister becomes aware of new information that demonstrates that the death of fish or the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat is or will be significantly greater than anticipated by the Minister at the time of issuance of the authorization; or

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation by Minister
paragraph: (d) the authorization holder has not paid a fine imposed on them under the Act.

heading: Notice and representations
paragraph: (2) If the Minister intends to amend or suspend, in whole or in part, or cancel the authorization, the Minister must notify the authorization holder in writing of this intention and give the authorization holder an opportunity to make written representations.

heading: Suspension in urgent situations
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), the Minister may suspend an authorization, in whole or in part, without giving the authorization holder an opportunity to make written representations if the suspension is required to prevent the imminent death of fish or the imminent harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat.

heading: Notice of amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (4) If the authorization is amended or suspended, in whole or in part, or cancelled by the Minister, the Minister must notify the authorization holder in writing of the amendment, suspension or cancellation, its effective date and, in the case of a suspension, the duration.

heading: Reinstatement of authorization
paragraph: (5) The Minister may reinstate the authorization at the expiry of the period indicated in the notice of suspension or, on written request, at any time during the suspension if the matter that gave rise to the suspension has been resolved or corrected. The Minister may require the authorization holder to submit a request for amendment in order to reinstate the authorization.

heading: SOR/2013-191
paragraph: 10 If an application for an authorization under paragraph 35(2)(b) of the Fisheries Act is made in accordance with the Applications for Authorization under Paragraph 35(2)(b) of the Fisheries Act Regulations before the coming into force of these Regulations, and the applicant has been notified by the Minister that the application is complete in accordance with the requirements of the Applications for Authorization under Paragraph 35(2)(b) of the Fisheries Act Regulations, then the Applications for Authorization under Paragraph 35(2)(b) of the Fisheries Act Regulations, as they read immediately before the coming into force of these Regulations, apply to the application.

heading: Location
paragraph: (b) a small-scale site plan identifying the general location and boundaries;

heading: Location
paragraph: (c) a large-scale site plan indicating the size and spatial relationship of the planned facilities, infrastructure and other components and of any existing structures, landmarks, water sources or water bodies and other geographic features; and

heading: Location
paragraph: (d) the name of any watersheds, water sources and water bodies that are likely to be affected and the geographic coordinates of the water sources and water bodies.

heading: Location
paragraph: 6 The name of the community nearest to the location and the name of the county, district or region and the province in which the proposed work, undertaking or activity will be carried on.

heading: Consultations
paragraph: 7 A description and the results of any consultations undertaken in relation to the proposed work, undertaking or activity, including with Indigenous communities or groups and the public.

heading: Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: 8 A detailed description of the fish and fish habitat found at the location of the proposed work, undertaking or activity and within the area likely to be affected by the proposed work, undertaking or activity, including

heading: Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (a) the type of water source or water body;

heading: Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (b) the characteristics of the fish habitat and how those characteristics directly or indirectly support fish in carrying out their life processes;

heading: Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (c) the fish species that are present and an estimate of the abundance of those species; and

heading: Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (d) a description of how the information provided under paragraphs (a) to (c) was obtained, including the sources, methods and sampling techniques used.

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: 9 (1) A detailed description of the likely effects of the proposed work, undertaking or activity on fish and fish habitat. The description must include

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (a) the fish species that are likely to be affected and the life stages of the individuals of those species;

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (b) the extent and type of fish habitat that is likely to be affected;

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (c) the probability, magnitude, geographic extent and duration of the likely effects on fish and fish habitat; and

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (d) a description of how the information provided under paragraphs (a) to (c) was derived, including the methodologies used.

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (2) A detailed description of

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (a) how the effects referred to in subsection (1) are likely to result in the death of fish or the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat; and

heading: Effects on Fish and Fish Habitat
paragraph: (b) the extent of the elements referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Measures and Standards
paragraph: 10 A detailed description of the measures and standards that will be implemented, including an analysis of the expected effectiveness of those measures and standards, to

heading: Measures and Standards
paragraph: (a) avoid the death of fish or to mitigate the extent of their death; or

heading: Measures and Standards
paragraph: (b) avoid or mitigate the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat.

heading: Measures and Standards
paragraph: 11 A detailed description of the monitoring measures that will be implemented to assess the effectiveness of the measures and standards referred to in section 10.

heading: Measures and Standards
paragraph: 12 A detailed description of the contingency measures that will be implemented if the measures and standards referred to in section 10 do not meet their objectives.

heading: Measures and Standards
paragraph: 13 A quantitative and detailed description of the death of fish referred to in subsection 9(2) after the measures and standards referred to in paragraph 10(a) are implemented.

heading: Measures and Standards
paragraph: 14 A quantitative and detailed description of the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat referred to in subsection 9(2) after the measures and standards referred to in paragraph 10(b) are implemented.

heading: Habitat Credit
paragraph: 15 The number of habitat credits that the applicant plans to use to offset the death of fish referred to in section 13 and the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat referred to in section 14, as well as the number of any certificate referred to in paragraph 42.02(1)(b) of the Act.

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: 16 A detailed description of a plan to offset the death of fish referred to in section 13 and the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat referred to in section 14 that were not offset by the habitat credits referred to in section 15, including

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (a) the geographic coordinates of the location where offsetting measures will be implemented;

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (b) a small-scale site plan identifying the general location and boundaries of the location where the measures will be implemented;

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (c) a detailed description of the measures and how those measures will meet their objectives;

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (d) a detailed description of the monitoring measures that will be implemented to assess the effectiveness of the measures referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (e) a detailed description of the contingency measures and associated monitoring measures that will be implemented if the measures referred to in paragraph (c) do not meet their objectives;

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (f) a detailed description of any adverse effects on fish and fish habitat that could result from the implementation of the plan;

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (g) a detailed description of the measures and standards that will be implemented to avoid or mitigate the adverse effects and how those measures will meet their objectives;

heading: Offsetting Plan

heading: Offsetting Plan
paragraph: (i) an estimate of the cost of implementing each element of the plan; and

heading: Offsetting Plan

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Annex means the Annex to the Convention. (Annexe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ballast water has the same meaning as in article 1 of the Convention. (eaux de ballast)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ballast water exchange standard means the standard set out in regulation D-1 of the Annex. (norme de renouvellement des eaux de ballast)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ballast water management has the same meaning as in article 1 of the Convention. (gestion des eaux de ballast)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ballast water management system has the same meaning as in the BWMS Code. (systeme de gestion des eaux de ballast)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ballast water performance standard means the standard set out in regulation D-2 of the Annex. (norme de qualite des eaux de ballast)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: BWMS Code means the Code for Approval of Ballast Water Management Systems, published by the International Maritime Organization. (Code BWMS)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian pleasure craft means a pleasure craft that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is licensed under Part 10 of the Act; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is principally maintained or operated in Canada, is not a Canadian vessel and is not registered or licensed under the laws of another state. (embarcation de plaisance canadienne)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Convention means the International Convention for the Control and Management of Ships' Ballast Water and Sediments, 2004, signed at London on February 13, 2004. (Convention)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Great Lakes Basin means the waters of the Great Lakes, their connecting and tributary waters and the waters of the St. Lawrence River as far as the lower exit of the St. Lambert Lock at Montreal in Quebec. (bassin des Grands Lacs)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: IBWM Certificate means the International Ballast Water Management Certificate issued under regulation E-2 or E-3 of the Annex. (certificat IGEB)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Transport. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: release, in respect of ballast water, includes leakage, pumping, pouring, emptying, dumping, spraying or placing. (deversement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: residual amounts means the quantity of ballast water that cannot be removed from a ballast tank using the equipment installed on the vessel for that purpose. (quantite residuelle)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sediments means matter settled out of ballast water within a vessel. (sediments)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: TP 13617 means the document entitled List of Canada's Designated Alternate Ballast Water Exchange Areas and Fresh Waters, published by the Department of Transport. (TP 13617)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: waters under Canadian jurisdiction means Canadian waters and waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada. (eaux de competence canadienne)

heading: Application

heading: Activities related to oil or gas
paragraph: (2) These Regulations apply in respect of vessels referred to in subsection (1) that are capable of engaging in the drilling for, or the production, conservation or processing of, oil or gas, except vessels that are on location and engaged in one of those activities in an area referred to in

heading: Activities related to oil or gas
paragraph: (a) section 3 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act;

heading: Activities related to oil or gas
paragraph: (b) subsection 8(1) of the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Act; or

heading: Activities related to oil or gas
paragraph: (c) subsection 8(1) of the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation Act.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) These Regulations do not apply in respect of

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) vessels operated under the authority of a state that is not a party to the Convention if they are operated exclusively in the Great Lakes Basin and if they do not take on board or release ballast water in waters under Canadian jurisdiction unless it is necessary to ensure the safety of the vessel during a voyage between ports located outside Canada;

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) vessels that are owned or operated by a state and used only in government non-commercial service; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (c) vessels that carry only permanent ballast water in sealed tanks such that it is not subject to release.

heading: Quantity
paragraph: (4) For greater certainty, these Regulations apply to the management of any quantity of ballast water that may be released from a vessel.

heading: Authorized representative and master - Annex
paragraph: 4 (1) Except as otherwise provided by these Regulations, the authorized representative and the master of a vessel must ensure that the requirements of the Annex are met in respect of the vessel.

heading: Authorized representative and master - certain provisions
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative and the master of a vessel must ensure that the requirements of section 8, subsections 14(1), 15(1) and 16(1) and sections 17 to 20, 22 and 23 are met.

heading: Master - ballast water record book
paragraph: (3) The master must ensure, in respect of the ballast water record book, that

heading: Master - ballast water record book
paragraph: (a) the requirements set out in the Annex to make entries are met;

heading: Master - ballast water record book
paragraph: (b) the signature requirements set out in regulation B-2 of the Annex are met;

heading: Master - ballast water record book
paragraph: (c) all entries are maintained on board the vessel in accordance with the requirements set out in regulation B-2 of the Annex; and

heading: Master - ballast water record book
paragraph: (d) the record book is kept readily available for inspection in accordance with the requirements set out in regulation B-2 of the Annex.

heading: Authorized representative - ballast water record book
paragraph: (4) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft must maintain the entries made in the ballast water record book, in accordance with regulation B-2 of the Annex, after the period during which the entries are to be maintained on board the vessel in accordance with that regulation.

heading: Authorized representative and master - regulation E-1
paragraph: (5) The authorized representative and the master of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft must ensure that the following requirements, as set out in regulation E-1 of the Annex, are met:

heading: Authorized representative and master - regulation E-1
paragraph: (a) the reporting requirements if an accident occurs to a vessel or a defect is discovered;

heading: Authorized representative and master - regulation E-1
paragraph: (b) the maintenance requirements; and

heading: Authorized representative and master - regulation E-1
paragraph: (c) the requirement to obtain approval of a change that is made after an inspection.

heading: Canadian vessels
paragraph: 5 (1) The Marine Technical Review Board established under section 26 of the Act is authorized, in respect of Canadian vessels, to exercise the powers of a Party to the Convention conferred by regulation A-4 of the Annex in respect of the requirements of sections 15 and 16 and of regulation B-3 of the Annex.

heading: Other vessels
paragraph: (2) On application by the authorized representative of a vessel other than a Canadian vessel, the Minister is authorized to exempt the vessel from the requirements of sections 15 and 16 and of regulation B-3 of the Annex if the application establishes that the applicable conditions described in regulation A-4 of the Annex are met.

heading: Application
paragraph: 6 (1) This section applies in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) vessels that are less than 50 m in overall length and vessels that are not self-propelled and that are of less than 3,000 gross tonnage, if they are operated exclusively

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, or

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) in waters under Canadian jurisdiction and on the high seas; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) vessels that are described in regulation A-5 of the Annex.

heading: Guidelines
paragraph: (2) A vessel described in subsection (1) may, instead of complying with these Regulations, elect to comply with the requirements set out in the Guidelines for ballast water management equivalent compliance (G3), published by the International Maritime Organization.

heading: Guidelines - recommendations
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of interpreting the guidelines referred to in subsection (2), with the exception of any provision relating to ballast water exchange, "should" is to be read as "must" and recommendations are mandatory.

heading: Approval
paragraph: 7 (1) On application by the authorized representative, the Minister must approve the ballast water management plan of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft if the plan meets the requirements set out in regulation B-1 of the Annex.

heading: Language of plan
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the ballast water management plan must be written in English or French, or in both.

heading: Maintenance
paragraph: 8 A vessel must ensure that its ballast water management plan remains up to date and reflects the means by which the vessel complies with the requirements of these Regulations.

heading: Submission to Minister
paragraph: 9 (1) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft must submit to the Minister any amendment to the ballast water management plan.

heading: Approval of amendments
paragraph: (2) The Minister must approve any amendment to the ballast water management plan if the amendment meets the requirements in respect of the plan that are set out in regulation B-1 of the Annex.

heading: Language of record book
paragraph: 10 Despite regulation B-2 of the Annex, entries made in the ballast water record book of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft must be written in English or French, or in both.

heading: Certain vessels
paragraph: 11 (1) Despite regulation B-3 of the Annex, a vessel constructed before the day on which these Regulations come into force is not required to conduct ballast water management to meet the ballast water performance standard until September 8, 2024, and a vessel constructed before January 1, 2009 is not required to conduct ballast water management to meet that standard until September 8, 2030, if the vessel is operated exclusively

heading: Certain vessels
paragraph: (a) in waters under Canadian jurisdiction and, if applicable, the United States' waters of the Great Lakes Basin; or

heading: Certain vessels
paragraph: (b) in waters described in paragraph (a) and on the high seas.

heading: Definition of constructed
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), constructed has the same meaning as in regulation A-1 of the Annex.

heading: Deemed compliance
paragraph: 12 (1) A vessel using a ballast water management system to meet the ballast water performance standard is deemed to have met that standard in respect of ballast water taken on board in the Great Lakes Basin or in the eastern waters of the St. Lawrence River, if

heading: Deemed compliance
paragraph: (a) the vessel's ballast water management system was installed before September 8, 2024 or, in the case of a vessel constructed before January 1, 2009 that is operated exclusively in waters described in paragraph 11(1)(a) or (b), the system was installed before September 8, 2030;

heading: Deemed compliance
paragraph: (b) the vessel meets the requirements of section 8;

heading: Deemed compliance
paragraph: (c) the vessel holds and keeps on board a valid IBWM Certificate or an equivalent document referred to in section 23;

heading: Deemed compliance
paragraph: (d) the vessel's ballast water management system is in good working order and has been maintained and operated in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions; and

heading: Deemed compliance
paragraph: (e) the ballast water is managed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions for the vessel's ballast water management system, subject to any limiting operating conditions or other restrictions identified in the Type Approval Certificate evidencing the system's approval under regulation D-3 of the Annex.

heading: Definition of eastern waters of the St. Lawrence River
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), eastern waters of the St. Lawrence River means the waters of the St. Lawrence River from the lower exit of the St. Lambert Lock at Montreal in Quebec as far seaward as a straight line drawn from Cap-des-Rosiers to Pointe Ouest, Anticosti Island, and from Anticosti Island to the north shore of the St. Lawrence River along the meridian of longitude 63° W, and their connecting and tributary waters.

heading: Alternative methods
paragraph: 13 A vessel may, instead of conducting ballast water management to meet the ballast water exchange standard or the ballast water performance standard, as applicable,

heading: Alternative methods
paragraph: (a) conduct ballast water management in accordance with an alternative method referred to in regulation B-3.7 of the Annex if that method has been approved in accordance with the requirements of that regulation; or

heading: Alternative methods
paragraph: (b) release potable water, taken on board as ballast water from a public or commercial source in Canada or the United States, into waters under Canadian jurisdiction or on the high seas if it has not been mixed with other ballast water, including residual amounts, or with sediments.

heading: Areas for exchange
paragraph: 14 (1) A vessel that enters waters under Canadian jurisdiction from waters other than the United States' waters of the Great Lakes Basin and that conducts ballast water management to meet the ballast water exchange standard must conduct the exchange

heading: Areas for exchange
paragraph: (a) in an area that is at least 200 nautical miles from the nearest land and where water depth is at least 2 000 m;

heading: Areas for exchange
paragraph: (b) in an area described in, and in accordance with, regulation B-4.1 of the Annex, if the vessel cannot meet the requirements of paragraph (a); or

heading: Areas for exchange
paragraph: (c) in one of the alternate ballast water exchange areas designated by the Minister in TP 13617, if the vessel cannot meet the requirements of paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Record keeping
paragraph: (2) The master of a vessel that does not comply with subsection (1) must enter the reasons in the ballast water record book.

heading: Exchange requirement
paragraph: 15 (1) In addition to meeting the requirements of the Convention, a vessel that conducts ballast water management to meet the ballast water performance standard must not release ballast water in Canadian fresh waters described in TP 13617 unless that ballast water was first exchanged in accordance with the ballast water exchange standard

heading: Exchange requirement
paragraph: (a) in an area, and in the manner, described in subsection 14(1), if the sequential method - as described in the 2017 Guidelines for ballast water exchange (G6), published by the International Maritime Organization - was used; or

heading: Exchange requirement
paragraph: (b) on the high seas, in any other case.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if the ballast water to be released was taken on board in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, in the United States' waters of the Great Lakes Basin or in waters in an area described in subsection 14(1) and has not been mixed with residual amounts taken elsewhere than from those waters.

heading: Exception - extraordinary conditions
paragraph: (3) A vessel is not required to exchange ballast water in accordance with subsection (1) if the master determines, on reasonable grounds, that the exchange would threaten the safety or stability of the vessel, its crew or its passengers because of adverse weather, vessel design or stress, equipment failure or any other extraordinary conditions.

heading: Record keeping
paragraph: (4) The master of a vessel that does not comply with subsection (1) must enter the reasons in the ballast water record book.

heading: Residual amounts
paragraph: 16 (1) In addition to meeting the requirements of the Convention, a vessel that conducts ballast water management to meet the ballast water exchange standard must conduct a saltwater flushing of tanks that contain only residual amounts unless those residual amounts were taken on board in accordance with the ballast water exchange standard and subsection 14(1).

heading: Saltwater flushing
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), saltwater flushing consists of the following measures undertaken in the following order:

heading: Saltwater flushing
paragraph: (a) the addition of water to the ballast tanks in accordance with the requirements for ballast water exchange set out in subsection 14(1);

heading: Saltwater flushing
paragraph: (b) the mixing, through the motion of the vessel, of the water added under paragraph (a) with the residual amounts and any sediments that have settled in the tanks; and

heading: Saltwater flushing
paragraph: (c) the release, in accordance with the requirements for ballast water exchange set out in subsection 14(1), of the waters mixed under paragraph (b) so that the salinity of the resulting residual amounts in the tanks exceeds 30 parts per thousand or is as close as possible to 30 parts per thousand.

heading: Minister's approval
paragraph: 17 Any ballast water management system used on a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft must be approved by the Minister in accordance with regulation D-3 of the Annex.

heading: Type Approval Certificate
paragraph: 18 A vessel must keep on board a copy of the Type Approval Certificate issued in respect of a ballast water management system installed on the vessel that evidences the system's approval under regulation D-3 of the Annex.

heading: Statement of Compliance
paragraph: 19 A vessel that is participating in one of the programs referred to in regulation D-4 of the Annex must hold and keep on board a valid Statement of Compliance referred to in the Guidelines for approval and oversight of prototype ballast water treatment technology programmes (G10), published by the International Maritime Organization.

heading: IBWM Certificate
paragraph: 20 Every vessel to which regulation E-1 of the Annex applies must hold and keep on board a valid IBWM Certificate.

heading: Issuance of certificate
paragraph: 21 On application by the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft, the Minister must issue an IBWM Certificate to the vessel or pleasure craft if the requirements of an initial or renewal inspection set out in section E of the Annex are met.

heading: Endorsements
paragraph: 22 A Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft that holds an IBWM Certificate must ensure that the certificate is endorsed by the Minister as required by section E of the Annex.

heading: Equivalent document
paragraph: 23 A vessel that is entitled to fly the flag of a state that is not a party to the Convention must not take on board or release ballast water in waters under Canadian jurisdiction unless that vessel holds and keeps on board a document issued by or on behalf of the government of that state that certifies that the vessel meets the requirements of the Convention.

heading: Canadian Ballast Water Reporting Form
paragraph: 24 The master of a vessel that is bound for a port, offshore terminal or anchorage area in Canada must, in the manner specified by the Minister, submit a completed Canadian Ballast Water Reporting Form to the Minister.

heading: Repeal
paragraph: Return to footnote 3SOR/2011-237
