paragraph: (2) If no notice is given under subsection (1), the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator shall, no later than one year after the day on which it receives data from the last of three drillings of the same geological feature in the perimeter, notify each appropriate regulator of its determination or that there is insufficient information to make a determination based on the data from those drillings.

heading: Notice - transboundary pool
paragraph: (3) If the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator determines that a pool exists, the Commission shall also specify in the notice whether or not there is, in its opinion, reason to believe that the pool is transboundary.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (4) The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator shall provide each appropriate regulator and the Minister with the reasons for its determination and opinion.

heading: Notice from Canadian Energy Regulator
paragraph: 48.13 (1) If the Canadian Energy Regulator receives a notice from a regulator indicating the regulator's determination as to whether a pool exists in an area adjoining the perimeter and, if applicable, whether there is reason to believe the pool extends into the perimeter, the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator shall, within 90 days after the day on which the notice is received, inform the regulator of its agreement or disagreement with the content of the notice.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (2) If the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator disagrees with the content of the notice, it shall provide the regulator with the reasons for its disagreement.

heading: Delineation
paragraph: 48.14 (1) If, after receiving a notice under section 48.12 or 48.13, the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator and the regulator in question agree that a pool exists, the Commission and that regulator shall jointly determine whether that pool is transboundary and, if so, they shall jointly delineate its boundaries.

heading: Disagreement
paragraph: (2) The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator or the regulator may, if they disagree about whether a pool exists, whether the pool is transboundary or its delineation, refer the matter to an expert, no later than 180 days after the day on which the Commission issues a notice under section 48.12, or the regulator issues an equivalent notice.

heading: Appropriate regulator
paragraph: 48.15 For the purposes of sections 48.16 to 48.27, the appropriate regulator is the regulator that has jurisdiction in an area into which the transboundary pool or field in question extends.

heading: Joint exploitation agreement
paragraph: 48.16 The Minister and the appropriate regulator may enter into a joint exploitation agreement providing for the development of a transboundary pool or field as a single field. The agreement shall include any matters provided for by regulation.

heading: Development as a single field
paragraph: 48.17 (1) If a joint exploitation agreement has been entered into, the transboundary pool or field may only be developed as a single field. The development of that field is subject to the following agreements having been entered into and subsequently approved under subsection 48.2(2) or 48.23(4):

heading: Development as a single field
paragraph: (a) a unit agreement that includes the details referred to in paragraphs 40(2)(a) to (d); and

heading: Development as a single field
paragraph: (b) a unit operating agreement that includes the details referred to in paragraphs 40(3)(a) to (e).

heading: Joint exploitation agreement prevails
paragraph: (2) The joint exploitation agreement prevails over the unit agreement and the unit operating agreement to the extent of any inconsistency between them.

heading: Intention to start production
paragraph: 48.18 (1) If an interest owner - as defined in the Canada Petroleum Resources Act - advises the Minister or the Canadian Energy Regulator, including by way of an application under paragraph 5(1)(b) of this Act or under section 38 of the Canada Petroleum Resources Act, that it intends to start production from a transboundary pool or field, the Minister shall notify the appropriate regulator as soon as feasible of the interest owner's intention.

heading: Referral to expert
paragraph: (2) If the Minister and the regulator have attempted to enter into a joint exploitation agreement but have been unsuccessful, the Minister or the regulator may, 180 days after the day on which the Minister gives notice under subsection (1), refer the matter to an expert to determine the particulars of the agreement. They may, however, agree to refer the matter to an expert at any time before the end of those 180 days.

heading: Unit agreement
paragraph: 48.19 (1) The royalty owners and the working interest owners in a transboundary pool or field that is to be developed as a single field may enter into a unit agreement and, once approved, shall operate their interests in accordance with it, including any amendment to it.

heading: Applicable provisions
paragraph: (2) Subsections 37(2) and (3) apply to the unit agreement.

heading: Condition precedent
paragraph: 48.2 (1) A unit agreement and unit operating agreement are to be jointly approved by the Minister and the appropriate regulator before an authorization is issued under paragraph 5(1)(b) for a work or activity proposed to be carried on in relation to the development of a transboundary pool or field as a single field.

heading: Approval
paragraph: (2) The Minister and the appropriate regulator may approve the unit agreement if all the royalty owners and all the working interest owners in the pool or field are parties to it; the Minister and the appropriate regulator may approve the unit operating agreement if all the working interest owners in the pool or field are parties to it.

heading: Application for unitization order
paragraph: 48.21 (1) One or more working interest owners who are parties to a unit agreement and a unit operating agreement and own in total 65% or more of the working interests in a transboundary pool or field that is to be developed as a single field may apply for a unitization order with respect to the agreements.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The application shall be submitted to both the Minister and the appropriate regulator. It shall include the documents and statements referred to in subsection 40(1) and may be made by the unit operator or proposed unit operator on behalf of the working interest owners.

heading: Appointment of expert
paragraph: (3) The Minister and the regulator shall, for the purposes of section 48.22, appoint an expert in accordance with subsections 48.27(2) to (4).

heading: Hearing
paragraph: 48.22 (1) Once seized of an application made under section 48.21, the expert shall hold a hearing at which all interested persons shall be given an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Conclusion of hearing
paragraph: (2) On the conclusion of the hearing, the expert shall request that the Minister and the appropriate regulator

heading: Conclusion of hearing
paragraph: (a) order that the unit agreement is a valid contract enuring to the benefit of all the royalty owners and working interest owners who have an interest in the unit area and binding on and enforceable against all such owners, and that the unit operating agreement is a valid contract enuring to the benefit of all the working interest owners who have an interest in the unit area and binding on and enforceable against all such owners; and

heading: Conclusion of hearing
paragraph: (b) include in the order any variations to the unit agreement or unit operating agreement that the expert determines are necessary to allow for the more efficient or more economical production of oil or gas from the unitized zone.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), the expert shall end the hearing and request that the Minister and the appropriate regulator take the measure outlined in paragraph (2)(a) if the expert finds that,

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) on the day on which the hearing begins,

heading: Exception
paragraph: (i) the unit agreement and the unit operating agreement have been executed by one or more working interest owners who own in total 65% or more of the total working interests in the unit area, and

heading: Exception
paragraph: (ii) the unit agreement has been executed by one or more royalty owners who own in total 65% or more of the total royalty interests in the unit area; and

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the unitization order applied for would allow for the more efficient or more economical production of oil or gas from the unitized zone.

heading: Unitization order
paragraph: 48.23 (1) The Minister shall issue an order in accordance with the expert's request under subsection 48.22(2) or (3).

heading: Effect of unitization order
paragraph: (2) The unit agreement and the unit operating agreement have the effect given to them by the Minister's order.

heading: Equivalent order
paragraph: (3) A unitization order becomes effective only if the appropriate regulator has issued an equivalent order.

heading: Joint approval
paragraph: (4) The issuance of a unitization order by the Minister and of an equivalent order by the regulator is deemed to be their joint approval of the unit agreement and the unit operating agreement.

heading: Effective date of unitization order
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsections (3) and (6), a unitization order becomes effective on the date set out in the order, but that date shall not be less than 30 days after the day on which the order is made.

heading: Order revoked
paragraph: (6) The Minister shall immediately revoke a unitization order that varies a unit agreement or a unit operating agreement if, before the effective date of that order, the applicant files with the Minister a notice withdrawing the application on behalf of the working interest owners or there are filed with the Minister statements objecting to the order and signed

heading: Order revoked
paragraph: (a) in the case of the unit agreement, by

heading: Order revoked
paragraph: (i) one or more working interest owners who own in total more than 25% of the total working interests in the unit area and are part of the group that owns 65% or more of the total working interests as described in subparagraph 48.22(3)(a)(i), and

heading: Order revoked
paragraph: (ii) one or more royalty owners who own in total more than 25% of the total royalty interests in the unit area and are part of the group that owns 65% or more of the total royalty interests as described in subparagraph 48.22(3)(a)(ii); or

heading: Order revoked
paragraph: (b) in the case of the unit operating agreement, by one or more working interest owners who own in total more than 25% of the total working interests in the unit area and are part of the group that owns 65% or more of the total working interests as described in subparagraph 48.22(3)(a)(i).

heading: Application of sections 43 and 46
paragraph: (7) Sections 43 and 46 apply to the unitization order.

heading: Amending unitization order
paragraph: 48.24 (1) A unitization order may be amended on the application of a working interest owner submitted to both the Minister and the appropriate regulator.

heading: Appointment of expert
paragraph: (2) The Minister and the regulator shall appoint an expert in accordance with subsections 48.27(2) to (4) for the purposes of this section.

heading: Hearing
paragraph: (3) Once seized of the application, the expert shall hold a hearing at which all interested persons shall be given an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Conclusion of hearing
paragraph: (4) On the conclusion of the hearing, the expert may request that the Minister order the amendment of the unitization order in accordance with the amendment proposed and to include in the order any variations to it that the expert determines are necessary to allow for the more efficient or more economical production of oil or gas from the unitized zone. If the expert makes such a request, the expert shall also request that the appropriate regulator order the amendment of its equivalent order in the same way.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (5) If the expert finds that, on the day on which the hearing begins, one or more working interest owners who own in total 65% or more of the total working interests and one or more royalty interest owners who own in total 65% or more of the total royalty interests in the unit area have consented to the proposed amendment, the expert may end the hearing and request that the Minister amend the unitization order in accordance with the amendment proposed. If the expert makes such a request, the expert shall also request that the appropriate regulator amend its equivalent order in the same way.

heading: Application of section 48.23
paragraph: (6) Section 48.23 applies, with any modifications that the circumstances require, to an amended unitization order.

heading: Protection of tract participation ratios
paragraph: 48.25 No amendment shall be made under section 48.24 that will alter the ratios between the tract participations of those tracts that were qualified for inclusion in the unit area before the commencement of the hearing, and, for the purposes of this section, the tract participations shall be those indicated in the unit agreement when it became subject to a unitization order.

heading: Determination - percentages of interests
paragraph: 48.26 The percentages of interests referred to in subsections 48.21(1), 48.22(3), 48.23(6) and 48.24(5) shall be determined in accordance with section 47.

heading: Notice
paragraph: 48.27 (1) The party that intends to refer a matter to an expert under subsection 5.1(9), 5.2(6), 48.14(2) or 48.18(2) shall notify the other party of their intention.

heading: Appointment - single expert
paragraph: (2) Within 30 days after the day on which a notice is given under subsection (1) or an application is made under subsection 48.21(1) or 48.24(1), the parties shall agree on the appointment of an expert who shall be seized of the matter.

heading: Appointment - expert panel
paragraph: (3) If the parties do not agree on the appointment of a single expert, they shall, within 30 days after the day on which the period to jointly appoint an expert under subsection (2) ends, each appoint one expert to a panel and those experts shall, in turn, jointly appoint an additional expert as chairperson. If there is no agreement on the appointment of a chairperson within 30 days after the day of the last appointment, the chairperson shall be appointed by the Chief Justice of the Federal Court within 30 days after the period for appointing a chairperson ends. Once the chairperson is appointed, the expert panel shall be seized of the matter.

heading: Qualifications - expert
paragraph: (4) An expert shall be impartial and independent, and have knowledge or experience relative to the subject of disagreement between the parties.

heading: Decisions
paragraph: (5) Decisions of an expert panel shall be made on the basis of a majority vote of the members. The chairperson's vote is the deciding vote in the case of a tie.

heading: Time limit
paragraph: (6) The expert's decision shall be made no later than 270 days after the day on which they were seized of the matter.

heading: Decision is final and binding
paragraph: (7) Subject to judicial review, a decision made by an expert is final and binding on all parties specified in the decision from the date specified in it.

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (8) An expert shall cause records to be kept of their hearings and proceedings and shall deposit their records with the Minister when their activities to which the records relate have ceased.

heading: Orders and decisions final
paragraph: 49 (1) Except as provided in this Act, every decision or order of the Committee is final and conclusive.

heading: Decision or order defined
paragraph: (2) Any minute or other record of the Committee or any document issued by the Committee, in the form of a decision or order, shall for the purposes of this section be deemed to be a decision or order of the Committee.

heading: Stated case for Federal Court
paragraph: 50 (1) The Committee may of its own motion, or at the request of the Minister, state a case, in writing, for the opinion of the Federal Court on any question that in the opinion of the Committee is a question of law or of the jurisdiction of the Committee.

heading: Proceedings thereon
paragraph: (2) The Federal Court shall hear and determine the case stated and remit the matter to the Committee with the opinion of the Court thereon.

heading: Governor in Council may review orders of Committee
paragraph: 51 The Governor in Council may at any time, in his discretion, either on petition of any interested person or of his own motion, vary or rescind any decision or order of the Committee made under this Act, whether the order is made between parties or otherwise and any order that the Governor in Council makes with respect thereto becomes a decision or order of the Committee and, subject to section 52, is binding on the Committee and on all parties.

heading: Appeal to Federal Court
paragraph: 52 (1) An appeal lies from a decision or order of the Committee to the Federal Court on a question of law, on leave therefor being obtained from the Federal Court, in accordance with the practice of that Court, on application made within one month after the making of the decision or order sought to be appealed from or within such further time as that Court may allow.

heading: Staying order
paragraph: (3) Where leave to appeal is granted pursuant to subsection (1), any order of the Committee in respect of which the appeal is made shall be stayed until the matter of the appeal is determined.

heading: Powers of the Court
paragraph: (4) After the hearing of the appeal pursuant to this section, the Supreme Court of Canada shall certify its opinion to the Committee and the Committee shall make any order necessary to comply with the opinion.

heading: Order subject to section 51
paragraph: (5) Any order made by the Committee pursuant to subsection (4), unless the order has already been dealt with by the Governor in Council pursuant to section 51, shall be subject to that section.

heading: Officers
paragraph: 53 The Chief Executive Officer of the Canadian Energy Regulator designates the safety officers and conservation officers necessary for the administration and enforcement of this Act and the regulations from among the employees of the Canadian Energy Regulator.

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: 54 (1) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this Act and the regulations, a safety officer, the Chief Safety Officer, a conservation officer or the Chief Conservation Officer may at any reasonable time

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (a) enter any place, including lands, buildings, installations, vessels, vehicles and aircraft, used for any work or activity in respect of which this Act applies, for the purpose of carrying out inspections, examinations, tests or inquiries or of directing that the person in charge of the place carry them out, and the officer may be accompanied by any other person that the officer believes is necessary to help carry out the inspection, examination, test or inquiry;

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (b) take photographs or make drawings of any place or thing referred to in this section;

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (c) order that any place or thing referred to in this section not be interfered with for a specified period;

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (d) require the production, for inspection or copying, of any books, records, documents, licences or permits required by this Act or the regulations;

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (e) take samples or particulars and carry out, or have carried out, any reasonable tests or examinations; and

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (f) require the person in charge of the place, or any other person in the place who has knowledge relevant to an inspection, examination, test or inquiry, to furnish information, either orally or in writing, in the form requested.

heading: Compliance audit
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, the powers set out in subsection (1) include the power to conduct a compliance audit.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: 55 The Chief Executive Officer of the Canadian Energy Regulator must provide every safety officer and conservation officer and the Chief Safety Officer and the Chief Conservation Officer with a certificate of appointment or designation and, on entering any place under this Act, the officer must, upon request, produce the certificate to the person in charge of the place.

heading: Assistance to officers
paragraph: 56 The owner, the person in charge of any place referred to in subsection 54(1) and every person found in the place shall give a safety officer, the Chief Safety Officer, a conservation officer or the Chief Conservation Officer, as the case may be, all reasonable assistance to enable the officer to carry out duties and functions under this Act or the regulations.

heading: Obstruction of officers and making of false statements
paragraph: 57 No person shall obstruct or hinder or make a false or misleading statement, either orally or in writing, to a safety officer, the Chief Safety Officer, a conservation officer or the Chief Conservation Officer who is engaged in carrying out duties and functions under this Act or the regulations.

heading: Power of officers
paragraph: 58 (1) A safety officer, the Chief Safety Officer, a conservation officer or the Chief Conservation Officer may order that an operation or activity in any area to which this Act applies cease or be continued only in accordance with the terms of the order if the officer, on reasonable grounds, is of the opinion that its continuation could result in harm to a person, damage to the environment or property or a breach of security, or is not in compliance with this Act or the regulations, and

heading: Power of officers
paragraph: (a) the operation is in relation to the exploration or drilling for or the production, conservation, processing or transportation of oil or gas; or

heading: Power of officers
paragraph: (b) the activity is prohibited by an order or regulation made under section 15.1.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) The officer who makes an order under subsection (1) shall affix at or near the scene of the operation a notice of the order in a form approved by the Canadian Energy Regulator.

heading: Expiry of order
paragraph: (3) An order made by a safety officer or a conservation officer under subsection (1) expires 72 hours after it is made unless it is confirmed before that time by order of the Chief Safety Officer or the Chief Conservation Officer, as the case may be.

heading: Modification or revocation
paragraph: (4) A safety officer or a conservation officer who makes an order under subsection (1) shall immediately so advise the Chief Safety Officer or the Chief Conservation Officer, as the case may be, and that Chief Officer may modify or revoke the order.

heading: Referral for review
paragraph: (5) A person carrying out an operation to which an order made under subsection (1) refers, or any person having a pecuniary interest in that operation, may, by notice in writing, request the Chief Safety Officer or the Chief Conservation Officer, as the case may be, to refer the order to the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator for a review of the need for the order under section 386 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act and, on receiving the notice, that Chief Officer must refer the order accordingly.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (6) A person is prohibited from continuing an operation in respect of which an order has been made under this section, except in accordance with the terms of the order or until the order has been set aside by the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator under section 386 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act.

heading: Priority
paragraph: 58.1 An order made by a safety officer or the Chief Safety Officer prevails over an order made by a conservation officer or the Chief Conservation Officer to the extent of any inconsistency between the orders.

heading: Installation manager
paragraph: 58.2 (1) Every holder of an authorization under paragraph 5(1)(b) in respect of a work or activity for which a prescribed installation is to be used shall put in command of the installation a manager who meets any prescribed qualifications, and the installation manager is responsible for the safety of the installation and the persons at it.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (2) Subject to this Act and any other Act of Parliament, an installation manager has the power to do such things as are required to ensure the safety of the installation and the persons at it and, more particularly, may

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) give orders to any person who is at the installation;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) order that any person who is at the installation be restrained or removed; and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) obtain information or documents.

heading: Emergency
paragraph: (3) In a prescribed emergency situation, an installation manager's powers are extended so that they also apply to each operator of a vessel, vehicle or aircraft that is at the installation or that is leaving or approaching it.

heading: Offences with respect to documents and records
paragraph: 59 A person is guilty of an offence who

heading: Offences with respect to documents and records
paragraph: (a) knowingly makes any false entry or statement in any report, record or document required by this Act or the regulations or by any order made pursuant to this Act or the regulations; or

heading: Offences with respect to documents and records
paragraph: (b) knowingly destroys, mutilates or falsifies any report or other document required by this Act or the regulations or by any order made pursuant to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Offences
paragraph: 60 (1) Every person is guilty of an offence who

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) contravenes this Act or the regulations;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) produces any oil or gas from a pool or field under the terms of a unit agreement within the meaning of Part II, or any amended unit agreement, before the unit agreement or amended unit agreement is filed with the Chief Conservation Officer;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) undertakes or carries on a work or activity without an authorization under paragraph 5(1)(b) or without complying with the approvals or requirements of such an authorization; or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) fails to comply with a direction, requirement or order of a safety officer, the Chief Safety Officer, a conservation officer, the Chief Conservation Officer or an installation manager or with an order of the Committee or the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator made under this Act.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who is guilty of an offence under subsection (1) is liable

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand dollars or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or to both; or

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine not exceeding one million dollars or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or to both.

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (3) In addition to the principles and factors that the court is otherwise required to consider, including those set out in sections 718.1 to 718.21 of the Criminal Code, the court shall consider the following principles when sentencing a person who is found guilty of an offence under this Act:

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (a) the amount of the fine should be increased to account for every aggravating factor associated with the offence, including the aggravating factors set out in subsection (4); and

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (b) the amount of the fine should reflect the gravity of each aggravating factor associated with the offence.

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (4) The aggravating factors are the following:

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (a) the offence caused harm or risk of harm to human health or safety;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (b) the offence caused damage or risk of damage to the environment or to environmental quality;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (c) the offence caused damage or risk of damage to any unique, rare, particularly important or vulnerable component of the environment;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (d) the damage or harm caused by the offence is extensive, persistent or irreparable;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (e) the offender committed the offence intentionally or recklessly;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (f) the offender failed to take reasonable steps to prevent the commission of the offence;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (g) by committing the offence or failing to take action to prevent its commission, the offender increased their revenue or decreased their costs or intended to increase their revenue or decrease their costs;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (h) the offender has a history of non-compliance with federal or provincial legislation that relates to safety or environmental conservation or protection; and

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) after the commission of the offence, the offender

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) attempted to conceal its commission,

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (ii) failed to take prompt action to prevent, mitigate or remediate its effects, or

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (iii) failed to take prompt action to reduce the risk of committing similar offences in the future.

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: (5) The absence of an aggravating factor set out in subsection (4) is not a mitigating factor.

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: Meaning of damage

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of paragraphs (4)(b) to (d), damage includes loss of use value and non-use value.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (7) If the court is satisfied of the existence of one or more of the aggravating factors set out in subsection (4) but decides not to increase the amount of the fine because of that factor, the court shall give reasons for that decision.

heading: Presumption against waste
paragraph: 63 A person does not commit an offence under subsection 18(1) by reason of committing waste as defined in paragraph 18(2)(f) or (g) unless the person has been ordered by the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator under section 385 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act to take measures to prevent the waste and has failed to comply.

heading: Order of court
paragraph: 65 (1) If a person is found guilty of an offence under this Act, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, in addition to any other punishment that may be imposed under this Act, make an order that has any or all of the following effects:

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the offender from committing an act or engaging in an activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (b) directing the offender to take any action that the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment that results or may result from the act or omission that constituted the offence;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (c) directing the offender to carry out environmental effects monitoring in the manner established by the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator or directing the offender to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount of money for the purposes of environmental effects monitoring;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (d) directing the offender to make changes to their environmental management system that are satisfactory to the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (e) directing the offender to have an environmental audit conducted by a person of a class and at the times specified by the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator and directing the offender to remedy any deficiencies revealed during the audit;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (f) directing the offender to pay to Her Majesty in right of Canada, for the purpose of promoting the conservation, protection or restoration of the environment, or to pay into the Environmental Damages Fund - an account in the accounts of Canada - an amount of money that the court considers appropriate;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (g) directing the offender to publish, in the manner specified by the court, the facts relating to the commission of the offence and the details of the punishment imposed, including any orders made under this subsection;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (h) directing the offender to notify, at the offender's own cost and in the manner specified by the court, any person aggrieved or affected by the offender's conduct of the facts relating to the commission of the offence and of the details of the punishment imposed, including any orders made under this subsection;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (i) directing the offender to post a bond or pay an amount of money into court that the court considers appropriate to ensure that the offender complies with any prohibition, direction, requirement or condition that is specified in the order;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (j) directing the offender to perform community service, subject to any reasonable conditions that may be imposed by the court;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (k) directing the offender to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount of money to environmental, health or other groups to assist in their work in the community where the offence was committed;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (l) directing the offender to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount of money to an educational institution including for scholarships for students enrolled in studies related to the environment;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (m) requiring the offender to comply with any conditions that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances for securing the offender's good conduct and for preventing the offender from repeating the same offence or committing another offence under this Act;

heading: Order of court
paragraph: (n) prohibiting the offender from taking measures to acquire an interest under the Canada Petroleum Resources Act or from applying for any new licence or other authorization under this Act during any period that the court considers appropriate.

heading: Coming into force and duration of order
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) comes into force on the day on which the order is made or on any other day that the court may determine, but shall not continue in force for more than three years after that day.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (3) If an offender does not comply with an order requiring the publication of facts relating to the offence and the details of the punishment, the Canadian Energy Regulator may, in the manner that the court directed the offender, publish those facts and details and recover the costs of publication from the offender.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (4) If the Canadian Energy Regulator incurs publication costs under subsection (3), the costs constitute a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Variation of sanctions
paragraph: 65.1 (1) Subject to subsection (2), if a court has made, in relation to an offender, an order under section 65, the court may, on application by the offender or the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator, require the offender to appear before it and, after hearing the offender and the Commission, vary the order in one or more of the following ways that the court considers appropriate because of a change in the offender's circumstances since the order was made:

heading: Variation of sanctions
paragraph: (a) by making changes to any prohibition, direction, requirement or condition that is specified in the order for any period or by extending the period during which the order is to remain in force, not exceeding one year; or

heading: Variation of sanctions
paragraph: (b) by decreasing the period during which the order is to remain in force or by relieving the offender of compliance with any condition that is specified in the order, either absolutely or partially or for any period.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) Before making an order under subsection (1), the court may direct that notice be given to any persons that the court considers to be interested, and may hear any of those persons.

heading: Subsequent applications with leave
paragraph: 65.2 If an application made under subsection 65.1(1) in relation to an offender has been heard by a court, no other application may be made under section 65.1 in relation to the offender except with leave of the court.

heading: Recovery of fines and amounts
paragraph: 65.3 If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act and a fine that is imposed is not paid when required or if a court orders an offender to pay an amount under subsection 65(1) or 65.1(1), the prosecutor may, by filing the conviction or order, as the case may be, enter as a judgment the amount of the fine or the amount ordered to be paid, and costs, if any, in any court of competent jurisdiction in Canada, and the judgment is enforceable against the person in the same manner as if it were a judgment rendered against them in that court in civil proceedings.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: 66 Where an offence under this Act is committed on more than one day or is continued for more than one day, it shall be deemed to be a separate offence for each day on which the offence is committed or continued.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 68 A prosecution for an offence under this Act may be instituted at any time within but not later than two years after the time when the subject-matter of the complaint arose.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: 69 In any prosecution for an offence under this Act, a copy of an order purporting to have been made pursuant to this Act or the regulations and purporting to have been signed by the person authorized by this Act or the regulations to make that order is evidence of the matters set out therein.

heading: Jurisdiction of judge or justice
paragraph: 70 Any complaint or information in respect of an offence under this Act may be heard, tried or determined by a justice or judge if the accused is resident or carrying on business within the territorial jurisdiction of that justice or judge although the matter of the complaint or information did not arise in that territorial jurisdiction.

heading: Action to enjoin not prejudiced by prosecution
paragraph: 71 (1) Notwithstanding that a prosecution has been instituted in respect of an offence under this Act, the regulations or any order made pursuant to this Act or the regulations, Her Majesty in right of Canada may commence and maintain an action to enjoin the committing of any contravention of this Act, the regulations or any order made pursuant to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Civil remedy not affected
paragraph: (2) No civil remedy for any act or omission is suspended or affected by reason that the act or omission is an offence under this Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 71.01 (1) The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) designating as a violation that may be proceeded with in accordance with this Act

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) the contravention of any specified provision of this Act or of any of its regulations,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii) the contravention of any direction, requirement, decision or order, or of any direction, requirement, decision or order of a specified class of directions, requirements, decisions or orders, made under this Act, or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (iii) the failure to comply with any term, condition or requirement of

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (A) an operating licence or authorization or any specified class of operating licences or authorizations, or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (B) any approval, leave or exemption or any specified class of approvals, leave or exemptions granted under this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the determination of, or the method of determining, the amount payable as the penalty, which may be different for individuals and other persons, for each violation; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the service of documents required or authorized under section 71.06, 71.2 or 71.5, including the manner and proof of service and the circumstances under which documents are considered to be served.

heading: Maximum penalty
paragraph: (2) The amount that may be determined under any regulations made under paragraph (1)(b) as the penalty for a violation shall not be more than $25,000, in the case of an individual, and $100,000, in the case of any other person.

heading: Powers
paragraph: 71.02 The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator may

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) establish the form of notices of violation;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) designate persons or classes of persons who are authorized to issue notices of violation;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) establish, in respect of each violation, a short-form description to be used in notices of violation; and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (d) designate persons or classes of persons to conduct reviews under section 71.4.

heading: Commission of violation
paragraph: 71.03 (1) Every person who contravenes or fails to comply with a provision, direction, requirement, decision or order, or term or condition the contravention of which, or the failure to comply with which, is designated to be a violation by a regulation made under paragraph 71.01(1)(a) commits a violation and is liable to a penalty of an amount to be determined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Purpose of penalty
paragraph: (2) The purpose of the penalty is to promote compliance with this Act and not to punish.

heading: Liability of directors, officers, etc.
paragraph: 71.04 If a corporation commits a violation, any director, officer, or agent or mandatary of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the violation is a party to the violation and is liable to a penalty of an amount to be determined in accordance with the regulations, whether or not the corporation has been proceeded against in accordance with this Act.

heading: Proof of violation
paragraph: 71.05 In any proceedings under this Act against a person in relation to a violation, it is sufficient proof of the violation to establish that it was committed by an employee, or agent or mandatary, of the person, whether or not the employee, or agent or mandatary is identified or proceeded against in accordance with this Act.

heading: Issuance and service of notice of violation
paragraph: 71.06 (1) If a person designated under paragraph 71.02(b) believes on reasonable grounds that a person has committed a violation, the designated person may issue a notice of violation and cause it to be served on the person.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The notice of violation shall

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) name the person that is believed to have committed the violation;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) set out the relevant facts surrounding the violation;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) set out the amount of the penalty for the violation;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) inform the person of their right, under section 71.2, to request a review with respect the amount of the penalty or the facts of the violation, and of the prescribed period within which that right is to be exercised;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) inform the person of the manner of paying the penalty set out in the notice; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (f) inform the person that, if they do not exercise their right to request a review or if they do not pay the penalty, they will be considered to have committed the violation and that they are liable to the penalty set out in the notice.

heading: Certain defences not available
paragraph: 71.07 (1) A person named in a notice of violation does not have a defence by reason that the person

heading: Certain defences not available
paragraph: (a) exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the violation; or

heading: Certain defences not available
paragraph: (b) reasonably and honestly believed in the existence of facts that, if true, would exonerate the person.

heading: Common law principles
paragraph: (2) Every rule and principle of the common law that renders any circumstance a justification or excuse in relation to a charge for an offence under this Act applies in respect of a violation to the extent that it is not inconsistent with this Act.

heading: Continuing violation
paragraph: 71.08 A violation that is committed or continued on more than one day constitutes a separate violation for each day on which it is committed or continued.

heading: Violation or offence
paragraph: 71.09 (1) Proceeding with any act or omission as a violation under this Act precludes proceeding with it as an offence under this Act, and proceeding with it as an offence under this Act precludes proceeding with it as a violation under this Act.

heading: Violations not offences
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, a violation is not an offence and, accordingly, section 126 of the Criminal Code does not apply in respect of a violation.

heading: Limitation or prescription period
paragraph: 71.1 No notice of violation is to be issued more than two years after the day on which the matter giving rise to the violation occurred.

heading: Right to request review
paragraph: 71.2 A person who is served with a notice of violation may, within 30 days after the day on which it is served, or within any longer period that the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator allows, make a request to that Commission for a review of the amount of the penalty or the facts of the violation, or both.

heading: Correction or cancellation of notice of violation
paragraph: 71.3 At any time before a request for a review in respect of a notice of violation is received by the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator, a person designated under paragraph 71.02(b) may cancel the notice of violation or correct an error in it.

heading: Review
paragraph: 71.4 (1) On receipt of a request made under section 71.2, the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator shall conduct the review or cause the review to be conducted by a person designated under paragraph 71.02(d).

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator shall conduct the review if the notice of violation was issued by a person designated under paragraph 71.02(d).

heading: Object of review
paragraph: 71.5 (1) The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator or the person conducting the review shall determine, as the case may be, whether the amount of the penalty for the violation was determined in accordance with the regulations or whether the person committed the violation, or both.

heading: Determination
paragraph: (2) The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator or the person conducting the review shall render a determination and the reasons for it in writing and cause the person who requested the review to be served with a copy of them.

heading: Correction of penalty
paragraph: (3) If the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator or the person conducting the review determines that the amount of the penalty for the violation was not determined in accordance with the regulations, the Commission or the person, as the case may be, shall correct the amount of the penalty.

heading: Responsibility
paragraph: (4) If the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator or the person conducting the review determines that the person who requested the review committed the violation, the person who requested the review is liable to the penalty as set out in the notice issued under section 71.06 or as set out in the determination if the amount of the penalty was corrected under subsection (3).

heading: Determination final
paragraph: (5) A determination made under this section is final and binding and, except for judicial review under the Federal Courts Act, is not subject to appeal or to review by any court.

heading: Federal Court
paragraph: (6) Despite section 28 of the Federal Courts Act, the Federal Court has exclusive original jurisdiction to hear and determine an application for judicial review of a determination made under this section by the Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator.

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: 71.6 If the facts of a violation are reviewed, the person who issued the notice of violation shall establish, on a balance of probabilities, that the person named in it committed the violation identified in it.

heading: Payment
paragraph: 71.7 If a person pays the penalty set out in a notice of violation, the person is considered to have committed the violation and proceedings in respect of it are ended.

heading: Failure to act
paragraph: 71.8 A person that neither pays the penalty imposed under this Act nor requests a review within the period referred to in section 71.2 is considered to have committed the violation and is liable to the penalty.

heading: Debt to Her Majesty
paragraph: 71.9 (1) A penalty constitutes a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in the Federal Court or any other court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (2) No proceedings to recover the debt are to be instituted more than five years after the day on which the debt becomes payable.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: 72 (1) The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator may issue a certificate of non-payment certifying the unpaid amount of any debt referred to in subsection 71.9(1).

heading: Registration in Federal Court
paragraph: (2) Registration in the Federal Court or in any other court of competent jurisdiction of a certificate of non-payment issued under subsection (1) has the same effect as a judgment of that court for a debt of the amount specified in the certificate and all related registration costs.

heading: Admissibility of documents
paragraph: 72.01 In the absence of evidence to the contrary, a document that appears to be a notice issued under subsection 71.06(1) is presumed to be authentic and is proof of its contents in any proceeding in respect of a violation.

heading: Publication
paragraph: 72.02 The Commission of the Canadian Energy Regulator may make public the nature of a violation, the name of the person who committed it and the amount of the penalty.

heading: Application
paragraph: 72.1 This Act applies to every interest or right in oil or gas acquired or vested before the coming into force of this section.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 73 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 The definitions in this section apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: authorized representative means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in respect of a Canadian vessel, the person referred to in subsection 14(1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in respect of a fleet registered under Part 2, the person referred to in subsection 75.03(5); and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in respect of a foreign vessel, the master. (representant autorise)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: bare-boat charter means a vessel charter agreement under which the charterer has complete possession and control of the vessel, including the right to appoint its master and crew. (affretement coque nue)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian maritime document means a licence, permit, certificate or other document that is issued by the Minister of Transport under Part 1 (General), 3 (Personnel), 4 (Safety), 9 (Pollution Prevention - Department of Transport) or 11 (Enforcement - Department of Transport) to verify that the person to whom or vessel to which it is issued has met requirements under that Part. (document maritime canadien)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian vessel means a vessel that is registered or listed under Part 2 (Registration, Listing and Recording) or that is exempted under the regulations from the registration requirement in subsection 46(1). (batiment canadien)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: foreign vessel means a vessel that is not a Canadian vessel or a pleasure craft. (batiment etranger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: government vessel means a vessel that is owned by and is in the service of Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province or that is in the exclusive possession of Her Majesty in that right. (batiment d'Etat)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: gross tonnage means the volume of a vessel as determined by a tonnage measurer or calculated in accordance with the regulations made under paragraph 77(h). (jauge brute)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hazardous and noxious substances handling facility means a facility that is used or that will be used in the loading or unloading of hazardous and noxious substances to or from vessels. (installation de manutention de substances nocives et potentiellement dangereuses)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: master means the person in command and charge of a vessel. It does not include a licensed pilot, within the meaning of section 1.1 of the Pilotage Act, while the pilot is performing pilotage duties under that Act. (capitaine)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: oil handling facility means a facility, including an oil terminal, that is used or that will be used in the loading or unloading of petroleum in any form, including crude oil, fuel oil, sludge, oil refuse and refined products, to or from vessels. (installation de manutention d'hydrocarbures)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: passenger means a person carried on a vessel by the owner or operator, other than

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person carried on a Safety Convention vessel who is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) the master, a member of the crew or a person employed or engaged in any capacity on board the vessel on the business of that vessel, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) under one year of age;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person carried on a vessel that is not a Safety Convention vessel who is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) the master, a member of the crew or a person employed or engaged in any capacity on board the vessel on the business of that vessel, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) a guest on board the vessel, if the vessel is used exclusively for pleasure and the guest is carried on it without remuneration or any object of profit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a person carried on a vessel in pursuance of the obligation on the master to carry shipwrecked, distressed or other persons or by reason of any circumstances that neither the master nor the owner could have prevented; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a person of a prescribed class. (passager)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pleasure craft means a vessel that is used for pleasure and does not carry passengers, and includes a vessel of a prescribed class. (embarcation de plaisance)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: port authority has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Marine Act. (administration portuaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed means prescribed by regulations made by the Governor in Council. (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: qualified person means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident within the meaning of subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a corporation incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province. (personne qualifiee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Register means the Canadian Register of Vessels established under section 43. (Registre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Safety Convention vessel means a vessel in respect of which the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, listed in Schedule 1, applies. (batiment assujetti a la Convention sur la securite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Tribunal means the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada established by subsection 2(1) of the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada Act. (Tribunal)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vessel means a boat, ship or craft designed, used or capable of being used solely or partly for navigation in, on, through or immediately above water, without regard to method or lack of propulsion, and includes such a vessel that is under construction. It does not include a floating object of a prescribed class. (batiment)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: wages includes emoluments. (gages)

heading: Descriptive cross-references
paragraph: 3 If, in any provision of this Act, a reference to another provision of this Act is followed by words in parentheses that are or purport to be descriptive of the subject-matter of the provision referred to, those words form no part of the provision in which they occur but are inserted for convenience of reference only.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 4 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Transport, make regulations prescribing anything that may be prescribed under section 2.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 5 Except as otherwise provided, this Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: 6 The objectives of this Act are to

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (a) protect the health and well-being of individuals, including the crews of vessels, who participate in marine transportation and commerce;

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (b) promote safety in marine transportation and recreational boating;

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (c) protect the marine environment from damage due to navigation and shipping activities;

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (d) develop a regulatory scheme that encourages viable, effective and economical marine transportation and commerce;

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (e) promote an efficient marine transportation system;

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (f) develop a regulatory scheme that encourages the viable, effective and economical use of Canadian waters by recreational boaters;

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (g) ensure that Canada can meet its international obligations under bilateral and multilateral agreements with respect to navigation and shipping;

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (h) encourage the harmonization of marine practices; and

heading: Objectives of Act
paragraph: (i) establish an effective inspection and enforcement program.

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: 7 (1) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, this Act does not apply in respect of a vessel, facility or aircraft that belongs to the Canadian Forces or a foreign military force or in respect of any other vessel, facility or aircraft that is under the command, control or direction of the Canadian Forces.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Transport, make regulations varying or excluding the application, in respect of government vessels, of any provision of this Act.

heading: Conflicts with foreign rules
paragraph: (3) Regulations made under this Act do not, unless they expressly provide otherwise, apply in respect of a Canadian vessel in the waters of a country other than Canada if the regulations are inconsistent with a law of that country that, by its terms, applies in respect of the vessel when in the waters of that country.

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph: 8 This Part applies in respect of Canadian vessels everywhere, in respect of foreign vessels in Canadian waters, and in respect of pleasure craft that are not Canadian vessels but that are in Canadian waters or in waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada. However

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph: (a) regulations made under paragraph 35(1)(d) in respect of pollution also apply, if they so state, in respect of foreign vessels in waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada; and

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph: (b) subsections 10(2.1) and 35.1(1) also apply in respect of foreign vessels in waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada.

heading: Role of Minister of Transport
paragraph: 9 Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the Minister of Transport is responsible for the administration of this Act.

heading: General
paragraph: 10 (1) The Minister of Transport or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, with respect to that Minister's responsibilities under this Act,

heading: General
paragraph: (a) establish consultative bodies;

heading: General
paragraph: (b) issue bulletins, guidelines and standards; and

heading: General
paragraph: (c) enter into agreements or arrangements respecting the administration or enforcement of any provision of this Act, the regulations or an interim order made under subsection 10.1(1) or (1.1) and authorize any person or organization - including a provincial government, a local authority and a government, council or other entity authorized to act on behalf of an Indigenous group - with whom or which an agreement or arrangement is entered into to exercise the powers or perform the duties and functions under this Act that are specified in the agreement or arrangement.

heading: Exemption power of Ministers
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Transport or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, with respect to that Minister's responsibilities under this Act, exempt for a specified period any authorized representative, person, class of persons, master, vessel, class of vessels, operator of an oil handling facility, oil handling facility or class of oil handling facilities, operator of a hazardous and noxious substances handling facility, hazardous and noxious substances handling facility or class of hazardous and noxious substances handling facilities from the application of any provision of this Act, the regulations or an interim order made under subsection 10.1(1) or (1.1), subject to any conditions that that Minister considers appropriate, if that Minister is of the opinion that the exemption is in the interest of preventing damage to property or the environment or is in the public interest or interest of public health or safety.

heading: Exemption power of Minister of Transport
paragraph: (2.1) The Minister of Transport may, with respect to his or her responsibilities under this Act, exempt for a period of not more than three years any person or vessel or class of persons or vessels from the application of any provisions of this Act or the regulations, subject to any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate, if the exemption would allow the undertaking of research and development, including in respect of any type of vessels, technologies, systems, components or procedures and practices that may, in the Minister's opinion, enhance marine safety or environmental protection.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (2.2) The Minister of Transport shall publish, on the Department of Transport's Internet site or by any other means that the Minister of Transport considers appropriate, a notice of every exemption granted under subsection (2.1), as soon as feasible after it is granted.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (3) Subject to any conditions that the Minister of Transport considers appropriate, the Minister may exempt for a specified period any vessel, or class of vessels, that is en route through Canadian waters but is not en route to or departing from a port in Canada, from the application of any provision of Part 3 (Personnel), 4 (Safety) or 9 (Pollution Prevention - Department of Transport) if the Minister is of the opinion that the provision is substantially similar to a provision of the laws of another state to which the vessel or class of vessels is subject.

heading: Publication - Canada Gazette
paragraph: (4) Notice of every exemption granted under subsection (2), (2.1) or (3) must be published in the Canada Gazette.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (5) The Minister of Transport or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may authorize any person employed in the federal public administration or any police officer, police constable, constable or other person employed for the preservation and maintenance of the public peace, or any class of any of those persons, that that Minister considers proper to exercise any of the powers and perform any of the duties and functions that may be or are required to be exercised or performed by that Minister under this Act.

heading: Interim order - Minister of Transport
paragraph: 10.1 (1) The Minister of Transport may make an interim order that contains any provision that may be contained in a regulation made, under this Act, on the recommendation of only that Minister, if he or she believes that immediate action is required to deal with a direct or indirect risk to marine safety or to the marine environment.

heading: Authorization to make interim order
paragraph: (1.1) The Minister of Transport may, subject to any restrictions or conditions that the Minister may specify, authorize the Deputy Minister of Transport to make, for the purpose referred to in subsection (1), an interim order that contains any provision that may be contained in a regulation made, under this Act, on the recommendation of only that Minister.

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (2) An interim order made under this section has effect from the time that it is made or from any later date that may be specified in the interim order, but ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (b) the day on which a regulation made under this Act that has the same effect as the interim order comes into force;

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (c) one year after the effective date of the interim order or any shorter period that may be specified in the interim order, unless the effective period is extended by the Minister of Transport or the Governor in Council;

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (c.1) the day that is specified in the order of the Minister of Transport extending the interim order, if the Minister extends the effective period of the interim order, unless the effective period is extended by the Governor in Council; and

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (d) the day that is specified in the order of the Governor in Council, if the Governor in Council extends the effective period of the interim order.

heading: Extension - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (2.1) If the period specified in the interim order is less than one year, the Minister of Transport may extend the effective period of the interim order for a period that ends no more than one year after the effective date.

heading: Extension - Governor in Council
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council may extend the effective period of the interim order for a period of no more than two years after the end of the applicable period referred to in paragraph (2)(c) or after the day referred to in paragraph (2)(c.1).

heading: Compliance with interim order
paragraph: (4) Every person or vessel subject to an interim order shall comply with it.

heading: Contravention of unpublished order
paragraph: (5) No person or vessel may be found guilty of an offence consisting of a contravention of an interim order that, at the time of the alleged contravention, had not been published in the Canada Gazette unless it is proved that, at the time of the alleged contravention, the person or vessel had been notified of the interim order or reasonable steps had been taken to bring the purport of the interim order to the notice of those persons or vessels likely to be affected by it.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (6) The Statutory Instruments Act does not apply to an interim order or an order extending the interim order. However, any such order must be published in the Canada Gazette within 23 days after it is made.

heading: Tabling of order
paragraph: (7) The Minister of Transport shall ensure that a copy of each interim order is tabled in each House of Parliament within 15 days after it is made. The copy is to be sent to the Clerk of the House if the House is not sitting.

heading: Appointment of marine safety inspectors
paragraph: 11 (1) Marine safety inspectors are appointed or deployed under the Public Service Employment Act.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Transport may authorize a marine safety inspector to exercise any power or perform any duty or function of the Minister under this Act, including quasi-judicial powers and the administration of examinations referred to in subsection 16(2), or to carry out inspections under section 211, including the following:

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (a) inspections of hulls;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (b) inspections of machinery;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (c) inspections of equipment;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (c.1) inspections respecting pollution prevention for the purpose of Part 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans);

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (d) inspections respecting the protection of the marine environment for the purpose of Part 9 (Pollution Prevention - Department of Transport); and

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (e) inspections of cargo.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Transport must furnish every marine safety inspector with a certificate of designation authorizing the inspector to carry out inspections under section 211 or to exercise any power or perform any duty or function of the Minister under this Act, including any quasi-judicial powers.

heading: Duties and powers
paragraph: (4) A marine safety inspector may exercise only those powers and perform only those duties and functions that are referred to in the inspector's certificate of designation.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: (5) Marine safety inspectors are not personally liable for anything they do or omit to do in good faith under this Act.

heading: Authorizing others to inspect
paragraph: 12 (1) The Minister of Transport may authorize any person, class of persons, classification society or other organization to issue any Canadian maritime document under this Act or to carry out inspections under section 211 if the Minister determines that the person, class of persons, classification society or other organization is qualified to issue the document or carry out the inspection.

heading: Certificate of authorization
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Transport must furnish the person, classification society or other organization with a certificate of authorization specifying the documents they are authorized to issue, the inspections they are authorized to carry out and any limitations on the powers they may exercise under subsection 211(4).

heading: Inspection records
paragraph: (3) A person, classification society or other organization authorized to carry out inspections must keep a record of each inspection in the form and manner specified by the Minister of Transport and, on request, provide the record to the Minister.

heading: Delivery of report
paragraph: (4) A person, classification society or other organization that does not, in respect of anything that they were authorized to inspect, issue a certificate because the requirements of the regulations have not been met must deliver their report in respect of that inspection to a marine safety inspector.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: (5) The person, classification society or other organization is not personally liable for anything they do or omit to do in good faith under this Act.

heading: Audit
paragraph: 13 The Minister of Transport may authorize any person or class of persons to audit inspections carried out under section 211. The auditor may exercise the powers under that section of the person, classification society or other organization whose inspections are being audited.

heading: Authorized representative
paragraph: 14 (1) Every Canadian vessel must have a person - the authorized representative - who is responsible under this Act for acting with respect to all matters relating to the vessel that are not otherwise assigned by this Act to any other person.

heading: Qualified person, bare-boat charterer or owner
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel is

heading: Qualified person, bare-boat charterer or owner
paragraph: (a) in the case of a vessel whose owner has entered into an arrangement with a qualified person, including an operator of the vessel, under which they are responsible for the matters referred to in subsection (1), the qualified person;

heading: Qualified person, bare-boat charterer or owner
paragraph: (b) in the case of a vessel described in section 48, the bare-boat charterer; or

heading: Qualified person, bare-boat charterer or owner
paragraph: (c) in any other case, the owner of the vessel.

heading: Representative if more than one owner
paragraph: (3) In the case of a Canadian vessel that is owned by more than one person, the owners must appoint as the authorized representative one of themselves or, in accordance with paragraph (2)(a), a qualified person.

heading: Representative of foreign corporation
paragraph: (4) In the case of a Canadian vessel that is owned by a corporation incorporated under the laws of a state other than Canada, the authorized representative must be

heading: Representative of foreign corporation
paragraph: (a) a subsidiary of the corporation incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province;

heading: Representative of foreign corporation
paragraph: (b) an employee or a director in Canada of a branch office of the corporation that is carrying on business in Canada; or

heading: Representative of foreign corporation
paragraph: (c) a ship management company incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province.

heading: Acts or omissions of authorized representative binding
paragraph: (5) The owner of a Canadian vessel is bound by the acts or omissions of their authorized representative with respect to the matters referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Application
paragraph: 16 (1) An application for a Canadian maritime document must be made in the form and manner, include the information and be accompanied by the documents specified by the Minister of Transport.

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (2) In addition to the specified information or documents, the Minister of Transport may

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (a) require that an applicant provide evidence, including declarations, that the Minister considers necessary to establish that the requirements for the issuance of the document have been met;

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (b) if the Canadian maritime document is in respect of a person,

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (i) set an examination that the person must undergo, and

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (ii) administer the examination; and

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (c) if the document is in respect of a vessel, require that the vessel or its machinery or equipment undergo any inspections that the Minister considers necessary to establish that the requirements for the issuance of the document have been met.

heading: Cheating
paragraph: (3) No person shall cheat on an examination referred to in paragraph (2)(b).

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (4) The Minister of Transport may refuse to issue a Canadian maritime document if

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (a) the applicant has not met the requirements for the issuance of the document;

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (b) the applicant has acted fraudulently or improperly or has misrepresented a material fact;

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (c) the Minister is of the opinion that the public interest and, in particular, the record of the applicant or of a principal of the applicant warrant it;

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (d) the applicant has not paid a fee for services related to the document or has not paid a fine or penalty imposed on them under this Act; or

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (e) in the case of a Canadian maritime document applied for under Part 3 (Personnel) by a master or crew member,

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (i) the master or crew member was on board a vessel that contravened any of sections 5.3 to 5.5 of the Coastal Fisheries Protection Act and knew, when the contravention occurred, that the vessel was committing the contravention, or

heading: Refusal to issue
paragraph: (ii) the master or crew member has been found guilty of an offence related to their duties on a vessel or has committed a violation in respect of which a notice of violation was issued under paragraph 229(1)(b).

heading: Notice after refusal to issue
paragraph: (5) The Minister of Transport must, immediately after refusing to issue a Canadian maritime document, give the applicant a notice

heading: Notice after refusal to issue
paragraph: (a) confirming the refusal and providing all relevant information concerning the grounds on which the Minister has refused to issue the document; and

heading: Notice after refusal to issue
paragraph: (b) indicating, in the case of a refusal to issue a document under Part 3 (Personnel) on the grounds set out in paragraph (4)(a), (b), (c) or (e), the address at which, and the date, being thirty days after the notice is given, on or before which, the applicant may file a request for a review of the Minister's decision.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: 16.1 (1) An applicant who receives a notice under subsection 16(5) may, on or before the date specified in the notice or within any further time that the Tribunal on application allows, file a written request for a review of the decision if

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (a) the request is in respect of a Canadian maritime document that is issued under Part 3 (Personnel); and

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (b) the grounds for refusing to issue the document are set out in paragraph 16(4)(a), (b), (c) or (e).

heading: Time and place for review
