paragraph: (2) On receipt of a request filed under subsection (1), the Tribunal must appoint a time and place for the review and must notify the Minister of Transport and the applicant of the time and place in writing.

heading: Review procedure
paragraph: (3) The member of the Tribunal assigned to conduct the review must provide the Minister of Transport and the applicant with an opportunity consistent with procedural fairness and natural justice to present evidence and make representations.

heading: Person not compelled to testify
paragraph: (4) In a review of a decision made under subparagraph 16(4)(e)(ii) on the ground that an applicant has committed a violation in respect of which a notice of violation has been issued to the applicant, the applicant is not required, and must not be compelled, to give any evidence or testimony in the matter before the matter that gave rise to the issue of the notice has been disposed of in accordance with sections 232 to 232.2.

heading: Determination
paragraph: (5) The member may

heading: Determination
paragraph: (a) in the case of a decision made under paragraph 16(4)(e), confirm the decision or substitute his or her own determination; or

heading: Determination
paragraph: (b) in any other case, confirm the decision or refer the matter back to the Minister of Transport for reconsideration.

heading: Period of validity
paragraph: 17 (1) Every Canadian maritime document is valid for the period specified by the Minister of Transport. The Minister may, on application made before a document expires and in the form and manner specified by the Minister, extend the period if the Minister is satisfied that it is not feasible to issue a new document before the document expires.

heading: Possession
paragraph: (2) Except as otherwise provided by this Act or the regulations, no person, other than the person to whom it was issued or their representative, shall possess a Canadian maritime document issued under Part 3 (Personnel).

heading: Production of document
paragraph: 18 Every holder of a Canadian maritime document shall produce it to the Minister of Transport on demand.

heading: Lost documents
paragraph: 19 If a Canadian maritime document is mislaid, lost or destroyed, the Minister of Transport may issue a replacement document on application made by the holder of the document in the form and manner and including the information and accompanied by the documents specified by the Minister.

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: 20 (1) Subject to section 20.1, the Minister of Transport may suspend, cancel or refuse to renew a Canadian maritime document if the Minister is satisfied that

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (a) the requirements for the issuance of the document are no longer met;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (b) a term or condition attached to the document has been contravened;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (c) the document was obtained by any fraudulent or improper means or a misrepresentation of any material fact;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (d) the holder of the document has not paid a fine or penalty imposed on them under this Act;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (e) the holder of the document has contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations that the Minister is responsible for administering;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (f) in the case of a Canadian maritime document issued under Part 3 (Personnel) to a master or crew member,

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (i) the master or crew member is incompetent or has committed an act of misconduct,

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (ii) the master or crew member was on board a vessel that contravened any of sections 5.3 to 5.5 of the Coastal Fisheries Protection Act and knew, when the contravention occurred, that the vessel was committing the contravention, or

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (iii) the master or crew member has been found guilty of an offence related to their duties on a vessel; or

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (g) in the case of a refusal to renew,

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (i) the applicant has not paid a fee for services related to the document, or

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to renew
paragraph: (ii) the Minister is of the opinion that the public interest and, in particular, the record of the applicant or of a principal of the applicant warrant it.

heading: Return of document
paragraph: (2) If a Canadian maritime document is suspended or cancelled, the person who held it shall return it on demand to the Minister of Transport.

heading: Notice before suspension or cancellation
paragraph: 20.1 The Minister of Transport must, before suspending or cancelling a Canadian maritime document issued under Part 3 (Personnel), give the holder 30 days notice of the proposed suspension or cancellation. The notice must

heading: Notice before suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (a) provide the holder with all relevant information concerning the grounds on which the Minister proposes to suspend or cancel the document; and

heading: Notice before suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (b) indicate, in the case of a proposed suspension or cancellation of a document on the grounds referred to in paragraph 20(1)(a), (b), (c), (e) or (f) or subparagraph 20(1)(g)(ii), the address at which, and the date, being 30 days after the notice is given, on or before which, the applicant may file a request for a review of the Minister's decision.

heading: Exception
paragraph: 20.2 (1) The Minister of Transport may suspend or cancel a Canadian maritime document issued under Part 3 (Personnel) without complying with section 20.1 if, on ex parte application by the Minister, the Tribunal determines that compliance with that section is not in the interest of public safety.

heading: Decision within 24 hours
paragraph: (2) An application by the Minister of Transport under subsection (1) must be heard by a member of the Tribunal, sitting alone, whose determination shall be made within 24 hours after the application is filed with the Tribunal.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Transport may, within 24 hours after the determination, appeal the determination to the Tribunal.

heading: Decision within 48 hours
paragraph: (4) The appeal panel of the Tribunal assigned to hear the appeal shall make a decision within 48 hours after the appeal is filed with the Tribunal.

heading: Notice after suspension, cancellation or refusal to renew
paragraph: 20.3 Except where notice of a proposed suspension or cancellation of a Canadian maritime document is given under section 20.1, the Minister of Transport must, immediately after suspending, cancelling or refusing to renew a Canadian maritime document, give the holder a notice that

heading: Notice after suspension, cancellation or refusal to renew
paragraph: (a) confirms the suspension, cancellation or refusal and provides all relevant information concerning the grounds on which the Minister suspended, cancelled or refused to renew the document; and

heading: Notice after suspension, cancellation or refusal to renew
paragraph: (b) indicates, in the case of the suspension or cancellation of, or the refusal to renew, a document on the grounds referred to in paragraph 20(1)(a), (b), (c), (e) or (f) or subparagraph 20(1)(g)(ii), the address at which, and the date, being 30 days after the notice is given, on or before which, the applicant may file a request for a review of the Minister's decision.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: 20.4 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the holder of a Canadian maritime document that is referred to in a notice under section 20.1 or 20.3 may, within the time specified in the notice or any further time that the Tribunal on application allows, file a written request for a review of the decision referred to in the notice.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A request for a review must not be filed with, or accepted by, the Tribunal if the grounds for suspending, cancelling or refusing to renew the document are set out in paragraph 20(1)(d) or subparagraph 20(1)(g)(i).

heading: Effect of request
paragraph: (3) The filing of a request for a review in respect of a notice under section 20.1 operates as a stay of the proposed suspension or cancellation until the matter is finally disposed of in accordance with this section or section 20.5.

heading: Time and place for review
paragraph: (4) On receipt of a request filed under subsection (1), the Tribunal must appoint a time and place for the review and must notify the Minister of Transport and the holder of the time and place in writing.

heading: Review procedure
paragraph: (5) The member of the Tribunal assigned to conduct the review must provide the Minister of Transport and the holder with an opportunity consistent with procedural fairness and natural justice to present evidence and make representations.

heading: Person not compelled to testify
paragraph: (6) In a review of a decision made under paragraph 20(1)(e), the holder is not required, and must not be compelled, to give any evidence or testimony in the matter.

heading: Determination
paragraph: (7) The member may

heading: Determination
paragraph: (a) in the case of a decision made under paragraph 20(1)(e) or subparagraph 20(1)(f)(ii) or (iii), confirm the Minister of Transport's decision or substitute his or her own determination; and

heading: Determination
paragraph: (b) in any other case, confirm the Minister of Transport's decision or refer the matter back to the Minister for reconsideration.

heading: Right of appeal
paragraph: 20.5 (1) The applicant for, or holder of, a Canadian maritime document may appeal to the Tribunal a determination made under subsection 16.1(5) or 20.4(7), and the Minister of Transport may appeal to the Tribunal a determination made under paragraph 16.1(5)(a) or 20.4(7)(a). The time limit for making an appeal is 30 days after the determination.

heading: Loss of right of appeal
paragraph: (2) A party that does not appear at a review hearing is not entitled to appeal a determination, unless they establish that there was sufficient reason to justify their absence.

heading: Disposition of appeal
paragraph: (3) The appeal panel of the Tribunal assigned to hear the appeal may

heading: Disposition of appeal
paragraph: (a) in the case of a determination made under paragraph 16.1(5)(a) or 20.4(7)(a), dismiss the appeal, or allow the appeal and substitute its own decision; or

heading: Disposition of appeal
paragraph: (b) in the case of a determination made under paragraph 16.1(5)(b) or 20.4(7)(b), dismiss the appeal or refer the matter back to the Minister of Transport for reconsideration.

heading: Issuance of documents to foreign vessels
paragraph: 21 The Minister of Transport may, at the request of the government of a state to which an international convention, protocol or resolution listed in Schedule 1 applies, issue in respect of a vessel registered in that state any document provided for by the convention, protocol or resolution, other than a Canadian maritime document, if the Minister is satisfied, in the same manner as in the case of a Canadian vessel, that the document may properly be issued. A document issued under this section must contain a statement that it has been issued at the request of that government.

heading: Foreign documents
paragraph: 22 The Minister of Transport may refuse to accept a foreign document required for the operation of a foreign vessel if in the Minister's opinion the conditions under which the document was issued do not comply with international agreements to which Canada is a signatory.

heading: Destruction of documents, fraud, obstruction and movement of detained vessel
paragraph: 23 No person shall

heading: Destruction of documents, fraud, obstruction and movement of detained vessel
paragraph: (a) wilfully destroy a document that is required under this Act to be kept;

heading: Destruction of documents, fraud, obstruction and movement of detained vessel
paragraph: (b) make or cause to be made a false entry in a log book required under this Act to be kept with intent to mislead or wilfully omit to make an entry;

heading: Destruction of documents, fraud, obstruction and movement of detained vessel
paragraph: (c) wilfully obstruct any inspector or other person or classification society or other organization that is exercising powers or performing duties under this Act;

heading: Destruction of documents, fraud, obstruction and movement of detained vessel
paragraph: (d) knowingly provide false or misleading information or make a false or misleading statement, either orally or in writing, to a person, classification society or other organization that is exercising powers or performing duties under this Act; or

heading: Destruction of documents, fraud, obstruction and movement of detained vessel
paragraph: (e) except as authorized under this Act, wilfully move a vessel that has been detained under this Act.

heading: Appointment of tonnage measurers
paragraph: 24 The Minister of Transport may appoint persons, to be known as tonnage measurers, to calculate vessels' tonnage under this Act.

heading: Fees and travel expenses
paragraph: 25 A tonnage measurer may withhold the tonnage certificate in respect of a vessel until the person requesting it pays the tonnage measurer's fees and travel expenses. The Minister of Transport may set limits on the fees and travel expenses that may be charged.

heading: Establishment
paragraph: 26 (1) For the purpose of ensuring the safety of the marine industry, the Marine Technical Review Board is established to make decisions on applications for an exemption from, or the replacement of, any requirement under the regulations or an interim order made under subsection 10.1(1) or (1.1) in respect of a Canadian vessel or in respect of the issuance of a Canadian maritime document to a person, other than a requirement with respect to fees, charges, costs or expenses.

heading: Members of the Board
paragraph: (2) The Board consists of a Chair, a National Vice-Chair and a maximum of five Regional Vice-Chairs.

heading: Chair
paragraph: (3) The Chair is appointed by the Minister of Transport and must be an employee of the Department of Transport who has expertise in marine matters.

heading: Vice-Chairs
paragraph: (4) The Vice-Chairs are appointed by the Chair and must be employees of the Department of Transport who have expertise in marine matters.

heading: Delegation
paragraph: (5) The Chair may delegate the Chair's powers and duties to the National Vice-Chair.

heading: Absence or incapacity
paragraph: (6) In the event of the absence or incapacity of the Chair or if the office of Chair is vacant, the National Vice-Chair may exercise all the powers and perform all the duties of the Chair.

heading: Striking panels
paragraph: 27 (1) When an application is made under subsection 28(1), the Chair must strike a panel of at least three persons.

heading: Constitution
paragraph: (2) Each panel consists of the Chair and the persons appointed by the Chair.

heading: Expertise
paragraph: (3) Any person to be appointed to a panel, other than a Vice-Chair, must have expertise in the matter in respect of which the panel is struck.

heading: Fee and expenses
paragraph: (4) Each panellist may be paid

heading: Fee and expenses
paragraph: (a) an amount fixed by the Minister of Transport for each day or part of a day that the panellist is performing duties under section 28, unless they are employed in the federal public administration; and

heading: Fee and expenses
paragraph: (b) reasonable travel and living expenses incurred by the panellist in the course of their duties under section 28.

heading: Casting vote
paragraph: (5) Matters before a panel are decided by a majority of the members of the panel. The Chair has a second vote in the case of a tie.

heading: Panel decisions
paragraph: (6) For greater certainty, a decision of a panel is a decision of the Marine Technical Review Board.

heading: Application
paragraph: 28 (1) Any person may, in respect of a requirement under the regulations or an interim order made under subsection 10.1(1) or (1.1) that applies in respect of a Canadian vessel or in respect of the issuance of a Canadian maritime document to a person, apply to the Marine Technical Review Board for a decision to exempt the applicant from the requirement or to replace it with another requirement.

heading: Form and manner
paragraph: (2) An application must be made in the form and manner, include the information and be accompanied by the documents specified by the Board.

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (3) In addition to the specified information and documents, the Board may require an applicant to provide evidence, including declarations, that the Board considers necessary.

heading: Grant of application
paragraph: (4) If the panel struck to decide the application is satisfied that the exemption or replacement is in the public interest and would not jeopardize marine safety or the marine environment and, in the case of an application to replace a requirement with respect to safety, the replacement would result in an equivalent or greater level of safety, the panel is to issue a decision granting the application, subject to any conditions and for the period that the panel considers appropriate.

heading: Applicant to be notified
paragraph: (5) The Chair is to notify the applicant of the decision to grant or deny the application.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (6) If the decision is to grant the application, the Chair must publish the decision in the manner that the Chair considers appropriate.

heading: Duty to inform
paragraph: (7) If a person has reason to believe that a decision to grant an application was based on false or misleading information or that the information provided with the application has changed, the person shall inform the Chair without delay.

heading: Decisions based on false or misleading information
paragraph: (8) If the Chair has reason to believe that a decision to grant an application was based on false or misleading information or that the information provided with the application has changed, the Chair may strike a panel in accordance with section 27 and the panel may confirm, cancel or vary the decision.

heading: Contravention
paragraph: (9) A contravention of a requirement that is substituted for another requirement as a result of a panel decision under subsection (4) is deemed to be a contravention of the original requirement.

heading: Rules
paragraph: (10) The Board must make rules respecting its procedure, with the approval of the Minister of Transport.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (11) As soon as feasible after the end of each fiscal year, the Chair must submit to the Minister of Transport a report of the Board's operations in that year.

heading: Schedule 1
paragraph: 29 (1) Schedule 1 lists the international conventions, protocols and resolutions that Canada has signed that relate to matters that are within the scope of this Act and that the Minister of Transport has determined should be brought into force, in whole or in part, in Canada by regulation.

heading: Schedule 2
paragraph: (2) Schedule 2 lists the international conventions, protocols and resolutions that Canada has signed that relate to matters that are within the scope of this Act and that the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans has determined should be brought into force, in whole or in part, in Canada by regulation.

heading: Codes and guidelines
paragraph: (3) A convention or protocol includes any code or guideline that is attached to it.

heading: Additions to Schedule 1 or 2
paragraph: 30 (1) The Governor in Council may, by order, add international conventions, protocols and resolutions described in subsection 29(1) to Schedule 1 or described in subsection 29(2) to Schedule 2.

heading: Order to be tabled and referred
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Transport is to cause a copy of each order related to Schedule 1 and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is to cause a copy of each order related to Schedule 2, together with a description of the objectives of the convention, protocol or resolution, to be laid before each House of Parliament on any of the first 10 days on which that House is sitting after the order is made. The order stands referred to the appropriate standing committee of each House.

heading: Deletions from Schedule 1 or 2
paragraph: 31 The Governor in Council may, by order, delete an international convention, protocol or resolution from Schedule 1 or 2 or amend Schedule 1 or 2 if the amendment would not, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, result in a material substantive change.

heading: Externally produced material
paragraph: 32 (1) A regulation made under this Act may incorporate by reference material produced by a person or body other than the Minister who recommended to the Governor in Council that the regulation be made, including by

heading: Externally produced material
paragraph: (a) an organization established for the purpose of writing standards, including an organization accredited by the Standards Council of Canada;

heading: Externally produced material
paragraph: (b) an industrial or a trade organization; or

heading: Externally produced material
paragraph: (c) a government, a government agency or an international body.

heading: Reproduced or translated material
paragraph: (2) A regulation made under this Act may incorporate by reference material that the Minister who recommended to the Governor in Council that the regulation be made reproduces or translates from material produced by a person or body other than that Minister

heading: Reproduced or translated material
paragraph: (a) with any adaptations of form and reference that will facilitate its incorporation into the regulation; or

heading: Reproduced or translated material
paragraph: (b) in a form that sets out only the parts of the material that apply for the purposes of the regulation.

heading: Jointly produced material
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under this Act may incorporate by reference material that the Minister who recommended to the Governor in Council that the regulation be made produces jointly with another government or government agency for the purpose of harmonizing the regulation with other laws.

heading: Internally produced standards
paragraph: (4) A regulation made under this Act may incorporate by reference technical or explanatory material that the Minister who recommended to the Governor in Council that the regulation be made produces, such as

heading: Internally produced standards
paragraph: (a) specifications, classifications, illustrations, graphs and other information of a technical nature; and

heading: Internally produced standards
paragraph: (b) test methods, procedures, operational standards, safety standards and performance standards of a technical nature.

heading: Material produced by Minister of Transport
paragraph: (4.01) A regulation made under paragraph 35.1(1)(k), 120(1)(f) or (k), 136(1)(a), (f) or (g) or 190(1)(a) may incorporate by reference material that the Minister of Transport produces.

heading: Variations of externally produced material
paragraph: (4.1) A regulation made under this Act on the recommendation of the Minister of Transport or on the joint recommendation of that Minister and the Minister of Natural Resources may incorporate by reference material produced by the Minister of Transport that varies material incorporated by reference under subsection (1).

heading: Scope of incorporation
paragraph: (5) Material referred to in subsections (1) to (4.01) may be incorporated by reference as amended from time to time or as it exists on a particular date. Material referred to in subsection (4.1) that is to be incorporated by reference must be incorporated as it exists on a particular date.

heading: Incorporated material is not a regulation
paragraph: (6) Material that is incorporated by reference in a regulation made under this Act is not a regulation for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (7) Subsections (1) to (6) are for greater certainty and do not limit any authority to make regulations incorporating material by reference that exists apart from those subsections.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 33 For greater certainty, no person or vessel may be convicted of an offence or subjected to a penalty for the contravention of a provision of a regulation made under this Act that incorporates material by reference unless it is proved that, at the time of the alleged contravention,

heading: Defence
paragraph: (a) the material was reasonably accessible to the person or vessel;

heading: Defence
paragraph: (b) reasonable steps had been taken to ensure that the material was accessible to persons or vessels likely to be affected by the regulation; or

heading: Defence
paragraph: (c) the material had been published in the Canada Gazette.

heading: In writing
paragraph: 34 (1) If this Act requires or authorizes an order or a direction to be given or made by the Minister of Transport to a person who is not an official of the Department of Transport, the order or direction must be given or made in writing.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (2) An order or direction referred to in subsection (1) is not a statutory instrument as defined in the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: 35 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Transport, make regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (b) respecting the issuance, amendment, suspension, reinstatement, cancellation or renewal of Canadian maritime documents;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (d) implementing, in whole or in part, an international convention, protocol or resolution that is listed in Schedule 1, as amended from time to time, including regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (i) implementing it in respect of persons, vessels, oil handling facilities or hazardous and noxious substances handling facilities to which it does not apply,

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (ii) establishing stricter standards than it sets out, or

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (iii) establishing additional or complementary standards to those it sets out if the Governor in Council is satisfied that the additional or complementary standards meet the objectives of the convention, protocol or resolution;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (e) respecting record keeping, information management and reporting for the purposes of this Part or Part 2 (Registration, Listing and Recording), 3 (Personnel), 4 (Safety), 6 (Incidents, Accidents and Casualties), 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans) to the extent that the Minister of Transport is responsible for that Part, 9 (Pollution Prevention - Department of Transport), 10 (Pleasure Craft) or 11 (Enforcement - Department of Transport) or the regulations made under subsection 136(1);

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (f) respecting the form and manner of giving notice under this Part or Part 2 (Registration, Listing and Recording), 3 (Personnel), 4 (Safety), 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans) to the extent that the Minister of Transport is responsible for that Part, 9 (Pollution Prevention - Department of Transport), 10 (Pleasure Craft) or 11 (Enforcement - Department of Transport) or the regulations made under subsection 136(1);

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (g) respecting fees, charges, costs and expenses to be paid in relation to

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (i) the administration of this Part or Part 2 (Registration, Listing and Recording), 3 (Personnel), 4 (Safety), 6 (Incidents, Accidents and Casualties), 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans) to the extent that the Minister of Transport is responsible for that Part, 9 (Pollution Prevention - Department of Transport), 10 (Pleasure Craft), 11 (Enforcement - Department of Transport) or 12 (Miscellaneous) to the extent that the Minister of Transport is responsible for that Part or the regulations made under any of those Parts or under subsection 136(1), including the development of those regulations, and

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (ii) the enforcement of any of those Parts or regulations;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (h) specifying the services for the purposes of paragraph 36.1(1)(d); and

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (i) specifying the services to which section 36.1 does not apply or the circumstances in which that section does not apply.

heading: Aircraft
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, regulations made under paragraph (1)(d) in respect of preventing collisions may apply to aircraft on or over Canadian waters.

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (a) implementing, in whole or in part, an international convention, protocol or resolution that is listed in Schedule 2, as amended from time to time, including regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (i) implementing it in respect of persons or vessels to which it does not apply,

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (ii) establishing stricter standards than it sets out, or

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (iii) establishing additional or complementary standards to those it sets out if the Governor in Council is satisfied that the additional or complementary standards meet the objectives of the convention, protocol or resolution;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (b) respecting record keeping, information management and reporting for the purposes of Part 5 (Navigation Services) or 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans), to the extent that the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is responsible for those Parts;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (c) respecting the form and manner of giving notice under Part 5 (Navigation Services) or 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans), to the extent that the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is responsible for those Parts; and

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (d) respecting the setting and payment of fees for services provided in the administration of

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (i) Part 5 (Navigation Services) or 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans), to the extent that the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is responsible for those Parts, or

heading: Regulations - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (ii) regulations made under subsection 136(2).

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: 35.1 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Transport, make regulations respecting the protection of the marine environment from the impacts of navigation and shipping activities, including regulations

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (a) respecting the design, construction, manufacture and maintenance of vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (b) specifying the machinery, equipment and supplies that are required or prohibited on board vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (c) respecting the design, construction, manufacture, maintenance, storage, testing, approval, arrangement and use of the machinery, equipment and supplies of vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (d) respecting the requirements that vessels, or classes of vessels, and their machinery and equipment are to meet;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (e) requiring the obtaining of certificates certifying that any of the requirements referred to in paragraph (d) are met;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (f) specifying the terms and conditions of certificates referred to in paragraph (e);

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (g) respecting the inspections and testing of vessels, or classes of vessels, and their machinery, equipment and supplies;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (h) respecting procedures and practices that are to be followed;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (i) respecting the development, maintenance and implementation of a management system that sets out the manner in which marine environment protection measures are to be integrated into day-to-day navigation and shipping operations and the criteria to which that management system is to conform as well as the components that are to be included in the system;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (j) respecting compulsory routes and recommended routes;

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (k) regulating or prohibiting the operation, navigation, anchoring, mooring or berthing of vessels or classes of vessels; and

heading: Regulations - protection of marine environment
paragraph: (l) regulating or prohibiting the loading or unloading of a vessel or a class of vessels.

heading: Amendment by Minister of Transport
paragraph: (2) A regulation made under any of paragraphs (1)(h), (j) and (k) may

heading: Amendment by Minister of Transport
paragraph: (a) authorize the Minister of Transport to amend, by order, that regulation; and

heading: Amendment by Minister of Transport
paragraph: (b) set out the terms and conditions under which the regulation may be amended by that order.

heading: Cessation of effect of order
paragraph: (3) An order referred to in subsection (2) has effect from the time that it is made and ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect of order
paragraph: (b) one year after the order is made or any shorter period that may be specified in the order.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (4) The Statutory Instruments Act does not apply to an order referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Publication of order
paragraph: (5) The Minister of Transport shall publish, on the Department of Transport's Internet site or by any other means that the Minister of Transport considers appropriate, a notice of every order referred to in subsection (2), as soon as feasible after it is made.

heading: Debt due to His Majesty
paragraph: 36 (1) All fees, charges, costs and expenses imposed under paragraph 35(1)(g) or (3)(d) and interest payable on them constitute a debt due to His Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Payment
paragraph: (2) If a fee, charge, cost or expense is imposed under paragraph 35(1)(g) or (3)(d)

heading: Payment
paragraph: (a) in respect of a pleasure craft that is not a Canadian vessel, its owner is liable for payment of the fee, charge, cost or expense and any interest payable on it;

heading: Payment
paragraph: (b) in respect of a Canadian vessel, the authorized representative, the owner and the master are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for payment of the fee, charge, cost or expense and any interest payable on it; and

heading: Payment
paragraph: (c) in respect of a foreign vessel, its owner and the authorized representative are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for payment of the fee, charge, cost or expense and any interest payable on it.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (3) If the amount of a fee, charge, cost or expense, or of interest due on it, owed by an authorized representative or owner of a Canadian vessel or by the owner of a foreign vessel, has not been paid, the Minister who recommended making the regulation under paragraph 35(1)(g) or (3)(d) may, in addition to any other remedy available for the collection of the amount and whether or not a judgment for the collection of the amount has been obtained, apply to the Federal Court for an order authorizing that Minister to seize, detain and sell any vessel belonging to the authorized representative or the owner, as the case may be. The Court may make the order on the terms that the Court considers appropriate.

heading: Release on security
paragraph: (4) A Minister who obtains an order under subsection (3) must release a seized vessel from detention if security in a form satisfactory to that Minister for the amount in respect of which the vessel was seized is deposited with the Minister.

heading: Agreement - cost recovery
paragraph: 36.01 (1) The Minister of Transport may enter into an agreement with any person or organization respecting any matter for which a regulation made under paragraph 35(1)(g) could prescribe a fee, charge, cost or expense.

heading: Regulations - exemption
paragraph: (2) If both an agreement entered into under subsection (1) and a regulation made under paragraph 35(1)(g) relate to the same matter, the regulation does not apply to the person or organization that has entered into the agreement in respect of the matter for which payment is required under the agreement.

heading: Recovery
paragraph: (3) When the Minister of Transport enters into an undertaking in respect of a matter for which payment of an amount is required from the other party under the terms of an agreement entered into under subsection (1), the undertaking is deemed, for the purposes of recovering that amount, not to be a duty of the Minister under this Act.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (4) All amounts payable under an agreement entered into under subsection (1) and any interest payable on them constitute a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Spending
paragraph: (5) The Minister of Transport may spend the amounts received under an agreement entered into under subsection (1) in the fiscal year in which they are received or in the next fiscal year.

heading: Services provided by third parties
paragraph: 36.1 (1) Unless otherwise provided in the regulations, any person or organization that provides, in the exercise of powers or the performance of duties under this Act in accordance with an agreement or arrangement entered into by the Minister of Transport under paragraph 10(1)(c), any of the following services may, if that person or organization is not part of the federal public administration, set the fees to be paid to it for those services:

heading: Services provided by third parties
paragraph: (a) services related to a Canadian maritime document;

heading: Services provided by third parties
paragraph: (b) services related to any approvals or certifications;

heading: Services provided by third parties
paragraph: (c) the conduct or witnessing of tests; and

heading: Services provided by third parties
paragraph: (d) services specified in the regulations.

heading: Not public money
paragraph: (2) Unless otherwise provided in the regulations, the fees referred to in subsection (1) are not public money within the meaning of the Financial Administration Act and the Service Fees Act does not apply in respect of them.

heading: Non-application of certain regulations
paragraph: (3) Unless otherwise provided in the regulations, the regulations made under paragraph 35(1)(g) do not apply in respect of any service referred to in any of paragraphs (1)(a) to (d) that is provided by any person or organization that is not part of the federal public administration in the exercise of powers or the performance of duties under this Act in accordance with an agreement or arrangement entered into by the Minister of Transport under paragraph 10(1)(c).

heading: Contravention of section 23
paragraph: 37 Every person who contravenes section 23 (destruction of documents, fraud, obstruction, false or misleading information or statement, movement of detained vessel) commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Contravention of regulations made under paragraph 35(1)(d) or (3)(a)
paragraph: 38 (1) Every person who, or vessel or oil handling facility that, contravenes a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 35(1)(d) or (3)(a) commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) If a court sentencing a person, vessel or oil handling facility under subsection (1) for contravening a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 35(1)(d) or (3)(a) is of the opinion that the provision that the person, vessel or facility contravened is equivalent to a provision of the regulations made under another provision of this Act and if the punishment provided under this Act for contravening that provision of the regulations is less than the punishment provided under subsection (1), the person, vessel or oil handling facility is liable to that lesser punishment.

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: 39 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a) subsection 17(2) (improper possession of a Canadian maritime document); or

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b) subsection 28(7) (inform Chair without delay).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 40 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) subsection 16(3) (cheating on an exam);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) section 18 (failure to produce Canadian maritime document);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) subsection 20(2) (failure to return suspended or cancelled Canadian maritime document); and

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d) a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 35(1)(e) or (3)(b).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $25,000.

heading: Contravention of interim order or regulations
paragraph: 40.1 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of interim order or regulations
paragraph: (a) subsection 10.1(4) (compliance with interim order); or

heading: Contravention of interim order or regulations
paragraph: (b) a provision of a regulation made under subsection 35.1(1).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Definition of Minister

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 41 In this Part, Minister means the Minister of Transport.

heading: Appointment of Chief Registrar
paragraph: 42 An officer, to be known as the Chief Registrar, is to be appointed or deployed under the Public Service Employment Act.

heading: Duties and powers of Chief Registrar
paragraph: 43 (1) The Chief Registrar is responsible for establishing and maintaining a register to be known as the Canadian Register of Vessels. The Chief Registrar is to divide the Register into parts, including a small vessel register, for the classes of vessels that the Chief Registrar specifies.

heading: Records
paragraph: (2) The Register is to contain records of the information and documents specified by the Chief Registrar in respect of a Canadian vessel or a fleet that is registered under this Part, including its description, its official number, the name and address of its owner and, in the case of a vessel that is not registered in the small vessel register, details of all mortgages registered in respect of it.

heading: Registrars
paragraph: 44 (1) The Chief Registrar may appoint the registrars that the Chief Registrar considers necessary.

heading: Duties of registrars
paragraph: (2) A registrar is to perform the duties and fulfil the responsibilities that the Chief Registrar assigns to the registrar.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: 45 The Chief Registrar and the registrars are not personally liable for anything they do or omit to do in good faith under this Act.

heading: Mandatory registration of vessels
paragraph: 46 (1) Unless it is exempted under the regulations, a vessel must be registered under this Part if it

heading: Mandatory registration of vessels
paragraph: (a) is not a pleasure craft;

heading: Mandatory registration of vessels
paragraph: (b) is wholly owned by qualified persons; and

heading: Mandatory registration of vessels
paragraph: (c) is not registered, listed or otherwise recorded in a foreign state.

heading: Owner's obligation
paragraph: (2) Every owner of a vessel that is required by subsection (1) to be registered under this Part shall ensure that it is so registered.

heading: Mandatory registration - government vessels
paragraph: (3) Every government vessel must be registered under this Part.

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: 47 Unless they are registered, listed or otherwise recorded in a foreign state, the following vessels may be registered under this Part:

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: (a) a pleasure craft that is wholly owned by qualified persons;

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: (a.1) a vessel that is exempted under the regulations from the registration requirement in subsection 46(1) and that is wholly owned by qualified persons;

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: (b) a vessel that is owned by a corporation incorporated under the laws of a foreign state if one of the following is acting with respect to all matters relating to the vessel, namely,

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: (i) a subsidiary of the corporation incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province,

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: (ii) an employee or a director in Canada of a branch office of the corporation that is carrying on business in Canada, or

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: (iii) a ship management company incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province; and

heading: Optional registration
paragraph: (c) a vessel that is in the exclusive possession of a qualified person under a financing agreement under which the person will acquire ownership on completion of the agreement.

heading: Bare-boat chartered vessels
paragraph: 48 A vessel that is registered in a foreign state and that is bare-boat chartered exclusively to a qualified person may be listed under this Part as a bare-boat chartered vessel for the duration of the charter if, for the duration of the charter, the registration is suspended in respect of the right to fly the flag of that state.

heading: Vessels under construction
paragraph: 49 A vessel that is about to be built or that is under construction in Canada may be temporarily recorded in the Register as a vessel being built in Canada.

heading: Vessels built outside Canada
paragraph: 50 Notwithstanding sections 46 to 48, the Minister may direct the Chief Registrar to refuse to register or list a vessel built outside Canada.

heading: Application
paragraph: 51 (1) An application for the registration, listing or recording of a vessel must be made in the form and manner, include the information and be accompanied by the documents specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (2) In addition to the specified information and documents, the Chief Registrar may require an applicant to provide evidence, including declarations, that the Chief Registrar considers necessary to establish that a vessel is required or entitled to be registered or is entitled to be listed or recorded.

heading: Before registration or listing
paragraph: 52 (1) Every vessel, other than one to be registered in the small vessel register, must be named in the form and manner specified by the Chief Registrar before it is registered or listed.

heading: Approval of names
paragraph: (2) The Chief Registrar may, on application, approve the name of a vessel before it is registered or listed and approve a change in the name of a Canadian vessel.

heading: Disallowance of names
paragraph: (3) The Chief Registrar must disallow a name if

heading: Disallowance of names
paragraph: (a) it is the same as the name of a Canadian vessel;

heading: Disallowance of names
paragraph: (b) it is likely, in the opinion of the Chief Registrar, to be confused with the name of a Canadian vessel or with a distress signal;

heading: Disallowance of names
paragraph: (c) it is likely, in the opinion of the Chief Registrar, to be offensive to members of the public; or

heading: Disallowance of names
paragraph: (d) its use is prohibited under an Act of Parliament.

heading: Requiring renaming
paragraph: (4) The Minister may order that a Canadian vessel be renamed if the Minister considers that its name would prejudice the international reputation of Canada.

heading: Shares
paragraph: 53 (1) For the purposes of registration, the property in a vessel is divided into 64 shares.

heading: Registered owners
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), only owners or joint owners of a vessel or of one or more shares in a vessel may be registered in the Register as owners of the vessel or shares, as the case may be.

heading: Registered owners - financing agreements
paragraph: (3) In the case of a vessel described in paragraph 47(c) (a vessel subject to a financing agreement), the persons referred to in that paragraph are to be registered in the Register as the owners of the vessel.

heading: Bare-boat charterers
paragraph: (4) In the case of a vessel described in section 48 (a bare-boat chartered vessel), no person may be registered in the Register as an owner of the vessel.

heading: Registration of joint owners
paragraph: (5) No more than five persons may be registered in the Register as joint owners of a vessel or a share in a vessel.

heading: Disposition of registered joint interests
paragraph: (6) A registered jointly owned interest in a vessel or a share in a vessel may be disposed of only by the joint owners acting together.

heading: Registration of fractions prohibited
paragraph: (7) No person may be registered as the owner of a fractional part of a share in a vessel.

heading: No effect on beneficial owners
paragraph: (8) This section does not affect the beneficial interests of a person represented by or claiming through an owner of a vessel or a share in a vessel.

heading: Trusts not recognized
paragraph: (9) No notice of a trust may be entered in the Register.

heading: Certificates of registry
paragraph: 54 (1) If the Chief Registrar is satisfied that all of the requirements of registration or listing have been met with respect to a vessel, the Chief Registrar must register or list the vessel, as the case may be, in the Register and issue a certificate of registry.

heading: Information
paragraph: (2) Every certificate of registry in respect of a vessel must contain the information specified by the Chief Registrar, including

heading: Information
paragraph: (a) its description;

heading: Information
paragraph: (b) its official number; and

heading: Information
paragraph: (c) the name and address of

heading: Information
paragraph: (i) in the case of a vessel described in paragraph 47(b) (a vessel owned by a foreign corporation), the authorized representative,

heading: Information
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a vessel described in section 48 (a bare-boat chartered vessel), the bare-boat charterer, and

heading: Information
paragraph: (iii) in any other case, its owner and the authorized representative.

heading: Period of validity
paragraph: (3) Every certificate of registry is valid for the period specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Provisional certificates
paragraph: 55 (1) The Chief Registrar may, on application, issue a provisional certificate in respect of a vessel that is required or entitled to be registered under this Part if

heading: Provisional certificates
paragraph: (a) the vessel is in a foreign port and a person intends to register it under this Part; or

heading: Provisional certificates
paragraph: (b) the vessel is in a port in Canada and the Chief Registrar is satisfied that permission to operate the vessel should be granted before a certificate of registry can be issued.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (2) The Chief Registrar may, on application, issue a provisional certificate in respect of a vessel that is not required or entitled to be registered under this Part if the Chief Registrar is satisfied that the vessel needs to undergo sea trials.

heading: Validity
paragraph: (3) A provisional certificate is valid for the purpose and the period specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Application
paragraph: (4) An application for a provisional certificate must be made in the form and manner, include the information and be accompanied by the documents specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Lost certificates
paragraph: 56 If a certificate of registry or provisional certificate is mislaid, lost or destroyed, the Chief Registrar must issue a replacement certificate of registry or provisional certificate, as the case may be, on application made by the authorized representative or owner in the form and manner and including the information and accompanied by the documents specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Refusal to issue, renew or amend certificate
paragraph: 56.1 Despite any other provision of this Act, the Chief Registrar may refuse to issue, in respect of a vessel, a certificate of registry, a provisional certificate or a replacement certificate of registry or provisional certificate, or to renew a certificate of registry or to amend one under paragraph 73(b), if the applicant for, or holder of, the certificate is in default of payment of a required fee, charge, cost or expense under this Act or the Wrecked, Abandoned or Hazardous Vessels Act in respect of that vessel.

heading: Marking
paragraph: 57 (1) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel shall, in the form and manner specified by the Chief Registrar, mark the vessel with its official number and any other information that the Chief Registrar specifies.

heading: Validity of certificate of registry
paragraph: (2) A vessel's certificate of registry is not valid until the vessel has been marked in accordance with subsection (1).

heading: Maintenance of markings
paragraph: (3) The authorized representative shall ensure that the vessel is kept marked.

heading: Defacing, etc., markings
paragraph: (4) No person shall wilfully deface, alter, conceal or remove the markings of a Canadian vessel.

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: 58 (1) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel shall notify the Chief Registrar within 30 days after any of the following occurs:

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (a) the vessel is lost, wrecked or removed from service;

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (b) there has been a change in the owner's, the authorized representative's or a registered mortgagee's name or address;

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (c) the information provided with the application under section 51 has changed; or

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (d) in the case of a vessel described in section 48 (a bare-boat chartered vessel),

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (i) the right to fly the flag of the foreign state is reinstated, or

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (ii) the charterer ceases to have complete control and possession of the vessel.

heading: Notification of alterations
paragraph: (2) If a Canadian vessel is altered to the extent that it no longer corresponds with its description or particulars set out on the certificate of registry, the authorized representative shall, within 30 days after the alteration, notify the Chief Registrar and provide the Chief Registrar with the relevant information and documents.

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (3) If for any reason a Canadian vessel does not have an authorized representative, its owner shall

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (a) notify the Chief Registrar of that fact as soon as possible in the circumstances; and

heading: Notification of changes
paragraph: (b) notify the Chief Registrar within 30 days after any event referred to in subsection (1) or (2) occurs.

heading: Notification of completion of construction
paragraph: (4) Within 30 days after completion of the construction of a vessel that is recorded as being built in Canada, the person in whose name the vessel is recorded shall notify the Chief Registrar of that fact and of the name and address of its owner.

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: 60 (1) Subject to the regulations, the Chief Registrar may suspend or cancel the registration or listing of a Canadian vessel if

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (a) it is not marked in accordance with subsection 57(1);

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (b) its certificate of registry has expired;

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (c) it does not have an authorized representative; or

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (d) section 58 has not been complied with.

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, the Chief Registrar must cancel the registration or listing of a Canadian vessel if

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (a) it has been lost, wrecked or removed from service;

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (b) it is no longer required or entitled to be registered or entitled to be listed under this Part; or

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (c) in the case of a registered vessel, a tonnage certificate provided by a tonnage measurer indicates that the vessel should be re-registered.

heading: Notice before cancellation
paragraph: (3) If a Canadian vessel is not required or entitled to be registered under this Part after its ownership changes, the Chief Registrar must, before cancelling its registration under paragraph (2)(b), give the owners and registered mortgagees

heading: Notice before cancellation
paragraph: (a) notice of the change in ownership; and

heading: Notice before cancellation
paragraph: (b) an opportunity that, in the opinion of the Chief Registrar, is sufficient to transfer the vessel or shares in the vessel to a qualified person or to make an application under section 74.

heading: Cancellation of registration
paragraph: (4) Except in the case of a vessel described in paragraph 47(c) (a vessel subject to a financing agreement), the Chief Registrar must cancel the registration of a vessel if a person who acquires the vessel or a share in it does not, within the prescribed period, provide evidence that satisfies the Chief Registrar that the vessel is required or entitled to be registered under this Part.

heading: Registration of mortgages not affected
paragraph: 61 The cancellation of the registration of a vessel does not affect the registration of mortgages in respect of the vessel.

heading: Reinstatement
paragraph: 62 The Chief Registrar may reinstate the registration or listing of a vessel if, in the Chief Registrar's opinion, the registration or listing of the vessel should not have been cancelled.

heading: Carrying on board
paragraph: 63 (1) Subject to subsection (3), no person shall operate a vessel in respect of which a certificate of registry or provisional certificate has been issued unless the certificate is on board.

heading: Delivery of certificate
paragraph: (2) A person who is in possession of a vessel's certificate of registry or provisional certificate shall deliver it to the person who is entitled to operate the vessel.

heading: Delivery of certificate
paragraph: (3) A person who is in possession of a certificate of registry or a provisional certificate issued under this Part shall deliver it to the Chief Registrar on request.

heading: Detention of certificate
paragraph: (4) A certificate of registry or provisional certificate is not subject to detention because of any title to, lien on, charge on or interest in the vessel that is claimed by an owner, a mortgagee, a charterer or an operator of the vessel, or by any other person.

heading: Right to fly Canadian flag
paragraph: 64 (1) A Canadian vessel has the right to fly the Canadian flag.

heading: Obligation to fly flag
paragraph: (2) The master of a Canadian vessel, other than one registered in the small vessel register, shall ensure that it flies the Canadian flag

heading: Obligation to fly flag
paragraph: (a) when signalled to do so by a government vessel or a vessel under the command of the Canadian Forces; or

heading: Obligation to fly flag
paragraph: (b) when entering or leaving, or while moored at or anchored in, a port.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) The Chief Registrar may, on application, suspend the registration of a Canadian vessel in respect of the right to fly the Canadian flag while the vessel is shown on the registry of a foreign state as a bare-boat chartered vessel.

heading: Mortgage of vessel or share
paragraph: 65 (1) The owner of a vessel registered under this Part other than in the small vessel register, of a share in such a vessel or of a vessel recorded as being built in Canada may give the vessel or share, as the case may be, as security for a mortgage to be registered under this Part.

heading: Filing of mortgage
paragraph: (2) A mortgage is to be filed with the Chief Registrar in the form and manner specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Date and time of registration
paragraph: (3) A mortgage is to be registered in the order in which it is filed, indicating the date and time of registration.

heading: Entry of discharge of mortgage
paragraph: 66 On receipt of satisfactory evidence that a mortgage has been discharged, the Chief Registrar is to enter the discharge in the Register.

heading: Priority of mortgages
paragraph: 67 (1) If more than one mortgage is registered in respect of the same vessel or share in a vessel, a mortgage registered before another mortgage has priority over that other mortgage.

heading: Consent to change in priority
paragraph: (2) The priority of mortgages may be changed if all of the mortgagees file their written consent with the Chief Registrar.

heading: Mortgagee not treated as owner
paragraph: 68 A mortgage of a vessel or a share in a vessel does not have the effect of the mortgagee becoming, or the mortgagor ceasing to be, the owner of the vessel, except to the extent necessary to make the vessel or share available as security under the mortgage.

heading: Mortgagee has power of sale
paragraph: 69 (1) A mortgagee of a vessel or a share in a vessel has the absolute power, subject to any limitation set out in the registered mortgage, to sell the vessel or the share.

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) If there is more than one registered mortgage of the same vessel or share, a subsequent mortgagee may not, except under an order of the Federal Court or of a court of competent jurisdiction whose rules provide for in rem procedure in respect of vessels, sell the vessel or share without the agreement of every prior mortgagee.

heading: Mortgage not affected by bankruptcy
paragraph: 70 The mortgage of a vessel or a share in a vessel is not affected by the bankruptcy of the mortgagor after the date of the registration of the mortgage, and the mortgage is to be preferred to any right, claim or interest in the vessel or share of the other creditors of the bankrupt or any trustee or assignee on their behalf.

heading: Transfer of mortgages
paragraph: 71 (1) A registered mortgage of a vessel or a share in a vessel may be transferred to any person, in which case the instrument effecting the transfer must be filed in the form and manner specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Entry of particulars
paragraph: (2) The Chief Registrar is to enter the particulars of the transfer in the Register.

heading: Transmission of interest of mortgagee
paragraph: 72 (1) If the interest of a mortgagee in a vessel or a share in a vessel is transmitted on death or bankruptcy, or by any lawful means other than by a transfer under section 71, the person to whom the interest is transmitted must file with the Chief Registrar the evidence of the transmission that the Chief Registrar specifies.

heading: Entry of particulars
paragraph: (2) The Chief Registrar is to enter the particulars of the transmission in the Register.

heading: Transfer
paragraph: 73 If the ownership of a Canadian vessel or a share in one changes and the vessel is still required or entitled to be registered under this Part,

heading: Transfer
paragraph: (a) the owner must provide the Chief Registrar with the evidence, including declarations, that the Chief Registrar considers necessary to establish that the vessel is required or entitled to be so registered; and

heading: Transfer
paragraph: (b) the Chief Registrar must amend the Register and the vessel's certificate of registry to reflect the change.

heading: Order for sale on acquisition by an unqualified person
paragraph: 74 If an unqualified person acquires a Canadian vessel, other than a vessel described in paragraph 47(b) (a vessel owned by a foreign corporation), a vessel described in paragraph 47(c) (a vessel subject to a financing agreement) or a vessel described in section 48 (a bare-boat chartered vessel), or a share in one, any interested person may apply to the Federal Court, or any court of competent jurisdiction whose rules provide for in rem procedure in respect of vessels, for an order that the vessel or share, as the case may be, be sold to a qualified person.

heading: Power of court to prohibit transfer
paragraph: 75 On the application of an interested person, the Federal Court, or any court of competent jurisdiction whose rules provide for in rem procedure in respect of vessels, may make an order prohibiting any dealing with a Canadian vessel or a share in one for a specified period.

heading: Application for fleet
paragraph: 75.01 (1) An applicant may, instead of applying to have vessels individually registered in the small vessel register, apply to register a group of two or more vessels as a fleet in that register.

heading: Form and manner
paragraph: (2) The application must be made in the form and manner, include the information and be accompanied by the documents specified by the Chief Registrar.

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (3) In addition to the specified information and documents, the Chief Registrar may require an applicant to provide evidence, including declarations, that the Chief Registrar considers necessary to establish that the group of vessels may be registered as a fleet.

heading: Registration - fleet
paragraph: 75.02 (1) The Chief Registrar may register a group of two or more vessels as a fleet if he or she is satisfied that

heading: Registration - fleet
paragraph: (a) all of the vessels are owned by the same owner;

heading: Registration - fleet
paragraph: (b) each vessel meets the requirements for registration in the small vessel register; and

heading: Registration - fleet
paragraph: (c) each vessel meets any other requirement - including with respect to a vessel's dimensions, usage or propulsion - that the Chief Registrar may establish for the vessels of a fleet.

heading: Small vessel register
paragraph: (2) A fleet that is accepted for registration must be registered in the small vessel register.

heading: Certificate of registry
paragraph: 75.03 (1) The Chief Registrar must issue a certificate of registry in respect of a fleet that he or she registers, and the certificate is valid for the period that he or she specifies.

heading: Information
paragraph: (2) A certificate of registry in respect of a fleet must contain the information specified by the Chief Registrar, including

heading: Information
paragraph: (a) a description of the fleet;

heading: Information
paragraph: (b) the fleet's official number; and

heading: Information
paragraph: (c) the name and address of the owner and the authorized representative of the fleet.

heading: Description - number of vessels
paragraph: (3) In the fleet's description, the Chief Registrar must specify either the number of vessels that are to be part of the fleet or the minimum and maximum numbers of vessels that can be part of it.

heading: Official number
paragraph: (4) The fleet's official number is also the official number of each vessel of that fleet.

heading: Authorized representative of fleet
paragraph: (5) The authorized representative of a fleet is the authorized representative, as determined under section 14, of the vessels of that fleet and must be the same authorized representative for all of the fleet's vessels.

heading: Acts or omissions of authorized representative binding
paragraph: (7) The owner of a fleet is bound by the acts or omissions of the authorized representative of the fleet with respect to all matters assigned by this Act to that representative.

heading: Refusal to issue, renew or amend certificate
paragraph: 75.031 Despite any other provision of this Act, the Chief Registrar may refuse to issue or renew a certificate of registry in respect of a fleet, or to amend one under paragraph 75.14(b), if the applicant for, or holder of, the certificate is in default of payment of a required fee, charge, cost or expense in respect of that fleet or a vessel of that fleet under this Act or the Wrecked, Abandoned or Hazardous Vessels Act.

heading: Addition or removal of vessels
paragraph: 75.04 Subject to subsection 75.1(2), an owner of a fleet may, after the fleet is registered, add a vessel to the fleet or remove a vessel from it. However, any vessel that is to be added must

heading: Addition or removal of vessels
paragraph: (a) be owned by the same owner as all of the other vessels of the fleet;

heading: Addition or removal of vessels
paragraph: (b) satisfy the conditions set out in paragraphs 75.02(1)(b) and (c); and

heading: Addition or removal of vessels
paragraph: (c) fit within the description or particulars set out in the fleet's certificate of registry.

heading: Vessels registered
paragraph: 75.05 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a vessel that is or becomes part of a fleet is considered to be registered under this Part and, for greater certainty, is a Canadian vessel.

heading: No longer registered
paragraph: (2) Unless it becomes part of another fleet, such a vessel ceases to be registered under this Part if

heading: No longer registered
paragraph: (a) there is a change in its ownership; or

heading: No longer registered
paragraph: (b) it is altered to the extent that it no longer fits within the description or particulars set out in the fleet's certificate of registry.

heading: Cancellation of individual registration
paragraph: 75.06 The Chief Registrar may cancel the registration of a Canadian vessel if the vessel becomes part of a fleet.

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: 75.07 The following provisions do not apply in respect of a fleet or a vessel of a fleet:

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: (a) subsections 57(2) and (3);

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: (b) section 58;

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: (c) section 60;

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: (d) section 62;

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: (e) subsections 63(1) and (2);

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: (f) section 73.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: 75.08 (1) For greater certainty, the following provisions apply in respect of a fleet or a vessel of a fleet:

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (a) section 56;

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (b) subsections 57(1) and (4);

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (c) subsections 63(3) and (4).

heading: Section 59
paragraph: (2) Section 59 applies in respect of a fleet, except that the reference to "section 58" is to be read as a reference to "section 75.1".

heading: Marking - validity of fleet's certificate of registry
paragraph: 75.09 (1) A fleet's certificate of registry is not valid unless each of the fleet's vessels has been marked in accordance with subsection 57(1).

heading: Maintenance of markings
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a fleet shall ensure that each of the fleet's vessels is kept marked.

heading: Notification of changes - name and address
paragraph: 75.1 (1) The authorized representative of a fleet shall notify the Chief Registrar within 30 days after there has been a change in the owner's or authorized representative's name or address.

heading: Notification of changes - number of vessels
paragraph: (2) If the number of vessels in a fleet changes to the extent that the fleet no longer corresponds with its description set out on the certificate of registry, its authorized representative shall, within 30 days after the change in number, notify the Chief Registrar and provide him or her with the relevant information and documents.

heading: Notification of changes - owner
paragraph: (3) If for any reason a fleet does not have an authorized representative, its owner shall

heading: Notification of changes - owner
paragraph: (a) notify the Chief Registrar of that fact as soon as possible in the circumstances; and

heading: Notification of changes - owner
paragraph: (b) notify the Chief Registrar within 30 days after any event referred to in subsection (1) or (2) occurs.

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: 75.11 (1) Subject to the regulations, the Chief Registrar may suspend or cancel the registration of a fleet if

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (a) any one of the fleet's vessels is not marked in accordance with subsection 57(1);

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (b) the fleet's certificate of registry has expired;

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (c) the fleet does not have an authorized representative; or

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (d) section 75.1 has not been complied with.

heading: Cancellation - fleet
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, the Chief Registrar must cancel the registration of a fleet if it no longer qualifies for registration under this Part.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (3) The Chief Registrar must cancel the registration of a fleet if a person who acquires the fleet does not, within the prescribed period, provide evidence that satisfies the Chief Registrar that the fleet still qualifies for registration under this Part.

heading: Reinstatement
paragraph: 75.12 The Chief Registrar may reinstate the registration of a fleet if, in his or her opinion, the registration of the fleet should not have been cancelled.

heading: Delivery of certificate
paragraph: 75.13 A person who is in possession of a fleet's certificate of registry shall deliver it to the person who is entitled to operate the fleet.

heading: Change of ownership
paragraph: 75.14 If the ownership of a fleet changes and the fleet still qualifies to be registered under this Part,

heading: Change of ownership
paragraph: (a) the owner must provide the Chief Registrar with the evidence, including declarations, that the Chief Registrar considers necessary to establish that the fleet still qualifies to be so registered; and

heading: Change of ownership
paragraph: (b) the Chief Registrar must amend the Register and the certificate of registry to reflect the change.

heading: Copies of entries
paragraph: 76 A person may examine or obtain copies of any entries in the Register with respect to a vessel or fleet.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 77 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Part, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the registration of vessels and fleets and the listing and recording of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the issuance and renewal of certificates of registry;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the suspension and cancellation of the registration of a Canadian vessel or a fleet, and the suspension and cancellation of the listing of a Canadian vessel;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the naming and marking of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the port of registration;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the form and manner of notifying the Chief Registrar under sections 58 and 75.1;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the evidence that owners of vessels previously registered in a foreign state must provide to prove that the vessels are no longer registered in the foreign state;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) respecting the calculation of the tonnage of vessels and the issuance of certificates of tonnage; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h.1) respecting the exemption of vessels or classes of vessels from the registration requirement in subsection 46(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h.2) authorizing the Minister to exempt, by order, vessels or classes of vessels from the registration requirement in subsection 46(1) for the period specified in the regulations and on any terms and conditions that he or she considers appropriate, if he or she is of the opinion that the exemption is not likely to adversely affect marine safety, and authorizing the Minister to amend or revoke an exemption;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h.3) respecting an authorization under paragraph (h.2); and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) prescribing anything that may be prescribed under this Part.
