heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 78 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) subsection 57(4) (wilfully defacing, altering, concealing or removing markings); or

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 77(h).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 79 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) subsection 46(2) (register vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) an order made under subsection 52(4) (renaming of vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) subsection 57(1) (mark vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d) subsection 57(3) (maintenance of markings);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (e) subsection 58(1) (notify of changes - authorized representative);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (f) subsection 58(2) (notify of alteration - authorized representative);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (g) subsection 58(3) (notify if no authorized representative - owner);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (h) subsection 58(4) (notify of completion of construction);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (i) subsection 63(1) (operation of vessel without a certificate on board);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (j) subsection 63(2) (deliver certificate to person entitled to operate vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (k) subsection 63(3) (deliver certificate to Chief Registrar);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l) subsection 64(2) (fly Canadian flag);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l.1) subsection 75.09(2) (maintenance of markings);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l.2) subsection 75.1(1) (notification of changes - name and address);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l.3) subsection 75.1(2) (notification of changes - number of vessels);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l.4) subsection 75.1(3) (notification of changes - owner);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l.5) section 75.13 (delivery of certificate); or

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (m) a provision of the regulations made under any of paragraphs 77(a) to (g).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $25,000.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph: (3) If an offence under paragraph (1)(a) or (c) is committed or continued on more than one day, the person who committed it is liable to be convicted for a separate offence for each day on which it is committed or continued.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Definition of Minister

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 80 In this Part, Minister means the Minister of Transport.

heading: Canadian vessels
paragraph: 81 This Part applies in respect of Canadian vessels, other than pleasure craft, everywhere. Subsections 86(2) to (4) also apply in respect of foreign vessels in Canadian waters.

heading: Presentation of documents
paragraph: 82 (1) The master of a Canadian vessel shall ensure that every person who is employed in a position on board presents to the master all Canadian maritime documents that they are required under this Part to have for that position.

heading: Sufficient and competent staff
paragraph: (2) No master of a Canadian vessel shall operate it unless it is staffed with a crew that is sufficient and competent for the safe operation of the vessel on its intended voyage, and is kept so staffed during the voyage.

heading: Obstruction prohibited
paragraph: (3) No crew member shall wilfully obstruct a master's operation of a Canadian vessel unless the master is, without just cause, putting at risk the safety of the vessel or of any person on board.

heading: Detention of persons
paragraph: 83 (1) The master of a Canadian vessel may detain any person on board if the master has reasonable grounds to believe that it is necessary to do so to maintain good order and discipline on the vessel or for the safety of the vessel or of persons or property on board. The detention may last only as long as necessary to maintain order and discipline or to ensure the safety of persons or property.

heading: Custody
paragraph: (2) The master of a Canadian vessel on a voyage may take into custody without warrant any person on board who the master has reasonable grounds to believe has committed an offence under this Act or any other Act of Parliament, and must as soon as feasible deliver that person to a peace officer.

heading: Use of force on a voyage
paragraph: (3) The master of a Canadian vessel on a voyage is justified in using as much force as the master believes on reasonable grounds is necessary for the purpose of maintaining good order and discipline on the vessel, but the master must not use force that is intended or is likely to cause death or grievous bodily harm unless the master believes on reasonable grounds that it is necessary for self-preservation or the preservation of anyone on the vessel from death or grievous bodily harm.

heading: Liable for discipline
paragraph: 84 Every person whom the master of a Canadian vessel is compelled to take on board and convey, and every person who stows away on a Canadian vessel or hides in cargo that is subsequently loaded on a Canadian vessel, is, as long as the person remains on board, subject to the same rules and orders for preserving discipline, and to the same punishments for contravening the rules or orders constituting or tending to a breach of discipline, as are crew members.

heading: Masters' contracts
paragraph: 85 (1) In every contract of employment between the authorized representative and the master of a Canadian vessel there is implied, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, an obligation on the authorized representative that the authorized representative and every agent charged with loading the vessel, preparing it for a voyage or sending it on a voyage use all reasonable means to ensure its seaworthiness for the voyage when the voyage commences and to keep the vessel in a seaworthy condition during the voyage.

heading: Crew members' contracts
paragraph: (2) In every contract of employment between the authorized representative and a crew member of a Canadian vessel there is implied, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, an obligation on the authorized representative that the authorized representative, the master and every agent charged with loading the vessel, preparing it for a voyage or sending it on a voyage use all reasonable means to ensure its seaworthiness for the voyage when the voyage commences and to keep the vessel in a seaworthy condition during the voyage.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Nothing in this section subjects the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel to any liability by reason of the vessel's being sent to sea in an unseaworthy condition if sending the vessel to sea in that condition was reasonable and justifiable in order to mitigate unsafe circumstances.

heading: Liens
paragraph: 86 (1) The master, and each crew member, of a Canadian vessel has a maritime lien against the vessel for claims that arise in respect of their employment on the vessel, including in respect of wages and costs of repatriation that are payable to the master or crew member under any law or custom.

heading: Foreign liens
paragraph: (2) The master and each crew member of a vessel on whom a maritime lien against the vessel is conferred by a jurisdiction other than Canada in respect of employment on the vessel has a maritime lien against the vessel.

heading: Liens for necessaries
paragraph: (2.1) The master of a Canadian vessel has a maritime lien against the vessel for claims that arise in respect of disbursements made or liabilities incurred by the master for necessaries on account of the vessel.

heading: Claims
paragraph: (3) The master, and each crew member, of a vessel may maintain an action against the vessel in the Federal Court, or any court of competent jurisdiction whose rules provide for in rem procedure in respect of vessels, for claims in respect of which a lien is conferred by subsection (1), (2) or (2.1).

heading: Priority
paragraph: (4) Liens conferred by subsection (1) or (2) rank in priority to all other claims, secured or unsecured, against the vessel, other than

heading: Priority
paragraph: (a) claims for costs relating to the arrest and the judicial sale of the vessel; or

heading: Priority
paragraph: (b) any lien arising from a claim for salvage in respect of the vessel.

heading: Priority - liens for necessaries
paragraph: (5) Liens conferred by subsection (2.1) rank in priority to all other claims, secured or unsecured, against the vessel, other than

heading: Priority - liens for necessaries
paragraph: (a) liens conferred by subsection (1) or (2);

heading: Priority - liens for necessaries
paragraph: (b) claims for costs relating to the arrest and the judicial sale of the vessel; or

heading: Priority - liens for necessaries
paragraph: (c) any lien arising from a claim for salvage in respect of the vessel.

heading: Positions on board Canadian vessels
paragraph: 87 Every person who is employed on board a Canadian vessel in a position in respect of which a certificate is required under this Part shall hold the certificate and comply with its terms and conditions.

heading: Eligibility
paragraph: 88 (1) Only a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident within the meaning of subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act may hold a certificate of competency that is issued under this Part.

heading: Foreign certificates of competency
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, on application by a person described in subsection (1), issue a certificate of competency in respect of certain requirements under this Act to the holder of a certificate of competency that was issued under the laws of a foreign state if the Minister is satisfied that the requirements under those laws for the foreign certificate meet or exceed the requirements under this Act. Before issuing the certificate, the Minister may require that the holder take an examination set by the Minister.

heading: Acceptance of foreign certificates
paragraph: 89 (1) If the government of a foreign state has entered into a reciprocal arrangement with the Government of Canada to accept certificates of competency issued under this Part in lieu of certificates of competency of that state and if the Minister is satisfied that the requirements under the laws of the foreign state for a certificate of competency meet or exceed the requirements under this Act, the Minister may direct, subject to any conditions that the Minister specifies, that the foreign certificate may be accepted in lieu of a certificate of competency issued under this Part.

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (2) A foreign certificate that is accepted under subsection (1) may, in so far only as concerns its validity in Canada, be suspended or cancelled by the Minister as though it were a Canadian maritime document, and the holder of any certificate so suspended or cancelled must deliver it to the Minister, who must then return it to the authority that issued it.

heading: Minister to be provided with information
paragraph: 90 (1) If a physician or an optometrist believes on reasonable grounds that the holder of a certificate issued under this Part has a medical or optometric condition that is likely to constitute a hazard to maritime safety, the physician or optometrist shall inform the Minister without delay of that opinion and the reasons for it.

heading: Patient to advise
paragraph: (2) The holder of a certificate issued under this Part in respect of which standards of medical or optometric fitness are required shall, before being examined by a physician or an optometrist, advise the physician or optometrist that they hold the certificate.

heading: Use by Minister
paragraph: (3) The Minister may use any information provided under subsection (1) for the purpose of determining whether the holder of a certificate meets the requirements in respect of that certificate.

heading: No proceedings shall lie
paragraph: (4) No legal, disciplinary or other proceedings lie against a physician or optometrist for anything they do in good faith in compliance with this section.

heading: Deemed consent
paragraph: (5) The holder of a certificate is deemed, for the purposes of this section, to have consented to the Minister being informed under subsection (1) in the circumstances referred to in that subsection.

heading: Articles of agreement
paragraph: 91 (1) The master of a vessel who is required by the regulations made under this Part to enter into articles of agreement shall

heading: Articles of agreement
paragraph: (a) ensure that every crew member has entered into and received articles of agreement, in the form and manner specified by the Minister, with respect to their position on the vessel; and

heading: Articles of agreement
paragraph: (b) display, in a location that is accessible to the crew, the provisions of the articles of agreement that are common to each crew member.

heading: Information
paragraph: (2) The articles of agreement between the master and a crew member must state the surname and other names of the crew member, the respective rights and obligations of each of the parties and any other information required by the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Discharge
paragraph: 92 When a crew member of a Canadian vessel is discharged, the authorized representative shall provide the member with a certificate of discharge in the form and manner specified by the Minister.

heading: Record of sea service
paragraph: 93 (1) The authorized representative and every crew member of a Canadian vessel shall each maintain, in the form and manner and for the period specified by the Minister, a record of sea service of the member.

heading: Copies to the Minister
paragraph: (2) On request, the authorized representative shall provide the Minister with a copy of, or an extract from, a crew member's record of sea service.

heading: Return and payment of expenses
paragraph: 94 (1) Subject to the regulations and except in the case of desertion or mutual agreement, if a crew member is left behind when a Canadian vessel sails or is shipwrecked, the authorized representative shall ensure that arrangements are made to return the crew member to the place where they first came on board or to another place to which they have agreed, and pay the expenses of returning the crew member as well as all expenses, including medical expenses, that the crew member reasonably incurs before being returned.

heading: Exception if insurance
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative is not responsible to pay any expenses covered by insurance for which the authorized representative paid.

heading: If authorized representative does not comply
paragraph: (3) If the authorized representative does not comply with subsection (1), the Minister may act in place of the authorized representative and any expenses incurred by the Minister constitute a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada by the authorized representative and may be recovered as such in a court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Desertion or serious violation of contract
paragraph: 95 If a crew member deserts a Canadian vessel or has committed a serious violation of their contract of employment, the authorized representative or, if the authorized representative entered into an agreement with another person to provide the crew member, that person may return the crew member to the place where they first came on board or to another place on which they and the authorized representative or the other person, as the case may be, have agreed. The expenses of returning the crew member may be deducted from any remuneration due to them.

heading: Informing the Minister
paragraph: 96 The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel must, in the form and manner specified by the Minister, inform the Minister of every birth or death on board.

heading: Death of crew member
paragraph: 97 (1) Subject to any other law, if a crew member of a Canadian vessel dies, the master shall

heading: Death of crew member
paragraph: (a) without delay inform the Minister or a diplomatic or consular officer of Canada of the circumstances surrounding the death; and

heading: Death of crew member
paragraph: (b) at the option of the person, if any, whom the crew member identified as a contact in case of emergency, arrange to bury or cremate the body or, if the person and the master agree on a place to return the body to, return it to that place.

heading: Cremation or burial
paragraph: (2) If the contact person referred to in paragraph (1)(b) cannot be consulted within a reasonable period, the master shall, subject to any other law, bury or cremate the body, taking into account the deceased's wishes if known.

heading: Exceptional circumstances
paragraph: (3) If, in the opinion of the master, it is not feasible, because of the type of voyage or the lack of facilities, to follow the wishes of the contact person referred to in paragraph (1)(b) or of the deceased crew member, the master shall, subject to any other law, bury or cremate the body.

heading: Property of a deceased crew member
paragraph: (4) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel shall give any property that belonged to a deceased crew member and was on board to the contact person referred to in paragraph (1)(b) or the deceased crew member's estate or succession.

heading: If an agreement to provide crew members
paragraph: 98 If the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel entered into an agreement with another person to provide crew members, that other person shall, in lieu of the authorized representative or the master with respect to those crew members, comply with the obligation of the authorized representative or master set out in

heading: If an agreement to provide crew members
paragraph: (a) paragraph 91(1)(a) (enter into articles);

heading: If an agreement to provide crew members
paragraph: (b) section 92 (provide certificate of discharge);

heading: If an agreement to provide crew members
paragraph: (c) subsection 93(1) (maintain record of sea service);

heading: If an agreement to provide crew members
paragraph: (d) subsection 93(2) (provide copy of record of sea service); and

heading: If an agreement to provide crew members
paragraph: (e) subsection 94(1) (pay expenses), except in respect of any expenses covered by insurance for which that other person or the authorized representative paid.

heading: Adjudication by Minister
paragraph: 99 The Minister may, on the request of the authorized representative or a crew member of a Canadian vessel, adjudicate any dispute between the authorized representative and crew member that arises under this Part. The Minister's decision is binding on the parties.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 100 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Part, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) specifying the positions that shall be occupied on board Canadian vessels, or classes of Canadian vessels, their minimum number and the types and classes of Canadian maritime documents that persons in those positions shall hold;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) specifying the requirements in respect of any position on board Canadian vessels or classes of Canadian vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) specifying the types and classes of certificates that may be issued in respect of positions on board Canadian vessels or classes of Canadian vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the qualifications required of applicants for any type or class of certificate specified under paragraph (c), including their medical fitness, minimum age, degree of knowledge, skill, training and experience;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the manner of determining whether a person meets the requirements specified under paragraph (b) in respect of a position or the qualifications required under paragraph (d) for any type or class of certificate of competency or other Canadian maritime document;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) specifying the terms and conditions of certificates of competency or other Canadian maritime documents issued under this Part;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) specifying the circumstances in which ensuring arrangements for a crew member's return and paying their expenses are not required for the purpose of subsection 94(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) respecting persons who enter into agreements to provide crew members, including requiring that those persons be licensed;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) specifying the Canadian vessels or classes of Canadian vessels in respect of which the master shall enter into articles of agreement with crew members;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) specifying the information that must be contained in articles of agreement;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) specifying what constitutes a serious violation of a contract of employment;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (l) respecting any occupational health or safety matter on board a vessel that is not regulated by the Canada Labour Code; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (m) respecting the payment and allotment of crew members' wages.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 101 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) subsection 82(2) (operating a vessel without sufficient and competent crew);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) subsection 82(3) (wilfully obstructing the operation of a vessel); or

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) a provision of the regulations made under any of paragraphs 100(a) to (i) and (k) to (m).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph: (3) If an offence under subsection (1) is committed or continued on more than one day, the person who committed it is liable to be convicted for a separate offence for each day on which it is committed or continued.

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: 102 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a) section 87 (hold certificate or document and comply with its terms and conditions);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b) subsection 90(1) (inform Minister of medical opinion);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (c) subsection 90(2) (inform that holder of a certificate);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (d) subsection 94(1) (pay expenses);

heading: Contravention of Act

heading: Punishment

paragraph: 103 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

paragraph: (a) subsection 82(1) (ensure employees present Canadian maritime documents);

paragraph: (b) paragraph 91(1)(a) (enter into articles);

paragraph: (c) paragraph 91(1)(b) (display articles);

paragraph: (e) subsection 93(1) (maintain record of sea service);

paragraph: (f) subsection 93(2) (provide copy of record of sea service);

paragraph: (g) paragraph 98(a) (enter into articles);

paragraph: (h) paragraph 98(b) (provide certificate of discharge);

paragraph: (i) paragraph 98(c) (maintain record of sea service);

paragraph: (j) paragraph 98(d) (provide copy of record of sea service); or

paragraph: (k) a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 100(j).

paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $25,000.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Definition of Minister

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 104 In this Part, Minister means the Minister of Transport.

heading: Canadian vessels and foreign vessels
paragraph: 105 This Part applies in respect of Canadian vessels, other than pleasure craft, everywhere and in respect of foreign vessels in Canadian waters.

heading: General duties
paragraph: 106 (1) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel shall

heading: General duties
paragraph: (a) ensure that the vessel and its machinery and equipment meet the requirements of the regulations made under this Part;

heading: General duties
paragraph: (b) develop procedures for the safe operation of the vessel and for dealing with emergencies; and

heading: General duties
paragraph: (c) ensure that the crew and passengers receive safety training.

heading: Duties re Canadian maritime documents
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel shall ensure that

heading: Duties re Canadian maritime documents
paragraph: (a) the vessel and its machinery and equipment are inspected for the purpose of obtaining all of the Canadian maritime documents that are required under this Part; and

heading: Duties re Canadian maritime documents
paragraph: (b) every term or condition attached to a Canadian maritime document issued in respect of the vessel or its machinery or equipment is met.

heading: Obtaining Canadian maritime documents
paragraph: 107 The master of a Canadian vessel shall, before the vessel embarks on a voyage from a port in Canada, ensure that all of the Canadian maritime documents required under this Part have been obtained.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: 108 (1) If the master of a Canadian vessel has had the vessel or its machinery or equipment inspected by an authority of a foreign state and that authority has issued a certificate that certifies that the vessel, machinery or equipment meets certain requirements of that state and the Minister is satisfied that those requirements meet or exceed the requirements for a Canadian maritime document required under this Part, the Minister may grant an exemption, for the period specified by the Minister, from the obligation to comply with subsection 106(2) and section 107 with respect to that certificate.

heading: Issuance of certificates by foreign states
paragraph: (2) The Minister may request the government of a state that is a party to a convention, protocol or resolution listed in Schedule 1 respecting the safety of vessels or of persons who are on board or are loading or unloading vessels to issue in respect of a Canadian vessel any certificate provided for by the convention, protocol or resolution. A certificate issued as a result of such a request and containing a statement that it has been so issued has effect for the purposes of this Act as if it had been issued under this Part and may be suspended or cancelled as though it were a Canadian maritime document.

heading: Safety of persons
paragraph: 109 (1) The master of a vessel shall take all reasonable steps to ensure the safety of the vessel and of persons who are on board or are loading or unloading it while using equipment on it.

heading: Protection from hazards
paragraph: (2) If the master of a vessel is informed of a safety hazard, the master shall, unless the master determines that the hazard does not exist, take reasonable measures to protect the vessel and persons on board from the hazard, including eliminating it if feasible. If it is not feasible to eliminate it, the master of a Canadian vessel shall notify the authorized representative.

heading: Carrying excess number of persons
paragraph: 110 (1) The master of a vessel must ensure that the number of persons carried on board is not more than the number of persons authorized to be on board under any certificate issued under this Part or under an international convention, protocol or resolution listed in Schedule 1.

heading: Submerging load lines
paragraph: (2) The master of a vessel shall ensure that the applicable load lines on the vessel are not submerged.

heading: Exception to subsection (1)
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a person carried on board a vessel in pursuance of the obligation on the master to carry shipwrecked or distressed persons.

heading: Direction to cease - master
paragraph: 111 (1) The Minister may direct a master to cease any operation that, in the Minister's opinion, poses an undue risk because of unsafe conditions.

heading: Direction to take measures - master
paragraph: (2) The Minister may direct a master to take measures that, in the Minister's opinion, are necessary to avoid an undue risk because of unsafe conditions, including a direction to

heading: Direction to take measures - master
paragraph: (a) provide the Minister with any information that the Minister considers appropriate to assess or deal with risks to marine safety;

heading: Direction to take measures - master
paragraph: (b) proceed by the route and in the manner that the Minister specifies; and

heading: Direction to take measures - master
paragraph: (c) proceed to a place that the Minister selects, by the route and in the manner that the Minister specifies, and

heading: Direction to take measures - master
paragraph: (i) unload the vessel's cargo, or

heading: Direction to take measures - master
paragraph: (ii) moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that the Minister specifies.

heading: Direction to authorize vessel
paragraph: (3) The Minister may direct a port authority or a person in charge of a port authority or place to authorize a vessel in respect of which a direction has been made under paragraph (2)(c) to proceed to the place selected by the Minister and to

heading: Direction to authorize vessel
paragraph: (a) unload the cargo; or

heading: Direction to authorize vessel
paragraph: (b) moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that the Minister may specify.

heading: Information to be sent respecting dangers to navigation
paragraph: 112 If the master of a Canadian vessel encounters dangerous ice, a dangerous derelict or other direct danger to navigation, a tropical storm, winds of a force of 10 or more on the Beaufort scale for which no storm warning has been received or subfreezing air temperatures associated with gale force winds and causing severe ice accretion on the superstructure of the vessel, the master shall give notice to all vessels in the vicinity and the prescribed authorities on shore of the danger.

heading: Carrying out duties and reporting
paragraph: 113 Every crew member on board a vessel shall

heading: Carrying out duties and reporting
paragraph: (a) carry out their duties and functions in a manner that does not jeopardize the safety of the vessel or of any person on board;

heading: Carrying out duties and reporting
paragraph: (b) report to the master any safety hazards of which they become aware;

heading: Carrying out duties and reporting
paragraph: (c) report to the master any change in their circumstances that could affect their ability to carry out their duties and functions safely; and

heading: Carrying out duties and reporting
paragraph: (d) comply with lawful directions given by the master.

heading: Direction to cease - crew
paragraph: 114 (1) The Minister may direct a crew member on board a vessel to cease any operation that, in the Minister's opinion, poses an undue risk because of unsafe conditions.

heading: Direction to take measures - crew
paragraph: (2) The Minister may direct a crew member on board a vessel to take measures that, in the Minister's opinion, are necessary to avoid an undue risk because of unsafe conditions, including a direction to provide the Minister with any information that the Minister considers appropriate to support assessing or addressing risks to marine safety.

heading: Compliance with directions
paragraph: 115 (1) Every passenger on board a vessel shall comply with any direction that is given to them by the master or a crew member to carry out the provisions of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Compliance with direction to leave a vessel
paragraph: (2) Every passenger on board a vessel shall comply with a direction to leave the vessel that is given to them by the master before the vessel embarks on a voyage.

heading: When boarding a vessel prohibited
paragraph: 116 Subject to sections 135 (stopping and boarding a vessel), 175.1 (powers of pollution response officers - general), 196 and 198 (pleasure craft inspections), 200 (stopping and boarding a vessel) and 211 (inspections) and to any other Act of Parliament, no person shall go or attempt to go on board a vessel or to leave or attempt to leave one

heading: When boarding a vessel prohibited
paragraph: (a) without the permission or against the orders of the master or the person in charge of embarkation or disembarkation; or

heading: When boarding a vessel prohibited
paragraph: (b) if there is no safe means of embarkation or disembarkation or every such means has been blocked.

heading: Tampering and vandalism
paragraph: 117 No person shall tamper with or vandalize a vessel or its machinery, equipment or notices or plans relating to emergency procedures, safety or navigation.

heading: Jeopardizing safety
paragraph: 118 No person shall take any action that might jeopardize the safety of a vessel or of persons on board.

heading: In accordance with plans
paragraph: 119 Subject to the regulations, no person shall construct, manufacture or alter a vessel of a prescribed class otherwise than in accordance with plans approved by the Minister as having met the requirements of the regulations respecting the design and construction of vessels of that class.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 120 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations respecting the safety of vessels or classes of vessels and of persons on board or loading or unloading a vessel, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the design, construction, manufacture and maintenance of vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) specifying the machinery, equipment and supplies that are required or prohibited on board vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the design, construction, manufacture, maintenance, storage, testing, approval, arrangement and use of a vessel's or a class of vessels' machinery, equipment and supplies;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the requirements that vessels, or classes of vessels, and their machinery and equipment must meet;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) requiring the obtaining of certificates certifying that any of the requirements referred to in paragraph (d) are met;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) specifying the terms and conditions of certificates issued under this Part;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the inspection and testing of vessels, or classes of vessels, and their machinery, equipment and supplies;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) respecting load lines and draught marks on vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) respecting procedures and practices that must be followed;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) respecting compulsory routes and recommended routes;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) regulating or prohibiting the operation of vessels for the purpose of protecting persons, vessels, artificial islands, installations, structures, works, shore areas or environmentally sensitive areas;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (l) respecting the prevention of collisions in Canadian waters or waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (m) respecting arrangements for ensuring communication between persons in different parts of a vessel and between persons on board and other persons;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (n) respecting information and documents that must be supplied to the master and kept on board vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (o) respecting the marking of vessels and the posting of notices, plans and Canadian maritime documents to show information relating to safety and to emergency procedures;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (p) respecting the number of passengers that may be on board a vessel and their safety;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (q) respecting the illumination of docks or wharfs at which vessels are berthed;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (r) respecting shore-based gangways;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (s) respecting cargo;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (s.1) respecting arrangements for emergency services, including requiring vessels or classes of vessels to enter into such arrangements; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (t) prescribing anything that may be prescribed under this Part.

heading: Application of regulations
paragraph: (2) Regulations made under this section apply in respect of vessels that are capable of engaging in the drilling for, or the production, conservation or processing of, oil or gas only if the regulations so state and were made on the joint recommendation of the Minister and the Minister of Natural Resources.

heading: Aircraft
paragraph: (3) Despite section 105, regulations referred to in paragraph (1)(k) or (l) may be made in respect of aircraft on or over Canadian waters.

heading: Pleasure craft
paragraph: (4) Despite section 105, regulations referred to in paragraph (1)(j), (k) or (l) may be made in respect of pleasure craft that are in Canadian waters.

heading: Contraventions of regulations
paragraph: (5) Despite section 105, paragraph 121(1)(s) applies in respect of contraventions of regulations made under subsection (3) or (4).

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 121 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) paragraph 106(1)(a) (ensure vessel meets requirements);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) paragraph 106(1)(b) (develop emergency procedures);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) paragraph 106(1)(c) (ensure training);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d) paragraph 106(2)(a) (ensure vessel inspected);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (e) paragraph 106(2)(b) (ensure terms and conditions met);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (f) section 107 (obtain Canadian maritime documents);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (g) subsection 109(1) (ensure safety);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (h) subsection 109(2) (protect from hazards and notify authorized representative);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (i) subsection 110(1) (too many persons);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (j) a direction given under subsection 111(1) (direction to cease - master);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (j.1) a direction given under subsection 111(2) (direction to take measures - master);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (j.2) a direction given under subsection 111(3) (direction to authorize vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (k) section 112 (inform of danger);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l) paragraph 113(a) (carry out duties and functions safely);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (m) paragraph 113(b) (report safety hazards);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (n) paragraph 113(c) (report change in circumstances);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (o) paragraph 113(d) (comply with lawful direction given by master);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (o.1) a direction given under subsection 114(2) (direction to take measures - crew);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (p) section 117 (tampering or vandalism);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (q) section 118 (jeopardizing safety);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (r) section 119 (constructing, manufacturing or altering a vessel not in accordance with approved plans); and

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (s) a provision of the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Contravention of subsection 110(2)
paragraph: 122 Every person who contravenes subsection 110(2) (submerged load lines) commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $500,000 in respect of each centimetre or part of a centimetre that the applicable load line is submerged or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: 123 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a) a direction given under subsection 114(1) (direction to cease - crew);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b) subsection 115(1) (passenger to comply with direction);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (c) subsection 115(2) (passenger to comply with direction to leave vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (d) paragraph 116(a) (boarding or attempting to board without permission); or

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (e) paragraph 116(b) (boarding or attempting to board after safety barriers are in place).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: When compliance agreement in effect
paragraph: 124 If an offence under any of sections 121 to 123 is committed while an agreement or arrangement is in effect between the Minister and the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel that provides that inspections of the vessel to ensure compliance with a provision referred to in subsection 121(1), section 122 or subsection 123(1) will be carried out by the authorized representative or a person or an organization acting on their behalf, the amount of any fine imposed under that section may be doubled.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 125 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aid to navigation means a buoy, beacon, lighthouse, landmark, radio aid to marine navigation or any other structure or device installed, built or maintained in or on water or on land for the purpose of assisting with marine navigation. (aide a la navigation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: VTS Zone means a Vessel Traffic Services Zone established under paragraph 136(1)(a). (zone STM)

heading: Entering, leaving or proceeding within a VTS Zone
paragraph: 126 (1) Subject to subsection (4), no vessel of a prescribed class shall

heading: Entering, leaving or proceeding within a VTS Zone
paragraph: (a) enter, leave or proceed within a VTS Zone without having previously obtained a clearance under this section; or

heading: Entering, leaving or proceeding within a VTS Zone
paragraph: (b) proceed within a VTS Zone unless able to maintain direct communication with a marine communications and traffic services officer in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Marine communications and traffic services officers
paragraph: (2) The Minister may designate as marine communications and traffic services officers persons in the federal public administration who meet the requirements specified by the Minister.

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (3) Subject to any regulations made under section 136, to any other Act of Parliament governing ports or harbours and to the regulations or by-laws made under such an Act, for the purpose of promoting safe and efficient navigation or environmental protection, a marine communications and traffic services officer may, with respect to any vessel of a prescribed class that is about to enter or is within a VTS Zone,

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (a) grant a clearance to the vessel to enter, leave or proceed within the VTS Zone;

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (b) direct the master, pilot or person in charge of the deck watch of the vessel to provide, in the manner and at any time that may be specified in the direction, any pertinent information in respect of the vessel that may be specified in the direction;

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (c) direct the vessel to use any radio frequencies in communications with coast stations or any other vessel that may be specified in the direction; and

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (d) direct the vessel, at the time, between the times or before or after any event that may be specified in the direction,

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (i) to leave the VTS Zone,

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (ii) to leave or refrain from entering any area within the VTS Zone that may be specified in the direction, or

heading: Powers of officers
paragraph: (iii) to proceed to or remain at any location within the VTS Zone that may be specified in the direction.

heading: If vessel unable to communicate
paragraph: (4) If a vessel

heading: If vessel unable to communicate
paragraph: (a) is unable to obtain a clearance required by subsection (1) because of an inability to establish direct communication with a marine communications and traffic services officer, or

heading: If vessel unable to communicate
paragraph: (b) after obtaining a clearance, is unable to maintain direct communication with a marine communications and traffic services officer,

heading: If vessel unable to communicate
paragraph: the vessel may, subject to subsection (6), nevertheless proceed on its route.

heading: Communication and obtaining clearance
paragraph: (5) The master shall

heading: Communication and obtaining clearance
paragraph: (a) in the circumstances described in subsection (4), take all reasonable measures to communicate with a marine communications and traffic services officer as soon as possible; and

heading: Communication and obtaining clearance
paragraph: (b) in the circumstances described in paragraph (4)(a), obtain a clearance as soon as possible after direct communication is established.

heading: Equipment failure
paragraph: (6) In the circumstances described in subsection (4), if the master is unable to establish or maintain direct communication because of an equipment failure on the vessel, the vessel shall

heading: Equipment failure
paragraph: (a) if it is in a port or anchorage where the equipment can be repaired, remain there until it is able to establish communication in accordance with the regulations; and

heading: Equipment failure
paragraph: (b) if it is not in a port or anchorage where the equipment can be repaired, proceed to the nearest reasonably safe port or anchorage on its route when it is safe to do so and remain there until it is able to establish communication in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Variations from requirements or conditions
paragraph: 127 (1) The Minister may, on request, vary in respect of a vessel a requirement or condition made under paragraph 136(1)(b) or (c) if the Minister is satisfied that the varied requirement or condition would result in an equivalent or greater level of safety.

heading: Contravention
paragraph: (2) A contravention of a requirement that is varied under subsection (1) is deemed to be a contravention of the original requirement.

heading: Aids to navigation vest in Her Majesty
paragraph: 128 All aids to navigation acquired, installed, built or maintained at the expense of a province before it became a part of Canada, or at the expense of the Government of Canada, and all buildings and other works relating to those aids, are vested in Her Majesty in right of Canada and are under the control and management of the Minister.

heading: Obligation to report damage
paragraph: 129 (1) If a vessel, or anything towed by a vessel, runs down, moves, damages or destroys an aid to navigation in Canadian waters, the person in charge of the vessel shall, without delay, make a report to a marine communications and traffic services officer or, if that is not feasible, to an officer of the Canadian Coast Guard.

heading: Obligation to report - navigation hazard
paragraph: (2) A person in charge of a vessel in Canadian waters who discovers an uncharted hazard to navigation, or discovers that an aid to navigation is missing, out of position or malfunctioning, shall make a report without delay to a marine communications and traffic services officer or, if that is not feasible, to an officer of the Canadian Coast Guard.

heading: Designation - search and rescue mission coordinators
paragraph: 130 (1) The Minister may designate persons as search and rescue mission coordinators to organize search and rescue operations.

heading: Powers - search and rescue mission coordinators
paragraph: (2) On being informed that a person, a vessel or an aircraft is in distress or is missing in Canadian waters, in the exclusive economic zone of Canada or on the high seas off any of the coasts of Canada under circumstances that indicate that they may be in distress, a search and rescue mission coordinator may

heading: Powers - search and rescue mission coordinators
paragraph: (a) direct all vessels within an area that the search and rescue mission coordinator specifies to report their positions;

heading: Powers - search and rescue mission coordinators
paragraph: (b) direct any vessel to take part in a search for that person, vessel or aircraft or to otherwise render assistance;

heading: Powers - search and rescue mission coordinators
paragraph: (c) give any other directions that the search and rescue mission coordinator considers necessary to carry out search and rescue operations for that person, vessel or aircraft; and

heading: Powers - search and rescue mission coordinators
paragraph: (d) use any lands if it is necessary to do so for the purpose of saving the life of a shipwrecked person.

heading: Duty to comply
paragraph: (3) Every vessel or person on board a vessel in Canadian waters and every vessel or person on board a vessel in any waters that has a master who is a qualified person shall comply with a direction given to it or them under subsection (2).

heading: Answering distress signal
paragraph: 131 (1) Subject to this section, the master of a vessel in Canadian waters and every qualified person who is the master of a vessel in any waters, on receiving a signal from any source that a person, a vessel or an aircraft is in distress, shall proceed with all speed to render assistance and shall, if possible, inform the persons in distress or the sender of the signal.

heading: Distress signal - no assistance
paragraph: (2) If the master is unable or, in the special circumstances of the case, considers it unreasonable or unnecessary to proceed to the assistance of a person, a vessel or an aircraft in distress, the master is not required to proceed to their assistance and is to enter the reason in the official log book of the vessel.

heading: Ships requisitioned
paragraph: (3) The master of any vessel in distress may requisition one or more of any vessels that answer the distress call to render assistance. The master of a requisitioned vessel in Canadian waters and every qualified person who is the master of a requisitioned vessel in any waters shall continue to proceed with all speed to render assistance to the vessel in distress.

heading: Release from obligation
paragraph: (4) The master of a vessel shall be released from the obligation imposed by subsection (1) when the master learns that another vessel is complying with a requisition referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Further release
paragraph: (5) The master of a vessel shall be released from an obligation imposed by subsection (1) or (3) if the master is informed by the persons in distress or by the master of another vessel that has reached those persons that assistance is no longer necessary.

heading: Assistance
paragraph: 132 The master of a vessel in Canadian waters and every qualified person who is the master of a vessel in any waters shall render assistance to every person who is found at sea and in danger of being lost.

heading: Aircraft treated as if vessel
paragraph: 133 Sections 130 to 132 apply in respect of aircraft on or over Canadian waters as they apply in respect of vessels in Canadian waters, with any modifications that the circumstances require.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 135 (1) The Minister may designate any person or class of persons for the purposes of enforcing this Part.

heading: Designation - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (1.1) The Minister of Transport may designate any person or class of persons for the purposes of enforcing a provision of this Part or of a regulation made under this Part that the Minister of Transport is responsible for administering.

heading: Stopping and boarding vessel
paragraph: (2) A person, or a member of a class of persons, designated under subsection (1) or (1.1) who has reasonable grounds to believe that an offence has been committed or is about to be committed under this Part by a vessel or any person on board a vessel may stop and board the vessel and take any reasonable action to ensure public safety or protect the public interest.

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: 136 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Transport, make regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (a) establishing VTS Zones within Canadian waters or in a shipping safety control zone prescribed under the Arctic Waters Pollution Prevention Act;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (b) respecting the information to be provided and the procedures and practices to be followed by vessels that are about to enter, leave or proceed within a VTS Zone;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (c) respecting the conditions under which a clearance under section 126 is to be granted;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (d) defining the expression about to enter for the purpose of this Part;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (e) respecting aids to navigation in Canadian waters;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (f) regulating or prohibiting the navigation, anchoring, mooring or berthing of vessels for the purposes of promoting the safe and efficient navigation of vessels and protecting the public interest and the environment;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (g) respecting the safety of persons on Canadian waters for the purposes of sporting, recreational or public events or activities;

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (h) specifying classes of persons, or appointing persons, to ensure compliance with regulations made under any of paragraphs (b) and (e) to (g) and specifying their powers and duties; and

heading: Regulations - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (i) prescribing anything that may be prescribed under this Part.

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (c) respecting maritime search and rescue.

heading: Order - Minister of Transport
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Transport may, by order, suspend or modify the operation of regulations made under paragraph (1)(f) or (g).

heading: Cessation of effect of order
paragraph: (4) An order made under subsection (3) has effect from the time that it is made or from any later date that may be specified in the order but ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect of order
paragraph: (b) the day on which a regulation made under this Act that has the same effect as the order comes into force; and

heading: Cessation of effect of order
paragraph: (c) two years after the effective date of the order or any shorter period that may be specified in the order.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (5) The Statutory Instruments Act does not apply to an order made under subsection (3). However, the order must be published in the Canada Gazette within 23 days after it is made.

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: 137 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a) subsection 131(1) (assist persons in distress);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b) subsection 131(3) (comply with requisition to assist person in distress); or

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (c) section 132 (assist a person found at sea).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Defence
paragraph: (3) No person on board a vessel may be convicted of an offence under paragraph (1)(a), (b) or (c) if they had reasonable grounds to believe that compliance with subsection 131(1) or (3) or section 132, as the case may be, would have imperilled life, the vessel or another vessel.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 138 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) paragraph 126(1)(a) (entering, leaving or proceeding within a VTS Zone without a clearance);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) paragraph 126(1)(b) (proceeding within a VTS Zone when unable to maintain direct communication);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) a direction given under paragraph 126(3)(b), (c) or (d) (to provide information, to use radio frequencies or to leave, refrain from entering, proceed to or remain in a VTS Zone);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d) paragraph 126(5)(a) (take all reasonable measures to communicate);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (e) paragraph 126(5)(b) (obtain clearance);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (f) subsection 126(6) (remain at port or proceed to safe port);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (g) subsection 129(1) (report disturbance of aid to navigation);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (h) subsection 129(2) (report navigation hazard);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (i) subsection 130(3) (comply with direction of search and rescue mission coordinator); or

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (j) a provision of the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Defence available in certain cases
paragraph: (3) No vessel or person on board a vessel may be convicted of contravening subsection 126(1) (entering, leaving or proceeding within a VTS Zone) or a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 136(1)(b) if they had reasonable grounds to believe that compliance with that provision would have imperilled life, the vessel, another vessel or any property.

heading: Vessel may be detained
paragraph: (4) If the Minister or a person authorized by the Minister for the purpose of this subsection believes on reasonable grounds that an offence referred to in subsection (1) has been committed by or in respect of a vessel, the Minister or that person may make a detention order in respect of the vessel, and section 222 (detention of vessels) applies to the detention order, with any modifications that the circumstances require.

heading: Definition of Minister
paragraph: 140 In this Part, Minister means the Minister of Transport.

heading: Duty of masters in collision
paragraph: 148 If vessels collide, the master or person in charge of each vessel shall, if and in so far as they can to do so without endangering their vessel, crew or passengers,

heading: Duty of masters in collision
paragraph: (a) render to the other vessel, its master, crew and passengers the assistance that may be necessary to save them from any danger caused by the collision, and to stay by the other vessel until the master or person has determined that it has no need of further assistance; and

heading: Duty of masters in collision
paragraph: (b) give the name of their vessel, if any, the name and address of its authorized representative, if any, and any other prescribed information to the master or person in charge of the other vessel.

heading: Inquiry into cause of death on board
paragraph: 149 (1) If a person dies on board a Canadian vessel, on the vessel's arrival at a port in Canada, the Minister is to endeavour to ascertain the cause of death and, for that purpose, may hold an inquiry.

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of the inquiry, the Minister has the powers of a commissioner under Part I of the Inquiries Act and may, if it appears to the Minister to be necessary for the purpose of the inquiry,

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (a) go on board any vessel and inspect it or any part of it, or any of its machinery, equipment or cargo, while not detaining the vessel for longer than necessary from proceeding on a voyage; and

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (b) enter and inspect any premises at any reasonable time.

heading: Warrant required to enter living quarters
paragraph: (3) Living quarters may not be entered under subsection (2) unless they are entered with the consent of the occupant or under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (4).

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (4) On ex parte application, a justice, within the meaning of section 2 of the Criminal Code, may issue a warrant authorizing the Minister to enter living quarters, subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that entry to the living quarters

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) is necessary for the purpose of an inquiry; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) has been refused or there are reasonable grounds for believing that it will be refused.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (5) In executing a warrant, the Minister may not use force unless the Minister is accompanied by a peace officer and the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: 150 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (a) respecting the reporting of accidents or dangerous occurrences happening to or on board vessels, whether or not attended with loss of life;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (c) respecting the use of photographs, film, video recordings or electronic images of the human remains of victims of accidents involving a wrecked vessel or an aircraft wrecked in waters; and

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (d) prescribing anything that may be prescribed under this Part.

heading: Contravention of paragraph 148(a) or the regulations
paragraph: 151 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of paragraph 148(a) or the regulations
paragraph: (a) paragraph 148(a) (render assistance after a collision); or

heading: Contravention of paragraph 148(a) or the regulations
paragraph: (b) a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 150(1)(a).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 152 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) paragraph 148(b) (failure to provide information after a collision); or

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) a provision of the regulations made under paragraph 150(1)(c).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $25,000.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 165 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: discharge means a discharge of a pollutant from a vessel, or a discharge of oil from an oil handling facility or of a hazardous and noxious substance from a hazardous and noxious substances handling facility if the facility is engaged in loading to or unloading from a vessel, that directly or indirectly results in the pollutant entering the water, and includes spilling, leaking, pumping, pouring, emitting, emptying, throwing and dumping. (rejet)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hazardous and noxious substance means a substance other than oil that, if introduced into the marine environment, is likely to create hazards to human health, harm living resources and marine life, damage amenities or interfere with legitimate uses of the marine environment. (substance nocive et potentiellement dangereuse)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hazardous and noxious substances pollution incident means any occurrence or series of occurrences having the same origin, including fire or explosion, that results or may result in a discharge of hazardous and noxious substances. (evenement de pollution par les substances nocives et potentiellement dangereuses)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Transport. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: oil means petroleum in any form, including crude oil, fuel oil, sludge, oil refuse and refined products. (hydrocarbures)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: oil pollution incident means an occurrence, or a series of occurrences having the same origin, that results or may result in a discharge of oil. (evenement de pollution par les hydrocarbures)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pollutant means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a substance that, if added to any waters, would degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of the waters to an extent that is detrimental to their use by humans or by an animal or a plant that is useful to humans; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any water that contains a substance in such a quantity or concentration, or that has been so treated, processed or changed, by heat or other means, from a natural state, that it would, if added to any waters, degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of the waters to an extent that is detrimental to their use by humans or by an animal or a plant that is useful to humans.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: It includes oil, hazardous and noxious substances and any substance or class of substances that is prescribed for the purpose of this Part to be a pollutant. (polluant)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pollution damage in relation to a vessel, an oil handling facility or a hazardous and noxious substances facility, means loss or damage outside the vessel or facility caused by contamination resulting from a discharge from the vessel or facility. (dommages dus a la pollution)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: response organization means a qualified person to whom the Minister issues a certificate of designation under subsection 169(1). (organisme d'intervention)

heading: Application
paragraph: 166 (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Part, this Part applies in respect of vessels in Canadian waters or waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada and in respect of oil handling facilities and hazardous and noxious substances handling facilities that are in Canada.

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: (2) This Part does not apply in respect of a vessel that is on location and engaged in the exploration or drilling for, or the production, conservation or processing of, oil or gas in an area described in paragraph 3(a) or (b) of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: Definition of oil and gas

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: (3) In subsection (2), oil and gas have the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.

heading: Vessels - requirements
paragraph: 167 (1) Subject to subsection (2), every prescribed vessel or vessel of a prescribed class shall

heading: Vessels - requirements
paragraph: (a) have an arrangement with a response organization in respect of a quantity of oil that is at least equal to the total amount of oil that the vessel carries, both as cargo and as fuel, to a prescribed maximum quantity, and in respect of waters where the vessel navigates or engages in a marine activity; and

heading: Vessels - requirements
paragraph: (b) have on board a declaration, in the form specified by the Minister, that

heading: Vessels - requirements
paragraph: (i) identifies the name and address of the vessel's insurer or, in the case of a subscription policy, the name and address of the lead insurer who provides pollution insurance coverage in respect of the vessel,

heading: Vessels - requirements
paragraph: (ii) confirms that the arrangement has been made, and

heading: Vessels - requirements
paragraph: (iii) identifies every person who is authorized to implement the arrangement.

heading: Certain provisions do not apply to certain vessels
paragraph: (2) Paragraph (1)(a) and subparagraphs (1)(b)(ii) and (iii) do not apply in respect of a vessel that is in prescribed waters.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (3) The Minister may exempt, subject to any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate, for a specified period any vessel, or class of vessels, that is en route through waters referred to in subsection 166(1), from the application of any provision of this Part if the Minister is of the opinion that the vessel or class of vessels is subject to a provision of the laws of another state that provides for standards that are equivalent to or stricter than the standards provided for in the provision of this Part.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (4) Notice of every exemption must be published in the Canada Gazette.

heading: Notification of proposed operations
paragraph: 167.1 Subject to the regulations, a person who proposes to operate an oil handling facility of a class established by the regulations shall, within the prescribed time, notify the Minister of the proposed operations relating to the loading or unloading of oil to or from vessels and shall submit to the Minister any information or documents required by the regulations and, within the time specified by the Minister, any information or documents requested by the Minister.

heading: Submission of plans
paragraph: 167.2 (1) Subject to the regulations, a person who proposes to operate an oil handling facility of a class established by the regulations shall, at least 90 days before the day on which the oil handling facility's operations relating to the loading or unloading of oil to or from vessels will begin - or within any other time specified by the Minister - submit to the Minister

heading: Submission of plans
paragraph: (a) an oil pollution prevention plan to prevent a discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel, which meets the requirements set out in the regulations; and

heading: Submission of plans
paragraph: (b) an oil pollution emergency plan to respond to a discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel, which meets the requirements set out in the regulations.

heading: Submission of information or documents
paragraph: (2) A person referred to in subsection (1) shall submit to the Minister any information or documents requested by the Minister, within the time specified by the Minister.

heading: Prohibition against beginning operations
paragraph: (3) A person referred to in subsection (1) shall not begin operations relating to the loading or unloading of oil to or from vessels unless the plans submitted under subsection (1) meet the requirements set out in the regulations.

heading: Notification of operations
paragraph: 167.3 Subject to the regulations, the operator of an oil handling facility of a class established by the regulations shall notify the Minister of the oil handling facility's operations relating to the loading or unloading of oil to or from vessels within 90 days after the day on which this section comes into force and shall submit to the Minister any information or documents required by the regulations and, within the time specified by the Minister, any information or documents requested by the Minister.

heading: Submission of plans
paragraph: 167.4 Subject to the regulations, unless the plans have already been submitted under subsection 167.2(1), the operator of an oil handling facility of a class established by the regulations shall submit to the Minister, within the time set out in the regulations, an oil pollution prevention plan to prevent a discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel and an oil pollution emergency plan to respond to a discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel - which meet the requirements set out in the regulations - and shall submit to the Minister any information or documents requested by the Minister, within the time specified by the Minister.

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: 168 (1) Subject to the regulations, the operator of an oil handling facility of a class established by the regulations shall

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (a) have an arrangement with a response organization in respect of any quantity of oil that is, at any time, involved in being loaded or unloaded to or from a vessel at the oil handling facility, to a prescribed maximum quantity;

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (b) have on site a declaration in the form specified by the Minister that

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (i) describes the manner in which the operator will comply with the regulations made under paragraph 182(1)(a),

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (ii) confirms that the arrangement has been made, and

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (iii) identifies every person who is authorized to implement the arrangement and the oil pollution emergency plan referred to in paragraph (d);

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (c) have on site an up-to-date oil pollution prevention plan to prevent a discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel, which meets the requirements set out in the regulations;

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (c.1) submit the up-to-date oil pollution prevention plan to the Minister within the time and in the circumstances set out in the regulations;

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (d) have on site an up-to-date oil pollution emergency plan to respond to a discharge or possible discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel, which meets the requirements set out in the regulations;

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (d.1) submit the up-to-date oil pollution emergency plan to the Minister within the time and in the circumstances set out in the regulations; and

heading: Oil handling facilities - requirements
paragraph: (e) have the procedures, equipment and resources required by the regulations available for immediate use in the event of a discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel.

heading: Duty to take reasonable measures - oil handling facilities
paragraph: (3) The operator of an oil handling facility referred to in subsection (1) shall take reasonable measures to implement

heading: Duty to take reasonable measures - oil handling facilities
paragraph: (a) the oil pollution prevention plan referred to in paragraph (1)(c); and

heading: Duty to take reasonable measures - oil handling facilities
paragraph: (b) in respect of an oil pollution incident, the oil pollution emergency plan referred to in paragraph (1)(d).

heading: Notification of proposed change to operations
paragraph: 168.01 (1) Subject to the regulations, an operator of an oil handling facility of a class established by the regulations that proposes to make a change, or permit a change to be made, to the oil handling facility's operations relating to the loading or unloading of oil to or from vessels shall - at least 180 days before the day on which it makes the change or permits the change to be made - notify the Minister of the change, including any of the following changes:

heading: Notification of proposed change to operations
paragraph: (a) a change in the oil handling facility's transfer rate, if the change would result in the oil handling facility becoming part of a different class established by the regulations;

heading: Notification of proposed change to operations
paragraph: (b) a change in the design of the oil handling facility, or a change in the oil handling facility's equipment; or

heading: Notification of proposed change to operations
paragraph: (c) a change in the type or composition of oil that is loaded or unloaded to or from vessels.

heading: Submission of information or documents
paragraph: (2) The operator referred to in subsection (1) shall submit to the Minister any information or documents required by the regulations and, within the time specified by the Minister, any information or documents requested by the Minister.

heading: Revise plans
paragraph: (3) The operator referred to in subsection (1) shall revise the oil pollution prevention plan and the oil pollution emergency plan and submit the revised plans to the Minister at least 90 days before making the change or permitting the change to be made, or within any other time specified by the Minister.

heading: Prohibition against making changes
