paragraph: (4) An operator shall not make a change referred to in subsection (1) or permit one to be made unless the plans submitted under subsection (3) meet the requirements set out in the regulations.

heading: Update or revise plans
paragraph: 168.1 Despite any other provision of this Part or the regulations, the Minister may direct the operator of an oil handling facility to update or revise an oil pollution prevention plan or an oil pollution emergency plan and to submit the up-to-date or revised plan to the Minister within the time specified by the Minister.

heading: Provide information
paragraph: 168.2 A marine safety inspector may direct any person to provide the inspector with any information that the inspector reasonably requires in the administration of this Part.

heading: Minister may take measures
paragraph: 168.3 If the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that an oil handling facility has discharged, is discharging or may discharge oil, that the oil pollution prevention plan or the oil pollution emergency plan for an oil handling facility does not meet the requirements set out in the regulations or that the operator of an oil handling facility does not have the procedures, equipment and resources required by the regulations available for immediate use in the event of a discharge of oil during the loading or unloading of a vessel, the Minister may

heading: Minister may take measures
paragraph: (a) monitor the measures taken by any person to repair, remedy, minimize or prevent pollution damage from the oil handling facility; or

heading: Minister may take measures
paragraph: (b) if he or she considers it necessary, direct the operator of the oil handling facility to take the measures that the Minister considers necessary to repair, remedy, minimize or prevent pollution damage from the oil handling facility, including to stop loading or unloading oil to or from vessels.

heading: Certificate of designation
paragraph: 169 (1) The Minister may, in respect of any geographic area and in respect of a prescribed quantity of oil, issue a certificate of designation as a response organization to a qualified person who makes an application.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) An application for a certificate must be made in the form and manner, include the information and be accompanied by the documents specified by the Minister.

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (3) In addition to the specified information and documents, the Minister may require that an applicant

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (a) provide evidence, including declarations, that the Minister considers necessary to establish that the requirements for the issuance of the certificate have been met; and

heading: Further evidence
paragraph: (b) undergo any examinations and have its installations undergo any inspections that the Minister considers necessary to establish that the requirements for the issuance of the certificate have been met.

heading: Period of validity
paragraph: (4) Every certificate is valid for the period specified by the Minister.

heading: Refusal to issue or renew
paragraph: (5) The Minister may refuse to issue or renew a certificate if the Minister is of the opinion that the public interest and, in particular, the record of the applicant or of a principal of the applicant warrant it.

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (6) The Minister may suspend or cancel a certificate in the circumstances and on the grounds set out in the regulations.

heading: Statement of fees
paragraph: 170 (1) A response organization, or a qualified person who makes an application under subsection 169(1), must notify the Minister, in the form and manner and including the information and accompanied by the documents specified by the Minister, of the fees that they propose to charge in relation to an arrangement referred to in paragraph 167(1)(a) or 168(1)(a).

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) A response organization, or a qualified person who makes an application under subsection 169(1), must give notice of the proposed fees in the prescribed manner.

heading: Charging fees
paragraph: (3) A response organization may not charge the fees before the expiry of 30 days after the notice is given.

heading: Fee review
paragraph: (4) On the application of any interested person in the prescribed manner within 30 days after the notice is given, the Minister is to review the reasonableness of the proposed fees.

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (5) The Minister may appoint a person to assist in the review. The person has all the powers of a commissioner under Part I of the Inquiries Act.

heading: Order to amend or eliminate fee
paragraph: (6) The Minister may, by order, amend or eliminate a fee reviewed under subsection (4). The order comes into effect on the first day that the fee is charged.

heading: Notice of order
paragraph: (7) The response organization affected by the order must give notice of it in the prescribed manner.

heading: Prescribed procedures, equipment and resources
paragraph: 171 Every response organization shall

heading: Prescribed procedures, equipment and resources
paragraph: (a) have a response plan that meets the prescribed requirements;

heading: Prescribed procedures, equipment and resources
paragraph: (b) have the prescribed equipment and resources at the site set out in the response plan;

heading: Prescribed procedures, equipment and resources
paragraph: (c) provide or arrange for prescribed training to prescribed classes of persons;

heading: Prescribed procedures, equipment and resources
paragraph: (d) undertake and participate in prescribed activities to evaluate the response plan or its implementation;

heading: Prescribed procedures, equipment and resources
paragraph: (e) on the request of a vessel or the operator of an oil handling facility with which the response organization has an arrangement referred to in paragraph 167(1)(a) or 168(1)(a), as the case may be, implement a response consistent with the response plan; and

heading: Prescribed procedures, equipment and resources
paragraph: (f) on the request of the Minister or an advisory council established under section 172, provide information regarding any of the matters referred to in paragraphs (a) to (e).

heading: Provide documents
paragraph: 171.1 A marine safety inspector may direct a response organization to provide the inspector with any document that the organization is required to have under this Part.

heading: Advisory councils
paragraph: 172 (1) The Minister may establish an advisory council in respect of any geographic area for the purpose of advising the Minister with respect to this Part.

heading: Members
paragraph: (2) Each advisory council is to be composed of no more than seven members who are appointed to the council by the Minister and who, in the Minister's opinion, can represent the communities and interests potentially affected by an oil spill in that area.

heading: Term
paragraph: (3) Each member of an advisory council is to be appointed for a term of not more than three years and is eligible for reappointment.

heading: President
paragraph: (4) An advisory council must elect one of its members to be its president.

heading: Honoraria and expenses
paragraph: (5) The members of an advisory council may be paid the honoraria that the Minister considers appropriate and may be paid any reasonable travel, living and child care expenses incurred by them when engaged on the business of the council while absent from their ordinary place of residence.

heading: Recommendations
paragraph: (6) An advisory council is to advise and may make recommendations to the Minister.

heading: Meetings in public
paragraph: (7) Advisory council meetings must be open to the public unless the council is satisfied that a public meeting would not be in the public interest, in which case the meeting or any part of it may be held in private.

heading: Review and report by Minister
paragraph: 173 Every five years, the Minister must review the operation of sections 167 to 172 and have laid before each House of Parliament a report setting out the results of the review.

heading: Designation of pollution response officer
paragraph: 174.1 (1) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may designate any persons or classes of persons as pollution response officers in respect of discharges or threats of discharges and may limit in any manner that he or she considers appropriate the powers that the officers may exercise under this Part.

heading: Certificate of designation
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans must furnish every pollution response officer with a certificate of designation and, if the officer's powers are limited under subsection (1), the certificate must specify the powers that the officer may exercise.

heading: Powers of pollution response officers - general
paragraph: 175.1 (1) A pollution response officer may

heading: Powers of pollution response officers - general
paragraph: (a) direct a vessel, if it is about to enter or is within waters in respect of which this Part applies, to provide him or her with any information that he or she considers appropriate for the administration of this Part;

heading: Powers of pollution response officers - general
paragraph: (b) direct any vessel that is within or about to enter waters in respect of which this Part applies and that he or she believes on reasonable grounds to be carrying a pollutant to proceed through those waters by the route, and at a speed not in excess of the speed, that he or she may specify;

heading: Powers of pollution response officers - general
paragraph: (c) direct a vessel that is required to have a shipboard oil pollution emergency plan under the regulations to provide information concerning it and its implementation;

heading: Powers of pollution response officers - general
paragraph: (d) direct the operator of an oil handling facility to provide any document that the operator is required to have on site under this Part; and

heading: Powers of pollution response officers - general
paragraph: (e) direct a response organization to provide any document that the organization is required to have under this Part.

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (2) If the pollution response officer believes on reasonable grounds that a vessel has discharged, is discharging or may discharge a pollutant, he or she may

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (a) direct a vessel that is within or about to enter waters in respect of which this Part applies to proceed through those waters by the route, and at a speed not in excess of the speed, that he or she may specify;

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (b) go on board and take samples of any substance that he or she believes to be the pollutant;

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (c) if the vessel is within or about to enter waters in respect of which this Part applies, direct the vessel to

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (i) proceed to the place within waters in respect of which this Part applies that he or she may specify, by the route and in the manner that he or she may specify, and to moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that he or she may specify,

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (ii) proceed out of waters in respect of which this Part applies, by the route and in the manner that he or she may specify, or

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (iii) remain outside waters in respect of which this Part applies; and

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (d) if he or she is informed that a substantial quantity of a pollutant has entered or been discharged in waters in respect of which this Part applies, or if on reasonable grounds he or she is satisfied that a grave and imminent danger of a substantial discharge of a pollutant in those waters exists, declare an emergency zone, the size of which is reasonable with regard to the seriousness of the situation, and

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (i) direct any vessel within that emergency zone to report its position to him or her,

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (ii) direct any vessel not to enter or not to leave the emergency zone, and

heading: Powers - discharge of pollutant
paragraph: (iii) direct any vessel within the emergency zone in respect of routes, speed limits and pilotage and equipment requirements.

heading: Disposition of samples
paragraph: (3) An officer who takes a sample under paragraph (2)(b) may dispose of it in any manner that he or she considers appropriate or may submit it for analysis or examination to a person designated by the Minister.

heading: Certificate or report
paragraph: (4) A person who has made an analysis or examination may issue a certificate or report that sets out the results of the analysis or examination.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsections (6) and (7), the certificate or report is admissible in evidence in any proceeding related to an offence under this Part and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, is proof of the statements contained in the certificate or report without proof of the signature or the official character of the person appearing to have signed it.

heading: Attendance of person
paragraph: (6) The party against whom the certificate or report is produced may, with leave of the court, require for the purposes of cross-examination the attendance of the person who issued it.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (7) The certificate or report may be admitted in evidence only if the party who intends to produce it has given to the party against whom it is intended to be produced reasonable notice of that intention, together with a copy of the certificate or report.

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: 176 (1) For the purpose of exercising his or her powers under this Part, a pollution response officer may

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (a) board any vessel or enter any premises or other place at any reasonable time;

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (b) direct any person to provide reasonable assistance or put into operation or cease operating any machinery or equipment;

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (c) direct any person to provide any information that the officer may reasonably require in the administration of this Part;

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (d) direct any person to produce for inspection, or for the purpose of making copies or taking extracts, any log book or other document;

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (e) take photographs and make video recordings and sketches;

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (f) use or cause to be used any computer system or data processing system at the place to examine any data contained in, or available to, the system;

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (g) reproduce or cause to be reproduced any record from the data in the form of a print-out or other intelligible output;

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (h) take any document or other thing from the place where the inspection is being carried out for examination or, in the case of a document, copying; and

heading: Powers of pollution response officer
paragraph: (i) use or cause to be used any copying equipment in the place where the inspection is being carried out to make copies of any documents.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) Living quarters may not be entered under subsection (1) unless they are entered with the consent of the occupant or under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (3).

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (3) On ex parte application, a justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing a pollution response officer to enter living quarters, subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that entry to the living quarters

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) is necessary for any purpose related to the carrying out of the officer's powers under this Part; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) has been refused or there are reasonable grounds for believing that it will be refused.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (4) No officer executing a warrant may use force unless they are accompanied by a peace officer and the use of force is specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Return of documents and things
paragraph: (5) Documents or other things taken under paragraph (1)(h) must be returned as soon as feasible after they are no longer required for the inspection or for any proceedings that may result from it.

heading: Detention
paragraph: 177 (1) If a pollution response officer believes on reasonable grounds that an offence under this Part has been committed by or in respect of a vessel, he or she may make a detention order in respect of the vessel.

heading: Order to be in writing
paragraph: (2) A detention order made under this section must be in writing and be addressed to every person empowered to grant clearance in respect of the vessel.

heading: Detention order to be served on master
paragraph: (3) Notice of a detention order made under this section in respect of a vessel must be served on the master

heading: Detention order to be served on master
paragraph: (a) by delivering a copy of the notice personally to the master; or

heading: Detention order to be served on master
paragraph: (b) if service cannot reasonably be effected in the manner provided in paragraph (a), by leaving a copy of the notice with the person who is, or appears to be, in charge of the vessel or, if there is no such person, by fixing a copy of the notice to a prominent part of the vessel.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (4) The notice must

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (a) indicate the measures to ensure compliance with this Part that must be taken for the detention order to be rescinded; and

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (b) if an indictment has been preferred in respect of the offence, indicate the amount and form of security that, pending the outcome of any proceedings related to the indictment, must be deposited with the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans for the detention order to be rescinded.

heading: Foreign state to be notified
paragraph: (5) If a vessel in respect of which a detention order is made under this section is registered in a foreign state, that state is to be notified that the order was made.

heading: Rescission of orders
paragraph: (6) A pollution response officer must

heading: Rescission of orders
paragraph: (a) rescind a detention order made under this section if he or she is satisfied that the measures indicated in the notice referred to in subsection (4) have been taken and, if applicable, security in the amount and form indicated in the notice referred to in that subsection has been deposited with the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans; and

heading: Rescission of orders
paragraph: (b) notify, in the form and manner specified by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, the master and the persons referred to in subsection (2) of the rescission.

heading: Duty of persons empowered to give clearance
paragraph: (7) No person to whom a detention order made under this section is addressed shall, after notice of the order is received by them, grant clearance to the vessel in respect of which the order was made unless they have been notified that the order has been rescinded under subsection (6).

heading: Movement of vessel prohibited
paragraph: (8) Subject to section 179, no person shall move a vessel that is subject to a detention order made under this section.

heading: Liability for expenses
paragraph: (9) The authorized representative or, if there is no authorized representative, the owner of a vessel that is detained under this section is liable for all expenses incurred in respect of the detained vessel.

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (10) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, after proceedings in respect of which security was deposited are concluded,

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (a) may apply the security to reimburse Her Majesty in right of Canada, either fully or partially, if any of the expenses or any fine has not been paid; and

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (b) is to return the security, or any part of it that remains if it is applied under paragraph (a), if all expenses and any fine imposed have been paid.

heading: Interference with service
paragraph: 178 No person shall wilfully interfere with the service of a notice of a detention order.

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: 179 The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: (a) on application made by the authorized representative or, if there is no authorized representative, the owner of a detained vessel, in the form and manner specified by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, permit the master to move it in accordance with the directions of the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans;

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: (b) on application made by the owner of a dock or wharf, or by the person in charge of a harbour, at which a detained vessel is situated, in the form and manner specified by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, direct the person who is, or appears to be, in charge of the vessel to move the vessel in accordance with the directions of the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans; and

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: (c) if a person to whom a direction is given under paragraph (b) does not comply with it and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is satisfied that the applicant for the direction has sufficient insurance in place to cover any incident that may arise from the moving of the vessel, authorize the applicant to move the vessel in accordance with the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans' directions and at the expense of the authorized representative or, if there is no authorized representative, the owner.

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - measures
paragraph: 180 (1) If the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans believes on reasonable grounds that a vessel, an oil handling facility or a hazardous and noxious substances handling facility has discharged, is discharging or may discharge a pollutant, that Minister may

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - measures
paragraph: (a) take the measures that that Minister considers necessary to repair, remedy, minimize or prevent pollution damage from the vessel or facility, including, in the case of a vessel, by removing - or by selling, dismantling, destroying or otherwise disposing of - the vessel or its contents;

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - measures
paragraph: (b) monitor the measures taken by any person or vessel to repair, remedy, minimize or prevent pollution damage from the vessel or facility; or

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - measures
paragraph: (c) if that Minister considers it necessary to do so, direct any person or vessel to take measures referred to in paragraph (a) or to refrain from doing so.

heading: Clear title
paragraph: (2) When a vessel or its contents are disposed of under paragraph 180(1)(a), the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may give the person acquiring them a valid title to the vessel or its contents free from any mortgage, hypothec, maritime lien or other interest or right that is in existence at the time of the disposition.

heading: At risk and expense of owner
paragraph: (2.1) The disposition is at the risk, cost and expense of the owner of the vessel or its contents.

heading: Payment of proceeds
paragraph: (2.2) When a vessel or its contents are disposed of under paragraph 180(1)(a), any surplus remaining from the proceeds of the disposition after deducting the costs and expenses incurred in respect of the disposition shall be paid to the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, in respect of all costs and expenses incurred in taking any other measures under this Part, and to the holders, if known at the time of the disposition, of any mortgages, hypothecs, maritime liens or other interests or rights that are in existence at the time of the disposition, and any amount that remains after paying the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans and the holders shall be paid to the owner of the vessel or the contents.

heading: Federal Court directions
paragraph: (2.3) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may apply to the Federal Court for directions as to the allocation of the surplus referred to in subsection (2.2).

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (3) Compensation must be paid by His Majesty in right of Canada for the services of any person or vessel, other than the operator of a vessel, an oil handling facility or a hazardous and noxious substances handling facility that had discharged, was discharging or may have discharged a pollutant, that has complied with a direction issued under paragraph (1)(c).

heading: Priority
paragraph: (4) A direction made by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans under paragraph (1)(c) prevails over an order or direction made under any Act of Parliament, to the extent of any inconsistency.

heading: Entry on private property
paragraph: 180.1 (1) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or a pollution response officer may enter private property - other than a dwelling-house - and pass through it, including with vehicles and equipment, for the purposes of exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under this Part.

heading: Accompanying persons
paragraph: (2) If the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or a pollution response officer enters private property and passes through it, they may be accompanied by any person who they believe is necessary to help them in exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under this Part.

heading: Use of property
paragraph: (3) If required, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or the pollution response officer may use property adjacent to or in the vicinity of a vessel, oil handling facility or hazardous and noxious substances handling facility - other than a dwelling-house - for the purposes of exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under this Part, and any person accompanying that Minister or the pollution response officer may use such property to help that Minister or officer exercise their powers or perform their duties or functions under this Part.

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (4) Her Majesty in right of Canada may compensate the owner of the property referred to in subsection (3), or any person that has, either by law or by contract, the rights of the owner of that property in respect of its possession and use, for any loss or damage caused by the use of that property under subsection (3) that exceeds the value of the benefit derived by the owner or person from that use.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: 180.2 An order or direction given under this Part by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or a pollution response officer is not a statutory instrument as defined in the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Immunity - taking or refraining from taking measures
paragraph: 181 (1) A person who, or vessel that, is directed to take or refrain from taking measures under paragraph 180(1)(c) is not personally liable, either civilly or criminally, for anything they do or omit to do in the course of complying with the direction, unless it is established that the act or omission was not reasonable in the circumstances.

heading: Immunity - providing assistance
paragraph: (1.1) A person who provides assistance or advice in taking or refraining from taking any measure under section 180 is not personally liable, either civilly or criminally, for anything that they do or omit to do in the course of providing the assistance or advice, unless it is established that the act or omission was not reasonable in the circumstances.

heading: Immunity - accompanying Minister or officer
paragraph: (1.2) A person who accompanies the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or a pollution response officer under subsection 180.1(2) or (3) is not personally liable, either civilly or criminally, for anything that they do or omit to do in the exercise of their powers under that subsection in accompanying the Minister or officer, unless it is established that the act or omission was not reasonable in the circumstances.

heading: Civil or criminal liability
paragraph: (2) Response organizations, their agents or mandataries, and persons who have been designated in writing by the Minister as approved responders, are not personally liable, either civilly or criminally, in respect of any act or omission occurring or arising during the course of a response operation unless it is shown that the act or omission was committed with the intent to cause loss or damage, or recklessly and with the knowledge that loss or damage would probably result.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Nothing in subsection (1) affects the liability of the owner of a vessel, or of the vessel, that had discharged, was discharging or may have discharged a pollutant in respect of

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) the occurrence that resulted in the taking of the measures referred to in subsection 180(1); and

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) any act or omission in the course of complying with a direction given under paragraph 180(1)(c).

heading: Definition of response operation
paragraph: (4) In this section, response operation means the activities undertaken following a discharge, or a grave and imminent threat of a discharge, from a vessel or an oil handling facility, including activities related to or connected with surveillance of and assessing areas of pollution, mobilizing and demobilizing response equipment and resources, protective booming, containment, recovery, dispersal or destruction of the pollutant, shoreline mitigation and restoration, transporting and disposing of recovered pollutant or waste materials and planning and supervising activities related to the response operation.

heading: Immunity - civil liability
paragraph: 181.1 The following persons are not civilly liable for anything they do or omit to do in good faith under this Part:

heading: Immunity - civil liability
paragraph: (a) a servant of the Crown, as those terms are defined in section 2 of the Crown Liability and Proceedings Act; and

heading: Immunity - civil liability
paragraph: (b) a pollution response officer.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 182 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Part, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the circumstances in which operators of oil handling facilities shall report discharges or anticipated discharges of pollutants, the manner of making the reports and the persons to whom the reports shall be made;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the issuance, amendment, suspension, reinstatement, cancellation or renewal of certificates referred to in section 169;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the purposes for which fees may be charged in relation to an arrangement referred to in paragraph 167(1)(a) or 168(1)(a) and the manner in which response organizations and persons who make an application under subsection 169(1) must calculate proposed fees before notifying the Minister of the fees under subsection 170(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the establishment by response organizations of committees of persons who have arrangements with them and the provision to the committees of information regarding fees and proposed fees;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d.1) establishing classes of oil handling facilities and determining which of the requirements set out in sections 167.1 to 168.01 apply to the operators of, or to persons who propose to operate, oil handling facilities of each class;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d.2) respecting oil pollution prevention plans and oil pollution emergency plans, including the time within which the plans shall be submitted to the Minister and the circumstances in which up-to-date plans shall be submitted to the Minister;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d.3) respecting the procedures, equipment and resources referred to in paragraph 168(1)(e) and section 168.3;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d.4) respecting the information and documents referred to in sections 167.1 and 167.3 and subsection 168.01(2), including the time within which the information and documents shall be submitted to the Minister; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) prescribing anything that by this Part is to be prescribed.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (2) Despite the regulations, the Minister may designate an oil handling facility that is part of a class established by the regulations to be part of a different class established by the regulations or an oil handling facility that is not part of a class established by the regulations to be part of one of those classes.

heading: Notification
paragraph: (3) The Minister shall notify the operator of an oil handling facility of any designation made in respect of it under subsection (2).

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: 183 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

paragraph: (a) paragraph 167(1)(a) (have an arrangement);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a.1) subsection 167.2(1) (submission of oil pollution prevention plan and oil pollution emergency plan);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a.2) subsection 167.2(3) (prohibition against beginning operations);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a.3) section 167.4 (submission of plans);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b) paragraph 168(1)(a) (have an arrangement);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b.1) paragraph 168(1)(c.1) (submission of up-to-date oil pollution prevention plan);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b.2) paragraph 168(1)(d.1) (submission of up-to-date oil pollution emergency plan);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (c) paragraph 168(1)(e) (have procedures, equipment and resources available for immediate use);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (d) paragraph 168(3)(a) (implement oil pollution prevention plan);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (e) paragraph 168(3)(b) (implement oil pollution emergency plan);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (e.01) subsection 168.01(3) (revise plans);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (e.02) subsection 168.01(4) (prohibition against making changes);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (e.1) a direction given under section 168.1 (to update or revise plans);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (e.2) a direction given under paragraph 168.3(b) (to take measures);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (f) paragraph 171(b) (have equipment and resources at the site);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (g) paragraph 171(e) (implement response plan);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (h) a direction given under paragraph 175.1(2)(a), (c) or (d) (direction resulting from a discharge or possible discharge of a pollutant);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (i) subsection 177(7) (giving clearance to detained vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (j) subsection 177(8) (moving detained vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (k) section 178 (wilfully interfering with service of notice); or

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (l) a direction given under paragraph 180(1)(c) (to take measures or refrain from doing so).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than eighteen months, or to both.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 184 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) paragraph 167(1)(b) (have a declaration on board);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.1) section 167.1 (notification of proposed operations);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.2) subsection 167.2(2) (submission of information or documents);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.3) section 167.3 (notification of operations);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) paragraph 168(1)(b) (have a declaration on site);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) paragraph 168(1)(c) (have oil pollution prevention plan on site);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d) paragraph 168(1)(d) (have oil pollution emergency plan on site);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d.01) subsection 168.01(1) (notification of proposed change to operations);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d.02) subsection 168.01(2) (submission of information or documents);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d.1) a direction given under section 168.2 (to provide information);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (e) paragraph 171(a) (have a response plan);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (f) paragraph 171(c) (provide or arrange for training);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (g) paragraph 171(d) (undertake and participate in activities to evaluate response plan);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (h) paragraph 171(f) (provide information);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (h.1) a direction given under section 171.1 (to provide documents);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (i) a direction given under paragraph 175.1(1)(a) (to provide information officer considers appropriate);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (j) a direction given under paragraph 175.1(1)(b) (to proceed by a route and not in excess of a speed);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (k) a direction given under paragraph 175.1(1)(c) (to provide information relating to pollution plan);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (l) a direction given under paragraph 175.1(1)(d) or (e) (to provide documents);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (m) a direction given under paragraph 176(1)(b) (to provide reasonable assistance);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (n) a direction given under paragraph 176(1)(c) or (d) (to provide information or to produce documents for inspection); and

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (o) a provision of the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 185 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: discharge means a discharge of a pollutant that directly or indirectly results in the pollutant entering waters, and includes spilling, leaking, pumping, pouring, emitting, emptying, throwing and dumping. (rejet)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hazardous and noxious substance means a substance other than oil that, if introduced into the marine environment, is likely to create hazards to human health, harm living resources and marine life, damage amenities or interfere with legitimate uses of the marine environment. (substance nocive et potentiellement dangereuse)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hazardous and noxious substances pollution incident means any occurrence or series of occurrences having the same origin, including fire or explosion, that results or may result in a discharge of hazardous and noxious substances. (evenement de pollution par les substances nocives et potentiellement dangereuses)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Transport. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: oil pollution incident means an occurrence, or a series of occurrences having the same origin, that results or may result in a discharge of oil. (evenement de pollution par les hydrocarbures)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pollutant means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a substance that, if added to any waters, would degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of the waters to an extent that is detrimental to their use by humans or by an animal or a plant that is useful to humans; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any water that contains a substance in such a quantity or concentration, or that has been so treated, processed or changed, by heat or other means, from a natural state, that it would, if added to any waters, degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of the waters to an extent that is detrimental to their use by humans or by an animal or a plant that is useful to humans.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: It includes oil, hazardous and noxious substances and any substance or class of substances that is prescribed for the purpose of Part 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans) to be a pollutant. (polluant)

heading: Application
paragraph: 186 (1) Subject to subsection (2), this Part applies in respect of vessels in Canadian waters or waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada.

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: (2) This Part does not apply in respect of a discharge of oil or gas from a vessel that is on location and engaged in the exploration or drilling for, or the production, conservation or processing of, oil or gas in an area described in paragraph 3(a) or (b) of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act, in so far as the discharge emanates from those activities.

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: Definition of oil and gas

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: (3) In subsection (2), oil and gas have the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.

heading: General duties
paragraph: 186.1 (1) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel must

heading: General duties
paragraph: (a) ensure that the vessel and its machinery and equipment meet the requirements of the regulations made under this Part;

heading: General duties
paragraph: (b) develop procedures for preventing the discharge of a pollutant and for dealing with emergencies;

heading: General duties
paragraph: (c) ensure that the crew receives training in emergency procedures; and

heading: General duties
paragraph: (d) ensure that the crew and passengers receive training in environmental protection.

heading: Duties - Canadian maritime documents inspection
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel must ensure that

heading: Duties - Canadian maritime documents inspection
paragraph: (a) the vessel and its machinery and equipment are inspected for the purpose of obtaining all of the Canadian maritime documents that are required under this Part; and

heading: Duties - Canadian maritime documents inspection
paragraph: (b) every term or condition attached to a Canadian maritime document issued in respect of the vessel or its machinery or equipment is met.

heading: Masters obtaining Canadian maritime documents
paragraph: 186.2 The master of a Canadian vessel must, before the vessel embarks on a voyage from a port in Canada, ensure that all of the Canadian maritime documents required under this Part have been obtained.

heading: Protection of marine environment
paragraph: 186.3 (1) The master of a vessel must take all reasonable measures to ensure the protection of the marine environment.

heading: Duty to take reasonable measures
paragraph: (2) If the master of a vessel is informed that the vessel may have discharged, has discharged, is discharging or may discharge a pollutant, the master must take reasonable measures to protect the marine environment from the discharge or risk of discharge, including eliminating the risk if feasible. The master of a Canadian vessel must notify the authorized representative of the discharge or risk, unless the risk has been eliminated.

heading: Discharge of pollutant prohibited
paragraph: 187 No person or vessel shall discharge a prescribed pollutant, except in accordance with the regulations made under this Part or a permit granted under Division 3 of Part 7 of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999.

heading: Implementation of oil pollution emergency plan
paragraph: 188 If a vessel is required by the regulations to have a shipboard oil pollution emergency plan, the vessel shall take reasonable measures to implement the plan in respect of an oil pollution incident.

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: 189 (1) If the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that a vessel may discharge, or may have discharged, a prescribed pollutant, the Minister may

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: (a) direct a vessel, if it is about to enter or is within waters to which this Part applies, to provide the Minister with any information that the Minister considers appropriate for the administration of this Part;

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: (a.1) direct a vessel that is required to have a shipboard oil pollution emergency plan under the regulations to provide him or her with any information concerning it and its implementation;

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: (b) direct a vessel that is required to have on board a declaration described in paragraph 167(1)(b) to provide information concerning it;

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: (c) direct a vessel that is within or about to enter waters in respect of which this Part applies to proceed through those waters by the route and in the manner that the Minister may specify; and

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: (d) direct the vessel to proceed to the place that the Minister may select, by the route and in the manner that the Minister may specify, and to

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: (i) unload the pollutant, or

heading: Powers in case of discharge
paragraph: (ii) moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that the Minister may specify.

heading: Direction to authorize vessel
paragraph: (2) The Minister may direct a port authority or a person in charge of a port authority or place to authorize a vessel in respect of which a direction has been made under paragraph (1)(d) to proceed to the place selected by the Minister and to

heading: Direction to authorize vessel
paragraph: (a) unload the pollutant; or

heading: Direction to authorize vessel
paragraph: (b) moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that the Minister may specify.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 190 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations respecting the protection of the marine environment, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing pollutants for the purpose of section 187 and subsection 189(1) and respecting the circumstances in which such pollutants may be discharged;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the circumstances in which persons on board vessels shall report discharges or anticipated discharges, the manner of making the reports and the persons to whom the reports shall be made;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the carrying of pollutants on board a vessel, whether as cargo or fuel;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the control and prevention of pollution of the air by vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting reception facilities for oily residues, chemical residues, garbage and sewage;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the control and management of ballast water;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) for preventing or reducing the release by vessels into waters of aquatic organisms or pathogens that, if released into those waters, could create hazards to human health, harm organisms, damage amenities, impair biological diversity or interfere with legitimate uses of the waters;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) respecting the design, construction, manufacture and maintenance of vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) specifying the machinery, equipment and supplies that must be on board vessels or classes of vessels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) respecting the design, construction, manufacture, maintenance, storage, testing, arrangement and use of vessels' or classes of vessels' machinery, equipment and supplies;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) respecting the requirements that vessels, or classes of vessels, and their machinery and equipment must meet;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (l) requiring the obtaining of certificates certifying that any of the requirements referred to in paragraph (k) are met;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (m) respecting the inspection and testing of vessels, or classes of vessels, and their machinery, equipment and supplies; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (n) respecting shipboard hazardous and noxious substances pollution emergency plans.

heading: Application of regulations
paragraph: (2) Regulations made under subsection (1) apply in respect of vessels that are capable of engaging in the drilling for, or the production, conservation or processing of, oil or gas only if the regulations so state and were made on the joint recommendation of the Minister and the Minister of Natural Resources.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 191 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) paragraph 186.1(1)(a) (ensure vessel meets requirements);

paragraph: (a.1) paragraph 186.1(1)(b) (develop procedures);

paragraph: (a.2) paragraph 186.1(1)(c) (ensure emergency procedures training);

paragraph: (a.3) paragraph 186.1(1)(d) (ensure environmental protection training);

paragraph: (a.4) paragraph 186.1(2)(a) (ensure vessel inspected);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.5) paragraph 186.1(2)(b) (ensure terms and conditions met);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.6) section 186.2 (obtain Canadian maritime documents);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.7) subsection 186.3(1) (protection of marine environment);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.8) subsection 186.3(2) (take reasonable measures);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a.9) section 187 (discharge of a pollutant);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) section 188 (implement shipboard oil pollution emergency plan);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) a direction given under subparagraph 189(1)(d)(i) (direction to proceed to a place and unload a pollutant);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c.1) a direction given under subsection 189(2) (direction to authorize a vessel); and

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d) a provision of the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person or vessel that commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph: (3) If an offence under paragraph (1)(a) is committed or continued on more than one day, the person or vessel that committed it is liable to be convicted for a separate offence for each day on which it is committed or continued.

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (4) In determining the punishment under subsection (2), the court may have regard to the following factors:

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (a) the harm or risk of harm caused by the offence;

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (b) an estimate of the total costs of clean-up, of harm caused, and of the best available mitigation measures;

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (c) the remedial action taken, or proposed to be taken, by the offender to mitigate the harm;

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (d) whether the discharge or anticipated discharge was reported in accordance with the regulations made under paragraph 190(1)(b);

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (e) any economic benefits accruing to the offender that, but for the offence, the offender would not have received; and

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (f) any evidence from which the court may reasonably conclude that the offender has a history of non-compliance with legislation designed to prevent or to minimize pollution.

heading: Contravention of directions
paragraph: 192 (1) Every vessel commits an offence that contravenes

heading: Contravention of directions
paragraph: (a) a direction given under paragraph 189(1)(a) or (b) (direction to provide information);

heading: Contravention of directions
paragraph: (a.1) a direction given under paragraph 189(1)(a.1) (direction to provide information - shipboard oil pollution emergency plan);

heading: Contravention of directions
paragraph: (b) a direction given under paragraph 189(1)(c) (direction to proceed by a specified route); or

heading: Contravention of directions
paragraph: (c) a direction given under subparagraph 189(1)(d)(ii) (direction to proceed to a place and remain there).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every vessel that commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000.

heading: Court orders
paragraph: 193 If an offender is convicted of an offence under this Part, in addition to imposing any other punishment that may be imposed under this Act, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order having any or all of the following effects:

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the offender from performing any act or engaging in any activity that may result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (b) directing the offender to publish the facts relating to the conviction;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (c) directing the offender to submit to the Minister, on application by the Minister made within three years after the date of the conviction, any information with respect to the offender's activities that the court considers appropriate and just in the circumstances;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (d) in the case of a discharge, directing the offender to pay an amount for the purpose of conducting research into the ecological use and disposal of the pollutant in respect of which the offence was committed; and

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (e) requiring the offender to comply with any other reasonable conditions that the court considers appropriate and just in the circumstances for securing the offender's good conduct and preventing the offender from repeating the same offence or committing other offences.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 194 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: enforcement officer means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a member of any harbour or river police force;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a member of any provincial, county or municipal police force; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any person, or member of a class of persons, designated under subsection 196(1). (agent de l'autorite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inspector means a pleasure craft safety inspector designated under subsection 195(1). (inspecteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: licence means a licence issued for a pleasure craft under this Part. (permis)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Transport. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pollutant means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a substance that, if added to any waters, would degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of the waters to an extent that is detrimental to their use by humans or by an animal or a plant that is useful to humans; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any water that contains a substance in such a quantity or concentration, or that has been so treated, processed or changed, by heat or other means, from a natural state, that it would, if added to any waters, degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of the waters to an extent that is detrimental to their use by humans or by an animal or a plant that is useful to humans.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: It includes oil, hazardous and noxious substances and any substance or class of substances that is prescribed for the purpose of Part 8 (Pollution Prevention and Response - Department of Transport and Department of Fisheries and Oceans) to be a pollutant. (polluant)

heading: Designation
paragraph: 195 (1) The Minister may designate persons or classes of persons as pleasure craft safety inspectors.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: (2) The Minister must furnish every inspector with a certificate of designation as a pleasure craft safety inspector authorizing the inspector to carry out inspections under sections 196 and 198.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: (3) Inspectors are not personally liable for anything they do or omit to do in good faith under this Part.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 196 (1) The Minister may designate persons or classes of persons as enforcement officers.

heading: Inspections - general
paragraph: (2) An enforcement officer may inspect a pleasure craft or any of its machinery or equipment for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any provision of this Part, other than section 197, or the regulations made under this Part, other than the regulations made under paragraph 207(1)(f), (g), (i) or (j).

heading: Inspections - structural integrity
paragraph: (3) An inspector may inspect a pleasure craft or any of its machinery or equipment for structural integrity or compliance with the regulations made under any of paragraphs 207(1)(f) to (m).

heading: Powers
paragraph: (4) Enforcement officers acting under subsection (2) and inspectors acting under subsection (3) may

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) stop or board the craft at any reasonable time;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) direct any person to put into operation or cease operating any machinery or equipment on the craft;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) direct that the craft not be moved until the inspection is completed;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (d) direct any person to move the craft to a safe place if the officer or inspector has reasonable grounds to believe that it does not meet the requirements of this Part or the regulations made under this Part or exposes any person to serious danger, and direct that it not be operated until it meets those requirements or no longer exposes any person to serious danger; and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (e) direct any person to move the craft to a safe place if the officer or inspector has reasonable grounds to believe that the operator does not meet the requirements of the regulations made under this Part, and direct that the operator not operate it until the operator meets those requirements.

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (5) The owner or person in charge of a pleasure craft and every person on board shall

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (a) give an officer or inspector all reasonable assistance to enable them to carry out an inspection and exercise any power conferred by this section; and

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (b) produce to an officer or inspector any document, or provide them with any information, that the officer or inspector may reasonably require, for the administration of this Part or Part 5 (Navigation Services) or the regulations made under either of those Parts.

heading: Manufacturers and importers
paragraph: 197 (1) Every manufacturer, builder or importer of a pleasure craft shall ensure that it is constructed in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Vendors
paragraph: (2) No person shall, in the course of a commercial enterprise, sell a pleasure craft that does not display a plate or label if required to do so by the regulations made under paragraph 207(1)(h).

heading: Powers
paragraph: 198 (1) An inspector may, for the purpose of ensuring that a manufacturer, importer or vendor is in compliance with section 197,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) enter any place, other than a dwelling-house, where the inspector has reasonable grounds to believe a pleasure craft is located;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) examine anything that the inspector finds and take samples of it;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) conduct any tests or analyses and take any measurements;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (d) inspect any books, records, electronic data or other documents that the inspector believes may contain information that is relevant to the inspection;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (e) use or cause to be used any computer system in the place where the inspection is being carried out to examine any data contained in or available to the computer system;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (f) reproduce or cause to be reproduced any record from the data in the form of a print-out or other intelligible output;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (g) take any document or other thing from the place where the inspection is being carried out for examination or, in the case of a document, copying; and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (h) use or cause to be used any copying equipment in the place where the inspection is being carried out to make copies of any documents.

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (2) When an inspector carries out an inspection under subsection (1), the importer, manufacturer or vendor of the pleasure craft, or the owner or person in control of a place where the pleasure craft is located, shall

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (a) give the inspector all reasonable assistance to enable them to carry out the inspection and exercise any power conferred by this section; and

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (b) produce to the inspector any document, or provide them with any information, that the inspector may reasonably require for the administration of this Part or the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Return of documents and things
paragraph: (3) Documents or other things obtained or taken under paragraph (1)(g) must be returned as soon as feasible after they are no longer required for the inspection or for any proceedings that may result from it.

heading: Disposition of samples
paragraph: (4) An inspector who takes a sample under paragraph (1)(b) may dispose of it in any manner that they consider appropriate.

heading: Operation prohibited
paragraph: 199 If an inspector considers that a pleasure craft does not meet the requirements of this Part or the regulations made under this Part, the inspector may direct any person not to operate it until it meets those requirements.

heading: Stopping and boarding vessels
paragraph: 200 An enforcement officer who has reasonable grounds to believe that an offence has been committed or is about to be committed under this Part by a pleasure craft or any person on board a vessel may stop and board the craft or vessel and take any reasonable action to ensure public safety or protect the public interest.

heading: Duty
paragraph: 201 Every operator of a pleasure craft shall ensure that it meets the requirements of the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Licensing of pleasure craft
paragraph: 202 (1) Subject to the regulations, if a pleasure craft is required by regulations made under this Part to be licensed, the owner of the craft must not operate it, or permit it to be operated, unless it is licensed.

heading: Transfer of licence
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, when the ownership of a pleasure craft referred to in subsection (1) changes, the new owner must not operate the craft, or permit it to be operated, until the licence for that craft is transferred to the new owner in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Application
paragraph: 203 (1) An application for a licence or for the transfer of a licence must be made in the form and manner, include the information and be accompanied by the documents specified by the Minister.

heading: Issuance of licence
paragraph: (2) The Minister may issue or transfer a licence to an applicant if the Minister is satisfied that all the requirements under subsection (1) have been met.

heading: Refusal to issue or transfer licence
paragraph: 203.1 Despite any other provision of this Act, the Minister may refuse to issue - including by way of renewal - or transfer a licence for a pleasure craft or may refuse to issue a replacement licence if the applicant for, or holder of, the licence is in default of payment of a required fee, charge, cost or expense in respect of that pleasure craft under this Act or the Wrecked, Abandoned or Hazardous Vessels Act.

heading: Licence number
paragraph: 204 No owner of a pleasure craft in respect of which a pleasure craft licence has been issued shall operate it or allow it to be operated unless the licence number is marked on the craft and maintained in the form and manner specified by the Minister.

heading: Defacing, etc., licence number
paragraph: 205 No person shall deface, alter, conceal or remove the licence number that is marked on a pleasure craft.

heading: Lost documents
paragraph: 206 If a pleasure craft licence is mislaid, lost or destroyed, the Minister, on application made by the holder of the licence in the form and manner and including the information and accompanied by the documents specified by the Minister, may issue a replacement licence.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 207 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations respecting pleasure craft licensing and the safety of pleasure craft or classes of pleasure craft and of persons on board, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the issuance, cancellation or transfer of pleasure craft licences;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting qualifications, including medical fitness, minimum age, degree of knowledge, skill, training and experience, for operators of pleasure craft or classes of pleasure craft, and the evidence required to prove compliance with those qualifications;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the operation of pleasure craft or classes of pleasure craft;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting training courses and examinations for pleasure craft operators, including the designation and accreditation of persons or organizations that provide them;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the issuance, cancellation or suspension of documents that demonstrate compliance with any regulations made under paragraph (b) or (d);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the design, construction or manufacture of pleasure craft or classes of pleasure craft;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the issuance or cancellation of plates or labels in respect of pleasure craft that comply with regulations made under paragraph (f);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) requiring that plates or labels referred to in paragraph (g) be displayed and specifying the manner in which they must be displayed;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) prohibiting the construction, manufacture, sale, lease, importation or operation of pleasure craft that do not meet the requirements of regulations made under paragraph (f);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) requiring owners, builders, manufacturers, importers or vendors of pleasure craft to modify their pleasure craft, at their own expense, in order to comply with regulations made under paragraph (f);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) respecting hull identification or serial numbers that identify pleasure craft;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (l) specifying the machinery and equipment that are required or prohibited on pleasure craft or classes of pleasure craft;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (m) respecting the design, construction, manufacture, maintenance, storage, testing, approval, arrangement and use of a pleasure craft's or a class of pleasure craft's machinery and equipment;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (n) respecting the requirements that pleasure craft, or classes of pleasure craft, and their machinery and equipment must meet;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (o) respecting documents that must be kept on board pleasure craft or classes of pleasure craft; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (p) respecting the reporting of accidents involving pleasure craft.

heading: Regulations - pollution
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations

heading: Regulations - pollution
paragraph: (a) regulating or prohibiting the discharge of pollutants from pleasure craft; and

heading: Regulations - pollution
paragraph: (b) regulating noise emissions from pleasure craft engines.

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: 208 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a) subsection 197(1) (ensure a pleasure craft is constructed in accordance with the regulations); or

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b) subsection 197(2) (selling a pleasure craft without a plate or label).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 209 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) a direction given under any of paragraphs 196(4)(b) to (e) (to operate or cease operating machinery or equipment, to not move a pleasure craft or to move a pleasure craft to a safe place);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) subsection 196(5) (give reasonable assistance, produce documents or provide information);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) subsection 198(2) (give reasonable assistance, produce documents or provide information);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (d) a direction given under section 199 (not to operate a pleasure craft);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (e) section 201 (ensure that a pleasure craft meets the requirements of the regulations);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (f) section 202 (obtain a licence for a pleasure craft);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (g) section 204 (operating pleasure craft without licence number marked);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (h) section 205 (defacing, altering, concealing or removing licence number); or

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (i) a provision of the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $25,000.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 210 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Transport. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: relevant provision means a provision of this Act or the regulations that the Minister is responsible for administering. (disposition visee)

heading: Authorized persons and organizations
paragraph: 211 (1) A marine safety inspector referred to in section 11 or a person, classification society or other organization authorized to carry out inspections under section 12 may, for the purpose of ensuring compliance with a relevant provision, board any vessel or enter any premises or other place at any reasonable time and carry out any inspection that the inspector, person, classification society or other organization considers necessary and that the Minister has authorized them to carry out.

heading: Living quarters
paragraph: (2) Living quarters may not be entered under subsection (1) unless they are entered with the consent of the occupant, under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (2.1) or for the purpose of ensuring that a vessel complies with a relevant provision.

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (2.1) On ex parte application, a justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing a marine safety inspector to enter living quarters, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that entry to the living quarters

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) is necessary for any purpose related to the administration of a relevant provision of Part 8; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) has been refused or there are reasonable grounds for believing that it will be refused.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (2.2) A marine safety inspector executing a warrant must not use force unless they are accompanied by a peace officer and the use of force is specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Stopping a vessel
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of carrying out an inspection, a marine safety inspector may direct the master of a vessel to stop the vessel or proceed to the place that the inspector may select, and to moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that the inspector may specify.

heading: Direction to authorize vessel
paragraph: (3.1) A marine safety inspector may direct a port authority or a person in charge of a port authority or place to authorize a vessel in respect of which a direction has been made under subsection (3) to proceed to the place selected by the inspector and moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that the inspector may specify.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (4) In carrying out an inspection, a marine safety inspector or, subject to any limitations set out under subsection 12(2) in their certificate of authorization, a person, classification society or other organization authorized to carry out inspections may

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) direct any person to answer reasonable questions, provide reasonable assistance or put into operation or cease operating any machinery or equipment being inspected;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) direct the master of a vessel to prohibit or limit access to any part of the vessel for as long as specified;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) direct the master of a vessel not to move the vessel until the inspection is completed;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (d) direct the master of a vessel to muster the crew or to carry out any emergency or safety procedure required by the regulations;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (d.1) direct the operator of an oil handling facility, or a person who proposes to operate an oil handling facility, to carry out any emergency or safety procedure that is required by the regulations or that is described in an oil pollution prevention plan or an oil pollution emergency plan referred to in Part 8;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (e) direct any person who is at the place where the inspection is being carried out to produce for inspection, or for the purpose of making copies or taking extracts, any document that they are required to have, or that the operator of an oil handling facility is required to have on site, under a relevant provision;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (f) take photographs and make video recordings and sketches;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (g) take or remove for analysis samples of any material or substance or any biological, chemical or physical agents or substances;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (h) use or cause to be used any computer system or data processing system at the place where the inspection is being carried out to examine any data contained in, or available to, the system;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (i) reproduce or cause to be reproduced any record from the data in the form of a print-out or other intelligible output;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (j) take any document or other thing from the place where the inspection is being carried out for examination or, in the case of a document, copying; and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (k) use or cause to be used any copying equipment in the place where the inspection is being carried out to make copies of any documents.

heading: Disposition of samples
paragraph: (5) A person who, or organization that, takes a sample under paragraph (4)(g) may dispose of it in any manner that the person or organization considers appropriate.

heading: Return of documents and things
paragraph: (6) Documents or other things taken under paragraph (4)(j) must be returned as soon as feasible after they are no longer required for the purpose for which they were taken.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: 212 (1) During an inspection, a marine safety inspector may seize and detain anything

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (a) by means of which or in relation to which the inspector believes on reasonable grounds that a relevant provision has been contravened; or

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (b) that the inspector believes on reasonable grounds will afford evidence in respect of a contravention of a relevant provision.

heading: Storage or removal
paragraph: (2) An inspector may direct the person in charge of the place where something was seized to store it in that place or may remove it to any other place.

heading: Return of things or forfeiture
paragraph: (3) Any thing seized must be returned as soon as feasible after it is no longer needed for any proceedings unless it cannot be brought into compliance with the relevant provisions and the Minister directs that it not be returned, in which case it is forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada after it is no longer needed for any proceedings and may be disposed of at the expense of the person from whom it was seized.

heading: No departure without clearance
paragraph: 213 Subject to the regulations, no vessel shall depart from a port in Canada unless clearance has been granted.

heading: Granting clearance
