paragraph: 214 Any person who is authorized under an Act of Parliament to grant clearance of a vessel at a port in Canada is not to grant it unless satisfied that the master has all of the documents required under this Act for the clearance.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 215 No master shall proceed on a voyage with a person on board who is exercising powers or performing duties relating to the administration or enforcement of a relevant provision unless the person consents.

heading: Reasonable grounds
paragraph: 216 (1) An individual who has reasonable grounds to believe that a person or vessel has contravened or intends to contravene a relevant provision may notify the Minister of the particulars of the matter and may request that their identity be kept confidential with respect to the notification.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (2) The identity of an individual to whom the Minister has provided an assurance of confidentiality may be disclosed by the Minister only in accordance with the Privacy Act.

heading: Inspection
paragraph: 217 (1) On being notified under subsection 216(1), the Minister is to determine whether an inspection should be carried out by a marine safety inspector.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (2) If a marine safety inspector determines that the individual who notified the Minister did not have reasonable grounds to believe that a person or vessel had contravened or had intended to contravene a relevant provision, the individual is liable to pay the costs of the inspection.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 218 (1) No employer shall dismiss, suspend, demote, discipline, harass or otherwise disadvantage an employee, or deny an employee a benefit of employment, by reason that

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (a) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, disclosed to the Minister that the employer or any other person had contravened or had intended to contravene a relevant provision;

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (b) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, refused or stated an intention of refusing to do anything that is a contravention of a relevant provision;

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (c) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, did or stated an intention of doing anything that is required to be done in order that a contravention of a relevant provision not be committed; or

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (d) the employer believes that the employee will do anything referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c).

heading: Saving
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section impairs any right of an employee either at law or under an employment contract or collective agreement.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (3) In this section, employee includes an independent contractor and employer has a corresponding meaning.

heading: Investigations
paragraph: 219 (1) The Minister may appoint any person to investigate a shipping casualty or an alleged contravention of a relevant provision.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) A person appointed under subsection (1) may not make findings as to the causes and contributing factors of a shipping casualty that has been or is being investigated by the Canadian Transportation Accident Investigation and Safety Board or that that Board has informed the Minister they propose to investigate.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: Definition of shipping casualty

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (3) In this section, shipping casualty means

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (a) any accident or incident associated with a vessel; and

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (b) any situation or condition that the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe could, if left unattended, induce an accident or incident described in paragraph (a).

heading: Search and seizure without warrant
paragraph: 220 (1) If the conditions for obtaining a warrant under section 487 of the Criminal Code exist in respect of the contravention of a relevant provision but by reason of exigent circumstances it would not be feasible to obtain one, a marine safety inspector may exercise the powers of search and seizure provided in that section without a warrant.

heading: Living quarters
paragraph: (2) A marine safety inspector may not search living quarters without a warrant unless the inspector first obtains the consent of the occupant.

heading: Additional powers
paragraph: (3) In the course of a search under subsection (1) or section 487 of the Criminal Code, a marine safety inspector has all the powers referred to in subsection 211(4) (inspections).

heading: Submission
paragraph: 221 (1) A marine safety inspector may submit to a person designated by the Minister, for analysis or examination, anything seized or any sample taken under this Part.

heading: Certificate or report
paragraph: (2) A person who has made an analysis or examination may issue a certificate or report that sets out the results of the analysis or examination.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the certificate or report is admissible in evidence in any proceeding related to the contravention of a relevant provision and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, is proof of the statements contained in the certificate or report without proof of the signature or the official character of the person appearing to have signed it.

heading: Attendance of analyst
paragraph: (4) The party against whom the certificate or report is produced may, with leave of the court, require for the purposes of cross-examination the attendance of the person who issued it.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (5) The certificate or report may be admitted in evidence only if the party who intends to produce it has given to the party against whom it is intended to be produced reasonable notice of that intention, together with a copy of the certificate or report.

heading: Optional detention
paragraph: 222 (1) If a marine safety inspector believes on reasonable grounds that a contravention of a relevant provision has been committed by or in respect of a vessel or that the vessel is not seaworthy, the inspector may make a detention order in respect of the vessel.

heading: Mandatory detention - unsafe vessels
paragraph: (2) The inspector must make a detention order if the contravention is a contravention of section 110 (too many passengers) or the inspector also believes on reasonable grounds that the vessel is unsafe, that it is unfit to carry passengers or crew members or that its machinery or equipment is defective in any way so as to expose persons on board to serious danger.

heading: Mandatory detention - foreign vessels
paragraph: (3) If an information has been laid, an indictment has been preferred or a notice of violation has been issued or an assurance of compliance has been entered into under section 229 in respect of a contravention of a relevant provision that is alleged to have been committed by or in respect of a foreign vessel, a marine safety inspector must make a detention order in respect of the vessel.

heading: Order to be in writing
paragraph: (4) A detention order made under this section must be in writing and be addressed to every person empowered to grant clearance in respect of the vessel.

heading: Detention order to be served on master
paragraph: (5) Notice of a detention order made under this section in respect of a vessel must be served on the master

heading: Detention order to be served on master
paragraph: (a) by delivering a copy of the notice personally to the master; or

heading: Detention order to be served on master
paragraph: (b) if service cannot reasonably be effected in the manner provided in paragraph (a), by leaving a copy of the notice with the person who is, or appears to be, in charge of the vessel or, if there is no such person, by fixing a copy of the notice to a prominent part of the vessel.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (6) The notice must

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (a) indicate the measures to ensure compliance with the relevant provision or to render the vessel seaworthy that must be taken for the detention order to be rescinded;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (b) in the case of a foreign vessel, if an information has been laid, an indictment has been preferred or a notice of violation has been issued or an assurance of compliance has been entered into under section 229 in respect of a contravention of a relevant provision, indicate the amount and form of security that, pending the outcome of any proceedings related to the information, indictment or notice, must be deposited with the Minister for the detention order to be rescinded; and

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (c) in the case of a Canadian vessel, if an indictment has been preferred in respect of a contravention of a relevant provision, indicate the amount and form of security that, pending the outcome of any proceedings related to the indictment, must be deposited with the Minister for the detention order to be rescinded.

heading: Foreign state to be notified
paragraph: (7) If a vessel in respect of which a detention order is made under this section is registered in a foreign state, that state is to be notified that the order was made.

heading: Rescission of orders
paragraph: (8) A marine safety inspector must

heading: Rescission of orders
paragraph: (a) rescind a detention order made under this section if the inspector is satisfied that the measures indicated in the notice referred to in subsection (6) have been taken and, if applicable, security in the amount and form indicated in the notice referred to in that subsection has been deposited with the Minister; and

heading: Rescission of orders
paragraph: (b) notify, in the form and manner specified by the Minister, the master and the persons referred to in subsection (4) of the rescission.

heading: Duty of persons empowered to give clearance
paragraph: (9) No person to whom a detention order made under this section is addressed shall, after notice of the order is received by them, grant clearance to the vessel in respect of which the order was made unless they have been notified that the order has been rescinded under subsection (8).

heading: Movement of vessel prohibited
paragraph: (10) Subject to section 224, no person shall move a vessel that is subject to a detention order made under this section.

heading: Liability for expenses
paragraph: (11) The authorized representative and the owner of a vessel that is detained under this section are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for all expenses incurred in respect of the detained vessel.

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (12) The Minister, after proceedings in respect of which security was deposited are concluded,

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (a) may apply the security to reimburse Her Majesty in right of Canada, either fully or partially, if any of the expenses or any fine or penalty has not been paid; and

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (b) is to return the security, or any part of it that remains if it is applied under paragraph (a), if all expenses and any fine or penalty imposed have been paid.

heading: Interference with service
paragraph: 223 No person shall wilfully interfere with the service of a notice of a detention order.

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: 224 The Minister may

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: (a) on application made by the authorized representative of a detained vessel in the form and manner specified by the Minister, permit the master to move it in accordance with the directions of the Minister;

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: (b) on application made by the owner of a dock or wharf or by the person in charge of a harbour at which a detained vessel is situated in the form and manner specified by the Minister, direct the person who is, or appears to be, in charge of the vessel to move the vessel in accordance with the directions of the Minister; and

heading: Direction to move a detained vessel
paragraph: (c) if a person to whom a direction is given under paragraph (b) does not comply with it and the Minister is satisfied that the applicant for the direction has sufficient insurance in place to cover any incident that may arise from the moving of the vessel, authorize the applicant to move the vessel in accordance with the Minister's directions and at the expense of the authorized representative and the owner of the vessel, for which the authorized representative and the owner are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for the expense of moving the vessel.

heading: Distress on vessel for sums ordered to be paid
paragraph: 225 A court, justice of the peace or provincial court judge that orders the authorized representative of a vessel to pay any fine, crew member's wages or other sum of money may, if payment is not made in accordance with the order, order the seizure and sale of the vessel or its machinery or equipment.

heading: Vessel may be seized and sold if fine or penalty not paid
paragraph: (2) At any time after a fine is imposed under a relevant provision against, or a certificate is registered in the Federal Court under subsection 235(2) in respect of, a vessel, its authorized representative or its owner, the Minister may, while the fine or debt remains unpaid, seize the vessel and, after giving notice to the authorized representative or owner, sell it and, by bill of sale, give the purchaser a valid title to the vessel free from any mortgage or other claim on the vessel that exists at the time of the sale.

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (3) Any surplus remaining from the proceeds of a sale is to be distributed in accordance with the regulations after satisfying the following claims in the following order:

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (a) the cost of the seizure and sale;

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (b) any claim for salvage in respect of the vessel;

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (c) the claims of masters and crew members for wages;

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (c.1) the claims of masters for disbursements made or liabilities incurred for necessaries on account of the vessel;

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (d) the amount of any fine imposed or debt due under a relevant provision; and

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (e) the cost of returning masters and crew members to the place where they first came on board or to another place to which they and the Minister have agreed.

heading: If proceeds insufficient
paragraph: (4) If the proceeds of sale of a vessel are insufficient to satisfy the claims described in subsection (3), the Minister may proceed for the balance owing against

heading: If proceeds insufficient
paragraph: (a) the authorized representative and the owner, jointly and severally, or solidarily, in the case of a Canadian vessel; and

heading: If proceeds insufficient
paragraph: (b) the owner, in the case of a foreign vessel.

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: 227 (1) If the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that a foreign vessel is in contravention of an international convention, protocol or resolution listed in Schedule 1, the Minister may

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (a) if the vessel has not entered Canadian waters, direct the vessel not to enter Canadian waters;

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (b) if the vessel has entered Canadian waters but is not in a port in Canada, direct the vessel to leave Canadian waters; and

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (c) if the vessel is in a port in Canada, direct the vessel to leave Canadian waters, subject to any terms and conditions that the Minister may specify.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) The Minister may not give a direction under subsection (1) if, in the Minister's opinion, doing so would put the safety of the vessel, any person on board or the environment at imminent risk.

heading: Notification
paragraph: (3) If the Minister gives a direction under subsection (1) in respect of a vessel, the Minister must notify the state where the vessel is registered of the direction given and the reason for it.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Definition of violation

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 228 In sections 229 to 244, violation means a contravention of a relevant provision, or a contravention of a direction given under a relevant provision, that is designated as a violation by the regulations made under this Part.

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: 229 (1) If the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that a person or vessel has committed a violation, the Minister may

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (a) enter into an assurance of compliance with the person or vessel that

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (i) identifies the violation and provides that the person or vessel will comply with the provision to which the violation relates within the period, and be subject to the terms and conditions, specified in the assurance,

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (ii) sets out the amount and form of any security that, pending compliance with the assurance, must be deposited with the Minister, and

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (iii) sets out the penalty, fixed by or within the range fixed by the regulations made under this Part, for the violation that the person or vessel would have been liable to pay if the assurance had not been entered into; or

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (b) issue, and cause to be served on the person or vessel, a notice of violation that names the person or vessel, identifies the violation and sets out

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (i) the penalty, fixed by or within the range fixed by the regulations made under this Part, for the violation that the person or vessel is liable to pay,

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (ii) the period, being thirty days after the notice is served, within which the penalty must be paid or a review of the notice requested, and

heading: If reasonable grounds to believe a violation
paragraph: (iii) particulars of the manner in which, and the address at which, the penalty must be paid or a review requested.

heading: Extension of period
paragraph: (2) The Minister may extend the period specified under subparagraph (1)(a)(i) if the Minister is satisfied that the person with whom or vessel with which the assurance of compliance was entered into is unable to comply with it because of reasons beyond the person's or vessel's control.

heading: Short-form descriptions in notices of violation
paragraph: (3) The Minister may establish, in respect of each violation, a short-form description to be used in notices of violation.

heading: Deemed violation
paragraph: 230 (1) A person who, or vessel that, enters into an assurance of compliance is, unless a review is requested under subsection (2), deemed to have committed the violation in respect of which the assurance was entered into.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (2) A person who, or vessel that, enters into an assurance of compliance may, within 48 hours after the assurance is signed, unless a notice of default is served within that period under section 231.1, request a review of the facts of the violation, in which case the assurance is deemed to be a notice of violation and a review under paragraph 232(1)(b) of the facts of the violation and the amount of the penalty is deemed to have been requested.

heading: When assurance of compliance complied with
paragraph: 231 If the Minister is satisfied that an assurance of compliance has been complied with, the Minister must cause a notice to that effect to be served on the person or vessel and, on the service of the notice,

heading: When assurance of compliance complied with
paragraph: (a) no further proceedings may be taken against the person or vessel with respect to the violation in respect of which the assurance was entered into; and

heading: When assurance of compliance complied with
paragraph: (b) any security deposited under subparagraph 229(1)(a)(ii) must be returned to the person or vessel.

heading: When assurance of compliance not complied with
paragraph: 231.1 (1) If the Minister is of the opinion that a person who, or vessel that, has entered into an assurance of compliance has not complied with it, the Minister may cause a notice of default to be served on the person or vessel to the effect that, unless a member determines under section 231.2, or an appeal panel decides under section 232.2, that the assurance has been complied with,

heading: When assurance of compliance not complied with
paragraph: (a) the person or vessel is liable to pay double the amount of the penalty set out in the assurance; or

heading: When assurance of compliance not complied with
paragraph: (b) the security deposited under subparagraph 229(1)(a)(ii) is forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) must include the address at which, and the date, being 30 days after the notice is served, on or before which, a request for a review may be filed.

heading: No set-off
paragraph: (3) On the service of a notice of default, the person or vessel served has no right of set-off against any amount spent by the person or vessel under the assurance of compliance.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: 231.2 (1) A person or vessel served with a notice under subsection 231.1(1) may, on or before the date specified in the notice or within any further time that the Tribunal on application allows, file a written request for a review.

heading: Time and place for review
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a request filed under subsection (1), the Tribunal must appoint a time and place for the review and must notify the Minister and the person who, or vessel that, filed the request of the time and place in writing.

heading: Review procedure
paragraph: (3) The member of the Tribunal assigned to conduct the review must provide the Minister and the person or vessel with an opportunity consistent with procedural fairness and natural justice to present evidence and make representations.

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: (4) The burden is on the Minister to establish that the person or vessel did not comply with the assurance of compliance referred to in the notice. The person is not required, and must not be compelled, to give any evidence or testimony in the matter.

heading: Certain defences not available
paragraph: (5) A person or vessel named in a notice of default does not have a defence by reason that the person or vessel exercised due diligence to comply with the assurance of compliance.

heading: Determination
paragraph: (6) The member may confirm the Minister's decision or determine that the person or vessel has complied with the assurance of compliance.

heading: Return of security
paragraph: 231.3 Any security deposited under subparagraph 229(1)(a)(ii) must be returned to the person or vessel if

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (a) the person or vessel pays double the amount of the penalty set out in the assurance of compliance in accordance with a notice of default under section 231.1; or

heading: Return of security
paragraph: (b) a member determines under section 231.2, or an appeal panel decides under section 232.2, that the assurance of compliance has been complied with.

heading: Notice of violation
paragraph: 232 (1) A person or vessel served with a notice of violation under paragraph 229(1)(b) must

heading: Notice of violation
paragraph: (a) pay the amount of the penalty; or

heading: Notice of violation
paragraph: (b) within thirty days after being served or any further time that the Tribunal on application allows, file with the Tribunal a written request for a review of the facts of the violation or the amount of the penalty.

heading: When review not requested
paragraph: (2) If a review of the facts of the violation is not requested, the person or vessel is deemed to have committed the violation in respect of which the notice was served.

heading: Time and place for review
paragraph: 232.1 (1) On receipt of a request filed under paragraph 232(1)(b), the Tribunal must appoint a time and place for the review and must notify the Minister and the person who, or vessel that, filed the request of the time and place in writing.

heading: Review procedure
paragraph: (2) The member of the Tribunal assigned to conduct the review must provide the Minister and the person or vessel with an opportunity consistent with procedural fairness and natural justice to present evidence and make representations.

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: (3) The burden is on the Minister to establish that the person or vessel committed the violation referred to in the notice. The person is not required, and must not be compelled, to give any evidence or testimony in the matter.

heading: Determination
paragraph: (4) The member may confirm the Minister's decision or, subject to any regulations made under paragraph 244(h), substitute his or her own determination.

heading: Right of appeal
paragraph: 232.2 (1) The Minister or the person who, or vessel that, requested the review may, within 30 days after the determination, appeal a determination made under subsection 231.2(6) or 232.1(4) to the Tribunal.

heading: Loss of right of appeal
paragraph: (2) A party that does not appear at a review hearing is not entitled to appeal a determination, unless they establish that there was sufficient reason to justify their absence.

heading: Disposition of appeal
paragraph: (3) The appeal panel of the Tribunal assigned to hear the appeal may

heading: Disposition of appeal
paragraph: (a) in the case of a determination made under subsection 231.2(6), dismiss the appeal or allow the appeal and substitute its own decision; or

heading: Disposition of appeal
paragraph: (b) in the case of a determination made under subsection 232.1(4), dismiss the appeal, or allow the appeal and, subject to regulations made under paragraph 244(h), substitute its own decision.

heading: How contravention may be proceeded with
paragraph: 233 If a contravention can be proceeded with as a violation or as an offence, the Minister may commence proceedings in respect of that contravention as a violation or recommend that it be proceeded with as an offence, but it may be proceeded with only as one or the other.

heading: Debts due to Her Majesty
paragraph: 234 The following amounts constitute debts due to Her Majesty in right of Canada that may be recovered in a court of competent jurisdiction:

heading: Debts due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (a) unless a review of the amount of the penalty is requested under paragraph 232(1)(b), the amount of a penalty set out in a notice of violation, from the time the notice is served;

heading: Debts due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (b) the amount that a notice of default served under subsection 231.1(1) provides that a person is liable to pay, from the time the notice is served;

heading: Debts due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (c) the amount of a penalty determined by a member after a review under section 232.1, or decided by an appeal panel after an appeal under section 232.2, from the time of the respective determination or decision; and

heading: Debts due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (d) the amount of any reasonable expenses incurred in attempting to recover an amount referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (c).

heading: Certificate
paragraph: 235 (1) All or part of a debt referred to in section 234 in respect of which there is a default of payment may be certified by the Minister or the Tribunal, as the case may be.

heading: Judgments
paragraph: (2) On production to the Federal Court, a certificate made under subsection (1) is to be registered in that Court and, when registered, has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment obtained in that Court for a debt of the amount specified in it and all reasonable costs and charges attendant in its registration.

heading: Violations are not offences
paragraph: 236 For greater certainty, a violation is not an offence and, accordingly, section 126 of the Criminal Code does not apply.

heading: Common law principles
paragraph: 237 Every rule and principle of the common law that renders any circumstance a justification or an excuse in relation to a charge for an offence under a relevant provision applies in respect of a violation to the extent that it is not inconsistent with this Act.

heading: Vicarious liability - Canadian maritime document holders
paragraph: 238 (1) The holder of a Canadian maritime document is liable for a violation that is committed in respect of any matter that relates to an activity or a requirement under that document, whether or not the person or vessel that actually committed the violation is identified or proceeded against in accordance with this Act.

heading: Vicarious liability - acts of employees and agents
paragraph: (2) A person or vessel is liable for a violation that is committed by an employee or agent of the person or vessel acting in the course of the employee's employment or within the scope of the agent's authority, whether or not the employee or agent who actually committed the violation is identified or proceeded against in accordance with this Act.

heading: Notations removed
paragraph: 239 (1) Unless the Minister is of the opinion that it is not in the public interest to do so, five years after the last day on which any of the following events occurs the Minister is to remove every notation of violation or default, and every suspension or cancellation of or refusal to issue or renew a Canadian maritime document on prescribed grounds, from any records that the Minister may keep respecting a person or vessel:

heading: Notations removed
paragraph: (a) the person or vessel pays every penalty that the person or vessel is liable to pay after a notice of violation, a notice of default, a determination of a member of the Tribunal on review or a decision of an appeal panel of the Tribunal;

heading: Notations removed
paragraph: (b) a suspension on prescribed grounds of a Canadian maritime document issued to the person or vessel ends;

heading: Notations removed
paragraph: (c) the Minister cancels, on prescribed grounds, a Canadian maritime document issued to the person or vessel; and

heading: Notations removed
paragraph: (d) the Minister refuses, on prescribed grounds, to issue a Canadian maritime document to the person or vessel or to renew a Canadian maritime document issued to the person or vessel.

heading: Duty to notify
paragraph: (2) The Minister is to give a person or vessel notice of a decision not to remove a notation in respect of the person or vessel and providing all relevant information concerning the grounds on which the Minister has refused to remove it.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (3) A notice under subsection (2) must include the address at which, and the date, being thirty days after the notice is served, on or before which, a request for a review may be filed.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (4) The person or vessel may, on or before the date specified in the notice or within any further time that the Tribunal on application allows, file a written request for a review.

heading: Time and place for review
paragraph: (5) On receipt of a request filed under subsection (4), the Tribunal must appoint a time and place for the review and must notify the Minister and the person who, or vessel that, filed the request of the time and place in writing.

heading: Review procedure
paragraph: (6) The member of the Tribunal assigned to conduct the review must provide the Minister and the person who, or vessel that, filed the request with an opportunity consistent with procedural fairness and natural justice to present evidence and make representations.

heading: Determination
paragraph: (7) The member may confirm the Minister's decision or refer the matter back to the Minister for reconsideration.

heading: Right of appeal
paragraph: (8) The person who, or vessel that, requested the review may, within 30 days after the determination, appeal a determination made under subsection (7) to the Tribunal.

heading: Loss of right of appeal
paragraph: (9) If the person or vessel does not appear at the review hearing, the person or vessel is not entitled to appeal a determination unless the person or vessel establishes that there was sufficient reason to justify the absence.

heading: Disposition of appeal
paragraph: (10) The appeal panel assigned to hear the appeal may dismiss the appeal or refer the matter back to the Minister for reconsideration.

heading: Disclosure of notations of violations
paragraph: 240 The Minister shall keep a public record of notations of violations or default kept on any record that the Minister may keep respecting the person or vessel.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 241 No notice of violation may be issued more than two years after the day on which the Minister becomes aware of the contravention.

heading: Certificate of Minister
paragraph: 242 A document that purports to have been issued by the Minister and certifies the day on which the Minister became aware of a violation is evidence, without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the document, that the Minister became aware of the violation on that day.

heading: When compliance agreement in effect
paragraph: 243 If a violation arising out of the contravention of any provision of Part 4, 8 or 9 or the regulations made under those Parts is committed while an agreement or arrangement is in effect between the Minister and the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel that provides that inspections of the vessel to ensure compliance with that provision will be carried out by the authorized representative or a person or an organization acting on their behalf, the penalty or range of penalties fixed under paragraph 244(h) in respect of the violation is doubled.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 244 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Part, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting clearances for departure from a port in Canada;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the investigation of shipping casualties, the alleged contravention of a relevant provision or an incident that involved a vessel and that, in the opinion of the Minister, jeopardized the safety of persons;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the detention of vessels, including the review of detention orders;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the sale of a vessel under section 226, including measures that must be taken before the vessel is sold and the manner of establishing, and the priority of payment of, claims against the vessel;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) designating as a violation that may be proceeded with in accordance with sections 229 to 242 the contravention of a relevant provision, or the contravention of a direction given under a relevant provision, that is an offence under this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) designating violations that, if continued on more than one day, constitute a separate violation for each day on which they are continued;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) designating violations that may be proceeded with by issuing notices of violation and fixing a penalty or a range of penalties in respect of each such violation, up to a maximum of $250,000 but in any event not greater than the maximum fine if the violation were proceeded with by way of summary conviction;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) respecting emergency and safety procedures for the purpose of paragraph 211(4)(d.1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) respecting the service of documents required or authorized to be served under this Part, including the manner of serving them, the proof of their service and the circumstances under which they are deemed to have been served; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) prescribing anything that by this Part is to be prescribed.

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: 245 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a) a direction given under subsection 211(3) (to stop a vessel or proceed as specified);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (a.1) a direction given under subsection 211(3.1) (direction to authorize a vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (b) a direction given under any of paragraphs 211(4)(a) to (e) (to answer reasonable questions, to provide reasonable assistance, to prohibit or limit access to part of a vessel, to operate or cease operating machinery or equipment, to not move a vessel, to muster crew or carry out emergency or safety procedures or to produce documents);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (c) section 215 (proceed to sea with a person without their consent);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (d) subsection 218(1) (disciplining employee);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (e) subsection 222(9) (giving clearance to detained vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (f) subsection 222(10) (moving detained vessel);

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (g) section 223 (wilfully interfering with service of notice); or

heading: Contravention of Act
paragraph: (h) a direction given under subsection 227(1) (not to enter or to leave Canadian waters).

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: 246 (1) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (a) a direction given under subsection 212(2) (to store something);

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (b) section 213 (departing without clearance); and

heading: Contravention of Act or regulations
paragraph: (c) a provision of the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who, or vessel that, commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Goods
paragraph: Definition of carrier

heading: Goods
paragraph: 247 In sections 248 and 250, carrier means a person with whom a shipper of goods enters into a contract of carriage of the goods by water.

heading: Carrier's lien
paragraph: 248 (1) A carrier has, on goods carried under a contract of carriage, a lien for any amount that is due to the carrier under the contract for freight or costs of storing, disposing of or preserving the goods.

heading: Notice of lien to owner of goods
paragraph: (2) Before exercising a lien, a carrier must give notice of it to the owner of the goods, specifying the amount claimed and the particulars of the claim.

heading: Notice of lien to third parties
paragraph: (3) If the carrier places the goods in the custody of a third party and gives the third party notice of the lien and the third party does not retain them until notified by the carrier that the lien is discharged or does not return them to the carrier, the third party is liable to the carrier. The third party may charge the carrier for storing the goods or for any reasonable action taken to preserve them or to protect property or human life from damage they may cause.

heading: Third party's protection
paragraph: (4) A third party who retains goods until notified by the carrier that the lien is discharged or who returns them to the carrier is not liable to the owner of the goods, regardless of whether the lien claimed by the carrier is valid.

heading: Sale or other disposition of goods
paragraph: 249 (1) If an owner of goods does not take delivery of the goods after notice of delivery has been given or fails to discharge a lien after it is exercised, the carrier may

heading: Sale or other disposition of goods
paragraph: (a) sell them by public auction at any time that is 90 days after the notice of delivery is given and 10 days after giving notice of the time and place of the auction in a newspaper that is circulated in the vicinity of the auction; or

heading: Sale or other disposition of goods
paragraph: (b) if the goods are perishable or pose a threat to public health or safety, sell or otherwise dispose of them in the manner and for the price that is reasonable in the circumstances after giving notice of the sale or other disposition to the owner of the goods.

heading: Application of proceeds of disposition
paragraph: (2) The proceeds of the disposition must be credited toward payment of the amounts due or payable under the contract of carriage or any other amounts reasonably incurred for storing, disposing of or preserving the goods. Any surplus must be paid to the owner of the goods.

heading: Responsibility for goods
paragraph: 250 Subject to Part 5 of the Marine Liability Act, carriers must use due care and diligence in the safe-keeping and punctual conveyance of goods delivered to them for carriage by water.

heading: Actions in rem
paragraph: 251 (1) A person who has contracted with the authorized representative or a bare-boat charterer of a vessel in Canada to provide stevedoring may maintain an action in rem in the Federal Court, or any court of competent jurisdiction whose rules provide for in rem procedure in respect of vessels, for a claim in respect of the stevedoring.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) The right of action in rem referred to in subsection (1) may be exercised only while the vessel is chartered to the bare-boat charterer and only if the bare-boat charterer is joined as a defendant.

heading: Does not affect other rights
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, nothing in this section limits the right of a person to maintain an action in rem for stevedoring under Canadian maritime law, within the meaning of subsection 2(1) of the Federal Courts Act.

heading: Does not affect other rights
paragraph: Definition of stevedoring

heading: Does not affect other rights
paragraph: (4) In this section, stevedoring includes trimming, lighterage and the supply of any goods or services in relation to stevedoring.

heading: Proof of offence
paragraph: 252 (1) In a prosecution of a vessel for an offence under this Act, it is sufficient proof that the vessel has committed the offence to establish that the act or omission that constitutes the offence was committed by the master or any person on board, other than a person carrying out an inspection under this Act or a pollution response officer, whether or not the person on board has been identified.

heading: Directions
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of prosecuting a vessel for contravening a direction given under this Act, a direction given to the master, a crew member or any person on board who is, or appears to be, in charge of the vessel, is deemed to have been given to the vessel.

heading: Damage to environment and risk of death or harm to persons
paragraph: 253 (1) Every person is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction on indictment to a fine or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years, or to both, who, in committing an offence under this Act,

heading: Damage to environment and risk of death or harm to persons
paragraph: (a) intentionally or recklessly causes a disaster that results in the loss of life or serious damage to the environment; or

heading: Damage to environment and risk of death or harm to persons
paragraph: (b) shows wanton or reckless disregard for the lives or safety of other persons and thereby causes a risk of death or bodily harm to another person.

heading: Criminal negligence
paragraph: (2) Every person who, in committing an offence under this Act, shows wanton or reckless disregard for the lives or safety of other persons and thereby causes death or bodily harm to another person is subject to prosecution and punishment under section 220 or 221 of the Criminal Code.

heading: Persons
paragraph: 254 (1) No person may be found guilty of an offence under this Act if the person establishes that they exercised due diligence to prevent its commission.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (2) No vessel may be found guilty of an offence under this Act if the person who committed the act or omission that constitutes the offence establishes that they exercised due diligence to prevent its commission.

heading: Court order
paragraph: 255 If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, the court may, in addition to any other punishment it may impose, make an order

heading: Court order
paragraph: (a) if the person is the holder of a Canadian maritime document, prohibiting the person from doing any act or thing authorized by the document at all times while the document is in force or for the period or at the times and places that may be specified in the order; or

heading: Court order
paragraph: (b) prohibiting the person from operating a vessel or providing services essential to the operation of a vessel for the period or at the times and places that may be specified in the order.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 256 (1) Proceedings by way of summary conviction under this Act may be instituted within two years after the day on which the Minister of Transport or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, as the case may be, becomes aware of the subject-matter of the proceedings.

heading: Certificate of Minister
paragraph: (2) A document that purports to have been issued by the Minister referred to in subsection (1), and that certifies the day on which that Minister became aware of the subject-matter of the proceedings, is admissible in evidence without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and is evidence that the Minister became aware of the subject-matter on that day.

heading: Defendant outside Canada
paragraph: (3) If the proceedings cannot be commenced within two years because the proposed defendant is outside Canada, the proceedings may be commenced not later than two months after they arrive in Canada.

heading: Jurisdiction in case of offences
paragraph: 257 (1) For the purpose of giving jurisdiction under this Act, every offence is deemed to have been committed and every cause of complaint to have arisen either in the place where the offence actually was committed or arose, or in any place where the offender or person or vessel complained against may be.

heading: Presumption of jurisdiction
paragraph: (2) If, in a legal proceeding under this Act, a question arises as to whether a vessel or person is within any of the provisions of this Act or the regulations, the vessel or person is deemed to be within those provisions unless the contrary is proved.

heading: Jurisdiction over vessels lying off coasts
paragraph: 258 (1) If a district within which a court, justice of the peace or provincial court judge has jurisdiction either under this Act or under any other Act or at common law, for any purpose whatever, is situated on the coast of a sea, or abuts on or projects into navigable waters, the court, justice or provincial court judge has jurisdiction over any vessel on, or lying or passing off, that coast or in or near those navigable waters, and over all persons on board, in the same manner as if the vessel or persons were within the limits of the original jurisdiction of the court, justice or provincial court judge.

heading: Added power of courts
paragraph: (2) The jurisdiction under this section is in addition to and not in derogation of any jurisdiction or power of a court under the Criminal Code.

heading: Power to detain foreign vessel that has caused damage
paragraph: 259 If the Federal Court is satisfied that damage or loss has in any part of the world been caused to property that belongs to Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province or to a qualified person by the fault, in whole or in part, of a foreign vessel that is at the time of the application in Canadian waters, on ex parte application the Federal Court may issue an order requiring any person named by the Court to detain the vessel until the applicant has been compensated for the damage or loss or until security, in the form and amount approved by the Court, is deposited with the Court.

heading: Defence available in certain cases
paragraph: 260 It is a defence in proceedings under this Act for contravening a direction that the vessel to which or person to whom the direction was given

heading: Defence available in certain cases
paragraph: (a) believed on reasonable grounds that complying with the direction would have imperilled life, the environment or any vessel or property; and

heading: Defence available in certain cases
paragraph: (b) notified the person who gave the direction, as soon as feasible, of the contravention and of the reasons for it.

heading: Depositions received when witness cannot be produced
paragraph: 261 (1) A deposition of a witness is admissible in evidence in the course of a proceeding under this Act if

heading: Depositions received when witness cannot be produced
paragraph: (a) the testimony of the witness is required in relation to the subject-matter of the proceeding and the witness cannot be found in Canada;

heading: Depositions received when witness cannot be produced
paragraph: (b) the deposition was made on oath outside Canada in relation to the same subject-matter before a justice or magistrate of another state or before a diplomatic or consular officer of Canada or a person recognized by Her Majesty in right of Canada as a diplomatic or consular officer of another state, and the deposition is signed by the justice, magistrate or officer; and

heading: Depositions received when witness cannot be produced
paragraph: (c) in the case of a criminal proceeding, the deposition was made in the presence of the person accused and that fact is certified by the justice, magistrate or officer.

heading: Certificate as evidence
paragraph: (2) It is not necessary in any case to prove the signature or official character of the person who appears to have signed the deposition, and in a criminal proceeding a certificate under this section is, unless the contrary is proved, sufficient evidence that the deposition was made in the presence of the person accused.

heading: Certified copies
paragraph: (3) A copy of the deposition or an extract from one is admissible in evidence if it purports to be signed and certified as a true copy or extract by the justice, magistrate or officer.

heading: Examination of persons before trial
paragraph: 262 (1) A crew member who is likely to be obliged to leave the province in which an offence under this Act is prosecuted, or a witness who is sick, infirm or about to leave the province, may be examined before a commissioner for oaths or other proper authority in the same manner that a deposition is taken in a civil case.

heading: Use of examination
paragraph: (2) An examination under subsection (1) may be used at the trial or proceeding in respect of which it was taken if the crew member or witness is unable to attend or cannot be produced.

heading: No stay of proceedings without order
paragraph: 263 The proceedings on a conviction or an order may not be stayed by reason of an application to remove the conviction or order to a superior court or of a notice of such an application unless the court or judge to whom the application is made or is to be made orders a stay of proceedings on special cause being shown.

heading: Jurisdiction
paragraph: 264 If there is no judge having jurisdiction in respect of writs of certiorari resident at or near the place where a conviction or an order is made, in Ontario, a judge of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, in Nova Scotia, British Columbia and Prince Edward Island, a judge of the Supreme Court, in Newfoundland and Labrador, a judge of the Trial Division of the Supreme Court, or, in New Brunswick, Manitoba, Saskatchewan or Alberta, a judge of the Court of Queen's Bench has power to hear and determine an application for a stay of proceedings on the conviction or order.

heading: Documents admissible in evidence
paragraph: 265 (1) A document made, given or issued under this Act and appearing to be signed by the Minister of Transport, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, the Chief Registrar or a registrar, a marine safety inspector, the Chair of the Marine Technical Review Board, a marine communications and traffic services officer, a person exercising powers under subsection 135(2), a pleasure craft safety inspector or an enforcement officer is admissible in evidence and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the statements contained in the document without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the document.

heading: Copies or extracts
paragraph: (2) A copy of or an extract from any record or other document that is made, given or issued under this Act by a person referred to in subsection (1) and that appears to have been certified under the signature of that person as a true copy or extract is admissible in evidence without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed it and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, has the same probative force as the original would have if it were proved in the ordinary way.

heading: Admissibility of documents in evidence
paragraph: 266 A document that this Act declares to be admissible in evidence is, on its production from the proper custody, admissible in evidence in any court or before any person having by law or consent of the parties authority to receive evidence, and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, is proof of the matters stated in the document without proof of the signature or the official character of the person appearing to have signed it.

heading: Document entries as proof
paragraph: 267 In an action or proceeding under this Act, an entry in a record required under this Act to be kept is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, proof of the matters stated as against the person who made the entry or was required to keep the record or, if the record was kept in respect of a vessel, against the authorized representative or master.

heading: Paid to Receiver General
paragraph: 268 (1) Subject to subsection (2), all fines imposed under this Act must, despite any other Act, be paid to the Receiver General and deposited to the credit of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

heading: Application of fines
paragraph: (2) A court, justice of the peace or provincial court judge who imposes a fine under this Act may direct that the whole or a portion of it may

heading: Application of fines
paragraph: (a) be applied in compensating a person for any wrong or damage that may have been caused by the act or default in respect of which the fine was imposed;

heading: Application of fines
paragraph: (b) be applied in or toward payment of the expenses of the proceedings; or

heading: Application of fines
paragraph: (c) be paid to the provincial, municipal or local authority bearing in whole or in part the expense of prosecuting the contravention of this Act in respect of which the fine was imposed.

heading: Crown not relieved
paragraph: 268.1 Subsections 11(5) and 12(5), section 45, paragraph 181.1(a) and subsection 195(3) do not, by reason of section 10 of the Crown Liability and Proceedings Act, relieve the Crown of liability in respect of a tort or extracontractual civil liability to which the Crown would otherwise be subject.

heading: Prohibition of shipment of articles of war
paragraph: 269 (1) No person shall, during a prescribed period,

heading: Prohibition of shipment of articles of war
paragraph: (a) discharge from a Canadian vessel a prescribed article in any prescribed territory or within the territorial waters adjacent to the territory;

heading: Prohibition of shipment of articles of war
paragraph: (b) tranship in Canadian waters, in the exclusive economic zone of Canada or on the high seas such an article from a Canadian vessel to any vessel bound for such a territory;

heading: Prohibition of shipment of articles of war
paragraph: (c) take on board or carry on a Canadian vessel such an article consigned to or destined for a place in such a territory; or

heading: Prohibition of shipment of articles of war
paragraph: (d) take on board or carry on any other vessel in Canadian waters such an article consigned to or destined for a place in such a territory.

heading: Powers if contravention suspected
paragraph: (2) Any person, or member of a class of persons, designated by the Minister of Transport or the Minister of National Defence for the purposes of this section, who has reason to suspect that a vessel is contravening or has contravened subsection (1) may

heading: Powers if contravention suspected
paragraph: (a) direct the master to stop the vessel or proceed to the place that the person may select, and to moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that the person may specify;

heading: Powers if contravention suspected
paragraph: (b) board the vessel;

heading: Powers if contravention suspected
paragraph: (c) direct the master to produce any documents relating to any cargo that is being carried or has been carried on the vessel;

heading: Powers if contravention suspected
paragraph: (d) search the vessel, examine the cargo and direct the master or a member of the crew to open any package or parcel that the person suspects contains articles prescribed for the purposes of subsection (1); and

heading: Powers if contravention suspected
paragraph: (e) make any other examination or inquiry that the person considers necessary to determine whether subsection (1) is being or has been contravened.

heading: Power to take vessel
paragraph: (3) If the person has reasonable grounds to believe that subsection (1) is being or has been contravened, the person may take the vessel to the nearest or most convenient port in order that the alleged contravention may be adjudicated by a court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (4) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Transport, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing any territory in which there is a state of war or armed conflict;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing anything else that may be prescribed under this section;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) exempting, in the case of any territory prescribed under paragraph (a), an article or class of articles from the application of this section; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this section.

heading: Contraventions
paragraph: (5) Every person who contravenes subsection (1) or a direction made under paragraph (2)(a) or (c) commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Authorized representative or master
paragraph: (6) If a person on a vessel commits an offence under this section and the authorized representative or master authorized or acquiesced in the offence, the authorized representative or master is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to the penalty provided for by this Act in respect of the offence committed by the person whether or not the person has been prosecuted.

heading: Decisions that cease to have effect
paragraph: 270 Decisions of the Board of Steamship Inspection that were made under the Canada Shipping Act, chapter S-9 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, cease to have effect five years after section 26 comes into force.

heading: Acquired rights - registered vessels
paragraph: 271 (1) Every vessel registered in Canada when Part 2 comes into force is deemed to be registered under that Part until its ownership changes.

heading: Grace period
paragraph: (3) A vessel that was not required to be registered under the Canada Shipping Act, chapter S-9 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, and that is required by subsection 46(1) to be registered under Part 2 has two years after that Part comes into force to comply with that requirement.

heading: Acquired rights - licensed vessels
paragraph: 272 Every vessel, other than a pleasure craft, licensed under section 108 of the Canada Shipping Act, chapter S-9 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, when Part 2 comes into force is deemed to be registered in the small vessel register referred to in subsection 43(1) until

heading: Acquired rights - licensed vessels
paragraph: (a) the earlier of the date the vessel's ownership changes and five years after Part 2 comes into force; or

heading: Acquired rights - licensed vessels
paragraph: (b) in the case of a vessel that was issued a licence under that Act, the expiry date of the licence.

heading: Certificates remain in force
paragraph: 273 Subject to the provisions of this Act or the regulations respecting the suspension or cancellation of Canadian maritime documents, certificates issued under Part II, III or V of the Canada Shipping Act, chapter S-9 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, remain in force for the purpose for which they were issued.

heading: Validity periods of certificates
paragraph: (3) Any certificate's period of validity that is provided for in a regulation referred to in subsection (1) is deemed to have been specified by the Minister under subsection 17(1).

heading: Canadian ships
paragraph: (4) Every reference to "Canadian ship" or "Canadian ships" in the regulations referred to in subsection (1) shall be read as a reference to "Canadian vessel" or "Canadian vessels", respectively.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (6) Every person who, or vessel that, contravenes a regulation that is in force under subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 18 months, or to both.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Canada Water Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 (1) In this Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: agency means a water quality management agency the incorporation of which is procured or that is named pursuant to section 11 or 13; (organisme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: analyst means an analyst designated pursuant to subsection 25(1); (analyste)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: boundary waters means the waters from main shore to main shore of the lakes and rivers and connecting waterways, or the portions thereof, along which the international boundary between the United States and Canada passes, including all bays, arms, and inlets thereof, but not including tributary waters which in their natural channels would flow into such lakes, rivers, and waterways, or waters flowing from such lakes, rivers, and waterways, or the waters of rivers flowing across the boundary; (eaux limitrophes)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal agency means a water quality management agency that is named pursuant to section 13; (organisme federal)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal waters means - other than in Yukon and the Northwest Territories - waters under the exclusive legislative jurisdiction of Parliament and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in Yukon, waters in a federal conservation area as defined in section 2 of the Yukon Act, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in the Northwest Territories, waters other than those in respect of which the Legislature of the Northwest Territories may make laws under paragraph 18(1)(n) of the Northwest Territories Act; (eaux federales)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inspector means an inspector designated pursuant to subsection 25(1); (inspecteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inter-jurisdictional waters means any waters, whether international, boundary or otherwise, that, whether wholly situated in a province or not, significantly affect the quantity or quality of waters outside the province; (eaux relevant de plusieurs juridictions)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: international waters means waters of rivers that flow across the international boundary between the United States and Canada; (eaux internationales)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed means prescribed by regulation; (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: waste means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any substance that, if added to any water, would degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of that water to an extent that is detrimental to their use by man or by any animal, fish or plant that is useful to man, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any water that contains a substance in such a quantity or concentration, or that has been so treated, processed or changed, by heat or other means, from a natural state that it would, if added to any other water, degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of that water to the extent described in paragraph (a); (dechet)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: water quality management means any aspect of water resource management that relates to restoring, maintaining or improving the quality of water; (gestion qualitative des eaux)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: water resource management means the conservation, development and utilization of water resources and includes, with respect thereto, research, data collection and the maintaining of inventories, planning and the implementation of plans, and the control and regulation of water quantity and quality. (gestion des ressources en eau)

heading: Prescribed substances and certain water deemed waste
paragraph: (2) Without limiting the generality of the definition waste in this Act,

heading: Prescribed substances and certain water deemed waste
paragraph: (a) any substance or any substance that is part of a class of substances prescribed pursuant to subparagraph 18(1)(a)(i),

heading: Prescribed substances and certain water deemed waste
paragraph: (b) any water that contains any substance or any substance that is part of a class of substances in a quantity or concentration that is equal to or in excess of a quantity or concentration prescribed in respect of that substance or class of substances pursuant to subparagraph 18(1)(a)(ii), and

heading: Prescribed substances and certain water deemed waste
paragraph: (c) any water that has been subjected to a treatment, process or change prescribed pursuant to subparagraph 18(1)(a)(iii),

heading: Prescribed substances and certain water deemed waste
paragraph: shall, for the purposes of this Act, be deemed to be waste.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 3 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Establishment of intergovernmental committees, etc.
paragraph: 4 For the purpose of facilitating the formulation of policies and programs with respect to the water resources of Canada and to ensure the optimum use of those resources for the benefit of all Canadians, having regard to the distinctive geography of Canada and the character of water as a natural resource, the Minister may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, enter into an arrangement with one or more provincial governments to establish, on a national, provincial, regional, lake or river-basin basis, intergovernmental committees or other bodies

heading: Establishment of intergovernmental committees, etc.
paragraph: (a) to maintain continuing consultation on water resource matters and to advise on priorities for research, planning, conservation, development and utilization relating thereto;

heading: Establishment of intergovernmental committees, etc.
paragraph: (b) to advise on the formulation of water policies and programs; and

heading: Establishment of intergovernmental committees, etc.
paragraph: (c) to facilitate the coordination and implementation of water policies and programs.

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: 5 Subject to this Act, the Minister may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, with respect to any waters where there is a significant national interest in the water resource management thereof, enter into agreements with one or more provincial governments having an interest in the water resource management of those waters, providing for programs to

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: (a) establish and maintain an inventory of those waters,

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: (b) collect, process and provide data on the quality, quantity, distribution and use of those waters,

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: (c) conduct research in connection with any aspect of those waters or provide for the conduct of any such research by or in cooperation with any government, institution or person,

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: (d) formulate comprehensive water resource management plans, including detailed estimates of the cost of implementation of those plans and of revenues and other benefits likely to be realized from the implementation thereof, based on an examination of the full range of reasonable alternatives and taking into account views expressed at public hearings and otherwise by persons likely to be affected by implementation of the plans,

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: (e) design projects for the efficient conservation, development and utilization of those waters, and

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: (f) implement any plans or projects referred to in paragraphs (d) and (e),

heading: Federal-provincial water resource management programs
paragraph: and establishing or naming joint commissions, boards or other bodies empowered to direct, supervise and coordinate those programs.

heading: Federal water resource management programs
paragraph: 6 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Minister shall, with the approval of the Governor in Council, undertake directly,

heading: Federal water resource management programs
paragraph: (a) with respect to any federal waters, any program described in any of paragraphs 5(a) to (e) and the implementation of any program described in paragraph 5(d) or (e);

heading: Federal water resource management programs
paragraph: (b) with respect to any inter-jurisdictional waters where there is a significant national interest in the water resource management thereof, any program described in paragraph 5(d) or (e); and

heading: Federal water resource management programs
paragraph: (c) with respect to any international or boundary waters where there is a significant national interest in the water resource management thereof, any program described in paragraph 5(d) or (e) and the implementation of any such program.

heading: Condition to approval of federal programs
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council shall not approve the undertaking by the Minister of any program pursuant to paragraph (1)(b) or (c) unless the Governor in Council is satisfied that all reasonable efforts have been made by the Minister to reach an agreement under section 5 with the one or more provincial governments having an interest in the water resource management of the waters in question and that those efforts have failed.

heading: Minister to consider priorities
paragraph: (3) In undertaking any programs pursuant to subsection (1), the Minister shall take into account any priorities for development recommended pursuant to paragraph 4(a).

heading: Research, data collection and inventory establishment
paragraph: 7 The Minister may conduct research, collect data and establish inventories respecting any aspect of water resource management or the management of any specific water resources or provide for the conduct of any such research, data collection or inventory establishment by or in cooperation with any government, institution or person.

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: 8 (1) Where, pursuant to section 5, the Minister enters into an agreement with one or more provincial governments, the agreement shall, where applicable, in respect of each program that is the subject of the agreement, specify

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (a) the respective parts of the program to be undertaken by the Minister and the provincial government or governments and the times at which and the manner in which those parts of the program are to be carried out;

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (b) the proportions of the cost of the respective parts of the program that are to be paid by the Minister and the provincial government or governments and the times at which amounts representing those proportions are to be paid;

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (c) the labour, land and materials that are to be supplied in relation to the respective parts of the program by the Minister and the provincial government or governments;

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (d) the proportions in which any compensation awarded or agreed to be paid to any body or person suffering loss as a result of the program is to be paid by the Minister and the provincial government or governments;

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (e) the amount of any loan or grant, constituting part or all of the cost of the program to be paid by the Minister, that is to be made or paid by the Minister to the provincial government or governments, and the manner in which the terms and conditions of the loan or grant are to be determined;

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (f) the authority or authorities, whether an agent or agents of Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province or otherwise as may be agreed to be appropriate, that will be responsible for the undertaking, operation or maintenance of projects that form part of the program;

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (g) the respective proportions of the revenues from the program that are to be paid to the Minister and the provincial government or governments; and

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
paragraph: (h) the terms and conditions relating to the undertaking, operation and maintenance of the program.

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (2) An agreement entered into pursuant to section 5 shall, where applicable, in respect of the joint commission, board or other body thereby established or named, provide for

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (a) the constitution thereof, the members thereof that are to be appointed by the Minister and the provincial government or governments that are parties to the agreement and the terms and conditions of the appointments;

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (b) the staff thereof that is to be supplied by the Minister and the provincial government or governments;

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (c) the duties of the body and the powers that it may exercise in directing, supervising and coordinating the program;

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (d) the keeping of accounts and records by the body;

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (e) the annual submission by the body to the Minister and the provincial government or governments of operating and capital budgets in connection with the programs directed, supervised and coordinated by the body for the next following fiscal year for approval by the Governor in Council and such persons on behalf of the provincial government or governments as are designated in the agreement; and

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (f) the submission by the body to the Minister and the provincial government or governments, within three months after the termination of each fiscal year, of an annual report containing such information as is specified in the agreement.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 9 Except in quantities and under conditions prescribed with respect to waste disposal in the water quality management area in question, including the payment of any effluent discharge fee prescribed therefor, no person shall deposit or permit the deposit of waste of any type in any waters composing a water quality management area designated pursuant to section 11 or 13, or in any place under any conditions where the waste or any other waste that results from the deposit of the waste may enter any such waters.

heading: Application of section 9
paragraph: 10 Section 9 is not applicable in respect of a water quality management area designated pursuant to section 11 or 13 until a proclamation has been issued declaring it to be applicable in respect of that area.

heading: Federal-provincial agreements
paragraph: 11 (1) The Minister may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, enter into agreements with one or more provincial governments that have an interest in the water quality management of

heading: Federal-provincial agreements
paragraph: (a) any federal waters; or

heading: Federal-provincial agreements
paragraph: (b) any waters, other than federal waters, the water quality management of which has become a matter of urgent national concern.

heading: Object of agreements
paragraph: (2) An agreement referred to in subsection (1) shall

heading: Object of agreements
paragraph: (a) designate the waters to which the agreement relates as a water quality management area;

heading: Object of agreements
paragraph: (b) provide for water quality management programs in respect of those waters; and

heading: Object of agreements
paragraph: (c) authorize the Minister, jointly with such one or more provincial governments, to procure the incorporation of a corporation without share capital, or to name an existing corporation that is an agent of Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province or that performs any function or duty on behalf of the Government of Canada or the government of a province, as a water quality management agency to plan, initiate and carry out, in conjunction with the Minister and the provincial government or governments referred to in subsection (1), programs described in section 15 in respect of the waters described in that subsection.

heading: Matters to be specified in agreements
