paragraph: 13.03 (1) For the purposes of subsections 13(2) to (4) and 13.01(2) to (4), a conviction for a particular offence under this Act is deemed to be a conviction for a second or subsequent offence if the court is satisfied that the offender has been previously convicted - under any Act of Parliament, or any Act of the legislature of a province, that relates to environmental or wildlife conservation or protection - of a substantially similar offence.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only to previous convictions on indictment and to previous convictions on summary conviction, and to previous convictions under any similar procedure under any Act of the legislature of a province.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: 13.04 If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act and the court is satisfied that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any property, benefit or advantage, the court shall order the person to pay an additional fine in an amount equal to the court's estimation of the value of that property, benefit or advantage. The additional fine may exceed the maximum amount of any fine that may otherwise be imposed under this Act.

heading: Notice to shareholders
paragraph: 13.05 If a corporation that has shareholders is convicted of an offence under this Act, the court shall make an order directing the corporation to notify its shareholders, in the manner and within the time directed by the court, of the facts relating to the commission of the offence and of the details of the punishment imposed.

heading: Liability of directors and officers, etc., of corporation
paragraph: 13.06 If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, any director, officer, agent or mandatary of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the penalty provided for by this Act for an individual in respect of the offence committed by the corporation, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Directors' duties
paragraph: 13.07 Every director and officer of a corporation shall take all reasonable care to ensure that the corporation complies with the provisions of this Act and the regulations and obligations and prohibitions arising from this Act or the regulations.

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: 13.08 The fundamental purpose of sentencing for offences under this Act is to contribute, in light of the significant and many threats to wildlife and the importance of wildlife to the well-being of Canadians, to respect for the law protecting wildlife through the imposition of just sanctions that have as their objectives

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: (a) to deter the offender and any other person from committing offences under this Act;

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: (b) to denounce unlawful conduct that damages or creates a risk of damage to wildlife; and

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: (c) to recover wildlife and restore wildlife habitat.

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: 13.09 (1) In addition to the principles and factors that the court is otherwise required to consider, including those set out in sections 718.1 to 718.21 of the Criminal Code, the court shall consider the following principles when sentencing a person who is convicted of an offence under this Act:

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (a) the amount of the fine should be increased to account for every aggravating factor associated with the offence, including the aggravating factors set out in subsection (2); and

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (b) the amount of the fine should reflect the gravity of each aggravating factor associated with the offence.

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (2) The aggravating factors are the following:

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (a) the offence caused damage or risk of damage to wildlife or wildlife habitat;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (b) the offence caused damage or risk of damage to any unique, rare, particularly important or vulnerable wildlife or wildlife habitat;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (c) the damage caused by the offence is extensive, persistent or irreparable;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (d) the offender committed the offence intentionally or recklessly;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (e) the offender failed to take reasonable steps to prevent the commission of the offence despite having the financial means to do so;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (f) by committing the offence or failing to take action to prevent its commission, the offender increased revenue or decreased costs or intended to increase revenue or decrease costs;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (g) the offender committed the offence despite having been warned by a wildlife officer of the circumstances that subsequently became the subject of the offence;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (h) the offender has a history of non-compliance with federal or provincial legislation that relates to environmental or wildlife conservation or protection; and

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) after the commission of the offence, the offender

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) attempted to conceal its commission,

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (ii) failed to take prompt action to prevent, mitigate or remediate its effects, or

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (iii) failed to take prompt action to reduce the risk of committing similar offences in the future.

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: (3) The absence of an aggravating factor set out in subsection (2) is not a mitigating factor.

heading: Meaning of damage
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of paragraphs (2)(a) to (c), damage includes loss of use value and non-use value.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (5) If the court is satisfied of the existence of one or more of the aggravating factors set out in subsection (2) but decides not to increase the amount of the fine because of that factor, the court shall give reasons for that decision.

heading: Documents admissible in evidence
paragraph: 13.091 (1) A document made, given or issued under this Act and appearing to be signed by an analyst is admissible in evidence and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the statements contained in the document without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the document.

heading: Attendance of analyst
paragraph: (2) The party against whom the document is produced may, with leave of the court, require the attendance of the analyst who signed it.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) No document referred to in subsection (1) may be received in evidence unless the party intending to produce it has given to the party against whom it is intended to be produced reasonable notice of that intention together with a copy of the document.

heading: Proof of offence
paragraph: 13.1 In any prosecution of an offence under this Act, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by an employee, agent or mandatary of the accused, whether or not the employee, agent or mandatary is identified or prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph: 13.11 A person who commits or continues an offence under this Act on more than one day is liable to be convicted for a separate offence for each day on which the offence is committed or continued.

heading: Offences involving more than one animal, plant or other organism
paragraph: 13.12 If an offence under this Act involves more than one animal, plant or other organism, the fine to be imposed in respect of that offence may, despite sections 13 and 13.01, be the total of the fines that would have been imposed if each of the animals, plants or other organisms had been the subject of a separate information.

heading: Application of fines
paragraph: 13.13 (1) All fines received by the Receiver General in respect of the commission of an offence under this Act, other than fines collected under the Contraventions Act, are to be credited to the Environmental Damages Fund, an account in the accounts of Canada, and used for purposes related to protecting, conserving or restoring the environment or for administering that Fund.

heading: Recommendations of court
paragraph: (2) The court imposing the fine may recommend to the Minister that all or a portion of the fine credited to the Environmental Damages Fund be paid to a person or an organization specified by the court for a purpose referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: 14 (1) Where a person is convicted of an offence, the convicting court may, in addition to any punishment imposed, order that any seized thing by means of or in relation to which the offence was committed, or any proceeds of its disposition, be forfeited to Her Majesty.

heading: Return where no forfeiture ordered
paragraph: (2) Where the convicting court does not order the forfeiture, the seized thing, or the proceeds of its disposition, must be returned to its lawful owner or the person lawfully entitled to it.

heading: Retention or sale
paragraph: 15 Where a fine is imposed on a person convicted of an offence, any seized thing, or any proceeds of its disposition, may be retained until the fine is paid or the thing may be sold in satisfaction of the fine and the proceeds applied, in whole or in part, in payment of the fine.

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: 16 Where a person is convicted of an offence, the court may, in addition to any punishment imposed and having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that could, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (b) directing the person to take any action that the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to any wildlife that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (b.1) directing the person to carry out environmental effects monitoring in the manner established by the Minister, or directing the person to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount for the purpose of environmental effects monitoring;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (b.2) directing the person to implement an environmental management system that meets a recognized Canadian or international standard specified by the court;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (b.3) directing the person to pay to Her Majesty in right of Canada an amount of money that the court considers appropriate for the purpose of promoting the proper management of wildlife or the conservation or protection of wildlife;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (c) directing the person to publish, in the manner specified by the court, the facts relating to the commission of the offence and the details of the punishment imposed, including any orders made under this subsection;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (c.1) directing the person to notify, at the person's own cost and in the manner specified by the court, any person aggrieved or affected by the person's conduct of the facts relating to the commission of the offence and of the details of the punishment imposed, including any orders made under this subsection;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (d) directing the person to compensate any person, monetarily or otherwise, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken, caused to be taken or to be taken as a result of the act or omission that constituted the offence, including costs of assessing appropriate remedial or preventive action;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (d.1) directing the person to pay, in a manner specified by the court, an amount to enable research to be conducted into the protection or conservation of the wildlife or the wildlife habitat in respect of which the offence was committed;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (d.2) directing the person to pay, in the manner prescribed by the court, an amount to an educational institution including for scholarships for students enrolled in studies related to the environment;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (d.3) directing the person to pay, in the manner prescribed by the court, an amount to environmental or other groups to assist in their work in or for the community where the offence was committed;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (e) directing the person to perform community service in accordance with any reasonable conditions that may be specified in the order;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (f) directing the person to submit to the Minister, on application to the court by the Minister within three years after the conviction, any information respecting the activities of the person that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (g) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances for securing the person's good conduct and for deterring the person and any other persons from committing offences under this Act;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (h) directing the person to post a bond or provide a suretyship or pay into court an amount of money that the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (i) requiring the person to surrender to the Minister any permit or other authorization issued under this Act to the person; and

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (j) prohibiting the person from applying for any new permit or other authorization under this Act during any period that the court considers appropriate.

heading: Coming into force and duration of order
paragraph: 16.1 An order made under section 16 comes into force on the day on which it is made or on any other day that the court may determine and shall not continue in force for more than three years after that day unless the court provides otherwise in the order.

heading: Publication
paragraph: 16.2 If a person fails to comply with an order made under paragraph 16(c), the Minister may, in the manner that the court directed the person to do so, publish the facts relating to the commission of the offence and the details of the punishment imposed and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: 16.3 If the court makes an order under paragraph 16(b.3) or (d) directing a person to pay an amount to Her Majesty in right of Canada, or if the Minister incurs publication costs under section 16.2, the amount or the costs, as the case may be, constitute a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Enforcement
paragraph: 16.4 If the court makes an order under paragraph 16(d) directing a person to pay an amount to another person, other than to Her Majesty in right of Canada, and the amount is not paid without delay, that other person may, by filing the order, enter as a judgment, in the superior court of the province in which the trial was held, the amount ordered to be paid, and that judgment is enforceable against the person who was directed to pay the amount in the same manner as if it were a judgment rendered against the offender in that court in civil proceedings.

heading: Cancellation or suspension of permits, etc.
paragraph: 16.5 If the court makes an order under paragraph 16(i), any permit or other authorization to which the order relates is cancelled unless the court makes an order suspending it for any period that the court considers appropriate.

heading: Suspended sentence
paragraph: 17 (1) Where a person is convicted of an offence and the court suspends the passing of sentence pursuant to paragraph 731(1)(a) of the Criminal Code, the court may, in addition to any probation order made under that paragraph, make an order containing one or more of the prohibitions, directions or requirements mentioned in section 16.

heading: Imposition of sentence
paragraph: (2) Where the person does not comply with the order or is convicted of another offence, within three years after the order was made, the court may, on the application of the prosecution, impose any sentence that could have been imposed if the passing of sentence had not been suspended.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 18 No proceedings by way of summary conviction in respect of an offence under this Act may be instituted more than five years after the day on which the subject matter of the proceedings arose, unless the prosecutor and the defendant agree that they may be instituted after the five years.

heading: Publication of information about contraventions
paragraph: 18.1 (1) For the purpose of encouraging compliance with this Act and the regulations, the Minister shall maintain, in a registry accessible to the public, information about all convictions of corporations for offences under this Act.

heading: Retention
paragraph: (2) Information in the registry is to be maintained for a minimum of five years.

heading: Minister may refuse or suspend permit, etc.
paragraph: 18.2 The Minister may refuse to issue a permit or other authorization under this Act, or may amend, suspend or cancel such a permit or other authorization, if the applicant or the holder has been convicted of an offence under this Act.

heading: Contraventions Act
paragraph: 18.3 If an offence under this Act is designated as a contravention under the Contraventions Act, subsection 8(5) of that Act does not apply in respect of the fine that may be established for that contravention.

heading: Review
paragraph: 18.4 (1) The Minister shall, 10 years after the day on which this section comes into force and every 10 years after that, undertake a review of sections 13 to 18.3.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall, no later than one year after the day on which the review is undertaken, cause a report on the review to be tabled in each House of Parliament.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: 19 (1) In addition to the procedures set out in the Criminal Code for commencing a proceeding, proceedings in respect of any offence prescribed by the regulations may be commenced by a wildlife officer

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (a) completing a ticket that consists of a summons portion and an information portion;

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (b) delivering the summons portion to the accused or mailing it to the accused at the accused's latest known address; and

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (c) filing the information portion with a court of competent jurisdiction before the summons portion has been delivered or mailed or as soon as is practicable afterward.

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (2) The summons and information portions of the ticket must

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (a) set out a description of the offence and the time and place of its alleged commission;

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (b) include a statement, signed by the wildlife officer who completes the ticket, that the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the accused committed the offence;

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (c) set out the amount of the fine prescribed by the regulations for the offence and the manner in which and period within which it may be paid;

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (d) include a statement that if the accused pays the fine within the period set out in the ticket, a conviction will be entered and recorded against the accused; and

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (e) include a statement that if the accused wishes to plead not guilty or for any other reason fails to pay the fine within the period set out in the ticket, the accused must appear in the court on the day and at the time set out in the ticket.

heading: Notice of forfeiture
paragraph: (3) Where a thing is seized under this Act and proceedings relating to it are commenced by way of the ticketing procedure, the wildlife officer who completes the ticket shall give written notice to the accused that, if the accused pays the fine prescribed by the regulations within the period set out in the ticket, the thing, or any proceeds of its disposition, will be immediately forfeited to Her Majesty.

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (4) Where an accused to whom the summons portion of a ticket is delivered or mailed pays the prescribed fine within the period set out in the ticket,

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (a) the payment constitutes a plea of guilty to the offence and a conviction must be entered against the accused and no further action may be taken against the accused in respect of that offence; and

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (b) notwithstanding section 11.3, any thing seized from the accused under this Act that relates to the offence, or any proceeds of its disposition, are forfeited to

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (i) Her Majesty in right of Canada, if the thing was seized by a wildlife officer employed in the federal public administration, or

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (ii) Her Majesty in right of a province, if the thing was seized by a wildlife officer employed by the government of that province.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (5) The Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) offences in respect of which this section applies and the manner in which the offences are to be described in tickets; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) the amount of the fine for a prescribed offence, but the amount may not exceed $1,000.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Canadian Energy Regulator Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 The following definitions apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: abandoned facility means an abandoned pipeline or an abandoned offshore facility. (installation abandonnee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: abandoned offshore facility means any facility, equipment, system or offshore power line that has been abandoned in accordance with an authorization issued under Part 5. (installation extracotiere abandonnee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: abandoned pipeline means a pipeline the operation of which has been abandoned in accordance with an order under subsection 241(1) and that remains in place. (pipeline abandonne)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Chief Executive Officer means the Chief Executive Officer appointed under subsection 21(1). (president-directeur general)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: company includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person having authority under a Special Act to construct or operate a pipeline; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a body corporate incorporated or continued under the Canada Business Corporations Act or an Act of the legislature of a province and not discontinued under the Act in question. (compagnie)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: designated officer means an employee of the Regulator designated under section 24. (responsable designe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: export means, in relation to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) electricity, to send from a place in Canada by a line of wire or other conductor electricity produced in Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) oil,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) to export within the meaning of any provision of the Energy Administration Act that defines export for the purposes of any charge imposed under that Act in relation to fuel for use by an aircraft or a vessel,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) to send or take, by any means, from a place in Canada, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii) to send or take, by any means, to a place outside Canada from any area of land, not within a province, that belongs to Her Majesty in right of Canada or in respect of which Her Majesty in right of Canada has the right to dispose of or exploit the natural resources and that is situated in submarine areas in the internal waters of Canada, the territorial sea of Canada or the continental shelf of Canada; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) gas, to effect any one of the operations referred to in subparagraph (b)(ii) or (iii). (exportation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: gas means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any hydrocarbon or mixture of hydrocarbons that, at a temperature of 15°C and a pressure of 101.325 kPa, is in a gaseous state; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any substance designated as a gas product by regulations made under section 390. (gaz)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ground disturbance means a ground disturbance other than one that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is caused by any activity that is specified in the orders or regulations made in respect of pipelines under section 335 or made in respect of international or interprovincial power lines under section 275;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is, in relation to a pipeline, caused by cultivation to a depth of less than 45 cm below the surface of the ground; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is, in relation to a pipeline, caused by any other activity to a depth of less than 30 cm and that does not result in a reduction of the earth cover over the pipeline to a depth that is less than the cover provided when the pipeline was constructed. (remuement du sol)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hydrocarbon means a hydrocarbon other than coal. (hydrocarbure)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: import means, in relation to gas or oil, to bring into Canada through pipelines, by railway tank car, by tank truck or by tanker. (importation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous governing body means a council, government or other entity that is authorized to act on behalf of an Indigenous group, community or people that holds rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982. (corps dirigeant autochtone)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous knowledge means the Indigenous knowledge of the Indigenous peoples of Canada. (connaissances autochtones)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous organization means an Indigenous governing body or any other entity that represents the interests of an Indigenous group and its members. (organisation autochtone)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous peoples of Canada has the meaning assigned by the definition aboriginal peoples of Canada in subsection 35(2) of the Constitution Act, 1982. (peuples autochtones du Canada)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inspection officer means a person designated under subsection 102(1). (inspecteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: international power line means facilities that are constructed or operated for the purpose of transmitting electricity from a place in Canada to a place outside Canada or from a place outside Canada to a place in Canada. It does not however include an offshore power line. (ligne internationale de transport d'electricite ou ligne internationale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: interprovincial power line means facilities that are constructed or operated for the purpose of transmitting electricity from a place in a province to a place in another province. (ligne interprovinciale de transport d'electricite ou ligne interprovinciale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: land registrar means an officer with whom titles, rights or interests relating to real property or immovables are registered or recorded. (directeur de l'enregistrement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: lands includes real property and any interest or right in real property or land and, in Quebec, any immovable, any right in an immovable and the right of a lessee in respect of any immovable. Those interests or rights may be in, to, on, under, over or in respect of the lands. (terrains)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the member of the Queen's Privy Council for Canada designated under section 8. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: navigable water has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canadian Navigable Waters Act. (eaux navigables)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: offshore area means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the part of the internal waters of Canada or of the territorial sea of Canada that is not situated in

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) a province other than the Northwest Territories, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) the onshore, as defined in section 2 of the Northwest Territories Act; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the continental shelf of Canada and the waters superjacent to the seabed of that shelf. (zone extracotiere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: offshore power line means facilities constructed or operated for the purpose of transmitting electricity from an offshore renewable energy project to a province or a place outside Canada. (ligne extracotiere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: offshore renewable energy project means any of the following that are carried on in the offshore area:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any research or assessment conducted in relation to the exploitation or potential exploitation of a renewable resource to produce energy;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any exploitation of a renewable resource to produce energy;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any storage of energy produced from a renewable resource; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any transmission of such energy, other than the transmission of electricity to a province or a place outside Canada. (projet d'energie renouvelable extracotiere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: oil means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any hydrocarbon or mixture of hydrocarbons other than gas; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any substance designated as an oil product by regulations made under section 390. (petrole)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: penalty means an administrative monetary penalty imposed under this Act for a violation. (penalite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pipeline means a line - including all branches, extensions, tanks, reservoirs, storage or loading facilities, pumps, racks, compressors, interstation communication systems, real or personal property, or immovable or movable, and any connected works - that connects at least two provinces or extends beyond the limits of a province, Sable Island or an area referred to in paragraph (c) of the definition designated area in section 368 and that is used or is to be used for the transmission of oil, gas or any other commodity. It does not however include a sewer or water pipeline that is used or is to be used solely for municipal purposes. (pipeline)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: power line means an international power line, an interprovincial power line or an offshore power line. (ligne de transport d'electricite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: regulated facility means a pipeline, an international power line, an interprovincial power line designated by an order made under section 261, an offshore power line, or any facility, equipment or system that is related to an offshore renewable energy project. (installation reglementee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Regulator means the corporation established under subsection 10(1). (Regie)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Special Act means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an Act of Parliament that authorizes a person named in the Act to construct or operate a pipeline or that is enacted with special reference to a pipeline that, by such an Act, a person is authorized to construct or operate; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) letters patent issued under section 5.1 or 5.4 of the Canada Corporations Act, chapter C-32 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1970, except for the purpose of paragraph 342(b) of this Act. (loi speciale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: toll includes any rate, charge or allowance charged or made

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) for the shipment, transportation, transmission, care, handling or delivery of hydrocarbons or of another commodity that is transmitted through a pipeline, or for storage or demurrage, or the like;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for the provision of a pipeline when the pipeline is available and ready to provide for the transmission of oil or gas; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in respect of the purchase and sale of gas that is the property of a company and that is transmitted by the company through its pipeline, excluding the cost to the company of the gas at the point where it enters the pipeline. (droit)

heading: Application - Special Act lands
paragraph: 4 A provision of this Act or a regulation made under it that applies to lands also applies to lands referred to in a Special Act.

heading: Powers of liquidators, trustees, etc.
paragraph: 5 (1) For the purposes of this Act, each of the following is considered to be a company:

heading: Powers of liquidators, trustees, etc.
paragraph: (a) a liquidator, receiver or manager of the property of a company, appointed by a court of competent jurisdiction to carry on the business of the company;

heading: Powers of liquidators, trustees, etc.
paragraph: (b) a trustee - or the holder of a power of attorney within the meaning of the Civil Code of Quebec - for the holders of bonds, debentures, debenture stock or other evidence of indebtedness of the company, secured under a trust deed, an act constituting a hypothec within the meaning of the Civil Code of Quebec or other instrument or act, on or against the property of the company, if the trustee or holder is authorized by the instrument or act to carry on the business of the company; and

heading: Powers of liquidators, trustees, etc.
paragraph: (c) a person, other than a company,

heading: Powers of liquidators, trustees, etc.
paragraph: (i) operating a pipeline constructed before October 1, 1953, or

heading: Powers of liquidators, trustees, etc.
paragraph: (ii) constructing, operating or abandoning a pipeline exempted from subsection 179(1) by an order made by the Commission under subsection 214(1).

heading: Administrator in Quebec
paragraph: (2) In Quebec, the administrator of the property of the company appointed by a court of competent jurisdiction to carry on the business of the company is also considered to be the company.

heading: Successor or assign - abandoned pipeline
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this Act, a successor or assign of a company is considered to be a company for any matter relating to an abandoned pipeline.

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: 6 The purpose of this Act is to regulate certain energy matters within Parliament's jurisdiction and, in particular,

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: (a) to ensure that pipelines and power lines as well as facilities, equipment or systems related to offshore renewable energy projects, are constructed, operated and abandoned in a manner that is safe, secure and efficient and that protects people, property and the environment;

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: (b) to ensure that the exploration for and exploitation of oil and gas, as defined in section 2 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act, is carried out in a manner that is safe and secure and that protects people, property and the environment;

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: (c) to regulate trade in energy products; and

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: (d) to ensure that regulatory hearings and decision-making processes related to those energy matters are fair, inclusive, transparent and efficient.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 7 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Order designating Minister
paragraph: 8 The Governor in Council may, by order, designate any member of the Queen's Privy Council for Canada to be the Minister for the purposes this Act.

heading: Definition of document of authorization
paragraph: 9 In this Part, document of authorization means a certificate issued under Part 3 or 4, a permit issued under Part 4 or 7, an authorization issued under Part 5, a licence issued under Part 7 or an order made under section 214.

heading: Canadian Energy Regulator
paragraph: 10 (1) A corporation is established to be called the Canadian Energy Regulator.

heading: Agent of Her Majesty
paragraph: (2) The Regulator is for all purposes an agent of Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Head office and other offices
paragraph: (3) The head office of the Regulator is to be in Calgary, Alberta. The Regulator's Chief Executive Officer may open or close other offices after consulting the board of directors.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (4) For greater certainty, the opening or closing of an office does not change the conditions of appointment of a director or commissioner.

heading: Mandate
paragraph: 11 The Regulator's mandate includes

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (a) making transparent decisions, orders and recommendations with respect to pipelines, power lines, offshore renewable energy projects and abandoned pipelines;

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (b) overseeing the construction, operation and abandonment of pipelines, interprovincial power lines and international power lines and overseeing work and activities authorized under Part 5 as well as abandoned facilities;

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (c) making orders with respect to traffic, tolls and tariffs and overseeing matters relating to traffic, tolls and tariffs;

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (d) making decisions and orders and giving directions under Part 8 with respect to oil and gas interests, production and conservation;

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (e) advising and reporting on energy matters;

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (f) providing alternative dispute resolution processes;

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (g) exercising powers and performing duties and functions that are conferred on the Regulator under any other Act of Parliament; and

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (h) exercising its powers and performing its duties and functions in a manner that respects the Government of Canada's commitments with respect to the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Canada.

heading: Jurisdiction - Inuvialuit Settlement Region
paragraph: 12 (1) Until March 31, 2034, the Regulator is to be the regulator - under any law of the Legislature of the Northwest Territories that is made under paragraph 19(1)(a), (b) or (c) of the Northwest Territories Act - in respect of that portion of the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, as defined in section 2 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act, that is situated in the onshore as defined in section 2 of the Northwest Territories Act.

heading: Successive periods and termination
paragraph: (2) After March 31, 2034, the Government of Canada and the Government of the Northwest Territories may agree that the Regulator is to continue to be the regulator for one or more periods of 20 years each; they may also, before the expiry of each successive period, agree to its earlier termination.

heading: Governor in Council directions
paragraph: 13 (1) The Governor in Council may, by order, give to the Regulator directions of general application on broad policy matters with respect to the Regulator's mandate.

heading: Directions binding
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) is binding on the Regulator.

heading: Publication and tabling
paragraph: (3) A copy of each order made under subsection (1) must be published in the Canada Gazette and tabled in each House of Parliament.

heading: Establishment and composition
paragraph: 14 (1) The Regulator is to have a board of directors consisting of at least five but not more than nine directors, including a Chairperson and a Vice-Chairperson.

heading: Indigenous representation
paragraph: (2) At least one of the directors must be an Indigenous person.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: 15 (1) The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and the other directors are to be appointed by the Governor in Council to hold office on a part-time basis and during pleasure for a term not exceeding five years.

heading: Reappointment
paragraph: (2) A director may be reappointed in the same or another capacity for one or more terms of up to five years each.

heading: Eligibility - directors
paragraph: (3) A person is not eligible to be a director if they are the Chief Executive Officer, a commissioner or an employee of the Regulator.

heading: Eligibility - Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson
paragraph: (4) A person is not eligible to be Chairperson or Vice-Chairperson unless they are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

heading: Remuneration and expenses
paragraph: (5) A director is to be paid the remuneration that is fixed by the Governor in Council and is entitled to be paid reasonable travel and other expenses while performing their duties and functions under this Act while absent from their ordinary place of residence.

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: 16 For the purposes of the Conflict of Interest Act, the circumstances in which a director is in a conflict of interest while exercising the powers or performing the duties and functions of a director include

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy;

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business; and

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with their powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it.

heading: Role of the board of directors
paragraph: 17 (1) The board of directors is responsible for the governance of the Regulator and its governance functions include providing strategic direction and advice to the Regulator. The board of directors must not however give directions or provide advice with respect to any particular decision, order or recommendation that is made by the Commission or a commissioner.

heading: By-laws
paragraph: (2) The board of directors may make by-laws respecting the conduct of its meetings and the general conduct of its activities.

heading: Quorum
paragraph: (3) A majority of the directors holding office, including the Chairperson, constitutes a quorum of the board of directors.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: 18 (1) The board of directors must, within 120 days after the end of each fiscal year, submit to the Minister a report on the Regulator's activities under this Act for that fiscal year, and the Minister must cause the report to be laid before each House of Parliament on any of the first 15 days on which that House is sitting after the day on which the report is received.

heading: Other reports
paragraph: (2) The board of directors may submit a report to the Minister on the Regulator's activities if the board considers it appropriate to do so.

heading: Definition of fiscal year
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), fiscal year means the period beginning on April 1 in one year and ending on March 31 in the next year.

heading: Role of Chairperson
paragraph: 19 (1) The Chairperson presides over meetings of the board of directors and may perform any duties or functions that are assigned to him or her by the board.

heading: Acting Chairperson
paragraph: (2) If the Chairperson is absent or is unable to act or if there is a vacancy in that office, the Vice-Chairperson acts as Chairperson.

heading: Governor in Council approval
paragraph: (3) The Vice-Chairperson is not authorized to act as Chairperson for a period of more than 90 days without the approval of the Governor in Council.

heading: Vacancy
paragraph: 20 A vacancy in the board of directors does not impair the right of the remaining directors to act.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: 21 (1) The Chief Executive Officer of the Regulator is to be appointed by the Governor in Council on the recommendation of the Minister after the Minister has consulted the directors.

heading: Term
paragraph: (2) The Chief Executive Officer is to hold office on a full-time basis during pleasure for a term of up to six years.

heading: Reappointment
paragraph: (3) The Chief Executive Officer may be reappointed for one or more terms of up to six years each. However, the Chief Executive Officer is to serve no more than 10 years in office in total.

heading: Eligibility
paragraph: (4) A person is not eligible to be the Chief Executive Officer unless they are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

heading: Eligibility
paragraph: (5) A director is not eligible to be the Chief Executive Officer.

heading: Remuneration and expenses
paragraph: (6) The Chief Executive Officer is to be paid the remuneration that is fixed by the Governor in Council and is entitled to be paid reasonable travel and other expenses while performing his or her duties and functions under this Act while absent from his or her ordinary place of work.

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: 22 For the purposes of the Conflict of Interest Act, the circumstances in which the Chief Executive Officer is in a conflict of interest while exercising the powers or performing the duties and functions of the Chief Executive Officer include

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy;

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business;

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with the Chief Executive Officer's powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it; and

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (d) holding office as a commissioner or being employed by the Regulator.

heading: Role of Chief Executive Officer
paragraph: 23 (1) The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the management of the Regulator's day-to-day business and affairs, including the supervision of its employees and their work. The Chief Executive Officer must not however give directions with respect to any particular decision, order or recommendation that is made by the Commission or a commissioner.

heading: Rank of deputy head
paragraph: (2) The Chief Executive Officer has the rank and the powers of a deputy head of a department.

heading: Acting Chief Executive Officer
paragraph: (3) If the Chief Executive Officer is absent or unable to act or if there is a vacancy in that office, an executive of the Regulator designated by the Minister acts as Chief Executive Officer.

heading: Governor in Council approval
paragraph: (4) The executive referred to in subsection (3) is not authorized to act as Chief Executive Officer for a period of more than 90 days without the approval of the Governor in Council.

heading: Designated officers
paragraph: 24 The Chief Executive Officer may designate employees of the Regulator as designated officers.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: 25 For greater certainty, the Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the provision of the support services and the facilities that are needed by the Commission to exercise its powers and perform its duties and functions in accordance with the rules that apply to its work.

heading: Commission
paragraph: 26 (1) The Regulator is to have a Commission that consists of up to seven full-time commissioners. It may also include a complement of part-time commissioners.

heading: Indigenous representation
paragraph: (2) At least one of the full-time commissioners must be an Indigenous person.

heading: Quorum
paragraph: 27 Subject to subsection 42(2), sections 45 to 47 and subsection 48(2), three commissioners constitutes a quorum of the Commission.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: 28 (1) The commissioners are to be appointed by the Governor in Council to hold office during good behaviour for a term not exceeding six years.

heading: Reappointment
paragraph: (2) A commissioner may be reappointed for one or more terms of up to six years each. However, a commissioner is to serve no more than 10 years in office in total.

heading: Removal
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council may remove a commissioner for cause.

heading: Eligibility
paragraph: (4) A person is not eligible to be a commissioner unless they are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

heading: Eligibility
paragraph: (5) A director is not eligible to be a commissioner.

heading: Remuneration and expenses - full-time commissioner
paragraph: (6) A full-time commissioner is to be paid the remuneration that is fixed by the Governor in Council and is entitled to be paid reasonable travel and other expenses while performing their duties and functions under this Act while absent from their ordinary place of work.

heading: Remuneration and expenses - part-time commissioner
paragraph: (7) A part-time commissioner is to be paid the remuneration that is fixed by the Governor in Council and is entitled to be paid reasonable travel and other expenses while performing their duties and functions under this Act while absent from their ordinary place of residence.

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: 29 For the purposes of the Conflict of Interest Act, the circumstances in which a commissioner is in a conflict of interest while exercising the powers or performing the duties and functions of a commissioner include

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (a) engaging in, as owner, shareholder, director, officer, partner or in any other way, the business of producing, selling, buying, transmitting, exporting, importing or otherwise dealing in hydrocarbons, electricity or offshore energy;

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (b) holding any bond, debenture or other security of a corporation engaged in any such business;

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (c) holding other employment that is inconsistent with their powers, duties and functions or with any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it; and

heading: Conflict of Interest Act
paragraph: (d) holding office as the Chief Executive Officer or being employed by the Regulator.

heading: Vacancy
paragraph: 30 A vacancy in the Commission does not impair the right of the remaining commissioners to act.

heading: Court of record
paragraph: 31 (1) The Commission is a court of record and the Regulator's seal must be judicially noticed as the Commission's official seal.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (2) The Commission has all the powers, rights and privileges vested in a superior court of record with respect to any matters within its jurisdiction, including the attendance, swearing and examination of witnesses, the production and inspection of documents, the enforcement of its orders and the entry on and inspection of property.

heading: Expeditious applications and proceedings
paragraph: (3) All applications and proceedings before the Commission must be dealt with as expeditiously as the circumstances and procedural fairness and natural justice permit, but, in any case, within any time limit provided for under this Act.

heading: Jurisdiction
paragraph: 32 (1) The Commission has full and exclusive jurisdiction to inquire into, hear and determine any matter if the Commission considers that

heading: Jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) a person has failed to do anything that is required to be done under this Act, under a condition of a document of authorization, or under an order made or direction given under this Act;

heading: Jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) a person has done or is doing anything that is contrary to or in contravention of this Act, a condition of a document of authorization or an order made or direction given under this Act; or

heading: Jurisdiction
paragraph: (c) the circumstances may require the Commission, in the public interest, to make any order or give any direction, leave, sanction or approval that it is authorized to make or give, or that relates to anything that is prohibited, sanctioned or required to be done under this Act, a condition of a document of authorization, or an order made or direction given under this Act.

heading: Inquiry
paragraph: (2) The Commission may inquire into any accident involving a pipeline, abandoned pipeline, international power line, offshore renewable energy project, offshore power line or other facility the construction or operation of which is regulated by the Regulator and may, at the conclusion of the inquiry, make

heading: Inquiry
paragraph: (a) findings as to the cause of the accident or factors contributing to it;

heading: Inquiry
paragraph: (b) recommendations relating to the prevention of future similar accidents; or

heading: Inquiry
paragraph: (c) any decision or order that the Commission is authorized to make.

heading: Matters of law and fact
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this Act, the Commission has full jurisdiction to hear and determine all matters, whether of law or of fact.

heading: Power to act on own initiative
paragraph: 33 The Commission may on its own initiative inquire into, hear and determine any matter that under this Act it may inquire into, hear and determine.

heading: Orders and prohibitions
paragraph: 34 The Commission may

heading: Orders and prohibitions
paragraph: (a) order any person to do, immediately or within or at any specified time and in any specified manner, anything that the person is or may be required to do under this Act, under a condition of a document of authorization, or under any order made or direction given by the Commission or a designated officer under this Act; and

heading: Orders and prohibitions
paragraph: (b) prohibit the doing or continuing of anything that is contrary to this Act, to a condition of the document of authorization or to the order or direction.

heading: Rules
paragraph: 35 The Commission may make rules generally for the carrying out of its work and the management of its internal affairs, including rules respecting

heading: Rules
paragraph: (a) the powers, duties and functions of the commissioners;

heading: Rules
paragraph: (b) its sittings;

heading: Rules
paragraph: (c) its decisions, orders and recommendations; and

heading: Rules
paragraph: (d) its procedures and practices.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: 36 (1) The Commission must, within 120 days after the end of each fiscal year, submit to the Minister a report on the Commission's activities under this Act for that fiscal year, and the Minister must cause the report to be laid before each House of Parliament on any of the first 15 days on which that House is sitting after the day on which the report is received.

heading: Other reports
paragraph: (2) The Commission may submit a report to the Minister on the Commission's activities if the Commission considers it appropriate to do so.

heading: Definition of fiscal year
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), fiscal year means the period beginning on April 1 in one year and ending on March 31 in the next year.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 37 The Governor in Council must designate one of the full-time commissioners to hold office as Lead Commissioner and one of the full-time commissioners to hold office as Deputy Lead Commissioner.

heading: Role of Lead Commissioner
paragraph: 38 The Lead Commissioner is responsible for the business and affairs of the Commission and, in particular, is responsible for apportioning the Commission's work among the commissioners and for establishing panels - of at least three commissioners - to exercise the powers of the Commission and perform its duties and functions in relation to a matter before it.

heading: Acting Lead Commissioner
paragraph: 39 (1) The Deputy Lead Commissioner acts as Lead Commissioner if the Lead Commissioner is absent or unable to act or if there is a vacancy in that office.

heading: Governor in Council approval
paragraph: (2) The Deputy Lead Commissioner is not authorized to act as Lead Commissioner for a period of more than 90 days without the approval of the Governor in Council.

heading: Acting Lead and Deputy Lead Commissioners
paragraph: 40 (1) If both the Lead Commissioner and Deputy Lead Commissioner are absent or unable to act or if there are vacancies in both of those offices, a commissioner designated by the Minister acts as Lead Commissioner.

heading: Governor in Council approval
paragraph: (2) The designated commissioner is not authorized to act as Lead Commissioner for a period of more than 90 days without the approval of the Governor in Council.

heading: Instructions regarding timeliness
paragraph: 41 To ensure that an application before the Commission is dealt with in a timely manner, the Lead Commissioner may give instructions to the commissioners authorized to deal with the application respecting the manner in which they are to do so.

heading: Measures to meet time limit
paragraph: 42 (1) If the Lead Commissioner is satisfied that a time limit imposed under any of sections 183, 214 and 262 is not likely to be met in respect of an application, the Lead Commissioner may take any measure that he or she considers appropriate to ensure that the time limit is met, including

heading: Measures to meet time limit
paragraph: (a) removing any or all commissioners from a panel authorized to deal with the application;

heading: Measures to meet time limit
paragraph: (b) authorizing one or more commissioners to deal with the application; and

heading: Measures to meet time limit
paragraph: (c) increasing or decreasing the number of commissioners dealing with the application.

heading: Clarification
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, the power referred to in subsection (1) includes the power to designate a single member, including the Lead Commissioner, as the sole commissioner who is authorized to deal with the application.

heading: Inconsistencies
paragraph: 43 In the event of any inconsistency between a instruction given under section 41 or a measure taken under subsection 42(1) and any rule made under section 35, the instruction or measure prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: 44 For greater certainty, sections 41 and 42 do not apply to an application with respect to a designated project, as defined in section 2 of the Impact Assessment Act, that is subject to an impact assessment under that Act.

heading: Authorization - powers, duties and functions
paragraph: 45 (1) The Lead Commissioner may authorize one or more commissioners, either jointly or severally, to exercise any of the powers of the Commission or to perform any of its duties and functions under this Act, except those under sections 95, 183, 184, 186, 195 to 197, subsection 211(3), sections 212 to 214, 231 to 234, 238 to 240, 248, 257, 262, 274, 285 to 287, 289 and under Parts 7 and 8.

heading: Presumption
paragraph: (2) A power exercised or a duty or function performed under the authorization is considered to have been exercised or performed by the Commission.

heading: Authorization - report
paragraph: 46 (1) The Lead Commissioner may authorize one or more of the commissioners to report to the Commission on any matter related to the work of the Commission or any application or proceeding before it. For the purpose of making a report related to an application or proceeding before the Commission, the authorized commissioners have all the powers of the Commission with respect to taking evidence or acquiring information.

heading: Not a quorum
paragraph: (2) Despite section 27 of this Act and paragraph 22(2)(a) of the Interpretation Act, three or more commissioners authorized to report in accordance with subsection (1) do not constitute a quorum of the Commission.

heading: Use of report
paragraph: (3) A report to the Commission under subsection (1) may be adopted as a decision or order of the Commission or be dealt with as the Commission considers appropriate.

heading: Replacement of commissioner during hearing
paragraph: 47 (1) If a commissioner who is conducting a hearing in accordance with an authorization under section 45 or 46 is unable to act or resigns during the hearing, the Lead Commissioner may authorize another commissioner to continue the hearing and to make the decision or report.

heading: Replacement of commissioner before decision or report
paragraph: (2) If a commissioner who is conducting a hearing in accordance with an authorization under section 45 or 46 is unable to act or resigns after the conclusion of the hearing but before the decision or report is made, the Lead Commissioner may authorize another commissioner to examine all the evidence presented at the hearing and to make the decision or report on the basis of that evidence.

heading: Replacement of panel member during hearing
paragraph: 48 (1) If a panel is conducting a hearing and a commissioner on the panel is unable to act or resigns during the hearing, the Lead Commissioner may authorize another commissioner to replace that commissioner for the rest of the hearing and to participate in the decision or, as applicable, finalize the report required under subsection 183(1).

heading: Replacement of panel member before decision or report
paragraph: (2) If a panel is conducting a hearing and a commissioner on the panel is unable to act or resigns after the conclusion of the hearing but before the decision is made or, as applicable, the report required under subsection 183(1) is finalized, the remaining commissioners may - if unanimous - make the decision or finalize the report as if the commissioner were present and participating.

heading: Lead Commissioner's powers
paragraph: 49 Nothing in section 47 or subsection 48(1) precludes the Lead Commissioner from taking a measure under subsection 42(1).

heading: Change in composition of panel
paragraph: 50 If the composition of a panel changes in accordance with subsection 42(1) or 48(1),

heading: Change in composition of panel
paragraph: (a) evidence and representations received by the Commission in relation to the matter being dealt with by the panel before the change are considered to have been received after the change; and

heading: Change in composition of panel
paragraph: (b) the Commission is bound by every decision made by the Commission in relation to the matter being dealt with by the panel before the change unless the Commission elects to review, vary or rescind it.

heading: Authorization to continue
paragraph: 51 If a commissioner resigns or their term expires, the Lead Commissioner may, on any conditions he or she specifies, authorize the former commissioner to continue to exercise powers and perform duties and functions as a commissioner in a matter to which they were assigned immediately before resigning or the expiry of their term until a final decision or recommendation in the matter is made, and the former commissioner is considered to be a commissioner for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Public hearings
paragraph: 52 (1) A hearing before the Commission with respect to the issuance, suspension or revocation of a certificate under Part 3 or 4 must be public.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a hearing with respect to the suspension or revocation of either of the following certificates if the holder applies for or consents to the suspension or revocation:

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) a certificate issued in respect of an international or interprovincial power line, whether or not the power line has been brought into commercial operation under the certificate; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) a certificate issued in respect of a pipeline that has not been brought into commercial operation under the certificate.

heading: Other matters
paragraph: (3) The Commission may hold a public hearing in respect of any other matter if the Commission considers it appropriate to do so and shall make public its reasons for holding the hearing.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (4) For greater certainty, subsection (1) does not affect the operation of subsection 241(3).

heading: Reasons
paragraph: 53 (1) The Commission must issue written reasons for each recommendation it makes to the Governor in Council or the Minister.

heading: Public availability
paragraph: (2) The Regulator must make the recommendations, and the reasons for them, publicly available.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 54 The Governor in Council may make regulations that specify

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) powers, duties and functions of the Commission that are technical or administrative in nature and may be exercised or performed by designated officers;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) any circumstances in which those powers are to be exercised and those duties and functions are to be performed only by designated officers; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) the procedures and practices that apply to the exercise of those powers and the performance of those duties and functions by designated officers.

heading: Apportionment of work
paragraph: 55 The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for apportioning among the designated officers any work related to a power, duty or function that is specified in a regulation made under section 54.

heading: Duty to consider - Commission
paragraph: 56 (1) When making a decision, an order or a recommendation under this Act, the Commission must consider any adverse effects that the decision, order or recommendation may have on the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Canada recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Duty to consider - designated officers
paragraph: (2) When making a decision or an order under this Act, a designated officer must consider any adverse effects that the decision or order may have on the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Canada recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Advisory committee
paragraph: 57 (1) The Regulator must establish an advisory committee for the purpose of enhancing the involvement, under Part 2, of the Indigenous peoples of Canada and Indigenous organizations in respect of pipelines, power lines and offshore renewable energy projects as well as abandoned pipelines.

heading: Membership
paragraph: (2) The membership of the advisory committee must include at least

heading: Membership
paragraph: (a) one person recommended by an Indigenous organization that represents the interests of First Nations;

heading: Membership
paragraph: (b) one person recommended by an Indigenous organization that represents the interests of the Inuit; and

heading: Membership
paragraph: (c) one person recommended by an Indigenous organization that represents the interests of the Metis.

heading: Confidentiality - Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: 58 (1) Any Indigenous knowledge that is provided in confidence to the Regulator under this Act or any other Act of Parliament that confers powers, duties or functions on the Regulator is confidential and must not knowingly be, or be permitted to be, disclosed without written consent.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the Indigenous knowledge referred to in that subsection may be disclosed if

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) it is publicly available;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the disclosure is necessary for the purposes of procedural fairness and natural justice or for use in legal proceedings; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) the disclosure is authorized in the circumstances set out in the regulations made under section 59.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2.1) Before disclosing Indigenous knowledge under paragraph 2(b) for the purposes of procedural fairness and natural justice, the Regulator must consult the person or entity who provided the Indigenous knowledge and the person or entity to whom it is proposed to be disclosed about the scope of the proposed disclosure and potential conditions under subsection (3).

heading: Further disclosure
paragraph: (3) The Regulator may, having regard to the consultation referred to in subsection (2.1), impose conditions with respect to the disclosure of Indigenous knowledge by any person or entity to whom it is disclosed under paragraph (2)(b) for the purposes of procedural fairness and natural justice.

heading: Duty to comply
paragraph: (4) The person or entity referred to in subsection (3) must comply with any conditions imposed by the Regulator under that subsection.

heading: Protection from civil proceeding or prosecution
paragraph: (5) Despite any other Act of Parliament, no civil or criminal proceedings lie against the Regulator or the Minister - or any person acting on behalf of, or under the direction of, either of them - and no proceedings lie against the Crown or the Regulator, for the disclosure in good faith of any Indigenous knowledge under this Act or any other Act of Parliament that confers powers, duties or functions on the Regulator or for any consequences that flow from that disclosure.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 59 The Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing the circumstances in which Indigenous knowledge that is provided to the Regulator under this Act in confidence may be disclosed without written consent.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: 60 The Commission or a designated officer may take any measures and make any order that the Commission or designated officer considers necessary to ensure the confidentiality of any information likely to be disclosed in any proceedings under this Act if the Commission or designated officer is satisfied that

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (a) disclosure of the information could reasonably be expected to result in a material loss or gain to a person directly affected by the proceedings, or could reasonably be expected to prejudice the person's competitive position;

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (b) the information is financial, commercial, scientific or technical information that is confidential information provided to the Regulator and

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (i) the information has been consistently treated as confidential information by a person directly affected by the proceedings, and

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (ii) the Commission or designated officer considers that the person's interest in confidentiality outweighs the public interest in disclosure of the proceedings; or

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (c) there is a real and substantial risk that disclosure of the information will compromise the safety and well-being of persons or cause harm to property or the environment.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: 61 The Commission or a designated officer may take any measures and make any order that the Commission or designated officer considers necessary to ensure the confidentiality of information that is contained in any order under this Act or that is likely to be disclosed in any proceedings under this Act if the Commission or designated officer is satisfied that

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (a) there is a real and substantial risk that disclosure of the information will pose a risk to the security of pipelines, abandoned pipelines, power lines, offshore renewable energy projects, including buildings, structures or systems - including computer or communication systems, or methods employed to protect them - and the need to prevent disclosure of the information outweighs the public interest in disclosure of orders and proceedings; or

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (b) there is a real and substantial risk that disclosure of the information will compromise the safety and well-being of persons or cause harm to property or the environment.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: 62 The Commission or a designated officer may take any measures and make any orders that are necessary to ensure compliance with section 58 or any regulations referred in subsection 114(3).

heading: Reasons
paragraph: 63 (1) The Commission must issue written reasons for each decision or order it makes. A designated officer must do the same for each decision or order they make.

heading: Public availability
paragraph: (2) The Regulator must make the decisions and orders, and the reasons for them, publicly available.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply to a decision or order that is made only in relation to the internal administrative affairs of the Regulator.

heading: Enforcement of orders
paragraph: 64 (1) A decision or order of the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer may be made an order of the Federal Court or of a superior court of a province and may be enforced in the same manner as an order of that court as if it had been an order of that court on the date of the decision or order.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (2) A decision or order of the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer may be made an order of a court in accordance with the usual practice and procedure of the court in such matters, if any, or by the filing with the registrar of the court of a copy of the decision certified by an employee of the Regulator who is authorized by the Chief Executive Officer to certify documents for the purposes of this section under the Regulator's seal.

heading: Effect of revocation or amendment
paragraph: (3) If a decision or order of the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer that has been made an order of a court is rescinded or varied by a subsequent decision or order, the order of the court is vacated and the decision or order of the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer as varied may be made an order of the court in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Conditions
paragraph: 65 A decision or order made by the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer under this Act may include any conditions that the Commission, designated officer or inspection officer considers appropriate.

heading: General or particular application
paragraph: 66 The Commission or a designated officer may, when making an order, giving a direction, imposing conditions or doing any other thing in relation to a person, do so either generally or in any particular case or class of cases.

heading: Coming into force and cessation of effect - Commission
paragraph: 67 (1) The Commission may, in issuing, varying or transferring a document of authorization, or when making or varying an order,

heading: Coming into force and cessation of effect - Commission
paragraph: (a) specify a day on which the document of authorization or order, or any part of it, comes into force or ceases to have effect; or

heading: Coming into force and cessation of effect - Commission
paragraph: (b) impose conditions governing when the document of authorization or order, or any part of it, comes into force or ceases to have effect.

heading: Coming into force and cessation of effect - designated officer or inspection officer
paragraph: (2) A designated officer or inspection officer may, when making or varying an order,

heading: Coming into force and cessation of effect - designated officer or inspection officer
paragraph: (a) specify a day on which the order, or any part of it, comes into force or ceases to have effect; or

heading: Coming into force and cessation of effect - designated officer or inspection officer
paragraph: (b) impose conditions governing when the order, or any part of it, comes into force or ceases to have effect.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to a certificate issued under Part 3.

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (4) The Commission, a designated officer or inspection officer may, instead of making an order final in the first instance, make an interim order, and may reserve their decision pending further proceedings in connection with any matter.

heading: Relief
paragraph: 68 (1) The Commission may make a decision or order that grants, in whole or in part, any application made to the Commission. The decision or order may also include - in addition to or in lieu of the relief applied for - any other relief that the Commission considers appropriate as if the application had been made for that other relief.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to an application made under Part 3 for a certificate.

heading: Power to review, vary or rescind - Commission
paragraph: 69 (1) The Commission may review, vary or rescind any decision or order it makes and, if applicable, may re-hear any application before deciding it.

heading: Power to vary or rescind - designated officer or inspection officer
paragraph: (2) A designated officer or inspection officer may vary or rescind any decision or order they make and, if applicable, may re-hear any application before deciding it.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply to a decision or order in relation to an operating licence or authorization to which section 382 or 383 applies or in relation to the approval of a development plan under section 5.1 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.

heading: Decisions final
paragraph: 70 (1) Except as provided for in this Act, every decision or order of the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer is final and conclusive.

heading: Decision or order
paragraph: (2) Any minute or other record of the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer or any document issued by one of them, in the form of a decision or order, is considered for the purposes of this section to be a decision or order, as the case may be, of the Commission, the designated officer or the inspection officer.

heading: Appeal to Commission
paragraph: 71 An appeal from a decision or order of a designated officer or an inspection officer may be brought before the Commission and the Commission may dismiss or allow the appeal and vary or rescind the decision or order.

heading: Appeal to Federal Court of Appeal
paragraph: 72 (1) An appeal from a decision or order of the Commission on any question of law or of jurisdiction may be brought in the Federal Court of Appeal with the leave of that Court.

heading: Application for leave to appeal
