paragraph: (2) Leave to appeal must be applied for within 30 days after the date of the decision or order appealed from or within any additional time that a judge of the Court grants in exceptional circumstances.

heading: Time limit for appeal
paragraph: (3) An appeal must be brought within 60 days after the day on which leave to appeal is granted.

heading: Argument by Regulator
paragraph: (4) The Regulator is entitled to be heard on an application for leave to appeal and at any stage of an appeal.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (5) In any appeal under this section, costs may not be awarded against any of the commissioners.

heading: Report not decision or order
paragraph: (6) For greater certainty, a report submitted by the Commission under section 183 or 184 - or under subsection 51(1) the Impact Assessment Act - is not a decision or order of the Commission for the purposes of this section and neither is any part of the report.

heading: Alternative dispute resolution
paragraph: 73 (1) If all the parties to a dispute that is directly related to a matter under this Act consent, the Regulator must provide or cause to be provided an alternative dispute resolution process for the dispute.

heading: Results
paragraph: (2) The results of the alternative dispute resolution process are not binding.

heading: Use of results by Commission
paragraph: (3) The Commission may take the results of the alternative dispute resolution process into account when making a decision, order or recommendation and may refer to them in the decision, order or recommendation.

heading: Use of results by designated officer
paragraph: (4) A designated officer may take the results of the alternative dispute resolution process into account when making a decision or order and may refer to them in the decision or order.

heading: Public availability of results
paragraph: (5) The Regulator may make the results of the alternative dispute resolution process public with the consent of the parties.

heading: Public engagement
paragraph: 74 The Regulator must establish processes that the Regulator considers appropriate to engage meaningfully with the public - and, in particular, the Indigenous peoples of Canada and Indigenous organizations - when public hearings are held under section 52 or subsection 241(3).

heading: Participant funding program
paragraph: 75 For the purposes of this Act, the Regulator must establish a participant funding program to facilitate the participation of the public - and, in particular, the Indigenous peoples of Canada and Indigenous organizations - in public hearings under section 52 or subsection 241(3) and any steps leading to those hearings.

heading: Collaborative processes
paragraph: 76 The Regulator may enter into arrangements with any government or Indigenous organization to establish collaborative processes.

heading: Ministerial arrangements
paragraph: 77 (1) If regulations are made under section 78, the Minister may, in accordance with those regulations, enter into arrangements with Indigenous governing bodies for carrying out the purposes of this Act and may authorize any Indigenous governing body with whom an arrangement is entered into to exercise the powers or perform the duties and functions under this Act that are specified in the arrangement.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (2) Within 30 days after the day on which the Minister enters into an arrangement, the Regulator must publish it on the Regulator's website.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 78 The Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the Minister's power to enter into arrangements under section 77, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting how they are to be entered into;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the circumstances under which they may be entered into;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting their contents; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) varying or excluding any provision of this Act or a regulation made under it as that provision applies to the subject matter of the arrangement.

heading: Inconsistencies
paragraph: 79 In the event of an inconsistency between an arrangement referred to in section 76 and an arrangement referred to in section 77, the arrangement referred to in section 77 prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Study and review
paragraph: 80 The Regulator must study and keep under review matters relating to

heading: Study and review
paragraph: (a) the exploration for, and the production, recovery, manufacture, processing, transmission, transportation, distribution, sale, purchase, lease, exchange and alienation of energy and sources of energy in and outside Canada; and

heading: Study and review
paragraph: (b) the safety and security of regulated facilities and abandoned facilities.

heading: Reports and recommendations to Minister
paragraph: 81 The Regulator may submit to the Minister reports on the matters referred to in section 80 from time to time and may recommend to the Minister any measures within Parliament's jurisdiction that the Regulator considers to be necessary or in the public interest for

heading: Reports and recommendations to Minister
paragraph: (a) the control, supervision, conservation, use, marketing and development of energy and sources of energy; and

heading: Reports and recommendations to Minister
paragraph: (b) the safety and security of regulated facilities and abandoned facilities.

heading: Recommendations on cooperative measures
paragraph: 82 The Regulator may - with respect to energy matters, sources of energy and the safety and security of regulated facilities and abandoned facilities - recommend to the Minister any measures that the Regulator considers necessary or appropriate for cooperation with governmental or other agencies in or outside Canada.

heading: Request of Minister
paragraph: 83 (1) The Regulator must - with respect to energy matters, sources of energy and the safety and security of regulated facilities and abandoned facilities - provide to the Minister any advice that the Minister requests, including advice relating to the export pricing of oil and gas, and prepare any study or report that the Minister requests.

heading: Prohibition on publication
paragraph: (2) The Regulator must not publish any advice, study or report referred to in subsection (1) without the Minister's consent.

heading: Other requests
paragraph: 84 The Regulator may, on request, provide advice about energy matters, sources of energy and the safety and security of regulated facilities and abandoned facilities to

heading: Other requests
paragraph: (a) ministers, officers and employees of any government department or ministry, whether federal, provincial or territorial; and

heading: Other requests
paragraph: (b) members, officers and employees of any government agency, whether federal, provincial or territorial.

heading: Powers - Inquiries Act
paragraph: 85 For the purposes of sections 80 to 84, the Regulator has all the powers of commissioners under Part I of the Inquiries Act.

heading: Use of government agencies
paragraph: 86 In exercising its powers and performing its duties and functions under sections 80 to 84, the Regulator must, to the extent that it is possible to do so, utilize agencies of the Government of Canada to obtain technical, economic and statistical information and advice.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 87 (1) The Regulator may, with the approval of the Treasury Board, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) providing for fees, levies or charges that are payable for the purpose of recovering all or a portion of any costs that the Regulator considers to be attributable to the carrying out of its mandate, including costs related to applications that are denied or withdrawn; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) providing for the manner of calculating those fees, levies or charges and their payment to the Regulator.

heading: Interest on late payments
paragraph: (2) A regulation made under subsection (1) may specify the rate of interest or the manner of calculating the rate of interest payable on any fee, levy or charge that is not paid on or before the date on which it is due and may specify the time from which interest is payable.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (3) Fees, levies or charges imposed under this section and any interest payable on them constitute a debt to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Service Fees Act
paragraph: 88 The Service Fees Act does not apply to the fees, levies and charges referred to in section 87.

heading: Definition of certified document
paragraph: 89 (1) In this section, certified document means a document purporting to be certified by an employee of the Regulator who is authorized by the Chief Executive Officer to certify documents for the purposes of this section and sealed with the Regulator's seal.

heading: Proof of documents - true copies
paragraph: (2) In any action or proceedings, a certified document that states that it is a true copy of all or any part of another document - including a minute, decision, document of authorization, order, instruction, book of reference, book entry, plan or drawing - is, without proof of the signature or of the official character of the person appearing to have signed the certified document, evidence

heading: Proof of documents - true copies
paragraph: (a) of the original document, or the part of it, that it purports to be a copy of;

heading: Proof of documents - true copies
paragraph: (b) that the original document, or the part of it, was made, given or issued under the authority of or deposited with the person named in it and was made, given, issued or deposited at the time stated in the certified copy, if a time is stated in it; and

heading: Proof of documents - true copies
paragraph: (c) that the original document, or the part of it, was signed, certified, attested or executed by the persons and in the manner shown in the certified copy.

heading: Proof of documents - documents issued by Regulator
paragraph: (3) In any action or proceedings, a certified document that states that a valid and subsisting document has or has not been issued by the Regulator to a person named in the certified document is evidence of the facts stated in it without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and without further proof.

heading: Compensation
paragraph: 90 (1) Directors and commissioners are considered to be employees for the purposes of the Government Employees Compensation Act and to be employed in the federal public administration for the purposes of any regulations made under section 9 of the Aeronautics Act.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, the Chief Executive Officer and employees of the Regulator are employees for the purposes of the Government Employees Compensation Act and are employed in the federal public administration for the purposes of any regulations made under section 9 of the Aeronautics Act.

heading: Public Service Superannuation Act
paragraph: 91 (1) Full-time commissioners are considered to be persons employed in the public service for the purposes of the Public Service Superannuation Act.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, directors and part-time commissioners are not persons employed in the public service for the purposes of the Public Service Superannuation Act.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, the Chief Executive Officer and employees of the Regulator are persons employed in the public service for the purposes of the Public Service Superannuation Act.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: 92 An order made or a direction given by the Commission, a designated officer or an inspection officer under this Act is not a statutory instrument as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Statutory Instruments Act if

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (a) the order or direction applies to a single person or entity;

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (b) the order or direction applies with respect to a single regulated facility or abandoned facility; or

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (c) the Commission, designated officer or inspection officer considers that the order or direction is required immediately for the safety or security of persons, regulated facilities or abandoned facilities or for the protection of property or the environment.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 93 The following definitions apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: compensable damage means the costs, losses and damages for which the Tribunal may award compensation. (dommages indemnisables)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: holder means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the holder of a certificate or permit issued under Part 3 or 4 in respect of a regulated facility;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person, company or other entity that is the subject of an order made under section 214 in respect of a pipeline;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a person, company or other entity authorized to operate a pipeline under a Special Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a company that has been granted leave under Part 3 to abandon a pipeline;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a person, company or other entity that has been granted leave under Part 4 to abandon an international power line or interprovincial power line; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) the holder of an authorization issued under Part 5 in respect of a work or activity. (titulaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Tribunal means a pipeline claims tribunal established under subsection 143(1). (Tribunal)

heading: Reasonable care
paragraph: 94 The holder must take all reasonable care to ensure the safety and security of persons, the safety and security of regulated facilities and abandoned facilities and the protection of property and the environment.

heading: Orders
paragraph: 95 (1) To promote the safety and security of the operation of a regulated facility, the Commission may, by order, direct the holder to repair, reconstruct or alter part of the regulated facility and direct that, until the work is done, that part of the regulated facility not be used or be used in accordance with any conditions specified by the Commission.

heading: Other measures
paragraph: (2) The Commission may, by order, direct any of the following persons or bodies to take measures in respect of a regulated facility, an abandoned facility or any work or activity authorized under Part 5 that the Commission considers necessary for the safety and security of persons, the safety and security of the regulated facility or abandoned facility or the protection of property or the environment:

heading: Other measures
paragraph: (a) an Indigenous governing body;

heading: Other measures
paragraph: (b) the holder or any other person;

heading: Other measures
paragraph: (c) the federal government or a federal Crown corporation;

heading: Other measures
paragraph: (d) a provincial government or a provincial Crown corporation;

heading: Other measures
paragraph: (e) a local authority.

heading: Measures to be taken
paragraph: (3) If a person or body does not comply with an order under subsection (2) or an order under section 109 in relation to an abandoned facility or to the abandonment of a pipeline, an offshore power line or any facility, equipment or system that is related to an offshore renewable energy project, the Commission may

heading: Measures to be taken
paragraph: (a) take any action or measure the Commission considers necessary;

heading: Measures to be taken
paragraph: (b) authorize an officer or employee, or class of officers or employees, of the Regulator to take the action or measure; or

heading: Measures to be taken
paragraph: (c) authorize a third party to take the action or measure.

heading: No liability
paragraph: (4) No action lies against the Regulator or an officer or employee of the Regulator or against a servant of the Crown, as those terms are defined in section 2 of the Crown Liability and Proceedings Act, in respect of any act or omission committed in taking an action or measure referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Third party liability
paragraph: (5) A third party that is authorized under subsection (3) to take an action or measure is not liable in respect of any act or omission committed in good faith in taking the action or measure.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 96 The Regulator may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the design, construction and operation of pipelines, international power lines and interprovincial power lines designated by an order made under section 261;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the abandonment of pipelines;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting surveillance or monitoring measures that, in relation to the activities referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b), are for the safety and security of persons and for the protection of property and the environment;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting abandoned facilities;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) requiring holders to have management systems in place and to comply with them; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) providing for the elements to be included in those management systems - including human or organizational factors - and respecting any criteria to be met by those management systems.

heading: Exemption orders
paragraph: 97 The Commission may make orders exempting holders, on any conditions that the Commission considers appropriate, from any or all provisions of a regulation made under section 96 or 312, in order to, among other things, ensure the safety and security of persons, the safety and security of regulated facilities or abandoned facilities or the protection of property or the environment.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 98 Without limiting the scope of the regulations that the Regulator may make under section 96, the Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) specifying requirements with respect to the monitoring of regulated facilities; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the actions or measures to be taken in preparation for, or in the case of, an unintended or uncontrolled release of oil, gas or any other commodity from a pipeline.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: 99 (1) Every person who contravenes an order made under subsection 95(1) or (2) or a regulation made under section 96 is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year or to both.

heading: Application of subsections 379(2) to (6)
paragraph: (2) Subsections 379(2) to (6) apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, to an offence referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Security regulations
paragraph: 100 (1) The Regulator may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, make regulations respecting the security of regulated facilities, including regulations respecting standards, plans and audits that are related to the security of regulated facilities and respecting cybersecurity matters that are related to regulated facilities and may, for that purpose, define what constitutes cybersecurity.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who contravenes any of the regulations made under subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year or to both.

heading: Application of subsections 379(2) to (6)
paragraph: (3) Subsections 379(2) to (6) apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, to the offence referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Abandoned facilities
paragraph: 101 (1) A person must not make contact with, alter or remove an abandoned facility unless they are authorized to do so in an order made under subsection (2).

heading: Order
paragraph: (2) A designated officer may make an order, subject to any conditions that the designated officer considers appropriate, authorizing a person to make contact with, alter or remove an abandoned facility.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (3) The Regulator may make regulations respecting the circumstances in which or conditions under which an order under subsection (2) is not necessary and the Commission may make orders respecting the circumstances in which or conditions under which an order under subsection (2) is not necessary.

heading: Designation of inspection officers
paragraph: 102 (1) The Chief Executive Officer may designate any person or member of any class of persons as an inspection officer to administer and enforce this Part, Parts 3 to 5 and section 335.

heading: Purposes of designation
paragraph: (2) The purposes for which an inspection officer may be designated are:

heading: Purposes of designation
paragraph: (a) to ensure the safety and security of persons;

heading: Purposes of designation
paragraph: (b) to ensure the safety and security of regulated facilities and abandoned facilities; and

heading: Purposes of designation
paragraph: (c) to ensure the protection of property and the environment.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: (3) The Regulator must provide every inspection officer designated under subsection (1) with a certificate of authority. That inspection officer must, if so requested, produce the certificate to the occupant or person in charge of a place referred to in subsection 103(1).

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: 103 (1) An inspection officer may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Part, any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335, or for a purpose referred to in subsection 102(2), enter a place in which the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: (a) there is anything to which this Part or any of Parts 3 to 5 applies, including a regulated facility or an abandoned facility;

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: (b) there has been carried on, is being carried on or is likely to be carried on any activity in respect of which this Part, any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335 applies; or

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: (c) there is any book, record, electronic data or other document relating to the application of this Part, any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335.

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (2) The inspection officer may, for that purpose,

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (a) examine anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (b) use any means of communication in the place or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (c) use any computer system in the place, or cause it to be used, to examine data contained in or available to it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (d) prepare a document, or cause one to be prepared, based on the data;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (e) make copies of any information contained in any books, records, electronic data or other documents or in computer systems and use any copying equipment in the place, or cause it to be used to make copies of the information;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (f) conduct tests or analyses of anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (g) take measurements or samples of anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (h) take photographs or make recordings or sketches of anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (i) remove anything from the place for examination or copying;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (j) direct any person to put any machinery, vehicle or equipment in the place into operation or to cease operating it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (k) prohibit or limit access to all or part of the place or to anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (l) direct the owner or person in charge of the place or a person at the place to establish their identity to the inspection officer's satisfaction or to stop or start an activity; or

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (m) direct the owner or a person having possession, care or control of anything in the place to not move it, or to restrict its movement, for as long as the inspection officer considers necessary.

heading: Compliance audit
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, the powers set out in subsection (2) include the power to conduct a compliance audit.

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (4) The owner or person in charge of the place and every person in the place must give all assistance that is reasonably required to enable the inspection officer to perform their duties and functions under this section and must provide any documents or information, and access to any data, that are reasonably required for that purpose.

heading: Persons accompanying
paragraph: (5) The inspection officer may be accompanied by any other person that they believe is necessary to help them perform their duties and functions under this section, and the person is not liable for doing so.

heading: Entry on private property
paragraph: (6) The inspection officer and any person accompanying them may enter private property - other than a dwelling-house or living quarters - and pass through it in order to gain entry to a place referred to in subsection (1) and the person is not liable for doing so. For greater certainty, no person has a right to object to that use of the property and no warrant is required for the entry, unless the property is a dwelling-house or living quarters.

heading: Warrant to enter dwelling-house or living quarters
paragraph: 104 (1) If the place is a dwelling-house or living quarters, the inspection officer may enter it without the occupant's consent only under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (2).

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (2) On ex parte application, a justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing the inspection officer to enter a dwelling-house or living quarters, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) the dwelling-house or living quarters is a place referred to in subsection 103(1);

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) entry to the dwelling-house or living quarters is necessary for a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Part, any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335, or for a purpose referred to in subsection 102(2); and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (c) entry was refused by the occupant or there are reasonable grounds to believe that entry will be refused by, or that consent to entry cannot be obtained from, the occupant.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (3) In executing a warrant to enter a dwelling-house or living quarters, an inspection officer may use force only if the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant and they are accompanied by a peace officer.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: 105 No action or other proceeding of a civil nature lies against an inspection officer in respect of anything that is done or omitted to be done in good faith while exercising their powers or performing their duties and functions under this Part.

heading: Prohibition - obstruction
paragraph: 106 It is prohibited to obstruct or hinder an inspection officer who is exercising their powers or performing their duties and functions under this Part.

heading: Prohibition - false statements or information
paragraph: 107 It is prohibited to knowingly make a false or misleading statement or knowingly provide false or misleading information in connection with any matter under this Part, any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335 to any inspection officer who is exercising their powers or performing their duties and functions under this Part.

heading: Notice of non-compliance
paragraph: 108 (1) If an inspection officer has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has contravened this Part, any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335, he or she may issue a notice of non-compliance to the person.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (2) A notice must be made in writing and must set out

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (a) the name of the person to whom the notice is directed;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (b) the provision of this Part, any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335 or any of their regulations that is alleged to have been contravened, the order or decision that is alleged to have been contravened, or the condition of any certificate, order or decision, permit or authorization, leave or exemption that is alleged to have been contravened;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (c) the relevant facts surrounding the alleged contravention; and

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (d) the period within which the person may provide comments in response to the notice.

heading: Grounds for making order
paragraph: 109 (1) If an inspection officer who is expressly authorized by the Chief Executive Officer to make orders under this section has reasonable grounds to believe that there is or is likely to be a contravention of this Part or any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335, or for a purpose referred to in subsection 102(2), the inspection officer may, by order, direct a person to

heading: Grounds for making order
paragraph: (a) stop doing something that is in contravention of this Part or any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335 or cause it to be stopped;

heading: Grounds for making order
paragraph: (b) take any measure that is necessary in order to comply with this Part or any of Parts 3 to 5 or section 335 or mitigate the effects of non-compliance;

heading: Grounds for making order
paragraph: (c) stop doing something that may cause a hazard to the safety or security of persons, or damage to property or the environment or cause it to be stopped; or

heading: Grounds for making order
paragraph: (d) take any measure that is necessary to prevent or mitigate the hazard to the safety or security of persons or damage to property or the environment.

heading: Terms of order
paragraph: (2) The order may require work associated with a facility, including a regulated facility, abandoned facility or ground disturbance to be suspended until the hazardous or detrimental situation has been remedied to the satisfaction of an inspection officer or the order is stayed or rescinded.

heading: Notice and report
paragraph: (3) An inspection officer who makes an order under this section must, as soon as possible,

heading: Notice and report
paragraph: (a) give written notice of the order to the person to whom it is directed, including the terms of the order and a statement of the reasons for the order; and

heading: Notice and report
paragraph: (b) report the circumstances and terms of the order to the Commission.

heading: Effect of appeal
paragraph: 110 For greater certainty, an appeal before the Commission from an order made under section 109 does not operate as a stay of the order, but the Commission may grant a stay pending the outcome of the appeal.

heading: Information confidential
paragraph: 111 An inspection officer must not disclose to any person any information regarding any secret process or trade secret obtained while performing duties and functions under this Part, except for the purposes of this Part or as required by law.

heading: Offence and punishment - duty to assist and orders
paragraph: 112 (1) Every person who contravenes subsection 103(4) or fails to comply with an order under section 109 is guilty of an offence and is liable

heading: Offence and punishment - duty to assist and orders
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment - duty to assist and orders
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year or to both.

heading: Defence - no notice
paragraph: (2) A person must not be found guilty of an offence for failing to comply with an order under section 109 unless the person was given written notice of the order in accordance with paragraph 109(3)(a).

heading: Offence and punishment - obstruction
paragraph: (3) Every person who contravenes section 106 is guilty of an offence punishable on summary conviction and is liable, for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $100,000 and, for any subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $300,000.

heading: Application of subsections 379(2) to (6)
paragraph: (4) Subsections 379(2) to (6) apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, in respect of an offence under subsections (1) and (3).

heading: Offence and punishment - false statements or information
paragraph: (5) Every person who contravenes section 107 is guilty of an offence punishable on summary conviction and is liable to a fine of not more than $300,000.

heading: Application of subsections 379(3) to (6)
paragraph: (6) Subsections 379(3) to (6) apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, in respect of an offence under subsection (5).

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 113 (1) The following definitions apply in this section.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: coroner includes any medical examiner or other person carrying out the duties and functions of a coroner. (coroner)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: recording means the whole or any part of either a recording of voice communications originating from, or received on or in, a regulated facility, or a video recording of the activities of the operating personnel of the regulated facility, which recording of voice communications or video recording is made, using recording equipment to which the operating personnel does not have access, in a place where operations of the facility are carried out and includes a transcript or substantial summary of such a recording. (enregistrement)

heading: Privilege for recordings
paragraph: (2) Every recording is privileged and, except as provided by this section, a person, including any person to whom access is provided under this section, must not

heading: Privilege for recordings
paragraph: (a) knowingly communicate a recording or permit it to be communicated to any person; or

heading: Privilege for recordings
paragraph: (b) be required to produce a recording or give evidence relating to it in any legal, disciplinary or other proceedings.

heading: Access by Regulator
paragraph: (3) Any recording that relates to an accident that is the subject of an inquiry under subsection 32(2) must be released to the Regulator on request for the purposes of the inquiry.

heading: Use by Regulator
paragraph: (4) The Regulator may make any use of any recording obtained under this Act that it considers necessary for the purposes of the inquiry under subsection 32(2), but, subject to subsection (5), must not knowingly communicate or permit to be communicated to anyone any portion of it that is unrelated to the inquiry.

heading: Access by peace officers, coroners and other investigators
paragraph: (5) The Regulator must make available any recording obtained under this Act to

heading: Access by peace officers, coroners and other investigators
paragraph: (a) a coroner who requests access to it for the purpose of an investigation that the coroner is conducting;

heading: Access by peace officers, coroners and other investigators
paragraph: (b) any person carrying out an inquiry under subsection 32(2); or

heading: Access by peace officers, coroners and other investigators
paragraph: (c) any person carrying out a coordinated investigation referred to in the Canadian Transportation Accident Investigation and Safety Board Act.

heading: Power of court or coroner
paragraph: (6) Despite any other provision of this section, if, in any proceedings before a court or coroner, a request for the production and discovery of a recording is made, the court or coroner must cause notice of the request to be given to the Regulator, if the Regulator is not a party to the proceedings and, in camera, examine the recording and give the Regulator a reasonable opportunity to make representations with respect to it. If the court or coroner concludes in the circumstances of the case that the public interest in the proper administration of justice outweighs in importance the privilege attached to the recording by virtue of this section, the court or coroner must order the production and discovery of the recording, subject to any restrictions or conditions that the court or coroner considers appropriate, and may require any person to give evidence that relates to the recording.

heading: Use prohibited
paragraph: (7) A recording is not to be used against agents or employees who are directly or indirectly involved in the operation of a regulated facility in disciplinary proceedings, in proceedings relating to their capacity or competence to perform their functions, or in legal or other proceedings.

heading: Definition of court
paragraph: (8) For the purposes of subsection (6), court includes any person appointed or designated to conduct a public inquiry into a pipeline occurrence, within the meaning of section 2 of the Canadian Transportation Accident Investigation and Safety Board Act, under the Inquiries Act.

heading: Voluntary reporting
paragraph: 114 (1) The Regulator may, subject to the approval of the Governor in Council, make regulations for the establishment and administration of systems for the voluntary reporting to the Regulator of alleged non-compliance with this Act.

heading: Use by Regulator
paragraph: (2) The Regulator may, subject to this section, make any use of any report made to it in accordance with regulations made under subsection (1) that it considers necessary for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Rules for protection of identity
paragraph: (3) Regulations made under subsection (1) may include rules for the protection of the identity of persons who make a report.

heading: Certain information privileged
paragraph: (4) Where the identity of a person who has made a report to the Regulator in accordance with regulations made under subsection (1) is protected by rules referred to in subsection (3), information that could reasonably be expected to reveal that identity is privileged, and a person must not

heading: Certain information privileged
paragraph: (a) knowingly communicate it or permit it to be communicated to any person; or

heading: Certain information privileged
paragraph: (b) be required to produce it or give evidence relating to it in any legal, disciplinary or other proceedings.

heading: Use prohibited
paragraph: (5) A report made to the Regulator under a voluntary reporting system established by regulations made under subsection (1) must not be used against the person who made the report in any legal, disciplinary or other proceedings if the person's identity is protected by rules referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 115 (1) The Regulator may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) designating as a violation that may be proceeded with in accordance with this Act

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) the contravention of any specified provision of this Act or the regulations,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii) the contravention of any order or decision, or of any order or decision of any specified class of orders or decisions, made under this Act, or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (iii) the failure to comply with any condition of

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (A) any certificate, licence, permit or authorization, or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (B) any leave or exemption granted under this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the determination of or the method of determining the amount payable as the penalty, which may be different for individuals and other persons, for each violation; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the service of documents required or authorized under section 120, 125 or 128, including the manner and proof of service and the circumstances under which documents are considered to be served.

heading: Maximum amount of penalty
paragraph: (2) The amount that may be determined under any regulations made under paragraph (1)(b) as the penalty for a violation must not be more than $25,000, in the case of an individual, and $100,000, in the case of any other person.

heading: Powers of Regulator
paragraph: 116 (1) The Regulator may

heading: Powers of Regulator
paragraph: (a) establish the form of notices of violation; and

heading: Powers of Regulator
paragraph: (b) establish, in respect of each violation, a short-form description to be used in notices of violation.

heading: Powers of Commission
paragraph: (1.1) The Commission may designate persons or classes of persons to conduct reviews under section 128.

heading: Powers of Chief Executive Officer
paragraph: (2) The Chief Executive Officer may designate persons or classes of persons who are authorized to issue notices of violation.

heading: Commission of violation
paragraph: 117 (1) Every person who contravenes or fails to comply with a provision, order, decision or condition designated under paragraph 115(1)(a) commits a violation and is liable to a penalty of an amount to be determined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Purpose of penalty
paragraph: (2) The purpose of the penalty is to promote compliance with this Act and not to punish.

heading: Liability of directors, officers, etc.
paragraph: 118 If a corporation commits a violation, any director, officer or agent or mandatary of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the violation is a party to the violation and is liable to a penalty of an amount to be determined in accordance with the regulations, whether or not the corporation has been proceeded against in accordance with this Act.

heading: Proof of violation
paragraph: 119 In any proceedings under this Act against a person in relation to a violation, it is sufficient proof of the violation to establish that it was committed by an employee or agent or mandatary of the person, whether or not the employee or agent or mandatary is identified or proceeded against in accordance with this Act.

heading: Issuance and service of notice of violation
paragraph: 120 (1) If a person designated under subsection 116(2) has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has committed a violation, the designated person may issue a notice of violation and cause it to be served on the person.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The notice of violation must

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) name the person that is believed to have committed the violation;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) set out the relevant facts surrounding the violation;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) set out the amount of the penalty for the violation;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) inform the person of their right to request a review with respect to the violation or the amount of the penalty, and of the period referred to in section 125 within which that right must be exercised;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) inform the person of the manner of paying the penalty set out in the notice; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (f) inform the person that, if they do not pay the penalty or exercise their right referred to in paragraph (d), they will be considered to have committed the violation and that they are liable to the penalty set out in the notice.

heading: Certain defences not available
paragraph: 121 (1) A person named in a notice of violation does not have a defence by reason that the person

heading: Certain defences not available
paragraph: (a) exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the violation; or

heading: Certain defences not available
paragraph: (b) reasonably and honestly believed in the existence of facts that, if true, would exonerate the person.

heading: Common law principles
paragraph: (2) Every rule and principle of the common law that makes any circumstance a justification or excuse in relation to a charge for an offence under this Act applies in respect of a violation to the extent that it is not inconsistent with this Act.

heading: Continuing violation
paragraph: 122 A violation that is committed or continued on more than one day constitutes a separate violation for each day on which it is committed or continued.

heading: Violation or offence
paragraph: 123 (1) Proceeding with any act or omission as a violation under this Act precludes proceeding with it as an offence under this Act, and proceeding with it as an offence under this Act precludes proceeding with it as a violation under this Act.

heading: Violations not offences
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, a violation is not an offence and, accordingly, section 126 of the Criminal Code does not apply in respect of a violation.

heading: Limitation period or prescription
paragraph: 124 No notice of violation in respect of a violation may be issued more than two years from the day on which the subject matter of the violation arises.

heading: Right to request review
paragraph: 125 A person who is served with a notice of violation may, within 30 days after the day on which it is served, or within any longer period that the Commission allows, make a request to the Commission for a review of the amount of the penalty or the facts of the violation, or both.

heading: Correction or cancellation of notice of violation
paragraph: 126 At any time before a request for a review in respect of a notice of violation is received by the Commission, a person designated under subsection 116(2) may cancel the notice of violation or correct an error in it.

heading: Review
paragraph: 127 (1) On receipt of a request made under section 125, the Commission must conduct the review or cause the review to be conducted by a person designated under subsection 116(1.1).

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) The Commission must conduct the review if the notice of violation was issued by a person designated under subsection 116(1.1).

heading: Object of review
paragraph: 128 (1) The Commission or the person conducting the review must determine, as the case may be, whether the amount of the penalty for the violation was determined in accordance with the regulations or whether the person committed the violation, or both.

heading: Determination
paragraph: (2) The Commission or the person conducting the review must make a determination in writing and cause the person who requested the review to be served with a copy of the determination and the reasons for it.

heading: Correction of penalty
paragraph: (3) If the Commission or the person conducting the review determines that the amount of the penalty for the violation was not determined in accordance with the regulations, the Commission or the person, as the case may be, must correct the amount of the penalty.

heading: Responsibility
paragraph: (4) If the Commission or the person conducting the review determines that the person who requested the review committed the violation, the person who requested the review is liable to the penalty as set out in the determination.

heading: Determination final
paragraph: (5) Despite subsection 69(1) and (2), a determination made under this section is final and binding and, except for judicial review under the Federal Courts Act, is not subject to appeal or to review by any court.

heading: Federal Court
paragraph: (6) Despite section 28 of the Federal Courts Act, the Federal Court has exclusive original jurisdiction to hear and determine an application for judicial review of a determination made under this section by the Commission.

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: 129 If the facts of a violation are reviewed, the person who issued the notice of violation must establish, on a balance of probabilities, that the person named in it committed the violation identified in it.

heading: Payment
paragraph: 130 If a person pays the penalty set out in a notice of violation, the person is considered to have committed the violation and proceedings in respect of it are ended.

heading: Failure to act
paragraph: 131 A person that neither pays the penalty imposed under this Act nor requests a review within the period referred to in section 125 is considered to have committed the violation and is liable to the penalty.

heading: Debts to Her Majesty
paragraph: 132 (1) A penalty constitutes a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered as such in the Federal Court or any other court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Limitation period or prescription
paragraph: (2) Proceedings to recover the debt may be instituted no later than the fifth anniversary of the day on which the debt becomes payable.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: 133 (1) The Commission may issue a certificate of non-payment certifying the unpaid amount of any debt referred to in subsection 132(1).

heading: Registration in Federal Court
paragraph: (2) Registration in the Federal Court or in any other court of competent jurisdiction of a certificate of non-payment issued under subsection (1) has the same effect as a judgment of that court for a debt of the amount specified in the certificate and all related registration costs.

heading: Admissibility of documents
paragraph: 134 In the absence of evidence to the contrary, a document that appears to be a notice issued under subsection 120(1) is presumed to be authentic and is proof of its contents in any proceeding in respect of a violation.

heading: Publication
paragraph: 135 The Regulator may make public the nature of a violation, the name of the person who committed it and the amount of the penalty.

heading: Purpose
paragraph: 136 The purpose of sections 137 to 142 is to reinforce the "polluter pays" principle by, among other things, imposing financial requirements on any company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate a pipeline.

heading: Recovery of loss, damage, costs, expenses
paragraph: 137 (1) If an unintended or uncontrolled release from a pipeline of oil, gas or any other commodity occurs, all persons to whose fault or negligence the release is attributable or who are by law responsible for others to whose fault or negligence the release is attributable are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for

heading: Recovery of loss, damage, costs, expenses
paragraph: (a) all actual loss or damage incurred by any person as a result of the release or as a result of any action or measure taken in relation to the release;

heading: Recovery of loss, damage, costs, expenses
paragraph: (b) the costs and expenses reasonably incurred by Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province, any Indigenous governing body or any other person in taking any action or measure in relation to the release; and

heading: Recovery of loss, damage, costs, expenses
paragraph: (c) all loss of non-use value relating to a public resource that is affected by the release or by any action or measure taken in relation to the release.

heading: Contribution based on degree of fault
paragraph: (2) The persons who are at fault or negligent or who are by law responsible for persons who are at fault or negligent are liable to make contributions to each other or to indemnify each other in the degree to which they are respectively at fault or negligent.

heading: Vicarious liability
paragraph: (3) The company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate the pipeline from which the release occurred is jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable with any contractor - to whose fault or negligence the release is attributable - that performs work for the company for the actual loss or damage, the costs and expenses and the loss of non-use value, described in paragraphs (1)(a) to (c).

heading: Absolute liability
paragraph: (4) If an unintended or uncontrolled release of oil, gas or any other commodity from a pipeline occurs, the company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate that pipeline is liable, without proof of fault or negligence, up to the applicable limit of liability that is set out in subsection (5) for the actual loss or damage, the costs and expenses and the loss of non-use value, described in paragraphs (1)(a) to (c).

heading: Limits of liability
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of subsection (4), the limits of liability are,

heading: Limits of liability
paragraph: (a) in respect of a company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate one or more pipelines that individually or in the aggregate have the capacity to transport at least 250,000 barrels of oil per day, $1 billion or, if a greater amount is prescribed by the regulations, that amount; and

heading: Limits of liability
paragraph: (b) in respect of a company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate any other pipeline, the amount prescribed by the regulations.

heading: Regulations - limits of liability
paragraph: (6) The Governor in Council may, by regulation, on the Minister's recommendation,

heading: Regulations - limits of liability
paragraph: (a) prescribe an amount greater than $1 billion for the purposes of paragraph (5)(a); and

heading: Regulations - limits of liability
paragraph: (b) prescribe an amount for the purposes of paragraph (5)(b) in respect of a company or class of companies.

heading: Liability under another law - subsection (4)
paragraph: (7) If a company is liable under subsection (4) with respect to a release and it is also liable under any other Act, without proof of fault or negligence, for that release, the company is liable up to the greater of the limit of liability referred to in subsection (5) that applies to it and the limit up to which it is liable under the other Act. If the other Act does not set out a limit of liability, the limits referred to in subsection (5) do not apply.

heading: Costs and expenses not recoverable under Fisheries Act
paragraph: (8) The costs and expenses that are recoverable by Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province under this section are not recoverable under subsection 42(1) of the Fisheries Act.

heading: Proceedings - loss of non-use value
paragraph: (9) Only Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province may institute proceedings to recover a loss of non-use value described in paragraph (1)(c).

heading: Claims
paragraph: (10) All claims under this section may be sued for and recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction in Canada. Claims in favour of persons incurring actual loss or damage described in paragraph (1)(a) are to be distributed pro rata and rank in priority over claims for costs and expenses described in paragraph (1)(b), and the claims for costs and expenses rank in priority over claims to recover a loss of non-use value described in paragraph (1)(c).

heading: Saving
paragraph: (11) Subject to subsections (8) and (9), nothing in this section suspends or limits

heading: Saving
paragraph: (a) any legal liability or remedy for an act or omission by reason only that the act or omission is an offence under this Act or gives rise to liability under this section;

heading: Saving
paragraph: (b) any recourse, indemnity or relief available at law to a person who is liable under this section against any other person; or

heading: Saving
paragraph: (c) the operation of any applicable law or rule of law that is consistent with this section.

heading: Limitation period or prescription
paragraph: (12) Proceedings in respect of claims under this section may be instituted no later than the third anniversary of the day on which the loss, damage or costs and expenses were incurred but in no case after the sixth anniversary of the day on which the release occurred.

heading: Financial resources
paragraph: 138 (1) A company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate a pipeline must maintain the amount of financial resources necessary to pay the amount of the limit of liability referred to in subsection 137(5) that applies to it or, if the Commission specifies a greater amount, that amount.

heading: Types of financial resources
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations made under subsection (7), the Commission may, by order, direct a company, either individually or as a member of a class of companies authorized under this Act to construct or operate a pipeline, to maintain the amount of financial resources that is referred to in subsection (1) of the types of financial resources that the Commission specifies, including types that must be readily accessible to the company and, if the Commission specifies types of financial resources, it may specify the amount that the company is required to maintain of each type.

heading: Duty to satisfy Commission
paragraph: (3) At the Commission's request, the company must satisfy the Commission that it meets the requirement to maintain the amount of financial resources referred to in subsection (1) and that it complies with any order made under subsection (2). The Commission may consider, among other things, the company's financial statements, letters of credit, guarantees, bonds or suretyships and insurance.

heading: Greater amount
paragraph: (4) The Commission may, by order, specify an amount for the purposes of subsection (1).

heading: Loss of non-use value
paragraph: (5) When the Commission specifies an amount for the purposes of subsection (1), it is not required to consider any potential loss of non-use value relating to a public resource that is affected by an unintended or uncontrolled release of oil, gas or any other commodity from a pipeline or by any action or measure taken in relation to the release.

heading: Continuing obligation
paragraph: (6) A company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate a pipeline must maintain the amount of financial resources referred to in subsection (1) and must comply with any order made under subsection (2) and any regulation made under subsection (7) only until it obtains leave from the Commission to abandon the operation of its pipeline.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (7) The Governor in Council may, on the Minister's recommendation, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) providing for the types of financial resources from which the Commission may choose if it specifies types of financial resources under subsection (2), including those from which the Commission may choose if it specifies types of financial resources that must be readily accessible to the company; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the amount of financial resources that must be readily accessible to a company individually or as a member of a class of companies.

heading: Pooled fund
paragraph: 139 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a company may meet all or a portion of its financial requirements under subsection 138(1) by participating in a pooled fund that is established by companies authorized under this Act to construct or operate a pipeline, that meets the requirements established by the regulations and from which the Regulator may withdraw any amount under subsection 141(6).

heading: Difference
paragraph: (2) If a company meets only a portion of its financial requirements by participating in a pooled fund and the amount of funds in the pooled fund to which it has access - in the event that there is an unintended or uncontrolled release of oil, gas or any other commodity from a pipeline that the company is authorized under this Act to construct or operate - is less than the amount of financial resources referred to in subsection 138(1), the company must maintain an amount equal to the difference between those amounts.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council may, on the Minister's recommendation, make regulations respecting a pooled fund referred to in subsection (1), including regulations specifying

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) the minimum amount of the pooled fund and the minimum amount of the pooled fund that must be readily accessible;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) any condition that a company must meet in order to participate in the pooled fund, including the minimum amount that a company must contribute to the pooled fund;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) the maximum amount that a company may withdraw from the pooled fund; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) the maximum portion of a company's financial requirements that may be met by participating in the pooled fund.

heading: Reimbursement -  measures taken by government institution
paragraph: 140 If an unintended or uncontrolled release of oil, gas or any other commodity from a pipeline occurs, the Commission may, by order, direct the company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate that pipeline to reimburse any federal, provincial or municipal government institution, any Indigenous governing body or any person for the costs and expenses that the Commission considers reasonable that they incurred in taking any reasonable action or measure in relation to the release, even if the costs and expenses are more than the amount of the limit of liability referred to in subsection 137(5) that applies to that company.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 141 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the Minister's recommendation, designate any company that is authorized under this Act to construct or operate a pipeline from which an unintended or uncontrolled release of oil, gas or any other commodity has occurred if

heading: Designation
paragraph: (a) the Governor in Council considers that the company does not have or is not likely to have the financial resources necessary to pay

heading: Designation
paragraph: (i) the costs and expenses incurred, or to be incurred, in taking any action or measure in relation to the release, and

heading: Designation
paragraph: (ii) the compensation that might be awarded for compensable damage caused by the release; or

heading: Designation
paragraph: (b) the company does not comply with an order of the Commission with respect to any action or measure to be taken in relation to the release.

heading: Measures to be taken
paragraph: (2) If the Governor in Council designates a company under subsection (1), the Regulator or any of its officers or employees - or class of officers or employees - that the Regulator authorizes may take any action or measure that they consider necessary in relation to the release or they may authorize a third party to take any action or measure.

heading: No liability
paragraph: (3) No action lies against the Regulator or an officer or employee of the Regulator or against a servant of the Crown, as those terms are defined in section 2 of the Crown Liability and Proceedings Act, in respect of any act or omission committed in taking any action or measure in relation to the release.

heading: Third party liability
paragraph: (4) A third party that is authorized under subsection (2) to take any action or measure referred to in that subsection is not liable in respect of any act or omission committed in good faith in taking the action or measure.

heading: Reimbursement -  measures taken by government institution
paragraph: (5) If the Governor in Council designates a company under subsection (1), the Regulator may reimburse any federal, provincial or municipal government institution, any Indigenous governing body or any person the costs and expenses that the Regulator considers reasonable that they incurred in taking any reasonable action or measure in relation to the release.

heading: Withdrawal from pooled fund
paragraph: (6) If the Governor in Council designates a company under subsection (1) and that company participates in a pooled fund described in subsection 139(1), the Regulator may withdraw any amount from the pooled fund that is necessary to pay the costs and expenses incurred in taking any action or measure under subsection (2) and to reimburse the costs and expenses referred to in subsection (5).

heading: Regulations imposing fees, etc.
paragraph: 142 (1) Subject to the Treasury Board's approval, the Regulator must, for the purposes of recovering the amounts paid out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund under subsection 171(1), even if those amounts are more than the amount of the limit of liability referred to in subsection 137(5) that applies to a designated company, make regulations

heading: Regulations imposing fees, etc.
paragraph: (a) imposing fees, levies or charges on a designated company and, if the amount recovered from the designated company is not sufficient to recover the amounts paid out, imposing fees, levies or charges on companies that are authorized under this Act to construct or operate pipelines that transport the same commodity or a commodity of the same class as the commodity that was released from a pipeline constructed or operated by the designated company; and

heading: Regulations imposing fees, etc.
paragraph: (b) prescribing the manner of calculating the fees, levies and charges and their payment to the Regulator.

heading: Interest on late payments
paragraph: (2) A regulation made under subsection (1) may specify the rate of interest or the manner of calculating the rate of interest payable by a company either individually or as a member of a class of companies on any fee, levy or charge not paid by the company on or before the date it is due and the time from which interest is payable.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (3) Fees, levies or charges imposed under this section and any interest payable on them constitute a debt that is due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Establishment of Tribunal
paragraph: 143 (1) The Governor in Council may, by order, after a designation is made under subsection 141(1), establish a pipeline claims tribunal whose purpose is to examine and adjudicate, as expeditiously as the circumstances and considerations of fairness permit, the claims for compensation made under this Act in relation to the release that occurred from the designated company's pipeline and specify the location of its head office.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (2) However, the Governor in Council may establish a pipeline claims tribunal only if, having regard to the extent of the compensable damage caused by the release, the estimated cost of paying compensation in respect of that damage and the advantages of having claims dealt with by an administrative tribunal, the Governor in Council considers it in the public interest to do so.

heading: Claims treated equitably
paragraph: (3) A Tribunal must exercise its powers and perform its duties and functions with respect to claims for compensation in an equitable manner, without discrimination on the basis of nationality or residence.

heading: Jurisdiction of courts
paragraph: 144 For greater certainty, nothing in sections 143 and 145 to 173 is to be construed as restricting the jurisdiction of a court of competent jurisdiction with respect to the release referred to in subsection 143(1).

heading: Public notice
paragraph: 145 Immediately after a Tribunal is established, the Regulator must notify the public, in a manner that the Tribunal considers appropriate, of the Tribunal's purpose and the manner in which to obtain information on making a claim for compensation and must publish in the Canada Gazette a notice setting out that purpose and the manner in which to obtain that information.

heading: Members of Tribunal
paragraph: 146 (1) A Tribunal is to have at least three members, each of whom is to be appointed by the Governor in Council, on the Minister's recommendation, to hold office for a term of not more than five years.

heading: Members' qualifications
paragraph: (2) The members of the Tribunal are to be appointed from among persons who are retired judges of a superior court or members of at least 10 years standing at either the bar of a province or the Chambre des notaires du Quebec.

heading: Replacing member
paragraph: (3) If a member is absent or becomes incapacitated, resigns or dies, the Governor in Council may appoint a replacement for that member.

heading: Remuneration
paragraph: (4) The Regulator must pay the members the remuneration and expenses that are fixed by the Governor in Council.

heading: Tenure
paragraph: 147 (1) Each member of a Tribunal is to hold office during good behaviour, but may be removed by the Governor in Council for cause.

heading: Termination of Tribunal
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may terminate the appointment of the members of the Tribunal if the Governor in Council is satisfied that the Tribunal has no work to carry out.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: 148 No action lies against any member of a Tribunal for anything done or omitted to be done by the member in the exercise or purported exercise of a power or in the performance or purported performance of a duty or function of the Tribunal.

heading: Chairperson
paragraph: 149 (1) The Governor in Council must, on the Minister's recommendation, designate one of the members of a Tribunal to be the Chairperson of the Tribunal.

heading: Chairperson's powers, duties and functions
paragraph: (2) The Chairperson apportions work among the members of the Tribunal and, if he or she establishes a panel, assigns members to the panel and designates a member to preside over it. The Chairperson also has supervision over and direction of the work of the Tribunal's staff.

heading: Staff
paragraph: 150 A Tribunal may employ the staff that it considers necessary for the proper exercise of its powers and performance of its duties and functions, prescribe their duties and, subject to any regulations, the conditions of their employment and, with the Treasury Board's approval, fix their remuneration.

heading: Technical or specialized knowledge
paragraph: 151 A Tribunal may engage, on a temporary basis, the services of counsel or notaries and other persons having technical or specialized knowledge to assist it in its work, prescribe their duties and the conditions of their employment and, with the Treasury Board's approval, fix their remuneration and expenses.

heading: Payment by Regulator
paragraph: 152 The Regulator must pay the remuneration and expenses referred to in sections 150 and 151.

heading: Staff and facilities
paragraph: 153 The Regulator must provide a Tribunal with any professional, technical, secretarial, clerical and other assistance and any facilities and supplies that the Regulator considers necessary to enable the Tribunal to exercise its powers and perform its duties and functions.

heading: Hearings
paragraph: 154 A Tribunal must conduct its hearings in Canada on the dates and at the times and locations that it considers appropriate.

heading: Powers
paragraph: 155 (1) A Tribunal has all the powers, rights and privileges vested in a superior court with respect to any matters within its jurisdiction, including the attendance, swearing and examination of witnesses, the production and inspection of documents and the enforcement of its orders.

heading: Evidence at hearings
paragraph: (2) The Tribunal is not, in the hearing of any matter, bound by the legal rules of evidence. However, it must not receive as evidence anything that would be inadmissible in a court by reason of any privilege under the law of evidence.

heading: Examinations
paragraph: 156 For the purposes of adjudicating a claim for compensation or an application for reconsideration, a Tribunal may require a claimant or applicant to undergo medical or other examinations that the Tribunal considers reasonably necessary.

heading: Frivolous or vexatious claims
paragraph: 157 A Tribunal may refuse to hear any claim for compensation or application for reconsideration that it considers to be frivolous or vexatious.

heading: Written submissions
paragraph: 158 A Tribunal may examine and adjudicate any claim for compensation or application for reconsideration based only on written submissions.

heading: Rules
paragraph: 159 A Tribunal may make the rules that it considers necessary for the exercise of its powers and the performance of its duties and functions, including rules respecting

heading: Rules
paragraph: (a) procedures for making a claim for compensation and those for making an application for reconsideration;

heading: Rules
paragraph: (b) the information that must be included with a claim for compensation or an application for reconsideration;

heading: Rules
paragraph: (c) the conduct of its examination of claims for compensation and applications for reconsideration, including the conduct of its hearings;

heading: Rules
paragraph: (d) the form and manner in which evidence must be submitted; and

heading: Rules
paragraph: (e) a quorum.

heading: Application
paragraph: 160 (1) Any person, partnership or unincorporated organization or federal, provincial or municipal government or any Indigenous governing body may, within the prescribed period, make to a Tribunal a claim for compensation for compensable damage caused by the release that occurred from a designated company's pipeline.

heading: Panel
paragraph: (2) As soon as feasible after the day on which the claim is made, the Chairperson must

heading: Panel
paragraph: (a) assign the claim to the Tribunal;

heading: Panel
paragraph: (b) establish a panel of the Tribunal and assign the claim to that panel; or

heading: Panel
paragraph: (c) assign the claim to an existing panel.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) The Chairperson must notify the claimant, the designated company and the Regulator that the claim has been assigned.

heading: Powers, duties and functions
paragraph: (4) A panel has the powers, other than the power described in section 159, and the duties and functions of the Tribunal with respect to any claim for compensation that is before that panel.

heading: Public hearings
paragraph: 161 Tribunal hearings are to be held in public. However, a Tribunal may hold all or part of a hearing in private if it considers that

heading: Public hearings
paragraph: (a) a public hearing would not be in the public interest;

heading: Public hearings
paragraph: (b) a person's privacy interest outweighs the principle that hearings be open to the public; or

heading: Public hearings
paragraph: (c) confidential business information may be disclosed.

heading: Interim award of compensation
paragraph: 162 If it is authorized to do so by the regulations, a Tribunal may award interim compensation in respect of a claim for compensation. If the Tribunal awards interim compensation, it must advise the Regulator, by notice, of the amount awarded.

heading: Determining compensation
paragraph: 163 (1) A Tribunal must decide whether to award a claimant compensation for the compensable damage that is referred to in their claim for compensation. If it decides to award compensation, it must, having regard to any other amount of compensation that the claimant has been paid for that damage, determine the amount of compensation in accordance with the regulations and, if it is authorized by the regulations to award costs with respect to a claimant's claim for compensation and it decides to do so, it must determine the amount of those costs.

heading: Notice - decision
paragraph: (2) The Tribunal must advise the claimant and the designated company, by notice, of its decision with respect to the claim for compensation and, if compensation or costs are awarded, it must also advise the Regulator by that notice.

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (3) The notice must indicate

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (a) the amount of any compensation or costs determined under subsection (1);

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (b) any reduction in the amount of compensation provided for by the regulations; and

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (c) any amounts that have already been paid to the claimant for the compensable damage that is referred to in their claim.

heading: Amount to be paid
paragraph: 164 (1) The Regulator must, subject to section 165 and within the prescribed period, pay to the claimant

heading: Amount to be paid
paragraph: (a) the amount of interim compensation indicated in the notice referred to in section 162;

heading: Amount to be paid
paragraph: (b) subject to the regulations, the amount of compensation and costs indicated in the notice referred to in subsection 163(2) and any interest payable; and

heading: Amount to be paid
paragraph: (c) if the amount of compensation and costs indicated in the notice referred to in subsection 169(2) is more than the amount paid by the Regulator under paragraph (b), subject to the regulations, an amount equal to the difference between those amounts.

heading: Interest on claim
paragraph: (2) If the regulations provide for interest with respect to a claim for compensation, the interest accrues at the rate prescribed under the Income Tax Act for amounts payable by the Minister of National Revenue as refunds of overpayments of tax under that Act that are in effect from time to time.

heading: Fees and travel expenses
paragraph: (3) If it is authorized to do so by the regulations, a Tribunal may, in accordance with the regulations, award fees and travel expenses. If the Tribunal awards fees and travel expenses, it must advise the Regulator, by notice, of the amount awarded and the Regulator must pay that amount.

heading: Total amount
paragraph: 165 The total amount that the Regulator pays under subsection 164(1) must not be more than the portion established by the Minister of Finance under subsection 171(2).

heading: Recovery of overpayment
paragraph: 166 The following are debts that are due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in accordance with section 155 of the Financial Administration Act:

heading: Recovery of overpayment
paragraph: (a) any overpayment to a claimant by the Regulator under subsection 164(1);

heading: Recovery of overpayment
paragraph: (b) any amount paid to a claimant under paragraph 164(1)(b) in respect of a Tribunal's decision that is rescinded; and

heading: Recovery of overpayment
paragraph: (c) if the amount paid by the Regulator under paragraph 164(1)(b) in respect of a Tribunal's decision that is amended under subsection 169(1) is more than the amount of compensation and costs indicated in the notice referred to in subsection 169(2), the amount that is equal to the difference between those amounts.

heading: Report
