paragraph: (5) In this section, Tetlit Gwich'in Yukon land means land as described in Annex B, as amended from time to time, to Appendix C of the Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement between Her Majesty in right of Canada and the Gwich'in, as represented by the Gwich'in Tribal Council, that was approved, given effect and declared valid by the Gwich'in Land Claim Settlement Act.

heading: Application restricted
paragraph: 319 The provisions of this Part to determine compensation matters apply in respect of all damage, including the loss of value of the lands, caused by the operation of section 335 or by the pipeline or abandoned pipeline or anything transmitted by the pipeline but do not apply to

heading: Application restricted
paragraph: (a) claims against a company arising out of activities of the company unless those activities are directly related to

heading: Application restricted
paragraph: (i) the acquisition or lease of lands for a pipeline or abandoned pipeline,

heading: Application restricted
paragraph: (ii) the construction of the pipeline, or

heading: Application restricted
paragraph: (iii) the inspection, maintenance or repair of the pipeline or abandoned pipeline;

heading: Application restricted
paragraph: (b) claims against a company for loss of life or injury to the person; or

heading: Application restricted
paragraph: (c) awards of compensation or agreements respecting compensation made or entered into prior to March 1, 1983.

heading: Definition of owner
paragraph: 320 In sections 321 to 334, owner means any person who is entitled to compensation under section 314.

heading: Methods of acquisition or lease
paragraph: 321 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a company may acquire or lease lands for a pipeline under a land acquisition or lease agreement entered into between the company and the owner of the lands or, in the absence of such an agreement, in accordance with this Part.

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (2) A company must not acquire or lease lands for a pipeline under an agreement referred to in subsection (1) unless the agreement includes provision for

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (a) compensation for the acquisition or lease of lands to be made, at the option of the owner of the lands, by one lump sum payment or by periodic payments of equal or different amounts over a specified period of time;

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (b) review every five years of the amount of any compensation payable in respect of which periodic payments have been selected;

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (c) compensation for damages caused by the company's operations, pipelines or abandoned pipelines;

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (d) indemnification from all liabilities, damages, claims, suits and actions resulting from the company's operations, pipelines or abandoned pipelines, other than liabilities, damages, claims, suits and actions resulting from

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (i) in Quebec, the gross or intentional fault of the owner of the lands, and

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (ii) elsewhere in Canada, the gross negligence or wilful misconduct of the owner of the lands;

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (e) restriction of the use of the lands to the line of pipe or other facility for which the lands are, by the agreement, specified to be required unless the owner of the lands consents to any proposed additional use at the time of the proposed additional use;

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (f) compensation to the owner of the lands if the use of those lands is restricted by the operation of section 335;

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (g) compensation to the owner of the lands for any adverse effect on the remaining lands of the owner, including the restriction of their use by the operation of section 335; and

heading: Form of agreement
paragraph: (h) any additional terms that are, at the time the agreement is entered into, required to be included in it by any regulations made under paragraph 333(d).

heading: Notice of proposed acquisition or lease of lands
paragraph: 322 (1) If a company has determined the lands that may be required for the purposes of a section or part of a pipeline, the company must serve a notice on all owners of the lands, to the extent that they can be ascertained, which notice must set out or be accompanied by

heading: Notice of proposed acquisition or lease of lands
paragraph: (a) a description of the lands of the owner that are required by the company for that section or part;

heading: Notice of proposed acquisition or lease of lands
paragraph: (b) details of the compensation offered by the company for the lands required;

heading: Notice of proposed acquisition or lease of lands
paragraph: (c) a detailed statement made by the company of the value of the lands required in respect of which compensation is offered;

heading: Notice of proposed acquisition or lease of lands
paragraph: (d) a description of the procedure for approval of the detailed route of the pipeline;

heading: Notice of proposed acquisition or lease of lands
paragraph: (e) a description of the procedure available under this Part in the event that the owner of the lands and the company are unable to agree on any matter respecting the compensation payable; and

heading: Notice of proposed acquisition or lease of lands
paragraph: (f) any prescribed information.

heading: Agreement void or null
paragraph: (2) If an agreement referred to in section 321 is entered into with an owner of lands before a notice is served on the owner under this section, that agreement is void or, in Quebec, null.

heading: Abandonment: company's liability
paragraph: (3) If a company serves a notice on an owner of lands under subsection (1) and subsequently decides not to acquire or lease all or part of the land described in the notice, it is liable to the owner for all damages suffered and reasonable costs incurred by the owner in consequence of the notice and the abandonment of the acquisition or lease of the land.

heading: Agreement of purchase and sale
paragraph: 323 Subsections 321(2) and 322(1) do not apply during any period in which an agreement of purchase and sale with respect to the lands referred to in those subsections is in effect between the company and the owner of those lands.

heading: Immediate right of entry
paragraph: 324 (1) Subject to subsection 317(1), if the Commission considers it appropriate to do so, the Commission may, by order, on application to the Regulator in writing by a company, grant to the company an immediate right to enter any lands on any conditions specified by the Commission in the order.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) The Commission is not authorized to make an order under subsection (1) unless the Commission is satisfied that the owner of the lands in question has, not less than 30 days and not more than 60 days before the date of the application, been served with a notice setting out

heading: Notice
paragraph: (a) the purpose of the right of entry referred to in subsection (1);

heading: Notice
paragraph: (b) the date on which the company intends to make its application to the Regulator under subsection (1);

heading: Notice
paragraph: (c) the date on which the company intends to enter the lands and the period during which the company intends to have access to the lands;

heading: Notice
paragraph: (d) the address of the Regulator to which any objection in writing that the owner may make concerning the issuance of the order may be sent; and

heading: Notice
paragraph: (e) a description of the right of the owner to an advance of compensation under section 325 if the order is issued and the amount of the advance that the company is prepared to make.

heading: Advance of compensation
paragraph: 325 If a company has been granted an immediate right to enter lands under subsection 324(1), the owner of the lands is entitled to receive from the company an amount as an advance of the compensation referred to in subsection 327(1).

heading: Vesting
paragraph: 326 (1) An order under subsection 324(1) that grants a company an immediate right to enter lands is deemed to have vested in the company any title, interest or right in the lands that is specified in the order.

heading: Registration, recording or filing
paragraph: (2) Within 30 business days after the day on which the order is made, the company must register or deposit the order with the appropriate land registrar and notify the Regulator and the owner of the lands of its deposit.

heading: Determinations regarding compensation
paragraph: 327 (1) If a company and an owner of lands have not agreed on any matter relating to the compensation payable under this Part, the Commission, on application by a company or any owner, must, by order, determine that matter.

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (2) In determining any matter under subsection (1) for the acquisition or lease of lands, the Commission must consider the following factors:

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (a) the market value of the lands taken by the company;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (b) if periodic payments are being made under an agreement or an order of the Commission, changes in the market value referred to in paragraph (a) since the agreement or order of the Commission or since the last review and adjustment of those payments, as the case may be;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (c) the loss of use to the owner of the lands taken by the company or whose use is otherwise restricted by the operation of section 335;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (d) the adverse effect of the taking of the lands by the company on the remaining lands of an owner, including by restricting their use by the operation of section 335;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (e) the nuisance, inconvenience and noise that may reasonably be expected to be caused by or arise from or in connection with the operations of the company;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (f) the damage to lands in the area of the lands taken by the company that might reasonably be expected to be caused by the operations of the company;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (g) loss of or damage to livestock or other personal property or movable affected by the operations of the company;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (h) any special difficulties in relocation of an owner or their property;

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (i) any other factors that the Commission considers appropriate in the circumstances; and

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (j) other prescribed factors that are prescribed under paragraph 333(e).

heading: Definition of market value
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of paragraph (2)(a), market value is the amount that would have been paid for the lands if, at the time of their taking, they had been sold in the open market by a willing seller to a willing buyer.

heading: Settlement land or Tetlit Gwich'in Yukon land
paragraph: 328 If the Commission determines a compensation matter involving land referred to in section 318, sections 3, 26 to 31, 36, 54 to 58, 63, 67 and 72 of the Yukon Surface Rights Board Act apply to the Commission as if it were the Yukon Surface Rights Board.

heading: Form of compensation payment if land taken
paragraph: 329 (1) If the Commission makes an award of compensation in favour of a person whose lands are taken by a company, the Commission must, by order, direct, at the option of that person, that the compensation or any part of it be made by one lump sum payment or by periodic payments of equal or different amounts over a specified period of time.

heading: Other awards
paragraph: (2) If the Commission makes an award of compensation in favour of any person other than a person referred to in subsection (1), the Commission may, by order, direct, at the request of that person, that the compensation or any part of it be made by periodic payments of equal or different amounts over a specified period of time and that there be a periodic review of the compensation or part of the compensation.

heading: Terms to be included in award
paragraph: (3) Every award of compensation made by the Commission in respect of lands acquired or leased by a company must include provision for those matters referred to in paragraphs 321(2)(b) to (h) that would be required to be included in a land acquisition or lease agreement referred to in section 321.

heading: Interest may be payable
paragraph: (4) The Commission may, by order, direct a company to pay interest on the amount of any compensation awarded by the Commission at the lowest rate of interest quoted by banks to the most credit-worthy borrowers for prime business loans, as determined and published by the Bank of Canada for the month in which, as the case may be,

heading: Interest may be payable
paragraph: (a) the company entered the lands in respect of which the compensation is awarded; or

heading: Interest may be payable
paragraph: (b) the damages suffered as a result of the operations of the company first occurred.

heading: Period during which interest payable
paragraph: (5) Interest may be awarded under subsection (4) from the date the event referred to in paragraph (4)(a) or (b), as the case may be, occurred or from any later date that the Commission may specify in its award.

heading: Costs
paragraph: 330 (1) If the amount of compensation awarded to a person by the Commission exceeds 85% of the amount of compensation offered by the company, the company must pay all legal, appraisal and other costs determined by the Commission to have been reasonably incurred by that person in asserting that person's claim for compensation.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (2) If the amount of compensation awarded to a person by the Commission does not exceed 85% of the amount of compensation offered by the company, the legal, appraisal and other costs incurred by that person in asserting their claim for compensation are at the discretion of the Commission, and the Commission may, by order, direct the company or any other party to the proceedings to pay the whole or any part of those costs.

heading: Decisions
paragraph: 331 The Commission must, within seven days after it makes a decision on an application, ensure that a copy of the decision is forwarded by mail to the company and to each other party to the proceeding.

heading: Agreements supersede Commission decisions
paragraph: 332 If, at any time after a decision of the Commission has been made in respect of lands acquired or leased by a company, the parties affected enter into a land acquisition or lease agreement referred to in subsection 321(1), the agreement supersedes the decision of the Commission.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 333 The Regulator may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, make regulations respecting the acquisition, lease or taking of lands and compensation matters, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing compensation matters related to the operation of section 335;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the form and manner in which a notice is served for the purpose of section 201 and subsection 322(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the procedures for the acquisition, lease or taking of lands for the purpose of subsection 321(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) prescribing additional terms to be added to those that must be included in a land acquisition or lease agreement under paragraphs 321(2)(a) to (g);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) prescribing additional factors to be added to those that the Commission must consider under paragraphs 327(2)(a) to (i);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) governing the procedures for the Commission to make orders under section 334;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the receipt and holding by the Regulator of copies of any agreements referred to in subsection 321(1) that are submitted voluntarily by a company and owner of the lands in question;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) prescribing any matter or thing that by this Part is to be or may be prescribed; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) generally to carry out the purposes and provisions of this Part.

heading: Orders of Commission
paragraph: 334 (1) On application, the Commission may, by order, give directions, including to determine any compensation payable under this Part, with respect to pipelines and abandoned pipelines in relation to

heading: Orders of Commission
paragraph: (a) the acquisition, lease or taking of lands;

heading: Orders of Commission
paragraph: (b) lands whose use is restricted by the operation of section 335, whether or not the lands were acquired, leased or taken; and

heading: Orders of Commission
paragraph: (c) damages caused by the activities of the company to any person, provincial government, local authority and government or Indigenous governing body during their planning, construction, operation or abandonment.

heading: Factors to consider
paragraph: (2) In determinating any compensation matter under paragraph (1)(a), the Commission must consider the factors referred to in paragraphs 327(2)(a) to (j).

heading: Prohibition - construction or ground disturbance
paragraph: 335 (1) It is prohibited for any person to construct a facility across, on, along or under a pipeline or engage in an activity that causes a ground disturbance within the prescribed area unless the construction or activity is authorized or required by the orders made under subsection (3) or (4) or regulations made under subsections (5) or (6) and done in accordance with them.

heading: Prohibition - vehicles and mobile equipment
paragraph: (2) It is prohibited for any person to operate a vehicle or mobile equipment across a pipeline unless

heading: Prohibition - vehicles and mobile equipment
paragraph: (a) that operation is authorized or required by orders made under subsection (3) or (4) or regulations made under subsections (5) or (6) and done in accordance with them; or

heading: Prohibition - vehicles and mobile equipment
paragraph: (b) the vehicle or equipment is operated within the travelled portion of a highway or public road.

heading: Order
paragraph: (3) The Commission may, by order, direct the owner of a facility constructed across, on, along or under a pipeline in contravention of this Act or the Commission's orders or regulations to do any things that the Commission considers necessary for the safety or security of the pipeline and, if the Commission considers that the facility may impair the safety or security of the operation of the pipeline, direct the owner to reconstruct, alter or remove the facility.

heading: Order
paragraph: (4) The Commission may, by order, give directions

heading: Order
paragraph: (a) governing the design, construction, operation and abandonment of facilities constructed across, on, along or under pipelines;

heading: Order
paragraph: (b) prescribing the area for the purposes of subsection (1);

heading: Order
paragraph: (c) authorizing the construction of facilities across, on, along or under pipelines;

heading: Order
paragraph: (d) authorizing ground disturbances within the prescribed area;

heading: Order
paragraph: (e) governing the measures to be taken in relation to

heading: Order
paragraph: (i) the construction of facilities across, on, along or under pipelines,

heading: Order
paragraph: (ii) the construction of pipelines across, on, along or under facilities, other than railways, and

heading: Order
paragraph: (iii) ground disturbances within the prescribed area;

heading: Order
paragraph: (f) authorizing the operation of vehicles or mobile equipment across a pipeline and governing the measures to be taken in relation to that operation;

heading: Order
paragraph: (g) governing the apportionment of costs directly incurred as a result of the construction or disturbance authorized under this section;

heading: Order
paragraph: (h) specifying activities for the purposes of paragraph (a) of the definition ground disturbance in section 2 in respect of pipelines; and

heading: Order
paragraph: (i) authorizing a company to give the authorization referred to in paragraph (c), (d) or (f) on any conditions that the company considers appropriate.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (5) The Regulator may make regulations respecting any matter referred to in paragraphs (4)(a) to (f) and (h).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (6) The Regulator may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) governing the apportionment of costs directly incurred as a result of the construction or disturbance authorized under this section; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) authorizing a company to give the authorization referred to in paragraph (4)(c), (d) or (f), subject to any conditions that the company considers appropriate.

heading: Temporary prohibition on ground disturbances
paragraph: (7) Orders made under subsection (4) and regulations made under subsection (5) may provide for the prohibition of ground disturbances in an area that is situated in the vicinity of a pipeline and that may extend beyond the prescribed area during the period that starts when a request is made to a pipeline company to locate its pipeline and ends

heading: Temporary prohibition on ground disturbances
paragraph: (a) at the end of the third working day after the day on which the request is made; or

heading: Temporary prohibition on ground disturbances
paragraph: (b) at any later time that is agreed to between the pipeline company and the person making the request.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (8) The Commission may, by order made subject to any conditions that the Commission considers appropriate, exempt any person from the application of an order made under subsection (4) or a regulation made under subsection (5) or (6).

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (9) Every person who contravenes subsection (1) or (2), an order made under subsection (3) or (4) or a regulation made under subsection (5) or (6) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year or to both.

heading: Application of subsections 379(2) to (6)
paragraph: (10) Subsections 379(2) to (6) apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, to an offence under subsection (9).

heading: Protection of mines
paragraph: 336 A company must not, without a designated officer having, by order, authorized it to do so, locate the line of its proposed pipeline, or construct the pipeline or any portion of the pipeline, so as to obstruct or interfere with or injuriously affect the working of or the access or adit to a mine then open, or for the opening of which preparations are, at the time of the location, being lawfully and openly made.

heading: Right to minerals
paragraph: 337 A company is not, unless they have been expressly purchased, entitled to mines, ores, metals, coal, slate, oil, gas or other minerals in or under lands purchased by it, or taken by it under compulsory powers given to it by this Act, except only the parts of them that are necessary to be dug, carried away or used in the construction of the works, and, except as provided in this section, all those mines and minerals are deemed to be excepted from the transfer of the lands, unless they have been expressly included in the transfer documents.

heading: Protection of pipeline from mining operations
paragraph: 338 (1) A person must not work or prospect for mines or minerals lying under a pipeline or any of the works connected with the pipeline, or within 40 m of the pipeline, without a designated officer having, by order, authorized it to do so.

heading: Use of oil and gas
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), an order from a designated officer is not required in the case of a well taking oil or gas from lands lying under a pipeline or any of the works connected with the pipeline if the well is not drilled within 40 m of the pipeline.

heading: Application for order
paragraph: (3) On an application for an order under subsection (1), the applicant must submit a plan and profile of the portion of the pipeline to be affected, giving all reasonable and necessary information respecting the proposed operations.

heading: Conditions of order
paragraph: (4) The designated officer may grant the application referred to in subsection (3), subject to any conditions for the protection, safety or security of persons that the designated officer considers appropriate, and may, by order, direct that any things be done that under the circumstances the designated officer considers to be best adapted to remove or diminish the danger arising or likely to arise from the proposed operations.

heading: Examination of site of mining operations
paragraph: 339 If necessary in order to ascertain whether any mining or prospecting operations have been carried on so as to injure or be detrimental to a pipeline or its safety or security or the safety or security of persons, a company may, if a designated officer, by order, authorizes it to do so and after giving 24 hours notice in writing, enter on any lands through or near which its pipeline passes where any mining or prospecting operations are being carried on, and enter into and return from the site of the operations, and for those purposes the company may make use of any apparatus used in connection with the operations and use all necessary means for discovering the distance from its pipeline to the place where the operations are being carried on.

heading: Compensation for severance, etc., of mining property
paragraph: 340 A company must, from time to time, pay to the owner, lessee or occupier of any mines any compensation that the Commission fixes and, by order, directs to be paid for or by reason of any severance by a pipeline of the land lying over the mines, the working of the mines being prevented, stopped or interrupted, or the mines having to be worked in any manner and under any restrictions so as not to injure or be detrimental to the pipeline, and also for any minerals not purchased by the company that cannot be obtained by reason of the construction and operation of its line.

heading: Assets of company subject to executions
paragraph: 341 (1) Nothing in this Act restricts or prohibits any of the following transactions:

heading: Assets of company subject to executions
paragraph: (a) the sale under execution of any property of a company;

heading: Assets of company subject to executions
paragraph: (b) the creation of any lien, mortgage, hypothec, charge or other security on the property of the company, or of any prior claim or right of retention within the meaning of the Civil Code of Quebec or any other statute of Quebec with respect to property of the company;

heading: Assets of company subject to executions
paragraph: (c) the sale, elsewhere than in Quebec, under an order of a court of any property of the company to enforce or realize on any lien, mortgage, charge or other security on the property of the company;

heading: Assets of company subject to executions
paragraph: (d) the sale, in Quebec, under an order of a court or by judicial authority, of any property of the company to enforce or realize on any hypothec, charge or other security on the property of the company; and

heading: Assets of company subject to executions
paragraph: (e) the exercise of remedies for the enforcement and realization of any prior claim referred to in paragraph (b) or the exercise of any right of retention referred to in that paragraph.

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: (2) A transaction mentioned in subsection (1) in respect of any property of a company is subject to the same laws to which it would be subject if the work and undertaking of the company were a local work or undertaking in the province in which that property is situated.

heading: Construing Special Acts
paragraph: 342 Except as otherwise provided in this Part,

heading: Construing Special Acts
paragraph: (a) this Act must be construed as incorporate with a Special Act; and

heading: Construing Special Acts
paragraph: (b) in the event of an inconsistency between a provision of this Part and of a provision of a Special Act, the provision of the Special Act prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Prohibition - export
paragraph: 343 A person must not export oil or gas except in accordance with a licence issued under this Part or as authorized under the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 344 (1) Subject to the regulations, the Commission may, with the Minister's approval, issue licences for the exportation of oil or gas and impose conditions on them.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (2) Every licence is subject to the condition that the provisions of this Act and its regulations, as well as every order made under this Act, will be complied with.

heading: Criteria
paragraph: 345 The Commission must not issue a licence unless it is satisfied that the quantity of oil or gas to be exported does not exceed the surplus remaining after allowance has been made for the reasonably foreseeable requirements for use in Canada, having regard to trends in the discovery of oil or gas in Canada.

heading: Time limit
paragraph: 346 (1) The Commission must decide whether to issue a licence for the exportation of oil or gas within 180 days after the day on which the Commission considers that the applicant has provided a complete application. The Commission must make that day public.

heading: Continuation of jurisdiction
paragraph: (2) A failure by the Commission to comply with subsection (1) within the required time limit does not affect its jurisdiction to issue the licence and anything done by it in relation to the issuance of that licence remains valid.

heading: Excluded period
paragraph: (3) If the Commission requires that the applicant provide information or undertake a study with respect to the application and the Commission states publicly that this subsection applies, the period that is taken by the applicant to comply with the requirement is not included in the calculation of the time limit.

heading: Public notice of excluded period
paragraph: (4) The Commission must make the day on which the period referred to in subsection (3) begins and the day on which it ends public as soon as each day is known.

heading: Extension
paragraph: (5) The Minister may, by order, extend the time limit by a maximum of 90 days. The Governor in Council may, on the Minister's recommendation, by order, further extend that time limit by any additional period or periods of time.

heading: Ministerial approval
paragraph: 347 (1) The Minister must decide whether to grant his or her approval of the issuance of a licence for the exportation of oil or gas within 90 days after the day on which the Commission makes its decision under subsection 346(1).

heading: Continuation of jurisdiction
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if the Minister grants his or her approval after the expiry of the time limit for doing so, the Commission's jurisdiction to issue the licence is not affected and anything done by it in relation to the issuance of that licence remains valid.

heading: Period for issuing licences
paragraph: (3) The Commission must issue the licence within seven days after the day on which the Minister grants his or her approval.

heading: Variation of licences
paragraph: 348 (1) The Commission may, on application or its own initiative, vary a licence issued under this Division. However, if the Commission considers that the variation is neither minor nor technical in nature, the Commission must not do so without the approval of the Minister.

heading: Public interest
paragraph: (2) The Minister may approve a variation under subsection (1) if he or she considers that it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (3) In varying a licence, the Commission may impose - in addition to or in lieu of any conditions to which the licence was previously subject - any conditions that the Commission considers necessary or appropriate to give effect to the purposes and provisions of this Act.

heading: Transfer of licences
paragraph: 349 (1) The Commission may, on application, transfer a licence issued under this Division. However, if the Commission considers that the transfer is neither minor nor technical in nature, the Commission must not do so without the approval of the Minister.

heading: Public interest
paragraph: (2) The Minister may approve a transfer of a licence if he or she considers that it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (3) In transferring a licence, the Commission may impose - in addition to or in lieu of any conditions to which the licence was previously subject - any conditions that the Commission considers necessary or appropriate to give effect to the purposes and provisions of this Act.

heading: Suspension or revocation of licences - application or consent
paragraph: 350 The Commission may, by order, suspend or revoke a licence issued under this Division if the holder applies for or consents to the suspension or revocation.

heading: Suspension or revocation of licences - contravention
paragraph: 351 (1) The Commission may, by order, suspend or revoke a licence issued under this Division if the holder has contravened a condition of the licence.

heading: Suspension or revocation of licences - public interest
paragraph: (2) The Commission may, by order and with the approval of the Minister, suspend or revoke a licence issued under this Division if the Commission considers that it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: Notice to licence holder
paragraph: (3) The Commission must not make an order under subsection (1) or (2) unless the Commission provides the holder of the licence with notice of the alleged contravention or the reasons why it considers a suspension or revocation to be in the public interest, as the case may be, and gives the holder an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Importer
paragraph: 352 Unless exempted by the regulations, for each prescribed reporting period every person who imports oil or gas must provide the prescribed information to the Regulator in the prescribed form and manner.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 353 (1) The Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of this Division, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the period of validity of licences, the quantities that may be exported under licences and any other conditions to which licences may be subject;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) authorizing the Commission to make orders authorizing the exportation of oil or gas and prescribing the circumstances in which the Commission may make, and the conditions that may be included in, those orders;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) prescribing the conditions under which the exportation of oil or gas may be carried out without a licence;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) prescribing the inspection of any instruments, devices, plant, equipment, books, records or accounts or any other thing used for or in connection with the exportation or importation of oil or gas;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) prescribing the immediate measures to take in respect of oil or gas seized by an officer referred to in section 380;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) prescribing, in respect of oil or gas the exportation of which is authorized under this Part, or any quality, kind or class of that oil or gas or type of service relating to it, the price at which or the range of prices within which that oil or gas must be sold; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) exempting oil or gas that is exported to Chile or Costa Rica, or any quality, kind or class of that oil or gas or type of service relating to it, from the application of regulations made under paragraph (f).

heading: Maximum validity
paragraph: (2) The period of validity referred to in paragraph (1)(a) begins on a date to be fixed in the licence and must not exceed

heading: Maximum validity
paragraph: (a) 40 years, in the case of a licence for the exportation of natural gas as defined by the regulations; and

heading: Maximum validity
paragraph: (b) 25 years, in any other case.

heading: Different prices or ranges of prices
paragraph: (3) Regulations made under paragraph (1)(f) may prescribe different prices or ranges of prices in respect of different countries.

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council approval
paragraph: 354 (1) Subject to the approval of the Governor in Council, the Regulator may make regulations

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council approval
paragraph: (a) exempting persons or classes of persons from the application of section 352; and

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council approval
paragraph: (b) prescribing anything that is to be prescribed under that section.

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (2) The Regulator may make regulations

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (a) respecting the information to be provided by applicants for licences and the procedure to be followed in applying for licences and in issuing licences; and

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (b) prescribing units of measurement and measuring instruments or devices to be used in connection with the exportation or importation of oil or gas.

heading: Export
paragraph: 355 A person must not export electricity except in accordance with a permit issued under section 356 or a licence issued under section 361.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 356 (1) Except in the case of an application designated by order of the Governor in Council under section 360, the Commission must, on application to it and without holding a public hearing, issue a permit authorizing the exportation of electricity.

heading: Information
paragraph: (2) The application must be accompanied by any information prescribed by regulation.

heading: Publication
paragraph: 357 (1) The applicant must cause a notice of the application to be published in the Canada Gazette and in any other publication that the Commission considers appropriate.

heading: Waiver
paragraph: (2) The Commission may waive the requirement set out in subsection (1) if it considers that there is a critical shortage of electricity outside Canada caused by terrorist activity, as defined in subsection 83.01(1) of the Criminal Code.

heading: Further information
paragraph: 358 The Commission may, within a reasonable time after the publication of the notice, require the applicant to provide any additional information that the Commission considers necessary to determine whether to make a recommendation under section 359.

heading: Delay of issuance
paragraph: 359 (1) The Commission may make a recommendation to the Minister, which it must make public, that an application for exportation of electricity be designated by order of the Governor in Council under section 360 and may delay issuing a permit during any period that is necessary for the purpose of making such an order.

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (2) In determining whether to make a recommendation, the Commission must seek to avoid the duplication of measures taken in respect of the exportation by the applicant and the government of the province from which the electricity is to be exported and must take into account

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (a) the effect of the exportation of the electricity on provinces other than that from which the electricity is to be exported;

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (b) whether the applicant has

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (i) informed those who have declared an interest in buying electricity for consumption in Canada of the quantities and classes of service available for sale, and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (ii) given an opportunity to buy electricity on conditions as favourable as the conditions specified in the application to those who, within a reasonable time after being so informed, demonstrate an intention to buy electricity for consumption in Canada; and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (c) any factors that are specified in the regulations.

heading: Where licence required
paragraph: 360 (1) The Governor in Council may make orders

heading: Where licence required
paragraph: (a) designating an application for exportation of electricity as an application in respect of which section 361 applies; and

heading: Where licence required
paragraph: (b) revoking any permit issued in respect of the exportation.

heading: Time limit
paragraph: (2) No order may be made under subsection (1) more than 45 days after the day on which a permit is issued in respect of the application.

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (3) If an order is made under subsection (1),

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (a) a permit must not be issued in respect of the application; and

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (b) any application in respect of the exportation must be dealt with as an application for a licence.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 361 (1) The Commission may, subject to the approval of the Governor in Council, issue a licence for the exportation of electricity in relation to which an order made under section 360 is in force.

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (2) Before issuing a licence, the Commission must take into account

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (a) the effect of the exportation of the electricity on provinces other than from which the electricity is to be exported;

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (b) whether the applicant has

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (i) informed those who have declared an interest in buying electricity for consumption in Canada of the quantities and classes of service available for sale, and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (ii) given an opportunity to buy electricity on conditions as favourable as the conditions specified in the application to those who, within a reasonable time after being so informed, demonstrate an intention to buy electricity for consumption in Canada; and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (c) any factors that are specified in the regulations.

heading: Conditions - permits
paragraph: 362 (1) The Commission may make a permit issued under section 356 subject to any conditions respecting the matters prescribed by the regulations that it considers necessary or in the public interest.

heading: Conditions - licences
paragraph: (2) The Commission may make a licence issued under section 361 subject to any conditions that it considers appropriate.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: 363 Every permit and licence is subject to the condition that the provisions of this Act and its regulations, as well as every order made under this Act, will be complied with.

heading: Period of validity
paragraph: 364 The period of validity of a permit or licence must not exceed 30 years.

heading: Variation or transfer of permits or licences
paragraph: 365 (1) The Commission may, on application or its own initiative, vary a permit or licence issued in respect of the exportation of electricity and may, on application, transfer such a permit or licence.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (2) In varying or transferring a permit or licence, the Commission may impose - in addition to or in lieu of any conditions to which the permit or licence was previously subject - any conditions that the Commission considers necessary or appropriate in order to give effect to the purposes and provisions of this Act.

heading: Suspension or revocation of permits or licences
paragraph: 366 (1) The Commission may, by order, suspend or revoke a permit or licence issued in respect of the exportation of electricity if the holder applies for or consents to the revocation or suspension or the holder has contravened a condition of the permit or licence.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) The Commission must not make an order under subsection (1) for a contravention unless the Commission provides the holder of the permit or licence with notice of the alleged contravention and gives the holder an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: 367 (1) The Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of this Division, including regulations

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (a) prescribing matters in respect of which conditions may be imposed on permits;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (b) specifying factors that the Commission must take into account in deciding whether to recommend to the Minister that an application for a permit for the exportation of electricity be designated by order of the Governor in Council under section 360;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (c) specifying factors that the Commission must take into account in deciding whether to issue a licence for the exportation of electricity in relation to which an order made under section 360 is in force; and

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (d) the inspection of any instruments, devices, plant, equipment, books, records or accounts or any other thing used for or in connection with the exportation of electricity.

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (2) The Regulator may make regulations prescribing

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (a) the information to be provided with applications for permits for the exportation of electricity; and

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (b) units of measurement and measuring instruments or devices to be used in connection with the exportation of electricity.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 368 The following definitions apply in this Division.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: designated area means any of the following, as referred to in an order made under subsection 369(1),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a province;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) Sable Island; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any area of land, not within a province, that belongs to Her Majesty in right of Canada or in respect of which Her Majesty in right of Canada has the right to dispose of or exploit the natural resources and that is situated in submarine areas in the internal waters of Canada, the territorial sea of Canada or the continental shelf of Canada. (region designee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: designated oil or gas means oil or gas, or both, or any quality or kind of oil or gas, or both, that is the subject of an order made under subsection 369(1). (petrole ou gaz designe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: movement, in respect of oil or gas, excludes an exportation. (acheminement)

heading: Order in Council
paragraph: 369 (1) The Governor in Council may, by order, give the supervision and control of the movement of designated oil or gas out of a designated area to the Regulator.

heading: Licence required
paragraph: (2) While an order made under subsection (1) remains in force, a person must not move designated oil or gas out of the designated area except in accordance with a licence issued under this Division or as authorized under the regulations made under this Division.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 370 (1) Subject to the regulations, the Commission may, on any conditions that it may impose, issue a licence to any person permitting the movement of designated oil or gas out of the designated area.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (2) Every licence is subject to the conditions that

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (a) the provisions of this Act and its regulations, as well as every order made under this Act, will be complied with; and

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (b) the provisions of the Energy Administration Act and its regulations that are applicable to the designated oil or gas in respect of which the licence is issued will be complied with.

heading: Criteria
paragraph: 371 (1) Before issuing a licence, the Commission must take into account all factors that it considers relevant, including the equitable distribution of designated oil or gas in Canada.

heading: Variation, transfer, suspension and revocation of licences
paragraph: (2) Sections 348 to 351 apply in respect of a licence issued under this Division.

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: 372 (1) The Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of this Division, including regulations

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (a) respecting the period of validity of licences, the approval required for the issuance of licences, the quantities that may be moved out of the designated area under the authority of a licence and any other conditions to which licences may be subject; and

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (b) prescribing the inspection of any instruments, devices, plant, equipment, books, records or accounts or any other thing used for or in connection with the movement of designated oil or gas out of the designated area.

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (2) The Regulator may make regulations prescribing

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (a) the information to be provided by applicants for licences and the procedure to be followed in applying for and issuing licences; and

heading: Regulations - Regulator
paragraph: (b) units of measurement and measuring instruments or devices to be used in connection with the movement of designated oil or gas out of the designated area.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 373 The following definitions apply in this Division.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: CCFTA has the same meaning as Agreement as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement Implementation Act. (ALECC)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: CCRFTA has the same meaning as Agreement as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada - Costa Rica Free Trade Agreement Implementation Act. (ALECCR)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: CUSMA has the meaning assigned by the definition Agreement in section 2 of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement Implementation Act. (ACEUM)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: energy goods means any goods for the exportation of which a licence or permit issued under this Part or an order made under the regulations is required. (produits energetiques)

heading: Principle
paragraph: 374 (1) In exercising its powers and performing its duties and functions, the Regulator must give effect to CUSMA, the CCFTA and the CCRFTA.

heading: Directions
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, either on the recommendation of the Minister made at the request of the Regulator or on the Governor in Council's own motion, give directions respecting the manner in which the Regulator is to perform the duty imposed on it by subsection (1) or the interpretation to be given to CUSMA, the CCFTA or the CCRFTA by the Regulator for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Effect
paragraph: (3) A direction issued under subsection (2) is binding on the Regulator from the time it comes into force and, unless it provides otherwise, applies in respect of matters pending before the Regulator at that time.

heading: Request of Regulator
paragraph: (4) The Regulator may, in order to request the issuance of a direction under subsection (2), suspend the determination of any matter of which it is seized.

heading: Declaration of Governor in Council
paragraph: 375 The Governor in Council may, by order, declare that the maintenance or introduction of a restriction on the exportation to Chile or Costa Rica of energy goods or of any quality, kind or class of energy goods is justified under Article C-13 of the CCFTA or Article III.11 of the CCRFTA, as the case may be.

heading: Request for declaration
paragraph: 376 If, in the course of determining an application for a licence or permit, or determining whether to make an order, for the exportation to Chile or Costa Rica of energy goods or of any quality, kind or class of energy goods, the Commission considers that the maintenance or introduction of a restriction on that exportation is in the public interest and that subparagraph 1(a), (b) or (c) of Article C-13 of the CCFTA or subparagraph 1(a), (b) or (c) of Article III.11 of the CCRFTA, as the case may be, would apply as a consequence of the restriction, the Commission may, in order to request that the Minister recommend to the Governor in Council that an order be made under section 375 in respect of the relevant energy goods, suspend the determination until not later than 120 days after the day on which the request is made.

heading: Exportation to Chile or Costa Rica
paragraph: 377 (1) The Commission may neither refuse to issue a licence or permit or make an order nor suspend, revoke or vary a licence, permit or order for the exportation to Chile or Costa Rica of energy goods or of any quality, kind or class of energy goods if that refusal, revocation, suspension or variation would constitute the maintenance or introduction of a restriction on that exportation as a consequence of which subparagraph 1(a), (b) or (c) of Article C-13 of the CCFTA or subparagraph 1(a), (b) or (c) of Article III.11 of the CCRFTA, as the case may be, would apply.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of the exportation to Chile or Costa Rica of any energy goods, or of any quality, kind or class of energy goods, referred to in an order made under section 375 while the order is in force.

heading: Application or consent
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), the Commission may suspend, revoke or vary a licence, permit or order if the holder of the licence, the holder of the permit or the person named in the order, as the case may be, applies for or consents to the suspension or revocation.

heading: No declaration made
paragraph: 378 Despite not being satisfied that the criteria set out in section 345 have been met, the Commission may issue a licence for the exportation to Chile or Costa Rica of any energy goods, or of any quality, kind or class of energy goods, referred to in a request made under section 376 if

heading: No declaration made
paragraph: (a) the Minister declines to recommend to the Governor in Council that an order be made under section 375;

heading: No declaration made
paragraph: (b) the Governor in Council declines to make the order; or

heading: No declaration made
paragraph: (c) no order is made within 120 days after the day on which the request is made.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: 379 (1) Every person who contravenes any of the provisions of this Part or the regulations made under this Part is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine not exceeding $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or to both.

heading: Due diligence
paragraph: (2) A person is not to be found guilty of an offence under subsection (1) if they establish that they exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence.

heading: Officers, directors, agents and mandataries
paragraph: (3) If a corporation commits an offence under subsection (1), any officer or director, or agent or mandatary, of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the punishment provided for the offence whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Proof of offence
paragraph: (4) In any prosecution for an offence under subsection (1), it is sufficient proof of the offence to show that it was committed by an employee, or an agent or mandatary, of the accused, whether or not the employee, or agent or mandatary, is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence, unless the accused establishes that the offence was committed without the knowledge or consent of the accused and that the accused exercised due diligence to prevent its commission.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph: (5) If an offence under subsection (1) is committed on more than one day, it is deemed to be a separate offence for each day on which the offence is committed or continued.

heading: Limitation period or prescription
paragraph: (6) Proceedings by way of summary conviction in respect of an offence under subsection (1) may be instituted at any time within but not later than one year after the day on which the subject matter of the proceedings arose.

heading: Powers of certain officers
paragraph: 380 An officer as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Customs Act has, in respect of the exportation or importation of oil or gas, all the powers of an officer under the Customs Act and, except to the extent that they are inconsistent with any regulations made under paragraph 353(1)(e), the provisions of that Act and any regulations made under that Act respecting search, detention, seizure, forfeiture, condemnation and disposition apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, to oil or gas tendered for exportation or importation or exported or imported or otherwise dealt with contrary to this Part.

heading: Definitions of oil and gas
paragraph: 381 For the purposes of this Part, oil and gas have the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: 382 (1) This section applies to any decision of the Commission to make, amend or revoke a declaration of significant discovery under section 28 of the Canada Petroleum Resources Act or a declaration of commercial discovery under section 35 of that Act.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) At least 30 days before making a decision to which this section applies, the Commission must give written notice of its intention to make the decision to any person the Commission considers to be directly affected by the decision.

heading: Request for hearing
paragraph: (3) A person to whom notice is given may, in writing, request a hearing in respect of the decision, but the request must be received by the Commission within 30 days after the day on which notice is given.

heading: No request for hearing
paragraph: (4) If no request is received in accordance with subsection (3), the Commission may make the decision.

heading: Hearing
paragraph: (5) If a request is received in accordance with subsection (3), the Commission must fix a time and place for the hearing and notify each person who requested the hearing.

heading: Representations
paragraph: (6) Each person who requests a hearing may make representations and introduce witnesses and documents at the hearing.

heading: Decision
paragraph: (7) The Commission must make its decision and give notice of that decision to each person who requested the hearing and, on that person's request, the Commission must make the reasons for its decision public.

heading: Variation of licences or authorizations
paragraph: 383 The Commission or a person to whom powers are delegated under section 4.1 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act may vary the conditions of any operating licence or authorization issued under section 5 of that Act.

heading: Application to appeals
paragraph: 384 (1) This section applies to appeals brought under section 21 or subsection 25(8) of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act by a person aggrieved by an order of the Chief Conservation Officer or by any action or measure taken or authorized or directed to be taken by that Officer, other than the referral of an order to the Commission under subsection 58(5) of that Act.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (2) After hearing an appeal to which this section applies, the Commission may

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) set aside, confirm or vary the order, action or measure that is the subject of the appeal;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) order any works to be undertaken that the Commission considers necessary to prevent waste, the escape of oil or gas or any other contravention of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act or the regulations made under that Act; or

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) make any other order that the Commission considers appropriate.

heading: Show cause hearing relating to waste
paragraph: 385 (1) This section applies to applications by the Chief Conservation Officer to the Commission under section 22 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act for a show cause hearing relating to waste, as defined in paragraph 18(2)(f) or (g) of that Act, in the recovery of oil or gas from a pool.

heading: Order
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application, the Commission must make an order requiring the operators within the pool to show cause at a hearing, to be held on a day specified in the order, why the Commission should not make a direction in respect of the waste.

heading: Hearing
paragraph: (3) On the day specified in the order, the Commission must hold a hearing at which the Chief Conservation Officer, the operators and other interested persons must be given an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Order
paragraph: (4) If, after the hearing, the Commission considers that waste is occurring in the recovery of oil or gas from a pool, it may, by order,

heading: Order
paragraph: (a) direct the introduction of a scheme for the collection, processing, disposition or reinjection of any gas produced from the pool; or

heading: Order
paragraph: (b) direct repressurizing, recycling or pressure maintenance for the pool or any part of the pool and for or incidental to that purpose, direct the introduction or injection of gas, water or any other substance into the pool or any part of the pool.

heading: Additional order
paragraph: (5) In addition to making an order under subsection (4), the Commission may, by order, direct that the pool or any part of the pool specified in the order be shut in if the requirements of the order are not met or unless a scheme is approved by the Commission and in operation by a date fixed in the order.

heading: Continuation pending approval
paragraph: (6) Despite subsections (4) and (5), the Commission may, by order, permit the continued operation of a pool or any part of a pool after the date fixed by an order made under this section if the Commission considers that a scheme or other action described in paragraph (4)(a) or (b) is in the course of preparation, but the continued operation is subject to any conditions the Regulator imposes.

heading: Application
paragraph: 386 (1) This section applies to an order referred by the Chief Safety Officer or the Chief Conservation Officer to the Commission under subsection 58(5) of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.

heading: Review and decision
paragraph: (2) The Commission must review the need for the order and may confirm it or set it aside.

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: (3) The burden of establishing that the order is not needed is on the person who requested that the order be referred to the Commission.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: 387 (1) Every person who fails to comply with an order of the Commission under section 384 or 385 is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding $100,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine not exceeding $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or to both.

heading: Due diligence
paragraph: (2) A person is not to be found guilty of an offence under subsection (1) if they establish that they exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence.

heading: Applicable provisions
paragraph: (3) Sections 65 to 71 of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, in respect of an offence under subsection (1).

heading: Statutory Instruments Act

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999.

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: 2 (1) In the administration of this Act, the Government of Canada shall, having regard to the Constitution and laws of Canada and subject to subsection (1.1),

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (a) exercise its powers in a manner that

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (i) protects the environment and human health, including the health of vulnerable populations,

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (ii) applies the precautionary principle, which provides that the lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures to prevent environmental degradation if there are threats of serious or irreversible damage, and

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (iii) promotes and reinforces enforceable pollution prevention approaches;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (a.1) take preventive and remedial measures to protect, enhance and restore the environment;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (a.2) protect the right of every individual in Canada to a healthy environment as provided under this Act, subject to any reasonable limits;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (a.3) in relation to paragraph (a.2), uphold principles such as principles of environmental justice - including the avoidance of adverse effects that disproportionately affect vulnerable populations - the principle of non-regression and the principle of intergenerational equity;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (b) take the necessity of protecting the environment into account in making social and economic decisions;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (c) implement an ecosystem approach that considers the unique and fundamental characteristics of ecosystems;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (d) endeavour to act in cooperation with governments to protect the environment;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (e) encourage the participation of the people of Canada in the making of decisions that affect the environment;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (f) facilitate the protection of the environment by the people of Canada;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (g) establish nationally consistent standards of environmental quality;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (h) provide information to the people of Canada on the state of the Canadian environment;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (i) apply knowledge, including traditional aboriginal knowledge, science and technology, to identify and resolve environmental problems;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (j) protect the environment, including its biological diversity, and human health, from the risk of any adverse effects of the use and release of toxic substances, pollutants and wastes;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (j.1) protect the environment, including its biological diversity, and human health, by ensuring the safe and effective use of biotechnology;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (k) endeavour to act expeditiously and diligently to assess whether existing substances or those new to Canada are toxic or capable of becoming toxic and assess the risk that such substances pose to the environment and human life and health;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (k.1) encourage the development and timely incorporation of scientifically justified alternative methods and strategies in the testing and assessment of substances to replace, reduce or refine the use of vertebrate animals;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (l) endeavour to act with regard to the intent of intergovernmental agreements and arrangements entered into for the purpose of achieving the highest level of environmental quality throughout Canada;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (m) ensure, to the extent that is reasonably possible, that all areas of federal regulation for the protection of the environment and human health are addressed in a complementary manner in order to avoid duplication and to provide effective and comprehensive protection;

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (n) endeavour to exercise its powers to require the provision of information in a coordinated manner; and

heading: Duties of the Government of Canada
paragraph: (o) apply and enforce this Act in a fair, predictable and consistent manner.

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (1.1) The Government of Canada shall consider the following before taking any measure under paragraph (1)(a.1):

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (a) the short- and long-term human and ecological benefits arising from the environmental protection measure;

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (b) the positive economic impacts arising from the measure, including those cost-savings arising from health, environmental and technological advances and innovation, among others; and

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (c) any other benefits accruing from the measure.

heading: Action not limited
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section shall be construed so as to prevent the taking of any action to protect the environment or human health for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 3 (1) The definitions in this subsection apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aboriginal government means a governing body that is established by or under or operating under an agreement between Her Majesty in right of Canada and aboriginal people and that is empowered to enact laws respecting

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the protection of the environment; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for the purposes of Division 5 of Part 7, the registration of vehicles or engines. (gouvernement autochtone)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aboriginal land means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) reserves, surrendered lands and any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band and that are subject to the Indian Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) land, including any water, that is subject to a comprehensive or specific claim agreement, or a self-government agreement, between the Government of Canada and aboriginal people where title remains with Her Majesty in right of Canada; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) air and all layers of the atmosphere above and the subsurface below land mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b). (terres autochtones)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: air pollution means a condition of the air, arising wholly or partly from the presence in the air of any substance, that directly or indirectly

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) endangers the health, safety or welfare of humans;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) interferes with the normal enjoyment of life or property;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) endangers the health of animal life;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) causes damage to plant life or to property; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) degrades or alters, or forms part of a process of degradation or alteration of, an ecosystem to an extent that is detrimental to its use by humans, animals or plants. (pollution atmospherique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: analyst means a person or a member of a class of persons designated as an analyst under subsection 217(1). (analyste)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: biological diversity means the variability among living organisms from all sources, including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, terrestrial and marine and other aquatic ecosystems and the ecological complexes of which they form a part and includes the diversity within and between species and of ecosystems. (diversite biologique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: biotechnology means the application of science and engineering in the direct or indirect use of living organisms or parts or products of living organisms in their natural or modified forms. (biotechnologie)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: class of substances means any two or more substances that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) contain the same portion of chemical structure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) have similar physico-chemical or toxicological properties; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) for the purposes of sections 68, 70 and 71, have similar types of use. (categorie de substances)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Committee means the National Advisory Committee established under section 6. (comite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ecosystem means a dynamic complex of plant, animal and micro-organism communities and their non-living environment interacting as a functional unit. (ecosysteme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: enforcement officer means a person or a member of a class of persons designated as an enforcement officer under section 217. (agent de l'autorite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environment means the components of the Earth and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) air, land and water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) all layers of the atmosphere;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) all organic and inorganic matter and living organisms; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the interacting natural systems that include components referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c). (environnement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environmental emergency has the meaning given that expression in Part 8. (urgence environnementale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environmental quality includes the health of ecosystems. (qualite de l'environnement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Environmental Registry means the registry established under section 12. (Registre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal land means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) land, including any water, that belongs to Her Majesty in right of Canada, or that Her Majesty in right of Canada has the right to dispose of, and the air and all layers of the atmosphere above and the subsurface below that land; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the following land and areas, namely,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) the internal waters of Canada as determined under the Oceans Act, including the seabed and subsoil below and the airspace above those waters, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) the territorial sea of Canada as determined under the Oceans Act, including the seabed and subsoil below and the air and all layers of the atmosphere above that sea. (territoire domanial)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal source means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a department of the Government of Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an agency of the Government of Canada or other body established by or under an Act of Parliament that is ultimately accountable through a minister of the Crown in right of Canada to Parliament for the conduct of its affairs;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a Crown corporation as defined in subsection 83(1) of the Financial Administration Act; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a federal work or undertaking. (source d'origine federale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal work or undertaking means any work or undertaking that is within the legislative authority of Parliament, including

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a work or undertaking operated for or in connection with navigation and shipping, whether inland or maritime, including the operation of ships and transportation by ship;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a railway, canal, telegraph or other work or undertaking connecting one province with another, or extending beyond the limits of a province;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a line of ships connecting a province with any other province, or extending beyond the limits of a province;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a ferry between any province and any other province or between any province and any country other than Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) airports, aircraft and commercial air services;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) a broadcast undertaking;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) a bank or an authorized foreign bank within the meaning of section 2 of the Bank Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) a work or undertaking that, although wholly situated within a province, is before or after its completion declared by Parliament to be for the general advantage of Canada or for the advantage of two or more provinces; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) a work or undertaking outside the exclusive legislative authority of the legislatures of the provinces. (entreprises federales)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fuel means any form of matter that is combusted or oxidized for the generation of energy. (combustible)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: government means the government of a province or of a territory or an aboriginal government. (gouvernement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: healthy environment means an environment that is clean, healthy and sustainable. (environnement sain)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: movement within Canada or transport within Canada means movement or transport between provinces. (mouvement au Canada ou transport au Canada)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pollution prevention means the use of processes, practices, materials, products, substances or energy that avoid or minimize the creation of pollutants and waste and reduce the overall risk to the environment or human health. (prevention de la pollution)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: precautionary principle means Principle 15 of the 1992 Rio Declaration on Environment and Development, which provides that the lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures to prevent environmental degradation if there are threats of serious or irreversible damage. (principe de precaution)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed means prescribed by regulations made under this Act. (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: province includes a territory. (province)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: release includes discharge, spray, inject, inoculate, abandon, deposit, spill, leak, seep, pour, emit, empty, throw, dump, place and exhaust. (rejet)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sell includes to offer for sale or lease, have in possession for sale or lease or deliver for sale or lease. (vente)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: substance means any distinguishable kind of organic or inorganic matter, whether animate or inanimate, and includes

heading: Definitions
