paragraph: (a) any matter that is capable of being dispersed in the environment or of being transformed in the environment into matter that is capable of being so dispersed or that is capable of causing such transformations in the environment,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any element or free radical,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any combination of elements of a particular molecular identity that occurs in nature or as a result of a chemical reaction, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) complex combinations of different molecules that originate in nature or are the result of chemical reactions but that could not practicably be formed by simply combining individual constituents,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and, except for the purposes of sections 66 to 66.2, 80 to 89 and 104 to 115, includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) any mixture that is a combination of substances and does not itself produce a substance that is different from the substances that were combined,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) any manufactured item that is formed into a specific physical shape or design during manufacture and has, for its final use, a function or functions dependent in whole or in part on its shape or design, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) any animate matter that is, or any complex mixtures of different molecules that are, contained in effluents, emissions or wastes that result from any work, undertaking or activity. (substance)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sustainable development means development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. (developpement durable)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: transient reaction intermediate means a substance that is formed and consumed in the course of a chemical reaction. (intermediaire de reaction)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: transit means, except for the purposes of sections 139 and 155, the portion of an international transboundary movement of waste or material referred to in subsection 185(1) through the territory of a country that is neither the country of origin nor the country of destination of the movement. (transit)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: undertaking includes a business. (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vulnerable population means a group of individuals within the Canadian population who, due to greater susceptibility or greater exposure, may be at an increased risk of experiencing adverse health effects from exposure to substances. (population vulnerable)

heading: Meaning of Ministers and either Minister
paragraph: (2) Where the word Ministers is used in this Act, it refers to both the Minister and the Minister of Health, and where the expression either Minister is used in this Act, it refers to either the Minister or the Minister of Health.

heading: Class of substances
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this Act, other than subsection (1), substance includes a class of substances.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 5 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Implementation framework
paragraph: 5.1 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 2(1)(a.2), the Ministers shall, within two years after the day on which this section comes into force, develop an implementation framework to set out how the right to a healthy environment will be considered in the administration of this Act.

heading: Right to a healthy environment
paragraph: (1.1) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the implementation framework shall set out

heading: Right to a healthy environment
paragraph: (a) the process under subsection 76.1(1) in respect of the protection of the right to a healthy environment.

heading: Content
paragraph: (2) The implementation framework, in a manner consistent with the purposes of this Act, shall, among other things, elaborate on

heading: Content
paragraph: (a) the principles to be considered in the administration of this Act, such as principles of environmental justice - including the avoidance of adverse effects that disproportionately affect vulnerable populations - the principle of non-regression and the principle of intergenerational equity, according to which it is important to meet the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs;

heading: Content
paragraph: (b) research, studies or monitoring activities to support the protection of the right to a healthy environment referred to in paragraph 2(1)(a.2);

heading: Content
paragraph: (c) the relevant factors to be taken into account in interpreting and applying that right and in determining the reasonable limits to which it is subject, including social, health, scientific and economic factors; and

heading: Content
paragraph: (d) mechanisms to support the protection of that right.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) In developing the implementation framework, the Ministers shall consult any interested persons.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall publish the implementation framework in the manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Report
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 a report on the implementation of the framework.

heading: National Advisory Committee
paragraph: 6 (1) For the purpose of enabling national action to be carried out and taking cooperative action in matters affecting the environment and for the purpose of avoiding duplication in regulatory activity among governments, the Minister shall establish a National Advisory Committee

heading: National Advisory Committee
paragraph: (a) to advise the Ministers on regulations proposed to be made under subsection 93(1);

heading: National Advisory Committee
paragraph: (b) to advise the Minister on a cooperative, coordinated intergovernmental approach for the management of toxic substances; and

heading: National Advisory Committee
paragraph: (c) to advise the Minister on other environmental matters that are of mutual interest to the Government of Canada and other governments and to which this Act relates.

heading: Precautionary principle
paragraph: (1.1) In giving its advice and recommendations, the Committee shall use the precautionary principle.

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (2) The Committee shall consist of the following members:

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (a) one representative for each of the Ministers;

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (b) one representative of the government of each of the provinces; and

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (c) subject to subsection (3), not more than six representatives of aboriginal governments, to be selected on the following regional basis,

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (i) one representative for all aboriginal governments, except Inuit, in Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick,

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (ii) one representative for all aboriginal governments, except Inuit, in Quebec,

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (iii) one representative for all aboriginal governments, except Inuit, in Ontario,

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (iv) one representative for all aboriginal governments, except Inuit, in Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut,

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (v) one representative for all aboriginal governments, except Inuit, in British Columbia and Yukon, and

heading: Composition of Committee
paragraph: (vi) one representative for all Inuit aboriginal governments.

heading: Provincial representatives
paragraph: (2.1) The representative of a provincial government shall be selected by that government.

heading: Aboriginal representatives
paragraph: (2.2) Subject to subsection (3), the representative of aboriginal governments shall be selected by the aboriginal governments he or she represents.

heading: Inuit aboriginal representatives
paragraph: (2.3) Subject to subsection (3), the representative of Inuit aboriginal governments shall be selected by those governments.

heading: Absence of aboriginal government
paragraph: (3) Where there is no Inuit aboriginal government or aboriginal government for a region referred to in any of subparagraphs (2)(c)(i) to (v), the representative of the Inuit or of aboriginal people for the region, as the case may be, may be selected in accordance with regulations made under subsection (4).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (4) The Minister may make regulations respecting the manner of selecting a representative under subsection (3).

heading: Ministerial advisory committees
paragraph: 7 (1) For the purpose of carrying out their duties under this Act, the Ministers or either Minister may

heading: Ministerial advisory committees
paragraph: (a) establish advisory committees to report to the Ministers or either Minister; and

heading: Ministerial advisory committees
paragraph: (b) specify the functions that the committees are to perform and the manner in which those functions are to be performed.

heading: Publication of report
paragraph: (2) The report of a committee established under subsection (1), including its recommendations and reasons, shall be made public.

heading: Report of various committees
paragraph: 8 The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 a report of the activities of the Committee and of any committees established under paragraph 7(1)(a).

heading: Negotiation of agreement
paragraph: 9 (1) The Minister may negotiate an agreement with a government or with an aboriginal people with respect to the administration of this Act.

heading: Publication of negotiated agreements
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall publish any agreement negotiated under subsection (1) before it is entered into, or give notice of its availability, in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Comments or objections
paragraph: (3) Within 60 days after the publication of an agreement or notice of its availability under subsection (2), any person may file with the Minister comments or a notice of objection.

heading: Publication by Minister of results
paragraph: (4) After the end of the period of 60 days referred to in subsection (3), the Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a report or a notice of the availability of a report that summarizes how any comments or notices of objection were dealt with.

heading: Entering into agreements
paragraph: (5) The Minister may, after publishing a report or notice under subsection (4),

heading: Entering into agreements
paragraph: (a) with the approval of the Governor in Council, enter into an agreement with a government or an aboriginal people with respect to the administration of this Act; and

heading: Entering into agreements
paragraph: (b) subject to any terms and conditions that the Governor in Council may specify in the approval, agree to amendments of the agreement.

heading: Publication of final agreements
paragraph: (6) The Minister shall publish any agreement under subsection (5), or give notice of its availability, in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Termination
paragraph: (7) An agreement made under subsection (5) terminates five years after the date on which it comes into force or may be terminated earlier by either party giving the other at least three months notice.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (8) The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 a report on the administration of this Act under agreements made under subsection (5).

heading: Action not limited by Agreement
paragraph: (9) No agreement made under this section shall limit or restrict the carrying out of any action the Minister deems necessary for the administration and enforcement of this Act, including the conduct of inspections or investigations.

heading: Non-application of regulations
paragraph: 10 (1) Except with respect to Her Majesty in right of Canada, the provisions of a regulation made under subsection 93(1), 200(1) or 209(1) or (2) do not apply within the jurisdiction of a government for which there is in force an order, made under subsection (3), declaring that the provisions do not apply within that jurisdiction.

heading: Non-application of regulations
paragraph: (2) Except with respect to a federal source, the provisions of a regulation made under section 167 or 177 do not apply within the jurisdiction of a government for which there is in force an order, made under subsection (3), declaring that the provisions do not apply within that jurisdiction.

heading: Declaration of equivalent provisions
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (4), (5) and (6), where the Minister and a government agree in writing that there are in force by or under the laws applicable to the jurisdiction of the government

heading: Declaration of equivalent provisions
paragraph: (a) provisions that are equivalent to a regulation made under a provision referred to in subsection (1) or (2), and

heading: Declaration of equivalent provisions
paragraph: (b) provisions that are similar to sections 17 to 20 for the investigation of alleged offences under environmental legislation of that jurisdiction,

heading: Declaration of equivalent provisions
paragraph: the Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make an order declaring that the provisions of the regulation do not apply in an area under the jurisdiction of the government.

heading: Publication of agreements
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall publish any agreement referred to in subsection (3) before it is entered into, or give notice of its availability, in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Comments or objections
paragraph: (5) Within 60 days after the publication of an agreement or notice of its availability under subsection (4), any person may file with the Minister comments or a notice of objection.

heading: Publication by Minister of results
paragraph: (6) After the end of the period of 60 days referred to in subsection (5), the Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a report or a notice of the availability of a report that summarizes how any comments or notices of objection were dealt with.

heading: Publication of final agreements
paragraph: (7) The Minister shall publish any agreement referred to in subsection (3) after it is entered into, or give notice of its availability, in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Termination
paragraph: (8) An agreement made under subsection (3) terminates five years after the date on which it comes into force or may be terminated earlier by either party giving the other at least three months notice.

heading: Revocation of order
paragraph: (9) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, revoke an order made under subsection (3) if the agreement referred to in that subsection terminates or is terminated.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: (10) The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 a report on the administration of this section.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Definition of environmental protection action

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 11 In this Part, environmental protection action means an action under section 22.

heading: Establishment of Environmental Registry
paragraph: 12 The Minister shall establish a registry, to be called the Environmental Registry, for the purpose of facilitating access to documents relating to matters under this Act.

heading: Contents of Environmental Registry
paragraph: 13 (1) The Environmental Registry shall contain notices and other documents published or made publicly available by the Ministers or either Minister under this Act, and shall also include, subject to the Access to Information Act and the Privacy Act,

heading: Contents of Environmental Registry
paragraph: (a) notices of objection and of any approval granted under this Act;

heading: Contents of Environmental Registry
paragraph: (b) a copy of every policy and of every proposed regulation or order made under this Act; and

heading: Contents of Environmental Registry
paragraph: (c) copies of documents submitted to a court by the Minister relating to any environmental protection action.

heading: Form and manner of Environmental Registry
paragraph: (2) The Minister may determine the form of the Environmental Registry and how it is to be kept, so long as the registry is publicly accessible and searchable and is in electronic form.

heading: Protection from civil proceeding or prosecution
paragraph: 14 (1) Despite any other Act of Parliament, no civil or criminal proceedings may be brought against any person mentioned in subsection (2) for the full or partial disclosure in good faith of any notice or other document through the Environmental Registry or any consequences of its disclosure.

heading: Persons protected
paragraph: (2) The persons against whom the proceedings may not be brought are Her Majesty in right of Canada, the Minister and any person acting on behalf of or under the direction of the Minister.

heading: Additional rights
paragraph: 15 The rights conferred by this Part are in addition to the right to request, under section 76, that a substance be assessed, the right to file a notice of objection under Parts 1, 7 and 11 and the right to request under Parts 7 and 11 that a board of review be established under section 333.

heading: Voluntary reports
paragraph: 16 (1) Where a person has knowledge of the commission or reasonable likelihood of the commission of an offence under this Act, but is not required to report the matter under this Act, the person may report any information relating to the offence or likely offence to an enforcement officer or any person to whom a report may be made under this Act.

heading: Request for confidentiality
paragraph: (2) The person making the report may request that their identity, and any information that could reasonably be expected to reveal their identity, not be disclosed.

heading: Requirement for confidentiality
paragraph: (3) No person shall disclose or cause to be disclosed the identity of a person who makes a request under subsection (2) or any information that could reasonably be expected to reveal their identity unless the person authorizes the disclosure in writing.

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (4) Despite any other Act of Parliament, no employer shall dismiss, suspend, demote, discipline, harass or otherwise disadvantage an employee, or deny an employee a benefit of employment, by reason that

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (a) the employee has made a report under subsection (1);

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (b) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, has refused or stated an intention of refusing to do anything that is an offence under this Act; or

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (c) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, has done or stated an intention of doing anything that is required to be done by or under this Act.

heading: Application for investigation by Minister
paragraph: 17 (1) An individual who is resident in Canada and at least 18 years of age may apply to the Minister for an investigation of any offence under this Act that the individual alleges has occurred.

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (2) The application shall include a solemn affirmation or declaration

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (a) stating the name and address of the applicant;

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (b) stating that the applicant is at least 18 years old and a resident of Canada;

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (c) stating the nature of the alleged offence and the name of each person alleged to have contravened, or to have done something in contravention of, this Act or the regulations; and

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (d) containing a concise statement of the evidence supporting the allegations of the applicant.

heading: Form
paragraph: (3) The Minister may prescribe the form in which an application under this section is required to be made.

heading: Investigation by Minister
paragraph: 18 The Minister shall acknowledge receipt of the application within 20 days of the receipt and shall investigate all matters that the Minister considers necessary to determine the facts relating to the alleged offence.

heading: Progress reports
paragraph: 19 After acknowledging receipt of the application, the Minister shall report to the applicant every 90 days on the progress of the investigation and the action, if any, that the Minister has taken or proposes to take, and the Minister shall include in the report an estimate of the time required to complete the investigation or to implement the action, but a report is not required if the investigation is discontinued before the end of the 90 days.

heading: Minister may send evidence to Attorney General of Canada
paragraph: 20 At any stage of an investigation, the Minister may send any documents or other evidence to the Attorney General of Canada for consideration of whether an offence has been or is about to be committed under this Act and for any action that the Attorney General may wish to take.

heading: Discontinuation of investigation
paragraph: 21 (1) The Minister may discontinue the investigation if the Minister is of the opinion that

heading: Discontinuation of investigation
paragraph: (a) the alleged offence does not require further investigation; or

heading: Discontinuation of investigation
paragraph: (b) the investigation does not substantiate the alleged offence.

heading: Report
paragraph: (2) If the investigation is discontinued, the Minister shall

heading: Report
paragraph: (a) prepare a report in writing describing the information obtained during the investigation and stating the reasons for its discontinuation; and

heading: Report
paragraph: (b) send a copy of the report to the applicant and to any person whose conduct was investigated.

heading: Report
paragraph: A copy of the report sent to a person whose conduct was investigated must not disclose the name or address of the applicant or any other personal information about them.

heading: Circumstances when an individual may bring an action
paragraph: 22 (1) An individual who has applied for an investigation may bring an environmental protection action if

heading: Circumstances when an individual may bring an action
paragraph: (a) the Minister failed to conduct an investigation and report within a reasonable time; or

heading: Circumstances when an individual may bring an action
paragraph: (b) the Minister's response to the investigation was unreasonable.

heading: Nature of the action
paragraph: (2) The action may be brought in any court of competent jurisdiction against a person who committed an offence under this Act that

heading: Nature of the action
paragraph: (a) was alleged in the application for the investigation; and

heading: Nature of the action
paragraph: (b) caused significant harm to the environment.

heading: Relief that may be claimed
paragraph: (3) In the action, the individual may claim any or all of the following:

heading: Relief that may be claimed
paragraph: (a) a declaratory order;

heading: Relief that may be claimed
paragraph: (b) an order, including an interlocutory order, requiring the defendant to refrain from doing anything that, in the opinion of the court, may constitute an offence under this Act;

heading: Relief that may be claimed
paragraph: (c) an order, including an interlocutory order, requiring the defendant to do anything that, in the opinion of the court, may prevent the continuation of an offence under this Act;

heading: Relief that may be claimed
paragraph: (d) an order to the parties to negotiate a plan to correct or mitigate the harm to the environment or to human, animal or plant life or health, and to report to the court on the negotiations within a time set by the court; and

heading: Relief that may be claimed
paragraph: (e) any other appropriate relief, including the costs of the action, but not including damages.

heading: Limitation period of two years
paragraph: 23 (1) An environmental protection action may be brought only within a limitation period of two years beginning when the plaintiff becomes aware of the conduct on which the action is based, or should have become aware of it.

heading: Time during investigation not included
paragraph: (2) The limitation period does not include any time following the plaintiff's application for an investigation, but before the plaintiff receives a report under subsection 21(2).

heading: No action for remedial conduct
paragraph: 24 An environmental protection action may not be brought if the alleged conduct

heading: No action for remedial conduct
paragraph: (a) was taken

heading: No action for remedial conduct
paragraph: (i) to correct or mitigate harm or the risk of harm to the environment or to human, animal or plant life or health, or

heading: No action for remedial conduct
paragraph: (ii) to protect national security, support humanitarian relief efforts, participate in multilateral military or peace-keeping activities under the auspices of international organizations or defend a member state of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization; and

heading: No action for remedial conduct
paragraph: (b) was reasonable and consistent with public safety.

heading: Exception
paragraph: 25 An environmental protection action may not be brought against a person if the person was convicted of an offence under this Act, or environmental protection alternative measures within the meaning of Part 10 were used to deal with the person, in respect of the alleged conduct on which the action is based.

heading: Notice of the action
paragraph: 26 (1) The plaintiff in an environmental protection action shall give notice of the action to the Minister no later than 10 days after the document originating the action is first served on a defendant, and the Minister shall give notice of the action in the Environmental Registry as soon as possible after receipt of the plaintiff's notice.

heading: Notice of other matters
paragraph: (2) In an environmental protection action,

heading: Notice of other matters
paragraph: (a) the court may order any party to the action to give notice to the Minister of any matter relating to the action, within the time specified by the court; and

heading: Notice of other matters
paragraph: (b) the Minister shall give notice of that matter in the Environmental Registry as soon as possible after receipt of the party's notice.

heading: Attorney General to be served
paragraph: 27 (1) A plaintiff shall serve the Attorney General of Canada with a copy of the document originating an environmental protection action within 20 days after first serving the document on a defendant.

heading: Attorney General may participate
paragraph: (2) The Attorney General of Canada is entitled to participate in the action, either as a party or otherwise. Notice of his or her decision to participate shall be given to the plaintiff and be included in the Environmental Registry within 45 days after the copy of the originating document is served on the Attorney General.

heading: Right of appeal
paragraph: (3) The Attorney General of Canada is entitled to appeal from a judgment in the action and to make submissions and present evidence in an appeal.

heading: Other participants
paragraph: 28 (1) A court may allow any person to participate in an environmental protection action in order to provide fair and adequate representation of the private and public interests involved.

heading: Manner and terms of participation
paragraph: (2) The court may determine the manner and terms of the person's participation, including the payment of costs.

heading: Burden of proof
paragraph: 29 The offence alleged in an environmental protection action and the resulting significant harm are to be proved on a balance of probabilities.

heading: Defences
paragraph: 30 (1) The following defences are available in an environmental protection action:

heading: Defences
paragraph: (a) the defence of due diligence in complying with this Act and the regulations;

heading: Defences
paragraph: (b) the defence that the alleged conduct is authorized by or under an Act of Parliament;

heading: Defences
paragraph: (c) except with respect to Her Majesty in right of Canada or a federal source, the defence that the alleged conduct is authorized by or under a law of a government that is the subject of an order made under subsection 10(3); and

heading: Defences
paragraph: (d) the defence of officially induced mistake of law.

heading: Other defences not excluded
paragraph: (2) This section does not limit the availability of any other defences.

heading: Undertakings to pay damages
paragraph: 31 In deciding whether to dispense with an undertaking to pay damages caused by an interlocutory order in an environmental protection action, the court may consider any special circumstances, including whether the action is a test case or raises a novel point of law.

heading: Stay or dismissal
paragraph: 32 (1) A court may stay or dismiss an environmental protection action if it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (2) In deciding whether to stay or dismiss the action, the court may consider

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (a) environmental, health, safety, economic and social concerns;

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (b) whether the issues raised in the action would be better resolved in some other way;

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (c) whether the Minister has an adequate plan to correct or mitigate the harm to the environment or human, animal or plant life or health or otherwise to address the issues raised in the action; and

heading: Factors to be considered
paragraph: (d) any other relevant matter.

heading: Remedies
paragraph: 33 If a court finds that the plaintiff is entitled to judgment in an environmental protection action, it may grant any relief mentioned in subsection 22(3).

heading: Orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: 34 (1) A court order to negotiate a plan to correct or mitigate the harm to the environment or human, animal or plant life or health may, to the extent that it is reasonable, practicable and ecologically sound, require the plan to provide for

heading: Orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: (a) the prevention, reduction or elimination of the harm;

heading: Orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: (b) the restoration of the environment;

heading: Orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: (c) the restoration of all uses, including enjoyment, of the environment affected by the offence;

heading: Orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: (d) the payment of money by the defendant as the court may direct to achieve the plan's purposes; and

heading: Orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: (e) monitoring the implementation of the plan and the progress made in achieving its purposes.

heading: Orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: Before making the order, the court must take into account any efforts that the defendant has already made to deal with the harm.

heading: Other orders
paragraph: (2) The court may also make interlocutory or ancillary orders to ensure that the negotiation of the plan runs smoothly, including orders

heading: Other orders
paragraph: (a) for the payment of the costs of negotiation;

heading: Other orders
paragraph: (b) requiring the plaintiff or the defendant to prepare a draft of the plan; and

heading: Other orders
paragraph: (c) setting a time limit for the negotiations.

heading: Appointment of other person to prepare plan
paragraph: (3) The court may appoint a person who is not a party to prepare a draft plan if the parties cannot agree on the plan or the court is not satisfied with the plan that they negotiate.

heading: Order to prepare another plan
paragraph: (4) The court may order the parties to prepare another plan if it is not satisfied with the plan that they negotiate.

heading: Approval and effective date
paragraph: (5) The court may approve a plan that the parties negotiate or a plan prepared by a person appointed under subsection (3) and the approved plan comes into effect on a day determined by the court.

heading: Restriction on orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: 35 A court may not order the negotiation of a plan to correct or mitigate the harm to the environment or human, animal or plant life or health if it determines that

heading: Restriction on orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: (a) the harm has already been corrected or mitigated; or

heading: Restriction on orders to negotiate plans
paragraph: (b) adequate measures to correct or mitigate the harm have already been ordered under this Act or any other law in force in Canada.

heading: Settlement or discontinuance
paragraph: 36 An environmental protection action may be settled or discontinued only with the approval of the court and on terms that it considers appropriate.

heading: Settlements and orders
paragraph: 37 If an environmental protection action results in an order of a court or a settlement approved by a court,

heading: Settlements and orders
paragraph: (a) the resolution of any question of fact by the order or settlement is binding on a court in any other environmental protection action in which that question arises; and

heading: Settlements and orders
paragraph: (b) no other environmental protection action may be brought with respect to the offence or alleged offence dealt with by the order or settlement.

heading: Costs
paragraph: 38 In deciding whether to award costs in an environmental protection action, the court may consider any special circumstances, including whether the action is a test case or raises a novel point of law.

heading: Injunction
paragraph: 39 Any person who suffers, or is about to suffer, loss or damage as a result of conduct that contravenes any provision of this Act or the regulations may seek an injunction from a court of competent jurisdiction ordering the person engaging in the conduct

heading: Injunction
paragraph: (a) to refrain from doing anything that it appears to the court causes or will cause the loss or damage; or

heading: Injunction
paragraph: (b) to do anything that it appears to the court prevents or will prevent the loss or damage.

heading: Civil cause of action
paragraph: 40 Any person who has suffered loss or damage as a result of conduct that contravenes any provision of this Act or the regulations may, in any court of competent jurisdiction, bring an action to recover from the person who engaged in the conduct

heading: Civil cause of action
paragraph: (a) an amount equal to the loss or damage proved to have been suffered by the person; and

heading: Civil cause of action
paragraph: (b) an amount to compensate for the costs that the person incurs in connection with the matter and proceedings under this section.

heading: Evidence of offence
paragraph: 41 (1) In an action under this Part, the record of proceedings in any court in which a defendant was convicted of an offence under this Act is evidence that the defendant committed the offence.

heading: Certificate evidence of conviction
paragraph: (2) In the action, evidence that a defendant was convicted of an offence under this Act may be given by a certificate stating with reasonable particularity the conviction and sentence of the defendant.

heading: Signature of certificate
paragraph: (3) The certificate shall be signed by

heading: Signature of certificate
paragraph: (a) the person who made the conviction; or

heading: Signature of certificate
paragraph: (b) the clerk of the court in which the conviction was made.

heading: Signature of certificate
paragraph: Once it is proved that the defendant is the offender mentioned in the certificate, it is evidence without proof of the signature or the official character of the person appearing to have signed it.

heading: Civil remedies not affected
paragraph: 42 (1) No civil remedy for any conduct is suspended or affected by reason only that the conduct is an offence under this Act.

heading: Damages caused by a ship
paragraph: (3) No claim for damage caused by a ship may be made under this Act to the extent that a claim for that damage may be made under the Marine Liability Act or the Arctic Waters Pollution Prevention Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 43 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fish has the meaning assigned by section 2 of the Fisheries Act. (poissons)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hormone disrupting substance means a substance having the ability to disrupt the synthesis, secretion, transport, binding, action or elimination of natural hormones in an organism, or its progeny, that are responsible for the maintenance of homeostasis, reproduction, development or behaviour of the organism. (substance hormonoperturbante)

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: 44 (1) The Minister shall

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (a) establish, operate and maintain a system for monitoring environmental quality;

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (b) conduct research and studies relating to pollution prevention, the nature, transportation, dispersion, effects, control and abatement of pollution and the effects of pollution on environmental quality, and provide advisory and technical services and information related to that research and those studies;

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (c) conduct research and studies relating to

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (i) environmental contamination arising from disturbances of ecosystems by human activity,

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (ii) changes in the normal geochemical cycling of toxic substances that are naturally present in the environment, and

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (iii) detection and damage to ecosystems;

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (d) collect, process, correlate, interpret, create an inventory of and publish on a periodic basis data on environmental quality in Canada from monitoring systems, research, studies and any other sources;

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (e) formulate plans for pollution prevention and the control and abatement of pollution, including plans respecting the prevention of, preparedness for and response to an environmental emergency and for restoring any part of the environment damaged by or during an emergency, and establish, operate and publicize demonstration projects and make them available for demonstration; and

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (f) publish, arrange for the publication of or distribute through an information clearing-house

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (i) information respecting pollution prevention,

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (ii) pertinent information in respect of all aspects of environmental quality, and

heading: Monitoring, research and publication
paragraph: (iii) a periodic report on the state of the Canadian environment.

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (2) The Minister may

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (a) in establishing a system referred to in paragraph (1)(a), cooperate with governments, foreign governments and aboriginal people and with any person who has established or proposes to establish any such system; and

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (b) with the approval of the Governor in Council, enter into agreements for the operation or maintenance of a system referred to in paragraph (1)(a) by the Minister on behalf of any government, aboriginal people or any person or for the operation or maintenance of any such system by the government or any person on behalf of the Minister.

heading: Cooperation with other bodies
paragraph: (3) The Minister may, in exercising the powers conferred by paragraphs (1)(b) to (e), act in cooperation with any government, foreign government, government department or agency, institution, aboriginal people or any person and may sponsor or assist in any of their research, studies, planning or activities in relation to environmental quality, pollution prevention, environmental emergencies or the control or abatement of pollution.

heading: Protection of right to healthy environment
paragraph: (3.1) The Ministers shall conduct research, studies or monitoring activities to support the Government of Canada in protecting the right to a healthy environment referred to in paragraph 2(1)(a.2).

heading: Hormone disrupting substances
paragraph: (4) The Ministers shall conduct research or studies relating to hormone disrupting substances, methods related to their detection, methods to determine their actual or likely short-term or long-term effect on the environment and human health, and preventive, control and abatement measures to deal with those substances to protect the environment and human health.

heading: Role of Minister of Health
paragraph: 45 (1) The Minister of Health shall

heading: Role of Minister of Health
paragraph: (a) conduct research and studies, including biomonitoring surveys, relating to the role of substances in illnesses or in health problems;

heading: Role of Minister of Health
paragraph: (b) collect, process, correlate and publish on a periodic basis data from any research or studies done under paragraph (a); and

heading: Role of Minister of Health
paragraph: (c) distribute available information to inform the public about the effects of substances on human health.

heading: Vulnerable populations
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, the research and studies referred to in paragraph (1)(a) may relate to vulnerable populations.

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: 46 (1) The Minister may, for the purpose of conducting research, creating an inventory of data, formulating objectives and codes of practice, issuing guidelines or assessing or reporting on the state of the environment, publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice requiring any person described in the notice to provide the Minister with any information that may be in the possession of that person or to which the person may reasonably be expected to have access, including information regarding the following:

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (a) substances specified in the plan developed under section 73;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (b) substances that have not been determined to be toxic under Part 5 because of the current extent of the environment's exposure to them, but whose presence in the environment must be monitored if the Minister considers that to be appropriate;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (c) substances, including nutrients, that can be released into water or are present in products like water conditioners and cleaning products;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (d) substances released, or disposed of, at or into the sea;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (e) substances that are toxic under section 64 or that may become toxic;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (e.1) products that contain a substance that is toxic under section 64 or that may become toxic, or products that may release such a substance into the environment;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (f) substances that may cause or contribute to international or interprovincial pollution of fresh water, salt water or the atmosphere;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (g) substances or fuels that may contribute significantly to air pollution;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (h) substances that, if released into Canadian waters, cause or may cause damage to fish or to their habitat;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (i) substances that, if released into areas of Canada where there are migratory birds, endangered species or other wildlife regulated under any other Act of Parliament, are harmful or capable of causing harm to those birds, species or wildlife;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (j) substances that are on the list established under regulations made under subsection 200(1);

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (k) the release of substances into the environment at any stage of their life-cycle;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (k.1) activities that may contribute to pollution;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (k.2) hydraulic fracturing;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (k.3) tailings ponds;

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (l) pollution prevention; and

heading: Notice requiring information
paragraph: (m) use of federal land and of aboriginal land.

heading: Other recipient
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, in accordance with an agreement signed with a government, require that a person to whom a notice is directed submit the information to the Minister or to that government.

heading: Conditions respecting access to information
paragraph: (3) An agreement referred to in subsection (2) shall set out conditions respecting access by the Minister or other government to all or part of the information that the person is required to submit and may set out any other conditions respecting the information.

heading: Period of notice and date for compliance
paragraph: (4) A notice referred to in subsection (1) must indicate the period during which it is in force, which may not exceed three years, and the date or dates within which the person to whom the notice is directed shall comply with the notice.

heading: Compliance with notice
paragraph: (5) Every person to whom a notice is directed shall comply with the notice.

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (6) The Minister may, on request in writing from any person to whom a notice is directed, extend the date or dates within which the person shall comply with the notice.

heading: Manner
paragraph: (7) The notice must indicate the manner in which the information is to be provided.

heading: Preservation of information
paragraph: (8) The notice may indicate the period during which, and the location where, the person to whom the notice is directed shall keep copies of the required information, together with any calculations, measurements and other data on which the information is based. The period may not exceed three years from the date the information is required to be submitted to the Minister.

heading: Guidelines
paragraph: 47 (1) The Minister shall issue guidelines respecting the use of the powers provided for by subsection 46(1) and, in issuing those guidelines, the Minister shall take into account any factor that the Minister considers relevant, including

heading: Guidelines
paragraph: (a) the costs and benefits to the Minister and the person to whom the notice under subsection 46(1) is directed;

heading: Guidelines
paragraph: (b) the co-ordination of requests for information with other governments, to the extent practicable; and

heading: Guidelines
paragraph: (c) the manner in which the information collected under subsection 46(1) is to be used.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) In carrying out the duties under subsection (1), the Minister shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in the quality of the environment.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (3) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with subsection (2), the Minister may act under subsection (1) if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: National inventory
paragraph: 48 The Minister shall establish a national inventory of releases of pollutants using the information collected under section 46 and any other information to which the Minister has access, and may use any information to which the Minister has access to establish any other inventory of information.

heading: Publication in whole or in part
paragraph: 49 The notice published under subsection 46(1) must indicate whether or not the Minister intends to publish the information and, if so, whether in whole or in part.

heading: Publication of inventory
paragraph: 50 Subject to subsection 53(4), the Minister shall publish the national inventory of releases of pollutants in any manner that the Minister considers appropriate and may publish or give notice of the availability of any other inventory of information established under section 48, in any manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Request for confidentiality
paragraph: 51 A person who provides information to the Minister under subsection 46(1) may, if the Minister's intention to publish the information has been indicated under section 49, submit with the information a written request, setting out a reason referred to in section 52, that the information be treated as confidential.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: 52 Despite Part 11, a request under section 51 may only be based on any of the following reasons:

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (a) the information constitutes a trade secret;

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (b) the disclosure of the information would likely cause material financial loss to, or prejudice to the competitive position of, the person providing the information or on whose behalf it is provided; and

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (c) the disclosure of the information would likely interfere with contractual or other negotiations being conducted by the person providing the information or on whose behalf it is provided.

heading: Additional justification
paragraph: 53 (1) The Minister may, after studying the reasons provided under section 52, require the person in question to provide, within 20 days and in writing, additional justification for the request for confidentiality.

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (2) The Minister may extend the period mentioned in subsection (1) by up to 10 days if the extension is necessary to permit adequate preparation of the additional justification.

heading: Minister's decision
paragraph: (3) In determining whether to accept or reject the request, the Minister shall consider whether the reasons are well-founded and, if they are, the Minister may nevertheless reject the request if

heading: Minister's decision
paragraph: (a) the disclosure is in the interest of the protection of the environment, public health or public safety; and

heading: Minister's decision
paragraph: (b) the public interest in the disclosure outweighs in importance

heading: Minister's decision
paragraph: (i) any material financial loss or prejudice to the competitive position of the person who provided the information or on whose behalf it was provided, and

heading: Minister's decision
paragraph: (ii) any damage to the privacy, reputation or human dignity of any individual that may result from the disclosure.

heading: Acceptance of request
paragraph: (4) If the Minister accepts the request, the information shall not be published.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (5) If the Minister rejects the request,

heading: Publication
paragraph: (a) the person has the right to ask the Federal Court to review the matter within 30 days after the person is notified that the request has been rejected or within any further time that the Court may, before the expiry of those 30 days, fix or allow; and

heading: Publication
paragraph: (b) the Minister shall advise the person in question of the Minister's intention to publish the information and of the person's right to ask the Federal Court to review the matter.

heading: Applicable provisions
paragraph: (6) Where a person asks the Federal Court to review the matter under paragraph (5)(a), sections 45, 46 and 47 of the Access to Information Act apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, in respect of a request for a review under that paragraph as if it were an application made under section 44 of that Act.

heading: Formulation by the Minister
paragraph: 54 (1) For the purpose of carrying out the Minister's mandate related to preserving the quality of the environment, the Minister shall issue

heading: Formulation by the Minister
paragraph: (a) environmental quality objectives specifying goals or purposes for pollution prevention or environmental control, including goals or purposes stated in quantitative or qualitative terms;

heading: Formulation by the Minister
paragraph: (b) environmental quality guidelines specifying recommendations in quantitative or qualitative terms to support and maintain particular uses of the environment;

heading: Formulation by the Minister
paragraph: (c) release guidelines recommending limits, including limits expressed as concentrations or quantities, for the release of substances into the environment from works, undertakings or activities; and

heading: Formulation by the Minister
paragraph: (d) codes of practice respecting pollution prevention or specifying procedures, practices or release limits for environmental control relating to works, undertakings and activities during any phase of their development and operation, including the location, design, construction, start-up, closure, dismantling and clean-up phases and any subsequent monitoring activities.

heading: Scope of objectives, etc.
paragraph: (2) The objectives, guidelines and codes of practice referred to in subsection (1) shall relate to

heading: Scope of objectives, etc.
paragraph: (a) the environment;

heading: Scope of objectives, etc.
paragraph: (b) pollution prevention or the recycling, reusing, treating, storing or disposing of substances or reducing the release of substances into the environment;

heading: Scope of objectives, etc.
paragraph: (c) works, undertakings or activities that affect or may affect the environment; or

heading: Scope of objectives, etc.
paragraph: (d) the conservation of natural resources and sustainable development.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) In carrying out the duties under subsection (1), the Minister shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in the quality of the environment.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (3.1) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with subsection (3), the Minister may act under subsection (1) if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall publish any objectives, guidelines or codes of practice issued under this section, or give notice of them, in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Formulation by the Minister of Health
paragraph: 55 (1) For the purpose of carrying out the mandate of the Minister of Health related to preserving and improving public health under this Act, the Minister of Health shall issue objectives, guidelines and codes of practice with respect to the elements of the environment that may affect the life and health of the people of Canada.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) In carrying out the duties under subsection (1), the Minister of Health may consult with a government, a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in the preservation and improvement of public health.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Health shall publish any objectives, guidelines or codes of practice issued under this section, or give notice of them, in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister of Health considers appropriate.

heading: Requirement for pollution prevention plans
paragraph: 56 (1) The Minister may, at any time, publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice requiring any person or class of persons described in the notice to prepare and implement a pollution prevention plan in respect of

heading: Requirement for pollution prevention plans
paragraph: (a) a substance or group of substances specified on the list of toxic substances in Schedule 1;

heading: Requirement for pollution prevention plans
paragraph: (b) a substance or group of substances with respect to which subsection 166(1) or 176(1) applies; or

heading: Requirement for pollution prevention plans
paragraph: (c) a product that contains a substance specified on the list of toxic substances in Schedule 1 or that may release such a substance into the environment.

heading: Alternatives
paragraph: (1.1) The notice may include a requirement that the plan prioritize the identification, development or use of safer or more sustainable alternatives to the substance, group of substances or product.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (2) The notice may specify

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (a) the substance, group of substances or product in relation to which the plan is to be prepared;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (b) the commercial, manufacturing, processing or other activity in relation to which the plan is to be prepared;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (c) the factors to be considered in preparing the plan;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (d) the period within which the plan is to be prepared;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (e) the period within which the plan is to be implemented; and

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (f) any administrative matter necessary for the purposes of this Part.

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (3) Where the Minister is of the opinion that further time is necessary to prepare or implement the plan, the Minister may extend the period for a person who submits a written request before the expiry of the period referred to in the notice or of any extended period.

heading: Publication of notice of extension
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall publish in the Environmental Registry and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice stating the name of any person for whom an extension is granted, whether the extension is for the preparation or the implementation of the plan, and the duration of the period of the extension.

heading: Application for waiver
paragraph: (5) On a written request submitted by any person to whom a notice under subsection (1) is directed, the Minister may waive the requirement for that person to consider a factor specified under paragraph (2)(c) where the Minister is of the opinion that it is not reasonable or practicable to consider the factor on the basis of reasons provided in the request.

heading: Progress reports
paragraph: (6) A notice under subsection (1) may include a requirement that the person to whom the notice is directed file with the Minister, within the periods specified in the notice, written reports on their progress in implementing the plan.

heading: Plan prepared or implemented for another purpose
paragraph: 57 (1) Subject to subsection (2), where a person who is required to prepare or implement a pollution prevention plan under a notice published under section 56 has prepared or implemented a plan in respect of pollution prevention on a voluntary basis or for another government or under another Act of Parliament that meets all or some of the requirements of the notice, the person may use that plan for the purposes of meeting the requirements of this Part and, in that case, the plan shall be considered to be a pollution prevention plan that has been prepared or implemented under this Part.

heading: Where partial requirements met
paragraph: (2) Where a person uses a plan under subsection (1) that does not meet all of the requirements of the notice, the person shall

heading: Where partial requirements met
paragraph: (a) amend the plan so that it meets all of those requirements; or

heading: Where partial requirements met
paragraph: (b) prepare an additional pollution prevention plan that meets the remainder of those requirements.

heading: Declaration of preparation
paragraph: 58 (1) Every person who is required to prepare a pollution prevention plan under section 56 or 291 or under an agreement in respect of environmental protection alternative measures shall file, within 30 days after the end of the period for the preparation of the plan specified in the notice referred to in subsection 56(1) or extended under subsection 56(3), or specified by the court under section 291 or in the agreement, as the case may be, a written declaration to the Minister that the plan has been prepared and is being implemented.

heading: Declaration of implementation
paragraph: (2) Every person who is required to implement a pollution prevention plan under section 56 or 291 or under an agreement in respect of environmental protection alternative measures shall file, within 30 days after the completion of the implementation of the plan, a written declaration to the Minister that the implementation of the plan has been completed.

heading: Filing of amended declaration
paragraph: (3) Where a person has filed a declaration under subsection (1) or (2) and the declaration contains information that, at any time after the filing, has become false or misleading, that person shall file an amended declaration to the Minister within 30 days after that time.

heading: Form of declaration
paragraph: (4) A declaration referred to in subsection (1), (2) or (3) shall be filed in the form and manner and contain the information specified by the Minister.

heading: Requirement to keep plan
paragraph: 59 Every person who is required to prepare a pollution prevention plan under section 56 or 291 or under an agreement in respect of environmental protection alternative measures shall keep a copy of the plan at the place in Canada in relation to which the plan is prepared.

heading: Requirement to submit certain plans
paragraph: 60 (1) The Minister may publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice requiring any person or class of persons described in the notice who are required to prepare and implement a pollution prevention plan under section 56 to submit, within the period specified by the Minister, the plan or any part of the plan for the purpose of determining and assessing preventive or control actions in respect of a substance, group of substances or product.

heading: Submission of plans required by court or agreement
paragraph: (2) The Minister may publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice requiring any person or class of persons described in the notice who are required to prepare and implement a pollution prevention plan under section 291 or under an agreement in respect of environmental protection alternative measures to submit, within the period specified by the Minister, the plan or any part of the plan.

heading: Model plans
paragraph: 61 For the purpose of providing guidance in the preparation of a pollution prevention plan, the Minister may publish in the Canada Gazette or in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a model pollution prevention plan or a notice stating where a copy of the plan may be obtained.

heading: Guidelines
paragraph: 62 (1) The Minister shall, with particular consideration of paragraph 2(1)(m), develop guidelines respecting the circumstances in which and the conditions under which pollution prevention planning is appropriate.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) In carrying out the duties under subsection (1), the Minister shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in the quality of the environment.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (3) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with subsection (2), the Minister may act under subsection (1) if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Information clearing-house
paragraph: 63 (1) The Minister may, for the purposes of encouraging and facilitating pollution prevention, establish and maintain a national pollution prevention information clearing-house in order to collect, exchange and distribute information relating to pollution prevention.

heading: Recognition program
paragraph: (2) The Minister may establish a program to publicly recognize significant achievements in the area of pollution prevention.

heading: Cooperation with other bodies
paragraph: (3) The Minister may, in exercising the powers conferred by subsections (1) and (2), act alone or in cooperation with any government in Canada or government of a foreign state or any of its institutions or any person.

heading: Toxic substances
paragraph: 64 For the purposes of this Part and Part 6, except where the expression "inherently toxic" appears, a substance is toxic if it is entering or may enter the environment in a quantity or concentration or under conditions that

heading: Toxic substances
paragraph: (a) have or may have an immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment or its biological diversity;

heading: Toxic substances
paragraph: (b) constitute or may constitute a danger to the environment on which life depends; or

heading: Toxic substances
paragraph: (c) constitute or may constitute a danger in Canada to human life or health.

heading: Domestic Substances List
paragraph: 66 (1) The Minister shall, for the purpose of section 81, maintain a list to be known as the Domestic Substances List and, subject to subsection 66.2(1), the List shall specify all substances that the Minister is satisfied were, between January 1, 1984 and December 31, 1986,

heading: Domestic Substances List
paragraph: (a) manufactured in or imported into Canada by any person in a quantity of not less than 100 kg in any one calendar year; or

heading: Domestic Substances List
paragraph: (b) in Canadian commerce or used for commercial manufacturing purposes in Canada.

heading: Non-domestic Substances List
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall, for the purpose of section 81, maintain a list to be known as the Non-domestic Substances List, and the List shall specify substances, other than

heading: Non-domestic Substances List
paragraph: (a) the substances referred to in subsection (1), unless the substance has been deleted from the Domestic Substances List under subsection 66.2(1); and

heading: Non-domestic Substances List
paragraph: (b) living organisms within the meaning of Part 6.

heading: Amendment of Lists
paragraph: (3) Where a substance was not included on the Domestic Substances List and the Minister subsequently learns that, between January 1, 1984 and December 31, 1986, the requirements set out in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) were met in respect of the substance, the Minister shall add the substance to the List and, where necessary, delete it from the Non-domestic Substances List.

heading: Amendment of Lists
paragraph: (4) Where the Minister includes a substance on the Domestic Substances List and subsequently learns that, between January 1, 1984 and December 31, 1986, the requirements set out in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) were not met in respect of the substance, the Minister shall delete the substance from the List and may add it to the Non-domestic Substances List.

heading: Publication of Lists
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate the Domestic Substances List, the Non-domestic Substances List and any amendments to those Lists.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (6) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions set out in this section.

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: 66.1 (1) The Minister may, for the purpose of section 81, add a substance to the Domestic Substances List if

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: (a) the substance was included on the version of the Revised In Commerce List that was prepared by the Minister of Health after the end, on November 3, 2019, of acceptance of substance nominations to that List and that is referred to in the Canada Gazette, Part I, Volume 152, Number 44, as the static list;

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: (b) the substance is not referred to in Annex I to the notice entitled "Removal of substances with no commercial activity from the Revised In Commerce List" published in the Canada Gazette, Part I, Volume 156, Number 8; and

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: (c) no conditions specified under paragraph 84(1)(a) in respect of the substance are in effect.

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: If the substance appears on the Non-domestic Substances List, the Minister shall delete it from that List.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the powers set out in subsection (1).

heading: Amendment of Lists
paragraph: 66.2 (1) If the Minister is satisfied that a substance referred to in subsection 66(1) that is specified on the Domestic Substances List - or a substance added to the List under subsection 66.1(1) or 87(1) or (5) - is not being manufactured in Canada, imported into Canada, in Canadian commerce or used for commercial manufacturing purposes in Canada, the Minister may delete the substance from the List and may add it to the Non-domestic Substances List.

heading: Publication - notice of intent
paragraph: (2) Before deleting a substance from the Domestic Substances List under subsection (1), the Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice indicating the Minister's intention to delete it from the List.

heading: Comments
paragraph: (3) Within 60 days after the publication of the notice, any person may file written comments with the Minister.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions set out in this section.

heading: Regulation of criteria
paragraph: 67 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Ministers, make regulations

heading: Regulation of criteria
paragraph: (a) respecting a property or characteristic of a substance, including persistence, bioaccumulation, carcinogenicity, mutagenicity and reproductive toxicity;

heading: Regulation of criteria
paragraph: (b) prescribing the substances or groups of substances in respect of which the property or characteristic may be applicable;

heading: Regulation of criteria
paragraph: (c) prescribing the conditions under which and the circumstances in which the property or characteristic may be applicable;

heading: Regulation of criteria
paragraph: (d) respecting the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for analysing, testing or measuring the property or characteristic, including conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for replacing, reducing or refining the use of vertebrate animals; and

heading: Regulation of criteria
paragraph: (e) respecting, for the purpose of subsection 77(3), the classification of a substance as a substance that poses the highest risk.

heading: Condition
paragraph: (2) No regulation that is applicable to a mineral or metal may be made under subsection (1) unless, in the opinion of the Ministers, the natural occurrence, properties and characteristics of that mineral or metal in the environment have been taken into consideration.

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: 68 For the purpose of assessing whether a substance is toxic or is capable of becoming toxic - or for the purpose of assessing whether to control, or the manner in which to control, a substance, a product that contains a substance or a product that may release a substance into the environment - including a substance specified on the list of toxic substances in Schedule 1, either Minister may

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (a) collect or generate data and conduct investigations respecting any matter in relation to the substance or product including

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (i) whether short-term exposure to the substance causes significant effects,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (ii) the potential of organisms in the environment to be widely exposed to the substance,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (iii) whether organisms are exposed to the substance via multiple pathways,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (iii.1) whether exposure to the substance in combination with exposure to other substances has the potential to cause cumulative effects,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (iii.2) whether there is a vulnerable population or environment in relation to the substance,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (iv) the ability of the substance to cause a reduction in metabolic functions of an organism,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (v) the ability of the substance to cause delayed or latent effects over the lifetime of an organism, including carcinogenic, mutagenic or neurotoxic effects,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (vi) the ability of the substance to cause survival impairment of an organism,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (vi.1) the ability of the substance to disrupt the reproductive system or endocrine system of an organism,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (vii) whether exposure to the substance has the potential to contribute to population failure of a species,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (viii) the ability of the substance to cause transgenerational effects,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (ix) quantities, uses and disposal of the substance,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (x) the manner in which the substance is released into the environment,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (xi) the extent to which the substance can be dispersed and will persist in the environment,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (xii) the existence, development and use of safer or more sustainable alternatives to the substance or product,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (xiii) methods of controlling the presence of the substance in the environment,

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (xiv) methods of reducing the quantity of the substance used or produced or the quantities or concentration of the substance released into the environment, and

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (xv) the manner in which the public may be provided with information regarding the substance or product, including, in the case of a product, by labelling it;

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (b) correlate and evaluate any data collected or generated under paragraph (a) and publish results of any investigations carried out under that paragraph; and

heading: Research, investigation and evaluation
paragraph: (c) provide information and make recommendations respecting any matter in relation to the substance or product, including measures to control the presence of the substance or product in the environment.

heading: Restriction - vertebrate animals
paragraph: 68.1 (1) The Ministers shall, to the extent practicable, use scientifically justified alternative methods and strategies to replace, reduce or refine the use of vertebrate animals in the generation of data and the conduct of investigations under paragraph 68(a).

heading: Methods and strategies to refine use
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), methods and strategies to refine the use of vertebrate animals include minimizing pain and distress caused to vertebrate animals used in the generation of data and the conduct of investigations under paragraph 68(a).

heading: Formulation of guidelines by the Ministers
paragraph: 69 (1) Either Minister or both Ministers, as the case may be, may issue guidelines for the purposes of the interpretation and application of the provisions of this Part for which they have responsibility.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) In exercising the powers under subsection (1), either Minister or both Ministers shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in assessing and controlling toxic substances.

heading: Saving
paragraph: (2.1) Nothing in subsection (2) shall prevent either Minister or both Ministers from exercising the powers under subsection (1) at any time after the 60th day following the day on which an offer is made under subsection (2).

heading: Guidelines public
paragraph: (3) Guidelines issued under this section shall be made available to the public, and the Minister who issued the guidelines shall give notice of them in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that that Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Notice to the Minister
paragraph: 70 Where a person

heading: Notice to the Minister
