paragraph: 101 (1) Subject to subsection (4), no person shall export a substance specified in the Export Control List in Schedule 3 unless the person provides prior notice of the proposed export to the Minister in accordance with the regulations made under subsection 102(1).

heading: Restrictions on export
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (4), no person shall export a substance specified in Part 1 of the Export Control List in Schedule 3 unless the export of the substance

heading: Restrictions on export
paragraph: (a) is for the purpose of destroying the substance or complying with a direction under subparagraph 99(b)(iii); and

heading: Restrictions on export
paragraph: (b) is done in accordance with any regulations made under subsection 102(1).

heading: Restrictions on export
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), no person shall export a substance specified in Part 2 or 3 of the Export Control List in Schedule 3 unless the export of the substance is done in accordance with any regulations made under subsection 102(1).

heading: Total prohibition on export
paragraph: (4) No person shall export a substance specified in the Export Control List in Schedule 3 if the export of the substance is prohibited by a regulation made under subsection 102(2).

heading: Regulations respecting exports
paragraph: 102 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Ministers, make regulations in relation to substances specified in the Export Control List in Schedule 3

heading: Regulations respecting exports
paragraph: (a) respecting the information that must be given to the Minister regarding an export of such a substance, the time when or period within which the information must be given, and the manner in which it must be given;

heading: Regulations respecting exports
paragraph: (b) respecting the information that must accompany an export of such a substance and the manner in which it must accompany the substance;

heading: Regulations respecting exports
paragraph: (c) respecting conditions under which a person may export such a substance;

heading: Regulations respecting exports
paragraph: (d) respecting the information that must be kept by a person who exports such a substance and the manner in which, the period for which and the place where the information must be kept; and

heading: Regulations respecting exports
paragraph: (e) generally for carrying out the purposes of section 101.

heading: Regulations prohibiting exports
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Ministers, make regulations prohibiting the export of a substance specified in the Export Control List in Schedule 3.

heading: Publication of exports
paragraph: 103 If a person exports a substance specified in the Export Control List in Schedule 3, the Minister shall publish in the Environmental Registry the name or specifications of the substance, the name of the exporter and the name of the country of destination.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 104 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: living organism means a substance that is an animate product of biotechnology. (organisme vivant)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: significant new activity includes, in respect of a living organism, any activity that results or may result in

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the entry or release of the living organism into the environment in a quantity or concentration that, in the Ministers' opinion, is significantly greater than the quantity or concentration of the living organism that previously entered or was released into the environment; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the entry or release of the living organism into the environment or the exposure or potential exposure of the environment to the living organism in a manner and circumstances that, in the Ministers' opinion, are significantly different from the manner and circumstances in which the living organism previously entered or was released into the environment or of any previous exposure or potential exposure of the environment to the living organism. (nouvelle activite)

heading: Adding living organisms to Domestic Substances List
paragraph: 105 (1) The Minister shall, for the purpose of section 106, add to the Domestic Substances List maintained under section 66 any living organism if the Minister is satisfied that, between January 1, 1984 and December 31, 1986, the living organism

heading: Adding living organisms to Domestic Substances List
paragraph: (a) was manufactured in or imported into Canada by any person; and

heading: Adding living organisms to Domestic Substances List
paragraph: (b) entered or was released into the environment without being subject to conditions under this or any other Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province.

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: (2) Where the Minister includes a living organism on the Domestic Substances List and subsequently learns that, between January 1, 1984 and December 31, 1986, the requirements set out in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) were not met, the Minister shall delete the substance from the List.

heading: Publication of List
paragraph: (3) The Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette the Domestic Substances List and any amendment to the List.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions set out in this section.

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: 105.1 (1) The Minister may, for the purpose of section 106, add a living organism to the Domestic Substances List if

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: (a) the living organism was included on the version of the Revised In Commerce List that was prepared by the Minister of Health after the end, on November 3, 2019, of acceptance of substance nominations to that List and that is referred to in the Canada Gazette, Part I, Volume 152, Number 44, as the static list; and

heading: Domestic Substances List - Food and Drugs Act
paragraph: (b) no conditions specified under paragraph 109(1)(a) in respect of the living organism are in effect.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the power set out in subsection (1).

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: 105.2 (1) If the Minister is satisfied that a living organism added to the Domestic Substances List under subsection 105(1), 105.1(1) or 112(1) is not being manufactured in Canada or imported into Canada the Minister may delete the living organism from the List.

heading: Publication - notice of intent
paragraph: (2) Before deleting a living organism from the Domestic Substances List under subsection (1), the Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice indicating the Minister's intention to delete it from the List.

heading: Comments
paragraph: (3) Within 60 days after the publication of the notice, any person may file written comments with the Minister.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions set out in this section.

heading: Manufacture or import of living organisms
paragraph: 106 (1) Where a living organism is not specified on the Domestic Substances List, no person shall manufacture or import the living organism unless

heading: Manufacture or import of living organisms
paragraph: (a) the prescribed information with respect to the living organism, accompanied by the prescribed fee, has been provided by that person to the Minister on or before the prescribed date; and

heading: Manufacture or import of living organisms
paragraph: (b) the period for assessing the information under section 108 has expired.

heading: Notification of significant new activity in respect of living organism on List
paragraph: (3) Where a living organism is specified on the Domestic Substances List with an indication that this subsection applies with respect to the living organism, no person shall use, manufacture or import the living organism for a significant new activity that is indicated on the List with respect to the living organism unless

heading: Notification of significant new activity in respect of living organism on List
paragraph: (a) the person has provided the Minister with the prescribed information, on or before the date that is specified by the Minister or prescribed, accompanied by the prescribed fee; and

heading: Notification of significant new activity in respect of living organism on List
paragraph: (b) the period for assessing the information specified by the Minister or provided under section 108 has expired.

heading: Notification of significant new activity in respect of living organism not on List
paragraph: (4) Where a living organism is not specified on the Domestic Substances List and the Minister publishes a notice in the Canada Gazette indicating that this subsection applies with respect to the living organism, no person shall use the living organism for a significant new activity that is indicated in the notice unless

heading: Notification of significant new activity in respect of living organism not on List
paragraph: (a) the person has provided the Minister with the prescribed information, on or before the date that is specified by the Minister or prescribed, accompanied by the prescribed fee; and

heading: Notification of significant new activity in respect of living organism not on List
paragraph: (b) the period for assessing the information specified by the Minister or provided under section 108 has expired.

heading: Transfer of rights in respect of substance
paragraph: (5) Where prescribed information with respect to a substance has been provided under subsection (1), (3) or (4) by a person who subsequently transfers the right or privilege in relation to the substance for which the information was provided, the information is, subject to any conditions that may be prescribed, deemed to have been provided by the transferee of that right or privilege.

heading: Application
paragraph: (6) Subsections (1), (3) and (4) do not apply to

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a living organism that is manufactured or imported for a use that is regulated under any other Act of Parliament that provides for notice to be given before the manufacture, import or sale of the living organism and for an assessment of whether it is toxic or capable of becoming toxic;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) a living organism that is manufactured, used or imported under the conditions and in the circumstances prescribed as exempt from this section; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) impurities and contaminants related to the preparation of a living organism.

heading: Governor in Council may amend Schedule 4
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of the administration of this section, the Governor in Council has the exclusive responsibility for determining whether or not the requirements referred to in paragraph (6)(a) are met by or under an Act of Parliament referred to in that paragraph, or regulations made under that Act, and

heading: Governor in Council may amend Schedule 4
paragraph: (a) if the Governor in Council determines that the requirements referred to in paragraph (6)(a) are met by or under an Act of Parliament referred to in that paragraph, or regulations made under that Act, the Governor in Council may by order add to Schedule 4 the name of that Act or those regulations, as the case may be, and the fact that an Act or regulations are listed in Schedule 4 is conclusive proof that the requirements referred to in paragraph (6)(a) are met; and

heading: Governor in Council may amend Schedule 4
paragraph: (b) if the Governor in Council determines that the requirements referred to in paragraph (6)(a) are no longer met by or under an Act of Parliament, or regulations, listed in Schedule 4, the Governor in Council may by order delete from Schedule 4 the name of that Act or those regulations, as the case may be.

heading: Waiver of information requirements
paragraph: (8) On the request of any person to whom subsection (1), (3) or (4) applies, the Minister may waive any of the requirements to provide information under that subsection if

heading: Waiver of information requirements
paragraph: (a) in the opinion of the Ministers, the information is not needed in order to determine whether the living organism is toxic or capable of becoming toxic;

heading: Waiver of information requirements
paragraph: (b) a living organism is to be used for a prescribed purpose or manufactured at a location where, in the opinion of the Ministers, the person requesting the waiver is able to contain the living organism so as to satisfactorily protect the environment and human health; or

heading: Waiver of information requirements
paragraph: (c) it is not, in the opinion of the Ministers, practicable or feasible to obtain the test data necessary to generate the information.

heading: Publication of notice of waiver
paragraph: (9) The Minister shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances, publish in the Canada Gazette a notice stating the name of any person to whom a waiver is granted and the type of information to which it relates.

heading: Compliance with waiver
paragraph: (10) Where the Minister waives any of the requirements for information under paragraph (8)(b), the person to whom the waiver is granted shall not use, manufacture or import the living organism unless it is for the purpose prescribed by regulations made under paragraph 114(1)(f) or at the location specified in the request for the waiver, as the case may be.

heading: Correction of information
paragraph: (11) A person who has provided information under this section, including for the purposes of a request for a waiver under subsection (8), or under section 107 or 109 shall notify the Minister of any corrections to the information as soon as possible after learning of them.

heading: Request for information previously waived
paragraph: (12) Where the Minister is notified of any corrections to information that was provided for the purposes of a request for a waiver under subsection (8), the Minister may, after consideration by the Ministers of those corrections, require the person to whom the waiver was granted to provide the Minister with the information to which the waiver related within the time specified by the Minister.

heading: Application of section 109
paragraph: (13) Where the Ministers suspect, after considering

heading: Application of section 109
paragraph: (a) any corrections received under subsection (11), or

heading: Application of section 109
paragraph: (b) the information provided under subsection (12),

heading: Application of section 109
paragraph: that a living organism is toxic or capable of becoming toxic, the Minister may exercise any of the powers referred to in paragraphs 109(1)(a) to (c).

heading: Prohibition of activity
paragraph: 107 (1) Where the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has used, manufactured or imported a living organism in contravention of subsection 106(1), (3) or (4), the Minister may, in writing, require the person to provide the information referred to in that subsection and prohibit any activity involving the living organism until the expiry of the period for assessing the information under section 108.

heading: Waiver of information requirements
paragraph: (2) On the request of any person required under subsection (1) to provide information, the Minister may waive any of the requirements for prescribed information if one of the conditions specified in paragraphs 106(8)(a) to (c) is met and, in that case, subsections 106(9) to (13) apply with respect to the waiver.

heading: Assessment of information
paragraph: 108 (1) Subject to subsection (4), the Ministers shall, within the prescribed assessment period, assess information provided under subsection 106(1), (3) or (4) or paragraph 109(1)(c) or otherwise available to them in respect of a living organism in order to determine whether it is toxic or capable of becoming toxic.

heading: Assessment of information
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), the Ministers shall assess information provided under subsection 107(1) or otherwise available to them in respect of a living organism in order to determine whether it is toxic or capable of becoming toxic.

heading: Time for assessment
paragraph: (3) An assessment of information under subsection (2) shall be made following the date on which the information is provided within a period that does not exceed the number of days in the prescribed assessment period.

heading: Extension of assessment period
paragraph: (4) Where the Ministers are of the opinion that further time is necessary to assess any information, the Minister may, before the expiry of the assessment period referred to in subsection (1) or (3), extend the period for assessing the information, but the extension shall not exceed the number of days in the prescribed assessment period.

heading: Notification of extension
paragraph: (5) Where the Minister extends the period for assessing information, the Minister shall, before the expiry of the assessment period referred to in subsection (1) or (3), notify the person who provided the information.

heading: Termination of period
paragraph: (6) The Minister may, before the expiry of the assessment period referred to in subsection (1) or (3), terminate the period for assessing information and, immediately before doing so, shall notify the person who provided the information.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: 108.1 (1) If the information that the Ministers assess under subsection 108(1) or (2) is in respect of a vertebrate animal or a prescribed living organism or group of living organisms, the Ministers shall consult any interested persons before the expiry of the period for assessing that information.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) Before undertaking consultations, the Minister shall publish a notice of consultation in any manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Action to be taken after assessment
paragraph: 109 (1) Where the Ministers have assessed any information under section 108 and they suspect that a living organism is toxic or capable of becoming toxic, the Minister may, before the expiry of the period for assessing the information,

heading: Action to be taken after assessment
paragraph: (a) permit any person to manufacture or import the living organism, subject to any conditions that the Ministers may specify;

heading: Action to be taken after assessment
paragraph: (b) prohibit any person from manufacturing or importing the living organism; or

heading: Action to be taken after assessment
paragraph: (c) request any person to provide any additional information or submit the results of any testing that the Ministers consider necessary for the purpose of assessing whether the living organism is toxic or capable of becoming toxic.

heading: Additional information or testing
paragraph: (2) Where the Minister requests additional information or test results under paragraph (1)(c), the person to whom the request is directed shall not manufacture or import the living organism unless

heading: Additional information or testing
paragraph: (a) the person provides the additional information or submits the test results; and

heading: Additional information or testing
paragraph: (b) the period for assessing information under section 108 has expired or a period of 120 days after the additional information or test results were provided has expired, whichever is later.

heading: Variation of conditions and prohibitions
paragraph: (3) The Minister may vary or rescind a condition or prohibition specified or imposed under paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

heading: Expiry of prohibition
paragraph: (4) Any prohibition on the manufacture or import of a living organism imposed under paragraph (1)(b) expires two years after the day on which it is imposed unless, before the expiry of the two years, there is published in the Canada Gazette

heading: Expiry of prohibition
paragraph: (a) a regulation respecting preventive or control actions, in relation to the living organism, that is proposed to be made under this Act; or

heading: Expiry of prohibition
paragraph: (b) a statement, identifying a regulation respecting preventive or control actions in relation to the living organism that is proposed to be made under any other Act of Parliament,

heading: Expiry of prohibition
paragraph: (i) made jointly by the Minister and the Minister responsible for the administration of the Act of Parliament under which the regulation is to be made, if the Act is not an Act referred to in subparagraph (ii), or

heading: Expiry of prohibition
paragraph: (ii) made by the Minister of Health, if the Act of Parliament is one for whose administration that Minister is responsible.

heading: Expiry of prohibition
paragraph: If such a proposed regulation - or such a statement identifying a proposed regulation - is so published, the prohibition expires on the day on which the regulation comes into force.

heading: Publication of conditions and prohibitions
paragraph: (5) Where the Minister specifies, imposes, varies or rescinds any condition for or prohibition on the manufacture or import of a living organism, the Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette a notice setting out the condition or prohibition and the living organism in respect of which it applies.

heading: Significant new activity
paragraph: 110 (1) Where the Ministers have assessed any information under section 108 in respect of a living organism that is not on the Domestic Substances List and they suspect that a significant new activity in relation to that living organism may result in the living organism becoming toxic, the Minister may, within 90 days after the expiry of the period for assessing the information, publish in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate a notice indicating that subsection 106(4) applies with respect to the living organism.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (2) A notice referred to in subsection (1)

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (a) shall indicate, by inclusion or exclusion, the significant new activities in relation to the living organism with respect to which subsection 106(4) is to apply and, if regulations in respect of those significant new activities are not made under paragraphs 114(1)(c), (d) and (g), specify the information to be provided to the Minister under that subsection, the date on or before which it is to be provided and the period within which it is to be assessed under section 108; and

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (b) may specify for the purpose of subsection 111(2) classes of persons who are not required to be notified under subsection 111(1) with respect to the living organism.

heading: Classes of persons
paragraph: (3) The Minister may, by notice published in the Canada Gazette, specify for the purpose of subsection 111(2) classes of persons who are not required to be notified under subsection 111(1) with respect to a living organism for which a notice was published under subsection (1), if no such class was specified in that notice.

heading: Subsequent notice
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, by notice published in the Canada Gazette,

heading: Subsequent notice
paragraph: (a) vary the significant new activities in relation to a living organism for which a notice has been published under subsection (1) or vary the information to be provided to the Minister under subsection 106(4), the date on or before which that information is to be provided or the period within which it is to be assessed under section 108;

heading: Subsequent notice
paragraph: (b) indicate that subsection 106(4) no longer applies with respect to that living organism;

heading: Subsequent notice
paragraph: (c) vary the classes of persons, if any, that are specified for the purpose of subsection 111(2) in a notice published under subsection (1) or (3); or

heading: Subsequent notice
paragraph: (d) indicate that a class of persons is no longer specified for the purpose of subsection 111(2).

heading: Notification of persons required to comply
paragraph: 111 (1) Where a notice is published in the Canada Gazette under subsection 110(1) in respect of a living organism, every person who transfers the physical possession or control of the living organism shall notify all persons to whom the possession or control is transferred of the obligation to comply with subsection 106(4).

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A person who is within a class of persons that is specified in a notice published under subsection 110(1) or (3) - or, if the class is varied by a notice published under subsection 110(4), within the class as varied - is not required to be notified under subsection (1) with respect to the living organism to which the notice relates.

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: 112 (1) The Minister shall add a living organism to the Domestic Substances List within 120 days after the following conditions are met:

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: (a) the Minister has been provided with information in respect of the living organism under section 106 or 107 and any additional information or test results required under subsection 109(1);

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: (b) the Ministers are satisfied that the living organism has been manufactured in or imported into Canada by the person who provided the information prescribed for the purpose of this paragraph;

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: (c) the period for assessing the information under section 108 has expired; and

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: (d) no conditions specified under paragraph 109(1)(a) in respect of the living organism remain in effect.

heading: Amendment of List
paragraph: (2) Where the Minister adds a living organism to the Domestic Substances List and subsequently learns that the living organism was not manufactured or imported as described in subsection (1), the Minister shall delete the living organism from the List.

heading: Significant new activity
paragraph: (3) If a living organism is on the Domestic Substances List or is to be added to the List under subsection (1) or 105.1(1), the Minister may amend the List to indicate that subsection 106(3) applies with respect to the living organism.

heading: Contents of amendment
paragraph: (4) An amendment referred to in subsection (3)

heading: Contents of amendment
paragraph: (a) shall indicate, by inclusion or exclusion, the significant new activities in relation to the living organism with respect to which subsection 106(3) is to apply and, if regulations in respect of those significant new activities are not made under paragraphs 114(1)(c), (d) and (g), specify the information to be provided to the Minister under that subsection, the date on or before which it is to be provided and the period within which it is to be assessed under section 108; and

heading: Contents of amendment
paragraph: (b) may specify for the purpose of subsection 112.1(2) classes of persons who are not required to be notified under subsection 112.1(1) with respect to the living organism.

heading: Subsequent amendment
paragraph: (5) The Minister may amend the Domestic Substances List in respect of a living organism with respect to which subsection 106(3) applies

heading: Subsequent amendment
paragraph: (a) to vary the significant new activities in relation to the living organism or vary the information to be provided to the Minister under subsection 106(3), the date on or before which that information is to be provided or the period within which it is to be assessed under section 108;

heading: Subsequent amendment
paragraph: (b) to indicate that subsection 106(3) no longer applies;

heading: Subsequent amendment
paragraph: (c) to specify classes of persons for the purpose of subsection 112.1(2), if no such classes are specified with respect to the living organism;

heading: Subsequent amendment
paragraph: (d) to vary the classes of persons, if any, that are specified for the purpose of subsection 112.1(2); or

heading: Subsequent amendment
paragraph: (e) to delete any class of persons that is specified for the purpose of subsection 112.1(2).

heading: Notification of persons required to comply
paragraph: 112.1 (1) If a living organism is specified on the Domestic Substances List with an indication that subsection 106(3) applies with respect to the living organism, every person who transfers the physical possession or control of the living organism shall notify all persons to whom the possession or control is transferred of the obligation to comply with that subsection.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A person is not required to be notified under subsection (1) with respect to a living organism if they are within a class of persons that is specified on the Domestic Substances List in respect of the living organism for the purpose of this subsection.

heading: Publication of masked name
paragraph: 113 Where the publication under this Part of the explicit biological name of a living organism would result in the release of confidential business information in contravention of section 314, the living organism shall be identified by a name determined in the prescribed manner.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 114 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Ministers, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting living organisms or establishing groups of living organisms for the purposes of the provision of information under section 106 or 107, including those that are exotic or indigenous, research and development living organisms and living organisms manufactured only for export, and designating ecozones or groups of ecozones;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing conditions and circumstances for the purpose of paragraph 106(6)(b);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the information that shall be provided to the Minister under subsection 106(1), (3) or (4) or section 107 and the form and manner in which it is to be provided;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) prescribing dates on or before which information shall be provided under subsection 106(1), (3) or (4);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the maintenance of books and records for the administration of any regulation made under this section;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) prescribing the purpose for which a living organism must be used so as to permit the waiver of information requirements under subsection 106(8);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) prescribing periods within which the Ministers shall assess information under subsection 108(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g.1) prescribing a living organism or group of living organisms for the purpose of subsection 108.1(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) respecting the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed in developing test data on a living organism in order to comply with the information requirements of section 106 or 107 or requests for information under paragraph 109(1)(c);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) prescribing information for the purpose of paragraph 112(1)(b);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) prescribing the manner of determining a name for a living organism for the purpose of section 113; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) generally for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Part.

heading: Prescribed assessment period
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of sections 106 and 108, where no assessment period is prescribed or specified with respect to a living organism, the prescribed assessment period is 120 days after the Minister is provided with the prescribed information.

heading: Prescription of conditions and circumstances
paragraph: (3) Regulations made under paragraph (1)(b) may prescribe conditions and circumstances in respect of a living organism in terms of

heading: Prescription of conditions and circumstances
paragraph: (a) whether or not the living organism is a member of a group of living organisms established by regulations made under paragraph (1)(a); or

heading: Prescription of conditions and circumstances
paragraph: (b) the purposes for which the living organism is manufactured or imported.

heading: Prescription of information and assessment periods
paragraph: (4) Regulations made under paragraph (1)(c), (d) or (g) may prescribe information, dates or periods in respect of a living organism in terms of

heading: Prescription of information and assessment periods
paragraph: (a) whether or not the living organism is a member of a group of living organisms established by regulations made under paragraph (1)(a);

heading: Prescription of information and assessment periods
paragraph: (b) the purposes for which the living organism is manufactured or imported; or

heading: Prescription of information and assessment periods
paragraph: (c) the conditions under which and the circumstances in which the living organism is manufactured or imported.

heading: Other regulations
paragraph: 115 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Ministers, make regulations

heading: Other regulations
paragraph: (a) for the purposes of implementing an international agreement,

heading: Other regulations
paragraph: (i) respecting living organisms, whether or not they are on the Domestic Substances List, and

heading: Other regulations
paragraph: (ii) respecting the safety of the environment or human health, including the safe transfer, handling and uses of any living organism that is moved across a boundary; and

heading: Other regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the effective and safe use of living organisms in pollution prevention.

heading: Living organisms regulated under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council shall not make a regulation under subsection (1) in respect of any living organism if the regulation regulates an aspect of the living organism that is regulated by or under any other Act of Parliament in a manner that provides, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, sufficient protection to the environment and human health.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 116 The definitions in this section apply in this Division and in Part 10.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: cleaning product means a phosphate compound or other substance that is intended to be used for cleaning purposes, and includes laundry detergents, dish-washing compounds, metal cleaners, de-greasing compounds and household, commercial and industrial cleaners. (produit de nettoyage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: nutrient means a substance or combination of substances that, if released in any waters, provides nourishment that promotes the growth of aquatic vegetation. (substance nutritive)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: water conditioner means a substance that is intended to be used to treat water, and includes water-softening chemicals, anti-scale chemicals and corrosion inhibiters. (conditionneur d'eau)

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 117 No person shall manufacture for use or sale in Canada or import a cleaning product or water conditioner that contains a prescribed nutrient in a concentration greater than the permissible concentration prescribed for that product or conditioner.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 118 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for the purpose of preventing or reducing the growth of aquatic vegetation that is caused by the release of nutrients in waters and that can interfere with the functioning of an ecosystem or degrade or alter, or form part of a process of degrading or altering, an ecosystem to an extent that is detrimental to its use by humans, animals or plants, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing nutrients;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing the permissible concentration of a prescribed nutrient in a cleaning product or water conditioner;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for analysing, testing, measuring or monitoring a nutrient, cleaning product or water conditioner; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) requiring persons who manufacture for use or sale in Canada or import a cleaning product or water conditioner

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) to maintain books and records for the proper administration of this Division and the regulations,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii) to submit samples of the cleaning product or water conditioner to the Minister, and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (iii) to submit to either Minister information regarding cleaning products, water conditioners and their ingredients.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (1.1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations exempting a cleaning product or water conditioner from the application of section 117.

heading: Class of cleaning product or water conditioner
paragraph: (1.2) Regulations made under subsection (1) or (1.1) may distinguish among classes of cleaning products or water conditioners that they may establish on the basis of any factor, including

heading: Class of cleaning product or water conditioner
paragraph: (a) the physical or chemical properties of the cleaning products or water conditioners; or

heading: Class of cleaning product or water conditioner
paragraph: (b) the conditions under which, the purposes for which or the manner or place in which the cleaning products or water conditioners are intended to be used.

heading: Nutrients regulated under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council shall not make a regulation under subsection (1) in respect of a nutrient to the extent that the nutrient, or a product in which the nutrient is contained, is, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, regulated by or under any other Act of Parliament in a manner that provides, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, sufficient protection to the environment.

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: 119 (1) Where there is a contravention of section 117 or the regulations, the Minister may, in writing, direct a manufacturer or importer of a nutrient, cleaning product or water conditioner to take any or all of the following measures in the manner and within the period directed by the Minister:

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (a) give public notice of the contravention and of any danger to the environment or to human life or health posed by the nutrient, cleaning product or water conditioner;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (b) mail a notice as described in paragraph (a) to manufacturers, processors, distributors or retailers of the nutrient, cleaning product or water conditioner;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (c) mail a notice as described in paragraph (a) to persons to whom the nutrient, cleaning product or water conditioner is known to have been delivered or sold;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (d) replace the nutrient, cleaning product or water conditioner with one that meets the applicable requirements;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (e) accept the return of the nutrient, cleaning product or water conditioner from the purchaser and refund the purchase price;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (f) take other measures for the protection of the environment or human life or health; and

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (g) report to the Minister on the steps taken in satisfaction of any direction under paragraphs (a) to (f).

heading: Intervention of Minister
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to take any measures required under paragraph (1)(a), (b), (c) or (f), the Minister may take those measures or cause them to be taken.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (3) Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover the costs and expenses of and incidental to taking any measures under subsection (2) from the person referred to in that subsection.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 120 The definitions in this section apply in this Division.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: land-based sources means point and diffuse sources on land from which substances or energy reach the sea by water, through the air or directly from the coast. It includes any sources under the sea bed made accessible from land by tunnel, pipeline or other means. (sources telluriques)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: marine pollution means the introduction by humans, directly or indirectly, of substances or energy into the sea that results, or is likely to result, in

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) hazards to human health;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) harm to living resources or marine ecosystems;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) damage to amenities; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) interference with other legitimate uses of the sea. (pollution des mers)

heading: Objectives, guidelines and codes of practice
paragraph: 121 (1) The Minister may, after consultation with any other affected minister, issue environmental objectives, release guidelines and codes of practice to prevent and reduce marine pollution from land-based sources.

heading: Consultation and conferences
paragraph: (2) To carry out the functions set out in subsection (1), the Minister

heading: Consultation and conferences
paragraph: (a) shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with any government department or agency or any person interested in the protection of the sea;

heading: Consultation and conferences
paragraph: (b) may organize conferences relating to the prevention or reduction of marine pollution from land-based sources; and

heading: Consultation and conferences
paragraph: (c) may meet with the representatives of international organizations and agencies and other countries to examine the rules, standards, practices and procedures recommended under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, signed by Canada on October 7, 1982.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (3) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with paragraph (2)(a), the Minister may act under subsection (1) if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 122 (1) The definitions in this subsection apply in this Division and in Part 10.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aircraft means a machine that is used or designed for navigation in the air, but does not include an air cushion vehicle. (aeronef)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian aircraft means an aircraft that is registered under an Act of Parliament. (aeronef canadien)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian permit means a permit that is issued under subsection 127(1) or 128(2). (permis canadien)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian ship means a ship that is registered under an Act of Parliament. (navire canadien)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: condition means, in respect of a permit, any term or condition of the permit. (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: contracting party means a state that is a contracting party to the Convention or the Protocol. (partie contractante)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Convention means the Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter signed by Canada on December 29, 1972, as amended from time to time. (Convention)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: disposal means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the disposal of a substance at sea from a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the disposal of dredged material into the sea from any source not mentioned in paragraph (a),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the storage on the seabed, in the subsoil of the seabed or on the ice in any area of the sea of a substance that comes from a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the deposit of a substance on the ice in an area of the sea,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) the disposal at sea of a ship or aircraft,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) the disposal or abandonment at sea of a platform or another structure, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) any other act or omission that constitutes a disposal under regulations made under paragraph 135(3)(c),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) a disposal of a substance that is incidental to or derived from the normal operations of a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure or of any equipment on a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure, other than the disposal of substances from a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure operated for the purpose of disposing of such substances at sea,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) the placement of a substance for a purpose other than its mere disposal if the placement is not contrary to the purposes of this Division and the aims of the Convention or the Protocol,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (j) the abandonment of any matter, such as a cable, pipeline or research device, placed on the seabed or in the subsoil of the seabed for a purpose other than its mere disposal, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (k) a discharge or storage directly arising from, or directly related to, the exploration for, exploitation of and associated off-shore processing of seabed mineral resources. (immersion)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: incineration means the combustion of a substance on board a ship, a platform or another structure at sea for the purpose of its thermal destruction. (incineration)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: master means the person in command or charge of a ship, but does not include a licensed pilot, within the meaning of section 1.1 of the Pilotage Act. (capitaine)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: owner, in relation to any ship, aircraft, platform or other structure, includes the person who has the possession or use, by law or contract, of the ship, aircraft, platform or other structure. (proprietaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Protocol means the 1996 Protocol to the Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes and Other Matter, 1972, as amended from time to time. (Protocole)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ship includes a vessel, boat or craft designed, used or capable of being used solely or partly for marine navigation, without regard to its method or lack of propulsion, and includes an air cushion vehicle. (navire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: structure means a structure that is made by a person. (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: waste or other matter means waste or other matter listed in Schedule 5. (dechets ou autres matieres)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Definition of sea

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) In this Division and in Part 10, sea means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the territorial sea of Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the internal waters of Canada, excluding all the rivers, lakes and other fresh waters in Canada and the St. Lawrence River as far seaward as the straight lines drawn

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) from Cap-des-Rosiers to the western-most point of Anticosti Island, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) from Anticosti Island to the north shore of the St. Lawrence River along the meridian of longitude sixty-three degrees west;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any exclusive economic zone that may be created by Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the arctic waters within the meaning of section 2 of the Arctic Waters Pollution Prevention Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) an area of the sea adjacent to the areas referred to in paragraphs (a) to (d) that is specified under paragraph 135(1)(g);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) an area of the sea under the jurisdiction of a foreign state, other than its internal waters; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) an area of the sea, other than the internal waters of a foreign state, not included in the areas of the sea referred to in paragraphs (a) to (f).

heading: Purpose
paragraph: 122.1 The purpose of this Division is to protect the marine environment, particularly by implementing the Convention and the Protocol.

heading: Imports for disposal in waters under Canadian jurisdiction
paragraph: 123 (1) No person or ship shall import a substance for disposal in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e).

heading: Export for disposal in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (2) No person or ship shall export a substance for disposal in an area of the sea under the jurisdiction of a foreign state or in its internal waters.

heading: Loading in Canada for disposal at sea
paragraph: 124 (1) No person shall, in Canada, load a substance onto any ship, aircraft, platform or other structure for the purpose of disposal in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) and (g) unless

heading: Loading in Canada for disposal at sea
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter; and

heading: Loading in Canada for disposal at sea
paragraph: (b) the loading is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Loading in Canada for disposal at sea
paragraph: (1.1) No ship shall, in Canada, load a substance onto itself for the purpose of disposal in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) and (g) unless

heading: Loading in Canada for disposal at sea
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter; and

heading: Loading in Canada for disposal at sea
paragraph: (b) the loading is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Responsibility of master and pilot in Canada
paragraph: (2) The master of a ship or pilot in command of an aircraft shall not permit a substance to be loaded onto their ship or aircraft in Canada for the purpose of disposal in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) and (g) unless

heading: Responsibility of master and pilot in Canada
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter; and

heading: Responsibility of master and pilot in Canada
paragraph: (b) the loading is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Responsibility of master and pilot outside Canada
paragraph: (3) The master of a Canadian ship or pilot in command of a Canadian aircraft shall not permit a substance to be loaded onto their ship or aircraft outside Canada for the purpose of disposal at sea.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not apply where

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the disposal occurs in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(g) or in an area of the sea that is under the jurisdiction of the foreign state where the substance is loaded;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) if the disposal occurs in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(g) and the loading occurs in the territory of a foreign state that is a contracting party, the loading and disposal are done in accordance with a permit issued under the Convention or the Protocol by that state;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (d) if the disposal occurs in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(g) and the loading occurs in the territory of a foreign state that is not a contracting party, the loading and disposal are done in accordance with a Canadian permit;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (e) if the disposal occurs in an area of the sea under the jurisdiction of a foreign state that is a contracting party, the loading and disposal are done in accordance with a permit issued under the Convention or the Protocol by that state; and

heading: Exception
paragraph: (f) if the disposal occurs in an area of the sea under the jurisdiction of a foreign state that is not a contracting party, the loading is done in accordance with a Canadian permit and the disposal is authorized by that state.

heading: Disposal in waters under Canadian jurisdiction
paragraph: 125 (1) No person or ship shall dispose of a substance in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) unless

heading: Disposal in waters under Canadian jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter; and

heading: Disposal in waters under Canadian jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) the disposal is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters that are not under the jurisdiction of any state
paragraph: (2) No person shall dispose of a substance from a Canadian ship, a Canadian aircraft or a Canadian platform or other structure in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(g) unless

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters that are not under the jurisdiction of any state
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter; and

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters that are not under the jurisdiction of any state
paragraph: (b) the disposal is done in accordance with a Canadian permit or, if the substance was loaded in the territory of a state that is a contracting party, a permit issued under the Convention or the Protocol by that state.

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters that are not under the jurisdiction of any state
paragraph: (2.1) No Canadian ship shall dispose of a substance in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(g) unless

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters that are not under the jurisdiction of any state
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter; and

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters that are not under the jurisdiction of any state
paragraph: (b) the disposal is done in accordance with a Canadian permit or, if the substance was loaded in the territory of a state that is a contracting party, a permit issued under the Convention or the Protocol by that state.

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (3) No person shall dispose of a substance from a Canadian ship, a Canadian aircraft or a Canadian platform or other structure in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(f) unless

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter;

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) the substance was loaded in the foreign state that has jurisdiction over that area;

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (c) if the foreign state is a contracting party, the disposal is done in accordance with a permit issued under the Convention or the Protocol by that contracting party; and

heading: Disposal from Canadian ship, etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (d) if the foreign state is not a contracting party, that state has authorized the disposal and it is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (3.1) No Canadian ship shall dispose of a substance in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(f) unless

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste or other matter;

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) the substance was loaded in the foreign state that has jurisdiction over that area;

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (c) if the foreign state is a contracting party, the disposal is done in accordance with a permit issued under the Convention or the Protocol by that contracting party; and

heading: Disposal by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (d) if the foreign state is not a contracting party, that state has authorized the disposal and it is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Disposal of Canadian ship, etc., in waters that are not under the jurisdiction of any state
paragraph: (4) No person shall dispose of a Canadian ship, a Canadian aircraft or a Canadian platform or other structure in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(g) unless the disposal is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Disposal of Canadian ship etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (5) No person shall dispose of a Canadian ship, a Canadian aircraft or a Canadian platform or other structure in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(f) unless

heading: Disposal of Canadian ship etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) if the foreign state that has jurisdiction over that area is a contracting party, the disposal is done in accordance with a permit issued under the Convention or the Protocol by that contracting party; and

heading: Disposal of Canadian ship etc., in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) if the foreign state that has jurisdiction over that area is not a contracting party, that state has authorized the disposal and it is done in accordance with a Canadian permit.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (6) This section does not apply in respect of any disposal that is authorized under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Incineration
paragraph: 126 (1) No person shall incinerate a substance on board a ship, a platform or another structure in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) unless

heading: Incineration
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste generated on board the ship, platform or other structure during normal operations; or

heading: Incineration
paragraph: (b) the incineration is done in accordance with a permit issued under subsection 128(2).

heading: Incineration by ship
paragraph: (1.1) No ship shall incinerate a substance on board the ship in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) unless

heading: Incineration by ship
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste generated on board the ship during normal operations; or

heading: Incineration by ship
paragraph: (b) the incineration is done in accordance with a permit issued under subsection 128(2).

heading: Incineration in waters under foreign jurisdiction, etc.
paragraph: (2) No person shall incinerate a substance on board a Canadian ship or a Canadian platform or other structure in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(f) or (g) unless

heading: Incineration in waters under foreign jurisdiction, etc.
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste generated on board the Canadian ship or the Canadian platform or other structure during normal operations; or

heading: Incineration in waters under foreign jurisdiction, etc.
paragraph: (b) the incineration is done in accordance with a permit issued under subsection 128(2).

heading: Incineration by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (3) No Canadian ship shall, in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(f) or (g), incinerate a substance on board the ship unless

heading: Incineration by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) the substance is waste generated on board the ship during normal operations; or

heading: Incineration by Canadian ship in waters under foreign jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) the incineration is done in accordance with a permit issued under subsection 128(2).

heading: Permit
paragraph: 127 (1) The Minister may, on application, issue a permit authorizing the loading for disposal and disposal of waste or other matter and, subject to the regulations, renew it no more than four times.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) The application must

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) be in the prescribed form;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) contain the information that may be prescribed or that may be required by the Minister for the purpose of complying with Schedule 6;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) be accompanied by the prescribed fees; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) be accompanied by evidence that notice of the application was published in a newspaper circulating in the vicinity of the loading or disposal described in the application or in any other publication specified by the Minister.

heading: Factors for consideration
paragraph: (3) Before issuing a permit under subsection (1) or renewing it, the Minister shall comply with Schedule 6 and shall take into account any factors that the Minister considers necessary.

heading: Exception
paragraph: 128 (1) Paragraphs 125(1)(a), (2)(a), (2.1)(a), (3)(a) and (3.1)(a) do not apply if a permit is issued under this section.

heading: Permits for emergency disposal
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, on application, issue a permit to dispose of or incinerate a substance if the Minister is of the opinion that

heading: Permits for emergency disposal
paragraph: (a) the disposal or incineration of a certain quantity of the substance is necessary to avert an emergency that poses an unacceptable risk relating to the environment or to human health; and

heading: Permits for emergency disposal
paragraph: (b) there is no other feasible solution.

heading: Application
paragraph: (3) An application for a permit must

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) be in the prescribed form;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) contain the information that may be prescribed or that may be required by the Minister for the purpose of complying with Schedule 6;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) be accompanied by the prescribed fees; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) subject to subsection (4), be accompanied by evidence that notice of the application was published in a newspaper circulating in the vicinity of the loading, disposal or incineration described in the application or in any other publication specified by the Minister.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (4) The Minister may permit the publication referred to in paragraph (3)(d) to be made at any time after the application is made.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (a) offer to consult with any foreign state that is likely to be affected by the disposal or incineration and with the International Maritime Organization; and

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (b) endeavour to follow any recommendations that are received from the International Maritime Organization.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (6) The Minister shall inform the International Maritime Organization of any action taken under this section.

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: 129 (1) A Canadian permit shall contain any conditions that the Minister considers necessary for the protection of marine life, any legitimate uses of the sea or human life, including conditions relating to the following:

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: (a) the nature and quantity of the substance for loading, disposal or incineration;

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: (b) the method and frequency of the disposal or incineration authorized including, if necessary, the date or dates on which disposal or incineration is authorized;

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: (c) the manner of loading and stowing the substance authorized for disposal or incineration;

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: (d) the site at which disposal or incineration may take place;

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: (e) the route to be followed by the ship or aircraft transporting the substance to the disposal or incineration site;

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: (f) any special precautions to be taken respecting the loading, transporting, disposal or incineration of the substance; and

heading: Conditions of permit
paragraph: (g) the monitoring of the disposal, the incineration and the disposal site to determine the effects of the disposal on the environment and human life.

heading: Duration of permit
paragraph: (2) A Canadian permit shall specify that it is valid for a particular date or dates or for a particular period that shall not exceed one year. For greater certainty, this subsection applies to each renewal of a permit issued under subsection 127(1).

heading: Powers to suspend, revoke or vary permit
paragraph: (3) The Minister may suspend or revoke a Canadian permit or vary its conditions where, having regard to Schedule 6 or the establishment of, or any report of, a board of review under section 333, the Minister considers it advisable to do so.

heading: Exception
paragraph: 130 (1) Despite the other provisions of this Division, a person may dispose of a substance if

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) it is necessary to avert a danger to human life or to a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure at sea in situations caused by stress of weather or in any other case that constitutes a danger to human life or a threat to a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure at sea;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the disposal appears to be the only way of averting the danger or threat; and

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) it is probable that the damage caused by the disposal would be less than would otherwise occur.

heading: Danger to be minimized
paragraph: (2) Any disposal under subsection (1) shall be carried out in a manner that minimizes, as far as possible, danger to human life and damage to the marine environment.

heading: Negligence not a defence
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply if the danger was caused or contributed to by the person's negligent act or omission.

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (4) If disposal takes place under subsection (1), the master of the ship, the pilot in command of the aircraft or the person in charge of the platform or other structure shall report the disposal without delay to an enforcement officer or any other person whom the Governor in Council may, by order, designate, at the location and in the manner that may be prescribed, and the report shall contain any information that may be prescribed.

heading: Fisheries Act not applicable
paragraph: 131 If a person disposes of a substance in accordance with the conditions of a Canadian permit or section 130, subsection 36(3) of the Fisheries Act is not applicable.

heading: Monitoring of sites
paragraph: 132 The Minister shall monitor sites selected by the Minister that are used for disposal or incineration at sea.

heading: Publication
paragraph: 133 (1) When issuing a Canadian permit or varying any of its conditions or renewing a permit issued under subsection 127(1), the Minister shall publish the text of the permit, the varied condition or the renewed permit, as the case may be, in the Environmental Registry.

heading: Publication before disposal or loading
paragraph: (2) Publication under subsection (1) shall be made

heading: Publication before disposal or loading
paragraph: (a) in the case of a permit issued under subsection 128(2), as soon as possible after the permit is issued; and

heading: Publication before disposal or loading
paragraph: (b) in every other case, at least seven days before the effective date of the permit, the variation of its conditions or its renewal.

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: 134 (1) Any person may file with the Minister a notice of objection requesting that a board of review be established under section 333 and stating the reasons for the objection, if the Minister

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: (a) issues or refuses a Canadian permit;

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: (a.1) renews or refuses to renew a permit issued under subsection 127(1); or

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: (b) suspends or revokes a Canadian permit or varies its conditions, otherwise than in accordance with the recommendations of a report of a board of review established under section 333 in respect of the permit.

heading: Time for filing notice of objection
paragraph: (2) The notice of objection shall be filed within seven days after

heading: Time for filing notice of objection
paragraph: (a) the date the text of the Canadian permit or the permit renewed under subsection 127(1), as the case may be, is published in the Environmental Registry; or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 135 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Division and Schedule 6, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) for carrying out and giving effect to the provisions of the Convention or the Protocol;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) defining the expression Canadian platform or other structure;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b.1) respecting time limits for issuing permits under subsection 127(1) or for refusing to issue them, specifying the circumstances under which any of those time limits do not apply and authorizing the Minister to extend any of those time limits or to decide that a time limit does not apply when the Minister considers that it is appropriate to do so;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b.2) respecting the renewal of permits under subsection 127(1), including regulations respecting time limits for renewing them or for refusing to renew them, specifying the circumstances under which any of those time limits do not apply and authorizing the Minister to extend any of those time limits or to decide that a time limit does not apply when the Minister considers that it is appropriate to do so;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the report referred to in subsection 130(4);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the conduct of sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for sampling, analysing, testing, measuring or monitoring;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the monitoring of disposal sites;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) specifying, for the purpose of paragraph 122(2)(e), areas of the sea adjacent to areas referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (d);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) limiting the quantity or concentration of a substance contained in waste or other matter for disposal; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) prescribing any other thing that by this Division is to be prescribed.

heading: Amendments to Schedules 5 and 6
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, by order, amend Schedules 5 and 6.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (3) The Minister may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing the form of an application for a Canadian permit or for the renewal of a permit issued under subsection 127(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) specifying the information required to be contained in or to accompany an application referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) specifying acts or omissions that constitute a disposal for the purposes of paragraph (g) of the definition disposal in subsection 122(1);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) specifying, for the purposes of paragraph (h) of the definition disposal in subsection 122(1), the operations that are deemed to be, or deemed not to be, the normal operations of a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure or of any equipment on a ship, an aircraft, a platform or another structure;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) specifying, for the purposes of subsections 125(1) to (3.1), disposals that are deemed to be, or deemed not to be, disposals of substances referred to in paragraph (h) of the definition disposal in subsection 122(1), which specifications may refer, among other things, to any quantity or concentration of any substance or to any place or area; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) specifying, for the purposes of section 126, the operations that are deemed to be, or deemed not to be, normal operations of ships, including Canadian ships.

heading: Costs and expenses recoverable
paragraph: 136 If the Minister directs an action to be taken by or on behalf of Her Majesty in right of Canada to remedy a condition or mitigate damage resulting from an offence under this Act that arises out of this Division, the costs and expenses of and incidental to taking that action, to the extent that they can be established to have been reasonably incurred in the circumstances, are recoverable by Her Majesty in right of Canada from the person or ship that committed the offence with costs in proceedings brought or taken therefor in the name of Her Majesty in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Manner of service
paragraph: 137 Except where otherwise provided by any rules of the Federal Court that are applicable to proceedings arising out of this Division, any document that, for the purposes of any such proceedings, is to be served on a person may be served

heading: Manner of service
paragraph: (a) in any case, by delivering a copy of the document personally to the person to be served or, if the person cannot be found, by leaving a copy at their latest known address;

heading: Manner of service
paragraph: (b) if the document is to be served on the master of a ship or on any other person employed on a ship and service cannot reasonably be effected in the manner provided in paragraph (a), by leaving a copy of the document for the master or other person on board the ship with the person who is, or appears to be, in command or charge of the ship;

heading: Manner of service
paragraph: (c) if the document is to be served on the pilot in command of an aircraft and service cannot reasonably be effected in the manner provided in paragraph (a), by leaving a copy of the document with the person who is, or appears to be, in charge of the aircraft; and

heading: Manner of service
paragraph: (d) if the document is to be served on a person in their capacity as owner or master of a ship or owner or pilot in command of an aircraft and service cannot reasonably be effected in the manner provided in paragraph (a) and the ship or aircraft is within an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) or in Canada, by leaving a copy of the document with any agent of the owner residing in Canada or, where no such agent is known or can be found, by affixing a copy of it to a prominent part of the ship or aircraft.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 138 The definitions in this section apply in this Division.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: engine means a device that transforms one form of energy into another. (moteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: national fuels mark means a mark established by regulation for use in respect of fuels. (marque nationale)

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 139 (1) No person shall produce, import or sell a fuel that does not meet the prescribed requirements.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (2) A person does not contravene subsection (1) if

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a) the fuel is in transit through Canada, from a place outside Canada to another place outside Canada, and there is written evidence establishing that the fuel is in transit;

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (b) subject to the regulations, the fuel is produced or sold for export and there is written evidence establishing that the fuel will be exported;

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (c) subject to the regulations, the fuel is being produced or imported and there is written evidence establishing that the fuel will meet the requirements of subsection (1) before the fuel is used or sold;

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (d) subject to the regulations, the fuel is being imported in a fuel tank that supplies the engine of a conveyance that is used for transportation by water, land or air; or

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (e) that person is exempted from the application of that subsection by a regulation made under subsection 140(3).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 140 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes of section 139 and may make regulations respecting

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) the concentrations or quantities of an element, component or additive in a fuel;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) the physical or chemical properties of a fuel;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) the characteristics of a fuel, based on a formula related to the fuel's properties or conditions of use;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c.1) the blending of fuels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) the transfer and handling of a fuel;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) the keeping of books and records by persons who produce, sell or import fuel or blend fuels;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) the auditing of the books and records and the submission of audit reports and copies of the books and records;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) the submission by persons who produce, sell or import fuel or blend fuels of information regarding

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) the fuel and any element, component or additive contained in the fuel,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii) any physical or chemical property of the fuel or any substance intended for use as an additive to the fuel,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (iii) the adverse effects from the use of the fuel, or any additive contained in the fuel, on the environment, on human life or health, on combustion technology and on emission control equipment, and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (iv) the techniques that may be used to detect and measure elements, components, additives and physical and chemical properties;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) the conduct of sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring of fuels and additives and the submission of the results;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) the submission of samples of fuels and additives;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for conducting sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) the submission of reports on the quantity of fuel produced, imported or sold for export.

heading: Significant contribution
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may make a regulation under any of paragraphs (1)(a) to (d) if the Governor in Council is of the opinion that the regulation could make a significant contribution to the prevention of, or reduction in, air pollution resulting from

heading: Significant contribution
paragraph: (a) directly or indirectly, the fuel or any of its components; or

heading: Significant contribution
