paragraph: (b) the fuel's effect on the operation, performance or introduction of combustion or other engine technology or emission control equipment.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations exempting from the application of subsection 139(1) any producer or importer in respect of any fuel that they produce or import in quantities of less than 400 m3 per year.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (4) Before recommending a regulation to the Governor in Council under subsection (1), the Minister shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in the quality of the environment.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (5) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with subsection (4), the Minister may recommend a regulation to the Governor in Council under subsection (1) if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Review
paragraph: (6) Within one year after this subsection comes into force and every two years thereafter, a comprehensive review of the environmental and economic aspects of biofuel production in Canada should be undertaken by such committee of the Senate, of the House of Commons or of both Houses of Parliament as may be designated or established by the Senate or the House of Commons, or by both Houses of Parliament, as the case may be, for that purpose.

heading: Report
paragraph: (7) The committee referred to in subsection (6) should, within one year after a review is undertaken pursuant to that subsection, submit a report on the review to Parliament, including a statement of any recommendations that the committee makes in respect of biofuel production in Canada.

heading: Nature of mark
paragraph: 141 (1) The national fuels marks are national trademarks.

heading: Property rights
paragraph: (2) The exclusive property in and, except as otherwise provided in this Division, the right to the use of the national fuels marks are hereby vested in Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 142 (1) No person shall use a national fuels mark except in accordance with this Division and the regulations.

heading: Confusing marks
paragraph: (2) No person shall use any other mark in such a manner that it is likely to be mistaken for a national fuels mark.

heading: Requirements for use
paragraph: 143 A person may use a national fuels mark in respect of a prescribed fuel if

heading: Requirements for use
paragraph: (a) the use is authorized by the Minister;

heading: Requirements for use
paragraph: (b) the fuel conforms to the requirements for that fuel provided for by regulations made under section 145 and any requirements that are applicable to that fuel and that may be provided for by regulations made under subsection 93(1) or 140(1);

heading: Requirements for use
paragraph: (c) evidence of such conformity has been obtained and produced in accordance with the regulations; and

heading: Requirements for use
paragraph: (d) prescribed information relating to the fuel has been submitted to the Minister in the prescribed manner.

heading: Cross-boundary shipments
paragraph: 144 (1) No person shall import, or transport within Canada, a prescribed fuel if the requirements set out in paragraphs 143(b) to (d) are not met.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (2) Except as otherwise provided by the regulations, subsection (1) does not apply if

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a) the requirements are met before the fuel is used or sold; or

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (b) the fuel is being used in a fuel tank that supplies the engine of a conveyance that is used for transportation by water, land or air.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 145 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of sections 141 to 144 and 147, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) establishing the national fuels marks;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) determining the fuels for which a national fuels mark may be used;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting any condition or requirement that must be met for a national fuels mark to be used if, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, regulations respecting that condition or requirement may not be made under section 140;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the conditions and procedures for obtaining authorization to use a national fuels mark;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the information or other evidence necessary under sections 143 and 144; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) prescribing or providing for anything that by sections 141 to 144 and 147 is to be prescribed or provided for by the regulations.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) Before recommending a regulation to the Governor in Council under subsection (1), the Minister shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in the quality of the environment.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (3) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with subsection (2), the Minister may recommend a regulation to the Governor in Council under subsection (1) if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Temporary waiver
paragraph: 147 The Minister may, in prescribed circumstances, grant a temporary waiver from any of the requirements of a regulation made under section 140 or 145 on any conditions and for any period that may be determined by the Minister.

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: 148 (1) If, in respect of a fuel, there is a contravention of this Division or a regulation made under this Division, the Minister may, in writing, direct a producer, processor, importer, retailer or distributor of the fuel to take any or all of the following measures in a manner and within the period directed by the Minister:

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (a) give public notice of the relevant characteristics of the fuel and of any danger to the environment or to human life or health that might be posed by the fuel;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (b) mail a notice as described in paragraph (a) to producers, processors, importers, retailers or distributors of the fuel;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (c) mail a notice as described in paragraph (a) to persons to whom the fuel is known to have been delivered or sold;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (d) replace the fuel with fuel that meets the applicable requirements;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (e) accept the return of the fuel from the purchaser and refund the purchase price;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (f) take other measures to mitigate the effect of the contravention on the environment or on human life or health; and

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (g) report to the Minister on the steps taken in satisfaction of any direction under paragraphs (a) to (f).

heading: Intervention of Minister
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to take any measures required under paragraph (1)(a), (b), (c) or (f), the Minister may take those measures or cause them to be taken.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (3) Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover the costs and expenses of and incidental to taking any measures under subsection (2) from the person referred to in that subsection.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 149 The definitions in this section apply in this Division and in Part 10 as it relates to the enforcement of this Division.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: company means a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is engaged in the business of manufacturing vehicles, engines or equipment in Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is engaged in the business of selling to other persons, for the purpose of resale by those persons, vehicles, engines or equipment obtained directly from a person described in paragraph (a) or the agent of such a person; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) imports any vehicle, engine or equipment into Canada for the purpose of sale. (entreprise)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: engine means any prescribed internal combustion engine, but does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an engine designed to propel an aircraft as defined in subsection 3(1) of the Aeronautics Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an engine designed to propel rolling stock as defined in section 6 of the Canada Transportation Act; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a marine compression-ignition engine that is rated at 37 kW or more and is designed to propel a vessel. (moteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: equipment means any prescribed equipment that is designed for use in or on a vehicle or engine. (equipement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: manufacture includes any process of assembling or altering any vehicle, engine or equipment before its sale to the first retail purchaser. (fabrication ou construction)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: national emissions mark means a mark established by regulation for use in respect of emissions from vehicles, engines or equipment. (marque nationale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: standard means a standard that governs the design, construction, functioning or marking of vehicles, engines or equipment for the purpose of controlling or monitoring their emissions. (norme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vehicle means any prescribed self-propelled vehicle, but does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an aircraft as defined in subsection 3(1) of the Aeronautics Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) rolling stock as defined in section 6 of the Canada Transportation Act; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a vessel that is fitted, for the purpose of propulsion, with a marine compression-ignition engine that is rated at 37 kW or more. (vehicule)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vessel means a boat, ship or craft designed, used or capable of being used solely or partly for navigation in, on, through or immediately above water. (batiment)

heading: Nature of marks
paragraph: 150 (1) The national emissions marks are national trademarks.

heading: Property rights
paragraph: (2) The exclusive property in and, except as otherwise provided in this Division, the right to use a national emissions mark are hereby vested in Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (3) No person shall use a national emissions mark except in accordance with this Division and the regulations.

heading: Confusing marks
paragraph: (4) No person shall use any other mark in such a manner that it is likely to be mistaken for a national emissions mark.

heading: Use of marks
paragraph: 151 A company authorized by the Minister may, subject to this Division and the regulations, apply a national emissions mark to vehicles, engines or equipment.

heading: Transportation within Canada
paragraph: 152 No company shall transport within Canada a prescribed vehicle, engine or equipment that does not have a national emissions mark applied to it.

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: 153 (1) No company shall apply a national emissions mark to any vehicle, engine or equipment, sell any vehicle, engine or equipment to which a national emissions mark has been applied or import any vehicle, engine or equipment unless

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (a) the vehicle, engine or equipment conforms to the standards prescribed for vehicles, engines or equipment of its class at the time its main assembly or manufacture was completed;

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (b) evidence of such conformity has been obtained and produced in the prescribed form and manner or, if the regulations so provide, in a form and manner satisfactory to the Minister;

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (c) prescribed information relating to standards for emissions from the vehicle, engine or equipment has been submitted to the Minister in the prescribed manner;

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (d) information is marked on the vehicle, engine or equipment in accordance with the regulations;

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (e) if required by the regulations, prescribed documentation or accessories accompany the vehicle, engine or equipment;

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (f) prescribed information relating to the operation or use of the vehicle, engine or equipment is disseminated in the prescribed form and manner;

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (g) records are maintained and furnished in the prescribed form and manner in relation to the design, manufacture, testing and field performance of the vehicle, engine or equipment, for the purpose of

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (i) enabling an enforcement officer to determine whether the vehicle, engine or equipment conforms to all prescribed standards applicable to it, and

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (ii) facilitating the identification and analysis of defects referred to in subsection 157(1); and

heading: Compliance by companies
paragraph: (h) in the case of engines and equipment, the company maintains a registration system in the prescribed form and manner.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Except as otherwise provided by the regulations, subsection (1) does not apply with respect to the application of a national emissions mark or an importation referred to in that subsection if the requirements under that subsection are met before the vehicle, engine or equipment leaves the possession or control of the company and, in the case of a vehicle, before the vehicle is presented for registration under the laws of a province or an aboriginal government.

heading: Certification by foreign agency
paragraph: (3) Any vehicle, engine or equipment is deemed to conform to a prescribed standard if

heading: Certification by foreign agency
paragraph: (a) the regulations provide that an enactment of a foreign government corresponds to that standard; and

heading: Certification by foreign agency
paragraph: (b) a prescribed agency of that government has certified that the vehicle, engine or equipment conforms to the enactment as applied by the agency, unless the Minister determines otherwise.

heading: Compliance on importation
paragraph: 154 No person shall import any vehicle, engine or equipment of a prescribed class unless the requirements of paragraphs 153(1)(a), (b), (d) and (e) are met in respect of the vehicle, engine or equipment.

heading: Exceptions for certain importations
paragraph: 155 (1) Sections 153 and 154 do not apply in respect of the importation of any vehicle, engine or equipment if

heading: Exceptions for certain importations
paragraph: (a) the person importing the vehicle, engine or equipment makes a declaration in the prescribed form and manner that the vehicle, engine or equipment will be used in Canada solely for purposes of exhibition, demonstration, evaluation or testing and will remain in Canada for not longer than one year or any other period that the Minister specifies;

heading: Exceptions for certain importations
paragraph: (b) the vehicle, engine or equipment is in transit through Canada, from a place outside Canada, to another place outside Canada and is accompanied by written evidence establishing that the vehicle, engine or equipment will not be sold or used in Canada; or

heading: Exceptions for certain importations
paragraph: (c) the vehicle, engine or equipment is being imported exclusively for use by a visitor to Canada or by a person passing through Canada to another country.

heading: Vehicle from United States or Mexico
paragraph: (2) Sections 153 and 154 do not apply in respect of the importation of a vehicle that has been sold at the retail level in the United States, or that is a prescribed vehicle from Mexico, if the vehicle satisfies the conditions specified in the regulations, if any, and if the person importing it makes a declaration in the prescribed form and manner that,

heading: Vehicle from United States or Mexico
paragraph: (a) within the prescribed period, the applicable requirements of those sections will be met and, if required by the regulations, the vehicle will be inspected in accordance with them; and

heading: Vehicle from United States or Mexico
paragraph: (b) before the vehicle is presented for licensing under the laws of a province or an aboriginal government, the vehicle will be certified, in accordance with the regulations, as conforming to the applicable requirements of those sections.

heading: Change in standard since manufacture
paragraph: (3) Sections 153 and 154 do not apply in respect of the importation of any vehicle, engine or equipment that does not conform to a standard prescribed for its class at the time of its main assembly or manufacture if, at the time of its importation, that standard is no longer in effect and

heading: Change in standard since manufacture
paragraph: (a) the vehicle, engine or equipment conforms to the corresponding standard prescribed for its class at that time; or

heading: Change in standard since manufacture
paragraph: (b) there is no corresponding standard at that time.

heading: Imported vehicle or engine
paragraph: (4) A vehicle or engine that is imported and for which there is no prescribed standard must conform to the standard prescribed for the class of equivalent vehicles or engines before presentation for registration under the laws of a province or an aboriginal government.

heading: Declarations binding
paragraph: (5) No person who makes a declaration referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or subsection (2), or provides evidence referred to in paragraph (1)(b), in respect of any vehicle, engine or equipment shall use or dispose of the vehicle, engine or equipment in a manner contrary to the terms of that declaration or evidence.

heading: Record keeping
paragraph: (6) Every person who makes a declaration referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or subsection (2), or provides evidence referred to in paragraph (1)(b), in respect of any vehicle, engine or equipment shall keep a record of the use or disposition of the vehicle, engine or equipment in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Exemption from standards
paragraph: 156 (1) On application by a company in the prescribed form, supported by prescribed technical and financial information, the Governor in Council may, by order, grant an exemption for a specified period, subject to any conditions specified in the order, for any model of vehicle or engine manufactured or imported by the company from conformity with any prescribed standard applicable to that model if conformity with that standard would, in the opinion of the Governor in Council,

heading: Exemption from standards
paragraph: (a) create substantial financial hardship for the company;

heading: Exemption from standards
paragraph: (b) impede the development of new features for safety, emission monitoring or emission control that are equivalent to or superior to those that conform to prescribed standards; or

heading: Exemption from standards
paragraph: (c) impede the development of new kinds of vehicles, engines or vehicle or engine systems or components.

heading: Period and extent of exemption
paragraph: (2) An exemption for a model may be granted for a period not exceeding

heading: Period and extent of exemption
paragraph: (a) three years, if paragraph (1)(a) applies; or

heading: Period and extent of exemption
paragraph: (b) two years, in respect of a stated number of units of that model not exceeding 1,000 units, if paragraph (1)(b) or (c) applies.

heading: Conditions for granting exemption
paragraph: (3) An exemption may not be granted for a model if the exemption would substantially diminish the control of emissions from it or if the company applying for the exemption has not provided evidence that satisfies the Governor in Council that it has attempted in good faith to bring the model into conformity with all applicable prescribed standards.

heading: Further conditions
paragraph: (4) An exemption for substantial financial hardship may not be granted under paragraph (1)(a) if

heading: Further conditions
paragraph: (a) the world production of vehicles or engines manufactured by the company, or by the manufacturer of the model that is the subject of the application, exceeded 10,000 vehicles or engines in the 12-month period beginning two years before the beginning of the exemption period; or

heading: Further conditions
paragraph: (b) the total number of vehicles or engines manufactured for, or imported into, the Canadian market by the company exceeded 1,000 vehicles or engines in that 12-month period.

heading: Renewal of exemption
paragraph: (5) On the expiry of the exemption period, a new exemption may be granted in accordance with this section.

heading: Obligation to give notice
paragraph: 157 (1) A company that manufactures, sells or imports any vehicle, engine or equipment of a class for which standards are prescribed shall, on becoming aware of a defect in the design, construction or functioning of the vehicle, engine or equipment that affects or is likely to affect its compliance with a prescribed standard, cause notice of the defect to be given in the prescribed manner to

heading: Obligation to give notice
paragraph: (a) the Minister;

heading: Obligation to give notice
paragraph: (b) each person who has obtained such a vehicle, engine or equipment from the company; and

heading: Obligation to give notice
paragraph: (c) each current owner of such a vehicle, engine or equipment.

heading: Determining owners
paragraph: (2) Current owners are to be determined for the purpose of subsection (1)

heading: Determining owners
paragraph: (a) from a warranty issued by the company with respect to the functioning of the vehicle, engine or equipment that has, to its knowledge, been given, sold or transferred to the current owner;

heading: Determining owners
paragraph: (b) in the case of a vehicle, from registration records of a government; or

heading: Determining owners
paragraph: (c) in the case of an engine or equipment, from a registration system referred to in paragraph 153(1)(h).

heading: If notice previously given
paragraph: (3) A company is not required to cause notice to be given of a defect of which notice has already been given under this section or under section 10 of the Motor Vehicle Safety Act.

heading: Publication of notice
paragraph: (4) If the Minister is satisfied that the name of the current owner of the vehicle, engine or equipment cannot reasonably be determined by a company in accordance with subsection (2), the Minister may

heading: Publication of notice
paragraph: (a) order the company to give notice of the defect by publication in the prescribed form for a period of five consecutive days in two major daily newspapers in each of the following six regions, namely, the Atlantic provinces, Quebec, Ontario, the Prairie provinces, British Columbia and the Territories, or by dissemination in an alternative medium for any period that the Minister determines; or

heading: Publication of notice
paragraph: (b) order that the current owner need not be notified.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (5) A notice required to be given under subsections (1) and (4) shall contain, in the form and to the extent prescribed, a description of the defect, an evaluation of the pollution risk arising from it and directions for correcting it.

heading: Particulars to responsible authorities
paragraph: (6) On receiving a notice under subsection (1), the Minister shall forward full particulars of the notice to the person responsible for vehicle or engine administration in each government.

heading: Follow-up reports
paragraph: (7) Every company that causes notice to be given under subsection (1) shall submit an initial report and subsequent regular reports respecting the defect and its correction in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Frequency of reports
paragraph: (8) Unless the Minister directs otherwise, the reports referred to in subsection (7) shall be submitted for a period of two years after the day on which notice was given under subsection (1).

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: 158 The Minister may

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (a) conduct any research, studies and evaluations that the Minister considers necessary for the administration and enforcement of this Division;

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (b) undertake research and development programs for the study of the effect of vehicles, engines or equipment or emissions on air pollution, energy conservation and the environment and for the promotion of measures to control that effect;

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (c) establish and operate facilities for the testing of vehicles, engines or equipment and components, and acquire test equipment for that purpose;

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (d) make the facilities referred to in paragraph (c) and all related material, parts and services available to any person; and

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (e) publish or otherwise disseminate information relating to the activities of the Minister under this section.

heading: Emission control tests
paragraph: 159 (1) At the request of the Minister and subject to payment by the Minister of the cost of transportation and of rental at a prescribed rate based on capital value, a company shall make available for testing any vehicle, engine, equipment or component that

heading: Emission control tests
paragraph: (a) was used in tests conducted by or for the company in order to establish information submitted to the Minister under paragraph 153(1)(c); or

heading: Emission control tests
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of that testing, is equivalent to a vehicle, an engine, equipment or a component referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Testing by Minister
paragraph: (2) The Minister may examine and dismantle any vehicle, engine, equipment or component made available under subsection (1) and conduct all necessary tests to verify the accuracy of tests referred to in paragraph (1)(a).

heading: Detention of vehicles or engines
paragraph: (3) The Minister may not detain any vehicle, engine, equipment or component for more than 90 days after completion of the tests conducted under subsection (2) unless, before that time, proceedings have been instituted in respect of an offence related to the vehicle, engine, equipment or component, in which case it may be detained until the proceedings are concluded.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 160 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Division, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting emissions and prescribing standards in relation to emissions;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) establishing the national emissions marks;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the conditions that must be met for a national emissions mark to be used in relation to vehicles, engines or equipment or a class of vehicles, engines or equipment;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the manner of applying national emissions marks;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) prescribing the period for which records referred to in paragraph 153(1)(g) or a registration system referred to in paragraph 153(1)(h) shall be retained;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting exemptions from sections 153 and 154;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the information to be submitted under section 153;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g.1) respecting inspection and certification referred to in subsection 155(2) and, in particular, designating any person who is authorized to inspect or certify vehicles; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) prescribing or providing for anything that by this Division is to be prescribed or provided for by the regulations.

heading: Progressive application
paragraph: (2) Regulations prescribing a standard may be made applicable in respect of a specified proportion of vehicles, engines or equipment of a class before they are made applicable in respect of all vehicles, engines or equipment of that class.

heading: Progressive application
paragraph: Definition of technical standards document

heading: Progressive application
paragraph: 161 (1) In this section, technical standards document means a document, published in the prescribed manner by authority of the Minister, that reproduces in the official languages of Canada an enactment of a foreign government with any adaptations of form and reference that will facilitate the incorporation of the enactment under this section.

heading: Incorporation of document
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, regulations made under this Division may incorporate by reference a technical standards document as it reads on a prescribed day or as it is amended from time to time following the incorporation by reference, and may extend, qualify or exclude the application of any provision of the document so incorporated.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (3) No person is required to comply with a provision of a technical standards document incorporated by the regulations until six months after the publication of the provision in the prescribed manner, if the person continues to comply with the provision for which that provision is substituted.

heading: Document not a regulation
paragraph: (4) A technical standards document is not a regulation for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Emission credits
paragraph: 162 (1) Regulations that prescribe standards in relation to emissions may provide for a system of credits based on the following principles:

heading: Emission credits
paragraph: (a) a company may establish that vehicles, engines or equipment conform to those standards by applying credits against emissions of the vehicles, engines or equipment in the prescribed manner and within prescribed limits;

heading: Emission credits
paragraph: (b) credits may be obtained by a company in the prescribed manner

heading: Emission credits
paragraph: (i) by reference to emissions of the vehicles, engines or equipment that more than meet the requirements of those standards, or

heading: Emission credits
paragraph: (ii) by the payment of an amount to the Receiver General determined at a prescribed rate in relation to emissions of the vehicle, engine or equipment; and

heading: Emission credits
paragraph: (c) credits obtained by reference to emissions may be transferred to or from a company in the prescribed manner.

heading: Deemed conformity to standard
paragraph: (2) Regulations referred to in subsection (1) may provide that any vehicle, engine or equipment is deemed to conform to a standard if the application of those regulations to all vehicles, engines or equipment of its class sold in Canada and the United States would result in that vehicle, engine or equipment so conforming.

heading: Emission report
paragraph: (3) Every company shall submit to the Minister, in the prescribed form and manner and at the prescribed time, a report setting out, with respect to a prescribed period, an account of any emission credits obtained or applied by the company and a description of each of the following vehicles, engines or pieces of equipment for which credits were obtained or applied:

heading: Emission report
paragraph: (a) vehicles, engines and equipment to which the company applied a national emissions mark during that period, other than those that were exported;

heading: Emission report
paragraph: (b) vehicles, engines and equipment bearing a national emissions mark that were sold by the company in Canada during that period; and

heading: Emission report
paragraph: (c) vehicles, engines and equipment that were imported by the company during that period for the purpose of sale in Canada.

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (4) If credits applied under this section were obtained on the basis of emissions from vehicles, engines or equipment not referred to in paragraph (3)(a), (b) or (c), the report submitted in respect of the application of those credits shall include a description of those vehicles, engines or equipment.

heading: Interim order
paragraph: 163 (1) If an enactment of a foreign government corresponds to the regulations made under this Division and that enactment is amended by that government or its operation is affected by a decision of a foreign court, the Minister may issue an interim order suspending or modifying the operation of the regulations to the extent that they are inconsistent with the enactment as amended or given effect.

heading: Effective date of order
paragraph: (2) An interim order has effect from the time it is made.

heading: Approval of Governor in Council
paragraph: (3) An interim order ceases to have effect 14 days after it is made unless it is approved by the Governor in Council within that period.

heading: Contravention of regulation modified by an unpublished order
paragraph: (4) No person shall be convicted of an offence consisting of a contravention of a regulation to the extent that it is modified or suspended by an interim order that, at the time of the alleged contravention, had not been published in the Canada Gazette unless it is proved that, at the time of the alleged contravention, the person had been notified of the interim order.

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (3), an interim order ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (c) one year after the order is made.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: 164 In a prosecution under this Act, evidence that any vehicle, engine or equipment bore a name or mark purporting to be the name or mark of a company engaged in the business of manufacturing, importing or selling vehicles, engines or equipment is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, proof that the vehicle, engine or equipment was manufactured, imported or sold, as the case may be, by the company.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: 165 In a prosecution under this Act, evidence that any vehicle, engine or equipment bearing a national emissions mark was manufactured by a company is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, proof that the national emissions mark was applied by the company.

heading: Determination of international air pollution
paragraph: 166 (1) Subject to subsection (4), the Minister shall act under subsections (2) and (3) only if the Ministers have reason to believe that a substance released from a source in Canada into the air creates, or may reasonably be anticipated to contribute to

heading: Determination of international air pollution
paragraph: (a) air pollution in a country other than Canada; or

heading: Determination of international air pollution
paragraph: (b) air pollution that violates, or is likely to violate, an international agreement binding on Canada in relation to the prevention, control or correction of pollution.

heading: Consultation with other governments
paragraph: (2) If the source referred to in subsection (1) is not a federal source, the Minister shall

heading: Consultation with other governments
paragraph: (a) consult with the government responsible for the area in which the source is situated to determine whether that government can prevent, control or correct the air pollution under its laws; and

heading: Consultation with other governments
paragraph: (b) if the government referred to in paragraph (a) can prevent, control or correct the air pollution, offer it an opportunity to do so.

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (3) If the source referred to in subsection (1) is a federal source or if the government referred to in paragraph (2)(a) cannot prevent, control or correct the air pollution under its laws or does not do so, the Minister shall take at least one of the following courses of action:

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (a) on approval by the Governor in Council, publish a notice under subsection 56(1); or

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (b) recommend regulations to the Governor in Council for the purpose of preventing, controlling or correcting the air pollution.

heading: Reciprocity with other country
paragraph: (4) If the air pollution referred to in paragraph (1)(a) is in a country where Canada does not have substantially the same rights with respect to the prevention, control or correction of air pollution as that country has under this Division, the Minister shall decide whether to act under subsections (2) and (3) or to take no action at all.

heading: Other factors
paragraph: (5) When recommending regulations under paragraph (3)(b), the Minister shall take into account comments made under subsection 168(2), notices of objection filed under subsection 332(2) and any report of a board of review submitted under subsection 340(1).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 167 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations with respect to a substance released from a source in Canada into the air that creates, or may reasonably be anticipated to contribute to air pollution referred to in subsection 166(1) for the purpose of preventing, controlling or correcting the air pollution, including regulations respecting

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) the quantity or concentration of the substance that may be released into the air;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) the manner in which and conditions under which the substance may be released into the air, either alone or in combination with any other substance;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) the maintenance of books and records for the administration of any regulation made under this section;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) the conduct of sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring of the substance and the submission of the results to the Minister; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for conducting sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring of the substance.

heading: Notice to other country
paragraph: 168 (1) The Minister shall advise the government of any country that would be affected by or benefit from the regulation before it is published under subsection 332(1).

heading: Comments
paragraph: (2) Within 60 days after the publication of a proposed regulation under subsection 332(1), any person, including a representative of the government of any country that would be affected by or benefit from it, may file with the Minister written comments on the proposed regulation.

heading: Notice to other governments
paragraph: (3) At the end of the period of 60 days referred to in subsection (2), the Minister

heading: Notice to other governments
paragraph: (a) shall advise each government referred to in paragraph 166(2)(a) of any notice of objection filed under subsection 332(2); and

heading: Notice to other governments
paragraph: (b) shall publish in the Canada Gazette, and may publish in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, a report or a notice of the availability of a report that summarizes how any written comments filed under subsection (2) or a notice of objection filed under subsection 332(2) were dealt with.

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: 169 (1) Where there occurs or there is a likelihood of a release into the air of a substance in contravention of a regulation made under section 167, any person described in subsection (2) shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances,

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (4) and the regulations, notify an enforcement officer or any other person designated pursuant to the regulations and provide a written report on the matter to the enforcement officer or other person;

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (b) take all reasonable measures consistent with the protection of the environment and public safety to prevent the release or, if it cannot be prevented, to remedy any dangerous condition or reduce or mitigate any danger to the environment or to human life or health that results from the release of the substance or may reasonably be expected to result if the substance is released; and

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (c) make a reasonable effort to notify any member of the public who may be adversely affected by the release or likely release.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies to any person who

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) owns or has charge of a substance immediately before its release or its likely release into the air; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) causes or contributes to the release or increases the likelihood of the release.

heading: Report by property owner
paragraph: (3) Where there occurs a release of a substance as described in subsection (1), any person, other than a person described in subsection (2), whose property is affected by the release shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances and subject to subsection (4), report the matter to an enforcement officer or to any person that is designated by regulation.

heading: Report to official
paragraph: (4) Where there are in force, by or under the laws of a province or an aboriginal government, provisions that the Governor in Council, by regulation, declares to be adequate for dealing with a release described in subsection (1), a report required by paragraph (1)(a) or subsection (3) shall be made to a person designated by those provisions.

heading: Intervention by enforcement officer
paragraph: (5) Where a person fails to take any measures required under subsection (1), an enforcement officer may take those measures, cause them to be taken or direct any person referred to in subsection (2) to take them.

heading: Limitation on power of direction
paragraph: (6) Any direction of an enforcement officer under subsection (5) that is inconsistent with a requirement imposed by or under any other Act of Parliament is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Access to property
paragraph: (7) Any enforcement officer or other person authorized or required to take any measures under subsection (1) or (5) may enter and have access to any place or property and may do any reasonable things that may be necessary in the circumstances.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: (8) Any person, other than a person described in subsection (2), who provides assistance or advice in taking the measures required by subsection (1) or who takes any measures authorized under subsection (5) is not personally liable either civilly or criminally in respect of any act or omission in the course of providing assistance or advice or taking any measures under those subsections unless it is established that the person acted in bad faith.

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: 170 (1) Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover the costs and expenses of and incidental to taking any measures under subsection 169(5) from

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: (a) any person referred to in paragraph 169(2)(a); and

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: (b) any person referred to in paragraph 169(2)(b) to the extent of the person's negligence in causing or contributing to the release.

heading: Only if reasonably incurred
paragraph: (2) The costs and expenses referred to in subsection (1) shall only be recovered to the extent that they can be established to have been reasonably incurred in the circumstances.

heading: Liability
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the persons referred to in subsection (1) are jointly and severally liable or solidarily liable for the costs and expenses referred to in that subsection.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (4) A person referred to in paragraph 169(2)(b) shall not be held liable under subsection (3) to an extent greater than the extent of the person's negligence in causing or contributing to the release.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (5) A claim under this section may be sued for and recovered by Her Majesty in right of Canada with costs in proceedings brought or taken therefor in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Recourse or indemnity
paragraph: (6) This section does not limit or restrict any right of recourse or indemnity that a person may have against any other person.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (7) Where events giving rise to a claim under this section occur, no proceedings in respect of the claim may be instituted after five years from the date on which the events occur or become evident to the Minister, whichever is later.

heading: Minister's certificate
paragraph: (8) A document purporting to have been issued by the Minister certifying the day on which the events giving rise to a claim under this section came to the knowledge of the Minister shall be received in evidence and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the document shall be considered as proof of that fact without proof of the signature or of the official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and without further proof.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 171 No person shall carry on a work, undertaking or activity that results in the release of a substance in contravention of a regulation made under section 167.

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: 172 (1) If a person carries on or proposes to carry on a work, undertaking or activity that results or may result in the release of a substance that creates, or may reasonably be anticipated to create, air pollution, the person shall, at the request of the Minister for the purposes of this Division and within the time that the Minister may specify, provide the Minister with plans, specifications, studies, procedures, schedules, analyses, samples or other information relating to the work, undertaking or activity and with analyses, samples, evaluations, studies, mitigation methodologies or other information relating to the substance.

heading: Obtaining information from government
paragraph: (2) Before making a request to a person under subsection (1), the Minister shall try to obtain, within a reasonable time, the samples or information from the government responsible for the area in which the person is situated.

heading: Interim order
paragraph: 173 (1) The Minister may make an interim order that contains any provision that may be contained in a regulation under section 167 if the Minister believes

heading: Interim order
paragraph: (a) that the substance or source referred to in subsection 166(1) is not adequately regulated; and

heading: Interim order
paragraph: (b) that immediate action is required to deal with a significant danger to the environment or to human life or health.

heading: Effective date of order
paragraph: (2) An interim order has effect from the time it is made.

heading: Approval of Governor in Council
paragraph: (3) An interim order ceases to have effect 14 days after it is made unless it is approved by the Governor in Council within that period.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (4) The Governor in Council shall not approve an interim order unless the Minister has

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (a) within 24 hours after making the order, offered to consult with all affected governments to determine whether they are prepared to take sufficient action to deal with the significant danger; and

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (b) consulted with other ministers of the Crown in right of Canada to determine whether any action can be taken under any other Act of Parliament to deal with the significant danger.

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (5) Where the Governor in Council approves an interim order, the Minister shall, within 90 days after the approval, take measures to comply with section 166 in order to address the significant danger that gave rise to the interim order.

heading: Contravention of unpublished order
paragraph: (6) No person shall be convicted of an offence consisting of a contravention of an interim order that, at the time of the alleged contravention, had not been published in the Canada Gazette unless it is proved that, at the time of the alleged contravention, the person had been notified of the interim order.

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (7) Subject to subsection (3), an interim order ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (b) the day a regulation is made in accordance with subsection (5), and

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (c) two years after the order is made.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: 174 The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 a report on the administration of this Division.

heading: DIVISION 7International Water Pollution
paragraph: Definition of water pollution

heading: DIVISION 7International Water Pollution
paragraph: 175 In this Division, water pollution means a condition of water, arising wholly or partly from the presence in water of any substance, that directly or indirectly

heading: DIVISION 7International Water Pollution
paragraph: (a) endangers the health, safety or welfare of humans;

heading: DIVISION 7International Water Pollution
paragraph: (b) interferes with the normal enjoyment of life or property;

heading: DIVISION 7International Water Pollution
paragraph: (c) endangers the health of animal life;

heading: DIVISION 7International Water Pollution
paragraph: (d) causes damage to plant life or to property; or

heading: DIVISION 7International Water Pollution
paragraph: (e) degrades or alters, or forms part of a process of degrading or alterating, an ecosystem to an extent that is detrimental to its use by humans, animals or plants.

heading: Determination of international water pollution
paragraph: 176 (1) Subject to subsection (4), the Minister shall act under subsections (2) and (3) only if the Ministers have reason to believe that a substance released from a source in Canada into water creates, or may reasonably be anticipated to create,

heading: Determination of international water pollution
paragraph: (a) water pollution in a country other than Canada; or

heading: Determination of international water pollution
paragraph: (b) water pollution that violates, or is likely to violate, an international agreement binding on Canada in relation to the prevention, control or correction of pollution.

heading: Consultation with other governments
paragraph: (2) If the source referred to in subsection (1) is a not a federal source, the Minister shall

heading: Consultation with other governments
paragraph: (a) consult with the government responsible for the area in which the source is situated to determine whether that government can prevent, control or correct the water pollution under its laws; and

heading: Consultation with other governments
paragraph: (b) if the government referred to in paragraph (a) can prevent, control or correct the water pollution, offer it an opportunity to do so.

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (3) If the source referred to in subsection (1) is a federal source, or if the government referred to in paragraph (2)(a) cannot prevent, control or correct the water pollution under its laws or does not do so, the Minister shall take at least one of the following courses of action:

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (a) on approval by the Governor in Council, publish a notice under subsection 56(1); or

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (b) recommend regulations to the Governor in Council for the purpose of preventing, controlling or correcting the water pollution.

heading: Reciprocity with other country
paragraph: (4) If the water pollution referred to in paragraph (1)(a) is in a country where Canada does not have substantially the same rights with respect to the prevention, control or correction of water pollution as that country has under this Division, the Minister shall decide whether to act under subsections (2) and (3).

heading: Other factors
paragraph: (5) When recommending regulations under paragraph (3)(b), the Minister shall take into account comments made under subsection 178(2), notices of objection filed under subsection 332(2) and any report of a board of review submitted under subsection 340(1).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 177 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations with respect to a substance released from a source in Canada into water that creates, or may reasonably be anticipated to create, water pollution referred to in subsection 176(1) for the purpose of preventing, controlling or correcting the water pollution, including regulations respecting

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) the quantity or concentration of the substance that may be released into water;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) the manner in which and conditions under which the substance may be released into water, either alone or in combination with any other substance;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) the maintenance of books and records for the administration of any regulation made under this section;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) the conduct of sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring of the substance and the submission of the results to the Minister; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for conducting sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring of the substance.

heading: Notice to other country
paragraph: 178 (1) The Minister shall advise the government of any country that would be affected by or benefit from the regulation before it is published under subsection 332(1).

heading: Comments
paragraph: (2) Within 60 days after the publication of a proposed regulation under subsection 332(1), any person, including a representative of the government of any country that would be affected by or benefit from it, may file with the Minister written comments on the proposed regulation.

heading: Notice to other governments
paragraph: (3) At the end of the period of 60 days referred to in subsection (2), the Minister

heading: Notice to other governments
paragraph: (a) shall advise each government referred to in paragraph 176(2)(a) of any notice of objection filed under subsection 332(2); and

heading: Notice to other governments
paragraph: (b) shall publish in the Canada Gazette, and may publish in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, a report or a notice of the availability of a report that summarizes how any written comments filed under subsection (2) or a notice of objection filed under subsection 332(2) were dealt with.

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: 179 (1) Where there occurs or there is a likelihood of a release into waters of a substance in contravention of a regulation made under section 177, any person described in subsection (2) shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances,

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (4) and the regulations, notify an enforcement officer or any other person designated pursuant to the regulations and provide a written report on the matter to the enforcement officer or other person;

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (b) take all reasonable measures consistent with the protection of the environment and public safety to prevent the release or, if it cannot be prevented, to remedy any dangerous condition or reduce or mitigate any danger to the environment or to human life or health that results from the release of the substance or may reasonably be expected to result if the substance is released; and

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (c) make a reasonable effort to notify any member of the public who may be adversely affected by the release or likely release.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies to any person who

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) owns or has charge of a substance immediately before its release or its likely release into water; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) causes or contributes to the release or increases the likelihood of the release.

heading: Report by property owner
paragraph: (3) Where there occurs a release of a substance as described in subsection (1), any person, other than a person described in subsection (2), whose property is affected by the release shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances and subject to subsection (4), report the matter to an enforcement officer or to any person that is designated by regulation.

heading: Report to official
paragraph: (4) Where there are in force, by or under the laws of a province or an aboriginal government, provisions that the Governor in Council, by regulation, declares to be adequate for dealing with a release described in subsection (1), a report required by paragraph (1)(a) or subsection (3) shall be made to a person designated by those provisions.

heading: Intervention by enforcement officer
paragraph: (5) Where any person fails to take any measures required under subsection (1), an enforcement officer may take those measures, cause them to be taken or direct any person referred to in subsection (2) to take them.

heading: Limitation on power of direction
paragraph: (6) Any direction of an enforcement officer under subsection (5) that is inconsistent with a requirement imposed by or under any other Act of Parliament is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Access to property
paragraph: (7) Any enforcement officer or other person authorized or required to take any measures under subsection (1) or (5) may enter and have access to any place or property and may do any reasonable things that may be necessary in the circumstances.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: (8) Any person, other than a person described in subsection (2), who provides assistance or advice in taking the measures required by subsection (1) or who takes any measures authorized under subsection (5) is not personally liable either civilly or criminally in respect of any act or omission in the course of providing assistance or advice or taking any measures under those subsections unless it is established that the person acted in bad faith.

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: 180 (1) Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover the costs and expenses of and incidental to taking any measures under subsection 179(5) from

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: (a) any person referred to in paragraph 179(2)(a); and

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: (b) any person referred to in paragraph 179(2)(b) to the extent of the person's negligence in causing or contributing to the release.

heading: Only if reasonably incurred
paragraph: (2) The costs and expenses referred to in subsection (1) shall only be recovered to the extent that they can be established to have been reasonably incurred in the circumstances.

heading: Liability
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the persons referred to in subsection (1) are jointly and severally liable or solidarily liable for the costs and expenses referred to in that subsection.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (4) A person referred to in paragraph 179(2)(b) shall not be held liable under subsection (3) to an extent greater than the extent of the person's negligence in causing or contributing to the release.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (5) A claim under this section may be sued for and recovered by Her Majesty in right of Canada with costs in proceedings brought or taken therefor in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Recourse or indemnity
paragraph: (6) This section does not limit or restrict any right of recourse or indemnity that a person may have against any other person.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (7) Where events giving rise to a claim under this section occur, no proceedings in respect of the claim may be instituted after five years from the date on which the events occur or become evident to the Minister, whichever is later.

heading: Minister's certificate
paragraph: (8) A document purporting to have been issued by the Minister certifying the day on which the events giving rise to a claim under this section came to the knowledge of the Minister shall be received in evidence and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the document shall be considered as proof of that fact without proof of the signature or of the official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and without further proof.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 181 No person shall carry on a work, undertaking or activity that results in the release of a substance in contravention of a regulation made under section 177.

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: 182 (1) If a person carries on or proposes to carry on a work, undertaking or activity that results or may result in the release of a substance that creates, or may reasonably be anticipated to create, water pollution, the person shall, at the request of the Minister for the purposes of this Division and within the time that the Minister may specify, provide the Minister with plans, specifications, studies, procedures, schedules, analyses, samples or other information relating to the work, undertaking or activity and with analyses, samples, evaluations, studies, mitigation methodologies or other information relating to the substance.

heading: Obtaining information from government
paragraph: (2) Before making a request to a person under subsection (1), the Minister shall try to obtain, within a reasonable time, the samples or information from the government responsible for the area in which the person is situated.

heading: Interim order
paragraph: 183 (1) The Minister may make an interim order that contains any provision that may be contained in a regulation under section 177 if the Minister believes

heading: Interim order
paragraph: (a) that the substance or source referred to in subsection 176(1) is not adequately regulated; and

heading: Interim order
paragraph: (b) that immediate action is required to deal with a significant danger to the environment or to human life or health.

heading: Effective date of order
paragraph: (2) An interim order has effect from the time it is made.

heading: Approval of Governor in Council
paragraph: (3) An interim order ceases to have effect 14 days after it is made unless it is approved by the Governor in Council within that period.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (4) The Governor in Council shall not approve an interim order unless the Minister has

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (a) within 24 hours after making the order, offered to consult with all affected governments to determine whether they are prepared to take sufficient action to deal with the significant danger; and

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (b) consulted with other ministers of the Crown in right of Canada to determine whether any action can be taken under any other Act of Parliament to deal with the significant danger.

heading: Ministerial action
paragraph: (5) Where the Governor in Council approves an interim order, the Minister shall, within 90 days after the approval, take measures to comply with section 176 in order to address the significant danger that gave rise to the interim order.

heading: Contravention of unpublished order
paragraph: (6) No person shall be convicted of an offence consisting of a contravention of an interim order that, at the time of the alleged contravention, had not been published in the Canada Gazette unless it is proved that, at the time of the alleged contravention, the person had been notified of the interim order.

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (7) Subject to subsection (3), an interim order ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (b) the day a regulation is made in accordance with subsection (5), and

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (c) two years after the order is made.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: 184 The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 a report on the administration of this Division.

heading: Import, export and transit
paragraph: 185 (1) No person shall import, export or convey in transit a hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material, or prescribed non-hazardous waste for final disposal, except

heading: Import, export and transit
paragraph: (a) after notifying the Minister and paying the prescribed fee;

heading: Import, export and transit
paragraph: (b) after receiving from the Minister whichever one of the following permits is applicable:

heading: Import, export and transit
paragraph: (i) an import permit or export permit that, except in the case of a permit issued under subsection (4), states that the authorities of the country of destination and, if applicable, of the country of transit have authorized the movement, and that the authorities of the jurisdiction of destination have authorized the final disposal or recycling of the waste or material, or

heading: Import, export and transit
paragraph: (ii) a transit permit that states that the Minister has authorized the movement; and

heading: Import, export and transit
paragraph: (c) in accordance with the prescribed conditions.

heading: Refusal to issue permit
paragraph: (2) If the Minister is of the opinion that the waste or material will not be managed in a manner that will protect the environment and human health against the adverse effects that may result from that waste or material, the Minister may refuse, in accordance with the criteria set out in the regulations, to issue a permit even if the relevant authorities have given their authorization.

heading: Consultation with governments
paragraph: (3) Before refusing under subsection (2) to issue a permit to import, the Minister shall consult with the government of the jurisdiction of destination.

heading: Special circumstances to issue permits
paragraph: (4) Where the Minister is of the opinion that the waste or material will be managed in a manner that will protect the environment and human health against the adverse effects that may result from that waste or material, the Minister may issue a permit if the relevant authorities inform the Minister that they lack the legal authority to authorize the movement, final disposal or recycling but are not opposed to it.

heading: Prohibitions - import, export and transit
paragraph: 186 (1) For the purpose of implementing international agreements respecting the environment, the Minister may, with the approval of the Governor in Council and taking into account Canada's international obligations, prohibit, completely or partially and under any conditions that may be prescribed, the import, export or transit of waste or material referred to in subsection 185(1).

heading: Prohibition of abandonment
paragraph: (2) No person shall abandon any waste or material referred to in subsection 185(1) in the course of import, export or transit.

heading: Publication
paragraph: 187 After the Minister receives a notification of the proposed import, export or transit of a waste or material referred to in paragraph 185(1)(a), the Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette, or in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, the name or specifications of the waste or material and

heading: Publication
paragraph: (a) in the case of a proposed import, the name of the jurisdiction of origin and the name of the importer;

heading: Publication
paragraph: (b) in the case of a proposed export, the name of the jurisdiction of destination and the name of the exporter; and

heading: Publication
paragraph: (c) in the case of a proposed transit, the names of the jurisdictions of origin and of destination and the name of the conveyor.

heading: Reduction of export for final disposal
paragraph: 188 (1) For the purpose of reducing or phasing out the export of hazardous waste or prescribed non-hazardous waste for final disposal, the Minister may require an exporter, or a class of exporters, of hazardous waste to

heading: Reduction of export for final disposal
paragraph: (a) submit to the Minister, at the same time as the notification referred to in paragraph 185(1)(a) and at any other prescribed time, a plan in accordance with the regulations; and

heading: Reduction of export for final disposal
paragraph: (b) implement that plan.

heading: Declaration of implementation
paragraph: (2) Every person who is required to implement a plan under paragraph (1)(b) shall file with the Minister, within 30 days after the completion of each stage of the plan, a written declaration that the implementation has been completed.

heading: Sanction
paragraph: (3) The Minister may refuse to issue a permit to an exporter who does not comply with subsection (1) or (2).

heading: Movement within Canada
paragraph: 189 (1) No person shall undertake movement within Canada of hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material otherwise than in accordance with this Division and the regulations and unless the person pays the prescribed fee.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette, or in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, information derived from documents received under regulations made for the purpose of this section.

heading: Permits based on equivalent environmental safety level
paragraph: 190 (1) The Minister may issue a permit authorizing, subject to conditions fixed by the Minister, any activity to be conducted in a manner that does not comply with this Division if the Minister is satisfied that

heading: Permits based on equivalent environmental safety level
paragraph: (a) the manner in which the activity will be conducted provides a level of environmental safety at least equivalent to that provided by compliance with this Division; and

heading: Permits based on equivalent environmental safety level
paragraph: (b) in the case of the importation, exportation or transit of a waste or material referred to in subsection 185(1), the activity is consistent with international environmental agreements binding on Canada.

heading: Scope of permit
paragraph: (2) The permit may authorize the activity in terms of the persons who may conduct the activity and in terms of the waste and material that it may involve.

heading: Revocation of permit
paragraph: (3) The Minister may revoke the permit if

heading: Revocation of permit
paragraph: (a) the Minister is of the opinion that paragraph (1)(a) or (b) no longer applies;

heading: Revocation of permit
paragraph: (b) the regulations have been amended and address the activity authorized by the permit; or

heading: Revocation of permit
paragraph: (c) the permit holder does not comply with the conditions of the permit.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette, or in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, a copy of each permit issued under this section.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 191 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations generally for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Division, including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) defining, for the purposes of this Division and Part 10, words and expressions used in this Division, and providing criteria, testing protocols and standards in relation to those definitions;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the notification referred to in paragraph 185(1)(a) and the procedure for applying for a permit under this Division;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) establishing criteria for the purpose of subsection 185(2) that take into account obligations arising from international agreements to which Canada is a party;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) for establishing a classification system for waste and material;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting information and documents to be provided to the Minister;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting conditions governing the import, export, transit and movement within Canada of waste and material;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting plans referred to in subsection 188(1), taking into account

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) the benefit of using the nearest appropriate disposal facility, and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii) changes in the quantity of goods the production of which generates hazardous waste to be disposed of by an exporter or class of exporters; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) prescribing anything that by this Division is to be prescribed.

heading: Forms
paragraph: 192 The Minister may establish forms for the purposes of this Division.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 193 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environmental emergency means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an uncontrolled, unplanned or accidental release, or release in contravention of regulations or interim orders made under this Part, of a substance into the environment; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the reasonable likelihood of such a release into the environment. (urgence environnementale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: substance means, except in sections 199 and 200.1, a substance on a list of substances established under regulations or interim orders made under this Part. (substance)

heading: Application
paragraph: 194 For the purposes of this Part, any power, duty or function conferred or imposed under this Part may only be exercised or performed in relation to those aspects of an environmental emergency that

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) have or may have an immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) constitute or may constitute a danger to the environment on which human life depends; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) constitute or may constitute a danger in Canada to human life or health.

heading: Research
paragraph: 195 Despite subsection 36(3) of the Fisheries Act, subsection 123(1) and regulations made under paragraphs 93(1)(a), (b), (c) and (d) and 209(2)(a), (b), (c) and (d), the Minister may

heading: Research
paragraph: (a) examine and conduct research, including tests, respecting the causes, circumstances and effects of and remedial measures for an environmental emergency; and

heading: Research
paragraph: (b) conduct and publicize demonstration projects.

heading: Guidelines and codes of practice
paragraph: 196 The Minister may issue guidelines and codes of practice respecting the prevention of, preparedness for and response to an environmental emergency and for restoring any part of the environment damaged by or during an emergency.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: 197 (1) In carrying out the responsibilities conferred by section 196, the Minister shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in the quality of the environment or environmental emergencies.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (2) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with subsection (1), the Minister may act under section 196 if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Publication of guidelines and codes of practice
paragraph: 198 The Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette, or in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, guidelines and codes of practice issued under section 196 or a notice stating where copies of those documents may be obtained.

heading: Requirements for environmental emergency plans
paragraph: 199 (1) The Minister may at any time publish in the Canada Gazette, and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, a notice requiring any person or class of persons described in the notice to prepare and implement an environmental emergency plan respecting the prevention of, preparedness for, response to or recovery from an environmental emergency in respect of

heading: Requirements for environmental emergency plans
paragraph: (a) a substance or group of substances specified in Part 1 or 2 of the list of toxic substances in Schedule 1; or

heading: Requirements for environmental emergency plans
paragraph: (b) a substance or group of substances in relation to which there has been published in the Canada Gazette

heading: Requirements for environmental emergency plans
paragraph: (i) a statement of the Ministers under paragraph 77(6)(b) indicating that the measure that they propose to take, as confirmed or amended, is a recommendation that the substance be added to Part 1 or 2 of the list of toxic substances in Schedule 1, or

heading: Requirements for environmental emergency plans
paragraph: (ii) a copy of an order proposed to be made under subsection 90(1).

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (2) The notice shall specify

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (a) the substance or group of substances in relation to which the plan is to be prepared;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (b) the period within which the plan is to be prepared;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (c) the period within which the plan is to be implemented; and

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (d) any other matter that the Minister considers necessary.

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (3) Where the Minister is of the opinion that further time is necessary to prepare or implement the plan, the Minister may extend the period for a person who submits a written request before the expiry of the period referred to in the notice or of any extended period.

heading: Plan prepared or implemented for another purpose
