paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), where a person who is required to prepare or implement an environmental emergency plan under a notice published under this section has prepared or implemented a plan in respect of environmental emergencies on a voluntary basis or for another government or under another Act of Parliament that meets all or some of the requirements of the notice, the person may use that plan for the purposes of meeting the requirements of this Part and, in that case, the plan shall be considered to be an environmental emergency plan that has been prepared or implemented under this Part.

heading: Where partial requirements met
paragraph: (5) Where a person uses a plan under subsection (4) that does not meet all of the requirements of the notice, the person shall

heading: Where partial requirements met
paragraph: (a) amend the plan so that it meets all of those requirements; or

heading: Where partial requirements met
paragraph: (b) prepare an additional environmental emergency plan that meets the remainder of those requirements.

heading: Application of provisions re declarations and keeping plans
paragraph: (6) Sections 58 and 59 apply to environmental emergency plans, with any modifications that the circumstances require, as if any reference to a pollution prevention plan were read as a reference to an environmental emergency plan.

heading: Submission of plans
paragraph: (7) The Minister may publish in the Canada Gazette, and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate, a notice requiring any person or class of persons described in the notice who are required to prepare or implement an environmental emergency plan under subsection (1) or section 291 or under an agreement in respect of environmental protection alternative measures to submit, within the period specified by the Minister, the plan or any part of the plan.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 200 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister and after the Committee is given an opportunity to provide its advice to the Minister under section 6, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) establishing a list of substances that, if they enter the environment as a result of an environmental emergency,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) have or may have an immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment or its biological diversity,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii) constitute or may constitute a danger to the environment on which human life depends, or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (iii) constitute or may constitute a danger in Canada to human life or health;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing, in respect of a substance on the list established under paragraph (a), a minimum quantity;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the identification of the places in Canada where a substance referred to in paragraph (a), in any quantity or in the quantity prescribed for that substance under paragraph (b), is located and requiring notification to the Minister of those places;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the prevention of, preparedness for, response to and recovery from an environmental emergency in respect of a substance;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the notification and reporting of an environmental emergency;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the notification and reporting of the measures taken

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) to prevent the environmental emergency, or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii) to repair, reduce or mitigate any negative effects on the environment or human life or health that result from the environmental emergency or that may reasonably be expected to result from it;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the implementation of international agreements entered into by Canada in relation to environmental emergencies; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) respecting any other matter necessary for the purposes of this Part.

heading: Environmental emergencies regulated under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council shall not make a regulation under subsection (1) in respect of a matter if, by order, the Governor in Council states that it is of the opinion that

heading: Environmental emergencies regulated under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: (a) the matter is regulated by or under any other Act of Parliament that contains provisions that are similar in effect to sections 194 to 205; and

heading: Environmental emergencies regulated under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: (b) that Act or any regulation made under that Act provides sufficient protection to human health and the environment or its biological diversity.

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: 200.1 (1) The Minister may make an interim order, in respect of a substance, that contains any provision that may be contained in a regulation made under this Part, if

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (a) the substance

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (i) is not on the list established under regulations made under this Part and the Ministers believe that, if it enters the environment as a result of an environmental emergency,

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (A) it would have or may have an immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment or its biological diversity,

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (B) it would constitute or may constitute a danger to the environment on which human life depends, or

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (C) it would constitute or may constitute a danger in Canada to human life or health, or

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (ii) is on that list and the Ministers believe that it is not adequately regulated; and

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: (b) the Ministers believe that immediate action is required to deal with a significant danger to the environment or to human life or health.

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), an interim order has effect

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (a) from the time it is made; and

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (b) as if it were a regulation made under this Part.

heading: Approval of Governor in Council
paragraph: (3) An interim order ceases to have effect unless it is approved by the Governor in Council within 14 days after it is made.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (4) The Governor in Council shall not approve an interim order unless the Minister has

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (a) within 24 hours after making the order, offered to consult with all affected governments to determine whether they are prepared to take sufficient action to deal with the significant danger; and

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (b) consulted with other ministers of the Crown in right of Canada to determine whether any action can be taken under any other Act of Parliament to deal with the significant danger.

heading: Recommendation of regulations
paragraph: (5) If the Governor in Council approves an interim order, the Minister shall, within 90 days after the approval, publish in the Canada Gazette a statement indicating whether the Minister intends to recommend to the Governor in Council

heading: Recommendation of regulations
paragraph: (a) that a regulation having the same effect as the order be made under this Part; and

heading: Recommendation of regulations
paragraph: (b) if the order was made in respect of a substance that was not on the list established under regulations made under this Part, that the substance be added to that list.

heading: Contravention of unpublished order
paragraph: (6) No person shall be convicted of an offence consisting of a contravention of an interim order that, at the time of the alleged contravention, had not been published in the Canada Gazette unless it is proved that, at the time of the alleged contravention, the person had been notified of the interim order or reasonable steps had been taken to bring the purport of the interim order to the notice of those persons likely to be affected by it.

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (7) Subject to subsection (3), an interim order ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (b) the day a regulation referred to in subsection (5) is made, and

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (c) two years after the order is made.

heading: Tabling of order
paragraph: (8) A copy of each interim order must be tabled in each House of Parliament within 15 days after it is made.

heading: House not sitting
paragraph: (9) In order to comply with subsection (8), the interim order may be sent to the Clerk of the House if the House is not sitting.

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: 201 (1) Subject to any regulations made under subsection 200(1) or any interim orders made under section 200.1, if there occurs an environmental emergency in respect of a substance on a list established under the regulations or interim orders, any person described in subsection (2) shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances,

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (a) notify an enforcement officer or any other person designated by regulation or interim order and provide a written report on the environmental emergency to the enforcement officer or other person;

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (b) take all reasonable emergency measures consistent with the protection of the environment and public safety

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (i) to prevent the environmental emergency, or

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (ii) to repair, reduce or mitigate any negative effects on the environment or human life or health that result from the environmental emergency or that may reasonably be expected to result from it; and

heading: Remedial measures
paragraph: (c) make a reasonable effort to notify any member of the public who may be adversely affected by the environmental emergency.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies to any person who

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) owns or has the charge, management or control of a substance immediately before the environmental emergency; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) causes or contributes to the environmental emergency.

heading: Report by other persons
paragraph: (3) A person, other than a person described in subsection (2), shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances, report an environmental emergency to an enforcement officer or to a person designated by regulation or interim order if their property is affected by the environmental emergency.

heading: Intervention by enforcement officer
paragraph: (4) Where any person fails to take any measures required under subsection (1), an enforcement officer may take those measures, cause them to be taken or direct any person referred to in subsection (2) to take them.

heading: Limitation on power of direction
paragraph: (5) Any direction of an enforcement officer under subsection (4) that is inconsistent with a requirement imposed by or under any other Act of Parliament is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Access to property
paragraph: (6) Any enforcement officer or other person authorized or required to take any measures under subsection (1) or (4) may enter and have access to any place or property and may do anything reasonable that may be necessary in the circumstances.

heading: Personal liability
paragraph: (7) Any person, other than a person described in subsection (2), who provides assistance or advice in taking the measures required by subsection (1) or who takes any measures authorized under subsection (4) is not personally liable either civilly or criminally in respect of any act or omission in the course of providing assistance or advice or taking any measures under those subsections unless it is established that the person acted in bad faith.

heading: Voluntary report
paragraph: 202 (1) If a person knows about an environmental emergency but the person is not required to report the matter under this Act, the person may report any information about the environmental emergency to an enforcement officer or to a person designated by regulation or interim order.

heading: Request for confidentiality
paragraph: (2) The person making the report may request that their identity and any information that could reasonably reveal their identity not be released.

heading: Requirement of confidentiality
paragraph: (3) No person shall disclose, or have disclosed, the identity of the person making the request or any information that could reasonably be expected to reveal their identity unless the person making the request authorizes the disclosure in writing.

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (4) Despite any other Act of Parliament, no employer shall dismiss, suspend, demote, discipline, harass or otherwise disadvantage an employee, or deny an employee a benefit of employment, by reason that

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (a) the employee has made a report under subsection (1);

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (b) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, has refused or stated an intention of refusing to do anything that is an offence under this Act; or

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (c) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, has done or stated an intention of doing anything that is required to be done by or under this Act.

heading: Recovery of costs and expenses
paragraph: 203 (1) Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover the costs and expenses of and incidental to taking any measures under subsection 201(4) from

heading: Recovery of costs and expenses
paragraph: (a) any person referred to in paragraph 201(2)(a); and

heading: Recovery of costs and expenses
paragraph: (b) any person referred to in paragraph 201(2)(b) to the extent of their negligence or wilful conduct in causing or contributing to the environmental emergency.

heading: Reasonably incurred
paragraph: (2) The costs and expenses referred to in subsection (1) shall only be recovered to the extent that they can be established to have been reasonably incurred in the circumstances.

heading: Liability
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the persons referred to in subsection (1) are jointly and severally liable or solidarily liable for the costs and expenses referred to in that subsection.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (4) A person referred to in paragraph 201(2)(b) shall not be held liable under subsection (3) to an extent greater than the extent of their negligence or wilful conduct in causing or contributing to the environmental emergency.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (5) A claim under this section may be sued for and recovered by Her Majesty in right of Canada with costs in proceedings brought or taken therefor in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Recourse or indemnity
paragraph: (6) This section does not limit or restrict any right of recourse or indemnity that a person may have against any other person.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (7) Where events giving rise to a claim under this section occur, no proceedings in respect of the claim may be instituted after five years from the date on which the events occur or become evident to the Minister, whichever is later.

heading: Minister's certificate
paragraph: (8) A document purporting to have been issued by the Minister certifying the day on which the events giving rise to a claim under this section came to the knowledge of the Minister shall be received in evidence and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the document shall be considered as proof of that fact without proof of the signature or of the official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and without further proof.

heading: National notification and reporting system
paragraph: 204 (1) The Minister may establish, in cooperation with the governments of the provinces and aboriginal governments and government departments or agencies, a national system for the notification and reporting of environmental emergencies.

heading: Copies
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 314, any person may have access to and a copy of any information contained in the national system established under subsection (1).

heading: Liability of owner of substance
paragraph: 205 (1) Subject to this Part, the person who owns or has the charge, management or control of a substance immediately before an environmental emergency is liable

heading: Liability of owner of substance
paragraph: (a) for restoring any part of the environment damaged by or during the emergency;

heading: Liability of owner of substance
paragraph: (b) for costs and expenses incurred by a public department within the meaning of the Criminal Code or other public authority in Canada in respect of measures taken to prevent, repair, remedy or minimize the damage to the environment resulting from the emergency, including measures taken in anticipation of the environmental emergency, to the extent that the measures taken and the costs and expenses are reasonable, and for any loss or damage caused by such measures; and

heading: Liability of owner of substance
paragraph: (c) for costs and expenses incurred by the Minister in respect of measures taken to prevent, repair, remedy or minimize the environmental emergency to the extent that the measures taken and the costs and expenses are reasonable, and for any loss or damage caused by such measures.

heading: Liability of owner of substance
paragraph: Definition of public authority in Canada

heading: Liability of owner of substance
paragraph: (2) In subsection (1), public authority in Canada means Her Majesty in right of a province, an aboriginal government or any other body designated by the Governor in Council for the purposes of that subsection as a public authority in Canada.

heading: Strict liability subject to certain defences
paragraph: (3) The person's liability under subsection (1) does not depend on proof of fault or negligence, but the owner is not liable under that subsection if the owner establishes that the environmental emergency

heading: Strict liability subject to certain defences
paragraph: (a) resulted from an act of war, hostilities or insurrection or from a natural phenomenon of an exceptional, inevitable and irresistible character;

heading: Strict liability subject to certain defences
paragraph: (b) was wholly caused by an act or omission of a third party with intent to cause damage; or

heading: Strict liability subject to certain defences
paragraph: (c) was wholly caused by the negligence or other wrongful act of government, public department or public authority.

heading: Reduced liability
paragraph: (4) Where the person who is liable under subsection (1) establishes that the environmental emergency resulted wholly or partially from

heading: Reduced liability
paragraph: (a) an act or omission done by the person who suffered the damage with intent to cause damage, or

heading: Reduced liability
paragraph: (b) the negligence or wilful conduct of that person,

heading: Reduced liability
paragraph: the liability of the person referred to in subsection (1) to that other person is reduced or nullified in proportion to the degree to which the environmental emergency resulted from the factors mentioned in paragraphs (a) and (b).

heading: Person's rights against third parties preserved
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this Part shall be construed as limiting or restricting any right of recourse that the person who is liable under subsection (1) may have against any other person.

heading: Person's own claim for costs and expenses
paragraph: (6) Costs and expenses incurred by the person referred to in subsection (1) in respect of measures voluntarily taken to prevent, repair, remedy or minimize damage from the environmental emergency, including measures taken in anticipation of an environmental emergency, to the extent that the measures taken and the costs and expenses are reasonable, rank equally with other claims against any security given by that person in respect of that person's liability under this section.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Definition of regulations

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 206 In this Part, regulations means regulations made under this Part.

heading: Application to Government, etc.
paragraph: 207 (1) This Part applies to

heading: Application to Government, etc.
paragraph: (a) departments, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada;

heading: Application to Government, etc.
paragraph: (b) federal works and undertakings;

heading: Application to Government, etc.
paragraph: (c) aboriginal land, federal land, persons on that land and other persons in so far as their activities involve that land; and

heading: Application to Government, etc.
paragraph: (d) Crown corporations, as defined in subsection 83(1) of the Financial Administration Act.

heading: Yukon
paragraph: (1.1) This Part does not apply to public real property under the administration and control of the Commissioner of Yukon pursuant to the Yukon Act.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) This Part does not restrict any of the following powers in so far as they may be exercised in relation to air and all layers of the atmosphere above federal land or aboriginal land:

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (a) powers under the Aeronautics Act or a provision of any other Act of Parliament relating to aeronautics or air transportation; or

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (b) powers under the National Defence Act or a provision of any other Act of Parliament relating to national defence and security.

heading: Minister shall establish
paragraph: 208 (1) The Minister shall establish objectives, guidelines and codes of practice for the purpose of carrying out the Minister's duties and functions under this Part related to the quality of the environment.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) In establishing an objective, a guideline or a code of practice under subsection (1), the Minister

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (a) shall offer to consult with the government of a territory if the objective, guideline or code of practice applies to that territory, and with the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments if it applies to aboriginal land over which an aboriginal government has jurisdiction; and

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (b) may consult with a department, board or agency of the Government of Canada, or a Crown corporation as defined in subsection 83(1) of the Financial Administration Act.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (3) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with paragraph (2)(a), the Minister may act under subsection (1) if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a territory or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: 209 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for the protection of the environment, including regulations respecting

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: (a) the establishment of environmental management systems;

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: (b) pollution prevention and pollution prevention plans;

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: (c) environmental emergencies, releases of substances and likely releases, including their prevention, preparedness for them, reporting them, both as soon as possible in the circumstances and in detail at a later stage, and the measures to be taken to respond to them and to correct damage to the environment;

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: (d) the designation of persons for the purposes of paragraph 212(1)(a) and subsections 212(3) and 213(1) and prescribing the form of the report to be made under those provisions and the information to be contained in it;

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: (e) the circumstances in which a report is not required under paragraph 212(1)(a);

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: (f) any substance; and

heading: Regulations for the protection of the environment
paragraph: (g) any other matter necessary to carry out the purposes of this Part.

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (2) Regulations with respect to any substance may provide for, or impose requirements respecting,

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (a) the quantity or concentration of any substance that may be released into the environment either alone or in combination with any other substance from any source or type of source;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (b) the places or areas where the substance may be released;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (c) the commercial, manufacturing, processing or other activity in the course of which the substance may be released;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (d) the manner in which and the conditions under which the substance may be released into the environment, either alone or in combination with any other substance;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (e) the quantity of the substance that may be manufactured, processed, used, offered for sale or sold in Canada;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (f) the purposes for which the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment may be imported, exported, manufactured, processed, used, offered for sale or sold;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (g) the manner in which and the conditions under which the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment may be imported, exported, manufactured, processed or used;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (h) the quantities or concentrations in which the substance may be used;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (i) the quantities or concentrations of the substance that may be imported or exported;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (j) the countries from or to which the substance may be imported or exported;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (k) the conditions under which, the manner in which and the purposes for which the substance may be imported or exported;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (l) the total, partial or conditional prohibition of the manufacture, use, processing, sale, offering for sale, import or export of the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment and the total, partial or conditional prohibition of the manufacture, import or export of a product that is intended to contain the substance;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (m) the quantity or concentration of the substance that may be contained in any product manufactured, imported, exported, sold or offered for sale in Canada, or that any such product may release into the environment;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (n) the manner in which, the conditions under which and the purposes for which the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment may be advertised or offered for sale;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (o) the manner in which and the conditions under which the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment may be stored, displayed, handled, transported or offered for transport;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (p) the packaging and labelling of the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (q) the manner, conditions, places and method of disposal or recycling of the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment, including standards for the construction, maintenance and inspection of disposal or recycling sites;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (r) the submission to the Minister, on request or at any times that are prescribed, of information relating to the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (s) the maintenance of books and records for the administration of any regulation made under this section;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (t) the conduct of sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring of the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment and the submission of the results to the Minister;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (u) the submission to the Minister of samples of the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (v) the conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices to be followed for conducting sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring of the substance, a product that contains the substance or a product that may release the substance into the environment;

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (w) the circumstances or conditions under which the Minister may, for the proper administration of this Act, modify

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (i) any requirement for sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring, or

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (ii) conditions, test procedures and laboratory practices for conducting any required sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring; and

heading: Content of the regulations
paragraph: (x) the decommissioning and decontamination of storage, handling, transportation, disposal and recycling sites for the substance.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) Before recommending to the Governor in Council a regulation under this section, the Minister

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (a) shall offer to consult with the government of a territory if the regulation applies to that territory, and with the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments if it applies to aboriginal land over which an aboriginal government has jurisdiction; and

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (b) may consult with a department, board or agency of the Government of Canada, or a Crown corporation as defined in subsection 83(1) of the Financial Administration Act.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (4) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with paragraph (3)(a), the Minister may recommend a regulation to the Governor in Council under this section if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a territory or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (5) Regulations made under this section may authorize the Minister, in the circumstances and subject to the conditions and limits that may be specified in the regulations, to issue, amend, suspend and revoke permits and other authorizations in relation to any matter that is the subject of the regulations and to set their terms and conditions.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (6) A permit or other authorization issued under regulations made under this section is not a statutory instrument as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Non-application of regulations
paragraph: 210 Where the Governor in Council is of the opinion that provisions of any other Part of this Act or any other Act of Parliament, or regulations made under them,

heading: Non-application of regulations
paragraph: (a) are in force in respect of an aspect of the protection of the environment,

heading: Non-application of regulations
paragraph: (b) apply to a federal work or undertaking, federal land or aboriginal land, and

heading: Non-application of regulations
paragraph: (c) provide sufficient protection to the environment and human health,

heading: Non-application of regulations
paragraph: the Governor in Council may make an order stating that opinion and, if such an order is made, regulations made under this Part relating to the same aspect do not apply to the federal work or undertaking, the federal land or the aboriginal land.

heading: Minister may require information
paragraph: 211 (1) For the purpose of making regulations, the Minister may require information from any person who carries on, or proposes to carry on, a federal work or undertaking or an activity on federal land or aboriginal land.

heading: Kind of information
paragraph: (2) The required information shall be information that will enable the Minister to determine any environmental effects that the work, undertaking or activity may have, and it may include

heading: Kind of information
paragraph: (a) plans, specifications, studies, procedures, schedules, analyses, samples or other information relating to the work, undertaking or activity; and

heading: Kind of information
paragraph: (b) analyses, samples, evaluations, studies or other information relating to the environment that is or is likely to be affected by the work, undertaking or activity.

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: 212 (1) If a substance is released into the environment in contravention of a regulation, or if there is a likelihood of such a release, a person described in subsection (2) shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances,

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (a) subject to the regulations, notify an enforcement officer or any other person designated pursuant to the regulations and provide a written report on the matter to the enforcement officer or other person;

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (b) take all reasonable measures consistent with the protection of the environment and public safety to prevent or eliminate any dangerous condition or minimize any danger to the environment or to human life or health that results from the release or may reasonably be expected to result if the substance is released; and

heading: Report and remedial measures
paragraph: (c) make a reasonable effort to notify any members of the public who may be adversely affected by the release or likely release.

heading: Application of subsection (1)
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies to any person who

heading: Application of subsection (1)
paragraph: (a) owns or has the charge, management or control of the substance immediately before its release or its likely release into the environment; or

heading: Application of subsection (1)
paragraph: (b) causes or contributes to the release or increases the likelihood of the release.

heading: Report by other persons
paragraph: (3) A person, other than a person described in subsection (2), shall, as soon as possible in the circumstances, report a release of a substance to an enforcement officer or to a person designated by the regulations if their property is affected by the release and they know that the substance has been released in contravention of a regulation.

heading: Intervention by enforcement officer
paragraph: (4) Where measures required by subsection (1) are not taken, an enforcement officer may take them, have them taken or direct a person described in subsection (2) to take them.

heading: Limitation on direction
paragraph: (5) If the direction to the person described in subsection (2) is inconsistent with a requirement imposed by or under any other Act of Parliament, it is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Access to property
paragraph: (6) An enforcement officer or other person authorized or required to take measures under subsection (1) or (4) may, for the purpose of taking those measures, enter and have access to any place or property and may do anything reasonable that may be necessary in the circumstances.

heading: Personal liability
paragraph: (7) A person who provides assistance or advice in taking the measures required by subsection (1), or who takes any measures authorized under subsection (4), is not personally liable either civilly or criminally for any act or omission in the course of providing assistance or advice or taking any measures under those subsections, unless it is established that the person acted in bad faith.

heading: Voluntary report
paragraph: 213 (1) If a person knows about a release or likely release of a substance into the environment in contravention of a regulation but the person is not required to report the matter under this Act, the person may report any information about the release or likely release to an enforcement officer or to a person designated by the regulations.

heading: Request for confidentiality
paragraph: (2) The person making the report may request that their identity and any information that could reasonably reveal their identity not be released.

heading: Requirement of confidentiality
paragraph: (3) No person shall disclose, or have disclosed, the identity of the person making the request or any information that could reasonably be expected to reveal their identity unless the person making the request authorizes the disclosure in writing.

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (4) Despite any other Act of Parliament, no employer shall dismiss, suspend, demote, discipline, harass or otherwise disadvantage an employee, or deny an employee a benefit of employment, by reason that

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (a) the employee has made a report under subsection (1);

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (b) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, has refused or stated an intention of refusing to do anything that is an offence under this Act; or

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (c) the employee, acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, has done or stated an intention of doing anything that is required to be done by or under this Act.

heading: Recovery of costs and expenses
paragraph: 214 (1) The costs and expenses related to taking any measures under subsection 212(4) may be recovered by Her Majesty in right of Canada from

heading: Recovery of costs and expenses
paragraph: (a) any person referred to in paragraph 212(2)(a); and

heading: Recovery of costs and expenses
paragraph: (b) any person referred to in paragraph 212(2)(b) to the extent of their negligence or wilful conduct in causing or contributing to the release.

heading: Reasonably incurred
paragraph: (2) The costs and expenses may only be recovered to the extent that they have been reasonably incurred in the circumstances.

heading: Liability
paragraph: (3) Persons from whom the costs and expenses may be recovered are jointly and severally liable or solidarily liable for them. However, a person mentioned in paragraph 212(2)(b) is not liable to an extent greater than the extent of their negligence or wilful conduct in causing or contributing to the release.

heading: Recourse or indemnity
paragraph: (4) This section does not limit or restrict any right of recourse or indemnity that a person may have against any other person.

heading: Court and costs
paragraph: 215 (1) A claim under section 214 may be recovered with costs in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (2) Where events giving rise to the claim occur, no proceedings in respect of the claim may be instituted more than five years after the date on which the events occur or the Minister becomes aware of them, whichever is later.

heading: Minister's certificate
paragraph: (3) A document purporting to have been issued by the Minister certifying the day on which the events giving rise to a claim under section 214 came to the knowledge of the Minister shall be received in evidence and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the document shall be considered as proof of that fact without proof of the signature or of the official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and without further proof.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 216 The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: conveyance includes any vehicle, ship or aircraft. (moyen de transport)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: foreign national has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. (etranger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: place includes any platform anchored at sea, shipping container or conveyance. (lieu)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: substance includes hazardous wastes, hazardous recyclable material or non-hazardous waste, as those expressions are defined by regulations made under section 191, and waste or other matter listed in Schedule 5. (substance)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Definition of ship that is not a Canadian ship

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 216.1 (1) For the purpose of subsections 217(6), 218(16) and (17) and 220(5.1) and section 275.1, a ship that is not a Canadian ship does not include a ship that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) that is not registered, listed or licensed under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 or under the laws of another state but is owned by one or more persons each of whom is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) a Canadian citizen,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a vessel that is not required to be registered, listed or licensed under that Act, a person who is resident and domiciled in Canada, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii) a corporation incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province, that has its principal place of business in Canada; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) that is not registered, listed or licensed under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 but is owned or operated by Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Definition of committed in the course of enforcement of this Act

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsections 217(4) and 271.1(2), sections 275.1 and 278.1 and subsections 279(1) and (3), committed in the course of enforcement of this Act means committed by or against a person who is engaged in carrying out duties or functions, or exercising a power, under this Act or a person acting under their direction and control.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 217 (1) The Minister may designate as enforcement officers or analysts for the purposes of this Act, or any provision of this Act,

heading: Designation
paragraph: (a) persons or classes of persons who, in the Minister's opinion, are qualified to be so designated; and

heading: Designation
paragraph: (b) with the approval of a government, persons or classes of persons employed by the government in the administration of a law respecting the protection of the environment.

heading: Production of certificate of designation
paragraph: (2) Every enforcement officer or analyst shall be furnished with a certificate of designation as an enforcement officer or analyst, as the case may be, and on entering any place under section 218 or 220, as the case may be, shall, if so requested, produce the certificate to the person in charge of the place.

heading: Powers of enforcement officers
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this Act and the regulations, enforcement officers have all the powers of a peace officer, but the Minister may specify limits on those powers when designating any person or class of persons.

heading: Powers in exclusive economic zone
paragraph: (4) Every power - including arrest, entry, search and seizure - that may be exercised in Canada in respect of an offence under this Act or the Criminal Code may, in respect of an offence arising out of a contravention of Division 3 of Part 7 or of any regulation made under that Division, or in respect of an offence under the Criminal Code that is committed in the course of enforcement of this Act, be exercised in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(c) if the offence was committed in that area of the sea.

heading: Exercising powers in cases of hot pursuit
paragraph: (5) The powers referred to in subsection (4) may be exercised in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(g) if hot pursuit has been commenced in Canada or in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e) and (g).

heading: When consent of Attorney General of Canada required
paragraph: (6) The powers referred to in subsection (4) may not be exercised under that subsection or subsection (5) in relation to a ship that is not a Canadian ship, or to a foreign national who is on board such a ship, without the consent of the Attorney General of Canada.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: 217.1 Enforcement officers and analysts are not personally liable for anything they do or omit to do in good faith while carrying out duties or exercising powers under this Act, including any failure to exercise a discretionary authority.

heading: Inspection
paragraph: 218 (1) Subject to subsection (2), for the purposes of this Act and the regulations, an enforcement officer may, at any reasonable time, enter and inspect any place if the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (a) there can be found in the place a substance with respect to which this Act applies, a product that contains such a substance or a product that may release such a substance into the environment;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (b) fuels to which this Act applies are being or have been produced or blended, or can be found, in the place;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (c) a cleaning product or water conditioner, as defined in section 116, is being or has been produced or can be found in the place;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (d) regulations made under section 209 apply to or in respect of the place;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (e) the place is a source in respect of which regulations have been made under section 167 or 177 or a place in respect of which regulations have been made under section 200;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (f) a substance is being loaded for the purpose of disposal at sea or is being disposed of at sea;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (g) any vehicle, engine or equipment of a class for which standards for emissions have been prescribed that is owned by or is on the premises of a company or a consignee of imported vehicles or engines or imported equipment can be found in the place;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (h) any component to be used in the manufacture of a vehicle, engine or equipment for which standards for emissions have been prescribed can be found in the place;

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (i) any record in relation to the design, manufacture, testing and field performance of a vehicle, engine or equipment in so far as it relates to emissions can be found in the place; or

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (j) any books, records, electronic data or other documents relevant to the administration of this Act can be found in the place.

heading: Private dwelling-place
paragraph: (2) An enforcement officer may not enter a private dwelling-place or any part of a place that is designed to be used and is being used as a permanent or temporary private dwelling-place except

heading: Private dwelling-place
paragraph: (a) with the consent of the occupant of the place; or

heading: Private dwelling-place
paragraph: (b) under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (3).

heading: Warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (3) Where on ex parte application a justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (a) the conditions for entry described in subsection (1) exist in relation to a private dwelling-place,

heading: Warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (b) entry to the dwelling-place is necessary for any purpose relating to the administration of this Act, and

heading: Warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (c) entry to the dwelling-place has been refused or there are reasonable grounds for believing that entry will be refused,

heading: Warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: the justice may issue a warrant authorizing the enforcement officer named in it to conduct an inspection of the dwelling-place subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant, and authorizing any other person named therein to accompany the enforcement officer and exercise any power specified in the warrant.

heading: Warrants for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (4) Where on ex parte application a justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Warrants for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (a) the conditions for entry described in subsection (1) exist in relation to a place other than a private dwelling-place,

heading: Warrants for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (b) entry to that place is necessary for any purpose relating to the administration of this Act,

heading: Warrants for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (c) entry to that place has been refused, the enforcement officer was not able to enter without the use of force or the place was abandoned, and

heading: Warrants for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (d) subject to subsection (5), all reasonable attempts were made to notify the owner, operator or person in charge of the place,

heading: Warrants for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: the justice may issue a warrant authorizing the enforcement officer named in it to conduct an inspection of the place, subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant, and authorizing any other person named therein to accompany the enforcement officer and exercise any power specified in the warrant.

heading: Waiving notice
paragraph: (5) The justice may waive the requirement to give notice referred to in subsection (4) where the justice is satisfied that attempts to give the notice would be unsuccessful because the owner, operator or person in charge is absent from the jurisdiction of the justice or that it is not in the public interest to give the notice.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (6) In executing a warrant issued under subsection (3) or (4), an enforcement officer shall not use force unless the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Stopping and detaining conveyances
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of this Act and the regulations, an enforcement officer may, at any reasonable time, direct that any conveyance be stopped - or be moved by the route and in the manner that the officer may specify, to a place specified by the officer where an inspection can be carried out - and the officer may, for a reasonable time, detain any conveyance, platform or other structure.

heading: Moving and detaining shipping containers
paragraph: (7.1) For the purposes of this Act and the regulations, an enforcement officer may, at any reasonable time, direct that any shipping container be moved to a place specified by the officer and the officer may, for a reasonable time, detain the container.

heading: Powers in relation to ships, etc.
paragraph: (8) Subject to subsection (2), for the purposes of this Act and the regulations, an enforcement officer may, at any reasonable time,

heading: Powers in relation to ships, etc.
paragraph: (a) board any ship, platform or other structure in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (e), or any aircraft in Canada, if the enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds that the ship, platform or other structure or aircraft has on board a substance to be disposed of at sea; and

heading: Powers in relation to ships, etc.
paragraph: (b) travel on any ship, aircraft, platform or other structure that is loaded with a substance to be disposed of at sea.

heading: Enforcement officer and analyst to receive accommodation
paragraph: (9) An enforcement officer who travels on a ship, aircraft, platform or other structure under paragraph (8)(b), and any analyst who accompanies the enforcement officer, shall be carried free of charge to and from the disposal site, and the person in command of the ship or aircraft or in charge of the platform or structure shall provide the enforcement officer and analyst with suitable accommodation and food free of charge.

heading: Powers of enforcement officer
paragraph: (10) In carrying out an inspection of a place under this section, an enforcement officer may, for the purposes of this Act,

heading: Powers of enforcement officer
paragraph: (a) examine any substance, product, fuel, cleaning product or water conditioner referred to in subsection (1) or any other thing relevant to the administration of this Act that is found in the place;

heading: Powers of enforcement officer
paragraph: (b) open and examine any receptacle or package found that the enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds contains any substance, product, air contaminant, fuel, cleaning product or water conditioner, engine, equipment or component;

heading: Powers of enforcement officer
paragraph: (c) examine any books, records, electronic data or other documents that the enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds contain any information relevant to the administration of this Act and make copies of them or take extracts from them;

heading: Powers of enforcement officer
paragraph: (d) take samples of anything relevant to the administration of this Act; and

heading: Powers of enforcement officer
paragraph: (e) conduct any tests or take any measurements.

heading: Disposition of samples
paragraph: (11) An enforcement officer may dispose a sample taken under paragraph (10)(d) in any manner that the enforcement officer considers appropriate.

heading: Analysts
paragraph: (12) An analyst may, for the purposes of this Act, accompany an enforcement officer who is carrying out an inspection of a place under this section and the analyst may, when so accompanying an enforcement officer, enter the place and exercise any of the powers described in subsections (8) and (10).

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (13) In carrying out an inspection of a place under this section, an enforcement officer may

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (a) use or cause to be used any computer system at the place to examine any data contained in or available to the computer system;

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (b) reproduce any record or cause it to be reproduced from the data in the form of a printout or other intelligible output;

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (c) take a printout or other output for examination or copying; and

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (d) use or cause to be used any copying equipment at the place to make copies of the record.

heading: Duty of person in possession or control
paragraph: (14) Every person who is in possession or control of a place being inspected under this section shall permit the enforcement officer to do anything referred to in subsection (13).

heading: Inspections in exclusive economic zone
paragraph: (15) For the purpose of verifying compliance with Division 3 of Part 7 and regulations made under that Division, subsections (1) to (14) also apply in respect of a place in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(c).

heading: Consent of Minister required
paragraph: (16) The consent of the Minister is required for the exercise in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(c) of any power under this section in relation to a ship that is not a Canadian ship.

heading: Consent of Attorney General not required
paragraph: (17) For greater certainty, the consent of the Attorney General of Canada is not required for the exercise of any power under this section in relation to a ship that is not a Canadian ship.

heading: Production of documents and samples
paragraph: 219 (1) The Minister may, for the purposes of this Act and the regulations, by registered letter or by a demand served personally, require any person to produce at a place specified by the Minister anything referred to in paragraph 218(10)(c) or any samples referred to in paragraph 218(10)(d) within any reasonable time and in any reasonable manner that may be stipulated therein.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (2) Any person who is required to produce anything under subsection (1) shall, despite any other law to the contrary, do so as required.

heading: Authority to issue warrant for search and seizure
paragraph: 220 (1) Where on ex parte application a justice is satisfied by information on oath that there are reasonable grounds to believe that there is in any place

heading: Authority to issue warrant for search and seizure
paragraph: (a) anything by means of or in relation to which any provision of this Act or the regulations has been contravened, or

heading: Authority to issue warrant for search and seizure
paragraph: (b) anything that there are reasonable grounds to believe will afford evidence with respect to the commission of an offence under this Act,

heading: Authority to issue warrant for search and seizure
paragraph: the justice may issue a warrant authorizing an enforcement officer, or authorizing any other person named in the warrant, to enter and search the place and to seize anything referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant.

heading: Warrant for seizure of ships, etc.
paragraph: (2) If on ex parte application a justice is satisfied by information on oath that there are reasonable grounds to believe that an offence under this Act has been committed by an owner of any ship, aircraft, platform or other structure, the justice may issue a warrant authorizing an enforcement officer, or authorizing any other person named in the warrant, to seize the ship, aircraft, platform or structure anywhere in Canada and, in the case of a ship, platform or structure, within Canadian waters.

heading: Search and seizure
paragraph: (3) A person authorized by a warrant issued under subsection (1) or (2) may

heading: Search and seizure
paragraph: (a) at any reasonable time enter and search a place referred to in the warrant;

heading: Search and seizure
paragraph: (b) seize and detain anything referred to in the warrant; and

heading: Search and seizure
paragraph: (c) exercise the powers described in subsection 218(10) or (13).

heading: Where warrant not necessary
paragraph: (4) An enforcement officer may exercise the powers described in subsection (3) without a warrant if the conditions for obtaining the warrant exist but by reason of exigent circumstances it would not be practical to obtain the warrant.

heading: Exigent circumstances
paragraph: (5) For greater certainty, exigent circumstances include circumstances in which the delay necessary to obtain a warrant under subsection (1) or (2) would result in danger to human life or the environment or the loss or destruction of evidence.

heading: Exception in relation to ships that are not Canadian ships
paragraph: (5.1) Despite subsection (4), an enforcement officer may exercise the powers described in subsection (3) without a warrant in relation to a ship that is not a Canadian ship if

heading: Exception in relation to ships that are not Canadian ships
paragraph: (a) the conditions for obtaining the warrant exist but by reason of exigent circumstances it would not be practical to obtain the warrant; and

heading: Exception in relation to ships that are not Canadian ships
paragraph: (b) the Attorney General of Canada has consented to the exercise of the powers without a warrant.

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (6) A person authorized under this section to search a place may

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (a) use or cause to be used any computer system at the place to search any data contained in or available to the computer system;

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (b) reproduce any record or cause it to be reproduced from the data in the form of a printout or other intelligible output;

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (c) seize any printout or other output for examination or copying; and

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (d) use or cause to be used any copying equipment at the place to make copies of the record.

heading: Duty of person in possession or control
paragraph: (7) Every person who is in possession or control of a place in respect of which a search is carried out under this section shall permit the person carrying out the search to do anything referred to in subsection (6).

heading: Accommodation
paragraph: (8) A person who is exercising powers described in subsection (3) on a ship, an aircraft, a platform or other structure shall be carried free of charge, and the person in command of the ship or aircraft or in charge of the platform or other structure shall provide the person exercising those powers with suitable accommodation and food free of charge.

heading: Custody
paragraph: 221 (1) Any thing seized under section 220 shall be delivered into the custody of any person that the Minister directs.

heading: Discharge of cargo
paragraph: (2) Where a thing seized under section 220 has cargo on board, the cargo may be discharged, under the supervision of

heading: Discharge of cargo
paragraph: (a) the enforcement officer or other person by whom the thing was seized, or

heading: Discharge of cargo
paragraph: (b) the person into whose custody the thing was delivered in accordance with subsection (1),

heading: Discharge of cargo
paragraph: at the place in Canada that is capable of receiving the cargo and that is nearest to the place of seizure, or at any other place that is satisfactory to the enforcement officer or other person supervising the discharge of the cargo.

heading: Sale of perishable cargo
paragraph: (3) Where a thing seized under section 220 has cargo on board that is perishable,

heading: Sale of perishable cargo
paragraph: (a) the enforcement officer or other person by whom the thing was seized, or

heading: Sale of perishable cargo
paragraph: (b) the person into whose custody the thing was delivered in accordance with subsection (1)

heading: Sale of perishable cargo
paragraph: may sell the cargo or the portion of it that is perishable, as the case may be, and the proceeds of the sale shall be paid to the Receiver General or shall be deposited in a bank to the credit of the Receiver General.

heading: Order for delivery of cargo
paragraph: (4) The owner of any cargo of anything seized under section 220 may apply to the Federal Court for an order requiring any person who has custody of the cargo or the proceeds of any sale thereof to deliver the cargo or the proceeds of sale to the owner, and the Court may make such an order where it is satisfied that the applicant is the owner of the cargo to which the application relates.

heading: Redelivery on deposit of security
paragraph: 222 (1) Where a thing has been seized under section 220, the Federal Court may, with the consent of the Minister, order redelivery of the thing or delivery of the proceeds realized from a sale of any perishable cargo under subsection 221(3) to the person from whom the thing was seized if security in the form of a bond in an amount and form satisfactory to the Minister is given to the Minister.

heading: Seized ship, etc., to be returned unless proceedings instituted
paragraph: (2) Anything referred to in subsection (1) that has been seized under section 220, or any security given to the Minister under subsection (1), shall be returned or paid to the person from whom the thing was seized within 30 days after the seizure unless, before the expiry of those 30 days, proceedings are instituted in respect of an offence under this Act alleged to have been committed by the owner of the thing.

heading: Arrest without warrant
paragraph: 222.1 An enforcement officer may arrest without warrant a person or ship that the enforcement officer believes, on reasonable grounds, has committed an offence against this Act or the regulations, or that the enforcement officer finds committing or about to commit an offence against this Act or the regulations.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: 223 (1) Whenever, during the course of an inspection or a search, an enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that a provision of this Act or the regulations has been contravened, the enforcement officer may seize and detain anything

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (a) by means of or in relation to which the enforcement officer reasonably believes the contravention occurred; or

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (b) that the enforcement officer reasonably believes will afford evidence of the contravention.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) An enforcement officer shall not seize anything under subsection (1) unless the thing is required as evidence or for purposes of analysis or the enforcement officer is of the opinion that the seizure is necessary in the public interest.

heading: Notice of contravention
paragraph: (3) An enforcement officer who has seized and detained a thing under subsection (1) shall, as soon as is practicable, advise the person in whose possession it was at the time of the seizure of the provision of this Act or the regulations that the enforcement officer believes has been contravened.

heading: Detention and release
paragraph: (4) Anything seized under subsection (1) or section 220, other than a ship, aircraft, platform or other structure, shall not be detained

heading: Detention and release
paragraph: (a) after the owner of the thing or the person in whose possession it was at the time of the seizure applies to the enforcement officer or to the Minister for its release and the enforcement officer or the Minister is satisfied that it is not necessary in the public interest to continue to detain the thing or that it is not required as evidence or for purposes of analysis; or

heading: Detention and release
paragraph: (b) after the expiry of 90 days after the day of seizure, unless before that time

heading: Detention and release
paragraph: (i) the thing has been forfeited under section 229,

heading: Detention and release
paragraph: (ii) proceedings have been instituted in respect of the contravention in relation to which the thing was seized, in which case it may be detained until the proceedings are finally concluded, or

heading: Detention and release
paragraph: (iii) the Minister has served or made reasonable efforts to serve notice of an application for an order extending the time during which the thing may be detained in accordance with section 224.

heading: Storage of seized thing
paragraph: (5) A thing seized by an enforcement officer under subsection (1) or section 220, other than a ship, aircraft, platform or other structure, shall be kept or stored in the place where it was seized except if

heading: Storage of seized thing
paragraph: (a) in the opinion of the enforcement officer,

heading: Storage of seized thing
paragraph: (i) it is not in the public interest to do so, or

heading: Storage of seized thing
paragraph: (ii) the thing seized, or a sample of it, is required as evidence and removal and storage of the thing seized is necessary to ensure that the thing or sample will be available as evidence in any related proceedings, or

heading: Storage of seized thing
paragraph: (b) the person in whose possession it was at the time of the seizure or the person entitled to possession of the place requests the enforcement officer to have it removed to some other place,

heading: Storage of seized thing
paragraph: in which case it may be removed to and stored in any other place at the direction of or with the concurrence of an enforcement officer and at the expense of the person who requested that it be so removed.

heading: Interference with seized thing
paragraph: (6) Unless authorized by an enforcement officer, no person shall remove, alter or interfere in any way with anything seized and detained by an enforcement officer under subsection (1) or section 220, but an enforcement officer shall, at the request of the person from whom it was seized, allow that person or any person authorized by that person to examine it and, where practicable, furnish a sample or copy of it to that person.

heading: Application to extend period of detention
paragraph: 224 (1) Where proceedings have not been instituted in respect of the contravention in relation to which a thing was seized under section 220 or subsection 223(1), the Minister may, before the expiry of 90 days after the day of the seizure and on serving prior notice in accordance with subsection (2) on the owner of the thing or on the person who at the time of the seizure was in possession of it, apply to a provincial court judge, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, within whose territorial jurisdiction the seizure was made for an order extending the time during which it may be detained.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) A notice shall be served by personal service at least five clear days before the day on which the application is to be made to the provincial court judge or by registered mail at least seven clear days before that day and shall specify

heading: Notice
paragraph: (a) the provincial court in which the application is to be made;

heading: Notice
paragraph: (b) the place where and the time when the application is to be heard;

heading: Notice
paragraph: (c) the thing seized in respect of which the application is to be made; and

heading: Notice
paragraph: (d) the grounds on which the Minister intends to rely to show why there should be an extension of the time during which the thing seized may be detained.

heading: Order of extension granted
paragraph: (3) Where, on the hearing of an application made under subsection (1), the judge is satisfied that the thing seized should continue to be detained, the judge shall order

heading: Order of extension granted
paragraph: (a) that the thing be detained for any additional period and on any conditions relating to the detention for that additional period that the judge considers proper; and

heading: Order of extension granted
paragraph: (b) on the expiry of the additional period, that the thing be restored to the person from whom it was seized or to any other person entitled to its possession unless, before the expiry of the additional period, an event referred to in subparagraph 223(4)(b)(i), (ii) or (iii) has occurred.

heading: Order of extension refused
paragraph: (4) Where, on the hearing of an application made under subsection (1), the judge is not satisfied that the thing seized should continue to be detained, the judge shall order that, on the expiry of 90 days after the day of the seizure, it be restored to the person from whom it was seized or to any other person entitled to its possession unless, before the expiry of the 90 days, an event referred to in subparagraph 223(4)(b)(i) or (ii) has occurred.

heading: Detention of ships
paragraph: 225 (1) If an enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the owner or master of a ship has committed an offence under this Act and that a ship was used in connection with the commission of the offence, the enforcement officer may make a detention order in respect of the ship.

heading: Order in writing
paragraph: (2) A detention order made under subsection (1) shall be in writing and be addressed to all persons at any port in Canada where the ship to which the order relates is or will be who are empowered to give a clearance in respect of the ship.

heading: Service of detention order
paragraph: (3) A detention order made under subsection (1) in respect of a ship shall be served

heading: Service of detention order
paragraph: (a) by delivering the order to the master of the ship; or

heading: Service of detention order
paragraph: (b) if service cannot reasonably be effected in the manner provided for in paragraph (a), by leaving the order with the person being or appearing to be in command or charge of the ship or, if there is no such person, by placing the order on a conspicuous part of the ship.

heading: Foreign state to be notified
paragraph: (3.1) If a ship in respect of which a detention order is made under subsection (1) is registered in a foreign state, that state is to be notified that the order was made.

heading: Duty of owner or master of ship
paragraph: (4) Where notice of a detention order made under subsection (1) has been served on the master of the ship, the owner or master of the ship shall not give an order for the ship to go into an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(f) or (g) during the term of the detention order.

heading: Duty of persons empowered to give clearance
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), no person to whom a detention order made under subsection (1) is addressed shall, after notice of the order is received by the person, give clearance in respect of the ship to which the order relates.

heading: When clearance given
paragraph: (6) A person to whom a detention order made under subsection (1) is addressed and who has received notice of the order may give clearance in respect of the ship to which the order relates where

heading: When clearance given
paragraph: (a) the owner or master of the ship

heading: When clearance given
paragraph: (i) has not, within 30 days after the order was made, been charged with the offence that gave rise to the making of the order, or

heading: When clearance given
paragraph: (ii) has, within 30 days after the order was made, been charged with that offence and appears in Canada to answer to the charge;

heading: When clearance given
paragraph: (b) if the alleged offence involves the contravention of Division 3 of Part 7 or of any regulation made under that Division, Her Majesty in right of Canada is given security, in a form determined by the Attorney General of Canada, for payment of the maximum fine that might be imposed as a result of a conviction of the person or ship charged with that offence and of costs related to proceedings in connection with the charge or charges, or payment of any lesser amount that is approved by the Attorney General of Canada;

heading: When clearance given
paragraph: (b.1) if the alleged offence involves the contravention of this Act or the regulations, other than a contravention referred to in paragraph (b), Her Majesty in right of Canada is given security for payment of the maximum fine that might be imposed as a result of a conviction of the person charged with that offence and of costs related to proceedings in connection with the charge, or payment of any lesser amount that is approved by the Minister or a person designated by the Minister for the purpose; or

heading: When clearance given
paragraph: (c) proceedings in respect of the alleged offence that gave rise to the making of the detention order are discontinued.

heading: Power to direct ship
paragraph: 225.1 (1) An enforcement officer may direct a ship that is in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (d) and (g) to proceed, by the route and in the manner that the enforcement officer may specify, to any place specified by the enforcement officer if the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Power to direct ship
paragraph: (a) the ship is committing, has committed or is about to commit in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (d) an offence arising out of a contravention of Division 3 of Part 7 or of any regulation made under that Division; or

heading: Power to direct ship
paragraph: (b) a person on board the ship is committing, has committed or is about to commit such an offence in such an area and the ship was, is being or is about to be used in connection with the commission of the offence.

heading: Power to direct ship
paragraph: (2) If a ship is in an area of the sea referred to in paragraph 122(2)(f), an enforcement officer may, with the consent of the foreign state that has jurisdiction in that area, direct the ship to proceed, by the route and in the manner that the enforcement officer may specify, to any place specified by the enforcement officer if the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Power to direct ship
paragraph: (a) the ship is committing, has committed or is about to commit in an area of the sea referred to in any of paragraphs 122(2)(a) to (d) an offence arising out of a contravention of Division 3 of Part 7 or of any regulation made under that Division; or

heading: Power to direct ship
paragraph: (b) a person on board the ship is committing, has committed or is about to commit such an offence in such an area and the ship was, is being or is about to be used in connection with the commission of the offence.

heading: Right of passage
paragraph: 226 While carrying out powers, duties or functions under this Act, enforcement officers and analysts, and any persons accompanying them, may enter on and pass through or over private property without being liable for doing so and without any person having the right to object to that use of the property.

heading: Assistance
paragraph: 227 The owner or the person in charge of a place entered by an enforcement officer or analyst under section 218 or 220, and every person found in the place, shall

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (a) give the enforcement officer or analyst all reasonable assistance to enable them to carry out duties and functions under this Act; and

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (b) provide the enforcement officer or analyst with any information with respect to the administration of this Act and the regulations that the enforcement officer or analyst may reasonably require.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: 228 While an enforcement officer or analyst is exercising powers or carrying out duties and functions under this Act, no person shall

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (a) knowingly make any false or misleading statement, either orally or in writing, to them; or

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (b) otherwise obstruct or hinder them.

heading: Liability for costs
