paragraph: (i) for the purpose of investigating an offence that the person is suspected on reasonable grounds of having committed, or in respect of which the person has been arrested or charged, or

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (ii) for any purpose that relates to the administration of the case to which the record relates;

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (c) any member of a department or agency of a government in Canada, or any agent of such a department or agency, that is

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (i) engaged in the administration of environmental protection alternative measures in respect of the person, or

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (ii) preparing a report in respect of the person under this Act; or

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (d) any other person who is deemed, or any person within a class of persons that is deemed, by a judge of a court to have a valid interest in the record, to the extent directed by the judge, if the judge is satisfied that the disclosure is

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (i) desirable in the public interest for research or statistical purposes, or

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (ii) desirable in the interest of the proper administration of justice,

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: and if that person gives a written undertaking not to subsequently disclose the information except in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Subsequent disclosure
paragraph: (2) Where a record is made available to a person under subparagraph (1)(d)(i), the person may subsequently disclose information contained in the record, but shall not disclose it in any form that could reasonably be expected to identify the person to whom it relates and any other person specified by the judge.

heading: Information, copies
paragraph: (3) Any person to whom a record is authorized to be made available under this section may be given any information that is contained in the record and may be given a copy of any part of the record.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (4) Nothing in this section authorizes the introduction into evidence of any part of a record that would not otherwise be admissible in evidence.

heading: Exception for public access to court record
paragraph: (5) For greater certainty, this section does not apply to an agreement, a varied agreement or report that is filed with the court in accordance with section 300.

heading: Agreements respecting exchange of information
paragraph: 308 The Minister may enter into an agreement with a department or agency of a government in Canada respecting the exchange of information for the purpose of administering environmental protection alternative measures or preparing a report in respect of a person's compliance with an agreement.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 309 The Minister may make regulations respecting the environmental protection alternative measures that may be used for the purposes of this Act including regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) excluding specified offences under this Act from the application of those measures;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing the form and manner in which and the period within which an application to participate in the measures is to be made, and the information that must be contained in or accompany the application;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the manner of preparing and filing reports relating to the administration of and compliance with agreements;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the types of reasonable costs and the manner of paying the costs associated with supervising and verifying compliance with an agreement; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the terms and conditions that may be provided for in an agreement and their effects.

heading: Ticketing
paragraph: 310 (1) Despite anything in this Act, the Governor in Council may, by regulation, on the recommendation of the Minister, designate any offence under this Act as an offence with respect to which, despite the Criminal Code, an enforcement officer may lay an information and issue and serve a summons by completing a ticket in the prescribed form, affixing to it the enforcement officer's signature and delivering it to the person who is alleged to have committed the offence specified in it at the time the offence is alleged to have been committed.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) Any regulations made under this section

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) shall establish a procedure for entering a plea and paying a fine in respect of each offence to which the regulations relate;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) shall prescribe the amount of the fine to be paid in respect of each offence; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) may prescribe any other matter necessary to carry out the purposes of this section.

heading: Failure to respond to ticket
paragraph: (3) Where a person is served with a ticket and does not enter a plea within the time prescribed by the regulations, a justice shall examine the ticket and

heading: Failure to respond to ticket
paragraph: (a) if the ticket is complete and regular on its face, the justice shall enter a conviction in the person's absence and impose a fine of the prescribed amount; or

heading: Failure to respond to ticket
paragraph: (b) if the ticket is not complete and regular on its face, the justice shall quash the proceedings.

heading: Injunction
paragraph: 311 (1) Where, on the application of the Minister, it appears to a court of competent jurisdiction that a person has done or is about to do or is likely to do any act or thing constituting or directed toward the commission of an offence under this Act, the court may issue an injunction ordering any person named in the application

heading: Injunction
paragraph: (a) to refrain from doing any act or thing that it appears to the court may constitute or be directed toward the commission of an offence under this Act; or

heading: Injunction
paragraph: (b) to do any act or thing that it appears to the court may prevent the commission of an offence under this Act.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) No injunction shall be issued under subsection (1) unless 48 hours notice is given to the party or parties named in the application or the urgency of the situation is such that service of notice would not be in the public interest.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 312 In a prosecution for a contravention of a provision of Division 5 of Part 7 by a company engaged in the business of assembling or altering vehicles, it is a defence for the company to establish that the contravention occurred as a result of work previously done on a vehicle by another company engaged in the manufacture of the vehicle.

heading: Request for confidentiality
paragraph: 313 (1) A person who provides information to the Minister under this Act, or to a board of review in respect of a notice of objection filed under this Act, may submit with the information a request that it be treated as confidential.

heading: Contents of request
paragraph: (2) A request for confidentiality shall be submitted, with reasons taking into account the criteria set out in paragraphs 20(1)(a) to (d) of the Access to Information Act, in writing and contain any supplementary information that may be prescribed.

heading: Review of requests
paragraph: (3) The Minister shall review a statistically valid representative sample of requests granted under subsection (1) and determine whether, in respect of each of those requests, the person who made the request demonstrated that it concerned any of the following:

heading: Review of requests
paragraph: (a) trade secrets of any person;

heading: Review of requests
paragraph: (b) financial, commercial, scientific or technical information that is confidential information and that is treated consistently in a confidential manner by any person;

heading: Review of requests
paragraph: (c) information the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to result in material financial loss or gain to, or could reasonably be expected to prejudice the competitive position of, any person; or

heading: Review of requests
paragraph: (d) information the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to interfere with contractual or other negotiations of any person.

heading: Requests deemed not to have been made
paragraph: (4) If the Minister determines that the person who made the request did not demonstrate that the request, in whole or in part, concerned information described in any of paragraphs (3)(a) to (d), then, for the purpose of any part of the request that does not concern such information, the request is deemed not to have been made.

heading: Report - number of requests
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall include in the annual report required under section 342 the number of requests made under subsection (1), the number of requests reviewed, the number of requests that, in whole or in part, were deemed not to have been made and a summary of the information disclosed under sections 315 to 317.2.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (6) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions set out in this section.

heading: Prohibition of disclosure
paragraph: 314 The Minister shall not disclose any information in respect of which a request for confidentiality has been made under section 313, except in accordance with any of sections 315 to 317.2.

heading: Disclosure by Minister for public interest
paragraph: 315 (1) The Minister may disclose information, other than information in respect of which section 318 applies, where

heading: Disclosure by Minister for public interest
paragraph: (a) the disclosure is in the interest of public health, public safety or the protection of the environment; and

heading: Disclosure by Minister for public interest
paragraph: (b) the public interest in the disclosure clearly outweighs in importance

heading: Disclosure by Minister for public interest
paragraph: (i) any material financial loss or prejudice to the competitive position of the person who provided the information or on whose behalf it was provided, and

heading: Disclosure by Minister for public interest
paragraph: (ii) any damage to the privacy, reputation or human dignity of any individual that may result from the disclosure.

heading: Notice of disclosure
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), at least 24 hours before disclosing any information under subsection (1), the Minister shall give notice of the proposed disclosure to the person who provided the information or on whose behalf it was provided.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Notice under subsection (2)

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) is not required where the person to whom it is to be given cannot be found after reasonable efforts have been made to do so; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) may be given later than the time required by that subsection where an emergency exists.

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: 316 (1) Information may be disclosed

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: (a) with the written consent of the person who provided it or on whose behalf it was provided;

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: (b) as may be necessary for the purposes of the administration or enforcement of this Act;

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: (c) under an agreement or arrangement between the Government of Canada or any of its institutions and any other government in Canada, the government of a foreign state or an international organization or any of its institutions, or between the Minister and any other minister of the Crown in right of Canada or a board or agency of the Government of Canada, if

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: (i) the purpose of the agreement or arrangement is the administration or enforcement of a law, and

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: (ii) the government, international organization, institution, other minister, board or agency undertakes to keep the information confidential;

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: (d) under an agreement or arrangement between the Government of Canada and the government of a foreign state or an international organization, where the government or organization undertakes to keep the information confidential; or

heading: Certain purposes for which information may be disclosed
paragraph: (e) to a physician or prescribed medical professional who requests the information for the purpose of making a medical diagnosis of, or rendering medical treatment to, a person in an emergency.

heading: Disclosure by physician, etc.
paragraph: (2) A physician or prescribed medical professional to whom information is disclosed under paragraph (1)(e) shall not disclose the information except as may be necessary for the purposes referred to in that paragraph.

heading: Disclosure of personal information
paragraph: (3) Personal information as defined in section 3 of the Privacy Act may not be disclosed under paragraph (1)(b) or (c) unless

heading: Disclosure of personal information
paragraph: (a) the disclosure is in the interest of public health, public safety or the protection of the environment; and

heading: Disclosure of personal information
paragraph: (b) the public interest in the disclosure clearly outweighs in importance any damage to the privacy, reputation or human dignity of any individual that may result from the disclosure.

heading: Disclosure by Minister
paragraph: 317 (1) The Minister may disclose information in respect of which a request for confidentiality has been made under section 313 where the Minister determines that the disclosure would not be prohibited under section 20 of the Access to Information Act.

heading: Application of certain provisions of Access to Information Act
paragraph: (2) Where the Minister intends to disclose information under subsection (1), sections 27, 28 and 44 of the Access to Information Act apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, and, for that purpose, that information is deemed to be contained in a record that the Minister intends to disclose and any reference in those sections to the person who requested access shall be disregarded.

heading: Protection from civil proceeding or prosecution
paragraph: (3) Despite any other Act of Parliament, no civil or criminal proceedings lie against the Minister, or against any person acting on behalf of or under the direction of the Minister, and no proceedings lie against the Crown for the disclosure in good faith of any information under this Act, for any consequences that flow from that disclosure or for the failure to give any notice required under section 27 or any other provision of the Access to Information Act if reasonable care is taken to give the required notice.

heading: Disclosure - substance
paragraph: 317.1 (1) The Minister may disclose the explicit chemical or biological name of a substance in respect of which a request for confidentiality has been made if the Minister takes or has taken any of the following measures:

heading: Disclosure - substance
paragraph: (a) to permit, under paragraph 84(1)(a), the manufacture or importation of the substance, subject to any conditions that are specified;

heading: Disclosure - substance
paragraph: (b) to prohibit the manufacture or importation of the substance under paragraph 84(1)(b);

heading: Disclosure - substance
paragraph: (c) to publish, in respect of the substance, a notice under subsection 85(1) or (4); or

heading: Disclosure - substance
paragraph: (d) to amend the Domestic Substances List in respect of the substance under subsection 87(3) or (4.1).

heading: Disclosure - living organism
paragraph: (2) The Minister may disclose the explicit biological name of a living organism in respect of which a request for confidentiality has been made if the Minister takes or has taken any of the following measures:

heading: Disclosure - living organism
paragraph: (a) to permit, under paragraph 109(1)(a), the manufacture or importation of the living organism, subject to any conditions that are specified;

heading: Disclosure - living organism
paragraph: (b) to prohibit the manufacture or importation of the living organism under paragraph 109(1)(b);

heading: Disclosure - living organism
paragraph: (c) to publish, in respect of the living organism, a notice under subsection 110(1) or (4); or

heading: Disclosure - living organism
paragraph: (d) to amend the Domestic Substances List in respect of the living organism under subsection 112(3) or (5).

heading: Disclosure - Ministers' recommendation
paragraph: (3) The Minister shall disclose the explicit chemical or biological name of a substance or the explicit biological name of a living organism in respect of which a request for confidentiality has been made if the Ministers recommend or have recommended to the Governor in Council the addition of the substance or the living organism to Part 1 or 2 of the list of toxic substances in Schedule 1 under subsection 90(1).

heading: Disclosure after expiry
paragraph: 317.2 (1) The Minister may disclose the explicit chemical or biological name of a substance or the explicit biological name of a living organism after the expiry of a period of 10 years after the day on which a request for confidentiality under section 313 is made.

heading: Publication - notice of intent
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall publish a notice in the Canada Gazette of the Minister's intention to disclose the explicit chemical or biological name under subsection (1) at least 60 days before the proposed disclosure.

heading: Comments
paragraph: (3) Within 60 days after the publication of the notice, the person who made the request for confidentiality or the person's successor or assign may file with the Minister comments respecting

heading: Comments
paragraph: (a) whether the public interest in the disclosure of the name clearly outweighs in importance

heading: Comments
paragraph: (i) any material financial loss or prejudice to the competitive position of the person or the person's successor or assign, and

heading: Comments
paragraph: (ii) any damage to the privacy, reputation or human dignity of any person that may result from the disclosure of that name; and

heading: Comments
paragraph: (b) whether the disclosure is prohibited under section 20 of the Access to Information Act.

heading: Notice of disclosure
paragraph: (4) At least 24 hours before disclosing the name under subsection (1), the Minister shall give notice of the proposed disclosure to the person who made the request for confidentiality or the person's successor or assign. The notice is not required if the person to whom it is to be given cannot be found after reasonable efforts have been made to do so.

heading: Emergency
paragraph: (5) If an emergency exists, subsections (2) and (3) do not apply and the notice of disclosure required in subsection (4) may be given later than the time provided for in that subsection.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: 317.3 The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 a report respecting the explicit chemical or biological names of substances and the explicit biological names of living organisms disclosed under section 317.1 or 317.2.

heading: Hazardous Materials Information Review Act
paragraph: 318 Except as provided in sections 316 and 317, information in respect of which a request for confidentiality has been made under section 313 shall not be disclosed where

heading: Hazardous Materials Information Review Act
paragraph: (a) a claim for exemption has been filed in respect of the information under section 11 of the Hazardous Materials Information Review Act;

heading: Hazardous Materials Information Review Act
paragraph: (b) the information is exempt under section 19 of that Act from the requirement in respect of which the exemption is claimed; and

heading: Hazardous Materials Information Review Act
paragraph: (c) the person claiming the exemption has disclosed the contents of the claim to the Minister.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 319 The Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) information that shall accompany a request made under section 313; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) medical professionals for the purposes of paragraph 316(1)(e).

heading: Non-disclosure by Minister of National Defence
paragraph: 320 Despite any other provision of this Act, the Minister of National Defence may refuse to disclose under this Part any information the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to be injurious to the defence or security of Canada or of a state allied or associated with Canada.

heading: Security requirements for disclosure
paragraph: 321 Any person, except an enforcement officer or analyst, who receives, obtains or has access to information under this Act shall comply with any security requirements applicable to, and take any oath of secrecy required to be taken by, persons who normally have access to and use of the information.

heading: Guidelines, programs and other measures
paragraph: 322 The Minister may establish guidelines, programs and other measures for the development and use of economic instruments and market-based approaches to further the purposes of this Act, respecting systems relating to

heading: Guidelines, programs and other measures
paragraph: (a) deposits and refunds; and

heading: Guidelines, programs and other measures
paragraph: (b) compliance units.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: 323 (1) In carrying out the responsibilities conferred by section 322, the Minister shall offer to consult with the government of a province and the members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments and may consult with a government department or agency, aboriginal people, representatives of industry and labour and municipal authorities or with persons interested in quality of the environment or the preservation and improvement of public health.

heading: Minister may act
paragraph: (2) At any time after the 60th day following the day on which the Minister offers to consult in accordance with subsection (1), the Minister may act under section 322 if the offer to consult is not accepted by the government of a province or members of the Committee who are representatives of aboriginal governments.

heading: Publication of guidelines and programs
paragraph: 324 The Minister shall publish any guidelines, programs and other measures established under section 322, or shall give notice of their availability, in the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: 325 The Governor in Council may, in the exercise of a regulation-making power under section 93, 118 or 209, make regulations respecting systems relating to deposits and refunds, including regulations providing for, or imposing requirements respecting,

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (a) deposits, including the amount of any deposit and the substance, product containing a substance or activity in relation to which a deposit is required, the conditions for the use of a deposit and the conditions for and manner of paying a deposit;

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (b) the period during which a deposit may be held;

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (c) refunds, including the amount of any refund and the substance, product containing a substance or activity in relation to which a refund may be granted and the conditions for and manner of paying a refund;

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (d) the establishment of a fund for deposits, and the operation, management and administration of the fund;

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (e) the designation of a person to administer the fund for deposits and the conditions for the designation;

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (f) reports and forms related to deposits, refunds and the fund for deposits;

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (g) the maintenance of books and records for the administration of any regulation made under this section; and

heading: Regulations for systems relating to deposits and refunds
paragraph: (h) the forfeiture of deposits, including unclaimed deposits and the conditions under which and the circumstances in which deposits may be forfeited.

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: 326 The Governor in Council may, in the exercise of a regulation-making power under section 93, 118, 140, 167, 177 or 209, make regulations respecting systems relating to compliance units, including regulations providing for, or imposing requirements respecting,

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (a) the substance, product containing a substance or quantity or concentration of the substance that is released or activity in relation to which the system is established;

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (b) the methods and procedures for conducting sampling, analyses, tests, measurements or monitoring under the system;

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (c) the description and nature of a compliance unit, including allowances, credits or coupons;

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (d) the baselines to be used for comparison or control purposes in relation to the system and the maximum limits applicable to the system and the manner of determining those baselines and maximum limits;

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (e) the conditions related to the creation, distribution, trade, sale, use, variation or cancellation of a compliance unit;

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (f) the creation, operation and management of a public registry related to the system;

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (g) the conditions for the use of and participation in the system, including environmental or temporal limits;

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (h) reports and forms related to the system; and

heading: Regulations for compliance units systems
paragraph: (i) the maintenance of books and records for the administration of any regulation made under this section.

heading: Ministerial orders
paragraph: 327 Despite any regulation made under section 326, the Minister may issue an order setting conditions in respect of the trading or suspend or cancel trading of compliance units or invalidate any trade of compliance units if the Ministers are of the opinion that the trade or use of a compliance unit

heading: Ministerial orders
paragraph: (a) has or may have an immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment;

heading: Ministerial orders
paragraph: (b) constitutes or may constitute a danger to the environment on which human life depends; or

heading: Ministerial orders
paragraph: (c) constitutes or may constitute a danger in Canada to human life or health.

heading: Environmental Economic Instruments Fund
paragraph: 327.1 (1) There is established an account in the accounts of Canada to be called the Environmental Economic Instruments Fund, consisting of a sub-account for each funding program that meets the following conditions:

heading: Environmental Economic Instruments Fund
paragraph: (a) its purpose is provided for in a regulation made under section 326 and any of sections 93, 118, 140, 167, 177 and 209; and

heading: Environmental Economic Instruments Fund
paragraph: (b) it is under the responsibility of the Minister.

heading: Amounts paid into C.R.F.
paragraph: (2) The amounts received by His Majesty in right of Canada as contributions to a funding program referred to in subsection (1) are to be paid into the Consolidated Revenue Fund and credited to the sub-account for that program.

heading: Interest
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Finance shall cause to be credited to each sub-account an amount representing interest, calculated in the manner and at the rate determined by the Governor in Council on the recommendation of that Minister, on the amount standing to the credit of that sub-account.

heading: Amounts paid out of C.R.F.
paragraph: (4) On the Minister's request, one or more amounts not exceeding in total the amount standing in the sub-account for a funding program referred to in subsection (1), including interest, may be paid out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the purpose for which that funding program was established. The amount of all such payments is to be charged to that sub-account.

heading: Administration of Fund
paragraph: (5) The Minister is responsible for the administration of the Environmental Economic Instruments Fund.

heading: Use of amounts
paragraph: (6) Amounts credited to a sub-account for a funding program referred to in subsection (1) may be used for the administration of that sub-account.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (7) The Minister may, by order, designate any person or class of persons to exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions set out in subsections (4) and (5).

heading: Services and facilities
paragraph: 328 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Minister may make regulations

heading: Services and facilities
paragraph: (a) prescribing the fees or a scale of fees or the manner of determining the fees to be paid for a service, the use of a facility or any right, privilege, process or approval;

heading: Services and facilities
paragraph: (b) prescribing the persons or classes of persons by whom or on whose behalf the fees are to be paid and requiring the fees to be paid by those persons or classes of persons;

heading: Services and facilities
paragraph: (c) exempting any person or class of persons from the requirement to pay any of those fees; and

heading: Services and facilities
paragraph: (d) generally, in respect of any condition or any other matter in relation to the payment of fees for a service, facility, right, privilege, process or approval referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Appropriate Minister
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), where the Minister or the Minister of Health or both Ministers have responsibility for a service, facility, right, privilege, process or approval referred to in paragraph (1)(a), that Minister or both Ministers, as the case may be, have the power to make the regulations under subsection (1) in relation to that service, facility, right, privilege, process or approval.

heading: Amount not to exceed cost
paragraph: (3) Fees for a service or the use of a facility that are prescribed by or under regulations made under subsection (1) may not exceed the cost to Her Majesty in right of Canada of providing the service or the use of the facility.

heading: Amount
paragraph: (4) Fees for processes or approvals that are prescribed by or under regulations made under subsection (1) shall in the aggregate not exceed an amount sufficient to compensate Her Majesty in right of Canada for any reasonable costs incurred by Her Majesty for the purpose of providing the processes or approvals.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: 329 The Minister making a regulation under section 328 shall do so after consulting with any persons or organizations that the Minister considers to be interested in the matter.

heading: Exercise of regulation-making power
paragraph: 330 (1) The Governor in Council may, in the exercise of any regulation-making power under this Act in respect of a substance, prescribe

heading: Exercise of regulation-making power
paragraph: (a) the minimum, average or maximum quantity or concentration of the substance; and

heading: Exercise of regulation-making power
paragraph: (b) the method of determining such a quantity or concentration.

heading: Incorporation by reference
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, a regulation made under this Act incorporating by reference a standard, specification, guideline, method, procedure or practice may incorporate the standard, specification, guideline, method, procedure or practice as amended from time to time.

heading: Variation
paragraph: (3.2) Regulations made under section 93, 140, 145, 167, 177 or 326 may distinguish among any class of persons, works, undertakings, activities or substances, including fuels, that they may establish on the basis of any factor, including

heading: Variation
paragraph: (a) quantities of releases;

heading: Variation
paragraph: (b) production capacity;

heading: Variation
paragraph: (c) technology or techniques used or manufacturing process;

heading: Variation
paragraph: (d) feedstocks used;

heading: Variation
paragraph: (e) in the case of works or undertakings, the date their operation commenced or the date on which any major alterations are completed;

heading: Variation
paragraph: (f) the substance or fuel's source;

heading: Variation
paragraph: (g) the substance or fuel's commercial designation;

heading: Variation
paragraph: (h) the substance or fuel's physical or chemical properties; and

heading: Variation
paragraph: (i) the substance or fuel's conditions of use or place or time of year of use.

heading: Limitation of Part 7
paragraph: (3.3) Nothing in Part 7 is to be construed so as to prevent the making of regulations under Part 5.

heading: Manner of service
paragraph: (4) The Minister may make regulations respecting the manner of providing or serving orders, copies of orders, notices or other documents that are to be provided under this Act.

heading: Exemption from Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: 331 An interim order made under section 94, 163, 173, 183 or 200.1

heading: Exemption from Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (a) is exempt from the application of sections 3, 5 and 11 of the Statutory Instruments Act; and

heading: Exemption from Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (b) shall be published in the Canada Gazette within 23 days after it is approved by the Governor in Council.

heading: Publication of proposed orders and regulations
paragraph: 332 (1) The Minister shall publish in the Canada Gazette a copy of every order or regulation proposed to be made by the Minister or the Governor in Council under this Act, except a list, or an amendment to a list, referred to in any of sections 66 to 66.2, 87, 105 to 105.2 and 112 or an interim order made under section 94, 163, 173, 183 or 200.1.

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: (2) Any person may file with the Minister comments, or a notice of objection requesting that a board of review be established under section 333 and stating the reasons for the objection, within 60 days after the publication of

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: (a) a proposed order or regulation referred to in subsection (1);

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: (b) a proposed instrument respecting preventive or control actions in relation to a substance that is required by section 91 to be published in the Canada Gazette; or

heading: Notice of objection
paragraph: (c) a statement referred to in subparagraph 91(1)(a)(ii) or (b)(ii).

heading: Single publication required
paragraph: (3) No order, regulation or instrument need be published more than once under subsection (1), whether or not it is altered after publication.

heading: Establishment of board of review
paragraph: 333 (1) If a person files a notice of objection under subsection 332(2) in respect of a decision or a proposed order, regulation or instrument made by the Governor in Council, a decision or a proposed order or instrument made by either or both Ministers or a statement referred to in subparagraph 91(1)(a)(ii) or (b)(ii), the Minister or the Ministers may establish a board of review to inquire into the nature and extent of the danger posed by the substance in respect of which the decision or statement is made or the order, regulation or instrument is proposed.

heading: Establishment of board of review
paragraph: (2) Where a person files a notice of objection under subsection 9(3) or 10(5) in respect of an agreement or a term or condition of the agreement, the Minister may establish a board of review to inquire into the matter.

heading: Mandatory review for international air and water
paragraph: (3) Where a person or government files with the Minister a notice of objection under subsection 332(2) with respect to regulations proposed to be made under section 167 or 177 within the time specified in that subsection, the Minister shall establish a board of review to inquire into the nature and extent of the danger posed by the release into the air or water of the substance in respect of which the regulations are proposed.

heading: Mandatory reviews for certain regulations
paragraph: (4) Where a person files with the Minister a notice of objection under subsection 332(2) with respect to regulations proposed to be made under Part 9 or section 118 within the time specified in that subsection, the Minister shall establish a board of review to inquire into the matter raised by the notice.

heading: Review for permits
paragraph: (5) Where a person files with the Minister a notice of objection under section 134 within the time specified in that section, the Minister may establish a board of review to inquire into the matter raised by the notice.

heading: Number of members of board
paragraph: 334 (1) A board of review shall consist of not fewer than three members.

heading: Knowledge requirement
paragraph: (2) A person is not eligible to be appointed as a member of a board of review unless the person is knowledgeable about the Canadian environment, environmental and human health or traditional aboriginal ecological knowledge.

heading: Appearance before board
paragraph: 335 A board of review shall give any person or government a reasonable opportunity, consistent with the rules of procedural fairness and natural justice, of appearing before it, presenting evidence and making representations.

heading: Withdrawal of notice of objection
paragraph: 336 Where a notice of objection referred to in section 333 is withdrawn by the person who filed it and no other notice of objection is filed in respect of the same matter, the Minister or Ministers may dissolve a board of review established in respect of the notice of objection.

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: 337 For the purposes of an inquiry under this Act, a board of review has all the powers of a person appointed as a commissioner under Part I of the Inquiries Act.

heading: Costs
paragraph: 338 (1) A board of review may award costs of, and incidental to, any proceedings before it on a final or interim basis and those costs may be fixed at a sum certain or may be taxed.

heading: Payment
paragraph: (2) A board of review may, in accordance with the rules, direct by whom and to whom any costs are to be paid and by whom they are to be taxed and allowed.

heading: Absent member of board
paragraph: 339 Where a member of a board of review is absent or unable to proceed with or complete an inquiry, the remaining members of the board may, if there is still a quorum, proceed with or complete the inquiry.

heading: Report
paragraph: 340 (1) As soon as possible after the conclusion of an inquiry, a board of review shall submit a report to the Minister or the Ministers who established the board, together with its recommendations and the evidence that was presented to it.

heading: Publication of report
paragraph: (2) The report of the board of review shall be made public immediately after its receipt by the Minister or Ministers, subject to section 314 or the conditions of any other Act of Parliament.

heading: Rules for boards of review
paragraph: 341 The Minister or the Ministers may, with respect to boards of review that the Minister or the Ministers establish, make rules of either particular or general application

heading: Rules for boards of review
paragraph: (a) for regulating the proceedings of the boards;

heading: Rules for boards of review
paragraph: (b) for regulating the conduct of hearings, including the presentation of evidence, the making of representations, the holding of hearings, the length of hearings and the date on or before which the boards shall report;

heading: Rules for boards of review
paragraph: (c) fixing the remuneration of board members and the travel and living expenses to which they are entitled;

heading: Rules for boards of review
paragraph: (d) prescribing the criteria to be considered by boards in directing interim or final costs to be paid, taxed and allowed and prescribing a scale under which costs are to be taxed; and

heading: Rules for boards of review
paragraph: (e) generally, for regulating the conduct and work of the boards.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: 342 (1) The Minister shall, as soon as possible after the end of each fiscal year, prepare and cause to be laid before each House of Parliament a report on the administration and enforcement of this Act for that year.

heading: Research
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall include in the annual report a report on the research conducted under the authority of this Act during the fiscal year being reported.

heading: Report - aboriginal peoples
paragraph: 342.1 The Minister shall include in the annual report required by section 342 information related to

heading: Report - aboriginal peoples
paragraph: (a) consultations with aboriginal peoples and aboriginal governments, including a summary of the key issues raised, in relation to matters under this Act;

heading: Report - aboriginal peoples
paragraph: (b) the administration of this Act in respect of aboriginal peoples and aboriginal governments, including the measures taken to advance reconciliation as reflected in section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 and in the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act; and

heading: Report - aboriginal peoples
paragraph: (c) the key findings or recommendations of any report made under an Act of Parliament in respect of the administration of this Act and aboriginal peoples and aboriginal governments.

heading: Permanent review of Act
paragraph: 343 (1) The administration of this Act shall, every five years after the coming into force of this Act, stand referred to such committee of the House of Commons, of the Senate or of both Houses of Parliament as may be designated or established for that purpose.

heading: Review and report
paragraph: (2) The committee designated or established for the purpose of subsection (1) shall, as soon as practicable, undertake a comprehensive review of the provisions and operation of this Act and shall, within one year after the review is undertaken or within such further time as the House of Commons, the Senate or both Houses of Parliament, as the case may be, may authorize, submit a report to Parliament thereon, including a statement of any changes to this Act or its administration that the committee would recommend.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 355.1 (1) Subject to subsection (2), any regulation that was

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) made under the Act mentioned in section 355, and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) in force immediately before the day on which this Act is assented to

heading: Where inconsistent with this Act
paragraph: (2) If a regulation continued in force by subsection (1) is not consistent with this Act at the end of the two-year period that starts on the day on which this Act is assented to, that regulation ceases to be in force at the end of that period.

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 1 Dredged material.

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 2 Fish waste and other organic matter resulting from industrial fish processing operations.

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 3 Ships, aircraft, platforms or other structures from which all material that can create floating debris or other marine pollution has been removed to the maximum extent possible if, in the case of disposal, those substances would not pose a serious obstacle to fishing or navigation after being disposed of.

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 4 Inert, inorganic geological matter.

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 5 Uncontaminated organic matter of natural origin.

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 6 Bulky substances that are primarily composed of iron, steel, concrete or other similar matter that does not have a significant adverse effect, other than a physical effect, on the sea or the seabed, if those substances

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (a) are in locations at which the disposal or incineration at sea is the only practicable manner of disposing of or thermally destroying the substances; and

heading: SCHEDULE 5(Subsections 122(1) and 135(2) and section 216)Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (b) in the case of disposal, would not pose a serious obstacle to fishing or navigation after being disposed of.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 1 This schedule shall be applied with a view that acceptance of disposal at sea under certain circumstances does not remove the obligation to make further attempts to reduce the necessity for disposal.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 2 The initial stages in assessing alternatives to disposal at sea shall, as appropriate, include an evaluation of

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (a) the types, amounts and relative hazard of waste or other matter generated;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (b) the details of the production process and sources of waste or other matter within that process; and

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (c) the feasibility of the following waste reduction or prevention techniques:

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (i) product reformulation,

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (ii) clean production technologies,

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (iii) process modification,

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (iv) input substitution, and

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (v) on-site, closed-loop recycling.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 3 In general terms, if the required audit reveals that opportunities exist for waste prevention at source, an applicant shall formulate and implement a waste prevention strategy, where it has jurisdiction to do so, (in collaboration with relevant local and national agencies) which includes specific waste reduction targets and provision for further waste prevention audits to ensure that these targets are being met. Permit issuance or renewal shall be subject to compliance with this requirement.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 4 For dredged material, the goal of waste management shall be to identify and control the sources of contamination. This should be achieved through implementation of waste prevention strategies and requires collaboration between the relevant local and national agencies involved with the control of point and non-point sources of pollution. Until this objective is met, the problems of contaminated dredged material may be addressed by using disposal management techniques at sea or on land.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 5 Applications to dispose of waste or other matter shall demonstrate that appropriate consideration has been given to the following hierarchy of waste management options, which implies an order of increasing environmental impact:

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (a) re-use;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (b) off-site recycling;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (c) destruction of hazardous constituents;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (d) treatment to reduce or remove the hazardous constituents; and

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (e) disposal on land, into the air and in water.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 6 A permit to dispose of waste or other matter shall be refused if opportunities exist to re-use, recycle or treat the waste or other matter without undue risks to human health or the environment or disproportionate costs. The practical availability of other means of disposal shall be considered in the light of a comparative risk assessment involving both disposal and the alternatives.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 7 A detailed description and characterization of the waste or other matter is an essential precondition for the consideration of alternatives and the basis for a decision as to whether the waste or other matter may be disposed of at sea. If the waste or other matter is so poorly characterized that proper assessment cannot be made of its potential impacts on human health and the environment, the waste or other matter shall not be disposed of at sea.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 8 Characterization of the waste or other matter and their constituents shall take into account

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (a) origin, total amount, form and average composition;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (b) properties: physical, chemical, biochemical and biological;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (c) toxicity;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (d) persistence: physical, chemical and biological; and

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (e) accumulation and biotransformation in biological materials or sediments.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 9 A national Action List shall be developed to provide a mechanism for screening candidate waste or other matter and their constituents on the basis of their potential effects on human health and the marine environment. In selecting substances for consideration in the Action List, priority shall be given to toxic, persistent and bio-accumulative substances from human sources (e.g. cadmium, mercury, organohalogens, petroleum hydrocarbons and, whenever relevant, arsenic, lead, copper, zinc, beryllium, chromium, nickel and vanadium, organosilicon compounds, cyanides, fluorides and pesticides or their by-products other than organohalogens). An Action List can also be used as a trigger mechanism for further waste prevention consideration.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 10 The Action List shall specify an upper level and may also specify a lower level. The upper level shall be set so as to avoid, as much as reasonably possible, acute or chronic effects on human health or on sensitive marine organisms representative of the marine ecosystem. Application of the Action List will result in three possible categories of waste or other matter:

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (a) waste or other matter that contain specified substances, or which cause biological responses, exceeding the relevant upper levels shall not be disposed of at sea, unless made acceptable for disposal through the use of management techniques or processes;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (b) waste or other matter that contain specified substances, or which cause biological responses, below the relevant lower levels should be considered to be of little environmental concern in relation to disposal at sea; and

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (c) waste or other matter that contain specified substances, or which cause biological responses, below the upper levels but above the lower levels require more detailed assessment before their suitability for disposal can be determined.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 11 Information required to select a disposal site shall include

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (a) physical, chemical and biological characteristics of the water-column and the sea-bed;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (b) location of amenities, values and other uses of the sea in the area under consideration;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (c) assessment of the constituent fluxes associated with disposal in relation to existing fluxes of substances in the marine environment; and

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (d) economic and operational feasibility.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 12 Assessment of potential effects shall lead to a concise statement of the expected consequences of the sea or land disposal options (i.e., the Impact Hypothesis). It provides a basis for deciding whether to approve or reject the proposed disposal option and for defining environmental monitoring requirements.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 13 The assessment for disposal shall, as appropriate, integrate information on waste characteristics, conditions at the proposed disposal site(s), fluxes and proposed disposal techniques and specify the potential effects on human health, living resources, amenities and other legitimate uses of the sea. It shall, where it is reasonably possible to do so, define the nature, temporal and spatial scales and duration of expected impacts based on reasonably conservative assumptions.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 14 An analysis of each disposal option shall be considered in light of a comparative assessment of the following concerns: human health risks, environmental costs, hazards (including accidents), economics and exclusion of future uses. If this assessment reveals that adequate information is not available to determine the likely effects of the proposed disposal option, then this option shall not be considered further. In addition, if the interpretation of the comparative assessment shows the disposal option to be less preferable, a permit for disposal at sea shall not be given.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 15 Each assessment shall conclude with a statement supporting a decision to issue or refuse a permit for disposal at sea.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 16 Monitoring is used to verify that permit conditions are met (compliance monitoring) and that the assumptions made during the permit review and site selection process were correct and sufficient to protect human health and the environment (field monitoring). It is essential that such monitoring programs have clearly defined objectives.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 17 A decision to issue a permit shall only be made if all impact evaluations are completed, and where reasonably possible, the monitoring requirements are determined. The provisions of the permit shall ensure, as far as practicable, that environmental disturbance and detriment are minimized and the benefits maximized. Any permit issued shall contain data and information specifying

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (a) the types and sources of materials to be disposed of;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (b) the location of the disposal site;

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (c) the method of disposal; and

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: (d) monitoring and reporting requirements.

heading: SCHEDULE 6(Subsections 127(2) and (3), 128(3) and 129(3) and section 135)Assessment of Waste or Other Matter
paragraph: 18 Disposal sites shall be reviewed at regular intervals, taking into account the results of monitoring and the objectives of monitoring programs. Review of monitoring results will indicate whether field programs need to be continued, revised or terminated, and will contribute to informed decisions regarding the continuance, modification or closure of disposal sites. This provides an important feedback mechanism for the protection of human health and the marine environment.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Canadian Navigable Waters Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 The following definitions apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous knowledge means the Indigenous knowledge of the Indigenous peoples of Canada. (connaissances autochtones)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous peoples of Canada has the meaning assigned by the definition aboriginal peoples of Canada in subsection 35(2) of the Constitution Act, 1982. (peuples autochtones du Canada)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: major work means any work designated under paragraph 28(2)(b). (ouvrage majeur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Transport. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: minor work means any work designated under paragraph 28(2)(a). (ouvrage secondaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: navigable water means a body of water, including a canal or any other body of water created or altered as a result of the construction of any work, that is used or where there is a reasonable likelihood that it will be used by vessels, in full or in part, for any part of the year as a means of transport or travel for commercial or recreational purposes, or as a means of transport or travel for Indigenous peoples of Canada exercising rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) there is public access, by land or by water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) there is no such public access but there are two or more riparian owners; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province is the only riparian owner. (eaux navigables)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: obstruction means any thing, including a vessel that is left anchored, moored or adrift or a wreck, that obstructs or impedes navigation or renders it more difficult or dangerous, but does not include a thing of natural origin unless a person causes the thing of natural origin to obstruct or impede navigation or to render it more difficult or dangerous. (obstacle)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: owner, in relation to a work, means the actual or reputed owner of the work or that owner's agent or mandatary. It includes a person who is in possession or claiming ownership of the work and a person who is authorizing or otherwise responsible for the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair, maintenance, operation, use or safety of the work. It also includes a person who proposes to construct or place a work. (proprietaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: person in charge, with respect to an obstruction, includes the owner of the obstruction and, in the case of a vessel, or part of one, that is an obstruction, the registered owner or other owner at the time the obstruction was occasioned, as well as the managing owner, master and any subsequent purchaser. (responsable)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Tribunal means the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada established by subsection 2(1) of the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada Act. (Tribunal)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vessel includes any description of ship, boat or floating craft designed, used or capable of being used for navigation, without regard to method or lack of propulsion, including everything forming part of its machinery, tackle, equipment, cargo, stores or ballast. (batiment)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: work includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any structure, device or other thing, whether temporary or permanent, that is made by humans, including a structure, device or other thing used for the repair or maintenance of another work; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any dumping of fill in any navigable water, or any excavation or dredging of materials from the bed of any navigable water. (ouvrage)

heading: For greater certainty - navigable water
paragraph: 2.01 For greater certainty, the definition navigable water in section 2 does not include artificial irrigation channels or drainage ditches.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 2.1 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Duty of Decision Maker
paragraph: 2.3 When making a decision under this Act, the Minister must consider any adverse effects that the decision may have on the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Canada recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Works
paragraph: 3 Except in accordance with this Act, it is prohibited to construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission a work in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water.

heading: Minor works
paragraph: 4 (1) An owner of a minor work may construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission the minor work in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water in accordance with the requirements under this Act.

heading: Repair, maintenance, operation and use
paragraph: (2) The owner must repair, maintain, operate and use the minor work in accordance with the requirements under this Act.

heading: Notice
paragraph: 4.1 An owner who proposes to construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission one of the following works may do so if the work, or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, would not interfere with navigation and the owner, before beginning the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, deposits any information specified by the Minister in any place specified by the Minister and publishes a notice in any manner, and including any information, specified by the Minister:

heading: Notice
paragraph: (a) a major work in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water; or

heading: Notice
paragraph: (b) a work - other than a minor work - in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water that is listed in the schedule.

heading: Application for approval
paragraph: 5 (1) An owner who proposes to construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission one of the following works must make an application for an approval to the Minister - in the form and manner, and containing the information, specified by the Minister - if the work, or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, may interfere with navigation:

heading: Application for approval
paragraph: (a) a major work in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water; or

heading: Application for approval
paragraph: (b) a work - other than a minor work - in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water that is listed in the schedule.

heading: Related works
paragraph: (2) If the Minister is of the opinion that two or more works are related, the Minister may consider them to be a single work.

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of determining whether the work or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning may interfere with navigation, the Minister may require from the owner any additional information that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: No interference with navigation
paragraph: 6 If the Minister is of the opinion that a work that is the subject of an application made under subsection 5(1), or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, would not interfere with navigation, including by changing the water level or water flow of a navigable water, he or she must inform the owner, in writing, of that opinion and no approval is required under subsection 7(6) for that work - or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning.

heading: Interference with navigation
paragraph: 7 (1) If the Minister is of the opinion that a work that is the subject of an application made under subsection 5(1), or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, may interfere with navigation, including by changing the water level or water flow of a navigable water, he or she must inform the owner, in writing, of that opinion and the owner may only construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission that work if the Minister issues an approval for the work.

heading: Information
paragraph: (2) The owner must deposit any information specified by the Minister in any place specified by the Minister.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) The owner must publish a notice containing any information specified by the Minister in any manner specified by the Minister.

heading: Comment period
paragraph: (4) The notice referred to in subsection (3) must invite interested persons to provide written comments on the owner's proposal to the Minister within 30 days after publication of the notice or within any other period specified by the Minister.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (5) If the Minister is satisfied that the owner has already deposited sufficient information in a place specified by the Minister or published a sufficient notice, the Minister may exempt the owner from the application of subsection (2) or (3), as the case may be.

heading: Approval
paragraph: (6) The Minister may issue an approval for the work, including its site and plans, if he or she considers it appropriate in the circumstances.

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (7) In determining whether to issue the approval, the Minister must consider the following:

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (a) the characteristics of the navigable water in question;

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (b) the safety of navigation in that navigable water;

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (c) the current or anticipated navigation in that navigable water;

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (d) the impact of the work on navigation, including as a result of its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair, maintenance, operation or use;

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (e) the impact of the work, in combination with other works, on navigation, if the Minister is provided with, or has in his or her possession, information relating to that cumulative impact;

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (f) any Indigenous knowledge that has been provided to the Minister;

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (g) any comments that he or she receives from interested persons within the period provided for under subsection (4);

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (h) the record of compliance of the owner under this Act; and

heading: Assessment - factors
paragraph: (i) any other information or factor that he or she considers relevant.

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (8) For the purpose of determining whether to issue the approval, the Minister may require from the owner any additional information that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Terms and conditions
paragraph: (9) The Minister may attach any term or condition that he or she considers appropriate to an approval including one that requires the owner to

heading: Terms and conditions
paragraph: (a) maintain the water level or water flow necessary for navigation purposes in a navigable water; or

heading: Terms and conditions
paragraph: (b) give security in the form of a letter of credit, guarantee, suretyship or indemnity bond or insurance or in any other form that is satisfactory to the Minister.

heading: Effect of approval
paragraph: (10) An approval issued under this section in relation to a work replaces any approval previously issued in relation to that work.

heading: Contiguous area
paragraph: (11) The Minister may, in an approval, designate an area contiguous to a work that is necessary for the safety of persons and navigation and, for the purposes of the approval, that area is considered to be part of the work.

heading: Compliance with requirements
paragraph: (12) The owner must comply with the approval and maintain, operate and use the work in accordance with the requirements under this Act.

heading: Approval after activity begins
paragraph: (13) The Minister may, if he or she considers that it is justified in the circumstances, approve the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning of a work after the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning begins or is completed.

heading: Transfer
paragraph: 8 If the ownership of a work to which an approval relates is transferred, the transferor and the transferee must immediately give written notice of the transfer to the Minister, in the form and manner, and containing the information, specified by the Minister.

heading: Amendment of approval
paragraph: 9 (1) The Minister may amend an approval by amending or revoking any term or condition of the approval.

heading: Amendment resulting from order
paragraph: (2) The Minister may otherwise amend the approval, including by adding terms and conditions, to reflect any changes to the work resulting from an order made under section 11 or 13.

heading: Other amendments
paragraph: (3) The Minister may otherwise amend the approval, including by adding terms and conditions, if he or she considers that

heading: Other amendments
paragraph: (a) the work that is the subject of the approval interferes more with navigation at the time in question than it did when the approval was issued;

heading: Other amendments
paragraph: (b) the work causes or is likely to cause a serious and imminent danger to navigation;

heading: Other amendments
paragraph: (c) the amendment of the approval is in the public interest; or

heading: Other amendments
paragraph: (d) the owner consents to the amendment.

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (4) The Minister may suspend or cancel an approval if he or she considers that

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (a) the owner has not complied with the approval;

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (b) the approval was obtained by a fraudulent or improper means or by the misrepresentation of a material fact;

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (c) the owner has not paid a fine or penalty imposed under this Act;

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (d) the owner has contravened this Act; or

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (e) the suspension or cancellation is in the public interest, including by reason of the record of compliance of the owner under this Act.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (5) The Minister must give the owner 30 days' notice setting out the grounds on which the Minister relies for the amendment, except in the case of an amendment made under subsection (2) or paragraph (3)(b), suspension or cancellation of the approval of a work if he or she is amending it without the owner's consent or suspending or cancelling it.

heading: Notice
paragraph: 9.1 An owner who proposes to construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission a work - other than a major work or a minor work - in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water that is not listed in the schedule may do so if

heading: Notice
paragraph: (a) the work, or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, would not interfere with navigation; and

heading: Notice
paragraph: (b) before beginning the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, the owner deposits any information specified by the Minister in any place specified by the Minister and publishes a notice in any manner, and including any information, specified by the Minister.

heading: Application or notice
paragraph: 10 (1) An owner who proposes to construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission a work - other than a major work or a minor work - in, on, over, under, through or across any navigable water that is not listed in the schedule must take one of the following steps if the work, or its construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning, may interfere with navigation:

heading: Application or notice
paragraph: (a) make an application for an approval to the Minister, in the form and manner, and containing the information, specified by the Minister; or

heading: Application or notice
paragraph: (b) deposit any information specified by the Minister in any place specified by the Minister and publish a notice in any manner, and including any information, specified by the Minister.

heading: Deeming
paragraph: (2) An application made under paragraph (1)(a) is deemed to be an application made under subsection 5(1) and, if an approval is issued under subsection 7(6) in respect of the application, the work to which the approval relates is deemed to be a work constructed or placed in, on, over, under, through or across a navigable water that is listed in the schedule.

heading: Comment period
paragraph: (3) The notice referred to in paragraph (1)(b) must invite interested persons to provide written comments on the proposal, as it relates to navigation, to the owner within 30 days after publication of the notice or within any other period prescribed by regulation.

heading: Attempt to resolve
paragraph: 10.1 (1) If a comment that is provided to an owner under subsection 10(3) expresses a concern relating to navigation, the owner and the person who made the comment must attempt to resolve the person's concern within 45 days after the end of the period set out in that subsection or within any other period prescribed by regulation.

heading: Change to proposal
paragraph: (2) If, as a result of an attempt to resolve a concern under subsection (1), the owner makes a material change to the proposal, he or she must deposit the new information and publish a new notice, in accordance with paragraph 10(1)(b).

heading: Request to Minister
paragraph: (3) If the concern is not resolved within the period referred to in subsection (1), the person who made the comment may, within 15 days after the end of that period or within any other period prescribed by regulation, make a request to the Minister - in the form and manner, and containing the information, specified by the Minister - for a decision on whether the owner is required to apply for an approval in relation to the work.

heading: Decision by Minister
paragraph: (4) On receipt of a request under subsection (3), the Minister may decide that the owner is required to apply for an approval in relation to the work.

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (5) For the purpose of deciding whether to require an application for an approval under subsection (4), the Minister may require from the owner any additional information that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (6) The Minister must inform the owner and the person who made the request of his or her decision.

heading: Work may commence
paragraph: 10.2 (1) An owner who publishes a notice referred to in paragraph 10(1)(b) may only construct, place, alter, rebuild, remove or decommission the work

heading: Work may commence
