heading: Definitions
paragraph: flag state means the state whose flag a fishing vessel is entitled to fly; (Etat du pavillon)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: foreign fishing vessel means a fishing vessel that is not a Canadian fishing vessel; (bateau de peche etranger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: government vessel means, subject to subsection 17(2), any vessel that belongs to or is in the service of Her Majesty in right of Canada; (bateau de l'Etat)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: marine plant means a saltwater plant, including benthic and detached algae, flowering plants, brown algae, red algae, green algae and phytoplankton, and any part or derivative of a saltwater plant; (plante marine)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: NAFO Regulatory Area means that part of the following area, being the Convention Area of the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization, that is on the high seas:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the waters of the Northwest Atlantic Ocean north of 35°00' north latitude and west of a line extending due north from 35°00' north latitude and 42°00' west longitude to 59°00' north latitude, thence due west to 44°00' west longitude, and thence due north to the coast of Greenland, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the waters of the Gulf of St. Lawrence, Davis Strait and Baffin Bay south of 78°10' north latitude; (zone de reglementation de l'OPAN)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Port State Measures Agreement means the Agreement on Port State Measures to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing, approved by the Conference of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in Rome on November 22, 2009; (Accord sur les mesures de l'Etat du port)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: protection officer means, subject to subsection 17(2),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a fishery officer within the meaning of the Fisheries Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any person authorized by the Governor in Council to enforce this Act. (garde-peche)

heading: Definitions

heading: Meaning of state
paragraph: (2) In section 5.4, subparagraphs 6(f)(iv) and (vi), paragraphs 16.1(b) and 17(2)(b), sections 18.01 and 18.02 and paragraph 18.1(a.2), state includes an organization of foreign states.

heading: Entry of foreign vessels into Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: 3 No foreign fishing vessel shall enter Canadian fisheries waters for any purpose unless authorized by this Act or the regulations, any other law of Canada or a treaty.

heading: Fishing, etc., in Canada and Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: 4 (1) No person, being aboard a foreign fishing vessel or being a member of the crew of or attached to or employed on a foreign fishing vessel, shall in Canada or in Canadian fisheries waters

heading: Fishing, etc., in Canada and Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: (a) fish or prepare to fish,

heading: Fishing, etc., in Canada and Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: (b) unload, land or tranship any fish, outfit or supplies,

heading: Fishing, etc., in Canada and Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: (c) ship or discharge any crew member or other person,

heading: Fishing, etc., in Canada and Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: (d) purchase or obtain bait or any supplies or outfits, or

heading: Fishing, etc., in Canada and Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: (e) take or prepare to take marine plants,

heading: Fishing, etc., in Canada and Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: unless authorized by this Act or the regulations, any other law of Canada or a treaty.

heading: Fishing of sedentary species
paragraph: (2) No person, being aboard a foreign fishing vessel or being a member of the crew of or attached to or employed on a foreign fishing vessel, shall fish or prepare to fish for a sedentary species of fish in any portion of the continental shelf of Canada that is beyond the limits of Canadian fisheries waters, unless authorized by this Act or the regulations or any other law of Canada.

heading: Definition of sedentary species
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), sedentary species means any living organism that, at the harvestable stage, either is immobile on or under the seabed or is unable to move except in constant physical contact with the seabed or subsoil.

heading: Transporting fish into Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: 5 No person, being aboard a Canadian fishing vessel, shall bring into Canadian fisheries waters fish received outside Canadian fisheries waters from a foreign fishing vessel, unless authorized by the regulations.

heading: Purpose
paragraph: 5.1 Parliament, recognizing

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (a) that straddling stocks on the Grand Banks of Newfoundland are a major renewable world food source having provided a livelihood for centuries to fishers,

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (b) that those stocks are threatened with extinction,

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (c) that there is an urgent need for all fishing vessels to comply in both Canadian fisheries waters and the NAFO Regulatory Area with sound conservation and management measures for those stocks, notably those measures that are taken under the Convention on Future Multilateral Cooperation in the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries, done at Ottawa on October 24, 1978, Canada Treaty Series 1979 No. 11, and

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (d) that some foreign fishing vessels continue to fish for those stocks in the NAFO Regulatory Area in a manner that undermines the effectiveness of sound conservation and management measures,

heading: Purpose
paragraph: declares that the purpose of section 5.2 is to enable Canada to take urgent action necessary to prevent further destruction of those stocks and to permit their rebuilding, while continuing to seek effective international solutions to the situation referred to in paragraph (d).

heading: Conservation and management measures for the NAFO Regulatory Area
paragraph: 5.2 No person, being aboard a foreign fishing vessel of a prescribed class, shall, in the NAFO Regulatory Area, fish or prepare to fish for a straddling stock in contravention of any of the prescribed conservation and management measures.

heading: Prohibition - Fish Stocks Agreement
paragraph: 5.3 No fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement shall, in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(e)(ii),

heading: Prohibition - Fish Stocks Agreement
paragraph: (a) contravene a measure or regulation designated under subparagraph 6(e)(i);

heading: Prohibition - Fish Stocks Agreement
paragraph: (b) conceal, tamper with or dispose of anything that may afford evidence of a contravention of a measure or regulation designated under subparagraph 6(e)(i); or

heading: Prohibition - Fish Stocks Agreement
paragraph: (c) conceal its identity or registration, including displaying a false marking, identity or registration.

heading: Prohibition on fishing vessels of states party to treaties or arrangements
paragraph: 5.4 No fishing vessel of a state that is party to a treaty or arrangement described in paragraph 6(f) shall, in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(f)(ii), contravene a measure or regulation designated under subparagraph 6(f)(i).

heading: Prohibition on fishing vessels without nationality
paragraph: 5.5 No fishing vessel without nationality shall

heading: Prohibition on fishing vessels without nationality
paragraph: (a) in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(e)(ii), fish or prepare to fish or contravene a measure or regulation designated under subparagraph 6(e)(i); or

heading: Prohibition on fishing vessels without nationality
paragraph: (b) in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(f)(ii), fish or prepare to fish or contravene a measure or regulation designated under subparagraph 6(f)(i).

heading: Prohibition - importation
paragraph: 5.6 (1) No person shall import any fish or marine plant knowing it to have been taken, harvested, possessed, transported, distributed or sold contrary to any of the following:

heading: Prohibition - importation
paragraph: (a) an international fisheries treaty or arrangement to which Canada is party, including any conservation, management or enforcement measures taken under the treaty or arrangement;

heading: Prohibition - importation
paragraph: (b) any conservation or management measures of a fisheries management organization of which Canada is not a member that is prescribed by regulation;

heading: Prohibition - importation
paragraph: (c) a law related to fisheries of a foreign state.

heading: Prohibition - other
paragraph: (2) No person shall, in connection with the importation of any fish or marine plant, transport, sell, distribute, buy or accept the delivery of the fish or marine plant knowing that it was taken, harvested, possessed, transported, distributed or sold contrary to any of the following:

heading: Prohibition - other
paragraph: (a) an international fisheries treaty or arrangement to which Canada is party, including any conservation, management or enforcement measures taken under the treaty or arrangement;

heading: Prohibition - other
paragraph: (b) any conservation or management measures of a fisheries management organization of which Canada is not a member that is prescribed by regulation;

heading: Prohibition - other
paragraph: (c) a law related to fisheries of a foreign state.

heading: Prohibition - importation
paragraph: (3) No person shall import any fish or marine plant that is not accompanied by the documentation required by regulation.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) for authorizing, by means of licences, permits or otherwise,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) foreign fishing vessels to enter Canadian fisheries waters for any purpose specified in the regulations,

paragraph: (ii) persons to do all or any of the things described in paragraphs 4(1)(a) to (e), subsection 4(2) or section 5, or

paragraph: (b) respecting the issuance, suspension and cancellation of any licences or permits provided for under paragraph (a) and prescribing their forms, the fees payable therefor and their terms and conditions, which are in addition to such terms and conditions, if any, as the Minister may specify therein;

paragraph: (c) for appointing or authorizing persons to enforce the provisions of this Act and the regulations;

paragraph: (d) for securing and keeping any fishing vessels or things seized pursuant to this Act;

paragraph: (d.1) respecting documentation required for the importation of fish and marine plants;

paragraph: (e) for the implementation of the Fish Stocks Agreement, including regulations

paragraph: (i) incorporating by reference, or carrying out and giving effect to, any conservation or management measures, as of a fixed date or as they are amended from time to time, of a regional fisheries management organization or arrangement established by two or more states, or by one or more states and an organization of states, for the purpose of the conservation or management of a straddling fish stock or highly migratory fish stock, and designating from among the measures incorporated by reference or regulations made under this subparagraph those the contravention of which is prohibited by paragraph 5.3(a),

paragraph: (iv) empowering the Minister to authorize a state that is party to the treaty or arrangement to take enforcement action in respect of a Canadian fishing vessel,

paragraph: (v) respecting the manner of service and the giving and sending of summonses, notices, statements and other documents, and

paragraph: (vi) permitting Her Majesty in right of Canada to recover any reasonable costs incurred as a result of the detention in port of a fishing vessel of a state that is party to the treaty or arrangement.

heading: Definition of place
paragraph: 7 For the purposes of sections 7.1, 7.4, 7.6 and 9, place includes

heading: Definition of place
paragraph: (a) a fishing vessel found within Canadian fisheries waters or the NAFO Regulatory Area;

heading: Definition of place
paragraph: (b) any other vehicle, including a vessel or aircraft; and

heading: Definition of place
paragraph: (c) a container.

heading: Entry - any place
paragraph: 7.1 (1) A protection officer may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance with this Act, enter any place in which the protection officer has reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Entry - any place
paragraph: (a) there is any fish, marine plant or other thing in respect of which this Act applies;

heading: Entry - any place
paragraph: (b) there has been carried on, is being carried on or is likely to be carried on any activity in respect of which this Act applies; or

heading: Entry - any place
paragraph: (c) there are any records, books or other documents, including documents in electronic form, concerning anything referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b).

heading: Entry - fishing vessel within Canadian fisheries waters or NAFO Regulatory Area
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a protection officer may board a fishing vessel found within Canadian fisheries waters or the NAFO Regulatory Area for a purpose related to verifying compliance with this Act.

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (3) The protection officer referred to in subsection (1) or (2) may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance with this Act,

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (a) examine anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (b) use any means of communication in the place or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (c) use any computer system in the place, or cause it to be used, to examine data contained in or available to it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (d) prepare a document, or cause one to be prepared, based on the data;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (e) use any copying equipment in the place or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (f) conduct tests or analyses of anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (g) take measurements or samples of anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (h) take photographs or make recordings or sketches of anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (i) remove anything found in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (j) direct any person to put any machinery, vehicle or equipment in the place into operation or to cease operating it; and

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (k) prohibit or limit access to all or part of the place or to anything in the place.

heading: Entry - fishing vessels ordered to port by flag state
paragraph: (4) A protection officer may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance with a law related to fisheries of a foreign state, with any conservation or management measures of a fisheries management organization or with an international fisheries treaty or arrangement to which Canada is party, including any conservation, management or enforcement measures taken under the treaty or arrangement, board a foreign fishing vessel that was authorized to enter Canadian fisheries waters under subparagraph 6(a)(iii).

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (5) The protection officer may, for the purpose referred to in subsection (4), exercise the powers referred to in subsection (3) to the extent that the exercise of those powers is authorized by the foreign state or is provided for in the measures, treaty or arrangement in question.

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (6) The owner or person in charge of a place and every person in the place shall give all assistance that is reasonably required to enable a protection officer to perform his or her functions under this section and shall provide any document or information, and access to any data, that is reasonably required for that purpose.

heading: Person accompanying protection officer
paragraph: 7.2 A protection officer may be accompanied by any other person that the protection officer believes is necessary to help him or her perform his or her functions under this Act.

heading: Stopping and detaining vehicle
paragraph: 7.3 A protection officer may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance with this Act, direct that any vehicle, including a fishing vessel found within Canadian fisheries waters or the NAFO Regulatory Area, be stopped and moved to another location and may detain it for a reasonable time. The person in charge of the vehicle shall comply with the directions.

heading: Warrant to enter dwelling place
paragraph: 7.4 (1) If a place is a dwelling place, a protection officer may enter it without the occupant's consent only under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (2).

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (2) On ex parte application, a justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing a protection officer to enter a dwelling place, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant, and authorizing any other person named in the warrant to accompany the protection officer, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) the dwelling place is a place referred to in section 7.1;

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) entry to the dwelling place is necessary to verify compliance with this Act; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (c) entry was refused by the occupant or there are reasonable grounds to believe that entry will be refused by, or that consent to entry cannot be obtained from, the occupant.

heading: Enforcement on high seas for unauthorized fishing in Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: 7.5 (1) If a protection officer has reasonable grounds to believe that a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement or of a state that is party to a treaty or arrangement described in paragraph 6(f) has engaged in unauthorized fishing in Canadian fisheries waters and the vessel is in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(e)(ii) or (f)(ii), the officer may, with the consent of that state, take any enforcement action that is consistent with this Act.

heading: Powers not affected in case of pursuit
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not affect any powers the protection officer has in the case of a pursuit that began while the vessel was in Canadian fisheries waters.

heading: Search
paragraph: 7.6 (1) A justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, who on ex parte application is satisfied by information on oath that there are reasonable grounds to believe that there is in a place any fish, marine plant or other thing that was obtained by or used in, or that will afford evidence in respect of, a contravention of this Act, may issue a warrant authorizing the protection officer named in the warrant to enter and search the place for the fish, marine plant or other thing, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant.

heading: Search without warrant
paragraph: (2) A protection officer may exercise the powers referred to in subsection (1) without a warrant if the conditions for obtaining a warrant exist but, by reason of exigent circumstances, it would not be practical to obtain a warrant.

heading: Search - fishing vessels ordered to port by flag state
paragraph: (3) A justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, on ex parte application by a protection officer, may issue a warrant authorizing the protection officer named in the warrant to board a foreign fishing vessel that was authorized to enter Canadian fisheries waters under subparagraph 6(a)(iii) and search the vessel, or to enter any other place and search the other place, for any fish, marine plant or other thing, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Search - fishing vessels ordered to port by flag state
paragraph: (a) there are reasonable grounds to believe that there is in the vessel any fish, marine plant or other thing that was obtained by or used in, or that will afford evidence in respect of, a contravention of a law related to fisheries of a foreign state, any conservation or management measures of a fisheries management organization or an international fisheries treaty or arrangement to which Canada is party, including any conservation, management or enforcement measures taken under the treaty or arrangement, or there is in the other place any such fish, marine plant or other thing and that fish, marine plant or other thing is from the vessel; and

heading: Search - fishing vessels ordered to port by flag state
paragraph: (b) the vessel's flag state does not object to the search of the vessel.

heading: Presumption
paragraph: (4) The foreign fishing vessel's flag state is deemed to not object to the search if the protection officer has informed the flag state of his or her intention to apply for the warrant referred to in subsection (3) and the flag state has not communicated its objection within the period prescribed by regulation.

heading: Arrest
paragraph: 8 A protection officer may arrest without warrant any person who the officer believes on reasonable grounds has committed an offence under this Act.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: 8.1 A protection officer may, in the manner and to the extent prescribed by the regulations, use force that is intended or is likely to disable a foreign fishing vessel, if the protection officer

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (a) is proceeding lawfully to arrest the master or other person in command of the vessel; and

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (b) believes on reasonable grounds that the force is necessary for the purpose of arresting that master or other person.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: 9 (1) A protection officer who believes on reasonable grounds that an offence under this Act has been committed may seize

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (a) any fishing vessel by means of or in relation to which the officer believes on reasonable grounds the offence was committed;

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (b) any goods aboard a fishing vessel described in paragraph (a) or in any other place, including fish, marine plants, tackle, rigging, apparel, furniture, stores and cargo; or

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (c) any fishing vessel described in paragraph (a) and any of the goods described in paragraph (b).

heading: Seizure - fishing vessels ordered to port by flag state
paragraph: (2) A justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, on ex parte application by a protection officer, may issue a warrant authorizing the protection officer named in the warrant to seize any fish, marine plant or other thing in a foreign fishing vessel that was authorized to enter Canadian fisheries waters under subparagraph 6(a)(iii) or in any other place, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Seizure - fishing vessels ordered to port by flag state
paragraph: (a) there are reasonable grounds to believe that there is in the vessel any fish, marine plant or other thing that was obtained by or used in, or that will afford evidence in respect of, a contravention of a law related to fisheries of a foreign state, any conservation or management measures of a fisheries management organization or an international fisheries treaty or arrangement to which Canada is party, including any conservation, management or enforcement measures taken under the treaty or arrangement, or there is in the other place any such fish, marine plant or other thing and that fish, marine plant or other thing is from the vessel; and

heading: Seizure - fishing vessels ordered to port by flag state
paragraph: (b) the vessel's flag state does not object to the seizure.

heading: Presumption
paragraph: (3) The foreign fishing vessel's flag state is deemed to not object to the seizure if the protection officer has informed the flag state of his or her intention to apply for the warrant and the flag state has not communicated its objection within the period prescribed by regulation.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (4) Before issuing a warrant under subsection (2), the justice may require that notice of the application be given to any person who has an interest in the application in order to allow that person the opportunity to make representations.

heading: Custody of seized vessels and goods
paragraph: 10 Subject to section 11, any fishing vessel and goods seized pursuant to section 9 shall be retained in the custody of the protection officer who made the seizure or delivered into the custody of such person as the Minister may direct.

heading: Disposition
paragraph: 11 If any fish, marine plant or other thing that is perishable or susceptible to deterioration is seized under section 9, the protection officer or other person having the custody of the thing may dispose of it in any manner that he or she considers appropriate and any proceeds shall be paid to the Receiver General or deposited in a bank to the credit of the Receiver General.

heading: Return - things seized under subsection 9(1)
paragraph: 12 (1) Any fishing vessel or goods seized under subsection 9(1) or the proceeds realized from a sale of the vessel or goods under section 11 shall be returned or paid to the person from whom the fishing vessel or goods were seized if the Minister decides not to institute a prosecution in respect of an offence under this Act and, in any event, shall be so returned or paid on the expiry of three months after the day on which the seizure is made unless before that time proceedings in respect of the offence are instituted.

heading: Return or payment subject to section 16.7
paragraph: (2) In any event, the return of the fishing vessel or goods or the payment of the proceeds from the sale of the fishing vessel or goods are subject to section 16.7.

heading: Order to extend period of detention
paragraph: (3) A court may, by order, permit the vessel or goods seized under subsection 9(1) or the proceeds realized from a sale of the vessel or goods under section 11 to be detained for any further period that may be specified in the order if the Minister makes a request to that effect before the end of the period of detention in question and if the court is satisfied that it is justified in the circumstances.

heading: Return - things seized under subsection 9(2)
paragraph: 12.1 (1) Subject to section 16.7, any fish, marine plant or other thing seized under subsection 9(2) or the proceeds realized from a sale of the fish, marine plant or other thing under section 11 shall be returned or paid to the person from whom the fish, marine plant or other thing was seized on the expiry of three months after the day on which the seizure is made unless before that time an application referred to in subsection 16.01(1) is filed.

heading: Order to extend period of detention
paragraph: (2) A court may, by order, permit the fish, marine plant or other thing seized under subsection 9(2) or the proceeds realized from a sale of the fish, marine plant or other thing under section 11 to be detained for any further period that may be specified in the order if the Minister makes a request to that effect before the end of the period of detention in question and if the court is satisfied that it is justified in the circumstances.

heading: Redelivery pending proceedings
paragraph: 13 If a fishing vessel or goods have been seized under subsection 9(1) and proceedings in respect of an offence under this Act have been instituted, the court or judge may, with the consent of the protection officer who made the seizure, order redelivery of the fishing vessel or goods to the person from whom the fishing vessel or goods were seized on security by bond, with two sureties, in an amount and form satisfactory to the Minister, being given to Her Majesty.

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: 14 When a person or a fishing vessel is convicted of an offence under this Act, the convicting court or judge may, in addition to any other punishment imposed, order that

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: (a) any fishing vessel seized under paragraph 9(1)(a) by means of or in relation to which the offence was committed, or, if the vessel has been sold, the proceeds of the sale,

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: (b) any goods aboard a fishing vessel described in paragraph (a), including fish, marine plants, tackle, rigging, apparel, furniture, stores and cargo, or, if any of the goods have been sold under section 11, the proceeds of the sale,

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: (b.1) any goods seized under paragraph 9(1)(b) in any other place, including fish, marine plants, tackle, rigging, apparel, furniture, stores and cargo, by means of or in relation to which the offence was committed, or that were obtained by or used in the commission of the offence, or, if any of the goods have been sold under section 11, the proceeds of the sale, or

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: (c) any fishing vessel described in paragraph (a), or the proceeds of the sale of the vessel, and any of the goods described in paragraph (b) or (b.1), or the proceeds of the sale of the goods,

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: be forfeited, and on the making of the order the fishing vessel, goods or proceeds so ordered to be forfeited are forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Disposal of forfeited vessel or goods
paragraph: 15 Where proceedings in respect of an offence under this Act have been instituted and a fishing vessel or goods are at the final conclusion of the proceedings ordered to be forfeited, they may be disposed of as the Minister directs.

heading: Return if no forfeiture ordered
paragraph: 16 (1) If a fishing vessel or goods have been seized under subsection 9(1) and proceedings in respect of an offence under this Act have been instituted, but the fishing vessel or goods or any proceeds realized from a sale of the fishing vessel or goods under section 11 are not ordered to be forfeited at the final conclusion of the proceedings, they shall, subject to subsection (2) and to section 16.7, be returned or the proceeds shall be paid to the person from whom the fishing vessel or goods were seized.

heading: Exception in case of conviction and fine
paragraph: (2) Where the proceedings referred to in subsection (1) result in a conviction and a fine is imposed, the fishing vessel or goods may be detained until the fine is paid, the fishing vessel and the goods may be sold under execution in satisfaction of the fine or the proceeds realized from a sale of any of the goods pursuant to section 11 may be applied in payment of the fine.

heading: Forfeiture - seizure under subsection 9(2)
paragraph: 16.01 (1) A justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, on ex parte application by a protection officer, may order the forfeiture to Her Majesty in right of Canada of any fish, marine plant or other thing seized under subsection 9(2) or of the proceeds realized from a sale under section 11 of that fish, marine plant or other thing, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Forfeiture - seizure under subsection 9(2)
paragraph: (a) there are reasonable grounds to believe that the fish, marine plant or other thing was obtained by or used in, or will afford evidence in respect of, a contravention of a law related to fisheries of a foreign state, any conservation or management measures of a fisheries management organization or an international fisheries treaty or arrangement to which Canada is party, including any conservation, management or enforcement measures taken under the treaty or arrangement; and

heading: Forfeiture - seizure under subsection 9(2)
paragraph: (b) the foreign fishing vessel's flag state does not object to the forfeiture.

heading: Presumption
paragraph: (2) The foreign fishing vessel's flag state is deemed to not object to the forfeiture if the protection officer has informed the flag state of his or her intention to request the forfeiture and the flag state has not communicated its objection within the period prescribed by regulation.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) Before making the order, the justice may require that notice of the application be given to any person who has an interest in the application in order to allow that person the opportunity to make representations.

heading: Disposal
paragraph: (4) Once forfeited, the fish, marine plant or other thing shall be disposed of as the Minister directs.

heading: Return if no forfeiture ordered
paragraph: (5) Any fish, marine plant or other thing seized under subsection 9(2) or the proceeds realized from a sale of the fish, marine plant or other thing under section 11 that are not ordered to be forfeited shall, subject to section 16.7, be returned, or the proceeds shall be paid, to the person from whom the fish, marine plant or other thing was seized.

heading: Protection officer's powers
paragraph: 16.1 Any power conferred on a protection officer by or under this Act may be exercised by the officer

heading: Protection officer's powers
paragraph: (a) subject to section 16.2 and to any regulation made under subparagraph 6(e)(iii), in respect of a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement that is found in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(e)(ii);

heading: Protection officer's powers
paragraph: (b) subject to any regulation made under subparagraph 6(f)(iii), in respect of a fishing vessel of a state party to a treaty or an arrangement described in paragraph 6(f) when the vessel is found in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(f)(ii); or

heading: Protection officer's powers
paragraph: (c) in respect of a fishing vessel without nationality found in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(e)(ii) or (f)(ii).

heading: Protection officer's powers
paragraph: 16.2 (1) A protection officer may, in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(e)(ii), for a purpose related to verifying compliance with section 5.3 and any regulations made under subparagraph 6(e)(i), board a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement and exercise the powers referred to in subsection 7.1(3).

heading: Search
paragraph: (1.1) If the protection officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the fishing vessel has contravened section 5.3, the officer may, with a warrant issued under section 7.6 or without a warrant in exigent circumstances, search the fishing vessel and exercise the power under subsection 9(1) to seize evidence.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) If the protection officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the fishing vessel has contravened section 5.3, the officer shall without delay inform the state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement.

heading: Consent
paragraph: (3) In addition to the powers referred to in subsections (1) and (1.1), a protection officer may, with the consent of the state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement, exercise any powers referred to in section 16.1. The officer is deemed to have received the consent of the state if the state has not responded within the period prescribed by regulation or has responded but is not fully investigating the alleged contravention.

heading: Forfeiture - treaty or arrangement
paragraph: 16.3 (1) A justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, on ex parte application by a protection officer, may order the forfeiture to Her Majesty in right of Canada of any fish or marine plant detained by a protection officer if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Forfeiture - treaty or arrangement
paragraph: (a) the detention of the fish or marine plant is consistent with an international fisheries treaty or arrangement to which Canada is party, including any conservation, management or enforcement measures taken under the treaty or arrangement;

heading: Forfeiture - treaty or arrangement
paragraph: (b) the forfeiture of the fish or marine plant is consistent with the treaty or arrangement; and

heading: Forfeiture - treaty or arrangement
paragraph: (c) the foreign fishing vessel's flag state has not provided the Minister, within the time period required by the treaty or arrangement, with the information required by the treaty or the arrangement to prevent the forfeiture.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) Before making the order, the justice may require that notice of the application be given to any person who has an interest in the application in order to allow that person the opportunity to make representations.

heading: Disposal
paragraph: (3) Once forfeited, the fish or marine plant shall be disposed of as directed by the Minister.

heading: Disclosure
paragraph: 16.4 The Minister may disclose to a foreign fishing vessel's flag state, to the state of nationality of the foreign fishing vessel's master or to a coastal state, fisheries management organization, organization of states or international organization information that relates to any of the following:

heading: Disclosure
paragraph: (a) a refusal to authorize the foreign fishing vessel to enter Canadian fisheries waters;

heading: Disclosure
paragraph: (b) a suspension, amendment or cancellation of an authorization granted to the foreign fishing vessel;

heading: Disclosure
paragraph: (c) a change to a decision referred to in paragraph (a) or (b);

heading: Disclosure
paragraph: (d) the outcome of any proceeding relating to a decision referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (c);

heading: Disclosure
paragraph: (e) an inspection report in respect of the foreign fishing vessel;

heading: Disclosure
paragraph: (f) an enforcement action taken by a protection officer in respect of the foreign fishing vessel.

heading: Measures - Canadian fishing vessel
paragraph: 16.5 The Minister may disclose to a party to the Port State Measures Agreement, coastal state, fisheries management organization or international organization information relating to any measure that is taken under the Fisheries Act in respect of a Canadian fishing vessel in response to a measure that is taken, in respect of that vessel, by another state under the Port State Measures Agreement.

heading: Canada Border Services Agency
paragraph: 16.6 For a purpose related to verifying compliance with this Act, the Minister may disclose to the Canada Border Services Agency information relating to the importation of any fish or marine plant.

heading: Sending abroad
paragraph: 16.7 (1) A justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, on ex parte application by a protection officer, may order that anything seized under this Act be sent to a foreign state if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that the foreign state has requested that the thing be sent to it for the purpose of administering or enforcing its laws.

heading: Terms and conditions
paragraph: (2) The justice may include in the order any terms and conditions that he or she considers appropriate, including those that are necessary to give effect to the request and those that relate to the preservation and return to Canada of the thing or the protection of the interests of third parties.

heading: Requirement to bring before justice
paragraph: (3) The justice may require that the thing be brought before him or her.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (4) Before making the order, the justice may require that notice of the application be given to any person who has an interest in the application in order to allow that person the opportunity to make representations.

heading: Offences
paragraph: 17 (1) Every person is guilty of an offence who

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) being master or in command of a fishing vessel,

heading: Offences
paragraph: (i) enters Canadian fisheries waters contrary to this Act, or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (ii) without legal excuse, the proof of which lies on that person, fails to bring to when required to do so by any protection officer or on signal of a government vessel;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) being aboard a fishing vessel, refuses to answer any questions on oath put to that person by a protection officer;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) after signal by a government vessel to bring to, throws overboard or staves or destroys any part of the vessel's cargo, outfit or equipment; or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) resists or wilfully obstructs any protection officer in the execution of the officer's duty.

heading: Meaning of government vessel and protection officer
paragraph: (2) In subsection (1), government vessel also includes a vessel that belongs to or is in the service of, and protection officer also includes an enforcement official of,

heading: Meaning of government vessel and protection officer
paragraph: (a) a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement if the vessel or official, as the case may be, is acting in the performance of their duties in relation to the Fish Stocks Agreement; or

heading: Meaning of government vessel and protection officer
paragraph: (b) a state that is party to a treaty or arrangement described in paragraph 6(f) if the vessel or official, as the case may be, is acting in the performance of their duties in relation to the treaty or arrangement.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: 18 (1) Every person who contravenes paragraph 4(1)(a), subsection 4(2) or section 5.2 is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine not exceeding seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding one hundred and fifty thousand dollars.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who contravenes any of paragraphs 4(1)(b) to (e), section 5 or the regulations and every fishing vessel that contravenes any of sections 5.3 to 5.5 or the regulations is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand dollars; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand dollars.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (3) Every person who commits an offence under paragraph 17(a), (b) or (c) is liable

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand dollars; or

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand dollars.

heading: Idem
paragraph: (4) Every person who commits an offence under paragraph 17(d) is liable

heading: Idem
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand dollars or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or to both; or

heading: Idem
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand dollars or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or to both.

heading: Proof of offence - Fish Stocks Agreement
paragraph: 18.01 (1) In a prosecution of a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement or a state that is party to a treaty or arrangement described in paragraph 6(f) or of a fishing vessel without nationality for an offence under this Act, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by a person on board the vessel, whether or not the person is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Appearance of vessel
paragraph: (2) A fishing vessel on which a summons is served shall appear by counsel or agent.

heading: Trial if vessel does not appear
paragraph: (3) If a fishing vessel does not appear, the court may, on proof of service of the summons, proceed with the trial in the absence of the vessel.

heading: Proceedings on indictment
paragraph: (4) For greater certainty, subsection (3) applies in respect of a trial on an indictment.

heading: Fines
paragraph: 18.02 If a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement or a state that is party to a treaty or arrangement described in paragraph 6(f) or a fishing vessel without nationality is convicted of an offence under this Act, the amount of the fine imposed on the vessel is a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada owed by the person who, at the time the offence was committed, was lawfully entitled to possession of the vessel, whether as owner or as charterer.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: 18.03 (1) Every person who contravenes subsection 5.6(1) or (2) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $100,000.

heading: Subsequent offences
paragraph: (2) If a person is convicted of an offence under subsection (1) a subsequent time, the amount of the fine for the subsequent offence may be up to double the amount set out in that subsection.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (3) Every person who contravenes subsection 5.6(3) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $100,000.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: 18.04 If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act and the court is satisfied that, as a result of committing the offence, financial benefits accrued to the person, the court may, despite the maximum amount of any fine that may otherwise be imposed under this Act, order the person to pay an additional fine in an amount equal to the court's estimation of those benefits.

heading: Application of criminal law
paragraph: 18.1 An act or omission that would be an offence under an Act of Parliament if it occurred in Canada is deemed to have been committed in Canada if it occurs, in the course of enforcing this Act,

heading: Application of criminal law
paragraph: (a) in the NAFO Regulatory Area on board or by means of a foreign fishing vessel on board or by means of which a contravention of section 5.2 has been committed;

heading: Application of criminal law
paragraph: (a.1) in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(e)(ii) on board or by means of a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement or of a fishing vessel without nationality;

heading: Application of criminal law
paragraph: (a.2) in an area of the sea designated under subparagraph 6(f)(ii) on board or by means of a fishing vessel of a state that is party to a treaty or arrangement referred to in that subparagraph or of a fishing vessel without nationality; or

heading: Application of criminal law
paragraph: (b) in the course of continuing pursuit that commenced while a foreign fishing vessel was in Canadian fisheries waters or the NAFO Regulatory Area.

heading: Exercising powers of arrest, entry, etc.
paragraph: 18.2 (1) Every power of arrest, entry, search or seizure or other power that could be exercised in Canada in respect of an act or omission referred to in section 18.1 in the circumstances referred to in that section may be exercised

heading: Exercising powers of arrest, entry, etc.
paragraph: (a) on board the foreign fishing vessel; or

heading: Exercising powers of arrest, entry, etc.
paragraph: (b) where pursuit has been commenced, at any place on the seas, other than a place that is in the territorial sea or internal waters of a state other than Canada.

heading: Arrest, search, seizure, etc.
paragraph: (2) A justice of the peace or judge in any territorial division in Canada has jurisdiction to authorize an arrest, entry, search or seizure or an investigation or other ancillary matter related to an offence referred to in section 18.1 in the same manner as if the offence had been committed in that territorial division.

heading: Attorney General of Canada
paragraph: (3) If an act or omission that is an offence by virtue only of paragraph 18.1(a) or (b) is alleged to have been committed on board or by means of a vessel that is registered or licensed under the laws of a state other than Canada, the powers referred to in subsection (1) may not be exercised outside Canada with respect to that act or omission without the consent of the Attorney General of Canada.

heading: Territorial division
paragraph: 18.3 A proceeding in respect of

heading: Territorial division
paragraph: (a) an offence under this Act consisting of a contravention of section 5.2, or

heading: Territorial division
paragraph: (b) an offence referred to in section 18.1

heading: Territorial division
paragraph: that is committed outside Canada may, whether or not the accused is in Canada, be commenced in any territorial division in Canada and the accused may be tried and punished for that offence in the same manner as if the offence had been committed in that territorial division.

heading: Attorney General of Canada
paragraph: 18.4 No proceeding in respect of

heading: Attorney General of Canada
paragraph: (a) an offence under this Act consisting of a contravention of any of sections 5.2 to 5.5,

heading: Attorney General of Canada
paragraph: (b) an offence referred to in section 18.1, or

heading: Attorney General of Canada
paragraph: (c) an offence under paragraph 17(1)(d) consisting of resistance to or obstruction of a protection officer in the execution of the officer's duty in relation to any of sections 5.2 to 5.5

heading: Attorney General of Canada
paragraph: may be commenced without the personal consent in writing of the Attorney General of Canada or the Deputy Attorney General, and such a proceeding may be conducted only by the Attorney General of Canada or counsel acting on his or her behalf.

heading: Proceedings against fishing vessels
paragraph: 18.5 All the provisions of this Act and the Criminal Code or the Fisheries Act and the Criminal Code relating to indictable offences that are applicable to or in respect of persons apply, in their application to indictable offences created by this Act or the Fisheries Act, to or in respect of fishing vessels, with such modifications as the circumstances require, and all the provisions of this Act and the Criminal Code or the Fisheries Act and the Criminal Code relating to summary conviction offences that are applicable to or in respect of persons apply, in their application to all other offences created by this Act or the Fisheries Act, to or in respect of fishing vessels, with such modifications as the circumstances require.

heading: Jurisdiction of courts
paragraph: 19 All courts, justices of the peace and provincial court judges in Canada have the same jurisdiction with respect to offences under this Act as they have under sections 257 and 258 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 with respect to offences under that Act, and those sections apply to offences under this Act in the same manner and to the same extent as they apply to offences under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Coastal Fisheries Protection Act; (Loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: applicant means a person signing an application for a licence pursuant to section 6; (requerant)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: CASPO Convention means the Convention for the Conservation of Anadromous Stocks in the North Pacific Ocean; (convention CPAPN)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: crew means, in relation to a foreign fishing vessel, any person on board that vessel other than a protection officer, observer or other representative of the Government of Canada on board the vessel in the course of his duties; (membre de l'equipage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Division 3L means Division 3L as described in paragraph 4(b) of Note A of Schedule III to the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985; (division 3L)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Division 3M means Division 3M as described in paragraph 4(b) of Note A of Schedule III to the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985; (division 3M)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Division 3N means Division 3N as described in paragraph 4(b) of Note A of Schedule III to the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985; (division 3N)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Division 3NO means Division 3NO as described in section 3 of note B of Schedule III to the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985; (division 3NO)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Division 3O means Division 3O as described in paragraph 4(b) of Note A of Schedule III to the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985; (division 3O)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Fishing Zone 4, Fishing Zone 5 or Fishing Zone 6 means the area of the sea described as Fishing Zone 4, Fishing Zone 5 or Fishing Zone 6 in the Fishing Zones of Canada (Zones 4 and 5) Order and the Fishing Zones of Canada (Zone 6) Order; (Zone de peche 4, Zone de peche 5, Zone de peche 6)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: flag state of a foreign fishing vessel means the state in which the vessel is registered or, where the vessel is not registered, the state whose flag the vessel is entitled to fly; (Etat du pavillon)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: International Code of Signals means the International Code of Signals published by the Department of Transport; (Code international de signaux)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: licence means a licence issued pursuant to section 5; (licence)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: master includes every person having command or charge of a fishing vessel but does not include a pilot; (capitaine)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: NAFO means the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization; (OPAN)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: NAFO Convention means the Convention on Future Multilateral Cooperation in the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries; (Convention de l'OPAN)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: NAFO Measures means the Conservation and Enforcement Measures adopted by NAFO; (mesures de l'OPAN)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: NPFC means the North Pacific Fisheries Commission established in accordance with the NPF Convention; (CPPN)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: NPF Convention means the Convention on the Conservation and Management of High Seas Fisheries Resources in the North Pacific Ocean; (Convention PPN)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: NPFC Convention Area means the area described in Part 1 of Schedule 2; (zone de la Convention de la CPPN)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: NPFC Measures means the Active Conservation and Management Measures adopted by the NPFC; (mesures de la CPPN)

heading: Interpretation

heading: Interpretation

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: processing includes cleaning, filleting, tubing, icing, packing, canning, freezing, smoking, salting, cooking, pickling, drying, or preparing fish for market in any other manner; (traitement)

heading: Interpretation

heading: Interpretation

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: WCPFC Measures means the Conservation and Management Measures adopted by the WCPFC; (mesures de la CPPOC)

paragraph: WCPFC Regulatory Area means the area described in Part 2 of Schedule 2. (zone de reglementation de la CPPOC)
