heading: Licences
paragraph: 5 (1) The Minister may, on receipt of an application for a licence, issue a licence authorizing

heading: Licences
paragraph: (a) a foreign fishing vessel and its crew to enter Canadian fisheries waters for any of the following purposes:

heading: Licences
paragraph: (i) to engage in commercial fishing,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (ii) to tranship or take on board any fish, outfit or supplies while at sea,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (iii) to process fish at sea,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (iv) to transport fish from fishing grounds,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (v) to provision, service, repair or maintain any other foreign fishing vessel while at sea,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (vi) to purchase or obtain bait, outfits or supplies at a Canadian port,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (vii) to effect repairs at a Canadian port,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (viii) to purchase, load, unload, transship, sell or process fish or fish products at a Canadian port,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (ix) to unload, land, re-embark or tranship at a Canadian port any equipment of that vessel or of any other fishing vessel of the same flag state,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (x) to grant shore leave to the crew of that vessel at a Canadian port, and

heading: Licences
paragraph: (xi) to discharge or take on board at a Canadian port a member of the crew of that vessel or of any other fishing vessel of the same flag state;

heading: Licences
paragraph: (b) a foreign fishing vessel and its crew to pass through any of the following Canadian fisheries waters during the course of a voyage to a destination outside Canadian fisheries waters, namely,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (i) the waters between Vancouver Island and the mainland of British Columbia bounded on the south by the 49th parallel of latitude and bounded on the north by a straight line from Cape Sutil on the northern end of Vancouver Island to Cape Caution on the mainland of British Columbia,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (ii) Fitz Hugh Sound bounded on the south by a straight line from Cape Calvert on Calvert Island to Cape Caution on the mainland of British Columbia and bounded on the north by a straight line from Carpenter Point on Hunter Island to Bernhardt Point on King Island,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (iii) Finlayson Channel bounded on the south by a straight line from Jorkins Point on Swindle Island to Keith Point on Dowager Island and bounded on the north by a straight line from Ohio Rock off Sarah Island to Finlayson Head on the mainland of British Columbia,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (iv) Laredo Channel bounded on the south by a straight line from Tildesley Point on Aristazabal Island to Dallain Point on Princess Royal Island and bounded on the north by a straight line from Ulric Point on Aristazabal Island to McPhee Point on Princess Royal Island,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (v) Princess Royal Channel bounded on the south by a straight line from Quarry Point on Princess Royal Island to Netherby Point on the mainland of British Columbia and bounded on the north by a straight line from Nelly Point on Princess Royal Island to Point Cumming on Gribbell Island,

heading: Licences
paragraph: (vi) Principe Channel bounded on the south by a straight line from Deer Point on Banks Island to Ring Point on Pitt Island and bounded on the north by a straight line true west from Keswar Point on McCauley Island to the shore of Banks Island, and

heading: Licences
paragraph: (vii) Grenville Channel bounded on the south by a straight line from Yolk Point on Farrant Island to Sainty Point on the mainland of British Columbia and bounded on the north by a straight line from Rippon Point on Pitt Island to Buckley Point on the mainland of British Columbia; and

heading: Licences
paragraph: (c) a foreign fishing vessel and its crew to enter Canadian fisheries waters to engage in fishing for purposes of scientific research or any activity described in any of subparagraphs (a)(ii) to (xi) or subsection (1.1) that relates to the scientific research.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (1.1) The Minister may, on receipt of an application for a licence, issue a licence authorizing a foreign fishing vessel and its crew to enter Canadian fisheries waters for any of the following purposes:

heading: Licences
paragraph: (a) to provide supplies to a Canadian fishing vessel or a foreign fishing vessel while it is at sea; and

heading: Licences
paragraph: (b) for the purpose described in paragraph (a), to purchase supplies at a Canadian port.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (1.11) The Minister shall not issue a licence under paragraph (1)(a) or subsection (1.1) unless the Minister determines that the Government of Canada has favourable fisheries relations with the government of the vessel's flag state and, if the licence relates to a specific fishery, that the Government of Canada has favourable fisheries relations with the government of the vessel's flag state with respect to that fishery.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (1.12) The Minister shall not issue a licence under paragraph (1)(a) or subsection (1.1) if there are reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Licences
paragraph: (a) the vessel is not licensed or otherwise authorized by its flag state to engage in fisheries activities;

heading: Licences
paragraph: (b) the vessel is not in compliance with relevant conservation and management measures;

heading: Licences
paragraph: (c) the vessel is providing supplies to a foreign fishing vessel that is not in compliance with relevant conservation and management measures;

heading: Licences
paragraph: (d) the proposed activity is not compatible with or will undermine relevant conservation and management measures; or

heading: Licences
paragraph: (e) the proposed activity is not consistent with the sustainable use of fisheries resources or will contribute to excess harvesting or processing capacity.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (1.2) The Minister shall, on receipt of an application for a licence and in accordance with the Proces-Verbal applying the March 27, 1972 Agreement between Canada and France on their Mutual Fishing Relations, signed on December 2, 1994, issue a licence authorizing a French fishing vessel and its crew to enter Canadian fisheries waters for any of the purposes set out in that Proces-Verbal.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (1.3) The Minister shall, on receipt of an application for a licence and in accordance with the Treaty between the Government of Canada and the Government of the United States of America on Pacific Coast Albacore Tuna Vessels and Port Privileges, signed on May 26, 1981, issue a licence authorizing a United States fishing vessel and its crew to enter Canadian fisheries waters for any of the purposes set out in that Treaty.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (1.4) The Minister shall, on receipt of an application for a licence and in accordance with the Convention between Canada and the United States of America for the Extension of Port Privileges to Halibut Fishing Vessels on the Pacific Coasts of the United States of America and Canada, signed on March 24, 1950, issue a licence authorizing a United States fishing vessel and its crew to enter Canadian fisheries waters for any of the purposes set out in that Convention.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (1.5) The Minister may refuse to issue a licence referred to in any of subsections (1.2) to (1.4) if he or she determines that one of the circumstances set out in paragraphs (1.12)(a) to (e) applies and that the flag state has taken insufficient measures to remedy the situation.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (2) The fees payable for a licence issued pursuant to this section are as set out in Schedule I.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (3) The licence fees for foreign fishing vessels shall be paid within 45 days from the date of billing.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, at the request of the master of a foreign fishing vessel that is in Canadian fisheries waters in the circumstances referred to in section 14 or 15, issue a licence authorizing that vessel and its crew to engage in all or any of the activities described in subparagraphs (1)(a)(vi) to (xi) and paragraph (1)(b).

heading: Order Made by Flag State
paragraph: 5.1 (1) The Minister may, further to an order made by the flag state, issue a permit authorizing a foreign fishing vessel and its crew to enter Canadian fisheries waters for the purpose of verifying compliance with a law, measure or treaty referred to in subparagraph 6(a)(iii) of the Act.

heading: Order Made by Flag State
paragraph: (2) If the Minister issues a permit under subsection (1), he or she must advise both the flag state and the foreign fishing vessel and inform them of the permit's conditions.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: 6 (1) Subject to subsection (3), the representative of the flag state of a foreign fishing vessel mentioned in paragraph 7(f) may apply for a licence referred to in section 5 in respect of that vessel and its crew by filing an application, signed by the representative, at the regional headquarters of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans responsible for issuing such licences for that flag state.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (2) An application referred to in subsection (1) shall be filed not less than 30 days prior to the first day on which the licence is required except that the Minister may, in order to prevent hardship, accept an application at any time.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (3) Where an application for a licence is in respect of a foreign fishing vessel that is under a charter to

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (a) an individual resident and domiciled in Canada,

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (b) a corporation incorporated under the laws of Canada or a province, or

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (c) Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province,

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: the application shall be signed by the charterer who shall, in respect of that vessel, be regarded as the representative designated pursuant to paragraph 7(f).

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: 7 The following information shall be furnished and forwarded with an application referred to in subsection 6(1) in respect of a foreign fishing vessel:

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (a) the name and description of the vessel, its equipment and complement;

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (b) the flag state and home port of the vessel;

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (c) the name of the owner and master of the vessel and, where applicable, its charterer;

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (d) the side number of the vessel, its radio frequencies and call sign;

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (e) a description of the proposed purpose and the period for which the licence is required;

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (f) the name and address of a person resident in Canada having a permanent office or establishment in Canada who is authorized by the flag state to represent that flag state for the purpose of providing liaison with the appropriate officials of the Government of Canada;

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (f.1) in the case of an application for a licence referred to in paragraph 5(1)(a) or subsection 5(1.1), any information or document that is relevant to the matters referred to in paragraphs 5(1.12)(a) to (e);

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (f.2) any information that is required by Annex A to the Port State Measures Agreement; and

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (g) any information the Minister considers necessary to clarify or complete the information furnished by the applicant.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: 7.1 (1) An application for a licence may be made on behalf of pair trawlers and shall contain the information required by section 7 in respect of both vessels.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (2) Where a licence is issued in respect of pair trawlers, it shall be issued in respect of the vessel designated in the application as the command vessel and shall be carried on board that vessel.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: 8 (1) Every licence shall

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (a) apply only to the foreign fishing vessel described therein and where applicable to the crew of that vessel;

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (b) be valid only for the period specified therein; and

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (c) cease to be valid on any change in the flag state registry or ownership of the vessel described in the licence.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (3) The Minister may amend any provision in the licence on receipt of an application from the person referred to in paragraph 7(f) or, if an error has been made in the licence, on his or her own initiative.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (4) An application referred to in subsection (3) shall be filed not less than 14 days prior to the first day on which the amendment is required except that the Minister may, in order to prevent hardship, accept an application at any time.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (5) An amendment referred to in subsection (3) is not binding on the master of the vessel to which the licence applies until it is received by the representative in Canada designated pursuant to paragraph 7(f).

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (6) The fees payable for amendment of a licence issued pursuant to subsection (3) are set out in Schedule I.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: 9 (1) Subject to subsection (2), every licence shall be kept on board the foreign fishing vessel described in the licence while that vessel is in Canadian fisheries waters and shall be produced for examination by a protection officer at his request.

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (2) Where a licence has been issued but not delivered, a Regional Director-General shall authorize the foreign fishing vessel described in the licence to enter Canadian fisheries waters and proceed directly to the Canadian port designated by him for the purpose of obtaining the licence if

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (a) all fishing gear on board the vessel is stowed below deck or otherwise removed from the place where it is normally used for fishing and placed where it is not readily available for fishing; and

heading: Application for Licence
paragraph: (b) the master of the vessel complies with any direction given to him by a protection officer.

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: 11 (1) Every licence or permit in respect of a foreign fishing vessel is subject to the following terms and conditions:

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (b) the vessel and its crew shall engage only in the activities that are authorized by the licence or permit;

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (c) the activities authorized by the licence or permit shall be carried out only at the times and in the areas of Canadian fisheries waters or ports specified in the licence or permit;

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (d) where fishing is authorized by the licence

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (i) the crew of the vessel shall fish only for a species of fish specified in the licence,

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (ii) the crew of the vessel shall not catch and retain any fish of a species, size or age specified in the licence as prohibited catch and any prohibited catch shall be returned to the water, alive if possible,

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (v) the crew of the vessel shall fish only by means of fishing equipment and gear of a type specified in the licence, and

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (vi) if a quantity of gear and equipment is specified in the licence, the crew of the vessel shall not fish with a quantity of gear and equipment that exceeds that specified quantity;

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (e) where the transporting of fish from fishing grounds is authorized by the licence

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (i) only the species and quantities of fish specified in the licence shall be taken on board the vessel for that purpose,

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (ii) the fish may be taken on board only from vessels of a class specified in the licence, and

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (iii) the master of the vessel shall cause written records to be maintained on a daily basis of the fish taken on board the vessel for transportation;

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (h) the vessel shall have on board at all times during the period it is in Canadian fisheries waters equipment and gear, including communications equipment, described in the licence or permit as "required equipment";

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (m) where the Minister requests the flag state of the vessel to carry out, from time to time, a program of sampling, observation or research in connection with fisheries in Canadian fisheries waters, the master shall comply with instructions issued to him by the authorized officials of that flag state in respect of that program;

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (u) the master or crew of the vessel shall not carry out any activity in any area of Canadian fisheries waters that is contrary to the Fisheries Act or regulations made under that Act.

heading: Terms and Conditions of a Licence or Permit
paragraph: (2) The master of a foreign vessel in respect of which a licence or permit has been issued shall not contravene or fail to comply with any condition of that licence or permit.

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: 12 (1) The master of a foreign fishing vessel operating under the authority of a licence shall

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (a) at least 24 hours or such shorter period as may be approved by the Regional Director-General prior to the entry of that vessel into Canadian fisheries waters notify the Regional Director-General designated in the licence of

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (i) the estimated time of entry of the vessel into such waters,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (ii) the location of such entry,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (iii) the approximate schedule of activities to be conducted while in such waters, and

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (iv) the quantity in metric tons of fish by species and product form on board the vessel;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (b) when authorized by the licence to enter a Canadian port, notify the Regional Director-General of the estimated time of entry into and departure from that port not less than 24 hours prior to those estimated times;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (c) where the vessel is in Canadian fisheries waters, notify the Regional Director-General of the estimated time of departure from such waters not less than 72 hours prior to that estimated time or such shorter period as may be approved by the Regional Director-General;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (d) where the vessel is in an area of Canadian fisheries waters and is not authorized by the licence to engage in fishing at that time in that area, ensure that all fishing gear on board the vessel is stored below deck or otherwise removed from the place where it is normally used for fishing and placed where it is not readily available for fishing;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (e) permit, when requested by the Regional Director-General, observers to go on board and remain on board the vessel at a time and for a period specified in the request for the purposes of recording scientific data, making observations and taking samples;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (f) embark or disembark the observers at a time and place specified in a request made under paragraph (e);

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (g) take all reasonable precautions to ensure the safety of any protection officer or observer boarding or leaving the vessel at sea including the observance of practices of good seamanship and, where necessary, the placing of a pilot ladder over the side of the vessel;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (h) where a protection officer or an observer is on board the vessel and remains on board the vessel for a period of more than four consecutive hours, provide the protection officer or observer with food and accommodation equivalent to that received by officers of the vessel;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (i) provide all reasonable assistance in his power to enable a protection officer or an observer on board the vessel to carry out his duties and in particular, but without restricting the generality of the foregoing, shall

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (i) provide him with a suitable work area including a table and sufficient lighting to carry out his work,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (ii) provide him with access to the vessel records and logs pertaining to its fishing activities,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (iii) provide him, on request, with the position of the vessel in latitude and longitude,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (iv) send and receive messages on his behalf by means of the communications equipment on board the vessel,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (v) provide him with access to all areas of the vessel involved in the fishing, processing and storage operations,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (vi) permit him to take samples and provide him with all reasonable assistance in his doing so,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (vii) provide him with suitable storage facilities for his samples,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (viii) permit him to examine and measure any fishing gear on board the vessel and provide him with all reasonable assistance in his doing so,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (ix) permit him to take photographs of the fisheries operations, including fishing gear and equipment, and

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (x) permit him to remove from the vessel samples, information, photographs or film taken or made during his time on board the vessel;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (j) where supplied with a log book requiring the recording of the fishing activities, catch, production and transfer of fish and fish products in accordance with the instructions contained in that log book

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (i) fully and accurately complete that log book on a daily basis, and

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (ii) provide the Regional Director-General with a copy of the information entered in that log book;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (k) send the original of the log book required to be completed under paragraph (j)

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (i) upon request, to a protection officer or a Regional Director-General as soon as the request is made, or

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (ii) where a request has not been made under subparagraph (i), to the Regional Director-General designated in the licence not later than 60 days after the expiration date of the licence;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (l) cause reports to be made containing the information specified, at the times specified, to the persons specified and by the means specified in the licence;

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (m) while in Canadian fisheries waters, at the request of a Regional Director-General or a protection officer proceed forthwith to the place at sea or the port specified in the request for the purpose of inspection; and

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (n) ensure that the vessel at all times while in Canadian fisheries waters is flying the flag of its flag state.

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (2) The master of a foreign fishing vessel in respect of which a licence has been issued shall not operate that vessel for fishing or cause it to be operated for fishing unless the side number specified in the licence is painted on the vessel or affixed permanently to the vessel by some other means and

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels

paragraph: (c) is white on a black background or black on a white background;

paragraph: (d) is in alignment and in a horizontal line; and

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: 12.1 (1) Subject to subsection (3), the master of a foreign fishing vessel entering Canadian fisheries waters shall, as soon as is reasonably possible, notify a protection officer or Regional Director-General of the name, flag state, location, route and destination of the vessel and of the circumstances under which it entered Canadian fisheries waters.

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the master of a foreign fishing vessel that has entered Canadian fisheries waters shall, while in those waters,

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (a) ensure that all fishing gear on board the vessel is stowed below deck or otherwise removed from the place where it is normally used for fishing and placed where it is not readily available for fishing; and

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (b) at the request of a protection officer, proceed to a location indicated by the officer for the purpose of carrying out an inspection of the vessel.

heading: Requirements of the Masters of Foreign Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (3) Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to a foreign fishing vessel in respect of which a licence has been issued under these Regulations or a United States sport fishing vessel authorized to enter Canadian fisheries waters pursuant to section 16.

heading: Authorization for Canadian Fishing Vessels to Land Fish Received from Foreign Vessels
paragraph: 13 The Minister may, at the request of the owner or master of a Canadian fishing vessel, issue a licence authorizing the master to bring into Canadian fisheries waters fish, of a species and quantity specified in the licence, received outside Canadian fisheries waters from a foreign fishing vessel.

heading: Importation
paragraph: 13.01 For the purposes of sections 13.02 to 13.06, meat means any part of the fish except the head, eyes, roe, guts, bones and tail.

heading: Importation
paragraph: 13.02 (1) For the purpose of subsection 5.6(3) of the Act, any of the following fish that is subject to measures established by the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas (ICCAT) and that is imported must be accompanied by:

heading: Importation
paragraph: (a) in the case of Atlantic bluefin tuna, a catch document or re-export certificate, as the case may be, that complies with the ICCAT Bluefin Tuna Catch Documentation Program that is current at the time that the fish are caught;

heading: Importation
paragraph: (b) in the case of Atlantic bigeye tuna, a statistical document or a re-export certificate, as the case may be, that complies with the ICCAT Bigeye Tuna Statistical Document Program that is current at the time that the fish are caught; or

heading: Importation
paragraph: (c) in the case of Atlantic swordfish meat, a statistical document or a re-export certificate, as the case may be, that complies with the ICCAT Swordfish Statistical Document Program that is current at the time that the fish are caught.

heading: Importation
paragraph: (2) The documents referred to in paragraph (1)(b) are not required in the case of Atlantic bigeye tuna that was caught by purse seiners or pole and line bait vessels and is destined principally for a cannery located in Canada.

heading: Importation
paragraph: 13.03 For the purpose of subsection 5.6(3) of the Act, any importation of Patagonian toothfish or Antarctic toothfish must be accompanied by a catch document or a re-export certificate, as the case may be, that complies with the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR) Catch Documentation Scheme for Dissostichus spp. that is current at the time that the fish are caught.

heading: Importation
paragraph: 13.04 For the purpose of subsection 5.6(3) of the Act, any importation of eastern Pacific bigeye tuna meat must be accompanied by a statistical document or a re-export certificate, as the case may be, that complies with the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission (IATTC) Bigeye Tuna Statistical Document Program that is current at the time that the fish are caught.

heading: Importation
paragraph: 13.05 For the purpose of subsection 5.6(3) of the Act, any importation of southern bluefin tuna meat must be accompanied by a catch monitoring form or a re-export or export after landing of domestic product form, as the case may be, that complies with the Commission for the Conservation of Southern Bluefin Tuna (CCSBT) Catch Documentation Scheme that is current at the time that the fish are caught.

heading: Importation
paragraph: 13.06 (1) For the purpose of subsection 5.6(3) of the Act, any importation of Indian Ocean bigeye tuna meat must be accompanied by a statistical document or a re-export certificate, as the case may be, that complies with the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC) Bigeye Tuna Statistical Document Programme that is current at the time that the fish are caught.

heading: Importation
paragraph: (2) The documents referred to in subsection (1) are not required in the case of Indian Ocean bigeye tuna that was caught by purse seiners or pole and line bait vessels and is destined principally for a cannery located in Canada.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences and Permits
paragraph: 13.1 (1) The Minister may suspend or cancel any licence or permit.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences and Permits
paragraph: (2) Where a licence or permit has been suspended or cancelled pursuant to subsection (1), the Minister

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences and Permits
paragraph: (a) shall, if requested, furnish reasons for the cancellation or suspension to the consular or the diplomatic authorities of the flag state of the foreign fishing vessel described in the licence or permit or the representative in Canada designated pursuant to paragraph 7(f);

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences and Permits
paragraph: (b) shall consider any written representation made with respect to the suspension or cancellation by or on behalf of the owner of the vessel; and

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences and Permits
paragraph: (c) may rescind the suspension or cancellation.

heading: Authorized Entry
paragraph: 14 A foreign fishing vessel may, without the authority of a licence, enter Canadian fisheries waters for the purpose of

heading: Authorized Entry
paragraph: (a) where the vessel is in distress, ensuring the safety of the vessel and its crew;

heading: Authorized Entry
paragraph: (b) rendering assistance to a vessel described in paragraph (a); or

heading: Authorized Entry
paragraph: (c) obtaining emergency medical assistance for a member of the crew at a Canadian port.

heading: Authorized Entry
paragraph: 15 A foreign fishing vessel may, without the authority of a licence, enter the territorial sea of Canada or Fishing Zone 4, Fishing Zone 5 or Fishing Zone 6 for the purpose of passing through such waters during the course of a voyage to a destination outside Canadian fisheries waters.

heading: Authorized Entry
paragraph: 16 Subject to the Fisheries Act and Regulations made thereunder, a United States sport fishing vessel and its crew may, without a licence, enter Canadian fisheries waters for the purpose of sport fishing and while in Canadian fisheries waters carry out the activities described in subparagraphs 5(1)(a)(vi), (vii) and (x).

heading: Signals
paragraph: 18 For the purposes of the Act and these Regulations, the signal requiring a fishing vessel to bring to is Signal L.

heading: Signals
paragraph: 18.1 When a protection officer on board an inspection vessel intends to board a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement, the signal to be used by the inspection vessel is Signal SQ 3.

heading: Signals
paragraph: 19 Where a protection officer or an observer on board a government vessel intends to board a fishing vessel at sea, the signal to be used by the government vessel is Signal SQ 3.

heading: Signals
paragraph: 19.1 For the purposes of the Act and these Regulations, the flying by a vessel of a pennant in the shape, size and colours set out in Schedule III identifies that vessel as a government vessel.

heading: Signals
paragraph: 19.2 The following methods of signalling may be used to send signals to fishing vessels:

heading: Signals
paragraph: (a) flag signalling using alphabetical flags;

heading: Signals
paragraph: (b) flashing light signalling using Morse symbols;

heading: Signals
paragraph: (c) sound signalling using Morse symbols;

heading: Signals
paragraph: (d) Morse signalling using hand-flags or arms;

heading: Signals
paragraph: (e) voice with or without using loud hailer;

heading: Signals
paragraph: (f) radiotelegraphy; and

heading: Signals
paragraph: (g) radiotelephony.

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: 19.3 A protection officer may use force under section 8.1 of the Act to arrest the master or other person in command of a foreign fishing vessel for the commission of an offence under section 3, paragraph 4(1)(a), section 5.2 or 5.5 or subparagraph 17(1)(a)(ii) of the Act.

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: 19.4 Before using force referred to in section 19.3, a protection officer shall

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: (a) consider all less violent means reasonable in the circumstances to have the foreign fishing vessel bring to, including

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: (i) interrupting the fishing operations of the vessel, including cutting the warps of a trawl net being towed by the vessel, and

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: (ii) boarding the vessel; and

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: (b) be satisfied that the foreign fishing vessel cannot be made to bring to by those means.

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: 19.5 A protection officer who has met the requirements of section 19.4 shall, before using force referred to in section 19.3,

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: (a) fire a warning shot or, if the protection officer considers it advisable, a series of warning shots in the vicinity of the foreign fishing vessel but at a safe distance and give the master or other person on board a reasonable opportunity to bring to; and

heading: Use of Force
paragraph: (b) signal the foreign fishing vessel by Signal SQ 1 and give the master or other person on board a reasonable opportunity to bring to.

heading: Return of Prohibited Species
paragraph: 20 The master of a foreign fishing vessel in respect of which a licence has been issued shall, if any fish of a species, size or age specified in the licence as prohibited catch is caught from the vessel, cause that fish to be immediately returned to the water in a manner that causes the least possible harm to that fish.

heading: States Party to the Fish Stocks Agreement
paragraph: 22 The foreign states and organizations of foreign states set out in Schedule IV are states party to the Fish Stocks Agreement.

heading: Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization
paragraph: 23 (1) The NAFO Regulatory Area is an area of the sea designated for the purposes of section 5.3 of the Act.

heading: Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization
paragraph: (2) The NAFO Regulatory Area is an area of the sea designated for the purposes of section 5.5 of the Act.

heading: Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization
paragraph: 24 (1) A fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement may fish in the NAFO Regulatory Area for fish of a stock set out in Annex I.A or I.B of the NAFO Measures only if the state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement is a party to the NAFO Convention.

heading: Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement that is not a party to the NAFO Convention may fish in the NAFO Regulatory Area for the fish referred to in that subsection if the fishing is done under an arrangement that is expressly contemplated by the NAFO Measures and in a manner that complies with this arrangement and the NAFO measures.

heading: Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: 25 (1) The WCPFC Regulatory Area is an area of the sea designated for the purposes of section 5.3 of the Act.

heading: Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: (2) The WCPFC Regulatory Area is an area of the sea designated for the purposes of section 5.5 of the Act.

heading: Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: 26 (1) A fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement may fish in the WCPFC Regulatory Area for fish of a stock regulated by the WCPFC Measures only if the state is a party to the WCPF Convention.

heading: Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement that is not a party to the WCPF Convention may fish in the WCPFC Regulatory Area for the fish referred to in subsection (1) if the fishing is done under an arrangement that is expressly contemplated by the WCPFC Measures and in a manner that complies with that arrangement and the WCPFC Measures.

heading: North Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: 27 (1) The NPFC Convention Area is an area of the sea designated for the purposes of section 5.3 of the Act.

heading: North Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: (2) The NPFC Convention Area is an area of the sea designated for the purposes of section 5.5 of the Act.

heading: North Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: 28 (1) A fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement may fish in the NPFC Convention Area for fish of a stock regulated by the NPFC Measures only if the state is a party to the NPF Convention.

heading: North Pacific Fisheries Commission
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement that is not a party to the NPF Convention may fish in the NPFC Convention Area for the fish referred to in subsection (1) if the fishing is done under an arrangement that is expressly contemplated by the NPFC Measures and in a manner that complies with that arrangement and the NPFC Measures.

heading: International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas
paragraph: 39 (1) All waters of the Atlantic Ocean and its adjacent seas beyond 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the territorial sea of a state is measured are hereby designated as areas of the sea regulated by the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas for the purposes of section 5.3 of the Act.

heading: International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas
paragraph: (2) All waters of the Atlantic Ocean and its adjacent seas beyond 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the territorial sea of a state is measured are hereby designated as areas of the sea regulated by the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas for the purposes of paragraph 5.5(a) of the Act.

heading: International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas
paragraph: 40 No fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement that is fishing in the waters referred to in subsection 39(1) shall have on board a bluefin tuna that weighs less than 3.2 kg.

heading: International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas
paragraph: 41 Sections 24, 26, 28 and 40 are designated as regulatory provisions whose contravention is prohibited under paragraph 5.3(a) of the Act.

heading: Enforcement Action in Respect of Canadian Fishing Vessels
paragraph: 42 The Minister may authorize a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement to take enforcement action in respect of a Canadian fishing vessel if there are reasonable grounds to believe the fishing vessel has contravened any measure established by the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas for the conservation or management of a highly migratory fish stock set out in the table to this section.

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: 43 (1) The waters of the North Pacific Ocean and its adjacent seas north of 33° N. latitude beyond 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the territorial sea of a state is measured are hereby designated as an area of the sea regulated by the CASPO Convention for the purposes of section 5.4 of the Act.

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: (2) The waters of the North Pacific Ocean and its adjacent seas north of 33° N. latitude beyond 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the territorial sea of a state is measured are hereby designated as an area of the sea regulated by the CASPO Convention for the purposes of paragraph 5.5(b) of the Act.

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: 44 (1) No fishing vessel of a state that is a party to the CASPO Convention shall

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: (a) engage in directed fishing for anadromous fish in the waters referred to in subsection 43(1); or

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: (b) retain any anadromous fish taken as an incidental taking while fishing for non-anadromous fish in the waters referred to in subsection 43(1).

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to fishing for scientific research purposes in accordance with Article VII of the CASPO Convention.

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) is hereby designated as a regulation the contravention of which is prohibited under section 5.4 of the Act.

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: 45 A protection officer may, in enforcing section 44, exercise the powers referred to in section 16.1 of the Act to the extent that they are consistent with the CASPO Convention.

heading: Implementation of the CASPO Convention
paragraph: 46 The Minister may authorize a state that is a party to the CASPO Convention to take enforcement action in respect of a Canadian fishing vessel if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the fishing vessel contravened any measure referred to in section 44.

heading: Implementation of the NAFO Measures
paragraph: 46.1 (1) A protection officer who is acting in the performance of their duties in relation to the NAFO Convention may exercise the enforcement powers set out in the NAFO Measures in the NAFO Regulatory Area with respect to

heading: Implementation of the NAFO Measures
paragraph: (a) a foreign fishing vessel of a state party to the NAFO Convention;

heading: Implementation of the NAFO Measures
paragraph: (b) a foreign fishing vessel that is authorized to fish in that Area under an arrangement that is expressly contemplated by the NAFO Measures; or

heading: Implementation of the NAFO Measures
paragraph: (c) any other foreign fishing vessel, except a foreign fishing vessel of a state that is set out in Table III or IV to section 21, if the master of the vessel consents to the protection officer exercising those enforcement powers.

heading: Implementation of the NAFO Measures
paragraph: (2) The protection officer may exercise those enforcement powers in Canadian fisheries waters with respect to a foreign fishing vessel referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

heading: Implementation of the NAFO Measures
paragraph: (3) The protection officer may detain fish unloaded in port from a foreign fishing vessel referred to in paragraph (1)(a) until the officer has received, from the flag state, the form or forms set out in Annex II.L of the NAFO Measures.

heading: Implementation of the WCPFC Measures
paragraph: 46.2 (1) A protection officer who is acting in the performance of their duties in relation to the WCPF Convention may exercise the enforcement powers set out in the WCPFC Measures in the WCPFC Regulatory Area with respect to

heading: Implementation of the WCPFC Measures
paragraph: (a) a foreign fishing vessel of a state party to the WCPF Convention;

heading: Implementation of the WCPFC Measures
paragraph: (b) a foreign fishing vessel that is authorized to fish in that Area under an arrangement that is expressly contemplated by the WCPFC Measures; or

heading: Implementation of the WCPFC Measures
paragraph: (c) any other foreign fishing vessel, if the master of the vessel consents to the protection officer exercising those enforcement powers.

heading: Implementation of the WCPFC Measures
paragraph: (2) The protection officer may exercise those enforcement powers in Canadian fisheries waters with respect to a foreign fishing vessel referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

heading: Implementation of the NPFC Measures
paragraph: 46.3 (1) A protection officer who is acting in the performance of their duties in relation to the NPF Convention may exercise the enforcement powers set out in the NPFC Measures in the NPFC Convention Area with respect to

heading: Implementation of the NPFC Measures
paragraph: (a) a foreign fishing vessel of a state party to the NPF Convention;

heading: Implementation of the NPFC Measures
paragraph: (b) a foreign fishing vessel that is authorized to fish in that Area under an arrangement that is expressly contemplated by the NPFC Measures; or

heading: Implementation of the NPFC Measures
paragraph: (c) any other foreign fishing vessel, if the master of the vessel consents to the protection officer exercising those enforcement powers.

heading: Implementation of the NPFC Measures
paragraph: (2) The protection officer may exercise those enforcement powers in Canadian fisheries waters with respect to a foreign fishing vessel referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

heading: Recovery of Costs
paragraph: 47 If a fishing vessel of a state party to the Fish Stocks Agreement is seized and, following a further investigation in port, the protection officer continues to have reasonable grounds to believe that an offence has been committed under section 24 or 40, Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover

heading: Recovery of Costs
paragraph: (a) any reasonable costs incurred for berthage of the fishing vessel;

heading: Recovery of Costs
paragraph: (b) any reasonable costs incurred for the security and maintenance of the fishing vessel; and

heading: Recovery of Costs
paragraph: (c) any reasonable costs incurred for the repatriation of the crew of the fishing vessel.

heading: Serving or Giving of Documents
paragraph: 48 In any proceeding against a fishing vessel in respect of an offence under any of sections 5.3 to 5.5 of the Act, a notice, statement, summons or other document may be given or served

heading: Serving or Giving of Documents
paragraph: (a) personally to a person who appears to be in charge of the fishing vessel;

heading: Serving or Giving of Documents
paragraph: (b) by mailing the document to the agent for the fishing vessel; or

heading: Serving or Giving of Documents
paragraph: (c) by posting the document in a conspicuous location on the fishing vessel.

heading: PART IVExemption from Amendment Fees

heading: PART IVExemption from Amendment Fees
paragraph: (b) early or late arrival of a vessel into Canadian fisheries waters within 14 days of the originally requested starting date on the initial entry of that vessel each year;

heading: PART IVExemption from Amendment Fees

heading: PART IVExemption from Amendment Fees

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: 2		  (1) For the purpose of minimizing the introduction of waste into the environment and preventing adverse impacts to the environment and human health, this code requires persons to use environmentally responsible and sustainable agricultural practices when carrying out agricultural operations and associated activities described in subsections (2.1) and (3).

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (2) This code applies to a person who carries out an agricultural operation described in subsection (2.1) or an associated activity described in subsection (3)

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (a) on an agricultural land base that is not zoned for residential purposes, and

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (b) whether or not for a commercial purpose.

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (2.1) Subject to subsection (4), rearing or keeping livestock, poultry or insects, or growing and harvesting agricultural products, is an agricultural operation for the purposes of this code if done for one or more of the following purposes:

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (a) for consumption or use by humans, including as food, fibre or fuel;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (b) for use as animal feed;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (c) for use as breeding stock or to produce seedlings or flowers;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (d) for work or recreational purposes, in the case of livestock or poultry;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (e) for use in landscaping or for ornamental purposes, in the case of plants, including trees.

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), if done together with an agricultural operation referred to in subsection (2.1), this code applies to the following activities:

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (a) storing nutrient sources;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (b) storing agricultural by-products that are not a source of nitrogen or phosphorus;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (b.1) storing the primary products of livestock, poultry, insects, plants and fungi;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (c) carrying out agricultural composting processes;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (d) applying nutrient sources to land;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (e) washing, grading or packaging agricultural products, if carried out on the same agricultural land base as the livestock or poultry were reared or kept or the agricultural products were grown or harvested;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (f) disposing of or incinerating mortalities and processing wastes, if carried out on the same agricultural land base as the livestock or poultry were reared or kept;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (g) operating equipment in relation to

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (i)  an activity referred to in this subsection, or

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (ii)  other activities in relation to agriculture, other than processing primary products beyond the activities described in paragraph (e).

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (4) The following are not agricultural operations for the purposes of this code:

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (a) aquaculture and activities described in subsection (3) that are carried out in respect of aquaculture;

heading: Agricultural operations to which this code applies
paragraph: (b) soil blending operations that bring manure, sand or other materials onto a parcel of land for the purpose of producing soil for use other than on that parcel.

heading: No registration required if small capacity or fuelled by electricity
paragraph: (A) §60.5475 Subpart QQQQ, "Standards of Performance for New Residential Hydronic Heaters and Forced-Air Furnaces", or

heading: No registration required if small capacity or fuelled by electricity
paragraph: (B) §60.536 Subpart AAA, "Standards of Performance for New Residential Wood Heaters".

heading: No registration required if small capacity or fuelled by electricity
paragraph: (2) A person is not required to be registered under section 4 of the Waste Discharge Regulation if the person uses only boilers and heaters that are fuelled by electricity.

heading: Air contaminants from forced air ventilation
paragraph:
6
		  A person who carries out an agricultural operation must ensure that emissions of air contaminants from forced air ventilation systems used in the agricultural operation do not enter a watercourse or cross a property boundary.

heading: When odours are not air contaminants
paragraph:
7
		  For the purposes of paragraph (d) of the definition of "air contaminant" in section 1 (1) of the Act, an odour does not interfere with the normal conduct of business if

heading: When odours are not air contaminants
paragraph: (a) the odour is produced in carrying out an agricultural operation in accordance with normal agricultural practices, and

heading: When odours are not air contaminants
paragraph: (b) ammonia, sulphur and other harmful compounds associated with the odour do not settle out of the air into a watercourse or across a property boundary at a level that would cause injury, interference, discomfort or damage as described in paragraphs (a) to (c), (e) or (f) of that definition.

heading: Application
paragraph:
8
		  (1) This Division applies to a person who uses a boiler or heater for the purposes of an agricultural operation, whether or not the person is required to be registered under section 4 of the Waste Discharge Regulation.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), this Division does not apply to a person who uses a boiler or heater that is fuelled only by electricity.

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph:
9
		  A person must use only the following as fuel for a boiler or heater:

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (a) biomass, including biomass that has been compressed, dried and processed into uniform, discrete pellets, pucks, bricks or other units and commonly referred to as manufactured fuel;

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (b) natural gas;

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (c) propane;

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (d) low-sulphur fuel that is

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (i)  No. 2 heating oil, or

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (ii)  diesel fuel for use in Canada in on-road vehicles;

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (e) biogas, a gas derived from the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter;

heading: Fuel restrictions
paragraph: (f) landfill gas, a mixture of gases generated by the decomposition of municipal solid waste within the meaning of Part 3 of the Act.

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A person who uses biomass as fuel for a boiler or heater to carry out an agricultural operation must visually assess the opacity of emissions from the boiler or heater at least once each day the boiler or heater is operating, during the period

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (a) that begins at least 60 minutes after the boiler or heater is started, and

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (b) that ends when shutdown procedures begin.

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (2) If a boiler or heater has a capacity of 1 MW or less, the person using the boiler or heater must

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (a) ensure that opacity levels do not exceed 20%, and

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (b) immediately take corrective action to reduce emissions if the assessment under subsection (1) indicates that the opacity level exceeds or is about to exceed 20%.

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (3) If a boiler or heater has a capacity of more than 1 MW, the person using the boiler or heater must

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (a) ensure that opacity levels do not exceed 10%, and

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (b) act in accordance with section 12 [taking corrective action] if the assessment under subsection (1) of this section indicates that the opacity level exceeds or is about to exceed 10%.

heading: Opacity limits
paragraph: (4) If more than one boiler or heater is connected to a single stack and the combined capacity is more than 1 MW, subsection (3) applies.

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph:
11
		  (1) A person who uses biomass as fuel for a boiler or heater that has a capacity of more than 1 MW to carry out an agricultural operation must test emissions of particulate matter from the boiler or heater as follows:

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (a) testing must be done within 6 months after

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (i)  installing the boiler or heater,

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (ii)  modifying a boiler or heater that had a capacity of 1 MW or less to increase its capacity to more than 1 MW, or

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (iii)  modifying the capacity of a boiler or heater described in subparagraph (i) or (ii) by more than 25%;

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (b) testing must be done during the period that begins on October 1 and that ends on April 30 of the next year,

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (i)  within the first year that the boiler or heater is operating, and

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (ii)  every second year afterwards, unless paragraph (a) (ii) or (iii) applies;

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (c) testing must be done when the boiler or heater is fuelled by biomass only and operating

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (i)  under normal operating conditions,

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (ii)  under standard conditions of 20°C, 101.3 kPa dry gas and 8% oxygen, and

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (iii)  at 75% or more of its capacity;

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (d) testing must be done during the period

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (i)  that begins at least 60 minutes after the boiler or heater is started, and

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (ii)  that ends when shutdown procedures begin;

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (e) unless a different method is specified by a director, testing must be done using a method set out in the British Columbia Field Sampling Manual or the British Columbia Environmental Laboratory Manual, as amended from time to time.

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (2) A person using a boiler or heater must

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (a) ensure that particulate matter emission levels do not exceed

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (i)  50 mg/m3, for a boiler or heater that has a capacity of more than 1 MW but equal to or less than 3 MW, or

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (ii)  35 mg/m3, for a boiler or heater that has a capacity of more than 3 MW, and

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (b) act in accordance with section 12 [taking corrective action] if testing under subsection (1) of this section indicates that the particulate matter emissions level exceeds or is about to exceed the applicable limit set under paragraph (a) of this subsection.

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (3) If more than one boiler or heater is connected to a single stack and the combined capacity is more than

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (a) 1 MW, subsection (2) (a) (i) applies, or

heading: Particulate matter limits
paragraph: (b) 3 MW, subsection (2) (a) (ii) applies.

heading: Taking corrective action
paragraph:
12
		  If an opacity limit under section 10 (3) (a) [opacity limits] or a particulate matter emissions limit under section 11 (2) (a) [particulate matter limits] is exceeded, the person using the boiler or heater must do all of the following:

heading: Taking corrective action
paragraph: (a) immediately notify a director;

heading: Taking corrective action
paragraph: (b) begin immediately to take corrective action to reduce the opacity level or the emissions to or below the applicable limit;

heading: Taking corrective action
paragraph: (c) assess opacity levels or test particulate matter emissions, as applicable,

heading: Taking corrective action
paragraph: (i)  immediately on completing the corrective action to confirm that limits are no longer being exceeded,

heading: Taking corrective action
paragraph: (ii)  again within 6 months after corrective action was taken, and

heading: Taking corrective action
paragraph: (iii)  at least once more in the next period that begins on October 1 and that ends on April 30 of the next year.

heading: Director may impose minimum stack height
paragraph:
13
		  A director may set a minimum stack discharge height for a boiler or heater fuelled by biomass, and, if set, the stack discharges from the boiler or heater must be no less than the height set.

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph:
14
		  A person who uses biomass as fuel for a boiler or heater must keep records and supporting documentation respecting all of the following:

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (a) the type and quantity of fuel burned by the boiler or heater;

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (b) all inspections and maintenance of the boiler or heater;

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (c) for each assessment and test conducted under this Part,

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (i)  the date and results of the assessment or test, and

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (ii)  the corrective actions, if any, taken under this Part.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
15
		  In this Part, "setback" means the distance between

heading: Definition
paragraph: (a) a structure or place where an activity is performed for the purposes of an agricultural operation, and

heading: Definition
paragraph: (b) a drinking water source, a watercourse or a property boundary.

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph:
16
		  (1) In this section, "high water mark" has the same meaning as in the Riparian Areas Regulation.

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of measuring a setback, measurements must be taken horizontally from the outer edge or limit of a structure or place where an activity occurs to the following:

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph: (a) in the case of a drinking water source

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph: (i)  that is groundwater, the outer edge of the well, reservoir or other structure used to collect the water, or

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph: (ii)  that is not groundwater, the top of its bank or its high water mark, as applicable;

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph: (b) in the case of a watercourse, the top of its bank or its high water mark, as applicable;

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph: (c) the property boundary.

heading: How to measure setbacks
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), if a setback is to be measured from a diversion point, measurements must be taken in a radius from the outer edge of the end of the pipe or other structure used to pump water out of a watercourse.

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph:
17
		  A person who, for the purposes of an agricultural operation, performs an activity described in column 1 of the following table must ensure a setback of at least the distances, in m, set out opposite the activity in columns 2 to 4:

heading: Exception for existing structures
paragraph:
18
		  Despite section 17 [setback requirements], the setbacks set out in column 4 of the table to that section do not apply to an existing permanent storage structure, or existing on-ground under-pen storage, if stored contents cannot escape.

heading: Director may impose greater setbacks
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Despite any other provision of this Part and without limiting section 7 of the Waste Discharge Regulation, a director may impose a greater setback than is otherwise required under this Part, or impose a setback where none is otherwise required under this Part, if the director has reason to believe that contaminated runoff, leachate or solids are or may be entering a drinking water source or watercourse, or crossing a property boundary.

heading: Director may impose greater setbacks
paragraph: (2) A person who, for the purposes of an agricultural operation, performs an activity in relation to which a setback is increased or imposed under subsection (1) must ensure a setback of at least the distance as increased or imposed under that subsection.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
20
		  (1) In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "high-precipitation area" means an area that has, on average, precipitation of 600 mm or more in total during the period that begins on October 1 and that ends on April 30 of the next year;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "high-risk area" means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a high-precipitation area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a vulnerable aquifer recharge area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a phosphorus-affected area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an area identified by a director as having permanent or usual geographic, topographic, weather-related or other features that present a high risk for adverse impacts on the environment or human health;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "high-risk condition" means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) strong, divergent windy conditions;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) storm events, or periods of short-term intense or high rainfall;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) seasonal high water tables or flooding;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the degree to which a field used for an agricultural operation slopes toward a watercourse, if sufficient to cause contaminated runoff;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a condition identified by a director as having temporary, intermittent or irregular topographic, weather-related or other features that present a high risk for adverse impact on the environment or human health.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), a director may identify an area as a high-risk area or a condition as a high-risk condition

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) on the director's own initiative, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) on application, made in the form and manner required by the director, by a person.

heading: Application
paragraph:
21
		  (1) This Part applies to a person who carries out an agricultural operation in a high-risk area or under conditions that are, or may become, high-risk conditions.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) If there is any inconsistency between a provision of this Part and any other provision of this code, the provision of this Part applies.

heading: Requirement to maintain protective base
paragraph:
22
		  A person who is required under this Part to have a protective base must do all of the following:

heading: Requirement to maintain protective base
paragraph: (a) maintain the base to prevent leakage and keep a record of all maintenance;

heading: Requirement to maintain protective base
paragraph: (b) assess the protective base for leakage at least once every 6 months;

heading: Requirement to maintain protective base
paragraph: (c) take corrective action to stop any leakage found on assessment and prevent further leaks;

heading: Requirement to maintain protective base
paragraph: (d) for each assessment conducted under paragraph (b), keep a record of

heading: Requirement to maintain protective base
paragraph: (i)  the date and results of the assessment, and

heading: Requirement to maintain protective base
paragraph: (ii)  the corrective actions taken under paragraph (c), if any.

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph:
23
		  (1) A person who uses a modified or new permanent storage structure in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area must ensure

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (a) that there is a protective base under the storage structure, and

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (b) that, if the structure is used to store liquid manure,

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (i)  the structure is designed by a qualified professional who has considered what is needed to protect aquifers located in the vulnerable aquifer recharge area, and is constructed according to that design,

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (ii)  either

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (A) the structure has a vertical distance of at least 1 m from the bottom of the protective base to the seasonal high water table, or

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (B) leak detection measures demonstrate that the structure is not leaking, and

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (iii)  the person keeps the design plans and a statement signed by the qualified professional indicating that the structure was constructed as designed.

heading: Permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas
paragraph: (2) A person who uses modified or new on-ground under-pen storage in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area must ensure that there is a protective base under the storage.

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph:
24
		  Despite section 23 (1) [permanent storage in vulnerable aquifer recharge areas], a person who began, before February 28, 2019, to store liquid manure in an earthen basin dug into the ground in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area must do all of the following:

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (a) have a qualified professional assess the storage basin for leaks of stored materials

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (i)  before February 28, 2021, and

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (ii)  until a protective base is installed, at least every 5 years after the last assessment or more often if the qualified professional believes it to be necessary;

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (b) if any leaks are found on assessment under paragraph (a),

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (i)  take immediate corrective action to stop the leaks and to prevent further leaks, and

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (ii)  take steps as soon as reasonably practicable to install a protective base on the bottom and sides of the storage basin;

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (c) keep a record of

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (i)  the date and results of each assessment conducted under paragraph (a), and

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (ii)  all actions taken under paragraph (b), if any;

heading: Earthen storage basins
paragraph: (d) whether or not any leaks are found on assessment under paragraph (a), have a protective base on the bottom and sides of the storage basin before February 28, 2029, or an earlier date required by a director.

heading: Temporary field storage and outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph:
25
		  (1) A person who uses temporary field storage or an outdoor agricultural composting pile in a high-precipitation area must cover the stored materials or the pile during the period that begins on October 1 and that ends on April 1 of the next year.

heading: Temporary field storage and outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (2) A person who uses temporary field storage for 2 weeks or more, or an outdoor agricultural composting pile, in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area must not locate the storage or pile directly on or over soil that has a saturated hydraulic conductivity of more than 10-3 cm/s, commonly referred to as coarse-textured soil.

heading: Irrigation
paragraph:
26
		  A person who irrigates land in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area must ensure that the quantity and timing of irrigation does not exceed crop needs.

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph:
27
		  (1) A person must not apply nutrient sources to land

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (a) in a high-precipitation area during the period that begins on November 1 and that ends on February 1 of the next year,

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (b) during strong, divergent windy conditions, unless the nutrient sources are applied

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (i)  below the soil surface, or

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (ii)  under a crop canopy having a height of at least 8 cm,

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (c) during storm events, or periods of short-term intense or high rainfall, or

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (d) during any high-risk conditions that are identified by a director under this Part and are relevant to the application of nutrient sources to land.

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (2) A person must not apply nutrient sources, other than wood residue, to land in a high-precipitation area during February, March or October unless both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (a) the nutrients are needed by, and will be available to, the intended crop;

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (b) a risk assessment is made in accordance with subsection (4) before application begins, and the assessment indicates that the risk of contaminated runoff is low.

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (2), a person may apply nutrient sources to bare soil in a high-precipitation area in the fall only if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (a) a crop is planted before the winter non-growing season begins;

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (b) the application is to medium or fine-textured soils with a low risk of leaching;

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (c) the nutrients will not enter a watercourse or go below the water table.

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (4) A person must prepare a risk assessment, in writing and in the form and manner required by a director,

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (a) for each field to which nutrient sources are to be applied, and

heading: Restrictions on applying nutrients
paragraph: (b) considering the special circumstances of the high-precipitation area and any high-risk conditions.

heading: Livestock or poultry
paragraph:
28
		  (1) A person responsible for a feedlot that will hold 10 animal units or more must comply with all applicable requirements of this section.

heading: Livestock or poultry
paragraph: (2) If the feedlot is located in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area but not in a high-precipitation area, the feedlot must have a protective base.

heading: Livestock or poultry
paragraph: (3) If the feedlot is located in a high-precipitation area, any part of the feedlot that is not covered by a roof must have a protective base if the feedlot

heading: Livestock or poultry
paragraph: (a) is also located in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area, or

heading: Livestock or poultry
paragraph: (b) is a new or modified feedlot.

heading: Livestock or poultry
paragraph: (4) If the feedlot is located in either a vulnerable aquifer recharge area or a high-precipitation area, there must be a vertical distance of at least 1.2 m from the bottom of the feedlot's protective base or self-sealing layer to the seasonal high water table.

heading: Burial pits
paragraph:
29
		  A person who buries mortalities, solid waste or semi-solid waste in a burial pit located in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area

heading: Burial pits
paragraph: (a) must not bury in a single pit more than 1 tonne of materials, and

heading: Burial pits
paragraph: (b) must ensure that there is a vertical distance of at least 2 m from the bottom of the pit to either the bedrock or the seasonal high water table.

heading: High-risk conditions
paragraph:
30
		  A person who carries out an agricultural operation, whether in a high-risk area or not, must do all of the following:

heading: High-risk conditions
paragraph: (a) monitor the agricultural operation for impending high-risk conditions;

heading: High-risk conditions
paragraph: (b) assess the effectiveness of existing measures and controls to prevent contaminated runoff, leachate and solids from entering a drinking water source or watercourse, or crossing a property boundary;

heading: High-risk conditions
paragraph: (c) if existing measures or controls are inadequate, take corrective action before high-risk conditions materialize.

heading: Application
paragraph:
31
		  This Division applies to a person who stores or uses agricultural by-products for the purposes of an agricultural operation.

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph:
32
