		  (1) A person may store and use solid agricultural by-products for the purposes of an agricultural operation only as follows:

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph: (a) solid agricultural by-products that are produced on the person's agricultural land base may be stored on that agricultural land base;

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph: (b) solid agricultural by-products that are not produced on the person's agricultural land base may be brought onto and stored on the person's agricultural land base only if subsequently used in agricultural operations carried out on that agricultural land base;

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph: (c) solid agricultural by-products may be stored only in a permanent storage structure or as temporary field storage;

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph: (d) manure and bedding from fur bearing animals may be stored in on-ground under-pen storage for no more than 7 months.

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph: (2) A person may carry out an agricultural composting process using solid agricultural by-products for the purposes of an agricultural operation only as follows:

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph: (a) solid agricultural by-products that are produced on the person's agricultural land base may be used in an agricultural composting process carried out on that agricultural land base;

heading: Allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products
paragraph: (b) solid agricultural by-products that are not produced on the person's agricultural land base may be brought onto the person's agricultural land base and used in an agricultural composting process only if the products of the agricultural composting process are subsequently used in agricultural operations carried out on that agricultural land base.

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A person may store liquid manure only as follows:

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (a) liquid manure may be stored on a person's agricultural land base only if the liquid manure is subsequently used in agricultural operations carried out on the agricultural land base on which the liquid manure was produced or stored;

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (2), liquid manure may be stored only in a permanent storage structure.

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (2) In an emergency affecting an agricultural operation, the person responsible for the agricultural operation may store liquid manure in a form of containment that is not a permanent storage structure if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (a) the person notifies a director immediately of the emergency;

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (b) within 5 days of notifying a director of the emergency, the person notifies a director of the person's plan to move the liquid manure to a permanent storage structure, or to apply the liquid manure to land, in a manner that complies with this code;

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (c) the person implements the plan in accordance with the notification under paragraph (b) and any directions of, or modifications required by, the director;

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (d) the stored liquid manure does not overflow;

heading: Allowable storage and use of liquid manure
paragraph: (e) the structure is monitored for leaks and corrective action is taken immediately if any leaks are found.

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph:
34
		  A person who stores agricultural by-products must ensure all of the following:

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (a) that any leachate generated during storage is

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (i)  collected or contained, and

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (ii)  not discharged directly to land or water;

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (b) that runoff is diverted away from the storage structure or storage area;

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (c) that the storage structure or storage area is maintained so as to prevent contaminated runoff, leachate, wastewater and solids from escaping;

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (d) if contaminated runoff, leachate, wastewater or solids escape from storage, they do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary, or go below the water table;

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (e) that air contaminants from stored agricultural by-products do not cross a property boundary;

heading: General storage requirements
paragraph: (f) that agricultural by-products are stored in a manner that will deter the attraction of, and access by, domestic pets, wildlife and vectors.

heading: General requirements for permanent storage structures
paragraph:
35
		  A person who uses a permanent storage structure must ensure that the structure has sufficient capacity to store agricultural by-products until they are

heading: General requirements for permanent storage structures
paragraph: (a) applied as a fertilizer or soil conditioner, or

heading: General requirements for permanent storage structures
paragraph: (b) transported away from the agricultural land base.

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph:
36
		  (1) A person who stores liquid manure in a permanent storage structure must ensure that the structure is one of the following:

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (a) an existing permanent storage structure;

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (b) a modified permanent storage structure and the modification was

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (i)  designed by a qualified professional who considered the entire structure and this code, and

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (ii)  constructed according to that design;

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (c) a new permanent storage structure that was designed by a qualified professional and constructed according to that design.

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (2) A person who stores liquid manure in a modified or new permanent storage structure must keep the design plans and a statement signed by the qualified professional indicating that the structure was constructed as designed.

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (3) A person who stores liquid manure in a permanent storage structure must ensure all of the following:

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (a) that the level of stored liquid manure reaches no more than 30 cm below the top of the structure;

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (b) that the structure has a protective base;

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (c) that the protective base is maintained to prevent leakage;

heading: Permanent storage structures for liquid manure
paragraph: (d) that the stored liquid manure does not leak from the structure or overflow.

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph:
37
		  (1) A person who uses temporary field storage to store solid agricultural by-products must ensure all of the following:

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (a) that field storage is not located

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (i)  in any area in which there is standing water or water-saturated soil, or

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (ii)  on any low-lying area of a field prone to annual seasonal flooding, during the flood season or when flooding is imminent;

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (b) that field storage is monitored at least once each week to ensure compliance with this code;

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (c) that, before the end of the growing period, but no later than 7 months after storage begins, all field-stored solid agricultural by-products are

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (i)  used,

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (ii)  moved to a permanent storage structure, if storage is allowed under section 32 (a) or (b) [allowable storage and use of solid agricultural by-products], or

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (iii)  transported away from the agricultural land base;

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (d) that vegetation is grown on the storage location after the field-stored solid agricultural by-products are used, moved or transported in accordance with paragraph (c), either in the current or next growing season;

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (e) that, if field storage is for a period of more than 2 weeks, temporary field storage does not occur in the same location again for at least 3 years.

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (2) A person who uses temporary field storage must keep a record of all of the following:

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (a) the type and source of the materials being stored and the date that storage began;

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (b) the location of the temporary field storage;

heading: Temporary field storage
paragraph: (c) the weekly results of monitoring conducted under subsection (1) (b).

heading: On-ground under-pen storage
paragraph:
38
		  (1) Without limiting section 34 [general storage requirements], a person who uses on-ground under-pen storage must ensure

heading: On-ground under-pen storage
paragraph: (a) that runoff is diverted away from stored materials, and

heading: On-ground under-pen storage
paragraph: (b) that, if contaminated runoff, leachate, solids or agricultural by-products escape from storage, steps are taken immediately to collect and contain them.

heading: On-ground under-pen storage
paragraph: (2) A person who uses on-ground under-pen storage must keep a record of the steps taken, if any, under subsection (1) (b).

heading: Application
paragraph:
39
		  This Division applies to a person who carries out an agricultural composting process for the purposes of an agricultural operation, other than to dispose of mortalities and processing wastes.

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph:
40
		  A person who carries out an agricultural composting process must ensure all of the following:

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (a) that only agricultural by-products and wood residue are used in the agricultural composting process;

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (a.1) that no non-agricultural waste materials are added to the agricultural composting process except as allowed under sections 67 (1), 71 and 72 [mortalities or processing waste];

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (a.2) that any leachate generated during the agricultural composting process is

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (i)  collected or contained, and

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (ii)  not discharged directly to land or water;

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (b) that runoff is diverted away from the agricultural composting process;

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (c) that the agricultural composting process is maintained so as to prevent contaminated runoff, leachate and solids from escaping;

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (d) that, if contaminated runoff, leachate or solids escape from the agricultural composting process, they do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (e) that air contaminants from the agricultural composting process do not cross a property boundary;

heading: General agricultural composting process requirements
paragraph: (f) that the agricultural composting process will be carried out in a manner that will deter the attraction of, and access by, domestic pets, wildlife and vectors.

heading: Requirements for composting structures
paragraph:
41
		  A person who uses a composting structure must ensure both of the following:

heading: Requirements for composting structures
paragraph: (a) that the structure has a protective base;

heading: Requirements for composting structures
paragraph: (b) that the protective base is maintained to prevent leakage.

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph:
42
		  (1) A person who uses outdoor agricultural composting piles must ensure all of the following:

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (a) that the pile is not located

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (i)  in any area in which there is standing water or water-saturated soil, or

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (ii)  on any low-lying area of a field prone to annual seasonal flooding, during the flood season or when flooding is imminent;

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (b) that the pile is monitored at least once each week to ensure compliance with this code;

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (c) that the pile does not remain for a period of more than 12 months;

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (d) that no other pile is erected in the same location for at least 3 years.

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (2) A person who uses outdoor agricultural composting piles must keep a record of all of the following:

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (a) the type and source of the materials being composted and the date that composting began;

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (b) the location of the pile;

heading: Requirements for outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (c) the weekly results of monitoring conducted under subsection (1) (b).

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph:
43
		  (1) This section applies to a person who

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (a) keeps 5 or more animal units, and

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (b) distributes from the person's agricultural land base any manure or product of an agricultural composting process that was produced on that agricultural land base.

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (2) A person who distributes manure or the product of an agricultural composting process in units of 5 m3 or less must keep an annual record of the following:

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (a) the total amount distributed, expressed in m3;

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (b) the dates that distribution began and ended;

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (c) the type of agricultural by-product distributed.

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (3) A person who distributes manure or the product of an agricultural composting process in units of more than 5 m3 must keep, for each distribution, a receipt that

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (a) is signed by the receiver, and

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (b) shows all of the following:

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (i)  the amount distributed, expressed in m3;

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (ii)  the date of distribution;

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (iii)  the type of agricultural by-product distributed;

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (iv)  the name and business contact information of the receiver.

heading: Distribution of manure or agricultural compost
paragraph: (4) A person who distributes a product resulting from an agricultural composting process must not describe the product as "compost" or "composted".

heading: Allowable storage and use of other nutrient sources
paragraph:
43.1
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person may do one or both of the following, but only if the nutrient sources are subsequently used in agricultural operations:

heading: Allowable storage and use of other nutrient sources
paragraph: (a) bring nutrient sources onto the person's agricultural land base;

heading: Allowable storage and use of other nutrient sources
paragraph: (b) store nutrient sources on the person's agricultural land base.

heading: Allowable storage and use of other nutrient sources
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to the following types of nutrient sources:

heading: Allowable storage and use of other nutrient sources
paragraph: (a) commercial fertilizers and soil conditioners;

heading: Allowable storage and use of other nutrient sources
paragraph: (b) agricultural by-products.

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph:
43.2
		  A person who stores nutrient sources to which section 43.1 applies must ensure all of the following:

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (a) that any leachate generated during storage is

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (i)  collected or contained, and

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (ii)  not discharged directly to land or water;

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (b) that runoff is diverted away from the storage structure or storage area;

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (c) that the storage structure or storage area is maintained so as to prevent contaminated runoff, leachate, wastewater and solids from escaping;

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (d) that if contaminated runoff, leachate, wastewater or solids escape from storage, they do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (e) that air contaminants from stored nutrient sources do not cross a property boundary;

heading: General storage requirements for other nutrient sources
paragraph: (f) that nutrient sources are stored in a manner that will deter the attraction of, and access by, domestic pets, wildlife and vectors.

heading: Application
paragraph:
44
		  This Division applies to a person who collects, stores or uses wood residue for the purposes of an agricultural operation.

heading: Allowable storage and use of wood residue
paragraph:
45
		  A person may do one or both of the following, but only if the wood residue is subsequently used in agricultural operations:

heading: Allowable storage and use of wood residue
paragraph: (a) bring wood residue onto the person's agricultural land base;

heading: Allowable storage and use of wood residue
paragraph: (b) store wood residue on the person's agricultural land base

heading: Allowable storage and use of wood residue
paragraph: (i)  in a permanent storage structure, or

heading: Allowable storage and use of wood residue
paragraph: (ii)  as temporary field storage for a period of no more than 12 months.

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph:
46
		  A person who stores wood residue or applies wood residue to land must ensure all of the following:

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph: (a) that storage is not located, or wood residue is not applied to land,

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph: (i)  in any area in which there is standing water or water-saturated soil, or

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph: (ii)  on any low-lying area of a field prone to annual seasonal flooding, during the flood season or when flooding is imminent;

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph: (b) that wood residue, contaminated runoff, leachate, solids and dust do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph: (c) in the case of storage,

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph: (i)  that leachate does not escape from the storage, and

heading: General storage and land application requirements
paragraph: (ii)  that runoff is diverted away from the storage.

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph:
47
		  (1) A person must not use wood residue

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (a) for the construction of berms,

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (b) as an envelope for tile drains,

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (c) as fill or to level a site,

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (d) to create an access way through a watercourse, or

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (e) for any other purpose, other than a purpose referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (2) Unless it would contravene subsection (1) (a) to (d), a person may use wood residue for the following purposes:

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (a) as plant mulch or for horticultural bedding;

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (b) as soil conditioner or ground cover;

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (c) as a component of growing media;

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (d) as a component of compost;

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (e) in confined livestock areas or confined poultry areas, or in areas where livestock and poultry are exercised;

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (f) as animal bedding;

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (g) to create an access way on an agricultural land base;

heading: Uses of wood residue
paragraph: (h) as fuel for wood-fired boilers.

heading: Application
paragraph:
48
		  This Division applies to a person who applies nutrient sources for the purposes of an agricultural operation.

heading: Prohibitions on applications to land
paragraph:
49
		  (1) A person must not apply nutrient sources to land

heading: Prohibitions on applications to land
paragraph: (a) on which there is standing water or water-saturated soil,

heading: Prohibitions on applications to land
paragraph: (b) on ground in which the top 5 cm of soil is frozen so as to be impenetrable to manually-operated equipment,

heading: Prohibitions on applications to land
paragraph: (c) on a field having at least 5 cm of ice or snow over at least 50% of its area, or

heading: Prohibitions on applications to land
paragraph: (d) at a rate of application, under meteorological, topographical or soil conditions, or in a manner, that may cause nutrient sources or contaminated runoff, leachate or solids to enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table.

heading: Prohibitions on applications to land
paragraph: (2) A person must not apply to land a material described in any of paragraphs (e) to (g) of the definition of "nutrient source" unless the material is treated, provided, used or produced, as applicable, in accordance with this code and the applicable regulation referred to in those paragraphs.

heading: Prohibitions on applying compost to land
paragraph:
50
		  (1) In this section, "foreign matter"

heading: Prohibitions on applying compost to land
paragraph: (a) means, subject to paragraph (b), a contaminant that does not readily decompose during an agricultural composting process, and

heading: Prohibitions on applying compost to land
paragraph: (b) does not include silt, sand, rocks or stones, gravel less than 2.5 cm in diameter, or other mineral materials naturally found in soil.

heading: Prohibitions on applying compost to land
paragraph: (2) A person must not apply to land the product of an agricultural composting process, or compost processed in accordance with the Organic Matter Recycling Regulation, if the product or compost contains any of the following:

heading: Prohibitions on applying compost to land
paragraph: (a) animal flesh, or bones with visible flesh attached;

heading: Prohibitions on applying compost to land
paragraph: (b) more than 1% foreign matter by dry weight;

heading: Prohibitions on applying compost to land
paragraph: (c) any sharp foreign matter in a size or shape that could cause injury to a person who or an animal that comes into contact with it.

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph:
51
		  (1) A person who applies nutrient sources to land must ensure all of the following:

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (a) that nutrient sources and leachate produced by nutrient sources do not escape during transportation or piping;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (b) that nutrient sources are not discharged or applied directly into a watercourse, across a property boundary or below the water table;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (c) that drift from nutrient sources sprayed onto land does not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (d) that the total amount of available nitrogen in the soil, if applicable, and from all nutrient sources applied in one year of application, is equal to or less than the amount of nitrogen needed for optimum crop growth and yield.

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (2) A person who applies nutrient sources to land, other than land that is part of an agricultural operation having an agricultural land base totalling less than 2 ha, must make and keep records of all of the following in respect of each field to which the nutrient sources are applied:

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (a) the location and size of the field;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (b) the crop nutrient requirements of the field;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (c) the crop yields of the field;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (d) the date and location of each application of nutrients;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (e) whether the nutrient sources were solids or liquids and the type of nutrient sources applied;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (f) the calculated nutrient application rate;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (g) the rate at which nutrients were actually applied;

heading: General requirements for applications to land
paragraph: (h) the results of testing conducted under section 53 [requirement to test soil].

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph:
52
		  (1) A person who applies nutrient sources to a crop but not to land must ensure all of the following:

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (a) that nutrient sources and leachate produced by nutrient sources do not escape during transportation or piping;

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (b) that, in the case of nutrient sources applied to crops in containers,

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (i)  nutrient sources are not discharged or applied directly into a watercourse, across a property boundary or below the water table, and

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (ii)  contaminated runoff, leachate, solids or drift from sprayed nutrient sources does not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (c) that the total amount of available nitrogen from all nutrient sources applied in one year of application is equal to or less than the amount of nitrogen needed for optimum crop growth and yield.

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (2) A person who applies nutrient sources to a crop but not to land must make and keep records of all of the following in respect of each crop to which nutrient sources are applied:

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (a) the crop nutrient requirements;

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (b) the calculated nutrient application rate;

heading: General requirements for applications other than to land
paragraph: (c) whether the nutrient sources were solids or liquids and the type of nutrient sources applied.

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph:
53
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person who applies nutrient sources to land must have the soil in each field tested as follows:

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph: (a) if the result of a nitrate test for the field is 100 kg N/ha or more, a nitrate test must be conducted again for that field the following year;

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph: (b) if paragraph (a) does not apply, a nitrate test must be conducted at least once every 3 years;

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph: (c) a phosphorus test must be conducted at least once every 3 years.

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if the land to which nutrient sources are being applied

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph: (a) is part of an agricultural operation having an agricultural land base totalling less than 2 ha,

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph: (b) is used to grow crops that are intentionally flooded for harvest, or

heading: Requirement to test soil
paragraph: (c) is composed of organic soils commonly referred to as peat or muck soils.

heading: Nitrate test
paragraph:
54
		  A nitrate test must be conducted in accordance with one of the following:

heading: Nitrate test
paragraph: (a) a post-harvest nitrate test that measures the amount of nitrate-nitrogen left in soil and not used by the most recently harvested crop must be conducted

heading: Nitrate test
paragraph: (i)  using a representative sample, and

heading: Nitrate test
paragraph: (ii)  after the last harvest of the growing season but before the autumn rains typically begin;

heading: Nitrate test
paragraph: (b) a test equivalent to a post-harvest nitrate test that will produce results representative of the amount of nitrate-nitrogen left in soil and not used by the most recently harvested crop.

heading: Phosphorus test
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A phosphorus test must

heading: Phosphorus test
paragraph: (a) measure the amount of available phosphorus in soil, and

heading: Phosphorus test
paragraph: (b) be conducted using a representative sample.

heading: Phosphorus test
paragraph: (2) If phosphorus test results are obtained using a method other than that commonly referred to as the "Kelowna method", the results must be converted to a value that is equivalent to the results that would have been obtained if the Kelowna method had been used.

heading: When nutrient management plan is required
paragraph:
56
		  Subject to section 58 [exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans], a person who applies nutrient sources to a field that is part of an agricultural operation having an agricultural land base totalling 5 ha or more must have a nutrient management plan if either of the following circumstances apply:

heading: When nutrient management plan is required
paragraph: (a) the field is located in a vulnerable aquifer recharge area and the result of a nitrate test for the field is 100 kg N/ha or more;

heading: When nutrient management plan is required
paragraph: (b) the field is located in a phosphorus-affected area and the result of a phosphorus test for the field is 200 ppm or more.

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph:
57
		  (1) A nutrient management plan must be prepared

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (a) by a qualified professional who has successfully completed a course in nutrient management planning, offered in British Columbia and approved by a director, if a result referred to in section 53 (1) is

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (i)  150 kg N/ha or more, for a nitrate test, or

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (ii)  300 ppm or more, for a phosphorus test, and

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (b) by an experienced person, in any other case.

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (1.1) Despite subsection (1) (b), if an agricultural operation spans multiple fields and a nutrient management plan must be prepared by a qualified professional for any one of the fields, the qualified professional must prepare the plan for the whole of the agricultural operation.

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (2) A person who prepares a nutrient management plan must

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (a) consider all nutrient sources available to the crop, including nutrients in the soil and nutrients applied to and removed from a field, and

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (b) design the plan to achieve the following objectives:

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (i)  to minimize the risk of nitrogen and phosphorus loss from a field to the environment;

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (ii)  to achieve an agronomic nitrogen balance of 0 for a field;

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (iii)  if the result of a phosphorus test for a field is 200 ppm or more, to achieve an annual phosphorus application rate that is less than the total crop  P removal plus up to a maximum of 90  kg P2O5 (phosphate)/ha per year so that soil phosphorus levels in a field are reduced over time until the result of a phosphorus test for the field is less than 200  ppm.

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (2.1) For the purposes of subsection (2) (b) (iii), "crop P removal" means the total amount of phosphorus in that portion of a crop that is removed from a harvested area.

heading: Preparation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (3) A person who prepares a nutrient management plan must sign and date the completed plan.

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph:
58
		  (1) A person may apply to a director, in the form and manner required by the director, for

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (a) an exemption from the requirement to have a nutrient management plan, or

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (b) a modification of a requirement of section 57 [preparation of nutrient management plan].

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (2) The director may grant an exemption or a modification if satisfied that the exemption or modification

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (a) is necessary because

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (i)  soil test results under section 53 [requirements to test soil] are unusually high due to a meteorological or other natural event, or

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (ii)  the person cannot comply with the requirement because no qualified professional, as described in section 57 (1) (a), or experienced person, as applicable, is reasonably available to the person, and

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (b) will not jeopardize the achievement of the purposes of this code, as stated under section 2 (1) [agricultural operations to which this code applies].

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (3) The director may grant an exemption or a modification

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (a) with or without conditions, and

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (b) for a period of up to one year.

heading: Exemptions or modifications to nutrient management plans
paragraph: (4) A person who is granted an exemption or modification under this section must comply with all conditions, if any, imposed under subsection (3) (a).

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph:
59
		  (1) A person who must have a nutrient management plan must do all of the following:

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (a) if the plan is prepared by a qualified professional, notify a director, in the form and manner required by the director, that a plan has been made or revised;

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (b) implement the plan;

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (c) keep a copy of the plan, the information on which it is based, including information from records made under section 51 (2) [general requirements for applications to land], and of any changes made to the plan, and make and keep records to demonstrate compliance with the plan.

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (2) A person who must have a nutrient management plan prepared must do the following:

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (a) review the plan at least once each year;

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (b) if no significant change has been made to the person's agricultural operation within the year, make any necessary changes identified by the review.

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (3) On making any significant change to the person's agricultural operations, a person who must have a nutrient management plan prepared must have a qualified professional or experienced person, as applicable under and in compliance with section 57 [preparation of nutrient management plan],

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (a) review the plan and make any necessary changes identified by the review, and

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (b) sign and date the plan on completing the review and any changes.

heading: Implementation of nutrient management plan
paragraph: (4) A nutrient management plan expires 5 years after the later of the dates referred to in section 57 (3) and subsection 3 (b) of this section.

heading: Director's powers respecting application of nutrient sources
paragraph:
60
		  (1) Despite any other provision of this Division, a director may do one or more of the following if the director has reason to believe that the application of nutrient sources is or may be having an adverse impact on the environment or human health:

heading: Director's powers respecting application of nutrient sources
paragraph: (a) prohibit the application of nutrient sources in one or more areas

heading: Director's powers respecting application of nutrient sources
paragraph: (i)  during a specified period, and

heading: Director's powers respecting application of nutrient sources
paragraph: (ii)  until soil testing, water quality monitoring or other testing indicates that the prohibition is not needed to protect the environment or human health;

heading: Director's powers respecting application of nutrient sources
paragraph: (b) require a person to have a qualified professional, as described in section 57 (1) (a), or an experienced person prepare or change a nutrient management plan.

heading: Director's powers respecting application of nutrient sources
paragraph: (2) A person must not contravene a prohibition made under subsection (1) (a).

heading: Director's powers respecting application of nutrient sources
paragraph: (3) A person who is subject to a requirement under subsection (1) (b) must comply with the requirement.

heading: Application
paragraph:
61
		  This Division applies to a person who keeps livestock or poultry for the purposes of an agricultural operation.

heading: Confined livestock or poultry areas
paragraph:
62
		  A person responsible for a confined livestock area or confined poultry area must ensure all of the following:

heading: Confined livestock or poultry areas
paragraph: (a) that livestock and poultry do not have direct access to a drinking water source or watercourse;

heading: Confined livestock or poultry areas
paragraph: (b) that contaminated runoff, leachate, solids and air contaminants do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: Confined livestock or poultry areas
paragraph: (c) that the accumulation of manure, animal bedding and feed within the area is managed so as to prevent contaminated runoff, leachate and solids from escaping;

heading: Confined livestock or poultry areas
paragraph: (d) that if contaminated runoff, leachate or solids escape from the area, they are

heading: Confined livestock or poultry areas
paragraph: (i)  collected and contained, and

heading: Confined livestock or poultry areas
paragraph: (ii)  not discharged directly to land or water.

heading: Feedlots
paragraph:
63
		  (1) A person responsible for a feedlot must ensure both of the following:

heading: Feedlots
paragraph: (a) that the self-sealing layer that forms under the feedlot is maintained so as to prevent leachate from entering groundwater;

heading: Feedlots
paragraph: (b) that runoff is diverted away from the feedlot.

heading: Feedlots
paragraph: (2) A person responsible for a feedlot that will no longer be used must decommission the feedlot by removing the manure pack that accumulated over the self-sealing layer and cleaning out the pens in a manner that

heading: Feedlots
paragraph: (a) prevents leachate from entering groundwater or a watercourse, and

heading: Feedlots
paragraph: (b) allows nutrients from the manure to be stored and applied to land in accordance with this code.

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph:
64
		  (1) A person responsible for a grazing area, seasonal feeding area or temporary holding area in which livestock or poultry have direct access to a watercourse must ensure that effective controls are in place to minimize

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (a) trampling and erosion of soil into the watercourse, and

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (b) contaminated runoff, leachate and solids entering the watercourse.

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (2) A person responsible for a grazing area must move livestock

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (a) from areas that are flooded or where flooding is imminent, and

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (b) during the flood season from areas that are prone to annual seasonal flooding.

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (3) A person responsible for a seasonal feeding area must ensure that, while livestock are present, on-ground feeding locations and mobile feeding bins are

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (a) not located

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (i)  in areas that are flooded or where flooding is imminent, or

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (ii)  during the flood season in areas that are prone to annual seasonal flooding, and

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (b) distributed evenly over the seasonal feeding area, in a manner that prevents the accumulation of manure near feeding locations or bins.

heading: Seasonal feeding, grazing and temporary holding areas
paragraph: (4) A person responsible for a temporary holding area must ensure that livestock or poultry are not held in the temporary holding area for a period of more than 72 hours.

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph:
65
		  A person who keeps 5 or more animal units must make and keep records of all of the following:

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (a) the total number of animals;

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (b) the total amount of manure, including bedding mixed with the manure, collected annually, expressed in m3, and divided according to the type of animal the manure is from and whether the manure is liquid or solid;

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (c) the amount of manure, expressed in m3, managed by

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (i)  distribution in accordance with section 43 [distribution of manure or agricultural compost], or

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (ii)  application as fertilizer or a soil conditioner in accordance with Division 4 [Nutrient Application and Management] of Part 6.

heading: Application
paragraph:
66
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), this Division applies to a person who does any of the following for the purposes of an agricultural operation:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) stores, transports or disposes of mortalities or processing waste, other than transporting mortalities and processing waste to a facility or place regulated under another enactment for the purpose of disposal;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) applies wastewater, within the meaning of the Code of Practice for the Slaughter and Poultry Processing Industries, to land.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) This Division does not apply to a person who disposes of multiple mortalities totalling 5 tonnes or more that died during a single event of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) fire, flood or other disaster, or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) disease outbreak.

heading: Allowable disposal
paragraph:
67
		  (1) Subject to the limits set out in this section, a person may dispose of mortalities or processing waste on the person's agricultural land base by adding the mortalities or processing waste to an agricultural composting process or by burial or incineration.

heading: Allowable disposal
paragraph: (2) A person may dispose only of mortalities that died on the person's agricultural land base.

heading: Allowable disposal
paragraph: (3) A person may dispose only of processing waste that comes from livestock or poultry that were reared, kept or slaughtered on the person's agricultural land base.

heading: Allowable disposal
paragraph: (4) A person must not dispose, in a year, of processing waste that comes from the slaughter of 5 tonnes or more of livestock or 1.5 tonnes or more of poultry, determined on a live weight basis.

heading: General requirements
paragraph:
68
		  A person who carries out an activity to which this Division applies must ensure all of the following:

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (a) that mortalities are not disposed of into, and are prevented from entering, a watercourse;

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (b) that, if a mortality enters a watercourse, the owner of the mortality removes that mortality immediately;

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (c) that processing waste does not enter a watercourse;

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (d) that contaminated runoff, leachate, solids and air contaminants from the activity do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (e) that odours and particulate matter from the activity are minimized;

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (f) that the activity will be carried out in a manner that will deter the attraction of, and access by, domestic pets, wildlife and vectors.

heading: Storage
paragraph:
69
		  (1) A person who stores mortalities must ensure that the mortalities are stored in a manner that prevents

heading: Storage
paragraph: (a) putrefaction, and

heading: Storage
paragraph: (b) leachate from escaping.

heading: Storage
paragraph: (2) A person may store processing waste and leachate on an agricultural land base only in a structure

heading: Storage
paragraph: (a) that is completely enclosed, and

heading: Storage
paragraph: (b) from which the processing waste and leachate cannot escape.

heading: Transport
paragraph:
70
		  A person may transport mortalities and processing waste from an agricultural land base only in containers from which the mortalities and processing waste, and leachate from them, cannot escape.

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph:
71
		  (1) A person who disposes of mortalities or processing waste by adding the mortalities or processing waste to an agricultural composting process must ensure all of the following:

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (a) that composting occurs only in a composting structure or in an outdoor agricultural composting pile;

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (b) that contaminated runoff, leachate and solids from the compost do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table;

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (c) that air contaminants from the compost do not cross a property boundary;

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (d) that composting will be carried out in a manner that will deter the attraction of, and access by, domestic pets, wildlife and vectors.

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (2) A person must not dispose of more than 5 tonnes of mortalities or processing waste by adding the mortalities or processing waste to an agricultural composting process in any 30-day period unless the person

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (a) notifies a director immediately on becoming aware that disposal is necessary and before disposal occurs, and

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (b) complies with the requirements, if any, imposed by the director.

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (3) A person who disposes of mortalities or processing waste by adding the mortalities or processing waste to an agricultural composting process must keep a record of all of the following:

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (a) the type and source of the mortalities or processing waste being composted;

heading: Agricultural composting processes
paragraph: (b) whether any of the mortalities or processing waste being composted contains specified risk material within the meaning of the Code of Practice for the Slaughter and Poultry Processing Industries.

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph:
72
		  (1) A person who uses an outdoor agricultural composting pile to dispose of mortalities or processing waste through agricultural composting processes must ensure all of the following:

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (a) that the pile is not located

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (i)  in any area in which there is standing water or water-saturated soil, or

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (ii)  on any low-lying area of a field prone to annual seasonal flooding;

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (b) that the pile does not remain for a period of more than 15 months;

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (c) that no other pile is erected in the same location for at least 3 years.

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (2) A person who uses an outdoor agricultural composting pile to dispose of mortalities or processing waste through an agricultural composting process must do all of the following:

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (a) monitor the pile at least once each week to ensure compliance with this code;

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (b) keep a record of

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (i)  the location of the pile,

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (ii)  the date the pile was formed, and

heading: Outdoor agricultural composting piles
paragraph: (iii)  the results of weekly monitoring under paragraph (a).

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph:
73
		  (1) In this section, the following terms have the same meaning as in the Code of Practice for the Slaughter and Poultry Processing Industries:

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (a) specified risk material;

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (b) wastewater.

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (2) A person who applies wastewater to land must ensure that the wastewater

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (a) contains no solid waste or visible tissue,

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (b) is applied only on the agricultural land base on which the wastewater was generated, and

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (c) is not applied to land used to grow crops for human consumption or to graze domestic ruminants, if the wastewater contains specified risk material.

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (3) A person who applies wastewater to land must comply with Division 4 [Nutrient Application and Management] of Part 6 as if the person were applying nutrient sources to the land.

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (4) A person who applies the product of an agricultural composting process to land must ensure all of the following:

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (a) that, if the product contains specified risk material, the product is not applied to land used to grow crops for human consumption or to graze domestic ruminants;

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (b) that composted mortalities and processing waste are applied to land only when fully composted;

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (c) that composted mortalities and processing waste from livestock are applied to land only on, and are not removed from, the agricultural land base on which the composting occurred;

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (d) that composted mortalities and processing waste from poultry are

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (i)  applied to land only on, and are not removed from, the agricultural land base on which the composting occurred, or

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (ii)  removed from the agricultural land base on which the composting occurred only if the composted mortalities and processing waste

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (A) are first mixed with poultry manure, and

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (B) form no more than 10% of the total volume of the mixture.

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (5) A person who applies wastewater or the product of an agricultural composting process to land must keep a record of all of the following:

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (a) the location of the fields to which the wastewater or product was applied;

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (b) the date of the application;

heading: Land applications of wastewater and agricultural compost
paragraph: (c) whether any of the applied wastewater or products contain specified risk material and, if so, the location of the fields to which that wastewater or those products have been applied.

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph:
74
		  (1) A person who buries mortalities, solid waste or semi-solid waste must ensure all of the following:

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (a) that no more than 2.5 tonnes are buried in a single burial pit;

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (b) that burial pits are not located

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (i)  closer than 60 m apart, unless each pit has been unused for at least 10 years,

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (ii)  in or over soil that has a saturated hydraulic conductivity of more than 10-3 cm/s, commonly referred to as coarse-textured soil,

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (iii)  in, or in the vicinity of, unstable soils that might cause the buried materials to escape the burial pit,

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (iv)  in any area in which there is standing water or water-saturated soil,

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (v)  in any low-lying area of a field prone to annual seasonal flooding, or

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (vi)  in a field within a 200-year flood plain;

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (c) that there is a vertical distance of at least 1.5 m from the bottom of the pit to either the bedrock or the seasonal high water table;

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (d) that buried materials are covered immediately after burial with at least 0.6 m of soil.

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (2) A person who closes a burial pit must ensure that the pit is covered with at least 1 m of soil that is compacted and mounded in a manner that will

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (a) minimize the percolation of precipitation into the pit,

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (b) divert runoff away from the pit, and

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (c) deter the attraction of, and access by, domestic pets, wildlife and vectors.

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (3) A person who buries mortalities, solid waste or semi-solid waste must make and keep records of all of the following in respect of each burial pit:

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (a) the location of the pit;

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (b) the type and amount, expressed in tonnes, of materials buried;

heading: Disposal by burial
paragraph: (c) the date the pit is closed, if applicable.

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph:
75
		  (1) A person who incinerates mortalities, solid waste or semi-solid waste must ensure that the incinerator is

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (a) designed and manufactured specifically for the incineration of mortalities, and

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (b) designed such that emissions of particulate matter from the incinerator, determined under standard conditions of an O2 reference level of 11%, at 25°C and 101.3 kPa, do not exceed the following limits:

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (i)  for an existing incinerator, 180 mg/m3;

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (ii)  for a new incinerator that has a chamber capacity of

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (A) less than 181 kg, 175 mg/m3, or

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (B) 181 kg or more, 155 mg/m3.

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (2) A person who incinerates mortalities, solid waste or semi-solid waste must

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (a) visually assess the opacity of emissions from the incinerator at least once

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (i)  every 12 hours, and

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (ii)  during each burn cycle, and

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (b) immediately take corrective action to reduce the opacity level to or below the following limit, as applicable, if the assessment indicates that the opacity level exceeds that limit:

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (i)  20%, for

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (A) an existing incinerator, or

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (B) a new incinerator that has a chamber capacity of less than 181 kg;

heading: Disposal by incineration
paragraph: (ii)  10%, for a new incinerator that has a chamber capacity of 181 kg or more, assessed after the incinerator has reached its operating temperature.

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph:
76
		  A person who uses an incinerator must make and keep records respecting all of the following:

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (a) the type and quantity of mortalities, solid waste and semi-solid waste incinerated and the date of each incineration;

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (b) all inspections and maintenance of the incinerator;

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (c) the results of all opacity assessments conducted under section 75 (2) [disposal by incineration];

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (d) if opacity limits under section 75 (2) are exceeded,

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (i)  the date on which the limit was exceeded,

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (ii)  the level of opacity, and

heading: Record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (iii)  the corrective action taken.

heading: Agricultural products
paragraph:
77
		  A person who manages, stores or uses agricultural products for the purposes of an agricultural operation must ensure that contaminated runoff, leachate and solids from the agricultural products do not enter a watercourse, cross a property boundary or go below the water table.

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph:
78
		  (1) This section applies to a person who, as part of an agricultural operation, collects and stores contaminated runoff, leachate or wastewater and treats the stored materials to remove pathogens, suspended solids, nutrients, metals and chemicals.

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (2) A person to whom this section applies and who uses an existing treatment system

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (a) may discharge the treated product to land or water,

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (b) must notify a director before February 28, 2021, that this section applies to the person, and

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (c) must provide to the director any information the director requires respecting the treatment system.

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (3) A person to whom this section applies and who uses a modified or new treatment system may discharge the treated product to land or water if the person does all of the following:

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (a) notifies a director at least 60 days before modifying or installing the treatment system by providing to the director

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (i)  the designs and plans for the treatment system, as prepared by a qualified professional,

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (ii)  the projected quality and rate of flow of the treated product, and

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (iii)  any further information required by the director;

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (b) makes any changes to the designs and plans required by the director;

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (c) receives approval from the director for modification or construction of the treatment system to begin;

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (d) modifies or constructs the treatment system according to the designs and plans approved by the director;

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (e) provides the director with drawings of the treatment system, as modified or constructed, within 30 days of completing the modification or construction;

heading: Treatment of contaminated runoff, leachate and wastewater
paragraph: (f) complies with the requirements and limits, if any, imposed by the director.

heading: General record-keeping requirements
paragraph:
79
		  A person who must make or keep records under this code must

heading: General record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (a) keep the records for at least 5 years, and

heading: General record-keeping requirements
paragraph: (b) submit the records to a director or an officer within 5 business days of being required by the director or officer.

heading: General powers of director
paragraph:
80
		  (1) This section applies if a director has reason to believe that

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (a) a person has not complied with this code, or

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (b) taking an action referred to in this section is necessary to ensure that the purposes of this code, as stated under section 2 (1) [agricultural operations to which this code applies], are being met.

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (2) In the circumstances set out in subsection (1) and without limiting the powers of a director under any other provision of this code, a director may do one or more of the following:

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (a) require a person to make or keep specified records or to provide specified information, in the form and manner required by the director;

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (b) require a person to keep the records referred to in paragraph (a) for the period specified by the director, and produce the records to the director within the time required by the director;

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (c) require assessments, tests, analysis or monitoring in respect of any activity carried out or structure or equipment used for the purposes of an agricultural operation;

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (d) require a qualified professional to conduct assessments, tests, analysis or monitoring for the purposes of paragraph (c), and to prepare a report;

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (e) specify the methodology to be used to conduct assessments, tests, analysis or monitoring for the purposes of paragraphs (c) and (d);

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (f) require a person to take corrective action if a provision of this code is contravened;

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (g) require a person who is complying with this code but whose agricultural operations are, or are likely, causing or contributing beyond a minimal extent to pollution, to take one or more actions to reduce or mitigate the effects of that pollution.

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty and without limiting section 7 of the Waste Discharge Regulation, a director may impose a requirement under subsection (2) of this section that is in addition to a requirement under this code or in circumstances in which this code does not otherwise impose the requirement.

heading: General powers of director
paragraph: (4) A person who is subject to a requirement under subsection (2) must comply with the requirement.

heading: Exercise of director's powers
paragraph:
81
		  If a director exercises a power under this code, the director must do so in writing and give reasons for exercising the power.

heading: Accessibility of maps
paragraph:
82
		  Each director must

heading: Accessibility of maps
paragraph: (a) ensure that copies of the maps referred to in the Schedules are available

heading: Accessibility of maps
paragraph: (i)  on a website that is maintained by or on behalf of the ministry of the minister and is publicly and freely accessible, and

heading: Accessibility of maps
paragraph: (ii)  in the office of the administrator, and

heading: Accessibility of maps
paragraph: (b) allow members of the public to access the maps during the director's regular business hours and without charge.
