heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: 1		  In this code:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "200 year floodplain" means land where the chance of a flood occurring in any given year is at least one in 200;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "Act" means the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "aquifer" has the same meaning as in the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "background concentration" means the concentration of a substance in an environmental medium in a geographic area, but does not include any contribution from local human-made point sources;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "cell" means a compartment within a landfill;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "conceptual closure plan" means a plan that meets the requirements of section 3 (2);

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "design plan" means a plan that meets the requirements of section 19 (2);

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "disease vector" means a carrier organism that is capable of transmitting a pathogen from one facility, waste source, product or organism to another facility, waste source, product or organism;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "dredgings" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) wood residue, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) sand, gravel and rock,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: gathered by dredging in water below the high water mark;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "electronic waste" means any waste from electronic products that are no longer in use, including television sets, computers, computer monitors and cell phones;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "final closure plan" means a plan that meets the requirements of section 15 (2), (4) and (5);

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "final closure report" means a report referred to in section 16;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "generic numerical water standard" has the same meaning as in the Contaminated Sites Regulation, B.C. Reg. 375/96;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "groundwater" has the same meaning as in the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "hazardous waste" has the same meaning as in the Hazardous Waste Regulation, B.C. Reg. 63/88;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "inert cover material" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) soil, gravel or rock, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) any material that

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (i)  if discharged to a landfill, cannot reasonably be expected to undergo a physical, chemical or biological change that will result in an adverse effect on the environment or human health, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (ii)  is approved by a director for discharge to a landfill;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "inert waste" means any of the following materials that have been used by a wood processing industry:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) cured concrete that has been used for structural or construction purposes and that consists of a mixture of Portland cement, sand and gravel with or without embedded wood or steel reinforcements;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) asphaltic material, except asphaltic roofing material and road grindings, that has been used for structural or construction purposes and that consists of a mixture of petroleum asphalt, sand and gravel;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) brick and masonry that have been used for structural or construction purposes;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (d) ceramic material that has been produced from fired clay or porcelain;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (e) glass, except glass derived from electronic waste;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (f) stainless steel and aluminum;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (g) any other material that

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (i)  if discharged to a landfill, cannot reasonably be expected to undergo a physical, chemical or biological change resulting in an adverse effect on the environment or human health, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (ii)  is approved by a director for discharge to a landfill;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "landfill" means the part of a landfill facility where solid waste referred to in section 8 is discharged;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "landfill facility" means a facility described in section 2;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "large landfill facility" means a landfill facility

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the total capacity or designed total capacity of which is more than 5 000 cubic metres of waste, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) at which more than 500 cubic metres of solid waste is discharged per year or is specified in registration information provided under section 3 (1) (c);

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "local government" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the council of a municipality, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) the board of a regional district;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "natural control landfill" means a landfill that relies on climatic and geologic conditions to renovate leachate in the subsurface;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "office or shop refuse" means waste originating from the office or shop of a wood processing industry, but does not include any of the following:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) liquid waste;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) putrescible waste;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) electronic waste;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (d) a product regulated under the Recycling Regulation, B.C. Reg. 449/2004;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (e) hazardous waste;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "operational plan" means a plan that meets the requirements of section 20;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "qualified professional", in relation to a duty or function under this code, means an individual who

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) is registered in British Columbia with a professional organization, is acting under that organization's code of ethics and is subject to disciplinary action by that organization, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) through suitable education, experience, accreditation and knowledge, may reasonably be relied on to provide advice within the individual's area of expertise, which area of expertise is applicable to the duty or function;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "slope failure" means a measurable downward or outward movement of soil, rocks, snow, ice, mud or debris caused by gravity acting on an unstable slope;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "surface water" means a natural watercourse, whether usually containing water or not, and includes

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a lake, river, creek, spring, ravine, stream, swamp, gulch and brook, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) marine water;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "unauthorized fire" means a fire or burning that is not authorized by or under an enactment;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "waste characterization report" means a report that meets the requirements of section 5 (3);

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "Waste Discharge Regulation" means the Waste Discharge Regulation, B.C. Reg. 320/2004;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "wood processing industry" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a wood processing industry-primary, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) a wood processing industry-secondary,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: as defined in Schedule 2 to the Waste Discharge Regulation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "wood waste" means wood residue, other than dredgings, that

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) originates from a wood processing industry, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) has not been treated with glue, paint or preservative,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: and includes bark, branches, broken logs, hog fuel, mill ends, wood chips, shavings and saw dust.

heading: Application of code
paragraph: 2		  This code applies to a person who conducts a wood processing industry and who operates, or proposes to operate, a landfill facility solely for the disposal of waste incidental to the wood processing operations of

heading: Application of code
paragraph: (a) that person, or

heading: Application of code
paragraph: (b) that person and one or more other persons, all of whom conduct a wood processing industry.

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph:
3
		  (1) A person must register under section 4 of the Waste Discharge Regulation for the purposes of an exemption under that section in relation to this code and must provide, with the other information required under section 4 (2) of that regulation, the following information:

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (a) the source and composition of the solid waste discharged or proposed to be discharged to the landfill;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (b) the total capacity or designed total capacity of the landfill;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (c) the maximum volume of solid waste, in cubic metres per year, discharged or to be discharged to the landfill;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (d) the address of the location where the landfill facility records referred to in section 18 will be kept;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (e) subject to subsection (3), confirmation that the appropriate local government has been notified of the landfill facility at least 30 days before the date on which the registration is provided to a director under section 4 (3) of the Waste Discharge Regulation;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (f) confirmation that a conceptual closure plan that complies with subsection (2) has been prepared for the landfill facility.

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (2) The conceptual closure plan must

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (a) specify the final design elevations of the landfill,

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (b) specify the maximum volume and area of the landfill at the time of closure,

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (c) include the design of the final slope of the landfill and identify

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (i)  the vegetation cover, and

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (ii)  the inert cover material proposed for the landfill,

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (d) identify the measures to be taken to prevent, or minimize the risk of, any of the following occurring after the closure of the landfill facility:

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (i)  an escape of leachate or waste from the landfill;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (ii)  erosion of the landfill cover;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (iii)  fire at the landfill facility;

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (iv)  water running onto the landfill facility,

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (e) identify maximum periods following the final discharge of waste before the implementation of the plan is initiated, and

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (f) include a site plan.

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (3) Confirmation is not required under subsection (1) (e) if

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (a) the registration relates to a landfill facility for which a permit has been issued before the date on which this section came into force, and

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (b) the permit remains in force until the registration becomes effective.

heading: Registration requirements for all landfill facilities
paragraph: (4) In this section, "appropriate local government" means the local government for the area within which the landfill facility will be located.

heading: Security requirements for landfill facilities - authorization to director
paragraph:
4
		  A director is authorized to require an owner or operator of a landfill facility to give security in the amount and form and subject to the conditions the director may specify.

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph:
5
		  (1) In addition to the information required under section 3, if the registration under section 4 of the Waste Discharge Regulation relates to a large landfill facility, confirmation must be provided that a waste characterization report, a design plan and an operational plan have been prepared for the landfill facility.

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (2) Confirmation is not required under subsection (1) if

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (a) the registration relates to a large landfill facility for which a permit has been issued before the date on which this section came into force, and

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (b) the permit remains in force until the registration becomes effective.

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (3) The waste characterization report for a large landfill facility must be prepared by a qualified professional and must

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (a) identify the types of solid waste to be discharged to the landfill,

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (b) specify the estimated volume of each type of waste that will be discharged annually,

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (c) specify the physical properties and the chemical properties of each type of waste,

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (d) indicate whether there is any possibility of landfill gas being generated at the landfill facility,

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (e) include an analysis of total concentrations and leachable concentrations of substances referred to in paragraph (g) in representative waste samples,

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (f) identify opportunities for the reduction, reuse or recycling of the types of solid wastes identified under paragraph (a), and

heading: Additional requirements for large landfill facilities
paragraph: (g) identify, based on the information provided under paragraphs (a) to (c), any substances in each type of waste that may adversely affect the environment or human health.

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph:
6
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: "seasonally high water table" means the highest level of rise of the free surface of water below the ground surface at any time during the year;

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: "water supply well" means a class of well for extracting and using groundwater, but does not include a drainage well, dewatering well or remediation well.

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (2) At registration, a landfill

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (a) must be located

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (i)  within a property so that there are at least 100 m between the property line and the boundary of the landfill,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (ii)  so that there are at least 1.2 m between the seasonally high water table beneath the landfill and each of the bottommost cells of the landfill, and

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (iii)  so that there are at least 2 m of low permeability soil with a hydraulic conductivity of 1 x 10-6 cm/s or less below each of the bottommost cells of the landfill,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (b) must not be located within

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (i)  100 m of any land that is subject to slope failure,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (ii)  5 vertical metres of high tide line,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (iii)  100 m of any surface water,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (iv)  300 m of a water supply well, or

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (v)  100 m of an existing residence,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (c) must not be located within 300 m of the boundaries of

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (i)  a national, Provincial, regional or municipal park,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (ii)  a conservancy as defined in the Park Act,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (iii)  a wildlife management area designated under section 4 of the Wildlife Act,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (iv)  a critical wildlife area or wildlife sanctuary designated under section 5 of the Wildlife Act,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (v)  any land acquired and administered under the Wildlife Act,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (vi)  an ecological reserve designated under the Ecological Reserve Act,

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (vii)  a bird sanctuary designated under the regulations pursuant to the Migratory Birds Convention Act (Canada), or

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (viii)  a wildlife area designated under the Canada Wildlife Act (Canada).

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (3) At registration, a natural control landfill must not be located on land above an aquifer that is classified as a level IA or IIA aquifer by an aquifer classification system approved by a director.

heading: Siting requirements for all landfills
paragraph: (4) The operator of a landfill must not increase the area of the landfill if the increase would contravene subsection (2) (b) or (c) or (3).

heading: Additional siting requirements for large landfills
paragraph: 7		  (1) In addition to meeting the requirements of section 6, at registration, a large landfill must not be located

heading: Additional siting requirements for large landfills
paragraph: (a) in a 200 year floodplain, or

heading: Additional siting requirements for large landfills
paragraph: (b) within 1 000 m of a holocene fault as defined in the Hazardous Waste Regulation.

heading: Additional siting requirements for large landfills
paragraph: (2) The operator of a landfill must not increase the area of the large landfill if the increase would contravene subsection (1).

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph:
8
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), only the following solid wastes may be discharged to a landfill:

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (a) wood waste;

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (b) dredgings;

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (c) sand, gravel and rocks;

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (d) ash produced by burning of wood waste, except ash from wood that has been immersed in marine waters;

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (e) inert waste;

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (f) inert cover materials;

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (g) other solid wastes approved by a director.

heading: Types of solid waste that may be discharged
paragraph: (2) In addition, office or shop refuse may be discharged to a landfill, but only if the total volume of that refuse in the landfill does not exceed 1% of the total capacity or designed total capacity, in cubic metres, of the landfill.

heading: Separation of certain materials
paragraph:
9
		  The following materials must be separated from other solid wastes and discharged at a location identified under section 17 (2) (b) in the annual report:

heading: Separation of certain materials
paragraph: (a) stainless steel and aluminum;

heading: Separation of certain materials
paragraph: (b) material described in paragraph (g) of the definition of "inert waste" in section 1 if a director specifies that this section applies to that material.

heading: Containment of discharged waste
paragraph:
10
		  Waste discharged to a landfill must be contained within a cell of the landfill.

heading: Compaction and intermediate cover requirements
paragraph:
11
		  Waste discharged to a landfill must be compacted and covered with an inert cover material to a depth and at a frequency necessary to control the following:

heading: Compaction and intermediate cover requirements
paragraph: (a) dust;

heading: Compaction and intermediate cover requirements
paragraph: (b) litter;

heading: Compaction and intermediate cover requirements
paragraph: (c) disease vectors;

heading: Compaction and intermediate cover requirements
paragraph: (d) fires;

heading: Compaction and intermediate cover requirements
paragraph: (e) objectionable odours.

heading: Maintenance of works
paragraph:
12
		  All works relating to a landfill facility must be maintained in good working order.

heading: Unauthorized fires
paragraph:
13
		  An unauthorized fire in or adjacent to discharged waste at a landfill facility must be extinguished immediately on detection.

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph:
14
		  (1) If the occurrence of an emergency or condition prevents the operator of a landfill facility from complying with this code, the operator must

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (a) take remedial action that is appropriate in the circumstances,

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (b) as soon as practicable but within 2 business days after becoming aware of the occurrence, notify a director, in the form and manner specified by the director, of the occurrence and the remedial action taken under paragraph (a), and

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (c) take any further remedial action specified by the director.

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (2) In this section "emergency" includes, but is not limited to,

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (a) an unauthorized fire at a landfill facility,

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (b) an unplanned escape of leachate or another substance from a landfill,

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (c) any subsidence or other sign of instability of a landfill, and

heading: Emergency procedures
paragraph: (d) any other occurrence at a landfill facility that poses a risk to the environment or human health.

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph:
15
		  (1) The operator of a landfill facility must, at least 3 months before the intended closure of a landfill facility,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (a) notify a director in writing of the closure, and

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (b) make available to the director a copy of the final closure plan for the landfill facility.

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (2) The final closure plan must be prepared by a qualified professional.

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (3) Before the final closure plan is prepared, the operator of a landfill facility must ensure that a qualified professional

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (a) reviews the conceptual closure plan for the landfill facility, and

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (b) if necessary, amends the conceptual closure plan to reflect any changes in the information provided in it arising, after the preparation or amendment of the conceptual closure plan, from the operation of the landfill facility or from site specific conditions.

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (4) The final closure plan for a landfill facility

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (a) must

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (i)  specify the final design elevation of the landfill,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (ii)  specify the area of the landfill,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (iii)  identify the measures to be taken to prevent, or minimize the risk of,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (A) leachate or waste escaping from the landfill,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (B) erosion of the landfill cover,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (C) fire occurring in the closed landfill or its cover, or

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (D) water running onto the closed landfill, and

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (iv)  identify maximum periods following the final discharge of waste before the implementation of the closure plan is initiated, and

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (b) include the following information relating to the landfill facility:

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (i)  a description of the final cover of the landfill;

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (ii)  an estimate of the total volume of solid waste discharged to the landfill;

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (iii)  a survey of the location of the landfill, prepared by a land surveyor admitted as a land surveyor under the Land Surveyors Act;

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (iv)  a description of how the operator of the landfill facility has managed

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (A) drainage restoration,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (B) soil replacement,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (C) the slope of the final cover,

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (D) erosion control, and

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (E) re-vegetation and conditioning of the site;

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (v)  a description of how the operator of the landfill facility will monitor the site of the landfill facility.

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), the final closure plan may not be implemented until it is approved by the director.

heading: Final closure plan
paragraph: (6) The final closure plan may be implemented after the date that is 45 days after the date the operator of a landfill facility makes available to the director a copy of the final closure plan under subsection (1) (b), unless the director notifies the operator that the director does not approve the plan.

heading: Final closure report
paragraph: 16		  The operator of a landfill facility must

heading: Final closure report
paragraph: (a) comply with the final closure plan, and

heading: Final closure report
paragraph: (b) within 3 months after the closure,

heading: Final closure report
paragraph: (i)  conduct the closure in accordance with the final closure plan, and

heading: Final closure report
paragraph: (ii)  ensure that a final closure report is prepared

heading: Final closure report
paragraph: and notify the director in writing that there has been compliance with both subparagraphs (i) and (ii).

heading: Annual report
paragraph:
17
		  (1) The operator of a landfill facility must ensure that an annual report is prepared in accordance with this section for each calendar year during any part of which the facility is in operation, beginning with the calendar year in which the registration under the Waste Discharge Regulation became effective in relation to the facility.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (2) An annual report must include the following information:

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) the types and volumes of waste discharged to the landfill during the calendar year;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) the location where any material to which section 9 applies has been discharged during that year;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (c) any other information requested by a director.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (3) If the annual report relates to a large landfill facility, the report must, in addition to the information required under subsection (2), include the following data and information:

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) data relating to the monitoring of groundwater and surface water;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) data relating to the monitoring of landfill gas;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (c) data relating to the monitoring of any leachate from the landfill;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (d) interpretation of the data included under this subsection;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (e) information about any remedial action taken by the operator of the landfill facility in response to the data referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c).

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (4) An annual report must be available for inspection under section 18 (3) (b) by April 1 of the year following the calendar year to which the report relates.

heading: Records
paragraph:
18
		  (1) The operator of a landfill facility must keep at the address provided under section 3 (1) (d) of this code or, if the address is changed, provided under section 4 (5) (b) (i) of the Waste Discharge Regulation, the following records:

heading: Records
paragraph: (a) a record containing the registration number under the Waste Discharge Regulation for the facility;

heading: Records
paragraph: (b) the conceptual closure plan, including any amendments;

heading: Records
paragraph: (c) the final closure plan and the final closure report for the landfill facility;

heading: Records
paragraph: (d) each annual report prepared under section 17.

heading: Records
paragraph: (2) In addition to the records referred to in subsection (1), the operator of a large landfill facility must keep at the address referred to in that section the following records relating to the facility:

heading: Records
paragraph: (a) the waste characterization report;

heading: Records
paragraph: (b) the design plan, if applicable;

heading: Records
paragraph: (c) the operational plan, if applicable;

heading: Records
paragraph: (d) each record made under section 22 (4).

heading: Records
paragraph: (3) The operator of a landfill facility must

heading: Records
paragraph: (a) ensure that the records kept under this section are retained for 10 years after the final closure of that facility,

heading: Records
paragraph: (b) subject to section 17 (4), make the records kept under this section available for inspection by a director or an officer, and

heading: Records
paragraph: (c) provide to a director or an officer, within 7 business days of being requested by the director or officer to do so, a copy of any records kept under this section.

heading: Design plan
paragraph:
19
		  (1) A large landfill facility must be located and constructed in accordance with the design plan for that facility.

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (2) The design plan must be prepared by a qualified professional and must include the following information:

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (a) an assessment of the climatic, geological and hydrogeological conditions at the landfill facility;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (b) an assessment of site specific conditions, including proximity to any sensitive area that may be adversely affected by the landfill;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (c) identification of siting and design measures necessary to minimize, limit, counteract or mitigate the effect of the landfill or landfill facility on the environment or human health, including its effect on any sensitive area or activity;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (d) identification of the design elements necessary to ensure that the requirements of this code are met;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (e) plans and specifications for the construction of the landfill facility that reflect the design measures referred to in paragraph (c) and the design elements referred to in paragraph (d).

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of subsection (2) (b) and (c), "sensitive area" means any of the following:

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (a) a ground or surface water source;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (b) a sensitive watershed;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (c) an archaeological site;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (d) a seismic area;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (e) a floodplain;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (f) a residential property;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (g) a school;

heading: Design plan
paragraph: (h) any other feature, area or activity that may be specified by the qualified professional who prepares the design plan.

heading: Operational plan
paragraph:
20
		  (1) A large landfill facility must be operated in accordance with the operational plan for the landfill facility.

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (2) An operational plan must be prepared by a qualified professional and must include a description of the procedures for

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (a) covering waste with inert cover material,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (b) monitoring groundwater,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (c) monitoring and managing surface water,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (d) monitoring and managing leachate,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (e) controlling dust, litter and disease vectors at the large landfill facility,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (f) controlling access to the large landfill by wildlife,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (g) accepting and diverting waste,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (h) responding to emergencies,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (i) monitoring and managing landfill gas, including by means of intercepting, venting, recovering or flaring,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (j) detecting and preventing the discharge of hazardous waste and other prohibited wastes, and

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (k) doing anything else the qualified professional who prepares the plan considers necessary to meet the requirements of this code.

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (3) The procedures for monitoring groundwater under subsection (2) (b) must

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (a) provide for

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (i)  an assessment of the risk to groundwater quality from the large landfill facility,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (ii)  the detection of changes in groundwater quality caused by the large landfill facility, and

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (iii)  sampling to measure seasonal variability,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (b) specify the number and location of monitoring locations for the monitoring network necessary to monitor groundwater quality, based on

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (i)  the volume and characteristics of the waste to be discharged to the large landfill,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (ii)  the location and capacity of the large landfill,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (iii)  the use of groundwater that can reasonably be expected to be made,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (iv)  the hydrogeology of the area where the large landfill is located, and

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (v)  the direction, the horizontal and vertical gradient and the velocity of the groundwater flow, and

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (c) based on the substances that are identified in the waste characterization report in accordance with section 5 (3) (e), specify the water quality parameters to be measured and the sampling frequency.

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (4) The procedures for monitoring and managing surface water under subsection (2) (c) must

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (a) provide for

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (i)  an assessment of the risk to surface water quality from the large landfill facility, and

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (ii)  the detection of changes in surface water quality caused by the large landfill facility,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (b) specify the number and location of monitoring locations for the monitoring network necessary to monitor surface water quality, based on

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (i)  the volume and characteristics of the waste to be discharged to the large landfill,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (ii)  the type of surface water in the vicinity of the large landfill,

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (iii)  the location and capacity of the large landfill, and

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (iv)  adjacent land uses and surface water receptors, and

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (c) be based on the substances that are identified in the waste characterization report in accordance with section 5 (3) (e) and specify the water quality parameters to be measured and the sampling frequency.

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (5) In developing procedures for monitoring groundwater and surface water, if the large landfill is located on land above an aquifer, a qualified professional must consider aquifer classification as set out in an aquifer classification system approved by a director.

heading: Operational plan
paragraph: (6) A director may require the operator of a large landfill facility to undertake monitoring that is specified by the director and is additional to the monitoring required under the operational plan for that facility.

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A large landfill facility must be operated and maintained so that

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (a) surface water entering the landfill facility does not contact any discharged waste,

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (b) infiltration at the landfill of water from precipitation is minimized,

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (c) discharged waste does not cause pollution of groundwater or surface water,

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (d) the groundwater at the monitoring locations identified in the operational plan for the facility does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (i)  the generic numerical water standard for that substance and the applicable water use, or

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (ii)  the background concentration of that substance in the groundwater at the landfill facility if the background concentration exceeds the generic numerical water standard, and

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (e) the surface water at the monitoring locations identified in the operational plan for the facility does not contain a substance

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (i)  with a concentration greater than a concentration approved by a director for that substance and the applicable water use, or

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (ii)  with a background concentration greater than the background concentration approved by a director.

heading: Water quality protection
paragraph: (2) A director may specify other numerical water quality standards and objectives that the operator of a landfill facility must meet if a substance has a concentration greater than the local background concentration of that substance in the groundwater or surface water at the landfill facility.

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph:
22
		  (1) The operator of a large landfill facility must ensure that groundwater and surface water at the monitoring locations specified in its operational plan are sampled and analyzed in accordance with that plan and this section.

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (2) The sampling must be performed using procedures approved by a director.

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (3) The analysis must be performed using procedures approved by a director.

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (4) A record of the sampling and analysis must be made and it must include all of the following information:

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (a) the name of the person performing the sampling and analysis;

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (b) the name of the person making the record;

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (c) the date of the sampling and the analysis;

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (d) the date on which the record is made;

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (e) the procedures used in performing the sampling or analysis, as the case may be;

heading: Sampling and analysis of groundwater and surface water
paragraph: (f) the results of the analysis with reference to the objective described in section 21 (1) (d) (ii) or (e) (ii) or specified by a director under section 21 (2), as the case may be.

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: 1		  (1) For the purposes of section 107 (1) (a) (ii) of the Environmental Management Act, a member of the Conservation Officer Service may exercise the powers and perform the duties of the official listed in Column 1 of the Table under the enactment listed opposite in Column 2 of the Table.

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 107 (1) (b) of the Environmental Management Act, the following enactments are prescribed as enactments that a member of the Conservation Officer Service may enforce:

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (a.1) Dike Maintenance Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (a.2) Ecological Reserve Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (a.3) Environmental Management Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (a.5) Fish and Seafood Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (a.6) Forest Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (b) Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (c) Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (c.1) Greenhouse Gas Industrial Reporting and Control Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (c.2) Integrated Pest Management Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (d) Land Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (e) sections 44 (6), 73 (1), 74 (1) and 76 (2) of the Liquor Control and Licensing Act;

heading: Powers and duties of members of the Conservation Officer Service

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agricultural land use" means the use of land for the primary purpose of producing agricultural products for human or animal consumption including, without limitation, livestock raising operations, croplands, orchards, pastures, greenhouses, plant nurseries and farms;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic life water use" means the use of water as habitat for any component of the freshwater or marine aquatic ecosystem, including phytoplankton, zooplankton, benthos, macrophytes and fish;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "background concentration"  means the naturally occurring concentration of a substance in an environmental medium at a geographic area, as determined in accordance with the director's protocols;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cancer risk" means the probability of the occurrence of cancer from exposure to a carcinogenic substance;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "carcinogenic substance" means any chemical classified as carcinogenic in accordance with a director's protocol;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commercial land use" means the use of land for the primary purpose of buying, selling or trading of merchandise or services including, without limitation, shopping malls, office complexes, restaurants, hotels, motels, grocery stores, automobile service stations, petroleum distribution operations, dry cleaning operations, municipal yards, warehouses, law courts, museums, churches, golf courses, government offices, air and sea terminals, bus and railway stations, and storage associated with these uses;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "confirmation of remediation report" means a report under section 49 (2) (b);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "director's interim standards" means the substances and risk based or numerical criteria, standards and conditions prescribed by the director under section 63.1 of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "director's protocol" means a protocol established by a director under section 64 of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "drinking water use" means the use of water for the purpose of consumption by humans;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environmental management area" means a site designated by the director under section 14;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environmental media" means soil, sediments, surface water, groundwater, air, vapour, animals and plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environmental risk assessment report" means a report under section 18 (6) or 18.1 (5);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "external contract reviewer" means a person with whom a director has entered into a contract under section 10 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "generic numerical sediment standard" means the concentration of a substance specified in Schedule 3.4 for a particular sediment use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "generic numerical soil standard" means the concentration of a substance in soil specified for a particular land use in Part 2 or 3 of Schedule 3.1;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "generic numerical vapour standard" means the concentration in vapour of a substance specified for a particular land use, or other use, in Schedule 3.3;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "generic numerical water standard" means the concentration of a substance in water specified for a particular water use in Schedule 3.2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "guidelines" includes criteria and objectives;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hazard index" means the sum of hazard quotients for any substance over all exposure pathways;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hazard quotient" or "HQ" means the quotient determined from the equation

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "high density residential land use" means, subject to section 1.2, a residential land use in respect of one of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a multiple-unit dwelling of 3 or more storeys;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an institutional facility in a building of 3 or more storeys;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "industrial land use" means the use of land for the primary purpose of conducting industrial manufacturing and assembling processes and their ancillary uses including, without limitation, factories, metal foundries, wood treatment facilities, mines, refineries, hydroelectric dams, metal smelters, automotive assembly plants, rail car or locomotive maintenance facilities, railyards, non-retail breweries and bakeries, roads and highways, wastewater and sewage treatment plants, electrical transformer stations and salvage yards;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "irrigation water use" means the use of water for the purpose of producing hay, forage crops, pasture, cereal crops, vegetables and fruit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "livestock water use" means the use of water for the purpose of consumption by livestock;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "low density residential land use" means, subject to section 1.2, a residential land use in respect of one of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a single residence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a multiple-unit dwelling of less than 3 storeys;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) an institutional facility in a building of less than 3 storeys;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "matrix numerical soil standard" means the concentration of a substance in soil specified for a particular land use and a particular site-specific factor in Part 1 of Schedule 3.1;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "medical health officer", in relation to a contaminated site, means a medical health officer within the meaning of the Public Health Act who has jurisdiction within the geographic area in which the contaminated site is located;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "natural wildlands land use" means a wildlands land use in respect of a protected area, except in respect of a portion of the protected area where there is, or previously has been, an agricultural, commercial, industrial, urban park or residential land use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "numerical standards" means generic numerical soil standards, generic numerical vapour standards, generic numerical water standards, matrix numerical soil standards, generic numerical sediment standards, director's interim standards and site-specific numerical standards;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ownership interest", when used in Part 2, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a fee simple interest,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a lease or similar form of tenure respecting real property having a term, including any option to renew, equal to or exceeding 30 years, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a licence of occupation under section 39 of the Land Act having a term, including any option to renew, equal to or exceeding 30 years,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include an interest in the nature of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a mortgage,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a right of way,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) a tenure under the Forest Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) a lien,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) a judgment,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) an interest in real property which deals exclusively with subsurface rights including a tenure under the Geothermal Resources Act, the Mineral Tenure Act or the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (j) an option to purchase,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (k) an equitable charge,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (l) a restrictive covenant,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (m) a covenant under section 219 of the Land Title Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (n) a right to purchase an ownership interest;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "parkade" means an enclosed building, storey of a building or other construction used for the parking of multiple motor vehicles, but does not include the parking of motor vehicles associated with a single residence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protected area" means an area of land set out in Column 1 of Schedule 2.1 that is established, named, designated or otherwise prescribed under the Act listed opposite in Column 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "provincial health officer" means the provincial health officer appointed under the Public Health Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "remediation plan" means a written document which may include, but is not necessarily limited to, plans and other information respecting

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) overall site location and delineated horizontal and vertical locations of contamination presented in maps, cross-sections and other graphic representations,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) remediation alternatives which were considered for managing contamination from or at a site, and evaluation methods used to assess the factors under section 56 of the Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) remediation methods selected to ensure compliance with the numerical standards, or the risk based standards prescribed in this regulation, and the conditions imposed by a director under section 53 of the Act or in a remediation order,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) identification and classification in accordance with the numerical standards of the substances in any soil, surface water, groundwater, sediment or vapour to remain in place,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d.1) identification and classification in accordance with the numerical standards of the substances in any soil or sediment to be relocated,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) risk assessment calculations and methodology to demonstrate compliance with risk-based remediation standards if remediation is assessed relative to the risk-based remediation standards,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) a schedule with estimated dates for implementing remediation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) identification and discussion of the effects of known regulatory requirements on remediation, including any authorizations which will be required to implement remediation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) proposed confirmatory sampling, analysis, testing or monitoring during and after treatment, management or removal of contamination,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) proposed measures and controls to ensure security, including covenants under section 219 of the Land Title Act, restrictive covenants and financial security in accordance with section 48 of this regulation, for ongoing management of any contamination if it will be managed at the site, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (j) any public consultation or review of remediation which has occurred or which is proposed during remediation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "residential land use" means the use of land for the primary purpose of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a residence by persons on a permanent, temporary or seasonal basis, including, without limitation, single family dwellings, cabins, apartments, condominiums or townhouses, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) institutional facilities, including, without limitation, schools, hospitals, daycare operations, prisons, correctional centres and community centres;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "reverted wildlands land use" means a wildlands land use other than a natural wildlands land use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "right of way" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an easement,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a statutory right of way, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a limited interest in the land or a licence or a permit that grants the right to construct, operate or maintain works of a lineal nature on, over or under land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "risk assessment" means the systematic process of identifying and evaluating substances, persons potentially affected, and exposures to the substances in order to estimate cancer risks or hazard indices in accordance with a director's protocol;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "risk management" means actions, including monitoring, designed to prevent or mitigate risks to human health or the environment caused by contamination at a site;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "screening level risk assessment" means a screening level risk assessment and report described in a director's protocol;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sediment" means particulate material that usually lies below water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sensitive sediment use" means the use as habitat for sensitive components of freshwater, marine or estuarine aquatic ecosystems of a site containing sediment, which sensitive components include, but are not limited to,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) phytoplankton, zooplankton, benthos, macrophytes and fish,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) habitats used by endangered or threatened species or species of special concern under the Species at Risk Act (Canada),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) watercourses, wetlands, forested riparian areas, mudflats and intertidal zones that are important to the preservation of fish or wildlife,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) reaches of aquatic habitats that are important to fish spawning or serve as important rearing habitat for fish,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) reaches of aquatic environments that encompass or border habitat compensation or restoration sites or other areas that are intended or designed to create, restore or enhance biological or habitat features, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) areas and aquatic habitat included in wild life management areas designated under the Wildlife Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "site-specific numerical standard" means the concentration of a substance in soil, water, sediment or vapour

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) determined for a particular land, water, sediment or vapour use at a specific site by applying the applicable director's protocol, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) approved by the director;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "soil" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) unconsolidated mineral or organic material,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) rock,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) fill, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) sediment deposited on land,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include the following, which are applied to land for a beneficial purpose in compliance with the Organic Matter Recycling Regulation or an authorization given under the Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) sewage sludge;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) composted organic materials;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) products derived from the materials described in paragraph (e) or (f);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "typical sediment use" means the use of a site containing sediment for a use that is not a sensitive sediment use;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "urban park land use" means the use of urban land for the primary purpose of outdoor recreation including, without limitation, municipal parks, fairgrounds, sports fields, rifle ranges, captive wildlife parks, biking and hiking areas, community beaches and picnic areas;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "vapour" means gaseous emissions from soil, sediment or water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wide area remediation plan" means a remediation plan for an environmental management area for one or more specific substances which have originated from one or more sources specified in the plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlands land use" means the use of land for a primary purpose other than an agricultural, commercial, industrial, urban park or residential land use.

heading: Interpretation - specified industrial or commercial uses
paragraph: 1.1		  For the purposes of the definition of "specified industrial or commercial use" in section 39 (1) of the Act, the purposes and activities set out in Schedule 2 of this regulation are prescribed as industrial and commercial purposes or activities.

heading: Interpretation - high and low density residential land uses
paragraph:
1.2
		  For the purposes of the definitions of "high density land use" and "low density land use" in section 1, a land use that would otherwise be a high density residential land use is to be considered to be a low density residential use if the land is also used

heading: Interpretation - high and low density residential land uses
paragraph: (a) to grow plants for human consumption, or

heading: Interpretation - high and low density residential land uses
paragraph: (b) as a playground, sports field, picnic area or other use that involves frequent contact with the soil by children.

heading: Interpretation - decommissioning a site
paragraph:
2.1
		  For the purposes of section 40 (2) (a) (i) of the Act and this Part, an owner or operator decommissions a site if the owner or operator does any of the following in a manner designed to stop all specified industrial or commercial uses of the site:

heading: Interpretation - decommissioning a site
paragraph: (a) removes or treats soil;

heading: Interpretation - decommissioning a site
paragraph: (b) removes, destroys or treats buildings or process equipment, including storage tanks.

heading: Interpretation - ceasing operations at a site
paragraph:
2.2
		  For the purposes of section 40 (2) (a) (ii) of the Act and this Part, an owner or operator ceases operations on land if

heading: Interpretation - ceasing operations at a site
paragraph: (a) the owner or operator ceases using the land for a specified industrial or commercial use, and

heading: Interpretation - ceasing operations at a site
paragraph: (b) the land is not used for any specified industrial or commercial uses for 12 months after the date on which the specified industrial or commercial use referred to in paragraph (a) ceases.

heading: Site disclosure statements by persons applying to approving officers or municipalities
paragraph:
3
		  A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement at the time of presenting, in writing, an application or request for approval described in that section.

heading: Site disclosure statements by municipalities undertaking zoning or rezoning
paragraph:
3.1
		  A municipality that, under section 40 (1) (b) (i) of the Act, is undertaking to zone or rezone land in which it has an ownership interest must provide a site disclosure statement to the registrar within 15 days after giving first reading to the applicable zoning bylaw.

heading: Site disclosure statements by owners or operators of land
paragraph:
3.2
		  (1) A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (a) of the Act in relation to land must provide the site disclosure statement to the registrar within 6 months after the owner or operator

heading: Site disclosure statements by owners or operators of land
paragraph: (a) decommissions a site on the land, or

heading: Site disclosure statements by owners or operators of land
paragraph: (b) ceases operations on the land.

heading: Site disclosure statements by owners or operators of land
paragraph: (2) A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (b) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement within 90 days after filing for protection under, or otherwise becoming subject to, the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act (Canada).

heading: Site disclosure statements by owners or operators of land
paragraph: (3) A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (c) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement within 90 days after filing a proposal, or a notice of intention to make a proposal, under Part III of the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada).

heading: Site disclosure statements by vendors of real property
paragraph: 3.3		  A vendor of real property who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (6) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement as follows:

heading: Site disclosure statements by vendors of real property
paragraph: (a) unless paragraph (b) applies, at least 30 days before the actual transfer of the real property;

heading: Site disclosure statements by vendors of real property
paragraph: (b) if the time between the written agreement for the transfer of the real property and the actual transfer is less than 30 days, before the written agreement is entered into.

heading: Site disclosure statements by persons who take possession or control of real property
paragraph:
3.4
		  A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (7) of the Act must provide the site disclosure statement to the registrar within 10 days after the person takes possession or control of real property referred to in that provision.

heading: Request for information by municipality or approving officer
paragraph:
3.5
		  Nothing in this Part restricts the authority of a municipality or approving officer to request a person applying for or otherwise seeking approval of a matter referred to in section 40 (1) of the Act to provide the information required by a site disclosure statement even though the person is not required under the Act to provide a site disclosure statement.

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph:
4
		  (1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) or (2) of the Act in relation to a site if

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (a) the site is the subject of an approval in principle or certificate of compliance relevant to

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (i)  the current use of the site, or

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (ii)  any use of the site proposed by the person, and

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (b) the person, after making reasonable inquiries, has no reason to believe that any further contamination occurred at the site after the approval in principle or certificate was issued.

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) or (2) of the Act in relation to a site if

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (a) the site is located within an environmental management area for which a director has approved

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (i)  a wide area remediation plan, or

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (ii)  the scope of a proposed wide area remediation plan, and

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (b) the site disclosure statement would be provided only as a result of uses or activities that caused contamination that is dealt with in the approved plan or scope.

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (3) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) or (2) of the Act in relation to a site if

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (a) a determination was made under section 44 of the Act that the site is not a contaminated site, and

heading: Exemption - other processes apply under the Act
paragraph: (b) the person, after making reasonable inquiries, has no reason to believe that any contamination occurred at the site after the determination was made.

heading: Exemption - persons applying to approving officers
paragraph:
4.1
		  (1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement to an approving officer under section 40 (1) (a) of the Act if either of the following applies:

heading: Exemption - persons applying to approving officers
paragraph: (a) the person is an applicant for subdivision under section 114 of the Land Title Act;

heading: Exemption - persons applying to approving officers
paragraph: (b) the proposed subdivision consists only of

heading: Exemption - persons applying to approving officers
paragraph: (i)  an adjustment to the boundary of a parcel, or

heading: Exemption - persons applying to approving officers
paragraph: (ii)  a consolidation of 2 or more parcels into a single parcel.

heading: Exemption - persons applying to approving officers
paragraph: (2) If, in relation to a development on land, a person applies for or otherwise seeks from an approving officer more than one approval for subdivision at the same time, the person may comply with the requirement under section 40 (1) (a) of the Act by providing a single site disclosure statement relating to the land for the purposes of all those approvals.

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: 4.2		  (1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement to a municipality under section 40 (1) (b) (i) of the Act if

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (a) the land in relation to which the person is seeking approval for zoning is being used for a specified industrial or commercial use, and

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (b) the specified industrial or commercial use would continue to be authorized on the land if the zoning were approved.

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (1.1) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement to a municipality under section 40 (1) (b) (ii) of the Act if the land is the site of a waste management facility that is

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (a) operated under a permit or operational certificate, and

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (b) actively accepting or processing waste.

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement to a municipality under section 40 (1) (b) (ii) of the Act if the development permit or building permit in relation to which the person is seeking approval is for only one or more of the following purposes:

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (a) demolition;

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (b) installing or replacing underground utilities;

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (c) installing or replacing fencing or signage;

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (c.1) installing or replacing posts for decks;

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (c.2) installing footings, pads or other concrete structures at or near the surface of the ground;

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (d) paving;

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (e) landscaping.

heading: Exemption - persons applying to municipalities
paragraph: (3) If, in relation to a development on land, a person applies for or otherwise seeks from a municipality more than one approval for zoning or permits at the same time, the person may comply with the requirement under section 40 (1) (b) of the Act by providing a single site disclosure statement relating to the land for the purposes of all those approvals.

heading: Exemption - municipalities undertaking zoning or rezoning
paragraph:
4.3
		  A municipality undertaking to zone or rezone land is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) (b) (i) of the Act if either of the following applies:

heading: Exemption - municipalities undertaking zoning or rezoning
paragraph: (a) the municipality does not have an ownership interest in the land;

heading: Exemption - municipalities undertaking zoning or rezoning
paragraph: (b) the municipality does not intend to develop any parcels of land in which it has an ownership interest that are located within the area being zoned or rezoned.

heading: Exemption - more than one owner or operator required to provide site disclosure statement when ceasing operations on land
paragraph:
4.4
		  A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (a) of the Act in relation to land if

heading: Exemption - more than one owner or operator required to provide site disclosure statement when ceasing operations on land
paragraph: (a) one or more other persons are also required to provide a site disclosure statement under that section as a result of a site being decommissioned on the land or operations ceasing on the land, as applicable, and

heading: Exemption - more than one owner or operator required to provide site disclosure statement when ceasing operations on land
paragraph: (b) the site disclosure statement is provided by one of those other persons.

heading: Exemption - operating areas under the Oil and Gas Activities Act
paragraph:
4.5
		  A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (b) and (c) of the Act in relation to land if the land is an operating area within the meaning of the Oil and Gas Activities Act.

heading: Exemption - vendors of real property
paragraph: 4.6		  A vendor of real property is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (6) of the Act if any of the following apply:

heading: Exemption - vendors of real property
paragraph: (a) the vendor does not have an ownership interest in the real property;

heading: Exemption - vendors of real property
paragraph: (b) the prospective purchaser waives, in writing, the entitlement to be provided with the site disclosure statement;

heading: Exemption - vendors of real property
paragraph: (c) at the time of the contract for purchase and sale, the real property

heading: Exemption - vendors of real property
paragraph: (i)  is used primarily for a residential purpose, or

heading: Exemption - vendors of real property
paragraph: (ii)  has never been zoned for any use other than primarily for residential purposes.

heading: Exemption - previous submission of site profile
paragraph:
4.7
		  (1) In this section, "site profile" means a site profile under section 40 of the Act as that section read immediately before February 1, 2021.

heading: Exemption - previous submission of site profile
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) of the Act in relation to land if all of the following criteria are met:

heading: Exemption - previous submission of site profile
paragraph: (a) a site profile that relates to the land was provided to a municipality or approving officer before February 1, 2021;

heading: Exemption - previous submission of site profile
paragraph: (b) the municipality or approving officer, after assessing the site profile, forwarded the site profile to the registrar instead of the director in accordance with section 6 (1) (c) (ii) of this regulation, as it read immediately before February 1, 2021;

heading: Exemption - previous submission of site profile
paragraph: (c) the land has not been used for a specified industrial or commercial use after the date on which the site profile was provided to the municipality or approving officer.

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph:
5
		  (1) The requirement of a person to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 of the Act is not satisfied until the following occurs:

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (a) in the case of a site disclosure statement required to be provided under section 40 (1) of the Act, the municipality or approving officer assesses, in accordance with section 40 (4) (a) of the Act and section 6 of this regulation, that the site disclosure statement form is satisfactorily complete;

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (b) in any other case, the person provides all the information required by the site disclosure statement form.

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (2) A site disclosure statement must be completed using the form set out in Schedule 1.

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (3) Only the following persons may complete a site disclosure statement:

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (a) an owner of the land to which the site disclosure statement relates;

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (b) an operator of a site on the land to which the site disclosure statement relates;

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (c) a person authorized by

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (i)  an owner referred to in paragraph (a), or

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (ii)  an operator referred to in paragraph (b).

heading: Requirements for completing site disclosure statement
paragraph: (4) Only a person referred to in subsection (3) (a) or (b) may sign the declaration on a site disclosure statement.

heading: Assessing and forwarding site disclosure statements
paragraph:
6
		  (1) For the purposes of section 40 (4) (a) of the Act, a municipality or approving officer must do the following within 15 days of receiving a site disclosure statement:

heading: Assessing and forwarding site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) assess whether the site disclosure statement is satisfactorily completed in accordance with the instructions provided by a director;

heading: Assessing and forwarding site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) if the municipality or approving officer assesses that the site disclosure statement is satisfactorily complete, forward the site disclosure statement to the registrar;

heading: Assessing and forwarding site disclosure statements
paragraph: (c) notify the person who provided the site disclosure statement of the following, as applicable:
