heading: Assessing and forwarding site disclosure statements
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of assessing a site disclosure statement under section 40 (4) (a) of the Act, a municipality or approving officer is not required to conduct a search of the records or archives maintained by the municipality or approving officer.

heading: Assessing and forwarding site disclosure statements
paragraph: (3) A municipality or approving officer that receives or assesses a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) or (4) of the Act is not required to do either of the following for the purposes of that section or this regulation:

paragraph:

		  (1) In this section, "notice" means a notice referred to in

heading: Investigations and reports required on submission of site disclosure statements to municipalities or approving officers
paragraph: (a) section 34.1 (2) (b) (iii) or (iv) of the Islands Trust Act,

heading: Investigations and reports required on submission of site disclosure statements to municipalities or approving officers

heading: Investigations and reports required on submission of site disclosure statements to municipalities or approving officers

heading: Investigations and reports required on submission of site disclosure statements to municipalities or approving officers
paragraph: (2) A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1) of the Act must do the following before the person seeks from a director a notice that relates to the land that is the subject of the site disclosure statement:

heading: Investigations and reports required on submission of site disclosure statements to municipalities or approving officers

paragraph: 6.3		  (1) A person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2) (a) or (7) of the Act must undertake the following investigations of the land that is the subject of the site disclosure statement:

heading: Investigations required on submission of site disclosure statements under section 40 (2) (a) or (7) of the Act
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in either of the following circumstances:

paragraph:
7.1
		  (1) A person applying for, requesting or seeking approval, consideration, review or a determination of any of the following in relation to a site must provide a summary of site condition, together with a recommendation by an approved professional in respect of the matter, to the director:

		  (1) Subject to this section, a person who undertakes an action described in Column 1 of Table 1 of Schedule 3 must pay the fee set out opposite the action in Column 2.

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph:
11
		  (1) Subject to section 12 and subsections (2), (3) and (4) of this section, the following substances, standards and conditions are prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "contaminated site" in section 39 of the Act:

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (a) the land use of the site is a land use specified in section 12 (3) (a) to (f) and the concentration of any substance in the soil is greater than

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (i)  the applicable generic numerical soil standard, or

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (ii)  the lowest value of the applicable matrix numerical soil standards;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (b) the surface or groundwater located on or flowing from the site is used or has a reasonable probability of being used for aquatic life, irrigation, livestock or drinking water and the concentration of any substance in the surface water or groundwater is greater than the applicable generic numerical water standard;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (b.1) the concentration of any of the following substances, as defined in Schedule 3.2, in surface water or groundwater at the site is greater than the applicable generic numerical water standard:

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (ii)  nonaqueous phase liquids;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (iii)  VHw6-10;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (c) the concentration of any substance in sediment at the site is greater than the applicable generic numerical sediment standard;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (c.1) the concentration of any substance in vapour at the site is greater than the applicable generic numerical vapour standard;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (c.2) despite paragraph (a), for land less than 15 metres from a natural gas or petroleum well head and the land use of the site is agricultural land use,

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (i)  the concentration of any substance in the soil at a depth of less than 2 metres is greater than the applicable agricultural land use standards for soil, or

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (ii)  the concentration of any substance in the soil at a depth of 2 metres or more is greater than the standards for soil that would apply if the land use of the site were commercial land use;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (c.3) despite paragraph (a), for Crown land less than 15 metres from a natural gas or petroleum well head and the land use of the site is wildlands land use,

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (i)  the concentration of any substance in the soil at a depth of less than 2 metres is greater than the standards for soil that would apply if the land use of the site were reverted wildlands land use, or

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (ii)  the concentration of any substance in the soil at a depth of 2 metres or more is greater than the standards for soil that would apply if the land use of the site were commercial land use;

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (d) the concentration of any substance at the site, not specified in Schedule 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 or 3.4, is greater than,

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (i)  if the substance is specified without a particular use, the concentration specified for that substance in a director's interim standard, and

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (ii)  if the substance is specified with a particular use, the concentration specified for that substance and use in a director's interim standard.

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a site in relation to a substance if the concentration of the substance in soil, surface water, groundwater, sediment or vapour at the site is not greater than the applicable site-specific numerical standard.

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to a site in relation to a substance in the soil, surface water, groundwater, sediment or vapour if the concentration of the substance in the soil, surface water, groundwater, sediment or vapour is not greater than the local background concentration of that substance in the soil, surface water, groundwater, sediment or vapour respectively.

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (4) Subsection (1) does not apply to a site in relation to a substance in the soil if

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (a) the site has been used for the application of

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (i)  managed organic matter, as defined in the Organic Matter Recycling Regulation, B.C. Reg. 18/2002,

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (ii)  retail-grade organic matter, as defined in the Organic Matter Recycling Regulation, or

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (iii)  products derived from the materials described in subparagraphs (i) or  (ii)

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: in a manner consistent with the Organic Matter Recycling Regulation or an authorization given under the Act, and

heading: Definition of contaminated site
paragraph: (b) the site has not been used for a specified industrial or commercial use.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph:
12
		  (1) For the purpose of using the standards in this regulation,

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) if a protocol provides for more than one land use at a particular site, the land uses that apply, at any given time, to the site or a part of the site are the land uses that apply in accordance with the protocol, and

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) otherwise, the land use that applies, at any given time, to a particular site or a part of a site is the primary land use at the surface of the site.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of using the standards in this regulation, the surface water uses or groundwater uses which apply, at any given time, to a particular site or part of a site are based on

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) the uses of the surface water or groundwater at the site or on neighbouring sites, and

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) the potential for the groundwater or surface water to cause pollution.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (2.1) For the purpose of using the standards in this regulation, the sediment use that applies, at any given time, to a particular site or a part of a site is based on

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) the use of sediment at the site or at neighbouring sites, and

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) the potential for the sediment to cause pollution.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (2.2) For the purpose of using the standards in this regulation, the vapour use that applies, at any given time, to a particular site or a part of a site is based on

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) the uses of the land at the surface of the site, and

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) the potential of the vapour to cause pollution.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (2.3) A director may specify the applicable land use under subsection (2.2) from the following:

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) a land use specified in subsection (3) (a) to (f);

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) if a parkade is located at the site, parkade use.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (6), a director may specify the applicable land use or uses, as the case may be, under subsection (1) from the following:

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) wildlands land use or, if applicable, one of the following:

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (i)  natural wildlands land use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (ii)  reverted wildlands land use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) agricultural land use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (c) urban park land use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (d) residential land use or, if applicable, one of the following:

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (i)  low density residential land use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (ii)  high density residential land use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (e) commercial land use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (f) industrial land use.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (4) A director may specify the applicable water uses under subsection (2) from the following:

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) aquatic life water use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) irrigation water use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (c) livestock water use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (d) drinking water use.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (4.1) A director may specify the applicable sediment use under subsection (2.1) from the following:

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) typical sediment use;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) sensitive sediment use.

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (5) In specifying the primary land use, water use or sediment use under subsections (3), (4) and (4.1), a director must take into account current and reasonable potential future land, water and sediment uses based on the following factors:

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (a) current and proposed zoning for the site;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (b) land use and planning policies of the government or the municipality or municipalities in which the site and neighbouring sites are situated;

heading: Specification of applicable land, water, sediment and vapour uses and site-specific factors
paragraph: (c) current site activities;

heading: Environmental management area
paragraph:
14
		  A director may designate a site as an environmental management area with respect to specified substances and specified sources if

heading: Environmental management area
paragraph: (a) the site covers an extensive geographic area and comprises many individual properties, and

heading: Environmental management area
paragraph: (b) many of the individual properties located within the bounds of the geographic area would, on an individual basis, likely be determined by the director to be contaminated with one or more of the specified substances in the designation.

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph:
15
		  (1) The numerical standards must be applied in determining whether a site is a contaminated site.

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (2) A director who makes a preliminary determination under section 44 (2) (a) of the Act must provide written reasons for the preliminary determination with the notice required by section 44 (2) (b) of the Act.

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (3) After making a preliminary determination under section 44 (2) (a) of the Act, the director must allow a period for comment under section 44 (2) (c) of the Act of not less than 30 days and not more than 60 days after delivery of the notice of preliminary determination.

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (4) Within 15 days after making a final determination under section 44 (2) (d) or (3) of the Act, the director must send the notice required by section 44 (2) (e) accompanied by written reasons for the final determination.

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (5) A director may require that an application for a determination under section 44 of the Act include a report and the recommendation of an approved professional in respect of whether the site is a contaminated site.

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (6) If the director does not impose a requirement under subsection (5), an application for a determination under section 44 of the Act may include a report and the recommendation of an approved professional in respect of whether the site is a contaminated site and, if so, section 49.1 applies.

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (7) If a director rejects the recommendation of an approved professional provided under subsection (5) or (6), the director, within 15 days of the rejection, must provide written reasons to

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (a) the applicant, and

heading: Procedures for determination of contaminated site
paragraph: (b) the professional association, in the Province, of which the approved professional is a member.

heading: Remediation options
paragraph:
16
		  The numerical standards, or the risk based standards prescribed in section 18 or 18.1, may be used in relation to the remediation of a contaminated site.

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph:
17
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a contaminated site has been remediated in accordance with the numerical standards if

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) the site is used for a land use specified in section 12 (3) (a) to (f) and the soil at the site does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than or equal to

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (i)  the applicable generic numerical soil standard, or

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  the lowest value of the applicable matrix numerical soil standards,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) surface water or groundwater used for, or which has a reasonable probability of being used for, aquatic life, irrigation, livestock or drinking water use does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than the generic numerical water standard for that substance and use,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (b.1) the sediment at the site does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than the generic numerical sediment standard for that substance for the applicable sediment use of the site,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (b.2) the vapour at the site does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than the generic numerical vapour standard for that substance for the applicable land use of the site,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (c) the soil, surface water, groundwater, sediment or vapour at the site does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than the concentration specified for that substance and use in a director's interim standard,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (d) despite paragraph (a), for land less than 15 metres from a natural gas or petroleum well head and the use of the site is agricultural land use,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (i)  the soil at a depth of less than 2 metres does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (A) the generic numerical soil standard, or

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (B) the lowest value of the applicable matrix numerical soil standard

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: that would apply if the land use of the site were agricultural land use, and

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  the soil at a depth of 2 metres or more does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (A) the generic numerical soil standard, or

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (B) the lowest value of the applicable matrix numerical soil standard

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: that would apply if the land use of the site were commercial land use, and

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (e) despite paragraph (a), for Crown land less than 15 metres from a natural gas or petroleum well head and the use of the site is wildlands land use,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (i)  the soil at a depth of less than 2 metres does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (A) the generic numerical soil standard, or

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (B) the lowest value of the applicable matrix numerical soil standard

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: that would apply if the land use of the site were reverted wildlands land use, and

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  the soil at a depth of 2 metres or more does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (A) the generic numerical soil standard, or

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (B) the lowest value of the applicable matrix numerical soil standard

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: that would apply if the land use of the site were commercial land use.

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (2) A contaminated site has been remediated in accordance with the numerical standards if

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) the soil, surface water, ground water, vapour or sediment at the site does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than or equal to the applicable site-specific numerical standard for the soil, surface water, groundwater, vapour or sediment, respectively, or

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) the soil, surface water, ground water, vapour or sediment at the site does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than the local background concentration of that substance in the soil, surface water, groundwater, vapour or sediment, respectively.

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), and regardless of the use of the land at the surface of this site, the soil beyond a depth of 3 metres below the surface of land at a contaminated site has been remediated in accordance with numerical standards prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "contaminated site" if it or the vapour in it does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than or equal to the concentration specified for that substance for industrial land use in

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) the generic numerical soil standard or the matrix numerical soil standard,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (a.1) the generic numerical vapour standard,

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) a director's interim standard for soil or vapour, or

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (c) the site-specific numerical standard for soil or vapour for that site.

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (4) A director may require the application of the standards for soil or vapour referred to in subsection (1) or (2) to a depth greater than 3 metres for any specific site if the nature of the contaminants, the land use or proposed land use, site-specific factors or other factors indicate such action is necessary.

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (4.1) Subsections (3) and (4) do not apply in relation to land to which subsection (1) (d) or (e) applies.

heading: Application of numerical standards for remediation
paragraph: (5) If surface water or groundwater is not currently being used at the contaminated site for any of the purposes specified in subsection (1) (b), a director may specify a numerical standard for the surface water or groundwater as necessary to protect the present and future surface water or groundwater uses on neighbouring sites or to prevent pollution.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph:
18
		  (1) The remediation standards have been met for a specific contaminated site if a responsible person satisfies a director that

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) for any non-threshold carcinogenic substance, the calculated human lifetime cancer risk due to exposure to that substance at the site is less than or equal to a risk value recommended by a medical health officer for the site, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) for any substance for which a hazard index is calculated, the hazard index due to exposure of a human to that substance at the site is less than a maximum hazard index recommended by a medical health officer for that site.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (2) A responsible person who asks a director for a decision that the standards in subsection (1) have been met for a contaminated site must

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) provide information to support and justify the basis for the request, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) participate in and pay for a public community based consultation process facilitated by a medical health officer which

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (i)  is for the purpose of developing a recommendation on the acceptable level of human health risk for the site,

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  will consider remediation options in relation to levels of resulting human health risk at the site,

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (iii)  will be conducted in conjunction with any requirement under section 52 of the Act and section 55 (1) of this regulation, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (iv)  is carried out over a time period not exceeding 3 months from the date of the request under subsection (1) unless the person making the request, a medical health officer and the director agree to an alternate time period.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), a director must consider a contaminated site to have been satisfactorily remediated without review and recommendation by a medical health officer if

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) for each non-threshold carcinogenic substance, the calculated human lifetime cancer risk due to exposure to that substance at the site is less than or equal to one in 100 000, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) for each substance for which a hazard index is calculated, the hazard index due to exposure of a human to that substance at the site is less than or equal to one.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (4) A director must not decide that the standards in subsection (1) have been met before receiving written recommendations with supporting rationale from a medical health officer respecting the matters described in subsection (1) (a) and (b).

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (5) If a person demonstrates to the satisfaction of a director that the local background concentration of any substance at a particular site results in the standards required by subsection (1) or (3) being exceeded, the remediation standards for that substance must be the calculated lifetime cancer risk and calculated hazard index which results from exposure of a human to the local background concentration of that substance at the site.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (6) A person who applies the risk-based standards of this section must also prepare an environmental risk assessment report which identifies

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) the potential onsite and offsite environmental risks of any substances causing contamination before and after remediation, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) procedures, including monitoring, designed to mitigate any significant potential risks identified in paragraph (a).

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (7) A director may impose requirements on a responsible person to prevent or mitigate risks identified

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (a) in the environmental risk assessment report required under subsection (6), or

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation
paragraph: (b) by the director using other available data.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph:
18.1
		  (1) The remediation standards have been met with respect to a substance from a source specified under section 14 if a director is satisfied that

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (a) the risk to human health due to exposure to that substance at the site is less than or equal to a maximum value recommended by a medical health officer for the environmental management area,

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (b) the maximum value recommended by a medical health officer under paragraph (a) takes a form other than that of a hazard index or cancer risk, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (c) the recommendation under paragraph (a) has been reviewed and endorsed by the provincial health officer.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (2) A responsible person who asks a director for a decision that the standards in subsection (1) have been met for a contaminated site must

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (a) provide information to support and justify the basis for the request, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (b) participate in and pay for a public community based consultation process, acceptable to and facilitated by a medical health officer, that

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (i)  is for the purpose of developing a recommendation on the acceptable level of human exposure and health risk for the site,

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (ii)  considers remediation options in relation to levels of human exposure and health risk at the site,

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (iii)  is conducted in conjunction with any requirement under section 52 of the Act and section 55 (1) of this regulation, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (iv)  is carried out over a time period not exceeding 6 months from the date of the request under subsection (1), unless the person making the request, a medical health officer and the director agree to an alternate time period.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (3) A director must not decide that the standards in subsection (1) have been met before receiving written recommendations with supporting rationale from a medical health officer respecting the matters described in subsection (1) (a) and a written review and endorsement of the recommendations from the provincial health officer under subsection (1) (c).

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (4) Despite subsections (1) and (2), the director must consider an environmental management area to have been satisfactorily remediated with respect to each substance from a source specified in section 14 without review and recommendation from a medical health officer if

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (a) for each non-threshold carcinogenic substance, the calculated human lifetime cancer risk due to exposure to that substance at the site is less than or equal to one in 100 000, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (b) for each substance for which a hazard index is calculated, the hazard index due to exposure of a human to that substance at the site is less than or equal to one.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (5) A person who applies the risk-based standards of this section with respect to specified substances must also prepare an environmental risk assessment report that identifies

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (a) the potential onsite and offsite environmental risks of each specified substance before and after the remediation, and

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (b) procedures, including monitoring, designed to mitigate any significant potential risks identified in paragraph (a).

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (5.1) If a person demonstrates to the satisfaction of a director that the local background concentration of any substance at a particular environmental management area results in the standards required by subsection (1) or (4) being exceeded, the remediation standards for that substance must be the calculated lifetime cancer risk and calculated hazard index that result from exposure of a human to the local background concentration of that substance at the environmental management area.

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (6) A director may impose requirements on a responsible person to prevent or mitigate risks identified

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (a) in the environmental risk assessment report required under subsection (5), or

heading: Application of risk-based standards for remediation at environmental management areas
paragraph: (b) by the director using other available data.

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters and arrangers
paragraph:
19
		  For the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, a person described in section 45 (1) (c) or (d) or (2) (c) or (d) of the Act is designated not responsible for remediation of a contaminated site in relation to a substance if the person

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters and arrangers
paragraph: (a) did not control the disposal, handling or treatment of the substance, or

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters and arrangers
paragraph: (b) by contract, agreement or otherwise merely required

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters and arrangers
paragraph: (i)  adoption of standards of design, construction or operation of works at the site which were intended to prevent contamination, or

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters and arrangers
paragraph: (ii)  compliance with environmental laws, standards, policies or codes of practice of government which applied at the time of producing, transporting or arranging for transport of the substance.

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph:
20
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a surety who issues a bid bond, performance bond or labour and materials payment bond for a contract with respect to construction activities at a site which

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (a) is a contaminated site at the effective date of issuance of the bond, or

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (b) became a contaminated site after the effective date of issuance of the bond

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: is designated for the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act not responsible for remediation of the contaminated site and is exempt from an order under section 83 (2) (f) of the Act in relation to the contaminated site, unless the surety exercised control over or imposed requirements on any person regarding the manner of treatment, disposal or handling of a substance and the control or requirements, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site.

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (2) A surety does not exercise control or impose requirements under subsection (1) if the surety acts under its rights or obligations with respect to the bond including, without limitation, any of the following:

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (a) participating only in purely financial matters related to construction activities at the site;

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (b) having the capacity or ability to influence any operation at the contaminated site in a way that would have the effect of causing or increasing contamination, but does not exercise that capacity or ability in such a way as to cause or increase contamination;

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (c) imposing requirements on any person if the requirements do not have a reasonable probability of causing or increasing contamination of the site;

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (d) appointing a person to inspect or investigate a contaminated site to determine future steps or actions that the surety might take;

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (e) imposing requirements on any person to comply with environmental laws, standards, policies or codes of practice of government or industry, including requirements to perform monitoring tests, scientific studies or to remediate contaminated sites.

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the liability of the surety is limited to the cost of remediation and the cost of completion of the bonded contract in accordance with the terms and conditions of the bond.

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (4) The liability of the surety under subsection (3) is limited to the penal sum of the bond.

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (5) The limitation under subsections (3) and (4) does not apply to a surety who intentionally caused environmental damage or was grossly negligent or guilty of wilful misconduct with respect to

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (a) the use of the environment, or

heading: Persons not responsible - sureties
paragraph: (b) the lives or safety of persons.

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph:
21
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), an insurer or insurance broker who undertakes risk evaluation, physical inspection of hazards or loss control activities at a site which

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (a) is a contaminated site at the date of such activities, or

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (b) became a contaminated site after the date of such activities

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: is designated for the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act not responsible for remediation of the contaminated site and is exempt from an order under section 83 (2) (f) of the Act in relation to the contaminated site, unless the insurer or insurance broker exercised control over or imposed requirements on any person regarding the manner of treatment, disposal or handling of a substance and the control or requirements, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site.

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (2) An insurer or insurance broker does not exercise control or impose requirements under subsection (1) if the insurer or insurance broker acts pursuant to rights or obligations with respect to an insurance policy including, without limitation, any of the following:

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (a) participating only in purely financial matters related to providing insurance at the site;

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (b) having the capacity or ability to influence any operation at the contaminated site in a way that would have the effect of causing or increasing contamination, but does not exercise the capacity or ability in such a way as to cause or increase contamination;

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (c) imposing requirements on any person if the requirements do not have a reasonable probability of causing or increasing contamination of the site;

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (d) appointing a person to inspect or investigate a contaminated site to determine future steps or actions that the insurer or insurance broker may take;

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (e) imposing requirements on any person to comply with environmental laws, standards, policies or codes of practice of government or industry, including requirements to perform monitoring tests, scientific studies or to remediate contaminated sites.

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), if an insurer or insurance broker is responsible for remediation, the liability of the insurer is limited to the cost of remediation, provided that such liability does not exceed the sum of any proceeds of any insurance coverage that is provided for the subject site for the purpose of covering such environmental risks.

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (4) The limitation under subsection (3) does not apply to an insurer or insurance broker who intentionally caused environmental damage or who was grossly negligent or guilty of wilful misconduct with respect to

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (a) the use of the environment, or

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (b) the lives or safety of persons.

heading: Persons not responsible - insurers and insurance brokers
paragraph: (5) This section does not affect any rights or obligations under an insurance policy.

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph:
22
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), for the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, a person is designated not responsible for remediation of a contaminated site if, with respect to the contaminated site, the person is a current or previous owner of

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (a) an easement,

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (b) a right of way,

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (c) a restrictive covenant,

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (d) a covenant under section 219 of the Land Title Act,

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (e) a lien,

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (f) a judgement,

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (g) a reservation in a Crown grant, or

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (h) an interest in real property which deals exclusively with subsurface rights including such a tenure under the Geothermal Resources Act, the Mineral Tenure Act or the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act.

heading: Persons not responsible - certain owners
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply unless the person can establish that there has been no use or exercise of any right of the interest specified in paragraphs (a) to (h) of that subsection in a manner that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site.

heading: Persons not responsible - producers arranging for transportation
paragraph: 23		  For the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, a person described in section 45 (1) (c) or (d) of the Act is designated not responsible for remediation of a contaminated site if

heading: Persons not responsible - producers arranging for transportation
paragraph: (a) the person transferred ownership of a substance and responsibility for managing the substance to a transporter who

heading: Persons not responsible - producers arranging for transportation
paragraph: (i)  intended at the time of the transfer to transport the substance to a site where the owner or operator of the site was at that time legally entitled to accept the substance, and

heading: Persons not responsible - producers arranging for transportation
paragraph: (ii)  spilled or otherwise discharged the substance after the transfer but before delivering the substance to the person described in subparagraph (i), and

heading: Persons not responsible - producers arranging for transportation
paragraph: (b) the person did not by contract, agreement or otherwise impose requirements on the transporter in a manner which caused, in whole or in part, the spill or discharge referred to in paragraph (a) (ii).

heading: Persons not responsible - construction on contaminated sites
paragraph:
24
		  For the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, a person is designated not responsible for remediation of a contaminated site if the person provided only contracting or consulting services related to the construction of buildings and facilities at the contaminated site.

heading: Persons not responsible - secured creditors
paragraph:
25
		  (1) For the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, a secured creditor described in section 45 (3) (a) of the Act is designated not responsible for remediation of a contaminated site if the secured creditor does any of the following:

heading: Persons not responsible - secured creditors
paragraph: (a) imposes requirements on any person to comply with environmental laws, standards, policies or codes of practice of government or industry, including requirements to perform monitoring tests, scientific studies or to remediate contaminated sites;

heading: Persons not responsible - secured creditors
paragraph: (b) participates in loan work out actions, including the giving of financial or other advice to a financially distressed borrower, restructuring or renegotiating the terms of a security interest, requiring additional payments or consideration, or exercising forbearance;

heading: Persons not responsible - secured creditors
paragraph: (c) takes steps, whether or not they are part of realization proceedings, to preserve, protect or enhance the value of the secured assets or to reduce or prevent future contamination or the migration of existing contaminants or otherwise conduct any independent remediation;

heading: Persons not responsible - secured creditors
paragraph: (d) subject to section 45 (3) (b) of the Act and subsection (2) of this section, undertakes realization proceedings.

heading: Persons not responsible - secured creditors
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the liability of a secured creditor who becomes a registered owner in fee simple of real property at a contaminated site exists and endures under section 45 (3) (b) of the Act only while the secured creditor is the registered owner in fee simple of the real property.

heading: Persons not responsible - secured creditors
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not remove the liability of a secured creditor for remediation of a contaminated site under Part 4 of the Act if the secured creditor who became the registered owner in fee simple of real property at the contaminated site at any time exercised control over or imposed requirements on any person regarding the manner of treatment, disposal or handling of a substance and the control or requirements, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site.

heading: Persons not responsible - receivers, receiver managers and bankruptcy trustees
paragraph:
26
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Persons not responsible - receivers, receiver managers and bankruptcy trustees
paragraph: "available funds" means any and all funds realized by a receiver less

heading: Persons not responsible - receivers, receiver managers and bankruptcy trustees

heading: Persons not responsible - clarification of innocent acquisition exemption
paragraph:
28
		  When judging whether an owner or operator has, under section 46 (1) (d) (i) (C) of the Act, undertaken all appropriate inquiries into the previous ownership and uses of a site and undertaken other investigations consistent with good commercial or customary practice at the time of acquisition of the property, consideration must be given to all of the following:

heading: Persons not responsible - clarification of innocent acquisition exemption
paragraph: (a) any personal knowledge or experience of the owner or operator respecting contamination at the time of the acquisition;

heading: Persons not responsible - clarification of innocent acquisition exemption
paragraph: (b) the relationship of the actual purchase price to the value of the property if it was uncontaminated;

heading: Persons not responsible - clarification of innocent acquisition exemption
paragraph: (c) commonly known or reasonably ascertainable information about the property at the time of the acquisition;

heading: Persons not responsible - clarification of innocent acquisition exemption
paragraph: (d) any obvious presence of contamination or indicators of contamination or the feasibility of detecting such contamination by appropriate inspection at the time of the acquisition.

heading: Persons not responsible - modification of lessor liability under section 46 (1) (e) of the Act
paragraph:
29
		  Subject to section 30, an owner of real property at a contaminated site is exempt from section 46 (1) (e) of the Act if

heading: Persons not responsible - modification of lessor liability under section 46 (1) (e) of the Act
paragraph: (a) the owner voluntarily leased, rented or otherwise allowed use of the real property by another person,

heading: Persons not responsible - modification of lessor liability under section 46 (1) (e) of the Act
paragraph: (b) the owner knew or had a reasonable basis for knowing that the other person described in paragraph (a) planned or intended to use the real property to dispose of, handle or treat a substance in a manner that, in whole or in part, would cause the site to become a contaminated site, and

heading: Persons not responsible - modification of lessor liability under section 46 (1) (e) of the Act
paragraph: (c) the person described in paragraph (a) used the real property to dispose of, handle or treat a substance in a manner that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site.

heading: Persons not responsible - lessors who provide surface access for subsurface use
paragraph:
30
		  A lessor who, under the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act, enters into a surface lease agreement with a lessee that allows the lessee access to subsurface resources is, for the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, designated not responsible for remediation of contamination caused by the lessee if the agreement requires the lessee to covenant and agree to indemnify and save harmless the lessor from any liabilities, damages, costs, claims, suits or actions arising out of the lessee's operations on the lessor's lands, except liabilities, damages, costs, claims, suits or actions arising out of the gross negligence or wilful misconduct of the lessor, its agents, servants, employees or contractors.

heading: Persons responsible - municipalities
paragraph: 31		  For the purposes of 45 (1) (e) of the Act, a government body that acquires an ownership interest in a contaminated site by a municipal boundary extension or a municipal amalgamation initiated by the municipality is designated responsible for remediation of the contaminated site.

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters of contaminated soil
paragraph:
32
		  (1) A transporter of contaminated soil who is otherwise in compliance with the Act and the regulations is, for the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, designated not responsible for remediation of a site which becomes contaminated by disposal or deposit of contaminated soil if there has been any misrepresentation to the transporter by

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters of contaminated soil
paragraph: (a) a person who arranged for the transportation of the contaminated soil respecting the quality or degree of contamination of the soil, or

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters of contaminated soil
paragraph: (b) a person who agrees to receive the contaminated soil respecting the quality, degree of contamination or acceptability of the disposal location in accordance with any requirement in Part 8.

heading: Persons not responsible - transporters of contaminated soil
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only if the transporter acted in good faith and without negligence.

heading: Persons not responsible - contamination which is subject to a wide area remediation plan
paragraph:
33
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person who is a current or previous owner or operator of a contaminated site is, for the purposes of section 46 (1) (n) of the Act, designated not responsible for remediation of the site if the site is contaminated only by substances being managed in accordance with a wide area remediation plan.

heading: Persons not responsible - contamination which is subject to a wide area remediation plan
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who caused the contamination which is the subject of a wide area remediation plan.

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph:
35
		  (1) For the purposes of determining compensation payable under section 47 (5) of the Act, a defendant named in a cost recovery action under that section may assert all legal and equitable defences, including any right to obtain relief under an agreement, other legislation or the common law.

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (2) In an action between 2 or more responsible persons under section 47 (5) of the Act, the following factors must be considered when determining the reasonably incurred costs of remediation:

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (a) the price paid for the property by the person seeking cost recovery;

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (b) the relative due diligence of the responsible persons involved in the action;

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (c) the amount of contaminating substances and the toxicity attributable to the persons involved in the action;

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (d) the relative degree of involvement, by each of the persons in the action, in the generation, transportation, treatment, storage or disposal of the substances that caused the site to become contaminated;

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (e) any remediation measures implemented and paid for by each of the persons in the action;

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (f) other factors relevant to a fair and just allocation.

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of section 47 of the Act, any compensation payable by a defendant in an action under section 47 (5) of the Act is a reasonably incurred cost of remediation for that responsible person and the defendant may seek contribution from any other responsible person in accordance with the procedures under section 4 of the Negligence Act.

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (4) In an action under section 47 (5) of the Act against a director, officer, employee or agent of a person or government body, the plaintiff must prove that the director, officer, employee or agent authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the activity which gave rise to the cost of remediation.

heading: Determining compensation under section 47 (5) of the Act
paragraph: (5) In an action under section 47 (5) of the Act, a corporation is not liable for the costs of remediation arising from the actions of a subsidiary corporation unless the plaintiff can prove that the corporation authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the activity of the subsidiary corporation which gave rise to the costs of remediation.

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: 36		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), a director who receives a request under section 48 (10) of the Act for notice respecting whether a remediation order will be issued must provide the notice within 10 days after receiving the request.

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), if a director is requested by a person to give consent under section 48 (8) of the Act, the director must consider the request and give written notice of the decision to the person within 10 days after receiving the request.

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: (3) If a director requires more than 10 days to obtain or consider information relevant to the request under subsection (1) or (2), the director must

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: (a) give notice to the person making the request under subsection (1) (b) or (2) that more time is required, and

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: (b) state, in the notice given under paragraph (a), how much more time is required.

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), a director must not take more than 30 days to review and respond to

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: (a) a person's request for consent under section 48 (8) of the Act, or

heading: Remediation orders - timing for consent and notice
paragraph: (b) a person's request for notice under section 48 (10) of the Act respecting whether a remediation order will be issued.

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph:
37
		  A person is exempt from the duty not to diminish or reduce assets under section 48 (8) or (10) of the Act to the extent that the person does any of the following:

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (a) converts or exchanges assets from one class or kind to another class or kind including, without limitation, allowing the sale and conversion of inventory to a receivable or the collection and conversion of a receivable into cash;

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (b) uses assets to satisfy liabilities as they become due, including paying fair value for supplies, services or other benefits conferred on the person, or on a receiver as defined in section 26 or a trustee as defined in section 27, carrying out the management function with respect to the asset;

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (c) makes or accepts payments on loans or advances, revolves an operating line of credit, makes demand on a term or operating loan, reduces the maximum available under an operating line of credit or refuses to advance further funds;

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (d) processes natural resources, including crude oil, natural gas and timber;

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (e) installs infrastructure to provide services;

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (f) provides services to customers;

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (g) is a receiver as defined in section 26 or trustee as defined in section 27 who complies with section 26 or 27 respectively;

heading: Remediation orders - diminishing or reducing assets
paragraph: (h) realizes on a mortgage, lien, charge or other security interest.

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph:
38
		  A responsible person applying for minor contributor status under section 50 of the Act must provide information to a director, to the extent the information is reasonably ascertainable, respecting all of the following:

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (a) the condition of the contaminated site at the time the applicant

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (i)  became an owner or operator at the site, and

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (ii)  if applicable, ceased to be an owner or operator at the site;

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (b) any activities and land uses carried out by the applicant while located at the site;

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (c) the nature and quantity of contamination at the site attributable to the applicant;

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (d) all measures taken by the applicant to prevent or remediate contamination;

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (e) contamination on the site or released from the site which is attributable to

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (i)  the applicant, and

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (ii)  other persons at the site;

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (f) all measures taken by the applicant to exercise due diligence with respect to any substance that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site, including any measures taken to prevent foreseeable acts of third parties which may have contributed to the contamination at the site.

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph:
39
		  (1) A responsible person requesting a voluntary remediation agreement in respect of a contaminated site, including an environmental management area, must provide all of the following information to a director:

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (a) a detailed site investigation;

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (b) a remediation plan;

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (c) a detailed description of the responsible person's past and present activities on the site, including the amount and characteristics of contamination at the site attributable to that person's activities;

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (d) an estimate of the total cost of remediation;

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (e) an estimate of the responsible person's share of the total cost of remediation and justification for the estimate;

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (f) the name and address of any other person who the responsible person has reason to believe may, with respect to the subject contaminated site, be a responsible person;

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (g) a statement describing the responsible person's ability and plans to conduct and finance the remediation.

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (3) Before a director enters into a voluntary remediation agreement with a responsible person, the director must notify any persons identified as other potential responsible persons under subsection (1) (f) and allow those persons not less than 15 days to give notice if they wish to review or make representations to the director about the proposed voluntary remediation agreement.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
40
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "federal land" means land under the administration and control of Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "highway" has the same meaning as in the Transportation Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "low-impact land use" means a land use described in any of paragraphs (a) to (d) of section 12 (3) [wildlands, agricultural, urban park or residential];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pipeline" has the same meaning as in the Oil and Gas Activities Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "preload" means soil that, for geotechnical purposes, is temporarily placed on the surface of a site to compress the underlying soil;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualified professional", in relation to a duty or function under this Part, means an individual who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is registered in British Columbia with a professional organization, acts under that organization's code of ethics and is subject to disciplinary action by that organization, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) through suitable education, experience, accreditation and knowledge may reasonably be relied on to provide advice within the individual's area of expertise, which area of expertise is applicable to the duty or function;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "receiving site" means a site at which soil is deposited;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "source site" means a site from which soil is removed;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transit system" has the same meaning as in the Transportation Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "winter-maintenance sand" means sand that is applied to roadways or other surfaces for the purpose of managing icy conditions.

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: 41		  (1) For the purposes of the definition of "waste" in section 1 (1) of the Act, a soil is prescribed as waste in relation to a receiving site if

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (a) the concentration of any substance in the soil is greater than

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (i)  the generic numerical soil standard applicable to the receiving site, or

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (ii)  the lowest value of the matrix numerical soil standards applicable to the receiving site, or

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (b) the concentration of any substance in vapour emissions from the soil is greater than the generic numerical vapour standard applicable to the receiving site.

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (a) does not apply in relation to a substance if the concentration of the substance in soil is not greater than

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (a) the applicable site-specific numerical standard, or

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (b) the background concentration of that substance in soil at the receiving site.

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) (b) does not apply in relation to a substance if

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (a) the concentration of the substance in vapour is not greater than

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (i)  the applicable site-specific numerical standard, or

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (ii)  the background concentration of that substance in vapour at the receiving site, or

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (b) the soil is exempt under subsection (4) from vapour analysis.

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (3) (b), soil is exempt from vapour analysis if

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (a) the soil does not contain any volatile chlorinated substance set out in Schedule 3.1, and

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (b) the soil does not contain any substance with a concentration greater than

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (i)  the generic numerical soil standard for a low density residential land use, or

heading: Definition of "waste" in the Act
paragraph: (ii)  the lowest value of the matrix numerical soil standards for a low density residential land use.

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph:
42
		  (1) Section 55 (1.1) [removal of soil - notice] of the Act applies to the removal of soil from a source site to a receiving site unless the soil is exempt under

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (a) section 55 (1.4) [removal of small amounts of soil] of the Act,

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (b) section 55 (5) [removal of soil that is waste] of the Act, or

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (c) subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (2) A removal of soil to a receiving site is exempt from section 55 (1.1) of the Act in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (a) the receiving site is outside of British Columbia;

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (b) the receiving site is on federal land, other than a reserve within the meaning of the Indian Act (Canada);

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (c) the source site has not been used other than for a low-impact land use or mining of marl, earth, soil, peat, sand, gravel, dimension stone, rock or any natural substance that is used for a construction purpose on land and the soil was

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (i)  extracted in accordance with a permit under the Mines Act, and

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (ii)  transported directly to the receiving site;

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (d) the soil is preload that was originally extracted from a site used for a low-impact land use, whether or not the source site is used for a low-impact land use;

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (e) the soil is winter-maintenance sand.

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of section 55 (1.4) of the Act, the following amount of soil is prescribed as exempt from section 55 (1.1) of the Act:

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (a) in the case of soil removed from a source site classified under a director's protocol as low, moderate, medium or intermediate risk, the prescribed amount is 30 cubic metres calculated in accordance with subsection (4) of this section;

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (b) in the case of soil removed from a source site classified under a director's protocol as high risk, no amount is prescribed.

heading: Removal of soil
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (3) (a), the amount of soil removed is to be calculated by adding the amounts removed over the course of the same project in any period of 2 years.

heading: Notice of removal of soil
paragraph: 43		  (1) A notice under section 55 (1.1) [removal of soil - notice] of the Act must be

heading: Notice of removal of soil
paragraph: (a) in the form set out in Schedule 8, and

heading: Notice of removal of soil
paragraph: (b) provided to the minister by a qualified professional, through a website maintained by or on behalf of the minister, at least one week and no more than 2 years before the removal of the soil to which the notice relates.

heading: Notice of removal of soil
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 55 (1.2) (a) (iv) of the Act, a summary of an analysis of the quality of soil must identify

heading: Notice of removal of soil
paragraph: (a) which substances in the soil or in vapours emitted from the soil were analyzed, and

heading: Notice of removal of soil
paragraph: (b) the concentrations of those substances.

heading: Notice of removal of soil
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of section 55 (1.2) (a) (v) of the Act, a notice under section 55 (1.1) must include the information specified in the form set out in Schedule 8.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
44
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "high volume site" means a site in relation to which section 55.1 (2) [high volume soil receiving sites] of the Act applies;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "managed soil", in relation to a high volume site, means relocated industrial or commercial site soil that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) relocated to the site, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) not exempt under section 45 (3).

heading: High volume sites
paragraph:
45
		  (1) For the purposes of section 55.1 (2) of the Act, the prescribed amount is 20 000 cubic metres.

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (2) Section 55.1 (2) of the Act does not apply in relation to a waste management facility.

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), section 55.1 (2) of the Act does not apply in relation to soil that is relocated to a site in any of the following circumstances:

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (a) the soil is relocated to the site before March 1, 2023,

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (b) the soil does not meet any of the following criteria:

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (i)  the concentration of any substance in the soil is greater than

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (A) the generic numerical soil standard applicable to a site that is used for a low-impact land use, or

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (B) the lowest value of the matrix numerical soil standards applicable to a site that is used for a low-impact land use;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (ii)  the concentration of any substance in vapour emissions from the soil is greater than the generic numerical vapour standard applicable to a site that is used for a low-impact land use;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (c) subject to subsection (4), the soil is relocated to a site of any of the following facilities in the course of constructing or maintaining the facility:

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (i)  a highway;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (ii)  a transit system;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (iii)  a pipeline;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (iv)  a sewage collection system;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (v)  a drainage collection system that is below ground;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (vi)  a water distribution system;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (vii)  an electricity transmission or distribution system;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (viii)  a telecommunications line or tower;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (ix)  a right of way required for infrastructure described in any of subparagraphs (i) to (viii);

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (x)  dikes, green shores or other structures constructed to prevent flooding or erosion.

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (4) The exemption under subsection (3) (c) does not apply in relation to soil that is relocated to a site described in that subsection if

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (a) the site is within 10 metres of

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (i)  a watercourse or body of water, whether or not usually containing water, or

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (ii)  any of the following that is connected by surface flow to a watercourse or body of water referred to in subparagraph (i):

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (A) a ditch, whether or not usually containing water;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (B) a spring, whether or not usually containing water;

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (C) a wetland, and

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (b) the soil contains an organic substance with a concentration greater than

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (i)  the generic numerical soil standard applicable to a site that is used for a low-impact land use, or

heading: High volume sites
paragraph: (ii)  the lowest value of the matrix numerical soil standards applicable to a site that is used for a low-impact land use.

heading: Registration of high volume site
paragraph:
46
		  (1) For the purposes of section 55.1 (2) (a) of the Act, the owner of a high volume site must register the site with the minister.

heading: Registration of high volume site
paragraph: (2) An application for registration under subsection (1) must be

heading: Registration of high volume site
paragraph: (a) in the form set out in Schedule 8.1, and

heading: Registration of high volume site
paragraph: (b) submitted by a qualified professional through a website maintained by or on behalf of the minister.

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph:
46.1
		  (1) For the purposes of section 55.1 (2) (a) of the Act, the owner of a high volume site must

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (a) have a soil management plan for the site, and

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (b) manage the site in accordance with that soil management plan until the site is closed.

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (2) A soil management plan for a high volume site must be

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (a) developed by a qualified professional, and

heading: Soil management plan
