paragraph: (b) approved by an approved professional other than the qualified professional who developed the plan.

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (3) A soil management plan for a high volume site must

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (a) ensure the managed soil at the site is contained so that substances in that soil do not migrate from the site in concentrations sufficient to cause contamination at another site, and

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (b) without limiting paragraph (a),

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (i)  set out procedures for

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (A) the detailed tracking of the source sites of the managed soil at the site and the locations at the site where the managed soil from each source site is deposited, and

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (B) seasonal groundwater monitoring, and

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (ii)  include a plan for closure of the high volume site.

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (4) A soil management plan under subsection (1) for a high volume site must be implemented under the supervision of a qualified professional.

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (5) A closure plan under subsection (3) (b) (ii) must provide that the site must not be closed until

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (a) the operator has ceased accepting relocated industrial or commercial site soil for deposit at the site, other than soil exempt under section 45 (3), and

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (b) an approved professional has given an opinion that

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (i)  the substances in the managed soil at the site are stable, in accordance with the director's protocols, and

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (ii)  seasonal groundwater monitoring is no longer required for the purposes described in subsection (3) (a) of this section.

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (6) An opinion referred to in subsection (5) (b) must be in writing and must set out the reasons on which the opinion is based.

heading: Soil management plan
paragraph: (7) The owner of a high volume site must retain a copy of the soil management plan for the site for at least 10 years after the site is closed.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph:
47
		  (1) A responsible person may apply for an approval in principle of a proposed remediation plan under section 53 (1.1) of the Act by submitting a request in writing to a director and attaching or ensuring the director already has

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (a) copies of any preliminary and detailed site investigation reports prepared for the site,

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (b) copies of any other site investigation and assessment reports prepared for the site, and

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (c) the proposed remediation plan for which the approval in principle is sought.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (1.1) A responsible person making an application described in subsection (1) or (4) respecting a site classified under a director's protocol as a low or moderate risk site must specify in writing whether the application shall be processed

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (a) in the manner for low or moderate risk sites, or

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (b) in the manner for medium, intermediate or high risk sites.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (1.2) A responsible person making an application described in subsection (1) or (4) respecting a site classified under a director's protocol as a medium, intermediate or high risk site, or not classified under a director's protocol, may specify in writing that the application be processed in the manner for low or moderate risk sites.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (1.3) A director may reject an application for which a written specification is made under subsection (1.1) (a) or (1.2) if the director is satisfied that, for the likely human health and environmental risks to be properly assessed, a site covered by the application must be processed in the manner for a medium, intermediate or high risk site before a decision can properly be made whether or not to issue an approval in principle under section 53 (1.1) of the Act.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (1.4) A director may require that an application for an approval in principle in relation to a contaminated site, including an environmental management area, that is classified under a director's protocol as a low or moderate risk site include a report and the recommendation of an approved professional that the application be approved.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (1.41) If the director does not impose a requirement under subsection (1.4), the application may include a report and the recommendation of an approved professional in respect of whether the application should be approved and, if so, section 49.1 applies.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (1.5) If the director rejects the recommendation of an approved professional provided under subsection (1.4) or (1.41), the director, within 15 days of the rejection, must provide written reasons to

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (a) the applicant, and

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (b) the professional association, in the Province, of which the approved professional is a member.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (2) Before issuing an approval in principle under section 53 (1.1) of the Act, a director may request any additional information and reports the director considers necessary to assess whether the standards, criteria or conditions prescribed in section 17, 18 or 18.1 of this regulation are likely to be complied with when the proposed remediation plan has been implemented.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (3) When issuing an approval in principle under section 53 (1.1) of the Act, a director may specify conditions for any or all of the following:

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (a) implementing some or all of the activities described in a proposed remediation plan;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (b) risk assessment and risk management measures which may be required for part or all of a site for any reason;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (c) preparation, registration, and criteria for final discharge of a covenant under section 219 of the Land Title Act as may be required under section 48;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (d) carrying out confirmatory sampling and analysis after treatment or removal of contamination;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (e) testing and monitoring to evaluate the quality and performance of any remediation measures;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (f) any financial security required by the director in accordance with section 48;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (g) any actions which the director could require in a permit under section 14 of the Act.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (4) A responsible person may apply under subsection (1) for approval in principle of a wide area remediation plan.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (5) A director may issue an approval in principle for a wide area remediation plan if the remediation plan complies with all the following:

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (a) the goal of the plan is to satisfy the applicable criteria, standards or conditions prescribed in this regulation;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (b) environmental risks are addressed in the plan to the satisfaction of the director;

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (c) the plan provides for the monitoring and assessment of public health and environmental parameters the director considers appropriate for evaluating progress in satisfying the applicable criteria, standards or conditions in relation to the contaminants specified in the plan.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (6) An approval in principle for a remediation plan issued under this section is a permit within the meaning of the Act for any facility which

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (a) is located on the site to which the remediation plan applies,

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (b) is specifically identified in the remediation plan, and

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (c) is used to manage any contamination which is located on the site for which the remediation plan applies.

heading: Approval in principle
paragraph: (7) In relation to an application for an approval in principle described in subsection (6), the Public Notification Regulation does not apply with respect to the facility.

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: 48		  (1) A director may require that a covenant be registered under section 219 of the Land Title Act for the purpose of any or all of

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (a) setting conditions regarding works, and their inspection and maintenance at a site, considered necessary to secure the contamination at the site and to protect human health or the environment,

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (b) setting conditions for restricting disturbance of soils, or preventing a changed use of a site, which would invalidate a risk assessment and potentially increase exposure of human and environmental receptors to site contamination,

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (c) specifying requirements to monitor for movement or impacts of contamination, and

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (d) indemnifying the Crown or its agents or employees from losses, charges, actions or suits related to contamination remaining at the site, if these purposes are unlikely to be satisfactorily met by the entry of notations in the site registry.

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (2) A person may request that a director have a covenant registered under the authority of subsection (1) discharged if the person believes that the conditions which gave rise to the covenant no longer exist or have been complied with.

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (3) A director must have a covenant registered under the authority of subsection (1) discharged when

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (a) remediation has been carried out in accordance with the numerical standards for remediation set out in section 17, and

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (b) the director issues a certificate of compliance for the remediation referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (4) A director may require financial security if

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (a) a significant risk could arise from conditions at a contaminated site because

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (i)  the site is left in an unremediated or partially remediated state, or

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (ii)  the site is remediated but requires ongoing management and monitoring because contamination is left at the site, and

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (b) a covenant under section 219 of the Land Title Act is, in the opinion of the director, unlikely to be an effective means to ensure that necessary remediation is carried out at the site.

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (5) The financial security required by a director under subsection (4) may be for the purpose of any or all of the following:

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (a) ensuring that a responsible person completes remediation or guarantees performance to the satisfaction of the director;

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (b) providing funds to further treat, remove or otherwise manage contamination;

heading: Covenants and financial security - general principles
paragraph: (c) complying with the applicable legislation and financial management and operating policies of British Columbia.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: 49		  (1) A person may apply for a certificate of compliance under section 53 (3) of the Act by submitting a request in writing to a director.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (2) In support of the application referred to in subsection (1), the person requesting the certificate of compliance must provide to the director the reports described in paragraphs (a) and (b) and ensure that the director has information on the items described in paragraphs (c) and (d):

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (a) preliminary and detailed site investigation reports;

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (b) a confirmation of remediation report which describes sampling and analyses carried out after remediation of the contamination including

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (i)  a description of sampling locations and methods used,

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (ii)  a schedule of sampling conducted, and

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (iii)  a summary and evaluation of results of field observations and of field and laboratory analyses of samples;

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (c) compliance with all conditions set by a director under section 47 (3) if an approval in principle was issued prior to remediation;

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (d) the quality and performance of remediation measures on completion of remediation, including compliance with the remediation standards, criteria or conditions prescribed in this regulation.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (3) A person making an application described in subsection (1) respecting a site classified under a director's protocol as a low or moderate risk site must specify in writing whether the application shall be processed

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (a) in the manner for low or moderate risk sites, or

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (b) in the manner for medium, intermediate or high risk sites.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (4) A person making an application described in subsection (1) respecting a site classified under a director's protocol as a medium, intermediate or high risk site, or not classified under a director's protocol, may specify in writing that the application be processed in the manner for low or moderate risk sites.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (5) A director may reject an application for which a written specification is made under subsection (3) (a) or (4) if the director is satisfied that, for the likely human health and environmental risks to be properly assessed, a site covered by the application must be processed in the manner for a medium, intermediate or high risk site before a decision can properly be made whether or not to issue a certificate under section 53 (3) of the Act.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (6) A director may require that an application described in subsection (1) for a certificate of compliance in relation to a contaminated site that is classified under a director's protocol as a low or moderate risk site include a report and the recommendation of an approved professional that the application be approved.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (7) If the director does not impose a requirement under subsection (6), the application may include a report and the recommendation of an approved professional in respect of whether the application should be approved and, if so, section 49.1 applies.

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (8) If a director rejects the recommendation of an approved professional provided under subsection (6) or (7), the director, within 15 days of the rejection, must provide written reasons to

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (a) the applicant, and

heading: Requests for certificates
paragraph: (b) the professional association, in the Province, of which the approved professional is a member.

heading: Director may consider recommendations of approved professionals
paragraph:
49.1
		  For the purpose of determining the manner and extent of the review that must be undertaken of the work on which an application referred to in section 15 (6), 43 (3), 47 (1.41) or 49 (7), a director may consider whether the application includes the recommendation of an approved professional in respect of the decision requested in the application.

heading: Financial security as a condition of a certificate
paragraph:
50
		  (1) If financial security is a condition of an approval in principle for a remediation plan for a particular site, all terms of the security requirement must be met before a director may issue a certificate of compliance for that site.

heading: Financial security as a condition of a certificate
paragraph: (2) If a director requires financial security in accordance with section 53 (3) (d) of the Act and section 48 (4) of this regulation, before the director issues a certificate of compliance, a responsible person must

heading: Financial security as a condition of a certificate
paragraph: (a) provide, to the director, satisfactory evidence of the availability of the required security, and

heading: Financial security as a condition of a certificate
paragraph: (b) provide any required contractual agreement relating to the terms and conditions of the security, signed by the responsible person.

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates for part of a site
paragraph:
51
		  If a responsible person applies for and a director issues an approval in principle or a certificate of compliance for a part of a contaminated site as authorized by section 53 (6) of the Act, the director must

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates for part of a site
paragraph: (a) provide to the registrar information respecting the part of the site to which the approval in principle or certificate of compliance applies, and

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates for part of a site
paragraph: (b) in accordance with section 48 of this regulation, consider whether a covenant under section 219 of the Land Title Act or financial security is required relative to one or more parts of the site not remediated.

heading: Duties of director respecting approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: 52		  (1) A director need not consider an application for an approval in principle or certificate of compliance until all required information has been provided to the director for review.

heading: Duties of director respecting approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (2) A director must send a copy of an approval in principle or certificate of compliance issued by the director in respect of a site to the municipality in which the subject contaminated site is located.

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph:
54
		  (1) If a director establishes an allocation panel to provide an opinion under section 49 (2) of the Act, the panel

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (a) must consider written and oral information submitted to it by the person who requested that a panel be established, and

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (b) may consider other written and oral information submitted to it by any other person.

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only if the information pertains to one or more of the factors described in section 49 (3) of the Act.

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (3) An allocation panel established under section 49 (2) of the Act must give advance notice of its planned deliberations to any person who the panel believes, on reasonable grounds, may be a responsible person.

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (4) An allocation panel established under section 49 (2) of the Act may determine its own procedures to be used in rendering an opinion, but the procedures must not conflict with a director's protocol.

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (5) A person who wishes to withdraw a request to obtain an opinion from an allocation panel must notify the director in writing.

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (6) The director who receives the notice referred to in subsection (5) may request that the allocation panel render an opinion on the basis of any information submitted to it before the withdrawal of the request.

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (7) A person who withdraws a request to obtain an opinion from an allocation panel is liable for the panel fees and costs incurred by the panel before the time of receipt by the director of the notice referred to in subsection (5).

heading: Allocation panel procedures
paragraph: (8) An allocation panel must, when rendering an opinion, state the information relied on to render the opinion, including the extent of information and facts available to it and any significant deficiencies in the information provided to it.

heading: Director's powers
paragraph:
55
		  (1) When ordering public consultation or a review under section 52 (1) of the Act, a director may require a person who proposes to carry out remediation to do any or all of the following:

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (a) post a notice of the proposed remediation, in a manner acceptable to the director, in a location visible to the public on the site or property which is the subject of the proposed remediation;

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (b) publish, as specified by the director, in 2 or more editions of one or more newspapers with circulation local to the subject site, a notice of availability of information respecting

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (i)  site investigations,

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (ii)  evaluation of remediation alternatives,

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (iii)  remediation plans,

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (iv)  site registry identification numbers, and

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (v)  any other documentation as may be specified by the director;

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (c) serve, on any person who, in the opinion of the director, may be adversely affected by the proposed remediation, a notice of availability of information respecting

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (i)  site investigations,

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (ii)  evaluation of remediation alternatives,

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (iii)  remediation plans, and

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (iv)  any other documentation that may be specified by the director;

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (d) undertake other notification requirements specified by the director;

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (e) hold public information meetings and use other public consultation methods, including providing public access to reports and studies at local public libraries, that the director specifies.

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (2) A director may, when considering the need for public consultation or review of remediation of a contaminated site under section 52 (2) of the Act, require a person who proposes to remediate the contaminated site to submit a report to the director which describes past and proposed public consultations regarding the contaminated site under consideration.

heading: Director's powers
paragraph: (3) After issuance of an approval in principle or a certificate of compliance, a director must not order public consultation with respect to the remediation which is the subject of the approval in principle or certificate of compliance, but this does not prevent the director from ordering the person to provide information to the public about the remediation.

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph:
57
		  (1) A responsible person who carries out independent remediation of a site pursuant to section 54 (1) of the Act must, if the responsible person knows that one or more substances has migrated or is likely to have migrated to a neighbouring site and is or is likely causing contamination of the neighbouring site, provide the notification described in subsection (1.1).

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (1.1) The responsible person must provide written notification to the person or persons who own the neighbouring site and a copy of the notification to a director, within 15 days after the responsible person becomes aware of the migration or likely migration of each substance to the neighbouring site, giving

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the person or persons who own the site or sites to be remediated,

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (b) the name, address and telephone number of the person to contact regarding the remediation activities to be undertaken at the site, and

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (c) a general description of the nature of the migration or likely migration of each substance.

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (1.2) A person who has a duty to provide notification to a director of commencement of independent remediation under section 54 (2) (a) of the Act must provide written notice to a director within 3 days after the commencement of any remediation activity involving handling, management or treatment of contamination, other than activity which has the purpose of obtaining results for investigation purposes, giving

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (a) the legal description, including parcel identifier numbers and latitudinal and longitudinal references, and civic address of the parcel or parcels of land at the site to be remediated,

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (b) the name and address of the person or persons who own the parcel or parcels of land at the site to be remediated,

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (c) the name, address and telephone number of the person to contact regarding the remediation activities to be undertaken at the site, and

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (d) a general description of the nature of the contaminated site and the remediation being conducted.

heading: Notifications for independent remediation
paragraph: (2) In the case of independent remediation arising from emergency response to a spill of a polluting substance, a person is exempt from the requirements of subsection (1.2) if the spill has been reported in accordance with the requirements of section 79 of the Act and the Spill Reporting Regulation.

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph:
58
		  (1) Subject to subsections (3) and (4) and subject to the terms and conditions of a remediation order, an order to investigate under section 41 of the Act or a pollution abatement order, a preliminary site investigation consists of the following 2 stages:

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (a) a first stage which includes

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (i)  a review of site historical use and records, including a search of the site registry, to determine current and past activities or uses, accidents and spills, and practices and management relating to potential contamination at the site and neighbouring sites,

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (ii)  one or more site reconnaissance visits with visual inspection of buildings, property, equipment, land, surface water and biota for indicators or presence of contamination,

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (iii)  interviews with current or former owners, occupants, neighbours, directors, employees and government officials who can, with reasonable attempts, be contacted respecting information on activities which may have caused contamination,

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (iv)  any information as to which substances on the site may cause contamination, and

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (v)  activities described in a director's protocol,

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: but does not include sampling of relevant environmental media or investigation of subsurface conditions;

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (b) a second stage which allows determination of the general location and degree of any contamination and which includes

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (i)  sampling of relevant environmental media,

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (ii)  laboratory or field instrumental analysis of sampled and selected environmental media for substances which may cause or threaten to cause contamination,

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (iii)  other intrusive or nonintrusive methods of investigating subsurface conditions,

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (iv)  assessment of substance concentrations relative to the criteria, standards and conditions prescribed in this regulation, and

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (v)  activities described in a director's protocol.

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (2) A person who carries out a preliminary site investigation may proceed sequentially through the 2 stages described in subsection (1) (a) and (b) or may proceed in a manner which combines the 2 stages.

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (3) A person who has been ordered to undertake a preliminary site investigation and who has proceeded using a staged approach in accordance with subsection (1) may

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (a) present to a director a report of the first stage of a preliminary site investigation, and

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (b) seek consent of the director that the second stage of the preliminary site investigation is not required.

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (4) A person who has been ordered to undertake a preliminary site investigation is not required to comply with the terms of the order if the person obtains the consent of a director to prepare a detailed site investigation which addresses the subject matter of the ordered preliminary site investigation.

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (5) A report of a preliminary site investigation prepared under section 41 of the Act must do all of the following:

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (a) indicate whether the investigation proceeded in stages as described in subsection (1) and, if so, the objectives, methods and procedures which were used in each stage;

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (b) describe the relationship of the 2 stages and, in particular, explain how the methods of investigation and findings of the first stage were used to design and carry out the second stage;

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (c) provide a compilation and presentation of all field observations, field measurement and analytical data and laboratory analytical data;

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (d) provide interpretation and evaluation of the data in a manner which clearly shows

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (i)  the contamination in soil, groundwater, sediments and surface water in relation to the criteria, standards and conditions prescribed in this regulation, and

heading: Preliminary site investigations
paragraph: (ii)  the general location and degree of contamination, including migration which may have occurred to adjoining properties.

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph:
59
		  (1) A person who is ordered to undertake a detailed site investigation under section 41 (1) of the Act must do one of the following:

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (a) carry out a preliminary site investigation before the detailed site investigation;

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (b) conduct a detailed site investigation in a manner which ensures that the information referred to in section 58 (1) is obtained.

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (2) A detailed site investigation must provide information necessary for conducting a risk assessment, if applicable, and for developing a remediation plan, and must, without limitation, include procedures to

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (a) identify which substances may cause or threaten to cause adverse effects and provide any applicable information on their form,

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (b) identify the specific areas, depths and degree of contamination on the site including areas and extent of migration if applicable, and

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (c) evaluate contamination relative to the standards in this regulation.

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (3) A report of a detailed site investigation prepared under section 41 (1) of the Act must do all of the following:

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (a) describe the relationship of the detailed site investigation and any prior preliminary site investigation and, in particular, explain how the methods of investigation and findings of the preliminary site investigation were used to design and carry out the detailed site investigation;

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (b) provide a compilation and presentation of all field observations, field measurement and analytical data and laboratory analytical data;

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (c) provide an interpretation and evaluation of the data in a manner which clearly shows

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (i)  the contamination in soil, groundwater, sediments or surface water in relation to the criteria, standards and conditions prescribed in this regulation, and

heading: Detailed site investigations
paragraph: (ii)  specific areas, depths and degree of contamination, including migration which may have occurred to adjoining properties.

heading: Summary of site investigations and remediation plans
paragraph:
60
		  Any preliminary site investigation report, detailed site investigation report or remediation plan submitted to a director for approval must include a summary of the report or plan for the purpose of entry on the site registry in a format which may be specified in a director's protocol.

heading: Notification of neighbouring site owners after site investigations
paragraph:
60.1
		  (1) A responsible person who carries out a site investigation that discloses that one or more substances has migrated or is likely to have migrated to a neighbouring site and is or is likely causing contamination of the neighbouring site must provide written notification described in subsection (2).

heading: Notification of neighbouring site owners after site investigations
paragraph: (2) The responsible person for the investigated site must provide written notification to the person or persons who own the neighbouring site and a copy of the notification to the director, within 15 days after the responsible person becomes aware of the migration or likely migration of each substance to the neighbouring site, giving

heading: Notification of neighbouring site owners after site investigations
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the person or persons who own the investigated site,

heading: Notification of neighbouring site owners after site investigations
paragraph: (b) the name, address and telephone number of the person to contact regarding the investigation, and

heading: Notification of neighbouring site owners after site investigations
paragraph: (c) a general description of the nature of the migration or likely migration of each substance.

heading: Criteria for determining orphan sites
paragraph:
61
		  A director may determine that a contaminated site is an orphan site if the contaminated site is a site for which

heading: Criteria for determining orphan sites
paragraph: (a) a responsible person cannot be found or is not willing or financially able to carry out remediation in a time frame specified by a director, or

heading: Criteria for determining orphan sites
paragraph: (b) a government body has become the owner subsequent to the failure of the former owner or other responsible person to comply with a requirement to carry out remediation at the site.

heading: High risk orphan sites
paragraph:
62
		  For the purposes of section 58 (1) (b) of the Act, the determination that an orphan site is a high risk orphan site must be made in accordance with a classification system in a director's protocol.

heading: Professional statements
paragraph:
63
		  A director need not consider an application for

heading: Professional statements
paragraph: (a) an approval in principle,

heading: Professional statements
paragraph: (b) a certificate of compliance, or

heading: Professional statements
paragraph: (d) an approval of a preliminary or detailed site investigation

heading: Professional statements
paragraph: until the applicant or the applicant's agent provides a written signed statement that

heading: Professional statements
paragraph: (e) any documentation in support of an application referred to in paragraphs (a) to (d) has been prepared in accordance with all requirements in the Act and the regulations, and

heading: Professional statements
paragraph: (f) certifies that the person signing the statement has demonstrable experience in remediation of the type of contamination at the site for which the statement applies and is familiar with the remediation carried out on the site.

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph:
67
		  For the purposes of protocols established under section 64 (1) of the Act, a director may establish protocols in respect of the following matters:

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph: (a) establishing the form of a summary of site condition;

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph: (b) establishing procedures for defining and determining the boundaries of a site;

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph: (c) establishing procedures for determining

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph: (i)  whether multiple land uses apply at a site, and

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph: (ii)  if multiple lands uses apply at a site, which land uses apply;

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph: (d) establishing procedures for testing or analyzing soil, water or other media to estimate the leachate from substances;

heading: Director's protocols
paragraph: (e) developing soil, sediment, water or vapour numerical standards for a substance.

heading: Review of numerical standards
paragraph:
68
		  (1) For the purpose of prescribing substances and risk-based or numerical criteria, standards and conditions under section 63 (1) (n) of the Act, the minister may, within 5 years of this section coming into force and once every 5 years after that date, consider the recommendations by a director made under subsection (2) of this section and conduct a review of the numerical standards.

heading: Review of numerical standards
paragraph: (2) Recommendations of the director under subsection (1) are to be developed in accordance with a protocol established under

heading: Review of numerical standards
paragraph: (a) section 64 (2) (n) of the Act, and

heading: Review of numerical standards
paragraph: (b) section 67 (e) of this regulation.

heading: Manner of publication
paragraph:
69
		  For the purposes of section 63 (1) (r) of the Act, a protocol referred to in section 64 (2) of the Act must be published by being published on a website maintained by or on behalf of the government.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
70
		  In respect of matters subject to approval, determination or other consideration by a director under this regulation, if a person has submitted the required documentation in substantial compliance with this regulation before November 1, 2017, the director may apply the numerical criteria, standards and conditions that were in effect immediately before that date.

heading: Transition - wide area site
paragraph:
71
		  If a designation by the director of a site as a wide area site with respect to specified substances and specified sources is in effect immediately before this section comes into force,

heading: Transition - wide area site
paragraph: (a) the site is deemed to be designated by the director as an environmental management area with respect to those substances and sources, and

heading: Transition - wide area site
paragraph: (b) a reference to the site as a wide area site in a document or other record made or issued under the Act or this regulation before this section comes into force is deemed to be a reference to the site as an environmental management area.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "accredited zoo or aquarium" means a zoo or an aquarium that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is accredited by Canada's Accredited Zoos and Aquariums, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) provides proof to the satisfaction of the director of meeting or exceeding the accreditation standards set by Canada's Accredited Zoos and Aquariums;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Wildlife Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aircraft" has the same meaning as in section 95 (1) of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic invasive species individual" means a single member of an aquatic invasive species;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "BC waters" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any part of a body of water that is located in British Columbia,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) fish habitat as defined in the Water Sustainability Regulation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a stream as defined in the Water Sustainability Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a ditch, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) any of the following that may leak, drain or empty, directly or indirectly, into any part of a body of water, fish habitat, stream or ditch referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d):

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a naturally-formed pool of water other than one referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a storm drain, sewer or other artificial conduit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  a tank or other container that holds or is intended to hold water or wastewater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "certified educational institution" means a body that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is an educational body within the meaning of paragraph (a), (c), (d) or (d.1) of Schedule 1 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) holds a valid Certificate of Good Animal Practice issued by the Canadian Council on Animal Care;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "certified research institution" means a body that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) holds a valid Certificate of Good Animal Practice issued by the Canadian Council on Animal Care, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) publishes the results of original research in a peer-reviewed scientific journal at least once each year;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "contaminated jurisdiction" means one or more of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a jurisdiction listed in Schedule 5;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a province of Canada that is not listed in Schedule 5 but has within its jurisdiction one or more bodies of water that are contaminated with mussels;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a state of the United States of America that is not listed in Schedule 5 but has within its jurisdiction one or more bodies of water that are contaminated with mussels;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mussel" means a single member of an aquatic invasive species designated in Schedule 4;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mussel prevention measure" means a measure taken by an officer under section 9.03 of this regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mussel prevention order" means an order issued by an officer under section 9.04 of this regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "prohibited species individual" means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in Schedule 1, at any developmental stage;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in section 1 (1) or (2) of Schedule 2 that is 3 metres or more in length when measured from the front of the snout to the tip of the tail while the animal is fully extended;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in section 1 (3) of Schedule 2 that is 2 metres or more in length when measured from the front of the snout to the tip of the tail while the animal is fully extended;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "release" includes, for the purpose of applying section 7 (3) [prohibitions] of this regulation and section 77 (2) [fail to make reasonable effort to recover escaped animal] of the Act to a mussel, allowing the mussel to come into contact with BC waters;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "restricted species individual" means a single live member of a controlled alien species designated in Schedule 2, at any developmental stage, but does not include a prohibited species individual;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "water-related equipment" has the same meaning as in section 95 (1) of the Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) In Schedules 1 to 4, if a reference to a species is followed by italicized text in square brackets that is or purports to be descriptive of the species, the italicized text in square brackets is not part of this regulation and is to be considered to have been added editorially for convenience of reference only.

heading: Designation of species as controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: 2		  (1) For the purposes of paragraph (a) of the definition of "controlled alien species" in section 1 (1) [definitions] of the Act, the species listed in Schedules 1, 2, 3 and 4 of this regulation are designated as controlled alien species.

heading: Designation of species as controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of the definition of "aquatic invasive species" in section 1 (1) of the Act, the species listed in Schedules 3 and 4 of this regulation are designated as aquatic invasive species.

heading: Possession
paragraph:
3
		  A person must not possess a prohibited species individual unless the person holds a permit authorizing the possession of that prohibited species individual.

heading: Breeding
paragraph:
4
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person who possesses a prohibited species individual must prevent the prohibited species individual from breeding.

heading: Breeding
paragraph: (2) A person who possesses a prohibited species individual may allow the prohibited species individual to breed if

heading: Breeding
paragraph: (a) the person

heading: Breeding
paragraph: (i)  operates an accredited zoo or aquarium,

heading: Breeding
paragraph: (ii)  is a certified educational institution, or

heading: Breeding
paragraph: (iii)  is a certified research institution,

heading: Breeding
paragraph: (b) the person holds a permit authorizing the person to allow that prohibited species individual to breed, and

heading: Breeding
paragraph: (c) the breeding is in accordance with a management plan approved by a regional manager.

heading: Release prohibited
paragraph:
5
		  A person must not release a restricted species individual or prohibited species individual or allow a restricted species individual or prohibited species individual to be released, or to escape.

heading: Shipping or transportation
paragraph:
5.1
		  A person must not ship or transport in British Columbia a prohibited species individual unless the person holds a permit authorizing the shipping or transportation of the prohibited species individual.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of the following sections commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) section 3 [prohibition against possession of prohibited species];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) section 4 (1) [prohibition against prohibited species breeding];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) section 5;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) section 5.1.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) An offence under subsection (1) (b) or (c) is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (a) (ii) [determining fines and penalties for offences] of the Act.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) An offence under subsection (1) (a) is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (b) (ii) of the Act.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph:
7
		  (1) A person must not possess an aquatic invasive species individual.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) A person who possesses an aquatic invasive species individual must prevent the aquatic invasive species individual from breeding.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) A person must not

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) release into BC waters an aquatic invasive species individual, or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) allow an aquatic invasive species individual to be released, or to escape, into BC waters.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (4) A person must not ship or transport in British Columbia an aquatic invasive species individual.

heading: Mandatory opening of drainage holes, valves and devices for transport
paragraph:
7.01
		  (1) A person must not transport, on land, a boat unless

heading: Mandatory opening of drainage holes, valves and devices for transport
paragraph: (a) all drainage holes, valves or other devices used to drain water from the boat are left open, other than holes, valves or devices used in kitchen or washroom facilities on the boat, or

heading: Mandatory opening of drainage holes, valves and devices for transport
paragraph: (b) the boat is transported in an inverted manner and the interior of the boat is drained, including draining any ballast tanks, bilge areas or compartments.

heading: Mandatory opening of drainage holes, valves and devices for transport
paragraph: (2) A person must not transport, on land, water-related equipment unless all drainage holes, valves or other devices used to drain water from the equipment are left open.

heading: Mandatory opening of drainage holes, valves and devices for transport
paragraph: (3) A person must not transport, on land, an aircraft designed to land on water unless all drainage holes, valves or other devices used to drain water from the aircraft's pontoons are left open, other than holes, valves or devices used in washroom facilities on the aircraft.

heading: Application of Act to dead mussels
paragraph:
7.1
		  The following sections of the Act apply as if a dead mussel were wildlife or an animal:

heading: Application of Act to dead mussels
paragraph: (a) section 33 (2) [offence to possess dead wildlife unless authorized];

heading: Application of Act to dead mussels
paragraph: (b) section 37 [offence to transport wildlife unless authorized];

heading: Application of Act to dead mussels
paragraph: (c) section 77 (2) [offence to release or abandon animal].

heading: Certified educational and research institutions exempt
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A certified educational institution and a certified research institution are exempt from

heading: Certified educational and research institutions exempt
paragraph: (a) the prohibitions set out in section 7 (1) and (4), and

heading: Certified educational and research institutions exempt
paragraph: (b) the requirement set out in section 7 (2).

heading: Certified educational and research institutions exempt
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the prohibitions set out in section 7 (1) and (4) in respect of a dead mussel if

heading: Certified educational and research institutions exempt
paragraph: (a) the dead mussel is fully encased in an acrylic resin or similar material, and

heading: Certified educational and research institutions exempt
paragraph: (b) the person is using the dead mussel for an educational or public awareness purpose.

heading: Officer uniform and identification required
paragraph:
9.01
		  An officer must be wearing an officer's official uniform or displaying an officer's official identification for the purposes of one or more of the following:

heading: Officer uniform and identification required
paragraph: (a) taking a mussel prevention measure in accordance with section 9.03;

heading: Officer uniform and identification required
paragraph: (b) issuing a mussel prevention order in accordance with section 9.04;

heading: Officer uniform and identification required
paragraph: (c) enforcing an offence under section 10 [offences].

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph:
9.02
		  An officer may take a mussel prevention measure or issue a mussel prevention order in respect of a vehicle, aircraft designed to land on water or boat or any water-related equipment if one or more of the following circumstances exist:

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (a) the officer inspected the vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment and determined that the vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (i)  may be or may have been contaminated with mussels, or

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (ii)  may be or may have been contaminated with suspected mussels;

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (b) the vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment is owned, or is registered, licensed, insured or otherwise authorized to be possessed or operated, in a contaminated jurisdiction;

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (c) the officer has reason to believe that the vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment was operated in, or otherwise came into contact with, water that is contaminated with mussels or water that is potentially contaminated with mussels;

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (d) the officer has reason to believe that a person may be in violation of one or more of the following provisions with respect to mussels:

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (i)  section 7 [prohibitions] of this regulation;

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (ii)  section 7.01 [mandatory opening of drainage holes, valves and devices for transport] of this regulation;

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (iii)  section 33 (2) [offence to possess dead wildlife unless authorized] of the Act;

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (iv)  section 37 [offence to transport wildlife unless authorized] of the Act;

heading: Grounds for mussel prevention measure or order
paragraph: (v)  section 77 (2) [offence to release or abandon animal] of the Act.

heading: Mussel prevention measures
paragraph:
9.03
		  An officer may take one or more of the following mussel prevention measures in respect of a vehicle, aircraft designed to land on water or boat or any water-related equipment:

heading: Mussel prevention measures
paragraph: (a) decontaminate all or part of the vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment;

heading: Mussel prevention measures
paragraph: (b) apply a seal to an aircraft or boat or any equipment.

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph:
9.04
		  (1) An officer may issue a mussel prevention order requiring a person to do one or more of the following in respect of a vehicle, aircraft designed to land on water or boat or any water-related equipment:

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (a) remove mussels or suspected mussels, within a period of time specified in the order, from the vehicle, aircraft or boat or equipment;

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (b) comply with any written directions contained or attached to the order with respect to the removal of mussels or suspected mussels;

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (c) ensure that the vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment does not come into contact with BC waters for

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (i)  a period of time specified in the order, or

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (ii)  until a condition specified in the order is satisfied;

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (d) report, within a period of time and in the manner specified in the order, with one or both of the following:

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (i)  proof, satisfactory to an officer, of compliance with the order;

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (ii)  the vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment that is the subject of the order, for the purposes of further inspection by an officer.

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (2) An officer may issue a mussel prevention order requiring a person to do one or more of the following in respect of an aircraft designed to land on water or boat or any water-related equipment:

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (a) remove a drainage plug, valve or device used to drain water in or on the aircraft, boat or equipment;

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (b) leave open, for a period of time specified in the order, a drainage plug, valve or device used to drain water in or on the aircraft, boat or equipment;

heading: Mussel prevention orders
paragraph: (c) ensure that a seal applied by an officer is not altered or removed from the aircraft, boat or equipment unless the removal is directed or completed by an officer.

heading: Interference with prevention measure
paragraph:
9.05
		  A person must not interfere with an officer who is taking or attempting to take a mussel prevention measure.

heading: Compliance with mussel prevention order
paragraph:
9.06
		  (1) A person to whom a mussel prevention order is issued must comply with the order.

heading: Compliance with mussel prevention order
paragraph: (2) A person to whom a mussel prevention order is issued must ensure that the subject vehicle, aircraft designed to land on water, boat or water-related equipment of the order does not come into contact with BC waters until the order is complied with.

heading: Compliance with mussel prevention order
paragraph: (3) A person who engages in procedures to remove mussels or suspected mussels must ensure that the water used in those procedures does not come into contact with BC waters.

heading: Immediate destruction
paragraph:
9.1
		  The disposal power set out in section 97.3 [if perishable wildlife seized] of the Act applies to an aquatic invasive species individual as if the aquatic invasive species individual were wildlife.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: authorized carrier means, as the case may be,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a carrier that, in accordance with the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and the regulations under that Act, transports - or is to transport - hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material by means of a boat, ship or craft designed, used or capable of being used solely or partly for navigation in, on, through or immediately above water; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a carrier that transports - or is to transport - hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material in accordance with the requirements of the jurisdiction in which the waste or recyclable material is transported. (transporteur agree)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: authorized facility means a facility that is authorized by the authorities of the jurisdiction in which it is located to dispose of hazardous waste by means of a disposal operation set out in column 2 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 or to recycle hazardous recyclable material by means of a recycling operation set out in column 2 of Part 2 of Schedule 1. (installation agreee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canada-USA Agreement means the Agreement Between the Government of Canada and the Government of the United States of America Concerning the Transboundary Movement of Hazardous Waste, which entered into force on November 8, 1986, as amended from time to time. (accord Canada - Etats-Unis)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: CAS Registry Number means the identification number assigned to a substance by the Chemical Abstracts Service Division of the American Chemical Society. (numero d'enregistrement CAS)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: competent authority means, in the case of a country that is a party to the Convention or is subject to OECD Decision C(2001)107/FINAL, the authority that is designated as the competent authority by that country under the Convention or under OECD Decision C(2001)107/FINAL, as the case may be, and, in the case of the United States, the United States Environmental Protection Agency. (autorite competente)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: consignee means a person that receives or is to receive delivery from a consignor of a shipment that contains hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material at a site that they own, operate or otherwise control. (destinataire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: consignor means a person that, on their own behalf or on behalf of another person under an agreement or arrangement with that person, sends or is to send a shipment that contains hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material from a site that is located in a province to a site that is located in another province and that is owned, operated or otherwise controlled by a consignee. (expediteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: contract means a contract - or, if all of the parties are the same legal entity, an arrangement among those parties - that is in writing and is signed and, if parties are the same legal entity that is doing business in both Canada and another country, is signed by the representatives of that entity in both countries. (contrat)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Convention means the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and Their Disposal, which entered into force on May 5, 1992. (Convention)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environmentally hazardous constituent means a constituent that is contained in a leachate and is set out in column 3 of Schedule 2 in a concentration that is determined to be equal to or greater than the concentration set out in column 4 of that Schedule in accordance with Method 1311: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure, as set out in Test Methods for Evaluating Solid Waste, Physical/Chemical Methods, SW-846, Third Edition, published by the United States Environmental Protection Agency. (constituant dangereux pour l'environnement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: final disposal operation means a disposal operation set out in column 2 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 that bears one of the disposal codes D1 to D12, DC1 and DC2 set out in column 1 of that Part. (operation finale d'elimination)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: final recycling operation means a recycling operation set out in column 2 of Part 2 of Schedule 1 that bears one of the recycling codes R1 to R11, RC1 and RC2 set out in column 1 of that Part. (operation finale de recyclage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: foreign exporter means a person, including a government entity, in a foreign country that exports hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material from that country for import into, or conveyance in transit through, Canada. (exportateur etranger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: foreign importer means a person, including a government entity, in a foreign country that imports into that country hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material that is exported from, or conveyed in transit through, Canada. (importateur etranger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: interim disposal operation means a disposal operation set out in column 2 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 that bears one of the disposal codes D13 to D15 set out in column 1 of that Part. (operation prealable d'elimination)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: interim recycling operation means a recycling operation set out in column 2 of Part 2 of Schedule 1 that bears one of the recycling codes R12, R13 and RC3 set out in column 1 of that Part. (operation prealable de recyclage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: line entry means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in respect of a notification, an entry that appears on a separate numbered line in the notification with respect to a type of hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material that is to be transported under the permit and that includes that line number and the information set out in subparagraphs 1(j)(i) to (iii), 2(j)(i) to (iii), 3(i)(i) to (iii), 4(i)(i) to (iii), 5(j)(i) to (iii) or 6(j)(i) to (iii) of Schedule 3, as the case may be;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in respect of a movement document referred to in Part 1, an entry that appears on a separate numbered line in the movement document with respect to a type of hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material that is to be transported under a permit and that includes that line number, the reference number of the notification for the permit and the line entry for that type of hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material that is set out in the notification, with the exception of the information set out in clauses 1(j)(iii)(A), (F) and (L), 2(j)(iii)(A), (F) and (L), 3(i)(iii)(A), (F) and (L), 4(i)(iii)(A), (F) and (L), 5(j)(iii)(A), (E) and (K) or 6(j)(iii)(A), (E) and (K) of Schedule 3, as the case may be; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in respect of a movement document referred to in Part 2, an entry that appears on a separate numbered line in the movement document with respect to a type of hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material that is to be shipped from a consignor to a site that is owned, operated or otherwise controlled by a consignee and that includes that line number and the information set out in paragraph 1(g) of Schedule 4. (ligne de renseignements)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: movement document means, with respect to a shipment of hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material, a document that is referred to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in sections 15 and 16, if the shipment is imported to Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in sections 27 and 28, if the shipment is exported from Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in sections 39 and 40, if the shipment is exported from Canada and is imported to Canada after it is conveyed in transit through a foreign country;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) in sections 49 and 50, if the shipment is conveyed in transit through Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) in sections 60 and 61, if the hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material is returned to Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) in sections 71 and 72, if the hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material is returned to a foreign country of origin; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) in section 80, if the shipment is moved within Canada. (document de mouvement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: municipality means an incorporated city, town, village, metropolitan authority, township, district, county or rural municipality in Canada. (municipalite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: notification means a notification referred to in paragraph 185(1)(a) of the Act. (notification)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: OECD Decision C(2001)107/FINAL means Decision C(2001)107/FINAL of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development, entitled Decision of the Council Concerning the Revision of Decision C(92)39/FINAL on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Wastes Destined for Recovery Operations, dated February 25, 2002. (decision C(2001)107/FINAL de l'OCDE)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: PCB means polychlorinated biphenyl. (BPC)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: permit means a permit referred to in paragraph 185(1)(b) of the Act. (permis)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: persistent organic pollutant means a substance set out in column 3 of Schedule 5 that is contained in hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material, if the concentration is equal to or greater than the concentration set out in column 4 of that Schedule. (substance polluante organique persistante)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: receiving facility means the first authorized facility that receives or is to receive hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material for disposal or recycling under a permit or permits, whether the disposal or recycling operation that is to be performed at that facility is interim or final. heading: Definitions
paragraph: recyclable material means anything that is to be recycled. (matiere recyclable)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: shipment means cargo, in one or more containers or in bulk, that is transported as a unit without being separated at any time during the movement and that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in the case of a return to Canada or to a foreign country of origin, is shipped to the facility from which it was originally shipped or to the facility identified in the permit for the return;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in the case of a movement within Canada, is shipped by a consignor to a site that is located in another province and that is owned, operated or otherwise controlled by a consignee; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in any other case, is shipped by one person from one facility in the country of origin to a receiving facility in the country of destination. (envoi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sign includes to sign by means of an electronic signature that is generated using a technology or process that is approved by the Minister for the purposes of submitting information to the Minister online. (signature)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: unique identification number means a number assigned by a province or a country to identify a person, entity or facility. (numero d'identification unique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: waste means anything that is to be disposed of. (dechet)

heading: Definition of hazardous waste
paragraph: 2 (1) For the purposes of Division 8 of Part 7 and Part 10 of the Act and these Regulations, hazardous waste means anything that is to be disposed of using one of the operations set out in column 2 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 and that

heading: Definition of hazardous waste
paragraph: (a) is set out in column 2 of Schedule 6;

heading: Definition of hazardous waste
paragraph: (b) meets the criteria for inclusion in one of Classes 2 to 6, 8 and 9 as set out in Part 2 of the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations;

heading: Definition of hazardous waste
paragraph: (c) contains a substance set out in column 3 of Schedule 7 that is in a concentration equal to or greater than the concentration set out in column 4 of that Schedule;

heading: Definition of hazardous waste
paragraph: (d) produces a leachate that contains an environmentally hazardous constituent set out in column 3 of Schedule 2 that is in a concentration equal to or greater than the concentration set out in column 4 of that Schedule; or

heading: Definition of hazardous waste
paragraph: (e) is set out in column 3 of Schedule 8, is either pure or the only active ingredient and is unused.

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (2) Hazardous waste referred to in subsection (1) does not include anything

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (a) that is to be transported in a quantity of less than 5 kg or 5 L per shipment, unless it contains mercury or meets the criteria for inclusion in Class 6.2 as set out in Part 2 of the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (b) that remains in a container that is to be transported after the contents of that container have been removed to the maximum extent feasible and before the container is either refilled or cleaned of its residual contents;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (c) that is mingled with non-hazardous waste or non-hazardous recyclable material and collected as part of the regular collection of non-hazardous waste and non-hazardous recyclable material by or on behalf of a municipality, unless it is separated from that waste or recyclable material during or after the collection;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (d) that is personal or household waste of the individual who transports it; or

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (e) that is generated from the normal operations of a ship and whose discharge is authorized under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Waste considered hazardous for export
paragraph: 3 (1) Anything that is to be disposed of using one of the operations set out in column 2 of Part 1 of Schedule 1, even if it is not hazardous waste within the meaning of subsection 2(1), is considered to be hazardous waste for the purposes of Division 8 of Part 7 and Part 10 of the Act and Divisions 1 to 4, 7 and 8 of Part 1 of these Regulations if it is to be exported to a country of destination or conveyed in transit through Canada or a foreign country and

heading: Waste considered hazardous for export
paragraph: (a) it is defined as, or considered to be, hazardous under the legislation of the country of destination or country of transit;

heading: Waste considered hazardous for export
paragraph: (b) its import is prohibited under the legislation of the country of destination; or

heading: Waste considered hazardous for export
paragraph: (c) it is one of the hazardous wastes referred to in Article 1, subparagraph 1(a) of the Convention or of the other wastes referred to in Article 1, paragraph 2 of the Convention, with the exception of wastes referred to in Article 1, paragraphs 3 and 4 of the Convention - as it read on May 5, 1992, as amended from time to time, to the extent that the amendments are binding on Canada - and the country of destination is a party to the Convention.

heading: Waste considered hazardous for return to foreign country of origin
paragraph: (2) Anything that is to be disposed of using one of the operations set out in column 2 of Part 1 of Schedule 1, even if it is not hazardous waste within the meaning of subsection 2(1), is considered to be hazardous waste for the purposes of Division 8 of Part 7 and Part 10 of the Act and Division 6 of Part 1 of these Regulations if it is to be conveyed in transit through a foreign country and it is defined as, or considered to be, hazardous under the legislation of that country.

heading: Definition of hazardous recyclable material
paragraph: 4 (1) For the purposes of Division 8 of Part 7 and Part 10 of the Act and these Regulations, hazardous recyclable material means anything that is to be recycled using one of the operations set out in column 2 of Part 2 of Schedule 1 and that

heading: Definition of hazardous recyclable material
paragraph: (a) is set out in column 2 of Schedule 6;

heading: Definition of hazardous recyclable material
paragraph: (b) meets the criteria for inclusion in one of Classes 2 to 6, 8 and 9 as set out in Part 2 of the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations;

heading: Definition of hazardous recyclable material
paragraph: (c) contains a substance set out in column 3 of Schedule 7 that is in a concentration equal to or greater than the concentration set out in column 4 of that Schedule;

heading: Definition of hazardous recyclable material
paragraph: (d) produces a leachate that contains an environmentally hazardous constituent set out in column 3 of Schedule 2 that is in a concentration equal to or greater than the concentration set out in column 4 of that Schedule; or

heading: Definition of hazardous recyclable material
paragraph: (e) is set out in column 3 of Schedule 8, is either pure or the only active ingredient and is unused.

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of the provisions of Division 8 of Part 7 and Part 10 of the Act that relate to the import, export and conveyance in transit of hazardous recyclable material and for the purposes of Part 1 of these Regulations, hazardous recyclable material referred to in subsection (1) does not include anything

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (a) that is to be transported in a quantity of less than 5 kg or 5 L per shipment, unless it contains mercury or meets the criteria for inclusion in Class 6.2 as set out in Part 2 of the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations;

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (b) that remains in a container that is to be transported after the contents of that container have been removed to the maximum extent feasible and before the container is either refilled or cleaned of its residual contents;

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (c) that is mingled with non-hazardous waste or non-hazardous recyclable material and collected as part of the regular collection of non-hazardous waste and non-hazardous recyclable material by or on behalf of a municipality, unless it is separated from that waste or recyclable material during or after the collection;

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (d) that is personal or household recyclable material of the individual who transports it;

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (e) that is generated from the normal operations of a ship and whose discharge is authorized under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001;

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (f) that is to be imported from a country of origin, or exported to a country of destination, that is subject to OECD Decision C(2001)107/FINAL, and, if applicable, that is to be conveyed in transit only through a country that is subject to that Decision, if it

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (i) is to be imported or exported in a quantity of 25 kg or 25 L or less per shipment for the purpose of conducting analysis or research with respect to the recycling of that recyclable material,

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
paragraph: (ii) does not contain an infectious substance that meets the criteria for inclusion in Class 6.2 as set out in Part 2 of the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations, and

heading: Exclusions - import, export and transit
