heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "dike" means an embankment, wall, fill, piling, pump, gate, floodbox, pipe, sluice, culvert, canal, ditch, drain or any other thing that is constructed, assembled or installed to prevent the flooding of land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "diking authority" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the commissioners of a district to which Part 2 of the Drainage, Ditch and Dike Act applies,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person owning or controlling a dike other than a private dike,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b.1) if the final agreement of a treaty first nation so provides, the treaty first nation in relation to dikes on its treaty lands,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a public authority designated by the minister as having any responsibility for maintenance of a dike other than a private dike, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a regional district, a municipality or an improvement district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "improvement district" means an improvement district within the meaning of the Local Government Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "inspector" means the inspector of dikes referred to in section 2 and includes any acting, deputy or assistant inspectors of dikes;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipality" means a municipality as defined for the purposes of the Community Charter;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "order" includes any direction, decision or order of the inspector under this Act, including a decision to grant or refuse an approval under section 2 (4);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "private dike" means a dike built on private property that protects only that property.

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: 2		  (1) The office of the inspector of dikes is continued under this section.

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (2) The inspector may

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (a) enter on any land and on a dike, with or without equipment, as necessary to carry out the purposes of this Act,

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (b) require a diking authority or a person on whose land a dike, other than a private dike, is located to repair, replace, renew, alter, add to, improve or remove a dike, or a part of a dike, or anything used in connection with a dike,

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (c) require a diking authority or a person on whose land a dike, other than a private dike, is located to construct or install a work or thing that in the opinion of the inspector is necessary to protect a dike or to increase its efficiency,

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (d) authorize and empower any diking authority or person, on conditions the inspector may impose, to

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (i)  place, construct, renew, alter, repair, maintain, operate and use any buildings, structures, machinery, ways, rails, roads, pipes, poles, towers, cables, wires, conduits, conveyors or other works on, along, across, through, over or under any dike, other than a private dike, or any land on which a dike is located, other than a private dike, and

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (ii)  enter with or without equipment onto a dike, other than a private dike, or on land on which a dike is located, other than a private dike, for the purposes set out in subparagraph (i) or section 3,

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (e) require a diking authority to provide routine or special reports on the construction or maintenance of dikes for which the diking authority is responsible,

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (f) inspect or make an order for the inspection of any books or records in connection with the construction or maintenance of dikes in the possession or control of a diking authority,

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (g) carry out or order an audit of a diking authority's program of construction and maintenance of dikes for which the diking authority is responsible, and

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (h) subject to this Act and the regulations, do any other thing or require a diking authority to do any other thing relative to the construction and maintenance of dikes, including orders respecting flood hazard planning.

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (3) The inspector and those employees considered necessary may be appointed under the Public Service Act.

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (4) A person or a diking authority must not do any of the following unless it is done either with the prior written approval of the inspector or in accordance with the regulations made under section 8 (2):

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (a) lower, or cause or allow to be lowered, the elevation of a dike or decrease, or cause or allow to be decreased, the width or cross section of a dike;

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (b) install, or cause or allow to be installed, any culvert, pipe, flood box or any structure through a dike;

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (c) construct, or cause or allow to be constructed, any works on or over a dike or dike right of way;

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (d) alter, or cause or allow to be altered, the foreshore or stream channel adjacent to a dike;

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (e) construct a new dike.

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (5) In granting an approval under subsection (4), the inspector must consider the appropriateness of a standard established by regulation under section 8 (2) in relation to the dike that is the subject of the request, in light of

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (a) the condition and location of the dike,

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (b) the surrounding land and bodies of water and stream channels that are in close proximity to the dike, and

heading: Inspector of dikes
paragraph: (c) the nature and condition of works related to the dike.

heading: Orders made by inspector
paragraph: 2.1		  (1) In this section, "registered mail" includes any method of mail delivery provided by Canada Post for which confirmation of delivery to a named person is available.

heading: Orders made by inspector
paragraph: (2) An order made by the inspector must be

heading: Orders made by inspector
paragraph: (a) in writing, signed by the inspector, and

heading: Orders made by inspector
paragraph: (b) delivered or sent by registered mail to the last known address of the person or diking authority to whom it is directed.

heading: Orders made by inspector
paragraph: (3) Anything sent by registered mail for the purposes of this Act is deemed to be received by the person to whom it is addressed on the 14th day after deposit with Canada Post, unless the person received actual service before that day.

heading: Orders made by inspector
paragraph: (4) The inspector may, at any time on notice to the person or diking authority to whom the order was directed, amend or revoke any order of the inspector.

heading: Failure to carry out an order of the inspector
paragraph:
3
		  (1) If a person or diking authority fails to carry out an order of the inspector

heading: Failure to carry out an order of the inspector
paragraph: (a) by the date specified in the order, or

heading: Failure to carry out an order of the inspector
paragraph: (b) to the satisfaction of the inspector,

heading: Failure to carry out an order of the inspector
paragraph: the inspector may take steps to fulfill the requirements of the order or authorize or employ another person to do so.

heading: Failure to carry out an order of the inspector
paragraph: (2) If the inspector acts under subsection (1), any expense incurred by the inspector in fulfilling the requirements of the order or in authorizing or employing another person to do so, including any interest the inspector may have to pay, is a debt owing to the government by the person or diking authority to whom the order was directed.

heading: Failure to carry out an order of the inspector
paragraph: (3) A debt owing under subsection (2) may be recovered in any court by the government from the person or diking authority to whom the order was directed.

heading: Failure to carry out an order of the inspector
paragraph: (4) In an action referred to in subsection (3), the inspector's certificate as to the amount of the expense is evidence of the amount of the debt owing and of the necessity of doing the work authorized under this section.

heading: Appeals
paragraph:
5
		  (1) Subject to subsection (1.1), an appeal lies to the minister from every order of the inspector.

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (1.1) An appeal must not be taken

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (a) from an order of the inspector requiring a person or a diking authority to comply with standards established by regulation under section 8 (2), unless the person or the diking authority to whom the order was directed is not responsible for the dike that is the subject of the order, or

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (b) from a decision of the inspector refusing to grant an approval under section 2 (4).

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (2) An appeal under this section must be taken within 15 days from the date on which the inspector makes the order appealed from.

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (3) An appeal is taken within the meaning of this section when notice of intention to appeal has been delivered to the minister and a copy delivered to the inspector.

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (4) The appellant must give such further notice of the appellant's intention to appeal as may be directed by the inspector.

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (5) On an appeal under this section, the minister may confirm, quash, vary or add to the order appealed from and make any order as to costs that the minister considers just.

heading: Appeals
paragraph: (6) The minister's decision under subsection (5) is final.

heading: Offence
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A person or a diking authority commits an offence if that person or diking authority does any of the following:

heading: Offence
paragraph: (a) injures or interferes with a dike or its operation;

heading: Offence
paragraph: (b) hinders a diking authority, the inspector or a person acting on behalf of either of them from protecting property from flooding;

heading: Offence
paragraph: (c) contravenes section 2 (4) or an order of the inspector or the minister.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (2) A person or diking authority who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction

heading: Offence
paragraph: (a) to a fine of not more than $200 000, and

heading: Offence
paragraph: (b) if the offence is a continuing one, to a fine of not more than $200 000 for each day the offence is continued

heading: Offence
paragraph: or to imprisonment not exceeding 12 months, or to both a fine and imprisonment.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (3) If a person or diking authority commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the person or diking authority who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence even though the person or diking authority is convicted.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (4) The time limit for laying an information respecting an offence under this Act is 2 years after the facts on which the information is based first comes to the knowledge of the inspector.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (5) A document purporting to have been issued by the inspector, certifying the day on which the inspector became aware of the facts on which an information is based, is admissible without proof of the signature or official character of the individual appearing to have signed the document and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the matter certified.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (6) A proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under this Act does not relieve a person or diking authority from any other liability.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
6.1
		  (1) If a person or diking authority is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any punishment imposed, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person or diking authority from doing any act or engaging in any activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (b) directing the person or diking authority to take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (c) directing the person or diking authority to pay the government an amount of money as compensation, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken by or caused to be taken on behalf of the government as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (d) directing the person or diking authority to perform community service;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (e) directing the person or diking authority to pay an amount of money the court considers appropriate to

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (i)  the trustee under Part 3 of the Wildlife Act for inclusion in the trust property, as that term is defined in section 118 of that Act, or

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (ii)  any other prescribed trust fund;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (f) directing the person or diking authority to post a bond or pay into court an amount of money the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (g) directing the person or diking authority to submit to the minister, on application by the minister within 3 years of the date of the conviction, any information respecting the activities of the person or diking authority that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (h) directing the person or diking authority to publish, in any manner the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (i) requiring the person or diking authority to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the person's or diking authority's good conduct and for preventing the person or diking authority from repeating the offence or committing other offences under this Act.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (2) If a person or diking authority fails to comply with an order referred to in subsection (1) (h) directing the person or diking authority to publish the facts relating to the commission of an offence, the minister may publish those facts and recover the costs of publication from the person or diking authority.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (3) If

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (a) an order under this section or section 6.2 directs a person or diking authority to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose, or

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (b) the minister incurs publication costs under subsection (2) of this section,

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: the amount and any interest payable on that amount constitute a debt due to the government and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: 6.2		  (1) An application for variation of an order under section 6.1 may be made to the court that made the order by

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (a) the Attorney General, or

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (b) the person or diking authority against whom the order under section 6.1 was made.

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (2) Before hearing an application under subsection (1), the court may order the applicant to give notice of the application in accordance with the directions of the court.

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (3) On an application under subsection (1), if the court considers variation appropriate because of a change in the circumstances, the court may make an order doing one or more of the following:

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (a) changing the original order or any conditions specified in it;

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (b) relieving the person or diking authority referred to in subsection (1) (b) absolutely or partially from compliance with all or part of the original order;

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (c) reducing the period for which the original order is to remain in effect;

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (d) extending the period for which the original order is to remain in effect, subject to the limit that this extension must not be longer than one year.

heading: Variation of section 6.1 orders
paragraph: (4) If an application under subsection (1) has been heard by a court, no other application may be made in respect of the order under section 6.1 except with leave of the court.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
8
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) establishing standards of construction, operation and maintenance in respect to the matters described in section 2, including but not limited to adopting any standard devised by any other body;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing trust funds to which a payment under section 6.1 (1) (e) may be made, if those trust funds include as a purpose or objective

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  the promotion of proper dike construction, maintenance or operation,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  the protection or restoration of the environment from or as a result of flooding,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iii)  the protection of persons or property from flooding, or

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iv)  a purpose similar to the trust purposes within the meaning of section 118 of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) A regulation under subsection (2) (a) may make different provisions for

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) different classes of dikes,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) different diking authorities, or

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) different classes of persons or diking authorities.

heading: National Action List
paragraph: 3 For the purposes of sections 9 and 10 of Schedule 6 to the Act, the National Action List mechanisms for screening waste or other matter shall consist of

heading: National Action List
paragraph: (a) with respect to the Lower Level, an assessment of the concentration of specified substances in the waste or other matter; and

heading: National Action List
paragraph: (b) with respect to the Upper Level, an assessment of biological responses.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: 4 Waste or other matter referred to in items 1 and 4 of Schedule 5 to the Act that contains any of the substances set out in column 1 of the table to this section, each at a concentration equal to or below the concentration set out in column 2, shall be considered to be below the Lower Level of the National Action List.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: TABLE LOWER LEVEL

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: 5 (1) Waste or other matter referred to in section 4 that contains any of the substances set out in column 1 of the table to that section at a concentration above the concentration set out in column 2, shall be assessed using three marine or estuarine biological tests for sediment assessment, namely, an acute lethality test and

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: (a) two sub-lethal tests; or

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: (b) one sub-lethal and one bioaccumulation test.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: (2) The acute lethality test shall be conducted using the test methodology entitled Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Sediment to Marine or Estuarine Amphipods (Reference Method EPS 1/RM/35), December 1998, published by the Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: (3) The sub-lethal tests shall be conducted using any of the test methodologies set out in Biological Test Method: Sublethal Toxicity Tests to Assess Sediments Intended for Disposal at Sea (Report; EPS 1/RM/40), May 2001, published by the Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: (4) The bioaccumulation test shall be conducted using the test methodology entitled Guidance Manual: Bedded Sediment Bioaccumulation Tests (EPA/600/R-93/183), September 1993, published by the United States Environmental Protection Agency, as amended from time to time.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: (5) The tests shall be performed, and their results interpreted, in accordance with generally accepted standards of good scientific practice at the time the tests are performed.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: 6 If the results of the three marine or estuarine biological tests set out in subsection 5(1) meet the criteria set out for those tests, the waste or other matter shall subsequently be considered to be below the Lower Level of the National Action List.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: 7 If the results of either the acute lethality test set out in subsection 5(1) or the two other tests set out in paragraph 5(1)(a) or (b) fail to meet the criteria set out for those tests, the waste or other matter shall be considered to be above the Upper Level of the National Action List.

heading: Mechanisms for Screening
paragraph: 8 If the results of the acute lethality test set out in subsection 5(1) and one of the tests set out in paragraph 5(1)(a) or (b) meet the criteria set out for those tests, the waste or other matter shall be considered to be below the Upper Level but above the Lower Level of the National Action List.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Dominion Water Power Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 In this Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Dominion water-powers means any water-powers on public lands, or any other water-powers that are the property of Canada and have been or may be placed under the administration of the Minister, but does not include water-powers on lands under the administration and control of the Commissioner of Yukon or the Northwest Territories; (forces hydrauliques du Canada)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Indigenous Services or, in relation to public lands in Nunavut, the Minister of Northern Affairs; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: public lands means lands belonging to Her Majesty in right of Canada and includes lands of which the Government of Canada has power to dispose but does not include lands under the administration and control of the Commissioner of Yukon or the Northwest Territories; (terres domaniales)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: stream or water means any river, brook, lake, pond, creek or other flowing or standing water; (cours d'eau ou eau)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: undertaking means the undertaking required or proposed to be established or carried on in pursuance of this Act or the regulations by Her Majesty or by any applicant, licensee or person in the development of any Dominion water-power or in the transmission, distribution or utilization of the force or energy produced from the water-power, and includes, in so far as authorized or required,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the storage, pondage, penning back, regulation, augmentation, carriage, diversion and use of water or of the flow thereof,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the generation of energy at any plant that is used as an auxiliary to the water-power plant,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the surveying, laying out, constructing, maintaining and operating of works, including dams, flumes, penstocks, power stations, transmission lines, terminal stations and substations,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the surveying of any public lands or other lands, the carrying on of investigations, and the collection of data,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) the acquisition and use of lands and properties or any interest therein,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) the administration and management of the required lands, works and properties, and the business connected therewith, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) matters incidental to any matters referred to in paragraphs (a) to (f); (entreprise)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: water-power includes any force or energy of whatever form or nature contained in or capable of being produced or generated from any flowing or falling water in such quantity as to make it of commercial value. (force hydraulique)

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: 3 This Act applies

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (a) to all Dominion water-powers;

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (b) to all public lands required in connection with the development or working of Dominion water-powers or for purposes incidental thereto;

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (c) to all lands and properties that may be acquired or authorized to be acquired under the terms and for the purposes of this Act, or may have been acquired and are still used or may be required in connection with Dominion water-powers;

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (d) to the power and energy produced or producible from the waters on or within the lands referred to in paragraph (c), whether the power or energy derived therefrom or any portion thereof is distributed or utilized on public lands or not;

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (e) to all undertakings established or carried on in respect of any Dominion water-powers; and

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (f) to all matters incidental to any matters referred to in paragraphs (a) to (e).

paragraph: (a) on or within which there is water-power,

heading: Essential lands also remain Crown property
paragraph: (b) required for the protection of any water-power, or

heading: Essential lands also remain Crown property
paragraph: (c) required for the purposes of any undertaking,

heading: Essential lands also remain Crown property
paragraph: and the water-powers and waters thereon shall not be open to entry, and except as otherwise provided in this Act, no interest therein shall be leased or otherwise granted or conveyed by the Crown.

heading: Idem
paragraph: (2) Any grant or conveyance made, on or after June 6, 1919, of any public lands referred to in subsection (1) or any interest therein, except in pursuance of this Act and the regulations, shall not vest in the grantee any exclusive or other property or interest with respect to those lands.

heading: Lands adjacent to submerged areas
paragraph: (3) Where small areas only of any parcel or subdivision of any public lands are required to be submerged along the bank of any stream in connection with an undertaking and it has not been found practicable or expedient to make surveys for the purpose of setting out the exact limits of the area to be flooded, the Minister may dispose of the parcel or subdivision in accordance with any other Act or regulation applicable to the disposal of those lands, but reserving the right at any time to raise the water surface to such elevation as may be required in connection with the undertaking.

heading: Expropriation by Crown
paragraph: 6 Where any land or any interest therein is required by Her Majesty for any undertaking or is necessary for creating, protecting or developing any water-power, the Governor in Council may direct the Minister on behalf of Her Majesty to acquire by expropriation the title to that land or interest therein as may be required, and thereupon the provisions of the Expropriation Act in so far as applicable apply as if included in this Act.

heading: Power to expropriate
paragraph: 7 (1) Any person who, pursuant to this Act or the regulations, is authorized to carry out any undertaking may, after receiving written permission from the Minister, expropriate in accordance with the Expropriation Act any land or interest in land, other than public lands or any interest in public lands, that may, in the opinion of the Minister, be required for the undertaking.

heading: Notice to appropriate minister
paragraph: (1.1) Where the Minister grants permission under subsection (1), the person to whom permission is granted shall so advise the appropriate minister in relation to Part I of the Expropriation Act.

heading: Expropriation Act
paragraph: (1.2) Land or an interest in land in respect of which the Minister has granted permission under subsection (1) is deemed to be, for the purposes of the Expropriation Act, an interest in land or an immovable real right that, in the opinion of the appropriate minister in relation to Part I of that Act, is required for a public work or other public purpose, and a reference to the Crown in that Act shall be construed as a reference to the person to whom the Minister granted permission.

heading: Charges for services
paragraph: (1.3) The appropriate minister in relation to Part I of the Expropriation Act may make regulations prescribing fees or charges to be paid, in respect of an expropriation referred to in subsection (1), by a person to whom the Minister has granted permission, and rates of interest payable in respect of those fees and charges.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (1.4) The fees or charges are a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada by the person to whom the Minister has granted permission, and shall bear interest at the prescribed rate from the date they are payable.

heading: Security
paragraph: (1.5) The Minister may require the person to whom the Minister has granted permission to provide security, in an amount determined by the Minister and subject to any terms and conditions that the Minister may specify, for the payment of any fees or charges that are or may become payable under this section.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) This section does not apply to lands belonging to any railway company that are used or required by the company for the purposes of its railway.

heading: Cancellation of entries, leases, etc.
paragraph: 8 (1) Where an entry, permit, lease or licence has been granted or issued, or the Crown has entered into any agreement or other form of conveyance under which public lands that are required, or any interest therein that is required, for an undertaking are occupied or held in a manner inconsistent with the carrying out of the undertaking, the Governor in Council may order and direct the cancellation of the entry, permit, lease, licence or agreement, in whole or in part, or may direct that the terms thereof be so modified as to reserve to the Crown the lands or rights in the lands that are required for the undertaking.

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (2) In every case compensation shall be paid to the permittee, entrant, lessee, licensee or party to an agreement or other form of conveyance referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Complete cancellation
paragraph: (3) In the case of a complete cancellation under subsection (1), compensation under subsection (2) shall include such sums as have been actually paid to the Crown on account of lands and expended for improvements thereon, with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum, as well as an amount to cover the estimated actual loss or damage, if any, sustained by reason of the cancellation.

heading: Partial cancellation
paragraph: (4) In the case of a partial cancellation under subsection (1), compensation under subsection (2) shall include the actual reasonable value, if any, of the lands or interest therein taken.

heading: Minister to fix amount
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall in each case fix the amount of the compensation to be paid, subject to appeal to the Federal Court.

heading: Joint development of water-powers
paragraph: 9 Where two or more water-powers are so situated that they can be more economically and satisfactorily utilized by being developed jointly and operated under one control, and

heading: Joint development of water-powers
paragraph: (a) if those water-powers have not been granted by the Crown, the Governor in Council may order that they be disposed of in such manner and subject to such conditions as will, in his opinion, secure the joint development and single control; or

heading: Joint development of water-powers
paragraph: (b) if the right to develop one or more of those water-powers has been granted to or is held by any person, and the Governor in Council is of the opinion that the public interest will best be served by reserving the remaining water-power or water-powers so as to bring about the joint development and single control of all of those water-powers, the Governor in Council may order the remaining water-power or water-powers to be reserved for such period as he deems necessary in order to secure the joint development and single control, and may authorize the Minister to enter into an agreement with the person holding the water-power or water-powers for the purposes described in this paragraph, and may prescribe the terms, conditions and covenants to be included in the agreement.

heading: Surveys, measurements, etc.
paragraph: 10 (1) The Minister may direct or order

heading: Surveys, measurements, etc.
paragraph: (a) that such surveys and other proceedings be taken as may, in his opinion, be required to ascertain the public lands or any other lands or any interests in any lands that it may be necessary to reserve or acquire for any undertaking, and the decision of the Minister with respect to the lands or interests therein that may in any case be required is final;

heading: Surveys, measurements, etc.
paragraph: (b) that a survey of all streams and all necessary investigations with respect to water-powers be taken to determine the total utilized and available water-power and the maximum that can be made available by storage, regulation or other artificial means;

heading: Surveys, measurements, etc.
paragraph: (c) that the volume or discharge of any stream or body of water, or the economic availability or usefulness thereof, for power purposes be ascertained;

heading: Surveys, measurements, etc.
paragraph: (d) that the flow or quantity of water used, and of the output of electrical or other form of energy produced from the use of water, by any licensee or other person be ascertained; and

heading: Surveys, measurements, etc.
paragraph: (e) that gauges, weirs, meters or other devices for water or water-power measurements or for measuring the output of electrical or other forms of energy be established.

heading: Records and plans
paragraph: (2) The records and plans of surveys and investigations taken under subsection (1) shall be kept on file in the Department of Indigenous Services, and may be published in such form and to such extent as the Minister may determine.

heading: Free access to works, books, plans or records
paragraph: 11 The Minister or any person appointed by him for the purpose shall have free access, in connection with any of the matters set out in this section, to all works, books, plans or records in so far as they relate to any undertaking, and may take such observations, make such measurements and do such other things of, on, within or with respect to the undertaking, books, plans or records as may be considered necessary or expedient for

heading: Free access to works, books, plans or records
paragraph: (a) ascertaining the quantity of water stored, diverted or used, or capable of being stored, diverted or used,

heading: Free access to works, books, plans or records
paragraph: (b) ascertaining the amount of power developed or capable of being developed,

heading: Free access to works, books, plans or records
paragraph: (c) ascertaining the condition of the works,

heading: Free access to works, books, plans or records
paragraph: (d) determining whether the conditions to be observed or performed by any licensee, lessee or other person are being satisfactorily observed and performed, and

heading: Free access to works, books, plans or records
paragraph: (e) any other purpose connected with the administration of this Act,

heading: Free access to works, books, plans or records
paragraph: and the findings of the Minister, with respect to the quantity of water stored, diverted or used, or capable of being stored, diverted or used, or the amount of power developed or capable of being developed, shall be conclusive.

heading: Agreements with provincial authorities
paragraph: 12 The Minister may enter into cooperative agreements with the authorities of any of the provinces for making stream measurements, carrying on investigations, collecting and publishing data respecting water and power resources and the best methods of utilizing water and power resources.

heading: Director of Water-Power
paragraph: 13 For the purposes of this Act, all investigations and surveys and all undertakings shall, subject to the control of the Minister, be under the direction of a duly qualified officer to be designated the Director of Water-Power.

heading: Powers of Governor in Council
paragraph: 14 The Governor in Council may make such orders as are deemed necessary to carry out the provisions of this Act and the regulations according to their true intent or to meet any cases that arise for which no provision is made in this Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 15 The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) for the storage, pondage, regulation, diversion, carriage or utilization of any water for power purposes and for the protection of any sources of the water supply;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) for the development, transmission, distribution, sale, exchange, disposal or use of water-power on, through or over public lands or any other lands;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) for the construction, maintenance, operation, purchase and taking over of all works that may be deemed necessary or desirable for any of the purposes set out in this Act, whether on, through or over public lands or any other lands, and for the regulation and control, in the interests of all water users, of the flow of water that may, from time to time, pass through, by or over those works;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) for the use and occupancy of public lands and other lands or of any interest therein required for any of the purposes set out in this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) for the withdrawal from disposal under any other Act of any public lands or of any interest therein required for any purposes set out in this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) for the granting and the administering of rights, powers and privileges in or with respect to water-powers or undertakings;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) prescribing the conditions on which the works, lands and properties held in respect of any undertaking may be taken over on the expiration of the term of any agreement, lease or licence or on the termination thereof for non-compliance with any of the covenants, terms or conditions contained in the agreement, lease or licence or for any other reason;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) for the construction by or at the instance of Her Majesty of regulation or storage works for regulating or augmenting the flow of water required for power and other purposes, for the purchase or taking over of works already constructed, and for the dividing and collecting of the cost of constructing, maintaining and operating from time to time such works among all persons benefiting or in a position to benefit therefrom;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) for the securing of such power output at any site, within the limits of its capacity, as may be required to supply the public demand, and the securing of the maximum power resources of all streams;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) for fixing the rentals, royalties, fees, dues or charges to be paid for the diversion, use or storage of water, for the use or occupancy of lands, or for any other privileges granted in pursuance of this Act, including charges for any additional flowage created by storage or regulation works constructed by or at the instance of Her Majesty;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) for regulating the passage of logs, timber and other products of the forest through or over any dams or other works erected under the authority of this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (l) for the appraisal, for the purposes of this Act, of the works, lands and properties required or used in connection with any undertaking;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (m) for regulating and controlling the stock and bond issues of persons establishing or conducting undertakings;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (n) for regulating and controlling the service given to the public by persons engaged in supplying water-power and for regulating and controlling the rates or charges for that service;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (o) for the appointment or the designation of the board or commission that, in any particular territory, may regulate and control stock and bond issues, service, rates and charges;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (p) for the appointment of a person to act with any existing authority constituted for the purposes of regulating and controlling the matters referred to in paragraphs (m) to (o);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (q) prescribing the manner in which accounts shall be kept for the purposes of this Act by persons conducting or managing undertakings and requiring the submitting of statements and reports, annual or otherwise, by those persons;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (r) prescribing the forms to be used in proceedings under this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (s) for the construction, maintenance and operation by the Minister of any undertaking on public lands; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (t) generally, for carrying into effect the purposes and provisions of this Act.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the Dominion Water Power Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: actual construction includes

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) any necessary and authorized work carried on in pursuance of these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) engineering investigations and reports,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) the clearing of lands,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) the construction of roads or railways,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) stream improvements, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (f) other essential work undertaken solely in the construction of works authorized and not used independently as a source of profit,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: but does not include

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (g) promotion work,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (h) the underwriting, sale or disposal of stocks and bonds, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (i) general administrative or directive functions exercised at some distance from the scene of operations; (construction reelle)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: actual cost of any development of works includes

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the actual legitimate cost of such development or works in use and useful for the purposes of the undertaking at the time that any particular inquiry is being made,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) the cost of engineering services appertaining to the construction of such development and works,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) interest during construction,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) taxes and insurance during construction,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) contractor's profit,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (f) the purchase of equipment,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (g) the cost of roads, railways, clearings or other essential works undertaken and carried on solely in the construction of such development or works and not independently profitable, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (h) such other expenditures as are necessary and inherent items of construction,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: but does not in any case include

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (i) promotion expenses,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (j) the cost of underwriting, selling or disposing of stocks and bonds, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (k) head office and other expenditures relating to general administration exercised at some distance from the development or works which are not necessary and inherent parts of the construction expenditures; (cout reel)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Department means the Department of Indian Affairs and Northern Development; (ministere)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Director means the Director of Water-Power, who shall be the Chief of the Water Resources Division of the Department or such other person designated by the Minister; (directeur)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: final construction plans means the plans of the power development or power system as actually constructed, and in every case includes plans of the lands as finally occupied to conform with sections 10 and 17; (plans definitifs de construction)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: final licence means a licence authorizing the diversion, use or storage of water for power purposes, or the transmission and distribution of water-power; (concession definitive)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: general construction plans means the plans of the works that are required to be approved by the Director before the interim licensee is permitted to commence the construction of the power development; (plans generaux de construction)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: general layout plans means the plans that are required to be filed by the applicant before an interim licence may be issued; (plans d'ensemble)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: independent works means all works and plants outside of the power system that may be classed as tributary to independent undertakings of the licensee and not to the undertaking authorized; (ouvrages independants)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: initial development means such portion of the power or storage development as is specified in the interim licence as being required to be constructed before a final licence may be issued; (premier amenagement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: interconnected systems means the power system and all plants and works connected therewith, related thereto, interdependent upon it and similarly used in the generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy; (reseaux conjugues)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: interim licence means a licence authorizing the preparation of general construction plans and the construction of works in pursuance of such plans; (concession interimaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Indian Affairs and Northern Development; (ministre)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: power development includes

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the physical structures within the severance line required for the storage or use of the stream-waters, for the production of power therefrom, and for the transmission thereof,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) the dams or other diversion works, the powerhouse, the conduits conducting water thereto and the transmission lines within the severance line,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) all hydraulic or electrical machinery, appliances, fixtures, equipment and appurtenances,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) lands and rights-of-way required in connection therewith, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) the clearings, roads, trails and railways required to be constructed that are still used and useful in connection therewith and not independently profitable; (amenagement de force hydraulique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: preliminary sketch plan means the preliminary plan or sketch filed by the applicant with his initial application; (croquis preliminaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: public lands means lands belonging to Her Majesty in right of Canada and includes lands of which the Government of Canada has power to dispose; (terres publiques)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: severance line means the dividing or boundary line that separates those lands, works and properties used or useful in connection with the undertaking and that are considered to be essential to the power or storage development from other lands, works and properties used or useful in connection with the undertaking but not considered to be essential to the development; (ligne separative)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: storage development includes

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the physical structures within the severance line required for the storage of the stream-waters for the production of power,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) the dams or other storage works, the intakes and water conduits within the severance line,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) all hydraulic or electrical machinery, appliances, fixtures, equipment and appurtenances,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) lands and rights-of-way required in connection therewith, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) the clearings, roads, trails and railways required to be constructed that are still used and useful in connection therewith and not independently profitable; (amenagement d'emmagasinage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: system or power system means all lands, structures and appurtenances required to complete the undertaking authorized, including the power development, works, reservoirs, transmission lines, distribution works, auxiliary steam or other fuel plants, the lands required to be occupied, clearings, roads and railways in so far as required in connection with the power development, and all mills, buildings, machines, appliances, fixtures, equipment and appurtenances required in connection therewith; (reseau ou reseau de distribution d'energie )

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: works, with reference to any power development, power system or undertaking, means all the physical structures, devices, equipment, appliances, appurtenances and things authorized or required to be constructed, maintained or operated by the applicant or licensee in respect of such power development, power system or undertaking. (ouvrages)

heading: Application
paragraph: 3 (1) An application for a licence to divert, use or store water for power purposes may be made to the Director and shall contain the following information:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) the name, address and occupation of the applicant;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) the name or a clear description of the river, lake or other watercourse from which the water is to be diverted or used;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) the place where the water is to be diverted from or in the said watercourse, referred if possible to an established monument of the existing system of land surveys, and the place where the water is to be returned or released;

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) the maximum quantity of water, expressed in cubic feet per second, which it is estimated will be ultimately diverted or used under the licence applied for;

heading: Application
paragraph: (e) the estimated average head in feet which will be available for the production of power according to the plan of development proposed;

heading: Application
paragraph: (f) the estimated minimum amount of energy expressed in horsepower that will be developed on the turbine shaft within five years from the date of the application or within such other period as the applicant may state to be required for the completion of his initial development;

heading: Application
paragraph: (g) the maximum amount of energy expressed in horsepower which it is estimated will ultimately be developed on the turbine shaft from the waters for which application is made;

heading: Application
paragraph: (h) a brief statement with respect to the character and extent of all principal works the applicant proposes to construct;

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) in respect of each dam involved, its approximate maximum length and height, its proposed type and the material to be used in its construction;

heading: Application
paragraph: (j) where storage is involved, the location of each lake, basin or other place in which the applicant wishes to store water;

heading: Application
paragraph: (k) for each storage reservoir, the approximate number of acres of land the applicant proposes to flood, the approximate area in acres of the surface of the reservoir when filled, the estimated vertical storage range in feet, and the total capacity of storage contemplated in acre-feet; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (l) a reasonably accurate description and the acreage of the lands required for occupation or use in the construction, maintenance or operation of the proposed works, noting separately lands required for rights-of-way and lands that are to be flooded

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) within public lands,

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) within provincial Crown lands, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (iii) within privately owned lands.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) An application for a licence shall be accompanied by

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a preliminary plan or sketch, with scale so selected as to show upon a single sheet the entire project applied for, with the approximate location of all the principal works and lands referred to in paragraph (1)(l);

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) a description of and a sketch showing the nearest neighbouring works or structures completed or in course of construction, both above and below the place of the proposed diversion, for diverting or using water for any purpose from the same source of supply and the approximate distance and direction of each such works from the proposed works;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) the names and locations of any other works or structures, including bridges, railways and canals, that might affect or be affected by the construction, maintenance or operation of the proposed works;

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) the approximate discharge in cubic feet per second at or near the place of diversion of the river, lake or other source from which the water is to be diverted at high, medium and low water stages, respectively, together with copies of any existing measurements of the flow of the stream in the applicant's possession and a reference to all other such measurements of which the applicant has knowledge; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (e) a brief outline of the undertaking in respect of which the licence is desired, including the use to which the power is to be applied, any sale, delivery or transfer thereof to other than the applicant that is contemplated, the territory, if any, within which such sale, delivery or transfer is to be exercised, the probable demand for power within such territory and an estimate of the capital cost of the entire undertaking.

heading: Application
paragraph: (3) Where the applicant is an incorporated company, the application, in addition to the information required by subsections (1) and (2), shall contain

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) the names of the directors and officers of the company and their places of residence;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) the address of the head office of the company in Canada;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) the amount of capital authorized, subscribed, and paid-up, specifying in regard to paid-up capital, the amount paid in cash and the manner of payment for the balance;

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) the proposed method of raising further funds, if required, for the construction and operation of the proposed works; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (e) a copy of the special act of incorporation or the memorandum of association.

heading: Application
paragraph: (4) Where the applicant is a municipality or municipal district, the application, in addition to the information required by subsections (1) and (2), shall contain

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) the location, area and boundaries of the municipality or district;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) the approximate number of inhabitants in the municipality or district;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) the present indebtedness and the borrowing limit of the municipality or district;

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) a certified copy of any by-law or resolution passed by the municipality or district respecting the application or the undertaking to which the application relates; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (e) a certified copy of any enabling Act or other statutory provision authorizing the municipality or district to engage in the proposed undertaking.

heading: Application
paragraph: (5) All elevations given in connection with the plans or other information filed by any applicant shall be referred, if feasible, to mean sea-level datum.

heading: Application
paragraph: (6) An applicant, when requested so to do by the Minister, shall file an affidavit setting forth such facts as may be required in respect of his financial standing and his ability to carry out the proposed undertaking.

heading: Application
paragraph: (7) The Director may, at any time while an application is pending, notwithstanding any other requirement of these Regulations, require such additional plans, descriptions, measurements, specifications or other data, whether related directly or indirectly to the proposed works and undertaking, as he considers necessary, and those plans, descriptions, measurements, specifications or data shall be furnished by and at the expense of the applicant.

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: 4 (1) Upon request in writing from the Director, an applicant shall, at his own expense, publish a notice of the application in at least one issue of the Canada Gazette and in one or more issues of such other publications as the Director may specify.

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (2) The notice shall be marked at the top in plain letters "Dominion Water-Power Application", shall be in a form approved by the Director, and shall give substantially the following information:

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the applicant;

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (b) the date of application;

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (c) the name or a clear description of the source of water supply;

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (d) a clear description of the place of diversion;

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (e) the maximum horsepower capacity of the proposed plant;

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (f) the nature of the undertaking and utilization of the power;

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (g) a statement that the application has been filed with the Director, and that protests or objections may be filed by any interested party with the Director or at certain designated local points;

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (h) when storage or pondage of water is contemplated, the place of storage, the capacity of the intended reservoir, and a general description of the lands that are to be flooded; and

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (i) such other information as the Director may require.

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (3) An applicant shall file proof of publication of the notice in the form of an affidavit, made by a person having knowledge of the publication, to which shall be attached a copy of the notice as published.

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (4) Following the completion of publication of the notice, a period of 30 days shall be allowed in which protests or objections may be filed with the Director.

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (5) Where a protest or objection is filed within the period specified in subsection (4), or when for other reasons, the Minister considers that a hearing should take place before action is taken, he shall designate a time and place for the hearing and shall name a person to preside over and conduct the hearing.

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (6) The hearing may be adjourned from time to time, and the applicant may be permitted for the time being to continue the preparation of his plans and the carrying on of investigations.

heading: Publication and Hearings
paragraph: (7) The person conducting the hearing shall report his findings and recommendations in writing to the Minister, and the Minister may in his discretion reject the application if he deems it necessary in the public interest.

heading: Survey Permit
paragraph: 5 (1) Subject to subsection (3), the Director may issue to an applicant a survey permit empowering the applicant during the period stated therein, which shall not exceed three years, to enter upon any public lands without other licence therefor, and upon the lands of any person for the purpose of making such surveys and investigations as may be necessary for the preparation of his general layout plans, but for no other purpose, and the applicant shall, in making such surveys and investigations, do as little damage as possible, and shall make full compensation to all persons sustaining damage.

heading: Survey Permit
paragraph: (2) The issuance of a survey permit does not give the applicant any priority over other applicants for the development of any water-power, or any special claim or right in respect of the water-power.

heading: Survey Permit
paragraph: (3) The applicant shall furnish such security as the Director may require for the payment of any sums that may be subsequently awarded for any damage caused by the applicant in making any surveys and investigations authorized under these Regulations.

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: 6 (1) An applicant shall file his general layout plans with the Director by such date as is specified by the Director.

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (2) The general layout plans and data shall be such as will enable the Director to determine whether

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (a) the proposed works are of suitable design to accomplish the purpose intended,

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (b) the proposed development is in general accord with the most beneficial utilization of the resources of the stream in Canada, and

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (c) the proposed undertaking is feasible and practicable and in the public interest,

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: and such plans shall further conform to any requirements of the Director not inconsistent with these Regulations.

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (3) The general layout plans and specifications shall

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (a) be based on actual and thorough surveys and investigations on the ground;

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (b) be in sufficient detail to enable the Director to determine exactly what is proposed to be done by the applicant;

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (c) show the position of the proposed works with reference to surrounding objects so that the exact scope of the project may be readily ascertained and located; and

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (d) show what provisions are being made for navigation, logging and other interests.

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (4) When the Director is of the opinion that further information and plans are necessary before an interim licence is issued, he may request the applicant to furnish additional information and plans.

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (5) Plans or maps shall in every case show the location and area of the lands that are required to be occupied, used or flooded in connection with the proposed works.

heading: General Layout Plans
paragraph: (6) Elevations wherever feasible shall be related to mean sea-level datum.

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: 7 (1) Where the applicant has completed satisfactorily the submission of such of the information required by section 3 and has supplied such of the plans and specifications as will satisfy the Minister that

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (a) the proposed development is in general accord with the most beneficial utilization of the stream waters,

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (b) the proposed undertaking is feasible and practicable and in the public interest, and

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (c) the applicant has the requisite financial ability to carry the project to a successful consummation,

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: the Minister may issue to the applicant a priority permit which shall give the applicant priority over other applicants in the consideration of his general layout plans if filed within the time specified in the permit.

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (2) In granting a priority permit the Minister may give preference to an application by a province, municipality or municipal district where he considers such preference to be in the public interest.

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (3) No priority permit shall be construed as binding the Minister to issue an interim licence, giving the applicant any exclusive claim or right, or relieving the Minister from considering other possible schemes for the development of the site, if there is reason to believe that they may result in a more beneficial utilization of the natural resources or be otherwise in the public interest.

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (4) A priority permit shall be effective for a period not to exceed one year but may be renewed.

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (5) No extensions of time to a priority permit shall be granted unless it is shown to the satisfaction of the Minister by statutory declaration by the applicant, and otherwise, that the applicant has promptly and diligently continued the surveys and preparation of the plans in good faith, and has been prevented by causes beyond his control, other than the want of funds, from completing the plans within the time fixed, but the applicant shall not be given an extension of more than one year from the expiry of the time originally fixed.

heading: Priority Permit
paragraph: (6) If the plans and information required are not completed and filed before the expiration of the initial period of the priority permit or of any extension thereof, the applicant's priority shall lapse.

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: 8 (1) The Minister, where he considers it advisable, may issue to the applicant an interim licence for the carrying out of the proposed development when he is satisfied that

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (a) the proposed works are of suitable design to accomplish the purpose intended;

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (b) the proposed development is feasible and practicable and is in accord with the most beneficial utilization of the resources of the stream; and

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (c) it is the best possible development in the public interest for which the site may be used, consideration being given to both present conditions and future requirements.

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (2) An interim licence shall contain

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (a) the times and manner of payment and the rates or amounts to be paid during the life of the interim licence as rentals or royalties for

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (i) lands occupied, and

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (ii) waters used for which the rental is based on the horsepower capacity of the installation in place or placed during the year but shall not be at a rate less than $0.75 per year per installed horsepower; and

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (b) such other terms and conditions, subject always to these Regulations, as may be imposed by the Minister.

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (3) Every interim or final licence shall

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (a) be deemed to incorporate and shall be subject to the provisions of the regulations in force at the time of the issue of and in so far as applicable to that interim or final licence;

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (b) be subject to such other stipulations, provisos and conditions, not inconsistent with these Regulations, as the Minister may impose; and

heading: Interim Licences
paragraph: (c) be subject to amendments to, changes in or additions to these Regulations made during the term of such licence that are not inconsistent with the rights and privileges granted under the licence.

heading: General Construction Plans
paragraph: 9 (1) An interim licensee shall file his general construction plans and specifications with the Director within the time specified in the interim licence.

heading: General Construction Plans
paragraph: (2) The plans and specifications filed by an interim licensee shall be such as would be required for submission to construction contractors for the purpose of receiving tenders and shall be in sufficiently advanced form to satisfy the Director.

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: 10 (1) An interim licensee shall, at a time fixed by the Director, supplement the general construction plans of the works by a plan of lands from an actual survey by a Canada Lands Surveyor acting under instructions from the Surveyor General of Canada.

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (2) A plan of lands shall be certified by a Canada Lands Surveyor and shall show and describe by section, township and range or lot number if in surveyed territory, or by other accurate description if in unsurveyed territory, the lands that are required to be occupied or used in the construction, maintenance and operation of the proposed works, noting separately,

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (a) public lands not covered by water required for main diverting works, powerhouses and other similar works;

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (b) public lands covered by water required for the purposes referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (c) public lands required only to be flooded in connection with the storage or pondage of water;

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (d) public lands required only for rights-of-way for water conduits, transmission lines and other similar works;

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (e) public lands, if any, required for substations, distributing stations, terminal stations and other similar buildings;

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (f) provincial Crown lands; and

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (g) privately owned lands.

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (3) The plan of lands shall be accompanied by a statement giving, with respect to each parcel of privately owned lands, the name of

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (a) the registered owner in fee thereof;

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (b) any registered mortgagee or lessee; and

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (c) any claimant in actual possession other than a registered owner, mortgagee or lessee.

heading: Plan of Lands
paragraph: (4) When required by the Director, the surveys and investigations required by this section shall be made by the Legal Surveys Division of the Department of Energy, Mines and Resources and in such case an interim licensee shall reimburse Her Majesty for all salaries and expenses paid for such surveys upon the presentation to the interim licensee of accounts properly certified.

heading: Approval of Plans
paragraph: 11 (1) The Director shall examine the general construction plans and specifications of the works and the plan of lands, and shall report thereon to the Minister.

heading: Approval of Plans
paragraph: (2) The Director shall notify the interim licensee in writing whether the plans have been approved subject to conditions, or have been rejected and the interim licence cancelled.

heading: Approval of Plans
paragraph: (3) Approval or non-approval of any plans shall neither incur the responsibility of the Crown nor relieve the interim licensee from the consequences that may result from the construction of the works, from imperfections in departmental requirements, or from the operation of the works.

heading: Commencement of Construction
paragraph: 12 (1) An interim licensee shall not commence the actual construction of the proposed works until he is notified by the Director that the general construction plans and specifications of such works have been approved either with or without conditions.

heading: Commencement of Construction
paragraph: (2) The Minister, prior to the approval of the general construction plans, may in his discretion grant permission to an interim licensee to carry on preliminary construction operations such as the clearing of sites for structures, the clearing of land that will be flooded, or any other work other than the actual construction of the permanent works.

heading: Commencement of Construction
paragraph: (3) Permission granted to an interim licensee under subsection (2) shall be without prejudice with respect to action by the Minister on the general construction plans or otherwise.

heading: Commencement of Construction
paragraph: (4) Within six months after receiving notification that the plans have been approved, an interim licensee shall commence the construction of the works and shall thereafter without interruption, other than want of funds, carry on and complete the construction according to the plans and specifications as approved, and subject to the terms of the interim licence and of these Regulations.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: 13 (1) Within 60 days after being notified in writing by the Director of the approval of the general construction plans and specifications, an interim licensee shall, for the purpose of guaranteeing the performance and fulfilment by the interim licensee of the terms and conditions of the licence, forward to the Director for deposit with the Department of Finance,

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (a) a guarantee deposit computed, in the case of a power undertaking, upon the horsepower capacity of the site as determined by the Director according to the following scale:

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (i) up to 1,000 h.p. $2.00 per h.p.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (ii) the next 9,000 h.p.   1.00 per h.p.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (iii) all over 10,000 h.p.   0.50 per h.p.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (b) a guarantee deposit computed, in the case of a storage undertaking, upon the estimated cost of the storage development as determined by the Director according to the following scale:

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (i) five per cent on the first $100,000 of estimated cost,

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (ii) 2 1/2 per cent on the next $900,000 of estimated cost,

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (iii) one per cent on the amount above $1,000,000 of estimated cost.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (2) A guarantee deposit required under this section shall not exceed $50,000 and shall be in one or more of the following forms:

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (a) a certified cheque drawn on a bank incorporated under the Bank Act or the Quebec Savings Banks Act;

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (b) bonds of the Government of Canada or of a company included in the National Railways as defined in the Canadian National Railways Capital Revision Act, 1952, unconditionally guaranteed as to principal and interest by the Government of Canada where such bonds are

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (i) payable to bearer,

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (ii) hypothecated to the Minister of Finance and Receiver General in accordance with the provision of the Domestic Bonds of Canada Regulations, or

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (iii) registered in the name of the Minister of Finance and Receiver General.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (3) A guarantee deposit may be refunded by the Minister to an interim licensee as the actual construction work progresses, the first, second and third quarters thereof to be refunded when one-quarter, one-half and three-quarters, respectively, of the initial development have been satisfactorily completed, the fourth quarter to be refunded when the final licence is issued.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (4) An interim licensee shall furnish to the Director, in the form of a statutory declaration or otherwise as may be required, evidence of satisfactory progress in the works to the stage that is required by the terms of his interim licence.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (5) The Minister is the final arbiter of the satisfactory completion of the first quarter of the initial development.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (6) Where an interim licensee has complied with all requirements in filing general construction plans, but the plans are rejected and the interim licence cancelled, the guarantee deposit shall be refunded upon application therefor, and the Minister may make such provision as he deems just for compensating the interim licensee for the plans where they prove to be valuable in connection with the disposition that is eventually made of the power site.

heading: Guarantee Deposit
paragraph: (7) Where an interim licensee fails to comply satisfactorily with the terms of his interim licence, the guarantee deposit, or such part thereof as the Minister may determine, shall be forfeited to the Crown.

heading: Rights in Lands Under Interim Licence
paragraph: 14 (1) Only such interim rights of entry upon or of the use or occupation of any public lands shall be acquired in virtue of any interim licence as may, in the opinion of the Minister, be necessary for the purpose of making surveys, preparing plans, constructing works and otherwise carrying out the terms of the licence, and in no case shall the rights granted by any interim licence be construed to interfere in any way with any interest in public lands previously disposed of by the Crown.
