paragraph: (b) a local Indigenous nation that is identified for the site,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a municipality, if all or part of the site is in the municipality, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a regional district, if all or part of the site is in the regional district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local Indigenous nation", in relation to a dormant site or former site, means an Indigenous nation that is identified for the site in a manner specified by the regulator;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permit holder" means,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to a dormant site, the person who holds the well permit, facility permit or pipeline permit, as the case may be, for the site, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to a former site, the former permit holder who held the well permit, facility permit or pipeline permit, as the case may be, for the site;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pipeline permit" means a permit that includes permission to construct or operate a pipeline;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "portfolio of current sites" has the same meaning as "portfolio" in section 43.1 of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "portfolio of former sites", in relation to a permit holder, means all of the former sites, if any, that are sites for which the permit holder held well permits, facility permits or pipeline permits;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "priority site" means a dormant site or former site identified under section 5 [identifying priority sites];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "reference year", in relation to a type B or C site, means the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) if the site became a dormant site under section 3 (1) (a), 3.01 (1) (a) or 3.02 (1) (a), the last of the 5 calendar years referred to in that section;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if the site became a dormant site under section 3 (1) (b), 3.01 (1) (b) or 3.02 (1) (b), the calendar year in which the notice referred to in that section was received;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) if the site is a former site, the calendar year in which the well permit, facility permit or pipeline permit, as the case may be, for the former site is cancelled, is declared spent or expires;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "remediate" has the meaning given to it in section 8 [remediation];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "restore" has the meaning given to it in section 9 [restoration];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "specified work" means work to decommission, assess or restore a dormant site or former site;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "type A site" means a dormant site or former site classified as a type A site under section 4 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "type B site" means a dormant site or former site classified as a type B site under section 4 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "type C site" means a dormant site or former site classified as a type C site under section 4 (3);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "well permit" means a permit that includes permission to drill or operate a well.

heading: Application
paragraph: 1.1		  (1) This regulation does not apply in relation to the following:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a processing facility as defined in section 1 of the Processing Facility Regulation;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) an LNG facility as defined in section 1 of the Liquefied Natural Gas Facility Regulation;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) a Class 1 hydrogen facility as defined in section 1 (1) of the Hydrogen Facility Regulation;

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) a Class 2 hydrogen facility as defined in section 1 (1) of the Hydrogen Facility Regulation.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) For certainty, this regulation applies in relation to a facility whether or not the facility is associated with a well.

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph:
2
		  (1) In this section,

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: "dormant facility" means a facility that is dormant in accordance with section 3.01 [when facilities are dormant];

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: "dormant pipeline" means a pipeline that is dormant in accordance with section 3.02 [when pipelines are dormant];

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: "dormant well" means a well that is dormant in accordance with section 3 [when wells are dormant].

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the operating area for a well permit, a facility permit or a pipeline permit, as the case may be, is a dormant site for the purposes of the definition of "dormant site" in section 43.1 [definitions] of the Act if

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (a) the well, the facility or the pipeline permitted by the permit is a dormant well, a dormant facility or a dormant pipeline, as the case may be, and

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (b) in the case of a well on a multi-well pad, the other wells on the pad are also dormant wells.

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (3) A portion of an operating area is not a dormant site for the purposes of the definition of "dormant site" in section 43.1 of the Act if any of the following is located in the portion:

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (a) a facility not solely associated with a dormant well, a dormant facility or a dormant pipeline;

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (b) a pipeline not solely associated with a dormant well, a dormant facility or a dormant pipeline;

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (c) a well not solely associated with a dormant well, a dormant facility or a dormant pipeline;

heading: Dormant sites
paragraph: (d) an energy resource road not solely associated with a dormant well, a dormant facility or a dormant pipeline.

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph:
3
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a well is dormant for the purposes of section 2 if

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (a) none of the following events has occurred for the well over the last 5 calendar years:

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (i)  production from or injection or disposal into the well occurs for a total of 720 or more hours in a calendar year;

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (ii)  a zone is completed;

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (iii)  a drilling event occurs;

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (iv)  in the case of an observation well, the well is active on at least one day;

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (v)  a certificate of restoration is issued for the site, or

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (b) the regulator has received a written notice from the permit holder that the well is dormant.

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (2) A well is not dormant for 2 years after the date on which the regulator gives to the permit holder for the well a written notice under subsection (3).

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (3) The regulator may give to a permit holder a written notice for the purposes of subsection (2) in relation to a well if the regulator is satisfied, having regard to the following factors, that an event referred to in subsection (1) (a) will occur for the well within a reasonable period of time:

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (a) available reserves;

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (b) economic factors, including, without limitation,

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (i)  the cost to bring the well online, and

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (ii)  forecasted production and prices;

heading: When wells are dormant
paragraph: (c) safety factors, including, without limitation, well integrity.

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph:
3.01
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a facility is dormant for the purposes of section 2 if

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (a) neither of the following has occurred for the facility over the last 5 calendar years:

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (i)  the facility has been operated;

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (ii)  a certificate of restoration has been issued for the site, or

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (b) the regulator has received a written notice from the permit holder that the facility is dormant.

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (2) A facility is not dormant for 2 years after the date on which the regulator gives to the permit holder for the facility a written notice under subsection (3).

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (3) The regulator may give to a permit holder a written notice for the purposes of subsection (2) in relation to a facility if the regulator is satisfied, having regard to the following factors, that the facility will be operated within a reasonable period of time:

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (a) available reserves of substances to be gathered, processed, measured, stored or disposed of at the facility;

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (b) economic factors, including, without limitation,

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (i)  the cost to resume the operation of the facility, and

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (ii)  forecast production and prices;

heading: When facilities are dormant
paragraph: (c) safety factors, including, without limitation, facility integrity.

heading: When pipelines are dormant
paragraph:
3.02
		  (1) A pipeline is dormant for the purposes of section 2 if

heading: When pipelines are dormant
paragraph:
(a) the pipeline or part of the pipeline has not transported fluids over the last 5
                calendar years, or

heading: When pipelines are dormant
paragraph:
(b) the regulator has received a written notice from the permit holder that the
                pipeline is dormant.

heading: When pipelines are dormant
paragraph: (2) The 5-year period set out in subsection (1) (a) includes any period for deactivating the pipeline or part of the pipeline set out in a plan approved by the regulator under section 9 (4) [deactivation] of the Pipeline Regulation or in a condition imposed with respect to an exemption granted under section 14 [exemptions] of the Pipeline Regulation.

heading: Former sites
paragraph:
3.1
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the operating area for a well permit, a facility permit or a pipeline permit is a former site for the purposes of this regulation if

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (a) the permit

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (i)  is cancelled under section 26 [actions by regulator respecting permit] or 33 [surrender of permit or permission] of the Act,

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (ii)  is declared spent under section 27 [spent permit or permission] of the Act, or

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (iii)  expires under section 32 [expiration of permit and authorizations] of the Act, and

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (b) a certificate of restoration has not been issued for the site.

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (2) A portion of an operating area is not a former site if any of the following is located on the portion:

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (a) a well not solely associated with the energy resource activity permitted by the permit referred to in subsection (1);

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (b) a facility not solely associated with the energy resource activity permitted by the permit referred to in subsection (1);

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (c) a pipeline not solely associated with the energy resource activity permitted by the permit referred to in subsection (1);

heading: Former sites
paragraph: (d) an energy resource road not solely associated with the energy resource activity permitted by the permit referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph:
4
		  (1) A site is a type A site if

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (a) the site became a dormant site under section 3 (1) (a) and the last of the 5 calendar years referred to in that section is 2018, or

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (b) the site is the former site for a well permit that was cancelled, declared spent or expired in 2018 or an earlier calendar year.

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (2) A site is a type B site if

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (a) the site became a dormant site under section 3 (1) (a) and the last of the 5 calendar years referred to in that section is after 2018 and before 2024,

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (b) the site became a dormant site under section 3 (1) (b) and the notice referred to in that section was received before 2024, or

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (c) the site is the former site for a well permit that was cancelled, declared spent or expired after 2018 and before 2024.

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (3) A site is a type C site if

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (a) the site became a dormant site under section 3 (1) (a), 3.01 (a) or 3.02 (a) and the last of the 5 calendar years referred to in that section is 2024 or a later calendar year,

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (b) the site became a dormant site under section 3 (1) (b), 3.01 (b) or 3.02 (b) and the notice referred to in that section was received in 2024 or a later calendar year, or

heading: Classifying dormant sites and former sites
paragraph: (c) the site is the former site for a well permit, a facility permit or pipeline permit that was cancelled, declared spent or expired in 2024 or a later calendar year.

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph:
5
		  The regulator may identify a type A, B or C site as a priority site, by giving to a permit holder for the site a written notice, if the regulator considers, having regard to the following factors, that it is in the public interest that the site be decommissioned, assessed and restored on an expedited basis:

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (a) the age of the site;

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (b) public safety, including human health;

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (c) the environment;

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (d) social and agricultural values;

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (e) impacts on local communities;

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (f) cultural and environmental values of local Indigenous nations;

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (g) the capacity of the permit holder;

heading: Identifying priority sites
paragraph: (h) the permit holder's portfolio of current sites and portfolio of former sites.

heading: Decommissioning
paragraph:
6
		  A dormant site or a former site is decommissioned for the purposes of this regulation if the permit holder for the site

heading: Decommissioning
paragraph: (a) does the following, as applicable:

heading: Decommissioning
paragraph: (i)  if the site is or was the operating area for a well permit, complies with the applicable requirements in section 26 (1) (a) to (c) [plugging requirements for wells] of the Drilling and Production Regulation;

heading: Decommissioning
paragraph: (ii)  if the site is or was the operating area for a facility permit, complies with the applicable requirements in section 79 [obligations on cancellation or cessation of operations] of the Drilling and Production Regulation;

heading: Decommissioning
paragraph: (iii)  if the site is or was the operating area for a pipeline permit, complies with the applicable requirements in section 11 [obligations on cancellation or cessation of operations] of the Pipeline Regulation,

heading: Decommissioning
paragraph: (b) removes from the site any facilities and other equipment that are associated with an energy resource activity that is permitted by the permit, and

heading: Decommissioning
paragraph: (c) removes from the site any facilities and other equipment that are associated with a related activity of an energy resource activity that is permitted by the permit.

heading: Assessment
paragraph:
7
		  A dormant site or former site is assessed for the purposes of this regulation if the permit holder for the site

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (a) has the following assessment carried out by or under the supervision of a professional satisfactory to the regulator:

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (i)  both stages of a preliminary site investigation described in section 58 (1) (a) and (b) [preliminary site investigations] of the Contaminated Sites Regulation;

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (ii)  unless the preliminary site investigation shows that the site meets the numerical standards under section 17 [numerical standards] of the Contaminated Sites Regulation, a detailed site investigation described in section 59 (1) and (2) [detailed site investigations] of that regulation;

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (b) submits to the regulator a report that

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (i)  describes the assessment carried out, and

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (ii)  includes the following:

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (A) the information required to be included in a report under section 58 (5) (c) and (d) of the Contaminated Sites Regulation;

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (B) if a detailed site investigation is required under paragraph (a) (ii) of this section, the information required to be included in a report under section 59 (3) of the Contaminated Sites Regulation;

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (C) any other information required by the regulator;

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (D) any signed statement, of the professional referred to in paragraph (a) or the permit holder, required by the regulator;

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (c) takes the actions identified in paragraphs (a) and (b) in relation to all facilities and other equipment that are associated with an energy resource activity permitted by the well permit or the facility permit, as the case may be, and

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (d) in the case of a dormant site or a former site that includes a pipeline right of way, does the following:

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (i)  ensures that all areas of potential environmental concern associated with the pipeline are identified and investigated by a person who

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (A) is a registrant within the meaning of the Professional Governance Act, and

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (B) through suitable education, experience, accreditation and knowledge, may be reasonably relied on to provide advice within the person's area of expertise as it relates to this regulation;

heading: Assessment
paragraph: (ii)  submits an investigation report to the regulator, in the form and manner required by the regulator.

heading: Remediation
paragraph: 8		  (1) A dormant site or former site is remediated for the purposes of this regulation if the regulator gives written notice to the permit holder for the site that

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (a) the regulator is satisfied that the site and any neighbouring lands to which contamination has migrated from the site meet the numerical standards under section 17 [numerical standards] of the Contaminated Sites Regulation,

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (b) the regulator is satisfied that

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (i)  the site and any neighbouring lands to which contamination has migrated from the site meet the risk-based standards under section 18 (3) (a) and (b) or (5) [risk-based standards], as applicable, of the Contaminated Sites Regulation, and

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (ii)  the permit holder has taken any actions identified under subsection (3), or

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (c) the regulator is satisfied that

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (i)  the site and any neighbouring lands to which contamination has migrated from the site have been remediated to an extent that provides a permanent solution to the maximum extent practicable, having regard to the following factors:

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (A) the risks to human health and the environment posed by contamination at the site and any neighbouring lands to which contamination has migrated from the site;

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (B) the local background concentration of any substances at the site and any neighbouring lands to which contamination has migrated from the site;

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (C) the potential effects on the environment of remediation to the standards referred to in paragraph (a) or (b);

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (D) the technical feasibility, risks and costs associated with remediation to the standards referred to in paragraph (a) or (b), and

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (ii)  the permit holder has taken any actions identified under subsection (3).

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1) (a) and (b) (i), a reference to a director in sections 17 (4) and (5) and 18 (5) of the Contaminated Sites Regulation is to be read as a reference to the regulator.

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1) (b) (ii) and (c) (ii), the regulator may, by written notice to a permit holder for a dormant site or former site, identify for the site or any neighbouring lands to which contamination has migrated from the site actions to be taken to prevent or mitigate risks to public safety, including human health, or to the environment posed by contamination.

heading: Remediation
paragraph: (4) For certainty, remediation under this section does not relieve a person from liability under Part 4 [Contaminated Site Remediation] of the Environmental Management Act.

heading: Restoration
paragraph: 9		  (1) A dormant site is restored for the purposes of this regulation if

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (a) the site is remediated, and

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (b) the regulator gives written notice to the permit holder for the site that the regulator is satisfied that the permit holder,

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (i)  unless otherwise ordered by the regulator, has performed each obligation imposed

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (A) under the Act or a specified enactment in relation to the permit, a permission specified in the permit or an authorization held by the permit holder for a related activity of an energy resource activity that is permitted by the permit, and

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (B) under the permit or an authorization referred to in clause (A), and

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a dormant site on Crown land, has complied with the applicable requirements in section 19 [areas to be restored] of the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation or is exempted under that regulation from the applicable requirements.

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (2) A former site is restored for the purposes of this regulation if

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (a) the site is remediated, and

heading: Restoration
paragraph: (b) in the case of a former site on Crown land, the permit holder has complied with the applicable requirements in section 19 of the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation or is exempted under that regulation from the applicable requirements.

heading: Application of this Division
paragraph:
10
		  (1) The requirements in this Division, as they relate to dormant sites, are prescribed for the purposes of section 43.2 [requirements to reduce liability] of the Act.

heading: Application of this Division
paragraph: (2) The requirements of this Division, as they relate to former sites, are prescribed for the purposes of section 40 (e) [obligations when permit, permission or authorization expires or is cancelled or spent] of the Act.

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph:
11
		  (1) A permit holder must, in accordance with this section, develop, and submit to the regulator a copy of, an annual work plan for a calendar year if

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (a) the permit holder's portfolio of current sites includes a dormant site, or

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (b) the permit holder has a portfolio of former sites.

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (1.1) An annual work plan under subsection (1) must do the following:

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (a) identify, by permit and type,

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  the dormant sites and former sites to be decommissioned in the calendar year,

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  the dormant sites and former sites to be assessed in the calendar year, and

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (iii)  the dormant sites and former sites to be restored in the calendar year;

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (b) set out the anticipated timelines for the work referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (c) identify any factors that might cause deviations from the plan;

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (d) include the following contact information:

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  if the permit holder is a corporation, the name, title, telephone number and, if any, email address of a director, officer or employee of the permit holder who may be contacted about the plan;

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  if the permit holder is an individual, the name, telephone number and, if any, email address of the permit holder;

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (e) be in the form specified by the regulator.

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (2) An annual work plan under subsection (1) must be developed, and a copy submitted to the regulator, by the following date:

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (a) in the case of an annual work plan for 2019, by August 31, 2019;

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (b) in the case of an annual work plan for any other calendar year, by the earlier of

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  January 30 of the calendar year, and

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  the date that is 60 days before the permit holder does specified work at a dormant site in the calendar year.

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph: (3) A copy of an annual work plan under subsection (1) must be submitted in the manner specified by the regulator.

heading: Annual report
paragraph:
12
		  (1) Within 60 days after the end of each calendar year, a permit holder must, in accordance with this section, submit to the regulator a report on the calendar year if

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) the permit holder's portfolio of current sites includes a dormant site, or

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) the permit holder has a portfolio of former sites.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (2) A report under subsection (1) must do the following:

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) demonstrate that the permit holder is on track to meet the applicable requirements in sections 15 to 18 [type A, B and C sites and priority sites];

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) identify, by permit and type,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (i)  the dormant sites and former sites that were decommissioned in the calendar year,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (ii)  the dormant sites and former sites that were assessed in the calendar year, and

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (iii)  the dormant sites and former sites that were restored in the calendar year;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (c) include a copy of the annual work plan for the calendar year and an explanation of any deviations from that plan;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (d) be in the form specified by the regulator;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (e) include any other information required by the regulator.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (3) A report under subsection (1) must be submitted in the manner specified by the regulator.

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph:
13
		  (1) Before doing specified work in a calendar year at a dormant site or former site, the permit holder for the site must give a written notice in accordance with this section to the interested persons, if any, for the site.

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) in relation to specified work to be done in a calendar year must be given by the following date:

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (a) in the case of 2019, by August 31, 2019;

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (b) in the case of any other calendar year, by the earlier of

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  January 30 of the calendar year, and

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  the date that is 60 days before the permit holder does specified work at the site in the calendar year.

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (3) A notice under subsection (1) in relation to specified work to be done in a calendar year must include

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (a) a draft of the annual work plan for the calendar year, and

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (b) a statement that an interested person may do one or both of the following:

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  request a meeting to discuss the plan;

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  make a written reply referred to in subsection (5).

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (4) If an interested person requests a meeting to discuss the annual work plan, the permit holder must

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (a) make reasonable efforts to meet with the person, and

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (b) submit a report to the regulator that

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  describes the efforts made to meet with the person, and

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  if a meeting is held, includes minutes of the meeting that

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (A) note the topics discussed and concerns raised at the meeting, and

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (B) describe any changes that the permit holder has agreed to make to the annual work plan.

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (5) If an interested person makes a written reply to a notice under subsection (1) within 30 days after receiving the notice, the permit holder must

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (a) consider any of following that is set out in the reply:

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  reasons why the specified work should be done on different timelines or in a particular way;

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  scientific, Indigenous and local knowledge,

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (b) within 30 days after receiving the written reply, give to the person a further written notice that includes

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (i)  a description of any changes made to the annual work plan, and

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (ii)  a statement that the permit holder will submit a copy of the notice, reply and further notice to the regulator, and

heading: Notification of annual work plan
paragraph: (c) as soon as practicable after giving the further notice, submit a copy of the notice, reply and further notice to the regulator.

heading: Notification of intention to begin work
paragraph:
14
		  At least 30 days before doing specified work at a dormant site or former site, the permit holder for the site must notify in writing the interested persons, if any, for the site.

heading: Type A sites
paragraph:
15
		  (1) A permit holder for type A sites that were not decommissioned by December 31, 2018 must decommission those sites as follows:

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (a) by December 31, 2021, the permit holder must have decommissioned at least one or 30% of those sites, whichever is greater;

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (b) by December 31, 2026, the permit holder must have decommissioned at least 2 or 70% of those sites, whichever is greater, unless there is only one site;

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (c) by December 31, 2031, the permit holder must have decommissioned all of those sites.

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (2) A permit holder for type A sites must assess each of those sites by the following date:

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (a) if the site was decommissioned by December 31, 2018, by December 31, 2030;

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (b) in any other case, by December 31 of the calendar year that is 2 calendar years after the calendar year in which the site is decommissioned.

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (3) A permit holder for type A sites must restore those sites as follows:

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (a) by December 31, 2024, the permit holder must have restored at least one or 40% of those sites, whichever is greater;

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (b) by December 31, 2030, the permit holder must have restored at least 2 or 70% of those sites, whichever is greater, unless there is only one site;

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (c) by December 31, 2036, the permit holder must have restored all of those sites.

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this section, if the result of taking a percentage of type A sites is not a whole number, the result is to be rounded

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (a) to the nearest whole number, or

heading: Type A sites
paragraph: (b) if the result is equidistant between 2 whole numbers, to the greater of those numbers.

heading: Type B sites
paragraph:
16
		  (1) A permit holder for a type B site must decommission the site by December 31 of the calendar year that is 8 calendar years after the reference year for the site.

heading: Type B sites
paragraph: (2) A permit holder for a type B site must assess the site by the following date:

heading: Type B sites
paragraph: (a) if the site was decommissioned in or before the reference year for the site, by December 31 of the calendar year that is 10 calendar years after that reference year;

heading: Type B sites
paragraph: (b) in any other case, by December 31 of the calendar year that is 2 calendar years after the calendar year in which the site is decommissioned.

heading: Type B sites
paragraph: (3) A permit holder for a type B site must restore the site by December 31 of the calendar year that is 13 calendar years after the reference year for the site.

heading: Type C sites
paragraph:
17
		  (1) Subject to subsection (4), a permit holder for a type C site must decommission the site by December 31 of the calendar year that is 5 calendar years after the reference year for the site.

heading: Type C sites
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (5), a permit holder for a type C site must assess the site by December 31 of the calendar year that is 2 calendar years after the calendar year in which the site is decommissioned.

heading: Type C sites
paragraph: (3) A permit holder for a type C site must restore the site by December 31 of the calendar year that is 10 calendar years after the reference year for the site.

heading: Type C sites
paragraph: (4) If the permit holder for a type C site complies with the applicable requirements in section 6 [decommissioning] of this regulation before December 31, 2024, the site that is the operating area for the permit is decommissioned for the purposes of this regulation.

heading: Type C sites
paragraph: (5) If subsection (4) applies, the permit holder for the site must assess the site by December 31, 2031.

heading: Priority sites
paragraph:
18
		  (1) In this section, "identification year", in relation to a priority site, means the calendar year in which the site is identified by notice under section 5 [identifying priority sites] as a priority site.

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (2) This section applies despite sections 15 (2) and (3), 16 and 17.

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (3) A permit holder for a priority site must decommission the site by the earlier of

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (a) the applicable date under section 15, 16 or 17, and

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (b) December 31 of the calendar year that is 2 years after the identification year for the site.

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (4) A permit holder for a priority site must assess the site by the earlier of

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (a) the applicable date under section 15, 16 or 17, and

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (b) December 31 of the calendar year that is 3 years after the identification year for the site.

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (5) A permit holder for a priority site must restore the site by the earlier of

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (a) the applicable date under section 15, 16 or 17, and

heading: Priority sites
paragraph: (b) December 31 of the calendar year that is 5 years after the identification year for the site.

heading: Liability reduction plans
paragraph:
19
		  (1) A permit holder may submit to the regulator a liability reduction plan if

heading: Liability reduction plans
paragraph: (a) the permit holder is eligible under section 20 of this regulation,

heading: Liability reduction plans
paragraph: (b) if applicable, the permit holder has engaged under section 21 of this regulation with local Indigenous nations in relation to the plan, and

heading: Liability reduction plans
paragraph: (c) the plan meets the requirements in sections 22 to 25 of this regulation.

heading: Liability reduction plans
paragraph: (2) Without limiting the authority of the regulator, section 26 (2) to (4) [actions by regulator respecting permit] of the Act applies to a determination of whether to approve a liability reduction plan.

heading: Approval of liability reduction plan for former sites
paragraph:
19.1
		  (1) If the regulator approves a liability reduction plan that covers a former site, the requirements in Division 1 do not apply in relation to the former site, except to the extent set out in the liability reduction plan.

heading: Approval of liability reduction plan for former sites
paragraph: (2) Without limiting any other power of the regulator, if a permit holder does not comply with an approved liability reduction plan that relates to a former site, the regulator may revoke the approval of that plan.

heading: Eligibility to submit liability reduction plan
paragraph:
20
		  A permit holder is eligible to submit a liability reduction plan if

heading: Eligibility to submit liability reduction plan
paragraph: (a) the permit holder's portfolio of current sites and portfolio of former sites includes, in combination, more than 100 type A sites, or

heading: Eligibility to submit liability reduction plan
paragraph: (b) the permit holder has previously had a liability reduction plan approved.

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph:
21
		  (1) This section applies in relation to a permit holder who intends to submit under section 19 a liability reduction plan that covers a dormant site or former site for which a local Indigenous nation is identified.

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (2) The permit holder must give a written notice to the local Indigenous nation that includes

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (a) a copy of the portion of the liability reduction plan that relates to the nation, and

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (b) a statement that the nation may do one or both of the following:

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (i)  request a meeting to discuss the plan;

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (ii)  make a written reply referred to in subsection (4).

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (3) If the local Indigenous nation requests a meeting to discuss the liability reduction plan, the permit holder must

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (a) make reasonable efforts to meet with the nation, and

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (b) submit a report to the regulator that

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (i)  describes the efforts made to meet with the nation, and

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (ii)  if a meeting is held, includes minutes of the meeting that

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (A) note the topics discussed and concerns raised at the meeting, and

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (B) describe any changes that the permit holder has agreed to make to the liability reduction plan.

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (4) If the local Indigenous nation makes a written reply to a notice under subsection (2) within 30 days after receiving the notice, the permit holder must

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (a) consider any of following that is set out in the reply:

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (i)  reasons why specified work covered by the plan should be done on different timelines or in a particular way;

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (ii)  scientific, Indigenous and local knowledge;

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (b) within 30 days after receiving the written reply, give to the nation a further written notice that includes

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (i)  a description of any changes made to the liability reduction plan, and

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (ii)  a statement that the permit holder will submit a copy of the notice, reply and further notice to the regulator, and

heading: Notification of liability reduction plan
paragraph: (c) as soon as practicable after giving the further notice, submit a copy of the notice, reply and further notice to the regulator.

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph:
22
		  (1) A liability reduction plan must identify

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (a) the dormant sites and former sites that are covered by the plan, and

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (b) any circumstances in which the following sites will become covered by the plan:

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (i)  a site that becomes a dormant site or former site after the plan is approved;

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (ii)  a dormant site for which the permit holder acquires the permit after the plan is approved.

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (2) A liability reduction plan must

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (a) cover a period of no more than 6 calendar years, and

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (b) for each of those calendar years, specify, by field and type,

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (i)  the number of dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan to be decommissioned in the calendar year,

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (ii)  the number of dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan to be assessed in the calendar year, and

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (iii)  the number of dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan to be restored in the calendar year.

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (3) A liability reduction plan must be consistent with the assessment of the dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan within the following timelines:

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (a) in the case of a type A site that was decommissioned by December 31, 2018, by December 31, 2033;

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (b) in the case of a type B site that was decommissioned in or before the reference year for the site, by December 31, 2033;

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (c) in the case of any other dormant site or former site, by December 31 of the calendar year that is 2 calendar years after the calendar year in which the site is decommissioned.

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (4) A liability reduction plan must be consistent with the restoration of the dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan within the following timelines:

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (a) in the case of a type A or B site, by December 31, 2036;

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (b) in the case of a type C site, by December 31 of the calendar year that is 10 calendar years after the reference year for the site.

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (5) A liability reduction plan must include specific plans for the decommissioning, assessment and restoration of priority sites.

heading: Basic requirements
paragraph: (6) A liability reduction plan must specify, for each type of dormant site that is covered by the plan, the maximum number of dormant sites of that type for which the permit holder may transfer the permit.

heading: Annual work plan
paragraph:
23
		  A liability reduction plan must require the permit holder to develop and submit to the regulator, in accordance with section 11 [annual work plan], an annual work plan for the calendar year.

heading: Annual report
paragraph:
24
		  (1) A liability reduction plan must require the permit holder to submit to the regulator, within 60 days after the end of each calendar year covered by the plan, a report on the calendar year.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (2) A report under subsection (1) must do the following:

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) identify, by permit and type,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (i)  the dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan that were decommissioned in the calendar year,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (ii)  the dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan that were assessed in the calendar year,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (iii)  the dormant sites and former sites covered by the plan that were restored in the calendar year, and

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (iv)  the dormant sites covered by the plan for which the permit holder transferred the permit in the calendar year;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) identify whether the permit holder is in compliance with the plan and, if not, the measures the permit holder proposes to take to correct the non-compliance and prevent further non-compliance with the plan;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (c) include the following:

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (i)  a copy of the annual work plan referred to in section 23 for the calendar year and an explanation of any deviations from that plan;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (ii)  any other information required by the regulator;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (iii)  a statement, signed by the permit holder or a director or officer of the permit holder, that the annual report is accurate and complete;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (d) be in the form specified by the regulator.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (3) A report under subsection (1) must be submitted in the manner specified by the regulator.

heading: Notification
paragraph:
25
		  A liability reduction plan must require the permit holder to comply with

heading: Notification
paragraph: (a) section 13 [notification of annual work plan], in relation to the annual work plan referred to in section 23, and

heading: Notification
paragraph: (b) section 14 [notification of intention to begin work].

heading: Pipeline deactivation timelines
paragraph:
25.1
		  In the event of a conflict, a timeline set out in section 17 [type C sites] or 22 [basic requirements] of this regulation prevails over a timeline set out in a plan approved by the regulator under section 9 (4) (a) [deactivation] of the Pipeline Regulation.

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
25.2
		  A person who carries out energy resource activities within an operating area must prepare
            and maintain an invasive plant compliance record that describes the activities carried
            out for the purpose of complying with the obligations described in section 15 of the
            Environmental Protection and Management Regulation, including all of the
            following:

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(a) the assessment and monitoring activities carried out for the purpose of
              determining whether invasive plants

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (i)  are present or established, or may become established, or

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (ii)  have spread to adjacent areas;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(b) the location, type and distribution of each species of invasive plants found
              through assessment and monitoring activities;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (c) the activities carried out for the purpose of preventing the following:

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(i)  the transportation of seed, plant parts or propagules of invasive
                plants;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(ii)  the establishment of invasive plants, including the removal of
                invasive plants;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(d) the revegetation activities carried out, including the plant species used for
              revegetation;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(e) the activities carried out for the purpose of ensuring that revegetated plants
              are successfully established;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (f) with respect to the activities described in this section,

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (i)  the dates on which the activities were carried out, and

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (ii)  the processes and equipment used in carrying out the activities;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (g) the qualifications of the persons

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (i)  carrying out assessment and monitoring activities, and

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (ii)  supervising the activities described in this section.

heading: Records
paragraph:
26
		  The records, reports and plans required under this regulation are prescribed for the
            purposes of section 38 of the Act.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph:
26.1
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), an official may exempt a permit holder from complying with any of the following provisions of this regulation:

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) section 15 [type A sites];

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) section 16 [type B sites];

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (c) section 17 [type C sites];

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (d) section 18 [priority sites].

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (2) Before granting an exemption under subsection (1), an official must be satisfied that, in the circumstances,

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) compliance with the provision or provisions is not reasonably practicable, or

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) the exemption is in the public interest.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (3) In granting an exemption under subsection (1), an official may impose any conditions on the exemption the official considers necessary.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
58
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "comptroller" means the person designated as the Comptroller of Water Rights under section 114 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "district" includes every drainage or diking district constituted before March 1, 1913 and all land constituted a drainage, diking or development district by order in council under this Part;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "electronic meeting" means a fully electronic meeting or a partially electronic meeting;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "engineer" means the civil engineer appointed by the commissioners under this Part;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "execute" has those meanings appropriate to describe the performance or construction of the particular works referred to in the context, and includes the acquisition of those works in any manner;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fully electronic meeting" means a meeting in which persons are entitled to participate solely by telephone or other communications medium, as set out in the notice of the meeting, if all persons attending the meeting are able to participate in it, whether by telephone or other communications medium;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "irrigation purpose" has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "judge" means a judge of the Supreme Court;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land" means all land in a district or proposed district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "majority in value of the owners" means owners of land in the district or the proposed district, representing in the aggregate more than 50% of the amount of the total assessments against the land in the district or the proposed district as appears by the last revised assessment roll of the district prepared and revised under this Part, or, if there is no assessment roll, then by the last revised Provincial or municipal assessment roll, or, if any parcel of land in the district is not separately shown as assessed by the Provincial or municipal assessment roll in force, the value of that parcel as determined by the comptroller for the purposes of this definition;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "owner" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the person registered in the register of indefeasible or absolute fees in the land title office as the registered owner of land within a district, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if an agreement to sell the land or any part of it is registered in the land title office, the person last registered as the holder of a right to purchase,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and includes the legal representative of the owner, the receiver or liquidator of a company that is an owner, and any pre-emptor, homesteader or purchaser from the Crown in right of either Canada or British Columbia of any land within the district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "partially electronic meeting" means a meeting in which persons are entitled to participate in person or by telephone or other communications medium, as set out in the notice of the meeting, if all persons attending the meeting are able to participate in it, whether by telephone, by other communications medium or in person;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "power purpose" has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "waterworks purpose" has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "works" includes all dikes, dams, weirs, locks, lock gates, flood gates, breakwaters, drains, ditches, flumes, aqueducts, pumps and pumping machinery, headworks, reservoirs, pipelines, tunnels, culverts, electric transmission lines, generators, accumulators, transformers, gauges, meters and all machinery, apparatus, plant, buildings, operation or construction of whatever kind or nature that may be necessary or convenient for the supply of water or electrical energy, or for the carrying out of drainage, diking, irrigation, waterworks, electric lighting or power development scheme, and, in the case of districts constituted by order in council under this Part for reclaiming and improving land by draining and diking, the straightening, deepening, clearing or improving or the changing of the course of any artificial or natural waterway.

heading: Electronic attendance at meetings
paragraph: 58.1		  (1) A person who is entitled to attend a meeting called under this Part may participate in and, if applicable, vote at the meeting by telephone or other communications medium if all persons attending the meeting are able to participate in it, whether by telephone, by other communications medium or in person.

heading: Electronic attendance at meetings
paragraph: (2) If the inspector, land settlement board or commissioners call an electronic meeting under this Part, the inspector, board or commissioners, as applicable, must permit and facilitate participation in the meeting by telephone or other communications medium.

heading: Electronic attendance at meetings
paragraph: (3) If the inspector, land settlement board or commissioners call a meeting under this Part that is not an electronic meeting, the inspector, board or commissioners, as applicable, are not required to take any action or provide any facility to permit or facilitate the use of any communications medium at the meeting.

heading: Electronic attendance at meetings
paragraph: (4) A person who participates in a meeting in a manner contemplated by subsection (1) is deemed, for the purposes of this Part, to be present in person.

heading: Location of meetings
paragraph:
58.2
		  If a meeting under this Part is held at a place, the place may be located in or outside the district.

heading: Commissioners a body corporation
paragraph:
59
		  (1) The commissioners of every district to which this Part applies are a corporation and may acquire, hold and dispose of property for the purposes of this Part.

heading: Commissioners a body corporation
paragraph: (2) The production of a copy of the Gazette containing notice of the order in council purporting to constitute the district is conclusive proof of the appointment of the commissioners and of the regularity of all proceedings leading to it.

heading: Power to dissolve corporation
paragraph:
60
		  On the petition of a majority in value of the owners of the land comprised in any district, and on proof to the satisfaction of the Lieutenant Governor in Council that provision has been made for the payment and discharge of all corporate debts and obligations of the commissioners of the district, and for the equitable distribution of the corporate assets of the commissioners, and on conditions and subject to provisions the Lieutenant Governor in Council thinks proper, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order published in the Gazette, revoke the incorporation of the commissioners, and declare the corporation to be dissolved.

heading: Vacancies to be filled by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph:
61
		  In the case of a vacancy in the office of commissioner, by death, resignation or removal as set out in this Part, the vacancy must be filled by the Lieutenant Governor in Council by order in council, and notice of the order in council must be published in the Gazette at the expense of the commissioners.

heading: Resignation and removal of commissioner
paragraph:
62
		  A commissioner may at any time resign, or be removed from office by the Lieutenant Governor in Council on receiving a petition signed by a majority in value of the owners in the district, and notice of the resignation or of the order in council making the removal must be published in the Gazette at the expense of the commissioners.

heading: Charge of works vested in commissioners and compliance with Water Sustainability Act
paragraph:
63
		  (1) Subject to this Part and any orders, rules or regulations made under it, full charge and authority over the extent and scope of the works and over their execution, maintenance, repair and operation is vested in the commissioners.

heading: Charge of works vested in commissioners and compliance with Water Sustainability Act
paragraph: (2) If the works proposed to be carried out include works for the diversion, storage, use or delivery of water, the commissioners must, in their corporate name, apply under the Water Sustainability Act for the approval of the undertaking of the corporation and obtain all necessary water licences, and must in all respects comply with that Act.

heading: Charge of works vested in commissioners and compliance with Water Sustainability Act
paragraph: (3) In addition to all other powers conferred on the commissioners, the commissioners have, in relation to the diversion, use, including storage, or delivery of water within the scope of the order in council constituting the district, all the powers given to a municipality under the Water Sustainability Act, and that Act applies for that purpose.

heading: Charge of works vested in commissioners and compliance with Water Sustainability Act
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of subsection (3), a reference in the Water Sustainability Act to a municipality is to be read as including a reference to a district constituted under this Part.

heading: Office and remuneration of commissioners
paragraph: 64		  (1) The office of the commissioners may be located in or out of the district and the books and records of the commissioners may be kept at that office.

heading: Office and remuneration of commissioners
paragraph: (3) The remuneration to be paid to the commissioners for their services may be determined at the meeting of the owners held under section 76 (1), and may be altered or determined at any annual meeting held under section 162.

heading: Appointment of staff
paragraph:
65
		  (1) The commissioners may appoint a clerk, collector, engineer and other subordinate officers and employees as necessary for carrying out their duties, and may set the remuneration of those employees.

heading: Appointment of staff
paragraph: (2) All appointments must be entered in the record book of the commissioners, and the entries are evidence of the appointments.

heading: Appointment of staff
paragraph: (3) The appointment of the engineer is subject to the written approval of the minister.

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph:
66
		  (1) The clerk of commissioners must keep the following:

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (a) a record of all the proceedings of the commissioners;

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (b) an account of all labour and materials furnished by the owners and their disposition;

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (c) an account of all money received and expended by the commissioners;

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (d) an account of all sinking funds and investments of them;

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (e) a copy of the assessment roll, in a book, prepared and approved in accordance with sections 75 and 76, and showing any amendments made in it by the Court of Revision, or the judge on appeal, and any changes that may be made in the ownership of the land, and all taxes levied on the land, and the respective owners of land and all payments made on account;

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (f) further records that the commissioners direct.

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (2) The clerk of commissioners must

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (a) be satisfied of, and certify, the correctness of all accounts submitted to the commissioners, and

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (b) countersign all cheques issued by them.

heading: Duties of clerk
paragraph: (3) On dismissal or resignation, the clerk of commissioners must hand over all records and papers in the clerk's hands to the commissioners, or to a person they appoint.

heading: Duties of collector
paragraph:
67
		  The collector must

heading: Duties of collector
paragraph: (a) collect all taxes, fines or money due or payable to the commissioners, and

heading: Duties of collector
paragraph: (b) deposit the money weekly in a savings institution to the credit of the commissioners.

heading: Collector to give security
paragraph:
68
		  The collector must furnish security to the satisfaction of the commissioners for the due accounting for, and payment over of, all money that may come to the collector's hands as collector, and for the faithful performance of the collector's duties, in the sum of $500, or in a larger sum as the commissioners require.

heading: Commissioner may act as clerk and collector
paragraph:
69
		  The offices of clerk and collector may be held by one person, and any commissioner may be appointed clerk or collector, or both, but a commissioner must not receive a fee for acting in that capacity.

heading: Officers as witnesses
paragraph:
70
		  Any of the following persons is a competent and compellable witness to prove any fact connected with the duties of the person's office:

heading: Officers as witnesses
paragraph: (a) a commissioner;

heading: Officers as witnesses
paragraph: (b) a clerk;

heading: Officers as witnesses
paragraph: (c) a collector;

heading: Officers as witnesses
paragraph: (d) an employee of the commissioners.

heading: Books and records open for inspection
paragraph:
71
		  (1) All books and records of the commissioners must at all reasonable times be open for the inspection of any of the owners, or of any creditor of the commissioners, on payment of 25¢ for each search and examination.

heading: Books and records open for inspection
paragraph: (2) A copy of any entry must be provided to an owner or creditor on demand and on payment of 25¢ for each folio of 100 words.

heading: Books and records open for inspection
paragraph: (3) The book referred to in section 66 must be open to inspection by the public at all reasonable times without charge.

heading: Engineer to make survey
paragraph:
72
		  (1) On the making of the order in council appointing the commissioners, the commissioners must appoint an engineer, whose appointment must be approved, to make a survey and prepare a plan in duplicate showing the land that in the engineer's opinion will be benefited by the proposed works.

heading: Engineer to make survey
paragraph: (2) One of the copies of the plan prepared under subsection (1) must be deposited in the land title office for the district in which the land is located, and one must be kept by the commissioners.

heading: Exclusion from district of land not benefited
paragraph:
73
		  (1) If the engineer, after making the survey, certifies in writing that certain land in the district constituted by the order in council appointing the commissioners will not be benefited by the proposed works, from the date of the depositing of the plan, that land ceases to be included within the limits of the district, and is free from all liability to assessment or otherwise, subject to alteration or amendment by the Court of Revision or by the judge on appeal.

heading: Exclusion from district of land not benefited
paragraph: (2) A notarial copy of the certificate must be deposited in the land title office.

heading: Enlargement of district to include other land benefited
paragraph:
74
		  (1) If the engineer, after making the survey, certifies in writing that there is other land that will be benefited by the works, but that is not within the district constituted by the order in council appointing the commissioners, that land must be included in the district.

heading: Enlargement of district to include other land benefited
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if the effect of any enlargement of the district would be that the original petitioners would not constitute a majority in value of the owners within the district so extended, the boundaries must not be extended unless a sufficient number of additional owners sign a supplementary petition so that, with the owners who signed the original petition, they constitute a majority in value of the owners of all the land within the extended district.

heading: Enlargement of district to include other land benefited
paragraph: (3) A notarial copy of the certificates and the supplementary petition, if any, must be deposited in the land title office.

heading: Engineer to prepare plan of works, estimate of cost and assessment roll
paragraph:
75
		  (1) As soon as the plan referred to in section 72 has been deposited in the land title office, the commissioners must have the engineer make

heading: Engineer to prepare plan of works, estimate of cost and assessment roll
paragraph: (a) plans of the proposed works and prepare an estimate of the cost of those works, and

heading: Engineer to prepare plan of works, estimate of cost and assessment roll
paragraph: (b) an assessment roll similar to Form I showing the area of each lot or parcel of land the subject of separate ownership within the district, the respective owners and their respective addresses.

heading: Engineer to prepare plan of works, estimate of cost and assessment roll
paragraph: (2) If the engineer is of the opinion that the benefit to be derived by the land in the district from the proposed works is not substantially a uniform benefit, the engineer must in the assessment roll divide the land into various classes according to the benefits to be derived from the proposed works, and must state the proportion that each class must bear of taxes to be levied on the land, and the owners, to meet the cost of the works and of maintenance, and all other expenses that the commissioners are authorized to raise by means of taxes under this Part.

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph:
76
		  (1) On completion of the plans and the estimate of cost referred to in section 75, and before the preparation of the assessment roll, the commissioners must, by giving notice in accordance with section 76.1, call a meeting of the owners to consider whether or not the works as detailed in the plans and estimate are to be executed, and to set the remuneration of the commissioners.

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (3) Every owner is entitled to vote at the meeting in person or by proxy, and may by instrument in writing filed with the commissioners appoint a person a proxy to represent the owner at the meeting.

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (4) All questions at the meeting must be determined by the majority in value of the owners voting on it and not by the number voting.

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (5) The meeting may appoint a chair and a secretary, and may determine

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (a) that the works be executed as detailed in the plans and estimate,

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (b) that the plans and estimate be returned to the commissioners for amendments that the meeting specifies, or

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (c) that the commissioners are not to take any further steps toward executing the works.

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (6) If the meeting determines that the plans and estimate are to be returned to the commissioners for amendment, the commissioners must have new plans and estimates prepared and submitted to another meeting of the owners, convened in a similar manner to the first meeting.

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (7) If the plans and estimate of cost are approved by the owners, at the first or at any subsequent meeting of the owners, the engineer must proceed to prepare the assessment roll in accordance with section 75.

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (8) On completion of the assessment roll,

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (a) the plans, estimate of cost and assessment roll must be signed in duplicate by the commissioners and engineer, and

heading: Meeting of owners
paragraph: (b) one copy of each must be deposited in the land title office and the other copy kept by the commissioners.

heading: Notice of meeting respecting works and remuneration
paragraph:
76.1
		  (1) Notice of a meeting called under section 76 must include

heading: Notice of meeting respecting works and remuneration
paragraph: (a) the date, time and, if applicable, place of the meeting,

heading: Notice of meeting respecting works and remuneration
paragraph: (b) a description of the purpose of the meeting, and

heading: Notice of meeting respecting works and remuneration
paragraph: (c) if the meeting is an electronic meeting, instructions for attending and participating in the meeting by telephone or other communications medium, including instructions for voting at the meeting.

heading: Notice of meeting respecting works and remuneration
paragraph: (2) The notice must be given not less than 10 days before the date of the meeting

heading: Notice of meeting respecting works and remuneration
paragraph: (a) by delivering it to each owner, and

heading: Notice of meeting respecting works and remuneration
paragraph: (b) by posting it in at least 3 conspicuous public places in the district.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph:
77
		  (1) This section applies only to drainage, diking or development districts constituted under this Part after March 31, 1919.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (2) After the expiration of the time limited for an appeal against the assessment roll provided by section 93, or if an appeal has been taken, then after the appeal has been adjudicated, the commissioners must, by giving notice in accordance with section 77.1, call a general meeting of the owners, to be held in the following January at a time they think convenient, in order to do the following:

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (a) elect a commissioner for the term of one year, a commissioner for the term of 2 years and a commissioner for the term of 3 years;

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (b) set the date at which annual general meetings must be held;

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (c) receive from the commissioners who have been in office a report on the condition of the works and a statement of the financial condition of the district;

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (d) discuss with the commissioners any matters relating to the works or finances of the district;

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (e) set the remuneration of the commissioners for the ensuing year.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (4) In each subsequent year, the commissioners must, by giving notice in accordance with section 77.1, call a general meeting for the purposes specified in subsection (2), but only one commissioner must be elected at any subsequent annual general meeting.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (5) At the general meeting provided for in subsection (2), and at any annual meeting after that, the owners may appoint a chair and secretary, and pass resolutions in accordance with the powers granted to them by this Part.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (6) The secretary must enter the resolutions and the result of any election in a book provided by the commissioners for that purpose.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (7) The commissioners must at once file with the comptroller copies of all reports and statements submitted by the commissioners, copies of the resolutions passed by the meeting and a certificate from the chair of the election of a commissioner or commissioners, together with the names of the commissioners elected.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (8) If at an annual general meeting the owners in a district fail to elect a commissioner, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may appoint a person as a commissioner for the district.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (9) A commissioner appointed under subsection (8) has the same rights and powers and holds office for the same term as if elected at the annual general meeting.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted after March 31, 1919
paragraph: (10) All appointments, elections and resolutions at a general meeting under this section must be determined by a majority in value of the owners present at the meeting and voting.

heading: Notice of general meeting
paragraph:
77.1
		  (1) Notice of a meeting called under section 77 must include

heading: Notice of general meeting
paragraph: (a) the date, time and, if applicable, place of the meeting,

heading: Notice of general meeting
paragraph: (b) a description of the purpose of the meeting, and

heading: Notice of general meeting
paragraph: (c) if the meeting is an electronic meeting, instructions for attending and participating in the meeting by telephone or other communications medium, including instructions for voting at the meeting.

heading: Notice of general meeting
paragraph: (2) The notice must be given not less than 15 days before the date of the meeting

heading: Notice of general meeting
paragraph: (a) by delivering it to each owner, and

heading: Notice of general meeting
paragraph: (b) by posting it in at least 3 conspicuous public places in the district.

heading: Methods of executing works
paragraph:
78
		  (1) The commissioners may, with the approval of a majority in value of the owners, execute the proposed works by means of labour, teams, tools and materials provided by the owners, or the commissioners may without that approval cause all or any part of the works to be executed, maintained or repaired by contract, and for that purpose may enter into a contract with any person.

heading: Methods of executing works
paragraph: (2) A contract under subsection (1) may be made subject to and contain powers, conditions and agreements as agreed on.

heading: Methods of executing works
paragraph: (3) The commissioners may pay for the contract by levying a tax on the owners based on and in accordance with the assessments contained in the assessment roll, or the commissioners may borrow money to pay for the cost of the works in accordance with this Act.

heading: Determination of owners not to execute works
paragraph:
79
		  (1) If the owners, at the first or at a subsequent meeting of owners held under section 76, determine that the commissioners are not to take any further steps toward executing the works, after that the commissioners only have power to levy on the land, and the owners of the land, taxes sufficient to pay the expenses incurred by the commissioners.

heading: Determination of owners not to execute works
paragraph: (2) On collection of the taxes and payment of the expenses, the corporation constituted for that district under section 59 ceases to exist.

heading: When commissioners may proceed with works
paragraph:
80
		  The commissioners must not proceed with the execution of the works set out in the order in council under which they are appointed until the expiry of the time limited for appeal against the present assessment roll.

heading: Purposes for which commissioners may levy taxes
paragraph:
81
		  (1) The commissioners may levy taxes to raise money for the following purposes:

heading: Purposes for which commissioners may levy taxes
