		  (1) If a dike or other portion of any works executed is injured by an owner or occupier in the district pasturing cattle or horses on marshes or other land adjacent to the dike, or making a road over the dike, or interfering with or breaking any watercourse constructed by the commissioners, or by any other act or default of an owner or occupier, the commissioners may make an order on that person as often as occasion requires to repair the injury at once or by a certain day to be named in the order, and in the case of a refusal to obey the order, or in case the commissioners consider it to be one of sudden emergency, the commissioners must repair the injury.

heading: Damage to dike
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes the order of the commissioners must forfeit and pay to the commissioners for every offence a sum of not more than $50, which, with the costs of repair, may be recovered by suit in a court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the commissioners.

heading: Damage to dike
paragraph: (3) In the case of an emergency the commissioners may recover from the person causing or allowing the injury to be done the costs of repair, which must be recovered as a debt due to the commissioners in a court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Wilful injury to works
paragraph:
159
		  If a person in any manner wilfully injures works executed under this Part or interferes with the commissioners in carrying out the works authorized under this Part, the person must forfeit for each offence a sum of not more than $50, together with the costs of the repair, which may be recovered on summary conviction before a justice.

heading: Commissioners not liable for acts of predecessors
paragraph:
160
		  A commissioner is not liable for an act of the commissioner's predecessor in office, about work in which the commissioner is engaged, except for money the commissioner might or could have collected on account of work done by the predecessor.

heading: How notice is to be given
paragraph:
161
		  Except as otherwise directed by this Part, a notice required to be given must be a written notice served on the parties in person, or left at their last known place of residence, or sent by registered letter mailed to their last address.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph:
162
		  (1) This section applies only to a district constituted before April 1, 1919.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (1.1) Each year, the commissioners of a district must, by giving notice in accordance with section 162.1, call a general meeting of the ratepayers of the district, to be held on a date not earlier than January 15 and not later than January 31 of that year.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (1.2) The commissioners must submit to the meeting

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (a) a report on the condition of the works under their charge, and

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (b) a statement of the financial condition of the district.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (1.3) At the meeting, the commissioners may discuss with the ratepayers matters relating to the condition and maintenance of the works under their charge.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (2) Any 3 owners in a district to which this section applies may, on or before December 31 in any year, give notice in writing to the commissioners that at the next annual general meeting they will move that the Lieutenant Governor in Council be requested to order that one of the commissioners retire from office at the end of one year after the meeting, and another at the end of 2 years after the meeting, and another at the end of 3 years after the meeting.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (3) If notice of a resolution is given under subsection (2), the notice referred to in subsection (1.1) must include a statement that the resolution will be submitted to the meeting.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (4) If the resolution is passed, a copy of the resolution must be forwarded to the minister, and on the recommendation of the minister the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order in council, provide that the commissioners must retire, and when each commissioner must retire.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (5) At any annual general meeting after that the owners may appoint a chair and secretary, and must elect a commissioner for a term of 3 years, and pass resolutions in accordance with the powers granted them by this Part.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (6) The secretary must enter the resolutions and the result of elections in a book provided by the commissioners for that purpose, and the commissioners must at once file with the comptroller copies of all reports and statements submitted by the commissioners, copies of the resolutions passed by the meeting, and a certificate from the chair of the election of a commissioner, together with the name of the commissioner elected.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (7) If, at an annual general meeting, the owners in any district fail to elect a commissioner, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may appoint a person a commissioner for the district, and the commissioner appointed has the same rights and powers and holds office for the same term as if elected at an annual meeting.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (8) All appointments, elections and resolutions at a general meeting under this section must be determined by a majority in value of the owners present in person or by proxy at the meeting and voting on them.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (9) Every instrument appointing a proxy for this section must be in writing signed by the appointor or an attorney authorized in writing, or, if the appointor is a corporation, under its common seal or by an authorized attorney.

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (10) A person must not act as a proxy unless the person

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (a) is the owner of land in the district, and

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (b) either

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (i)  is qualified on the person's own behalf to vote at the meeting at which the person acts as proxy, or

heading: Annual meetings in district constituted before April 1, 1919
paragraph: (ii)  has been appointed to act at that meeting as proxy for a corporation.

heading: Notice of annual meeting of ratepayers
paragraph:
162.1
		  (1) Notice of a meeting called under section 162 must include

heading: Notice of annual meeting of ratepayers
paragraph: (a) the date, time and, if applicable, place of the meeting,

heading: Notice of annual meeting of ratepayers
paragraph: (b) a description of the purpose of the meeting, and

heading: Notice of annual meeting of ratepayers
paragraph: (c) if the meeting is an electronic meeting, instructions for attending and participating in the meeting by telephone or other communications medium, including instructions for voting at the meeting.

heading: Notice of annual meeting of ratepayers
paragraph: (2) The notice must be given not less than 10 days before the date of the meeting

heading: Notice of annual meeting of ratepayers
paragraph: (a) by posting it in a conspicuous place at each post office in the district, or

heading: Notice of annual meeting of ratepayers
paragraph: (b) if there is no post office in the district, by posting it in at least 3 conspicuous public places in the district.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
163
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) providing for the procedure to be followed in any proceeding, petition, application, complaint, reference or appeal;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing the forms to be used by commissioners;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) providing for the procedure at elections.

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: 164		  (1) If an owner is dissatisfied with an order or decision of the comptroller, the owner may appeal to the minister.

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: (2) An owner who appeals must

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: (a) within 10 days after the date of the order or decision, serve the comptroller with a written notice of the owner's intention to appeal to the minister, stating the grounds of the appeal, and

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: (b) within 30 days after the date, apply to the minister to set a day for the hearing of the appeal.

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: (3) The minister must set a day and place for the hearing of the appeal, notice of which must be given in writing by the comptroller to those interested persons as the minister may direct.

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: (4) At the time and place set by the minister, the minister must hear in a summary manner the appeal and the evidence given on oath, and may adjourn the hearing and defer judgment as the minister thinks advisable.

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: (5) The minister may direct the comptroller to amend or cancel the order or decision, or may order a rehearing or may dismiss the appeal.

heading: Appeal to minister from comptroller
paragraph: (6) Costs of the appeal must not be allowed to any party.

heading: Sections applicable on transfer of duties
paragraph:
165
		  (1) Sections 77, 162, 163 and 164 do not apply in districts where the powers and duties of the commissioners have been transferred to an inspector of dikes or to the land settlement board.

heading: Sections applicable on transfer of duties
paragraph: (2) In districts referred to in subsection (1), the inspector or board must, by giving notice in accordance with section 165.1, call a general meeting of the owners for the purpose of receiving a report on the condition of the works and a statement of financial condition of the district, and to discuss any matters relating to the works or the finances of the district.

heading: Inspector's or board's notice of general meeting of owners
paragraph:
165.1
		  (1) Notice of a meeting called under section 165 must include

heading: Inspector's or board's notice of general meeting of owners
paragraph: (a) the date, time and, if applicable, place of the meeting,

heading: Inspector's or board's notice of general meeting of owners
paragraph: (b) a description of the purpose of the meeting, and

heading: Inspector's or board's notice of general meeting of owners
paragraph: (c) if the meeting is an electronic meeting, instructions for attending and participating in the meeting by telephone or other communications medium, including instructions for voting at the meeting.

heading: Inspector's or board's notice of general meeting of owners
paragraph: (2) The notice must be given not less than 10 days before the date of the meeting

heading: Inspector's or board's notice of general meeting of owners
paragraph: (a) by delivering it to each owner, and

heading: Inspector's or board's notice of general meeting of owners
paragraph: (b) by posting it in at least 3 conspicuous public places in the district.

heading: Order of transference
paragraph:
166
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may order that the powers and duties of the commissioners of any district be transferred to an inspector of dikes.

heading: Order of transference
paragraph: (2) In an order under subsection (1) or in a subsequent order, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may give discretion to the minister to further transfer the powers and duties of the commissioners of the district from the inspector to a municipality or regional district.

heading: Order of transference
paragraph: (3) The minister may make an order transferring the powers and duties of the commissioners of the district from the inspector to a municipality or regional district if

heading: Order of transference
paragraph: (a) permitted to do so under subsection (2), or

heading: Order of transference
paragraph: (b) despite subsection (2), the municipality or regional district requests the transfer.

heading: Effect of order
paragraph:
167
		  (1) On the making of an order under section 166 (1), the inspector of dikes named in the order and the inspector's successors in office

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (a) are a corporation under the name of the inspector of dikes of the district,

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (b) have power to acquire, hold and dispose of property for the purposes of this Part, and

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (c) are vested with all the powers and subject to all the duties of the commissioners under this Part.

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (2) On the making of an order under section 166 (1), the appointment and office of the commissioners for the district is abrogated.

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (3) On the making of an order under section 166 (3), the municipality or regional district named in the order holds separate corporate status under the name of the district, and that corporation

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (a) has the power to acquire, hold and dispose of property for the purposes of this Part, and

heading: Effect of order
paragraph: (b) is vested with all the powers and subject to all the duties of the commissioners under this Part.

heading: Commissioner to prepare statement of accounts and transfer all documents
paragraph:
168
		  On the making of an order under section 166 (1), the commissioners whose powers are transferred must

heading: Commissioner to prepare statement of accounts and transfer all documents
paragraph: (a) at once prepare and forward to the inspector of dikes to whom the powers are transferred a true and accurate statement of the accounts of the commissioners, and

heading: Commissioner to prepare statement of accounts and transfer all documents
paragraph: (b) deliver to the inspector of dikes all deeds, accounts, books of accounts, vouchers, receipts, letters, memoranda, papers, writings, maps, plans and documents relating to the affairs of the district.

heading: Dissolving development districts
paragraph:
170
		  (1) In this section, "development district" includes a district, and every drainage, diking or development district incorporated before January 1, 1965 under any Act except the Water Act.

heading: Dissolving development districts
paragraph: (2) Despite any other statute, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may dissolve any development district.

heading: Dissolving development districts
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations to carry out the spirit and intent of this section.

heading: Transfer of development district assets
paragraph: 170.1		  If a development district is dissolved under section 170, the minister responsible for the administration of the Local Government Act may transfer, to either the municipality or to the regional district in which the works of the development district were located, its assets, rights, claims, obligations and liabilities and section 171 or 172 applies, as applicable.

heading: Transfer to a municipality
paragraph: (2) After a transfer to a municipality under section 170.1 has been made, the area that was included in the development district is deemed to be a local service area under Division 5 [Local Service Taxes] of Part 7 of the Community Charter, and for these purposes that Division applies.

heading: Transfer to a municipality
paragraph: (3) If the works of a development district are located in more than one municipality, the municipalities may assume the assets, rights, claims, obligations and liabilities in accordance with the apportionment set out in the order dissolving the development district, and that portion of the development district in each municipality is a local service area of that municipality.

heading: Transfer to a municipality
paragraph: (4) A council may provide that some or all of the assets of the development district be credited to the local service area and that some or all of the liabilities be charged to the local service area.

heading: Transfer to a municipality
paragraph: (5) Without limiting section 8 (1) [natural person powers] of the Community Charter, a council may enter into an agreement with the Provincial government for the joint undertaking of additional works of a similar nature and for their maintenance.

heading: Transfer to a municipality
paragraph: (6) A council may, by bylaw adopted without the assent of the electors or approval of the electors but otherwise in accordance with the Community Charter, borrow sums required under any agreement with the Provincial government.

heading: Transfer to a municipality
paragraph: (7) The entire cost or the parts of the cost of an existing work or a work to be constructed under the terms of an agreement under this section, and of its maintenance and operation, as may be determined by the council, must be borne by the owners of real property in the local service area.

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: 172		  (1) After a transfer to a regional district under section 170.1 has been made, the area that was included in the development district is deemed to be a service area under Part 10 [Regional Districts: Service Structure and Establishing Bylaws] of the Local Government Act and, for these purposes, the following apply:

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (a) the following Divisions of Part 10 of that Act:

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (i)  Division 3 [Establishing Bylaws for Services];

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (ii)  Division 4 [Approval of Establishing Bylaws];

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (iii)  Division 5 [Changes to Establishing Bylaws];

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (b) the following Divisions of Part 11 [Regional Districts: Financial Management] of that Act:

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (i)  Division 2 [Cost Recovery for Services];

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (ii)  Division 3 [Requisition and Tax Collection];

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (iii)  Division 4 [Tax Rates and Exemptions].

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (2) If the works of a development district are located in more than one regional district, the regional districts may assume the assets, rights, claims, obligations and liabilities in accordance with the apportionment set out in the order dissolving the development district, and that portion of the development district in each regional district is a service area of that regional district.

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (3) A board may provide that some or all of the assets of the development district be credited to the service area and that some or all of the liabilities be charged to the service area.

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (4) Without limiting section 263 [corporate powers] of the Local Government Act, a board may enter into an agreement with the Provincial government for the joint undertaking of additional works of a similar nature and for their maintenance.

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (5) A board may, by bylaw adopted without the assent or approval of the electors but otherwise in accordance with the Local Government Act, borrow sums required under any agreement with the Provincial government.

heading: Transfer to a regional district
paragraph: (6) The entire cost or the parts of the cost of an existing work or a work to be constructed under the terms of an agreement under this section, and of its maintenance and operation, as may be determined by the board, must be borne by the owners of real property in the service area.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquifer" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assessment" means an assessment under section 18 [water source and system assessments];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "construction permit" means a permit required under section 7 [construction permits and requirements for water supply            systems];

heading: Definitions
Definitions
paragraph: "domestic purposes" means the use of water for

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) human consumption, food preparation or sanitation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) household purposes not covered by paragraph (a), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) other prescribed purposes;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"domestic water system" means a system by which water is
            provided or offered for domestic purposes, including

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) works used to obtain intake water,

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b) equipment, works and facilities used for treatment, diversion, storage,
              pumping, transmission and distribution,

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(c) any other equipment, works or facilities prescribed by regulation as being
              included,

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(d) a tank truck, vehicle water tank or other prescribed means of transporting
              drinking water, whether or not there are any related works or facilities,
              and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) the intake water and the water in the system,

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
but excluding equipment, works or facilities prescribed by regulation as being
            excluded;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "drill", in relation to a well, has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "drinking water" means water used or intended to be used for            domestic purposes;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "drinking water health hazard" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(a) a condition or thing in relation to drinking water that does or is likely
              to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  endanger the public health, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  prevent or hinder the prevention or suppression of disease,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a prescribed condition or thing, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(c) a prescribed condition or thing that fails to meet a prescribed
              standard;

heading: Definitions
Definitions
paragraph:
"drinking water protection plan" means a drinking water
            protection plan approved by the Lieutenant Governor in Council under section 34 [approval of drinking water protection plan];

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"drinking water source" means a stream, reservoir, well or
            aquifer from which drinking water is taken;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "groundwater" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"immediate reporting standard" means, in relation to a water            supply system, a standard established by regulation or operating permit as an immediate
            reporting standard for the purposes of section 12 [notice if immediate reporting standard not met];

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"intake water" means, in relation to a domestic water system,
            the water at or near the point of intake into the system;

heading: Definitions
Definitions
paragraph:
"laboratory" means a corporation, agency or other person
            engaged in conducting analyses for the purposes of this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local authority" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a local government,

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b) an improvement district, as defined in the Local Government                  Act, that is responsible for the provision of drinking
              water,

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b.1) a greater board, as defined in the Community                  Charter, that is responsible for the provision of drinking
              water, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(c) a local body prescribed by regulation as a local authority for the purposes of
              the provision in which the term appears;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local government" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the council of a municipality,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the board of a regional district, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a local trust committee under the Islands Trust                  Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"medical health officer" has the same meaning as in the
              Public Health Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "operating permit" means a permit under section 8 [operating permits and requirements for water supply            systems];

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"owner" in relation to a water supply system
            includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person who is

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(i)  responsible for the ongoing operation of the water supply system,
                or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  in charge of managing that operation, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(i)  parts of the water supply system are owned by different persons,
                or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  all or part of the system is jointly owned by different persons,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: all of those persons;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"potable water" means water provided by a domestic water system
            that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) meets the standards prescribed by regulation, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b) is safe to drink and fit for domestic purposes without further
              treatment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"prescribed water supply system" means a water supply system
            that is of a class prescribed by regulation or is prescribed by regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "private dwelling" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a structure that is occupied as a private residence, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b) if only part of a structure is occupied as a private residence, that part of
              the structure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"Provincial health officer" has the same meaning as in the
              Public Health Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"threat" means, in relation to drinking water, a condition or            thing, or circumstances that may lead to a condition or thing, that may result in
            drinking water provided by a domestic water system not being potable water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"water supplier" means a person who is the owner of a water
            supply system;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"water supply system" means a domestic water system, other
            than

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(a) a domestic water system that serves only one single-family residence,
              and

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b) equipment, works or facilities prescribed by regulation as being
              excluded;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "well" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"well recharge zone" means the area of land from which water            percolates into an aquifer and is transmitted from there into one or more wells that are
            used, or are intended to be used, to provide drinking water.

heading: Relationship with other Acts
paragraph:
2
		  (1) The authority that is provided under this Act is in addition to and does not
            restrict authority provided under any other enactment that may be used to protect
            drinking water.

heading: Relationship with other Acts
paragraph:
(2) Nothing in this Act affects the powers, duties and functions of a medical health
            officer under the Public Health Act or any other            enactment.

heading: Drinking water officers
paragraph:
3
		  (1) Unless another person is appointed under subsection (2), the drinking
            water officer for an area is

heading: Drinking water officers
paragraph:
(a) the person appointed by the medical health officer as the drinking water
              officer, or

heading: Drinking water officers
paragraph:
(b) if no appointment is made under paragraph (a), the medical
              health officer.

heading: Drinking water officers
paragraph:
(2) The minister may, by order, appoint persons, by name or by title, as drinking
            water officers and establish the area of their jurisdiction.

heading: Drinking water officers
paragraph:
(3) In determining the qualifications for appointments under subsection
              (2), the minister must consult with the Provincial health
            officer.

heading: Drinking water officers
paragraph:
(4) Subject to the regulations, a drinking water officer may, in writing, delegate
            to any person a power or duty of the drinking water officer under this or another
            enactment.

heading:
Guidelines and directives respecting drinking water
          protection
paragraph:
4
		  (1) The minister may establish

heading:
Guidelines and directives respecting drinking water
          protection
paragraph: (a) guidelines that must be considered, and

heading:
Guidelines and directives respecting drinking water
          protection
paragraph: (b) directives that must be followed

heading:
Guidelines and directives respecting drinking water
          protection
paragraph:
by drinking water officers and other officials in exercising powers and
            performing duties or functions under this Act and the Public Health                Act in relation to drinking water.

heading:
Guidelines and directives respecting drinking water
          protection
paragraph:
(2) The Provincial health officer must monitor compliance of drinking water officers
            with guidelines and directives established under this section.

heading: Annual drinking water protection report
paragraph:
4.1
		  (1) The Provincial health officer must prepare and deliver to the minister an annual
            report respecting activities under this Act for the past year.

heading: Annual drinking water protection report
paragraph: (2) After receiving an annual report under subsection (1),

heading: Annual drinking water protection report
paragraph:
(a) the minister must promptly lay the report before the Legislative Assembly if
              it is in session, or

heading: Annual drinking water protection report
paragraph:
(b) if the Legislative Assembly is not in session, the minister must file the
              report with the Clerk of the Legislative Assembly.

heading:
Reports respecting problems related to Provincial government
          actions
paragraph:
4.2
		  (1) The Provincial health officer must report to the minister on any situation
            that

heading:
Reports respecting problems related to Provincial government
          actions
paragraph:
(a) in the opinion of the Provincial health officer, significantly impedes the
              protection of public health in relation to drinking water, and

heading:
Reports respecting problems related to Provincial government
          actions
paragraph:
(b) arises in relation to the actions or inaction of one or more ministries,
              government corporations or other agents of the government.

heading:
Reports respecting problems related to Provincial government
          actions
paragraph:
(2) If the Provincial health officer makes a report under subsection
              (1) and the situation cannot be resolved to the satisfaction of the
            Provincial health officer, the minister must bring the situation to the attention of the
            Executive Council.

heading: Drinking water advisory committees
paragraph:
5
		  (1) The minister may, after consultation with the Provincial health officer,
            establish an advisory committee to provide advice and recommendations with respect to
            drinking water matters referred to the committee by the minister.

heading: Drinking water advisory committees
paragraph:
(2) Without limiting subsection (1), the minister may establish an advisory
            committee to provide advice and recommendations respecting standards and requirements to
            be established under this Act.

heading: Drinking water advisory committees
paragraph: (3) A person appointed to an advisory committee

heading: Drinking water advisory committees
paragraph:
(a) must be reimbursed in accordance with the directives of Treasury Board for
              reasonable travelling and out of pocket expenses necessarily incurred in discharging
              the person's duties under this Act, and

heading: Drinking water advisory committees
paragraph:
(b) may be paid remuneration in accordance with the directives of Treasury Board,
              if the person is not an employee under the Public Service                  Act.

heading: Water supply systems must provide potable water
paragraph:
6
		  Subject to the regulations, a water supplier must provide, to the users served by
          its water supply system, drinking water from the water supply system that

heading: Water supply systems must provide potable water
paragraph: (a) is potable water, and

heading: Water supply systems must provide potable water
paragraph:
(b) meets any additional requirements established by the regulations or by its
            operating permit.

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
7
		  (1) This section applies in relation to the construction, installation, alteration
            or extension of

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph: (a) a water supply system, or

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(b) works, facilities or equipment that are intended to be a water supply system
              or part of a water supply system.

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, a person

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(a) must not undertake activities referred to in subsection (1) unless a
              construction permit for this has been issued in accordance with the regulations,
              and

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph: (b) must not undertake those activities except

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(i)  in accordance with the regulations or the plans approved in accordance with
                the regulations, and

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(ii)  in accordance with the terms and conditions of the construction
                permit.

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(3) In addition to any other requirements established by the regulations, a person
            applying for a construction permit must submit to an issuing official,

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(a) in the case of a permit for the construction of a water supply system, the
              results of water quality analyses in accordance with the regulations, and

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(b) in any case, the results of any water quality analyses required by the issuing
              official or drinking water officer.

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(4) The issuing official may refuse to issue a permit until satisfied that the
            applicant has identified an owner of the water supply system who is to be responsible
            for the ongoing operation of the system, or in charge of managing that operation, in
            accordance with this Act.

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(4.1) An issuing official may include in a construction permit terms and conditions
            the official considers advisable respecting the construction, installation, alteration
            or extension.

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(5) Terms and conditions included in a construction permit may set requirements and
            standards that are more stringent than those established by the regulations.

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph: (6) A construction permit

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(a) is valid for one year, unless a different period is specified in the
              permit,

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(b) is not transferable unless the transfer is approved by an issuing official,
              and

heading:
Construction permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(c) cannot be varied except by the issuance of a new construction
              permit.

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
8
		  (1) In the case of a prescribed water supply system, the water supplier

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(a) must not operate the water supply system unless the water supplier holds a
              valid operating permit issued in accordance with the regulations,

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(b) must comply with all terms and conditions of its operating permit,
              and

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(c) must operate the water supply system in accordance with any applicable
              regulations.

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(2) An issuing official may include in an operating permit terms and conditions the
            official considers advisable respecting the water supply system.

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(3) As examples, but without limiting the authority under this section, terms and
            conditions respecting the following may be included in an operating permit:

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph: (a) treatment requirements;

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph: (b) equipment, works, facilities and operating requirements;

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(c) qualifications and training of the persons operating, maintaining or repairing
              the water supply system;

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(d) monitoring of the drinking water source and the water in the water supply
              system;

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph: (e) standards applicable to the water in the water supply system;

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(f) reporting and publication of monitoring results or other information
              respecting the water supply system.

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(4) The drinking water officer or an issuing official may change the terms and
            conditions of an operating permit if the officer or issuing official considers this
            advisable, but must first consult with the water supplier respecting the proposed
            changes and must consider any comments of the water supplier in response.

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(5) Terms and conditions included in an operating permit under this section may set
            requirements and standards that are more stringent than those established under this
            Act.

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(6) If the drinking water officer considers that further information is necessary to
            determine whether

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(a) the water provided by a water supply system meets the requirements of
                section
                6 [water supply systems must provide potable water], or

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(b) a water supply system meets the requirements and standards established by the
              regulations and its operating permit,

heading:
Operating permits and requirements for water supply
          systems
paragraph:
the drinking water officer may order the water supplier to undertake additional
            monitoring or testing as directed by the officer, and to report the results and make
            them public as directed by the officer.

heading:
Qualification standards for persons operating water supply
          systems
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, a person must not operate, maintain or repair a
            prescribed water supply system unless

heading:
Qualification standards for persons operating water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(a) the person is qualified in accordance with the regulations to do this,
              or

heading:
Qualification standards for persons operating water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(b) is doing this under the supervision of a person who is qualified in accordance
              with the regulations.

heading:
Qualification standards for persons operating water supply
          systems
paragraph:
(2) A water supplier must ensure that subsection (1) is not
            contravened in relation to its water supply system.

heading: Emergency response and contingency plans
paragraph:
10
		  (1) In the case of a prescribed water supply system, the water supplier must have a
            written emergency response and contingency plan in accordance with the regulations, to
            be implemented in the event of an emergency or abnormal operational circumstances
            affecting its water supply system or drinking water source.

heading: Emergency response and contingency plans
paragraph:
(2) The drinking water officer may order a water supplier to review and update its
            emergency response and contingency plan.

heading: Water monitoring requirements
paragraph:
11
		  (1) In the case of a prescribed water supply system, the water supplier
            must

heading: Water monitoring requirements
paragraph:
(a) monitor its drinking water source, the water in its system and the water it
              provides for the parameters, and at the frequency, established by the regulations and
              by its operating permit,

heading: Water monitoring requirements
paragraph:
(b) have the sampling required for that monitoring carried out in accordance with
              the regulations and the directions of the drinking water officer, and

heading: Water monitoring requirements
paragraph:
(c) have the analyses required for that monitoring carried out in accordance with
              the regulations, through laboratories that meet the requirements established by the
              regulations and by individuals who are qualified in accordance with the
              regulations.

heading: Water monitoring requirements
paragraph:
(2) The laboratory conducting monitoring analyses under this section must report the
            results in accordance with the regulations to the drinking water officer and, subject to
            the regulations, to the water supplier.

heading: Water monitoring requirements
paragraph:
(3) A water supplier must ensure that a laboratory conducting monitoring analyses
            under this section is aware of the applicable standards and requirements established by
            the regulations and the operating permit for the water supply system.

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph:
12
		  (1) If a monitored parameter in relation to a water supply system fails to meet an
            established immediate reporting standard for that system, the laboratory conducting the
            analysis must immediately give notice to

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph: (a) the water supplier,

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph: (b) the drinking water officer, and

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph: (c) the medical health officer.

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph:
(2) In addition, a water supplier who receives notice under subsection
              (1) must give immediate notice to the drinking water officer advising that
            the water supplier has been notified by the laboratory as required by this
            section.

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph:
(3) For the purposes of this section, the person giving the immediate notice
            must

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph:
(a) take all reasonable steps to give this notice by speaking directly to or by
              telephone with

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph: (i)  each person required to be notified,

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph:
(ii)  a person designated for this purpose by the person required to be notified,
                or

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph:
(iii)  a person answering the telephone number designated for this purpose by the
                person required to be notified, and

heading: Notice if immediate reporting standard not met
paragraph: (b) follow with notice in writing to each person within 24 hours.

heading: Water supplier must report threats to drinking water
paragraph:
13
		  (1) In addition to the requirements under section 12, a water supplier
            must immediately notify the drinking water officer if the supplier considers there is a
            threat that is likely to result in the drinking water provided by its water supply
            system not meeting the requirements of section 6 [water supply systems must provide potable water].

heading: Water supplier must report threats to drinking water
paragraph:
(2) Notice required by subsection (1) must be given in accordance with section 12
              (3).

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph:
14
		  (1) The drinking water officer may request or order a water supplier to give public
            notice in a manner approved by the drinking water officer, or in accordance with the
            directions of the drinking water officer, if

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph: (a) the drinking water officer has received a report under section 12 [notice if immediate reporting standard not met],

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph: (b) the drinking water officer has received a report under section 13 [water supplier must report threats], or

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph:
(c) the drinking water officer considers that there is, was or may be a threat to
              the drinking water provided by a water supply system.

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph:
(2) In addition to any requirement under subsection (1), if a water
            supplier

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph:
(a) has received a report under section 12 or considers that
              there may otherwise be a drinking water health hazard in relation to its water supply
              system, and

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph: (b) is not able to immediately notify the drinking water officer,

heading: Public notice of threats to drinking water
paragraph:
the water supplier must immediately give notice of the possible hazard to the
            users of drinking water from that water supply system.

heading: Publication of other information
paragraph:
15
		  A water supplier must ensure that the following information is made public in
          accordance with the regulations and any requirements of the drinking water
          officer:

heading: Publication of other information
paragraph: (a) the water supplier's emergency response and contingency plan;

heading: Publication of other information
Publication of other information
paragraph: (c) if applicable, its current assessment under section 18 [water source and system assessments];

heading: Publication of other information
paragraph: (d) if applicable, its current plan under section 22 [assessment response plans];

heading: Publication of other information
paragraph:
(e) other information required to be made public by the regulations, its operating
            permit or the drinking water officer.

heading:
Floodproofing required for drinking water and other
          wells
paragraph:
16
		  (1) If required by regulation, the owner or operator of a well that provides
            drinking water must floodproof the well in accordance with the regulations.

heading:
Floodproofing required for drinking water and other
          wells
paragraph:
(2) For the purpose of protecting the drinking water provided by a well that is
            subject to a requirement under subsection (1), the drinking water officer may, by
            order,

heading:
Floodproofing required for drinking water and other
          wells
paragraph:
(a) require the owner or operator of another well that the drinking water officer
              has reason to believe

heading:
Floodproofing required for drinking water and other
          wells
paragraph: (i)  is in the same well recharge zone, or

heading:
Floodproofing required for drinking water and other
          wells
paragraph: (ii)  may otherwise affect the drinking water well

heading:
Floodproofing required for drinking water and other
          wells
paragraph: to floodproof the other well in accordance with the regulations, or

heading:
Floodproofing required for drinking water and other
          wells
paragraph:
(b) if the drinking water officer is not reasonably able to determine who is the
              owner or operator of the other well, require the owner of the land on which that well
              is located to floodproof that well in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Water supply systems with multiple owners
paragraph:
17
		  (1) If a water supply system is owned by 2 or more persons, or parts of the water
            supply system are owned by different persons, the drinking water officer may require
            those persons

heading: Water supply systems with multiple owners
paragraph:
(a) to designate one of their number for the purposes of receiving and providing
              information and records as required or authorized under this Act, and

heading: Water supply systems with multiple owners
paragraph:
(b) to provide to the drinking water officer the person's name, address and other
              contact information as required by the drinking water officer.

heading: Water supply systems with multiple owners
paragraph:
(2) If subsection (1) applies and the owners do not make the required
            designation, the drinking water officer may designate one of the owners for the purposes
            of this section.

heading: Water source and system assessments
paragraph:
18
		  (1) A water supplier must prepare an assessment in accordance with this Part if
            required by the regulations or ordered by the drinking water officer.

heading: Water source and system assessments
paragraph: (2) The purpose of an assessment is to identify, inventory and assess

heading: Water source and system assessments
paragraph:
(a) the drinking water source for the water supply system, including land use and
              other activities and conditions that may affect that source,

heading: Water source and system assessments
paragraph: (b) the water supply system, including treatment and operation,

heading: Water source and system assessments
paragraph:
(c) monitoring requirements for the drinking water source and water supply system,
              and

heading: Water source and system assessments
paragraph: (d) threats to drinking water that is provided by the system.

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
19
		  (1) In addition to any requirement established by regulation, the drinking water
            officer may order a water supplier to prepare an assessment if

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
(a) the drinking water officer has reason to believe that an assessment is
              necessary to properly identify and assess threats to drinking water in relation to the
              water supply system, or

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
(b) more than the prescribed number of years have passed since the previous
              assessment.

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
(2) In addition to any requirement established by regulation or by order under
              subsection
              (1), if

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
(a) more than one water supplier uses the same drinking water source or related
              drinking water sources, and

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
(b) at least one of the water suppliers is required to prepare an assessment, by
              regulation or by order under subsection (1),

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
the drinking water officer may order 2 or more of those water suppliers to
            prepare a joint assessment, regardless of whether the water suppliers are otherwise
            required to prepare an assessment.

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
(3) Despite any other provision of this Act or the regulations, a drinking water
            officer may

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph: (a) postpone the time for beginning an assessment,

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph: (b) extend the time for completing an assessment, or

heading:
Drinking water officer authority in relation to
          assessments
paragraph:
(c) in the case of an assessment that has been ordered by the drinking water
              officer, limit or expand the scope of the assessment from that otherwise required
              under the regulations.

heading: Assessment process
paragraph:
20
		  (1) The process, preparation, form, content, area of coverage and time for
            completing an assessment must be in accordance with any applicable regulations and the
            directions of the drinking water officer.

heading: Assessment process
paragraph:
(2) In determining the directions to give for the purposes of subsection
              (1), the drinking water officer must consult with the medical health
            officer.

heading: Assessment process
paragraph:
(3) In addition, the drinking water officer may establish a technical advisory
            committee for the purposes of

heading: Assessment process
paragraph:
(a) providing advice respecting directions to be given under subsection
                (1), and

heading: Assessment process
paragraph:
(b) reviewing the draft assessment before it is filed under subsection
                (4).

heading: Assessment process
paragraph:
(4) On completion, the water supplier must file the assessment with the drinking
            water officer.

heading: Public notice
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A water supplier that is required to prepare an assessment must give advance
            public notice that the assessment is being prepared, with the notice to be given in
            accordance with the regulations and any directions of the drinking water
            officer.

heading: Public notice
paragraph:
(2) After the assessment has been filed under section 20 (4) [assessment process], the water supplier must make the assessment
            public in accordance with section 15 [publication of other information].

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
22
		  (1) In addition to any changes to the terms and conditions of an operating permit
            made in response to an assessment, the drinking water officer may order the water
            supplier to prepare an assessment response plan if

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
(a) an assessment has identified threats to the drinking water provided by the
              water supply system, and

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph: (b) the water supply system is of a prescribed class.

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
(2) The purpose of an assessment response plan is to identify the measures that may
            reasonably be taken in order to address identified threats to the drinking water that is
            provided by the water supply system.

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
(3) An assessment response plan must be prepared in accordance with the regulations
            and the directions of the drinking water officer.

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
(4) As examples of provisions that may be included in an assessment response plan,
            but without limiting the issues that may be addressed, the drinking water officer may
            require a plan to include provisions respecting any or all of the following:

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
(a) public education and other means of encouraging drinking water source
              protection;

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph: (b) guides to best management and conservation practices;

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph: (c) infrastructure improvements;

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph: (d) cooperative planning and voluntary programs;

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
(e) input respecting local authority zoning and other land use
              regulation.

heading: Assessment response plans
paragraph:
(5) The drinking water officer may order a water supplier to review and revise its
            assessment response plan in accordance with the directions of the drinking water
            officer.

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
23
		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), a person must not

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
(a) introduce anything or cause or allow anything to be introduced into a domestic
              water system, a drinking water source, a well recharge zone or an area adjacent to a
              drinking water source, or

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph: (b) do or cause any other thing to be done or to occur,

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
if this will result or is likely to result in a drinking water health hazard in
            relation to a domestic water system.

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), a person must not

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph: (a) destroy, damage or tamper with any part of a domestic water system,

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph: (b) open or close any part of a domestic water system,

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
(c) introduce anything or cause or allow anything to be introduced into a domestic
              water system, a drinking water source, a well recharge zone or an area adjacent to a
              drinking water source, or

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph: (d) do or cause any other thing to be done or to occur,

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
if it is reasonably foreseeable that, as a result, the owner of the domestic
            water system would have to limit the use of the water provided by the system on the
            basis that there may be a risk of a drinking water health hazard.

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph: (3) The prohibitions in subsection (1) and (2) do not apply

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
(a) in relation to anything required for the proper operation, maintenance or
              repair of a domestic water system or the treatment of water in the system,

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
(b) if the introduction or activity is authorized or required under an enactment
              or the person is otherwise acting with lawful authority, or

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
(c) in relation to an activity prescribed by regulation that is undertaken in
              accordance with any conditions prescribed by regulation.

heading:
Prohibition against contaminating drinking water or tampering with
          system
paragraph:
(4) For the purposes of prosecuting a contravention of subsection (1) (a), it is not
            necessary to prove that the thing, if diluted at or subsequent to the point at which it
            was introduced, continued to result in or be likely to result in a drinking water health
            hazard.

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph:
24
		  (1) If a person

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph: (a) is required to report under

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph: (i)  section 11 [mandatory reporting of health hazards] of the Public Health Act in respect of a toxic spill,                or

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph: (ii)  section 91.2 (1) (a) [responsible persons - spill response] of the Environmental Management Act, and

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph: (b) considers that the event reported may result in a threat to drinking              water,

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph:
the person must also promptly report the situation to the drinking water
            officer.

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph: (2) Despite any other enactment, if a regulation designates

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph: (a) persons employed in the public service of the Province, or

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph: (b) officials acting under the authority of a specified enactment

heading: Requirement to report threats to drinking water
paragraph:
for the purposes of this section, by title or otherwise, those designated must
            report to the drinking water officer any situation they observe, or of which they become
            aware, that they consider may be a threat to drinking water.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
25
		  (1) A drinking water officer may make an order under this section if the drinking
            water officer has reason to believe that

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph: (a) a drinking water health hazard exists, or

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(b) there is a significant risk of an imminent drinking water health
              hazard.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph: (2) An order under this section may be directed to

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(a) a person whose action or omission, in the opinion of the drinking water
              officer, resulted in or significantly contributed to the drinking water health hazard
              or risk, or

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(b) a person who had possession, charge or control of a condition or thing that,
              in the opinion of the drinking water officer, caused or significantly contributed to
              the drinking water health hazard or risk.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(3) The order must be served on the person to whom it is directed and may require
            that person, at the person's own expense, to do one or more of the following:

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
Hazard abatement and prevention orders
Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph: (c) abate the drinking water health hazard;

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(e) adjust, repair or alter any works to the extent reasonably necessary to
              control, abate, stop or prevent the drinking water health hazard;

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(f) give public notice in a manner approved by the drinking water officer or in
              accordance with the directions of the drinking water officer;

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(g) prepare and implement a hazard remediation plan or hazard prevention plan
              acceptable to the drinking water officer.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(4) If the order is directed to a person who is not the registered owner of the
            property on which action is required to be taken under subsection (3) (c), (d) or (e),
            a copy of the order must also be served on the registered owner.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(5) An order under this section may authorize persons designated by the drinking
            water officer to enter on or into property for the purpose of controlling, abating,
            stopping, remedying or preventing the drinking water health hazard.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph: (6) As restrictions on subsection (5),

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(a) except in the case of an emergency, a person authorized under that subsection
              must take reasonable steps to notify the owner or occupier before entering the
              property, and

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(b) the authority must not be used to enter a private dwelling except with the
              consent of the occupant or as authorized by a warrant under this or another
              Act.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(7) If the drinking water officer considers that the situation is urgent, the
            officer may issue an order under this section orally, in which case the officer must
            serve a written version of the order in accordance with this section as soon as
            reasonably possible.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(8) A drinking water officer may amend or cancel an order made under this
            section.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(9) The authority to make an order under this section, and to take action in
            relation to the order under section 27 [action in default], applies despite any other enactment, and the
            order applies despite any other enactment or authorization under an
            enactment.

heading: Hazard abatement and prevention orders
paragraph:
(10) In the event of a conflict between an order under this section and an order of a
            health officer under the Public Health Act, the order of the            health officer prevails.

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
26
		  (1) If a drinking water officer has reason to believe that a person is in
            contravention of this Act or the regulations, the drinking water officer may make an
            order under this section directed at the person.

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
(2) An order under this section must be served on the person to whom it is directed
            and must set out the reasons why it was made, what the person is required to do and the
            time within which this must be done.

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
(3) As examples of provisions that may be included in an order under this section,
            but without limiting the authority of a drinking water officer under subsection
              (1), an order may include provisions for the following:

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph: (a) requiring the person to provide information respecting an activity;

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
(b) requiring the person to take specified actions to comply with the Act or the
              regulations;

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
(c) prohibiting the person from starting or continuing specified actions until
              compliance is achieved;

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph: (d) requiring the closure of all or part of a domestic water system;

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
(e) requiring public notice to be given in a manner approved by the drinking water
              officer or in accordance with the directions of the drinking water officer;

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
(g) prohibiting a water supplier from providing water, or from using a specified
              drinking water source or fill location, until compliance has been achieved.

heading: Orders respecting contraventions
paragraph:
(4) Section 25 (4) to (10) [hazard abatement and prevention
              orders] applies to an order under this section.

heading: Action in default
paragraph:
27
		  (1) If a drinking water officer makes an order under section 25 [hazard abatement and prevention orders] or 26 [orders
              respecting contraventions], the drinking water officer may

heading: Action in default
paragraph:
(a) direct that, if the person fails to take the action required by the order, the
              action is to be done at the expense of that person, with the costs and expenses
              incurred recoverable under this section, and

heading: Action in default
paragraph:
(b) enter or authorize other persons to enter on or into any property for the
              purpose of

heading: Action in default
paragraph: (i)  determining whether the order is being complied with, or

heading: Action in default
paragraph: (ii)  taking action in default under paragraph (a).

heading: Action in default
paragraph: (2) As restrictions on subsection (1),

heading: Action in default
paragraph:
(a) except in the case of an emergency, before taking action under that
              subsection, the drinking water officer must give notice to the person subject to the
              order, and

heading: Action in default
paragraph:
(b) 
              section 25 (6) [restrictions on entry] applies.

heading: Action in default
paragraph:
(3) All reasonable costs and expenses incurred in taking action in default under
            this section are deemed to be money paid for the use and at the request of the person to
            whom the order was directed, and may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction
            by the person who incurred those costs and expenses as a debt owed to that
            person.

heading: Action in default
paragraph:
(4) In addition to recovery under subsection (3), in the case of
            recovery against a property owner or an occupier of property who is subject to property
            taxation under the Community Charter, Local                Government Act, Vancouver                Charter or Taxation (Rural Area)                Act, the costs and expenses may be recovered in accordance with
              section
              35 [recovery of costs by health authorities] of the Public                Health Act, with the required certificate to be filed by the
            drinking water officer.

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
28
		  (1) Despite any other provision of this Act, if a drinking water officer

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
(a) has reason to believe that a drinking water health hazard exists or that there
              is a significant risk of an imminent drinking water health hazard, and

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
(b) is not aware of a person against whom an order under section 25 [hazard abatement and prevention orders] or 26 [orders
                respecting contraventions] may appropriately be made,

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
the drinking water officer may take any actions the drinking water officer
            considers necessary to address the health hazard or risk or may authorize a water
            supplier or other person to do this.

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
(2) For the purposes of this section, the drinking water officer may authorize any
            persons designated by the drinking water officer to enter on or into property and take
            the necessary actions.

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph: (3) As restrictions on subsection (2), section 25 (6) [restrictions on entry] applies.

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph: (4) If

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph: (a) action is taken under this section, and

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
(b) the drinking water officer afterwards determines that there was a person
              against whom an order referred to in subsection (1) could have been
              made,

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
the drinking water officer may, by order, require the person to pay all or some
            of the reasonable costs and expenses incurred in taking action.

heading: Direct action by drinking water officer
paragraph:
(5) Section 27 (3) and (4) [action in default - cost recovery]
            applies in relation to an order under subsection (4) of this
            section.

heading: Request for investigation
paragraph:
29
		  (1) If a person considers that there is a threat to their drinking water, the person
            may request the drinking water officer to investigate the matter.

heading: Request for investigation
paragraph:
(2) A request under subsection (1) must be in writing and must include
            specifics of the facts that the person considers constitute the threat.

heading: Request for investigation
paragraph:
(3) On receiving a request under subsection (1), the drinking water officer must review
            the request and consider whether an investigation is warranted.

heading: Request for investigation
paragraph: (4) As applicable,

heading: Request for investigation
paragraph:
(a) if the drinking water officer decides against undertaking an investigation,
              the officer must advise the requesting person of this, and

heading: Request for investigation
paragraph:
(b) if the drinking water officer undertakes an investigation, the drinking water
              officer must advise the requesting person of the results of the
              investigation.

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
30
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph: (a) prescribing enactments for the purposes of this section, and

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(b) prescribing that all or specified classes of decisions under a prescribed
              enactment may be made subject to this section.

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(2) If a regulation under subsection (1) applies to an area, the minister may,
            by regulation applicable to all or part of that area,

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(a) provide that all or specified classes of the prescribed decisions are subject
              to this section,

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(b) identify local authorities, drinking water officers and water suppliers who
              must be

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(i)  provided an opportunity to comment on proposed decisions that are subject to
                this section, and

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph: (ii)  advised as to the decisions when they have been made, and

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(c) specify whether persons identified under paragraph (b) may require a written
              response under subsection (6).

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
