(3) Before making a regulation under subsection (2), the minister
            must consult with the minister responsible for the enactment in relation to which the
            regulation is intended to be made.

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(4) Before making a decision that is subject to this section, the decision
            maker

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(a) must provide the identified persons with an opportunity to comment on the
              proposed decision, and

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(b) may, in relation to this, specify a time by which any comments the persons
              wish to make must be received by the decision maker in order to be
              considered.

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(5) If a decision is to be made at the request of a person, by application or
            otherwise,

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(a) the decision maker may satisfy the requirement of subsection
                (4) by requiring the requesting person to obtain comments for the purpose
              of this section and report them to the decision maker, or

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(b) if no requirement is made under paragraph (a), the decision
              maker must provide a copy of any comments under this section to the requesting
              person.

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(6) Despite any other enactment, a person making a decision that is subject to this
            section must,

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(a) in making the decision, consider the comments provided under this section in
              relation to drinking water, and

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(b) if requested by a person specified under subsection (2) (c), provide a
              written response respecting the decision maker's consideration of the person's
              comments in making the decision.

heading: Required consultations respecting drinking water
paragraph:
(7) Failure to provide an opportunity to comment in accordance with this section
            does not of itself render a decision invalid.

heading: Order designating area for planning process
paragraph:
31
		  (1) The minister may, by order made on the recommendation of the Provincial health
            officer, designate an area for the purpose of developing a drinking water protection
            plan for the area.

heading: Order designating area for planning process
paragraph:
(2) The Provincial health officer may only recommend that an order be made under
            this section if

heading: Order designating area for planning process
paragraph:
(a) based on monitoring or assessment results, the Provincial health officer is
              satisfied that a drinking water protection plan will assist in addressing or
              preventing a threat to drinking water that the Provincial health officer considers may
              result in a drinking water health hazard, and

heading: Order designating area for planning process
paragraph:
(b) no other practicable measures available under this Act are sufficient to
              address or prevent the drinking water health hazard.

heading: Order designating area for planning process
paragraph:
(3) The Provincial health officer must consider whether to make a recommendation
            under this section if requested by a drinking water officer.

heading: Order designating area for planning process
paragraph:
(4) A local authority or water supplier may request a drinking water officer to make
            a request under subsection (3).

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
32
		  (1) The minister may, by order, establish the process by which a proposed drinking
            water protection plan for a designated area is to be developed.

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
(2) Without limiting subsection (1), an order under that subsection
            may

heading: Plan development process
paragraph: (a) establish who is to be responsible for preparing the proposed plan,

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
(b) establish the terms of reference for the plan, or authorize the preparation of
              some or all of the terms of reference subject to approval by the minister,
              and

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
(c) require the establishment of a technical advisory committee in relation to
              development of the plan.

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
(3) The terms of reference for a proposed drinking water protection plan must
            include

heading: Plan development process
paragraph: (a) the purpose of the plan,

heading: Plan development process
paragraph: (b) the issues to be addressed in the plan,

heading: Plan development process
paragraph: (c) a process for public and stakeholder consultation, and

heading: Plan development process
paragraph: (d) a time limit for completing the plan.

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
(4) As examples of terms of reference that may be established for a plan, but
            without limiting the issues that may be addressed, the terms of reference for a drinking
            water protection plan may include one or more of the following:

heading: Plan development process
Plan development process
Plan development process
paragraph:
(c) consideration of the economic and social costs and benefits of addressing
              risks through treatment, source protection or other means;

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
(d) whether an implementation regulation under any of sections 35 to
                38 should be made.

heading: Plan development process
paragraph:
(5) In preparing a proposed drinking water protection plan, consideration must be
            given to the results or progress of Provincial government or local government strategic,
            operational and land use or water use planning processes within the designated
            area.

heading: Plan development process
paragraph: (6) A proposed drinking water protection plan may be prepared in conjunction with a proposed water sustainability plan under the Water Sustainability Act.

heading: Plan development process
paragraph: (7) The minister may, by order, extend the time for completing a proposed drinking            water protection plan whether or not the time previously set has expired.

heading: Drinking water officer authority
paragraph:
33
		  (1) For the purposes of developing a proposed drinking water protection plan, the
            drinking water officer may do one or more of the following:

heading: Drinking water officer authority
paragraph: (a) order a water supplier to participate in the process;

heading: Drinking water officer authority
paragraph:
(b) undertake investigations, tests and surveys that the drinking water officer
              considers advisable;

heading: Drinking water officer authority
paragraph:
(c) authorize persons to undertake investigations, tests and surveys referred to
              in paragraph
                (b).

heading: Drinking water officer authority
paragraph:
(2) The drinking water officer or any person authorized under subsection (1) (c) may
            exercise any of the powers under section 40 [inspection authority] for the purposes of investigations, tests and
            surveys under subsection (1).

heading: Approval of drinking water protection plan
paragraph:
34
		  (1) After a proposed plan has been prepared, it must be submitted to the minister,
            who must refer it to the Provincial health officer for review.

heading: Approval of drinking water protection plan
paragraph:
(2) After the review required by subsection (1), the minister must place the proposed
            plan and the comments of the Provincial health officer before the Lieutenant Governor in
            Council, who may approve all or part of the proposed plan as a drinking water protection
            plan.

heading: Approval of drinking water protection plan
paragraph:
(3) If a drinking water protection plan is approved under subsection
              (2), the minister must arrange for the plan to be made public.

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph:
35
		  (1) For the purposes of implementing a drinking water protection plan, the
            Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation applicable in relation to all or part
            of the designated area for the plan, do one or more of the following:

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph:
(a) require that persons making decisions or classes of decisions under a
              specified enactment must consider the plan in making those decisions;

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph:
(b) restrict the issuance or amendment of licences, approvals, permits or other
              authorizations under a specified enactment;

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph: (c) restrict the exercise of a power under a specified enactment;

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph:
(d) provide that specified provisions of the plan are a higher level plan for the
              purposes of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia                Act.

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph:
(2) Despite an enactment specified under subsection (1), a regulation under
              subsection
              (1) (b) may establish requirements that must be imposed in issuing or
            amending a licence, approval, permit or other authorization under an
            enactment.

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph:
(3) Requirements imposed under subsection (2) are deemed to be imposed under the
            enactment under which the authorization is issued or amended.

heading: Implementing a plan: effect on statutory decisions
paragraph:
(4) The issuance or amendment of a licence, approval, permit or other authorization
            contrary to a regulation under subsection (1) (b), or the exercise of a power
            contrary to a regulation under subsection (1) (c), has no effect.

heading:
Implementing a plan: relationship with other planning
          processes
paragraph:
35.1
		  (1) For the purposes of implementing a drinking water protection plan, the
            Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, do one or more of the
            following:

heading:
Implementing a plan: relationship with other planning
          processes

Implementing a plan: relationship with other planning
          processes

Implementing a plan: relationship with other planning
          processes
paragraph:
(c) provide that specified Provincial government or local authority strategic or
              operational plans, bylaws or other planning documents, or classes of such plans,
              bylaws or other documents, do not have legal effect to the extent of any inconsistency
              with the drinking water protection plan.

heading:
Implementing a plan: relationship with other planning
          processes
paragraph:
(2) A provision under subsection (1) (c) applies despite any other
            enactment.

heading: Implementing a plan: restrictions on groundwater activities
paragraph:
36
		  (1) For the purposes of implementing a drinking water protection plan, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation applicable to all or part of the designated area for the plan, restrict or prohibit one or more of the following or may impose requirements on a person doing one or more of the following:

heading: Implementing a plan: restrictions on groundwater activities
paragraph: (a) constructing a well;

heading: Implementing a plan: restrictions on groundwater activities
paragraph: (b) installing well pumps;

heading: Implementing a plan: restrictions on groundwater activities
paragraph: (c) conducting flow tests;

heading: Implementing a plan: restrictions on groundwater activities
paragraph: (d) performing another activity in relation to a well or groundwater.

heading: Implementing a plan: restrictions on groundwater activities
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a restriction in a regulation under that subsection may include a requirement that a person hold a drilling authorization in order to carry out one or more of the activities referred to in section 62 (1) [drilling authorizations] of the Water Sustainability Act.

heading: Implementing a plan: enforcement of water source          standards
paragraph:
37
		  (1) For the purposes of implementing a drinking water protection plan, the
            Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation,

heading: Implementing a plan: enforcement of water source          standards
paragraph: (a) prescribe all or part of a drinking water source,

heading: Implementing a plan: enforcement of water source          standards
paragraph:
(b) establish water quality standards in relation to the prescribed drinking water
              source or part of a drinking water source,

heading: Implementing a plan: enforcement of water source          standards
paragraph:
(c) prohibit persons from doing anything that results in the prescribed standards
              not being met, and

heading: Implementing a plan: enforcement of water source          standards
paragraph: (d) establish exceptions to a prohibition under paragraph (c).

heading: Implementing a plan: enforcement of water source          standards
paragraph:
(2) A prohibition under subsection (1) applies despite any other enactment or
            authorization under an enactment.

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
38
		  (1) If requested by a local government for the purposes of implementing a drinking
            water protection plan, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation applicable
            to all or part of the designated area for the plan,

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph: (a) provide that

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(i)  the issuance or amendment of licences, approvals, permits or other
                authorizations under a specified enactment, or

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph: (ii)  the exercise of a power under a specified enactment,

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph: is subject to this section, and

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(b) despite an enactment specified under paragraph (a) but subject to subsection
                (2), authorize the local government to

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(i)  establish terms and conditions that must be included in an authorization
                under a specified enactment, or

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph: (ii)  restrict the exercise of a specified power under an enactment,

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph: subject to any limits or conditions established by the regulation.

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(2) A local government may only exercise an authority under subsection
              (1)

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(a) after consultation with the relevant decision maker and the drinking water
              officer, if this consultation is required by regulation, and

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(b) in each case, if the local government has reason to believe this is necessary
              for the purpose of protecting the potability of drinking water.

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(3) Terms and conditions established under this section are deemed to be imposed
            under the specified enactment to which they relate.

heading: Implementing a plan: local government authority
paragraph:
(4) For the purposes of undertaking work specifically contemplated by a drinking
            water protection plan, the minister responsible for the Local Government                Act may, by order, exempt a local government from the
            requirement for approval of the electors, assent of the electors or other elector
            approval under the Community Charter, the Local                Government Act, the Vancouver                Charter or another enactment, subject to any conditions
            established by the minister.

heading: Review and amendment of plans
paragraph:
39
		  The minister may, by order made on the recommendation of the Provincial health
          officer, direct that a current drinking water protection plan be reviewed to determine
          whether amendments should be made, and this Part applies to the review and to any
          amendment to the plan proposed by the review.

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
39.1
		  (1) In this section, "decision" means a decision of a drinking
            water officer under any of the following:

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions

Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(b) 
              section 25 [hazard abatement and prevention orders];

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(c) 
              section 26 [orders respecting contraventions];

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(d) 
              section 31 (4) [request respecting plan initiation];

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(e) a decision resulting from a reconsideration under subsection
                (3) of this section.

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, a person affected by a decision may

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(a) request a reconsideration of the decision under subsection (3), if the person
              considers that there is sufficient new evidence for this purpose, or

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph: (b) request a review of the decision under subsection (4).

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(3) If a reconsideration is requested and the drinking water officer is satisfied
            that there is sufficient new evidence respecting the matter to justify a
            reconsideration, the drinking water officer may reconsider the matter and may confirm,
            vary or reverse the initial decision.

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph: (4) If a review is requested,

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(a) the review is to be conducted by the Provincial health officer or a medical
              health officer designated by the Provincial health officer,

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph: (b) the review is to be a review based on the record,

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(c) the person conducting the review may require the applicant to give notice of
              the review in accordance with the person's directions, and

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph: (d) the person conducting the review may

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph: (i)  confirm, vary or reverse the initial decision, or

heading:
Reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer
          decisions
paragraph:
(ii)  refer the matter back to the drinking water officer, with or without
                directions.

heading: Inspection authority
paragraph:
40
		  (1) For the purposes of this Act, a drinking water officer or issuing official may
            enter on or into any property and conduct an inspection and, in relation to this, has
            the same authority as a medical health officer under Division 1 [Inspections] of Part 4 of the Public Health                Act.

heading: Inspection authority
paragraph:
(2) The authority under subsection (1) must not be used to enter a private
            dwelling except with the consent of the occupant or as authorized by a warrant under
            this or another Act.

heading: Entry warrant
paragraph:
41
		  If satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation that access on or into property is
          necessary for the purposes of this Act, a justice may issue a warrant authorizing a person
          named in the warrant to enter on or into property and conduct an inspection, undertake
          hazard abatement or prevention activities or take other action as authorized by the
          warrant.

heading: Court order requiring compliance
paragraph:
42
		  (1) On application by a drinking water officer, the Supreme Court may grant an
            injunction against a person who has contravened this Act, the regulations or an order
            under this Act,

heading: Court order requiring compliance
paragraph:
(a) restraining the person from contravening the Act, regulations or order,
              or

heading: Court order requiring compliance
paragraph:
(b) requiring the person to take action as directed by the court for the purpose
              of achieving compliance or remedying or preventing a drinking water health
              hazard.

heading: Court order requiring compliance
paragraph:
(2) An order under subsection (1) does not prevent the imposition of a
            penalty in respect of an offence in relation to the same matter.

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph:
43
		  (1) No action for damages lies or may be brought against a drinking water officer,
            delegate or issuing official because of anything done or omitted

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph:
(a) in the performance or intended performance of any duty under this Act,
              or

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph: (b) in the exercise or intended exercise of any power under this Act,

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph: unless the person was acting in bad faith.

heading:
Prohibition against providing false information or obstructing
          officials
paragraph:
44
		  A person must not

heading:
Prohibition against providing false information or obstructing
          officials
paragraph:
(a) provide false or misleading information when required under this Act to provide
            information, or

heading:
Prohibition against providing false information or obstructing
          officials
paragraph:
(b) hinder, obstruct, impede or otherwise interfere with a drinking water officer,
            delegate or issuing official in the performance of their duties or the exercise of their
            powers under this Act.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
45
		  (1) A person who contravenes this Act, or a regulation, order, direction or permit
            under this Act, commits an offence.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(2) Unless a lower penalty is specified by regulation, a person who commits an
            offence under subsection (1) is liable on conviction to the following:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(a) in the case of an offence that is not a continuing offence, a fine of not more
              than $200 000 or imprisonment for not longer than 12 months, or both;

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(b) in the case of a continuing offence, a fine of not more than $200 000 for each
              day the offence is continued or imprisonment for not longer than 12 months, or
              both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(3) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, a sentencing judge may
            order the convicted person to do one or more things described in section 107 (1) of
            the Public Health Act, and, for these purposes, section 107 (2)            applies.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(4) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer,
            director or agent of the corporation who authorizes, permits or acquiesces in the
            commission of the offence commits an offence.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(5) 
            Subsection (4) applies whether or not the corporation is prosecuted for
            the offence.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(6) The time limit for laying an information respecting an offence under this Act is
            2 years after the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of
            a drinking water officer.

heading: Service of documents
paragraph:
46
		  Service of documents under this Act must be in accordance with the
          regulations.

heading: Area descriptions
paragraph:
47
		  Where this Act or the regulations authorize or require the description or
          designation of an area, this may be by any delineation of the area that adequately
          describes it including, for example, name, map, plan, legal description, reference to a
          stream, reference to an aquifer or other geological formation or part of one, depth or
          other dimension, or by any combination of methods.

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph:
48
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41
            of the Interpretation Act.

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (a) matters that are referred to in a provision of this Act as being subject to              the regulations or as having to be in accordance with the regulations, or

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph:
(b) any other matter for which regulations are contemplated by this
              Act.

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph:
(3) Without limiting subsection (1) or (2), the Lieutenant Governor in
            Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (a) respecting water quality standards, including

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (i)  standards that are requirements for potable water,

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (ii)  standards for which monitoring must be conducted and reported,

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph:
(iii)  standards for which immediate reporting is required if the standards are not
                met, and

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (iv)  standards for any other purpose established by regulation;

heading: General regulation making authority
General regulation making authority
paragraph:
(c) respecting the issuance, amendment, renewal, suspension or cancellation of
              permits under this Act;

heading: General regulation making authority
General regulation making authority
paragraph: (e) respecting water treatment requirements;

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (f) respecting the preparation, retention and publication of records;

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph:
(g) respecting fees for applications, permits and services provided under this
              Act;

heading: General regulation making authority
General regulation making authority
paragraph:
(h.1) restricting who may request reconsiderations or reviews under section
                39.1 [reconsiderations and reviews of drinking water officer decisions],
              restricting what decisions may be reconsidered or reviewed and establishing
              procedures, time limits, fees, evidentiary rules and other matters respecting such
              reconsiderations and reviews;

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph:
(i) providing for reconsiderations, reviews or appeals of orders and other
              decisions under this Act, other than those referred to in section 39.1, including
              restricting who may request them and establishing procedures, time limits, fees,
              evidentiary rules and other matters respecting them;

heading: General regulation making authority
General regulation making authority
paragraph: (k) respecting testing required for the purposes of section 63 [water analyses for new or altered wells] of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: General regulation making authority
paragraph: (l) providing for any other matter that the Lieutenant Governor in Council              considers advisable in relation to the protection of drinking water.

heading: Authority in relation to regulations
paragraph:
49
		  (1) In making a regulation under this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council or
            minister may do one or more of the following:

heading: Authority in relation to regulations
paragraph:
(a) make different provisions for different areas as specified in the
              regulation;

heading: Authority in relation to regulations
paragraph:
(b) make different regulations for different classes of persons, places,
              activities, conditions or things as specified in the regulation;

heading: Authority in relation to regulations

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Drinking Water Protection Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "building system" means a system, within a building, to which the British Columbia Plumbing Code applies, that receives water from a water supply system operating under a valid operating permit under the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "connection" means the line from the water main to a dwelling, campsite or premises;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "decal" means an adhesive label that is issued and affixed to an operating permit at the time fees under this regulation are paid or remitted;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fiscal year" means the period from April 1 in one year to March 31 in the next year;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "small system" means a water supply system that serves up to 500 individuals during any 24 hour period;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "system within a system" means a water supply system that, in the opinion of a drinking water officer or issuing official,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) redistributes water from a water supply system operating under a valid operating permit under the Act, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) does not require further treatment processes, additional infrastructure or ongoing maintenance to prevent a drinking water health hazard.

heading: Standards for potable water
paragraph: 2		  The prescribed water quality standards for potable water are set out in Schedule A.

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph:
3
		  The following are excluded from the definition of "domestic water system" in the Act:

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph: (a) equipment, works and facilities constructed, operated or maintained

heading: Domestic water system

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph: (ii)  under a permit issued under the Water Sustainability Act,

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph: (iii)  for bottled water production or distribution, or

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph: (iv)  for drinking water dispensing machines;

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph: (b) a reservoir relating to a licence or permit referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph: (c) a building system;

heading: Domestic water system
paragraph: (d) a system within a system.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: 3.1		  The following are exempt from section 6 of the Act:

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) a small system, if

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (i)  each recipient of the water from the small system has a point of entry or point of use treatment system that makes the water potable, and

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  the water supplier ensures that the location of non-potable water discharge and non-potable water piping are identified by markings that are permanent, distinct and easily recognized;

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) a water supply system, including a small system, if

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (i)  the system does not provide water for human consumption or food preparation purposes,

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  the system is not connected to a water supply system that provides water for human consumption or food preparation purposes, and

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (iii)  the water supplier ensures that the location of non-potable water discharge and non-potable water piping are identified by markings that are permanent, distinct and easily recognized.

paragraph:

heading: Operating permits and fees
paragraph: (a) an application for an operating permit in a form satisfactory to the drinking water officer, and

heading: Operating permits and fees

heading: Operating permits and fees

paragraph:

paragraph:

paragraph: (b) the operating permit is not required to bear a decal to be valid.

heading: Water monitoring analysis
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A water supplier must transport water samples to a laboratory in accordance with the procedures established by a drinking water officer.

heading: Water monitoring analysis
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of section 11 (1) of the Act, a water supplier must monitor for total coliform bacteria and, effective April 1, 2006, Escherichia coli, at the frequencies set out in Schedule B of this regulation.

heading: Water monitoring analysis
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), a drinking water officer may establish different sampling frequencies for a water supplier.

heading: Water monitoring analysis
paragraph: (4) A laboratory carrying out monitoring analyses for the parameters referred to in subsection (2) must be approved in writing by the Provincial health officer.

heading: Water monitoring analysis
paragraph: (5) If requested to do so by a drinking water officer, a laboratory must provide to the drinking water officer, the water supplier, or both, a report

heading: Water monitoring analysis
paragraph: (a) listing all water samples sent by the water supplier to the laboratory, and

heading: Water monitoring analysis
paragraph: (b) describing, for all samples analyzed, the results of any monitoring analyses for total coliform bacteria and Escherichia coli.

heading: Immediate reporting standard
paragraph:
9

heading: Immediate reporting standard

heading: Public notification
paragraph:
10
		  If water provided by a domestic water system is not or may not be potable water, the owner of a public premises that is served by the domestic water system must do both of the following:

heading: Public notification
paragraph: (a) notify the public that the water is not potable water by posting a sign at every sink or drinking water fountain accessible to the public;

heading: Public notification
paragraph: (b) if normal business practices provide an opportunity,

heading: Public notification
paragraph: (i)  verbally advise or notify by email any person who may use the domestic water system for a domestic purpose that the water is not potable water, or

heading: Public notification
paragraph: (ii)  post on the website maintained by or on behalf of the owner a notice that the water provided by the domestic water system is not or may not be potable water.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "disposition" means and includes every act of the government where Crown land, mines, minerals, coal, petroleum, natural gas, timber and water, or any right, title, interest or estate in them is granted, disposed of or affected, or by which the government divests itself of or creates a right, title, interest or estate in, or permits the use of land, mines, minerals, coal, petroleum, natural gas, timber and water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ecology" means the study of the interrelations between human beings, other animals, or plants and their environment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ecosystem" means a complete system composed of human beings, other animals and plants in a defined area, and with the soil and climate comprising their habitat in that area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environment" means all the external conditions or influences under which human beings, animals and plants live or are developed;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "habitat" means that kind of place or situation in which a human being, animal or a plant lives.

heading: Purpose
paragraph:
2
		  The purpose of this Act is to reserve Crown land for ecological purposes, including the following areas:

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (a) areas suitable for scientific research and educational purposes associated with studies in productivity and other aspects of the natural environment;

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (b) areas that are representative examples of natural ecosystems in British Columbia;

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (c) areas that serve as examples of ecosystems that have been modified by human beings and offer an opportunity to study the recovery of the natural ecosystem from modification;

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (d) areas where rare or endangered native plants and animals in their natural habitat may be preserved;

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (e) areas that contain unique and rare examples of botanical, zoological or geological phenomena.

heading: Establishing and modifying ecological reserves
paragraph:
3
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order,

heading: Establishing and modifying ecological reserves
paragraph: (a) establish an area of Crown land as an ecological reserve, and

heading: Establishing and modifying ecological reserves
paragraph: (b) declare the name by which the ecological reserve is to be known.

heading: Establishing and modifying ecological reserves
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, add to, cancel in its entirety or delete any portion of an ecological reserve established under subsection (1).

heading: Establishing and modifying ecological reserves
paragraph:
(3) 
          Subsection (2) does not apply to an ecological reserve referenced in Schedule A or B of the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act.

heading: Establishing and modifying ecological reserves
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, add to an ecological reserve referenced in Schedule A or B of the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act.

heading: Establishing and modifying ecological reserves
paragraph: (5) Except as permitted by subsection (4), the boundaries of an ecological reserve referenced in Schedule A or B of the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act must not be affected except by an Act of the Legislature.

heading: Publication in Gazette
paragraph: 4		  An order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council under this Act establishing or modifying an ecological reserve must be published in the Gazette.

heading: Ecological reserves not available for disposition
paragraph:
5
		  (1) Any area established or continued as an ecological reserve under this Act or by the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act must be immediately withdrawn and reserved from any further disposition that might otherwise be granted under any Act or law in force in British Columbia.

heading: Ecological reserves not available for disposition
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), that subsection applies to dispositions under the following Acts: Coal Act, Forest Act, Land Act, Mineral Tenure Act, Mining Right of Way Act, Petroleum and Natural Gas Act, Range Act and Water Sustainability Act.

heading: Ecological reserves not available for disposition
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to a disposition by permit under section 5.1.

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: 5.1		  (1) In accordance with the regulations, the minister may issue a permit to a person authorizing use and occupation of an ecological reserve for ecological scientific research or educational purposes under section 2.

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (2) A permit under subsection (1) may be limited to one entry or may cover a specified period of time.

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (3) It is a condition of a permit issued under subsection (1) that the permittee comply with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (4) If necessary and incidental to the scientific research or educational purpose for which a permit is issued, the minister may authorize in the permit one or more of the following uses or activities:

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (a) entry to and access through the ecological reserve by specified means of conveyance or transportation;

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (b) introduction of a specified plant or animal species.

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (5) A permit issued under this section must include terms and conditions that the minister considers advisable to protect the ecological reserve and the natural resources in it.

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (6) In accordance with the regulations, the minister may suspend, modify or cancel a permit issued under this section if the minister considers it advisable for the protection of the ecological reserve or its natural resources.

heading: Permits for scientific research and educational purposes
paragraph: (7) Subject to the regulations, the minister may delegate to any person or class of persons any of the minister's powers, duties and functions under this section.

heading: Designated wildland area as ecological reserve
paragraph:
6
		  Despite the Park Act, a designated wildland area or any portion of it, designated as such under that Act, may be established as an ecological reserve under this Act or by the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act.

heading: Designation and delegation by minister
paragraph: 6.1		  (1) The minister may designate as a director a person appointed under the Public Service Act.

heading: Designation and delegation by minister
paragraph: (2) The minister may delegate to a director designated under subsection (1) any of the minister's powers or duties under sections 6.2 to 6.4.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: 6.2		  (1) After providing a person with an opportunity to be heard, the minister may, in accordance with the regulations, impose an administrative penalty on the person if the minister is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that the person has

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of the regulations, or

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with a term or condition of a permit issued under this Act.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) An administrative penalty imposed under this section must be paid to the government within the prescribed time and in accordance with any other prescribed requirements.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) If, under this section, the minister imposes an administrative penalty on a person, a prosecution for an offence under this Act in respect of the same contravention may not be brought against the person.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) If a corporation contravenes a prescribed provision of the regulations or fails to comply with a term or condition of a permit, as described in subsection (1), an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure is liable for an administrative penalty under this section even if the corporation is liable for or pays an administrative penalty.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (5) All revenue the government derives from administrative penalties imposed under this section must be paid into the Park Enhancement Fund special account established by section 9.6 (2) of the Special Accounts Appropriation and Control Act.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: 6.3		  (1) Before the date an administrative penalty under section 6.2 is due, the minister may, in accordance with the regulations, enter into an agreement with the person who is liable for the administrative penalty.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (2) An agreement under subsection (1) may provide, in accordance with the regulations, for the reduction or cancellation of the administrative penalty subject to the terms and conditions the minister considers necessary or desirable.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (3) An agreement under subsection (1) must specify the time for performing any terms and conditions and, if the person fails to perform the terms and conditions by the date specified, the administrative penalty imposed under section 6.2 is due and payable on that date.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
6.4
		  (1) An administrative penalty under section 6.2 may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required under section 6.2, the minister may file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) must be signed by the minister and must contain the following information:

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the administrative penalty;

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) particulars of the administrative penalty;

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the administrative penalty.

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph:
6.5
		  (1) In this section, "appeal board" means the Environmental Appeal Board continued under section 93 of the Environmental Management Act.

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) A person who is liable for an administrative penalty under section 6.2 may appeal the following decisions under this Act to the appeal board:

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) a decision of the minister, under section 6.2 (1), to impose the administrative penalty on the person;

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) a decision of the minister, under section 6.3 (3), that the person failed to perform a term or condition of an agreement under section 6.3 (1).

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) The following provisions of the Environmental Management Act apply in relation to an appeal under this section:

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) section 93.1 [application of Administrative Tribunals Act];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) section 94 [parties and witnesses];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) section 96 [decision of appeal board];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (d) section 97 [varying and rescinding orders of appeal board];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (e) section 98 [appeal board power to enter property];

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: 7		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act and orders.

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: (a) for the control, restriction or prohibition of any use, development or occupation of the land or any of the natural resources in an ecological reserve;

heading: General regulation authority

heading: General regulation authority

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: (c.1) respecting permits under section 5.1, including, without limitation, providing for their issue, suspension, modification or cancellation;

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: (c.2) requiring and prescribing a fee payable for a permit under section 5.1 and for a permit application;

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: (c.3) respecting the delegation of the powers, duties and functions of the minister under section 5.1;

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: (d) creating an offence for the contravention of a regulation;

heading: General regulation authority
paragraph: (e) generally for any other matter or thing necessary or incidental to the protection of an ecological reserve.

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: 7.01		  Without limiting section 7, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) prescribing provisions of the regulations in relation to the contravention of which an administrative penalty may be imposed;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) prescribing, in relation to a contravention or failure referred to in section 6.2 (1) [administrative penalties], whether an administrative penalty must be cancelled if the person on whom it was imposed demonstrates to the satisfaction of the minister that the person exercised due diligence to prevent the specified contravention or failure;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (f) prescribing a schedule of administrative penalties that may be imposed and the matters that must be considered by the minister in establishing an administrative penalty in a particular case;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (g) establishing the required content of notices related to administrative penalties;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (h) authorizing administrative penalties to be imposed on a daily basis for continuing contraventions or failures;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (i) respecting time limits, and the manner and process, for paying administrative penalties;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (j) prescribing the consequences for failing to pay an administrative penalty, which may include, but are not limited to, imposing additional administrative penalties under section 6.2;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (k) providing for the publication of information respecting the imposition of an administrative penalty;

heading: Regulations in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (l) respecting agreements under section 6.3 [compliance agreements].

		  (1) A person who commits an offence under the regulations is liable to a fine of up to $200 000.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (2) If an offence under subsection (1) is of a continuing nature, each day that the offence continues constitutes a separate offence.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (3) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (4) A person who has been charged with an offence under this Act may not be subject to an administrative penalty in respect of the circumstances that gave rise to the charge.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: 7.2		  (1) The time limit for laying an information for an offence under this Act is

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (a) 3 years after the date that the facts on which the information is based arose, or

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) if the minister issues a certificate described in subsection (2), 18 months after the date that the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the minister, certifying the date that the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the minister,

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (a) is admissible without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the certificate, and

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) is proof of the certified matters.

heading: Administration
paragraph:
8
		  Subject to the regulations and orders made under this Act, land established or continued as an ecological reserve under this Act or by the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act is under the jurisdiction of and is to be administered by the minister.

heading: Advisers
paragraph: 9		  (1) The minister may appoint a person or persons to advise the minister on any matter relating to the establishment and administration of ecological reserves.

heading: Advisers
paragraph: (2) A person appointed under subsection (1) has the duties specified by the minister and is subject to the regulations.

heading: Other Acts
paragraph:
10
		  This Act, and any regulation or order made under this Act, applies to every ecological reserve, despite any other Act or regulation.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Ecological Reserve Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "activated e-cigarette" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aircraft" means a device in, on or by which a person is transported or drawn by air, whether using a motorized or non-motorized means of propulsion, and includes fixed or rotary wing airplanes and gliders;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "camp" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Park, Conservancy and Recreation Area Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cannabis" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Cannabis Control and Licensing Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "domesticated animal" means an animal that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) tame,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) under the care or control of a person, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) kept by a person for a commercial purpose;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "drone" means an aerial device that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is not occupied or operated by a person within the device, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is operated by one or more of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  remote control;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  pre-programmed software;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  onboard computer autonomy or artificial intelligence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "e-cigarette" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "e-substance" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish" includes the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a vertebrate of the order Petromyzontiformes (lampreys) or class Osteichthyes (bony fishes);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an invertebrate of the phylum Echinodermata (echinoderms), class Crustacea (crustaceans) or class Mollusca (mollusks);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any other aquatic animal, except a bird or mammal;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an egg or juvenile stage of an animal described in any of paragraphs (a) to (c);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hunt" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Park, Conservancy and Recreation Area Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "motorized boat" means a device in, on or by which a person is transported or drawn on water using a motorized means of propulsion;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "natural resources" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Park Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "non-motorized boat" means a device in, on or by which a person is transported or drawn on water using a non-motorized means of propulsion;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "tobacco" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "trap" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Park, Conservancy and Recreation Area Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "vehicle" means a device in, on or by which a person or thing is transported or drawn on land, whether using a motorized or non-motorized means of propulsion;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "waste" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Park, Conservancy and Recreation Area Regulation.

heading: Ecological reserve entry, use and occupation restricted
paragraph: 2		  (1) Subject to this section, a person must not enter, use or occupy an ecological reserve unless authorized by a permit issued under section 5.1 (1) of the Act.

heading: Ecological reserve entry, use and occupation restricted
paragraph: (2) A person may, without a permit, enter and travel in or through, by foot or by non-motorized boat, an ecological reserve other than an ecological reserve set out in the Schedule.

heading: Ecological reserve entry, use and occupation restricted
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not authorize entry to an ecological reserve if a heat or rainfall warning issued by Environment and Climate Change Canada is in effect in relation to an area that encompasses, overlaps with or abuts the ecological reserve.

heading: Ecological reserve entry, use and occupation restricted
paragraph: (4) A permittee must comply with the terms and conditions included in the permittee's permit under section 5.1 (5) of the Act.

heading: Notice of conditions
paragraph:
3
		  The minister must, if satisfied that the circumstances set out in section 2 (3) exist in relation to an ecological reserve, provide public notice, in the manner the minister considers appropriate, that entry to the ecological reserve is prohibited under section 2 unless authorized by a permit.

heading: Application for permit
paragraph:
4
		  (1) For the purposes of section 5.1 (1) of the Act, a person may apply to the minister for a permit authorizing the use and occupation of an ecological reserve for ecological scientific research or educational purposes.

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (2) An application for a permit must include the following:

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (a) a description of the proposed scientific research or educational uses and activities;

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (b) a description and map of the areas of land that would be affected by the uses and activities;

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (c) a description of the proposed means of entry to and access through the ecological reserve;

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (d) the proposed duration of the uses and activities;

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (e) the expected ecological impact of the uses and activities;

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (f) the number of individuals proposed to enter the ecological reserve and, if known, their names;

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (g) the name of the individual proposed to direct the uses and activities.

heading: Hearing
paragraph:
5
		  (1) The minister is not required to hold a hearing before suspending, modifying or cancelling a permit.

heading: Hearing
paragraph: (2) If the minister holds a hearing, it may be held in writing, electronically or in person, or by any combination of written, electronic or in-person hearings.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A person must not do or attempt to do any of the following in an ecological reserve:

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) prospect or explore for, or extract, coal, petroleum or natural gas;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) drill for or divert water or dam a waterway.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) A person must not do or attempt to do any of the following unless authorized to do so under a permit issued under section 5.1 (1) of the Act:

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) introduce a plant or animal species in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) operate a vehicle or a motorized boat, or conduct a take-off or landing of an aircraft or a drone, in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) deposit waste in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (d) allow or cause waste to flow onto or seep into land in an ecological reserve or to flow or seep into water in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (e) allow or cause waste to be emitted into the air from within an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (f) mine or quarry earth, soil, peat, marl, sand, gravel, rock or another mineral resource in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (g) make an alteration to land on or beneath its surface in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (h) damage, destroy or take a sample of a natural resource in, or remove a natural resource from, an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (i) disturb an animal in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (j) hunt or trap in, catch fish in, or take fish or wildlife from, an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (k) touch or feed wildlife in an ecological reserve or entice wildlife in an ecological reserve to approach by any means, including by holding out or setting out a decoy, lure, food or bait or by using a wildlife caller;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (l) light, fuel or use a fire in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (m) allow a domesticated animal to graze in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (n) cut or fell timber in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (o) construct or modify a road or trail in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (p) camp in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (q) establish, construct or modify a building or other structure in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (r) smoke cannabis, or hold lighted cannabis, in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (s) use or hold, in an ecological reserve, an activated e-cigarette that is vapourizing cannabis;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (t) smoke tobacco, or hold lighted tobacco, in an ecological reserve;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (u) use or hold, in an ecological reserve, an activated e-cigarette that is vapourizing an e-substance other than cannabis.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply in relation to a use or activity carried out

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) under section 18 of the Wildfire Act, or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) by or on behalf of the minister for the purposes of one or more of the following:

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (i)  restoring an ecosystem;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (ii)  protecting a rare or endangered native plant or animal;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (iii)  carrying out ecological scientific research or education.

paragraph: 7		  A person who contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) section 2 (1) or (4);

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) section 6 (1) or (2).

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "animals" means the following types of animals:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) domestic pets;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) animals trained to assist in law enforcement activities, whether the animals are used by a peace officer or by a person acting under the direction of a peace officer;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (c) guide dogs and service dogs within the meaning of the Guide Dog and Service Dog Act;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (d) livestock within the meaning of the Livestock Act;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (e) animals that are lawfully kept in zoos, sanctuaries, rehabilitation centres or facilities for education or research;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (f) without limiting paragraph (e), live animals that are lawfully possessed under the Wildlife Act;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "business continuity plan" means a business continuity plan prepared in accordance with section 53 [business continuity plans];

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "comprehensive emergency management plan" means the emergency management plan for the government, as referred to in section 39 (1) (a) [emergency management planning and information];

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "critical incident" means a single incident to which all of the following apply:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) the incident requires the prompt coordination of actions at a particular location

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (i)  to protect the health, safety or well-being of one or more persons, or

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (ii)  for a prescribed purpose;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) the actions required under paragraph (a) are beyond the capability or capacity of the responsible emergency service provider;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (c) the incident does not include an emergency in relation to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency or a declaration of a state of local emergency has been made;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "critical infrastructure" means a system, network, facility, asset or land described in section 48 [critical infrastructure identified];

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "critical infrastructure owner" means the following:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) a person who possesses, occupies, controls the use of or has the right to control the use of critical infrastructure;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) subject to the regulations, a person who has an estate or interest, whether legal or equitable, in critical infrastructure;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "critical infrastructure sector" means a prescribed critical infrastructure sector, which sector is necessary to protect, maintain or restore one or more of the matters referred to in section 48 (2) (b);

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "Crown land" means land, whether or not it is covered by water, that is vested in the government;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency" means a state that

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) is the result of any of the following:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (i)  an event that

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (A) has occurred, is ongoing or appears imminent, and

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (B) is caused by one or more incidents, whether or not those incidents occur in the same location or at the same time, of accident, fire, explosion, technical failure, rioting, security threat, terrorist activity within the meaning of section 83.01 of the Criminal Code, force of nature or a prescribed type of incident;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (ii)  the presence, suspected presence or imminent spread of a transmissible disease or an environmental toxin;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (iii)  a prescribed type of event or the presence or suspected presence of prescribed circumstances, and

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) requires the prompt coordination of action, or the special regulation of persons or property, to protect

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (i)  the health, safety or well-being of persons, or

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (ii)  the safety of property or of objects or sites of heritage value;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency instrument" means the following:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) if made by an individual, an order;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) if made by a person or entity other than an individual, a bylaw, resolution, law or other type of legal instrument by which the person or entity may lawfully exercise statutory powers or perform statutory duties;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency management" means the development and implementation of policies and plans with respect to the measures to be taken in each phase;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency management organization" means an entity referred to in section 20 [emergency management organizations];

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency management plan" means an emergency management plan prepared in accordance with section 52 [emergency management plans];

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency measure" means an action that is necessary or advisable to be taken during one or more phases, whether or not the action

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) is described in an emergency management plan, or

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) is taken as a result of the exercise of a response power or a recovery power;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency measures agreement" means an agreement made under Division 4 [Emergency Measures Agreements] of Part 2;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency resources" includes any personnel, supplies, services, personal property, equipment and facilities that are necessary or advisable for the purpose of taking emergency measures and does not include land;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "emergency system" means a prescribed system, or a system having prescribed characteristics, designed

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) to give warnings or notices to the public if an emergency is present, or

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) to facilitate, coordinate or carry out activities in relation to emergency management;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "employer" means a person who has responsibility, directly or indirectly, for

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) the employment of an employee, or

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) the management of another person who, under contract, provides services to the person;

heading: Definitions and application

paragraph: (b) the ministry of the member referred to in paragraph (a);
