paragraph: (2) An order or emergency instrument made under this Act does not apply to an Indigenous governing body unless the Indigenous governing body consents.

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: 2		  (1) Effective emergency management in British Columbia requires that the government, regulated entities, Indigenous governing bodies and other parties engaged in emergency management, in their relationships,

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (a) acknowledge and respect the authority of each party,

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (b) work towards harmonization and coordination of emergency measures, plans, policies and programs, and

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (c) foster collaborative approaches to matters of mutual interest.

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (2) Effective emergency management in British Columbia is based on the following principles:

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (a) practising emergency and disaster risk reduction, including by working proactively to prevent the creation of new risks, to reduce existing and future risks and to increase resilience;

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (b) investing in the measures necessary to reduce the risk of an emergency occurring and to enhance the economic, social, health and cultural resilience of society and the resilience of the environment to emergencies and any related adverse effects;

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (c) recognizing the relationship between a changing climate and emergency management, including recognizing that a changing climate contributes to the increased occurrence and adverse effects of some hazards and emergencies;

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (d) promoting cultural safety in emergency management, including by incorporating relevant actions in emergency management plans, policies and programs;

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (e) recognizing that the inherent right of self-government of Indigenous peoples includes authority to make laws in relation to emergency management;

heading: Principles of emergency management
paragraph: (f) recognizing the importance of Indigenous advice, input and stewardship activities in emergency management.

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph:
3
		  (1) Emergency management consists of the following phases:

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (a) the mitigation phase, in which measures are taken for the purposes of identifying and removing or reducing hazards so as to

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (i)  prevent emergencies from occurring, or

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (ii)  reduce, to the extent reasonably practicable, the scale, scope and adverse effects of an emergency that may occur;

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (b) the preparation phase, in which measures are taken for the purpose of establishing the knowledge, capability and capacity to anticipate, respond to and recover from the adverse effects of an emergency;

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (c) the response phase, in which measures are taken for the purpose of responding to an emergency, including preventing and reducing the adverse effects of the emergency;

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (d) the recovery phase, in which measures are taken for the purpose of recovering from an emergency, including measures to

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (i)  restore the health, safety and well-being of affected persons,

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (ii)  restore the safety of property or of objects or sites of heritage value, and

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (iii)  improve, to the extent reasonably practicable, assets, services and processes so as to reduce the risk of and increase resilience to emergencies.

heading: Emergency management phases
paragraph: (2) For certainty, measures relevant to one phase may be taken at the same time as measures taken in relation to any other phase.

heading: Standards, protocols and procedures
paragraph:
4
		  The minister may do one or both of the following:

heading: Standards, protocols and procedures
paragraph: (a) establish standards, protocols and procedures for the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty under this Act;

heading: Standards, protocols and procedures
paragraph: (b) require, by order, a person or a class of persons to comply with one or more of the standards, protocols and procedures referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph:
5
		  (1) The minister may make an order under this section if the minister is satisfied of either of the following:

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (a) that a person has not exercised the person's powers or performed the person's duties under this Act, or has not done so adequately;

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (b) that the order is necessary to achieve the objectives of this Act.

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by order, require a person to do any of the following with respect to the person's powers or duties under this Act:

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (a) exercise a power or perform a duty;

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (b) comply with the directions of the minister or the provincial administrator with respect to exercising a power or performing a duty;

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (c) consult and coordinate with another person or entity in exercising a power or performing a duty, including requiring consultation and coordination in accordance with

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (i)  the regulations, or

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (ii)  the directions of the minister or the provincial administrator.

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (3) The minister may include in an order made under this section a requirement that a person do one or both of the following:

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (a) comply with the order by a specified date or in accordance with a schedule;

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (b) give evidence satisfactory to the minister or the provincial administrator of the person's compliance.

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (4) For certainty, the minister may make an order under this section in relation to a participating authority's exercise of a power or performance of a duty under an emergency measures agreement.

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (5) The minister may not make an order under this section in relation to the Lieutenant Governor in Council's powers or duties under this Act.

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (6) The minister may not make an order under this section in relation to the Nisga'a Nation's or a treaty first nation's powers or duties under this Act.

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (7) The minister may request the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation to take an action referred to in subsection (2) in relation to the Nisga'a Nation's or the treaty first nation's powers or duties under this Act.

heading: Ensuring Act's objectives are met
paragraph: (8) If the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation does not intend to comply with a request made under subsection (7), the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation must inform the minister in writing of the reasons for not complying with the request.

heading: Committees
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The minister may establish committees to advise or assist the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister or the provincial administrator with respect to matters under this Act.

heading: Committees
paragraph: (2) The minister may appoint members to a committee.

heading: Committees
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), a committee member may

heading: Committees
paragraph: (a) be reimbursed for reasonable travelling and out-of-pocket expenses necessarily incurred in discharging the member's responsibilities as a committee member, and

heading: Committees
paragraph: (b) be paid remuneration for discharging the member's responsibilities as a committee member, unless the person is a public service employee, in which case, no remuneration may be paid.

heading: Committees
paragraph: (4) Reimbursement and remuneration of committee members are subject to the direction of the minister and must be in accordance with the directives of Treasury Board.

heading: Committees
paragraph: (5) The minister may, in writing, delegate to the provincial administrator any of the minister's powers under this section.

heading: Procurement powers
paragraph:
7

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph:
8

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) to cooperate in taking emergency measures;

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) to provide or receive assistance, including in the form of financial aid, emergency resources and the use of land, in taking emergency measures;

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph: (c) to recover costs in relation to the provision of assistance.

heading: Payments and transfers
paragraph:
9
		  The minister may make payments and transfers, subject to any terms or conditions that the minister may impose, for the purposes of one or more of the following:

heading: Payments and transfers
paragraph: (a) to prepare for, respond to and recover from critical incidents;

heading: Payments and transfers
paragraph: (b) to take emergency measures;

heading: Payments and transfers
paragraph: (c) to acquire emergency resources.

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund
paragraph:
10
		  (1) In this section, "fiscal year" means the period beginning on April 1 in one year and ending on March 31 in the next year.

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund
paragraph: (2) The minister may pay money out of the consolidated revenue fund for the purposes of one or more of the following:

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund
paragraph: (a) to respond to critical incidents;

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund
paragraph: (b) to take emergency measures in relation to the response and recovery phases;

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund
paragraph: (c) to acquire emergency resources in relation to the response and recovery phases.

paragraph: (3) Nothing in subsection (2) authorizes the minister to make a payment out of the consolidated revenue fund for financial assistance under Division 3 [Financial Assistance] of Part 7.

paragraph: (4) The minister must prepare a report for each fiscal year, with respect to payments made under subsection (2) in the fiscal year, that summarizes all of the following:

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund
paragraph: (a) the nature of the critical incident or emergency;

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund
paragraph: (b) the total amount of the payments made under subsection (2) in the fiscal year in respect of each critical incident or emergency;

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund

paragraph: (5) The minister must, as soon as practicable, submit a copy of the report to the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.

heading: Money from consolidated revenue fund

heading: Provincial emergency management organization
paragraph:
11
		  (1) The minister must ensure that there is, within the ministry of the minister, an office of the government responsible for emergency management throughout British Columbia.

heading: Provincial emergency management organization
paragraph: (2) A deputy minister responsible for the provincial emergency management organization must be appointed under the Public Service Act.

heading: Provincial emergency management organization
paragraph: (3) The minister must designate, as the provincial administrator, a person appointed under the Public Service Act.

heading: Provincial emergency management organization
paragraph: (4) The deputy minister referred to in subsection (2) must, in accordance with the Public Service Act, appoint officers and employees that the deputy minister considers necessary to assist the minister and the provincial administrator to exercise powers and perform duties under this Act.

heading: General purposes
paragraph: 12		  The purposes of the provincial emergency management organization are as follows:

heading: General purposes
paragraph: (a) to provide, throughout British Columbia, oversight, leadership and coordination of activities with respect to each phase of emergency management;

heading: General purposes
paragraph: (b) to make recommendations to the minister respecting emergency management;

heading: General purposes
paragraph: (c) to participate on behalf of the government, if required by the minister, in initiatives that foster mutual aid between the government and any other person, organization or entity;

heading: General purposes
paragraph: (d) to fulfill other prescribed purposes.

heading: Authority to act as provincial administrator
paragraph:
13
		  (1) The provincial administrator may authorize one or more persons appointed under the Public Service Act to exercise a power or perform a duty of the provincial administrator under this Act.

heading: Authority to act as provincial administrator
paragraph: (2) An authorization made under subsection (1)

heading: Authority to act as provincial administrator
paragraph: (a) must be in writing, with authorized members identified by name, title or position, and

heading: Authority to act as provincial administrator
paragraph: (b) must not include a power delegated to the provincial administrator under section 6 (5) [committees].

heading: General powers of provincial administrator
paragraph: 14		  The provincial administrator may do one or more of the following:

heading: General powers of provincial administrator
paragraph: (a) give advice and assistance to regulated entities, on their request, respecting any matter under this Act;

heading: General powers of provincial administrator
paragraph: (b) conduct public information programs relating to emergency management;

heading: General powers of provincial administrator
paragraph: (c) coordinate emergency management activities, including by collaborating with persons in other jurisdictions;

heading: General powers of provincial administrator
paragraph: (d) exercise additional prescribed powers.

heading: Publishing minister's orders
paragraph:
15
		  Subject to the regulations and section 159 [duty to protect confidentiality], and without limiting any other provision of this Act that requires a matter to be published, the minister must publish an order made by the minister under this Act.

heading: Disclosing and publishing information
paragraph:
16
		  Subject to the regulations and Division 2 [Personal and Sensitive Information and Indigenous Knowledge] of Part 9, the provincial administrator may disclose to a person, or publish, any of the following:

heading: Disclosing and publishing information
paragraph: (a) information obtained, directly or indirectly, under this Act;

heading: Disclosing and publishing information
paragraph: (b) information respecting advice, assistance and directions given by the minister or the provincial administrator under this Act;

heading: Disclosing and publishing information
paragraph: (c) surveys, studies, reports and other records made or received by the provincial administrator under this Act.

heading: Annual meeting to review agreements with Indigenous peoples
paragraph:
17
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the provincial administrator must ensure that Indigenous governing bodies that are parties to agreements made under this Act are invited to meet at least once each calendar year with one or more members of the provincial emergency management organization to discuss the effectiveness of the agreements.

heading: Annual meeting to review agreements with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (2) In consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing bodies referred to in subsection (1), the minister may direct that the meeting referred to in that subsection be deferred to a later time, including to a time in a subsequent calendar year, as specified by the minister.

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph:
18
		  (1) Subject to this Act,

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) a municipality or regional district may exercise powers and must perform duties under this Act as follows:

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (i)  in the case of a municipality, within the boundaries of the municipality;

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a regional district, within the boundaries of any electoral areas within the regional district, and

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation may exercise powers under this Act as follows:

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (i)  in the case of the Nisga'a Nation, within the boundaries of Nisga'a Lands;

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a treaty first nation, within the boundaries of the treaty first nation's treaty lands.

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (2) For certainty,

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) a municipality or regional district may exercise powers and must perform duties under this Act in relation to any Crown land within the boundaries of the areas referred to in subsection (1) (a) (i) or (ii), as applicable, and

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation may exercise powers under this Act in relation to any Crown land within the boundaries of the areas referred to in subsection (1) (b) (i) or (ii), as applicable.

heading: Local authority jurisdiction
paragraph: (3) Except as otherwise provided for under this Act, a local authority's responsibilities under this Act continue to apply regardless of whether any other person is responsible for performing duties under this Act with respect to an area within the jurisdiction of the local authority.

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Subject to subsection (5) and any limits or conditions otherwise provided for under this Act, the head of a local authority may exercise a power or perform a duty of a local authority under this Act.

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (5), a local authority may designate one or more of the following to act on behalf of the local authority:

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (a) a member of the local authority's emergency management organization;

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (b) in a case where powers or duties have been set out in an agreement or other instrument made for the purposes of joining a multijurisdictional emergency management organization, an employee of a member of the multijurisdictional emergency management organization;

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (c) if the local authority is the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, any other person or entity.

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (3) A designation must be in writing, with designated persons or entities identified by name, title or position.

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (4) A local authority must ensure that the process for determining who among the local authority's designates may exercise powers or perform duties is set out

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (a) in the local authority's emergency management plan, or

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (b) in an agreement or other instrument made for the purposes of joining a multijurisdictional emergency management organization.

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (5) The head of a local authority or a person designated under subsection (2) must not exercise a power under any of the following sections:

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (a) section 110 [response borrowing];

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (b) section 118 [recovery powers];

heading: Authority to act as or on behalf of local authority
paragraph: (c) section 119 [recovery borrowing].

heading: Emergency management organizations
paragraph:
20
		  (1) The purposes of a local authority's emergency management organization include the following:

heading: Emergency management organizations
paragraph: (a) to provide, in all or part of the area within the jurisdiction of the local authority, oversight, leadership and coordination of activities with respect to each phase of emergency management;

heading: Emergency management organizations
paragraph: (b) to make recommendations to the local authority respecting emergency management.

heading: Emergency management organizations
paragraph: (2) A local authority must do at least one of the following:

heading: Emergency management organizations
paragraph: (a) in accordance with the regulations, if any, establish, appoint members to and maintain an emergency management organization;

heading: Emergency management organizations
paragraph: (b) join a multijurisdictional emergency management organization established under section 21.

heading: Emergency management organizations
paragraph: (3) If a local authority has more than one emergency management organization, or has one or more emergency management organizations and joins a multijurisdictional emergency management organization, the local authority must ensure that, in the aggregate, the purposes referred to in subsection (1) are fulfilled in relation to all of the areas within the jurisdiction of the local authority.

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A multijurisdictional emergency management organization may be established, in accordance with the regulations, if any, by 2 or more of the following:

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (a) a local authority;

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (b) the government;

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (c) an Indigenous governing body.

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (2) The purposes of a multijurisdictional emergency management organization include the following:

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (a) to provide, in relation to the areas or matters for which the organization has responsibility, oversight, leadership and coordination of activities with respect to each phase of emergency management;

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (b) to make recommendations to organization members respecting emergency management.

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (3) A local authority that joins a multijurisdictional emergency management organization must

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (a) give to the provincial administrator all of the following:

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (i)  a copy of all prescribed records relevant to the local authority's participation in the organization;

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (ii)  any information required by the provincial administrator, and

heading: Multijurisdictional emergency management organizations
paragraph: (b) comply with any directions given by the provincial administrator with respect to ensuring that the local authority's powers and duties under this Act are carried out in accordance with the Act.

heading: Minister may require local authority to establish or join multijurisdictional emergency management organization
paragraph:
22
		  The minister may, by order, require

heading: Minister may require local authority to establish or join multijurisdictional emergency management organization
paragraph: (a) 2 or more local authorities, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, to establish a multijurisdictional emergency management organization under section 21, or

heading: Minister may require local authority to establish or join multijurisdictional emergency management organization
paragraph: (b) a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, to join a multijurisdictional emergency management organization.

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph:
23
		  (1) Subject to this section, a local authority may enter into agreements, including with the government of Canada or of another jurisdiction of Canada or with persons located outside British Columbia, for any of the following purposes:

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) to cooperate in taking emergency measures;

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) to provide and receive assistance, including in the form of financial aid, emergency resources and the use of land, in taking emergency measures;

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (c) to recover costs in relation to the provision of assistance.

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (2) A local authority must not enter into an agreement under this section in relation to the use of land within the specified land of an Indigenous people, unless an Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of the Indigenous people consents to the agreement.

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (3) If a local authority enters into an agreement with a government or an agency of a government outside British Columbia, the following apply:

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) in the case of an agreement with the council of a municipality other than the City of Vancouver, section 23 [agreements with other public authorities] of the Community Charter;

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) in the case of an agreement with the board of a regional district, sections 263 [corporate powers] and 264 [minister approval required for certain out-of-Province or out-of-country agreements] of the Local Government Act.

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (4) A term or condition of an agreement made under this section has no effect to the extent that compliance with the term or condition, by any party to the agreement, prevents or interferes with compliance with any part of

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) an agreement made with the minister for the purposes of responding to or recovering from an emergency,

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) an order of the minister or provincial administrator made under Part 5 [Provincial Response and Recovery Phases], or

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (c) an order made under Part 6 [Local Authority Response and Recovery Phases].

heading: Local authority may enter into agreements
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this section is intended to limit the authority of a local authority to make an agreement under any other enactment.

heading: General report to minister
paragraph: 24		  Without limiting any reporting requirement imposed under the regulations, a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, must

heading: General report to minister
paragraph: (a) prepare a report on any matter required by the minister, and

heading: General report to minister
paragraph: (b) provide the report to the provincial administrator

heading: General report to minister
paragraph: (i)  within the period required by the minister, and

heading: General report to minister
paragraph: (ii)  in the form and manner required by the provincial administrator.

heading: Making emergency measures agreements
paragraph:
25
		  (1) In this section, "party" means a party to an emergency measures agreement.

heading: Making emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (2) The minister and another party may enter into an emergency measures agreement under which the other party, or a person for which the other party has responsibility, may exercise one or more powers, and agrees to perform one or more duties, that may be exercised or performed by a local authority under this Act.

heading: Making emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (3) An emergency measures agreement must be made in accordance with this Division.

heading: Making emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (4) An emergency measures agreement must include as a party to the agreement each local authority having jurisdiction over an area, other than Crown land or prescribed land, that is subject to the agreement.

heading: Making emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (5) The provincial administrator must publish a copy of each emergency measures agreement and any amendments to those agreements.

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph:
26
		  (1) An emergency measures agreement must provide that a participating authority may exercise powers and must perform duties under the following provisions:

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (a) Divisions 1 and 2 [local authority response and recovery phases] of Part 6;

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (b) sections 107 [response powers] and 118 (2) [recovery powers];

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (c) a regulation made in relation to any provision referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (2) The following provisions apply to a participating authority that exercises response powers or recovery powers, as applicable, under an emergency measures agreement:

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (a) sections 105, 106, 116 and 117 [when and how response and recovery powers may be exercised];

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (b) section 108 [consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry];

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (c) section 120 [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples].

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (3) An emergency measures agreement must list any other provisions of this Act and the regulations

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (a) under which a participating authority may exercise powers and must perform duties, or

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (b) that apply for the purposes of exercising powers and performing duties under the agreement.

heading: Powers and duties under emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (4) A participating authority that has entered into an emergency measures agreement in relation to powers and duties under this Act must exercise the powers and perform the duties in accordance with the agreement.

heading: Additional content of emergency measures agreements
paragraph:
27
		  (1) An emergency measures agreement must include at least the following:

heading: Additional content of emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (a) a description of the area within which a participating authority may exercise powers and must perform duties under the agreement;

heading: Additional content of emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (b) a provision identifying the head of the participating authority by the individual's name, title or position;

heading: Additional content of emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (c) a provision identifying any limits and conditions on the designation, by the participating authority or the head of the participating authority, of persons to act on behalf of the participating authority;

heading: Additional content of emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (d) a provision identifying the type of emergency instrument to be used to exercise powers and perform duties under the agreement;

heading: Additional content of emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (e) an agreement to publish each emergency instrument made by or on behalf of the participating authority.

heading: Additional content of emergency measures agreements
paragraph: (2) An emergency measures agreement may include other provisions as agreed to by the parties, including terms and conditions of the participating authority's exercise of powers and performance of duties.

heading: Limits on minister's powers
paragraph:
28
		  (1) This section applies despite anything to the contrary in Divisions 1 and 2 [local authority response and recovery phases] of Part 6.

heading: Limits on minister's powers
paragraph: (2) If a participating authority acting under an emergency measures agreement is the government of Canada, or a person or entity for which that government has responsibility,

heading: Limits on minister's powers
paragraph: (a) the participating authority is not required to seek the approval of the minister to exercise a power under Division 1 or 2 of Part 6, and

heading: Limits on minister's powers
paragraph: (b) the minister may not cancel a declaration of a state of local emergency or a declaration of a local recovery period made by the participating authority.

heading: References for interpretive purposes
paragraph:
29
		  For the purposes of a provision of this Act or the regulations that applies under an emergency measures agreement with a participating authority,

heading: References for interpretive purposes
paragraph: (a) a reference to a local authority must be read as a reference to the participating authority, and

heading: References for interpretive purposes
paragraph: (b) a reference to the head of a local authority must be read as a reference to the head of the participating authority identified under section 27 (1) (b).

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph:
30
		  (1) If the provincial administrator is of the opinion that there is a need for volunteers with respect to a specialized measure, the provincial administrator may invite persons to apply to be authorized as public safety providers.

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (2) An application must be made in the form and manner required by the provincial administrator.

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (3) The provincial administrator may grant an authorization to a person if the provincial administrator is satisfied that the person

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (a) has volunteers who are trained and qualified to take the specialized measure referred to in subsection (1),

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (b) will comply with all applicable orders made, and directions given, under this Act by the provincial administrator, and

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (c) meets any prescribed criteria.

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (4) The provincial administrator may revoke all or part of an authorization granted under subsection (3) in the following circumstances:

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (a) the person no longer has volunteers who are trained and qualified to take the specialized measure that was the basis for granting the authorization;

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (b) the person fails to comply with any applicable orders made, or directions given, under this Act by the provincial administrator;

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (c) the person, or one or more volunteers for whom the person has responsibility, fails to comply with any applicable standards, protocols or procedures referred to in section 31 (1) (a) (i), whether or not an order has been made under section 31 (1) (b);

heading: Authorization of public safety providers
paragraph: (d) prescribed circumstances.

paragraph: (ii)  the taking of specialized measures by volunteers;

heading: Standards, protocols and procedures
paragraph: (b) require, by order, a person or a class of persons to comply with one or more of the standards, protocols and procedures referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Standards, protocols and procedures
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, the provincial administrator must publish an order made under subsection (1) (b).

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph:
32
		  (1) A person or entity referred to in subsection (2) may request the provincial administrator to assist in coordinating the deployment of volunteers in response to a critical incident or an emergency.

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (2) The following may make a request:

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (a) a local authority;

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (b) an Indigenous governing body;

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (c) a department of the government of Canada;

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (d) a person who is a party to an agreement under section 8 [minister may enter into agreements];

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (e) a police or emergency health service;

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (f) a prescribed person or a person in a prescribed class of persons.

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (3) A request made under subsection (1) must be made in the form and manner required by the provincial administrator.

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (4) The provincial administrator, if satisfied that it is necessary to respond to a critical incident or an emergency, may do one or both of the following:

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (a) deploy volunteers who are registered with the provincial administrator;

heading: Requests for deployment
paragraph: (b) authorize the deployment, by a local authority, a public safety provider or a person or entity that under the regulations is authorized for the purposes of this subsection, of volunteers who are registered with the local authority, public safety provider or authorized person or entity.

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph:
33
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: "coordination agreement" means an agreement entered into under section 6 of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: (a) relating to the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty under Part 5 [Provincial Response and Recovery Phases] or 6 [Local Authority Response and Recovery Phases] of this Act, or

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: (b) for a purpose referred to in section 34 (1) (b) of this Act,

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: but does not include a decision-making agreement or statutory power agreement in relation to the exercise of a power under Part 5 or 6;

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: "decision-making agreement" means an agreement negotiated and entered into under section 7 of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act  relating to statutory powers of decision under this Act;

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: "specified coordination agreement" means a coordination agreement described in paragraph (a) of the definition of "coordination agreement";

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: "statutory power" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Judicial Review Procedure Act but does not include a power or right conferred by this Act to exercise a statutory power of decision;

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: "statutory power agreement" means an agreement entered into under section 6 of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act that relates to one or both of the following:

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: (a) the exercise of a statutory power under this Act jointly by

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: (i)  an Indigenous governing body, and

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: (ii)  a person or entity that is authorized to exercise the statutory power under this Act;

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: (b) the consent of an Indigenous governing body before the exercise of a statutory power under this Act;

heading: Definitions for this Part
paragraph: "statutory power of decision" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Judicial Review Procedure Act.

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: 34		  (1) Subject to this Division, the minister may enter into a coordination agreement with an Indigenous governing body for one or more of the following purposes:

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (a) to coordinate

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (i)  the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty under Part 5 [Provincial Response and Recovery Phases] or 6 [Local Authority Response and Recovery Phases], and

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (ii)  the exercise of the inherent right of self-government by the Indigenous governing body in responding to or recovering from an emergency;

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (b) to harmonize and coordinate plans, policies and programs in relation to the response and recovery phases.

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), a coordination agreement made with an Indigenous governing body may relate to all or part of the traditional territory or treaty area of the Indigenous people on whose behalf the Indigenous governing body acts.

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (3) The minister must not enter into a coordination agreement that relates to an area that is within Nisga'a Lands or treaty lands of a treaty first nation unless the Nisga'a Nation or the treaty first nation, as applicable, consents.

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (4) Without limiting subsection (3), the minister must, before entering into a coordination agreement that relates to an area within a treaty area of the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (a) consult and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the Nisga'a Nation and the treaty first nation;

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (b) consider

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (i)  any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation or the treaty first nation, and

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (ii)  the rights of the Indigenous peoples on whose behalf the Nisga'a Nation or the treaty first nation acts.

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (5) A coordination agreement may include one or more of the following as parties to the agreement:

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (a) a local authority;

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (b) another Indigenous governing body;

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (c) a participating authority;

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (d) the government of Canada;

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (e) the government of another jurisdiction of Canada.

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (6) A coordination agreement must include a process for resolving any disputes in relation to the agreement.

heading: Coordination agreements
paragraph: (7) The provincial administrator must publish a copy of each coordination agreement and any amendments to each agreement.

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph:
35
		  (1) For the purposes of this Act, the minister may enter into a specified coordination agreement only in accordance with this Division.

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (2) A specified coordination agreement may do any of the following in relation to the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty under Part 5 [Provincial Response and Recovery Phases] or 6 [Local Authority Response and Recovery Phases]:

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (3) of this section, require the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister, a local authority or a participating authority to exercise the power or perform the duty;

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (b) require the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister, a local authority or a participating authority to refrain from exercising the power or performing the duty;

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (c) set limits or conditions on the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister, a local authority or a participating authority;

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (d) impose requirements in relation to the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister, a local authority or a participating authority;

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (e) require the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister, a local authority or a participating authority to consult and cooperate, in accordance with the agreement, with an Indigenous governing body that is a party to the agreement in exercising the power or performing the duty.

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (3) A specified coordination agreement may not require the Lieutenant Governor in Council to exercise a power under Division 5 or 6 of Part 5 or Division 5 of Part 6.

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (4) The minister must not enter into a specified coordination agreement that relates to the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty by the Lieutenant Governor in Council unless the Lieutenant Governor in Council authorizes the minister to negotiate and enter into the agreement.

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (5) A specified coordination agreement is not effective until the agreement is published, or until a later date specified in the agreement.

heading: Specified coordination agreements
paragraph: (6) For certainty, subsection (5) applies to an agreement that amends a specified coordination agreement.

heading: Effect of specified coordination agreement
paragraph:
36
		  If a specified coordination agreement has been entered into in relation to a power or duty referred to in Part 5 [Provincial Response and Recovery Phases] or 6 [Local Authority Response and Recovery Phases],

heading: Effect of specified coordination agreement
paragraph: (a) the power must be exercised and the duty must be performed, as applicable, in accordance with the agreement,

heading: Effect of specified coordination agreement
paragraph: (b) a reference under this Act to the power or duty is to be read as a reference to the power as exercised or the duty as performed in accordance with the agreement, and

heading: Effect of specified coordination agreement
paragraph: (c) the terms of the agreement relating to any requirements, limits, conditions or procedures referred to in section 35 (2) in respect of the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty have the force of law.

heading: Decision-making agreements and statutory power agreements
paragraph:
37
		  (1) For the purposes of this Act, the minister may enter into a statutory power agreement only in accordance with this section.

heading: Decision-making agreements and statutory power agreements
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may authorize the minister, on behalf of the government, to negotiate and enter into a statutory power agreement with an Indigenous governing body.

heading: Decision-making agreements and statutory power agreements
paragraph: (3) A decision-making agreement and a statutory power agreement must include a process for resolving any disputes in relation to the agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreements and statutory power agreements
paragraph: (4) Section 7 (2) to (5) of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act applies to a statutory power agreement.

heading: Effect of agreement
paragraph: 38		  If a decision-making agreement or a statutory power agreement has been entered into,

heading: Effect of agreement
paragraph: (a) the statutory power of decision or the statutory power, as applicable, must be exercised in accordance with the agreement,

heading: Effect of agreement
paragraph: (b) a reference under this Act to the statutory power of decision referred to in paragraph (a) or the statutory power referred to in paragraph (a) is to be read as a reference to the statutory power of decision or the statutory power as exercised in accordance with the agreement, and

heading: Effect of agreement
paragraph: (c) the following terms of the agreement have the force of law:

heading: Effect of agreement
paragraph: (i)  terms identifying the person or entity that is exercising, or providing consent in relation to, a statutory power of decision or a statutory power in accordance with the agreement;

heading: Effect of agreement
paragraph: (ii)  terms relating to the criteria or procedures for the exercise of, or consent in relation to, a statutory power of decision or a statutory power in accordance with the agreement.

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph:
39
		  (1) The provincial administrator must prepare, maintain and implement the following:

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (a) a comprehensive emergency management plan that

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (i)  applies throughout British Columbia, and

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (ii)  includes the emergency management plans given to the provincial administrator under section 44 (2) (c) [emergency management planning by lead ministers];

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (b) one or more emergency management plans.

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (2) An emergency management plan must, in relation to the area that the plan applies to,

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (a) include a description of each area, if any, that is described for the purposes of

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (i)  section 90 [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples] in one or more of the following:

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (A) an agreement made under section 41 (1) (d);

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (B) any other agreement with an Indigenous governing body, or

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (ii)  section 120 [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples] in an agreement made under section 55 (1) (e) [consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples], and

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (b) specify the Indigenous governing body in relation to each area described.

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (3) The provincial administrator must review and revise, in accordance with the regulations, the comprehensive emergency management plan and the emergency management plan or plans referred to in subsection (1) (b).

heading: Emergency management planning and information
paragraph: (4) The provincial administrator must make prescribed information available to the public in relation to potential emergencies that could affect all or part of British Columbia, including information relating to hazards, risks and vulnerabilities.

heading: Consultation with local authorities
paragraph:
40
		  When preparing or reviewing and revising a comprehensive emergency management plan or an emergency management plan under section 39, the provincial administrator must

heading: Consultation with local authorities
paragraph: (a) consult and coordinate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with a local authority in a prescribed class of local authorities, and

heading: Consultation with local authorities
paragraph: (b) consider any comments received from a local authority consulted in accordance with paragraph (a).

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph:
41
		  (1) When preparing or reviewing and revising a comprehensive emergency management plan or an emergency management plan under section 39, the provincial administrator must do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) consult and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with each Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of Indigenous peoples whose traditional territory or treaty area includes an area to which the plan applies;

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) consider

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  any comments received from an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a), and

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  the rights of the Indigenous peoples referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (c) incorporate into the plan Indigenous knowledge, if available.

heading: Oversight of emergency management planning
paragraph:
42
		  The provincial administrator may do one or more of the following:

heading: Oversight of emergency management planning
paragraph: (a) require, by order, one or more regulated entities, other than a government minister, the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, to provide information and records respecting emergency management planning prepared by the regulated entities;

heading: Oversight of emergency management planning
paragraph: (b) request a government minister, the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation to provide information and records respecting emergency management planning prepared by the government minister, Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation;

heading: Oversight of emergency management planning
paragraph: (c) with respect to any information or records received under this Act, give advice and directions, including requiring changes to records.

heading: Government continuity plans
paragraph:
43
		  (1) The Legislative Assembly must prepare and maintain a plan to ensure the continued delivery, during an emergency, of leadership and services necessary for the effective functioning of the legislative branch of government.

heading: Government continuity plans
paragraph: (2) The Executive Council must prepare and maintain a plan to ensure the continued delivery, during an emergency, of leadership and services necessary for the effective functioning of the Executive Council.

heading: Government continuity plans
paragraph: (3) The office of the Lieutenant Governor must prepare and maintain a plan to ensure the continued delivery, during an emergency, of leadership and services necessary for the effective functioning of the office of the Lieutenant Governor.

heading: Government continuity plans
paragraph: (6) The provincial administrator must give advice and assistance with respect to preparing or maintaining a plan referred to in this section as follows:

heading: Government continuity plans
paragraph: (a) to the Legislative Assembly, if requested in writing by the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly;

heading: Government continuity plans
paragraph: (b) to the Executive Council, if requested in writing by the Premier of British Columbia;

heading: Government continuity plans
paragraph: (c) to the office of the Lieutenant Governor, if requested in writing by the Executive Director of the office of the Lieutenant Governor.

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph:
44
		  (1) On request of the provincial administrator, a lead minister must exercise the powers of the provincial administrator under section 42 with respect to a prescribed public sector agency or critical infrastructure owner, or a public sector agency or critical infrastructure owner in a prescribed class.

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (2) A lead minister must do all of the following:

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (a) prepare and maintain one or more risk assessments with respect to prescribed types of hazards;

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (b) prepare and maintain one or more emergency management plans with respect to prescribed types of hazards and any other prescribed persons, places, matters or things;

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (c) give copies of the risk assessments and emergency management plans to the provincial administrator;

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (d) take any emergency measures identified in the comprehensive emergency management plan as emergency measures to be taken by the lead minister.

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (3) A lead minister must prepare and maintain a business continuity plan.

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (4) A lead minister must review and revise, in accordance with the regulations, the lead minister's risk assessments, emergency management plans and business continuity plan.

heading: Emergency management planning by lead ministers
paragraph: (5) A lead minister is responsible for performing the lead minister's duties under this Act throughout British Columbia with respect to the matters for which the lead minister has responsibility.

heading: Emergency management planning by non-lead ministers
paragraph:
45
		  (1) A government minister that is not a lead minister must do all of the following:

heading: Emergency management planning by non-lead ministers
paragraph: (a) prepare and maintain a business continuity plan;

heading: Emergency management planning by non-lead ministers
paragraph: (b) take any emergency measures identified in the comprehensive emergency management plan as emergency measures to be taken by the government minister.

heading: Emergency management planning by non-lead ministers
paragraph: (2) A government minister that is not a lead minister must review and revise, in accordance with the regulations, the government minister's business continuity plan.

heading: Emergency management planning by public sector agencies
paragraph:
46
		  (1) A public sector agency must, if required by the regulations,

heading: Emergency management planning by public sector agencies
paragraph: (a) prepare and maintain a risk assessment with respect to prescribed types of hazards,

heading: Emergency management planning by public sector agencies
paragraph: (b) prepare, maintain and implement an emergency management plan, and

heading: Emergency management planning by public sector agencies
paragraph: (c) prepare and maintain a business continuity plan.

heading: Emergency management planning by public sector agencies
paragraph: (2) A public sector agency must review and revise, in accordance with the regulations, the public sector agency's risk assessment, emergency management plan and business continuity plan.

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph:
48
		  (1) A system, network, facility or asset, whether physical or virtual and whether publicly or privately owned, is critical infrastructure for the purposes of this Act and the regulations if

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (a) it is prescribed as critical infrastructure, or

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (b) it is within a prescribed class of systems, networks, facilities or assets.

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (2) A system, network, facility or asset, or a class of systems, networks, facilities or assets, must not be prescribed unless the system, network, facility or asset, or a class of any of these, is

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (a) designed, used or intended to be used in relation to functions performed by persons acting within a critical infrastructure sector, or

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (b) necessary to protect, maintain or restore one or more of the following:

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (i)  the health, safety or well-being of persons;

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (ii)  the environment;

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (iii)  the economy;

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (iv)  the security of the province;

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (v)  the effective functioning of any branch of government;

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (vi)  the provision of emergency resources;

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (vii)  a prescribed matter.

heading: Critical infrastructure identified
paragraph: (3) Land is critical infrastructure for the purposes of this Act and the regulations if the land is occupied by, used in association with or necessary to access a system, network, facility or asset referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Emergency management planning by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph:
49
		  (1) A critical infrastructure owner must, if required by the regulations,

heading: Emergency management planning by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (a) prepare and maintain a risk assessment with respect to the types of hazards that may affect the critical infrastructure,

heading: Emergency management planning by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (b) prepare, maintain and implement an emergency management plan, and

heading: Emergency management planning by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (c) prepare and maintain a business continuity plan.

heading: Emergency management planning by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (2) A critical infrastructure owner must review and revise, in accordance with the regulations, the critical infrastructure owner's risk assessment, emergency management plan and business continuity plan.

heading: Emergency management planning by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (3) A critical infrastructure owner is responsible for performing its duties under this Act throughout British Columbia with respect to the persons, places and things for which the critical infrastructure owner has responsibility.

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph:
50
		  (1) If required by the regulations, a critical infrastructure owner must give to the provincial administrator the following information and records:

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (a) a copy of the critical infrastructure owner's risk assessment, emergency management plan and business continuity plan, including any revisions;

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (b) any prescribed information and records;

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (c) if required by the provincial administrator,

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (i)  a copy of the information and records used to prepare the records referred to in paragraph (a), and

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (ii)  any information specified by the provincial administrator.

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (2) Information and records referred to in this section must be given to the provincial administrator

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (a) in the form and manner required by the provincial administrator, and

heading: Reporting by critical infrastructure owners
paragraph: (b) within the period specified by the regulations or, if the regulations do not specify a period or do not apply, by the date specified by the provincial administrator.

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph:
51
		  (1) In this section and section 52, "vulnerable", in relation to an individual, animal, place or thing, or a class of individuals, animals, places or things, means the following:

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (a) particularly susceptible, due to physical or geographic location or environmental factors, or other similar factors, to the adverse effects of an emergency;

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (b) having prescribed characteristics.

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (2) A risk assessment must be prepared in accordance with this section and the regulations.

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (3) Subject to Division 2 [Duties of Regulated Entities] of this Part and the regulations, a risk assessment must identify all reasonably foreseeable hazards and assess all of the following:

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (a) the extent of the risk that each hazard presents, including

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (i)  the likelihood that an emergency may occur, and

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (ii)  the potential scale and scope of each emergency identified under subparagraph (i);

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (b) the potential consequences for persons or property, or for objects or sites of heritage value, if an emergency occurs, giving special consideration to

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (i)  individuals who may experience intersectional disadvantage, and

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (ii)  vulnerable individuals, animals, places or things;

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (c) any prescribed matters.

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (4) A risk assessment must be based on all of the following:

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (a) studies and surveys;

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (b) Indigenous knowledge and local knowledge, if available;

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (c) changes in the local climate or extreme weather events that can reasonably be expected to result from a changing global climate;

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (d) other relevant information that is reasonably available from prescribed sources of information or any other source;

heading: Risk assessments
paragraph: (e) the results of the actions required under sections 54 [consultation and coordination with local authorities] and 55 [consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples].

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph:
52
		  (1) An emergency management plan must be prepared in accordance with this section and the regulations.

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, an emergency management plan must describe at least the following:

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (a) measures that are necessary or advisable for the purposes of each phase;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (b) the roles, powers and duties of persons identified in the plan by name, title or position;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (c) requirements for emergency resources;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (d) procedures for engaging emergency systems;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (e) the emergency management training and exercise programs that will be conducted;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (f) measures to mitigate any adverse effects of an emergency on

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (i)  individuals who may experience intersectional disadvantage, and

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (ii)  vulnerable individuals, animals, places or things;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (g) measures to promote cultural safety;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (h) any prescribed matters.

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (3) In addition to the requirements of subsection (2), the emergency management plan of a local authority must

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (a) include a plan for the evacuation and care of individuals and animals in the area within the jurisdiction of the local authority,

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (b) include a description of each area, if any, that is described for the purposes of section 120 [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples] in one or more of the following:

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (i)  an agreement made under section 55 (1) (e) [consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples];

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (ii)  any other agreement with an Indigenous governing body, and

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (c) specify the Indigenous governing body in relation to each area described.

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (4) An emergency management plan must be based on all of the following:

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (a) all applicable risk assessments that are available;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (b) the results of the actions required under sections 54 and 55;

heading: Emergency management plans
paragraph: (c) any prescribed matters.

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph:
53
		  (1) A business continuity plan must be prepared in accordance with this section and the regulations.

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (2) A business continuity plan of a regulated entity other than a critical infrastructure owner must describe

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (a) the measures to be taken to ensure the continued delivery, during an emergency, of leadership and services necessary for the effective functioning of the regulated entity, and

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (b) any prescribed matter.

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (3) A business continuity plan of a critical infrastructure owner must describe all of the following:

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (a) the essential systems, networks, facilities or assets, or parts of any of these that must continue to function effectively during an emergency, including

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (i)  the level at which services must be provided by the essential systems, networks, facilities or assets, or parts of these,

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (ii)  the measures to be taken to ensure the continued provision of the services, and

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (iii)  if the services are interrupted or discontinued, the targeted period for restoring them to the level referred to in subparagraph (i);

heading: Business continuity plans
paragraph: (b) any prescribed matter.

heading: Consultation and coordination with local authorities
paragraph:
54
		  A regulated entity that is required to prepare or review and revise a risk assessment or an emergency management plan must make reasonable efforts to do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation and coordination with local authorities
paragraph: (a) consult and coordinate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the following:

heading: Consultation and coordination with local authorities
paragraph: (i)  a local authority in a prescribed class of local authorities;

heading: Consultation and coordination with local authorities
paragraph: (ii)  a person in a prescribed class of persons;

heading: Consultation and coordination with local authorities
paragraph: (iii)  without limiting subparagraph (i), in the case of a regulated entity that is a local authority, each local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, having jurisdiction over an area that is adjacent to an area within the jurisdiction of the regulated entity;

heading: Consultation and coordination with local authorities
paragraph: (b) consider any comments received from the persons with whom the regulated entity consulted in accordance with paragraph (a);

heading: Consultation and coordination with local authorities
paragraph: (c) in the case of an emergency management plan, coordinate the plan with the emergency management plans, if any, of the persons with whom the regulated entity consulted in accordance with paragraph (a) to ensure that the plans can be implemented, and emergency measures taken under them, in an integrated manner.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A lead minister, local authority, public sector agency or critical infrastructure owner that is required to prepare or review and revise a risk assessment or an emergency management plan must do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) consult and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the following:

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  each Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of Indigenous peoples whose traditional territory or treaty area includes

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (A) an area or people in an area that may be affected by a hazard that is required to be included in the risk assessment, or

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (B) an area to which the emergency management plan applies;

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  without limiting subparagraph (i), in the case of a local authority,

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (A) each Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of Indigenous peoples whose traditional territory or treaty area includes an area that is within the jurisdiction of the local authority, and

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (B) the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation if the Nisga'a Lands or the treaty lands of the treaty first nation, as applicable, are adjacent to an area within the jurisdiction of the local authority;

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) consider

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation, a treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a), and

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  the rights of the Indigenous peoples on whose behalf the Nisga'a Nation, treaty first nation or Indigenous governing body referred to in subparagraph (i) acts;

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (c) incorporate into the risk assessment or emergency management plan Indigenous knowledge, if available;

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (d) in the case of an emergency management plan, coordinate the plan with the plans, if any, of the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a) to ensure that the plans can be implemented, and emergency measures taken under them, in an integrated manner;

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (e) in the case of an emergency management plan prepared by a local authority, make reasonable efforts to reach agreement respecting areas to be described in the plan for the purposes of section 120 [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples] with each Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of Indigenous peoples whose traditional territory or treaty area includes an area that is within the jurisdiction of the local authority.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (2) If a local authority enters into an agreement with an Indigenous governing body under subsection (1) (e), the local authority must provide to the provincial administrator a description of each area agreed to and the Indigenous governing body that is specified in the agreement in relation to each area.

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph:
56
		  (1) The minister may make an order under this section if the minister is satisfied that, based on one or more risk assessments, the order is necessary for any of the following purposes:

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (a) to mitigate a specific hazard that presents a significant risk of giving rise to an emergency;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (b) to prepare for a specific type of hazard that presents a significant risk of becoming an emergency;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (c) to support a specific initiative in relation to the mitigation and preparation phases.

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by order, require a regulated entity, other than a government minister, the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, to provide to the provincial administrator or a lead minister one or more of the following:

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (a) information respecting particular infrastructure, facilities, equipment and related components, including maps showing the location of any of these;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (b) with respect to a hazard,

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (i)  a description of how the hazard may affect the regulated entity or persons, places and things for which the regulated entity has responsibility,

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (ii)  a statement of whether the regulated entity has undertaken studies or surveys of the hazard and, if so, copies of the results and any reports related to the studies or surveys, and

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (iii)  a description of the potential consequences for persons or property, or for objects or sites of heritage value, if an emergency occurs;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (c) if an event or circumstance referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition of "emergency" in section 1 (1) [definitions] has occurred, a description of
