heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (i)  the event or circumstance and its location and cause, and

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (ii)  the consequences for, or the likely consequences for, the regulated entity and other persons or property, or for objects or sites of heritage value;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (d) any prescribed information;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (e) any information requested by the provincial administrator or lead minister.

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (3) The minister may, by order, require a regulated entity, other than a government minister, the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, to do one or more of the following:

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (a) make changes to a risk assessment, emergency management plan or business continuity plan according to the directions of the minister, the provincial administrator or a lead minister;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (b) take particular emergency measures for the purposes of the mitigation or preparation phases;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (c) support or participate in specific emergency management training and exercise programs, including emergency planning sessions or programs relating to cultural safety or intersectional disadvantage;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (d) obtain or upgrade infrastructure, facilities, equipment and related components, whether physical or virtual;

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (e) take a prescribed type of action.

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (4) Before making an order under subsection (3) (b) or (d), the minister must

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (a) consult and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with each Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of Indigenous peoples whose traditional territory or treaty area includes an area or people in an area that will be affected by the order, and

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (b) consider

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (i)  any comments received from an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a), and

heading: Directed mitigation and preparation measures
paragraph: (ii)  the rights of the Indigenous peoples referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph:
57
		  (1) This section applies despite any other provision of this Part or a regulation made in relation to this Part.

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (2) The minister may make an order under this section if the minister is satisfied that

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (a) complying with a requirement of this Part or a regulation made in relation to this Part would cause a regulated entity undue hardship, or

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (b) a regulated entity is subject to, and is complying with, an enactment of British Columbia or Canada that imposes a requirement with respect to emergency management, and the requirement is equivalent to, or achieves the same objectives as, a requirement of this Part or a regulation made in relation to this Part.

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (3) The minister may, by order, do any of the following:

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (a) waive or modify a requirement under this Part, other than section 55, or a regulation made in relation to this Part;

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (b) impose limits and conditions on a waiver or modification;

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (c) substitute a different requirement for one that is waived.

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (4) The minister may, for the purpose of making an order under this section, or varying or determining compliance with an order made under this section, do any of the following:

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (a) collect and use information provided by the regulator of a regulated entity;

heading: Exceptions to requirements
paragraph: (b) request a regulated entity to provide information, records or proof of a matter to the minister, the provincial administrator or a lead minister.

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph:
58
		  (1) The minister may, by order, require a person who is not a regulated entity to provide to the provincial administrator or a lead minister any of the information referred to in section 56 (2)

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (a) if the minister has reason to believe that any of the circumstances referred to in subsection (3) of this section apply, or

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of determining whether a system, network, facility or asset, or a class of any of these, should be prescribed as critical infrastructure.

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (2) If the minister has reason to believe that any of the circumstances referred to in subsection (3) apply, the minister may, by order, require a person who is not a regulated entity to do one or more of the following:

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (a) prepare and maintain a risk assessment;

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (b) prepare, maintain and implement an emergency management plan;

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (c) prepare and maintain a business continuity plan.

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (3) The circumstances for the purposes of subsections (1) (a) and (2) are as follows:

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (a) the person engages in an activity that is or may create a hazard;

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (b) the person uses a process or property in a manner that is or may create a hazard;

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (c) a condition that is or may create a hazard exists or may exist on land that the person owns or occupies;

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (d) the person provides or may be able to provide emergency resources or the use of land.

heading: Imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities
paragraph: (4) If the minister makes an order under this section, the minister may include in the order a requirement that a person comply with one or more provisions, with or without modifications, of this Part or a regulation made in relation to this Part, as if the person were a regulated entity.

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph:
59
		  (1) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the minister is satisfied that an emergency is present, the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the minister, as applicable, may, by order, make a declaration of a state of provincial emergency relating to all or part of British Columbia.

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (2) A declaration must identify the nature of the emergency and the area to which the declaration applies.

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (3) The minister may make a declaration orally or in writing.

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (4) As soon as reasonably practicable after a declaration is made, the minister must,

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (a) in the case of a declaration made orally, reduce the declaration to writing and publish the declaration, and

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (b) in the case of a declaration made in writing, publish the declaration.

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (5) For certainty, a declaration of a state of provincial emergency does not affect the authority of any person to declare, continue or extend

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (a) a state of local emergency or a local recovery period under Part 6, except to the extent that the minister has cancelled a declaration of a state of local emergency or a declaration of a local recovery period, or

heading: Declaration of state of provincial emergency
paragraph: (b) an order made under another enactment with respect to an emergency within the meaning of that enactment.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph:
60
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, do one or both of the following:

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) amend an order that makes a declaration of a state of provincial emergency with respect to the nature of the emergency or the area to which the declaration applies, or both;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) extend the period for which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies for additional periods of not more than 28 days each.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) (a) to amend an order that makes a declaration does not extend or otherwise affect the period for which the declaration applies.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (3) An order made under subsection (1) to amend an order that makes a declaration or to extend the period for which a declaration applies must

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) identify the order number and date of the original declaration and of each previous amendment or extension, if any, and

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) in the case of an extension of the period for which the declaration applies, specify the period of the extension.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (4) As soon as reasonably practicable after an order is made under this section, the minister must publish the order.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph:
61
		  (1) Unless extended under section 60 (1) (b), a declaration of a state of provincial emergency expires

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (a) 28 days after being made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, or

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (b) 14 days after being made by the minister.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (2) If, in the opinion of the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the minister, as applicable, the emergency to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency relates is no longer present in an area,

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (a) the Lieutenant Governor in Council

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (i)  must, by order, cancel the declaration with respect to the area if the Lieutenant Governor in Council made the declaration, and

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (ii)  may, by order, cancel the declaration with respect to the area if the minister made the declaration, and

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (b) the minister must, by order, cancel the declaration with respect to the area if the minister made the declaration and the declaration was not cancelled under paragraph (a) (ii).

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (3) If a declaration of a provincial recovery period is made with respect to an area in relation to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies, the declaration of a state of provincial emergency is cancelled with respect to that area.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (4) As soon as reasonably practicable after a declaration of a state of provincial emergency expires or is cancelled, the minister must publish the details of the expiry or cancellation.

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph:
62
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, make a declaration of a provincial recovery period if the Lieutenant Governor in Council is satisfied of both of the following:

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (a) that the nature or scope of the emergency that is the subject of a declaration of a state of provincial emergency has subsided sufficiently in an area that it is appropriate to transition the taking of emergency measures in that area from the response phase to the recovery phase;

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (b) that the exercise in that area of one or more recovery powers is necessary for the area to recover from the emergency.

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (2) A declaration of a provincial recovery period may specify that any of the following continue to have effect during the provincial recovery period if the Lieutenant Governor in Council is satisfied that a continuation is necessary to recover from the emergency referred to in subsection (1):

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (a) an order made under

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (i)  section 75 [essential matters], other than section 75 (1) (d),

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (ii)  section 76 [land and other property], or

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (iii)  section 78 [general restrictions];

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (b) a regulation made under

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (i)  section 83 [modifying enactments and authorizations],

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (ii)  section 84 [modifying time periods], or

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (iii)  section 86 [enforcement of modified enactments and authorizations].

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (3) A declaration of a provincial recovery period must specify all of the following:

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (a) the order number and date of the original declaration of a state of provincial emergency and of each amendment and extension, if any;

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (b) the period for which the declaration of a provincial recovery period applies if that period is less than 90 days;

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (c) the area to which the declaration of a provincial recovery period applies;

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (d) the orders and regulations referred to in subsection (2) that continue to have effect, if any, during all or part of the provincial recovery period.

heading: Declaration of provincial recovery period
paragraph: (4) As soon as reasonably practicable after a declaration of a provincial recovery period is made, the minister must publish the declaration.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph:
63
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, do one or both of the following:

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) amend an order that makes a declaration of a provincial recovery period with respect to the area to which the declaration applies;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) extend the period for which a declaration of a provincial recovery period applies for additional periods of not more than 90 days each.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) to amend an order that makes a declaration or to extend the period for which a declaration applies must specify all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) the order number and date of the original declaration of a provincial recovery period and of each previous amendment or extension, if any;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) in the case of an extension of the period for which the declaration applies, the period of the extension;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (c) the matters referred to in section 62 (3) (c) and (d) that apply in relation to the declaration as amended or extended.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (3) Section 60 (2) and (4) [amendment or extension of declaration] applies to an order made under this section.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph:
64
		  (1) Unless extended under section 63 (1) (b), a declaration of a provincial recovery period expires 90 days after being made or at the end of the period specified in the declaration, whichever is earlier.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must, by order, cancel a declaration of a provincial recovery period with respect to any area

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (a) in which, in the Lieutenant Governor in Council's opinion, the exercise of recovery powers is no longer necessary for the area to recover from the emergency to which the declaration relates, or

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (b) in relation to which a new declaration of a state of provincial emergency has been made in response to an emergency that is related to the original emergency to which the declaration of a provincial recovery period relates.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (3) A cancellation under subsection (2) (b) must be made as soon as reasonably practicable after the new declaration of a state of provincial emergency is made.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (4) As soon as reasonably practicable after a declaration of a provincial recovery period expires or is cancelled, the minister must publish the details of the expiry or cancellation.

heading: When general powers and duties apply
paragraph:
65
		  A person may exercise a power and must perform a duty under this Division whether or not a declaration of a state of provincial emergency or a declaration of a state of local emergency has been made.

heading: Minister must consider comprehensive emergency management plan
paragraph:
66
		  Before taking any action for the purpose of responding to or recovering from an emergency, the minister must consider the comprehensive emergency management plan and any applicable emergency management plans prepared by the provincial administrator.

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph:
67
		  (1) For the purpose of responding to or recovering from an emergency, the minister and the provincial administrator

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (a) must coordinate the actions of the government or, if another person is responsible for coordinating particular actions of the government, may assist the other person in coordinating the actions of the government,

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (b) may give advice and assistance to any person, and

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (c) may request a lead minister to coordinate the taking of emergency measures by prescribed public sector agencies or critical infrastructure owners, or public sector agencies or critical infrastructure owners in a prescribed class.

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1) (a), the minister or the provincial administrator may give directions to one or more of the following:

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (a) members of the provincial emergency management organization;

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (b) government employees and persons who provide services to government under an agreement;

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (c) public sector agencies that have emergency management plans.

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1) (c), a lead minister may give directions to a prescribed public sector agency or critical infrastructure owner, or a public sector agency or critical infrastructure owner in a prescribed class.

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph:
68
		  (1) The minister may make an order under this section if the minister is satisfied that an order is necessary to respond to or recover from an emergency.

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by order, require any of the following to take one or more actions referred to in subsection (3):

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (a) a regulated entity other than a government minister, the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation;

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (b) a person required to take an action under section 58 [imposing duties on persons who are not regulated entities].

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (3) The actions that may be the subject of an order are as follows:

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (a) providing to the provincial administrator or a lead minister any of the information referred to in section 56 (2) [directed mitigation and preparation measures];

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (b) consulting and coordinating with a person with respect to assessing an emergency and the emergency measures to be taken;

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (c) taking one or more emergency measures;

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (d) providing emergency resources or the use of land, including with respect to individuals and animals evacuated from another jurisdiction and personal property removed from another jurisdiction;

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (e) complying with the directions of the provincial administrator or a lead minister with respect to any matters referred to in paragraphs (a) to (d).

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (4) The minister may request a government minister, the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation to do one or more of the things described in subsection (3).

heading: Requiring actions
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this section affects the authority of any person to take, or continue to take, emergency measures set out in the person's emergency management plan.

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph:
69
		  (1) In this section, "specified authority" means the following:

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (a) a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation;

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (b) a participating authority.

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (2) The minister may make an order or request under this section if the minister is satisfied that a person who is authorized under this Act to exercise response or recovery powers is unable to adequately respond to or recover from an emergency.

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (3) The minister may, by order, require a specified authority to take an action referred to in subsection (5)

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (a) in an area within another person's jurisdiction, or

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (b) in relation to an emergency in an area within another person's jurisdiction, as follows:

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (i)  in the case of a local authority, in an area within the local authority's jurisdiction;

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a participating authority, in an area that is subject to the participating authority's emergency measures agreement.

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (4) The minister may request the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation to take an action referred to in subsection (5)

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (a) in an area within another person's jurisdiction, or

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (b) in relation to an emergency in an area within another person's jurisdiction, in an area within the Nisga'a Nation's or treaty first nation's jurisdiction.

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (5) The actions that may be the subject of an order or request under this section are as follows:

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (a) taking one or more emergency measures;

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (b) providing emergency resources or the use of land;

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (c) complying with the directions of the provincial administrator or a lead minister with respect to a matter referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (6) If the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation does not intend to comply with a request made under subsection (4), the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation must inform the minister in writing of the reasons for not complying with the request.

heading: Requirement to support others
paragraph: (7) The minister may not make an order under subsection (3) in relation to an area within the specified land of an Indigenous people, unless an Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of the Indigenous people consents to the order.

heading: Regulated entity must consider emergency management plan
paragraph:
70
		  Before taking any action for the purpose of responding to or recovering from an emergency, a regulated entity, other than a critical infrastructure owner or local authority, that is required to prepare an emergency management plan must consider the emergency management plan.

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph:
71
		  (1) The minister may make an order under this Division during the period for which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies.

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) Before making an order under this Division, the minister must be satisfied that any prohibitions, requirements, limits or conditions imposed, or authorizations made, under the order are necessary to respond to the emergency.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph:
72
		  (1) The minister may make an order under this Division orally or in writing.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) The minister may provide in an order made under this Division that the order applies

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) to all or part of the area to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies,

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) to an area to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency does not apply,

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) for all or part of the period for which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies, and

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (d) to a person or thing, or a class of persons or things, as established by the minister.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) (b) does not apply to an order made under 77 (1) [evacuations and removals].

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (4) The minister must identify in the order the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the order relates.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (5) As soon as reasonably practicable after the minister makes an order under this Division, the minister must

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) in the case of an order made orally, reduce the order to writing and publish the order, and

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) in the case of an order made in writing, publish the order.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (6) An order made under this Division ceases to have effect on the earliest of the following dates:

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) the date provided for in the order;

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) the date on which the minister rescinds the order;

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) the date on which the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the order relates expires or is cancelled, unless the order is identified under section 62 (2) (a) [declaration of provincial recovery period] as an order that continues to have effect.

heading: General power to do all things necessary
paragraph:
73
		  (1) The minister may, by order, do all acts and implement all procedures that the minister is satisfied are necessary to respond to an emergency.

heading: General power to do all things necessary
paragraph: (2) For certainty, nothing in this Division is intended to limit the power conferred under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Emergency information and measures
paragraph:
74
		  (1) If the minister is satisfied that a person possesses or controls information needed by another person to exercise a power or perform a duty under this Act, the minister may, by order, require the person to give the information to

heading: Emergency information and measures
paragraph: (a) the other person, or

heading: Emergency information and measures
paragraph: (b) the provincial administrator or a lead minister.

heading: Emergency information and measures
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by order, require a person to do one or both of the following:

heading: Emergency information and measures
paragraph: (a) take one or more emergency measures;

heading: Emergency information and measures
paragraph: (b) comply with the directions of the provincial administrator, a lead minister or a person in a specified class of persons, with respect to the taking of emergency measures.

heading: Essential matters
paragraph:
75
		  (1) The minister may, by order, do one or more of the following:

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (a) identify supplies, equipment or other items, services, property or facilities, or a class of any of these, as essential;

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (b) for things identified under paragraph (a) as essential,

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (i)  establish or restrain increases in prices or rents for them,

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (ii)  ration or otherwise provide for their distribution or use,

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (iii)  provide for their restoration, and

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (iv)  prohibit or limit seizures of them or evictions from them;

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (c) authorize a person to provide a service or give assistance of a type that the person is qualified to provide or give;

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (d) require a person to provide a service or give assistance of a type that the person is qualified to provide or give;

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (e) provide for, maintain and coordinate the provision and maintenance of necessities.

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (b) (i) and (iv) applies despite any enactment governing tenancies or the recovery of property.

heading: Essential matters
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) (c) and (d) applies despite any contract, including a collective agreement.

heading: Land and other property
paragraph:
76
		  (1) The minister may, by order, do one or more of the following:

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (a) appropriate, use or control the use of any personal property;

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (b) use or control the use of any land;

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (c) authorize the entry without warrant into any structure or onto any land by any person for the purpose of taking emergency measures;

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (d) prohibit the entry into any structure or onto any land by any person;

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (e) authorize or require the alteration, removal or demolition of any trees, crops, structures or landscapes;

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (f) authorize or require the construction, alteration, removal or demolition of works;

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (g) require the owner of a structure to

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (i)  have any damage to the structure assessed, and

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (ii)  give the results of the assessment to the minister or a person in a class of persons specified by the minister.

heading: Land and other property
paragraph: (2) The power under subsection (1) (b) to use or control the use of land does not apply to specified land.

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph:
77
		  (1) The minister may, by order, do one or more of the following in relation to any area to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies:

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (a) require a person to evacuate from the area;

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (b) authorize the evacuation of individuals or animals, or both, from the area;

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (c) authorize the removal of personal property from the area.

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (2) If the minister makes an order under subsection (1), the minister may arrange for

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (a) the adequate care and protection of evacuated individuals or animals, or both, and

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (b) the adequate protection of personal property that has been removed.

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (3) Unless the minister directs otherwise, the provincial administrator may do all the things that the minister may do as described under this section with respect to any area that is not within the jurisdiction of a local authority.

heading: Evacuations and removals
paragraph: (4) Sections 71 and 72 [when and how response powers may be exercised] apply to an exercise of power under subsection (3) of this section as if the provincial administrator were the minister.

heading: General restrictions
paragraph:
78
		  (1) The minister may, by order, control or prohibit one or more of the following:

heading: General restrictions
paragraph: (a) travel to or from any area;

heading: General restrictions
paragraph: (b) the carrying on of a business or a type of business;

heading: General restrictions
paragraph: (c) an event or a type of event.

heading: General restrictions
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by order, do one or more of the following:

heading: General restrictions
paragraph: (a) require a person to stop doing an activity, including an activity that a person is licensed, permitted or otherwise authorized to do under an enactment;

heading: General restrictions
paragraph: (b) put limits or conditions on doing an activity, including limits or conditions that have the effect of modifying a licence, permit or other authorization issued under an enactment.

heading: Control of emergency fire services
paragraph:
79
		  (1) The minister responsible for the administration of section 4 (1) (b) [powers and duties of fire commissioner] of the Fire Safety Act may, by order,

heading: Control of emergency fire services
paragraph: (a) assume control over one or more fire fighting and fire prevention services in British Columbia, and

heading: Control of emergency fire services
paragraph: (b) designate the fire commissioner under that Act to exercise authority over those services.

heading: Control of emergency fire services
paragraph: (2) Sections 71 and 72 [when and how response powers may be exercised] apply to an exercise of power under subsection (1) of this section as if the minister referred to in subsection (1) were the minister responsible for the administration of this Act.

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: 80		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation under this Division during the period for which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies.

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) Before making a regulation under this Division, the Lieutenant Governor in Council must be satisfied that

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) the regulation is necessary to respond to the emergency, and

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) in the case of a regulation that has the effect of modifying an enactment, the benefit of making the regulation is greater than the benefit of the continued application of the enactment without the modification.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph:
81
		  (1) Without limiting section 41 of the Interpretation Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide in a regulation made under this Division that the regulation applies

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) to all or part of the area to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies,

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) to an area to which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency does not apply,

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) for all or part of the period for which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency applies, and

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (d) to a person or thing, or a class of persons or things, as established by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must identify in the regulation the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the regulation relates.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under this Division ceases to have effect on the earliest of the following dates:

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) the date provided for in the regulation;

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) the date on which the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the regulation relates expires or is cancelled, unless the regulation is identified under section 62 (2) (b) [declaration of provincial recovery period] as a regulation that continues to have effect.

heading: Retroactive application of response powers
paragraph: 82		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation under this Division retroactive to a specified date.

heading: Retroactive application of response powers
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may not do either of the following:

heading: Retroactive application of response powers
paragraph: (a) make a regulation under section 86 [enforcement of modified enactments and authorizations] that is retroactive;

heading: Retroactive application of response powers
paragraph: (b) make a regulation retroactive to a date that is earlier than the date on which the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the regulation relates was made.

heading: Retroactive application of response powers
paragraph: (3) A regulation made retroactive under subsection (1) is deemed to have come into force on the specified date.

heading: Modifying enactments and authorizations
paragraph:
83
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, do one or more of the following:

heading: Modifying enactments and authorizations
paragraph: (a) make an exemption from one or more requirements under an enactment;

heading: Modifying enactments and authorizations
paragraph: (b) modify a requirement set under an enactment;

heading: Modifying enactments and authorizations
paragraph: (c) establish limits on the application of an enactment;

heading: Modifying enactments and authorizations
paragraph: (d) establish powers or duties that apply in place of or in addition to an enactment;

heading: Modifying enactments and authorizations
paragraph: (e) establish terms and conditions in relation to anything done under paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d);

heading: Modifying enactments and authorizations
paragraph: (f) authorize issuers of licences, permits or other authorizations issued under enactments to modify, add or remove limits or conditions, or the term, of the licences, permits or other authorizations.

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph:
84
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: "statutory power of decision" has the same meaning as in section 33 [definitions for Part 3];

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: "time period" means the following:

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (a) a limitation period established under an enactment;

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (b) a period of time, established under an enactment, within which

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (i)  a proceeding must be commenced or a process must be begun, or

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (ii)  a step must be taken in a proceeding or process.

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, do one or more of the following:

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (a) suspend the running of a time period;

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (b) extend a time period;

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (c) replace a time period with a different time period;

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (d) authorize a person, tribunal or other body that, under an enactment, has a statutory power of decision to waive, suspend the running of or extend a mandatory time period relating to the exercise of that power.

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (3) A time period must not be shortened by

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (a) a regulation made under this section, or

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (b) a person, tribunal or other body acting under the authority referred to in subsection (2) (d).

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (4) A time period extended or replaced under this section may extend beyond the date on which the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the regulation relates expires or is cancelled.

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (5) If the running of a time period is suspended by a regulation made under this section or by a person, tribunal or other body acting under the authority referred to in subsection (2) (d), and the regulation, person, tribunal or body does not extend or replace the suspended time period,

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (a) the time period resumes running on the date of the expiry or cancellation of the following, whichever is later:

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (i)  the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the regulation relates;

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (ii)  the declaration of a provincial recovery period that followed the declaration of a state of provincial emergency, if any, and

heading: Modifying time periods
paragraph: (b) the period of the suspension is not to be counted for the purposes of calculating the time period.

heading: Modifying fee requirements
paragraph:
85
		  (1) If a regulation made under this Division suspends a requirement to pay a fee and does not provide for the payment of a replacement fee, no fee is payable at any time with respect to things done during the period of the suspension.

heading: Modifying fee requirements
paragraph: (2) A regulation made under this Division must not increase the amount of a fee.

heading: Enforcement of modified enactments and authorizations
paragraph:
86
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, specify that a failure to comply with a provision of a regulation made under this Division is to be treated as though it were a failure to comply with the enactment to which that provision relates.

heading: When recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph:
87
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation under this Division during the period for which a declaration of a provincial recovery period applies.

heading: When recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) Before making a regulation under this Division, the Lieutenant Governor in Council must be satisfied that any prohibitions, requirements, limits or conditions imposed, or authorizations made, under the regulation are necessary to recover from the emergency.

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph:
88
		  (1) Without limiting section 41 of the Interpretation Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide in a regulation made under this Division that the regulation applies

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) to all or part of the area of British Columbia to which a declaration of a provincial recovery period applies,

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) to an area of British Columbia to which a declaration of a provincial recovery period does not apply,

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) for all or part of the period for which a declaration of a provincial recovery period applies, and

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (d) to a person or thing, or a class of persons or things, as established by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must identify in the regulation the declaration of a provincial recovery period to which the regulation relates.

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under this Division, and a regulation or order continued under section 62 (2) (a) or (b) [declaration of provincial recovery period], ceases to have effect on the earliest of the following dates:

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) the date provided for

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (i)  in the declaration of a provincial recovery period, in the case of a regulation or order identified under section 62 (2) (a) or (b), or

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (ii)  in the regulation or order, in any case;

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) the date on which the declaration of a provincial recovery period to which the regulation or order relates expires or is cancelled.

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: 89		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, do all the things that the minister may do as described under the following provisions:

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (a) section 75 [essential matters], other than section 75 (1) (d);

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (b) section 76 [land and other property];

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (c) section 78 [general restrictions].

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1) (b), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, prohibit the entry into any structure or onto any land, by any person and for any purpose related to

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (a) protecting the health, safety or well-being of persons, or the safety of property or of objects or sites of heritage value, or

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (b) taking emergency measures to recover from the emergency.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph:
90
		  (1) In this section, "specified action" means an action described in subsection (2) (a) in relation to a provision referred to in subsection (6) (a), (b) or (c) of this section.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (2) This section applies if

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) the minister is intending to do any of the following in relation to a provision set out in subsection (6) of this section, as applicable:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  make an order;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  recommend that the Lieutenant Governor in Council make a regulation;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iii)  take any other action, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) the order, regulation or other action will affect an area, or the people in an area, that is

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  within Nisga'a Lands or treaty lands of a treaty first nation, or

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  described for the purposes of this section in one or more of the following:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (A) an emergency management plan referred to in section 39 (1) (b) [emergency management planning and information];

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (B) an agreement made under this Act with an Indigenous governing body.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (5), the minister must, before taking an action described in subsection (2) (a) and (b), do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) in the case of an action that will affect an area, or the people in an area, that is referred to in subsection (2) (b) (ii), consult and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the Indigenous governing body that is specified in the emergency management plan or agreement, as applicable, in relation to the area;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) give notice to the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation, or an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a), as applicable, of the details of the intended action and, if applicable, of any arrangements the minister intends to make under section 77 (2) [evacuations and removals] with respect to evacuated individuals;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (c) consider

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a), and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  the rights of the Indigenous peoples on whose behalf the Nisga'a Nation, treaty first nation or Indigenous governing body referred to in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph acts.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (4) The minister must not take an action described in subsection (2) (a) that will affect an area, or the people in an area, that is referred to in subsection (2) (b) (i) unless the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation, as applicable, consents to the action being taken.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (5) If, in the opinion of the minister, it would not be practicable to comply with subsection (3) (a), (b) or (c), or to seek to obtain consent under subsection (4), in relation to a specified action due to an imminent risk of loss of life or risk of injury to individuals or animals, or risk of significant loss or damage to property,

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) the requirements of that provision do not apply, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) the minister must, as soon as reasonably practicable after taking the action, do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  in the case of subsection (3) (a), engage and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the Indigenous governing body referred to in that subsection;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of subsection (3) (b), give to the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation, or an Indigenous governing body engaged in accordance with subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, as applicable, notice of the details of the action taken and, if applicable, of any arrangements the minister made or intends to make under section 77 (2) with respect to evacuated individuals;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iii)  in the case of subsection (3) (c), consider

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (A) any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body engaged in accordance with subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (B) the rights of the Indigenous peoples on whose behalf the Nisga'a Nation, treaty first nation or Indigenous governing body referred to in clause (A) acts.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of subsection (2) (a), the following provisions are set out:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) section 76 (1) (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f) [land and other property];

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) section 77 (1) or (2);

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (c) section 78 (1) (a) [general restrictions];

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (d) section 89 (1) (b) and (c) [recovery powers], to the extent that provision authorizes the Lieutenant Governor in Council to do things the minister may do under a provision referred to in paragraph (a) or (c) of this subsection;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (e) section 89 (2).

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (7) This section applies to the provincial administrator in relation to an exercise of power under section 77 (3) as if the provincial administrator were the minister.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
91
		  In this Division, "business day" means a day other than a Saturday or a holiday.

heading: Report on exercise of response or recovery powers
paragraph:
92
		  (1) The minister must, within 5 business days from the date on which a response power or a recovery power is exercised by the minister or the Lieutenant Governor in Council, do both of the following:

heading: Report on exercise of response or recovery powers
paragraph: (a) submit a report to the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly on the exercise of the power;

heading: Report on exercise of response or recovery powers
paragraph: (b) include with the report a copy of the relevant regulation or order.

heading: Report on exercise of response or recovery powers
paragraph: (2) If the minister, under section 90 (5) [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples], was of the opinion that it was not practicable to comply with subsection (3) (a), (b) or (c) of that section, or to seek to obtain consent under subsection (4) of that section, the report under subsection (1) of this section must include the reasons for the minister's opinion.

heading: Final report
paragraph:
93
		  (1) The provincial administrator must prepare a report with respect to a declaration of a state of provincial emergency and, if applicable, with respect to a declaration of a provincial recovery period, that summarizes all of the following:

heading: Final report
paragraph: (a) the nature of the emergency;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (b) the response powers and recovery powers exercised with respect to the emergency;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (c) any other matter as required by the minister and the regulations.

heading: Final report
paragraph: (2) The provincial administrator must provide the report to the minister within 120 days of the expiry or cancellation of the following, whichever is later:

heading: Final report
paragraph: (a) the declaration of a state of provincial emergency to which the report relates;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (b) the declaration of a provincial recovery period that followed the declaration of a state of provincial emergency, if any.

heading: Final report
paragraph: (3) The minister must, within 5 business days of receiving the report, submit a copy of the report to the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.

heading: Report to Legislative Assembly
paragraph:
94
		  (1) If there is no Speaker of the Legislative Assembly,

heading: Report to Legislative Assembly
paragraph: (a) the minister must submit a report made under this Division to the Clerk of the Legislative Assembly, and

heading: Report to Legislative Assembly
paragraph: (b) the Clerk must provide the report to the Speaker as soon as possible after the Speaker's election.

heading: Report to Legislative Assembly
paragraph: (2) The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly must, on receiving a report under this Division, table the report in the Legislative Assembly as soon as possible.

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph:
95
		  (1) A declaration of a state of local emergency relating to all or part of the area within a local authority's jurisdiction may be made, by emergency instrument, by the following:

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (a) the local authority, if the local authority is satisfied that an emergency is present;

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (b) the head of the local authority, if the head

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (i)  is satisfied that an emergency is present, and

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (ii)  has used reasonable efforts to obtain the consent, to the declaration, of the other governing members of the local authority.

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (2) A declaration of a state of local emergency must identify the nature of the emergency and the area to which the declaration applies.

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (3) As soon as reasonably practicable after a declaration is made under this section, the local authority must

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (a) give a copy of the declaration to the minister, and

heading: Declaration of state of local emergency
paragraph: (b) publish the declaration.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph:
96
		  (1) Subject to this section, a local authority may, by emergency instrument, do one or both of the following:

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) amend an emergency instrument that makes a declaration of a state of local emergency with respect to the nature of the emergency or the area to which the declaration relates, or both;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) extend the period for which a declaration of a state of local emergency applies for additional periods of not more than 14 days each.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (2) A local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, must not make an emergency instrument under subsection (1) unless, before the instrument is made,

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) in the case of a proposed extension, the local authority gives notice to the minister of the types of response powers the local authority proposes to exercise during the proposed extension,

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) the local authority gives to the minister a summary of any consultation or engagement undertaken in accordance with section 120 (3) or (5) [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples], as applicable, in relation to an action referred to in that section, which action is in respect of the declaration of a state of local emergency referred to in subsection (1) of this section, including any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation, a treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body, as applicable, and

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (c) the minister approves, in writing, the proposed amendment or extension.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (3) The head of a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, must not make an emergency instrument under subsection (1) unless the head of the local authority, before making the emergency instrument, makes reasonable efforts to obtain the consent of the other governing members of the local authority.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (4) An emergency instrument made under subsection (1) (a) to amend an emergency instrument that makes a declaration of a state of local emergency does not extend or otherwise affect the period for which the declaration applies.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (5) An emergency instrument made under subsection (1) to amend an emergency instrument that makes a declaration or to extend the period for which a declaration applies must

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) specify the date of the original declaration and of each previous amendment or extension, if any, and

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) in the case of an extension of the period for which the declaration applies, specify the period of the extension.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (6) As soon as reasonably practicable after an emergency instrument is made under this section, the local authority must

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) give notice to the minister, and

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) publish the amendment or extension.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph:
97
		  (1) Unless extended under section 96, a declaration of a state of local emergency expires 14 days after being made.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (2) If, in the opinion of the local authority, the emergency to which a declaration of a state of local emergency relates is no longer present in an area, the local authority must, by emergency instrument, cancel the declaration with respect to the area.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (3) The minister may, by order, cancel at any time a declaration of a state of local emergency made by a local authority, or the head of a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (4) A declaration of a state of local emergency is cancelled with respect to any area to which a declaration of a local recovery period, made in relation to the declaration of a state of local emergency, applies.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (5) As soon as reasonably practicable after a declaration of a state of local emergency expires or is cancelled, the local authority must

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (a) give notice to the minister, and

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (b) publish the expiry or cancellation.

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph:
98
		  (1) Subject to this section, a local authority may, by emergency instrument, make a declaration of a local recovery period.

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (2) A local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, must not make a declaration under subsection (1) unless, before the declaration is made,

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (a) the local authority gives to the minister

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (i)  notice of

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (A) the types of recovery powers the local authority proposes to exercise during the local recovery period, and

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (B) the emergency instruments referred to in subsection (4), if any, the local authority proposes would continue to have effect during all or part of the local recovery period, and

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (ii)  a summary of any consultation or engagement undertaken in accordance with section 120 (3) or (5) [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples], as applicable, in relation to an action referred to in that section, which action is in respect of the original declaration of a state of local emergency, including any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation, a treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body, as applicable, and

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (b) the minister approves, in writing, all of the following:

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (i)  the area to which the declaration applies;

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (ii)  the emergency instruments referred to in subsection (4) that continue to have effect, if any, during all or part of the local recovery period.

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (3) The minister may give the approval referred to in subsection (2) (b) (i) if the minister is satisfied of both of the following:

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (a) that the nature or scope of the emergency that is the subject of the declaration of a state of local emergency has subsided sufficiently in an area that it is appropriate to transition the taking of emergency measures in that area from the response phase to the recovery phase;

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (b) that the exercise in that area of one or more recovery powers is necessary for the area to recover from the emergency.

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (2) (b) (ii), the minister may approve an emergency instrument made under any of the following provisions to continue to have effect during the local recovery period if the minister is satisfied that a continuation is necessary to recover from the emergency:

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (a) section 107 (1) (a) [response powers], to the extent that provision authorizes the local authority to do things the minister may do under section 75 (1) [essential matters], other than section 75 (1) (d);

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (b) section 107 (1) (b) and (d);

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (c) section 110 [response borrowing].

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (5) The minister may impose prohibitions, requirements, limits or conditions on giving an approval under subsection (2) (b).

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (6) A declaration of a local recovery period must specify all of the following:

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (a) the instrument number and date of the original declaration of a state of local emergency and of each amendment and extension, if any;

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (b) the period for which the declaration of a local recovery period applies if that period is less than 90 days;

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (c) the area to which the declaration of a local recovery period applies;

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (d) in the case of a declaration made by a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation,

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (i)  the emergency instruments referred to in subsections (4) and (8) that continue to have effect, if any, during all or part of the local recovery period, and

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (ii)  any prohibitions, requirements, limits or conditions imposed by the minister under subsection (5), if applicable.

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (7) If the minister approves a bylaw adopted under section 110 to continue to have effect during the local recovery period, money may be borrowed under the bylaw to pay expenses incurred in responding to or recovering from the emergency to which the declaration relates.

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (9) As soon as reasonably practicable after a declaration is made under subsection (1), the local authority must

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (a) give a copy of the declaration to the minister, and

heading: Declaration of local recovery period
paragraph: (b) publish the declaration.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph:
99
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a local authority may, by emergency instrument, do one or both of the following:

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) amend an emergency instrument that makes a declaration of a local recovery period with respect to the area to which the declaration applies or the recovery powers that may be exercised under the declaration, or both;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) extend the period for which a declaration of a local recovery period applies for additional periods of not more than 90 days each.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (2) A local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, must not make an emergency instrument under subsection (1) unless, before the instrument is made,

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) the local authority gives to the minister a summary of any consultation or engagement undertaken in accordance with section 120 (3) or (5) [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples], as applicable, in relation to an action referred to in that section, which action is in respect of the declaration of a local recovery period referred to in subsection (1) of this section, including any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation, a treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body, as applicable, and

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) the minister approves, in writing, the proposed amendment or extension.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (3) An emergency instrument made under subsection (1) (a) to amend an emergency instrument that makes a declaration does not extend or otherwise affect the period for which the declaration applies.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (4) An emergency instrument made under subsection (1) to amend an emergency instrument that makes a declaration or to extend the period for which a declaration applies must specify all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (a) the date of the original declaration of a local recovery period and of each previous amendment or extension, if any;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (b) in the case of an extension of the period for which the declaration applies, the period of the extension;

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (c) the matters referred to in section 98 (6) (c) and (d) [declaration of local recovery period], as applicable, that apply in relation to the declaration as amended or extended.

heading: Amendment or extension of declaration
paragraph: (5) Section 96 (6) [amendment or extension of declaration] applies in relation to an emergency instrument made under this section.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph:
100
		  (1) Unless extended under section 99, a declaration of a local recovery period expires 90 days after being made or at the end of the period specified in the declaration, whichever is earlier.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (2) A local authority must, by emergency instrument, cancel a declaration of a local recovery period with respect to any area

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (a) in which, in the local authority's opinion, the exercise of recovery powers is no longer necessary for the area to recover from the emergency to which the declaration relates, or

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (b) in relation to which a new declaration of a state of local emergency has been made in response to an emergency that is related to the original emergency to which the declaration of a local recovery period relates.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (3) A cancellation under subsection (2) (b) must be made as soon as reasonably practicable after the new declaration of a state of local emergency is made.

heading: Expiry or cancellation of declaration
paragraph: (4) Section 97 (3) and (5) [expiry or cancellation of declaration] applies in relation to a declaration of a local recovery period.

heading: When general powers and duties apply
paragraph:
101
		  (1) A local authority may exercise a power and must perform a duty under this Division whether or not a declaration of a state of provincial emergency or a declaration of a state of local emergency has been made.

heading: When general powers and duties apply
paragraph: (2) The minister may make an order under section 104 [restrictions on exercising powers] during the period for which a declaration of a state of local emergency or a declaration of a local recovery period applies.

heading: Local authority must consider emergency management plan
paragraph:
102
		  Before taking any action for the purpose of responding to or recovering from an emergency, the local authority must consider the local authority's emergency management plan.

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph:
103
		  For the purpose of responding to or recovering from an emergency in an area within a local authority's jurisdiction, the local authority

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (a) must coordinate actions in the area or, if another person is responsible for coordinating particular actions in the area, assist the other person in coordinating actions in that area,

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (b) may, for the purposes of paragraph (a), give directions to members of the local authority's emergency management organization, and

heading: Coordination of response and recovery efforts
paragraph: (c) may give advice and assistance to any person.

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph:
104
		  (1) Before making an order under this section, the minister must be satisfied that the order is necessary for one or both of the following purposes:

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (a) to coordinate the exercise of response powers or recovery powers;

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (b) to provide certainty to persons affected by the exercise of response powers or recovery powers.

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by order, do any of the following:

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (a) require a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, to refrain from or stop exercising one or more response powers or recovery powers;

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (b) require a participating authority exercising response powers or recovery powers under an emergency measures agreement to refrain from or stop exercising one or more of the response powers or recovery powers;

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (c) set limits or conditions on the exercise, by a local authority or participating authority referred to in paragraph (a) or (b), of one or more response powers or recovery powers.

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (3) Immediately on making an order under this section, the minister must notify the local authority or participating authority, or its head, of the details of the order.

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (4) The minister

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (a) may make an order under this section orally or in writing, and

heading: Restrictions on exercising powers
paragraph: (b) as soon as reasonably practicable after making an order orally, must reduce the order to writing.

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph:
105
		  (1) A local authority may make an emergency instrument under this Division during the period for which a declaration of a state of local emergency applies, except as permitted under section 110 [response borrowing].

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) Before making an emergency instrument under this Division, a local authority must be satisfied that any prohibitions, requirements, limits or conditions imposed, or authorizations made, under the emergency instrument are necessary to respond to the emergency.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph:
106
		  (1) A local authority may make an emergency instrument under this Division

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) in writing, or

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) orally, if the emergency instrument is an order made by an individual.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) A local authority may provide in an emergency instrument made under this Division that the instrument applies

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) to all or part of the area to which a declaration of a state of local emergency applies,

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) for all or part of the period for which a declaration of a state of local emergency applies, and

heading: How response powers may be exercised
