paragraph: (c) to a person or thing, or a class of persons or things, as established by the local authority.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (3) A local authority must, if applicable, identify in an emergency instrument the declaration of a state of local emergency to which the emergency instrument relates.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (4) As soon as reasonably practicable after a local authority makes an emergency instrument under this Division, the local authority must

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) in the case of an emergency instrument made orally, reduce the emergency instrument to writing and publish the emergency instrument, and

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) in the case of an emergency instrument made in writing, publish the emergency instrument.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (5) Subject to section 110 [response borrowing], an emergency instrument made under this Division ceases to have effect on the earliest of the following dates:

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) the date provided for in the emergency instrument;

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) the date on which the local authority rescinds or repeals the emergency instrument;

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) the date on which the declaration of a state of local emergency to which the emergency instrument relates expires or is cancelled, unless the emergency instrument is approved under section 98 (4) [declaration of local recovery period] as an emergency instrument that continues to have effect.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (6) For certainty, the powers of a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, under this Division are subject to any

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) prescribed prohibitions, requirements, limits or conditions, and

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) orders made under section 104 (2) [restrictions on exercising powers].

heading: Response powers
paragraph:
107
		  (1) For the purposes of this Division, a local authority may, by emergency instrument, do all the things that the minister may do as described under the following provisions:

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (a) section 75 [essential matters], other than section 75 (1) (b) (iv);

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (b) section 76 (1) [land and other property];

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (c) section 77 (1) or (2) [evacuations and removals];

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (d) section 78 [general restrictions].

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (2) The exception in subsection (1) (a) does not apply in relation to the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation.

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph:
108
		  (1) This section applies if

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (a) a local authority is intending to do any of the following:

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (i)  make an emergency instrument under section 107 (1) (c) requiring persons to evacuate an area;

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (ii)  issue a warning that the evacuation of an area may be required;

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (iii)  permit evacuated persons to return to an evacuated area, and

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (b) the area that will be affected by the evacuation, warning or permission is adjacent to an area that is within the jurisdiction of another local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation.

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), a local authority must, before taking an action described in subsection (1) (a), do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (a) consult and coordinate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the other local authority in whose jurisdiction the area referred to in subsection (1) (b) is located;

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (b) give to a local authority consulted in accordance with paragraph (a) notice of the details of the intended action and, if applicable, of any arrangements the local authority intends to make under section 107 (1) (c) with respect to evacuated persons;

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (c) consider any comments received from a local authority consulted in accordance with paragraph (a);

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (d) coordinate with a local authority consulted in accordance with paragraph (a) in respect of

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (i)  the prohibitions, requirements, limits and conditions that apply to the evacuation and re-entry, and

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (ii)  the form, content and timing of any warnings.

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (3) If, in the opinion of the head of the local authority, it would not be practicable to comply with subsection (2) (a), (b), (c) or (d) due to an imminent risk of loss of life or risk of injury to individuals or animals, or risk of significant loss or damage to property,

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (a) the requirements of that provision do not apply, and

heading: Consultation and coordination before evacuation and re-entry
paragraph: (b) in the case of subsection (2) (b), the local authority must, as soon as reasonably practicable after taking the action referred to in subsection (1) (a), give notice to the other local authority in whose jurisdiction the area referred to in subsection (1) (b) is located of the details of the action taken and, if applicable, of any arrangements the local authority made or intends to make under section 107 (1) (c) with respect to evacuated persons.

heading: General power of Nisga'a Nation and treaty first nations to do all things necessary
paragraph:
109
		  (1) The head of the Nisga'a Nation or of a treaty first nation may, by emergency instrument, do all acts and implement all procedures that the head of the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation is satisfied are necessary to respond to an emergency.

heading: General power of Nisga'a Nation and treaty first nations to do all things necessary
paragraph: (2) For certainty, nothing in this Division is intended to limit the power conferred under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph:
110
		  (1) A municipality or regional district may adopt a bylaw to borrow money to pay expenses incurred in responding to an emergency in an area within the jurisdiction of the municipality or regional district.

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (2) A municipality or regional district may adopt a bylaw under this section no later than 60 days after the latest date on which

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (a) the municipality or regional district makes a declaration of, or extends the period of, a state of local emergency in relation to the emergency, or

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (b) the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the minister makes a declaration of, or the Lieutenant Governor in Council extends the period of, a state of provincial emergency in relation to the emergency.

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), a municipality or regional district may adopt a bylaw under this section later than the period referred to in that subsection if the provincial administrator extends that period or grants an exception to that period.

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (4) Despite anything to the contrary in the Community Charter, the Local Government Act or the Vancouver Charter,

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (a) the borrowing of money under a bylaw adopted under this section need not be of a capital nature, and

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (b) the approval of the electors is not required to adopt the bylaw referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (5) A bylaw adopted under this section has no effect until the bylaw is approved by the minister responsible for the administration of the Community Charter and by the inspector of municipalities, appointed under the Local Government Act.

heading: Response borrowing
paragraph: (6) Subsection (5) does not apply to the City of Vancouver.

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: 111		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation under this Division during the period for which a declaration of a state of local emergency applies.

heading: When response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may not make a regulation under this Division in relation to a declaration of a state of local emergency made by the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, or the head of the Nisga'a Nation or of a treaty first nation, unless the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation consents to the regulation being made.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph:
112
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation under this Division after consulting with a local authority that has made an emergency instrument declaring a state of local emergency.

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) A regulation made under this Division ceases to have effect on the earliest of the following dates:

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) the date provided for in the regulation;

heading: How response powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) the date on which the declaration of a state of local emergency to which the regulation relates expires or is cancelled, unless the regulation is approved under section 98 (4) [declaration of local recovery period] as a regulation that continues to have effect.

heading: Response powers
paragraph:
113
		  For the purposes of this Division, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as described under the following provisions:

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (a) section 83 [modifying enactments and authorizations];

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (b) section 84 [modifying time periods];

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (c) section 85 [modifying fee requirements];

heading: Response powers
paragraph: (d) section 86 [enforcement of modified enactments and authorizations].

heading: Application of other provisions
paragraph:
114
		  (1) The following provisions apply in relation to a regulation made under this Division:

heading: Application of other provisions
paragraph: (a) section 80 (2) [when response powers may be exercised];

heading: Application of other provisions
paragraph: (b) section 81 (1) and (2) [how response powers may be exercised];

heading: Application of other provisions
paragraph: (c) section 82 [retroactive application of response powers].

heading: Application of other provisions
paragraph: (2) Section 84 (3), (4) and (5) [modifying time periods] applies in relation to a time period suspended, extended or replaced, as applicable, by a regulation made under section 113 (b).

heading: References for interpretive purposes
paragraph:
115
		  For the purposes of a provision that applies under this Division, a reference to a declaration of a state of provincial emergency must be read as a reference to a declaration of a state of local emergency.

heading: When recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph:
116
		  (1) A local authority may make an emergency instrument under this Division during the period for which a declaration of a local recovery period applies, except as permitted under section 119 [recovery borrowing].

heading: When recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) Before making an emergency instrument under this Division, a local authority must be satisfied that any prohibitions, requirements, limits or conditions imposed, or authorizations made, under the emergency instrument are necessary to recover from the emergency.

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph:
117
		  (1) Section 106 (2), (3) and (6) [how response powers may be exercised] applies in relation to an emergency instrument made under this Division.

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 119, an emergency instrument made under this Division ceases to have effect on the earliest of the following dates:

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) the date provided for

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (i)  in a declaration of a provincial recovery period, in the case of an emergency instrument approved under section 98 (4) [declaration of local recovery period], or

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (ii)  in the emergency instrument, in any case;

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (c) the date on which the declaration of a local recovery period to which the emergency instrument relates expires or is cancelled.

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (3) As soon as reasonably practicable after an emergency instrument is made under this Division, the local authority must

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (a) give notice to the minister, and

heading: How recovery powers may be exercised
paragraph: (b) publish the emergency instrument.

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph:
118
		  (1) For the purposes of this Division, a local authority may, by emergency instrument, do all the things that the minister may do as described under the following provisions:

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (a) section 75 (1) [essential matters], other than section 75 (1) (b) (iv) or (d);

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (b) section 76 (1) [land and other property];

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (c) section 78 [general restrictions].

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1) (b), a local authority may, by emergency instrument, prohibit the entry into any structure or onto any land, by any person and for any purpose related to

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (a) protecting the health, safety or well-being of persons, or the safety of property or of objects or sites of heritage value, or

heading: Recovery powers
paragraph: (b) taking emergency measures to recover from the emergency.

heading: Recovery borrowing
paragraph:
119
		  (1) A municipality or regional district may adopt a bylaw to borrow money to pay expenses incurred in recovering from an emergency in an area within the jurisdiction of the municipality or regional district.

heading: Recovery borrowing
paragraph: (2) A municipality or regional district may adopt a bylaw under this section no later than 90 days after the latest date on which

heading: Recovery borrowing
paragraph: (a) the municipality or regional district declares or extends the period of a declaration of a local recovery period in relation to the emergency, or

heading: Recovery borrowing
paragraph: (b) the Lieutenant Governor in Council declares or extends the period of a declaration of a provincial recovery period in relation to the emergency.

heading: Recovery borrowing
paragraph: (3) Section 110 (3), (4), (5) and (6) [response borrowing] applies in relation to a bylaw adopted under this section.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph:
120
		  (1) In this section, "specified action" means an action described in subsection (2) (a) (i) in relation to a provision set out in subsection (6) (a) or (b) of this section.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (2) This section applies if

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, is intending to do any of the following:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  make an emergency instrument or take any other action under a provision set out in subsection (6) of this section, as applicable;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  issue a warning that the evacuation of an area may be required;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iii)  permit evacuated persons to return to an evacuated area, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) the emergency instrument or action, warning or permission will affect an area, or the people in an area, that is

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  within Nisga'a Lands or treaty lands of a treaty first nation,

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  described for the purposes of this section in one or more of the following:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (A) the local authority's emergency management plan;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (B) an agreement made under this Act with an Indigenous governing body, or

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iii)  if the local authority was unable to reach agreement with an Indigenous governing body under section 55 (1) (e) [consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples], described for the purposes of section 90 [consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples] in an emergency management plan referred to in section 39 (1) (b) [emergency management planning and information] for that Indigenous governing body.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (5), the local authority must, before the local authority takes an action described in subsection (2) (a) and (b), do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) in the case of an action that will affect an area, or the people in an area, that is referred to in subsection (2) (b) (ii) or (iii), consult and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the Indigenous governing body that is specified in the plan or agreement, as applicable, in relation to the area;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) give to the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation, or an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a) of this subsection, as applicable, notice of the details of the intended action and, if applicable, of any arrangements the local authority intends to make under section 107 (1) (c) [response powers] with respect to evacuated individuals;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (c) consider

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body consulted in accordance with paragraph (a), and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  the rights of the Indigenous peoples on whose behalf the Nisga'a Nation, treaty first nation or Indigenous governing body referred to in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph acts.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (4) The local authority must not take an action described in subsection (2) (a) that will affect an area, or the people in an area, that is referred to in subsection (2) (b) (i) unless the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation, as applicable, consents to the action being taken.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (5) If, in the opinion of the head of the local authority, it would not be practicable to comply with subsection (3) (a), (b) or (c), or to seek to obtain consent under subsection (4), in relation to a specified action due to an imminent risk of loss of life or risk of injury to individuals or animals, or risk of significant loss or damage to property,

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) the requirements of that provision do not apply, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) the local authority must, as soon as reasonably practicable after taking the specified action, do all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  in the case of subsection (3) (a), engage and cooperate, in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the Indigenous governing body referred to in that subsection;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of subsection (3) (b), give to the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation, or an Indigenous governing body engaged under subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, as applicable, notice of the details of the action taken and, if applicable, of any arrangements the local authority made or intends to make under section 107 (1) (c) with respect to evacuated persons;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iii)  in the case of subsection (3) (c), consider

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (A) any comments received from the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation or an Indigenous governing body engaged under subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (B) the rights of the Indigenous peoples on whose behalf the Nisga'a Nation, treaty first nation or Indigenous governing body referred to in clause (A) acts.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of this section, the following provisions are set out:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) sections 107 (1) (b) and 118 (1) (b) [recovery powers], to the extent those provisions authorize the local authority to do things the minister may do under section 76 (1) (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) and (f) [land and other property];

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) section 107 (1) (c);

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (c) sections 107 (1) (d) and 118 (1) (c), to the extent those provisions authorize the local authority to do things the minister may do under section 78 (1) (a) [general restrictions];

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (d) section 118 (2).

heading: Final report
paragraph:
121
		  (1) A local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, must prepare a report with respect to a declaration of a state of local emergency and, if applicable, a declaration of a local recovery period, by the local authority that summarizes all of the following:

heading: Final report
paragraph: (a) the nature of the emergency;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (b) the response powers and recovery powers exercised with respect to the emergency;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (c) if the head of the local authority, under section 120 (5), was of the opinion that it was not practicable to comply with subsection (3) (a), (b) or (c) of that section, or to seek to obtain consent under subsection (4) of that section, the reasons for the head of the local authority's opinion;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (d) any other matter as required by the minister and the regulations.

heading: Final report
paragraph: (2) The local authority must provide a copy of the report to the provincial administrator

heading: Final report
paragraph: (a) in the form and manner required by the provincial administrator, and

heading: Final report
paragraph: (b) within 120 days of the expiry or cancellation of the following, whichever is later:

heading: Final report
paragraph: (i)  the declaration of a state of local emergency to which the report relates;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (ii)  the declaration of a local recovery period, if any, that followed the declaration of a state of local emergency to which the report relates.

heading: Final report
paragraph: (3) If required by the regulations, the local authority must publish the report in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Final report
paragraph: (4) The minister may request the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation to prepare a report described in subsection (1) in relation to a declaration of a state of local emergency and, if applicable, a declaration of a local recovery period, by the Nisga'a Nation or treaty first nation.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
122
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "claimant" means a person who makes a claim for compensation under this Division in accordance with section 126 [claiming compensation];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "specified date", in relation to an area in which property that is the subject of a claim for compensation is located, means the latest of the following dates that applies:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the date on which a declaration of a state of provincial emergency or a declaration of a state of local emergency made with respect to the area, or the last extension of that declaration, if any, is cancelled or expires;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if a declaration of a provincial recovery period or a declaration of a local recovery period is made with respect to the area, the date on which that declaration, or the last extension of it, if any, is cancelled or expires.

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph:
123
		  (1) Subject to this Division and the regulations, a person is entitled to compensation for loss of or damage to property if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (a) the loss of or damage to the property was caused by the exercise of a power under any of the following provisions:

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (i)  section 76 (1) (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) or (f) [land and other property] or 89 (1) (b) [recovery powers];

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (ii)  sections 107 (1) (b) [response powers] or 118 (1) (b) [recovery powers], to the extent those provisions authorize things the minister may do under section 76 (1) (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) or (f);

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (b) the person owned the property at the time the loss or damage was caused.

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (2) A person is entitled to claim compensation under subsection (1) from

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (a) the government, if the minister or the Lieutenant Governor in Council exercised the power,

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (b) a local authority, if the local authority exercised the power, or

heading: Persons entitled to compensation
paragraph: (c) a participating authority, if the participating authority exercised the power under an emergency measures agreement.

heading: Persons not entitled to compensation
paragraph:
124
		  (1) A person is not entitled to compensation under this Division if the loss or damage has a value of less than a prescribed amount.

heading: Persons not entitled to compensation
paragraph: (2) A person is not entitled to compensation under this Division in prescribed circumstances.

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph:
125
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the amount of compensation to which a person is entitled under this Division is the least of the following amounts:

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (a) the prescribed amount, if any;

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (b) the amount required to repair the property that is the subject of the claim to the property's condition as it was immediately before the loss or damage was caused;

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (c) the amount required to replace the property that is the subject of the claim with property that is of similar nature, value and quality to that of the property as it was immediately before the loss or damage was caused.

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (2) The amount of compensation to which a person is entitled under this Division does not include an amount equal to any amount of compensation for the loss or damage that is paid or payable, to any person, in prescribed circumstances or under any of the following:

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (a) Division 3 [Financial Assistance] of this Part;

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (b) another enactment of British Columbia or an enactment of Canada;

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (c) an agreement, including a contract of insurance;

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (d) a settlement of or judgment in legal proceedings.

heading: Amount of compensation
paragraph: (3) The value of property and the amounts referred to in subsections (1) (b) and (c) and (2) must be determined in accordance with the regulations, if any.

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph:
126
		  To claim compensation under this Division, a person must do all of the following:

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph: (a) make the claim in writing;

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph: (b) include with the claim

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph: (i)  a written assessment of the loss or damage, prepared by the claimant's insurer or by another person who is qualified to perform assessments and is independent of the claimant, and

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph: (ii)  the information or records required by the regulations, if any;

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph: (c) submit the claim

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph: (i)  in the form and manner required by the government, local authority or participating authority, as applicable, and

heading: Claiming compensation
paragraph: (ii)  no later than 60 days after the specified date in relation to the area in which the property that is the subject of the claim is located.

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph:
127
		  (1) On receiving a claim made in accordance with section 126, the government, local authority or participating authority, as applicable, must

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (a) determine, in accordance with this Division and the regulations, whether the claimant is entitled to compensation under this Division, and

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (b) if the claimant is entitled to compensation, either

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (i)  offer to the claimant an amount as compensation, or

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (ii)  designate an adjuster to determine the amount of compensation to which the claimant is entitled.

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (2) On making a determination respecting compensation, the government, local authority or participating authority must notify the claimant as follows:

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (a) the notice must be in writing;

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (b) the notice must include all of the following:

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (i)  a statement of whether the claimant is entitled to compensation and, if so, an offer of an amount as compensation or details of the designation of an adjuster, as applicable;

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (ii)  the reasons for the determination.

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (3) The government, local authority or participating authority must make the determination respecting compensation no later than 90 days after the latest of the following:

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (a) the specified date in relation to the area in which the property that is the subject of the claim is located;

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (b) the date the claim was received.

heading: If claim for compensation made
paragraph: (4) If an offer was made under subsection (1) (b) (i) and the amount offered was refused within the time stated in the offer, the government, local authority or participating authority must designate an adjuster no later than 60 days after the date on which the offer was refused.

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph:
128
		  (1) If an adjuster is designated under section 127, the adjuster must

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (a) determine, in accordance with this Division and the regulations, the amount of compensation to which the claimant is entitled,

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (b) notify the claimant, in writing,

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (i)  of the determination and the reasons for it, and

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (ii)  that the determination may be disputed before an arbitrator, and

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (c) notify the government, local authority or participating authority, as applicable, of the determination and whether the claimant accepts the determination.

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (2) If the claimant or the government, local authority or participating authority disputes the adjuster's determination, the government, local authority or participating authority, as applicable, must initiate arbitration no later than 60 days after the date on which it was notified of the determination.

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (3) The Arbitration Act applies to an arbitration under subsection (2), except that an arbitral tribunal may be composed of only one arbitrator.

heading: If adjuster designated
paragraph: (4) An adjuster, other than a person appointed under the Public Service Act, may be remunerated, in accordance with the regulations, if any, for performing duties under this section.

heading: Paying compensation
paragraph: 129		  If a claimant is entitled to compensation under this Division, the government, local authority or participating authority, as applicable, must promptly pay to the claimant whichever of the following amounts applies:

heading: Paying compensation
paragraph: (a) the amount the claimant accepted under an offer or after a determination by an adjuster under section 128;

heading: Paying compensation
paragraph: (b) the amount determined on arbitration.

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph:
130
		  (1) The government may pay compensation to a person for loss of or damage to property as a result of taking an emergency measure if

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (a) the person is not entitled to compensation under Division 1 [Compensation for Exercise of Response or Recovery Power] of this Part,

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (b) compensation under this Division is authorized under the regulations,

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (c) the person is eligible, under the regulations, for compensation under this Division,

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (d) a request for compensation is made in accordance with the regulations, and

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (e) compensation is determined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (2) A local authority may pay compensation to a person for loss of or damage to property as a result of taking an emergency measure if

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (a) the person is not entitled to compensation under Division 1 of this Part,

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (b) compensation under this Division is authorized under a bylaw adopted by the local authority,

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (c) the person is eligible, under the bylaw, for compensation under this Division,

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (d) a request for compensation is made in accordance with the bylaw, and

heading: Discretionary compensation
paragraph: (e) compensation is determined in accordance with the bylaw.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
131
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "financial assistance authorization" means an authorization made under section 132 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "loss" means a financial loss, loss of or damage to property, a cost or an expense, or a type of any of these,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) that a person incurred or is likely to incur as a result of an emergency, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for which, under the regulations, financial assistance is available.

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph:
132
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister or the provincial administrator may authorize financial assistance to be paid under this Division with respect to an emergency if the Lieutenant Governor in Council, minister or provincial administrator is satisfied that

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph: (a) the emergency meets prescribed criteria, and

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph: (b) any additional prescribed conditions are met.

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph: (2) A financial assistance authorization may be made whether or not a declaration of a state of provincial emergency or a declaration of a state of local emergency is made.

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph: (3) A financial assistance authorization must be made in writing and identify

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph: (a) the emergency to which the authorization relates, and

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph: (b) the area in respect of which financial assistance is authorized.

heading: Authorizing financial assistance
paragraph: (4) As soon as reasonably practicable after a financial assistance authorization is made, the minister must publish the authorization.

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph:
133
		  (1) To request financial assistance under this Division, a person must do all of the following:

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph: (a) within the prescribed period after the date on which the applicable financial assistance authorization is made, notify the provincial administrator that the person intends to request financial assistance;

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph: (b) make the request in writing;

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph: (c) include with the request any prescribed information and records;

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph: (d) submit the request to the provincial administrator within the prescribed period and in the form and manner required by the provincial administrator.

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1) (a) and (d), a person may notify, or submit a request to, the provincial administrator after the period referred to in that provision, as applicable, if

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph: (a) the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister or the provincial administrator extends, or grants an exception to, the period, and

heading: Requesting financial assistance
paragraph: (b) the person is eligible for the extension or exception.

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph:
134
		  (1) On receiving a request made in accordance with section 133, the provincial administrator must determine, in accordance with this Division and the regulations,

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph: (a) whether the person is eligible to receive financial assistance under this Division, and

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph: (b) if financial assistance is to be paid, the amount payable.

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph: (2) The provincial administrator may refuse financial assistance or reduce the amount payable in relation to property in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph: (a) compensation for the loss is paid or payable, to any person, in prescribed circumstances or under

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph: (i)  Division 1 [Compensation for Exercise of Response or Recovery Power] or 2 [Compensation for Taking Emergency Measure] of this Part, or

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph: (ii)  a settlement of or judgment in legal proceedings;

heading: Determining financial assistance
paragraph: (b) prescribed circumstances.

heading: Further information and evaluators
paragraph:
135
		  For the purposes of making a determination under section 134, the provincial administrator may do one or more of the following:

heading: Further information and evaluators
paragraph: (a) require the person making the request to provide additional information or records, including proof of a loss;

heading: Further information and evaluators
paragraph: (b) subject to the regulations, request a person who has relevant training and qualifications to do one or more of the following:

heading: Further information and evaluators
paragraph: (i)  evaluate damaged property;

heading: Further information and evaluators
paragraph: (ii)  assess the amount of a loss, including an amount needed to repair or replace lost or damaged property;

heading: Further information and evaluators
paragraph: (iii)  give advice on any matter referred to in section 134.

heading: Notice of determination
paragraph:
136
		  On making a determination respecting financial assistance, the provincial administrator must notify the person who requested assistance of the determination as follows:

heading: Notice of determination
paragraph: (a) the notice must be in writing;

heading: Notice of determination
paragraph: (b) the notice must include all of the following:

heading: Notice of determination
paragraph: (i)  a statement of whether financial assistance is to be paid and, if so, the amount payable;

heading: Notice of determination
paragraph: (ii)  the reasons for the determination;

heading: Notice of determination
paragraph: (iii)  procedural information respecting how the determination may be reconsidered or appealed.

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph:
137
		  (1) A person who requested financial assistance may appeal a determination made under section 136 to the minister if

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (a) the determination has been reconsidered in accordance with the regulations, and

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (b) the appeal is made on one or more of the following grounds:

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (i)  the provincial administrator erred in law;

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (ii)  the provincial administrator failed to observe the rules of procedural fairness;

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (iii)  prescribed grounds.

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (2) An appeal may be made by

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (a) submitting the appeal, in writing,

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (i)  in the form and manner required by the minister, and

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (ii)  no later than 90 days after the date on which the person received notice of the result of the reconsideration, and

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (b) including with the appeal any prescribed information or records.

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2) (a) (ii), a person may submit an appeal after the period referred to in that provision if the minister extends that period.

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (4) On receiving an appeal, the minister may do one or more of the following:

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (a) request the appellant to provide additional information or records;

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (b) reject the appeal for a failure to comply with this section, the regulations made with respect to this section or a request made under paragraph (a) of this subsection;

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (c) confirm or vary the result of the reconsideration.

heading: Appeal of determination
paragraph: (5) The minister must notify the appellant, in writing, of the minister's decision under subsection (4) (b) or (c) and of the reasons for the decision.

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph:
138
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the minister may, by order, require a person who received an amount under this Division as financial assistance to repay all or part of the amount to the government if any of the following circumstances apply:

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (a) the person was not entitled to the amount;

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (b) the amount was not authorized under or determined in accordance with this Division or the regulations;

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (c) the amount was incorrectly calculated;

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (d) the person received full or partial compensation from another source for the loss with respect to which the person received financial assistance, including under

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (i)  Division 1 [Compensation for Exercise of Response or Recovery Power] or 2 [Compensation for Taking Emergency Measure] of this Part, or

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (ii)  a settlement of or judgment in legal proceedings;

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (e) the person obtained the financial assistance by fraudulent means;

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (f) prescribed circumstances.

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (2) An order under this section may be made no later than 5 years after the date on which the person was notified under section 136 of the amount of financial assistance payable to the person.

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (3) The minister must determine the amount to be repaid under subsection (1) in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (4) If a person fails to comply with an order made under this section,

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (a) the amount that must be repaid may be recovered as a debt due to the government,

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (b) the minister may, in accordance with the regulations, file a certificate in the prescribed form with a court that has jurisdiction, and

heading: Recovering amounts paid
paragraph: (c) on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Mandatory compliance
paragraph:
139
		  A person must comply with

heading: Mandatory compliance
paragraph: (a) this Act and the regulations, and

heading: Mandatory compliance
paragraph: (b) all orders and emergency instruments made under this Act that apply to the person.

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph:
140
		  (1) The provincial administrator may request that a peace officer assist a person in the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty with respect to the taking of an emergency measure.

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph: (2) A peace officer whose assistance is requested under this section may take any action that the peace officer considers necessary for a purpose described in subsection (1).

heading: Injunctions
paragraph:
141
		  (1) Without notice to any person, the minister or a local authority may apply, in the manner set out in the regulations, if any, to the Supreme Court for an order under this section.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (2) The court may order a person to do or refrain from doing those things that the court considers necessary if the court is satisfied that there is reason to believe the person is interfering with or obstructing, or will likely interfere with or obstruct, a person or peace officer who is

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (a) exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act, or

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (b) taking an emergency measure in relation to a declaration of a state of provincial emergency, a declaration of a state of local emergency, a declaration of a provincial recovery period or a declaration of a local recovery period

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (i)  in accordance with an emergency management plan, or

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (ii)  under an order of the minister or an emergency instrument of a local authority.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (3) If the court is satisfied that there has been or will be a contravention of this Act or the regulations, or an order or emergency instrument, the court may grant an injunction requiring a person to comply with, or restraining a person from contravening,

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (a) the Act or a regulation made under it, or

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (b) an order or emergency instrument made in the exercise of a response power or a recovery power.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (4) The court may grant an interim order or injunction until the outcome of an application under this section is determined.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
142
		  In this Division, "costs or penalty order" means an order made under section 143 or 145 [order to impose administrative penalty].

heading: Order to recover costs
paragraph:
143
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, the provincial administrator may, by order, require a person to pay costs in an amount determined in accordance with section 144 if both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Order to recover costs
paragraph: (a) an emergency is threatened or caused in whole or in part by the person's acts or omissions;

heading: Order to recover costs
paragraph: (b) the government or a local authority, or a participating authority acting under an emergency measures agreement, incurs an expense to mitigate or prepare for the threat or to respond to or recover from the emergency.

heading: Order to recover costs
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this section, an emergency is threatened or caused by a person's acts or omissions if those acts or omissions

heading: Order to recover costs
paragraph: (a) contribute, directly or indirectly and beyond a minimal extent, to the presence of the threat or emergency, or

heading: Order to recover costs
paragraph: (b) change the nature or scope of the emergency or disaster so as to increase, directly or indirectly and beyond a minimal extent, the severity of the emergency.

heading: Order to recover costs
paragraph: (3) The provincial administrator may, for the purposes of this section, collect information from another person, organization or entity.

heading: Amount of costs
paragraph:
144
		  (1) The amount of costs that a person may be required to pay under section 143 is the lesser of the following:

heading: Amount of costs
paragraph: (a) the amount determined under subsection (2) (b);

heading: Amount of costs
paragraph: (b) the amount demanded by the minister, local authority or participating authority referred to in section 143 (1) (b), as applicable.

heading: Amount of costs
paragraph: (2) The provincial administrator must determine, in accordance with the regulations, if any, the following amounts:

heading: Amount of costs
paragraph: (a) the amount of the costs incurred by the government, local authority or participating authority to mitigate or prepare for the threat of, or to respond to or recover from, the emergency;

heading: Amount of costs
paragraph: (b) the portion of those costs that equals the portion of the liability for the threat or emergency that is attributable to the person's acts or omissions.

heading: Order to impose administrative penalty
paragraph:
145
		  Subject to the regulations, the provincial administrator may, by order, impose an administrative penalty on a person if both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Order to impose administrative penalty
paragraph: (a) the provincial administrator determines that a person has contravened

heading: Order to impose administrative penalty
paragraph: (i)  a prescribed provision of this Act or the regulations, or

heading: Order to impose administrative penalty
paragraph: (ii)  an order made under a prescribed provision of this Act or the regulations by the minister or provincial administrator;

heading: Order to impose administrative penalty
paragraph: (b) the person has not been charged with an offence with respect to the same incident.

heading: Making costs or penalty orders
paragraph:
146
		  (1) When making a costs or penalty order, the provincial administrator must

heading: Making costs or penalty orders
paragraph: (a) make the order in the prescribed form, and

heading: Making costs or penalty orders
paragraph: (b) include in the order any prescribed information.

heading: Making costs or penalty orders
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations and section 159 [duty to protect confidentiality], on making an order under section 145, the provincial administrator may publish the following information:

heading: Making costs or penalty orders
paragraph: (a) the details of the contravention that was the subject of the order, including the name of the person who must pay the administrative penalty;

heading: Making costs or penalty orders
paragraph: (b) the amount of the administrative penalty;

heading: Making costs or penalty orders
paragraph: (c) prescribed information.

heading: Payment of costs or penalty order
paragraph:
147
		  (1) A person who is subject to a costs or penalty order must pay the amount of the costs or of the penalty stated in the order

heading: Payment of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (a) within the prescribed period after the order is made, and

heading: Payment of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (b) in the prescribed manner.

heading: Payment of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 145 (b), nothing in this Division relieves a person from any other liability under another enactment for the person's acts or omissions in relation to a matter that is the subject of a costs or penalty order.

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph:
148
		  (1) A person who is subject to a costs or penalty order may appeal the order on one or more of the following grounds:

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (a) the provincial administrator erred in law;

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (b) the provincial administrator failed to observe the rules of procedural fairness;

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (c) relevant evidence that was not reasonably available at the time the provincial administrator made the order has become available;

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (d) prescribed grounds.

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (2) An appeal may be made by

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (a) submitting the appeal, in writing,

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (i)  in the form and manner required by the minister, and

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (ii)  no later than 60 days after the date on which the person was served with the order being appealed, and

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (b) including with the appeal the prescribed information or records.

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (3) On receiving an appeal, the minister may

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (a) reject the appeal for a failure to comply with this section or the regulations made with respect to this section, or

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (b) confirm, vary or rescind the order being appealed.

heading: Appeal of costs or penalty order
paragraph: (4) The minister must notify the appellant, in writing, of the minister's decision and the reasons for it.

heading: Amount under order is debt due
paragraph:
149
		  If a person fails to pay an amount in accordance with section 147,

heading: Amount under order is debt due
paragraph: (a) the amount that must be paid under the order may be recovered as a debt due to the government,

heading: Amount under order is debt due
paragraph: (b) the minister may, in accordance with the regulations, file a certificate in the prescribed form with a court that has jurisdiction, and

heading: Amount under order is debt due
paragraph: (c) on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
150
		  (1) Sections 4 and 5 of the Offence Act do not apply with respect to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) contravenes an order made under section 56 [directed mitigation and preparation measures];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) contravenes an order or emergency instrument made under any of sections 73 to 78, 89, 107, 109 or 118 [response or recovery powers];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) provides false or misleading information with respect to

heading: Offences
paragraph: (i)  a claim for compensation under section 126 [claiming compensation],

heading: Offences
paragraph: (ii)  a request for compensation under section 130 [discretionary compensation],

heading: Offences
paragraph: (iii)  a request for financial assistance under section 133 [requesting financial assistance], or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (iv)  a request for information under section 158 (1) (c) (i) [information about persons needing services];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) interferes with or obstructs, in the exercise of a power, the performance of a duty or the taking of an emergency measure by a person who is a protected person within the meaning of section 154 [protection against legal proceedings] or a peace officer;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (e) contravenes section 158 (3).

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) A proceeding for an offence under this section may not be commenced

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) in any court more than 2 years after the facts on which the proceeding is based first come to the knowledge of the minister, or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) if an order imposing an administrative penalty is made under section 145 [order to impose administrative penalty] with respect to the same incident that gave rise to the offence.

heading: Offence involving corporation
paragraph: 151		  If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an officer, director, employee or agent of the corporation who directs, authorizes, permits, participates or acquiesces in the offence also commits the offence, whether or not the corporation is prosecuted.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph:
152
		  If a person commits an offence under this Act and continues to commit the offence, separate penalties may be imposed with respect to the offence for each day the offence continues.

heading: Penalties
paragraph:
153
		  (1) If an individual commits an offence under this Act, the individual is liable to one or both of the following:

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) imprisonment for a term of not more than one year;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) a fine of not more than $100 000.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (2) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act,

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) the corporation is liable to a fine of not more than $1 000 000, and

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) an officer, director, employee or agent of the corporation who directed, authorized, permitted, participated or acquiesced in the offence is liable to one or both of the following:

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (i)  imprisonment for a term of not more than one year;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (ii)  a fine of not more than $300 000.

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph:
154
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: "decision-making agreement" has the same meaning as in section 33 [definitions for Part 3];

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: "official guidance" means guidance or direction, with respect to taking an action or refraining from taking an action, that is issued for the purposes of mitigating, preparing for, responding to or recovering from a critical incident or emergency by any of the following:

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (a) a regulated entity or a member, officer or employee of a regulated entity;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (b) the provincial administrator or a member of the provincial emergency management organization;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (c) a local authority or a member of an emergency management organization or a multijurisdictional emergency management organization;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (d) a participating authority;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (e) a department or agency of the government of Canada that

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (i)  takes emergency measures or provides assistance under an agreement made under section 8 [minister may enter into agreements], or

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (ii)  is responsible for national defence;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (f) the person who is responsible for coordinating actions taken in relation to the critical incident or emergency;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (g) in the case of a volunteer, the person who is responsible for the immediate supervision of the volunteer or coordinating the actions taken by the volunteer;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: "person" includes an Indigenous governing body;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: "protected person" means the following:

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (a) the government;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (b) a local authority;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (c) an Indigenous governing body;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (d) a participating authority;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (e) a person who exercises a power or performs a duty under this Act;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (f) a person who, in accordance with a decision-making agreement or a statutory power agreement, provides or does not provide consent in relation to a statutory power of decision or a statutory power;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (g) a person who, under this Act, takes emergency measures or provides emergency resources or the use of land;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (h) a public safety provider, a person or entity that under the regulations is authorized for the purposes of section 32 (4) [requests for deployment] or a person or entity in a prescribed class, which provider, person or entity registers volunteers in accordance with the regulations, if any;

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (i) a person who is an employer, member, director, officer or employee of a person or entity referred to in paragraph (e), (f), (g) or (h);

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (j) a volunteer who is registered in accordance with the regulations, if any, with the provincial administrator, a local authority or a person or entity referred to in paragraph (h);

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (k) a person who is an employer of a volunteer referred to in paragraph (j);

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (l) a person who acts under the order, emergency instrument or direction, as applicable, of

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (i)  a person referred to in paragraph (e), (h) or (j), or

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (ii)  a person who is an employer, member, director, officer or employee of a person or entity referred to in paragraph (e) or (h);

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (m) a person who is an employer, member, director, officer or employee of a person referred to in paragraph (l);

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: "statutory power agreement" has the same meaning as in section 33.

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), no legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against a protected person because of anything done or omitted

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (a) in the exercise or intended exercise of a power under this Act,

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (b) in the performance or intended performance of a duty under this Act,

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (c) without limiting paragraph (a) or (b), in respect of the provision of consent in relation to a statutory power of decision or a statutory power in accordance with a decision-making agreement or a statutory power agreement,

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (d) in taking an action that the person is authorized or required to take under this Act, including under an agreement made in respect of this Act, or

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (e) in complying with, or intending to comply with,

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (i)  a direction given by a person who is taking an action described in paragraph (a), (b) or (d), or

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (ii)  official guidance.

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply to a protected person in relation to anything done or omitted in bad faith or if the protected person was grossly negligent.

heading: Protection against legal proceedings
paragraph: (4) Subsection (2) does not affect an obligation of the government to pay compensation under Division 1 [Compensation for Exercise of Response or Recovery Power] of Part 7.

heading: Employment protection
paragraph:
155
		  (1) In this section and section 156, "protected employee" means a person who is employed by, or provides services under contract to, an employer and either

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (a) is a volunteer

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (i)  who, because of the person's unique training and experience, is identified by name by the provincial administrator, a public safety provider or a person who makes a request under section 32 [requests for deployment] in response to a critical incident or emergency, and

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (ii)  who is deployed under section 32 (4) to take specialized measures, or

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (b) is required, by an order made under section 75 (1) (d) [essential matters] or an emergency instrument made under section 107 (1) (a) [response powers], to provide a service or give assistance.

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (2) An employer must not terminate, or change the terms or conditions of, the employment of a protected employee on the grounds that the protected employee failed to attend as scheduled or otherwise contravened a term or condition of employment if

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (a) the protected employee gives, in accordance with the regulations, written notice to the employer of being a protected employee, and

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (b) the failure or contravention occurred as a result of

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (i)  being deployed under section 32 (4) to take specialized measures, or

heading: Employment protection
paragraph: (ii)  complying with, or intending to comply with, an order made under section 75 (1) (d) or an emergency instrument made under section 107 (1) (a) to provide a service or give assistance.

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph:
156
		  (1) An employer may apply in accordance with this section to request that a protected employee to whom section 155 applies be released from deployment or from complying with the order or emergency instrument referred to in subsection (2) (b) (ii) of that section.

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph: (2) An application under this section may be made only on the grounds that the deployment or compliance with the order

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph: (a) unduly interferes with the employer's ability to carry on business, or

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph: (b) otherwise creates undue financial hardship for the employer.

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph: (3) An application under this section must be made

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph: (a) to the local authority, in the form and manner required by the local authority, in the case of a protected employee acting under an emergency instrument made under section 107 (1) (a) [response powers] to provide a service or give assistance, or

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph: (b) to the provincial administrator, in the form and manner required by the provincial administrator, in any other case.

heading: Application to release protected employee
paragraph: (4) An application under this section must include the records, including proof of a matter, required by the local authority or provincial administrator, as applicable.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
157
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorized person" means a person or entity who is any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a regulated entity;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the provincial administrator or a member of the provincial emergency management organization;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a member of an emergency management organization or a member of a multijurisdictional emergency management organization;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an Indigenous governing body;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a participating authority that has entered into an emergency measures agreement;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) a prescribed person or public safety provider, or a person or public safety provider in a prescribed class;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) an individual who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  is a member, officer or employee of a person or entity referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) or (f) of this definition, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  has responsibilities in relation to emergency management;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "essential information" means the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) information necessary to identify a person, including the person's age, date of birth, gender and image;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) information that enables a person to be contacted other than at a place of business;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) information about a person's current or last known location;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) to the extent that it is relevant to whether or how an emergency measure is or may be taken, information about a person's requirements with respect to one or more types of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  necessities,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  transportation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  counselling, health care or social services,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iv)  child care, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (v)  animal care;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) prescribed types of information;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "person needing services" means the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an individual who is believed to be in an area where there is a critical incident or emergency and who may be disproportionately affected, including as a result of intersectional disadvantage or vulnerability;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an individual whose health, safety or well-being is significantly at risk due to a critical incident or emergency;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) an individual who has responsibility for an animal or property that is significantly at risk due to a critical incident or emergency;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sensitive information" means information that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) could reasonably be expected, if disclosed, to compromise the security of critical infrastructure or employees of critical infrastructure owners,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is commercial, financial, labour relations, scientific or technical information of or about a regulated entity,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is a trade secret within the meaning of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) is a prescribed type of information.

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: 158		  (1) Subject to the regulations and subsection (2), an authorized person may do the following:

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (a) collect and use essential information about a person needing services from a family member of, or a person who resides with, the person needing services;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (b) if a person is or may be a person needing services and the person's location is not immediately known, collect and use essential information about the person from any other person who may have information relevant to determining the person's whereabouts;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (c) if a person's health, safety or well-being is significantly at risk due to a critical incident or emergency,

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (i)  request essential information about the person from any other person who may have information about the person, and

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (ii)  collect and use any essential information about the person that is provided to the authorized person as a result of the request;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (d) disclose, to another authorized person, essential information about a person needing services.

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (2) The collection, use and disclosure of essential information may be for one or more of the following purposes only:

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (a) to take an emergency measure;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (b) to locate and contact a person who is or may be a person needing services;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (c) to provide assistance to a person needing services, including assistance that may reduce the person's level of vulnerability;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (d) to protect or reduce risk to the animals or property of a person needing services;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (e) in the case of the disclosure of essential information, a purpose referred to in section 159;

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (f) a prescribed purpose.

heading: Information about persons needing services
paragraph: (3) A person who has custody or control of essential information requested under subsection (1) (c) (i) must, promptly after receiving the request, disclose that information to the authorized person.

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph:
159
		  (1) A person who obtains personal information or sensitive information under this Act must keep the information confidential and not disclose it except as follows:

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (a) for the purpose of administering or enforcing this Act and the regulations;

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (b) for a purpose authorized under this Act, other than section 16 [disclosing and publishing information];

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (c) for the purpose of taking an emergency measure or supporting another person to take an emergency measure;

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (d) in accordance with an agreement made under this Act;

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (e) as required under an enactment of British Columbia or Canada;

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (f) for the purposes of a legal proceeding before a court or tribunal, including a quasi-judicial tribunal;

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (g) to publish or disclose information that, in the opinion of the minister, must be published or disclosed in the public interest.

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (2) Personal information or sensitive information may be disclosed for a purpose referred to in subsection (1)

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (a) without the consent of or notice to the person to whom the information relates, and

heading: Duty to protect confidentiality
paragraph: (b) to a person outside British Columbia, if the person is in a prescribed class of persons.

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph:
160
		  (1) Any Indigenous knowledge of an Indigenous people that is provided in confidence by the Indigenous people in relation to the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty under this Act may be

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) used only for the purposes for which the Indigenous knowledge is provided, and

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) disclosed only as authorized under subsection (2).

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (2) Indigenous knowledge referred to in subsection (1) may be disclosed as follows:
