heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) with the written consent of the Indigenous governing body of the Indigenous people;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) without restriction if the Indigenous knowledge is publicly available;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (c) to a person for the purposes of the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty under this Act if the Indigenous knowledge is necessary for the exercise of the power or performance of the duty as they relate to the purposes for which the Indigenous knowledge was provided;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (d) to legal counsel for the purposes of obtaining legal advice;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (e) by order of a court;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (f) in prescribed circumstances.

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (3) Before disclosing Indigenous knowledge under any of the following provisions, a person must give written notice of the contemplated disclosure to the Indigenous governing body of the Indigenous people that provided the knowledge:

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) subsection (2) (e);

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) if required by regulation, subsection (2) (f).

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (4) If a person discloses Indigenous knowledge under subsection (2) (c), unless subsection (2) (a) or (b) applies, the person must, as soon as practicable after the disclosure, give written notice of the disclosure to an Indigenous governing body that acts on behalf of the Indigenous people that provided the knowledge.

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (5) The following persons may impose conditions on the further disclosure of Indigenous knowledge by the person to whom the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2):

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) a justice, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (e);

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) a prescribed person, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (f).

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph:
161
		  (1) An order or emergency instrument made or direction given under this Act has no effect to the extent that it prevents or interferes with any of the following:

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (a) the chief veterinarian's exercise of a power under the Animal Health Act in relation to an emergency declared under section 59 of that Act;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (b) the minister responsible for the administration of the Environmental Management Act, or a public officer authorized by that minister, in exercising a power under section 87 of that Act in relation to an environmental emergency;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (c) a fire chief, or a person authorized by a fire chief, in exercising a power under section 13 of the Fire Safety Act in relation to an immediate threat to life due to a fire hazard or explosion;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (d) the exercise of a power under section 7 (3) of the Ministry of Energy and Mines Act by the minister responsible for the administration of that Act, or a person's exercise of a power under a regulation made under that section, in relation to controlling and regulating the use and supply of, and the demand for, energy resources in an emergency;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (e) an official in restricting or prohibiting access to a public area under section 51 (1) of the Energy Resource Activities Act or in the exercise of a power under section 52 (1) of that Act in relation to an emergency;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (f) the provincial health officer's exercise of a power under the Public Health Act in relation to an emergency for which the provincial health officer has given notice under section 52 (2) of that Act;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (g) the commission's making of an order under section 125.2 of the Utilities Commission Act in relation to the adoption and administration of reliability standards;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (h) the exercise of a power under a regulation made under section 127 (1) (g) of the Water Sustainability Act by the minister responsible for the administration of that Act, or an engineer's or officer's exercise of a power under section 93 of that Act, in relation to the diversion and use of water;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (i) the comptroller's authorization of a thing to be done under section 91 (4) of the Water Sustainability Act in relation to a risk or hazard;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (j) the exercise of a power under section 11 (1) of the Wildfire Act by the minister responsible for the administration of that Act, or an official's exercise of a power under section 9 (1), (2) or (3), 11 (2), 13 (1) or 16 (1) of that Act, in relation to carrying out fire control;

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (k) a prescribed person's exercise of a prescribed power or type of power in relation to a prescribed type of hazard or an emergency.

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a local authority must not exercise a power or perform a duty under this Act to the extent that it prevents or interferes with the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty by

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (a) the minister or the provincial administrator under this Act, or

heading: Conflict of laws
paragraph: (b) a public officer under another enactment.

heading: Resolving conflicts between laws
paragraph: 162		  If there is a conflict between a provision of this Act, or of an order, emergency instrument or regulation made under this Act, and another Act or regulation, this Act and the order, emergency instrument or regulation made under this Act prevail.

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph:
163
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (a) designating government ministers as lead ministers, based on

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (i)  the types of functions for which government ministers are responsible under the Constitution Act,

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (ii)  the critical infrastructure sectors with which ministries are associated,

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (iii)  the types of expertise held by ministry officials,

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (iv)  the emergency resources available to ministries, or

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (v)  any other criteria;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (b) respecting the responsibilities of government ministers, including lead ministers, in relation to emergency management and the taking, or coordinating the taking, of emergency measures;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (c) respecting the coordination of responsibilities

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (i)  among the provincial administrator and lead ministers, and

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (ii)  among lead ministers, if there is overlap or conflict between the responsibilities of lead ministers;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (d) respecting persons who are or are not critical infrastructure owners for the purposes of this Act;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (e) authorizing the minister to determine who is responsible for performing duties under this Act if multiple persons are critical infrastructure owners with respect to a single system, network, facility or asset that is prescribed as critical infrastructure;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (f) establishing classes of critical infrastructure based on

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (i)  how critical the infrastructure is considered to be,

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (ii)  common characteristics, or

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (iii)  other criteria;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (g) requiring a public sector agency or critical infrastructure owner, or a public sector agency or critical infrastructure owner in a prescribed class, to prepare, maintain and, if applicable, implement one or more of the following:

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (i)  a risk assessment with respect to prescribed types of hazards;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (ii)  an emergency management plan;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (iii)  a business continuity plan;

heading: Provincial matters
paragraph: (h) for the purposes of section 50 [reporting by critical infrastructure owners], respecting the giving of information and records to the provincial administrator by critical infrastructure owners.

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: 164		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: (a) respecting the establishment of, appointment of members to, and maintenance of an emergency management organization by a local authority other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation;

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: (b) respecting the establishment, governance and responsibilities of multijurisdictional emergency management organizations;

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: (c) without limiting paragraph (a) or (b), respecting the terms and conditions of agreements to establish or join multijurisdictional emergency management organizations;

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: (d) providing for the resolution of any conflicts or inconsistencies relating to the exercise of response powers and recovery powers in

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: (i)  an area that is within the jurisdiction of a local authority, and

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: (ii)  an area that is subject to an emergency measures agreement;

heading: Local authority matters
paragraph: (e) imposing prohibitions, requirements, limits and conditions on the exercise, by a local authority, other than the Nisga'a Nation or a treaty first nation, of response powers and recovery powers.

heading: Volunteers
paragraph:
165
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting volunteers as follows:

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (a) respecting the types of actions that are specialized measures for the purposes of this Act;

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (b) respecting the actions that may or may not be undertaken by volunteers in relation to critical incidents or emergencies;

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (c) for the purposes of the definition of "volunteer" in section 1 (1) [definitions], respecting the receipt of compensation, remuneration or other benefits by volunteers;

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (d) respecting the recruitment, management, registration and deployment of volunteers;

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (e) respecting the authorization of public safety providers under section 30 [authorization of public safety providers];

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (f) respecting the training of volunteers, including in respect of

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (i)  training in relation to cultural safety or intersectional disadvantage,

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (ii)  training or qualifications that persons must have before taking a type of specialized measure, and

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (iii)  participation in critical incident or emergency management training and exercise programs, including respecting the payment of fees to participate in programs provided by the provincial emergency management organization;

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (g) respecting the reimbursement of expenses incurred by public safety providers and volunteers, including

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (i)  respecting making and determining claims for reimbursement,

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (ii)  respecting the types of expenses that may, or must not, be reimbursed,

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (iii)  setting a schedule, rate or flat fee or providing any other method for calculating the amount of expenses that may be reimbursed, and

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (iv)  prescribing the maximum amount that will be reimbursed, in total or by type of expense;

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (h) respecting the authorization for the purposes of section 32 (4) [requests for deployment] of persons or entities that register volunteers, other than local authorities or public safety providers, including

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (i)  establishing a process and criteria in relation to applications to be authorized,

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (ii)  respecting the revocation of authorizations, and

heading: Volunteers
paragraph: (iii)  respecting the duties of authorized persons or entities.

heading: Emergency management
paragraph:
166
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting emergency management as follows:

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (a) respecting matters to be assessed under risk assessments;

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (b) respecting standards and procedures for conducting risk assessments and for preparing emergency management plans and business continuity plans, including

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (i)  respecting the sources of information on which assessments or plans are to be based,

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (ii)  respecting the obtaining and incorporating of Indigenous knowledge, local knowledge and other information,

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (iii)  respecting cultural safety and intersectional disadvantage, and

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (iv)  respecting matters that must be considered or addressed;

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (c) respecting the form and content of emergency management plans and business continuity plans;

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (d) for the purposes of section 47 (2) [emergency management planning by local authorities], respecting areas within the jurisdiction of a regional district in respect of which the regional district is not required to prepare a risk assessment or an emergency management plan, or both;

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (e) respecting the review and revision of risk assessments, the comprehensive emergency management plan, emergency management plans and business continuity plans, including

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (i)  requiring reviews according to a schedule or when certain circumstances exist,

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (ii)  respecting standards and procedures for conducting reviews, and

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (iii)  respecting circumstances in which a new assessment or plan must be completed;

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (f) respecting emergency systems and requirements for the provincial emergency management organization and regulated entities to adopt emergency systems;

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (g) establishing, adopting or setting standards respecting emergency management training and exercise programs, including programs in relation to cultural safety or intersectional disadvantage, and respecting qualifications to conduct such programs;

heading: Emergency management
paragraph: (h) requiring persons to conduct or participate in emergency management training and exercise programs, including according to a schedule.

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph:
167
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting consultation and coordination with local authorities and other persons as follows:

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (a) respecting who must be consulted, including

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (i)  providing methods for determining who must be consulted and authorizing the provincial administrator to determine who must be consulted, and

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (ii)  providing for requests for consultation;

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (b) respecting the form and level of consultation required, including

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (i)  procedural matters and the sharing of information,

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (ii)  the stages at which consultation must occur,

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (iii)  the actions that must be taken during or after consultation, and

heading: Consultation and coordination
paragraph: (iv)  the obtaining and incorporating of Indigenous knowledge, local knowledge and other information.

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph:
168
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples as follows:

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (a) respecting who must be consulted, including

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  providing methods for determining who must be consulted and authorizing the provincial administrator to determine who must be consulted, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  providing for requests for consultation or cooperation;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (b) respecting the form and level of consultation or engagement required, including

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  procedural matters and the sharing of information,

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  the stages at which consultation or engagement must occur,

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iii)  the actions that must be taken during or after consultation or engagement, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iv)  the obtaining of Indigenous knowledge and other information;

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (c) respecting the form and level of cooperation required, including

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (i)  procedural matters and the sharing of information,

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (ii)  the actions that must be taken, and

heading: Consultation, engagement and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (iii)  the incorporating of Indigenous knowledge.

heading: Compensation and financial assistance
paragraph:
169
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of Part 7 as follows:

heading: Compensation and financial assistance

paragraph: "CSA Z246.2" means the standard published by the Canadian Standards Association as CSA Z246.2, Emergency preparedness and response for petroleum and natural gas industry systems, as amended from time to time;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "emergency" means an incident classified in accordance with section 10 as a level 1, 2 or 3 incident that requires action by a permit holder to protect persons, property or the environment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "emergency management system" means a system for the control, command and coordination of emergency response operations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "emergency planning zone" means a geographical area that encompasses all the hazard planning zones for an energy resource activity that is the subject of a plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hazard" has the same meaning as in CSA Z246.2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hazard planning distance" means a hazard planning distance within the meaning of section 7;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hazard planning zone" means a geographical area

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) determined by using the hazard planning distance as a radius, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) within which persons, property or the environment may be affected by an emergency;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "incident" has the same meaning as in CSA Z246.2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local authority" means a municipality or a regional district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local Indigenous nation", in relation to a hazard planning zone, means an Indigenous nation that is identified for the hazard planning zone in a manner specified by the regulator;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipal highway" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Transportation Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mutual aid agreement" has the same meaning as in CSA Z246.2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "plan" means a response contingency plan within the meaning of section 5;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "program" means an emergency response program within the meaning of section 3;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualified professional", in relation to a matter, means an individual who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is registered with a regulatory body as defined in section 1 (1) [definitions and interpretation] of the Professional Governance Act, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) through suitable education, experience, accreditation and knowledge, may reasonably be relied on to provide advice within the individual's area of expertise as it relates to the matter;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "rights holder" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Requirements for Consultation and Notification Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "training association" means a safety training association approved by an official.

heading: Application
paragraph: 1.1		  This regulation does not apply in relation to the following:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a Class 1 hydrogen facility as defined in section 1 (1) of the Hydrogen Facility Regulation;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) a Class 2 hydrogen facility as defined in section 1 (1) of the Hydrogen Facility Regulation.

heading: Application and interpretation of CSA Z246.2
paragraph:
2
		  (1) For the purposes of this regulation, a permit holder must comply with CSA Z246.2.

heading: Application and interpretation of CSA Z246.2
paragraph: (2) A reference in a clause of CSA Z246.2 or Annex A of CSA Z246.2 to a term set out in Column 1 of the following table is to be read as a reference to the term set out opposite in Column 2 as that term is defined in this regulation:

heading: Application and interpretation of CSA Z246.2
paragraph: (3) A reference in a clause of CSA Z246.2 or Annex A of CSA Z246.2 to "operator" is to be read as a reference to "permit holder" as defined in the Act.

heading: Application and interpretation of CSA Z246.2
paragraph: (4) Unless the context otherwise requires, a reference to "should" in a clause of CSA Z246.2 is to be read as a reference to "must".

heading: Emergency response program
paragraph:
3
		  (1) A permit holder must prepare and maintain a program in accordance with CSA Z246.2.

heading: Emergency response program
paragraph: (2) A permit holder must review and, if necessary, update the program

heading: Emergency response program
paragraph: (a) at least once every 3 years,

heading: Emergency response program
paragraph: (b) after a significant change occurs in the types of hazards and risks arising from the permit holder's energy resource activities that are the subject of the permit holder's plan,

heading: Emergency response program
paragraph: (c) after an evaluation of the response to a level 3 incident is completed in accordance with CSA Z246.2, and

heading: Emergency response program
paragraph: (d) at any time the permit holder becomes aware of a deficiency in the program that risks the safety of emergency response staff, the permit holder's employees or the public.

heading: Emergency response program
paragraph: (3) A program is prescribed for the purposes of section 38 (1) (b) of the Act.

heading: Training plan
paragraph:
4
		  A permit holder must develop a training plan that takes into account all of the elements referred to in clause A.4.9.2 of Annex A of CSA Z246.2.

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph:
4.1
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: "full-scale exercise" means a full-scale (major) exercise described in Annex A of CSA Z246.2;

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: "LNG facility" has the same meaning as in the Liquefied Natural Gas Facility Regulation;

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: "processing facility" has the same meaning as in the Processing Facility Regulation.

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (2) A permit holder must conduct a full-scale exercise as follows:

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (a) at least once every 3 years;

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (b) before the first time process fluid is introduced to a facility, a pipeline or equipment described in subsection (3);

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (c) at any time required by an official under section 4.3.

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the following facilities, pipelines and equipment require a full-scale exercise in accordance with subsection (2) (b):

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (a) a processing facility;

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (b) an LNG facility;

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (c) a petroleum or natural gas pipeline, other than a petroleum or natural gas pipeline that is part of a gathering system or a fuel gas system;

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (d) any other facility, pipeline or equipment that has

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (i)  a supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system, and

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (ii)  the potential to create a hazard.

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (4) A full-scale exercise is required in relation to the addition of a facility or pipeline or equipment referred to in subsection (3) (a) to (d) to an operating area only if

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (a) a full-scale exercise has not previously been conducted in relation to another facility or pipeline, or equipment, in the operating area that is of a similar type and nature as the facility, pipeline or equipment to be added, or

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (b) the addition of the facility, pipeline or equipment does not increase the hazard planning zone for the energy resource activity.

heading: Full-scale exercise
paragraph: (5) At least 30 days before conducting a full-scale exercise, a permit holder must give the regulator notice that the exercise will be conducted and include with the notice a description of the exercise.

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph:
4.2
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: "functional exercise" means a functional exercise described in Annex A of CSA Z246.2;

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: "tabletop exercise" means a tabletop exercise described in Annex A of CSA Z246.2.

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (2) A permit holder must conduct a tabletop exercise or a functional exercise as follows:

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (a) at least once in each year that a full-scale exercise referred to in section 4.1 is not conducted;

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (b) within 3 months after the first day the permit holder carries out an energy resource activity;

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (c) within 3 months after a change in the permit holder's emergency response staff, if both of the following conditions are met:

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (i)  there is a change in at least 1/3 of the permit holder's emergency response staff since the permit holder last conducted a tabletop exercise or a functional exercise;

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (ii)  none of the new emergency response staff have previously participated in a tabletop exercise or a functional exercise under the permit holder's program for a similar energy resource activity;

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (d) as required by an official under section 4.3.

heading: Tabletop exercise
paragraph: (3) At least 30 days before conducting a tabletop exercise or a functional exercise, a permit holder must give the regulator notice that the exercise will be conducted and include with the notice a description of the exercise.

heading: If official is not satisfied
paragraph:
4.3
		  If an official is not satisfied that a permit holder has conducted an exercise referred to in section 4.1 or 4.2 in accordance with Annex A of CSA Z246.2, the official may require the permit holder to do one or more of the following:

heading: If official is not satisfied
paragraph: (a) conduct the exercise again;

heading: If official is not satisfied
paragraph: (b) provide additional information or training to its employees, directors or officers;

heading: If official is not satisfied
paragraph: (c) implement a system or procedure that the official considers necessary to improve the permit holder's capacity to respond in an emergency.

heading: Regulator may publish
paragraph:
4.4
		  The regulator may publish information relating to a permit holder's conduct of an exercise, including

heading: Regulator may publish
paragraph: (a) whether an official was satisfied with the permit holder's conduct of the exercise, and

heading: Regulator may publish
paragraph: (b) a requirement imposed by an official under section 4.3.

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph:
5
		  (1) Subject to this section, a permit holder must prepare and maintain a plan in accordance with CSA Z246.2.

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (2) If both of the following conditions are met, the permit holder may prepare a single, coordinated plan for more than one of the permit holder's energy resource activities:

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (a) the site-specific hazards and risks of each energy resource activity that would be the subject of a plan are the same;

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (b) the same emergency response staff are assigned, in accordance with the permit holder's emergency management system, to the energy resource activities.

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (3) A permit holder must prepare a plan in 2 parts so that the regulator can make one part of the plan publicly available.

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (4) A permit holder must not include the following information in the part of the plan to be made publicly available:

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (a) personal information, as defined in the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act;

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (b) information the permit holder considers to be confidential business information.

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (5) If part of the emergency planning zone for an energy resource activity is located within an airport zoning area, a plan for the energy resource activity must include contact information for the operator of the airport.

heading: Response contingency plans
paragraph: (6) A plan is prescribed for the purposes of section 38 (1) (b) of the Act.

heading: Response contingency plans required
paragraph: 6		  A permit holder must not carry out an energy resource activity that is the subject of a plan unless the permit holder has, in respect of a plan,

heading: Response contingency plans required
paragraph: (a) determined that there is no emergency planning zone, or

heading: Response contingency plans required
paragraph: (b) complied with section 5.

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph:
7
		  (1) For the purposes of this regulation, a hazard planning distance is

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (a) the greatest horizontal distance calculated under subsection (2) or (3), as applicable, in respect of an energy resource activity that is the subject of a plan, and

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (b) measured from the site of the energy resource activity.

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (2) For a hazard involving hydrogen sulphide, the hazard planning distance must be equal to or greater than one of the following:

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (a) a distance recommended for the hazard in an assessment conducted by a qualified professional;

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (b) a distance determined for the hazard using a table, software application or other resource evaluated and approved by a qualified professional;

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (c) a distance determined in accordance with Schedule A, B or C, as applicable.

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (3) For a hazard other than a hazard involving hydrogen sulphide, the hazard planning distance must be equal to or greater than one of the following:

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (a) a distance recommended for the hazard in an assessment conducted by a qualified professional;

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (b) a distance determined for the hazard using a table, software application or other resource evaluated and approved by a qualified professional;

heading: Hazard planning distances
paragraph: (c) unless the hazard is a well, pipeline, or other energy resource activity with a fluid capacity greater than 200 m3, a distance recommended for the hazard by the Emergency Response Guidebook published by Transport Canada, as amended from time to time.

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A permit holder must review and, if necessary, update the information included in a plan

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (a) at least once a year,

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (b) after an evaluation of the response to an emergency is completed in accordance with CSA Z246.2,

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (c) if the site-specific hazards and risks of the energy resource activity that is the subject of the plan change significantly,

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (d) at any time the permit holder becomes aware of a deficiency in the plan that risks the safety of emergency response staff, the permit holder's employees, or the public, and

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (e) if a mutual aid agreement is cancelled, expires or is otherwise terminated.

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (2) As part of the review referred to in subsection (1), a permit holder must

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (a) review the information included in the plan,

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (b) make reasonable efforts to determine whether the persons or other entities referred to in section 13 (1) (a) to (g) have changed, and

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (c) consider any responses to requests under section 13 (2) (d) (ii) received after the permit holder submitted the plan or updated information to the regulator.

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (3) If, as a result of reviewing the plan, the permit holder determines that the persons or other entities referred to in section 13 (1) (a) to (g) have changed, the permit holder must, as soon as possible, give the information set out in section 13 (2) respecting the plan to the persons or other entities not previously given the information.

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (4) If, as a result of updating the plan, the information given under section 13 (2) has changed, the permit holder must, as soon as possible, give the updated information to those persons or other entities referred to in section 13 (1) (a) to (g) who are affected by the change.

heading: Review and update of plans
paragraph: (5) A permit holder must give information that is updated under subsection (1) to all emergency response staff to whom powers and duties are assigned in accordance with the permit holder's emergency management system.

heading: Access to plans
paragraph:
9
		  A permit holder must make a copy of the permit holder's plans, in paper or electronic form, available to emergency response staff as follows:

heading: Access to plans
paragraph: (a) at the permit holder's head office, a copy of each of the permit holder's plans;

heading: Access to plans
paragraph: (b) at the permit holder's regional offices, a copy of each plan relevant to the regional office.

heading: Incident classification and management
paragraph:
10
		  (1) Immediately after a permit holder becomes aware of an incident, the permit holder must classify the incident according to the event or consequence in the Incident Classification Matrix in Schedule D that most closely describes the most severe event or consequence of the incident.

heading: Incident classification and management
paragraph: (2) A permit holder must adopt the Incident Command System as the permit holder's emergency management system.

heading: During emergencies
paragraph:
11
		  (1) When an emergency occurs, a permit holder must do the following:

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (a) immediately respond to the emergency in accordance with the permit holder's plan;

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (b) notify local Indigenous nations as soon as possible, after the permit holder has taken any immediate actions necessary

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (i)  for public safety, or

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (ii)  to minimize immediate environmental impacts;

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (c) notify the regulator within one hour of becoming aware of the incident.

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (2) During an emergency involving a special sour well, a permit holder must do all of the following:

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (a) ensure that a person certified in accordance with subsection (4) is available and equipped to ignite the well within the time limits set out in the plan in respect of which the emergency planning zone was determined;

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (b) ensure that a dual ignition system is on site during

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (i)  drilling or completion operations, or

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (ii)  workover operations being carried out at any time when the wellhead is not in place;

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (c) ensure that a person authorized to ignite flammable liquids or ignitable vapours released from the well is on site.

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), a sour well is special if either of the following applies:

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (a) the hydrogen sulphide release rate from the well is equal to or greater than 2.0 m3/s;

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (b) the hydrogen sulphide release rate from the well is less than 2.0 m3/s but greater than 0.5 m3/s and the well is located within a distance that is twice the hazard planning distance from the corporate boundaries of an urban centre.

heading: During emergencies
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (2) (a), the person must have a vapour plume ignition certificate issued by a training association.

heading: Notify regulator after a minor incident
paragraph:
11.1
		  A permit holder must notify the regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of an incident classified in accordance with section 10 as a minor incident.

heading: Emergency communication system
paragraph:
12
		  Each year, a permit holder must

heading: Emergency communication system
paragraph: (a) test the permit holder's procedures for communication during an emergency to ensure the procedures are effective, and

heading: Emergency communication system
paragraph: (b) ensure any equipment needed by the permit holder for communication during an emergency is functional.

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph:
13
		  (1) Before submitting a plan to the regulator, a permit holder must give the information set out in subsection (2) to the following persons or other entities:

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (a) a person who occupies land that is located within the emergency planning zone;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (b) a local authority, if

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (i)  any part of the emergency planning zone is located within the boundary of the local authority's territory, or

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (ii)  the local authority is identified in the plan as a party to a mutual aid agreement;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (c) the government of Canada, if an existing building or structure owned by the government of Canada is within the emergency planning zone;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (d) a local Indigenous nation;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (e) a rights holder, if an area subject to a right of the rights holder is located within the emergency planning zone;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (f) the ministry of the minister responsible for the administration of the Transportation Act and the municipal council, if any part of the emergency planning zone is located within a municipality and within the right of way of an arterial highway or municipal highway;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (g) a health authority, if any part of the emergency planning zone is located within the geographic area for which the health authority is responsible;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (h) the operator of an airport, if part of the airport zoning area for the airport is located within the emergency planning zone.

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (2) The information given under subsection (1) must include all of the following:

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the permit holder;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (b) a map that shows the location of the emergency planning zone in relation to

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (i)  roads, including energy resource roads,

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (ii)  dwellings, schools and public facilities, and

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (iii)  private property the permit holder has identified in a plan as property that may potentially be used by the public in an emergency;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (c) a description of

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (i)  the site-specific hazards and risks of the energy resource activity that is the subject of the plan,

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (ii)  how the permit holder's response to an emergency may affect the person or other entity receiving the information,

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (iii)  how the permit holder will notify the person or other entity receiving the information if and when the permit holder thinks the person or other entity should shelter in place or evacuate in an emergency, and

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (iv)  how the person or other entity receiving the information can get to safety in an emergency;

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (d) a statement requesting that the person or other entity receiving the information provide to the permit holder

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (i)  the name and contact information of a contact person,

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (ii)  a description of how the person or other entity may be affected by an emergency, and

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (iii)  if the person or other entity is a local Indigenous nation, a description of any sites or areas in the emergency planning zone that are likely to be in use by members of the local Indigenous nation.

heading: Obligation to provide information - general
paragraph: (3) If a permit holder receives a response to a request under subsection (2) (d) (ii) or (iii) before submitting a plan to the regulator, the permit holder must consider the response in the preparation of the plan.

heading: Obligation to provide information - temporary change
paragraph: 14		  (1) This section applies if both of the following circumstances exist:

heading: Obligation to provide information - temporary change
paragraph: (a) there is a change in operations that temporarily increases the site-specific hazards and risks of an energy resource activity that is the subject of a plan;

heading: Obligation to provide information - temporary change
paragraph: (b) in respect of the plan, a permit holder determines an expanded emergency planning zone because of the temporary increase in the site-specific hazards and risks of the energy resource activity.

heading: Obligation to provide information - temporary change
paragraph: (2) In the circumstances set out in subsection (1), a permit holder must give a person or other entity referred to in section 13 (1) (a) to (g) the following information:

heading: Obligation to provide information - temporary change
paragraph: (a) all of the information described in section 13 (2) if the person or other entity located within the expanded emergency planning zone was not previously given that information;

heading: Obligation to provide information - temporary change
paragraph: (b) only the information described in section 13 (2) (b) and (c) (i) and (ii) if the person or other entity located within the expanded emergency planning zone was previously given the information described in section 13 (2).

heading: Submission of information to regulator
paragraph:
15
		  (1) Within 14 days after appointing a coordinator in accordance with clause 4.6 of CSA Z246.2, a permit holder must submit to the regulator the name and contact information of the coordinator.

heading: Submission of information to regulator
paragraph: (2) Within 60 days after completing an exercise described in sections 4.1 or 4.2, a permit holder must submit to the regulator the report described in section 16 (2).

heading: Submission of information to regulator
paragraph: (3) Within 30 days after preparing a plan under section 5, a permit holder must submit to the regulator, in both paper and electronic form, a copy of the plan.

heading: Submission of information to regulator
paragraph: (4) Within 30 days after reviewing a plan under section 8, a permit holder must submit to the regulator, in both paper and electronic form, the following, as applicable:

heading: Submission of information to regulator
paragraph: (a) a copy of any information updated under section 8 (1);

heading: Submission of information to regulator
paragraph: (b) if no information is updated under section 8 (1), a record showing the date the plan was reviewed and the name of the permit holder's representative who is responsible for the review.

heading: Reports and records
paragraph:
16
		  (1) A permit holder must prepare and maintain a written record of participants in training or in an exercise described in sections 4.1 or 4.2.

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (2) On completing an exercise described in sections 4.1 or 4.2, a permit holder must prepare a report that does all of the following:

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (a) states whether the objectives of the exercise were met;

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (b) makes recommendations for improvement, including improvement to the exercise plan or training plan;

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (c) includes a strategy to implement the recommendations for improvement referred to in paragraph (b).

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (2.1) If spillage that is reportable under section 91.2 (1) (a) of the Environmental Management Act occurs in relation to an energy resource activity, a permit holder for the energy resource activity must provide a written report to the regulator at the following times:

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (a) within 30 days of the date on which the spillage was discovered;

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (b) at least once every 30 days after the first report, until the spillage is contained and eliminated, and

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (c) within 30 days of the date on which the spillage has been contained and eliminated.

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (3) A permit holder must prepare a report of the results of an evaluation of a response to an emergency and maintain the report until the permit for the energy resource activity that is the subject of the plan is cancelled by the regulator or declared by the regulator to be spent.

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (4) A report under subsection (3) must include

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (a) a description of the emergency, including the cause or suspected cause,

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (b) a description of the permit holder's response to the emergency, and

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (c) an assessment of the permit holder's response.

heading: Reports and records
paragraph: (5) A report or a record required by this regulation or CSA Z246.2 is prescribed for the purposes of section 38 (1) (a) of the Act.

heading: Information in writing
paragraph:
17
		  Information required to be given or submitted under this regulation must be given or submitted in writing and, except for the information required by section 15 (3) and (4), may be in either paper or electronic form.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph:
18
		  (1) An official may exempt a permit holder from complying with one or more provisions of this regulation if the official is satisfied that, in the circumstances,

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) compliance with the provision or provisions is not reasonably practicable, or

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) the exemption is in the public interest.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (2) In granting an exemption under subsection (1), an official may impose any conditions on the exemption the official considers necessary.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: 1 For a proposed well, the maximum gas rate (AOF) values and maximum H2S concentrations for each H2S-bearing formation must be determined for each of at least 5 wells drilled and tested in an analogous geological area or pool within 5 km of the proposed well.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: 2 The H2S release rates for all potential H2S-bearing formations in the proposed well must be determined based on the highest AOF and highest H2S concentration for each formation and the sum of the H2S release rates for all the formations that will be open to the well bore during drilling operations.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: 3 If appropriate data does not exist or is otherwise inadequate, the hazard planning distance is 3 km.

paragraph: Completion or re-completion operations
