paragraph: (5) The eligible person must make the request in writing and must identify the error the eligible person believes was made or the other grounds on which a review is requested.

heading: Review by review official
paragraph: (6) On receipt by the review official of a request under subsection (1), the determination to be reviewed as a result of the request

heading: Review by review official
paragraph: (a) is stayed, if the determination is an administrative penalty imposed under section 63, and

heading: Review by review official
paragraph: (b) is not stayed, if the determination is not an administrative penalty referred to in paragraph (a), unless the review official orders that the determination is stayed.

heading: Review by review official
paragraph: (7) The review official may conduct a written, electronic or oral review, or any combination of them, as the review official, in the review official's sole discretion, considers appropriate.

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph:
71
		  (1) As soon as practicable after receiving a request under section 70 (1), the review official must

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (a) confirm, vary or rescind the determination, and

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (b) notify, in writing, the eligible person of the following:

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (i)  the review official's decision;

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (ii)  the reasons for the decision;

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (iii)  the eligible person's right to appeal the decision under section 72.

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (2) If the review official varies a determination under subsection (1) so that

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (a) a permit is amended and the amendment changes the effect of the permit on the land of the land owner, or

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: (b) a permit is issued that locates an operating area on the land of a land owner,

heading: Powers of review official
paragraph: the review official must notify the land owner of the amendment or issuance in accordance with section 25 (4) or 31 (9), as applicable.

heading: Appeal
paragraph:
72
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), an eligible person may appeal to the appeal tribunal

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (a) a decision made under section 71, if the eligible person was a party to the review under that section, and

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (b) a determination, if the eligible person has not, by the date the person commences the appeal, applied under section 70 (1) for a review of the determination.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (2) A land owner of land on which an operating area is located may appeal a determination under this section only on the basis that the determination was made without due regard to

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (a) a submission previously made by the land owner under section 22 (5) or 31 (2) of this Act, or

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (b) a written report submitted under section 24 (1) (c) or 31 (6).

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the commencement of an appeal does not operate as a stay or suspend the operation of the determination or decision being appealed, unless the appeal tribunal orders otherwise.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (4) The commencement of an appeal with respect to an administrative penalty operates as a stay of the determination that imposed the penalty or the decision that did not rescind the penalty, unless the appeal tribunal orders otherwise.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (5) The appellant and the regulator are parties to an appeal, and

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (a) if a person to whom an order under section 49 (1) has been issued files an appeal, the following persons, as applicable and if different from the appellant, are also parties to the appeal:

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (i)  in the case of an order with respect to an energy resource activity permitted, or an off-site environmental mitigation activity required, by a permit, or a related activity of either of those activities, the permit holder;

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of an order with respect to a related activity of an application for a permit under section 24, the applicant,

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (b) if a land owner of land on which an operating area is located files an appeal, the permit holder with respect to the energy resource activity is also a party to the appeal,

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (c) if an applicant for a permit appeals a refusal to issue a permit, a land owner notified by the applicant under section 22 (2) is, on request, also a party to the appeal, and

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (d) if a permit holder appeals a refusal to amend a permit, the land owner of the land on which an operating area is located is, on request, also a party to the appeal.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (6) On an appeal under subsection (1), the appeal tribunal may

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (a) confirm, vary, or rescind the decision made under section 71 or the determination, or

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (b) send the matter back, with directions, to the review official who made the decision or to the person who made the determination, as applicable.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (7) Despite the application of section 24 (1) of the Administrative Tribunals Act to the appeal tribunal, a land owner must file a notice of appeal within 15 days of the day the determination being appealed was made.

heading: Publication
paragraph: 73		  The regulator may direct a person to publish, at the person's own cost, the facts relating to the imposition of an administrative penalty or to an order issued under Division 2 of Part 5, if the person's rights of review and appeal have elapsed without the penalty or order being rescinded or dealt with as described in section 72 (6) (b).

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph:
74
		  (1) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it necessary or in the public interest, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may order a pipeline permit holder to do any or all of the following:

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph: (a) to extend or improve its pipeline for the junction with a pipeline of a person or local authority distributing or authorized to distribute gas to the public;

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph: (b) to sell gas to the person or local authority referred to in paragraph (a), if to do so would not impair the pipeline permit holder's ability to render adequate service to its existing customers;

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph: (c) for the purposes in paragraph (a), to construct pipelines to communities immediately adjacent to its pipeline, if the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers that the construction would not place an undue burden on the pipeline permit holder.

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, in an order under subsection (1),

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph: (a) may order that a person other than a pipeline permit holder referred to in that subsection must pay the costs, or a portion of the costs, incurred in carrying out the order, or

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph: (b) may approve the payment of any of those costs from the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council may order extension of pipeline
paragraph: (3) If an order is made under subsection (1), the regulator must amend under section 26 (1) the pipeline permit holder's permit to the extent necessary to make the permit consistent with the order.

heading: Special projects
paragraph:
75
		  (1) The regulator, on its own initiative or on application by a permit holder or an applicant for a permit, may designate, by order or in a permit, any of the following as a special project:

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (a) the development or production of petroleum, natural gas, or both, from a field or pool or portion of a field or pool, using repressuring, recycling, pressure maintenance or any other technique to enhance recovery;

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (b) the application of innovative technology, as defined by regulation;

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (c) an innovative method of carrying out energy resource activities and related activities;

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (c.1) the development or use of a storage reservoir;

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (d) any other prescribed energy resource activity or method of carrying out an energy resource activity.

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (2) The regulator may

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (a) make a designation under subsection (1) with or without conditions, and

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (b) cancel, suspend or amend a designation

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (i)  at the request of the permit holder to whom the designation was given,

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (ii)  if it appears to the regulator that there has been a contravention of this Act, the regulations, a permit, an authorization or an order respecting the designation or a condition of the designation,

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (iii)  if the regulator considers that the designation is spent, or

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (iv)  if the regulator considers that the designation is no longer appropriate, including, without limitation, for reasons of

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (A) public safety,

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (B) protection of the environment, or

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (C) conservation of petroleum and natural gas resources.

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (3) A permit holder with a permit for an energy resource activity that has been designated as a special project under subsection (1) may apply to the regulator for other than normal spacing under section 65.1 of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act.

heading: Special projects
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of a special project or of special projects generally, the Lieutenant Governor in Council and the board may each, in exercising a regulation-making power under this Act, make a regulation that is contrary to or inconsistent with a provision of this Act.

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: 76		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), a person must not

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (a) construct

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (i)  a highway, road or railway,

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (ii)  an underground communication or power line, or

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (iii)  any other prescribed work, or

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (b) carry out a prescribed activity

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: along, over or under a pipeline or within a prescribed distance of a pipeline unless

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (c) the pipeline permit holder agrees in writing to the construction or the carrying out of the prescribed activity, either specifically or by reference to a class of construction projects or activities,

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (d) the regulator, by order issued under subsection (2), approves the construction or the carrying out of the prescribed activity, either specifically or by reference to a class of construction projects or activities, or

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (e) the construction or prescribed activity is carried out in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (2) The regulator, on application by a person referred to in subsection (1), may issue an order for the purposes of subsection (1) (d) and in doing so may impose any conditions that the regulator considers necessary to protect the pipeline.

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (3) The regulator must approve

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (a) the construction referred to in subsection (1) (a), and

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (b) the carrying out of a prescribed activity under subsection (1) (b)

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: by the government or a municipality, but may impose conditions referred to in subsection (2) in the order issued under that subsection.

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (4) The regulator, for the purposes of deciding whether to issue an order under subsection (1) or impose conditions under subsection (2), may require a pipeline permit holder to submit information regarding the pipeline permit holder's pipeline.

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (5) The regulator may order a pipeline permit holder whose pipeline is the subject of an order issued under subsection (2) to do one or both of the following:

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (a) with the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, relocate the pipeline to facilitate the construction or prescribed activity approved by the order issued under subsection (2);

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (b) take the actions specified in the order that the regulator considers necessary to protect the pipeline.

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (6) In relation to an order of the regulator referred to in subsection (5), the Lieutenant Governor in Council

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (a) may order that a person other than the pipeline permit holder must pay the costs, or a portion of the costs, incurred in carrying out the regulator's order, or

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (b) may approve the payment of any of those costs from the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Pipeline crossings
paragraph: (7) If there is an inconsistency between an order or an approval made under subsection (6) and a regulation made under section 99 (1) (m.1), the order or approval prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Registry
paragraph:
77
		  The regulator must maintain a registry containing the prescribed information about energy resource activities.

heading: Correction or clarification of a decision
paragraph:
78
		  (1) In this section, "decision" means any determination, declaration, order, finding or other decision made under this Act by the regulator.

heading: Correction or clarification of a decision
paragraph: (2) If the regulator makes a decision, the regulator may

heading: Correction or clarification of a decision
paragraph: (a) correct a typographical, an arithmetical or another similar error in the decision, and

heading: Correction or clarification of a decision
paragraph: (b) correct an obvious error or omission in the decision.

heading: Correction or clarification of a decision
paragraph: (3) If the regulator corrects a decision under this section, the regulator must notify the person who is the subject of the decision and the correction does not take effect until that notification is given.

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph:
79
		  (1) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), all documents that are required or permitted under this Act to be given to or served on a person must be given or served in one of the following ways:

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (a) by leaving a copy with the person;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (b) if the person is a permit holder, an authorization holder or the holder of an authorization under section 138 of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act,

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (i)  by leaving a copy with an agent of that person,

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (ii)  by sending a copy by ordinary mail or registered mail to the address at which that person carries on business,

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (iii)  by sending a copy by electronic mail to the electronic mail address provided by that person,

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (iv)  by leaving a copy in a mailbox or mail slot for the address at which that person carries on business, or

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (v)  by attaching a copy to a door or other conspicuous place at the address at which that person carries on business;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (c) by transmitting a copy to a facsimile number provided as an address for service by the person;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (d) by any other prescribed method of service.

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (2) A document given or served in accordance with subsection (1), (3) or (4) is deemed to be received as follows:

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (a) if given or served by sending a copy by ordinary or registered mail, on the 5th day after it is mailed;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (b) if given or served by sending a copy by electronic mail, on the 3rd day after it is sent;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (c) if given or served by leaving a copy in a mailbox or mail slot, on the 3rd day after it is left;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (d) if given or served by attaching a copy to a door or other conspicuous place, on the 3rd day after it is attached;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (e) if given or served by transmitting a copy by facsimile, on the 3rd day after it is transmitted;

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (f) if given or served by any other method of service prescribed under subsection (1) (d), as prescribed.

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (3) The regulator, on application by an applicant, may authorize the applicant to serve a document on a person by sending a copy of the document by registered mail to the last known address of the person if the regulator is satisfied that the applicant has made a reasonable attempt to serve that person in accordance with subsection (1) but has been unable to effect the service.

heading: How to serve documents and notices
paragraph: (4) The regulator may serve a notice, required under section 25 (4), 26 (7) or 31 (9) or (11) to be provided to a land owner, by sending a copy of the notice by registered mail to the last known address of the land owner if the regulator is satisfied that service under subsection (1) of this section is impracticable in the circumstances.

heading: Opportunity to be heard
paragraph: 80		  (1) In any circumstances in which, under this Act, an opportunity to be heard is provided, the regulator may conduct a written, electronic or oral hearing, or any combination of them, as the regulator, in its sole discretion, considers appropriate.

heading: Opportunity to be heard
paragraph: (2) The regulator may make rules respecting the circumstances and place in which and the process by which written, electronic or oral hearings may be conducted under subsection (1) and specifying the form and content of materials to be provided for written, electronic or oral hearings.

heading: False or misleading statements
paragraph:
81
		  A person must not make a false or misleading statement in any application or other record submitted under this Act, or otherwise make a false statement to, or mislead or attempt to mislead, a person exercising a power or performing a duty or function under this Act.

heading: Compliance with orders
paragraph:
82
		  A person to whom an order under this Act applies must comply with the order.

heading: Application of Act to Muskwa-Kechika Management Area
paragraph:
83
		  If there is a conflict or inconsistency between this Act and the Muskwa-Kechika Management Area Act, the Muskwa-Kechika Management Area Act prevails.

heading: Relationship with aboriginal and treaty rights
paragraph: 84		  For greater certainty, the provisions of this Act are intended to respect aboriginal and treaty rights in a manner consistent with section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Time limit for commencing a prosecution
paragraph:
85
		  (1) The time limit for laying an information to commence a prosecution for an offence under this Act is

heading: Time limit for commencing a prosecution
paragraph: (a) 3 years after the date on which the act or omission that is alleged to constitute the offence occurred, or

heading: Time limit for commencing a prosecution
paragraph: (b) if the commissioner issues a certificate described in subsection (2), 3 years after the date on which the commissioner learned of the act or omission referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Time limit for commencing a prosecution
paragraph: (2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the commissioner certifying the date referred to in subsection (1) (b) is proof of that date.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
86
		  (1) A person who contravenes section 21, 35 (1), 36 (1), 37 (1) or (2), 39 (3), 40, 61 or 81, or in relation to an order issued under section 49, section 82, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 500 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 3 years, or to both.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes section 35 (3) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 000 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 2 years, or to both.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) A person who contravenes section 34, 38 (1) or 39 (1), or in relation to an order issued under section 53 (2) (a), section 82, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $500 000 or to imprisonment for not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (4) A person who contravenes section 35 (2) or 76 (1), or in relation to an order issued under a section not referred to in subsections (1) to (3) of this section, section 82, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $100 000.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (5) A person who contravenes section 37 (3) or 60 (1) or (2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $25 000.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (6) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide by regulation that

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) a contravention of a regulation is an offence, and

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) a person convicted of an offence for a contravention of a regulation is liable to a fine not exceeding a maximum amount, or to imprisonment not exceeding a maximum length, or to both.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (7) If the maximum fine or imprisonment provided by a regulation under subsection (6) (b) is less than that provided by a provision of this Act, the regulation prevails.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (8) If a contravention continues for more than one day, the offender is liable to a separate penalty, without notice and without a separate count being laid, for each day that the contravention occurs.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (9) In a prosecution for an offence under this Act, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by the defendant's contractor, employee or agent.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (10) Subsection (9) applies even if the contractor, employee or agent has not been identified or prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (11) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, a director or officer of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence also commits the offence.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (12) If a person commits an offence under this Act, any other person who

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) is directly or indirectly responsible for the act or omission that constitutes the offence, and

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) is a contractor, employee or agent of the person or of an other person described in paragraph (a)

heading: Offences
paragraph: also commits the offence.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (13) Due diligence, mistake of fact and officially induced error are defences to a prosecution under this Act.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) a corporation referred to in subsection (11), or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) a person referred to in subsection (12),

heading: Offences
paragraph: has not committed an offence under this Act as a result of subsection (13), the other persons referred to in subsections (11) and (12) may be found guilty of an offence, subject to subsection (13).

heading: Offences
paragraph: (15) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: 87		  (1) Subject to section 63 (3), a proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under this Part does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: (2) If the regulator imposes an administrative penalty on a person, a prosecution for an offence under this Act for the same contravention may not be brought against the person.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph:
88
		  (1) If the regulator considers that a person is not complying, or has not complied, with an order issued under this Act, the regulator may apply to the Supreme Court for either or both of the following:

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (a) an order directing the person to comply with the order or restraining the person from violating the order;

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (b) an order directing the directors and officers of the person to cause the person to comply with or to stop violating the order.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (2) On application by the regulator under this section, the Supreme Court may make an order it considers appropriate.

heading: Court order to comply
paragraph:
89
		  If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, then, in addition to any punishment the court may impose, the court may order the person to comply with the provision.

heading: Restitution
paragraph:
90
		  If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, then, in addition to any other penalty, the court may order the person to pay compensation or make restitution.

heading: Court orders
paragraph:
91
		  If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, then, in addition to any other punishment that may be imposed, the court may, by order, do one or more of the following:

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (a) prohibit the person from doing anything that may result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (b) direct the person to take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment or public safety that results or may result from the act or omission that constituted the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (c) direct the person to publish, at the person's own cost, the facts relating to the conviction;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (d) direct the person to compensate the regulator for all or part of the cost of any remedial or preventative action taken by or on behalf of the regulator as a result of the act or omission that constituted the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (e) direct the person to pay court costs;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (f) direct the person to pay the costs of the investigation.

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph:
92
		  (1) If the court convicts a person of an offence under this Act, the court may increase a fine imposed on the person by an amount equal to the court's estimation of the amount of the monetary benefit acquired by or that accrued to the person as a result of the regulator of the offence.

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (2) A fine increased under subsection (1)

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (a) applies despite any provision that provides for a maximum fine, and

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (b) is in addition to any other fine under this Act.

heading: Recovery of debts due
paragraph:
93
		  An amount that a person is required under this Act, other than section 18, to pay to the regulator or the government is a debt due by that person to the government or the regulator, as the case may be, and the debt may be recovered by the government or the regulator in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Certificate of debts due
paragraph:
93.1
		  (1) If a person fails to pay an amount owing to the regulator under this Act, other than section 18, the commissioner may issue, and file with a court having jurisdiction, a certificate specifying the amount owed and the name of the person who owes it.

heading: Certificate of debts due
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an amount owing to the government under this Act, the minister may issue, and file with a court having jurisdiction, a certificate specifying the amount owed and the name of the person who owes it.

heading: Certificate of debts due
paragraph: (3) A certificate filed under this section has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on the certificate, as if it were a judgment of the court in favour of the regulator or the government, as the case may be, for the recovery of a debt in the amount specified in the certificate against the person named in the certificate.

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph:
94
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) In making a regulation under this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may do one or more of the following:

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) delegate a matter to a person, with or without directions on how the delegated power is to be exercised;

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) confer a discretion on a person;

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) make different regulations for different persons, places, things, decisions, transactions, activities or circumstances.

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph: (2.1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations establishing criteria that a person must use when exercising a discretionary or delegated power conferred on the person by a regulation under this Division.

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation defining a word or expression used but not defined in this Act.

heading: General power to make regulations
paragraph: (4) Sections 95 to 105.1 do not limit the authority of the Lieutenant Governor in Council to make regulations under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Policies and permitting authority of the regulator
paragraph: 95		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting policies and procedures to be followed by the regulator in conducting its affairs, exercising its powers and discretion, carrying out its functions and duties and discharging its responsibilities.

heading: Policies and permitting authority of the regulator
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of section 25 (1.1).

heading: Criteria for exercise of discretionary powers
paragraph:
96
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the criteria that a person must use in exercising a discretionary power conferred on the person under this Act.

heading: Criteria for exercise of discretionary powers
paragraph: (2) Criteria prescribed under subsection (1) are in addition to any criteria required by this Act.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph:
97
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the carrying out of any energy resource activity or related activity at any point within a specified distance of any boundary, roadway, road allowance, right of way, building of any prescribed type or any specified works;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) despite anything in the Local Government Act and the Community Charter, prohibiting the construction of a building or structure within a specified distance of a well, pipeline or facility, if the Lieutenant Governor in Council is satisfied that the prohibition is necessary to protect the public.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: 98		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the exemption of a person, class of persons, place, thing, transaction or activity from a provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (2) In making a regulation under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make the exemption subject to conditions.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations restricting the regulator's authority

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) to exempt a person or class of persons from section 22 or from a requirement referred to in section 36, or

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) to authorize an official to exempt a person from a provision referred to in section 103 (2).

heading: Administrative penalties

102

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph:
103
		  (1) For the purposes of environmental protection and management, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting actions that a permit holder and a person carrying out an energy resource activity or an off-site environmental mitigation activity must take or refrain from taking to protect or effectively manage the environment.

paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting actions that a permit holder and a person carrying out an energy resource activity or an off-site environmental mitigation activity must take or refrain from taking with respect to any of the following:

paragraph: (k) wildlife trees;

paragraph: (l) commercial timber;

heading: Environmental protection and management

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (o) biodiversity;

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (p) invasive plants, as identified under section 104 (3) (c);

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (q) resource features;

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (r) range;

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (s) forest resources;

heading: Environmental protection and management

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (v) ungulate winter ranges, as established under section 104 (1) (a) (i);

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (w) wildlife habitat areas, as established under section 104 (1) (a) (ii);

heading: Environmental protection and management
paragraph: (x) fisheries sensitive watersheds, as established under section 104 (1) (a) (iv).

paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

paragraph: 207		  This Act comes into force by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Energy Resource Activities Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "affected permit holder", in relation to an energy resource road, means a permit holder whose rights under the permit might be affected by construction of the road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "affected rights holder", in relation to an energy resource road, means a "rights holder" as defined in section 1 of the Requirements for Consultation and Notification Regulation whose rights under the applicable instrument might be affected by construction of the road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "construction", in respect of an energy resource road, includes modifications to the road within the road right of way;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "deactivate", in relation to an energy resource road, means deactivate in accordance with Part 6;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "engineered retaining wall" means a retaining wall greater than 1.5 m in height;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish stream" has the same meaning as in the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local Indigenous nation", in relation to an energy resource road, means an Indigenous nation that is identified for the road in a manner specified by the regulator;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "maintain", in relation to an energy resource road, means maintain in accordance with the provisions of Part 3 respecting maintenance or restoration;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "major culvert" means a culvert crossing a stream or wetland that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is one of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a pipe having a diameter of 2 000 mm or greater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a pipe arch having a span greater than 2 130 mm;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  an open bottom arch having a span greater than 2 130 mm, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has a design discharge rate of 6 m3 per second or greater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "modification", in relation to an energy resource road, means the widening of the running surface of the road, the realigning of a portion of the road or the reconstructing of a portion of a road, and includes the installing or replacing of a bridge or major culvert associated with the road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "motor vehicle" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Motor Vehicle Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "primary activity" means an energy resource activity or a related activity other than the construction, maintenance, operation or use of an energy resource road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protection measures" means sections 11 and 12 of the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualified person" means, in relation to a specified duty, a person who has the qualifications specified by the regulator to perform that duty safely and properly;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road permit" means a permit that includes permission to construct or maintain an energy resource road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road permit holder" means a permit holder of a road permit and a person who is otherwise required to maintain an energy resource road or was required, immediately before the coming into force of this regulation, to maintain an energy resource road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road prism", in relation to a road, means an area consisting of the road surface and any cut slope, ditch and road fill;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road right of way", in relation to an energy resource road, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the area that is shown or described in the permit as the road corridor within which the energy resource road may be constructed or modified, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if the permit does not show or describe the area within which the energy resource road may be constructed or modified, the area 17.5 m of either side of the centre line of the energy resource road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "roadwork area", in relation to an energy resource road, means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the road right of way;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an area that is adjacent to the road right of way and has been used for construction, operation or maintenance of the road under a permit or authorization held by the road permit holder;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream" has the same meaning as in the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream channel" has the same meaning as in the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "traffic control device" means a gate, signal or notice that regulates the operation of a motor vehicle and includes informational, cautionary, restrictive and prohibitory signals and notices;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wetland" has the same meaning as in the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation.

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: 2		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the following are prescribed for the purposes of paragraph (g) of the definition of "energy resource activity" in section 1 (2) of the Act:

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: (a) a road or portion of a road that is constructed or maintained to facilitate the carrying out of a primary activity;

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: (b) a road or portion of a road that was constructed before June 3, 2013 under the Land Act, the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act or the Pipeline Act and has been used to facilitate the carrying out of a primary activity.

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a road that

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: (a) has been deactivated, or

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: (b) is required to be maintained under an enactment other than

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: (i)  this regulation, and

heading: Energy resource roads prescribed
paragraph: (ii)  an Act referred to in subsection (1) (b).

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: 3		  A person applying for a permit, or an amendment to a permit, to construct or maintain an energy resource road must submit to the regulator

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (a) a map identifying the area the applicant wishes to have shown or described in the permit as the road right of way within which the road will be constructed or maintained, and

heading: Application for permit
paragraph: (b) with respect to a permit to construct a road, information respecting why the area referred to in paragraph (a) was chosen.

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph:
4
		  (1) A road permit holder must notify the regulator, local Indigenous nations, affected land owners, affected permit holders and affected rights holders of the construction of the energy resource road

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (a) not more than 30 days and not less than 72 hours before beginning construction, or

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (b) if the construction must be carried out expeditiously to address an environmental or operational emergency, as soon as practicable.

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) must be in writing and must specify

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (a) the location of the road,

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (b) the applicable road permit number and any administrative identifier that relates to the road,

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (c) a contact name and contact information, and

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (d) the date construction will begin or began, as applicable, and the date construction will be completed or was completed, as applicable.

heading: Notice of construction
paragraph: (3) A notice under subsection (1) to a local Indigenous nation must be provided in the form and manner that are identified for the nation in a manner specified by the regulator, if a manner is specified.

heading: Use of qualified person
paragraph:
4.1
		  (1) A road permit holder who constructs an energy resource road must ensure that the design and construction of the road are carried out under the supervision of a qualified person.

heading: Use of qualified person
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder who maintains an energy resource road must ensure that maintenance of the road is carried out under the supervision of a qualified person.

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph:
5
		  A road permit holder who constructs an energy resource road must ensure that the road's clearing widths are within the road right of way and are wide enough to ensure all of the following:

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (a) the safety of permit holders using the energy resource road;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (b) the integrity of the topography of the area;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (c) the maintenance of drainage of water in the area;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (d) the stability of terrain in the area;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (e) the safe conduct of operations, considering at least all of the following:

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (i)  the placement of borrow pits, quarries, landings or waste areas;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (ii)  the storage of material and equipment as authorized under section 19.1 (2) or (3);

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (iii)  the amount of area required to operate equipment within the clearing width, including equipment turnaround sites;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (iv)  the need to remove snow;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (v)  the need to construct fencing or other ancillary structures;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (vi)  the need to maintain sight lines, including, without limitation, at

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (A) curves and hills,

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (B) locations where the road crosses a road or railway, and

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (C) locations where the road crosses a bridge or major culvert.

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph:
6
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), a road permit holder may not construct or install a bridge or culvert on an energy resource road unless all of the applicable following requirements are met:

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (a) the bridge is designed, fabricated and installed in compliance with

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (i)  the Canadian Highway Bridge Design Code, CAN/CSA-S6, of the Canadian Standards Association, and

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (ii)  soil properties standards, as they apply to bridge piers and abutments, set out in the Canadian Foundation Engineering Manual;

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (b) the culvert is designed and fabricated

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (i)  in compliance with whichever of the following, as amended from time to time, is applicable:

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (A) Canadian Standards Association standard CAN/CSA G401, Corrugated Steel Pipe Products;

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (B) section B182.8 of Canadian Standards Association standard CSA B1800, Plastic Nonpressure Pipe Compendium, or

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (ii)  so that it is as strong as a culvert designed and fabricated in accordance with subparagraph (i);

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (c) the bridge, if it will cross a stream or a fish stream, or the culvert, if it will be in a stream or a fish stream, is designed to pass the highest peak flow of the stream that can reasonably be expected within the return periods set out in column 2 of the following table for the period the road permit holder anticipates the bridge or culvert will remain on the site, as set out opposite in column 1 of the table:

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder may construct or install a bridge that does not comply with subsection (1) (c) if

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (a) the bridge is designed to pass expected flows during the period the bridge is anticipated to remain on the site, and

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (b) the construction, installation and use of the bridge occurs during a period of low flow.

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (3) A road permit holder may construct or install a culvert that does not comply with subsection (1) (c) if

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (a) the installation is temporary and the person does not expect to subsequently install a replacement culvert at that location,

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (b) the stream in which the culvert is being installed is not a fish stream,

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (c) the culvert will pass the flow that will occur during the period the culvert remains on the site, and

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (d) the installation of the culvert occurs during a period of low flow.

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (3.1) A road permit holder must remove the following structures from the energy resource road before any period of high flow begins:

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (a) a bridge referred to in subsection (2), or the components of the bridge that are vulnerable to damage by high flow;

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (b) a culvert referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (4) A road permit holder may construct or install a bridge barrier that does not comply with subsection (1) (a) (i) if the bridge barrier's bridge

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (a) is intended primarily for industrial traffic and no pedestrian traffic,

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (b) is less than 5 m above water,

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (c) has good vertical and horizontal alignment, and

heading: Bridges and culverts
paragraph: (d) is designed to ensure the safety of permit holders.

heading: Signs and markers for bridges

paragraph: (c) if the road permit holder knows of a structural defect or deficiency on the bridge, a sign that states the maximum load capacity of the bridge.

heading: Signs and markers for bridges
paragraph: (2) A sign required under this section must be placed at a distance from the bridge sufficient to enable users of the road to stop safely before reaching the bridge.

heading: Signs and markers for bridges
paragraph: (3) A sign or marker required under this section must be designed and maintained in accordance with any requirements specified by the regulator.

heading: Hazard warning
paragraph:
10
		  (1) At all times while an energy resource road is being modified, the road permit holder must have a warning sign posted at each junction of the energy resource road with another energy resource road, a road that is required to be maintained under another enactment or authorization or a highway within the meaning of the Transportation Act.

heading: Hazard warning
paragraph: (2) A sign posted under subsection (1) must indicate the portion of the energy resource road that is being modified.

heading: Report regarding construction
paragraph: 11		  Within 60 days of completion of the construction of an energy resource road under a permit, the road permit holder must submit to the regulator a report, in the form and manner specified by the regulator, describing the location of the constructed road.

heading: Ongoing restoration - disturbed areas
paragraph:
11.1
		  A road permit holder who is not using a roadwork area for the energy resource road for the construction, operation or maintenance of the road must restore the roadwork area, as soon as weather and ground conditions permit, by

heading: Ongoing restoration - disturbed areas
paragraph: (a) revegetating the area, using ecologically suitable species, so as to maintain bank and slope stability, and

heading: Ongoing restoration - disturbed areas
paragraph: (b) implementing measures in the area, until the vegetation referred to in paragraph (a) is established, to

heading: Ongoing restoration - disturbed areas
paragraph: (i)  conserve soil in the area, and

heading: Ongoing restoration - disturbed areas
paragraph: (ii)  prevent erosion, and sediment transport, from the area into streams and bodies of water.

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph:
11.2
		  (1) A road permit holder must ensure that invasive plants do not

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph: (a) become established in the roadwork areas for the energy resource road, or

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph: (b) spread from a roadwork area for the energy resource road into areas that are immediately adjacent to the roadwork area.

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a road permit holder must

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph: (a) make reasonable efforts to ensure that seed, plant parts and propagules of invasive plants are not transported into the roadwork areas for the energy resource road, and

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph: (b) promptly remove invasive plants from

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph: (i)  the roadwork areas for the energy resource road, and

heading: Ongoing restoration - invasive plants
paragraph: (ii)  any immediately adjacent areas referred to in subsection (1) (b) into which invasive plants have spread from a roadwork area for the energy resource road.

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
11.3
		  A person who carries out energy resource activities within an operating area must prepare
          and maintain an invasive plant compliance record that describes the activities carried
          out for the purpose of complying with the obligations described in section 11.2 of this
          regulation and section 15 of the Environmental Protection and Management
          Regulation, including all of the following:

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(a) the assessment and monitoring activities carried out for the purpose of
            determining whether invasive plants

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (i)  are present or established, or may become established, or

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (ii)  have spread to adjacent areas;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(b) the location, type and distribution of each species of invasive plants found
            through assessment and monitoring activities;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (c) the activities carried out for the purpose of preventing the following:

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(i)  the transportation of seed, plant parts or propagules of invasive
              plants;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(ii)  the establishment of invasive plants, including the removal of
              invasive plants;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(d) the revegetation activities carried out, including the plant species used for
            revegetation;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph:
(e) the activities carried out for the purpose of ensuring that revegetated plants
            are successfully established;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (f) with respect to the activities described in this section,

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (i)  the dates on which the activities were carried out, and

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (ii)  the processes and equipment used in carrying out the activities;

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (g) the qualifications of the persons

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (i)  carrying out assessment and monitoring activities, and

heading: Invasive plant compliance record
paragraph: (ii)  supervising the activities described in this section.

heading: Road maintenance: general
paragraph:
12
		  Subject to section 15, a road permit holder must perform the maintenance and undertake the modifications necessary to ensure that

heading: Road maintenance: general
paragraph: (a) the clearing width for the road complies with this regulation,

heading: Road maintenance: general
paragraph: (b) the road prism and all access structures related to the road are stable,

heading: Road maintenance: general
paragraph: (c) the bridges, culverts, fords and other structures and works associated with the road are functional and appropriate for the uses of the road, and

heading: Road maintenance: general
paragraph: (d) the road can be used safely by permit holders.

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph:
13
		  (1) A road permit holder must

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (a) ensure that road surface and slope drainage systems, including inlets, drainage structures, ditches, culverts, bridges, road crowning, insloping and outsloping, are functional,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (b) remove all vegetative growth and cuttings from road surfaces, roadsides and inlets from drainage structures and ditches if

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (i)  the vegetative growth impedes or reduces sight distance to the extent that the road is not safe for use by permit holders,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (ii)  the removal of the vegetative growth is necessary to enable placement of snow that has been removed from the road at a sufficient distance from the road surface to maintain the sight distance that is adequate for the safe use of the road by motor vehicles, or

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (iii)  the vegetative growth is encroaching on the road surface such that the usable road width has been reduced to the extent that vehicles cannot safely pass each other at road widenings or turnouts,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (c) unless the surface consists of ballast rock surfaces, grade the surface of the energy resource road to facilitate industrial use, provide proper road surface drainage and prevent pooling on the surface by

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (i)  grading during industrial use of the road as often as needed, avoiding the creation of berms along shoulders, to provide a road surface that self drains,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (ii)  grading and shaping the existing road surface and shoulders, including turnouts,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (iii)  placing surface aggregate where necessary to provide a surface that self drains,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (iv)  loosening surfacing materials to a depth sufficient to remove potholes, rutting or washboarding without causing contamination of the surfacing materials with subgrade materials or unsuitable ditch materials, and

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (v)  grading only when the moisture content is suitable,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (d) maintain turnout size, number and location to accommodate the vehicles that are in regular use on the road, and

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (e) ensure that signs, posts and markers, if any, are legible and visible.

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (2) If a road permit holder is using the energy resource road in winter, the road permit holder must

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (a) remove snow from all or part of the travelled portion of the road, including sufficient turnouts, to provide for efficient and safe use by permit holders of the road,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (b) remove snow to create breaches in snow berms for wildlife crossings,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (c) not undercut cut slopes,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (d) not blade gravel or other surfacing materials off of the road,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (e) remove snow only from the portions of the road having roadbed support, including turnouts, and reshape any over-width ploughing as necessary to define the usable width,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (f) if chains on the vehicles used to carry out energy resource activities are not suitable or sufficient to enable safe use of the frozen energy resource road, add sand to the bladed road surface as and when required to provide sufficient traction for the vehicles, and

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (g) during periods of snowmelt,

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (i)  wing back or breach snow berms to facilitate surface drainage in a manner that prevents water flow along the road, and

heading: Road maintenance: technical
paragraph: (ii)  keep roadbed drainage ditches, drainage dips and culverts functional.

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph:
13.1
		  (1) A road permit holder who holds an authorization for a borrow pit that the road permit holder has used for construction, maintenance or deactivation of the energy resource road must ensure that the cut slopes of the borrow pit are

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph: (a) stable, and

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph: (b) graded to a resting angle that

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph: (i)  facilitates reasonable egress by wildlife and livestock, and

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph: (ii)  does not exceed a grade of 2:1.

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder who holds an authorization for a borrow pit described in subsection (1) that the road permit holder is not using for construction, maintenance or deactivation of the energy resource road must deactivate the borrow pit, as soon as weather and ground conditions permit, by

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph: (a) spreading topsoil evenly around the perimeter and edges of the borrow pit, and

heading: Maintenance and deactivation of borrow pits
paragraph: (b) revegetating the perimeter and edges of the borrow pit with ecologically suitable species.

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph:
14
		  (0.1) This section applies in relation to the following structures:

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (a) a bridge;

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (b) a major culvert;

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (c) an engineered retaining wall.

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (1) A road permit holder must

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (a) ensure that a qualified person carries out a visual inspection of each structure associated with the road at least once every year after the structure is constructed, and

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (b) make a record of the inspection.

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder must

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (a) ensure that a qualified person carries out a detailed inspection of each structure associated with the road, and

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (b) make a record of the inspection,

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (i)  subject to subparagraph (ii), at least once every 3 years after the structure is constructed, or

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (ii)  at such intervals as specified in writing by a professional engineer.

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (3) The written specification referred to in subsection (2) (b) must be retained by the road permit holder as part of the record of inspection for at least one year after

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (a) the structure is removed from the site, or

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (b) the road permit holder

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (i)  submits a signed statement under section 27 (1) respecting the energy resource road, or

heading: Maintenance of bridges, major culverts and engineered retaining walls
paragraph: (ii)  is prohibited under section 23 (4) (b) from deactivating the energy resource road.

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph:
15
		  (1) If a road permit holder temporarily stops using the energy resource road to carry out a primary activity for a period anticipated to be greater than 6 months, the person is not required to perform the maintenance and undertake the modifications set out in section 12 but must ensure

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (a) the structural integrity of the road prism and clearing width are stable, and

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (b) the drainage systems of the road are functional

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: to the extent necessary to ensure there is no material adverse effect on fish, fish habitat, water quality or quantity, wildlife or wildlife habitat.

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder referred to in subsection (1) must notify the regulator not more than 30 days after a stoppage referred to in that subsection, and the notice must specify all of the following:

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (a) the location of the road;

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (b) the road permit;

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (c) a contact name and contact information;

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (d) the projected duration of the stoppage.

heading: Limited maintenance
paragraph: (3) A road permit holder referred to in subsection (1) must notify the regulator when the road permit holder resumes using the energy resource road.

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph:
15.1
		  (1) A permit holder who constructs, operates, maintains or deactivates an energy resource road must comply with the protection measures, whether the road right of way is on Crown land or land other than Crown land.

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph: (2) A permit holder who uses an energy resource road must comply with the protection measures, whether the road right of way is on Crown land or on land other than Crown land, as though that use were an energy resource activity.

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph: (3) A road permit holder must not construct or place at a stream crossing for the energy resource road anything except a bridge, culvert, ice bridge or snow fill.

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph: (4) A road permit holder must ensure that

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph: (a) any abutments, footings and scour protection of bridges and culverts associated with the energy resource road are located outside stream channels, and

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph: (b) equipment used for the construction, operation, maintenance or deactivation of the energy resource road is not located in a stream channel unless

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph: (i)  the stream channel is dry, or

heading: Streams and stream crossings
paragraph: (ii)  the stream is frozen to the bottom.

heading: Spring freshet
paragraph:
15.2
		  A road permit holder must remove the following stream crossings from the energy resource road before the spring freshet:

heading: Spring freshet
paragraph: (a) snow fills;

heading: Spring freshet
paragraph: (b) culverts used in snow fills or ice bridges.

heading: Use of energy resource road
paragraph:
15.3
		  (1) A permit holder must not use an energy resource road unless the road is safe for the intended use.

heading: Use of energy resource road
paragraph: (2) A permit holder must not use an energy resource road if

heading: Use of energy resource road
paragraph: (a) there is no road permit holder for the road,

heading: Use of energy resource road
paragraph: (b) the road is causing damage to the environment, or

heading: Use of energy resource road
paragraph: (c) the intended use will damage the road or the environment.

heading: Right of access
paragraph:
16
		  A road permit holder may not

heading: Right of access
paragraph: (a) close the energy resource road, or

heading: Right of access
paragraph: (b) restrict the use of the road by a permit holder or other person,

heading: Right of access
paragraph: except as provided under section 20 or to the extent necessary to carry out maintenance on the road as required under this regulation.

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph:
17
		  (1) The following provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act apply to permit holders using an energy resource road, and the provisions apply as if the road were a highway:

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (a) section 1;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (b) section 2 (5), (6) and (7);

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (c) section 24 (1);

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (d) section 33 (1) insofar as it applies to a driver's licence or a driver's certificate;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (e) section 68;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (f) section 70;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (g) section 73;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (h) section 84;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (i) sections 141 and 142;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (j) sections 144 and 145;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (k) sections 149 and 150;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (l) sections 157 to 160;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (m) section 162;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (n) sections 169 to 172;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (o) sections 185 and 186;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (p) section 194;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (q) sections 206 (1) and (3) and 207;

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (r) sections 224 to 229.

heading: Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act applicable to energy resource roads
paragraph: (2) For certainty, a permit holder who fails to comply with a provision referred to in subsection (1) may not be charged with an offence, or levied with a penalty, for that failure under the Motor Vehicle Act.

heading: Speed restriction
paragraph:
18		  A permit holder must not operate a motor vehicle on an energy resource road at a speed
          that

heading: Speed restriction
paragraph: (a) is unsafe for the conditions, or

heading: Speed restriction
paragraph: (b) exceeds the lesser of

heading: Speed restriction
paragraph: (i)  80 km/h, and

heading: Speed restriction
paragraph: (ii)  the speed posted on a relevant traffic control device.

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Subject to the terms of the road permit, if any, and section 16, a road permit holder may erect a traffic control device in the form of a signal or notice on the road if the road permit holder considers that the device is necessary to promote the safe use of the road.

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (2) An official may erect or order a road permit holder to erect a traffic control device on an energy resource road if the official considers that the device is necessary to promote the safe use of the road.

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1) or (2), a traffic control device may be used in any of the following ways:

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (a) to close the road to all traffic or to specified categories or sizes of motor vehicles, including those not engaged in commercial activities;

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (b) to close the road totally or for a specified period of time;

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (c) to regulate the movement of traffic;

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (d) to require the use of 2-way radio systems during certain hours in order to coordinate the movement of traffic, including specifying the radio frequency to be used on portions of an energy resource road;

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (e) to restrict the use of vehicles having characteristics that could damage the energy resource road or create a safety risk;

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (f) to warn drivers of hazardous or unusual conditions existing on an energy resource road.

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (4) A permit holder using an energy resource road must comply with all traffic control devices on the road.

heading: Traffic control devices
paragraph: (5) An official may remove or order a road permit holder to remove a traffic control device on an energy resource road.

heading: Storage and disposal in right of way
paragraph:
19.1
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), a permit holder must not store or dispose of material, equipment, garbage or anything else in a roadwork area.

heading: Storage and disposal in right of way
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder for a seasonal energy resource road may store bridge and culvert material in a roadwork area for the road during the off-season for the road, if the material will be required for construction, operation or maintenance of the road in the next season.

heading: Storage and disposal in right of way
paragraph: (3) A road permit holder may store material and equipment in a roadwork area for the energy resource road temporarily during construction, operation, maintenance or deactivation of the road if the material and equipment are required for that activity.

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph:
20
		  (1) A road permit holder or the regulator may

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (a) temporarily close the energy resource road, or

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (b) restrict the use of the energy resource road

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: if the action is necessary to address an existing or imminent threat that may

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (c) cause damage to the energy resource road or the environment, or

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (d) endanger human life or property.

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (1.1) The regulator may restrict access to or close, or order a permit holder to restrict access to or close, permanently or temporarily, an energy resource road if the regulator is satisfied that the action is necessary in the public interest.

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (1.2) A road permit holder may restrict access to any portion of the energy resource road located on private property other than access in accordance with section 21 or for land owner uses.

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder or the regulator may remove a motor vehicle, animal or thing from the road at the expense of the owner of the motor vehicle, animal or thing if the road permit holder or the regulator believes that the presence on the road of the motor vehicle, animal or thing may

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (a) cause damage to the energy resource road or the environment,

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (b) endanger human life or property, or

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (c) prevent or impede a permit holder from using the energy resource road.

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (3) A road permit holder who, under subsection (1), temporarily closes an energy resource road or restricts its use must

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (a) temporarily close the energy resource road or restrict its use by ensuring

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (i)  any access control structure erected to restrict motor vehicle traffic

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (A) will not be, or become, a hazard to the users of the road, and

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (B) is placed in a conspicuous location and clearly visible to the operator of a motor vehicle from a safe stopping distance, and

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (ii)  signs are posted at locations that give vehicle operators adequate warning of the access control structure,

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (b) promptly give notice of the temporary closure or restriction to the regulator, and

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph:
(c) reopen the energy resource road or remove the restriction promptly
              after

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph:
(i)  the justification for that temporary closure or restriction ceases to exist,
                or

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (ii)  the regulator requires the reopening or removal.

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (4) Nothing in this section
