heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (a) affects the right of the regulator to use an energy resource road at any time, or

heading: Power to temporarily close, restrict access or remove motor vehicles, animals or things
paragraph: (b) authorizes the removal from an energy resource road of any motor vehicle, animal or thing of the regulator.

heading: Contribution to maintenance costs
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A permit holder who intends to use an energy resource road maintained by a road permit holder must notify the road permit holder at least 14 days before the intended use will begin.

heading: Contribution to maintenance costs
paragraph: (2) A permit holder referred to in subsection (1) must provide to the road permit holder referred to in that subsection a reasonable contribution to the expense

heading: Contribution to maintenance costs
paragraph: (a) of maintaining the energy resource road to accommodate the permit holder's use of the road,

heading: Contribution to maintenance costs
paragraph: (b) of modifying the road to accommodate the special needs of the permit holder, if any, and

heading: Contribution to maintenance costs
paragraph: (c) of repairing any damage to the road caused by the permit holder's use of the road.

heading: Contribution to maintenance costs
paragraph: (3) On receiving a notice under subsection (1), the road permit holder must provide to the permit holder an estimate of the costs relating to the matters referred to in subsection (2) (a) to (c), including supporting data and records.

heading: Deactivation
paragraph:
22
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2) and section 23 (4) (b), a road permit holder who is permitted to maintain an energy resource road may deactivate the road at any time.

heading: Deactivation
paragraph: (1.1) Subject to subsection (2), a road permit holder must deactivate the energy resource road when restoring the land that was used for the primary activity in respect of which the road was used, unless the road is required for monitoring purposes.

heading: Deactivation
paragraph: (2) A road permit holder must deactivate the portion of an energy resource road that provides access to the site of the well, pipeline or facility of the road permit holder when restoring that site.

heading: Deactivation
paragraph: (3) A road permit holder who deactivates an energy resource road must deactivate the road

heading: Deactivation
paragraph: (a) under the supervision of a qualified person, and

heading: Deactivation
paragraph: (b) in accordance with this Part.

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph:
23
		  (1) A road permit holder who intends to deactivate an energy resource road must provide written notice of the intention to all of the following:

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (a) the regulator;

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (b) affected land owners;

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (c) local Indigenous nations;

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (d) users of the road known to the road permit holder;

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (e) the district office for the forest district, as established in the Administrative Boundaries Regulation, B.C. Reg. 137/2014, in which the road is located.

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) must identify the road to be deactivated and specify the date when deactivation will begin.

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (2.1) A notice under subsection (1) to a local Indigenous nation must be provided in the form and manner that are identified for the nation in a manner specified by the regulator, if a manner is specified.

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (3) A road permit holder may not begin deactivating an energy resource road unless at least 30 days and not more than 60 days have elapsed since the road permit holder provided notice under subsection (1) in relation to the deactivation.

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (4) On receiving notice under subsection (1), the regulator may do one or both of the following:

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (a) extend the period referred to in subsection (3);

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (b) prohibit the road permit holder from deactivating the road.

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (5) A road permit holder who provides written notice under subsection (1) must

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (a) retain a copy of the notice, and

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (b) if the road permit holder receives written responses from or on behalf of the entities referred to in that subsection,

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (i)  retain a copy of each response,

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (ii)  if a response objects to the deactivation, promptly submit to the regulator a copy of the response, and

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (iii)  if the road permit holder completes the deactivation,

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (A) prepare a written report, within 30 days after the completion, that summarizes the responses and identifies the measures, if any, that the road permit holder took to address them, and

heading: Notice of deactivation
paragraph: (B) retain a copy of the report.

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph:
24
		  A road permit holder who deactivates an energy resource road must do all of the following:

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph: (a) barricade the road surface width in a clearly visible manner to prevent access by motor vehicles, other than all-terrain vehicles;

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph: (b) remove stream pipe culverts and arch culverts;

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph: (c) remove bridge and log or box culvert superstructures;

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph: (d) remove bridge and log or box culvert substructures, if the failure of those substructures would have a material adverse effect on downstream property, improvements or the environment;

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph: (d.1) remove engineered retaining walls, if the failure of those walls would have a material adverse effect on property, improvements or the environment;

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph: (e) stabilize the road prism and the clearing width of the road;

heading: Deactivation requirements
paragraph: (f) comply with section 19 (1) (c) and (d) of the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation, whether the road right of way is on Crown land or land other than Crown land.

heading: Maintenance requirements during deactivation
paragraph:
25
		  (1) A road permit holder who deactivates an energy resource road must

heading: Maintenance requirements during deactivation
paragraph: (a) maintain any portion of the energy resource road that is not being deactivated, and

heading: Maintenance requirements during deactivation
paragraph: (b) for any portion of the energy resource road that is being deactivated, maintain the portion but only to the extent necessary to ensure that the structural integrity of the road prism and the clearing width are stable and that the drainage systems of the road are functional.

heading: Maintenance requirements during deactivation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), a portion of an energy resource road is being deactivated when the road permit holder has begun but not completed on that portion of the energy resource road requirements referred to in section 24.

heading: Hazard warning during deactivation
paragraph:
26
		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), at all times while an energy resource road is being deactivated, the road permit holder must have a warning sign posted at each junction of the road with another energy resource road, a road that is required to be maintained under another enactment or authorization or a highway within the meaning of the Transportation Act.

heading: Hazard warning during deactivation
paragraph: (2) A warning sign posted under subsection (1) must indicate the portion of the road that is being deactivated.

heading: Hazard warning during deactivation
paragraph: (3) If a road permit holder is exempted from the requirement under section 24 (a) to barricade the road, the road permit holder must ensure that the sign posted under subsection (1) of this section remains on the site until the later of the following:

heading: Hazard warning during deactivation
paragraph: (a) the date 12 months after the date deactivation begins;

heading: Hazard warning during deactivation
paragraph: (b) the date deactivation is completed.

heading: Signed statement to the regulator
paragraph: 27		  (1) A road permit holder who completes deactivation of an energy resource road must, within 30 days after the completion, submit to the regulator a signed statement stating that the road permit holder has complied with

heading: Signed statement to the regulator
paragraph: (a) section 24, and

heading: Signed statement to the regulator
paragraph: (b) section 19 of the Environmental Protection and Management Regulation, as applicable.

heading: Signed statement to the regulator
paragraph: (2) A signed statement under subsection (1) must

heading: Signed statement to the regulator
paragraph: (a) be signed by the road permit holder or a director or officer of the road permit holder, and

heading: Signed statement to the regulator
paragraph: (b) specify the date on which the statement is signed.

heading: Exemption by official
paragraph:
28
		  An official may exempt a permit holder from complying with one or more provisions of this regulation and may impose one or more conditions with respect to the exemption.

heading: Records
paragraph:
29
		  The records and reports required under this regulation are prescribed for the purposes
          of section 38 of the Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Professional Governance Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "former Act" means the Engineers and Geoscientists Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 116;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protective purposes" means the safety, health and welfare of the public, including the protection of the environment and the promotion of health and safety in the workplace.

heading: Definitions in relation to professional engineering
paragraph: 2		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions in relation to professional engineering
paragraph: "engineering discipline" means agricultural, biomedical, bioresource, biosystems, building, chemical, civil, computer, electrical, environmental, food, forest, geological, geomatics, industrial, marine, mechanical, mechatronics, metallurgical, mining, naval architecture, nuclear, petroleum, software and structural engineering and engineering physics;

heading: Definitions in relation to professional engineering
paragraph: "practice of professional engineering" means the provision of

heading: Definitions in relation to professional engineering
paragraph: (a) advice or services that are based on an engineering discipline, or

heading: Definitions in relation to professional engineering
paragraph: (b) advice or services that are ancillary to those described in paragraph (a);

heading: Definitions in relation to professional engineering
paragraph: "professional licensee engineering" means a registrant who is authorized by the regulatory body to use the title "professional licensee engineering".

heading: Regulated practice
paragraph:
3
		  For the purposes of the definition of "practice of professional engineering" in section 5 [definitions in respect of the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of the Province of British Columbia] of Schedule 1 of the Act, the practice of professional engineering is prescribed.

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph:
4
		  For the purposes of section 51 (1) (a) [reserved titles] of the Act, the following titles are reserved for the exclusive use of registrants:

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph: (a) "professional engineer";

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph: (b) "professional licensee engineering";

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph: (c) "engineer in training".

heading: Reserved practice
paragraph:
5
		  (1) For the purposes of section 51 (1) (b) [reserved practice] of the Act, the practice of professional engineering, as it relates to matters that, having regard to the protective purposes, require the experience or technical knowledge of a professional engineer or professional licensee engineering, is a reserved practice that may only be carried out by or under the supervision of a registrant.

heading: Definitions in relation to professional geoscience
paragraph:
6
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions in relation to professional geoscience
paragraph: "practice of professional geoscience" means the provision of

heading: Definitions in relation to professional geoscience
paragraph: (a) advice or services that

heading: Definitions in relation to professional geoscience
paragraph: (i)  are based on environmental geoscience, geology, geophysics or geochemistry, and

heading: Definitions in relation to professional geoscience
paragraph: (ii)  relate to the discovery or development of oil, natural gas, coal, metallic or non-metallic minerals, precious stones, other natural resources or water or the investigation of surface or subsurface geological conditions;

heading: Definitions in relation to professional geoscience
paragraph: (b) advice or services that are ancillary to those described in paragraph (a);

heading: Definitions in relation to professional geoscience
paragraph: "professional licensee geoscience" means a registrant who is authorized by the regulatory body to use the title "professional licensee geoscience".

heading: Regulated practice
paragraph:
7
		  For the purposes of the definition of "practice of professional geoscience" in section 5 [definitions in respect of the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of the Province of British Columbia] of Schedule 1 of the Act, the practice of professional geoscience is prescribed.

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph:
8
		  For the purposes of section 51 (1) (a) [reserved titles] of the Act, the following titles are reserved for the exclusive use of registrants:

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph: (a) "professional geoscientist";

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph: (b) "professional licensee geoscience";

heading: Reserved titles
paragraph: (c) "geoscientist in training".

heading: Reserved practice
paragraph:
9
		  (1) For the purposes of section 51 (1) (b) [reserved practice] of the Act, the practice of professional geoscience, as it relates to matters that, having regard to the protective purposes, require the experience or technical knowledge of a professional geoscientist or professional licensee geoscience, is a reserved practice that may only be carried out by or under the supervision of a registrant.

heading: Registration of firms
paragraph:
10
		  For the purposes of section 3 [application to firms as registrants] of the Act, the regulatory body is authorized to register firms in that regulatory body as registrants.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "committee" means the Environment and Land Use Committee continued under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environment" means all the external conditions or influences under which humans, animals and plants live or are developed.

heading: Committee continued
paragraph:
2
		  (1) The Environment and Land Use Committee is continued and consists of the following:

heading: Committee continued
paragraph: (a) a member of the Executive Council appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council and designated in the appointment as chair;

heading: Committee continued
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (1.1), other members of the Legislative Assembly appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Committee continued
paragraph: (1.1) The majority of members of the Environment and Land Use Committee must be members of the Executive Council.

heading: Committee continued
paragraph: (2) The committee may determine its own procedure and may elect an acting chair to act in the absence of the chair.

heading: Committee continued
paragraph: (3) If the committee has more than 3 members its quorum is 3.

heading: Duties of the committee
paragraph:
3
		  The committee has the following duties and powers:

heading: Duties of the committee
paragraph: (a) to establish and recommend programs designed to foster increased public concern and awareness of the environment;

heading: Duties of the committee
paragraph: (b) to ensure that all the aspects of preservation and maintenance of the natural environment are fully considered in the administration of land use and resource development commensurate with a maximum beneficial land use, and minimize and prevent waste of those resources, and despoliation of the environment occasioned by that use;

heading: Duties of the committee
paragraph: (c) if considered advisable, to make recommendations to the Lieutenant Governor in Council respecting any matter relating to the environment and the development and use of land and other natural resources;

heading: Duties of the committee
paragraph: (d) to inquire into and study any matter related to the environment or land use;

heading: Duties of the committee
paragraph: (e) to prepare reports, and, if advisable, to make recommendations to the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Powers of committee
paragraph:
4
		  The committee may do one or more of the following:

heading: Powers of committee
paragraph: (a) hold a public inquiry if it appears to the committee that the proper determination of any matter within its jurisdiction requires an inquiry;

heading: Powers of committee
paragraph: (b) appoint technical committees;

heading: Powers of committee
paragraph: (c) subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, provide for the remuneration of experts, specialists and researchers and, under the Public Service Act, of clerks and other employees as required.

heading: Powers of chair and members for public inquiry
paragraph: 5		  For a public inquiry under section 4 (a), the chair of the committee or a member of the committee authorized by the committee to hold a hearing has the powers and jurisdiction of a justice under the Offence Act.

heading: Expenses of committee members
paragraph: 6		  (1) No member of the committee is entitled to remuneration as a member of the committee.

heading: Expenses of committee members
paragraph: (2) A member may be paid and receive travelling and out of pocket expenses in accordance with the general directives of the Treasury Board.

heading: Orders of Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph:
7
		  (1) On the recommendation of the committee, and despite any other Act or regulation, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make orders the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers necessary or advisable respecting the environment or land use.

heading: Orders of Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (2) A minister, ministry or agent of the Crown specified in an order under subsection (1) must not exercise a power under any other Act or regulation except in accordance with the order.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
8
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "approval under another enactment" means an approval, licence, permit or other authorization under another enactment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assessment", other than in, or in reference to, section 35 or 73, means an assessment under this Act of a reviewable project's potential effects that is conducted in relation to an application for

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an environmental assessment certificate, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an amendment of an environmental assessment certificate;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assessment body" means a body referred to in section 24 (3) (a) that is required to conduct an assessment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assessment report" means a written report submitted to the ministers under section 28 summarizing the procedures followed during, and the findings of, an assessment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "chief executive assessment officer" means the individual appointed under section 3 as the chief executive assessment officer of the Environmental Assessment Office;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "class assessment" means an assessment conducted under section 34;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "compliance and enforcement officer" means an individual appointed under section 49 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "dispute resolution facilitator" means an individual appointed under section 5 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environmental assessment certificate" means an environmental assessment certificate issued by the ministers under section 29 (4);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "exemption order" means an order made under section 17 (1) (b);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ministers" means the minister and the responsible minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mitigation" includes actions to offset the potential adverse effects of a project;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "office" means the Environmental Assessment Office continued under section 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "participating Indigenous nation" means an Indigenous nation that provides notice to the chief executive assessment officer under section 14 (1) and has not, in relation to a project, been provided a notice by the chief executive assessment officer under section 14 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "process order" means an order made under section 19 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "project" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any activity that has or may have adverse effects, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any construction, operation, modification, dismantling or abandonment of a physical work;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "proponent" means a person or organization that proposes to undertake a reviewable project, and includes the government of Canada, British Columbia, a municipality or regional district, another province, another jurisdiction and an Indigenous nation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "responsible minister" means the member of the Executive Council that the Lieutenant Governor in Council designates by order as the minister responsible for a specified reviewable project or specified category of reviewable projects;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "reviewable project" means a project that is within a category of projects prescribed under section 9 or that is designated as a reviewable project by the minister under section 11 or the chief executive assessment officer under section 12, and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the facilities at the main site of the project,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any off-site facilities related to the project that the chief executive assessment officer or the minister may designate, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any activities related to the project that the chief executive assessment officer or the minister may designate;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "termination order" means an order issued under section 17 (1) (a).

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph:
2
		  (1) The Environmental Assessment Office is continued as an office of the government.

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (2) The purposes of the office are

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (a) to carry out its responsibilities under this Act, and

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (b) to do the following in carrying out the purpose referred to in paragraph (a):

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (i)  promote sustainability by protecting the environment and fostering a sound economy and the well-being of British Columbians and their communities by

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (A) carrying out assessments in a thorough, timely, transparent and impartial way, considering the environmental, economic, social, cultural and health effects of assessed projects,

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (B) facilitating meaningful public participation throughout assessments,

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (C) using the best available science, Indigenous knowledge and local knowledge in decision making under the Act, and

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (D) coordinating assessments with other governments, where appropriate, including Indigenous nations, and with other provincial ministries and agencies;

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (ii)  support reconciliation with Indigenous peoples in British Columbia by

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (A) supporting the implementation of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples,

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (B) recognizing the inherent jurisdiction of Indigenous nations and their right to participate in decision making in matters that would affect their rights, through representatives chosen by themselves,

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (C) collaborating with Indigenous nations in relation to reviewable projects, consistent with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, and

heading: Environmental Assessment Office
paragraph: (D) acknowledging Indigenous peoples' rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 in the course of assessments and decision making under this Act.

heading: Appointment of chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: 3		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may appoint an individual to be the chief executive assessment officer.

heading: Appointment of chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may establish the remuneration and other terms of the appointment of the chief executive assessment officer.

heading: Appointment of chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (3) The chief executive assessment officer is an employee as defined in the Public Service Act.

heading: Delegation by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: 4		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer, by conditional or unconditional written authority, may delegate any of the powers and duties of the chief executive assessment officer under this Act to any person

heading: Delegation by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (a) employed in the office, or

heading: Delegation by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (b) assigned to the office but not employed in the office.

heading: Delegation by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (2) A person to whom the chief executive assessment officer delegates powers and duties under subsection (1) may exercise the powers and must perform the duties in accordance with the written authority.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph:
5
		  (1) Subject to regulations made under subsection (4) (a), the minister, after considering a recommendation, if any, of an Indigenous nation, may appoint individuals to facilitate the resolution of disputes in relation to a matter referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (2) A participating Indigenous nation or the chief executive assessment officer may refer one or more of the following matters to a dispute resolution facilitator:

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (a) a matter pending decision under section 14 (2), 17, 18, 19, 28 or 29;

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (b) the provision of a notice under section 14 (1);

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (c) any other prescribed matter.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (3) On completion of a facilitation, a dispute resolution facilitator must provide a report to the participants and to the applicable of the chief executive assessment officer or the minister.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the powers and duties of dispute resolution facilitators under this Act, including, without limitation, regulations respecting the following:

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (a) qualifications of individuals who may be appointed under subsection (1);

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (b) the powers and obligations of a dispute resolution facilitator to manage a referral made to the facilitator;

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (c) matters that a dispute resolution facilitator must consider before making a report;

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (d) referrals to a dispute resolution facilitator;

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (e) the time by which a dispute resolution facilitator must complete a facilitation and provide a report.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (5) If a matter pending decision is referred to a dispute resolution facilitator,

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (a) a decision on the matter may not be made under the applicable section until after the facilitator has provided a report, and

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (b) if the participating Indigenous nation requests that the chief executive assessment officer take part in the dispute resolution process, the chief executive assessment officer must take part in the process.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (6) Despite subsection (2), an Indigenous nation that has provided notice under section 14 (1) may refer to a dispute resolution facilitator a matter pending decision under section 14 (2).

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (7) A report of a dispute resolution facilitator is not to be taken as guiding

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (a) the chief executive assessment officer or minister respecting a project not addressed in the report, or

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (b) a decision maker under another enactment.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (8) This section is not to be taken as limiting any right a participating Indigenous nation may have to seek a remedy from a court.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitators
paragraph: (9) For certainty, nothing in this section, nor anything done under this section, abrogates or derogates from the rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: 6		  (1) Despite any other enactment, a person must not

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) undertake or carry on any activity that is a reviewable project, or

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) construct, operate, modify, dismantle or abandon all or part of the facilities of a reviewable project,

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: unless the person

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (c) first obtains an environmental assessment certificate for the reviewable project, or

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (d) has been issued an exemption order.

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (2) Despite any other enactment, if an environmental assessment certificate has been issued for a reviewable project, a person must not, except in accordance with the certificate,

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) undertake or carry on any activity that is authorized by the certificate, or

heading: Requirement for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) construct, operate, modify, dismantle or abandon all or part of the project facilities that are authorized by the certificate.

heading: Required consent
paragraph:
7
		  Despite any other enactment and whether or not an environmental assessment certificate is required, a reviewable project may not, without the consent of an Indigenous nation, proceed

heading: Required consent
paragraph: (a) on treaty lands if the final agreement with the Indigenous nation requires this consent, or

heading: Required consent
paragraph: (b) in an area that is the subject of an agreement, between an Indigenous nation and the government, that

heading: Required consent
paragraph: (i)  requires this consent, and

heading: Required consent
paragraph: (ii)  is prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Effect on approvals under other enactments
paragraph:
8
		  (1) Despite any other enactment, a minister who administers another enactment, or an employee or agent of the government or of a municipality or regional district, must not issue an approval under another enactment for a person to

heading: Effect on approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (a) undertake or carry on an activity that is, in whole or in part, a reviewable project, or

heading: Effect on approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (b) construct, operate, modify, dismantle or abandon all or part of the facilities of a reviewable project,

heading: Effect on approvals under other enactments
paragraph: unless satisfied that the person has

heading: Effect on approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (c) a valid environmental assessment certificate for the reviewable project, or

heading: Effect on approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (d) a valid exemption order for the reviewable project.

heading: Effect on approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (2) Despite any other enactment, an approval under another enactment is without effect if it is issued contrary to subsection (1).

heading: Reviewable projects established by regulation
paragraph:
9
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing what constitutes a reviewable project for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Reviewable projects established by regulation
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of a regulation under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation,

heading: Reviewable projects established by regulation
paragraph: (a) categorize projects on the basis of size, production or storage capacity, timing, geographical location, potential adverse effects, type of industry to which the projects are related, type of proponent or any other basis that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers appropriate, and

heading: Reviewable projects established by regulation
paragraph: (b) provide differently for different categories of projects.

heading: Project notifications
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A person who proposes a project that is not a reviewable project under the regulations under section 9 but is within a prescribed category of projects must, within the prescribed period, submit to the chief executive assessment officer a project notification.

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (2) A project notification must include

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (a) the prescribed information, and

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (b) any other information the chief executive assessment officer requires.

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (3) A person referred to in subsection (1) must not

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (a) undertake or carry on any activity that is the project referred to in the project notification, or

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (b) construct, operate, modify, dismantle or abandon all or part of the facilities of the project referred to in the project notification

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: unless one of the following has occurred:

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (c) the person has been notified under subsection (4) (c) that no further review of the project under this section is required;

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (d) any review of the project that is required has been completed.

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (4) Within 60 days of receiving a project notification, the chief executive assessment officer must do one of the following:

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (a) submit the project notification to the minister for consideration under section 11 and provide notice to the person who proposes the project that the project notification has been submitted to the minister for that purpose;

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (b) provide notice to the person who proposes the project that further review of the project under this section is required;

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (c) provide notice to the person who proposes the project that no further review of the project under this section is required.

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (5) A notice provided under subsection (4) (b) may include

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (a) procedures and consultations respecting the project that must be carried out by the person who proposes the project, and

heading: Project notifications
paragraph: (b) instructions respecting the submission of a revised project notification once the procedures and consultations referred to in paragraph (a) have been carried out.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph:
11
		  (1) In this section, "eligible project" means a project that is not substantially started and is not a reviewable project under a regulation under section 9.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (2) A person may apply to the minister to have an eligible project designated as a reviewable project under this section.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (3) An application under subsection (2) must

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (a) be in writing,

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (b) state why the applicant wishes the eligible project to be designated as a reviewable project, and

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (c) include any other information the minister requires.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (4) On receiving an application under subsection (2), the minister must consider the following:

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (a) whether the applicant is an Indigenous nation;

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (b) whether the eligible project could have effects on an Indigenous nation and the rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982;

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (c) if the eligible project is in a category of projects described in a regulation under section 9, whether the potential effects of the eligible project will be equivalent to or greater than the potential effects of projects in that category that are reviewable projects;

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (d) whether an assessment of the eligible project is consistent with the purposes set out in section 2.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsections (6) and (7), after considering an application as required under subsection (4), the minister must, within 30 days of receiving the application,

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (a) designate the eligible project as a reviewable project, or

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (b) decline to make that designation.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (6) The minister may make a designation under subsection (5) respecting a project that is subject to a prescribed regulatory process only if the minister is satisfied that the designation is in the public interest.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (7) The minister may exercise the power under subsection (5) on the minister's own initiative after considering the matters set out in subsection (4) with respect to the eligible project.

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (8) The minister may, by order, require a person proposing to undertake a project to provide information to the minister for the purpose of exercising the power under subsection (5).

heading: Minister's power to designate a project as reviewable
paragraph: (9) If the minister declines to make a designation under subsection (5), the minister must provide reasons for that decision to the applicant.

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: 12		  (1) A person who proposes a project that is not a reviewable project under section 11 or under the regulations under section 9 may apply to the chief executive assessment officer for the project to be designated as a reviewable project.

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: (2) An application under subsection (1) must

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: (a) be in writing,

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: (b) state why the applicant wishes the project to be designated as a reviewable project, and

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: (c) include any other information the chief executive assessment officer requires.

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: (3) After considering an application under subsection (1), the chief executive assessment officer may, by order,

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: (a) designate the project as a reviewable project, or

heading: Application to chief executive assessment officer for reviewable project designation
paragraph: (b) decline to make that designation.

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph:
13
		  (1) A proponent of a reviewable project may submit to the chief executive assessment officer, in accordance with the requirements of the chief executive assessment officer,

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (a) an initial project description, and

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (b) an engagement plan, including a proposal respecting engagement among the proponent, the office, Indigenous nations, municipalities, government agencies and the public during the early engagement part of the assessment.

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer may make requirements for the purposes of subsection (1) that apply generally or to a specific reviewable project.

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (3) After receiving the initial project description and engagement plan referred to in subsection (1), the chief executive assessment officer must, by order,

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (a) approve the description and plan, or

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (b) require the proponent to

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (i)  make changes to the description and plan in accordance with the directions of the chief executive assessment officer, and

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (ii)  submit the revised description and plan in accordance with subsection (1) within the time indicated by the chief executive assessment officer.

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (4) After making an order under subsection (3) (a), the chief executive assessment officer must publish the approved description for at least 30 days and, during that period, invite comment from the public on the description.

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (5) Within 90 days of making an order under subsection (3) (a), the chief executive assessment officer must provide a notice to the proponent setting out

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (a) a summary of comments received during the period referred to in subsection (4), and

heading: Initial project descriptions and engagement plans
paragraph: (b) the Indigenous nations that are participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Participating Indigenous nations
paragraph:
14
		  (1) Within 80 days of the first day of publication of the initial project description, an Indigenous nation may provide notice to the chief executive assessment officer that the Indigenous nation intends to participate in the assessment of the project.

heading: Participating Indigenous nations
paragraph: (2) After giving an Indigenous nation that has provided notice under subsection (1) an opportunity to be heard, the chief executive assessment officer may provide notice to the Indigenous nation that the chief executive assessment officer has determined that there is no reasonable possibility the Indigenous nation or its rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 will be adversely affected by the project.

heading: Participating Indigenous nations
paragraph: (3) A notice provided by the chief executive assessment officer under subsection (2) must set out the reasons for the determination.

heading: Detailed project description
paragraph: 15		  (1) A proponent who has been issued an approval under section 13 (3) (a) and received notice under section 13 (5) may submit to the chief executive assessment officer, in accordance with the requirements, if any, of the chief executive assessment officer, a detailed project description.

heading: Detailed project description
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer may make requirements for the purposes of subsection (1) that apply generally or to a specific project.

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph:
16
		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer, in relation to a project, must seek to achieve consensus with participating Indigenous nations before exercising the power under subsection (2) or complying with the obligation under subsection (4) (a) or (5) (a).

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (2) After receiving a detailed project description under section 15, the chief executive assessment officer must do one of the following once the requirements of subsection (1) have been met:

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (a) require the proponent to submit a revised detailed project description;

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (3), if the chief executive assessment officer, taking into account practical means of preventing or reducing to an acceptable level any potential adverse effects of the project, considers that the project

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (i)  will not have a significant adverse environmental, economic, social, cultural or health effect, or

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (ii)  will not have serious effects on an Indigenous nation or the rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982,

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: refer the project to the minister for a decision under section 17 with a recommendation that the minister issue an exemption order under that section;

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (c) if the chief executive assessment officer considers that the project

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (i)  will have extraordinarily adverse effects

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (A) generally, or

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (B) on an Indigenous nation or the rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982,

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (ii)  will have extraordinarily adverse effects on a prescribed protected area,

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (iii)  is, on the advice of the minister or another minister, clearly incompatible with a government policy, or

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (iv)  is substantially the same as a project that has previously been the subject of an order under section 17 (1) (a) or 29 (4) (c) (ii),

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: refer the project to the minister for a decision under section 17 with a recommendation that the minister issue a termination order under that section;

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (d) make a decision under section 18.

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (3) The chief executive assessment officer may not make a referral under subsection (2) (b) respecting a project that has been designated under section 11.

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (4) A referral under subsection (2) (b) must be accompanied by

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (a) a report that addresses the following:

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (i)  the matters considered under subsection (2) (b);

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (ii)  results of public engagements;

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (iii)  applicable assessments undertaken under section 35 or 73;

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (iv)  consistency with any land-use plan of the government or an Indigenous nation if the plan is relevant to the assessment;

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (v)  whether another assessment of the project has been or will be conducted;

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (vi)  whether potential effects of the project can be adequately addressed by another regulatory process,

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (b) notification, if any, provided by a participating Indigenous nation of the nation's consent or lack of consent to issuing an exemption order and reasons for that consent or lack of consent, and

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (c) information, if any, respecting an arrangement reached with a participating Indigenous nation in relation to the potential effects of the project on the Indigenous nation.

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (5) A referral under subsection (2) (c) must be accompanied by

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (a) a report that

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (i)  addresses the matters considered under subsection (2) (c),

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (ii)  explains the grounds for the recommendation, and

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (iii)  addresses the matters referred to in subsection (4) (a) (ii) to (iv),

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (b) notification, if any, provided by a participating Indigenous nation of the nation's consent or lack of consent to issuing a termination order and reasons for that consent or lack of consent, and

heading: Recommendation whether to proceed with assessment
paragraph: (c) information, if any, respecting an arrangement reached with a participating Indigenous nation in relation to the potential effects of the project on the Indigenous nation.

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: 17		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), on receiving a referral and recommendation under section 16, the minister may

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (3), order that the project may not proceed as proposed,

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (b) order that the proponent is exempt from the requirement under section 6 to obtain an environmental assessment certificate for the project, or

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (c) refer the project to the chief executive assessment officer for a further decision under section 16.

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (2) In making a decision under subsection (1), the minister must consider the sustainability purpose referred to in section 2 (2) (b) (i), the reconciliation purpose referred to in section 2 (2) (b) (ii) and the prescribed matters, if any.

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (3) Before issuing an order under subsection (1) (a), the minister must give the proponent an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (4) The minister may attach to an order under subsection (1) (a) or (b) conditions that the minister considers necessary.

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (5) An order under subsection (1) (a) or (b) does not relieve the proponent from compliance with the applicable requirements that pertain to the project under other enactments.

heading: Minister's decision whether to terminate or exempt a project
paragraph: (6) An order under subsection (1) (a) or (b) must set out the reasons for the order and must, in a case where a notification referred to in section 16 (4) (b) or (5) (b) indicates a lack of consent to the issuance of the order, give reasons for why the decision to issue the order was made.

heading: Chief executive assessment officer's decision on type of assessment
paragraph:
18
		  (1) If the chief executive assessment officer does not exercise the power under section 16 (2) (a), (b) or (c), the chief executive assessment officer must

heading: Chief executive assessment officer's decision on type of assessment
paragraph: (a) consider the project under section 19, or

heading: Chief executive assessment officer's decision on type of assessment
paragraph: (b) refer the project to the minister for a determination under section 24, with recommendations, including recommendations respecting whether the assessment should be conducted by an assessment body.

heading: Chief executive assessment officer's decision on type of assessment
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer must publish a notice of a decision under subsection (1).

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Before making a process order, the chief executive assessment officer must seek to achieve, with respect to the order, consensus with participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 25 and subsections (4) and (5) of this section, if the chief executive assessment officer makes a determination set out in section 18 (1) (a) for a reviewable project, the chief executive assessment officer must issue, within 120 days after publishing a notice under section 18 (2), a process order that does all of the following:

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (a) determines the scope of the required assessment of the reviewable project, including, without limitation, the scope of the assessment of the effects referred to in section 25 (2) (a), the facilities at the main site of the reviewable project, any of its off-site facilities and any activities related to the reviewable project;

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (b) includes an assessment plan, setting out the procedures and methods for conducting the assessment, including, without limitation,

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (i)  consensus-seeking opportunities between the office and participating Indigenous nations,

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (ii)  hearings, if any, to be conducted during the assessment, and

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (iii)  the roles of the technical advisory committee and the community advisory committee in the assessment, if any;

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (c) includes information requirements, setting out, without limitation,

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (i)  the information required from the proponent

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (A) in relation to or supplementary to the proponent's application, and

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (B) at specified times during the assessment, in relation to the matters set out in section 25,

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (ii)  reviews, if any, that must be undertaken of information specified in the order,

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (iii)  methods by which information must be obtained, and

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (iv)  information, if any, to be obtained from persons other than the proponent with respect to the potential effects specified under paragraph (a) of this subsection.

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (3) The chief executive assessment officer's discretion under subsection (2) includes, but is not limited to, the discretion to specify by order one or more of the following:

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (a) how the matters set out in section 25 are to be addressed in the assessment;

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (b) the timelines according to which the assessment will be conducted;

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (c) the persons and organizations, including but not limited to the public, Indigenous nations, government agencies and neighbouring jurisdictions, to be consulted by the proponent or the office during the assessment, and the means by which the persons and organizations are to be provided with notice of the assessment, access to information during the assessment and opportunities to be consulted;

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (d) the opportunities for the persons and organizations specified under paragraph (c), and for the proponent, to provide comments during the assessment of the reviewable project.

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (4) If a participating Indigenous nation notifies the chief executive assessment officer of the nation's intent to carry out an assessment with respect to the potential effects of the project on the nation and on its rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982, the chief executive assessment officer, in the order made under subsection (2), must specify

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (a) the portion of the assessment to be carried out by the nation, and

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (b) the date by which the assessment by the nation must be completed.

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (5) Before making a process order, the chief executive assessment officer must publish the proposed order for at least 30 days and, during that period, invite comment from the public on the proposed order.

heading: Process planning by chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: (6) The assessment of the potential effects of a reviewable project must take into account and reflect government policy identified for the chief executive assessment officer, during the course of the assessment, by a government agency or organization responsible for the identified policy area.

heading: Limit on discretion of chief executive assessment officer
paragraph: 20		  The chief executive assessment officer may not, under section 19, do anything referred to in section 24 (3) (a).

heading: Technical advisory committee
paragraph:
21
		  (1)  For every assessment, the chief executive assessment officer must establish a technical advisory committee

heading: Technical advisory committee
paragraph: (a) to advise the chief executive assessment officer and participating Indigenous nations on technical matters related to the assessment, and

heading: Technical advisory committee
paragraph: (b) to review the proponent's application under section 27.

heading: Technical advisory committee
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer may establish rules and procedures respecting meetings of a technical advisory committee.

heading: Technical advisory committee
paragraph: (3) The chief executive assessment officer must invite participating Indigenous nations to be on a technical advisory committee and may invite any other persons the chief executive assessment officer considers appropriate.

heading: Community advisory committee
paragraph:
22
		  (1) For an assessment or a class of assessments, the chief executive assessment officer must, if the chief executive assessment officer considers that there is sufficient community interest in a project, establish one or more community advisory committees to advise the chief executive assessment officer on the potential effects of the applicable project or class of projects on the community.

heading: Community advisory committee
paragraph: (2) An individual appointed to a community advisory committee under subsection (1) may be paid reasonable and necessary travelling and out-of-pocket expenses incurred by the person in carrying out duties of the committee.

heading: Public engagement
paragraph:
23
		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer may conduct public comment periods in addition to those referred to in sections 13 (4), 19 (5), 27 (2) (a) and 28 (2) (b) and carry out other public engagement activities in relation to a project.

heading: Public engagement
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer may order that a public comment period referred to in sections 13 (4), 19 (5), 27 (2) (a) and 28 (2) (b) need not be carried out if satisfied that the period is unnecessary because the public has not demonstrated sufficient interest in the assessment of the reviewable project.

heading: Public engagement
paragraph: (3) An order under subsection (2) must set out the reasons for the order.

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph:
24
		  (1) If the chief executive assessment officer under section 18 (1) (b) refers a reviewable project to the minister, the minister may determine, by order,

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (a) the scope of the required assessment of the reviewable project, and

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (b) procedures and methods for conducting the assessment.

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (2) The minister's discretion under this section to determine scope, procedures and methods includes, but is not limited to, the discretion to exercise, by order, any of the powers under section 19 (2).

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (3) An order of the minister under this section may

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (a) require that the assessment be conducted

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (i)  by a commission that the minister may constitute for the purpose of the assessment, consisting of one or more individuals that the minister may appoint to the commission,

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (ii)  by a hearing panel, with a public hearing to be held by one or more individuals that the minister may appoint to the hearing panel, or

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (iii)  by the chief executive assessment officer, an Indigenous nation or an individual that the minister may appoint by any method or procedure that the minister considers appropriate and specifies in the order, and

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (b) delegate any of the minister's powers under this section to make orders determining scope, procedures and methods to

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (i)  the chief executive assessment officer, or

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (ii)  an Indigenous nation, a commission member, hearing panel member or other individual, depending on which of them is responsible for conducting the assessment.

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (4) The minister may authorize the chief executive assessment officer or, if an order under subsection (3) (a) has been made, the assessment body conducting the assessment to vary the scope, procedures and methods of the assessment.

heading: Process planning by minister
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of an assessment conducted under this section by a commission or hearing panel, the minister, by order, may confer on the commission or hearing panel, as the case may be, the powers, privileges and protection of a commission under sections 16, 17, 22 (1), 23 (a), (b) and (d) to (f) and 32 of the Public Inquiry Act.

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: 25		  (1) The effects of a project on Indigenous nations and rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 must be assessed in every assessment.

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (2) The following matters must be considered in every assessment:

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (a) positive and negative direct and indirect effects of the reviewable project, including environmental, economic, social, cultural and health effects and adverse cumulative effects;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (b) risks and uncertainties associated with those effects, including the results of any interaction between effects;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (c) risks of malfunctions or accidents;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (d) disproportionate effects on distinct human populations, including populations identified by gender;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (e) effects on biophysical factors that support ecosystem function;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (f) effects on current and future generations;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (g) consistency with any land-use plan of the government or an Indigenous nation if the plan is relevant to the assessment and to any assessment conducted under section 35 or 73;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (h) greenhouse gas emissions, including the potential effects on the province being able to meet its targets under the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Targets Act;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (i) alternative means of carrying out the project that are technically and economically feasible, including through the use of the best available technologies, and the potential effects, risks and uncertainties of those alternatives;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (j) potential changes to the reviewable project that may be caused by the environment;

heading: Required assessment matters
paragraph: (k) other prescribed matters.

heading: Advice from consultants, mediators and experts during assessment
paragraph: 26		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer and, subject to any restrictions imposed by the minister, an assessment body appointed under section 24 (3) (a) may retain consultants, mediators and experts and set their remuneration and the terms of their retainers.

heading: Advice from consultants, mediators and experts during assessment
paragraph: (2) All or part of the advice and recommendations of consultants, mediators and experts retained under subsection (1) may be reflected in the assessment report and in any recommendations submitted to the ministers under section 29 (2).

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph:
27
		  (1) The proponent of a reviewable project for which an environmental assessment certificate is required may apply for an environmental assessment certificate in writing to the chief executive assessment officer.

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (2) Within 180 days of receiving an application under subsection (1), the chief executive assessment officer must

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) publish an application received under subsection (1) for 30 days and invite comment from the public on the application, and

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) provide notice to the proponent

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (i)  of the results of the invitation made under paragraph (a),

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (ii)  respecting matters addressed in advice, if any, provided by the technical advisory committee or the community advisory committee, and

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (iii)  respecting any other matter the chief executive assessment officer considers relevant.

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (3) After receiving the notice provided under subsection (2) (b), a proponent may submit a revised application for an environmental assessment certificate.

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (4) The chief executive assessment officer may accept a revised application for review only if the chief executive assessment officer is satisfied that the revised application

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) contains the information required by a process order issued, and

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) responds to the matters set out in the notice provided under subsection (2) (b).

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (5) Before deciding whether to accept a revised application under subsection (4), the chief executive assessment officer must seek to achieve, with respect to the sufficiency of the application under subsection (4), consensus with participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (6) The proponent of a reviewable project for which the minister has made a determination under section 24 may apply for an environmental assessment certificate in the manner determined by the minister.

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph:
28
		  (1) Without limiting sections 19 or 24, on accepting a revised application for review under section 27, the chief executive assessment officer or assessment body, as applicable, must

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (a) provide notice to the proponent of the acceptance of the revised application for review,

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (b) publish a notice that the application meets the applicable requirements of an order issued under section 19 and has been accepted for review, and

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (c) proceed with the assessment procedures determined under section 19 or 24.

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (2) On completion of the assessment, the chief executive assessment officer or assessment body, as applicable, must do all of the following:

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (a) prepare the following:

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (i)  a draft assessment report;

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (ii)  a draft environmental assessment certificate, with certificate conditions and project description;

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (b) publish the documents referred to in paragraph (a) for at least 30 days and invite comment from the public on those documents;

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (c) consider the public comments received and prepare final versions of the documents referred to in paragraph (a), adjusting those documents as the chief executive assessment officer or assessment body, as applicable, considers appropriate.

heading: Effects assessment
paragraph: (3) Before complying with subsection (2) with respect to a project, the chief executive assessment officer must seek to achieve, with respect to the matters referred to in that subsection, consensus with participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph:
29
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), on completion of the requirements set out in section 28 (2) (c), the chief executive assessment officer or assessment body, as applicable, must refer the proponent's revised application for an environmental assessment certificate to the ministers for a decision under subsection (4) of this section.

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (2) A referral under subsection (1) must be made no later than 150 days from acceptance of a proponent's revised application and be accompanied by all of the following:

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) the final versions of the documents referred to in section 28 (2) (c);

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) recommendations respecting the ministers' decision under subsection (4) of this section, including

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (i)  recommendations respecting whether the project is consistent with the promotion of sustainability by protecting the environment and fostering a sound economy and the well-being of British Columbians and their communities,

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (ii)  recommendations respecting the matters referred to in section 25,

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (iii)  a recommendation respecting the duration of the environmental assessment certificate, if issued, and

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (iv)  reasons for the recommendations;

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (c) notification, if any, provided, during the period referred to in section 28 (2) (b), by a participating Indigenous nation of the nation's consent or lack of consent to issuing the environmental assessment certificate and reasons for that consent or lack of consent;

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (d) information, if any, respecting an arrangement reached with a participating Indigenous nation in relation to the potential effects of the project on the nation.

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (3) Before making a recommendation for the purposes of subsection (2) (b) (i), the chief executive assessment officer must seek to achieve, with respect to the recommendation, consensus with participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), on receipt of a referral under subsection (1), the ministers

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) must consider, in addition to the material referred to in subsection (2), the sustainability purpose referred to in section 2 (2) (b) (i), the reconciliation purpose referred to in section 2 (2) (b) (ii) and the prescribed matters, if any,

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) may consider any other matters that they consider relevant to the public interest in making their decision on the application, and

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (c) must, within 30 days of receiving the referral,

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (i)  issue an environmental assessment certificate to the proponent and attach any conditions to the certificate that the ministers consider necessary, including, without limitation, conditions respecting payments to be made for initiatives to mitigate effects of the project, or

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (ii)  refuse to issue the certificate to the proponent.

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (5) If a recommendation under subsection (2) (b) (i) is contrary to the consent or lack of consent indicated in a notice referred to in subsection (2) (c), the ministers must, before making a decision under subsection (4) (c), offer to meet with the participating Indigenous nation that provided the notice.

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (6) If the offer referred to in subsection (5) is accepted within 3 days of the offer being made, the ministers must

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) provide a notice to the proponent that a meeting with the participating Indigenous nation will take place for the purposes of this section, and

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) attend the meeting in an attempt to achieve consensus with the participating Indigenous nation on the decision to be made by the ministers under subsection (4) (c).

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
