paragraph: (7) The ministers must publish reasons for a decision made under subsection (4) (c) and must, in a case where a notification referred to in subsection (2) (c) indicates a lack of consent and the ministers' decision is to issue an environmental assessment certificate, provide reasons for why the decision to issue the certificate was made.

heading: Decision on application for environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (8) The chief executive assessment officer must, at the request of the ministers, assist the ministers with the exercising of their powers and the carrying out of their duties under this section.

heading: Mitigation effectiveness reports
paragraph:
30
		  The holder of an environmental assessment certificate must, in accordance with the direction of the chief executive assessment officer, report to the chief executive assessment officer respecting the effectiveness of mitigation measures specified in the certificate.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph:
31
		  (1) An environmental assessment certificate must specify a deadline, not more than 10 years after the issue date of the certificate, by which deadline the holder of the certificate, in the reasonable opinion of the minister, must have substantially started the project.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (2) The holder of an environmental assessment certificate may apply in writing to the chief executive assessment officer for an extension of the deadline specified in the environmental assessment certificate, providing reasons for why the holder wishes an extension of the deadline.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (3) On receipt of an application under subsection (2), the chief executive assessment officer must complete a review of

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (a) the application, and

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (b) the reasons provided under subsection (2),

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: in accordance with any procedure determined by the minister or the chief executive assessment officer to assess the proposed extension.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (4) The chief executive assessment officer may, on an application under subsection (2),

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (a) extend the deadline specified in the environmental assessment certificate, on one occasion only, for not more than 5 years, and attach any additional conditions that the minister or chief executive assessment officer considers appropriate, or

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (b) refuse to extend the deadline.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (5) Before making a decision under subsection (4) with respect to a project, the chief executive assessment officer must seek to achieve, with respect to the application being considered under that subsection, consensus with participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (6) If, in the reasonable opinion of the minister, the project has not yet been substantially started by the deadline specified in the environmental assessment certificate or by the end of the period of the extension if an extension is granted under subsection (4), the environmental assessment certificate expires.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (7) If, in the reasonable opinion of the minister as set out in subsection (1) or (6), a reviewable project is substantially started, the certificate remains in effect for the life of the project, subject to cancellation or suspension under section 56.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (8) Despite the expiry of a certificate,

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (a) any conditions in the certificate respecting the decommissioning of the project or reclamation activities remain in effect, and

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (b) the minister may issue an order to the former certificate holder respecting decommissioning of the project and reclamation activities.

heading: Duration and effect of certificate
paragraph: (9) Section 53 (2) to (6) applies to orders made under subsection (8) (b) of this section.

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph:
32
		  (1) The holder of an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order may apply in writing to the chief executive assessment officer to amend the certificate or order, providing the holder's reasons for the application.

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer must consider an application under subsection (1) and the reasons provided, in accordance with any procedures determined by the chief executive assessment officer for the assessment of the proposed change, including any time limits.

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (3) After considering the application under subsection (1), the chief executive assessment officer, or the minister if the chief executive assessment officer refers the application to the minister, must

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) amend the environmental assessment certificate or exemption order, varying or removing conditions of the certificate or order or attaching new conditions to the certificate or order that the chief executive assessment officer or minister considers necessary, or

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) refuse to amend the certificate.

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (4) The chief executive assessment officer must provide notice of a decision under subsection (3) to the holder of the environmental assessment certificate.

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (5) The chief executive assessment officer may, without application under subsection (1), amend an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order as described in subsection (3) (a) if

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (a) a person, board, tribunal or agency that has issued or is considering whether to issue an approval under another enactment respecting the project recommends that the amendment be made,

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (b) the chief executive assessment officer considers the amendment appropriate given a report under section 30 or 74,

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (c) in the case of an environmental assessment certificate that has a deadline specified under section 31 (1) of 5 years or more, the fifth anniversary of the issuance of the certificate has occurred, or

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (d) an application has been made under section 31 (2).

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (6) An amendment under subsection (5) (c) may not be made later than 6 months after the anniversary referred to in that provision.

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (7) Before making a decision under subsection (3), (5) (b), (5) (c) or (5) (d) with respect to a project, the chief executive assessment officer must seek to achieve, with respect to the amendment, consensus with participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Amending environmental assessment certificate
paragraph: (8) Before making a decision under subsection (5) (a) with respect to a project, the chief executive assessment officer must be satisfied that the applicable of the person, board, tribunal or agency referred to in that subsection sought to achieve, with respect to the amendment, consensus with participating Indigenous nations.

heading: Transfer of certificate or exemption
paragraph:
33
		  (1) On application by the holder of an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order, the chief executive assessment officer may transfer the certificate or order to another person on any conditions the chief executive assessment officer considers appropriate.

heading: Transfer of certificate or exemption
paragraph: (2) An application under subsection (1) must be made in accordance with the requirements of the chief executive assessment officer.

heading: Transfer of certificate or exemption
paragraph: (3) The chief executive assessment officer may make requirements for the purposes of this section that apply generally or with respect to a specific reviewable project.

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph:
34
		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer may undertake and approve

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (a) partial class assessments that address the matters referred to in section 25 in relation to a specified category of reviewable projects, or

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (b) a full class assessment of the matters referred to in section 25 in relation to a specified category of reviewable projects.

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer may specify conditions and circumstances under which

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (a) a proponent of a reviewable project in a specified category referred to in subsection (1) (a), in applying for an environmental assessment certificate, is exempt from the requirement to provide information for the assessment of effects of the type that were the subject of the partial class assessment, or

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (b) a proponent of a reviewable project in a specified category referred to in subsection (1) (b) may proceed with the reviewable project without an assessment or environmental assessment certificate, subject to compliance with the requirements for the project under other enactments.

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (3) Before exercising a power under subsection (1) or (2), the chief executive assessment officer must seek to achieve consensus with Indigenous nations having rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 that could be affected by the assessment.

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (4) A proponent of a reviewable project in a specified category referred to in subsection (1) (a) to whom subsection (2) (a) applies must comply with the requirements of the relevant partial class assessment referred to in subsection (1) (a).

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (5) A proponent of a reviewable project in a specified category referred to in subsection (1) (b) to whom subsection (2) (b) applies must comply with

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (a) the requirements of the relevant full class assessment referred to in subsection (1) (b), and

heading: Class assessments and their effect on application requirements
paragraph: (b) the requirements for the project under other enactments.

heading: Regional assessments
paragraph: 35		  (1) The minister may direct the chief executive assessment officer or an assessment body to do the following, in accordance with terms of reference established by the minister and with regulations made under subsection (3):

heading: Regional assessments
paragraph: (a) undertake an assessment of the environmental, economic, social, cultural and health effects of any projects in a region of the province;

heading: Regional assessments
paragraph: (b) provide a report and recommendations to the minister at the conclusion of the assessment.

heading: Regional assessments
paragraph: (2) Before making a direction under subsection (1), the minister must seek to achieve consensus respecting the direction and the terms of reference with Indigenous nations having rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 that could be affected by the assessment.

heading: Regional assessments
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting regional assessments under this section, including, without limitation, regulations respecting

heading: Regional assessments
paragraph: (a) the scope, conduct and funding of an assessment under this section, and

heading: Regional assessments
paragraph: (b) the obligations of the minister when an Indigenous nation proposes that an assessment be carried out under this section.

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: 36		  (1) If an application for an environmental assessment certificate is considered under section 27, or an application to amend an environmental assessment certificate is reviewed under section 32, the chief executive assessment officer, either before or during the consideration or review, may refer a policy matter to the minister responsible or ministers responsible for the policy area for clarification and direction.

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: (2) Any clarification and direction provided under subsection (1) to the chief executive assessment officer by one or more ministers must be reflected in the assessment conducted by the chief executive assessment officer under section 27 or 32.

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: (3) The minister or ministers providing clarification and direction under this section may also recommend to the ministers responsible for making a decision under section 29 (4) that

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: (a) the assessment being conducted by the chief executive assessment officer be terminated, and

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: (b) an environmental assessment certificate not be issued for the reviewable project that is the subject of the assessment.

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: (4) On receipt of any recommendations under subsection (3), or if the ministers to whom a referral is made under subsection (1) are the same ministers who are responsible for making a decision under section 29 (4), the ministers may

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: (a) terminate the review, and provide notice to the proponent that an environmental assessment certificate will not be issued for the project, providing reasons for their decision, or

heading: Policy direction from ministers during assessment
paragraph: (b) decline to terminate the review, and instruct the chief executive assessment officer to continue the assessment in accordance with any direction they may provide.

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph:
37
		  (1) The minister, in relation to an application for an environmental assessment certificate referred to that minister for a determination under section 24,

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (a) may require the chief executive assessment officer or an assessment body, as applicable, to inquire into and recommend whether applications made by the proponent for one or more approvals under other enactments that the minister specifies should be approved, and

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (b) if approval is recommended, and the ministers issue an environmental assessment certificate, may order the person, board, tribunal or agency that has the authority to issue the approvals under other enactments to issue them

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (i)  within a specified time,

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (ii)  in accordance with any conditions specified in the order, and

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (iii)  subject to other reasonable conditions that the person, board, tribunal or agency considers appropriate.

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (2) Despite another enactment, the issuance of an approval under another enactment specified under subsection (1) is

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (a) final and binding, and

heading: Approvals under other enactments
paragraph: (b) not subject to review or appeal under that specified enactment or under the Act of which that enactment forms a part.

heading: Time limits
paragraph:
38
		  (1) If the minister or chief executive assessment officer considers it appropriate in the circumstances, the minister or chief executive assessment officer, on the minister's or officer's own initiative or on application by the proponent or a participating Indigenous nation, may

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (a) extend or impose a time limit for doing anything under this Act, and

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (b) impose conditions in making an extension or imposing a time limit.

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply with respect to section 31.

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (3) An extension of a time limit may be made under subsection (1) even if the previous time limit has expired.

heading: Termination of assessment
paragraph:
39
		  The minister or chief executive assessment officer may terminate an assessment under this Act in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Termination of assessment
paragraph: (a) one year has elapsed since the notice under section 13 (5) was provided and the proponent has not submitted a detailed project description under section 15;

heading: Termination of assessment
paragraph: (b) 3 years have elapsed since a proponent was required to provide information by an order made under section 19 or 24 and the proponent has not provided the information;

heading: Termination of assessment
paragraph: (c) one year has elapsed since the notice under section 27 (2) (b) was provided and the proponent has not submitted a revised application under section 27 (3);

heading: Termination of assessment
paragraph: (d) the proponent otherwise fails to do something required under the Act by the time required.

heading: Project information centre
paragraph:
40
		  (1) For the purpose of facilitating public access to information, data and records relating to assessments conducted under this Act, the project information centre is continued and must be administered and maintained by the chief executive assessment officer.

heading: Project information centre
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer may determine

heading: Project information centre
paragraph: (a) which information, data and records or classes of information, data and records relating to any matter under this Act are to be available to the public through the project information centre,

heading: Project information centre
paragraph: (b) in which form or format the records or classes of records are to be available, and

heading: Project information centre
paragraph: (c) the time during which the records are to be available.

heading: Agreements
paragraph:
41
		  (1) The minister may enter into an agreement with respect to any aspect of an assessment or of an assessment under section 35 or 73 with the following:

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (a) the government of Canada;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (b) the government of one or more provinces or territories;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (c) one or more Indigenous nations;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (d) one or more municipalities or regional districts in British Columbia;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (e) one or more neighbouring jurisdictions outside Canada;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (f) any agency, board, commission, ministry or other organization of British Columbia or of another jurisdiction.

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1) but subject to subsection (5), an agreement under this section may

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (a) provide for a means to substitute another party's or jurisdiction's assessment for an assessment required under this Act, and

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (b) establish procedures with another party or jurisdiction to cooperatively complete an assessment of and regulate a reviewable project.

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (3) For certainty, subsection (2) (a) does not authorize the minister to delegate the ministers' authority to make a decision under section 29.

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (4) If an Indigenous nation indicates interest in entering into an agreement under subsection (1), the chief executive assessment officer must, within 6 months of receiving that indication, enter into discussions with the Indigenous nation if the chief executive assessment officer is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so given

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (a) the projects currently undergoing or anticipated to undergo an assessment under this Act that will affect the Indigenous nation, and

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (b) other discussions taking place or impending under this subsection.

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (5) The minister may not enter into an agreement under subsection (1) with respect to the matter referred to in subsection (2) (a) unless the minister is satisfied that the substituted assessment will do all of the following:

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (a) take into consideration all of the matters referred to in section 25;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (b) give provincial authorities under other provincial enactments an opportunity to participate in the assessment;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (c) require obligations respecting the seeking of consensus with participating Indigenous nations that are similar to obligations under this Act;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (d) give the public an opportunity to participate in the assessment and to access records under the assessment;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (e) result in a report submitted to the chief executive assessment officer for referral to the ministers for a decision;

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (f) give the chief executive assessment officer a right to require from the other party or jurisdiction further information regarding the assessment after the chief executive assessment officer has reviewed the report referred to in paragraph (e).

heading: Agreements
paragraph: (6) The minister may not enter into an agreement under subsection (1) if the agreement would alter an obligation to seek consensus with participating Indigenous nations under this Act or limit a participating Indigenous nation's opportunity to provide notice under section 29 (2) (c).

heading: Variations to accommodate agreements with other jurisdictions
paragraph:
42
		  Effective on the date of an agreement under section 41, and for as long as the agreement remains in effect, both this Act and the regulations are by this section deemed to be varied, in their application to or in respect of a reviewable project that is the subject of the agreement, to the extent necessary to accommodate that agreement.

heading: Agreements with Nisga'a Nation
paragraph:
43
		  The minister may enter into agreements for the purposes set out in paragraph 1 of chapter 10 [Environmental Assessment and Protection] of the Nisga'a Final Agreement.

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph:
44
		  (1) If a final agreement requires the government to negotiate with a treaty first nation and attempt to reach agreement on harmonizing the government's and treaty first nation's procedures in relation to evaluating proposed developments on the treaty lands of the treaty first nation, the minister, on behalf of the government, may enter into an agreement reached in the negotiation.

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph: (2) If a reviewable project

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph: (a) is proposed for land specified in a final agreement as land in relation to which notice of a reviewable project is required in the circumstances described in paragraph (b), and

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph: (b) may reasonably be expected to adversely affect the treaty lands of the treaty first nation, the residents of those treaty lands or the rights of the treaty first nation under the final agreement,

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph: the chief executive assessment officer, on receiving the proposal, must

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph: (c) promptly provide notice of the project, along with relevant information about the project, to the treaty first nation,

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph: (d) consult, within the meaning of the final agreement of the treaty first nation, with the treaty first nation, and

heading: Agreements and consultations with treaty first nations
paragraph: (e) ensure that the treaty first nation has an opportunity to participate in any environmental assessment of the project.

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph:
45
		  (1) At any time before a decision is made under section 29 (4) about the proponent's revised application for an environmental assessment certificate or before a decision is made under section 32 (3) about the proponent's application to amend an environmental assessment certificate, the minister may, by order, suspend a process under this Act until the outcome is reached of any investigation, inquiry, hearing, assessment under section 35 or 73 or other process that

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (a) is being or will be conducted by any of the following or any combination of the following:

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (i)  the government of British Columbia, including any agency, board or commission of British Columbia;

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (ii)  the government of Canada;

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (iii)  an Indigenous nation;

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (iv)  a municipality or regional district in British Columbia;

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (v)  a jurisdiction bordering on British Columbia;

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (vi)  another organization, and

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (b) is material, in the reasonable opinion of the minister, to the assessment of the reviewable project under this Act.

heading: Suspension of assessment process pending other inquiries
paragraph: (2) If a time limit is in effect under this Act at the time that an assessment is suspended under subsection (1), the minister may suspend the time limit until the assessment resumes.

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph:
46
		  (1) If the minister considers that

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (a) there is or will be an emergency or other comparable circumstance that warrants or will warrant the variation of one or more provisions of this Act or the regulations, as the provisions apply to or in respect of a specified reviewable project or a specified category of reviewable projects, and

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (b) the variation is in the public interest,

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: the minister may order a variation that the minister considers necessary to respond to the emergency or other circumstance.

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (2) The minister may

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (a) attach conditions to an order made under subsection (1),

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (b) categorize reviewable projects for the purpose of an order made under this section, including into categories that may differ from the categories of reviewable projects prescribed under section 9, and

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (c) provide differently in an order under this section for different reviewable projects or for different categories of reviewable projects.

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (3) An order under subsection (1) is final and binding.

heading: Varying assessment process for emergency or other circumstance
paragraph: (4) In an order under subsection (1), the minister must identify the nature of the emergency or other circumstance.

heading: Assessment costs may be recovered
paragraph:
47
		  (1) The minister or chief executive assessment officer may order the proponent of a reviewable project or the holder of an environmental assessment certificate to pay prescribed fees or prescribed charges for all or part of the costs that are or were incurred by or on behalf of an assessment body in carrying out an assessment of the reviewable project under this Act or in administering this Act.

heading: Assessment costs may be recovered
paragraph: (2) The chief executive assessment officer may require the proponent of a reviewable project or the holder of an environmental assessment certificate to provide security, in the amount and form, and subject to the conditions, specified by the chief executive assessment officer, against the non-payment of fees or charges under this Act.

heading: Assessment costs may be recovered
paragraph: (3) If the proponent of a reviewable project or the holder of an environmental assessment certificate fails to pay a fee or charge required to be paid under this Act, the chief executive assessment officer, after providing notice to the proponent or holder to remedy the failure, may apply all or part of the security toward payment of the fee or charge.

heading: Assessment costs may be recovered
paragraph: (4) The chief executive assessment officer may refund to the proponent or holder all or a portion of the security provided by the proponent under this section, and interest earned on the security, if the chief executive assessment officer considers the refunded amount is no longer required for the purpose referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Participation costs
paragraph:
48
		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer may establish a tariff of costs to be paid by proponents to participating Indigenous nations to defray the nations' following costs:

heading: Participation costs
paragraph: (a) costs of participating in an assessment, including participating in proceedings under section 5;

heading: Participation costs
paragraph: (b) costs of assisting with inspections under section 49.

heading: Participation costs
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a tariff established under that subsection may set out different costs for different classes of costs and for different classes of projects depending on

heading: Participation costs
paragraph: (a) the size and complexity of the projects,

heading: Participation costs
paragraph: (b) potential effects of the projects on Indigenous nations, and

heading: Participation costs
paragraph: (c) any other criteria the chief executive assessment officer considers appropriate.

heading: Inspection power
paragraph:
49
		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer may appoint individuals, by name or by title, as compliance and enforcement officers.

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (2) In making appointments under subsection (1), the chief executive assessment officer may restrict the powers of the individuals appointed to a subset of powers set out in this Act.

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (3) For any purpose related to the administration of this Act or the regulations, a compliance and enforcement officer may enter at any reasonable time on property that is the site of a reviewable project or on property that is the site of facilities that are ancillary to the reviewable project or on any other property where the officer reasonably believes that relevant things referred to in paragraphs (b) to (d) may be stored, and may do any or all of the following:

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (a) inspect any works or activity connected with the reviewable project;

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (b) take away samples;

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (c) examine and take away copies of records related to the reviewable project;

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (d) use any machine, structure, material or equipment in the place that is being inspected as is necessary to carry out the inspection;

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (e) take photographs or make audio or video records.

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (4) A compliance and enforcement officer who enters on property under subsection (3), on request of a person present on the property, must provide evidence to the person of the officer's authorization to enter the property.

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (5) A person must, on request of a compliance and enforcement officer,

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (a) produce, without charge or unreasonable delay, for examination by the compliance and enforcement officer any document related to the reviewable project as requested by the officer,

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (b) provide the compliance and enforcement officer with information relevant to the purposes of the inspection, and

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (c) operate a thing, carry out a procedure or demonstrate a relevant skill, as the officer directs.

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (6) A person must not

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (a) obstruct or interfere with a compliance and enforcement officer acting under the authority of this section, or

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (b) withhold, destroy, tamper with, alter, conceal or refuse to produce anything requested under subsection (5).

heading: Inspection power
paragraph: (7) A compliance and enforcement officer who enters on property under subsection (3) may take with the officer any individuals and equipment that may be necessary for the purpose of the entry.

heading: Compliance and enforcement agreements
paragraph:
50
		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer may enter into an agreement with any of the entities referred to in section 41 (1) respecting the exercising of the powers under section 49, 52 or 53.

heading: Compliance and enforcement agreements
paragraph: (2) In addition to the power referred to in section 4, the chief executive assessment officer may, in an agreement under subsection (1), delegate a power referred to in that section.

heading: Compliance and enforcement agreements
paragraph: (3) If an Indigenous nation indicates interest in entering into an agreement under subsection (1), the chief executive assessment officer must, within 6 months of receiving that indication, enter into discussions with the Indigenous nation unless the chief executive assessment officer considers that there are insufficient resources to enter into those discussions at that time.

heading: Protection of compliance and enforcement officers
paragraph:
51
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), no legal proceedings for damages lie or may be commenced or maintained against a compliance and enforcement officer for anything done or omitted

heading: Protection of compliance and enforcement officers
paragraph: (a) in the performance or intended performance of any duty under this or another enactment, or

heading: Protection of compliance and enforcement officers
paragraph: (b) in the exercise or intended exercise of any power under this or another enactment.

heading: Protection of compliance and enforcement officers
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to anything done or omitted in bad faith.

heading: Investigation power
paragraph:
52
		  (1) On information on oath from a compliance and enforcement officer that there are reasonable grounds to believe that an offence under this Act has occurred or is occurring, a justice, on being satisfied that an entry and a search are likely to provide evidence of such an offence, may issue a warrant authorizing a compliance and enforcement officer

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (a) to enter and search the real or personal property specified in the warrant,

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (b) to seize and remove anything that the officer has reasonable grounds to believe is evidence of an offence,

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (c) to take other actions as the justice considers appropriate in the circumstances and authorizes in the warrant, and

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (d) to take with the officer individuals and equipment that may be necessary for the purpose of the entry.

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a compliance and enforcement officer may do the following without a warrant, if the conditions for obtaining a warrant exist but because of exigent circumstances it is not practicable to obtain the warrant:

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (a) search real or personal property;

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (b) seize and remove anything that the officer has reasonable grounds to believe may provide evidence of the commission of an offence under this Act.

heading: Investigation power
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), "exigent circumstances" means circumstances in which the delay necessary to obtain the warrant would result in danger to human life or safety or the loss or destruction of evidence.

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph:
53
		  (1) If the chief executive assessment officer considers that there is or is likely to be a contravention of this Act, an environmental assessment certificate or an exemption order, the chief executive assessment officer may order a person to

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (a) stop doing something that is or is likely to be in contravention of this Act, the certificate or the order, or cause it to be stopped,

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (b) take any measure that the chief executive assessment officer considers necessary in order to comply with this Act, the certificate or exemption order to mitigate the effects of non-compliance, or

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (c) cease, either altogether or to the extent specified by the chief executive assessment officer, the construction, operation, modification, dismantling or abandonment of anything or any other activities under the certificate or order.

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (2) If the person does not comply with the order within the time specified, the chief executive assessment officer may carry out the measures required.

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (3) An order under this section may be made to apply generally or to one or more persons named in the order.

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (4) Costs incurred by the chief executive assessment officer under subsection (2) may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (5) If a person fails to pay a debt referred to in subsection (4), the chief executive assessment officer may file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, upon filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (6) A certificate under subsection (5) may be in the prescribed form, must be signed by the chief executive assessment officer and must contain

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the debt,

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (b) the contravention or failure in relation to which the costs were incurred, and

heading: Order to cease or remedy
paragraph: (c) the amount of the costs.

heading: Supreme Court order for compliance
paragraph:
54
		  (1) If the minister considers that any person or organization is not complying or has not complied with an order made under this Act, the minister may apply to the Supreme Court for either or both of the following:

heading: Supreme Court order for compliance
paragraph: (a) an order directing the person or organization to comply with the order or restraining the person or organization from violating the order;

heading: Supreme Court order for compliance
paragraph: (b) an order directing the directors and officers of the person or organization to cause the person or organization to comply with or cease violating the order.

heading: Supreme Court order for compliance
paragraph: (2) On application by the minister under this section, the Supreme Court may make an order it considers appropriate.

heading: Compliance agreement
paragraph:
55
		  (1) If the minister considers it appropriate to do so, the minister may give the holder of an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order an opportunity to make a written compliance agreement with the minister, by which the holder undertakes to comply with the environmental assessment certificate or exemption order within the time and on the terms specified in the agreement.

heading: Compliance agreement
paragraph: (2) Despite a written compliance agreement, the minister may make an order referred to in section 53 in respect of the holder of an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order or another person that is the subject of an order under section 53

heading: Compliance agreement
paragraph: (a) on matters not covered by the agreement,

heading: Compliance agreement
paragraph: (b) on matters covered in the agreement if the agreement is not complied with, and

heading: Compliance agreement
paragraph: (c) on matters covered in the agreement if not all the material facts related to those matters were known by the minister at the time of the agreement.

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph:
56
		  (1) If the minister considers that a circumstance listed in subsection (2) is the case, the minister may, by order,

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (a) suspend all or some of the rights of the holder of an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order under the certificate or order or cancel an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order, or

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (b) amend or attach new conditions to an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order.

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (2) The circumstances referred to in subsection (1) are the applicable of the following:

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (a) the holder of the environmental assessment certificate does not substantially start the project by the deadline specified in the certificate;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (b) on the twentieth anniversary of the issuance of the certificate the project is not operational;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (c) the minister has reasonable and probable grounds to believe that the holder of the certificate or exemption order is in default of

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (i)  an order of the Supreme Court made under section 54, 69 or 71,

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (ii)  an order of the chief executive assessment officer or minister made under section 53 or 55 (2), as the case may be, or

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (iii)  one or more requirements of the certificate;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (d) the holder of the certificate or exemption order has been convicted of an offence under this Act;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (e) the holder of the certificate or exemption order is in default of an order made under section 47 to pay costs;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (f) the holder of the certificate or exemption order fails to pay a penalty imposed under section 60 within the prescribed time.

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (3) Any amendment made or condition attached to an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order under this section is conclusively deemed to be part of the certificate or order, whether contained in or attached to it or contained in a separate document.

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (4) The chief executive assessment officer, on request by a holder of an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order, may, by order, cancel the environmental assessment certificate or rescind the order.

heading: Suspension, cancellation and amendment of certificates and exemption orders
paragraph: (5) The chief executive assessment officer may attach conditions the officer considers necessary to an order made under subsection (4).

heading: Notice requirements
paragraph:
57
		  (1) Except in a situation that the minister considers to be an emergency that warrants immediate action without notice to the holder or former holder of an environmental assessment certificate, the minister must not make an order under section 56 without first giving the holder or former holder an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Notice requirements
paragraph: (2) Immediately after the minister makes an order under section 56 or provides notice under subsection (1) of this section, the chief executive assessment officer must deliver a copy of the order to the holder of the certificate or the former holder, as the case may be.

heading: Notice requirements
paragraph: (3) Not later than 15 days after delivery under subsection (2) of a copy of the order, the holder or former holder of the certificate, if not given an opportunity to be heard before the making of the order, may require an opportunity to be heard by the minister, by written notice provided to the minister.

heading: Opportunity to be heard
paragraph:
58
		  As soon as practicable after receiving written notice under section 57 (3), the minister must give the holder or former holder who provided the notice an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Reinstatement of certificate
paragraph:
59
		  The minister may, by order,

heading: Reinstatement of certificate
paragraph: (a) cancel a condition attached to an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order under section 56, or

heading: Reinstatement of certificate
paragraph: (b) subject to any conditions the minister considers appropriate, reinstate an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order that has been suspended or cancelled under section 56.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
60
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, if the chief executive assessment officer is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that a person has

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of this Act or the regulations,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (i)  an order under this Act, or

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (ii)  an environmental assessment certificate, or

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) made a statement in a record filed or provided under this Act that is false or misleading with respect to a material fact or that omits to state a material fact, the omission of which makes the statement false or misleading,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: the chief executive assessment officer may serve the person with a determination requiring the person to pay an administrative penalty in the amount specified in the determination.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) A determination under subsection (1) must be in the prescribed form and contain the prescribed information.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) An administrative penalty imposed under this section must be paid within the prescribed time.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) If the chief executive assessment officer provides an administrative penalty notice to a person in respect of a contravention, failure or statement referred to in subsection (1), a prosecution for an offence under this Act in respect of the same contravention, failure or statement may not be brought against the person.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (5) If a corporation contravenes a provision referred to in subsection (1) (a), fails to comply as set out in subsection (1) (b) or makes a statement as described in subsection (1) (c), an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention, failure or statement is also liable under this section even though the corporation is liable for or pays an administrative penalty.

heading: Effect of charging an offence
paragraph:
61
		  A person who has been charged with an offence under this Act may not be subject to an administrative penalty in respect of the circumstances that gave rise to the charge.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
62
		  (1) An administrative penalty under this Act may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required under section 60, the chief executive assessment officer may file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, upon filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) may be in the prescribed form, must be signed by the chief executive assessment officer and must contain

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the penalty,

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) the contravention or failure in relation to which the penalty is imposed, and

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the penalty that remains unpaid.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
63
		  (1) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) contravenes section 6 (1) or (2) or 49 (5) or (6);

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) fails to comply with

heading: Offences
paragraph: (i)  an order under this Act, or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (ii)  an environmental assessment certificate;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) makes a statement in a record filed or provided under this Act that is false or misleading with respect to a material fact or that omits to state a material fact, the omission of which makes the statement false or misleading.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) A person does not commit an offence under subsection (2) (c) if, at the time of the statement, the person did not know that the statement was false or misleading and could not reasonably have known that the statement was false or misleading.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (4) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, any employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorizes, permits or acquiesces in the offence commits the same offence, whether or not the corporation is convicted of the offence.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (5) If a contravention continues for more than one day, the offender is liable to a separate penalty, without notice and without a separate count being laid, for each day that the contravention occurs.

heading: Effect of voluntary compliance agreement
paragraph: 64		  A holder of an environmental assessment certificate that

heading: Effect of voluntary compliance agreement
paragraph: (a) enters into a voluntary compliance agreement approved under section 55 by the minister, and

heading: Effect of voluntary compliance agreement
paragraph: (b) is complying fully with the agreement

heading: Effect of voluntary compliance agreement
paragraph: does not commit an offence under section 63 (2) in respect of a contravention of this Act that the agreement is intended to rectify.

heading: Penalties
paragraph:
65
		  A person who commits an offence under section 63 is liable,

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) in the case of a corporation on a first conviction, to a fine of not more than $1 000 000 and, on each subsequent conviction, to a fine of not more than $2 000 000, and

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) in the case of an individual

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (i)  on a first conviction, to a fine of not more than $1 000 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 6 months or to both, and

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (ii)  on each subsequent conviction, to a fine of not more than $2 000 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 12 months or to both.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph:
66
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any punishment imposed, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order that does one or more of the following:

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (a) prohibits the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (b) directs the person to take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (c) directs the person to pay the government an amount of money as compensation, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken by or caused to be taken on behalf of the government as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (d) directs the person to perform community service;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (e) directs the person to post a bond or pay into court an amount of money the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (f) directs the person to publish, in any manner and by the time the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (g) requires the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the person's good conduct and for preventing the person from repeating the offence or committing other offences under this Act.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to comply with an order referred to in subsection (1) (f) directing the person to publish the facts relating to the commission of an offence, the minister may publish those facts and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (3) If an order under this section directs a person to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose, or if the minister incurs publication costs under subsection (2), the amounts and any interest payable on those amounts constitute a debt due to the government and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (4) A person who contravenes an order under this section commits an offence and is liable to the penalties provided for the offence in relation to which the order was made.

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph:
67
		  (1) An application for variation of an order under section 66 may be made to the court that made the order by

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (a) the Attorney General, or

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (b) the person against whom the order under section 66 was made.

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (2) Before hearing an application under subsection (1), the court may order the applicant to provide notice of the application in accordance with the directions of the court.

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (3) On an application under subsection (1), if the court considers variation appropriate because of a change in circumstances, the court may make an order that does one or more of the following:

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (a) changes the original order or any conditions specified in it;

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (b) relieves the person referred to in subsection (1) (b) absolutely or partially from compliance with all or part of the original order;

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (c) reduces the period for which the original order is to remain in effect;

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (d) extends by no more than one year the period for which the original order is to remain in effect.

heading: Variation of section 66 orders
paragraph: (4) If an application under subsection (1) has been heard by a court, no other application may be made in respect of the order under section 66 except with leave of the court.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph:
68
		  Subject to sections 60 (4) and 61, a proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under this Act does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Court order to comply
paragraph:
69
		  If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, then, in addition to any punishment the court may impose, the court may order the person to comply with the provisions of this Act.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph:
70
		  A proceeding for an offence under this Act may not be commenced in any court more than 3 years after the facts on which the proceedings are based first come to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Restitution
paragraph:
71
		  If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, then, in addition to any other penalty, the court may order the person convicted to pay compensation or make restitution.

heading: Ministerial delegation
paragraph:
72
		  The minister may delegate in writing to any employee of the office any power or duty conferred or imposed on the minister under this Act.

heading: Strategic assessments
paragraph:
73
		  (1) The minister may direct the chief executive assessment officer to do the following, in accordance with terms of reference established by the minister:

heading: Strategic assessments
paragraph: (a) undertake an assessment of any policy, enactment, plan, practice or procedure of the government;

heading: Strategic assessments
paragraph: (b) provide a report and recommendations to the minister at the conclusion of the assessment.

heading: Strategic assessments
paragraph: (2) Before making a direction under subsection (1), the minister must seek to achieve, with respect to the direction and the terms of reference, consensus with Indigenous nations having rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 that could be affected by the assessment.

heading: Strategic assessments
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting

heading: Strategic assessments
paragraph: (a) the scope, conduct and funding of an assessment under this section, and

heading: Strategic assessments
paragraph: (b) the obligations of the office when an Indigenous nation proposes that an assessment be carried out under this section.

heading: Audits
paragraph: 74		  (1) The chief executive assessment officer may order an independent audit of the carrying out of a reviewable project that has been issued an environmental assessment certificate or exemption order.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) must include terms of reference for the audit, which may include terms of reference respecting the use of new mitigation measures.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (3) If requested by an auditor appointed for the purposes of subsection (1), the holder of the environmental assessment certificate or exemption order must submit records in its possession that the auditor determines are relevant to the audit.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (4) Before an audit report is finalized, the auditor must provide to the holder of the environmental assessment certificate or exemption order

heading: Audits
paragraph: (a) a copy of the draft audit report, and

heading: Audits
paragraph: (b) a reasonable opportunity to review and comment on the report.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (5) As soon as practicable after completing an audit, the auditor must submit the final audit report and any comments of the holder of the environmental assessment certificate or exemption order to

heading: Audits
paragraph: (a) the chief executive assessment officer, and

heading: Audits
paragraph: (b) the holder.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph:
75
		  (1) Any Indigenous knowledge of an Indigenous nation that is provided in confidence to the minister, the ministers, the chief executive assessment officer or a dispute resolution officer under this Act is confidential and must not knowingly be, or be permitted to be, disclosed without written consent.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the Indigenous knowledge referred to in that subsection may be disclosed

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (a) if the knowledge is publicly available,

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (b) by court order,

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (c) by the chief executive assessment officer, if the officer considers that the disclosure is necessary for the purposes of procedural fairness, or

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (d) in the prescribed circumstances.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (3) Conditions with respect to the further disclosure of Indigenous knowledge by any person to whom it is disclosed under subsection (2) may be imposed by

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (a) the court, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (b),

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (b) the chief executive assessment officer, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (c), and

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (c) by the prescribed person, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (d).

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (4) The person to whom Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (3) must comply with any conditions imposed under that subsection.

heading: Review of Act
paragraph:
76
		  Within 5 years after the date this section comes into force, the minister must initiate a review of this Act to determine what changes, if any, should be made.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
77
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) In addition to regulations under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting any matter for which regulations are contemplated by this Act;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting fees and charges for the purposes of section 47 and other fees and charges to be paid in respect of any matter in relation to which a service is provided or a duty is performed under this Act, and prescribing by whom the fees and charges are to be paid;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the suspension or termination of a service being provided or a duty being performed under this Act on non-payment of fees or charges or of costs under section 48;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting administrative penalties under section 60, including

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  setting maximum penalties that may be imposed in relation to a specified contravention or failure,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  authorizing administrative penalties to be imposed on a daily basis for continuing contraventions or failures,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iii)  prescribing time limits for paying administrative penalties, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iv)  the consequences of failing to pay an administrative penalty, which may include, but are not limited to, imposing additional penalties;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting qualifications of individuals who may serve on the technical advisory committee, of persons who may undertake reviews referred to in section 19 (2) (c) (ii) and of persons referred to in section 19 (2) (c) (iv) or 26, including, without limitation, qualifications respecting impartiality;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (f) prescribing additional powers and duties of the chief executive assessment officer;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (g) defining a word or expression used but not defined in this Act;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (h) providing that a provision of this Act or of the regulations does not apply to or in respect of a proponent or reviewable project, and prescribing circumstances in which or conditions on which the provision is made inapplicable under this paragraph.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under subsection (2) (a) to (g) may

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) be made applicable generally or to a specific category of proponents or reviewable projects,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) categorize proponents and reviewable projects for the purpose of the regulation, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) provide differently for different categories of proponents and reviewable projects.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: 78		  (1) In this section, "former Act" means the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 43, as it read on the day immediately before the date this section comes into force.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (2) The appointment of the executive director under the former Act is continued as an appointment as the first chief executive assessment officer under this Act.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (3) An environmental assessment certificate issued under the former Act is continued as an environmental assessment certificate under this Act.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (4) A condition in an environmental assessment certificate referred to in subsection (3) that is in respect of the transfer of the certificate to another person is, on the coming into force of this section, cancelled and section 33 of this Act applies.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (5) Despite section 56 (2) (b) of this Act, a circumstance for the purpose of section 56 (1) of this Act in relation to an environmental assessment certificate issued under the former Act is that on the later of the following dates the project is not operational:

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (a) the date that is 5 years after the date this section comes into force;

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (b) the twentieth anniversary of the date the certificate was issued under the former Act.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (7) If an assessment continued under subsection (6) is not completed within 3 years after the date this section comes into force, or if a proponent elects not to provide a notice under subsection (6) with respect to an assessment, the assessment must be completed under this Act and the chief executive assessment officer may make an order

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (a) specifying the step in the environmental assessment process under this Act to which the project must proceed, or

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (b) varying the assessment process to the extent necessary to accommodate the assessment under this Act of that project.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (8) The chief executive assessment officer must give reasons for an order made under subsection (7) and may attach conditions to the order.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (9) If an application under section 19 (1) of the former Act has been made and a decision under subsection (3) of that section has not been made before the date this section comes into force, the former Act applies to that application.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (10) Records that, before the coming into force of this section, were filed or submitted under the former Act may be accepted by the chief executive assessment officer in full or partial fulfillment of the requirements of this Act.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (11) Any order, approval or decision that, immediately before the coming into force of this subsection, is in effect under the former Act

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (a) is deemed to have been issued under this Act, and

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (13), continues in force until it expires or, under this Act, is suspended or cancelled.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (12) An energy operation certificate or energy project certificate under the Utilities Commission Act, S.B.C. 1980, c. 60, an order issued under section 19 (1) of that Act, a mine development certificate or mine operation certificate under the Mine Development Assessment Act, S.B.C. 1990, c. 55, or an approval given as part of the major project review process, if the certificate, order or approval is in effect immediately before the coming into force of this subsection, remains in effect, despite its term or expiry date, for the life of the project in respect of which it was issued, unless it is suspended or cancelled under this Act.

heading: Transitional provisions
paragraph: (13) During the 6-month period beginning on the date this subsection comes into force, the chief executive assessment officer, with respect to a certificate that remains in effect under subsection (3), may remove or amend, by order, any condition that requires the holder of the certificate, for the life of the certificate, to seek the written consent of the minister before materially altering the project that is the subject of the certificate.

heading: Repealed
paragraph: Consequential Amendment

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 82		  This Act comes into force by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "accreditation body" means a body that

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) is authorized by the ILAC to perform accreditation with respect to the standard referred to in the definition of "accredited" in this section, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) has, with the ILAC, entered into an agreement known as a Mutual Recognition Agreement;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "accredited" means to have attained impartial and independent accreditation from an accreditation body as conforming with ISO/IEC Standard17043, "Conformity assessment - General requirements for proficiency testing", as amended from time to time;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "air audit" means an ambient particulate monitor audit or a gas analyzer audit (stack and ambient) performed by an employee of the minister's ministry on monitoring equipment required under the terms of an order, permit, licence, approval or certificate;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "ambient particulate monitor audit" means an audit of

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the performance of an ambient particulate monitor and associated equipment used to produce or gather air samples, analytic results, data and reports, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) records related to that performance;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "director" includes the administrator, or an inspector, as defined in the Integrated Pest Management Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "directory"means the directory of qualified laboratories, published by the ministry of the minister for the purposes of this regulation;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "gas analyzer audit (stack and ambient)" means an audit of

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the performance of a gas analyzer and associated equipment used to produce or gather air samples, analytic results, data and reports, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) records related to that performance;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "ILAC" means the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "interlaboratory comparison study" means a comparison of the results of testing conducted by 2 or more laboratories with respect to the same or similar parameters;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "ISO/IEC" means the International Organization for Standardization and the International Electrotechnical Commission;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "officer" includes a person employed by a municipality who is

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) designated in writing by a director, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) a member of a class designated in writing by a director;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "parameter" means a chemical, biological or physical constituent with respect to which sampling, analysis and environmental monitoring is required under an authorization;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "proficiency testing program" means an interlaboratory comparison program

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) that is administered by an accredited proficiency testing provider, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) under which laboratories participating in interlaboratory comparison studies analyze reference samples and report, to the accredited proficiency testing provider, results for evaluation;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "qualified laboratory", in respect of a test, means a laboratory that is listed in the directory of qualified laboratories as qualified to perform the test;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "reference laboratory" means a laboratory, designated by the director, whose performance is unbiased as demonstrated in inter-laboratory performance studies or blind audits;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "reference sample" means a sample with assigned design, or assigned consensus concentration values, for one or more parameters;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "split sample" means a liquid sample which is split and added to 2 separate containers so that each part of the split sample has identical parameters whose reference concentration values are assigned by analysis by a reference laboratory;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "standard sample" means a sample whose reference concentration value for one or more characteristics is assigned by using a design value based on gravimetric or volumetric measurement.

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: 2		  (1) A person required to collect samples and submit environmental monitoring data as a requirement of an order, permit, licence, approval or certificate issued under an enactment administered by the minister must

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (a) cause the samples to be analyzed by a qualified laboratory for the parameters specified in the order, permit, licence, approval or certificate, and

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (b) provide to the director, not later than 45 days after the date the sample is collected, the results of the qualified laboratory's analysis.

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (2) If a director requires that an officer, or another person the director designates, collect a split sample in respect of monitoring required under an order, permit, licence, approval or certificate referred to in subsection (1), the person subject to the order, permit, licence, approval or certificate must

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (a) cause one part of the split sample to be analyzed by a qualified laboratory for the parameters specified by the director, and

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (b) provide to the director, not later than 45 days after the date the sample is collected, the results of the qualified laboratory's analysis.

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (3) A person required to collect samples and submit environmental monitoring data as a requirement of an order, permit, licence, approval or certificate issued under an enactment administered by the minister, must, on the request of a director, provide to the director, not later than 45 days after the date the samples are analyzed, the results of the analysis of standard samples of gases introduced to an emission analyzer, or ambient air analyzer, operated as a requirement of the order, permit, licence, approval or certificate.

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (4) A person required to collect samples under this section must

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (a) follow the sampling procedures as specified or authorized by the director, and

heading: Sampling, analytical, quality control and reporting procedures
paragraph: (b) on the request of a director, provide a report describing the methods used to collect and analyze the samples.

heading: Cost recovery
paragraph:
4
