		  (1) A person required to submit environmental monitoring data as a requirement of an order, permit, licence, approval or certificate under an enactment administered by the Minister of Environment shall reimburse the Ministry of Environment for the ministry's costs of auditing samples, analytical results and data submitted to the director.

heading: Cost recovery
paragraph: (1.1) Despite subsection (1), the amount set out in column 2 of the following table opposite the class of air audit set out in column 1 of the table is the fee payable for an air audit in that class.

heading: Cost recovery
paragraph: (2) Amounts under subsection (1) or (1.1) must be paid to the minister within 30 days after the date on the invoice provided to the person by the minister.

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph:
5
		  (1) To become and remain listed in the directory as a qualified laboratory with respect to testing for a parameter, a laboratory must do both of the following:

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph: (a) achieve satisfactory testing performance in a proficiency testing program for the parameter, or, if a proficiency testing program is not available with respect to the parameter, either of the following, as approved by a director:

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph: (i)  an interlaboratory comparison study;

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph: (ii)  an analyst competency study;

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph: (b) give to the director authorization for the accredited proficiency testing provider that administers the proficiency testing program or study referred to in paragraph (a) to inform the director of all parameters with respect to which the laboratory has either

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph: (i)  achieved satisfactory testing performance, or

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph: (ii)  failed to maintain satisfactory testing performance.

heading: Directory of qualified laboratories
paragraph: (2) A laboratory must give the authorization referred to in subsection (1) (b) in the form and manner required by the director.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: CAS registry number means the identification number assigned to a substance by the Chemical Abstracts Service, a division of the American Chemical Society. (numero d'enregistrement CAS)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: container system means any receptacle or network of receptacles that is used to contain a substance - including any connected pipelines or piping - except any part of that network that is automatically or remotely segregated from the rest of the network by shut-off valves, or other mechanisms, in the event of any environmental emergency. (systeme de reservoirs)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: simulation exercise means an exercise simulating the response to an environmental emergency involving the release of a substance. (exercice de simulation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: facility means a property on which one or more fixed onshore installations are located and where a substance is present. (installation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: full-scale simulation exercise means an action-based simulation exercise requiring the deployment of personnel, resources and equipment. (exercice general de simulation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: maximum capacity means, in respect of a container system, its full physical capacity, expressed in tonnes, including any capacity that is beyond the safe-fill limit set by the manufacturer of the receptacles that comprise the container system. (capacite maximale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: responsible person means any person who owns or has the charge, management or control of a substance that is located at a facility. (responsable)

heading: Maximum expected quantity
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of these Regulations, the maximum expected quantity of a substance is to be determined in accordance with subsections 3(1) to (4) for the one-year period beginning on the day on which the applicable situation referred to in subsection 3(1) or (5) occurs or the one-year period beginning on the day on which a notice is submitted under section 13.

heading: List
paragraph: 2 (1) For the purposes of the definition substance in section 193 of the Act, the list of substances consists of

heading: List
paragraph: (a) the substances having a CAS registry number set out in column 1 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 and that, if present in a mixture, are in a concentration that is greater than or equal to the concentration set out in column 3 of that Part; and

heading: List
paragraph: (b) the solutions having a CAS registry number set out in column 1 of Part 2 of Schedule 1, if the concentration of the solute in the solution is greater than or equal to the concentration set out in column 3 of that Part and, in the case of a solution that is present in a mixture, if the concentration of the solute in the mixture is greater than or equal to the concentration set out in column 3 of that Part.

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (2) The following substances are excluded from the list referred to in subsection (1):

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (a) a substance that is identified in column 5 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 as combustible or likely to explode and

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (i) is in a mixture that has a flashpoint greater than 23 °C and a boiling point greater than 35 °C, or

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (ii) is a component of natural gas in its gaseous form;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (b) a substance that is identified in column 5 of Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 1 as an inhalation hazard and is in a mixture, in gaseous or liquid form, that has a total vapour pressure of less than 1.33 kPa;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (c) a substance that is used to fuel a heating appliance or to generate power at the facility where it is located and is present in a quantity that is less than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 for that substance;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (d) a substance that is regulated under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992 or the Canada Shipping Act, 2001;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (e) a substance that is in a pipeline that is regulated under the National Energy Board Onshore Pipeline Regulations or in a processing plant that is regulated under the National Energy Board Processing Plant Regulations;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (f) a substance that is in a pipeline located entirely within a province and that is on a property where there are no fixed onshore installations other than pipelines, compressor stations or pump stations;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (g) a substance that is in a fuel tank that is connected to and supplies the engine of a conveyance that is used for transportation;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (h) the substance set out in item 57 of Part 1 of Schedule 1, if it is in a solid form;

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (i) the substance set out in item 143 of Part 1 of Schedule 1, if it is in the form of solid particles that measure more than 10 μm in diameter; and

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (j) the substance set out in item 167 of Part 1 of Schedule 1, if it is in a form other than white phosphorous.

heading: Notice
paragraph: 3 (1) A responsible person must, within 90 days after the day on which either of the following situations occurs, submit to the Minister a notice containing the information referred to in Schedule 2 for each facility at which a substance is located:

heading: Notice
paragraph: (a) the total quantity of the substance, whether it is in a container system or not, is equal to or greater than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 1 for that substance; or

heading: Notice
paragraph: (b) a quantity of the substance is placed in a container system that has a maximum capacity that is equal to or greater than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 1 for that substance.

heading: Excluded quantities
paragraph: (2) In determining the quantity of a substance for the purposes of subsection (1), the following quantities are excluded:

heading: Excluded quantities
paragraph: (a) quantities of the substance that are located at the facility for a period of 72 hours or less, unless the substance is loaded or unloaded at the facility, if, during that period, the person keeps evidence of the date and time at which the quantities of the substance arrived at the facility;

heading: Excluded quantities
paragraph: (b) quantities of the substance that are in a container system that has a maximum capacity of 0.03 t or less;

heading: Excluded quantities
paragraph: (c) quantities of the substance that are found in slag, waste rock, tailings, solid residues, ores and ore concentrates;

heading: Excluded quantities
paragraph: (d) quantities of the substance set out in item 17 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 that are in a container system that has a maximum capacity of less than 10 t and is located at least 360 m from all points along the boundary of the facility; and

heading: Excluded quantities
paragraph: (e) quantities of a substance set out in item 163 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 or item 5 or 9 of Part 2 of that Schedule that are located at a farming operation for on-site use as an agricultural nutrient.

heading: Determination of Quantity - Part 1 of Schedule 1
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), the quantity of a substance set out in Part 1 of Schedule 1 that is in a mixture is to be determined by multiplying the quantity of the mixture, expressed in tonnes, by the concentration, expressed in percentage (mass/mass), of the substance in the mixture.

heading: Determination of Quantity - Part 2 of Schedule 1
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (1), the quantity of a substance that is a solution set out in Part 2 of Schedule 1 is to be determined

heading: Determination of Quantity - Part 2 of Schedule 1
paragraph: (a) in the case of a solution that is not in a mixture, by multiplying the quantity of the solution, expressed in tonnes, by the concentration expressed in percentage (mass/mass) of the solute in the solution; and

heading: Determination of Quantity - Part 2 of Schedule 1
paragraph: (b) in the case of a solution that is in a mixture,

heading: Determination of Quantity - Part 2 of Schedule 1
paragraph: (i) if the concentration of the solute in the solution is available, by multiplying the quantity of the mixture, expressed in tonnes, by the concentration expressed in percentage (mass/mass) of the solute in the solution and the concentration expressed in percentage (mass/mass) of the solution in the mixture, and

heading: Determination of Quantity - Part 2 of Schedule 1
paragraph: (ii) if the concentration of the solute in the solution is not available, by multiplying the quantity of the mixture, expressed in tonnes, by the percentage (mass/mass) of the solution in the mixture.

heading: Notice of change
paragraph: (5) A responsible person must, within 60 days after the day on which any of the following situations occurs, submit an updated notice to the Minister that contains the information referred to in Schedule 2:

heading: Notice of change
paragraph: (a) the information that was reported under section 1 or 2 of Schedule 2 has changed;

heading: Notice of change
paragraph: (b) the maximum expected quantity that was most recently reported under paragraph 3(d) of Schedule 2 in respect of a substance has increased by 10% or more; or

heading: Notice of change
paragraph: (c) the maximum capacity that was most recently reported under paragraph 3(f) of Schedule 2 in respect of a container system, in which a quantity of a substance is contained, has increased by 10% or more.

heading: Preparation
paragraph: 4 (1) A responsible person must, for each facility at which a substance is located, prepare an environmental emergency plan with respect to the substance under the following circumstances:

heading: Preparation
paragraph: (a) if some or all of the substance is not in a container system, a responsible person has reported a maximum expected quantity under paragraph 3(d) of Schedule 2 that is equal to or greater than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 for that substance; or

heading: Preparation
paragraph: (b) if the substance is in a container system, a responsible person has reported

heading: Preparation
paragraph: (i) under paragraph 3(d) of Schedule 2, a maximum expected quantity that is equal to or greater than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 1 for that substance, and

heading: Preparation
paragraph: (ii) under paragraph 3(f) of Schedule 2, a maximum capacity that is equal to or greater than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 1 for that substance.

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (2) The environmental emergency plan must include the following:

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (a) a description of the properties and characteristics of the substance and the maximum expected quantity of the substance at the facility;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (b) a description of the commercial, manufacturing, processing or other activity involving the substance that takes place at the facility;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (c) a description of the facility and of the area surrounding the facility that may be affected by an environmental emergency referred to in paragraph (d), including any hospitals, schools, residential, commercial or industrial buildings and any highways, public transit infrastructure, parks, forests, wildlife habitats, water sources or water bodies;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (d) an identification of any environmental emergency that could reasonably be expected to occur at the facility and that would likely cause harm to the environment or constitute a danger to human life or health, including the environmental emergency referred to in paragraph (e) and, if applicable, the environmental emergency that is more likely to occur than the environmental emergency referred to in paragraph (e) and that would have the longest impact distance outside the boundary of the facility;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (e) an identification of the harm to the environment or danger to human life or health that would likely result from an environmental emergency involving the release of

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (i) the maximum quantity of the substance that could be contained in the container system that has the largest maximum capacity, if a quantity of the substance is in a container system, and

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (ii) the maximum expected quantity of the substance that will not be in a container system, if a quantity of the substance is not in a container system;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (f) an identification of the harm to the environment or danger to human life or health that would likely result from the environmental emergency identified under paragraph (d), if any, that is more likely to occur than the environmental emergency referred to in paragraph (e) and would have the longest impact distance outside the boundary of the facility;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (g) a description of the measures to be taken to prevent and prepare for the environmental emergencies identified under paragraph (d) and the measures that will be taken to respond to and recover from such emergencies if they were to occur;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (h) a list of the position titles of the persons who will make decisions and take a leadership role in the event of an environmental emergency and a description of their roles and responsibilities;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (i) a list of the environmental emergency training that has been or will be provided to prepare personnel at the facility who will respond in the event that an environmental emergency identified under paragraph (d) occurs;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (j) a list of the emergency response equipment that is necessary for the measures described in paragraph (g) and the equipment's location;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (k) a description of the measures that will be taken by a responsible person or by a responsible person and local authorities, acting jointly, to communicate with the members of the public who may be adversely affected by the environmental emergency referred to in paragraph (f) to inform them, before the environmental emergency occurs, of

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (i) the possibility that the environmental emergency could occur,

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (ii) the potential effects of the environmental emergency on the environment and on human life or health, taking into account the factors referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c), and

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (iii) the measures that will be taken by the responsible person to protect the environment and human life or health, and the means by which the responsible person will communicate with them, in the event that the environmental emergency occurs;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (l) a description of the measures that will be taken by a responsible person or by a responsible person and local authorities, acting jointly, to, in the event that an environmental emergency involving the release of a substance occurs, communicate with the members of the public who may be adversely affected to provide them, during and after its occurrence, with information and guidance concerning the actions that could be taken by them to reduce the potential harm to the environment and danger to human life or health, including an explanation of how those actions may help to reduce the harm or danger;

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (m) the position title of the person who will communicate with the members of the public referred to in paragraphs (k) and (l);

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (n) a description of the consultations that a responsible person had with local authorities, if any, with respect to the measures referred to in paragraph (k) and (l); and

heading: Required contents
paragraph: (o) a plan of the facility showing the location of any substances in relation to the physical features of the facility.

heading: Existing plan
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), a responsible person may use an environmental emergency plan that has been prepared on a voluntary basis, or for another government or under another Act of Parliament, if that plan meets the requirements of subsection (2) or is amended so that it meets those requirements.

heading: Adequate measures
paragraph: (4) The measures included in the environmental emergency plan must be adequate to address the objectives of preventing, preparing for, responding to and recovering from the environmental emergencies identified under paragraph (2)(d).

heading: Notice - preparation of plan
paragraph: 5 Within six months after the day on which an environmental emergency plan is required to be prepared under subsection 4(1), a responsible person must inform the Minister that they have prepared the plan or are using a previously prepared plan in accordance with subsection 4(3) by submitting a notice that contains the information referred to in Schedule 3.

heading: Bringing into effect
paragraph: 6 Within 12 months after the day on which an environmental emergency plan is required to be prepared under subsection 4(1), a responsible person must bring the plan into effect and submit a notice to the Minister that contains the information referred to in Schedule 4.

heading: Simulation exercise
paragraph: 7 (1) A responsible person must conduct simulation exercises in relation to each environmental emergency plan that is prepared under subsection 4(1) as follows:

heading: Simulation exercise
paragraph: (a) each year, beginning on the day on which the plan is brought into effect, a simulation exercise in respect of one substance from each of the hazard categories referred to in column 5 of Parts 1 and 2 of Schedule 1, using an environmental emergency identified under paragraph 4(2)(d) as the emergency being simulated; and

heading: Simulation exercise
paragraph: (b) every five years, beginning on the day on which the plan is brought into effect, a full-scale simulation exercise in respect of any one substance, using an environmental emergency referred to in paragraph 4(2)(e) or (f) as the emergency being simulated.

heading: Cycle for simulation exercises
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(a), a simulation exercise conducted in respect of a substance belonging to a given hazard category must simulate a different environmental emergency for each subsequent simulation exercise until all of the environmental emergencies identified under paragraph 4(2)(d) for each of the substances belonging to that hazard category have been simulated, after which the environmental emergencies must be cycled through again.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply in respect of a year during which a full-scale simulation exercise is conducted under paragraph (1)(b).

heading: Record of simulation exercise
paragraph: 8 After each simulation exercise is conducted in relation to the environmental emergency plan, a responsible person must prepare a record that contains the date, a summary and the results of the simulation exercise and any modifications to be made to the plan as a result of the simulation exercise.

heading: Notice - simulation exercises conducted
paragraph: 9 A responsible person must, within five years after the day on which the environmental emergency plan is brought into effect under section 6, submit a notice to the Minister containing the information referred to in Schedule 5 concerning the simulation exercises conducted in relation to an environmental emergency plan.

heading: Updates to the plan
paragraph: 10 A responsible person must review and, if necessary, update the environmental emergency plan at least once a year to ensure that it continues to meet the requirements of subsection 4(2) and keep a record of the date of the review.

heading: Access
paragraph: 11 A responsible person must make a copy of the environmental emergency plan readily available at the facility referred to in subsection 4(1) and at any other place where a copy of the plan needs to be kept for consultation by the individuals who are to carry it out.

heading: Measures under paragraph 201(1)(b) of Act
paragraph: 12 The emergency measures that are to be taken under paragraph 201(1)(b) of the Act include the measures to respond to and recover from an environmental emergency that are set out in the environmental emergency plan.

heading: Notice regarding a substance
paragraph: 13 If a notice has been submitted under subsection 3(1), a responsible person must submit a new notice to the Minister that contains the information referred to in Schedule 2 no later than five years after the day on which the most recent notice containing that information was submitted.

heading: Notice of simulation exercise
paragraph: 14 If a notice has been submitted under section 9, a responsible person must submit a new notice to the Minister that contains the information referred to in Schedule 5 no later than five years after the day on which the most recent notice containing that information was submitted.

heading: Change in quantity or capacity
paragraph: 15 (1) If a notice has been submitted under subsection 3(1) in respect of a substance located at a facility, a responsible person must submit a notice to the Minister if

heading: Change in quantity or capacity
paragraph: (a) the total quantity of the substance located at the facility is, for a period of one year, less than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 1 for that substance; or

heading: Change in quantity or capacity
paragraph: (b) a quantity of the substance is, for a period of one year, no longer found in a container system at the facility that has a maximum capacity that is equal to or greater than the quantity set out in column 4 of Part 1 or 2 of Schedule 1 for that substance.

heading: Time limit for submission
paragraph: (2) The notice must contain the information referred to in Schedule 6 and be submitted no later than 60 days after the end of the period referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b), as the case may be.

heading: Cessation of operations
paragraph: 16 A responsible person who intends to cease operations for a period of one year or more at a facility where a substance is located, for any purpose other than maintenance, must submit a notice containing the information referred to in Schedule 7 to the Minister at least 30 days before the day on which operations are to cease, or as soon as feasible in the case of extraordinary circumstances such as fire, major accident, vandalism, natural disaster or act of terrorism.

heading: Transfer of ownership of facility
paragraph: 17 If there is a transfer of the ownership of a facility where a substance is located, a responsible person must, if a notice has been submitted under subsection 3(1) in respect of the substance, submit a notice containing the information referred to in Schedule 7 to the Minister on or before the date of the transfer.

heading: Paragraph 201(1)(a) of Act
paragraph: 18 (1) For the purposes of these Regulations, paragraph 201(1)(a) of the Act applies only in relation to an environmental emergency that

heading: Paragraph 201(1)(a) of Act
paragraph: (a) has or may have an immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment;

heading: Paragraph 201(1)(a) of Act
paragraph: (b) constitutes or may constitute a danger to the environment on which human life depends; or

heading: Paragraph 201(1)(a) of Act
paragraph: (c) constitutes or may constitute a danger in Canada to human life or health.

heading: Written Report - designated person
paragraph: (2) The person who is designated to be provided with a written report respecting the occurrence of an environmental emergency involving a substance that is on the list referred to in section 2 is the Regional Director, Environmental Enforcement Directorate, Enforcement Branch, Department of the Environment, in the region where the environmental emergency occurs.

heading: Written Report - required contents
paragraph: (3) The written report must include the information referred to in Schedule 8.

heading: Certification
paragraph: 19 (1) Any information that is required to be submitted under these Regulations, and any written report provided under paragraph 201(1)(a) of the Act, must be accompanied by a certification, signed and dated by the person who is required to submit the information or provide the report, or by their authorized representative, stating that the information or report is accurate and complete.

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (2) If the certification is provided by an authorized representative, the authorized representative must provide their name, telephone number and email address.

heading: Electronic submission under these Regulations
paragraph: 20 (1) Any information that is required to be submitted to the Minister under these Regulations must be submitted electronically in the form and format specified by the Minister and bear the electronic signature of the person who is required to submit the information or of their authorized representative.

heading: Electronic submission - written report of environmental emergency
paragraph: (2) Any written report provided under paragraph 201(1)(a) of the Act to an enforcement officer or the person referred to in subsection 18(2) must be submitted electronically in the form and format specified by the Minister and bear the electronic signature of the person who is required to submit the report or of their authorized representative.

heading: Submission on paper
paragraph: (3) If the Minister has not specified a form and format or if it is not feasible to submit the information or report electronically because of circumstances beyond the person's control, the information or report, as the case may be, must be submitted on paper in the form and format specified by the Minister, if any, and be signed by the person or their authorized representative.

heading: Record keeping
paragraph: 21 (1) Any records prepared in accordance with sections 8 and 10 must be kept at the facility referred to in subsection 4(1).

heading: Seven years
paragraph: (2) The records referred to in subsection (1) must be kept for a period of not less than seven years beginning on the day on which they are prepared.

heading: Application of section 3
paragraph: 22 For the purposes of section 3, if either of the situations described in paragraph 3(1)(a) or (b) occurs in respect of a facility before the day on which these Regulations come into force, a responsible person must submit the notice referred to in subsection 3(1) to the Minister within 90 days after the day on which these Regulations come into force.

heading: Repeal
paragraph: Return to footnote 1SOR/2003-307

heading: 180th day after registration
paragraph: 24 These Regulations come into force on the 180th day after the day on which they are registered.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "air" means the atmosphere but does not include the atmosphere inside

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a human made enclosure that is not open to the weather,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an underground mine, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a place designated by order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "air contaminant" means a substance that is introduced into the air and that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) injures or is capable of injuring the health or safety of a person,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) injures or is capable of injuring property or any life form,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) interferes with or is capable of interfering with visibility,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) interferes with or is capable of interfering with the normal conduct of business,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) causes or is capable of causing material physical discomfort to a person, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) damages or is capable of damaging the environment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "appeal board" means the Environmental Appeal Board continued under section 93 [environmental appeal board];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "approval" means an approval under section 15 [approvals] or under a regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "auxiliary conservation officer" means a person designated as an auxiliary conservation officer under section 106 (3) [conservation officer service];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "biomedical waste" has the prescribed meaning;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "chief conservation officer" means the person appointed as chief conservation officer under section 106 (2) [conservation officer service];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "code of practice", except in Part 3 [Municipal Waste Management], means a code of practice established by the minister under section 22 [minister's regulations - codes of practice];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "conservation officer" means a person described in section 106 (2) (a) or (b) [conservation officer service] and includes, in relation to a specific power or duty, an auxiliary conservation officer and a special conservation officer who has been authorized under section 106 (3) (b) (iv) to exercise the power or perform the duty;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Conservation Officer Service" means the Conservation Officer Service established under section 106 [conservation officer service];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "director" means a person employed by the government and designated in writing by the minister as a director of waste management or as an acting, deputy or assistant director of waste management;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "district director" means,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) except in sections 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] and 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts], a person appointed under section 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver] as district director by the board of the Metro Vancouver Regional District,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of section 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver], a person appointed under section 32 (3) as district director by the Administration Board of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) for the purpose of section 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts], a person appointed under section 33 as district director by a regional district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "effluent" means a substance that is introduced into water or onto land and that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) injures or is capable of injuring the health or safety of a person,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) injures or is capable of injuring property or any life form,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) interferes with or is capable of interfering with visibility,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) interferes with or is capable of interfering with the normal conduct of business,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) causes or is capable of causing material physical discomfort to a person, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) damages or is capable of damaging the environment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environment" means air, land, water and all other external conditions or influences under which humans, animals and plants live or are developed;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "facility" includes any land or building, and any machinery, equipment, device, tank, system or other works;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "greenhouse gas" has the same meaning as in the Climate Change Accountability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hazardous waste" has the prescribed meaning;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "introduce into the environment", in relation to waste, includes discharge, emit, dump, abandon, spill, release and allow to escape into the environment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land" means the solid part of the earth's surface including the foreshore and land covered by water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "manager" means a person appointed under the Public Service Act as a manager in the ministry and designated in writing by the minister as a regional manager or as an acting, assistant or deputy regional manager;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipality", except in Part 4 [Contaminated Site Remediation], includes,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a regional district,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an improvement district that has as an object

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the disposal of sewage or refuse, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the provision of a system for the disposal of sewage or refuse or both, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "officer" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person or class of persons employed by the government, a government corporation or a municipality and designated in writing by a director as an officer, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a conservation officer;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "operational certificate" means a certificate issued under section 28 [operational certificates] for the design, operation, maintenance, performance and closure of sites or facilities used for the storage, treatment or disposal of waste or recyclable material;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "order" means an order made or given under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "packaging" means a material, substance or object that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) used to protect, contain or transport a commodity or product, including a material, substance or object that is sold or distributed separately from the commodity or product that it will protect, contain or transport, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) attached to a commodity or product or its container for the purpose of marketing or communicating information about the commodity or product;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permit" means a permit issued under section 14 [permits] or under the regulations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pollution" means the presence in the environment of substances or contaminants that substantially alter or impair the usefulness of the environment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "recyclable material" means a product or substance that has been diverted from disposal, and satisfies at least one of the following criteria:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is organic material from residential, commercial or institutional sources and is capable of being composted, or is being composted, at a site;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is managed as a marketable commodity with an established market by the owner or operator of a site;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is being used in the manufacture of a new product that has an established market or is being processed as an intermediate stage of an existing manufacturing process;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) has been identified as a recyclable material in a waste management plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) is any other material prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, or the minister under section 22 [minister's regulations - codes of practice];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "refuse" means discarded or abandoned materials, substances or objects;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regional district", except in the definition of "municipality" and in sections 25, 26 and 30, includes the Northern Rockies Regional Municipality;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "registered mail" includes any method of mail delivery provided by Canada Post for which confirmation of delivery to a named person is available;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "remediation" means action to eliminate, limit, correct, counteract, mitigate or remove any contaminant or the adverse effects on the environment or human health of any contaminant, and includes, but is not limited to, the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) preliminary site investigations, detailed site investigations, analysis and interpretation, including tests, sampling, surveys, data evaluation, risk assessment and environmental impact assessment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) evaluation of alternative methods of remediation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) preparation of a remediation plan, including a plan for any consequential or associated removal of soil or soil relocation from the site;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) implementation of a remediation plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) monitoring, verification and confirmation of whether the remediation complies with the remediation plan, applicable standards and requirements imposed by a director;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) other activities prescribed by the minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "single-use product" means a product that is ordinarily disposed of after a single use or short-term use, whether or not the product could be reused;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "special conservation officer" means a person designated as a special conservation officer under section 106 (3) [conservation officer service];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "waste" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) air contaminants,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) litter,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) effluent,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) refuse,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) biomedical waste,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) hazardous waste, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) any other substance prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, or the minister under section 22 [minister's regulations - codes of practice], or, if either of them prescribes circumstances in which a substance is a waste, a substance that is present in those circumstances,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: whether or not the type of waste referred to in paragraphs (a) to (f) or prescribed under paragraph (g) has any commercial value or is capable of being used for a useful purpose;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "waste management facility" means a facility for the treatment, recycling, storage, disposal or destruction of a waste, or recovery of reusable resources, including energy potential from waste;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "waste management plan" means a plan that contains provisions or requirements for the management of recyclable material or other waste or a class of waste within all or a part of one or more municipalities;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "water" includes groundwater, as defined in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act, and ice;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "works" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a drain, ditch and sewer,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a waste disposal system including a sewage treatment plant, pumping station and outfall,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a device, equipment, land and a structure that is used to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  measure, handle, transport, store, treat or destroy waste or a substance that is capable of causing pollution, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  introduce into the environment waste or a substance that is capable of causing pollution,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an installation, plant, machinery, equipment, land or a process that causes or may cause pollution or is designed or used to measure or control the introduction of waste into the environment or to measure or control a substance that is capable of causing pollution, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) an installation, plant, machinery, equipment, land or a process that is used to monitor or clean up pollution or waste.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Act, a detrimental environmental impact occurs when a change in the quality of air, land or water substantially reduces the usefulness of the environment or its capacity to support life.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of the definition of "air contaminant" and "effluent", it is not necessary to prove

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) that the air contaminant or effluent, if diluted at or subsequent to the point of introduction, continues to be capable of harming, injuring or damaging a person, life form, property or the environment, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the actual presence of a person who, or a life form that, is capable of being harmed or injured by the introduction of the air contaminant or effluent.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (4) If a regulation under this Act authorizes the minister or a director to substitute a different requirement for any requirement in the regulations, a reference to the regulations includes a reference to the substituted requirement.

heading: Powers conferred on included officials
paragraph: 2		  A provision of this Act or the regulations that confers powers on an officer also confers them on a director and a manager.

heading: Director includes delegate
paragraph:
3
		  (1) Subject to the limitations in section 57 [delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries], a director may delegate any of the director's powers, duties or functions under this Act, except the power to establish protocols, to any person, subject to the terms and conditions the director considers necessary or advisable.

heading: Director includes delegate
paragraph: (2) In this Act a reference to the director includes a reference to a delegate of the director.

heading: Conflicts with other enactments
paragraph:
4
		  If there is a conflict between this Act or its regulations or an approval, a licence, an order, a permit or an approved waste management plan under this Act and

heading: Conflicts with other enactments
paragraph: (a) the Geothermal Resources Act or the regulations under that Act, or a permit, a licence, a lease, an authorization, an order or an agreement under that Act, or

heading: Conflicts with other enactments
paragraph: (b) the Transport of Dangerous Goods Act or the regulations under that Act,

heading: Conflicts with other enactments
paragraph: this Act, its regulations and an approval, a licence, an order, a permit or an approved waste management plan subsisting under this Act prevail.

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: 5		  The duties, powers and functions of the minister extend to any matter relating to the management, protection and enhancement of the environment including, but not limited to, the following matters:

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (a) planning, research and investigation in relation to the environment;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (b) development of policies for the management, protection and use of the environment;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (c) planning, design, construction, operation and maintenance of works and undertakings for the management, protection or enhancement of the environment;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (d) providing information to the public about the quality and use of the environment;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (e) preparing and publishing policies, strategies, objectives, guidelines and standards for the protection and management of the environment;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (f) preparing and publishing environmental management plans for specific areas of British Columbia which may include, but need not be limited to, measures with respect to the following:

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (i)  flood control, flood hazard management and development of land that is subject to flooding;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (ii)  drainage;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (iii)  soil conservation;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (iv)  water resource management;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (v)  fisheries and aquatic life management;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (vi)  wildlife management;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (vii)  waste management;

heading: Minister's authority
paragraph: (viii)  air management.

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph:
6
		  (1) For the purposes of this section, "the conduct of a prescribed industry, trade or business" includes the operation by any person of facilities or vehicles for the collection, storage, treatment, handling, transportation, discharge, destruction or other disposal of waste in relation to the prescribed industry, trade or business.

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (5), a person must not introduce or cause or allow waste to be introduced into the environment in the course of conducting a prescribed industry, trade or business.

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (5), a person must not introduce or cause or allow to be introduced into the environment, waste produced by a prescribed activity or operation.

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), a person must not introduce waste into the environment in such a manner or quantity as to cause pollution.

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this section or in a regulation made under subsection (2) or (3) prohibits any of the following:

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (a) the disposition of waste in compliance with this Act and with all of the following that are required or apply in respect of the disposition:

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (i)  a valid and subsisting permit;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (ii)  a valid and subsisting approval;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (iii)  a valid and subsisting order;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (iv)  a regulation;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (v)  a waste management plan approved by the minister;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (b) the discharge into the air of an air contaminant from an incinerator operated under an authority, licence or permit of a municipality;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (c) the disposition of human remains in crematoria in compliance with the Cremation, Interment and Funeral Services Act;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (d) the discharge of air contaminants authorized by a bylaw made under section 31 (3) (d) [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver];

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (e) the burning of leaves, foliage, weeds, crops or stubble for domestic or agricultural purposes or in compliance with the Weed Control Act;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (f) the use of pesticides or biocides for agricultural, domestic or forestry purposes in compliance with the Integrated Pest Management Act, the Pest Control Products Act (Canada) and any other Act and regulation governing their use;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (g) fires set or controlled by a person

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (i)  acting under the direction of a local authority, as defined in the Fire Safety Act, if the local authority authorizes the fires for training purposes,

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (ii)  carrying out fire control under section 9 of the Wildfire Act, or

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (iii)  if the fires are resource management open fires under the Wildfire Act and are lit, fuelled or used in accordance with that Act and the regulations under that Act;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (h) emissions from steam powered or internal combustion engines in compliance, if applicable, with the Motor Vehicle Act and regulations;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (i) emission into the air of soil particles or grit in the course of agriculture or horticulture;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (j) the disposal of waste by a person other than a municipality

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (i)  by means of a system of waste disposal lawfully operated by a municipality or other public authority, and

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (ii)  in compliance with the rules and regulations that apply to that system;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (k) emission of an air contaminant from combustion of wood or fossil fuels used solely for the purpose of comfort heating of domestic, institutional or commercial buildings;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (l) emission of an air contaminant from food preparation in

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (i)  residential premises, or

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (ii)  retail food outlets;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (m) an owner, agent or manager, as those terms are defined in the Mines Act, from carrying out an activity related to mineral and coal exploration if that activity is exempted under section 10 (2.1) of that Act.

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (6) Nothing in subsection (5) (b) or (k) authorizes the use of an incinerator or domestic, institutional or commercial heating equipment for the purpose of destroying hazardous waste by means of combustion.

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (7) In subsection (5) (l):

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: "residential premises" includes hospitals, clinics, logging camps, factory and office canteens and other similar premises;

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: "retail food outlets" means

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (a) restaurants, hotels, motels and similar premises, and

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (b) premises in which food is prepared and sold by retail sale, such as

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (i)  exclusively retail bakeries, and

heading: Waste disposal
paragraph: (ii)  premises selling take out food.

heading: Hazardous waste - confinement
paragraph: 7		  (1) A person who produces, stores, transports, handles, treats, recycles, deals with, processes or owns a hazardous waste must keep the hazardous waste confined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Hazardous waste - confinement
paragraph: (2) Except to the extent expressly authorized by a permit, an approval, an order, a waste management plan or the regulations, a person must not release a hazardous waste from the confinement required by subsection (1).

heading: Hazardous waste management facility
paragraph:
8
		  A person must not construct, establish, alter, enlarge, extend, use or operate a facility for the treatment, recycling, storage, disposal or destruction of a hazardous waste except in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Hazardous waste storage and disposal
paragraph:
9
		  (1) A person must not store more than a prescribed amount of a hazardous waste except in accordance with any of the following that apply:

heading: Hazardous waste storage and disposal
paragraph: (a) the regulations in relation to storing hazardous waste;

heading: Hazardous waste storage and disposal
paragraph: (b) an order that requires the person to store that kind of hazardous waste;

heading: Hazardous waste storage and disposal
paragraph: (c) an approved waste management plan that provides for storage of hazardous waste.

heading: Hazardous waste storage and disposal
paragraph: (2) A person who is storing a quantity of a substance at the time that the substance is prescribed to be a hazardous waste does not contravene subsection (1) by continuing to store the same or a different quantity of that substance if the person notifies a director, in accordance with the regulations, of the location, quantity and type of substance that the person is storing.

heading: Hazardous waste storage and disposal
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), a director may serve a person referred to in that subsection with a written order to comply with the regulations or the approved waste management plan, and, if a director does so, subject to subsection (4), the person must comply with the order within the period the director specifies in that order.

heading: Hazardous waste storage and disposal
paragraph: (4) If a person who is served with an order under subsection (3) does not comply with the regulations in the period specified by the director, the person must dispose of the hazardous waste as directed by a director.

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A person who produces or stores a hazardous waste

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (a) must not cause or allow more than a prescribed quantity of the hazardous waste to be transported from the property where the person produces or stores the hazardous waste unless the person first

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (i)  completes, in the form and manner prescribed, the part of a manifest that applies to the person, and

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (ii)  files the manifest in the manner prescribed,

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (b) must ensure that the person transporting more than the prescribed quantity of the hazardous waste from the place where it is produced or stored has a licence for that purpose, if a licence is required by the regulations, and

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (c) must not cause or allow more than the prescribed quantity of the hazardous waste to be transported to a place unless

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (i)  an order, waste management plan or regulation authorizes or requires it to be stored at that place,

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (ii)  a permit, approval, order, waste management plan or regulation authorizes or requires it to be introduced into the environment or treated at that place, or

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (iii)  storage of the hazardous waste at that place is otherwise not prohibited under section 9 [hazardous waste storage and disposal].

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (2) A person must not transport more than a prescribed quantity of a hazardous waste unless the person

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (a) carries with the person

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (i)  a manifest completed as required by subsection (1) and this subsection, and

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (ii)  if required by the regulations, a licence, and

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (b) has completed, in accordance with the regulations, that part of the manifest that applies to the person.

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (3) A person must not accept delivery of more than a prescribed quantity of a hazardous waste unless the person

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (a) receives from the transporter a manifest that has been completed as required by subsections (1) and (2),

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (b) completes the part of the manifest that applies to the person and files the manifest in the form and manner prescribed, and

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (c) has a permit or an approval authorizing the person to introduce into the environment that kind and quantity of hazardous waste, is authorized under the regulations to treat or recycle that kind and quantity of hazardous waste or is not prohibited under section 9 (1) [hazardous waste storage and disposal] from storing that kind and quantity of hazardous waste.

heading: Transportation of hazardous waste
paragraph: (4) In a prosecution for a contravention of this section, the burden of proving compliance with subsection (1) (a) or (c) or with subsection (2) or (3) is on the defendant.

heading: Packaging, product containers and single-use products
paragraph:
11
		  A person must not use, distribute, offer for sale or sell packaging, product containers or single-use products, or any material used in packaging, product containers or single-use products, contrary to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Littering
paragraph:
12
		  (1) In this section, "public place" means

heading: Littering
paragraph: (a) a place that is open to the air, including a covered place that is open to the air on at least one side, and to which the public is entitled or permitted to have access without payment, and

heading: Littering
paragraph: (b) a park or public campground.

heading: Littering
paragraph: (2) A person must not throw down, drop or otherwise deposit, and leave litter in a public place.

heading: Littering
paragraph: (3) The prohibition in subsection (2) does not apply if the depositing and leaving was authorized by law, or was done with the consent of the owner, occupier or other person or authority having the control of the public place.

heading: Littering
paragraph: (4) In a prosecution, the burden of establishing that subsection (3) applies is on the defendant.

heading: Discharge of waste from recreational vehicles
paragraph:
13
		  A person must not discharge domestic sewage or waste from a trailer, camper, transportable housing unit, boat or house boat onto land, into any reservoir or into any lake, pond, stream or other natural body of water, except

heading: Discharge of waste from recreational vehicles
paragraph: (a) in compliance with a permit, an approval, an order, a waste management plan or a regulation, or

heading: Discharge of waste from recreational vehicles
paragraph: (b) if disposal facilities are provided, in accordance with proper and accepted methods of disposal using those facilities, and in accordance with the Public Health Act and regulations.

heading: Permits
paragraph: 14		  (1) A director may issue a permit authorizing the introduction of waste into the environment subject to requirements for the protection of the environment that the director considers advisable and, without limiting that power, may do one or more of the following in the permit:

heading: Permits
paragraph: (a) require the permittee to repair, alter, remove, improve or add to works or to construct new works and to submit plans and specifications for works specified in the permit;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (b) require the permittee to give security in the amount and form and subject to conditions the director specifies;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (c) require the permittee to monitor, in the manner specified by the director, the waste, the method of handling, treating, transporting, discharging and storing the waste and the places and things that the director considers will be affected by the discharge of the waste or the handling, treatment, transportation or storage of the waste;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (d) require the permittee to conduct studies and to report information specified by the director in the manner specified by the director;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (e) specify procedures for monitoring and analysis, and procedures or requirements respecting the handling, treatment, transportation, discharge or storage of waste that the permittee must fulfill;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (f) require the permittee to recycle certain wastes, and to recover certain reusable resources, including energy potential from wastes.

heading: Permits
paragraph: (2) A permit does not authorize the introduction of hazardous waste into the environment unless it specifies the characteristics and quantity of hazardous waste that may be introduced.

heading: Permits
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), a director may not issue or, subject to subsection (4), amend, a permit authorizing the introduction of waste into the environment if the introduction is governed by

heading: Permits
paragraph: (a) a code of practice that is established in the regulations in relation to the industry, trade or business that applies for the permit or amendment,

heading: Permits
paragraph: (b) a code of practice that is established in the regulations in relation to the activity or operation in respect of which the permit or amendment is applied for, or

heading: Permits
paragraph: (c) a regulation, unless the regulation requires that a permit be obtained in relation to the discharge of the industry, trade, or business, activity or operation.

heading: Permits
paragraph: (4) A director, on receipt of an application or on the director's own initiative, may amend a permit authorizing an introduction of waste described in subsection (3) (a), (b) or (c), if

heading: Permits
paragraph: (a) in the opinion of the director, the amendment is necessary for the protection of the environment, or

heading: Permits
paragraph: (b) the amendment is for one or more or the following purposes:

heading: Permits
paragraph: (i)  a change of ownership or name;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (ii)  a change of address;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (iii)  a decrease in the authorized quantity of the discharge, emission or stored material;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (iv)  an increase of not more than 10% in the authorized quantity of the discharge, emission or stored material;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (v)  a change in the authorized quality of the discharge, emission or stored material such that, in the opinion of the director, the change has resulted in or will result in an equal or lesser impact on the environment;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (vi)  a change in a monitoring program;

heading: Permits
paragraph: (vii)  a change to the works, method of treatment or any other condition of a permit or an approval such that, in the opinion of the director, the change has resulted in or will result in an equal or lesser impact on the environment.

heading: Approvals
paragraph:
15
		  (1) A director may approve the introduction of waste into the environment for a period of up to 15 months without issuing a permit.

heading: Approvals
paragraph: (2) A director may issue the director's approval subject to requirements for the protection of the environment that the director considers advisable and, without restricting that power, may include as a requirement anything referred to in section 14 (1) [permits].

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph:
16
		  (1) A director may, subject to section 14 (3) [permits], this section and the regulations, for the protection of the environment,

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (a) on the director's own initiative if the director considers it necessary, or

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (b) on application by a holder of a permit or an approval,

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: amend the requirements of the permit or approval.

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (2) A director may, after consultation with the minister, amend

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (a) a permit ordered by the minister under section 90.1 (1) [permits under area based management plan], or

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (b) a permit or approval issued by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (3) If a permit or an approval is subject to conditions imposed pursuant to a decision made in an appeal to the appeal board under Division 2 [Appeals under this Act] of Part 8, those conditions must not be amended except

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (a) by the appeal board, and

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (b) after the appeal board has given the parties an opportunity to be heard on the question of whether the conditions should be amended.

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (4) A director's power to amend a permit or an approval includes all of the following:

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (a) authorizing or requiring the construction of new works in addition to or instead of works previously authorized or required;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (b) authorizing or requiring the repair of, alteration to, improvement of, removal of or addition to existing works;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (c) requiring security, altering the security required or changing the type of security required or the conditions of giving security;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (d) extending or reducing the term of or renewing the permit or approval;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (e) authorizing or requiring a change in the characteristics or components of waste discharged, treated, handled or transported;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (f) authorizing or requiring a change in the quantity of waste discharged, treated, handled or transported;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (g) authorizing or requiring a change in the location of the discharge, treatment, handling or transportation of the waste;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (h) altering the time specified for the construction of works or the time in which to meet other requirements imposed on the holder of the permit or approval;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (i) authorizing or requiring a change in the method of discharging, treating, handling or transporting the waste;

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (j) changing or imposing any procedure or requirement that was imposed or could have been imposed under section 14 [permits] or 15 [approvals].

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (5) A director may renew an approval before or after the end of the term of the approval.

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (6) A director may not renew an approval if the term of the approval and the term of renewal, when taken together, would exceed 15 months.

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (7) If a director amends a permit or approval, the director

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (a) may require that the holder of the permit or approval supply the director with plans, specifications and other information the director requests, and

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (b) must give the holder of the permit or approval notice in writing of the amendment and publish notice of the amendment in the prescribed manner.

heading: Amendment of permits and approvals
paragraph: (8) Despite subsection (7) (b), the director may give the notice by electronic means to an address provided by the holder of the permit or approval.

heading: Transfers of permits, approvals, etc.
paragraph:
17
		  (1) A transfer of a permit or approval is without effect unless a director has consented in writing to the transfer.

heading: Transfers of permits, approvals, etc.
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the director may consent to a transfer by electronic means to an address provided by the holder of the permit or approval.

heading: Transfers of permits, approvals, etc.
paragraph: (3) A licence referred to in section 10 [transportation of hazardous waste] is not transferable.

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph:
18
		  (1) Subject to this section, the minister or a director, by notice served on the holder of a permit or approval, may

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (a) suspend the permit or approval for any period, or

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (b) cancel the permit or approval.

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (2) A notice served under subsection (1) must state the time at which the suspension or cancellation takes effect.

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (3) The minister may exercise the authority under subsection (1) in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (a) a holder of a permit

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (i)  fails to complete construction of works specified in the permit within the time specified in the permit or, if no time is specified in the permit, within 3 years after issuance of the permit, or

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (ii)  does not exercise any rights under the permit for a period of 3 years;

heading: Suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals
paragraph: (b) a holder of a permit or an approval fails to pay money owing to the government under the permit or approval;
