heading: Definitions
paragraph:
23
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "code of practice" means a code of practice attached to and forming part of a bylaw made under section 25 [authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "hauler" means a person who picks up, delivers, hauls or transports municipal solid waste or recyclable material on a commercial basis;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "manage" or "management" includes the collection, transportation, handling, processing, storage, treatment, utilization and disposal of any substance;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipal liquid waste" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) effluent that originates from any source and is discharged into a municipal sewer system,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) effluent from residential sources that is discharged to the ground, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) effluent specified by a director to be included in a waste management plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipal solid waste" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) refuse that originates from residential, commercial, institutional, demolition, land clearing or construction sources, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) refuse specified by a director to be included in a waste management plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sewage facility" means works operated by a municipality to gather, treat, transport, store, utilize or discharge sewage.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph:
24
		  (1) A municipality, alone or with one or more other municipalities, may submit for approval by the minister a waste management plan, that complies with the regulations respecting the management of municipal liquid waste.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (2) On the written request of the minister, a regional district must submit for approval by the minister a waste management plan that

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (a) is for the benefit of the whole area of the regional district,

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (b) complies with the regulations, and

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (c) is in respect of biomedical waste.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (3) Despite any other requirement of this Act, the minister, by notice in writing, may

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (a) direct a municipality to prepare a waste management plan that complies with the regulations or revise a waste management plan and submit it to the minister for approval on or before a date specified by the minister, or

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (b) specify a date by which a municipality must provide proof, in a form satisfactory to the minister, of the progress that the municipality is making to comply with this section.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (4) If the minister considers it to be in the public interest and is satisfied that a municipality is making efforts in good faith to complete a waste management plan in accordance with this Act and the regulations, the minister may, on conditions specified by the minister, grant an extension of a date specified under this section.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (5) Subject to section 27 (2) [public consultation process], the minister may, at any time, with or without conditions, approve all or part of a waste management plan or an amendment to a waste management plan.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (6) The minister may, by order, amend or cancel a waste management plan and, if cancelled, the waste management plan ceases to have force or effect.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (7) Despite anything in the Community Charter or the Local Government Act, if a waste management plan

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (a) is required under subsection (2) or (3) (a), or

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (b) has been approved by the minister under subsection (5),

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: a bylaw adopted by a municipality for the purpose of preparing the waste management plan referred to in paragraph (a), or implementing the waste management plan referred to in paragraph (b), does not require a petition, the assent of the electors or the approval of the electors.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (8) Nothing in a waste management plan prevents the exercise of rights conferred by a permit or approval subsisting on the date the waste management plan is approved unless the permit or approval is suspended or cancelled by the minister under section 18 (1) [suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals].

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (9) Despite subsection (8), if a provision of a permit or approval conflicts with a requirement of an approved waste management plan, that provision has no force or effect after the waste management plan is approved.

heading: Waste management plans
paragraph: (10) Despite subsection (8), if an operational certificate is issued under section 28 (1) [operational certificates] in respect of a site or facility for which a permit or approval authorizing the discharge of waste was previously issued, the permit or approval is cancelled.

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: 25		  (1) In this section and sections 26 [municipal solid waste disposal fees], 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver] and 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver]:

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: "hauler licence" means a licence issued by a regional district to a hauler, under the authority of a bylaw made under subsection (3) (h) (i);

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: "recycler licence" means a licence issued by a regional district, under the authority of a bylaw made under subsection (3) (h) (i), to the owner or operator of a site that accepts and manages recyclable material;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: "regional district" means

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (a) a regional district as defined in the Local Government Act,

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (a.1) except in section 26, the Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, or

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (b) the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District constituted under the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District Act;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: "site" means any site or facility, including those identified specifically or by class in an approved waste management plan for the management of municipal solid waste or recyclable material;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: "waste stream management licence" means a licence issued by a regional district, under the authority of a bylaw made under subsection (3) (h) (i), to the owner or operator of a site that accepts and manages municipal solid waste.

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (2) Despite any other Act, a person must manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material at a site in accordance with

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (a) any applicable approved waste management plan for the site,

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (b) any requirements or conditions that a director includes in an operational certificate or permit issued for the site, and

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (c) any applicable bylaw made under subsection (3) of this section or section 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver] or 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver].

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of implementing an approved waste management plan, a regional district may make bylaws to regulate the management of municipal solid waste or recyclable material including, without limitation, bylaws regulating, prohibiting or respecting one or more of the following:

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (a) the types, quality or quantities of municipal solid waste or recyclable material that may be brought onto or removed from a site;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (b) the discarding or abandonment of municipal solid waste or recyclable material;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (c) the burning of any class or quantity of municipal solid waste or recyclable material;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (d) the delivery, deposit, storage or abandonment of municipal solid waste or recyclable material at authorized or unauthorized sites;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (e) the transport of municipal solid waste or recyclable material within or through the area covered by the waste management plan;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (f) the operation, closure or post-closure of sites, including requirements for

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (i)  the recording and submission of information,

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (ii)  audited statements respecting the municipal solid waste or recyclable material received at and shipped from a site, and

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (iii)  the installation and maintenance of works;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (g) respecting fees, including

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (i)  setting fees and charges that may vary according to

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (A) the quantity, volume, composition or type of municipal solid waste or recyclable material, or

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (B) the class of persons, sites, operations, activities, municipal solid wastes or recyclable materials, and

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (ii)  specifying the manner and timing of the payment of those fees and charges;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (h) requiring the owner or operator of a site or a hauler to

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (i)  hold a recycler licence, a waste stream management licence or a hauler licence, or

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (ii)  comply with a code of practice;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (i) setting the terms and conditions for issuing, suspending, amending or cancelling a licence referred to in paragraph (h);

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (j) requiring an owner or operator of a site or a licence holder to obtain insurance or provide security satisfactory to the regional district to ensure

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (i)  compliance with the bylaws, and

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (ii)  that sufficient funding is available for site operations, remediation, closure and post-closure monitoring;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (k) requiring the owner or operator of a site to contain municipal solid waste or recyclable material within specified height and area limits, and specify requirements and terms for confirming compliance with those limits;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (l) prohibiting unauthorized persons from handling or removing municipal solid waste or recyclable material that is deposited at a site or set out for collection;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (m) establishing different prohibitions, conditions, requirements and exemptions for different classes of persons, sites, operations, activities, municipal solid wastes or recyclable materials;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (n) requiring an owner of municipal solid waste or recyclable material, the deposit of which has been prohibited by bylaw, to pay the cost of its disposal in a manner specified in the bylaw;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (o) authorizing designated persons to enter a site or inspect the contents of a vehicle for the purpose of enforcing a bylaw made under this subsection and, for this purpose, sections 109 [entry on property] and 111 (2) [inspection of vehicles] apply to a designated person as if the designated person is an officer referred to in those sections, but only in respect of municipal solid waste and recyclable material;

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (p) providing that

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (i)  a contravention of a provision of the bylaws is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding $200 000, and

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (ii)  if a corporation commits an offence under the bylaws, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence even though the corporation is convicted.

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (4) Before exercising the authority under this section, a regional district must

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (a) indicate in its waste management plan its intention to undertake consultations with affected stakeholders in accordance with section 27 (1) [public consultation process], and

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (b) undertake the consultations.

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (5) This section does not apply to the management of municipal solid waste or recyclable material at the site at which it originates.

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (6) A regional district, including its employees and elected officials, is not liable

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: (a) to any person for environmental conditions at a site, or

paragraph: (b) to remediate a site included in a waste management plan,

heading: Authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts
paragraph: solely because it holds security as required under a bylaw made under this Part.

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: 26		  (1) In this section, "waste hauler" means

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (a) a municipality that picks up, delivers, hauls or transports municipal solid waste, or

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (b) a person who, on a commercial basis, picks up, delivers, hauls or transports municipal solid waste.

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (2) In addition to its other powers, a regional district may, by bylaw, exercise one or more of the following powers in relation to the collection and disposal of municipal solid waste generated within its area or within a municipality that has contracted with the regional district for the disposal of municipal solid waste from the municipality:

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (a) setting fees payable by persons who use the services of a waste hauler or by generators of municipal solid waste;

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (b) setting levels of fees based on

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (i)  the quantity, volume, type or composition of municipal solid waste generated,

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (ii)  the fees charged by the applicable waste hauler for its services, or

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (iii)  any other criteria prescribed by regulation;

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (c) varying fees by class of persons, operations, activities, industries, trades, businesses, works, sites or municipal solid wastes;

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (d) requiring waste haulers to

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (i)  act as agents of the regional district when collecting fees under this section,

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (ii)  remit fees to the regional district in accordance with the bylaw,

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (iii)  maintain records in accordance with the bylaw, and

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (iv)  permit an employee or agent of the regional district to inspect and make copies of these records during the waste hauler's normal business hours;

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (e) setting conditions respecting the collection and remittance of fees by waste haulers and setting compensation payable to the waste haulers for this service;

heading: Municipal solid waste disposal fees
paragraph: (f) establishing fines for failure to comply with a bylaw made under this section.

heading: Public consultation process
paragraph:
27
		  (1) A municipality must provide for a process for comprehensive review and consultation with the public respecting all aspects of the development, amendment and final content of a waste management plan that applies to that municipality.

heading: Public consultation process
paragraph: (2) The minister may not approve a waste management plan unless the minister is satisfied that there has been adequate public review and consultation with respect to the development, amendment and final content of the waste management plan.

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph:
28
		  (1) If a waste management plan is approved by the minister, a director may, in accordance with the regulations, issue an operational certificate, with or without conditions, to the municipality or to any person who is the owner of a site or facility covered by the waste management plan.

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (2) An operational certificate issued under subsection (1) forms part of and must not conflict with the approved waste management plan.

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (3) A director may exercise a power or authority in relation to an operational certificate in the same manner and to the same extent as provided by this Act with respect to a permit.

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (4) At least 14 days before issuing an operational certificate, a director must give notice of the director's intention to issue the operational certificate

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (a) in writing to the person named in the operational certificate, and

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (b) to the public in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (5) A director who gives notice under subsection (4) must allow any person who has been given notice under that subsection to

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (a) inspect the proposed operational certificate, and

heading: Operational certificates
paragraph: (b) provide comments to the director respecting the requirements or conditions of the proposed operational certificate.

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph:
29
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may designate all or a specified part of a municipality as a sewage control area, and on the designation the council, board or other governing body of the municipality

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (a) must appoint one or more persons as sewage control managers, and

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (b) may appoint one or more persons as municipal sewage control officers

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: who have and may exercise, in relation to the sewage control area, the powers of an officer set out in section 109 [entry on property].

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (2) A sewage control manager may, subject to any applicable waste management plan, by order, prohibit or regulate the discharge of any type of waste other than domestic sewage into a sewage facility.

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (2), a sewage control manager may

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (a) in an order made under subsection (2), specify

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (i)  the conditions under which the waste may be discharged into a sewage facility, and

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (ii)  that the person who discharges, or the council, board or other governing body that permits the waste to be discharged into the sewage facility in the municipality, or both of them, monitor the waste discharged in the manner and at the times specified, or

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (b) amend or revoke an order made by the sewage control manager under subsection (2).

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (4) A sewage control manager may order a person who discharges waste other than domestic sewage into a sewage facility, or who possesses waste other than domestic sewage that may ultimately be discharged into a sewage facility, to keep records and provide information in the form and manner required by the sewage control manager respecting the waste discharged, handled, stored, treated or transported.

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (5) A person affected by an order of a sewage control manager under this section may appeal the order under Division 2 [Appeals from Decisions under this Act] of Part 8 in the same manner as if the order were a decision of the director, and Part 8 applies.

heading: Sewage control areas
paragraph: (6) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may reduce or extend the boundaries of a sewage control area, and may disestablish a sewage control area.

heading: Sewage in regional districts
paragraph:
30
		  (1) The board of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District or, if a regional district exercises a power to provide a service related to the disposal or treatment of sewage, the board of the district, may make bylaws respecting the direct or indirect discharge of wastes into any sewer or drain connected to a sewerage facility operated by the district.

heading: Sewage in regional districts
paragraph: (2) A bylaw made under this section may provide that its contravention is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding $10 000.

heading: Sewage in regional districts
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1), a bylaw under this section may do one or more of the following:

heading: Sewage in regional districts
paragraph: (a) require the keeping of records and the provision of information respecting waste produced on property other than residential property;

heading: Sewage in regional districts
paragraph: (b) impose conditions respecting the discharge into sewers of waste produced on property other than residential property;

heading: Sewage in regional districts
paragraph: (c) provide that its prohibitions, restrictions and requirements apply only to specified persons or classes of persons.

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph:
31
		  (1) Despite anything in its letters patent, the Metro Vancouver Regional District may provide the service of air pollution control and air quality management and, for that purpose, the board of the regional district may, by bylaw, prohibit, regulate and otherwise control and prevent the discharge of air contaminants.

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (2) The board of the Metro Vancouver Regional District must appoint

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (a) officers who may, with respect to the discharge of air contaminants in the Metro Vancouver Regional District, exercise all the powers of an officer under section 109 [entry on property] and the regulations, and

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (b) a district director and one or more assistant district directors who may, with respect to the discharge of air contaminants in the Metro Vancouver Regional District, exercise all the powers of a director under this Act.

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1), a bylaw under this section may do one or more of the following:

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (a) provide that contravention of a provision of the bylaw that is intended to limit the quantity of air contaminants or that specifies the characteristics of air contaminants that may be discharged into the air is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding $1 000 000;

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (b) provide that a contravention of a provision of the bylaw, other than a provision referred to in paragraph (a), is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding $200 000;

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (c) require the keeping of records and the provision of information respecting air contaminants and their discharge;

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (d) exempt from the application of section 6 (2) and (3) [waste disposal], in relation to the discharge of air contaminants, any operation, activity, industry, trade, business, air contaminant or works that complies with the bylaw, if it also complies with any further restrictions or conditions imposed under this Act;

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (e) establish different prohibitions, regulations, rates or levels of fees, conditions, requirements and exemptions

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (i)  for different persons, operations, activities, industries, trades, businesses, air contaminants or works, and

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (ii)  for different classes of persons, operations, activities, industries, trades, businesses, air contaminants or works.

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (4) A district director may, by order, impose on a person further restrictions or conditions in relation to an operation, activity, industry, trade, business, air contaminant or works covered by a bylaw under subsection (3) (d) in order that the person may qualify for an exemption under that subsection, including a condition that the person obtain a permit.

heading: Control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (5) The minister may require the Metro Vancouver Regional District to amend, suspend or cancel any bylaw or part of a bylaw made under this section if the minister considers it necessary in the public interest.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph:
32
		  (1) In addition to anything in the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District Act, the Administration Board of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District may make bylaws to prohibit, regulate or otherwise control the introduction into the environment of municipal solid waste.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a bylaw under this section may do one or more of the following:

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (a) provide that contravention of a provision of the bylaw that is intended to limit the quantity of municipal solid waste, or that specifies the characteristics of municipal solid waste that may be discharged into the environment, is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding $1 000 000;

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (b) provide that a contravention of a provision of the bylaw, other than a provision referred to in paragraph (a), is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding $200 000;

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (c) require the keeping of records and the provision of information respecting municipal solid waste and its discharge;

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (d) exempt from the application of section 6 (2) and (3) [waste disposal], in relation to the discharge of municipal solid waste, any operation, activity, industry, trade, business, works, site, facility or municipal solid waste that complies with the bylaw, if it also complies with any further restrictions or conditions imposed under this Act;

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (e) establish different prohibitions, regulations, rates or levels of fees, conditions, requirements and exemptions for different classes of persons, operations, activities, industries, trades, businesses, works, sites or municipal solid wastes.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (3) The Administration Board of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District, before exercising a power under subsection (1) or (2), must

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (a) appoint a district director and one or more assistant district directors who may, with respect to the management of municipal solid waste and recyclable material at sites within the area of the Metro Vancouver Regional District, exercise all the powers of a director under this Act, and

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (b) appoint officers who may, with respect to the management of municipal solid waste and recyclable material at sites within the area of the Metro Vancouver Regional District, exercise all the powers of an officer under sections 109 [entry on property] and 111 [inspection of vehicles] of this Act and under the regulations.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (4) If the minister considers it necessary in the public interest with respect to the exercise of the powers granted under subsections (1) and (2), the minister may

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (a) require a person designated by the minister to carry out a review of the manner in which the powers have been exercised by the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District, or

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (b) take any action to ensure proper administration of the powers granted, including authorizing the designated person to carry out the duties associated with those powers.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (5) After the minister receives a report and recommendation from the officers referred to in subsection (4) (a), and after any consultation the minister considers necessary, the minister may revoke any or all of the powers granted under subsection (1) or (2).

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (6) No action lies, and no proceedings may be brought, against the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District or an officer, employee or elected or appointed official of the Metro Vancouver Regional District because of anything arising out of the administration of the powers, duties and functions under this section unless a person establishes that the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District or an officer, employee or elected or appointed official of the Metro Vancouver Regional District has acted in bad faith.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (7) Division 2 [Appeals from Decisions under this Act] of Part 8 and section 133 [service] apply to a decision of the Administration Board of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District, or a decision of an officer, employee or elected or appointed official of the Metro Vancouver Regional District, made under the authority of a bylaw made under subsection (1) or (2).

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver
paragraph: (8) This section does not apply to a site owned or operated by the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District or one of its member municipalities.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts
paragraph: 33		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, on receipt of a written request from a regional district, other than a regional district that is within the area of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District, and after appropriate consultation with the regional district and affected stakeholders, may make regulations

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts
paragraph: (a) giving the regional district the authority to make bylaws to prohibit, regulate or otherwise control the introduction into the environment of municipal solid waste within the area covered by the regional district's approved solid waste management plan, and

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts
paragraph: (b) specifying the terms and conditions, including terms and conditions respecting the collection of fees, to which the authority under paragraph (a) is subject.

heading: Disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts
paragraph: (2) Section 32 (2) to (8) [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] applies in relation to a regional district in respect of which the Lieutenant Governor in Council has made regulations under subsection (1).

heading: Bylaw approval or amendment
paragraph:
34
		  (1) A bylaw made by a regional district under the authority of section 25 [authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts], 26 [municipal solid waste disposal fees] or 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts] or made by the Administration Board of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District under the authority of section 25, 26 or 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver], may not be adopted without the prior written approval of the minister.

heading: Bylaw approval or amendment
paragraph: (2) If the minister considers it necessary in the public interest, the minister may require a regional district or the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District to amend, suspend or cancel a bylaw or part of a bylaw, or any authorization given under a bylaw made under section 25 [authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts], 26 [municipal solid waste disposal fees], 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] or 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts].

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph:
35
		  (1) For the purposes of sections 25 [authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional districts], 26 [municipal solid waste disposal fees], 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] and 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts], a regional district may, by bylaw, delegate to an officer or employee of the regional district the power to perform the functions and duties of the regional district in bylaws made under those sections.

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of sections 25 [authority to manage municipal solid waste and recyclable material in regional district], 26 [municipal solid waste disposal fees] and 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver], the Administration Board of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District may, by bylaw, delegate to an officer or employee of the Metro Vancouver Regional District the power to perform the functions and duties of the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District in bylaws made under those sections.

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph: (3) A bylaw referred to in subsection (1) or (2) must include an appeal mechanism from a decision of the officer or employee.

heading: Municipal administration of storage tanks
paragraph:
36
		  (1) A municipality may, on giving notice to a director, administer regulations made under this Act respecting tanks used to store petroleum products or other substances.

heading: Municipal administration of storage tanks
paragraph: (2) No action or other proceeding for damages lies or may be instituted against a municipality or a member of its council or an officer or employee of the municipality for anything done or omitted to be done in the exercise or intended exercise of any authority conferred on it by subsection (1) unless the person acted negligently or in bad faith.

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph:
37
		  (1) Despite the Community Charter, the Local Government Act, the Vancouver Charter or the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District Act,

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (a) a bylaw of a municipality, other than a bylaw under section 30 [sewage in regional districts], 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver], 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] or 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts], or

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (b) a permit, licence, approval or other document issued under the authority of a municipal bylaw

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: that conflicts with this Act, the regulations, an approved waste management plan or a permit, approval or order under this Act is without effect to the extent of the conflict.

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (2) A bylaw under section 30 [sewage in regional districts], 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver], 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] or 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts] that conflicts with this Act, the regulations, an approved waste management plan or a permit, approval or order, other than one issued by a district director, is without effect to the extent of the conflict.

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (3) A permit, approval or order issued by a district director that conflicts with this Act, the regulations, an approved waste management plan or a bylaw under section 30 [sewage in regional districts], 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver], 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] or 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts], is without effect to the extent of the conflict.

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (4) A bylaw of a municipality that conflicts with a bylaw under section 30 [sewage in regional districts], 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver], 32 [disposal of municipal solid waste in Greater Vancouver] or 33 [disposal of municipal solid waste in other regional districts], is without effect to the extent of the conflict.

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of subsections (1) to (4), a conflict does not exist solely because further restrictions or conditions are imposed by the bylaw, permit, licence, approval, order or other document, unless the minister by order declares that a conflict exists.

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (6) Despite the Local Government Act and the Vancouver Charter, if

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (a) a bylaw of a municipality purports to zone land for a use, or

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: (b) a land use contract under the Local Government Act purports to restrict the use of land to a use

heading: Conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality
paragraph: that would not allow the land to be used for the purpose allowed under a permit, approval or order issued in respect of the land or an approved waste management plan respecting the land, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, suspend the operation of the bylaw or contract to the extent the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers necessary to enable the rights given by the permit approval or order to be exercised.

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 3
paragraph: 38		  (1) Without limiting section 138 (1) [general authority to make regulations], the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 3
paragraph: (a) respecting the development, content, amendment, approval and review of waste management plans and operational certificates;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 3
paragraph: (b) establishing municipal solid waste reduction targets for the purpose of assessing waste management plans;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 3
paragraph: (c) prescribing the criteria for setting fees for the purposes of section 26 (2) (b) (iii) [municipal solid waste disposal fees].

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 3
paragraph: (2) Section 139 [regulations - general rules] applies for the purpose of making regulations under this section.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph:
39
		  (1) In this Part and Part 5 [Remediation of Mineral Exploration Sites and Mines]:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "allocation panel" means an allocation panel appointed under section 49 (2) [allocation panel];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "approval in principle" means an approval in principle under section 53 [approvals in principle and certificates of compliance];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "approved professional" means a person who is named on a roster established under section 42 (2) [approved professionals];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "approving officer" means an approving officer as defined in the Land Title Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "certificate of compliance" means a certificate of compliance under section 53 [approvals in principle and certificates of compliance];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "contaminated site" means an area of the land in which the soil or any groundwater lying beneath it, or the water or the underlying sediment, contains a prescribed substance in quantities or concentrations exceeding prescribed risk based or numerical

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) criteria,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) standards, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) conditions;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "contamination" means the presence in soil, sediment, water or groundwater of a substance prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "contaminated site" in quantities or concentrations exceeding the risk based or numerical

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) criteria,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) standards, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) conditions

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: also prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "contaminated site";

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "detailed site investigation" means a detailed site investigation and report under section 41 [site investigations] that complies with the regulations;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "government body" means a federal, provincial, municipal or treaty first nation body, including an agency or ministry of the Crown in right of Canada or British Columbia and an agency of a municipality or treaty first nation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "high risk orphan site" means an orphan site determined under section 58 [orphan sites] to be a high risk orphan site;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "minor contributor" means a responsible person determined under section 50 [minor contributors] to be a minor contributor;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "municipality" means a municipality as defined in section 1 but including the Islands Trust and not including an improvement district or the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "operator" means, subject to subsection (2), a person who is or was in control of or responsible for any operation located at a site, but does not include a secured creditor unless the secured creditor is described in section 45 (3) [persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "orphan site" means a contaminated site determined under section 58 [orphan sites] to be an orphan site;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "owner" means a person who

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) is in possession,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) has the right of control, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) occupies or controls the use

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: of real property, and includes, without limitation, a person who has an estate or interest, legal or equitable, in the real property, but does not include a secured creditor unless the secured creditor is described in section 45 (3) [persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "person" includes a government body and any director, officer, employee or agent of a person or government body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "preliminary site investigation" means a preliminary site investigation and report under section 41 [site investigations] that complies with the regulations;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "protocol" means a protocol established by a director under section 64 [director's protocols];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "registrar" means the registrar appointed under section 43 [site registry];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "regulator" has the same meaning as in the Energy Resource Activities Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "remediation order" means a remediation order under section 48 [remediation orders];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "remediation standards" means numerical standards relating to concentrations of substances and standards relating to risk assessment, as prescribed in the regulations;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "responsible person" means a person described in section 45 [persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "secured creditor" means a person who holds a mortgage, charge, debenture, hypothecation or other security interest in property at a contaminated site, and includes an agent for that person;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "site disclosure statement" means a site disclosure statement under section 40 [site disclosure statements];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "site investigation" means a detailed or preliminary site investigation referred to in section 41 [site investigations];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "site registry" means the site registry established under section 43 [site registry];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "specified industrial or commercial use" means a use of land for a prescribed industrial or commercial purpose or activity;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "subdivision" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a subdivision as defined in the Land Title Act, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) a subdivision under the Strata Property Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "summary of site condition" means a document that complies with subsection (3);

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "voluntary remediation agreement" means a voluntary remediation agreement referred to in section 51 [voluntary remediation agreements].

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (2) A government body is not an operator only as a result of

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) exercising regulatory authority with respect to a contaminated site,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) carrying out remediation of a contaminated site, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) providing advice or information with respect to a contaminated site or an activity that took place on the contaminated site.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (3) A summary of site condition must be

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) prepared

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (i)  by an approved professional,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (ii)  in the form established in a protocol, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (iii)  in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the minister, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) signed by the approved professional.

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: 40		  (1) A person must provide, in accordance with the regulations, a site disclosure statement to the following, as applicable, for land that the person knows or reasonably should know has been used for a specified industrial or commercial use:

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) the approving officer, if the person applies for or otherwise seeks approval for subdivision of the land;

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) the applicable municipality, if the person applies for or otherwise seeks approval for

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (i)  zoning of the land,

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (ii)  a development permit, or a building permit, for an activity that will likely disturb soil on the land, or

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (iii)  a prescribed activity on the land.

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (2) A person who is an owner or operator in relation to land that the person knows or reasonably should know has been used for a specified industrial or commercial use must provide to the registrar a site disclosure statement for that land if any of the following applies:

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) the person, to the extent provided in the regulations,

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (i)  decommissions a site on the land, or

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (ii)  ceases operations on the land;

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) the person files for protection under, or otherwise becomes subject to, the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act (Canada);

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (c) the person files a proposal, or a notice of intention to make a proposal, under Part III of the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada).

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (3) A permit holder under the Energy Resource Activities Act who is required under subsection (2) to provide a site disclosure statement must provide a copy of the site disclosure statement to the regulator.

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (4) A municipality or an approving officer, as applicable, must

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) assess, in accordance with the regulations, a site disclosure statement received under subsection (1), and

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) forward a copy of the site disclosure statement to the registrar.

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (5) A municipality or an approving officer may require a person to pay a fee for an assessment under subsection (4) (a).

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (6) A vendor of real property must provide, in accordance with the regulations, a site disclosure statement to a prospective purchaser of the real property if the vendor knows or reasonably should know that the real property has been used for a specified industrial or commercial use.

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (7) A person

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) who is a trustee, receiver or liquidator or who commences foreclosure proceedings, and

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) who takes possession or control of real property for the benefit of one or more creditors

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: must, immediately on taking possession or control of the real property, provide to the registrar a site disclosure statement if the person knows or reasonably should know that the real property has been used for a specified industrial or commercial use.

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (8) A director may order a person to prepare and provide to the director a site disclosure statement if that person

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) owns or occupies land that, in the opinion of the director, may be a contaminated site on account of any past or current use on that or other land, or

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) is a person referred to in subsection (1), (2) or (7) and fails to provide a satisfactorily completed site disclosure statement.

heading: Site disclosure statements
paragraph: (9) If the director orders the preparation of a site disclosure statement respecting land that is subsequently determined not to be a contaminated site, the director is not liable for any costs incurred by a person in preparing the site disclosure statement.

heading: Investigations required with provision of site disclosure statements
paragraph: 40.1		  (1) This section applies

heading: Investigations required with provision of site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) to a person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (1), and

heading: Investigations required with provision of site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) in prescribed circumstances, to a person who is required to provide a site disclosure statement under section 40 (2), (7) or (8).

heading: Investigations required with provision of site disclosure statements
paragraph: (2) Unless a director specifies otherwise, a person referred to in subsection (1) who is required to provide a site disclosure statement for land must, as required by the regulations, do the following in relation to that land:

heading: Investigations required with provision of site disclosure statements
paragraph: (a) undertake investigations;

heading: Investigations required with provision of site disclosure statements
paragraph: (b) prepare and submit, to a director, reports on the investigations referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection;

heading: Investigations required with provision of site disclosure statements
paragraph: (c) provide to a director other prescribed information.

heading: Site investigations
paragraph:
41
		  (1) A director may order an owner or operator of a site, at the owner's or operator's own expense, to undertake a preliminary site investigation or a detailed site investigation and to prepare a report of the investigation in accordance with the regulations and any applicable protocol if the director reasonably suspects on the basis of a site disclosure statement, or any other information, that the site

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (a) may be a contaminated site, or

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (b) contains substances that may cause or threaten to cause adverse effects on human health or the environment.

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (2) If a director orders a preliminary site investigation or a detailed site investigation respecting a site that is subsequently determined not to be a contaminated site, the director is not liable for any costs incurred by a person for completing the investigation and the related report.

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (3) On receipt of a report of a preliminary site investigation or a detailed site investigation submitted under this section, the director

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (a) must determine whether the report and investigation comply with any applicable regulations and orders,

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (b) must give notice to the owner or operator of the site of the determination under paragraph (a), and

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (c) may require the additional investigation and reporting the director considers necessary for the report and investigation to comply with any applicable regulations or orders.

heading: Site investigations
paragraph: (4) The duty to undertake a preliminary site investigation or a detailed site investigation and to prepare a report of the investigation under this section does not apply if a person seeks and obtains a determination that a site is a contaminated site under section 44 (3) [determination of contaminated sites].

heading: Approved professionals
paragraph:
42
		  (1) A director may designate classes of persons who are qualified to perform classes of activities, prepare classes of reports and other documents or make classes of recommendations that under this Act may be or are required to be performed, prepared or made by an approved professional.

heading: Approved professionals
paragraph: (2) The director may establish a roster of persons who are in a class designated under subsection (1).

heading: Approved professionals
paragraph: (3) A director may

heading: Approved professionals
paragraph: (a) make changes to the roster that are necessitated by the removal of a designation, and

heading: Approved professionals
paragraph: (b) add and remove names from the roster.

heading: Approved professionals
paragraph: (4) If a qualified professional has performed activities in a manner that a director has reasonable grounds to believe does not satisfy the applicable protocol established under section 64 [director's protocols], the director may suspend the qualified professional from the roster on terms and conditions.

heading: Site registry
paragraph:
43
		  (1) The minister must

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (a) establish a site registry, and

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (b) appoint a registrar to manage the site registry.

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (2) A director must provide to the registrar, in a form suitable for inclusion in the site registry, information respecting

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (a) all site disclosure statements, preliminary site investigations and detailed site investigations that the director receives,

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (b) all orders, approvals, voluntary remediation agreements and decisions, including determinations under section 44 (3) [determination of contaminated sites], made by the director under this Part,

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (c) pollution abatement orders under section 83 [pollution abatement orders] that impose a requirement for remediation,

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (d) notifications under section 54 [independent remediation procedures] respecting independent remediation,

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (e) declarations and orders made by the minister under section 58 [orphan sites], and

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (f) other information required by the regulations.

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (3) A director may request the registrar to enter in the site registry information that

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (a) is already available to the director, and

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (b) would normally be obtained through a site disclosure statement or site investigation,

heading: Site registry
paragraph: if, before requesting the registrar to do so, the director provides

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (c) notice to the owners or operators of the site, if known to the director, of the intention to make the request, and

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (d) an opportunity for those owners or operators to show cause to the director why the information contained in the request should not be entered into the site registry.

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (4) The registrar must enter by notation into the site registry

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (a) information referred to in subsections (2) and (3),

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (b) information respecting site disclosure statements that the registrar receives under section 40, and

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (c) decisions of the appeal board.

heading: Site registry
paragraph: (5) In accordance with the regulations, the registrar must provide for reasonable public access to information in the site registry.

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph:
44
		  (1) A director may determine whether a site is a contaminated site and, if the site is a contaminated site, the director may determine the boundaries of the contaminated site.

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), in determining whether a site is a contaminated site, the director must do all of the following:

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) make a preliminary determination of whether or not a site is a contaminated site, on the basis of a site disclosure statement, a preliminary site investigation, a detailed site investigation or other available information;

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) give notice in writing of the preliminary determination to

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (i)  the person who submitted the site disclosure statement, preliminary site investigation or detailed site investigation for the site,

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (ii)  any municipality or approving officer that has received, assessed and forwarded to the registrar a site disclosure statement for the site to which the preliminary determination pertains,

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (iii)  any person with a registered interest in the site as shown in the records of the land title office or a land registry office of a treaty first nation at the time the director searches the land title records, and

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (iv)  any person known to the director who may be a responsible person under section 45 [persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites] if the site is finally determined to be a contaminated site;

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (c) provide an opportunity for any person to comment on the preliminary determination;

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (d) make a final determination of whether or not a site is a contaminated site;

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (e) give notice in writing of the final determination to

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (i)  the person who submitted the site disclosure statement, preliminary site investigation or detailed site investigation for the site,

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (ii)  any municipality or approving officer that has received, assessed and forwarded to the registrar a site disclosure statement for the site to which the final determination pertains,

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (iii)  any person with a registered interest in the site as shown in the records of the land title office or a land registry office of a treaty first nation at the time of the final determination,

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (iv)  any person known to the director who may be a responsible person under section 45 [persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites], and

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (v)  any person who has commented under paragraph (c);

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (f) carry out any other procedures specified in the regulations.

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (3) A director, on request by any person, may omit the procedures set out in subsection (2) (a) to (c) and make a final determination that a site is a contaminated site if the person

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) provides reasonably sufficient information to determine that the site is a contaminated site, and

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) agrees to be a responsible person for the contaminated site.

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (4) The lack of a determination under subsection (2) or (3) does not mean that a site is not a contaminated site.

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (5) In addition to a site in respect of which a director makes a determination under subsection (1), a site is considered to be or to have been a contaminated site if a director has done any of the following:

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) appointed an allocation panel with respect to the site under section 49 [allocation panel];

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) determined that a responsible person is a minor contributor with respect to the site under section 50 [minor contributors];

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (c) entered into a voluntary remediation agreement with respect to the site under section 51 [voluntary remediation agreements];

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (d) issued an approval in principle with respect to a proposed remediation plan for the site under section 53 (1) [approvals in principle and certificates of compliance];

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (e) issued a certificate of compliance with respect to remediation of the site under section 53 (3) [approvals in principle and certificates of compliance].

heading: Determination of contaminated sites
paragraph: (6) A final determination made under this section is a decision that may be appealed under Division 2 [Appeals from Decisions under this Act] of Part 8.

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph:
45
		  (1) Subject to section 46 [persons not responsible for remediation], the following persons are responsible for remediation of a contaminated site:

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) a current owner or operator of the site;

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) a previous owner or operator of the site;

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (c) a person who

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (i)  produced a substance, and

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (ii)  by contract, agreement or otherwise caused the substance to be disposed of, handled or treated in a manner that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site;

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (d) a person who

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (i)  transported or arranged for transport of a substance, and

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (ii)  by contract, agreement or otherwise caused the substance to be disposed of, handled or treated in a manner that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site;

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (e) a person who is in a class designated in the regulations as responsible for remediation.

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (2) In addition to the persons referred to in subsection (1), the following persons are responsible for remediation of a contaminated site that was contaminated by migration of a substance to the contaminated site:

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) a current owner or operator of the site from which the substance migrated;

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) a previous owner or operator of the site from which the substance migrated;

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (c) a person who

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (i)  produced the substance, and

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (ii)  by contract, agreement or otherwise caused the substance to be disposed of, handled or treated in a manner that, in whole or in part, caused the substance to migrate to the contaminated site;

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (d) a person who

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (i)  transported or arranged for transport of the substance, and

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (ii)  by contract, agreement or otherwise caused the substance to be disposed of, handled or treated in a manner that, in whole or in part, caused the substance to migrate to the contaminated site.

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (3) A secured creditor is responsible for remediation of a contaminated site if

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) the secured creditor at any time exercised control over or imposed requirements on any person regarding the manner of treatment, disposal or handling of a substance and the control or requirements, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site, or

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) the secured creditor becomes the registered owner in fee simple of the real property at the contaminated site.

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (4) A secured creditor is not responsible for remediation if it acts primarily to protect its security interest, including, without limitation, if the secured creditor

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) participates only in purely financial matters related to the site,

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) has the capacity or ability to influence any operation at the contaminated site in a manner that would have the effect of causing or increasing contamination, but does not exercise that capacity or ability in such a manner as to cause or increase contamination,

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (c) imposes requirements on any person, if the requirements do not have a reasonable probability of causing or increasing contamination at the site, or

heading: Persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites
paragraph: (d) appoints a person to inspect or investigate a contaminated site to determine future steps or actions that the secured creditor might take.

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph:
46
		  (1) The following persons are not responsible for remediation of a contaminated site:

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (a) a person who would become a responsible person only because of an act of God that occurred before April 1, 1997, if the person exercised due diligence with respect to any substance that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (b) a person who would become a responsible person only because of an act of war if the person exercised due diligence with respect to any substance that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (c) a person who would become a responsible person only because of an act or omission of a third party, other than

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (i)  an employee,

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  an agent, or

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (iii)  a party with whom the person has a contractual relationship,

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: if the person exercised due diligence with respect to any substance that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (d) an owner or operator who establishes that

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (i)  at the time the person became an owner or operator of the site,

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (A) the site was a contaminated site,

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (B) the person had no knowledge or reason to know or suspect that the site was a contaminated site, and

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (C) the person undertook all appropriate inquiries into the previous ownership and uses of the site and undertook other investigations, consistent with good commercial or customary practice at that time, in an effort to minimize potential liability,

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  if the person was an owner of the site, the person did not transfer any interest in the site without first disclosing any known contamination to the transferee, and

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (iii)  the owner or operator did not, by any act or omission, cause or contribute to the contamination of the site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (e) an owner or operator who

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (i)  owned or occupied a site that at the time of acquisition was not a contaminated site, and

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  during the ownership or operation, did not dispose of, handle or treat a substance in a manner that, in whole or in part, caused the site to become a contaminated site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (f) a person described in section 45 (1) (c) or (d) or (2) (c) or (d) [persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites] who

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (i)  transported or arranged to transport the substance to the site, if the owner or operator of the site was authorized under an Act to accept the substance at the time of its deposit, and

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  received permission from the owner or operator described in subparagraph (i) to deposit the substance;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (g) a government body that involuntarily acquires an ownership interest in the contaminated site, other than by government restructuring or expropriation, unless the government body caused or contributed to the contamination of the site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (g.1) a government body that takes possession of or acquires an ownership interest in the contaminated site under an order of the court under section 6, 9 (4) or 28 of the Civil Forfeiture Act or a delegate under section 66 (2) of that Act who is exercising powers or performing duties and functions of the director, as defined in that Act, in relation to the contaminated site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (h) a person who provides assistance respecting remediation work at a contaminated site, unless the assistance is carried out in a negligent fashion;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (i) a person who provides advice respecting remediation work at a contaminated site unless the advice is negligent;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
