paragraph: (j) a person who owns or operates a contaminated site that was contaminated only by the migration of a substance from other real property not owned or operated by the person;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (k) an owner or operator of a contaminated site containing substances that are present only as natural occurrences not assisted by human activity and if those substances alone caused the site to be a contaminated site;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (l) subject to subsection (2), a government body that possesses, owns or operates a roadway, highway or right of way for sewerage or waterworks on a contaminated site, to the extent of the possession, ownership or operation;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (m) a person who was a responsible person for a contaminated site for which a certificate of compliance was issued and for which another person subsequently proposes or undertakes to

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (i)  change the use of the contaminated site, and

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (ii)  provide additional remediation;

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (n) a person who is in a class designated in the regulations as not responsible for remediation.

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (2)               Subsection (1) (l) does not apply with respect to contamination placed or deposited below a roadway, highway or right of way for sewerage or waterworks by the government body that possesses, owns or operates the roadway, highway or right of way for sewerage or waterworks.

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph:
(2.1) 
              Subsection (1) (g.1) does not apply with respect to contamination if the government body or delegate referred to in that provision caused or contributed to the contamination of the site.

heading: Persons not responsible for remediation
paragraph: (3) A person seeking to establish that they are not a responsible person under subsection (1) has the burden to prove all elements of the exemption on a balance of probabilities.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph:
47
		  (1) A person who is responsible for remediation of a contaminated site is absolutely, retroactively and jointly and separately liable to any person or government body for reasonably incurred costs of remediation of the contaminated site, whether incurred on or off the contaminated site.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) must not be construed as prohibiting the apportionment of a share of liability to one or more responsible persons by the court in an action or proceeding under subsection (5) or by a director in an order under section 48 [remediation orders].

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of this section, "costs of remediation" means all costs of remediation and includes, without limitation,

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (a) costs of preparing a site disclosure statement,

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (b) costs of carrying out a site investigation and preparing a report, whether or not there has been a determination under section 44 [determination of contaminated sites] as to whether or not the site is a contaminated site,

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (c) legal and consultant costs associated with seeking contributions from other responsible persons, and

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (d) fees imposed by a director, a municipality, an approving officer or the regulator under this Part.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (4) Liability under this Part applies

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (a) even though the introduction of a substance into the environment is or was not prohibited by any legislation if the introduction contributed in whole or in part to the site becoming a contaminated site, and

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (b) despite the terms of any cancelled, expired, abandoned or current permit or approval or waste management plan and its associated operational certificate that authorizes the discharge of waste into the environment.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (5) Subject to section 50 (3) [minor contributors], any person, including, but not limited to, a responsible person and a director, who incurs costs in carrying out remediation of a contaminated site may commence an action or a proceeding to recover the reasonably incurred costs of remediation from one or more responsible persons in accordance with the principles of liability set out in this Part.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (6) Subject to subsections (7) and (8), a person is not required to obtain, as a condition of an action or proceeding under subsection (5) being heard by a court,

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (a) a decision, determination, opinion or apportionment of liability for remediation from a director, or

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (b) an opinion respecting liability from an allocation panel.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (7) In all cases, the site that is the subject of an action or proceeding must be determined or considered under section 44 [determination of contaminated sites] to be or to have been a contaminated site before the court can hear the matter.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (8) Despite subsection (7), if independent remediation has been carried out at a site and the site has not been determined or considered under section 44 [determination of contaminated sites] to be or to have been a contaminated site, the court must determine whether the site is or was a contaminated site.

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (9) The court may determine in accordance with the regulations, unless otherwise determined or established under this Part, any of the following:

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (a) whether a person is responsible for remediation of a contaminated site;

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (b) whether the costs of remediation of a contaminated site have been reasonably incurred and the amount of the reasonably incurred costs of remediation;

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (c) the apportionment of the reasonably incurred costs of remediation of a contaminated site among one or more responsible persons in accordance with the principles of liability set out in this Part;

heading: General principles of liability for remediation
paragraph: (d) such other determinations as are necessary to a fair and just disposition of these matters.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph:
48
		  (1) A director may issue a remediation order to any responsible person.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (2) A remediation order may require a person referred to in subsection (1) to do any or all of the following:

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) undertake remediation;

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) contribute, in cash or in kind, towards the costs of another person who has reasonably incurred costs of remediation;

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (c) give security, which may include real and personal property, in the amount and form the director specifies.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of deciding whether to require a person to undertake remediation under subsection (2), a director may consider whether remediation should begin promptly, and must consider each of the following:

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) adverse effects on human health or pollution of the environment caused by contamination at the site;

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) the potential for adverse effects on human health or pollution of the environment arising from contamination at the site;

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (c) the likelihood of the responsible persons or other persons not acting expeditiously or satisfactorily in implementing remediation;

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (d) in consultation with the chief permitting officer designated under the Mines Act, the requirements of a permit issued under section 10 of that Act;

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (e) in consultation with the regulator, the adequacy of remediation being undertaken under section 41 of the Energy Resource Activities Act;

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (e.1) the actions being undertaken or to be undertaken under a recovery plan approved under section 91.2 (5) [responsible persons - spill response];

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (f) other factors prescribed in the regulations.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of deciding who will be ordered to undertake or contribute to remediation under subsections (1) and (2), a director, to the extent feasible without jeopardizing remediation requirements, must

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) take into account private agreements between or among responsible persons respecting liability for remediation, if those agreements are known to the director, and

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) on the basis of information known to the director, name one or more persons whose activities, directly or indirectly, contributed most substantially to the site becoming a contaminated site, taking into account such factors as

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (i)  the degree of involvement by the persons in the generation, transportation, treatment, storage or disposal of any substance that contributed, in whole or in part, to the site becoming a contaminated site, and

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (ii)  the diligence exercised by persons with respect to the contamination.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (5) A remediation order does not affect or modify a right of a person affected by the order to seek or obtain relief under an agreement, other legislation or common law, including, but not limited to, damages for injury or loss resulting from a release or threatened release of a contaminating substance.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (6) If a remediation order, or a pollution abatement order under section 83 [pollution abatement orders] that imposes a requirement for remediation, is issued in respect of a site, and the director has not yet determined under section 44 [determination of contaminated sites] whether the site is a contaminated site, as soon as reasonably possible after the issuance of the order, the director must determine

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) whether the site is a contaminated site, in accordance with section 44 [determination of contaminated sites], and

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) whether the person named in the order is a responsible person under section 45 [persons responsible for remediation of contaminated sites].

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (7) If a person named in an order referred to in subsection (6) is determined not to be a responsible person, the government must compensate the person, in accordance with the regulations, for any costs directly incurred by the person in complying with the order.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (8) A person who receives a remediation order under subsection (1) or notice of a remediation order under subsection (13) must not, without the consent of the director, knowingly do anything that diminishes or reduces assets that could be used to satisfy the terms and conditions of the remediation order, and if the person does so, the director despite any other remedy sought, may commence an action against the person to recover the amount of the diminishment or reduction.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (9) The director may provide in a remediation order that a responsible person is not required to begin remediation of a contaminated site for a specified period of time if the contaminated site does not present an imminent and significant threat or risk to

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) human health, given current and anticipated human exposure, or

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) the environment.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (10) A person who has submitted a site disclosure statement under section 40 (7) [site disclosure statements of trustee, receiver, etc.] must not directly or indirectly diminish or reduce assets at a site designated in the site registry as a contaminated site, including, without limitation, by

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) disposing of real or personal assets, or

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) subdividing land

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: unless the person first requests and obtains written notice from a director that the director does not intend to issue a remediation order.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (11) If a director issues or gives notice of the intention to issue a remediation order to a person referred to in subsection (10), subsection (8) applies.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (12) A director may amend or cancel a remediation order.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (13) A director, on making a remediation order must, within a reasonable time, provide notice of the order in writing to every person holding an interest in the contaminated site if the interest is registered in the land title office or a land registry office of a treaty first nation at the time of issuing the order.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (14) A remediation order may authorize, subject to the terms and conditions a director considers necessary and reasonable, any person designated by the director to enter specified land for the purpose of ensuring that the remediation order is carried out according to its terms.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (15) If a remediation order authorizes a person to enter specified land, the person who owns or occupies the land must allow the authorized person to enter in accordance with the authorization.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (16)               Subsections (14) and (15) do not authorize any person to enter any structure or part of a structure that is used solely as a private residence.

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph:
49
		  (1) The minister may appoint up to 12 persons with specialized knowledge in contamination, remediation or methods of dispute resolution to act as allocation advisors under this section.

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (2) A director, on request by any person, may appoint an allocation panel consisting of 3 allocation advisors to provide an opinion as to any or all of the following:

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (a) whether the person is a responsible person;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (b) whether a responsible person is a minor contributor;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (c) the responsible person's contribution to the contamination and, if the costs of remediation are known or reasonably ascertainable, the share of those costs attributable to that contamination.

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of providing an opinion under subsection (2) (b) and (c), the allocation panel must, to the extent of available information, consider the following:

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (a) the information available to identify a person's relative contribution to the contamination;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (b) the nature and quantity of substances causing the contamination;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (c) the degree of toxicity of the substances causing the contamination;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (d) the degree of involvement by the responsible person, compared with one or more other responsible persons, in the generation, transportation, treatment, storage or disposal of the substances that caused the contamination;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (e) the degree of diligence exercised by the responsible person, compared with one or more other responsible persons, with respect to the generation, transportation, treatment, storage or disposal of the substances causing contamination, taking into account the characteristics of the substances;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (f) the degree of cooperation by the responsible person with government officials to prevent harm to human health or the environment;

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (g) in the case of a minor contributor, factors set out in section 50 (1) (a) and (b) [minor contributors];

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (h) other factors considered by the panel to be relevant to apportioning liability.

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (4) A director may require, as a condition of entering a voluntary remediation agreement with a responsible person, that the responsible person, at the responsible person's own expense, seek and provide to the director the opinion of an allocation panel under subsection (2).

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (5) If a director appoints an allocation panel with respect to a site, the site is considered to be a contaminated site at the time the allocation panel is appointed, despite the absence of a determination under section 44 (1) [determination of contaminated sites].

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (6) A director may consider, but is not bound by, the opinion of an allocation panel.

heading: Allocation panel
paragraph: (7) Work performed by the allocation panel must be paid for by the person who requests the opinion.

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph:
50
		  (1) A director may determine that a responsible person is a minor contributor if the person demonstrates that

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (a) only a minor portion of the contamination present at the site can be attributed to the person,

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (b) either

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (i)  no remediation would be required solely as a result of the contribution of the person to the contamination at the site, or

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (ii)  the cost of remediation attributable to the person would be only a minor portion of the total cost of the remediation required at the site, and

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (c) in all circumstances the application of joint and separate liability to the person would be unduly harsh.

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (2) If a director makes a determination under subsection (1) that a responsible person is a minor contributor, the director must determine the amount or portion of remediation costs attributable to the responsible person.

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (3) A responsible person determined to be a minor contributor under subsection (1) is liable for remediation costs in an action or proceeding brought by another person or the government under section 47 [general principles of liability for remediation] only up to the amount or portion specified by the director in the determination under subsection (2).

heading: Minor contributors
paragraph: (4) If a director has determined that a responsible person is a minor contributor for a site, the site is considered to be a contaminated site at the time of that determination, despite the absence of a determination under section 44 (1) [determination of contaminated sites].

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph:
51
		  (1) On the request of a responsible person, including a minor contributor, a director may enter into a voluntary remediation agreement in accordance with the regulations, consisting of

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (a) provisions for financial or other contributions by the responsible person,

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (b) a certification by the responsible person that the person has fully and accurately disclosed all information in the person's possession or control regarding site conditions and the person's activities respecting that site,

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (c) security, which may include real and personal property, in the amount and form, and subject to the conditions the director specifies,

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (d) a schedule of remediation acceptable to the director, and

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (e) requirements that the director considers to be reasonably necessary to achieve remediation.

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (2) If a responsible person enters into and performs a voluntary remediation agreement according to its terms,

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (a) the responsible person is discharged from further liability,

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (b) other responsible persons not named in the voluntary remediation agreement are not discharged from liability,

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (c) the total potential liability of other responsible persons is reduced by any amount specified in the voluntary remediation agreement,

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (d) the right of any person to seek or obtain relief under other legislation or under the common law, including, but not limited to, damages for injury or loss resulting from contamination, is not affected or modified in any way, and

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (e) the director is not prevented from entering into another voluntary remediation agreement in respect of the same site.

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (3) A director may stipulate in a voluntary remediation agreement that a responsible person is not required to begin remediation of a contaminated site for a specified period of time if the responsible person demonstrates that the contaminated site does not present an imminent and significant threat or risk to

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (a) human health, given current and anticipated human exposure, or

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (b) the environment.

heading: Voluntary remediation agreements
paragraph: (4) If a director has entered into a voluntary remediation agreement for a site, the site is considered to be a contaminated site at the time the agreement was made, despite the absence of a determination under section 44 (1) [determination of contaminated sites].

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph:
52
		  (1) A director may order that a responsible person, at the person's own expense, provide, in accordance with any regulations, for public consultation on a proposed remediation or a public review of remediation activities.

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of deciding whether to make an order under subsection (1), the director may take into account any factors the director considers relevant, including without limitation, the following:

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (a) the size and location of the contaminated site;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (b) the nature of contamination at the contaminated site;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (c) the potential for human exposure to contamination;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (d) the impact on the environment of the contamination;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (e) migration of contamination off the site;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (f) the remediation methods proposed to be used and the potential for long term health, environmental or financial impacts;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (g) opportunities for public involvement provided by any municipal development approval process;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (h) whether consultation with the public would improve the quality of information in a site investigation;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (i) whether consultation with the public would enable a well informed choice on the preferred remediation alternative;

heading: Public consultation and review
paragraph: (j) the extent to which public consultation has already taken place.

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph:
53
		  (1) For the purposes of exercising powers and performing duties under this section, a director may rely on any information the director considers sufficient for the purpose, including, but not limited to, a preliminary site investigation, a detailed site investigation, a risk assessment, a remediation plan or a summary of site condition.

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (1.1) On application by a responsible person, a director, in accordance with the regulations, may issue an approval in principle stating that a remediation plan for a contaminated site

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (a) has been reviewed by the director,

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (b) has been approved by the director, and

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (c) may be implemented in accordance with conditions specified by the director.

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1.1), if a director has issued an approval in principle with respect to a proposed remediation plan for a site, the site is considered to be a contaminated site at the time the approval in principle was issued, despite the absence of a determination under section 44 (1) [determination of contaminated sites].

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (3) A director, in accordance with the regulations, may issue a certificate of compliance with respect to remediation of a contaminated site if

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (a) the contaminated site has been remediated in accordance with

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (i)  the numerical or risk based standards prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "contaminated site",

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (ii)  any orders under this Act,

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (iii)  any remediation plan approved by the director, and

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (iv)  any requirements imposed by the director,

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (c) a plan has been prepared for the purposes of containing, controlling and monitoring any substances remaining on the site and, if required by the director, works have been installed to implement the plan,

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (d) any security in relation to the management of contamination, which security may include real and personal property in the amount and form and subject to the conditions specified by the director, has been provided in accordance with the minister's regulations, and

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (e) the responsible person, if required by the director in prescribed circumstances or for prescribed purposes, has prepared and provided to the director proof of registration of a restrictive covenant under section 219 of the Land Title Act acceptable to the director.

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of subsection (3) if a director has issued a certificate of compliance with respect to remediation of a site, the site is considered to have been a contaminated site at the time remediation of the site began, despite the absence of a determination under section 44 (1) [determination of contaminated sites].

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (5) A director may withhold or rescind an approval in principle or a certificate of compliance if

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (a) conditions imposed on the approval or certificate are not complied with, or

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (b) any fees payable under this Part or the regulations are outstanding.

heading: Approvals in principle and certificates of compliance
paragraph: (6) A director may issue an approval in principle or a certificate of compliance for a part of a contaminated site.

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: 54		  (1) A responsible person may carry out independent remediation in accordance with the minister's regulations whether or not

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (a) a determination has been made as to whether the site is a contaminated site,

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (b) a remediation order has been issued with respect to the site, or

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (c) a voluntary remediation agreement with respect to the site has been entered into.

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (2) Any person undertaking independent remediation of a contaminated site must

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (a) notify a director in writing promptly on initiating remediation, and

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (b) notify the director in writing within 90 days of completing remediation.

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (3) A director may at any time during independent remediation by any person

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (a) inspect and monitor any aspect of the remediation to determine compliance with the regulations,

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (b) issue a remediation order as appropriate,

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (c) order public consultation and review under section 52 [public consultation and review], or

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (d) impose requirements that the director considers are reasonably necessary to achieve remediation.

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (4) On request of a person carrying out independent remediation and on receiving adequate information respecting the independent remediation, a director may

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (a) review the remediation in accordance with the regulations and any requirements imposed under subsection (3) (d), and

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (b) issue an approval in principle or a certificate of compliance under section 53 [approvals in principle and certificates of compliance].

heading: Independent remediation procedures
paragraph: (5) The director may assess against a person, in accordance with the regulations, the prescribed fees for carrying out the actions referred to in subsection (4).

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (1.1) A person must not remove soil from a site that has been used for a specified industrial or commercial use unless the person has

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (a) analyzed the quality of the soil, in accordance with the regulations, if any, and

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (b) provided notice of the removal to the prescribed persons, in accordance with subsection (1.2).

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (1.2) Notice under subsection (1.1) (b) must

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (a) include the following information:

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (i)  the site from which the soil will be removed;

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (ii)  the site or sites at which the soil will be deposited;

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (iii)  the maximum amount of soil that will be deposited at each site;

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (iv)  a summary, prepared in accordance with the regulations, if any, of the analysis referred to in subsection (1.1) (a);

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (v)  the prescribed information,

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (b) be provided in the prescribed form and manner, if any, and

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (c) be provided by the prescribed date.

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (1.3) If notice under subsection (1.1) is required to remove soil from a site, a person must not deposit the soil at another site unless

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (a) the other site is specified in the notice in accordance with subsection (1.2) (a) (ii), and

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (b) the amount of soil deposited is equal to or less than the maximum amount specified in relation to the other site in the notice, in accordance with subsection (1.2) (a) (iii).

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (1.4) Subsection (1.1) does not apply in relation to the removal of soil if the amount of soil removed is less than the amount set out in the regulations.

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this Part prevents a person from depositing soil at a site if the deposit is authorized by

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (a) a valid and subsisting permit or approval,

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (b) an order,

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (c) a waste management plan approved by the minister, and its associated operational certificate, or

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (d) the regulations.

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (6) A municipality or treaty first nation, including its employees or members of its governing body, does not incur any liability and must not be considered a responsible person under this Act as a result of any bylaw, law, permit, licence, approval or other document adopted or issued under the Community Charter, the Islands Trust Act, the Local Government Act, the Vancouver Charter or a law of a treaty first nation that authorizes the removal or deposit of contaminated soil in the municipality or treaty lands.

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (7) Despite section 37 (5) [conflicts between this Act and bylaws, permits, etc. issued by a municipality], subsection (6) of this section does not apply if

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (a) a bylaw of a municipality or law of a treaty first nation, or

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (b) a permit, licence, approval or other document issued under the authority of a municipal bylaw or law of a treaty first nation

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: establishes standards or procedures for testing, excavating, storing, removing, relocating or depositing contaminated soil that conflict with this Act or the regulations or a permit, approval, order or approved waste management plan.

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (8)               Subsection (6) does not give immunity to any municipality or treaty first nation from obligations the municipality or treaty first nation may have under this Act with respect to

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (a) a contaminated site owned by the municipality or treaty first nation,

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (b) contaminated soil that originated from property owned by the municipality or treaty first nation, or

heading: Removal and deposit of soil
paragraph: (c) activities of the municipality or treaty first nation, other than regulatory activities, that caused or contributed to property becoming a contaminated site.

heading: High volume soil receiving sites
paragraph:
55.1
		  (1) In this section, "relocated industrial or commercial site soil" means soil that has been relocated from a site that has been used for a specified industrial or commercial use.

heading: High volume soil receiving sites
paragraph: (2) If the total amount of relocated industrial or commercial site soil present at a site is greater than the prescribed amount, the owner of the site must do the following, as required by the regulations:

heading: High volume soil receiving sites
paragraph: (a) prepare plans, and carry out actions, to prevent, contain, control and monitor the adverse effects, and potential adverse effects, on the environment or human health caused by the soil being present at the site;

heading: High volume soil receiving sites
paragraph: (b) provide to the director the prescribed information.

heading: Selection of remediation options
paragraph:
56
		  (1) A person conducting or otherwise providing for remediation of a site must give preference to remediation alternatives that provide permanent solutions to the maximum extent practicable, taking into account the following factors:

heading: Selection of remediation options
paragraph: (a) any potential for adverse effects on human health or for pollution of the environment;

heading: Selection of remediation options
paragraph: (b) the technical feasibility and risks associated with alternative remediation options;

heading: Selection of remediation options
paragraph: (c) remediation costs associated with alternative remediation options and the potential economic benefits, costs and effects of the remediation options;

heading: Selection of remediation options
paragraph: (d) other prescribed factors.

heading: Selection of remediation options
paragraph: (2) When issuing an approval in principle or a certificate of compliance, a director must consider whether permanent solutions have been given preference to the maximum extent practicable as determined in accordance with any guidelines set out in the regulations.

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph:
57
		  (1) The minister and a municipality may enter into an agreement authorizing the municipality to exercise powers and perform functions described in subsection (3), except in relation to a contaminated site that is owned by a municipality or for which a municipality is a responsible person.

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of enhancing coordination of Provincial regulatory activities, the minister and any other minister of the government may enter into an arrangement enabling officials of the ministry of the other minister to exercise or perform one or more powers and functions described in this Part, except in relation to a contaminated site that is owned by that ministry or for which that ministry is a responsible person.

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (3) If an agreement or arrangement under subsection (1) or (2) has been entered into, a director may delegate to one or more officials of a municipality or another ministry the powers and functions of a director respecting any or all of the following:

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (a) site disclosure statements;

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (b) site investigations;

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (c) remediation orders;

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (d) voluntary remediation agreements;

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (e) public consultations or reviews;

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (f) approvals in principle;

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (g) certificates of compliance.

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (4) A director may not delegate under subsection (3) any of the powers or functions with respect to the following:

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (a) determining whether a site is a contaminated site;

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (b) determining whether a responsible person is a minor contributor.

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (5) If a power or function is delegated to a municipality or another ministry under this section, the municipality or other minister may assess the fees prescribed in the regulations with respect to that power or function.

heading: Delegation of responsibilities to municipalities or other ministries
paragraph: (6) If a power or function has been delegated to an official of a municipality or a ministry, a decision of the official is a decision that may be appealed to the appeal board under Division 2 [Appeals of Decisions under this Act] of Part 8.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph:
58
		  (1) A director may determine in accordance with the regulations whether

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (a) a contaminated site is an orphan site, and

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (b) an orphan site is a high risk orphan site.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (2) The minister may declare, in writing, that it is necessary for the protection of human health or the environment for the government to undertake remediation of

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (a) a contaminated site that is not otherwise being adequately remediated, or

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (b) a high risk orphan site.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (3) If the minister has made a declaration under subsection (2), the minister may carry out remediation and recover the reasonably incurred costs of the remediation and the minister, or an officer authorized in writing by the minister, may, even though the ordered action interferes with or abrogates property rights, order any person to

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (a) provide labour, services, material, equipment or facilities, or

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (b) allow the use of land for the purpose of undertaking the remediation.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (4) If the minister has made a declaration under subsection (2), a director, an officer or any person directed to do so by the officer, may enter property and carry out remediation, even though the entry or remediation interferes with or abrogates property rights.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (5) A person affected by an order made under subsection (3) must comply with the order despite any other enactment.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (6) If the minister certifies that money is required to undertake remediation under this section, the amount the minister certifies to be required may be paid out of the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (7) A certificate signed by the minister and showing an amount of money spent by the government under this section is conclusive proof of the amount spent.

heading: Orphan sites
paragraph: (8) If the minister makes a declaration under subsection (2) or an order under subsection (3), the registrar must make a notation of the declaration or order on the site registry.

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph:
59
		  (1) A director may recover all or a portion of the cost of remediation by

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (a) taking steps to identify and recover costs from responsible persons during or after remediation,

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (b) arranging to sell or selling any property comprising all or part of the site, or

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (c) seeking contributions from available cost sharing agreements with government bodies or other persons.

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (2) The amount shown on the certificate under section 58 (7) [orphan sites] is a debt due to the government and, subject to subsection (3) of this section, is recoverable

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (a) from any responsible person, by action in the Supreme Court, or

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (b) by order of the minister directing a person who is purchasing or otherwise acquiring an interest in land that is subject to remediation under section 58 [orphan sites] to pay to the minister, in respect of the amounts spent in remediation, instead of to the vendor, an amount not exceeding the amount owing to the vendor, and the purchaser is discharged in the amount paid to the minister from the obligation to pay the vendor.

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (3) If the Supreme Court is satisfied that the expenditure incurred by the government under section 58 [orphan sites] is either

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (a) excessive, taking into consideration the requirements of the regulations governing remediation, or

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (b) unnecessary, taking into consideration the regulations governing remediation,

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: the Supreme Court may reduce or extinguish the amount of the judgment that it would otherwise have ordered to be entered against the person against whom the action has been brought.

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (4) The minister may register a lien at the land title office against a contaminated site for the costs of remediation incurred by the government at the contaminated site that has been remediated under section 58 [orphan sites].

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (5) A lien under subsection (4) is payable in priority over all liens, charges or mortgages of every person, whenever created or to be created, with respect to the site or proceeds of the site, except for liens for wages due to workers by their employer and liens under section 265 of the Workers Compensation Act.

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (6) The exception in subsection (5) does not apply in respect of a lien for wages that is, by section 87 (5) of the Employment Standards Act, postponed to a mortgage or debenture.

heading: Cost recovery if minister carries out remediation
paragraph: (7) If the minister makes an order under subsection (2) (b), the registrar must make a notation of the order on the site registry.

heading: Government retains right to take future action
paragraph: 60		  A director may exercise any of a director's powers or functions under this Part, even though they have been previously exercised and despite any voluntary remediation agreement, if

heading: Government retains right to take future action
paragraph: (a) additional information relevant to establishing liability for remediation becomes available, including information that indicates that a responsible person does not meet the requirements of a minor contributor,

heading: Government retains right to take future action
paragraph: (b) activities occur on a site that may change its condition or use,

heading: Government retains right to take future action
paragraph: (c) information becomes available about a site or a contaminating substance at the site that leads to a reasonable inference that the site poses a threat to human health or the environment,

heading: Government retains right to take future action
paragraph: (d) a responsible person fails to exercise due care with respect to any contamination at the site, or

heading: Government retains right to take future action
paragraph: (e) a responsible person directly or indirectly contributes to contamination at the site after previous action.

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph:
61
		  (1) In this section, "protected person" means

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) the government,

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) the minister,

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (c) a municipality,

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (d) a current or former approving officer,

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (e) a current or former employee or agent of the government,

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (f) a current or former elected official of the government,

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (g) a current or former "local public officer" as defined in section 738 (1) [immunity for individual local public officers] of the Local Government Act, and

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (h) a current or former "civic public officer" as defined in section 294 (4) of the Vancouver Charter.

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), no action lies and no proceedings may be brought against a protected person because of

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) any

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (i)  act, advice, including pre-application advice, or recommendation, or

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: (ii)  failure to act, failure to provide advice, including pre-application advice, or failure to make recommendations

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites
paragraph: in relation to this Part, regulations under this Part, section 85.1 of the Land Title Act, section 556 or 557 of the Local Government Act, section 571B of the Vancouver Charter or section 34.1 of the Islands Trust Act, or

heading: Immunity in relation to contaminated sites

paragraph: (b) prescribing fees and charges to be paid in respect of any matter for which the ministry provides a service or performs a duty in relation to the testing and certification of fuels for compliance with the regulations, and prescribing by whom the fees and charges are to be paid;

heading: Fuel emission regulations
paragraph: (c) requiring manufacturers and persons who test, certify or sell fuels to record and report specified information at the times and in the manner provided in the regulations;

heading: Fuel emission regulations
paragraph: (d) specifying the areas in British Columbia to which the regulations apply and specifying the date on which the regulations become effective in those areas;

heading: Fuel emission regulations
paragraph: (e) classifying fuels for the purpose of a regulation and exempting a class of fuel from a regulation.

heading: Fuel emission regulations

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph:
74
		  (1) Without limiting section 138 (1) [general authority to make regulations], the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purpose of preventing and reducing emissions from new motor vehicles and from engines including, without limiting that power, regulations for one or more of the following:

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (a) requiring motor vehicles or engines to have installed on or incorporated in them one or more emission control systems;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (b) requiring motor vehicles, engines or emission control systems to meet prescribed standards, specifications and design requirements;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (c) prescribing standards, specifications and design requirements for the purposes of paragraph (b);

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (d) providing for the testing and certification of motor vehicles, engines and emission control systems for compliance with prescribed standards, specifications and design requirements;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (e) requiring motor vehicles or engines to meet design requirements that are certified in a specified jurisdiction to conform to the emission control standards of that jurisdiction;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (f) prohibiting the sale of a new motor vehicle or engine unless it meets prescribed requirements for labelling as to

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (i)  the emission control performance of the motor vehicle or engine,

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (ii)  compliance with requirements under this Act, and

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (iii)  maintenance specifications in relation to emission control;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (g) prescribing the form, content and manner of placement for labels required under paragraph (f);

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (h) prohibiting, if a manufacturer produces within the same motor vehicle product line, or within a class within that product line, motor vehicles with different designs certified in a specified jurisdiction to conform to different emission control standards, the sale of motor vehicles within that product line or class that meet the less stringent emission control standards;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (i) requiring manufacturers of new motor vehicles or engines to deliver and have available for sale in British Columbia a model of motor vehicle or engine that meets specified emission control standards;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (j) establishing a scheme under which, for each manufacturer of new motor vehicles, the motor vehicles that are produced and delivered for sale in British Columbia during a specified time period must be a mix of motor vehicles determined in accordance with a specified formula;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (k) requiring each manufacturer of new motor vehicles to

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (i)  develop, submit and have approved by the minister a plan for reducing emissions from motor vehicles in British Columbia that, in the opinion of the minister, meets the prescribed requirements for such plans, and

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (ii)  implement and comply with the plan approved under subparagraph (i);

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (l) prescribing requirements for the contents of, and emission reduction goals that must be met by, a plan under paragraph (k);

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (m) prohibiting the sale of a class of new motor vehicles or a class of engines produced by a manufacturer if, in relation to the manufacturer, requirements established under paragraph (i), (j) or (k) are not met;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (n) prohibiting the sale of a new motor vehicle or engine unless it is sold with an emission control warranty that is provided by the manufacturer and that meets the content requirements specified in the regulation;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (o) prescribing fees and charges to be paid in respect of any matter for which the ministry provides a service or performs a duty in relation to the testing and certification of motor vehicles or engines for compliance with the regulations, and prescribing by whom the fees and charges are to be paid;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (p) requiring manufacturers and persons who test, certify or sell motor vehicles or engines to record and report specified information at the times and in the manner provided in the regulation;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (q) defining words and expressions used in this section that are not otherwise defined by this Act;

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations
paragraph: (r) classifying motor vehicles, engines, emission control systems and manufacturers for the purpose of a regulation and exempting such a class from a regulation.

heading: Motor vehicle and engine emission regulations

            Section 139 [regulations - general rules] applies for the purpose of making regulations under this section.

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph:
75
		  (1) Without limiting section 138 (1) [general authority to make regulations], the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of preventing or reducing pollution from new solid fuel burning domestic appliances including, without limitation, regulations for any of the following purposes:

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (a) regulating or imposing requirements or prohibitions in relation to the availability, sale, conditions of sale and lease of solid fuel burning domestic appliances for the purposes of preventing or reducing pollution;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing emission limits for solid fuel burning domestic appliances or classes of solid fuel burning domestic appliances for the purposes of preventing or reducing pollution;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (c) prescribing standards for and specifications of solid fuels burned in solid fuel burning domestic appliances for the purposes of preventing or reducing pollution;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (d) regulating and requiring the testing and certification of solid fuel burning domestic appliances;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (e) designating persons or organizations to test and certify solid fuel burning domestic appliances;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (f) prescribing the form and content of labels that may be placed on a solid fuel burning domestic appliance;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (g) providing for the manner of placing a prescribed label on a solid fuel burning domestic appliance that conforms to the prescribed standards of operation;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (h) prescribing fees and charges to be paid in respect of any matter for which the ministry provides a service or performs a duty in relation to solid fuel burning domestic appliances, and prescribing by whom the fees and charges are to be paid;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (i) exempting any solid fuel burning domestic appliance or class of solid fuel burning domestic appliance from any provision of this Act or the regulations;

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph: (j) providing for the recording and reporting of information by persons who manufacture, test, certify, offer for sale, sell, lease or otherwise dispose of solid fuel burning domestic appliances, including the frequency, time and manner for reporting.

heading: Solid fuel burning domestic appliance regulations
paragraph:

            Section 139 [regulations - general rules] applies for the purpose of making regulations under this section.

heading: Burning regulations
paragraph:
76
		  (1) Without limiting section 138 (1) [general authority to make regulations], the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing conditions that must be met and controls that must be provided for the burning of material derived from land clearing, land grading or tilling.

heading: Burning regulations
paragraph:

heading: Management of greenhouse gases at waste management facilities
paragraph:
76.2
		  The owner or operator of a waste management facility of a prescribed class must manage, in accordance with the regulations, specified greenhouse gases produced from wastes handled at the waste management facility.

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph:
76.21
		  (1) Without limiting section 138 (1) [general authority to make regulations], the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (a) specifying greenhouse gases for the purposes of this Division;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (b) prescribing actions that must be taken in relation to either or both of the following:

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (i)  the management or reduction of specified greenhouse gases;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (ii)  the recovery of energy potential from specified greenhouse gases;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (c) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions in relation to actions required under paragraph (b);

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (d) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions for the design, siting and operation of any works, activities or operations related to the management of, or the recovery of energy potential from, greenhouse gases;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (e) exempting any works, activities or operations or any class of persons, works, activities or operations from any or all of the provisions of the regulations in circumstances or on conditions that the Lieutenant Governor in Council prescribes;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (f) imposing monitoring and reporting requirements in relation to

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (i)  greenhouse gases or the recovery of energy potential from greenhouse gases,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (ii)  handling, treating, transporting, discharging or storing greenhouse gases or energy potential recovered from greenhouse gases, and

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (iii)  places and things that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers may be affected by the handling, treatment, transportation, discharge or storage of greenhouse gases or energy potential recovered from greenhouse gases,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: including, without limitation, prescribing requirements for the publication of information and respecting to whom reports are to be submitted and the timing, form, content, supporting evidence, verification, certification and manner of submission of the reports;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (g) establishing requirements respecting the retention of records that support reports and information required to be provided to the director under this Division;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Division 2
paragraph: (h) defining words or expressions used but not defined in this Division.

paragraph:
