              Section 139 [regulations - general rules] applies for the purpose of making regulations under this Division.

heading: This Part does not affect authority under other Parts
paragraph:
76.5
		  Nothing in this Part affects the authority to deal with greenhouse gases under any other Part of this Act.

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph:
77
		  (1) For the purpose of determining whether there are reasonable grounds for making a pollution prevention order under section 81 [pollution prevention orders] or a pollution abatement order under section 83 [pollution abatement orders], a director may order a person who is conducting an industry, trade or business to provide to the director the information described in subsection (2) that the director requests, whether or not

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (a) the industry, trade or business is prescribed for the purposes of section 6 (2) [waste disposal], or

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (b) an activity or operation of the industry, trade or business is prescribed for the purposes of section 6 (3) [waste disposal].

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) must be served on the person to whom it applies and may require the person to provide, at the person's own expense, information relating to

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (a) the operations or activities of the industry, trade or business, or

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (b) substances used, stored, treated or introduced or caused or allowed to be introduced into the environment in the course of the industry, trade or business.

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (3) Information required by an order under this section must be provided in the time and manner specified in the order.

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this section, "person" does not include a municipality.

heading: Minister may require environmental impact assessment
paragraph:
78
		  If the minister considers that

heading: Minister may require environmental impact assessment
paragraph: (a) something a person proposes to do will have a detrimental environmental impact, and

heading: Minister may require environmental impact assessment
paragraph: (b) the environmental impact cannot be assessed from information available to the minister,

heading: Minister may require environmental impact assessment
paragraph: the minister may require the person to provide an environmental impact assessment in respect of that thing, prepared in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph:
79
		  (1) In this section, "polluting substance" means any substance, whether gaseous, liquid or solid that, in the opinion of the minister, is capable of causing pollution if it were to

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (a) escape into the air,

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (b) be spilled onto any land or into any body of water, or

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (c) escape onto any land or into any body of water.

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (2) If a person has possession, charge or control of any polluting substance, the minister may, if the minister considers it reasonable and necessary to lessen the risk of an escape or spill of the substance, order that person

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (a) to undertake investigations, tests, surveys and any other action the minister considers necessary to determine the magnitude of the risk and to report the results to the minister,

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (b) to prepare, in accordance with the minister's directions, a contingency plan containing information the minister requires, and

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (c) to construct, alter or acquire, at the person's expense, any works, or carry out at the person's expense any measures that the minister considers reasonable and necessary to prevent or abate an escape or spill of the substance.

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (3) If an escape or spill occurs of a polluting substance for which a contingency plan was prepared, a director may order any person having possession, charge or control of the substance at the time it escaped or was spilled, or the person who prepared the plan or all of them to put the contingency plan into operation at their expense.

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (4) The minister may order a person who prepared a contingency plan to test the plan.

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (5) If a polluting substance escapes or is spilled or waste is introduced into the environment other than as allowed or authorized by

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph:
(a) 
                section 6 [waste disposal], or

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (b) a bylaw under section 31 [control of air contaminants in Greater Vancouver],

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: the person who had possession, charge or control of the substance or waste immediately before the escape, spill or introduction must, immediately after the person learns of the escape, spill or introduction, report the escape, spill or introduction in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (6) In a prosecution for a contravention of subsection (5), it is presumed that the accused knew of the escape, spill or introduction at the time of the alleged contravention and the burden of proving that the accused did not know is on the accused.

heading: Spill prevention and reporting
paragraph: (7) The minister may amend or cancel an order made under this section.

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph:
81
		  (1) If a director is satisfied on reasonable grounds that an activity or operation has been or is being performed by a person in a manner that is likely to release a substance that will cause pollution, the director may order a person referred to in subsection (2), at that person's expense, to do any of the following:

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (a) provide to the director information the director requests relating to the activity, operation or substance;

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (b) undertake investigations, tests, surveys or any other action the director considers necessary to prevent the pollution and report the results to the director;

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (c) acquire, construct or carry out any works or measures that are reasonably necessary to prevent the pollution;

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (d) adjust, repair or alter any works to the extent reasonably necessary to prevent the pollution.

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) may be served on one or more of the following persons:

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (a) a person who previously had or now has possession, charge or control of the substance;

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (b) a person who previously did anything, or who is now doing anything, which may cause the release of the substance;

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (c) a person who previously owned or occupied, or now owns or occupies, the land on which the substance is located.

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (3) An order made under subsection (1) may authorize a person or persons designated by the director to enter land for the purpose of preventing the pollution.

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (4) The powers of a director under this section may not be exercised in relation to any part of an activity or operation that is in compliance with the regulations or a permit, approval, order, waste management plan or operational certificate or an authorization made under the regulations.

heading: Pollution prevention orders
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of this section, "person" does not include a municipality.

heading: Preventing municipal pollution
paragraph:
82
		  If the minister is satisfied on reasonable grounds that an activity or operation has been or is being performed by a municipality in a manner that is likely to release a substance that will cause pollution of the environment, the minister may, with respect to the municipality, exercise the powers that a director may exercise under section 81 (1) [pollution prevention orders] in relation to other persons.

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph:
83
		  (1) If a director is satisfied on reasonable grounds that a substance is causing pollution, the director may order any of the following persons to do any of the things referred to in subsection (2):

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (a) a person who had possession, charge or control of the substance at the time it was introduced or escaped into the environment;

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (b) a person who owns or occupies the land on which the substance is located or on which the substance was located immediately before it was introduced into the environment;

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (c) a person who caused or authorized the pollution.

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) must be served on the person to whom it applies and may require that person, at that person's own expense, to do one or more of the following:

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (a) provide to the director information that the director requests relating to the pollution;

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (b) undertake investigations, tests, surveys and any other action the director considers necessary to determine the extent and effects of the pollution and to report the results to the director;

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (c) acquire, construct or carry out any works or measures that are reasonably necessary to control, abate or stop the pollution;

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (d) adjust, repair or alter any works to the extent reasonably necessary to control, abate or stop the pollution;

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (e) abate the pollution;

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (f) carry out remediation in accordance with any criteria established by the director.

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (3) An order under subsection (1) may authorize any persons designated by the director to enter land for the purpose of controlling, abating or stopping the pollution or to carry out remediation.

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (4) A director may amend or cancel an order made under this section.

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (5) The powers given by this section may be exercised even though the introduction of the substance into the environment is not prohibited under this Act or is authorized under this Act.

heading: Pollution abatement orders
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of this section, "person" does not include a municipality.

heading: Abatement of municipal pollution
paragraph:
84
		  If the minister considers that a municipality is causing pollution, the minister may, with respect to the municipality, exercise the powers that a director may exercise under section 83 [pollution abatement orders] in relation to other persons.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph:
85
		  (1) The minister may declare that an existing or proposed work, undertaking, product use or resource use has, or potentially has, a detrimental environmental impact.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (2) A declaration under subsection (1)

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (a) must be in writing,

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (b) must state the facts on which it is based,

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (c) is conclusive proof of those facts for the purposes of the declaration, and

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (d) is binding on all persons and courts.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (3) If a declaration has been made under subsection (1), the minister, after notifying the person affected, but without the necessity of holding a hearing, may make an interim order

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (a) restricting, modifying or prohibiting the operation of the work or undertaking or the use of the product or resource, or

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (b) requiring the person to do anything that the minister requires to be done in relation to the work or undertaking or the use of the product or resource

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: for a period not exceeding 15 days and in a manner specified in the order.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (4) The minister may not extend or renew an interim order.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (5) Whether or not an interim order has been made or has expired, if a declaration has been made under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council, after notifying the person affected, but without the necessity of holding a hearing, may make an order

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (a) restricting, modifying or prohibiting the operation of the work or undertaking or the use of the product or resource, or

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (b) requiring the person to do anything that the Lieutenant Governor in Council requires to be done in relation to the work or undertaking or the use of the product or resource

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: either permanently or for a specified period in a manner specified in the order.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (6) When an order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council under subsection (5) comes into force, an interim order in relation to the same subject matter expires.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (7) An order under subsection (3) or (5)

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (a) may not be made later than one year after the date of the minister's declaration under subsection (1), and

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (b) must state the reasons for making the order.

heading: Environmental protection orders
paragraph: (8) Despite any other enactment, a person to whom an order under subsection (3) or (5) is expressed to apply must comply with the order.

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph:
86
		  (1) If the minister has made a declaration under section 85 (1) [environmental protection orders] respecting a detrimental environmental impact, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may direct the minister to prepare an environmental management plan for the locality that is, or would be, impacted.

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph: (2) If an environmental management plan has been prepared under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph: (a) approve the plan with or without modification, and

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of implementing the plan, order that

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph: (i)  no licence, permit or power under an enactment may be issued or exercised in the locality, and

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph: (ii)  no waste may be discharged in the locality

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph: except as authorized by and in accordance with the order.

heading: Environmental management plan - in relation to environmental protection order
paragraph: (3) A licence or permit issued, or a power exercised, contrary to an order under subsection (2) (b) has no effect.

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph:
87
		  (1) In this section and section 88 [recovery of costs - environmental emergency], "environmental emergency" means an occurrence or natural disaster that affects the environment and includes the following:

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (a) a flood;

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (b) a landslide;

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (c) a spill or leakage of oil or of a poisonous or dangerous substance.

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (2) If the minister considers that

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (a) an environmental emergency exists, and

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (b) immediate action is necessary to prevent, lessen or control any hazard that the emergency presents,

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: the minister may make a declaration in writing that an environmental emergency under this section exists.

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (3) If the minister has made a declaration under subsection (2), the minister, or a public officer authorized by the minister in writing, may order any person to

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (a) provide labour, services, material, equipment or facilities, or

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (b) allow the use of land

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: for the purpose of preventing, lessening or controlling the hazard presented by the emergency,

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (4) If an order is made under subsection (3),

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (a) compensation for labour or services must be paid as the Lieutenant Governor in Council provides, and

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (b) compensation for material, equipment, facilities or the use of land, if not agreed on, must be set by arbitration under the Arbitration Act.

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (5) An order under subsection (3)

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (a) expires 15 days after it is made unless rescinded earlier under subsection (6), and

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (b) does not require any person to supply labour who is unfit to do so or is under the age of 19.

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (6) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may by order

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (a) confirm, modify or rescind an order under subsection (3), and

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (b) extend the term of an order under subsection (3) for a period the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers necessary.

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (7)               Subsection (6) (b) may not be applied to extend a requirement that a person supply labour.

heading: Environmental emergency measures
paragraph: (8) Despite any other enactment, a person affected by an order under subsection (3) or (6) must comply with the order.

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph:
88
		  (1) If the minister certifies that money is required for immediate response to an environmental emergency, the amount the minister certifies to be required may be paid out of the consolidated revenue fund without an appropriation other than this section.

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph: (2) A certificate signed by the minister and showing an amount of money expended by the government under this section is conclusive as to the amount expended.

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph: (3) An amount shown by a certificate referred to in subsection (2) is a debt due to the government and, subject to subsection (4), is recoverable, by action in the Supreme Court from any person whose act or omission caused or who authorized the events that caused the environmental emergency in proportions the court determines.

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph: (4) If the court is satisfied that the expenditure incurred by the government under this section was either

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph: (a) excessive, taking into consideration the magnitude of the emergency and the results achieved by the expenditure, or

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph: (b) unnecessary, taking into consideration the unlikelihood of significant material loss to any person had the government not acted under this section,

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph: the court may reduce or extinguish the amount of the judgment that it otherwise would have ordered be entered against the person against whom the action has been brought.

heading: Recovery of costs - environmental emergency
paragraph: (5) For the purpose of subsection (3), anything done or omitted by a person acting in the course of the person's employment is also the act or omission of the person's employer.

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph:
89
		  (1) If the minister considers it advisable for purposes of environmental management in an area, the minister may, by order,

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (a) designate the area for the purpose of developing an area based management plan for the area, and

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (b) establish a process for the development of the area based management plan for the designated area.

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) may, without limitation,

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (a) establish who is to be responsible for preparing the area based management plan,

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (b) establish the terms of reference for the plan or authorize the preparation of some or all of the terms of reference subject to the approval of the minister,

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (c) require the establishment of a technical advisory committee in relation to the development of the plan, and

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (d) require the participation in the development of the plan by specified licensees, permit holders or other persons the minister considers will be affected by the plan.

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (3) The terms of reference for an area based management plan must include

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (a) the purpose of the plan,

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (b) the issues to be addressed in the plan,

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (c) a process for public and stakeholder consultation,

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (d) if a management plan under another enactment is proposed or exists in relation to the same area, directions for coordination with persons responsible for that plan, and

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (e) a time limit for completing the plan.

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (4) Without limiting subsection (2) (b), the terms of reference for an area based management plan may include consideration of any of the following:

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (a) the impact of point and non point sources of waste;

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (b) cumulative impacts of point and non point sources of waste;

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (c) the economic and social costs and benefits of addressing risks to the environment through treatment;

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (d) environmental management objectives and outcomes for the area;

heading: Area based management plans - plan development
paragraph: (e) ongoing monitoring and reporting required to implement the plan.

heading: Approval and effect of area based management plan
paragraph:
90
		  (1) The minister may approve, with or without amendment, an area based management plan ordered under section 89 [area based management plans - plan development].

heading: Approval and effect of area based management plan
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of implementing an approved area based management plan, the minister, by order made applicable in relation to all or part of the designated area for the plan, may require that persons making decisions or classes of decisions under this Act consider the plan in making the decisions.

heading: Permits under area based management plan
paragraph:
90.1
		  (1) Despite section 14 [permits], if the introduction of waste into the environment is provided for under an area based management plan, the minister may, in writing, order a director to issue a permit under that section authorizing the introduction of waste

heading: Permits under area based management plan
paragraph: (a) within a specified time,

heading: Permits under area based management plan
paragraph: (b) in accordance with any requirements or conditions, under section 14 (1) (a) to (f), specified in the order, and

heading: Permits under area based management plan
paragraph: (c) subject to other requirements or conditions, under section 14 (1) (a) to (f), the director considers advisable for the protection of the environment.

heading: Permits under area based management plan
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3) and section 16 (2) [amendment of permits and approvals], the issuance of a permit under this section is final and binding and may not be appealed under Division 2 [Appeals from Decisions under this Act] of Part 8.

heading: Permits under area based management plan
paragraph: (3) Requirements or conditions the director considers advisable under subsection (1) (c) and amendments the director makes under section 16 (2) may be appealed under Division 2 of Part 8.

heading: Amendments to area based management plan
paragraph:
90.2
		  (1) If the minister considers it advisable for the purposes of environmental management, the minister may, by order, establish a process for the development of an amendment to an approved area based management plan.

heading: Amendments to area based management plan
paragraph: (2) Section 89 (2) and (3) [area based management plans - plan development] applies to an order to amend an area based management plan.

heading: Amendments to area based management plan
paragraph: (3) The minister may approve, with or without further amendment, an amendment to an area based management plan.

heading: Amendments to area based management plan
paragraph: (4) Upon approval of an amendment, the area based management plan is conclusively deemed, for all purposes, to be as modified by the amendment.

heading: Publication obligations
paragraph:
91
		  The minister must publish in the prescribed manner

heading: Publication obligations
paragraph: (a) on the making of an order under section 89 (1) [area based management plans - plan development], the order,

heading: Publication obligations
paragraph: (b) if an area based plan is approved under section 90 [approval and effect of area based management plan], the plan and any order under section 90 (2),

heading: Publication obligations
paragraph: (c) an order under section 90.1 (1) [permits under area based management plan],

heading: Publication obligations
paragraph: (d) an order under section 90.2 (1) [amendments to area based management plan], and

heading: Publication obligations
paragraph: (e) if an amendment is approved under section 90.2 (3), the amendment.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
91.1
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "area response plan" means a plan referred to in section 91.51 (1) [area response plans];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "conditional PRO" means a preparedness and response organization that holds a conditional PRO certificate;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "conditional PRO certificate" means a certificate issued under section 91.41 (1) [preparedness and response organizations];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environment" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) flora and fauna, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for certainty, animal, fish and plant habitat;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "first nation government" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the governing body of a band, as defined in the Indian Act (Canada),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a treaty first nation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a Nisga'a Government, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the council of the shishalh Nation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "geographic response area" means the area designated under section 91.31 (2) [geographic response plans] for a geographic response plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "geographic response plan" means a plan referred to in section 91.31 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "infrastructure" includes buildings, bridges, drinking water intakes, utility conduits and wastewater treatment plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local government" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the council of a municipality,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the board of a regional district,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a local trust committee, or the trust council, as defined in section 1 of the Islands Trust Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a greater board, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) an improvement district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "preparedness and response organization" means an organization that provides or intends to provide spill preparedness and response services in British Columbia;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "PRO" means a preparedness and response organization that holds a PRO certificate;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "PRO certificate" means a certificate issued under section 91.41 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regulated person" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person who, in the course of operating an industry, trade or business, has possession, charge or control of a prescribed substance in prescribed quantities, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person referred to in paragraph (a) whose employee, under the person's direction, has possession, charge or control of a prescribed substance in prescribed quantities;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "responsible person" means a person who has possession, charge or control of a substance or thing when a spill of the substance or thing occurs or is at imminent risk of occurring;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "spill" means the introduction into the environment, other than as authorized under this Act and whether intentional or unintentional, of a substance or thing that has the potential to cause adverse effects to the environment, human health or infrastructure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "spill contingency plan" means a plan described in section 91.11 (1).

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: 91.11		  (1) A regulated person must ensure that

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (a) on or before the prescribed date, the regulated person has a spill contingency plan that complies with the regulations,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (b) the spill contingency plan is reviewed, updated and tested in the prescribed manner and at the prescribed frequency,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (c) the spill contingency plan is made available to employees of the regulated person in accordance with the regulations,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (d) the spill contingency plan demonstrates that the regulated person has the capability to effectively respond to a spill, and

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (e) if required by the regulations, the spill contingency plan is published in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (2) Before a spill contingency plan is prepared in relation to a regulated person, the regulated person must ensure that investigations, tests and surveys are undertaken in accordance with the regulations, if any, that are necessary to determine the magnitude of the risk to

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (a) the environment and human health, and

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (b) infrastructure

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: that would result from a spill of the substance in respect of which the person is a regulated person.

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (3) A regulated person must ensure that, in accordance with the regulations,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (a) records respecting investigations, tests and surveys referred to in subsection (2) are prepared and kept for the prescribed period,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (b) prescribed reports are prepared and submitted to a director,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (c) employees of the regulated person receive prescribed training to prescribed standards, and

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (d) employees of the regulated person engage in spill response training exercises and drills in the prescribed manner and at the prescribed frequency.

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (4) A regulated person must ensure that, if a spill occurs, a spill contingency plan is implemented to the extent the plan is applicable.

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (5) If ordered by a director, a regulated person must provide to the director, at the regulated person's own expense and in the time and manner specified by the director,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (a) a copy of the regulated person's spill contingency plan,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (b) information relating to

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (i)  the operations or activities of the industry, trade or business, or

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (ii)  substances used, stored, treated, produced or transported by the regulated person,

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (c) prescribed declarations in respect of spill preparedness and response capability, and

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (d) prescribed information.

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (6) A director who requests a copy of a spill contingency plan may order that the spill contingency plan be amended in accordance with the director's directions and resubmitted in the time specified by the director, if the director is satisfied that the spill contingency plan does not comply with this Act or the regulations.

heading: Regulated persons - spill contingency planning
paragraph: (7) A director may order a regulated person to test the efficacy of the regulated person's spill contingency plan in the time and manner specified by the director.

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph:
91.2
		  (1) A responsible person in relation to a spill must, in accordance with the regulations,

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (a) report the prescribed information about the spill to the prescribed persons in the prescribed time and manner,

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (b) provide any information to an officer that the officer requests respecting response activities in relation to the spill, and

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (c) ensure that persons with the skills, experience, resources and equipment necessary to properly deal with the spill

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (i)  arrive at the spill site, sites affected by the spill and prescribed sites associated with the spill within the prescribed period after the spill, and

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (ii)  implement an incident command system in the prescribed time and manner.

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, if a spill occurs or is at imminent risk of occurring, the responsible person in relation to the spill must ensure that the actions necessary to address the threat or hazard caused by the spill are taken, which actions may include, but are not limited to, the following actions, if applicable:

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (a) assess, monitor and prevent, or prevent the continuation of, the threat or hazard caused by the spill;

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (b) stabilize, contain, remove and clean up the spill;

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (c) identify and evaluate the immediate risks to and impacts on the environment, human health or infrastructure and, as necessary,

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (i)  advise persons to take protective action in relation to the spill,

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (ii)  protect infrastructure, and

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (iii)  protect, recover and restore the environment;

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (d) identify and evaluate the long term impacts of the spill;

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (e) take steps to resolve or mitigate those immediate and long term impacts.

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (3) If a director is satisfied on reasonable grounds that compliance with the regulations is not sufficient to fully deal with the adverse effects of a spill on the environment, human health or infrastructure, the director may order the responsible person to take specified spill response actions that the director considers are necessary or advisable in addition to the regulatory requirements.

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (4) A director may order a responsible person in relation to a spill to prepare, in accordance with the regulations, and submit to the director, in the time and manner specified by the director, a recovery plan, or an amended recovery plan, to resolve or mitigate the impacts of the spill.

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (5) The director may

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (a) approve, by order, a recovery plan submitted under subsection (4), or

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (b) direct that the recovery plan be amended in accordance with the director's directions and resubmitted in the time and manner specified by the director.

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (6) A responsible person must ensure that

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (a) an approved recovery plan is carried out by a person the director is satisfied has

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (i)  the qualifications necessary to properly carry out the plan, and

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (ii)  access to personnel with the necessary skills and training,

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (b) an approved recovery plan is carried out by the date specified by the director, and

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (c) at the conclusion of the recovery process, in accordance with the regulations, a report is prepared and submitted to the director.

heading: Responsible persons - spill response
paragraph: (7) Section 91.4 (8) and (9) (a) [government spill response] applies to a director in relation to the exercise of the director's powers and performance of the director's duties under this section.

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph:
91.21
		  (1) This section applies

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (a) if a director is satisfied that

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (i)  the impacts of a spill on the environment cannot be restored, or cannot be completely restored, at sites affected by the spill,

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (ii)  the impacts of a spill on the environment cannot reasonably be restored, or cannot reasonably be completely restored, because the following would not be commensurate with the result of restoration or complete restoration activities:

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (A) damage to the environment or human health;

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (B) the costs of the restoration activities, or

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (iii)  it is not safe to undertake restoration activities at sites affected by the spill, or

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (b) in prescribed circumstances.

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (2) In the circumstances described in subsection (1), the director may order that the recovery plan for the spill provide for

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (a) mitigation measures, to be taken elsewhere, that compensate, or partially compensate, for the type of damage caused by the spill, or

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (b) payment by the responsible person, to a person specified by the director, of an amount the director considers equivalent to the amount the responsible person would have been liable to if restoration or complete restoration were reasonably or safely achievable.

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (3) A director may specify a person for the purposes of subsection (2) (b) only if the director is satisfied that

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (a) the person operates on a predominately not-for-profit basis and has purposes restricted to

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (i)  the conservation or enhancement of biological diversity, fish, fish habitat, wildlife or wildlife habitat, or

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (ii)  a prescribed purpose, and

heading: When restoration not reasonably achievable
paragraph: (b) the person will apply the funds to a project that will, in whole or in part, compensate for the damage caused by the spill.

heading: Certificate of recovery
paragraph:
91.3
		  If a director is satisfied on the basis of a report under section 91.2 (6) (c) [responsible persons - spill response] that an approved recovery plan has been carried out, the director may issue to the responsible person a certificate to that effect.

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph:
91.31
		  (1) For the purposes of this section, "plan leaders" means the regulated persons ordered under subsection (3) to prepare a geographic response plan.

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (2) The minister, by order, may designate an area for the purpose of the development of a geographic response plan applicable throughout the area

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (a) if the minister considers that a geographic response plan will assist

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (i)  in minimizing the effects of a spill on a body of water, a sensitive ecosystem or a culturally sensitive or archaeologically, socially, economically or historically significant site in the area, or

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (ii)  in increasing the efficiency of spill response in the area, or

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (b) in prescribed circumstances.

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (3) In an order under subsection (2), the minister may order the regulated persons who carry on an industry, trade or business, or related activities, in the geographic response area, or a class of those regulated persons, to prepare, or to review, update and test, a geographic response plan in accordance with the minister's order and the regulations.

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (4) An order under subsection (2) must establish the terms of reference for the geographic response plan, or authorize the preparation of some or all of the terms of reference subject to the approval of the minister, which terms of reference must include, but are not limited to,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (a) the matters to be addressed in the proposed geographic response plan, which matters may include, but are not limited to,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (i)  locations of bodies of water, sensitive ecosystems, culturally sensitive or archeologically, socially, economically or historically significant sites in the area,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (ii)  locations of potential response staging sites,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (iii)  locations and profiles of the biological and other resources that could be affected by a spill, including, without limitation,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (A) threatened and endangered species,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (B) important or unique animal, fish or plant habitat,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (C) areas of human habitation and recreational activities, and

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (D) water and agricultural resources,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (iv)  locations of key infrastructure,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (v)  tactics for addressing spills and impacts of spills in the area, including, without limitation, collection techniques, and

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (vi)  prescribed matters,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (b) a time limit for completing the proposed plan, and

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (c) any other prescribed information.

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (5) An order under subsection (2) may, subject to the regulations,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (a) require the establishment of an advisory committee in relation to the development, review, testing and updating of the geographic response plan and the reimbursement of the members of the committee for reasonable travelling and out-of-pocket expenses necessarily incurred in carrying out their duties,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (b) specify persons and organizations or classes of persons or organizations whose input must be invited and considered,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (c) require the plan leaders to carry out a public consultation in accordance with the regulations, and

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (d) specify persons or organizations or classes of persons or organizations who are responsible for paying the reasonable costs of developing, reviewing, testing and updating the geographic response plan.

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (6) A geographic response plan must

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (a) be in the prescribed form,

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (b) contain provisions respecting the prescribed matters, and

heading: Geographic response plans
paragraph: (c) be published in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph:
91.4
		  (1) The government may carry out actions described in section 91.2 (2) [responsible persons - spill response] if an officer considers that

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (a) a spill has occurred or there is an imminent risk of a spill occurring,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (b) action is necessary to address a spill or the risk of a spill or to resolve or mitigate long term effects of a spill, and

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (c) one or more of the following apply:

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (i)  there is no responsible person in relation to the spill;

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (ii)  an officer has reasonable grounds to believe that government action is required to safeguard the environment, human health or infrastructure;

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (iii)  the responsible person in relation to the spill requests that the government assist with spill response and recovery actions.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (2) In addition to actions under section 91.2 (2), if a director considers it necessary or desirable in the event of a spill, the government may take actions in relation to any of the following:

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (a) any aspect of the management of the spill and its effects;

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (b) impacts of the spill on public property, public amenities or areas to which the public has access;

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (c) impacts of the spill on private property;

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (d) impacts of the spill on any part of the environment.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (3) Subject to the regulations, the costs incurred by the government under this Division in relation to a spill are a debt due to the government by the responsible person and the owner of the substance or thing spilled.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (4) The costs referred to in subsection (3) include all of the government's costs in relation to the spill, including, without limitation,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (a) for

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (i)  the use of government employees or contractors in the response, including hourly rates and expenses, including food, accommodation and mileage,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (ii)  the use of government vehicles, including mileage,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (iii)  the use of consulting and other professional services,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (iv)  the use, maintenance and repair of government equipment,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (v)  private goods and services contracted, hired, rented or purchased,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (vi)  research and analytical services related to recovery actions, and

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (vii)  mitigating the effects of the spill on the public, and

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (b) a prescribed percentage of those costs the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers is sufficient to meet the government's administrative costs.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (5) The responsible person and owner referred to in subsection (3) are jointly and separately liable for amounts described in that subsection.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (6) For the purpose of recovering costs referred to in subsection (3), a director may file a certificate with a court that has jurisdiction, and, upon filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed against the persons named, and in the amount set out, in that certificate.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (7) A certificate under subsection (6) may be in the prescribed form, must be signed by a director and must contain

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (a) the name of the responsible person in relation to the spill and the owner of the substance or thing that was spilled,

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (b) the date and place of the spill to which the certificate relates, and

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (c) the costs referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (8) No legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against the government, an employee of the government or a person acting on behalf of or under the direction of the government because of anything done or omitted

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (a) in the performance or intended performance of any duty under this section in relation to a spill, or

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (b) in the exercise or intended exercise of any power under this section in relation to a spill.

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (9) Subsection (8) does not apply to

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (a) a person referred to in that subsection in relation to anything done or omitted by that person in bad faith, or

heading: Government spill response
paragraph: (b) a responsible person, whether or not the responsible person is acting under the direction of the government.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph:
91.41
		  (1) On application in accordance with the directions of the minister and the regulations, if any, the minister may issue a conditional PRO certificate to a preparedness and response organization that demonstrates to the minister's satisfaction that the organization has the capacity to be fully capable and intends to be fully capable, within the period and the area specified by the minister, to

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (a) promptly and capably deal with spills and the impacts of spills within that area, including having access to the necessary equipment, personnel and other resources, and

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (b) perform prescribed duties given under this Part to a regulated person or a PRO.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (2) On application by a conditional PRO or on the minister's own initiative, the minister may, if the minister is satisfied that the conditional PRO is fully capable as described in subsection (1), issue a PRO certificate to the conditional PRO or, on the minister's own initiative, the minister may, at the expiry of a conditional PRO certificate, revoke the conditional PRO certificate.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (3) A conditional PRO certificate and a PRO certificate

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (a) must contain the prescribed terms and conditions, if any, and

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (b) may contain the terms and conditions the minister considers necessary or advisable.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (4) A conditional PRO and a PRO must comply with the terms and conditions of the conditional PRO certificate or the PRO certificate, as applicable.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (5) To ensure that a conditional PRO or PRO, as applicable, becomes or remains, as applicable, fully capable as described in subsection (1) (a) and (b), the minister may amend, as the minister considers necessary or advisable for that purpose, the terms and conditions of

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (a) a conditional PRO certificate, including by extending the period specified in the conditional PRO certificate if the minister is satisfied that the conditional PRO has the capacity to be capable as described in subsection (1) by the end of the extension, or

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (b) a PRO certificate.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (6) An application under subsection (1) must include, for the approval of the minister,

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (a) a business plan that demonstrates that the organization has the capacity to be fully capable as described in subsection (1) within the period specified under that subsection,

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (b) prescribed information and records, if any, and

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (c) any other information or records the minister requests.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (7) To be eligible for a PRO certificate, a conditional PRO must provide all of the following:

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (a) an area response plan, prepared by the conditional PRO, that demonstrates to the satisfaction of the minister that the conditional PRO, in accordance with the regulations,

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (i)  consulted any person who would have an interest in the event of a spill in the specified area, and

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (ii)  enabled the participation of persons referred to subparagraph (i) in the development of the area response plan, including, in the case of local governments and first nation governments, providing reimbursement of reasonable travelling and out-of-pocket expenses necessarily incurred as a result of that participation;

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (b) prescribed information and records, if any;

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (c) any other information or records the minister requests.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (8) It is a term of a PRO certificate that the PRO must establish, and include in its arrangements with regulated persons, a procedure for dealing with complaints made to the PRO by those regulated persons, in respect of the fees and other amounts charged by the PRO.

heading: Preparedness and response organizations
paragraph: (9) Subject to the regulations, if the minister is satisfied that a conditional PRO or a PRO is not complying with the terms and conditions of the conditional PRO certificate or PRO certificate, as applicable, the minister may cancel the certificate.

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph:
91.5
		  (1) A person who is required under the regulations to use the services of a PRO and who has a complaint about the fees or other charges the PRO is imposing for those services may, on payment of the prescribed fee for filing a complaint, if any, file a complaint with the minister.

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (2) On receiving a complaint under subsection (1), the minister may, by order,

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (a) dismiss the complaint, or

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (b) after hearing from the PRO and the complainant in any manner the minister considers appropriate,

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (i)  dismiss the complaint,

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (ii)  order the PRO to adjust its fees,

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (iii)  waive a fee payable by the complainant to the PRO, or

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (iv)  prohibit the fee being imposed on any person.

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (3) After exercising authority under subsection (2) in relation to a complaint, the minister may, by order, award costs to the PRO or the complainant in the amount the minister considers appropriate.

heading: Complaint to minister respecting fees
paragraph: (4) A person in whose favour an order is made under subsection (3) may file the order with a court that has jurisdiction and, upon filing, that order has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed against the person named, and in the amount set out, in the order.

heading: Area response plans
paragraph:
91.51
		  (1) A conditional PRO that wishes to be certified as a PRO must prepare, and publish, in accordance with the regulations and in the time specified by the minister, a response plan for the area designated in its conditional PRO certificate.

heading: Area response plans
paragraph: (2) A PRO, in accordance with the regulations, must review, update, test and republish an area response plan prepared under subsection (1).

heading: Area response plans
paragraph: (3) Subject to the regulations, an area response plan must include information respecting spill response procedures and strategies, including, without limitation,

heading: Area response plans
paragraph: (a) available equipment and other resources,

heading: Area response plans
paragraph: (b) where the equipment and resources can be obtained,

heading: Area response plans
paragraph: (c) other logistical information, and

heading: Area response plans
paragraph: (d) prescribed information respecting prescribed matters.

heading: Area response plans

heading: Right of entry to respond to spill
paragraph:
91.6
		  The government, and any person directed by the government, may carry out spill response actions anywhere and, without limiting this, may enter on private property for the purpose of carrying out those actions.

heading: Minister's advisory committee respecting spill response
paragraph:
91.61
		  (1) The minister may establish an advisory committee, consisting of individuals appointed by the minister, to provide advice and recommendations to the minister on any aspect of spill preparedness, response or recovery under this Division.

heading: Minister's advisory committee respecting spill response
paragraph: (2) The minister may appoint to a minister's advisory committee any individual whose advice or recommendations the minister considers desirable, including, without limitation,

heading: Minister's advisory committee respecting spill response
paragraph: (a) representatives of local governments,

heading: Minister's advisory committee respecting spill response
paragraph: (b) representatives of first nation governments, and

heading: Minister's advisory committee respecting spill response
paragraph: (c) individuals with technical expertise in relation to spill preparedness, response or recovery.

heading: Minister's advisory committee respecting spill response
paragraph: (3) An individual appointed to a minister's advisory committee must be reimbursed, in accordance with the general directives of Treasury Board, for reasonable travelling and out-of-pocket expenses necessarily incurred in carrying out the individual's duties.

heading: Report to the Legislative Assembly
paragraph:
91.7
		  At the prescribed frequency, the minister must lay before the Legislative Assembly a report respecting the administration and operation of this Division, and the effectiveness of the spill response scheme under this Division, for the period beginning, as applicable,

heading: Report to the Legislative Assembly
paragraph: (a) on the date this section comes into force, or

heading: Report to the Legislative Assembly
paragraph: (b) on the date the last report under this section is laid before the Legislative Assembly.

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph:
91.71
		  (1) A person who, in the course of operating an industry, trade or business, has possession, charge or control of a substance, other than a substance prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "regulated person" in section 91.1, that a director has reasonable grounds to believe may, if spilled, cause adverse effects on the environment, human health or infrastructure must, on request of the director, provide the following within the time specified by the director:

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (a) information respecting the substance and its properties;

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (b) information respecting the potential adverse effects that would be caused to the environment, human health or infrastructure were the substance spilled;

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (c) information respecting the quantities of the substance of which the person has, or intends to have, possession, charge or control;

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (d) prescribed information.

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (2) A person who, in the course of operating an industry, trade or business, has possession, charge or control of a substance prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "regulated person" in section 91.1 must, on request of a director, provide information, within the time specified by the director, respecting the quantities of the substance of which the person has, or intends to have, possession, charge or control.

heading: Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph:
93
		  (1) The Environmental Appeal Board is continued to hear appeals that under the provisions of any enactment are to be heard by the appeal board.

heading: Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (2) In relation to an appeal under another enactment, the appeal board has the powers given to it by that other enactment.

heading: Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (3) The appeal board consists of the following individuals appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council after a merit-based process:

heading: Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (a) a member designated as the chair;

heading: Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (b) one or more members designated as vice chairs after consultation with the chair;

heading: Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (c) other members appointed after consultation with the chair.

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph:
93.1
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), for the purposes of an appeal, the following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the appeal board:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a) Part 1 [Interpretation and Application];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b) Part 2 [Appointments];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (c) Part 3 [Clustering];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a) the appeal board has given the person or body the right to appear before it;

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b) the person or body does not have full party status.

heading: Parties and witnesses
paragraph: 94		  (1) In an appeal, the appeal board or panel

heading: Parties and witnesses
paragraph: (a) may hear the evidence of any person, including a person the appeal board or a panel invites to appear before it, and

heading: Parties and witnesses
paragraph: (b) on request of

heading: Parties and witnesses
paragraph: (i)  the person,

heading: Parties and witnesses
paragraph: (ii)  a member of the body, or

heading: Parties and witnesses
paragraph: (iii)  a representative of the person or body,

heading: Parties and witnesses
paragraph: whose decision is the subject of the appeal or review, must give that person or body full party status.

heading: Decision of appeal board
paragraph:
96
		  If the appeal board or a panel makes an order or decision with respect to an appeal the chair must send a copy of the order or decision to the minister and to the parties.

heading: Varying and rescinding orders of appeal board
paragraph:
97
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, in the public interest, vary or rescind an order or decision of the appeal board.

heading: Appeal board power to enter property
paragraph:
98
		  The members of the appeal board have, for the purposes of an appeal, the right to enter any property except a private residence.

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph:
99
		  For the purpose of this Division, "decision" means

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph: (a) making an order,

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph: (b) imposing a requirement,

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph: (c) exercising a power except a power of delegation,

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph: (d) issuing, amending, renewing, suspending, refusing, cancelling or refusing to amend a permit, approval or operational certificate,

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph: (e) including a requirement or a condition in an order, permit, approval or operational certificate,

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph: (f) determining to impose an administrative penalty, and

heading: Definition of "decision"
paragraph: (g) determining that the terms and conditions of an agreement under section 115 (4) [administrative penalties] have not been performed.

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph:
100
		  (1) A person aggrieved by a decision of a director or a district director may appeal the decision to the appeal board in accordance with this Division.

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (2) For certainty, a decision under this Act of the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the minister is not appealable to the appeal board.

heading: Time limit for commencing appeal
paragraph:
101
		  The time limit for commencing an appeal of a decision is 30 days after notice of the decision is given.

heading: Procedure on appeals
paragraph:
102
		  (1) Division 1 [Environmental Appeal Board] of this Part applies to an appeal under this Division.

heading: Procedure on appeals
paragraph: (2) The appeal board may conduct an appeal under this Division by way of a new hearing.

heading: Powers of appeal board in deciding appeal
paragraph:
103
		  On an appeal under this Division, the appeal board may

heading: Powers of appeal board in deciding appeal
paragraph: (a) send the matter back to the person who made the decision, with directions,

heading: Powers of appeal board in deciding appeal
paragraph: (b) confirm, reverse or vary the decision being appealed, or

heading: Powers of appeal board in deciding appeal
paragraph: (c) make any decision that the person whose decision is appealed could have made, and that the appeal board considers appropriate in the circumstances.

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph:
106
		  (1) The Conservation Officer Service is continued.

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (2) The Conservation Officer Service consists of

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (a) a person employed in the ministry who is appointed by the minister as the chief conservation officer, and

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (b) the persons designated under subsection (3) (b) (i).

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (3) Subject to the direction of the minister,

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (a) the chief conservation officer has general supervision over the Conservation Officer Service, and

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (b) the chief conservation officer, or a member of the Conservation Officer Service designated by the chief conservation officer for the purpose, may do all the following:

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (i)  designate persons employed in the ministry, each of whom the chief conservation officer considers suitable, as members of the Conservation Officer Service;

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (ii)  designate persons, or a class of persons, employed in the ministry as auxiliary conservation officers;

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (iii)  designate persons, or a class of persons, as special conservation officers;

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (iv)  impose and confer on an auxiliary or a special conservation officer, or on a class of auxiliary or special conservation officers, any of the duties imposed and powers conferred on a member of the Conservation Officer Service under this Act or another enactment;

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (v)  establish standards and procedures, including, but not limited to, establishing training and retraining standards and specifying operational procedures for the efficient discharge of duties and functions by the Conservation Officer Service and its members;

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (vi)  specify equipment, including, but not limited to, uniform apparel, vehicles and firearms to be used by members of the Conservation Officer Service;

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (vii)  establish rules for the prevention of neglect and abuse by members of the Conservation Officer Service.

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (4) An auxiliary or a special conservation officer may perform and exercise the duties and powers imposed and conferred on the officer under subsection (3) (b) (iv).

heading: Conservation Officer Service
paragraph: (5) Members of the Conservation Officer Service

paragraph: (a) may exercise the powers and perform the duties of a conservation officer under this Act or any other enactment,

heading: Conservation Officer Service

paragraph: (i)  exercising the powers and performing the duties of a conservation officer under this Act or another enactment,

heading: Powers and duties of conservation officers

heading: Powers and duties of conservation officers
paragraph: (ii)  a prescribed official under a prescribed enactment, and

heading: Definition
paragraph:
107.01
		  In this Division, "designated enactment" means an enactment referred to in section 106 (5) (b).

heading: Search warrant
paragraph:
107.02
		  (1) On information on oath that there are reasonable grounds to believe that an offence under a designated enactment has occurred or is occurring, a justice, on being satisfied that an entry and a search are likely to provide evidence of such an offence, may issue a warrant authorizing a conservation officer

heading: Search warrant
paragraph: (a) to enter and search the real or personal property specified in the warrant,

heading: Search warrant
paragraph: (b) to seize and remove anything that the conservation officer has reasonable grounds for believing is evidence of an offence, and

heading: Search warrant
paragraph: (c) to take other actions as the justice considers appropriate in the circumstances and authorizes in the warrant.

heading: Search warrant
paragraph: (2) A conservation officer who enters on property in accordance with a warrant issued under subsection (1) may bring persons and equipment that may be necessary for the purpose of the warrant.

heading: Warrantless search in exigent circumstances
paragraph:
107.03
		  (1) This section applies despite section 107.02.

heading: Warrantless search in exigent circumstances
paragraph: (2) If the conditions necessary for obtaining a warrant under section 107.02 exist but the delay necessary to obtain the warrant would result in a danger to human life or safety, a member of the Conservation Officer Service may, without a warrant,

heading: Warrantless search in exigent circumstances
paragraph: (a) search real or personal property, including premises or a part of premises occupied solely as a private residence, and

heading: Warrantless search in exigent circumstances
paragraph: (b) seize and remove anything that the member has reasonable or probable grounds for believing may provide evidence of the commission of an offence under a designated enactment.

heading: Warrantless search in exigent circumstances
paragraph: (3) If the conditions necessary for obtaining a warrant under section 107.02 exist but the delay necessary to obtain the warrant would result in the loss or destruction of evidence, a member of the Conservation Officer Service may, without a warrant,

heading: Warrantless search in exigent circumstances
paragraph: (a) search real or personal property, except premises or a part of premises occupied solely as a private residence, and

heading: Warrantless search in exigent circumstances
paragraph: (b) seize and remove anything that the member has reasonable or probable grounds for believing may provide evidence of the commission of an offence under a designated enactment.

heading: Inspection of records and warrant to seize records
paragraph:
107.04
		  (1) A person required by a designated enactment to keep records must submit the records to a conservation officer for inspection on request.

heading: Inspection of records and warrant to seize records
paragraph: (2) If a person refuses to submit records for inspection as required under this section, a justice, on being satisfied that an inspection of the records is necessary for the administration of the enactment that requires them to be kept, may issue a warrant authorizing a conservation officer to enter property specified in the warrant and to seize the records.

heading: Inspection of records and warrant to seize records
paragraph: (3) A conservation officer who enters on property in accordance with a warrant issued under subsection (2) may bring persons and equipment that may be necessary for the purpose of the warrant.

paragraph:

heading: Application of Offence Act in relation to sections 107.02 and 107.03 and to inspections
paragraph: (2) If, under section 24 (2) (a) of the Offence Act, a justice orders that something referred to in subsection (1) of this section be detained, despite section 24 (3) of the Offence Act, the thing may be detained for up to one year before an order under section 24 (5) of that Act, authorizing its continued detention, is required.

paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2) or anything to the contrary in the enactment authorizing the inspection, if the chief conservation officer, or a member of the Conservation Officer Service designated by the chief conservation officer for the purpose, considers anything seized in a search under section 107.02 or 107.03 or in an inspection under a designated enactment
