heading: Inspections
paragraph: 109		  (1) For the purposes of ensuring compliance with this Act and the regulations, an officer may enter land or premises, except premises or a part of premises occupied solely as a private residence, at any reasonable time and inspect any process, works or activity that

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) produces or is capable of producing waste,

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) causes or is capable of causing pollution, or

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) is used for the storage, handling, treatment, destruction or disposal of waste.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (2) An officer may exercise powers under this section in respect of premises or a part of premises occupied solely as a private residence only

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) with the consent of the occupant, or

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) under the authority of a warrant under subsection (3) or another enactment.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (3) If satisfied by evidence on oath that access to premises or a part of premises occupied solely as a private residence is necessary for the purposes of this Act, a justice may issue a warrant authorizing a person named in the warrant to enter the premises and conduct an inspection.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (4) An officer who enters on land or premises under subsection (1), with consent under subsection (2) or under a warrant under subsection (3), may do any of the following:

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) inspect, analyze, measure, sample or test land, and any article, substance or waste located on or in the land, and premises to ascertain

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (i)  whether pollution is present,

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (ii)  the quantity of waste produced, treated, stored, handled, transported or discharged, or

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (iii)  the characteristics of waste produced, treated, stored, handled, transported or discharged;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) take away samples of land, articles, substances or waste;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) examine and take away copies of records relating to

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (i)  the production, treatment, storage, handling, transportation and discharge of waste, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (ii)  the characteristics of the waste produced, treated, stored, handled, transported or discharged;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (d) require that anything related to the production, treatment, storage, handling, transportation or discharge of waste be operated, used or set in motion under conditions specified by the officer;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (e) use a computer system at the place that is being inspected to examine data, contained in or available to the computer system, related to the production, treatment, storage, handling, transportation or discharge of waste;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (f) record or copy by any method any information related to the production, treatment, storage, handling, transportation or discharge of waste;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (g) use any machine, structure, material or equipment in the place that is being inspected as is necessary to carry out the inspection;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (h) use copying equipment located at the place that is being inspected to make copies to take away;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (i) take photographs or make audio or video records.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (5) An officer who enters land or premises in accordance with this section

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) may take with the officer the persons and equipment that may be necessary for the purposes of the inspection, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) on request, must provide proof of identity to a person present on the land or premises entered.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (6) A person who is or was a director, receiver, receiver manager, officer, employee, banker, auditor or agent of a person who is the subject of an inspection under this section must, on request of the inspecting officer,

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) produce, without charge or unreasonable delay, for examination by the inspecting officer

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (i)  any approval, licence, order, permit or waste management plan related to waste produced, treated, stored, handled, transported or discharged on or from the land or premises, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (ii)  any other record that touches on any matter relating to the production, treatment, storage, handling, transport or discharge of waste on or from the land or premises, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) provide the inspecting officer with information relevant to the purposes of the inspection.

heading: Minister may enter on private land
paragraph:
110
		  The minister and other persons the minister designates in writing have for the purposes of this Act the right to enter any property except premises or a part of premises occupied solely as a private residence.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
111
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: "officer" includes a peace officer as defined in the Motor Vehicle Act;

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: "vehicle" includes a vehicle as defined in the Motor Vehicle Act, an off-road vehicle as defined in the Off-Road Vehicle Act, a rail vehicle as defined in the Transport of Dangerous Goods Act and a vessel.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of ensuring compliance with this Act or the regulations, including with a permit, licence, order, waste management plan or approval, if an officer has reasonable grounds for believing that a vehicle is being used for the transportation or handling of waste, the officer may, at any reasonable time,

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (a) require a person operating the vehicle to stop the vehicle and provide identification, and

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (b) carry out an inspection in accordance with this section.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (2.1) When requested or signalled to do so by an officer who is readily identifiable as a conservation officer, or as a peace officer as defined in the Motor Vehicle Act, the operator of a motor vehicle must immediately

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (a) stop the vehicle, and

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (b) provide identification and the information that the officer or peace officer considers necessary to determine whether this Act and the regulations are being complied with.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (2.2) For the purposes of carrying out an inspection under this section, an officer may

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (a) require that any compartment of the vehicle or any container in or on the vehicle be opened, and

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (b) exercise any of the powers under section 109 (4) [inspections].

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (3) If, as a result of an inspection or a test carried out under this section, it appears to the officer that the vehicle is transporting hazardous waste in a manner that creates a risk of harm to the public or the environment, the officer may require the driver to drive the vehicle to a place the officer specifies and the officer may do one or more of the following:

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (a) order one or more of the following persons to deal with the hazardous waste in accordance with the officer's directions:

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (i)  the owner of the hazardous waste;

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (ii)  the person operating the vehicle;

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (iii)  the owner of the vehicle;

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (b) seize and, in accordance with the regulations, dispose of

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (i)  the hazardous waste, and

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (ii)  any package or container holding the hazardous waste;

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (c) detain the vehicle for any period that the officer considers necessary in order to exercise the officer's powers under paragraphs (a) and  (b).

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (4) The owner of the hazardous waste, package or container and the owner of the vehicle that was transporting the hazardous waste, package or container are jointly and separately liable to the government for the cost of disposing of the hazardous waste, package or container under subsection (3) (b), and that cost is recoverable from them by the government as a simple contract debt.

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: 112		  (1) If an officer concludes in the course of an inspection under this Act that the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has contravened or is contravening this Act or the regulations, the officer may

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (a) order a person to do anything the officer considers necessary to stop the contravention or prevent another contravention, and

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (b) seize anything validly inspected by the officer that the officer believes on reasonable grounds

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (i)  was used or is being used in the contravention, or

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (ii)  will afford evidence of the contravention.

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (2) Sections 23 (4) and 24 to 24.2 of the Offence Act apply in respect of anything seized under subsection (1) of this section and, for the purposes of section 23 (4) of the Offence Act, an officer is deemed to be a peace officer.

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (3) If, under section 24 (2) (a) of the Offence Act, a justice orders that something referred to in subsection (2) of this section be detained, despite section 24 (3) of the Offence Act, the thing may be detained for up to one year before an order under section 24 (5) of that Act, authorizing its continued detention, is required.

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (4) If a director considers that a thing seized in an inspection or, despite subsections (2) and (3), under subsection (1), is

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (a) a pollutant or an environmental hazard, it must not be returned, or

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (b) contaminated by a pollutant, it must not be returned unless it is decontaminated at the expense of the person entitled to it.

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (5) Compensation is not payable by the government in respect of anything lawfully seized, detained or destroyed under this Act.

heading: Seizures and prevention orders
paragraph: (6) Sections 23 to 24.2 of the Offence Act do not apply in relation to anything taken in the course of an inspection under section 109 or 111 of this Act unless subsection (1) of this section applies.

heading: Inquiries
paragraph: 113		  (1) If the minister considers it necessary, the minister may

heading: Inquiries
paragraph: (a) order an inquiry with respect to the environment, and

heading: Inquiries
paragraph: (b) appoint a person to conduct the inquiry.

heading: Inquiries
paragraph: (2) A person appointed under subsection (1) must conduct the inquiry in accordance with terms of reference and any procedural guidelines specified by the minister for the inquiry.

heading: Inquiries
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of an inquiry under this section, the minister or person appointed under subsection (1) has the powers, privileges and protection of a commission under sections 16, 17, 22 (1), 23 (a), (b) and (d) to (f) and 32 of the Public Inquiry Act.

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph: 114		  (1) If a person, by carrying on an activity or operation, contravenes any of the following, the activity or operation may be restrained in a proceeding brought by the minister in the Supreme Court:

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph:
(a) 
                section 6 [waste disposal];

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph:
(b) 
                section 9 [hazardous waste storage and disposal];

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph:
(c) 
                section 10 [transportation of hazardous waste];

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph: (d) a suspension or cancellation made under section 18 [suspension or cancellation of permits and approvals];

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph: (e) an order made under Part 4 [Contaminated Site Remediation];

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph:
(f) 
                section 76.2 [management of greenhouse gases at waste management facilities];

heading: Restraining orders
paragraph: (2) The making of an order by the court under subsection (1) in relation to a matter does not interfere with the imposition of a penalty in respect of an offence in relation to the same contravention.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
115
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, if a director is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that a person has

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of this Act or the regulations,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with an order under this Act,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) failed to comply with a requirement of a permit or approval issued or given under this Act, or

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (d) failed to comply with a term or condition of a conditional PRO certificate, or a PRO certificate, as those terms are defined in section 91.1,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: the director may serve the person with a determination requiring the person to pay an administrative penalty in the amount specified in the determination.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) A determination under subsection (1) must be in the prescribed form and contain the prescribed information.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) A penalty imposed under this section must be paid within the prescribed time.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) Before the date an administrative penalty under this section is due, the director may, subject to the regulations, enter into an agreement with the person who is liable for the penalty.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (5) An agreement under subsection (4) may provide, in accordance with the regulations, for the reduction or cancellation of the penalty subject to the terms and conditions the director considers necessary or desirable.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (6) An agreement under subsection (4) must specify the time for performing the terms and conditions and if the person fails to perform those terms and conditions by the date specified, the penalty specified in the notice under subsection (1) is due and payable on that date.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (7) Neither a director's decision whether to enter into an agreement nor the terms and conditions of an agreement under subsection (4) may be appealed under Division 2 [Appeals from Decisions under this Act] of Part 8.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (8) If a director issues an administrative penalty notice to a person in respect of a contravention or failure referred to in subsection (1), a prosecution for an offence under this Act in respect of the same contravention or failure may not be brought against the person.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (9) If a corporation contravenes the Act or regulation or fails to comply with an order, permit or approval as described under subsection (1), an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure is also liable under this section even though the corporation is liable for or pays an administrative penalty.

heading: Effect of charging an offence
paragraph:
116
		  A person who has been charged with an offence under this Act may not be subject to an administrative penalty in respect of the circumstances that gave rise to the charge.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
117
		  (1) Subject to a decision of the appeal board cancelling a determination under section 115 (1) [administrative penalties], an administrative penalty under this Act may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required under section 115 [administrative penalties], the officer who made the determination may file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, upon filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) may be in the prescribed form, must be signed by the officer and must contain

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the penalty,

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) the contravention or failure in relation to which the penalty is imposed, and

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the penalty.

heading: Environmental certification
paragraph:
118
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by regulation, may limit the circumstances in which prescribed words, names, phrases, symbols, labels, marks or packaging may be used in relation to products or services to indicate that the product or service

heading: Environmental certification
paragraph: (a) was produced or provided using prescribed environmental practices, or

heading: Environmental certification
paragraph: (b) meets prescribed environmental quality or production standards.

heading: Environmental certification
paragraph: (2) A regulation referred to in subsection (1) may adopt standards developed by a prescribed person for use of the prescribed word, name, phrase, symbol, label, mark or packaging.

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph:
119
		  (1) Without limiting section 138 (1) [general authority to make regulations], the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make the following regulations:

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (a) for the purposes of providing economic incentives to promote environmentally responsible behaviour,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (i)  respecting the variation of fees payable by a person under this Act, including without limitation,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (A) authorizing a director to vary fees,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (B) establishing the criteria the person must satisfy to be eligible for or subject to a variation, and

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (C) limiting the amount of a variation authorized by the director,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (ii)  respecting agreements under which the requirements of this Act or the regulations may be varied, including by adding to, restricting the application of or eliminating requirements, in relation to that person for the term of the agreement, including without limitation

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (A) authorizing the minister to enter into agreements,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (B) establishing the criteria the person must satisfy to be eligible for an agreement,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (C) specifying the provisions of the Act or regulations that may be varied under an agreement, and

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (D) requiring public notification to persons affected by an agreement, and

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (iii)  respecting the establishment of a program of discharge monitoring, registration and trading, including offsets or credits;

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (b) for the purposes of section 115 [administrative penalties],

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (i)  prescribing procedures for making a determination including, but not limited to,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (A) prescribing the form and content of an administrative penalty notice,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (B) prescribing contraventions in relation to which an administrative penalty notice may be sent and a determination made, and

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (C) establishing procedures for providing a person on whom a notice of an administrative penalty has been served with an opportunity to make representations which need not entail an oral hearing,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (ii)  prescribing a schedule of monetary penalties that may be imposed and the matters that must be considered by an officer in establishing a penalty in a particular case,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (iii)  authorizing administrative penalties to be imposed on a daily basis for continuing contraventions or failures,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (iv)  prescribing time limits for paying administrative penalties,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (v)  prescribing, in relation to a contravention or failure described in section 115 (1), whether a notice of an administrative penalty must be cancelled if the person on whom it was served demonstrates to the satisfaction of a director that the person exercised due diligence to prevent the specified contravention or failure,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (vi)  respecting agreements, including prescribing terms and conditions that must be included, under section 115 (4),

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (vii)  prescribing a limitation period for imposing an administrative penalty and evidentiary matters in relation to that period,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (viii)  prescribing for manners of paying a monetary penalty,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (ix)  prescribing the consequences of failing to pay an administrative penalty which may include, but are not limited to, imposing additional penalties,

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (x)  providing for the publication of an officer's determination to impose an administrative penalty, and

heading: Regulations for purposes of Part 9.1
paragraph: (xi)  prescribing the form of a certificate under section 117 [recovery of administrative penalties].

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
120
		  (1) A person who contravenes section 12 [littering] or 13 [discharge of waste from recreational vehicles] commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $2 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes any of the following commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(a) 
                section 9 (3) [hazardous waste storage and disposal];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) section 10 (1) (a), (b) or (c) or (2) [transportation of hazardous waste];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (c) section 11 [packaging, product containers and single-use products];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (d) section 72 (1) or (2) [control of air contaminants];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(g) 
                section 131 (1) [confidentiality];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (h) a regulation under section 74 (1) (i), (j) or (k) [motor vehicle and engine emission regulations];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (i) section 91.2 (1) (a) [responsible persons - spill response] by

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (i)  failing to report the prescribed information,

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (ii)  failing to report to the prescribed persons, or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (iii)  failing to report in the prescribed time or manner;

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (j) section 91.2 (1) (c) by

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (i)  failing to ensure that the persons, resources and equipment described in that section arrive at the spill site within the prescribed period, or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (ii)  failing to ensure that those persons implement an incident command system in the prescribed time and manner.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (3) A person who contravenes any of the following commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 000 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) section 6 (2), (3) or (4) [waste disposal];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) section 7 (1) or (2) [hazardous waste - confinement];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(c) 
                section 8 [hazardous waste disposal facility];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (d) section 9 (1) or (4) [hazardous waste storage and disposal];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(e) 
                section 76.2 [management of greenhouse gases at waste management facilities];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (4) A person who inserts in a manifest required by section 10 [transportation of hazardous waste] information that the person knows to be untrue or misleading commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (5) A person who obstructs or resists an officer who is performing duties under this Act or who fails to comply with a requirement of an officer imposed under this Act commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (6) A person who, holding a permit or approval issued to the person under this Act to introduce waste into the environment, introduces waste into the environment without having complied with the requirements of the permit or approval commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 000 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (7) A person who, holding a permit or approval issued under this Act to introduce waste into the environment, fails to comply with the requirements of the permit or approval commits an offence and is liable to a penalty not exceeding $300 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (8) A person who contravenes section 10 (3) [transportation of hazardous waste] by failing to comply with a requirement of section 10 (3) (a) or (b) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (9) A person who contravenes section 10 (3) [transportation of hazardous waste] by failing to comply with a requirement of section 10 (3) (c) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $300 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (10) A person who contravenes an order or requirement, other than an order under section 9 (3) [hazardous waste storage and disposal] or 90.1 (1) [permits under area based management plan], that is given, made or imposed under this Act by a sewage control manager, a district director, a director, the minister or the appeal board commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $300 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both, but an order or requirement is not contravened unless it

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) was given in writing, and

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) specified a reasonable period of time for compliance and that period has expired.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (11) A municipality that

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) fails to submit to the minister a waste management plan as requested or directed by the minister under section 24 (2) or (3) [waste management plans], or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) contravenes a waste management plan that has been approved by the minister

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $300 000.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (12) A person who contravenes a requirement of the regulations respecting hazardous waste commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 000 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (13) A person who contravenes a requirement of a regulation that specifies the quantity or characteristics of waste that may be introduced into the environment commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 000 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (14) A person who contravenes an order under section 127 [additional sentencing orders] or 128 [variation of section 127 orders] commits an offence and is liable to the penalties provided for the offence in relation to which the order was made.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (15) A person who

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) neglects or refuses to supply an environmental impact assessment if required to do so under section 78 [environmental impact assessment], or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) contravenes section 87 (8) [environmental emergency measures]

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $10 000.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (16) A person who

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) supplies an environmental impact assessment under section 78 [environmental impact assessment] that the person knows to be false or misleading, or to contain false or misleading information, or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) contravenes section 85 (8) [environmental protection orders]

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $100 000.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (17) A person who

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) fails to submit a site disclosure statement as required under section 40 [site disclosure statements] or the regulations or supplies a site disclosure statement that the person knows to contain false or misleading information,

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a.1) contravenes section 40.1 (2),

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) fails to undertake a preliminary site investigation or a detailed site investigation and to prepare a report of the investigation as required under section 41 (1) or (3) [site investigations],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (c) fails to comply with a remediation order under section 48 [remediation orders],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (d) contravenes section 48 (8) [remediation orders],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (e) fails to seek an opinion from an allocation panel if required to do so under section 49 (4) [allocation panel],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (f) fails to comply with the requirements of a director in a voluntary remediation agreement under section 51 (1) [voluntary remediation agreements],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (g) fails to notify a director of initiating or completing independent remediation under section 54 (2) [independent remediation procedures],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (h) fails to comply with requirements of a director under section 54 (3) [independent remediation procedures] regarding independent remediation,

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (i) contravenes section 55 (1.1) or (1.3) [removal and deposit of soil],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (i.1) contravenes section 55.1 (2) [high volume soil receiving sites], or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (j) fails to comply with a provision of the regulations under section 62 [contaminated site regulations] or 63 [minister's regulations - contaminated sites]

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (18) A person who contravenes a requirement that has been substituted by a director or the minister for a requirement under the regulations, including a code of practice, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 000 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (19) A person who contravenes a requirement of a protocol under section 64 [director's protocols] commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (20) A proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under this Act does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (21) A person who does any of the following commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $300 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) contravenes section 91.2 (2) [responsible persons - spill response] by failing to ensure that the actions necessary to address the threat or hazard created by the spill are taken;

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) fails to comply with an order under section 91.2 (4) by

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (i)  failing to prepare or amend a recovery plan, or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (ii)  failing to submit a recovery plan in the time and manner specified by the director;

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (c) contravenes section 91.2 (6) by

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (i)  failing to have an approved recovery plan carried out,

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (ii)  failing to have a person described in section 91.2 (6) (a) carry out an approved recovery plan,

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (iii)  failing to have an approved recovery plan carried out by the date specified by the director under section 91.2 (6) (b),

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (iv)  failing to have a report prepared and submitted to the director, or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (v)  submitting a report that does not comply with the regulations.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (22) A regulated person who does any of the following commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $400 000 or imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or both:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) fails to have a spill contingency plan on or before the prescribed date;

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) prepares a spill contingency plan that does not comply with this Act or the regulations;

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (c) fails to comply with section 91.11 (2) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (d) contravenes section 91.11 (3) (a), (b), (c) or (d);

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (e) contravenes section 91.11 (4) by failing to implement an applicable spill contingency plan;

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (f) fails to comply with an order of a director under section 91.11 (5) (a), (b) (i) or (ii), (c) or (d), (6) or (7).

heading: Offence by a corporation
paragraph:
121
		  (1) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence whether or not the corporation is convicted.

heading: Offence by a corporation
paragraph: (2) In a prosecution for an offence under or arising out of a contravention of section 9 (1) [hazardous waste storage and disposal] or 10 (1) or (3) [transportation of hazardous waste], or of a regulation made with respect to hazardous waste, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by an employee or agent of the accused whether or not the employee or agent is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence, unless the accused establishes that the offence was committed without the accused's knowledge or consent or that the accused exercised all due diligence to prevent its commission.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph:
122
		  (1) If an offence under section 120 [offences and penalties] or an offence, established by a regulation, that is prescribed for the purposes of this section continues for more than one day, separate fines, each not exceeding the maximum fine for that offence, may be imposed for each day the offence continues.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a continuing offence under section 120 (15) or (16) (a) [offences and penalties].

heading: Offence Act application
paragraph:
123
		  Sections 4 and 5 of the Offence Act do not apply in respect of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: 124		  (1) The time limit for laying an information for an offence under this Act is

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (a) 5 years after the date that the facts on which the information is based arose, or

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) if the minister completes a certificate described in subsection (2), 18 months after the date that the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the minister, certifying the date that the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the minister,

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (a) is admissible without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the certificate, and

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) is proof of the certified matters.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph:
125
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act and the court is satisfied that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any monetary benefits or that monetary benefits accrued to the person, the court may order the person to pay a fine equal to the court's estimation of the amount of those monetary benefits.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: (2) A fine under subsection (1) is in addition to and not in place of a fine under section 120 [offences and penalties] or 126 [intentional damage].

heading: Intentional damage
paragraph:
126
		  A person who, in contravention of this Act,

heading: Intentional damage
paragraph: (a) intentionally causes damage to or loss of the use of the environment, or

heading: Intentional damage
paragraph: (b) shows wanton or reckless disregard for the lives or safety of other persons by causing a risk of death or harm to other persons

heading: Intentional damage
paragraph: commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $3 000 000 or imprisonment for not more than 3 years, or both.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
127
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any punishment imposed, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (b) directing the person to take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (c) directing the person to pay the government an amount of money as compensation, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken by or caused to be taken on behalf of the government as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (d) directing the person to perform community service;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (e) directing the person to pay an amount of money the court considers appropriate to the trustee under Part 3 of the Wildlife Act for inclusion in the trust property, as that term is defined in section 118 of that Act;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (f) directing the person to post a bond or pay into court an amount of money the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (g) directing the person to submit to the minister, on application by the minister within 3 years after the date of the conviction, any information respecting the activities of the person that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (h) directing the person to publish, in any manner the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (i) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the person's good conduct and for preventing the person from repeating the offence or committing other offences under this Act.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to comply with an order referred to in subsection (1) (h) directing the person to publish the facts relating to the commission of an offence, the minister may publish those facts and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (3) If

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (a) an order under this section or section 128 [variation of section 127 orders] directs a person to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose, or

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (b) the minister incurs publication costs under subsection (2) of this section,

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: the amount and any interest payable on that amount constitute a debt due to the government and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: 128		  (1) An application for variation of an order under section 127 [additional sentencing orders] may be made to the court that made the order by

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (a) the Attorney General, or

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (b) the person against whom the order under section 127 [additional sentencing orders] was made.

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (2) Before hearing an application under subsection (1), the court may order the applicant to give notice of the application in accordance with the directions of the court.

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (3) On an application under subsection (1), if the court considers variation appropriate because of a change in circumstances, the court may make an order doing one or more of the following:

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (a) changing the original order or any conditions specified in it;

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (b) relieving the person referred to in subsection (1) (b) absolutely or partially from compliance with all or part of the original order;

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (c) reducing the period for which the original order is to remain in effect;

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (d) extending the period for which the original order is to remain in effect, subject to the limit that this extension must not be longer than one year.

heading: Variation of section 127 orders
paragraph: (4) If an application under subsection (1) has been heard by a court, no other application may be made in respect of the order under section 127 [additional sentencing orders] except with leave of the court.

heading: Conservation officers exempt
paragraph:
129
		  The offence provisions of an enactment do not apply to a conservation officer engaged in the performance of the conservation officer's duties under that enactment.

heading: Evidence
paragraph:
130
		  (1) An order, permit, licence, approval or certificate that is issued under this Act or any other enactment administered by the minister and that purports to be signed by, or a copy that purports to be certified as a true copy and to be signed by,

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (a) the minister, the chief conservation officer, a director or a manager,

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (b) a public officer designated by the minister, or

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (c) an analyst designated by the minister under subsection (2),

heading: Evidence
paragraph: is admissible in a proceeding without proof of office or signature of the person signing, and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is evidence of the order, permit, licence, approval or certificate and of the matters set out in it.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (2) For purposes of this or any other enactment administered by the minister, the minister may designate as an analyst a person the minister considers qualified.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (3) A person designated as an analyst under subsection (2) may issue a certificate of analysis with respect to a sample held in the person's custody and analyzed by the person.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph:
131
		  (1) If, under this Act, information relating to any trade secret or any proprietary right in a process or technique that the user keeps confidential is disclosed to or obtained by any person engaged in the administration of this Act, a person who has access to the information so disclosed or obtained must not disclose the information except

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (a) as may be required in connection with the administration of this Act or any proceeding under this Act,

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (b) to the person's counsel, or

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (c) with the consent of the person rightfully possessing or using the trade secret, process or technique to which the information relates.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (2) Except in a proceeding under this Act, a person is not required to give testimony, other than testimony in respect of the deposit, addition, emission or discharge of a contaminant into the natural environment, in any civil suit or proceeding with regard to information obtained by or in the course of any investigation, survey, examination, test or inquiry under this Act.

heading: Ownership of waste
paragraph:
132
		  (1) The ownership of waste that is accepted at a waste management facility by the owner of the facility is transferred to the owner of the facility on acceptance.

heading: Ownership of waste
paragraph: (2) If, at a waste management facility, waste is stored or introduced into the environment without having been accepted by the owner of the facility, the ownership of the waste is deemed to have been transferred to the owner of the facility immediately before the waste was stored or introduced into the environment.

heading: Ownership of waste
paragraph:
(3) 
              Subsections (1) and (2) apply only in respect of a waste management facility that is authorized in accordance with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Ownership of waste
paragraph:
(4) 
              Subsection (1) applies only in the absence of a contract to the contrary.

heading: Ownership of waste
paragraph:
(5) 
              Subsections (1) to (4) do not relieve any person from liability except liability as owner of waste that is delivered to and accepted by the owner of a waste management facility in accordance with this section.

heading: Ownership of waste
paragraph: (6) If the owner of a waste management facility is not the owner of the land on which the facility is located, subsections (1) and (2) do not prevent the ownership of waste that is accepted or deposited at the site from being transferred to the owner of the land.

heading: Service
paragraph:
133
		  (1) Anything that under this Act must be given to or served on an individual may be given or served

heading: Service
paragraph: (a) by leaving it with the individual,

heading: Service
paragraph: (b) by sending it by registered mail to the last known address of the individual, or

heading: Service
paragraph: (c) by sending it by electronic mail to the last known electronic mail address of the individual used in relation to a registration, permit, approval, order, waste management plan, inspection or investigation under this Act.

heading: Service
paragraph: (2) Anything that under this Act must be given or served on a corporation may be given or served

heading: Service
paragraph: (a) by leaving it with any director, senior officer, liquidator or receiver manager of the corporation,

heading: Service
paragraph: (b) by sending it by registered mail as follows:

heading: Service
paragraph: (i)  if the corporation is a company within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act, to the mailing address shown for the registered office of the corporation in the corporate register;

heading: Service
paragraph: (ii)  if the corporation is an extraprovincial company within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act,

heading: Service
paragraph: (A) to the mailing address shown in the corporate register for the head office of the corporation if the head office is in British Columbia, or

heading: Service
paragraph: (B) to the mailing address shown in the corporate register for any attorney of the corporation;

heading: Service
paragraph: (iii)  in all other cases, to the head office of the corporation, or

heading: Service
paragraph: (c) by sending it by electronic mail to the last known electronic mail address

heading: Service
paragraph: (i)  of the corporation or of a director, officer or employee of the corporation, and

heading: Service
paragraph: (ii)  used in relation to a registration, permit, approval, order, waste management plan inspection or investigation under this Act.

heading: Service
paragraph: (3) Anything sent by registered mail for the purposes of this Act is deemed to be received by the person to whom it is addressed on the 14th day after deposit with Canada Post, unless the person received actual service before that day.

heading: Service
paragraph: (4) Anything sent by electronic mail for the purposes of this Act is deemed to be received by the person to whom it is addressed on the third day after it is sent.

heading: Service
paragraph: (5) This section does not apply to notices or documents of the appeal board.

heading: Charges, fees and costs to be paid to the government
paragraph: 134		  Each of the following must pay to the government, in the time and manner prescribed in the regulations, the fees and charges established by the regulations:

heading: Charges, fees and costs to be paid to the government
paragraph: (a) a holder of a permit or approval;

heading: Charges, fees and costs to be paid to the government
paragraph: (b) the holder of a licence for the transportation of hazardous wastes;

heading: Charges, fees and costs to be paid to the government
paragraph: (c) the subject of an order under this Act;

heading: Charges, fees and costs to be paid to the government
paragraph: (d) a municipality in respect of which a waste management plan has been approved under Part 3 [Municipal Waste Management].

heading: Interagency agreements
paragraph:
135
		  (1) Subject to the direction of the minister, the chief conservation officer or any other person designated by the minister may enter into agreements with other agencies of government, including those of the federal government and of provincial, municipal and first nations governments, respecting

heading: Interagency agreements
paragraph: (a) law enforcement delivery related to environmental protection or natural resource use,

heading: Interagency agreements
paragraph: (b) activities that may be carried out by an officer, as defined in the Wildlife Act, related to wildlife-human conflict response and management, and

heading: Interagency agreements
paragraph: (c) cooperative working agreements between the Conservation Officer Service and another enforcement agency that are within the mandate of either agency.

heading: Interagency agreements
paragraph: (2) Agreements entered into under subsection (1) may contain provisions setting out requirements for compensation or other legal recourse in the event that the agreement is breached by one or more of the parties to the agreement.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: 136		  (1) The minister may establish a fund to be known as the Waste Management Trust Fund.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (2) The money in the Waste Management Trust Fund must be held in trust by the government for the purposes specified in this section.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (3) The object of the Waste Management Trust Fund is to provide money for the purposes of

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (a) environmental clean up necessitated by inadequate closure of waste management facilities, and

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (b) long term care and maintenance of waste management facilities.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (4) Money collected or received under the regulations for the purposes of the Waste Management Trust Fund must be paid into the Waste Management Trust Fund.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (5) Money may be paid out of the Waste Management Trust Fund in a manner the minister considers appropriate on the requisition of the minister for the purposes of the fund.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (6) If money of the Waste Management Trust Fund is spent for the purpose referred to in subsection (3) (a), a certificate signed by the minister and showing the amount spent is conclusive proof as to the amount spent.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (7) An amount shown by a certificate referred to in subsection (6) is a debt due to the government recoverable, subject to subsection (8), by action in the Supreme Court from the person who was the owner of the waste management facility immediately before its closure.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (8) If the Supreme Court is satisfied that the expenditure incurred by the government under this section was either

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (a) excessive, taking into consideration the reasons for the clean up and the results achieved by the expenditure, or

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (b) unnecessary, taking into consideration the unlikelihood of significant material damage to any person had the government not acted under this section,

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: the court may reduce or extinguish the amount of the judgment that it would otherwise have ordered be entered against the person against whom the action has been brought.

heading: Waste Management Trust Fund
paragraph: (9) Money recovered under subsection (7) must be paid into the Waste Management Trust Fund and may be spent for the purposes of that fund.

heading: Powers that Lieutenant Governor in Council may exercise
paragraph:
137
		  (1) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it to be necessary in the public interest, the Lieutenant Governor in Council has and may exercise, in respect of wastes, all the powers that a director may exercise under this Act in respect of wastes.

heading: Powers that Lieutenant Governor in Council may exercise
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council, after any consultations the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers desirable, may issue permits for the construction and operation of facilities for the management, treatment, disposal, recycling, storage and destruction of wastes or for the introduction of wastes into the environment.

heading: Powers that Lieutenant Governor in Council may exercise
paragraph: (3) In acting under this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may act in a manner the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers to be in the public interest and is not limited to the considerations that would be taken into account by a director, district director or officer.

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph:
138
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (a) establishing an area of British Columbia as a waste management region, abolishing and varying boundaries and names of waste management regions and consolidating waste management regions;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing the form and content of any notice;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (c) requiring applicants to pay fees for making applications under this Act, and prescribing the amount of those fees;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (d) requiring persons to whom a permit, approval, operational certificate, exemption or other licence or privilege is issued under this Act to pay to the government charges in respect of the permit, approval, operational certificate, exemption, licence or privilege, establishing the amount of those charges or the method of their determination and requiring that they be paid yearly or otherwise;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (e) establishing procedures for making applications under this Act, and establishing the information that must be submitted in those applications;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (f) requiring consultations among ministries before an application under this Act is disposed of, setting time limits for those consultations and authorizing a director to extend those time limits;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (g) requiring that any person who is authorized to make a decision or a determination under this Act give notice in writing and publish the decision or determination;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (h) authorizing and establishing amounts for the rebate of fees or charges under this Act to foster expenditures in or contributions towards projects or purposes that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers to be in the interest of the environment including authorizing the minister to pay money out of the Sustainable Environment Fund continued under the Sustainable Environment Fund Act for the issuance of any rebate authorized under the regulations;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (i) prescribing a material as a recyclable material and for this purpose may establish conditions and circumstances when a prescribed material is a recyclable material;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (j) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions respecting

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  the transportation, labelling, handling, treatment, recycling, recovery, storage, disposal and destruction, and

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  the selling, giving or otherwise transferring of the ownership or possession,

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: of recyclable materials or wastes or classes of wastes or reusable resources, including energy potential recovered from wastes;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (k) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions respecting the siting, planning, construction and operation of facilities for the treatment, recycling, storage, disposal and destruction of recyclable materials or wastes;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (l) authorizing the minister or a director, on receipt of an application or on the minister's or director's own initiative, to substitute a different requirement for a requirement contained in the regulations, including a code of practice prescribed under section 22 [minister's regulations - codes of practice], if the minister or director considers that, in the individual case,

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  the substitution is necessary to protect the public or the environment, or

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  the intent of the regulations will be met by the substitution;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (m) requiring the director to give or require notification to the public of an application or a decision to substitute a different requirement for a requirement in a regulation, including a code of practice;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (n) requiring that the owner or operator of the waste management facility make adequate arrangements to maintain the facility after it has been closed and, if required by the government, to transfer to the government ownership of the facility after its closure;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (o) requiring that the owner or operator of the waste management facility make contributions to the Waste Management Trust Fund, the amount of the contributions to be prescribed or established by agreement or both;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (o.1) requiring the owner or operator of a waste management facility to give security to the minister in the amount and form and subject to the conditions specified, or authorizing a director to require the owner or operator of a waste management facility to give security in the amount and form and subject to the conditions the director may specify;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (o.2) requiring the owner or operator of a waste management facility to provide evidence that a covenant under section 219 of the Land Title Act has been entered into in favour of the Crown, and respecting the provisions that are to be included in the covenant, or authorizing a director to require evidence of such a covenant and specify the provisions that are to be included in the covenant;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (p) prescribing a substance as a waste and prescribing circumstances in which a substance is a waste;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (q) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions respecting the quantity of wastes and the characteristics and components of wastes that may be discharged into sewage facilities owned by a municipality;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (r) prohibiting, regulating or restricting the use, supply, storage, transportation, handling, treatment or disposal of any substance specified in the regulations, whether natural or artificial and whether in a solid or liquid or other form, if the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it appropriate to do so for the purpose of preventing the substance from causing damage to persons, animals or plants or polluting air, water or land;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (s) exempting any operation, activity, industry, waste or works or any class of persons, operations, activities, industries, wastes or works from any or all of the provisions of this Act or the regulations in circumstances and on conditions that the Lieutenant Governor in Council prescribes;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (t) requiring the keeping of and allowing the inspection of records;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (u) requiring, on request of the minister, that a person or a class of persons involved in the manufacture, distribution, sale, transportation or importation of empty or filled beverage containers of a prescribed type, or a person or association on behalf of that class of persons, supply information respecting the use, reuse and wastage of a prescribed type of beverage container;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (v) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions for the design, siting and operation of any works, activities or operations that produce waste;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (w) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions for the installation of septic tanks, the siting and performance standards to be met if sewage disposal systems using septic tanks are installed, and respecting the use and operation of systems using septic tanks;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (x) requiring a municipality designated by the minister to administer regulations under this section relating to hazardous wastes as they apply to effluent discharged by an industry connected to the municipal sewer system;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (y) authorizing a municipality designated under paragraph (x) to collect fees from industries for the purpose of administering the regulations relating to hazardous wastes and respecting the amount of those fees;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (z) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions for the registration, siting, installation, testing, use and removal of tanks used to store petroleum products, or used to store any other prescribed substance, and prescribing performance and operating standards for those tanks.

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (a) requiring and establishing requirements for the certification or licensing of persons who install the tanks described under subsection (2) (z);

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (b) requiring persons to pay fees with respect to services provided by the government or a municipality with respect to the tanks described under subsection (2) (z), and prescribing the amount of those fees;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (c) authorizing a municipality to collect and retain the fees prescribed under paragraph (b);

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (d) prescribing for a contravention of a regulation a penalty not exceeding $200 000;

heading: General authority to make regulations
paragraph: (e) regulating and imposing requirements and prohibitions respecting flood hazard management, including without limitation, requiring a diking authority as defined in the Dike Maintenance Act, or a local authority as defined in the Community Charter to develop plans or programs in accordance with those regulations or requirements for the purposes of

heading: General authority to make regulations

paragraph:

              be located within

heading: Riparian values
paragraph:
5
		  The following objectives with respect to riparian values are prescribed for the
            purposes of the definition of "government's environmental objectives" in section 1 (2)
            of the Act:

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (a) that operating areas not be located within any of the following:

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (i)  a stream, except to facilitate the crossing of the stream;

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (ii)  a lake, except to facilitate

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (A) the crossing of the lake, or

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (B) geophysical exploration on lakes that are frozen to the bottom;

heading: Riparian values
paragraph:
(iii)  a wetland with a riparian class of W2, except to facilitate the crossing of
                the wetland;

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (iv)  an enclosed upland within a wetland, unless

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (A) the wetland has a riparian class of W1 or W3,

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (B) the enclosed upland is greater than 5 ha, and

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (C) it is not practicable to locate the operating area elsewhere;

heading: Riparian values
paragraph:
(v)  a riparian reserve zone except to facilitate a crossing of the applicable
                stream, wetland or lake;

heading: Riparian values
paragraph:
(vi)  except to facilitate a crossing, a riparian management zone, unless an
                operating area will not have a material adverse effect on the ability of the
                riparian management zone to

heading: Riparian values
paragraph:
(A) conserve the fish habitat, wildlife habitat, biodiversity and the water
                  values of the riparian management zone, and

heading: Riparian values
paragraph: (B) protect the riparian reserve zone, if any, and

paragraph:
(b) that sufficient streamside trees and understory vegetation be retained to
              prevent the temperature of a temperature sensitive stream from increasing or
              decreasing to an extent that would have a material adverse impact on the fish in the
              stream.

heading: Wildlife and wildlife habitat
paragraph:
6
		  The following objectives with respect to wildlife and wildlife habitat are
            prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "government's environmental objectives"
            in section 1
              (2) of the Act:

heading: Wildlife and wildlife habitat
paragraph: (a) that operating areas not be located within any of the following:

paragraph:
(i)  a wildlife habitat area, unless an operating area will not have a material
                adverse effect on the ability of the wildlife habitat within the wildlife habitat
                area to provide for the survival, within the wildlife habitat area, of the wildlife
                species for which the wildlife habitat area was established;

heading: Wildlife and wildlife habitat
paragraph:
(ii)  an ungulate winter range, unless an operating area will not have a material
                adverse effect on the ability of the wildlife habitat within the ungulate winter
                range to provide for the survival, within the ungulate winter range, of the ungulate
                species for which the ungulate winter range was established;

heading: Wildlife and wildlife habitat
paragraph:
(iii)  a fisheries sensitive watershed, unless an operating area will not have a
                material adverse effect on the ability of the fisheries sensitive watershed to
                protect downstream fisheries and watershed values,

heading: Wildlife and wildlife habitat
paragraph:
(b) that energy resource activities on an operating area outside of a wildlife habitat
              area be carried out at a time and in a manner that does not result in physical
              disturbance to high priority wildlife or their habitat, including disturbance during
              sensitive seasons and critical life-cycle stages,

paragraph:
(c) that no portion of an operating area be within a wildlife tree retention area,
              and

paragraph:
(d) that energy resource activities not damage or render ineffective a wildlife
              habitat feature.
