heading: Water quality
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person who is carrying out an energy resource activity on an operating area that contains a waterworks or water supply well
              must ensure that the energy resource activity does not cause a material adverse effect on
              the quality, quantity or flow of the water to the waterworks or water supply
              well.

heading: Water quality
paragraph:
(2) A person is not prohibited from carrying out an energy resource activity under
                subsection
                (1) if

heading: Water quality
paragraph: (a) it is not practicable to comply with subsection (1),

heading: Water quality
paragraph: (b) the adverse effect is minimized, and

heading: Water quality
paragraph: (c) the person

heading: Water quality
paragraph:
(i)  gives notice to the owner or user of the waterworks or water supply well
                  at least 72 hours before adversely affecting the water supply, and

heading: Water quality
paragraph:
(ii)  for the period in which the water supply will be adversely affected,
                  provides the owner or user of the waterworks or water supply well with an
                  alternate supply of water of equal or better quality.

heading: Aquifers
paragraph:
10
		  A person carrying out an energy resource activity on an operating area on top of an
            aquifer must ensure that the activity does not cause a material adverse effect on the
            quality, quantity or natural timing of flow of water in the aquifer.

heading: Crossings of streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph:
11
		  A person who carries out an energy resource activity on an operating area must, for
            each crossing of a stream, wetland and lake, ensure all of the following:

heading: Crossings of streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph:
(a) the crossing is constructed and maintained at times and in a manner that is
              unlikely to harm fish or destroy, damage or harmfully alter fish habitat;

heading: Crossings of streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (b) the crossing does not

heading: Crossings of streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (i)  prevent the movement of fish, nor

heading: Crossings of streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph:
(ii)  impede the movement of fish to the extent that it is harmful to the survival
                of the fish;

heading: Crossings of streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph:
(c) the side of the stream, wetland or lake is protected at the
              crossing;

heading: Crossings of streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph:
(d) any disturbance to the stream channel and stream bank, wetland, or lake
              bottom, as applicable, is mitigated.

heading:
No deleterious materials into streams, wetlands or
            lakes
paragraph:
12
		  A person who carries out an energy resource activity on an operating area must
            ensure that the energy resource activity does not result in any deleterious materials being
            deposited into a stream, wetland or lake.

heading: Operations within wetlands
paragraph:
13
		  A person carrying out an energy resource activity in a wetland must, to the extent
            practicable, maintain natural flow of water in the wetland.

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph:
14
		  If a person carrying out an energy resource activity on an operating area causes the
            removal or the rendering ineffective of a natural range barrier, the person must, before
            livestock is turned out on the area, or, if turnout has occurred, as soon as
            practicable, construct a replacement barrier that is at least as effective as the one
            removed or rendered ineffective was before the removal or rendering
            ineffective.

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph:
15
		  A person carrying out an energy resource activity on an operating area
            must

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph:
(a) make reasonable efforts to ensure that seed, plant parts or propagules of an
              invasive plant are not transported into the area while carrying out the energy resource
              activities,

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph:
(b) to prevent invasive plants from becoming established, revegetate areas
              disturbed by the energy resource activity using seed of ecologically suitable species as
              soon as practicable after the disturbance, and

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph:
(c) if on a well site or a facility area, ensure that invasive plants do not
              become established on the wellsite or facility area.

heading: Forest health
paragraph:
16
		  A person carrying out an energy resource activity on an operating area that is
            occupied by insects harmful to forest health must not create conditions for the spread
            of the insects.

heading: Conserving soil
paragraph:
17
		  A person carrying out an energy resource activity that disturbs the surface of an
            operating area must

heading: Conserving soil
paragraph: (a) not cause the soil of the area to become unstable, and

heading: Conserving soil
paragraph:
(b) minimize any alteration to the natural surface drainage patterns on the
              area.

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph:
18
		  (1) A person constructing a seismic line on an enclosed upland must, to the extent
              practicable, construct a cut line that

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph: (a) is a maximum of 3.0 metres in width,

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph: (b) avoids large standing trees, and

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph: (c) leaves the soil and ground cover generally undisturbed.

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph:
(2) A person constructing a seismic line within a riparian reserve zone
              must

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph:
(a) construct a cut line as described in subsection (1),
                and

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph: (b) to the extent practicable, retain forest cover and mature trees.

heading: Seismic lines
paragraph:
(3) A person constructing a seismic line must not damage or render ineffective a
              wildlife habitat feature or a resource feature.

heading: Areas to be restored
paragraph:
19
		  (1) A person who carried out an energy resource activity on an operating area and who
              no longer intends to do so must, as soon as practicable, restore the operating area by
              doing the following:

heading: Areas to be restored
paragraph: (a) de-compacting any soils compacted by the energy resource activity;

heading: Areas to be restored
paragraph:
(b) redistributing any retrievable surface soils that were removed from the
                operating area during construction so that the soil structure is restored, to the
                extent practicable, to its condition before the energy resource activity was
                begun;

heading: Areas to be restored
Areas to be restored
paragraph:
(d) re-vegetating any exposed soil on the operating area using seed or
                vegetative propagules of an ecologically suitable species that

heading: Areas to be restored
paragraph:
(i)  promote the restoration of the wildlife habitat that existed on the area
                  before the energy resource activity was begun, and

heading: Areas to be restored
paragraph: (ii)  stabilize the soil if it is highly susceptible to erosion;

heading: Areas to be restored
Areas to be restored
paragraph:
(f) stabilizing any cut slopes or fill slopes in wellsites and facility
                areas;

heading: Areas to be restored
paragraph:
(g) re-contouring bladed areas or excavations in pipeline corridors and seismic
                lines.

heading: Classes
paragraph: 2 (1) The following classes of vessels are prescribed for the purposes of subsection 167(1) of the Act:

heading: Classes

heading: Exclusions

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (c) government vessels, naval auxiliary vessels or vessels owned or operated by a foreign state and used only on government non-commercial service.

heading: Definition of oil tanker
paragraph: (3) In this section, oil tanker means a vessel constructed or adapted primarily to carry oil in bulk in its cargo spaces and includes the following vessels that are carrying a cargo or part cargo of oil in bulk:

heading: Definition of oil tanker
paragraph: (a) a combination carrier, which is a vessel designed to carry oil or solid cargoes in bulk;

paragraph: (c) a gas carrier, which is a cargo vessel constructed or adapted for the carriage in bulk of any liquefied gas or other products listed in Chapter 19 of the International Code for the Construction and Equipment of Ships Carrying Liquefied Gases in Bulk, published by the International Maritime Organization.

heading: Content
paragraph: 10 The oil pollution prevention plan must contain the following:

heading: Content
paragraph: (a) the position of the person who is responsible for supervising in person the loading or unloading of oil to or from a vessel;

heading: Content
paragraph: (b) the types and quantity of equipment for use in the loading or unloading of oil to or from a vessel and the measures to be taken in order to meet the manufacturer's specifications in respect of the maintenance and certification of that equipment;

heading: Content
paragraph: (c) the procedures to be followed by the oil handling facility's personnel before and during the loading or unloading of oil to or from a vessel;

heading: Content
paragraph: (d) the procedures to be followed in order to meet the requirements of subsection 38(2) of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations and in order to reduce the rate of flow or pressure in a safe and efficient manner when the supervisor on board a vessel gives notice of the stopping of the loading or unloading of oil to or from the vessel to the person referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Content
paragraph: (e) the measures to be taken in order to meet the requirements of section 33 of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations and, in the event of failure of the means of communication referred to in that section, in order to ensure that effective two-way communication between the person referred to in paragraph (a) and the supervisor on board the vessel is continuously maintained before and during the loading or unloading of oil to or from the vessel;

heading: Content
paragraph: (f) a description of the lighting to be provided in order to meet the requirements of section 34 of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations;

heading: Content
paragraph: (g) documentation that demonstrates that the transfer conduit at the oil handling facility meets the requirements of subsection 35(1) of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations;

heading: Content
paragraph: (h) the measures to be taken in order to meet the requirements of subsection 35(3) of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations;

heading: Content
paragraph: (i) the procedures to be followed by the person referred to in paragraph (a) in order to meet the requirements of subsection 35(4) of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations;

heading: Content
paragraph: (j) the procedures to be followed by the operator of the oil handling facility in order to prevent a discharge of oil;

heading: Content

paragraph: (vii) the environmental impact of a discharge, and

heading: Content
paragraph: (viii) the measures to be taken for clean-up following the oil pollution incident, including with respect to areas of environmental sensitivities and surrounding ecosystems;

heading: Content
paragraph: (d) the types and quantity of equipment and resources referred to in subsection 13(2) that are available for immediate use at the location of the discharge;

heading: Content
paragraph: (e) the name of each person or organization and the location from which the equipment and resources will be obtained in the event of an oil pollution incident, and the manner in which the equipment and resources will be deployed at the location of the incident;

heading: Content
paragraph: (f) the name and the position of the persons who are authorized and responsible for ensuring that the response to an oil pollution incident is immediate, effective and sustained;

heading: Content
paragraph: (g) the name or the position of each person who has received oil pollution incident response training or any other training in relation to an oil pollution incident;

heading: Content
paragraph: (h) a description of the training provided, or to be provided, to the oil handling facility's personnel or other individuals in preparation for the responsibilities that they may be requested to undertake in response to an oil pollution incident;

heading: Content
paragraph: (i) an oil pollution incident exercise program established to evaluate the effectiveness of all aspects of the procedures, equipment and resources that are identified in the plan, including exercises to be coordinated with vessels engaged in the loading or unloading of oil, vessels used to respond to oil pollution incidents, response organizations, the Department of Transport and the Canadian Coast Guard;

heading: Content
paragraph: (j) the measures to be taken by the operator, in accordance with applicable federal and provincial regulations relating to health and safety, to protect the health and safety of personnel and of other individuals who are involved in responding to an oil pollution incident at the operator's request;

heading: Content
paragraph: (k) the procedures to be followed for the review and updating of the plan in order to meet the requirements of section 12;

heading: Content
paragraph: (l) the procedures to be followed by the operator in order to meet the requirements of section 39 of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations; and

heading: Content
paragraph: (m) the procedures to be followed by the operator to investigate any oil pollution incident in order to determine the causes and contributing factors and the actions that are needed to reduce the risk of reoccurrence.

heading: Other plans
paragraph: (2) The operator must ensure that the oil pollution emergency plan takes into account any contingency plan for its geographical area that may affect the facility's plan, including contingency plans that are issued by the Canadian Coast Guard or provincial or municipal governments.

heading: Notification - exercise
paragraph: (3) The operator must submit a written description of any exercise referred to in paragraph (1)(i) to the Minister at least 30 days before the day on which it conducts the exercise.

heading: Annual review
paragraph: 12 (1) The operator of an oil handling facility must review the oil pollution prevention plan and the oil pollution emergency plan annually and, if necessary, update the plans to ensure that they meet the requirements of section 10 or 11, as the case may be.

heading: Review - events
paragraph: (2) The operator of an oil handling facility must review the oil pollution prevention plan and the oil pollution emergency plan when any of the following events occur and, if necessary, update those plans within 90 days after the day on which the event occurred:

heading: Review - events
paragraph: (a) any change in the law or in environmental factors that could affect the loading or unloading of oil to or from a vessel;

heading: Review - events
paragraph: (b) any change in personnel involved in the loading or unloading of oil to or from a vessel;

heading: Review - events
paragraph: (c) the identification of a gap in either of the plans after an oil pollution incident or exercise; and

heading: Review - events
paragraph: (d) any change in the business practices, policies or operational procedures of the facility that could affect the loading or unloading of oil to or from a vessel.

heading: Submission of updates to Minister
paragraph: (3) If the operator of an oil handling facility updates the oil pollution prevention plan or the oil pollution emergency plan, the operator must submit the up-to-date plan to the Minister no later than one year after the update.

heading: Record
paragraph: (4) The operator of an oil handling facility must keep a record of the date and the results of each review of the oil pollution prevention plan and the oil pollution emergency plan conducted under subsections (1) and (2), including any updates, and must maintain the record for three years after the day on which it is created.

heading: Procedures
paragraph: 13 (1) The procedures referred to in paragraph 168(1)(e) of the Act must include the following:

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (a) the immediate shut down of loading or unloading operations and their restart in a manner that would not interfere with the immediate, effective and sustained response to the discharge;

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (b) the reporting of the discharge in accordance with section 133 of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations;

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (c) the coordination of the oil handling facility's response operation with the activities of the Canadian Coast Guard and federal, provincial and other bodies responsible for, or involved in, the protection of the marine environment;

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (d) the taking into account by the operator of the oil handling facility of the priorities set out in paragraph 11(1)(c) during the entire response to the discharge;

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (e) the making available of at least one of the persons referred to in paragraph 11(1)(f) to the Department of Transport and the Canadian Coast Guard during the entire response to the discharge;

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (f) the measures necessary to ensure that the operator of the oil handling facility is prepared to respond in the event of a discharge of oil of at least the applicable quantity set out in clauses 11(1)(b)(i)(A) to (D);

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (g) the deployment of the equipment and resources referred to in subsection (2) at the location of the discharge within the time frames set out in that subsection; and

heading: Procedures
paragraph: (h) the undertaking of an investigation of the discharge in order to determine the causes and contributing factors, and the actions that are needed to reduce the risk of reoccurrence.

heading: Equipment and resources
paragraph: (2) The equipment and resources that the operator of the oil handling facility must have available for immediate use in accordance with paragraph 168(1)(e) of the Act are those

heading: Equipment and resources
paragraph: (a) that are required to contain, control, recover and clean up a discharge of oil of at least the applicable quantity set out in clauses 11(1)(b)(i)(A) to (D); and

heading: Equipment and resources
paragraph: (b) that can be deployed, if it is possible to do so in a safe, effective and practicable manner, at the location of the discharge,

heading: Equipment and resources
paragraph: (i) for the purposes of containing and controlling the oil, within one hour after the discovery of the discharge, and

heading: Equipment and resources
paragraph: (ii) for the purposes of recovering the oil and cleaning up, within six hours after the discovery of the discharge.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agricultural land reserve" has the same meaning as in the Agricultural Land Commission Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "board" means the Provincial board under the Natural Products Marketing (BC) Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "complainant" means a person who under section 3 applies for a determination referred to in that section;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Crown land" means land, whether or not it is covered by water, or an interest in land, vested in the government;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "farm business" means a business in which one or more farm operations are conducted, and includes a farm education or farm research institution to the extent that the institution conducts one or more farm operations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "farm operation" means any of the following activities involved in carrying on a farm business:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) growing, producing, raising or keeping animals or plants, including mushrooms, or the primary products of those plants or animals;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) clearing, draining, irrigating or cultivating land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) using farm machinery, equipment, devices, materials and structures;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) applying fertilizers, manure, pesticides and biological control agents, including by ground and aerial spraying;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) conducting any other agricultural activity on, in or over agricultural land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) intensively cultivating in plantations, any

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  specialty wood crops, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  specialty fibre crops

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed by the minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) conducting turf production

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  outside of the agricultural land reserve, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  in the agricultural land reserve with the approval under the Agricultural Land Commission Act of the Provincial Agricultural Land Commission;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) prescribed types of aquaculture;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) raising or keeping fur bearing animals or game, within the meaning of a regulation made under the Animal Health Act, by a person licensed or permitted to do so under that Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (k) processing or direct marketing by a farmer of one or both of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the products of a farm owned or operated by the farmer, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  within limits prescribed by the minister, products not of that farm,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: to the extent that the processing or marketing of those products is conducted on the farmer's farm;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (l) an activity, other than grazing or hay cutting, if the activity constitutes a forest practice as defined in the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (m) breeding pets or operating a kennel;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (n) growing, producing, raising or keeping exotic animals, except types of exotic animals prescribed by the minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "farmer" means the owner or operator of a farm business;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land use regulation" means an enactment that restricts or prescribes the use to which land or premises may be put or the nature of business or activities that may be conducted on land or premises, but does not include the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a bylaw under the following provisions of the Community Charter:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 8 (3) (d) [firecrackers, fireworks and explosives];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 8 (3) (e) [weapons other than firearms];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 8 (3) (h) [nuisances, disturbances and other situations];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 8 (3) (k) [animals];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 8 (5) [firearms];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a bylaw under the following provisions of the Local Government Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 318 [general animal control powers];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 324 [noise control];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 325 [nuisances and disturbances];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: section 326 [fireworks restrictions];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "normal farm practice" means a practice that is conducted by a farm business in a manner consistent with

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) proper and accepted customs and standards as established and followed by similar farm businesses under similar circumstances, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any standards prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and includes a practice that makes use of innovative technology in a manner consistent with proper advanced farm management practices and with any standards prescribed under paragraph (b).

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: 2		  (1) If each of the requirements of subsection (2) is fulfilled in relation to a farm operation conducted as part of a farm business,

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (a) the farmer is not liable in nuisance to any person for any odour, noise, dust or other disturbance resulting from the farm operation, and

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (b) the farmer must not be prevented by injunction or other order of a court from conducting that farm operation.

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (2) The requirements referred to in subsection (1) are that the farm operation must

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (a) be conducted in accordance with normal farm practices,

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (b) be conducted on, in or over land

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (i)  that is in the agricultural land reserve,

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (ii)  on which, under the Local Government Act, farm use is allowed,

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (iii)  that is used for a type of aquaculture prescribed for the purpose of paragraph (h) of the definition of "farm operation", or

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (iv)  that is Crown land designated as a farming area under subsection (2.1), and

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (c) not be conducted in contravention of the Public Health Act, Integrated Pest Management Act, Environmental Management Act, the regulations under those Acts or any land use regulation.

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (2.1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may designate Crown land as a farming area for the purposes of subsection (2) (b) (iv).

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (3) The following apply if each of the requirements of subsection (2), except subsection (2) (b) (ii), is fulfilled in relation to a farm operation conducted as part of a farm business:

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (a) despite section 260 (3) [bylaw contraventions] of the Community Charter, a farmer does not contravene a bylaw made under the following provisions of the Community Charter only by conducting that farm operation:

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 8 (3) (d) [firecrackers, fireworks and explosives];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 8 (3) (e) [weapons other than firearms];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 8 (3) (h) [nuisances, disturbances and other situations];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 8 (3) (k) [animals];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 8 (5) [firearms];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (b) despite section 416 [bylaw contraventions - offences and prosecutions] of the Local Government Act, a farmer does not contravene a bylaw made under the following provisions of the Local Government Act only by conducting that farm operation:

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 318 [general animal control powers];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 324 [noise control];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 325 [nuisances and disturbances];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: section 326 [fireworks restrictions];

heading: Normal farm practices protected
paragraph: (c) despite section 274 [actions by municipality] of the Community Charter and section 420 [enforcement by civil proceedings] of the Local Government Act, a farmer must not be prevented by injunction or other order of a court from conducting that farm operation.

heading: Complaints to board
paragraph: 3		  (1) If a person is aggrieved by any odour, noise, dust or other disturbance resulting from a farm operation conducted as part of a farm business, the person may apply in writing to the board for a determination as to whether the odour, noise, dust or other disturbance results from a normal farm practice.

heading: Complaints to board
paragraph: (2) Every application under subsection (1) must

heading: Complaints to board
paragraph: (a) contain a statement of the nature of the complaint, the name and address of the person making the application, the name and address of the farmer and the location of the farm,

heading: Complaints to board
paragraph: (b) be in a form acceptable to the chair of board, and

heading: Complaints to board
paragraph: (c) be accompanied by the fee prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Settlement of complaints
paragraph:
4
		  In the interest of reaching a settlement of a complaint that is the subject of an application under section 3 (1), the chair of the board, at any time before a panel of the board has decided the application, may inquire into matters relevant to the complaint, and, as part of that inquiry, may

heading: Settlement of complaints
paragraph: (a) obtain the advice of persons who are knowledgeable about normal farm practices, and

heading: Settlement of complaints
paragraph: (b) consult with the farmer identified in the application and the complainant.

heading: Establishing panels to hear complaints
paragraph:
5
		  After receipt of an application that meets the requirements of section 3, the chair of the board, if satisfied that any consultations under section 4 have been terminated without achieving a settlement of the complaint, or that settlement is unlikely, must establish a panel of the board to hear the complaint.

heading: Hearing of complaints
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The panel established to hear an application must hold a hearing and must

heading: Hearing of complaints
paragraph: (a) dismiss the complaint if the panel is of the opinion that the odour, noise, dust or other disturbance results from a normal farm practice, or

heading: Hearing of complaints
paragraph: (b) order the farmer to cease the practice that causes the odour, noise, dust or other disturbance if it is not a normal farm practice, or to modify the practice in the manner set out in the order, to be consistent with normal farm practice.

heading: Hearing of complaints
paragraph: (2) The chair of the board, after giving the complainant an opportunity to be heard, may refuse to refer an application to a panel for the purpose of a hearing, or, after a hearing has begun, the panel to which an application has been referred may refuse to continue the hearing or to make a decision if, in the opinion of the chair of the board or the panel, as the case may be,

heading: Hearing of complaints
paragraph: (a) the subject matter of the application is trivial,

heading: Hearing of complaints
paragraph: (b) the application is frivolous or vexatious or is not made in good faith, or

heading: Hearing of complaints
paragraph: (c) the complainant does not have a sufficient personal interest in the subject matter of the application.

heading: Appeal
paragraph:
8
		  (1) Within 60 days after receiving written notice of a decision of the chair or a panel of the board made under section 6, the complainant or farmer affected by the decision may appeal the decision to the Supreme Court on a question of law or jurisdiction.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (2) An appeal from a decision of the Supreme Court lies to the Court of Appeal with leave of a justice of the Court of Appeal.

heading: Responsibilities of board
paragraph:
11
		  (1) The board, the chair of the board or a panel of the board may exercise the powers and perform the duties that are conferred or imposed on it under this Act.

heading: Responsibilities of board
paragraph: (2) On the board's own initiative or at the request of a municipality or regional district, or of a trust council under the Islands Trust Act, the board may study, report on, and make recommendations concerning, any matter related to farm practices.

heading: Responsibilities of board
paragraph: (3) The board must provide the minister with any information requested by the minister regarding the policies and procedures of the board.

heading: Responsibilities of board
paragraph: (4) The minister may order the board to study any matter related to farm practices and the board must conduct the study and report its findings and recommendations to the minister.

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: 11.1		  (1) For the purposes of exercising its powers and performing duties under this Act, the following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the board in addition to those incorporated under section 3.1 [application of Administrative Tribunals Act to the board] of the Natural Products Marketing (BC) Act:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a) Part 4 [Practice and Procedure], except the following:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (i)  section 21 [notice of hearing by publication];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (ii)  section 22 [notice of appeal (inclusive of prescribed fee)];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (iii)  section 23 [notice of appeal (exclusive of prescribed fee)];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (iv)  section 24 [time limit for appeals];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (v)  section 25 [appeal does not operate as stay];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (vi)  section 31 (1) (b) [summary dismissal for not filing within time limit];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (vii)  section 34 (1) and (2) [party power to compel witnesses and require disclosure];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b) section 47 [power to award costs];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (c) section 49 [contempt proceedings for uncooperative witness or other person];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (d) Part 7 [Decisions], except section 50 (1) [money order set out as principal and interest];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (e) section 56 [immunity protection for tribunal and members];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (f) section 60 (1) (a) to (i) and (2) [power to make regulations].

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (2) Despite section 3.1 of the Natural Products Marketing (BC) Act, the following sections of the Administrative Tribunals Act do not apply to the board in relation to this Act:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a) section 57 [time limit for judicial review];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b) section 58 [standard of review with privative clause].

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: 12		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting standards for the purpose of the definition of "normal farm practice";

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) governing practices and procedures for

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  hearings before a panel of the board, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  inquiries and consultations respecting complaints or other matters before the board, the chair of the board or a panel of the board;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting the engagement or retention of specialists and consultants by the board.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) The minister may make regulations prescribing one or more of the following:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) specialty wood crops or specialty fibre crops for the purpose of paragraph (f) of the definition of "farm operation";

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a.1) types of aquaculture for the purpose of paragraph (h) of the definition of "farm operation";

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) limits referred to in paragraph (k) of the definition of "farm operation";

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) exceptions for the purpose of paragraph (n) of the definition of "farm operation".

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic plants" includes any parts, products or by-products of these plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commodity" means a product derived from plants or animals, including parts, products or by-products, and fish or aquatic plants, that are raised or gathered for profit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "council" means a council established under section 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish" means an aquatic animal, including aquatic invertebrates, and any parts, products or by-products of such an animal;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fund" means a fund established under section 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "producer" includes a gatherer of plants or animals.

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph:
2
		  (1) Before the minister may establish a fund under this Act to promote the interests of all producers of a commodity, producers of that commodity must

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (a) obtain the minister's approval to a plan for

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (i)  informing the producers about

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (A) the proposed fund, levy and council,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (B) whether there will be any provision for refunding all or part of the levy, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (C) any other related matters that the minister requires, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (ii)  determining whether the producers of the commodity support the proposals, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (b) in accordance with the approved plan, satisfy the minister that the producers of the commodity support the proposals in the plan.

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (2) The minister may require different levels of support for

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (a) different plans, or

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (b) different proposals in the same plan.

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (3) The plan must meet the minimum requirements established by regulation respecting the content of the proposals and the method for informing producers about the proposals and for determining whether they support the proposals.

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), on being satisfied that there is producer support, the minister may

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (a) appoint a council composed of

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (i)  one or more representatives of the government, at least one of whom must be a representative of the ministry which administers this Act,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (ii)  producers of the commodity in sufficient numbers to constitute a majority of the council, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (iii)  one or more persons who the minister considers represent people involved in

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (A) the supply of goods or services to the producers, or

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (B) the processing, distribution or consumption of the commodity, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (b) establish and name a fund for that commodity.

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (5) If a plan

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (a) is supported by the producers,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (b) is approved by the minister, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (c) establishes a method by which the producer members of a council are to be chosen by election, by appointment or partly by election and partly by appointment,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: the minister must comply with the plan's proposals about the appointment or election of producer members to the council.

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (6) If, in relation to a commodity, a council and fund are established under this section,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (a) the council is responsible to the minister for the administration of the fund, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (b) the management, administration and control of the fund are vested in the council.

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (7) If a council exists on July 24, 1992,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (a) the council, the fund it administers and the regulation that relates to the council and the fund are continued,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (b) section 5 applies as if the Lieutenant Governor in Council has prescribed a regulation that allows a refund,

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (c) a plan is not required in respect of the commodity that relates to the council and subsection (1) does not apply to the producers of that commodity, and

heading: Plan, council and fund
paragraph: (d) the council may present to the minister a plan for determining producer support for a levy that is not refundable or for any proposal that producers may present to the minister under subsection (1), and this Act applies as if the plan were presented by the producers of the commodity.

heading: Powers of a council
paragraph:
3
		  (1) A council is a corporation and, subject to subsections (2) and (3), has all the powers of a corporation under section 17 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Powers of a council
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Powers of a council
paragraph: (a) restricting the powers of a council under subsection (1), and

heading: Powers of a council
paragraph: (b) authorizing a council to exercise powers in addition to the powers under subsection (1).

heading: Powers of a council
paragraph: (3) A council may not enter into an agreement to co-operate with or act as agent of any entity established by an Act or regulation of Canada or of any province or territory, without the approval of the minister.

heading: Revenue and expenditure
paragraph: 4		  (1) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, a council must establish a levy or class of levy that at the time and in the manner specified in the regulations must be paid by producers or a class of producers of the commodity for which the fund was established.

heading: Revenue and expenditure
paragraph: (2) The council may pay out of the fund the amounts it considers appropriate to

heading: Revenue and expenditure
paragraph: (a) pay an expense approved by the minister as being necessary for or incidental to the administration of this Act in relation to the fund, or

heading: Revenue and expenditure
paragraph: (b) pay to a person, including a person representing the producers of a commodity, a sum to

heading: Revenue and expenditure
paragraph: (i)  benefit and promote the industry in British Columbia in respect of a commodity, or

heading: Revenue and expenditure
paragraph: (ii)  conduct or support research or educational programs in British Columbia in respect of the development and promotion of a commodity.

heading: Revenue and expenditure
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by regulation, may prohibit a council from making payment for purposes specified in the regulations.

heading: Refund of levy
paragraph:
5
		  (1) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council has prescribed a regulation that allows a refund of a levy or class of levy, a producer who has paid to a council a levy established under section 4 (1) may apply to the council to have the levy refunded

heading: Refund of levy
paragraph: (a) as prescribed by the minister, and

heading: Refund of levy
paragraph: (b) not later than January 31 in the year following the year that the producer paid the levy.

heading: Refund of levy
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application in compliance with subsection (1), the council must refund the levy to the applicant.

heading: Audits
paragraph:
6
		  (1) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this Act and the regulations, any person authorized in writing by the council may

heading: Audits
paragraph: (a) at any reasonable time, enter the business premises of a person required to collect and remit levies, and

heading: Audits
paragraph: (b) inspect records relating to that requirement.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (2) A person required to collect and remit levies under this Act must make the records referred to in subsection (1) available for inspection.

heading: Annual report
paragraph:
7
		  (1) Within 3 months of the end of a council's financial year, each council must make to the minister a report of its business and affairs during that year.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (2) A report under subsection (1) must contain

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) a balance sheet,

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) a statement of revenue and expenditures, and

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (c) other particulars the minister requires.

heading: Annual general meeting
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A council must hold an annual general meeting in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Annual general meeting
paragraph: (2) A person who is required to pay or collect the levy may attend the annual general meeting, but only a person who is required to pay the levy may vote unless a regulation provides otherwise.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph:
9
		  (1) A person who fails to comply with or contravenes this Act commits an offence.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (2) A person who commits an offence is liable on conviction

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (a) to a fine of not more than $500, if the person is a corporation, and

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (b) to a fine of not more than $200, if the person is an individual.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
10
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) establishing the time and manner for payment of a levy established under section 4 (1);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) requiring one or more of the following persons to collect the levy established under section 4 (1) in the manner and within the time prescribed and to remit the amount collected, less any prescribed commission, to a prescribed person in the manner and within the time prescribed:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  a producer of the commodity;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  a distributor of the commodity;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iii)  the first person who purchases the commodity from the producer;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iv)  a person who supplies goods or services to the producer;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (v)  any other person involved in the production, processing, distribution or retailing of the commodity;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) authorizing a council to charge interest, at a rate determined by the council from time to time, on an amount that has not been remitted within the time prescribed under paragraph (b);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting section 4 (2);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (e) exempting a class of producers from payment of a levy, a class of levy or all levies;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (f) providing for refunds of levies;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (g) establishing practices and procedures for a council;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (h) requiring a council to report particulars of its operations in a manner and at times specified by the regulations;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i) respecting the minimum requirements referred to in section 2 (3);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (j) respecting the calling of annual general meetings by a council and the matters required to be dealt with and the conduct of business and votes at those meetings;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (k) respecting business plans and operational guidelines for councils;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (l) respecting the election of council members;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (m) respecting procedures that can be used by persons who are entitled to vote at annual general meetings to dissolve a council and distribute the fund and the council's assets;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (n) respecting a plan, including implementing a proposal in a plan.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under subsection (1) or (2) may

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) make different provisions for different commodities, councils, classes of producers or persons who may be subject to a levy,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) authorize a council or person to exercise a discretionary power, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) delegate a matter to a council or person.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) authorizing a council to exercise a power or perform a duty conferred on it under an Act or regulation of Canada, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) granting to an entity established by an Act or regulation of Canada some or all of the powers and duties that a council has under this Act or that a council may be given by a regulation made under this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "analyses" includes the taking of samples and the conducting of tests and visual examinations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "analyst" means a person

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) designated as an analyst under section 43 [power to designate analysts], or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) retained to exercise the powers of an analyst under section 44 [power to retain other persons];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic plants" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) benthic and detached algae, brown algae, green algae, red algae, marine flowering plants and phytoplankton, whether grown domestically or wild,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the products and byproducts of the aquatic plants described in paragraph (a), and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) part of an aquatic plant described in paragraph (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "byproduct" means materials, taken from fish or aquatic plants, that are not intended to be used for human consumption;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cause" includes to contribute to, directly or indirectly, beyond a minimal extent;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "distribute" includes to provide or offer to provide fish or aquatic plants to a person, whether directly or indirectly and with or without a fee;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "employee" includes a person who provides services

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) under contract, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) under the direction or supervision of an operator, whether or not for a fee;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "facility" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the premises on which a facility is located,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the soil and water

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  on or in which a facility is located, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  that are used while a person does, in a facility, an activity described in section 2 [activities to which this Act applies], and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) vehicles that are used while a person does an activity described in section 2, unless the vehicles are used only to transport fish or aquatic plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) crustaceans and mollusks,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) echinoderms,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) other aquatic animals, except birds and mammals,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the products and byproducts of fish and of the animals described in paragraphs (a) to (c), and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) parts of fish and of the animals described in paragraphs (a) to (c);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "inspector" means a person who is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an inspector under section 41 [inspectors], or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) retained to exercise the powers of an inspector under section 44;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licensing officer" means a person

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) designated as a licensing officer under section 40 [power to designate licensing and reviewing officers], or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) retained to exercise the powers of a licensing officer under section 44;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "operator" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person licensed under this Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an owner, manager or lessee of a facility that is the subject of a licence under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "personal information" means recorded information about an identifiable individual;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "process" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) to preserve, by any method, fish or aquatic plants for future consumption,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) to prepare, by any method, fish or aquatic plants,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) to hold or maintain live fish or aquatic plants until their preservation or preparation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) to kill fish held under paragraph (c), and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) to package fish or aquatic plants that have been preserved or prepared;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "product" means materials, taken from fish or aquatic plants, that are intended to be used for human consumption;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regional health board" means a regional health board as designated under the Health Authorities Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "reviewing officer" means a person

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) appointed as a reviewing officer under section 40, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) retained to exercise the powers of a reviewing officer under section 44;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "traceability system" means a system designed to track the location or transport of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) fish or aquatic plants, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) prescribed things in relation to fish or aquatic plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "unsafe food" means fish or aquatic plants that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) do not meet the requirements of section 3 (1) (a) [duty to ensure food safety], or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) have been possessed, reared, grown, harvested, processed, stored, transported or distributed in contravention of a regulation made for the purposes of section 3 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "vehicle" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any means of transporting fish or aquatic plants, whether by land, water or air, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) trailers and cargo containers used in transporting fish or aquatic plants.

heading: Activities to which this Act applies
paragraph: 2		  This Act applies to a person who possesses, rears, grows, harvests, processes, stores, transports or distributes fish or aquatic plants that may be distributed to the public for human consumption.

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph:
3
		  (1) A person must ensure that fish or aquatic plants the person possesses, rears, grows, harvests, processes, stores, transports or distributes

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph: (a) are safe for human consumption, are not contaminated and are not otherwise unfit for human consumption, or

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph: (b) if the standards under paragraph (a) are not met, are not distributed for human consumption and do not come into contact with products that may be distributed for human consumption.

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph: (2) If fish or aquatic plants that a person possesses, rears, grows, harvests, processes, stores, transports or distributes may be consumed by humans or come into contact with products that may be consumed by humans, the person must ensure that all applicable prescribed standards are met and all applicable prescribed measures are taken to ensure the safety and quality of the fish or aquatic plants.

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1) (a), fish or aquatic plants are contaminated if the fish or aquatic plants have been, or may have been, exposed to conditions that may permit the presence of any of the following:

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph: (a) foreign matter, including filth, a poisonous substance or a pest;

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph: (b) disease-causing micro-organisms or parasites;

heading: Duty to ensure food safety
paragraph: (c) toxins.

heading: If licence required
paragraph:
4
		  If a regulation made under this Act requires a person to be licensed to do an activity described in section 2 [activities to which this Act applies], a person must not do the activity unless licensed, or exempted from being licensed, under this Act.

heading: No possession or distribution if Act contravened
paragraph:
5
		  A person must not possess or distribute fish or aquatic plants that the person knows or has reason to believe have been possessed, reared, grown, harvested, processed, stored, transported or distributed in contravention of this Act.

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph:
6
		  (1) In this section, "restricted fish or aquatic plants" means prescribed fish or aquatic plants that

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (a) are subject to prohibitions or restrictions on harvesting under an enactment of Canada or an international agreement to which Canada is a party, or

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (b) may be subject to harvesting practices that are inhumane or unsustainable.

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (2) A person must not possess or distribute for human consumption restricted fish or aquatic plants except as authorized under

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (a) a licence, permit or other authorization issued under an enactment of Canada, or

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (b) a permit issued by a licensing officer.

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (3) A licensing officer may issue a permit, with or without terms or conditions, for the purposes of subsection (2) (b)

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (a) subject to the regulations, and

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (b) only for a purpose that, in the opinion of the licensing officer, is in the public interest.

heading: Possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants
paragraph: (4) A person who holds a permit issued under subsection (3) must comply with all terms and conditions of the permit.

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph:
7
		  (1) If a person is required by regulation to be licensed to do an activity described in section 2 [activities to which this Act applies], the person may apply for a licence by submitting to a licensing officer

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (a) an application, and

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (b) the prescribed records and fees, if any.

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application for a licence, a licensing officer may do one or more of the following:

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (a) request, in writing, from the applicant or from a person referred to by the applicant further information, samples, proof of a fact, records or any other thing necessary to evaluate the application;

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (b) refer the application to an inspector for an inspection under Division 1 [Inspections and Orders] of Part 4;

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (c) refer the application for review and comment to

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (i)  a public officer,

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (ii)  an employee of Canada, or

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (iii)  a person who has special expertise;

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (d) issue the licence with or without terms or conditions;

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (e) reject the application, providing to the applicant, in writing, the reason for the rejection.

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (3) A licence issued under this section is not transferable.

heading: Issuing licences
paragraph: (4) A licensing officer may waive the fee for a licence if the licensing officer is of the opinion that activities to be conducted under the licence will have an educational, scientific or research purpose.

heading: If food offered directly to public
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A person who intends to distribute fish or aquatic plants directly to the public for human consumption must state this in an application made under section 7 [issuing licences].

heading: If food offered directly to public
paragraph: (2) Without limiting any other reason for which a licence may be refused under this Act, a licensing officer may refuse to issue a licence to a person referred to in subsection (1) on the grounds that the person has been denied a licence or permit, or has been or is subject to a licensing action or a prosecution, under the Food Safety Act or the Public Health Act.

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: 9		  (1) An operator may request a variation of the operator's licence by

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: (a) submitting to a licensing officer

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: (i)  an application, and

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: (ii)  the prescribed records and fees, if any, and

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: (b) providing to the licensing officer information, samples, proof of a fact, records or any other thing necessary to evaluate the application.

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application for a variation, a licensing officer may do the following:

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: (a) exercise any of the powers set out in section 7 (2) (a) to (c) and (e) [issuing licences];

heading: Varying licences
paragraph: (b) vary the licence.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph:
10
		  (1) In this section, "administrative action" means to vary, suspend or cancel an operator's licence.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (2) In addition to any other action that may be taken under this Act, a licensing officer may take an administrative action if

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (a) an operator has contravened a provision of this Act,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (b) an operator is carrying out an activity, to which the licence applies, in a manner that the licensing officer reasonably believes may cause the distribution of unsafe food, or

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (c) both of the following apply to an operator:

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (i)  the operator is distributing, or has distributed, fish or aquatic plants directly to the public for human consumption, and

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (ii)  the operator is the subject of a licensing action or a prosecution under the Food Safety Act or the Public Health Act.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (3) Before taking an administrative action, the licensing officer must give to the operator

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (a) a written notice stating

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (i)  the administrative action the licensing officer proposes to take,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (ii)  the reason for taking the proposed administrative action,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (iii)  the date the proposed administrative action is to take effect, and

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (iv)  the manner in which the operator may respond to the proposed administrative action, and

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (b) a reasonable opportunity to respond, in writing, to the proposed administrative action.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (4) After providing the operator with a reasonable opportunity to respond in accordance with the manner set out in the notice given under subsection (3) (a), the licensing officer may do one or both of the following:

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (a) delay the date the administrative action is to take effect or suspend the administrative action, if satisfied that the delay or suspension would not cause the distribution of unsafe food;

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (b) after considering the operator's response, if any, and any supporting records or written submissions of the operator,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (i)  take the proposed administrative action,

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (ii)  take a different administrative action, or

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (iii)  rescind the notice and take no administrative action.

heading: Taking administrative action
paragraph: (5) The licensing officer must give written reasons for a decision made under subsection (4) (b) (i) or (ii).

heading: Taking licensing action to protect marine beds
paragraph: 11		  (1) A licensing officer may refuse to issue or renew, add terms or conditions on, or vary, suspend or cancel, a licence to harvest aquatic plants if the licensing officer is of the opinion that doing so is necessary to protect, or to prevent, reduce or address any adverse effect on, all or part of a bed on which aquatic plants grow.

heading: Taking licensing action to protect marine beds
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section limits any other reason for which a licensing officer may make a decision or take an action under this Act with respect to a licence, or an application for a licence, to harvest aquatic plants.

heading: Reconsideration of licensing decisions
paragraph:
12
		  (1) In this section and section 13 [review of licensing decisions], "decision" means a decision of a licensing officer to

heading: Reconsideration of licensing decisions
paragraph: (a) reject an application for a licence or an application to vary a licence,

heading: Reconsideration of licensing decisions
paragraph: (b) issue a licence subject to terms and conditions, or

heading: Reconsideration of licensing decisions
paragraph: (c) vary, suspend or cancel a licence.

heading: Reconsideration of licensing decisions
paragraph: (2) On receiving notice of a decision, a person subject to the decision may request the licensing officer who made the decision to reconsider the decision by submitting a request to the licensing officer within 30 days after receiving the notice.

heading: Reconsideration of licensing decisions
paragraph: (3) After considering a request for reconsideration, the licensing officer may take, as applicable, one or more of the actions described in section 7 (2) [issuing licences], 9 (2) (b) [varying licences] or 10 (4) [taking administrative action].

heading: Reconsideration of licensing decisions
paragraph: (4) The licensing officer must give written reasons for an action taken under subsection (3), and a person may not request further reconsideration.

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph:
13
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2) and the regulations, a person subject to a decision may request a reviewing officer to review the decision by submitting a request and the prescribed fee to the reviewing officer.

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph: (2) A request for a review may be made only

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph: (a) if a reconsideration has been completed under section 12 [reconsideration of licensing decisions], and

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph: (b) within 20 days after written reasons are given under section 12 (4).

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph: (3) A review must be based on the record.

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph: (4) A decision is not suspended during the period of review unless the reviewing officer states, in writing, that the decision is suspended.

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph: (5) After considering a request for a review, the reviewing officer may confirm, vary or rescind the decision under review.

heading: Review of licensing decisions
paragraph: (6) The reviewing officer must give written reasons for confirming or varying the decision under review, and the person subject to the decision may not request further review of the decision.

heading: General duty of compliance
paragraph:
14
		  An operator must comply with

heading: General duty of compliance
paragraph: (a) this Act,

heading: General duty of compliance
paragraph: (b) all regulations made under this Act respecting the activity for which the operator is licensed, and

heading: General duty of compliance
paragraph: (c) all terms and conditions of the operator's licence.

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph:
15
		  (1) Without limiting section 3 [duty to ensure food safety], an operator who engages in fish or aquatic plant processing must take preventive measures consistent with reasonable practices of fish or aquatic plant processing, as applicable, including the following:

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (a) applying disinfection and decontamination measures;

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (b) using a type of equipment or implementing a process, or removing or altering equipment or processes;

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (c) meeting any standard or taking any measure set out in the regulations;

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (d) taking any measure required by an inspector in an order made under this Act.

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (2) An operator must conduct, in accordance with the regulations,

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (a) analyses of fish and aquatic plants the operator possesses, rears, grows, harvests, processes, stores, transports or distributes, and

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (b) monitoring of activities, carried out under the operator's licence, for conditions that may cause unsafe food.

heading: Duties with respect to food safety
paragraph: (3) An operator must ensure that the operator's employees are adequately trained and sufficiently equipped for the purpose of complying with section 3 and this section.

heading: Duties with respect to facilities, vehicles and equipment
paragraph:
16
		  (1) An operator must ensure that facilities the operator uses

heading: Duties with respect to facilities, vehicles and equipment
paragraph: (a) are sufficiently maintained and equipped for the purpose of complying with section 3 [duty to ensure food safety], and

heading: Duties with respect to facilities, vehicles and equipment
paragraph: (b) meet all applicable prescribed requirements with respect to construction, maintenance, management, sanitation and operation.

heading: Duties with respect to facilities, vehicles and equipment
paragraph: (2) An operator must ensure that vehicles and equipment the operator uses are sufficiently maintained and sanitized for the purpose of complying with section 3.

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph:
17
		  (1) An operator must

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph: (a) keep, in accordance with the regulations, the prescribed records, and

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph: (b) produce the records required under paragraph (a)

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph: (i)  to the minister or an inspector, on request and within the time requested, and

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph: (ii)  to the minister, at prescribed intervals or under prescribed circumstances.

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph: (2) An operator must make reports as required by the regulations.

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph: (3) On receiving a report under this section, the minister may order the operator to take one or more prescribed actions.

heading: Duty to keep records and make reports
paragraph: (4) Division 2 [Making and Reviewing Orders] of Part 4 and section 35 [duty to comply with orders] apply to an order made under subsection (3) of this section as if it were an order made under that Part.

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph:
18
		  (1) If an operator has reason to believe that fish or aquatic plants the operator has distributed may be unsafe food, the operator must promptly

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (a) take measures to prevent further distribution of the fish or aquatic plants, and

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (b) report to an inspector the following information:

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (i)  the identity and contact information, if known, of all persons to whom the fish or aquatic plants have been distributed;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (ii)  the reason for believing the fish or aquatic plants the operator has distributed may be unsafe food;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (iii)  if analyses of the fish or aquatic plants were conducted, the nature of the analyses and the results;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (iv)  any measures taken under paragraph (a);

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (v)  any prescribed information;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (vi)  any other relevant information the inspector requests.

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (2) On receiving a report under this section, the inspector may order the operator to do one or more of the following:

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (a) give specified information by specified means to one or more persons or to the public;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (b) conduct specified forms of analyses or submit samples to an analyst for analyses;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (c) take specified measures to prevent further distribution, by the operator or by a person referred to in subsection (1) (b) (i), of fish or aquatic plants that may be unsafe food;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (d) make records and further reports;

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (e) take other prescribed actions.

heading: Duty to report unsafe food
paragraph: (3) Division 2 [Making and Reviewing Orders] of Part 4 and section 35 [duty to comply with orders] apply to an order made under subsection (2) of this section as if it were an order made under that Part.

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph:
19
		  (1) In this section and section 61 [regulations respecting traceability and certification]:

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: "traceability program" means a program established and maintained, or designated, under subsection (2) (b) of this section;

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: "traceable food" means fish or aquatic plants that are subject to a traceability system.

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (2) The minister may, for the purposes of this Act, establish and maintain, or designate, one or both of the following:

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (a) traceability systems;

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (b) programs that, in the opinion of the minister,

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (i)  facilitate the effectiveness of a traceability system, or

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (ii)  are an integral part of a traceability system.

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (3) A program may be designated under subsection (2) (b) whether

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (a) the program is established or maintained by a public or private body, including, without limitation, the government of another jurisdiction and a voluntary association, or

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (b) the traceability system to which the program relates, or is intended to relate, has not yet been established or designated.

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (4) An operator must do all of the following if and as required by a regulation made under section 60 [regulations respecting operators]:

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (a) obtain unique identifiers for traceable food, facilities, vehicles or things associated with the activity for which the operator is licensed;

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (b) attach identifiers or notices of identifiers to the corresponding traceable food, facilities, vehicles or things;

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (c) make records respecting traceable food, facilities, vehicles or things, and, if applicable, conduct analyses;

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
