paragraph: (d) report to the minister or a prescribed person all prescribed information respecting

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (i)  traceable food, facilities, vehicles or things,

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (ii)  facilities, vehicles or things used in connection with traceable food, even if those facilities, vehicles or things are not themselves subject to a traceability program, and

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (iii)  the transport or other movement of traceable food, including the means of transport or movement and the destination;

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (e) take other prescribed actions.

heading: Duty to participate in traceability system
paragraph: (5) Requirements made under this Act in relation to traceable food may be made with respect to containers or packages of traceable food rather than with respect to single items of traceable food.

heading: Duties if certification program prescribed
paragraph:
20
		  If a certification program is prescribed for the purposes of this section,

heading: Duties if certification program prescribed
paragraph: (a) a person must not hold themselves out as being certified unless the person is certified in accordance with the regulations, and

heading: Duties if certification program prescribed
paragraph: (b) a person who is certified must meet all prescribed standards.

heading: Duty to pay royalties
paragraph:
21
		  (1) An operator who harvests wild aquatic plants must pay to the government royalties in an amount, at the times and in the manner prescribed.

heading: Duty to pay royalties
paragraph: (2) Royalties owing under this section constitute a debt due to the government and are recoverable by action in a court that has jurisdiction.

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph:
22
		  (1) Inspections under this section are subject to the limits set out in section 24 [entering to inspect].

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (2) On referral under section 7 (2) (b) [issuing licences] or 9 (2) (a) [varying licences], an inspector may enter and inspect a vehicle or place to determine whether

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (a) a licence should be issued, or

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (b) a term or condition of a licence should be varied or rescinded.

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (3) An inspector may stop a vehicle, and enter and inspect a vehicle or place, if

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (a) the inspector reasonably believes that the vehicle or place

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (i)  is being or will be used, by an operator or employee, in relation to an activity for which the operator is licensed under this Act,

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (ii)  is being or will be used, by any person, in relation to an activity for which the person must be licensed under this Act, or

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (iii)  is the subject of an order made under this Act, and

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (b) the purpose of the inspection is

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (i)  to monitor or confirm compliance with this Act, the order or a provision of another enactment, including an enactment of Canada, in respect of which the inspector has a power of inspection, or

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (ii)  to determine whether the order should be varied or terminated.

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), an inspector may stop a person or vehicle, and enter and inspect a vehicle or place, if the inspector reasonably believes that

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (a) the person possesses or may possess, or the vehicle or place contains or may contain, fish or aquatic plants, and

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (b) the fish or aquatic plants

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (i)  may be unsafe food, or

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (ii)  are being, have been or may be possessed, reared, grown, harvested, processed, stored, transported or distributed in contravention of this Act.

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (5) An action may be taken under subsection (4) for one or more of the following purposes only:

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (a) to determine if the fish or aquatic plants described in subsection (4) are in a person's possession or present in a vehicle or place;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (b) if a report is made under section 17 [duty to keep records and make reports] or 18 [duty to report unsafe food], to confirm the information given in the report or to obtain further information;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (c) to take measures to stop or prevent a contravention of this Act;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (d) for any other purpose for which an inspection by an inspector is authorized under this or any other enactment, including an enactment of Canada;

heading: When inspections may be made
paragraph: (e) for a prescribed purpose.

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph:
23
		  (1) An inspector may do one or more of the following for the purpose of an inspection:

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (a) pass through a place to reach a vehicle or place that is to be the subject of the inspection;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (b) be accompanied or assisted by an analyst or a person who has special, expert or professional knowledge of a matter relevant to the inspection;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (c) require a person to produce relevant records or things in the person's possession or control;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (d) inspect, copy or remove relevant records or things, and, for this purpose, open any container or package;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (e) make records in respect of a person, place or thing;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (f) require a person to stop doing an activity or stop the operation of a thing;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (g) require a person whom the inspector reasonably believes to have relevant information to answer questions and otherwise give that information;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (h) conduct analyses, including removing fish, aquatic plants or samples from a container, package or facility for the purpose of having an analyst conduct analyses;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (i) require that a place or thing not be altered or disturbed for a reasonable period of time;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (j) require a person to operate a thing, carry out a procedure or demonstrate a relevant skill, as the inspector directs;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (k) attach to fish or aquatic plants, or to containers or packages, identifying marks or tags that permit identification of the fish or aquatic plants as having been inspected;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (l) make an order that is necessary for the purpose of exercising a power of inspection, including ordering a person found in a vehicle or place under inspection to assist in the inspection.

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (2) If an inspector removes records or things under subsection (1) (d), the inspector must do both of the following:

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (a) give a receipt for the records or things to the person from whom the records or things were taken;

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (b) subject to a power under this or any other enactment to order a thing destroyed, promptly return the records or things

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (i)  when the records or things have served the purposes for which the records or things were taken, or

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (ii)  if a proceeding is taken under this or any other enactment as a result of an inspection and the records or things are relevant to the proceeding, in accordance with an order of a court, or, if no order is made, no later than 3 months after the conclusion of the proceeding.

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (3) Sections 23 (4) and 24 to 24.2 of the Offence Act do not apply for the purposes of subsections (1) (d) and (2) of this section.

heading: Inspection powers
paragraph: (4) An inspector must, on request, produce, to a person subject to an inspection, identification as described under section 42 (3) [powers respecting inspectors].

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: 24		  (1) An inspector may conduct an inspection at any reasonable hour.

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (2) Before entering a place, an inspector must

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (a) take reasonable steps to notify the owner or occupier of the place of the date and time that the inspector will be entering, and

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (b) if the place is a private dwelling, obtain either the consent of the owner or occupier or a warrant to enter.

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2) (a), an inspector may conduct an inspection without providing notice in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (a) the thing to be inspected is on display in a public place;

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (b) providing notice would not be reasonably practical in the circumstances;

heading: Entering to inspect
paragraph: (c) providing notice might frustrate the purpose of the inspection.

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph:
25
		  (1) An inspector may order a person to do one or more of the following:

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (a) keep fish, aquatic plants or vehicles in a specified place;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (b) prevent fish or aquatic plants from

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (i)  being transported to or from a place,

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (ii)  being unloaded from a vehicle, or

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (iii)  entering a specified place;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (c) give to the inspector or a specified person information, records, samples or other things relevant to the purpose of the inspection, including information respecting persons to whom fish or aquatic plants have been distributed or were intended to be distributed;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (d) have fish or aquatic plants undergo analyses, including requiring fish, aquatic plants or samples to be given to an analyst to conduct analyses;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (e) take specified measures to prevent a contravention of this Act;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (f) do specified work in respect of a facility, vehicle or place, including removing or altering things found in the facility, vehicle or place and altering or locking the facility, vehicle or place to restrict or prevent entry to the facility, vehicle or place;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (g) not deal with or dispose of fish or aquatic plants, or do so only in accordance with a specified procedure;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (h) stop operating, or not operate, a thing;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (i) attach an identifying mark or tag to fish, aquatic plants or things;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (j) make or keep a specified record;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (k) stop distribution of fish or aquatic plants that are being, have been or may be possessed, reared, grown, harvested, processed, stored, transported or distributed in contravention of this Act;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (l) if the person is an operator, take specified measures to bring the operator into compliance with this Act;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (m) take specified measures to monitor activities, carried out under the operator's licence, for conditions that may cause unsafe food;

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (n) take a prescribed action.

heading: Orders that may be made
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty but subject to section 4 [if licence required], an inspector may make an order under this section even if the person subject to the order complies with all terms and conditions of a licence issued under this or any other enactment.

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph:
26
		  (1) If an inspector reasonably believes that fish or aquatic plants may be unsafe food, the inspector may

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (a) seize the fish or aquatic plants, and

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (b) conduct analyses of the fish or aquatic plants or submit the fish or aquatic plants, or samples of them, to an analyst for analyses.

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (2) If, on analysis, seized fish or aquatic plants are not found to be unsafe food, an inspector

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (a) must return the fish or aquatic plants to the person from whom the fish or aquatic plants were seized, or

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (b) may dispose of or destroy the fish or aquatic plants if return under paragraph (a) is not reasonably practical.

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (3) If, on analysis, seized fish or aquatic plants are found to be unsafe food, an inspector may do one or more of the following:

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (a) detain the fish or aquatic plants;

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (b) dispose of or destroy the fish or aquatic plants, or order another person to dispose of or destroy the fish or aquatic plants;

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (c) make any order that may be made under section 25 [orders that may be made].

heading: Seizure and destruction
paragraph: (4) An inspector must give written notice to a person from whom fish or aquatic plants are seized before taking an action under subsection (2) (b) or (3) (a) or (b).

heading: Recall orders
paragraph:
27
		  If an inspector acts under section 26 (3) [seizure or destruction], the minister may

heading: Recall orders
paragraph: (a) order an operator to recall any fish or aquatic plants that the operator has distributed, and

heading: Recall orders
paragraph: (b) take, or order the operator to take, any other action the minister reasonably believes is necessary to protect the public from unsafe food the operator has distributed or may have distributed.

heading: Costs
paragraph:
28
		  (1) This section applies to

heading: Costs
paragraph: (a) an order made under section 25 [orders that may be made] or 27 [recall orders], or

heading: Costs
paragraph: (b) the seizure, and disposal or destruction, under section 26 [seizure and destruction] of fish or aquatic plants.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (2) A person subject to an order or from whom fish or aquatic plants were seized is responsible for all costs incurred under section 25, 26 or 27, as applicable, by an inspector or the minister, including costs to have another person take an action on behalf of the inspector or minister.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (3) The costs referred to in subsection (2) constitute a debt due to the government and are recoverable by action in a court that has jurisdiction.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (4) A person has no right of action as a result of an action referred to in subsection (1) and must not commence or maintain proceedings

heading: Costs
paragraph: (a) to claim damages or compensation of any kind from the government, or

heading: Costs
paragraph: (b) to obtain a declaration that damages or compensation is payable by the government.

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph:
29
		  (1) An order made under this Part must be made in writing and describe all of the following:

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (a) who must comply with the order;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (b) what must be done or not done, and any conditions, including, if applicable, the date by which something must be done;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (c) the date on which, or the circumstances under which, the order is to terminate, if the date or circumstances are known;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (d) subject to the regulations, information sufficient to enable a person to contact the person who made the order;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (e) how the person subject to the order may have the order reconsidered;

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (f) any prescribed matter.

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (2) Two or more orders may be combined in a single written notice.

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), an inspector or the minister may make an order under this Part orally and describe only the matters set out in subsection (1) (a), (b) and (d) if the inspector or minister

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (a) reasonably believes that immediate action is necessary to

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (i)  prevent the distribution of unsafe food, or

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (ii)  protect the public from unsafe food that may have been distributed, and

heading: Contents of orders
paragraph: (b) makes the order in accordance with subsection (1) within 2 days of making the order orally.

heading: Service of orders
paragraph:
30
		  An order made under this Part must be served in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph:
31
		  (1) A person who makes an order under this Part may vary or terminate the order, at any time, on the person's own initiative.

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations, a person subject to an order under this Part may request the person who made the order to

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (a) reassess the relevant circumstances,

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (b) assess the extent to which the order has been complied with, and

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (c) determine whether the order continues to be necessary for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Variation and reassessment of orders
paragraph: (3) On receiving a request under subsection (2), the person who made the order may, based on the matters referred to in that subsection, confirm, vary or terminate the order.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph:
32
		  (1) A person subject to an order made under this Part may request the person who made the order to reconsider the order if

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (a) the person subject to the order has additional relevant information that was not reasonably available at the time the order was made, and

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (b) fewer than 20 days have passed since the order was made.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (2) After considering a request for reconsideration, the person who made the order may do one or more of the following:

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (a) reject the request on the basis that the information submitted in support of the request is not relevant or was reasonably available at the time the order was made;

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (b) delay the date the order is to take effect or suspend the order, if satisfied that the delay or suspension would not cause the distribution of unsafe food;

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (c) confirm, vary or rescind the order.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (3) The person who made the order must give written reasons for a decision to reject the request under subsection (2) (a) or to confirm or vary the order under subsection (2) (c), and the person subject to the order may not request further reconsideration.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (4) An order is not suspended during the period of reconsideration unless the person who made the order states, in writing, that the order is suspended.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of this section, if multiple orders are made that address related matters or issues, the person who made the orders may reconsider the orders separately or together.

heading: Reconsideration of orders
paragraph: (6) If a person is unable or unavailable to reconsider an order the person made, a person the minister designates may act under this section in respect of the order as if the designated person had made the order.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph:
33
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person subject to an order made under this Part may request a reviewing officer to review the order by submitting a request and the prescribed fee to the reviewing officer.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (2) A request for a review may be made only if less than 20 days has passed since

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (a) the order was made, if reconsideration is not available under section 32 (1) (a) [reconsideration of orders], or

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (b) an action was taken under section 32 (2).

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (3) A review must be based on the record.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (4) An order is not suspended during the period of review unless the reviewing officer states, in writing, that the order is suspended.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (5) After considering a request for a review, the reviewing officer may do one or more of the following in relation to the order under review:

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (a) delay the date the order is to take effect or suspend the order, if satisfied that the delay or suspension would not cause the distribution of unsafe food;

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (b) confirm, vary or rescind the order;

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (c) refer the matter back to the person who made the order, with or without directions.

heading: Review of orders
paragraph: (6) The reviewing officer must give written reasons for an action taken under subsection (5) (b) or (c), and the person subject to the order under review may not request further review of the order.

heading: Summary action
paragraph:
34
		  Despite sections 31 (2) and (3) [variation and reassessment of orders], 32 [reconsideration of orders] and 33 [review of orders], requests may not be made under those sections if

heading: Summary action
paragraph: (a) fish or aquatic plants are found under section 26 (3) [seizure and destruction] to be unsafe food, and

heading: Summary action
paragraph: (b) an inspector reasonably believes that the fish or aquatic plants must be destroyed immediately to prevent the distribution of unsafe food.

heading: Duty to comply with orders
paragraph:
35
		  A person subject to an order made under this Part must comply with the order.

heading: Postings and identification
paragraph:
36
		  (1) If the minister or an inspector, or a person acting under the direction of either of them, posts an order or a notice under this Act, a person other than the minister, an inspector or a person acting under the direction of either of them must not remove, deface or alter the posted order or notice.

heading: Postings and identification
paragraph: (2) If the minister or an inspector requires that fish or aquatic plants, or containers or packages of fish or aquatic plants, have identifying marks or tags, a person other than the minister, an inspector or a person acting under the direction of either of them must not remove, deface or alter the identifying marks or tags.

heading: Warrants
paragraph:
37
		  (1) Without notice to any person, an inspector may apply, in the manner set out in the regulations, to a justice of the peace for a warrant under this section.

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (2) A justice of the peace may issue a warrant in the prescribed form authorizing an inspector, or a person acting on behalf of an inspector, to enter and search a place, including a private dwelling, and take any necessary action if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation that doing so is necessary for the purpose of

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (a) taking an action authorized under this Act, or

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (b) determining whether an action authorized under this Act should be taken.

heading: Warrants
paragraph: (3) If an inspector is of the opinion that it would be impractical to appear personally before a justice of the peace to apply for a warrant under this section, the inspector may submit an information on oath by telephone or other means of telecommunication and, for this purpose, section 22 of the Offence Act applies.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: 38		  (1) Without notice to any person, an inspector may apply, in the manner set out in the regulations, to a judge of the Supreme Court for an injunction or an order under this section.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (2) A judge of the Supreme Court may grant an injunction restraining a person from contravening, or requiring a person to comply with, a provision of this Act if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation that there has been or will be a contravention of this Act.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (3) A judge of the Supreme Court may order a person to do or refrain from doing those things the judge considers necessary if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation that the person is interfering with or obstructing, or will likely interfere with or obstruct, a person who is exercising powers or performing duties under this Act.

heading: Injunctions
paragraph: (4) A judge of the Supreme Court may grant an interim injunction or order until the outcome of an application commenced under this section.

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph:
39
		  (1) An inspector may call on the assistance of a peace officer for the purpose of taking an action authorized under this or any other enactment, including, without limitation, for either of the following purposes:

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph: (a) making or enforcing an order or carrying out an inspection;

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph: (b) assisting a person to comply with or to carry out an order of the inspector.

heading: Peace officer assistance
paragraph: (2) A peace officer called on under this section may take any action that is necessary for a purpose described in subsection (1) and may use such force as is reasonably required for that purpose.

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph:
40
		  (1) The minister may designate, by order,

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (a) employees of the ministry of the minister as licensing officers,

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (b) employees of a regional health board as licensing officers if

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (i)  the employee, in the opinion of the minister, has sufficient training, knowledge, skills and experience to exercise the powers and perform the duties of a licensing officer, and

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (ii)  the regional health board approves the designation, and

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (c) employees of a ministry of the government as reviewing officers.

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (2) A person may not be both a licensing officer and a reviewing officer.

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (3) The minister may do one or more of the following in an order made under subsection (1):

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (a) name a specific person as a licensing officer or a reviewing officer;

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (b) provide that a person who holds a specified title or position is a licensing officer or a reviewing officer;

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (c) limit the powers and duties of a person designated as

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (i)  a licensing officer or a reviewing officer to a class of fish, aquatic plants, operators or facilities, or

heading: Power to designate licensing and reviewing officers
paragraph: (ii)  a reviewing officer to a review under section 13 [review of licensing decisions] or 33 [review of orders].

heading: Inspectors
paragraph:
41
		  (1) Subject to any limits imposed under subsection (4), the following persons may exercise powers and perform duties as inspectors for the purposes of this Act:

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (a) inspectors under the Fish Inspection Act (Canada);

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (b) fishery officers and fishery guardians under the Fisheries Act (Canada);

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (c) conservation officers under the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (d) officers of the provincial police force under the Police Act;

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (e) persons the minister designates under subsection (2).

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (2) The minister may designate as inspectors, by order,

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (a) employees of a ministry of the government,

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (b) employees of a regional health board if

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (i)  the employee, in the opinion of the minister, has sufficient training, knowledge, skills and experience to exercise the powers and perform the duties of an inspector, and

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (ii)  the regional health board approves the designation, or

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (c) employees of the government of Canada having duties under an enactment of Canada related to animal or food inspection.

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (3) The minister may do one or both of the following in an order made under subsection (2):

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (a) name a specific person as an inspector;

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (b) provide that a person who holds a specified title or position is an inspector.

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (4) The minister may limit, by order, the powers and duties of an inspector or a class of inspectors, including to one or both of the following:

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (a) a geographic area;

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: (b) a class of fish, aquatic plants, operators or facilities.

heading: Powers respecting inspectors
paragraph: 42		  (1) The minister may do, by order, one or more of the following:

heading: Powers respecting inspectors
paragraph: (a) establish training and qualifications for inspectors, including requiring that inspectors designated under section 41 (2) [inspectors] participate in ongoing training;

heading: Powers respecting inspectors
paragraph: (b) establish standards of practice for inspectors, and issue instructions to inspectors designated under section 41 (2), in relation to the exercise of their powers and the performance of their duties under this or any other enactment.

heading: Powers respecting inspectors
paragraph: (2) An inspector designated under section 41 (2) must comply with all applicable standards established, and instructions issued, under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Powers respecting inspectors
paragraph: (3) The minister may give to inspectors identification for use in exercising powers and performing duties under this Act.

heading: Power to designate analysts
paragraph:
43
		  The minister may designate, by order, employees of the ministry of the minister for the purpose of conducting analyses under this Act and, for this purpose, may

heading: Power to designate analysts
paragraph: (a) name a specific person as an analyst, or

heading: Power to designate analysts
paragraph: (b) provide that a person who holds a specified title or position, or who is employed for the purpose of conducting analyses by a specified laboratory or other facility, is an analyst.

heading: Power to retain other persons
paragraph:
44
		  (1) This section applies despite sections 40 (1) [power to designate licensing and reviewing officers], 41 (1) and (2) [inspectors] and 43 [power to designate analysts].

heading: Power to retain other persons
paragraph: (2) The minister may retain, as necessary, persons who are not employees of a ministry of the government to be licensing officers, reviewing officers, inspectors or analysts and, for this purpose, grant to those persons any power or duty of a licensing officer, a reviewing officer, an inspector or an analyst.

heading: Power to retain other persons
paragraph: (3) A person retained under subsection (2) may be remunerated in accordance with the prescribed fees for being a licensing officer, a reviewing officer, an inspector or an analyst, as applicable.

heading: Power to retain other persons
paragraph: (4) The Public Service Act does not apply to a person retained under subsection (2).

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: 45		  The minister may enter into agreements with any person or body, including the government of another jurisdiction, for one or more of the following purposes:

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) to administer this Act;

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) to exercise powers or perform duties, in relation to fish or aquatic plants, under an enactment of another jurisdiction;

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (c) to exchange information, including personal information,

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (i)  under an agreement referred to in paragraph (a) or (b),

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (ii)  for the purpose of a traceability system, or

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (iii)  if necessary or advisable for the protection of public health in relation to unsafe food.

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph:
46
		  (1) The minister may collect or disclose information under this Act for one or more of the following purposes:

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph: (a) to administer this Act;

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph: (b) to administer or to assist with the administration of an enactment or a government program, of Canada or any jurisdiction in Canada, that has as one of its purposes the protection or promotion of human or animal health;

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph: (c) to disclose, in accordance with the regulations, prescribed information contained in a traceability system;

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph: (d) to disclose prescribed information in respect of an order made under this Act;

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph: (e) to publish or disclose statistical information for economic, educational, scientific or research purposes in relation to fish or aquatic plants;

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph: (f) to publish or disclose information if, in the opinion of the minister, it would be in the public interest to publish or disclose that information.

heading: Power to collect or disclose information
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, information that may be collected or disclosed under subsection (1) (a) to (d) and (f) includes personal information.

heading: Power to delegate
paragraph:
47
		  (1) The minister may delegate, in writing, to a person or class of persons any of the minister's powers or duties under the following provisions:

heading: Power to delegate
paragraph: (a) section 17 [duty to keep records and make reports];

heading: Power to delegate
paragraph: (b) section 27 [recall orders];

heading: Power to delegate
paragraph: (c) section 46 [power to collect or disclose information].

heading: Power to delegate
paragraph: (2) A person to whom the minister delegates a power or duty referred to in subsection (1) may not further delegate the power or duty.

heading: General administrative powers
paragraph:
48
		  (1) The minister may make, by order, forms for the purposes of this Act and the regulations made under it, other than a form for the purposes of section 53 (3) [recovery of administrative penalties].

heading: General administrative powers
paragraph: (2) Unless the minister provides otherwise, use of a form made under subsection (1) is compulsory.

heading: General administrative powers
paragraph: (3) The minister may specify, by order, the manner in which applications, requests or reports may be made, or notices or information must be given, under this Act.

heading: General administrative powers
paragraph: (4) An application, a record or a report made under this Act must include all information the minister requires.

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph:
49
		  (1) A copy of a document issued under this Act by an inspector or the minister, and certified by the inspector or minister as a true copy, is

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph: (a) evidence of the document, and

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph: (b) evidence that the inspector or minister was authorized to issue the document.

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph: (2) In a proceeding under this Act, a certificate, as to the results of analyses, that is signed, or purports to be signed, by an analyst is

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph: (a) evidence of the facts stated in the certificate, and

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph: (b) evidence that the person who signed the certificate was authorized to sign the certificate.

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph: (3) Subsections (1) and (2) apply without proof of the person's signature, appointment or authorization.

heading: Documentary and certificate evidence
paragraph: (4) A person against whom a certificate under subsection (2) is produced may, with leave of the court, require for the purpose of cross examination the attendance of the analyst who signed the certificate.

heading: Inspector may seize offence-related things
paragraph:
50
		  (1) If, on inspection, an inspector reasonably believes that an offence under this Act has been committed, the inspector may seize anything that may constitute evidence of the offence.

heading: Inspector may seize offence-related things
paragraph: (2) If things seized under subsection (1) are fish or aquatic plants and the inspector reasonably believes the fish or aquatic plants are unsafe food, sections 26 (1) (b), (2) (b), (3) (a) and (b) and (4) [seizure and destruction] and 28 [costs] apply.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph:
51
		  (1) If authorized by regulation to impose an administrative penalty, the minister may impose an administrative penalty in the amount permitted by the regulations if satisfied on a balance of probabilities that a person has done either of the following:

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of this Act or a regulation made under it;

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with an order made under this Act.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) An administrative penalty may be imposed by serving notice of the administrative penalty in the prescribed manner.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) If a person is subject to an administrative penalty, the person must do one of the following within the prescribed time:

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) pay the administrative penalty;

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) dispute the administrative penalty in accordance with the regulations, including disputing the amount of the administrative penalty on any ground permitted by the regulations;

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) agree, in writing, with the minister to do one or more things, including paying a reduced administrative penalty, that the minister is of the opinion would

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (i)  be sufficient for the protection of public health in relation to unsafe food, and

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (ii)  if applicable, bring the person into compliance with this Act or the regulations or an order made under it.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) If an administrative penalty is disputed or made the subject of an agreement under subsection (3) (b) or (c), as the case may be, the person subject to the administrative penalty must pay the administrative penalty, or any part of it that remains outstanding,

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) under the terms of the agreement,

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) on receiving notice, following a dispute, that the person remains subject to all or part of the administrative penalty, or

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) on receiving notice that the person failed to meet the terms of the agreement to the satisfaction of the person who imposed the administrative penalty.

heading: Imposing administrative penalties
paragraph: (5) If a corporation contravenes this Act or a regulation made under it, or fails to comply with an order made under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure to comply is also liable under this section even though the corporation is liable for or pays an administrative penalty.

heading: Operator not to be subject to both administrative penalty and offence
paragraph:
52
		  (1) A person who must pay an administrative penalty must not be convicted of an offence in respect of the same incident that gave rise to the administrative penalty.

heading: Operator not to be subject to both administrative penalty and offence
paragraph: (2) A person convicted of an offence must not be required to pay an administrative penalty in respect of the same incident that gave rise to the conviction.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
53
		  (1) An administrative penalty under this Act may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required, the minister may file a certificate with a court that has jurisdiction, and, on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) must be in the prescribed form, be signed by the minister and contain

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the administrative penalty,

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) the contravention or failure in relation to which the administrative penalty is imposed, and

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the administrative penalty.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) All administrative penalties received under this Division must be paid into the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
54
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of the following provisions commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) section 3 [failure to ensure safe food];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) section 4 [failure to be licensed as required];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) section 5 [possession or distribution of unlawful fish or aquatic plants];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) section 6 [unlawful possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (e) section 14 [failure to comply with Act, regulations or licence];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (f) section 15 [failure to undertake preventive measures, analyses or monitoring or to train and equip employees];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (g) section 16 [failure to meet requirements respecting facilities, vehicles and equipment];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (h) section 17 [failure to keep or produce records or make reports as required];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (i) section 18 [failure to make reports or comply with orders respecting unsafe food];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (j) section 19 [failure to participate in traceability system as required];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (k) section 20 (a) [falsely holding oneself out as certified];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (l) section 20 (b) [failure to meet prescribed standards];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (m) section 35 [failure to comply with order];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (n) section 36 [unlawful removal, defacement or alteration of order, notice, mark or tag].

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who does either of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) knowingly gives false or misleading information to a person exercising powers or duties under this Act, or to a person acting under the order or direction of a person exercising powers or duties under this Act;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) wilfully interferes with, or obstructs, a person exercising powers or duties under this Act, or a person acting under the order or direction of a person exercising powers or duties under this Act.

heading: Other matters respecting offences
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A person who commits an offence under this Act may be liable for the offence whether or not an order is made under this Act in respect of the matter that is the subject of the offence.

heading: Other matters respecting offences
paragraph: (2) A proceeding for an offence under this Act may not be commenced in any court more than 2 years after the facts on which the proceeding is based first come to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Other matters respecting offences
paragraph: (3) A document purporting to have been issued by the minister, certifying the date on which the minister became aware of the facts on which a proceeding is based,

heading: Other matters respecting offences
paragraph: (a) is admissible without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the certificate, and

heading: Other matters respecting offences
paragraph: (b) is proof of the certified facts.

heading: Other matters respecting offences
paragraph: (4) If a person commits an offence under this Act and an order is made by an inspector in respect of the matter that is the subject of the offence, but the offence continues after the date by which the order is to be complied with, the person may be prosecuted both for the original offence and for the additional offence of contravening the order.

heading: Other matters respecting offences
paragraph: (5) Sections 4 and 5 of the Offence Act do not apply in respect of this Act or the regulations made under it.

heading: Offence by corporation or employee
paragraph: 56		  (1) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence whether or not the corporation is convicted.

heading: Offence by corporation or employee
paragraph: (2) If an employee commits an offence under this Act, an employer who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence whether or not the employee is identified or convicted.

heading: Penalties
paragraph:
57
		  (1) An individual who commits an offence under this Act is liable to the following:

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) on a first conviction, a fine of not more than $25 000 for each day or part of a day on which the offence occurs or continues;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) on each subsequent conviction, a fine of not more than $50 000 for each day or part of a day on which the offence occurs or continues;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (c) imprisonment for not more than 6 months;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (d) both the fine referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) and the imprisonment referred to in paragraph (c).

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (2) A corporation that commits an offence under this Act is liable to the following:

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) on a first conviction, a fine of not more than $100 000 for each day or part of a day on which the offence occurs or continues;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) on each subsequent conviction, a fine of not more than $200 000 for each day or part of a day on which the offence occurs or continues.

heading: Sentencing
paragraph:
58
		  (1) When sentencing a person convicted of an offence under this Act, the court may order the offender to pay compensation or make restitution to the government or a person for the actual loss or damage caused by or arising out of the commission of the offence, including, without limitation, compensation or restitution for any costs incurred in relation to

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (a) any inspection related to an investigation of the offence, and

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (b) an investigation of the offence.

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (2) When sentencing a person convicted of an offence under this Act, the court may order that any fish or aquatic plants in relation to which the offence was committed are forfeited, without compensation to any person, to the government and may be disposed of or destroyed as the minister may direct.

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (3) An order for compensation or restitution under subsection (1) or forfeiture under subsection (2) is in addition to and not in place of any other fine or penalty under this Act.

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (4) If an order is made under subsection (1) in favour of the government or a person,

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (a) the government or person may, by filing the order in a registry of the Supreme Court, enter as a judgment the amount ordered to be paid, and

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (b) that judgment is enforceable against the offender in the same manner as if it were a judgment against that offender in civil proceedings in that court.

heading: Sentencing
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this section precludes the government or any person from taking any civil action or exercising any right of recovery against a person who commits an offence under this Act.

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph:
59
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (a) prescribing species of fish or aquatic plants to which this Act does not apply;

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (b) respecting standards that must be met or measures that must be taken for the purposes of section 3 (2) [duty to ensure food safety];

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (c) exempting classes of persons from a requirement to hold a licence under this Act, including

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (i)  exempting persons who, under the Food Safety Act, the Public Health Act or an enactment of Canada, hold or are required to hold a licence or permit, or are registered or are required to be registered, in relation to a class of activities or facilities,

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (ii)  making exemptions based on the type of activities being carried out or the circumstances in which the activities are carried out,

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (iii)  putting limits or conditions on an exemption, and

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (iv)  requiring an exempted person to comply with one or more provisions of Division 2 [Duties of Operators] of Part 3 as if the person were an operator;

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (d) prescribing fish and aquatic plants for the purposes of section 6 [possession or distribution of restricted fish or aquatic plants];

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (e) respecting applications for, renewals of and the issuance of permits for the purposes of section 6 (2) (b), including

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (i)  requiring a fee to be paid on application or renewal, and

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (ii)  applying or modifying any provision of Part 3 [Licensing and Duties of Operators] or a regulation made under section 60 [regulations respecting operators] as if the permit were a licence and the holder of the permit were an operator.

heading: Regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe, in a regulation made under subsection (1) (d), products or byproducts of fish or aquatic plants that are not themselves prescribed.

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: 60		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the licensing of operators as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (a) requiring persons to be licensed to do one or more of the activities described in section 2 [activities to which this Act applies];

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (b) respecting applications and renewals;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (c) requiring certification under section 20 [duties if certification program prescribed] as a condition of licensing;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (d) prescribing factors that may or must be considered in determining whether to issue a licence;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (e) respecting terms and conditions that may be attached to a licence;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (f) prescribing fees for applications, variations, renewals and reviews of licensing decisions, and prescribing different fees based on

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (i)  the class of licence,

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (ii)  the species of fish or aquatic plants to which the licence will apply, or

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (iii)  the class or size of facilities used for the purpose of doing the activity to which the licence will apply;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (g) respecting actions operators must take during a suspension or cancellation of a licence, or after a cancellation of a licence, in relation to their facilities or the fish or aquatic plants in their possession or control.

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the duties of operators as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (a) prohibiting matters in respect of the activities described in section 2, and regulating, restricting or putting conditions on the performance of those activities;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (b) respecting analyses and monitoring for the purposes of section 15 (2) [duties with respect to food safety], including requiring samples to be submitted for analyses;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (c) without limiting section 59 (1) (b) [regulations respecting application of Act and general prohibitions], respecting standards that must be met or measures that must be taken in relation to the safety and quality of fish and aquatic plants;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (d) respecting information that must be given by an operator to the government or the public about fish or aquatic plants that an operator distributes, has distributed or intends to distribute;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (e) respecting the disposition of unsafe food by an operator, including prohibiting and putting conditions on the disposition;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (f) without limiting section 61 (2) (c) [regulations respecting traceability and certification], respecting training and qualifications for operators and employees, including

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (i)  requiring ongoing training, and

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (ii)  setting examinations and charging fees for taking examinations;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (g) respecting the construction, maintenance, management, sanitation and operation of facilities, vehicles and equipment used by operators while the operators do an activity for which the operators are licensed;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (h) respecting the making, keeping and production of records by an operator;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (i) respecting the making of reports by an operator and the actions that the minister may require an operator to take on making a report, including requiring monitoring, making records, conducting analyses or submitting samples for analyses;

heading: Regulations respecting operators
paragraph: (j) respecting royalties payable by an operator who harvests wild aquatic plants.

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph:
61
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of section 19 [duty to participate in traceability system] as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (a) prescribing traceability systems and traceability programs in respect of which section 19 applies;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (b) respecting unique identifiers, including respecting fees for the issuance of unique identifiers and their replacement;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (c) respecting the making of reports, including

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (i)  prescribing persons to whom reports must be made or persons who must receive a copy of a report,

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (ii)  respecting the form of a report and the manner of making the report,

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (iii)  respecting information, in addition to anything described in this Act, that must be reported, and

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (iv)  respecting records or analyses that must accompany a report;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (d) respecting actions that must be taken by a person subject to section 19 (4), including conducting analyses or submitting traceable food or samples for analyses;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (e) prohibiting or putting conditions on the distribution or disposition of traceable food;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (f) respecting audits of traceability systems and traceability programs;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (g) respecting the types of, the linking and disclosure of, and access to information kept in respect of a traceability system or traceability program;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (h) respecting the participation by British Columbia in extrajurisdictional traceability systems or extrajurisdictional traceability programs;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (i) authorizing the collection, use and disclosure of information contained in the assessment roll, as that term is defined in the Assessment Act, for the purpose of a traceability system or traceability program.

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting certification programs as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (a) prescribing certification programs;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (b) respecting applications and fees for certification;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (c) respecting the training and qualifications an operator must have to be certified, including requiring a licence or certification under another enactment or an enactment of the government of Canada;

heading: Regulations respecting traceability and certification
paragraph: (d) respecting standards that a certified operator must meet.

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: 62		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting inspections as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (a) authorizing further purposes for which an inspection may be made;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (b) requiring a person who is subject to an order to pay a fee for each inspection conducted for the purpose of monitoring or confirming compliance with the order;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (c) prescribing fees for the purposes of paragraph (b).

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting orders made under this Act as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (a) respecting measures that an inspector may require to be taken by order for the purposes of section 25 (1) (m) [orders that may be made];

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (b) respecting the contents of an order;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (c) respecting service of orders, including service by posting or publishing notice of the order or by any other means;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (d) respecting reassessments under section 31 [variation and reassessment of orders], including limiting the circumstances in which and how often a request may be made;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (e) prescribing fees for reviews of orders, and prescribing different fees based on

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (i)  the provision of this Act or of a regulation under which the order was made,

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (ii)  the class of licence held by the person who is subject to the order,

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (iii)  the species of fish or aquatic plants to which the order will apply, or

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (iv)  the class or size of facilities to which the order will apply;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (f) respecting the publication of orders, including the disclosure of information in respect of an order.

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting enforcement as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (a) respecting the process for making an application to the court, including

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (i)  authorizing applications to be made electronically or by any other means,

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (ii)  respecting the giving of notice of an application, and

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (iii)  respecting affidavits or other evidence that must accompany an application;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (b) prescribing the rules that apply to the hearing of an application by the court, including providing that the Supreme Court Civil Rules apply with or without modification;

heading: Regulations respecting enforcement
paragraph: (c) prescribing the form of a warrant for the purposes of section 37 [warrants].

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph:
63
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting administrative penalties under Division 2 [Administrative Penalties] of Part 6 as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) authorizing the imposition of administrative penalties;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) prescribing provisions of this Act or the regulations made under it in respect of which administrative penalties may be imposed;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) respecting an administrative penalty that may be imposed in respect of any failure to comply with a provision of this Act, including

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (i)  providing for greater penalties for subsequent contraventions,

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (ii)  setting the maximum and minimum penalties that may be imposed,

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (iii)  providing, if the penalty is expressed as a range, factors to be considered in the determination of the appropriate penalty, and

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (iv)  prescribing the grounds on which a penalty may be reduced;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (d) respecting notices for the purposes of that Division, including the form, content and service of notices;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (e) prescribing the time in which an administrative penalty must be paid, disputed or made the subject of an agreement, including the time in which the penalty must be paid following a dispute, an agreement or a failure to meet the terms of an agreement;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (f) providing for payment, by instalments, of an administrative penalty;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (g) respecting disputes of administrative penalties, including

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (i)  providing for a reconsideration of the penalty, and

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (ii)  authorizing a reconsideration of the penalty to be considered together with a reconsideration of an order made under this Act;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (h) respecting the form of a certificate under section 53 (3) [recovery of administrative penalties].

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) A penalty prescribed under subsection (1) (c) must not be greater than $25 000.

heading: Other regulation-making powers
paragraph:
64
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations exempting a class of persons, fish, aquatic plants, facilities or things from one or more provisions of the regulations.

heading: Other regulation-making powers
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting service and deemed receipt of a notice that an inspector or the minister must give under this Act.

heading: Other regulation-making powers
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing fees for the purposes of section 44 (3) [power to retain other persons].

heading: Other regulation-making powers
paragraph: (4) To the extent that regulation-making authority has not already been provided for in this Part, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting any matter for which regulations are contemplated by this Act.

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph:
65
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (2) A person must not read any section of this Part as limiting the general powers to make regulations described in subsection (1) of this section or as limiting the specific powers to make regulations described in each section of this Part.

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under this Act may

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (a) establish classes of persons, fish, aquatic plants, facilities, things or activities to which this Act applies, and

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (b) make regulations that are different for different classes.

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (4) A regulation made under this Act may limit the application of the regulation

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (a) to one or more geographic areas, and

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (b) to one or more classes of persons, fish, aquatic plants, facilities, things or activities to which this Act applies.

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (5) A regulation made under this Act may confer a discretion on the minister, a licensing officer, a reviewing officer or an inspector.

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (6) A regulation made under this Act may adopt by reference, in whole or in part and with any changes the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers appropriate, a regulation, code, standard or rule

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (a) enacted as or under a law of another jurisdiction, including a foreign jurisdiction, or

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (b) set by a provincial, national or international body or any other body that may make codes, standards or rules.

heading: General powers respecting regulations
paragraph: (7) If, in a regulation made under this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council provides that contravention of the regulation is an offence, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide that a person who commits the offence is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $75 000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 6 months, or to both.
