paragraph: 75		  This Act comes into force by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Fish and Seafood Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "applicant" includes an applicant to renew a licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic plant culturer" means a person who holds an aquatic plant culture licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic plant group" means a group of aquatic plant species as described in the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic plant species" means a species of aquatic plant as described in the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "bivalve mollusc" means all or part of a shellfish of the phylum Mollusca, class Bivalvia, commonly known as a clam, oyster, scallop or mussel, whether or not the shellfish has been shucked;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cold storage facility" means a facility used primarily for the purpose of freezing fish or storing frozen fish;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commercial fisher" means a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) holds a fisher's registration card as described in Item 1 of Part I of Schedule II to the Pacific Fishery Regulations, 1993 (Canada),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) holds a commercial fishing licence of a category described in Item 3 of Part I of Schedule II to the Pacific Fishery Regulations, 1993 (Canada), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is designated as a person who is authorized to fish under a communal licence issued under the Aboriginal Communal Fishing Licences Regulations (Canada) and who distributes fish for a commercial purpose;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "container" means any form of container or packaging used in relation to fish or aquatic plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "contaminated" has the meaning set out in section 3 (3) of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "equipment" includes containers, utensils and any items used to carry out an activity under a licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "federal licence" means a licence or other authorization issued under a federal enactment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish receiver" means a person who holds a fish receiver licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fisher vendor" means a person who holds a fisher vendor licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "food contact surface" means that part of equipment with which fish or aquatic plants normally come into contact;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fresh", in relation to fish, means dead but not frozen;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "harvest agreement" means the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a harvest agreement within the meaning of settlement legislation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an agreement described in section 7 of the Nisga'a Final Agreement Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "harvest plan proposal" means a harvest plan proposal made in accordance with section 10 [harvest plan proposal];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licence", in relation to a licence issued under this regulation, means one or more of the following, as applicable in the context:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an aquatic plant culture licence issued with respect to activities described in section 3 [aquatic plant culture licence];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a wild aquatic plant harvester licence issued with respect to activities described in section 8 [wild aquatic plant harvester licence];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a fisher vendor licence issued with respect to activities described in section 16 [fisher vendor licence];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a fish receiver licence issued with respect to activities described in section 21 [fish receiver licence];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a seafood processor licence issued with respect to activities described in section 27 [seafood processor licence];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licensed facility" means a facility used by a person who holds a licence for the purpose of carrying out activities authorized by the person's licence, whether or not the facility is specifically referenced in the licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "provincial food enactment" means the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the Food Safety Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the Public Health Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a regulation made under the Food Safety Act or the Public Health Act with respect to the processing or distribution of food for public consumption;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "seafood processor" means a person who holds a seafood processor licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transport" includes to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) load for transport, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) unload after transport;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transporter" means a person who transports fish or aquatic plants that may be distributed to the public for human consumption, whether or not the transporter holds a licence under this regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wild aquatic plant harvester" means a person who holds a wild aquatic plant harvester licence.

heading: Seafood present in licensed facility
paragraph: 2		  Fish and aquatic plants present in a licensed facility are deemed to be intended for distribution to the public for human consumption, unless an inspector is satisfied that the fish and aquatic plants will not be distributed to the public for human consumption.

heading: Aquatic plant culture licence
paragraph:
3
		  A person must not grow aquatic plants that may be distributed to the public for human consumption unless the person

heading: Aquatic plant culture licence
paragraph: (a) holds an aquatic plant culture licence, or

heading: Aquatic plant culture licence
paragraph: (b) is an employee, acting in the course of employment, of a person who holds an aquatic plant culture licence.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph:
4
		  Subject to section 7 (4) of the Act, an applicant for an aquatic plant culture licence must include with the application a fee of $50.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph:
5
		  (1) An aquatic plant culture licence expires on the date set by a licensing officer under section 7 (2) (d) of the Act.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph: (2) A licensing officer may not set a licence term under subsection (1) for a period longer than 10 years.

heading: Aquatic plant culturer records
paragraph:
6
		  An aquatic plant culturer must keep records that include at least the following information:

heading: Aquatic plant culturer records
paragraph: (a) a description of the aquatic plants grown, divided according to aquatic plant group and aquatic plant species;

heading: Aquatic plant culturer records
paragraph: (b) the quantity of aquatic plants grown;

heading: Aquatic plant culturer records
paragraph: (c) with respect to each delivery of aquatic plants distributed by the aquatic plant culturer,

heading: Aquatic plant culturer records
paragraph: (i)  the quantity of aquatic plants distributed,

heading: Aquatic plant culturer records
paragraph: (ii)  the contact information of the person to whom aquatic plants were distributed, and

heading: Aquatic plant culturer records
paragraph: (iii)  the amount received for the aquatic plants.

heading: Waivers by licensing officers
paragraph:
7
		  The following powers of a licensing officer may not be exercised with respect to a class of persons:

heading: Waivers by licensing officers
paragraph: (a) to waive a requirement under this Division;

heading: Waivers by licensing officers
paragraph: (b) to set a different schedule under section 15 (3) [submission of harvest records and royalties].

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A person must not harvest wild aquatic plants that may be distributed to the public for human consumption unless the person

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (a) holds a wild aquatic plant harvester licence,

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (b) is an employee, acting in the course of employment, of a person who holds a wild aquatic plant harvester licence,

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (c) is exempt under subsection (3) or is an employee, acting in the course of employment, of a person who is exempt under subsection (3), or

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (d) is exempt under subsection (5) or (6).

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (2) A person who possesses 100 kg of aquatic plants or more, measured while wet, is deemed to have harvested the aquatic plants for the purpose of distribution to the public for human consumption.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), a person is exempt from the requirement to hold a wild aquatic plant harvester licence if

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (a) a licensing officer waives that requirement,

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (b) harvested aquatic plants will be used for an educational or experimental purpose only, and

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (c) harvested aquatic plants will not be further used for a commercial purpose.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (4) A person who is exempt, under subsection (3), from the requirement to hold a licence must comply with section 13 [harvest of aquatic plants] as if the person were a wild aquatic plant harvester.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (5) A person is exempt from the requirement to hold a wild aquatic plant harvester licence if the person harvests wild aquatic plants only

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (a) for a food, social or ceremonial purpose,

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (i)  further to an aboriginal right, or

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (ii)  in accordance with a provision of a final agreement with a treaty first nation or the Nisga'a Final Agreement, and

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (b) in accordance with all applicable Nisga'a laws or laws made by a treaty first nation, if any.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (6) A person is exempt from the requirement to hold a wild aquatic plant harvester licence if

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (a) a harvest agreement that applies to the person provides that a licence is not required, and

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (b) the person harvests wild aquatic plants only in accordance with

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (i)  a harvest agreement, and

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester licence
paragraph: (ii)  all applicable Nisga'a laws or laws made by a treaty first nation, if any.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Subject to section 7 (4) of the Act and subsection (2) of this section, an applicant for a wild aquatic plant harvester licence must include with the application

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (a) a fee of $110, and

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (b) a harvest plan proposal, if required by a licensing officer.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (2) If a person is required under a harvest agreement to hold a wild aquatic plant harvester licence, the person

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (a) must include with the application for the licence a fee and a harvest plan proposal in accordance with the terms and conditions of the harvest agreement, or

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (b) is exempt from the requirement to submit

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (i)  an application fee if the harvest agreement provides that no fee is payable for the licence, and

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (ii)  a harvest plan proposal if the harvest agreement provides that a licensing officer may not request a harvest plan proposal.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (3) For a licence to be issued with respect to the following year, an applicant must apply for the licence on or before October 1 unless

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (a) a licensing officer waives this requirement, or

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (b) a harvest agreement provides otherwise.

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph:
10
		  (1) In determining whether to issue a wild aquatic plant harvester licence, a licensing officer must consider the management of aquatic plant resources.

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1) but subject to section 9 (2) (b) (ii) [application for wild aquatic plant harvester licence], a licensing officer may require an applicant to submit a harvest plan proposal.

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (3) A harvest plan proposal must include at least the following:

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (a) scientific information, including data, respecting

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (i)  the distribution and quantity of the aquatic plants to be harvested in the proposed harvest area, divided according to aquatic plant group and aquatic plant species, and

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (ii)  the environment and ecology of the proposed harvest area;

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (b) a description of the proposed method of harvesting aquatic plants and the equipment to be used;

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (c) a description, based on scientific information and including data, of the potential adverse effects of the proposed harvest on the environment and ecology of the proposed harvest area;

heading: Harvest plan proposal
paragraph: (d) any additional information required by the licensing officer.

heading: Terms and conditions on licence
paragraph:
11
		  (1) Without limiting section 7 (2) (d) of the Act but subject to the terms and conditions of an applicable harvest agreement, if any, a licensing officer may impose limits or conditions on a wild aquatic plant harvester licence with respect to the following:

heading: Terms and conditions on licence
paragraph: (a) the geographic area within which harvesting of aquatic plants may occur;

heading: Terms and conditions on licence
paragraph: (b) the quantity of aquatic plants that may be harvested;

heading: Terms and conditions on licence
paragraph: (c) the aquatic plants that may be harvested, described by aquatic plant groups, aquatic plant species or both.

heading: Terms and conditions on licence
paragraph: (2) Without limiting section 7 (2) (d) of the Act or subsection (1) of this section, a licensing officer who receives a harvest plan proposal may

heading: Terms and conditions on licence
paragraph: (a) impose limits or conditions on a wild aquatic plant harvester licence with respect to harvesting equipment, the methods of harvest or both, and

heading: Terms and conditions on licence
paragraph: (b) require the harvest plan proposal to be modified and implemented according to the licensing officer's directions.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph:
12
		  (1) A wild aquatic plant harvester licence expires

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph: (a) on the date set by a licensing officer under section 7 (2) (d) of the Act, or

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph: (b) according to the terms and conditions of an applicable harvest agreement, if any.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph: (2) A licensing officer may not set a licence term under subsection (1) (a) for a period longer than 3 years.

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph:
13
		  (1) In this section, "holdfast" means that part of an aquatic plant by which the aquatic plant is attached to the substrate.

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (2) A wild aquatic plant harvester must ensure that aquatic plants are not harvested under a wild aquatic plant harvester licence except in accordance with this section.

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (3) Unless permitted in writing by a licensing officer or under the terms and conditions of an applicable harvest agreement, if any, the following harvest methods are prohibited:

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (a) harvesting by raking, dredging or diving;

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (b) harvesting by any method that impairs

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (i)  the regrowth of the aquatic plant, including practices that harvest the holdfast itself or strain, break or tear the aquatic plant from all or part of the holdfast, or

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (ii)  the integrity of the aquatic plant bed within the area permitted to be harvested;

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (c) harvesting detached aquatic plants from the foreshore in any manner that disturbs or exposes the substrate.

heading: Harvest of aquatic plants
paragraph: (4) Unless permitted in writing by a licensing officer or under the terms and conditions of an applicable harvest agreement, if any, harvesting must be done by hand, using a sharp cutting instrument.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph:
14
		  (1) A wild aquatic plant harvester must keep records in accordance with

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (a) this section, or

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (b) the terms of an applicable harvest agreement, if any.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (2) A harvest record must include at least the following information with respect to each harvest made during the term of the licence:

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (a) the licence number;

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (b) the date and location of the harvest;

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (c) the aquatic plant species harvested;

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (d) the weight of the harvest

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (i)  divided according to aquatic plant species,

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (ii)  measured while the aquatic plants are wet, and

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (iii)  expressed in tonnes, to the nearest tenth of a tonne.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (3) If no harvest was made during the term of the licence, the harvest record must include the licence number and a statement indicating that no harvest was made.

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (4) A distribution record must include at least the following information with respect to each delivery of aquatic plants distributed by the wild aquatic plant harvester:

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (a) the quantity, expressed in tonnes, of aquatic plants distributed;

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (b) the contact information of the person to whom aquatic plants were distributed;

heading: Wild aquatic plant harvester records
paragraph: (c) the amount received for the aquatic plants.

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph:
15
		  (1) Subject to the terms and conditions of an applicable harvest agreement, if any, a wild aquatic plant harvester must submit to a licensing officer, in accordance with this section,

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (a) the harvest records prepared under section 14 [wild aquatic plant harvester records], and

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (b) a royalty payment determined in accordance with subsection (4).

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), harvest records and royalty payments must be submitted as follows:

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (a) within 10 days after harvesting under the licence ends or the licence expires, whichever is earliest;

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (b) if the term of the licence is for more than one year,

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (i)  before December 31 of the first year of the term and

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (ii)  annually after the first submission, until paragraph (a) applies.

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (3) Without limiting section 7 (2) (d) of the Act, a licensing officer may require harvest records and royalty payments to be submitted sooner or more often than would be required under subsection (2), and may set a schedule for this purpose.

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (4) With respect to each tonne or part of a tonne, measured while wet, of aquatic plants harvested from each aquatic plant group, the amount of the royalty payment owing is as follows:

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (a) for aquatic plants within aquatic plant group 1, 2 or 5, $10;

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (b) for aquatic plants within aquatic plant group 3, 4 or 7 to 9, $50;

heading: Submission of harvest record and royalties
paragraph: (c) for aquatic plants within aquatic plant group 6, $100.

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph:
16
		  (1) A commercial fisher must not distribute the commercial fisher's catch to a person unless the commercial fisher

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (a) holds a fisher vendor licence and distributes the catch only

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (i)  to a person holding a licence or other authorization under a provincial food enactment, or

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (ii)  to a person directly from the vessel from which the catch was harvested,

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (b) is exempt under subsection (2), or

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (c) is an employee, acting in the course of employment, of a person referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (2) A commercial fisher is exempt from the requirement to hold a fisher vendor licence if the commercial fisher distributes fish only as follows:

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (a) to a fish receiver or a seafood processor;

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (b) to a person who holds a federal licence to

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (i)  possess, process, store or transport fish, or

heading: Fisher vendor licence
paragraph: (ii)  operate a cold storage facility that stores frozen fish.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph:
17
		  Subject to section 7 (4) of the Act, an applicant for a fisher vendor licence must include with the application a fee of $30.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph:
18
		  (1) A fisher vendor licence expires on the date set by a licensing officer under section 7 (2) (d) of the Act.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph: (2) A licensing officer may not set a licence term under subsection (1) for a period longer than one year.

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph:
19
		  (1) A fisher vendor must comply with the following provisions as if the fisher vendor were a seafood processor:

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (a) section 32 (1) (b) [general construction requirements];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (b) section 33 [washrooms and hand washing stations], unless only containers of fish are handled and not the fish themselves;

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (c) section 34 [maintenance of licensed facility];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (d) section 35 (b) [pests];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (e) section 36 [equipment and food contact surfaces];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (f) section 37 [cold storage equipment];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (g) section 38 [protection of food];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (h) section 40 [temperature, water and ice standards];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (i) section 42 (a) [sanitation];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (j) section 43 [hygiene];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (k) section 44 [illnesses];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (l) section 45 [animals];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (m) section 49 [no storage of unnecessary items].

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (2) If a provision referred to in subsection (1) applies to an employee, the provision is deemed to also apply to the fisher vendor while the fisher vendor is

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (a) present in the fisher vendor's licensed facility, or

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fisher vendors
paragraph: (b) personally engaging in activities under the fisher vendor's licence.

heading: Fisher vendor records
paragraph:
20
		  A fisher vendor must keep records with respect to each delivery of fish distributed by the fisher vendor that include at least the following information:

heading: Fisher vendor records
paragraph: (a) the contact information of the person to whom fish were distributed, if that person is a person described in section 16 (1) (a) (i) or (2) (a) or (b) [fisher vendor licence];

heading: Fisher vendor records
paragraph: (b) the date of distribution;

heading: Fisher vendor records
paragraph: (c) the quantity of fish distributed, divided according to species;

heading: Fisher vendor records
paragraph: (d) the amount received for fish distributed.

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A person must not possess, store or transport fish the person receives directly from a commercial fisher and that may be distributed to the public for human consumption unless the person

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (a) holds a fish receiver licence,

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (b) is exempt under subsection (2), or

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (c) is an employee, acting in the course of employment, of a person referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement to hold a fish receiver licence if one of the following applies:

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (a) the person holds a licence or other authorization under a provincial food enactment and receives fish directly from a fisher vendor;

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (b) the person holds a seafood processor licence;

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (c) the person holds a federal licence to

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (i)  possess, process, store or transport fish or aquatic plants, or

heading: Fish receiver licence
paragraph: (ii)  operate a cold storage facility that stores frozen fish.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph:
22
		  Subject to section 7 (4) of the Act, an applicant for a fish receiver licence must include with the application a fee as follows:

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (a) to receive salmon, $230;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (b) to receive fin fish other than salmon, $150;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (c) to receive roe herring, $230;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (d) to receive invertebrates, $150.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph:
23
		  (1) A fish receiver licence expires on the date set by a licensing officer under section 7 (2) (d) of the Act.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph: (2) A licensing officer may not set a licence term under subsection (1) for a period longer than one year.

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph:
24
		  (1) A fish receiver must comply with the following provisions as if the fish receiver were a seafood processor:

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (a) section 32 (1) (b), (2) (a) and (3) [general construction requirements];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (b) section 33 [washrooms and hand washing stations], unless only containers of fish are handled and not the fish themselves;

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (c) section 34 [maintenance of licensed facility];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (d) section 35 [pests], except that if the licensed facility is not fully enclosed, only section 35 (b) applies;

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (e) section 36 [equipment and food contact surfaces];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (f) section 37 [cold storage equipment];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (g) section 38 [protection of food];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (h) section 40 [temperature, water and ice standards];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (i) section 42 (a) [sanitation];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (j) section 43 [hygiene];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (k) section 44 [illnesses];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (l) section 45 [animals];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (m) section 46 (a) [storage of chemicals];

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (n) section 49 [no storage of unnecessary items].

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (2) If a provision referred to in subsection (1) applies to an employee, the provision is deemed to also apply to the fish receiver while the fish receiver is

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (a) present in the fish receiver's licensed facility, or

heading: Part 6 requirements applicable to fish receivers
paragraph: (b) personally engaging in activities under the fish receiver's licence.

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph:
25
		  (1) A fish receiver must keep records, in accordance with this section, with respect to each delivery of fish

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (a) received by the fish receiver, and

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (b) distributed by the fish receiver.

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (2) Records must include at least the following information:

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (a) if applicable, the federal licence number of the person from whom fish were received;

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (b) the contact information of the person

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (i)  from whom fish were received, or

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (ii)  to whom fish were distributed;

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (c) the date and location of receipt or distribution;

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (d) the quantity of fish received or distributed, divided according to species and, if processed, manner of processing;

heading: Fish receiver records
paragraph: (e) the amount paid or received for fish received or distributed.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
26
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cultured fish" means fish that have been raised domestically under a federal licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pest" means any animal, whether vertebrate or invertebrate, that is potentially harmful to the sanitary operation of a licensed facility;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sanitize" means to treat equipment by any method that destroys disease-causing micro-organisms for the purpose of preventing fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sport caught fish" means fish that have been harvested

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) under a tidal water sport fishing licence issued under section 17 of the British Columbia Sport Fishing Regulations, 1996 (Canada), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in accordance with section 15 (1) of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Seafood processor licence
paragraph: 27		  A person must not process fish or aquatic plants, or operate a cold storage facility that stores frozen fish, that may be distributed to the public for human consumption unless the person

heading: Seafood processor licence
paragraph: (a) holds a seafood processor licence,

heading: Seafood processor licence
paragraph: (b) is exempt under section 28 [exemptions from licence requirement], or

heading: Seafood processor licence
paragraph: (c) is an employee, acting in the course of employment, of a person referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph:
28
		  (1) In this section, "exempt" means exempt, under this section, from the requirement to hold a seafood processor licence.

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (2) A commercial fisher is exempt if the commercial fisher

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (a) only stuns, bleeds, heads, eviscerates, ices, freezes or packages fish, and

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (b) engages in the processing activities referred to in paragraph (a) only

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (i)  while at sea and aboard the commercial fisher's own vessel, and

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (ii)  with respect to the commercial fisher's own catch.

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (3) A fish receiver is exempt if the fish receiver only ices fish received under that fish receiver's licence.

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (4) A person who holds a licence or other authorization under a provincial food enactment is exempt if the person processes fish or aquatic plants, or operates a cold storage facility that stores frozen fish, only in connection with the activities regulated under the enactment.

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (5) A person is exempt if the person

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (a) only stuns, bleeds, heads, eviscerates, fillets, ices, freezes or packages sport caught fish, and

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (b) engages in the processing activities referred to in paragraph (a) only for the person who caught the fish.

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (6) A person is exempt if the person holds a federal licence to

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (a) process fish or aquatic plants, or

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (b) operate a cold storage facility that stores frozen fish.

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (7) A person who raises cultured fish by freshwater aquaculture is exempt if the person

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (a) only stuns, bleeds, heads, eviscerates, ices or packages the person's own cultured fish, and

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (b) distributes the cultured fish only

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (i)  to a person who holds a seafood processor licence, or

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (ii)  to the public from the place where the fish are raised, at a seasonal farmer's market or similar temporary location.

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (8) A person who raises cultured fish by marine aquaculture is exempt if the person

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (a) only stuns, bleeds, or ices the person's own cultured fish, and

heading: Exemptions from licence requirement
paragraph: (b) distributes the cultured fish only to a person who holds a federal licence to process fish.

heading: Conditions of exemption
paragraph:
29
		  (1) A person who is exempt under section 28 (6) must comply with all of the following as if the exempt person were a seafood processor:

heading: Conditions of exemption
paragraph: (a) Division 6 [Records Requirements] of this Part;

heading: Conditions of exemption
paragraph: (b) section 66 [reporting information to minister].

heading: Conditions of exemption
paragraph: (2) A person who is exempt under section 28 (7) or (8) must comply with both of the following as if the exempt person were a fisher vendor:

heading: Conditions of exemption
paragraph: (a) section 20 [fisher vendor records];

heading: Conditions of exemption
paragraph: (b) section 66.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph:
30
		  (1) Subject to section 7 (4) of the Act, an applicant for a seafood processor licence must include with the application a fee as follows:

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (a) to only freeze or store frozen fish,

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (i)  $420, if the cold storage facility has a capacity of more than 80 m3, or

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (ii)  $110, if the cold storage facility has a capacity of 80 m3 or less;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (b) to process salmon by canning,

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (i)  $1 800, if 32.66 tonnes or more is intended to be packaged, or

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (ii)  $900, if less than 32.66 tonnes is intended to be packaged;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (c) to process salmon, if paragraph (a), (b) or (e) does not apply, $640;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (d) if paragraph (a) or (e) does not apply,

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (i)  to process fin fish other than salmon or roe herring, $290,

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (ii)  to process roe herring, $640,

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (iii)  to process invertebrates, $290, and

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (iv)  to process freshwater fish, $50;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (e) to process sport caught fish, $210;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (f) to process aquatic plants, $210.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (2) An applicant must include with the application a copy of the design and construction plans, including specifications, as follows:

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (a) if applying for a new seafood processor licence, for the facility to which the application relates;

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (b) if applying to renew a seafood processor licence, of any alterations made to the licensed facility during the most recent term of the licence.

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (3) An applicant must submit a separate fee with respect to

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (a) each facility in which or on which the applicant intends to operate under the licence, whether or not all or part of the facility is also used by another person or for another purpose, and

heading: Application for licence
paragraph: (b) each activity referred to in subsection (1) in which the applicant intends to engage under the licence.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph:
31
		  (1) A seafood processor licence expires on the date set by a licensing officer under section 7 (2) (d) of the Act.

heading: Expiry of licence
paragraph: (2) A licensing officer may not set a licence term under subsection (1) for a period longer than one year.

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph:
32
		  (1) A seafood processor must ensure that all of the following requirements are met with respect to the seafood processor's licensed facility:

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (a) the licensed facility is designed so as to ensure that activities carried out under the licence will be carried out in a manner that prevents fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food;

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (b) the licensed facility is constructed from materials that are

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (i)  suitable for their intended purpose, and

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (ii)  durable, easily cleaned and free from any noxious or toxic substance;

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (c) there is no direct access between the licensed facility and

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (i)  living quarters, or

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (ii)  areas in which activities are carried out that are incompatible with meeting the duty set out in section 38 [protection of food];

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (d) the licensed facility is of sound construction overall.

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor's licensed facility is equipped with both of the following:

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (a) artificial lighting adequate in intensity and designed or protected to permit activities carried out under the licence to be carried out in a manner that will prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food;

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (b) ventilation equipment that prevents the accumulation of smoke, grease, water vapour and objectionable odours.

heading: General construction requirements
paragraph: (3) A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor's licensed facility is connected to, or that employees have ready access to, a waste disposal system that cannot cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food.

heading: Washrooms and hand washing stations
paragraph:
33
		  A seafood processor must ensure that employees of the seafood processor's licensed facility have ready access to washrooms and hand washing stations that

heading: Washrooms and hand washing stations
paragraph: (a) are adequate in number for all employees,

heading: Washrooms and hand washing stations
paragraph: (b) have hot and cold running water, and

heading: Washrooms and hand washing stations
paragraph: (c) are equipped with soap in a dispenser and a method of hand drying that uses single service products.

heading: Maintenance of licensed facility
paragraph:
34
		  A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor's licensed facility is maintained so as to ensure that fish and aquatic plants cannot become unsafe food.

heading: Pests
paragraph:
35
		  A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor's licensed facility is constructed and maintained so as to be

heading: Pests
paragraph: (a) free, to the greatest extent possible, of pests,

heading: Pests
paragraph: (b) free of conditions that lead to the harbouring or breeding of pests, and

heading: Pests
paragraph: (c) protected against the entrance of pests.

heading: Equipment and food contact surfaces
paragraph:
36
		  A seafood processor must ensure that all equipment in the seafood processor's licensed facility meets all of the following requirements:

heading: Equipment and food contact surfaces
paragraph: (a) the equipment is constructed from materials that

heading: Equipment and food contact surfaces
paragraph: (i)  are durable and suitable for their intended purpose, and

heading: Equipment and food contact surfaces
paragraph: (ii)  ensure that food contact surfaces are easily cleaned and free from any noxious or toxic substance,

heading: Equipment and food contact surfaces
paragraph: (b) the equipment is in good working order, and

heading: Equipment and food contact surfaces
paragraph: (c) the equipment is used in a manner that will prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

heading: Cold storage equipment
paragraph:
37
		  (1) A seafood processor must ensure that refrigeration equipment in the seafood processor's licensed facility meets all of the following requirements:

heading: Cold storage equipment
paragraph: (a) the equipment is adequate, in both type and capacity, to meet the needs of the persons carrying out activities under the licence;

heading: Cold storage equipment
paragraph: (b) the equipment is capable of maintaining temperatures necessary to comply with section 40 (1) [temperature standards];

heading: Cold storage equipment
paragraph: (c) the equipment is equipped with a device to measure temperature that is accurate to within 1°C.

heading: Cold storage equipment
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must ensure that the temperature inside refrigeration equipment in the seafood processor's licensed facility is measured and recorded at least once in each 24 hour period.

heading: Protection of food
paragraph:
38
		  A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor's licensed facility is operated, and activities carried out under the licence are conducted, in a manner that will prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph:
39
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: "critical control point" means a procedural step, when carrying out activities under a licence, at which an action can be taken to prevent, eliminate, or reduce to an acceptable level, the risk of fish and aquatic plants becoming unsafe food;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: "critical limit" means a threshold, limit or standard that must be met at a critical control point to ensure that fish and aquatic plants do not become unsafe food.

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must do all of the following:

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (a) develop and maintain a food safety plan in accordance with subsection (3);

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (b) ensure that the food safety plan is implemented in the seafood processor's licensed facility;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (c) keep records respecting

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (i)  the results of monitoring and verification activities under the food safety plan, and

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (ii)  the corrective actions that have been taken when critical limits have not been met;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (d) keep the food safety plan in a conspicuous location in the seafood processor's licensed facility;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (e) make the food safety plan and the records referred to in paragraph (c) available to an inspector on request;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (f) review the food safety plan, and change it if necessary,

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (i)  at least annually, and

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (ii)  if any significant change is made to the construction or operation of the seafood processor's licensed facility.

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (3) A food safety plan must be in writing and must identify all of the following:

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (a) those hazards that may cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food, and the measures needed to address those hazards;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (b) the process and information used for the purpose of identifying the hazards and measures under paragraph (a);

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (c) based on the hazard analysis under paragraph (a), all critical control points and, for each critical control point,

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (i)  the critical limit, and

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (ii)  procedures to monitor the critical control point and to determine whether the critical limit has been met;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (d) if a critical limit has not been met, corrective actions that must be taken to meet the critical limit or eliminate unsafe food;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (e) verification procedures, including procedures, tests, sampling and other evaluative methods, to be taken to ensure that monitoring procedures under paragraph (c) (ii) and corrective actions under paragraph (d) are being carried out as intended;

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (f) the form of the records that must be kept under subsection (2) (c).

heading: Food safety plans
paragraph: (4) A seafood processor must change the seafood processor's food safety plan in accordance with the directions of an inspector.

heading: Temperature, water and ice standards
paragraph:
40
		  (1) A seafood processor must ensure that fish in the seafood processor's licensed facility are maintained as follows:

heading: Temperature, water and ice standards
paragraph: (a) in the case of live fish, at a temperature and in other conditions suitable to the species of fish;

heading: Temperature, water and ice standards
paragraph: (b) in the case of fresh fish, at a temperature of no less than 0°C and no more than 4°C;

heading: Temperature, water and ice standards
paragraph: (c) in the case of frozen fish, at a temperature of -18°C or less.

heading: Temperature, water and ice standards
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must ensure that water and ice used in the seafood processor's licensed facility for the purpose of carrying out activities under the licence is of adequate quality to prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph:
41
		  (1) A seafood processor must do all of the following with respect to the seafood processor's licensed facility:

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (a) develop and maintain a sanitation plan in accordance with subsection (2);

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (b) ensure that the sanitation plan is implemented;

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (c) keep records respecting activities carried out for the purpose of implementing the sanitation plan;

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (d) make the sanitation plan and the records referred to in paragraph (c) available to an inspector on request.

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (2) A sanitation plan must be in writing and must identify all of the following:

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (a) the cleaning and sanitizing requirements, with respect to the licensed facility and all equipment used in the licensed facility, necessary to keep fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food;

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (b) the cleaning and sanitizing agents, and pesticides, used in the licensed facility, including their concentrations, uses and storage requirements.

heading: Sanitation plans
paragraph: (3) A seafood processor must change the seafood processor's sanitation plan in accordance with the directions of an inspector.

heading: Sanitation
paragraph:
42
		  A seafood processor must ensure that the seafood processor's licensed facility and the equipment used in the licensed facility are maintained in a condition that will prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food, including ensuring that

heading: Sanitation
paragraph: (a) equipment is regularly sanitized, with food contact surfaces kept as free as possible of disease-causing micro-organisms, and

heading: Sanitation
paragraph: (b) pest-proof containers for the disposal of refuse are readily accessible.

heading: Hygiene
paragraph:
43
		  (1) A seafood processor must ensure that employees, while in the seafood processor's licensed facility,

heading: Hygiene
paragraph: (a) wear clothing, footwear and coverings on their hands that is clean and appropriate to the activity in which employees are engaged,

heading: Hygiene
paragraph: (b) exhibit cleanliness and good personal hygiene, and

heading: Hygiene
paragraph: (c) do not engage in any activity that may cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food.

heading: Hygiene
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must ensure that employees wash their hands as often as necessary to prevent fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

heading: Hygiene
paragraph: (3) A seafood processor must ensure that persons do not use tobacco or vapour products, within the meaning of the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act, in any area of the licensee's licensed facility where fish or aquatic plants are processed, stored or distributed.

heading: Illnesses
paragraph: 44		  A seafood processor must not permit a person suspected to suffer from, or be the carrier of, an illness communicable through food to come into contact with any fish, aquatic plants or equipment in the licensee's licensed facility.

heading: Animals
paragraph:
45
		  A seafood processor must ensure that live animals are not in or on the seafood processor's licensed facility, except as follows:

heading: Animals
paragraph: (a) a guide dog or a service dog within the meaning of the Guide Dog and Service Dog Act is permitted, except in any area in which fish or aquatic plants are processed or stored;

heading: Animals
paragraph: (b) live fish may be kept as permitted by an inspector.

heading: Storage of chemicals
paragraph: 46		  A seafood processor must ensure that chemicals, cleansers and similar agents are stored in the seafood processor's licensed facility

heading: Storage of chemicals
paragraph: (a) in a manner that cannot cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food, and

heading: Storage of chemicals
paragraph: (b) in containers that are clearly labelled to identify the contents.

heading: Storage of packaging, ingredients and additives
paragraph:
47
		  (1) A seafood processor must ensure that the following items, if stored in the seafood processor's licensed facility, are stored only in dedicated areas in the licensed facility:

heading: Storage of packaging, ingredients and additives
paragraph: (a) items to be used as packaging, including labels;

heading: Storage of packaging, ingredients and additives
paragraph: (b) ingredients and additives used in processing.

heading: Storage of packaging, ingredients and additives
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must ensure that items, ingredients and additives referred to in subsection (1) are each

heading: Storage of packaging, ingredients and additives
paragraph: (a) stored in a manner that will protect them from conditions that may cause them to become damaged or altered in a manner that may cause fish and aquatic plants to become unsafe food, and

heading: Storage of packaging, ingredients and additives
paragraph: (b) clearly identified with a label.

heading: Storage of inedible products and fish offal
paragraph:
48
		  A seafood processor must ensure that unsafe food, fish offal and byproducts are stored in containers that are

heading: Storage of inedible products and fish offal
paragraph: (a) kept separate from fish, aquatic plants and products that may be distributed for human consumption, and

heading: Storage of inedible products and fish offal
paragraph: (b) are clearly labelled as being unfit for human consumption.

heading: No storage of unnecessary items
paragraph:
49
		  A seafood processor must ensure that items that are not required for the carrying out of activities under the licence are not stored in or on the seafood processor's licensed facility.

heading: Prohibitions on processing
paragraph:
50
		  (1) A seafood processor must not process fish or aquatic plants unless the fish or aquatic plants are received by the seafood processor from one of the following sources:

heading: Prohibitions on processing
paragraph: (a) a person who holds a licence under this regulation with respect to the fish or aquatic plant, as applicable;

heading: Prohibitions on processing
paragraph: (b) a person who holds a licence or other authorization under a provincial food enactment;

heading: Prohibitions on processing
paragraph: (c) subject to subsection (2), a person who holds a federal licence to conduct activities in relation to food for public consumption;

heading: Prohibitions on processing
paragraph: (d) a person having lawful authority to harvest the fish or aquatic plant.

heading: Prohibitions on processing
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must not receive for processing cultured fish raised by marine aquaculture unless the cultured fish have been previously processed or held by a person holding a federal licence to process cultured fish.

heading: Processing lobsters and crab
paragraph:
51
		  A seafood processor must not process any lobster or crab that is dead before processing begins, unless the lobster or crab is being further processed after previous processing.

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph:
52
		  (1) This section applies despite section 3 of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada).

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must comply with all applicable requirements and prohibitions of the following provisions of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada) as if the seafood processor was a registered establishment within the meaning of that regulation:

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (a) section 34;

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (b) section 35;

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (c) section 37;

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (d) section 38 (1);

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (e) section 39 (1);

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (f) section 40 (1);

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (g) section 42;

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (h) sections 47 to 50.

heading: Federal canning regulations apply
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of section 49 of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada), the requirements of section 25 of that regulation also apply.

heading: Processing bivalve molluscs
paragraph:
53
		  (1) A seafood processor must not receive bivalve molluscs for processing unless

heading: Processing bivalve molluscs
paragraph: (a) the bivalve molluscs have been previously processed or held by a person holding a federal licence to process bivalve molluscs, and

heading: Processing bivalve molluscs
paragraph: (b) the processed bivalve molluscs are in containers that are tagged according to the requirements of the Canadian Shellfish Sanitation Program Manual of Operations, made under section 15 (8) (c) of the Fish Inspection Regulations (Canada).

heading: Processing bivalve molluscs
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must ensure that shucked bivalve molluscs are packed for transport and distribution only in containers that are sealed in a manner that readily allows detection of any tampering.

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph:
54
		  (1) A seafood processor must ensure that marks made in accordance with this section are legible, readily visible and permanent.

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must ensure that each container of sport caught fish is marked with all of the following:

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (a) the species of fish in the container;

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (b) the name of the seafood processor, as shown on the seafood processor's licence, and the address of the seafood processor;

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (c) the date on which the fish were processed;

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (d) the words, "sport caught fish - not for sale".

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (3) A seafood processor must ensure that each carton of containers of sport caught fish is marked with all of the following:

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (a) the information required under subsection (2) (b) and (d);

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (b) the name of the fisher who harvested the fish.

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (2) (c), the date must be expressed in the format "year month day", as follows:

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (a) the year must be expressed by using all 4 numerals that comprise the year;

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (b) the month must be expressed by using the code that corresponds to the month as shown in the table below:

heading: Information on sport caught fish containers
paragraph: (c) the day must be expressed by using the 2 numerals that comprise the calendar date, with the first numeral being "0" if the calendar date is less than 10.

heading: Tracking system for sport caught fish
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A seafood processor who processes sport caught fish must ensure that processed sport caught fish are distributed only to the fisher who harvested the fish.

heading: Tracking system for sport caught fish
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), a seafood processor must have in place a system that does all of the following:

heading: Tracking system for sport caught fish
paragraph: (a) marks or otherwise identifies sport caught fish, on receipt for processing, in a manner that enables a person to readily determine the fisher of the sport caught fish;

heading: Tracking system for sport caught fish
paragraph: (b) maintains the mark or other identification throughout processing and until distribution;

heading: Tracking system for sport caught fish
paragraph: (c) verifies on distribution that the recipient of the processed sport caught fish is the fisher.

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph:
56
		  (1) A seafood processor must keep records, in accordance with this section, with respect to each delivery of fish and aquatic plants

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (a) received by the seafood processor for processing, and

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (b) distributed by the seafood processor.

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (2) Records must include at least the following information:

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (a) if applicable, the licence number or federal licence number of the person from whom fish or aquatic plants were received;

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (b) the contact information of the person

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (i)  from whom fish or aquatic plants were received, or

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (ii)  to whom fish or aquatic plants were distributed;

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (c) the date of receipt or transport for distribution;

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (d) the quantity of

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (i)  fish received or distributed, divided according to species and, once processed, manner of processing, and

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (ii)  aquatic plants received or distributed, divided according to aquatic plant group and aquatic plant species;

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (e) the amount paid or received for fish and aquatic plants received or distributed;

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (f) the contact information of the transporter that distributed the fish or aquatic plants.

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (3) A seafood processor that distributes bivalve molluscs must do both of the following:

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (a) in addition to the information required under subsection (2), include the information contained on the tag referred to in section 53 (1) (b) [processing bivalve molluscs];

heading: Seafood processor receipt and distribution records
paragraph: (b) provide to a transporter of the bivalve molluscs a copy of the information referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph:
57
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: "custom processing" means the processing of fish and aquatic plants for the purpose of returning the fish and aquatic plants to the person from whom they were received;

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: "processing for distribution" means the processing of fish and aquatic plants for the purpose of distributing the fish and aquatic plants to persons other than the person from whom they were received.

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: (2) A seafood processor must keep records, in accordance with this section, with respect to each calendar month or part of a calendar month the seafood processor is engaged in activities under the licence.

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: (3) Employment records must include at least the following information:

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: (a) the number of employees, divided according to the type of activity in which those employees are primarily employed;

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: (b) the number of employees engaged in custom processing activities, with those activities divided according to species.

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: (4) Processing records must include at least the following information, divided according to custom processing activities and processing for distribution activities:

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: (a) the total quantity of fish and aquatic plants received by the seafood processor;

heading: Other seafood processor records
paragraph: (b) the total quantity of fish and aquatic plants processed by the seafood processor, divided according to species and manner of processing.

heading: Operational requirements
paragraph:
58
		  (1) A transporter must ensure that all equipment the transporter uses to transport fish and aquatic plants is constructed from materials that

heading: Operational requirements
paragraph: (a) are durable and suitable for their intended purpose, and

heading: Operational requirements
paragraph: (b) ensure that food contact surfaces are easily cleaned and free from any noxious or toxic substance.

heading: Operational requirements
paragraph: (2) A transporter must ensure that all equipment the transporter uses to store fish and aquatic plants is constructed in a manner that protects the fish and aquatic plants from becoming unsafe food.

heading: Temperature of transported fish
paragraph:
59
		  (1) A transporter of fish must ensure that the temperature of fish being transported is maintained in accordance with section 40 (1) [temperature, water and ice standards].

heading: Temperature of transported fish
paragraph: (2) A transporter of fish must comply with section 40 (2) as if the transporter were a seafood processor.

heading: Live bivalve mollusc transporter records
paragraph:
60
		  (1) A transporter of live bivalve molluscs must carry during transport the record referred to in section 56 (3) (b) [seafood processor receipt and distribution records].

heading: Live bivalve mollusc transporter records
paragraph: (2) A transporter must provide the record referred to in section 56 (3) (b) to the person who receives the bivalve molluscs.

heading: Must keep record of live bivalve molluscs
paragraph:
61
		  A person who receives live bivalve molluscs from a transporter must do both of the following:

heading: Must keep record of live bivalve molluscs
paragraph: (a) add to the record received under section 60 (2) [live bivalve mollusc transporter records] a notation of the date on which the bivalve molluscs were received;

heading: Must keep record of live bivalve molluscs
paragraph: (b) keep the record referred to in paragraph (a) for at least one year.

heading: No distribution of unlawfully processed aquatic plants
paragraph:
62
		  A person must not distribute, or offer to distribute, to the public for human consumption an aquatic plant that has been processed by a person other than a person who holds, or who is exempt from holding, a seafood processor licence.

heading: How to express quantity
paragraph:
63
		  Subject to section 14 [wild aquatic plant harvester records], a person who must keep a record of the quantity of fish or aquatic plants grown, harvested, received, distributed or transported, must express the quantity as follows:

heading: How to express quantity
paragraph: (a) with respect to fish or aquatic plants grown, harvested or received, in kilograms or tonnes;

heading: How to express quantity
paragraph: (b) with respect to fish or aquatic plants distributed or transported, in kilograms, tonnes or as the number of cartons distributed, if a description is given of the

heading: How to express quantity
paragraph: (i)  number of containers in each carton, and

heading: How to express quantity
paragraph: (ii)  the weight of each container.

heading: How to express amounts paid and received
paragraph:
64
		  A person who must keep a record of the amount paid or received for fish and aquatic plants received or distributed, must express the amount in Canadian dollars.

heading: Records to be kept for 3 years
paragraph:
65
		  Subject to any provision to the contrary, a person who must keep records under this regulation must ensure that each record is kept for a period of at least 3 years.

heading: Reporting information to minister
paragraph:
66
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2) and the terms of an applicable harvest agreement, if any, a person who must keep a record under this regulation, other than a transporter, must report to the minister the information, or a consolidation of the information, that the person must keep

heading: Reporting information to minister
paragraph: (a) annually, for the period beginning January 1 and ending December 31, and

heading: Reporting information to minister
paragraph: (b) as required by the minister.

heading: Reporting information to minister
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (a) does not apply to the following records:

heading: Reporting information to minister
paragraph: (a) harvest records prepared under section 14 [wild aquatic plant harvester records];

heading: Reporting information to minister
paragraph: (b) records respecting food safety plans prepared under section 39 [food safety plans];

heading: Reporting information to minister
paragraph: (c) records respecting sanitation plans prepared under section 41 [sanitation plans].

heading: Repealed
paragraph: Schedule

heading: Repealed
paragraph: Aquatic Plants

heading: Interpretation
paragraph:
1
		  In this Schedule, the notation "spp." refers to all species within the genus preceding the notation.

heading: Group 1 aquatic plants
