heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the Fish Toxicant Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Fisheries Act; (Loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fish toxicant means a pest control product that conforms to the requirements of the Pest Control Products Act and the Pest Control Products Regulations and that is used for the purpose of destroying any fish that is a pest as defined in section 2 of that Act. (produit ichtyotoxique)

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: 3 For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, fish toxicants are prescribed as deleterious substances that are authorized to be deposited.

heading: Waters
paragraph: 4 For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the waters where fish toxicants are authorized to be deposited are the waters of the provinces of Saskatchewan and Alberta and the non-tidal waters of the provinces of Ontario, Quebec and Manitoba.

heading: Persons Authorized
paragraph: 5 For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act and subject to section 6, the following persons are prescribed as persons who may, in the absence of any other authority, authorize the deposit of any fish toxicant:

heading: Persons Authorized
paragraph: (a) in relation to the Province of Ontario, the Minister of Natural Resources for that Province;

heading: Persons Authorized
paragraph: (b) in relation to Quebec, the Minister responsible in the Province of Quebec for the application of An Act respecting the conservation and development of wildlife, R.S.Q., c. C-61.1,

heading: Persons Authorized
paragraph: (c) in relation to the Province of Manitoba, the Minister of Natural Resources for that Province;

heading: Persons Authorized
paragraph: (d) in relation to the Province of Saskatchewan, the Minister of Parks, Recreation and Culture for that Province; and

heading: Persons Authorized
paragraph: (e) in relation to the Province of Alberta, the chief fishery officer as defined in the Alberta Fishery Regulations.

heading: Conditions for Granting the Authorization
paragraph: 6 For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the prescribed conditions for granting the authorization referred to in section 5 are the following:

heading: Conditions for Granting the Authorization
paragraph: (a) the Minister or the chief fishery officer is satisfied that the eradication of any fish that is a pest by the use of fish toxicants in any waters set out in section 4 and the subsequent restocking of those waters will enhance fishing in those waters; and

heading: Conditions for Granting the Authorization
paragraph: (b) the authorization is given in writing.

heading: Condition for Authorizing the Deposit of Fish Toxicants
paragraph: 7 For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the condition under which fish toxicants are authorized to be deposited in the waters referred to in section 4 is that the deposit does not adversely affect fish in the waters adjacent to the waters where the deposit is made.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Fisheries Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 (1) In this Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: analyst means a person who is designated under subsection 56.1(1) to perform the functions of an analyst; (analyste)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian fisheries waters means all waters in the fishing zones of Canada, all waters in the territorial sea of Canada and all internal waters of Canada; (eaux de peche canadiennes)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: close time means a specified period during which fish to which it applies may not be fished, and "closed time" or "closed season" has a similar meaning; (periode d'interdiction et periode de fermeture ou saison de fermeture)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fish includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) parts of fish,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) shellfish, crustaceans, marine animals and any parts of shellfish, crustaceans or marine animals, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the eggs, sperm, spawn, larvae, spat and juvenile stages of fish, shellfish, crustaceans and marine animals; (poissons)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishery with respect to any fish, includes,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any of its species, populations, assemblages and stocks, whether the fish is fished or not,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any place where fishing may be carried on,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any period during which fishing may be carried on,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any method of fishing used, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) any type of fishing gear or equipment or fishing vessel used; (peche)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishery guardian means a person who is designated as a fishery guardian pursuant to subsection 5(1); (garde-peche)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishery officer means a person who is designated as a fishery officer pursuant to subsection 5(1); (agent des peches)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fish habitat means water frequented by fish and any other areas on which fish depend directly or indirectly to carry out their life processes, including spawning grounds and nursery, rearing, food supply and migration areas; (habitat)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishing means fishing for, catching or attempting to catch fish by any method; (peche)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishing vessel means any vessel used, outfitted or designed for the purpose of catching, processing or transporting fish; (bateau de peche)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishway means any device, work or other thing that provides for the free passage of fish, including a canal, a fish pump, a fish ladder, a fish elevator and a fish lock; (passe migratoire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous governing body means a council, government or other entity that is authorized to act on behalf of an Indigenous group, community or people that holds rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982; (corps dirigeant autochtone)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous peoples of Canada has the meaning assigned by the definition aboriginal peoples of Canada in subsection 35(2) of the Constitution Act, 1982; (peuples autochtones du Canada)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inspector means a person who is designated as an inspector pursuant to subsection 38(1); (inspecteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: laws includes the by-laws made by an Indigenous governing body; (lois)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or, in respect of any matter related to the Northern Pipeline referred to in the Northern Pipeline Act, the member of the Queen's Privy Council for Canada designated as the Minister for the purposes of that Act; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: obstruction means any slide, dam or other thing impeding wholly or partially the free passage of fish; (obstacle)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vehicle means any conveyance that may be used for transportation, including aircraft. (vehicule)

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: 2.1 The purpose of this Act is to provide a framework for

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: (a) the proper management and control of fisheries; and

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: (b) the conservation and protection of fish and fish habitat, including by preventing pollution.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.2 (1) This Act applies in Canada, and also to

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) Canadian fisheries waters; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) with respect to a sedentary species, any portion of the continental shelf of Canada that is beyond the limits of Canadian fisheries waters.

heading: Definition of sedentary species
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of paragraph (1)(b), sedentary species means any organism that, at the harvestable stage, either is immobile on or under the seabed or is unable to move except by remaining in constant physical contact with the seabed or subsoil.

heading: Duty of Minister
paragraph: 2.4 When making a decision under this Act, the Minister shall consider any adverse effects that the decision may have on the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Canada recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: 2.5 Except as otherwise provided in this Act, when making a decision under this Act, the Minister may consider, among other things,

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (a) the application of a precautionary approach and an ecosystem approach;

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (b) the sustainability of fisheries;

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (c) scientific information;

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (d) Indigenous knowledge of the Indigenous peoples of Canada that has been provided to the Minister;

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (e) community knowledge;

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (f) cooperation with any government of a province, any Indigenous governing body and any body - including a co-management body - established under a land claims agreement;

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (g) social, economic and cultural factors in the management of fisheries;

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (h) the preservation or promotion of the independence of licence holders in commercial inshore fisheries; and

heading: Considerations for decision making
paragraph: (i) the intersection of sex and gender with other identity factors.

heading: Provincial rights not affected
paragraph: 3 (1) Nothing in this Act shall be taken to authorize the granting of fishery leases that confer an exclusive right to fish in property belonging to a province.

heading: Application of Act to Her Majesty
paragraph: (2) This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Licences to take spawn
paragraph: 4 Nothing in this Act precludes the granting by the Minister of written permission to obtain fish for purposes of stocking or artificial breeding or for scientific purposes.

heading: Minister may establish advisory panels
paragraph: 4.01 (1) The Minister may, in order to carry out the purpose of this Act, establish advisory panels and provide for their membership, functions and operation.

heading: Remuneration of members
paragraph: (2) Members of an advisory panel established under subsection (1) are to be paid any amount that is fixed by the Governor in Council for each day that they attend any of the advisory panel's meetings.

heading: Expenses
paragraph: (3) The members are also entitled to be reimbursed, in accordance with Treasury Board directives, for the travel, living and other expenses incurred in connection with their work for the panel while absent from their ordinary place of work, in the case of full-time members, or from their ordinary place of residence, in the case of part-time members.

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph: 4.1 (1) The Minister may enter into an agreement with any government of a province, any Indigenous governing body and any body - including a co-management body - established under a land claims agreement, to further the purpose of this Act, including an agreement with respect to one or more of the following:

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) facilitating cooperation between the parties to the agreement, including facilitating joint action in areas of common interest, reducing overlap between their respective programs and otherwise harmonizing those programs;

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) facilitating enhanced communication between the parties, including the exchange of scientific and other information; and

heading: Minister may enter into agreements
paragraph: (c) facilitating public consultation or the entry into arrangements with third-party stakeholders.

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (2) An agreement may establish

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (a) the roles, powers and functions of the parties;

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (b) programs and projects;

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (c) principles and objectives of the parties' respective programs and projects;

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (d) standards, guidelines and codes of practice to be followed by the parties in the administration of their respective programs and projects;

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (e) processes for policy development, operational planning and communication between the parties, including the exchange of scientific and other information;

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (f) the administrative structures that will be used to carry out the agreement's objectives;

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (g) the power of the parties to create committees and public panels and to conduct public consultations; and

heading: Contents of agreement
paragraph: (h) the circumstances and manner in which the government of the province or the Indigenous governing body is to provide information on the administration and enforcement of a provision of the laws of the province or the Indigenous governing body that the agreement provides is equivalent in effect to a provision of the regulations.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council may make regulations establishing the conditions under which the Minister may enter into or renew an agreement, including procedures for entering into or renewing the agreement.

heading: Agreements to be published
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsections (5) to (8), the Minister shall publish an agreement in the manner that he or she considers appropriate.

heading: Publication of negotiated agreement
paragraph: (5) Before any agreement that is negotiated for the purposes of section 4.2 is entered into, the Minister shall publish the agreement, or give notice of its availability, in Part I of the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that he or she considers appropriate.

heading: Comments
paragraph: (6) Within 60 days after the publication of an agreement or the giving of notice of its availability, any person may file comments with the Minister.

heading: Publication by Minister of results
paragraph: (7) After the end of the 60-day period, the Minister shall publish in Part I of the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that he or she considers appropriate a report that summarizes how any comments were dealt with or a notice of the availability of that report.

heading: Publication of final agreements
paragraph: (8) The Minister shall publish any final agreement, or give notice of its availability, in Part I of the Canada Gazette and in any other manner that he or she considers appropriate.

heading: Rights of Indigenous peoples
paragraph: (9) An agreement entered into under subsection (1) must respect the rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Declaration of equivalent provisions
paragraph: 4.2 (1) If an agreement entered into under section 4.1 provides that there is in force a provision of the laws of the province or the Indigenous governing body that is equivalent in effect to a provision of the regulations, the Governor in Council may, by order, declare that certain provisions of this Act or of the regulations do not apply in the province or the territory governed by the Indigenous governing body, as the case may be, with respect to the subject matter of the provision of the laws of the province or the Indigenous governing body.

heading: Non-application of provisions
paragraph: (2) Except with respect to Her Majesty in right of Canada, the provisions of this Act or of the regulations that are set out in the order do not apply within the province or the territory governed by the Indigenous governing body, as the case may be, with respect to the subject matter of the provision of the laws of the province or the Indigenous governing body.

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council may revoke the order if the Governor in Council is satisfied that the provision of the laws of the province or the Indigenous governing body, as the case may be, is no longer equivalent in effect to the provision of the regulations or is not being adequately administered or enforced.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (4) The Governor in Council may revoke the order only if the Minister has given notice of the proposed revocation to the government of the province or to the Indigenous governing body, as the case may be.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: 4.3 The Minister shall, as soon as feasible after the end of each fiscal year, prepare and cause to be laid before each house of Parliament a report on the administration of sections 4.1 and 4.2 in that fiscal year.

heading: Objectives
paragraph: 4.4 (1) The Minister may implement programs and projects for the purposes of this Act and, to facilitate the implementation of a program or project, may

heading: Objectives
paragraph: (a) make grants and contributions;

heading: Objectives
paragraph: (b) make loans;

heading: Objectives
paragraph: (c) make recoverable expenditures on behalf of any person or body, or any federal or provincial minister, department or agency; and

heading: Objectives
paragraph: (d) guarantee the repayment of any financial obligation, or provide loan insurance or credit insurance in respect of such an obligation.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister and the Minister of Finance, make regulations respecting such grants, contributions, loans, guarantees and insurance.

heading: Agreements, etc.
paragraph: (3) In exercising powers and performing functions under subsection (1), the Minister may

heading: Agreements, etc.
paragraph: (a) enter into agreements - including an agreement under section 4.1 - or arrangements or transactions with any person or body, or any federal or provincial minister, department or agency; and

heading: Agreements, etc.
paragraph: (b) with the approval of the Minister of Finance, requisition amounts in respect of such an agreement, arrangement or transaction to be paid out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 5 (1) The Minister may designate any persons or classes of persons as fishery officers or fishery guardians for the purposes of this Act and may limit in any manner the Minister considers appropriate the powers that a fishery officer or fishery guardian may exercise under this Act or any other Act of Parliament.

heading: Certificate of designation
paragraph: (2) Each fishery officer and fishery guardian shall be provided with a certificate in a form the Minister considers appropriate certifying their designation as such and, where the powers of a fishery officer or fishery guardian are limited pursuant to subsection (1), specifying the powers that the officer or guardian may exercise under this Act or any other Act of Parliament.

heading: Presentation of certificate
paragraph: (3) On entering any place under this Act or any other Act of Parliament, a fishery officer or fishery guardian shall, on request, show the certificate of designation to the person in charge of the place.

heading: Laws of certain First Nations
paragraph: (4) The powers and protections that a fishery officer or fishery guardian has under this or any other Act of Parliament, including the powers and protections of a peace officer under the Criminal Code, apply to a fishery officer or fishery guardian enforcing

heading: Laws of certain First Nations
paragraph: (a) Nisga'a laws made under the Fisheries Chapter of the Nisga'a Final Agreement given effect by the Nisga'a Final Agreement Act;

heading: Laws of certain First Nations
paragraph: (a.1) Tla'amin Laws, as defined in subsection 2(2) of the Tla'amin Final Agreement Act, made under Chapter 9 of the Agreement, as defined in subsection 2(1) of that Act, given effect by that Act;

heading: Laws of certain First Nations
paragraph: (b) Tsawwassen Laws, within the meaning of subsection 2(2) of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement Act, made under chapter 9 of the Agreement, as defined in subsection 2(1) of that Act, given effect by that Act; or

heading: Laws of certain First Nations
paragraph: (c) Maanulth Laws, within the meaning of subsection 2(2) of the Maanulth First Nations Final Agreement Act, made under chapter 10 of the Agreement, as defined in subsection 2(1) of that Act, given effect by that Act.

heading: Exercise of powers
paragraph: 5.1 Every power that may be exercised in Canada by a fishery officer or fishery guardian under this Act may be exercised anywhere this Act applies.

heading: Measures to maintain fish stocks
paragraph: 6.1 (1) In the management of fisheries, the Minister shall implement measures to maintain major fish stocks at or above the level necessary to promote the sustainability of the stock, taking into account the biology of the fish and the environmental conditions affecting the stock.

heading: Limit reference point
paragraph: (2) If the Minister is of the opinion that it is not feasible or appropriate, for cultural reasons or because of adverse socio-economic impacts, to implement the measures referred to in subsection (1), the Minister shall set a limit reference point and implement measures to maintain the fish stock above that point, taking into account the biology of the fish and the environmental conditions affecting the stock.

heading: Publication of decision
paragraph: (3) If the Minister sets a limit reference point in accordance with subsection (2), he or she shall publish the decision to do so, within a reasonable time and with reasons, on the Internet site of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans.

heading: Plan to rebuild
paragraph: 6.2 (1) If a major fish stock has declined to or below its limit reference point, the Minister shall develop a plan to rebuild the stock above that point in the affected area, taking into account the biology of the fish and the environmental conditions affecting the stock, and implement it within the period provided for in the plan.

heading: Amendment
paragraph: (2) If the Minister is of the opinion that such a plan could result in adverse socio-economic or cultural impacts, the Minister may amend the plan or the implementation period in order to mitigate those impacts while minimizing further decline of the fish stock.

heading: Endangered or threatened species
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply if the affected fish stock is an endangered species or a threatened species under the Species at Risk Act or if the implementation of international management measures by Canada does not permit it.

heading: Publication of decision
paragraph: (4) If the Minister amends a plan in accordance with subsection (2) or decides not to make one in accordance with subsection (3), he or she shall publish the decision to do so, within a reasonable time and with reasons, on the Internet site of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans.

heading: Restoration measures
paragraph: (5) In the management of fisheries, if the Minister is of the opinion that the loss or degradation of the stock's fish habitat has contributed to the stock's decline, he or she shall take into account whether there are measures in place aimed at restoring that fish habitat.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 6.3 The major fish stocks referred to in sections 6.1 and 6.2 are to be prescribed by regulations.

heading: Fishery leases and licences
paragraph: 7 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Minister may, in his absolute discretion, wherever the exclusive right of fishing does not already exist by law, issue or authorize to be issued leases and licences for fisheries or fishing, wherever situated or carried on.

heading: Default of payment of fine
paragraph: (1.1) The Minister may refuse to issue a lease or licence for fisheries or fishing to a person, if, among other things, they are in default of payment of a fine in relation to a contravention of the Act and the proceeds of the fine belong to Her Majesty in Right of Canada or of a province or to any other person or entity.

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) Except as otherwise provided in this Act or regulations made under it, leases or licences for any term of more than nine years shall be issued only under the authority of the Governor in Council.

heading: Fees
paragraph: 8 (1) Except if fees are prescribed in this Act, the Governor in Council may, by regulation and on the recommendation of the Minister, prescribe the fees that are to be charged for fishery or fishing licences and for fishing quotas.

heading: Periodic adjustment
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, the regulations made under subsection (1) may provide for periodic adjustment of the fees referred to in that subsection.

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: 9 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Minister may suspend or cancel any lease or licence issued under the authority of this Act, if

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (a) he or she determines that any provision of that lease or licence was not complied with;

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (b) he or she determines that the lease or licence holder has, with respect to the lease or licence, entered into an agreement that contravenes any provision of this Act or of the regulations; or

heading: Suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (c) the lease or licence holder is in default of payment of a fine in relation to a contravention of this Act and the proceeds of the fine belong to Her Majesty in right of Canada or of a province or to any other person or entity.

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) The Minister may suspend or cancel a lease or licence under paragraph (1)(a) or (b) only if no proceedings under this Act have been commenced with respect to the non-compliance or contravention referred to in those paragraphs, as the case may be.

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: 9.1 (1) The Minister may, if he or she is of the opinion that prompt measures are required to address a threat to the proper management and control of fisheries and the conservation and protection of fish, make a fisheries management order with respect to any aspect of fisheries in any area of Canadian fisheries waters specified in the order

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (a) prohibiting fishing of one or more species, populations, assemblages or stocks of fish;

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (b) prohibiting any type of fishing gear or equipment or fishing vessel from being used;

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (c) limiting the fishing of any specified size, weight or quantity of any species, populations, assemblages or stocks of fish; and

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (d) imposing any requirements with respect to fishing.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (2) The Minister may impose any conditions that he or she considers appropriate in the order.

heading: Application of order
paragraph: (3) The fisheries management order may provide that it applies only to

heading: Application of order
paragraph: (a) a particular class of persons, including

heading: Application of order
paragraph: (i) persons who fish using a particular method or a particular type of gear or equipment, and

heading: Application of order
paragraph: (ii) persons who use fishing vessels of a particular class; or

heading: Application of order
paragraph: (b) holders of a particular class of licence.

heading: Duty to comply
paragraph: 9.2 Every person or holder to whom a fisheries management order applies shall comply with it.

heading: Duration
paragraph: 9.3 (1) A fisheries management order issued under section 9.1 shall be in effect for the term specified in the order, which shall not exceed 45 days from the day on which the order is issued.

heading: Renewal of order
paragraph: (2) If the Minister is of the opinion that prompt measures continue to be required to address the threat referred to in subsection 9.1(1), he or she may renew the order for a term that does not exceed 45 days from the day on which it is issued.

heading: Amendment of order
paragraph: 9.4 (1) The Minister may amend a fisheries management order, other than its term, if he or she is of the opinion that the measures specified in the order are inadequate to address the threat referred to in subsection 9.1(1).

heading: Revocation of order
paragraph: (2) If the Minister is of the opinion that the measures specified in the order are no longer necessary to address the threat or if the threat no longer exists, he or she may revoke the order.

heading: Notice
paragraph: 9.5 (1) Notice of a fisheries management order shall be given to the persons or holders to whom it applies, in the prescribed manner or, if there is no prescribed manner, using a method provided under section 7 of the Fishery (General) Regulations, with any necessary modifications.

heading: If notice not given
paragraph: (2) If notice is not given, then the contravention of a fisheries management order is not an offence under this Act unless, at the time of the contravention, reasonable steps had been taken to bring the substance of the order to the notice of the persons or holders to whom it applies.

heading: Inconsistency
paragraph: 9.6 If there is an inconsistency between a fisheries management order and any regulations made under this Act, orders issued under those regulations or conditions of any lease or licence issued under this Act, the fisheries management order prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: 9.7 Orders made under section 9.1 are not statutory instruments for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Allocation of fish
paragraph: 10 (1) For the proper management and control of fisheries and the conservation and protection of fish, the Minister may determine a quantity of fish or of fishing gear and equipment that may be allocated for the purpose of financing scientific and fisheries management activities that are described in a joint project agreement entered into with any person or body, or any federal or provincial minister, department or agency.

heading: Quantity in licence
paragraph: (2) The Minister may specify, in a licence issued under this Act, a quantity of fish or of fishing gear and equipment allocated for the purpose of financing those activities.

heading: Fees for services or use of facilities
paragraph: 11 (1) The Minister may fix, by regulation, the fees to be paid for a service or the use of a facility provided under this Act by him or her, the Department of Fisheries and Oceans or any board or agency of the Government of Canada for which he or she has responsibility.

heading: Amount not to exceed cost
paragraph: (2) Fees that are fixed under subsection (1) shall not exceed the cost to Her Majesty in right of Canada of providing the service or the use of the facility.

heading: Fees for products or cost recovery
paragraph: 12 (1) The Minister may fix, by regulation, fees in respect of the products provided or the recovery, in whole or in part, of costs that are incurred in relation to the administration of this Act by him or her, the Department of Fisheries and Oceans or any board or agency of the Government of Canada for which he or she has responsibility.

heading: Amount not to exceed cost
paragraph: (2) Fees in respect of the product or recovery of costs that are fixed under subsection (1) shall not exceed the cost to Her Majesty in right of Canada of providing the product or recovering of costs.

heading: Fees for rights and privileges
paragraph: 13 Subject to section 8, the Minister may fix, by regulation, fees payable in respect of a conferral, by means of a permit or authorization, of a right or privilege provided under this Act.

heading: Fees for providing regulatory processes
paragraph: 14 (1) The Minister may fix, by regulation, fees in respect of the provision of regulatory processes under this Act by him or her, the Department of Fisheries and Oceans or any board or agency of the Government of Canada for which he or she has responsibility.

heading: Amount
paragraph: (2) Fees that are fixed under subsection (1) shall in the aggregate not exceed an amount sufficient to compensate Her Majesty in right of Canada for any reasonable expenses incurred by Her Majesty for the purpose of providing regulatory processes under this Act.

heading: Periodic adjustment
paragraph: 15 Regulations made under any of sections 11 to 14 may provide for the periodic adjustment of the fees referred to in those sections.

heading: Proceeds of fees - provinces
paragraph: 16 Any fees charged in relation to the issuance of a licence by an employee of a provincial government belong to Her Majesty in right of that province.

heading: Licences for lobster pounds
paragraph: 18 (1) No one shall maintain a pound or enclosure in which lobsters, legally caught during the open season, are retained for sale during the close season at a place where the pound or enclosure is located, or for export therefrom, except under a licence from the Minister, and no lobsters shall be taken from any such pound or enclosure and disposed of during the close season at the place where it is located, except under a certificate from a fishery officer or fishery guardian, setting out the pound or enclosure from which the lobsters were taken and that they had been legally caught during the open season.

heading: Marking of pounds
paragraph: (2) Each pound or enclosure referred to in subsection (1) shall be marked with the name of the licensee and the number of his licence, and the marking shall be in black on a white ground, with letters and figures that are at least six inches in height.

heading: Fee
paragraph: (3) The annual fee for a licence referred to in subsection (1) shall be seventy-five dollars.

heading: Devices to prevent escape of fish
paragraph: 21 (1) The Minister may authorize the installation and maintenance of fish guards, screens, coverings, netting or other devices in waters to prevent fish held for breeding from escaping or for any other purpose that the Minister considers to be in the public interest.

heading: Removal
paragraph: (2) No person shall damage, remove or authorize the removal of such a fish guard, screen, covering, netting or other device, unless they are authorized to do so by the Minister.

heading: Fishing in limits leased to another prohibited
paragraph: 23 No one shall fish for, take, catch or kill fish in any water, along any beach or within any fishery described in any lease or licence, or place, use, draw or set therein any fishing gear or apparatus, except by permission of the occupant under the lease or licence for the time being, or shall disturb or injure any such fishery.

heading: Taking cetaceans into captivity
paragraph: 23.1 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no one shall fish for a cetacean with the intent to take it into captivity.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, subject to any conditions that he or she may specify, authorize a person to fish for a cetacean with the intent to take it into captivity if he or she is of the opinion that the circumstances so require, including when the cetacean is injured or in distress or is in need of care.

heading: Importation and exportation - cetaceans
paragraph: 23.2 (1) No person shall import into Canada or export from Canada, or attempt to import or export, a living cetacean or sperm, an egg or an embryo of a cetacean, except in accordance with a permit issued under subsection (2).

heading: Issuance of permit
paragraph: (2) The Minister may issue a permit authorizing the importation or exportation of a living cetacean or sperm, an egg or an embryo of a cetacean and impose any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate in the permit, if the importation or exportation is for the purpose of

heading: Issuance of permit
paragraph: (a) conducting scientific research; or

heading: Issuance of permit
paragraph: (b) keeping the cetacean in captivity if it is in the best interests of the cetacean's welfare to do so.

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (3) The Minister may amend, suspend or cancel a permit issued under subsection (2).

heading: Exception to the Criminal Code - scientific research
paragraph: 23.3 (1) Subsection 445.2(2) of the Criminal Code does not apply to a person who conducts scientific research in accordance with a licence issued by the Minister under subsection (2).

heading: Issuance of licence
paragraph: (2) The Minister may issue a licence authorizing any person to conduct scientific research with respect to cetaceans and impose any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate in the licence.

heading: Exception to the Criminal Code - cetacean's captivity in its best interests
paragraph: 23.4 (1) Paragraph 445.2(2)(a) of the Criminal Code does not apply to a person who keeps a cetacean in captivity in the best interests of the cetacean's welfare in accordance with a licence issued by the Minister under subsection (2).

heading: Issuance of licence
paragraph: (2) The Minister may issue a licence authorizing any person to keep a cetacean in captivity in the best interests of the cetacean's welfare and impose any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate in the licence.

heading: Exception to the Criminal Code - scientific research by federal employees
paragraph: 23.5 Subsection 445.2(2) of the Criminal Code does not apply to the employees of any federal entity set out in Schedules I to V of the Financial Administration Act who are performing their duties or functions in relation to scientific research with respect to cetaceans and to persons who are assisting them.

heading: Exception to the Criminal Code - federal employees keeping cetaceans in captivity
paragraph: 23.6 Paragraph 445.2(2)(a) of the Criminal Code does not apply to the employees of any federal entity set out in Schedules I to V of the Financial Administration Act who are performing their duties or functions in relation to the keeping of a cetacean in captivity in the best interests of the cetacean's welfare and to persons who are assisting them.

heading: Seines, nets, etc., not to obstruct navigation
paragraph: 24 Seines, nets or other fishing apparatus shall not be set or used in such a manner or in such a place that they or any equipment that is attached to any of them obstructs the navigation of boats and vessels and no boats or vessels shall destroy or wantonly injure in any way seines, nets or other fishing apparatus lawfully set or used or any equipment that is attached to any of them.

heading: Setting gear during close time
paragraph: 25 (1) Subject to the regulations, no person shall place or set any fishing gear or apparatus in any water, along any beach or within any fishery during a close time.

heading: Removal of gear
paragraph: (2) Subject to the regulations and subsection (3), any person who places or sets any fishing gear or apparatus in any water, along any beach or within any fishery shall remove it when the gear or apparatus is not being tended and prior to the commencement of a close time.

heading: Officer's discretion
paragraph: (3) A fishery officer may permit fishing gear or apparatus to remain in the water, along a beach or within a fishery after the commencement of a close time for any period the fishery officer considers necessary to permit the removal of the gear or apparatus.

heading: Obstructing passage of fish or waters
paragraph: 29 (1) No person shall, for the purpose of fishing, place, erect, use or maintain any seine, net, weir or other fishing gear or apparatus, or any log, rock or material of any kind that

heading: Obstructing passage of fish or waters
paragraph: (a) unduly obstructs the passage of fish in any Canadian fisheries waters, whether subject to any exclusive right of fishery or not; or

heading: Obstructing passage of fish or waters
paragraph: (b) obstructs more than two thirds of the width of any river or stream or more than one third of the width of the main channel at low tide of any tidal stream.

heading: Removal
paragraph: (2) The Minister or a fishery officer may order the removal of or remove any seine, net, weir or other fishing gear or apparatus, or any log, rock or material of any kind that, in the opinion of the Minister or fishery officer, results in an obstruction referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

heading: Tidal streams
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), if a tidal stream has no main channel at low tide, then the tidal stream's width is considered to be the width of its main channel.

heading: Permit required
paragraph: 31 (1) No one shall catch, fish for, take, buy, sell, possess or export any fish for the purposes of converting it into fish meal, manure, guano or fertilizer, or for the manufacture or conversion of the fish into oil, fish meal or manure or other fertilizing product, except under authority of the Minister.

heading: Exception by Minister
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, by notice published in the Canada Gazette, except any kind or kinds of fish from the operation of all or any part of subsection (1).

heading: Shark finning
paragraph: 32 (1) No person shall engage in the practice of shark finning.

heading: Definition of shark finning
paragraph: (2) In this section, shark finning means the practice of removing the fins from a shark and discarding the remainder of the shark while at sea.

heading: Importation and exportation
paragraph: 32.1 (1) No person shall import into Canada or export from Canada, or attempt to so import or export, any shark fins or parts of shark fins that are not attached to a shark carcass except in accordance with a permit issued under subsection (2).

heading: Issuance of permit
paragraph: (2) The Minister may issue a permit authorizing the importation or exportation into or from Canada of any shark fins or parts of shark fins that are not attached to a shark carcass and impose any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate in the permit

heading: Issuance of permit
paragraph: (a) if the importation or exportation is for the purpose of scientific research relating to shark conservation; and

heading: Issuance of permit
paragraph: (b) if, in the Minister's opinion, the scientific research is likely to benefit the survival of any shark species or is required to enhance the chances of survival of any shark species in the wild.

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (3) The Minister may amend, suspend or cancel a permit issued under subsection (2).

heading: Unlawful sale or possession
paragraph: 33 No person shall purchase, sell or possess any fish that has been caught in contravention of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Definition of "fishing plan"
paragraph: 33.1 (1) In this section, fishing plan means a Nisga'a annual fishing plan, as defined in the Fisheries Chapter of the Nisga'a Final Agreement given effect by the Nisga'a Final Agreement Act, that is approved, or varied and approved, by the Minister in accordance with that Agreement.

heading: Contravention of fishing plan
paragraph: (2) Where a fishing plan stipulates that this subsection applies to certain of its provisions relating to persons engaged in harvesting, sale or related activities, no person shall contravene any of those provisions.

heading: Conditions of prosecution
paragraph: (3) No proceedings may be commenced in respect of an offence for the contravention of subsection (2)

heading: Conditions of prosecution
paragraph: (a) except in accordance with an agreement, made under paragraph 93 of the Fisheries Chapter of the Nisga'a Final Agreement, concerning enforcement of federal laws or Nisga'a laws; or

heading: Conditions of prosecution
paragraph: (b) unless the Minister, or a person appointed to a position in the Department of Fisheries and Oceans who is authorized by the Minister, considers such proceedings to be necessary to ensure compliance with the fishing plan.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 34 (1) The following definitions apply in this section and sections 34.1 to 42.5.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: deleterious substance means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any substance that, if added to any water, would degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of that water so that it is rendered or is likely to be rendered deleterious to fish or fish habitat or to the use by man of fish that frequent that water, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any water that contains a substance in such quantity or concentration, or that has been so treated, processed or changed, by heat or other means, from a natural state that it would, if added to any other water, degrade or alter or form part of a process of degradation or alteration of the quality of that water so that it is rendered or is likely to be rendered deleterious to fish or fish habitat or to the use by man of fish that frequent that water,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and without limiting the generality of the foregoing includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any substance or class of substances prescribed pursuant to paragraph (2)(a),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any water that contains any substance or class of substances in a quantity or concentration that is equal to or in excess of a quantity or concentration prescribed in respect of that substance or class of substances pursuant to paragraph (2)(b), and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) any water that has been subjected to a treatment, process or change prescribed pursuant to paragraph (2)(c); (substance nocive)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: deposit means any discharging, spraying, releasing, spilling, leaking, seeping, pouring, emitting, emptying, throwing, dumping or placing; (immersion ou rejet)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: designated project means a project that is designated by regulations made under paragraph 43(1)(i.5) or that belongs to a class of projects that is designated by those regulations and that consists of works, undertakings or activities, including any works, undertakings or activities that the Minister designates to be associated with the project; (projet designe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ecologically significant area means an area designated by regulations made under subsection 35.2(2); (zone d'importance ecologique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: water frequented by fish means Canadian fisheries waters. (eaux ou vivent des poissons)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Regulations for purpose of definition deleterious substance

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) substances and classes of substances,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) quantities or concentrations of substances and classes of substances in water, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) treatments, processes and changes of water

heading: Definitions
paragraph: for the purpose of paragraphs (c) to (e) of the definition deleterious substance in subsection (1).

heading: Application - Designated project
paragraph: (3) Any provision of this Act that applies to works, undertakings or activities also applies to the works, undertakings or activities of a designated project, except paragraphs 34.4(2)(a) to (c) and (e) and 35(2)(a) to (c) and (e).

heading: Factors
paragraph: 34.1 (1) Before recommending to the Governor in Council that a regulation be made in respect of section 34.4, 35 or 35.1 or under subsection 35.2(10), 36(5) or (5.1), paragraph 43(1)(b.2) or subsection 43(5) or before exercising any power under subsection 34.3(2), (3) or (7), paragraph 34.4(2)(b) or (c), subsection 34.4(4), paragraph 35(2)(b) or (c) or subsection 35(4), 35.1(3), 35.2(7) or 36(5.2), or under subsection 37(2) with regard to an offence under subsection 40(1), the Minister, prescribed person or prescribed entity, as the case may be, shall consider the following factors:

heading: Factors
paragraph: (a) the contribution to the productivity of relevant fisheries by the fish or fish habitat that is likely to be affected;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (b) fisheries management objectives;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (c) whether there are measures and standards

heading: Factors
paragraph: (i) to avoid the death of fish or to mitigate the extent of their death or offset their death, or

heading: Factors
paragraph: (ii) to avoid, mitigate or offset the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (d) the cumulative effects of the carrying on of the work, undertaking or activity referred to in a recommendation or an exercise of power, in combination with other works, undertakings or activities that have been or are being carried on, on fish and fish habitat;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (e) any fish habitat banks, as defined in section 42.01, that may be affected;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (f) whether any measures and standards to offset the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat give priority to the restoration of degraded fish habitat;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (g) Indigenous knowledge of the Indigenous peoples of Canada that has been provided to the Minister; and

heading: Factors
paragraph: (h) any other factor that the Minister considers relevant.

heading: Application of subsection (1)
paragraph: (2) The obligation to consider the factors set out in subsection (1) applies only to the recommendations and powers that continue to be made or exercised by the Minister after an order is made under subsection 43.2(1) that sets out the powers, duties or functions that the designated minister may exercise or perform.

heading: Standards and codes of practice
paragraph: 34.2 (1) The Minister may establish standards and codes of practice for

heading: Standards and codes of practice
paragraph: (a) the avoidance of death to fish and harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat;

heading: Standards and codes of practice
paragraph: (b) the conservation and protection of fish or fish habitat; and

heading: Standards and codes of practice
paragraph: (c) the prevention of pollution.

heading: Content
paragraph: (2) The standards and codes of practice may specify procedures, practices or standards in relation to works, undertakings and activities during any phase of their construction, operation, modification, decommissioning or abandonment.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) Before establishing any standards and codes of practice, the Minister may consult with any provincial government, any Indigenous governing body, any government department or agency or any persons interested in the protection of fish or fish habitat and the prevention of pollution.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall publish any standards and codes of practice established under this section, or give notice of them, in the Canada Gazette and he or she may also do so in any other manner that he or she considers appropriate.

heading: Studies, etc. - management or control of obstruction
paragraph: 34.3 (1) If the Minister considers that doing so is necessary to ensure the free passage of fish or the protection of fish or fish habitat, the owner or person who has the charge, management or control of an obstruction or any other thing that is detrimental to fish or fish habitat shall, on the Minister's request and within the period specified by him or her, conduct studies, analyses, samplings and evaluations, and provide the Minister with any document and other information relating to them, to the obstruction or thing or to the fish or fish habitat that is or is likely to be affected by the obstruction or thing.

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (2) If the Minister considers that doing so is necessary to ensure the free passage of fish or the protection of fish or fish habitat, the owner or person who has the charge, management or control of an obstruction or any other thing that is detrimental to fish or fish habitat shall, on the Minister's order, within the period specified by him or her and in accordance with any of his or her specifications,

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (a) remove the obstruction or thing;

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (b) construct a fishway;

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (c) implement a system of catching fish before the obstruction or thing, transporting them beyond it and releasing them back into the water;

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (d) install a fish stop or a diverter;

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (e) install a fish guard, a screen, a covering, netting or any other device to prevent the passage of fish into any water intake, ditch, channel or canal;

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (f) maintain the flow of water necessary to permit the free passage of fish; or

heading: Minister's order
paragraph: (g) maintain at all times the characteristics of the water and the water flow downstream of the obstruction or thing that are sufficient for the conservation and protection of the fish and fish habitat.

heading: Modification, repair and maintenance
paragraph: (3) On the Minister's order, the owner or person referred to in subsection (2) shall

heading: Modification, repair and maintenance
paragraph: (a) make any provision that the Minister considers necessary for the free passage of fish or the protection of fish or fish habitat during the carrying on of any activity mentioned in that subsection;

heading: Modification, repair and maintenance
paragraph: (b) operate and maintain anything referred to in that subsection in a good and effective condition and in accordance with any specifications of the Minister; and

heading: Modification, repair and maintenance
paragraph: (c) modify or repair it in accordance with any specifications of the Minister.

heading: Obstruction of free passage of fish
paragraph: (4) No person shall

heading: Obstruction of free passage of fish
paragraph: (a) damage or obstruct any fishway constructed or used to enable fish to pass over or around any obstruction;

heading: Obstruction of free passage of fish
paragraph: (b) damage or obstruct any fishway, fish stop or diverter constructed or installed on the Minister's order;

heading: Obstruction of free passage of fish
paragraph: (c) stop, impede or hinder fish from entering or passing through any fishway, or stop, impede or hinder fish from surmounting any obstruction or leap;

heading: Obstruction of free passage of fish
paragraph: (d) damage, remove or authorize the removal of any fish guard, screen, covering, netting or other device installed on the Minister's order; or

heading: Obstruction of free passage of fish
paragraph: (e) fish in any manner within 23 m downstream from the lower entrance to any fishway, obstruction or leap.

heading: Exception - removal for repairs
paragraph: (5) Despite paragraph (4)(d), a person may remove or authorize the removal of any fish guard, screen, covering, netting or other device installed on the Minister's order if the removal is required for modification, repair or maintenance.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (6) Orders made under this section are not statutory instruments for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (7) The Minister may make regulations respecting the flow of water that is to be maintained to ensure the free passage of fish or the protection of fish or fish habitat.

heading: Death of fish
paragraph: 34.4 (1) No person shall carry on any work, undertaking or activity, other than fishing, that results in the death of fish.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A person may carry on a work, undertaking or activity without contravening subsection (1) if

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) the work, undertaking or activity is a prescribed work, undertaking or activity or belongs to a prescribed class of works, undertakings or activities, as the case may be, or is carried on in or around prescribed Canadian fisheries waters, and the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the prescribed conditions;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the carrying on of the work, undertaking or activity is authorized by the Minister and the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the conditions established by the Minister;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) the carrying on of the work, undertaking or activity is authorized by a prescribed person or prescribed entity and the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the conditions set out in the authorization;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (d) the death results from the doing of anything that is authorized, permitted or required under this Act;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (e) the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the regulations;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (f) the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with a permit issued under subsection 35.1(3), in the case of a work, undertaking or activity that is part of a designated project and that is designated by the Minister under subsection 35.1(2); or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (g) the work, undertaking or activity is a prescribed work, undertaking or activity under paragraph 35.2(10)(a) or belongs to a prescribed class of works, undertakings or activities under that paragraph, as the case may be, and carried on in an ecologically significant area in accordance with an authorization issued under subsection 35.2(7).

heading: Other conditions
paragraph: (3) The prescribed person or prescribed entity referred to in paragraph (2)(c) may, in addition to the prescribed classes of conditions impose, subject to the regulations, any other conditions that they consider appropriate in the circumstances.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, for the purposes of paragraph (2)(a) and subject to paragraph 43(1)(i.1), make regulations prescribing anything that is authorized to be prescribed.

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation - paragraph (2)(b)
paragraph: (5) The Minister may amend, suspend or cancel an authorization issued under paragraph (2)(b).

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation - paragraph (2)(c)
paragraph: (6) A prescribed person or prescribed entity referred to in paragraph (2)(c) may amend, suspend or cancel an authorization issued under that paragraph.

heading: Harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat
paragraph: 35 (1) No person shall carry on any work, undertaking or activity that results in the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A person may carry on a work, undertaking or activity without contravening subsection (1) if

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) the work, undertaking or activity is a prescribed work, undertaking or activity or belongs to a prescribed class of works, undertakings or activities, as the case may be, or is carried on in or around prescribed Canadian fisheries waters, and the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the prescribed conditions;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the carrying on of the work, undertaking or activity is authorized by the Minister and the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the conditions established by the Minister;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) the carrying on of the work, undertaking or activity is authorized by a prescribed person or prescribed entity and the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the conditions set out in the authorization;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (d) the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction results from the doing of anything that is authorized, permitted or required under this Act;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (e) the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with the regulations;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (f) the work, undertaking or activity is carried on in accordance with a permit issued under subsection 35.1(3), in the case of a work, undertaking or activity that is part of a designated project and that is designated by the Minister under subsection 35.1(2); or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (g) the work, undertaking or activity is a prescribed work, undertaking or activity under paragraph 35.2(10)(a) or belongs to a prescribed class of works, undertakings or activities under that paragraph, as the case may be, and is carried on in an ecologically significant area in accordance with an authorization issued under subsection 35.2(7).

heading: Other conditions
paragraph: (3) The prescribed person or prescribed entity referred to in paragraph (2)(c) may, in addition to the prescribed classes of conditions impose, subject to the regulations, any other conditions that they consider appropriate in the circumstances.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, for the purposes of paragraph (2)(a) and subject to paragraph 43(1)(i.1), make regulations prescribing anything that is authorized to be prescribed.

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation - paragraph (2)(b)
paragraph: (5) The Minister may amend, suspend or cancel an authorization issued under paragraph (2)(b).

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation - paragraph (2)(c)
paragraph: (6) A prescribed person or prescribed entity referred to in paragraph (2)(c) may amend, suspend or cancel an authorization issued under that paragraph.

heading: Designated project
paragraph: 35.1 (1) The Minister may designate, as a work, undertaking or activity that is associated with a designated project, any work, undertaking or activity that the Minister considers likely to result in the death of fish or the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat.

heading: Work, undertaking or activity designated by Minister
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall designate any work, undertaking or activity that is part of a designated project and that the Minister considers likely to result in the death of fish or the harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of fish habitat.

heading: Issuance of permit
paragraph: (3) The Minister may issue a permit to carry on any work, undertaking or activity designated under subsection (2) and attach any conditions to it.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (4) No person shall carry on any work, undertaking or activity that is designated under subsection (2) except in accordance with a permit issued under subsection (3).

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (5) The Minister may amend, suspend or cancel a permit issued under subsection (3).

heading: Ecologically significant area
paragraph: 35.2 (1) No person shall carry on a work, undertaking or activity prescribed under paragraph (10)(a) or that belongs to a prescribed class under that paragraph, in an ecologically significant area except in accordance with an authorization issued under subsection (7).

heading: Designation - ecologically significant area
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations designating ecologically significant areas.

heading: Requirement to provide information
paragraph: (3) Any person who proposes to carry on a work, undertaking or activity referred to in subsection (1) in an ecologically significant area shall provide the Minister with any document and other information that is required by regulation in respect of the prescribed work, undertaking or activity, or the water, place, fish or fish habitat that is likely to be affected by the prescribed work, undertaking or activity.

heading: Request for additional information
paragraph: (4) Regulations made for the purpose of subsection (3) do not prevent the Minister from requesting additional information that he or she considers necessary in the circumstances.

heading: Compliance with request
paragraph: (5) Every person who is required to provide any additional information must provide it within the time and in the manner that the Minister specifies.

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (6) The Minister may, on request in writing from any person who is required to provide any additional information, extend the specified time.

heading: Powers of Minister
paragraph: (7) If the Minister is satisfied, after having reviewed any document and other information provided under subsection (3) or (4), that avoidance and mitigation measures may be implemented to achieve the prescribed objectives for the conservation and protection of fish and fish habitat, he or she may authorize, subject to the regulations made under subsection (10), the carrying on of the work, undertaking or activity referred to in subsection (1) in an ecologically significant area, on any conditions that he or she considers appropriate.

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation - authorization
paragraph: (8) The Minister may amend, suspend or cancel an authorization issued under subsection (7).

heading: Fish habitat restoration plan
paragraph: (9) The Minister shall, as soon as feasible, prepare a fish habitat restoration plan for an ecologically significant area, if he or she is of the opinion that fish habitat restoration in that ecologically significant area is required in order to meet any prescribed objectives for the conservation and protection of fish and fish habitat.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (10) The Governor in Council may, on the Minister's recommendation, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing works, undertakings or activities or classes of works, undertakings or activities, for the purposes of this section;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting any document or other information that is required to be provided under subsection (3), including the manner in which and the time within which it is to be provided;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the objectives for the conservation and protection of fish and fish habitat in an ecologically significant area;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) prescribing works, undertakings or activities or classes of works, undertakings or activities that the Minister shall not authorize under paragraphs 34.4(2)(b) and 35(2)(b) to be carried on in an ecologically significant area;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) prescribing conditions under which and requirements subject to which the Minister may issue an authorization under subsection (7);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the manner and circumstances relating to the amendment, suspension or cancellation of an authorization referred to in subsection (7); and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the process by which a person may request an amendment, suspension or cancellation of an authorization under subsection (7).

heading: Throwing overboard of certain substances prohibited
paragraph: 36 (1) No one shall

heading: Throwing overboard of certain substances prohibited
paragraph: (a) throw overboard ballast, coal ashes, stones or other prejudicial or deleterious substances in any river, harbour or roadstead, or in any water where fishing is carried on;

heading: Throwing overboard of certain substances prohibited
paragraph: (b) leave or deposit or cause to be thrown, left or deposited, on the shore, beach or bank of any water or on the beach between high and low water mark, remains or offal of fish or of marine animals; or

heading: Throwing overboard of certain substances prohibited
paragraph: (c) leave decayed or decaying fish in any net or other fishing apparatus.

heading: Disposal of remains, etc.
paragraph: (2) Remains or offal described in subsection (1) may be buried ashore, above high water mark.

paragraph: (3) Where, as a result of a deposit that is not authorized under section 36, a deleterious substance enters water frequented by fish, the persons described in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) are, subject to subsection (4) in the case of the persons described in paragraph (1)(a) and to the extent determined according to their respective degrees of fault or negligence in the case of the persons described in paragraph (1)(b), jointly and severally liable for all loss of income incurred by any licensed commercial fisherman, to the extent that the loss can be established to have been incurred as a result of the deposit or of a prohibition to fish resulting therefrom, and all such loss is recoverable with costs in proceedings brought or taken therefor in any court of competent jurisdiction.

paragraph: (4) The liability of any person described in paragraph (1)(a) is absolute and does not depend on proof of fault or negligence but no such person is liable for any costs and expenses pursuant to subsection (1) or loss of income pursuant to subsection (3) if he establishes that the occurrence giving rise to the liability was wholly caused by

heading: Defences to liability
paragraph: (a) an act of war, hostilities, civil war, insurrection or a natural phenomenon of an exceptional, inevitable and irresistible character; or

heading: Defences to liability
paragraph: (b) an act or omission with intent to cause damage by a person other than a person for whose wrongful act or omission he is by law responsible.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this section limits or restricts any right of recourse that any person who is liable pursuant to this section may have against any other person.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (6) No proceedings may be commenced under subsections (1) to (3) at any time later than two years after the occurrence to which the proceedings relate could reasonably be expected to have become known to Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province or to any licensed commercial fisherman, as the case may be.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (7) Subsections (1) to (3) do not apply in respect of any deposit of a deleterious substance that, within the meaning of Part 8 or 9 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, constitutes a discharge of a pollutant caused by or otherwise attributable to a vessel.

heading: Other civil remedies not affected
paragraph: (8) No civil remedy for any act or omission is suspended or affected by reason only that the act or omission is authorized under this Act, is an offence under this Act or gives rise to civil liability under this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 42.01 The following definitions apply in this section and sections 42.02 to 42.04.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: conservation project means a work, undertaking or activity that is carried on by a proponent for the purpose of creating, restoring or enhancing fish habitat within a service area in order to acquire habitat credits. (projet de conservation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fish habitat bank means an area of a fish habitat that has been created, restored or enhanced by the carrying on of one or more conservation projects within a service area and in respect of which area the Minister has certified any habitat credit under paragraph 42.02(1)(b). (reserve d'habitats)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: habitat credit means a unit of measure that is agreed to between any proponent and the Minister under section 42.02 that quantifies the benefits of a conservation project. (credit d'habitat)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: proponent means a person who proposes the carrying on of a conservation project and any other work, undertaking or activity within a proposed service area. (promoteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: service area means the geographical area that encompasses a fish habitat bank and one or more conservation projects and within which area a proponent carries on a work, undertaking or activity. (zone de service)

heading: Arrangements respecting fish habitat banks
paragraph: 42.02 (1) For the purposes of sections 42.01 to 42.04, the Minister may

heading: Arrangements respecting fish habitat banks
paragraph: (a) establish a system for the creation, allocation and management of a proponent's habitat credits in relation to a conservation project; and

heading: Arrangements respecting fish habitat banks
paragraph: (b) issue a certificate to the proponent respecting the validity of any habitat credit acquired from the carrying on of a conservation project.

heading: Arrangements
paragraph: (2) In exercising the powers referred to in subsection (1), the Minister may enter into arrangements with any proponent.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (3) An arrangement referred to in subsection (2) shall include, among other things,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) any document and other information that describes the proposed fish habitat bank, conservation project and service area;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) a written confirmation that the Department of Fisheries and Oceans and anyone authorized to act on the Department's behalf is authorized to access the site of the conservation project for the term of the arrangement;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) a description of the administration, management and general operation of the arrangement by the parties, including

heading: Contents
paragraph: (i) a procedure for proposing a conservation project and an approval process,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (ii) a habitat credit certification process,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (iii) a process for habitat credit evaluation and any re-evaluation that may be required by the Minister,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (iv) habitat credit accounting procedures respecting the habitat credit ledger,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (v) progress reports on the conservation project, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (vi) any other relevant matters respecting the administration of the arrangement;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) reports on the performance of the arrangement;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) the form and manner in which the arrangement may be amended;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (f) the date on which the arrangement comes into force; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (g) the signatures of the parties.

heading: Use of habitat credit within service area
paragraph: 42.03 A proponent may only use their certified habitat credits in respect of a fish habitat bank within a service area to offset the adverse effects on fish or fish habitat from the carrying on of a work, undertaking or activity authorized or permitted to be carried on in that service area.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 42.04 The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the establishment of a system for the creation, allocation and management of habitat credits referred to in paragraph 42.02(1)(a);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the issuance of a certificate of validity of any habitat credit referred to in paragraph 42.02(1)(b); and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting an arrangement with any proponent.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: 42.1 (1) The Minister shall, as soon as feasible after the end of each fiscal year, prepare and cause to be laid before each house of Parliament a report on the administration and enforcement of the provisions of this Act relating to fish and fish habitat protection and pollution prevention for that year.

heading: Statistical summary
paragraph: (2) The annual report shall include a statistical summary of convictions under section 40 for that year.

paragraph: (h) respecting the obstruction and pollution of any waters frequented by fish;

paragraph: (i.11) respecting the process relating to the issuance of the authorizations referred to in paragraph 34.4(2)(b) or (c) or 35(2)(b) or (c) or the permits referred to in subsection 35.1(3);

paragraph: (i.2) prescribing the documents or other information that are to be provided for the obtaining of the authorizations referred to in paragraph 34.4(2)(b) or (c) or 35(2)(b) or (c) or the permits referred to in subsection 35.1(3), or for the amendment, suspension or cancellation of those authorizations or permits;

paragraph: (i.8) respecting the process by which a person may request an amendment, suspension or cancellation of an authorization under subsection 34.4(5) or (6) or 35(5) or (6), or a permit under subsection 35.1(5), as the case may be;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) respecting the import or export of fish;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j.1) prescribing the circumstances in which the Indigenous knowledge of the Indigenous peoples of Canada that is provided to the Minister under this Act in confidence may be disclosed without written consent;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) respecting the taking or carrying of fish or any part thereof from one province to any other province;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (l) prescribing the powers and duties of persons engaged or employed in the administration or enforcement of this Act and providing for the carrying out of those powers and duties;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (m) if a close time, fishing quota or limit on the size or weight of fish or fishing gear or equipment has been fixed in respect of an area under the regulations, authorizing persons referred to in paragraph (l) to vary the close time, fishing quota or limit or fishing gear or equipment in respect of that area or any portion of that area;

paragraph: (n) establishing a list of aquatic invasive species;

paragraph: (o) respecting the management and control of aquatic invasive species, including regulations

paragraph: (ii) respecting the possession of members of such species, and their import, export and transport,

paragraph: (iv) respecting the handling of members of such species,

paragraph: (v) respecting the treatment and destruction of members of those species,

paragraph: (vii) respecting the powers of a fishery officer and fishery guardian to manage and control those species,

paragraph: (viii) authorizing a fishery officer and fishery guardian to exercise their powers with respect to a species that the officer or guardian, as the case may be, has reasonable grounds to believe is an aquatic invasive species, or

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may make regulations establishing conditions for the exercise of the Minister's power to make regulations under subsection (3).

heading: Amendments to list of aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (3) The Minister may, by regulation, add species to the list of aquatic invasive species established by regulations made under paragraph (1)(n) or remove species from that list, and vary the places to which regulations made under paragraph (1)(o) apply.

heading: Paragraph 43(1)(i.5)
paragraph: (4) Regulations made under paragraph (1)(i.5) may include as a criterion for designation the fact that a decision has been made under an Act of Parliament to subject the project to an impact assessment.

heading: Regulations exempting certain Canadian fisheries waters
paragraph: (5) The Governor in Council may make regulations exempting any Canadian fisheries waters from the application of sections 34.3, 34.4 and 35 and subsections 38(4) and (4.1).

heading: Recommendation
