paragraph: (n) the Possession and Export of Elvers Regulations.

heading: Application
paragraph: (5) Sections 18 to 21, 23 and 26 to 29 do not apply with respect to fishing and related activities carried out under the authority of a licence issued under the Aboriginal Communal Fishing Licences Regulations.

heading: Application
paragraph: (6) Sections 18 to 21, 23, 26 and 29 do not apply in respect of Inuit domestic fishing, being the exercise by a person of the right to harvest any species or stock of fish for food, social and ceremonial purposes in accordance with the Agreement defined in section 2 of the Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement Act.

heading: Periods of Time
paragraph: 4 Where a period of time is set out in any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4), the period

heading: Periods of Time
paragraph: (a) unless otherwise specified, begins at 00:00 h on the first day set out and ends at 24:00 h on the last day set out; and

heading: Periods of Time
paragraph: (b) begins and ends in each calendar year except that where the period is stated to end on a day in a month that occurs earlier in a calendar year than the month in which the period begins, that period begins in one calendar year and ends in the next calendar year.

heading: Periods of Time
paragraph: 5 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a reference to time in a provision of any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4) or a notice given under section 7 is a reference to local time in effect in the province or portion thereof that is closest to the waters in respect of which the provision or the notice applies unless, in the case of a notice, it is otherwise stated in the notice.

heading: Periods of Time
paragraph: (2) Where notice is given under section 7 in respect of any close time set out in the Foreign Vessel Fishing Regulations, that time is a reference to Greenwich time.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: 6 (1) If a close time, fishing quota, limit on the size or weight of fish or fishing gear or equipment is fixed in respect of an area under any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4), the Regional Director-General may, by order, vary that close time, quota, limit, gear or equipment in respect of that area or any portion of that area.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (2) If a close time, fishing quota or fishing gear or equipment for herring or salmon fishing is fixed in respect of an area under the Pacific Fishery Regulations, 1993, a fishery officer may, by order, vary that close time, quota, gear or equipment in respect of that area or any portion of that area.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (3) If a close time, fishing quota, limit on the size or weight of fish or fishing gear or equipment is fixed in respect of an area of non-tidal waters for any species of fish other than salmon under the British Columbia Sport Fishing Regulations, 1996, the director responsible for fisheries management in the ministry responsible for fisheries in the Government of British Columbia may, by order, vary that close time, quota, limit, gear or equipment in respect of that area or any portion of that area.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (4) If a close time, fishing quota, limit on the size or weight of fish or fishing gear or equipment is fixed in respect of an area of non-tidal waters for any species of fish other than salmon under the Yukon Territory Fishery Regulations, the Director of the Fish and Wildlife Branch of the Department of Environment for the Yukon Territory may, by order, vary that close time, quota, limit, gear or equipment in respect of that area or any portion of that area.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (5) If a close time, fishing quota, limit on the size or weight of fish or fishing gear or equipment is fixed in respect of an area of the province of New Brunswick under the Maritime Provinces Fishery Regulations, the director responsible for fisheries management in the ministry responsible for fisheries in the Government of New Brunswick may, by order, vary that close time, quota, limit, gear or equipment in respect of that area or any portion of that area for any species of fish listed in Appendix A of the Canada-New Brunswick Memorandum of Understanding on Recreational Fisheries, dated June 18, 2001, as amended from time to time.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (6) If a close time, fishing quota, limit on the size or weight of fish or fishing gear or equipment is fixed in respect of an area of the province of Nova Scotia under the Maritime Provinces Fishery Regulations, the director responsible for fisheries management in the ministry responsible for fisheries in the Government of Nova Scotia may, by order, vary that close time, quota, limit, gear or equipment in respect of that area or any portion of that area for any species of fish listed in Appendix A to the Canada-Nova Scotia Memorandum of Understanding on Recreational Fisheries, dated September 17, 2003, as amended from time to time.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: 7 (1) Subject to subsection (3), where a variation order is made under section 6, notice of the variation shall be given to the persons affected or likely to be affected by the variation by one or more of the following methods:

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (a) broadcasting the notice over a commercial or marine radio station, a radio station operated by the Department or a radio station located on a vessel under contract to the Department that broadcasts in the area or in the vicinity of the area affected by the variation;

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (b) publishing the notice in a newspaper that is circulated in the vicinity of the area affected by the variation;

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (c) posting the notice in the area or in the vicinity of the area affected by the variation;

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (d) transmitting the notice by electronic means to those persons;

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (d.1) posting the notice on the web site of the Department or of the province;

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (e) having a fishery officer or fishery guardian give oral notice thereof to those persons; and

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (f) publishing the notice in the next issue of a sport fishing publication, published periodically by the applicable province or by the Department.

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (3) Where a variation order is made under subsection 6(1) in respect of the Foreign Vessel Fishing Regulations, notice of the variation shall be given to the persons affected or likely to be affected by the variation

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (a) by one or more of the methods set out in paragraphs (1)(a) to (e); or

heading: Variation Orders
paragraph: (b) by transmitting the notice to the consular or diplomatic authorities of the flag state of the foreign fishing vessel carrying those persons, or to the representative of the flag state named in an application referred to in paragraph 7(f) of the Coastal Fisheries Protection Regulations in respect of the foreign fishing vessel carrying those persons.

heading: Application for Documents
paragraph: 8 (1) The Minister may require an applicant for a document to submit

heading: Application for Documents
paragraph: (a) such information in addition to that included in the application as may reasonably be regarded as relevant; and

heading: Application for Documents
paragraph: (b) a statutory declaration verifying the information given in the application or verifying the information submitted under paragraph (a).

heading: Application for Documents
paragraph: (2) An application from a corporation for a document shall be signed by an officer of the corporation.

heading: Signing of Documents
paragraph: 9 Where it is indicated in a document that it is not valid unless signed, the holder of the document shall, on receipt of the document, immediately sign it in ink in the space provided.

heading: Expiration of Documents
paragraph: 10 Unless otherwise specified in a document, a document expires

heading: Expiration of Documents
paragraph: (a) where it is issued for a calendar year, on December 31 of the year for which it is issued; or

heading: Expiration of Documents
paragraph: (b) where it is issued for a fiscal year, on March 31 of the year for which it is issued.

heading: Carrying and Producing Licences, Registration Cards and Certificates
paragraph: 11 Every holder of a licence, a fisher's registration card or a provincial or territorial fisher's certificate shall carry it at all times while engaged in any activity to which it relates and shall produce it on the demand of a fishery officer or fishery guardian.

heading: Carrying and Producing Licences, Registration Cards and Certificates
paragraph: 12 The operator of a vessel in respect of which a vessel registration card has been issued shall have the vessel registration card and the licence authorizing the use of the vessel on board the vessel whenever the vessel is engaged as a fishing vessel and shall produce them on the demand of a fishery officer or fishery guardian.

heading: Amending Documents
paragraph: 14 (1) Notwithstanding paragraph 15(1)(a), a fishery officer who is employed by the Department or any employee of the Department engaged in the issuance of documents may, on the request of the holder of a document,

heading: Amending Documents
paragraph: (a) amend the document and sign and date the amendment; or

heading: Amending Documents
paragraph: (b) cancel the document and issue a replacement document.

heading: Amending Documents
paragraph: (2) Where a document contains an error or was issued in error, a fishery officer or an employee referred to in subsection (1) may request the holder of the document to surrender it.

heading: Amending Documents
paragraph: (3) Where the holder of a document receives a request referred to in subsection (2), that person shall immediately comply with the request.

heading: Alteration and Use of Documents
paragraph: 15 (1) No person shall

heading: Alteration and Use of Documents
paragraph: (a) alter or deface any document;

heading: Alteration and Use of Documents
paragraph: (b) use or produce any document that has been altered or defaced; or

heading: Alteration and Use of Documents
paragraph: (c) use or produce any document issued to another person under the pretence of being the holder thereof.

heading: Alteration and Use of Documents
paragraph: (2) No holder of a fisher's registration card shall permit another person to use that registration card.

heading: Alteration and Use of Documents
paragraph: (3) Where a licence specifies the person or persons who may fish under the licence, the holder of that licence shall not permit any person other than the person or persons so specified to use that licence.

heading: Transfer of Documents and Rights and Privileges
paragraph: 16 (1) A document is the property of the Crown and is not transferable.

heading: Transfer of Documents and Rights and Privileges
paragraph: (2) The issuance of a document of any type to any person does not imply or confer any future right or privilege for that person to be issued a document of the same type or any other type.

heading: Change of Name or Address and Replacement of Documents
paragraph: 17 (1) Where a person is the holder of a document and has a change of name or address, or the document is lost, stolen or destroyed or becomes illegible, that person shall notify the Minister in writing within 15 days after the occurrence of the event and the Minister may issue a replacement document showing any applicable changes.

heading: Change of Name or Address and Replacement of Documents
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a replacement document, the holder shall immediately return to the Department the document being replaced if it is still in the holder's possession.

heading: Change of Name or Address and Replacement of Documents
paragraph: (3) A holder of a replacement document who recovers the document that was replaced shall immediately return it to the Department.

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: 18 (1) Where there is a transfer of ownership of a registered vessel or a loss, destruction, dismantling or other removal of a registered vessel from use as a fishing vessel, the person in whose name the vessel is registered shall

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: (a) notify the Minister in writing of the event within 15 days after the occurrence of the event; and

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: (b) where the person is still in possession of the vessel registration card or any licence issued in respect of the vessel, return the document to the Minister with the notification required under paragraph (a).

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: (2) A notification of transfer of ownership given under paragraph (1)(a) shall include the name and address of the new owner.

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: 19 Where there is a transfer of ownership of a registered vessel and the vessel is not registered in the name of the new owner,

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: (a) no person shall use that vessel as a fishing vessel; and

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: (b) the new owner of that vessel shall not permit another person to use the vessel as a fishing vessel.

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: 20 Where a transfer of ownership of a registered vessel is to take place and it is not intended that the vessel will be used in any activity that requires the vessel to be registered, the person in whose name the vessel is registered shall, prior to the transfer, remove the vessel registration number that is painted on or affixed to the vessel in accordance with section 26.

heading: Transfer of Ownership or Loss of Vessel
paragraph: 21 Where there is a change in the registered ownership of shares of a corporation that holds a licence that results in a different person being the registered owner of the largest number of shares of the corporation or that results in any one person being the registered owner of more than 50 per cent of the shares of that corporation, the corporation shall notify the Minister in writing of the change within 15 days after the date of the change.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: 22 (1) For the proper management and control of fisheries and the conservation and protection of fish, the Minister may specify in a licence any condition that is not inconsistent with these Regulations or any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4) and in particular, but not restricting the generality of the foregoing, may specify conditions respecting any of the following matters:

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (a) the species of fish and quantities thereof that are permitted to be taken or transported;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (b) the age, sex, stage of development or size of fish that are permitted to be taken or transported;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (c) the waters in which fishing is permitted to be carried out;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (d) the location from which and to which fish is permitted to be transported;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (e) the vessel from which and to which fish is permitted to be transhipped;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (f) the period during which fishing or transporting fish is permitted to be carried out;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (g) the vessel that is permitted to be used and the persons who are permitted to operate it;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (h) the type, size and quantity of fishing gear and equipment that is permitted to be used and the manner in which it is permitted to be used;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (i) the specific location at which fishing gear is permitted to be set;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (j) the distance to be maintained between fishing gear;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (k) information that the holder of the licence shall report to the Department prior to commencement of a fishing trip with respect to where and when fishing will be carried out, including the method by which, the times at which and the person to whom the report is to be made;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (l) information that the master of the vessel shall report to the Department from sea, including the method by which, the times at which and the person to whom the report is to be made;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (m) the location and times at which landing of fish from the vessel is permitted;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (n) verification by an observer of the weight and species of any fish caught and retained;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (o) the method permitted for landing of fish from the vessel and the method by which the weight of the fish is to be determined;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (p) records that the master of the vessel shall keep of any fishing activity carried out under the licence or of the sale or transporting of fish caught under the licence, including the manner and form in which the records are to be kept, the times at which and the person to whom the records are to be produced and the period for which the records are to be retained;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (q) the type, size and colour of containers to hold or transport fish and the marking of such containers for identification of the source of the fish;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (r) the marking or tagging of fish for identification of the source of the fish;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (s) the segregation of fish by species on board the vessel;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (t) the time within which findings and data obtained as a result of fishing for an experimental or scientific purpose are to be forwarded to the Minister;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (u) the manner in which fish caught for an educational or public display purpose are to be held and transported;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (v) the species and quantities of fish that may be released or transferred under a licence issued under Part VIII;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (w) the period during which the release or transfer of fish is to be carried out under a licence issued under Part VIII;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (x) the waters or fish rearing facility into which the fish are to be released or transferred under a licence issued under Part VIII;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (y) the waters or fish rearing facility from which the fish are to be taken under a licence issued under Part VIII;

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (z) the method and manner of transporting the fish to be released or transferred under a licence issued under Part VIII; and

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (z.1) the method of disposing of any water, container or other material used in the transporting of fish under a licence issued under Part VIII.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, for the purposes of the conservation and protection of fish, amend the conditions of a licence.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (3) A notice of any amendment referred to in subsection (2) shall be

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (a) sent to the licence holder by registered mail; or

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (b) personally delivered to the licence holder by a fishery officer.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (4) An amendment referred to in subsection (2) is effective from the time the licence holder receives the notice referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (5) A notice referred to in subsection (3) forms part of the licence to which it relates and the licence holder shall, on receipt of such a notice, attach the notice to the licence.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (6) Compliance with the Act and the regulations made under the Act is a condition of every licence.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (7) No person carrying out any activity under the authority of a licence shall contravene or fail to comply with any condition of the licence.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: 23 (1) This section does not apply in respect of a licence issued for the purpose of recreational or sport fishing.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (2) Where the holder of a licence or the operator named in a licence is unable to engage in the activity authorized by the licence or use the vessel specified in the licence because of circumstances beyond the control of the holder or operator, a fishery officer who is employed by the Department or any employee of the Department engaged in the issuance of licences may, on the request of the holder or the holder's agent, authorize in writing

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (a) another person to carry out the activity under the licence; or

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (b) the use of another vessel under the licence.

heading: Conditions of Licences
paragraph: (3) Where an authorization is given under subsection (2), the authorization forms part of the licence and the person given the authorization shall attach it to the licence.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: 24 (1) Where considering suspending or cancelling a lease or licence under section 9 of the Act, the Minister shall notify the holder thereof in writing by

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (a) sending a notice by registered mail to the holder; or

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (b) having a fishery officer personally deliver a notice to the holder or, if the holder cannot conveniently be found, leave a notice for the holder at the holder's last known place of abode with any person who resides therein who appears to be at least 16 years of age.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (2) A notice referred to in subsection (1) shall set out the reasons for the suspension or cancellation being considered and the period of suspension or the effective date of cancellation, as the case may be.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (3) Where the holder of a lease or licence receives a notice referred to in subsection (1), the holder may, in writing and within 30 days after receiving the notice, make representations to the Minister.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (4) Where the Minister receives representations pursuant to subsection (3), the Minister shall, within a reasonable time, review the matter and, in writing, inform the holder referred to in subsection (3) of the decision.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: 25 (1) Where a licence is suspended or cancelled under section 9 or 79.1 of the Act, the holder of the licence shall

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (a) immediately surrender the licence to a fishery officer; and

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (b) immediately remove from the water all fishing gear operated under the licence.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (2) No person whose licence is suspended under section 9 or 79.1 of the Act shall, during the period of suspension,

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (a) engage in fishing for any species of fish for which fishing was authorized by the licence; or

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (b) be on board a vessel engaged in fishing for any species of fish for which fishing was authorized by the licence.

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (3) No person whose licence is cancelled under section 9 or 79.1 of the Act shall, during the remaining period for which the licence was issued,

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (a) engage in fishing for any species of fish for which fishing was authorized by the licence; or

heading: Suspension or Cancellation of Licences
paragraph: (b) be on board a vessel engaged in fishing for any species of fish for which fishing was authorized by the licence.

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: 26 (1) No person shall operate or cause to be operated a registered vessel

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (a) on which the vessel registration number is not painted or securely affixed by some other means; or

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (b) that displays a vessel registration number that does not meet the requirements set out in subsection (2).

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (2) A vessel registration number shall be

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (a) legible and unobstructed when viewed from an aircraft in flight, from another vessel or from shore;

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (b) in solid Arabic numerals without ornamentation;

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (c) white on a black background or black on a white background;

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (d) aligned horizontally;

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (e) of dimensions in accordance with the table to this subsection and subsections (4) and (5); and

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (f) located on the vessel in accordance with subsection (6).

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (2.1) Where compliance with paragraph (2)(e) is impossible because of a vessel's structural characteristics, the vessel registration number may be of dimensions that are smaller than those prescribed in this section if the numerals are of the greatest dimensions permitted by the vessel's structural characteristics.

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of subsections (4) and (5), "h" is the height of the numerals forming the vessel registration number.

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (4) The numerals forming the vessel registration number shall

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (a) have a stroke width of h/6; and

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (b) be spaced apart not less than h/6 and not more than h/4.

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (5) The background shall extend to provide a border of not less than h/6 around the vessel registration number.

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (6) The vessel registration number shall be located as high as is practicable on both sides of the vessel.

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (7) Subject to subsection (8), no person shall operate or cause to be operated a fishing vessel that displays, on the exterior of the vessel, any number other than the vessel registration number.

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (8) Subsection (7) does not apply with respect to

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (a) a foreign fishing vessel operating under a licence issued under the Coastal Fisheries Protection Regulations; or

heading: Identification of Fishing Vessels
paragraph: (b) a vessel displaying a licence number in accordance with the Small Vessel Regulations.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: 27 (1) It is prohibited for any person to set, operate or leave unattended in the water any fishing gear other than mobile gear or handlines unless the gear is marked in accordance with subsections (2) to (6) with

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (a) where a vessel registration number is set out in the licence authorizing the use of that gear, the vessel registration number; or

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (b) in any other case, the name of the person who owns the gear.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (2) The vessel registration number or name referred to in subsection (1) shall be painted on or otherwise securely affixed to a tag, float or buoy attached to the gear and be legible and readily visible at all times without the necessity of raising the gear from the water or, where the water is ice covered, without the necessity of removing any snow or ice.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (3) The numerals in a vessel registration number referred to in paragraph (1)(a) shall be solid block Arabic numerals

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (a) without ornamentation;

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (b) not less than 75 mm in height; and

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (c) in a colour that contrasts with their background.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (4) The letters forming a name referred to in paragraph (1)(b) shall be solid block capital letters in Roman characters

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (a) without ornamentation;

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (b) not less than 75 mm in height; and

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (c) in a colour that contrasts with their background.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (5) The tag, float or buoy referred to in subsection (2) shall have displayed on it only one vessel registration number or one name, as the case may be.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (6) Except as otherwise provided as a condition of a licence, a tag, float or buoy referred to in subsection (2) shall

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (a) where the waters are tidal waters and one end of the fishing gear is fastened to the shore, be affixed to the end of the gear farthest from the shore; and

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (b) in any other case, be affixed to each end of the gear.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: (7) The Minister may specify a licence condition referred to in subsection (6) only if the purpose of the condition is to mitigate marine mammal entanglement.

heading: Identification of Fishing Gear
paragraph: 29 It is prohibited for any person to display any number or name on fishing gear or on a tag, float or buoy attached to fishing gear that is so similar to a number or name required by section 27 as to be capable of being mistaken for that number or name.

heading: Obstruction of Mesh
paragraph: 30 Subject to section 31, where a person is fishing for a species of fish with fishing gear for which any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4) prescribe a minimum mesh size, that person shall not use any device by means of which openings that are smaller in size than the mesh size prescribed for that species are created in any part of the gear.

heading: Chafing Gear
paragraph: 31 (1) For the purposes of this section, cod-end means a bag-like extension that is attached to the after end of the belly of a trawl net and is used to retain the catch.

heading: Chafing Gear
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of preventing wear and tear to a trawl net, a person may attach

heading: Chafing Gear
paragraph: (a) to the underside of the cod-end of the trawl net, any hides, canvas, netting or other similar material; and

heading: Chafing Gear
paragraph: (b) to the topside of the cod-end, a topside chafer described in Schedule I.

heading: Chafing Gear
paragraph: (3) No person shall use on an otter trawl any topside chafer other than one that meets the description of one of the topside chafers described in Schedule I.

heading: Trans-shipment of Fish
paragraph: 32 No person shall trans-ship any fish from a Canadian fishing vessel to a foreign fishing vessel unless that foreign fishing vessel is licensed under the Coastal Fisheries Protection Regulations to take on board the fish.

heading: Release of Incidental Catch
paragraph: 33 (1) Subsection (2) applies where a person catches a fish

heading: Release of Incidental Catch
paragraph: (a) at a time or place at which the person is prohibited from fishing for that fish;

heading: Release of Incidental Catch
paragraph: (b) by a method or with fishing gear that the person is prohibited from using to fish for that fish; or

heading: Release of Incidental Catch
paragraph: (c) the possession or retention of which is prohibited.

heading: Release of Incidental Catch
paragraph: (2) Except where the retention of an incidental catch is expressly authorized by any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4), every person who catches a fish incidentally shall forthwith return it

heading: Release of Incidental Catch
paragraph: (a) to the place from which it was taken; and

heading: Release of Incidental Catch
paragraph: (b) where it is alive, in a manner that causes it the least harm.

heading: Dumping and Wasting of Fish
paragraph: 34 (1) This section does not apply in respect of marine mammals.

heading: Dumping and Wasting of Fish
paragraph: (2) No person who is fishing under the authority of a licence issued for the purpose of commercial fishing shall dump from a vessel any fish that has been caught in accordance with the Act and the regulations made thereunder.

heading: Dumping and Wasting of Fish
paragraph: (3) No person who is food fishing for personal use or fishing for recreational or sport purposes shall waste any fish that is suitable for human consumption.

heading: Sale of Fish
paragraph: 35 (1) This section does not apply in respect of fish cultivated in an aquaculture facility or in respect of marine mammals.

heading: Sale of Fish
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), no person shall buy, sell, trade, barter or offer to buy, sell, trade or barter any fish unless it was caught and retained under the authority of a licence issued for the purpose of commercial fishing, a licence issued under Part VII, a licence issued under the Aboriginal Communal Fishing Licences Regulations in which the Minister has authorized the sale of fish or an Excess Salmon to Spawning Requirement Licence issued under the Pacific Fishery Regulations, 1993.

heading: Sale of Fish
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if the buying, selling, trading or bartering is carried out in accordance with the terms of the Agreement defined in section 2 of the Western Arctic (Inuvialuit) Claims Settlement Act, the Agreement defined in section 2 of the James Bay and Northern Quebec Native Claims Settlement Act or the Agreement defined in section 2 of the Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement Act.

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: 36 (1) No person shall possess fish that were caught by any person while fishing for recreational or sport purposes and that have been skinned, cut, packed or otherwise dealt with in such a manner that

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (a) the species cannot be readily determined;

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (b) the number of fish cannot be readily determined;

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (c) where weight is used to determine catch limits, the weight of the fish cannot be readily determined; and

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (d) where size limits are applicable, the size of the fish cannot be readily determined.

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (2) No person who catches and retains a fish under the authority of a licence issued for the purpose of commercial fishing shall have the fish in possession if the fish is skinned, cut, packed or otherwise dealt with in such a manner that

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (a) the species cannot be readily identified;

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (b) the number of fish cannot be readily determined;

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (c) the weight of the fish cannot be readily determined; and

heading: Identify, Count, Weigh and Measure Fish
paragraph: (d) where size limits are applicable, the size of the fish cannot be readily determined.

heading: Fishing in or Near Government Facilities
paragraph: 37 (1) Unless authorized under the Act, these Regulations or any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4), no person shall fish in or remove fish from a fish hatchery, fish rearing establishment, fish holding facility or fish collection facility operated by the Department.

heading: Fishing in or Near Government Facilities
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), no person shall fish within a 100 m radius of any facility operated by or on behalf of the Department, the Province of Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, British Columbia, Prince Edward Island or Newfoundland and Labrador, the Yukon Territory or the Northwest Territories for the purpose of the counting, passage or rearing of fish.

heading: Fishing in or Near Government Facilities
paragraph: (3) A fishery officer may determine, taking into account the configuration of the waters, the amount of water flow and any other relevant circumstances, that the distance set out in subsection (2) is longer than required to protect fish, and may shorten the distance by placing a sign or signs, as may be appropriate, to delimit the shorter distance.

heading: Fishing in or Near Government Facilities
paragraph: (4) Where a sign has been placed under subsection (3), no person shall fish between that sign and any facility referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Authorization to Place Nets in Waters for Cleaning
paragraph: 38 (1) Notwithstanding section 25 of the Act, a fishery officer may, in writing, authorize a person to place a net in waters closed to fishing with that net for the purposes of cleaning the net.

heading: Authorization to Place Nets in Waters for Cleaning
paragraph: (2) An authorization given under subsection (1) shall specify the location at which the net may be placed, the manner in which the net may be placed and the period of time for which the authorization is valid.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: 39 (1) The Regional Director-General may designate as an observer any individual who is qualified and trained to perform any of the duties described in subsection (2) and who

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (a) does not hold a fisher's registration card or a provincial or territorial fisher's certificate;

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (b) does not purchase fish for the purpose of resale; and

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (c) is not an owner, operator, manager or employee of an enterprise that catches, cultures, processes or transports fish.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (2) The Regional Director-General shall assign to an observer designated under subsection (1) one or more of the following duties:

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (a) the monitoring of fishing activities, the examination and measurement of fishing gear, the recording of scientific data and observations and the taking of samples;

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (b) the monitoring of the landing of fish and the verification of the weight and species of fish caught and retained; and

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (c) conducting biological examination and sampling of fish.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (2.1) An observer designated under subsection (1) shall transmit in a timely manner to the Department or to a corporation designated under subsection 39.1(1), as the case may be, the information collected and compiled in the course of their duties under subsection 39(2).

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (3) An observer who is assigned the duties set out in paragraph (2)(a) shall perform those duties while on board a fishing vessel or in an aquaculture facility.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (4) An observer who is assigned the duties set out in paragraph (2)(b) shall perform those duties while at a fish landing station or in an aquaculture facility.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (5) An observer who is assigned the duties set out in paragraph (2)(c) shall perform those duties while on board a fishing vessel, at a fish landing station or in an aquaculture facility.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (6) The Regional Director-General may revoke the designation of an observer designated under subsection (1) if the observer

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (a) no longer complies with the criteria set out in that subsection;

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (b) performs his or her duties in respect of a fisher with whom the observer is not dealing at arm's length;

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (c) falsifies any information transmitted in the course of his or her duties or fails to perform those duties; or

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (d) fails to perform his or her duties in a competent and professional manner.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: 39.1 (1) The Regional Director-General may designate as an observer any corporation that has submitted

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (a) a description of a program that is capable of accurately collecting and compiling information obtained by individual observers in the course of their duties under subsection 39(2) and that includes

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (i) a business plan for the corporation that describes the organization of the corporation, its human resources and its plan of operations,

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (ii) a plan for the training and independent examination of individuals who will be designated as observers to perform the duties described in subsection 39(2), and for the supervision of those observers, and

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (iii) a quality control system for ensuring the integrity of the information collected and compiled that identifies a person responsible for the system and his or her duties, and that describes the operation of the system, the manner in which records are kept, the control points, the verification procedures and the process for correcting deficiencies in the system;

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (b) a statement that discloses all conflicts of interest that the corporation or any of its directors, officers or employees, or any shareholder having a significant interest in the corporation may have with the fishing industry, and that explains how those conflicts are to be resolved; and

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (c) evidence of the corporation's financial viability, or a performance bond guaranteeing three months of operation.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (2) An observer designated under subsection (1) has the following duties:

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (a) to comply with the program submitted under paragraph (1)(a);

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (b) to transmit to the Department, in a timely manner, the information collected and compiled as part of the program;

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (c) to disclose all conflicts of interest that arise after the observer's designation and explain how they are to be resolved; and

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (d) to resolve any conflicts of interest disclosed under paragraph (c) or paragraph (1)(b).

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (3) The Regional Director-General may revoke the designation of an observer designated under subsection (1) if the observer

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (a) falsifies any information transmitted in the course of its duties or fails to perform those duties; or

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (b) fails to maintain the performance bond submitted under paragraph (1)(c).

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: 39.2 The designation of an observer is valid for

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (a) six months for the first designation and 36 months for any subsequent designation, in the case of an individual; and

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (b) 12 months for the first and second designations and 24 months for any subsequent designation, in the case of a corporation.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: 39.3 (1) No person shall submit false information to the Regional Director-General for the purpose of obtaining their designation as an observer.

heading: Designation and Duties
paragraph: (2) No observer shall provide false information in the course of their duties.

heading: Certificate of Designation
paragraph: 40 (1) The Regional Director-General shall provide each observer with a certificate that certifies the observer's designation as such and specifies the duties that have been assigned to the observer.

heading: Certificate of Designation
paragraph: (2) An observer shall, on entering any place to perform the observer's duties, on request, show the certificate of designation to the person in charge of the place.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 41 In this Part,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fisheries patrol-boat pennant means a pennant in the shape set out in Part I of Schedule II and the colours set out in Parts I and II of Schedule II, the crest of which has the details set out in Part II of Schedule II; (fanion de patrouilleur des peches)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: inspection pennant means a pennant in the shape, size and colours set out in Schedule III; (fanion d'inspection)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: inspector means a person named by a contracting party set out in Schedule IV to carry out inspections in the Regulatory Area in accordance with the scheme of joint international enforcement established pursuant to Article XVIII of the Convention of Future Multilateral Cooperation in the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries that was ratified by Canada on November 30, 1978 and came into force on January 1, 1979, and who is in possession of an identification card issued by that contracting party in the form set out in Schedule V; (inspecteur)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: International Code of Signals means the International Code of Signals published by Transport Canada; (Code international de signaux)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Signal L means the signal prescribed in the International Code of Signals to mean You should stop your vessel instantly; (signal L)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Signal SQ 1 means the signal prescribed in the International Code of Signals to mean You should stop or heave to, otherwise I shall open fire on you; (signal SQ 1)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Signal SQ 3 means the signal prescribed in the International Code of Signals to mean You should stop, or heave to; I am going to board you. (signal SQ 3)

heading: Flying of Pennants
paragraph: 42 (1) The flying of a fisheries patrol-boat pennant on a vessel identifies that vessel as a vessel with a fishery officer or fishery guardian on board.

heading: Flying of Pennants
paragraph: (2) The flying of an inspection pennant on a vessel identifies that vessel as a vessel with an inspector on board.

heading: Signalling
paragraph: 43 (1) Where a fishery officer or fishery guardian sends the Signal L, the Signal SQ 1 or the Signal SQ 3 to a vessel by any of the methods set out in subsection (2), the master of the vessel shall immediately comply with the direction of that signal.

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (2) The following methods of signalling may be used to send signals to vessels:

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (a) flag signalling using alphabetical flags;

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (b) flashing light signalling using Morse symbols;

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (c) sound signalling using Morse symbols;

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (d) Morse signalling using hand-flags or arms;

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (e) voice with or without using loud hailer;

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (f) radiotelegraphy; and

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (g) radiotelephony.

heading: Signalling
paragraph: (3) Where any signal referred to in subsection (1) has been sent to a vessel, no person on board that vessel shall dump or throw anything overboard from that vessel until the fishery officer or fishery guardian who sent the signal indicates to the master of the vessel that the vessel may proceed.

heading: Assisting Fishery Officer and Fishery Guardian
paragraph: 44 The master of a fishing vessel shall provide all reasonable assistance to a fishery officer or fishery guardian, including

heading: Assisting Fishery Officer and Fishery Guardian
paragraph: (a) making the fishing gear used on or from the vessel available for inspection and for that purpose hauling in such gear and thawing the nets, where necessary;

heading: Assisting Fishery Officer and Fishery Guardian
paragraph: (b) permitting the taking of photographs of the fisheries operations, including fishing gear and equipment; and

heading: Assisting Fishery Officer and Fishery Guardian
paragraph: (c) where the fishery officer or fishery guardian is on board for more than four consecutive hours, providing food and accommodation equivalent to that provided to officers of the vessel.

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: 45 (1) Where an inspector sends the Signal L or the Signal SQ 3 by any of the methods set out in subsection 43(2) to a fishing vessel operating in the Regulatory Area, the master of the vessel shall immediately comply with the direction of that signal.

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (2) The master of a fishing vessel operating in the Regulatory Area shall

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (a) at the request of an inspector, permit the inspector to board the vessel; and

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (b) provide the inspector with all reasonable assistance necessary to enable the inspector to carry out an inspection of the fishing operations, including

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (i) making the fishing gear used on or from the vessel available for inspection and for that purpose hauling in such gear and thawing the nets, where necessary,

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (ii) permitting the taking of photographs of the fisheries operations, including fishing gear and equipment, and

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (iii) where the inspector is on board for more than four consecutive hours, providing food and accommodation equivalent to that provided to officers of the vessel.

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (2.1) Where an inspector sends the Signal SQ 3 to a fishing vessel, no person on board that vessel shall retrieve any gear from the water for the period of 30 minutes after the signal is sent.

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (3) Where, during an inspection in the Regulatory Area, an inspector finds any fishing gear or equipment the use or possession of which is contrary to the Act, the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985 or these Regulations, the inspector may place a mark or seal on that fishing gear or equipment in a manner that will preserve the identity of the gear or equipment.

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (4) No person other than a fishery officer shall remove a mark or seal placed on any fishing gear or equipment in accordance with subsection (3).

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (5) Where a mark or seal has been placed on any fishing gear or equipment in accordance with subsection (3), no person shall

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (a) alter or tamper with that mark or seal; or

heading: Assisting Inspector
paragraph: (b) use, destroy or dispose of that fishing gear or equipment unless the mark or seal has been removed by a fishery officer.

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: 46 (1) This section does not apply in respect of a foreign fishing vessel.

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (2) The owner or master of a fishing vessel shall, at the request of the Regional Director-General,

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (a) permit an observer who is assigned the duties set out in paragraph 39(2)(a) to go on board that vessel to perform those duties and to remain on board for the period of time specified in the request; and

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (b) arrange for the embarkation or disembarkation of the observer at such time and place as is specified in the request.

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (3) The master of a fishing vessel shall provide all reasonable assistance to an observer who is assigned the duties set out in paragraph 39(2)(a), including

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (a) providing a suitable work area, including a table and adequate lighting;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (b) providing, at the request of the observer, information relating to any matter mentioned in subsection 61(2) of the Act;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (c) providing, at the request of the observer, the position of the vessel in latitude and longitude;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (d) facilitating the sending and receiving of messages by means of the communications equipment on board the vessel;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (e) giving access to all areas of the vessel involved in fishing, processing and storage operations;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (f) permitting the taking of samples free of charge;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (g) providing suitable storage facilities for samples;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (h) assisting, at the request of the observer, in the examination and measurement of fishing gear on board the vessel;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (i) permitting the taking of photographs of the fisheries operations, including fishing gear and equipment;

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (j) permitting the removal from the vessel of samples, records, photographs or film taken or made on board the vessel; and

heading: Monitoring Fishing Activities
paragraph: (k) where the observer is on board for more than four consecutive hours, providing food and accommodation equivalent to that provided to officers of the vessel.

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: 47 The master of a fishing vessel that is landing fish at a fish landing station shall

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: (a) at the request of an observer who is assigned the duties set out in paragraph 39(2)(b), permit the observer to go on board the vessel to perform those duties; and

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: (b) provide the observer with such assistance as is reasonably necessary to enable the observer to perform those duties.

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: 48 The owner or any person who has the care, charge or control of a fish landing station shall

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: (a) at the request of an observer who is assigned the duties set out in paragraph 39(2)(b) or (c), provide the observer with access to the fish landing station; and

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: (b) provide the observer with such assistance as is reasonably necessary to enable the observer to perform those duties, including

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: (i) making the fish at the fish landing station readily accessible to the observer,

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: (ii) providing the observer with a suitable work area, including a table and adequate lighting, and

heading: Monitoring Landing and Conducting Biological Examinations
paragraph: (iii) permitting the observer to remove whole fish or portions of fish from the fish landing station free of charge.

heading: Embarking and Disembarking Assistance
paragraph: 49 Where a fishery officer, fishery guardian, inspector or observer has to climb up or down more than 1.2 m to embark or disembark from a fishing vessel, sections 4 to 16 of the Pilot Ladder Regulations apply to the master of the fishing vessel, with such modifications as the circumstances may require.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 50 In this Part, licence means a licence to fish for experimental, scientific, educational, aquatic invasive species control or public display purposes.

heading: Licence
paragraph: 51 No person shall fish for experimental, scientific, educational, aquatic invasive species control or public display purposes unless authorized to do so under a licence.

heading: Licence
paragraph: 52 Despite any provisions of any of the Regulations listed in subsection 3(4), the Minister may issue a licence if fishing for experimental, scientific, educational, aquatic invasive species control or public display purposes would be in keeping with the proper management and control of fisheries.

heading: Licence Fee
paragraph: 53 (1) The fee for a licence to fish for public display purposes is $100.

heading: Licence Fee
paragraph: (2) There is no fee for a licence to fish for experimental, scientific, educational or aquatic invasive species control purposes.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 54 In this Part, licence means a licence to release live fish into fish habitat or to transfer live fish to a fish rearing facility.

heading: Release or Transfer of Fish
paragraph: 55 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall, unless authorized to do so under a licence,

heading: Release or Transfer of Fish
paragraph: (a) release live fish into any fish habitat; or

heading: Release or Transfer of Fish
paragraph: (b) transfer any live fish to any fish rearing facility.

heading: Release or Transfer of Fish
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of fish that is immediately returned to the waters in which it was caught.

heading: Licence to Release or Transfer Fish
paragraph: 56 The Minister may issue a licence if

heading: Licence to Release or Transfer Fish
paragraph: (a) the release or transfer of the fish would be in keeping with the proper management and control of fisheries;

heading: Licence to Release or Transfer Fish
paragraph: (b) the fish do not have any disease or disease agent that may be harmful to the protection and conservation of fish; and

heading: Licence to Release or Transfer Fish
paragraph: (c) the release or transfer of the fish will not have an adverse effect on the stock size of fish or the genetic characteristics of fish or fish stocks.

heading: Licence Fee
paragraph: 57 There is no fee for a licence issued under this Part.

heading: PART XRemoval of Obstructions to the Passage of Fish
paragraph: 59 Where the Minister is satisfied that any natural obstruction that exists in any waters is interfering or is likely to interfere with the free passage of fish, the Minister may cause the obstruction to be removed in whole or in part.

heading: To Government of Canada
paragraph: 60 (1) Where an information is laid by a fishery officer or a fishery guardian employed by the Government of Canada relating to an offence under the Act, the payment of the proceeds of any penalty imposed arising from a conviction for the offence shall be made to the Minister.

heading: To Government of Canada
paragraph: (2) Where an information is laid by a fishery officer or a fishery guardian employed by the Government of Canada relating to an offence under the Act, the payment of any proceeds of the sale of any forfeited articles arising from a conviction for the offence shall be made to the Minister.

heading: To Provincial Government
paragraph: 61 (1) Where an information is laid by a fishery officer or a fishery guardian employed by a provincial government relating to an offence under the Act and all of the expenses incurred in the prosecution of the offence are paid by the provincial government, the payment of the proceeds of any penalty imposed arising from a conviction for that offence shall be made to that provincial government.

heading: To Provincial Government
paragraph: (2) Where an information is laid by a fishery officer or a fishery guardian employed by a provincial government relating to an offence under the Act and all of the expenses incurred in the prosecution of the offence and in connection with the custody and disposal of any forfeited articles are paid by the provincial government, the payment of any proceeds of the sale of the forfeited articles arising from a conviction for that offence shall be made to that provincial government.

heading: To Persons
paragraph: 62 (1) Where an information is laid by a person in circumstances other than those referred to in section 60 or 61 relating to an offence under the Act, the payment of the proceeds of any penalty imposed arising from a conviction for the offence shall be made

heading: To Persons
paragraph: (a) one half to the person; and

heading: To Persons
paragraph: (b) one half to the Minister or, where all of the expenses incurred in the prosecution of the offence are paid by a provincial government, to that provincial government.

heading: To Persons
paragraph: (2) Where an information is laid by a person in circumstances other than those referred to in section 60 or 61 relating to an offence under the Act, the payment of any proceeds of the sale of any forfeited articles arising from a conviction for the offence shall be made, net of any expenses incurred in connection with the custody and sale of the forfeited articles,

heading: To Persons
paragraph: (a) one half to the person; and

heading: To Persons
paragraph: (b) one half to the Minister or, where all of the expenses incurred in the prosecution of the offence are paid by a provincial government, to that provincial government.

heading: Prescribed Offences
paragraph: 63 The contravention of any provision of these Regulations set out in column I of an item of Schedule VIII is an offence to which section 79.7 of the Act applies and which may be described in tickets in the manner set out in column II of that item.

heading: Fines
paragraph: 64 Where proceedings are commenced under section 79.7 of the Act, the amount of the fine for an offence described in column II of an item of Schedule VIII is the amount set out in column III of that item.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 65 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person on board a fishing vessel that is subject to the jurisdiction of Canada shall fish or trans-ship fish in waters other than Canadian fisheries waters except under the authority of a licence issued under section 68.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person on board a fishing vessel that is subject to the jurisdiction of Canada who is fishing

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) in the Regulatory Area under the authority of a licence issued under the Atlantic Fishery Regulations, 1985; or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) in the Pacific Ocean for tuna under the authority of a licence issued under the Pacific Fishery Regulations, 1993.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 66 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person on board a fishing vessel that is subject to the jurisdiction of Canada shall, in waters that are subject to the jurisdiction of the United States, have any fishing gear on board the fishing vessel unless it is

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) stored below deck; or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) otherwise removed from the place where it is normally used for fishing and placed where it is not readily available for fishing.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who is fishing under the authority of a licence issued under section 68.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 67 No person who is on board a fishing vessel that is subject to the jurisdiction of Canada shall, while the fishing vessel is in waters that are subject to the jurisdiction of the United States, resist or obstruct any enforcement officer of the United States while the officer is engaged in the enforcement of the fisheries laws of the United States.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 68 (1) The Minister may issue a licence authorizing the use of a vessel that is subject to the jurisdiction of Canada in fishing or trans-shipping fish in waters other than Canadian fisheries waters if

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) the fishing or trans-shipping of fish carried out under the authority of the licence would not contravene or undermine any international fisheries conservation scheme; and

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) in the case where the fishing or trans-shipping of fish is to be carried out in waters that are subject to the jurisdiction of another state, the fishing or trans-shipping of fish by that vessel is authorized by a competent authority of that state.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the fee for a licence referred to in subsection (1) is $500.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) There is no fee for a licence referred to in subsection (1) that is issued in respect of waters subject to the jurisdiction of Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: 69 For the purposes of section 6.3 of the Act, the major fish stocks referred to in sections 6.1 and 6.2 of the Act are listed in the table in Schedule IX.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: 70 (1) A plan to rebuild a major fish stock, required under subsection 6.2(1) of the Act, shall contain the following information:

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (a) the stock status and stock trends;

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (b) the probable causes for the stock's decline;

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (c) measurable objectives aimed at rebuilding the stock, including a target for rebuilding the stock;

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (d) the timelines for achieving the objectives;

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (e) the management measures aimed at achieving the objectives;

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (f) a method to track progress towards achieving the objectives; and

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (g) a schedule for a periodic review of the plan in order to assess progress towards achieving the objectives and to determine whether an adjustment to the plan is needed.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (2) The plan shall be developed within 24 months after the day on which the Minister first had knowledge that the major fish stock had declined to or below its limit reference point.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (3) The Minister may extend the time period to the extent necessary for completing the plan, by a period not exceeding 12 months.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (4) If the Minister extends the time period, the Minister shall publish the reasons for doing so on the Internet site of the Department.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (5) If fishing of the major fish stock while the plan is being developed is permitted by the Minister, the Minister shall ensure that the level of fishing of the stock during that time is consistent with the rebuilding of the stock above the limit reference point.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (6) Despite paragraph 1(d), if the Minister determines that it is not feasible to establish a timeline for achieving the target for rebuilding the major fish stock, the plan shall include, instead of such a timeline, the reasons why it is not feasible to do so.

heading: PART XIVFish Stocks
paragraph: (7) The Minister shall publish the plan to rebuild a major fish stock and the results of any periodic review of the plan on the Internet site of the Department.

heading: Regular Topside Chafer
paragraph: 1 A rectangular piece of netting that

heading: Regular Topside Chafer
paragraph: a) is at least 1  1/2 times the width of the area of the cod-end that is covered, where the width is measured at right angles to the long axis of the cod-end;

heading: Regular Topside Chafer
paragraph: b) has a mesh size that is not less than the mesh size of the cod-end; and

heading: Regular Topside Chafer
paragraph: c) is fastened to the cod-end only along the forward and lateral edges of the netting in a manner that will permit it to extend

heading: Regular Topside Chafer
paragraph: (i) where a splitting strap is used, over not more of the cod-end than that part between the fourth mesh forward of the cod line mesh and the fourth mesh forward of the splitting strap, and

heading: Regular Topside Chafer
paragraph: (ii) where a splitting strap is not used, over not more than one-third of the cod-end, measured from not less than the fourth mesh forward of the cod line mesh.

heading: Modified Polish Topside Chafer
paragraph: 2 A rectangular piece of netting that

heading: Modified Polish Topside Chafer
paragraph: a) is made of twine of the same material and size as that of the cod-end, or of any single, thick, knotless twine material;

heading: Modified Polish Topside Chafer
paragraph: b) has a mesh size that is twice as large as the mesh size of the cod-end;

heading: Modified Polish Topside Chafer
paragraph: c) is attached to the rear portion of the topside of the cod-end; and

heading: Modified Polish Topside Chafer
paragraph: d) is fastened to the cod-end along the forward, lateral and rear edges of the netting in a manner that will cause each mesh to exactly overlie four meshes of the cod-end over which it extends.

heading: Multiple Flap-Type Topside Chafer
paragraph: 3 A series of pieces of netting where

heading: Multiple Flap-Type Topside Chafer
paragraph: a) the aggregate length extends less than two-thirds of the length of the cod-end; and

heading: Multiple Flap-Type Topside Chafer
paragraph: b) each piece of netting

heading: Multiple Flap-Type Topside Chafer
paragraph: (i) is attached to the topside of the cod-end so that it overlaps the piece of netting immediately to its rear, if any,

heading: Multiple Flap-Type Topside Chafer
paragraph: (ii) has a mesh size that is not less than the mesh size of the cod-end,

heading: Multiple Flap-Type Topside Chafer
paragraph: (iii) is at least as wide as the cod-end, where the width is measured at right angles to the cod-end,

heading: Multiple Flap-Type Topside Chafer
