heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Fishing and Recreational Harbours Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 In this Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: agency, in relation to a province, includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any incorporated or unincorporated city, town, municipality, village, township, rural municipality, regional district administration or local improvement district administration,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any council of a band within the meaning of the Indian Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the Council, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the shishalh Nation Self-Government Act, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a first nation named in Schedule II to the Yukon First Nations Self-Government Act; (organisme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishing or recreational harbour means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any harbour, wharf, pier, breakwater, slipway, marina or part thereof, together with machinery, works, land and structures related or attached thereto, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any other facility, installation, works or part thereof located on or adjacent to water

heading: Definitions
paragraph: where accommodation or services are provided principally for fishing or recreational vessels or the occupants thereof; (port de peche ou de plaisance)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: goods means tangible personal property other than vessels; (marchandises)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means such member of the Queen's Privy Council for Canada as is designated by the Governor in Council as the Minister for the purposes of this Act; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: scheduled harbour means any fishing or recreational harbour or portion thereof included in a schedule prescribed by the regulations; (ports inscrits)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vessel includes every description of ship, boat, craft, floating home or other structure used or capable of being used solely or partly for aquatic navigation without regard to method or lack of propulsion. (bateau)

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: 3 (1) Nothing in this Act applies to

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (a) any port, as defined in section 5 of the Canada Marine Act, or any harbour, works or property under the jurisdiction of a harbour commission established under an Act of Parliament; or

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (b) any harbour, wharf, pier or breakwater under the control and management of any member of the Queen's Privy Council for Canada other than the Minister.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (2) This Act does not affect any of the powers or duties of the Minister of Transport or the Minister of Public Works and Government Services under any other Act of Parliament or regulations made pursuant thereto.

heading: Harbours under control of Minister
paragraph: 4 The use, management and maintenance of every scheduled harbour, the enforcement of regulations relating thereto and the collection of charges for the use of every scheduled harbour are under the control and administration of the Minister.

heading: Minister may undertake projects
paragraph: 5 (1) The Minister may undertake projects for the acquisition, development, construction, improvement or repair of any scheduled harbour or any fishing or recreational harbour to which this Act applies.

heading: Agreements with provinces
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, subject to the regulations, enter into an agreement with any province to provide for

heading: Agreements with provinces
paragraph: (a) the undertaking jointly with the government of the province or any agency thereof of any project that the Minister is authorized to undertake under subsection (1); and

heading: Agreements with provinces
paragraph: (b) the payment to the province of contributions or grants in respect of the cost or any part of the cost of any project that is undertaken by the government of the province or any agency thereof and that the Minister is authorized to undertake under subsection (1).

heading: Agreements with persons
paragraph: (3) The Minister may, subject to the regulations, enter into an agreement with any person to provide for

heading: Agreements with persons
paragraph: (a) the undertaking jointly with that person of any project that the Minister is authorized to undertake under subsection (1); and

heading: Agreements with persons
paragraph: (b) the payment to that person of contributions or grants in respect of the cost or any part of the cost of any project that is undertaken by that person and that the Minister is authorized to undertake under subsection (1) and in respect of the cost of any planning studies and advisory services relating to any such project.

heading: Studies
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of assisting the formulation and assessment of projects undertaken under subsection (1), the Minister may, subject to the regulations, undertake economic or other studies alone or jointly with the government of any province or agency thereof or with any person or educational institution.

heading: Services of other departments
paragraph: 6 The Minister shall, in carrying out any project or study under this Act, make use, wherever possible, of the services and facilities of other departments, boards or agencies of the Government of Canada.

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: 7 Every agreement entered into pursuant to subsection 5(2) or (3) shall specify

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (a) the respective proportions of the cost of any project to which the agreement relates that shall be paid by the Minister and the province or person or the contributions or grants in respect of that project that shall be paid by the Minister, and the times at which those amounts to be paid by the Minister or the province or person shall be paid;

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (b) the authority that shall be responsible for the undertaking, operation and maintenance of any project or any part thereof to which the agreement relates;

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (c) the respective proportions of the revenues from any project to which the agreement relates that are to be paid to the Minister and the province or person; and

heading: Provisions to be included in agreements
paragraph: (d) the terms and conditions respecting the operation and maintenance of any project to which the agreement relates and the charges, if any, to be charged to persons to whom any of the benefits of the project are made available.

heading: Leases, licences and agreements for use of scheduled harbours
paragraph: 8 The Minister may, subject to the regulations,

heading: Leases, licences and agreements for use of scheduled harbours
paragraph: (a) lease any scheduled harbour or any part thereof to any person;

heading: Leases, licences and agreements for use of scheduled harbours
paragraph: (b) grant a licence to any person for the use of any scheduled harbour or any part thereof; and

heading: Leases, licences and agreements for use of scheduled harbours
paragraph: (c) enter into an agreement with the government of any province or any agency thereof for the occupancy and use of any scheduled harbour or any part thereof.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 9 The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing schedules naming and delimiting or describing the fishing or recreational harbours or portions thereof belonging to Her Majesty in right of Canada that are under the control and administration of the Minister for the purposes of this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) for the maintenance of order and the safety of persons and property at any scheduled harbour;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) not inconsistent with any other Act of Parliament or regulations made thereunder, for the control of mooring, berthing, loading and discharging of vessels at any scheduled harbour;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) not inconsistent with any other Act of Parliament or regulations made thereunder, for the control of pollution at any scheduled harbour;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) prescribing standards for the accommodation and services provided or to be provided at any scheduled harbour;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) prescribing charges for the use of any scheduled harbour;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (g) prescribing the duties or functions of persons appointed or designated under this Act or any other Act of Parliament to supervise or manage any fishing or recreational harbour to which this Act applies;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (h) governing inquiries into accidents and incidents held under section 26;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i) prescribing terms and conditions of agreements entered into pursuant to subsection 5(2) or (3);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (j) prescribing the manner of undertaking economic or other studies pursuant to subsection 5(4);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (k) prescribing terms and conditions of leases, licences and agreements entered into or granted pursuant to section 8;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (l) prescribing the form of the tickets that may be issued pursuant to paragraph 25(1)(a);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (m) respecting the detention and safe-keeping of vessels and goods seized under this Act and the payment of any reasonable costs incidental thereto;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (n) prescribing the manner of disposing of anything forfeited under this Act; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (o) generally for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act.

heading: Enforcement officers
paragraph: 10 (1) For the purposes of enforcing this Act and the regulations, the Minister may designate as an enforcement officer any person who is, in the opinion of the Minister, qualified to be so designated and furnish that person with a certificate of his designation.

heading: Production of certificate of designation
paragraph: (2) In carrying out the duties and functions of an enforcement officer under this Act, an enforcement officer shall, if so requested, produce the certificate of designation of the enforcement officer as such to the person appearing to be in charge of any vessel, vehicle, premises or goods in respect of which the officer is acting.

heading: Powers of enforcement officers
paragraph: 11 Where an enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds that a provision of this Act or the regulations is not being complied with, the officer may

heading: Powers of enforcement officers
paragraph: (a) with a warrant issued under section 11.1, board any vessel or enter any vehicle or premises where or in respect of which the officer believes on reasonable grounds there may be evidence of the non-compliance and make any inspection the officer deems necessary;

heading: Powers of enforcement officers
paragraph: (b) require the person appearing to be in charge of the vessel, vehicle or premises to produce for inspection, or for the purpose of making copies or extracts therefrom, any log book, document or paper that may, in the officer's opinion, provide evidence of that non-compliance;

heading: Powers of enforcement officers
paragraph: (c) require any person found on board any vessel or in any vehicle or premises to give all reasonable assistance to enable the officer to carry out his duties and functions under this Act; and

heading: Powers of enforcement officers
paragraph: (d) prohibit the use of any scheduled harbour by any person, vessel or vehicle that the officer believes on reasonable grounds to be involved in that non-compliance and direct the removal of that person, vessel or vehicle from the harbour.

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: 11.1 Where on ex parte application a justice of the peace is satisfied by information on oath that there are reasonable grounds to believe that there is in any vessel, vehicle or premises

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) anything on or in respect of which any contravention under this Act has been or is suspected to have been committed, or

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) anything that there are reasonable grounds to believe will afford evidence with respect to the commission of any contravention under this Act,

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: the justice of the peace may issue a warrant under his hand authorizing the enforcement officer named therein to enter that vessel, vehicle or premises subject to such conditions as may be specified in the warrant in order to make any inspection the enforcement officer deems necessary.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: 11.2 In executing a warrant issued under section 11.1, the enforcement officer named therein shall not use force unless the officer is accompanied by a peace officer and the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Where warrant not necessary
paragraph: 11.3 An enforcement officer may exercise the powers referred to in paragraph 11(a) without a warrant issued under section 11.1 if the conditions for obtaining the warrant exist but by reason of exigent circumstances it would not be practical to obtain the warrant.

heading: Exigent circumstances
paragraph: 11.4 For the purposes of section 11.3, exigent circumstances include circumstances in which the delay necessary to obtain a warrant under section 11.1 would result in danger to human life or safety or the loss or destruction of evidence.

heading: Obstruction of enforcement officer
paragraph: 12 Where an enforcement officer is carrying out the duties and functions of an enforcement officer under this Act, no person shall

heading: Obstruction of enforcement officer
paragraph: (a) fail to comply with any reasonable requirement or direction of the officer;

heading: Obstruction of enforcement officer
paragraph: (b) knowingly make a false or misleading statement, either orally or in writing, to the officer; or

heading: Obstruction of enforcement officer
paragraph: (c) otherwise obstruct or hinder the officer.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: 13 (1) All charges prescribed by regulations made under this Act for the use of any scheduled harbour constitute a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada jointly and severally by the owner and any other person in charge of the vessel or goods in respect of which the charges are payable.

heading: Other remedies available
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this Act prevents a debt payable under this Act from being recovered, together with all costs, from the debtor in any court of competent jurisdiction or the exercise against the debtor of any other right or remedy available at law.

heading: Obstruction of scheduled harbours
paragraph: 14 (1) Where any vessel or goods are left or abandoned at any scheduled harbour and an enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds that the vessel or goods impede, interfere with or render difficult or dangerous the use of the harbour, the officer may direct the person appearing to be in charge of the vessel or goods to remove the vessel or goods from the harbour to such place as the officer deems suitable.

heading: Seizure and removal
paragraph: (2) If the person to whom a direction is given pursuant to subsection (1) fails to comply with the direction or if no person appears to be in charge of the vessel or goods, the enforcement officer may seize the vessel or goods and remove them to such place as the officer deems suitable, and the costs of the seizure and removal are recoverable in the same manner as a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada for charges under this Act.

heading: Seizure and detention
paragraph: 15 Where an enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds that

heading: Seizure and detention
paragraph: (a) any amount is due and payable under this Act for charges in respect of any vessel or goods, or

heading: Seizure and detention
paragraph: (b) any provision of this Act or the regulations relating to any vessel or goods has been contravened,

heading: Seizure and detention
paragraph: the officer may seize and detain the vessel or goods.

heading: Application for order directing forfeiture
paragraph: 16 (1) Where, at the time any vessel or goods are seized under this Act, no person appears to be in possession thereof or to have the right to the possession thereof, the Minister may apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for an order directing the forfeiture of the vessel or goods to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Forfeiture granted
paragraph: (2) Where, on the hearing of an application made under subsection (1), the court is satisfied that no person appears to be in possession or to have the right to the possession of the vessel or goods seized, it may order the forfeiture thereof to Her Majesty in right of Canada and on such forfeiture the vessel or goods may be disposed of as the Minister directs.

heading: Protection of persons claiming interest
paragraph: (3) Sections 74 to 77 of the Fisheries Act applies, with such modifications as the circumstances require, in respect of anything forfeited under subsection (2) as though it were an article forfeited under subsection 72(1) of that Act.

heading: Forfeiture refused
paragraph: (4) Where, on the hearing of an application made under subsection (1), the court is not satisfied that the vessel or goods seized should be forfeited, it shall order the vessel or goods to be dealt with according to the other provisions of this Act and the regulations applicable thereto.

heading: Sale of perishable goods
paragraph: 17 (1) Where, in the opinion of the enforcement officer, any goods seized and detained under this Act are likely to rot, spoil or otherwise perish, the officer may sell or otherwise dispose of the goods in such manner and for such price as is reasonable in the circumstances.

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (2) The proceeds of a sale or other disposition referred to in subsection (1) shall be paid to the Receiver General or deposited to the credit of the Receiver General in a bank.

heading: Return of property seized
paragraph: 18 (1) Subject to subsection (2), any vessel or goods seized under this Act and any proceeds of a sale or other disposition thereof made under section 17 shall be returned to the person from whom the vessel or goods were seized or to any other person entitled to the possession thereof after

heading: Return of property seized
paragraph: (a) the provisions of this Act and the regulations that apply to the vessel or goods have, in the opinion of an enforcement officer, been complied with; or

heading: Return of property seized
paragraph: (b) the expiration of twenty-one days from the day of the seizure, unless before that time an application for an order authorizing the sale of the vessel or goods has been made pursuant to section 19.

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of any vessel or goods forfeited pursuant to section 16.

heading: Application for order authorizing sale
paragraph: 19 (1) The Minister may, before the expiration of twenty-one days from the day of the seizure of any vessel or goods under this Act, apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for an order authorizing the sale of the vessel or goods.

heading: Redelivery on security
paragraph: (2) The court may order the redelivery of any vessel or goods seized under this Act to the person from whom the vessel or goods were seized or to any other person entitled to the possession thereof after security by bond, with two sureties, in such amount and form as is satisfactory to the Minister, is given to Her Majesty in right of Canada or after security of a cash deposit, in an amount satisfactory to the Minister, is given to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Order of sale refused
paragraph: (3) Where, on the hearing of an application made under subsection (1), the court is not satisfied that the vessel or goods seized should be sold, it may order that the vessel or goods be returned or, if a sale or other disposition of the goods has been made pursuant to section 17, it may order that any proceeds thereof be remitted to the person from whom the vessel or goods were seized or to any other person entitled to the possession thereof.

heading: Order of sale granted
paragraph: (4) Where, on the hearing of an application made under subsection (1), the court is satisfied that the vessel or goods seized should be sold, it may order the sale thereof and thereupon the Minister may sell the vessel or goods in such manner and for such price as the court determines is reasonable in the circumstances.

heading: Proceeds of sale
paragraph: (5) Where the total amount realized from a sale made under subsection (4) or any other disposition made under section 17, or both, exceeds the amount payable for rates and charges under this Act together with all costs and reasonable expenses incurred in connection with the sale or other disposition and any removal, seizure or detention under this Act, the Minister shall remit the excess amount to the person then appearing to be entitled thereto.

heading: Idem
paragraph: (6) Where it appears to the Minister that no person is entitled to the excess amount mentioned in subsection (5), that amount shall be paid to the Receiver General.

heading: Contravening section 12 or regulations
paragraph: 20 Every person who contravenes section 12 or the regulations is guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding twenty-five thousand dollars or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or to both.

heading: Officers, etc., of corporations
paragraph: 21 Where a corporation commits an offence under this Act, any officer, director or agent of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the punishment provided for the offence whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Trial of offences
paragraph: 22 A complaint or information in respect of an offence under this Act may be heard, tried or determined by a court if the accused is resident or carrying on business within the territorial jurisdiction of that court although the matter of the complaint or information did not arise in that territorial jurisdiction.

heading: Offence by employee or agent
paragraph: 23 In any prosecution for an offence under this Act, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by an employee or agent of the accused whether or not the employee or agent is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence, unless the accused establishes that the offence was committed without the knowledge or consent of the accused and that the accused exercised all due diligence to prevent its commission.

heading: Copies and extracts as evidence
paragraph: 24 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), a copy or extract made by an enforcement officer pursuant to paragraph 11(b) and purporting to be certified under the signature of that enforcement officer as a true copy or extract is admissible in evidence in any prosecution for an offence under this Act without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the copy or extract and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, has the same probative force as the original document would have if it had been proved in the ordinary way.

heading: Attendance of enforcement officer
paragraph: (2) The party against whom any copy or extract is produced pursuant to subsection (1) may, with leave of the court, require the attendance of the enforcement officer for the purposes of cross-examination.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) No copy or extract referred to in subsection (1) shall be admitted in evidence unless the party intending to produce it has given to the party against whom it is intended to be produced reasonable notice of that intention together with a duplicate of the copy or extract.

heading: Regulations relating to offences
paragraph: 25 (1) The Governor in Council may by regulation designate any offence under this Act or the regulations as an offence with respect to which

heading: Regulations relating to offences
paragraph: (a) notwithstanding the provisions of the Criminal Code, any person designated as an enforcement officer pursuant to section 10 may lay an information and issue and serve a summons by completing a ticket in the form prescribed by regulation, affixing that person's signature thereto and delivering the ticket to the person alleged to have committed the offence specified therein at the time the offence is alleged to have been committed; or

heading: Regulations relating to offences
paragraph: (b) the summons may be served on an accused by mailing the summons to the accused at the latest known address of the accused.

heading: Voluntary payment of fine
paragraph: (2) A regulation made under this section shall establish a procedure for voluntarily entering a plea of guilty and paying a fine in respect of each offence to which the regulation relates and shall fix the amount of the fine that may be so paid in respect of each such offence.

heading: Fixing of fines
paragraph: (3) A fine fixed in respect of an offence by a regulation made under this section may be lower for a first offence than for any subsequent offence but in no case shall it be greater than fifty dollars.

heading: Minister may direct inquiry
paragraph: 26 (1) The Minister may direct an inquiry to be made, subject to the Canadian Transportation Accident Investigation and Safety Board Act, whenever an accident or incident that results or is likely to result in death or injury to any person, damage to property or danger to the health or safety of the public has occurred at any scheduled harbour and authorize any qualified persons to conduct the inquiry.

heading: Powers of persons conducting inquiries
paragraph: (2) Every person authorized by the Minister to conduct an inquiry under subsection (1) shall have all the powers of a commissioner appointed under Part I of the Inquiries Act.

heading: Appointment of officers or employees
paragraph: 27 For the purposes of this Act, the Minister may appoint and fix the remuneration of such officers or employees as the Minister thinks proper for the operation, administration and management of any scheduled harbours, and the officers or employees so appointed shall perform such duties or functions as the Minister may direct or as may be prescribed by regulations made under this Act.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Fishing and Recreational Harbours Act; (loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: berthage means a charge for the occupation by a vessel of a berth or other space at a harbour; (droit d'amarrage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: enforcement officer means a person designated as such pursuant to section 10 of the Act; (agent d'execution)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: harbour means a scheduled harbour; (port)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: harbour manager means a person appointed under section 27 of the Act or under any other Act of Parliament to manage a harbour; (responsable du port)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: harbour property means any real property at a harbour, including marine facilities; (propriete portuaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: lease means a lease referred to in section 8 of the Act; (bail)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: length means

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) in the case of a commercial fishing vessel, the length shown in the fishing vessel registration of that vessel, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) in the case of a recreational or other vessel, the horizontal distance measured between perpendiculars erected at the extreme ends of the vessel; (longueur)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: licence means a licence referred to in section 8 of the Act; (permis)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: owner means,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) in the case of a vessel, the master, operator or person in charge of the vessel, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) in the case of goods, the agent, consignor, consignee or carrier of the goods; (proprietaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: wharfage means a charge for placing goods on a wharf or for loading goods on or unloading goods from a vessel at a wharf. (droit de quayage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 3 For the purposes of the definition scheduled harbour in section 2 of the Act, the harbours set out in Schedule I are fishing or recreational harbours.

heading: Application
paragraph: 4 These Regulations apply to every scheduled harbour.

heading: Leases and Licences
paragraph: 5 No lease or licence shall be for any term exceeding 20 years except with the approval of the Governor in Council.

heading: Leases and Licences
paragraph: 6 No lease or licence of a harbour or any part of a harbour shall be granted except on terms and conditions that ensure access by the public to the harbour.

heading: Leases and Licences
paragraph: 7 (1) No person shall erect, maintain or occupy a building, structure or other work at a scheduled harbour except under a lease or licence.

heading: Leases and Licences
paragraph: (2) No person shall, except with the permission in writing of the harbour manager, install electric power lines, water supply lines or drainage pipes on harbour property.

heading: Leases and Licences
paragraph: 7.1 No person shall berth, in a harbour, a vessel to be used as a residence unless there is an authorization to berth the vessel in that harbour under a lease or licence.

heading: General
paragraph: 8 (1) No person shall bring dangerous, explosive or combustible goods on harbour property unless the goods are required for the ordinary purposes of a vessel in a harbour and prior notice has been given to the harbour manager of the proposed location of the goods and of the manner in which they will be handled and dealt with.

heading: General
paragraph: (2) Where the harbour manager has reasonable grounds to believe that the safety of the harbour or of the public may be endangered by the proposed location of any dangerous, explosive or combustible goods on harbour property or by the manner in which such goods are to be handled or dealt with on harbour property, he shall prohibit the goods from being brought on the harbour property or being so handled or dealt with, as the case may be.

heading: General
paragraph: (3) No person shall bring on harbour property goods the entry of which has been prohibited pursuant to subsection (2) or handle or deal with goods in a manner that has been prohibited pursuant to that subsection.

heading: General
paragraph: 9 No person shall, in a harbour,

heading: General
paragraph: (a) have an open fire on a vessel, or

heading: General
paragraph: (b) berth a vessel that, because of its size or dangerous condition, may endanger or damage the harbour facilities or other vessels;

heading: General
paragraph: without the approval of the harbour manager.

heading: General
paragraph: 10 Where harbour property is damaged in any manner by a vessel or vehicle, or by the use of machinery or equipment, the damage shall be reported forthwith to the harbour manager by the master or other person in charge of the vessel or the operator of the vehicle, or the person who was in charge of the machinery or equipment at the time the damage occurred.

heading: General
paragraph: 11 No person shall remove, damage or destroy any notice posted at a harbour by the Minister.

heading: General
paragraph: 13 No person shall obstruct or impede in any way the docking or undocking of any vessel in a harbour.

heading: General
paragraph: 14 Where a harbour manager has directed orally or by notice in writing the place where, the manner in which and the time when a vessel is to be berthed, moored, moved, loaded or unloaded, no person shall berth, moor, move, load or unload a vessel except as so directed.

heading: General
paragraph: 16 No person shall, on harbour property, without the approval of the harbour manager

heading: General
paragraph: (a) engage in equipment or machinery tests that are likely to endanger harbour property or vessels or persons in the harbour; or

heading: General
paragraph: (b) engage in repairs to the hull, machinery, tackle or gear of a vessel beyond normal routine maintenance.

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: 17 No person shall permit the lines of a vessel that is berthed or moored at a harbour to be made fast to anything other than the facilities provided for berthing or mooring or permit such lines to lie across any wharf or across any channel in such a manner as to obstruct or interfere with any other vessel, vehicle or person.

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: 18 Where a vessel is moored in a harbour, the master or person in charge shall, where necessary, permit another vessel to move alongside and make fast to it.

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: 19 Where two or more vessels are lying at the same wharf, one vessel outside the other, and the vessel on the outside does not have a gangway extending to the wharf, the person in charge of the vessel lying nearer to the wharf shall allow persons on the vessel farther from the wharf free and unencumbered passage over its deck.

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: 20 (1) Where a vessel is made fast to or secured alongside another vessel, one vessel outside the other,

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: (a) the lines of the vessel that is so made fast or secured shall not, except in an emergency, be cut or cast off by any person unless that person gives notice of his intention to do so to the master or person in charge of that vessel; and

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: (b) the master or person in charge of the inside vessel, when ready to leave harbour, may move any outside vessel if the owner or persons in charge of any such vessel cannot be located.

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: (2) Where a person moves a vessel pursuant to paragraph (1)(b), that person shall resecure any vessel that has been so moved.

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: 21 (1) Where goods or articles fall overboard from a vessel, the master or person in charge of the vessel shall make every reasonable effort to recover those goods or articles.

heading: Mooring Vessels
paragraph: (2) Where the master or person in charge referred to in subsection (1) is unable to recover any goods or articles referred to therein, he shall report such failure to the harbour manager.

heading: Mooring Vessels

heading: Mooring Vessels

heading: Mooring Vessels

heading: Mooring Vessels

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "board" has the same meaning as in the Code;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Code" means the Labour Relations Code;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "collective agreement" means a written agreement between an employer or an employers' organization authorized by the employer, and a trade union providing for minimum prices or prices of fish, share arrangements between vessel owners and crew members on fishing vessels, hours of work or other conditions of employment and includes any such agreement that was entered into before June 30, 1994 and that is still in force;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "employee" means a person engaged in commercial fishing and includes a person who agrees to accept as remuneration a share or portion of the proceeds of a fishing venture;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "employer" means a person who employs one or more employees and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person who purchases fish from a commercial fisher,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person who provides as remuneration a share or portion of the proceeds of a fishing venture, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) an employers' organization;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish" means any species of animal living in water, including its eggs or roe;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "lockout" means a lockout as defined in the Code and includes a refusal by an employer to accept or purchase fish, done to compel the employer's employees or to aid another employer in compelling that employer's employees to agree to conditions of employment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "strike" means a strike as defined in the Code and includes a refusal to engage in fishing or to sell or deliver fish by employees in combination or in concert or in accordance with a common understanding.

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: 2		  This Act applies to persons engaged in the catching or harvesting of fish and to persons purchasing fish.

heading: Application of Labour Relations Code
paragraph:
3
		  The Code and the regulations under it apply in respect of the matters to which this Act applies, but if there is a conflict or inconsistency between this Act and the Code, this Act applies.

heading: Voluntary recognition
paragraph:
4
		  Nothing in this Act prohibits or terminates any voluntary recognition of trade unions by employers.

heading: Unfair labour practices
paragraph:
5
		  (1) An employer or a person acting on behalf of an employer must not refuse to purchase fish from a person because the person

heading: Unfair labour practices
paragraph: (a) is or proposes to become or seeks to induce another person to become a member or officer of a trade union, or

heading: Unfair labour practices
paragraph: (b) participates in the promotion, formation or administration of a trade union.

heading: Unfair labour practices
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), this Act must not be interpreted to limit or otherwise affect the right of an employer to make a change in the operation of the employer's business reasonably necessary for the proper conduct of that business.

heading: Unfair labour practices
paragraph: (3) Section 14 of the Code applies with respect to an act prohibited by this section.

heading: Successor rights
paragraph:
6
		  Section 35 of the Code does not apply with respect to the sale of a fishing vessel.

heading: Strike or lockout
paragraph:
7
		  Despite section 57 of the Code, a strike or lockout arising from collective bargaining in respect of a species of fish is not unlawful only because it occurs during the term of a collective agreement in respect of a different species of fish.

heading: Dismissal provision in collective agreement
paragraph:
8
		  Section 84 (1) and (3) of the Code does not apply

heading: Dismissal provision in collective agreement
paragraph: (a) to a collective agreement in respect of the price or minimum price of fish, or

heading: Dismissal provision in collective agreement
paragraph: (b) to an employment relationship where the employer maintains no control over the discipline or dismissal of the employee.

heading: Determination of appropriate unit
paragraph:
9
		  When the board, under section 22.1 (a) of the Code, is determining whether a unit is appropriate for collective bargaining, it may consider, in addition to other matters it considers relevant, the manner in which negotiations in the fishing industry have taken place in the past, including such matters as whether negotiations have taken place based on fish species and gear type.

heading: First collective agreement
paragraph:
10
		  Section 55 of the Code does not apply to collective bargaining between a trade union and an employer if the trade union and the employer have negotiated one or more collective agreements with each other before June 30, 1994.

heading: Change during certification or bargaining
paragraph:
11
		  (1) Despite section 32 (1) of the Code, an employer may alter the price or minimum price that it offers for fish while an application for certification is pending.

heading: Change during certification or bargaining
paragraph: (2) Despite section 45 (1) (b) of the Code, an employer may alter the price or minimum price that it offers for fish during the 4 month period following certification.

heading: Change during certification or bargaining
paragraph: (3) Despite section 45 (2) of the Code, an employer may alter the price or minimum price that it offers for fish if the term of a collective agreement that was in force between the parties has expired.

heading: Change during certification or bargaining
paragraph: (4) This section does not apply where the alteration is made in a manner inconsistent with section 5, 6, 9 or 11 of the Code or section 5 of this Act.

heading: Effect of certification
paragraph:
12
		  It is not inconsistent with section 27 (1) (a) or section 48 of the Code for an employer to pay bonuses or make other payments to employees above the minimum price in a collective agreement.

heading: Refusal to purchase fish
paragraph:
13
		  This Act must not be construed to prohibit a refusal to purchase fish for a cause not constituting a lockout.

heading: Jurisdiction of Labour Relations Board
paragraph:
14
		  The board has exclusive jurisdiction to decide a question arising under this Act, including jurisdiction to decide

heading: Jurisdiction of Labour Relations Board
paragraph: (a) that a person may be an employee for some purposes and an employer for other purposes, and

heading: Jurisdiction of Labour Relations Board
paragraph: (b) that the relationship between a person engaged in commercial fishing and a purchaser of fish constitutes an employment relationship.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: amidships means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in Part 0.1, the mid-point of the hull length of a fishing vessel; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in Parts I and II, the mid-point of the length of a fishing vessel. (milieu du batiment)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: closed construction, in respect of a fishing vessel, means that more than 50 per cent of the length of the vessel is covered full width, at or above the gunwale level, by decks or permanent enclosures. (ponte)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: existing, in respect of a fishing vessel, means that the vessel is not new. (existant)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fishing vessel means a vessel that is used or is to be used for commercially catching, harvesting or transporting fish or other living marine resources. (batiment de peche)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: length, in respect of a fishing vessel, means, in Parts I and II,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the distance from the fore part of the uppermost end of the stem to the aft side of the head of the stern post, except that if a stern post is not fitted to the vessel, the measurement shall be taken to the foreside of the head of the rudder stock; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if the vessel has no rudder stock or has a rudder stock situated outside the hull at the stern, the distance from the foreside of the foremost permanent structure of the vessel to the aft side of the aftermost permanent structure of the vessel, not including guards or rubbing strakes. (longueur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: new, in respect of a fishing vessel, means, in Parts I and II, that construction of the vessel started on or after January 6, 1965. This definition applies also to any foreign fishing vessel brought under Canadian registry, regardless of the date on which its construction started. (neuf)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: open construction, in respect of a fishing vessel, means that the vessel is not one of closed construction. (non ponte)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: TP 127 means the Ship Safety Electrical Standards, issued by the Department of Transport, as amended from time to time. (TP 127)

heading: Canadian vessels
paragraph: 3 These Regulations apply in respect of fishing vessels that are Canadian vessels and that are not more than 24.4 m in length and not more than 150 gross tonnage.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 3.01 (1) The following definitions apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: breadth means the maximum breadth of a fishing vessel, measured amidships to the moulded line of the frame in the case of a vessel with metal shell plating, and measured to the outer surface of the shell plating in any other case. (largeur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: classification society means a classification society that is a member of the International Association of Classification Societies (IACS).  (societe de classification)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: engine space means any space that contains a permanently installed propulsion engine or auxiliary engine, and includes any connected spaces.  (compartiment moteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: EPIRB means an emergency position-indicating radio beacon. (RLS)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hull length, in respect of a fishing vessel, means the distance measured from the forward end of the foremost outside surface of the hull shell to the aft end of the aftermost outside surface of the hull shell. (longueur de coque)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: IMO Resolution MSC.81(70) means the annex to International Maritime Organization Resolution MSC.81(70), Revised Recommendation on Testing of Life-Saving Appliances. (resolution MSC.81(70) de l'OMI)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inland voyage has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations. (voyage en eaux internes)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: IS Code means the annex to International Maritime Organization Resolution MSC.267(85), International Code on Intact Stability, 2008. (recueil IS)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: lifebuoy means a SOLAS lifebuoy or a small vessel lifebuoy. (bouee de sauvetage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: lifejacket means a small vessel lifejacket, a standard lifejacket, a Class 1 or Class 2 lifejacket or a SOLAS lifejacket. (gilet de sauvetage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: life raft means a SOLAS life raft, a reduced capacity life raft or a coastal life raft. (radeau de sauvetage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: LSA Code means the annex to International Maritime Organization Resolution MSC.48(66), International Life-Saving Appliance (LSA) Code. (recueil LSA)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: machinery space means any space containing propelling machinery, steering gears, boilers, steam and internal combustion engines, generators and major electrical machinery, oil filling stations, refrigerating, stabilizing, ventilation and air-conditioning machinery, and any similar spaces and trunks to those spaces. (tranche des machines)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: near coastal voyage, Class 1 has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations. (voyage a proximite du littoral, classe 1)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: near coastal voyage, Class 2 has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations. (voyage a proximite du littoral, classe 2)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: near coastal voyage, Class 2, restricted to 2 nautical miles means a near coastal voyage, Class 2, during which the fishing vessel engaged on the voyage is always within 2 nautical miles from shore. (voyage a proximite du littoral, classe 2, limite a 2 milles)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: new, in respect of a fishing vessel, means that construction of the vessel started - or that a contract was signed for the construction of the vessel or that the vessel was imported into Canada and registered for the first time in Canada - more than one year after the day on which these Regulations come into force. (neuf)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: permanently installed, in respect of an object, means securely fastened so that tools must be used for its removal. (fixe a demeure)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: power-driven, in respect of a fishing vessel, means that the fishing vessel is propelled by an engine or has an engine on board to propel it. (a propulsion mecanique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: product certification body means a body that is accredited by the Standards Council of Canada, or by any other national accreditation organization that is a member of the International Accreditation Forum Multilateral Recognition Arrangement, to give third-party written assurance that a product meets the specified requirements for the product, including initial certification of the product and maintenance of that certification. (organisme de certification de produits)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pyrotechnic distress signal means a rocket parachute flare, a multi-star flare, a hand flare, or a buoyant or hand smoke signal. (signal de detresse pyrotechnique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: readily accessible means capable of being reached easily and safely under emergency conditions without the use of tools. (facilement accessible)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: reboarding device means a ladder, lifting harness or other apparatus, not including any part of a fishing vessel's propulsion unit, that assists a person to reboard the vessel from the water. (dispositif de remontee a bord)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: recommended practices and standards means the recommended practices and standards for marine use issued by a marine classification society, standards development organization, industrial or trade organization, government, government agency or international body. (normes et pratiques recommandees)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: recovery boat means a boat that is auxiliary to a fishing vessel and that can be used in an emergency. (embarcation de recuperation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sheltered waters voyage has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations. (voyage en eaux abritees)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: SOLAS means the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, 1974. (SOLAS)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sound-signalling device means a pealess whistle or a compressed-gas or electric horn. (dispositif de signalisation sonore)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: TP 1332 means the Construction Standards for Small Vessels, published by the Department of Transport. (TP 1332)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: TP 14475 means the Canadian Life Saving Appliance Standard, published by the Department of Transport. (TP 14475)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: unlimited voyage has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations. (voyage illimite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: watertight, in respect of a structure, means capable of preventing the passage of water through the structure in any direction under a head of water for which the structure is designed. (etanche a l'eau)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: weathertight, in respect of a fishing vessel, means that in any sea conditions water will not penetrate into the vessel. (etanche aux intemperies)

heading: Near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (1.1) For the purposes of this Part, a reference to "near coastal voyage, Class 2" shall be read as including a reference to "inland voyage", except in the following provisions:

heading: Near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (a) subsection 3.25(1); and

heading: Near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (b) subparagraphs 2(b)(ii), 3(b)(ii), 4(b)(ii) and 5(b)(ii) of the table to subsection 3.27(1).

heading: Near coastal voyage, Class 2, restricted to 2 nautical miles
paragraph: (1.2) For the purposes of this Part, a reference to "near coastal voyage, Class 2, restricted to 2 nautical miles" shall be read as including a reference to "inland voyage" during which the fishing vessel engaged on the inland voyage is always within 2 nautical miles from shore.

heading: Documents incorporated by reference
paragraph: (2) Except as otherwise indicated in this Part, any reference in this Part to a document is a reference to that document as amended from time to time.

heading: Inconsistencies
paragraph: (3) In the event of an inconsistency between a provision in a document incorporated by reference and a provision in this Part, the provision in this Part prevails.

heading: Date of construction
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this Part, a reference to the date of construction, manufacture or rebuilding of a fishing vessel is to be read as a reference to the date on which the actual construction, manufacture or rebuilding starts.

heading: IS Code
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of the application of the IS Code,

heading: IS Code
paragraph: (a) "Administration" shall be read as "Minister";

heading: IS Code
paragraph: (b) "should" shall be read as "shall", and any recommendations are to be considered mandatory; and

heading: IS Code
paragraph: (c) any guidelines, explanatory notes, requirements or similar matters set out in a document referred to in a footnote to the IS Code are to be considered mandatory.

heading: Responsibility
paragraph: 3.02 Unless otherwise indicated in this Part, the authorized representative and the master of a fishing vessel shall ensure that the requirements of this Part are met.

heading: Design, construction and equipment
paragraph: 3.03 (1) The authorized representative of a fishing vessel shall ensure that the vessel is designed, constructed and equipped to operate safely and be seaworthy in its area of operation.

heading: Safe operation and seaworthiness
paragraph: (2) If the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the design, construction or equipment of a fishing vessel adversely affects its safe operation or seaworthiness in its area of operation, the Minister shall request the authorized representative of the vessel to establish that the vessel meets the requirements of subsection (1).

heading: Maintenance of machinery and equipment
paragraph: 3.04 (1) A fishing vessel, as well as its machinery and equipment, shall be maintained to ensure that it is in a safe operating condition.

heading: Maintenance records
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a fishing vessel shall maintain records on the maintenance of the vessel and of its machinery and equipment.

heading: Prohibition - freezing spray
paragraph: 3.05 (1) No person shall operate, or permit another person to operate, a fishing vessel in an area for which a freezing spray warning has been issued by Environment Canada unless the stability assessment for the vessel has demonstrated that the vessel has the capability to operate safely in freezing spray conditions when ice accretion is likely to occur.

heading: Accumulated ice
paragraph: (2) If a freezing spray warning has been issued by Environment Canada for an area in which a fishing vessel is operated or is intended to be operated, the vessel shall carry on board a means to remove accumulated ice from the vessel.

heading: Before first putting into service
paragraph: 3.06 (1) The authorized representative of a fishing vessel shall not operate, or permit another person to operate, the fishing vessel unless, before the vessel is first put into service, its authorized representative has informed the Minister of

heading: Before first putting into service
paragraph: (a) the intention to operate the vessel or permit its operation;

heading: Before first putting into service
paragraph: (b) the physical characteristics of the vessel; and

heading: Before first putting into service
paragraph: (c) the nature of its operation.

heading: Information provided to Minister
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a fishing vessel shall provide the Minister, on request, with information respecting the physical characteristics of the fishing vessel and the nature of its operation.

heading: Exceeding design limitations
paragraph: 3.07 No person shall operate, or permit another person to operate, a fishing vessel under circumstances that exceed its design limitations.

heading: Careless operation
paragraph: 3.08 No person shall operate a fishing vessel in a careless manner, without due care and attention or without reasonable consideration for other persons.

heading: Safety of persons on board jeopardized
paragraph: 3.09 No person shall operate, or permit another person to operate, a fishing vessel in environmental conditions or circumstances that could jeopardize the safety of persons on board unless a lifejacket required by this Part, or a personal flotation device that meets the requirements of section 3.2, is worn

heading: Safety of persons on board jeopardized
paragraph: (a) by all persons on board, in the case of a fishing vessel that has no deck or deck structure; or

heading: Safety of persons on board jeopardized
paragraph: (b) by all persons on the deck or in the cockpit, in the case of a fishing vessel that has a deck or deck structure.

heading: Openings closed at sea
paragraph: 3.1 When a fishing vessel is at sea, openings on the vessel that are exposed to the weather and to the sea and that can be closed shall be kept closed unless they must be kept open for the operation of the vessel, in which case they shall be closed immediately if there is a danger of water entering the interior spaces of the hull.

heading: Stowage of tools and spare parts
paragraph: 3.11 Tools and spare parts necessary for performing routine maintenance on and minor repairs to machinery, electrical equipment and installations shall be carried on board a fishing vessel and securely stowed in a readily accessible location.

heading: Record of modifications affecting stability
paragraph: 3.12 The authorized representative of a fishing vessel shall ensure that a record is kept of any modification or series of modifications that affects the stability of the vessel. The record shall be in the form and manner specified by the Minister.

heading: Engine space blower
paragraph: 3.13 No person shall start a gasoline-powered fishing vessel unless the engine space blower has been operated for a period of not less than four minutes immediately before the engine is started.

heading: Leakage of fuel
paragraph: 3.14 (1) No person shall permit fuel leakage within or from a fishing vessel.

heading: Discharge of fuel or oil
paragraph: (2) No person shall permit fuel or oil to be discharged from a fishing vessel except in accordance with the provisions relating to discharges of oil or oily mixtures in section 5 of Part 1 and Subdivision 4 of Division 1 of Part 2 of the Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations.

heading: Fuelling
paragraph: (3) No person shall fuel a gasoline-powered fishing vessel that is at dockside or beached unless

heading: Fuelling
paragraph: (a) if the vessel is equipped with a portable fuel tank, the tank is first removed from it; or

heading: Fuelling
paragraph: (b) if the vessel is equipped with a fixed fuel tank, the person fuelling the vessel is the only person on board.

heading: Fuelling - fixed fuel tank
paragraph: (4) No person shall fuel a gasoline-powered fishing vessel that is equipped with a fixed fuel tank unless all electrical equipment is switched off, all doors, windows and ports are closed, all engines are shut off and all open flames, including pilot lights, are extinguished.

heading: Portable container
paragraph: (5) No person shall carry liquid fuel on board a fishing vessel in a portable container that has not been designed to carry the fuel.

heading: Storage of portable fuel tank
paragraph: (6) A portable fuel tank containing fuel and carried on board a fishing vessel shall be stored as far away as practicable from heat and ignition sources, machinery spaces and crew's quarters.

heading: Filling of fixed fuel tank
paragraph: (7) No person shall fill a fixed fuel tank on board a fishing vessel by means of a funnel, nozzle or similar device unless continuous contact is maintained between the shipboard filling pipe and the filling device immediately prior to and during the fuelling operation.

heading: Portable fuel-burning equipment or appliance
paragraph: 3.15 Any portable fuel-burning equipment or appliance used on a fishing vessel shall be

heading: Portable fuel-burning equipment or appliance
paragraph: (a) used only in a well-ventilated location that is in an open space or on an open deck;

heading: Portable fuel-burning equipment or appliance
paragraph: (b) well secured to prevent its movement while in use; and

heading: Portable fuel-burning equipment or appliance
paragraph: (c) when not in use, stored in a well-ventilated location that is isolated from heat and ignition sources.

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: 3.16 (1) Safety procedures shall be established in writing, in English or French or in both, according to the needs of the crew, and implemented to familiarize persons on board a fishing vessel with

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: (a) the location and use of all safety equipment;

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: (b) all the measures that must be taken to protect persons on board, in particular measures to prevent persons from falling overboard, measures to retrieve persons who have fallen overboard, measures to protect limbs from rotating equipment, and measures to avoid ropes, docking lines, nets and other fishing equipment that may pose a safety hazard to persons on board;

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: (c) in the case of beam trawling and purse seining operations, the quick release of loads that can be activated in an emergency;

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: (d) all the measures that must be taken to prevent fires and explosions on the vessel;

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: (e) if the vessel has a deck or deck structure, all the measures that must be taken to maintain watertightness and weathertightness and to prevent flooding of the interior spaces of the hull or, if the vessel has no deck or deck structure, all the measures that must be taken to prevent swamping of the vessel;

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: (f) all the measures that must be taken to ensure safe loading, stowage and unloading of fish catches, baits and consumables; and

heading: Written safety procedures
paragraph: (g) the operation of towing and lifting equipment and the measures that must be taken to prevent overloading of the vessel.

heading: Drills on procedures
paragraph: (2) Drills on the safety procedures shall be held to ensure that the crew is at all times proficient in carrying out those procedures.

heading: Record of drills
paragraph: (3) A record shall be kept of every drill.

heading: Record keeping - maintenance and drills
paragraph: 3.17 (1) A record on the maintenance of a fishing vessel and a record of a drill on the safety procedures shall be kept for a period of seven years after the day on which it is established.

heading: Record of modifications affecting stability
paragraph: (2) In the case of a fishing vessel that has undergone a stability assessment, a record of a modification or series of modifications that affects the stability of the vessel shall be kept until the vessel undergoes a new stability assessment that takes into account the modification or series of modifications.

heading: Transfer of ownership
paragraph: (3) When ownership of a fishing vessel is transferred, the authorized representative of the vessel shall provide the new owner with any records kept in respect of the vessel.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 3.18 (1) No person shall operate, or permit another person to operate, a fishing vessel unless the safety equipment required by this Division is carried on board the vessel and the equipment meets the requirements of this Division.

heading: Replacement of safety equipment
paragraph: (2) However, equipment that was acquired before the day on which this Division comes into force may replace any safety equipment required by this Division if the equipment meets the requirements of these Regulations as they read before that day and if the equipment is in good working order or, in the case of equipment that bears an expiry date, that date has not expired.

heading: Quantity in excess - previously acquired equipment
paragraph: (3) Any equipment that exceeds the quantity of safety equipment required and that was acquired before the day on which this Division comes into force may be carried on board a fishing vessel if the equipment meets the requirements of these Regulations as they read before that day and if the equipment is in good working order or, in the case of equipment that bears an expiry date, that date has not expired.

heading: Quantity in excess - recently acquired equipment
paragraph: (4) Any equipment that exceeds the quantity of safety equipment required and that was acquired on or after the day on which this Division comes into force may be carried on board a fishing vessel if the equipment meets the requirements of this Division.

heading: Other equipment
paragraph: (5) Any equipment that is not of a type referred to in this Division may be carried on board a fishing vessel if the equipment is not likely to be confused with safety equipment.

heading: Mark or label indicating approval by Minister
paragraph: 3.19 (1) An immersion suit, anti-exposure suit, emergency boat, recovery boat or rescue boat that is referred to in these Regulations and that may be carried on board a fishing vessel shall bear a mark or label indicating that it is of a type approved by the Minister.

heading: Applicable standards and test
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall approve a type of equipment referred to in subsection (1) if it is shown to meet the applicable standards and tests referred to in Schedule X.

heading: Mark or label - Small Vessel Regulations
paragraph: 3.2 (1) A personal flotation device, lifejacket, lifebuoy, self-igniting light, pyrotechnic distress signal or life raft referred to in these Regulations shall bear a mark or label indicating that it is of a type approved by the Minister under the Small Vessel Regulations.

heading: Alternative mark or label
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a personal flotation device if it has been approved by the Director of Ship Safety of the Department of Transport or by the Department of Fisheries and Oceans and if it bears a mark or label indicating that it was approved by one of those departments or by the Canadian Coast Guard.

heading: Personal flotation device
paragraph: (3) An approved personal flotation device

heading: Personal flotation device
paragraph: (a) shall be fitted with retro-reflective tape and a whistle; and

heading: Personal flotation device
paragraph: (b) shall have an outer covering of a highly visible colour or, in the case of an inflatable personal flotation device, shall have an internal bladder of a highly visible colour.

heading: Equivalent level of safety
paragraph: 3.21 (1) If the Minister determines that there are circumstances in which equipment other than the safety equipment required by these Regulations provides a level of safety at least equivalent to that provided by the required safety equipment, the other equipment may be substituted for the required safety equipment in those circumstances.

heading: Factors
paragraph: (2) To determine the level of safety provided by the substitute equipment in the circumstances, the Minister shall assess the following factors:

heading: Factors
paragraph: (a) the nature of the activity;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (b) the environmental conditions;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (c) the nature of the risks to which persons on board are exposed;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (d) the specific characteristics of the equipment;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (e) the recommended practices and standards to which the equipment conforms;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (f) the manner in which the equipment will be used; and

heading: Factors
paragraph: (g) the ability of the equipment to protect a person from injury.

heading: Mark or label
paragraph: (3) The substitute equipment shall bear a mark or label indicating that it conforms to the recommended practices and standards applicable to that type of equipment.

heading: Requirements for safety equipment
paragraph: 3.22 (1) The safety equipment required by these Regulations shall

heading: Requirements for safety equipment
paragraph: (a) be in good working order;

heading: Requirements for safety equipment
paragraph: (b) be readily accessible and available for immediate use; and

heading: Requirements for safety equipment
paragraph: (c) except for a life raft, be maintained and replaced in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions or recommendations.

heading: Alterations
paragraph: (2) Safety equipment shall not be altered in any way that compromises its performance or that diminishes the integrity or readability of a marking set out in a standard related to it.

heading: Extinguishers
paragraph: (3) A portable fire extinguisher and a fixed fire extinguishing system required by these Regulations shall be kept fully charged.

heading: English and French
paragraph: 3.23 A mark or label on the safety equipment required by this Division, and any related manufacturer's instructions or recommendations, shall be in English and French.

heading: Contents
paragraph: 3.24 A fishing vessel shall carry on board one of the following first aid kits, which shall be packed in a waterproof case that is capable of being tightly closed after use:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) a marine emergency first aid kit that contains the following:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (i) an up-to-date first aid manual or up-to-date first aid instructions, in English and French,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (ii) 48 doses of analgesic medication of a non-narcotic type,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (iii) six safety pins or one roll of adhesive first aid tape,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (iv) one pair of bandage scissors or safety scissors,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (v) one resuscitation face shield,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (vi) two pairs of examination gloves,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (vii) 10 applications of antiseptic preparations,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (viii) 12 applications of burn preparations,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (ix) 20 adhesive plasters in assorted sizes,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (x) 10 sterile compression bandages in assorted sizes,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (xi) 4 m of elastic bandage,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (xii) two sterile gauze compresses,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (xiii) two triangular bandages, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (xiv) a waterproof list of the contents, in English and French; or

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) a first aid kit that meets the requirements of the Maritime Occupational Health and Safety Regulations or of provincial regulations governing workers' compensation, with the addition of a resuscitation face shield and two pairs of examination gloves if the kit is not required to contain them.

heading: Lifejacket
paragraph: 3.25 (1) A fishing vessel shall carry on board a lifejacket of an appropriate size for each person on board, but the lifejacket shall not be a Class 2 lifejacket or a small vessel lifejacket if the vessel is engaged on a voyage beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, Class 2.

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (2) Instead of the lifejacket referred to in subsection (1), a fishing vessel that has a hull length of not more than 12 m and that is engaged on a near coastal voyage, Class 2, may carry on board a personal flotation device that meets the requirements of section 3.2 if

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (a) the personal flotation device

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (i) provides at least 100 N of buoyancy and has a turning capability, or

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (ii) is designed to provide thermal protection; and

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2
paragraph: (b) in the case of a fishing vessel that has no deck or deck structure and that is underway, the personal flotation device is worn by everyone on board or, in the case of a fishing vessel that has a deck or deck structure and that is underway, it is worn by the persons on deck or in the cockpit.

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2, etc.
paragraph: (3) Instead of the lifejacket referred to in subsection (1), a fishing vessel that has a hull length of not more than 12 m and that is engaged on a near coastal voyage, Class 2, restricted to 2 nautical miles, or a sheltered waters voyage, may carry on board a personal flotation device that meets the requirements of section 3.2 if

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2, etc.
paragraph: (a) in the case of a fishing vessel that has no deck or deck structure and that is underway, the personal flotation device is worn by everyone on board; or

heading: Replacement of a lifejacket - near coastal voyage, Class 2, etc.
paragraph: (b) in the case of a fishing vessel that has a deck or deck structure and that is underway, it is worn by the persons on deck or in the cockpit.

heading: Additional personal life-saving appliances
paragraph: 3.26 (1) A fishing vessel shall carry on board the following additional personal life-saving appliances:

heading: Additional personal life-saving appliances
paragraph: (a) a reboarding device;

heading: Additional personal life-saving appliances
paragraph: (b) an apparatus that can be used to retrieve a person who has fallen overboard without the assistance of the person overboard, unless the vessel carries a recovery boat or the operator of the vessel is the only person on board; and

heading: Additional personal life-saving appliances
paragraph: (c) in the case of a fishing vessel that has a hull length set out in column 1 of the table to this paragraph, the additional personal life-saving appliances set out in column 2.

paragraph: (b) a SOLAS lifebuoy that is equipped with a self-igniting light or that is attached to a buoyant line of not less than 30 m in length

paragraph: (a) a buoyant heaving line of not less than 30 m in length;

heading: Additional personal life-saving appliances
paragraph: (b) a SOLAS lifebuoy attached to a buoyant line of not less than 30 m in length; and

heading: Additional personal life-saving appliances
paragraph: (c) a SOLAS lifebuoy that is equipped with a self-igniting light

heading: Buoyant heaving line
paragraph: (2) A buoyant heaving line set out in the table to paragraph (1)(c) shall be fitted at one end with a buoyant mass that will assist in carrying out the end of the line when the line is thrown.

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: 3.27 (1) A fishing vessel that has a hull length set out in column 1 of the table to this subsection shall carry on board the visual signals set out in column 2.

paragraph: TABLE

paragraph: (a) a watertight flashlight; and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) three pyrotechnic distress signals other than smoke signals

paragraph: (a) a watertight flashlight; and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) the following visual signals:

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (i) for a voyage that is not beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, Class 2, six pyrotechnic distress signals other than smoke signals, or

paragraph: (ii) for a voyage that is beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, class 2, six pyrotechnic distress signals - other than smoke signals - of which at least two are rocket parachute flares

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) the following visual signals:

paragraph: (i) for a voyage that is not beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, Class 2, six pyrotechnic distress signals of which not more than three are smoke signals, or

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (ii) for a voyage that is beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, class 2, six pyrotechnic distress signals of which at least two are rocket parachute flares and not more than three are smoke signals, which shall be buoyant smoke signals; and

paragraph: (c) a signalling mirror

paragraph: (ii) for a voyage that is beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, class 2, twelve pyrotechnic distress signals of which at least four are rocket parachute flares and not more than six are smoke signals, which shall be buoyant smoke signals; and

paragraph: (i) for a voyage that is not beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, Class 2, twelve pyrotechnic distress signals of which not more than six are smoke signals, or

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (ii) for a voyage that is beyond the limits of a near coastal voyage, class 2, twelve pyrotechnic distress signals of which at least six are rocket parachute flares and not more than six are smoke signals, which shall be buoyant smoke signals; and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (c) a signalling mirror

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A fishing vessel is not required to carry on board pyrotechnic distress signals if the vessel is equipped with a two-way radio communication system that makes it possible to maintain communication and the vessel is operated

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) on a river, canal or lake where it cannot at any time be more than one nautical mile from the closest shore;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) exclusively within the confines of a manned aquaculture facility; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) within 500 m from shore.

heading: Expiry
paragraph: (3) A pyrotechnic distress signal expires four years after its date of manufacture.

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: 3.28 (1) A fishing vessel that is engaged on a voyage set out in column 1 of the table to this subsection, and that has a hull length set out in column 2, shall carry on board the life-saving appliances set out in column 3.

heading: Requirement to carry on board
