heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (a) two or more SOLAS life rafts or reduced capacity life rafts with a total capacity that is sufficient to carry, on each side of the vessel, the number of persons on board;

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) one recovery boat; and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (c) an immersion suit of an appropriate size for each person on board

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (a) one or more SOLAS life rafts or reduced capacity life rafts with total a capacity that is sufficient to carry the number of persons on board; and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) an immersion suit of an appropriate size for each person on board

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (a) one or more life rafts, or a combination of life rafts and recovery boats, with a total capacity that is sufficient to carry the number of persons on board;

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) an EPIRB, unless the vessel is carrying on board an EPIRB required under the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020; and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (c) if the water temperature is less than 15°C, an immersion suit or an anti-exposure work suit of an appropriate size for each person on board

paragraph: (a) one or more life rafts, or a combination of life rafts and recovery boats, with a total capacity that is sufficient to carry the number of persons on board; or

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) the following equipment:

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (i) an EPIRB or a means of two-way radio communication, unless the vessel is carrying on board an EPIRB required under the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (ii) if the water temperature is less than 15°C, an immersion suit or an anti-exposure work suit of an appropriate size for each person on board

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (a) one or more life rafts or recovery boats with a total capacity that is sufficient to carry the number of the persons on board; or

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) the following equipment:

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (i) an EPIRB or a means of two-way radio communication, unless the vessel is carrying on board an EPIRB required under the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, and

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (ii) if the water temperature is less than 15°C, an immersion suit or an anti-exposure work suit of an appropriate size for each person on board

heading: Appliances or written procedures
paragraph: (2) Instead of carrying on board the appliances referred to in subparagraph 5(b)(ii) of the table to subsection (1), a fishing vessel engaged on a sheltered waters voyage may carry on board appliances or written procedures, or a combination of both, for protecting all persons on board from the effects of hypothermia or cold shock resulting from swamping, capsizing or falling overboard.

heading: Substitute for recovery boat
paragraph: (3) A fishing vessel referred in subsection (1) is not required to carry on board a recovery boat if the vessel carries on board an emergency boat, a rescue boat, or a seine skiff that is ordinarily used in the fishing vessel's fishing operations.

heading: Requirements for life rafts
paragraph: 3.29 A life raft that is carried on board a fishing vessel shall

heading: Requirements for life rafts
paragraph: (a) be marked with the date and place of last service;

heading: Requirements for life rafts
paragraph: (b) be serviced, at the intervals set out in section 119 of the Life Saving Equipment Regulations, at a service station that is accredited by the manufacturer of the life raft; and

heading: Requirements for life rafts
paragraph: (c) except in the case of a coastal life raft that is packed in a valise-type container, be stored in a manner that allows it to automatically float free if the vessel sinks.

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: 3.3 A recovery boat that is carried on board a fishing vessel shall carry on board the following equipment:

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (a) a buoyant safety knife secured near the painter;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (b) a bailer secured within the boat;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (c) a set of oars or paddles, with locks, secured within the boat;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (d) a boat hook;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (e) a painter secured forward, or a quick release slip that can be operated under strain;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (f) if there are plugholes, a plug for each plughole, secured near the plughole;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (g) a buoyant heaving line of not less than 15 m in length;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (h) a flash light with spare bulb and batteries;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (i) a rustproof whistle;

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (j) two red hand flares; and

heading: Requirements for recovery boats
paragraph: (k) in the case of an inflatable boat, an air pump with fittings suitable for replenishing the inflated chambers.

heading: Launching appliance
paragraph: 3.31 A life raft, emergency boat, recovery boat or rescue boat shall be equipped with a launching appliance, unless it is capable of being launched safely and rapidly by manual means.

heading: Bailers and bilge pumps
paragraph: 3.32 (1) A fishing vessel that has a hull length of not more than 9 m shall carry on board a bailer or a manual bilge pump.

heading: Manual bilge pump
paragraph: (2) A fishing vessel that has a hull length of more than 9 m shall carry on board a manual bilge pump.

heading: Dimensions - bailer
paragraph: (3) The bailer referred to in subsection (1) shall be made of plastic or metal, have an opening of at least 65 cm2 and have a capacity of at least 750 mL.

heading: Manual bilge pump - piping and operation
paragraph: (4) The manual bilge pump referred to in subsections (1) and (2) shall be

heading: Manual bilge pump - piping and operation
paragraph: (a) fitted with or accompanied by a sufficient length of piping or hose to enable water to be pumped from the bilge space of the fishing vessel over the side of the vessel; and

heading: Manual bilge pump - piping and operation
paragraph: (b) capable of being operated from a position above the deck of the fishing vessel.

heading: Manual propelling device
paragraph: 3.33 A fishing vessel that has no deck or deck structure and that has a hull length of not more than 6 m shall carry on board a set of oars, a paddle or another device that uses human power to propel the vessel.

heading: Anchoring and mooring equipment
paragraph: 3.34 (1) A fishing vessel shall carry on board

heading: Anchoring and mooring equipment
paragraph: (a) anchoring equipment that conforms to recommended practices and standards and that is arranged in such a way that the anchor can be deployed and retrieved effectively;

heading: Anchoring and mooring equipment
paragraph: (b) means to fix the anchor rope to the vessel and to protect the rope against chafing; and

heading: Anchoring and mooring equipment
paragraph: (c) equipment and fittings that are arranged in such a way that the vessel can be effectively secured alongside or moored.

heading: Anchor dragging
paragraph: (2) The anchoring equipment shall be resistant to dragging under normal operating conditions, taking into account the fishing vessel's displacement and windage area.

heading: Illumination of compasses
paragraph: 3.35 (1) A compass that is required to be fitted on a fishing vessel under the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, shall be capable of being illuminated.

heading: Choice of compass
paragraph: (2) A fishing vessel that has a hull length of not more than 8 m and navigates within sight of seamarks shall either carry on board a handheld compass or be fitted with a compass that meets the requirements of the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020 and can be illuminated.

heading: Other navigation equipment
paragraph: 3.36 A fishing vessel

heading: Other navigation equipment
paragraph: (a) shall be equipped with means for determining the depth of water under the vessel, unless the vessel is equipped with lead lines in accordance with the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020; and

heading: Other navigation equipment
paragraph: (b) shall carry on board a sound-signalling device, unless the vessel is carrying on board a sound-signalling appliance required by the Collision Regulations.

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: 3.37 (1) A fishing vessel that has a hull length set out in column 1 of the table to this subsection shall carry on board the firefighting equipment set out in column 2 as indicated in that column.

heading: Requirement to carry on board
paragraph: (b) a 1A:5B:C portable fire extinguisher, if the vessel is equipped with a fuel-burning cooking, heating or refrigerating appliance

paragraph: (a) a 2A:10B:C portable fire extinguisher;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A fishing vessel that is not power-driven and is not equipped with an electrical system is not required to carry on board a portable fire extinguisher set out in paragraphs 1(a), 2(a), 3(a) and 4(a) of the table to subsection (1).

heading: Reduced number of portable fire extinguishers
paragraph: (3) The total number of portable fire extinguishers that must be carried on board a fishing vessel may be reduced by one if the remaining fire extinguishers are arranged so as to be readily accessible near the equipment or locations referred to in paragraphs 1(b), 2(b) and (c), 3(b) and (c) and 4(b) and (c) of the table to subsection (1).

heading: Bucket
paragraph: (4) A bucket set out in paragraphs 3(e) and 4(e) of the table to subsection (1) shall have a capacity of 10 L or more and be fitted with a lanyard of sufficient length to reach the water from the location in which it is stored.

heading: Portable fire extinguishers
paragraph: 3.38 (1) A portable fire extinguisher required by these Regulations to be carried on board a fishing vessel shall

heading: Portable fire extinguishers
paragraph: (a) bear a mark indicating that it is certified for marine use by a product certification body; or

heading: Portable fire extinguishers
paragraph: (b) be of a type that is approved by the United States Coast Guard.

heading: Imported vessel
paragraph: (2) A portable fire extinguisher that is carried on board a fishing vessel imported into Canada and that does not meet the requirements of subsection (1) shall be certified for marine use by a product certification body or a classification society.

heading: Classes of fires
paragraph: 3.39 In any reference in these Regulations to the classification of a portable fire extinguisher, the letters in the classification refer to the following classes of fires:

heading: Classes of fires
paragraph: (a) Class A fires, namely, fires that involve combustible materials such as wood, cloth, paper, rubber and plastic;

heading: Classes of fires
paragraph: (b) Class B fires, namely, fires that involve inflammable liquids, gases and greases;

heading: Classes of fires
paragraph: (c) Class C fires, namely, fires in energized electrical equipment, where the electrical non-conductivity of the extinguishing media is of importance; and

heading: Classes of fires
paragraph: (d) Class K fires, namely, fires in cooking appliances that involve combustible cooking media such as vegetable or animal oils or fats.

heading: Exception
paragraph: 3.4 A fishing vessel may carry on board a portable fire extinguisher that is not marked with a classification set out in column 1 of the table to this section if the fire extinguisher contains an extinguishing agent that is set out in column 2, 3 or 4 and that is of a net weight that corresponds to the classification set out in column 1, and if the fire extinguisher meets the requirements of these Regulations in all other respects.

heading: Exception
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Exceeds classification
paragraph: 3.41 A fishing vessel may carry on board a portable fire extinguisher that exceeds the classification set out for that fire extinguisher in this Division.

heading: Extinguishing agent
paragraph: 3.42 (1) A portable fire extinguisher required by these Regulations to be carried on board a fishing vessel shall contain an extinguishing agent capable of extinguishing any potential fire in the compartment for which the fire extinguisher is intended, and shall not weigh more than 23 kg.

heading: Alternative rating
paragraph: (2) A portable fire extinguisher rated for Class B fires and required by these Regulations to be carried on board a fishing vessel may be replaced with a portable fire extinguisher rated for Class K fires if it is intended for use in an area with cooking appliances that use combustible cooking media.

heading: Carbon dioxide fire extinguisher
paragraph: (3) A portable carbon dioxide fire extinguisher shall be fitted with an electrically non-conductive horn.

heading: Mounting
paragraph: 3.43 (1) A portable fire extinguisher set out in column 2 of the table to subsection 3.37(1) shall be mounted with a clamp or bracket that provides a quick and positive release.

heading: Gas extinguishing agent
paragraph: (2) A portable fire extinguisher intended for use in an accommodation space, or stored in an accommodation space, shall not contain a gas extinguishing agent.

heading: Application
paragraph: 3.44 (1) This Division applies in respect of a fishing vessel that is propelled or designed to be propelled by an engine.

heading: Wooden vessels
paragraph: (2) This Division does not apply in respect of a wooden fishing vessel that was designed to be human-powered but has been modified for propulsion by an outboard motor and

heading: Wooden vessels
paragraph: (a) has no deck or deck structure;

heading: Wooden vessels
paragraph: (b) is not mass produced; and

heading: Wooden vessels
paragraph: (c) has been constructed following traditional methods that have been proven to be effective and reliable over time.

heading: Existing vessels - adequate stability
paragraph: 3.45 The stability and, if applicable, the buoyancy and flotation of an existing fishing vessel that is not required to undergo a stability assessment shall be adequate to safely carry out the vessel's intended operations.

heading: New vessels of more than 6 m but not more than 9 m
paragraph: 3.46 (1) The stability of a new fishing vessel that has a hull length of more than 6 m and not more than 9 m shall conform to recommended practices and standards that are appropriate to the type of vessel and that take into account its intended operations.

heading: Demonstration of conformity with standards
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of the fishing vessel shall demonstrate, on the request of the Minister, that the stability of the vessel conforms to the selected recommended practices and standards.

heading: Some activities - consistency with good practices
paragraph: (3) If the selected recommended practices and standards do not take into account some of the activities of the fishing vessel, its authorized representative shall demonstrate, on the request of the Minister, that the stability of the vessel is adequate to safely carry out those activities, using first principles of naval architecture, appropriate testing, or any other method that is consistent with good practices for assessing the stability of a fishing vessel.

heading: New vessels of not more than 6 m
paragraph: 3.47 (1) The stability of a new fishing vessel that has a hull length of not more than 6 m shall conform to the standards for buoyancy, flotation and stability that are set out in Section 4 of TP 1332.

heading: Demonstration of conformity with TP 1332
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of the fishing vessel shall demonstrate, on the request of the Minister, that the stability of the vessel conforms to the standards for buoyancy, flotation and stability that are set out in Section 4 of TP 1332.

heading: Some activities - consistency with good practices
paragraph: (3) If Section 4 of TP 1332 does not contain standards respecting some of the activities of the fishing vessel, its authorized representative shall demonstrate, on the request of the Minister, that the stability of the vessel is adequate to safely carry out those activities, using first principles of naval architecture, appropriate testing, or any other method that is consistent with good practices for assessing the stability of a fishing vessel.

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: 3.48 (1) No person shall operate, or permit another person to operate, a fishing vessel in the following cases unless the vessel has successfully undergone a stability assessment conducted by a competent person:

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (a) the vessel has a hull length of more than 9 m and

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (i) it is new, or

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (ii) it has undergone a major modification or a change in activity that is likely to adversely affect its stability;

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (b) the vessel is an existing vessel of closed construction, is of more than 15 gross tonnage, is used for catching herring or capelin and, during the period beginning on July 6, 1977 and ending on the day before this Division comes into force,

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (i) its keel was laid,

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (ii) it was registered under Part 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, or under Part 1 the Canada Shipping Act, chapter S-9 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985,

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (iii) it was converted to herring or capelin fishing, or

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (iv) it underwent any modifications that adversely affected its stability characteristics; or

heading: Stability assessment required
paragraph: (c) the vessel is fitted with an anti-roll tank.

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (2) The fishing vessel may undergo either a full or a simplified stability assessment, but shall undergo a full stability assessment

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (a) if the vessel is carrying fish in bulk that exhibit free surface effect, unless

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (i) the fish are carried in containers such as pails, boxes or tote tanks of which none exceed one third of the breadth of the vessel, or

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (ii) the fish hold or deck is divided by two fishtight longitudinal divisions, secured in place;

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (b) if the vessel is carrying fish or liquids that exhibit free surface effect in containers such as live wells, tote tanks or tanked fish holds of which any exceed one third of the breadth of the vessel and

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (i) are not designed to be used at maximum capacity only,

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (ii) are not filled before the vessel's departure or in calm waters, and

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (iii) are not fitted with an alarm to indicate when the tank is not at maximum capacity;

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (c) if the vessel is fitted with an anti-roll tank; or

heading: Type of assessment
paragraph: (d) if the vessel is new and has a hull length of more than 18 m.

heading: Major modification
paragraph: (3) In this section, major modification means a modification or repair, or a series of modifications or repairs, that substantially changes the capacity or size of a fishing vessel or the nature of a system on board a fishing vessel, that affects its watertight integrity or its stability.

heading: Simplified stability assessment
paragraph: 3.49 (1) The stability of a fishing vessel that undergoes a simplified stability assessment shall conform to recommended practices and standards that are appropriate to the type of vessel and that take into account its intended operations.

heading: Some activities - consistency with good practices
paragraph: (2) If the selected recommended practices and standards do not take into account some of the activities of the fishing vessel, the impact of those activities on the stability of the vessel shall be assessed using first principles of naval architecture, appropriate testing, or any other method that is consistent with good practices for assessing the stability of a fishing vessel.

heading: Full stability assessment
paragraph: 3.5 (1) The stability of a fishing vessel that undergoes a full stability assessment shall conform to the applicable standards set out in Chapter 2 of Part A of the IS Code, in sections 2.1.1 to 2.1.4 of Chapter 2 of Part B of the IS Code, in Chapters 3, 6 and in sections 8.1 to 8.4 in Chapter 8 of Part B of the IS Code, and in Annex 1 to the IS Code.

heading: Some activities - consistency with good practices
paragraph: (2) If the standards set out in the IS Code do not take into account some of the activities of the fishing vessel, the impact of those activities on the stability of the vessel shall be assessed using first principles of naval architecture, appropriate testing, or any other method that is consistent with good practices for assessing the stability of a fishing vessel.

heading: Regulatory authorization - full or simplified stability assessment
paragraph: 3.51 The following persons and organizations are competent to conduct a full or simplified stability assessment:

heading: Regulatory authorization - full or simplified stability assessment
paragraph: (a) an engineer who is a member in good standing of the Ordre des ingenieurs du Quebec or an association of professional engineers of a province of Canada or a state of the United States;

heading: Regulatory authorization - full or simplified stability assessment
paragraph: (b) a classification society; and

heading: Regulatory authorization - full or simplified stability assessment
paragraph: (c) a person who has at least three years of post-secondary education in the field of naval architecture, who is a member in good standing of an order or an association of technologists or technicians of a province of Canada, and who has at least five years' experience in the marine transportation industry.

heading: Regulatory authorization - simplified stability assessment
paragraph: 3.52 (1) The following persons are competent to conduct a simplified stability assessment if they have received training, from a training institution or any other organization, in the application of the standards used to conduct a simplified stability assessment and if they have practical experience in the application of those standards:

heading: Regulatory authorization - simplified stability assessment
paragraph: (a) a marine surveyor who is a member in good standing of a national association of accredited or certified marine surveyors of Canada or of the United States; and

heading: Regulatory authorization - simplified stability assessment
paragraph: (b) a builder, manufacturer or rebuilder of fishing vessels.

heading: Training with competent person
paragraph: (2) A person who meets the following requirements is also competent to conduct a simplified stability assessment:

heading: Training with competent person
paragraph: (a) the person has received training from a competent person in the application of the standards used to conduct a simplified stability assessment; and

heading: Training with competent person
paragraph: (b) the person has, after receiving the training, acquired practical experience in the application of those standards.

heading: Designation by Minister - full or simplified stability assessment
paragraph: 3.53 (1) The Minister shall designate a person or class of persons as competent to conduct a full or simplified stability assessment if the person or class of persons has received training in the application of the standards that will be used to conduct the assessment and has the knowledge and experience to conduct the assessment.

heading: Contact information of applicant for designation
paragraph: (2) A person who applies to the Minister to be designated as competent to conduct a full or simplified stability assessment shall provide the Minister with the person's contact information.

heading: Update of contact information
paragraph: 3.54 A person designated by the Minister as competent to conduct a full or simplified stability assessment shall provide the Minister with updated contact information as soon as possible.

heading: Cancellation of designation
paragraph: 3.55 The Minister shall cancel the designation of a person or class of persons as competent to conduct a full or simplified stability assessment if the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the person or class of persons no longer meets the criteria for the designation or, in the case of a person, that the person has acted fraudulently in the performance of his or her duties.

heading: Suspension of designation
paragraph: 3.56 The Minister shall suspend the designation of a person as competent to conduct a full or simplified stability assessment if the person does not provide the Minister with updated contact information.

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: 3.57 A competent person who conducts a stability assessment for a fishing vessel shall

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (a) verify whether the vessel conforms to the stability standards that are applied to the vessel and, if those standards do not take into account some of the activities of the vessel, assess the impact of those activities on the stability of the vessel;

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (b) provide the authorized representative of the vessel, in English or French or in both, according to the needs of the crew, with a stability booklet in the case of a full stability assessment, or with a record of stability in the case of a simplified stability assessment, that sets out

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (i) the stability standards that were applied to the vessel,

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (ii) information, in the form and manner set out in the standards, respecting the stability characteristics of the vessel and, if those standards do not take into account some of the activities of the vessel, the results of the assessment of the impact of those activities on the stability of the vessel,

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (iii) the vessel's safe operating limits, and

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (iv) a signed declaration confirming, on the basis of the information provided to the competent person by the authorized representative, that the stability characteristics of the vessel conform to the standards that were applied to vessel; and

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (c) prepare a stability notice for the vessel that sets out

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (i) the stability standards that were applied to the vessel for the stability assessment,

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (ii) a graphical representation, including a description or legend, of the operational practices necessary to operate the vessel within the safe operating limits set out in the vessel's stability booklet or record of stability, and

heading: Assessment of compliance
paragraph: (iii) a statement indicating whether the vessel has been assessed for operations in freezing spray conditions.

heading: Stability booklet or record of stability
paragraph: 3.58 (1) The authorized representative of a fishing vessel

heading: Stability booklet or record of stability
paragraph: (a) shall provide the competent person who prepares the stability booklet or record of stability with information that sets out the configuration and activities of the vessel;

heading: Stability booklet or record of stability
paragraph: (b) shall provide the Minister with a copy of the stability booklet or record of stability upon request; and

heading: Stability booklet or record of stability
paragraph: (c) shall ensure that a copy of the stability booklet or record of stability is kept on board the vessel.

heading: Transfer of ownership
paragraph: (2) When ownership of a fishing vessel is transferred, the authorized representative of the vessel shall provide the new owner with a copy of the vessel's stability booklet or record of stability.

heading: Safe operating limits
paragraph: 3.59 A fishing vessel shall be operated within its safe operating limits and in accordance with the information set out in the stability booklet or record of stability.

heading: Accessibility of and familiarity with stability notice
paragraph: 3.6 (1) The stability notice for a fishing vessel shall be posted in a conspicuous location on board the vessel, and the crew shall be familiar with its content.

heading: Transfer of ownership
paragraph: (2) When ownership of a fishing vessel is transferred, the authorized representative of the vessel shall provide the new owner with a copy of the stability notice for the vessel.

heading: Written procedures
paragraph: 3.61 (1) If the stability notice for a fishing vessel does not fully describe the operational practices referred to in subparagraph 3.57(c)(ii), the authorized representative of the vessel shall establish written procedures, in plain language, and in English or French or in both, according to the needs of the crew, to ensure that the vessel is operated within the safe operating limits set out in the vessel's stability booklet or record of stability.

heading: Written procedures carried on board
paragraph: (2) The written procedures shall be carried on board the fishing vessel, and the crew shall be familiar with their content.

heading: Permanent draft marks
paragraph: 3.62 A fishing vessel that has undergone a full stability assessment shall be permanently marked, forward and aft, with draft marks or other means of accurately identifying the draft.

heading: Request to Minister - group of authorized representatives
paragraph: 3.63 (1) A group of authorized representatives of fishing vessels may request to the Minister that a population of fishing vessels not be required to undergo a stability assessment if it demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Minister that

heading: Request to Minister - group of authorized representatives
paragraph: (a) each vessel in the population is similar to a vessel representative of the population that has successfully undergone a full stability assessment; and

heading: Request to Minister - group of authorized representatives
paragraph: (b) not requiring a stability assessment for each vessel will not decrease the level of safety of the population.

heading: Factors - similar vessels
paragraph: (2) A fishing vessel in a population of fishing vessels is similar to the vessel representative of the population if

heading: Factors - similar vessels
paragraph: (a) it is operated or is to be operated in the same fishery, in the same environmental conditions and with the same fishing gear as the representative vessel;

heading: Factors - similar vessels
paragraph: (b) its physical characteristics are similar to those of the representative vessel; and

heading: Factors - similar vessels
paragraph: (c) its stability characteristics are equivalent to those set out in the stability booklet of the representative vessel.

heading: Content of request
paragraph: 3.64 The request referred to in section 3.63 shall be submitted in the form and manner established by the Minister, and shall include the following documents and information in order to demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Minister that the conditions set out in paragraphs 3.63(1)(a) and (b) are met:

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (a) data relating to any accidents and incidents that have been reported under the Transportation Safety Board Regulations in respect of each vessel in the population and in respect of any other fishing vessel similar to the representative vessel;

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (b) a copy of the stability booklet of the representative vessel;

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (c) an analysis of the likelihood that a stability-related accident or incident will occur if a stability assessment is not conducted for each vessel in the population, which analysis shall be based on

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (i) the similarity of each vessel in the population to the representative vessel,

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (ii) the nature of the risks to which the vessels in the population and persons on board are exposed,

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (iii) the accident and incident history of the vessels in the population and any other similar vessels,

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (iv) the operating parameters of each vessel in the population, and

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (v) the information contained in the stability booklet of the representative vessel; and

heading: Content of request
paragraph: (d) a description of the measures that are proposed in order to decrease the likelihood, or mitigate the consequences, of a stability-related accident or incident identified in the analysis.

heading: Minister - assessment of request
paragraph: 3.65 (1) To determine whether the fishing vessels in a population of fishing vessels are not required to undergo a stability assessment, the Minister must be satisfied, on the basis of the documents and information submitted in the request, and the extent to which the operating parameters of each vessel in the population are equivalent to those of the representative vessel, that the conditions set out in paragraphs 3.63(1)(a) and (b) are met.

heading: Decision of Minister
paragraph: (2) If the Minister determines that the conditions set out in paragraphs 3.63(1)(a) and (b) are met, the Minister shall send to the authorized representative of each fishing vessel in the population of fishing vessels a document informing the authorized representative of the decision.

heading: Conditions and exemption
paragraph: 3.66 None of the fishing vessels in a population of fishing vessels are required to undergo a stability assessment referred to in section 3.48 or to meet the related requirements set out in sections 3.49 to 3.62 if each vessel in the population

heading: Conditions and exemption
paragraph: (a) carries on board the document referred to in subsection 3.65(2);

heading: Conditions and exemption
paragraph: (b) is operated within the operating parameters referred to in subparagraph 3.64(c)(iv); and

heading: Conditions and exemption
paragraph: (c) is operated in accordance with the proposed measures referred to in paragraph 3.64(d).

heading: Operating parameters
paragraph: 3.67 (1) The authorized representative of each fishing vessel in a population of fishing vessels that is not subject to the requirement referred to in section 3.66 shall establish written procedures, in plain language, and in English or French or in both, according to the needs of the crew, for the operation of the vessel in accordance with the operating parameters referred to in subparagraph 3.64(c)(iv) and the proposed measures referred to in paragraph 3.64(d).

heading: Written procedures carried on board
paragraph: (2) The written procedures shall be carried on board the fishing vessel, and the crew shall be familiar with their content.

heading: Application
paragraph: 5 (1) This Part applies in respect of a fishing vessel of more than 15 gross tonnage.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Sections 9 and 11 to 28 apply only to a new fishing vessel.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: 9 (1) Every fishing vessel not exceeding 15.2 m in length shall be provided with one bilge power or hand pump having a capacity of not less than 1.14 L/s.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (2) Every fishing vessel exceeding 15.2 m and not exceeding 19.8 m in length shall be provided with two bilge pumps, each having a capacity of not less than 1.14 L/s, one of which shall be a power pump and the other either a power pump or a hand pump, but where two power pumps are provided, they are not to be driven by the same engine.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), every fishing vessel exceeding 19.8 m and not exceeding 24.4 m in length shall be provided with at least two bilge pumps, each having a capacity of not less than 2.28 L/s, one of which shall be a power pump and the other either a power pump or a hand pump, but where two power pumps are provided, they are not to be driven by the same engine.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (4) Two or more pumps, each with a capacity of not less than 1.14 L/s, may, if they can be used simultaneously, be provided on a fishing vessel in lieu of one only of the pumps required by subsection (3); if the pumps provided under this subsection are power pumps, they may be driven from the one engine, but not from the engine that is used to drive the mandatory power pump.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), bilge piping arrangements on a fishing vessel shall be such that each of the bilge pumps required by subsection (1), (2), (3) or (4) can draw water from each of the bilge suctions required by subsection (7) or (8).

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (6) Bilge piping and pumping arrangements that provide a piping and pumping system at least as efficient as those described in subsection (5) may be provided on a fishing vessel.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (7) Bilge suctions and means for drainage on a fishing vessel that is divided into watertight compartments shall be so arranged that any water that enters any main watertight compartment can be pumped out, through at least one bilge suction situated in that compartment, and all compartments within each main division shall be arranged to drain to that bilge suction.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (8) Bilge suctions and means for drainage on a fishing vessel that is not divided into watertight compartments shall be so arranged that any water that enters the vessel is able to drain to at least one bilge suction.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (9) Bilge piping on a fishing vessel shall have an internal diameter of not less than 38 mm except in the case of bilge piping on a fishing vessel not exceeding 15.2 m in length in which fish sludge, scale or offal is not usually pumped, in which case the bilge piping shall have an internal diameter of not less than 25 mm.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (10) Hand bilge pumps on a fishing vessel shall be capable of being worked from a position above the load water line.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (11) Each bilge branch suction line on a fishing vessel, except hand pumps with only one suction, shall be fitted with a stop valve that is readily accessible at all times.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (12) Where a bilge pump on a fishing vessel is fitted with a connection to the sea, a non-return valve or swing check valve that is readily accessible shall be fitted between the sea connection and the bilge main so that sea water cannot flow into the bilges when sea connection and bilge valves are open.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (13) Bilge suctions that lead into crew spaces or engine rooms of a fishing vessel shall be fitted with strainers and the area of the openings of such strainers shall not be less than twice the cross-sectional area of the bilge pipe.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (14) Subject to subsection (15), the piping for bilge pumps on a fishing vessel shall be of steel, bronze or other material that is suitable for the purpose, and the joints for such piping shall be flanged or screwed.

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (15) Where it is necessary to reduce the effect of vibration, short lengths of rubber or plastic hose may be installed and shall

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (a) be clearly visible at all times;

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (b) be of sufficient strength to withstand collapsing due to suction; and

heading: Bilge Pumping Arrangements
paragraph: (c) have joints made with clamps suitable for the purpose.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: 10 (1) A fuel tank on a fishing vessel that is separate from the hull shall comply with the following rules:

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (a) it shall be made of steel or other suitable material the strength of which is equivalent to that of steel;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) where a fuel tank is made of material other than steel and the vessel is a steel vessel, the fuel tank shall be efficiently isolated from the steel structure of the vessel;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c) where a fuel tank is made of steel, the steel plating shall have a minimum thickness calculated in accordance with the following table:

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c.1) where a fuel tank is made of material other than steel, the material used for plating shall be of such thickness as to provide a strength equal to or greater than the strength of the steel plating required in accordance with paragraph (c);

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c.2) subject to paragraph (c.3), where the capacity of a fuel tank is more than 114 L, the tank is made of steel and the thickness of the plating is the thickness set out in Column I of an item of the table to this paragraph, the tank shall be fitted with stiffeners so that the unsupported flat surfaces of the tank do not exceed, in square metres, the area set out in Column II of that item:

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c.3) where the thickness of the tank plating is intermediate to any set out in the table to paragraph (c.2), the unsupported flat surface area shall be calculated by interpolation and, where such thickness exceeds 6 mm, the unsupported flat surface shall be calculated in accordance with that table by extrapolation;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c.4) subject to paragraphs (c.5) and (c.6), where the capacity of a fuel tank is more than 114 L, the tank is made of material other than steel and the thickness of the tank's plating is such as to provide a strength equal to or greater than the strength of steel plating having a thickness set out in Column I of an item of the table to paragraph (c.2), the tank shall be fitted with stiffeners so that the unsupported flat surfaces of the tank do not exceed, in square metres, the area set out in Column II of that item;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c.5) where the thickness of the tank plating made of material other than steel is such as to provide a strength equal to the strength of steel plating referred to in the table to paragraph (c.2) and is intermediate to any set out in that table, the unsupported flat surface area shall be calculated by interpolation;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c.6) where the thickness of the tank plating made of material other than steel is such as to provide a strength that exceeds the strength of 6 mm of steel, the unsupported flat surface area shall be calculated in accordance with the table to paragraph (c.2) by extrapolation;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (d) where the length or breadth of a fuel tank is greater than 1.22 m, baffle plates shall be fitted inside the tank in sufficient numbers that the distance between baffle plates or between a baffle plate and a side plate is not greater than 1.22 m;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (e) a fuel tank having a capacity exceeding 1 364 L and not exceeding 4 550 L shall be fitted with a suitable clean-out door, and a fuel tank having a capacity of more than 4 550 L shall be fitted with a manhole door;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (f) where the capacity does not exceed 114 L it may be constructed of material that is less than 3 mm in thickness, but when such tank is to be used for gasoline and has a capacity exceeding 23 L and is made of material of less than 3 mm in thickness that is not corrosion resistant, it shall be galvanized inside and outside by the hot-dipped process after construction is completed;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (g) mass produced cylindrical gasoline drums having a capacity exceeding 23 L and not exceeding 227 L may be used as fuel tanks without alteration if they

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (i) have been galvanized inside and out and are constructed of steel plate having a thickness of not less than 1.5 mm, corrugated to give extra strength, and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (ii) do not weigh less than 32 kg when empty if they have a capacity of approximately 205 L;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (h) a fuel tank having a capacity exceeding 114 L shall be tested hydrostatically, on completion of its construction, to a head of at least 2.44 m above the crown or to the maximum head to which the tank will be subjected, whichever is the greater, and a written statement from the manufacturer shall be provided to the Minister certifying that the hydrostatic test described in this paragraph has been carried out and that no defects were revealed; and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (i) seams shall be welded, brazed or double riveted, but soldered joints may be used on a tank having a capacity of not over 114 L if the solder has a melting point of not less than 427°C.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (2) A fuel tank that is not separate from the hull of a fishing vessel shall be considered as part of the hull, taking into consideration the strength requirements of the vessel and the possibility of contamination of oil fuel with water, but the standards of construction and testing shall not be less than those set out in this section for a fuel tank that is separate from the hull.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (3) Where the capacity of a fuel tank exceeds 114 L, it shall be provided with the following:

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (a) a filling pipe that

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (i) is at least 38 mm inch in internal diameter,

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (ii) leads from the top of the tank to the weatherdeck, the connection through the deck being watertight,

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (iii) is fitted with a screwed brass plug or cap, and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (iv) is made sufficiently flexible to absorb any vibration or sinkage of the tank; and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) a vent or breather pipe that

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (i) leads from the top of the tank to a safe height and location above the weather deck and is clear of all openings into the hull or deck house,

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (ii) has the end covered with wire gauze and turned down through an angle of 180 degrees,

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (iii) has a weathertight deck connection,

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (iv) may have two or more vent pipes branching off from the pipe leading to the deck if that pipe is increased in diameter to maintain the required cross sectional area, and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (v) shall, for each tank, be,

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (A) where the only exit for overflow is the vent pipe, not less in internal diameter than the filling pipe, and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (B) where the overflow can take place from the filling pipe and the arrangements are such that supply nozzles cannot plug the filling pipe, not less in internal diameter than one-fifth of the internal diameter of the filling pipe.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (4) Glass tubing shall not, on a fishing vessel, be used as a gauge glass on a fuel tank that has a capacity of more than 114 L or on any fuel tank that contains fuel having a flashpoint of less than 52°‍C (Pensky-Marten closed cup), but flat glass gauges of a type approved by a product certification body or a marine classification society may be used on any fuel tank if they are fitted with self-closing cocks or valves.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (5) Where glass tubing is used as a gauge on a fuel tank on a fishing vessel, the gauge shall be fitted with a cock or valve at the top and at the bottom.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (6) Where a drain valve or cock is provided on a fuel tank on a fishing vessel, it shall have a standard screwed outlet that shall be kept plugged with a screwed plug whenever the cock or valve is not in use.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (7) The piping from any fuel tank on a fishing vessel shall be fitted at the tank with a valve or cock that is capable of being operated from outside the compartment in which the tank is situated.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (8) Where a new or existing fishing vessel is equipped with an oil-fired power boiler for main or auxiliary steam, each valve or cock fitted to a fuel tank shall be so controlled that it is capable of being shut off from a position that is

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (a) outside the compartment in which the fuel tank is situated; and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) always accessible in the event of fire taking place in the compartment in which the fuel tank is situated.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (9) The means of control of a valve or cock referred to in subsection (8) shall consist of

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) a self-closing valve actuated by a trip wire; or

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (10) Where an aluminum fuel tank is fitted on a fishing vessel, all valves, fittings and piping fitted to the fuel tank shall be of a material compatible with aluminum.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: 11 Every fuel tank on a fishing vessel shall be securely chocked, fastened in place and electrically bonded to the vessel's ground plate or to the engine.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: 12 Every fuel tank containing gasoline on a fishing vessel shall be situated remote from heated surfaces.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: 12.1 (1) Every permanent fuel tank on a fishing vessel shall be

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (a) bonded electrically to the fuel piping system and engine; and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) installed and maintained so as to prevent fuel leakage.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (3) Fuel tank filling arrangements on a fishing vessel shall be such as to prevent spillage into shipboard spaces, including bilges.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: 12.2 Every inboard gasoline-fuelled engine on a fishing vessel shall

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (a) be equipped to prevent fuel leakage into bilges or enclosed spaces;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) have a wire gauze-covered drip pan located below the carburetor;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c) where the engine is located below deck or in an enclosure where fuel vapour will not readily dissipate, have an air intake arrangement that will arrest back-fire flame; and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (d) where the engine is located in a space required by subsection 12.3(2) to be mechanically ventilated, have a starting switch arrangement that will cause the ventilation fan to operate for a suitable period prior to engine ignition.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: 12.3 (1) Every space on a fishing vessel in which machinery is located shall be ventilated so that in all weather conditions where the engines and other fuel-burning appliances are operating at full power, an adequate supply of air is maintained to ensure the safety and comfort of the crew and the operation of the engines and appliances.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (2) A mechanical ventilation system shall be installed on a fishing vessel in accordance with subsection (3) in

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (a) every space that is below deck and in which a gasoline-fuelled engine is located; and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) every other space, including bilges, in which gasoline fuel vapours may collect and may not readily dissipate.

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (3) The mechanical ventilation system referred to in subsection (2) shall meet the following requirements:

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (a) the system shall include both inlet and exhaust ducts;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (b) the exhaust duct opening shall be located in a low position in the space that permits the most efficient ventilation;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (c) the exhaust duct outlet shall lead to a location on the open deck where fumes may safely dissipate;

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (d) the fan in the exhaust duct shall be spark proof; and

heading: Fuel Systems Including Ventilating Arrangements
paragraph: (e) where the fan motor is located in an area where ignitable vapours may be generated or collect, the fan motor shall be spark proof.

heading: Exhaust Pipes
paragraph: 13 (1) Exhaust pipes from the main engines and from auxiliary engines of a fishing vessel shall be permanently mounted and shall lead to the open air outside the vessel through the uppermost deck or canopy or through the side.

heading: Exhaust Pipes
paragraph: (2) Where the exhaust pipes referred to in subsection (1) pass through the uppermost deck or canopy, they shall be of sufficient height to ensure that exhaust gases are prevented from escaping into the fishing vessel.

heading: Exhaust Pipes
paragraph: (3) Where the exhaust pipes referred to in subsection (1) pass through the side of a fishing vessel, the connection shall be watertight and provision shall be made to prevent the engine from being flooded.

heading: Exhaust Pipes
paragraph: (4) All exhaust pipes on a fishing vessel shall be well secured, shall be clear of all woodwork and other combustible materials, and, if there is a risk of contact with heated surfaces, shall be covered with lagging.

heading: Machinery Controls
paragraph: 14 (1) Means of stopping the propulsion of a fishing vessel, other than by shutting off a valve or cock fitted to the fuel tank, shall be provided outside the space where the machinery is located and such means shall be fire resistant.

heading: Machinery Controls
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a fishing vessel the construction of which was commenced before June 1, 1974.

heading: Steering Gear
paragraph: 14.1 Where a manually operated hydraulic steering system is the auxiliary system to a powered hydraulic steering system, the change-over mechanism shall be located in the wheelhouse.

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: 15 (1) Valves or cocks shall be fitted to all suctions and discharges that pass through the hull of a fishing vessel below the weatherdeck.

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (a) pump discharges of 38 mm or less in internal diameter that are situated above the load water line;

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (b) keel cooling systems; or

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (c) scuppers that pass from the weatherdeck to the ship's side above the load water line.

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (3) The cocks or valves required by subsection (1) shall be fitted as close to the side of the fishing vessel as possible.

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (4) Suction and discharge valves and cocks on a steel fishing vessel shall be attached to the plating of the hull or to the plating of fabricated water boxes by

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (a) bolts with countersunk heads tapped through the plating, or

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (b) studs that are screwed into heavy steel pads welded or riveted to the plating and that do not penetrate the plating,

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: and such valves or cocks shall be fitted with spigots passing through the plating.

heading: Underwater Fittings
paragraph: (5) Suction and discharge valves and cocks on a wooden fishing vessel shall be attached to the hull by the methods shown in Schedule VII or by any other method that conforms to the recommended practices and standards.

heading: Stern Bearings
paragraph: 16 Stern bearing assemblies of a fishing vessel shall consist of

heading: Stern Bearings
paragraph: (a) a stern bearing not less than 3 1/2 shaft diameters in length;

heading: Stern Bearings
paragraph: (b) a gland situated inside the vessel; and

heading: Stern Bearings
paragraph: (c) a watertight tube fitted between the bearing and the gland.

heading: Shafting

heading: Shafting

paragraph: (2) Where the propulsion shafting of a fishing vessel is driven by a diesel engine, the tailshaft shall

heading: Shafting

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 21 (1) Where the engine room and crew space of a fishing vessel exceeding 15.2 m but not exceeding 24.4 m in length are in adjoining compartments or are connected in any way, the bulkheads or decks between the engine room and the crew spaces shall be either

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (a) watertight, or

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (b) closely fitted to prevent fumes from the engine room entering the crew spaces,

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: and access openings in such bulkheads or decks shall be fitted with doors or covers of similar construction.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) Where, on a fishing vessel not exceeding 15.2 m in length,

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (a) the engine room and the crew spaces are in adjoining compartments or connected in any way, or

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (b) the crew spaces open to the engine room,

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: the inlet and outlet ventilation area required by section 22 shall each be increased by 2 000 mm2 for each member of the crew berthed in such compartment.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 22 (1) An engine room on a fishing vessel shall be provided with ventilators of a total cross-sectional area of not less than 16 000 mm2.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) Crew sleeping spaces on a fishing vessel shall be provided with inlet ventilators and exhaust ventilators of a sufficient size and number to ensure that the total inlet area and the total exhaust area are each not less than 2 000 mm2 for each berthed crew member.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 23 (1) Scantling of hatch coamings, beams and covers of a fishing vessel shall not be less than is set forth in Schedule II.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) Hatchways on a fishing vessel shall be provided with efficient means for battening them down and making them watertight.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (3) Flush deck scuttles on a fishing vessel shall be watertight and strongly constructed of steel, bronze or aluminum and shall have effectively secured covers that are retained on hinges or by a chain permanently attached to the ship's structure.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (4) Non-ferrous deck scuttles on a steel fishing vessel shall be isolated from the steel structure of the vessel.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 24 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a fishing vessel shall be fitted with two main transverse watertight bulkheads, one located forward of amidships at a distance not exceeding 35 per cent of the length of the vessel and the other located aft of amidships at a distance not exceeding 45 per cent of the length of the vessel, and the construction of the bulkheads shall be in accordance with Schedule III.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (1.1) The main transverse watertight bulkheads may be constructed otherwise than in accordance with Schedule III if they provide at least equivalent strength and watertightness.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (a) a fishing vessel of open construction; or

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (b) a fishing vessel operating in fresh water where the keel of the fishing vessel was laid prior to May 1, 1988.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 24.1 Every fishing vessel carrying fish in bulk that exhibit free surface effect shall be provided with both longitudinal and transverse portable fish hold divisions that meet the requirements of in Schedule VIII.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 24.2 Where a shaft tunnel access cover is fitted in a fish hold, it shall be fitted and secured in such a manner as to prevent dislodgment.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 25 Stern posts and shaft logs on a fishing vessel shall be sufficiently large to enable tailshafts of diameters required by section 19 to be fitted without unduly weakening the structure.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 26 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the sills of doors giving access to the main hull of a fishing vessel shall have a minimum height of 300 mm of which at least 230 mm shall be permanent and the remaining height of sill may be portable, if they are properly stowed in convenient positions.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) Where doors are situated on top of any superstructure, deck house or raised forecastle on a fishing vessel, the height of permanent sills shall be at least 150 mm.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 27 (1) Where side scuttles are fitted below the weatherdeck of a fishing vessel, deadlights or plugs, attached by hinges or a chain, shall be provided adjacent to the scuttle.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) Where a fishing vessel proceeds more than 20 nautical miles from land and there is no method of preventing water from entering the main hull through a broken window or port light, storm shutters and deadlights respectively shall be fitted to those openings.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (3) Plate glass having a minimum thickness of 6 mm shall be fitted in the wheelhouse windows of

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (a) all new fishing vessels; and

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (b) new vessels when replacement of those windows becomes necessary.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (4) All doors giving access to the main hull of a fishing vessel shall be strongly constructed and hung on substantial hinges and locking arrangements shall be such that a door can be opened from either side.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (4.1) Subject to subsection (4.3), a fishing vessel shall have at least two means of escape, including the main entrance, in each crew space and area in which the crew may be normally employed.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (4.2) For the purposes of subsection (4.1), one of the means of escape shall be located as far as possible from the main entrance and may be a window or a scuttle that is of sufficient proportions to provide for easy exit by the crew members and that is capable of being retained in an open position while being used as an escape route.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (4.3) The requirements of subsections (4.1) and (4.2) do not apply

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (a) in respect of a fishing vessel the keel of which was laid prior to May 1, 1988; or

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (b) in respect of a fishing vessel where a second means of escape is not practicable due to the size limitations or spatial layout of a crew space or an area in which the crew may be normally employed.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (5) Where entrance to the crew space on a fishing vessel is by way of the engine room, an escape hatch shall be fitted from the crew space to the open deck.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (6) Where exit from the crew space of a fishing vessel to the open deck is provided by one means only, it shall be of sufficient proportions to provide for easy exit for the number of men berthed and shall be as near the centre line of the ship as is practicable.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (7) Two engine room entrances providing easy access, each measuring at least 560 mm by 560 mm, shall be fitted on a fishing vessel unless this is not practicable, in which case one engine room entrance shall be fitted that is placed as near the centre line of the vessel as is practicable and that measures

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (a) in the case of a vessel exceeding 15.2 m and not exceeding 24.4 m in length, at least 610 mm by 1 220 mm; and

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (b) in the case of a vessel not exceeding 15.2 m in length, at least 610 mm by 915 mm.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 28 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), bulwark, rails, chains, wire rope or any combination of these shall be fitted around the weather deck of a fishing vessel at least 760 mm in height above the weatherdeck.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) The bulwarks, rails, chains and wire rope referred to in subsection (1) may be portable or be dispensed with in places where they would interfere with the fishing operations of the vessel.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (3) The bulwarks, rails, chains or wire rope referred to in subsection (1) may be less than 760 mm in height in way of deckhouses if suitable handrails are fitted on the sides of such deckhouses.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: 29.1 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), where bulwarks on weather parts of the working deck of a fishing vessel form wells, the minimum freeing port area, expressed in square metres, in respect of each such bulwark shall be not less than

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (a) 0.7 + 0.035 l, where l is 20 m or less, and

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (b) 0.07 l, where l exceeds 20 m,

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: where l, expressed in metres, is the lesser of the length of bulwark in the well and 70 per cent of the length of the vessel.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (2) Where the height of the bulwark in a well on the working deck is more than 1,200 mm, the minimum freeing port area shall be increased, for each 100 mm in excess of 1,200 mm, by 0.004 m2 per metre of length of well.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (3) Where the height of the bulwark in a well on the working deck is less than 900 mm, the minimum freeing port area may be decreased, for each 100 mm less than 900 mm, by 0.004 m2 per metre of length of well.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (4) Where the vessel's sheer is such that the minimum freeing port areas, calculated in accordance with subsections (1) to (3), do not provide rapid and effective freeing of water from the deck, those areas shall be increased by such amount as will provide rapid and effective freeing of water from the deck.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (5) The freeing ports of every fishing vessel shall be arranged along the length of bulwarks so as to provide rapid and effective freeing of water from the deck of the vessel, and the lower edges of the freeing ports shall be as close to the deck as possible.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (6) On every fishing vessel, poundboards shall be stowed, and means of stowage of fishing gear shall be arranged, in such a manner that the effectiveness of the freeing ports of the vessel is not impaired.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (7) Every poundboard on a fishing vessel shall be so constructed that it can be secured in position when in use and will not hamper the rapid and effective freeing of water from the deck of the vessel.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (8) Every freeing port over 300 mm in depth of a fishing vessel, shall be fitted with bars spaced not more than 230 mm apart, or with other suitable protective devices.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (9) Where the protective devices fitted in accordance with subsection (8) are covers, they shall be of a construction approved by the Minister.

heading: Construction of Hulls
paragraph: (10) In a fishing vessel intended to operate in areas subject to icing, protective devices fitted in accordance with subsection (8) shall be capable of being easily removed to restrict or reduce ice accretion.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: 38 (1) Every fishing vessel exceeding 12.2 m in length shall be equipped with at least one hand or engine driven pump and apparatus whereby a suitable jet of water can be directed into any part of the ship.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (2) The internal diameter of the pipes for the pump mentioned in subsection (1) shall be not less than 19 mm.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), bilge pumps on a fishing vessel may be used as fire pumps by using them to pump sea water on deck.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (4) Where two bilge pumps are required on a fishing vessel, neither pump shall be used to pump sea water on deck unless it is possible for one bilge pump to pump bilge water overboard while the other pumps sea water on deck.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), the piping for a fire pump on a fishing vessel shall be of steel, bronze or other material that is suitable for the purpose, and the joints for such piping shall be flanged or screwed.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (6) Where it is necessary to reduce the effect of vibration, short lengths of rubber or plastic hose may be installed and shall

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (a) be clearly visible at all times;

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (b) be of sufficient strength to withstand collapsing due to suction; and

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (c) have joints made with clamps suitable for the purpose.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: 39 (1) Appliances that are installed on a fishing vessel and that burn liquid or gaseous fuel shall be so fitted that there is a free circulation of air all around and below the appliance.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (2) Wooden bulkheads behind cooking or heating appliances on a fishing vessel shall be insulated if space constraints do not allow the free circulation of air all around and below the appliance.

heading: Fire Extinguishing Equipment
paragraph: (3) Every fishing vessel of not more than 24.4 m in length that is provided with a liquefied petroleum gas installation shall comply with the requirements of the Marine Machinery Regulations for such vessels.

heading: Emergency Electrical Lighting
paragraph: 43.1 (1) Every fishing vessel, other than one certified to operate only between sunrise and sunset, shall be fitted with permanent or portable lights capable of illuminating the launching stations and stowage positions of all life rafts, emergency boats, recovery boats or rescue boats for at least one hour.

heading: Emergency Electrical Lighting
paragraph: (2) Where non-rechargeable battery-operated hand lanterns are provided pursuant to subsection (1), the batteries shall be changed annually.

heading: Electrical Equipment, Installations and Appliances
paragraph: 44.1 (1) Subject to subsection (1.3), where the construction of a fishing vessel begins after April 27, 1996, the electrical equipment, installations and appliances on the fishing vessel shall be constructed in accordance with TP 127 as it reads on the day the construction begins.

heading: Electrical Equipment, Installations and Appliances
paragraph: (1.2) Subject to subsection (1.3), any substantial reconstruction or modification of the electrical equipment, installations or appliances on a fishing vessel shall, insofar as it is practicable, bring the electrical equipment, installations or appliances into compliance with TP 127 as it reads on the day the reconstruction or modification begins.

heading: Electrical Equipment, Installations and Appliances
paragraph: (1.3) Where TP 127 does not set out a standard in respect of a particular piece of electrical equipment or a particular electrical installation or appliance, the electrical equipment, installation or appliance shall be safe and effectively fulfil the purpose for which it is intended.

heading: Application
paragraph: 52 This Part applies in respect of a fishing vessel of not more than 15 gross tonnage.

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: 56 (1) Every permanent fuel tank on a fishing vessel shall be

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (a) bonded electrically to the fuel piping system and engine; and

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (b) installed and maintained so as to prevent fuel leakage.

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (6) Every inboard gasoline-fuelled engine on a fishing vessel shall

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (a) be equipped to prevent fuel leakage into bilges or enclosed spaces;

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (b) have a wire gauze-covered drip pan located below the carburetor;

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (c) where the engine is located below deck or in an enclosure where fuel vapour will not readily dissipate, have an air intake arrangement that will arrest back-fire flame; and

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (d) where the engine is located in a space required by subsection (8) to be mechanically ventilated, have a starting switch arrangement that will cause the ventilation fan to operate for a suitable period prior to engine ignition.

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (7) Every space on a fishing vessel in which machinery is located shall be ventilated so that in all weather conditions where the engines and other fuel-burning appliances are operating at full power, an adequate supply of air is maintained to ensure the safety and comfort of the crew and the operation of the engines and appliances.

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (8) A mechanical ventilation system shall be installed in a fishing vessel in accordance with subsection (9) in

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (a) every space that is below deck and in which a gasoline-fuelled engine is located; and

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (b) every other space, including bilges, in which gasoline fuel vapours may collect and may not readily dissipate.

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (9) The mechanical ventilation system referred to in subsection (8) shall meet the following requirements:

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (a) the system shall include both inlet and exhaust ducts;

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (b) the exhaust duct opening shall be located in a low position in the space that permits the most efficient ventilation;

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (c) the exhaust duct outlet shall lead to a location on the open deck where fumes may safely dissipate;

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (d) the fan in the exhaust duct shall be spark proof; and

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (e) where the fan motor is located in an area where ignitable vapours may be generated or collect, the fan motor shall be spark proof.

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (10) An appliance that burns liquid or gas fuel shall be so installed that air circulates freely all around the appliance.

heading: Precautions Against Fire
paragraph: (11) Insulation to prevent combustion shall be placed between woodwork or other inflammable material and adjacent surfaces of engine exhaust piping, heating appliances or other components that may become heated.

heading: SCHEDULE VIII(s. 24.1)Portable Fish Hold Divisions
paragraph: 1 Every portable fish hold division shall be fishtight and shall extend from the bottom of the hold to the deckhead, with due regard to the loading and unloading of the vessel.

heading: SCHEDULE VIII(s. 24.1)Portable Fish Hold Divisions
paragraph: 2 Provision shall be made to allow water to drain into the bilge, and bilge suctions shall be adequately protected to prevent clogging.

heading: SCHEDULE VIII(s. 24.1)Portable Fish Hold Divisions
paragraph: 3 Portable penboards shall be installed in such a manner as to prevent dislodgment when fish are being pumped into and out of the hold.

heading: SCHEDULE VIII(s. 24.1)Portable Fish Hold Divisions
paragraph: 4 Where wooden stanchions are installed, the penboards shall be secured in such a manner as to withstand the loads imposed.

heading: SCHEDULE VIII(s. 24.1)Portable Fish Hold Divisions
