heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (a) to refuse or decline to approve an application for the specified authorization;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (b) to refuse to enter into, grant or give the specified authorization;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: "replacement agreement" means an agreement, entered into under section 15 (6), 36 (6), 43.4 (9), 43.56 (5) or 46 (7), that is a replacement for another agreement;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: "specified authorization" means

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (a) an agreement listed in section 12, other than the following agreements:

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (i)  a replacement agreement;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (ii)  a cutting permit,

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (b) a fibre recovery permit referred to in section 47.72 (1) (c),

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (c) a road use permit, other than a road use permit that the minister is required to issue under section 120.1 (2),

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (d) a log salvage permit referred to in section 124,

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (e) an exemption, under section 128, from section 127, and

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (f) a special use permit.

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (2) An application under this Act for a specified authorization may be refused, and a person who has discretion under this Act or the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act to refuse to issue a specified authorization may do so, on one or more of the following grounds:

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (a) the applicant, or a related person of the applicant, has failed to pay by the due date money that is required to be paid to the government in a circumstance set out in section 130 (1.1) of this Act, regardless of whether, at the time the specified authorization is sought,

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (i)  the money has been paid, or

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (ii)  payment arrangements satisfactory to the revenue minister have been made;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (b) the applicant is not in compliance with, or has failed in the past to comply with, a requirement under this Act or the Forest and Range Practices Act to provide security or a deposit;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (c) the applicant holds another specified authorization or a replacement agreement and

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (i)  rights under the other specified authorization or replacement agreement, or a cutting permit issued for it, are under suspension, or

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (ii)  the applicant is not in compliance with, or has failed in the past to comply with,

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (A) a requirement under the other specified authorization or replacement agreement, or a cutting permit issued for it, or

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (B) a requirement under the Acts in respect of activities carried out under the other specified authorization or replacement agreement.

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (3) The minister may refuse to issue a cutting permit for an agreement on one or more of the following grounds:

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (a) the applicant, or a related person of the applicant, has not yet paid money required to be paid to the government in a circumstance set out in section 130 (1.1) of this Act and the due date for paying the money has passed, regardless of whether payment arrangements satisfactory to the revenue minister have been made;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (b) the applicant is not in compliance with a requirement under this Act or the Forest and Range Practices Act to provide security or a deposit;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (c) rights under a cutting permit previously issued for the agreement are under suspension;

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (d) the applicant is not in compliance with

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (i)  a requirement under the agreement or a cutting permit previously issued for the agreement,

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (ii)  a requirement under a road permit or road use permit associated with the agreement, or

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (iii)  a requirement under the Acts in respect of activities carried out under a permit referred to in subparagraph (i) or (ii).

heading: Grounds for refusing to issue authorization
paragraph: (4) Nothing in this section limits a person's discretion under this Act, on grounds other than those set out in this section, to refuse to issue a specified authorization or a cutting permit.

heading: Timber marking: interpretation
paragraph:
82
		  In this Part:

heading: Timber marking: interpretation
paragraph: "registrar" means the registrar designated by the minister to administer timber marks and marine log brands;

heading: Timber marking: interpretation
paragraph: "unscaled timber" includes timber for which the amount of stumpage has been calculated under section 106.

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph:
83
		  (1) A timber mark held under an agreement listed in section 12

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (a) is suspended if, under this Act, the agreement is suspended, or

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (b) is cancelled, if under this Act, the agreement expires or is surrendered or cancelled.

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (2) A timber mark held under a certificate issued under section 85, other than a certificate issued in respect of private land that is subject to an area-based licence, expires on the fifth anniversary of the issue date of the certificate or, by consent of the applicant, on an earlier date specified in the certificate.

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (3) A timber mark held under a renewal certificate issued under section 85, other than a certificate issued in respect of private land that is subject to an area-based licence, expires on the fifth anniversary of the renewal date of the certificate or, by consent of the applicant, on an earlier date specified in the certificate.

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (4) A timber mark held under a certificate or renewal certificate issued under section 85 that is in respect of private land subject to an area-based licence does not expire but

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (a) is suspended if, under this Act, the licence or agreement is suspended,

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (b) is cancelled if, under this Act, the licence or agreement expires or is surrendered or cancelled, or

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (c) subject to subsection (5) of this section, is cancelled if the private land is otherwise no longer subject to the licence or agreement.

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (5) If

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (a) a certificate or renewal certificate issued under section 85 is in respect of private land subject to an area-based licence, and

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: (b) subsequently that private land is no longer subject to the licence or agreement but the owner of the land remains the same,

heading: Timber mark duration
paragraph: the timber mark held under the certificate expires on the fifth anniversary of the date the private land is no longer subject to the licence or agreement.

heading: Timber marks
paragraph:
84
		  (1) Each of

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (a) the holder of a timber mark, and

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (b) a person acting with the consent of the holder of a timber mark

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: must ensure that unscaled timber that is

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (c) stored in decks or piles on Crown land or private land, or

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (d) removed or transported from Crown land or private land

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: has been marked in the prescribed manner with the timber mark that pertains to that land.

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (3) A person must not

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (a) store unscaled timber in decks or piles on Crown land or, in prescribed circumstances, on private land, or

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (b) remove or transport unscaled timber from Crown land or private land

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: unless the timber has been marked in the prescribed manner with a timber mark that pertains to that land.

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (4) Before timber marked under this section is used in manufacturing, a person must not remove, obliterate or alter a timber mark that has been applied to timber.

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (5) The minister may exempt unscaled timber from subsection (1) or (3) and may attach conditions to the exemption.

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (6) Each of the following must ensure compliance with the conditions attached to an exemption under subsection (5):

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (a) the holder of a timber mark;

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (b) a person acting with the consent of the holder of a timber mark;

heading: Timber marks
paragraph: (c) a person storing unscaled timber on Crown land or private land or removing or transporting unscaled timber from Crown land or private land.

heading: Applications
paragraph:
85
		  (1) On application that identifies private land on which there is timber, in a form required by the minister, and on payment of the fee, if any, required by the minister, the registrar must

heading: Applications
paragraph: (a) issue a certificate, or a renewal certificate, that describes a timber mark and identifies the private land

heading: Applications
paragraph: (i)  to the person, if any, who is identified as the owner of the timber under a charge registered in the land title office against the private land, or

heading: Applications
paragraph: (ii)  if no charge as described in subparagraph (i) is registered in the land title office against the private land, to the person who, according to the records of the land title office, is the beneficial owner of the private land as

heading: Applications
paragraph: (A) the registered owner in fee simple, or

heading: Applications
paragraph: (B) the holder of an agreement to purchase the private land,

heading: Applications
paragraph: (b) issue to an agent of the government or to a private utility company a certificate or renewal certificate that describes a timber mark and identifies the private land and the agent or company to which the certificate pertains, if the registrar is satisfied that the agent or utility has the authority to harvest the timber, and

heading: Applications
paragraph: (c) issue to the holder of a woodlot licence a certificate that describes a timber mark and identifies the private land that is subject to the woodlot licence to which the certificate pertains, if the registrar is satisfied that the woodlot licence holder has the authority to harvest the timber.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (2) The registrar may include terms and conditions in the certificate and the holder of the certificate must comply with those terms and conditions.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (3) On application by the holder of a certificate issued under subsection (1) (a), the registrar may approve the use of a timber mark described in the certificate, for timber owned by the applicant and cut on private land other than the private land originally described in the certificate.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (3.1) On application by the holder of a certificate issued under subsection (1) (b), the registrar may approve the use of a timber mark described in the certificate, for timber cut on private land other than the private land originally described in the certificate, if the registrar is satisfied that the agent or utility has the authority to harvest the timber from that other private land.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (3.2) As a condition precedent to issuing a timber mark under subsection (1) or granting an approval under subsection (3) or (3.1), the registrar may require evidence to his or her satisfaction that the applicant for the timber mark or approval is the owner of the timber according to the records of the land title office.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (4) If the registrar exercises his or her powers under subsection (3) or (3.1), the registrar must amend accordingly the certificate issued under subsection (1) and the timber mark register.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (5) After giving the holder of a timber mark an opportunity to be heard, the registrar may cancel a certificate or renewal certificate issued under this section and the timber mark described in it

heading: Applications
paragraph: (a) if the holder of the timber mark contravenes a provision of Part 5 or 6, or

heading: Applications
paragraph: (b) for other sufficient cause.

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph:
86
		  (1) Each of

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (a) the holder of a scaled timber brand, and

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (b) a person acting with the consent of the holder of a scaled timber brand

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: must ensure that timber removed or transported from the scale site to which the scaled timber brand pertains has been marked in the prescribed manner with that scaled timber brand.

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (2) A person must not

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (a) remove or transport scaled timber from a scale site unless the timber has been marked in the prescribed manner with a scaled timber brand, or

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (b) apply a scaled timber brand to timber except at

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (i)  the scale site to which the scaled timber brand applies, or

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (ii)  another location approved by the minister.

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (3) The minister may exempt scaled timber from subsection (1) or (2) and may attach conditions to the exemption.

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (3.1) Each of the following must ensure compliance with the conditions attached to an exemption under subsection (3):

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (a) the holder of a scaled timber brand;

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (b) a person acting with the consent of the holder of a scaled timber brand;

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (c) a person removing or transporting scaled timber from a scale site.

heading: Scaled timber brands
paragraph: (4) Before use of the timber in manufacturing, a person must not remove, obliterate or alter a scaled timber brand that has been applied to timber.

heading: Applications
paragraph:
87
		  (1) On application by the scale site operator in a form required by the minister, the minister must issue to the applicant a certificate that describes a scaled timber brand and identifies the scale site to which it pertains, and may attach conditions to the certificate.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (2) After giving the holder of a scaled timber brand an opportunity to be heard, the minister may suspend a certificate issued under subsection (1) and the scaled timber brand described in it

heading: Applications
paragraph: (a) if the scale site operator contravenes a provision of Part 5 or 6, or

heading: Applications
paragraph: (b) for other sufficient cause.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (3) On application of the holder of the scaled timber brand, the minister must give the holder an opportunity to be heard and must rescind the suspension if

heading: Applications
paragraph: (a) the holder is no longer in contravention of the provision that gave rise to the suspension, or

heading: Applications
paragraph: (b) the suspension was for sufficient cause under subsection (2) (b), and the holder has remedied the circumstances that gave rise to the suspension.

heading: Applications
paragraph: (4) If a certificate and the scaled timber brand described in it are under suspension, the minister may cancel them.

heading: Marine log brand
paragraph:
88
		  (1) On receiving an application the registrar may approve a marine log brand that, in his or her opinion, does not so closely resemble any other marine log brand as to be misleading.

heading: Marine log brand
paragraph: (2) An application must be in the form required by the minister, include a prescribed fee and contain a facsimile of the marine log brand applied for.

heading: Marine log brand
paragraph: (3) If the registrar approves a marine log brand the registrar must issue to the applicant a certificate containing a facsimile of the marine log brand.

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph:
89
		  (1) A person must not apply a marine log brand to timber unless

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph: (a) the person has obtained

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph: (i)  a certificate under section 88 (3) for the marine log brand, or

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph: (ii)  the consent of a person who has obtained a certificate under section 88 (3) for the marine log brand, and

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph: (b) the timber has been

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph: (i)  marked with a timber mark in accordance with this Part, and

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph: (ii)  scaled in accordance with Part 6.

heading: Marking with marine log brand
paragraph: (2) A person who applies a marine log brand under subsection (1) must mark the timber in the prescribed manner.

heading: Transfer
paragraph:
90
		  (1) A person must not use a timber mark, scaled timber brand or marine log brand without the consent of the holder.

heading: Transfer
paragraph: (2) The holder of a marine log brand must not transfer the right to use it to another person without the written consent of the minister and without giving prior notice to the registrar.

heading: Transfer
paragraph: (3) Each of

heading: Transfer
paragraph: (a) a timber mark held under a certificate or renewal certificate issued under section 85 and the certificate, and

heading: Transfer
paragraph: (b) a scaled timber brand held under a certificate issued under section 87 and the certificate,

heading: Transfer
paragraph: is not transferable.

heading: Transfer
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not apply to a timber mark or certificate that pertains to an agreement that is disposed of in accordance with section 54.

heading: Evidence
paragraph:
91
		  A certificate, purporting to be signed by the registrar or the chief forester, to the effect that a timber mark certificate has been issued to, or a marine log brand has been approved for use by, a person, must be received in court as proof of the facts stated in it.

heading: Registers
paragraph:
92
		  The registrar must keep

heading: Registers
paragraph: (a) a timber mark register in which must be noted the characters of each timber mark, the name of its holder and the land the mark pertains to, and

heading: Registers
paragraph: (b) a marine log brand register in which must be noted the characters of each marine log brand approved and the name of its holder.

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph:
93
		  In this Part:

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph: "acting scaler" means a person appointed under section 100 (3) (a);

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph: "forest service scaler" means a forest officer appointed under section 100 (3) (b);

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph: "licensed scaler" means a person who holds a scaling licence issued under section 100 (2);

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph: "official scaler" means a licensed scaler appointed under section 100 (3) (c);

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph: "scale" means to do one or more of the following:

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph: (a) determine the volume or quantity of timber;

heading: Timber scaling: interpretation
paragraph: (b) classify the quality of timber.

heading: Misrepresentation prohibited
paragraph:
93.1
		  A person must not represent that the person is authorized to perform a scale under this Part if not so authorized.

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph:
94
		  (1) Subject to section 94.1, a person must not manufacture products from, sell or transport to a place, other than the place where it is required to be sent for scaling,

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (a) timber that is cut from private land unless it is scaled by a licensed scaler authorized by the minister to scale the timber, and

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (b) timber that

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (i)  is cut from Crown land and that under the terms of the authority to cut is required to be scaled, or

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (ii)  is salvaged from water or foreshore,

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: unless it is scaled by an official scaler authorized by the minister to scale the timber or scaled by a forest service scaler.

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (2) If the minister considers it necessary to avoid unreasonable delays or costs, he or she may order that

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (a) timber that is required to be scaled by an official scaler or a forest service scaler may be scaled by a licensed scaler who is not an official scaler or a forest service scaler or by an acting scaler, and

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (b) timber that is required to be scaled by a licensed scaler may be scaled by an acting scaler.

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (4) Each of

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (a) the owner of a scale site,

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (b) the operator of a scale site, and

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (c) the person whose timber is scaled under this Part

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: must ensure that the parcel or lot of timber that has been most recently scaled by each of the scalers employed at the site is retained at the site and made accessible for check scale by a licensed scaler who is a forest officer.

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (5) The minister may exempt timber or a person from subsection (1) or  (4).

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (6) The minister may attach conditions to an exemption under subsection (5) and may attach, remove or alter a condition at any time.

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (7) A person who

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (a) is subject to an exemption under subsection (5), or

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: (b) whose timber is subject to an exemption under subsection (5)

heading: Timber to be scaled
paragraph: must comply with a condition attached to the exemption.

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph:
94.1
		  (1) In this section, "waste assessment" means an assessment, for determining the volumes of merchantable timber and waste left on a harvested area, conducted in accordance with the procedures set out in the publication of the Ministry of Forests and Range, Provincial Logging Residue and Waste Measurement Procedures Manual, as amended from time to time.

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (2) If timber is to be manufactured into a special forest product at the place where the timber is felled, the special forest product may be scaled instead of the timber.

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (3) A person may, for timber that is cut from Crown land and that under the terms of the authority to cut is required to be scaled,

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (a) transport the timber to a place other than the place where it is required to be sent for scaling if the timber is to be manufactured into a special forest product at that place, or

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (b) at a place other than the place where the timber is felled, manufacture timber into a special forest product before it is scaled,

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: if all of the following apply:

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (c) the person is authorized to do so by the minister;

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (d) a waste assessment for the timber has been approved by the minister;

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (e) the person scales the special forest product at a scale site designated by the minister, which may include the site at which the timber is manufactured into the special forest product.

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (4) The minister may attach conditions to an authorization granted under subsection (3), and may attach, remove or alter a condition at any time.

heading: Scaling of special forest products
paragraph: (5) A person who is subject to a condition imposed under subsection (4) must comply with the condition.

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph:
95
		  (1) Each of

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (a) the owner of a scale site, and

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (b) the operator of a scale site

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: must ensure that no timber is scaled at the site unless a scale site authorization has been issued under subsection (2) for the site.

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (2) On application the minister must issue to the applicant a scale site authorization on being satisfied that a complete and accurate scale can be performed at the site.

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2) an applicant may be refused if

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (a) the applicant previously held a scale site authorization which was cancelled,

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (a.1) the applicant, or a related person of the applicant, has failed to pay by the due date money that is required to be paid to the government in a circumstance set out in section 130 (1.1), regardless of whether, at the time the application is made,

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (i)  the money has been paid, or

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (ii)  payment arrangements satisfactory to the revenue minister have been made, or

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (b) the minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the applicant will fail to comply with

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (ii)  a regulation made under section 151 (2) (c), (d), (h), (i) or (n), or

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (iii)  the conditions attached to a scale site authorization.

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (4) The minister may attach conditions to the scale site authorization to ensure a complete and accurate scale and may attach, remove or alter a condition at any time.

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (5) A condition under subsection (4) may be applied to a specific scale site authorization, a class of scale site authorizations or all scale site authorizations.

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (6) The minister, after giving the holder of a scale site authorization an opportunity to be heard, may suspend or cancel a scale site authorization upon being satisfied that there has been failure to comply with

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (b) a regulation made under section 151 (2) (c), (d), (h), (i) or (n), or

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (c) a condition attached to a scale site authorization.

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (7) Each of

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (a) a person to whom a scale site authorization has been issued,

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (b) the owner of the scale site, and

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: (c) the operator of the scale site

heading: Scale site authorization
paragraph: must ensure that the conditions attached to the scale site authorization are complied with.

heading: Scale
paragraph:
96
		  (1) A person who scales or purports to scale timber under this Act

heading: Scale
paragraph: (a) must carry out the scale according to the prescribed procedures, and

heading: Scale
paragraph: (b) must express the scale in cubic metres or another unit of metric measure required by the minister for special forest products.

heading: Scale
paragraph: (2) A scale that is expressed in cubic metres is to be known as British Columbia metric scale.

heading: Scale
paragraph: (3) A person whose timber is scaled under this Part must ensure that a complete and accurate scale of the timber is performed.

heading: Scale return
paragraph:
97
		  (1) Each of

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (a) the owner of a scale site,

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (b) the operator of a scale site,

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (c) the person whose timber is scaled under this Part, and

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (d) the person who performs the scale

heading: Scale return
paragraph: must ensure that

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (e) the scale details are recorded in a form approved by the minister and retained in that form at the scale site, and

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (f) a scale return in the form approved by the minister is completed and delivered within the prescribed time to the person whose timber is scaled and to a person designated by the minister.

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (2) If the scale return referred to in subsection (1) (f) is not completed and delivered to a person designated under subsection (1), within the time prescribed for the purpose of that subsection, the person must pay to the government a penalty in the amount prescribed for the purpose of this section.

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of section 131 the penalty imposed by subsection (2) is money payable to the government in respect of the timber.

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (4) Subject to section 99 (5), if, according to a check scale referred to in section 94 (4), the volume or value of the parcel or lot of scaled timber computed from the check scale details varies by more than a prescribed percentage from the volume or value computed from the original scale details, then the check scale governs for all purposes of this Act and the regulations.

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (5) The minister may order that subsection (4) does not apply in respect of a check scale if satisfied that the original scale was performed in accordance with good scaling practices and the differences between it and the check scale are attributable to the condition of the timber.

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (6) When and as directed by the minister, each of

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (a) the owner of a scale site,

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (b) the operator of a scale site,

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (c) the person whose timber is scaled under this Part, and

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (d) the person who performs the scale

heading: Scale return
paragraph: must ensure that the check scale details are incorporated in the scale return submitted under subsection (1) (e).

heading: Scale return
paragraph: (7) If the minister estimates that the annual volume of timber scaled at a scale site will exceed the prescribed volume, he or she may order the owner or operator of the scale site to enter into an arrangement to deliver, by electronic means to the ministry, the scale returns required under this section.

heading: Scaling charges, costs and expenses
paragraph:
98
		  (1) A person whose timber is scaled by an employee of the government must pay to the government the charges, costs and expenses incurred by the government in respect of

heading: Scaling charges, costs and expenses
paragraph: (a) making and recording the scale measurements,

heading: Scaling charges, costs and expenses
paragraph: (b) preparing and submitting the scale return, and

heading: Scaling charges, costs and expenses
paragraph: (c) the scale computation, summarization and billing.

heading: Scaling charges, costs and expenses
paragraph: (2) A person whose timber is scaled by a person who is not an employee of the government must pay to the government the charges, costs and expenses incurred by the government in respect of preparing, compiling and submitting the scale return.

heading: Scaling charges, costs and expenses
paragraph: (3) A person is not required to pay charges, costs and expenses under subsection (2) that total less than a prescribed amount.

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph:
99
		  (1) If it is feasible to perform a subsequent scale of timber that has been scaled under section 94, the minister

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (a) may have the timber scaled again and a second scale return prepared, or

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (b) must have the timber scaled again and a second scale return prepared if a person whose interest is affected by the scale objects to the scale return completed for the scale, in a notice served on the minister.

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (2) If the volume or value of the timber computed from the second scale return

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (a) varies by more than a prescribed percentage from the volume or value computed from the original scale return,

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (i)  the second scale return governs for all purposes of this Act and the regulations,

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (ii)  no scaling fees, charges, costs and expenses are payable to the government in respect of the original scale, and

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (iii)  the person who was liable to pay for the original scale must pay to the government the scaling fees and the charges, costs and expenses incurred by the government in respect of the second scale, or

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (b) does not vary by more than a prescribed percentage from the volume or value computed from the original scale return,

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (i)  the original scale return governs for all purposes of this Act and the regulations, and

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (ii)  the person who objected to the original scale return must pay to the government the charges, costs and expenses incurred by the government in respect of the second scale.

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (3) A scaler whose scale has been replaced by a check scale under section 97 (4) may request a second check scale, by notice served on a person designated by the minister.

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (4) The minister must have a second check scale performed, if feasible.

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (5) If the volume or value of the timber computed from the second check scale details

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (a) varies from the volume or value of the timber computed from the original scale details by more than a prescribed percentage,

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (i)  the second check scale governs for all purposes of this Act and the regulations, and

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (ii)  the scaler who requested the second check scale must pay to the government the charges, costs and expenses incurred by the government in respect of the second check scale, or

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (b) does not vary from the volume or value of the timber computed from the original scale details by more than a prescribed percentage,

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (i)  the original scale governs for all purposes of this Act and the regulations, and

heading: Second scale and second check scale
paragraph: (ii)  no charges, costs and expenses are payable to the government.

heading: Scaling
paragraph:
100
		  (1) A person who applies for a scaling licence must be examined by one or more scaling examiners appointed by the minister.

heading: Scaling
paragraph: (2) If an applicant passes the examinations approved by the minister, the minister may issue a scaling licence to the applicant.

heading: Scaling
paragraph: (3) The minister may appoint

heading: Scaling
paragraph: (a) any person as an acting scaler,

heading: Scaling
paragraph: (b) a licensed scaler who is a forest officer as a forest service scaler, and

heading: Scaling
paragraph: (c) a licensed scaler other than a forest officer as an official scaler for a term specified in the appointment.

heading: Re-examination
paragraph:
101
		  (1) The minister, in a notice served on a licensed scaler, may require the licensed scaler to be examined under section 100.

heading: Re-examination
paragraph: (2) Unless the licensed scaler passes the examination within the time specified by the minister in the notice, the licensed scaler's scaling licence terminates at the end of the specified time.

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph:
102
		  (1) If a licensed scaler fails to properly perform the licensed scaler's duties or comply with this Part or the regulations respecting scaling,

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (a) the minister, in a notice served on the licensed scaler, may suspend the latter's scaling licence for a period of time, and

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (b) the minister, whether or not the licence is under suspension, in a notice served on the licensed scaler, may cancel the latter's scaling licence.

heading: Suspension and cancellation
paragraph: (2) Before the minister cancels a scaling licence, the minister must give the licensed scaler an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Definitions for Part 6.1
paragraph:
102.1
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions for Part 6.1
paragraph: "forest resource" means a resource or feature set out in section 102.2 (1);

heading: Definitions for Part 6.1
paragraph: "information" includes a record;

heading: Definitions for Part 6.1
paragraph: "recreation resource" has the same meaning as in the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Definitions for Part 6.1
paragraph: "visual resource" means a resource or feature in relation to which a visual quality objective is established under the Forest and Range Practices Act.

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: 102.2		  (1) The holder of an area-based licence must, in accordance with this Part, prepare and maintain a complete and accurate inventory of each of the following resources and features in the licence area:

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (a) timber;

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (b) soil and terrain;

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (c) water resources, including streams, wetlands, lakes and riparian areas;

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (d) fish and wildlife;

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (e) ecosystems;

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (f) recreation resources;

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (g) visual resources.

heading: Requirement to prepare and maintain forest resource inventories
paragraph: (2) The chief forester may specify the form in which the holder of an area-based licence must prepare and maintain an inventory of a forest resource.

heading: Time periods within which forest resource inventories must be prepared
paragraph:
102.3
		  (1) In this section, "pre-existing licence" means a licence that is in effect on January 1, 2022.

heading: Time periods within which forest resource inventories must be prepared
paragraph: (2) The holder of an area-based licence that is entered into after January 1, 2022 must prepare an inventory of each forest resource by no later than 2 years after the date the area-based licence is entered into.

heading: Time periods within which forest resource inventories must be prepared
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if the area-based licence is a replacement for another licence.

heading: Time periods within which forest resource inventories must be prepared
paragraph: (4) The holder of a tree farm licence that is a pre-existing licence must prepare an inventory of each forest resource by no later than January 1, 2024.

heading: Time periods within which forest resource inventories must be prepared
paragraph: (5) The holder of a community forest agreement, first nations woodland licence or woodlot licence that is a pre-existing licence must prepare an inventory of each forest resource by no later than January 1, 2026.

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph:
102.4
		  (1) An inventory of a forest resource must include sufficient information about the forest resource such that a professional forester who is relying on the inventory could do all the following, to the standard expected of a professional forester:

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (a) assess the impacts that the following would have on the forest resource:

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (i)  timber harvesting;

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (ii)  road construction, road maintenance, road use and road deactivation;

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (iii)  wildfire, disease and insect infestation;

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (b) assess the impact that management of the forest resource would have on the timber supply in the licence area;

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (c) prepare the following in relation to the licence area:

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (i)  an operational plan that meets the requirements under the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (ii)  a management plan that meets the requirements under this Act or the licence;

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (d) advise the holder of the area-based licence about the actions that are necessary to adequately manage and conserve the forest resource.

heading: Content of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (2) The chief forester may specify information that must be included in an inventory of a forest resource.

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: 102.5		  (1) After the holder of an area-based licence has prepared an inventory of a forest resource, the holder must maintain the inventory in accordance with the following requirements:

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (a) within each of the applicable time periods described in subsection (2), the holder must review the information in the inventory to determine whether the information is complete and accurate;

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (b) if information in the inventory is determined to be no longer complete and accurate, the holder must update the inventory by adding complete and accurate information about the forest resource.

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (2) The review of an inventory of a forest resource must be carried out

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (a) at least once in the 10-year period following the date the inventory is first prepared,

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (b) at least once in each successive 10-year period following, as applicable,

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (i)  the date a determination is made that the information included in the inventory is complete and accurate, or

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (ii)  the date the inventory is updated by adding complete and accurate information about the forest resource, and

heading: Maintenance of forest resource inventory
paragraph: (c) at other times that may be specified by regulation.

heading: Requirement to keep records respecting forest resource inventory
paragraph:
102.6
		  (1) Information that the holder of an area-based licence includes in the holder's inventory of a forest resource must be kept

heading: Requirement to keep records respecting forest resource inventory
paragraph: (a) for a period of 10 years following the date the inventory of the forest resource is first prepared, or

heading: Requirement to keep records respecting forest resource inventory
paragraph: (b) if the information is added to the inventory of the forest resource after the inventory is first prepared, for a period of 10 years following the date the information is added.

heading: Requirement to keep records respecting forest resource inventory
paragraph: (2) The holder of an area-based licence must keep a record of the following dates that relate to the holder's inventory of a forest resource:

heading: Requirement to keep records respecting forest resource inventory
paragraph: (a) each date a determination under section 102.5 (1) (a) is made as to whether information included in the inventory is complete and accurate;

heading: Requirement to keep records respecting forest resource inventory
paragraph: (b) each date the inventory is updated under section 102.5 (1) (b) by adding complete and accurate information about the forest resource.

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph:
102.7
		  (1) The holder of an area-based licence must, within or at each of the applicable times described in subsection (2), submit the following to the chief forester:

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (a) the information included in the holder's inventory of a forest resource;

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (b) the record of dates relating to the forest resource that the holder is required to keep under section 102.6 (2).

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (2) Unless a later date is permitted by the chief forester, the information and record of dates referred to in subsection (1) must be submitted to the chief forester

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (a) within 30 days after the chief forester requests the holder to submit the information and record of dates,

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (b) on the expiration, surrender or cancellation of the area-based licence, and

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (c) at other times that may be specified by regulation.

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) (b) does not apply in respect of the expiration, surrender or cancellation of an area-based licence if the holder enters into a replacement agreement that has the same licence area.

heading: Requirement to submit forest resource inventory to chief forester
paragraph: (4) Information and records of dates submitted under this section must be submitted in the form and manner specified by the chief forester.

heading: Requirement to review forest resource inventory in special circumstances
paragraph:
102.8
		  (1) The chief forester may, by order, require the holder of an area-based licence to conduct a review and make the determinations and, if applicable, the updates described in section 102.5 (1) if the chief forester considers that a portion of the licence area has been significantly impacted by any of the following:

heading: Requirement to review forest resource inventory in special circumstances
paragraph: (a) wildfire, disease or insect infestation;

heading: Requirement to review forest resource inventory in special circumstances
paragraph: (b) windthrow;

heading: Requirement to review forest resource inventory in special circumstances
paragraph: (c) a prescribed natural event.

heading: Requirement to review forest resource inventory in special circumstances
paragraph: (2) Unless a later date is specified in an order under subsection (1), the holder to which the order relates must complete the review, and make the required determinations and updates, by no later than 2 years after the effective date of that order.

heading: Verification of information in forest resource inventory
paragraph:
102.9
		  (1) In this section, "inventory official" means a person designated by the minister as an inventory official.

heading: Verification of information in forest resource inventory
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of verifying information in an inventory of a forest resource prepared by the holder of an area-based licence, an inventory official may do any of the following:

heading: Verification of information in forest resource inventory
paragraph: (a) require a person to produce for inspection or copying records that relate to the information;

heading: Verification of information in forest resource inventory
paragraph: (b) enter, at any reasonable time, onto land in the licence area to carry out surveys, tests or examinations;

heading: Verification of information in forest resource inventory
paragraph: (c) pass over land for the purposes of accessing land in the licence area.

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph:
103
		  (1) Subject to sections 107, 108 and 142.7, if stumpage under section 104 or under an agreement entered into under this Act is payable to the government in respect of Crown timber, the amount payable must be calculated by multiplying the volume or quantity of the timber

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (a) reported in a scale made under Part 6, or

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (b) calculated using the information required to be submitted to the government under section 106 (2)

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: by the sum of

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (c) the rate of stumpage applicable to the timber under section 105, and

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (d) if applicable, the bonus bid offered in respect of the timber.

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (2) Nothing in subsection (1) limits a requirement under this Act, or under an agreement entered into under this Act, to pay a bonus offer.

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (3) Despite sections 107 and 108 but subject to section 142.7, a person who cuts, damages, destroys or removes Crown timber without authorization must pay, in addition to all other amounts payable under this Act or another enactment, stumpage calculated by multiplying the volume or quantity of the timber that was cut, damaged, destroyed or removed without authorization, as determined by an official designated by the minister, by the sum of

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (a) the rate of stumpage that an employee of the ministry referred to in section 105 (1) determines would likely have applied to the timber under that section if rights to the timber had been granted under an agreement entered into under this Act, and

heading: Amount of stumpage
paragraph: (b) if applicable, the bonus bid that an employee of the ministry referred to in section 105 (1) determines would likely have been offered for the timber if rights to the timber had been granted under an agreement entered into under this Act.

heading: Assessments for merchantable Crown timber that is not cut and removed
paragraph:
103.1
		  (1) If an agreement entered into under this Act specifies that waste assessments are payable to the government in respect of merchantable Crown timber that could have been cut and removed under the agreement, but, at the agreement holder's discretion, is not cut and removed, the amount payable must be calculated in accordance with the agreement.

heading: Assessments for merchantable Crown timber that is not cut and removed
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), a requirement in an agreement entered into under this Act is without effect to the extent that it requires the holder of the agreement, on or after November 4, 2003, to cut and remove timber in accordance with the agreement.

heading: Assessments for merchantable Crown timber that is not cut and removed
paragraph: (3) If an agreement referred to in subsection (2) requires its holder to pay an amount determined in accordance with the agreement for timber that is not cut and removed in accordance with the agreement, the holder must pay the amount required to be paid under the agreement.

heading: Assessments for merchantable Crown timber that is not cut and removed
paragraph: (4) Despite subsections (1) to (3), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations specifying circumstances under which waste assessments are payable to the government in respect of merchantable Crown timber that could have been cut and removed under the agreement but, at the agreement holder's discretion, is not cut and removed.

heading: Assessments for merchantable Crown timber that is not cut and removed
paragraph: (5) If a provision in an agreement entered into under this Act conflicts or is inconsistent with a regulation made under subsection (4), the regulation prevails.

heading: Assessments for merchantable Crown timber that is not cut under road permit and stored
paragraph:
103.2
		  If a road permit specifies that waste assessments are payable to the government in respect of merchantable Crown timber described in section 119.1 (3) (a) (i) or (ii) of this Act, the amount payable must be calculated in accordance with the road permit.

heading: Stumpage rate for timber licence
paragraph: (2) Despite another Act or a grant of Crown land, no royalty is reserved or payable to the government in respect of timber cut from private land and scaled after January 1, 1979.

heading: Stumpage rate for timber licence
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), no stumpage is payable in respect of timber cut on land granted by Canada by letters patent and situated within the Railway Belt or Peace River Block.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph:
105
		  (1) Subject to the regulations made under subsection (6) and orders under subsection (7), if stumpage is payable to the government under an agreement entered into under this Act or under section 103 (3), the rates of stumpage must be determined, redetermined and varied

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (a) by an employee of the ministry, identified in the policies and procedures referred to in paragraph (c),

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (b) at the times specified by the minister, and

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (c) in accordance with the policies and procedures approved by the minister.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (1.1) For the purpose of taking into account differences in the obligations of the holders of agreements in respect of their agreements, Treasury Board may make regulations prescribing adjustments to be incorporated in the policies and procedures approved under subsection (1) (c).

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (1.2) A regulation under subsection (1.1) may be different for different timber, places, transactions or holders of agreements entered into under this Act.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (2) Rates, policies and procedures under subsection (1) may be different for different timber, places, transactions or holders of agreements entered into under this Act, and the policies and procedures referred to in subsection (1) may, for stumpage paid or payable in respect of timber cut under a cutting authority issued after July 31, 2005, provide that the determination, redetermination or variation of a rate of stumpage is effective at any date, including, without limitation, at any date before or after

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (a) the harvesting or scaling of the timber in respect of which the stumpage has been or is to be paid, or

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (b) the payment of stumpage based on any earlier determined, redetermined or varied rate of stumpage.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (2.1) For the purposes of subsection (2), "cutting authority" has the same meaning as in the policies and procedures approved under subsection (1) (c).

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), but subject to the regulations made under subsection (6) and orders under subsection (7), the holder of a timber licence must pay stumpage to the government at a percentage of the rates determined under subsection (1).

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (4) The percentage referred to in subsection (3) is

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (a) 100% of the rates referred to as "miscellaneous stumpage rates", in policies and procedures approved from time to time by the minister under subsection (1), and

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (b) for rates not referred to in paragraph (a), the percentage set out in column 2 opposite the time period in column 1 in which the stumpage rate is determined.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (5) Within 30 days after the minister approves the policies and procedures referred to in subsection (1) (c), they must be posted on a publicly accessible government website or published in any other manner that the minister considers will allow the public to have access to those policies and procedures.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (5.1) The policies and procedures referred to in subsection (1) (c) may require the holder of an agreement to submit information to the government as necessary or desirable for the determination, redetermination or variation of a stumpage rate.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (5.2) The holder of an agreement who is required, under the policies and procedures referred to in subsection (1) (c), to submit the information referred to in subsection (5.1) must comply with the requirement.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (6) A stumpage rate must not be lower than the prescribed minimum.

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (7) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it to be in the public interest, he or she may

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (6), order that stumpage rates applicable to all timber or a class of timber in an area of British Columbia or cut under an agreement are to be lower than the rates determined under subsection (1) for a period not exceeding one year, and

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (b) attach conditions to an order made under paragraph (a).

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (8) On the date that a condition attached to an order made under subsection (7) (a) is not complied with,

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (a) the order is terminated, and

heading: Stumpage rate determined
paragraph: (b) the stumpage rate must be determined, redetermined or varied in the same manner as it was determined, redetermined or varied immediately before the order was made.

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph:
105.1
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: "agreement" means an agreement in the form of a licence, permit or agreement referred to in section 12;

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: "applicant" means a person who applies for an agreement.

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: (2) An applicant who is required under this Act to submit information to the government must ensure that, at the time the information is submitted, the information is complete and accurate.

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: (3) The holder of an agreement who is required under the agreement or this Act to submit information to the government

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: (a) for use in determining, redetermining or varying a stumpage rate, or

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: (b) for any other purpose under this Act,

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: must ensure that, at the time the information is submitted, the information is complete and accurate.

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph:
105.2
		  (1) In this section, "policies and procedures" means the policies and procedures referred to in section 105 (1) (c).

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (2) The minister may direct under this subsection that a stumpage rate be redetermined or varied under section 105 (1) if the minister is of the opinion that the stumpage rate was determined, redetermined or varied under that section based on information, submitted by or on behalf of the holder of an agreement, to which one or both of the following apply:

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (a) at the time the information was submitted, the information was incomplete or inaccurate;

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (b) at the time the information was submitted, the information did not meet the requirements of the policies and procedures.

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (3) The minister may direct under this subsection that a stumpage rate be redetermined or varied under section 105 (1) if the minister is of the opinion that both of the following apply:

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (a) after the stumpage rate was determined, redetermined or varied under section 105 (1), the minister became aware of information that

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (i)  existed but was not taken into account when the stumpage rate was determined, redetermined or varied, or

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (ii)  did not exist when the stumpage rate was determined, redetermined or varied;

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (b) a redetermination or variation that takes into account the information described in paragraph (a) of this subsection is likely to result in a stumpage rate that is different from the earlier determined, redetermined or varied stumpage rate.

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (4) A direction of the minister under this section may be made at any time,

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (a) whether the earlier determined, redetermined or varied stumpage rate is still in effect or has expired, and

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (b) whether before or after stumpage is paid in respect of the timber to which the stumpage rate relates.

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (5) If the minister directs under this section that an earlier determined, redetermined or varied stumpage rate be redetermined or varied under section 105 (1),

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (a) in the case of a direction issued under subsection (2) of this section, the redetermination or variation must take into account the information that is necessary to completely and accurately meet the requirements of the policies and procedures,

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (b) in the case of a direction issued under subsection (3) of this section, the redetermination or variation must take into account the information described in paragraph (a) of that subsection, and

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (c) the redetermination or variation must be made in accordance with the policies and procedures that were in effect at the time the earlier stumpage rate was determined, redetermined or varied.

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (6) A stumpage rate that, at the direction of the minister under this section, is redetermined or varied under section 105 (1)

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (a) is deemed to have taken effect on the day after the date on which the earlier determined, redetermined or varied stumpage rate took effect, or

heading: Redetermination of stumpage rate at direction of minister
paragraph: (b) takes effect on the day after the intended effective date for the earlier determined, redetermined or varied stumpage rate, if that earlier rate is not in effect when the redetermination or variation is made.

heading: Small scale salvage costs portion to be paid into special account
paragraph:
105.3
		  All revenue derived from the small scale salvage costs portion, if any, of a stumpage rate imposed in accordance with the policies and procedures referred to in section 105 (1) (c) must be paid into the Small Scale Salvage Sub-account of the Forest Stand Management Fund special account established by the Special Accounts Appropriation and Control Act.

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: 106		  (1) The amount of stumpage payable on Crown timber

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: (a) may, with the approval of the minister, or

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: (b) must, in the circumstances provided for in the policies and procedures referred to in section 105 (1) (c),

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: be calculated using the information provided by a cruise of the timber conducted before the timber is cut, instead of the volume reported in a scale of the timber made under Part 6.

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of calculating the amount of stumpage payable using information provided by a cruise of the timber conducted before the timber is cut, the minister may require the holder of an agreement to submit the following information to the government:

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: (a) some or all of the information provided by the cruise of the timber;

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: (b) an estimate, in hectares, of the size of the area from which the timber is cut;

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: (c) any other information the minister considers necessary.

heading: Cruise instead of scale
paragraph: (3) The holder of an agreement who is required under subsection (2) to submit information to the government must submit the information in the manner and at the times required by the minister.

heading: More than one rate
paragraph:
107
		  If the minister considers it appropriate and more than one stumpage rate applies to timber cut in a timber harvesting operation, a single rate of stumpage, calculated as the average of the rates that otherwise would be applicable and weighted according to the respective volumes of timber estimated by the minister to be subject to each rate, is payable on the timber.

heading: Rate on unscaled or incorrectly scaled timber
paragraph:
108
		  Subject to section 142.7, if Crown timber on which royalty or stumpage is payable is

heading: Rate on unscaled or incorrectly scaled timber
paragraph: (a) processed,

heading: Rate on unscaled or incorrectly scaled timber
paragraph: (b) sold, or

heading: Rate on unscaled or incorrectly scaled timber
paragraph: (c) removed from British Columbia

heading: Rate on unscaled or incorrectly scaled timber
paragraph: without first being scaled correctly under Part 6, the amount of royalty or stumpage payable must be calculated by multiplying the minister's estimate of the volume or quantity of the timber by the rate of royalty or stumpage, as the case may be, that the minister considers would have applied if the timber had been scaled correctly under Part 6.

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph:
109
		  (0.1) In this section, "BC Timber Sales official" means a person who

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (a) is employed in the ministry of the minister, and

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (b) is designated by the minister, by name or title, as a BC Timber Sales official.

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (1) The Small Business Forest Enterprise Account is renamed as the BC Timber Sales Account and continued as a special account in the general fund of the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (2) The revenue due to the government under this Act, derived from the following sources, must be credited to the BC Timber Sales Account:

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (a) fees and charges that BC timber sales enterprises are required to pay under this Act or a BC timber sales agreement;

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (c) timber sale licences entered into under section 20;

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (f) forestry licences to cut entered into under sections 24.8, 24.9 and 47.6 (3);

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (f.1) a road permit issued to the holder of a licence referred to in this subsection, if the road permit is associated with the licence;

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (g) security for BC timber sales agreements realized under the regulations made under section 79 (1.4);

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (h) deposits for BC timber sales agreements realized under a regulation made under section 151 (11) or (12);

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (i) if the crediting is approved by Treasury Board, money derived from an expenditure made under subsection (3) (e);

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (j) dispositions of property under subsection (5).

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (2.1) Amounts, other than taxes, payable to the government under an agreement entered into under section 118 of the Forests and Range Practices Act must be credited to the BC Timber Sales Account if the agreement is entered into by a BC Timber Sales official who is authorized or designated, under that section, to enter into the agreement.

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (2.2) Costs recovered from a ministry, including costs recovered from the ministry of the minister responsible for the administration of this Act, in relation to any of the following services must be credited to the BC Timber Sales Account if the services are provided to the ministry, on direction of the minister responsible for the administration of this Act, by or through a BC Timber Sales official:

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (a) silviculture services;

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (b) forest protection services;

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (c) services respecting the classification or rehabilitation of forest resources;

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (d) prescribed services.

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), money in the BC Timber Sales Account may be expended

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (a) to defray the costs of

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (i)  preparing or purchasing operational plans for agreements that yield revenue referred to in subsection (2), and

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (ii)  carrying out or purchasing assessments to formulate the plans,

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (a.1) to defray the costs of consideration provided under BCTS disposition agreements referred to in section 22.2 and to defray any other costs associated with those agreements,

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (a.2) to make payments as described in section 22.4 (2) and to defray any other costs associated with making those payments,

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (b) to defray the costs that are necessary to meet the requirements of section 29 (2) of the Forest and Range Practices Act, and that are incidental to operations that yield BC timber sales revenue,

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (c) to defray the costs of construction and maintenance of logging roads and bridges, protection of forests and administration and other forest management requirements that are incidental to operations that yield revenue referred to in subsection (2),

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (d) to purchase, rent or lease a logging road or bridge for a purpose that is incidental to operations that yield revenue referred to in subsection (2),

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (d.1) to defray the costs associated with agreements in relation to which subsection (2.1) applies,

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (d.2) to defray the costs associated with the provision of services in relation to which subsection (2.2) applies,

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (d.3) to defray the costs associated with dispositions of property under subsection (5), and

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (e) if the expenditure is for a prescribed purpose and is approved by Treasury Board.

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (4) After consultation with the minister, the Treasury Board may direct that the balance of the BC Timber Sales Account be reduced by an amount equal to any part of the balance not required for the purposes set out in subsection (3).

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (5) The minister may dispose of any of the following property:

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (a) any property of the government, other than logging roads, acquired with money derived from expenditures made under section 109 (3) (a), (b) or (c);

heading: BC Timber Sales Account
paragraph: (b) bridges purchased by the government with money derived from expenditures made under section 109 (3) (d).

heading: Annual rent
paragraph:
111
		  (1) The holder of a

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: (a) forest licence other than a supplemental forest licence, timber licence or area-based licence,

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: (a.1) cutting permit issued for a supplemental forest licence, or

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: (b) forestry licence to cut issued under a pulpwood agreement

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: must pay to the government, on or before a date specified by the minister, annual rent at the rates prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council even if the licence, agreement or permit does not contain a provision to that effect.

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: (2) If a timber licence expires under Part 3, Division 5, and is replaced by a timber licence, annual rent that is paid and attributable to the unexpired portion of its term must be credited to the annual rent payable for the first year of the term of the timber licence.

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: (4) In prescribing the rates of annual rent, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may classify licences, agreements or permits granting rights to harvest Crown timber and set different rates for different

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: (a) classes of licences, agreements or permits, or

heading: Annual rent
paragraph: (b) forms of licences, agreements or permits.

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph:
112
		  (1) The annual rent payable for a tree farm licence must be calculated by adding

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: (a) the total annual rent payable for timber licences in the tree farm licence area, and

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: (b) the portion of the allowable annual cut available to the licence holder during the year to which the total annual rent pertains, that the chief forester determines is attributable to

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: (i)  Crown land referred to in section 35 (1) (b), other than Crown land subject to a timber licence, and

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: (ii)  land referred to in sections 37 (1) and 38,

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: multiplied by the annual rent rate prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council for tree farm licences.

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: (2) The annual rent payable for a woodlot licence is the portion of the allowable annual cut authorized for the woodlot licence that the minister determines is attributable to land referred to in section 45 (1) (b) (ii), multiplied by the annual rent rate prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council for woodlot licences.

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: (3) The annual rent payable for a community forest agreement is the portion of the allowable annual cut available to the holder of the agreement, during the year to which the total annual rent pertains, that the minister determines is attributable to the Crown land referred to in section 43.3 (1) (b), multiplied by the annual rent rate prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council for community forest agreements.

heading: Calculation of annual rent
paragraph: (4) The annual rent payable for a first nations woodland licence is the portion of the allowable annual cut available to the holder of the licence, during the year to which the total annual rent pertains, that the minister determines is attributable to the Crown land referred to in section 43.55 (1) (b), multiplied by the annual rent rate prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council for first nations woodland licences.

heading: Annual rent for council
paragraph:
112.1
		  (1) If authorized by the regulations and in accordance with the regulations, the Lieutenant Governor in Council, in prescribing the rate of annual rent for a woodlot licence, under section 111 (1), may allocate a portion of that rate to represent money payable to the Woodlot Product Development Council by producers, under the Farming and Fishing Industries Development Act, in respect of a levy established by the council under that Act.

heading: Annual rent for council
