paragraph: (2) The revenue from the portion of annual rent payable for woodlot licences that is attributable to the allocated portion of the rate of annual rent under subsection (1)

heading: Annual rent for council
paragraph: (a) must be paid out of the consolidated revenue fund to the Woodlot Product Development Council, and

heading: Annual rent for council
paragraph: (b) when so paid, is deemed to have been paid in satisfaction of the levy referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Timber cruise
paragraph: 113		  (1) If Crown timber is to be disposed of under this Act, the minister or timber sales manager may require that the person who requests the disposal of the timber provide, at the person's own expense, a cruise of the timber by a cruiser approved by the minister or timber sales manager.

heading: Timber cruise
paragraph: (2) If a person, at the person's own expense, has provided a cruise of timber as required under subsection (1), but is not granted a licence or cutting permit in respect of the timber, the person who is granted a licence or cutting permit, as a condition of receiving it, must reimburse the costs of the cruise to the person who provided the cruise.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
114
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "eligible holder" means a person who has the right to harvest timber under a

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) forest licence,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) timber licence,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) area-based licence,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) Christmas tree permit,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) timber sale licence, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) forestry licence to cut;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "forest development plan" means a forest development plan under the Forest and Range Practices Act.

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: 115		  (1) Subject to this Part and section 215, the minister or timber sales manager may, on application by an eligible holder, issue a road permit authorizing the holder to do one or both of the following for the purpose of accessing timber:

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (a) construct a road on Crown land;

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (b) maintain an existing road on Crown land, other than a forest service road.

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (2) Without limiting the discretion of the minister or timber sales manager under subsection (1) to consider other matters, in deciding whether to issue a road permit, the minister or timber sales manager must consider all of the following:

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (a) the impact that construction, maintenance or use of the road, as applicable, would have on

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (i)  the management and conservation of forest resources,

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (ii)  cultural heritage resources,

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (iii)  public health and safety,

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (iv)  if applicable, rights in relation to timber proposed to be cut under the road permit that are held by a person other than the applicant under an agreement entered into under this Act, and

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (v)  prescribed matters;

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (b) in the case of an application for a road permit to construct a road,

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (i)  whether alternative means of accessing the relevant timber exist, and

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (ii)  the impact of those alternative means on the matters listed in paragraph (a).

heading: Issuance of road permit
paragraph: (3) The duty of the minister or timber sales manager under section 117 to refuse to issue a road permit does not limit the discretion of the minister or timber sales manager under this section to refuse to issue a road permit.

heading: Application for road permit
paragraph:
116
		  (1) An application made under section 115 must be submitted in the form and manner specified by the minister or timber sales manager.

heading: Application for road permit
paragraph: (2) The minister or timber sales manager may require an applicant to include in an application for a road permit, at the applicant's expense,

heading: Application for road permit
paragraph: (a) information, plans, studies or analyses that the minister or timber sales manager considers will assist in considering the matters referred to in section 115 (2), and

heading: Application for road permit
paragraph: (b) any other information the minister or timber sales manager considers relevant to the application.

heading: Application for road permit
paragraph: (3) The minister or timber sales manager may require that the information, plans, studies or analyses required under subsection (2) (a) of this section be prepared by a person with the qualifications specified by the minister or timber sales manager.

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph:
117
		  (1) In this section, "road permit area", in relation to a proposed road permit, means the area of land to which the road permit would apply, if issued.

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (2) The minister must refuse to issue a road permit if one or more of the following circumstances apply:

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (a) the minister determines that, taking into account the prescribed matters, if any, issuance of the road permit would compromise a prescribed government objective;

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (b) in the case of a road permit to construct a road, a circumstance set out in subsection (3);

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (c) a prescribed circumstance.

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (3) The circumstances for the purposes of subsection (2) (b) are as follows:

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (a) the road permit area is located outside a forest landscape area and one or more of the following apply:

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (i)  the applicant does not hold a forest stewardship plan or woodlot licence plan, as required under the Forest and Range Practices Act, in relation to the road permit area;

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (ii)  the applicant was required, under section 15.1 of the Forest and Range Practices Act, to prepare and make publicly available a forest operations map before applying for the road permit, and the minister considers that, taking into account the prescribed matters, if any,

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (A) the applicant has not complied with section 15.1 of that Act, or

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (B) the location of the proposed road is inconsistent with the approximate locations of roads shown in the forest operations map;

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (b) the road permit area is located in a forest landscape area and either of the following applies:

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (i)  the applicant does not hold a forest operations plan, as required under the Forest and Range Practices Act, that applies to the road permit area;

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (ii)  the minister considers that, taking into account the prescribed matters, if any, the location of the proposed road is inconsistent with the approximate locations of proposed roads shown in a forest operations plan held by the applicant.

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (4) If a person applies for a road permit and only a portion of the road permit area is located outside a forest landscape area,

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (a) subsection (3) (a) applies to the application as it relates to the portion of the road permit area located outside the forest landscape area, and

heading: Mandatory refusal to issue road permit
paragraph: (b) subsection (3) (b) applies to the application as it relates to the portion of the road permit area located in the forest landscape area.

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: 118		  (1) A road permit must

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (a) describe the location of the road that is or will be subject to the road permit, and

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (b) include the prescribed terms and conditions, if any.

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (2) A road permit authorizing the holder to construct a road must also authorize the holder to use, maintain and deactivate the road.

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (3) A road permit authorizing the holder to maintain an existing road must also authorize the holder to use and deactivate the road.

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (4) A road permit may do one or both of the following:

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (a) specify a date by which the road must be deactivated;

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (b) authorize the holder to, on Crown land that is in a Provincial forest and in the right of way of the road,

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (i)  manage and use the land for sand pits, gravel pits, rock quarries or other quarries that are in the right of way, and

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (ii)  use the materials in the pits and quarries referred to in subparagraph (i) for constructing or maintaining the road, as applicable.

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (5) A road permit associated with a timber sale licence may

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (a) specify standards and programs established by one or more standard making bodies,

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (b) require the holder of the road permit to meet the standards and programs specified under paragraph (a), and

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (c) specify the manner in which the holder of the road permit must conduct operations under the road permit in order to meet the standards and programs specified under paragraph (a).

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (6) A road permit may include other terms and conditions that, subject to subsection (8), are consistent with this Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act, the Wildfire Act and any regulations or standards made under those Acts.

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (7) The terms and conditions referred to in subsection (6) may include, without limitation, terms and conditions respecting one or more of the following:

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (a) the storage of timber cut under the road permit;

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (b) periods during which the holder may not carry out activities related to the construction, maintenance or deactivation of the road, including, without limitation, blasting activities;

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (c) the manner in which the holder may carry out activities referred to in paragraph (b), either during specified periods or generally;

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (d) vehicles, machinery or equipment that may not be used by the holder when constructing, maintaining, using or deactivating the road, either during specified periods or generally;

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (e) periods during which the holder may not use the road;

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (f) specified signage that is to be posted by the holder on the road.

heading: Road permit content - general
paragraph: (8) Terms and conditions included in a road permit may set requirements or restrictions that are more stringent than the requirements and restrictions that apply to the holder under this Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act, the Wildfire Act or any standards made under those Acts.

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph:
119
		  (1) In this section and in section 119.1, "roadway timber", in relation to a road authorized to be constructed under a road permit, means Crown timber that the minister is satisfied must be cut to construct the road.

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (2) A road permit to construct a road must authorize the holder to harvest roadway timber if the roadway timber meets both of the following conditions:

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (a) the roadway timber is located in an area described in subsection (3);

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (b) no other person has the right to harvest the roadway timber under one or more of the following:

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (i)  a cutting permit;

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (ii)  a forestry licence to cut;

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (iii)  an area-based licence;

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (iv)  a timber licence.

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (3) The areas for the purposes of subsection (2) (a) are as follows:

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (a) a timber supply area specified in a forest licence held by the road permit holder;

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (b) the licence area of an area-based licence or timber licence held by the road permit holder;

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (c) in relation to a forestry licence to cut held by the road permit holder,

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (i)  an area of land described in the licence, and

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (ii)  a timber supply area in which the area referred to in subparagraph (i) is located;

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (d) the area specified in a master licence to cut or occupant licence to cut held by a person other than the road permit holder.

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (4) If a road permit authorizes the holder to harvest timber, the road permit must require the holder to pay to the government, in addition to other amounts payable under this Act,

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (a) stumpage under Part 7, and

heading: Road permit content - right to harvest timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (b) waste assessments for merchantable Crown timber, whether standing or felled, that could have been cut and removed under the road permit but, at the holder's discretion, is not cut and removed.

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph:
119.1
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: "encumbered roadway timber", in relation to a road permit to construct a road, means roadway timber that meets one or both of the following conditions:

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (a) the roadway timber is not located in an area described in section 119 (3);

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (b) a person other than the road permit holder has the right to harvest the roadway timber under a permit or licence referred to in section 119 (2) (b);

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: "underlying rights-holder", in relation to encumbered roadway timber, means a person who holds an agreement under this Act that grants rights with respect to the encumbered roadway timber.

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (2) A road permit to construct a road

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (a) must not grant to the holder the right to harvest encumbered roadway timber, and

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (b) may grant to the holder the right to cut encumbered roadway timber.

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (3) If a road permit grants to the holder the right to cut encumbered roadway timber,

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (a) the road permit may require the road permit holder to pay to the government, in addition to other amounts payable under this Act, waste assessments for one or both of the following:

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (i)  merchantable Crown timber that could have been cut under the road permit but, at the road permit holder's discretion, is not cut;

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (ii)  merchantable Crown timber cut under the road permit that could have been stored in decks or piles but, at the road permit holder's discretion, is not stored in decks or piles, and

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (b) an underlying rights-holder is relieved from any requirement under an agreement entered into under this Act to pay waste assessments in relation to timber described in paragraph (a) (i) and (ii).

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (4) The conferral of the right to cut encumbered roadway timber under a road permit does not affect an obligation of an underlying rights-holder to pay stumpage to the government in relation to the encumbered roadway timber.

heading: Road permit content - right to cut timber in right-of-way
paragraph: (5) For certainty, the rights of an underlying rights-holder with respect to encumbered roadway timber are subject to the right of a road permit holder to cut the encumbered roadway timber.

heading: Volume cut under road permit deemed to be harvested under licence for cut control purposes
paragraph:
119.2
		  (1) This section applies to timber cut under a road permit if a person, other than the road permit holder, has the right to remove the timber under

heading: Volume cut under road permit deemed to be harvested under licence for cut control purposes
paragraph: (a) a cutting permit issued for a licence, as defined in a provision of Division 3.1 of Part 4, or

heading: Volume cut under road permit deemed to be harvested under licence for cut control purposes
paragraph: (b) a forestry licence to cut that does not require the holder to obtain a cutting permit before harvesting Crown timber under the licence.

heading: Volume cut under road permit deemed to be harvested under licence for cut control purposes
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of paragraph (a) of the definition of "volume of timber harvested" in section 75.1 (1) and the definition of "volume of timber harvested" in a licence referred to in section 75.11 (1), and despite the definition of "timber volumes" in section 75.1 (2), the amount of timber cut under a road permit is deemed to be harvested under the licence referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (b) of this section.

heading: Deactivation of road
paragraph:
119.3
		  (1) In this section, "deactivate", in relation to a road, means to deactivate the road in accordance with the requirements under the Forest and Range Practices Act that apply to the deactivation of the road.

heading: Deactivation of road
paragraph: (2) Except in prescribed circumstances, the holder of a road permit must deactivate a road authorized under the road permit by the earliest of the following:

heading: Deactivation of road
paragraph: (a) the date on which the road permit expires or is surrendered;

heading: Deactivation of road
paragraph: (b) the date on which rights under the road permit that relate to the road expire or are surrendered;

heading: Deactivation of road
paragraph: (c) the date of deactivation specified in the road permit;

heading: Deactivation of road
paragraph: (d) if the road permit is cancelled under section 77, the date of deactivation specified under section 77 (6).

heading: Duty to comply with terms and conditions of road permit
paragraph: 119.4		  The holder of a road permit must comply with the terms and conditions of the road permit.

heading: Issuance of road use permit to eligible holder
paragraph:
119.5
		  The minister may, on application by an eligible holder, issue a road use permit authorizing the eligible holder to use a forest service road if the minister is satisfied that use of the road by the applicant will not

heading: Issuance of road use permit to eligible holder
paragraph: (a) adversely affect authorized users of the road, or

heading: Issuance of road use permit to eligible holder
paragraph: (b) compromise a forest operations plan, forest stewardship plan, forest development plan or woodlot licence plan.

heading: Issuance of road use permit for natural resource development purpose
paragraph:
119.6
		  (1) In this section, "natural resource development purpose" has the same meaning as in section 21.1 of the Forest and Range Practices Act.

heading: Issuance of road use permit for natural resource development purpose
paragraph: (2) The minister may, on application by a person other than an eligible holder, issue a road use permit authorizing the person to use a forest service road for a natural resource development purpose if the minister is satisfied that use of the road under the permit will not

heading: Issuance of road use permit for natural resource development purpose
paragraph: (a) cause inordinate disturbance to the natural environment,

heading: Issuance of road use permit for natural resource development purpose
paragraph: (b) adversely affect authorized users of the road, or

heading: Issuance of road use permit for natural resource development purpose
paragraph: (c) compromise a forest operations plan, forest stewardship plan, forest development plan or woodlot licence plan.

heading: Road use permit content
paragraph: 119.7		  (1) A road use permit must describe the forest service road that the holder is authorized to use.

heading: Road use permit content
paragraph: (2) A road use permit may include terms and conditions that are consistent with this Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act, the Wildfire Act and any regulations or standards made under those Acts.

heading: Declaration of forest service road
paragraph:
120.1
		  (1) The minister may declare a road on Crown land to be a forest service road if any of the following applies:

heading: Declaration of forest service road
paragraph: (a) the road is the subject of a road permit;

heading: Declaration of forest service road
paragraph: (b) the road is a forest resource road within the meaning of section 21.1 of the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Declaration of forest service road
paragraph: (c) the road is constructed or maintained by the minister under section 121 (1) of this Act, or is on private land taken by the minister under that section;

heading: Declaration of forest service road
paragraph: (d) the road is on land dedicated to the government under section 121 (8) of this Act.

heading: Declaration of forest service road
paragraph: (2) If a road referred to in subsection (1) (a) is declared to be a forest service road, the minister must issue a road use permit in relation to the road to the holder of the road permit.

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: 121		  (1) The minister, for the purpose of providing access to timber or for any other purpose consistent with this Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act or the Wildfire Act may do one or more of the following:

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (a) construct and maintain roads and trails;

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (b) enter on and take possession of private land, and of roads and trails on private land;

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (c) enter on private land and take from it timber, stones, gravel, sand, clay or other materials for the purpose of constructing roads and trails;

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (d) construct, take possession of and use temporarily roads for the purposes of paragraph (c);

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (e) enter on private land and construct and maintain on it drains to carry water from a road;

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (f) enter into an agreement with an owner of land, under section 3 (1) of the Expropriation Act or otherwise, that provides for the dedication of the land, in accordance with subsection (8) of this section, to the government for use as a road.

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (2) If private land is taken under subsection (1) (b) and, as a result of the taking, the total area in the original grant of the private land from the government or Her Majesty in right of Canada, that is taken by the government

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (b) under this Act

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: since the date of the original grant from the government or Her Majesty in right of Canada, exceeds 5% of the total area in the original grant, the government must pay compensation in respect of the area exceeding 5%.

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (3) If, since the date of the government grant, private land taken under subsection (1) has been subdivided into 2 or more parcels by a registered conveyance or subdivision plan,

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (a) the area of a parcel that may be taken without compensation must not exceed 5% of the area of the parcel, and

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (b) the total area to be taken without compensation must be apportioned among all parcels, portions of which are taken at the same time, in proportion to the area taken from each.

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (4) The government must pay compensation in respect of improvements on all private land taken under subsection (1).

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (5) If land is expropriated under subsection (1), the Expropriation Act applies.

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (8) If the minister enters into an agreement under subsection (1) (f) with an owner of land, the minister may, for the purposes of causing the land to be dedicated to the government under section 107 of the Land Title Act, deposit in the land title office a reference plan or explanatory plan that shows the portion of land subject to the agreement as a road and, in that event, section 107 (1) (c), (d) and (e) and (3) of the Land Title Act applies to that portion of land.

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (9) The minister

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (a) may, by notice in the form established under paragraph (a.1) and published or broadcast, or both, in the manner the minister considers appropriate, discontinue and close a right of way or forest service road or a part of either, in which event the right of way or forest service road or the part is discontinued and closed,

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (i)  if the notice specifies the date on which and the time at which the discontinuance and closure become effective, on that specified date and at that specified time,

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (ii)  if the notice specifies the date on which but not the time at which the discontinuance and closure become effective, at the beginning of that specified date, or

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (iii)  if the notice specifies neither the date on which nor the time at which the discontinuance and closure become effective, at the beginning of the day following the day on which the first of such publications or broadcasts occurred,

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (a.1) may establish a form of notice for the purposes of paragraph (a),

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (b) may limit a discontinuance and closure under paragraph (a) to a specified period,

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (c) may assign a right of way or forest service road or a part of either to the minister responsible for the administration of the Transportation Act, and

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (d) in the case of a discontinuance or closure not limited to a specified period, may dispose of any land that was comprised in the right of way or forest service road to

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (i)  an owner of the land of which the right of way or forest service road originally formed part, or

heading: Road and trail construction
paragraph: (ii)  an owner of land adjoining that land.

heading: Log salvage district
paragraph:
122
		  The minister, by publishing a notice in the Gazette, may

heading: Log salvage district
paragraph: (a) establish an area of British Columbia as a log salvage district, and

heading: Log salvage district
paragraph: (b) abolish, or change the boundaries of, a log salvage district.

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph:
123
		  (1) The minister may grant to a person who meets the prescribed qualifications a receiving station licence authorizing its holder to accept delivery of salvaged logs within a log salvage district.

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (2) A receiving station licence must contain the terms and conditions, consistent with this Act and the regulations, determined by the minister.

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (3) The holder of a receiving station licence must,

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (a) after the date specified in the licence, maintain facilities in the log salvage district for receiving, storing and sorting salvaged logs,

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (b) dispose of salvaged logs in the prescribed manner,

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (c) pay to the government the prescribed licence fees,

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (d) account for, hold, disburse and use the revenue the holder of the receiving station receives from the sale of salvaged logs in the prescribed manner, and

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (e) subject to the regulations, pay to holders of log salvage permits for salvaged logs delivered to the holder of the receiving station or a place specified by that holder, compensation in the prescribed amount.

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (4) If a holder of a receiving station licence fails to comply with the licence, this Part or the regulations respecting log salvage, the minister may suspend the licence for a period of time and, whether or not the licence is under suspension, may cancel the licence.

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (5) Before the minister cancels a receiving station licence the minister must give the holder of the licence an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Receiving station licence
paragraph: (6) A log receiving station licence granted under the former Act continues in force under this Act as a receiving station licence.

heading: Log salvage permit
paragraph:
124
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, a person must not salvage logs in a log salvage district without a log salvage permit.

heading: Log salvage permit
paragraph: (2) The minister may grant a log salvage permit to a person who meets the prescribed qualifications.

heading: Log salvage permit
paragraph: (3) A log salvage permit must contain the terms and conditions, consistent with this Act and the regulations, determined by the minister.

heading: Log salvage permit
paragraph: (4) If the holder of a log salvage permit no longer meets the prescribed qualifications or fails to comply with the permit, this Part or the regulations respecting log salvage,

heading: Log salvage permit
paragraph: (a) the minister may suspend the permit for a period of time, and

heading: Log salvage permit
paragraph: (b) the minister, whether or not the permit is under suspension, may cancel the permit.

heading: Log salvage permit
paragraph: (5) Before the minister cancels a log salvage permit the minister must give the permit holder an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Disposal and acquisition of salvaged logs
paragraph:
125
		  A person must not dispose of a log salvaged from a log salvage district and a person must not accept delivery of a log salvaged from a log salvage district, except as provided in the regulations.

heading: Area closure
paragraph:
126
		  (1) If notified that logs have been lost in an area of coastal waters, the minister, in a notice published or broadcast, or both, in or near the area may

heading: Area closure
paragraph: (a) order that the area described in the notice be closed to log salvaging for a period not exceeding 10 days for each order, and

heading: Area closure
paragraph: (b) amend the description of the area and, subject to the 10 day maximum, extend or shorten the period of the order.

heading: Area closure
paragraph: (2) While an area is closed a person, other than the owner of a log or the owner's agent, must not salvage a log in the area described in the order.

heading: Crown timber to be used in British Columbia
paragraph:
127
		  Unless exempted under this Part, timber that is harvested from Crown land, from land granted by the government after March 12, 1906 or from land granted by the government before March 12, 1906 in a tree farm licence area, and wood residue produced from the timber, must be

heading: Crown timber to be used in British Columbia
paragraph: (a) used in British Columbia, or

heading: Crown timber to be used in British Columbia
paragraph: (b) manufactured in British Columbia into wood products to the extent of manufacture specified by regulation.

heading: Attempt to export timber or wood residue
paragraph:
127.1
		  A person must not attempt to remove from British Columbia

heading: Attempt to export timber or wood residue
paragraph: (a) timber that is harvested from

heading: Attempt to export timber or wood residue
paragraph: (i)  Crown land,

heading: Attempt to export timber or wood residue
paragraph: (ii)  land granted by the government after March 12, 1906, or

heading: Attempt to export timber or wood residue
paragraph: (iii)  land granted by the government before March 12, 1906 in a tree farm licence area, or

heading: Attempt to export timber or wood residue
paragraph: (b) wood residue produced from timber referred to in paragraph (a),

heading: Attempt to export timber or wood residue
paragraph: unless the timber or wood residue is exempted under this Part.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph:
128
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may exempt from section 127

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) a species of timber or kind of wood residue and may limit the volume of a species of timber or kind of wood residue to which the exemption applies for a period or for successive periods of time, and

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) a volume of timber, whether or not harvested, or a volume of a wood residue, on receiving an application in a form required by the minister.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application in the form required by the minister, the minister may exempt from section 127

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) a volume of timber that has been harvested, not exceeding 15 000 m3 for each application, and

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) a volume of wood residue, not exceeding 200 000 bone dry units for each application.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (3) An exemption must not be given under this section unless the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the minister, as the case may be, is satisfied that

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (a) the timber or wood residue will be surplus to requirements of timber processing facilities in British Columbia,

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (b) the timber or wood residue cannot be processed economically in the vicinity of the land from which it is cut or produced, and cannot be transported economically to a processing facility located elsewhere in British Columbia, or

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (c) the exemption would prevent the waste of or improve the utilization of timber cut from Crown land.

heading: Exemption conditions and permit
paragraph:
129
		  An exemption made under section 128 may

heading: Exemption conditions and permit
paragraph: (a) stipulate conditions to be met and fees to be paid to the government, and

heading: Exemption conditions and permit
paragraph: (b) provide for the granting of a permit in respect of the timber or wood residue described in the exemption.

heading: Lien
paragraph:
130
		  (1) Money that is required to be paid to the government under the circumstances set out in subsection (1.1)

heading: Lien
paragraph: (a) is due and payable by the date specified for payment in a statement to, or notice served on, the person who is required to pay it,

heading: Lien
paragraph: (b) bears interest as prescribed, and in the case of an amount due under

heading: Lien
paragraph: (i)  section 108, the interest runs from the date determined by the minister to be the date stumpage or royalty would have been due if the timber referred to in section 108 had been scaled correctly under Part 6,

heading: Lien
paragraph: (ii)  an assessment made under section 142.51 (5) or 142.61 (4) (a), the interest runs from the date determined by the commissioner to be the date stumpage would have been due if none of the events referred to in section 142.51 (1) (a) to (d) had occurred, and

heading: Lien
paragraph: (iii)  an assessment made under section 142.52 (6) or 142.61 (4) (b), the interest runs from the applicable date on which the fee in lieu is deemed to have been due under section 142.52 (7),

heading: Lien
paragraph: (c) may be recovered in a court as a debt due to the government, and

heading: Lien
paragraph: (d) constitutes, in favour of the government,

heading: Lien
paragraph: (i)  a lien on timber, lumber, veneer, plywood, pulp, newsprint, special forest products and wood residue owned by the person who owes the money, and

heading: Lien
paragraph: (ii)  a lien on chattels or an interest in them, other than chattels referred to in subparagraph (i), owned by the person who owes the money.

heading: Lien
paragraph: (1.1) The circumstances referred to in subsection (1) are that money is required to be paid

heading: Lien
paragraph: (a) under this Act, the former Act, the Range Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act or the Wildfire Act,

heading: Lien
paragraph: (b) under an agreement entered into under this Act, the former Act or the Range Act,

heading: Lien
paragraph: (c) under a permit issued under the Forest and Range Practices Act, the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act or the Wildfire Act, or

heading: Lien
paragraph: (d) for goods, services or both provided by the ministry.

heading: Lien
paragraph: (2) A lien under subsection (1) (d) (i) has priority over all other claims, and a lien under subsection (1) (d) (ii) has priority over all other claims other than claims secured by liens, charges and encumbrances registered against the chattels before the money is due and payable.

heading: Lien
paragraph: (3) A lien constituted under subsection (1) is not lost or impaired only because

heading: Lien
paragraph: (a) proceedings to recover the money are taken or not,

heading: Lien
paragraph: (b) partial payment of the money is tendered or accepted, or

heading: Lien
paragraph: (c) the lien is not registered.

heading: Lien
paragraph: (4) If default is made in the payment of all or part of the money due and payable, the revenue minister may issue, and file with a court having jurisdiction, a certificate stating

heading: Lien
paragraph: (a) the amount that remains unpaid, including interest, and

heading: Lien
paragraph: (b) the name of the person who is required to pay it.

heading: Lien
paragraph: (5) A certificate filed under subsection (4) has the same effect as an order of the court for the recovery of a debt in the amount stated in the certificate against the person named in it, and all proceedings may be taken as if it were an order of the court.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 130.1		  (1) In this section, "proceeding" means

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (a) an action for the recovery of money under section 130 (1),

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (b) the enforcement of a lien under section 130 (1), and

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (c) the filing of a certificate under section 130 (4).

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (2) A proceeding may be commenced at any time within 7 years of the date that money claimed in the proceeding or to which the proceeding relates became due and payable under section 130 (1) (a).

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), a proceeding that relates to a contravention of this Act or the regulations and that involves wilful default or fraud may be commenced at any time.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (4) Section 24 of the Limitation Act applies to the limitation period set by this section.

heading: Person acquiring or dealing in timber responsible for payment
paragraph: 131		  A person who acquires or deals in timber on which stumpage or royalty has not been paid must

heading: Person acquiring or dealing in timber responsible for payment
paragraph: (a) report the acquisition or dealing to a person designated by the minister, in a form required by the minister, not later than 10 days following the date on which the event occurred, and

heading: Person acquiring or dealing in timber responsible for payment
paragraph: (b) pay to the government all money payable to the government in respect of the timber under this Act or under an agreement entered into under this Act.

heading: Removal permit
paragraph:
132
		  (1) The minister may order a person who has failed to pay money owing to the government by the date specified in a statement under section 130 (1) (a) to pay up to 10% of the fair market value, as estimated by the minister, of

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (a) timber, or

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (b) products manufactured from timber

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: that are from time to time located at the person's place of business.

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (2) A person who is subject to an order under subsection (1) must not remove or dispose of timber, or any products manufactured from timber, that are from time to time located at the person's place of business unless

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (a) the person complies with the order and receives a permit under subsection (3) for the timber, or the products manufactured from timber, that are removed or disposed of,

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (b) the person is no longer in default, or

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (c) the minister rescinds the order.

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (3) On application the minister must issue a permit in respect of specific timber or specific products manufactured from timber to a person if satisfied that the person has paid the amount required under the order in respect of the specific timber or products.

heading: Removal permit
paragraph: (4) Amounts paid to the government under this section must be applied to the default.

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph:
133
		  (1) The powers in this Division for the government to recover money by proceeding in court, or by filing a certificate, and the powers of seizure and sale under the Forest and Range Practices Act, may be exercised separately, concurrently or cumulatively.

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: (2) The imposition of a fine or penalty on a person under this Act or the Forest and Range Practices Act does not affect the powers of the government in this Division.

heading: Records and returns
paragraph:
136
		  (1) In this section, "fibre supply arrangement" means a contract or other arrangement for timber or wood residue to be regularly or periodically supplied to

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (a) a timber processing facility in British Columbia, or

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (b) a prescribed facility in British Columbia.

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (2) This section applies to the following persons, unless exempted by regulation:

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (a) the holder of an agreement under this Act;

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (b) a person who harvests timber;

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (c) a person who buys or sells timber;

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (d) an operator of a timber processing facility;

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (e) a party to a fibre supply arrangement;

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (f) a prescribed person.

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (3) A person referred to in subsection (2) must, in accordance with the regulations, if any, keep accurate records of the following, as applicable to the person:

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (a) with respect to timber harvesting,

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (i)  the volume of timber harvested,

heading: Records and returns
paragraph: (ii)  the nature and extent of silviculture carried out, and

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: 142.1		  (1) In this Part:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "assessment" includes reassessment;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "exemption" means an exemption given under section 128;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "fee in lieu" means a fee stipulated in an exemption;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "forest revenue official" means a person who is designated as a forest revenue official under section 142.11 (2) and includes, other than in section 142.11, the commissioner;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "permit" means a permit referred to in section 129 (b);

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: "scale" has the same meaning as in section 93.

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (2) This Part applies to the following:

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (a) the harvesting of Crown timber if the harvesting occurs on or after March 30, 2006;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (b) stumpage and the payment of stumpage if the stumpage relates to Crown timber harvested on or after March 30, 2006;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (c) the removal from British Columbia of timber referred to in section 127.1 (a) or wood residue referred to in section 127.1 (b) if the removal occurs on or after November 25, 2021;

heading: Definitions and application
paragraph: (d) a fee in lieu and the payment of a fee in lieu if the fee in lieu relates to

paragraph: (i)  a permit granted under an exemption on or after November 25, 2021, or

paragraph: (ii)  timber referred to in section 127.1 (a) or wood residue referred to in section 127.1 (b) that is removed from British Columbia on or after November 25, 2021.

heading: Officials
paragraph:
142.11
		  (1) The revenue minister may designate a person by name or title as the commissioner.

heading: Officials
paragraph: (2) The commissioner may designate a person by name or title as a forest revenue official.

heading: Officials
paragraph: (3) The commissioner may delegate, with or without conditions, any of the commissioner's powers, functions or duties under this Part to a person or a class of persons.

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph:
142.2
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a forest revenue official may enter, at any reasonable time, on any land or premises and conduct an inspection or audit referred to in section 142.21 for the purposes of ensuring compliance with the provisions of this Act, the regulations or an agreement that relate to any of the following:

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph: (a) the harvesting of Crown timber;

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph: (b) stumpage or the payment of stumpage;

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph: (c) the removal from British Columbia of timber referred to in section 127.1 (a) or wood residue referred to in section 127.1 (b);

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph: (d) a fee in lieu or the payment of a fee in lieu.

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph: (2) A forest revenue official may not enter a dwelling under subsection (1) unless a person who occupies the dwelling consents or a warrant authorizes the entry.

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph: (3) If satisfied by evidence given under oath that entry into a dwelling is necessary in order to exercise the powers under section 142.21 (a), a justice may issue a warrant, subject to any conditions the justice considers appropriate, authorizing a forest revenue official to enter the dwelling.

heading: Entry on land or premises
paragraph: (4) The commissioner may apply for a warrant under subsection (3) without notice to any other person.

heading: Inspection
paragraph:
142.21
		  A forest revenue official who enters on land or premises under section 142.2 may

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (a) inspect or conduct an audit of any record, or inspect any thing or any activity, that is related to information or records required to be kept by the person or to be provided to the government under this Act or an agreement entered into under this Act, and

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (b) require production of and copy any record referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Retention of records
paragraph:
142.3
		  (1) Subject to this section, a person who is required to keep records under this Act must keep each record in a prescribed category of records for a period of 6 years after the date the record was created.

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (2) If a person referred to in subsection (1) files a document under section 142.6 (3) or (3.1) consenting to waive section 142.6 (1) and allowing the commissioner to consider a different period in making an assessment, the person must keep all records related to the making of the assessment for the longer of the following periods:

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (a) 6 years after the date the record was created;

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (b) 90 days after the waiver ceases to have effect.

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (3) If a person referred to in subsection (1) is assessed under section 142.42 (1), 142.51 (4) or (5), 142.52 (4), (5) or (6) or 142.61 (1), (2) or (4), the person must keep all records related to the assessment for the longer of the following periods:

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (a) 6 years after the date the record was created;

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (b) the time for all appeals of the assessment has elapsed.

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (4) On receipt of a written request, the commissioner may authorize the destruction of a record before the end of the period required under this section.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph:
142.31
		  (1) For the purposes described in section 142.2 (1), a forest revenue official may require a person, by serving a demand notice on that person, to provide information and produce specified records that the person is required to keep or provide to the government.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a demand notice under subsection (1), a person must prepare and deliver to the forest revenue official the information and records required within the time specified in the demand notice.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (3) A forest revenue official must not require a person under subsection (1) to provide information or records relating to a person referred to in section 142.51 (4) (a) or (b) or 142.52 (4) or (5) (a) or (b) who is unnamed, unless

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (a) the commissioner first obtains the authorization of a judge under subsection (5) of this section, or

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (b) the requirement under subsection (1) is imposed in the circumstances, if any, prescribed for a person who is within a prescribed class of persons.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (4) The commissioner may apply for an authorization under subsection (5) with or without notice to any other person.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (5) A judge of the Supreme Court, subject to any conditions the judge considers appropriate, may make an order authorizing the commissioner to require a person under subsection (1) to provide information or records related to an unnamed person, if satisfied by evidence given under oath that

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (a) the identity of the unnamed person referred to is ascertainable, and

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (b) the requirement under subsection (1) is for the purpose of verifying that the unnamed person is in compliance with any obligation under this Act.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (6) If authorization is granted under subsection (5), a copy of the court order must be served together with the demand notice referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (7) If a person

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (a) did not have notice of an application made under subsection (4), and

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (b) is served with a court order granting an authorization under subsection (5),

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: the person, within 15 days of the service of the order, may apply to the Supreme Court for a review of the order.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (8) On hearing an application under subsection (7), a judge may

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (a) cancel the authorization previously granted, if the judge is not satisfied that the conditions in subsection (5) (a) and (b) have been met, or

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (b) confirm or vary the authorization, if the judge is satisfied that those conditions have been met.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (9) Nothing in subsection (1) affects solicitor-client privilege.

heading: Obligation of a forest revenue official
paragraph:
142.4
		  A forest revenue official who, under this Division, enters on land or premises, conducts an inspection or audit or requests information or records must provide proof of identity, on the request of the person who

heading: Obligation of a forest revenue official
paragraph: (a) is in possession or apparent possession of the land or premises,

heading: Obligation of a forest revenue official
paragraph: (b) has apparent custody or control of the records or property being inspected or audited, or

heading: Obligation of a forest revenue official
paragraph: (c) is in charge of the activity being inspected or audited.

paragraph:

		  A person who

heading: Obligation of person on request of forest revenue official
paragraph: (a) is in possession or apparent possession of land or premises entered on by a forest revenue official under this Division,

heading: Obligation of person on request of forest revenue official
paragraph: (b) has apparent custody or control of records or property being inspected or audited, or

heading: Obligation of person on request of forest revenue official
paragraph: (c) is in charge of an activity being inspected or audited,

paragraph: must produce, if and as requested by the forest revenue official,

paragraph: (d) proof of identity, and
