heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph:
142.42
		  (1) If the commissioner is satisfied that a person has failed to comply with

heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph: (a) a demand notice served under section 142.31, or

heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph: (b) a request made under section 142.41 (e),

heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph: the commissioner may assess against the person, in addition to any other penalty, a penalty equal to the product obtained by multiplying $100 and the number of days during which the failure continues, to a maximum penalty of $10 000.

heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph: (2) Sections 142.7 to 142.81 apply in relation to an assessment made under subsection (1) of this section, as if an assessment made under subsection (1) of this section were an assessment made under a provision referred to in section 142.7 (a) to (c).

heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph: (3) This section and section 142.43 apply with respect to

heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph: (a) a demand notice under section 142.31, if the demand notice is served on or after the date this section comes into force, and

heading: Penalty for failure to provide information
paragraph: (b) a request under section 142.41 (e), if the request is made on or after the date this section comes into force.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph:
142.43
		  (1) If the commissioner considers that a person has failed to comply with

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (a) a demand notice served under section 142.31, or

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (b) a request made under section 142.41 (e),

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: the commissioner may apply to the Supreme Court for either or both of the following:

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (c) an order directing the person to comply with the demand notice or request;

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (d) an order directing the directors and officers of the person to cause the person to comply with the demand notice or request.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (2) On application by the commissioner under this section, the Supreme Court may make an order it considers appropriate.

heading: Evidence
paragraph:
142.5
		  An affidavit by a forest revenue official that states the facts necessary to establish

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (a) compliance with section 142.4 by the forest revenue official and default under section 142.41 by a person to whom a request was made, or

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (b) default by a person served with a demand notice under section 142.31

heading: Evidence
paragraph: must be admitted as evidence in any court and is proof, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, of the facts stated.

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph:
142.51
		  (1) If it appears to the commissioner, from an inspection or audit of any records or from other information available, that one or more of the following has occurred, the commissioner may estimate, in accordance with subsections (2) and (3), the total amount of stumpage required to be paid in respect of the Crown timber harvested:

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (a) some or all of the Crown timber harvested was

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (i)  not scaled,

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (ii)  inaccurately scaled,

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (iii)  not reported in a scale, or

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (iv)  reported incorrectly in a scale;

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (b) the volume or quantity or quality of some or all of the Crown timber was calculated on the basis of incorrect information provided by a cruise of the timber or on the basis of other incorrect information;

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (c) the incorrect rate was applied to some or all of the Crown timber harvested;

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (d) the information relating to the Crown timber harvested that is required to be provided to the government under this Act or under an agreement entered into under this Act was incomplete or inaccurate, or was not provided.

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (2) In making an estimate under subsection (1), the commissioner must multiply

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (a) the commissioner's estimate of the volume or quantity of the Crown timber harvested, and

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (b) the sum of the commissioner's estimate of

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (i)  the rate of stumpage applicable to the Crown timber, and

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (ii)  the bonus bid, if any, offered or the bonus bid that in the opinion of the commissioner would likely have been offered in respect of the Crown timber harvested without authorization.

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (3) The commissioner may make an estimate under subsection (2) (a) or (b) in a manner and form and by a procedure the commissioner considers adequate and expedient.

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (4) If an estimate is made under subsection (1), the commissioner may assess

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (a) the person who harvested the Crown timber, and

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (b) a person who acquires, has acquired, deals in or has dealt in the Crown timber harvested

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: for the amount estimated under subsection (1), less the amount of stumpage that the government has previously billed for that Crown timber.

heading: Assessment of estimated stumpage and interest
paragraph: (5) After assessing a person under subsection (4), the commissioner may assess the amount of interest payable under section 130 (1) (b) (ii) on the amount assessed.

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph:
142.52
		  (1) If it appears to the commissioner, from an inspection or audit of any records or from other information available, that an amount of a fee in lieu is required to be paid in respect of a permit granted under an exemption, the commissioner may estimate the amount of the fee in lieu.

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (2) If it appears to the commissioner, from an inspection or audit of any records or from other information available, that

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (a) timber or wood residue to which an exemption applies has been removed from British Columbia, and

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (b) a permit required under the exemption was not granted in respect of the removal of the timber or wood residue,

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: the commissioner may estimate the amount of the fee in lieu that would have been required to be paid in respect of the permit if the permit had been granted.

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (3) The commissioner may make an estimate under subsection (1) or (2) in a manner and form and by a procedure the commissioner considers adequate.

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (4) If an estimate is made under subsection (1), the commissioner may assess the holder of the permit for the amount estimated under that subsection.

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (5) If an estimate is made under subsection (2), the commissioner may assess one or both of the following for the amount estimated under that subsection:

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (a) the person who removed from British Columbia the timber or wood residue;

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (b) a person who, for compensation or reward, arranged or facilitated the removal from British Columbia of the timber or wood residue.

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (6) After assessing a person under subsection (4) or (5), the commissioner may assess the amount of interest payable under section 130 (1) (b) (iii) on the amount assessed.

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of this Part and section 130,

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (a) a fee in lieu estimated under subsection (1) is deemed to have been due on the date on which the permit was granted, and

heading: Assessment of estimated fee in lieu and interest
paragraph: (b) a fee in lieu estimated under subsection (2) is deemed to have been due on January 1 of the year in which the timber or wood residue referred to in that subsection was removed from British Columbia.

heading: Period to be considered in making an assessment
paragraph:
142.6
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), in making an assessment under section 142.51 (4) or 142.52 (4) or (5), the commissioner must not consider or include a period greater than 6 years before the date of issue of the first notice of assessment issued with respect to the timber or wood residue that is the subject of the assessment.

heading: Period to be considered in making an assessment
paragraph: (2) If an assessment under section 142.51 (4) or 142.52 (4) or (5) is based on one or more events that involve wilful default or fraud by a person, the commissioner may consider and include any period in making an assessment against the person under section 142.51 or 142.52, as applicable.

heading: Period to be considered in making an assessment
paragraph: (3) If a person referred to in section 142.51 (4) (a) or (b) files a document with the commissioner in a form and containing the information required by the commissioner within a period of 6 years from the date stumpage would have been due if none of the events referred to in section 142.51 (1) (a) to (d) had occurred, consenting to waive subsection (1) of this section and to allow the commissioner in making an assessment under section 142.51 to consider a different period, the commissioner may consider any period to which the person consents.

heading: Period to be considered in making an assessment
paragraph: (3.1) If a person referred to in section 142.52 (4) or (5) (a) or (b) files a document with the commissioner in a form and containing the information required by the commissioner within a period of 6 years from the date the fee in lieu referred to in section 142.52 (1) or (2), as applicable, is deemed to have been due under section 142.52 (7), consenting to waive subsection (1) of this section and to allow the commissioner in making an assessment under section 142.52 to consider a different period, the commissioner may consider any period to which the person consents.

heading: Period to be considered in making an assessment
paragraph: (4) A waiver filed under subsection (3) or (3.1) continues in effect for 6 months after the person files with the commissioner a notice revoking the waiver in the form and containing the information required by the commissioner.

heading: Penalty
paragraph:
142.61
		  (1) If the commissioner is satisfied that an assessment against a person under section 142.51 (4) or 142.52 (4) or (5) is based on the person's wilful

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (a) contravention of this Act, the regulations or an agreement entered into under this Act, or

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (b) provision of a false or deceptive statement,

heading: Penalty
paragraph: the commissioner may assess against the person, in addition to any other penalty, a penalty that does not exceed 100% of the assessment under that section.

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (2) If the commissioner is satisfied that an assessment against a person under section 142.51 (4) or 142.52 (4) or (5) is based on the person's contravention of this Act, the regulations or an agreement entered into under this Act, the commissioner may assess against the person, in addition to any other penalty, a penalty that does not exceed 25% of the assessment under that section.

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (3) If the commissioner assesses a penalty under subsection (1) against a person, the commissioner may not impose a penalty under subsection (2) with respect to the same assessment against that person.

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (4) After assessing a penalty against a person under subsection (1) or (2), the commissioner may do the following:

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (a) if the penalty is assessed in relation to an assessment made under section 142.51 (4), assess the amount of interest payable under section 130 (1) (b) (ii) on the amount assessed for the penalty;

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (b) if the penalty is assessed in relation to an assessment made under section 142.52 (4) or (5), assess the amount of interest payable under section 130 (1) (b) (iii) on the amount assessed for the penalty.

heading: Payment of assessed amount
paragraph:
142.7
		  In addition to any other money required to be paid to the government in the circumstances set out in section 130 (1.1), a person assessed under any of the following provisions must pay to the government the amount assessed under that provision:

heading: Payment of assessed amount
paragraph: (a) section 142.51 (4) or (5);

heading: Notice of assessment
paragraph:
142.71
		  After making an assessment under a provision referred to in section 142.7 (a) to (c), the commissioner must serve on the person assessed a notice of assessment that sets out the amount assessed under the provision.

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph:
142.8
		  (1) A notice of assessment required to be served on a person under section 142.71 must be served in one of the following ways:

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (a) by leaving the notice of assessment with the person;

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (b) by sending the notice of assessment

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (i)  by ordinary mail or registered mail to the person's address,

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (ii)  by electronic mail to the person's electronic mail address, or

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (iii)  by facsimile to the person's facsimile number

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: as last known to the commissioner.

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (2) A notice of assessment served in accordance with subsection (1) (b) is deemed to have been received on the date the notice of assessment was sent.

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (3) If a person carries on business under a name or style other than the person's own name, the notice of assessment may be addressed to the name or style under which the person carries on business and, in the case of leaving the notice of assessment with a person, the notice of assessment is deemed to have been validly served if left with an adult person employed at the place of business of the addressee.

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (4) If persons carry on business in partnership, the notice of assessment may be addressed to the partnership name and, in the case of leaving the notice of assessment with a person, the notice of assessment is deemed to have been validly served if left with one of the partners or left with an adult person employed at the place of business of the partnership.

heading: Serving a notice of assessment
paragraph: (5) Proof of the receipt by a person of the notice of assessment may be established in any court by showing that the notice of assessment was sent in accordance with this section, and the burden of proof is on the person seeking to establish the fact that the notice of assessment was not received by that person.

heading: Proof and onus
paragraph:
142.81
		  (1) Evidence that an assessment has been made under a provision referred to in section 142.7 (a) to (c) is proof, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, that the amount assessed is due and owing in accordance with the notice of assessment referred to in section 142.71, and the onus of proving otherwise is on the person liable to pay the amount assessed.

heading: Proof and onus
paragraph: (2) Subject to being amended, changed or varied on appeal under this Part, an amount assessed under a provision referred to in section 142.7 (a) to (c) is valid and binding despite any error, defect or omission in the estimate or assessment or in procedure.

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph:
142.9
		  (1) If a person disputes an assessment made under any of the following provisions, the person or the person's agent may appeal to the revenue minister in accordance with this section:

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (a) section 142.42 (1);

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (b) section 142.51 (4) or (5);

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (2) An appeal under this section may be commenced by serving a notice of appeal on the revenue minister within 90 days of the date that the notice of assessment referred to in section 142.71 is served on the appellant.

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (3) The notice of appeal must

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (a) be in writing,

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (b) be addressed to the revenue minister in the City of Victoria, and

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (c) set out clearly the reasons for the appeal and all the facts relevant to it.

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (4) On receiving the notice of appeal, the revenue minister must

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (a) consider the matter,

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (b) affirm, amend, change or vary the assessment or penalty, and

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (c) promptly notify the appellant in writing of the result of the appeal.

heading: Appeal to revenue minister
paragraph: (5) The revenue minister may, in writing and with or without conditions, delegate any of the revenue minister's powers, functions or duties under this section to a person or a class of persons.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph:
142.91
		  (1) A decision of the revenue minister under section 142.9 may be appealed to the Supreme Court by way of a petition proceeding.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (2) The Supreme Court Civil Rules relating to petition proceedings apply to appeals under this section, but Rule 18-3 of those rules does not apply.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (3) A petition commencing an appeal under this section must be filed in the court registry within 90 days of the date of the revenue minister's notification of the result of the appeal.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (4) Within 14 days of the filing of a petition under subsection (3), the petition must be served on the government in accordance with section 8 of the Crown Proceeding Act and in the petition the government must be designated "Her Majesty the Queen in right of the Province of British Columbia".

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (5) An appeal under this section is a new hearing that is not limited to the evidence and issues that were before the revenue minister.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (6) The Supreme Court may

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (a) dismiss the appeal,

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (b) allow the appeal,

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (c) vary the decision from which the appeal is made, or

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (d) refer the decision back to the commissioner for reconsideration.

heading: Affect of pending appeals
paragraph: 142.92		  Neither the serving of a notice of appeal by a person nor a delay in the hearing of the appeal

heading: Affect of pending appeals
paragraph: (a) affects the date of payment, the interest or penalties or the liability for payment in respect of the assessment that is the subject matter of the appeal, or

heading: Affect of pending appeals
paragraph: (b) delays collection of the assessment.

heading: Part 12 does not apply
paragraph:
142.921
		  Part 12 does not apply to an appeal under this Division.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph:
142.93
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: "authorized person" means a person who is engaged or employed, or was formerly engaged or employed, by or on behalf of the government, to assist in carrying out Part 11.1 of this Act;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: "confidential information" means information of any kind and in any form, relating to one or more persons,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) that is obtained for the purposes of Part 11.1 of this Act by or on behalf of the revenue minister, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) that is prepared from information referred to in paragraph (a),

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: but does not include information that does not directly or indirectly reveal the identity of the person to whom the information relates;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: "official" means any person

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) who is employed in the service of, is engaged by or on behalf of, or occupies a position of responsibility in the service of the government of British Columbia, another province or Canada, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) who was formerly so employed or engaged or formerly occupied such a position;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: "police officer" means a police officer as defined in section 462.48 (17) of the Criminal Code;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: "US state official" means any person

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) who is employed in the service of, is engaged by or on behalf of, or occupies a position of responsibility in the service of the government of a state of the United States of America, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) who was formerly so employed or engaged or formerly occupied such a position.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (2) Despite any other enactment or law, except as authorized by this section, an official must not

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) knowingly provide, or knowingly allow to be provided, any confidential information to any person,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) knowingly allow any person to have access to any confidential information, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (c) knowingly use any confidential information otherwise than in the course of the administration and enforcement of this Act or for a purpose for which it was provided under this section.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (3) Despite any other enactment or law, an official must not be required, in connection with any legal proceedings, to give or produce evidence relating to any confidential information.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (4) Subsections (2) and (3) do not apply in relation to the following:

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) criminal proceedings that have been commenced by the laying of an information or the preferring of an indictment under an Act of the Parliament of Canada;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) any legal proceedings relating to the administration or enforcement of any enactment of British Columbia, another province or Canada that provides for the imposition or collection of a tax or duty.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), an official may do one or more of the following:

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) provide to any person confidential information that can reasonably be considered necessary for the purposes of the administration or enforcement of this Act or another Act administered by the minister, solely for those purposes;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) provide to any person confidential information that can reasonably be considered necessary for the purposes of determining

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (i)  any interest, penalty or other amount that is or may become payable by the person under this Act,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (ii)  any refund to which the person is or may become entitled under this Act, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (iii)  any other amount that is relevant for the purposes of a determination under subparagraph (i) or (ii);

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (c) provide confidential information as follows:

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (i)  to an official of the Department of Finance of the government of Canada, solely for the purposes of the formulation or evaluation of fiscal policy;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (ii)  to an official solely for the purposes of the initial implementation of a fiscal policy;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (iii)  to an official of the ministry of the minister, solely for the purposes of the formulation or evaluation of policy;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (iv)  to an official of the ministry of the revenue minister, solely for the purposes of the formulation or evaluation of fiscal policy;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (v)  to an official solely for the purposes of the administration or enforcement of an enactment of British Columbia that provides for the imposition or collection of a tax or duty;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (vi)  to an official solely for the purposes of the administration or enforcement of an Act of the Parliament of Canada, or an enactment of another province, that provides for the imposition or collection of a tax or duty;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (vii)  to an official solely for the purposes of the compilation of statistical information by the government or the government of Canada, as the case may be;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (viii)  to an official solely for the purposes of setting off, against any sum of money that may be due or payable by the government, a debt due to the government;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (d) provide confidential information to a US state official solely for the purposes of the administration or enforcement of an enactment of a state of the United States of America that provides for the imposition or collection of a tax or duty;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (e) provide confidential information, or allow inspection of or access to confidential information, as the case may be, under, and solely for the purposes of,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (i)  sections 44 (1) and 61 (1) of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (ii)  sections 15, 16 and 17 of the Auditor General Act;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (f) provide confidential information as provided for in, or ordered under, section 239 or 242 of the Family Law Act or section 8.2 or 9 of the Family Maintenance Enforcement Act;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (g) provide confidential information relating to a person

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (i)  to the person, and

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (ii)  with the consent of the person, to any other person;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (h) use confidential information to compile information in a form that does not directly or indirectly reveal the identity of the person to whom the information relates;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (i) provide confidential information solely for the purposes of sections 17, 18 and 19 of the Financial Administration Act;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (j) use, or provide to any person, confidential information solely for a purpose relating to the supervision, evaluation or discipline of an authorized person by the government in respect of a period during which the authorized person was employed by, or engaged by or on behalf of, the government to assist in the administration or enforcement of this Act, to the extent that the information is relevant for the purpose;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (k) provide confidential information to a police officer, solely for the purposes of an investigation into whether an offence has been committed under the Criminal Code, or the laying of an information or the preferring of an indictment, if

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (i)  the confidential information can reasonably be considered necessary for the purpose of ascertaining, with respect to an official, or with respect to any person related to the official,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (A) the circumstances in which an offence under the Criminal Code may have been committed, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (B) the identity of the person who may have committed an offence under the Criminal Code,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (ii)  the official was or is engaged in the administration or enforcement of this Act, and

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (iii)  the offence can reasonably be considered to be related to the administration or enforcement of this Act;

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (l) provide confidential information to, or allow inspection of or access to confidential information by, any person otherwise legally entitled to the information under a prescribed enactment of British Columbia, solely for the purposes for which the person is entitled to the information.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (6) Except in accordance with an information-sharing agreement entered into under section 142.931, an official must not, under subsection (5) (a) to (d) and (i) to (l) of this section, provide confidential information to, or allow inspection of or access to confidential information by,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) an official of a public body, as defined in the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, other than the ministry of the revenue minister,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) an official of the government of Canada,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (c) an official of the government of another province, or

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (d) a US state official.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (7) An official may provide to appropriate persons any confidential information relating to imminent danger of death or physical injury to any individual.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (8) The person who presides at a legal proceeding relating to the supervision, evaluation or discipline of an authorized person may make orders necessary to ensure that confidential information is not used or provided to any person for any purpose unrelated to the proceeding, including

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (a) an order that the proceeding be held in private,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (b) an order banning publication of the confidential information,

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (c) an order to conceal the identity of the person to whom the confidential information relates, and

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (d) an order sealing the records of the proceeding.

heading: Information sharing
paragraph: (9) To the extent of any inconsistency or conflict with section 32 or 33 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, this section applies despite that Act.

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: 142.931		  (1) In this section:

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: "confidential information" has the same meaning as in section 142.93;

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: "information-sharing agreement" means an agreement or arrangement to exchange, by electronic data transmission, electronic data matching or any other means, information for a purpose described in section 142.93 (5).

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (2) The revenue minister may enter into an information-sharing agreement with

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (a) a public body as defined in the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act,

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (b) the government of Canada or an agency of that government,

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (c) the government of a province or other jurisdiction in Canada or an agency of that government, or

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (d) the government of a state of the United States of America or an agency of that government.

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), confidential information obtained by the revenue minister under an information-sharing agreement may be used or disclosed only for the purposes for which it was obtained under the applicable agreement.

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not prevent

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (a) any confidential information obtained by the revenue minister under an information-sharing agreement with the government of Canada or an agency of that government from being used or disclosed for the purpose of administering and enforcing an enactment administered by the revenue minister that provides for the imposition or collection of a tax or duty, or

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (b) any confidential information obtained by the revenue minister under an information-sharing agreement from being used or disclosed for the purpose of administering and enforcing an Act of the Parliament of Canada that provides for the imposition or collection of a tax or duty.

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe terms and conditions to be included in the information-sharing agreements entered into by the revenue minister.

heading: Information-sharing agreements
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of section 142.93 (6), an information-sharing agreement entered into before the coming into force of this section is considered to be an information-sharing agreement entered into by the revenue minister under this section.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 142.94		  Without limiting Division 3 of Part 12, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting inspections and audits conducted by forest revenue officials;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the conduct of appeals to the revenue minister under this Part;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) prescribing one or more categories of records for the purpose of section 142.3;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) prescribing a class of persons and circumstances for the purpose of section 142.31 (3);

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting assessments under this Part;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (f) requiring a person to keep records or types of records for the purposes of this Act or a provision of this Act.

heading: Determination that may be reviewed
paragraph:
143
		  (1) A review of the following may be required under this Division:

heading: Determination that may be reviewed
paragraph: (a) a determination, an order or a decision of a timber sales manager under section 78;

heading: Determination that may be reviewed
paragraph: (b) a determination, an order or a decision of the minister under section 70 (4), 75, 76 (1), (2), (2.1) or (2.2), 76.1 (5), 77 (1), 78.1 or 112 (2) or (3);

heading: Determination that may be reviewed
paragraph: (c) an order made under section 75.02 (2) or (3) (b), unless the order specifies limits on the harvested volume respecting all of the forest licences in a timber supply area.

heading: Determination that may be reviewed
paragraph: (2) A review of the determinations, orders and decisions referred to in subsection (1) is to be conducted by a person authorized by the minister.

heading: Request for review
paragraph:
144
		  (1) If under the provisions referred to in section 143 (1) a determination, order or decision is made, the person

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (a) in respect of whom it is made, or

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (b) in respect of whose agreement it is made

heading: Request for review
paragraph: may request a review of the determination, order or decision by serving a request for review on the person responsible for conducting the review under section 143 (2).

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (2) The person must ensure that the request for review meets the content requirements of the regulations.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (3) The person must serve the request for review on the person responsible for conducting the review under section 143 (2) not later than 3 weeks after the date the notice of determination, order or decision is served on the person.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (3.1) After the request for review is served under subsection (1), the person requesting the review and the government must disclose the facts and law on which the person or government will rely at the review if required by the regulations and in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (4) Before or after the time limit in subsection (3) expires, the person responsible for conducting the review under section 143 (2) may extend it.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: (5) A person who does not serve the request for review within the time required under subsection (3) or (4) loses the right to require a review.

heading: Powers on review
paragraph:
145
		  (1) The person responsible for conducting a review under section 143 (2) may decide the matter based on one or more of the following:

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (a) the request for review and a review of the ministry's files;

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (b) the request for review, the ministry's files and any other communication with persons that the person conducting the review considers necessary to decide the matter, including communication with the person requesting the review and with the person who made the determination, order or decision;

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (c) an oral hearing.

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for conducting the review may confirm, vary or rescind the determination, order or decision or refer it back to the person who made it, with or without directions.

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (3) A written decision must be served on the person who requested the review within

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (a) the prescribed period after the request for review was received by the person responsible for conducting the review under section 143 (2), or

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (b) another period agreed to by the person who requested the review and the government.

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), if the person conducting the review determines that the request for review does not comply with the content requirements of the regulations, or that there was a failure to disclose facts and law required under section 144 (3.1), the prescribed period referred to in subsection (3) of this section does not begin until a request for review that does comply with the content requirements of the regulations is served on the person conducting the review, or the facts and law are disclosed as required under section 144 (3.1).

heading: Powers on review
paragraph: (6) Unless the minister orders otherwise, a review of a determination, order or decision does not operate as a stay or suspend the operation of the determination, order or decision.

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph:
146
		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), an appeal may be made to the Forest Appeals Commission from a determination, order or decision that was the subject of a review required under Division 1 of this Part.

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph: (2) An appeal may be made to the Forest Appeals Commission from

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph: (a) a determination, order or decision of the chief forester, under section 68, 70 (2) or 112 (1), and

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph: (b) a determination of an employee of the ministry under section 105 (1).

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph: (3) No appeal may be made under subsection (1) unless the determination, order or decision has first been reviewed under Division 1 of this Part.

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph: (4) If a determination, order or decision referred to in subsection (1) is varied by the person conducting the review, the appeal to the commission is from the determination, order or decision as varied under section 145.

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph: (5) This Division does not apply to an appeal under the Forest and Range Practices Act in respect of a contravention of this Act or the regulations under this Act.

heading: Determinations that may be appealed
paragraph: (6) For the purpose of subsection (2), a redetermination or variation of stumpage rates under section 105 (1) is considered to be a determination.

heading: Part 8.1 of Forest and Range Practices Act applies
paragraph: 146.1		  Part 8.1 of the Forest and Range Practices Act applies to an appeal referred to in section 146 (1) or (2) of this Act.

heading: Parties to appeal
paragraph: 147		  (1) If a determination, order or decision referred to in section 146 (1) or (2) is made, the determination, order or decision may be appealed by the person

heading: Parties to appeal
paragraph: (a) in respect of whom it is made, or

heading: Parties to appeal
paragraph: (b) in respect of whose agreement it is made.

heading: Parties to appeal
paragraph: (2) Only the appellant and the government are parties to the appeal.

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph:
149
		  (1) On an appeal, whether or not the person who conducted the review confirmed, varied or rescinded the determination, order or decision being appealed, the commission may consider the findings of

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph: (a) the person who made the initial determination, order or decision, and

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph: (b) the person who conducted the review.

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph: (2) On an appeal, the commission may

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph: (a) confirm, vary or rescind the determination, order or decision, or

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph: (b) refer the matter back to the person who made the initial determination, order or decision with or without directions.

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph: (3) If the commission decides an appeal of a determination made under section 105, the commission must, in deciding the appeal, apply the policies and procedures approved by the minister under section 105 that were in effect at the time of the initial determination.

heading: Powers of commission
paragraph: (6) Unless the minister orders otherwise, an appeal under this Division does not operate as a stay or suspend the operation of the determination, order or decision under appeal.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph:
149.2
		  If it appears that a person has failed to comply with an order or decision of the commission or a member of it, the commission, minister or appellant may apply to the Supreme Court for an order

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (a) directing the person to comply with the order or decision, and

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (b) directing the directors and officers of the person to cause the person to comply with the order or decision.

heading: Forest and Range Practices Act applies to contravention appeals
paragraph:
150.1
		  Division 4 of Part 6 of the Forest and Range Practices Act applies to a correction, review or appeal under the Forest and Range Practices Act in respect of a contravention of this Act or the regulations under this Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 151		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (1.01) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting any matter for which regulations are contemplated by this Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (1.02) The authority to make regulations under another provision of this Act does not limit subsection (1), (1.01) or (1.1).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (1.1) In making a regulation under this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may do one or more of the following:

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) delegate a matter to a person;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) confer a discretion on a person;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) make different regulations for different persons, places, things, circumstances or transactions;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) adopt the provisions of a publication or adopt them as they are amended from time to time;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (e) adopt by reference, in whole or in part and with any changes considered appropriate by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, a regulation, code, standard or rule

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i)  enacted as or under a law of a jurisdiction in Canada, or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii)  set by a provincial, national or international body or any other body that makes codes, standards or rules.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (1.2) Unless stated otherwise, a regulation, code, standard or rule referred to in subsection (1.1) (e) is adopted as amended from time to time.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting any or all of the following:

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a.1) for the purpose of the definition of "allowable annual cut available" in section 1 (1), specifying the criteria, circumstances, rules, methods or formulas to be used in relation to

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i)  the reservations, deletions or reductions respecting a tree farm licence,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii)  the reservations or reductions respecting a community forest agreement, and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (iii)  the reservations or reductions respecting a first nations woodland licence;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a.2) authorizing the minister to enter into agreements with one or more tree farm licence holders to offset, in whole or in part, a reduction under section 3 (3) of the Forestry Revitalization Act, or a reservation referred to in section 35 (1) (h) of this Act, with a deletion of Crown land from the tree farm licence area under section 39.1 of this Act;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b.1) for the purposes of section 1.1 (1) (a), specifying which powers and duties of the minister under this Act must not be delegated;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b.2) for the purposes of section 8.1,

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (i)  prescribing the formulas or methods to be used to adjust the allowable annual cut, and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (ii)  prescribing additional circumstances in respect of which the allowable annual cut is adjusted;

heading: Regulations

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph:
152
		  In this section and sections 153 to 162:

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "contract" has a meaning corresponding to the definition of "contractor" below;

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "contractor" means a person who has an agreement with the holder of a forest licence, timber licence or tree farm licence to carry out one or more aspects of the holder's timber harvesting operations under the licence, and includes "person under contract" as defined by the regulations;

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "replaceable contract" means a contract

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (a) that includes a requirement that the holder of the forest licence, timber licence or tree farm licence, as the case may be, by a prescribed time before expiry of the existing contract, must, if the contractor has satisfactorily performed the existing contract up to the time of the offer, make an offer to the contractor, conditional on the contractor continuing to satisfactorily perform the existing contract, of a replacement contract that

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (i)  provides for payment to the contractor of the amounts agreed by the parties, or failing agreement, of the amounts settled by the method of dispute resolution provided under the existing contract at the time of the offer, and

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (ii)  subject to a requirement as to length of term prescribed under section 157 (d) (ii), is otherwise on substantially the same terms and conditions as the existing contract, and

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (b) that conforms to the requirements for replaceable contracts prescribed under section 157;

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "replaceable forest licence" means a forest licence for which the minister must make an offer of replacement, as set out in section 15;

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "replaceable subcontract" means a subcontract

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (a) that includes a requirement that the contractor, by a prescribed time before expiry of the existing subcontract, must, if the subcontractor has satisfactorily performed the existing subcontract up to the time of the offer, make an offer to the subcontractor, conditional on the subcontractor continuing to satisfactorily perform the existing subcontract, of a replacement subcontract that

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (i)  provides for payment to the subcontractor of the amounts agreed by the parties, or failing agreement, of the amounts settled by the method of dispute resolution provided under the existing subcontract at the time of the offer, and

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (ii)  subject to a requirement as to length of term prescribed under section 157 (d) (ii), is otherwise on substantially the same terms and conditions as the existing subcontract, and

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: (b) that conforms to the requirements for replaceable subcontracts prescribed under section 157;

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "replaceable tree farm licence" means a tree farm licence for which the minister must make an offer of replacement, as set out in section 36;

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "subcontract" has a meaning corresponding to the definition of "subcontractor" below;

heading: Interpretation for sections 152 to 162
paragraph: "subcontractor" means a person who has an agreement with a contractor to carry out one or more aspects of the contractor's responsibilities to the holder of the forest licence, timber licence or tree farm licence, as the case may be.

heading: Requirement for written contracts and subcontracts
paragraph:
153

heading: Requirement for written contracts and subcontracts

heading: Requirement for written contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (ii)  a contractor who enters into a subcontract

paragraph: to do so only by a written contract or written subcontract, as the case may be, and

heading: Requirement for written contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (b) requiring the parties to a contract or subcontract that is not in writing to exert their best efforts to convert the contract or subcontract into a written one.

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts
paragraph:

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (i)  the subcontractor's interest is assignable to another person with the consent of the contractor who is the other party to the subcontract, and

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (ii)  consent of the contractor to the assignment must not be unreasonably withheld, or

heading: Assignability of contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (c) prescribing, for use in contracts or subcontracts, standard provisions representing the requirements prescribed under paragraph (a) or  (b).

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph:
155
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting mediation and arbitration of all or certain disputes that have arisen or may arise between the parties to a contract or subcontract, including, but not limited to, regulations

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (a) establishing a system of mediation and arbitration and making the system applicable to

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (i)  contracts, or

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (ii)  subcontracts

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: that do not make any provision or do not make adequate provision for mediation and arbitration,

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (b) respecting contracts to which or subcontracts to which the system of mediation and arbitration established under this section is made applicable, including, but not limited to, regulations prescribing the following types of requirements for those contracts or subcontracts:

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (i)  requirements under which the parties to the contract or subcontract, as the case may be, are obliged, under the system of mediation and arbitration established under this section, to settle by mediation, and in the event of unsuccessful mediation, by arbitration,

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (A) all disputes, or

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (B) certain disputes as specified by regulation

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: that have arisen or may arise between the parties under the contract or subcontract;

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (ii)  requirements under which the parties to the contract or subcontract, as the case may be, must select the mediators and arbitrators to be used in the settlement of disputes under the contract or subcontract only from the Register of Timber Harvesting Contract Mediators and Arbitrators established under section 156,

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (c) prescribing, for use in contracts or subcontracts, standard provisions representing the requirements prescribed under paragraph (b) (i) and (ii),

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (d) prescribing what constitutes making "adequate provision" for the purposes of paragraph (a), and

heading: Mediation and arbitration under contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (e) adopting by reference for the purpose of the system of mediation and arbitration established under this section any provisions of the Arbitration Act, either without variation or with variations that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers necessary or desirable.

heading: Register of Timber Harvesting Contract Mediators and Arbitrators
paragraph: 156		  For the purpose of implementing a system of mediation and arbitration established under section 155, the minister may

heading: Register of Timber Harvesting Contract Mediators and Arbitrators
paragraph: (a) establish and maintain a Register of Timber Harvesting Contract Mediators and Arbitrators,

heading: Register of Timber Harvesting Contract Mediators and Arbitrators
paragraph: (b) enter in the register the names of at least 9 individuals whom the minister considers qualified to mediate or arbitrate disputes under contracts and subcontracts, and

heading: Register of Timber Harvesting Contract Mediators and Arbitrators
paragraph: (c) amend the register from time to time by removing names or by adding the names of individuals the minister considers qualified to mediate or arbitrate disputes under contracts and subcontracts.

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph:
157
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (a) requiring the holder of a timber licence, replaceable forest licence or replaceable tree farm licence who enters into a contract, including a replacement contract, to do so only by means of a replaceable contract,

paragraph: (a.1) despite paragraph (a), permitting the holder of a timber licence, replaceable forest licence or replaceable tree farm licence who enters into a contract to agree in writing with the intended contractor that the contract is not a replaceable contract,

paragraph: (b) requiring the holder of a replaceable contract who enters into a subcontract, including a replacement subcontract, to do so only by means of a replaceable subcontract,

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (d) respecting replaceable contracts and replaceable subcontracts, including, but not limited to, regulations prescribing the following types of requirements for replaceable contracts or for replaceable subcontracts:

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (i)  requirements governing the length of the term of

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (A) replaceable contracts, or

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (B) replaceable subcontracts

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: that are made after the effective date of the regulation prescribing the requirements referred to in this subparagraph;

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (ii)  requirements governing the commencement and length of the term of the replacement contract or replacement subcontract, as the case may be, that must be offered under an offer referred to in

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (A) paragraph (a) of the definitions in section 152 of "replaceable contract" and "replaceable subcontract", or

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (B) section 158;

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (iii)  requirements respecting the respective rights of the parties to the replaceable contracts or replaceable subcontracts in the event of contingencies not under the control of either party, including, but not limited to,

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (A) a reduction in allowable annual cut under the forest licence, timber licence or tree farm licence to which the replaceable contract or replaceable subcontract pertains, or

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (B) a change in harvesting methods that is approved or required by the government or a licence holder under the forest licence, timber licence or tree farm licence to which the replaceable contract or replaceable subcontract pertains;

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (iv)  requirements relating to the amount of work to be allocated to and performed by a contractor or subcontractor;

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (v)  requirements relating to the replacement of contracts or subcontracts on the transfer, subdivision or consolidation of licences and the replacement of subcontracts on the transfer of contracts;

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (vi)  requirements relating to the determination of rates under contracts and subcontracts;

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (vii)  requirements relating to the operational and commercial terms of contracts and subcontracts,

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (e) prescribing,

heading: Requirements for replaceable contracts and subcontracts
paragraph: (i)  for use in contracts made by holders of timber licences, replaceable forest licences or replaceable tree farm licences with contractors, a standard provision representing the requirement referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition of "replaceable contract" in section 152,

paragraph: (ii)  for use in subcontracts made by contractors described in subparagraph (i) with subcontractors, a standard provision representing the requirement referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition of "replaceable subcontract" in section 152, and

paragraph: (iii)  for use in replaceable contracts or replaceable subcontracts, standard provisions representing any of the requirements prescribed under paragraph (d) (i) to (vii) of this section,

heading: Agreement to make a replaceable contract or subcontract non-replaceable
paragraph:
157.1
		  (1) Despite section 160 or a regulation under section 157, the Lieutenant Governor in Council by regulation

heading: Agreement to make a replaceable contract or subcontract non-replaceable
paragraph: (a) may permit the holder of a licence and the contractor who are the parties to a replaceable contract pertaining to the licence to amend the replaceable contract by written agreement to provide that it is not replaceable, and

paragraph: (b) may permit the holder of a replaceable contract and the subcontractor who are the parties to a replaceable subcontract pertaining to the replaceable contract to amend the replaceable subcontract by written agreement to provide that it is not replaceable.

heading: Agreement to make a replaceable contract or subcontract non-replaceable

heading: Agreement to make a replaceable contract or subcontract non-replaceable

paragraph: (4) A regulation under subsection (1) (a) granting permission to amend a replaceable contract by written agreement to provide that it is not replaceable does not affect any rights, against the contractor or another person, of a subcontractor who has a replaceable subcontract with the contractor pertaining to the contract.

paragraph: (3) On and after the effective date of an amendment permitted by regulation under subsection (1) (b), the specified provisions of the regulations that are the subject of the amendment do not apply in respect of the subcontract.

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph:
158
		  (1) If a contract between the holder of a timber licence, replaceable forest licence or replaceable tree farm licence and a contractor expired or expires, or was or is wrongfully terminated by the holder, on or after January 25, 1991 but before the end of September 30, 1991, and

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: (a) the parties to the contract have not, by the end of September 30, 1991, entered into a new contract on substantially the same terms and conditions as those of the expired contract or on other terms and conditions agreed by the parties, and

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: (b) the contractor satisfactorily performed the contractor's obligations under the expired contract,

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: then, on or before October 15, 1991 or a later date that, on application by the holder, the minister may specify by order, the holder of the licence must make an offer to the contractor of a replacement contract that

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: (c) provides for payment to the contractor of the amounts agreed by the parties or, failing agreement, of the amounts settled by mediation and arbitration under the system established under section 155,

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: (d) subject to a requirement as to length of term prescribed under section 157 (d) (ii), is otherwise on substantially the same terms and conditions as the expired or terminated contract, and

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: (2) In the absence of agreement between the parties to an expired or terminated contract referred to in subsection (1) as to whether the contractor satisfactorily performed the contractor's obligations under the expired or terminated contract

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: (a) the parties must settle that issue by mediation and arbitration under the system established under section 155, and

heading: Special provision for certain expired contracts
paragraph: (b) the time within which the holder of the licence must offer a replacement contract under subsection (1) is extended to a date 15 days after the settlement of that issue.

heading: Fines
paragraph:

heading: Fines

heading: Fines
paragraph: (4) A person who contravenes section 90 (1) or (2), 96 (1), 124 (1), 125 or 132 (2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 6 months or to both.

paragraph: (5) A person who contravenes section 86 (1) or (2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 6 months or to both.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (6) A person who contravenes section 136.1 (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $2 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 6 months or to both.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (7) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide by regulation that

heading: Fines
paragraph: (a) a contravention of a regulation is an offence, and

heading: Fines
paragraph: (b) a person convicted of an offence for a contravention of a regulation is liable to a fine not exceeding a maximum amount or to imprisonment not exceeding a maximum amount or to both.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (8) If the maximum fine or imprisonment provided by a regulation under subsection (7) (b) is less than that provided by a provision of this Act, the regulation prevails.

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph:
163.1
		  (1) In this section, "person acting in an official capacity" means an individual who is

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (a) employed under the Public Service Act, and

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (b) is exercising a power or performing a duty or function under this Act.

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (2) A person must not

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (a) without lawful excuse, intentionally interfere with a person acting in an official capacity,

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (b) without lawful excuse, intentionally not comply with a lawful requirement of a person acting in an official capacity, or

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (c) intentionally make a false statement to, or mislead or attempt to mislead a person acting in an official capacity.

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: 164		  (1) A person must not

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (a) by intimidation or threat hinder or prevent a person from making an application for an agreement, or from submitting a tender or bid, under Part 3,

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (b) for an improper purpose threaten to make an application for an agreement, or to submit a tender or bid, under Part 3, or

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (c) participate in or be a party to an agreement or arrangement among 2 or more persons, under which

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (i)  one or more of the persons agrees or undertakes not to make an application for an agreement, or to submit a tender or bid, under Part 3, or

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (ii)  particulars in an application made for an agreement, or the amount of a tender or bid submitted, under Part 3, by one or more of the persons are decided.

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph:
(2) 
              Subsection (1) (c) does not apply to

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (a) an agreement or arrangement made only among 2 or more corporations that are affiliated within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act, or

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (b) an application for an agreement under this Act made jointly by 2 or more persons.

heading: Part 3 offence
paragraph: (3) A person who is convicted of an offence under subsection (1), and a corporation controlled by that person, is disqualified from making an application under Part 3, either on the person's own application or through an agent, for 2 years after the date of the person's conviction.

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: 164.01		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (a) contravenes section 142.93 (2), or

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (b) knowingly contravenes an order made under section 142.93 (8).

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (a) the person has been provided with confidential information for a particular purpose under section 142.93 (5) (a) to (c), (e), (f), (i), (j) or (l), and

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (b) the person knowingly, for a purpose other than the purpose referred to in paragraph (a), uses the information, provides the information or allows the information to be provided to any person or allows any person to access the information.

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (3) A person who commits an offence under subsection (1) or (2) is liable on conviction to one or both of the following:

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (a) a fine of not more than $5 000;

heading: Offences in relation to confidential information
paragraph: (b) imprisonment for not more than 12 months.

heading: Cancellation and disqualification
paragraph:
164.1
		  (1) In this section, "official" means an official designated by the minister.

heading: Cancellation and disqualification
paragraph: (2) If, after giving a person an opportunity to be heard, an official determines that the person has contravened any of paragraphs (a) to (c) of section 164 (1), the official may do either or both of the following:

heading: Cancellation and disqualification
paragraph: (a) cancel an agreement referred to in section 12 that is held by or on behalf of the person, if the official believes on reasonable grounds that the person, in relation to the agreement, derived or could have derived any benefit as a result of the contravention;

heading: Cancellation and disqualification
paragraph: (b) disqualify the person from making an application under Part 3 or 3.1, either on the person's own application or through an agent, for not more than 10 years.

heading: Cancellation and disqualification
paragraph: (3) If, under subsection (2), an official determines that a corporation has contravened any of paragraphs (a) to (c) of section 164 (1), a person who is an officer, director or agent of the corporation is subject to the consequences described in subsection (2) if, after giving the person an opportunity to be heard, an official determines that the person authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention.

heading: Prohibition against restricting competition in sale or purchase of logs
paragraph:
165.1
		  (1) In this section, "timber" means timber harvested under an agreement referred to in section 12 and offered by or on behalf of the holder for sale as logs.

heading: Prohibition against restricting competition in sale or purchase of logs
paragraph: (2) A person must not conspire, combine, agree or arrange with another person to prevent, limit or lessen competition in the purchase or sale of timber

heading: Prohibition against restricting competition in sale or purchase of logs
paragraph: (a) by arriving at a maximum amount to be paid by the person or persons for the timber,

heading: Prohibition against restricting competition in sale or purchase of logs
paragraph: (b) by implementing a strategy in relation to the purchase or sale of the timber, or

heading: Prohibition against restricting competition in sale or purchase of logs
paragraph: (c) by another method.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph:
165.2
		  A proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under this Act does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Officers of corporation
paragraph:
166
		  If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence and, despite that the corporation is convicted, is liable on conviction to fine and imprisonment.

heading: Defences to a prosecution
paragraph:
167.1
		  Due diligence, mistake of fact and officially induced error are defences to a prosecution under this Act.

heading: Section 5 of the Offence Act
paragraph:
167.2
		  Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Part 6 of the Forest and Range Practices Act applies
paragraph: 167.3		  (1) Divisions 1 to 3 of Part 6 of the Forest and Range Practices Act apply to this Act and the regulations under this Act, unless the context indicates otherwise.

heading: Definition
paragraph: 168		  In this Part:

heading: Definition
paragraph: "agreement" means an agreement in the form of a licence, permit or agreement referred to in section 12;

heading: Definition
paragraph: "designated area" means an area of Crown land specified under section 169 (1).

heading: Specifying Crown land as a designated area
paragraph:
169
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by regulation, may

heading: Specifying Crown land as a designated area
paragraph: (a) specify Crown land as a designated area, for a period set out in the regulation, if the Lieutenant Governor in Council believes it is in the public interest to specify the Crown land as a designated area, and

heading: Specifying Crown land as a designated area
paragraph: (2) The maximum period during which Crown land may continue as a designated area under regulations made under this section is 10 years, beginning on the day the Crown land first becomes a designated area.

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph:
170
		  (1) In this section, "issue" means issue, grant, enter into or approve.

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (2) If a permit, licence or plan referred to in subsection (3) relates to all or part of a designated area, the minister, by written order, may

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (a) suspend in whole or in part or vary the permit, licence or plan, or

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (b) direct a person who, under this Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act or the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act, has a discretion to issue the permit, licence or plan

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (i)  to not issue the permit, licence or plan, or

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (ii)  in whole or in part, to issue the permit, licence or plan with terms and conditions, if any, that the person considers appropriate to take into account the relationship of the permit, licence or plan to the designated area.

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (3) The following are the permits, licences or plans to which subsection (2) applies:

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (a) a cutting permit;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (b) a road permit or road use permit;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (c) a timber sale licence;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (d) a free use permit;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (e) a licence to cut;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (f) a special use permit;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (g) an operational plan;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (h) the management plan for an area-based licence or pulpwood agreement;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (i) a plan required under an agreement;

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (j) a plan relating to an agreement for the management, development or use of Crown land.

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (4) If a permit, licence or plan is suspended or varied under subsection (2) (a) and the Crown land to which the suspension or variation relates ceases to be a designated area, the minister may, by order,

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (a) restore the permit, licence or plan, in whole or in part, and

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (b) extend the term of the permit, licence or plan, as that permit, licence or plan relates to the area that has ceased to be a designated area.

heading: What is the effect of specifying a designated area?
paragraph: (4.1) The period of time by which the minister may extend the term of the permit, licence or plan under subsection (4) (b) must not exceed the period of time that remained on the term of the permit, licence or plan as at the effective date of the suspension or variation.
