heading: Interpretation - forest landscape plans and planning guidelines
paragraph: 2.01		  (1) For the purposes of this Act, a forest landscape plan applies to a forest operations plan if any portion of the forest operations area is within the forest landscape area.

heading: Interpretation - forest landscape plans and planning guidelines
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Act, a planning guideline applies to a forest operations plan if the forest landscape plan that includes the planning guideline applies to the forest operations plan.

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph:
2.1
		  (1) Subject to a regulation made under section 153 (3), this Act and the regulations and standards made under this Act apply to or in respect of a first nations woodland licence described in subsection (2) as if

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (a) the first nations woodland licence were a community forest agreement,

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (b) the first nations woodland licence area were a community forest agreement area, and

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (c) the holder of the first nations woodland licence were a holder of a community forest agreement.

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph:
(2) 
            Subsection (1) applies to or in respect of a first nations woodland licence if

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (a) the size of the Crown land in the first nations woodland licence area is more than

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (i)  800 ha, if the area is located in the Coast Forest Region, or

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (ii)  1200 ha, if the area is not located in the Coast Forest Region, or

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (b) the licence specifies that it is to be treated as if it were a community forest agreement for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (3) Subject to a regulation made under section 153 (3), this Act and the regulations and standards made under this Act apply to or in respect of a first nations woodland licence described in subsection (4) as if

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (a) the first nations woodland licence were a woodlot licence,

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (b) the first nations woodland licence area were a woodlot licence area, and

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (c) a holder of the first nations woodland licence were a holder of a woodlot licence.

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph:
(4) 
            Subsection (3) applies to or in respect of a first nations woodland licence if the size of the Crown land in the first nations woodland licence area is equal to or less than

paragraph: (a) 800 ha, if the area is located in the Coast Forest Region, or

paragraph: (b) 1200 ha, if the area is not located in the Coast Forest Region.

heading: Application of Act to first nations woodland licences
paragraph: (5) A woodlot licence plan for a first nations woodland licence to which subsection (3) applies expires on the date the size of the Crown land in the first nations woodland licence area increases from a size described in subsection (4) to a size described in subsection (2) (a).

paragraph:
2.2
		  (1) In this Part:

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (a) a forest licence;

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (b) a tree farm licence;

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (c) a community forest agreement if the community forest agreement area

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (i)  is located inside the Coast Forest Region and includes Crown land of more than 800 ha, or

paragraph: (ii)  is located outside the Coast Forest Region and includes Crown land of more than 1 200 ha;

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (d) a first nations woodland licence if the first nations woodland licence area

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (i)  is located inside the Coast Forest Region and includes Crown land of more than 800 ha, or

paragraph: (ii)  is located outside the Coast Forest Region and includes Crown land of more than 1 200 ha;

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (e) a timber licence;

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (f) a forestry licence to cut that is a major licence;

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: "Indigenous governing body" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation for Part 1.1
paragraph: (2) Despite section 2.1, that section does not apply to this Part.

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: 2.21		  (1) The chief forester may, by order, establish a forest landscape plan for the following land:

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: (a) Crown land;

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: (b) private land that is subject to an agreement under the Forest Act.

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: (2) Notice of an order establishing a forest landscape plan must be published in the Gazette.

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: (3) A forest landscape plan established by order of the chief forester takes effect on the later of the following:

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: (a) the date on which notice of the order is published in the Gazette;

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: (b) the date, if any, specified in the order as the effective date of the plan.

heading: Chief forester may establish forest landscape plan
paragraph: (4) A forest landscape plan does not apply in relation to a woodlot licence.

heading: Preparation of forest landscape plan
paragraph: 2.22		  The chief forester, in preparing a forest landscape plan, must consider the following objectives:

heading: Preparation of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (a) supporting the production and supply of timber in the forest landscape area;

heading: Preparation of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (b) supporting the protection and conservation of the environment;

heading: Preparation of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (c) managing the values placed on forest ecosystems by Indigenous peoples;

heading: Preparation of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (d) managing the values placed on forest ecosystems by local communities;

heading: Preparation of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (e) preventing, mitigating and adapting to impacts caused by significant disturbances to forests and forest health, including wildfire, insects, disease and drought.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous peoples
paragraph:
2.23
		  Before establishing a forest landscape plan, the chief forester must consult and cooperate with Indigenous peoples whose rights could be affected by the establishment of the forest landscape plan.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body
paragraph:
2.24
		  (1) For the purposes of section 2.23, the chief forester must, before preparing a forest landscape plan, provide notice to any Indigenous governing body that is authorized to act on behalf of Indigenous peoples whose rights could be affected by the establishment of the forest landscape plan.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body
paragraph: (2) On providing notice under subsection (1) to an Indigenous governing body, the chief forester must attempt to establish, with the Indigenous governing body, a process for consultation and cooperation in the preparation of the forest landscape plan.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body
paragraph: (3) If a process for consultation and cooperation is established under subsection (2) with an Indigenous governing body within 60 days of the provision of notice under subsection (1) to the Indigenous governing body, the chief forester must implement the process before establishing the forest landscape plan.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph:
2.25
		  (1) If a process for consultation and cooperation in the preparation of a forest landscape plan is not established under section 2.24 (2) with an Indigenous governing body referred to in that subsection within 60 days of the provision of notice, the chief forester must,

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (a) before preparing the forest landscape plan, provide the information proposed to be used by the chief forester for the purposes of preparing the forest landscape plan to the Indigenous governing body, and

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (b) on completing a proposed forest landscape plan, provide the proposed forest landscape plan to the Indigenous governing body.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (2) An Indigenous governing body may, within 60 days after receiving the information referred to in subsection (1) (a) or the proposed forest landscape plan referred to subsection (1) (b), provide comments to the chief forester.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (3) The chief forester must,

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (a) after considering any comments received from an Indigenous governing body under subsection (2), make the proposed forest landscape plan publicly available for review and comment, and

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (b) after considering any comments received from the public under paragraph (a), provide the proposed forest landscape plan to the Indigenous governing body.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (4) An Indigenous governing body may, within 60 days after receiving a proposed forest landscape plan under subsection (3) (b), provide notice to the chief forester of its consent or lack of consent to the proposed forest landscape plan.

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (5) The chief forester must

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (a) offer to meet with an Indigenous governing body that provides notice of its lack of consent under subsection (4), and

heading: Consultation and cooperation with Indigenous governing body if process not established
paragraph: (b) attempt to achieve consensus with the Indigenous governing body respecting the proposed forest landscape plan.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph:
2.26
		  (1) In this section, "facilitator" means an individual appointed under subsection (2).

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (2) If a dispute arises between the chief forester and an Indigenous governing body to which notice was provided under section 2.24 (1) relating to a matter described in section 2.25 (5) and the chief forester and the Indigenous governing body cannot resolve the dispute, the chief forester must appoint an individual to facilitate the resolution of the dispute.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (3) Before appointing a facilitator, the chief forester must consider any comments of the Indigenous governing body referred to in subsection (2) respecting the appointment.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (4) The chief forester must participate in a dispute resolution facilitation in respect of a dispute referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (5) A facilitator must provide a report on a completed dispute resolution facilitation to each participant.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (6) The chief forester must not take further action in respect of a decision or matter that is the subject of a dispute resolution facilitation until after the facilitator provides a report.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (7) A report of a facilitator does not limit the power of the chief forester in respect of the decision or matter that is the subject of the report.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (8) This section and section 2.27 do not apply in respect of a dispute between the chief forester and an Indigenous governing body if a process for consultation and cooperation referred to in section 2.24 (3) established with the Indigenous governing body provides for the resolution of disputes.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (9) This section and section 2.27 are not to be taken as limiting any right an Indigenous governing body may have to seek a remedy from a court.

heading: Dispute resolution facilitation
paragraph: (10) For certainty, this section and section 2.27 must be construed in accordance with section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Alternative dispute resolution process
paragraph: 2.27		  (1) Despite section 2.26, the chief forester and an Indigenous governing body to which notice is provided under section 2.24 (1) may agree to participate in an alternative dispute resolution process other than a dispute resolution facilitation referred to in section 2.26 if the participants are satisfied that the alternative dispute resolution process gives due consideration to the customs, traditions, rules and legal systems of the Indigenous governing body.

heading: Alternative dispute resolution process
paragraph: (2) The conclusion of an alternative dispute resolution process referred to in subsection (1) does not limit the power of the chief forester in respect of the decision or matter that was the subject of the alternative dispute resolution process.

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph:
2.28
		  (1) A forest landscape plan must include the following:

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (a) a map that shows the forest landscape area;

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (b) outcomes in relation to the objectives referred to in section 2.22;

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (c) a description of how the objectives referred to in section 2.22 were taken into consideration in establishing the outcomes referred to in paragraph (b) of this subsection.

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of achieving the outcomes referred to in subsection (1) (b), a forest landscape plan may include planning guidelines for forest operations plans in relation to one or more of the following matters:

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (a) areas in which new cutblocks or roads should not be located;

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (b) limits that should apply to the sizes or configurations of cutblocks;

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (c) requirements relating to forest practices, silvicultural systems or stocking standards that should be included in the forest operations plans.

heading: Content of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (3) A forest landscape plan must be consistent with any objectives established under section 93.4 of the Land Act.

heading: Term of forest landscape plans
paragraph: 2.29		  (1) The term of a forest landscape plan is 10 years.

heading: Term of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), when the term of a replacement forest landscape plan begins, the forest landscape plan that is being replaced ceases to apply to the forest landscape area of the replacement plan.

heading: Extension of forest landscape plan
paragraph:
2.3
		  (1) The chief forester may, by order, extend the term of a forest landscape plan on one or more occasions.

heading: Extension of forest landscape plan
paragraph: (2) Each extension under subsection (1) may be for a period of up to 5 years.

heading: Report on forest landscape plans
paragraph:
2.31
		  (1) In this section, "reporting period", in relation to a forest landscape plan, means each successive 5-year period during the term of the plan, beginning on the effective date of the plan.

heading: Report on forest landscape plans
paragraph: (2) Within 2 years after the end of a reporting period for a forest landscape plan, the chief forester must publish a report on a ministry website setting out the extent to which the outcomes identified in the plan have been achieved during the reporting period.

heading: Plans, studies, analyses and information
paragraph:
2.32
		  (1) The chief forester may, by order, for the purposes of preparing or amending a forest landscape plan or preparing a report under section 2.31 in relation to a forest landscape plan, require a person referred to in subsection (2) of this section to take one or more of the following actions, as the chief forester considers adequate:

heading: Plans, studies, analyses and information
paragraph: (a) prepare and submit to the chief forester plans, studies or analyses;

heading: Plans, studies, analyses and information
paragraph: (b) obtain and submit to the chief forester information.

heading: Plans, studies, analyses and information
paragraph: (2) The following persons may be the subject of an order under subsection (1):

heading: Plans, studies, analyses and information
paragraph: (a) the holder of an agreement that authorizes timber harvesting in the forest landscape area;

heading: Plans, studies, analyses and information
paragraph: (b) the holder of a forest operations plan to which the forest landscape plan applies or will apply, as applicable.

heading: Plans, studies, analyses and information
paragraph: (3) A plan, study or analysis or information required under subsection (1) must be prepared, submitted or obtained within the time and in the form and manner specified in the order.

heading: Notice of decisions in relation to forest landscape plans
paragraph:
2.33
		  (1) The chief forester must give notice to the holder of an agreement that grants rights to harvest timber in a forest landscape area if, in relation to the forest landscape plan, the chief forester makes an order that

heading: Notice of decisions in relation to forest landscape plans
paragraph: (a) amends the plan,

heading: Notice of decisions in relation to forest landscape plans
paragraph: (b) extends the term of the plan, or

heading: Notice of decisions in relation to forest landscape plans
paragraph: (c) cancels the plan.

heading: Notice of decisions in relation to forest landscape plans
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), if the holder of an agreement submits a forest operations plan or amendment for approval under Division 2 of this Part before the chief forester gives notice to the holder of an order under subsection (1), that Division applies to the submission for approval as though the order were not made.

heading: Notice of decisions in relation to forest landscape plans
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if the holder of the agreement waives the right to be given notice of the order.

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph:
2.34
		  (1) The chief forester must keep a record of each forest landscape plan and of each of the following, as applicable, that relates to the plan:

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (a) the order establishing the plan;

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (b) an order that

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (i)  amends the plan,

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (ii)  extends the term of the plan, or

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (iii)  cancels the plan;

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (c) a report published under section 2.31.

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (2) The chief forester must, in a manner the chief forester considers adequate, make available to a person on request a copy of each record referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (3) During the term of a forest landscape plan, the chief forester must publish on a ministry website

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (a) the plan, and

heading: Requirement to keep records of forest landscape plans
paragraph: (b) the records referred to in subsection (1) (a), (b) (i) and (ii) and (c) that relate to the plan.

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph:
2.35
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: "approved forest operations plan" means a forest operations plan that is approved by the minister;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: "forest landscape area" includes an area of land that was formerly a forest landscape area.

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) If land subject to an agreement is located inside a forest landscape area, the holder of the agreement must not do any of the following unless the holder holds an approved forest operations plan that applies to the land:

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) apply for a cutting permit to harvest timber on the land;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) apply for a road permit to construct a road on the land;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) harvest timber on the land;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) construct a road on the land.

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (3) A timber sales manager may not do any of the following in relation to land located inside a forest landscape area unless the timber sales manager holds an approved forest operations plan that applies to the land:

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) invite applications for, or enter into, a timber sale licence that grants rights to harvest timber on the land;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) issue to the holder of a timber sale licence a road permit to construct a road on the land;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) construct a road on the land for access to an area to be harvested under a timber sale licence.

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (4) The holder of an agreement is exempt from subsection (2) (c) and (d) if the holder harvests timber or constructs roads in an area of land that is subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued before

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) the expiry of a forest operations plan that applied to the area subject to the permit, or

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) the removal of the holder as a party to a forest operations plan that applied to the area subject to the permit.

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (5) The holder of an agreement is exempt from subsection (2) if the holder only does one or more of the following on land subject to the agreement:

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) harvests timber to eliminate a safety hazard;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) harvests timber to facilitate the collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) removes felled trees from landings and road rights of way;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) harvests timber not exceeding a volume of 500 m3 that, in the opinion of the minister,

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  is in danger of being significantly reduced in value, lost or destroyed, by insect infestation, fire or disease, or

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  has been treated or will be treated by the holder to facilitate the entrapment or elimination of pests;

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (e) harvests timber or constructs roads for a prescribed purpose.

heading: Forest operations plan
paragraph: (6) A timber sales manager is exempt from subsection (3) in prescribed circumstances.

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph:
2.36
		  (1) A forest operations plan must do the following:

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) specify the forest operations area;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) include requirements for the forest operations area in respect of forest practices, silvicultural systems and stocking standards;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) meet the prescribed requirements.

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) A forest operations plan held by the holder of an agreement must include a map, in a scale and form satisfactory to the minister, that shows the following:

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) the approximate location of each proposed cutblock that is to be the subject of a cutting permit that the holder intends to apply for during the term of the forest operations plan;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) the approximate location of each proposed road that is to be the subject of a road permit that the holder intends to apply for during the term of the forest operations plan;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) the location of each existing cutblock

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  that is within a prescribed distance of a proposed cutblock referred to in paragraph (a), and

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  in which the holder has harvested or started harvesting timber under the agreement;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) the location of each existing road

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  that is continuous to or within a prescribed distance of a proposed road referred to in paragraph (b), and

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  that has been constructed by the holder under a cutting permit or road permit or that is authorized under a cutting permit or road permit held by the holder;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (e) the location of each area that is subject to a cutting permit or road permit held by the holder of the agreement.

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (3) A forest operations plan held by a timber sales manager must include a map, in a scale and form satisfactory to the minister, that shows the following:

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) the approximate location of each proposed cutblock that the timber sales manager intends to include in timber sale licences for which the timber sales manager will invite applications during the term of the forest operations plan;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) the approximate location of each proposed road that the timber sales manager intends to construct during the term of the forest operations plan;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) the location of each area that is subject to a timber sale licence;

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) the location of each existing road that has been constructed for access to an area that is subject to a timber sale licence.

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of complying with subsection (1) (b), a forest operations plan may incorporate by reference a requirement described in a planning guideline that applies to the forest operations plan.

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (5) A requirement in a planning guideline that is incorporated by reference in a forest operations plan under subsection (4)

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) is deemed to be included in the forest operations plan, and

heading: Content of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) is incorporated as it read in the planning guideline on the date on which the forest operations plan is approved or amended to include the requirement, as applicable.

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph:
2.37
		  (1) If either of the following shown in a forest operations plan is inconsistent with a planning guideline under section 2.28 (2) (a) or (b) that applies to the forest operations plan, the forest operations plan must include a statement of the reasons for the inconsistency:

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph: (a) the location, size or configuration of a proposed cutblock;

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph: (b) the location of a proposed road.

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph: (2) If a forest operations plan does not include a requirement respecting forest practices, silvicultural systems or stocking standards described in a planning guideline under section 2.28 (2) (c) that applies to the forest operations plan, the forest operations plan must include one of the following:

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph: (a) a statement setting out why the requirement in the planning guideline is not included in the forest operations plan;

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph: (b) a substitution for the requirement in the planning guideline, together with a statement setting out

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph: (i)  why the substituted requirement is included in the forest operations plan, and

heading: Additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines
paragraph: (ii)  how the substituted requirement will achieve an outcome similar to the outcome to which the requirement in the planning guideline relates.

heading: Engagement on and review of forest operations plans
paragraph:
2.38
		  (1) A person must not submit to the minister for approval a forest operations plan or an amendment to a forest operations plan unless the person has done the following, in accordance with the regulations:

heading: Engagement on and review of forest operations plans
paragraph: (a) made reasonable efforts to engage with Indigenous nations affected by the plan;

heading: Engagement on and review of forest operations plans
paragraph: (b) made the plan publicly available for review and comment.

heading: Engagement on and review of forest operations plans
paragraph: (2) In submitting a forest operations plan or amendment to the minister for approval, the person submitting the plan or amendment must include the following:

heading: Engagement on and review of forest operations plans
paragraph: (a) a summary of the engagement referred to in subsection (1) (a) and a description of any changes made to the plan to address matters raised by Indigenous nations;

heading: Engagement on and review of forest operations plans
paragraph: (b) a summary of the public review and comment referred to in subsection (1) (b) and a description of any changes made to the plan to address comments received from the public.

heading: Engagement on and review of forest operations plans
paragraph: (3) If the minister requests a person to resubmit a forest operations plan or amendment to address changes requested by the minister, the minister may relieve the person from the requirements under subsections (1) and (2) for the purposes of resubmitting the plan or amendment.

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph:
2.39
		  (1) Subject to section 2.4, the minister may approve a forest operations plan or an amendment to a forest operations plan if satisfied of all of the following:

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (a) the plan or amendment meets the requirements set out in sections 2.36 and 2.37, as applicable;

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (b) the person who submitted the plan or amendment has complied with section 2.38 (1) and (2);

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (c) the person who submitted the plan or amendment has given sufficient consideration to

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (i)  matters raised by Indigenous nations during engagement under section 2.38 (1) (a), and

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (ii)  comments received from the public under section 2.38 (1) (b).

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the minister may, in approving a forest operations plan or amendment, impose a condition under section 112 (1) that the holder, by the date specified by the minister, deactivate a road authorized under a road permit or cutting permit held by the holder, including a road that is located outside of the forest operations area.

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (3) A condition under subsection (2) may be imposed only in prescribed circumstances.

heading: Approval of forest operations plans
paragraph: (4) Except to the extent provided in subsection (3), nothing in subsection (2) limits the discretion of the minister under section 112 to attach a condition to the approval of a forest operations plan or amendment.

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph:
2.4
		  (1) If a forest operations plan is inconsistent with a forest landscape plan, or would be inconsistent with a forest landscape plan as a result of an amendment to the forest operations plan, the minister may not approve the forest operations plan or amendment unless the minister is satisfied of all of the following:

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (a) the part of the forest operations plan or amendment that is inconsistent with the forest landscape plan nevertheless supports the outcomes included in the forest landscape plan;

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (b) the forest operations plan or amendment supports the proper management and conservation of forests and forest ecosystems;

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (c) the prescribed criteria, if any, are met.

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this section, a forest operations plan is deemed to be inconsistent with a forest landscape plan if any of the following applies:

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (a) a proposed cutblock is located in an area, or has a size or configuration, contrary to a planning guideline under section 2.28 (2) (a) or (b);

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (b) a proposed road is located in an area contrary to a planning guideline under section 2.28 (2) (a);

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (c) the forest operations plan does not include, under section 2.36 (1) (b), a requirement relating to forest practices, silvicultural systems or stocking standards that is described in a planning guideline under section 2.28 (2) (c).

heading: Approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not limit the circumstances in which a forest operations plan may be considered to be inconsistent with a forest landscape plan.

heading: Limited protection of certain roads and cutblocks
paragraph:
2.41
		  (1) A proposed forest operations plan or an amendment to a forest operations plan must be considered to have received the minister's approval under section 2.39 for the parts of the plan, if any, that relate to a cutting permit, road permit or timber sale licence that is in effect on the date on which the proposed forest operations plan is submitted for approval.

heading: Limited protection of certain roads and cutblocks
paragraph: (2) In prescribed circumstances, a forest operations plan or amendment must be considered to have received the minister's approval under section 2.39 for the parts of the plan that relate to prescribed matters or things.

heading: Term of forest operations plan
paragraph:
2.42
		  (1) The term of a forest operations plan

heading: Term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) is the period, not exceeding 5 years, that the person submitting the plan for approval specifies at the time of submission, and

heading: Term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) begins on the date specified in writing by the minister in approving the plan.

heading: Term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), when the term of a replacement forest operations plan begins, the forest operations plan that is being replaced ceases to apply to the forest operations area of the replacement plan.

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph:
2.43
		  (1) In this section, "original expiry date", in relation to a forest operations plan, means the date on which the term of the plan would expire if no extension were made under this section.

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the minister, by giving written notice to the holder of a forest operations plan, may extend the term of the plan as follows:

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) in prescribed circumstances, for a period of one year or less on one or more occasions;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) for a period of 2 years or less on one or more occasions if the minister considers that the government, before the plan expires, is unlikely to complete consultations with Indigenous nations in relation to a replacement forest operations plan.

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (3) The term of a forest operations plan may not be extended

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) under subsection (2) (a) to a date later than one year after the plan's original expiry date, and

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) under subsection (2) (b) to a date later than 2 years after the plan's original expiry date.

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (4) The term of a forest operations plan may be extended under this section before or after the plan expires.

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (5) A forest operations plan that is extended under this section may include changes to the extent provided in the regulations.

heading: Amendments to forest operations plan not effective unless approved
paragraph:
2.44
		  Unless the regulations provide otherwise, an amendment to a forest operations plan is not effective unless the amendment is approved by the minister under section 2.39.

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph:
2.45
		  (1) Unless the regulations provide otherwise, the holder of a forest operations plan must propose and submit, for approval by the minister under section 2.39 and in accordance with this section, an amendment to the plan if any of the following applies:

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) the area specified in the plan as the location of a proposed cutblock or proposed road is affected by an amendment to any of the following enactments:

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  this Act;

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  the regulations;

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (iii)  a prescribed enactment;

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) the holder is required by the regulations to propose and submit the amendment to the plan.

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) An amendment required under this section must address the following, as applicable:

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) an amendment to an enactment referred to in subsection (1) (a);

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) a regulation referred to in subsection (1) (b).

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (3) An amendment required under this section must be submitted within the following period, as applicable:

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) in the case of a plan amendment required under subsection (1) (a), the longer of

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  6 months from the date that the enactment referred to in subsection (1) (a) is amended, and

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  the period, if any, specified in the enactment referred to in subsection (1) (a);

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) in the case of a plan amendment required by a regulation referred to in subsection (1) (b), a period of 6 months or longer specified in the regulation.

heading: Mandatory amendments to forest operations plan
paragraph: (4) In prescribed circumstances, the minister may exempt a person from a requirement to amend a plan under subsection (1).

heading: Annual forest development schedule
paragraph:
2.46
		  (1) On or before December 31 of each calendar year, the holder of a forest operations plan, other than a timber sales manager, must make publicly available, in accordance with the regulations, a forest development schedule that shows each location in the forest operations area where the holder intends to start harvesting timber or constructing roads in the next calendar year.

heading: Annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (2) On or before December 31 of each calendar year, a timber sales manager who holds a forest operations plan must publish on a ministry website a forest development schedule that shows each location in the forest operations area that will be included in timber sale licences for which the timber sales manager intends to invite applications in the next calendar year.

heading: Annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (3) A forest development schedule must be consistent with the forest operations plan to which the schedule relates.

heading: Annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (4) A forest development schedule must meet the prescribed requirements, if any.

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph:
2.47
		  (1) Unless the regulations provide otherwise, the holder of a forest operations plan must prepare a site level plan

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (a) for a cutblock, before the holder starts harvesting timber on the cutblock, and

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (b) for a road, before the holder starts harvesting timber for the purposes of constructing the road.

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (2) A site level plan must do the following:

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (a) identify the approximate locations of cutblocks and roads;

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (b) be consistent with the forest landscape plan and forest operations plan that applies to the plan area of the site level plan;

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (c) meet the prescribed requirements.

heading: Site level plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (3) A site level plan may apply to one or more cutblocks and roads whether the cutblocks and roads are located within one forest operations area or more than one forest operations area.

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph:
2.48
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: "new forest landscape area" has the meaning given to it in subsection (2);

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: "related forest landscape plan" means the forest landscape plan that establishes a new forest landscape area.

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this section, an area of land is a new forest landscape area if, immediately before the establishment of a forest landscape plan that applies to the area, the area has never been included in a forest landscape area.

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the holder of a forest stewardship plan is exempt from section 2.35 (2) and (3) in relation to a portion of a forest development unit included in the plan if the portion is within a new forest landscape area and either of the following applies:

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (a) the forest stewardship plan is approved by the minister before the date on which the related forest landscape plan takes effect;

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (b) the forest stewardship plan, or an amendment to the forest stewardship plan to add the portion to the forest development unit,

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (i)  is submitted to the minister for approval before the date on which the related forest landscape plan takes effect, and

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (ii)  is approved by the minister on or after the date on which the related forest landscape plan takes effect.

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (4) The exemption under subsection (3) ceases to apply to the person on the following date, as applicable:

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (a) unless paragraph (b) of this subsection applies, the date that is one year after the date on which the related forest landscape plan takes effect;

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (b) if the holder, within 6 months after the date on which the related forest landscape plan takes effect, submits to the minister for approval a forest operations plan that applies to the portion, the date on which the forest operations plan is approved or rejected by the minister.

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under forest stewardship plans in new forest landscape areas
paragraph: (5) Despite section 16 (1.02), that section does not apply to a forest stewardship plan or amendment referred to in subsection (3) (b) of this section that is submitted to the minister for approval before the date on which the related forest landscape plan referred to in subsection (3) (b) of this section takes effect.

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under cutting permits or road permits issued in relation to forest stewardship plans
paragraph:
2.49
		  The holder of an agreement is exempt from section 2.35 (2) (c) and (d) if the holder harvests timber or constructs roads in an area of land that is subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued before

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under cutting permits or road permits issued in relation to forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (a) the expiry of a forest stewardship plan that included a forest development unit containing the area subject to the permit, or

heading: Exemption from requirement to hold forest operations plan - activities under cutting permits or road permits issued in relation to forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (b) the removal of the holder as a party to a forest stewardship plan that included a forest development unit containing the area subject to the permit.

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph:
2.5
		  (1) In this Division:

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: "decision-making agreement" means an agreement entered into under section 7 of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act by the minister, on behalf of the government, and an Indigenous governing body relating to one or both of the following:

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: (a) the exercise of a statutory power of decision under this Part jointly by

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: (i)  the Indigenous governing body, and

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: (ii)  the minister or the chief forester;

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: (b) the consent of the Indigenous governing body before the exercise of a statutory power of decision of the minister or the chief forester under this Part;

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: "statutory power of decision" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act.

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: (2) The definition of "agreement" in section 2.2 does not apply for the purposes of the definition of "decision-making agreement" in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Decision-making agreement
paragraph: (3) This Division applies despite Divisions 1 and 2 of this Part and sections 79 to 83.1 and 84 (1).

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: 2.51		  (1) This section applies in respect of the power of the chief forester to make the following orders:

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (a) an order under section 2.21 (1) establishing a forest landscape plan;

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (b) an order under section 2.3 (1) extending the term of a forest landscape plan;

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (c) an order amending or cancelling a forest landscape plan.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) to (7), if a decision-making agreement has been entered into in respect of the power of the chief forester to make an order referred to in subsection (1),

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (a) the power must be exercised in accordance with the decision-making agreement, and

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (b) a reference in this Act or the regulations to the order is to be read as a reference to the order as made in accordance with the decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (3) A decision-making agreement may establish objectives in addition to those set out in section 2.22 that must be considered in the preparation of a forest landscape plan.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), sections 2.23 to 2.27 apply in respect of the preparation of a forest landscape plan to be established by an order made in accordance with a decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (5) If a decision-making agreement so provides, sections 2.23 to 2.27 do not apply in respect of an Indigenous governing body that is a party to the decision-making agreement in relation to a forest landscape plan to be established by an order made in accordance with the decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (6) Section 2.28 applies to a forest landscape plan established by an order made in accordance with a decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester
paragraph: (7) The term of a forest landscape plan established by an order made in accordance with a decision-making agreement is the period of not less than 5 years and not more than 10 years specified in the order.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of chief forester
paragraph:
2.52
		  (1) This section applies in respect of the power of the chief forester under section 2.32 (1) to, by order, require the submission of plans, studies, analyses or information for the purposes of preparing or amending a forest landscape plan or preparing a report under section 2.31.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of chief forester
paragraph: (2) If a decision-making agreement provides for the exercise of the power of the chief forester to make an order referred to in subsection (1),

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of chief forester
paragraph: (a) the power must be exercised in accordance with the decision-making agreement, and

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of chief forester
paragraph: (b) a reference in this Act or the regulations to the order is to be read as a reference to the order as made in accordance with the decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of minister
paragraph:
2.53
		  (1) This section applies in respect of the following powers of the minister:

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of minister
paragraph: (a) the power under section 2.38 (3) to relieve a person from the requirements under section 2.38 (1) and (2) for the purposes of resubmitting a forest operations plan or an amendment to a forest operations plan;

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of minister
paragraph: (b) the power under section 2.45 (4) to exempt a person from a requirement under section 2.45 (1) to amend a forest operations plan.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of minister
paragraph: (2) If a decision-making agreement provides for the exercise of a power of the minister referred to in subsection (1),

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of minister
paragraph: (a) the power must be exercised in accordance with the decision-making agreement, and

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of minister
paragraph: (b) a reference in this Act or the regulations to the power exercised by the minister is to be read as a reference to the power as exercised in accordance with the decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph:
2.54
		  (1) This section applies in respect of the following powers of the minister:

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (a) the power under section 2.39 to approve a forest operations plan or an amendment to a forest operations plan;

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (b) the power under section 2.43 to extend the term of a forest operations plan;

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (c) the power under section 112 to impose, remove or vary conditions in respect of an approval of a forest operations plan or of an amendment to a forest operations plan.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), if a decision-making agreement has been entered into in respect of a power of the minister referred to in subsection (1),

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (a) the power must be exercised in accordance with the decision-making agreement, and

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (b) a reference in this Act or the regulations to the power exercised by the minister is to be read as a reference to the power as exercised in accordance with the decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (3) The criteria set out in sections 2.39 (1) (a) to (c) and 2.4 (1) (a) to (c) apply to the granting of an approval of a forest operations plan or of an amendment to a forest operations plan in accordance with a decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (4) Section 2.39 (2) to (4) applies, with the necessary changes, to the imposition of conditions in respect of an approval of a forest operations plan or of an amendment to a forest operations plan in accordance with a decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (5) Section 79 applies to a correction of an approval granted under section 2.39 (1) in accordance with a decision-making agreement, except that the reference in that section to the person who made the determination is to be read as a reference to the minister.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (6) A review required under section 80 (1) of an approval granted under section 2.39 (1) in accordance with a decision-making agreement must be conducted in accordance with the decision-making agreement.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (7) A review referred to in subsection (6) may be conducted only if there is evidence that was not available at the time of the original determination.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (8) Section 80 (2), (3) and (5) applies, with the necessary changes, to a review referred to in subsection (6).

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (9) The minister may extend the time limit for requiring a review referred to in subsection (6) before or after its expiry.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (10) Unless a decision-making agreement so provides, sections 81 to 83.1 and 84 (1) do not apply with respect to

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (a) an approval granted under section 2.39 (1) in accordance with the decision-making agreement, and

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (b) a decision made after completion of a review of the approval.

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (11) If a decision-making agreement provides that section 81 applies with respect to an approval referred to in subsection (10) (a) of this section,

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (a) a review required by the board under section 81 (1) must be conducted in accordance with the decision-making agreement, and

heading: Decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of minister
paragraph: (b) the minister may extend the time limit for requiring a review referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection before or after its expiry.

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph:
3
		  (0.1) In this section:

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: "agreement" means any of the following agreements under the Forest Act:

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (a) a forest licence;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (b) a tree farm licence;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (c) a community forest agreement;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (d) a timber licence;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (e) a forestry licence to cut that is a major licence;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: "approved forest stewardship plan" means a forest stewardship plan that is approved by the minister;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: "forest landscape area" includes an area of land that was formerly a forest landscape area.

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (1) If land subject to an agreement is located outside a forest landscape area, the holder of the agreement must not do any of the following unless the holder holds an approved forest stewardship plan that includes a forest development unit that contains the land:

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (a) apply for a cutting permit to harvest timber on the land;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (b) apply for a road permit to construct a road on the land;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (c) harvest timber on the land;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (d) construct a road on the land.

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (1.1) The holder of an agreement is exempt from subsection (1) (c) and (d) if the holder harvests timber or constructs roads in an area of land that is subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued before

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (a) the expiry of a forest stewardship plan that included a forest development unit containing the area subject to the permit, or

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (b) the removal of the holder as a party to a forest stewardship plan that included a forest development unit containing the area subject to the permit.

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (2) A timber sales manager may not do any of the following in relation to land located outside a forest landscape area unless the timber sales manager holds an approved forest stewardship plan that includes a forest development unit that contains the land:

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (a) invite applications for, or enter into, a timber sale licence that grants rights to harvest timber on the land;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (b) issue to the holder of a timber sale licence a road permit to construct a road on the land;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (c) construct a road on the land for access to an area to be harvested under a timber sale licence.

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (4) A forest stewardship plan may apply to one or more of each of the following:

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (a) holders of agreements under the Forest Act;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (b) agreements under the Forest Act;

heading: Forest stewardship plan required
paragraph: (c) areas of land located outside a forest landscape area that are, or will be, subject to an agreement under the Forest Act.

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: 4		  (1) If a forest stewardship plan held by the holder of an agreement referred to in section 3 (1) or by the timber sales manager referred to in section 3 (2) does not apply to an area outside the forest development unit to which the plan pertains, in which area the holder or timber sales manager will harvest timber or construct a road, the holder or timber sales manager, as the case may be, is exempt in respect of the outside area from the requirement for a forest stewardship plan, but only for the following purposes:

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (a) harvesting timber to eliminate a safety hazard;

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (b) harvesting timber to facilitate the collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha;

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (c) removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way;

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (d) harvesting timber not exceeding a volume of 500 m3 that, in the opinion of the minister,

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (i)  is in danger of being significantly reduced in value, lost or destroyed, by insect infestation, fire or disease, or

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (ii)  has been treated or will be treated by the holder or timber sales manager to facilitate the entrapment or elimination of pests;

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (e) other prescribed purposes.

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (2) A person is not required to prepare a forest stewardship plan under section 3 (1) or (2) for timber to be harvested or roads to be constructed if the timber harvesting or the road construction

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (a) is only for one or more of the purposes referred to in subsection (1) (a) to (e) of this section, or

heading: Exemption from forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (b) is to be carried out in prescribed circumstances or under prescribed conditions.

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A forest stewardship plan must

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (a) include a map that

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (i)  uses a scale and format satisfactory to the minister, and

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (ii)  shows the boundaries of all forest development units,

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (b) specify intended results or strategies, each in relation to

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (i)  objectives set by government,

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (i.1)  if a portion of a forest development unit is within an area prescribed by the minister under section 168.1, the objectives prescribed by the minister under that section for prescribed resources and features in that area, and

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (ii)  other objectives that are established under this Act and that pertain to all or part of the area subject to the plan, and

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (c) conform to prescribed requirements.

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (1.1) The results and strategies referred to in subsection (1) (b) must be consistent to the prescribed extent with objectives set by government and with the other objectives referred to in subsection (1) (b) (ii).

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (2) A forest stewardship plan must be consistent with timber harvesting rights granted by the government for any of the following to which the plan applies:

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (a) the timber supply area;

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (b) the community forest agreement area;

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (c) the tree farm licence area;

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (d) the pulpwood area.

heading: Content of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (3) A forest stewardship plan or an amendment to a forest stewardship plan must be signed by the person required to prepare the plan, if an individual or, if a corporation, by an individual or the individuals authorized to sign on behalf of the corporation.

heading: Term of forest stewardship plan
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The term of a forest stewardship plan

heading: Term of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (a) is the period, not exceeding 5 years, that the person submitting the plan for approval specifies at the time of submission, and

heading: Term of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (b) begins on the date specified in writing by the minister in approving the plan.

heading: Term of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (2) The minister by written notice given to the holder may extend the term of a forest stewardship plan, before or after it expires for an additional period not exceeding 5 years in the circumstances specified by regulation.

heading: Term of forest stewardship plan
paragraph: (3) The extended forest stewardship plan may include changes to the extent authorized by regulation.

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph:
7
		  (1) A proposed forest stewardship plan must be considered to have received the minister's approval under section 16 (1) for the parts, if any, of the forest stewardship plan that pertain to

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (a) a cutting permit, road permit or timber sale licence if the permit or licence is in effect on the date of the submission of the forest stewardship plan to the minister, or

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (b) an area that conforms to the prescribed requirements.

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (1.1) A proposed forest stewardship plan must be considered to have received the minister's approval under section 16 (1) for the parts, if any, of the plan, including but not limited to results and strategies described in it, that pertain to a forest development unit that is in effect on the date of the submission of the forest stewardship plan to the minister unless

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (a) one or more of the following events occur during the period specified in subsection (2):

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (i)  an enactment applicable to the forest development unit is made or amended;

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (ii)  an objective set by government applicable to the forest development unit is established, varied or cancelled;

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (iii)  if specified by regulation, another objective applicable to the forest development unit is established, varied or cancelled by order under this Act;

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (iv)  an area of land in or adjacent to the forest development unit is designated by order under the regulations as a community watershed;

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (v)  a community watershed in or adjacent to the forest development unit is varied or cancelled by order under the regulations;

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (vi)  timber in the vicinity of the forest development unit has suffered catastrophic damage, and

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (b) the minister considers that the forest development unit is inconsistent with the events described in paragraph (a) that occur.

heading: Limited protection for forest development units
paragraph: (2) The specified period under subsection (1.1) begins 4 months before the date the existing plan was submitted for approval and ends 4 months before the date the proposed plan was submitted for approval.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph:
8
		  (1) The holder of a forest stewardship plan must propose and submit, for approval by the minister and in accordance with this section, an amendment to the plan if any of the following apply:

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) a forest development unit included in the plan is affected by any of the following events:

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (i)  an amendment to this Act, the regulations or a prescribed enactment;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (ii)  the establishment, variation or cancellation of an objective set by government or, if specified by regulation, another objective that is established under this Act;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) the holder is required by either of the following to propose and submit an amendment to the plan:

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (i)  the regulations;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (ii)  an order made under subsection (2).

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (2) The minister may order the holder of a forest stewardship plan to propose and submit for approval an amendment to the plan if the minister considers that timber in or within the vicinity of a forest development unit included in the plan has suffered catastrophic damage.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (3) An amendment required under this section must address the following, as applicable:

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) an event referred to in subsection (1) (a);

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) a regulation referred to in subsection (1) (b);

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (c) a minister's order referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (4) An amendment required under this section must be submitted within the following period, as applicable:

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) in the case of a plan amendment required under subsection (1) (a), the longer of

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (i)  6 months from the date of the event referred to in that subsection, and

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (ii)  the period, if any, specified in the enactment or objective that relates to the event;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) in the case of a plan amendment required by a regulation referred to in subsection (1) (b) (i), a period of 6 months or longer specified in the regulation;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (c) in the case of a plan amendment required by an order referred to in subsection (2), the longer of

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (i)  6 months from the date the order is made, and

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (ii)  the period, if any, specified in the order.

heading: Proportional objectives
paragraph:
9
		  In prescribed circumstances, the minister may establish targets, in specified proportions between or among the holders of forest stewardship plans, for sharing the responsibility to obtain results consistent with objectives set by government.

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph:
10
		  (1) Except in prescribed circumstances, the holder of a forest stewardship plan must prepare a site plan in accordance with prescribed requirements for any

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (a) cutblock before the start of timber harvesting on the cutblock, and

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (b) road before the start of timber harvesting related to the road's construction.

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (2) A site plan must

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (a) identify the approximate locations of cutblocks and roads,

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (b) be consistent with the forest stewardship plan, this Act and the regulations, and

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (c) identify how the intended results or strategies described in the forest stewardship plan apply to the site.

heading: Site plans for cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (3) A site plan may apply to one or more cutblocks and roads whether within the area of one or more forest stewardship plans.

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph:
12
		  (0.1) In this section, "approved woodlot licence plan" means a woodlot licence plan that is approved by the minister.

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (1) The holder of a woodlot licence must not do any of the following on land within the woodlot licence area unless the holder holds an approved woodlot licence plan that includes the land:

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (a) apply for a cutting permit to harvest timber on the land;

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (b) apply for a road permit to construct a road on the land;

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (c) harvest timber on the land;

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (d) construct a road on the land.

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (1.1) The holder of a woodlot licence is exempt from subsection (1) (c) and (d) if the holder harvests timber or constructs roads in an area of land that is subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued before the expiry of a woodlot licence plan that included the area subject to the permit.

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (2) The holder of a woodlot licence may obtain a cutting permit or road permit only if it is consistent with a woodlot licence plan.

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), the minister, in the circumstances and on the conditions, if any, that are prescribed may authorize the holder of a woodlot licence to obtain a cutting permit or road permit

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (a) to deal with a forest health emergency, or

heading: Woodlot licence plan required
paragraph: (b) to harvest timber that has been damaged and is in danger of being significantly reduced in value, lost or destroyed.

heading: Content of woodlot licence plan
paragraph:
13
		  (1) A woodlot licence plan must

heading: Content of woodlot licence plan
