		  (1) The minister must approve a range use plan, a range stewardship plan or an amendment to either if the minister determines that the plan or amendment

heading: Approval of a range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (a) is consistent with the agreement under the Range Act that pertains to the plan, and

heading: Approval of a range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (b) conforms to this Act, the regulations and the standards.

heading: Approval of a range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (2) A range use plan, a range stewardship plan or an amendment to either that is submitted to the minister for approval must be considered to have conformed to this Act, the regulations, the standards and the objectives set by government if the plan or amendment conforms to the relevant provisions of this Act, the regulations, the standards and the objectives as they were 4 months before the date of the submission of the plan or amendment to the minister.

heading: Approval of a range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (2.1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by order, may declare that a range use plan, a range stewardship plan or an amendment to either that is submitted to the minister for approval, despite subsection (2), must immediately conform to some or all of this Act, the regulations, the standards and the objectives set by government as set out in the order.

heading: Approval of a range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (3) The minister or the person seeking approval of a range use plan, a range stewardship plan or an amendment to either may refer the plan to an advisory committee for its recommendations, and the minister may consider those recommendations when making a determination under subsection (1).

heading: Approval of a range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (4) The minister must give reasons for refusing to approve a range use plan, a range stewardship plan or an amendment to either.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: 38		  (1) The holder of a range stewardship plan that includes the matters described in section 35 (2), must ensure that the strategies or actions specified in the plan continue during the term of the plan to be sufficient to achieve the intended results specified in the plan.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (2) The holder of

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) a range stewardship plan that does not include the matters described in section 35 (2), or

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) a range use plan

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: must ensure that the actions specified in the plan to deal with issues identified by the minister continue during the term of the plan to be sufficient to deal with those issues.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (3) The holder of a range stewardship plan described in subsection (1) who knows or reasonably ought to know that the strategies or actions specified in the plan, are not sufficient to achieve the intended results specified in the plan, must prepare and submit to the minister an amendment to the plan so that the plan, as approved, is sufficient to achieve those intended results.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (4) The holder of a range stewardship plan described in subsection (2) (a) or a range use plan mentioned in subsection (2) (b) who knows or reasonably ought to know that the actions specified in the plan are not sufficient to deal with issues identified by the minister must amend the plan so that it is sufficient to deal with those issues.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (5) The holder of a range use plan or range stewardship plan, if and as directed by order of the minister, must prepare and submit an amendment to the plan to take into account prescribed circumstances.

heading: Cumulative impacts require plan amendment
paragraph:
39
		  (1) At the request of a holder of an agreement under the Range Act, the minister may determine whether range use plans or range stewardship plans held by other holders of agreements under the Range Act prevent or are likely to prevent the holder making the request from

heading: Cumulative impacts require plan amendment
paragraph: (a) exercising the holder's rights under the holder's own agreement, or

heading: Cumulative impacts require plan amendment
paragraph: (b) achieving a requirement of the holder's own range use plan or range stewardship plan.

heading: Cumulative impacts require plan amendment
paragraph: (2) If the determination under subsection (1) is that the requesting holder is prevented or is likely to be prevented from doing the things described in subsection (1) (a) or (b), the minister by order may require one or more of the other holders of agreements referred to in subsection (1) to prepare and submit for the minister's approval the appropriate amendments to one or more range use or range stewardship plans so that the holder making the request does not continue to be prevented from doing those things.

heading: Cumulative impacts require plan amendment
paragraph: (3) Before making a determination under this section, the minister must give the holders of range use plans or range stewardship plans affected an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Minor changes to range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: 40		  Despite section 37 (1) and unless otherwise prescribed, an approval is not required to amend a range use plan or range stewardship plan if its holder determines that the proposed amendment

heading: Minor changes to range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (a) otherwise conforms to this Act, the regulations and the standards, and

heading: Minor changes to range use plan or range stewardship plan
paragraph: (b) does not materially affect the likelihood of achieving the intended results specified in the plan.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph:
41
		  (1) In prescribed circumstances, before a person submits for approval a range use plan, range stewardship plan or an amendment to either, the person must make the plan or amendment available for

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (a) review, and

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (b) comment.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the minister may approve a range use plan or an amendment to one that has not been made available for review and comment if

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (a) the plan or amendment is for an area that is subject to a temporary grazing permit or temporary hay cutting permit, and

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (b) the minister determines that the range use plan, range stewardship plan or amendment otherwise meets the requirements of this Act, the regulations and the standards.

heading: Proportional objectives
paragraph:
42
		  In prescribed circumstances, the minister may establish targets for sharing, in specified proportions between or among the holders of range use plans and range stewardship plans, the responsibility to achieve objectives set by government.

heading: Grazing schedule required
paragraph:
43
		  (1) The holder of a range stewardship plan must prepare a grazing schedule that includes for each area that will be used for grazing, all of the following:

heading: Grazing schedule required
paragraph: (a) the livestock class;

heading: Grazing schedule required
paragraph: (b) the number of livestock;

heading: Grazing schedule required
paragraph: (c) the period of use.

heading: Grazing schedule required
paragraph: (2) The grazing schedule must be submitted each year to the district manager before the holder grazes livestock on Crown range.

heading: Grazing schedule available to public
paragraph:
44
		  A person who has prepared a grazing schedule must make it available to a person on request.

heading: General
paragraph:
45
		  (1) A person who grazes livestock, cuts hay or carries out or maintains a range development on Crown range must do so in accordance with

heading: General
paragraph: (a) this Act, the regulations and the standards, and

heading: General
paragraph: (b) the applicable range use or range stewardship plan.

heading: General
paragraph: (2) The holder of an agreement under the Range Act that authorizes grazing of livestock must ensure that all livestock authorized to graze on Crown range under the agreement are

heading: General
paragraph: (a) marked with the holder's registered brand or marked in another manner approved by the minister, and

heading: General
paragraph: (b) identified by a mark or tag designating them as animals pastured under the agreement, if the minister requires it.

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: 46		  (1) A person must not carry out a forest practice, a range practice or another activity that results in damage to the environment, unless in doing so

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (a) the person

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (i)  is acting in accordance with a plan, authorization or permit under this Act,

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (ii)  is not required to hold a plan or permit because of an exemption under this Act and is acting in accordance with this Act, the regulations and the standards, or

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (iv)  is acting in accordance with another enactment, and

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (b) the person does not know and cannot reasonably be expected to know that, because of weather conditions or site factors, the carrying out of the forest practice, range practice or other activity may result, directly or indirectly, in damage specified by regulation.

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (1.1) A person, other than a person described in subsection (1), must not engage in any activity on Crown land that results in damage to the environment, unless in doing so

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (a) the person

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (i)  is acting in accordance with a plan, authorization or permit under this Act,

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (ii)  is not required to hold a plan or permit because of an exemption under this Act and is acting in accordance with this Act, the regulations and the standards, or

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (iii)  is acting in accordance with another enactment, and

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (b) the person does not know and cannot reasonably be expected to know that, because of weather conditions or site factors, engaging in the activity may result, directly or indirectly, in damage specified by regulation.

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes subsection (1) or (1.1) must

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (a) take appropriate action to prevent any further damage,

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (b) promptly notify the district manager of the damage, and

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (c) take any remedial measures that the minister requires under section 74.

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (3) A person who discontinues a forest practice, a range practice or another activity referred to in subsection (1) or an activity referred to in subsection (1.1) may resume that practice or activity only if and when

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (a) it can be resumed without contravening subsection (1) or (1.1), as the case may be, and

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (b) the minister is satisfied that any remedial measures required under subsection (2) (c)

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (i)  have been carried out, or

heading: Protection of the environment
paragraph: (ii)  will be carried out at the appropriate time.

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph:
47
		  (1) A person carrying out a forest practice or a range practice must carry out measures that are

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (a) specified in the applicable operational plan, or

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (b) authorized by the minister

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: to prevent the introduction or spread of prescribed species of invasive plants.

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (2) Despite expiry of the operational plan referred to in subsection (1) (a), subsection (1) continues to apply to the holder of that plan in respect of any area that is

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (a) in a forest development unit included in the plan, and

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (b) subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued in respect of the plan before the plan expired.

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (3) If a forest stewardship plan is amended to remove the holder of a licence or an agreement as a party to the plan, subsection (1) continues to apply to that holder in respect of any area that is

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (a) in a forest development unit included in the plan, and

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph: (b) subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued in respect of the plan before the plan was amended.

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph:
48
		  (1) A person carrying out

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (a) a forest practice, or

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (b) a range practice

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: that directly or indirectly removes or renders ineffective a natural range barrier must carry out measures that are

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (c) specified in an operational plan for the area, or

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (d) authorized by the minister

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: to mitigate the removal or the ineffectiveness of the natural range barrier.

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (2) Despite expiry of the operational plan referred to in subsection (1) (c), subsection (1) continues to apply to the holder of that plan in respect of any area that is

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (a) in a forest development unit included in the plan, and

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (b) subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued in respect of the plan before the plan expired.

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (3) If a forest stewardship plan is amended to remove the holder of a licence or an agreement as a party to the plan, subsection (1) continues to apply to that holder in respect of any area that is

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (a) in a forest development unit included in the plan, and

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph: (b) subject to a cutting permit or road permit issued in respect of the plan before the plan was amended.

heading: Exemption for fighting out of control fire
paragraph:
49
		  A person does not contravene this Act or the regulations by doing or omitting to do something that is reasonably necessary to control a fire, unless the person knows or reasonably ought to know, that an official has declared that the fire is under control.

heading: Unauthorized range activities
paragraph:
50
		  (1) A person must not cause or permit livestock to be driven on or to graze on Crown range unless

heading: Unauthorized range activities
paragraph: (a) authorized to do so under an agreement under the Range Act or under the regulations under this Act, and

heading: Unauthorized range activities
paragraph: (b) the person acts in accordance with this Act, the regulations, the standards and any applicable range use plan or range stewardship plan.

heading: Unauthorized range activities
paragraph: (2) A person must not cut, remove, damage or destroy hay on Crown range unless

heading: Unauthorized range activities
paragraph: (a) authorized to do so under an agreement under the Range Act or the regulations under this Act, and

heading: Unauthorized range activities
paragraph: (b) the person acts in accordance with this Act, the regulations, the standards and any applicable range use plan.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: 51		  (1) Unless authorized in writing by the minister, a person must not

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (a) store hay on Crown range, or

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (b) carry out, construct, modify, remove, damage or destroy a range development on Crown range.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (2) A person, other than the holder of an agreement under the Range Act, must obtain the authorization of the minister before maintaining a range development on Crown land.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (3) The minister may

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (a) require a person seeking authorization under this section to submit the matter for which the authorization is sought for review in accordance with prescribed requirements, and for comments by interested parties during the course of the review,

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (b) grant or refuse the authorization, depending on the outcome of a review required under paragraph (a), and

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (c) impose pre-conditions or conditions of an authorization that the minister considers necessary or desirable, to be met by the person, including, but not limited to, requiring that the person provide security.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (4) The minister may grant an authorization under this section only if

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (a) it is consistent with any range use plans, range stewardship plans and objectives set by government for the area covered by the authorization, and

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (b) the minister is satisfied that the authorization will adequately provide for the range resources of the area to which it applies.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (5) If the minister requires security under subsection (3) (c), the minister may specify

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (a) when the security must be paid,

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (b) the amount of security that is required,

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (c) the form of the security, and

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (d) the circumstances under which the security may be realized.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (6) A person who obtains an authorization under this section must comply with any conditions of the authorization.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (7) If the minister determines under section 71 that a person has contravened subsection (1) or (6), the minister may order the person to

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (a) remove or destroy or remove and destroy the stored hay or the range development,

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (b) restore the land under the stored hay or the range development, or both, or

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (c) repair or rehabilitate the range development.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (8) If satisfied that a range development is not effective, or is no longer needed for its original purpose, the minister may order the person responsible for the range development to remove it and rehabilitate areas that were affected by it.

heading: Range developments
paragraph: (9) The minister may revoke or vary an authorization under this section.

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: 52		  (1) A person must not cut, damage or destroy Crown timber unless authorized to do so

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (a) under this Act, the Forest Act or an agreement under the Forest Act,

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (b) by the minister, for silviculture, stand tending, forest health, abating a fire hazard related to wildfires or another purpose,

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (b.1) under the Wildfire Act,

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (c) under a grant of Crown land made under the Land Act,

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (d) under the Park Act, or

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (e) under the regulations, in the course of carrying out activities

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (i)  under an authorization referred in section 51 or 57, or

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (ii)  that are incidental to or required to carry out activities authorized or approved under this Act, the Forest Act, the Range Act or another prescribed enactment.

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (2) A person is authorized to cut, damage or destroy Crown timber for the purpose of carrying out a forest practice that is funded under a vote as defined in section 1 of the Financial Administration Act.

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (3) A person must not remove Crown timber unless authorized to do so

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (a) under the Forest Act or an agreement under the Forest Act,

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (b) under a grant of Crown land made under the Land Act, or

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (c) under the Park Act.

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (4) If a person, at the direction of or on behalf of another person,

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (a) cuts, damages or destroys Crown timber contrary to subsection (1), or

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: (b) removes Crown timber contrary to subsection (3),

heading: Unauthorized timber harvesting
paragraph: that other person also contravenes subsection (1) or  (3).

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: 52.1		  (1) The minister, in respect of an authorization under section 52 (1) (b), may

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (a) require the person seeking the authorization to submit the matter for which the authorization is sought for review in accordance with prescribed requirements, and for comments by interested parties during the course of the review,

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (b) grant or refuse the authorization, depending on the outcome of a review required under paragraph (a) of this subsection, and

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (c) impose pre-conditions or conditions of an authorization that the minister considers necessary or desirable, to be met by the person, including, but not limited to, requiring that the person provide security.

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (2) If the minister requires security under subsection (1) (c), the minister may specify

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (a) when the security must be paid,

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (b) the amount of security that is required,

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (c) the form of the security, and

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (d) the circumstances under which the security may be realized.

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (3) A person who obtains an authorization under section 52 (1) (b) must comply with any conditions of the authorization.

heading: Authorization for silviculture, stand tending, forest health or another purpose
paragraph: (4) The minister may revoke or vary an authorization under section 52 (1) (b).

heading: Private land adjacent to Crown land
paragraph:
53
		  (1) Before an owner or occupier of private land that is adjacent to Crown land authorizes another person to cut or remove timber from the private land, the owner or occupier must inform that other person of the boundaries of the private land.

heading: Private land adjacent to Crown land
paragraph: (2) Before a person cuts or removes timber from private land adjacent to Crown land, the person must ascertain the boundaries of the private land.

heading: Unauthorized construction and occupation
paragraph:
54
		  (1) A person must obtain the consent of the minister before constructing or occupying a building or other structure on Crown land in a Provincial forest unless the construction or occupation is authorized under another enactment.

heading: Unauthorized construction and occupation
paragraph: (2) If the minister determines under section 71 that a person has contravened subsection (1), the minister may order the person to do one or more of the following:

heading: Unauthorized construction and occupation
paragraph: (a) remove the building or other structure;

heading: Unauthorized construction and occupation
paragraph: (b) destroy the building or other structure;

heading: Unauthorized construction and occupation
paragraph: (c) restore the land under the building or other structure.

heading: Tree spiking prohibited
paragraph:
55
		  On private land that is subject to an agreement under the Forest Act or on Crown land, a person must not

heading: Tree spiking prohibited
paragraph: (a) drive or place any nail, spike or other potentially hazardous object into any timber that the person does not own or is not authorized to alter,

heading: Tree spiking prohibited
paragraph: (b) possess any nail, spike or other potentially hazardous object with the intention of driving or placing it into any timber that the person does not own or is not authorized to alter, or

heading: Tree spiking prohibited
paragraph: (c) solicit funds or materials from another person with the stated intention that the funds or material will be used to enable any person to drive or place any nail, spike or other potentially hazardous object into any timber that the person does not own or is not authorized to alter.

heading: Interpretive forest sites, recreation sites and recreation trails
paragraph: 56		  (1) The minister may order

heading: Interpretive forest sites, recreation sites and recreation trails
paragraph: (a) the establishment of Crown land as an interpretive forest site, a recreation site, a recreation trail or a trail-based recreation area, except Crown land that is being administered by another minister, branch or agency of government,

heading: Interpretive forest sites, recreation sites and recreation trails
paragraph: (b) the variance of the boundaries of an interpretive forest site, a recreation site, a recreation trail or a trail-based recreation area, and

heading: Interpretive forest sites, recreation sites and recreation trails
paragraph: (c) the disestablishment of an interpretive forest site, a recreation site, a recreation trail or a trail-based recreation area.

heading: Interpretive forest sites, recreation sites and recreation trails
paragraph: (3) The minister may establish an objective for an interpretive forest site, a recreation site, a recreation trail or a trail-based recreation area established under subsection (1).

heading: Interpretive forest sites, recreation sites and recreation trails
paragraph: (4) An objective established under subsection (1) must be consistent with objectives set by government that pertain to the area.

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph:
57
		  (1) Unless authorized in writing by the minister or under another enactment, a person must not

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (a) construct,

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (b) rehabilitate, or

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (c) maintain

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: a trail or other recreation facility on Crown land.

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (2) The minister may impose pre-conditions or conditions of an authorization that the minister considers necessary or desirable, to be met by the person, including, but not limited to, requiring that the person provide security.

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (2.1) If the minister requires security under subsection (2), the minister may specify

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (a) when the security must be paid,

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (b) the amount of security that is required,

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (c) the form of the security, and

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (d) the circumstances under which the security may be realized.

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (3) A person who obtains an authorization under subsection (1) must comply with any conditions of the authorization.

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (4) If the minister determines under section 71 that a person has contravened subsection (1), the minister may order the person to

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (a) remove or destroy or remove and destroy the trail or facility, and

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (b) restore the land underlying the trail or facility.

heading: Unauthorized trail or recreation facility construction
paragraph: (5) The minister may revoke or vary an authorization granted under this section.

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph:
58
		  (1) If the minister determines that it is necessary to protect a recreation or range resource or to manage public recreation use on Crown land, he or she by order may restrict or prohibit

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (a) a non-recreational use of

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (i)  any of the following established under the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act for recreation:

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (A) a resource management zone;

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (B) a landscape unit;

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (C) a sensitive area, or

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (ii)  any of the following that is on Crown land:

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (A) an interpretive forest site;

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (B) a recreation site;

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (C) a recreation trail;

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (D) a trail-based recreation area,

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: except any non-recreational use permitted under the Coal Act, the Mineral Tenure Act or the Energy Resource Activities Act, or

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (b) a recreational use anywhere on Crown land, except a use that is specifically permitted under another enactment.

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (2) The minister may make different orders under subsection (1) for different uses and locations.

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (3) The minister must post a notice of an order under subsection (1) in the area to which the order applies.

heading: Protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land
paragraph: (4) Without lawful authority, a person must not remove, alter, destroy or deface a notice posted under subsection (3).

heading: Definition for Part 6
paragraph: 58.1		  In this Part, "Acts" means one or more of the following:

heading: Definition for Part 6
paragraph: (a) this Act, the regulations or the standards;

heading: Definition for Part 6
paragraph: (b) the Forest Act or a regulation made under that Act;

heading: Definition for Part 6
paragraph: (c) the Range Act or a regulation made under that Act;

heading: Definition for Part 6
paragraph: (d) a provision, other than a prescribed provision, of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act or of a regulation made under that Act.

heading: Applicability of certain provisions of Part 6 of this Act for the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act
paragraph: 58.2		  (0.1) A reference in this section to a provision of this Act is to be read as a reference to the provision as it read immediately before the date this subsection comes into force.

paragraph: (1) Sections 59 to 70, 71 (1), (2), (5) and (6), 72 to 86, 88 to 96, 98 to 101 and 103 of this Act apply to and in respect of

paragraph: (b) the regulations or standards under that Act

paragraph: in relation to the period that ended at midnight on January 30, 2004.

paragraph: (a) the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act, or

paragraph: (b) the regulations or standards under that Act

paragraph: that occurred before midnight on January 30, 2004,

paragraph: (c) the maximum administrative penalties, and

paragraph: (d) the maximum fines and periods of imprisonment

paragraph: are as provided for under the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act at the time of the contravention.

paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this section,

paragraph: (a) the references in section 67 of this Act to sections 52, 50 (2) and 51 must be read as references to sections 96, 100 and 101, respectively, of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act,

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (1.1) In subsection (2), "dwelling" means

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (a) a structure that is occupied as a private residence, and

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (b) if only part of a structure is occupied as a private residence, that part of the structure.

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (2) For any purpose related to the administration or enforcement of the Acts or an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act, or related to the verification of a statement made in an application for an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act, an official may enter, at any reasonable time, on land or premises, other than a dwelling, if the official has reasonable grounds to believe that the land or premises

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (a) has located on it timber that is required to be scaled or marked with a timber mark under the Forest Act,

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (b) is the site of a forest or range practice that is regulated under the Acts or is carried on by a person who is required under the Acts to hold a licence or permit to carry out that practice,

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (c) is the site of trading in botanical forest products, or

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (e) is the site of an activity that under the Acts requires a licence, a permit, a plan or an approval.

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (3) At any reasonable time an official may enter on land that is in or within 1 km of a forest to inspect for fire hazards if the official has reasonable grounds to believe that an activity is being carried out or a condition exists on the land that might cause or produce a fire hazard.

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (4) An official who enters on land or premises under this section may

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (a) inspect anything or any activity that is reasonably related to the purpose of the inspection, and

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (b) require production for the purposes of inspection or copying of

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (i)  a licence, a permit or an operational plan that is required for the activity, and

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (ii)  a record required to be kept under the Acts.

heading: Entry and inspection
paragraph: (5) A peace officer has the powers and duties of an official under subsections (2) and (4) with respect to the enforcement of the provisions of the Forest Act and regulations respecting marine log salvage.

heading: Inspection of vehicle or vessel
paragraph: 60		  For any purpose related to the administration and enforcement of the Acts, an official or a peace officer may

heading: Inspection of vehicle or vessel
paragraph: (a) require a person operating a vehicle or vessel to stop the vehicle or vessel, and

heading: Inspection of vehicle or vessel
paragraph: (b) carry out an inspection of a vehicle or vessel,

heading: Inspection of vehicle or vessel
paragraph: if the official or peace officer has reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Inspection of vehicle or vessel
paragraph: (c) the vehicle or vessel contains or is transporting timber, special forest products, seed, botanical forest products or hay, or

heading: Inspection of vehicle or vessel
paragraph: (d) a person is contravening or has contravened one or more provisions of the Acts.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph:
61
		  (1) The minister may order the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act to produce to the minister specified records that are related to an activity that requires a licence, a permit, a plan or an approval under the Acts or under the agreement.

heading: Delivery of records
paragraph: (2) At any reasonable time, an official may enter the business premises of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act in which records are kept, for the purpose of inspecting or copying records that are required to be kept under the Acts.

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: 62		  An official who

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: (a) under this Division enters onto land or premises, conducts an inspection, stops a vehicle or vessel or requests records, or

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: (b) under Division 2 of this Part seizes goods

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: must provide proof of identity, on the request of the person who

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: (c) is in possession or apparent possession of the land or premises,

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: (d) has apparent custody or control of the records or property being inspected,

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: (e) is in charge of the activity being inspected, or

heading: Obligation of an official
paragraph: (f) is operating a vehicle or vessel stopped under section 60.

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph:
63
		  (1) The operator of a vehicle or vessel must stop the vehicle or vessel when required to do so by

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (a) a peace officer, or

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (b) an official referred to in section 60

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: who

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (c) is in uniform,

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (d) displays his or her official badge, or

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (e) is in or near a vehicle or vessel that is readily identifiable as a government vehicle or vessel.

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (2) A person who

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (a) is in possession or apparent possession of the land or premises,

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (b) has apparent custody or control of the records or property being inspected,

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (c) is in charge of the activity being inspected, or

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (d) is operating a vehicle or vessel stopped under section 60,

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: must produce if and as required by the official

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (e) proof of identity,

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (f) a licence, a permit or an operational plan held by the person under the Acts, or

heading: Obligation of person inspected
paragraph: (g) a record required under section 59 (4).

heading: Warrant to search and seize evidence
paragraph:
64
		  (1) A justice of the peace may issue a warrant under section 21 or 22 of the Offence Act to an official to enter premises and search for and seize evidence of a contravention of the Acts.

heading: Warrant to search and seize evidence
paragraph: (2) The Offence Act applies to the search and seizure.

heading: Peace officers may accompany
paragraph: 65		  An official exercising powers or performing duties or functions under this Part may be accompanied by a peace officer.

heading: Stop work order
paragraph:
66
		  (1) If an official has reasonable grounds to believe that a person is contravening a provision of the Acts, the official may order that the contravention stop, or stop to the extent specified by the order, until the person has a required licence, permit, plan, approval, variance, exemption or other authorization.

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (2) An order to stop work under subsection (1) must be in writing and include all of the following:

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (a) the nature of the contravention;

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (b) the extent to which the contravention or activity must cease;

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (c) the date by which the requirements of paragraph (b) must be met;

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (d) notice of the person's right under section 80 to a review or under section 82 to an appeal;

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (e) an address to which a request for a review may be delivered.

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (3) In addition to the methods of giving notice under section 110, the official who issues a stop work order may give it to a corporation or partnership, by giving the order to an individual who is working at the site on behalf of the corporation or partnership.

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (4) An official who exercises the discretion under subsection (3) must also notify the corporation or partnership as specified in section 110, within 72 hours after giving the order to the individual mentioned in subsection (3).

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (5) An order under this section may be made to apply generally or to one or more persons named in the order.

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (6) The official who issued an order under subsection (1) or the minister

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (a) must rescind the order if the official or the minister determines that there were insufficient grounds for issuing the order, and

heading: Stop work order
paragraph: (b) may rescind the order in prescribed circumstances.

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph:
67
		  (1) An official may seize the following:

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (a) Crown timber that the official has reasonable grounds to believe was cut or removed in contravention of section 52;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (b) timber, lumber, veneer, plywood, pulp, newsprint, special forest products, wood residue and chattels on which the government has a lien under section 130 (1) (d) of the Forest Act;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (c) timber, including special forest products, that the official has reasonable grounds to believe

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (i)  was removed from land in contravention of section 84 (1) or (3) of the Forest Act,

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (ii)  is being or has been manufactured, sold or transported contrary to section 94 or 94.1 of the Forest Act,

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (iii)  is being transported outside British Columbia in contravention of section 127 of the Forest Act,

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (iii.1)  a person is attempting to remove from British Columbia in contravention of section 127.1 of the Forest Act,

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (iv)  is being or has been transported in contravention of any regulation made under the Forest Act, or

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (v)  is mixed with timber to which this subsection applies;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (e) seed that the official has reasonable grounds to believe has been collected contrary to the prescribed requirements;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (f) hay that the official has reasonable grounds to believe has been cut, removed or damaged contrary to section 50 (2);

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (g) hay that the official has reasonable grounds to believe has been stored contrary to section 51;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (h) a botanical forest product that the official has reasonable grounds to believe has been obtained contrary to the regulations;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (i) a vehicle or vessel transporting any of the following to which paragraphs (a) to (h) apply:

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (i)  timber;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (ii)  timber products;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (iii)  seed;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (iv)  hay;

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (v)  botanical forest products.

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (2) If satisfied, after reconsidering the circumstances of a seizure under this section, that there is no longer any basis for retaining the things seized, the official who seized the things may release them and

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (a) return them to the person from whom they were seized, or

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (b) deliver them at the direction of that person to another person.

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (3) The minister may

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (a) deal with, at his or her discretion, Crown timber seized under subsection (1) (a), seed seized under subsection (1) (e), hay seized under subsection (1) (f), botanical forest products seized under subsection (1) (h), or

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (b) after giving the person from whom the timber, chattels, timber products or hay seized under subsection (1) (b), (c) or (g) an opportunity to be heard, sell at a public auction the timber, chattels, timber products or hay.

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (4) If timber, chattels or timber products are sold under subsection (3) (b), notice of the public auction must be published at least 10 days in advance, in or near the area where the sale is to take place, and must

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (a) specify the time and place of the auction, and

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (b) identify by name the person from whom the timber, chattel or timber product was seized.

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (5) If the money realized from the public auction exceeds the money that is payable to the government, including interest and the costs of seizure, storage and sale, the surplus must be paid to the person who possessed the property when it was seized if the property is

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (a) timber, a chattel or a timber product seized under subsection (1) (b), or

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (b) timber seized under subsection (1) (c) (v).

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (6) Despite subsection (5), if within 30 days after the sale a person other than the person referred to in subsection (5) serves a notice of a claim to the surplus on a person designated by the minister, the surplus must be retained until the determination of the respective rights of persons claiming the surplus.

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (7) The proceeds from the sale of timber, a chattel or a timber product seized and sold under this section, other than

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (a) timber, chattels or timber products referred to in subsection (5) (a) or (b), and

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (b) an amount equal to the costs of seizure, storage and sale

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: must be paid into the consolidated revenue fund, and an amount equal to the costs of seizure, storage and sale may be used to pay those costs or reimburse the payment of those costs.

heading: Seizure of timber, chattels, hay, etc.
paragraph: (8) A vehicle or vessel seized under subsection (1) (i) must be released from seizure once the timber, chattel, timber product, seed, hay or botanical forest product is delivered to a location specified by the official.

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: 68		  (1) If an official has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has contravened section 50 (1), the official, or person authorized by the official, may do one or more of the following:

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (a) drive the livestock that are the subject of the contravention from Crown range;

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (b) round up, seize, tranquilize and hold the livestock;

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (c) destroy the livestock if

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (i)  the safety of a person acting under this section is threatened by an animal that is being driven, rounded up, seized, tranquilized or held,

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (ii)  it is impracticable to round up the livestock, or

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (iii)  it would be humane treatment to do so.

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (2) If livestock are held under subsection (1),

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (a) an official may return the livestock to the owner

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (i)  on payment of the reasonable costs of driving, rounding up, seizing, tranquilizing, holding, maintaining and returning the livestock or of disposing of a destroyed animal, or

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (ii)  if satisfied, after reconsidering the circumstances that led to the livestock being held, that there is no longer any basis for holding the livestock, or

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (b) the minister may sell the livestock.

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (3) The minister, an official or a person authorized by an official must take reasonable care of livestock while driving, rounding up, seizing, tranquilizing, holding, returning or selling them under this section.

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (4) If livestock is sold under subsection (2)

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (a) the government must pay the balance of proceeds realized from the sale, after deducting the costs incurred for the driving, rounding up, seizing, holding and selling the livestock to a person who

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (i)  provides evidence satisfactory to the district manager that the person owned the livestock immediately before the sale, and

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (ii)  applies in writing to the district manager for the balance within 6 months after the sale,

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (b) the balance of proceeds from the sale, after deducting the costs incurred for driving, rounding up, seizing, holding and selling the livestock, if not paid under paragraph (a), must be paid into the consolidated revenue fund, and

heading: Seizure and forfeiture of livestock
paragraph: (c) an amount equal to the costs of seizure, storage and sale may by used to pay those costs or reimburse the payment of those costs.

heading: Common provisions for seizure and forfeiture
paragraph:
69
		  (1) The minister may release things seized under section 67 or 68 and

heading: Common provisions for seizure and forfeiture
paragraph: (a) return them to the person from whom they were seized, or

heading: Common provisions for seizure and forfeiture
paragraph: (b) deliver them at the direction of that person to another person.

heading: Common provisions for seizure and forfeiture
paragraph: (2) On a sale under section 67 or 68 the purchaser acquires absolute ownership free of encumbrances.

heading: No interference with notice
paragraph:
70
		  Without the permission of the minister a person must not, remove, alter, destroy or deface a notice posted by the government for the purposes of notifying the public of a seizure under section 67 or 68.

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph:
70.1
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: "remedial action", in relation to a contravention of a provision of the Acts, means any of the following:

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (a) repairing or replacing a building, structure, bridge, culvert, work, installation or other improvement owned by the government that was damaged or destroyed as a direct or indirect result of the contravention;

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (b) replicating work, including, without limitation, silviculture treatment or wildlife habitat restoration or enhancement, that has been

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (i)  carried out on Crown land, and

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (ii)  rendered ineffective as a direct or indirect result of the contravention;

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (c) re-establishing a free growing stand on an area affected by the contravention;

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (d) doing any other work that the minister considers is reasonably necessary to remedy or avoid harm that results or may result, directly or indirectly, from the contravention;

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: "remedial work order" means

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (a) an order under section 51 (7), 54 (2) or 57 (4), or

heading: Definitions for Division 3 of Part 6
paragraph: (b) an order under section 74.2.

heading: Determination of contravention
paragraph:
71
		  After giving notice and an opportunity to be heard to a person who is alleged to have contravened a provision of the Acts, the minister may determine whether the person has contravened the provision.

heading: Defences in relation to administrative proceedings
paragraph:
72
		  The minister may not determine under section 71 that a person has contravened a provision of the Acts if the person establishes that

heading: Defences in relation to administrative proceedings
paragraph: (a) the person exercised due diligence to prevent the contravention,

heading: Defences in relation to administrative proceedings
paragraph: (b) the person reasonably believed in the existence of facts that, if true, would establish that the person did not contravene the provision, or

heading: Defences in relation to administrative proceedings
paragraph: (c) the person's actions relevant to the provision were the result of an officially induced error.

heading: Liability of employers, directors and officers
paragraph:
73
		  (1) Subject to section 72, if a person's contractor, employee or agent contravenes a provision of the Acts in the course of carrying out the contract, employment or agency, the person also contravenes the provision.

heading: Liability of employers, directors and officers
paragraph: (2) If a corporation contravenes a provision of the Acts, a director or an officer of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention also contravenes the provision.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
74
		  (1) If the minister determines under section 71 that a person has contravened a provision of the Acts, the minister may, by order, impose an administrative penalty on the person in an amount that does not exceed the amount determined in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) Before the minister imposes an administrative penalty under this section, the minister must consider the following:

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) previous contraventions of a similar nature by the person;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) the gravity and magnitude of the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) whether the contravention was repeated or continuous;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (d) whether the contravention was deliberate;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (e) any economic benefit derived by the person from the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (f) the person's cooperativeness and efforts to correct the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (g) prescribed matters.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations providing for the determination of penalties that vary according to any of the following:

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the size of the area affected by the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) the volume of timber affected by the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the number of trees affected by the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (d) the number of livestock affected by the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (e) the amount of forage destroyed by the contravention;

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (f) the amount of hay affected by the contravention.

heading: Notice of administrative penalty
paragraph:
74.1
		  If an administrative penalty under section 74 is imposed on a person, the minister must give to the person a notice that specifies the following:

heading: Notice of administrative penalty
paragraph: (a) the provision contravened;

heading: Notice of administrative penalty
paragraph: (b) the amount of the penalty;

heading: Notice of administrative penalty
paragraph: (c) the date by which the penalty must be paid;

heading: Notice of administrative penalty
paragraph: (d) the applicability of section 130 of the Forest Act in relation to the penalty and the consequences of failing to pay the penalty by the due date;

heading: Notice of administrative penalty
paragraph: (e) the person's right to a review under section 80 of this Act or to an appeal under section 82 of this Act;

heading: Notice of administrative penalty
paragraph: (f) an address to which a request for a review or appeal may be delivered.

heading: Remedial work order for contravention of Acts
paragraph: 74.2		  (1) This section applies in relation to a person who

heading: Remedial work order for contravention of Acts
paragraph: (a) is a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act, or

heading: Remedial work order for contravention of Acts
paragraph: (b) is in a prescribed class of persons.

heading: Remedial work order for contravention of Acts
paragraph: (2) If the minister determines under section 71 that a person has contravened a provision of the Acts, the minister may make an order requiring the person to carry out a remedial action.

heading: Remedial work order for contravention of Acts
paragraph: (3) If an order made under subsection (2) against a person is rescinded on review or appeal and the person has carried out the remedial action specified in the order, the government must, to the extent provided in the regulations, pay to the person an amount to cover any expenses incurred by the person in excess of the expenses that the person would have incurred if the order had not been made.

heading: Notice of remedial work order
paragraph: 74.3		  If the minister makes a remedial work order against a person, the minister must give to the person a notice that specifies the following:

heading: Notice of remedial work order
paragraph: (a) the provision contravened;

heading: Notice of remedial work order
paragraph: (b) the action to be carried out by the person;

heading: Notice of remedial work order
paragraph: (c) the date by which the action must be completed;

heading: Notice of remedial work order
paragraph: (d) the person's right to a review under section 80 or to an appeal under section 82;

heading: Notice of remedial work order
paragraph: (e) an address to which a request for a review or appeal may be delivered;

heading: Notice of remedial work order
paragraph: (f) the minister's authority to make orders under section 74.4 if the person does not comply with the order.

heading: Non-compliance with remedial work order
paragraph:
74.4
		  (1) If a person does not comply with a remedial work order by the date specified in the notice given under section 74.3, the minister may do one or more of the following:

heading: Non-compliance with remedial work order
paragraph: (a) on giving notice to the person, restrict or prohibit the person from carrying out the action referred to in the order;

heading: Non-compliance with remedial work order
paragraph: (b) carry out the action;

heading: Non-compliance with remedial work order
paragraph: (c) if the minister carries out the action, make an order requiring the person to pay to the government the amount of all direct and indirect costs that the minister considers were reasonably incurred in carrying out the action;

heading: Non-compliance with remedial work order
paragraph: (d) whether or not an order is made under paragraph (c), make an order imposing an administrative penalty not exceeding the amount determined in accordance with the regulations;

heading: Non-compliance with remedial work order
paragraph: (e) for the purpose of recovering the costs referred to in paragraph (c), realize any security or deposit provided under the Acts by the person.

heading: Non-compliance with remedial work order

heading: Remedial cost recovery order
paragraph: 74.6		  If the minister determines under section 71 that a person has contravened a provision of the Acts and the person is not required, by an order made under section 74.2 of this Act, to carry out a given remedial action, the minister may make an order requiring the person to pay either of the following amounts in relation to the remedial action:

heading: Remedial cost recovery order
paragraph: (a) if the government has carried out the remedial action, the amount of all direct and indirect costs that the minister considers were reasonably incurred by the government in carrying out the remedial action;

heading: Remedial cost recovery order
paragraph: (b) if the government has not carried out or will not carry out the remedial action, an amount that the minister considers is equivalent to the direct and indirect costs that would be incurred by the government in carrying out the remedial action if the government were to carry it out.

heading: Notice of remedial cost recovery order
paragraph:
74.7
		  If an order under section 74.6 is made against a person, the minister must give to the person a notice that specifies the following:

heading: Notice of remedial cost recovery order

paragraph: (b) the amounts determined under section 74.6;

heading: Notice of remedial cost recovery order
paragraph: (c) the date by which the amounts must be paid;

heading: Notice of remedial cost recovery order
paragraph: (d) the applicability of section 130 of the Forest Act in relation to the amounts and the consequences of failing to pay the amounts by the due date;

heading: Notice of remedial cost recovery order
paragraph: (e) the person's right to a review under section 80 of this Act or to an appeal under section 82 of this Act;

heading: Notice of remedial cost recovery order
paragraph: (f) an address to which a request for a review or appeal may be delivered.

heading: Revenue to be paid into special account
paragraph: 74.8		  All revenue derived from the following must be paid into the Environmental Remediation Sub-account of the Forest Stand Management Fund special account established by the Special Accounts Appropriation and Control Act:

heading: Revenue to be paid into special account
paragraph: (a) administrative penalties imposed under this Division;

heading: Revenue to be paid into special account
paragraph: (b) orders made under sections 74.4 and 74.6 of this Act.

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: 77		  (1) The minister, by order that meets the prescribed requirements, may require a person who is the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act or is in a prescribed category of persons to

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (a) remedy,

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (b) mitigate, or

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (c) stop,

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: in a manner and to the extent that is reasonable in the circumstances, an act or omission of the person that the minister reasonably believes will result in a contravention of the Acts and will or probably will cause

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (d) a catastrophic impact on public health or safety,

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (e) any prescribed event or circumstance that will result in a free growing stand required under this Act not being established, or

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (f) any prescribed event or circumstance having an adverse impact on the environment.

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (2) If the minister believes on reasonable grounds that a person is transporting or is about to transport beetle-infested timber and that the transportation of the timber will or probably will cause or has caused an adverse impact on the environment, the minister, by order that meets the prescribed requirements, may require the person

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (a) to stop or refrain from transporting the beetle-infested timber, and

paragraph: (b) to carry out specified measures to reduce the potential for the adverse impact on the environment.

heading: Power of intervention: general
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe the circumstances in which and the conditions on which a person who has taken measures under subsection (1) or (2) may recover all or part of an amount reasonably incurred for the direct costs of carrying out the measures.

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: 77.1		  (1) If an operational plan for an area is approved and the minister subsequently concludes, on the basis of information that was not known to the person who granted the approval, that carrying out a forest practice or range practice under the plan will continue or result in a potential unjustifiable infringement of an aboriginal right or title in respect of the area, the minister

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (a) must notify the holder of the plan of the previously unavailable information,

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (b) by order given to the holder of the plan, may vary or suspend to the extent the minister considers necessary one or more of the following:

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (i)  the operational plan;

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (iii)  a cutting permit;

paragraph: (iv)  a road permit, and

paragraph: (c) by order given to the holder of a BC timber sales agreement who is operating under the plan, may vary or suspend to the extent the minister considers necessary one or both of the following:

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (ii)  a BC timber sales agreement.

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (2) If the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act is exempt under this Act from the requirement to have an operational plan for an area and the minister subsequently concludes, on the basis of information that was not known to the person who granted the exemption, that carrying out a forest practice or range practice under the exemption will continue or result in a potential unjustifiable infringement of an aboriginal right or title in respect of the area, the minister

paragraph: (a) must notify the following of the previously unavailable information:

paragraph: (ii)  a forest practice or range practice;

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (3) If the minister considers that an order under subsection (1) (b) or (2) (b) is no longer necessary, in whole or in part, the minister must promptly rescind the order except for those aspects, if any, that the minister considers are still necessary.

heading: Power of intervention: Indigenous nations
paragraph: (4) If an order under this section requires the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act to carry out a measure that results in the holder incurring expenses that are greater than if the order had not been made, then, to the extent provided in the regulations, the additional expenses of the measure are to be paid by the government.

heading: Determinations stayed until proceedings concluded
paragraph: 78		  (1) A determination that may be reviewed under section 80 or appealed under section 82 is stayed until the person who is the subject of the determination has no further right to have the determination reviewed or appealed.

heading: Determinations stayed until proceedings concluded
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the minister may order that a determination, other than a determination to impose an administrative penalty under section 74 or 74.4 (1) (d) or to make an order under section 74.6, is not stayed or is stayed subject to conditions, on being satisfied that a stay or a stay without those conditions, as the case may be, would be contrary to the public interest.

heading: Determinations stayed until proceedings concluded
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), a determination is not stayed if the determination is made under prescribed sections or for prescribed purposes.

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph:
79
		  (1) Within 15 days after a determination is made under section 2.39 (1), 16, 26 (2), 27 (2), 32 (2), 37, 51 (7), 54 (2), 57 (4), 66, 71, 74, 74.2, 74.4, 74.6 or 77 of this Act, the person who made the determination may

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (a) correct a typographical, an arithmetical or another similar error in the determination, and

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (c) correct an obvious error or omission in the determination.

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (2) The correction does not take effect until the date on which the person who is the subject of the determination is notified of it under subsection (4).

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (3) The discretion conferred under subsection (1)

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (a) is to be exercised in the same manner as the determination affected by it, and

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (b) is exercisable with or without a hearing and

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (i)  on the initiative of the person who made the determination, or

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (ii)  at the request of the person who is the subject of the determination.

heading: Correction of a determination
paragraph: (4) The person who corrected a determination under this section must notify the person who is the subject of the determination.

heading: Review of a determination
paragraph:
80
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), at the request of a person who is the subject of a determination under section 2.39 (1), 16, 20 (3), 26 (2), 27 (2), 32 (2), 37, 38 (5), 39, 51 (7), 54 (2), 57 (4), 66, 71, 74, 74.2, 74.4, 74.6, 77, 77.1, 97 (3), 107, 108 (1) or (2), 108.3 (2), 112 (1) (a) or 155 (2) of this Act, the person who made the determination, or another person employed in the ministry and designated in writing by the minister must review the determination, but only if satisfied that there is evidence that was not available at the time of the original determination.

heading: Review of a determination
paragraph: (2) On a review required under subsection (1) the person conducting the review may consider only

heading: Review of a determination
paragraph: (a) evidence that was not available at the time of the original determination, and

heading: Review of a determination
paragraph: (b) the record pertaining to the original determination.

heading: Review of a determination
paragraph: (3) To obtain a review of a determination under subsection (1) the person must request the review not later than 3 weeks after the date the notice of determination was given to the person.

heading: Review of a determination
paragraph: (4) The minister may extend the time limit for requiring a review under this section before or after its expiry.

heading: Review of a determination
paragraph: (5) The person conducting the review has the same discretion to make a decision that the original decision maker had at the time of the determination under the review.

heading: Board may require review of a determination
paragraph:
81
		  (1) If the board first receives the consent of the person who is the subject of a determination under section 2.39 (1), 16, 37, 71, 74, 74.2, 74.4 or 74.6 of this Act, the board may require a review of the determination by the person who made the determination, or another person employed in the ministry and designated in writing by the minister.

heading: Board may require review of a determination
paragraph: (2) To obtain a review of a determination under subsection (1), the board must require the review not later than 3 weeks after the date the notice of determination was given to the person.

heading: Board may require review of a determination
paragraph: (3) The minister may extend the time limit for requiring a review under this section before or after its expiry.

heading: Board may require review of a determination
paragraph: (4) The person conducting the review has the same discretion to make a decision that the original decision maker had at the time of the determination under the review.

heading: Appeal to the commission by a person who is the subject of a determination
paragraph:
82
		  (1) The person who is the subject of a determination referred to in section 80, other than a determination made under section 77.1, may appeal to the commission either of the following, but not both:

heading: Appeal to the commission by a person who is the subject of a determination
paragraph: (a) the determination;

heading: Appeal to the commission by a person who is the subject of a determination
paragraph: (b) a decision made after completion of a review of the determination.

heading: Appeal to the commission by a person who is the subject of a determination
paragraph: (2) The board, if it so requests, has standing to be a party to an appeal under this section.

heading: Appeal to the commission by the board
paragraph:
83
		  (1) The board may appeal to the commission either of the following, but not both:

heading: Appeal to the commission by the board

heading: Appeal to the commission by the board
paragraph: (b) a decision made after completion of a review of the determination.

paragraph: (a) by a person under section 82 (1), or

paragraph: (b) by the board under section 83 (1),

paragraph: (c) consider the findings of the person who made the determination or decision, and

paragraph: (i)  confirm, vary or rescind the determination or decision, or

paragraph: (2) On application under section 83 (2) by the board, the commission may order the minister to make a determination under the applicable provision referred to in section 83 (2) (a).

85
		  (1) The minister must publish an annual report on enforcement activities.

paragraph: (a) is admissible without proof of the signature or official character of the individual appearing to have signed the document, and
