heading: Fines
paragraph:
87
		  (1) A person who contravenes section 46 (1), 52 (1) or (3) or 112 (3) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1 000 000, or to imprisonment for not more than 3 years, or to both.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes section 20.21 (1), 20.22 (1), 22 (2), 22.1 (1), 23.1 (1), 29 (0.1), (1) or (3), 55 (a) or 110.1 (1) or (2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $500 000, or to imprisonment for not more than 2 years, or to both.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (3) A person who

heading: Fines
paragraph: commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $100 000, or to imprisonment for not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (5) The maximum fine to which a person is liable on a second or subsequent conviction for the same offence under subsections (1) to (4) is double the amount set out in the applicable subsection.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (6) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide by regulation that

heading: Fines
paragraph: (a) a contravention of a regulation or standard is an offence, and

heading: Fines
paragraph: (b) a person convicted of an offence for a contravention of a regulation or standard is liable to a fine not exceeding a maximum amount, or to imprisonment not exceeding a maximum length, or to both.

heading: Fines
paragraph: (7) If the maximum fine or imprisonment provided by a regulation under subsection (6) (b) is less than that provided by a provision of this Act, the regulation prevails.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph:
88
		  (1) A proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under this Act does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: (2) The provisions of this Part are in addition to the provisions of any other enactment or rule of law under which

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: (a) a remedy or right of appeal or objection is provided, or

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: (b) a procedure is provided for inquiry into or investigation of a matter,

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: and nothing in this Act limits or affects that remedy, right, objection or procedure.

heading: Limitation on proceedings

89
		  (1) The government may not proceed under this Act with both an offence and an administrative penalty for the same contravention.

heading: Limitation on proceedings
paragraph:
(2) 
              Subsection (1) does not derogate from the government's ability to make an order respecting compensation or remediation.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph:
90
		  (1) If the minister considers that a person is not complying, or has not complied, with an order made under section 26 (6), 27 (2), 38 (5), 39 (2), 51 (7), 54 (2), 57 (4), 58 (1), 61 (1), 66 (1), 74.2 (2) or 77 of this Act, the minister may apply to the Supreme Court for either or both of the following:

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (a) an order directing the person to comply with the order or restraining the person from violating the order;

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (b) an order directing the directors and officers of the person to cause the person to comply with or to stop violating the order.

heading: Order for compliance
paragraph: (2) On application by the minister under this section, the Supreme Court may make an order it considers appropriate.

heading: Court order to comply
paragraph:
91
		  If a person is convicted of an offence under a provision of this Act or of the regulations, then, in addition to any punishment the court may impose, the court may order the person to comply with the provision.

heading: Restitution
paragraph:
92
		  If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, then, in addition to any other penalty, the court may order the person to pay compensation or make restitution.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph:
93
		  If a contravention of section 46 (1), 50 (1) and (2), 54 (1), 55 or 57 (1) continues for more than one day, the offender is liable to a separate penalty, without notice and without a separate count being laid, for each day that the contravention occurs.

heading: Prosecution for unauthorized timber cutting
paragraph:
94
		  It is not a defence to a prosecution under section 52 or 53 that the person charged with the offence had the right to cut or remove timber on private land adjacent to Crown land and did not know the boundaries of the private land.

heading: Prosecution for unauthorized grazing or unauthorized cutting or storage of hay
paragraph:
95
		  It is not a defence to a prosecution under section 50 that the person charged with the offence had the right to graze livestock or cut, remove or store hay on private land adjacent to Crown land and did not know the boundaries of the private land.

heading: Prosecution for unauthorized trail or recreational facility construction
paragraph:
96
		  It is not a defence to a prosecution under section 57 that the person charged with the offence had the right to construct, rehabilitate or maintain a recreation site or trail

heading: Prosecution for unauthorized trail or recreational facility construction
paragraph: (a) on private land adjacent to Crown land and did not know the boundaries of the private land, or

heading: Prosecution for unauthorized trail or recreational facility construction
paragraph: (b) on Crown land on which the person was authorized under another enactment to carry out the activities and did not know the boundaries of that parcel of Crown land.

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph:
97
		  (1) In this section, "person acting in an official capacity" means an individual who is

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (a) employed under the Public Service Act or is a member of the board, the commission or the council, if any, or is a person retained under section 138 (2), and

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (b) exercising a power or performing a duty or function under this Act.

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (2) A person must not

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (a) without lawful excuse, intentionally interfere with a person acting in an official capacity,

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (b) without lawful excuse, intentionally not comply with a lawful requirement of a person acting in an official capacity, or

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (c) intentionally make a false statement to, or mislead or attempt to mislead, a person acting in an official capacity.

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (3) The minister may suspend or cancel

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (a) a forest operations plan, forest stewardship plan, a woodlot licence plan, a range use plan or a range stewardship plan, or

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: (b) a permit under this Act

heading: Interference, non-compliance and misleading
paragraph: if the minister, after giving a person who is alleged to have contravened subsection (2) an opportunity to be heard, considers that the person has contravened subsection (2) and that a plan or permit has been obtained as a result of that contravention.

heading: Court orders
paragraph: 98		  If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, then in addition to any other punishment that may be imposed, the court may, by order, do one or more of the following:

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (a) prohibit the person from doing anything that may result in the continuation or repetition of the offence or contravention;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (b) direct the person to take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment that results or may result from the act or omission that constituted the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (c) direct the person to publish, at the person's own cost, the facts relating to the conviction;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (d) direct the person to compensate the minister for all or part of the cost of any remedial or preventative action taken by or caused to be taken on behalf of the ministry as a result of the act or omission that constituted the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (e) direct the person to pay court costs;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (f) direct the person to pay the costs of the investigation.

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph:
99
		  (1) The court that convicts a person of an offence under this Act may increase a fine imposed on the person by an amount equal to the court's estimation of the amount of the monetary benefit acquired by or that accrued to the person as a result of the commission of the offence.

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (2) A fine increased under subsection (1)

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (a) applies despite any provision that provides for a maximum fine, and

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (b) is in addition to any other fine under this Act.

heading: Employer liability
paragraph:
100
		  (1) In a prosecution for an offence under this Act, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by the defendant's contractor, employee or agent.

heading: Employer liability
paragraph: (2) This section applies even if the contractor, employee or agent has not been identified or prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Defences to a prosecution
paragraph:
101
		  Due diligence, mistake of fact and officially induced error are defences to a prosecution under this Act.

heading: Offence by directors and officers
paragraph:
102
		  If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, a director or officer of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence also commits the offence.

heading: Section 5 Offence Act
paragraph:
103
		  Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act, the regulations or the standards.

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: 103.1		  (1) In this section:

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: "fine" means an amount payable under the Acts or the Offence Act in respect of a conviction, or a violation ticket issued, for an offence against a provision of the Acts, whether payable as a penalty or otherwise and whether payable to the government, the court or another person or entity, and includes a victim surcharge levy under section 8.1 of the Victims of Crime Act;

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: "sanction" includes a direction, decision or order.

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (2) In accordance with section 33 (2) (e) of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, the minister may disclose the following information inside or outside Canada with respect to a person who is convicted of an offence, has paid or is liable to pay an administrative penalty or is subject to another sanction under a provision of the Acts:

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (a) the name of the person;

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (b) the provision of the Acts

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (i)  that the person contravened, or

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (ii)  under which a sanction has been imposed;

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (c) the location at which

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (i)  the contravention occurred, or

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (ii)  the conduct or circumstances that resulted in the sanction arose;

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (d) a description of

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (i)  the contravention, or

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (ii)  the conduct or circumstances that resulted in the sanction;

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (e) the fine, sentence, administrative penalty or other sanction to which the person is subject;

heading: Disclosure of information
paragraph: (f) if a fine, administrative penalty or other amount owing as a result of a sanction is overdue, the date it was due and the outstanding amount.

heading: Protection against libel and slander
paragraph:
105
		  For the purposes of any Act or law respecting libel or slander,

heading: Protection against libel and slander
paragraph: (a) anything said, all information supplied and all records and things produced in the course of an investigation, an inquiry or proceedings before the board, commission or council, if any, under this Act are privileged to the same extent as if the investigation, inquiry or proceedings were proceedings in a court, and

heading: Protection against libel and slander
paragraph: (b) a report made by the board and a fair and accurate account of the report in a newspaper, periodical publication or broadcast is privileged to the same extent as if the report of the board were the order of the court.

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph:
106
		  (1) A person is liable to the government

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) for costs incurred by the government in controlling or disposing of insects, diseases, animals or abiotic factors, and

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) the value of Crown timber damaged or destroyed or of forage damaged or destroyed,

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph: directly or indirectly, as a result of the person's non-compliance with an order under section 26 or 27.

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph: (2) A person is liable to the government for the market value of any

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) timber cut, damaged or destroyed without authorization under this Act, or

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) forage or hay cut, damaged or destroyed without authorization under this Act.

heading: Liability of persons to government
paragraph: (3) A person is liable to the government for an economic gain that results, directly or indirectly, from the person's act or omission that would have been a contravention or an offence under this Act if it were not for the defence of due diligence, mistake of fact or officially induced error.

heading: Definition for sections 107 and 108
paragraph:
106.1
		  In sections 107 and 108, "operational plan" includes

heading: Definition for sections 107 and 108
paragraph: (a) a forest development plan,

heading: Definition for sections 107 and 108
paragraph: (b) a logging plan,

heading: Definition for sections 107 and 108
paragraph: (c) a range use plan, and

heading: Definition for sections 107 and 108
paragraph: (d) a site level plan

heading: Definition for sections 107 and 108
paragraph: to which Part 11 of this Act applies.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph:
107
		  (1) Subject to subsections (1.1) and (1.2), a person who holds an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act or who meets the prescribed requirements may submit to the district manager a written declaration specifying that one or more of the following have been fulfilled:

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) an obligation under this Act;

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) an obligation under an operational plan;

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (c) an obligation under a permit or other authorization.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (1.1) A person who holds an agreement under the Forest Act must submit to the district manager a written declaration if the person has fulfilled an obligation under section 29 to establish a free growing stand.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (1.2) In prescribed circumstances, a person who holds an agreement under the Forest Act must submit to the district manager a written declaration if the person has fulfilled an obligation referred to in subsection (1) (a), (b) or (c) to deactivate a road.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (2) A declaration submitted by a person under subsection (1) must

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) be signed by

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (i)  the person, or

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (ii)  one or more individuals whom the person authorizes to sign the declaration on the person's behalf,

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) specify the date on which the declaration is made, and

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (c) specify any of the following things that are relevant to the fulfillment of the obligation:

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (i)  cutblocks and roads;

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (ii)  operational plans;

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (iii)  permits.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (2.1) A declaration under subsection (1.1) or (1.2) must

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) meet the requirements set out in subsection (2), and

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) be submitted by the prescribed date, if any.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (4) to (6), on the date that a written declaration under subsection (1), (1.1) or (1.2) has been submitted, the person who submitted the declaration is deemed to have fulfilled the obligation specified in the declaration.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (4) If

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) within the prescribed period after receiving a declaration submitted by a person under subsection (1), and

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) after giving the person an opportunity to be heard,

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: the minister determines by order that an obligation specified in the declaration has not been fulfilled, the minister must give written notice of the order to the person, including with the notice the reasons for the order.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (5) The minister must not give written notice under subsection (4) of an order to the effect that an obligation in respect of establishing a free growing stand on an area has not been fulfilled unless the minister has determined that

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) a free growing stand has not been established, or

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) a free growing stand has been established and the following circumstances apply:

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (i)  at the time the declaration was made, the stand was under threat from

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (A) competing plants, shrubs or other trees established on the area, or

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (B) factors adverse to forest health in the area;

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (ii)  as a result of the threats referred to in subparagraph (i), the stand is unlikely to remain a free growing stand without further treatment.

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (6) A person who submits a declaration under this section remains responsible for fulfilling an obligation that was specified under the declaration as having been fulfilled if

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (a) the minister has determined by order under subsection (4), of which notice has been given in accordance with that section, that the obligation has not been fulfilled, or

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (b) the person

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (i)  made a material misrepresentation or misstatement of fact in the declaration in relation to the obligation, or

heading: Limitation on liability of persons to government
paragraph: (ii)  omitted information from the declaration that the person knew or ought to have known was material to determining whether the obligation had been fulfilled.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: 108		  (0.1) A person may apply to the minister, in accordance with the regulations,

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (a) for relief under subsection (1) if the person has an obligation under this Act or an operational plan, other than

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (i)  an obligation to establish a free growing stand, or

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (ii)  a prescribed obligation, or

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (b) for relief or funding under subsection (2) if the person has an obligation to establish a free growing stand.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (1) On application under subsection (0.1) (a) by a person who has an obligation referred to in that subsection, the minister must grant the relief described in subsection (3) if the minister is satisfied that

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (a) because of an event causing damage in an area, the obligation cannot be met in the area without significant extra expense than would have been the case if the damage had not occurred, and

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (b) any of the following applies:

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (i)  the person did not cause or contribute to the cause of the damage;

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (ii)  the person exercised due diligence in relation to the cause of the damage;

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (iii)  the person did contribute to the cause of the damage but only as a result of an officially induced error.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (2) On application under subsection (0.1) (b) by a person who has an obligation to establish a free growing stand, the minister must grant one of the following if satisfied that the criteria described in subsection (1) (a) and (b) are met:

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (a) relief from the obligation, as described in subsection (3);

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (b) funding for establishing the free growing stand, as described in subsection (4).

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (3) The relief, that must be granted under subsection (1) or that may be granted under subsection (2) (a), from an obligation by the minister to a person is relief from

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (a) the person's obligation to the extent only that the obligation cannot be met without significant extra expense related to the damage referred to in subsection (1) or (2), or

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (b) the person's obligation in full if the minister considers that the remaining obligation, after taking paragraph (a) of this subsection into account, is inconsequential.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (4) The funding for establishing a free growing stand, that may be granted under subsection (2) (b) by the minister to a person, is funding to the extent only that is required for the purpose of restoring the stand of trees on the area affected by the event referred to in subsection (2)

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (a) to the stage the stand had reached at the time of the damage caused by the event, or

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (b) to the stage that is consistent with an agreement between the person and the minister.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (4.1) The minister, in granting relief under subsection (2) (a) from an obligation to establish a free growing stand, may impose a condition that the person pay to the government the amount that would have been spent to establish the free growing stand from the stage the stand had reached at the time the damage occurred.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (4.3) After granting funding to a person under subsection (2) (b), the minister may grant relief to that person from the obligation to establish the free growing stand if, as a result of a change of circumstances or based on new information, the minister is satisfied that the obligation cannot be met without significant extra expense.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (5) A decision in any proceedings, that a person having an obligation referred to in subsection (0.1) (a) or (b) did or did not do any of the things described in subsection (1) (b), is binding on the minister.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (6) The minister may not under this section grant relief or funding in respect of an event causing damage if the event occurred before December 17, 2002.

heading: Government may fund extra expense or waive obligation
paragraph: (8) The minister may not under subsection (2) grant relief from or funding for an obligation to establish a free growing stand in an area of catastrophic damage if the relief or funding is being sought in relation to the event that caused the catastrophic damage.

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph:
108.2
		  (1) The minister may, by order, designate an area of land as an area of catastrophic damage if catastrophic damage has occurred on the land as a result of either of the following events:

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (a) wildfire;

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (b) a prescribed natural event.

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (2) The minister may do one or both of the following in an order made under subsection (1):

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (a) grant relief to a person or a class of persons from an obligation under this Act or an operational plan to establish a free growing stand in the area of catastrophic damage;

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (b) impose conditions in relation to relief granted under paragraph (a), including requiring payment to the government for the amount that would have been spent to establish a free growing stand from the stage the stand had reached at the time the catastrophic damage occurred.

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (3) The minister's discretion under subsection (2) may be exercised differently for

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (a) different persons or classes of persons, and

heading: Areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (b) different locations within an area of catastrophic damage.

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph:
108.3
		  (1) A person may apply to the minister, in accordance with the regulations, for relief under subsection (2) if the person has an obligation under this Act or an operational plan to establish a free growing stand in an area of catastrophic damage.

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (2) On application under subsection (1) by a person who has an obligation to establish a free growing stand, the minister may grant to the person one of the following:

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (a) relief from the obligation if the minister is satisfied that it is not practicable for the person to complete the obligation given the circumstances or conditions of the area to which the obligation relates;

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (b) funding for establishing the free growing stand, but only to the extent that is required for the purposes of restoring the stand of trees on the area of catastrophic damage

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (i)  to the stage the stand had reached at the time the catastrophic damage occurred, or

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (ii)  to the stage that is consistent with an agreement between the person and the minister.

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (3) The minister, in granting relief under subsection (2) (a), may impose a condition that the person pay to the government the amount that would have been spent to establish the free growing stand from the stage the stand had reached at the time the catastrophic damage occurred.

heading: Relief and funding for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (5) After granting funding to a person under subsection (2) (b), the minister may grant relief to that person from the obligation to establish the free growing stand if, as a result of a change of circumstances or based on new information, the minister is satisfied that it is not practicable for the person to complete the obligation given the circumstances or conditions of the area to which the obligation relates.

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph:
108.4
		  (1) The minister may establish a plan for reforesting an area of catastrophic damage.

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (2) If a person has an obligation under this Act or an operational plan to establish a free growing stand at a particular location in an area of catastrophic damage, the minister may, after establishing a plan under subsection (1), authorize the person to instead establish a free growing stand at a different location in the area of catastrophic damage.

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (3) The minister may not under subsection (2) authorize a person to establish a free growing stand at a different location, unless

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (a) the plan under subsection (1) provides for establishing the free growing stand at the different location,

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (b) the cost of establishing the free growing stand at the different location will be similar to the cost of establishing the free growing stand required at the original location, and

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (c) the person agrees to establish the free growing stand at the different location.

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (4) If the minister authorizes a person to establish a free growing stand at a different location under subsection (2) and funding may be granted under section 108.3 (2) (b) to the person to establish the free growing stand required at the original location, the minister may grant that funding to the person for the purposes of establishing the free growing stand at the different location.

heading: Plans for areas of catastrophic damage
paragraph: (5) If a person fails to establish a free growing stand at a different location as authorized under subsection (2), the person contravenes the obligation under the Act or operational plan to establish the free growing stand at the original location.

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (a) providing that the funding will be paid in instalments;

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (b) specifying that one or more of the following must happen before or after funding is paid:

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (i)  an event occur;

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (ii)  an action be taken;

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (iii)  a specific requirement or specific criteria be met;

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (c) requiring the person who is granted funding to prepare and submit plans or reports;

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (d) providing for a person designated by the minister to

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (i)  carry out surveys, investigations or analyses, or

heading: Conditions in relation to funding
paragraph: (ii)  perform audits.

heading: Payment of monies into Silviculture Payments Sub-account
paragraph:
108.6
		  The following money collected by the government must be paid into the Silviculture Payments Sub-account of the Forest Stand Management Fund special account established by the Special Accounts Appropriation and Control Act:

heading: Payment of monies into Silviculture Payments Sub-account
paragraph: (a) money paid to fulfill a condition imposed under section 108 (4.1) or 108.3 (3);

heading: Payment of monies into Silviculture Payments Sub-account
paragraph: (b) money paid to fulfill a condition imposed under section 108.2 (2) (b) in an order made under section 108.2 (1).

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: 109		  (1) In this section:

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: "information" includes a record;

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: "person" means

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (a) the government, board, commission or council, if any,

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (b) an employee, agent and independent contractor of the government, board, commission or council, if any, or

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (c) a member of the board, commission or council, if any.

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (2) Each of the following persons must take an oath that he or she will not disclose information obtained under this Act except as permitted by this section and under the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act:

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (a) a member of the board, commission or council, if any;

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (b) an employee of the board, commission or council, if any;

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (c) a person appointed to carry out an audit referred to in section 122;

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (d) a specialist or consultant retained by the board, commission or council, if any.

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (3) A person must not disclose any information obtained in the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty or function under this Act except

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (a) as required for the performance of his or her duties under this Act, or

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (b) as permitted in this section or under the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act.

heading: Confidentiality and disclosure to government
paragraph: (4) A person may disclose to the government any information obtained in the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty or function under this Act.

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: 110		  (1) A notice or another document that the government or board is required or permitted to give to a person under this Act may be given by giving it, or a copy of it, to the person as follows:

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (a) if the person is an individual,

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (i)  by leaving it with the individual,

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (ii)  by leaving it at the individual's last or most usual place of residence with someone who is or appears to be at least 16 years of age, or

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (iii)  by mailing it by registered mail to the individual's last known postal address;

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (b) if the person is a corporation,

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (i)  by leaving it with

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (A) a director, an officer or a manager of the corporation,

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (B) a receptionist at a place of business of the corporation, or

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (C) if the corporation is an extraprovincial company within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act, the corporation's attorney, if any, within the meaning of that Act,

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (ii)  by leaving it at the registered office of the corporation if the corporation is a company within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act or, if that office has been eliminated under section 40 of the Business Corporations Act, the address ordered by the court under section 40 (4) (b) of that Act, or

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (iii)  by mailing it by registered mail to

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (A) the registered office of the corporation or, if that office has been eliminated under section 40 of the Business Corporations Act, the address ordered by the court under section 40 (4) (b) of that Act,

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (B) if the corporation is an extraprovincial company within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act, the corporation's attorney, if any, within the meaning of that Act, or

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (C) an address provided by the corporation for service;

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (c) if the person is a municipal corporation, regional district or other local government body, by leaving it with or sending it by registered mail to the local government corporate officer, the deputy of that officer or some similar local government officer.

heading: How notice may be given
paragraph: (2) A notice or another document that is mailed to a person by registered mail under subsection (1) is conclusively deemed to be received by the person on the eighth day after it is mailed.

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: 110.1		  (1) A person who submits information to the government for the purposes of seeking approval by the minister in relation to a matter under this Act must ensure that, at the time the information is submitted, the information is complete and accurate.

heading: Complete and accurate information
paragraph: (2) A person who is required under this Act to submit information to the government must ensure that, at the time the information is submitted, the information is complete and accurate.

heading: Orders
paragraph:
111
		  An order of the minister under this Act must be in writing and given to each person to whom the order pertains.

heading: Power to impose conditions
paragraph:
112
		  (1) Except in prescribed circumstances a person with a discretion under this Act to make an order, grant an exemption, give a consent, grant an approval, or grant an authorization under this Act may

heading: Power to impose conditions
paragraph: (a) impose conditions that the person considers necessary or desirable in respect of the order, exemption, consent, approval or authorization, and

heading: Power to impose conditions
paragraph: (b) remove or vary the conditions by own motion or on the application of a person who is the subject of the order, exemption, consent, approval or authorization.

heading: Power to impose conditions
paragraph: (2) A condition imposed under subsection (1) is conclusively deemed to be part of the order, exemption, consent, approval or authorization in respect of which it is imposed, whether contained in or attached to it or contained in a separate document.

heading: Power to impose conditions
paragraph: (3) If a person is the subject of an order, exemption or condition under this Act, the person must comply with the order, exemption or condition.

heading: Extension of time
paragraph:
113
		  The minister, or a person the minister authorizes in writing, may extend a time required to do anything under this Act other than

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (a) an appeal of a determination,

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (b) the time within which a proceeding must or may be commenced,

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (c) the time within which the minister must give the notice referred to in section 107 (4), or

heading: Extension of time
paragraph: (d) anything under the regulations or standards if the regulations or standards specifically provide otherwise.

heading: Evidence of designation
paragraph:
114
		  A document purporting to have been issued by a minister referred to in the definition of "official" in section 1, certifying that the minister has designated a person as an official under this Act, is admissible as evidence of the designation without proof of the signature or official character of the minister purporting to have signed the document.

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph:
115
		  A power under this Act of the minister or an official to

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: (a) make an order,

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: (b) impose a fine or penalty, or

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: (c) commence a proceeding

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: may be exercised separately, concurrently or cumulatively, and does not affect the exercise of any other powers of the minister, official or both under this or another enactment.

heading: Amendment or remedial action does not affect offences or penalties
paragraph:
116
		  (1) An amendment to an operational plan does not affect any fine, imprisonment, fee, charge or penalty to which a person may be liable under this Act, if the offence or contravention occurred before the amendment.

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph:
118
		  (1) The government may enter into agreements to assist in ensuring that forest resources and range resources are properly managed and conserved.

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), on behalf of the government,

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) the chief forester or a person authorized by the chief forester may enter into agreements in respect of

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (i)  the growing and disposing of seed and tree gene resources, and

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (ii)  intellectual property associated with seed and tree gene resources that is owned by the government,

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (a.1) an official designated by the minister may enter into an agreement with a person to develop, maintain or remove a range development,

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) an official designated by the minister may enter into agreements for the control and disposal of insects, diseases, animals and abiotic factors on forest land and for sharing costs of control and disposal,

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (c) the minister or an official designated by the minister may enter into agreements under which the government provides

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (i)  forest or range protection services,

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (ii)  forest or range health services, or

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (iii)  services related to operations under agreements under the Forest Act that are carried out before or after timber is harvested, or

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (d) an official designated by the minister may enter into an agreement with a person to develop, expand, maintain, repair or close an interpretive forest site, a recreation site, a recreation trail or a trail-based recreation area.

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), an amount equal to any money paid to the government under an agreement referred to in subsection (2) (c) for a purpose specified in that subsection

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (a) is appropriated for that purpose,

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (b) is in addition to any other amount appropriated for that purpose, and

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (c) is to be paid out of the consolidated revenue fund without any other appropriation other than this subsection.

heading: Power to enter into agreements
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not apply if the official designated to enter into the agreement is a BC Timber Sales official.

heading: Whistle-blower protection
paragraph: 119		  A person must not evict, discharge, suspend, expel, intimidate, coerce, impose any pecuniary or other penalty on, or otherwise discriminate against, a person because that person complains or is named in a complaint, gives evidence or otherwise assists in respect of a prosecution, a complaint or another proceeding under this Act.

heading: Costs of performing obligations
paragraph:
120
		  (1) If this Act, a regulation or a standard requires a person to perform an obligation or otherwise comply with this Act, the regulations or the standards, the person must do so at the person's own expense unless another provision of this Act or the regulations specifically provides otherwise.

heading: Costs of performing obligations
paragraph: (2) If a person is required under this Act to submit an operational plan for approval to a person acting on behalf of the government, any implementation of the plan is at the person's own expense unless another provision of this Act or the regulations specifically provides otherwise.

heading: Delegation power
paragraph:
120.1
		  (1) Subject to a regulation made under section 141 (3) (b), each of the ministers responsible, respectively, for this Act, Part 7.1 of the Land Act and the Wildlife Act, in writing, may delegate a power or duty of that minister under this Act, including a quasi-judicial power or duty, to

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (a) a person employed in a ministry,

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (b) a class of persons employed in a ministry, or

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (c) an agent of the Crown.

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a minister authorized by a regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council under section 149.1 (1) (a), 150 (1) (a), 150.1 (1), 150.2 (1) (a) or (b), 150.3 (1) (a) or (b), 150.5 (e), 154 (2) (a) or 157 (2) (d) to exercise a power or perform a duty may delegate that power or duty only to

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (a) a person employed in a ministry, or

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (b) a class of persons employed in a ministry.

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (3) In respect of a power or duty delegated under this section, this Act and the regulations and standards apply to the delegate as if the delegate were the minister who made the delegation.

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (4) A minister referred to in subsection (1) or (2) may

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (a) provide directions that are binding on the delegate respecting the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty, and

heading: Delegation power
paragraph: (b) vary or revoke a delegation or direction.

heading: Subdelegation
paragraph: 120.2		  (1) Except in prescribed circumstances and if not prohibited by a direction of the minister under section 120.1 (4) (a), a delegate under section 120.1 (1) may subdelegate the power or duty to

heading: Subdelegation
paragraph: (a) a person employed in a ministry,

heading: Subdelegation
paragraph: (b) a class of persons employed in a ministry, or

heading: Subdelegation
paragraph: (c) an agent of the Crown.

heading: Subdelegation
paragraph: (2) Except in prescribed circumstances and if not prohibited by a direction of the minister under section 120.1 (4) (a), a delegate under section 120.1 (2) may subdelegate the power or duty to

heading: Subdelegation
paragraph: (a) a person employed in a ministry, or

heading: Subdelegation
paragraph: (b) a class of persons employed in a ministry.

heading: Evidence of delegation
paragraph:
120.3
		  A document purporting to have been issued by a minister referred to in section 120.1 (1) or (2), certifying that the minister has made a delegation under this Act, is admissible as evidence of the delegation without proof of the signature or official character of the minister purporting to have signed the document.

heading: Definition of "party"
paragraph:
121
		  In this Part and the regulations related to this Part, "party" means

heading: Definition of "party"
paragraph: (a) the government,

heading: Definition of "party"
paragraph: (b) the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act,

heading: Definition of "party"
paragraph: (c) the holder of an agreement under the Range Act,

heading: Definition of "party"
paragraph: (d) a person responsible for establishing a free growing stand as a result of an agreement referred to in section 29.1 (1) or (3),

heading: Definition of "party"
paragraph: (e) a person responsible for maintaining or deactivating a road, under a regulation under section 155 (1) (d), or

heading: Definition of "party"
paragraph: (f) a person referred to in section 122 (2) who may be audited or investigated under that section.

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: 122		  (1) In accordance with the regulations, the board

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (a) must carry out periodic independent audits, and

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (b) may carry out special investigations

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: to determine

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (c) compliance with the requirements of Parts 1.1 to 5 and the regulations and standards made in relation to those Parts by a party, and

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (d) the appropriateness of government enforcement under Part 6.

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (2) If

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (a) while carrying out under subsection (1) (a) or (b) an audit or investigation of a party in respect of a matter referred to in subsection (1) (c), the board finds that the party complied with the requirements audited or investigated, and

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (b) the only reason for that finding is that

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (i)  the party exercised due diligence to prevent non-compliance,

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (ii)  the party reasonably believed in the existence of facts that if true would establish that the party complied with the requirement, or

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: (iii)  the party's actions relevant to the requirement were the result of an officially induced error,

heading: Audits and special investigations
paragraph: the board may audit or investigate whether a person other than that party did not comply with the requirements, in the course of acting for or at the direction of the party.

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph:
123
		  (1) In accordance with the regulations, the board must deal with complaints from the public respecting prescribed matters that relate to this Act.

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the board may refuse to investigate a complaint, or may stop investigating a complaint, if, in the opinion of the chair, any of the following applies:

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (a) the complainant knew or ought to have known of the determination to which his or her complaint relates, more than one year before the complaint was received by the board;

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (b) the law or existing administrative procedure provides a remedy adequate in the circumstances for the person aggrieved and, if the person aggrieved has not taken advantage of the remedy, there is no reasonable justification for the failure to do so;

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (c) the complaint is frivolous, vexatious, not made in good faith or concerns a trivial matter;

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (d) having regard to all the circumstances, further investigation is not necessary in order to consider the complaint;

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (e) in the circumstances, investigation would not benefit the complainant.

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (3) The board must promptly notify, in writing, the complainant and the party of its decision and the reasons for it and may indicate any other recourse that may be available to the complainant if it decides

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (a) to not investigate or further investigate a complaint, or

heading: Complaints from public
paragraph: (b) that the complaint has not been substantiated.

heading: Powers of investigation
paragraph:
124
		  (1) Without limiting sections 122 and 123, for the purposes of those sections the board may investigate a determination.

heading: Powers of investigation
paragraph: (2) The board may conduct an audit, a special investigation or a complaint investigation despite a provision to the effect that a determination is final and regardless of any right of appeal.

heading: Powers of investigation
paragraph: (3) The board may not investigate conduct occurring before the commencement of Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act.

heading: Powers of investigation
paragraph: (4) If a question arises as to the board's jurisdiction to investigate a case or class of cases, the chair may apply to the Supreme Court for a declaratory order determining the question.

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: 125		  (1) The board may require a party to provide information or records related to an audit, a special investigation or a complaint investigation.

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (2) The board may require the party to provide the information in the form and manner the board considers appropriate.

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (3) The party must comply with a requirement of the board under subsection (1) or (2).

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (4) Without restricting subsection (1), the board may do all of the following:

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (a) at any reasonable time enter and inspect business premises occupied by a party, speak in private with any person there and otherwise investigate matters within the board's jurisdiction;

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (b) require a person to provide information or produce a record or thing in his or her possession or control that relates to an investigation at a time and place the board specifies;

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (c) make copies of information provided or a record or thing produced under this section.

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (5) If the board obtains a record or thing under subsection (4) and the person from whom it was obtained requests its return, the board must, within 48 hours after receiving the request, return it to the person, but the board may again require its production in accordance with this section.

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (6) At any time while conducting an audit, a special investigation or a complaint investigation under this Act, the board may make an order requiring a person

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (a) to attend an oral or electronic hearing to give evidence on oath or affirmation or in any other manner that is admissible and relevant to an issue in the audit, special investigation or complaint investigation, or

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (b) to produce for the board a document or other thing in the person's possession or control, as specified by the board, that is admissible and relevant to an issue in the audit, special investigation or complaint investigation.

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (7) The board may apply to the court for an order

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (a) directing a person to comply with an order made by the board under subsection (6), or

heading: Power to obtain information
paragraph: (b) directing any directors and officers of a person to cause the person to comply with an order made by the board under subsection (6).

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph:
125.1
		  The failure or refusal of a person summoned as a witness under section 125 (6) to do any of the following makes the person, on application to the court by the board, liable to be committed for contempt as if in breach of an order or judgment of the court:

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph: (a) attend a hearing;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph: (b) take an oath or affirmation;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph: (c) answer questions;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph: (d) produce the records or things in their custody or possession.

heading: Immunity protection for board and members
paragraph:
125.2
		  (1) In this section, "decision maker" includes a board member, registrar or other officer who conducts an audit, a special investigation or a complaint investigation under this Act or a person who conducts a dispute resolution process for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Immunity protection for board and members
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), no legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against a decision maker, the board or the government because of anything done or omitted

heading: Immunity protection for board and members
paragraph: (a) in the performance or intended performance of any duty under this Act, or

heading: Immunity protection for board and members
paragraph: (b) in the exercise or intended exercise of any power under this Act.

heading: Immunity protection for board and members
paragraph:
(3) 
              Subsection (2) does not apply to a person referred to in that subsection in relation to anything done or omitted by that person in bad faith.

heading: Power to obtain information limited
paragraph:
126
		  The board must not require information or a record to be produced if the Attorney General certifies that the giving of the information or record may

heading: Power to obtain information limited
paragraph: (a) interfere with or impede investigation or detection of offences,

heading: Power to obtain information limited
paragraph: (b) involve the disclosure of the deliberations of the Executive Council, or

heading: Power to obtain information limited
paragraph: (c) involve the disclosure of proceedings of the Executive Council or of any committee of the Executive Council, relating to matters of a secret or confidential nature, and would be harmful to the public interest.

heading: Board must notify and consult party
paragraph:
127
		  (1) If the board conducts an audit or investigation, the board must notify the party affected and any other person the board considers appropriate.

heading: Board must notify and consult party
paragraph: (2) The board must consult with a party if the board receives a request for consultation from the party before the board has made its report under section 131.

heading: Opportunity to make representations
paragraph:
128
		  If it appears to the board that there may be sufficient grounds for making a report or recommendation under this Act that may adversely affect a party or person, the board must inform the party or person of the grounds and must give the party or person the opportunity to make representations, either orally or in writing at the discretion of the board, before it decides the matter.

heading: Evidence not admissible
paragraph:
129
		  Evidence given by a person in proceedings before the board and evidence of the existence of the proceedings are inadmissible against the person in a court or in any other proceeding of a judicial nature except for the following:

heading: Evidence not admissible
paragraph: (a) the trial of a person for perjury;

heading: Evidence not admissible
paragraph: (b) the trial of a person for an offence under section 97;

heading: Evidence not admissible
paragraph: (c) an application for judicial review or an appeal from a decision with respect to that application.

heading: Person may be reimbursed for expenses
paragraph:
130
		  If a person incurs expenses in complying with a request of the board for production of documents or other information, the board may reimburse that person for reasonable expenses.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph:
131
		  (1) Subject to subsection (1.1), after completing an audit or investigation, the board must report its conclusions, with reasons, to any complainant, to the party and, if the government is not the party affected by the audit or investigation, to the ministers.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (1.1) If an audit or investigation referred to in subsection (1) includes more than one party, the board may report its overall conclusions without reporting on compliance by each party.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (2) If the board makes a report under subsection (1), it may make recommendations it considers appropriate.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (2), the board may make any of the following recommendations:

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (a) a matter be referred to the appropriate party for further consideration;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (b) an act be remedied;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (c) an omission or delay be rectified;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (d) a decision or recommendation be cancelled or varied;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (e) reasons be given;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (f) a practice, procedure or course of conduct be altered;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (g) an enactment or other rule of law be reconsidered;

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (h) any other steps be taken.

heading: Report and recommendations
paragraph: (4) Without limiting subsection (1), the chair may, if the regulations provide and in the manner they provide, make an application under section 83 for an appeal of a determination or failure to make a determination.

heading: Party to notify board of steps taken
paragraph:
132
		  (1) If the board makes a recommendation under section 131 the board may request that the party notify it within a specified time

heading: Party to notify board of steps taken
paragraph: (a) of the steps that have been taken or are proposed to be taken to give effect to its recommendation, or

heading: Party to notify board of steps taken
paragraph: (b) if no steps have been taken or are proposed to be taken, of the reasons for not following the recommendation.

heading: Party to notify board of steps taken
paragraph: (2) If, after considering a response made by a party, the board believes it advisable to modify or further modify its recommendation, the board must notify the party and the complainant of its recommendation as modified and may request that the party notify it

heading: Party to notify board of steps taken
paragraph: (a) of the steps that have been taken or are proposed to be taken to give effect to the modified recommendation, or

heading: Party to notify board of steps taken
paragraph: (b) if no steps have been taken or are proposed to be taken, of the reasons for not following the modified recommendation.

heading: Party to notify board of steps taken
paragraph: (3) The party must respond promptly to the board's request under subsection (1) or (2).

heading: Report of board if no suitable action taken
paragraph:
133
		  (1) If, within a reasonable time after a request by the board under section 132, no action is taken that the board believes adequate or appropriate, the chair may, after considering any reasons given by the party,

heading: Report of board if no suitable action taken
paragraph: (a) submit a report on the matter to the ministers, and

heading: Report of board if no suitable action taken
paragraph: (b) after submitting a report under paragraph (a), submit a report to the Lieutenant Governor in Council respecting the matter.

heading: Report of board if no suitable action taken
paragraph: (2) The chair

heading: Report of board if no suitable action taken
paragraph: (a) must attach to the report a copy of the board's recommendation and any response made to the board under section 132,

heading: Report of board if no suitable action taken
paragraph: (b) must delete from his or her recommendation and from the response any material that would unreasonably invade any person's privacy, and

heading: Report of board if no suitable action taken
paragraph: (c) may in his or her discretion delete material revealing the identity of a member, an officer or an employee of a party.

heading: Complainant to be informed
paragraph:
134
		  After a complaint investigation, if the board makes a recommendation under section 131 or 132 (2) and no action that the board believes adequate or appropriate is taken within a reasonable time, the board must inform the complainant of its recommendation and make such additional comments as it considers appropriate.

heading: Special reports
paragraph:
135
		  If the chair considers a special report to be in the public interest, he or she may make a special report to the minister or comment publicly respecting a matter relating generally to the performance of the board's duties under this Act or to a particular case investigated by the board.

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph:
136
		  (1) The Forest Practices Board is continued.

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph: (2) The board consists of the following members appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council after a merit-based process:

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph: (a) a member designated as the chair;

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph: (b) one or more members designated as vice chairs after consultation with the chair;

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph: (c) other members appointed after consultation with the chair.

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph: (5) Sections 1 to 10, 44, 46.2 and 55 of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the board.

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph: (6) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may determine the remuneration, reimbursement of expenses and other conditions of employment of persons appointed under the regulations to carry out audits.

heading: Forest Practices Board continued
paragraph: (7) Board members must faithfully, honestly and impartially perform their duties.

heading: Panels of the board
paragraph: 137		  (1) The board may organize itself into panels, each comprised of one or more members.

heading: Panels of the board
paragraph: (2) The members of the board may sit as a board or as a panel of the board, and 2 or more panels may sit at the same time.

heading: Panels of the board
paragraph: (3) A panel of the board has the jurisdiction of the board and may exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the board.

heading: Panels of the board
paragraph: (4) A report, a recommendation or an action of a panel of the board is a report, recommendation or action of the board.

heading: Board staff
paragraph:
138
		  (1) Employees necessary to carry out the powers and duties of the board may be appointed under the Public Service Act.

heading: Board staff
paragraph: (2) In accordance with the regulations, the board may engage or retain specialists, consultants and auditors that the board considers necessary to carry out the powers and duties of the office and may determine their remuneration.

heading: Board staff
paragraph: (3) The Public Service Act does not apply to the retention, engagement or remuneration of specialists, consultants and auditors retained under subsection (2).

heading: No hearing as of right
paragraph: 139		  A person is not entitled to an oral hearing before the board.

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph:
140
		  (1) The chair may delegate in writing to a person or class of persons any of the board's powers or duties under this Act, except the power

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph: (a) of delegation under this section, or

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph: (b) to make a report under this Act.

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph: (2) A delegation under this section is revocable and does not prevent the board exercising a delegated power.

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph: (3) A delegation may be made subject to terms the chair considers appropriate.

heading: Delegation of powers
paragraph: (5) A person purporting to exercise a power of the board by virtue of a delegation under this section must, when requested to do so, produce evidence of his or her authority to exercise the power.

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph:
140.1
		  (1) The Forest Appeals Commission is continued.

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph: (2) The commission is to hear appeals under

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph: (a) section 82 or 83, or

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph: (b) the Forest Act, the Private Managed Forest Land Act, the Range Act or the Wildfire Act and, in relation to appeals under those Acts, the commission has the powers given to it by those Acts.

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph: (3) The commission consists of the following members appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council after a merit-based process:

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph: (a) a member designated as the chair;

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph: (b) one or more members designated as vice chairs after consultation with the chair;

heading: Forest Appeals Commission continued
paragraph: (c) other members appointed after consultation with the chair.

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: 140.2		  The following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the commission:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a) Part 1 [Interpretation and Application];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b) Part 2 [Appointments];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (c) Part 3 [Clustering];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (d) Part 4 [Practice and Procedure], except the following:

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (i)  section 22 [notice of appeal (inclusive of prescribed fee)];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (ii)  section 25 [appeal does not operate as stay];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (iii)  section 33 [interveners];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (iv)  section 34 (1) and (2) [party power to compel witnesses and require disclosure];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (e) Part 6 [Costs and Sanctions], except sections 47.1 [security for costs] and 47.2 [government and agents of government];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (f) Part 7 [Decisions];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (g) Part 8 [Immunities];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (h) section 59.1 [surveys];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (i) section 59.2 [reporting];

heading: Application of Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (j) Part 10 [Miscellaneous], except section 62 [application of Act to BC Review Board].

heading: Mandate of commission
paragraph: 140.3		  (1) In accordance with the regulations, the commission must

heading: Mandate of commission
paragraph: (a) hear appeals under this Act, the Forest Act, the Private Managed Forest Land Act, the Range Act or the Wildfire Act,

heading: Mandate of commission
paragraph: (b) provide the minister with an annual evaluation of the manner in which reviews and appeals under this Act, the Forest Act, the Private Managed Forest Land Act, the Range Act and the Wildfire Act are functioning and identify problems that may have arisen under the provisions of those Acts,

heading: Mandate of commission
paragraph: (c) make recommendations to the minister annually, and at other times it considers appropriate, concerning the need for amendments to this Act, the Forest Act, the Private Managed Forest Land Act, the Range Act and the Wildfire Act and related regulations respecting reviews and appeals, and

heading: Mandate of commission
paragraph: (d) perform other functions required by the regulations.

heading: Mandate of commission
paragraph: (2) The chair must give to the minister an annual report concerning the commission's activities.

heading: Mandate of commission
paragraph: (3) The minister must promptly lay the report before the Legislative Assembly if it is in session or, if it is not in session when the report is submitted, file the report with the Clerk of the Legislative Assembly.

heading: Time for appeal by board
paragraph: 140.4		  (1) If the board may appeal a decision, order or determination, the board must do so no later than 60 days after the latest of the following to occur:

heading: Time for appeal by board
paragraph: (a) the original decision, order or determination;

heading: Time for appeal by board
paragraph: (b) any correction of the original decision, order or determination;

heading: Time for appeal by board
paragraph: (c) any review of the original decision, order or determination.

heading: Time for appeal by board
paragraph: (2) The board may apply for an order under section 84 (2) no later than 60 days after the period prescribed for section 83 (2) (b) has elapsed.

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph:
140.5
		  (1) In this section, "minister" means the minister responsible for the administration of the section of the Act under which the decision, order or determination giving rise to an appeal was made.

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a notice of appeal, the commission must give a copy of the notice of appeal to the minister.

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (3) On receipt of a notice of appeal in which the board has standing, the commission must give a copy of the notice,

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (a) if a person other than the board delivered the notice, to the board, or

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (b) if the board delivered the notice,

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (i)  to the person who is the subject of the determination, or

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (ii)  for an appeal of a failure to make a determination, to the person who would be subject to the determination, if made.

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (4) The following are parties to an appeal:

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (a) the government;

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (b) the board, if it has standing and so requests;

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (c) the person who is the subject of the determination or would be the subject of the determination, if made.

heading: Persons and bodies entitled to notice and to be parties to appeal
paragraph: (5) At any stage of an appeal, the commission or a member of it may direct that a person who may be affected by the appeal be added as a party to the appeal.

heading: Appeal by new hearing
paragraph:
140.6
		  The commission may conduct an appeal by way of a new hearing.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph:
140.7
		  (1) A party to an appeal, or the minister, may appeal the decision of the commission to the Supreme Court on a question of law or jurisdiction.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (2) An appeal under subsection (1) must be filed no later than 3 weeks after the date the person filing the appeal receives the decision of the commission.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (3) On an appeal under subsection (1), a judge of the Supreme Court, on terms the judge considers appropriate, may order that all or part of the decision or order of the commission be stayed.

heading: Appeal to court
paragraph: (4) An appeal from a decision of the Supreme Court lies to the Court of Appeal with leave of a justice of the Court of Appeal.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
141
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting matters that are

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) referred to in a provision of this Act as having to be in accordance with the regulations, or

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) indicated by a provision of this Act as being a matter for a regulation.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsections (1) and (2), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) defining a word or expression used but not defined in this Act;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) for the purposes of section 120.1 (1), specifying which powers and duties of a minister under this Act must not be delegated.
