heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (4) In making a regulation under this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may do one or more of the following:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) delegate a matter to a person;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) confer a discretion on a person;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) make different regulations for different persons, places, things or transactions;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) adopt the provisions of a publication or adopt them as they are amended from time to time.

heading: Forms
paragraph: 142		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe forms for this Act.

heading: Forms
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the provision of information, to the minister or to an employee in the ministry of the minister responsible for the administration of this Act, including but not limited to regulations concerning matters related to

heading: Forms
paragraph: (a) agreements under the Forest Act, and

heading: Forms
paragraph: (b) agreements under the Range Act.

heading: Forms
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsections (1) and (2), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the form and manner in which, and time when, information must be provided.

heading: Fees or charges
paragraph: 143		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting fees or charges for the provision under this Act to any person by the government, or by the board, commission or council, if any, under this Act, of a service or any property or use of property.

heading: Fees or charges
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of this section, the preparation of a range use plan or an amendment to a range use plan by the minister is a service provided by the government to the person required to follow the plan.

heading: Fees or charges
paragraph:
(3) 
            Subsection (1) applies whether or not there is an obligation on the government to provide the service, property or use of property.

heading: Security
paragraph:
144
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting deposits and security of any kind, including but not limited to money, to be provided by the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act to ensure the performance of an obligation under this Act, the Forest Act, the Range Act or an agreement entered into under any of those Acts.

heading: Security
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the following:

heading: Security
paragraph: (a) the type of security that is acceptable or unacceptable;

heading: Security
paragraph: (b) the form and content of the security;

heading: Security
paragraph: (c) the circumstances under which the security may be realized.

heading: Recovery of money
paragraph: 145		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the recovery of money that is required to be paid to the government under this Act.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph:
146
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the exemption of a person, place, thing or transaction from a provision of this Act, the regulations or the standards.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (2) In making a regulation under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make the exemption subject to conditions.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations restricting the minister's authority to exempt a person from a provision under this Act.

heading: Criteria for exercise of discretionary powers
paragraph:
147
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the criteria that a person must use and the matters that a person must consider in exercising a discretionary power conferred on the person under this Act.

heading: Criteria for exercise of discretionary powers
paragraph: (2) Criteria or matters prescribed under subsection (1) are additional to any criteria or matters that a person is required to use or consider in exercising a discretionary power under this Act.

heading: Interpretive forest sites, recreation sites, recreation trails and trail-based recreation areas
paragraph:
148
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting interpretive forest sites, recreation sites, recreation trails and trail-based recreation areas, including but not limited to regulations that restrict, prohibit or attach conditions to the use of the interpretive forest sites, recreation sites, recreation trails and trail-based recreation areas.

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph:
149
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations prescribing objectives in relation to one or more of the following subjects:

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (a) soils;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (b) visual quality;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (c) timber;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (d) forage and associated plant communities;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (e) water;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (f) fish;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (g) wildlife;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (h) biodiversity;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (i) recreation resources;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (j) resource features;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (k) cultural heritage resources;

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (l) wildfires.

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (2) In case of an inconsistency between

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (a) an objective set by government prescribed under this section, and

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: (b) an objective referred to in paragraph (b) or (c) of the definition of "objectives set by government" in section 1 (1),

heading: Objectives set by government
paragraph: the objective referred to in paragraph (b) or (c) of that definition prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph:
149.1
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (a) authorizing the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act to establish one or more of the following:

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (i)  an area as an ungulate winter range and objectives for the ungulate winter range;

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (ii)  an area as a wildlife habitat area and objectives for the wildlife habitat area;

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (iii)  a general wildlife measure;

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (iii.1)  a general measure in relation to ecological communities;

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (iv)  categories of wildlife for the purposes of subparagraphs (i) to (iii),

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (v)  categories of ecological communities for the purposes of subparagraph (iii.1), and

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (b) prescribing the circumstances in which the discretion conferred in the authorization may be exercised.

heading: Ungulate winter range, wildlife habitat areas and general wildlife measures
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act may not establish an objective referred to in subsection (1) (a) (i) or (ii) for an area unless the objective is consistent with the objectives set by government that pertain to the area.

heading: Community watersheds
paragraph: 150		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Community watersheds
paragraph: (a) authorizing

heading: Community watersheds
paragraph: (i)  the minister responsible for the Land Act to designate an area of land in a watershed as a community watershed, or

heading: Community watersheds
paragraph: (ii)  the minister responsible for the Water Sustainability Act to establish water quality objectives in relation to a community watershed, and

heading: Community watersheds
paragraph: (b) prescribing the circumstances in which the discretion conferred in the authorization may be exercised.

heading: Community watersheds
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting community watersheds, including but not limited to prescribing requirements in relation to community watersheds.

heading: Watersheds with significant downstream fisheries values and significant watershed sensitivity
paragraph: 150.1		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations authorizing the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act to

heading: Watersheds with significant downstream fisheries values and significant watershed sensitivity
paragraph: (a) identify an area of land in a watershed that has

heading: Watersheds with significant downstream fisheries values and significant watershed sensitivity
paragraph: (i)  significant downstream fisheries values, and

heading: Watersheds with significant downstream fisheries values and significant watershed sensitivity
paragraph: (ii)  significant watershed sensitivity, and

heading: Watersheds with significant downstream fisheries values and significant watershed sensitivity
paragraph: (b) specify objectives in relation to the areas of land identified under this section.

heading: Watersheds with significant downstream fisheries values and significant watershed sensitivity
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act may not specify an objective referred to in subsection (1) (b) for an area unless the objective is consistent with the objectives set by government that pertain to the area.

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: 150.2		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (a) authorizing the minister to designate an area of land as a lakeshore management zone,

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (b) authorizing the minister to establish objectives in relation to lakeshore management zones,

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (c) prescribing the circumstances in which the discretion conferred in the authorization may be exercised, and

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (d) respecting lakeshore management zones.

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister may not specify an objective referred to in subsection (1) (b) for an area unless the objective is consistent with the objectives set by government that pertain to the area.

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph:
150.3
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (a) authorizing the minister responsible for the Land Act to designate an area of land as a scenic area,

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (b) authorizing the minister to establish visual quality objectives in relation to a scenic area,

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (c) prescribing the circumstances in which the discretion conferred in the authorization may be exercised, and

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (d) respecting scenic areas.

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister may not specify an objective referred to in subsection (1) (b) for an area unless the objective is consistent with the objectives set by government that pertain to the area.

heading: Consistency among objectives
paragraph: 150.4		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting objectives set by government and other objectives that are established under this Act, including but not limited to regulations

heading: Consistency among objectives
paragraph: (a) respecting procedures and criteria that are to be followed in establishing objectives

heading: Consistency among objectives
paragraph: (i)  referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of "objectives set by government" in section 1 (1), or

heading: Consistency among objectives
paragraph: (ii)  other objectives that are established under this Act, and

heading: Consistency among objectives
paragraph: (b) resolving inconsistencies among those objectives by varying or limiting the application of

heading: Consistency among objectives
paragraph: (i)  objectives set by government, or

heading: Consistency among objectives
paragraph: (ii)  other objectives that are established under this Act.

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph:
150.5
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (a) establishing criteria for classifying streams, wetlands and lakes,

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (b) respecting the classification of streams, wetlands and lakes,

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (c) establishing riparian reserve zones, riparian management zones and riparian management areas for different classes of streams, wetlands and lakes,

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (d) respecting

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (i)  streams, wetlands and lakes, and

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (ii)  riparian reserve zones, riparian management zones and riparian management areas, and

heading: Streams, wetlands and lakes
paragraph: (e) authorizing the minister responsible for the administration of the Wildlife Act, in prescribed circumstances, to designate streams as temperature sensitive streams.

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: 151		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting operational plans, including but not limited to regulations prescribing

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (a) their form and content,

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (b) the form and content of maps included in the plans,

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (c) the manner of, and time for, submitting the plans for approval,

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (f) respecting the extension of the term for an operational plan,

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (g) amendments to plans including specifying what amendments are not minor amendments,

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (h) respecting balancing objectives or other plan contents when approving a plan, and

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (i) how a forest stewardship plan must take into account other currently existing or future forest stewardship plans.

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting surveys, records and reports required or permitted under this Act.

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the transfer of obligations to establish a free growing stand, including but not limited to prescribing

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (a) stocking requirements that must be met, and

heading: Plans and practices
paragraph: (b) security that must be provided as part of the transfer of the obligation.

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph:
151.1
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting forest operations maps under Division 3.1 of Part 2, including but not limited to regulations

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (a) prescribing their form and content,

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (b) specifying the date on which a forest operations map is deemed to have been made publicly available under section 15.1 (2) (b),

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (c) requiring that a forest stewardship plan holder identify, in a forest operations map, the approximate periods during which harvesting under a cutting permit, or road construction under a road permit, is intended to occur,

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (d) specifying the start and end date of an operating period under section 15.2,

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (e) specifying the date by which a timber sales manager must publish a forest operations map before the start of an operating period under section 15.2,

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (f) requiring a timber sales manager to identify, in a forest operations map, the approximate locations of any

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (i)  cutblocks that are to be harvested under forestry licences to cut that a timber sales manager intends to enter into, or

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (ii)  roads that will be constructed to access timber to be harvested under forestry licences to cut that are entered into with a timber sales manager, and,

heading: Forest operations maps
paragraph: (g) exempting a timber sales manager from section 15.2 (2) if the timber sales manager makes the information referred to in section 15.2 (2) (a) (i) and (ii) publicly available for review and comment by means other than a forest operations map.

heading: Dispute resolution - forest landscape plans
paragraph:
151.2
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the resolution of disputes under sections 2.26 and 2.27 relating to the preparation and establishment of forest landscape plans, including, without limitation, regulations respecting the following:

heading: Dispute resolution - forest landscape plans
paragraph: (a) the qualifications, powers and duties of facilitators;

heading: Dispute resolution - forest landscape plans
paragraph: (b) the process for making referrals to a facilitator, the management of referrals and the conduct of dispute resolution facilitations;

heading: Dispute resolution - forest landscape plans
paragraph: (c) the time by which a facilitator must complete a dispute resolution facilitation and provide a report under section 2.26 (5);

heading: Dispute resolution - forest landscape plans
paragraph: (d) the matters that a facilitator must consider in making a report under section 2.26 (5);

heading: Dispute resolution - forest landscape plans
paragraph: (e) the time by which an alternative dispute resolution process referred to in section 2.27 must be established and completed.

heading: Dispute resolution - forest landscape plans
paragraph: (2) In subsection (1), "facilitator" has the same meaning as in section 2.26 (1).

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph:
153
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (a) woodlot licences, woodlot licence areas and holders of woodlot licences, and

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (b) community forest agreements, community forest agreement areas and holders of community forest agreements.

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the following:

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (a) establishing requirements and restrictions regarding the planning and forest practices, including the establishment of a free growing stand on a community forest agreement area or a woodlot licence area;

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (b) establishing conditions that must be complied with by the holder of a community forest agreement or a woodlot licence before, during and after forest practices;

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (b.1) requiring woodlot licence plans or amendments to woodlot licence plans to be made publicly available for review and comment before the plan or amendment is submitted to the minister for approval;

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (c) requiring site plans to be prepared by the holder of a community forest agreement or a woodlot licence and approved by the minister before forest practices are carried out on the community forest agreement area or a woodlot licence area;

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (d) requiring that authority to carry out a forest practice on a community forest agreement area or a woodlot licence area be obtained before the forest practice begins;

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (e) requiring persons to carry out actions for maintaining or improving forest health;

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (f) establishing requirements for wildlife tree retention for areas within woodlot licence areas that apply despite any objective set by government with respect to wildlife tree retention;

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (g) establishing or varying objectives for ungulate winter range to reduce the impact to the allowable annual cut of a woodlot licence.

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting first nations woodland licences, first nations woodland licence areas and holders of first nations woodland licences, including regulations

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (a) without limiting section 146, providing that specified provisions of regulations made under subsection (1) or (2) do not apply to or in respect of first nations woodland licences, first nations woodland licence areas or holders of first nations woodland licences,

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (b) prescribing provisions, in addition to the provisions of regulations made under subsection (1) or (2), that apply to or in respect of first nations woodland licences, first nations woodland licence areas or holders of first nations woodland licences, and

heading: Practices and planning - community forest agreements, woodlot licences
paragraph: (c) varying provisions of regulations made under subsection (1) or (2) as the provisions apply to or in respect of first nations woodland licences, first nations woodland licence areas or holders of first nations woodland licences.

heading: Forest and range resources
paragraph:
154
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting forest resources and range resources.

heading: Forest and range resources
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting

heading: Forest and range resources
paragraph: (a) resource features, including but not limited to

heading: Forest and range resources
paragraph: (i)  authorizing the minister to identify resource features other than a resource feature that is a wildlife habitat feature, and

heading: Forest and range resources
paragraph: (ii)  authorizing the minister responsible for the administration of the Wildlife Act to identify a resource feature that is a wildlife habitat feature, and

heading: Forest and range resources
paragraph: (b) forest health, including but not limited to forest health emergency management areas designated under section 27 (1).

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: 155		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the following:

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (a) the use of forest service roads, forest resource roads and rights of way;

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (b) the regulation or prohibition of the use and operation of vehicles or classes of vehicles on forest service roads, forest resource roads or rights of way;

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (c) the regulation or prohibition of road construction, maintenance or deactivation;

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (d) the transfer of an obligation to maintain or deactivate a forest service road or road that is authorized under an agreement under the Forest Act, including authorizing the minister to make orders that transfer obligations to maintain or deactivate a road;

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (e) requirements for the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act to deactivate a road authorized or constructed under the agreement, including but not limited to regulations requiring

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (i)  roads to be deactivated by a prescribed date, or

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (ii)  plans or reports to be submitted;

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (f) requirements for a person who uses a forest service road to provide notice to the minister or a prescribed person in relation to the person's use of the forest service road;

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (g) authorizing a person to fell trees, on Crown land in or adjacent to the right of way of a forest service road or forest resource road, that are a danger to persons or property;

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (h) the regulation of significant road work carried out in relation to forest service roads.

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (2) The minister may exempt a person from all or part of a regulation made under subsection (1) (a) or (b), subject to conditions or alternative requirements the minister may specify.

heading: Roads and rights of way
paragraph: (3) For certainty, a regulation under subsection (1) (e) may be made applicable to a road that was authorized or constructed under an agreement before the date on which the regulation comes into force.

heading: Forest practices
paragraph:
156.1
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting forest practices, including but not limited to the following:

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (a) regulating, restricting or prohibiting the carrying out of forest practices;

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (b) imposing requirements for managing and conserving forest resources, range resources and resource features;

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (c) imposing requirements for managing the risk of wildfire;

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (d) requiring the holder of an operational plan to comply with a provision of the operational plan;

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (e) providing that a provision of an operational plan referred to in paragraph (d) may be amended even if

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (i)  the plan has expired, or

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (ii)  the person to whom the provision applies no longer holds the plan.

heading: Forest practices
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations authorizing the minister to designate an area as a wildland urban interface area.

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph:
157
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments.

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (a) clearcutting, including but not limited to restricting or prohibiting clearcutting,

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (b) silviculture treatments, including but not limited to restricting or prohibiting various types of silviculture treatments,

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (c) rehabilitation of areas,

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (d) requirements for establishing a free growing stand on an area under an agreement under the Forest Act in which timber has been

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (i)  harvested under an agreement under the Forest Act,

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (ii)  harvested from an area where the holder of the agreement is exempt from the requirement to prepare a forest operations plan, a forest stewardship plan or a woodlot licence plan,

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (iii)  damaged or destroyed by natural causes, or

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (iv)  harvested other than in accordance with this Act, the regulations and the standards, and

heading: Silvicultural systems and silviculture treatments
paragraph: (e) exempting persons from the requirements to establish a free growing stand under section 29 or on areas referred to in paragraph (d).

heading: Gene resources
paragraph: 158		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting seed and tree gene resources including but not limited to regulations respecting the collection, processing, storage, registration, transportation, purchase, sale, selection, conservation and use of seed and tree gene resources.

heading: Terrain stability and soil disturbance
paragraph:
159
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting terrain stability and soil disturbance.

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph:
160
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting cutblocks, including but not limited to regulations prescribing

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (a) the size, including the maximum allowable size of a cutblock,

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (b) the shape of a cutblock, and

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (c) the spatial distribution of cutblocks, including green-up.

heading: Use of Crown range and range developments
paragraph:
161
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting range practices, the use of Crown range and range developments.

heading: Use of Crown range and range developments
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the following:

heading: Use of Crown range and range developments
paragraph: (a) the use of Crown range for grazing of livestock, hay cutting and other purposes;

heading: Use of Crown range and range developments
paragraph: (b) promoting health of Crown range;

heading: Use of Crown range and range developments
paragraph: (c) the identification of livestock pastured on Crown range;

heading: Use of Crown range and range developments
paragraph: (d) range developments and the payment of costs for range developments.

heading: Notification requirements
paragraph:
162
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations requiring persons to give written notice to an official concerning when, whether or not and to what extent the person has completed or will complete an obligation of the person under an operational plan or this Act.

heading: Relief and funding
paragraph:
162.1
		  For the purposes of sections 108 and 108.3, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting any of the following:

heading: Relief and funding
paragraph: (a) requirements for applications under section 108 (0.1) or 108.3 (1), including prescribing the period within which an application under section 108 (0.1) or 108.3 (1) must be submitted;

heading: Relief and funding
paragraph: (b) authorizing a person to submit under section 108 (0.1) or 108.3 (1) an application submission plan pending the submission of the application;

heading: Relief and funding
paragraph: (c) specifying under section 108 (1) (a)

heading: Relief and funding
paragraph: (i)  what constitutes an event causing damage, or

heading: Relief and funding
paragraph: (ii)  when an event causing damage must be considered to have occurred.

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph:
163
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting administrative remedies under this Act, the Forest Act or the Range Act.

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting charges and penalties in cases in which a person does not comply with one or more of the following:

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (a) this Act, the regulations or the standards or the Forest Act, the Range Act or a regulation made under the Forest Act or the Range Act;

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (b) an operational plan;

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (c) a permit under this Act.

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the imposition of an administrative penalty or of administrative penalties in equal or unequal proportions against 2 or more persons involved in the contravention that gives rise to the penalty or penalties, including regulations prescribing

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (a) circumstances in which the penalties may be imposed, and

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (b) formulas that may be applied in imposing the penalties.

heading: Administrative remedies
paragraph: (4) Without limiting subsection (1), for the purposes of sections 74 (1) and 74.4 (1) (d), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations establishing formulas or other methods to be used in determining the maximum amount of an administrative penalty under those provisions.

heading: Intervention and remediation
paragraph: 164		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting compliance with this Act and remediation related to a forest practice or range practice.

heading: Intervention and remediation
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting

heading: Intervention and remediation
paragraph: (a) the power of the minister to require the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act to take action to achieve a requirement of this Act or the regulations or to prevent damage to the environment if the damage is associated with a forest practice, range practice or range authorization,

heading: Intervention and remediation
paragraph: (c) stop work orders, and

heading: Intervention and remediation
paragraph: (d) remediation orders.

heading: Reconsideration
paragraph: 165		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the review, correction or clarification of a determination under this Act.

heading: Appeals and the commission
paragraph:
166
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting appeals and the commission.

heading: Appeals and the commission
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Appeals and the commission
paragraph: (a) prescribing the period that must elapse after the facts relevant to a determination first come to the knowledge of an official or a minister before the board may apply to the commission for an order under section 83;

heading: Appeals and the commission
paragraph: (b) prescribing the period in which the commission must deliver a decision after holding a hearing;

heading: Appeals and the commission
paragraph: (c) prescribing the form and content of annual reports made by the commission.

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph:
167
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the Forest Practices Board.

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the following:

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (a) audits referred to in section 122,

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (b) complaints to the board, including

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (i)  the manner of making a complaint,

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (ii)  specifying which complaints may be heard,

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (iii)  the manner of dealing with complaints, and

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (iv)  the nature and extent of investigations which may be taken in relation to a complaint;

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (c) procedures for notifying the board of determinations;

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (d) reports made by the board;

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (e) the qualifications of board members;

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (f) fees with respect to complaint investigations;

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (g) restricting the board's authority to carry out, or prohibiting the board from carrying out, audits or investigations referred to in section 122 in respect of a matter that is the subject of a decision-making agreement.

heading: Forest Practices Board
paragraph: (3) In subsection (2) (g), "decision-making agreement" has the same meaning as in section 2.5 (1).

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph:
168
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting botanical forest products.

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (2) Without restricting subsection (1), Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting:

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (a) obtaining botanical forest products from Crown land;

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (a.1) identifying a plant or fungus that occurs naturally on Crown land as being a botanical forest product;

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (b) establishing a licensing scheme for the purposes of regulating botanical forest products;

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (c) issuing, amending, renewing, suspending or cancelling licences;

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (d) applications for licences;

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (e) fees for licences and applications;

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (f) inspectors and inspections for the purposes of enforcing licensing;

heading: Botanical forest products
paragraph: (g) appeals.

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph:
168.1
		  (1) For the purposes of section 5 (1) (b) (i.1), the minister may make regulations as follows:

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing areas;

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing resources or features located in an area prescribed under paragraph (a), including but not limited to resources or features described in section 149 (1);

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (c) prescribing objectives for resources or features prescribed under paragraph (b).

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (2) In making a regulation under subsection (1), the minister may prescribe

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (a) different resources and features for different areas, and

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (b) different objectives for different areas, resources and features.

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (3) If an objective prescribed under this section is inconsistent with an objective set by government, the objective set by government prevails.

heading: Chief forester standards for forest and range resources

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "access structure" means a road, landing, pit, quarry, excavated or bladed trail or other logging trail;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agreement holder" means a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act, other than a woodlot licence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "altered forest landscape" means forest landscape that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is viewable from a significant public viewpoint,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) contains cutblocks or roads, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is in one of the categories prescribed under section 1.1;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorized in respect of a road" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a district manager, timber sales manager or other government employee or agent who is authorized by the minister to construct, maintain or deactivate a forest service road,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a.1) a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  is the holder of a road use permit for a forest service road, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  receives an order from the minister under section 79 (4),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an agreement holder who is authorized to construct, maintain or deactivate a road under a road permit, cutting permit or an agreement that does not provide for cutting permits, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a person, other than a woodlot licence holder, who is authorized to construct, maintain or deactivate a road under a special use permit or within a Provincial forest under an Act other than

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the Transportation Act, Land Act or Local Government Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the Coal Act, Mineral Tenure Act, Mines Act or Mining Right of Way Act, if the road is located within the boundaries of a claim, lease, permit or other authorization granted or issued under the applicable Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorized person" means a person who is any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an agreement holder;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person described in paragraph (a), (a.1) or (c) of the definition of "authorized in respect of a road";

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a person who holds a special use permit that authorizes the person to manage or use Crown land for silviculture treatments or wildlife habitat enhancement;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "basal area" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) for the purposes of stocking standards, the cross-sectional area per hectare of the crop trees, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for the purposes of retention of basal area in a riparian management zone, the cross-sectional area per hectare of standing trees, whether living or dead;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "BC timber sales business area" means a BC timber sales business area established under section 10 of the Administrative Boundaries Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "biodiversity" means the biological diversity of plants, animals and other living organisms in all their forms and levels of organization, including the biological diversity of genes, species and ecosystems;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "biogeoclimatic zone" or "biogeoclimatic subzone" means a biogeoclimatic zone or biogeoclimatic subzone as described in the Ministry of Forests and Range's publication Biogeoclimatic Ecosystem Classification Codes and Names, as amended from time to time;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "clearing width" means an area within a road right of way that is cleared of standing trees for the purpose of constructing or maintaining a road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Coast" means an area of British Columbia located in the South Coast Forest Region, West Coast Forest Region or Coast Mountains Forest District, as established by the Administrative Boundaries Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commencement date" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the date on which timber harvesting, other than on road rights of way or landings, begins on a cutblock, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in the case of timber harvesting carried out in contravention of section 52 (1) [unauthorized timber harvesting] of the Act, the date a determination under section 71 [administrative penalties] of the Act takes effect, without any further opportunity for review or appeal in respect of the contravention;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "community watershed" means a community watershed

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) established under section 41 (8) to (13) [approval of plans by the district manager or designated environment official] of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) continued under section 180 (e) [grandparenting specified designations] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) designated under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "delivered wood costs" means the costs associated with accessing and harvesting timber and delivering it to a timber processing facility;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "direct tributary" means a portion of a tributary stream that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is a minimum of 100 m in length, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has the same stream order as the most downstream reach of the tributary;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "established objective" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an objective continued under section 181 of the Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an objective described in Division 1 of Part 2,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a land use objective, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an objective established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "excavated or bladed trail" means a constructed trail that has

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an excavated or bladed width greater than 1.5 m, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a mineral soil cutbank height greater than 30 cm;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fan destabilization" means one or more of the following that occur beyond the naturally occurring range of variability:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an increase in the depth of a channel within an alluvial or colluvial fan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) water and sediment that overflows the banks of a channel within an alluvial or colluvial fan and spreads out across the surface of the fan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the creation of a new channel within an alluvial or colluvial fan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fibre recovery tenure holder" means a person that holds

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a forestry licence to cut entered into under section 47.6 (2.11) of the Forest Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a fibre supply licence to cut entered into under section 47.3 (1) or 47.71 (6) of the Forest Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish stream" means a watercourse that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is frequented by any of the following species of fish:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  anadromous salmonids;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  rainbow trout, cutthroat trout, brown trout, bull trout, Dolly Varden char, lake trout, brook trout, kokanee, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, mountain whitefish, lake whitefish, arctic grayling, burbot, white sturgeon, black crappie, yellow perch, walleye or northern pike;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  a species identified as a species at risk;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iv)  a species identified as regionally important wildlife, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has a slope gradient of less than 20%, unless the watercourse

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  does not contain any of the species of fish referred to in paragraph (a),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  is located upstream of a barrier to fish passage and all reaches upstream of the barrier are simultaneously dry at any time during the year, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  is located upstream of a barrier to fish passage and no perennial fish habitat exists upstream of the barrier;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fisheries sensitive feature" means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the littoral zone of a lake;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a freshwater area where the water is less than 10 m deep;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a flooded depression, pond or swamp that is not a stream, wetland or lake, but

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  either perennially or seasonally contains water, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  is seasonally occupied by a species of fish referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition of "fish stream";

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fisheries sensitive watershed" means an area of land identified under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fisheries sensitive watershed objective" means an objective

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 181 [grandparenting objectives] of the Act in respect of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  an area with significant downstream fisheries values continued under section 180 (f) [grandparenting specified designations] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  an area with significant watershed sensitivity continued under section 180 (g) of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "forest cover inventory" means a survey of trees and tree-related matters in an area that includes information required by the minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "forest development unit" means an area identified in a forest stewardship plan

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) where forest development may occur during the term of the plan, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) within which, during the term of the plan, timber to be harvested or roads to be constructed are entirely located;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "forest health factors" means biotic and abiotic influences on a forest that have an adverse effect on the health of trees and other plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "free growing date" means the end of the period, following the commencement date, by which a free growing stand being established on the net area to be reforested must conform to stocking standards set in respect of the free growing stand;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "free growing height" means the minimum height that a crop tree must attain before it forms part of a free growing stand;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "general ecological community measure" means a general measure in relation to ecological communities established under section 9.1 of the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "general wildlife measure" means a general wildlife measure

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 182 [general wildlife measures] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "gully process" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a rapid erosion of sediment that creates a channel or increases the depth of an existing channel, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a debris flood;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "harvest", in relation to timber, means to fell or remove timber, other than under a silviculture treatment, including to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) yard, deck or load timber,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) process timber on site,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) pile or dispose of logging debris,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) construct excavated or bladed trails or other logging trails,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) rehabilitate an area referred to in section 35, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) carry out sanitation treatments associated with operations referred to in paragraphs (a) to (e);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "industrial user" means a person referred to in section 22.1 [industrial use of a road] of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Interior" means an area of British Columbia, other than the Coast;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "lakeshore management zone" means a lakeshore management zone established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land use objective" means an objective referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of "objectives set by government" in section 1 [definitions] of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "landing" means an area of land that has been modified by equipment to make it suitable as a site for gathering logs before they are transported, and that is located within a cutblock or the clearing width of a road identified in a road permit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licensed waterworks" means a water supply intake or a water storage and delivery infrastructure that is licensed under the Water Sustainability Act or authorized under an operating permit issued under the Drinking Water Protection Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "major culvert" means a stream culvert that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is one of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a pipe having a diameter of 2 000 mm or greater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a pipe arch having a span greater than 2 130 mm;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  an open bottom arch having a span greater than 2 130 mm, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has a maximum design discharge of 6 m3 per second or greater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "marine sensitive feature" means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) herring spawning areas, shellfish beds, saltwater marsh areas, aquaculture sites, juvenile salmonid rearing areas and adult salmon holding areas;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the littoral zone of a marine or estuary system;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a marine area where the water is less than 10 m deep;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "minor tenure" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a free use permit,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a Christmas tree permit,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) an occupant licence to cut, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a forestry licence to cut that is not a major licence and limits

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the area from which timber may be harvested to 1 ha or less, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the volume of timber to be harvested to 2 000 m3 or less;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "newspaper" means a newspaper circulating in the area covered by the matter being advertised, or if no newspaper circulates in that area, then a newspaper that circulates nearest to that area, and includes a newspaper that is free and one that does not have subscribers;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "old growth management area" means an area that is subject to old growth management objectives established under section 3 [resource management zones and objectives] or 4 [landscape units and objectives] of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permanent access structure" means an access structure in a cutblock that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) at the time of its construction, is reasonably expected to provide access for timber harvesting and other activities that are not wholly contained in the cutblock, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is constructed on or through, or contains, materials unsuitable for the establishment of a commercial crop of trees and is not an excavated or bladed trail,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include an area that contained an access structure before rehabilitation of the area under section 36;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "primary forest activity" means one or more of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) timber harvesting;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) silviculture treatments;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b.1) wildlife habitat enhancement;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) road construction, maintenance and deactivation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regeneration date" means the end of the period, following the commencement date, by which a stand being established on the net area to be reforested must conform to stocking standards set in respect of regeneration;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regionally important wildlife" means a species of wildlife identified within a category established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "resource feature" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a recreation site, recreation trail, trail-based recreation area or interpretive forest site, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a resource feature identified under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian class" means the riparian class of a stream, wetland or lake as determined under Division 3 [Riparian Areas] of Part 4 [Practice Requirements];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian management area" means an area described under Division 3 [Riparian Areas] of Part 4 [Practice Requirements], that consists of a riparian management zone and a riparian reserve zone;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian management zone" means an area described under Division 3 [Riparian Areas] of Part 4 [Practice Requirements], that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is a portion of the riparian management area, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is established to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  conserve the fish, wildlife habitat, biodiversity and the water values of the riparian management zone, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  protect the riparian reserve zone, if any, within the riparian management area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian reserve zone" means an area described under Division 3 [Riparian Areas] of Part 4 [Practice Requirements], that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is a portion of a riparian management area, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is established to protect fish, wildlife habitat, biodiversity and the water values of the riparian reserve zone;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road" means all or part of a road that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a forest service road,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) authorized under a road permit, a cutting permit, an agreement under the Forest Act that does not provide for cutting permits, or a special use permit, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) located within a Provincial forest and authorized under an Act or its regulations, other than

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the Community Charter, Transportation Act, Land Act or Local Government Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the Coal Act, Mineral Tenure Act, Mines Act or Mining Right of Way Act, if the road is located within the boundaries of a claim, lease, permit or other authorization granted or issued under the applicable Act or regulation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and includes any of a tote road, pit, quarry, landing or waste area that is located within the road's clearing width, that is used in conjunction with the road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road prism" means an area consisting of the road surface and any cut slope and road fill;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "scenic area" means a scenic area

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 180 (c) [grandparenting specified designations] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "silviculture treatment" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) site preparation for the purposes of reforestation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) planting trees,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) brushing, including grazing for the purposes of brushing,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) juvenile spacing,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) fertilization,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) pruning,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) sanitation treatments associated with a silviculture treatment, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) pest management treatments, other than sanitation treatments;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "soil disturbance" means disturbance to the soil in the net area to be reforested in a cutblock because of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) temporary access structures,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) gouges, ruts and scalps, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) compacted areas,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include the effect on the soil of rehabilitating an area in accordance with section 35;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "species at risk" means a species identified within a category established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "specified ungulate species" means an ungulate species identified within a category established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "standards unit" means one or more parts of a cutblock for which part or parts there is only one of each of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) soil disturbance limit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) regeneration date;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) stocking standard;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) free growing date;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) free growing height for each species that contributes to establishing a free growing stand on the cutblock;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stocking standards" means the stocking standards that apply when

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) establishing a free growing stand, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) meeting the requirements of section 44 (4) [free growing stands generally];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream" means a watercourse, including a watercourse that is obscured by overhanging or bridging vegetation or soil mats, that contains water on a perennial or seasonal basis, is scoured by water or contains observable deposits of mineral alluvium, and that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) has a continuous channel bed that is 100 m or more in length, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) flows directly into

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a fish stream or a fish-bearing lake or wetland, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a licensed waterworks;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "temporary access structure" means an access structure that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is in a cutblock, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) does not conform to the criteria described in paragraph (a) or (b) of the definition of "permanent access structure"

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and does not include a pit or quarry;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "temperature sensitive stream" means a fish stream designated as a temperature sensitive stream under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ungulate winter range" means an ungulate winter range

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 180 (a) [grandparenting specified designations] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ungulate winter range objective" means an objective for ungulate winter range

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 181 [grandparenting objectives] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "visual quality objective" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an objective continued, in respect of a scenic area, under section 181 of the Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an objective established for a scenic area under the Government Actions Regulation, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a visual quality class continued, for a scenic area, under section 17 of the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "water quality objective" means a water quality objective for a community watershed

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 181 [grandparenting objectives] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wetland" means a swamp, marsh, bog, or other similar area that supports natural vegetation, that is distinct from adjacent upland areas;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife habitat area" means a wildlife habitat area

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 180 (b) [grandparenting specified designations] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife habitat area objective" means an objective for a wildlife habitat area

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) continued under section 181 [grandparenting objectives] of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) established under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife habitat feature" means a wildlife habitat feature identified under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife tree retention area" means an area occupied by wildlife trees that is located

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in a cutblock,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in an area that is contiguous to a cutblock, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in an area that is sufficiently close to the cutblock that the wildlife trees could directly impact on, or be directly impacted by, a forest practice carried out in the cutblock;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife trees" means a tree or group of trees that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) provide wildlife habitat, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) assist in the conservation of stand level biodiversity;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "written" or "in writing" includes written messages transmitted electronically.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) In the Act and this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "natural range barrier" means a naturally occurring feature or a combination of naturally occurring features, including the following, that stops or significantly impedes livestock movement to and from an area adjacent to the feature or combination of features:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a lake, pond, river, creek or wetland;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a rock face;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a talus slope;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an embankment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) vegetation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) standing or non-standing timber;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "net area to be reforested" means the portion of a cutblock that remains after the following have been excluded:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) areas occupied by permanent access structures;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) contiguous areas that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  in their natural state, are not capable of supporting a stand of trees in order to meet the stocking standards for un-excluded areas, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  are at least 0.1 ha in size and 10 m wide or are identified under section 86;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) contiguous areas of non-commercial forest cover that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  are present on the cutblock at the commencement of timber harvesting, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  are at least 0.1 ha in size and 10 m wide or are identified under section 86;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) wildlife tree retention areas;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) riparian reserve zones;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) areas reserved for purposes other than timber harvesting;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "result" means a description of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) measurable or verifiable outcomes in respect of a particular established objective, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the situations or circumstances that determine where in a forest development unit the outcomes under paragraph (a) will be applied;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "strategy" means a description of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) measurable or verifiable steps or practices that will be carried out in respect of a particular established objective, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the situations or circumstances that determine where in a forest development unit the steps or practices will be applied;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (3) Section 177 (2) and (3) of the Act and the definitions of "Code", "Code Regulation", "effective date" and "site level plan" in section 177 (1) of the Act apply for the purposes of this regulation.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (4) In sections 12.21, 43.1, 43.2, and section 1.1 in Schedule 1 of this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "adequate stocking density" means a stand of trees comprised of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) at least 700 trees per ha that are

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  at least 1.6 m apart from each other, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  6 m or greater in height, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) at least 900 trees per ha that are

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  at least 1.6 m apart from each other, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  4 m or greater in height;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "suitable secondary structure" means the saplings, poles, sub-canopy and canopy trees within a stand of trees that are

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) likely to survive an attack from mountain pine beetle,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a species of tree

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  specified in a forest stewardship plan applicable to the area, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  if there is no forest stewardship plan applicable to the area, specified as a preferred or acceptable species in the publication of the Ministry of Forests and Range, Reference Guide for Forest Development Plan Stocking Standards, as amended from time to time,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: for the purposes of establishing a free growing stand on the site series, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) of sufficiently good form, health and vigor to provide merchantable trees for future harvesting;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "targeted pine leading stand" means a stand of trees that has all of the following attributes:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is depicted on a government-endorsed forest cover map that indicates lodgepole pine is the leading tree species;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is at least 5 ha in size with an adequate stocking density of suitable secondary structure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is located in

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a timber supply area or tree farm licence area designated by the chief forester in an order made under section 43.2 (1) (a), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  an area within

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (A) the 100 Mile House timber supply area, the Kamloops timber supply area, the Lakes timber supply area, the Merritt timber supply area, the Prince George timber supply area, the Quesnel timber supply area, the Williams Lake timber supply area or the Okanagan timber supply area, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (B) Tree Farm Licence 18, 35, 42, 48, 49, 52 or 53

heading: Definitions
paragraph: unless the timber supply area or tree farm licence area is designated by the chief forester in an order made under section 43.2 (1) (b) as an area which may not contain a targeted pine leading stand.

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: 1.1		  For the purposes of paragraph (c) of the definition of "altered forest landscape" in section 1, the following categories are prescribed, each according to the extent of alteration resulting from the size, shape and location of cutblocks and roads:

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (a) preservation: consisting of an altered forest landscape in which the alteration, when assessed from a significant public viewpoint, is

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (i)  very small in scale, and

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (ii)  not easily distinguishable from the pre-harvest landscape;

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (b) retention: consisting of an altered forest landscape in which the alteration, when assessed from a significant public viewpoint, is

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (i)  difficult to see,

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (ii)  small in scale, and

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (iii)  natural in appearance;

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (c) partial retention: consisting of an altered forest landscape in which the alteration, when assessed from a significant public viewpoint, is

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (i)  easy to see,

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (ii)  small to medium in scale, and

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (iii)  natural and not rectilinear or geometric in shape;

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (d) modification: consisting of an altered forest landscape in which the alteration, when assessed from a significant public viewpoint,

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (i)  is very easy to see, and

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (ii)  is

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (A) large in scale and natural in its appearance, or

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (B) small to medium in scale but with some angular characteristics;

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (e) maximum modification: consisting of an altered forest landscape in which the alteration, when assessed from a significant public viewpoint,

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (i)  is very easy to see, and

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (ii)  is

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (A) very large in scale,

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (B) rectilinear and geometric in shape, or

heading: Categories of visually altered forest landscape
paragraph: (C) both.

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph:
1.2
		  (1) The following activities are prescribed for the purposes of the definition of "forest practice" in section 1 (1) of the Act:

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph: (a) timber harvesting, road construction, road maintenance, road use, road deactivation, silviculture treatments, botanical forest product collecting and fire use, control and suppression;

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph: (b) an activity carried out under an agreement under the Forest Act, a special use permit or a road use permit;

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph: (c) an activity related to an activity described in paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph: (2) The following categories of persons are prescribed for the purposes of paragraph (c) of the definition of "forest practice" in section 1 (1) of the Act:

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph: (a) contractors, employees and agents of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act;

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph: (b) persons with an obligation to establish a free growing stand in accordance with an agreement made under section 29.1 of the Act;

heading: Activities and categories of persons prescribed for forest practices
paragraph: (c) a holder of a special use permit that authorizes the holder to manage or use Crown land for silviculture treatments or wildlife habitat enhancement.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: 2		  (1) This regulation does not apply in respect of a person who is authorized to carry out a forest practice that is

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (a) funded under a vote as defined in section 1 of the Financial Administration Act, and

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (b) administered under the Forest Investment Account, under the Financial Administration Act

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: unless the funding is provided as set out in section 96 of this regulation.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (2) In this regulation, a reference to distance in respect to riparian management areas, riparian management zones and riparian reserve zones, and in Division 4 of Part 4, is a reference to the slope distance.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (3) A person is exempt from

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a requirement of Parts 4 and 5 of this regulation, or

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (b) an obligation under section 21, 29, 47 or 48 of the Act

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: as necessary to allow the person to conform to the Workers Compensation Act and the regulations under that Act.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (4) Until June 1, 2005, Parts 2 and 3 of this regulation and the standards and objectives made under Parts 2 and 3 apply immediately, despite section 16 (2) of the Act, to a forest stewardship plan.

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: 3		  (1) For the purpose of section 46 (1) and (1.1) [protection of the environment] of the Act, "damage" means any of the following that adversely alters an ecosystem:

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (a) a landslide;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (b) a gully process on the Coast;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (c) a fan destabilization on the Coast;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (d) soil disturbance;
