heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (e) the deposit into a stream, wetland or lake of

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (i)  a petroleum product,

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (ii)  a fluid used to service industrial equipment, or

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (iii)  any other similar harmful substance;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (f) a debris torrent that enters a fish stream;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (g) changes to soil.

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (2) A person who is carrying out fire control or suppression in accordance with an enactment is exempt from section 46 of the Act.

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph:
4
		  (1) The following enactments are prescribed enactments for the purposes of section 52 (1) (e) (ii) [unauthorized timber harvesting] of the Act:

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (a) this regulation;

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (b) the Mineral Tenure Act, for the purpose of locating a claim.

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (1.1) An agreement holder and the timber sales manager may cut, damage or destroy Crown timber as necessary for the purpose of carrying out silviculture treatments, stand tending treatments or forest health treatments.

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (2) A free miner under the Mineral Tenure Act may cut, damage or destroy Crown timber before the free miner requires a permit under section 10 [permits] of the Mines Act if Crown timber is cut, damaged or destroyed only

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (a) by hand held tools, and

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of mineral exploration.

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (2.1) A land surveyor may cut, damage or destroy Crown timber as necessary in the course of carrying out duties as a land surveyor.

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (3) Except for minor clearing of brush and downed trees, subsection (2) does not permit cutting, damaging or destroying Crown timber beyond the minimum necessary for the safety of persons carrying out the activities.

heading: Removing Crown timber to protect a community from wildfire
paragraph: 4.01		  The minister may exempt a person from section 52 (3) of the Act if the minister is satisfied that the Crown timber to be removed

heading: Removing Crown timber to protect a community from wildfire
paragraph: (a) is non-merchantable timber,

heading: Removing Crown timber to protect a community from wildfire
paragraph: (b) is to be removed for the purpose of protecting a community from wildfire, and

heading: Removing Crown timber to protect a community from wildfire
paragraph: (c) will not be sold to others.

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph:
4.02
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: "additional measure" means a measure included in a forest operations plan that imposes a requirement on the holder of the forest operations plan other than or in addition to one or more of the following requirements:

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (a) a planning guideline requirement;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (b) a substituted requirement;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (c) a practice requirement set out in Part 4 of this regulation;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: "amendment" means an amendment to a forest operations plan;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: "existing cutblock", in relation to a holder of a forest operations plan, means a cutblock

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (a) for which the holder has been granted a cutting permit or for which the holder has issued a timber sales licence, or

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (b) in which the holder has harvested timber under an agreement;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: "existing road", in relation to a holder of a forest operations plan, means a road that the holder is authorized to construct or has constructed under a cutting permit or road permit;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: "forest operations plan requirement" includes the following requirements in relation to a forest operations plan:

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (a) a planning guideline requirement;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (b) a substituted requirement;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (c) a practice requirement set out in Part 4 of this regulation from which the holder of the forest operations plan is not exempt;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: (d) an additional measure;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph: "planning guideline requirement" means a requirement included under section 2.28 (2) (c) [planning guidelines regarding forest practices, silvicultural systems or stocking standards] of the Act in a planning guideline;

heading: Definitions for Part 1.1
paragraph:
"substituted requirement" means a requirement substituted under 
              section 2.37 (2) (b) [additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines] of the Act for a planning guideline requirement.

heading: Information requirements for forest operations plan
paragraph:
4.03
		  A person who submits or holds a forest operations plan must include in the plan all of the information required under this Division.

heading: Business contact information
paragraph:
4.04
		  (1) A forest operations plan must include the following current information in relation to the person who is or will be the holder of the plan:

heading: Business contact information
paragraph: (a) the person's name;

heading: Business contact information
paragraph: (b) the person's address in British Columbia, other than a post office box;

heading: Business contact information
paragraph: (c) regular business hours;

heading: Business contact information
paragraph: (d) email address;

heading: Business contact information
paragraph: (e) website address, if applicable.

heading: Business contact information
paragraph: (2) A forest operations plan held by more than one person must include the information referred to in subsection (1) in relation to each holder.

heading: Business contact information
paragraph: (3) A forest operations plan must be amended if information included under this section changes or is no longer accurate.

heading: Identification number and amendment number
paragraph:
4.05
		  A forest operations plan must

heading: Identification number and amendment number
paragraph: (a) include a unique name, number or code for the purposes of identifying the plan, and

heading: Identification number and amendment number
paragraph: (b) if the plan has been amended, indicate the number of times the plan has been amended.

heading: Date of approval
paragraph:
4.06
		  (1) A forest operations plan or amendment must include the date on which the plan or amendment is submitted to the minister for approval.

heading: Date of approval
paragraph: (2) After a forest operations plan or amendment has been approved, the plan must be amended to include the date on which the plan or amendment was approved.

heading: Term and expiry
paragraph:
4.07
		  After a forest operations plan or amendment has been approved, the plan must be amended to include

heading: Term and expiry
paragraph: (a) the term of the plan, and

heading: Term and expiry
paragraph: (b) the date on which the plan will expire.

heading: Date of extension
paragraph:
4.08
		  After a forest operations plan has been extended under section 2.43 [extension of term of forest operations plan] of the Act, the plan must be amended to include

heading: Date of extension
paragraph: (a) the date on which the minister extended the term of the plan, and

heading: Date of extension
paragraph: (b) the date on which the extended plan will expire.

heading: Forest region and forest district
paragraph:
4.09
		  A forest operations plan must identify the forest districts and forest regions, as those terms are defined under the Forest Act, in which the forest operations area is located.

heading: Cutblocks and roads
paragraph: 4.11		  (1) A forest operations plan must list

heading: Cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (a) each existing cutblock and proposed cutblock, and

heading: Cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (b) each existing road and proposed road.

heading: Cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (2) A forest operations plan must identify each proposed cutblock and proposed road with a unique name, number or code.

heading: Cutblocks and roads
paragraph: (3) A forest operations plan held by more than one person must list the cutblocks and roads referred to in subsection (1) according to which person proposes the harvesting of timber on the cutblock or the construction of the road.

heading: Commencement dates
paragraph:
4.12
		  A forest operations plan must include, for each cutblock and road proposed in the plan, the year in which the person who will hold the forest operations plan proposes to begin

heading: Commencement dates
paragraph: (a) harvesting timber on the cutblock, or

heading: Commencement dates
paragraph: (b) constructing the road.

heading: Assessments
paragraph:
4.13
		  If a planning guideline requires an assessment to be conducted before a forest operations plan or an amendment is submitted to the minister for approval, a copy of the assessment must be submitted to the minister together with the plan or amendment.

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph:
4.14
		  (1) A forest operations plan must specify the situations or circumstances that determine when section 44 (1) [free growing stands generally] or section 45 [free growing stands collectively across cutblocks] will apply to an area.

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) The forest operations plan must specify the following for each of the situations or circumstances specified under subsection (1) of this section:

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) if section 44 (1) (a) will apply, the regeneration date and stocking standards;

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) if section 44 (1) (b) will apply, the free growing height and stocking standards;

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) if section 45 (1) will apply, the regeneration date and the stocking standards;

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) if section 45 (2) will apply, the free growing date and the stocking standards, as approved by the chief forester.

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph: (3) The forest operations plan must specify stocking standards for areas referred to in section 44 (4) and the situations or circumstances that determine when the stocking standards will be applied.

heading: Specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan
paragraph: (4) This section does not apply if the forest operations plan incorporates by reference a planning guideline requirement that specifies stocking standards for the forest operations area.

heading: Map requirements
paragraph:
4.15
		  A person who submits or holds a forest operations plan must include in the plan a map of the forest operations area that meets all of the requirements set out in this Division.

heading: Landscape features
paragraph:
4.16
		  The map must show

heading: Landscape features
paragraph: (a) elevation and relief, and

heading: Landscape features
paragraph: (b) streams, rivers, wetlands and lakes, if any.

heading: Agreement boundaries, land use objectives and other areas of land use
paragraph:
4.17
		  The map must show the following areas:

heading: Agreement boundaries, land use objectives and other areas of land use
paragraph: (a) the boundaries of each area that is subject to an agreement held by a person who is or will be a holder of the forest operations plan;

heading: Agreement boundaries, land use objectives and other areas of land use
paragraph: (b) the boundaries of areas subject to an order

heading: Agreement boundaries, land use objectives and other areas of land use
paragraph: (i)  made under section 93.4 of the Land Act, or

heading: Agreement boundaries, land use objectives and other areas of land use
paragraph: (ii)  continued under section 93.8 of the Land Act;

heading: Agreement boundaries, land use objectives and other areas of land use
paragraph: (c) the boundaries of parks, private land, municipalities, regional districts, agreements under the Forest Act, agreements under the Range Act and other areas of land use.

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: 4.18		  The map must show the boundaries and approximate location of the following areas:

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (a) an area in which the harvesting of timber is restricted or prohibited under the applicable forest landscape plan;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (b) a forested area on Crown land that the minister has determined, under section 26 [control of insects, diseases, animals or abiotic factors] of the Act, is being damaged by insects, diseases, animals or abiotic factors that are causing damage to the forest;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (c) an area designated under section 27 [forest health emergency] of the Act as a forest health emergency management area;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (d) an area subject to an order under section 56 [interpretive forest sites, recreation sites and trails] of the Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (e) an area subject to an order under section 58 [protection of recreation and range resources on Crown land] of the Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (f) an area designated under section 108.2 [areas of catastrophic damage] of the Act as an area of catastrophic damage;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (g) an area continued under section 180 [grandparenting specified designations] of the Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (h) a general wildlife measure continued under section 182 [general wildlife measures] of the Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (i) an area subject to an order under section 7 [orders of Lieutenant Governor in Council] of the Environment and Land Use Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (j) an area subject to a designation under Part 13 [Designated Areas] or Part 15 [Special Purpose Areas] of the Forest Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (k) an area subject to an order under the Government Actions Regulation;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (l) a watershed, stream, aquifer or other specified area or environmental feature subject to a water objective established under section 43 [water objectives] of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (m) an area designated under section 65 [order designating area for planning process] of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Areas subject to harvesting constraints
paragraph: (n) an area designated under section 4 [power to designate wildlife management areas] of the Wildlife Act as a wildlife management area.

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: 4.19		  (1) The map must indicate

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (a) if the forest operations plan is or will be held by the holder of an agreement, the year in which the holder of the agreement proposes to begin harvesting timber on each proposed cutblock, or

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (b) if the forest operations plan is or will be held by a timber sales manager, the year in which the timber sales manager intends to invite applications for each timber sale licence.

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (2) The map must identify each proposed cutblock with the unique name, number or code required under section 4.11 (2) [cutblocks and roads].

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (3) If the forest operations plan is or will be held by more than one person, the map must identify which of the persons holds or proposes to hold a cutting permit for each existing cutblock and proposed cutblock.

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (4) The map must show the location of each existing cutblock, including a cutblock in which a person other than the holder of the forest operations plan has harvested timber, that is within five kilometres of horizontal distance of the boundary of a proposed cutblock.

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (5) If a forest operations plan is held by a timber sales manager, the map must show the location of each existing cutblock that is within five kilometres of horizontal distance of a proposed cutblock that the timber sales manager intends to include in timber sale licences for which the timber sales manager will invite applications during the term of the forest operations plan.

heading: Cutblocks
paragraph: (6) The map does not need to show existing cutblocks in which timber harvesting was completed more than 20 years before the date on which the forest operations plan is submitted for approval.

heading: Prescribed distance
paragraph:
4.2
		  For the purposes of section 2.36 (2) (c) (i) and (d) (i) [location of each existing cutblock or road] of the Act, the prescribed distance is five kilometres of horizontal distance from

heading: Prescribed distance
paragraph: (a) the boundary of a proposed cutblock, or

heading: Prescribed distance
paragraph: (b) the centerline of a proposed road.

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph:
4.21
		  (1) The map must indicate the year in which the holder of the plan

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph: (a) intends to begin constructing each proposed road, and

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph: (b) proposes to deactivate each road.

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph: (2) The map must label each proposed road with the unique name, number or code required under section 4.11 [cutblocks and roads].

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph: (3) The map must identify each road that

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph: (a) has been included in a previously approved forest operations plan or forest stewardship plan held by a person who will hold the proposed forest operations plan, and

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph: (b) has not yet been constructed.

heading: Proposed roads
paragraph: (4) If the forest operations plan is or will be held by more than one person, the map must identify which of the persons holds or proposes to hold the road permit for each proposed road.

heading: Existing roads
paragraph:
4.22
		  (1) The map must show each of the following roads that is within five kilometres of horizontal distance of the centerline of a proposed road:

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (a) a road that has been constructed by, or that is authorized to be constructed by, a person other than the holder of the forest operations plan;

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (b) a forest service road;

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (c) a forest resource road;

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (d) a road that is excluded under section 21.1 (2) [roads excluded from definition of "forest resource road"] of the Act from the definition of "forest resource road" under subsection (1) of that section.

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (2) The map must indicate the following for each road shown:

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (a) whether the road is temporary or permanent;

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (b) the year that the road is proposed to be deactivated;

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (c) the level of deactivation.

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (3) A forest operations plan held by more than one person must identify which of the persons holds or proposes to hold the road permit for each existing road.

heading: Existing roads
paragraph: (4) If the forest operations plan is or will be held by a timber sales manager, the map must show the location of each existing road that is continuous to or within five kilometres of horizontal distance from the centerline of a proposed road that the timber sales manager intends to construct during the term of the forest operations plan.

heading: Roads subject to deactivation order
paragraph:
4.23
		  The map must show roads that are the subject of an order under section 23.2 [order to deactivate road] of the Act.

heading: Requirements for engaging with Indigenous nations
paragraph:
4.24
		  For the purposes of section 2.38 (1) (a) [engagement with Indigenous nations affected by forest operations plans] of the Act, a person who submits a forest operations plan or amendment must comply with the requirements set out in this Division.

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph:
4.25
		  (1) The person must provide the following information to the Indigenous nation at the start of the engagement process:

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who holds or will hold the proposed forest operations plan;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (b) the person's address in British Columbia, other than a post office box, at which a hard copy of the forest operations plan will be made available for review;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (c) the business hours during which a hard copy of the forest operations plan will be made available for review;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (d) the email address of the person who will hold the proposed forest operations plan;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (e) a website address for the person who will hold the proposed forest operations plan, if applicable;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (f) the date on which the person intends to submit the forest operations plan or amendment to the minister for approval;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (g) if engagement is in relation to an amendment, the substance of the amendment;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (h) the proposed term of the forest operations plan;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (i) the types of activities proposed under the forest operations plan;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (j) the text of each planning guideline requirement incorporated by reference into the forest operations plan;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (k) the text of the forest landscape plan outcome to which the planning guideline referred to in paragraph (j) relates;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (l) whether the forest operations plan includes a substituted requirement and the text of the forest landscape plan outcome to which the substituted requirement relates;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (m) whether the forest operations plan includes an additional measure;

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (n) if the engagement is in relation to an amendment, whether the amendment requires approval from the minister under section 2.39 [approval of forest operations plans] of the Act.

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (2) The person must promptly provide updated information to the Indigenous nation if any of the information referred to in subsection (1) changes.

heading: Initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations
paragraph: (3) If more than one person will hold the forest operations plan, the name, address and email address of each of those persons must be provided.

heading: Forest operations plan must be available digitally and in person
paragraph:
4.26
		  The person must

heading: Forest operations plan must be available digitally and in person
paragraph: (a) make a digital copy of the proposed forest operations plan or amendment available to the Indigenous nation,

heading: Forest operations plan must be available digitally and in person
paragraph: (b) make a paper copy of the proposed forest operations plan or amendment available for review at the person's place of business, and

heading: Forest operations plan must be available digitally and in person
paragraph: (c) provide a paper copy of the proposed forest operations plan or amendment to the Indigenous nation, if requested by the Indigenous nation.

heading: Provide assessments to Indigenous nation on request
paragraph:
4.27
		  If a planning guideline requires an assessment to be conducted before a forest operations plan or an amendment is submitted to the minister for approval, the person must provide a copy of the assessment to the Indigenous nation if the Indigenous nation requests a copy.

heading: Meeting with Indigenous nation
paragraph:
4.28
		  The person must offer to meet, or offer for the person's representative to meet, with the Indigenous nation to discuss the forest operations plan or amendment.

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph:
4.29
		  In addition to the summary required under section 2.38 (2) (a) [summary of engagement with Indigenous nations] of the Act, when submitting a forest operations plan or amendment to the minister for approval the person must provide the following information in relation to each Indigenous nation with whom the person engaged:

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (a) a copy of the information referred to in section 4.25 [initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations];

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (b) a copy of the version of the forest operations plan provided to the Indigenous nation;

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (c) a description of matters raised by the Indigenous nation that were not addressed through a change to the forest operations plan;

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (d) the timing of engagement with the Indigenous nation, including

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (i)  the date on which engagement with the Indigenous nation began,

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (ii)  the deadline by which the Indigenous nation was asked to provide comments, and

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (iii)  if the Indigenous nation requested that a deadline under subparagraph (ii) be extended, whether the deadline was extended and for how long;

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (e) a description of the person's efforts to engage with the Indigenous nation, including

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (i)  a list of correspondence and meetings with the Indigenous nation, and

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (ii)  a copy of comments received from the Indigenous nation.

heading: Application
paragraph:
4.3
		  For the purposes of section 2.38 (1) (b) [public review and comment] of the Act, a person who submits a forest operations plan or amendment must comply with the requirements set out in this Division.

heading: Information to be included when making plan publicly available
paragraph:
4.31
		  (1) In making the forest operations plan publicly available for review and comment, the person must include a notice containing the following information:

heading: Information to be included when making plan publicly available
paragraph: (a) the information described in section 4.25 (1) (a) to (e) and (g) to (n) [initial information to be provided to Indigenous nations];

heading: Information to be included when making plan publicly available
paragraph: (b) the period of time during which the forest operations plan will be available for review and comment.

heading: Information to be included when making plan publicly available
paragraph: (2) The person must promptly update the notice if any of the information referred to in subsection (1) changes.

heading: Information to be included when making plan publicly available
paragraph: (3) If more than one person will hold the forest operations plan, the name, address and email address of each of those persons must be included in the notice.

heading: Digital copy and hard copy
paragraph:
4.32
		  The person must make the forest operations plan and the notice described in section 4.31 of this regulation publicly available

heading: Digital copy and hard copy
paragraph: (a) as a digital copy, and

heading: Digital copy and hard copy
paragraph: (b) as a paper copy at the person's place of business.

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph:
4.33
		  (1) The person must make the forest operations plan publicly available for review and comment for a period of 60 days, unless the minister authorizes a shorter period under subsection (2).

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph: (2) The minister may authorize a shorter public review and comment period of not less than 10 days if the minister is satisfied that the 60-day period under subsection (1) would likely result in

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph: (a) an unacceptable impact on the proper management and conservation of forests and forest ecosystems,

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph: (b) an increased risk of wildfire, or

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph: (c) an increased risk to public safety.

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph: (3) The person must publish notice of the review and comment period described in subsection (1) of this section on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the person and in one of the following:

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph: (a) a newspaper published in British Columbia and circulating in the areas subject to the forest operations plan;

heading: Public review and comment period
paragraph: (b) the Gazette.

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph:
4.34
		  (1) A person must make an amendment described in section 4.43 [amendments that do not require minister's approval] publicly available for review and comment for a period of 30 days, unless the minister authorizes a shorter period under subsection (2).

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (2) The minister may authorize a shorter public review and comment period of not less than 10 days if the minister is satisfied that the 30-day period under subsection (1) would likely result in

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (a) an unacceptable impact on the proper management and conservation of forests and forest ecosystems,

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (b) an increased risk of wildfire, or

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (c) an increased risk to public safety.

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (3) The person must publish notice of the review and comment period described in subsection (1) of this section on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the person and in one of the following:

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (a) a newspaper published in British Columbia and circulating in the areas subject to the forest operations plan;

heading: Public review and comment period - amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (b) the Gazette.

heading: Provide assessments to public on request
paragraph:
4.35
		  If a planning guideline requires an assessment to be conducted before a forest operations plan or an amendment is submitted to the minister for approval, the person must provide a copy of the assessment to any individual who requests a copy.

heading: Review and comment by rights-holders
paragraph:
4.36
		  (1) The person must give notice of the forest operations plan or amendment to each person whose rights are likely to be affected by the forest operations plan or amendment.

heading: Review and comment by rights-holders
paragraph: (2) If a person to whom notice is given under subsection (1) requests an extension to the time period for reviewing and providing comments on the forest operations plan or amendment, the person must be provided with an extension, up to a maximum total review and comment period of 60 days.

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph:
4.37
		  In addition to the summary required under section 2.38 (2) (b) of the Act, the person submitting the forest operations plan or amendment to the minister for approval must provide the following:

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (a) a copy of the notice included under section 4.31 [information to be included when making plan publicly available] of this regulation;

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (b) a copy of the version of the forest operations plan that was made publicly available for review and comment;

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (c) a description of matters raised and changes proposed that were not addressed through changes to the forest operations plan;

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (d) the period of time during which the forest operations plan was made available for review and comment;

heading: Information to be provided to minister about engagement
paragraph: (e) a list of all notices, correspondence, meetings, or other engagement activities relating to the plan or amendment that took place during the public review and comment period.

heading: How to submit a forest operations plan for approval
paragraph:
4.38
		  A forest operations plan or an amendment must be submitted to the minister electronically.

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph:
4.39
		  The minister must not approve a forest operations plan or amendment unless the minister is satisfied that the following criteria are met:

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) the forest operations plan includes planning guideline requirements, substituted requirements or additional measures respecting the matters referred to in section 2.28 (2) (a) to (c) of the Act that are measurable or verifiable;

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) the forest operations plan sufficiently supports

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  the objectives set out in section 2.22 [preparation of forest landscape plan] of the Act, and

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  any objectives established under section 2.51 [decision-making agreement - statutory power of decision of chief forester] of the Act by a decision-making agreement;

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) the forest operations plan is not likely to result in an increased fire hazard within a wildland urban interface area;

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) the forest operations plan is not likely to result in an increased risk to public safety;

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (e) the forest operations plan is not likely to negatively impact cultural heritage resources;

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (f) the cumulative impact of the forest operations plans in an area is not likely to

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  exceed a threshold established in a forest operations plan requirement, or

heading: Criteria for minister's approval of forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  prevent the achievement of one or more outcomes of the applicable forest landscape plan.

heading: Criteria for inconsistent forest operations plan
paragraph:
4.4
		  (1) This section applies in relation to a proposed forest operations plan that includes a statement referred to in section 2.37 (2) (a) [additional requirements if forest operations plan is inconsistent with planning guidelines] of the Act.

heading: Criteria for inconsistent forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) In addition to the criteria set out in section 4.39 and for the purposes of section 2.4 (1) (c) [approval of forest operations plans that are inconsistent with forest landscape plans] of the Act, the minister must not approve a proposed forest operations plan to which this section applies unless the minister is satisfied that circumstances or conditions described in the statement make it impracticable for the plan to include the planning guideline requirement or substituted requirement to which the statement relates.

heading: Road deactivation as condition of approval
paragraph:
4.41
		  For the purposes of section 2.39 (3) [approval of forest operations plans] of the Act, the minister may require the holder of a forest operations plan, as a condition of approval and as contemplated by subsection (2) of that section, to deactivate an existing road if the following circumstances apply:

heading: Road deactivation as condition of approval
paragraph: (a) all or part of a proposed road is located in an area that has reached a level of disturbance to the natural environment that the minister considers to be the maximum level of acceptable disturbance for the area;

heading: Road deactivation as condition of approval
paragraph: (b) there is an existing road in the area and the existing road is authorized under a road permit or cutting permit held by the holder of the forest operations plan;

heading: Road deactivation as condition of approval
paragraph: (c) the minister considers that the deactivation of the existing road is necessary for the proper management and conservation of the forest and forest ecosystems in the area of the proposed new road.

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph:
4.42
		  (1) The minister may extend the term of a forest operations plan under 
              section 2.43 (2) (a) [extension of term of forest operations plan] of the Act if the following circumstances apply:

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) the holder of the forest operations plan holds a forest licence that provides that a replacement for the licence must not be offered, within the meaning of section 15 of the Forest Act;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) the extension will not extend the term of the forest operations plan beyond the term of the forest licence referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) the forest operations plan will expire in less than 12 months;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) the minister considers that additional time is required for a reason set out in subsection (2) or (3).

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) The minister may consider that additional time is required if the minister reasonably believes all of the following:

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) that one of the following circumstances exists:

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (i)  a potential threat to cultural heritage resources;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (ii)  an ecological condition such as forest health factors, landslides, wildfires, floods or droughts, in the forest operations plan area;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) that when the forest operations plan was approved the circumstance referred to in paragraph (a) was not known to the plan holder or did not exist;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) that the circumstance is beyond the plan holder's control;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (d) that the need for an extension is unrelated to the plan holder's financial situation.

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (3) The minister may consider that additional time is required if the forest operations plan is affected by an amendment to any of the following enactments:

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) the Act;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) the regulations under the Act;

heading: Extension of term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (c) an enactment listed in 4.47 [prescribed enactments].

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: 4.43		  (1) Subject to section 4.45, an amendment does not require the approval of the minister under section 2.39 of the Act if all of the following criteria apply:

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (a) the amendment will not result in timber harvesting or road construction being proposed in any of the following areas:

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (i)  an area listed in section 4.18 [areas subject to harvesting constraints];

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (ii)  a riparian management area, other than a riparian management area in relation to a stream that is not a fish stream (riparian class S5 or S6);

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (iii)  a wildlife tree retention area;

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (iv)  the location of a cultural heritage resource or an area that an Indigenous nation has identified to the holder of the forest operations plan as being a culturally significant area for the Indigenous nation;

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (b) the amendment does not change a planning guideline requirement, a substituted requirement or an additional measure, other than to replace a substituted requirement with the planning guideline requirement for which it was substituted;

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (c) the amendment and the forest operations plan as amended are consistent with all conditions imposed by the minister in relation to the forest operations plan;

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (d) the amendment and the forest operations plan as amended are consistent with any objectives established under sections 93.4 and 93.8 of the Land Act;

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (e) the amendment and the forest operations plan as amended comply with section 2.36 of the Act and the requirements of Divisions 2 and 3 of this Part;

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (f) the amendment does not materially change the nature or scope of the activities proposed by the forest operations plan.

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (2) The holder of a forest operations plan who proposes an amendment referred to in subsection (1) must, in accordance with Divisions 4 and 5 of this Part,

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (a) make reasonable efforts to engage with Indigenous nations affected by the amendment, and

heading: Amendments that do not require minister's approval
paragraph: (b) make the amendment publicly available for review and comment.

heading: Amendment that does not require approval is             effective 30 days after documents submitted
paragraph:
4.44
		  Subject to section 4.45, an amendment referred to in section 4.43 is effective 30 days after the following documents have been provided to the minister:

heading: Amendment that does not require approval is             effective 30 days after documents submitted
paragraph: (a) the amended forest operations plan;

heading: Amendment that does not require approval is             effective 30 days after documents submitted
paragraph: (b) a written statement from a person authorized to prepare an operational plan under the Professional Governance Act describing the effect of the amendment in relation to the criteria set out in section 4.43;

heading: Amendment that does not require approval is             effective 30 days after documents submitted
paragraph: (c) the information set out in section 4.29 [information to be provided to minister about engagement] regarding engagement with Indigenous nations;

heading: Amendment that does not require approval is             effective 30 days after documents submitted
paragraph: (d) the information set out in section 4.37 [information to be provided to minister about engagement] regarding public review and comment.

heading: Minister may determine that approval is required
paragraph: 4.45		  (1) Within 30 days after receiving the documents referred to in section 4.44 in relation to a proposed amendment that meets the criteria set out in section 4.43, the minister may determine that approval under section 2.39 of the Act is required in relation to the proposed amendment if the minister considers that the approval process under section 2.39 of the Act is necessary to protect one of the following:

heading: Minister may determine that approval is required
paragraph: (a) public health and safety;

heading: Minister may determine that approval is required
paragraph: (b) the environment;

heading: Minister may determine that approval is required
paragraph: (c) a cultural heritage resource, as defined in the Forest Act.

heading: Minister may determine that approval is required
paragraph: (2) If the minister determines that approval is required in relation to a proposed amendment, the proposed amendment is not effective without the minister's approval under section 2.39 of the Act.

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: 4.46		  (1) The following amendments to a forest operations plan do not require the approval of the minister under section 2.39 of the Act:

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (a) adding the following information to a forest operations plan:

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (i)  the date on which a forest operations plan or amendment was approved by the minister;

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (ii)  the date on which the minister extended the term of a forest operations plan;

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (iii)  the date on which a forest operations plan will expire;

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (b) a change to a person's business hours, website address, address or email address.

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (2) Divisions 4 to 6 of this Part do not apply to an amendment under subsection (1).

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (3) A holder of the forest operations plan must

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (a) update the publicly available copies of the forest operations plan to reflect the amendment, and

heading: Updates to basic information
paragraph: (b) submit the amended forest operations plan to the minister.

heading: Prescribed enactments
paragraph: (a) Environment and Land Use Act;

heading: Prescribed enactments
paragraph: (b) Forest Act;

heading: Prescribed enactments
paragraph: (c) Land Act;

heading: Prescribed enactments
paragraph: (d) Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Prescribed enactments
paragraph: (e) Wildlife Act.

heading: Cumulative impacts
paragraph: 4.48		  (1) The holder of a forest operations plan must propose and submit an amendment if the minister determines that the amendment is necessary in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Cumulative impacts
paragraph: (2) The minister may determine that an amendment to a forest operations plan is necessary if the minister reasonably considers that

heading: Cumulative impacts
paragraph: (a) the cumulative impact of the forest operations plans in an area

heading: Cumulative impacts
paragraph: (i)  exceeds, or is likely to exceed, a threshold established in a forest operations plan requirement, or

heading: Cumulative impacts
paragraph: (ii)  prevents, or is likely to prevent, the achievement of one or more outcomes of the applicable forest landscape plan, and

heading: Cumulative impacts
paragraph: (b) the mandatory amendment would reduce the cumulative impact of the forest operations plans in the area.

heading: Cumulative impacts
paragraph: (3) Before making a determination under this section, the minister must give the holder of the forest operations plan an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Exemption from requirement to amend forest operations plan
paragraph:
4.49
		  A person is exempt from the requirements under section 2.45 [mandatory amendments to forest operations plan] of the Act if one of the following circumstances applies:

heading: Exemption from requirement to amend forest operations plan
paragraph: (a) there are less than six months remaining in the term of the forest operations plan;

heading: Exemption from requirement to amend forest operations plan
paragraph: (b) there are six months or more remaining in the term of the forest operations plan and the holder of the forest operations plan has submitted a new forest operations plan for approval.

heading: Minister may exempt
paragraph:
4.5
		  The minister may exempt a person from the requirement to amend a plan under section 2.45 (1) of the Act if the minister considers that the amendment to the plan does not materially change

heading: Minister may exempt
paragraph: (a) a forest operations plan requirement, or

heading: Minister may exempt
paragraph: (b) the location of a cutblock or road included in the forest operations plan.

heading: Exemption from practice requirements
paragraph:
4.51
		  The minister may exempt an agreement holder who holds a forest operations plan, or a holder of a timber sales licence or road permit to which a forest operations plan relates, from a provision of Part 4 listed in column 1 of the following table if

heading: Exemption from practice requirements
paragraph: (a) the forest operations plan includes a planning guideline requirement, substituted requirement or additional measure that addresses the matter listed in column 2 opposite the provision in column 1, and

heading: Exemption from practice requirements
paragraph: (b) the minister considers the planning guideline requirement, substituted requirement or additional measure to be at least as effective as the provision listed in column 1 in addressing the matter in column 2.

heading: Publish annual forest development schedule
paragraph:
4.52
		  (1) For the purposes of section 2.46 (1) [annual forest development schedule] of the Act, the holder of a forest operations plan, other than a timber sales manager, must make an annual forest development schedule available throughout the calendar year to which the schedule relates, in both of the following ways:

heading: Publish annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (a) as a digital copy on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the holder;

heading: Publish annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (b) as a paper copy in the holder's place of business.

heading: Publish annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (2) If a forest operations plan is held by more than one person, the annual forest development schedule for the plan must indicate, for each location in the forest operations area where the holders intend to start harvesting timber or constructing roads in the next calendar year,

heading: Publish annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (a) which plan holder holds, or intends to hold, a cutting permit or road permit for the location, or

heading: Publish annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (b) if applicable, that a timber sales licence will be issued for the location.

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph:
4.53
		  (1) The holder of a forest operations plan must publish with the annual forest development schedule a notice that includes the following information:

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who will hold the proposed forest operations plan;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (b) the person's address in British Columbia, other than a post office box, at which a hard copy of the annual forest development schedule will be made available for review;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (c) the business hours during which a hard copy of the annual forest development schedule will be made available for review;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (d) the email address of the person who will hold the proposed forest operations plan;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (e) a website address for the person who will hold the proposed forest operations plan, if applicable;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (f) the identification name, number or code of the forest operations plan to which the annual forest development schedule relates;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (g) the calendar year to which the annual forest development schedule relates;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (h) a website address for the publicly accessible digital copy of the annual forest development schedule;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (i) the purpose of the annual forest development schedule;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (j) a description of the information contained in the annual forest development schedule.

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (2) The notice referred to in subsection (1) must be

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (a) published on a ministry website or on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the holder and in one of the following:

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (i)  a newspaper published in British Columbia and circulating in the areas subject to the forest operations plan;

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (ii)  the Gazette, and

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (b) provided to

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (i)  each holder of a forest operations plan in the forest landscape area to which the annual forest development schedule relates, and

heading: Notice of annual forest development schedule
paragraph: (ii)  each person whose rights the forest operations plan holder knows or ought to know are likely to be affected by the activities referred to in the annual forest development schedule.

heading: Information requirements for site level plan
paragraph:
4.54
		  A holder of a forest operations plan who is required to prepare a site level plan must include in the plan all of the information required under this Division.

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph:
4.55
		  The site level plan must include the following information:

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (a) the name of each holder of the forest operations plan;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (b) the identification name, number or code of the forest operations plan that applies to the site level plan;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (c) the unique name, number or code for each cutblock and road shown in the site level plan;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (d) a website address at which a copy of the forest operations plan is available, if applicable;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (e) the standards units for the area of the site level plan;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (f) the stocking standards for the area of the site level plan;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (g) the soil disturbance limits for the area of the site level plan;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (h) a copy of a site level assessment, if any, for the area of the site level plan;

heading: Information to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (i) a map described in section 4.56.

heading: Map to be included in a site level plan
paragraph:
4.56
		  The site level plan map must show the following:

heading: Map to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (a) water resources, including streams, wetlands, lakes and riparian areas;

heading: Map to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (b) elevation and relief;

heading: Map to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (c) names, numbers or codes that identify cutblocks and roads shown on the map;

heading: Map to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (d) standards units;

heading: Map to be included in a site level plan
paragraph: (e) the boundaries of parks, private land, municipalities, regional districts, agreements under the Forest Act, agreements under the Range Act and other areas of land use.

heading: Site level plan must be kept until obligations complete
paragraph: 4.57		  A holder of a site level plan must keep a copy of the site level plan until the date that the holder has completed, or been granted relief under section 108 of the Act from, all of the obligations under the forest operations plan in relation to the area of the site level plan.

heading: Site level plan must be made available on request
paragraph:
4.58
		  A holder of a site level plan must

heading: Site level plan must be made available on request
paragraph: (a) publish notice of the site level plan on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the holder, and

heading: Site level plan must be made available on request
paragraph: (b) make the plan publicly available on request at any reasonable time at the holder's place of business nearest to the area to which the site level plan applies.

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph:
4.59
		  The holder of a forest operations plan is not required to prepare a site level plan under section 2.47 (1) (a) [site level plans for cutblocks] of the Act if one or more of the following circumstances applies:

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (a) timber harvesting must proceed expeditiously to eliminate a safety hazard;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (b) timber harvesting is needed to facilitate collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (c) timber harvesting is limited to a volume of 50 m3 or less;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (d) timber harvesting is restricted to one or more of the following:

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (i)  removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (ii)  harvesting trees on land that is, or will be, exclusively used for harvesting hay or grazing livestock in accordance with an agreement under the Range Act;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (iii)  harvesting timber for experimental purposes if, in the opinion of the minister, the harvesting will be carried out under controlled scientific or investigative conditions;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (iv)  clearing areas for or within a recreation site or recreation trail;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (v)  felling and removing trees that have been or will be treated to facilitate the entrapment of pests;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (vi)  commercial thinning, removal of individual trees, or a similar type of intermediate cutting;

heading: When site level plan not required for cutblocks
paragraph: (vii)  harvesting special forest products other than woodchips or hogged tree material.

heading: When site level plan not required for roads
paragraph: 4.6		  The holder of a forest operations plan is not required to prepare a site level plan under section 2.47 (1) (b) [site level plans for roads] of the Act if the timber harvesting is limited to removal of timber to improve safety for road users by

heading: When site level plan not required for roads
paragraph: (a) eliminating a safety hazard,

heading: When site level plan not required for roads
paragraph: (b) improving visibility, or

heading: When site level plan not required for roads
paragraph: (c) increasing the number of pullouts or the size of existing pullouts.

heading: Additional parties to plans
paragraph:
4.61
		  A forest operations plan may be held by more than one person.

heading: Forest operations plan must be signed
paragraph:
4.62
		  A forest operations plan or an amendment must be signed by

heading: Forest operations plan must be signed
paragraph: (a) each person who will hold the forest operations plan, and

heading: Forest operations plan must be signed
paragraph: (b) a person who prepares the forest operations plan on the behalf of the person or persons who will hold the forest operations plan.

heading: Map must be kept throughout term of forest operations plan
paragraph:
4.63
		  (1) A holder of a forest operations plan must keep a copy of the forest operations plan, including all maps and amendments, for the term of the forest landscape plan that applies to the forest operations area.

heading: Map must be kept throughout term of forest operations plan
paragraph: (2) During the term of the forest landscape plan, the holder of a forest operations plan must promptly provide a copy of the forest operations plan to the minister if the minister requests a copy.

heading: How to make forest operations plan publicly available
paragraph:
4.64
		  The holder of a forest operations plan must make the plan publicly available in both of the following ways throughout the term of the forest operations plan:

heading: How to make forest operations plan publicly available
paragraph: (a) on a ministry website or on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the holder;

heading: How to make forest operations plan publicly available
paragraph: (b) as a paper copy in the place of business of the holder of the forest operations plan.

heading: Application of this Division to forest stewardship plans
paragraph:
4.99
		  The objectives prescribed under sections 5 to 10 of this regulation are objectives set by government referred to in section 5 (1) (b) (i) of the Act and are applicable only to forest stewardship plans.

heading: Objectives set by government for soils
paragraph:
5
		  The objective set by government for soils is to conserve the productivity and the hydrologic function of soils.

heading: Objectives set by government for timber
paragraph:
6
		  The objectives set by government for timber are to

heading: Objectives set by government for timber
paragraph: (a) maintain or enhance an economically valuable supply of commercial timber from British Columbia's forests,

heading: Objectives set by government for timber
paragraph: (b) ensure that delivered wood costs, generally, after taking into account the effect on them of the relevant provisions of this regulation and of the Act, are competitive in relation to equivalent costs in relation to regulated primary forest activities in other jurisdictions, and

heading: Objectives set by government for timber
paragraph: (c) ensure that the provisions of this regulation and of the Act that pertain to primary forest activities do not unduly constrain the ability of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act to exercise the holder's rights under the agreement.

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: 7		  (1) The objective set by government for wildlife is to conserve sufficient wildlife habitat in terms of amount of area, distribution of areas and attributes of those areas, for

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (a) the survival of species at risk,

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (b) the survival of regionally important wildlife, and

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (c) the winter survival of specified ungulate species.

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (2) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must specify a result or strategy in respect of the objective stated under subsection (1) only if the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act gives notice to the person of the applicable

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (a) species referred to in subsection (1), and

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (b) indicators of the amount, distribution and attributes of wildlife habitat described in subsection (1).

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (3) If satisfied that the objective set out in subsection (1) is addressed, in whole or in part, by an objective in relation to a wildlife habitat area or an ungulate winter range, a general wildlife measure, or a wildlife habitat feature, the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act must exempt a person from the obligation to specify a result or strategy in relation to the objective set out in subsection (1) to the extent that the objective is already addressed.

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife
paragraph: (4) On or after December 31, 2004, a notice described in subsection (2) must be given at least 4 months before the forest stewardship plan is submitted for approval.

heading: Objectives set by government for water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity within riparian areas
paragraph: 8		  The objective set by government for water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity within riparian areas is to conserve, at the landscape level, the water quality, fish habitat, wildlife habitat and biodiversity associated with those riparian areas.

heading: Objectives set by government for fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph:
8.1
		  (1) In this section, "fisheries sensitive watershed" means an area identified in Schedule 2 of this regulation

heading: Objectives set by government for fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (a) with significant downstream fisheries values continued under section 180 (f) of the Act and significant watershed sensitivity continued under section 180 (g) of the Act, and

heading: Objectives set by government for fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (b) for which there is no fisheries sensitive watershed objective.

heading: Objectives set by government for fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (2) Until December 31, 2005 the objective set by government for fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds is to prevent to the extent described in subsection (3) the cumulative hydrological effects of primary forest activities in the fisheries sensitive watershed from resulting in a material adverse impact on the habitat of the fish species for which the fisheries sensitive watershed was established.

heading: Objectives set by government for fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (4) If satisfied that the objective set out in subsection (2) is not required to provide special management, the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act must exempt a person from the requirement to specify a result or strategy in relation to the objective.

heading: Objectives set by government for fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (5) If satisfied that the objective set out in subsection (2) is addressed, in whole or in part, by an enactment, the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act must exempt a person from the requirement to specify a result or strategy in relation to the objective set out in subsection (2) to the extent that the objective is already addressed.

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: 8.2		  (1) In this section, "community watershed" means a community watershed

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (a) that is continued under section 180 (e) of the Act, and

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (b) for which a water quality objective has not been

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (i)  continued under section 181 of the Act, or

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (ii)  established under the Government Actions Regulation.

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (2) The objective set by government for water being diverted for human consumption through a licensed waterworks in a community watershed is to prevent to the extent described in subsection (3) the cumulative hydrological effects of primary forest activities within the community watershed from resulting in

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (a) a material adverse impact on the quantity of water or the timing of the flow of the water to the waterworks, or

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (b) the water from the waterworks having a material adverse impact on human health that cannot be addressed by water treatment required under

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (i)  an enactment, or

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (ii)  the licence pertaining to the waterworks.

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (4) If satisfied that the objective set out in subsection (2) is not required to provide special management the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act must exempt a person from the requirement to specify a result or strategy in relation to the objective.

heading: Objectives set by government for water in community watersheds
paragraph: (5) If satisfied that the objective set out in subsection (2) is addressed, in whole or in part, by an enactment, the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act must exempt a person from the requirement to specify a result or strategy in relation to the objective set out in subsection (2) to the extent that the objective is already addressed.

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife and biodiversity - landscape level
paragraph: 9		  The objective set by government for wildlife and biodiversity at the landscape level is, to the extent practicable, to design areas on which timber harvesting is to be carried out that resemble, both spatially and temporally, the patterns of natural disturbance that occur within the landscape.

heading: Objectives set by government for wildlife and biodiversity - stand level
paragraph:
9.1
		  The objective set by government for wildlife and biodiversity at the stand level is to retain wildlife trees.

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph:
9.2
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: "scenic area" means an area of land established as a scenic area under the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act on or before October 24, 2002 and continued as a scenic area under section 180 (c) of the Act;

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: "visual sensitivity class" means a visual sensitivity class established on or before October 24, 2002, particulars of which are publicly available in the Land and Resource Data Warehouse maintained by the minister responsible for the Land Act.

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (2) The objective set by government in relation to visual quality for a scenic area, that

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (a) was established on or before October 24, 2002, and

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
