paragraph: (a) prepares and submits to the minister the proposed forest stewardship plan, including an intended result or strategy for the objective for wildlife and biodiversity at the landscape level set out in section 9, in relation to the areas of primary forest activity under the plan, and

heading: Conditional exemption - section 64 or 65
paragraph: (b) receives the minister's approval to the plan.

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph:
12.5
		  (1) An agreement holder who is required to prepare a forest stewardship plan is exempt from section 66 if the person

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (a) prepares and submits to the minister the proposed plan, including an intended result or strategy for wildlife and biodiversity at the stand level set out in section 9.1, in relation to the areas of primary forest activity under the plan, and

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (b) receives the minister's approval to the plan.

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (2) An agreement holder who is required to prepare a forest stewardship plan is exempt from section 67 if the person

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (a) prepares and submits to the minister the proposed plan, including an intended result or strategy for wildlife and biodiversity at the stand level set out in section 9.1, in relation to the areas of primary forest activity under the plan, and

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (b) receives the minister's approval to the plan.

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (3) A holder of a timber sale licence or road permit to which a proposed forest stewardship plan relates is exempt from section 66 if the timber sales manager

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (a) prepares and submits to the minister the proposed forest stewardship plan, including an intended result or strategy for the objective for wildlife and biodiversity at the stand level set out in section 9.1, in relation to the areas of primary forest activity under the plan, and

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (b) receives the minister's approval to the plan.

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (4) A holder of a timber sale licence or road permit to which a proposed forest stewardship plan relates is exempt from section 67 if the timber sales manager

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (a) prepares and submits to the minister the proposed forest stewardship plan, including an intended result or strategy for the objective for wildlife and biodiversity at the stand level set out in section 9.1, in relation to the areas of primary forest activity under the plan, and

heading: Conditional exemption - section 66 or 67
paragraph: (b) receives the minister's approval to the plan.

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph:
14
		  (1) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan may specify in the plan or an amendment to it,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (a) a new forest development unit,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (b) a forest development unit that is in effect on the date of the submission of the forest stewardship plan to the minister,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (c) an area to which section 196 (1) or (2) of the Act is applicable that is in a forest development unit referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (d) an area to which section 197 (4) or (7) of the Act is applicable that is in a forest development unit referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection, or

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (e) cutblocks to which section 197 (5) of the Act is applicable that is in a forest development unit referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection.

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (2) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan identifies for the forest development units specified under subsection (1) those things described in subsection (3) that

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (a) are in the forest development unit, and

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (b) are in effect

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (i)  on the date the plan or amendment to it is submitted for approval, if the plan is submitted on or before December 31, 2005, or

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (ii)  4 months before the date the plan or amendment to it, as the case may be, is submitted for approval, if the plan or amendment to it is submitted after December 31, 2005.

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (3) The things that under subsection (2) are to be identified in a forest stewardship plan referred to in that subsection are each

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (a) ungulate winter range,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (b) wildlife habitat area,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (c) fisheries sensitive watershed,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (d) lakeshore management zone, including specifying the width of the zone, if the zone is identified on a map accompanying the establishment of the lakeshore management zone,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (e) scenic area,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (f) lake identified as an L1 lake under section 49 (1) (b) (ii) if the lake has been identified on a map accompanying the identification,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (g) community watershed,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (h) old growth management area,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (i) area in which commercial timber harvesting is prohibited by another enactment,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (j) cutting permit and road permit held by the agreement holder if that is the person required to prepare the plan, and

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (k) road permit or timber sale licence issued or entered into by the timber sales manager if the timber sales manager is the person required to prepare the plan.

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (4) A person who prepares a forest stewardship plan may identify an area as a declared area if, on the date that the area is identified,

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (a) the area is in a forest development unit in effect, and

heading: Identifying forest development units
paragraph: (b) all activities and evaluations that are necessary in relation to inclusion of cutblocks and roads in the area have been completed.

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph:
16
		  (1) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan specifies the situations or circumstances that determine when section 44 (1) [free growing stands generally] or section 45 [free growing stands collectively across cutblocks] will apply to an area.

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph: (2) In specifying a stocking standard under this section, a person who prepares a forest stewardship plan may consider the factors set out in section 6 [factors relating to stocking standards] of Schedule 1.

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph: (3) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan specifies, for each of the situations or circumstances specified under subsection (1) where

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph: (a) section 44 (1) (a) will apply, the regeneration date and stocking standards,

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph: (b) section 44 (1) (b) will apply, the free growing height and stocking standards,

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph: (c) section 45 (1) will apply, the regeneration date and the stocking standards, and

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph: (d) section 45 (2) will apply, the free growing date and the stocking standards, as approved by the chief forester.

heading: Stocking standards
paragraph: (4) A person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan must ensure that the plan specifies stocking standards for areas referred to in section 44 (4), and the situations or circumstances that determine when the stocking standards will be applied.

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph:
16.1
		  (1) The chief forester may make an order under section 31.1 of the Act requiring the holder of a forest stewardship plan to comply with stocking standards set out in the order if the chief forester

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (a) has information relating to forest health, natural hazards or ecological conditions in the area covered by the forest stewardship plan that was not available when the plan was approved,

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (b) is satisfied that either of the following applies:

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (i)  the stocking standard specified under section 16 of this regulation does not adequately address any of the following matters in relation to the area covered by the forest stewardship plan:

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (A) ecological sustainability or ecological resilience;

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (B) wildfire risk reduction;

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (C) the preservation of non-timber stewardship values, including the forest ecosystems or non-timber forest resources of interest to First Nation groups;

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (ii)  the stocking standard specified under section 16 of this regulation is not consistent with the timber supply analysis and forest management assumptions that apply to the area covered by the forest stewardship plan, and

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (c) is satisfied that the continuation of the stocking standard specified under section 16 of this regulation would

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (i)  have unacceptable adverse effects on any of the following:

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (A) forest resources or range resources;

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (B) the matters set out in paragraph (b) (i) (A) or (C), or

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (ii)  increase wildfire risk to an unacceptable level.

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (2) The chief forester may make an order referred to in subsection (1) at any time during the term of the forest stewardship plan.

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (3) An order referred to in subsection (1) applies to any cutblock, in the area covered by the forest stewardship plan, in which harvesting has not yet begun.

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (4) Before making an order referred to in subsection (1), the chief forester must consider both of the following:

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (a) the financial impact of the order on the holder of the forest stewardship plan;

heading: Order specifying new stocking standard
paragraph: (b) whether complying with the order is practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to the area covered by the forest stewardship plan.

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph:
17
		  For the purpose of section 47 [invasive plants] of the Act, a person who prepares a forest stewardship plan must specify measures in the plan to prevent the introduction or spread of species of plants that are invasive plants under the Invasive Plants Regulation, if the introduction or spread is likely to be the result of the person's forest practices.

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph:
18
		  For the purpose of section 48 [natural range barriers] of the Act, a person who prepares a forest stewardship plan must specify measures to mitigate the effect of removing or rendering ineffective natural range barriers.

heading: Cumulative effect of multiple forest stewardship plans
paragraph:
19
		  For the purpose of section 9 [proportional objectives] of the Act, the minister may establish targets referred to in that section, if, where there are likely to be multiple forest stewardship plans within an area,

heading: Cumulative effect of multiple forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (a) one or more holders of a forest stewardship plan may be unduly constrained in the specifying of results or strategies in the holder's plan unless targets are established under section 9 of the Act, and

heading: Cumulative effect of multiple forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (b) the holders of a forest stewardship plan within the area are unable to reach an agreement that would remove the constraints referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Limited content forest stewardship plans
paragraph:
19.1
		  The minister may exempt the holder of

heading: Limited content forest stewardship plans
paragraph: (a) a forestry licence to cut that is a major licence, or

heading: Limited content forest stewardship plans
paragraph: from one or more of the requirements of Divisions 1 and 2 if the minister is satisfied that the exemption is appropriate, given the nature and extent of the timber harvesting proposed by the holder.

heading: When forest stewardship plan not required
paragraph:
19.2
		  For the purpose of section 4 (2) of the Act, the holder of a forestry licence to cut entered into under section 47.3 (1) (a) of the Forest Act is not required to prepare a forest stewardship plan under section 3 (1) of the Act if timber harvesting under the licence is restricted to an area which is subject to a contract that

heading: When forest stewardship plan not required
paragraph: (a) provides for the preparation of the area for reforestation,

heading: When forest stewardship plan not required
paragraph: (b) is funded under a vote as defined in section 1 of the Financial Administration Act, and

heading: When forest stewardship plan not required
paragraph: (c) is under a program administered by the minister.

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: 20		  (1) Before a person submits to the minister for approval a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to one, the person must publish a notice at least once in a newspaper, and may publish the notice more frequently, stating

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (a) that the plan or amendment is publicly available for review and for written comment at the person's place of business or at another place specified in the notice,

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (b) persons may attend at that place during business hours to review the plan or amendment, and

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (c) the address of the person proposing the plan or amendment to which address persons may submit written comments about the plan by mail or in person.

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), the period during which persons have the opportunity to review a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to one begins on the date the notice is first published and ends

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (a) 60 days after that date, if no greater or lesser number of days is determined under paragraph (b) or (c) and paragraph (d) is inapplicable,

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (b) a greater number of days after that date that the minister may determine if paragraph (d) is inapplicable and the minister considers that the greater number of days is necessary to provide an adequate opportunity for review and comment under section 21,

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (c) a lesser number of days that the minister may determine if paragraph (d) is inapplicable and the minister considers that the lesser number of days will provide an adequate opportunity for review and comment under section 21, or

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (d) 10 days after that date if all or a substantial part of the timber to which the plan pertains

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (i)  is dead, infested with pests or otherwise damaged, or is required to be harvested to facilitate the removal of dead, infested or damaged timber, and

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (ii)  must be harvested expeditiously to prevent

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (A) the spread of pests, or

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (B) a significant reduction in the economic value of the timber due to a deterioration in the quality of the timber.

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (3) The minister by order may grant an exemption to a person who proposes a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to one from the requirement to publish a notice under subsection (1).

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (4) If the minister makes an order under subsection (3) and the forest stewardship plan or amendment is approved, the person exempted under the order must publish in a newspaper a notice specifying

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (a) that the forest stewardship plan or the amendment has been approved without having been made publicly available for review and comment, and

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (b) the date on which operations under the plan have been authorized to begin.

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (5) Despite subsection (1), a person who proposes an amendment to a forest stewardship plan in respect of section 16 is not required to publish a notice in a newspaper.

heading: Providing notice
paragraph: (6) Despite subsection (1), a person who prepares and submits to the minister an amendment to a forest stewardship plan under section 12.21 (1) or (2) is not required to publish a notice in a newspaper.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A person who publishes a notice under section 20 (1), during the applicable period referred to in section 20 (2),

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (a) if required by the minister, must refer a copy of the forest stewardship plan, or a portion of the plan, to

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (i)  any agency of government, or

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (ii)  any agency of the Government of Canada,

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (b) must provide a person who is interested in the plan with an opportunity to review the plan during normal business hours at the place of business of the person who published the notice or other venue specified in the notice under section 20 (1),

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (c) must provide a person whose rights may be affected by the plan with an opportunity to review the plan in a manner that is commensurate with the nature and extent to which the person's rights may be affected,

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (c.1) must refer a copy of the plan to a timber sales manager who may be affected by the plan, and

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (d) must make reasonable efforts to meet with First Nation groups affected by the plan to discuss the plan.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (2) A person given the opportunity to review or discuss the plan under subsection (1) may submit written comments in respect of the plan during the period and to the address specified in the notice under section 20 (1).

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph:
22
		  (1) A person who publishes a notice under section 20 (1)

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (a) must consider any written comments received under section 21 that are

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (i)  relevant to the plan, or

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of an amendment, relevant to the amendment, and

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (b) is not required to consider comments in respect of

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (i)  areas described in section 14 (1) (b), (c) or (d), (3) (j) or (k) or (4), or

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (ii)  results and strategies that relate to the areas referred to in subparagraph (i).

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (2) A person who submits a forest stewardship plan to the minister for approval must submit with the proposed plan

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (a) a copy of the notice published under section 20,

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (b) a copy of each written comment received under section 21,

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (c) a description of any changes made to the plan as a result of the comments received under section 21, and

heading: Responding to review and comment
paragraph: (d) a description of the efforts made to comply with the requirements of section 21 (1) (d).

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph:
23
		  (1) Each of the following is prescribed as being one of the prescribed requirements referred to in section 7 (1) (b) of the Act in relation to an area referred to in that provision:

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (a) the area is identified in the plan as a declared area;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (b) the area is the subject of a cutting permit, road permit or timber sale licence with a term that begins after the date of submission of the plan to the minister;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (c) the area is one to which section 196 (1) of the Act applies.

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (2) Until December 31, 2005, for the purposes of section 7 (1.1) (a) (iii) of the Act the following objectives are prescribed as specified other objectives, in relation to a forest development unit referred to in section 7 (1.1) of the Act:

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (a) an objective established under section 56 (3) of the Act for a recreation site, recreation trail, trail-based recreation area or interpretive forest site;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (b) a wildlife habitat area objective;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (c) an ungulate winter range objective;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (d) a lakeshore management zone objective;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (e) a water quality objective;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (f) a fisheries sensitive watershed objective;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (g) a visual quality objective.

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (3) Effective January 1, 2006, for the purposes of section 7 (1.1) (a) (iii) of the Act the following objectives are prescribed as specified other objectives in relation to a forest development unit referred to in section 7 (1.1) of the Act:

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (a) a water quality objective;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (b) a fisheries sensitive watershed objective;

heading: Deemed approval
paragraph: (c) a wildlife habitat area objective.

heading: Requiring additional information
paragraph:
24
		  (1) If, in specifying a result or strategy for an objective, a person satisfies the minister that the person addressed all of the factors contained in Schedule 1 to which the result or strategy relates, the minister must not require the person to address other factors.

heading: Requiring additional information
paragraph: (2) The minister may request information under section 16 (2.1) [approval of forest stewardship plan or amendment] of the Act in respect of a result or strategy if the information is

heading: Requiring additional information
paragraph: (a) relevant to the factors in Schedule 1 that were addressed, if any,

heading: Requiring additional information
paragraph: (b) relevant to any factor that the person addressed that is not a factor listed in Schedule 1, and

heading: Requiring additional information
paragraph: (c) either available to the person or in the control or possession of the person.

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph:
25
		  (1) An intended result or strategy is not inconsistent with an established objective only because it

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (a) is capable of producing a condition outside the range of natural variation characteristic of a season, an area or a forest resource,

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (b) proposes an innovative means of addressing the established objective, or

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (c) is based on a factor other than one specified in Schedule 1.

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (2) On application by a person required to prepare a forest stewardship plan, the minister responsible for the Land Act may exempt the person from the requirement that an intended result or strategy specified in the plan, in relation to an objective that was

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (a) established or continued under section 3 or 4 of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act, and

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (b) in effect on January 31, 2004,

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: be consistent with the objective, if the minister determines that requiring the result or strategy to be consistent with the objective would

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (c) have a material adverse impact on the delivered wood costs of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act to which the plan applies, and

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (d) unduly constrain the ability of a holder referred to in paragraph (c) to exercise the holder's rights under the agreement, and

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: the material adverse impact and undue constraint outweigh the benefits to the public that would be achieved by requiring the result or strategy to be consistent with the objective.

heading: Consistency of results and strategies with established objectives
paragraph: (3) In making a determination under section 16 of the Act in respect of a forest stewardship plan or an amendment to a forest stewardship plan, the minister responsible for the Forest Act must consider any exemption granted by the minister responsible for the Land Act under subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Consistency of intended results and strategies with objectives
paragraph: 25.1		  (1) For the purpose of section 5 (1.1) of the Act, each intended result or strategy in a forest stewardship plan must be consistent with the established objectives to the extent practicable, to take into account the circumstances or conditions applicable to that area or that part.

heading: Consistency of intended results and strategies with objectives
paragraph: (2) If an established objective is comprised of measurable or verifiable steps, processes or outcomes, an intended result or strategy that

heading: Consistency of intended results and strategies with objectives
paragraph: (a) is specified in a forest stewardship plan for that objective,

heading: Consistency of intended results and strategies with objectives
paragraph: (b) restates the same measurable or verifiable steps, practices or outcomes, and

heading: Consistency of intended results and strategies with objectives
paragraph: (c) describes the circumstances in which those measurable or verifiable steps, practices or outcomes are to be achieved or carried out,

heading: Consistency of intended results and strategies with objectives
paragraph: is to be considered to be consistent with objectives set by government and with the other established objectives to the extent practicable, as described in subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph:
26
		  (1) If, in specifying stocking standards under section 16, a person satisfies the minister that the person addressed only those factors contained in section 6 of Schedule 1, the minister must not require the person to address other factors.

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (2) The minister may request information under section 16 (2.1) of the Act in respect of stocking standards if the information is

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (a) relevant to the factors in section 6 of Schedule 1 that were addressed, if any,

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (b) relevant to any factor that the person addressed that is not a factor listed in section 6 of Schedule 1, and

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (c) either available to the person or in the control or possession of the person.

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (3) The minister must approve the regeneration date, free growing height and stocking standards referred to in section 16 (3) if the minister is satisfied that

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (a) the regeneration date and the standards will result in the area being stocked with ecologically suitable species that address immediate and long-term forest health issues on the area, to a density or to a basal area that, in either case,

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (i)  is consistent with maintaining or enhancing an economically valuable supply of commercial timber from British Columbia's forests, and

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (ii)  is consistent with the timber supply analysis and forest management assumptions that apply to the area covered by the plan on the date that the plan is submitted for approval, and

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (b) the free growing height is of sufficient height to demonstrate that the tree is adapted to the site, and is growing well and can reasonably be expected to continue to do so.

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (4) The minister must approve the stocking standards referred to in section 16 (4) if the minister is satisfied that the standards will result in the area being stocked with ecologically suitable species that address immediate and long-term forest health issues on the area, to a density or to a basal area that, in either case, is consistent with

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (a) maintaining or enhancing an economically valuable supply of commercial timber from British Columbia's forests, and

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (b) the timber supply analysis and forest management assumptions that apply to the area covered by the plan on the date that the plan is submitted for approval.

heading: Minister's consideration of stocking standards
paragraph: (5) The minister may approve the stocking standards referred to in section 16 (3) or (4), even though they do not conform to subsection (3) or (4) of this section, if the minister is satisfied that the regeneration date and stocking standards are reasonable, having regard to the future timber supply for the area.

heading: Balancing objectives
paragraph:
27
		  The minister may balance established objectives, results, strategies or other plan content when making a determination under section 16 [approval of forest stewardship plan or amendment] of the Act.

heading: Approval in emergency cases
paragraph:
27.1
		  For the purpose of section 17 of the Act, the prescribed circumstances are those described in that section.

heading: Extending term
paragraph:
28
		  For the purpose of section 6 (2) [term of forest stewardship plan] of the Act, the minister may extend the term of a forest stewardship plan if

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (a) the holder of the plan requests an extension, and

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (b) the minister is satisfied that the forest development units and the results and strategies in the plan

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (i)  continue to be consistent with established objectives, or

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (ii)  will be amended so as to be consistent with established objectives.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph:
28.1
		  (1) For the purposes of section 8 (1) (a) (ii) of the Act, the holder of a forest stewardship plan must propose and submit, for approval by the minister and in accordance with that section, an amendment to the plan if a forest development unit included in the plan is affected by the establishment, variation or cancellation of any of the following:

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) a lakeshore management zone objective;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) a water quality objective;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (c) a wildlife habitat area objective;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (d) an ungulate winter range objective;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (e) a fisheries sensitive watershed objective.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 8 (1) (b) (i) of the Act, the holder of a forest stewardship plan must propose and submit, for approval by the minister and in accordance with that section, an amendment to the plan if a forest development unit included in the plan is affected by the designation of a temperature sensitive stream under section 15 of the Government Actions Regulation.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of section 8 (4) (b) of the Act, an amendment required under subsection (2) of this section must be submitted within 1 year after the date on which the temperature sensitive stream is designated.

heading: Amendments that require approval
paragraph:
29
		  The following are the prescribed circumstances, referred to in section 20 (1) of the Act, in which an approval is required to amend a forest stewardship plan, despite a determination under that provision:

heading: Amendments that require approval
paragraph: (a) the addition of a new forest development unit;

heading: Amendments that require approval
paragraph: (b) a material change to an existing forest development unit;

heading: Amendments that require approval
paragraph: (c) an intended result or strategy described in section 12.2 to 12.5 of this regulation;

heading: Amendments that require approval
paragraph: (d) a result or strategy in respect of which a remediation order under section 74 of the Act is outstanding;

heading: Amendments that require approval
paragraph: (e) a change to the regeneration date, free growing date, free growing height or stocking standards that apply to an area in a manner that would be a significant departure from that originally approved in the plan;

heading: Amendments that require approval
paragraph: (f) a matter referred to in section 8 (1) or (2) of the Act.

heading: Amendments that do not require approval
paragraph:
30
		  (1) For the purpose of section 20 (1) (b) of the Act, a proposed amendment to a forest stewardship plan to identify a declared area does not require approval of the minister.

heading: Amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (2) An amendment under section 20 (1) of the Act that does not require the approval of the minister takes effect on the date a copy of it is provided to the district manager in accordance with section 20 (2) of the Act.

heading: Amendment wrongly made
paragraph:
31
		  (1) Under section 20 (3) of the Act, if after giving the holder of a forest stewardship plan who made a determination under section 20 (1) of the Act an opportunity to be heard, the minister determines that the holder's determination was wrongly made, the minister may

heading: Amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (a) declare the amendment that was the subject of the holder's determination to be without effect, and

heading: Amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (b) if the minister considers it appropriate, require the holder to suspend operations that are not authorized in the absence of the amendment.

heading: Amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (2) The holder of a forest stewardship plan referred to in subsection (1) does not contravene the Act or this regulation by carrying out, before the minister makes a determination under subsection (1), operations that are not authorized in the absence of the amendment if

heading: Amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (a) the minister is satisfied, or

heading: Amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (b) the holder establishes that the holder had reason to believe

heading: Amendment wrongly made
paragraph: that the amendment would have been approved under section 16 (1) of the Act, had the amendment been properly submitted for approval.

heading: Exemption from review and comment process for mandatory amendments
paragraph:
32
		  The minister may exempt a holder of a forest stewardship plan from a requirement of Division 3 pertaining to an amendment under section 8 (1) or (2) of the Act, if the minister is satisfied that the requirement is not practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to a particular area.

heading: Criteria for when section 8 of the Act does not apply
paragraph:
32.1
		  The prescribed criteria with which a portion of the area to which a forest stewardship plan applies must conform under section 19 (2) (c) of the Act, so that section 8 of the Act will not apply, are that the portion is

heading: Criteria for when section 8 of the Act does not apply
paragraph: (a) a declared area, or

heading: Criteria for when section 8 of the Act does not apply
paragraph: (c) an area for which a forestry licence to cut is issued under a pulpwood agreement.

heading: Exemptions under section 4 (1) (e) of the Act
paragraph:
32.3
		  The following are prescribed purposes under section 4 (1) (e) of the Act:

heading: Exemptions under section 4 (1) (e) of the Act
paragraph: (a) timber harvesting or road construction incidental to one or more primary forest activities, if the timber harvested outside the forest development unit does not exceed 50 m3;

heading: Exemptions under section 4 (1) (e) of the Act
paragraph: (b) timber harvesting or road construction related to a research installation that is approved by the government.

heading: Exemptions under section 4 (2) of the Act
paragraph:
32.4
		  The following are prescribed circumstances under section 4 (2) (b) of the Act:

heading: Exemptions under section 4 (2) of the Act
paragraph: (a) the timber harvesting or road construction is needed in relation to a research installation approved by the minister;

heading: Exemptions under section 4 (2) of the Act
paragraph: (b) timber harvesting or road construction is needed in support of activities authorized or required under an enactment other than the Forest Act.

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: 33		  (1) For section 10 (1) of the Act, the prescribed circumstances, in which the holder of a forest stewardship plan need not prepare a site plan in accordance with section 10 (1) (a) of the Act, are

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (a) that timber harvesting

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (i)  must proceed expeditiously to eliminate a safety hazard,

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (ii)  is needed to facilitate the collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha, or

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (iii)  is limited to a volume of timber of 50 m3 or less,

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (b) the holder is exempt under section 44 (3) of this regulation, or

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (2) For section 10 (1) of the Act, a prescribed circumstance, in which the holder of a forest stewardship plan need not prepare a site plan in accordance with section 10 (1) (b) of the Act, is that timber harvesting associated with a road referred to in that provision is limited to removal of timber to improve safety for road users by

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (a) eliminating a safety hazard,

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (b) improving visibility, or

heading: When site plans not required
paragraph: (c) increasing the number of pullouts or the size of existing pullouts.

heading: Content of site plans
paragraph:
34
		  (1) A person who prepares a site plan for an area referred to in section 29 (1) or (2) [free growing stands] of the Act must ensure that the plan identifies

heading: Content of site plans
paragraph: (a) the standards units for the area, and

heading: Content of site plans
paragraph: (b) the stocking standards and soil disturbance limits that apply to those standards units.

heading: Content of site plans
paragraph: (2) A holder of a site plan must retain the plan until the holder

heading: Content of site plans
paragraph: (a) has met the requirements in respect of the area to which the plan relates, or

heading: Content of site plans
paragraph: (b) has been relieved under section 108 [government may fund extra expense or waive obligations] of the Act of the requirements in respect of the area to which the plan relates.

heading: Forest operations map requirements - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph:
34.1
		  For the purposes of section 15.1 (2) (a) (ii) of the Act, a forest operations map prepared by the holder of a forest stewardship plan must

heading: Forest operations map requirements - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (a) be of a scale and size that the minister considers sufficient for meaningful review and comment, and

heading: Forest operations map requirements - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (b) identify

heading: Forest operations map requirements - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (i)  the holder of the forest stewardship plan who prepared the map,

heading: Forest operations map requirements - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (ii)  the forest stewardship plan to which the map relates,

heading: Forest operations map requirements - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (iii)  the approximate periods during which timber harvesting under a cutting permit is intended to occur on each cutblock required under section 15.1 (2) (a) (i) of the Act to be shown on the map, and

heading: Forest operations map requirements - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (iv)  the approximate periods during which road construction under a road permit is intended to occur on each proposed road required under section 15.1 (2)  (a) (i) of the Act to be shown on the map.

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph:
34.2
		  (1) For the purposes of making a forest operations map publicly available for review and comment under section 15.1 (2) (b) of the Act, the holder of a forest stewardship plan must publish a notice that meets the requirements set out in subsection (2)

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (a) on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the plan holder or the government, and

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (b) at least once in a newspaper.

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (2) A notice referred to in subsection (1) must include the following information, which must be the same in each notice:

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (a) a statement that the map is publicly available for review and comment at the plan holder's place of business or at another place specified in the notice;

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (b) the beginning and end dates of the period during which persons may review the map and provide comments;

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (c) an address at which and the hours during which persons may attend at the place to review the map;

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (d) if applicable, a website address at which the map may be accessed;

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (e) details regarding how comments may be submitted, including

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (i)  an address for personal delivery and the hours during which comments may be delivered,

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (ii)  a mailing address,

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (iii)  an email address, and

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (iv)  if applicable, a website address for online submission;

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (f) the 3-year period referred to in section 34.5 during which the plan holder may rely on the map for the purpose of applying for a cutting permit, or for a road permit to construct a road.

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2) (b), the period during which persons may review and provide comments in relation to the map

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (4), begins on the date specified in the notices published under subsection (1), and

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (b) ends

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (i)  30 days after that date, if no lesser number of days is determined under subparagraph (ii), or

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (ii)  a lesser number of days after that date that the minister may determine if the minister considers that the lesser number of days is necessary in order to respond to risks relating to the environment, forest health or wildfire.

heading: Publication of notice - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (4) The review period for a forest operations map must not begin until the notice required under subsection (1) in relation to the map has been published both on a publicly accessible website and at least once in a newspaper.

heading: Review and comment - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph:
34.3
		  (1) A holder of a forest stewardship plan who publishes a notice in relation to a forest operations map under section 34.2 (1) must, within the period referred to in section 34.2 (3),

heading: Review and comment - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (a) if required by the minister, refer a copy of the map to an agency of government, or of the government of Canada, specified by the minister,

heading: Review and comment - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (b) provide a person who is interested in the map with an opportunity to review the map during normal business hours at the holder's place of business or other place specified in the notice, and

heading: Review and comment - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (c) refer a copy of the map to a timber sales manager who may be affected by the proposed timber harvesting or road construction shown on the map.

heading: Review and comment - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (2) A person may submit comments in respect of the map, by the means specified in the notice, during the period referred to in section 34.2 (3).

heading: Review and comment - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (3) The holder of the forest stewardship plan must consider any comments received under subsection (2) that are relevant to the forest operations map.

heading: Report to minister - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph:
34.4
		  For the purposes of section 15.1 (2) (c) of the Act, a report prepared by the holder of a forest stewardship plan on the public review of a forest operations map must include the following:

heading: Report to minister - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (a) a copy of the notice published in relation to the forest operations map under section 34.2 (1);

heading: Report to minister - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (b) a copy of the map, in a form and manner that is satisfactory to the minister;

heading: Report to minister - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph: (c) a description of any changes made to the map as a result of the comments received under section 34.3 (2).

heading: Period during which forest operations map may be relied on
paragraph:
34.5
		  For the purposes of section 15.1 (3) (b) of the Act, a holder of a forest stewardship plan who intends to rely on a forest operations map for the purposes of applying for a cutting permit or road permit must apply for the cutting permit or road permit, as applicable, within 3 years after the date referred to in section 34.2 (3) (a).

heading: Period during which record must be kept - forest stewardship plan holder
paragraph:
34.6
		  A holder of a forest stewardship plan who publishes a notice in relation to a forest operations map under section 34.2 (1) must keep a record of the map for at least five years after the date referred to in section 34.2 (3) (a).

heading: Operating period
paragraph:
34.7
		  For the purposes of section 15.2 (1) (b) of the Act, 3 years is prescribed as the length of an operating period.

heading: Forest operations map requirements - timber sales manager
paragraph:
34.8
		  For the purposes of section 15.2 (2) (a) (iii) of the Act, a forest operations map prepared by a timber sales manager must

heading: Forest operations map requirements - timber sales manager
paragraph: (a) be of a scale and size that the minister considers sufficient for meaningful review and comment, and

heading: Forest operations map requirements - timber sales manager
paragraph: (b) identify

heading: Forest operations map requirements - timber sales manager
paragraph: (i)  the timber sales manager who prepared the map,

heading: Forest operations map requirements - timber sales manager
paragraph: (ii)  the BC timber sales business area to which the timber sales manager is appointed, and

heading: Forest operations map requirements - timber sales manager
paragraph: (iii)  the forest stewardship plan to which the map relates.

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph:
34.9
		  (1) For the purposes of making a forest operations map publicly available for review and comment under section 15.2 (2) (b) of the Act, a timber sales manager must, at least 30 days before the date the operating period to which the map relates begins, publish a notice that meets the requirements set out in subsection (2)

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (a) on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the timber sales manager or the government, and

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (b) at least once in a newspaper.

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (2) A notice referred to in subsection (1) must include the following information, which must be the same in each notice:

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (a) a statement that the map is publicly available for review and comment at the office of the timber sales manager or at another place specified in the notice;

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (b) the beginning and end dates of the period during which persons may review the map and provide comments;

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (c) an address at which and the hours during which persons may attend at the place to review the map;

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (d) if applicable, a website address at which the map may be accessed;

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (e) details regarding how comments may be submitted, including

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (i)  an address for personal delivery and the hours during which comments may be delivered,

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (ii)  a mailing address,

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (iii)  an email address, and

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (iv)  if applicable, a website address for online submission;

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (f) a statement that the timber sales manager may

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (i)  invite applications for timber sales licences for the harvesting of cutblocks shown on the map, and

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (ii)  apply for road permits to construct roads shown on the map.

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2) (b), the period during which persons may review and provide comments in relation to the map

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (4), begins on the date specified in the notices published under subsection (1), and

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (b) ends

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (i)  30 days after that date, if no lesser number of days is determined under subparagraph (ii), or

heading: Publication of notice - timber sales manager
paragraph: (ii)  a lesser number of days after that date that the minister may determine if the minister considers that the lesser number of days is necessary in order to respond to risks relating to the environment, forest health or wildfire.

paragraph: (4) The review period for a forest operations map must not begin until the notice required under subsection (1) in relation to the map has been published both on a publicly accessible website and at least once in a newspaper.

heading: Review and comment - timber sales manager
paragraph:
34.10
		  (1) A timber sales manager who publishes a notice in relation to a forest operations map under section 34.9 (1) must, within the period referred to in section 34.9 (3),

heading: Review and comment - timber sales manager
paragraph: (a) if required by the minister, refer a copy of the map to an agency of government, or of the government of Canada, specified by the minister, and

paragraph: (b) provide a person who is interested in the map with an opportunity to review the map during normal business hours at the timber sales manager's office or other place specified in the notice.

paragraph: (2) A person may submit comments in respect of the map, by the means specified in the notice, during the period referred to in section 34.9 (3).

paragraph: (3) The timber sales manager must consider any comments received under subsection (2) that are relevant to the forest operations map.

heading: Period during which record must be kept - timber sales manager
paragraph:
34.11
		  A timber sales manager who publishes a notice in relation to a forest operations map under section 34.9 (1) must keep a record of the map for at least five years after the date referred to in section 34.9 (3) (a).

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph:
35
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: "first agreement holder" means an agreement holder that is not a fibre recovery tenure holder;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: "roadside work area" means the area adjacent to a road where one or both of the following are carried out:

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) decking, processing or loading timber;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) piling or disposing of logging debris;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: "sensitive soils" means soils that, because of their slope gradient, texture class, moisture regime, or organic matter content have the following risk of displacement, surface erosion or compaction:

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) for the Interior, a very high hazard;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) for the Coast, a high or very high hazard.

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (3) An agreement holder other than a holder of a minor tenure or a fibre supply licence to cut, which holder is carrying out timber harvesting, must not cause the amount of soil disturbance on the net area to be reforested to exceed the following limits:

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) if the standards unit is predominantly comprised of sensitive soils, 5% of the area covered by the standards unit, excluding any area covered by a roadside work area;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) if the standards unit not is not predominantly comprised of sensitive soils, 10% of the area covered by the standards unit, excluding any area covered by a roadside work area;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (c) 25% of the area covered by a roadside work area.

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (4) An agreement holder may cause soil disturbance that exceeds the limits specified in subsection (3) if the holder

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) is removing infected stumps or salvaging windthrow and the additional disturbance is the minimum necessary, or

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) is constructing a temporary access structure and both of the following apply:

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (i)  the limit set out in subsection (3) (a) or (b), as applicable, is not exceeded by more than 5% of the area covered by the standards unit, excluding the area covered by a roadside work area;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (ii)  before the regeneration date, a sufficient amount of the area within the standards unit is rehabilitated such that the agreement holder is in compliance with the limits set out in subsection (3).

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (4.1) Despite subsections (3) and (4), if a first agreement holder is authorized to carry out timber harvesting in an area and a fibre recovery tenure holder is authorized to carry out timber harvesting in an area that overlaps with the area of the first agreement holder, the agreement holders must not cause the cumulative amount of soil disturbance from all primary forest activities carried out on the area of overlap to exceed 25% of that area.

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (4.2) Subsection (4.1) does not apply in respect of any area of overlap occupied by a permanent access structure.

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (5) The minister may require an agreement holder to rehabilitate an area of compacted soil if all of the following apply:

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) the area of compacted soil

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (i)  was created by activities of the holder,

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (ii)  is within the net area to be reforested, and

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (iii)  is a minimum of 1 ha in size;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) the holder has not exceeded the limits described in subsection (3) or the holders have not exceeded the limit described in subsection (4.1), as applicable;

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (c) rehabilitation would, in the opinion of the minister,

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (i)  materially improve the productivity and the hydrologic function of the soil within the area, and

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (ii)  not create an unacceptable risk of further damage or harm to, or impairment of, forest resource values related to one or more of the subjects listed in section 149 (1) of the Act.

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (6) An agreement holder who rehabilitates an area under subsection (4) or (5) must

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) remove or redistribute woody materials that are exposed on the surface of the area and are concentrating subsurface moisture, to the extent necessary to limit the concentration of subsurface moisture on the area,

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) de-compact compacted soils, and

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (c) return displaced surface soils, retrievable side-cast and berm materials.

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (7) If an agreement holder rehabilitates an area under subsection (4) or (5) and erosion of exposed soil from the area would cause sediment to enter a stream, wetland or lake, or a material adverse effect in relation to one or more of the subjects listed in section 149 (1) of the Act, the agreement holder, unless placing debris or revegetation would not materially reduce the likelihood of erosion, must

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) place woody debris on the exposed soils, or

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) revegetate the exposed mineral soils.

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph:
36
		  (1) An agreement holder must ensure that the area in a cutblock that is occupied by permanent access structures built by the holder or used by the holder does not exceed 7% of the cutblock, unless

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (a) there is no other practicable option on that cutblock, having regard to

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (i)  the size, topography and engineering constraints of the cutblock,

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a road, the safety of road users, or

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (iii)  the requirement in selection harvesting systems for excavated or bladed trails or other logging trails, or

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (b) additional permanent access structures are necessary to provide access beyond the cutblock.

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (2) If an agreement holder exceeds the limit for permanent access structures described in subsection (1) for either of the reasons set out in that subsection, the holder must ensure that the limit is exceeded as little as practicable.

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (3) An agreement holder may rehabilitate an area occupied by permanent access structures in one of the following ways:

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (a) in accordance with the results or strategies specified in the forest stewardship plan;

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (b) in accordance with the planning guideline requirements, substituted requirements or additional measures specified in the forest operations plan;

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (c) under subsection (3.1).

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (3.1) An agreement holder may rehabilitate an area occupied by permanent access structures by

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (a) removing or redistributing woody materials that are exposed on the surface of the area and are concentrating subsurface moisture, as necessary to limit the concentration of subsurface moisture on the area,

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (b) de-compacting compacted soils, and

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (c) returning displaced surface soils, retrievable side-cast and berm materials.

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (4) If an agreement holder rehabilitates an area under subsection (3.1) (a) and erosion of exposed soil from the area would cause sediment to enter a stream, wetland or lake, or a material adverse effect in relation to one or more of the subjects listed in section 149 (1) of the Act, the agreement holder, unless placing debris or revegetation would not materially reduce the likelihood of erosion, must

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (a) place woody debris on the exposed soils, or

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (b) revegetate the exposed mineral soils.

heading: Landslides
paragraph:
37
		  An authorized person who carries out a primary forest activity must ensure that the primary forest activity does not cause a landslide that has a material adverse effect in relation to one or more of the subjects listed in section 149 (1) of the Act.

heading: Gully processes
paragraph:
38
		  An authorized person who carries out a primary forest activity on the Coast must ensure that the primary forest activity does not cause a gully process that has a material adverse effect in relation to one or more of the subjects listed in section 149 (1) of the Act.

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph:
39
		  (1) If an authorized person constructs a road, a temporary access structure or a permanent access structure on an area, the person must maintain natural surface drainage patterns on the area both during and after construction.

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if it is not practicable for an authorized person to maintain natural surface drainage patterns during the construction of a road, a temporary access structure or permanent access structure, the person must ensure that the altered surface drainage pattern is compatible with the original natural surface drainage pattern by the earlier of

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (a) the end of the construction, and

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (b) the next freshet.

heading: Revegetation
paragraph:
40
		  An authorized person who constructs or deactivates a road must ensure that soil exposed by the construction or deactivation is revegetated within two years after the construction or deactivation is completed if it is reasonably foreseeable that

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (a) the erosion of the soil would cause

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (i)  sediment to enter a stream, wetland or lake, or

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (ii)  a material adverse effect in relation to one or more of the subjects listed in section 149 (1) of the Act, and

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (b) revegetation would materially reduce the likelihood of erosion.

heading: Modification of insect behaviour
paragraph:
41
		  An agreement holder or a timber sales manager who uses trap trees or pheromones to concentrate insect populations must ensure that the insect brood is destroyed before the insects emerge.

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph:
42
		  If a person required to establish a free growing stand uses livestock for site preparation or brush control, the person must ensure that all necessary measures are taken to

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph: (a) control the location and movement of the livestock to minimize conflict with wildlife that could prey on the livestock,

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph: (b) prevent the transmission of disease from the livestock to wildlife, and

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph: (c) maintain the health of the livestock.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph:
43
		  (1) In this section, "transfer" means the process by which seed is selected and used, based on the origin of the seed and its genetic suitability for the site on which trees grown from the seed are to be planted.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (2) The chief forester may make standards for matters referred to in section 169 (1) (a) (i) to (v) [chief forester standards for forest practices] of the Act if the chief forester considers such standards to be necessary or appropriate for the purpose of regulating the use, registration, storage, selection or transfer of seed to be used in the establishment of free growing stands.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (3) The chief forester may authorize a person to exercise a discretion of the chief forester described in subsection (5), (6) or (7).

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (4) Unless an alternative is approved under subsection (6), a person who plants trees while establishing a free growing stand must use only seed registered, stored, selected and transferred in accordance with the standards, if any, established by the chief forester.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (5) A person referred to in subsection (4) may submit to the chief forester for approval an alternative to any standard established by the chief forester under subsection (2).

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (6) The chief forester may approve an alternative submitted under subsection (5) if the chief forester considers that the alternative is consistent with achieving the intent of the standard.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (7) If the chief forester approves an alternative submitted under subsection (5), the person who submitted the alternative

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (a) is exempt from the requirement of subsection (4) for which the alternative has been approved, and

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (b) must comply with the alternative.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (8) A person who is required to establish a free growing stand must keep a record of the registration numbers of the seed that is used, if any, and a map of the location where the trees grown from the seed are planted.

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands
paragraph:
43.1
		  (1) A holder of a cutting permit, a forestry licence to cut that does not provide for cutting permits or a timber sale licence must not carry out timber harvesting in a targeted pine leading stand, unless

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a holder of a cutting permit, a forestry licence to cut that does not provide for cutting permits or a timber sale licence may harvest timber in a targeted pine leading stand without retaining an adequate stocking density of suitable secondary structure if

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands

heading: Secondary structure retention in mountain pine beetle affected stands
paragraph: (3) Without limiting the stocking standards applicable under section 29 (1) or (2) of the Act or section 46 of this regulation, if a person referred to in subsection (1) (c) carries out harvesting in a targeted pine leading stand that creates an obligation to establish a free growing stand, each tree of suitable secondary structure retained in the stand is considered to be a tree of a preferred species for the purpose of establishing a free growing stand on the area where the adequate stocking density of suitable secondary structure was retained.

paragraph: (f) an area that is subject to a cutting permit, a forestry licence to cut that does not provide for cutting permits or a timber sale licence if the timber cruising or field layout for the cutting permit, forestry licence to cut or timber sale licence has been completed before this section comes into force,

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph:
44
		  (1) A person who has an obligation to establish a free growing stand must establish, for areas that have been identified under section 16 (1) [stocking standards] or section 4.14 [specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan] as areas to which this section will apply, a stand that

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (a) meets the applicable stocking standards set out in the forest stewardship plan for the area, by the applicable regeneration date specified for the area, and

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (b) meets the applicable stocking standards and free growing height set out in the forest stewardship plan for the area by a free growing date that is no more than 20 years from the commencement date, unless the minister permits a later free growing date.

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (2) If an agreement holder contravenes section 52 (1) [unauthorized timber harvesting] of the Act, the holder must establish, on the area on which the contravention occurred, a stand that meets the requirements specified in the holder's forest stewardship plan or forest operations plan for an area with similar attributes, as if the area on which the contravention occurred had been identified under section 16 (1) or 4.14 as being subject to this section.

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (3) A person is exempt from the requirements of section 29 (1) and (2) [free growing stands] of the Act in respect of an area if timber harvesting is restricted to one or more of the following:

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (a) harvesting timber to eliminate a safety hazard;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (b) harvesting timber to facilitate the collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (c) removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (d) harvesting trees on land that is, or will be, exclusively used for harvesting hay or grazing livestock in accordance with an agreement under the Range Act;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (e) harvesting timber for experimental purposes if, in the opinion of the minister, the harvesting will be carried out under controlled scientific or investigative conditions;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (f) clearing areas for or within a recreation site or recreation trail;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (g) felling and removing trees that have been or will be treated to facilitate the entrapment of pests;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (h) commercial thinning, removal of individual trees, or a similar type of intermediate cutting;

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (i) harvesting special forest products other than woodchips or hogged tree material.

heading: Free growing stands generally
paragraph: (4) A person who harvests timber for the reasons referred to in subsection (3) (h) and (i) must ensure that, for a period of 12 months after completion of harvest, the area on which timber harvesting was carried out conforms to the stocking standards specified in section 16 (4) for the area.

heading: Free growing stands collectively across cutblocks
paragraph: 45		  (1) If a person specifies in a forest stewardship plan under section 16 (1) [specifying stocking standards in forest stewardship plan] or forest operations plan under section 4.14 [specifying stocking standards in forest operations plan] that the requirement to be met by the regeneration date relates to a group of cutblocks, the person must establish stands on the net areas to be reforested that conform to the applicable stocking standards by the applicable regeneration date, as identified under section 16 (3) (c).

heading: Free growing stands collectively across cutblocks
paragraph: (2) If a person specifies in a forest stewardship plan under section 16 (1) or forest operations plan under section 4.14 that the requirement to be met by the free growing date relates to a group of cutblocks, the person must establish stands on the net areas to be reforested that conform to the applicable stocking standards by the applicable free growing date as identified under section 16 (3) (d).

paragraph:
