heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Freshwater Fish Marketing Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 In this Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Board means the Board of Directors of the Corporation; (conseil)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Chairperson means the Chairperson of the Board; (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: container includes any type of receptacle, package, wrapper or confining band, used in packing or marketing fish; (emballage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Corporation means the Freshwater Fish Marketing Corporation established by subsection 3(1); (Office)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means such member of the Queen's Privy Council for Canada as is designated by the Governor in Council as the Minister for the purposes of this Act; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: participating province means a province in respect of which there is in force an agreement entered into under section 24 with the government of that province; (province participante)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: President means the President of the Corporation. (president)

heading: Corporation established
paragraph: 3 (1) A corporation is hereby established, to be known as the Freshwater Fish Marketing Corporation, consisting of a Board of Directors composed of a Chairperson, a President, one director for each participating province and four other directors.

heading: Appointment of Chairperson and President
paragraph: (2) The Chairperson and the President shall each be appointed by the Governor in Council to hold office during pleasure for such term as the Governor in Council considers appropriate.

heading: Appointment of directors
paragraph: (3) Each director, other than the Chairperson and the President, shall be appointed by the Minister, with the approval of the Governor in Council, to hold office during pleasure for a term not exceeding four years that will ensure, as far as possible, the expiration in any one year of the terms of office of not more than one half of the directors.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: (4) A director of the Corporation for a participating province shall be appointed on the recommendation of the lieutenant governor in council of the participating province.

heading: Eligibility
paragraph: (5) A person who has reached the age of seventy years is not eligible to be appointed a director of the Corporation and a director of the Corporation ceases to hold office on reaching the age of seventy years.

heading: Re-appointment
paragraph: (6) A director of the Corporation on the expiration of that director's term of office is, if not disqualified by age, eligible for re-appointment.

heading: Vacancies
paragraph: (7) A vacancy on the Board does not impair the right of the remaining directors of the Corporation to act, but where the vacancy relates to the office of a director for a participating province, it shall be filled as soon as practicable in the manner provided in this section.

heading: Temporary substitute directors
paragraph: (8) If any director of the Corporation, other than the Chairperson or the President, is absent or unable to act, the Governor in Council may appoint a temporary substitute director on such conditions as the Governor in Council prescribes.

heading: Chairperson to preside at meetings
paragraph: 4 The Chairperson shall preside at meetings of the Board, but in the event of the absence or incapacity of the Chairperson, or if the office of Chairperson is vacant, the President shall preside at those meetings.

heading: Management vested in President
paragraph: 5 (1) The President is the chief executive officer of the Corporation and the general manager of its undertakings and has on behalf of the Board the direction and control of the business of the Corporation with authority to act in the conduct of the business of the Corporation in all matters that are not by this Act or by the by-laws of the Board specifically reserved to be done by the Board.

heading: Absence or incapacity of President
paragraph: (2) In the event of the absence or incapacity of the President, or if the office of President is vacant, the Board shall authorize an officer or director of the Corporation to act as President for the time being, but no person so authorized by the Board has authority to act as President for a period exceeding sixty days without the approval of the Governor in Council.

heading: Salaries and fees
paragraph: 6 (1) The President shall be paid by the Corporation a salary to be fixed by the Governor in Council and the Chairperson and the other directors of the Corporation other than the President shall be paid by the Corporation such fees for attendances at meetings of the Board or any committee thereof as are fixed by the Governor in Council.

heading: Expenses
paragraph: (2) Each director of the Corporation is entitled to be paid by the Corporation such travel and living expenses incurred by the director in the performance of his duties as are fixed by by-law of the Board.

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: 7 The Corporation is established for the purpose of marketing and trading in fish, fish products and fish by-products in and outside Canada and, in addition to the powers conferred by other provisions of this Act and by any other Act, has for that purpose power to

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (a) buy fish and dress, fillet, freeze, package or otherwise prepare fish for market;

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (b) buy, manufacture or produce fish products and fish by-products and package or otherwise prepare fish products and fish by-products for market;

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (c) store, ship, insure, import, export, market, sell or otherwise dispose of fish, fish products and fish by-products bought, prepared, manufactured or produced by it;

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (d) purchase, lease or otherwise acquire and hold, sell or otherwise deal with any real property;

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (e) establish branches or employ agents in Canada or elsewhere;

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (f) invest any money in its possession or under its control that in its opinion is not immediately required for the purposes of its operations, in securities of or guaranteed by the Government of Canada and sell any securities so acquired by it and reinvest the proceeds or any part of the proceeds thereof in like manner;

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (g) borrow money from any bank on the credit of the Corporation;

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (h) make loans of working capital on a seasonal basis to persons engaged in fishing for commercial purposes in a participating province; and

heading: Purpose and powers
paragraph: (i) do all such other things as are necessary or incidental to the exercise of any of its powers or the carrying out of any of its functions under this Act.

heading: Acceptance and exercise of additional powers
paragraph: 8 The Corporation may enter into and carry out arrangements with any government or person that the Corporation deems necessary or desirable in furtherance of the purpose for which it is established, and may receive and exercise any grants, rights, franchises, privileges and concessions that may be granted to or conferred on it by any government or person.

heading: Employment of staff
paragraph: 9 (1) The Corporation may employ such officers and employees as it considers necessary for the proper conduct of its activities.

heading: Terms and conditions of employment
paragraph: (2) The Board may by by-law prescribe the duties of the officers and employees of the Corporation and the terms and conditions of their employment.

heading: Remuneration
paragraph: (3) The persons employed pursuant to subsection (1) shall be paid by the Corporation such remuneration as is fixed by by-law of the Board.

heading: Application of certain Acts and regulations
paragraph: 10 (1) The President and the officers and employees of the Corporation shall be deemed to be employed in the public service for the purposes of the Public Service Superannuation Act and the Corporation shall be deemed to be a Public Service corporation for the purposes of section 37 of that Act.

heading: Idem
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of the Government Employees Compensation Act and any regulation made pursuant to section 9 of the Aeronautics Act, the President and the officers and employees of the Corporation shall be deemed to be employed in the federal public administration.

heading: Directors, officers and employees not part of federal public administration
paragraph: 11 Except as provided in section 10, a director or an officer or employee of the Corporation is not in that capacity part of the federal public administration.

heading: Board may make by-laws
paragraph: 12 The Board may make by-laws

heading: Board may make by-laws
paragraph: (a) respecting the calling of meetings of the Board;

heading: Board may make by-laws
paragraph: (b) respecting the conduct of business at meetings of the Board and the establishment of committees thereof, the delegation of duties to those committees and the fixing of quorums for meetings of the Board and committees thereof;

heading: Board may make by-laws
paragraph: (c) subject to the approval of the Treasury Board, fixing the travel and living expenses to be paid to the directors of the Corporation;

heading: Board may make by-laws
paragraph: (d) respecting the duties and conduct of the directors of the Corporation; and

heading: Board may make by-laws
paragraph: (e) generally, for the conduct and management of the affairs of the Corporation.

heading: Head office
paragraph: 13 The head office of the Corporation shall be at the city of Winnipeg or in the immediate vicinity thereof, in the Province of Manitoba, but meetings of the Board may be held at such other places in Canada as the Board may determine.

heading: Agent of Her Majesty
paragraph: 14 The Corporation is for all purposes of this Act an agent of Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Conduct of financial operations
paragraph: 15 (1) The Corporation shall conduct its operations on a self-sustaining financial basis without appropriations therefor by Parliament.

heading: Payments in lieu of land taxes
paragraph: (2) The Corporation may make grants in lieu of taxes to any municipality in Canada not exceeding the taxes that might be levied by the municipality in respect of any lands of the Corporation if the Corporation were not an agent of Her Majesty.

heading: Minister of Finance may guarantee borrowing by and make loans to Corporation
paragraph: 16 (1) For the purpose of enabling the Corporation to carry on its operations under this Act, the Governor in Council may authorize the Minister of Finance, on such terms and conditions as may be agreed on,

heading: Minister of Finance may guarantee borrowing by and make loans to Corporation
paragraph: (a) to guarantee repayment of loans, and interest thereon, made by any bank to the Corporation; and

heading: Minister of Finance may guarantee borrowing by and make loans to Corporation
paragraph: (b) to make loans to the Corporation.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) The aggregate outstanding at any time of the amounts borrowed by the Corporation pursuant to paragraph 7(g) and the amounts lent by the Minister of Finance under this section shall not exceed fifty million dollars.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 19 In this Part, except section 30,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fish means round, dressed or filleted fish of any species enumerated in the schedule, whether fresh or frozen and whether packaged or unpackaged, that are fished for commercial purposes in a participating province, and includes parts of any such fish; (poisson)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fisherman means a person licensed pursuant to the Fisheries Act or the regulations thereunder to fish for commercial purposes in a participating province, and includes any person acting on behalf of and representing any two or more persons so licensed. (pecheur)

heading: Trade in fish
paragraph: 20 (1) Except in accordance with the terms and conditions set out in any licence that may be issued by the Corporation in that behalf, no person, other than the Corporation or an agent of the Corporation, shall

heading: Trade in fish
paragraph: (a) export fish from Canada;

heading: Trade in fish
paragraph: (b) send, convey or carry fish from a participating province to another participating province or to any other province;

heading: Trade in fish
paragraph: (c) in a participating province, receive fish for conveyance or carriage to a destination outside the province; or

heading: Trade in fish
paragraph: (d) sell or buy, or agree to sell or buy, fish situated in a participating province for delivery in another participating province or any other province, or outside Canada.

heading: By-laws respecting licences
paragraph: (2) The Board may, for the purposes of this section, make by-laws providing for the issue of licences by the Corporation and prescribing the form of and the terms and conditions to be set out in those licences.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 21 The Governor in Council may by regulation

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) add to the schedule any species of fish that are fished in a participating province or delete from the schedule any species of fish enumerated therein; or

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) exempt from the application of all or any of the provisions of this Part, either conditionally or unconditionally and either in general terms or for a specified period, any species of fish enumerated in the schedule, any area or region in a participating province or any transaction, person or class of transactions or persons.

heading: Corporation to undertake interprovincial and export marketing of fish
paragraph: 22 (1) Subject to section 20, the Corporation has the exclusive right to trade in and to market fish in interprovincial and export trade and shall exercise that right, either by itself or by its agents, with the object of

heading: Corporation to undertake interprovincial and export marketing of fish
paragraph: (a) marketing fish in an orderly manner;

heading: Corporation to undertake interprovincial and export marketing of fish
paragraph: (b) increasing returns to fishermen; and

heading: Corporation to undertake interprovincial and export marketing of fish
paragraph: (c) promoting international markets for, and increasing interprovincial and export trade in, fish.

heading: Corporation to buy all fish offered
paragraph: (2) All fish lawfully fished by a fisherman and offered by the fisherman for sale to the Corporation for disposal in interprovincial or export trade shall be bought by the Corporation from the fisherman on such terms and conditions and for such price as may be agreed on by the Corporation and the fisherman subject to any applicable scheme for payment established and operated by the Corporation pursuant to section 23.

heading: Marketing of fish
paragraph: (3) The Corporation shall determine the form in which fish bought by it pursuant to this section shall be marketed and shall carry out or cause to be carried out any processing or preparation for market that it deems necessary, and the Corporation shall market the fish at such times and places and in such manner as in its opinion will best achieve the attainment of the objects mentioned in subsection (1).

heading: Price systems and pooling authorized
paragraph: 23 The Corporation may develop, establish and operate schemes for payment for fish bought by it pursuant to this Part that provide for either or both

heading: Price systems and pooling authorized
paragraph: (a) a system of initial and final prices or payments; and

heading: Price systems and pooling authorized
paragraph: (b) the pooling of receipts for fish, including the operation of pool accounts, either generally or in relation to the area or region where the fish were fished, or the species, volume or quality of the fish sold to the Corporation, or on such other basis as the Corporation deems appropriate.

heading: Agreements Respecting Participation
paragraph: Definition of province to which this section applies

heading: Agreements Respecting Participation
paragraph: 24 (1) In this section, province to which this section applies means any of the following provinces or territories, namely, Ontario, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, the Northwest Territories or Nunavut.

heading: Participation agreements
paragraph: (2) With the approval of the Governor in Council, the Minister may, on behalf of the Government of Canada, enter into an agreement with the government of any province to which this section applies, providing for

heading: Participation agreements
paragraph: (a) the sharing by the province with the Government of Canada of initial operating and establishment expenses of the Corporation and of any losses incurred as a result of the guarantee, under paragraph 16(1)(a), of repayments of loans, and interest thereon, made by any bank to the Corporation;

heading: Participation agreements
paragraph: (b) the performance by the Corporation, on behalf of the province, of functions relating to intraprovincial trade in fish;

heading: Participation agreements
paragraph: (c) the undertaking by the province of arrangements for the payment, to the owner of any plant or equipment used in storing, processing or otherwise preparing fish for market, of compensation for any such plant or equipment that will or may be rendered redundant by reason of any operations authorized to be carried out by the Corporation under this Part; and

heading: Participation agreements
paragraph: (d) such other matters as may be agreed on by the Minister and the government of the province.

heading: Inspectors
paragraph: 25 (1) The Governor in Council may designate any qualified person as an inspector for the purposes of this Part.

heading: Certificate to be produced
paragraph: (2) An inspector shall be furnished with a certificate of his designation as an inspector and on entering any place, premises or conveyance referred to in subsection 26(1) shall, if so required, produce the certificate to the person in charge thereof.

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: 26 (1) Subject to subsection (1.1), an inspector may at any reasonable time

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (a) enter any place or premises that the inspector believes on reasonable grounds is being used to store, pack, process or prepare fish for market or shipment or any vehicle, trailer, vessel, railway car or aircraft that the inspector believes on reasonable grounds is being used to ship or convey fish for market;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (b) open any container found therein or examine anything found therein that the inspector believes on reasonable grounds contains any such fish, and take samples thereof; and

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (c) require any person to produce for inspection or for the purpose of obtaining copies thereof or extracts therefrom, any books, shipping bills, bills of lading, invoices or other documents or papers concerning any matter relevant to the administration of this Part.

heading: Warrant required to enter dwelling-house
paragraph: (1.1) Where any place or premises referred to in paragraph (1)(a) is a dwelling-house, an inspector may not enter that dwelling-house without the consent of the occupant except under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (1.2).

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (1.2) Where on ex parte application a justice of the peace is satisfied by information on oath

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) that the conditions for entry described in paragraph (1)(a) exist in relation to a dwelling-house,

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) that entry to the dwelling-house is necessary for any purpose relating to the administration or enforcement of this Act, and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (c) that entry to the dwelling-house has been refused or that there are reasonable grounds for believing that entry thereto will be refused,

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: the justice of the peace may issue a warrant under his hand authorizing the inspector named therein to enter that dwelling-house subject to such conditions as may be specified in the warrant.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (1.3) In executing a warrant issued under subsection (1.2), the inspector named therein shall not use force unless the inspector is accompanied by a peace officer and the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: (2) The owner or person in charge of any place, premises or conveyance referred to in subsection (1) and every person found therein shall give an inspector all reasonable assistance to enable the inspector to carry out his duties and functions under this Part and shall furnish the inspector with any information he may reasonably require with respect to the administration of this Part.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: 27 (1) Where an inspector believes on reasonable grounds that any provision of this Part has been contravened, the inspector may seize and detain the fish by means of or in relation to which he believes on reasonable grounds the contravention was committed.

heading: Detention
paragraph: (2) Any fish seized and detained pursuant to subsection (1) shall not be detained after

heading: Detention
paragraph: (a) in the opinion of an inspector, the provisions of this Part have been complied with, or

heading: Detention
paragraph: (b) the expiration of ninety days after the date of seizure,

heading: Detention
paragraph: unless before that time proceedings have been instituted in respect of the contravention, in which event the fish may be detained until the proceedings are finally concluded.

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: (3) Where a person has been convicted of a contravention of any provision of this Part, any fish by means of or in relation to which the offence was committed is, on the conviction, in addition to any punishment imposed, forfeited to Her Majesty if the forfeiture is directed by the court.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (4) The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) respecting the detention of fish seized under this section and for preserving or safeguarding the fish so detained; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the disposition of fish forfeited under this section.

heading: Obstruction and false statements
paragraph: 28 No person shall obstruct or hinder, or make a false or misleading statement either orally or in writing to, an inspector while the inspector is engaged in carrying out his duties or functions under this Part.

heading: Contravention of this Part
paragraph: 29 (1) Every person who, or whose employee or agent, contravenes any provision of this Part

heading: Contravention of this Part
paragraph: (a) is guilty of an indictable offence and liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years; or

heading: Contravention of this Part
paragraph: (b) is guilty of an offence punishable on summary conviction.

heading: Offence by employee or agent
paragraph: (2) In any prosecution for an offence under this Part, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by an employee or agent of the accused whether or not the employee or agent is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence, unless the accused establishes that the offence was committed without the knowledge or consent of the accused and that the accused exercised all due diligence to prevent its commission.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (3) Any proceedings by way of summary conviction in respect of an offence under this Part may be instituted at any time within but not later than one year after the time when the subject-matter of the proceedings arose.

heading: Evidence with respect to geographical origin
paragraph: 30 In any prosecution for an offence under this Part, evidence that a container was marked in such a manner as to indicate or give rise to a reasonable belief that the fish contained therein were the product of or were fished in a particular participating province or a particular area or region in the province is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, proof that the fish contained therein were fished in that province.

heading: Venue
paragraph: 31 A complaint or information in respect of an offence under this Part may be heard, tried or determined by a provincial court judge or a justice if the accused is resident or carrying on business within the territorial jurisdiction of that provincial court judge or justice, although the matter of the complaint or information did not arise in that territorial jurisdiction.

heading: Submission to lieutenant governors
paragraph: 32 The Corporation shall submit a copy of each annual report of the Corporation prepared in accordance with section 150 of the Financial Administration Act to the lieutenant governor in council of each participating province.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation, "fish" means a freshwater species of

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) Order Petromyzoniformes (lampreys),

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) Class Osteichthyes (bony fishes),

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) Class Crustacea (crustaceans), or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) Class Mollusca

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: and their eggs and juvenile stages but does not include

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) goldfish, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (f) species of ornamental tropical fishes.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
2
		  A person commits an offence where the person

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) has in possession,

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) transports, or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) traffics in

heading: Offences
paragraph: live fish unless authorized by a permit or a licence.

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph:
3
		  A regional manager or a person authorized by a regional manager may issue a permit in accordance with this regulation on the terms and for the period the regional manager or the person authorized by the regional manager specifies authorizing a person to

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (a) possess,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (b) transport, or

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (c) traffic in

paragraph: live fish.

heading: Fee for authorization by permit
paragraph:
4
		  The fee for a permit issued under section 3 is $25 and the habitat conservation trust fund surcharge to be paid is $5.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation "Act" means the Forest and Range Practices Act.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) Words and expressions not defined in this regulation have the meanings given to them in section 1 of the Forest Planning and Practices Regulation unless the context indicates otherwise.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (3) This regulation applies despite section 16 (2) of the Act.

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: 2		  (1) In addition to the criteria and procedures to be followed by a minister in making an order under any of sections 5 to 15 in relation to an area specified in the order, the minister must be satisfied that

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (a) the order is consistent with established objectives, and

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (c) the benefits to the public derived from the order would outweigh any

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (i)  material adverse impact of the order on the delivered wood costs of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act that would be affected by the order, and

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (ii)  undue constraint on the ability of a holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or the Range Act that would be affected by the order to exercise the holder's rights under the agreement.

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (2) An order under any of sections 5 to 15 does not apply in respect of

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (a) any of the following entered into before the order takes effect:

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (i)  a cutting permit;

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (ii)  a road permit;

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (iii)  a timber sale licence that does not provide for cutting permits;

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (iv)  a forestry licence to cut issued by a timber sales manager under section 47.6 (3) of the Forest Act;

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (v)  subject to subsection (3), a minor tenure,

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (b) a declared area,

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (c) areas described in section 196 (1) of the Act, and

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (d) areas referred to in section 110 of the Forest Planning and Practices Regulation.

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (3) A minister who makes an order under any of sections 5 to 15

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (a) may specify in the order that it applies to a minor tenure entered into before the order, and

heading: Limitation on actions
paragraph: (b) may specify an effective date for the order that is later than the date of publication, under section 4 (2) (b), of the notice in the Gazette.

heading: Consultations and reviews
paragraph: 3		  (1) Before a minister makes an order under any of sections 5 to 15, the minister must provide an opportunity for review and comment,

heading: Consultations and reviews
paragraph: (a) in the case of an order under section 13 establishing a species category, to organizations that the minister considers representative of holders of agreements under the Forest Act or the Range Act that may be affected by the order, or

heading: Consultations and reviews
paragraph: (b) in the case of any other order, to the holders of agreements under the Forest Act or the Range Act that will be affected by the order.

heading: Consultations and reviews
paragraph: (2) A minister before making an order under any of sections 5 to 12, 14 or 15 must consult holders referred to in section 2 (1) (c) on whom the order may have a material adverse effect.

heading: Notice of an order under this regulation
paragraph: 4		  (1) Notice must be given in accordance with this section of an order made under any of sections 5 to 15.

heading: Notice of an order under this regulation
paragraph: (2) The notice required under subsection (1) is sufficiently given if the notice includes a copy of the order or contains particulars or a summary of the order and is

heading: Notice of an order under this regulation
paragraph: (b) published in the Gazette, and

heading: Notice of an order under this regulation
paragraph: (c) made publicly available at the regional office of the forest region to which the order relates.

heading: Notice of an order under this regulation
paragraph: (3) An order made under any of sections 5 to 15 takes effect

heading: Notice of an order under this regulation
paragraph: (a) on the effective date specified under section 2 (3) (b), or

heading: Notice of an order under this regulation
paragraph: (b) if no effective date is specified under section 2 (3) (b), on the date notice is published under subsection (2) (b) of this section.

heading: Resource features
paragraph:
5
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the minister responsible for the Forest Act by order may identify one or more of the following as resource features in relation to a specified area:

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (a) a surface or subsurface element of a karst system;

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (b) a range development;

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (c) Crown land used for research or experimental purposes;

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (d) a permanent sample site used as a snow course by or on behalf of the federal or Provincial government for the purpose of measuring the water content of the snow pack on a given area;

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (e) a cultural heritage resource that is the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people and that is not regulated by the Heritage Conservation Act;

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (g) a trail or other recreation facility referred to in section 57 of the Act that is authorized by the minister or under another enactment;

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (h) a recreation feature that the minister considers to be of significant recreational value.

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Forest Act may make an order under subsection (1) if the minister is satisfied that the resource feature requires special management not otherwise provided for under this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (3) The identification of a resource feature under subsection (1)

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (a) may be by category or type, and may be restricted to a specified geographic location, and

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (b) must be sufficiently specific to enable a person affected by it to identify the resource feature in the ordinary course of carrying out forest practices or range practices.

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (4) Despite subsections (1) to (3), if the minister responsible for the Forest Act reasonably believes that a resource feature may be subject to damage or disturbance if the location of the resource feature is disclosed, that minister

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (a) must not disclose the location of the feature in the order,

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (b) must provide written notice of the location of the feature to the holders of agreements under the Forest Act or the Range Act that will be affected by the order, and

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (c) may attach conditions to the order

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (i)  prohibiting those holders from disclosing the location of the feature, or

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (ii)  restricting the extent to which, or the persons to whom, those holders may disclose the location of the feature.

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (5) A person to whom a condition referred to in subsection (4) (c) applies must comply with the condition.

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: 6		  (1) The minister responsible for the Forest Act by order may

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (a) establish as a lakeshore management zone an area adjacent to a lake with a riparian class of L1, and

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (b) specify a width for the lakeshore management zone

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: if satisfied that the forest resources within the area require special management that has not otherwise been provided for by this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Lakeshore management zones and objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Forest Act by order may establish for a lakeshore management zone objectives that are consistent with subsection (1).

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: 7		  (1) The minister responsible for the Land Act by order may establish an area as a scenic area if satisfied that the area

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (a) is visually important based on its physical characteristics and public use, and

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (b) requires special management that has not otherwise been provided for by this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Scenic areas and visual quality objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Forest Act by order may establish for a scenic area visual quality objectives that are consistent with subsection (1) and are within the categories of altered forest landscape prescribed under section 1.1 of the Forest Planning and Practices Regulation.

heading: Community watersheds and water quality objectives
paragraph: 8		  (1) The minister responsible for the Land Act by order may designate as a community watershed all or part of the drainage area that is upslope of the lowest point from which water is diverted for human consumption by a licensed waterworks, if satisfied that, to protect the water that is diverted for human consumption, the area requires special management, that is not otherwise provided for under this regulation or another enactment,

heading: Community watersheds and water quality objectives
paragraph: (a) to conserve the quality, quantity and timing of water flow, or

heading: Community watersheds and water quality objectives
paragraph: (b) to prevent cumulative hydrological effects that would have a material adverse effect on the water.

heading: Community watersheds and water quality objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish for a community watershed water quality objectives respecting a matter referred to in subsection (1).

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: 9		  (1) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish a general wildlife measure, to be applied to a specified area, for a category of species at risk, regionally important wildlife or specified ungulate species, if satisfied that

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (a) the measure is necessary to protect or conserve the species in the category in the area to which the measure relates, and

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (b) this regulation or another enactment does not otherwise provide for that protection or conservation.

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish a general wildlife measure for a wildlife habitat area or an ungulate winter range if satisfied that

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (a) the measure is necessary to protect or conserve the wildlife habitat area or ungulate winter range, and

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (b) this regulation or another enactment does not otherwise provide for that protection or conservation.

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: 9.1		  The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish a general measure in relation to ecological communities, to be applied to a specified area, for a category of ecological community at risk if satisfied that

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: (a) the measure is necessary to protect or conserve the ecological community in the category in the area to which the measure relates, and

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: (b) this regulation or another enactment does not otherwise provide for that protection or conservation.

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: 10		  (1) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish an area as a wildlife habitat area if satisfied that the area is necessary to meet the habitat requirements of a category of species at risk or regionally important wildlife.

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish a wildlife habitat area objective for a wildlife habitat area if satisfied that the wildlife habitat area requires special management that has not otherwise been provided for under this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), if the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act reasonably believes that a wildlife habitat area is sensitive to damage or disturbance, that minister

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (a) must not disclose the location of the wildlife habitat area in the order,

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (b) must provide written notice of the location of the wildlife habitat area to the holders of agreements under the Forest Act or the Range Act that will be affected by the order, and

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (c) may attach conditions to the order

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (i)  prohibiting those holders from disclosing the location of the wildlife habitat area, or

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (ii)  restricting the extent to which, or the persons to whom, those holders may disclose the location of the wildlife habitat area.

heading: Wildlife habitat areas and objectives
paragraph: (4) A person to whom a condition referred to in subsection (3) (c) applies must comply with the condition.

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: 11		  (1) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may identify any or all of the following as a wildlife habitat feature:

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (a) a fisheries sensitive feature;

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (b) a marine sensitive feature;

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (c) a significant mineral lick or wallow;

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (d) a nest of

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (i)  a bald eagle,

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (ii)  an osprey,

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (iii)  a great blue heron, or

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (iv)  a category of species at risk that is limited to birds;

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (e) any other localized feature that the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act considers to be a wildlife habitat feature;

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: if satisfied that the wildlife habitat feature requires special management that has not otherwise been provided for under this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (2) Identification of a wildlife habitat feature under subsection (1)

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (a) may be by category or type, and may be restricted to a specified geographic location, and

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (b) must be sufficiently specific to enable a person affected by it to identify the wildlife habitat feature in the ordinary course of carrying out forest practices or range practices.

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), if the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act reasonably believes that a wildlife habitat feature is sensitive to damage or disturbance, that minister

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (a) must not disclose the location of the feature in the order,

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (b) must provide written notice of the location of the feature to the holders of agreements under the Forest Act or the Range Act that will be affected by the order, and

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (c) may attach conditions to the order

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (i)  prohibiting those holders from disclosing the location of the feature, or

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (ii)  restricting the extent to which, or the persons to whom, those holders may disclose the location of the feature.

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (4) A person to whom a condition referred to in subsection (3) (c) applies must comply with the condition.

heading: Ungulate winter ranges and objectives
paragraph: 12		  (1) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish an area as an ungulate winter range if satisfied that

heading: Ungulate winter ranges and objectives
paragraph: (a) the area contains habitat that is necessary to meet the winter habitat requirements for a category of specified ungulate species, and

heading: Ungulate winter ranges and objectives
paragraph: (b) the habitat referred to in paragraph (a) requires special management that is not otherwise provided for under this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Ungulate winter ranges and objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish an ungulate winter range objective for an ungulate winter range if satisfied that the ungulate winter range requires special management that is not otherwise provided for under this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Species at risk, regionally important wildlife and ungulate species
paragraph: 13		  (1) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish one or more categories identifying species of wildlife as species at risk if satisfied that the species are endangered, threatened or vulnerable.

heading: Species at risk, regionally important wildlife and ungulate species
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish one or more categories identifying species of wildlife as regionally important wildlife if satisfied that the species

heading: Species at risk, regionally important wildlife and ungulate species
paragraph: (a) are important to a region of British Columbia,

heading: Species at risk, regionally important wildlife and ungulate species
paragraph: (b) rely on habitat that requires special management that is not otherwise provided for in this regulation or another enactment, and

heading: Species at risk, regionally important wildlife and ungulate species
paragraph: (c) may be adversely impacted by forest practices or range practices.

heading: Species at risk, regionally important wildlife and ungulate species
paragraph: (3) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish one or more categories identifying ungulate species for which an ungulate winter range is required if satisfied that the range is necessary for the winter survival of the identified species.

heading: Ecological communities and objectives
paragraph: 13.1		  (1) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish one or more categories identifying ecological communities at risk if satisfied that the ecological communities are endangered, threatened or vulnerable.

heading: Ecological communities and objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish one or more categories identifying ecological communities as regionally important if satisfied that the communities

heading: Ecological communities and objectives
paragraph: (a) are important to a region of British Columbia,

heading: Ecological communities and objectives
paragraph: (b) provide habitat that requires special management that is not otherwise provided for in this regulation or another enactment, and

heading: Ecological communities and objectives
paragraph: (c) may be adversely impacted by forest practices or range practices.

heading: Fisheries sensitive watersheds and objectives
paragraph: 14		  (1) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may identify as a fisheries sensitive watershed an area of land in a watershed that has significant downstream fisheries values and significant watershed sensitivity if satisfied that the area requires special management to protect fish, that is not otherwise provided for under this regulation or another enactment, by

heading: Fisheries sensitive watersheds and objectives
paragraph: (a) conserving

heading: Fisheries sensitive watersheds and objectives
paragraph: (i)  the natural hydrological conditions, natural stream bed dynamics and stream channel integrity, and

heading: Fisheries sensitive watersheds and objectives
paragraph: (ii)  the quality, quantity and timing of water flow, or

heading: Fisheries sensitive watersheds and objectives
paragraph: (b) preventing cumulative hydrological effects that would have a material adverse effect on fish.

heading: Fisheries sensitive watersheds and objectives
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may establish a fisheries sensitive watershed objective respecting a matter referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Temperature sensitive streams
paragraph: 15		  The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act by order may designate a portion of a fish stream as a temperature sensitive stream if satisfied that

heading: Temperature sensitive streams
paragraph: (a) trees are required adjacent to the stream to manage the temperature of the designated portion for the protection of fish, and

heading: Temperature sensitive streams
paragraph: (b) management of the temperature of the designated portion is not otherwise provided for under this regulation or another enactment.

heading: Community watershed continued
paragraph: 16		  A community watershed is continued as a community watershed under this regulation if the community watershed was

heading: Community watershed continued
paragraph: (b) in existence on the coming into force of this section.

heading: Visual quality class continued
paragraph: 17		  A visual quality class for a scenic area is continued under this regulation as a visual quality objective if

heading: Visual quality class continued
paragraph: (a) the visual quality class has been

heading: Visual quality class continued
paragraph: (i)  set out before October 24, 2002 in a letter from the district manager to the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act, or

heading: Visual quality class continued
paragraph: (ii)  included in the most recent tree farm licence visual landscape inventory prepared by the holder of a tree farm licence and approved by the regional manager, and

heading: Visual quality class continued
paragraph: (b) in existence on the coming into force of this section.

heading: Categories of landscape modification apply to continued visual quality objectives
paragraph: 18		  The categories of altered forest landscape prescribed in section 1.1 of the Forest Planning and Practices Regulation apply to visual quality objectives continued under section 181 of the Act or under section 17 of this regulation.

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (a) contained in a higher level plan that is applicable to the area and is still in effect, or

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (b) made available, in accordance with paragraph (b) of the definition of "known" in section 1 (1) of the Operational and Site Planning Regulation, to one or more holders of

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (i)  agreements under the Forest Act or Range Act, or

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (ii)  agreements entered into under the Forest Act or Range Act, in replacement for agreements referred to in subparagraph (i), and

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: in effect on the coming into force of this section.

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (a) contained in a higher level plan that is applicable to the area and is in effect on the coming into force of this section, or

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (b) made available, in accordance with paragraph (b) of the definition of "known" in section 1 (1) of the Woodlot Licence Forest Management Regulation, to one or more holders of

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (i)  woodlot licences under the Forest Act, or

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: (ii)  woodlot licences entered into under the Forest Act in replacement for licences referred to in subparagraph (i), and

heading: Resource features continued
paragraph: in effect on the coming into force of this section.

heading: Orders apply to Code and Code regulations
paragraph: 20		  An order under any of sections 5 to 15 in relation to an area specified in the order applies in respect of the holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or Range Act who, under Part 11 of the Forest and Range Practices Act, must comply with the requirements of the Code and Code regulations that pertain to the area.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Crown land" means ungranted Crown or public land or Crown domain within British Columbia that belongs to the government, whether or not waters flow over or cover it, and includes any right, title, estate or interest of the government in land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "greenbelt land" means land that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) considered by the minister to be suitable for preservation as greenbelt land under this Act, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) reserved or acquired for that purpose under section 3.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph:
2
		  (1) Except as provided in this Act or the regulations, greenbelt land is not subject to any other enactment, whenever enacted or made.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (2) Except in accordance with this Act or the regulations, no person may exercise a power granted under any other enactment so as to affect greenbelt land.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), this Act is subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act, the Ecological Reserve Act, the Environment and Land Use Act, the Environmental Management Act and the Water Sustainability Act.

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: 3		  For establishing and preserving greenbelt land,

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (a) the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, reserve Crown land as greenbelt land,

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (b) with the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister may acquire land on behalf of the government as greenbelt land, and

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (c) with the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister may make an agreement on behalf of the government with any of the following for the acquisition by the government of land owned by them as greenbelt land:

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (i)  Canada;

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (ii)  an agency of Canada;

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (iii)  an agency of the government;

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (iv)  a municipality or regional district;

heading: Preservation of greenbelt land
paragraph: (v)  an agency of a municipality or regional district.

heading: Greenbelt register
paragraph:
4
		  (1) The minister must maintain a greenbelt register to record all land reserved or acquired under section 3.

heading: Greenbelt register
paragraph: (2) The record may include the following:

heading: Greenbelt register
paragraph: (a) the legal description of the land;

heading: Greenbelt register
paragraph: (b) the name of the owner of the fee simple if other than the government;

heading: Greenbelt register
paragraph: (c) the estate or interest in the land held by the government and the method of acquisition;

heading: Greenbelt register
paragraph: (d) the area;

heading: Greenbelt register
paragraph: (e) the date of entry in the register.

heading: Gifts of money
paragraph:
5
		  (1) The Minister of Finance may accept money, received from a gift or grant, for the acquisition or maintenance of greenbelt land.

heading: Gifts of money
paragraph: (2) On the requisition of the minister, money accepted under subsection (1) may be paid out for this Act without any other appropriation.

heading: Disposition of greenbelt land
paragraph:
6
		  (1) With the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council and after public notice, the minister may dispose of greenbelt land in accordance with the Land Act.

heading: Disposition of greenbelt land
paragraph: (2) On disposal, the minister must delete the record of that land from the greenbelt register.

heading: Disposition of greenbelt land
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply to land acquired by gift under the former Greenbelt Protection Fund Act.

heading: Inconsistent use under existing lease or agreement
paragraph: 7		  (1) Land that, at the time it is recorded in the greenbelt register is being used, under a lease or other agreement, for a purpose inconsistent with the nature and use of the land as greenbelt land, may continue to be used for that purpose until the expiry of the term of that lease or other agreement and any extension specifically permitted by the lease or other agreement.

heading: Inconsistent use under existing lease or agreement
paragraph: (2) If, at the time it is recorded in the greenbelt register, there are buildings on greenbelt land, the minister may lease the buildings.

heading: Management of greenbelt land
paragraph:
8
		  (1) The minister is responsible for the management of greenbelt land.

heading: Management of greenbelt land
paragraph: (2) The minister may carry out maintenance, improvement and development work on greenbelt land.

heading: Management of greenbelt land
paragraph: (3) The minister may, in writing, delegate the management of greenbelt land.

heading: Lease, right of way or easement over greenbelt land
paragraph:
9
		  Despite section 6, the minister may lease or grant a right of way or easement over greenbelt land in accordance with the Land Act to any person on terms consistent with the continued existence, nature and use of the land as greenbelt land.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: 10		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "Act" means the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "annular space" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) an open space between the outside of the casing of a well and the surrounding geological formation, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) an open space between 2 or more casings in the same well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "backfill materials" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) uncontaminated natural geological materials,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) uncontaminated drill cuttings, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) uncontaminated non-toxic synthetic materials;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "borehole" means a drilled geotechnical well, other than a test pit, that is intended to remain in service for a period of not more than 30 days after construction;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "casing" means the piping or tubing installed in a well to support the sides of the well and includes production casing and surface casing;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "casing stick-up", in relation to a well, means the length of the production casing in the well that is above

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the surface of the ground adjacent to the well, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) the floor of the well sump, pump house or well pit;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "closed-loop geoexchange well" means a well, other than an open-loop geoexchange well, used or intended to be used for the purpose of heat exchange in a closed-loop geoexchange system in which there is no transfer of water between an aquifer and the well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "closure plug" means the sealant placed in the uppermost portion of a well that is being decommissioned;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "develop", in relation to a well, means remove from an aquifer the fine sediment and other organic or inorganic material that immediately surrounds the well screen, the drill hole or the intake area at the bottom of the well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "dewatering well" means a well used or intended to be used for the purpose of diverting or conveying groundwater by pumping in order to

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) facilitate an excavation,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) stabilize an area of land, a building or any other improvement, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) reduce water pressure in a geological formation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "drainage well" means a well used or intended to be used for the purpose of diverting or conveying groundwater by the force of gravity and without pumping in order to

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) facilitate an excavation,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) stabilize an area of land, a building or any other improvement, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) reduce water pressure in a geological formation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "drive shoe" means a commercially-manufactured, forged or tempered steel sleeve with a cutting edge attached to the bottom of a drive pipe or casing to act as a cutting edge or protector for the lower edge of the drive pipe or casing during drilling;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "excavated well" means a well, commonly known as a dug well, excavated by

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) digging in unconsolidated materials using manual or mechanical methods, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) blasting in consolidated materials;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "flood debris" means material, natural or otherwise, that is relocated by the movement of flood waters;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "foreign matter" means a thing, matter or substance described in section 59 (1) (a) to (g) [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into well] of the Act and includes the substances prescribed under section 2 of this regulation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "former regulation" means the Ground Water Protection Regulation, B.C. Reg. 299/2004;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "injection well" means a well used or intended to be used for the purpose of conveying water into a geological formation with the aid of a well pump;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "liner" means piping or tubing installed in a well to protect the well pump or other works in the well from damage;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "modify" means make a change, other than an alteration, to a well or wellhead;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "open-loop geoexchange well" means a water supply well that is used or intended to be used for the purpose of heat exchange in an open-loop geoexchange system in which there is a transfer of water between an aquifer and the well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "permanent" means,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) in relation to a well, a well that is intended to be in service for a period of more than 90 days after construction, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) in relation to a well pump, a well pump that is intended to remain installed in a well for a period of more than 90 days after installation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "pitless adapter" means a mechanical device attached to a casing for the underground conveyance of water to or from a well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "pumping test" means a flow test of a well in which the well is pumped and the quantity of water pumped, pumping water levels and recovery water levels are measured

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) to provide an estimate of the capacity of the well to produce groundwater, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) to assess aquifer characteristics;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "recharge well" means a well used or intended to be used for the purpose of conveying water into a geological formation without the aid of a well pump and includes soakaway pits that are unfilled and cased;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "register" means a register of registered persons maintained by the comptroller, as described in section 7 [registers of well drillers and well pump installers], in respect of

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) registered well drillers, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) registered well pump installers;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "registration number" means,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) in relation to a well driller, the registration number recorded for the well driller by the comptroller on the register of well drillers, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) in relation to a well pump installer, the registration number recorded for the well pump installer by the comptroller on the register of well pump installers;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "rehabilitate", in relation to a well, means use chemical, mechanical or physical methods to improve or restore the capacity of the well to produce groundwater;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "remediation well" means a well that is used or intended to be used for the purpose of groundwater remediation, including the removal or treatment of contaminants that have entered an aquifer;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "screen assembly", in relation to a well, means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a screen in the well,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) a closed bottom, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) any other related components, including a riser pipe, packer, screen blank or tail pipe, that are required for

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (i)  the method or type of installation of the screen, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (ii)  the nature of the geological formation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "sealant" means a sealing material or mixture of sealing materials that is

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) less permeable than the surrounding geological formation to be sealed,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) appropriate for the particular soil and water conditions, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) non-toxic and does not have an adverse impact on the quality of the groundwater in an aquifer or a well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "shut-in pressure", in relation to a flowing artesian well, means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the water pressure after the artesian flow has been stopped, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) the height of the water above the top of the production casing or above the surface of the ground after the artesian flow has been stopped;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "sounding tube" means a tube that enables the groundwater level in a well to be measured;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "static water level", in relation to a well, means the distance from the top of the production casing or the surface of the ground to the groundwater level in the well, when the groundwater level is not affected by pumping activities in the well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "surface casing" means a casing that surrounds the production casing of a well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "surface seal" means a sealant that

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) is installed in the annular space around the outside of the outermost casing and between multiple casings, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) extends to or just below the surface of the ground;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "temporary" means,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) in relation to a well, a well that is intended to be in service for a period of not more than 90 days after construction, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) in relation to a well pump, a well pump that is intended to remain installed in a well for a period of not more than 90 days after installation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "test pit" means an excavated geotechnical well that is intended to remain in service for a period of not more than 30 days after construction;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "unconsolidated aquifer" means an aquifer composed of sediment, such as gravel or sand;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "water supply well" means a well used or intended to be used for the purpose of exploring for, diverting or using groundwater, and includes a water source well, but does not include a drainage well, dewatering well or remediation well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "well construction report" means a report required under section 57 (1) [well reports] of the Act relating to the construction of a well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "well decommission report" means a report required under section 57 (1) of the Act relating to the decommissioning of a well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "well identification report" means a report required under section 55 (4) [well identification] of the Act relating to the identification of a well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "well pit" means an excavated artificial opening in the ground, lined with concrete, metal or wood, that contains a wellhead that is below the surface of the ground;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "well tag number" means the file number assigned in the government's records to the records in relation to a particular well;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "well yield test" means a flow test of a well that

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) is conducted by airlifting, bailing or a similar method, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) provides an approximate estimate of the capacity of the well to produce groundwater.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (2) In the Act and this regulation:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "flow test" means a pumping test or a well yield test;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "flowing artesian well" means a well in which water, without the aid of a well pump,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) rises above the surface of the ground or the top of the casing, if any, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) flows, either continuously or periodically.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of sections 54 [attachment of well identification plates by owner of well supplying water supply system] and 63 [protection of water supply system wells from entry of foreign matter and physical damage], "owner" and "water supply system" have the same meaning as in section 55 of the Act.

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: 2		  The following matters or substances are prescribed for the purposes of section 59 (1) (f) [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into well] of the Act:

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: (a) paint and paint products;

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: (b) liquid fuels;

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: (c) fuel additives;

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: (d) lubricants, other than water;

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: (e) solvents, other than water;

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: (f) herbicides and fungicides;

heading: Prescribed matters or substances
paragraph: (g) flood waters and flood debris.

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph:
3
		  The following artificial openings in the ground are excluded from the definition of "well" in section 1 [definitions] of the Act:

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph: (a) the following artificial openings made for the purpose of drainage:

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph: (i)  drains, including building perimeter drains, curtain drains, French drains and backfilled soakaway pits;

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph: (ii)  sumps in buildings that are part of the drainage systems of the buildings;

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph: (iii)  ditches or infiltration trenches of a shallow and linear nature;

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph: (b) prefabricated vertical drains, vertical strip drains, wick drains and sand drains made for the purpose of facilitating soil consolidation prior to building construction;

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph: (c) seismic relief holes, including stone columns and stone densification points, made for the purpose of dissipating excess water pressure caused by seismic activity;

heading: Exclusions from definition of "well"
paragraph: (d) drill holes made for the purpose of mineral exploration.

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph:
4
		  (1) The following are exempt from the requirements of this regulation and of Division 3 [Wells and Groundwater Protection] of Part 3 of the Act:

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (a) water source wells that are used to divert deep groundwater in the subject area, as "deep groundwater" and "subject area" are defined in section 51 of the Water Sustainability Regulation, and from which wells deep groundwater is used for an oil and gas purpose in the subject area;

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (b) drainage wells;

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (c) horizontal closed-loop geoexchange wells that are less than 5 m deep;

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (d) test pits.

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the following provisions apply in relation to the wells referred to in that subsection:

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (a) Part 8 [Artesian Flow];

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (b) sections 74 (2) [decommissioning boreholes and test pits] and 80 [well decommission reports for flowing artesian wells];

heading: Exemptions for certain wells
paragraph: (c) sections 52 [controlling artesian flow during construction], 53 [controlling flowing artesian well], 57 (3) (b) [well reports in prescribed circumstances], 59 [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into well], 60 [remediation orders in relation to foreign matter in well] and 61 [wells on Crown land] of the Act.

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph:
5
		  (1) For the purposes of this regulation, each of the following is a class of well:

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (a) water supply wells;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (b) monitoring wells;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (c) recharge wells;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (d) injection wells;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (e) dewatering wells;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (f) remediation wells;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (g) geotechnical wells;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (h) closed-loop geoexchange wells.

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this regulation, each of the following is a subclass of the geotechnical well class:

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (a) boreholes;

heading: Well classes and subclasses
paragraph: (b) test pits.

heading: Application of standards to well classes
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The owner of a well that is being changed to a different class, or the person responsible for changing the class of a well, as applicable, must ensure that the well meets the standards and requirements of the Act and this regulation that apply to the new class of well.

heading: Application of standards to well classes
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for drilling or altering either of the following wells must ensure that the well meets the highest standards and requirements of the Act and this regulation for any class or subclass that apply in respect of either of the following wells:

heading: Application of standards to well classes
paragraph: (a) a well that is drilled or altered so that the well is in more than one class or subclass of well;

heading: Application of standards to well classes
paragraph: (b) a well the use or purpose of which is changed so that the well is in more than one class or subclass of well.

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph:
7
		  The comptroller must

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (a) establish and maintain

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (i)  a register of well drillers who are authorized to operate in British Columbia, and

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (ii)  a register of well pump installers who are authorized to operate in British Columbia,

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (b) include in the registers the following information in respect of each well driller and well pump installer:

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (i)  full name;

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (ii)  business contact information, including business name, if any, address, telephone number and, if available, email address and fax number;

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (iii)  the registration number issued by the comptroller and the date of registration;

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (iv)  a reference to any certificates of qualification held by the well driller or qualified well pump installer;

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (v)  in the case of a well driller, the class of well driller assigned by the comptroller in accordance with section 9 [registration and classification of well driller],

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (c) make available to the public during normal business hours, or by posting on a publicly available website, a list of well drillers and well pump installers, which list may include any of the information set out in paragraph (b), and

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (d) remove from the register any person who

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
