paragraph: (i)  fails to meet a requirement for registration,

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (ii)  fails to maintain a requirement for registration, including any requirement for maintaining a certificate issued by another province or territory of Canada, or

heading: Registers of well drillers and well pump installers
paragraph: (iii)  is no longer actively working in Canada as a well driller or well pump installer.

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A person may apply to the comptroller for registration as a well driller by completing and submitting an application in the form and with the content specified by the comptroller.

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (2) A prospective registrant described in subsection (1) must provide with an application proof satisfactory to the comptroller that the prospective registrant

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (a) is an individual who is at least 19 years of age, and

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (b) holds, for the purposes of the definition of "well driller" in section 48 (1) [definitions] of the Act, one of the following prescribed qualifications:

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (i)  a certificate of qualification as a Water Well Driller issued by SkilledTradesBC under the Skilled Trades BC Act;

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (ii)  a certificate of qualification as a Geoexchange Driller issued by SkilledTradesBC under the Skilled Trades BC Act;

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (iii)  a certificate of qualification as a Geotechnical/Environmental Driller issued by SkilledTradesBC under the Skilled Trades BC Act;

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (iv)  a certificate issued by another province or territory of Canada that is equivalent to a certificate referred to in subparagraph (i), (ii) or (iii);

heading: Application for registration as well driller
paragraph: (v)  a certificate as a Ground Water Drilling Technician issued by the Canadian Ground Water Association before April 26, 2013.

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: 9		  (1) If the comptroller approves a person's application under section 8 (1) to be registered as a well driller, the comptroller must

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (a) classify the person as being in one or more of the following classes, based on the comptroller's assessment of the person's qualifications:

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (i)  a water well driller, if the person has a qualification described in section 8 (2) (b) (i), (iv) or (v);

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (ii)  a geoexchange driller, if the person has a qualification described in section 8 (2) (b) (ii) or (iv);

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (iii)  a geotechnical / environmental driller, if the person has a qualification described in section 8 (2) (b) (iii) or (iv),

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (b) add the person to the register of well drillers, and

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (c) issue an identification card to the person that includes reference to the classification of that person under paragraph (a) as one or more of the following:

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (i)  a water well driller;

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (ii)  a geoexchange driller;

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (iii)  a geotechnical / environmental driller.

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (2) Promptly after this regulation comes into force, the comptroller must

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (a) classify every person who was registered in the register of qualified well drillers under the former regulation immediately before the date this regulation comes into force as all of the following:

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (i)  a water well driller;

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (ii)  a geoexchange driller;

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (iii)  a geotechnical / environmental driller,

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (b) ensure that every person classified as a well driller under paragraph (a) is added to the register of well drillers, and

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (c) issue an identification card to every person classified as a well driller under paragraph (a) that includes reference to the classification of that person as all of the following:

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (i)  a water well driller;

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (ii)  a geoexchange driller;

heading: Registration and classification of well driller
paragraph: (iii)  a geotechnical / environmental driller.

heading: Application for registration as well pump installer
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A person may apply to the comptroller for registration as a well pump installer by completing and submitting an application in the form and with the content specified by the comptroller.

heading: Application for registration as well pump installer
paragraph: (2) A prospective registrant described in subsection (1) must provide with an application proof satisfactory to the comptroller that the prospective registrant

heading: Application for registration as well pump installer
paragraph: (a) is an individual who is at least 19 years of age, and

heading: Application for registration as well pump installer
paragraph: (b) holds, for the purposes of the definition of "well pump installer" in section 48 (1) [definitions] of the Act, one of the following prescribed qualifications:

heading: Application for registration as well pump installer
paragraph: (i)  a certificate of qualification as a Well Pump Installer issued by SkilledTradesBC under the Skilled Trades BC Act;

heading: Application for registration as well pump installer
paragraph: (ii)  a certificate issued by another province or territory of Canada that is equivalent to a certificate referred to in subparagraph (i);

heading: Application for registration as well pump installer
paragraph: (iii)  a certificate as a Ground Water Pump Technician issued by the Canadian Ground Water Association before April 26, 2013.

heading: Registration of well pump installer
paragraph: 11		  (1) If the comptroller approves a person's application under section 10 (1) to be registered as a well pump installer, the comptroller must

heading: Registration of well pump installer
paragraph: (a) add the person to the register of well pump installers, and

heading: Registration of well pump installer
paragraph: (b) issue an identification card to the person that identifies that person as a well pump installer.

heading: Registration of well pump installer
paragraph: (2) Promptly after this regulation comes into force, the comptroller must

heading: Registration of well pump installer
paragraph: (a) ensure that every person is added to the register of well pump installers who, immediately before the date this regulation comes into force, was registered in the register of qualified well pump installers under the former regulation, and

heading: Registration of well pump installer
paragraph: (b) issue an identification card to every person added to the register of well pump installers under paragraph (a) that identifies that person as a well pump installer.

heading: Notice to comptroller
paragraph:
12
		  (1) A registered well driller or registered well pump installer must advise the comptroller in writing within 60 days after

heading: Notice to comptroller
paragraph: (a) any changes to the information included in the register in relation to the well driller or well pump installer, as the case may be, or

heading: Notice to comptroller
paragraph: (b) the person ceasing to work in Canada as a well driller or well pump installer, as the case may be.

heading: Notice to comptroller
paragraph: (2) The comptroller is not required to issue an identification card under section 9 or 11, as applicable, to a registered well driller or registered well pump installer if the registered well driller or registered well pump installer has not complied with subsection (1).

heading: Proof of qualifications - identification card
paragraph:
13
		  For the purposes of section 51 (3) [proof of qualifications and insurance] of the Act, the proof of qualifications that must be provided by a well driller or well pump installer is the identification card issued to the well driller or well pump installer by the comptroller under section 9 [registration and classification of well driller] or 11 [registration of well pump installer] of this regulation.

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph:
14
		  (1) For the purposes of sections 48 (1) [definitions] and 49 (2) (b) (i) [restrictions on constructing or decommissioning wells and related activities] of the Act,

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (a) a registered well driller who is classified as a water well driller under section 9 (1) (a) (i) or (2) (a) [registration and classification of well driller] of this regulation is qualified in respect of constructing any class of well other than closed-loop geoexchange wells,

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (b) a registered well driller who is classified as a geoexchange driller under section 9 (1) (a) (ii) or (2) (a) of this regulation is qualified in respect of constructing closed-loop geoexchange wells,

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (c) a registered well driller who is classified as a geotechnical / environmental driller under section 9 (1) (a) (iii) or (2) (a) of this regulation is qualified in respect of constructing the following classes of well:

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (i)  monitoring wells;

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (ii)  geotechnical wells;

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (iii)  remediation wells, and

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (d) subject to section 15 of this regulation, a registered well driller is qualified in respect of decommissioning or deactivating any class of well.

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well drillers
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 50 [restrictions respecting well pumps and flow tests] of the Act, registered well drillers referred to in subsection (1) (a) are qualified to carry out the activities under section 50 (1) (a) to (c) of the Act in respect of water supply wells, dewatering wells, injection wells and remediation wells.

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to artesian flow - well drillers
paragraph:
15
		  (1) For the purposes of sections 52 (3) and (5) [controlling artesian flow during construction] and 53 (1) [controlling flowing artesian well] of the Act, a registered well driller is qualified to stop or control artesian flow in relation to a well if the well driller has competency in stopping or controlling artesian flow as a result of the well driller's training, experience, knowledge or skills.

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to artesian flow - well drillers
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a registered well driller who is not qualified to stop or control artesian flow in relation to a well may undertake that activity if the well driller is supervised by another registered well driller, or a professional, who has competency in stopping or controlling artesian flow as a result of the training, experience, knowledge or skills of the other well driller or the professional, as the case may be.

heading: Qualifications for activities in relation to wells - well pump installers
paragraph:
16
		  For the purposes of sections 48 (1) [definitions] and 49 (3) (e) [restrictions on constructing or decommissioning wells and related activities] of the Act, a well pump installer is qualified in respect of decommissioning or deactivating a well, other than a flowing artesian well.

heading: No restriction on who may decommission certain wells
paragraph:
17
		  For the purposes of section 49 (3) [restrictions on constructing or decommissioning wells and related activities] of the Act, any person may decommission the following wells, other than a flowing artesian well:

heading: No restriction on who may decommission certain wells
paragraph: (a) a well that has a depth of not more than 5 m;

heading: No restriction on who may decommission certain wells
paragraph: (b) an excavated well that has a depth of not more than 15 m.

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph:
18
		  (1) The person responsible for drilling a proposed water supply well or a proposed permanent dewatering well must site the proposed well so that the horizontal setback distance is not less than 15 m from any part of the proposed well to an existing water supply well, unless

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (a) the existing water supply well is not in use and is not intended to be in use, or

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (b) the owner of the proposed well also owns the existing water supply well and only one well is proposed to be drilled.

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for drilling a proposed water supply well or proposed permanent dewatering well referred to in subsection (1) may, if the person responsible determines that it is not practicable to site the well as described in that subsection, site the proposed well with a horizontal setback distance from any part of the proposed well to an existing water supply well that is less than 15 m in accordance with alternative specifications that meet the requirements of subsection (3).

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (3) A proposed well under subsection (2) may be sited in accordance with alternative specifications for the siting of the proposed well if

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (a) a professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology prepares the alternative specifications for the siting of the proposed well so that the existing uses of the existing water supply well will not be adversely affected,

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (b) the person responsible for drilling the well submits the alternative specifications to an engineer for acceptance by the engineer before the proposed well is drilled,

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (c) the engineer accepts the alternative specifications, with any terms and conditions the engineer may specify, and

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (d) the person responsible drills the water supply well, or permanent dewatering well, in accordance with

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (i)  the alternative specifications accepted by the engineer under paragraph (c), and

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (ii)  the terms and conditions, if any, specified by the engineer under that paragraph.

heading: Siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells
paragraph: (4) If a water supply well or permanent dewatering well is drilled in accordance with alternative specifications under subsection (3), the person responsible for drilling the well must include the accepted alternative specifications, including the terms and conditions specified by the engineer, if any, with the well construction report required under section 76 [well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner].

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Before a recharge well or injection well is constructed for the purpose of conveying urban runoff into the ground,

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (a) the owner of the proposed recharge well or injection well must retain a professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology or geotechnical engineering to design the proposed well, and

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (b) the professional must

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (i)  design the proposed well so that the proposed well does not cause a significant adverse impact on the quality of water in an aquifer or in another well that diverts water from the aquifer, and

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (ii)  specify the following distances in the design:

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (A) a minimum horizontal distance between the proposed well and an existing water supply well;

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (B) a minimum vertical distance between the point of infiltration of the proposed well and the water table below to ensure that the point of infiltration of the proposed well is and will remain above the water table at all times.

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (2) If the point of infiltration of treated water for a proposed recharge well or injection well is below the seasonal high water table, the professional, or the owner of the proposed recharge well or injection well, must submit the design described in subsection (1) to an engineer, who may

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (a) accept the design, and may specify terms and conditions on the acceptance, and

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (b) determine whether the recharge well or injection well may be exempted from the minimum vertical distance specification described in subsection (1) (b) (ii) (B).

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (3) The person responsible for drilling a proposed recharge well or injection well must include the accepted design referred to in subsection (2), including the terms and conditions, if any, specified by the engineer with the well construction report if that report is required under section 76 [well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner].

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (4) The owner of a proposed recharge well or injection well must ensure that the person responsible constructs the well in accordance with

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (a) the design of the proposed recharge well or injection well made by the professional under subsection (1) (b), and

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (b) in the case of a proposed recharge well or injection well to which subsection (2) applies, the accepted design and the terms and conditions, if any, specified by the engineer under that subsection.

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (5) The owner of a recharge well or injection well must

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (a) ensure that the professional prepares as-built drawings of the well, and

heading: Siting of recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (b) retain the design and any as-built drawings prepared by the professional until the well is decommissioned.

heading: Casings and liners - general requirements
paragraph:
20
		  If a casing or liner is to be installed in a well in the course of drilling or altering the well, the person responsible for drilling or altering the well must install a casing or liner that is

heading: Casings and liners - general requirements
paragraph: (a) composed of new material or used material in like-new condition, and

heading: Casings and liners - general requirements
paragraph: (b) strong enough to withstand the pressure or force exerted on the casing or liner during the installation of the casing or liner and the operation of the well.

heading: Thermoplastic casings and liners for water supply wells
paragraph:
21
		  If a thermoplastic casing or thermoplastic liner is to be installed in a water supply well in the course of drilling or altering the well, the person responsible for drilling or altering the well must install a thermoplastic casing or thermoplastic liner that is approved or certified by one of the following for use for drinking water:

heading: Thermoplastic casings and liners for water supply wells
paragraph: (a) Canadian Standards Association;

heading: Thermoplastic casings and liners for water supply wells
paragraph: (b) Underwriters' Laboratories of Canada;

heading: Thermoplastic casings and liners for water supply wells
paragraph: (c) ASTM International;

heading: Thermoplastic casings and liners for water supply wells
paragraph: (d) NSF International.

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph:
22
		  (1) The person responsible for drilling a well that has one or more casings must complete the well with an effective, permanent and continuous surface seal, as shown in Figures 1 and 2 of Schedule 5.

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (2) A surface seal required under subsection (1) must be installed in accordance with the applicable requirements of this Part to prevent the entry of any foreign matter from the surface of the ground into the well or the aquifer, if any, penetrated by the well.

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (3) A surface seal required under subsection (1) must be

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (a) installed in all annular spaces of the well,

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (b) not less than 2.54 cm thick, including the wall thickness of any surface casing left permanently in place, and

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (c) not less than

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (i)  1 m in length,

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a water supply well, the length determined in accordance with section 23, or

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (iii)  in the case of a closed-loop geoexchange well, the entire length of the ground loop, in accordance with section 25 [sealing closed-loop geoexchange wells].

heading: Surface seal - general requirements
paragraph: (4) All openings in the production casing of a well, including, without limitation, joints, lifting holes, perforations and pitless adapter holes, that are within the length of the surface seal must be made watertight with non-toxic materials.

heading: Surface seal - water supply wells
paragraph:
23
		  (1) The person responsible for drilling a water supply well that has one or more casings must, in addition to meeting the requirements under section 22, complete the water supply well with a surface seal that is not less than 5 m in length, unless

heading: Surface seal - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) the depth of the water supply well is insufficient to have a surface seal length of 5 m, in which case the surface seal must be the greatest possible length up to 5 m, or

heading: Surface seal - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) the method of drilling the water supply well is by driving, in which case the surface seal must be not less than 1 m in length.

heading: Surface seal - water supply wells
paragraph: (2) In addition to the requirements set out in subsection (1), if bedrock is encountered at or within 5 m of the surface of the ground in the circumstances described in subsection (1), other than those circumstances described in paragraph (b) of that subsection, the surface seal must extend to a minimum depth of 1 m into competent bedrock, as shown in Figure 3 of Schedule 5.

heading: Multiple annular spaces
paragraph:
24
		  (1) If an annular space is created during the installation of a surface casing, the person responsible for drilling the well must

heading: Multiple annular spaces
paragraph: (a) subject to paragraph (b), remove the surface casing and install the surface seal between the next outermost casing and the geological formation, or

heading: Multiple annular spaces
paragraph: (b) if the surface casing cannot be removed,

heading: Multiple annular spaces
paragraph: (i)  excavate the immediate area around the surface casing,

heading: Multiple annular spaces
paragraph: (ii)  install sealant in the immediate area around the surface casing, as shown in Figure 2 of Schedule 5, to a length that is not less than 1 m and extends laterally from the surface casing to completely fill the excavated area, and

heading: Multiple annular spaces
paragraph: (iii)  install sealant in the next outermost annular space, as shown in Figure 2 of Schedule 5, to a length that is not less than the minimum length required under section 22 (3) (c) [surface seal - general requirements].

heading: Multiple annular spaces
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (1) (b), the open annular space, if any, between multiple casings must be effectively capped with a well cap or sealed with a surface seal.

heading: Sealing closed-loop geoexchange wells
paragraph:
25
		  (1) The person responsible for constructing a closed-loop geoexchange well must seal the closed-loop geoexchange well along the entire length of the ground loop, from the bottom upward, promptly after installing the ground loop.

heading: Sealing closed-loop geoexchange wells
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for converting an existing well into a closed-loop geoexchange well must seal the closed-loop geoexchange well the ground loop is in along the entire length of the ground loop, from the bottom upward, promptly after installing the ground loop.

heading: Backfill materials above surface seal
paragraph:
26
		  A surface seal may extend to within 0.3 m of the surface of the ground to allow for up to 0.3 m of backfill materials above the surface seal, but the total length of the surface seal must not be less than the length required under section 22 (3) (c) [surface seal - general requirements].

heading: Surface sealing for alterations
paragraph:
27
		  (1) If an alteration to a well impairs the integrity of the existing surface seal, the person responsible for altering the well must ensure that the integrity of the surface seal is restored as soon as practicable.

heading: Surface sealing for alterations
paragraph: (2) If a structural change is made to the depth, diameter or screen assembly of a well that has a casing installed and that does not have a surface seal, the person responsible for making the structural change must install a surface seal that

heading: Surface sealing for alterations
paragraph: (a) is not less than 1 m in length or extends to bedrock, whichever is shorter, and

heading: Surface sealing for alterations
paragraph: (b) is not less than 2.54 cm thick.

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph:
28
		  (1) In this Division, "alter" does not include the installation of a surface seal.

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for drilling, altering or rehabilitating a water supply well must develop the water supply well in a manner that prevents the following during the development or operation of the water supply well:

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) significant collapse of the surface of the ground around the water supply well;

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) damage to the surface seal of the water supply well.

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (3) The person responsible for drilling a water supply well into an unconsolidated aquifer, or altering a water supply well so that the well penetrates an unconsolidated aquifer, must equip the well with a screen assembly

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) that is securely attached to the production casing, and

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) the screen component of which

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (i)  is composed of durable material having strength suited to the particular soil and water conditions encountered during drilling or alteration, and

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (ii)  has slot openings that are appropriately sized so that the depth of the well does not change as a result of sand or other unconsolidated material being drawn in during operation of the well or building up in the well.

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (4) A screen assembly is not required under subsection (3) if

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) the water supply well is an excavated well, or

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) the gravel or other unconsolidated material naturally exposed at the bottom of the production casing is coarse enough to allow the water supply well to be developed so that

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (i)  the bottom of the production casing is stable, and

heading: Development and screens - water supply wells
paragraph: (ii)  the depth of the well does not change as a result of sand or other unconsolidated material being drawn in during operation of the well or building up in the production casing.

heading: Use of certain substances - water supply wells
paragraph:
29
		  (1) For the purposes of section 59 (2) (d) [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into well] of the Act, drilling, altering, developing and rehabilitating are prescribed activities.

heading: Use of certain substances - water supply wells
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for performing an activity referred to in subsection (1) may introduce acids, lubricants, bactericides or other similar substances into a water supply well in order to perform the activity in accordance with subsection (3).

heading: Use of certain substances - water supply wells
paragraph: (3) If acids, lubricants, bactericides or other similar substances are used in connection with an activity under subsection (2), the person responsible for performing the activity must

heading: Use of certain substances - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) promptly after using the acids, lubricants, bactericides or other similar substances, remove groundwater from the water supply well until the remaining concentrations of acids, lubricants, bactericides and other similar substances in the remaining groundwater in the well would not prevent the use of the water supply well for its intended purpose, and

heading: Use of certain substances - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) dispose of the groundwater removed from the water supply well in a manner that does not pose a threat to the aquatic ecosystem of a stream or an aquifer or to property, public safety or the environment.

heading: Disinfection of water supply wells
paragraph:
30
		  The person responsible for drilling, altering, developing or rehabilitating a water supply well must, promptly after performing the activity, disinfect the groundwater in the well to destroy micro-organisms introduced by the activity.

heading: Well yield tests and reports
paragraph:
31
		  (1) The person responsible for drilling or altering a water supply well or a permanent dewatering well must

heading: Well yield tests and reports
paragraph: (a) conduct a well yield test, and

heading: Well yield tests and reports
paragraph: (b) include the details of the well yield test in the well construction report required under section 76 [well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner].

heading: Well yield tests and reports
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a well yield test is not required if there is insufficient water in the well to conduct the test.

heading: Pumping tests
paragraph:
32
		  (1) A well owner who is required to carry out a pumping test as part of an application for an authorization or by order of the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer must ensure that a professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology

heading: Pumping tests
paragraph: (a) designs the test,

heading: Pumping tests
paragraph: (b) performs or directly supervises the test, and

heading: Pumping tests
paragraph: (c) interprets the results of the test.

heading: Pumping tests
paragraph: (2) A professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology may install a temporary well pump to carry out a pumping test.

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph:
33
		  (1) The person responsible for drilling or altering a well must ensure that the casing stick-up is continuous and extends a minimum of 0.3 m above

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph: (a) the surface of the ground adjacent to the well, or

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph: (b) if applicable, the floor of the well sump, pump house or well pit.

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph: (a) a geotechnical well,

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph: (b) a closed-loop geoexchange well,

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph: (c) a temporary dewatering well, or

heading: Casing stick-up
paragraph: (d) a monitoring well drilled under the supervision of a professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology or geotechnical engineering.

heading: Protection of thermoplastic casings
paragraph:
34
		  The person responsible for drilling or altering a well must ensure that thermoplastic casing at or above the surface of the ground is completely protected from damage and material breakdown.

heading: Slope of surface of ground around wellhead
paragraph:
35
		  The person responsible for drilling or altering a well must slope the surface of the ground immediately around the wellhead to ensure that water does not pond around the wellhead or in the area disturbed during drilling.

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph:
36
		  (1) Except as provided in this section, a person must not construct a well pit for the following activities:

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) constructing a new water supply well;

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) adding a well pit to an existing water supply well that does not have an existing well pit.

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (2) If a water supply well that has an existing well pit is being altered, a person must either

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) remove the well pit, or

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) comply with subsections (3), (4), (5) and (6).

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (3) A person may construct a well pit for a water supply well if the well pit is designed by a professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology or geotechnical engineering to ensure that

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (a) water does not pond in the well pit, and

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (b) any water that enters the well pit is conveyed away in a manner that is not likely to cause an adverse impact on the quality of water in an aquifer.

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (4) The construction of a well pit must be supervised by the professional who designs the well pit under subsection (3).

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (5) The owner of a water supply well with a well pit must ensure that the professional who designs the well pit under subsection (3) prepares as-built drawings of the well pit.

heading: Well pit restrictions - water supply wells
paragraph: (6) The professional who designs the well pit under subsection (3) must submit the design and as-built drawings to the owner and the comptroller within 90 days after the construction of the well pit.

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph:
37
		  (1) The person responsible for constructing

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph: (a) a well sump,

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph: (b) a pump house for a well, or

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph: (c) a well pit for a well

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph: must ensure that the well sump, pump house or well pit is designed and constructed so that water entering the well sump, pump house or well pit is conveyed away from the wellhead.

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to a well sump, pump house or well pit for a monitoring well if the well and the well sump, pump house or well pit are

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph: (a) designed by a professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology or geotechnical engineering to prevent adverse impacts on the quality of water in an aquifer, and

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - construction of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph: (b) constructed in accordance with that design.

heading: Well caps
paragraph:
38
		  (1) Subject to subsections (3) to (5), the person responsible for drilling or altering a well must, promptly on completing the drilling or alteration, securely attach to the top of the production casing a well cap that does all of the following:

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (a) prevents direct and unintended entry into the well of

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (i)  any water at the surface of the ground, including floodwater and ponded water, and

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (ii)  any foreign matter;

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (b) prevents persons or animals from entering the well;

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (c) prevents or minimizes the flow of water from a flowing artesian well.

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (2) A well cap required under subsection (1) must be

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (a) commercially manufactured, or

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (b) fabricated from durable material having strength suited to the location of the well cap and the local environmental conditions.

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (3) A steel plate welded to the top of the production casing may be used instead of a well cap on a well that is not yet in service.

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (4) The person responsible for drilling or altering a well that has an annular space between multiple casings must securely attach to the casings at the top of the annular space a permanent and watertight well cap that complies with subsection (2).

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (5) Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (a) a geotechnical well,

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (b) a closed-loop geoexchange well, or

heading: Well caps
paragraph: (c) a water supply well equipped with a hand pump that meets the requirements of subsection (1) for a well cap.

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph:
39
		  (1) A well owner must ensure that

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (a) a well cap that meets the applicable requirements of this Part remains securely attached to the top of the production casing or, if the well is not yet in service, a steel plate remains welded to the top of the production casing, and

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (b) the well cap or steel plate is maintained in good operating condition.

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 42 [custom-designed well caps and well covers], if a well does not already have a well cap securely attached to the top of the production casing, the well owner must promptly and securely attach to the top of the production casing a well cap that meets the requirements of this Part.

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (3) A steel plate welded to the production casing may be used instead of a well cap on a well referred to in subsection (2) that is not yet in service.

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (4) Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply in relation to

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (a) a geotechnical well,

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (b) a closed-loop geoexchange well, or

heading: Maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates
paragraph: (c) a water supply well equipped with a hand pump that meets the requirements of section 38 (1) for a well cap.

heading: Well covers
paragraph:
40
		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), the person responsible for drilling or altering a well in which the top of the casing is below the surface of the ground must, in addition to complying with section 38 [well caps], promptly and securely install at or above the surface of the ground a well cover that does both of the following:

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (a) prevents direct and unintended entry into the well of

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (i)  any water at the surface of the ground, including floodwater and ponded water, and

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (ii)  any foreign matter;

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (b) prevents persons or animals from entering the well.

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (2) A well cover required under subsection (1) must be

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (a) commercially manufactured, or

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (b) fabricated from durable material having strength suited to the location of the well cover and the local environmental conditions.

heading: Well covers
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to a geotechnical well or a closed-loop geoexchange well.

heading: Maintenance and installation of well covers
paragraph:
41
		  (1) The owner of a well that is completed below the surface of the ground, or in which the casing does not extend above the surface of the ground, must ensure that

heading: Maintenance and installation of well covers
paragraph: (a) a well cover that meets the applicable requirements of this Part remains securely installed, and

heading: Maintenance and installation of well covers
paragraph: (b) the well cover is maintained in good operating condition.

heading: Maintenance and installation of well covers
paragraph: (2) If a well completed below the surface of the ground, or in which the casing does not extend above the surface of the ground, does not already have a well cover, the well owner must promptly and securely install at or above the surface of the ground a well cover that meets the applicable requirements of this Part.

heading: Maintenance and installation of well covers
paragraph: (3) Without limiting section 36 [well pit restrictions - water supply wells], this section does not apply in relation to a geotechnical well or a closed-loop geoexchange well.

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph:
42
		  (1) If it is not practicable for the owner of a well referred to in section 39 (2) [maintenance and attachment of well caps or steel plates] or 41 (2) to attach a well cap or install a well cover that meets the requirements of this Part, the well owner must engage a qualified well driller, qualified well pump installer or professional to design and attach an effective well cap or design and install an effective well cover.

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), a well cap is effective if it does all of the following:

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (a) prevents direct and unintended entry into the well of

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (i)  any water at the surface of the ground, including floodwater and ponded water, and

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (ii)  any foreign matter;

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (b) prevents persons or animals from entering the well;

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (c) stops or brings under control the flow of water from a flowing artesian well.

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), a well cover is effective if the requirements of subsection (2) (a) and (b) are met.

heading: Custom-designed well caps and well covers
paragraph: (4) The owner of a well must ensure that a well cap attached or well cover installed under this section is maintained in good operating condition.

heading: Definition of "related works"
paragraph:
43
		  In this Part, "related works", in relation to a well pump, includes, without limitation, the pump motor, pump column, pitless adapter and sounding tube.

heading: Pump installation - general requirements
paragraph:
44
		  The person responsible for installing a well pump must

heading: Pump installation - general requirements
paragraph: (a) install the well pump and related works so that there is no damage to or movement of the casing during the installation or operation of the well pump,

heading: Pump installation - general requirements
paragraph: (b) ensure that the well pump is protected by a liner if the well is unstable, and

heading: Pump installation - general requirements
paragraph: (c) install the well pump and related works in a manner that

heading: Pump installation - general requirements
paragraph: (i)  prevents the entry into the well of any foreign matter, and

heading: Pump installation - general requirements
paragraph: (ii)  allows the well, well pump and related works to be properly disinfected.

heading: Pitless adapter installation, replacement or repair
paragraph:
45
		  The person responsible for installing, replacing or repairing a pitless adapter must ensure that

heading: Pitless adapter installation, replacement or repair
paragraph: (a) the pitless adapter is constructed with materials that will likely not have a significant adverse impact on water quality,

heading: Pitless adapter installation, replacement or repair
paragraph: (b) the pitless adapter is installed in a manner that will prevent corrosion of metal, and

heading: Pitless adapter installation, replacement or repair
paragraph: (c) the connection or seal between the pitless adapter and the production casing is watertight.

heading: Thermoplastic liner, drop pipes and sounding tubes for water supply wells
paragraph:
46
		  If a thermoplastic liner, drop pipe or sounding tube is to be installed in a water supply well, the person responsible must ensure the thermoplastic liner, drop pipe or sounding tube is approved or certified by one of the following for use for drinking water:

heading: Thermoplastic liner, drop pipes and sounding tubes for water supply wells
paragraph: (a) Canadian Standards Association;

heading: Thermoplastic liner, drop pipes and sounding tubes for water supply wells
paragraph: (b) Underwriters' Laboratories of Canada;

heading: Thermoplastic liner, drop pipes and sounding tubes for water supply wells
paragraph: (c) ASTM International;

heading: Thermoplastic liner, drop pipes and sounding tubes for water supply wells
paragraph: (d) NSF International.

heading: Devices to prevent flow of water back into well
paragraph:
47
		  The person responsible for installing a permanent well pump into a well must ensure that the well is equipped with a device that prevents the flow of water back into the well.

heading: Sealing after installation of well pump or related works
paragraph:
48
		  (1) If the installation of a well pump or related works in a well impairs the integrity of the existing surface seal, the person responsible for installing the well pump or related works must repair or replace the surface seal to meet the requirements of Division 3 [Surface Seals] of Part 3 [Well Construction].

heading: Sealing after installation of well pump or related works
paragraph: (2) If the installation of a well pump or related works in a well that does not have a surface seal creates a visible annular space between the outermost casing of the well and the surrounding geological formation, the person responsible for installing the well pump or related works must seal the annular space with sealant.

heading: Modification of wellhead
paragraph:
49
		  If the installation of a well pump or related works requires modification of the wellhead, the person responsible for the installation must ensure that, after the modification, the wellhead

heading: Modification of wellhead
paragraph: (a) meets, or continues to meet, the requirements of this regulation, and

heading: Modification of wellhead
paragraph: (b) remains compliant with the design of the professional referred to in section 36 (3) [well pit restrictions - water supply wells].

heading: Use of non-toxic lubricants and solvents
paragraph:
50
		  (1) For the purposes of section 59 (2) (d) [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into well] of the Act, the activity of installing, maintaining or repairing a well pump is a prescribed activity.

heading: Use of non-toxic lubricants and solvents
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for performing an activity referred to in subsection (1) may use a lubricant or solvent for the activity if the lubricant or solvent is non-toxic.

heading: Hand pumps in water supply wells
paragraph:
51
		  (1) The person responsible for installing a hand pump in a water supply well must ensure that the hand pump is installed so that it meets the requirements of section 38 (1) [well caps] that apply in respect of a well cap.

heading: Hand pumps in water supply wells
paragraph: (2) If a water supply well is equipped with a hand pump that is not installed as described in subsection (1), the owner of the water supply well must ensure that the hand pump is upgraded or replaced before March 1, 2018 so as to comply with that subsection.

heading: Disinfection of water supply wells after well pump activities
paragraph:
52
		  The person responsible, in respect of a water supply well, for installing a permanent well pump or removing a temporary well pump must disinfect the groundwater in the well to destroy any micro-organisms introduced by that activity.

heading: Attachment of well identification plates by person responsible for drilling or alteration
paragraph:
53
		  (1) If a well identification plate is required for a well under column 3 of the table in Schedule 6, the person responsible for drilling the well must, promptly on completing the drilling, securely attach to the well, in accordance with section 55 [well identification plate attachment], a well identification plate that has been obtained from the comptroller.

heading: Attachment of well identification plates by person responsible for drilling or alteration
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for altering a well that does not have a well identification plate as required under column 3 of the table in Schedule 6 must, promptly on completing the alteration, securely attach to the well, in accordance with section 55, a well identification plate that has been obtained from the comptroller.

heading: Attachment of well identification plates by person responsible for drilling or alteration
paragraph: (3) The person responsible referred to in subsection (1) or (2) must report the well identification in the well construction report made under section 76 [well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner].

heading: Attachment of well identification plates by owner of well supplying water supply system
paragraph:
54
		  (1) The owner of a well drilled for the purpose of supplying a water supply system must, if a well identification plate has not already been attached to the well, promptly and securely attach to the well, in accordance with section 55, a well identification plate that has been obtained from the comptroller.

heading: Attachment of well identification plates by owner of well supplying water supply system
paragraph: (2) As soon as practicable after attaching a well identification plate, the well identification must be reported in a well identification report in accordance with section 75 [well identification reports by owner of well supplying water supply system].

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A well identification plate required under this Part must be securely attached to the casing, well cap or well cover of the well so that the well identification number is plainly visible.

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph: (2) If it is not possible to securely attach the well identification plate to the casing, well cap or well cover, the well identification plate may be securely attached to any of the following so that the well identification number is plainly visible:

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph: (a) the discharge pipe;

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph: (b) the pump motor housing;

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph: (c) the stand at the top of the well;

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph: (d) the pump house;

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph: (e) a nearby post.

heading: Well identification plate attachment
paragraph: (3) If 2 or more wells are contained in a single protective casing, each of those wells must have a well identification plate.

heading: Protection and replacement of well identification plates
paragraph:
56
		  (1) The owner of a well that is required under section 53 [attachment of well identification plates by person responsible for drilling or alteration] or 54 [attachment of well identification plates by owner of well supplying water supply system] to have a well identification plate attached must

heading: Protection and replacement of well identification plates
paragraph: (a) protect the well identification plate from any physical damage,

heading: Protection and replacement of well identification plates
paragraph: (b) ensure that the well identification plate is promptly attached and remains securely attached in accordance with section 55 so that the well identification number remains plainly visible, and

heading: Protection and replacement of well identification plates
paragraph: (c) if the well identification plate is missing or damaged,

heading: Protection and replacement of well identification plates
paragraph: (i)  report the loss or damage to the comptroller within 30 days after discovering the loss or damage, and

heading: Protection and replacement of well identification plates
paragraph: (ii)  request the comptroller to supply a replacement well identification plate.

heading: Protection and replacement of well identification plates
paragraph: (2) If a replacement well identification plate is supplied by the comptroller, the well owner must ensure that the well identification plate is promptly attached and remains securely attached in accordance with section 55.

heading: Application of Part 7
paragraph:
57
		  This Part applies in relation to a well whether or not the well is in use, in service or deactivated, but does not apply in relation to a well that has been decommissioned in accordance with this regulation.

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph:
58
		  (1) The owner of a well must ensure the following in respect of the operation of a well and wellhead:

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (a) the surface of the ground immediately around the wellhead remains sloped so that water does not pond around the wellhead;

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (b) the well and the area immediately around the wellhead are maintained in a manner that prevents the entry into the well of any foreign matter;

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (c) any repairs to the well or wellhead are promptly undertaken when required to ensure that the well and wellhead are maintained in good operating condition.

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (2) The owner of a well must ensure the following in respect of a well and wellhead:

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (a) access to the well and wellhead is maintained for inspections undertaken in accordance with section 89 [right of access to land and premises by authorized persons] of the Act;

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (b) the area immediately around the wellhead is kept clear of all obstructions, including vegetation, that might interfere with

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (i)  the alteration, repair, maintenance or inspection of the well, or

heading: General operating requirements for well and area around wellhead
paragraph: (ii)  the alteration, repair, maintenance, replacement, removal or inspection of works.

heading: Drainage away from wellhead - maintenance of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits
paragraph:
59
		  The owner of a well that is in a well sump, pump house or well pit must ensure that the well sump, pump house or well pit is maintained in a manner so that any water entering the well sump, pump house or well pit is conveyed away from the wellhead.

heading: Operation of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells with alternative specifications
paragraph:
60
		  The owner of a water supply well or permanent dewatering well that is drilled in accordance with alternative specifications under section 18 (3) [siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells] must ensure that the well is completed, equipped, operated and maintained in accordance with the accepted alternative specifications, including any terms and conditions specified by the engineer.

heading: Conveyance of urban runoff - recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph:
61
		  The owner of a recharge well or injection well constructed for the purpose of conveying urban runoff into the ground must ensure that the recharge well or injection well is completed, equipped, operated and maintained

heading: Conveyance of urban runoff - recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (a) in accordance with the design referred to in section 19 (1) [siting of recharge wells and injection wells] and the applicable terms and conditions, if any, and

heading: Conveyance of urban runoff - recharge wells and injection wells
paragraph: (b) so that the recharge well or injection well does not cause a significant adverse impact on the quality of water in an aquifer or in another well that diverts water from the aquifer.

heading: Storage near water supply wells
paragraph:
62
		  (1) A person must not leave any foreign matter, store any foreign matter or allow any foreign matter to accumulate within 3 m of the wellhead of a water supply well.

heading: Storage near water supply wells
paragraph: (2) A person must ensure that any foreign matter that the person leaves, stores or allows to accumulate beyond the 3 m referred to in subsection (1) does not travel to within that 3 m.

heading: Protection of water supply system wells from entry of foreign matter and physical damage
paragraph:
63
		  The owner of a well constructed or altered for the purpose of supplying a water supply system must ensure that the well is completed, equipped and maintained in a manner that

heading: Protection of water supply system wells from entry of foreign matter and physical damage
paragraph: (a) prevents any foreign matter from entering from the surface of the ground into the well, either directly into the top of the well or through an annular space, and

heading: Protection of water supply system wells from entry of foreign matter and physical damage
paragraph: (b) protects the well and wellhead from physical damage due to flood debris, ice or erosion.

heading: Maintenance of surface seal
paragraph:
64
		  (1) The owner of a well that has a surface seal must ensure that

heading: Maintenance of surface seal
paragraph: (a) the integrity of the surface seal is maintained, and

heading: Maintenance of surface seal
paragraph: (b) in the case of a closed-loop geoexchange well, any visible openings in the well are sealed with sealant.

heading: Maintenance of surface seal
paragraph: (2) If a visible annular space appears around the outermost casing of a well, the owner of the well must ensure that the visible annular space is sealed with sealant.

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph:
65
		  (1) The owner of a well to which section 33 [casing stick-up] applies must ensure that the production casing

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (a) is maintained in a manner that ensures that the production casing remains continuous and the casing stick-up extends a minimum of 0.3 m above

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (i)  the surface of the ground adjacent to the well, or

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (ii)  the floor of the well sump, pump house or well pit, and

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (b) if damaged, is repaired or replaced with production casing that meets the requirements of

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (i)  section 20 [casings and liners - general requirements],

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (ii)  section 21 [thermoplastic casings and liners for water supply wells], if applicable, and

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (iii)  section 34 [protection of thermoplastic casings], if applicable.

heading: Maintenance of casing and stick-up
paragraph: (2) The owner of a well must ensure that thermoplastic casing used in the well remains protected from damage and material breakdown.

heading: Additional requirements - stopping or controlling artesian flow
paragraph:
66
		  The person responsible for stopping or controlling artesian flow of a well under section 52 (7) [controlling artesian flow during construction] of the Act must, in addition to the requirements of the Act,

heading: Additional requirements - stopping or controlling artesian flow
paragraph: (a) configure the wellhead or equip the well with a device that prevents the flow of water back into the well, and

heading: Additional requirements - stopping or controlling artesian flow
paragraph: (b) measure the shut-in pressure or static water level and record that measurement on the well construction report required under section 76 [well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner] of this regulation.

heading: Report on artesian flow management
paragraph:
67
		  (1) The professional who, in relation to a flowing artesian well, prepares a report for the purposes of section 52 (6) [controlling artesian flow during construction] of the Act must

heading: Report on artesian flow management
paragraph: (a) have competency in the field of hydrogeology or geotechnical engineering,

heading: Report on artesian flow management
paragraph: (b) assess the artesian flow conditions of the flowing artesian well, and

heading: Report on artesian flow management
paragraph: (c) record the assessment of the artesian flow conditions.

heading: Report on artesian flow management
paragraph: (2) A report referred to in subsection (1), in relation to a flowing artesian well, must include the information set out in Schedule 1 and be submitted as soon as practicable after the assessment of the artesian flow conditions.

heading: Maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow
paragraph:
68
		  The owner of a flowing artesian well must ensure that equipment installed to control the artesian flow

heading: Maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow
paragraph: (a) is maintained in a manner that allows the artesian flow to be controlled and the flow of water back into the well to be prevented,

heading: Maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow
paragraph: (b) is protected from damage caused by freezing conditions,

heading: Maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow
paragraph: (c) is not removed from the well except for the purpose of

heading: Maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow
paragraph: (i)  inspecting, repairing or replacing the equipment, or

heading: Maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow
paragraph: (ii)  an activity relating to the well that requires the temporary removal of the equipment, and

heading: Maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow
paragraph: (d) if removed for a purpose described in paragraph (c), is replaced promptly.

heading: Deactivating or decommissioning wells - general
paragraph:
69
		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), for the purposes of section 56 (2) (a) [decommissioning or deactivating well] of the Act, the prescribed period for a well to be considered to be not in service is 5 years.

heading: Deactivating or decommissioning wells - general
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), for the purposes of section 56 (4) of the Act, the prescribed period for a deactivated well to be considered to be not in service is 5 years.

heading: Deactivating or decommissioning wells - general
paragraph: (3) The prescribed periods set out in subsections (1) and (2) do not apply in the case of a flowing artesian well that is managed in accordance with section 52 (6) [controlling artesian flow during construction] or 53 (3) [controlling flowing artesian well] of the Act.

heading: Deactivating or decommissioning wells - general
paragraph: (4) If a flowing artesian well is managed in accordance with section 52 (6) or 53 (3) of the Act, the requirements of this Part do not apply in respect of the well until it is possible to deactivate or decommission the well in accordance with the recommendations of a professional, as accepted by an engineer.

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph:
70
		  (1) The person responsible for deactivating a water supply well, an injection well, a dewatering well or a remediation well must take the well pump out of operation by

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (a) shutting off the power supply to the well pump, or

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (b) removing or disconnecting the manual pump handle.

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (2) In the case of a flowing artesian well, the person responsible for deactivating the well must, in addition to complying with subsection (1),

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (a) prevent any flow of water back into the well,

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (b) stop any artesian flow through the casing, and

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (c) prevent any leakage of the artesian flow at the surface of the ground or into another aquifer.

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (3) The person responsible for deactivating a recharge well must install equipment that prevents water, contaminants and foreign matter from entering the well through the top of the well.

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (4) The person responsible for deactivating a monitoring well must take out of operation any equipment used for monitoring.

heading: Requirements for deactivating wells
paragraph: (5) The person responsible for deactivating a closed-loop geoexchange well must take out of operation any equipment used for the geoexchange system.

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph:
71
		  (1) Subject to section 72, the person responsible for decommissioning a well must

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (a) if practicable, remove from the well the well pump and all other equipment and instrumentation,

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (b) fill the well throughout its depth with layers of sealant and backfill materials in a manner that precludes any lengthwise movement of liquids

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (i)  within the well,

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (ii)  in any visible annular space between the outer casing and the surrounding geological formation, and

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (iii)  between casings,

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (c) seal off all known aquifers and known water-bearing zones within an aquifer, as shown in Figure 4 of Schedule 5, to prevent mixing of groundwater from different aquifers or different water-bearing zones within an aquifer,

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (d) subject to paragraph (e), subsection (5) of this section and section 74 (2), install a closure plug that is at least 1 m in length and, if the depth of the well is insufficient to have a closure plug length of 1 m, the greatest possible length up to 1 m, and

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (e) if the well is a water supply well, or a well that was used at any time as a water supply well, install a closure plug that, subject to subsection (5), is not less than 5 m in length and, if the depth of the water supply well is insufficient to have a closure plug length of 5 m, the greatest possible length up to 5 m.

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (2) The person responsible for decommissioning a well may leave casings in place.

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (3) If there is a potential for entry of liquids into a well, the person responsible for decommissioning the well must fill any entry points or openings with sealant.

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (4) The person responsible for decommissioning a well must ensure that

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (a) the uncased portion of the well has layers of sealant, as shown in Figure 4 of Schedule 5, that are

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (i)  at least 1 m in length, and

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (ii)  separated by not more than 6 m of backfill materials, and

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (b) all sealant is placed in the well in a manner that ensures the physical integrity and continuity of the seal.

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (5) A closure plug may extend to within 0.3 m of the surface of the ground to allow for up to 0.3 m of backfill materials above the closure plug, but the total length of the closure plug must not be less than the length required under subsection (1) (d) or (e), as applicable.

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (6) If a well that is being decommissioned is a closed-loop geoexchange well, the person responsible for decommissioning the well must remove the circulation fluids from the ground loops in the closed-loop geoexchange system.

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (7) If a well that is being decommissioned is a flowing artesian well, the person responsible for decommissioning the well must, in addition to complying with this section,

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (a) stop the artesian flow through the casing, and

heading: Requirements for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (b) prevent any leakage of the artesian flow at the surface of the ground or into another aquifer.

heading: Alternative specifications for decommissioning wells
paragraph:
72
		  (1) If the person responsible for decommissioning a well determines, before decommissioning the well, that it is not practicable to comply with section 71 (1) (b), (d) or (e), (4) or (5), the person may decommission the well in accordance with alternative specifications prepared by a professional under subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Alternative specifications for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (2) A well referred to in subsection (1) may be decommissioned in accordance with alternative specifications in respect of section 71 (1) (b), (d) or (e), (4) or (5) if

heading: Alternative specifications for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (a) a professional who has competency in the field of hydrogeology or geotechnical engineering prepares alternative specifications for the decommissioning of the well that ensure that isolated groundwater from different aquifers, or from different water-bearing zones within an aquifer, remain isolated,

heading: Alternative specifications for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (b) the person responsible for decommissioning the well submits the alternative specifications to an engineer for acceptance by the engineer before the well is decommissioned,

heading: Alternative specifications for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (c) the engineer accepts in writing the alternative specifications, with any terms and conditions that the engineer may specify, and

heading: Alternative specifications for decommissioning wells
paragraph: (d) the person responsible decommissions the well in accordance with the alternative specifications accepted by the engineer under paragraph (c) and any terms and conditions specified by the engineer.

heading: Decommissioning temporary wells
paragraph:
73
		  The owner of a temporary well must ensure that, within 90 days after drilling is completed, the temporary well is

heading: Decommissioning temporary wells
paragraph: (a) decommissioned in accordance with section 71 [requirements for decommissioning wells] or 72, as applicable, or

heading: Decommissioning temporary wells
paragraph: (b) made into a permanent well that meets the standards and requirements of the Act and this regulation that apply to a permanent well of the applicable class.

heading: Decommissioning boreholes and test pits
paragraph:
74
		  (1) The owner of a borehole must ensure that, within 30 days after drilling is completed, the borehole is

heading: Decommissioning boreholes and test pits
paragraph: (a) decommissioned in accordance with section 71 [requirements for decommissioning wells] or 72 [alternative specifications for decommissioning wells], as applicable, or

heading: Decommissioning boreholes and test pits
paragraph: (b) made into a temporary or permanent well that meets the standards and requirements of the Act and this regulation that apply to a temporary or permanent well of the applicable class.

heading: Decommissioning boreholes and test pits
paragraph: (2) The owner of a test pit must ensure that, within 30 days after excavation is completed, the test pit is decommissioned by backfilling with backfill materials.

heading: Well identification reports by owner of well supplying water supply system
paragraph:
75
		  The owner of a well that supplies a water supply system who attaches a well identification plate in accordance with section 54 [attachment of well identification plates by owner of well supplying water supply system] must

heading: Well identification reports by owner of well supplying water supply system
paragraph: (a) complete a well identification report in the form specified by the comptroller that includes the information set out in Schedule 2, and

heading: Well identification reports by owner of well supplying water supply system
paragraph: (b) submit to the comptroller, in the manner specified by the comptroller, a copy of the well identification report within 90 days after attaching the well identification plate.

heading: Well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph:
76
		  If a well construction report must be completed under column 4 of the table in Schedule 6 and must be submitted to both the comptroller and the well owner under column 6 of that table in respect of a class of well, the person responsible for drilling or altering a well in that class must do all of the following:

heading: Well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (a) complete a well construction report, in the form specified by the comptroller, that includes the information set out in Schedule 3;

heading: Well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (b) submit a copy of the well construction report, within 90 days after completing the drilling or alteration,

heading: Well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (i)  to the comptroller in the manner specified by the comptroller, and

heading: Well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (ii)  to the well owner;

heading: Well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (c) retain the well construction report for at least 10 years.

heading: Well construction reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph:
77
		  If a well construction report must be completed under column 4 of the table in Schedule 6 and must be submitted to only the well owner under column 6 of that table in respect of a class of well, the person responsible for drilling or altering a well in that class must do all of the following:

heading: Well construction reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph: (a) complete a well construction report, in the form specified by the comptroller, that includes the information set out in Schedule 3;

heading: Well construction reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph: (b) submit a copy of the well construction report, within 90 days after completing the drilling or alteration, to the well owner;
