heading: Well construction reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph: (c) retain the well construction report for at least 10 years.

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph:
78
		  If a well decommission report must be completed under column 5 of the table in Schedule 6 and must be submitted to both the comptroller and the well owner under column 6 of that table in respect of a class of well, the person responsible for decommissioning a well in that class must do all of the following:

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (a) complete a well decommission report, in the form specified by the comptroller, that includes the information set out in Schedule 4;

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (b) submit a copy of the well decommission report, within 90 days after decommissioning the well,

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (i)  to the comptroller in the manner specified by the comptroller, together with the well identification plate, if applicable, and

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (ii)  to the well owner;

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner
paragraph: (c) retain the well decommission report for at least 10 years.

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph:
79
		  If a well decommission report must be completed under column 5 of the table in Schedule 6 and must be submitted only to the well owner under column 6 of that table in respect of a class of well, the person responsible for decommissioning a well in that class must do all of the following:

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph: (a) complete a well decommission report, in the form specified by the comptroller, that includes the information set out in Schedule 4;

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph: (b) submit a copy of the well decommission report, within 90 days after decommissioning the well, to the well owner;

heading: Well decommission reports submitted to well owner only
paragraph: (c) retain the well decommission report for at least 10 years.

heading: Well decommission reports for flowing artesian wells
paragraph:
80
		  If a well that is decommissioned in accordance with section 71 [requirements for decommissioning wells] or 72 [alternative specifications for decommissioning wells] is a flowing artesian well, or if artesian flow is encountered during the decommissioning of a well, the person responsible for decommissioning the well must complete and submit a well decommission report to both the comptroller and the owner of the well in accordance with section 78 [well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner].

heading: Retention of records
paragraph:
81
		  (1) For the purposes of section 116 (1) [records and reporting] of the Act, the prescribed period during which the owner of a well must keep information and records under this section is

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (a) in the case of information and records described in subsection (2) of this section, until the well is decommissioned, and

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (b) in the case of information and records described in subsection (3) of this section, until 10 years after the well is decommissioned.

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 116 (1) (b) of the Act, the owner of a well must keep, for the period set out in subsection (1) (a), the following information and records:

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (a) every well identification report and well construction report required in respect of the well;

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (b) a report on every flow test conducted in respect of the well;

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (c) if the well is an injection well, every as-built drawing, if any, prepared under section 19 (5) (a) [siting of recharge wells and injection wells] of this regulation;

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (d) if the well is in a well pit, every as-built drawing, if any, prepared under section 36 (5) [well pit restrictions - water supply wells] of this regulation.

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (3) The owner of a well must keep, for the period set out in subsection (1) (b), a well decommission report made in respect of the well under section 78 [well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner], 79 [well decommission reports submitted to well owner only] or 80, which is prescribed for the purposes of section 116 (1) (b) of the Act.

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (4) If the owner of a well conveys or disposes of the well owner's interest in the well, the well owner must transfer all information and records referred to in subsection (2) that are in the custody or under control of the well owner to the new owner of the well or other person to whom the interest in the well is conveyed or otherwise disposed.

heading: General offences
paragraph:
82
		  (1) A person who does either of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) fails to advise the comptroller of changes to the information included in the register as and when required to do so under section 12 (1) (a) [notice to comptroller];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) fails to advise the comptroller of ceasing to work in Canada as a well driller or well pump installer as and when required to do so under section 12 (1) (b).

heading: General offences
paragraph: (2) A person who fails to remove a well pit as and when required to do so under section 36 (2) [well pit restrictions - water supply wells] commits an offence.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (3) A person who fails to upgrade or replace an existing hand pump as required under section 51 (2) [hand pumps in water supply wells] commits an offence.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (4) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) fails to protect a well identification plate from physical damage as and when required to do so under section 56 (1) (a) [protection and replacement of well identification plates];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) fails to ensure that a well identification plate remains securely attached to the well and plainly visible as and when required to do so under section 56 (1) (b);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (c) fails to report the loss or damage of a well identification plate to the comptroller and request a replacement as and when required to do so under section 56 (1) (c);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (d) fails to install a replacement well identification plate as and when required to do so under section 56 (2).

heading: General offences
paragraph: (5) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) fails to ensure that the surface of the ground immediately around a wellhead remains sloped to prevent ponding around the wellhead as required under section 58 (1) (a) [general operating requirements for well and area around wellhead];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) fails to ensure that access to the well and wellhead is maintained for inspection purposes as and when required to do so under section 58 (2) (a);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (c) fails to ensure that the area immediately around a wellhead is kept clear of all obstructions as and when required to do so under section 58 (2) (b).

heading: General offences
paragraph: (6) A person who fails to ensure that any water is conveyed away from a wellhead within a well sump, pump house or well pit as and when required to do so under section 59 [drainage away from wellhead - maintenance of wells in well sumps, pump houses or well pits] commits an offence.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (7) A person who does either of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) fails to comply with the storage requirements under section 62 (1) [storage near water supply wells] by leaving, storing or allowing to accumulate any foreign matter within 3 m of the wellhead of a water supply well;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) fails to prevent any foreign matter that is left, stored or allowed to accumulate more than 3 m from a water supply well from travelling to within 3 m of the wellhead of a water supply well as and when required to do so under section 62 (2).

heading: General offences
paragraph: (8) A person who fails to configure the wellhead or equip a well in a manner that prevents the flow of water back into the well as required under section 66 (a) [additional requirements - stopping or controlling artesian flow] commits an offence.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (9) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) fails to ensure that any equipment installed to control artesian flow and prevent water from flowing back into a well is maintained as required under section 68 (a) [maintenance of equipment installed to control artesian flow];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) fails to protect any equipment installed to control artesian flow and prevent water from flowing back into a well from damage caused by freezing as required under section 68 (b);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (c) removes any equipment installed to control artesian flow and prevent water from flowing back into a well for purposes other than those permitted under section 68 (c);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (d) fails to ensure that any equipment installed to control artesian flow and prevent water from flowing back into a well is replaced as and when required under section 68 (d).

heading: General offences
paragraph: (10) A person who fails to complete and submit a well identification report as and when required to do so under section 75 [well identification reports by owner of well supplying water supply system] commits an offence.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (11) A person who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction to the penalties set out in section 106 (6) [general offences] of the Act.

heading: Transition - certification
paragraph:
83
		  The comptroller must not, under section 7 (d) (ii) [registers of well drillers and well pump installers], remove any person from the register of well drillers or the register of well pump installers, as the case may be, merely because the person fails to maintain a requirement for registration on or after April 26, 2013, in relation to certification as a Ground Water Drilling Technician or a Ground Water Pump Technician issued by the Canadian Ground Water Association before April 26, 2013.

heading: Transition - well identification report
paragraph:
84
		  For the purposes of section 81 (2) [retention of records], a reference to a "well identification report" includes information regarding the identification, if any, of a well that was reported under the former regulation.

heading: Transition - well construction report
paragraph:
85
		  The definition of "well construction report" in section 1 (1) [definitions and interpretation] includes a well construction report relating to the construction or alteration of a well that was completed before this regulation came into force, if available.

heading: Transition - well decommission report and well closure report
paragraph:
86
		  The definition of "well decommission report" in section 1 (1) [definitions and interpretation] includes a well closure report relating to the decommissioning or closure of a well that was completed under the former regulation.

heading: Required information
paragraph:
1
		  A report by a professional in respect of artesian flow management required under section 67 [report on artesian flow management] of this regulation must include

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the following information relating to the owner, location and identification of the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the name, mailing address, telephone number and, if available, the email address of the owner of the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the property on which the well is located, described by its site address, legal description or parcel identifier number (PID);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  either

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the universal transverse mercator (UTM) zone and the UTM coordinates of the well recorded to the nearest metre, or

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the latitude and longitude of the well recorded in decimal degrees to at least 5 decimal places, or recorded in degrees, minutes and seconds with the seconds recorded to at least 2 decimal places;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iv)  if a well identification plate is attached to the well, the well identification number,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the following information relating to actions taken to mitigate or remediate damage caused by artesian flow:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  a description of the assessment of artesian flow, including rate of flow, artesian pressure, site conditions and visible impacts;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  a description of the construction of the well and the observed state of the artesian flow in respect of the well, including a scaled drawing that shows the construction and the observed state;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  in respect of any actions taken to attempt to stop or bring the artesian flow under control, or remediate any damage caused by the artesian flow, a description of the following:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) any actions taken by the professional or, to the knowledge of the professional, by another person;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the timeline for the actions;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (C) if known, the name and contact information of another person who took the actions;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (D) any observations, or proof, of the actions taken by another person under clause (A);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (E) any material, including sealant, added into the flowing artesian well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (F) the reasons for the failure of the attempts to stop or bring the artesian flow under control,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (c) an evaluation by the professional in respect of the following:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  a description of the proposed manner of managing the artesian flow, including the following:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the exceptional circumstances that make it not practicable to stop or bring the artesian flow under control under section 52 (1) (a) or (b) [controlling artesian flow during construction] of the Act;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the method by which the flow of water will be prevented from flowing back into the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (C) if the well will be altered, modified or configured differently, a description of what is proposed and a scaled drawing of the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (D) the anticipated work plan and timeline for implementation;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (E) the estimated reduction of artesian flow;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (F) options, if any, for managing the artesian flow other than the proposed manner;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (G) any potential threats to property, public safety or the environment that may be posed by the proposed manner;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (H) any other potential impacts that may be caused by the proposed manner, including to any public or private lands or activities, to infrastructure, to stream water, to any aquifer, to other water users or holders of water rights or to wildlife, fisheries, habitats or other ecosystems;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (I) options, if any, for potential remediation of any adverse impacts that may be caused by the proposed manner, such as those described in clauses (G) and (H);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (J) the estimated cost of managing the artesian flow in accordance with the proposed manner, including maintenance and monitoring costs that may be anticipated;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (K) the estimated cost of stopping or bringing the artesian flow under control;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  any conclusions as to whether the proposed manner of managing the artesian flow

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) would be more suitable than stopping or bringing the artesian flow under control, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) would not pose a threat to property, public safety or the environment;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  the reasons or basis for the conclusions under subparagraph (ii), including the following:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) an evaluation of the risks and consequences of the proposed manner of managing the artesian flow as compared to other options;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) an evaluation of the likelihood that the proposed manner of managing the artesian flow will satisfy the requirements of section 52 (6) of the Act, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (d) the following information:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the name and business contact information of the professional, including business name, if any, address, telephone number and, if available, email address and fax number;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  a summary of the professional's experience with controlling or managing artesian flow.

heading: Other information requirements
paragraph:
2
		  Section 1 of this Schedule does not limit any other provision of this regulation that may require the inclusion of information in a report in respect of artesian flow management.

heading: Required information
paragraph:
1
		  A well identification report required under section 75 [well identification reports by owner of well supplying water supply system] of this regulation must include

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the following information relating to the owner and location of the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the name, mailing address, telephone number and, if available, the email address of the owner of the well that is for the purpose of supplying a water supply system;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the name of the well, if any;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  the name of the water supply system;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iv)  the property on which the well is located described by its site address, legal description or parcel identifier number (PID);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (v)  either

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the universal transverse mercator (UTM) zone and the UTM coordinates of the well recorded to the nearest metre, or

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the latitude and longitude of the well recorded in decimal degrees to at least 5 decimal places or recorded in degrees, minutes and seconds with the seconds recorded to at least 2 decimal places,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the following information relating to the well identification plate:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the well identification number;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  a description of where the well identification plate is attached;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  the name of the person attaching the well identification plate;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iv)  the date of attachment of the well identification plate, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (c) a copy of

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  any available well construction report relating to the well, or

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  any information on the depth and diameter of the well.

heading: Other information requirements
paragraph:
2
		  Section 1 of this Schedule does not limit any other provision of this regulation requiring the inclusion of information in a well identification report.

heading: Required information
paragraph:
1
		  A well construction report required under section 76 [well construction reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner] or 77 [well construction reports submitted to well owner only] of this regulation must include

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the following information relating to the owner and location of the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the name, mailing address, telephone number and, if available, the email address of the owner of the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the property on which the well is located, described by its site address, legal description or parcel identifier number (PID);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  either

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the universal transverse mercator (UTM) zone and the UTM coordinates of the well recorded to the nearest metre, or

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the latitude and longitude of the well recorded in decimal degrees to at least 5 decimal places or recorded in degrees, minutes and seconds with the seconds recorded to at least 2 decimal places,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the following information relating to the type of work, class of well and method of drilling:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  whether the report relates to the drilling of, or an alteration to, the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the class and, if applicable, category or subclass of the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  if the well is a water supply well, the intended use or purpose of the water supply well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iv)  the method of drilling the well,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (c) the following information relating to geological materials and their water-bearing characteristics:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  a description of the geological materials encountered during drilling or alteration, including the depth at which the materials are encountered and whether they are water-bearing;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  if the well is drilled into bedrock, the depth of water-bearing zones, if any, encountered in bedrock and their estimated flow,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (d) the following information relating to the construction of the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the details of casings used, if any, including surface casing;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  if a drive shoe was used;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  the diameter of the hole;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iv)  the total depth drilled;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (v)  the finished well depth;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (vi)  the type and depth of any backfill materials or sealant placed in the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (vii)  the details of the surface seal and the method of its installation, if a surface seal was installed;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (viii)  the details of the screen assembly and filter pack material, if any;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ix)  the details of liner used, if any,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (e) if the well was developed, the following information relating to the development of the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the method of development;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the duration of development,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (f) if a well yield test was conducted, the following information relating to the well yield test:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the method, rate and duration of well yield testing;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the drawdown in water level at the end of well yield testing;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  the well yield estimated from the test;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iv)  if the well was hydrofractured, any increase in well yield resulting from hydrofracturing,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (g) the following information relating to the completion of the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  if a casing was installed, the final length of the casing stick-up;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the static water level or shut-in pressure level, whichever is applicable;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  whether the well was disinfected;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iv)  the type of well cap used, and if a well cover was also used, the type of well cover used,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (h) if a well identification plate is required, the following information:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the well identification number;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the location where the well identification plate is attached,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) if available, the well tag number,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (j) the following information relating to the person responsible for drilling or altering the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  if applicable, the registration number of

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the person responsible for drilling or altering the well, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the person who drilled or altered the well, if different from the person referred to in clause (A);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the name and business contact information, including business name, if any, address, telephone number and, if available, email address and fax number of

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the person responsible for drilling or altering the well, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the person who drilled or altered the well, if different from the person referred to in clause (A),

heading: Required information
paragraph: (k) the starting and completion dates of the work,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (l) a copy of alternative specifications relating to the well, if any, made under section 18 (3) [siting of water supply wells and permanent dewatering wells] of this regulation, including the engineer's acceptance and the terms and conditions, if any, relating to the alternative specifications,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (m) a copy of the documentation referred to in section 19 (2) [siting of recharge wells and injection wells] of the regulation, including the design, the engineer's acceptance and the terms and conditions, if any, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (n) a copy of any drilling authorization for the well.

heading: Other information requirements
paragraph:
2
		  Section 1 of this Schedule does not limit any other provision of this regulation requiring the inclusion of information in a well construction report.

heading: Required information
paragraph:
1
		  A well decommission report required under section 78 [well decommission reports submitted to both comptroller and well owner], 79 [well decommission reports submitted to well owner only] or 80 [well decommission reports for flowing artesian wells] of this regulation must include

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the following information relating to the owner and location of the well:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i)  the name, mailing address, telephone number and, if available, the email address of the owner of the well;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii)  the property on which the well is located described by its site address, legal description or parcel identifier number (PID);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii)  either

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the universal transverse mercator (UTM) zone and the UTM coordinates of the well recorded to the nearest metre, or

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) the latitude and longitude of the well recorded in decimal degrees to at least 5 decimal places or recorded in degrees, minutes and seconds with the seconds recorded to at least 2 decimal places,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the following information relating to the well:

heading: Required information

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authority" means the British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority continued under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commission" means the British Columbia Utilities Commission continued under the Utilities Commission Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "generation" means production by hydraulic, electrical, steam, internal combustion engine, gas, oil or by any other process;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "judge" means a justice of the Court of Appeal or a judge of the Supreme Court;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "owner",

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to land, means a person registered in the books of a land title office as owner of land or of a charge on land, whether entitled to it in the person's own right or in a representative capacity or otherwise and includes a lessee in possession for a term of 3 years or less and a person who is the owner, although unregistered, of an estate less than the fee simple granted by the Crown, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to other property, includes a mortgagee, person entitled to a limited estate or interest and a guardian, executor, administrator or trustee in whom any property or interest in any property is vested;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "power", except in sections 12 (1) and 38 (2), includes energy, light and heat however developed or produced, and includes electricity and natural, manufactured or mixed gas, or liquefied petroleum gas;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "power plant" or "plant" includes all land, water, rights to the use of water, buildings, works, machinery, installations, materials, devices, fittings, apparatus, appliances, offices, furniture and equipment, vehicles, tools, stores and supplies, including office stores and supplies, constructed, acquired or used or adapted, or that, in the opinion of the authority, might be used or adapted for or in connection with the generation or supply of power;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "power project" includes any charter, franchise, privilege or other right, or land, buildings, plant, machinery or equipment acquired, or proposed to be acquired, by a person with a view to the generation or supply of power, or any plans, surveys or data made or assembled with a view to the generation or supply of power;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "power site" includes any land, or any lake, river, stream, watercourse or body of water, water licence or privilege, or reservoir, dam, water storage, sluice, canal, raceway, tunnel or aqueduct that is used or that, in the opinion of the authority, might be used for or in connection with the generation or supply of power;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "supply" as a noun means reservation, transmission, distribution, capacity to provide, dealing in and sale, and as a verb has a corresponding meaning.

heading: Authority continued
paragraph: 2		  The corporation known as the British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority is continued, consisting of persons who are appointed as directors and who hold office as provided in this Act.

heading: Agent of government
paragraph:
3
		  (1) The authority is for all its purposes an agent of the government and its powers may be exercised only as an agent of the government.

heading: Agent of government
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Finance is the fiscal agent of the authority.

heading: Agent of government
paragraph: (3) The authority, on behalf of the government, may contract in its corporate name without specific reference to the government.

heading: Directors
paragraph:
4
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council appoints the directors of the authority who hold office during pleasure.

heading: Directors
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must appoint one or more of the directors to chair the authority.

heading: Directors
paragraph: (3) A chair or other director must be paid by the authority the salary, directors' fee and other remuneration the Lieutenant Governor in Council determines.

heading: Powers of directors
paragraph:
5
		  The directors must manage the affairs of the authority or supervise the management of those affairs, and may

heading: Powers of directors
paragraph: (a) exercise the powers conferred on them under this Act,

heading: Powers of directors
paragraph: (b) exercise the powers of the authority on behalf of the authority, and

heading: Powers of directors
paragraph: (c) delegate the exercise or performance of a power or duty conferred or imposed on them to anyone employed by the authority.

heading: Directors' proceedings
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The directors may, on behalf of the authority, pass resolutions thought by them necessary or advisable for the

heading: Directors' proceedings
paragraph: (a) conduct of the affairs of the authority, and

heading: Directors' proceedings
paragraph: (b) times, places, calling and regulation of meetings of directors and of committees of directors.

heading: Directors' proceedings
paragraph: (2) The authority may exercise any of its powers or duties by resolution unless otherwise provided in this Act.

heading: Interests of directors
paragraph:
7
		  A director of the authority must not, directly or indirectly,

heading: Interests of directors
paragraph: (b) have an interest in any device, appliance, machine, article, patent or patented process that is used in the generation or supply of power, or

heading: Interests of directors
paragraph: (c) have an interest in a contract for the construction of, or doing any work on, a power plant.

heading: Resolutions
paragraph:
8
		  A resolution in writing signed by all the directors is as valid and effectual as if it had been passed at a properly called and constituted meeting of directors.

heading: Executive committee
paragraph:
9
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may appoint an executive management committee of the authority that is composed of not more than 5 directors, and that must, subject to the direction of the directors of the authority, manage the operations of the authority.

heading: Executive committee
paragraph: (2) The members of the executive management committee may be paid remuneration determined by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Appointment of employees
paragraph:
10
		  The authority may, without regard to the Public Service Act, appoint a secretary and executive officers, engineers, solicitors, accountants, employees, consultants and agents it thinks necessary for its business, and may define their duties, determine their compensation and provide a system of organization to establish responsibility and promote efficiency.

heading: Bonds
paragraph: 11		  The authority may require bonds of the officers and employees it designates.

heading: Powers
paragraph:
12
		  (1) Subject to this Act and the regulations, the authority has the capacity and the rights, powers and privileges of an individual of full capacity and, in addition, has

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) the power to amalgamate in any manner with a firm or person, and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) any other power prescribed.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (1.1) The authority's purposes are

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) to generate, manufacture, conserve, supply, acquire and dispose of power and related products,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) to supply and acquire services related to anything in paragraph (a), and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) to do other things as may be prescribed.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (1.2) The authority may not engage in activities or classes of activities prescribed for the purposes of this subsection without obtaining an applicable approval as prescribed.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (2) If the authority

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) acquires all of the property, assets or undertaking of a firm or person,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) assumes the obligations and liabilities of a firm or person,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) amalgamates in any manner with a firm or person, or

heading: Powers
paragraph: (d) takes over the management, supervision or control of the business of a firm or person,

heading: Powers
paragraph: the authority or the amalgamated corporation, if there is an amalgamation, may exercise and perform any power or duty conferred or imposed on it or on that other firm or person under this or any other Act for and on behalf of that other firm or person, or the amalgamated corporation, or with respect to the property or undertaking of that other firm or person, or the amalgamated corporation, with or without exercising or performing any other resulting power or duty.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (3) If the authority amalgamates with a firm or person, this Act applies as if the amalgamated corporation were the authority.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, prescribe the procedure to be followed in amalgamation of the authority with a firm or person.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (5) Despite the Land Title Act, if the authority acquires all of the property, assets or undertaking of, or amalgamates in any manner with, a firm or person,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) all of the interests of that firm or person that are registered in a land title office are deemed to be registered interests of the authority or the amalgamated corporation, as the case may be,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) the registrar of that land title office must accordingly make all necessary amendments to the register, and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) the amendments constitute registration of the interests under the Land Title Act in favour of the authority or the amalgamated corporation, as the case may be.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (6) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations necessary for carrying out subsection (5).

heading: Powers
paragraph: (7) Fees must not be paid for anything done under subsection (5) or  (6).

heading: Powers
paragraph: (8) Nothing in this section relieves the authority from any requirement of the Utilities Commission Act that applies to the authority under section 32 (7).

heading: Powers
paragraph: (9) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by order, may designate any agreement entered into or to be entered into by the authority that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers relates to the provision of support services to or on behalf of the authority.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (10) For the purposes of subsection (9), "support services" means services that support or are ancillary to the activities of the authority from time to time, and includes services related to metering for, billing and collecting fees, charges, tariffs, rates and other compensation for electricity sold, delivered or provided by the authority, but does not include the production, generation, storage, transmission, sale, delivery or provision of electricity.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (11) Despite the common law and the provisions of this or any other enactment, if an agreement is designated under subsection (9),

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) the authority is deemed to have, and to have always had, the power and capacity to enter into the agreement,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) the agreement and all actions of the authority taken in accordance with the provisions of the agreement are authorized, valid and deemed to be required for the public convenience and necessity,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) the authority is deemed to have, and to have always had, the power and capacity to carry out all of the obligations imposed under, and to exercise all of the rights, powers and privileges granted by, the agreement according to its terms,

heading: Powers
paragraph: (d) the agreement is binding on and enforceable by the authority, according to the agreement's terms, and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (e) subject to subsection (12), the authority is not required to obtain any approval, authorization, permit or order under the Utilities Commission Act in connection with the agreement or any actions taken in accordance with the terms of the agreement, and the commission must not prohibit the authority from taking any action that the authority is entitled or required to take under the terms of the agreement.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (12) Nothing in subsection (11) (e) precludes the commission from considering the costs incurred, or to be incurred, in relation to an agreement designated under subsection (9) when establishing the revenue requirements and setting the rates of the authority.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph:
16
		  (1) The authority may, for any purpose related to the exercise of its powers,

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (a) expropriate any property, power site, power project or power plant,

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (b) enter, remain on, take possession of and use any property,

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (c) on land that it expropriates,

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (i)  erect, make or place on the land any structure, installation, excavation or power plant, and

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (ii)  flood and overflow the land and accumulate and store water on it, and

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (d) require and compel a person who generates or supplies power to enter into an agreement to supply to the authority as much of that power as the authority requires.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (2) If land is expropriated under subsection (1), the Expropriation Act applies.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (3) If the authority exercises a power under subsection (1) that does not constitute the expropriation of land requiring approval under the Expropriation Act, it must obtain the approval of the minister before the power is exercised.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (4) If the authority expropriates property under subsection (1) other than land, the authority must notify the Attorney General and, if required by the Attorney General, file a notice describing the property at a place designated by the Attorney General.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (5) Despite any other Act, the property referred to in subsection (3) that is expropriated vests in the authority free and clear of all encumbrances

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (a) when the notice is filed under subsection (4), or

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (b) if no filing is requested, when the Attorney General receives the notification under subsection (4).

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (6) After property vests under subsection (5), the authority must serve on the owner of the property a notice containing a description of the property sufficient to identify it, together with a declaration of readiness to pay compensation in an amount to be agreed on or to be determined under subsection (9).

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (7) If an owner is absent from British Columbia or is unknown or cannot be served, the Supreme Court may, on the application of the authority, order that the notice under subsection (6) be published in a manner and for a time that the court thinks proper, and, on publication, the owner is deemed to have been served with the notice.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (8) If the authority exercises its powers under subsection (1), other than in relation to the expropriation of land, it must pay compensation for

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (a) the interest, property, matter or thing expropriated, entered on or used, and

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (b) damages to any property that directly result from the expropriation, entry or use.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: (9) If the authority and a person entitled to compensation fail to agree on the amount of compensation payable under subsection (8), the amount must be determined by the Supreme Court.

heading: Compulsory supply of power
paragraph: 17		  (1) If the authority is unable to agree with a person required or compelled to supply power under section 16 (1) (d) on the amount of power available for the authority's use or the price to be paid for it or on any matter relating to supplying the power desired, the commission must, on application of either party, after a hearing, determine the amount of power, if any, to be supplied and the price to be paid for it, and also any other matter on which agreement has not been reached.

heading: Compulsory supply of power
paragraph: (2) A determination of the commission under subsection (1) is final.

heading: Release on expropriation
paragraph:
18
		  (1) If any power of expropriation is exercised by the authority, the authority must, by order in writing, release the person whose property has been expropriated from any obligation relating to the purchase or supply of power or to the purchase or sale of anything required for a power plant.

heading: Release on expropriation
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) is binding on all parties concerned.

heading: Release on expropriation
paragraph: (3) An order made under subsection (1) has effect only in regard to matters connected with the property expropriated.

heading: Application of expropriation power
paragraph:
19
		  The power of expropriation conferred on the authority extends to property, plants, rights, powers and privileges, even though

heading: Application of expropriation power
paragraph: (a) they are or may be deemed to be devoted to public use, or

heading: Application of expropriation power
paragraph: (b) the owner possesses the power of taking land compulsorily,

heading: Application of expropriation power
paragraph: but the authority does not have the power to take by expropriation land or a plant of a municipality that may be used for the generation or supply of power.

heading: Power of entry, etc.
paragraph:
20
		  (1) The authority may, by itself, or by its engineers, surveyors, agents, contractors, subcontractors or employees, for any purpose relating to the use, construction, maintenance, safeguarding or repair of its plants or projected plants, or for better access to them and without the consent of the owner, enter any land and

heading: Power of entry, etc.
paragraph: (a) survey and take levels of it and make the borings, tests or sink the trial pits it thinks necessary,

heading: Power of entry, etc.
paragraph: (b) cut down any trees that, in its opinion, might, in falling or otherwise, endanger the conductors, wires or equipment or other plant of the authority, or that may obstruct the running of survey lines, and

heading: Power of entry, etc.
paragraph: (c) make or use all roads, trails, bridges, wharves and other works and facilities, whether permanent or temporary, that may be required for the convenient passing to and from its survey lines, plants and projected plants.

heading: Power of entry, etc.
paragraph: (2) Despite anything in this Act, if a claim is made against the authority for damage to crops, gardens, shrubs, trees or other growing things, or other damage caused by or incidental to the exercise of powers conferred by this section, if the amount of compensation for damage is not agreed on, compensation must be determined by the Supreme Court.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph:
21
		  (1) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the authority, for any of the purposes of the authority, may

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (a) borrow sums of money the authority thinks are required, and

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (b) issue notes, bonds, debentures and other securities bearing interest at rates and payable as to principal and interest in currencies and at places and at times and in a manner the authority determines.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (2) The directors of the authority may, by resolution, delegate any of their powers or the powers of the authority under this section to any director or officer of the authority.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (3) A resolution under this section that is approved by the required number of directors by telephone or any other means of communication and that is confirmed in writing or other graphic communication is as valid and effectual as if it had been passed at a meeting of the directors properly called and constituted.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (4) The notes, bonds, debentures and other securities of the authority may be made redeemable in advance of maturity at times and at prices the directors of the authority determine at the time of the issue.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (5) For this section, the purposes of the authority, without limiting any other provision of this Act, include the following:

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (a) payment, refunding, exchange or renewal of all or any part of a loan raised or securities issued by the authority, except to the extent that a sinking fund is available for the payment of the loan or securities, and a recital or declaration in the resolution or minutes of the authority authorizing the issue of securities as to the amount of any sinking fund so available is conclusive evidence of the fact;

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (b) payment of all or any part of a loan, liability or bonds, debentures or other securities, payment of which is guaranteed or assumed by the authority;

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (c) payment of any other liability or indebtedness of the authority;

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (d) carrying out any of the powers referred to in this Act, providing in whole or in part for expenditures of the authority made or to be made in connection with them, reimbursing the authority for any of those expenditures and repaying all or part of any temporary borrowings of the authority for any of those purposes;

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (e) the exercise of a power, right, function or duty conferred or imposed on the authority under this or any other Act or law.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (6) The authority may borrow and may issue under subsection (1) in amounts that will realize the net sum required by the authority for its purposes, and a recital or declaration in the resolution or minutes of the authority authorizing the issue of securities to the effect that the issue of the authorized securities is being made for the purposes of the authority and that the amount is necessary to realize the net sum required for the purposes of the authority is conclusive evidence of the fact.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (7) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, on terms and conditions thought advisable, the authority may dispose of the notes, bonds, debentures and other securities of the authority, either at the par value of them or at less or more than the par value, and may charge, pledge, hypothecate, deposit or otherwise deal with the securities as collateral security.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (8) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council on terms and conditions thought advisable, the authority may exchange notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority for securities of another corporation

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (a) in an amount or amounts equal to or greater or smaller than the amount or amounts of the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority,

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (b) bearing interest payable at the same or different time or times as the interest payable under the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority,

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (c) bearing interest at the same or a greater or smaller rate as or than the interest payable under the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority,

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (d) due on the same or on an earlier or later date as or than the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority, and

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (e) callable whether or not the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority are callable and on the same or different terms and conditions as or than the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority if they are callable.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (9) Securities of the authority, dealt with as collateral security,

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (a) when redelivered to the authority or its nominees on or after payment, satisfaction, release or discharge, in whole or in part, of any indebtedness or obligation for which the securities may have been given as collateral, or

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (b) when the authority again becomes entitled to the securities,

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: may be treated by the authority as unissued and, subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council,

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (c) may be issued, reissued, charged, pledged, hypothecated, deposited, dealt with as collateral security, sold or otherwise disposed of on terms and conditions the directors of the authority think advisable, or

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (d) at the option of the authority, may be cancelled, at which time, subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, fresh securities to the same amount and in the same form may be issued in place of them with the same consequences, and on the issue or reissue a person entitled to them has the same rights and remedies as if the securities had not been previously issued,

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: but the borrowing power of the authority is deemed not to have been affected by the issuance, reissuance, pledging, depositing or selling of securities under this section.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (10) The notes, bonds, debentures and other securities of the authority must be in a form determined by the directors of the authority or on behalf of the authority by the Minister of Finance as fiscal agent for the authority.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (11) The notes, bonds, debentures and other securities must bear the seal of the authority and, together with any coupons attached, must bear the signatures in writing of

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (a) the chair and another director or officer, or

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (b) other directors or officers as the authority may determine.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (12) The directors of the authority may provide that the seal of the authority may be engraved, lithographed, printed or otherwise mechanically reproduced on any security to which it is to be affixed.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (13) The seal of the authority, when mechanically reproduced, has the same effect as if manually affixed, and any mechanically reproduced signature or signatures are for all purposes valid and binding on the authority even though the person whose signature is reproduced has ceased to hold office before the date of the security or before its issue.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (14) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the authority may also borrow by way of temporary loans from any person the sums on the terms, for the purposes and on the conditions the directors of the authority determine, by way of bank overdraft or line of credit, or by the pledging as security for the temporary loans of notes, bonds, debentures or other securities of the authority pending the sale of them or in place of selling them, or in whatever other manner the directors of the authority determine.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (15) Any cheques, promissory notes or other instruments necessary or desirable in connection with the borrowing of money and the obtaining of advances by way of temporary loans as set out in subsection (14) may be executed in whatever manner the directors of the authority determine.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (16) The Minister of Finance, as fiscal agent of the authority, may arrange all details and do, transact and execute all deeds, matters and things that are required during the negotiation of a loan or for placing a loan.

heading: Borrowing by authority
paragraph: (17) Money raised by the authority under this section must be paid by the authority into the fund established under section 27.

heading: Authorization to borrow from Canada Pension Plan Investment Fund
paragraph:
22
		  Despite anything in this Act, the authority may, in the resolution under section 21, authorize the Minister of Finance or, with the concurrence of the Minister of Finance, authorize the Minister of Finance of Canada to determine any matter required to be determined under section 21 for

heading: Authorization to borrow from Canada Pension Plan Investment Fund
paragraph: (a) borrowing money from the Canada Pension Plan Investment Fund established under the Canada Pension Plan, and

heading: Authorization to borrow from Canada Pension Plan Investment Fund
paragraph: (b) issuing and selling to the Receiver General and Minister of Finance of Canada for the credit of the Canada Pension Plan Investment Fund debentures as security for the loans.

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: 23		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, for and on behalf of the government, may guarantee the payment of the principal and interest of and on any of the following:

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (a) notes, bonds, securities, debentures, debenture stock, loans or obligations issued by the authority or the payment of which is assumed by the authority;

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (b) notes, bonds, securities, debentures, debenture stock or loans issued by a firm or person if

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (i)  all of the property, assets or undertaking of the firm or person has been acquired by the authority,

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (ii)  the obligations and liabilities of the firm or person has been assumed by the authority,

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (iii)  the firm or person is amalgamated with the authority, or

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (iv)  the management, supervision or control of the business of the firm or person has been taken over by the authority.

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (2) The guarantee under subsection (1) must bear the manual, engraved, lithographed or printed signature of the Minister of Finance, or the manual, engraved, lithographed or printed signature or signatures of the other officer or officers of the Ministry of Finance of British Columbia designated by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (3) The engraved, lithographed or printed signature of the Minister of Finance or of any other officer is for all purposes the signature of that person, and is binding on the government even though the person whose signature is reproduced may not have held office at the date of the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities or at the date of the delivery of them, and despite any change in any of the persons holding the office between the time when the signature is affixed and the date of delivery of the notes, bonds, debentures or other securities.

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make arrangements for the supply of money necessary to fulfill the requirements of a guarantee, and may advance the amount necessary out of the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Guarantee of principal and interest
paragraph: (5) In the hands of a holder of a note, bond, security or debenture, a guarantee signed in accordance with subsection (2) is conclusive evidence that this section has been complied with, and the government becomes liable for the payment of the principal and interest of the note, bond, security or debenture guaranteed, according to its tenor.

heading: Guarantees respecting leases
paragraph:
24
		  (1) The government may, on terms approved by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, guarantee payments of the authority under a lease made by or to the authority.

heading: Guarantees respecting leases
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may authorize

heading: Guarantees respecting leases
paragraph: (a) the Minister of Finance, or

heading: Guarantees respecting leases
paragraph: (b) an officer of the Ministry of Finance,

heading: Guarantees respecting leases
paragraph: to sign the guarantee on behalf of the government, and the signature of that person on the guarantee is conclusive proof that this section has been complied with.

heading: Guarantees respecting leases
paragraph: (3) Money required to be paid by the government in respect of a guarantee given under this section must be paid out of the consolidated revenue fund without an appropriation other than this Act.

heading: All funds paid into one fund
paragraph:
27
		  (1) All funds, including borrowings, income and revenue, that come into the hands of the authority, whether as agent, trustee, owner or otherwise, form one fund, out of which the authority must make any and all expenditures necessary for its purpose.

heading: All funds paid into one fund
paragraph: (2) The authority must account for the fund and payments from the fund in its annual report as provided in this Act.

heading: Financial reporting and auditing
paragraph:
28
		  (1) The Minister of Finance may direct the Comptroller General of British Columbia to examine and report to the Treasury Board on any or all of the financial and accounting operations of the authority.

heading: Financial reporting and auditing
paragraph: (2) Unless the Auditor General is appointed in accordance with the Auditor General Act as the auditor of the authority, the authority must appoint an auditor to audit the accounts of the authority at least once each year.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Impact Assessment Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 The following definitions apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: adverse effects within federal jurisdiction means, with respect to a physical activity or a designated project,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a non-negligible adverse change to the following components of the environment that are within the legislative authority of Parliament:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) fish and fish habitat, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Fisheries Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) aquatic species, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Species at Risk Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii) migratory birds, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iv) any other component of the environment that is set out in Schedule 3;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a non-negligible adverse change to the environment that would occur on federal lands;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a non-negligible adverse change to the marine environment that is caused by pollution and that would occur outside Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a non-negligible adverse change - that is caused by pollution - to boundary waters or international waters, as those terms are defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Water Act, or to interprovincial waters;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) with respect to the Indigenous peoples of Canada, a non-negligible adverse impact - occurring in Canada and resulting from any change to the environment - on

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) physical and cultural heritage,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) the current use of lands and resources for traditional purposes, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii) any structure, site or thing that is of historical, archaeological, paleontological or architectural significance;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) a non-negligible adverse change occurring in Canada to the health, social or economic conditions of the Indigenous peoples of Canada; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) a non-negligible adverse change to a health, social or economic matter that is within the legislative authority of Parliament that is set out in Schedule 3.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: In the case of a physical activity or a designated project that is carried out on federal lands or is a federal work or undertaking, as defined in subsection 3(1) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, this definition also includes the non-negligible adverse effects of that activity or project. (effets negatifs relevant d'un domaine de competence federale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Agency means the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada that is continued under section 153. (Agence)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: analyst means a person or a member of a class of persons designated as an analyst under subsection 120(1). (analyste)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: assessment by a review panel means an impact assessment that is conducted by a review panel. (examen par une commission)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian Energy Regulator means the Canadian Energy Regulator established by subsection 10(1) of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act. (Regie canadienne de l'energie)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission means the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission established by section 8 of the Nuclear Safety and Control Act. (Commission canadienne de surete nucleaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: designated project means one or more physical activities that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) are carried out in Canada or on federal lands; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) are designated by regulations made under paragraph 109(b) or designated in an order made by the Minister under subsection 9(1).

heading: Definitions
paragraph: It includes any physical activity that is incidental to those physical activities, but it does not include a physical activity designated by regulations made under paragraph 112(1)(a.2). (projet designe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: direct or incidental adverse effects means non-negligible adverse effects that are directly linked or necessarily incidental to a federal authority's exercise of a power or performance of a duty or function that would permit the carrying out, in whole or in part, of a physical activity or designated project, or to a federal authority's provision of financial assistance to a person for the purpose of enabling that activity or project to be carried out, in whole or in part. (effets directs ou accessoires negatifs)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: effects means, unless the context requires otherwise, changes to the environment or to health, social or economic conditions and the positive and negative consequences of these changes. (effets)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: enforcement officer means a person or a member of a class of persons designated as an enforcement officer under subsection 120(1). (agent de l'autorite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environment means the components of the Earth, and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) land, water and air, including all layers of the atmosphere;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) all organic and inorganic matter and living organisms; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the interacting natural systems that include components referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b). (environnement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal authority means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a Minister of the Crown in right of Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an agency of the Government of Canada or a parent Crown corporation, as defined in subsection 83(1) of the Financial Administration Act, or any other body established by or under an Act of Parliament that is ultimately accountable through a Minister of the Crown in right of Canada to Parliament for the conduct of its affairs;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any department or departmental corporation that is set out in Schedule I, I.1 or II to the Financial Administration Act; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any other body that is set out in Schedule 1.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: It does not include the Executive Council of - or a minister, department, agency or body of the government of - Yukon, the Northwest Territories or Nunavut, a council of the band within the meaning of the Indian Act, Export Development Canada or the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board. It also does not include a Crown corporation, as defined in subsection 83(1) of the Financial Administration Act, that is a wholly-owned subsidiary, as defined in that subsection, a harbour commission established under the Harbour Commissions Act or a not-for-profit corporation that enters into an agreement under subsection 80(5) of the Canada Marine Act, that is not set out in Schedule 1. (autorite federale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal lands means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) lands that belong to Her Majesty in right of Canada, or that Her Majesty in right of Canada has the power to dispose of, and all waters on and airspace above those lands, other than lands under the administration and control of the Commissioner of Yukon, the Northwest Territories or Nunavut;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the following lands and areas:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) the internal waters of Canada, in any area of the sea not within a province,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) the territorial sea of Canada, in any area of the sea not within a province,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii) the exclusive economic zone of Canada, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iv) the continental shelf of Canada; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) reserves, surrendered lands and any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band and that are subject to the Indian Act, and all waters on and airspace above those reserves or lands. (territoire domanial)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: follow-up program means a program for verifying the accuracy of the impact assessment of a designated project and determining the effectiveness of any mitigation measures. (programme de suivi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: impact assessment means an assessment of the effects of a designated project that is conducted in accordance with this Act. (evaluation d'impact)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous governing body means a council, government or other entity that is authorized to act on behalf of an Indigenous group, community or people that holds rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982. (corps dirigeant autochtone)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous knowledge means the Indigenous knowledge of the Indigenous peoples of Canada. (connaissances autochtones)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous peoples of Canada has the meaning assigned by the definition aboriginal peoples of Canada in subsection 35(2) of the Constitution Act, 1982. (peuples autochtones du Canada)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Internet site means the Internet site that is established under section 105. (site Internet)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: jurisdiction means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a federal authority;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any agency or body that is established under an Act of Parliament and that has powers, duties or functions in relation to an assessment of the environmental effects of a designated project;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the government of a province;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any agency or body that is established under an Act of the legislature of a province and that has powers, duties or functions in relation to an assessment of the environmental effects of a designated project;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) any body - including a co-management body - established under a land claim agreement referred to in section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 and that has powers, duties or functions in relation to an assessment of the environmental effects of a designated project;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) an Indigenous governing body that has powers, duties or functions in relation to an assessment of the environmental effects of a designated project

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) under a land claim agreement referred to in section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) under an Act of Parliament other than this Act or under an Act of the legislature of a province, including a law that implements a self-government agreement;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) an Indigenous governing body that has entered into an agreement or arrangement referred to in paragraph 114(1)(e);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) a government of a foreign state or of a subdivision of a foreign state, or any institution of such a government; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) an international organization of states or any institution of such an organization. (instance)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: mitigation measures means measures to eliminate, reduce, control or offset adverse effects within federal jurisdiction, direct or incidental adverse effects or adverse environmental effects, as defined in section 81, and includes restitution for any damage caused by those effects through replacement, restoration, compensation or any other means. (mesures d'attenuation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed means prescribed by the regulations. (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: proponent means the person or entity - federal authority, government or body - that proposes the carrying out of, or carries out, a designated project. (promoteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: record includes any correspondence, memorandum, book, plan, map, drawing, diagram, pictorial or graphic work, photograph, film, microform, sound recording, videotape and machine readable record, and any other documentary material, regardless of physical form or characteristics, and any copy of it. (document)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Registry means the Canadian Impact Assessment Registry established under section 104. (registre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: review panel means a review panel established

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) under section 41;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) under subsection 44(1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) under subsection 47(1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) under an agreement or arrangement entered into under subsection 39(1) or (3); or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) by document referred to in subsection 40(2). (commission)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sustainability means the ability to protect the environment, contribute to the social and economic well-being of the people of Canada and preserve their health in a manner that benefits present and future generations. (durabilite)

heading: Non-application
paragraph: 4 This Act does not apply in respect of physical activities to be carried out wholly within lands described in Schedule 2.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 5 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Purpose
paragraph: 6 (1) The purpose of this Act is to prevent or mitigate significant adverse effects within federal jurisdiction - and significant direct or incidental adverse effects - that may be caused by the carrying out of designated projects, as well as significant adverse environmental effects, as defined in section 81, that may be caused by the carrying out of projects, as defined in that section, by establishing processes to anticipate, identify and assess the potential effects of those projects in order to inform decision making under this or any other Act of Parliament in respect of those effects.

heading: Mandate
paragraph: (2) The Government of Canada, the Minister, the Agency and federal authorities, in the administration of this Act, must exercise their powers in a manner that fosters sustainability, respects the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Canada recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982, takes into account Indigenous knowledge, considers the cumulative effects of physical activities, applies the precautionary principle and promotes cooperation among jurisdictions and with the Indigenous peoples of Canada.

heading: Application of principles to powers
paragraph: (3) The Government of Canada, the Minister, the Agency and federal authorities must, in the administration of this Act, exercise their powers in a manner that

heading: Application of principles to powers
paragraph: (a) ensures that processes referred to in subsection (1) are fair, predictable and efficient; and

heading: Application of principles to powers
paragraph: (b) adheres to the principles of scientific integrity, honesty, objectivity, thoroughness and accuracy.

heading: Proponent
paragraph: 7 (1) Subject to subsection (3), the proponent of a designated project must not do any act or thing in connection with the carrying out of the designated project, in whole or in part, if that act or thing may cause any adverse effects within federal jurisdiction.

heading: Schedule 3
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, by order, amend Schedule 3 to add or remove a component of the environment or a health, social or economic matter.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (3) The proponent of a designated project may do an act or thing in connection with the carrying out of the designated project, in whole or in part, that may cause adverse effects within federal jurisdiction if

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (a) the Agency makes a decision under subsection 16(1) that no impact assessment of the designated project is required and posts that decision on the Internet site;

heading: Conditions
