paragraph: (2) The Minister must, based on any determination made by the Minister under subsection 60(1) or any determination made by the Governor in Council under section 62, as the case may be, establish in relation to the direct or incidental adverse effects that are indicated in the report any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate and that are directly linked or necessarily incidental to the exercise of a power or performance of a duty or function by a federal authority that would permit the designated project to be carried out, in whole or in part, or to the provision of financial assistance by a federal authority to a person for the purpose of enabling the carrying out, in whole or in part, of that project. The proponent of the designated project must comply with those conditions.

heading: Conditions subject to exercise of power or performance of duty or function
paragraph: (3) The conditions referred to in subsection (2) take effect only if the federal authority exercises the power or performs the duty or function or provides the financial assistance.

heading: Mitigation measures and follow-up program
paragraph: (4) The conditions referred to in subsections (1) and (2) must include

heading: Mitigation measures and follow-up program
paragraph: (a) the implementation of the mitigation measures that the Minister takes into account in making any determination under subsection 60(1), or that the Governor in Council takes into account in making any determination under section 62, other than those the implementation of which the Minister is satisfied will be ensured by another person or by a jurisdiction; and

heading: Mitigation measures and follow-up program
paragraph: (b) the implementation of a follow-up program and, if the Minister considers it appropriate, an adaptive management plan.

heading: Decision statement issued to proponent
paragraph: 65 (1) The Minister must issue a decision statement to the proponent of a designated project that

heading: Decision statement issued to proponent
paragraph: (a) informs the proponent of any determination made under subsection 60(1) or section 62 in relation to that project and the reasons for the determination;

heading: Decision statement issued to proponent
paragraph: (b) includes any conditions that are established under section 64 in relation to the designated project and that must be complied with by the proponent;

heading: Decision statement issued to proponent
paragraph: (c) sets out the period established under subsection 70(1); and

heading: Decision statement issued to proponent
paragraph: (d) includes a description of the designated project.

heading: Detailed reasons
paragraph: (2) The reasons for the determination must demonstrate that the Minister or the Governor in Council, as the case may be, based the determination on the report with respect to the impact assessment of the designated project and considered each of the factors referred to in section 63.

heading: Time limit - Minister's determination
paragraph: (3) The Minister must issue the decision statement no later than 30 days after the day on which the report with respect to the impact assessment of the designated project, or a summary of that report, is posted on the Internet site if the Minister

heading: Time limit - Minister's determination
paragraph: (a) makes a determination under paragraph 60(1)(a) that the adverse effects within federal jurisdiction - and the direct or incidental adverse effects - that are indicated in the report are not likely to be, to some extent, significant; or

heading: Time limit - Minister's determination
paragraph: (b) makes a determination under paragraph 60(1)(b).

heading: Time limit - Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (4) If the Governor in Council makes a determination under paragraph 62(a) that the adverse effects within federal jurisdiction - and the direct or incidental adverse effects - that are indicated in the report are not likely to be, to some extent, significant or makes a determination under paragraph 62(b), the Minister must issue the decision statement no later than 90 days after

heading: Time limit - Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (a) the day on which the report with respect to the impact assessment of the designated project, or a summary of that report, is posted on the Internet site, if the report is submitted to the Minister under subsection 28(2) or section 59 or at the end of the assessment under the process approved under section 31; or

heading: Time limit - Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (b) the day on which the Agency posts its recommendations on the Internet site under subsection 55.1(2), if the recommendations are in respect of a designated project that is the subject of a report received by the Minister under section 55.

heading: Extension of time limit by Minister
paragraph: (5) The Minister may extend the time limit referred to in subsection (3) or (4) by any period - up to a maximum of 90 days - that is necessary to take into account circumstances that are specific to the designated project or to facilitate cooperation with a jurisdiction referred to in section 21.

heading: Extension of time limit by Governor in Council
paragraph: (6) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, extend the time limit extended under subsection (5) by any period that is necessary to take into account circumstances that are specific to the designated project or to facilitate cooperation with a jurisdiction referred to in section 21.

heading: Proponent informed of extension
paragraph: (7) The Minister must inform the proponent in writing of any extension granted under this section and the reasons for granting it and ensure that a notice of the extension and the reasons for granting it are posted on the Internet site.

heading: Posting of decision statement on Internet site
paragraph: 66 The Agency must post on the Internet site any decision statement that the Minister issues under section 65.

heading: Decision statement considered to be part of licence under Nuclear Safety and Control Act
paragraph: 67 (1) The Minister may, in a decision statement issued in relation to a designated project that includes activities that are regulated under the Nuclear Safety and Control Act, designate any condition that is included in the decision statement, and any condition designated by the Minister is considered to be a part of the licence issued under section 24 of that Act in relation to the designated project.

heading: Decision statement considered part of certificate, etc., under Canadian Energy Regulator Act
paragraph: (2) A decision statement issued in relation to a designated project that includes activities that are regulated under the Canadian Energy Regulator Act is considered to be a part of the certificate, order, permit, licence or authorization issued, the leave or exemption granted or the direction or approval given under that Act in relation to the designated project.

heading: Decision statement considered to be part of authorization, etc., under Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act
paragraph: (3) A decision statement issued in relation to a designated project that includes activities that are regulated under the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act is considered to be a part of the authorization or licence issued, the approval granted or the leave given under that Act in relation to the designated project.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3.1) Sections 120 to 152 do not apply to the administration or enforcement of this Act as it relates to a condition of a decision statement that is issued in relation to a designated project that includes activities that are regulated, as applicable, under the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Act or the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation and Offshore Renewable Energy Management Act if the condition is a requirement of an authorization issued under the Act in question in relation to that designated project.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (4) Sections 120 to 152 do not apply to the administration or enforcement of this Act as it relates to any condition that is considered to be a part of a licence and any decision statement that is considered to be a part of a licence, certificate, order, permit, authorization, leave, exemption, direction or approval.

heading: Minister's power - decision statement
paragraph: 68 (1) The Minister may amend a decision statement, including to add or remove a condition, to amend any condition or to modify the designated project's description. However, the Minister is not permitted to amend the decision statement to change the decision included in it.

heading: Limitation - condition
paragraph: (2) The Minister may add, remove or amend a condition only if he or she is of the opinion that doing so will not increase the extent to which the effects that are indicated in the report with respect to the impact assessment of the designated project are adverse.

heading: Limitation and application
paragraph: (3) The Minister may add or amend a condition only if the new or amended condition could be established under subsection 64(1) or (2). Subsection 64(3) applies with respect to the new or amended condition if it could be established under subsection 64(2).

heading: Limitation - Nuclear Safety and Control Act
paragraph: (4) The Minister is not permitted to amend or remove a condition designated under subsection 67(1) and is not permitted to designate, under that subsection, any condition added under this section.

heading: Public notice - amendment to decision statement
paragraph: 69 (1) If the Minister intends to amend a decision statement under section 68, the Minister must ensure that the following are posted on the Internet site:

heading: Public notice - amendment to decision statement
paragraph: (a) a draft of the amended decision statement; and

heading: Public notice - amendment to decision statement
paragraph: (b) a notice that invites the public to provide comments on the draft within the period specified.

heading: Posting of amended decision statement on Internet site
paragraph: (2) If, after taking into account any comments received from the public, the Minister decides to amend the decision statement, he or she must ensure that the amended decision statement and his or her reasons for amending the decision statement are posted on the Internet site.

heading: Minister's obligation
paragraph: 70 (1) The Minister must, after considering any views provided by the proponent on the matter, establish the period within which the proponent must substantially begin to carry out the designated project.

heading: Extension
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, after considering any views provided by the proponent on the matter, extend the period by any period that the Minister considers reasonable and, in that case, must ensure that a notice of the extension and the reasons for the extension are posted on the Internet site.

heading: Expiry of decision statement
paragraph: (3) If the proponent does not substantially begin to carry out the designated project within the period established by the Minister, or any extension of that period, the decision statement expires on the expiry of that period or any extension of that period.

heading: Notice posted on Internet site
paragraph: (4) The Agency must post on the Internet site a notice that a decision statement has expired.

heading: Revocation of decision statement
paragraph: 71 If the proponent of a designated project advises the Minister in writing that the designated project will not - or will no longer - be carried out, the Minister may revoke the decision statement issued in respect of that project.

heading: Amending decision statement - information
paragraph: 72 (1) The Minister may, before amending a decision statement, require the proponent of the designated project described in the decision statement to provide the Minister with any information that he or she considers necessary for the purpose of amending the decision statement.

heading: Offer to consult
paragraph: (2) If the decision statement is considered to be a part of a licence, certificate, order, permit, authorization, leave, exemption, direction or approval referred to in section 67, the Minister must, before amending or revoking the decision statement, offer to consult with the entity that issues the certificate, order, permit, licence or authorization, grants the exemption, gives the direction or gives or grants the leave or approval, as the case may be.

heading: Offer to consult - Nuclear Safety and Control Act
paragraph: (3) Before the Minister amends any portion of a decision statement referred to in subsection 67(1) that is not considered to be part of a licence referred to in that subsection, or revokes such a decision statement, he or she must offer to consult with the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

heading: Termination by Agency or Minister
paragraph: 73 The Agency - or the Minister if the impact assessment of the designated project has been referred to a review panel - may terminate the impact assessment if the proponent advises the Agency or the Minister in writing that the designated project will not be carried out.

heading: No disclosure
paragraph: 74 Despite any other provision of this Act, no confidence of the Queen's Privy Council for Canada in respect of which subsection 39(1) of the Canada Evidence Act applies is to be disclosed or made available under this Act to any person.

heading: Agency's obligation
paragraph: 75 (1) The Agency must establish a participant funding program to facilitate the participation of the public in

heading: Agency's obligation
paragraph: (a) the Agency's preparations for a possible impact assessment of - or the impact assessment of and the design or implementation of follow-up programs in relation to - designated projects that include physical activities that are designated by regulations made under paragraph 112(1)(e) or that are part of a class of activities designated by those regulations;

heading: Agency's obligation
paragraph: (b) the impact assessment of, and the design or implementation of follow-up programs in relation to, designated projects that are referred to a review panel and that do not include physical activities that are designated by regulations made under paragraph 112(1)(e) or that are not part of a class of activities designated by those regulations; and

heading: Agency's obligation
paragraph: (c) regional assessments and strategic assessments.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) The obligation does not apply with respect to any designated project for which the Minister has approved the substitution of a process under section 31.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 76 (1) The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) providing for fees, charges or levies that are payable for the purpose of recovering all or a portion of any costs incurred by the Agency or a review panel in relation to the exercise of its powers or the performance of its duties and functions; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) providing for the manner of calculating those fees, charges or levies and their payment to the Agency.

heading: Proponent's obligation to pay costs
paragraph: (2) If the Agency or a review panel incurs a cost in relation to the exercise of its powers or the performance of its duties and functions in respect of which no fee, charge or levy is provided for under subsection (1), the proponent of the designated project in respect of which the power is exercised or the duty or function is performed must pay to the Agency

heading: Proponent's obligation to pay costs
paragraph: (a) any costs that the Agency or review panel incurs for prescribed services provided by a third party in the exercise of that power or the performance of that duty or function; and

heading: Proponent's obligation to pay costs
paragraph: (b) any prescribed amount that is related to the exercise by the Agency or review panel of that power or the performance by it of that duty or function.

heading: Service Fees Act
paragraph: (3) The Service Fees Act does not apply to the fees, charges or levies referred to in subsection (1) or the prescribed amount referred to in paragraph (2)(b).

heading: Powers exercised, duties and functions performed during a given period
paragraph: 77 For the purposes of section 76, the powers, duties and functions are limited to those exercised or performed during the period that begins on the day on which the initial description of a designated project referred to in subsection 10(1) is received by the Agency and ends on the day on which the follow-up program in respect of the project is completed.

heading: Expenditure of fees, charges, etc.
paragraph: 78 The Agency may spend for any prescribed purpose the fees, charges, levies, costs and amounts referred to in section 76 in the fiscal year in which they are paid or, unless an appropriation Act provides otherwise, in the next fiscal year.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: 79 The fees, charges and levies that are payable, and the costs and amounts that the proponent must pay, under section 76 constitute a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Unpaid fees, charges, etc.
paragraph: 80 If a proponent does not pay a fee, charge, levy, cost or amount referred to in section 76 that they owe within 90 days after the day on which it is due,

heading: Unpaid fees, charges, etc.
paragraph: (a) the Agency is authorized, despite any other provision of this Act, to not exercise any of its powers or not perform any of its duties or functions in relation to an impact assessment of any designated project that the proponent proposes to carry out until the proponent pays the debt; or

heading: Unpaid fees, charges, etc.
paragraph: (b) the Minister may, if an impact assessment of any designated project that the proponent proposes to carry out has been referred to a review panel, make an order directing the review panel to, despite any other provision of this Act, not exercise any of its powers or not perform any of its duties or functions in relation to the impact assessment until the proponent pays the debt.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 81 The following definitions apply in this section and sections 82 to 91.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: authority means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a federal authority; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any other body that is set out in Schedule 4. (autorite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environmental effects means changes to the environment and the impact of these changes on the Indigenous peoples of Canada and on health, social or economic conditions. (effets environnementaux)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: project means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a physical activity that is carried out on federal lands or outside Canada in relation to a physical work and that is not a designated project or a physical activity designated by regulations made under paragraph 112(1)(a.2); and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a physical activity that is designated under section 87 or that is part of a class of physical activities that is designated under that section. (projet)

heading: Project carried out on federal lands
paragraph: 82 An authority must not carry out a project on federal lands, exercise any power or perform any duty or function conferred on it under any Act of Parliament other than this Act that could permit a project to be carried out, in whole or in part, on federal lands or provide financial assistance to any person for the purpose of enabling that project to be carried out, in whole or in part, on federal lands, unless

heading: Project carried out on federal lands
paragraph: (a) the authority determines that the carrying out of the project is not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects; or

heading: Project carried out on federal lands
paragraph: (b) the authority determines that the carrying out of the project is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects and the Governor in Council decides, under subsection 90(3), that those effects are justified in the circumstances.

heading: Project outside Canada
paragraph: 83 A federal authority must not carry out a project outside Canada, or provide financial assistance to any person for the purpose of enabling that project to be carried out, in whole or in part, outside Canada, unless

heading: Project outside Canada
paragraph: (a) the federal authority determines that the carrying out of the project is not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects; or

heading: Project outside Canada
paragraph: (b) the federal authority determines that the carrying out of the project is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects and the Governor in Council decides, under subsection 90(3), that those effects are justified in the circumstances.

heading: Factors
paragraph: 84 (1) An authority's determination regarding whether the carrying out of the project is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects must be based on a consideration of the following factors:

heading: Factors
paragraph: (a) any adverse impact that the project may have on the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Canada recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (b) Indigenous knowledge provided with respect to the project;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (c) community knowledge provided with respect to the project;

heading: Factors
paragraph: (d) comments received from the public under subsection 86(1); and

heading: Factors
paragraph: (e) the mitigation measures that are technically and economically feasible and that would mitigate any significant adverse environmental effects of the project that the authority is satisfied will be implemented.

heading: Factors - project outside Canada
paragraph: (2) However, if the project is to be carried out outside Canada, the authority's determination need not include a consideration of the factors set out in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b).

heading: Federal authority's obligation
paragraph: 85 Every federal authority that is in possession of specialist or expert information or knowledge with respect to a project must, on an authority's request and within the period that it specifies, make that information or knowledge available to the authority.

heading: Notice posted on Internet site
paragraph: 86 (1) Before making a determination under section 82 or 83, an authority must post on the Internet site a notice that indicates that it intends to make such a determination and that invites the public to provide comments respecting that determination.

heading: Notice of determination posted on Internet site
paragraph: (2) No sooner than 30 days after the day on which it posts the notice referred to in subsection (1), the authority must post on the Internet site a notice of its determination, including any mitigation measures that it took into account in making the determination.

heading: Power to designate physical activities
paragraph: 87 The Minister may, by order, designate a physical activity, or a class of physical activities, carried out on federal lands or outside Canada that is not in relation to a physical work and is not a designated project, but that, in the Minister's opinion, may cause significant adverse environmental effects.

heading: Designation of class of projects
paragraph: 88 (1) The Minister may, by order, designate a class of projects if, in the Minister's opinion, the carrying out of a project that is a part of the class will cause only insignificant adverse environmental effects.

heading: Projects excluded
paragraph: (2) Sections 82 and 83 do not apply to an authority in respect of a project that is part of a class of projects that is designated under subsection (1).

heading: Notice inviting public comments
paragraph: 89 (1) If the Minister intends to designate a physical activity, or a class of physical activities, under section 87 or a class of projects under subsection 88(1), the Agency must post on the Internet site a notice that invites the public to provide comments respecting the designation within 30 days after the day on which the notice is posted.

heading: Minister must consider public comments
paragraph: (2) The Minister must consider any comments received from the public in deciding whether to make the designation.

heading: Posting notice on Internet site
paragraph: (3) If the Minister designates a physical activity, or a class of physical activities, under section 87 or a class of projects under subsection 88(1), the Agency must post on the Internet site a notice that includes a description of the physical activity, the class of physical activities or the class of projects, as the case may be, and the Minister's reasons for making the designation.

heading: Referral to Governor in Council
paragraph: 90 (1) If the authority determines that the carrying out of a project on federal lands or outside Canada is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects, the authority may refer to the Governor in Council the matter of whether those effects are justified in the circumstances.

heading: Referral through Minister
paragraph: (2) When the determination is made by an authority other than a federal Minister, then the referral to the Governor in Council is made through the Minister responsible before Parliament for that authority.

heading: Governor in Council's decision
paragraph: (3) When a matter has been referred to the Governor in Council, the Governor in Council must decide whether the significant adverse environmental effects are justified in the circumstances and must inform the authority of its decision.

heading: Non-application - national emergency or emergency
paragraph: 91 Sections 82 and 83 do not apply to an authority in respect of a project

heading: Non-application - national emergency or emergency
paragraph: (a) in relation to which there are matters of national security;

heading: Non-application - national emergency or emergency
paragraph: (b) that is to be carried out in response to a national emergency for which special temporary measures are being taken under the Emergencies Act; or

heading: Non-application - national emergency or emergency
paragraph: (c) that is to be carried out in response to an emergency, and the carrying out of the project without delay is in the interest of preventing damage to property or the environment or is in the interest of public health or safety.

heading: Regional assessments - region entirely on federal lands
paragraph: 92 The Minister may establish a committee - or authorize the Agency - to conduct a regional assessment of the effects of existing or future physical activities carried out in a region that is entirely on federal lands.

heading: Regional assessments - other regions
paragraph: 93 (1) If the Minister is of the opinion that it is appropriate to conduct a regional assessment of the effects of existing or future physical activities carried out in a region that is composed in part of federal lands or in a region that is entirely outside federal lands,

heading: Regional assessments - other regions
paragraph: (a) the Minister may

heading: Regional assessments - other regions
paragraph: (i) enter into an agreement or arrangement with any jurisdiction referred to in paragraphs (a) to (g) of the definition jurisdiction in section 2 respecting the joint establishment of a committee to conduct the assessment and the manner in which the assessment is to be conducted, or

heading: Regional assessments - other regions
paragraph: (ii) authorize the Agency to conduct the assessment; and

heading: Regional assessments - other regions
paragraph: (b) the Minister and the Minister of Foreign Affairs may enter into an agreement or arrangement with any jurisdiction referred to in paragraph (h) or (i) of that definition respecting the joint establishment of a committee to conduct the assessment and the manner in which the assessment is to be conducted.

heading: Committee - foreign state or international organization of states
paragraph: (2) If an agreement or arrangement referred to in paragraph (1)(b) is entered into, the Minister must establish - or approve - the committee's terms of reference and appoint as a member of the committee one or more persons, or approve their appointment.

heading: Committee - federal authority, etc.
paragraph: (3) In respect of an agreement or arrangement entered into under subparagraph (1)(a)(i), the Minister must

heading: Committee - federal authority, etc.
paragraph: (a) establish or approve the committee's terms of reference, including a specified time limit within which the assessment must be completed; and

heading: Committee - federal authority, etc.
paragraph: (b) appoint or approve the appointment of the members of the committee, of which at least one person must have been recommended by the jurisdiction with which the agreement or arrangement was entered into.

heading: Agency's obligation to offer to consult
paragraph: 94 If the Agency conducts an assessment referred to in subsection 92 or 93, it must offer to consult and cooperate with any jurisdiction referred to in paragraphs (a) to (g) of the definition jurisdiction in section 2 that has powers, duties or functions in relation to the physical activities in respect of which the assessment is conducted.

heading: Assessments
paragraph: 95 (1) The Minister may establish a committee - or authorize the Agency - to conduct an assessment of

heading: Assessments
paragraph: (a) any Government of Canada policy, plan or program - proposed or existing - that is relevant to conducting impact assessments; or

heading: Assessments
paragraph: (b) any issue that is relevant to conducting impact assessments of designated projects or of a class of designated projects.

heading: Minister's power
paragraph: (2) The Minister may deem any assessment that provides guidance on how Canada's commitments in respect of climate change should be considered in impact assessments and that is prepared by a federal authority and commenced before the day on which this Act comes into force to be an assessment conducted under this section.

heading: Committee's mandate and appointment of members
paragraph: 96 (1) If the Minister establishes a committee under section 92 or 95, he or she must establish its terms of reference and appoint as a member of the committee one or more persons.

heading: Agency's mandate
paragraph: (2) If the Minister authorizes the Agency to conduct an assessment under section 92, subsection 93(1) or section 95, he or she must establish the Agency's terms of reference with respect to the assessment.

heading: Minister's obligations - request for assessment
paragraph: 97 (1) The Minister must respond, with reasons and within the prescribed time limit, to any request that an assessment referred to in section 92, 93 or 95 be conducted. The Minister must ensure that his or her response is posted on the Internet site.

heading: Committee's or Agency's obligation
paragraph: (2) When conducting an assessment referred to in section 92, 93 or 95, the Agency or committee, as the case may be, must take into account any scientific information and Indigenous knowledge - including the knowledge of Indigenous women - provided with respect to the assessment.

heading: Information available to public
paragraph: 98 Subject to section 119, the Agency, or the committee, must ensure that the information that it uses when conducting an assessment referred to in section 92, 93 or 95 is made available to the public.

heading: Public participation
paragraph: 99 The Agency, or the committee, must ensure that the public is provided with an opportunity to participate meaningfully, in a manner that the Agency or committee, as the case may be, considers appropriate, in any assessment referred to in section 92, 93 or 95 that it conducts.

heading: Federal authority's obligation
paragraph: 100 Every federal authority that is in possession of specialist or expert information or knowledge with respect to the physical activities in respect of which an assessment referred to in section 92 or 93 is conducted - or with respect to any policy, plan, program or issue in respect of which an assessment referred to in section 95 is conducted - must, on request, make that information or knowledge available to the committee or Agency that conducts the assessment within the specified period.

heading: Application of section 53
paragraph: 101 Section 53 applies, with any necessary modifications, to a committee established under section 92 or 95 or under an agreement or arrangement entered into under subparagraph 93(1)(a)(i) or paragraph 93(1)(b) and, for the purpose of applying section 53 to a committee, a reference in that section to a review panel is a reference to a committee.

heading: Report to Minister
paragraph: 102 (1) On completion of the assessment that it conducts, the committee established under section 92 or 95 or under an agreement or arrangement entered into under subparagraph 93(1)(a)(i) or paragraph 93(1)(b) or the Agency, as the case may be, must provide a report to the Minister.

heading: Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 119, the report must set out how the Agency or committee, as the case may be, took into account and used any Indigenous knowledge provided with respect to the assessment.

heading: Copy of report posted on Internet site
paragraph: 103 The Agency must post a copy of the report on the Internet site.

heading: Canadian Impact Assessment Registry
paragraph: 104 (1) There is to be a registry called the Canadian Impact Assessment Registry, consisting of an Internet site and project files.

heading: Right of access
paragraph: (2) The Registry must be operated in a manner that ensures convenient public access to it. That right of access to the Registry is in addition to any right of access provided under any other Act of Parliament.

heading: Copy
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of facilitating public access to records included in the Registry, the Agency must ensure that a copy of any of those records is provided in a timely manner on request.

heading: Establishment and maintenance
paragraph: 105 (1) The Agency must establish and maintain an Internet site that is available to the public.

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (2) The Agency must ensure that the following records and information relating to the impact assessment of the designated project that it conducts are posted and, subject to paragraph (4)(c), maintained on the Internet site:

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (a) any public notice that is issued by the Agency to request the participation of the public in the impact assessment;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (b) a description of the factors to be taken into account in the impact assessment and of the scope of those factors;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (c) the report with respect to the impact assessment that is taken into account by the Minister under subsection 60(1) or (1.1), or a summary of the report and an indication of how a copy of the report may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (d) any scientific information that the Agency receives from a proponent or federal authority, or a summary of the scientific information and an indication of how that information may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (e) a description of the results of the follow-up program that is implemented with respect to that designated project or a summary of the results and an indication of how such a description may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (f) notice of the Agency's decision to terminate the impact assessment under section 73;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (g) any other information that the Agency considers appropriate, including information in the form of a list of relevant records and an indication of how a copy of them may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (g.1) any public comments received during the impact assessment; and

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by Agency
paragraph: (h) any other record or information prescribed by regulations made under paragraph 112(1)(f).

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (3) The Agency must ensure that, in the case of an assessment conducted by a review panel or an impact assessment completed under section 59, the following records or information are posted and, subject to paragraph (4)(c), maintained on the Internet site:

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (a) the review panel's terms of reference;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (b) any public notice that is issued by the review panel to request the participation of the public in an impact assessment;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (c) the report with respect to the review panel's impact assessment referred to in section 55 or the impact assessment completed under section 59, or a summary of the report and an indication of how a copy of the report may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (d) any scientific information that the Agency or the review panel receives from a proponent or federal authority, or a summary of the scientific information and an indication of how that information may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (e) a description of the results of the follow-up program that is implemented with respect to that designated project or a summary of the results and an indication of how such a description may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (f) notice of the termination of an assessment by the review panel under section 58;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (g) notice of the Minister's decision to terminate an impact assessment under section 73;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (h) any other information that the Agency considers appropriate, including information in the form of a list of relevant documents and an indication of how a copy of them may be obtained;

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (h.1) any public comments received in the course of the impact assessment; and

heading: Contents - assessment conducted by review panel
paragraph: (i) any other record or information prescribed by regulations made under paragraph 112(1)(f).

heading: Management of Internet site
paragraph: (4) The Agency must determine

heading: Management of Internet site
paragraph: (a) what the form of the Internet site is to be and how it is to be kept;

heading: Management of Internet site
paragraph: (b) what information must be contained in any record required to be posted on the Internet site under this Act; and

heading: Management of Internet site
paragraph: (c) when information may be removed from the Internet site.

heading: Establishment and maintenance
paragraph: 106 (1) Subject to subsection (2), in respect of every designated project, a project file must be established by the Agency on the day on which the notice referred to in subsection 10(1) in respect of the designated project is posted on the Internet site and maintained until the day on which any follow-up program in respect of that designated project is completed.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) The obligation set out in subsection (1) ends on the earliest of the following days:

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) the day on which the Agency under subsection 16(1) decides that an impact assessment in respect of the designated project is not required;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the day on which the impact assessment in respect of the designated project is terminated under subsection 20(1) or section 73;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) the day on which the Minister issues a decision statement that informs the proponent of the designated project of the Minister's, or the Governor in Council's, determination that the effects referred to in paragraph 60(1)(a) or 62(a), as the case may be, that are likely to be, to some extent, significant are not justified in the public interest; and

heading: Contents of project file
paragraph: (3) A project file must contain all records produced, collected or received in relation to the Agency's preparations for a possible impact assessment of a designated project and in relation to the impact assessment of that designated project, including

heading: Contents of project file
paragraph: (a) all records posted on the Internet site;

heading: Contents of project file
paragraph: (b) any report relating to the impact assessment;

heading: Contents of project file
paragraph: (c) any comments that are received from the public in relation to the Agency's preparations for a possible impact assessment and in relation to the impact assessment;

heading: Contents of project file
paragraph: (d) any records relating to the design or implementation of any follow-up program; and

heading: Contents of project file
paragraph: (e) any records relating to the implementation of any mitigation measures.

heading: Categories of available information
paragraph: 107 (1) Despite any other provision of this Act, the Registry is to contain a record, part of a record or information only if

heading: Categories of available information
paragraph: (a) it has otherwise been made publicly available; or

heading: Categories of available information
paragraph: (b) the Minister determines

heading: Categories of available information
paragraph: (i) that it would have been disclosed to the public in accordance with the Access to Information Act if a request had been made in respect of that record under that Act at the time the record came under the control of the Agency, including any record that would be disclosed in the public interest under subsection 20(6) of that Act, or

heading: Categories of available information
paragraph: (ii) that there are reasonable grounds to believe that it would be in the public interest to disclose it because it is required for the public to participate effectively in the Agency's preparations for a possible impact assessment or the impact assessment - other than any record the disclosure of which would be prohibited under section 20 of the Access to Information Act.

heading: Applicability of sections 27, 28 and 44 of Access to Information Act
paragraph: (2) Sections 27, 28 and 44 of the Access to Information Act apply to any information described in subsection 27(1) of that Act that the Agency intends to be included in the Registry with any necessary modifications, including the following:

heading: Applicability of sections 27, 28 and 44 of Access to Information Act
paragraph: (a) the information is deemed to be a record that the head of a government institution intends to disclose; and

heading: Applicability of sections 27, 28 and 44 of Access to Information Act
paragraph: (b) any reference to the person who requested access must be disregarded.

heading: Protection from civil proceeding or prosecution
paragraph: 108 Despite any other Act of Parliament, no civil or criminal proceedings lie against the Agency or the Minister - or any person acting on behalf of, or under the direction of, either of them - and no proceedings lie against the Crown or the Agency, for the disclosure in good faith of any record or any part of a record or any Indigenous knowledge under this Act or for any consequences that flow from that disclosure or for the failure to give any notice required under section 27 or 28 of the Access to Information Act if reasonable care is taken to give the required notice.

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: 109 The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (a) amending Schedule 1 or 4 by adding or deleting a body or a class of bodies;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of the definition designated project in section 2, designating a physical activity - or class of physical activities - the carrying out of which may, in the Governor in Council's opinion, cause adverse effects within federal jurisdiction or direct or incidental adverse effects and specifying which physical activity or class of physical activities may be designated by the Minister under paragraph 112(1)(a.2);

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (c) exempting any class of proponents or class of designated projects from the application of section 76;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (d) varying or excluding any requirement set out in this Act or the regulations as it applies to physical activities to be carried out

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (i) on reserves, surrendered lands or other lands that are vested in Her Majesty and subject to the Indian Act,

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (ii) on lands covered by land claim agreements referred to in section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982,

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (iii) on lands with respect to which agreements or arrangements referred to in paragraph 114(1)(d) or (e) apply,

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (iv) under international agreements or arrangements entered into by the Government of Canada, or

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (v) in relation to which there are matters of national security;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (e) respecting agreements or arrangements referred to in paragraph 114(1)(d) or (e);

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (f) prescribing - other than the time limit referred to in subsection 97(1) - anything that, by this Act, is to be prescribed;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (g) prescribing the way in which anything that is required or authorized by this Act to be prescribed is to be determined; and

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (h) generally, for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act.

heading: Amendment of Schedule 2
paragraph: 110 The Governor in Council may, by order, amend Schedule 2 by adding, replacing or deleting a description of lands that are subject to a land claim agreement referred to in section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Review of regulations
paragraph: 111 (1) The Agency must review, within the prescribed period, any regulations made under paragraph 109(b).

heading: Report
paragraph: (2) After completing its review the Agency must submit to the Minister a report setting out its conclusions and recommendations.

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: 112 (1) The Minister may make regulations

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (a) prescribing the information that must be contained in the description referred to in subsection 10(1) or 15(1.1) and the documents referred to in paragraph 18(1)(b);

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (a.1) respecting the form and format of a description referred to in subsection 10(1), of a notice referred to in subsection 15(1) and of any information or study provided under this Act and the manner of providing the description, notice, information or study;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (a.2) designating, for the purposes of section 112.1, a physical activity or class of physical activities from among those specified by the Governor in Council under paragraph 109(b), establishing the conditions that must be met for the purposes of the designation and setting out the information that a person or entity - federal authority, government or body - that is referred to in subsection (3) must provide the Agency in respect of the physical activity that they propose to carry out;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (a.3) respecting the procedures and requirements relating to assessments referred to in section 92, 93 or 95;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (b) respecting the procedures, requirements and time periods relating to impact assessments, including the manner of designing a follow-up program;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (c) prescribing, for the purposes of any of subsections 9(5), 18(6), 28(9), 36(3) and 37(6), any activity in respect of which a time limit may be suspended and respecting circumstances, in relation to an activity, in which a time limit may be suspended;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (d) respecting a participant funding program established under section 75;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (e) designating, for the purposes of section 75, a physical activity or class of physical activities;

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (e.1) prescribing the time limit referred to in subsection 97(1);

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (f) respecting the Registry, including the identification of records or information to be posted on the Internet site and the establishment and maintenance of project files referred to in section 106; and

heading: Regulations - Minister
paragraph: (g) respecting the charging of fees for providing copies of documents contained in the Registry.

heading: Condition
paragraph: (2) The Minister may make a regulation designating a physical activity or class of physical activities under paragraph (1)(a.2) only after considering an assessment referred to in section 92 or 93 that is in relation to that physical activity or class of physical activities.

heading: Written notice
paragraph: (3) A person or entity - federal authority, government or body - that proposes the carrying out of a physical activity that is designated by the Minister under paragraph 112(1)(a.2) or that is part of a class of physical activities that is designated by the Minister under that paragraph must notify the Agency in writing that they propose to do so.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (4) The Statutory Instruments Act does not apply to a regulation made under paragraph 112(1)(a.2).

heading: Regulation posted on Internet site
paragraph: (5) The Agency must post any regulation made under paragraph 112(1)(a.2) on the Internet site.

heading: Physical activity excluded
paragraph: 112.1 A physical activity or class of physical activities that is designated by the Minister under paragraph 112(1)(a.2) is excluded from the physical activities or class of physical activities that is designated by the Governor in Council under paragraph 109(b) if it meets the conditions established by the Minister.

heading: Externally produced documents
paragraph: 113 (1) A regulation made under this Act may incorporate by reference documents that are produced by a person or body other than the Agency, including a federal authority referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (d) of the definition federal authority in section 2.

heading: Ambulatory incorporation by reference
paragraph: (2) A document may be incorporated by reference either as it exists on a particular date or as amended from time to time.

heading: Accessibility of incorporated document
paragraph: (3) The Minister must ensure that any document incorporated by reference in a regulation is accessible.

heading: No registration or publication
paragraph: (4) For greater certainty, a document that is incorporated by reference into a regulation is not required to be transmitted for registration or published in the Canada Gazette by reason only that it is incorporated by reference.

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: 114 (1) For the purposes of this Act, the Minister may

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (a) issue guidelines and codes of practice respecting the application of this Act;

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (b) establish research and advisory bodies in the area of impact assessment, including with respect to the interests and concerns of Indigenous peoples of Canada, and appoint as a member of any such bodies one or more persons;

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (c) enter into agreements or arrangements with any jurisdiction referred to in paragraphs (a) to (g) of the definition jurisdiction in section 2 respecting assessments of effects;

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (d) if authorized by the regulations, enter into agreements or arrangements with any jurisdiction referred to in paragraph (e) or (f) of the definition jurisdiction in section 2 to

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (i) authorize the jurisdiction, on lands with respect to which it already has powers, duties or functions in relation to an assessment of the environmental effects of a designated project, to exercise powers or perform duties or functions in relation to impact assessments under this Act - except for those set out in section 16 - that are specified in the agreement or arrangement, or

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (ii) in relation to lands, specified in the agreement or arrangement, with respect to which it does not already have powers, duties or functions in relation to an assessment of the environmental effects of a designated project,

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (A) provide that the jurisdiction is considered to be a jurisdiction for the application of this Act on those lands, and

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (B) authorize the jurisdiction, on those lands, to exercise powers or perform duties or functions in relation to impact assessments under this Act - except for those set out in section 16 - that are specified in the agreement or arrangement;

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (e) if authorized by the regulations, enter into agreements or arrangements with any Indigenous governing body not referred to in paragraph (f) of the definition jurisdiction in section 2 to

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (i) provide that the Indigenous governing body is considered to be a jurisdiction for the application of this Act on the lands specified in the agreement or arrangement, and

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (ii) authorize the Indigenous governing body, with respect to those lands, to exercise powers or perform duties or functions in relation to impact assessments under this Act - except for those set out in section 16 - that are specified in the agreement or arrangement;

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (f) enter into agreements or arrangements with any jurisdiction for the purposes of coordination, consultation, exchange of information and the determination of factors to be considered in relation to the assessment of the effects of designated projects of common interest;

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (g) establish criteria for the appointment of members of review panels; and

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (h) establish criteria for the appointment of members of committees established under section 92 or 93.

heading: International agreements and arrangements
paragraph: (2) The Minister and the Minister of Foreign Affairs may enter into agreements or arrangements with any jurisdiction referred to in paragraphs (h) and (i) of the definition jurisdiction in section 2 respecting assessments of environmental effects, including for the purposes of implementing the provisions of any international agreement or arrangement respecting the assessment of environmental effects to which the Government of Canada is a party.

heading: Opportunity for public to comment
paragraph: (3) The Minister must provide reasonable public notice of and a reasonable opportunity for anyone to comment on draft guidelines, codes of practice, agreements, arrangements or criteria under this section.

heading: Availability to public
paragraph: (4) Any guidelines, codes of practice, agreements, arrangements or criteria must be made available to the public.

heading: Agreements or arrangements posted on Internet site
paragraph: (5) The Minister must ensure that an agreement or arrangement referred to in paragraph (1)(d) or (e) is posted on the Internet site.

heading: Non-application - national security
paragraph: 115 (1) The Governor in Council may, by order, exclude a designated project from the application of this Act if, in the Governor in Council's opinion, the designated project is one in relation to which there are matters of national security.

heading: Non-application - national emergency or emergency
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, by order, exclude a designated project from the application of this Act if, in the Minister's opinion, the designated project is one to be carried out in response to

heading: Non-application - national emergency or emergency
paragraph: (a) a national emergency for which special temporary measures are being taken under the Emergencies Act; or

heading: Non-application - national emergency or emergency
paragraph: (b) an emergency, and carrying out the designated project without delay is in the interest of preventing damage to property or the environment or is in the interest of public health or safety.

heading: Posting of notice of order on Internet site
paragraph: (3) The Agency must post on the Internet site a notice of any order made under subsection (2).

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: 116 An order made under subsection 9(1) or 115(1) or (2) is not a statutory instrument for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Advisory council to be established
paragraph: 117 (1) The Minister must establish an advisory council to advise him or her on issues related to the implementation of the impact assessment and regional and strategic assessment regimes set out under this Act.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: (2) The Minister must appoint members to the advisory council, including a chairperson.

heading: Membership
paragraph: (3) The membership of the council must include at least

heading: Membership
paragraph: (a) one person recommended by an Indigenous governing body or other entity that represents the interests of First Nations;

heading: Membership
paragraph: (b) one person recommended by an Indigenous governing body or other entity that represents the interests of the Inuit; and

heading: Membership
paragraph: (c) one person recommended by an Indigenous governing body or other entity that represents the interests of the Metis.

heading: Meetings
paragraph: 118 (1) The advisory council must meet at least once a year.

heading: First report
paragraph: (2) Within three months after the end of the fiscal year during which the first anniversary of the coming into force of this Act occurs, the advisory council must submit to the Minister a report setting out the advice it provided during the period beginning on the day on which this Act comes into force and ending on the day on which that fiscal year ends, including the advice with respect to regional and strategic assessments to be given priority.

heading: Subsequent reports
paragraph: (3) Within three months after the end of each period of two fiscal years not addressed by the previous report, the advisory council must provide to the Minister a report setting out the advice it provided during that period of two fiscal years, including the advice with respect to regional and strategic assessments to be given priority.

heading: Tabling of report
paragraph: (4) The Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of Parliament on any of the first 15 days on which that House is sitting after the Minister receives the report and then ensure the report is posted on the Internet site.

heading: Minister's comments
paragraph: (5) Within 90 days after the day on which he or she receives the report, the Minister must provide his or her comments on the report to the advisory council, including with respect to the advice the council provided about regional and strategic assessments, and then ensure they are posted on the Internet site.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: 119 (1) Any Indigenous knowledge that is provided to the Minister, the Agency, a committee referred to in section 92, 93 or 95 or a review panel under this Act in confidence is confidential and must not knowingly be, or be permitted to be, disclosed without written consent.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the Indigenous knowledge referred to in that subsection may be disclosed if

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) it is publicly available;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the disclosure is necessary for the purposes of procedural fairness and natural justice or for use in legal proceedings; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) the disclosure is authorized in the prescribed circumstances.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2.1) Before disclosing Indigenous knowledge under paragraph 2(b) for the purposes of procedural fairness and natural justice, the Minister, the Agency, the committee or the review panel, as the case may be, must consult the person or entity who provided the Indigenous knowledge and the person or entity to whom it is proposed to be disclosed about the scope of the proposed disclosure and potential conditions under subsection (3).

heading: Further disclosure
paragraph: (3) The Minister, the Agency, the committee or the review panel, as the case may be, may, having regard to the consultation referred to in subsection (2.1), impose conditions with respect to the disclosure of Indigenous knowledge by any person or entity to whom it is disclosed under paragraph (2)(b) for the purposes of procedural fairness and natural justice.

heading: Duty to comply
paragraph: (4) The person or entity referred to in subsection (3) must comply with any conditions imposed under that subsection.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 120 (1) The President of the Agency may designate persons or classes of persons as enforcement officers or analysts for the purposes of the administration and enforcement of this Act.

heading: Certificate
paragraph: (2) The President of the Agency must provide every person designated under subsection (1) with a certificate of designation. That person must, if so requested, produce the certificate to the occupant or person in charge of a place referred to in subsection 122(1).

heading: Immunity
paragraph: 121 No action or other proceeding of a civil nature lies against an enforcement officer or analyst in respect of anything that is done or omitted to be done in good faith while exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under this Act.

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: 122 (1) An enforcement officer may, for the purpose of verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Act, including an injunction ordered under section 140, enter a place in which they have reasonable grounds to believe a designated project is or was being carried out or a record or anything relating to a designated project is located.

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (2) The enforcement officer may, for those purposes,

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (a) examine anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (b) use any means of communication in the place or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (c) use any computer system in the place, or cause it to be used, to examine data contained in or available to it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (d) prepare a document, or cause one to be prepared, based on the data;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (e) use any copying equipment in the place, or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (f) remove anything from the place for examination or copying;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (g) take photographs and make recordings or sketches;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (h) direct the owner or person in charge of the place or a person at the place to establish their identity to the enforcement officer's satisfaction or to stop or start an activity;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (i) direct the owner or a person having possession, care or control of anything in the place not to move it, or to restrict its movement, for as long as, in the enforcement officer's opinion, is necessary;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (j) direct any person to put any machinery, vehicle or equipment in the place into operation or to cease operating it; and

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (k) prohibit or limit access to all or part of the place.

heading: Person accompanying enforcement officer
paragraph: (3) An enforcement officer who enters a place under subsection (1) may be accompanied by any other person that they believe is necessary to help them exercise their powers and perform their duties and functions under this section.

heading: Analysts
paragraph: (4) An analyst who accompanies an enforcement officer may exercise any of the powers referred to in paragraphs (2)(a) to (g).

heading: Duty to assist
paragraph: (5) The owner or person in charge of the place and every person in the place must give all assistance that is reasonably required to enable the enforcement officer or analyst to exercise a power or perform a duty or function under this section and must provide any documents, data or information that are reasonably required for that purpose.

heading: Warrant for dwelling-house
paragraph: 123 (1) If the place is a dwelling-house, the enforcement officer may enter it without the occupant's consent only under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (2).

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (2) On ex parte application, a justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing an enforcement officer who is named in it to enter a dwelling-house, subject to any conditions specified in the warrant, and authorizing any analyst named in the warrant to accompany the enforcement officer, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) the dwelling-house is a place referred to in subsection 122(1);

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) entry to the dwelling-house is necessary for any of the purposes of that subsection; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (c) entry was refused by the occupant or there are reasonable grounds to believe that entry will be refused or that consent to entry cannot be obtained from the occupant.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (3) In executing a warrant to enter a dwelling-house, an enforcement officer or analyst may use force only if the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant and the enforcement officer or analyst is accompanied by a peace officer.

heading: Entry on private property
paragraph: 124 (1) For the purpose of gaining entry to a place referred to in subsection 122(1), an enforcement officer and analyst may enter private property and pass through it, and are not liable for doing so. For greater certainty, no person has a right to object to that use of the property and no warrant is required for the entry, unless the property is a dwelling-house.

heading: Person accompanying
paragraph: (2) A person may, at an enforcement officer or analyst's request, accompany them to assist them to gain entry to the place referred to in subsection 122(1) and is not liable for doing so.

heading: Production of documents
paragraph: 125 (1) An enforcement officer may, for the purpose of verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Act, including an injunction ordered under section 140, require any person to produce at a place specified by the enforcement officer, within any reasonable time and in the manner specified, any books, records, electronic data or other documents that the enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds contain any information relevant to the administration of this Act.

heading: Proof of delivery
paragraph: (2) The enforcement officer must make the request by a means that provides a record of delivery.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (3) Any person who is required to produce anything under subsection (1) must, despite any other law to the contrary, do so as required.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 126 (1) If an enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds that a person or entity has contravened this Act, they may issue a notice of non-compliance to that person or entity.

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (2) The notice must be made in writing and must set out

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (a) the name of the person or entity to whom it is directed;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (b) the provision of this Act or the regulations, or the condition established under section 64, amended under subsection 68(1) or added to a decision statement under that subsection, that is alleged to have been contravened;

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (c) the relevant facts surrounding the alleged contravention; and

heading: Contents of notice
paragraph: (d) a statement that the person or entity may provide comments in response to the notice and the time within which they may do so.

heading: Measures required
paragraph: 127 (1) If an enforcement officer believes on reasonable grounds that there is or is likely to be a contravention of this Act, they may, among other things, order a person or entity to

heading: Measures required
paragraph: (a) stop doing something that is or is likely to be in contravention of this Act or cause it to be stopped; or

heading: Measures required
paragraph: (b) take any measure that is necessary in order to comply with this Act or to mitigate the effects of non-compliance.

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 128, the order must be made in writing and must set out

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (a) the name of the person or entity to whom it is directed;

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (b) the provision of this Act or the regulations, or the condition established under section 64 or added or amended under section 68, that is alleged to have been or that is likely to be contravened;

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (c) the relevant facts surrounding the alleged contravention;

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (d) the measures to be taken;

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (e) the time or the day when each measure is to begin or the period during which it is to be carried out;

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (f) the duration of the order;

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (g) a statement that the person or entity may provide comments to the enforcement officer in response to the order; and

heading: Contents of order
paragraph: (h) a statement that a request for a review may be made to the President of the Agency and the time period for doing so.

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (3) The enforcement officer may, after giving reasonable notice to all persons or entities named in the order, and so long as the President of the Agency has not received a notice requesting a review of the order,

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (a) amend or suspend a condition of the order, add a condition to it or delete a condition from it;

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (b) cancel the order;

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (c) correct a clerical error in the order; or

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (d) extend the order's duration.

heading: Exigent circumstances
paragraph: 128 (1) In the case of exigent circumstances, an order may be given orally on the condition that it is followed, within seven days, by a written order issued in accordance with section 127.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, exigent circumstances includes circumstances in which the delay necessary to issue a written order that meets the requirements of subsection 127(2) would likely result in danger to the environment, human life or health or public safety.

heading: Duty to comply with order
paragraph: 129 (1) Any person or entity to whom an order is given under section 127 or 128 must comply with the order.

heading: Measures taken by enforcement officer
paragraph: (2) If the person or entity does not comply with the order within the time specified, the enforcement officer may, on their own initiative and at that person or entity's expense, carry out the measure required.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: 130 (1) Any person or entity to whom an order is given under section 127 or 128 may, by notice in writing given to the President of the Agency within 30 days after the day on which the person or entity receives a copy of the order, make a request to the President for a review of the order.

heading: Extension of period for request
paragraph: (2) The President of the Agency may extend the period within which a request for a review may be made if, in the President's opinion, it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: Review
paragraph: 131 On receipt of a request made under subsection 130(1), the President of the Agency must designate an individual as a review officer to review the order.

heading: No automatic stay on review
paragraph: 132 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the request for a review of an order does not suspend the operation of an order.

heading: Suspension on application
paragraph: (2) A review officer may, on application made by a person or entity to whom an order is given, suspend the operation of the order if the review officer considers it appropriate and, in that case, impose on all persons or entities subject to the order conditions that are reasonable in the circumstances and consistent with the protection of the environment, human life or health or public safety.

heading: Duration of suspension
paragraph: (3) If the operation of an order is suspended under subsection (2), the period for which the order is issued is suspended until the review is completed.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: 133 (1) A review officer may order any person to give evidence in writing or produce any documents and things that the review officer considers relevant for the purpose of performing any of their functions.

heading: Enforcement of orders
paragraph: (2) Any order made under subsection (1) may be made an order of the Federal Court or of the superior court of a province and is enforceable in the same manner as an order of that court.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (3) An order made under subsection (1) may be made an order of the Federal Court or of the superior court of a province by following the usual practice and procedure of the court in such matters, or by filing a certified copy of the order with the registrar of the court.

heading: Powers of review officer
paragraph: 134 A review officer, after considering the order under review and giving all persons or entities who are subject to it a reasonable opportunity to make representations, may

heading: Powers of review officer
paragraph: (a) confirm or cancel the order;

heading: Powers of review officer
paragraph: (b) amend or suspend a condition of the order, add a condition to it or delete a condition from it; or

heading: Powers of review officer
paragraph: (c) extend the order's duration.

heading: Decision
paragraph: 135 (1) A review officer must render a written decision, with reasons, and provide all persons or entities to whom the order was given and the President of the Agency with a copy of the decision and the reasons.

heading: Duty to comply with revised order
paragraph: (2) Any person or entity that is subject to an order confirmed or varied under section 134 must comply with the order.

heading: Immunity
paragraph: 136 No action or other proceeding of a civil nature may be brought against a review officer in respect of anything that is done or omitted to be done in good faith while exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under this Act.

heading: Rules
paragraph: 137 The Agency may make rules

heading: Rules
paragraph: (a) governing the practice and procedure for the review of orders;

heading: Rules
paragraph: (b) generally, respecting the work of review officers; and

heading: Rules
paragraph: (c) for preventing trade secrets and information described in section 20 of the Access to Information Act from being disclosed or made public as a result of their being used as evidence before a review officer.

heading: Appeal to Federal Court
paragraph: 138 The Minister or any person or entity to whom an order, as confirmed or varied by a review officer, is directed may, by filing a written notice of appeal within 30 days after the day on which the written reasons are provided by the review officer under section 135, appeal to the Federal Court from the review officer's decision.

heading: Order not suspended
paragraph: 139 The filing of a notice of appeal under section 138 does not suspend the operation of an order, as confirmed or varied by a review officer.

heading: Court's power
paragraph: 140 (1) If, on the Minister's application, it appears to a court of competent jurisdiction that a person or entity has done, is about to do or is likely to do any act constituting or directed toward the commission of an offence under this Act, the court may issue an injunction ordering the person or entity who is named in the application to

heading: Court's power
paragraph: (a) refrain from doing an act that, in the court's opinion, may constitute or be directed toward the commission of the offence; or

heading: Court's power
paragraph: (b) do an act that, in the court's opinion, may prevent the commission of the offence.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) No injunction is to be issued under subsection (1) unless 48 hours' notice is served on the party or parties who are named in the application or unless the urgency of the situation is such that service of notice would not be in the public interest.

heading: Voluntary reports
paragraph: 141 (1) If a person has knowledge of the commission or reasonable likelihood of the commission of an offence under this Act, but is not required to report the matter under this Act, the person may report any information relating to the offence or likely offence to an enforcement officer or the Agency.

heading: Request for confidentiality
paragraph: (2) The person making the report may request that their identity, and any information that may reveal their identity, not be disclosed.

heading: Due diligence
paragraph: (3) An enforcement officer and the Agency must exercise all due diligence to not disclose the identity of a person who makes a request under subsection (2) or any information that may reveal their identity.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (4) A person not referred to in subsection (3), or an entity, must not disclose the identity of a person who makes a request under subsection (2) or any information that may reveal that person's identity unless that person authorizes the disclosure in writing.

heading: Employee protection
