paragraph: (5) Despite any other Act of Parliament, an employer must not dismiss, suspend, demote, discipline, harass or otherwise disadvantage an employee, or deny an employee a benefit of employment, with the intent to retaliate against the employee because the employee has

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (a) made a report under subsection (1);

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (b) acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, refused or stated an intention of refusing to do anything that is an offence under this Act; or

heading: Employee protection
paragraph: (c) acting in good faith and on the basis of reasonable belief, done or stated an intention of doing anything that is required to be done by or under this Act.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: 142 A person or entity must not obstruct or hinder an enforcement officer or analyst who is exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under this Act.

heading: False statements or information
paragraph: 143 A person or entity must not make a false or misleading statement or provide false or misleading information in connection with any matter under this Act to any person who is exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under this Act.

heading: Offences
paragraph: 144 (1) Every person or entity commits an offence that

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) contravenes section 7, subsection 122(5), 125(3), 129(1), 135(2) or 141(4) or (5) or section 142 or 143;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) contravenes a condition established under subsection 64(2) or added or amended under section 68 with which the person or entity must comply; or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) omits to provide to the Minister information required to be provided under subsection 72(1).

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (2) Every individual who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (a) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $5,000 and not more than $300,000; and

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (b) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $10,000 and not more than $600,000.

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations or entities
paragraph: (3) Every corporation or entity that commits an offence under subsection (1) and that the court determines under section 145 to be a small revenue corporation or entity is liable on summary conviction

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations or entities
paragraph: (a) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $25,000 and not more than $2,000,000; and

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations or entities
paragraph: (b) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $50,000 and not more than $4,000,000.

heading: Penalty - other corporations or entities
paragraph: (4) Every corporation or entity, other than a corporation or entity referred to in subsection (3), that commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction

heading: Penalty - other corporations or entities
paragraph: (a) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $100,000 and not more than $4,000,000; and

heading: Penalty - other corporations or entities
paragraph: (b) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $200,000 and not more than $8,000,000.

heading: Determination of small revenue corporation or entity status
paragraph: 145 For the purpose of subsection 144(3), a court may determine a corporation or entity to be a small revenue corporation or entity if the court is satisfied that the gross revenues of the corporation or entity for the 12 months immediately before the day on which the subject matter of the proceedings arose - or, if it arose on more than one day, for the 12 months immediately before the first day on which the subject matter of the proceedings arose - were not more than $5,000,000.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: 146 (1) If an offence of contravening section 7, subsection 129(1) or 135(2) or section 142, or an offence under paragraph 144(1)(b), is committed or continued on more than one day, it constitutes a separate offence for each day on which it is committed or continued.

heading: Due diligence defence
paragraph: (2) A person or entity must not be found guilty of an offence for a contravention of section 7, subsection 129(1) or 135(2) or section 142, or of an offence under paragraph 144(1)(b), if they establish that they exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence.

heading: Liability of senior officers
paragraph: 147 If a corporation or entity commits an offence under this Act, any senior officer, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, of the corporation or entity who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence, and is liable on conviction to the penalty provided for by this Act for an individual in respect of the offence committed by the corporation or entity, whether or not the corporation or entity has been prosecuted.

heading: Duties of senior officers
paragraph: 148 Every senior officer, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, of a corporation or entity must take all reasonable care to ensure that the corporation or entity complies with this Act and any order issued by an enforcement officer or review officer.

heading: Limitation period or prescription
paragraph: 149 Proceedings by way of summary conviction in respect of an offence under this Act may be instituted at any time within two years after the day on which the Minister becomes aware of the acts or omissions that constitute the alleged offence.

heading: Admissibility of evidence
paragraph: 150 (1) In proceedings for an offence under this Act, a statement, certificate, report or other document of the Minister, an officer or employee of the Agency, an enforcement officer or an analyst that is purported to have been signed by that person is admissible in evidence without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed it and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the matters asserted in it.

heading: Copies and extracts
paragraph: (2) In proceedings for an offence under this Act, a copy of or an extract from any document that is made by the Minister, an officer or employee of the Agency, an enforcement officer or an analyst that appears to have been certified under the signature of that person as a true copy or extract is admissible in evidence without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed it and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, has the same probative force as the original would have if it were proved in the ordinary way.

heading: Presumed date of issue
paragraph: (3) A document referred to in this section is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, presumed to have been issued on the date that it bears.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (4) No document referred to in this section may be received in evidence unless the party intending to produce it has provided reasonable notice of that intention to the party against whom it is intended to be produced together with a copy of the document.

heading: Notice to shareholders
paragraph: 151 If a corporation that has shareholders is convicted of an offence under this Act, the court must make an order directing the corporation to notify its shareholders, in the manner and within the time directed by the court, of the facts relating to the commission of the offence and of the details of the punishment imposed.

heading: Power
paragraph: 152 The Agency must publish, in the manner it considers appropriate,

heading: Power
paragraph: (a) information or a document provided by a proponent to comply with a condition established under section 64 or added or amended under section 68;

heading: Power
paragraph: (b) a summary of a report that an enforcement officer or analyst may prepare in the exercise of their powers or the performance of their duties and functions under sections 122 to 125;

heading: Power
paragraph: (c) a notice of non-compliance referred to in section 126;

heading: Power
paragraph: (d) a written order issued by an enforcement officer in accordance with section 127 or by a review officer under section 134; or

heading: Power
paragraph: (e) a decision rendered under section 135.

heading: Agency continued
paragraph: 153 (1) The Canadian Environmental Assessment Agency is continued as the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada. The Impact Assessment Agency must advise and assist the Minister in exercising the powers and performing the duties and functions conferred on him or her by this Act.

heading: Minister's responsibility
paragraph: (2) The Minister is responsible for the Agency. The Minister may not, except as provided in this Act, direct the President of the Agency or its employees, or any review panel members, with respect to a report, decision, order or recommendation to be made under this Act.

heading: Delegation to Agency
paragraph: 154 (1) The Minister may, subject to any terms and conditions that the Minister specifies, delegate to an officer or employee of the Agency any of the powers, duties and functions that the Minister is authorized to exercise or perform under this Act.

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) However, the Minister is not authorized to delegate a power to make regulations or a power to delegate under subsection (1).

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: 155 The Agency's objects are

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (a) to conduct or administer impact assessments and administer any other requirements and procedures established by this Act and the regulations;

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (b) to coordinate - during the period that begins on the day on which a copy of the description of the project referred to in subsection 10(1) is posted on the Internet site, and that ends on the day on which the decision statement in respect of the project is issued - consultations with Indigenous groups that may be affected by the carrying out of a designated project;

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (c) to promote harmonization in relation to the assessment of effects across Canada at all levels of government;

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (d) to promote or conduct research in matters of impact assessment and to encourage the development of impact assessment techniques and practices, including testing programs, alone or in cooperation with other agencies or organizations;

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (e) to promote impact assessment in a manner that is consistent with the purposes of this Act;

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (f) to promote, monitor and facilitate compliance with this Act;

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (g) to promote and monitor the quality of impact assessments conducted under this Act;

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (h) to develop policy related to this Act; and

heading: Agency's objects
paragraph: (i) to engage in consultation with the Indigenous peoples of Canada on policy issues related to this Act.

heading: Agency's duties
paragraph: 156 (1) In carrying out its objects, the Agency must

heading: Agency's duties
paragraph: (a) provide support for review panels and any committees established under section 92 or under an agreement or arrangement entered into under paragraph 93(1)(a) or (b);

heading: Agency's duties
paragraph: (b) provide, on the Minister's request, administrative support for any research and advisory body established under paragraph 114(1)(b); and

heading: Agency's duties
paragraph: (c) provide information or training to facilitate the application of this Act.

heading: Agency's powers
paragraph: (2) In carrying out its objects, the Agency may

heading: Agency's powers
paragraph: (a) undertake studies or activities or conduct research relating to impact assessment;

heading: Agency's powers
paragraph: (b) advise persons and organizations on matters relating to the assessment of effects;

heading: Agency's powers
paragraph: (c) issue guidelines and codes of practice;

heading: Agency's powers
paragraph: (d) negotiate agreements or arrangements referred to in paragraphs 114(1)(c) to (f) on the Minister's behalf; and

heading: Agency's powers
paragraph: (e) establish research and advisory bodies for matters related to impact assessment and monitoring committees for matters related to the implementation of follow-up programs and adaptive management plans, including with respect to the interests and concerns of Indigenous peoples of Canada, and appoint as a member of any such bodies one or more persons.

heading: Expert committee
paragraph: 157 (1) The Agency must establish an expert committee to advise it on issues related to impact assessments and regional and strategic assessments, including scientific, environmental, health, social or economic issues.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: (2) The Agency may appoint any person with relevant knowledge or experience as a member of the expert committee. The membership of the committee must include at least one Indigenous person.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (3) The Agency must post on the Internet site all advice it receives from the expert committee.

heading: Advisory committee - interests and concerns of Indigenous peoples
paragraph: 158 (1) The Agency must establish an advisory committee to advise it with respect to the interests and concerns of the Indigenous peoples of Canada in relation to assessments to be conducted under this Act.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: (2) The Agency may appoint any person with relevant knowledge or experience as a member of the advisory committee.

heading: Membership
paragraph: (2.1) The membership of the committee must include at least

heading: Membership
paragraph: (a) one person recommended by an Indigenous governing body or other entity that represents the interests of First Nations;

heading: Membership
paragraph: (b) one person recommended by an Indigenous governing body or other entity that represents the interests of the Inuit; and

heading: Membership
paragraph: (c) one person recommended by an Indigenous governing body or other entity that represents the interests of the Metis.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (3) The Agency must post on the Internet site all advice it receives from the advisory committee.

heading: Using government facilities
paragraph: 159 In exercising its powers and performing its duties and functions under this Act, the Agency must, when appropriate, make use of the services and facilities of departments, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada.

heading: President
paragraph: 160 (1) The Governor in Council appoints an officer to be the President of the Agency, to hold office during pleasure, who is, for the purposes of this Act, a deputy of the Minister.

heading: President - chief executive officer
paragraph: (2) The President is the Agency's chief executive officer, and may exercise all of the Minister's powers under this Act as authorized by the Minister.

heading: Acting President - Executive Vice-president
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (5), in the event of the absence or incapacity of the President or a vacancy in that office, the Executive Vice-president acts as, and exercises the powers of, the President in the interim.

heading: Acting President - other person
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), the Minister may appoint a person other than the Executive Vice-president to act as the President in the interim.

heading: Governor in Council's approval required
paragraph: (5) The Executive Vice-president, or a person appointed under subsection (4), must not act as the President for a period exceeding 90 days without the Governor in Council's approval.

heading: Executive Vice-president
paragraph: 161 (1) The Governor in Council may appoint an officer to be the Executive Vice-president of the Agency and to hold office during pleasure.

heading: Powers, duties and functions
paragraph: (2) The Executive Vice-president must exercise any powers and perform any duties and functions that the President may assign.

heading: Remuneration
paragraph: 162 The President and the Executive Vice-president are to be paid any remuneration that the Governor in Council may fix.

heading: Appointment under Public Service Employment Act
paragraph: 163 The employees who are necessary to carry out the Agency's work are to be appointed in accordance with the Public Service Employment Act.

heading: Head office
paragraph: 164 The head office of the Agency is to be in the National Capital Region as described in the schedule to the National Capital Act.

heading: Contracts, etc., binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 165 (1) Every contract, memorandum of understanding and arrangement entered into by the Agency in its own name is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada to the same extent as it is binding on the Agency.

heading: Legal proceedings
paragraph: (2) Actions, suits or other legal proceedings in respect of any right or obligation acquired or incurred by the Agency, whether in its own name or in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada, may be brought or taken by or against the Agency in its own name in any court that would have jurisdiction if the Agency were a corporation that is not an agent of Her Majesty.

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: 166 (1) The Minister must, at the end of each fiscal year, prepare a report on the Agency's activities and the administration and implementation of this Act during the previous fiscal year.

heading: Tabling in Parliament
paragraph: (2) The Minister must, during the fiscal year after the fiscal year for which the report is prepared, cause the report to be laid before each House of Parliament.

heading: Review of Act after 10 years
paragraph: 167 Ten years after the day on which this Act comes into force, a comprehensive review of the provisions and operation of the Act is to be undertaken by the committee of the Senate, of the House of Commons or of both Houses of Parliament that is designated or established by the Senate or the House of Commons, or by both Houses of Parliament, as the case may be, for that purpose.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 168 The following definitions apply in this section and sections 169 to 188.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1992 Act means the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act. (Loi de 1992)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2012 Act means the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012. (Loi de 2012)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environmental assessment has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the 2012 Act. (evaluation environnementale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: former Agency means the Canadian Environmental Assessment Agency continued under section 103 of the 2012 Act. (ancienne Agence)

heading: President of former Agency
paragraph: 169 The person who holds the office of President of the former Agency immediately before the day on which this Act comes into force continues in office as the President of the Agency until the expiry or revocation of the appointment.

heading: Executive Vice-president of former Agency
paragraph: 170 The person who holds the office of Executive Vice-president of the former Agency immediately before the day on which this Act comes into force continues in office as the Executive Vice-president of the Agency until the expiry or revocation of the appointment.

heading: Employment continued
paragraph: 171 (1) Nothing in this Act is to be construed to affect the status of an employee who, immediately before the day on which this Act comes into force, occupies a position in the former Agency, except that the employee, on that day, occupies their position in the Agency.

heading: Definition of employee
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this section, employee has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Public Service Employment Act.

heading: References
paragraph: 172 Every reference to the former Agency in any deed, contract, agreement or other document executed, or in Quebec, signed, by the former Agency in its own name is, unless the context otherwise requires, to be read as a reference to the Agency.

heading: Transfer of rights and obligations
paragraph: 173 All rights and property of the former Agency and of Her Majesty in right of Canada that are under the administration and control of the former Agency and all obligations of the former Agency are transferred to the Agency.

heading: Commencement of legal proceedings
paragraph: 174 Any action, suit or other legal proceeding in respect of an obligation or liability incurred by the former Agency may be brought against the Agency in any court that would have had jurisdiction if the action, suit or other legal proceeding had been brought against the former Agency.

heading: Continuation of legal proceedings
paragraph: 175 Any action, suit or other legal proceeding to which the former Agency is party that is pending in any court immediately before the day on which this Act comes into force may be continued by or against the Agency in the same manner and to the same extent as it could have been continued by or against the former Agency.

heading: Appropriations
paragraph: 176 Any amount that is appropriated by an Act of Parliament for the fiscal year in which this Act comes into force to defray the expenditures of the former Agency and that is unexpended on the day on which this Act comes into force is deemed to be an amount appropriated to defray the expenditures of the Agency.

heading: Persons designated
paragraph: 177 A person or class of persons who are designated under subsection 89(1) of the 2012 Act, immediately before the day on which this Act comes into force, are deemed to have been designated as enforcement officers under subsection 120(1) of this Act.

heading: Screenings commenced under 1992 Act
paragraph: 178 Any screening of a project commenced under the 1992 Act in respect of which the responsible authority has not, before the day on which this Act comes into force, taken a course of action under section 20 of that Act is terminated.

heading: Comprehensive studies commenced under 1992 Act
paragraph: 179 (1) Any comprehensive study of a project commenced under the 1992 Act in respect of which the former Agency has not, before the day on which this Act comes into force, published a notice under subsection 22(1) of that Act is terminated.

heading: Screenings under 2012 Act
paragraph: 180 If the proponent of a designated project provided the former Agency with a description of the designated project under subsection 8(1) of the 2012 Act and the former Agency has not, before the day on which this Act comes into force, posted a notice under section 12 of the 2012 Act of its decision with respect to the designated project, the screening is terminated. The description of the designated project that was provided under subsection 8(1) of the 2012 Act is deemed to be an initial description of the project provided under subsection 10(1) of this Act on the day on which this Act comes into force.

heading: Information or studies
paragraph: (2) The proponent of a designated project referred to in subsection (1) must provide the Agency with any information or studies required by the Agency or the former Agency under subsection 23(2) of the 2012 Act within three years after the day on which this Act comes into force.

heading: Extension of time limit
paragraph: (2.1) At the proponent's request, the Agency may, before the time limit referred to in subsection (2) has expired, extend the time limit by any period that is necessary for the proponent to provide the Agency with the information or studies.

heading: Continuance or termination of environmental assessment
paragraph: (3) If the proponent fails to provide the information or studies within the time limit referred to in subsection (2) or within any extension of that time limit or notifies the Agency that it will fail to do so, the Agency may decide that the environmental assessment of the designated project is to be continued as an impact assessment under this Act or is to be terminated.

heading: Posting of notice on Internet site
paragraph: (4) The Agency must post on the Internet site a notice of any decision made under subsection (3).

heading: No review panel
paragraph: (4.1) Despite subsection 36(1), the Minister is not permitted to refer to a review panel an environmental assessment that, in accordance with subsection (3), is continued as an impact assessment under this Act.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (5) This section does not apply to an environmental assessment of a project that was the subject of an order made by the Minister under subsection 125(7) of the 2012 Act.

heading: Request of proponent
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), on request made to the Minister by the proponent of a designated project referred to in that subsection, the environmental assessment is continued as an impact assessment under this Act as if the impact assessment had been referred by the Minister to a review panel under subsection 36(1) of this Act.

heading: Power of Agency
paragraph: (2.1) If, within one year after the day on which this subsection comes into force, the proponent of a designated project referred to in subsection (1) fails to collect the information or undertake the studies required by the Agency under section 39 of the 2012 Act, the Agency may, despite subsection (1), decide that the environmental assessment of that project is to be continued as an impact assessment under this Act as if the impact assessment had been referred by the Minister to a review panel under subsection 36(1) of this Act.

heading: Posting of notice on Internet site
paragraph: (2.2) The Agency must post on the Internet site a notice of any decision made under subsection (2.1).

heading: Rules concerning review panels
paragraph: (3) The following rules apply in respect of an impact assessment referred to in subsection (2):

heading: Rules concerning review panels
paragraph: (a) if, before the day on which this Act comes into force, a review panel was established under subsection 42(1) of the 2012 Act, that review panel is deemed to have been established - and its members are deemed to have been appointed - under section 41 of this Act;

heading: Rules concerning review panels
paragraph: (b) if, before that day, an agreement or arrangement was entered into under section 40 of the 2012 Act, that agreement or arrangement is deemed to have been entered into under section 39 of this Act; and

heading: Rules concerning review panels
paragraph: (c) if, before that day, a review panel was established by an agreement or arrangement entered into under section 40 of the 2012 Act or by document referred to in subsection 41(2) of the 2012 Act, it is deemed to have been established by - and its members are deemed to have been appointed under - an agreement or arrangement entered into under section 39 of this Act or by document referred to in subsection 40(2) of this Act.

heading: Non-application of this Act
paragraph: 185.1 (1) This Act does not apply to a designated project, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the 2012 Act, that is a designated project, as defined in section 2 of this Act, if the former Agency determined that no environmental assessment was required under the 2012 Act or that section 128 of that Act applied to the project.

heading: Non-application of this Act
paragraph: (2) This Act does not apply to a designated project, as defined in section 2 of this Act, that is not a designated project, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the 2012 Act, if one of the following conditions applies:

heading: Non-application of this Act
paragraph: (a) the proponent began the carrying out of the project before the day on which this Act comes into force;

heading: Non-application of this Act
paragraph: (b) a federal authority, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the 2012 Act, exercised a power or performed a duty or function conferred on it under any Act of Parliament, other than this Act, that could permit the project to be carried out, in whole or in part;

heading: Non-application of this Act
paragraph: (c) an environmental assessment of the project was commenced or completed before the day on which this Act comes into force by a jurisdiction other than a federal authority, as those terms are defined in subsection 2(1) of the 2012 Act.

heading: Unpaid costs
paragraph: 186 If the proponent of a designated project has not paid any costs or amounts referred to in section 59 of the 2012 Act that were due more than 90 days before the day on which this Act comes into force, the Agency is authorized, despite any other provision of the 2012 Act or this Act, to not commence any preparations for a possible impact assessment of any designated project the proponent proposes to carry out on or after the day on which this Act comes into force until the proponent pays the costs or amounts.

heading: Privileged evidence, documents or things
paragraph: 187 The evidence, documents or things that, before the day on which this Act comes into force, are privileged under subsection 45(4) or (5) of the 2012 Act are considered to be privileged under subsection 53(4) or (5), respectively, of this Act.

heading: Regional studies commenced under 2012 Act
paragraph: 187.1 (1) A study referred to in subsection 73(1) or 74(1) of the 2012 Act that was commenced under that Act but was not completed before the day on which this Act comes into force is continued as an assessment referred to in section 92 or 93, respectively, of this Act.

heading: Report provided under 2012 Act
paragraph: (2) A report referred to in section 75 of the 2012 Act is deemed to be a report referred to in subsection 102(1) of this Act that is provided to the Minister on completion of an assessment referred to in section 92 or 93 of this Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 188 The Governor in Council may make any regulations that the Governor in Council considers necessary to provide for any other transitional matter arising from the coming into force of this Act.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2 and paragraph 109(a))Federal Authorities
paragraph: 1 Port authority as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Marine Act.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2 and paragraph 109(a))Federal Authorities
paragraph: 2 Board as defined in section 2 of the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Act.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2 and paragraph 109(a))Federal Authorities
paragraph: 3 Board as defined in section 2 of the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation and Offshore Renewable Energy Management Act.

heading: SCHEDULE 4(Section 81 and paragraph 109(a))Bodies
paragraph: 1 Designated airport authority as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Airport Transfer (Miscellaneous Matters) Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"administrator" means the administrator appointed under section
              9 [administrator];

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"adverse effect" means harm to humans, animals or the
            environment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"animal" includes vertebrates and invertebrates, whether living or
            dead, but does not include humans;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"appeal board" means the Environmental Appeal Board continued under the
              Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "applicant" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person applying for a licence, certificate or permit under this Act,              or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a person who gives the administrator a pesticide use notice;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"certificate", except in sections 20 (5) and (6) [seizure and
              prevention order], 25 [recovery of administrative
              penalties], 29 [time limit for prosecuting offence] and
            34 [evidence], means a certificate issued under section
              5 [certificate for sale or use of pesticides by
              individuals];

Definitions
paragraph:
"confirmation" means a confirmation under section 7 (3) [use of
              pesticides in accordance with a pesticide use notice];

heading: Definitions
Definitions
paragraph: "inspector" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(a) a person designated under section 11 [inspectors] as an
              inspector for the purposes of this Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a conservation officer as defined in section 1 (1) of the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "integrated pest management" means a process for managing pest            populations that includes the following elements:

paragraph:
(a) planning and managing ecosystems to prevent organisms from becoming
              pests;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) identifying pest problems and potential pest problems;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(c) monitoring populations of pests and beneficial organisms, damage caused by

          contravention
paragraph:
a particular pesticide, if the administrator considers that this activity has
            caused or is likely to cause an unreasonable adverse effect.

heading:
Administrator's order - unreasonable adverse effect or
          contravention
paragraph:
(3) If the administrator believes on reasonable grounds that a person has
            contravened this Act or the regulations, the administrator may order the person to do
            anything the administrator is authorized to order a person to do under subsection
              (1) or (2), whether or not an unreasonable adverse effect
            has resulted.

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
17
		  (1) For the purposes of ensuring compliance with this Act and the regulations, an
            inspector may enter land or premises, except premises or a part of premises occupied
            solely as a private residence, at any reasonable time if the inspector has reasonable
            grounds to believe that

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) a pesticide is located on or in the land or premises,

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(b) the land or premises is the site of an activity for which a licence,
              certificate, permit or confirmation is required, or

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(c) a container or equipment that is or may be used to contain, mix, store or
              apply a pesticide is located on the land or in the premises.

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(2) An inspector who enters land or premises under subsection (1), with consent
            under section
              18 (1) or with a warrant under section 18 (2) may do any of the
            following:

heading: Inspections
Inspections
paragraph:
(b) investigate the manner in which a pesticide has been, is being or may be used,
              sold, stored, transported or disposed of;

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(c) inspect any place at which the inspector believes a pesticide has been, is
              being or may be used, sold, stored, transported or disposed of;

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(d) inspect records that the inspector believes relate to a pest management plan
              or the use, sale, storage, transportation or disposal of a pesticide;

heading: Inspections
Inspections
paragraph:
(f) for the purposes of paragraphs (a) and (e), take away a sample of
              anything;

heading: Inspections
Inspections
Inspections
paragraph:
(i) record or copy any information related to the use, manner of application,
              storage, sale, transport or disposal of a pesticide by any method;

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(j) use a machine, a structure, material or equipment in the place that is being
              inspected as is necessary to carry out the inspection;

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(k) use copying equipment located at the place that is being inspected to make
              copies to take away;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (l) take photographs or make audio or video records.

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(3) An inspector exercising authority under this section must produce proof of
            identity on the request of a person whose land or premises the inspector
            enters.

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(4) A person who is or was a director, receiver, receiver manager, officer,
            employee, banker, auditor or agent of a person who is the subject of an inspection under
            this section must, on the request of the inspector,

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(a) produce, without charge or unreasonable delay, for examination by the
              inspector

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(i)  any licence, certificate, permit, pest management plan, confirmation or
                record of pesticide use or sale, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(ii)  any other record that touches on any matter relating to the use, handling,
                transporting, storage, disposal, purchase or sale of pesticides by the person who is
                the subject of the inspection, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
(b) provide the inspector with information relevant to the purposes of the
              inspection.

heading: Inspection of private residence
paragraph:
18
		  (1) An inspector may exercise the powers under section
              17 [inspections] in respect of premises used as a
            private residence only with the consent of the occupant or under the authority of a
            warrant under subsection (2) or another Act.

heading: Inspection of private residence
paragraph:
(2) If satisfied by evidence on oath that access to premises, or a part of premises,
            used solely as a private residence is necessary for the purposes of this Act, a justice
            may issue a warrant authorizing a person named in the warrant to enter into the premises
            and conduct an inspection.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
19
		  (1) In this section, "vehicle" includes a motor vehicle as defined
            in the Motor Vehicle Act and a vessel.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
(2) For the purposes of ensuring compliance with this Act and the regulations, if an            inspector has reasonable grounds to believe that a vehicle is being used to transport a
            pesticide, an inspector may

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
(a) require a person operating the vehicle to stop the vehicle and provide
              identification, and

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (b) carry out an inspection of the vehicle.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
(3) When requested or signalled to do so by an inspector who is readily identifiable
            as a conservation officer, the operator of a motor vehicle must immediately

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph: (a) stop the vehicle, and

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
(b) provide identification and the information that the inspector considers
              necessary to determine whether this Act and the regulations are being complied
              with.

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
(4) For the purposes of carrying out an inspection under this section, an inspector
            may

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
(a) require that any compartment of the vehicle or any container in or on the
              vehicle be opened, and

heading: Inspection of vehicles
paragraph:
(b) exercise any of the powers under section 17
                (2) [inspections].

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
20
		  (1) If an inspector concludes in the course of an inspection under this Act that the
            inspector has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has contravened or is
            contravening this Act or the regulations, the inspector may

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(a) order a person to do anything the inspector considers necessary to stop the
              contravention or prevent another contravention, and

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(b) seize anything validly inspected by the inspector that the inspector believes
              on reasonable grounds

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph: (i)  was used or is being used in the contravention, or

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph: (ii)  will afford evidence of the contravention.

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(2) Sections 23 (4) and 24 to 24.2 of the Offence              Act apply in respect of anything seized under subsection
              (1) of this section and, for the purposes of section 23 (4) of the
              Offence Act, an inspector is deemed to be a peace            officer.

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(3) If, under section 24 (2) (a) of the Offence              Act, a justice orders that something referred to in subsection
              (2) of this section be detained, despite section 24 (3) of the Offence                Act, the thing may be detained for up to one year before an
            order under section 24 (5) of that Act, authorizing its continued detention, is
            required.

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph: (4) Despite subsections (2) and (3),

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(a) nothing seized under this Act may be returned unless, in the opinion of the
              administrator, any risk of an unreasonable adverse effect has been
              eliminated,

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(b) if, in the opinion of the administrator, something seized under this Act must
              be destroyed or decontaminated in order to eliminate a risk of an unreasonable adverse
              effect, the administrator may order the thing to be decontaminated or destroyed and
              the cost of decontamination or destruction is a debt due to the government by the
              person from whom it was seized and may be recovered in accordance with subsection
                (5), and

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(c) 
              section
                22 of this Act applies in respect of anything destroyed by order under
              paragraph (b).

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(5) For the purpose of recovering a debt referred to in subsection (4)
              (b) the administrator may

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(a) issue a certificate setting out the name of the person who is liable for the
              debt and the amount owing by that person, and

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph: (b) file the certificate with a court that has jurisdiction.

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(6) A certificate filed with a court under subsection (5) has the same
            force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of
            the court with which it is filed

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(a) for the recovery of a debt of the amount set out in the certificate,
              and

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph: (b) against the person named in the certificate.

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(7) Sections 23 to 24.2 of the Offence              Act and subsection (3) of this section do not apply in respect
            of anything ordered destroyed under subsection (4) (b) of this section.

heading: Seizure and prevention order
paragraph:
(8) Sections 23 to 24.2 of the Offence              Act do not apply in relation to anything taken in the course of an
            inspection under section 17, 18 or 19 of this
            Act unless subsection (1) of this section applies.

heading: Duty of persons being inspected
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A person must not interfere with an inspector's rights of entry and inspection
            under this Part [Compliance].

heading: Duty of persons being inspected
paragraph:
(2) On the request of an inspector, a person on the land, premises or vehicle and
            who the inspector reasonably believes is involved in the use, activity or equipment
            being inspected must provide proof of identity.

heading: No compensation
paragraph:
22
		  Compensation is not payable in respect of anything lawfully seized, detained,
          treated or destroyed under this Act.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
23
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, if the administrator is satisfied on a balance of
            probabilities that a person has

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of this Act or the regulations,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with an order under this Act, or

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(c) failed to comply with a requirement of a licence, certificate or permit
              issued, or a pesticide use notice given, under this Act,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
the administrator may serve the person with a determination requiring the person
            to pay an administrative penalty in the amount specified in the
            determination.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(2) A determination under subsection (1) must be in the prescribed form and
            contain the prescribed information.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(3) A penalty imposed under this section must be paid within the prescribed
            time.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(4) Before the date an administrative penalty under this section is due, the
            administrator may, subject to the regulations, enter into an agreement with the person
            who is liable for the penalty.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(5) An agreement under subsection (4) may provide, in accordance with the
            regulations, for the reduction or cancellation of the penalty subject to the terms and
            conditions the administrator considers necessary or desirable.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(6) An agreement under subsection (4) must specify the time for performing
            the terms and conditions, and if the person fails to perform them by the date specified,
            the penalty specified in the determination under subsection (1) is due and
            payable on that date.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(7) Neither the administrator's decision whether to enter into an agreement under
            subsection (4) nor the terms and conditions of such an agreement may be appealed under
              Part
              4 [Appeals to the Environmental Appeal
            Board].

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(8) If the administrator makes a determination requiring a person to pay an administrative penalty in
            respect of a contravention or failure referred to in subsection (1), a prosecution
            for an offence under this Act in respect of the same contravention or failure may not be
            brought against the person.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
(9) If a corporation contravenes this Act or the regulations or fails to comply with
            an order or the terms of a licence, certificate or permit as described under subsection
              (1), an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who
            authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure is also liable under
            this section, even though the corporation is liable for or pays an administrative
            penalty.

heading: Effect of charging an offence
paragraph:
24
		  An administrative penalty under this Act may not be determined against a person in
          respect of an act or omission if the person has been charged with an offence under this
          Act in respect of the same act or omission.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
25
		  (1) Subject to a decision of the appeal board cancelling a determination under
              section 23
              (1) [administrative penalties], an administrative
            penalty under this Act may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
(2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required under section
              23 [administrative penalties], the administrator may
            file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, upon filing, the certificate
            has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a
            judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
(3) A certificate under subsection (2) may be in the prescribed form, must be
            signed by the administrator and must contain

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the penalty,

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
(b) the contravention or failure in relation to which the penalty is imposed,
              and

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the penalty.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
26
		  (1) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) contravenes

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(i)  section 3 (1) (a), (b) or (c) or (2) (a), (b) or (c) [general
                  prohibitions and restrictions],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(ii)  section 4 (1) (a), (b), (c) or (d) [licence for sale or use of
                  pesticides],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(iii)  section 5 (1), (2) or (3) [certificate for use or sale of
                  pesticides by individuals],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(iv)  
                section 6
                  (1) [permit for use of pesticides],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(v)  section 7 (1), (6) (a), (b) or (c) or (7) [use of pesticides in
                  accordance with a pesticide use notice],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (vi)  section 12 (1) or (2) [qualified monitors], or

heading: Offences and penalties
Offences and penalties
Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(c) refuses or fails to comply with an order of the minister, the
              administrator, the appeal board or an inspector;

heading: Offences and penalties
Offences and penalties
Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(f) fails to comply with an order under section
                31 [additional sentencing orders] or a variation under
                section
                32 [variation of section 31
              orders].

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(2) An individual who is convicted of an offence under this Act is liable to a fine
            of not more than $200 000 or to imprisonment for 6 months, or to both, and if convicted
            of a subsequent similar offence, to a fine of not more than $400 000 or to imprisonment
            for 6 months, or to both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
(3) A corporation that is convicted of an offence under this Act is liable to a fine
            of not more than $400 000, and if convicted of a subsequent similar offence, to a fine
            of not more than $800 000.

heading: Offence by a corporation
paragraph:
27
		  (1) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer,
            director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the
            offence commits the offence, whether or not the corporation is convicted.

heading: Offence by a corporation
paragraph:
(2) In a prosecution for an offence, it is sufficient proof of the offence to
            establish that the offence was committed by an employee or agent of the accused, whether
            or not the employee or agent is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence,
            unless the accused establishes that the offence was committed without the accused's
            knowledge or consent or that the accused exercised all due diligence to prevent the
            commission of the offence.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph:
28
		  If a contravention under section 26 [offences and penalties]
          continues for more than one day, on conviction, the offender is liable to a separate
          penalty in the applicable amount under section 26, without notice and without a separate count
          being laid, for each day that the contravention occurs.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph:
29
		  (1) The time limit for laying an information for an offence under this Act
            is

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph:
(a) 3 years after the date that the facts on which the information is based arose,
              or

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph:
(b) if the minister issues a certificate described in subsection
                (2), 18 months after the date that the facts on which the information is
              based first came to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph:
(2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the minister, certifying the
            date that the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the
            minister,

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph:
(a) is admissible without proof of the signature or official character of the
              person appearing to have signed the certificate, and

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) is proof of the certified matters.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph:
30
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act and the court is satisfied
            that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any monetary
            benefits or that monetary benefits accrued to the person, the court may order the person
            to pay a fine equal to the court's estimation of the amount of those monetary
            benefits.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph:
(2) A fine under subsection (1) is in addition to and not in place of a fine under
              section
              26 [offences and penalties].

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
31
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any
            punishment imposed, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the
            circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the
            following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Additional sentencing orders
Additional sentencing orders
Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
(c) directing the person to pay the government an amount of money as compensation,
              in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken by or
              caused to be taken on behalf of the government as a result of the commission of the
              offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (d) directing the person to perform community service;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
Additional sentencing orders
Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
(g) directing the person to submit to the minister, on application by the minister
              within 3 years after the date of the conviction, any information respecting the
              activities of the person that the court considers appropriate in the
              circumstances;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
(h) directing the person to publish, in any manner the court considers
              appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
(i) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court
              considers appropriate to secure the person's good conduct and to prevent the person
              from repeating the offence or committing other offences under this Act.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
(2) If a person fails to comply with an order referred to in subsection (1)
              (h), the minister may publish the facts relating to the commission of the
            offence and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph: (3) If

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
(a) an order under this section or section
                32 [variation of section 31 orders] directs a
              person to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose,
              or

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
(b) the minister incurs publication costs under subsection (2) of this
              section,

heading: Additional sentencing orders
paragraph:
the amount and any interest payable on that amount constitute a debt due to the
            government and may be recovered as such in any court of competent
            jurisdiction.

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
32
		  (1) An application for variation of an order under section 31 [additional
              sentencing orders] may be made to the court that made the order
            by

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph: (a) the Attorney General, or

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
(b) the person against whom the order under section 31 was
              made.

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
(2) Before hearing an application under subsection (1), the court may
            order the applicant to give notice of the application in accordance with the directions
            of the court.

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
(3) On an application under subsection (1), if the court considers variation to be
            appropriate because of a change in circumstances, the court may make an order doing one
            or more of the following:

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph: (a) changing the original order or any conditions specified in it;

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
(b) relieving the person referred to in subsection (1) (b) absolutely
              or partially from compliance with all or part of the original order;

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
(c) reducing the period for which the original order is to remain in
              effect;

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
(d) extending the period for which the original order is to remain in effect,
              subject to the limit that this extension must not be longer than one year.

heading: Variation of section 31 orders
paragraph:
(4) If an application under subsection (1) has been heard by a court, no other
            application may be made in respect of the order under section 31 except with leave of
            the court.

heading: Sections 4 and 5 of the Offence Act
paragraph:
33
		  Sections 4 and 5 of the Offence            Act do not apply in respect of this Act or the
          regulations.

heading: Evidence
paragraph:
34
		  (1) A certificate signed by an analyst designated by the minister, stating that the
            analyst has analyzed or examined a substance and stating the result of the analysis or
            examination, is admissible in evidence in a proceeding under this Act as proof of the
            facts stated in the certificate without proof of the signature or designation of the
            person signing the certificate.

heading: Evidence
paragraph:
(2) The minister may, in writing, designate analysts for the purposes of this
            section.

heading: Service
paragraph:
35
		  (1) Anything that under this Act must be given or served on an individual may be given or served

heading: Service
paragraph: (a) by leaving it with the individual,

heading: Service
paragraph: (b) by sending it by registered mail to the last known address of the individual, or

heading: Service
paragraph: (c) by sending it by electronic mail to the last known electronic mail address of the individual used in relation to a licence, permit, certificate, pesticide use notice, order, inspection or investigation under this Act.

heading: Service
paragraph: (2) Anything that under this Act must be given or served on a corporation may be given or served

heading: Service
paragraph: (a) by leaving it with any director, senior officer, liquidator or receiver manager of the corporation,

heading: Service
paragraph: (b) by sending it by registered mail as follows:

heading: Service
paragraph: (i)  if the corporation is a company within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act, to the mailing address shown in the corporate register for the registered office of the corporation;

heading: Service
paragraph: (ii)  if the corporation is an extraprovincial company within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act,

heading: Service
paragraph: (A) to the mailing address shown in the corporate register for the corporation if that head office is in British Columbia, or

heading: Service
paragraph: (B) to the mailing address shown in the corporate register for any attorney of the corporation;

heading: Service
paragraph: (iii)  in all other cases, to the head office of the corporation, or

heading: Service
paragraph: (c) by sending it by electronic mail to the last known electronic mail address

heading: Service
paragraph: (i)  of the corporation or of a director, officer or employee of the corporation, and

heading: Service
paragraph: (ii)  used in relation to a licence, permit, certificate, pesticide use notice, order, inspection or investigation under this Act.

heading: Service
paragraph: (3) Anything sent by registered mail for the purposes of this Act is deemed to be received by the person to whom it is addressed on the 14th day after deposit with Canada Post, unless the person received actual service before that day.

heading: Service
paragraph: (4) Anything sent by electronic mail for the purposes of this Act is deemed to be received by the person to whom it is addressed on the third day after it is sent.

heading: Service
paragraph: (5) This section does not apply to notices or documents of the appeal board.

heading: Regulations - general rules
paragraph:
36		  (1) Regulations under this Act may be different for different classes of pesticides,
            pesticide sales or pesticide uses and in relation to different categories of licences,
            permits, certificates or confirmations.

heading: Regulations - general rules
paragraph:
(2) If a regulation under this Act may establish standards, the regulation may adopt
            by reference, in whole or in part and with any changes considered appropriate by the
            minister or the administrator, as applicable, a code, standard or rule

heading: Regulations - general rules
paragraph:
(a) set by a provincial, national, international or any other code or standard
              making body, or

heading: Regulations - general rules
paragraph:
(b) enacted as or under a law of another jurisdiction, including a foreign
              jurisdiction.

heading: Regulations - general rules
paragraph:
(3) A code, standard or rule referred to in subsection (2) may be adopted as
            amended from time to time.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
37
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41
            of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may            make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(a) for the purposes of section 23 [administrative
                penalties],

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(i)  prescribing procedures for making a determination including, but not limited
                to,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (A) prescribing the form of and information to be contained in a notice of intent to make a determination,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(B) prescribing contraventions of this Act or the regulations in relation to
                  which a notice of intent to make a determination may be sent and a determination made,
                  and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(C) establishing procedures for providing a person on whom a notice of intent to make a determination has been served with an opportunity to make
                  representations, which need not entail an oral hearing,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(ii)  prescribing a schedule of administrative penalties that may be imposed and
                the matters that must be considered by the administrator in establishing a penalty
                in a particular case,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(iii)  authorizing administrative penalties to be imposed on a daily basis for
                continuing contraventions or failures,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iv)  prescribing time limits for paying administrative penalties,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(v)  prescribing, in relation to a contravention or failure described in
                  section
                    23 (1), whether a notice of intent to make a determination must be cancelled
                if the person on whom it was served demonstrates to the satisfaction of the
                administrator that the person exercised due diligence to prevent the specified
                contravention or failure,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(vi)  respecting agreements, including prescribing terms and conditions that must
                be included, under section 23 (4),

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(vii)  prescribing a limitation period for imposing an administrative penalty and
                evidentiary matters in relation to that period,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (viii)  prescribing methods of paying a monetary penalty,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(ix)  prescribing the consequences of failing to pay an administrative penalty
                which may include, but are not limited to, imposing additional penalties,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(x)  providing for the publication of the administrator's determination to impose an
                administrative penalty, and

heading: Power to make regulations
Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(b) despite any other enactment, restricting the authority of a municipality or a
              regional district to make bylaws in relation to prescribed pesticide uses, which may
              include, but are not limited to, uses of pesticide

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(i)  in the management of pests for purposes of protecting human health and the
                environment,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  in the management of non-indigenous pests, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
(iii)  on land used for agriculture, forestry, transportation, public utilities and
                pipelines.

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph:
38
		  (1) The minister may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the minister may make regulations as            follows:

heading: Minister's regulations
paragraph: (a) classifying substances as pesticides;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Integrated Pest Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agriculture" has the same meaning as "qualifying agricultural use" in the Classification of Land as a Farm Regulation, but does not include aquaculture, or aquacultural activities, carried on in a body of water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commercial pesticide" means a pesticide described in section 2 (c) [classes of pesticides];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Crown land" means land, or an interest in land, vested in the government;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "domestic pesticide" means a pesticide described in section 2 (d) [classes of pesticides];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "essential service location" means a location described in column 3 of the table in Schedule 6;

paragraph: (d) incinerators, landfills, sewage treatment plants and other facilities for the disposal or treatment of waste,

paragraph: (e) dams, dikes and reservoirs, and

paragraph: but does not include landscaped land;

paragraph: "injury threshold" means the point at which the abundance of pests and the damage they are causing or are likely to cause indicates that pest control is necessary or desirable;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "invasive plant" means a prescribed species of invasive plant listed under the Invasive Plants Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land" includes foreshore, bodies of water on land and land covered by water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "landscape" means an area of land that has been improved by planting with ornamental plants or is maintained for ornamental purposes;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "multi-residence building" means a building that contains two or more separate units occupied as living accommodation and includes, without limiting this, apartment buildings, hotels, and strata titled buildings that contain two or more separate units occupied as living accommodation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permit-restricted pesticide" means a pesticide described in section 2 (a) [classes of pesticides] and set out in Schedule 1;

heading: Definitions

heading: Exclusions from the definition of "pesticide"
paragraph:
3
		  The following micro-organisms, materials, substances and control products are excluded from the definition of "pesticide" in section 1 of the Act:

heading: Exclusions from the definition of "pesticide"
paragraph: (a) an article, instrument, apparatus, contrivance or gadget that, by itself or in conjunction with another control product, is used as a means to control pests directly or indirectly;

heading: Exclusions from the definition of "pesticide"
paragraph: (b) a control product that is

heading: Exclusions from the definition of "pesticide"
paragraph: (i)  used to control arthropods on or in humans, livestock or domestic animals, and

heading: Exclusions from the definition of "pesticide"
paragraph: (ii)  administered internally by mouth or injection;

heading: Exclusions from the definition of "pesticide"
paragraph: (c) a control product that is used to destroy, inactivate or reduce viruses, bacteria or other micro-organisms for the purposes of treating, mitigating or preventing a disease in humans or animals;

heading: Exclusions from the definition of "pesticide"
paragraph: (d) a control product that is used to destroy, inactivate or reduce mould, mildew or odours, except when used as a wood preservative.

paragraph: (ii)  complies with the conditions set out in section 54.2, as if the user held a residential applicator certificate, and with the terms and conditions, if any, of the pesticide applicator certificate.

heading: Licence requirement exemptions
paragraph:
7
		  (1) A licensee is exempt from the requirements under section 68 [licensee use of pesticide - integrated pest management] in relation to the use of wood preservatives on land described in section 5 (1) (a).

heading: Licence requirement exemptions
paragraph: (2) A licensee is exempt from a requirement under section 33 (3) (b) [containment, storage, transportation, disposal and use of pesticides] in relation to a pesticide use if the licensee holds a permit issued under section 6 (1) of the Act authorizing the exemption in relation to the use and setting out terms and conditions the licensee must comply with instead.

heading: Licence criteria
paragraph:
8
		  For the purpose of section 4 (3) (b) of the Act, the administrator must be satisfied that the applicant

heading: Licence criteria
paragraph: (a) holds, or employs a person who holds, the category of certificate that under section 50 [category of certificate required] is required in relation to the category of licence applied for, and

heading: Licence criteria
paragraph: (b) maintains a business location in British Columbia for doing business in the Province or provides the administrator with an address in British Columbia at which the person may be served with documents.

heading: Public consultation requirements - licensee
paragraph:
9
		  A licensee must conduct public consultations in the manner and to the extent set out in section 62 [public consultations - licensees in respect of forest land] if the licensee intends to use a pesticide for a use described in section 5 (1) (g) [pesticide uses requiring a licence] on more than 20 ha per year managed by a single entity.

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph:
10
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: "multi-residence common area" means

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) an indoor area of a multi-residence property to which all or most occupants of the property have access, and

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (b) an outdoor area of a multi-residence property that is

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (i)  within 5 m of an entrance or a window to living accommodations, or

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (ii)  maintained for purposes of passage, parking or recreation;

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: "multi-residence restricted access area" means an area of a multi-residence property that

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) is not used or intended to be used as living accommodation, and

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (b) is not accessible to the general public and most occupants of the property;

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: "outdoor public use area" means an outdoor landscaped area of

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) public land that is maintained for purposes of public passage or recreation, or

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (b) private commercial land to which members of the public may reasonably be expected to have access.

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (2) At least 72 hours before using a pesticide in occupied living accommodations, a licensee must provide a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) [treatment notice - form and content] to

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) the occupant of the living accommodations, and

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (b) if different from the occupant, the owner or manager of the building or the agent of either.

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (3) A licensee who uses a pesticide in unoccupied living accommodations must

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) provide, before or immediately following the use, a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) to the owner or manager of the building or the agent of either, and

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (b) either

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (i)  provide a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) to a person who will be occupying the living accommodations within 48 hours after the pesticide use, or

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (ii)  immediately following the use, post a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) and (2) at each entrance to the unoccupied living accommodation, which notice must not be removed by the licensee for 48 hours after the pesticide use.

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (4) At least 48 hours before using a pesticide in a multi-residence common area, a licensee must

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) provide a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) to the owner or manager of the building or the agent of either, and

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (b) either

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (i)  provide a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) to each person who has access to the common area within 48 hours after the use, or

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (ii)  post a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) and (2)

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (A) at each entrance to an indoor treatment area,

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (B) if the common area is an outdoor area that is fenced, at each gate or opening that provides access to the common area, and

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (C) if the common area is an outdoor area that is not fenced, at intervals around the common area so that the notice is clearly visible and will provide notice of the pesticide use to any person approaching the common area,

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: which treatment notice must not be removed by the licensee within 48 hours after the pesticide use.

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (5) A licensee who uses a pesticide in a multi-residence restricted access area must

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) before or immediately following the use, provide a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) to the owner or manager of the building or the agent of either, and

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (b) either

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (i)  provide a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) to each person who has access to the treatment area within 48 hours after the use, or

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (ii)  immediately following the use, post a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) and (2) at each entrance to the treatment area, which notice must not be removed by the licensee for at least 48 hours after the pesticide use.

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (5.1) Subject to subsection (5.3), before using a pesticide, other than an excluded pesticide, in an outdoor area of private residential land, a licensee or, if there is no licensee, a certificate holder, must provide a treatment notice that complies with section 63 (1) to

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
paragraph: (a) the occupant of the land,

heading: Public notification requirements - licensee
