paragraph: (5) For the purposes of subsection (1), a person who commits an offence by failing to file a report required by this Act or the regulations is deemed to be continuing the commission of the offence each day that the report is not filed.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (6) An order is not a statutory instrument for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Exigent circumstances
paragraph: 22 (1) In the case of exigent circumstances, an order may be given orally on the condition that it is followed, within seven days, by a written order issued in accordance with section 21.

heading: Exigent circumstances
paragraph: Meaning of exigent circumstances

heading: Exigent circumstances
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, exigent circumstances includes circumstances in which the delay that is necessary to issue a written order that meets the requirements of subsection 21(3) would result in danger to human life or to the environment.

heading: Notice of intent
paragraph: 23 (1) Except in exigent circumstances, an enforcement officer shall, whenever practicable, before issuing an order,

heading: Notice of intent
paragraph: (a) provide every person who will be subject to the order with an oral or written notice of the officer's intention to issue it; and

heading: Notice of intent
paragraph: (b) allow a reasonable opportunity in the circumstances for the person to make oral representations.

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (2) The notice of intent to issue the order must include

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (a) a statement of the purpose of the notice;

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (b) a reference to the statutory authority under which the order is to be issued; and

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (c) a statement that the party notified may make oral representations to the enforcement officer within the period stated in the notice.

heading: Compliance with order
paragraph: 24 (1) A person to whom an order is directed shall, immediately on receipt of the order or a copy of it or on being directed by an enforcement officer in an order given orally under subsection 22(1), comply with the order.

heading: No bar to proceedings
paragraph: (2) The issuance of or compliance with an order in respect of a person's alleged contravention of this Act or the regulations is not a bar to any proceedings against the person under this or any other Act in relation to the alleged contravention.

heading: Intervention by enforcement officer
paragraph: 25 (1) If a person to whom an order is directed fails to take any measures specified in it, an enforcement officer may take the measures or cause them to be taken.

heading: Access to property
paragraph: (2) An enforcement officer or other person authorized or required by an enforcement officer to take measures under subsection (1) may enter and have access to any place or property and may do any reasonable thing that may be necessary in the circumstances.

heading: Personal liability
paragraph: (3) Any person, other than a person referred to in subsection 21(1), who provides assistance or advice in taking the measures specified in an order or who takes any measures authorized or required by an enforcement officer under subsection (1) is not personally liable either civilly or criminally in respect of any act or omission in the course of providing assistance or advice or taking any measures under that subsection unless it is established that the person acted in bad faith.

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: 26 (1) Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover the costs and expenses of and incidental to any measures taken under subsection 25(1) from any person who caused or contributed to the alleged contravention, to the extent of the person's negligence in causing or contributing to the alleged contravention.

heading: Costs must have been reasonably incurred
paragraph: (2) The costs and expenses may only be recovered to the extent that they can be established to have been reasonably incurred in the circumstances.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (3) A claim under this section may be sued for and recovered by Her Majesty in right of Canada with costs in proceedings brought or taken in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Recourse or indemnity
paragraph: (4) This section does not limit or restrict any right of recourse or indemnity that a person may have against any other person.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (5) If events giving rise to a claim under this section occur, no proceedings in respect of the claim may be instituted more than five years after the day on which the events occur or become evident to the Minister, whichever is later.

heading: Minister's certificate
paragraph: (6) A document purporting to have been issued by the Minister certifying the day on which the events giving rise to a claim under this section came to the knowledge of the Minister shall be received in evidence and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the document is to be considered as proof of that fact without proof of the signature or of the official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and without further proof.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: 27 (1) Any person to whom an order is directed may, by notice in writing given to the Chief Review Officer within 30 days after the day on which the person receives a copy of the written order or after the oral order is given, make a request to the Chief Review Officer for a review of the order.

heading: Extension of period for request
paragraph: (2) The Chief Review Officer may extend the period within which a request for a review may be made if, in his or her opinion, it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: 28 (1) At any time before a notice requesting a review of an order is received by the Chief Review Officer, the enforcement officer may, after giving reasonable notice,

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (a) amend or suspend a term or condition of the order, or add a term or condition to, or delete a term or condition from, the order;

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (b) cancel the order;

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (c) correct a clerical error in the order; or

heading: Variation or cancellation of order
paragraph: (d) extend the duration of the order for a period of not more than 180 days less the number of days that have passed after the day on which the order was received by the person who is subject to it.

heading: Notice of intent
paragraph: (2) Except in exigent circumstances, an enforcement officer shall, whenever practicable, before exercising a power under paragraph (1)(a) or (d),

heading: Notice of intent
paragraph: (a) provide every person who will be subject to the order with an oral or written notice of the officer's intention to exercise the power; and

heading: Notice of intent
paragraph: (b) allow a reasonable opportunity in the circumstances for the person to make oral representations.

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (3) The notice of intent to exercise a power under paragraph (1)(a) must include

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (a) a statement of the purpose of the notice;

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (b) a reference to the statutory authority under which the power is to be exercised; and

heading: Contents of notice of intent
paragraph: (c) a statement that the party notified may make oral representations to the enforcement officer within the period stated in the notice.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 29 The Minister may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing the form of reporting to enforcement officers under subparagraph 21(2)(f)(ii) and specifying the information required to be contained in or to accompany the report; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) of either particular or general application, respecting representations made to enforcement officers under paragraph 23(1)(b) or 28(2)(b).

heading: Review
paragraph: 30 Sections 257 to 271 of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 apply, with any modifications that the circumstances require, to a review requested of any order.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: 31 No person shall obstruct an enforcement officer or analyst or hinder any of them in carrying out their functions under this Act.

heading: Knowingly providing false or misleading information, etc.
paragraph: 32 (1) No person shall, with respect to any matter related to this Act, knowingly

heading: Knowingly providing false or misleading information, etc.
paragraph: (a) provide any person with false or misleading information, results or samples; or

heading: Knowingly providing false or misleading information, etc.
paragraph: (b) file a document that contains false or misleading information.

heading: Negligently providing false or misleading information, etc.
paragraph: (2) No person shall, with respect to any matter related to this Act, negligently

heading: Negligently providing false or misleading information, etc.
paragraph: (a) provide any person with false or misleading information, results or samples; or

heading: Negligently providing false or misleading information, etc.
paragraph: (b) file a document that contains false or misleading information.

heading: Offence
paragraph: 33 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes

heading: Offence
paragraph: (a) section 4, subsection 24(1), section 31 or subsection 32(1);

heading: Offence
paragraph: (b) any provision of the regulations designated by regulations made under paragraph 3(f); or

heading: Offence
paragraph: (c) an order made by a court under this Act.

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (2) Every individual who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable,

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $15,000 and not more than $1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years, or to both, and

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $30,000 and not more than $2,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years, or to both; or

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $5,000 and not more than $300,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both, and

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $10,000 and not more than $600,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both.

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (3) Every person, other than an individual or a corporation referred to in subsection (4), who commits and offence under subsection (1) is liable,

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $500,000 and not more than $6,000,000, and

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $1,000,000 and not more than $12,000,000; or

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $100,000 and not more than $4,000,000, and

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $200,000 and not more than $8,000,000.

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (4) Every corporation that commits an offence under subsection (1) and that the court determines under section 37 to be a small revenue corporation is liable,

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $75,000 and not more than $4,000,000, and

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $150,000 and not more than $8,000,000; or

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $25,000 and not more than $2,000,000, and

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $50,000 and not more than $4,000,000.

heading: Offence
paragraph: 34 (1) Every person commits an offence who contravenes any provision of the Act or the regulations, other than a provision the contravention of which is an offence under subsection 33(1).

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (2) Every individual who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable,

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $100,000, and

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $200,000; or

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $25,000, and

heading: Penalty - individuals
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $50,000.

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (3) Every person, other than an individual or a corporation referred to in subsection (4), that commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable,

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $500,000, and

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $1,000,000; or

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $250,000, and

heading: Penalty - other persons
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $500,000.

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (4) Every corporation that commits an offence under subsection (1) and that the court determines under section 37 to be a small revenue corporation is liable,

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $250,000, and

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $500,000; or

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $50,000, and

heading: Penalty - small revenue corporations
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $100,000.

heading: Continuing offences
paragraph: 35 If a contravention of a provision of this Act or of the regulations is committed or continued on more than one day, it constitutes a separate offence for each day on which it is committed or continued.

heading: Deeming - second and subsequent offence
paragraph: 36 (1) For the purposes of sections 33 and 34, a conviction for a particular offence under this Act is deemed to be a conviction for a second or subsequent offence if the court is satisfied that the offender has been previously convicted - under any Act of Parliament, or any Act of the legislature of a province, that relates to water resource management - of a substantially similar offence.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only to previous convictions on indictment and to previous convictions on summary conviction, and to previous convictions under any similar procedure under any Act of the legislature of a province.

heading: Determination of small revenue corporation status
paragraph: 37 For the purpose of sections 33 and 34, a court may determine a corporation to be a small revenue corporation if the court is satisfied that the corporation's gross revenues for the 12 months immediately before the day on which the subject matter of the proceedings arose - or, if it arose on more than one day, for the 12 months immediately before the first day on which the subject matter of the proceedings arose - were not more than $5,000,000.

heading: Relief from minimum fine
paragraph: 38 The court may impose a fine that is less than the minimum amount provided for in any of subsections 33(2) to (4) if it is satisfied, on the basis of evidence submitted to the court, that the minimum fine would cause undue financial hardship. The court shall provide reasons if it imposes a fine that is less than the minimum amount provided for in that subsection.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: 39 If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act and the court is satisfied that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any property, benefit or advantage, the court shall order the person to pay an additional fine in an amount equal to the court's estimation of the value of that property, benefit or advantage. The additional fine may exceed the maximum amount of any fine that may otherwise be imposed under this Act.

heading: Notice to shareholders
paragraph: 40 If a corporation that has shareholders has been convicted of an offence under this Act, the court shall make an order directing the corporation to notify its shareholders, in the manner and within the time directed by the court, of the facts relating to the commission of the offence and of the details of the punishment imposed.

heading: Liability of directors, officers, etc., of corporation
paragraph: 41 (1) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, any director, officer, agent or mandatary of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the penalty provided for by this Act for an individual in respect of the offence committed by the corporation, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Directors' and officers' duties
paragraph: (2) Every director and officer of a corporation shall take all reasonable care to ensure that the corporation complies with

heading: Directors' and officers' duties
paragraph: (a) this Act and the regulations; and

heading: Directors' and officers' duties
paragraph: (b) any orders and directions of, and prohibitions and requirements imposed by, any court, the Minister, enforcement officers and analysts.

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: 42 The fundamental purpose of sentencing for offences under this Act is to contribute to respect for this Act through the imposition of just sanctions that have as their objectives

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: (a) to deter the offender and any other person from committing offences under this Act;

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: (b) to denounce unlawful conduct that harms water resources; and

heading: Fundamental purpose of sentencing
paragraph: (c) to restore the environment harmed by the offence.

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: 43 (1) In addition to the principles and factors that the court is otherwise required to consider, including those set out in sections 718.1 to 718.21 of the Criminal Code, the court shall consider the following principles when sentencing a person who is convicted of an offence under this Act:

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (a) the amount of the fine should be increased to account for every aggravating factor associated with the offence, including the aggravating factors set out in subsection (2); and

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (b) the amount of the fine should reflect the gravity of each aggravating factor associated with the offence.

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (2) The aggravating factors are the following:

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (a) the offence caused damage or risk of damage to the environment;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (b) the offence caused damage or risk of damage to any unique, particularly important or vulnerable environment;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (c) the damage caused by the offence is extensive, persistent or irreparable;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (d) the offender committed the offence intentionally or recklessly;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (e) the offender failed to take reasonable steps to prevent the commission of the offence despite having the financial means to do so;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (f) by committing the offence or failing to take action to prevent its commission, the offender increased revenue or decreased costs or intended to increase revenue or decrease costs;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (g) the offender committed the offence despite having been warned by an enforcement officer of the circumstances that subsequently became the subject of the offence;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (h) the offender has a history of non-compliance with federal or provincial legislation that relates to water resource management; and

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) after the commission of the offence, the offender

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) attempted to conceal its commission,

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (ii) failed to take prompt action to prevent, mitigate or remediate its effects, or

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (iii) failed to take prompt action to reduce the risk of committing similar offences in the future.

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: (3) The absence of an aggravating factor set out in subsection (2) is not a mitigating factor.

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: Meaning of damage

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of paragraphs (2)(a) to (c), damage includes loss of use value and non-use value.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (5) If the court is satisfied of the existence of one or more of the aggravating factors set out in subsection (2) but decides not to increase the amount of the fine because of that factor, the court shall give reasons for that decision.

heading: Application of fines
paragraph: 44 (1) All fines received by the Receiver General in respect of the commission of an offence under this Act, other than fines collected under the Contraventions Act, are to be credited to the Environmental Damages Fund, an account in the accounts of Canada, and used for purposes related to protecting, conserving or restoring the environment or for administering that Fund.

heading: Recommendations of court
paragraph: (2) The court imposing the fine may recommend to the Minister that all or a portion of the fine credited to the Environmental Damages Fund be paid to a person or an organization specified by the court for a purpose referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: 45 (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any punishment imposed, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (b) directing the person to take any action that the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any damage to the environment that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (c) directing the person to post a bond, provide surety or pay into court an amount of money that the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement mentioned in this section;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (d) directing the person to carry out environmental effects monitoring in the manner established by the Minister or directing the person to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount for the purposes of environmental effects monitoring;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (e) directing the person to implement an environmental management system that meets a recognized Canadian or international standard specified by the court;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (f) directing the person to have an environmental audit conducted by a person of a class and at the times specified by the Minister and directing the person to remedy any deficiencies revealed during the audit;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (g) directing the person to pay to Her Majesty in right of Canada an amount of money that the court considers appropriate for the purpose of promoting sustainable water resource management;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (h) directing the person to publish, in the manner specified by the court, the facts relating to the commission of the offence and the details of the punishment imposed, including any orders made under this subsection;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (i) directing the person to notify, at the person's own cost and in the manner specified by the court, any person aggrieved or affected by the person's conduct of the facts relating to the commission of the offence and of the details of the punishment imposed, including any orders made under this subsection;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (j) directing the person to submit to the Minister, when requested to do so by the Minister at any time within three years after the date of conviction, any information with respect to the person's activities that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (k) directing the person to compensate any person, monetarily or otherwise, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken, caused to be taken or to be taken as a result of the act or omission that constituted the offence, including costs of assessing appropriate remedial or preventive action;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (l) directing the person to perform community service, subject to any reasonable conditions that may be imposed in the order;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (m) requiring the person to surrender to the Minister any licence issued under the regulations to the person;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (n) prohibiting the person from applying for any new licence under the regulations during any period that the court considers appropriate;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (o) directing the person to pay, in the manner prescribed by the court, an amount to environmental or other groups to assist in their work in or for a community near the place where the offence was committed;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (p) directing the person to pay, in a manner specified by the court, an amount to enable research to be conducted into the protection, conservation or restoration of international rivers;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (q) directing the person to pay, in the manner prescribed by the court, an amount to an educational institution including for scholarships for students enrolled in studies related to the environment; and

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (r) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the offender's good conduct and for deterring the person and any other person from committing offences under this Act.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to comply with an order made under paragraph (1)(h), the Minister may, in the manner that the court directed the person to do so, publish the facts relating to the commission of the offence and the details of the punishment imposed and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (3) If the court makes an order under paragraph (1)(g) or (k) directing a person to pay an amount to Her Majesty in right of Canada, or if the Minister incurs publication costs under subsection (2), the amount or the costs, as the case may be, constitute a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Enforcement
paragraph: (4) If the court makes an order under paragraph (1)(k) directing a person to pay an amount to another person, other than to Her Majesty in right of Canada, that other person may, by filing the order, enter as a judgment, in the superior court of the province in which the trial was held, the amount ordered to be paid, and that judgment is enforceable against the person who was directed to pay the amount in the same manner as if it were a judgment rendered against the offender in that court in civil proceedings.

heading: Cancellation or suspension of licences
paragraph: (5) If the court makes an order under paragraph (1)(m), any licence to which the order relates is cancelled unless the court makes an order suspending it for any period that the court considers appropriate.

heading: Coming into force and duration of order
paragraph: (6) An order made under subsection (1) comes into force on the day on which it is made or on any other day that the court may determine and shall not continue in force for more than three years after that day unless the court provides otherwise in the order.

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: 46 (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, the court may, in addition to any punishment imposed, order that any seized thing by means of or in relation to which the offence was committed, or any proceeds of its disposition, be forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Return if no forfeiture ordered
paragraph: (2) If the court does not order the forfeiture, the seized thing or the proceeds of its disposition shall be returned or paid to its lawful owner or the person lawfully entitled to it.

heading: Retention or sale
paragraph: 47 If a fine is imposed on a person who is convicted of an offence, any seized thing, or any proceeds of its disposition, may be retained until the fine is paid or the thing may be sold in satisfaction of the fine and the proceeds applied, in whole or in part, in payment of the fine.

heading: Compensation for loss of property
paragraph: 48 (1) If a person has been convicted of an offence under this Act, the court may, at the time sentence is imposed and on the application of the person aggrieved, order the offender to pay to the aggrieved person an amount by way of satisfaction or compensation for loss of or damage to property suffered by that person as a result of the commission of the offence.

heading: Enforcement
paragraph: (2) If the amount ordered to be paid under subsection (1) is not paid without delay, the aggrieved person may, by filing the order, enter as a judgment, in the superior court of the province in which the trial was held, the amount ordered to be paid, and that judgment is enforceable against the offender in the same manner as if it were a judgment rendered against the offender in that court in civil proceedings.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 49 No proceedings by way of summary conviction in respect of an offence under this Act may be instituted more than five years after the day on which the subject matter of the proceedings arose, unless the prosecutor and the defendant agree that they may be instituted after the five years.

heading: Publication of information about contraventions
paragraph: 50 (1) For the purpose of encouraging compliance with this Act and the regulations, the Minister shall maintain, in a registry accessible to the public, information about all convictions of corporations for offences under this Act.

heading: Retention
paragraph: (2) Information in the registry is to be maintained for a minimum of five years.

heading: Report - operations under the Act
paragraph: 51 As soon as practicable after the 31st day of December of each year, the Minister shall prepare and cause a report of the operations under this Act for that year to be tabled in each House of Parliament.

heading: Review - sections 33 to 50
paragraph: 52 (1) The Minister shall, 10 years after the day on which this section comes into force and every 10 years after that, undertake a review of sections 33 to 50.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall, no later than one year after the day on which the review is undertaken, cause a report on the review to be tabled in each House of Parliament.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the International River Improvements Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the International River Improvements Act; (Loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: international river means water flowing from any place in Canada to any place outside Canada; (cours d'eau international)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: international river improvement means a dam, obstruction, canal, reservoir or other work the purpose or effect of which is

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) to increase, decrease or alter the natural flow of an international river, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) to interfere with, alter or affect the actual or potential use of the international river outside Canada; (ouvrage destine a l'amelioration d'un cours d'eau international)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment. (ministre)

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: 3 (1) An international river improvement is excepted from the operation of the Act if:

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a) the improvement has or will have in its operation an effect of less than 3 cm on the level or less than 0.3 m3/s on the flow of water at the Canadian boundary; or

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (b) the improvement is of a temporary nature, to be operated for a period not exceeding two years.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (2) A person who intends to construct an international river improvement that is excepted from the application of the Act under subsection (1) shall notify and provide the Minister in writing with the information referred to in paragraphs 6(a) to (e).

heading: Applications
paragraph: 6 An application for a licence under the Act shall be addressed to the Minister and shall contain the following information:

heading: Applications
paragraph: (a) the name, address and occupation of the applicant;

heading: Applications
paragraph: (b) the name and a clear description of the international river on which an international river improvement is to be made;

heading: Applications
paragraph: (c) the place where the said improvement is to be made and a description of the improvement;

heading: Applications
paragraph: (d) details as to the effect of the improvement on the level or flow of water at the Canadian boundary;

heading: Applications
paragraph: (e) details as to the effect of the improvement on the use of water outside Canada;

heading: Applications
paragraph: (f) details of the adverse effects of the improvement on flood control and other uses of water together with information as to plans to minimize such effects;

heading: Applications
paragraph: (g) a brief economic analysis of the direct and indirect benefit and costs of and resulting from the improvement; and

heading: Applications
paragraph: (h) any further details concerning the improvement tending to indicate that it is compatible with a sound development of the resources and economy of Canada.

heading: Applications
paragraph: 7 An application for a licence shall be accompanied by

heading: Applications
paragraph: (a) details of any agreement if it is intended to sell outside Canada, any part of the Canadian share of down-stream power resulting from a proposed international river improvement; and

heading: Applications
paragraph: (b) a copy of the licence for the project issued by the appropriate provincial authority.

heading: Applications
paragraph: 8 The Minister may, on receipt of an application for a licence, require that such further information pertaining to the international river improvement be submitted as is necessary to enable the Minister to dispose of the application.

heading: Licences
paragraph: 10 (1) Where an applicant for a licence has supplied all the information required by these Regulations the Minister may

heading: Licences
paragraph: (a) issue to him a licence for a period not exceeding 50 years; and

heading: Licences
paragraph: (b) upon the expiration of any licence issue a further licence for a period not exceeding 50 years.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (2) Each licence shall stipulate the terms and conditions under which the international river improvement may be constructed, operated and maintained, and the period for which it is issued.

heading: Licences
paragraph: 11 Any person who assigns or transfers a licence shall, at least one month before the assignment or the transfer, inform the Minister in writing.

heading: Licences
paragraph: 12 Upon the request of a licensee, his heirs, executors, administrators, successors or assigns, the Minister may vary the terms and conditions of a licence.

heading: Licences
paragraph: 13 (1) Subject to subsection (2), where a licensee has failed to comply with the terms and conditions of the licence within six months after being requested in writing by the Minister to do so, the Minister may cancel the licence.

heading: Licences
paragraph: (2) Before a licence is cancelled, the Minister shall cause to be given to the licensee

heading: Licences
paragraph: (a) reasonable notice in writing of the proposed cancellation, explaining the grounds on which the Minister proposes to cancel the licence; and

heading: Licences
paragraph: (b) reasonable opportunity to respond and to make representations as to why the licence should not be cancelled.

heading: Application of sections 16 (2) and 37 (2) of the Act
paragraph: 1		  Until June 1, 2004, this regulation applies immediately, despite sections 16 (2) and 37 (2) of the Act, to a forest stewardship plan, woodlot licence plan, range use plan, and range stewardship plan, as applicable.

heading: Invasive plant species specified
paragraph:
2
		  For the purposes of section 47 of the Forest and Range Practices Act, the prescribed species of invasive plants are as follows:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "dilution ratio" means a ratio calculated by dividing the best estimate of the 10-year return period 7-day low flow in the receiving stream by the maximum 7 day average effluent flow, where

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the 10-year return period 7-day low flow is the magnitude of flow such that the average flow for 7 consecutive days is expected to be less than this magnitude once in any 10 year period, based on statistical analysis of observed stream flow, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) if sufficient data is not available to calculate the 10-year return period 7-day low flow or the discharge is to a lake, the dilution ratio must be calculated using a method and data that are to the satisfaction of a director;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "land-based finfish facility" means a fish hatchery, rearing pond, or other similar facility where finfish are fed, nurtured, held, maintained or reared in fresh water to reach a size for release or for market sale, but does not include a net pen facility or spawning channel;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "non-filterable residue concentration" means the concentration of non-filterable residue determined according to the British Columbia Laboratory Methods Manual: 2003 - for the Analysis of Water, Wastewater, Sediment, Biological Materials and Discrete Ambient Air Samples, Victoria, August 2003, as updated from time to time, published by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "total phosphorous concentration" means the total concentration of phosphorus determined according to the British Columbia Laboratory Methods Manual: 2003 - for the Analysis of Water, Wastewater, Sediment, Biological Materials and Discrete Ambient Air Samples, Victoria, August 2003, as updated from time to time, published by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy.

heading: Exemption
paragraph:
2
		  The owner of a land-based finfish facility is exempt from section 6 (2) and (3) of the Environmental Management Act with respect to the discharge of wastes from the land-based finfish facility if the owner

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (a) submits a preoperational report, if required under section 3,

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (b) registers under section 4 of this regulation, and

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (c) complies with the requirements set out in this regulation.

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: 3		  (1) Subject to subsection (2) the owner of a land-based finfish facility must submit a receiving water quality report to a director before construction begins on

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: (a) a land-based finfish facility built after the date this regulation comes into force, or

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: (b) an expansion of a land-based finfish facility if the proposed resulting annual production is 20% greater than the annual production before the expansion.

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: (2) Unless requested by a director, a receiving water quality report is not required for facilities with a dilution ratio greater than 20 to 1.

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: (3) The receiving water quality report must include an analysis of the proposed discharge, the existing beneficial uses of the receiving water and predicted effects the proposed discharge will have on the receiving water, including, but not limited to

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: (a) hydraulic effects,

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: (b) the effects of both nitrogen and phosphorous compounds and the potential for eutrophication of the receiving waters, and

heading: Water quality report
paragraph: (c) the effect on receiving water temperature and dissolved oxygen concentrations.

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph:
4
		  (1) An owner of a land-based finfish facility must submit a completed registration to a director before construction of the facility begins.

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (2) A registration under subsection (1) must include

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (a) the name, mailing address and phone number of the owner of the land-based finfish facility,

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (b) the name, mailing address and phone number of the operator of the land-based finfish facility if these differ from those of the owner,

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (c) the location and mailing address of the land-based finfish facility,

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (d) a site plan showing

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (i)  the site boundaries,

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (ii)  all building and works, and

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (iii)  all water courses, nearby wells, water intake and effluent discharge locations,

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (e) the annual finfish production rate in kilograms,

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (f) the maximum daily amount of effluent in cubic metres to be discharged by the land-based finfish facility into the receiving waters,

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (g) the dilution ratio, and

heading: Registration for exemption
paragraph: (h) the number printed on the aquaculture licence issued by the minister charged with the administration of the Fisheries Act.

heading: Reporting requirements
paragraph: 5		  The owner of a land-based finfish facility must give 60 days prior notice in writing to a director of any substantial change in registration information submitted under section 4.

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A person must not discharge effluent from a land-based finfish facility to the environment

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (a) if the non-filterable residue concentration in the effluent exceeds

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (i)  10 mg/L and the dilution ratio is less than 20 to 1, or

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (ii)  20 mg/L and the dilution ratio is 20 to 1 or greater,

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (b) if the total phosphorous concentration in the effluent exceeds

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (i)  0.1 mg/L and the dilution ratio is less than 20 to 1, or

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (ii)  0.2 mg/L and the dilution ratio is 20 to 1 or greater, or

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (c) if the effluent has detectable chlorine as measured by the amperometric titration method as defined by the American Public Health Association, Standard Methods 17th Edition, New York, 1989.

heading: Effluent standards
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1) (b), a total phosphorous concentration more or less stringent than (1) (b) (i) or (ii) may be specified by a director.

heading: General requirements
paragraph:
7
		  (1) The operator of a land-based finfish facility must not discharge to surface water or ground water

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (a) sand, silt, mud, solids, sludges, filter backwash, debris or other pollutants arising from treatment or control of water supply or effluent,

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (b) untreated cleaning wastes such as those obtained from a vacuum or standpipe bottom drain system,

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (c) accumulated solids from raceways or ponds,

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (d) detergents, disinfecting agents, cleaning agents or chemicals, if the effluent does not pass a 96 hour LC20 bioassay test as defined by Environment Canada's Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Effluents to Rainbow Trout, or

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (e) dead fish, blood, or processing wastes.

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (2) The operator of a federal or provincial land-based finfish facility that rears fish for release into the wild may release fish carcasses to the originating surface waters if the carcasses result from the removal of eggs and sperm.

heading: Waste management plan
paragraph:
8
		  An owner of a land-based finfish farm must, upon request of a director, prepare and submit to a director a written waste management plan.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "applicant" means a person applying for a disposition of Crown land under this Act or a former or other Act respecting Crown land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "boundary by agreement" means a conventional boundary located by agreement between the government and the adjoining owner;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commissioner" means the person appointed under the Public Service Act as commissioner in charge of any land recording district, and includes the minister, deputy minister, an assistant deputy minister and a person authorized by the minister to act for the minister in the portion of British Columbia for which the person may be appointed to discharge the duties of a commissioner under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "construction purpose" includes, without limitation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the building or maintenance of a road, railway bed, runway, berm, dam, impoundment, breakwater, dike, levee, foundation, rock wall and other similar thing, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the providing of fill and riprap;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "conventional boundary" means a boundary consisting of a straight line or a series of straight lines of fixed direction and length conforming as nearly as possible to the natural boundary, but eliminating minor sinuosities;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "corporation" means a corporation incorporated or registered in British Columbia;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Crown grant" means an instrument in writing conveying Crown land in fee simple;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Crown land", subject to section 1.1, means land, whether or not it is covered by water, or an interest in land, vested in the government;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "director" means a person employed under the Public Service Act and designated by the minister as a director for the purposes of this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "disposition" means the act of disposal or an instrument by which the act of disposal is effected or evidenced, or by which an interest in Crown land is disposed of or effected, or by which the government divests itself of or creates an interest in Crown land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fossil" means fossil as defined by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "interest" in reference to land includes a right or estate in that land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land district" means a portion of British Columbia that is a land district under section 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land recording district" means a portion of British Columbia that is a land recording district under section 3;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "natural boundary" means the visible high water mark of any lake, river, stream or other body of water where the presence and action of the water are so common and usual, and so long continued in all ordinary years, as to mark on the soil of the bed of the body of water a character distinct from that of its banks, in vegetation, as well as in the nature of the soil itself;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "public road" means a portion of Crown land designated or indicated as a road on a plan of survey made under this Act, whether or not a road is constructed, and includes a road allowance or walkway allowance established under section 79;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "registrar" means the registrar under the Land Title Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "registry", except in Part 1.1, means the Crown land registry continued under section 7;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "reserved land" means Crown land that has been withdrawn from disposition under this or any other Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "right of way" means a statutory right of way as defined in the Land Title Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "surveyed land" means land the survey of which is accepted and confirmed by the signature of the Surveyor General on a plan made under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Surveyor General" means the Surveyor General of British Columbia.

heading: Exclusions from Crown land definition
paragraph: 1.1		  A reference in a provision of this Act to Crown land does not include land referred to in section 6 (1) of the Public Agency Accommodation Act unless that provision of this Act is expressly made applicable to that land under section 6 (2) or (3) of the Public Agency Accommodation Act.

heading: Land districts
paragraph: 2		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation,

heading: Land districts
paragraph: (a) constitute a part of British Columbia as a land district, and

heading: Land districts
paragraph: (b) amend or cancel a land district whether constituted under this or a former Act.

heading: Land recording districts
paragraph:
3
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation,

heading: Land recording districts
paragraph: (a) constitute a part of British Columbia as a land recording district, and

heading: Land recording districts
paragraph: (b) amend or cancel a land recording district whether constituted under this or a former Act.

heading: Administration of Crown land
paragraph:
4
		  The minister has the administration of all Crown land except land specifically under the administration of another minister, branch or agency of government.

heading: Geographical names
paragraph:
5
		  The minister is responsible for geographical names in British Columbia.

heading: Base mapping and land related information systems
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The minister is responsible for and may undertake, commission, coordinate and set standards for base mapping and land related information systems in British Columbia and for related remote sensing and survey control functions.

heading: Base mapping and land related information systems
paragraph: (2) The minister may distribute to any person a copy of any map, air photo or land related information made or obtained under subsection (1).

heading: Base mapping and land related information systems
paragraph: (3) The minister may make regulations prescribing fees for the purposes of subsection (2) of this section, section 7.1 (4) of the Park Act and section 3 (4) of the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act.

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: 7		  (1) The Crown land registry is continued to record all lands administered by the government, and to record the acquisition and disposition of those lands, for the purpose of maintaining an inventory of Crown land.

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (2) The minister is responsible for the security and maintenance of the registry.

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (3) The registry is to be open to any person during regular business hours for the examination and inspection of the records of the registry.

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (4) Every ministry of the government must record in the registry all Crown lands under its administration, and the acquisition in fee simple and disposition of those lands, in a manner acceptable to the minister.

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (4.1) If the final agreement of a treaty first nation requires that survey plans of treaty lands be filed in the registry, the Surveyor General must file a copy of a final plan to which the requirement applies in the registry, whether or not the treaty lands include or consist of former federal Crown land.

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph:
(5) 
            Subsection (4) does not apply to the following:

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (a) a public road or highway established under this Act, the Highway Act, the Transportation Act, the Community Charter or the Local Government Act;

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (b) a forest service road established under the Forest Act;

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (c) an agreement to harvest Crown timber under the Forest Act;

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (d) a grazing or hay cutting licence or permit under the Range Act;

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (e) lands dedicated, transferred or vested in the government under section 107 (1) or 108 (2) of the Land Title Act.

heading: Crown land registry
paragraph: (6) No action may be brought by any person against the government for loss or damage caused by reliance on the records of the registry by that person for any reason or purpose including, without limitation, reliance for the purpose of establishing priorities of interest or reliance on the completeness of the records.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 7.1		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "integrated registry" means the Integrated Land and Resource Registry referred to in section 7.2 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "tenure" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any interest in Crown land that is granted or otherwise established under a prescribed instrument, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a prescribed designation or other status that, under an enactment, is given to, conferred on, or made or otherwise established in relation to Crown land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "tenure authority", in relation to a tenure, means a prescribed person.

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph:
7.2
		  (1) The minister must maintain the electronic database known as the Integrated Land and Resource Registry established by the ministry of the minister.

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (2) A tenure authority must submit prescribed information in respect of a tenure to the integrated registry

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (a) in the form and manner and within the time period required by the minister, and

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (b) in accordance with the standards established by the minister.

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (3) The minister may include in the integrated registry information other than information submitted under subsection (2) to the integrated registry.

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of facilitating the identification of information in the integrated registry, the minister may

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (a) assign a unique number to identify information submitted to or included in the integrated registry, and

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (b) include in a record of information in the integrated registry the unique number assigned to that information.

heading: Integrated Land and Resource Registry
paragraph: (5) The minister may delete or correct information in the integrated registry.

heading: No notice or knowledge of information in integrated registry
paragraph:
7.3
		  The inclusion of information in the integrated registry does not constitute

heading: No notice or knowledge of information in integrated registry
paragraph: (a) express, constructive or implied notice of the information to any person, or

heading: No notice or knowledge of information in integrated registry
paragraph: (b) express, constructive or implied knowledge of the information on the part of any person.

heading: Public access to integrated registry
paragraph:
7.4
		  (1) Subject to this section, the minister must make information in the integrated registry accessible to the public by electronic means and on conditions satisfactory to the minister.

heading: Public access to integrated registry
paragraph: (2) The minister may suspend one or more of the services provided in relation to the integrated registry if the minister is satisfied that circumstances are such that it is not practicable to provide those services.

heading: Public access to integrated registry
paragraph: (3) The minister may restrict access to designated information in the integrated registry.

heading: Public access to integrated registry
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (3), the minister may do one or more of the following:

heading: Public access to integrated registry
paragraph: (a) designate information in the integrated registry;

heading: Public access to integrated registry
paragraph: (b) define classes of persons or designated information;

heading: Public access to integrated registry
paragraph: (c) make different restrictions for different classes of persons or designated information.

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph:
7.5
		  (1) No legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against the government, the minister or an individual acting on behalf of or under the direction of the minister

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph: (a) because of anything done or omitted

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph: (i)  in the performance or intended performance of any duty under this Part, or

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph: (ii)  in the exercise or intended exercise of any power under this Part, or

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph: (b) for loss or damage caused by reliance on the information in the integrated registry for any reason or purpose including, without limitation, reliance for the purpose of establishing priorities of interest or reliance on the completeness of the information in the integrated registry.

heading: Personal liability protection
paragraph:
(2) 
            Subsection (1) does not apply to a person referred to in that subsection in relation to anything done or omitted by that person in bad faith.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
7.7
		  Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Part or the regulations made under this Part.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: 7.8		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing instruments for the purposes of the definition of "tenure";

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) prescribing designations or other statuses for the purposes of the definition of "tenure";

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) prescribing persons in relation to a tenure for the purposes of the definition of "tenure authority";

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) prescribing information that must be submitted to the integrated registry in respect of a tenure.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) In making regulations under this Part, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) define classes of persons or things, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) make different regulations for different classes of persons or things.

heading: If no disposition
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A person may not acquire by prescription, occupation not lawfully authorized or a colour of right, an interest in Crown land, or in any land as against the government's interest in it.

heading: If no disposition
paragraph: (2) A person does not acquire a right, vested or contingent, in Crown land, or a priority to Crown land by filing an application for Crown land under this Act.

heading: If no disposition
paragraph: (3) A disposition of Crown land is not binding on the government until the certificate of purchase, grant, lease, licence of occupation, right of way or easement is executed by the government under this Act.

heading: If no disposition
paragraph: (4) Negotiations or arrangements, whether in writing or otherwise, before the execution of the documents referred to in subsection (3) are not binding on and do not commit the government to perform or complete a disposition.

heading: Citizenship of grantee
paragraph:
9
		  A person who is not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada is not entitled to a Crown grant unless the person's application for a disposition of Crown land was allowed before May 1, 1970.

heading: Application for Crown land
paragraph:
10
		  (1) Subject to compliance with this Act and the regulations, a person of age 19 or over or a corporation or other association may apply for Crown land.

heading: Application for Crown land
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this Act obliges the government to consider an application for Crown land, or to dispose of Crown land on an application.

heading: Application for Crown land
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), the minister may refuse to receive an application for Crown land if

heading: Application for Crown land
paragraph: (a) the application is incomplete,

heading: Application for Crown land
paragraph: (b) the land is reserved from disposition under section 15,

heading: Application for Crown land
paragraph: (c) the land is withdrawn from disposition under section 16, or

heading: Application for Crown land
paragraph: (d) the Crown land is the subject of a minister's order under section 10.1.

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph:
10.1
		  (1) The minister may, by order, specify that no application for Crown land may be made in respect of one or more of the following:

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph: (a) an area of the province;

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph: (b) an activity;

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph: (c) a use;

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph: (d) a period of time;

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph: (e) a class of applicant.

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph: (2) An order made under subsection (1) must be published by the minister for the term of the order on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the minister.

heading: When no application for Crown land may be made
paragraph: (3) An order made under subsection (1) does not apply to an application that was received by the minister prior to the making of the order.

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph:
11
		  (1) Subject to compliance with this Act and the regulations, the minister may dispose of surveyed or unsurveyed Crown land by any of the following means, as the minister considers advisable in the public interest, to a person entitled under this Act:

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (a) application;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (b) public auction;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (c) public notice of tender;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (d) public drawing of lots;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (e) public request for proposals;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (f) listing with a brokerage licensed under the Real Estate Services Act;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (g) land exchanges.

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (2) The minister may, under subsection (1),

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (a) sell Crown land,

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (b) lease Crown land,

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (c) grant a right of way or easement over Crown land,

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (d) grant a licence to occupy Crown land, or

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (e) transfer ownership of fossils located on Crown land, grant the right to remove fossils from Crown land, or both, if done in accordance with section 50 (3.1).

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (3) In a disposition of Crown land under this section, the minister may impose the terms, covenants, stipulations and reservations the minister considers advisable, and without limiting those powers, the minister may impose some or all of the following terms:

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (a) the applicant must personally occupy and reside on the Crown land for a period set by the minister;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (b) the applicant must do that work and spend that money for permanent improvement of the Crown land within that period the minister requires;

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (c) the consideration that must be paid for a disposition of Crown land.

heading: Minister may dispose of Crown land
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not apply to a disposition under section 51 (1) or an exchange of Crown land under section 95.

heading: Crown grant of cancelled dedicated land
paragraph: 12		  (1) If, under Part 8 of the Land Title Act, a petitioner establishes to the satisfaction of the minister that

heading: Crown grant of cancelled dedicated land
paragraph: (a) the registrar has made an order under Part 8 of the Land Title Act cancelling all or part of the areas that were dedicated by the deposit of a plan in the land title office, and

heading: Crown grant of cancelled dedicated land
paragraph: (b) none of the dedicated areas cancelled by the order are required by the government or are otherwise reserved from disposition,

heading: Crown grant of cancelled dedicated land
paragraph: the minister, on application by the petitioner, on terms the minister considers appropriate and on payment of the prescribed fees, may make a fee simple grant to the petitioner of all or part of a cancelled dedicated area on payment of consideration determined by the minister.

heading: Crown grant of cancelled dedicated land
paragraph: (2) An application under this section must be accompanied by a certified copy of the order of the registrar made under Part 8 of the Land Title Act.

heading: Crown grant of cancelled dedicated land
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply to land in respect of which the registrar has made a vesting order under section 135 of the Land Title Act.

heading: Roads
paragraph: 13		  (1) In a disposition of Crown land under this or a former Act in which a portion of the land is designated as a road in the instrument evidencing the disposition or in a map or plan attached to it, unless there is express provision in the instrument to the contrary, the road is deemed to be,

heading: Roads
paragraph: (a) in the case of a disposition made before January 3, 1977, 20.1168 m in width, being 10.0584 m on each side of the centre line of the travelled portion of the road, and

heading: Roads
paragraph: (b) in the case of a disposition made after January 2, 1977, 20 m in width, being 10 m on each side of the centre line of the travelled portion of the road.

heading: Roads
paragraph: (2) No part of the road referred to in subsection (1) passes to any person under the instrument.

heading: Reserves
paragraph:
15
		  (1) In this section and section 16, "government body" means the Provincial government, a government corporation as defined in paragraphs (b) and (c) of the definition of "government corporation" in the Financial Administration Act, the federal government or a prescribed organization.

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, reserve Crown land from disposition under this Act for any purpose that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers advisable in the public interest, including for the use of a government body.

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (3) An order under subsection (2) may authorize a government body to place, construct, maintain or operate any works, structures or other improvements on the reserved land.

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (4) An order under subsection (2) may be subject to any terms and conditions the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers necessary or advisable.

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may amend or cancel all or part of a reserve established under this or a former Act.

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (6) An order under subsection (2) does not prevent the minister from issuing to an applicant a licence to occupy the Crown land reserved by the order for any of the following:

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (a) a period not longer than 2 years to conduct appraisals, inspections, analyses, inventories, surveys or other investigations of the land or of its natural resources;

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (b) a period not longer than 2 years for any purpose authorized under this Act;

heading: Reserves
paragraph: (c) construction of a road, non-commercial airstrip, bridge or trail over the land.

heading: Withdrawal from disposition
paragraph: 16		  (1) The minister may temporarily withdraw Crown land from disposition under this Act for any purpose the minister considers advisable in the public interest, including for the use of a government body.

heading: Withdrawal from disposition
paragraph: (2) The minister may authorize a government body to place, construct, maintain or operate any works, structures or other improvements on the land withdrawn under subsection (1).

heading: Withdrawal from disposition
paragraph: (3) The minister may impose any terms and conditions the minister considers necessary or advisable on the use of land temporarily withdrawn under subsection (1).

heading: Withdrawal from disposition
paragraph: (4) The minister may amend or cancel a withdrawal under subsection (1).

heading: Conditional withdrawal
paragraph:
17
		  (1) The minister may, if the minister considers it advisable in the public interest, designate a portion of Crown land for a particular use or for the conservation of natural or heritage resources.

heading: Conditional withdrawal
paragraph: (1.1) The minister may impose any terms and conditions the minister considers necessary or advisable on the use of land designated under subsection (1).

heading: Conditional withdrawal
paragraph: (2) A portion of Crown land designated under subsection (1) is withdrawn from disposition under this Act for any purpose that is not, in the opinion of the minister, compatible with the purpose for which the land has been designated.

heading: Conditional withdrawal
paragraph: (3) The minister may amend or cancel a designation made under subsection (1).

heading: Land below natural water boundary
paragraph:
18
		  (1) Except by order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, on the terms the Lieutenant Governor in Council may specify, unfilled Crown land below the natural boundary of a body of water must not be disposed of by Crown grant under this Act.

heading: Land below natural water boundary
paragraph: (2) Except by order of the minister, on the terms the minister may specify, filled Crown land below the natural boundary of a body of water must not be disposed of by Crown grant under this Act.

heading: Quarrying land
paragraph:
19
		  Except by order of the minister, on the terms the minister may specify, Crown land must not be disposed of by Crown grant under this Act if the minister believes it is suitable for mining, quarrying, digging or removal of building or construction materials, including, without limitation,

heading: Quarrying land
paragraph: (a) earth, soil, peat, marl, sand and gravel,

heading: Quarrying land
paragraph: (b) rock and natural substances that are used for a construction purpose on land that is not within a mineral title or group of mineral titles from which the rock or natural substance is mined, and

heading: Quarrying land
paragraph: (c) rock or a natural substance prescribed under section 2 (2) of the Mineral Tenure Act.

heading: Limit on area of Crown grant
paragraph: 20		  (1) Unless the applicant has first obtained a Crown grant to land covered by a prior certificate of purchase in the applicant's name, Crown land of an area greater than 520 ha must not be disposed of by Crown grant under this Act at any one time to any one applicant.

heading: Limit on area of Crown grant
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the minister may dispose of an area greater than 520 ha, by Crown grant, for commercial, industrial, railway or airport purposes.

heading: Limit on area of lease
paragraph:
21
		  (1) Crown land of an area greater than 520 ha must not be disposed of by lease under this Act to any one applicant.

heading: Limit on area of lease
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the minister may dispose of, by lease, an area greater than 520 ha for grazing, commercial, industrial, railway, airport or watershed purposes.

heading: Term of lease
paragraph:
22
		  Except with the prior approval of the minister, Crown land must not be leased under this Act for a term longer than 60 years.

heading: Timbered land
paragraph:
23
		  Unless, in the opinion of the minister, Crown land is required for agricultural settlement and development or other higher economic use, Crown land that is suitable for the production of timber and pulpwood must not be disposed of by Crown grant under this Act.

heading: Payment for timber
paragraph:
24
		  A disposition of Crown land under this Act may provide for payment to the government of the value of the timber or a royalty on the timber on that land.

heading: Method of payment
paragraph:
25
		  If an applicant purchases Crown land under section 11, the minister may, despite section 48, if the unpaid balance of the purchase price has been secured to the minister's satisfaction, issue a Crown grant before the full purchase price has been paid.

heading: Interest on deferred payments
paragraph:
26
		  (1) Unless the minister orders otherwise in a particular case, if payment for Crown land is deferred, interest is to be charged at a prescribed rate on the outstanding balance from the date of the disposition.

heading: Interest on deferred payments
paragraph: (2) If money payable for a lease, right of way, easement, licence of occupation or royalty is not paid on the due date, interest may be charged at a prescribed rate on the unpaid sum from the date due.

heading: Interest on deferred payments
paragraph: (3) If payment of money for a survey carried out by or for the Surveyor General for a disposition of Crown land is deferred, interest on the deferred sum may be charged at a prescribed rate.

heading: Reservations to which purchasers are subject
paragraph:
27
		  Unless otherwise expressly provided in the certificate of purchase, the right of a purchaser under a certificate of purchase is, from the date of the certificate, subject to all of the following:

heading: Reservations to which purchasers are subject
paragraph: (a) the terms, covenants, stipulations, reservations and exemptions contained in this Act, the regulations or in the Crown grant;

heading: Reservations to which purchasers are subject
paragraph: (b) highways, streets, roads, trails and other ways existing at that date over or through the land;

heading: Reservations to which purchasers are subject
paragraph: (c) the reservations, exceptions and rights of way endorsed at the minister's direction on the certificate.

heading: Royalty on removal of certain materials
paragraph:
28
		  Leases or other dispositions granted for mining, quarrying, digging or removal of building or construction materials, including without limitation

heading: Royalty on removal of certain materials
paragraph: (a) earth, soil, peat, marl, sand and gravel,

heading: Royalty on removal of certain materials
paragraph: (b) rock and natural substances that are used for a construction purpose on land that is not within a mineral title or group of mineral titles from which the rock or natural substance is mined, and

heading: Royalty on removal of certain materials
paragraph: (c) rock or a natural substance prescribed under section 2 (2) of the Mineral Tenure Act,

heading: Royalty on removal of certain materials
