paragraph: may provide for payment of a royalty for material removed from the land at rates to be determined by the minister.

heading: Survey fees
paragraph: 29		  A disposition may provide for payment by the applicant of the cost of a survey of the land by or for the Surveyor General.

heading: Amendment of area under application
paragraph:
30
		  Subject to sections 20 and 21, on an application for a disposition, the minister may

heading: Amendment of area under application
paragraph: (a) reduce or extend the area applied for or the length of the boundary lines of the area, or

heading: Amendment of area under application
paragraph: (b) vary the location of the area.

heading: Transfers to Canada
paragraph:
31
		  (1) Subject to the terms, reservations and restrictions the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers advisable, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may transfer the administration, control and benefit of Crown land to the government of Canada either in perpetuity or for a specified period, and with or without consideration.

heading: Transfers to Canada
paragraph: (2) Except to the extent that it so provides, a transfer under subsection (1) is not subject to section 50.

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph:
32
		  (1) An application for disposition by purchase, lease, licence of occupation, easement or right of way must be

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (a) made to the minister in the form specified by the minister, and

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (b) accompanied by the application fee and the information required by the minister.

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (2) If the application complies with this Act and the regulations and has been accepted, the minister must publish the application on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the minister.

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (3) If the land is unsurveyed or if no evidence of survey is available, the applicant must

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (a) before making the application, fix securely in the ground, at one corner of the land to be applied for, a squared post or squared tree, at least 1 m above the ground level, and securely attach to the post or tree a written notice in the form specified by the minister of the applicant's intention to make an application for a disposition of the land described in the notice, and

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (b) with the application, provide the proof of the posting of the notice as required by the minister.

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (3.1) The minister may waive compliance with subsection (3).

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph:
(4) 
            Subsection (3) does not apply to

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (a) a licence of occupation for a year or less, or

heading: Application procedure for dispositions
paragraph: (b) a grant of right of way or easement.

heading: Public notice
paragraph:
33
		  (1) If the minister considers it advisable in the public interest, the minister may require the applicant to publish a notice of the applicant's application.

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (2) The notice must

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (a) be headed "Land Act: Notice of Application for a Disposition of Crown Land",

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (b) state the land recording district and location of the land,

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (c) state the applicant's address,

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (d) state the purpose for which the land is required, and

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (f) give notice that the named applicant has applied for specific land or land described in relation to the post, of a named area, more or less.

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (3) The applicant must publish the notice in the Gazette or a newspaper circulating in the land recording district where the land is located, or in both, for the number of issues and within the period required by the minister.

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (4) The applicant must provide proof of publication of the notice.

heading: Public comments on notice of application
paragraph:
33.1
		  (1) Before a disposition is made, a person may provide comments to the minister on the application for disposition.

heading: Public comments on notice of application
paragraph: (2) In the case of a disposition in relation to which the minister has required publication of a notice of the application in accordance with section 33 (1), the minister must accept comments for no less than 14 days after the notice is first published under section 33 (3).

heading: Public comments on notice of application
paragraph: (3) Failure to provide an opportunity to comment in accordance with this section, and including, without limitation, failure to publish an application in accordance with section 32 (2) does not render a disposition invalid.

heading: Disposition by minor
paragraph:
34
		  (1) A person who is eligible to hold a disposition under this Act, but is a minor, may hold and assign the land as if the person were of full age.

heading: Disposition by minor
paragraph: (2) A person who is a minor and who holds a certificate of purchase, lease, licence of occupation, right of way or easement of Crown land may hold and assign it as if the person were of full age.

heading: Feasibility studies, costs
paragraph:
35
		  (1) The minister may require an applicant to obtain and file with the minister, at the applicant's expense, feasibility studies, environmental assessments, timber cruises, land valuation appraisals, or other information about the application required by the minister.

heading: Feasibility studies, costs
paragraph: (2) If an application is made under section 32 or 40, or notice is given of an intention to make the application, the minister may estimate the cost

heading: Feasibility studies, costs
paragraph: (a) to assess the impact of making the disposition, or

heading: Feasibility studies, costs
paragraph: (b) to monitor compliance with terms to which the disposition would be subject if made.

heading: Feasibility studies, costs
paragraph: (3) The minister may require the applicant or proposed applicant to pay to the Minister of Finance all or part of the anticipated cost before the notice is acted on, the application considered or the disposition made.

heading: Security may be required
paragraph:
36
		  (1) The minister may require an applicant to deposit with the Minister of Finance a bond or other security for the performance and completion by the applicant of all the obligations and requirements specified by the minister.

heading: Security may be required
paragraph: (2) The security must be payable to the Minister of Finance for the amount and containing the terms required by the minister.

heading: Necessary information to be supplied on request
paragraph:
37
		  (1) The minister may require an applicant to provide proof, by signed statement or otherwise, with respect to a matter arising out of the application or with respect to the applicant's financial affairs.

heading: Necessary information to be supplied on request
paragraph: (2) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Necessary information to be supplied on request
paragraph: (a) knowingly provides information that is false or misleading with respect to a material fact contained in a signed statement under this section;

heading: Necessary information to be supplied on request
paragraph: (b) produces or relies upon a signed statement given by another person under this section while knowing the signed statement to be false or misleading with respect to a material fact contained in that signed statement.

heading: Lease
paragraph:
38
		  The minister may issue a lease of Crown land subject to the terms and reservations the minister considers advisable, including an option to purchase the land.

heading: Licence of occupation
paragraph:
39
		  The minister may issue a licence to occupy and use Crown land, called a "licence of occupation", subject to the terms and reservations the minister considers advisable.

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph:
40
		  (1) The minister may, subject to terms and conditions the minister considers advisable,

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (a) grant or otherwise create a right of way or easement over Crown land, and

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (b) grant or otherwise create over Crown land, the title to which is not registered under the Land Title Act, an easement without a dominant tenement for any purpose necessary for the operation and maintenance of the grantee's undertaking, including a right to flood.

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (2) An easement of the kind described in subsection (1) (b)

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (a) is not registrable, and

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (b) ceases to exist over land forming all or part of its servient tenement the title to which becomes registered under the Land Title Act, but continues over any part of its servient tenement the title to which remains unregistered.

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (4) An easement or right of way granted before or after May 1, 1970 may be continued or renewed by the minister for the period the minister believes proper, despite this Act or the Land Title Act, and even if the servient tenement has ceased to be Crown land.

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (5) To the extent necessary to give effect to this section, the rule requiring an easement to have a dominant and a servient tenement is abrogated.

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (6) In respect of easements other than rights of way

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (a) this section is retroactive in its application and applies to all easements over Crown land whenever created, and

heading: Right of way and easement
paragraph: (b) the government is deemed always to have been able to create easements by grant or otherwise.

heading: Failure to complete survey
paragraph: 41		  If an application for a disposition of unsurveyed Crown land has been approved subject to completion of a satisfactory survey, the minister may disallow the application if the survey is not completed in the time required by the minister or as extended by the Surveyor General.

heading: Date of disposition
paragraph:
42
		  (1) Unless otherwise specified by the minister, the date of a disposition under this Act is the date on which the instrument creating the disposition is executed on behalf of the government.

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph:
43
		  (1) If a person who holds a disposition of Crown land

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (a) defaults in payment of money due to the government, or

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (b) fails or neglects to observe or perform a covenant, stipulation or term required by the minister, or set out in the disposition,

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: the minister may send a notice by registered mail, addressed to the person at the person's last known address, requiring the person to pay the money due or to comply with the covenant, stipulation or term within 60 days after the notice is mailed.

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (2) If the default, failure or neglect continues after the 60 day period, the minister may cancel the disposition.

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (3) If the minister cancels a disposition under this section

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (a) the interest in the Crown land of the holder of the disposition and of all persons claiming through the holder is forfeited and at an end,

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (b) improvements to the land become government property, and

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (c) money paid for the disposition is forfeited to the government.

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (4) If the disposition is in respect of a right of way or easement, the minister may extend the time to pay or comply up to 2 years after the notice is mailed.

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (5) If a disposition, registered in a land title office, is cancelled, the minister may, by a certificate signed and sealed by the minister and setting out the reason for the cancellation, require the registrar to cancel registration.

heading: Cancellation of disposition
paragraph: (6) The certificate referred to in subsection (5) is the authority for the registrar of the land title office to cancel the registration.

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph:
44
		  (1) If the minister considers it advisable, the minister may, for an approved application or a disposition, amend or correct the approval or disposition, disallow the application or cancel the disposition, or make those changes and adjustments in the approval or disposition the minister considers advisable, if the minister finds any of the following:

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (a) a clerical error in the names or description of the applicant, the description of the Crown land, or any other material part of the approval or disposition;

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (b) that the Crown land is not available for disposition;

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (c) that the survey is incorrect;

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (d) that information provided by the applicant is incorrect.

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (2) If the minister disallows an application or cancels a disposition under this section, the minister may

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (a) repay to the applicant all or part of the money paid on the application or disposition,

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (b) repay to the applicant the applicant's survey costs, and

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (c) pay to the applicant that compensation the minister considers advisable.

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (3) If a cancelled or amended disposition is registered in a land title office, the minister may, by a certificate signed and sealed by the minister and setting out the reason for the cancellation or amendment, require the registrar to cancel or amend the registration.

heading: Amendment and cancellation if approval or grant improper
paragraph: (4) The minister's certificate referred to in subsection (3) is authority for the registrar to cancel or amend the registration.

heading: Abandonment of disposition
paragraph:
45
		  (1) A person holding a disposition of Crown land may abandon and terminate a disposition by notifying the minister in writing.

heading: Abandonment of disposition
paragraph: (2) All improvements on the land and all money paid on account are absolutely forfeited to and become the property of the government on abandonment and termination of a disposition under subsection (1).

heading: Debts payable on cancelled disposition
paragraph:
46
		  (1) Despite the cancellation or abandonment, unless the minister otherwise directs, the holder of a disposition that is cancelled or abandoned must pay all money and observe and perform all covenants, stipulations and terms of the disposition.

heading: Debts payable on cancelled disposition
paragraph: (2) Money remaining due to the government on a disposition is recoverable by the Minister of Finance as a debt due to the government.

heading: Delay on new disposition
paragraph:
47
		  The minister may, in the minister's discretion, withhold from disposition, for a period of not longer than one year, Crown land in a cancelled or abandoned disposition.

heading: Issue of Crown grant
paragraph:
48
		  (1) A Crown grant must issue in the name of an applicant for a disposition by purchase, subject to this Act, the regulations and the applicable terms, covenants and stipulations of any certificate of purchase, if the applicant pays the prescribed Crown grant fee and

heading: Issue of Crown grant
paragraph: (a) pays to the Minister of Finance the full purchase price, interest and all other money required to be paid for the disposition, and

heading: Issue of Crown grant
paragraph: (b) complies with the covenants, conditions and stipulations of the disposition.

heading: Issue of Crown grant
paragraph: (2) If an applicant dies and the conditions in subsection (1) are complied with, a Crown grant must issue to the personal representative of the deceased applicant.

heading: Form of Crown grant
paragraph:
49
		  (1) A disposition of Crown land in fee simple may be in a form specified by the minister.

heading: Form of Crown grant
paragraph: (2) The minister may, in a form specified by the minister, issue a supplementary grant of the timber to the registered owner of the land if

heading: Form of Crown grant
paragraph: (a) in a grant of Crown land, timber is reserved to the government, and

heading: Form of Crown grant
paragraph: (b) the reserved timber is not held by any other person under licence, lease, permit, sale or other instrument from the government.

heading: Form of Crown grant
paragraph: (3) A supplementary Crown grant is not to be issued under subsection (2) unless

heading: Form of Crown grant
paragraph: (a) the minister considers it advisable, and

heading: Form of Crown grant
paragraph: (b) the minister ascertains that the stumpage value of the timber is fully paid to the government.

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph:
50
		  (1) A disposition of Crown land under this or another Act

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (a) excepts and reserves the following interests, rights, privileges and titles:

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (i)  a right in the government, or any person acting for it, to resume any part of the land that is deemed to be necessary by the government for making roads, canals, bridges or other public works, but not more than 1/20 part of the whole of the land, and no resumption may be made of any land on which a building has been erected, or that may be in use as a garden or otherwise;

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (ii)  a right in the government, or any person acting for it or under its authority, to enter any part of the land, and to raise and get out of it any geothermal resources, fossils, minerals, whether precious or base, as defined in section 1 of the Mineral Tenure Act, coal, petroleum and any gas or gases, that may be found in, on or under the land, and to use and enjoy any and every part of the land, and its easements and privileges, for the purpose of the raising and getting, and every other purpose connected with them, paying reasonable compensation for the raising, getting and use;

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (iii)  a right in any person authorized by the government to take and occupy water privileges and to have and enjoy the rights of carrying water over, through or under any part of the land granted, as may be reasonably required for mining or agricultural purposes in the vicinity of the land, paying a reasonable compensation to the grantee, the grantee's successors and assigns;

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (iv)  a right in any person authorized by the government to take from any part of the land granted, without compensation, gravel, sand, stone, lime, timber or other material that may be required in the construction, maintenance or repair of a road, ferry, bridge or other public work,

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (b) conveys no right, title or interest to

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (i)  geothermal resources as defined in the Geothermal Resources Act,

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (ii)  minerals and placer minerals as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act,

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (iii)  coal,

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (iv)  petroleum as defined in the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act,

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (v)  gas, or

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (vi)  fossils

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: that may be found in or under the land, and

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (c) conveys no right, interest or estate to highways, within the meaning of the Transportation Act, existing over or through the land at the date of the disposition.

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (2)             Subsection (1) applies whether or not express words are used in the disposition, but is subject to subsections (3), (3.1) and (3.2).

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (3) A disposition of Crown land under another Act that expressly authorizes the disposition on terms different from those referred to in subsection (1) may be made on those terms, and in that case the disposition must refer to the Act that authorizes the different terms and state the terms on which the disposition is made.

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (3.1) A disposition referred to in section 11 (2) (e) may be made, if express words are used in the disposition.

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (3.2) If a final agreement of a treaty first nation provides for the addition to the treaty lands of the treaty first nation, a disposition of Crown land for the purpose of adding to those treaty lands may be made on terms different from those referred to in subsection (1), and in that case the disposition must refer to the final agreement and state the terms on which the disposition is made.

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (4) A disposition of Crown land may, by express words, except or reserve to the government rights and privileges more extensive than those referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (5) For all purposes, including section 23 of the Land Title Act, every disposition of Crown land is conclusively deemed to contain express words making the exceptions and reservations referred to in subsection (1) of this section, except to the extent that the disposition is made on different terms under subsection (3), (3.1) or (3.2).

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (6) The power under subsection (4) to except and reserve rights and privileges includes a power to create a right of way, and if this is done

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (a) the government is, with respect to the right of way, a grantee,

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (b) the right of way is conclusively deemed to be necessary for the operation and maintenance of the government's undertaking, and

heading: Exceptions and reservations
paragraph: (c) section 218 of the Land Title Act applies.

heading: Grant of Crown land to government corporations and bodies
paragraph: 51		  (1) Despite any other provision of this Act, Crown land may, with the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council and subject to the terms, reservations and restrictions that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers advisable, be disposed of by Crown grant under this Act, free or otherwise, to a government corporation, municipality, regional district, hospital board, university, college, board of education, francophone education authority as defined in the School Act or other government related body or to the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority continued under the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority Act or any of its subsidiaries.

heading: Grant of Crown land to government corporations and bodies
paragraph: (2) A disposition under subsection (1) may be limited to a specific public purpose.

heading: Power to delete terms in Crown grants
paragraph: 52		  (1) If the minister finds that a term, covenant, stipulation, reservation or exemption in a Crown grant issued under this or a former Act, other than one contained in the forms prescribed by the Act under which the Crown grant was issued, has been included in error or is no longer required in the public interest, the minister may declare the Crown grant to be void and of no effect or may amend or replace it.

heading: Power to delete terms in Crown grants
paragraph: (2) A certified copy of the declaration made under subsection (1) may be filed with the registrar of the land title district.

heading: Power to delete terms in Crown grants
paragraph: (3) The registrar must attach the copy of the declaration referred to in subsection (2) to the Crown grant and make appropriate entries in the register as the registrar considers necessary.

heading: Power to delete terms in Crown grants
paragraph: (4) The power conferred by this section may be exercised whether or not title to the land is registered in a land title office.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph:
53
		  (1) If, in a Crown grant under this Act, the minister finds an omission of the conditions of the Crown grant or the issue of a Crown grant under this or a former Act in the name of the wrong person or with a clerical error or defective description of the land intended to be granted, the minister may, if the minister considers it advisable, direct the defective Crown grant to be cancelled and a correct one issued, or make the changes and adjustments the minister considers advisable to rectify the error.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (2) A corrected Crown grant relates back to the date of the cancelled grant and has the same effect as if issued at the date of the cancelled grant.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (3) If the minister cancels a Crown grant under this section or if the minister finds that the Crown land was not available for disposition, or that the survey or information provided by the applicant was incorrect,

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph:
(a) 
              section 44 (2) applies, or

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (b) the minister may substitute other Crown land of a value that the minister considers reasonable in the circumstances.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (4) If other land is substituted, the minister must issue a Crown grant for the substituted land and, if the minister considers it advisable, the new grant may be dated as of the date of the original Crown grant.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (5) The substituted Crown grant has the same effect as if it had been issued on the original date.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (6) The power conferred by this section may be exercised whether or not title to the land has been registered in a land title office.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (7) If a grant is cancelled, the registrar of the appropriate land title office must cancel registration of the indefeasible title or absolute title of the land.

heading: Procedure to cancel defective grants
paragraph: (8) A person who has possession of a cancelled Crown grant must deliver it to the minister when required to do so.

heading: Delivery and registration of Crown grants
paragraph:
54
		  (1) A Crown grant issued after April 5, 1968 for land sold or for the issue of which provision is made under this Act or any other Act, general or special, must, on its issue, be transmitted to the proper land title office for registration.

heading: Delivery and registration of Crown grants
paragraph: (2) If the registrar is satisfied that the boundaries of the land are sufficiently defined by the description, the registrar must

heading: Delivery and registration of Crown grants
paragraph: (a) register the title granted in the register, subject to the provisions of the grant, in the name of the grantee, without application for registration, and

heading: Delivery and registration of Crown grants
paragraph: (b) give notice of the registration to the grantee.

heading: Delivery and registration of Crown grants
paragraph: (4) A Crown grant issued before April 6, 1968 is registrable under the law in force immediately before that date, but the fees for registration are those currently applicable and, on registration, the grantee is entitled to become the registered owner of the indefeasible title to the land.

heading: Bodies of water
paragraph:
55
		  (1) If Crown land is or has, before March 27, 1961, been disposed of by the government by Crown grant, and the map or plan attached to the grant shows a lake, river, stream or other body of water coloured, outlined or designated in a colour other than red, no part of the bed or shore of the body of water below its natural boundary passes or is deemed to have passed to the person acquiring the grant unless

heading: Bodies of water
paragraph: (a) there is express provision in the grant to the contrary, or

heading: Bodies of water
paragraph: (b) the minister endorses a declaration on the plan under section 58.

heading: Bodies of water
paragraph: (2) Nothing in any Act or rule of law to the contrary is to be construed to vest or to have vested in any person the land that comprises the bed or shore of the body of water below the natural boundary, and despite an indefeasible or absolute title to land, the title must be construed accordingly.

heading: Bodies of water
paragraph: (3) When land, the title to which has been forfeited, reverted or otherwise returned to the government, is or has been granted by the government and the grant does not have a map or plan attached but describes the land granted by reference to its official plan, the description used is deemed not to include or to have included any land below the natural boundary of the body of water coloured, outlined or designated in a colour other than red on the map or plan attached to the last preceding Crown grant of that land, and the grant must be construed accordingly.

heading: Bodies of water
paragraph: (4) Despite a rule of law to the contrary, if Crown land bordering on a lake, river, stream or a body of water is or has been granted by the government, in the absence of an express provision in the Crown grant to the contrary, no part of the bed or shore of the body of water below its natural boundary passes or is deemed to have passed to the person acquiring the land, and the Crown grant must be construed accordingly.

heading: Application
paragraph:
56
		  (1) Section 55 (1), (2) and (3) applies regardless of the area shown on the Crown grant or on the official plan, and the area of land shown on the map or plan attached to the Crown grant must not be reduced by any lettering or numbering on the map or plan.

heading: Application
paragraph:
(2) 
            Section 55 does not affect the right of any of the following:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a grantee from the government or a person claiming under the government, if the right has been determined by a court before March 27, 1961;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) the registered owner of land to whom an indefeasible or absolute title has issued before March 27, 1961 that specifically includes the bed of a body of water coloured, outlined or designated in a colour other than red on the map or plan attached to a Crown grant;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) the owner of land in a subdivision, the plan of which was deposited in the appropriate land title office before March 27, 1961, if the plan includes the bed of a body of water coloured, outlined or otherwise designated in a colour other than red on the map or plan attached to a Crown grant.

heading: Roads
paragraph:
57
		  If Crown land is disposed of by Crown grant and the map or plan attached to the grant shows a road coloured, outlined or designated in a colour other than red, no part of the road passes to the grantee, and, unless there is express provision in the grant to the contrary, the road is deemed to be, for a grant issued

heading: Roads
paragraph: (a) before January 3, 1977, 20.1168 m in width, and

heading: Roads
paragraph: (b) after January 2, 1977, 20 m in width.

heading: Application to include body of water or road in subdivision
paragraph:
58
		  (1) If doubt exists whether a body of water or road shown on the map or plan attached to a grant from the government is included in the grant, or whether it is in the public interest that the part coloured other than in red need be retained by the government, a person proposing to subdivide may apply to the minister for a declaration of intention about that part.

heading: Application to include body of water or road in subdivision
paragraph: (2) The application must be accompanied by a print of the proposed plan of subdivision.

heading: Application to include body of water or road in subdivision
paragraph: (3) On receiving a plan certified by the registrar as being otherwise acceptable for deposit, the minister may, if the minister considers it advisable, endorse a declaration on the plan that the land is included in the grant or need not be retained by the government.

heading: Application to include body of water or road in subdivision
paragraph: (4) The deposit in the land title office of an endorsed plan vests title to the land referred to in the declaration in the owner of the land covered by the plan without an instrument of transfer.

heading: Application to include body of water or road in subdivision
paragraph: (5) If the title to the land contained in the plan is subject to a registered charge, the charge is deemed to be modified by including the land described in the declaration.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph:
59
		  (1) If a person does anything that is an offence under section 60 (a) to (g), the minister may, on notice to that person, do one or more of the following:

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (a) require the person to cease the unauthorized occupation of the Crown land, give up possession of the land and restore the land to a condition satisfactory to the minister;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (b) require the person to cease the unauthorized use of the Crown land and restore the land to a condition satisfactory to the minister;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (c) require the person to pay to the Minister of Finance a sum of money considered by the minister reasonable in the circumstances

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (i)  for the occupation or possession or the restoration, or both the occupation or possession and the restoration, of the Crown land, or

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (ii)  for the use or the restoration, or both the use and the restoration, of the Crown land;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (d) cancel any lease, right of way, easement, licence of occupation, permit or other disposition held by the person under this Act;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (e) direct a sheriff or a public officer to seize on behalf of the government all improvements, goods, chattels or other materials on the Crown land or in or on water on the Crown land;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (f) require the person to remove any improvements made by the person on the Crown land, to the satisfaction of the minister, within the time specified in the notice and, on failure of the person to comply, the minister may remove the improvements and require the person to pay the cost of removal.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (2) The notice under subsection (1) or (4) must state the following:

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (a) the time and place of the unauthorized occupation or possession, unauthorized use or other contravention;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (b) details of the unauthorized occupation or possession, unauthorized use or other contravention;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (c) the requirement, action or direction of the minister under subsection (1);

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (d) if applicable, the time period within which the person must act on a requirement of the minister;

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (e) if applicable, the amount of the penalty imposed under subsection (4) and the date by which the penalty must be paid.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (3) The notice under subsection (1) may be given

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (a) by personal service on the person or by registered mail addressed to the person, or

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (b) by posting it on the Crown land if the person is unknown.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (4) If a person to whom this section applies fails to act in accordance with the notice given under subsection (1), a government corporation or public officer to whom a power is delegated under section 97 (1) or (1.1) may, on notice to the person, require the person to pay to the government, in addition to any other amount or penalty under this Act, a penalty of up to $1 000 for non-compliance with the notice.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (5) A notice may be issued more than once in respect of the same matter if a person does not comply with the first notice issued in respect of that matter.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (6) A person who has not been given notice by personal service or by registered mail is not liable for the penalty under subsection (4).

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (7) Money required to be paid under this section is recoverable by the Minister of Finance as a debt due to the government.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (8) Anything seized under this section becomes the property of the government and the minister may, at the discretion of the minister, authorize it to be sold, rented, removed or destroyed.

heading: Trespass on Crown land
paragraph: (9) Nothing in this section limits, restricts or derogates from a court's power and jurisdiction in respect of an offence under section 60.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
60
		  A person commits an offence if the person does any of the following:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) occupies or possesses Crown land without lawful authority;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) uses Crown land without lawful authority;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) being the holder of a lease, right of way, easement, licence of occupation, permit or other disposition issued under this Act, uses Crown land for a purpose not provided for in the disposition;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) is guilty of an act or default by which a lease, right of way, easement, licence of occupation, permit or other disposition issued under this Act may be terminated;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (e) constructs on Crown land a building, structure, enclosure or other works, or does or performs any dredging, excavation or filling, without the authorization of the minister;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (f) abandons on Crown land any vehicle or vessel without the authorization of the minister;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (g) unlawfully interferes with or removes a sign erected by or on behalf of the minister.

heading: Enforcement of payment
paragraph:
61
		  (1) If a person is required to pay money under section 59, the money

heading: Enforcement of payment
paragraph: (a) is due and payable by the date specified for payment in the notice served on or delivered to the person who is required to pay it, and

heading: Enforcement of payment
paragraph: (b) bears interest at a prescribed rate.

heading: Enforcement of payment
paragraph: (2) If the person fails to pay the money after service or delivery of the notice referred to in subsection (1), the minister may issue and file with a court having jurisdiction a certificate stating

heading: Enforcement of payment
paragraph: (a) the amount that remains unpaid including interest, and

heading: Enforcement of payment
paragraph: (b) the name of the person who is required to pay.

heading: Enforcement of payment
paragraph: (3) A certificate filed under subsection (2) has the same effect as an order of the court for the recovery of a debt in the amount stated in the certificate against the person named in it, and all proceedings may be taken as if it were an order of the court.

heading: Liability for contravention of section 60
paragraph:
62
		  A person who does anything that is an offence under section 60, or who directs or causes an offence to be committed under section 60, is liable to compensate the government or the person against whom the offence is committed for loss or damage suffered by the government or by that person because of the contravention.

heading: Right of possession to acquired Crown land
paragraph:
65
		  Except as otherwise provided in this Act, a person lawfully entitled to occupy Crown land under a certificate of purchase, lease, right of way, easement or licence of occupation may, for that land, take proceedings against any person for recovery of possession of, or for trespass to, the interest in the land in the same manner and to the same extent as if the person were the registered owner of the land.

heading: Prohibition of use of Crown land in designated areas
paragraph:
66
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, prohibit a specific use of Crown land in a designated area.

heading: Prohibition of use of Crown land in designated areas
paragraph: (2) A person who uses Crown land in a designated area in a manner prohibited under subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Garbage on Crown land prohibited
paragraph:
67
		  (1) A person must not throw, deposit, dump or in any way cause to be placed on Crown land any glass, metal, garbage, soil or other substance without the authority of the minister.

heading: Garbage on Crown land prohibited
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes this section commits an offence.

heading: Garbage on Crown land prohibited
paragraph: (3) A member of the Provincial police force or a municipal police department may arrest, without warrant, a person whom the member finds committing an offence under this section, and may detain the person until the person can be brought before a justice to be dealt with according to law.

heading: Penalty
paragraph:
68
		  Every person who is convicted of an offence against this Act for which no penalty is provided is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $20 000 or to imprisonment for a term not longer than 60 days, or to both the fine and imprisonment.

heading: Surveys: district lots
paragraph:
69
		  (1) Crown land may be surveyed into district lots, rectangular in shape and bounded by lines run as nearly as may be true north and south and east and west.

heading: Surveys: district lots
paragraph: (2) Lots may, at the discretion of the Surveyor General, be polygonal in shape and oriented to conform to topography.

heading: Surveys: district lots
paragraph: (3) The natural boundary of a body of water may be adopted as a boundary of adjoining land.

heading: Surveys: district lots
paragraph: (4) A conventional boundary may be established in a survey of Crown land, and land defined by a conventional boundary carries with it the rights and incidents as if it were bounded by the natural boundary.

heading: Surveys: district lots
paragraph: (5) Lots surveyed in a land district must be numbered in a consecutive numbering system for each land district.

heading: Surveys: district lots
paragraph: (6) A location reference from the national topographic map system may be added.

heading: Survey to be confirmed
paragraph:
72
		  (1) A survey may not be used or adopted for the purpose of this Act unless it is accepted and confirmed in writing by the Surveyor General on the official plan.

heading: Survey to be confirmed
paragraph: (2) A survey confirmed under subsection (1) is deemed for all purposes to have been made in compliance with this Act.

heading: Survey rules and regulations
paragraph:
73
		  (1) The Association of British Columbia Land Surveyors may make rules under section 75 of the Land Surveyors Act for surveys under this Part.

heading: Survey rules and regulations
paragraph: (2) The Surveyor General may make regulations necessary or advisable for surveys conducted for the purposes of the Nisga'a Final Agreement as defined in the Nisga'a Final Agreement Act.

heading: Authorized surveyor
paragraph: 74		  A person who is not a British Columbia land surveyor acting under instruction of the Surveyor General may not carry out a survey under this Act.

heading: Power to cancel survey and order resurvey
paragraph:
75
		  If examination discloses that a survey on the ground differs materially from the field notes or plan of survey of land filed in the ministry and confirmed by notice in the Gazette, or by the signature of the Surveyor General, or if for any other reason the Surveyor General considers it advisable, the Surveyor General may, by notice in the Gazette, cancel the field notes or plan of survey, and may order a resurvey of the land affected.

heading: Power to order survey
paragraph:
76
		  (1) The minister may cause a survey to be made of Crown land.

heading: Power to order survey
paragraph: (2) Unless the minister otherwise orders, an applicant for unsurveyed Crown land must pay the cost of a survey of that land.

heading: Survey instructions by Surveyor General
paragraph:
77
		  (1) On the request of a British Columbia land surveyor engaged by the applicant, the Surveyor General may issue instructions about the survey to the surveyor.

heading: Survey instructions by Surveyor General
paragraph: (2) The survey must be completed in the time specified in the instructions, and the survey records must be forwarded immediately to the Surveyor General, unless, in special circumstances, the Surveyor General extends the date for completion.

heading: Survey instructions by Surveyor General
paragraph: (3) If the survey is not completed and forwarded by the date or extended date specified, the surveyor must discontinue the survey and advise the applicant.

heading: Survey instructions by Surveyor General
paragraph: (4) A surveyor who discontinues a survey must immediately forward to the Surveyor General the field notes and the results of the work to date.

heading: Survey instructions by Surveyor General
paragraph: (5) If for any reason the survey is not satisfactory to the Surveyor General, the Surveyor General may require a further survey or report.

heading: Treaty lands - survey instructions
paragraph:
77.1
		  Despite this Part, for the purposes of a survey of treaty lands, the Surveyor General may issue instructions to a British Columbia land surveyor that

heading: Treaty lands - survey instructions
paragraph: (a) the Surveyor General considers necessary or advisable, and

heading: Treaty lands - survey instructions
paragraph: (b) are consistent with the final agreement of the treaty first nation.

heading: Survey may be refused
paragraph:
78
		  (1) The Surveyor General may reject a survey if the Surveyor General considers it is not in the public interest to dispose of the Crown land because of

heading: Survey may be refused
paragraph: (a) a report or a survey of a British Columbia land surveyor, or

heading: Survey may be refused
paragraph: (b) information received after the acceptance of an application for a disposition.

heading: Road and walkway allowances
paragraph:
79
		  The Surveyor General may establish or cancel an allowance for a road or walkway on the border of or through a section, lot or block of Crown land.

heading: Access to private land
paragraph:
80
		  (1) If the minister considers it advisable, the minister may authorize the Surveyor General to establish a public road allowance through Crown land to give access to privately owned land being subdivided.

heading: Access to private land
paragraph: (2) The Surveyor General may sign the subdivision plan.

heading: Agreed boundary
paragraph:
81
		  (1) If land, subdivided under the Land Title Act by plan or description, has a natural boundary that adjoins Crown land, the owner may apply to the Surveyor General to replace the natural boundary by a boundary by agreement by deposit of a new subdivision plan in a land title office.

heading: Agreed boundary
paragraph: (2) The Surveyor General may by endorsement on the plan agree to the boundary by agreement and the subdivision plan.

heading: Power to carry out reposting survey
paragraph: 82		  The Surveyor General may, if the Surveyor General considers it advisable, carry out a reposting survey to replace lost original posts or monuments of a district lot or section, whether owned by the government or otherwise.

heading: Power to order resurvey for replacement of boundary
paragraph:
83
		  (1) The Surveyor General may, if the Surveyor General considers it advisable to replace a boundary established under an original survey and confirmed under any Act with a boundary by agreement, order a resurvey of that boundary.

heading: Power to order resurvey for replacement of boundary
paragraph: (2) A resurvey under this section must not be ordered unless

heading: Power to order resurvey for replacement of boundary
paragraph: (a) the Surveyor General receives an application from the owner of the land affected by the boundary,

heading: Power to order resurvey for replacement of boundary
paragraph: (b) the owners, if any, of all registered charges against the land consent to the resurvey, and

heading: Power to order resurvey for replacement of boundary
paragraph: (c) the land adjoins Crown land.

heading: Power to order resurvey for lost posts or boundaries
paragraph:
84
		  (1) If the Surveyor General considers it advisable, the Surveyor General may order a resurvey of land where posts or boundaries of an original survey of a district lot or section have disappeared and cannot be located.

heading: Power to order resurvey for lost posts or boundaries
paragraph: (2) If Crown land has been disposed of, the Surveyor General must not order a resurvey under this section unless the Surveyor General receives an application for a resurvey from an owner of land within the area of the proposed resurvey.

heading: Limit on resurvey power
paragraph:
85
		  (1) 
            Section 75 does not apply to land granted by the government unless the grant or indefeasible or absolute title has been cancelled.

heading: Limit on resurvey power
paragraph:
(2) 
            Sections 83 (1) and 84 (1) do not apply if land is subdivided or if a survey is directed under the Land Survey Act.

heading: Persons likely to be affected by resurvey
paragraph: 86		  (1) If a person makes an application to the Surveyor General for a resurvey under section 83 or 84, and the Surveyor General believes that other persons or owners of land are likely to be adversely affected by a resurvey, the Surveyor General must direct the applicant for the resurvey to publish a notice in a satisfactory form in one issue of the Gazette and one issue of a newspaper circulating in the land district.

heading: Persons likely to be affected by resurvey
paragraph: (2) The notice must set out a time and place for a hearing of the resurvey application by the Surveyor General.

heading: Persons likely to be affected by resurvey
paragraph: (3) At the time and place, the Surveyor General or a person appointed by the Surveyor General must

heading: Persons likely to be affected by resurvey
paragraph: (a) hear the evidence of the applicant for a resurvey and of any person adversely affected, and

heading: Persons likely to be affected by resurvey
paragraph: (b) decide whether to order the resurvey.

heading: Persons likely to be affected by resurvey
paragraph: (4) The order of the Surveyor General under subsection (3) is final and binding on all persons, subject to appeal to the minister.

heading: Hearing of protest
paragraph:
87
		  (1) The Surveyor General or the person appointed, on a hearing under section 86, may do the following:

heading: Hearing of protest
paragraph: (a) receive any evidence the Surveyor General or the person appointed thinks proper to admit;

heading: Hearing of protest
paragraph: (b) examine on oath a person affected and the person's witnesses;

heading: Hearing of protest
paragraph: (c) adjourn the hearing as the Surveyor General or the person appointed considers advisable.

heading: Hearing of protest
paragraph: (2) If the hearing is conducted by a person appointed by the Surveyor General, the person must report the person's decision immediately to the Surveyor General.

heading: Confirmation of resurvey plan
paragraph:
88
		  (1) The Surveyor General may by signing the plan confirm a plan of resurvey ordered by the Surveyor General, or, if the Surveyor General considers it advisable, may order supplementary work.

heading: Confirmation of resurvey plan
paragraph: (2) On receiving the British Columbia land surveyor's report of the supplementary work, the Surveyor General may confirm the resurvey as originally submitted or with the amendments that the Surveyor General considers advisable.

heading: Deposit of plan on resurvey under section 86
paragraph:
89
		  If section 86 applies and the resurvey is complete, the person applying for it must deposit a copy of the new plan in the office of

heading: Deposit of plan on resurvey under section 86
paragraph: (a) the commissioner of the land recording district, or

heading: Deposit of plan on resurvey under section 86
paragraph: (b) the corporate officer of the municipality where the land is located.

heading: Resurvey binding
paragraph:
90
		  On confirmation by the Surveyor General of a resurvey,

heading: Resurvey binding
paragraph: (a) the resurvey becomes and is for all purposes deemed to be the original survey of the land in or affected by the resurvey,

heading: Resurvey binding
paragraph: (b) the boundaries established by the previous survey have no further effect,

heading: Resurvey binding
paragraph: (c) the notes or plans of the previous confirmed survey have no further effect, and

heading: Resurvey binding
paragraph: (d) the Surveyor General must deposit a copy of the confirmed resurvey plan in the proper land title office.

heading: Resurvey: gain or loss of property
paragraph:
91
		  (1) If on a resurvey a person acquires land and its improvements, the person must pay the person from whom the land and improvements are taken by the resurvey compensation in an amount set by the minister.

heading: Resurvey: gain or loss of property
paragraph: (2) If either person is dissatisfied with the amount of compensation set by the minister, the person may submit the dispute for arbitration

heading: Resurvey: gain or loss of property
paragraph: (a) by a single arbitrator, if both persons concur in the arbitrator's appointment, or

heading: Resurvey: gain or loss of property
paragraph: (b) by 3 arbitrators appointed under the Arbitration Act.

heading: Resurvey: gain or loss of property
paragraph: (3) The Arbitration Act applies to an arbitration under this section and the award is binding on the parties to the arbitration.

heading: Cost of resurvey
paragraph: 92		  (1) If land is resurveyed under this Part, the owners or holders of dispositions contained in the plan of resurvey must jointly pay

heading: Cost of resurvey
paragraph: (a) the cost of the resurvey,

heading: Cost of resurvey
paragraph: (b) the fee and expense of a person appointed to hear objections under section 86, and

heading: Cost of resurvey
paragraph: (c) any other cost and expense to complete and register the plan of resurvey.

heading: Cost of resurvey
paragraph: (2) The minister must set the amount payable by each owner or holder of the total amount payable in the same proportion as each person's area bears to the total area of land contained in the plan of survey.

heading: Cost of resurvey
paragraph: (3) If it is considered advisable by the minister or a municipality, the government or the municipality may assume all or part of the cost or expense referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph:
93
		  (1) If the land of an owner or holder of a disposition is in a rural area, the government may recover the amount payable by the owner or holder and not paid by the owner or holder, as if it were a tax levied under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (2) The assessor must, on receipt of the minister's certificate of the amount owing, place the amount on the assessment roll against the land for recovery as tax.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (3) If the land of the owner or holder of a disposition is in a municipality, the municipality must pay the cost and expense not paid by the owner or holder.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (4) The municipality may recover an amount paid by it under this section as if it were a tax imposed under the Community Charter.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (5) The designated municipal officer must place the amount on the assessment roll against the land for recovery as tax.

heading: Definition
paragraph: 93.01		  In this Part, "official" includes a minister of the government.

heading: Effect of this Part on the government
paragraph:
93.02
		  Despite section 14 (2) of the Interpretation Act, this Part and the regulations and orders made under it affect and are binding on the government.

heading: Objectives for Haida Gwaii
paragraph: 93.03		  The powers provided by sections 93.4 and 93.7 may not be exercised in respect of the management area, as defined in section 1 (1) of the Haida Gwaii Reconciliation Act.

heading: Minister may establish Forest and Range Practices Act objectives by order
paragraph:
93.4
		  (1) For the purposes of the Forest and Range Practices Act, the minister by order may establish objectives for the use and management of

heading: Minister may establish Forest and Range Practices Act objectives by order
paragraph: (a) Crown resources,

heading: Minister may establish Forest and Range Practices Act objectives by order
paragraph: (b) Crown land, or

heading: Minister may establish Forest and Range Practices Act objectives by order
paragraph: (c) private land that is subject to a tree farm licence, woodlot licence or community forest agreement.

heading: Minister may establish Forest and Range Practices Act objectives by order
paragraph: (2) An order of the minister under subsection (1) may apply in respect of Crown resources or Crown land, whether or not the Crown resources or Crown land are also the subject of a designation made or an objective established by the Lieutenant Governor in Council under this Part.

heading: Consistency among designations and objectives
paragraph: 93.5		  (1) The minister must not establish an objective under section 93.4 in respect of Crown resources or Crown land unless the objective is consistent with every

heading: Consistency among designations and objectives
paragraph: (a) designation made under section 93.1, and

heading: Consistency among designations and objectives
paragraph: (b) objective established under section 93.3

heading: Consistency among designations and objectives
paragraph: that also applies in respect of the Crown resources or Crown land.

heading: Consistency among designations and objectives
paragraph: (2) In case of a conflict or inconsistency between an order of the minister under section 93.4 and a designation made under section 93.1 or an objective established under section 93.3 by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the designation made or objective established by the Lieutenant Governor in Council prevails over the order of the minister.

heading: Public review of proposed objectives by minister's order
paragraph:
93.6
		  (1) Before making an order under section 93.4 establishing or significantly amending an objective, the minister must make the proposed objective or particulars of the proposed amendment publicly available for

heading: Public review of proposed objectives by minister's order
paragraph: (a) review, and

heading: Public review of proposed objectives by minister's order
paragraph: (b) comment.

heading: Public review of proposed objectives by minister's order
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an order under section 93.4 if the minister

heading: Public review of proposed objectives by minister's order
paragraph: (a) is of the opinion that the order is urgently required to protect a resource value, and

heading: Public review of proposed objectives by minister's order
paragraph: (b) states that opinion in the order.

heading: Delegation by minister
paragraph:
93.7
		  (1) The minister, in writing, may

heading: Delegation by minister
paragraph: (a) delegate a power or duty of the minister under sections 93.4 to 93.6 or under the regulations to a person, designated by name or position and employed in the ministry of the minister or in another ministry, and this Act applies to the delegate as if the delegate were the minister, except that the delegate may not sub-delegate the power or duty,

heading: Delegation by minister
paragraph: (b) provide directions that are binding on the delegate respecting the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty, and

heading: Delegation by minister
paragraph: (c) vary or revoke a delegation or direction.

heading: Delegation by minister
paragraph: (2) A delegation under any of sections 3 to 5 of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act, which delegation was in effect immediately before the coming into force of this subsection, is continued as a delegation of the minister under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act objectives continued
paragraph: 93.8		  An objective established under section 3, 4 or 5 of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act that, immediately before the coming into force of section 93.4 of this Act, was in effect for an area of

heading: Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act objectives continued
paragraph: (a) Crown land, or

heading: Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act objectives continued
paragraph: (b) private land that is subject to a tree farm licence, woodlot licence or community forest agreement

heading: Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act objectives continued
paragraph: in a resource management zone or in a landscape unit or sensitive area is continued as an objective established by the minister under section 93.4 of this Act for that Crown land or private land.

heading: Regulations for this Part
paragraph: 93.81		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting objectives established under section 93.4, including but not limited to regulations prescribing procedures and criteria that are to be followed by the minister or a delegate of the minister in establishing the objectives.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
93.9
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "certificate" means a computer-based record created by a certification authority and issued to a subscriber for the purposes of permitting a subscriber to sign electronic plans;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "certification authority" means a certification authority recognized by the Surveyor General under section 93.95;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "certification practice statement" means the statement approved by the Surveyor General under section 93.95;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "electronic plan" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a plan that is made in relation to Crown land and that is in electronic format, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any other document that is in the electronic form designated by the Surveyor General;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "electronic signature" means a signature in electronic format that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) created by a subscriber using a private cryptographic key under the control of the subscriber that corresponds to a public cryptographic key contained in a certificate, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) recognized by the Surveyor General;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "subscriber" means an individual who is authorized by a certificate to sign electronic plans.

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph:
93.901
		  This Part applies only to those plans and other documents the electronic form of which is designated by the Surveyor General for the purposes of this Part.

heading: Effect of electronic plan
paragraph:
93.91
		  Except as provided in this Part, an electronic plan that meets the requirements of this Part has the same effect for all purposes as a plan or other document in writing that meets the requirements of this Act or any other enactment.

heading: Submission of electronic plans
paragraph:
93.911
		  A person may submit an electronic plan to the Surveyor General in accordance with this Part

heading: Submission of electronic plans
paragraph: (a) for filing or deposit in the registry, or

heading: Submission of electronic plans
paragraph: (b) for approval, acceptance, confirmation or certification by the Surveyor General.

heading: Form and manner of completion
paragraph:
93.92
		  (1) Electronic plans submitted to the Surveyor General under section 93.94 must

heading: Form and manner of completion
paragraph: (a) be in the form designated by the Surveyor General,

heading: Form and manner of completion
paragraph: (b) contain the information required by the Surveyor General, and

heading: Form and manner of completion
paragraph: (c) be completed in the manner established by the Surveyor General.

heading: Form and manner of completion
paragraph: (2) Unless the Surveyor General otherwise permits, all information in an electronic plan must be depicted in black on a white background.

heading: Signing requirements - British Columbia land surveyor
paragraph: (2) An electronic plan must be signed in accordance with this section before it is submitted to the Surveyor General under section 93.94.

heading: Signing requirements - British Columbia land surveyor
paragraph: (3) An electronic plan is signed for the purposes of this section when a British Columbia land surveyor electronically signs the electronic plan in accordance with the requirements established by the Surveyor General.

heading: Signing requirements - British Columbia land surveyor
paragraph: (4) The incorporation of the electronic signature of a British Columbia land surveyor into an electronic plan is a certification by the land surveyor

heading: Signing requirements - British Columbia land surveyor
paragraph: (a) that the requirements established by the Surveyor General are met, and

heading: Signing requirements - British Columbia land surveyor
paragraph: (b) that the information contained in each notation, endorsement, statement or certification made by the land surveyor and set out in the plan is correct.

heading: Signing requirements - British Columbia land surveyor
paragraph: (5) Despite any enactment or rule of law to the contrary, an electronic plan that has been signed by a British Columbia land surveyor in accordance with this section is conclusively deemed to be in writing and signed by the British Columbia land surveyor.

heading: Submitting electronic plans
paragraph:
93.94
		  An electronic plan is submitted to the Surveyor General when the plan is transmitted electronically to the Surveyor General in the manner established by the Surveyor General using the technology established by the Surveyor General.

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph:
93.941
		  (1) If an electronic plan is submitted to the Surveyor General under section 93.94 and, in accordance with this Act or another enactment, the Surveyor General approves, accepts or confirms the electronic plan or certifies the electronic plan as an official plan, the Surveyor General must

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (a) sign a copy of the electronic plan, or

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (b) sign the electronic plan in accordance with this section.

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (2) The Surveyor General may sign an electronic plan under subsection (1) (a) or (b) if

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (a) the electronic plan is submitted to the Surveyor General under section 93.94, and

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (b) this Act or another enactment does not require the Surveyor General to approve, accept or confirm a plan or certify a plan as an official plan.

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (3) An electronic plan is signed for the purposes of subsection (1) (b) when the Surveyor General electronically signs the electronic plan in accordance with the requirements established by the Surveyor General.

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (4) The incorporation of the electronic signature of the Surveyor General into an electronic plan is a certification by the Surveyor General

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (a) that the requirements established under subsection (3) are met, and

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (b) that the information contained in each notation, endorsement, statement or certification made by the Surveyor General and set out in the plan is correct.

heading: Signing requirements - Surveyor General
paragraph: (5) Despite any enactment or rule of law to the contrary, an electronic plan that has been signed by the Surveyor General in accordance with this section is conclusively deemed to be in writing and signed by the Surveyor General.

heading: Certification authority
paragraph:
93.95
		  For the purposes of this Act, the Surveyor General may recognize a person as a certification authority if

heading: Certification authority
paragraph: (a) the person has adopted and published a certification practice statement that has been approved by the Surveyor General, and

heading: Certification authority
paragraph: (b) the Surveyor General is satisfied that

heading: Certification authority
paragraph: (i)  the person is capable of administering the certification practice statement, and

heading: Certification authority
paragraph: (ii)  subscribers named in certificates issued by the person are required to observe and comply with the certification practice statement.

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph:
93.96
		  A certification practice statement must contain

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (a) the policies, practices and procedures to be used by a certification authority in

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (i)  issuing, administering, suspending and revoking a certificate,

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (ii)  providing access to the information contained in a certificate, and

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (iii)  establishing and maintaining the security and validity of electronic signatures of subscribers, and

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (b) other provisions that the Surveyor General considers necessary, including provisions relating to the form and content of certificates and provisions to ensure

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (i)  that an electronic signature is unique to a specific subscriber,

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (ii)  that a subscriber named in a certificate is eligible to be a subscriber under the requirements established by the Surveyor General, and

heading: Certification practice statement
paragraph: (iii)  the security of the electronic filing system contemplated by this Part.

heading: Warranties of certification authorities
paragraph:
93.97
		  (1) The issuance of a certificate by a certification authority constitutes a warranty by the certification authority of the following matters:

heading: Warranties of certification authorities
paragraph: (a) the information contained in the certificate is, to the knowledge of the certification authority, true;

heading: Warranties of certification authorities
paragraph: (b) the certificate was issued in accordance with the certification practice statement;

heading: Warranties of certification authorities
paragraph: (c) the subscriber to whom the certificate was issued has agreed to observe and comply with the requirements of the certification practice statement;

heading: Warranties of certification authorities
paragraph: (d) the subscriber named or identified in the certificate is eligible to be a subscriber under the requirements established by the Surveyor General;

heading: Warranties of certification authorities
paragraph: (e) the certification authority will act promptly to suspend or revoke a certificate in accordance with the requirements of the certification practice statement.

heading: Warranties of certification authorities
paragraph: (2) The Surveyor General and the minister are entitled to rely on the warranties referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Immunity
paragraph:
93.98
		  In the absence of an unlawful or negligent act or omission by a certification authority in relation to its powers or duties under this Act, no action for damages lies or may be brought against a certification authority in respect of any loss or damage arising out of an unlawful or negligent act or omission of a subscriber under this Act.

heading: Delegation of powers to Director of Land Titles
paragraph:
93.99
		  The Surveyor General may delegate the Surveyor General's powers under this Division to the Director of Land Titles.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
93.991
		  (1) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Part.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (1.1) Despite section 68 of this Act, section 4 of the Offence Act applies in relation to an offence under this section.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if the person wilfully makes a false certification under any of the following provisions:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) section 93.93 (4) (b);

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) A person commits an offence if the person

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) signs an electronic plan using an electronic signature of another person, or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) permits an electronic signature of the person to be used by another person to sign an electronic plan.

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: 94		  (1) Despite section 48, the minister may authorize the execution of a Crown grant if all money payable to the government for it has not been paid, as long as payment of the money has been secured to the satisfaction of the minister.

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (2) If a Crown grant is executed under subsection (1), the minister may send to the registrar for the land title district in which the land is located a certificate signed by the minister containing the following:

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (a) a description of the land satisfactory to the registrar;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (b) a statement of the principal sum remaining payable for the grant;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (c) the rate of interest payable;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (d) the terms of repayment;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (e) the name, address and occupation of the person who is to pay the money;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (f) an application, in a form that complies with the Land Title Act, to register the certificate as a charge in the land title office.

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) is deemed to be a mortgage to which sections 9 and 10 of the Land Transfer Form Act apply.

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (4) The registrar must, without fee, register a certificate under subsection (2) as a charge against the title to the land described in it.

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (5) Registration of the certificate creates a legal mortgage

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (a) of the land described in it;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (b) by the person named in it as mortgagor;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (c) to the government as mortgagee;

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (d) on terms prescribed under this Act for these mortgages, and on any other terms stated in it.

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (6) The general law between mortgagor and mortgagee applies to a mortgage created under this section, and the government may enforce the mortgage by a proceeding in a court for foreclosure, payment of the mortgage debt, possession, judicial sale, the appointment of a receiver and by any other remedy ordinarily available to a mortgagee to enforce the security.

heading: Crown grant payments
paragraph: (7) On payment of the mortgage debt, the minister must send a certificate of discharge to the registrar, who must cancel the registration of the charge.

heading: Powers to exchange
paragraph: 95		  (1) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it advisable in the public interest, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may

heading: Powers to exchange
paragraph: (a) authorize the exchange of Crown land for other land of substantially the same value, or

heading: Powers to exchange
paragraph: (b) accept in exchange for Crown land other land of less value, together with payment of money for the difference in value.

heading: Powers to exchange
paragraph: (2) Crown land exchanged under this section must be conveyed by Crown grant under this Act, subject to the terms, covenants, stipulations, reservations or exemptions the minister considers advisable.

heading: Powers to exchange
paragraph: (3) Despite any other Act, if timber on the Crown land and on the other land exchanged under this section are not, under the Forest Act, subject to the same royalty rates, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by increasing or decreasing the royalty rate on the timber on the Crown land, equalize the royalty rates.

heading: Occupational rental
paragraph: 96		  (1) If Crown land is occupied, with or without lawful authority, before the issue of a disposition under this Act, the minister may require payment of rent by the occupier for the period of occupation at a rate the minister determines.

heading: Occupational rental
paragraph: (2) Payment of the rent is a condition precedent to the issue of a disposition.

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph:
97
		  (1) The minister may delegate in writing, on the terms and conditions the minister considers appropriate, the power to act on the minister's behalf respecting any of the minister's powers or functions under this Act to

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph: (a) a public officer in the minister's ministry,

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
