paragraph: (b) a government corporation as defined in the Financial Administration Act, or

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph: (c) another member of the Executive Council.

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph: (1.1) A member of the Executive Council to whom a minister's delegation is made under subsection (1) (c) may, subject to the terms and conditions specified in the minister's delegation, delegate powers or functions under this Act that are covered by the minister's delegation to

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph: (a) a public officer in the member's ministry, or

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph: (b) a government corporation as defined in the Financial Administration Act.

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph: (1.2) The minister or a member of the Executive Council to whom the minister's delegation is made under subsection (1) (c) may delegate in writing to the Surveyor General, on terms and conditions the minister considers appropriate, the powers to act on the minister's or member's behalf under sections 6 (1) and (2), 52, 53, 58 and 103.

heading: Minister may delegate; may amend terms
paragraph: (2) If an applicant, because of illness or other unforeseen circumstances, does not comply with a provision of this Act, the regulations, or a term, covenant or stipulation in a disposition, the minister may, if the minister considers it advisable, if no other person is or is likely to be prejudiced and if all other provisions of this Act and the regulations have been complied with, extend the time for compliance by the applicant or vary the terms, covenants or stipulations of the disposition.

heading: Disposition to applicant only
paragraph: 98		  A disposition of Crown land must be in the applicant's name only.

heading: Assignment of disposition
paragraph:
99
		  (1) An assignment, quit claim or other transfer of land for which an application for a disposition has been filed under this Act is not valid until after a certificate of purchase, a lease or licence has been issued.

heading: Assignment of disposition
paragraph: (2) A person may not dispose of or deal with an interest in Crown land held under a disposition, other than a Crown grant, unless

heading: Assignment of disposition
paragraph: (a) the disposition under which the interest is held expressly allows it, or

heading: Assignment of disposition
paragraph: (b) the minister approves in writing the disposition or dealing.

heading: Assignment of disposition
paragraph: (3) A purported disposition made in contravention of this section is void and the minister may, if the minister considers it advisable, cancel the disposition.

heading: Assignment of disposition
paragraph: (4) As a condition precedent to an approval under subsection (2) (b), the minister may require the applicant to carry out and perform, in respect of the land, additional terms, covenants or stipulations that are to be binding on every successor in title to the land.

heading: Minister may require purchaser to obtain Crown grant
paragraph:
100
		  (1) The minister may give notice to the holder of a certificate of purchase requiring the holder within 6 months from the date of the notice to apply for the Crown grant if

heading: Minister may require purchaser to obtain Crown grant
paragraph: (a) the purchase price is paid in full and all other terms, covenants and stipulations of the certificate of purchase are complied with, and

heading: Minister may require purchaser to obtain Crown grant
paragraph: (b) the purchaser has not applied for a Crown grant.

heading: Minister may require purchaser to obtain Crown grant
paragraph: (2) The minister must mail the notice by registered mail addressed to the purchaser at the purchaser's last known address, and may give additional notice in a manner the minister considers advisable.

heading: Minister may require purchaser to obtain Crown grant
paragraph: (3) If the purchaser does not apply for the Crown grant within the time set by this section, the minister may cancel the certificate of purchase by an entry on the records in the ministry.

heading: Minister may require purchaser to obtain Crown grant
paragraph: (4) On cancellation all improvements on the land, all rights of the purchaser to the land and improvements and all money paid on account of the purchase price are forfeited to and vested in the government.

heading: Examination of claim
paragraph:
101
		  (1) If a person claims an interest in Crown land, the minister may require the person to file with the minister a statement of the person's claim within a specified time.

heading: Examination of claim
paragraph: (2) The minister must examine and consider the claim and may confirm or reject all or part of it and make the disposition of the Crown land the minister considers advisable.

heading: Examination of claim
paragraph: (3) The claim is extinguished if

heading: Examination of claim
paragraph: (a) the claimant fails to file a statement within the time specified, or

heading: Examination of claim
paragraph: (b) the minister rejects the claim.

heading: Minister may consent to plan proceedings
paragraph:
102
		  If the government is the owner of land in a subdivision plan and proceedings are proposed under part of the land title legislation, the minister, if the minister considers it advisable, may sign a petition or give a consent on behalf of the government if either may be required for the proceedings.

heading: Minister may order government title cancelled
paragraph:
103
		  (1) If the government is a registered owner of an indefeasible or absolute title to land free of encumbrances, the minister may order that the registration be removed from the operation of the Land Title Act.

heading: Minister may order government title cancelled
paragraph: (2) On receiving an order of the minister under subsection (1), the registrar of the land title office must cancel the registration of the indefeasible or absolute title to the land described in the order and call in and cancel any duplicate indefeasible title or certificate of title that has been issued.

heading: Minister may order government title cancelled
paragraph: (3) On cancellation under subsection (2), the land must be dealt with under this Act.

heading: Affidavits
paragraph: 104		  In addition to persons authorized by the Evidence Act, the deputy minister, an assistant deputy minister, the Surveyor General, a commissioner and a director are commissioners for taking affidavits for British Columbia for an affidavit required under this Act.

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: 105		  For the purpose of discharging their duties under this Act, each of the following persons has at reasonable times a right to enter Crown land and premises:

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: (a) the minister;

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: (b) the deputy minister;

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: (c) an employee of the ministry who has identification from the ministry for the purpose;

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: (c.1) an employee of a government corporation to which a power is delegated under section 97 (1) or (1.1) who has identification from the government corporation for the purpose;

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: (d) a commissioner;

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: (e) the Surveyor General;

heading: Right of entry
paragraph: (f) a person acting under the direction of the Surveyor General who has identification from the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia for the purpose.

heading: Land revested in government
paragraph:
106
		  (1) Land acquired by a ministry on behalf of the government is to be administered by the minister of that ministry.

heading: Land revested in government
paragraph: (2) Despite anything in this Act, the minister may transfer, on terms and conditions the minister considers appropriate, the administration of Crown land to any ministry of the government or may accept a transfer of Crown land from any ministry of the government to the minister's ministry.

heading: Land revested in government
paragraph: (3) A power under any Act, other than the Ministry of Lands, Parks and Housing Act or the Public Agency Accommodation Act, to dispose of the fee simple in Crown land as defined in this Act, must be exercised in compliance with this Act.

heading: Land revested in government
paragraph: (4) Despite any other Act, a transfer of the administration of Crown land to the minister authorizes the minister to exercise the minister's powers in relation to that land under this Act or any other Act under the minister's administration.

heading: Land revested in government
paragraph: (5) Subsection (3) does not apply to a disposition made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council under section 59 of the Transportation Act.

heading: Land revested in government
paragraph: (6) The requirement in section 218 (1) of the Land Title Act that a statutory right of way be for a purpose necessary for the operation and maintenance of a grantee's undertaking does not apply if the grantee is the government.

heading: Restriction as to right of action
paragraph: 107		  An action may not be brought against the minister, a public official in the ministry or a land commissioner for an act or omission done or omitted in good faith in the performance of a duty imposed or authority conferred under this Act.

heading: Registers
paragraph:
108
		  (1) The commissioner of each land recording district must keep a register of applications for a disposition filed with the commissioner under this Act, which must include for each application its number, the applicant's name and address and a short description of the Crown land applied for.

heading: Registers
paragraph: (2) A person may search the register during business hours.

heading: Execution of documents
paragraph:
109
		  (1) A disposition, other than a Crown grant, must be executed by the director or another person designated in writing by the minister.

heading: Execution of documents
paragraph: (2) A Crown grant must be executed under the corporate seal of the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia by a person designated by resolution of the board of directors of the Authority.

heading: Execution of documents
paragraph: (3) A disposition purporting to be executed as provided in this section is evidence in a proceeding of the disposition, without proof of the signature of the person executing it.

heading: Execution of documents
paragraph: (4) The minister is to have a seal of office imprinted with the minister's title of office.

heading: Fees for services provided by Surveyor General
paragraph:
109.1
		  (1) There must be paid to the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia, in respect of services provided under this Act by the Surveyor General or persons under the Surveyor General's direction, the respective fees the board of directors of the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia may establish by bylaw.

heading: Fees for services provided by Surveyor General
paragraph: (2) The government is exempt from paying any fees payable under subsection (1).

heading: Fees for services provided by Surveyor General
paragraph: (3) Canada and a treaty first nation are exempt from paying fees under subsection (1) that are payable in relation to services provided under this Act in respect of a survey required by or for the purposes of the final agreement of the treaty first nation.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
110
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), but subject to section 6 (3), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing the rate of interest for the purpose of section 61 (1);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting fees for applications required under this Act or for the provision of a service or the performance of a duty by the government under this Act, including, without limitation, the following:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  prescribing the amount of a fee or a method for calculating the amount of a fee;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  identifying the person who is required to pay a fee;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iii)  respecting the time a fee must be paid;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iv)  prescribing minimum fees.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) Regulations under subsection (2) (b) and the fees established under that subsection may be different

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) for different applications,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) for different services and duties or classes of services and duties,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) for different classes of persons, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) for services and duties provided in different circumstances.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (4) Regulations under subsection (2) (b) may exempt, with or without conditions, persons or classes of persons from the payment of one or more fees.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Land Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agreement" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an agreement in the form of a licence, permit or agreement referred to in section 12 of the Forest Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a licence or permit under the Range Act

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and includes a pulpwood agreement;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land use objective" means an objective

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) established under section 93.4 of the Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) referred to in section 93.8 of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "minister" means the minister responsible for the administration of the Land Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "section 93.4 order" means an order made under section 93.4 of the Act for the purposes of the Forest and Range Practices Act.

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: 2		  (1) In making a section 93.4 order establishing or significantly amending a land use objective for an area, the minister may consider information that

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (a) is contained in a land use plan that is endorsed by the Executive Council and that relates to the area, or

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (b) is relevant to the management and use of the forest and range resources within the area.

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (2) Before making a section 93.4 order establishing or significantly amending a land use objective, the minister must be satisfied that

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (a) the land use objective or amendment will

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (i)  provide for management and use of forest or range resources in a manner that has not otherwise been provided for under this regulation or another enactment, and

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (ii)  provide for an appropriate balance of social, economic and environmental benefits, and

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (b) the importance of the land use objective or amendment outweighs any adverse impact on opportunities for timber harvesting or forage use within or adjacent to the area that will be affected.

heading: Criteria for establishing land use objectives
paragraph: (3) In making a section 93.4 order establishing or significantly amending a land use objective the minister must consider any written comment received under whichever is applicable of section 3 or 4.

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph:
3

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

paragraph: "order" does not include a section 93.4 order that is the subject of an opinion of the minister under section 93.6 (2) of the Act, stated in the order, that the order is urgently required to protect a resource value.

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (2) If the minister proposes by order to establish or significantly amend a land use objective, the minister, before making the order, must publish a notice, briefly describing the land use objective or amendment, in a newspaper circulating in

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (a) the area in which the land use objective applies, or

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (b) if no newspaper circulates in that area, the area nearest to that area,

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (c) that the proposed order is publicly available for review and comment at the ministry's regional office for the region that includes the area referred to in paragraph (a),

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (d) the date on which the land use objective or the amendment is to take effect,

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

paragraph: (ii)  the date the notice is published in the Gazette

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: in accordance with subsection (2), or

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (b) a different period that the minister, before publication of the notice, may specify, beginning on the later of the dates referred to in paragraph (a), which period may be

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (4) Before the minister makes an order to establish or significantly amend a land use objective, a holder of a forest stewardship plan, forest operations plan, woodlot licence plan, range use plan or range stewardship plan must be consulted by an official of the ministry only if both of the following conditions are fulfilled:

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment
paragraph: (a) the land use objective or amendment, as proposed, would have a material adverse impact on the holder, in relation to any

heading: Orders that must be made available for public review and comment

paragraph:

heading: Review and comment on urgent orders by affected agreement holders
paragraph: (2) If the minister proposes by order to establish or significantly amend a land use objective, the minister, before making the order, must provide agreement holders that may be affected by the order an opportunity to review, and to provide written comments about, the land use objective or amendment.

heading: Specifying conflicts with Forest and Range Practices Act objectives
paragraph:
5

heading: Specifying conflicts with Forest and Range Practices Act objectives
paragraph: (2) If the minister determines that the order, if made, would result in a conflict referred to in subsection (1), the minister may make the order

paragraph: (a) in an amended form that avoids the conflict, or

heading: Content of order establishing or amending a land use objective
paragraph: 6		  (1) A section 93.4 order that establishes or amends a land use objective must be in writing and must specify all of the following:

heading: Content of order establishing or amending a land use objective

heading: Content of order establishing or amending a land use objective

heading: Content of order establishing or amending a land use objective

heading: Content of order establishing or amending a land use objective
paragraph: (2) A section 93.4 order that establishes or amends a land use objective must be filed at the regional office for the forest region to which the order relates by the date notice of the order is posted or published under section 7.

paragraph: 7		  (1) If the minister makes a section 93.4 order establishing or significantly amending a land use objective, the minister must

heading: Notice of order establishing or amending a land use objective
paragraph: (b) publish notice of the order in the Gazette.

heading: Notice of order establishing or amending a land use objective
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) must

paragraph: (a) identify that an order has been made that has established or amended a land use objective,

paragraph: (b) identify where the land use objective or the amendment, as applicable, applies,

paragraph: (c) specify the date on which the land use objective or the amendment takes effect,

heading: Notice of order establishing or amending a land use objective
paragraph: (d) state that the order is filed at the regional office for the forest region to which the order relates, and

heading: Notice of order establishing or amending a land use objective
paragraph: (e) state that there is available a summary, filed with the order, of any revision made to the objective as a result of the proposed objective having been made available for review and comment under this regulation.

heading: Effective date of a section 93.4 order
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A section 93.4 order takes effect on the later of

paragraph: (a) the date notice is published under section 7 (1) (b), and

heading: Definition

heading: Ministry or agency to acquire land
paragraph:
2
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by an order published in the Gazette, may appoint a ministry or a statutory agency of the government to acquire, on behalf and in the name of the government, all land in British Columbia necessary or convenient for

paragraph: (a) the creation of a storage reservoir in accordance with the obligation undertaken by British Columbia under section 3 (c) of the agreement,

heading: Ministry or agency to acquire land
paragraph: (b) works, undertakings, ways or water or conservation systems incidental to it, or which may, with advantage, be combined with it, and

heading: Powers of acquisition
paragraph:

		  (1) If the ministry or agency appointed under section 2 is empowered by another Act to acquire land,

heading: Powers of acquisition
paragraph: (a) it has and may exercise powers for acquiring land for the purposes set out in section 2 as if those purposes were included among the purposes set out in that other Act, and may exercise, in relation to the acquisition of land, all other or incidental powers that it may exercise under that other Act, and

heading: Powers of acquisition
paragraph: (b) that other Act applies to the acquisition of land under this Act.

heading: Powers of acquisition
paragraph: (2) If the ministry or agency appointed under section 2 is not empowered by another Act to acquire land, it has and may exercise, for acquiring land for the purposes set out in section 2, the same powers that are conferred by the Transportation Act on the minister charged with the administration of that Act for the purposes set out in section 8 (2) of that Act, and has and may exercise, in relation to the acquisition of land, all other and incidental powers that the minister responsible for the administration of the Transportation Act may exercise under that Act.

heading: Powers of acquisition

heading: Powers of acquisition

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Maanulth First Nations Final Agreement Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 (1) The following definitions apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Agreement means the Maa-nulth First Nations Final Agreement, between the Maanulth First Nations, Her Majesty in right of Canada and Her Majesty in right of British Columbia, including any amendments made to it. (accord)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Tax Treatment Agreement means the tax treatment agreement referred to in paragraph 19.6.1 of the Agreement, including any amendments made to it. (accord sur le traitement fiscal)

heading: Definitions in Agreement
paragraph: (2) In this Act, Maanulthaht, Maanulth Citizen, Maanulth Corporation, Maanulth First Nation, Maanulth Government, Maanulth Lands, Maanulth Law, Maanulth Public Institution and Other Maanulth Lands have the same meanings as Maa-nulth-aht, Maa-nulth First Nation Citizen, Maa-nulth First Nation Corporation, Maa-nulth First Nation, Maa-nulth First Nation Government, Maa-nulth First Nation Lands, Maa-nulth First Nation Law, Maa-nulth First Nation Public Institution and Other Maa-nulth First Nation Lands, respectively, in paragraph 29.1.1 of the Agreement.

heading: Status of Agreement
paragraph: 3 The Agreement is a treaty and a land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Agreement given effect
paragraph: 4 (1) The Agreement is approved, given effect and declared valid and has the force of law.

heading: Rights and obligations
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, any person or body has the powers, rights, privileges and benefits conferred on the person or body by the Agreement and shall perform the duties, and is subject to the liabilities, imposed on the person or body by the Agreement.

heading: Third parties
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, the Agreement is binding on, and may be relied on by, all persons and bodies.

heading: Inconsistency with Agreement
paragraph: 5 (1) The Agreement prevails over this Act and any other federal law to the extent of any inconsistency or conflict between them.

heading: Conflict with Act
paragraph: (2) This Act prevails over any other federal law to the extent of any conflict between them.

heading: Payments out of C.R.F.
paragraph: 6 There shall be paid out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund any sums that are required to meet the monetary obligations of Her Majesty in right of Canada under Chapters 16 and 17 of the Agreement.

heading: Fee simple estate
paragraph: 7 On the effective date of the Agreement, each Maanulth First Nation owns the estate in fee simple, as set out in Chapter 2 of the Agreement, in the Maanulth Lands referred to in relation to it in subparagraph 2.1.1a., b., c., d. or e. of the Agreement, as the case may be. In addition, the Ucluelet First Nation owns the estate in fee simple, as set out in Chapter 2 of the Agreement, in the Other Maanulth Lands referred to in paragraph 2.2.1 of the Agreement.

heading: Tax Treatment Agreement given effect
paragraph: 8 The Tax Treatment Agreement is approved, given effect and declared valid and has the force of law during the period that it is in effect.

heading: Not a treaty
paragraph: 9 The Tax Treatment Agreement does not form part of the Agreement and is not a treaty or a land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Powers of Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: 10 Despite section 7 of the Fisheries Act, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, on behalf of Her Majesty in right of Canada, enter into and implement the Maa-nulth Harvest Agreement referred to in paragraph 10.2.1 of the Agreement, including any amendments made to it.

heading: Not a treaty
paragraph: 11 That Harvest Agreement does not form part of the Agreement and is not a treaty or a land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Indian Act
paragraph: 12 Subject to the provisions of Chapter 15 of the Agreement that deal with the continuing application of the Indian Act, and paragraphs 19.5.1 to 19.5.6 of the Agreement, the Indian Act does not apply to Maanulthaht, Maanulth First Nations, Maanulth Governments, Maanulth Public Institutions or Maanulth Corporations as of the effective date of the Agreement, except for the purpose of determining whether an individual is an Indian.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: 13 Maanulth Laws and other instruments made under the Agreement are not statutory instruments for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Incorporation by reference
paragraph: 14 To the extent that a law of British Columbia does not apply of its own force to a Maanulthaht, a Maanulth Citizen, a Maanulth First Nation, a Maanulth Government, a Maanulth Public Institution, a Maanulth Corporation, Maanulth Lands or Other Maanulth Lands, because of the exclusive legislative authority of Parliament set out in Class 24 of section 91 of the Constitution Act, 1867, that law of British Columbia applies to it or to them by virtue of this section, in accordance with the Agreement and subject to this Act and any other Act of Parliament.

heading: Judicial notice of Agreements
paragraph: 15 (1) Judicial notice shall be taken of the Agreement and the Tax Treatment Agreement.

heading: Publication of Agreements
paragraph: (2) The Agreement and the Tax Treatment Agreement shall be published by the Queen's Printer.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (3) A copy of the Agreement or the Tax Treatment Agreement published by the Queen's Printer is evidence of that agreement and of its contents, and a copy purporting to be published by the Queen's Printer is deemed to be so published, unless the contrary is shown.

heading: Judicial notice of Maanulth Laws
paragraph: 16 (1) Judicial notice shall be taken of Maanulth Laws.

heading: Evidence of Maanulth Laws
paragraph: (2) A copy of a Maanulth Law purporting to be deposited in a public registry of laws referred to in subparagraph 13.5.1a. of the Agreement is evidence of that law and of its contents, unless the contrary is shown.

heading: Orders and regulations
paragraph: 17 The Governor in Council may make any orders and regulations that are necessary for the purpose of carrying out any of the provisions of the Agreement or of the Tax Treatment Agreement.

heading: Chapters 26 and 28 of Agreement
paragraph: 18 Despite subsection 4(1), Chapters 26 and 28 of the Agreement are deemed to have effect as of December 9, 2006.

heading: Notice of issues arising
paragraph: 19 (1) If an issue arises in any judicial or administrative proceeding in respect of the interpretation or validity of the Agreement, or the validity or applicability of this Act, the British Columbia Maa-nulth First Nations Final Agreement Act or any Maanulth Law, then the issue shall not be decided until the party raising the issue has served notice on the Attorney General of Canada, the Attorney General of British Columbia and each applicable Maanulth First Nation.

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (2) The notice shall

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (a) describe the judicial or administrative proceeding;

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (b) specify what the issue arises in respect of;

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (c) state the day on which the issue is to be argued;

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (d) give particulars necessary to show the point to be argued; and

heading: Content of notice
paragraph: (e) be served at least 14 days before the day of argument, unless the court or tribunal authorizes a shorter period.

heading: Participation in proceedings
paragraph: (3) In any judicial or administrative proceeding in respect of which subsection (1) applies, the Attorney General of Canada, the Attorney General of British Columbia and the applicable Maanulth First Nation may appear and participate in the proceeding as parties with the same rights as any other party.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the Management of Contaminated Fisheries Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: contaminated, with respect to fish, means fish in or on which bacteria, toxins, chemical compounds or other substances are present to a degree that may constitute a danger to public health; (contamine)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Regional Director General means a Regional Director General or an Associate Regional Director General of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans. (directeur general regional)

heading: Prohibition Order
paragraph: 3 (1) Where a Regional Director General has reason to believe that fish of any species in any area are contaminated, the Regional Director General may issue an order prohibiting fishing in that area for that species.

heading: Prohibition Order
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding any other regulations made under the Fisheries Act, where a Regional Director General issues an order under subsection (1) in respect of an area, no person shall, in that area, fish for or catch and retain any species of fish specified in the order unless

heading: Prohibition Order
paragraph: (a) the person is the holder of a licence issued under subsection 4(1) and is carrying that licence; or

heading: Prohibition Order
paragraph: (b) the person is named in a licence issued under subsection 4(1) and is carrying a copy of that licence.

heading: Licence
paragraph: 4 (1) Subject to subsection (2), on application and payment by a person of the appropriate fee set out in the table to this subsection, the Minister may issue the person a licence authorizing the person and any other person named in the licence to fish in any area in respect of which an order is issued under subsection 3(1), for any species specified in that order.

paragraph: (2) Where a person wishes to obtain a licence to fish for food purposes, the person shall submit to the Minister a decontamination plan that satisfies the Minister that the fish will be decontaminated before being used for human consumption.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 7 (1) No person shall disturb a marine mammal except

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) when carrying on a work, undertaking or activity that is authorized, otherwise permitted or required under the Act;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) when fishing for marine mammals under the authority of these Regulations;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) in the manner set out in a licence issued under the Fishery (General) Regulations authorizing them to fish for marine mammals for experimental, scientific, educational or public display purposes; or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (d) in the manner authorized under the Species at Risk Act.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), disturb includes to approach the marine mammal to, or to attempt to,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) feed it;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) swim with it or interact with it;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) move it or entice or cause it to move from the immediate vicinity in which it is found;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (d) separate it from members of its group or go between it and a calf;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (e) trap it or its group between a vessel and the shore or between a vessel and one or more other vessels; or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (f) tag or mark it.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), in the case of a marine mammal that is of a species set out in column 1 of Schedule VI, disturb also includes to approach the marine mammal with a vehicle of the type set out in column 2 within the approach distance set out in column 3 in the area set out in column 4 during the period set out in column 5.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (1), in the case of a whale, dolphin or porpoise in resting position or with its calf, disturb also includes to approach the whale, dolphin or porpoise with a vehicle of the type set out in column 2 of Schedule VI, at an approach distance of less than 200 m in all Canadian fisheries waters from January 1 to December 31.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (5) The requirement to respect the approach distances set out in Schedule VI and in subsection (4) does not apply to

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) a vessel that is in transit; or

heading: Prohibitions

heading: Prohibitions

heading: Prohibitions

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 7.2 (1) When an aircraft is being operated at an altitude of less than 304.8 m (1,000 ft.) within a radius of one-half nautical mile from a marine mammal, no person shall perform a flight manoeuvre - including taking off, landing or altering the course or altitude of the aircraft - for the purpose of bringing the aircraft closer to the marine mammal or otherwise disturbing it.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply

heading: Prohibitions

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) a round club made of hardwood that measures not less than 60 cm and not more than 1 m in length and that, for at least half of its length, beginning at one end, measures not less than 5 cm and not more than 7.6 cm in diameter;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) an instrument known as a hakapik, consisting of a metal ferrule that weighs at least 340 g with a slightly bent spike not more than 14 cm in length on one side of the ferrule and a blunt projection not more than 1.3 cm in length on the opposite side of the ferrule and that is attached to a wooden handle that measures not less than 105 cm and not more than 153 cm in length and not less than 3 cm and not more than 5.1 cm in diameter;

heading: Prohibitions

heading: Prohibitions

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (1.1) No person shall use a club or hakapik to strike a seal older than one year unless the seal has been shot with a firearm.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) Every person who strikes a seal with a club or hakapik shall strike the seal on the top of the cranium until it has been crushed and shall immediately palpate the cranium to confirm that it has been crushed.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) If a firearm is used to fish for a seal, the person who shoots the seal or retrieves it shall palpate the cranium as soon as possible after it is shot to confirm that the cranium has been crushed.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (4) Every person who palpates the cranium of a seal and determines that the cranium is not crushed shall immediately strike the seal with a club or hakapik on the top of its cranium until the cranium has been crushed.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 29 No person shall skin a seal until the cranium has been crushed and at least one minute has elapsed after the two axillary arteries of the seal located beneath its front flippers have been severed to bleed the seal.

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: 38 (1) Despite sections 7 and 7.2, the Minister may authorize the disturbance of marine mammals if it is established that the activity causing the disturbance

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (a) could benefit marine mammals without jeopardizing the survival of the species in the wild;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (b) could improve a marine mammal's immediate chance of survival;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (c) would contribute to the conservation and protection of marine mammals;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (d) could ease the pain and suffering of a marine mammal that is in distress;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (e) would contribute to marine scientific research; or

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (f) would permit the production of audiovisual records of activities of marine mammals, which could facilitate a better understanding of marine mammals and thereby contribute to their conservation and protection.

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (2) The authorization may be subject to any condition respecting

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (a) the waters in which marine mammals may be disturbed;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (b) the marine mammals that may be disturbed;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (c) the period during which marine mammals may be disturbed;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (d) the type, size, number and identification of vehicles that are permitted to be used and the persons who are permitted to operate them;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (e) the manner in which those vehicles are to be operated, including the distance they are required to maintain from marine mammals, their speed and direction and the requirement to avoid impeding the path of marine mammals;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (f) the manner in which marine mammals may be disturbed and the measures that are required to mitigate or minimize the negative effects of disturbing them;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (g) the diagnostic assessment or any other assessments that are to be carried out in respect of marine mammals before, during and after the disturbance;

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (h) the information that must be reported to the Minister, as well as the method by which, the times at which and the person for whom the report is to be made; and

heading: Authorized Disturbance
paragraph: (i) the records that must be maintained with respect to the activity causing the disturbance as well as the manner and form in which the records are to be maintained, the times at which and the person for whom the records are to be produced and the period for which the records are to be retained.

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: 39 Immediately after any accidental contact between a vehicle or fishing gear and a marine mammal, the operator of the vehicle or the fishing gear, as the case may be, shall - unless the contact is reported as a bycatch in a log book - notify the Minister of

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: (a) the date, time and location of the incident;

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: (b) the species of marine mammal involved in the incident;

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: (c) the circumstances of the incident;

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: (d) the size and type of vehicle and, if applicable, the type of fishing gear involved in the incident;

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: (e) the weather and sea conditions at the time of the incident;

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: (f) the observed state of the marine mammal after the incident; and

heading: Accidental Contact with Marine Mammals
paragraph: (g) the direction of travel of the marine mammal after the incident, to the extent that it can be determined.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the Meat and Poultry Products Plant Liquid Effluent Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 (1) In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Fisheries Act; (Loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: ammonia nitrogen means the nitrogen in ammonia that results from the operation of a plant and that is contained in the effluent from that plant; (azote ammoniacal)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: biochemical oxygen demanding matter means the substance contained in the effluent from a plant that results from the operation of a plant and that will exert a biochemical oxygen demand; (matiere ayant une demande biochimique en oxygene)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: composite sample means a sample obtained in accordance with section 7; (echantillon composite)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: deposit means to deposit or to permit the deposit into water frequented by fish; (rejeter)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effluent means all wastewaters deposited by a plant and includes process water, wash water, tank drainage, storm water and wastes from water and wastewater treatment facilities, but does not include

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) storm water that is protected from contamination by a deleterious substance prescribed by section 4 originating from the plant, where the average concentration of biochemical oxygen demanding matter in at least 3 samples of the storm water, taken at intervals of 15 minutes, does not exceed 50 mg/L, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) wastewater from the plant that, prior to being deposited, is treated at a site outside a plant for the purpose of controlling the pH of the wastewater and removing from the wastewater the deleterious substances prescribed by section 4, in such a manner that

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (i) the pH of the wastewater, determined in accordance with subsection 9(3), is between 6.0 and 9.0, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (ii) the quantity of deleterious substances remaining in that wastewater after the treatment, when added to the quantity of deleterious substances deposited directly, does not exceed the deposit of deleterious substances authorized under section 5; (effluent)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: equivalent month means a period of time equal to or greater than four weeks but not exceeding six weeks declared by the owner under subsection 12(2) or (3) for the purposes of these Regulations; (equivalent d'un mois)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: existing plant means a plant that commenced commercial production before March 31, 1977; (etablissement existant)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: expanded plant means any integrated or processing plant in which the total amount of finished product produced or any rendering plant in which the total amount of raw material processed during any year exceeds

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) in the case of a plant that commenced production on or before January 1, 1971, 2.5 times the average annual amount of finished product produced or raw material processed in that plant during the five-year period from 1971 to 1975, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) in the case of a plant that commenced production after January 1, 1971, 2.5 times the average annual amount of finished product produced or raw material processed in that plant from the date the plant commenced production to March 31, 1977; (etablissement a capacite accrue)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: finished product means the net quantity of saleable material produced by a plant; (produits finis)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: grease means the grease that results from the operation of a plant and that is contained in the effluent from that plant; (graisses)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: new plant means a plant that did not commence commercial production before March 31, 1977 and that commences commercial production on or after that date; (nouvel etablissement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: operating day means a period of 24 consecutive hours or part thereof during which the plant is in operation; (jour d'exploitation)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: owner of a plant means the owner or operator or his authorized representative; (proprietaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: plant includes facilities intended primarily for the slaughtering, dressing, processing or edible or inedible rendering of any meat or poultry products and associated livestock holding and receiving facilities and truck washing areas but does not include facilities

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) where only edible oils are produced,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) where only hides are processed, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) where no slaughtering is performed and the entire finished product is retailed to the public on the premises; (etablissement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: poultry integrated plant includes any plant that slaughters and dresses poultry; (abattoir de volailles)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: processing plant includes any plant that is not an integrated plant and that performs operations subsequent to slaughtering and dressing but does not include rendering plants; (etablissement de preparation)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: raw material means the material that is received at a rendering plant for processing and used to produce a finished product and includes blood, bones, fat, grease, offal, feathers and waste meat and poultry products; (matieres premieres)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: red meat integrated plant includes any plant that slaughters and dresses meat other than poultry; (abattoir de betail)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: rendering plant includes any plant that performs operations solely for the purpose of edible or inedible rendering of meat or poultry products, with or without oil refining; (fondoir)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: saleable material includes dressed carcasses, processed meats, inedible offal, hides and rendered or renderable products that are produced by a plant; (produit vendable)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: slaughtering day means a period of 24 consecutive hours or part thereof during which slaughtering takes place; (jour d'abattage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: storm water means water run-off that results from precipitation of any kind that falls on a plant or that passes over or through the plant; (eaux pluviales)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: total suspended matter means the non-filterable residue that results from the operation of a plant, that is contained in the effluent from that plant. (matieres totales en suspension)

heading: Application
paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to subsection (2), these Regulations apply to every new plant and every expanded plant.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Where a plant becomes an expanded plant, these Regulations apply to the expanded plant on the first day of the month following the month in which the plant became an expanded plant.

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: 4 For the purpose of the definition deleterious substance in subsection 34(1) of the Act, the following substances resulting from the operations of a plant to which these Regulations apply are hereby prescribed as deleterious substances:

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (a) biochemical oxygen demanding matter;

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (b) total suspended matter; and

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (c) grease.

heading: Authorized Deposit of Deleterious Substances
paragraph: 5 Subject to these Regulations, the owner of a plant of a class set out in Column I of Schedule I may deposit a deleterious substance prescribed by section 4 if

heading: Authorized Deposit of Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (a) the actual daily deposit of each deleterious substance, determined in accordance with subsection 11(1), does not exceed the authorized daily deposit of that substance for that class of plant as set out in Column III of that Schedule;

heading: Authorized Deposit of Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (b) the average daily deposit of each deleterious substance during an equivalent month, determined in accordance with subsection 11(2), does not exceed the authorized average daily deposit of that substance for that class of plant as set out in Column IV of that Schedule; and

heading: Authorized Deposit of Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (c) the pH of each composite sample of effluent, determined in accordance with subsection 9(3), is between 6.0 and 9.0.

heading: General
paragraph: 6 The owner of a plant shall, for each type of effluent deposited by the plant,

heading: General
paragraph: (a) install and maintain facilities, including sampling connections and flow measuring devices, of such type as the Minister may in writing approve for sampling and analysing effluents for the purpose of enabling the Minister to determine whether the owner is complying with the limits of authorized deposits prescribed by section 5;

heading: General
paragraph: (b) take a composite sample on the regular basis prescribed by section 8;

heading: General
paragraph: (c) analyse the sample referred to in paragraph (b) in accordance with section 9;

heading: General
paragraph: (d) measure the flow in accordance with section 10;

heading: General
paragraph: (e) determine the actual and average daily deposits of each deleterious substance in accordance with section 11; and

heading: General
paragraph: (f) conduct the acute lethality test on a composite sample from a plant referred to in Column I of Schedule II at the frequency set out opposite that plant in Column II thereof.

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: 7 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), a composite sample shall be obtained by collecting effluent discharged from a plant during an operating day

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: (a) continually during a sampling period of 24 hours at a rate in proportion to the flow rate of the effluent discharged; or

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: (b) in such a manner that equal volumes of effluent are delivered into a receptacle at equal intervals not longer than one hour during a sampling period of 24 hours.

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: (2) In the case of

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: (a) a red meat integrated plant producing less than 500 tonnes of finished product annually, or

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: (b) a poultry integrated plant producing less than 2 500 tonnes of finished product annually,

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: a composite sample shall be obtained by collecting effluent discharged from the plant in such a manner that a minimum of four equal volumes of effluent are delivered into a receptacle at equal intervals during a sampling period of not less than four hours during which slaughtering is performed.

heading: Method of Collecting Composite Samples
paragraph: (3) In the case of a processing plant producing less than 500 tonnes of finished product annually, a composite sample shall be obtained by collecting effluent discharged from the plant in such a manner that a minimum of four equal volumes of effluent are delivered into a receptacle at equal intervals during a sampling period of not less than four hours during which processing is performed.

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: 8 The sampling referred to in paragraph 6(b) shall be made

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (a) once every equivalent month in the case of

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (i) red meat integrated plants producing less than 500 tonnes of finished product annually,

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (ii) processing plants producing less than 500 tonnes of finished product annually, and

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (iii) poultry integrated plants producing less than 2 500 tonnes of finished product annually;

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (b) once a week in the case of

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (i) red meat integrated plants producing between 500 and 10 000 tonnes of finished product annually,

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (ii) processing plants producing more than 500 tonnes of finished product annually,

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (iii) poultry integrated plants producing between 2 500 and 7 000 tonnes of finished product annually, and

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (iv) all rendering plants;

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (c) twice a week in the case of

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (i) red meat integrated plants producing more than 10 000 tonnes of finished product annually, and

heading: Frequency of Sampling and Analysis
paragraph: (ii) poultry integrated plants producing more than 7 000 tonnes of finished product annually.

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: 9 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 6(c), the concentration in milligrams per litre of a substance described in an item of Schedule III, in each composite sample, shall be determined using

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (a) the test method set out in Column I and modified in Column II of that item; or

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (b) any other method, approved in writing by the Minister, the results of which can be confirmed by the method referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of paragraph 6(c), procedures pertaining to sampling, preservation and storage of samples and prevention of interference relating to the test methods referred to in paragraph (1)(a), as outlined in the general sections of the publication Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, 14th Edition (1975), published jointly by the American Public Health Association, American Water Works Association and the Water Pollution Control Federation, shall be adhered to.

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of paragraph 6(c), the pH of a composite sample shall be determined using

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (a) the test method prescribed by section 424 of the publication referred to in subsection (2); or

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (b) any other method, approved in writing by the Minister, the results of which can be confirmed by the method referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of paragraph 6(f), the acute lethality test shall be conducted using

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (a) the procedure for the 96-hour acute lethality static test described in Schedule IV; or

heading: Analytical and Other Test Methods
paragraph: (b) any other method, approved in writing by the Minister, the results of which can be confirmed by the method referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Flow Measurement
paragraph: 10 (1) Subject to subsection (2), for the purpose of paragraph 6(d), the flow of each type of effluent deposited by a plant shall be measured and recorded continuously.

heading: Flow Measurement
paragraph: (2) In the case of

heading: Flow Measurement
paragraph: (a) a red meat integrated plant producing less than 500 tonnes of finished product annually,

heading: Flow Measurement
paragraph: (b) a poultry integrated plant producing less than 2 500 tonnes of finished product annually, or

heading: Flow Measurement
paragraph: (c) a processing plant producing less than 500 tonnes of finished product annually,

heading: Flow Measurement
paragraph: the flow of effluent may be determined by measuring the total quantity of water taken in daily by the plant or the total quantity of effluent deposited daily by the plant if the effluent is deposited as a single flow.

heading: Calculation of Actual Deposit
paragraph: 11 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 6(e), the actual daily deposit per unit of production of each deleterious substance prescribed by section 4 shall be determined using the data obtained under subsection 9(1) and section 10 and shall be expressed

heading: Calculation of Actual Deposit
paragraph: (a) in the case of integrated plants or processing plants, in terms of kilograms per tonne of finished product per day; and

heading: Calculation of Actual Deposit
paragraph: (b) in the case of rendering plants, in terms of kilograms per tonne of raw material per day.

heading: Calculation of Actual Deposit
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of paragraph 6(e), the average daily deposit per unit of production during an equivalent month of each deleterious substance prescribed by section 4 shall be determined by calculating the average of the results obtained under subsection (1) and shall be expressed in the terms set out in that subsection.

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: 12 (1) The owner of a plant shall, within 30 days after the end of each equivalent month, sign, date and forward to the Minister a report, in such form as the Minister may in writing approve, showing for that equivalent month

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (a) the actual daily deposit of deleterious substances deposited by the plant on each day that samples were taken, determined and expressed in accordance with subsection 11(1);

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (b) the average daily deposit of deleterious substances deposited by the plant, determined and expressed in accordance with subsection 11(2);

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (c) the pH of composite samples, determined in accordance with subsection 9(3);

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (d) the production of the plant expressed in terms of tonnes of finished product for integrated and processing plants and in terms of tonnes of raw material for rendering plants;

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (e) the number of operating days;

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (f) the total daily flow, in litres, of each type of effluent discharged on each day that samples were taken;

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (g) the concentration of ammonia nitrogen for each composite sample analysed in the manner prescribed by subsection 9(1); and

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (h) the following details of any acute lethality test conducted in accordance with subsection 9(4), namely,

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (i) the date and time period of the composite sample collection,

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (ii) details on refrigeration, transportation and storage of the sample,

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (iii) the date and time the test commenced,

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (iv) the number of dead fish observed in the test and control vessels for the exposure times outlined in the test procedure used,

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (v) the per cent mortality of fish exposed to the toxicity test sample and to the control water at the completion of the test, and

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (vi) any other information that the Minister may require.

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (2) The owner of a new plant shall, before he deposits any deleterious substance prescribed by section 4, and the owner of an expanded plant shall, within 30 days of becoming subject to these Regulations, sign, date and forward to the Minister a declaration, in such form as the Minister may in writing approve,

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (a) showing whether the plant is an integrated plant, processing plant or rendering plant;

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (b) showing whether the plant will process red meat or poultry or both;

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (c) showing the projected annual production of the plant; and

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (d) declaring equivalent months for the remainder of the calendar year.

heading: Reporting and Records
paragraph: (3) The owner of a plant shall, within 30 days after the end of each calendar year, sign, date and forward to the Minister a declaration in such form as the Minister may in writing approve, showing the actual production of the plant for the previous year, in terms of tonnes of finished product for integrated and processing plants and tonnes of raw material for rendering plants and declaring equivalent months for the forthcoming year.

heading: Permitted Variation in Additional Conditions
paragraph: 13 Where the owner of a plant establishes to the satisfaction of the Minister that for scientific and technical reasons a scheme of sampling and analysis, measurement or reporting referred to in sections 7, 9, 10 and 12 other than at the regular time interval frequencies required by section 8 is sufficient to enable the Minister to determine whether the owner is complying with the limits of authorized deposits prescribed by section 5, the Minister may, in writing, permit the owner to

heading: Permitted Variation in Additional Conditions
paragraph: (a) take and analyse samples of each effluent in accordance with the scheme on a regular basis specified in the permit,

heading: Permitted Variation in Additional Conditions
paragraph: (b) measure the volume of each effluent in accordance with the scheme on a regular basis specified in the permit, or

heading: Permitted Variation in Additional Conditions
paragraph: (c) report to the Minister in accordance with the scheme on a regular basis specified in the permit

heading: Permitted Variation in Additional Conditions
paragraph: and sections 7 to 10 and 12 do not apply to the owner if he complies with the scheme on the regular basis specified in the permit.
