heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: 1 The applicable portions of APHAFootnote *, sections 801 and 810, shall be used as a basis for this test procedure with the following modifications:

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: Return to footnote *Refers to the publication Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, 14th Edition (1975), published jointly by the American Public Health Association, American Water Works Association and the Water Pollution Control Federation.

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (a) rainbow trout (Salmo gairdneri Richardson) shall be used as the standard test organism for the test procedure;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (b) only healthy, standardized stocks of properly acclimated rainbow trout shall be used;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (c) for each acute lethality test, at least 10 fish shall be exposed to a representative portion of the composite sample for a period of 96 hours and an equal number of fish shall be exposed for the same period under identical conditions to water used for holding fish stocks (control fish);

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (d) this test is invalid if greater than 10 per cent of the control fish die;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (e) for each gram of fish there shall be at least 1.5 litres of fresh test sample per 96-hour test;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (f) the minimum water depth in any test vessel shall be 10 cm;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (g) the test sample shall be aerated or oxygenated with only that amount of air or oxygen required to maintain a minimum dissolved oxygen level of 8 mg/l and aeration or oxygenation shall be minimized to reduce the stripping of volatile compounds or the oxidation of acutely lethal components in the test sample. A maximum of two hours aeration of the test sample is allowed prior to the commencement of the test;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (h) in any test, individual fish shall weigh between 0.5 and 10 grams and the weight of the largest fish shall not be more than twice the smallest;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (i) the test shall be conducted at 15° +/- 1° Celsius;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (j) the number of dead fish in the treatment and control vessels shall be recorded at 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (k) there shall be no direct adjustment of the pH or other chemical characteristics of the test sample;

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (l) when transportation or storage of a composite sample is necessary, special precautions shall be used to minimize degradation as follows:

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (i) the sample shall be kept in sealed containers which are completely filled to the exclusion of all air,

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (ii) if it is necessary for the sample to be stored more than 60 hours between collection and testing, the sample shall be brought to a temperature range of 1° to 6 °C as soon as possible after collection and maintained at this temperature range until just prior to being tested, and

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Section 9)Test Procedure for 96 Hour Acute Lethality Static Test
paragraph: (iii) acute lethality testing shall commence as soon as possible but in no case shall it commence later than four days after sampling.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Fisheries Act. (Loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: acutely lethal, in respect of an effluent, means that the effluent at 100% concentration kills

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) more than 50% of the rainbow trout subjected to it for a period of 96 hours, when tested in accordance with the acute lethality test set out in section 14.1;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) more than 50% of the threespine stickleback subjected to it for a period of 96 hours, when tested in accordance with the acute lethality test set out in section 14.2;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) more than 50% of the Daphnia magna subjected to it for a period of 48 hours, when tested in accordance with the acute lethality test set out in section 14.3; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) more than 50% of the Acartia tonsa subjected to it for a period of 48 hours, when tested in accordance with the acute lethality test set out in section 14.4. (letalite aigue)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: commercial operation, in respect of a mine, means an average rate of production equal to or greater than 10% of the design-rated capacity of the mine over a period of 90 consecutive days. (exploitation commerciale)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: composite sample means

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) a quantity of effluent consisting of not less than three equal volumes or three volumes proportionate to flow that have been collected at approximately equal time intervals over a sampling period of not less than seven hours and not more than 24 hours; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) a quantity of effluent collected continuously at a constant rate or at a rate proportionate to the rate of flow of the effluent over a sampling period of not less than seven hours and not more than 24 hours. (echantillon composite)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: diamond mine means any work or undertaking that is designed or is used, or has been used, in connection with a mining or milling activity to produce a diamond or an ore from which a diamond may be produced. It includes any cleared or disturbed area that is adjacent to such a work or undertaking. (mine de diamants)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effluent means any of the following:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) hydrometallurgical facility effluent, milling facility effluent, mine water effluent, tailings impoundment area effluent, treatment pond effluent or treatment facility effluent other than effluent from a sewage treatment facility; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) any seepage or surface runoff containing any deleterious substance that flows over, through or out of the site of a mine. (effluent)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: final discharge point, in respect of an effluent, means an identifiable discharge point of a mine beyond which the operator of the mine no longer exercises control over the quality of the effluent. (point de rejet final)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: hydrometallurgical facility effluent means effluent from the acidic leaching, solution concentration and recovery of metals by means of aqueous chemical methods, tailings slurries, and all other effluents deposited from a hydrometallurgical facility. (effluent d'installations d'hydrometallurgie)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: hydrometallurgy means the production of a metal by means of aqueous chemical methods for acidic leaching, solution concentration and recovery of metals from metal-bearing minerals other than metal-bearing minerals that have been thermally pre-treated or blended with metal-bearing minerals that have been thermally pre-treated. (hydrometallurgie)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: metal mine means any work or undertaking that is designed or is used, or has been used, in connection with a mining, milling or hydrometallurgical activity to produce a metal or a metal concentrate or an ore from which a metal or a metal concentrate may be produced, as well as any cleared or disturbed area that is adjacent to such a work or undertaking. It includes any work or undertaking, such as a smelter, pelletizing plant, sintering plant, refinery or acid plant, if its effluent is combined with the effluent from a mining, milling or hydrometallurgical activity whose purpose is to produce a metal or a metal concentrate or an ore from which a metal or a metal concentrate may be produced. (mine de metaux)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: milling means any of the following activities for the purpose of producing a diamond, metal or metal concentrate:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the crushing or grinding of ore or kimberlite;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) the processing of uranium ore or uranium enriched solution; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) the processing of tailings. (preparation du minerai)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: milling facility effluent means tailing slurries, heap leaching effluent, solution mining effluent and all other effluent deposited from a milling facility. (effluent d'installations de preparation du minerai)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: mine water effluent means, in respect of mining activities, water that is pumped from or flows out of any underground works, solution chambers or open pits. (effluent d'eau de mine)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: monthly mean concentration means the average value of the concentrations measured in all composite or grab samples collected from each final discharge point during each month when a deleterious substance is deposited. (concentration moyenne mensuelle)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: operator means any person who operates, has control or custody of or is in charge of a mine. (exploitant)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: placer mining means a mining operation that extracts minerals or metals from stream sediments by gravity or magnetic separation. (exploitation des placers)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Reference Method EPS 1/RM/10 means Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality Using Threespine Stickleback, published in December 2017 by the Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time. (methode de reference SPE 1/RM/10)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 means Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Effluents to Rainbow Trout (Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13), July 1990, published by the Department of the Environment, as amended in December 2000, and as may be further amended from time to time. (methode de reference SPE 1/RM/13)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 means Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Effluents to Daphnia magna (Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14), July 1990, published by the Department of the Environment, as amended in December 2000, and as may be further amended from time to time. (methode de reference SPE 1/RM/14)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Reference Method STB 1/RM/60 means Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality Using Acartia tonsa, published in June 2019 by the Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time. (methode de reference DGST 1/RM/60)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: suspended solids means any solid matter contained in an effluent that is retained on a 1.5 micron pore filter paper when the effluent is tested in compliance with the analytical requirements set out in Table 1 of Schedule 3. (matieres en suspension)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: treatment facility effluent means water from a polishing pond, treatment pond, settling pond or water treatment plant or from any mine effluent treatment facility. (effluent d'installations de traitement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) Every reference in these Regulations to column 1, 2, 3 or 4 of Schedule 4 shall be read as

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) a reference to column 1, 2, 3 or 4 of Table 1 of Schedule 4, in the case of a mine to which subparagraph 4(1)(a)(i) applies; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) a reference to column 1, 2, 3 or 4 of Table 2 of Schedule 4, in the case of a mine to which subparagraph 4(1)(a)(ii) applies.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2 (1) These Regulations apply in respect of the following mines:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) metal mines that, at any time on or after June 6, 2002,

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) exceed an effluent flow rate of 50 m3 per day, based on the effluent deposited from all the final discharge points of the mine, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) deposit a deleterious substance in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) diamond mines that, at any time on or after June 1, 2018,

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) exceed an effluent flow rate of 50 m3 per day, based on the effluent deposited from all the final discharge points of the mine, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) deposit a deleterious substance in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) However, these Regulations do not apply in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) placer mining;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) a metal mine that stopped commercial operation before June 6, 2002, unless it returns to commercial operation on or after that date; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) a diamond mine that stopped commercial operation before June 1, 2018, unless it returns to commercial operation on or after that date.

heading: Application
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), sections 4 to 31 do not apply in respect of a mine that is a recognized closed mine under subsection 32(2) unless it returns to commercial operation, in which case it ceases to be a recognized closed mine.

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: 3 For the purpose of the definition deleterious substance in subsection 34(1) of the Act, the following substances or classes of substances are prescribed as deleterious substances:

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (a) arsenic;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (b) copper;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (c) cyanide;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (d) lead;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (e) nickel;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (f) zinc;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (g) suspended solids;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (h) radium 226; and

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (i) un-ionized ammonia.

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: 4 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of a mine is authorized to deposit, or to permit the deposit of, an effluent containing any deleterious substance that is prescribed in section 3 in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act if

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: (a) the concentration of the deleterious substance in the effluent does not exceed the maximum authorized concentrations that are set out in columns 2, 3 and 4 of

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: (i) Table 1 of Schedule 4, in the case of a mine in respect of which these Regulations apply for the first time on or after June 1, 2021 or in the case of a recognized closed mine that returns to commercial operation on or after June 1, 2021, or

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: (ii) Table 2 of Schedule 4, in any other case;

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: (b) the pH of the effluent is equal to or greater than 6.0 but is not greater than 9.5; and

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: (c) the effluent is not acutely lethal.

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: (2) The authority in subsection (1) is conditional on the owner or operator complying with sections 6 to 27.

heading: Authority to Deposit in Water or Place Referred to in Subsection 36(3) of Act
paragraph: 4.1 Paragraph 4(1)(c) does not apply in the case where the effluent is determined to be acutely lethal in accordance with the procedures set out in section 5 or 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 when the owner or operator of a mine is testing at the frequency prescribed in subsection 14(1), unless the effluent is determined to be acutely lethal in accordance with any other acute lethality test.

heading: Authority to Deposit in Tailings Impoundment Areas
paragraph: 5 (1) Despite section 4, the owner or operator of a mine may deposit or permit the deposit of waste rock, acutely lethal effluent or effluent of any pH and containing any concentration of a deleterious substance that is prescribed in section 3 into a tailings impoundment area that is either

heading: Authority to Deposit in Tailings Impoundment Areas
paragraph: (a) a water or place set out in Schedule 2; or

heading: Authority to Deposit in Tailings Impoundment Areas
paragraph: (b) a disposal area that is confined by anthropogenic or natural structures or by both, other than a disposal area that is, or is part of, a natural water body that is frequented by fish.

heading: Authority to Deposit in Tailings Impoundment Areas
paragraph: (2) The authority in subsection (1) is conditional on the owner or operator complying with sections 7 to 28.

heading: Authority to Deposit in Tailings Impoundment Areas
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this section, any acutely lethal effluent is prescribed as a deleterious substance.

heading: Prohibition on Diluting Effluent
paragraph: 6 The owner or operator of a mine shall not combine effluent with water or any other effluent for the purpose of diluting effluent before it is deposited.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring
paragraph: 7 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall conduct environmental effects monitoring studies in accordance with the requirements and within the periods set out in Schedule 5.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring
paragraph: (2) The studies shall be conducted using documented and validated methods, and their results interpreted and reported on in accordance with generally accepted standards of good scientific practice at the time that the studies are conducted.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator shall record the results of the studies and submit to the Minister of the Environment, in accordance with the requirements set out in Schedule 5, the reports and information required by that Schedule.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: 8 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall submit in writing to the Minister of the Environment the information referred to in subsection (2) not later than 60 days after the day on which any of the following occur:

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (a) the mine becomes subject to these Regulations;

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (b) ownership of the mine is transferred; and

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (c) the mine returns to commercial operation after it has become a recognized closed mine.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (2) The information that shall be submitted is

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (a) the name and address of both the owner and the operator of the mine;

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (b) the name and address of any parent company of the owner and the operator; and

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (c) the design-rated capacity of the mine, expressed as tonnes per year, and a description and rationale of how the design-rated capacity was determined.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator shall submit in writing to the Minister of the Environment any change in the information not later than 60 days after the change occurs.

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: 9 The owner or operator of a mine shall identify each final discharge point and submit in writing to the Minister of the Environment, not later than 60 days after the day on which the mine becomes subject to these Regulations, the following information:

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: (a) plans, specifications and a general description of each final discharge point together with its location by latitude and longitude;

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: (b) a description of how each final discharge point is designed and maintained in respect of the deposit of deleterious substances; and

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: (c) the name of the receiving body of water, if there is a name.

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: 10 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall submit in writing to the Minister of the Environment the information required by section 9, for

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: (a) any final discharge point that is identified by an inspector, and that was not identified as required by section 9, within 30 days after the discharge point is identified; and

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: (b) each new final discharge point, at least 60 days before depositing effluent from that new final discharge point.

heading: Final Discharge Points
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator shall submit in writing to the Minister of the Environment the information on any proposed change to a final discharge point at least 60 days before the change is to be made.

heading: Monitoring Equipment Information
paragraph: 11 The owner or operator of a mine shall keep records relating to effluent monitoring equipment that contain

heading: Monitoring Equipment Information
paragraph: (a) a description of the equipment and, if applicable, the manufacturer's specifications and the year and model number of the equipment; and

heading: Monitoring Equipment Information
paragraph: (b) the results of the calibration tests of the equipment.

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: 12 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall, not less than once per week and at least 24 hours apart, collect from each final discharge point

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (a) a grab sample or composite sample of effluent and record the pH of the sample at the time of its collection and record, without delay after collecting the sample, the concentrations of the deleterious substances prescribed in section 3 except un-ionized ammonia; and

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (b) a grab sample of effluent and record the temperature and the pH of the sample at the time of its collection and record, without delay after collecting the sample, the concentrations of total ammonia expressed as nitrogen (N).

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (2) Testing conducted under subsection (1) shall comply with the analytical requirements set out in Table 1 of Schedule 3 and shall be done in accordance with generally accepted standards of good scientific practice at the time of the sampling using documented and validated methods.

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), the owner or operator of a mine is not required to collect samples for the purpose of recording the concentrations of cyanide if cyanide has never been used as a process reagent at the mine.

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator of a mine shall determine and record the concentration of un-ionized ammonia, using the temperature, pH and concentration of total ammonia recorded under paragraph (1)(b), in accordance with the following formula:

paragraph: where

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: 13 (1) The owner or operator of a mine may reduce the frequency of conducting tests relating to the concentrations of arsenic, copper, cyanide, lead, nickel, zinc or un-ionized ammonia at a final discharge point to not less than once in each calendar quarter, each test being conducted at least one month apart, if that substance's monthly mean concentration at that final discharge point is less than 10% of the value set out in column 2 of Schedule 4 for 12 consecutive months.

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of a mine, other than an uranium mine, may reduce the frequency of conducting tests relating to the concentration of radium 226 at a final discharge point to not less than once in each calendar quarter, each test being conducted at least one month apart, if the concentration of radium 226 at that final discharge point is less than 0.037 Bq/L for 10 consecutive weeks.

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of a mine shall increase the frequency of conducting tests relating to the concentration of a deleterious substance at a final discharge point to the frequency prescribed in section 12

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (a) in the case of a deleterious substance mentioned in subsection (1), if that substance's monthly mean concentration at that final discharge point is equal to or greater than 10% of the value set out in column 2 of Schedule 4; and

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (b) in the case of radium 226, if the concentration of radium 226 at that final discharge point is equal to or greater than 0.037 Bq/L.

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator of a mine shall increase the frequency of conducting tests relating to the concentration of a deleterious substance at all final discharge points to the frequency prescribed in section 12 for all the substances mentioned in subsections (1) and (2) if the owner or operator

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (a) fails to perform a test required under those subsections in accordance with the prescribed frequency; or

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (b) fails to submit a report required under subsection 21(1) or section 22 within the prescribed time.

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (5) If the owner or operator of a mine changes the location of a final discharge point, the owner or operator shall increase the frequency of conducting tests relating to the concentration of a deleterious substance at that final discharge point to the frequency prescribed in section 12 for all the deleterious substances mentioned in subsections (1) and (2).

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (6) The owner or operator of a mine who reduces the frequency of conducting tests under subsection (1) or (2) shall

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (a) notify the Minister of the Environment, in writing, at least 30 days in advance, of that fact;

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (b) select and record the sampling dates not less than 30 days in advance of collecting the samples of effluent; and

heading: Deleterious Substance and pH Testing
paragraph: (c) collect the sample on the selected day except if, owing to unforeseen circumstances, they cannot sample on that day, in which case, they shall do so as soon as practicable after that day.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 14 (1) Subject to section 15, the owner or operator of a mine shall collect, once a month, a grab sample of effluent from each final discharge point and determine whether the effluent is acutely lethal by conducting acute lethality tests on aliquots of each effluent sample in accordance with sections 14.1 to 14.4.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), the owner or operator of a mine

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (a) shall select and record the sampling date not less than 30 days in advance of collecting the grab sample;

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (b) shall collect the sample on the selected day except if, owing to unforeseen circumstances, they cannot sample on that day, in which case, they shall do so as soon as practicable after that day; and

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (c) shall collect the grab samples not less than 15 days apart.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (3) When collecting a grab sample of effluent for the purposes of subsection (1), the owner or operator of a mine shall

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (a) collect a sufficient volume of effluent to enable the owner or operator to comply with paragraph 15(1)(a); and

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (b) record the temperature and the pH of each grab sample of effluent at the time of the sample's collection.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 14.1 Unless the salinity value of the effluent is greater than ten parts per thousand and the effluent is deposited into marine waters, the owner or operator of a mine shall determine whether the effluent is acutely lethal by conducting an acute lethality test in accordance with the procedures set out in section 5 or 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 14.2 If the salinity value of the effluent is greater than ten parts per thousand and the effluent is deposited into marine waters, the owner or operator of a mine shall determine whether the effluent is acutely lethal by conducting an acute lethality test in accordance with the procedures set out in section 5 or 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/10.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 14.3 Unless the salinity value of the effluent is greater than four parts per thousand and the effluent is deposited into marine waters, the owner or operator of a mine shall, in addition to conducting the acute lethality test set out in section 14.1, determine whether the effluent is acutely lethal by conducting an acute lethality test in accordance with the procedures set out in section 5 or 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 14.4 If the salinity value of the effluent is greater than four parts per thousand and the effluent is deposited into marine waters, the owner or operator of a mine shall, in addition to conducting the acute lethality test set out in either section 14.1 or 14.2, determine whether the effluent is acutely lethal by conducting an acute lethality test in accordance with the procedures set out in section 5 or 6 of Reference Method STB 1/RM/60.

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 15 (1) If an effluent sample is determined to be acutely lethal by an acute lethality test, the owner or operator of a mine shall

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (a) without delay,

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (i) conduct the effluent characterization set out in subsection 4(1) of Schedule 5 on the aliquot of each grab sample collected under subsection 14(1),

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (ii) record the concentration of total ammonia and, using that concentration and using the temperature and pH recorded under paragraph 14(3)(b), determine the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in accordance with the formula set out in subsection 12(4), and

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (iii) record the concentrations of the deleterious substances prescribed in section 3;

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (b) collect a grab sample twice a month from the final discharge point from which the effluent sample determined to be acutely lethal was collected, record the temperature and the pH of each sample at the time of its collection and, without delay, conduct the acute lethality test that determined the effluent sample to be acutely lethal on each grab sample in accordance with the procedure set out in section 6 of the applicable reference method and, if the sample is determined to be acutely lethal, without delay,

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (i) conduct the effluent characterization set out in subsection 4(1) of Schedule 5 on the aliquot of each grab sample,

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (ii) record the concentration of total ammonia and, using that concentration and using the temperature and pH recorded under this paragraph, determine the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in accordance with the formula set out in subsection 12(4), and

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (iii) record the concentrations of the deleterious substances prescribed in section 3; and

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (c) collect the grab samples not less than seven days apart.

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator may resume sampling and testing at the frequency prescribed in section 14 if the effluent is determined not to be acutely lethal in three consecutive tests conducted under paragraph (1)(b).

heading: Increased Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 15.1 Despite paragraph 15(1)(c), if an effluent sample is determined to be acutely lethal when tested using the acute lethality test set out in section 14.3, the owner or operator of a mine shall, without delay, collect the first grab sample required by paragraph 15(1)(b) and comply with the requirements of that paragraph.

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 16 (1) The owner or operator of a mine may reduce the frequency of conducting an acute lethality test at a final discharge point to once in each calendar quarter if the effluent from that final discharge point is determined not to be acutely lethal by that acute lethality test for 12 consecutive months.

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of determining whether that effluent is acutely lethal for the 12-month period referred to in subsection (1), the owner or operator of a mine shall use the results of the acute lethality tests conducted under subsection 14(1).

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of a mine shall notify the Minister of the Environment in writing at least 30 days before the reduction of the frequency of acute lethality testing.

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator who reduces the frequency of conducting acute lethality testing under subsection (1) shall

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (a) select and record the sampling date not less than 30 days in advance of collecting the grab samples; and

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (b) collect the grab samples not less than 45 days apart.

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (5) If a grab sample is determined to be acutely lethal by an acute lethality test when the owner or operator of a mine is testing at the frequency prescribed in subsection (1), the owner or operator shall increase the frequency of conducting that test to the frequency prescribed in section 15 and conduct that test in accordance with that section.

heading: Reduced Frequency of Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (6) If the location of a final discharge point is changed, the owner or operator of a mine shall, at that final discharge point, increase the frequency of conducting all the acute lethality tests to the frequency prescribed in subsection 14(1) and conduct those tests in accordance with that subsection.

heading: Obligation to Record All Test Results
paragraph: 18 The owner or operator of a mine shall record without delay the data referred to in section 9.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/10, section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13, section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 and section 9.1 of Reference Method STB 1/RM/60 for each acute lethality test.

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: 19 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall record, in cubic metres, the total monthly volume of effluent deposited from each final discharge point for each month during which there was a deposit.

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (2) The total monthly volume of effluent deposited shall be either

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (a) determined on the basis of the average of the flow rates, expressed in cubic metres per day, measured and calculated as follows:

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (i) by measuring the flow rate at the same time as samples are collected under section 12,

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (ii) by calculating the average monthly flow rate by adding the flow rate measurements taken during the month and dividing the total by the number of times the flow rate was measured, and

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (iii) by multiplying the average monthly flow rate by the number of days during the month that effluent was deposited; or

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (b) determined by using a monitoring system that provides a continuous measure of the volume of effluent deposited.

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator shall

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (a) measure the flow rate or volume of effluent deposited by using a monitoring system that is accurate to within 15% of measured flow rate or volume; and

heading: Volume of Effluent

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: 21 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall submit to the Minister of the Environment an effluent monitoring report for all tests and monitoring conducted during each calendar quarter not later than 45 days after the end of the quarter.

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the effluent monitoring report shall include

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (a) the data referred to in section 9.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/10, section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 and section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 as required by section 18;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (a.1) for each acute lethality test that is conducted under section 14.4,

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (i) the date and time when the effluent sample was collected,

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (ii) the location of the final discharge point from which the sample was collected, and

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (iii) the percentage mortality in 100% effluent test concentration;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (b) the concentration and monthly mean concentration of each deleterious substance prescribed in section 3 that is contained in the effluent samples collected under subsection 12(1) and the concentrations of such deleterious substances contained in the effluent samples collected under subsection 13(1) or (2);

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (c) the pH of the effluent samples as required by subsection 12(1);

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (d) whether a composite or grab sample collection method was used for each effluent sample as required by subsection 12(1);

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (d.1) for each month of the calendar quarter, the number of days that effluent was deposited;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (e) the total volume of effluent deposited during each month of the reporting quarter as recorded under section 19;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (f) the mass loading of the deleterious substances prescribed in section 3 as recorded under section 20; and

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (g) the results of the effluent characterization conducted under paragraph 15(1)(a).

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (3) If no effluent is deposited in a calendar quarter, the report shall only include a statement to that effect.

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: 22 The owner or operator of a mine shall submit to the Minister of the Environment, not later than March 31 in each year, a report that shall include

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (a) the identifying information set out in Part 1 of Schedule 6;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (b) the effluent monitoring results for the previous calendar year for each final discharge point, including

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (i) for test results respecting the prescribed deleterious substances and the pH, the information set out in Part 2 of Schedule 6, and

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (ii) for each acute lethality test,

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (A) the date when the sample was collected,

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (B) the location of the final discharge point from which the sample was collected, and

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (C) the percentage mortality in 100% effluent test concentration; and

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (c) the following information regarding non-compliance:

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (i) if the results of any effluent monitoring tests indicate that the maximum authorized concentrations set out in Schedule 4 were exceeded or that the pH of the effluent is less than 6.0 or greater than 9.5, the causes of that non-compliance and the remedial measures that are planned or that have been implemented, and

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (ii) if the results of any acute lethality tests indicate that an effluent sample was determined to be acutely lethal, the remedial measures that are planned or that have been implemented.

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: 23 Any report or information referred to in sections 7, 21 and 22 shall be submitted electronically in the format provided by the Department of the Environment, but the report or information shall be submitted in writing if

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (a) no such format has been provided; or

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (b) it is, owing to circumstances beyond the control of either the owner or the operator, impracticable to submit the report or information electronically in the format provided.

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: 24 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall notify an inspector without delay if the results of the effluent monitoring tests conducted under section 12 or 13, subsection 14(1) or section 15 or 16 indicate that

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (a) the limits set out in Schedule 4 are being or have been exceeded;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (b) the pH of the effluent is less than 6.0 or greater than 9.5; or

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (c) an effluent is acutely lethal.

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator shall provide a written report of the test results to the inspector within 30 days after the tests have been completed.

heading: Relief
paragraph: 25 (1) Any time period specified for collecting samples of effluent referred to in this Division may be extended if

heading: Relief
paragraph: (a) unforeseen circumstances cause safety concerns or access problems and render the collection of samples of effluent impracticable; and

heading: Relief
paragraph: (b) the owner or operator of a mine notifies an inspector, without delay, of the circumstances and indicates when they expect to be able to collect the samples.

heading: Relief
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator shall collect the samples of effluent without delay when the circumstances permit.

heading: End of Commercial Operation Notice
paragraph: 26 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall notify the Minister of the Environment in writing of the day on which the mine has stopped commercial operation not later than 90 days after the end of commercial operation.

heading: End of Commercial Operation Notice
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator shall notify the Minister of the Environment in writing without delay if the mine returns to commercial operation.

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: 27 The owner or operator of a mine shall keep all records, books of account or other documents required by these Regulations at the mine for a period of not less than five years, beginning on the day on which they are made, including

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (a) records relating to all final discharge points, including any changes to those records;

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (b) records relating to effluent monitoring equipment, including the calibration of that equipment;

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (c) records relating to the data referred to in section 9.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/10, section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13, section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 and section 9.1 of Reference Method STB 1/RM/60;

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (d) compensation plans;

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (e) emergency response plans, including each update to the plan;

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (f) reports on any unauthorized deposits;

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (g) reports or other documents prepared and data collected for the purposes of environmental effects monitoring studies; and

heading: Records, Books of Account or Other Documents
paragraph: (h) records and reports of measurements with respect to the pH, temperature and concentration of any deleterious substance prescribed in section 3.

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: 27.1 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall, before depositing a deleterious substance into a tailings impoundment area that is set out in Schedule 2, submit to the Minister of the Environment a compensation plan that includes the information described in subsection (2) and obtain that Minister's approval of the plan.

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (2) The purpose of the compensation plan is to offset the loss of fish habitat resulting from the deposit of any deleterious substance into the tailings impoundment area. It shall contain the following information:

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (a) a description of the location of the tailings impoundment area and of fish habitat that will be affected by the deposit;

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (b) a quantitative impact assessment of the deposit on fish habitat;

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (c) a description of the measures to be taken to offset the loss of fish habitat;

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (d) a description of the measures to be taken during the planning and implementation of the compensation plan to mitigate any potential adverse effects on fish habitat that could result from the plan's implementation;

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (e) a description of the measures to be taken to monitor the plan's implementation;

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (f) a description of the measures to be taken to verify the extent to which the plan's purpose has been achieved;

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (g) the time required to implement the plan that allows for the achievement of the plan's purpose within a reasonable time; and

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (h) an estimate of the cost of implementing each element of the plan.

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of a mine shall submit with the compensation plan an irrevocable letter of credit issued by a recognized Canadian financial institution, or another equivalent financial guarantee, including a performance bond, to cover the costs of implementing the plan.

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (4) The Minister of the Environment shall approve the compensation plan if it meets the requirements of subsection (2) and the owner or operator of a mine has complied with subsection (3).

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (5) The owner or operator of a mine shall ensure that the compensation plan approved by the Minister of the Environment is implemented and, if the compensation plan's purpose is not being achieved, the owner or operator shall inform the Minister of the Environment.

heading: Compensation Plan
paragraph: (6) If the compensation plan's purpose is not being achieved, the owner or operator of a mine shall, as soon as practicable in the circumstances, identify and implement all necessary remedial measures to ensure that the purpose is achieved.

heading: Deposits from Tailings Impoundment Areas
paragraph: 28 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall deposit effluent from a tailings impoundment area only through a final discharge point that is monitored and reported on in accordance with the requirements of these Regulations.

heading: Deposits from Tailings Impoundment Areas
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of a mine shall comply with section 6 and the conditions prescribed in paragraphs 4(1)(a) to (c) for all effluent that exits a tailing impoundment area.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: 30 (1) The owner or operator of a mine shall prepare an emergency response plan that describes the measures to be taken in respect of a deleterious substance within the meaning of subsection 34(1) of the Act to prevent any unauthorized deposit of such a substance or to mitigate the effects of such a deposit.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (2) The emergency response plan shall include the following elements:

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (a) the identification of any unauthorized deposit that can reasonably be expected to occur at the mine and that can reasonably be expected to result in damage or danger to fish habitat or fish or the use by man of fish, and the identification of the damage or danger;

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (b) a description of the measures to be used to prevent, prepare for, respond to and recover from a deposit identified under paragraph (a);

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (c) a list of the individuals who are to implement the plan in the event of an unauthorized deposit, and a description of their roles and responsibilities;

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (d) the identification of the emergency response training required for each of the individuals listed under paragraph (c);

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (e) a list of the emergency response equipment included as part of the plan, and the equipment's location; and

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (f) alerting and notification procedures including the measures to be taken to notify members of the public who may be adversely affected by a deposit identified under paragraph (a).

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator shall complete the emergency response plan and have it available for inspection no later than 60 days after the mine becomes subject to this section.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator shall update and test the emergency response plan at least once each year to ensure that the plan continues to meet the requirements of subsection (2).

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (4.1) The owner or operator of a mine shall, each time the emergency response plan is tested, record the following information and keep the record for at least five years:

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (a) a summary of the test;

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (b) the test results; and

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (c) any modifications that are made to the plan as a consequence of the test.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (4.2) The owner or operator of a mine shall ensure that a copy of the most recent version of the emergency response plan is kept at the mine in a location that is readily available to the individuals who are responsible for implementing the plan.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (5) If a mine has not been subject to the requirements of this section for more than one year, a new emergency response plan shall be prepared and completed no later than 60 days after the day on which the mine again becomes subject to this section.

heading: Reporting
paragraph: 31 A report required by subsection 38(7) of the Act in respect of the unauthorized deposit of a deleterious substance shall contain the following information:

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (a) the name, description and concentration of the deleterious substance deposited;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (b) the estimated quantity of the deposit and how the estimate was achieved;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (c) the day on which, and hour at which, the deposit occurred;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (d) the quantity of the deleterious substance that was deposited at a place other than through a final discharge point and the identification of that place, including the location by latitude and longitude and, if applicable, the civic address;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (e) the quantity of the deleterious substance that was deposited through a final discharge point and the identification of that discharge point;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (f) the name of the receiving body of water, if there is a name, and the location by latitude and longitude where the deleterious substance entered the receiving body of water;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (g) the results of the acute lethality tests conducted under subsection 31.1(1) or a statement indicating that acute lethality tests were not conducted but that notification was given under subsection 31.1(2);

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (h) the circumstances of the deposit, the measures that were taken to mitigate the effects of the deposit and, if the emergency response plan was implemented, details concerning its implementation; and

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (i) the measures that were taken, or that are intended to be taken, to prevent any similar occurrence of an unauthorized deposit.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: 31.1 (1) If an unauthorized deposit of a deleterious substance occurs, the owner or operator of a mine shall, without delay, collect a grab sample of effluent at the place where the deposit occurred and determine whether the effluent is acutely lethal by conducting tests on aliquots of each effluent sample in accordance with sections 14.1 to 14.4.

heading: Acute Lethality Testing
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the owner or operator of a mine is not required to conduct those tests if they notify an inspector, without delay, that the deposit is an acutely lethal effluent.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 32 (1) An owner or operator who intends to close a mine shall

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) provide written notice of that intention to the Minister of the Environment;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) maintain the mine's rate of production at less than 10% of its design-rated capacity for a continuous period of three years starting on the day on which the written notice is received by the Minister of the Environment; and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (c) conduct a biological monitoring study during the three-year period referred to in paragraph (b) in accordance with Division 3 of Part 2 of Schedule 5.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (2) If the owner or operator has complied with all of the requirements set out in paragraphs (1)(a) to (c), the mine becomes a recognized closed mine after the expiry of the three-year period referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator shall notify the Minister of the Environment in writing at least 60 days before reopening the recognized closed mine.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator referred to in this section shall keep at any place in Canada all records, books of account or other documents required by these Regulations for a period of not less than five years beginning on the day they are made, and shall notify the Minister of the Environment in writing of their location.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: 33 (1) The owner or operator of a recognized closed mine shall submit in writing to the Minister of the Environment the information referred to in subsection (2) not later than 60 days after the day on which

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (a) the recognized closed mine becomes subject to these Regulations; or

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (b) ownership of the recognized closed mine is transferred.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (2) The information that shall be submitted is the name and address of

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (a) both the owner and the operator of the recognized closed mine; and

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (b) any parent company of the owner or the operator.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator shall notify the Minister of the Environment of any change in the information not later than 60 days after the change occurs.
