heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in this Schedule.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: biological monitoring study means a study referred to in section 9. (etude de suivi biologique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effect on fish tissue from mercury means a concentration of total mercury that exceeds 0.5 μg/g wet weight in fish tissue that is taken in an exposure area and that is statistically different from and higher than the concentration of total mercury in fish tissue that is taken in a reference area. (effet du mercure sur les tissus de poissons)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effect on the benthic invertebrate community means a statistical difference between data referred to in subparagraph 12(1)(e)(ii) and paragraph 12(1)(f) from a study respecting the benthic invertebrate community conducted in

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) an exposure area and a reference area; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) sampling areas within an exposure area where there are gradually decreasing effluent concentrations. (effet sur la communaute d'invertebres benthiques)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effect on the fish population means a statistical difference between data relating to the indicators referred to in subparagraph 12(1)(e)(i) from a study respecting fish population conducted in

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) an exposure area and a reference area; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) sampling areas within an exposure area where there are gradually decreasing effluent concentrations. (effet sur la population de poissons)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: exposure area means all fish habitat and waters frequented by fish that are exposed to effluent. (zone exposee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fish has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Act but does not include parts of fish, parts of shellfish, parts of crustaceans or parts of marine animals. (poisson)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: reference area means water frequented by fish that is not exposed to effluent and that has fish habitat that, as far as practicable, is most similar to that of the exposure area. (zone de reference)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: sampling area means the area within an exposure or reference area where representative samples are collected. (zone d'echantillonnage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of this schedule, critical effect size, in relation to an effect indicator set out in column 1 of the following table, means the critical effect size set out in column 2:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 Environmental effects monitoring studies consist of the effluent and water quality monitoring studies set out in Part 1 and the biological monitoring studies set out in Part 2.

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: 3 Effluent and water quality monitoring studies consist of effluent characterization, sublethal toxicity testing and water quality monitoring.

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: 4 (1) Effluent characterization is conducted by analyzing a sample of effluent and recording the hardness, alkalinity, electrical conductivity and temperature of the sample and the concentrations, in total values, of the following substances:

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (a) aluminum;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (b) cadmium;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (c) iron;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (d) subject to subsection (4), mercury;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (e) molybdenum;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (f) selenium;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (g) nitrate (concentration in units of nitrogen);

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (h) chloride;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (i) chromium;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (j) cobalt;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (k) sulphate;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (l) thallium;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (m) uranium;

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (n) phosphorus (concentration in units of phosphorus); and

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (o) manganese.

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (2) The analysis shall comply with the analytical requirements set out in Table 2 of Schedule 3.

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (3) The effluent characterization shall be conducted once per calendar quarter on an aliquot of effluent sample collected under sections 12 and 13 of these Regulations from each final discharge point at least one month after the sample on which the previous characterization was conducted.

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (4) The recording of the concentration of mercury in effluent referred to in paragraph (1)(d) may be discontinued if that concentration is less than 0.10 µg/L in 12 consecutive samples collected under subsection (3).

heading: Effluent Characterization
paragraph: (5) Quality assurance and quality control measures shall be implemented that will ensure the accuracy of the effluent characterization data.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: 5 (1) Sublethal toxicity testing shall, in the case of effluent deposited into fresh waters, be conducted using the following test methodologies, as amended from time to time:

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (a) in the case of a fish species,

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (i) Biological Test Method: Test of Larval Growth and Survival Using Fathead Minnows (Report EPS 1/RM/22), published by the Department of the Environment, or

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (ii) Biological Test Method: Toxicity Tests Using Early Life Stages of Salmonid Fish (Rainbow Trout) (Reference Method EPS 1/RM/28), published by the Department of the Environment;

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (b) in the case of an invertebrate species, Biological Test Method: Test of Reproduction and Survival Using the Cladoceran Ceriodaphnia dubia (Report EPS 1/RM/21), published by the Department of the Environment;

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (c) in the case of a plant species, Biological Test Method: Test for Measuring the Inhibition of Growth Using the Freshwater Macrophyte, Lemna minor (Reference Method EPS 1/RM/37), published by the Department of the Environment, as it applies to the biological endpoint based on the number of fronds; and

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (d) in the case of an algal species,

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (i) Biological Test Method: Growth Inhibition Test Using a Freshwater Alga (Report EPS 1/RM/25), published by the Department of the Environment, or

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (ii) Determination de la toxicite : inhibition de la croissance chez l'algue Pseudokirchneriella subcapitata, (Methode de reference MA 500 - P. sub. 1.0, rev. 3), published by the Centre d'expertise en analyse environnementale du Quebec du ministere du Developpement durable, de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques du Quebec.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (2) Sublethal toxicity testing shall, in the case of effluent deposited into marine or estuarine waters, be conducted for fish species, invertebrate species and algal species using the following test methodologies, as amended from time to time, as applicable to each species:

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (a) Biological Test Method: Fertilization Assay Using Echinoids (Sea Urchins and Sand Dollars) (Report EPS 1/RM/27), published by the Department of the Environment;

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (b) Short-term Methods for Estimating the Chronic Toxicity of Effluents and Receiving Waters to Marine and Estuarine Organisms (Reference Method EPA/821/R-02/014), published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency; and

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (c) Short-term Methods for Estimating the Chronic Toxicity of Effluent and Receiving Waters to West Coast Marine and Estuarine Organisms (Reference Method EPA/600/R-95-136), published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (3) The sublethal toxicity tests shall be conducted on aliquots of the same effluent sample collected for effluent characterization collected from the mine's final discharge point that has potentially the most adverse environmental impact on the environment, taking into account

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (a) the loading of the deleterious substances contained in the effluent as determined under subsection 20(2) of these Regulations; and

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (b) the manner in which the effluent mixes within the exposure area.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: 6 (1) The sublethal toxicity tests shall be conducted on the species referred to in subsections 5(1) and (2) two times each calendar year for three years and each test shall be conducted on an aliquot of effluent sample collected at least one month after the collection of the sample used in the previous tests.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (2) However, if effluent is discharged for 31 consecutive days or less in a calendar year, the tests may be conducted only once in that year.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (3) After three years, the tests shall be conducted once per calendar quarter on the species referred to in subsection 5(1) or (2), as the case may be, whose results for all the tests conducted in accordance with subsections (1) and (2) - including such tests conducted in addition to the number required by those subsections - produce the lowest geometric mean, taking into account the inhibition concentration that produces a 25% effect or an effective concentration of 25%.

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: 7 (1) Water quality monitoring is conducted by

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (a) collecting samples of water from

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (i) the exposure area surrounding the point of entry of effluent into water from each final discharge point and from the related reference areas, and

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (ii) the sampling areas that are selected under clauses 10(b)(i)(B) and 10(c)(i)(A);

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (b) recording the temperature of the water and the dissolved oxygen concentration in the water in the exposure and reference areas where the samples are collected;

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (c) recording the concentration of the substances set out in paragraphs 4(1)(a) to (p) and,

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (i) in the case of effluent that is deposited into fresh water, recording the pH, hardness, alkalinity and electrical conductivity of the water samples,

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (ii) in the case of effluent that is deposited into estuarine waters, recording the pH, hardness, alkalinity, electrical conductivity and salinity of the water samples, and

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (iii) in the case of effluent that is deposited into marine waters, recording the salinity of the water samples;

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (d) recording the concentration of the deleterious substances prescribed in section 3 of these Regulations, but

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (i) not recording the concentrations of cyanide if that substance is not used as a process reagent within the operations area, and

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (ii) not recording the concentrations of radium 226 if the conditions of subsection 13(2) of these Regulations are met; and

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (e) implementing quality assurance and quality control measures that will ensure the accuracy of water quality monitoring data.

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (2) The water quality monitoring shall be conducted

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (a) four times per calendar year and at least one month apart on the samples of water collected, while the mine is depositing effluent, from the areas referred to in subparagraph (1)(a)(i); and

heading: Water Quality Monitoring
paragraph: (b) at the same time that the biological monitoring studies are conducted on samples of water collected in the areas referred to in subparagraph (1)(a)(ii).

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 8 The following information in relation to the effluent and water quality monitoring studies conducted during a calendar year under sections 4 to 7 shall be submitted to the Minister of the Environment not later than March 31 of the following year:

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) the dates on which samples were collected for effluent characterization, sublethal toxicity testing and water quality monitoring;

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) for each sample collected for effluent characterization, the location of the final discharge point from which samples were collected for effluent characterization;

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (c) the location of the final discharge point from which samples were collected for sublethal toxicity testing and the data used in selecting the final discharge point in accordance with subsection 5(3);

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (d) the latitude and longitude of sampling areas for water quality monitoring and a description that is sufficient to identify the location of the sampling areas;

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (e) the results of effluent characterization, sublethal toxicity testing and water quality monitoring;

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (f) the methodologies used to conduct effluent characterization and water quality monitoring, and the related method detection limits;

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (g) a description of the quality assurance and quality control measures that were implemented and the data related to the implementation of those measures; and

heading: Information Related to Effluent and Water Quality Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (h) with respect to every effluent sample collected at each final discharge point, the annual mean concentration of mercury and selenium.

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: 9 (1) Biological monitoring studies shall include

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (a) a study respecting fish population, if the highest concentration of effluent in the exposure area, during a period in which there are deposits, is greater than 1% at any location that is 250 m from a point at which the effluent enters the area from a final discharge point, unless the results of the previous two biological monitoring studies indicate

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (i) for all effect indicators with no assigned critical effect size, no effect on the fish population, and

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (ii) for all effect indicators with an assigned critical effect size, no effect on the fish population or an effect on the fish population the absolute value of the magnitude of which is less than the absolute value of its assigned critical effect size;

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (b) a study respecting the benthic invertebrate community, if the highest concentration of effluent in the exposure area, during a period in which there are deposits, is greater than 1% at any location that is 100 m from a point at which the effluent enters the area from a final discharge point, unless the results of the previous two biological monitoring studies indicate

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (i) for all effect indicators with no assigned critical effect size, no effect on the benthic invertebrate community, and

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (ii) for all effect indicators with an assigned critical effect size, no effect on the benthic invertebrate community or an effect on the benthic invertebrate community the absolute value of the magnitude of which is less than the absolute value of its assigned critical effect size;

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (c) a study respecting fish tissue mercury, if

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (i) effluent characterization reveals an annual mean concentration of total mercury in the effluent that is equal to or greater than 0.10 µg/L, based on a calendar year, unless the results of the previous two biological monitoring studies indicate no effect on fish tissue from mercury, or

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (ii) the method detection limit used in respect of mercury for the analysis of at least two of four effluent samples in a calendar year is equal to or greater than 0.10 µg/L;

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (d) a study respecting fish tissue selenium, if

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (i) effluent characterization reveals a concentration of total selenium in the effluent that is equal to or greater than 10 µg/L,

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (ii) effluent characterization reveals an annual mean concentration of total selenium in the effluent that is equal to or greater than 5 µg/L, based on a calendar year, or

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (iii) the method detection limit used in respect of selenium for the analysis of any effluent sample is equal to or greater than 10 µg/L, or the method detection limit used in respect of selenium for the analysis of at least two of four effluent samples in a calendar year is equal to or greater than 5 µg/L; and

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (e) if the cause of any effect on the fish population, on fish tissue from mercury or on the benthic invertebrate community is not known, a study that will be used to determine the cause of the effect if

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (i) the results of the previous two biological monitoring studies indicate a similar type of effect, and

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (ii) for an effect indicator with an assigned critical effect size, the absolute value of the magnitude of the effect is equal to or greater than the absolute value of its critical effect size in either of those studies.

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (2) If the results of the previous two biological monitoring studies are used to lift the requirement to conduct a study under any of paragraphs (1)(a), (b), (c) or (e), the earlier of those two studies shall not be used to lift a requirement to conduct a subsequent study.

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), the concentration of effluent shall be determined or the effluent characterization shall be carried out, as the case may be,

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (a) in the case of the first biological monitoring studies, beginning on the day on which the mine becomes subject to section 7 of these Regulations and ending on the day before the day on which the first study design is required to be submitted; and

heading: Required Studies
paragraph: (b) for any subsequent biological monitoring studies, beginning on the day on which the previous study design was required to be submitted and ending on the day before the day on which the subsequent study design is required to be submitted.

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 10 A first study design shall be submitted to the Minister of the Environment not later than 12 months after the day on which a mine becomes subject to section 7 of these Regulations. It shall contain

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) a site characterization that includes

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) a description of the manner in which the effluent mixes within each exposure area, during a period in which there are deposits, including an estimate of the concentration of effluent in the exposure area at 100 m and 250 m from every point at which the effluent enters the area from a final discharge point and - in respect of each calendar year - any supporting data, including raw data, for the estimate,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (ii) a description of the exposure and reference areas where the biological monitoring studies would be conducted - whether or not they are required - that includes information on the geological, hydrological, oceanographical, limnological, chemical and biological features of those areas,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (iii) the type of production process used by the mine and the environmental protection practices in place at the mine,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (iv) a description of any anthropogenic, natural or other factors that are not related to the effluent but that may reasonably be expected to affect the results of any biological monitoring study, whether or not it is required, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (v) any additional information that would enable a determination as to whether studies would be conducted in accordance with generally accepted standards of good scientific practice;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) a description of how any required study respecting fish population, fish tissue mercury and fish tissue selenium will be conducted that includes

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) a description of and the scientific rationale for

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (A) the fish species selected, taking into account the abundance of the species most exposed to effluent,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (B) the sampling areas selected within the exposure area and the reference area,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (C) the sampling period selected,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (D) the sample size selected, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (E) the field and laboratory methodologies selected, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (ii) an explanation as to how, in the case of the study respecting fish population or fish tissue mercury, the study will provide the information necessary to determine if the effluent has an effect on fish population or on fish tissue from mercury;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (c) a description of how any required study respecting the benthic invertebrate community will be conducted that includes

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) a description of and the scientific rationale for

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (A) the sampling areas selected, taking into account the benthic invertebrate diversity and the area most exposed to effluent,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (B) the sampling period selected,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (C) the sample size selected, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (D) the field and laboratory methodologies selected, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (ii) an explanation as to how the study will provide the information necessary to determine if the effluent has an effect on the benthic invertebrate community;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (d) the month in which the samples will be collected for each required biological monitoring study;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (e) a description of the quality assurance and quality control measures that will be implemented for each required biological monitoring study to ensure the validity of the data that is collected; and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (f) a summary of the results of any studies to determine whether the effluent was causing an effect on the fish population, fish tissue from mercury or the benthic invertebrate community and of any studies in the exposure and reference areas respecting fish tissue selenium completed before the mine becomes subject to section 7 of these Regulations and any scientific data to support the results.

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 11 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the first biological monitoring studies shall start not earlier than six months after the day on which the first study design is submitted under section 10, and shall be conducted in accordance with that study design.

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (2) If the owner or operator is unable to follow the study design due to circumstances beyond their control, the owner or operator shall inform the Minister of the Environment without delay of those circumstances and of the changes that are made to the study.

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 12 (1) A first interpretative report shall be submitted to the Minister of the Environment not later than 36 months after the day on which the mine becomes subject to section 7 of these Regulations. It shall contain

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) a description of any deviation from the study design that occurred while the biological monitoring studies were being conducted and any impact that the deviation had on the studies;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) the latitude and longitude of sampling areas and a description of the sampling areas sufficient to identify the location of the sampling areas;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (c) the dates and times when samples were collected;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (d) the sample sizes;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (e) the mean, median, standard deviation, standard error and minimum and maximum values in the sampling areas for

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) in the case of the study respecting fish population, effect indicators of growth, reproduction, condition and survival that include, if practicable, the length, total body weight and age of the fish, the weight of its liver or hepatopancreas and, if the fish are sexually mature, the egg weight, fecundity and gonad weight of the fish,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (ii) in the case of the study respecting the benthic invertebrate community, effect indicators of the total benthic invertebrate density, evenness index, taxa richness and, if the study is conducted in an area where it is possible to sample sediment, total organic carbon content of sediment and particle size distribution of sediment,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (iii) in the case of the study respecting fish tissue mercury, the effect indicator of the concentration of total mercury (wet weight) in the fish tissue, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (iv) in the case of the study respecting fish tissue selenium, the concentration - in the muscle or whole body and, if practicable, in the ovaries or eggs - of total selenium (dry weight) reported in µg/g and the percentage of the moisture content of the sample;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (f) in the case of the study respecting the benthic invertebrate community, a calculation of the similarity index effect indicator;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (g) an identification of the sex of the fish sampled and of the presence of any lesions, tumours, parasites or other abnormalities and, in the case of the study respecting fish tissue selenium, the type of fish tissue studied and the scientific rationale for the selection of that tissue;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (h) a determination as to whether there is a statistically significant difference between the sampling areas for the calculations under subparagraphs (e)(i) to (iii) and paragraph (f) taking into consideration the information identified under paragraph (g), with the statistical comparison made separately and independently for each effect indicator;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) a statistical analysis of the results of the calculations under subparagraphs (e)(i) to (iii) and paragraph (g) that indicates the probability of correctly detecting an effect of a pre-defined size and the degree of confidence that can be placed in the calculations;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (j) for an effect indicator referred to in paragraph (e) with an assigned critical effect size, a comparison of the magnitude of the effect - calculated in accordance with subsection (2) or (3), as the case may be - to its critical effect size;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (k) any supporting data, including raw data, for the information provided under paragraphs (e) to (j);

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (l) a description of any quality assurance or quality control measures that were implemented and the data related to the implementation of those measures;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (m) based on the information referred to in paragraphs (e) to (k), the identification of

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) any effect on the fish population,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (ii) any effect on the benthic invertebrate community, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (iii) any effect on fish tissue from mercury;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (n) for an effect indicator with an assigned critical effect size, a statement as to whether the absolute value of the magnitude of the effect is equal to or greater than the absolute value of its critical effect size;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (o) a summary of the results of effluent characterization, sublethal toxicity testing and water quality monitoring reported under paragraph 8(e) beginning on the day on which the mine becomes subject to section 7 of these Regulations;

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (p) the conclusions of the biological monitoring studies, and a description of how those conclusions will impact the study design for subsequent biological monitoring studies, taking into account

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) the results of any studies referred to in paragraph 10(f),

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (ii) the presence of anthropogenic, natural or other factors that are not related to the effluent under study and that may reasonably be expected to contribute to any observed effect,

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (iii) the results of the statistical analysis conducted under paragraphs (h) and (i), and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (iv) the data referred to in paragraph (l);

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (q) the month in which the next biological monitoring studies will start, if any biological monitoring studies are required; and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (r) the date when the next interpretative report is required to be submitted or would be required to be submitted but for the application of subsection 16(3).

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of the study respecting fish population, the magnitude of the effect for an effect indicator is to be calculated using the following formula:

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: where

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) for the purpose of the age indicator, the mean value for the indicator in the exposure area, and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of the indicators other than age, the adjusted mean value - obtained using the analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) statistical test method - for the indicator in the exposure area; and

heading: DiVISION 1First Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) for the purpose of the age indicator, the mean value for the indicator in the reference area, and

paragraph: 2 These Regulations do not apply to a prescription drug within the meaning of section A.01.010 of the Food and Drug Regulations.

paragraph: 4 No person contravenes subsection 3(1) if the toiletries are in transit through Canada, from a place outside Canada to another place outside Canada.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "abandoned mine" means a mine for which all permit obligations under this Act have been satisfied and in respect of which the mineral claims have reverted to the government;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agent" means a person having control of a mine on behalf of the owner;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorized person" means a qualified person appointed or designated by the manager to perform specified duties;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "chief auditor" means the person designated under section 2.1 as the chief auditor;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "chief inspector" means the person designated under section 3 as the Chief Inspector of Mines;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "chief permitting officer" means the person designated under section 8.2 as the chief permitting officer;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "closed mine" means a mine at which all mining activities have ceased but in respect of which the owner, agent, manager or permittee remains responsible for compliance with this Act, the regulations, the code and that person's obligations under the permit for that mine;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "code" means the health, safety and reclamation code established under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cultural heritage resource" means a cultural heritage resource as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "detrimental environmental impact" occurs when the quality of air, land or water substantially reduces the usefulness of the environment or its capacity to support life;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "inspector" means a person appointed by the chief inspector as an inspector of mines;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local union" means a union certified under the Labour Relations Code as the bargaining agent for employees or a unit of employees at a mine;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "management" means employees of a mine who act as supervisors;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "management co-chair" means the co-chair chosen for the occupational health and safety committee by the manager;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "manager" means the person appointed under section 21 to be responsible for the management and operation of a mine;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mine" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a place where mechanical disturbance of the ground or any excavation is made to explore for or to produce coal, mineral bearing substances, placer minerals, rock, limestone, earth, clay, sand or gravel,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) all cleared areas, machinery and equipment for use in servicing a mine or for use in connection with a mine and buildings other than bunkhouses, cook houses and related residential facilities,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) all activities including exploratory drilling, excavation, processing, concentrating, waste disposal and site reclamation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) closed and abandoned mines, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a place designated by the chief inspector as a mine;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mineral title" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a claim or lease as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a lease or licence as defined in the Coal Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "mining activity" means any activity related to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the exploration and development of a mineral, a placer mineral, coal, sand, gravel or rock, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the production of a mineral, a placer mineral, coal, sand, gravel or rock,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: and includes the reclamation of a mine;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "occupational health and safety committee" means the joint worker management committee established for each mine under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "official" means any of the following persons:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the chief auditor;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the chief inspector;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the chief permitting officer;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an inspector;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "owner" includes every person who is the immediate holder, proprietor, lessee, occupier or permittee of a mine or of any part of it, but does not include a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) receives only a royalty or rent from a mine that is subject to a lease, grant or other authority for its working, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is the owner of the surface rights of land in, on or under which a mine exists but who is not the immediate holder, proprietor, lessee, occupier or permittee;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permit" means a permit issued under section 10;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permittee" means the holder of a permit issued under section 10;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualified person" means a person who, in the opinion of the manager, is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) qualified because of the person's knowledge, training and experience to design, organize, supervise and perform the duties for which the person is appointed,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) familiar with the provisions of this Act, the code and the regulations that apply to the duties for which the person is appointed, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) capable of identifying any potential or actual danger to health or safety in the workplace;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "supervisor" means a person who instructs, directs or controls workers in the performance of their duties and who is authorized by the manager to take or recommend disciplinary action against workers;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "worker" means a person who is an employee but does not include a supervisor;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "worker co-chair" means the co-chair chosen for the occupational, health and safety committee by the workers;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "workplace" means a place where work is carried out in, on or about a mine.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2		  This Act applies to all mines during exploration, development, construction, production, closure, reclamation and abandonment.

heading: Chief auditor
paragraph:
2.1
		  (1) The minister must designate in writing a person appointed under the Public Service Act, as the chief auditor.

heading: Chief auditor
paragraph: (2) The minister may not designate any of the following persons as the chief auditor:

heading: Chief auditor
paragraph: (a) the chief inspector;

heading: Chief auditor
paragraph: (b) the chief permitting officer;

heading: Chief auditor
paragraph: (c) an inspector.

heading: Authority of chief auditor
paragraph: 2.2		  The chief auditor may conduct audits for the purpose of evaluating the effectiveness of any of the following:

heading: Authority of chief auditor
paragraph: (a) the regulatory framework for mining in British Columbia;

heading: Authority of chief auditor
paragraph: (b) policies, programs, practices and actions to fulfill the objectives of that framework.

heading: Audit plan
paragraph:
2.3
		  Each year, the chief auditor must

heading: Audit plan
paragraph: (a) develop an audit plan identifying the subject matter of the audits to be given priority in that year, and

heading: Audit plan
paragraph: (b) publish the audit plan on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the chief auditor.

heading: Chief auditor's authority to delegate
paragraph:
2.4
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the chief auditor may delegate in writing to any person a power or duty of the chief auditor under this Act.

heading: Chief auditor's authority to delegate
paragraph: (2) The chief auditor may not delegate a power or duty to any of the following persons:

heading: Chief auditor's authority to delegate
paragraph: (a) the chief inspector;

heading: Chief auditor's authority to delegate
paragraph: (b) the chief permitting officer;

heading: Chief auditor's authority to delegate
paragraph: (c) an inspector.

heading: Audits
paragraph:
2.5
		  (1) For the purpose of conducting an audit, the chief auditor may do any of the following:

heading: Audits
paragraph: (a) at any reasonable time, enter and inspect the following places:

heading: Audits
paragraph: (i)  land covered by a mineral title;

heading: Audits
paragraph: (ii)  a mine;

heading: Audits
paragraph: (b) inspect records or things;

heading: Audits
paragraph: (c) require a person to produce a record or thing in the person's possession or control.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (2) The chief auditor, on entering a place under subsection (1), may bring any persons and equipment that the chief auditor considers necessary for the purpose of the audit.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (3) If, in inspecting a place under subsection (1), the chief auditor identifies a hazard and is of the opinion that a delay in remedying the hazard would be dangerous to persons, property or the environment, the chief auditor may issue an order

heading: Audits
paragraph: (a) for immediate remedial action,

heading: Audits
paragraph: (b) to suspend the regular work until remedial action is taken, or

heading: Audits
paragraph: (c) to close the mine or part of it until remedial action is taken.

heading: Audits
paragraph: (4) As soon as practicable after issuing an order under subsection (3), the chief auditor must

heading: Audits
paragraph: (a) notify the chief inspector that the order was issued, and

heading: Audits
paragraph: (b) provide to the chief inspector any information requested by the chief inspector respecting the hazard or the order.

heading: Audit reports
paragraph:
2.6
		  (1) After completing an audit, the chief auditor must provide a report to the minister respecting the following:

heading: Audit reports
paragraph: (a) the conclusions reached by the chief auditor;

heading: Audit reports
paragraph: (b) the chief auditor's reasons for those conclusions;

heading: Audit reports
paragraph: (c) the chief auditor's recommendations, if any, arising from the audit.

heading: Audit reports
paragraph: (2) The chief auditor must publish, on a publicly accessible website maintained by or on behalf of the chief auditor, the reports provided to the minister under subsection (1).

heading: Chief inspector
paragraph:
3

heading: Authority of chief inspector
paragraph: 4		  The chief inspector has the rights and powers conferred on an inspector under this Act.

paragraph:
5

6

paragraph:
8.1
		  The failure or refusal of a person subject to an order under section 8 to do any of the following makes the person, on application to the Supreme Court by an inspector, liable to be committed for contempt as if in breach of an order or judgment of the Supreme Court:

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative person
paragraph: (a) attend before the inspector;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative person
paragraph: (b) take an oath or make an affirmation;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative person
paragraph: (c) answer questions;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative person
paragraph: (d) produce records or things in the person's possession or control.

paragraph:

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (a) the requirements respecting reclamation in the code or regulations;

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (b) the conditions of the permit, including the conditions respecting reclamation.

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (2) If the chief inspector issues an order under subsection (1) and the person to whom the order was issued has not complied with the order by the date specified in the order, the chief inspector may do one or more of the following:

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (a) order the owner, agent, manager or permittee to stop the mining operation;

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (b) enter on or below the surface of the mine and cause the required work to be performed or completed;

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (c) apply all or part of the security toward payment of the cost of the work required to be performed or completed;

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (d) close the mine;

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (e) cancel the permit.

heading: Chief inspector's authority on failure to comply with code, regulations or permit
paragraph: (3) Nothing in this section affects the powers or duties of an inspector under this Act.

heading: Permits - powers of minister
paragraph:
11
		  If the minister considers it to be necessary in the public interest, the minister, in respect of the issuing of permits, has and may exercise all the powers that the chief permitting officer may exercise under this Act.

heading: Acquisition of a mine
paragraph:
11.1
		  If a person acquires a mine, before the person engages in mining activity the person must apply to the chief permitting officer to

heading: Acquisition of a mine
paragraph: (a) obtain a permit, or

heading: Acquisition of a mine
paragraph: (b) amend an existing permit for the mine to identify the applicant as the holder of the permit.

heading: Mine reclamation fund
paragraph:
12
		  (1) In this section, "fund" means the mine reclamation fund.

heading: Mine reclamation fund
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, establish a fund to be known as the mine reclamation fund into which must be paid security, that is in the form of money, given by the owner, agent or manager of a mine under section 10.

heading: Mine reclamation fund
paragraph: (3) Money received from an owner, agent or a manager must be credited to a separate account in the fund in the name of the mine.

heading: Mine reclamation fund
paragraph: (4) The minister may requisition payments from an account in the fund

heading: Mine reclamation fund
paragraph: (a) to refund money and interest earned on it to the owner, agent or manager of a mine from time to time if in the opinion of the chief inspector it is no longer required for mine reclamation and protection of, and mitigation of damage to, land and watercourses affected by the mine, or

heading: Mine reclamation fund
paragraph: (b) to pay for the cost of work required under section 10.1 (2) (b).

heading: Variance of regulations or code for individual mine
paragraph:
13
		  (1) On receiving a written application from the manager, the occupational health and safety committee or the local union requesting the suspension or variance of a provision of the regulations or of the code, the chief inspector may suspend or vary the provision if the chief inspector is of the opinion that the provision does not operate in the best interest of, or is not necessary to, health and safety in an individual mine.

heading: Variance of regulations or code for individual mine
paragraph: (2) The chief inspector must ensure that the parties affected by the application are advised of the application for, and the subsequent decision respecting, a variance.

heading: Variance of regulations or code for individual mine
paragraph: (3) The chief inspector must maintain a register of all variances.

heading: Variance of regulations or code for individual mine
paragraph: (4) At least once every 5 years, the chief inspector

heading: Variance of regulations or code for individual mine
paragraph: (a) must review each variance and advise the manager, occupational health and safety committee and local union that the chief inspector intends to review the variance, and

heading: Variance of regulations or code for individual mine
paragraph: (b) after reviewing any submissions, must advise them whether or not the variance is to continue.

heading: Discrimination
paragraph:
14
		  (1) Each manager must ensure that no employee is discriminated against in any manner, including adversely affecting any term or condition of employment, for complying with this Act, the regulations or the code.

heading: Discrimination
paragraph: (2) If advised in writing of an alleged case of discrimination against an employee for complying with this Act, the regulations or the code or refusing to work because it would result in a contravention of this Act, the regulations or the code, the chief inspector must investigate and report the findings to the manager and occupational health and safety committee, and the local union, if any.

heading: Discrimination
paragraph: (3) If the chief inspector is satisfied that the allegation is true, the chief inspector may make one or more orders requiring the employer to do one or more of the following:

heading: Discrimination
paragraph: (a) cease the discrimination;

heading: Discrimination
paragraph: (b) hire or reinstate the employee;

heading: Discrimination
paragraph: (c) pay the employee any wages lost by reason of the discrimination;

heading: Discrimination
paragraph: (d) pay the employee reasonable and actual out of pocket expenses incurred by the employee by reason of the discrimination.

heading: Inspections
paragraph:
15
		  (1) For the purposes of administering or enforcing this Act, the regulations, the code, a permit or an order issued under this Act, an inspector may do any of the following:

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) at any reasonable time, enter and inspect the following places:

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (i)  a mine;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (ii)  a site at which the inspector considers mining activity to be taking place, including mining activity not authorized by a permit;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) inspect records or things at a place referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) require a person at a place referred to in paragraph (a) to produce a record or thing in the person's possession or control.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (1.1) An inspector who enters a place under subsection (1) may bring any persons and equipment that the inspector considers necessary for the purpose of the inspection.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (2) If an inspector is making a health and safety inspection, on arrival at the mine the inspector must request the manager to arrange for the worker co-chair or designate and the management co-chair or designate each to appoint a representative to accompany the inspector on the inspection.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), an inspector may perform the inspection without either or both management and worker representatives, if on completion of the inspection the inspector meets with or otherwise communicates with each co-chair or each designate of a co-chair to discuss the inspector's findings and their occupational, health and safety concerns, if any.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (4) An inspector must complete an inspection report within 7 business days of completing the inspection and promptly provide the manager, and, in the case of a health and safety inspection, the occupational health and safety committee and local union with a copy of the inspection report on its completion, and the report must

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) list the workplaces inspected,

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) note any contraventions of an order under this section,

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) note any contraventions of the Act, the regulations, the code or a permit, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (d) order remedial action, specify the results to be obtained by the remedial action and specify time limits for compliance with the order or any provision of the Act, the regulations, the code or a permit.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (4.1) If an inspector believes on reasonable grounds that a person has contravened or is contravening an order under this section or a provision of the Act, the code, the regulations or a permit and that the contravention has a detrimental environmental impact, the inspector may order the owner, agent, manager, permittee or any other person apparently in charge in, on or about a mine to do any of the following:

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) take immediate remedial action;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) suspend regular work until remedial action is taken;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) close the mine or part of it until remedial action is taken.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (4.2) An order under this section may be made against an owner, agent, manager, permittee, contractor or other person who carries out mining activity without a permit.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (5) If an inspector is of the opinion that a delay in remedying a hazard would be dangerous to persons, property or the environment, the inspector must issue an order

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) for immediate remedial action,

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) to suspend regular work until remedial action is taken, or

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) to close the mine or part of it until remedial action is taken.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (6) Within 15 business days after receiving the inspection report, the manager must

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) submit a written report outlining the remedial steps taken and the work still outstanding, and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) promptly provide a copy to the inspector, and, in the case of health and safety matters, the occupational health and safety committee and the local union.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (7) The owner, agent, manager, permittee, and all persons in, on or about a mine must provide an inspector with all assistance necessary for the completion of an inspection or investigation.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (8) For the purposes of subsections (4) and (6), a business day is a day other than Saturday or a holiday.

heading: Order not to interfere with public works, etc.
paragraph:
16
		  An inspector may order the operation of a mine to be conducted in a manner that will not interfere with a public work, public service, public utility, highway or railway, or with a pipeline as defined in section 1 (2) of the Energy Resource Activities Act or an adjacent mine property.

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: 17		  (1) The chief inspector may take an action described in subsection (1.1) if the chief inspector considers that any of the following applies:

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (a) there is an emergency at a mine;

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (b) work may be necessary in, on or about a closed or abandoned mine in order to prevent danger to persons or property or to abate pollution of the land and watercourses affected by the mine.

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (1.1) For the purpose of subsection (1), the chief inspector may do either or both of the following:

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (a) issue an order restricting or prohibiting a person from carrying out an action referred to in the order;

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (b) enter on or below the surface of the mine and cause work to be done to remove or alleviate the danger or remedy the pollution.

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (2) The costs incurred for work done under this section must be paid from the consolidated revenue fund without an appropriation other than this subsection.

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (3) The amount expended plus interest at a prescribed rate is a debt due to the government and forms a lien and charge on the mine or mineral title in favour of the government.

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (4) Notice of the debt in the prescribed form may be registered as a charge in the land title office or in the office of the chief gold commissioner, and no transfer of title or other dealing with the mine may take place until the debt is paid and the notice cancelled.

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (5) With or without payment and on conditions the minister may impose, the minister may cancel the notice registered under subsection (4) and, on that happening, the mine may be transferred or otherwise dealt with.

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (6) For the purpose of recovering the costs referred to in subsection (2), the chief inspector may do one or more of the following:

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (a) order the owner, agent, manager or permittee to pay the costs;

heading: Chief inspector's authority to cause work to be done
paragraph: (b) realize all or part of the security provided under section 10 and order the owner, agent, manager or permittee to replace, by the time specified in the order, the security realized under this paragraph.

heading: Engineering report
paragraph:
18
		  An inspector may order the owner, agent or manager to provide at the owner's expense an independent study prepared by an engineer or other licensed professional acceptable to the inspector

heading: Engineering report
paragraph: (a) respecting health and safety at the mine or safety of its equipment, buildings, workings or structures,

heading: Engineering report
paragraph: (a.1) respecting actual or potential environmental damage resulting from mining activity at the mine, or

heading: Engineering report
paragraph: (b) in connection with an incident that the inspector is investigating.

heading: Appointment of manager
paragraph:
21
		  An owner or agent must,

heading: Appointment of manager
paragraph: (a) before work begins, appoint a manager and ensure that there is a person acting in that capacity at all times,

heading: Appointment of manager
paragraph: (b) immediately after each appointment, notify the inspector in writing, of the name of the manager, and

heading: Appointment of manager
paragraph: (c) provide the manager or the manager's designate with every facility for conducting the operation of the mine in accordance with the requirements of this Act, the regulations and the code.

heading: Manager's qualifications and responsibility
paragraph:
22
		  (1) Each manager and designate must possess qualifications established by the regulations or the code.

heading: Manager's qualifications and responsibility
paragraph: (2) The manager or designate must attend daily at an operating mine.

heading: Manager's absence
paragraph:
23
		  Each manager must designate in writing a qualified person to be responsible during the manager's absence to ensure compliance with this Act, the regulations, the code and the permit.

heading: Compliance
paragraph:
24
		  (1) An owner, agent, manager or permittee must take all reasonable measures to ensure compliance with the following:

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (a) this Act, the regulations and the code;

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (b) the permit issued for the mine;

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (c) an order issued under this Act in relation to the mine.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (2) A person who performs or supervises work in, on or about a mine must take all reasonable measures to ensure compliance with the requirements applicable to the person's work or supervision under the following:

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (a) this Act, the regulations and the code;

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (b) the permit issued for the mine;

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (c) an order issued under this Act in relation to the mine.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1), the owner, agent, manager or permittee must carry out reclamation in accordance with the regulations, the code, the permit for the mine, and the orders issued under this Act in relation to the mine.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (4) This section applies whether or not any of the following applies in relation to the mine:

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (a) security has been provided under section 10 (5);

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (b) the chief inspector has exercised a power under section 10.1;

heading: Compliance
paragraph: (c) the chief inspector has caused work to be done under section 17.

heading: Contractors
paragraph:
25
		  (1) If work in or about a mine is let to a contractor, the contractor and the contractor's manager, as well as the owner, agent and manager of the mine, must take all reasonable measures to ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act, the regulations, the code, the permit and orders under this Act pertaining to the work over which they have control.

heading: Contractors
paragraph: (2) In a case of noncompliance with subsection (1), the contractor and the contractor's manager commit an offence that is punishable in the same manner as if the contractor and contractor's manager were the owner, agent or manager of the mine.

heading: Supervision required
paragraph:
26
		  Each manager must ensure that every person employed at a mine, if required by the regulations or the code, is under the daily supervision of a person who holds a valid and appropriate certificate as required by the regulations or the code.

heading: Mine plans
paragraph:
27
		  Each manager must keep in the office at the mine site accurate plans that

heading: Mine plans
paragraph: (a) are updated every 3 months,

heading: Mine plans
paragraph: (b) are prepared on a scale that accords with good engineering practice, and

heading: Mine plans
paragraph: (c) contain particulars established by the regulations or the code.

heading: Alternative employment
paragraph:
29
		  If an inspector makes an order under section 15 (5) (b) or (c), and the manager is unable to provide alternate employment, the manager must pay or cause to be paid to each worker the amount that the worker would have earned or been likely to earn for each day the closure continues, up to a maximum of 3 working days.

heading: Posting of reports and orders
paragraph:
30
		  (1) Each manager must post in a conspicuous place at the mine all inspection reports and orders issued by an inspector and must maintain them there for 30 days.

heading: Posting of reports and orders
paragraph: (2) Each manager must ensure that all documents required to be posted are maintained in a legible condition.

heading: Occupational health and safety committee
paragraph:
32
		  (1) Each manager must ensure that an occupational health and safety committee is established in accordance with the regulations or the code.

heading: Occupational health and safety committee
paragraph: (2) A manager must allow committee members to participate in inspections, investigations and meetings of the committee under this Act, and that participation must be considered as time worked.

heading: Appeal to chief inspector
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A person who is adversely affected by a decision or order of an inspector or an order of the chief auditor may, within 30 days of its issue, appeal the decision or order to the chief inspector.

heading: Appeal to chief inspector
paragraph: (2) The manager, occupational health and safety committee and local union must be given an opportunity to make a submission on the matter of the appeal, receive copies of all submissions and be notified of the chief inspector's decision on the appeal.

heading: Appeal to chief inspector
paragraph: (3) An appeal taken under this section does not operate as a stay or suspend the operation of the decision being appealed unless the chief inspector orders otherwise.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph:
34
		  (1) The minister must establish a health, safety and reclamation code committee consisting of the members the minister appoints.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (2) The chief inspector is a member and the chair.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (3) The committee must prepare a code dealing with all aspects of health, safety and reclamation in the operation of a mine and may amend the code from time to time as required.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (4) A provision of the code may specify that the approval or consent of an inspector or some other person is required before a specified action may be taken.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (5) Without limiting subsection (4), the code may require approval or consent before a specified type of equipment is used at a mine or continues to be used in specified circumstances.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (6) The code and any amendments to it come into force on approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (7) If there is a conflict between a provision of the code and a provision of the regulations, the regulations apply.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (8) Where there is a conflict between a provision of the code and a provision of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, the code applies.

heading: Health, safety and reclamation code committee
paragraph: (9)           Subsection (8) does not apply to personal information, as defined in the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, that has been in existence for 100 or more years or to other information that has been in existence for 50 or more years.

heading: Enforcement of Act, regulations, code, permit or order
paragraph: 35		  (1) If an inspector finds that a mine is not being operated in accordance with an order under section 15 or a provision of the Act, the regulations, the code or a permit, the inspector may order the owner, agent, manager, permittee or person apparently in charge in, on or about a mine to comply with the order or provision.

heading: Enforcement of Act, regulations, code, permit or order
paragraph: (2) If a person fails or refuses to comply with an order of an inspector under subsection (1) of this section or under section 15, the inspector may apply to the Supreme Court for an order directing the person to comply.

heading: Annual report
paragraph:
36
		  The chief inspector must publish an annual report showing results during the previous year in achieving the purposes of this Act.

heading: Contraventions
paragraph:
36.1
		  (1) After giving a person an opportunity to be heard, the chief inspector may find on a balance of probabilities that the person has contravened or failed to comply with any of the following provisions:

heading: Contraventions
paragraph: (a) a prescribed provision of this Act, the regulations or the code;

heading: Contraventions
paragraph: (b) a provision of an order made under this Act;

heading: Contraventions
paragraph: (c) a term or condition imposed under section 10 (1.1), (2), (2.01), (3), (4) or (7), 17 (5) or 38 (4) of this Act.

heading: Contraventions
paragraph: (2) If a corporation contravenes or fails to comply with a provision referred to in subsection (1), a director, officer or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure also contravenes or fails to comply with the provision and is also liable to an administrative penalty under section 36.2.

heading: Contraventions
paragraph: (3) If an employee, contractor or agent of a corporation contravenes or fails to comply with a provision referred to in subsection (1) in the course of carrying out the employment, contract or agency, the corporation also contravenes or fails to comply with the provision and is also liable to an administrative penalty under section 36.2.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
36.2
		  (1) If the chief inspector finds that a person has contravened or failed to comply with a provision referred to in section 36.1 (1), the chief inspector may, after considering the prescribed matters, impose an administrative penalty on the person in an amount that does not exceed the prescribed limit.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) A person may be prosecuted under this Act for a contravention or failure in relation to which an administrative penalty has been imposed.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) In imposing a sentence for an offence under this Act, the court may consider an administrative penalty imposed in relation to the same matter.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, an administrative penalty may not be imposed on the person in respect of the same circumstances that gave rise to the conviction.

heading: Notice of contravention or penalty
paragraph:
36.3
		  If the chief inspector finds that a person has contravened or failed to comply with a provision referred to in section 36.1 (1) or if the chief inspector imposes an administrative penalty on the person under section 36.2 (1), the chief inspector

heading: Notice of contravention or penalty
paragraph: (a) must give to the person a notice of the decision, and the notice must

heading: Notice of contravention or penalty
paragraph: (i)  identify the contravention,

heading: Notice of contravention or penalty
paragraph: (ii)  advise the person of the person's right to appeal the decision under section 36.7, and

heading: Notice of contravention or penalty
paragraph: (iii)  if an administrative penalty is being imposed, specify the amount of the penalty and the date by which the penalty must be paid, and

heading: Notice of contravention or penalty
paragraph: (b) may make public the reasons for the decision and the amount of the penalty, if any.

heading: Due date of penalty
paragraph:
36.4
		  A person on whom an administrative penalty is imposed under section 36.2 must pay the penalty within 40 days after the later of the following dates, as applicable:

heading: Due date of penalty
paragraph: (a) the date on which the notice referred to in section 36.3 is given to the person;

heading: Due date of penalty
paragraph: (b) if the person commences an appeal under section 36.7, the date on which the notice referred to in section 36.7 (4) (b) is given to the person.

heading: Enforcement of administrative penalty
paragraph:
36.5
		  (1) An administrative penalty constitutes a debt payable to the government by the person on whom the penalty is imposed.

heading: Enforcement of administrative penalty
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required under section 36.4, the government may file with the Supreme Court or Provincial Court a certified copy of the notice imposing the penalty and, on being filed, the notice has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on the notice, as if the notice were a judgment of that court.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph:
36.6
		  (1) The time limit for giving a notice under section 36.3 is 3 years after the date on which the act or omission alleged to constitute the contravention or failure to comply first came to the attention of the chief inspector.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the chief inspector and certifying the date referred to in subsection (1) is proof of that date.

heading: Appeal
paragraph:
36.7
		  (1) In this section, "appeal tribunal" means a tribunal identified by regulation for the purposes of this section.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (2) A person to whom a notice has been given under section 36.3 may appeal to the appeal tribunal a decision that is the subject of the notice.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (3) The time limit for a person to commence an appeal is 30 days after the date on which the notice under section 36.3 is given to the person.

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (4) On an appeal under subsection (2), the appeal tribunal

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (a) may confirm, vary or rescind the decision that is the subject of the notice, and

heading: Appeal
paragraph: (b) must notify the person of the decision made under paragraph (a) of this subsection.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph:
37
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person obstructs, impedes or otherwise interferes with, or knowingly provides false or misleading information or records to, an official while the official is exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (a) a provision of this Act, the regulations or the code;

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (b) a condition of a permit;

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (c) an order made under this Act.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (3) A person who commits an offence is liable to a fine of not more than $1 000 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 3 years or both.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (3.1) The time limit for laying an information to commence a prosecution for an offence under this Act is 5 years after the date on which the chief inspector learned of the facts on which the information is based.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (3.2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the chief inspector certifying the date referred to in subsection (3.1) is proof of that date.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (4) If an inspector serves a written notice on a person alleging a contravention of this Act, the regulations or the code, or an order under any of them, that person, on conviction, is liable to a penalty, in addition to the penalties provided under subsection (3), of not more than $5 000 and not less than $500 for every day during which the offence continues to be committed after receipt of the notice.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (5) If a corporation commits an offence, a director or officer of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence is, even if the corporation is convicted, liable to the penalty set out in subsection (3).

heading: Section 5 of Offence Act does not apply
paragraph:
37.1
		  Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: 38		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) governing exploration, development, operation, closure and abandonment of mines and mining property;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a.1) respecting applications for, and the issuance of, permits and approvals, including but not limited to prescribing time limits within which specified steps in the application process must be taken;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a.2) for the purposes of section 10 (1.1) and (2.01);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the type, application, use and operation of equipment, machinery and other property in, on or about mines, whether moveable or immovable or whether used in mining operations or not;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) relating directly or indirectly to the health and safety of all persons, including the public, in, on or about mines, either underground or on the surface;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting standards for environmental protection and reclamation;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting the conservation of cultural heritage resources;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (f) requiring management to give members of the occupational health and safety committee access to relevant records;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (g) requiring management to give access to the mine and to its records for the purposes of investigation of death or injury, accidents or dangerous or unusual occurrences;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (h) requiring management to forbid a person to enter or engage in work if the person is impaired or has drugs or liquor in the person's possession;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i) requiring management to forbid persons to engage in horseplay;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (l) prescribing fees and charges that must be paid in respect of any matter for which a service is provided or a duty performed under this Act and prescribing the time and manner of payment of the fees and charges;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (m) prescribing provisions for the purposes of section 36.1 (1) (a);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (n) prescribing matters and limits for the purposes of section 36.2 (1);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (o) authorizing administrative penalties to be imposed on a daily basis for continuing contraventions or failures;

heading: Power to make regulations
