paragraph: (p) prescribing the consequences of failing to pay an administrative penalty, which consequences may include, but are not limited to, imposing additional penalties;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (q) for the purposes of section 36.7, identifying a tribunal and specifying the provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act that apply to the tribunal for the purposes of hearing appeals under this Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) A regulation under subsections (1) or (2) may

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) make different provisions for different mines or for different classes or types of mines,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) adopt all or part of a code or standard published by a national or international standards association, as amended from time to time,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) specify that the approval or consent of an inspector or some other person is required before a specified action may be taken, and, without limiting this section, may require approval or consent before a specified type of equipment is used at a mine or continues to be used in specified circumstances,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) delegate to inspectors the power, by order, to vary codes, standards and other prescribed matters in the interests of health and safety in individual mines, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (e) limit, restrict or prohibit, for a prescribed period of time, exploration or mining of uranium, if the uranium is more than a prescribed amount or proportion, within any or all mines, and to close, in the interest of health or safety, any mining operation in which more uranium than the prescribed amount or proportion is found.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (4) If a regulation is made that results in a limitation, restriction or prohibition on exploration or development or results in the closure of a mining operation, the chief inspector may, on conditions ordered by the chief inspector, consent to

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) the recommencement of exploration or development, or

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) the opening of a mining operation that has been closed under that regulation.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in this Order.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Canadian Navigable Waters Act. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aerial cables means cables that are in the air and includes the towers and poles from which they are suspended. (cables aeriens)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: charted navigable water means a navigable water for which nautical charts are produced by the Canadian Hydrographic Service or the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the United States. (eaux navigables cartographiees)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: erosion-protection work means any stones, rocks, concrete, logs or other common building materials or living plants placed to protect the bank of a navigable water from erosion. (ouvrages de protection contre l'erosion)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: navigation channel means a channel represented on a nautical chart produced by the Canadian Hydrographic Service or the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the United States or a channel for which markers have been placed by a federal, provincial or municipal government or by a port authority, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Marine Act. (chenal de navigation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: navigation route means a channel, other than a navigation channel, formed by the connection of the deep sections of a navigable water that, based on local knowledge, is predominantly used by vessels for navigation purposes. (voie de navigation)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) In this Order, submarine cables includes concrete blocks, concrete mattresses and any other objects attached to, laid on or placed under submarine cables to hold them in place or to protect them from being damaged.

heading: Measurements - length or width of minor work
paragraph: 2 (1) Unless otherwise indicated, any length or width of a minor work referred to in this Order is measured from the ordinary high water mark at the site where the minor work is situated.

heading: Measurements - width of navigable water
paragraph: (2) Unless otherwise indicated, any width of a navigable water referred to in this Order is measured from the ordinary high water mark on one side of the navigable water to the ordinary high water mark on the other side of the navigable water at the site where the minor work is situated.

heading: Measurements - depth or height
paragraph: (3) Unless otherwise indicated, any depth or height referred to in this Order is measured from the ordinary high water level at the site where the minor work is situated.

heading: Application
paragraph: 3 (1) Subsections (2) and (3) apply to the following minor works:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) erosion-protection works referred to in subsection 12(1);

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) aerial cables referred to in subsection 16(1);

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) submarine cables referred to in section 17;

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) buried pipelines referred to in section 19;

heading: Application
paragraph: (e) outfalls and water intakes referred to in section 26;

heading: Application
paragraph: (f) dredging referred to in section 28; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (g) watercourse crossings referred to in section 34.

heading: Deposit of information
paragraph: (2) Before beginning the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning of a minor work, the owner must deposit information in the registry established under section 27.2 of the Act describing the proposed activity and the minor work's location.

heading: Publication of notice
paragraph: (3) Before beginning the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning of a minor work, the owner must publish a notice in accordance with the requirements set out on the Internet site maintained by the Government of Canada entitled Navigation Protection Program External Submission Site under the heading "Create a Notification of a Minor Work", as amended from time to time, unless the proposed minor work has gone through a federal or provincial review process.

heading: Prior notification of Canadian Coast Guard
paragraph: 4 At least 48 hours before beginning the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning of a minor work in, on, over, under, through or across a charted navigable water, the owner of the minor work must, in writing, notify a Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services Centre of the day on which the activity is expected to begin.

heading: Buoys
paragraph: 5 A buoy referred to in this Order must meet the following criteria:

heading: Buoys
paragraph: (a) the part of the buoy that shows above the surface of the water is at least 15.25 cm wide and at least 30.5 cm high;

heading: Buoys
paragraph: (b) the buoy, including its anchor, remains in position after it has been anchored; and

heading: Buoys
paragraph: (c) the buoy complies with the requirements set out in the section entitled "Floating Aids to Navigation (Buoys)" of TP 968, entitled Canadian Aids to Navigation System and published by the Canadian Coast Guard, as amended from time to time.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 6 During the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of a minor work, the owner of the minor work must ensure

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) that vessels can navigate safely through or around the work site or, if navigation is interrupted by any activity related to the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of the minor work, that a suitable means, such as a portage, exists to allow vessels to resume navigation upstream and downstream of the work site;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) that the perimeter of the work site is visible from sunset to sunrise and during periods of restricted visibility by the placement of

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) yellow flashing lights,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) cautionary buoys with retro-reflective material, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (iii) cautionary buoys with yellow flashing lights; and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (c) that any cable or pipe that is in, on, over, through or across the navigable water is not left unattended unless

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) the cable or pipe is lying on the bed of the navigable water, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) the cable meets the requirements referred to in paragraph 16(1)(e).

heading: Application
paragraph: 7 (1) Subsection (2) applies to the following minor works:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) erosion-protection works referred to in subsection 12(1);

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) aerial cables referred to in subsection 16(1);

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) buried pipelines referred to in section 19; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) watercourse crossings referred to in section 34.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (2) During the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of a minor work, the owner of the minor work must ensure that navigators are notified of the work site both upstream and downstream of the work site by one of the following means:

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) signs stating "Construction Ahead" and "Travaux de construction", legible from a distance of at least 50 m;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) a vessel tasked with notifying navigators; or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (c) cautionary buoys.

heading: Notification on completion
paragraph: 8 On completion of the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal or decommissioning of a minor work in, on, over, under, through or across a charted navigable water, the owner of the minor work must, in writing, notify:

heading: Notification on completion
paragraph: (a) a Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services Centre; and

heading: Notification on completion
paragraph: (b) the Canadian Hydrographic Service.

heading: Designation - temporary works
paragraph: 9 A work that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - temporary works
paragraph: (a) the work is installed exclusively for the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of another minor work;

heading: Designation - temporary works
paragraph: (b) the work is not situated in, on, over, under, through or across a navigation channel or, if there is no navigation channel, a navigation route; and

heading: Designation - temporary works
paragraph: (c) the work does not occupy more than one-third of the width of the navigable water.

heading: Removal
paragraph: 10 The owner of a work that is designated as a minor work under section 9 must ensure that it is removed on completion of the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of the minor work for which it was installed.

heading: Bed contours of navigable water
paragraph: 11 If the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of a work that is designated, or intended to be designated, as a minor work under section 9 disturbs the bed contours of a navigable water to the point of interfering or likely to interfere with navigation, the owner of the work must ensure, on completion of the removal of the work, that the bed contours of the navigable water do not and are not likely to interfere with navigation.

heading: Designation - erosion-protection works
paragraph: 12 (1) An erosion-protection work that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - erosion-protection works
paragraph: (a) the erosion-protection work is integrated with and follows the bank of the navigable water;

heading: Designation - erosion-protection works
paragraph: (b) if the submerged part of the erosion-protection work extends horizontally into the navigable water further than the non-submerged part of the erosion-protection work, the submerged part is integrated with and follows the slope of the bed of the navigable water;

heading: Designation - erosion-protection works
paragraph: (c) the erosion-protection work does not extend horizontally more than 5 m into the navigable water;

heading: Designation - erosion-protection works
paragraph: (d) the erosion-protection work does not occupy more than one-third of the width of the navigable water;

heading: Designation - erosion-protection works
paragraph: (e) the erosion-protection work is not associated with an existing or proposed work, unless the existing or proposed work is a minor work; and

heading: Designation - erosion-protection works
paragraph: (f) the erosion-protection work does not include groynes or other structures to deflect the current.

heading: Definition of groyne
paragraph: (2) In this section, groyne means a structure built out from the bank of a navigable water in a direction transverse to the current in order to prevent erosion of the bank.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 13 The following definitions apply in section 14.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: dock includes a wharf, a pier and a jetty. (quai)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: similar means used for the same purpose - commercial or recreational - and under the same type of ownership - public or private. (similaire)

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: 14 A dock or boathouse that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (a) the dock or boathouse is situated 5 m or more from the adjacent property boundaries and property line extensions;

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (b) the dock or boathouse is situated more than 10 m from any work that is situated in, on, over, through or across the navigable water and is not owned by the owner of the dock or boathouse;

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (c) the dock or boathouse is situated 30 m or more from a navigation channel or, if there is no navigation channel, is not situated in, on, over, through or across a navigation route;

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (d) the dock or boathouse does not extend horizontally into, onto, over, through or across the navigable water

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (i) more than the length of a similar dock or boathouse situated 100 m or less, on the same bank, from the dock or boathouse, to a maximum length of 50 m, or

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (ii) more than 30 m, in any other case;

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (e) the dock or boathouse does not occupy more than one-third of the width of the navigable water;

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (f) the dock or boathouse is not associated with an existing or proposed work, unless the existing or proposed work is a minor work; and

heading: Designation - docks and boathouses
paragraph: (g) the dock or boathouse is not used for float planes or other aircraft equipped with floats.

heading: Designation - slipways and boat-launching ramps
paragraph: 15 A slipway or boat-launching ramp that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - slipways and boat-launching ramps
paragraph: (a) the slipway or boat-launching ramp does not include a marine railway;

heading: Designation - slipways and boat-launching ramps
paragraph: (b) the slipway or boat-launching ramp is situated 5 m or more from the adjacent property boundaries and property line extensions;

heading: Designation - slipways and boat-launching ramps
paragraph: (c) the portion of the slipway or boat-launching ramp that is situated below the ordinary high water mark lies on the bed of the navigable water; and

heading: Designation - slipways and boat-launching ramps
paragraph: (d) the slipway or boat-launching ramp is not associated with an existing or proposed work, unless the existing or proposed work is a minor work.

heading: Designation - aerial cables
paragraph: 16 (1) An aerial cable that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - aerial cables
paragraph: (a) the cable is used exclusively for power or telecommunication purposes;

heading: Designation - aerial cables
paragraph: (b) the cable is not over or across a charted navigable water or a navigation channel;

heading: Designation - aerial cables
paragraph: (c) the cable is not over or across a Canadian heritage river or a river, harbour or historic canal, as defined in section 2 of the Historic Canals Regulations, that is maintained by the Government of Canada;

heading: Designation - aerial cables
paragraph: (d) the towers and poles are not in the area between the ordinary high water marks on each side of the navigable water; and

heading: Designation - aerial cables
paragraph: (e) the cable meets the requirements of section 5.3.3 of Overhead Systems, CAN/CSA C22.3 No. 1, as amended from time to time.

heading: Amendments to the standard
paragraph: (2) Amendments to one language version of the standard referred to in paragraph (1)(e) are not incorporated by reference until the corresponding amendments are published in the other language version.

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: 17 A submarine cable that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (a) the submarine cable is used exclusively for power or telecommunication purposes;

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (b) the submarine cable lies on or is buried under the bed of the navigable water;

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (c) the submarine cable does not extend vertically above the bed of the navigable water more than

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (i) if the navigable water is less than 15 m in depth, 5% of the depth of the water, or

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (ii) in any other case, 1 m;

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (d) the submarine cable is not situated at or under the entrance to any port, including a marina;

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (e) the submarine cable is not in an area where routine dredging occurs; and

heading: Designation - submarine cables
paragraph: (f) the submarine cable is not in an area that is identified as an anchorage area on a nautical chart produced by the Canadian Hydrographic Service or the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the United States.

heading: Re-lay, rebury or remove cables
paragraph: 18 If a submarine cable that was designated as a minor work under section 17 is no longer lying on or buried under the bed of the navigable water, the owner of the submarine cable must, as soon as feasible, re-lay the cable on the bed of the navigable water, rebury the cable under the bed of the navigable water or remove the cable.

heading: Designation - buried pipelines
paragraph: 19 A pipeline that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - buried pipelines
paragraph: (a) the pipeline is buried under the bed of the navigable water;

heading: Designation - buried pipelines
paragraph: (b) the pipeline is not in an area where routine dredging occurs; and

heading: Designation - buried pipelines
paragraph: (c) the pipeline is not in an area that is identified as an anchorage area on a nautical chart produced by the Canadian Hydrographic Service or the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the United States.

heading: Requirement - water with width of more than 50 m
paragraph: 20 During the construction or placement of a pipeline that is intended to be designated as a minor work under section 19 in navigable water the width of which is more than 50 m at the location of the burial, the owner of the pipeline must ensure that the pipeline is buried using the horizontal directional drilling method.

heading: Horizontal directional drilling method with guiding cables
paragraph: 21 If the owner of a pipeline that is intended to be designated as a minor work under section 19 buries the pipeline using the horizontal directional drilling method with guiding cables placed in the navigable water, the owner must ensure that

heading: Horizontal directional drilling method with guiding cables
paragraph: (a) no equipment is placed in the navigable water, except the guiding cables and equipment required to use those cables; and

heading: Horizontal directional drilling method with guiding cables
paragraph: (b) the guiding cables and equipment required to use those cables do not extend vertically above the bed of the navigable water more than

heading: Horizontal directional drilling method with guiding cables
paragraph: (i) if the navigable water is less than 15 m in depth, 5% of the depth of the water, or

heading: Horizontal directional drilling method with guiding cables
paragraph: (ii) in any other case, 1 m.

heading: Bed contours of navigable water
paragraph: 22 If the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of a pipeline that is designated, or intended to be designated, as a minor work under section 19 disturbs the bed contours of a navigable water to the point of interfering or likely to interfere with navigation, the owner of the pipeline must ensure, on completion of the activity, that the bed contours of the navigable water do not and are not likely to interfere with navigation.

heading: Rebury or remove pipelines
paragraph: 23 If a pipeline that was designated as a minor work under section 19 is no longer buried under the bed of the navigable water, the owner of the pipeline must, as soon as feasible, rebury the pipeline under the bed of the navigable water or remove the pipeline.

heading: Designation - pipelines and certain cables
paragraph: 24 A pipeline or a cable used exclusively for power or telecommunication purposes that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - pipelines and certain cables
paragraph: (a) the pipeline or cable is attached to an existing work that was approved, validly constructed or placed under the Act; and

heading: Designation - pipelines and certain cables
paragraph: (b) the pipeline or cable does not increase the interference with navigation caused by the existing work.

heading: Designation - certain works
paragraph: 25 A work that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - certain works
paragraph: (a) the work is within an area bounded by a boom that was approved, validly constructed or placed under the Act upstream or downstream of a water control structure that was approved, validly constructed or placed under the Act;

heading: Designation - certain works
paragraph: (b) the work does not adversely affect the efficacy of the boom;

heading: Designation - certain works
paragraph: (c) the work does not alter either the level or the flow of the navigable water outside the area bounded by the boom;

heading: Designation - certain works
paragraph: (d) the work is not related to rebuilding or altering the boom or the water control structure; and

heading: Designation - certain works
paragraph: (e) the work is owned by the owner of the boom or the water control structure.

heading: Designation - outfalls and water intakes
paragraph: 26 An outfall or a water intake that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - outfalls and water intakes
paragraph: (a) the outfall or water intake does not extend vertically above the bed of the navigable water more than

heading: Designation - outfalls and water intakes
paragraph: (i) if the navigable water is less than 15 m in depth, 5% of the depth of the water, or

heading: Designation - outfalls and water intakes
paragraph: (ii) in any other case, 1 m;

heading: Designation - outfalls and water intakes
paragraph: (b) the outfall or water intake does not alter either the level or the flow of the navigable water to the point of interfering with navigation;

heading: Designation - outfalls and water intakes
paragraph: (c) the outfall or water intake is more than 30 m from a navigation channel; and

heading: Designation - outfalls and water intakes
paragraph: (d) the outfall or water intake is not associated with an existing or proposed dam or weir or an existing or proposed reservoir of water created by the construction of a dam or weir.

heading: Reposition or remove
paragraph: 27 If an outfall or water intake that was designated as a minor work under section 26 no longer meets the criteria set out in paragraph 26(a), the owner of the outfall or water intake must, as soon as feasible, reposition the outfall or water intake to meet this criteria or remove the outfall or water intake.

heading: Designation - dredging
paragraph: 28 Dredging to maintain the charted width or depth of a charted navigable water or the width or depth of any other navigable water is designated as a minor work.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 29 (1) The owner of dredging designated as a minor work under section 28 must ensure that

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) if the dredging uses floating pipes,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) the pipes are not situated in, on, over or across a navigation channel, and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) the pipes are visible from sunset to sunrise and during periods of restricted visibility by the placement of

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (A) cautionary buoys with yellow flashing lights,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (B) cautionary buoys with retro-reflective material, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (C) floats with retro-reflective material;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) if the dredging uses submerged pipes,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) the pipes are not situated in, under, through or across a navigation channel,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) the portion of the pipes not lying on the bed of the navigable water are marked by the placement of

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (A) cautionary buoys with yellow flashing lights, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (B) cautionary buoys with retro-reflective material, and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (iii) the pipes do not extend vertically above the bed of the navigable water more than

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (A) if the navigable water is less than 15 m in depth, 5% of the depth of the water, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (B) in any other case, 1 m;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (c) the dredging does not use cables that are situated in, on, over, through or across the navigable water;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (d) the dredging does not include blasting; and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (e) all materials removed by the dredging are disposed of

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) on land above the ordinary high water mark, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) in water where the disposal is authorized by or under an Act of Parliament.

heading: Exception - turbidity curtain
paragraph: (2) Subparagraphs (1)(a)(ii) and (b)(ii) do not apply if the owner of the dredging

heading: Exception - turbidity curtain
paragraph: (a) uses a turbidity curtain with a yellow or orange flotation system marked with retro-reflective material; and

heading: Exception - turbidity curtain
paragraph: (b) ensures that all dredging equipment is located within the area demarcated by the turbidity curtain.

heading: Bed contours of navigable water
paragraph: 30 If dredging designated as a minor work under section 28 disturbs the bed contours of a navigable water to the point of interfering, or likely to interfere, with navigation, the owner of the dredging must ensure, on completion of the activity, that the bed contours of the navigable water do not and are not likely to interfere with navigation.

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: 31 (1) A mooring system that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (a) on completion of its construction or placement, the mooring system consists of the following components:

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (i) an anchor that is set in or on the bed of a navigable water,

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (ii) a single anchor line,

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (iii) a single mooring buoy, and

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (iv) a mooring line that attaches to a vessel;

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (b) when a vessel is moored to the mooring system, the swing area

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (i) is more than 20 m from a work, other than an overhead cable, or from the swing area of another mooring system that is not owned by the owner of the mooring system,

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (ii) is more than 50 m from a marina or public boat-launching ramp,

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (iii) is more than 50 m from a navigation channel or, if there is no navigation channel, is not in, on, through or across a navigation route, and

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (iv) does not exceed the maximum diameter set out in column 2 of the table to this section when

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (A) if the mooring system is situated in tidal waters, the location where the mooring system is situated has the depth set out in column 1 of the table according to nautical charts produced by the Canadian Hydrographic Service or the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the United States, or

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (B) in any other case, the location where the mooring system is situated has the depth set out in column 1 of the table;

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (c) the mooring system is not associated with an existing or proposed marina;

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (d) the mooring system is situated in a location where the width of the navigable water is more than 100 m; and

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: (e) the anchor of the mooring system remains in the location where it was set in or on the bed of the navigable water.

heading: Designation - mooring systems
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Definition of swing area
paragraph: (2) In this section, swing area means the area created by the swinging of a vessel moored to a mooring system.

heading: Vessels of more than 12 m
paragraph: 32 The owner of a mooring system that is designated as a minor work under subsection 31(1) must not moor, or permit others to moor, to the mooring system a vessel that is more than 12 m in length, as measured between the fore and aft extremities of the vessel.

heading: Removal of mooring system
paragraph: 33 The owner of a mooring system that is designated as a minor work under subsection 31(1) must remove the mooring system as soon as feasible if

heading: Removal of mooring system
paragraph: (a) any component of the mooring system has been removed; or

heading: Removal of mooring system
paragraph: (b) during any two-year period, no vessel has moored to the mooring system.

heading: Designation - watercourse crossings
paragraph: 34 A watercourse crossing, including its abutments, footings and armouring, that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - watercourse crossings
paragraph: (a) the watercourse crossing is not a major work;

heading: Designation - watercourse crossings
paragraph: (b) the watercourse crossing is not a zipline or other cable used for transportation;

heading: Designation - watercourse crossings
paragraph: (c) the watercourse crossing is situated over or across a navigable water and the width of the navigable water is 30 m or less;

heading: Designation - watercourse crossings
paragraph: (d) the watercourse crossing is situated above the ordinary high water mark; and

heading: Designation - watercourse crossings
paragraph: (e) the watercourse crossing is designed to ensure that the clearance available below the watercourse crossing is at least 1 m more than the height of the tallest vessel that may navigate on the navigable water at the site where the watercourse crossing is situated.

heading: Infilling
paragraph: 35 During the construction, placement, alteration, rebuilding, removal, decommissioning, repair or maintenance of a watercourse crossing that is designated, or intended to be designated, as a minor work under section 34, the owner of the watercourse crossing must ensure that there is no infilling of navigable water.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 36 The following definitions apply in this section and in sections 37 and 38.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Indigenous governing body means a council, government or other entity that is authorized to act on behalf of an Indigenous group, community or people that holds rights recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982. (corps dirigeant autochtone)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: local authority means a government of a municipality, township, county or regional district, an Indigenous governing body, any other government constituted under the laws of a province or territory or a department of a provincial or territorial government or of the federal government. (administration locale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: swim area means an area for swimming that has been demarcated with ropes by, or on behalf of, a local authority. (zone de baignade)

heading: Designation - swim areas
paragraph: 37 A swim area that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - swim areas
paragraph: (a) the swim area is situated 30 m or more from a navigation channel or, if there is no navigation channel, is not situated in, on, over, through or across a navigation route;

heading: Designation - swim areas
paragraph: (b) the swim area does not extend more than 30 m into or on the navigable water;

heading: Designation - swim areas
paragraph: (c) the swim area does not occupy more than one-third of the width of the navigable water;

heading: Designation - swim areas
paragraph: (d) the ropes used to demarcate the swim area are marked by line floats;

heading: Designation - swim areas
paragraph: (e) the perimeter of the swim area is marked by swimming buoys; and

heading: Designation - swim areas
paragraph: (f) the swim area is situated 5 m or more from the adjacent property boundaries and property line extensions.

heading: Designation - works used by swimmers
paragraph: 38 A work that is used by swimmers in a swim area that is designated as a minor work under section 37 is designated as a minor work.

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: 39 (1) Scientific equipment that meets the following criteria is designated as a minor work:

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (a) the scientific equipment is required to perform scientific research and is being used for this sole purpose;

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (b) the scientific equipment is not being used for geotechnical testing or geotechnical investigations;

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (c) the scientific equipment is situated 30 m or more from a navigation channel or, if there is no navigation channel, is not situated in, on, over, through or across a navigation route;

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (d) if the scientific equipment does not lie on the bed of the navigable water, it is marked by

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (i) a cautionary buoy with retro-reflective material, or

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (ii) an Ocean Data Acquisition System (ODAS) buoy with retro-reflective material;

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (e) if the scientific equipment lies on the bed of the navigable water, it does not extend vertically above the bed of the navigable water more than

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (i) if the navigable water is less than 15 m in depth, 5% of the depth of the water, or

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (ii) in any other case, 1 m; and

heading: Designation - scientific equipment
paragraph: (f) the scientific equipment is situated more than 20 m from any work that is situated in, on, over, under, through or across the navigable water and is not owned by the owner of the equipment.

heading: Definition of scientific equipment
paragraph: (2) In this section, scientific equipment means monitoring and measurement devices, and any associated buoys, platforms or other similar structures, installed in, on, under, through or across a navigable water.

heading: Registration
paragraph: 40 This Order comes into force on the day on which it is registered.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "advanced treatment" means any form of treatment, other than dilution, that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) produces a municipal effluent quality with CBOD5 and TSS being 10 mg/L or less each, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) meets applicable substituted requirements identified by a director under section 8 [director may substitute requirements];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ADWF" means the average dry weather flow,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) being the daily municipal wastewater flow to a wastewater facility that occurs after an extended period of dry weather such that the inflow and infiltration has been minimized to the greatest extent practicable, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) calculated in accordance with section 2 [calculation of ADWF and dilution ratio];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assurance plan" means a program described in section 31 [assurance plan];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "capital replacement fund" means a fund described in section 29 (b) [security];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "CBOD5" means the carbonaceous 5-day biochemical oxygen demand;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "CFU" means a colony forming unit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "combined sewer system" means ditches, drains, sewers, treatment facilities and disposal facilities that collect, transport, treat or discharge a combination of municipal wastewater and stormwater in a single system;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "continuous monitoring system" means a communications system that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) enables operating conditions of a wastewater facility to be continuously monitored,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) provides an alarm if operating conditions deviate from established operating conditions, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) enables operating conditions to be adjusted, remotely or by service call, to within normal efficient operating range within 24 hours of any alarm;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "contributory population" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the number of persons connected to the municipal wastewater collection system, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the equivalent commercial and industrial contributions of municipal wastewater to that municipal wastewater collection system;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "dilution ratio" means the dilution ratio calculated in accordance with section 2 [calculation of ADWF and dilution ratio];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "discharge" means,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) when used as a noun, the total amount of municipal wastewater, including reclaimed water, released into the receiving environment from works, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) when used as a verb, to release a discharge;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "discharger" means a person authorized under this regulation to discharge;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "disinfection" means the destruction, inactivation or removal by any means of pathogenic microorganisms;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "domestic wastewater" has the same meaning as "domestic sewage" in the Sewerage System Regulation, B.C. Reg. 326/2004;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "embayed marine waters" means marine waters

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) located within a bay from which the access to the sea, by any route, has a maximum width of less than 1.5 km,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) located, if a line less than 6 km long is drawn between any 2 points on a continuous coastline, on the shore side of the line, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) in which flushing action is identified in a notice given by a director to be inadequate;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "environmental impact study" means an environmental impact study conducted in accordance with Division 3 [Environmental Impact Studies] of Part 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "EOCP" means Environmental Operators Certification Program;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "filtration" means the removal of solid particles from municipal effluent by passing the municipal effluent through

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a filtering medium such as sand, membrane or anthracite, or any other comparable filtering medium or combination of filtering media, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a physical barrier, device or septum onto which the solids are deposited;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "groundwater" means subsurface water at or below a water table in fully saturated geologic materials and formations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "health officer" has the same meaning as in the Public Health Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "inflow and infiltration" means water that enters a municipal wastewater collection system

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) directly from a stormwater connection (inflow),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) indirectly through the land (infiltration), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) through both (a) and (b);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "irrigation" means the application of reclaimed water at agronomic rates when irrigating vegetation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land" means the solid part of the earth's surface, and includes the foreshore and land covered by water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "MPN" means most probable number;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipal effluent" means the liquid resulting from the treatment of municipal wastewater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipal wastewater" means domestic wastewater or municipal liquid waste, including contributions from

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) holding tanks in recreational vehicles, boats and houseboats,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) commercial, institutional and industrial sources,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) inflow and infiltration,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) septic tank pumpage,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) holding tank solids, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) sludge from wastewater facilities;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipal wastewater collection system" means a conveyance system operated and maintained for the purpose of transporting municipal wastewater to a wastewater treatment facility, but does not include wastewater treatment and discharge facilities;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "NTU" means nephelometric turbidity unit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "open marine waters" means marine waters other than embayed marine waters;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "primary treatment" means any form of treatment, other than dilution, that produces a municipal effluent quality with CBOD5 and TSS being not more than 130 mg/L each;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualified professional" means an applied scientist or technologist specializing in a particular applied science or technology, including agrology, biology, chemistry, engineering, geology or hydrogeology,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) who is registered in British Columbia with the professional organization responsible for the applied scientist's or techonologist's area of expertise, acting under that professional association's code of ethics and subject to disciplinary action by that association, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) who, through suitable education, experience, accreditation and knowledge, may be reasonably relied on to provide advice within the applied scientist's or techonologist's area of expertise as it relates to this regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "reclaimed water" means municipal wastewater that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) treated by a wastewater facility, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) suitable for reuse in accordance with this regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "residential development" means a dwelling or collection of dwellings that serve as the primary residence of the majority of their inhabitants, all of whom rely on a discharger to provide a municipal wastewater system;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "secondary treatment" means any form of treatment, other than dilution, that produces a municipal effluent quality with,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in the case of a lagoon system, CBOD5 being not more than 45 mg/L and TSS being not more than 60 mg/L, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in any other case, CBOD5 and TSS being not more than 45 mg/L each;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "security" means security calculated in accordance with section 29 [security];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "septic tank" means a watertight vessel into which municipal wastewater is continually conveyed such that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) solids within the municipal wastewater settle,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) anaerobic digestion of organic materials occurs, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) municipal effluent is discharged;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stormwater" means runoff from rainfall, snow or snowmelt;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "TSS" means the total suspended solids or non-filterable residue;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wastewater facility" means any facility or works that gathers, treats, transports, stores, uses or discharges municipal wastewater or reclaimed water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "water quality guidelines" means, as published under the authority of the minister,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the water quality guidelines that, by approval of the minister, apply in British Columbia to groundwater and surface water,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to a body of water for which water quality objectives have been established, the most recent water quality objectives, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) if neither of paragraphs (a) or (b) applies, any other water quality standard acceptable to the minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "water table" means the surface

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) along which the fluid pressure is atmospheric, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) below which the fluid pressure is greater than atmospheric;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "water well" means a well used to supply water for domestic purposes and, for the purposes of this definition,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) "domestic purposes" has the same meaning as in the Drinking Water Protection Act, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) "well" has the same meaning as in the Water Sustainability Act.

heading: Calculation of ADWF and dilution ratio
paragraph: 2		  (1) The ADWF is calculated by dividing the total flow to the wastewater facility during the dry weather period by the number of days in that period.

heading: Calculation of ADWF and dilution ratio
paragraph: (2) The dilution ratio is calculated

heading: Calculation of ADWF and dilution ratio
paragraph: (a) by dividing the 2-year return period 7-day low flow in the receiving stream by the maximum weekly (7-day) municipal effluent flow, or

heading: Calculation of ADWF and dilution ratio
paragraph: (b) if sufficient data are not available to calculate the 2-year return period 7-day low flow or if the discharge is to a lake or marine waters, a ratio calculated using a method and data as authorized by a director.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements not to be exceeded
paragraph:
3
		  Unless stated otherwise, the municipal effluent quality requirements set out in Parts 5 to 7 are maximum values and must not be exceeded.

heading: Application
paragraph:
4
		  (1) In this section, "parcel", "sewerage system" and "strata lot" have the same meanings as in the Sewerage System Regulation, B.C. Reg. 326/2004.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), this regulation applies to all discharges

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) to ground, if the discharge

heading: Application
paragraph: (i)  is equal to or exceeds maximum daily flows of 22.7 m3/d, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii)  is from a sewerage system or combination of sewerage systems that serve structures on one or more parcels or strata lots, or on a shared interest, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) to water.

heading: Application
paragraph: (3) This regulation does not apply to a discharge to ground or water if the discharge is from a sewerage system that serves only a single family residence or duplex.

heading: Application
paragraph: (4) This regulation applies to all uses of reclaimed water unless the reclaimed water is from a sewerage system that serves only a single family residence or duplex.

heading: Persons who may discharge or provide reclaimed water
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A person is exempt from section 6 (2) and (3) of the Act and may discharge municipal effluent or provide reclaimed water if the person does so

heading: Persons who may discharge or provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) in accordance with this regulation, or

heading: Persons who may discharge or provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) to a wastewater facility that

heading: Persons who may discharge or provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (i)  is authorized under the Act to discharge to the receiving environment, and

heading: Persons who may discharge or provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (ii)  accepts and processes municipal wastewater as 10% or less of its waste stream.

heading: Persons who may discharge or provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from section 6 (2) and (3) of the Act and may discharge domestic wastewater to a sewerage system within the meaning of the Sewerage System Regulation, B.C. Reg. 326/2004, if the person is subject to, and complies with, that regulation.

heading: Prohibited or limited discharges
paragraph:
6
		  (1) This section applies despite any provision of this regulation.

heading: Prohibited or limited discharges
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), a person must not discharge municipal effluent, or register under Part 2 of this regulation for the purposes of discharging municipal effluent, in a manner that would conflict with a liquid waste management plan that is approved by the minister.

heading: Prohibited or limited discharges
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply to a discharger registered before November 17, 2005 with a director in relation to a discharge to Shuswap Lake.

heading: Discharge of non-domestic waste
paragraph:
7
		  (1) In this section, "non-domestic waste" means liquid waste other than domestic wastewater.

heading: Discharge of non-domestic waste
paragraph: (2) A person must not discharge non-domestic waste to a municipal wastewater facility unless the person ensures that the pre-discharge quality of the non-domestic waste meets the standards or is within the ranges specified in the Standard for Discharges Directed to Municipal or Industrial Effluent Treatment Works under Column 3 of Schedule 1.2 of the Hazardous Waste Regulation, B.C. Reg. 63/88.

heading: Discharge of non-domestic waste
paragraph: (3) A municipality must not accept non-domestic waste to a municipal wastewater collection system unless the municipality

heading: Discharge of non-domestic waste
paragraph: (a) regulates the introduction of non-domestic waste through a source control bylaw, or equivalent measures, that provides for the pre-treatment of industrial, commercial and institutional discharges to the system, or

heading: Discharge of non-domestic waste
paragraph: (b) demonstrates, by way of a study, that a source control bylaw, or equivalent measures, is not required to protect

heading: Discharge of non-domestic waste
paragraph: (i)  the wastewater facility that receives and processes the municipal wastewater, or

heading: Discharge of non-domestic waste
paragraph: (ii)  the receiving environment.

heading: Director may substitute requirements
paragraph:
8
		  (1) A director may, on receipt of an application or on the director's own initiative, substitute a different requirement for a requirement contained in this regulation if

heading: Director may substitute requirements
paragraph: (a) the substitution is necessary to protect the public or the receiving environment, or

heading: Director may substitute requirements
paragraph: (b) the intent of this regulation will be met by the substitution.

heading: Director may substitute requirements
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), if water quality objectives have not been established, the director may require a discharger to establish a background water quality limit for the receiving environment.

heading: Director must act in writing
paragraph:
9
		  If a director

heading: Director must act in writing
paragraph: (a) makes a substitution under section 8 [director may substitute requirements],

heading: Director must act in writing
paragraph: (b) gives notice of, authorizes or accepts a matter under this regulation, or

heading: Director must act in writing
paragraph: (c) waives a requirement under section 39 (2) [septic tanks], 54 [monitoring facilities and devices], 58 [toxicity monitoring requirements] or 114 (2) or (3) [alternate disposal or storage],

heading: Director must act in writing
paragraph: the substitution, notice, authorization, acceptance or waiver must be made in writing.

heading: Registration
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A person who registers in accordance with this Division is authorized to do either of the following in accordance with this regulation:

heading: Registration
paragraph: (a) discharge municipal effluent to ground or water;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (b) discharge or use reclaimed water.

heading: Registration
paragraph: (2) Registration takes effect on the date a director notifies the person that all of the following have been received in the form and manner acceptable to the director:

heading: Registration
paragraph: (a) the information and records required under sections 11 [administrative information] to 15 [certification by qualified professionals];

heading: Registration
paragraph: (b) any other relevant information or record requested by the director;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (c) payment in accordance with section 2 of the Permit and Approval Fees and Charges Regulation, B.C. Reg. 299/92;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (d) if required under Division 5 [Security and Assurance Plans],

heading: Registration
paragraph: (i)  proof that the person has established security and a capital replacement fund, or

heading: Registration
paragraph: (ii)  an assurance plan acceptable to a director

heading: Registration
paragraph: in compliance with the requirements of that Division.

heading: Registration
paragraph: (3) Notification under subsection (2) is not evidence that the requirements of the Act or this regulation have been met.

heading: Administrative information
paragraph:
11
		  The following administrative information is required for registration:

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (a) the full legal name and address of the person to be registered;

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (b) the name of a local contact for the person to be registered, and the contact's local address;

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (c) the name of the operator of the wastewater facility;

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (d) in respect of the land on which the wastewater facility is to be located,

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (i)  the address and legal description, or the name, latitude and longitude, and

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (ii)  the name of the registered owner;

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (e) the address and legal description, or the name, latitude and longitude, of the location of the discharge;

heading: Administrative information
paragraph: (f) if the person to be registered has a previous waste management permit respecting discharges to the environment that will be the subject of registration under this regulation, the permit number.

heading: Technical information
paragraph:
12
		  The following technical information is required for registration:

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (a) a description of the wastewater facility;

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (b) in respect of the discharge from the wastewater facility, a statement of

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (i)  the maximum daily flow of the discharge,

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (ii)  the applicable municipal effluent quality requirements, and

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (iii)  the municipal effluent and receiving environment monitoring program, including frequency, notification and reporting requirements;

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (c) for reclaimed water uses, a statement of

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (i)  the applicable category as described in section 104 [categories of reclaimed water], and

heading: Technical information
paragraph: (ii)  the rationale for selecting that category.

heading: Information respecting wastewater facility design, plans and studies
paragraph:
13
		  The following information respecting wastewater facility design, plans and studies is required for registration:

heading: Information respecting wastewater facility design, plans and studies
paragraph: (a) a copy of all environmental impact studies;

heading: Information respecting wastewater facility design, plans and studies
paragraph: (b) a copy of design drawings for the wastewater facility, including the discharge works, signed and sealed by a qualified professional;

heading: Information respecting wastewater facility design, plans and studies
paragraph: (c) an operating plan made in accordance with Division 4 [Operating Plans];

heading: Information respecting wastewater facility design, plans and studies
paragraph: (d) a site plan showing the receiving environment monitoring sites in relation to the location of the wastewater facility and the discharge.

heading: Proof of certain matters
paragraph:
14
		  (1) Proof of the following is required for registration:

heading: Proof of certain matters
paragraph: (a) if water conservation measures are significant to the design of the wastewater facility, that restrictive covenants respecting the measures are in place;

heading: Proof of certain matters
paragraph: (b) if approval to construct the wastewater facility is required by the relevant municipality, that the person has

heading: Proof of certain matters
paragraph: (i)  applied for a development permit, and

heading: Proof of certain matters
paragraph: (ii)  notified the relevant municipality of the intent to register under this regulation;

heading: Proof of certain matters
paragraph: (c) if the approval of a health officer is required for the use of reclaimed water under this regulation, that a health officer has been notified of, or has approved, the use.

heading: Proof of certain matters
paragraph: (2) If a local service area bylaw applies to the construction or operation of a wastewater facility, a copy of the bylaw must be included with the registration.

heading: Certification by qualified professionals
paragraph:
15
		  Statements, signed and sealed by the appropriate qualified professionals, certifying all of the following must be provided on registration:

heading: Certification by qualified professionals
paragraph: (a) the design of the proposed wastewater facility and the associated documentation meet the requirements of this regulation;

heading: Certification by qualified professionals
paragraph: (b) the proposed discharge from the wastewater facility will meet the requirements of this regulation;

heading: Certification by qualified professionals
paragraph: (c) all required environmental impact studies have been conducted in accordance with this regulation;

heading: Certification by qualified professionals
paragraph: (d) the operating plan for the proposed wastewater facility is adequate for its design;

heading: Certification by qualified professionals
paragraph: (e) if an assurance plan is provided, the assurance plan is adequate to provide for repairs to, or the operation, maintenance or replacement of, the wastewater facility;

heading: Certification by qualified professionals
paragraph: (f) if a director imposes conditions, limitations or requirements in respect of a substitution, notice, authorization, acceptance or waiver referred to in section 9 [director must act in writing], those conditions, limitations or requirements have been addressed.

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph:
16
		  (1) If there is a change in the information referred to in subsection (2), a discharger is not required to re-register, but the discharger must

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (a) notify a director within 30 days of the change, and

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (b) provide the director with the revised information.

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (2) The information for the purposes of subsection (1) is as follows:

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (a) a change in the information submitted for registration under section 11 (a), (b), (c) or (d) (ii) [administrative information];

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (b) a change in the quantity of the discharge if the resulting quantity, measured in relation to the quantity initially registered, is

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (i)  decreased, or

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (ii)  increased by not more than 10%;

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (c) a change in the quality of the discharge if the resulting quality, measured in relation to the quality initially registered, has no greater impact on public health or the receiving environment.

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (3) A registration may be transferred as follows:

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (a) at least 30 days before the transfer, the discharger must notify a director of the intended transfer;

heading: Changes to registration
paragraph: (b) after notification under paragraph (a) but at least 30 days before the transfer, the person to whom the registration is being transferred must provide the director with all applicable changes to the information required under this Division in respect of the registration.

heading: Suspension or cancellation of registration
paragraph:
17
		  (1) A director may suspend or cancel a registration in the same manner and for the same reasons as a director could suspend or cancel a permit or approval under section 18 of the Act.

heading: Suspension or cancellation of registration
paragraph: (2) A discharger must not release a discharge

heading: Suspension or cancellation of registration
paragraph: (a) during any period during which the discharger's registration is suspended, or

heading: Suspension or cancellation of registration
paragraph: (b) if the discharger's registration is cancelled.

heading: When environmental impact study required
paragraph:
18
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person must conduct an environmental impact study as follows:

heading: When environmental impact study required
paragraph: (a) for the purposes of registration under Division 2 [Registration];

heading: When environmental impact study required
paragraph: (b) if registered under Division 2, before expanding or making a material change to the person's wastewater facility.

heading: When environmental impact study required
paragraph: (2) If a person was authorized, before July 15, 1999, to discharge or use reclaimed water, subsection (1) (b) does not apply unless

heading: When environmental impact study required
paragraph: (a) a director notifies the person otherwise, or

heading: When environmental impact study required
paragraph: (b) the person is making a material change in respect of treatment, effluent quality or amount of discharge, if the amount is to be increased, from that which was authorized.

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph:
19
		  (1) A qualified professional must conduct for a wastewater facility an environmental impact study that includes provisions for controlling environmental impacts during the construction and operation of the wastewater facility or site.

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (2) A qualified professional must conduct for the receiving environment an environmental impact study that does all of the following:

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (a) considers the potential cumulative effects of the discharge on the receiving environment;

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (b) establishes additional municipal effluent quality requirements if necessary to protect public health or the receiving environment;

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (c) for the purposes of section 20 [receiving environment monitoring program], establishes in relation to both pre- and post-discharge

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (i)  receiving environment monitoring locations, and

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (ii)  sampling parameters and frequencies;

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (d) demonstrates, with regard to the nature of the discharge and the receiving environment, that the proposed disposal system, treatment and reuse, and the discharges from these, will not adversely affect public health or the receiving environment;

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (e) addresses any impact on the receiving environment when

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (i)  municipal effluent quality or reclaimed water requirements are met, and

heading: Requirements for environmental impact studies
paragraph: (ii)  municipal effluent or reclaimed water is degraded.

heading: Receiving environment monitoring program
paragraph:
20
		  (1) A discharger must establish a receiving environment monitoring program that does all of the following:

heading: Receiving environment monitoring program
paragraph: (a) provides for at least one control sampling station located upstream, upgradient or outside the influence of the initial dilution zone of the municipal effluent;

heading: Receiving environment monitoring program
paragraph: (b) obtains data to

heading: Receiving environment monitoring program
paragraph: (i)  assess the potential impact of the discharge or reclaimed water, and

heading: Receiving environment monitoring program
paragraph: (ii)  ensure that the discharge or reclaimed water does not or will not cause water quality parameters, outside the initial dilution zone, to fail to meet water quality guidelines;

heading: Receiving environment monitoring program
paragraph: (c) documents pre-discharge conditions.

heading: Receiving environment monitoring program
paragraph: (2) If seasonal variations are significant in the receiving environment, a discharger must conduct pre-discharge monitoring during the most critical period of the year.

heading: Environmental impact study if overflows
paragraph:
21
		  If section 42 [overflows] applies to a discharge, a qualified professional must conduct an environmental impact study that identifies

heading: Environmental impact study if overflows
paragraph: (a) any measures necessary to protect public health and the receiving environment, and

heading: Environmental impact study if overflows
paragraph: (b) any treatment needed to protect the designated uses of waters receiving combined sewer system overflows or municipal wastewater collection system overflows.

heading: Municipal wastewater collection systems excluded
paragraph:
22
		  This Division does not apply to a municipal wastewater collection system.

heading: General requirements of operating plans
paragraph:
23
		  A qualified professional must prepare for a wastewater facility an operating plan that details the requirements for all of the following:

heading: General requirements of operating plans
paragraph: (a) the proper operation, maintenance and monitoring of the wastewater facility, including lift stations;

heading: General requirements of operating plans
paragraph: (b) staff education and certification;

heading: General requirements of operating plans
paragraph: (c) a commissioning plan, a contingency plan and, if applicable, an irrigation plan, each made by the qualified professional in accordance with this Division;

heading: General requirements of operating plans
paragraph: (d) in the case of a temporary treatment system, a closure plan, made by the qualified professional, that describes the procedures for decommissioning the system when it is no longer required.

heading: Commissioning plan
paragraph:
24
		  A commissioning plan must include the operational procedures required to commission the wastewater facility, including the monitoring required to demonstrate that no adverse environmental impacts result from commissioning.

heading: Contingency plan
paragraph:
25
		  A contingency plan must describe all of the following:

heading: Contingency plan
paragraph: (a) emergency procedures for the wastewater facility, including lift stations;

heading: Contingency plan
paragraph: (b) procedures for notifying a health officer when necessary;

heading: Contingency plan
paragraph: (c) actions to be taken if municipal effluent quality fails to meet the requirements of this regulation;

heading: Contingency plan
paragraph: (d) an alternate method of disposal or storage if reclaimed water use is not possible.

heading: Irrigation plan
paragraph:
26
		  An irrigation plan must describe all of the following:

heading: Irrigation plan
paragraph: (a) the appropriate use, including the time of use, of reclaimed water;

heading: Irrigation plan
paragraph: (b) the maximum application rate, and the growing season, for the crop or vegetation to which the reclaimed water is applied;

heading: Irrigation plan
paragraph: (c) the site-specific loading, vegetation nutrient and metal limits.

heading: Application
paragraph:
27
		  This Division does not apply to

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a municipality, or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) a person who discharges from a service area defined and governed by a local service area bylaw.

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph:
28
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), a discharger who is an individual, company or strata corporation must not treat, reuse or discharge municipal wastewater generated by a residential development unless all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph: (a) security is maintained with a financial institution in

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph: (i)  an amount calculated in accordance with section 29 (a) [security], and

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph: (ii)  a form acceptable to a director;

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph: (b) the discharger provides to a director, within 90 days of the end of the discharger's fiscal year, audited annual financial statements of the discharger's capital replacement fund;

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph: (c) the discharger ensures that a director can act in a timely manner as set out in section 30 [use of security and capital replacement fund] respecting the security and capital replacement fund.

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph: (2)  Subsection (1) does not apply to a discharger who is covered by an assurance plan acceptable to a director under this Division.

heading: Maintenance of security
paragraph: (3)  Subsection (1) (b) does not apply to a discharger who has been registered under Division 2 [Registration] for less than one year.

heading: Security
paragraph:
29
		  For the purposes of submitting proof under section 10 (2) (d) (i) [registration] that a person has established security and a capital replacement fund, a person must establish both of the following:

heading: Security
paragraph: (a) security in an amount calculated by multiplying the maximum daily flow in m3/d by $1 400, rounded up to the nearest $1 000, and

heading: Security
paragraph: (b) a capital replacement fund composed of cash, securities, bonds or other financial instruments or insurance, or a combination of these, that

heading: Security
paragraph: (i)  ensures that the potential cost, whenever it may arise, of full replacement of a wastewater facility will be covered,

heading: Security
paragraph: (ii)  is adjusted annually to match inflation based on the Industrial Product Price Index in respect of machinery and equipment, produced by Statistics Canada, with the year the wastewater facility was registered as the base year, and

heading: Security
paragraph: (iii)  is not assignable or refundable.

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph:
30
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the security or contributions, or both, from the capital replacement fund established under section 29 [security] may, at the discretion of a director, be accessed and used for

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (a) the repair, operation, maintenance, replacement or improvement of a wastewater facility, or

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (b) the payment of any insurance policy premiums or deductibles.

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only if

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (a) the director notifies the discharger that

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (i)  one or more of the actions listed in subsection (1) (a) or (b) must be taken within a reasonable time specified by the director, and

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (ii)  if the action or actions are not taken, the security or contributions, or both, are required, and

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (b) the actions are not taken within the time specified by the director.

heading: Use of security and capital replacement fund
paragraph: (3) A discharger must replenish a capital replacement fund from which contributions are made unless a director authorizes alternative arrangements to ensure that the potential cost, whenever it may arise, of full replacement of the wastewater facility will be covered.

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph:
31
		  (1) For the purposes of having an assurance plan that is acceptable to a director under section 10 (2) (d) (ii) [registration], a person must do all of the following:

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (a) register the wastewater facility with a program

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (i)  for which insurance instruments are provided by a company registered under the Insurance Act with the Superintendent of Insurance, and

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (ii)  that has sufficient quality assurance and technical, financial and management resources to provide, or secure the provision of, repairs to, or for the operation, maintenance or replacement of, each wastewater facility registered with the program;

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (b) at the person's expense, ensure that an expert consultant whose qualifications are acceptable to the director has

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (i)  reviewed the assurance plan, and

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (ii)  made a recommendation to the director on the acceptability of the assurance plan;

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (c) attach to the assurance plan the findings of the expert consultant who reviewed the plan.

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (3) A person must not select an expert consultant who has

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (a) been involved in developing the assurance plan being reviewed, or

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (b) a personal or business relationship with the person requiring the review.

heading: Assurance plan
paragraph: (4) A director may accept an assurance plan if satisfied that it adequately provides for the matters described in subsection (1) (a) (ii).

heading: Qualified professionals
paragraph: 32		  A person must not design a wastewater facility, including a pumping facility, outfall or other works associated with a wastewater facility, for the purposes of this regulation unless the person is a qualified professional.

heading: Wastewater facilities
paragraph:
33
		  In designing a wastewater facility, a qualified professional must ensure that the wastewater facility will at all times achieve the applicable municipal effluent quality requirements under this regulation.

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph:
34
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: "long term effluent degradation" means a degradation in the quality of municipal effluent for a period continuing over several days;

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: "shellfish waters" means bodies of water capable of supporting shellfish in quantities that permit aboriginal, commercial or recreational shellfish harvesting;

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: "short term effluent degradation" means a degradation in the quality of municipal effluent for a period of even a few hours.

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this regulation, reliability categories are defined as follows:

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (a) category I, being wastewater facilities
