heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (i)  that discharge to ground or water, and

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (ii)  in respect of which short term effluent degradation could cause permanent or unacceptable damage to the receiving environment, including discharges near drinking water sources, shellfish waters or recreational waters in which direct human contact occurs;

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (b) category II, being wastewater facilities

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (i)  that discharge to ground or water, and

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (ii)  in respect of which permanent or unacceptable damage to the receiving environment, including discharges to recreational waters and land, would not be caused by short term effluent degradation but would be caused by long term effluent degradation;

heading: Reliability categories for wastewater facilities
paragraph: (c) category III, being wastewater facilities that do not fall within reliability category I or II.

heading: General component and reliability requirements
paragraph:
35
		  (1) A qualified professional must

heading: General component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (a) determine, based on an environmental impact study, which reliability category applies to a proposed wastewater facility, and

heading: General component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (b) ensure that the design of the wastewater facility meets the applicable requirements of Table 1 and section 36 [additional component and reliability requirements].

heading: General component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of Table 1, the remaining capacity with the largest unit out of service must be at least

heading: General component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (a) 50% of the design maximum flow where the notation "a" appears, or

heading: General component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (b) 75% of the design maximum flow where the notation "b" appears.

heading: General component and reliability requirements
paragraph: Table 1 - Component and Reliability Requirements for Wastewater Facilities

heading: Additional component and reliability requirements
paragraph:
36
		  (1) In respect of diffuser requirements, a qualified professional must ensure that

heading: Additional component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (a) diffusers must have multiple sections, and

heading: Additional component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (b) the maximum oxygen transfer capability must not be measurably impaired with the largest section out of service.

heading: Additional component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (2) In respect of blowers or mechanical aerators, a qualified professional must ensure that the remaining capacity with the largest unit out of service is able to achieve design maximum oxygen transfer.

heading: Additional component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (3) In respect of holding basin requirements for a wastewater facility within reliability category I, a qualified professional must ensure that the treatment system has adequate capacity for all flows.

heading: Additional component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (4) In respect of chemical flash mixer requirements for a wastewater facility within reliability category I and having only one basin, a qualified professional must provide for a backup system with at least 2 mixing devices, one of which may be installed.

heading: Additional component and reliability requirements
paragraph: (5) In respect of package treatment plants for a wastewater facility within reliability category I, a qualified professional must provide for municipal effluent filtration in conjunction with discharging to ground.

heading: Pumping facility requirements
paragraph:
37
		  In designing pumping facilities, a qualified professional must ensure that all of the following requirements are met:

heading: Pumping facility requirements
paragraph: (a) there are at least 2 pumps, with each pump capable of pumping peak design flows;

heading: Pumping facility requirements
paragraph: (b) for pumping stations requiring multiple pumps, the station must have sufficient capacity to pump peak design flow when the largest pump is out of service;

heading: Pumping facility requirements
paragraph: (c) for a 2-pump station, a receptacle for a portable generator must be available for standby power;

heading: Pumping facility requirements
paragraph: (d) for a multiple pump station, an on-site generator must be available for standby power;

heading: Pumping facility requirements
paragraph: (e) standby power must be capable of being activated before the hydraulic capacity of the pump station is exceeded.

heading: Combined sewers
paragraph:
38
		  (1) A qualified professional must not design the construction or expansion of a combined sewer system.

heading: Combined sewers
paragraph: (2) Nothing in subsection (1) prevents a person from making emergency repairs to an existing combined sewer system.

heading: Combined sewers
paragraph: (3) If repairs are made to a combined sewer system, a discharger must ensure that the person responsible for the municipal wastewater collection system

heading: Combined sewers
paragraph: (a) assesses the feasibility of sewer separation, and

heading: Combined sewers
paragraph: (b) separates, if possible, the storm and municipal wastewater collection systems at the time of repair.

heading: Septic tanks
paragraph:
39
		  (1) In designing a wastewater facility using a septic tank, a qualified professional must ensure that all of the following requirements are met:

heading: Septic tanks
paragraph: (a) the tank has a hydraulic capacity of at least 2 days' minimum detention time at the design maximum daily flow;

heading: Septic tanks
paragraph: (b) the tank is fitted with an effluent filter, a screen or an equivalent measure to protect pumps and prevent discharge of solids and floatables;

heading: Septic tanks
paragraph: (c) the tank is accessible for pump out.

heading: Septic tanks
paragraph: (2) A director may waive the requirement set out in subsection (1) (b) in respect of small, remote, seasonal discharges to water.

heading: Construction of facility
paragraph:
40
		  A person must not begin construction of a wastewater facility until the earlier of

heading: Construction of facility
paragraph: (a) being notified under section 10 (2) [registration] that registration is effective, and

heading: Construction of facility
paragraph: (b) receiving notice from a director that construction may begin.

heading: Definitions and extension of dates
paragraph:
41
		  (1) In this Division:

heading: Definitions and extension of dates
paragraph: "combined sewer overflow" means a discharge from a combined sewer system to a location other than a wastewater facility;

heading: Definitions and extension of dates
paragraph: "municipal wastewater collection system overflow" means a discharge from a municipal wastewater collection system to a location other than a wastewater facility, commonly referred to as a sanitary sewer overflow.

heading: Definitions and extension of dates
paragraph: (2) The minister may, on written request from a discharger, extend any date in this Division.

heading: Overflows
paragraph:
42
		  (1) A discharger must ensure that an overflow does not occur during storm or snowmelt events with a less than 5-year return period, unless

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (a) for municipal wastewater collection systems for which the contributory population is 10 000 persons or more, the person responsible for the municipal wastewater collection system develops and implements, as part of a liquid waste management plan, measures to eliminate overflows, or

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (b) if paragraph (a) does not apply, the person responsible for the municipal wastewater collection system or combined sewer system

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (i)  develops a liquid waste management plan or conducts a study, and

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (ii)  develops and implements measures to eventually eliminate overflows.

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), on the request of a director, a discharger must ensure that the person responsible for the municipal wastewater collection system or combined sewer system prepares a record at least once in each 10-year period containing all of the following:

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (a) an estimate of the volume, frequency and number of overflow occurrences for each overflow location;

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (b) an assessment of the potential impact of overflow occurrences on the receiving environment at each overflow location;

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (c) a record of each overflow occurrence that occurs during storm or snowmelt events with a less than 5-year return period;

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (d) based on the estimate in paragraph (a), an estimate of the total annual volume of all overflow occurrences that occur during storm or snowmelt events with a less than 5-year return period;

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (e) a plan for reducing the volume estimated under paragraph (d) by an average of,

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (i)  in the case of combined sewer overflows, 1% per year over a 10-year period, or

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of municipal wastewater collection system overflows, 10% per year over a 10-year period;

heading: Overflows
paragraph: (f) the steps that have been or will be taken to reduce the volume, frequency and number of overflow occurrences.

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph:
43
		  (1) A discharger may not use storage or conveyance facilities to reduce

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (a) the amount of sewer separation required, or

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (b) the amount of inflow and infiltration reduction required

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: unless the facilities immediately reduce and ultimately prevent the occurrence of combined sewer overflows.

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (2) If facilities are used under subsection (1) and primary and secondary treatment is available, the discharger must do all of the following:

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (a) provide at least primary treatment for flows greater than 2 times the ADWF;

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (b) use the full secondary capacity of the treatment system;

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (c) combine the primary and secondary municipal effluent prior to discharge;

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (d) maintain a minimum receiving environment-to-discharge dilution ratio of 40:1;

heading: Use of storage or conveyance facilities
paragraph: (e) if disinfection is required, provide adequate excess disinfection capacity to ensure disinfection of the entire discharge flow.

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph:
44
		  (1) A discharger must ensure that inflow and infiltration does not occur such that the maximum average daily flow exceeds 2 times the ADWF at the treatment plant during storm or snowmelt events with a less than 5-year return period, unless

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph: (a) for municipal wastewater collection systems for which the contributory population to the treatment plant is 10 000 persons or more, the person responsible for the municipal wastewater collection system addresses, as part of a liquid waste management plan, how inflow and infiltration can be reduced, or

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph: (b) if paragraph (a) does not apply, the person responsible for the municipal wastewater collection system

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph: (i)  develops a liquid waste management plan or conducts a study, and

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph: (ii)  develops and implements measures to reduce inflow and infiltration.

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if reductions below 2 times the ADWF are not possible or cost effective based on a cost-benefit analysis, the discharger must

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph: (a) provide full secondary treatment for the entire flow at all times, or

heading: Inflow and infiltration
paragraph: (b) undertake to do all of the things listed in section 43 (2) (a) to (e) [use of storage or conveyance facilities].

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph:
45
		  A discharger must not discharge until ensuring that all of the following requirements are met:

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (a) the design of the wastewater facility meets, and is capable of consistently meeting,

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (i)  the requirements of this regulation, or

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (ii)  the requirements, if any, substituted under section 8 [director may substitute requirements];

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (b) a qualified professional having expertise in the particular aspect of the design has undertaken

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (i)  the flow calculation,

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (ii)  the wastewater facility design, and

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (iii)  an inspection to ensure that the construction methods and materials, and the wastewater facility as constructed, meet the design criteria;

heading: Before discharge begins
paragraph: (c) the wastewater facility is classified under the EOCP.

heading: Notification of discharge
paragraph:
46
		  A discharger must do both of the following:

heading: Notification of discharge
paragraph: (a) within 30 to 60 days before beginning to discharge, provide to a director

heading: Notification of discharge
paragraph: (i)  notice that discharge will begin, and

heading: Notification of discharge
paragraph: (ii)  a copy of final design drawings reflecting the actual construction of the wastewater facility, certified as correct and signed and sealed by a qualified professional;

heading: Notification of discharge
paragraph: (b) not more than 7 days after beginning to discharge, provide to a director notice of the date that discharge began.

heading: Operator qualifications and certification
paragraph:
47
		  A discharger must not discharge unless the wastewater facility is operated and maintained by persons who

heading: Operator qualifications and certification
paragraph: (a) have the education, experience and qualifications specified in the operating plan, and

heading: Operator qualifications and certification
paragraph: (b) are certified under the EOCP.

heading: Operating plan
paragraph:
48
		  A discharger must adhere to the operating plan.

heading: Bypasses
paragraph:
49
		  (1) A person must not bypass a wastewater facility, or any component of the wastewater facility, for the purpose of scheduled maintenance unless maintenance cannot reasonably be undertaken without the bypass.

heading: Bypasses
paragraph: (2) If a bypass under subsection (1) may cause a discharge to fail to meet a requirement set out in this regulation, the discharger must do all of the following:

heading: Bypasses
paragraph: (a) notify a director at least 30 days before beginning the bypass;

heading: Bypasses
paragraph: (b) receive authorization from a director before beginning the bypass;

heading: Bypasses
paragraph: (c) comply with any conditions imposed by the director.

heading: Bypasses
paragraph: (3) All unauthorized bypasses, overflows and spills must be reported in accordance with the Spill Reporting Regulation, B.C. Reg. 263/90.

heading: Malfunctions
paragraph:
50
		  (1) If a malfunction or other condition results, or may result, in a discharge that fails to meet a requirement of this regulation, a discharger must notify a director immediately.

heading: Malfunctions
paragraph: (2) A discharger must notify a health officer immediately of any malfunction or other condition related to the wastewater facility that may result in a risk to public health.

heading: Water quality standards
paragraph:
51
		  The discharger must not discharge municipal effluent unless, at the edge of the initial dilution zone, all water quality guidelines are met.

heading: Disinfection and chlorination
paragraph:
52
		  (1) A discharger must disinfect municipal effluent if necessary to ensure that receiving water or groundwater used for domestic or agricultural water extraction, recreational uses or aquatic food production meets water quality guidelines.

heading: Disinfection and chlorination
paragraph: (2) A discharger must not use chlorination to disinfect municipal effluent without authorization from a director unless

heading: Disinfection and chlorination
paragraph: (a) the discharger first considers alternative disinfection methods, and

heading: Disinfection and chlorination
paragraph: (b) the municipal effluent discharged to surface water is dechlorinated below 0.02 mg/L total residual chlorine before discharge.

heading: Monitoring required
paragraph:
53
		  A person must not discharge, or provide or use reclaimed water, unless the discharger monitors

heading: Monitoring required
paragraph: (a) the discharge or reclaimed water, and

heading: Monitoring required
paragraph: (b) the receiving environment

heading: Monitoring required
paragraph: to determine compliance with this regulation.

heading: Monitoring facilities and devices
paragraph:
54
		  A discharger must do both of the following, unless one or both requirements are waived by a director:

heading: Monitoring facilities and devices
paragraph: (a) install, or provide, a suitable sampling facility for obtaining a sample of the municipal effluent or reclaimed water;

heading: Monitoring facilities and devices
paragraph: (b) provide and maintain a suitable flow measuring device to record, for each 24-hour period,

heading: Monitoring facilities and devices
paragraph: (i)  the municipal effluent volume discharged, and

heading: Monitoring facilities and devices
paragraph: (ii)  the volume of reclaimed water treated and used.

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A discharger must monitor the quality and quantity of municipal effluent or reclaimed water, as applicable, in accordance with Parts 5 [Specific Requirements for Discharge to Ground] to 7 [Reclaimed Water Requirements] for at least the first 2 years of discharge.

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (2) In respect of seasonal or intermittent discharges, a director may authorize an alternate monitoring schedule.

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (3) For new discharges, a person must begin monitoring on beginning to discharge or provide reclaimed water.

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (4) After 2 years of discharging or providing reclaimed water, a director may authorize alternate monitoring requirements based on

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (a) the monitoring data,

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (b) written recommendations of a qualified professional, or

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (c) any other information related to the discharge or the receiving environment.

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (5) A discharger must submit municipal effluent flow, municipal effluent quality and receiving environment monitoring data, and associated quality control data,

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (a) by electronic transmission directly to the central computer system of the ministry of the minister, or

heading: General monitoring requirements
paragraph: (b) in a form acceptable to a director.

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph:
56
		  (1) A discharger must adhere to the following requirements:

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (a) if required to sample quarterly, there must be at least 2 months between samples;

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (b) if required to sample monthly, there must be at least 10 days between samples;

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (c) if required to sample twice a month, there must be at least 7 days between samples;

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (d) if required to sample weekly, there must be at least 5 days between samples;

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (e) weekly composite samples must include samples from 3 days each week, with at least one day between samples;

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (f) if required to sample twice a week, there must be at least 2 days between samples;

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (g) daily composite samples must be composited in proportion to flow over 24 hours.

heading: Sampling schedule and requirements
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of sections 86 [monitoring requirements for discharges to ground] and 103 [monitoring requirements for discharges to water], chemical oxygen demand may be used in place of CBOD5 if CBOD5 is examined with chemical oxygen demand every fifth sampling.

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph:
57
		  (1) In subsections (2) and (3) (a):

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: "ministry" means the ministry of the minister;

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: "standard practice" means those standards and procedures that are necessary to ensure that measurements and analyses produce valid and reliable results.

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: (2) A discharger must ensure that sampling and flow measurements are carried out in accordance with standard practice and, for this purpose, may have regard to

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: (a) the standards and procedures as set out in the sampling and laboratory manuals posted to the ministry website, or

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: (b) if the standards and procedures described in paragraph (a) do not apply, the standards and procedures as described in British Columbia Field Sampling Manual: 2003 - For Continuous Monitoring and the Collection of Air, Air-Emission, Water, Wastewater, Soil, Sediment and Biological Samples, as published by the ministry and as amended from time to time.

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: (3) A discharger must ensure that analysis is carried out in accordance with standard practice and, for this purpose, may have regard to

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: (a) the standards and procedures as described in British Columbia Environmental Laboratory Manual: 2009, as published by the ministry and as amended from time to time, or

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: (b) suitable alternative procedures as authorized by the Resources Information Standards Committee of the ministry of the minister responsible for the Forest Act.

heading: Sampling and analysis
paragraph: (4) A discharger must submit laboratory analyses required by this regulation in accordance with the Environmental Data Quality Assurance Regulation.

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: 58		  (1) In addition to the requirements under section 103 [monitoring requirements for discharges to water], a person must not discharge to water, other than open marine waters, unless the discharge is monitored for toxicity in accordance with Table 2.

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: (a) the discharge quality does not exceed a maximum CBOD5 and TSS of 10 mg/L each;

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: (b) the discharge does not exceed a maximum daily flow of 50 m3/d;

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: (c) the discharge is diluted such that, at the outside boundary of the initial dilution zone, the dilution ratio exceeds 100:1;

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: (d) a director waives the requirement on the basis that the discharge does not adversely affect the receiving environment.

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: (3) A provider of reclaimed water must conduct toxicity testing if an environmental impact study indicates that testing is necessary.

heading: Toxicity monitoring requirements
paragraph: Table 2 - Toxicity Monitoring Requirements

heading: Determining toxicity
paragraph:
59
		  (1) A discharger must determine toxicity in accordance with

heading: Determining toxicity
paragraph: (a) Environment Canada's Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Effluents to Rainbow Trout (Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13), and

heading: Determining toxicity
paragraph: (b) if applicable, Environment Canada's Procedure for pH Stabilization During the Testing of Acute Lethality of Wastewater Effluent to Rainbow Trout (Reference Method EPS 1/RM/50).

heading: Determining toxicity
paragraph: (2) Discharge is not toxic if it passes a 96-hour bioassay test with a mortality rate of no more than 50%, as defined by the method referred to in subsection (1) (a).

heading: Failed water toxicity tests
paragraph:
60
		  (1) If a discharge fails a routine toxicity test under section 58 [toxicity monitoring requirements], the discharger must

heading: Failed water toxicity tests
paragraph: (a) notify a director immediately, and

heading: Failed water toxicity tests
paragraph: (b) conduct a confirmation toxicity test within 14 days of the date the previous toxicity sample was taken.

heading: Failed water toxicity tests
paragraph: (2) When conducting a confirmation toxicity test or when monitoring after a confirmed failure of a toxicity test, a discharger must

heading: Failed water toxicity tests
paragraph: (a) monitor ammonia levels at the same time, and

heading: Failed water toxicity tests
paragraph: (b) record the temperature and pH of the sample at the time of sampling.

heading: Failed water toxicity tests
paragraph: (3) If a discharge fails 2 consecutive toxicity tests, the discharger must conduct monitoring at the frequency specified in Column 3 of Table 2 in section 58 until the discharge passes 3 consecutive toxicity tests, after which time testing reverts to the frequency specified in Column 2 of that table.

heading: Further payments required
paragraph:
61
		  A discharger must pay the following to a director:

heading: Further payments required
paragraph: (a) on giving notice under section 16 (1) [changes to registration], an application fee in accordance with section 2 of the Permit and Approval Fees and Charges Regulation;

heading: Further payments required
paragraph: (b) on each anniversary of the date on which registration is effective under section 10 (2) [registration], an annual charge in accordance with section 3 of the Permit and Approval Fees and Charges Regulation, based on the quality and quantity of the discharge as indicated under section 12 (b) [technical information] of this regulation.

heading: Records respecting septic tank pump outs
paragraph:
62
		  A discharger using a septic tank must provide pump out records to a director in the frequency set out in the operating plan prepared under section 23 [general requirements of operating plans].

heading: Information and records to be retained
paragraph:
63
		  A discharger must retain for inspection by an officer at any time a copy of, as applicable,

heading: Information and records to be retained
paragraph: (a) the information and records submitted on registration under Division 2 [Registration] of Part 2,

heading: Information and records to be retained
paragraph: (b) a record prepared under section 42 (2) [overflows],

heading: Information and records to be retained
paragraph: (c) all outfall inspection reports,

heading: Information and records to be retained
paragraph: (d) municipal effluent flow and municipal effluent quality monitoring data, and

heading: Information and records to be retained
paragraph: (e) receiving environment monitoring data.

heading: Notice of assurance plan lapse
paragraph:
64
		  If a discharger is no longer covered under an assurance plan acceptable to a director, the discharger must notify a director in writing within 30 days of the date coverage ends.

heading: Annual report respecting assurance plans
paragraph:
65
		  (1) A discharger who is covered by an assurance plan accepted under Division 5 [Security and Assurance Plans] of Part 2 must, on or before March 31 of each year, provide to a director an annual report detailing

heading: Annual report respecting assurance plans
paragraph: (a) what quality assurance and technical, financial and management resources are in place under the assurance plan, and

heading: Annual report respecting assurance plans
paragraph: (b) how effective the quality assurance and technical, financial and management resources have been during the previous calendar year.

heading: Annual report respecting assurance plans
paragraph: (2) On receiving a report, a director may give notice requiring the discharger to

heading: Annual report respecting assurance plans
paragraph: (a) amend the assurance plan, or

heading: Annual report respecting assurance plans
paragraph: (b) submit a new assurance plan for review and acceptance.

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph:
66
		  (1) For discharges for which the contributory population is less than 10 000 persons, a discharger, on receiving notice from a director, must prepare and submit a report

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (a) on or before a date specified by the director,

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (b) in a form acceptable to, and containing any information requested by, the director.

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (2) For discharges for which the contributory population is 10 000 persons or more, a discharger must submit an annual report that includes all of the following:

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (a) a compendium of the municipal effluent flow, municipal effluent quality and receiving environment monitoring data and associated quality control work submitted under sections 86 [monitoring requirements for discharges to ground] and 87 [additional monitoring requirements];

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (b) any effect of the discharge on the quality of the receiving environment, using appropriate statistical and graphical analysis;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (c) any trends in environmental quality in receiving environments affected by the discharge, using background or pre-discharge data and all the years of record in which the discharge has taken place;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (d) if source control, water conservation and education programs related to municipal wastewater quality or quantity, or both, have been implemented, an update of the previous year's achievements;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (e) an update of the problems identified in the previous year and the corrective actions taken;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (f) any planned improvements of wastewater facilities for the coming year;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (g) if reduce, reuse and recycle initiatives related to municipal wastewater quality or quantity, or both, have been implemented, an update of the previous year's achievements;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (h) documentation of historic and projected contributory population and remaining plant capacity;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (i) if applicable, the status of any capital replacement fund established by the discharger;

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (j) an outline of the projected monitoring dates for the next year.

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (3) An annual report under subsection (2) must

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (a) be prepared, and the analysis done, by a suitably qualified professional,

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (b) provide an interpretation of monitoring data,

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (c) be in a form acceptable to, and contain any information requested by, a director, and

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (d) be submitted to a director before May 1 of each year.

heading: Reports respecting discharge to ground and water
paragraph: (4) On receiving notice from a director, a discharger must make an annual report under subsection (2) available to an individual requesting it, or to the public, by posting it on the Internet or providing a copy to the local public library, or both.

heading: Annual reports respecting reclaimed water
paragraph:
67
		  A provider of reclaimed water must submit to a director and a health officer an annual report containing all of the following information:

heading: Annual reports respecting reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) the quality and quantity of reclaimed water;

heading: Annual reports respecting reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) the method of use and any diversion to an alternate disposal method or to storage;

heading: Annual reports respecting reclaimed water
paragraph: (c) user information, and communication materials related to the use of reclaimed water;

heading: Annual reports respecting reclaimed water
paragraph: (d) the results of any receiving environment monitoring required under this regulation;

heading: Annual reports respecting reclaimed water
paragraph: (e) the projected monitoring dates for the next year;

heading: Annual reports respecting reclaimed water
paragraph: (f) the reason for any non-compliance with this regulation and the corrective action taken.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph:
68
		  (1) This Part applies only in respect of discharging to ground.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (2) In this Part:

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: "aquifer" includes any soil or rock formation that has sufficient porosity and water yielding ability to permit the extraction or injection of water at rates of 5 L/minute or more;

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: "disposal site perimeter" means the outer edge of the subsurface treatment works;

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: "groundwater mounding effect" means the vertical rise in the water table that occurs in response to a discharge.

heading: Municipal effluent classes
paragraph:
69
		  For the purposes of this Part, municipal effluent is classed as follows:

heading: Municipal effluent classes
paragraph: (a) class A, being high quality municipal effluent resulting from advanced treatment with the addition of disinfection and nitrogen reduction;

heading: Municipal effluent classes
paragraph: (b) class B, being high quality municipal effluent resulting from advanced treatment;

heading: Municipal effluent classes
paragraph: (c) class C, being municipal effluent resulting from secondary treatment;

heading: Municipal effluent classes
paragraph: (d) class D, being municipal effluent resulting from treatment in a septic tank.

heading: Discharge
paragraph:
70
		  (1) In this section, "zone of influence" means the zone around a water well that, in the opinion of a qualified professional, supplies water to the well.

heading: Discharge
paragraph: (2) A person must not discharge, within the zone of influence, municipal effluent to ground unless

heading: Discharge
paragraph: (a) the requirements set out in this Part are met, and

heading: Discharge
paragraph: (b) the discharged effluent is disinfected.

heading: Discharge
paragraph: (3) A person must ensure that a discharge of municipal effluent within 300 m of a drinking water source meets class A municipal effluent requirements.

heading: Initial dilution zone
paragraph:
71
		  If a person discharges municipal effluent to ground,

heading: Initial dilution zone
paragraph: (a) the initial dilution zone is the 3-dimensional subsurface zone where mixing of the municipal effluent and groundwater occurs, and

heading: Initial dilution zone
paragraph: (b) the boundary of the initial dilution zone is the vertical extension into the ground of the property boundaries of the land into which discharging occurs.

heading: Subsurface travel time
paragraph:
72
		  (1) In this section, "subsurface travel time" means the actual time, including the time spent in the unsaturated and saturated zones, required for municipal effluent to travel from the disposal site perimeter to the point where the municipal effluent

heading: Subsurface travel time
paragraph: (a) surfaces,

heading: Subsurface travel time
paragraph: (b) reaches a property line, or

heading: Subsurface travel time
paragraph: (c) is intercepted by a water well.

heading: Subsurface travel time
paragraph: (2) A discharger must ensure that the subsurface travel time is at least,

heading: Subsurface travel time
paragraph: (a) for class A or B municipal effluent, 6 days, or

heading: Subsurface travel time
paragraph: (b) for class C or D municipal effluent, 10 days.

heading: Surfacing of discharge
paragraph:
73
		  A discharger must ensure that discharge does not surface, or cause the groundwater table to be raised to the surface, as follows:

heading: Surfacing of discharge
paragraph: (a) within 30 m beyond the disposal site perimeter;

heading: Surfacing of discharge
paragraph: (b) more than 30 m beyond the disposal site perimeter, unless

heading: Surfacing of discharge
paragraph: (i)  the discharge does not cause water quality parameters to fail to meet water quality guidelines, and

heading: Surfacing of discharge
paragraph: (ii)  there will be no adverse impacts from the surfaced municipal effluent.

heading: Calculating flow
paragraph:
74
		  (1) A qualified professional must determine the calculated or actual maximum daily flow.

heading: Calculating flow
paragraph: (2) A qualified professional may use the actual maximum daily flow to design the wastewater facility if

heading: Calculating flow
paragraph: (a) the actual daily flow is equal to or greater than 37 m3/d,

heading: Calculating flow
paragraph: (b) water conservation measures are used, and

heading: Calculating flow
paragraph: (c) a restrictive covenant is placed on each property requiring that water conservation measures are continuously used.

heading: Calculating flow
paragraph: (3) If actual maximum daily flow is used under subsection (2), daily discharge volume monitoring is required.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph:
75
		  (1) A discharger of class A, B or C municipal effluent must meet the applicable municipal effluent quality requirements set out in this section and listed in Table 3.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (2) The median coliform values for 7 consecutive daily tests and any single value test must be less than the value specified in Table 3.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), for class C lagoon systems, the maximum TSS level must not exceed 60 mg/L.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (4) In respect of class A and B municipal effluent that is discharged to a drainfield,

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (a) filtration is required to prevent solids carrying over into the disposal field, and

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (b) monitoring controls must be maintained to signal an alarm when filtration begins to malfunction.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: Table 3 - Municipal Effluent Quality Requirements

heading: Unsaturated soil depth
paragraph:
76
		  (1) For the purposes of this section, "unsaturated soil" means the soil between the land surface and the water table where the soil pore spaces contain water at less than atmospheric pressure, as well as air and other gases.

heading: Unsaturated soil depth
paragraph: (2) The minimum unsaturated soil depth must be measured from the infiltrative surface to the highest water table, including the groundwater mounding effect or restrictive layer.

heading: Unsaturated soil depth
paragraph: (3) For chamber distribution systems, the bottom of the sidewall, or "foot" of the chamber, is considered to be the infiltrative surface.

heading: Unsaturated soil depth
paragraph: (4) For class A or B municipal effluent, a discharger must ensure that the minimum unsaturated soil depth is 0.5 m.

heading: Unsaturated soil depth
paragraph: (5) For class C or D municipal effluent, a discharger must ensure that the minimum unsaturated soil depth for maximum daily flows of

heading: Unsaturated soil depth
paragraph: (a) less than 37 m3/d is 0.75 m, and

heading: Unsaturated soil depth
paragraph: (b) 37 m3/d or more is 1 m.

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph:
77
		  A discharger must not discharge, above the following aquifer areas, municipal effluent having a total nitrogen content of more than 10 mg/L:

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (a) the Abbotsford-Sumas Aquifer in Abbotsford;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (b) the Hopington and Langley/Brookswood Aquifers in Langley;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (c) the Lower Nechako River Aquifer in Prince George;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (d) the Lower Cowichan River Aquifer in Duncan;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (e) the Grand Forks Aquifer in Grand Forks;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (f) the Merritt Aquifer in Merritt;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (g) the Osoyoos West and Osoyoos East Aquifers in Osoyoos;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (h) the Vedder River Fan Aquifer in Chilliwack;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (i) the aquifers stretching from Osoyoos Lake to Tuc-el-Nuit Lake and from Tuc-el-Nuit Lake to Vaseux Lake.

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph:
78
		  (1) A discharger must ensure that drainage pipes are at least the length set out for the applicable municipal effluent class and percolation rate, as listed in Table 4.

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a discharger may use a chamber distribution system with an equivalent length to the minimum pipe length listed in Table 4.

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (3) If

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (a) percolation rates are less than 2 minutes per 25 mm,

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (b) the maximum daily flow is less than 37 m3/d, and

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (c) class A or B municipal effluent is discharged by pressure distribution,

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: a discharger may use American Society for Testing and Materials C33 sand-filled trenches to reduce percolation.

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (4) If percolation rates exceed 20 minutes per 25 mm, a qualified professional must

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (a) supervise construction, and

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: (b) ensure that construction has not reduced the trench wall permeability, except that, for maximum daily flows of less than 37 m3/d, permeability may be reduced if the native undisturbed permeable soil depth exceeds 1.35 m as measured from the bottom of the field to the level of the water table.

heading: Drainage pipe length requirements
paragraph: Table 4 - Minimum Drainage Pipe Length for Each Field

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph:
79
		  (1) Despite section 78 (1) [drainage pipe length requirements], a qualified professional may provide for a reduction in drainage pipe length to a maximum of 40% if both of the following requirements are met:

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (a) under section 74 (2) [calculating flow], a qualified professional uses the actual maximum daily flow to design the wastewater facility;

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (b) the drainfield discharges class A or B effluent.

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (2) In the circumstances set out in subsection (3), a qualified professional may design a drainfield with deeper, narrower trenches and reduce the drainage pipe length to a value equal to the product of

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (a) the pipe length required under section 78, and

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (b) a factor of 1/H0.5 or 0.8, whichever is greater, where H is the drainage trench depth below pipe invert in metres.

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (3) The circumstances for the purposes of subsection (2) are as follows:

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (a) percolation rates are less than 5 minutes per 25 mm;

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (b) the maximum daily flow is equal to or greater than 37 m3/d;

heading: Reductions in drainage pipe length
paragraph: (c) the depth to groundwater, including any groundwater mounding effect, is more than 1 m below the bottom of the drainage trench.

heading: Drainage pipes
paragraph:
80
		  A discharger must ensure that all of the following requirements are met:

heading: Drainage pipes
paragraph: (a) a pressure distribution system is used for drainage pipes fed by a dosing syphon or pump;

heading: Drainage pipes
paragraph: (b) unless a pressure distribution system is used, the drainage pipe is at least 70 mm in diameter;

heading: Drainage pipes
paragraph: (c) the drainage pipe cover is at least 0.15 m and meets local frost protection requirements.

heading: Drain fields
paragraph:
81
		  (1) A discharger must ensure that visual inspection ports are installed in the drain field.

heading: Drain fields
paragraph: (2) A discharger must ensure that all of the following requirements are met:

heading: Drain fields
paragraph: (a) drainage pipes are provided in 2 drain fields, each having at least the length of drainage pipe required under section 78 [drainage pipe length requirements] unless a reduction is permitted under section 79 [reductions in drainage pipe length];

heading: Drain fields
paragraph: (b) a third undeveloped drain field is retained as a standby area;

heading: Drain fields
paragraph: (c) drain fields are constructed with trenches spaced

heading: Drain fields
paragraph: (i)  such that there is at least 3 m between the centre of each trench, or

heading: Drain fields
paragraph: (ii)  if the performance of the drain field would not be adversely affected, at least 2 m apart from each other with at least double the standby area;

heading: Drain fields
paragraph: (d) trenches are at least 0.6 m in width, with trench bottoms at least 0.3 m below the pipe invert.

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph:
82
		  (1) For all discharges to ground and standby areas, a discharger must ensure that setbacks from the area into which discharging occurs are at least the distance set out in Table 5.

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: (2) A discharger must ensure that subsurface fields, the standby area and a surrounding buffer strip as set out in row 2 ("building drain, buffer strip") of Table 5

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: (a) are kept free of buildings or hard surfacing of any kind, and

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: (b) are not used for building drains or any activity that may cause damage to the system or interfere with its operation.

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: (3) The wastewater facility itself is a building for the purposes of row 2 of Table 5.

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of row 6 of Table 5, if, based on a hydrogeological assessment to determine the minimum distance required to protect the water quality of a water well,

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: (a) the distance from the water well must be extended in accordance with the hydrogeological assessment, or

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: (b) the maximum daily flow is more than or equal to 37 m3/d,

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: the distance from the water well may be decreased, if authorized by a director, to a distance of no less than 90 m.

heading: Setback requirements
paragraph: Table 5 - Minimum Setback Requirements

heading: Infiltration basins
paragraph:
83
		  A discharger must ensure that infiltration basins meet the following requirements:

heading: Infiltration basins
paragraph: (a) at least 2 basins must be provided to allow cleaning of one basin while the other is operating and to act as a safety factor for unusual conditions;

heading: Infiltration basins
paragraph: (b) for 2 basin systems, each basin must be capable of accepting all the municipal effluent under annual average rainfall conditions;

heading: Infiltration basins
paragraph: (c) subject to Division 1 [General Requirements], discharge of municipal effluent to an infiltration basin meets at least class C requirements.

heading: Sand mounds and seepage beds
paragraph:
84
		  A discharger may use sand mounds and seepage beds only if both of the following requirements are met:

heading: Sand mounds and seepage beds
paragraph: (a) sand mounds and seepage beds are constructed using American Society for Testing and Materials C33 sand to reduce percolation;

heading: Sand mounds and seepage beds
paragraph: (b) the discharger is authorized by a director to use the sand mounds and seepage beds.

heading: Monitoring wells
paragraph:
85
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), a discharger must install monitoring wells in sufficient number and orientation, as determined by a qualified professional, to measure background and receiving environment water quality.

heading: Monitoring wells
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1),

heading: Monitoring wells
paragraph: (a) the qualified professional must consider horizontal as well as vertical arrays for sampling, and

heading: Monitoring wells
paragraph: (b) at least 4 wells per aquifer are required, one of which must be a background monitoring well.

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to ground
paragraph:
86
		  A discharger must monitor municipal effluent quality and quantity in accordance with section 87 [additional monitoring requirements] and Table 6, 7 or 8, as applicable, of this section.

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to ground
paragraph: Table 6 - Monitoring Requirements If Maximum Daily Flow < 50 m3/d

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to ground
paragraph: Table 7 - Monitoring Requirements If Maximum Daily Flow ≥ 50 m3/d and < 500 m3/d

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to ground
paragraph: Table 8 - Monitoring Requirements If Maximum Daily Flow ≥ 500 m3/d

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph:
87
		  (1) In respect of a discharge having a maximum daily flow of 500 m3/d or more, after 60 days of compliance with the quality limit,

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (a) the discharger must conduct weekly presence or absence testing for coliform monitoring,

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (b) if the presence of any coliform is detected, daily fecal coliform testing must be reinstated until the quality limit is in compliance, and

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (c) for the purpose of paragraph (b), 7 tests must be conducted to demonstrate compliance before weekly presence or absence testing may be resumed.

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (2) A discharger of class D municipal effluent must monitor 24-hour flow as follows:

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (a) if the maximum daily flow is less than 50 m3/d, weekly;

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (b) if the maximum daily flow is 50 m3/d or more but less than 500 m3d, twice each week, and

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (c) if the maximum daily flow is 500 m3/d or more, daily.

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (3) A discharger must submit gathered data under this section to a director, if the maximum daily flow is

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (a) less than 50 m3/d, twice each year, or

heading: Additional monitoring requirements
paragraph: (b) 50 m3/d or more, quarterly.

heading: Continuous monitoring system
paragraph:
88
		  A discharger of class A or B municipal effluent must install a continuous monitoring system.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph:
89
		  (1) This Part applies only in respect of discharging to water.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (2) In this Division:

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: "diffuser" means a section of pipe that diffuses municipal effluent into water through a series of ports;

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: "estuary" means that portion of a receiving water lying below the farthest point upstream of detectable changes in water movement or chemistry through mixing of fresh and salt water and due to tidal action;

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: "mean low water" means,

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (a) for marine waters, the datum provided on the most recently published marine chart published by the Canadian Hydrographic Service for the location,

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (b) for lakes, the point of contact between the lake surface and the shore at the time when the surface is at its average annual minimum elevation based on the last 10 years of records, and

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (c) for streams and rivers, the point of contact between the stream or river surface and the shore during the 2-year return period 7-day low flow.

heading: Discharge
paragraph:
90
		  A person must not discharge municipal effluent to water unless the requirements set out in this Part are met.

heading: Initial dilution zone for water generally
paragraph:
91
		  (1) If a person discharges municipal effluent to water, the initial dilution zone is the 3-dimensional zone around the point of discharge where mixing of the municipal effluent and the receiving water occurs.

heading: Initial dilution zone for water generally
paragraph: (2) The edge of the initial dilution zone must be located at least 300 m away from the following:

heading: Initial dilution zone for water generally
paragraph: (a) recreational areas;

heading: Initial dilution zone for water generally
paragraph: (b) aboriginal, commercial or recreational shellfish harvesting areas;

heading: Initial dilution zone for water generally
paragraph: (c) domestic or agricultural water intakes;

heading: Initial dilution zone for water generally
paragraph: (d) any sensitive area requiring protection identified in a notice given by a director.

heading: Initial dilution zone for water generally
paragraph: (3) Initial dilution zones may overlap only if the combined effects do not cause water quality parameters, outside the combined initial dilution zone, to fail to meet water quality guidelines.

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph:
92
		  (1) For the purpose of calculating the initial dilution zone for marine waters or a lake, both of the following, measured from the point of discharge and from mean low water, apply:

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph: (a) the height is the distance from the bed to the water surface;

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph: (b) the radius is the lesser of

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph: (i)  100 m, and

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph: (ii)  25% of the width of the body of water.

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph: (2) For discharge from an outfall diffuser, the radius referred to in subsection (1) (b) (i) must be measured from the first and last diffuser ports.

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph: (3) In embayed marine waters and lakes, the initial dilution zone must not extend closer to shore than mean low water.

heading: Initial dilution zone for marine waters and lakes
paragraph: (4) In open marine waters, the edge of the initial dilution zone must be located outside of the shallow water zone in which surf will form along the shore.

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph:
93
		  (1) For the purpose of calculating the initial dilution zone for a stream, river or estuary, all of the following, measured from the point of discharge and from mean low water, apply:

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (a) the height is the distance from the bed to the water surface;

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (b) the width, perpendicular to the path of the stream, is the lesser of

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (i)  100 m, and

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (ii)  25% of the width of the stream or estuary;

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (c) the length, parallel to the path of the stream, is the distance between a point 100 m upstream and a point that is the lesser of

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (i)  100 m downstream, and

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (ii)  a distance downstream at which the width of the municipal effluent plume equals the width determined under paragraph (b).

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (2) For estuaries,

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (a) the stream flow is the fresh water content, and

heading: Initial dilution zone for streams, rivers and estuaries
paragraph: (b) the initial dilution zone must not extend closer to shore than mean low water.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph:
94
		  (1) A discharger must meet the applicable municipal effluent quality requirements as set out in this section and as listed in Table 9, 10 or 11.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (5), if the dilution ratio in respect of discharges to streams, rivers and estuaries is less than 100:1, a qualified professional conducting an environmental impact study must determine if municipal effluent quality must be better than that shown in Table 9, 10 or 11, as applicable.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (5), if the dilution ratio in respect of discharges to streams, rivers and estuaries used for recreational or domestic water extraction is less than 40:1, a person must not discharge unless all of the following requirements are met:

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (a) the discharge meets advanced treatment requirements;

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (b) no other discharge options are available;

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (c) the discharge is authorized by a director.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), in respect of seasonal discharges or discharges to streams, rivers and estuaries that are not used for recreational or domestic water extraction, a director may approve the use of secondary treatment if there is a minimum dilution ratio of 20:1.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (5) Discharge is prohibited if the dilution ratio is less than 10:1.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (6) For discharges to marine waters having a maximum daily flow of less than 10 m3/d, a discharger must use a septic tank that meets the design requirements set out in section 39 [septic tanks].

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (7) For all lagoon systems, the maximum TSS level is 60 mg/L.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: Table 9 - Municipal Effluent Quality RequirementsIf Maximum Daily Flow < 10 m3/d

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: Table 10 - Municipal Effluent Quality RequirementsIf Maximum Daily Flow ≥ 10 m3/d - < 50 m3/d

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: Table 11 - Municipal Effluent Quality Requirements If Maximum Daily Flow > 50 m3/d

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph:
95
		  (1) This section applies only if the maximum daily flow is more than or equal to 50 m3/day.

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (2) For flows up to and equaling 2 times the ADWF, treatment and municipal effluent quality requirements are determined by daily flow multiples that require secondary treatment.

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (3) If flows are more than 2 times the ADWF during a storm or equivalent snowmelt event with a less than 5-year return period, a discharger must

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (a) have a liquid waste management plan or specific study, and

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (b) implement the plan's or study's measures.

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsections (2) and (3), a director may give notice that the factor is increased to a maximum of 3 times the ADWF for areas of the province where

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (a) permafrost or freezing ground conditions require roof drains to be connected to the municipal wastewater collection system, and

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (b) connections must be made in accordance with a practice acceptable to a local building inspector or an equivalent practice.

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (5) A director may substitute, in accordance with section 8 [director may substitute requirements], different requirements for the total phosphorus and orthophosphate requirements specified in Table 11, as set out in section 94 [municipal effluent quality requirements], if an environmental impact study demonstrates that

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (a) receiving waters would not be subject to an undesirable degree of increased biological activity because of the phosphorus addition,

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (b) lower municipal effluent concentrations than those shown in Table 11 in section 94 are necessary, or

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (c) a mass load criteria may be needed.

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (6) A discharger must determine the maximum allowable municipal effluent ammonia concentration at the "end of pipe" by a back calculation, from the edge of the initial dilution zone, that considers

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (a) the ambient temperature and pH characteristics of the receiving water, and

heading: If maximum daily flow ≥ 50 m3/d
paragraph: (b) water quality guidelines for chronic ammonia.

heading: Allowable fecal coliform organisms
paragraph:
96
		  (1) A discharger, unless using a septic tank, must ensure that the number of fecal coliform organisms meets the following requirements, as applicable:

heading: Allowable fecal coliform organisms
paragraph: (a) if discharging to shellfish bearing waters at the edge of the initial dilution zone, the median or geometric mean MPN of fecal coliform organisms must be less than 14/100 mL, with not more than 10% of the samples exceeding 43/100 mL;

heading: Allowable fecal coliform organisms
paragraph: (b) if discharging to recreational use waters, the geometric mean number of fecal coliform organisms at the edge of the initial dilution zone must be less than or equal to 200/100 mL.

heading: Allowable fecal coliform organisms
paragraph: (2) The geometric mean, as determined from the bacteriological results of the last 5 samples for which analyses have been completed over the last 30 days, must not be more than the coliform limits specified in subsection (1) (a) or (b), as applicable.

heading: Allowable fecal coliform organisms
paragraph: (3) The median coliform values for 7 consecutive daily tests and any single value test must be less than the values specified in this section.

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph:
97
		  (1) Unless a director gives notice of a maximum seasonal loading rate in respect of the body of water, a discharger must not discharge to the following bodies of water municipal effluent having a total annual average phosphorus content of more than 0.25 mg/L:

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (a) the Okanagan Basin;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (b) the Christina Lake Basin;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (c) the Thompson River at Kamloops;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (d) the Cowichan River;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (e) the Nicola River at Merritt;

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (f) the Cheakamus River at Whistler.

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (2) The annual average phosphorus content must be calculated based on a sampling method and frequency acceptable to a director.

heading: Advanced treatment requirements
paragraph: (3) A person other than a municipality must not discharge into the Okanagan Basin, and a municipality that discharges into the Okanagan Basin must not discharge effluent that has a total nitrogen content of 6 mg/L or more.

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph:
98
		  (1) The terms of reference of an enhanced environmental impact study under this section must be established in consultation with a director.

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (2) Discharge to the Saanich Inlet is under a moratorium, and a discharger must not discharge to the Saanich Inlet unless the discharger first conducts an enhanced environmental impact study as recommended by the Saanich Inlet Study.

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (3) A discharger must not discharge municipal effluent to any of the following areas unless the discharger first conducts an enhanced environmental impact study and a director gives notice that advanced treatment will protect the receiving environment:

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (a) lakes having a surface area of less than 100 ha;

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (b) waters within

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (i)  the Southern Interior Region,

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (ii)  the Interior Douglas Fir Biogeoclimatic Zone,

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (iii)  the Ponderosa Pine Biogeoclimatic Zone,

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (iv)  the Montane Spruce Biogeoclimatic Zone, or

heading: Enhanced environmental impact study needed
paragraph: (v)  the Bunchgrass Biogeoclimatic Zone.

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph:
99
		  (1) A qualified professional must design an outfall such that

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (a) initial dilution zone requirements under this regulation are met,

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (b) air entrapment is prevented,

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (c) adequate weighting is provided to prevent movement from currents, ice or possible entrainment of air, and

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (d) the outfall is protected from corrosion.

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (2) A qualified professional must ensure that outfall diffusers are

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (a) located at a sufficient depth to maximize the frequency that municipal effluent is trapped below the surface of the water,

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (b) located to intercept the predominant current and avoid small currents that tend to move toward the shore,

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (c) designed to ensure that

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (i)  each diffuser section will provide at least 10:1 dilution within the initial dilution zone, and

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (ii)  outside the initial dilution zone, discharge does not cause water quality parameters to fail to meet water quality guidelines, and

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (d) designed to achieve maximum dilution in a river, stream or estuary located in the channel in which most of the water flows.

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (3) A qualified professional must ensure that outfalls are located

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (a) such that they are protected from wave, boat and marine activity, and

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (b) at a depth of at least

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (i)  40 m below mean low water in the Okanagan Basin, and

heading: Outfall requirements
paragraph: (ii)  subject to subparagraph (i), 10 m below mean low water in estuaries, lakes or marine waters with a surface area greater than 100 ha.

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph:
100
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph: "D1" means the depth (m) of the shallowest diffuser port below mean low water;

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph: "D2" means the distance (m) to the closest port of the diffuser from mean low water.

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph: (2) A qualified professional must ensure that outfalls to estuaries, lakes or marine waters with a surface area greater than 100 ha meet the following depth, flow and distance requirements:

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph: (a) D1 must be at least 10 m and D2 must be at least 30 m;

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph: (b) subject to paragraph (a), for discharges of less than 5 000 m3/d, the calculated critical flow must be greater than or equal to the maximum daily flow (m3/d), with the calculated critical flow being the greater positive value of

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph: (c) subject to paragraph (a), for discharges equal to or more than 5 000 m3/d, D1 and D2 must be determined by an environmental impact study and computer modelling of the discharge.

heading: Additional outfall requirements for estuaries, lakes and marine waters
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2) (b), if an outfall has a diffuser, the terminus of the outfall is the closest and shallowest port.

heading: Marking of outfalls
paragraph:
101
		  A discharger must ensure that all outfalls are marked on shore with a sign that meets the following requirements:

heading: Marking of outfalls
paragraph: (a) the sign must indicate, with wording acceptable to a director, the length and depth of the outfall;

heading: Marking of outfalls
paragraph: (b) the sign must be at least 1 m2;

heading: Marking of outfalls
paragraph: (c) the colours of the lettering and the background of the sign must contrast sufficiently with each other, and the sign must be located, such that the wording is clearly visible from both land and water.

heading: Inspection of outfalls
paragraph:
102
		  (1) To ensure the outfall is operating as designed, a discharger must have each outfall associated with a discharge inspected by a qualified person

heading: Inspection of outfalls
paragraph: (a) once every 5 years, or

heading: Inspection of outfalls
paragraph: (b) at a frequency specified in a notice given by a director.

heading: Inspection of outfalls
paragraph: (2) An inspection must include examination of the entire length of the pipe and diffuser for leaks, breaks and blockages.

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to water
paragraph:
103
		  (1) A discharger must monitor the applicable municipal effluent quality and quantity in accordance with this section and Table 12.

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to water
paragraph: (2) In respect of discharging to open marine waters that have a maximum daily flow of less than 10 m3/d, monitoring of CBOD5, TSS and fecal coliforms is not required.

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to water
paragraph: (3) A discharger must submit to a director data gathered under this section,

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to water
paragraph: (a) in respect of discharges having a maximum daily flow range of less than 50 000 m3/d, twice each year, and

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to water
paragraph: (b) in respect of discharges having a maximum daily flow range of 50 000 m3/d or more, quarterly.

heading: Monitoring requirements for discharges to water
paragraph: Table 12 - Monitoring Requirements

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph:
104
		  (1) For the purposes of this Part, uses of reclaimed water are categorized as follows:

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) indirect potable reuse, being any use of reclaimed water to replenish a potential potable water source;

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) greater exposure potential, being uses for which public contact is likely or that present a risk to the receiving environment;

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (c) moderate exposure potential, being uses

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (i)  for which public contact is likely minimal,

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (ii)  for which public access to the reclaimed water is restricted and users are educated as to the risks posed by the use of the reclaimed water, or

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (iii)  that present a moderate risk to the receiving environment;

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (d) lower exposure potential, being uses

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (i)  for which public access to the reclaimed water is restricted and users are not likely to have contact with the reclaimed water,

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (ii)  that are commercial or industrial in nature and users are educated as to the risks posed by the use of the reclaimed water, or

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (iii)  that present a low risk to the receiving environment.

heading: Categories of reclaimed water
paragraph: (2) Categories of reclaimed water are determined based on the point of distribution or use.

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph:
105
		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), a person must not provide reclaimed water unless the person

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) gives written notice to a health officer, at least 60 days before registering under Division 2 [Registration] of Part 2, of the proposed use of the reclaimed water, and

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) receives authorization under subsection (2) (b).

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (2) Within 60 days of receiving notice under subsection (1), a health officer may, in writing,

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) prohibit the person from providing reclaimed water for the proposed use, or

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) authorize the person to provide reclaimed water for the proposed use, subject to the conditions specified by the health officer.

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (3) A person may provide reclaimed water without the notice or authorization referred to in subsection (1) if

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) use of the reclaimed water is specifically authorized under a local service area bylaw, and

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) under the bylaw, the municipality or a person under contract to the municipality is responsible for ensuring

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (i)  compliance with this regulation, and

heading: Authorization to provide reclaimed water
paragraph: (ii)  that proper operation and maintenance will occur.

heading: Indirect potable reuse of reclaimed water
paragraph:
106
		  If reclaimed water is to be used for indirect potable reuse, a provider of reclaimed water must

heading: Indirect potable reuse of reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) conduct an enhanced environmental impact study, having terms of reference established in consultation with a director,

heading: Indirect potable reuse of reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) consult with all persons and organizations who may have an interest or duty that may be impacted by the use of the reclaimed water, and

heading: Indirect potable reuse of reclaimed water
paragraph: (c) be authorized by a director to use the reclaimed water for indirect potable reuse.

heading: Initial dilution zones not applicable
paragraph:
107
		  Unless a director provides otherwise under section 8 [director may substitute requirements], initial dilution zones are not applicable to reclaimed water used for

heading: Initial dilution zones not applicable
paragraph: (a) stream augmentation,

heading: Initial dilution zones not applicable
paragraph: (b) creating impoundments, or

heading: Initial dilution zones not applicable
paragraph: (c) maintaining wetlands or marshes.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph:
108
		  (1) A provider of reclaimed water must meet the applicable municipal effluent quality requirements set out in this section and listed in Table 13.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements for reclaimed water
