paragraph: (2) Turbidity limits under Table 13 must be met before disinfection of the reclaimed water.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of fecal coliform monitoring requirements under Table 13,

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) the median value, as determined from the bacteriological results of the last 5 samples for which analyses have been completed, must not be more than the coliform limits specified in Table 13, and

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) if irrigating food crops that will be eaten raw, Escherichia coli must be monitored daily and be less than 1 CFU/100 mL or 2 MPN/100 mL.

heading: Municipal effluent quality requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: Table 13 - Municipal Effluent Quality Requirements For Reclaimed Water

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph:
109
		  (1) This section applies to municipal effluent quality requirements if the use of reclaimed water is categorized as having greater, moderate or lower exposure potential.

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph: (2) A provider of reclaimed water must ensure that reclaimed water is not used for irrigation, or is not impounded, within 30 m of any water well or in-ground reservoir used for domestic supply unless a director authorizes a lesser distance on the basis that special circumstances exist.

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph: (3) A provider of reclaimed water must ensure that the reclaimed water is not used for irrigation within the 3 days before, and during, the harvesting of crops.

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph: (4) A provider of reclaimed water must ensure that windblown spray will not

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph: (a) go beyond the boundaries of the property to which the reclaimed water is applied, or

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph: (b) reach areas accessible to the public.

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph: (5) A provider of reclaimed water must ensure that the maximum ground surface slope when applying the reclaimed water is not more than 20%.

heading: Additional requirements if exposure potential
paragraph: (6) A provider of reclaimed water must develop information and communication materials related to the use of the reclaimed water, and provide copies annually to all users.

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph:
110
		  (1) This section applies to municipal effluent quality requirements only if the use of reclaimed water is categorized as having greater exposure potential.

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (2) To remove viruses, a provider of reclaimed water must do one or more of the following:

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (a) provide for the chemical addition of a coagulant or polymer, followed by filtration;

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (b) provide for 60-day storage after secondary treatment, if

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (i)  municipal effluent quality requirements are met after storage and treatment,

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (ii)  no short circuiting is occurring or likely to occur, and

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (iii)  no viruses at levels of concern to a health officer are detected in the reclaimed water;

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (c) provide an equivalent form of treatment that is authorized by a director.

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (3) In respect of fecal coliform monitoring,

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (a) based on an initial 60 days of compliance with the daily fecal coliform quality limit, a provider of reclaimed water may conduct weekly fecal coliform testing, and

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (b) if the presence of fecal coliform is detected, daily testing must be reinstated and 7 consecutive non-detect results must be achieved before weekly testing may be resumed.

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (4) If ground discharge is the alternate disposal method and 5 years have elapsed without issue, the constructed drainage pipe length as specified in section 78 [drainage pipe length requirements] may be reduced if

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (a) recommended by a suitably qualified professional, and

heading: Additional requirements if greater exposure potential
paragraph: (b) a director authorizes the reduction.

heading: Additional requirements if moderate exposure potential
paragraph:
111
		  (1) This section applies to municipal effluent quality requirements only if the use of reclaimed water is categorized as having moderate exposure potential.

heading: Additional requirements if moderate exposure potential
paragraph: (2) A provider of reclaimed water must ensure that, if the reclaimed water is used to irrigate commercially processed food crops, the crops undergo chemical or physical processing sufficient to destroy pathogens, including canning, heat treatment, fermentation or pickling, before sale to the public or others.

heading: Additional requirements if moderate exposure potential
paragraph: (3) A provider of reclaimed water must ensure that, if the reclaimed water is used to irrigate livestock grazing fields,

heading: Additional requirements if moderate exposure potential
paragraph: (a) milking animals are prohibited from grazing for 6 days after irrigation ends, and

heading: Additional requirements if moderate exposure potential
paragraph: (b) other livestock are prohibited from grazing for 3 days after irrigation ends, unless the meat is inspected under the Meat Inspection Act (Canada).

heading: Additional requirement if moderate orlow exposure potential
paragraph: 112		  If the use of reclaimed water is categorized as having moderate or low exposure potential, a provider of reclaimed water must

heading: Additional requirement if moderate orlow exposure potential
paragraph: (a) ensure that worker contact with the reclaimed water is minimized, and

heading: Additional requirement if moderate orlow exposure potential
paragraph: (b) provide, if frequent worker contact with the reclaimed water is likely, a higher level of disinfection to a maximum fecal coliform CFU of less than 14/100 mL, or equivalent MPN, based on daily sampling.

heading: Disinfection of reclaimed water
paragraph:
113
		  (1) A provider of reclaimed water must not provide the reclaimed water for use unless it is first disinfected.

heading: Disinfection of reclaimed water
paragraph: (2) Despite section 52 (2) [disinfection and chlorination], a provider of reclaimed water must ensure that, when distributing reclaimed water, the minimal total chlorine residual at the point of use is maintained at 0.5 mg/L unless

heading: Disinfection of reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) the addition of chlorine will detrimentally impact aquatic flora or fauna, or

heading: Disinfection of reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) at the point of use, fecal coliforms remain below the levels set in Table 13 in section 108 [municipal effluent quality requirements for reclaimed water], and users are adequately informed regarding appropriate use of the reclaimed water.

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph:
114
		  (1) A person must not provide or use reclaimed water unless all of the following requirements are met:

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (a) there is an alternate method of disposing of the reclaimed water that meets the requirements of this regulation or is authorized by a director;

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (b) treatment processes are built with the minimum number of components specified in the applicable reliability category for the alternate method of disposal, as described in section 35 [general component and reliability requirements];

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (c) if there is no immediate means of conveyance of the municipal effluent or reclaimed water to the alternate disposal method, the wastewater facility has 48 hours' emergency storage outside the treatment system.

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1) (a), a director may waive the requirement for an alternate method of disposal for reclaimed water that is not generated from residential development or institutional settings if an alternate method is not required to protect public health or the receiving environment and the wastewater facility has

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (a) 48 hours' emergency storage outside the treatment system and the ability to shut down generation of municipal wastewater within 24 hours, or

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (b) a dedicated storage system that is designed to accommodate

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (i)  at least 20 days of design average daily municipal effluent flow at any time,

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (ii)  the maximum anticipated volume of surplus reclaimed water, and

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (iii)  storm or snowmelt events with a less than 5-year return period.

heading: Alternate disposal or storage
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) (a) and (2), if reclaimed water is discharged from a wastewater facility directly into a wetland, a director may waive the requirement for an alternate method of disposal if an alternate method of disposal is not required to protect public health or the receiving environment.

heading: Failure to meet municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph:
115
		  (1) If municipal effluent does not meet municipal effluent quality requirements, a provider of reclaimed water must ensure that the municipal effluent is diverted immediately to

heading: Failure to meet municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (a) an alternate method of disposal, as provided for in section 114 (1) (a) [alternate disposal or storage], or

heading: Failure to meet municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (b) emergency storage or a dedicated storage system, as described in section 114 (1) (c) or (2),

heading: Failure to meet municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: until municipal effluent quality requirements are met and reclaimed water uses may continue.

heading: Failure to meet municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (2) A provider of reclaimed water must identify in the operating plan under section 23 [general requirements of operating plans]

heading: Failure to meet municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (a) the diversion procedures under subsection (1), and

heading: Failure to meet municipal effluent quality requirements
paragraph: (b) the conditions under which the reclaimed water is redirected back to the reclaimed water use.

heading: Use of emergency storage
paragraph:
116
		  If emergency storage as described under section 114 [alternate disposal or storage], is used, a provider of reclaimed water must ensure that the wastewater facility

heading: Use of emergency storage
paragraph: (a) immediately begins conveyance of municipal effluent or the reclaimed water to an alternate disposal method before emergency storage capacity is reached, or

heading: Use of emergency storage
paragraph: (b) stops generating municipal wastewater within 24 hours.

heading: Distribution of reclaimed water
paragraph:
117
		  (1) In this section, "dual distribution system" means a water distribution system that distributes both potable and non-potable water to the same service area.

heading: Distribution of reclaimed water
paragraph: (2) A provider of reclaimed water must not use a dual distribution system to convey reclaimed water unless the system has design, construction, maintenance and inspection safeguards to prevent cross connections.

heading: Distribution of reclaimed water
paragraph: (3) A person must not operate or maintain a reclaimed water distribution system unless the person is certified in cross connection control inspections, conducted for the purposes of controlling and protecting potable water systems against contamination from unprotected cross connections.

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph:
118
		  (1) A provider of reclaimed water must monitor the applicable discharge quality and quantity in accordance with this section and Table 14.

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (2) A provider of reclaimed water must monitor groundwater levels and water flows to ensure that reclaimed water use, or an alternate method of discharge, is managed to avoid adverse effects.

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (3) A provider of reclaimed water must submit reports as follows:

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (a) for reclaimed water categorized as having indirect potable use, weekly;

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (b) for reclaimed water categorized as having greater exposure potential, monthly;

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (c) for reclaimed water categorized as having moderate or lower exposure potential, quarterly.

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), a director may authorize reports to be submitted less often than is required under that subsection.

heading: Monitoring requirements for reclaimed water
paragraph: Table 14 - Monitoring Requirements For Reclaimed Water

heading: Continuous monitoring system
paragraph:
119
		  A provider of reclaimed water categorized as having indirect potable use or greater exposure potential must install a continuous monitoring system.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
120
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of sections 23, 32, 33, 40, 45 (a), (b) or (c), 47, 48, 50 (1) or (2), 53, 63, 67 (c), 105 (1) or 117 (2) or (3) commits an offence.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if the person, with intent to mislead,

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) submits false monitoring data,

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) fails to retain monitoring data under section 63 (d) or (e) [information and records to be retained],

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (c) makes a false report, or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (d) fails to submit a report under section 66 (1) [reports respecting discharge to ground and water], or a report containing the information required under section 66 (2) (a) or (3) (c).

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (3) A person who commits an offence as described in subsection (1) or (2) is liable to a penalty not exceeding $200 000.

heading: Transition - registrations under the Municipal Sewage Regulation
paragraph: (2) A person deemed to be registered under subsection (1) of this section must, subject to the exercise of the director's discretion under the Act and this regulation,

heading: Transition - registrations under the Municipal Sewage Regulation
paragraph: (a) provide all information required under Division 2 of Part 2 and comply with all applicable requirements under Part 2 within one year of this section coming into force, and

heading: Transition - registrations under the Municipal Sewage Regulation
paragraph: (b) comply with all applicable requirements in Parts 3 to 7.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the National Historic Parks General Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: archaeological site means any site or area containing historical resources buried or partially buried on land, resting on the surface of land or submerged or partially submerged beneath the surface of any watercourse or body of water in a Park; (site archeologique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Director means the Director of a Region of Parks Canada, Department of the Environment; (directeur)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: diver's marker means a floating device that incorporates a marker in the form of a red square flag with a white diagonal stripe extending from the head of the hoist; (indicateur de plongee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: explosive means any substance or device other than a firearm made, manufactured or used to produce a violent effect by explosion or pyrotechnic effect; (explosif)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fauna means all vertebrates or invertebrates, living or dead, or parts thereof and includes the eggs or young of fauna but does not include the fossil remains of any fauna; (faune)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fireplace means a grill or stove or other such device designed for the kindling or maintenance of fire; (foyer)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: flora means any plant matter, living or dead, and includes fungi and moulds but does not include the fossil remains of any flora; (flore)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: historical object means any historical resource of a movable nature and includes any specimen, artifact, document or work of art, or any reproduction thereof; (objet historique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: historical resource means any work of nature or of man that is primarily of interest for its palaeontological, prehistorical, historical, cultural, natural, scientific or aesthetic value including, but not limited to, a palaeontological, prehistorical, historical or natural site, structure or object or any remains, restoration or reconstruction thereof; (ressource historique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: kindle means to start, or attempt to start, a fire; (allumer)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: maintain means, with respect to a fire, to add fuel to enjoy the use of, or allow to burn; (alimenter)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment; (ministre)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: moor means to make fast or tie up a watercraft to a wharf or to another watercraft or to use a space or stall at a wharf and includes to dock, beach, store or anchor a watercraft; (amarrer)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: natural object means any natural material, soil, sand, gravel, rock, mineral or other object or natural phenomenon not included within the terms flora and fauna that is located within a Park, but does not include the fossil remains of any flora or fauna; (objet naturel)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Park means any area set apart as a National Historic Park in accordance with Part II of the National Parks Act; (parc)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Superintendent means the Superintendent of a Park; (directeur du parc)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: vessel includes any boat, canoe, raft, amphibious vehicle or any other structure or device, other than a seaplane, used or capable of being used for transportation on water; (bateau)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: wharf means any wharf, dock, pier, jetty, quay, landing, breakwater, mole or sea-wall or any floating structure or device that may be used to moor watercraft. (quai)

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 3 (1) No person shall disturb, remove, deface, damage or destroy any archaeological site or historical resource in a Park.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), a Director may issue a permit to any person authorizing the person to remove historical resources from a Park for management of the Park or scientific purposes or for the purpose of public display.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 4 (1) No person shall remove, deface, damage or destroy flora, fauna or natural objects in a Park.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), a Superintendent may issue a permit to any person authorizing the person to remove, deface, damage or destroy flora, fauna or natural objects in a Park for management of the Park or scientific purposes.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (3) A permit issued by the Superintendent under subsection (2) shall specify the kind and amount of, and the location from which, flora, fauna or natural objects may be removed, defaced, damaged or destroyed, and any other conditions applicable to the permit.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 5 No person shall remove, deface, damage or destroy any public building, fence or other structure in a Park or any signboard, sign or notice placed, posted or erected in a Park.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 6 No person shall deposit any snow, leaves, rubbish or other matter in a Park except in such places, at such times and under such conditions as may be specified by the Superintendent.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 7 No person shall pollute any watercourse in a Park.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 8 Subject to sections 9 to 11, no person shall obstruct, divert or otherwise interfere with any watercourse.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 9 The Superintendent of a Park may permit the taking of water from any watercourse or water supply system in the Park to a place outside the Park in the case of drought, fire, contamination of a water supply or other emergency.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 10 A Director may issue a permit to any person, for a period not exceeding 10 years, authorizing the person to take water for domestic or business water supply purposes within a Park from any watercourse, well or water supply system in the Park.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 11 (1) The Minister may enter into an agreement with a municipality or water district adjacent to a Park for the supply of water from the Park.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (2) The Minister may enter into an agreement with persons residing on land adjacent to a Park for the supply of water from the Park for domestic purposes and for use in establishments providing tourist accommodation.

heading: Restricted Areas and Activities
paragraph: 12 (1) The Superintendent of a Park shall designate any activity or area in the Park as restricted if it is necessary for the preservation, control or management of the Park.

heading: Restricted Areas and Activities
paragraph: (2) Where the Superintendent of a Park designates any activity or area as restricted pursuant to subsection (1), he or she shall so inform the public by the posting, at all information offices or centres located in the Park, of notices describing the activity and of maps showing the area.

heading: Restricted Areas and Activities
paragraph: (3) The Superintendent of a Park may, on application to him or her by any person, authorize that person to engage in an activity in the Park or to enter an area of the Park that has been designated as restricted pursuant to subsection (1) on such terms and conditions as the Superintendent may prescribe.

heading: Restricted Areas and Activities
paragraph: (4) The Superintendent of a Park may suspend or cancel any authorization issued under subsection (3) if it is necessary to do so for the preservation, control or management of a Park.

heading: Restricted Areas and Activities
paragraph: (5) No person shall engage in an activity or enter an area that has been designated as restricted pursuant to subsection (1) except in accordance with the terms and conditions prescribed by the Superintendent.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: 13 (1) In this section,

heading: Authorization
paragraph: authorization means a pass, licence, ticket or other form of permission, issued pursuant to subsection (4) in respect of a designated activity, authorizing the holder to carry on the designated activity; (autorisation)

heading: Authorization
paragraph: designated activity means any activity in a Park, including travel, entry into an area of the Park and the use of any facility in the Park, that is designated pursuant to subsection (2). (activite designee)

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (2) The Superintendent may, for the proper management of the Park, designate any activity, other than an activity referred to in section 12, that may be carried on only by the holder of an authorization issued in respect of that activity.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (3) The Superintendent shall post a list of designated activities and their description at information offices or centers located in the Park or at the entrances to the Park.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (4) The Superintendent shall, on request, issue an authorization in respect of a designated activity if the designated activity will not result in

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (a) any significant adverse effects on the natural and cultural resources of the Park;

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (b) any adverse effects on the safety and health of persons using the Park;

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (c) any significant adverse effects on the enjoyment of persons using the Park; or

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (d) any significant adverse effects on the preservation, control and management of the Park.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (4.1) The Superintendent shall set in the authorization any terms and conditions that are necessary for the preservation, control and management of the Park or for the safety of the public.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (5) No person shall carry on a designated activity unless the person is the holder of an authorization issued in respect of that designated activity.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (6) The holder of an authorization shall, at the request of the Superintendent or a warden or other officer of the Park, produce the authorization for inspection.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (7) The Superintendent may

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (a) suspend an authorization, where the holder fails to comply with any prescribed term or condition of it;

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (b) reinstate any authorization suspended pursuant to paragraph (a), where the failure referred to in that paragraph has been remedied; and

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (c) revoke an authorization, where the holder is convicted of a contravention of these Regulations.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: 14 (1) If a nuisance exists on any premises in a Park, the Superintendent of the Park is authorized to order the owner, lessee, licensee or occupier of the premises to abate the nuisance and, if necessary, to clean up the premises.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (2) Where the owner, lessee, licensee or occupier of any premises where a nuisance exists fails, after reasonable notice from the Superintendent, to abate the nuisance and, where necessary, clean up the premises, the Superintendent may take such steps as are necessary to abate the nuisance and clean up the premises.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 15 (1) It is prohibited, without a permit issued for this purpose, for any person to use, occupy, reside or camp on any land in a Park or erect or use any structure in a Park or park any vehicle in a Park for the purpose of camping.

heading: Camping
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section prevents a person from using the facilities provided in a public picnic ground for the preparation and consumption of meals.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 16 (1) Subject to these Regulations, on receipt of an application, the Superintendent may issue a camping permit to the applicant for the use of an area for such period and under such conditions as the Superintendent specifies in the permit.

heading: Camping
paragraph: (2) The Superintendent shall cancel a camping permit issued under subsection (1) if it is necessary for the preservation, control or management of the Park or for the safety of the public.

heading: Camping
paragraph: (3) No person who holds a camping permit is eligible to apply for another camping permit for the period or any part of the period for which their camping permit is valid.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 17 No person shall, for valuable consideration or for gain, permit another person to use, occupy, reside on or camp on any land in a Park or erect or use any structure in a Park or park any vehicle thereon for any purpose whatever.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 18 (1) A camping permit is not transferable and is valid only during such period as the area to which the permit applies is occupied by the holder thereof.

heading: Camping
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1) and paragraph 21(a), an area to which a camping permit applies is deemed not to be occupied where a tent or trailer or similar device has been unoccupied for a period exceeding 24 hours or has been removed from the area for a period exceeding 24 hours.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 19 A camping permit expires on the expiry date specified thereon.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 20 The holder of a camping permit shall, at all times, maintain the area to which the permit applies in a satisfactory condition.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 21 The Superintendent is authorized to cancel a camping permit if

heading: Camping
paragraph: (a) the area to which the permit applies is not occupied;

heading: Camping
paragraph: (b) the holder of the permit fails to maintain the area to which the permit applies in a satisfactory condition;

heading: Camping
paragraph: (c) the holder of the permit has furnished the Superintendent with false or misleading information in order to secure the permit or maintain it in force; or

heading: Camping
paragraph: (d) the holder of the permit fails to comply with

heading: Camping
paragraph: (i) the conditions of the permit, or

heading: Camping
paragraph: (ii) a directive, instruction or order of the Superintendent made pursuant to these Regulations or to any other Regulations that apply in the Park.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 22 Where a camping permit has been cancelled, the Superintendent shall give notice of the cancellation to the holder of the permit by mailing a copy of the notice to the holder or by posting a copy of the notice of cancellation in the vicinity of the entrance to any structure or vehicle used for camping in the area in respect of which the permit was issued, and the cancellation takes effect on the date the notice was so mailed or posted.

heading: Camping
paragraph: 23 (1) The holder of a camping permit shall, before the expiration of the permit or, where the permit is cancelled, on receipt of the notice of cancellation, remove from the area in respect of which the permit was issued, any trailer or other vehicle or any structure, chattel or article that the holder placed in that area.

heading: Camping
paragraph: (2) The Superintendent may remove any trailer or other vehicle or any structure, chattel or article left in a Park in violation of subsection (1).

heading: Fires
paragraph: 24 No person shall, in a Park, kindle or maintain any fire except

heading: Fires
paragraph: (a) in a fireplace provided by the Superintendent;

heading: Fires
paragraph: (b) in a portable stove burning fuel other than wood or charcoal; or

heading: Fires
paragraph: (c) in a charcoal or gas-fired barbecue.

heading: Fires
paragraph: 25 Notwithstanding section 24, the Superintendent may, by written authorization, permit a person to kindle and maintain a fire and may stipulate the terms and conditions under which the fire shall be kindled and maintained.

heading: Fires
paragraph: 26 No person shall, in a Park, be in possession of more than five gallons of gasoline or other inflammable liquid, unless the gasoline or other inflammable liquid is stored in the tank of a motor vehicle, a motor-driven boat or an aircraft or unless a permit has been obtained for possession of the gasoline or other inflammable liquid.

heading: Fires
paragraph: 27 No person shall, in a Park,

heading: Fires
paragraph: (a) allow a fire to spread beyond the confines of the fireplace, portable stove or barbecue;

heading: Fires
paragraph: (b) discard a lighted cigar, cigarette, match or other burning substance, except in a receptacle provided for that purpose by the Superintendent;

heading: Fires
paragraph: (c) discard any unused match or any article or substance that could cause the kindling of a fire, except in a receptacle provided for that purpose by the Superintendent;

heading: Fires
paragraph: (d) operate any machine or equipment that may cause the kindling of a fire, unless reasonable precautions have been taken;

heading: Fires
paragraph: (e) when removing or disposing of brush or any inflammable material, allow the brush or inflammable material to be accumulated, stored, handled, transported or disposed of in an unreasonable manner; or

heading: Fires
paragraph: (f) leave any fire unattended.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: 28 (1) Subject to subsection (4), no person shall, except in accordance with a permit issued pursuant to subsection (2), have in their possession, store or use any explosive or bring any explosive into a Park.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (2) A Superintendent may issue a permit authorizing a person described in subsection (3) to have in  their possession, store or use any explosive in a Park, where that person is authorized under the Explosives Act to have in their possession, store, use, make, manufacture or sell such an explosive in any other part of Canada.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (3) A permit referred to in subsection (2) may be issued to the following persons:

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (a) a person engaged in construction or demolition work who requires the explosive for their work;

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (b) a person representing an organization retained by written agreement with the Director to present a reenactment of a historic event or other program for the education or entertainment of the public; and

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (c) a person in the employ of Her Majesty in right of Canada whose duties include the presentation of programs for the education or entertainment of the public.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (4) Notwithstanding subsection (1), any person may

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (a) transport explosives through a Park in accordance with the Explosives Act or any provincial regulation respecting explosives; or

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (b) possess flares or fuses for use as safety equipment for motor vehicles, trains or boats in accordance with any federal or provincial requirements.

heading: Aircraft
paragraph: 29 Except as authorized by the Superintendent for the control or management of the Park, no person shall, in a Park, take off or land or deposit persons or objects from any aircraft, sail plane, glider, body kite, hang glider or other device designed or used to carry persons or objects through the air in powerless flight.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: 30 (1) No person shall operate or use, or cause to be operated or used, on or under any watercourse in a Park any type of motorized vessel, water-skiing equipment or subsurface diving equipment unless a sign or notice authorized by the Superintendent permitting such operation or use is posted on or near the watercourse.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), the Superintendent may operate or use, or cause to be operated or used, any vessel or equipment referred to in subsection (1) on or under any watercourse in the Park where such operation or use is necessary for the management of the Park or for the safety of the public.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (3) No person shall drain, dump or discharge any waste or refuse from a vessel into any watercourse in a Park.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: 31 No person shall moor any vessel in the approach to or in the lee of any wharf in a Park in such a manner as to obstruct the free flow of vessels to and from the wharf.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: 32 (1) No person shall moor any vessel at any wharf or area in a Park except in accordance with a traffic control device erected by the Superintendent pursuant to subsection (2).

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (2) The Superintendent may designate any wharf or area in the Park or any portion thereof as a wharf or area where mooring is allowed or where mooring is allowed only

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (a) in accordance with a permit issued by the Superintendent,

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (b) during specified periods of time, or

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (c) for particular types of vessels

heading: Vessels
paragraph: and the Superintendent shall erect a traffic control device at or near the designated wharf or area to indicate such designation.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: 33 (1) No person shall undertake any underwater activities in a Park unless he or she first places a diver's marker in the vicinity of the dive site so that the marker is clearly visible to vessel operators.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: (2) Every person who operates a vessel in the vicinity of a diver's marker referred to in subsection (1) shall proceed with due caution and at a slow speed.

heading: Agreements
paragraph: 34 The Minister may enter into an agreement with a province or any person for the development, operation and maintenance in a Park of telephone, telegraph, natural gas and electrical, other than hydro-electrical, services for use only in the Park.

heading: Advertisements
paragraph: 35 No person shall display or distribute any advertisement or handbill in a Park except under and in accordance with a permit issued by the Superintendent.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 36 (1) No person shall, in a Park,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) cause any excessive noise;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) behave in a manner that unreasonably disturbs other persons in the Park or unreasonably interferes with their enjoyment of the Park;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) carry out any action that unreasonably interferes with fauna or the natural beauty of the Park;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (d) carry out any action that threatens the historic resources in the Park; or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (e) create or cause any nuisance in the Park.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) The Superintendent may remove or have removed from a Park any person who by their disorderly conduct, behaviour or action is in violation of subsection (1).

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) No person who has been removed from a Park under subsection (2) shall enter or attempt to enter that Park for one year following the date of removal unless that person applies for and obtains permission from the Director to enter the Park.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the National Parks General Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the National Parks Act; (version anglaise seulement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: cave means any subterranean cavern or area, either natural or man-made; (cavernes)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: commercial boat means a vessel that carries persons or cargo for hire or reward and includes a vessel chartered or hired for pleasure purposes by or on behalf of the persons carried on the vessel. (bateau commercial)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: explosive means gunpowder, blasting powder, nitroglycerine, gun-cotton, dynamite, blasting gelatine, gelignite, fulminates of mercury or other metals, coloured fires and every other substance made, manufactured or used to produce a violent effect by explosion or a pyrotechnic effect and includes fuses, fireworks, rockets, percussion caps, detonators, cartridges, ammunition of all descriptions, railway track torpedoes, fusees and other signals and every other adaptation or preparation of any such substance; (explosifs)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: flora means any plant matter, living or dead, and includes fungi and moulds; (version anglaise seulement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: moor means to make fast or tie up a watercraft to a wharf or to another watercraft or to use a space or stall at a wharf and includes to dock, beach, store or anchor a watercraft; (amarrage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: natural object means any natural material, soil, sand, gravel, rock, mineral, fossil or other object of natural phenomenon not included within the terms flora and fauna that is located within a Park; (matieres naturelles)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: public recreational facilities means a lawn bowling green, golf course, swimming pool and assembly hall in a park; (installation recreative publique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: watercourse means any river, stream, brook, lake, pond, creek or other flowing or standing water in a Park; (version anglaise seulement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: watercraft means any boat, canoe, raft, amphibious craft or other type or class of vessel; (embarcation)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: wharf means any wharf, dock, pier, jetty, quay, landing, breakwater, mole or sea-wall or any floating structure or device that may be used to moor watercraft. (quais)

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.1 Sections 28 to 35, 37 and 39 do not apply in the Town of Banff.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.2 Subsections 5(1) and (2), sections 29 to 31, paragraphs 32(1)(a) and (b) and sections 33 to 35, 37 and 39 do not apply in the Town of Jasper.

heading: Use of Public Lands or other Public Property Within a Park
paragraph: 3 A person may use or occupy public lands or other public property within a Park if that person does so in accordance with the Act, the regulations made thereunder and any agreement made between the Government of Canada and the government of the province within which the Park is situated.

heading: Use of Public Lands or other Public Property Within a Park
paragraph: 4 The Minister may, from time to time, arrange to have public lands in a Park surveyed or resurveyed

heading: Use of Public Lands or other Public Property Within a Park
paragraph: (a) into lots in townsites or other subdivisions;

heading: Use of Public Lands or other Public Property Within a Park
paragraph: (b) for any right-of-way of the type referred to in subsection 6(2) of the Act;

heading: Use of Public Lands or other Public Property Within a Park
paragraph: (c) for the purposes of schools, hospitals, churches and the entertainment of persons visiting the Park; and

heading: Use of Public Lands or other Public Property Within a Park
paragraph: (d) for the purposes of a cemetery.

heading: Public Recreational Facilities
paragraph: 5 (1) The superintendent may, by posting notices on or in the immediate vicinity of public recreational facilities, fix the days and the hours of the day during which such facilities shall be open to the public.

heading: Public Recreational Facilities
paragraph: (2) Except with the permission of the superintendent, no person shall enter on or use public recreational facilities when they are closed to the public.

heading: Public Recreational Facilities
paragraph: (5) In Georgian Bay Islands National Park and St. Lawrence Islands National Park, no person shall use firewood supplied by the superintendent unless that person is issued a camping permit pursuant to the National Parks Camping Regulations or is issued a firewood permit.

heading: Public Recreational Facilities
paragraph: (6) In Georgian Bay Islands National Park and St. Lawrence Islands National Park, a shower permit, a firewood permit and a mooring permit may be obtained at designated self-registration sites.

heading: Hazardous Activities
paragraph: 6 (1) The superintendent may require any person to register at the office of the superintendent or at such other place as may be specified by the superintendent prior to and on completing, in a Park, any activity that, in the opinion of the superintendent, may present a hazard to the person.

heading: Hazardous Activities
paragraph: (2) The superintendent shall designate any activity in respect of which registration is required pursuant to subsection (1) by posting notices at the office of the superintendent, at all information offices or centres located in a Park and at any place specified by the superintendent pursuant to subsection (1).

heading: Hazardous Activities
paragraph: (3) No person shall, in a Park, undertake any activity designated by the superintendent pursuant to subsection (2) without registering as required by the superintendent

heading: Hazardous Activities
paragraph: (a) prior to undertaking any such activity; and

heading: Hazardous Activities
paragraph: (b) immediately on completing or returning from such activity.

heading: Hazardous Activities
paragraph: (4) Where an activity has not been designated by the superintendent pursuant to subsection (2), a person who wishes to do so may, prior to undertaking that activity, register at the office of the superintendent or at such other place as may be specified by the superintendent, on condition that the person register again immediately on completing or returning from that activity.

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: 7 (1) The superintendent may, where it is necessary for the proper management of the Park to do so, designate certain activities, uses or entry and travel in areas in a Park as restricted or prohibited.

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (2) Notice of a restriction or prohibition referred to in subsection (1) shall be posted by the superintendent at park warden offices and information bureaus in the Park or at entrances to the Park.

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (3) A notice posted in accordance with subsection (2) shall include

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (a) a description of the activity or use to which the restriction or prohibition applies;

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (b) the extent of restriction, where an activity or use is being restricted;

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (c) a description of the area to which the restriction or prohibition of entry or travel in that area applies; and

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (d) a map of the area in which the restriction or prohibition, applies, where that area is not the total area of the Park.

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (4) No person shall engage in an activity or use or enter and travel in an area that has been designated as restricted or prohibited pursuant to subsection (1) otherwise than in accordance with the terms and conditions prescribed in a permit issued under subsection (5).

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (5) The superintendent may, on application to him by any person, in respect of any activity or use restricted or prohibited pursuant to subsection (1) or any entry and travel in an area that has been restricted or prohibited, pursuant to that subsection, issue to that person a permit to

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (a) engage in that activity or use, or

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (b) enter and travel in that area

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: on such terms and conditions as the superintendent may prescribe in the permit.

heading: Restricted and Prohibited Activities, Uses and Travel
paragraph: (6) The superintendent may, if it is necessary for the preservation, control and management of the Park, suspend or revoke a permit issued under subsection (5).

heading: Authorization
paragraph: 7.1 (1) In this section,

heading: Authorization
paragraph: authorization means a pass, licence, ticket or other form of permission authorizing the holder to carry on any designated activity; (autorisation)

heading: Authorization
paragraph: designated activity means any activity in a park, including travel, entry in an area of a park and the use of any facility in a park, that is designated in accordance with subsection (2). (activite designee)

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (2) The superintendent may, where it is necessary for the proper management of the park, designate the activities other than those referred to in section 7 that may be carried on only by the holder of an authorization for that purpose.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (3) The superintendent shall post a list of designated activities and their description in the park warden offices and information bureaus in the park or at the entrances to the park.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (4) No person other than the holder of an authorization issued for that purpose in accordance with this section shall engage in a designated activity.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (5) The superintendent may, on request, issue an authorization and may prescribe terms and conditions in any such authorization, taking into account

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (a) the natural and cultural resources of the park;

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (b) the safety, health and enjoyment of persons visiting or residing in the park; and

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (c) the preservation, control and management of the park.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (6) The holder of an authorization shall, at the request of the superintendent or a park warden or other park officer, produce the authorization for inspection.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (7) The superintendent may

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (a) suspend an authorization, where the holder of it fails to comply with any prescribed term or condition;

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (b) reinstate the authorization, when the failure referred to in paragraph (a) has been remedied; and

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (c) revoke an authorization, where the holder of it is convicted of a contravention of these Regulations.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: 8 Except where it is indicated by a notice posted by the superintendent at the entrance to a cave that entry therein is permitted, no person shall enter any cave in a Park without the permission, in writing, of the superintendent.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 10 No person shall remove, deface, damage or destroy any flora or natural objects in a Park, other than in accordance with a permit issued under subsection 11(1) or 12(1) or an authorization or permit issued under the National Parks of Canada Land Use Planning Regulations.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 11 (1) The superintendent is authorized, on application, to issue a permit authorizing the permit holder to take flora or natural objects for scientific purposes from a park, or for the removal and use of natural objects for construction purposes within a park, if the applicant demonstrates in writing that the performance of those activities will not

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (a) have a significant adverse environmental impact on the park and its natural resources;

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (b) jeopardize any cultural, historical and archaeological resources; and

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (c) pose a danger to public health or public safety.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (2) The permit shall specify the kind and amount of and the location from which flora or natural objects may be removed and set out the terms and conditions.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (3) Where natural objects are removed for the purpose of constructing other than a public work within a Park, every person on removal of such natural objects shall pay to the superintendent the sum of 25 cents for each cubic yard of such natural objects or fraction thereof.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 12 (1) The superintendent may issue a permit to any person authorizing the person to remove, deface, damage or destroy any flora or natural objects in a Park for purposes of Park management.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (2) A permit issued by the superintendent under subsection (1) shall specify the kind and amount of and the location from which flora or natural objects may be removed, defaced, damaged or destroyed and the conditions applicable to the permit.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 13 No person shall remove, deface, damage or destroy any signboard, sign or notice placed, posted or erected in a Park by the superintendent, or any public building, fence or other structure in a Park.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: 14 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall wilfully remove, deface, damage or destroy any prehistoric or historic artifacts or structures in a Park.

heading: Preservation of Property
paragraph: (2) A superintendent may issue a permit to any person authorizing that person to remove specimens of prehistoric or historic artifacts or structures from a Park for the purpose of public display in a museum.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 16 No person shall pollute any watercourse.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 17 No person shall obstruct or divert, by means of a pipe or otherwise, any watercourse, except as authorized by a permit issued by a superintendent.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 18 (1) A superintendent may issue a permit to any person for a period not exceeding 10 years authorizing the person to take water for domestic, business or railway water supply purposes within a Park from

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (a) any watercourse;

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (b) any Park well; or

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (c) any Park water supply system other than a waterworks system for a townsite or subdivision.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1), a superintendent shall not issue a permit to any person to take water unless the person submits to the superintendent

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (a) a statement specifying the purpose for which the water is required;

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (b) a description of the method to be used to take the water;

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (c) a statement specifying the location of any equipment to be installed in taking the water;

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (d) a document setting out the results of a water quality test that show that the quality of the water to be taken is suitable for the purpose for which it is required; and

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (e) a description of any impairment to the resources of the Park that may result from the installation of the equipment referred to in paragraph (c).

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (3) The superintendent shall revoke a permit issued under subsection (1) if its holder is convicted of a contravention of these Regulations.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (4) On the expiry or revocation of a permit issued under subsection (1), the person who was issued that permit shall immediately remove any equipment installed in taking the water and restore the site of the equipment to the extent possible to its original state.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 19 The superintendent may permit the temporary taking of water from any watercourse or Park water supply system to a place outside the Park in the case of drought, fire, contamination of a water supply or other emergency, for the duration of such emergency.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: 20 (1) The Minister may enter into an agreement with a municipality or water district adjacent to a Park for the supply of water from the Park.

heading: Use of Water Resources
paragraph: (2) The Minister may enter into an agreement with persons residing on land adjacent to a Park for the supply of water from the Park for domestic purposes and for use in establishments providing tourist accommodation.

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: 21 The use on a watercourse of any type of motorized watercraft, water-skiing equipment or sub-surface diving equipment is prohibited except as permitted by a sign or notice placed, posted or erected by the superintendent at or near the watercourse.

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: (2) No person shall use on a watercourse a watercraft that contains washroom facilities unless that watercraft is equipped with a holding tank and a pumping system.

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: 23 No person shall moor any watercraft in the approach to or in the lee of any wharf in such a manner as to obstruct the free flow of water traffic to and from such wharf.

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: 24 (1) The superintendent may erect lettered or symbolic signs or devices designating a wharf or other location in a Park as requiring a mooring permit.

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: (2) No person shall moor a watercraft at a wharf or other location designated pursuant to subsection (1) without a mooring permit issued by the superintendent or obtained in the manner described in subsection 5(7).

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: 25 (1) The superintendent may erect signs or devices at a stall or space in or alongside a wharf, or at any other location designated pursuant to subsection 24(1), reserving the stall, space or location for use by a type or class of watercraft and for the period set out on the signs or devices.

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: (2) Where a stall or space or other location is reserved for a particular type or class of watercraft for a period of time, no person shall moor any watercraft of another type or class in that stall, space or location during that period.

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: 26 (1) The superintendent may erect signs or devices specifying the period of time during which any watercraft may be moored at any wharf or at any other location designated pursuant to subsection 24(1).

heading: Watercraft and Aquatic Sports
paragraph: (2) No person shall moor a watercraft at a wharf or other location for a period longer than that specified by the superintendent pursuant to subsection (1).

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: 27 (1) Where, in the opinion of the superintendent or of a Park Medical Officer or a medical or sanitary inspector, a nuisance exists on any premises in a Park, the superintendent may order the owner, lessee, licencee or any other occupier of the premises to abate the nuisance and cleanse the premises.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (2) Where the owner, lessee, licencee or any other occupier of any premises where a nuisance exists fails, after reasonable notice from the superintendent, to abate the nuisance and cleanse the premises, the superintendent may take such steps as are necessary to abate the nuisance and to cleanse the premises.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (3) The owner, lessee, licencee or other occupier of the premises shall pay the costs of abating the nuisance and cleansing any premises referred to in subsection (2) that are incurred by the superintendent.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: 28 No person shall deposit any snow, leaves, rubbish or any matter of an offensive nature in a Park except in such places, at such times and under such conditions as the superintendent specifies.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: 29 (1) No earth-pit privy, out-closet or privy vault shall be erected or used in any townsite or subdivision in a Park in which a water and sewer system has been installed.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (2) All earth-pit privies, out-closets or privy vaults on property that is not capable of being serviced by a Park water and sewer system shall be designed, located and maintained in accordance with standards approved by the superintendent.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: 30 (1) All buildings in a Park used for the purpose of residence, business or tourist accommodation shall have a plumbing system including an adequate supply of potable water and suitable sanitary fixtures, except that such buildings in outlying areas not serviced by a Park water supply and sewer system shall have sanitary privies, chemical closets or other such conveniences as the superintendent may approve.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (2) Where there is no Park water supply and sewer system in a Park, sewage or water waste shall be drained into a septic tank or other disposal system approved by the superintendent, which shall, where considered necessary by the superintendent, be equipped to chlorinate or otherwise treat the effluent.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: 31 (1) Any person occupying or using a public area in a Park shall

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (a) at all times maintain the area in a satisfactory condition; and

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (b) when vacating the area, restore the area to its natural condition as nearly as possible.

heading: Prevention of Nuisances
paragraph: (2) Where incinerators or trash receptacles are provided in a Park, all refuse, waste paper or other material being discarded shall be placed therein.

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: 32 (1) No person shall, in a Park,

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (a) cause any excessive noise;

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (b) conduct or behave in a manner that unreasonably disturbs other persons in the Park or unreasonably interferes with their enjoyment of the Park; or

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (c) carry out any action that unreasonably interferes with fauna or the natural beauty of the Park.

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (2) The superintendent may remove or have removed from a Park any person who by his disorderly conduct, behaviour or action is in violation of subsection (1).

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (3) No person who has been removed from a Park under subsection (2) shall enter or attempt to enter that Park for one year following the date of removal unless that person applies for and obtains permission from the superintendent to enter the Park.

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: 33 No person shall display or distribute any advertisement or handbill in a Park, except as authorized in writing by the superintendent.

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: 33.1 (1) The superintendent shall, on application, issue a permit authorizing the permit holder to display or distribute any promotional or informational material in a park if it

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (b) does not contravene any Act or regulation that applies in respect of the park; and

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (c) does not promote the contravention of an Act or regulation that applies in respect of the park.

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (2) The superintendent shall set out the following terms and conditions in respect of promotional or informational material in the permit:

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (a) the areas where it may be distributed or displayed;

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (b) the period during which it may be displayed or the date and time at which it may be distributed; and

heading: Prohibited Conduct
paragraph: (c) the permit holder's obligation to take reasonable care to ensure that the material is not littered in the park and that, if it is posted, it is removed immediately after the end of the period identified in the permit.

heading: Cleaning of Sidewalks
paragraph: 34 (1) The owner, lessee, licensee or other occupier of any lot in a townsite in a Park on which residence or the operation of a business is permitted shall remove snow, leaves or other material that has accumulated on any sidewalk bordering the lot in accordance with subsections (2) and (3).

heading: Cleaning of Sidewalks
paragraph: (2) Any snow required to be removed by subsection (1) shall be removed within a period of 12 hours after it has fallen or within such longer period as may be specified by the superintendent.

heading: Cleaning of Sidewalks
paragraph: (3) Any leaves or other material required to be removed by subsection (1) shall be removed whenever such leaves or other material interferes with or endangers pedestrian traffic or creates an obstructive, dangerous or unsightly condition or whenever removal is directed by the superintendent.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: 35 (1) Subject to subsection (4), no person shall, without an appropriate permit issued by the superintendent pursuant to subsection (2), bring into a Park or, in a Park, have in his possession, store, use, sell or offer for sale, any explosive.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (2) The superintendent may, on any conditions that he may prescribe, issue a permit to have in possession, store, use or sell any explosive in a Park to a person described in subsection (3) who is authorized under the Explosives Act to have in possession, store, use, make, manufacture or sell such an explosive in any other part of Canada.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), the following persons are described:

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (a) a person engaged in construction or demolition work who requires the explosive for his work;

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (b) a person representing a fraternal organization, service or other group that is sponsoring recreational or sport activities and requires the explosive in order to present a fireworks display on the occasion of a public holiday or celebration; or

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (c) a person who is licensed under the National Parks Businesses Regulations to sell small arms ammunition.

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (4) Any person may, without obtaining a permit under this section,

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (a) transport any explosive through a Park by railway in a manner authorized by the Railway Act or a regulation or order under that Act;

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (b) transport explosives through a Park in accordance with the Explosives Act or any provincial regulation respecting explosives;

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (c) be in possession of flares or fuses for use as safety equipment for motor vehicles, trains or boats in accordance with any provincial or federal requirements; or

heading: Explosives
paragraph: (d) be in possession of small arms ammunition for his personal use.

heading: Closing of Areas and Ways
paragraph: 36 (1) Where the superintendent deems it necessary for the prevention of any seasonal or temporary danger to persons, flora, fauna or natural objects in a Park, he may by notice in writing close to public use or traffic any area in the Park for the period he considers the danger will continue.

heading: Closing of Areas and Ways
paragraph: (2) A notice referred to in subsection (1) shall be displayed on each approach road, trail or other way of access to the area in the Park closed to public use or traffic.

heading: Closing of Areas and Ways
paragraph: (3) No person shall enter any area in a Park during the period that it is closed to public use or traffic pursuant to subsection (1) except with the permission of the superintendent.

heading: Closing of Areas and Ways
paragraph: 37 Where the Minister is of the opinion that any road, street, sidewalk, trail, wharf, bridge or other way or portion thereof in a Park has been rendered unnecessary for public use or traffic, he may by order close to public use or traffic that way or portion thereof.

heading: Utilities
paragraph: 38 The Minister may enter into an agreement with a province or any person for the development, operation and maintenance in a Park of

heading: Utilities
paragraph: (a) telephone, telegraph, electrical, other than hydro-electrical, and natural gas services for use only in the Park; and

heading: Utilities
paragraph: (b) hydro-electrical power, pursuant to the Dominion Water Power Act, for the use of such power only in the Park.

heading: Miscellaneous
paragraph: 39 No person shall sell any intoxicating beverage in a Park unless he has obtained a licence for such a sale under the National Parks Businesses Regulations and the sale

heading: Miscellaneous
paragraph: (a) is in accordance with the laws of the province in which the Park is situated; and

heading: Miscellaneous
paragraph: (b) has been approved by the superintendent.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Canada National Parks Act; (Loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: angling means fishing with a hook and line held in the hand or with a hook, line and rod held in the hand but does not include fishing with a set line; (peche a la ligne)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: artificial fly means a single or double hook on a common shank, dressed with silk, tinsel, wool, fur, feathers or other material, or any combination thereof, without a spinning device whether attached to the hook or line; (mouche artificielle)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: chemical attractant means a chemical or scented substance that is applied inside or onto a lure in order to attract fish; (attractif chimique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fillet includes any piece of fish from which the internal organs, the head, the fins and the bones, except intramuscular or lateral bones, have been removed; (filet)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fish includes a soft-shell clam (Mya arenaria); (poisson)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fish finder means a sonar device for detecting fish; (detecteur de poissons)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fishing permit means a fishing permit that is issued pursuant to paragraph 4(a); (permis de peche)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: foul hooking means fishing with a hook or hooks attached to a line manipulated in such a manner as to pierce a fish in any part of its body other than its mouth; (hamecon illicite)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: gaff-hook means any hook attached directly to the end of a rod or pole for the purpose of landing a fish or piercing a fish in any part of its body; (gaffeau)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: game fish means any of the species of fish set out in Schedule I; (poisson de sport)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: gang-hook means a combination of two or more hooks used as a unit; (hamecon multiple)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: lake trout endorsement means an endorsement to fish for lake trout in the waters of Prince Albert National Park of Canada, issued pursuant to section 4.1; (autorisation de pecher le touladi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: lead jig means one or more weighted hooks that contain more than 1.0 per cent lead by weight and that are tied to a fishing line and used for catching fish; (turlutte plombee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: lead sinker means an object that contains more than 1.0 per cent lead by weight and that can be used to sink a fishing line by attachment of the object to the fishing line; (lest en plomb)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: natural bait means any material used to attract fish that is partly or wholly composed of plants, animals or plant and animal products, but does not include an artificial fly or a wooden plug; (appat naturel)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: open season, with respect to any species of fish, means the period of each year during which fishing for that species is permitted in any park waters; (saison de peche)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: overall length, with respect to a fish other than a soft-shell clam, means the distance measured from the tip of the nose to the fork of the tail or, if there is no fork, to the tip of the tail and, in respect of a soft-shell clam, means the distance measured in a straight line through the longest part of the shell; (longueur totale)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: possession has the same meaning as in subsection 4(3) of the Criminal Code; (possession)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: salmon licence means a salmon licence that is issued pursuant to paragraph 4(b); (permis de peche du saumon)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: soft-shell clam permit means a permit that is issued for recreational clam fishing under paragraph 4(c); (permis de peche de la mye)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: tailer means a device consisting of a wire, cord or rope arranged on a rod or pole in such a manner as to form a noose or snare for the purpose of landing or catching a fish; (serre-queue)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: year means the 12-month period commencing on April 1st in any calendar year and terminating on March 31st in the calendar year next following. (annee)

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.01 These Regulations apply to parks and, subject to sections 40 and 41 of the Act, to park reserves as if they were parks.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.1 (1) These Regulations do not apply in respect of fishing for commercial purposes for eel, smelt or gaspereau in Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada by persons who

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) in 1967, 1968 or 1969, possessed a commercial fishing licence under the authority of the New Brunswick Fishery Regulations, C.R.C., c. 844, to fish for eel, smelt or gaspereau within the waters of that park; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) in 1979, were registered as commercial fishers under the authority of the New Brunswick Fishery Regulations, C.R.C., c. 844, and fished from the Cap St.-Louis or Loggiecroft wharf areas within that park.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Fishing for commercial purposes for eel, smelt or gaspereau within Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada shall be subject to the requirements of the Fisheries Act and the regulations made under that Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.2 With the exception of paragraphs 15.1(a) and (b), these Regulations do not apply in respect of fishing in the marine portion of Forillon National Park of Canada.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.3 For those parks within the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, these Regulations do not apply to the beneficiaries of the Inuvialuit Final Agreement as approved, given effect and declared valid by the Western Arctic (Inuvialuit) Claims Settlement Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.4 For those parks within the Nunavut Settlement Area, these Regulations do not apply to the beneficiaries of the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement as approved, given effect and declared valid by the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.5 For those parks within the Yukon Territory, south of the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, these Regulations do not apply to the beneficiaries, within their respective traditional territories, of the Champagne and Aishihik First Nations Final Agreement and of the Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation Final Agreement as approved, given effect and declared valid by the Yukon First Nations Land Claims Settlement Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.6 For the Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve of Canada, these Regulations do not apply to people of the Haida Nation to whom the Gwaii Haanas Agreement, authorized by Order in Council P.C. 1992-1591 dated July 16, 1992, applies.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), no person shall fish

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) in any park waters set out in column I of Schedule II unless that person is the holder of a fishing permit;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) for salmon in any waters in Terra Nova National Park of Canada unless that person is the holder of a salmon licence and is in possession of at least one unused salmon tag;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (c) for lake trout in any waters of Prince Albert National Park of Canada unless that person is the holder of a lake trout endorsement and a fishing permit issued pursuant to paragraph 4(a) and is in possession of at least one unused lake trout tag;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (d) for soft-shell clams in any waters in Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada unless that person is the holder of a soft-shell clam permit;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (e) for salmon in any waters in Cape Breton Highlands National Park of Canada unless that person is the holder of a salmon licence; or

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (f) for salmon in any waters in Gros Morne National Park of Canada unless that person is

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (i) the holder of a salmon licence and in possession of at least one unused salmon tag, and

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (ii) the holder of a salmon licence issued under the Wild Life Regulations, Consolidated Newfoundland and Labrador Regulation 1156/96, made under the Wild Life Act, chapter W-8 of the Revised Statutes of Newfoundland, 1990, and in possession of at least one unused salmon tag issued under those Regulations.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (2) Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply to a person under 16 years of age who is accompanied by a person 16 years of age or older who is the holder of a fishing permit.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (3) Paragraph (1)(b) does not apply to a person under 16 years of age who is accompanied by a person 16 years of age or older who is the holder of a salmon licence and is in possession of at least one unused salmon tag.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (4) Paragraph (1)(c) does not apply to a person under 16 years of age who is accompanied by a person 16 years of age or older who is the holder of a lake trout endorsement and is in possession of at least one unused lake trout tag.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (5) Paragraph (1)(d) does not apply to a person under 16 years of age who is accompanied by a person 16 years of age or older who is the holder of a soft-shell clam permit.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (6) Paragraph (1)(e) does not apply to a person under 16 years of age who is accompanied by a person 16 years of age or older who is the holder of a salmon licence.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 4 A superintendent shall, on application by any person and payment by that person of the applicable fee fixed under section 24 of the Parks Canada Agency Act, issue to that person

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) a fishing permit;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) a salmon licence and, where applicable, one salmon tag; or

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (c) a soft-shell clam permit.

heading: Fishing Permits
