paragraph: 4.1 A superintendent shall, on application by any person who holds a fishing permit, issue to that person a lake trout endorsement and a maximum of two lake trout tags.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 5 A fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) is valid for the period in respect of which it is issued; and

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) is valid only when signed by the person to whom it is issued.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 6 Where a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement has been lost, a superintendent shall issue, without charge, a new permit, licence or endorsement, as the case may be, to a person who establishes that the person is the holder of the lost permit, licence or endorsement.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 7 Every person shall, when fishing, carry any fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement issued to that person and shall, on request by a superintendent or park warden, produce the permit, licence or endorsement for examination.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 7.1 (1) Every person who holds a salmon licence and who catches salmon in a park shall, in the manner set out in a notice posted by the superintendent or, where no such notice is posted, in the manner set out in the salmon licence,

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) register their catch of salmon;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) maintain a record of their catch of salmon; and

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (c) submit that record to a park warden.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (2) Every person who registers a catch of salmon pursuant to paragraph (1)(a) shall present the entire salmon at the time of registration.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 7.2 (1) Every person who catches and retains a salmon in Gros Morne or Terra Nova National Park of Canada shall immediately affix a salmon tag to it in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (2) A salmon tag shall be affixed through the gill cavity and mouth of the salmon and securely locked.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (3) No person shall remove a salmon tag from a salmon except at the time the salmon is prepared for consumption.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (4) No person shall be in possession of salmon in Gros Morne or Terra Nova National Park of Canada unless

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) a salmon tag has been affixed to the salmon in accordance with subsection (1); or

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) in the case of salmon caught or taken outside the waters described in subsection (1), the person has possession of the salmon in accordance with the laws of the province within which the park is situated.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (5) No person shall affix a salmon tag issued to the person under paragraph 4(b) to a salmon that is caught by another person unless that other person is a person who is under 16 years of age and referred to in subsection 3(3).

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 7.3 All persons fishing in La Mauricie National Park of Canada shall, in the manner set out in a notice posted by the superintendent at a park wardens' office, a park information booth or a park entrance, register their daily catch.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 7.4 Every person who holds a lake trout endorsement shall, in the manner set out in a notice posted by the superintendent or, where no such notice is posted, in the manner set out in the lake trout endorsement,

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) register their catch of lake trout;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) maintain a record of their catch of lake trout; and

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (c) submit that record to a park warden.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 7.5 (1) Every person who catches and retains a lake trout in Prince Albert National Park of Canada shall immediately affix to it a lake trout tag in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (2) A lake trout tag shall be affixed through the gill cavity and mouth of the lake trout and securely locked.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (3) No person shall remove a lake trout tag from a lake trout except at the time the lake trout is prepared for consumption.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (4) No person shall be in possession of lake trout in Prince Albert National Park of Canada unless

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) in the case of lake trout caught or taken outside Prince Albert National Park of Canada, the person has possession of the lake trout in accordance with the laws of Saskatchewan and has declared possession of the lake trout on entering Prince Albert National Park of Canada in the form provided by the superintendent; and

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) in any other case, a lake trout tag has been affixed to the lake trout in accordance with subsection (1).

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (5) No person shall affix a lake trout tag issued to the person under section 4.1 to a lake trout that is caught by another person unless that other person is a person who is under 16 years of age and referred to in subsection 3(4).

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 7.6 (1) Every person who holds a soft-shell clam permit and who catches soft-shell clams in Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada shall, in the manner set out in a notice posted by the superintendent or, where no such notice is posted, in the manner set out in the permit

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) register their catch of soft-shell clams;

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) maintain a record of their catch of soft-shell clams; and

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (c) submit the record to a park warden.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (2) The superintendent shall, in determining the manner in which the responsibilities referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) to (c) are fulfilled, take into account the park's natural and cultural resources and the preservation, control and management of the park.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: 8 (1) A superintendent or park warden who has reasonable grounds to believe that a person who is the holder of a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement has violated these Regulations may suspend and take possession of the fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement, as the case may be, held by that person.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (2) Where a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement has been suspended pursuant to subsection (1), the suspension shall be cancelled and the fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement shall be revalidated and returned to the person to whom it was issued

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (a) after the expiration of 30 days from the date of the suspension unless before that time proceedings have been instituted in respect of the alleged violation for which the fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement was suspended; or

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (b) after that person is acquitted of the alleged violation for which the fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement was suspended.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (3) Where a person who is the holder of a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement has been convicted of a violation of these Regulations, any fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement held by that person shall be cancelled.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (4) Where a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement has been suspended pursuant to subsection (1), the person to whom it was issued shall not obtain or be in possession of any other of those documents at any time during the period of suspension.

heading: Fishing Permits
paragraph: (5) Where a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement is cancelled pursuant to subsection (3), the person to whom it was issued shall not obtain or be in possession of any other of those documents at any time during the period of one year following the date of cancellation.

heading: Open Seasons
paragraph: 9 (1) Subject to subsections (3) and (4) and section 20, the open season in each year in park waters set out in Column I of an item of Schedule II for the species of fish set out in Column II of that item is the period set out in Column III of that item inclusive of the opening and closing dates.

heading: Open Seasons
paragraph: (2) No person shall fish for any species of fish in a park except in park waters set out in Column I of an item of Schedule II for the species of fish set out in Column II of that item and during the open season for fish of that species set out in Column III of that item.

heading: Open Seasons
paragraph: (3) Where the first day of an open season falls on a Sunday or Monday in any year, the open season shall begin on the Saturday immediately preceding that Sunday or Monday.

heading: Open Seasons
paragraph: (4) Where the last day of an open season falls on a Friday or Saturday in any year, the open season shall end on the Sunday immediately following that Friday or Saturday.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 10 (1) No person shall, on any day, catch in the park waters set out in column I of Part I of Schedule III and retain in respect of a species of fish set out in column II, fish that are

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (a) in total, a number in excess of

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (i) in the case of the park waters set out in items 1 to 26, the daily catch and possession limit set out in column III, and

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (ii) in the case of the park waters set out in item 27, the daily catch limit set out in column III; or

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (b) of an overall length in excess of or less than, as the case may be, the overall length, if any, set out in column III of that item.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (2) No person shall have in possession within the boundaries of a park referred to in column I of Part I of Schedule III in respect of a species of fish set out in column II, fish that are

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (a) in total, a number in excess of

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (i) in the case of a park referred to in items 1 to 26, the daily catch and possession limit set out in column III, and

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (ii) in the case of the park referred to in item 27, the possession limit set out in column III; or

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (b) of an overall length in excess of or less than, as the case may be, the overall length, if any, set out in column III of that item.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 11 No person shall,

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (a) on any day, catch in the park waters set out in column I of Part II of Schedule III and retain a number of fish of the species set out in column II, that is in excess of

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (i) in the case of the park waters set out in items 1 to 25, the aggregate daily catch and possession limit set out in column III, and

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (ii) in the case of the park waters set out in item 26, the aggregate daily catch limit set out in column III;

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (b) have in possession within the boundaries of a park referred to in column I of Part II of Schedule III, a number of fish of the species set out in column II that is in excess of

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (i) in the case of a park referred to in items 1 to 25, the aggregate daily catch and possession limit set out in column III, and

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (ii) in the case of the park referred to in item 26, the aggregate possession limit set out in column III; or

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (c) fish in park waters set out in column I of Part II of Schedule III, on any day after having, on that day, caught in those waters and retained a number of fish of the species set out in column II that is

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (i) in the case of the park waters set out in items 1 to 25, the aggregate daily catch and possession limit set out in column III, and

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (ii) in the case of the park waters set out in item 26, the aggregate possession limit set out in column III.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 12 Notwithstanding Parts I and II of Schedule III, no person shall fish in La Mauricie National Park of Canada on any day after having on that day caught in the waters of that park and retained

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (a) two lake trout; or

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: (b) three northern pike.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 12.1 If the daily catch and possession limit set out in column III of Part I of Schedule III is 0, any person who catches a fish of a species set out in column II shall immediately unhook the fish and return it to the water with as little damage to the fish as possible.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 12.2 Nothwithstanding the limit set out in column III of paragraph 8(a) of Parts I and II of Schedule III, no person shall, in any year, in the waters of Prince Albert National Park of Canada, catch and retain more than two lake trout.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 12.3 Notwithstanding Schedule III, no person shall fish for atlantic salmon in any waters of Cape Breton Highlands National Park of Canada on any day after having caught and released two atlantic salmon measuring 30 cm or more.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 13 Where a fish has been filleted, two fillets shall be treated as one fish and, unless the body is shown, every fillet shall be treated as having been taken from a game fish.

heading: Catch and Possession Limits
paragraph: 14 For the purposes of these Regulations, a fish in the possession of a person under 16 years of age who does not hold a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement, but who is accompanied by a person holding a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement, shall be considered to be in the possession of the holder of the fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 15 (1) Except as otherwise provided in these Regulations, no person shall fish in park waters by any method other than angling.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) No person shall be in possession, within 100 m of any park waters, of any equipment that can be used to catch or take fish, unless fishing in those waters by means of that equipment is permitted by these Regulations.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (3) Notwithstanding subsection (2), no person shall be in possession at any time, within the boundaries of a park, of any equipment that can be used to catch or take fish, other than equipment used for angling or for taking soft-shell clams or American eel, except when carrying such equipment through the park in a vehicle to a destination outside the park or to a residence in the park.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (4) No person shall fish from a bridge or any other structure that crosses the waters of Cape Breton Highlands, Fundy, Gros Morne, Prince Edward Island or Terra Nova National Park of Canada.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (5) No person in La Mauricie or Forillon National Park of Canada shall have in possession fishing equipment unless

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) the person holds a fishing permit; or

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) the fishing equipment is kept inside a motor vehicle.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (6) No person shall, while fishing in Fundy, Kouchibouguac, Cape Breton Highlands or Terra Nova National Park of Canada, use an artificial fly that incorporates a weight as an integral part of the artificial fly, that is attached to a sinking line, or that has a weight attached to the hook or line, for the purpose of causing the artificial fly to sink.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (7) No person shall use a fish finder while fishing in Kejimkujik or La Mauricie National Park of Canada.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 15.1 No person shall catch and retain

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) subject to paragraph (b), invertebrates from the marine portion of Forillon National Park of Canada unless the person is the holder of a fishing permit, issued by the superintendent, authorizing their removal for scientific or park management purposes;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) for commercial purposes, lobster or fish used as lobster bait, from the marine part of Forillon National Park of Canada unless the person is the holder of a licence, issued under the National Parks Businesses Regulations, 1998, to carry on that business;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (c) subject to paragraph (d), invertebrates from Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada unless the person is the holder of a fishing permit, issued by the superintendent, authorizing their removal for scientific or park management purposes; or

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (d) for commercial purposes, soft-shell clams from Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada unless the person is the holder of a licence that authorizes that activity and that is issued under the National Parks of Canada Businesses Regulations.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 16 No person shall fish in park waters by foul hooking.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 17 No person shall, when fishing in park waters, use

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) more than one fishing line;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) a fishing line having more than one artificial fly or other type of bait;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (c) a fishing line having an artificial fly to which is attached any live or dead natural bait;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (d) a fishing line having any combination of hooks capable of catching more than one fish at a time;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (e) a fishing line having more than one type of lure;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (f) a lure having more than

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (i) two single hooks,

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (ii) two gang-hooks, or

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (iii) one single hook and one gang-hook;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (g) a gang-hook having more than three hooks; or

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (h) a lead sinker or lead jig that weighs less than 50 g.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 17.1 No person shall, while fishing for any species of fish in the waters of Riding Mountain or Point Pelee National Park of Canada, use a hook from which the barbs have not been removed unless the barbs have been pinched to the shaft of the hook.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 17.2 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall, while fishing in any waters in Kluane National Park of Canada or in Kluane National Park Reserve of Canada, use a hook from which the barbs have not been removed unless the barbs have been pinched to the shaft of the hook.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) No person shall, while fishing in the waters of the Kathleen River that are located in the area of land referred to in subsection (1), use a hook unless it is a single hook and

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) the barbs have been removed from it; or

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) the barbs have been pinched to the shaft of the hook.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 17.3 No person shall, while fishing in the waters of Kejimkujik National Park of Canada set out in column II of paragraph 2(e) of Schedule V for any species of fish set out in column I of that paragraph, use

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) any method other than angling with an artificial fly; and

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) a hook from which the barbs have not been removed, unless the barbs have been pinched to the shaft of the hook.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 17.4 No person shall, while fishing in park waters for any species of fish, be in possession of any lead sinker or lead jig that weighs less than 50 g.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 18 No person shall, when angling, leave a fishing line unattended.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 19 (1) Subject to subsection (4), no person shall have in possession, within 100 metres of park waters, a net capable of being used for fishing unless the person

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) is the holder of a fishing permit, salmon licence, soft-shell clam permit or lake trout endorsement;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) keeps the net inside a motor vehicle;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (d) is in possession of the net in Point Pelee National Park of Canada for purposes of fishing in waters outside the park.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) No person shall use or have in his possession in a park a gaff-hook or tailer.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply in respect of Riding Mountain National Park of Canada.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (4) Nothing in these Regulations prohibits the use of a landing net or a dip net to land a fish caught by angling.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 20 No person shall fish in

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) any park waters set out in Schedule IV or, where applicable, during the time set out in that schedule;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) any park waters used for propagating, protecting, conserving or displaying fish; or

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (c) any part of park waters designated by a superintendent for public swimming or as a marina.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 20.1 (1) Despite column I of item 42.2 of Schedule II, no person shall fish for soft-shell clams in any waters of Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada except where waters are marked for that purpose and in the manner set out in a notice posted by the superintendent or, where no such notice is posted, in the manner set out in the soft-shell clam permit.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) The superintendent shall, in determining the manner in which a person may fish for soft-shell clams, take into account the park's natural and cultural resources and the preservation, control and management of the park.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 21 (1) No person shall fish for any species of fish set out in Column I of an item of Schedule V in any park waters set out in Column II of that item by any method except angling with an artificial fly.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) No person shall fish for salmon in any parks waters set out in Schedule VI.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 22 (1) No person shall fish in park waters, other than in the waters of those parks referred to in subsection (2), during the period from two hours after sunset on any day until one hour before sunrise on the day immediately following.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) No person shall fish in the waters of Cape Breton Highlands, Fundy, Georgian Bay Islands, Gros Morne, Kejimkujik, Kouchibouguac, La Mauricie, Point Pelee, Prince Edward Island or Terra Nova National Park of Canada during the period starting one hour after sunset on any day and ending one hour before sunrise on the next day.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 23 No person shall fish for or have in his possession in a park any salmon fry, parr, smolt or spent salmon, also known as slink, black or kelt salmon.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 24 (1) No person shall use for bait or have in his possession in a park live fish eggs or live minnows.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) No person shall use or have in possession for use as bait live or dead fish or any parts thereof

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) in Jasper, Banff, Waterton Lakes, Yoho, Kootenay, Glacier, Mount Revelstoke, Prince Albert, Riding Mountain, Wood Buffalo or La Mauricie National Park of Canada;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) in Kluane National Park of Canada or in Kluane National Park Reserve of Canada; or

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (c) in Nahanni National Park Reserve of Canada.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (3) No person shall use for bait, or be in possession of, dead fish eggs in La Mauricie, Wood Buffalo, Prince Albert or Riding Mountain National Park of Canada.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (4) No person shall use any natural bait or any chemical attractant in any park waters set out in an item of Schedule VII.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 24.1 No person shall fish for soft-shell clams within Kejimkujik or Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada, except through the use of their hands or hand tools.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 25 Unless authorized by a superintendent, no person shall place in park waters or transfer between bodies of park waters live fish eggs or live fish.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 26 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall put any meat, bones, dead fish or offal, grain, dry feed or other food for fish in park waters.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) A superintendent may designate park waters where offal from fish caught in those park waters is permitted to be put.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 27 No person hired or employed in a park as a boatman or fishing guide shall fish in park waters while carrying out the duties for which that person was hired or employed.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 28 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall, when fishing, swimming or diving in park waters, have in his possession a spear, spear-gun or any underwater equipment that may be used for fishing.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) A person diving in park waters may have in his possession underwater equipment that facilitates diving.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 29 Unless authorized by a superintendent, no person shall obstruct or alter any park waters in such manner as to prevent, obstruct or redirect the free passage of fish.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 29.1 (1) For the purposes of this section, a fish-counting fence means a structure placed in park waters by a superintendent for the purpose of capturing fish or controlling the movement of fish in those waters.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) No person shall disturb or tamper with a fish-counting fence.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (3) No person shall fish within 100 metres of a fish-counting fence.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 30 Unless authorized by a superintendent, no person shall sell, offer for sale, trade or barter any fish caught in park waters.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 31 No person who has caught, in park waters, a fish suitable for human consumption shall allow that fish to spoil or otherwise be wasted.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 31.1 No person shall harass, disturb or chase, or attempt to harass, disturb or chase fish in park waters by throwing stones or by any means other than fishing.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 33 These Regulations do not apply to a person authorized by a superintendent carry out functions related to fisheries management, investigation or research in a park while the person is engaged in carrying out such functions.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 33.1 Notwithstanding section 15 and subsection 28(1), but subject to section 9, in Kouchibouguac National Park of Canada, a person may fish for American eel by means of a spear held in the hand.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 34 (1) Every person who engages in ice fishing in park waters shall keep any fish, offal, refuse and deleterious substances in containers suitable for their temporary storage and shall remove the containers at the end of each day of fishing from any area in which the person has been fishing.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) Where, in any park waters, ice conditions are unsafe for ice-fishing, a superintendent may, by notice in writing, prohibit ice-fishing in any such waters.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (3) Every notice issued pursuant to subsection (2) shall contain a description of the park waters in respect of which the notice is issued and shall be posted by the superintendent in a conspicuous place in the park.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (4) Where a notice is issued pursuant to subsection (2), no person shall ice-fish in any park waters described in that notice.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (5) No person shall engage in ice fishing in any flowing waters in Banff National Park of Canada.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (6) No person shall engage in ice fishing in any waters in Cape Breton Highlands National Park of Canada unless otherwise indicated by a notice posted by the superintendent in accordance with section 35.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 35 (1) Notwithstanding sections 3 and 10 and Schedule II, a superintendent may, by notice in writing, during an open season close any park waters to fishing or restrict the extent of fishing in such waters where it is necessary to do so for the protection, conservation and management of fish in those waters.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (2) Every notice issued pursuant to subsection (1) shall contain a description of park waters in respect of which the notice is issued and shall be posted by the superintendent in conspicuous places in the park.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (3) Where a notice is issued pursuant to subsection (1), no person shall

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) fish in any park waters described in that notice, where the notice closes those park waters to fishing; and

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) exceed the extent of fishing set out in the notice, where the notice restricts the extent of fishing in any park waters.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 36 Every person shall, when fishing in park waters or when in possession of fishing equipment or bait or any fish in a park, on request by a superintendent or park warden, produce the fishing equipment or bait or the fish for examination.

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: 37 Every person who fishes in Banff, Waterton Lakes, Yoho, Kootenay, Glacier, Jasper or Mount Revelstoke National Park of Canada shall, in the manner set out in a notice posted by the superintendent at a park wardens' office, a park information booth or any park entrance,

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (a) register the person's catch of fish;

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (b) maintain a record of the person's catch of fish; and

heading: Prohibitions and General Provisions
paragraph: (c) submit that record to a park warden.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: assessed value, in respect of a lot in a park, means the value of the lot, including improvements, determined according to a provincial assessment completed for the park or, where no provincial assessment has been completed, determined on the basis of an expert appraisal of the lot or of an equivalent lot; (evaluation)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: base factor, in respect of water services or sewer services, means the numerical value assigned to a unit each year by a council or committee of residents of a park and representatives of Parks Canada for purposes of determining the owner's share of recoverable capital costs incurred in respect of the park to deliver water services or sewer services, as the case may be, to lots in the park; (facteur de base)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: business includes any trade, calling, industry, employment or occupation carried on for gain or profit in a park; (commerce)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: dwelling unit means two or more rooms used or intended for use as a single domestic housekeeping unit with cooking, living, sleeping and sanitary facilities; (logement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: lot volume value means the result obtained by multiplying the aggregate of the volume values for the units on a lot by the number of months of occupancy permitted under the lease, permit or licence of occupation for that lot divided by 12; (valeur volumetrique du lot)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: owner means an individual, syndicate, association, corporation, company, club or organization in charge of, or responsible for, a residence or for the operation of any accommodation, activity, business, entertainment, church, hospital, school, university or other facility within a park, and includes an employee, manager, lessee, transferee or partner of such an individual, syndicate, association, corporation, company, club or organization; (proprietaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: street includes a lane; (rue)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: total capital costs means

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) in respect of a water system in a park, the capital cost incurred to deliver water services to lots in the park, calculated on an annual basis, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) in respect of a sewer system in a park, the capital cost incurred to deliver sewer services to lots in the park, calculated on an annual basis; (cout total en capital)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: total operating and maintenance costs means

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) in respect of a water system in a park, the operating and maintenance costs incurred to deliver water services to lots in the park, calculated on an annual basis, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) in respect of a sewer system in a park, the operating and maintenance costs incurred to deliver sewer services to lots in the park, calculated on an annual basis; (cout total de fonctionnement et d'entretien)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: unit means a building, or a portion of a building, in a park designated as a unit by a council or committee of residents of the park and representatives of Parks Canada; (unite)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: volume value, in respect of water services or sewer services, means the numerical value assigned to a unit, determined by comparing the estimated annual volume of water that the unit will use or the sewage that it will generate annually, as the case may be, to the volume of water used or sewage generated by a building that has been established as the benchmark of one volume value for the park in which the unit is located. (valeur volumetrique)

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.1 Sections 3 to 5 and 7 to 24 do not apply to the town of Banff.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2.2 These Regulations do not apply in the Town of Jasper.

heading: Building Connections
paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to sections 4 and 11.1, the owner of every building on a lot that fronts or abuts on any part of a street on which a water main or sewer main has been laid shall connect the building directly to that water main or sewer main, as the case may be.

heading: Building Connections
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a garage, detached structure designed to provide accommodation for tourists or any other building on a lot that is appurtenant to, and designed to improve the usefulness and convenience of, a building on a lot that is connected to a water or sewer main referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 4 (1) No person shall, in any park,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) make any connection with a water or sewer main,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) make any connection with a water pipe connected to a water main, or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) make any connection with a sewer pipe connected to a sewer main,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: without the permission in writing of the superintendent.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) The superintendent is authorized to grant the permission after taking into consideration

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) the capacity of the park's sewer and water systems;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) any technical or material constraints;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) the preservation of the park's natural resources and the protection of its cultural, historical and archaeological resources;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (d) the safety, health and enjoyment of persons who are visiting or residing in the park; and

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (e) the preservation, control and management of the park.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 5 No person, other than the superintendent, a municipal water system operator or a fire department officer authorized by the superintendent, and in the exercise of their functions, shall manipulate a hydrant, valve, stop-cock, pipe, water meter or other portion of a water system in a park.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 6 No person shall

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) trespass,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) deposit refuse or other matter,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) fish,

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (d) bathe, or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (e) wash any person, article or thing

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: in or upon any area in a park that has been designated by the superintendent and marked by appropriate signs as a source of water supply.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 7 No person shall

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) tamper with or damage any structure or appliance forming part of the sewer system in a park; or

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) deposit refuse or other matter into any pipe, fixture, manhole or other appurtenance of the sewer system in a park that is likely to damage or cause any failure or blockage of the system.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 8 (1) No person shall construct or maintain any well in a park, for the supply of water for his own use, or the use of any other person, without the permission in writing of the superintendent.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) The superintendent is authorized to grant permission for the construction or maintenance of a well in a park if the water drawn from the well is to be used for geothermal purposes or if the park has no water system to which a connection can be made.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: 9 (1) No person shall install a septic tank or dry privy in a park without the permission in writing of the superintendent.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) No person shall install a sewer in a park that is not to be connected to the sewer system in that park without the permission in writing of the superintendent.

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) An application for permission to install a septic tank or a sewer that is not to be connected to the sewer system in a park shall be accompanied by

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) plans and specifications of the proposed septic tank or sewer, including an estimate of the cost thereof; and

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) a fee of $1 for each $1,000 or fraction thereof of the cost of such septic tank or sewer as stated in the estimate referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (4) The superintendent is authorized to grant permission for the installation of a septic tank, dry privy or sewer in a park if the park has no sewer system to which a connection can be made, after taking into consideration

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) the capacity of the park's sewer and water distribution systems;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) any technical or material constraints;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) the preservation of the park's natural resources and the protection of its cultural, historical and archaeological resources;

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (d) the safety, health and enjoyment of persons who are visiting or residing in the park; and

heading: Prohibitions
paragraph: (e) the preservation, control and management of the park.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: 10 Each application for the making of a connection to a water main or sewer main in a park shall be made to the superintendent on a prescribed form obtainable from the superintendent and shall

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (a) be signed by the owner of the lot in respect of which the application is made or his agent authorized in writing for the purpose;

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (b) state the type of premises in respect of which the water is to be used or the sewer connected; and

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (c) state the number of rooms or the floor area of any building in respect of which the water is to be used or the sewer connected, where these are factors in establishing the water or sewer rate payable.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: 11 (1) The owner of a building who is required pursuant to subsection 3(1) to connect his building to a water main or sewer main shall pay

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (a) all the costs for the construction of that part of the connection that is within his lot line; and

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (b) the extra costs for the construction of that part of the connection that is outside his lot line that arise because of the presence of rock, frost or other obstacles or because of the removal and replacement during the construction of any portion of a street, sidewalk or boulevard.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (2) On receiving an application made in accordance with section 10 and receiving a security deposit from the applicant in the form of a certified cheque or cash deposit in an amount equal to the portion of the estimated cost of construction for which the owner is responsible under subsection (1), the superintendent shall cause the connection to be made and any soil or portion of a street, sidewalk or boulevard that was removed for the making of the connection to be replaced.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (3) On completion of a connection to a water main or sewer main, the superintendent shall prepare a statement setting out the portion of the actual costs for which the owner is responsible and shall

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (a) where the amount of the security deposit referred to in subsection (2) exceeds the portion of the actual costs for which the owner is responsible, deposit that portion to the credit of the Receiver General and refund the balance to the owner; and

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (b) where the amount of the security deposit referred to in subsection (2) is equal to or less than the portion of the actual costs for which the owner is responsible, deposit that portion to the credit of the Receiver General and notify the owner of the amount of the balance, if any, of the portion payable by him.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: 11.1 (1) Where an additional building is erected on a lot on which there is another building already connected to a water main or sewer main or where an existing building on a lot is altered, the owner of the building shall apply to the superintendent for permission to make an additional connection or to alter an existing connection.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (2) On approving an application made pursuant to subsection (1) and receiving from the applicant a security deposit in the form of a certified cheque or cash deposit in an amount equal to the estimated cost of the construction for which the owner of the building is responsible under section 11.2, the superintendent may prescribe terms respecting

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (a) the location of the connection to a previously installed connection or to a water main or sewer main;

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (b) the manner in which the connection is to be constructed, including

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (i) the grade, type and size of pipe;

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (ii) the quality and extent of pipe bedding; and

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (iii) the quality and extent of pipe trench backfill material.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (3) Where the owner of a building does not comply with any terms prescribed by the superintendent pursuant to subsection (2), the superintendent may cause the connection to be made in accordance with the terms.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (4) The owner of the building may enter into an agreement with the superintendent permitting the superintendent to cause the connection to a water main or sewer main to be made.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (5) On completion of a connection to a water main or sewer main made pursuant to subsection (3) or (4), the superintendent shall prepare a statement setting out the costs for which the owner is responsible under section 11.2 and shall

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (a) where the amount of the security deposit referred to in subsection (2) exceeds the costs for which the owner is responsible, deposit that amount to the credit of the Receiver General and refund the balance to the owner; and

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (b) where the amount of the security deposit referred to in subsection (2) is equal to or less than the costs for which the owner is responsible, deposit that amount to the credit of the Receiver General and notify the owner of the amount of the balance, if any, of the amount payable by him.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: 11.2 (1) Where a connection is made pursuant to subsection 11.1(1) or (3), the owner of the building shall pay the costs

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (a) if he is erecting an additional building, of connecting that bulding to the existing connection to the water main or sewer main at a point within his lot line; or

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (b) if he is erecting an additional building or altering an existing building and the existing connection is inadequate in size or so located as to be unsuitable for the additional building or altered bulding, of connecting the building to the water or sewer main at a point outside his lot line.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (2) In addition to the costs payable under subsection (1), the owner of a building shall pay the extra costs for the construction of that part of the connection that is outside his lot line that arise because of the presence of rock, frost or other obstacles or because of the removal and replacement during the construction of any portion of a street, sidewalk or boulevard.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: 11.3 Any part of a connection that is made outside the lot line of an owner of a building pursuant to section 11 or 11.2 is the property of Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: 12 (1) The superintendent may at any reasonable time enter any lot or building in respect of which a water or sewer connection has been made to examine the plumbing, drain and vent piping and to ascertain the amount of water used and the manner of use.

heading: Connections to Water Main and Sewer Main
paragraph: (2) The superintendent may, with the permission of the owner or occupant, enter any lot or building for the purpose of installing a water meter.

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: 13 (1) The superintendent may shut off the water supply in respect of any lot or building where

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: (a) any fixture or appliance is causing a wastage of water;

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: (b) a water fixture has been installed or connection made without his approval; or

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: (c) water or sewer charges have not been paid within 30 days after the due date for payment thereof.

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: (2) Where any water is shut off pursuant to subsection (1) it shall not be turned on again until the fixture, appliance or connection has been removed, repaired or replaced to the satisfaction of the superintendent or the charges have been paid, as the case may be.

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: 14 The superintendent may shut off or interrupt the supply of water in respect of any or all buildings or lots in the park for such periods as are required where

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: (a) it is expedient to repair, replace or install any water main or other work; or

heading: Discontinuance of Water Supply
paragraph: (b) there is a conflagration or other circumstance that, in the opinion of the superintendent, requires such action.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: 15 (1) Every owner of a lot located in Kootenay National Park of Canada or Fundy National Park of Canada shall

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a) inform the superintendent of that park of the number of rooms - excluding any halls, vestibules, bathrooms, pantries or closets - the floor area of those rooms and the use of any buildings on the lot for the purposes of determining the annual quantity charge for water or sewerage payable by the owner; and

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) if the lot is connected to the park water system, pay an annual quantity charge for water at the rate set out in Schedule IV or VIII, as the case may be.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (2) Every owner of a lot located in Kootenay National Park of Canada shall

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a) if the lot is connected to the park water or sewer system, pay an annual service connection charge at the rate set out in Schedule IV;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a.1) if the lot is connected to the park sewer system, pay an annual quantity charge for the sewer at the rate set out in Schedule IV; and

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) if the lot is connected to the park water or sewer system and the lot fronts or abuts on a street along which a water main or sewer main has been laid, pay

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (i) an annual general assessment charge, based on the assessed value of the lot, at the rate set out in Schedule IV, and

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (ii) an annual special assessment charge for water and sewerage, based on the frontage and the area of the lot, at the rate set out in Schedule IV.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2), in determining the frontage of a lot,

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a) the frontage of a lot fronting or abutting on only one street is the length of the side of the lot that fronts or abuts on that street;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) the frontage of a lot fronting or abutting on two or more streets along which water mains have been laid and from one of which a connection has been made is the length of the side of the lot that fronts or abuts on the street from which the connection was made;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (c) notwithstanding paragraph (b), the frontage of a corner lot at an intersection of water mains is the length of the longest side of the lot plus 25 feet, except that where the shortest side of the lot is less than 25 feet in length, the frontage is the aggregate of the longest and shortest sides;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (d) notwithstanding paragraph (c), the frontage of a lot fronting or abutting on two or more streets along which water mains have been laid and from more than one of which connections have been made is twice the length of the longest side of the lot;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (e) for the purposes of paragraphs (a) to (d), the frontage of a lot the sides of which are not parallel is that number of feet that bears the same ratio to the frontage in feet of the nearest rectangular lot in the same block as the square root of the area of the irregular lot is to the square root of the area of the rectangular lot; and

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (f) notwithstanding paragraphs (a) to (e), where a lot has no buildings, or where each building on the lot has a floor area of less than 300 square feet, and the lot forms part of a group of lots, having a combined frontage, calculated under those paragraphs, of more than 200 feet, each of which is being used in connection with a single enterprise, the frontage of the lot is one-half the amount determined under any of paragraphs (a) to (e).

paragraph: 16 (1) Every owner of a lot located in Prince Albert National Park of Canada, Riding Mountain National Park of Canada or Waterton Lakes National Park of Canada shall pay

paragraph: 17 For the purposes of sections 17.1 and 17.2, year means a period commencing on April 1 in one calendar year and ending on March 31 in the next calendar year.

paragraph: 17.1 (1) Every owner of a lot located in Banff National Park of Canada, Jasper National Park of Canada or Yoho National Park of Canada shall, where the lot is connected to the park water system, pay an annual water charge that is calculated by multiplying the volume of water consumed that year indicated by the lot's water meter by the rate determined under subsection (2).

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (2) The superintendent of each of the parks referred to in subsection (1) shall, on or before March 31 of each year, determine the rate, corresponding to the estimated cost per cubic metre of water, of providing water service in the park in the following year, in accordance with the formula

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a) water collection and distribution;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) water treatment;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (c) facility maintenance;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (d) reservoir maintenance;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (e) pumping;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (f) water meter maintenance and reading;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (g) testing of valves and hydrants;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (h) maintenance relating to thawing, leak detection and main breaks;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (i) capital infrastructure;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (m) water utility fee invoicing and invoice collection and recording; and

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (n) anything else related to the establishment, operation, maintenance and administration of the water service system.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (4) The superintendent of each of the parks referred to in subsection (1) shall, on or before June 30 of each year, calculate the actual total cost of providing water service in the park for the immediately preceding year in accordance with the description of B of the formula in subsection (2) by substituting actual costs for estimated costs.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (5) If the actual total cost of providing water service in the park for the immediately preceding year calculated in accordance with subsection (4) differs from the estimated total cost of providing water service in the park for that year, the estimated total cost of providing water service in the park for the current year shall be adjusted as follows:

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a) if the actual total cost is greater than the estimated total cost, the difference shall be added to the estimated total cost of providing water service in the park for the current year; or

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) if the actual total cost is less than the estimated total cost, the difference shall be deducted from the estimated total cost of providing water service in the park for the current year.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (6) The following charges are payable separately by an owner of a lot in any of the parks referred to in subsection (1) for services requested by the owner:

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a) each time the water supply in respect of the lot is turned on or off, a service charge of $25;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) when the water meter serving a lot is tested by a qualified person hired by the superintendent, a service charge equivalent to the amount charged by that person to the superintendent; and

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (c) when water from any source in the park is purchased by an owner of a lot and delivered to the lot by truck or through hydrants, a service charge calculated by multiplying the number of cubic metres of water purchased by the rate applicable for that year as determined under subsection (2).

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (7) Any person who, for construction purposes, purchases water from any source in any of the parks referred to in subsection (1) shall pay a service charge calculated by multiplying the number of cubic metres of water purchased by the rate applicable for that year as determined under subsection (2).

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: 17.2 (1) Every owner of a lot located in Banff National Park of Canada, Jasper National Park of Canada or Yoho National Park of Canada shall, where the lot is connected to the park sewer system, pay an annual sewerage charge that is calculated by multiplying the volume of water consumed that year indicated by the lot's water meter by the rate determined under subsection (2).

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (2) The superintendent of each of the parks referred to in subsection (1) shall, on or before March 31 of each year, determine the rate, corresponding to the estimated cost per cubic metre of water, of providing sewerage services in the park in the following year, in accordance with the formula

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) facility maintenance;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (5) If the actual total cost of providing sewerage services in the park for the immediately preceding year calculated in accordance with subsection (4) differs from the estimated total cost of providing sewerage services in the park for that year, the estimated total cost of providing sewerage services in the park for the current year shall be adjusted as follows:

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) if the actual total cost is less than the estimated total cost, the difference shall be deducted from the estimated total cost of providing sewerage services in the park for the current year.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (6) Every owner of a lot located in any of the parks referred to in subsection (1) shall, if the lot is not connected to the park water system and the lot is served with water from another source, install a water meter, approved by the superintendent under subsection (7), to measure the quantity of water consumed from that other source for the purpose of calculating the annual sewerage charge in accordance with subsections (1) to (3).

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (7) The superintendent shall approve any water meter that an owner proposes to install if the water meter is operational and compatible with the water metering system in the park.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (8) Every owner of a lot located in any of the parks referred to in subsection (1) shall, if the owner uses a septic tank or holding tank sewage system and the sewage must be removed from the lot by mechanical means and delivered to a sewage treatment plant by truck, pay a sewage treatment fee of $40 per truckload.

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: 18 For the purposes of subsection 16(1), the superintendent of each park referred to in that subsection shall, on March 31 of each year, make available to each owner of a lot in that park

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (a) the volume value of each unit on the lot;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (b) the lot volume value for the lot;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (d) the total operating and maintenance costs and total capital costs incurred to provide water services in the park;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (e) the total operating and maintenance costs and total capital costs incurred to provide sewer services in the park;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (f) the aggregate of the lot volume values for all lots in the park that are connected to the water system;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (g) the aggregate of the lot volume values for all lots in the park that are connected to the sewer system;

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (h) the aggregate of the base factors for all units in the park that are connected to the water system; and

heading: Applicable Charges for Water and Sewerage
paragraph: (i) the aggregate of the base factors for all units in the park that are connected to the sewer system.

heading: General
