heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the National Parks Wildlife Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: exotic wildlife means all wildlife that is not indigenous to a park or that has been declared, pursuant to these Regulations, to be exotic wildlife; (faune exotique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: firearm means any weapon from which any shot, bullet or other missile can be discharged and that is capable of causing injury or death to wildlife and includes anything that can be adapted for use as a firearm and anything that is designed for or capable of being used for the purpose of causing injury or death to wildlife; (arme a feu)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: guide means a person who holds a valid licence issued pursuant to the National Parks Businesses Regulations to carry on the business of a guide; (guide)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: hunt means to trap, chase, pursue, worry, follow after or on the trail of, search for, shoot at, stalk, lie in wait for, or to attempt, in any manner, to capture, kill or injure any wildlife whether or not the wildlife is captured, killed or injured; (chasser)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: loaded with respect to a firearm, means that a live shell or cartridge is present in the breach, chamber or attached magazine of the firearm or that a projectile is present in the barrel of the firearm; (chargee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: possession means possession within the meaning of subsection 4(3) of the Criminal Code; (possession)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: through highway means

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the Trans-Canada Highway in Banff, Yoho, Glacier and Mount Revelstoke National Parks,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) the Yellowhead Highway in Jasper National Park,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) the Banff-Windermere Highway in Banff and Kootenay National Parks,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) Highways 10 and 19 in Riding Mountain National Park,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) the Trans-Canada Highway, the Charlottetown Highway, the East Port area Highway 310 and the Terra Nova area Highway 301 in Terra Nova National Park,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (f) Highway 114 and the unnumbered roads leading to Teahans Corner in Fundy National Park,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (g) the Cabot Trail (Highway 19) in Cape Breton Highlands National Park,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (h) Highway 132 between Cap-aux-Os and Cap-des-Rosiers in Forillon National Park,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (i) Highway 117 in Kouchibouguac National Park, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (j) Highway 93 in Banff National Park and Jasper National Park; (route de transit)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: trap means a structure, contrivance or device that is capable of capturing wildlife by affording entrance but not exit, and includes a snare; (piege)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: vehicle means every device in, on or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn on land; (vehicule)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: vessel includes any boat, canoe, raft, amphibious vehicle or any other structure, other than a sea plane, used or capable of being used for transportation on water; (bateau)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: wildlife means all wild mammals, amphibians, reptiles, birds, fish, insects and other invertebrates and any part thereof, and includes their eggs and young; (faune ou animaux sauvages)

heading: Application
paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to sections 40 and 41 of the Canada National Parks Act, these Regulations apply to all parks other than Wood Buffalo National Park of Canada and to all park reserves as if they were parks.

heading: Application
paragraph: (1.1) In the event of an inconsistency between these Regulations and the National Parks of Canada Fishing Regulations or the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve of Canada Snowshoe Hare Regulations, the National Parks of Canada Fishing Regulations and the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve of Canada Snowshoe Hare Regulations prevail, respectively, to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) These Regulations do not apply to a superintendent, park warden, peace officer or any other person authorized by the superintendent to carry out functions related to the management of a park while any of those persons is engaged in carrying out such functions.

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: 4 (1) Except as otherwise provided in these Regulations, no person shall

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) hunt, disturb, hold in captivity or destroy any wildlife within, or remove any wildlife from, a park;

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) in La Mauricie National Park, Georgian Bay Islands National Park, St. Lawrence Islands National Park or the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve, have in the person's possession any wildlife;

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (c) in any park other than a park referred to in paragraph (b), or outside a park, be in possession of any wildlife killed or procured within a park, unless the wildlife is in that person's possession in accordance with subsection (4);

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (e) disturb or destroy a nest, lair, den or beaver house or dam in a park;

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (f) touch or feed wildlife in a park or entice wildlife that is in a park to approach by holding out or setting out decoys or any such devices, foodstuffs or bait of any kind; or

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (g) release any exotic wildlife within a park.

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (2) No person shall shine a movable light having a voltage greater than 4.5 volts in any area frequented by wildlife between sunset and sunrise.

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (3) A person may, in the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve, have in the person's possession wild ducks, if

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) the ducks have been hunted in accordance with these Regulations; and

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) at the request of a park warden or other park officer, the person in possession of the ducks produces a hunting permit issued pursuant to section 13.1.

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (4) A person may, in any park other than a park referred to in paragraph (1)(b), have in the person's possession any wildlife if

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (5), the person in possession of the wildlife produces, on the request of a park warden or other park officer,

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (i) an export permit as issued pursuant to the Game Export Act,

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (ii) a hunting licence or permit or a trapping licence or permit issued by the province in which the wildlife was procured,

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (iii) a hunting tag issued by the province in which the wildlife was procured and the tag is properly placed on the wildlife as required by the laws of that province, or

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (iv) where the wildlife has been obtained as a gift, a valid licence or permit issued by the province in which the wildlife was procured permitting a person to give such wildlife to another person or a statement signed by the donor of the gift that includes the date of the gift, the type and number of wildlife, the name of the person receiving the gift and the licence or permit number under which the wildlife was procured; and

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (5), the person is in possession of the wildlife in the park for the purpose of

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (i) storing it at a permanent residence in the park,

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (ii) transporting it directly on a through highway to a permanent residence within the park,

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (iii) transporting it directly through the park to private property outside the park on a road that is the sole means of access to that property, or

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (iv) in the case of the Prince Edward Island National Park and where entrance onto the Gulf Shore Parkway was made solely for the purpose of travelling the most direct route to a private or public road outside the Park, transporting it on the Gulf Shore Parkway.

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (5) Subsection (4) does not apply to a person who is in possession of wildlife that the person is authorized under paragraph 15(1)(a) to remove, relocate or destroy.

heading: General Prohibitions
paragraph: (6) Notwithstanding subsection (1), reasonable protection from biting or stinging insects is permitted.

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: 13.1 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (5), the superintendent of the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve may, upon receiving an application, issue a hunting permit, to the person named in the application permitting that person to hunt Eider and Long-tailed duck within the boundaries of that Reserve during the open season set out for those species in that area in the Migratory Birds Regulations, 2022.

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (2) No person is eligible for a hunting permit unless that person

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (a) is a permanent resident of the communities of Longue Pointe de Mingan, Mingan, Havre St-Pierre or Baie John Beetz in the Province of Quebec; and

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (b) holds a valid migratory game bird hunting permit issued under the Migratory Birds Regulations, 2022.

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (3) No person shall hunt for duck unless the person is the holder and is in possession of a hunting permit issued under subsection (1).

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (4) The superintendent may specify, in the hunting permit

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (a) the period of time for which the permit is valid;

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (b) the locations in the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve where the hunting of duck may take place; and

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (c) such other conditions as are necessary to ensure public safety and the protection of resources in the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve.

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (5) The holder of a hunting permit may hunt Eider and Long-tailed duck

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (a) between one-half hour before sunrise and one-half hour after sunset during the period referred to in subsection (1); and

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (b) in an amount not exceeding the daily bag limit prescribed by the Migratory Birds Regulations, 2022 for the Province of Quebec.

heading: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve
paragraph: (6) This section does not apply to any aboriginal peoples who have existing aboriginal or treaty rights to hunt in the lands constituting the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve.

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: 15 (1) A superintendent may authorize

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (a) the removal, relocation or destruction of wildlife for scientific purposes or park management purposes;

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (b) the sale or public disposal of wildlife or wildlife products from a park; and

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (c) the introduction into a park of wildlife that is or was exotic wildlife.

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: 16 (1) A superintendent may, where it is necessary for the protection, conservation or management of the wildlife in a park, by notice in writing, prohibit the possession of firearms or other devices for capturing or destroying wildlife during specified periods and in specified areas of a park.

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (2) A notice of prohibition issued pursuant to subsection (1) shall be posted at

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (a) park warden offices;

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (b) the information bureaus in the park; and

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (c) all entrances to the park.

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (3) A notice posted in accordance with subsection (2) shall contain

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (a) a description of the areas in the park to which the prohibition applies; and

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: (b) the period of time during which the prohibition applies.

heading: Powers of Superintendent
paragraph: 18 Where a notice is posted pursuant to section 16, no person shall be in possession of a firearm in the area described in the notice during the time the notice is in effect.

heading: Dogs
paragraph: 19 No person shall use a dog for the purpose of hunting wildlife.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: 20 (1) No person shall be in possession of a firearm in a park unless the firearm is not loaded and is transported in a case or is wrapped and tied securely in such a manner that no part of the firearm is exposed.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (a) a person in Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve who is hunting pursuant to a hunting permit issued under subsection 13.1(1); or

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (b) a bonded armoured car service guard who is carrying out assigned duties in the park.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (3) No person shall

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (a) have a loaded firearm in or on a vehicle, vessel or aircraft; or

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (b) discharge a firearm from a vehicle, vessel or aircraft.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (4) The superintendent may issue a permit authorizing a person to carry a firearm or trap where the firearm or trap is to be carried through the park for use outside the park.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (5) No person shall carry a firearm or trap outside a vehicle, vessel or aircraft unless

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (a) that person

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (i) has a permit from the superintendent authorizing the carrying of a firearm or trap, whichever is applicable, and

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (ii) complies with these Regulations; or

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (b) the firearm or trap is being carried directly

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (i) from a vehicle, vessel or aircraft to that person's premises, or

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (ii) to a vehicle, vessel or aircraft from that person's premises.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (6) No person, other than a bonded armoured car service guard in the performance of that person's duties in a park, shall discharge a firearm, except on a rifle range or when shooting wild ducks in the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve in accordance with these Regulations.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (7) No person shall possess a firearm or other device for capturing or destroying wildlife in Kejimkujik, La Mauricie or Point Pelee National Parks, or in Forillon National Park except when traversing the park along Highway 132, unless the person has been authorized under paragraph 15(1)(a) to remove, relocate or destroy wildlife.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: 21 Every person who is in possession of a firearm or trap shall, on the request of a park warden or other peace officer, allow the park warden or peace officer to inspect

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (a) the firearm or trap; and

heading: Firearms
paragraph: (b) the permit required for carrying the firearm or trap.

heading: Firearms
paragraph: 22 Every person acting as a guide for any individual or group carrying firearms or traps shall ensure that they are carried in accordance with these Regulations.

heading: Poison
paragraph: 23 No person shall possess any poison, poisonous substance, gas, narcotic or drug that can be used for the purpose of capturing, injuring or killing wildlife.

heading: General
paragraph: 24 No person shall by radio, telephone, walkie-talkie or any other means communicate the location of wildlife within a park to any other person within or outside a park if either of the persons is hunting.

heading: General
paragraph: 25 No person shall sell or offer for sale in a park any firearm or trap.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ministry" means the ministry of the minister responsible for the administration of this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "natural resource officer" means a person designated under section 2.

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph:
2
		  (1) Subject to the regulations, if any, the minister may designate in writing persons or a class of persons as natural resource officers.

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph: (2) In designating natural resource officers under subsection (1), the minister may

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph: (a) describe a person by name, title, position or class,

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph: (b) limit the designation to a specified time period or geographical area,

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph: (c) limit the powers and duties conferred under section 3 to the officials or enactments specified in the designation,

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph: (d) describe the limitations, if any, on the natural resource officer's powers and duties, or

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph: (e) make the designation subject to other terms and conditions.

heading: Natural resource officers - designation
paragraph: (3) The minister may vary or revoke a designation.

heading: Natural resource officers - powers and duties
paragraph:
3
		  (1) Despite any other enactment, but subject to the limitations, terms and conditions, if any, imposed by the minister under section 2 (2), a natural resource officer may

heading: Natural resource officers - powers and duties
paragraph: (a) exercise the powers and perform the duties of a prescribed official under a prescribed enactment, and

heading: Natural resource officers - powers and duties
paragraph: (b) enforce the prohibitions or requirements of prescribed enactments.

heading: Natural resource officers - powers and duties
paragraph: (2) Subject to this Act, the exercise of powers and the performance of duties conferred on a natural resource officer under subsection (1) (a) remain subject to the prescribed enactment.

heading: Delegation

4
		  The minister may, in writing,

heading: Delegation

paragraph: (b) provide directions that are binding on the delegate respecting the exercise of the power, and

5
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

paragraph: (b) prescribing officials and enactments for the purpose of section 3 (1) (a);

paragraph: (3) In making a regulation under this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make different regulations for different persons, classes of persons, places or activities.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the Navigable Waters Works Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Canadian Navigable Waters Act; (loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: engineer means a district marine agent, district manager or superintending engineer of Marine Services of the Department of Transport; (ingenieur)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: work means a work to which Part I of the Canadian Navigable Waters Act applies. (ouvrage)

heading: Duration of Approval
paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to subsection (2), where the Minister has approved a work and the site and plans thereof pursuant to paragraph 5(1)(a) or subsection 6(4) of the Act, such approval is valid for a type of work set out in Column I of an item of the schedule for the period of time set out in Column II of that item.

heading: Buoys and Marks
paragraph: 4 No person shall build or place a work in a navigable water unless all lights, buoys and other marks required in the approval are installed and maintained to the satisfaction of the Minister.

heading: Equipment and Debris
paragraph: 5 No person shall permit any tools, equipment, vehicles, temporary structures or parts thereof used or maintained for the purpose of building or placing a work in a navigable water to remain in such water after the completion of the project.

heading: Equipment and Debris
paragraph: 6 Where a work or a portion of a work that is being constructed or maintained in a navigable water causes debris or other material to accumulate on the bed or on the surface of such water, the owner of that work or portion of that work shall cause the debris or other material to be removed to the satisfaction of the Minister.

heading: Dams
paragraph: 7 (1) In this section, work means a dam or power plant in a navigable water.

heading: Dams
paragraph: (2) The owner of a work shall, when required by the Minister,

heading: Dams
paragraph: (a) install, maintain and operate log chutes to permit the transport of logs through or over the work;

heading: Dams
paragraph: (b) provide and maintain roads or foot-ways for the free passage of the public by vehicle or foot around the work between the upper and lower reaches of the river; and

heading: Dams
paragraph: (c) furnish to the Minister the records of flow, elevation of water above and below the work and all plans and other material relating to navigation that may be required by the Minister.

heading: Dams
paragraph: (3) The Minister or his authorized representative shall be permitted to measure the discharge of water in the various channels and passages through or over a work.

heading: Dams
paragraph: (4) The owner of a work shall maintain the limits of flow and elevation of water for navigation purposes as required by the Minister.

heading: Lights
paragraph: 8 (1) The owner of a work built or placed for the purposes of exploration or development of natural resources, and the transport, removal or handling of such resources from the waters or bed of a navigable water shall, whether such work is of a permanent, temporary or floating character and whether fixed to the bed or otherwise moored by anchors, spuds or cables, install and maintain

heading: Lights
paragraph: (a) on a work having a maximum horizontal dimension of 9 m or less on any one side or through any diameter thereof, one light visible in all directions;

heading: Lights
paragraph: (b) on a work having a maximum horizontal dimension of over 9 m but less than 15 m on any one side or through any diameter thereof, two lights on diagonally opposite corners or in a position satisfactory to the Minister, each visible in all directions and mounted on the same horizontal plane; and

heading: Lights
paragraph: (c) on a work having a maximum horizontal dimension of 15 m or more on one side or through any diameter thereof, a light visible in all directions at each corner of the work or at the outer limits of each quadrant thereof with 90° separation, mounted on the same horizontal plane.

heading: Lights
paragraph: (2) A light installed pursuant to subsection (1) shall

heading: Lights
paragraph: (a) be white, displaying a quick flash characteristic of 60 flashes per minute;

heading: Lights
paragraph: (b) have a nominal range of at least 12.8 km;

heading: Lights
paragraph: (c) be powered by a reliable power source and possess an auxiliary power source; and

heading: Lights
paragraph: (d) be installed not less than 6 m above the water so that at least one light will be visible from any angle of approach until within 15 m of the work.

heading: Lights
paragraph: (3) Lights shall be displayed between sunset and sunrise, and from sunrise to sunset in periods of restricted visibility, and where more than one light is installed the lights shall flash in unison.

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: 9 The owner of a work referred to in subsection 8(1) shall install and maintain thereon a sound signal

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (a) that is powered by a reliable source of power;

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (b) that possesses an auxiliary power source;

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (c) that emits a sound of two seconds duration with an 18-second pause during every period of 20 seconds;

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (d) that has its maximum intensity at a frequency between 100 and 1 000 Hertz and has a usual range of 3.2 km in any horizontal direction, measured at a height not exceeding 7.5 m;

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (e) that has not more than eight sound sources;

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (f) that is not less than 3 m or more than 30 m above the surface of the water and is so placed that the signal emitted is audible, up to and including the required range, in all directions in a horizontal plane from the work when there is no wind; and

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (g) that is sounded whenever the visibility is less than 8 km in any direction.

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: 10 The owner of a work referred to in subsection 8(1) shall install thereon identification panels displaying block letters for the purpose of identifying his work, which letters shall be

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (a) black in colour;

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (b) on a yellow background;

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (c) not less than 1 m in height; and

heading: Sound Signals
paragraph: (d) outlined in retro-reflectors or retro-reflecting material or otherwise illuminated at night.

heading: General
paragraph: 14 The owner of a work shall notify the office of the engineer within whose district the work has been located of any lights or sound signals that have ceased to function or of any change in the position of a work or any other facts affecting the safety of navigation.

heading: General
paragraph: 15 Every person who violates any provision of these Regulations is liable on summary conviction to a fine of $500 or to imprisonment for a term of six months or to both.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian Biosafety Standards and Guidelines means the documents entitled Canadian Biosafety Standard, 2nd Edition, published in 2015, and the Canadian Biosafety Guideline: Containment Level 1: Physical Design and Operational Practices, published in 2017, both developed by the Public Health Agency of Canada and the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, as amended from time to time. (Normes et lignes directrices canadiennes sur la biosecurite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: confinement procedures means any physical, chemical, biological or operational control, or combination of those controls, to restrict the exit or dispersal of a micro-organism. (methodes de confinement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: contained facility means an enclosed building with walls, floor and ceiling, or an area within such a building, where the containment is in accordance with the physical and operational requirements of a level set out in either the Canadian Biosafety Standards and Guidelines or Appendix K of the NIH Guidelines. (installation etanche)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ecozone means one of the ecozones shown on the map entitled Terrestrial Ecozones and Ecoregions of Canada 1995, dated May 6, 1999, Catalogue No. cas016e, whose boundaries are more particularly described in the National Soil Data Base (NSDB) of the Canada Soil Information System (CanSIS), developed by the Department of Agriculture and Agri-Food and the Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time. (ecozone)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: experimental field study means a study of a research and development organism that is a micro-organism, which study uses the minimum area, consisting of one or more sites whose total area does not exceed one hundred hectares, and the minimum quantity of the micro-organism as are required to meet the objectives of the study. (etude experimentale sur le terrain)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: indigenous, in respect of a micro-organism, means occurring naturally in the ecozone into which the micro-organism is intended to be introduced. (indigene)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: micro-organism means a microscopic organism that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) classified in the Bacteria, the Archaea, the Protista, which includes protozoa and algae, or the Fungi, which includes yeasts;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a virus, virus-like particle or sub-viral particle;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a cultured cell of an organism not referred to in paragraph (a) or (b), other than a cell used to propagate the organism; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any culture other than a pure culture. (micro-organisme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: NIH Guidelines means the Guidelines for Research Involving Recombinant DNA Molecules (NIH Guidelines) June 1994, published in the Federal Register by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, 59 FR 34472 (July 5, 1994), as amended from time to time. (NIH Guidelines)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: organism means a living organism as defined in section 104 of the Act, except in the following provisions:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) paragraph (c) of the definition micro-organism;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) paragraphs 2(4)(b) and (c);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) paragraph 1(d) and subparagraphs 1(e)(vi) and (viii) of Schedule 5;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) paragraph 2(d) of Schedule 5;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) subparagraph 3(d)(iii) and paragraph 3(f) of Schedule 5; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) items 5 to 7 in Schedule 5. (organisme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: research and development organism means an organism that is undergoing systematic investigation or research, by means of experimentation or analysis other than test marketing, whose primary objective is any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) to create or improve a product or process;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) to determine the technical viability or performance characteristics of a product or process; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) to evaluate the organism prior to its commercialization, by pilot plant trials, production trials, including scale-up, or customer plant trials so that technical specifications can be modified in response to the performance requirements of potential customers. (destine a la recherche et au developpement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: test marketing, in respect of a product, means the exploration of its market capability in a competitive situation in which the creation or improvement of the product is not the primary objective. (test de marche)

heading: Government agencies
paragraph: (2) The definition of government in subsection 3(1) of the Act does not apply to the expression "government agencies" in these Regulations.

heading: Avoiding regulatory duplication
paragraph: 2 (1) For greater certainty, these Regulations do not apply in respect of an organism that is manufactured or imported for a use that is regulated under any other Act or regulations listed in Schedule 4 to the Act.

heading: Transit
paragraph: (2) These Regulations do not apply in respect of an organism that is loaded on a carrier outside Canada and moved through Canada to a location outside Canada, whether or not there is a change of carrier during transit.

heading: Research and development micro-organisms
paragraph: (3) These Regulations do not apply in respect of a micro-organism that is a research and development organism not for introduction outside a contained facility, if

heading: Research and development micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) the containment of the micro-organism is in accordance with the Canadian Biosafety Standards and Guidelines or Appendix K of the NIH Guidelines; and

heading: Research and development micro-organisms
paragraph: (b) the micro-organism is

heading: Research and development micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) imported to a contained facility in a quantity that, at the time of the import, is less than 50 mL or 50 g, or

heading: Research and development micro-organisms
paragraph: (ii) manufactured in a contained facility under one of the following conditions:

heading: Research and development micro-organisms
paragraph: (A) the micro-organism does not require containment level 2, 3 or 4 as identified in the Canadian Biosafety Standards and Guidelines and at any given moment there is less than 1 000 L of the micro-organism present at that facility, and

heading: Research and development micro-organisms
paragraph: (B) the micro-organism requires containment level 2, 3 or 4 as identified in the Canadian Biosafety Standards and Guidelines, its manufacture is a controlled activity authorized under a licence issued under section 18 of the Human Pathogens and Toxins Act whose conditions of licence are complied with and at any given moment there is less than 250 L of the micro-organism present at that facility.

heading: Research and development organism other than a micro-organism
paragraph: (4) These Regulations do not apply in respect of an organism, other than a micro-organism, that is a research and development organism and is imported to or manufactured in a facility from which there is no release into the environment of

heading: Research and development organism other than a micro-organism
paragraph: (a) the organism;

heading: Research and development organism other than a micro-organism
paragraph: (b) the genetic material of the organism; or

heading: Research and development organism other than a micro-organism
paragraph: (c) material from the organism involved in toxicity.

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: 2.1 (1) Despite subsection 3(5), if the following conditions are met, these Regulations do not apply in respect of a micro-organism that is a research and development organism for introduction in an agricultural research study conducted on plants:

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) the study is conducted and supervised by an agronomist, a plant pathologist or a researcher who is trained in conducting agricultural research;

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (b) the micro-organism

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) is not modified from its natural form and occurs naturally in, and has been isolated from, an ecozone that is the same as the one in which the study is located, and

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (ii) is identified at a taxonomic level that enables the persons referred to in paragraph (a) to

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (A) consider its overall characteristics and the potential hazards to the environment and human health that are associated with its release in the study, and

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (B) ensure that the study is conducted as set out in paragraphs (c) to (e);

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (c) the manufacture of the micro-organism for the purpose of the study employs laboratory and operation practices to minimize contamination of the formulation and minimize the unintentional release of the micro-organism from the manufacturing facility;

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (d) the study is conducted in a manner that follows field and sanitation practices to minimize the likelihood of the micro-organism's dispersal outside the study area where it may be a hazard to the environment and human health; and

heading: Agricultural research study - micro-organisms
paragraph: (e) the manufacturer has operational procedures in place to ensure that physical possession or control of the micro-organism is transferred only to individuals who are made aware of the conditions of this subsection and the manufacturer has reason to believe that they are capable of meeting those conditions when conducting the study;

heading: Agricultural research study
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), agricultural research study means an experimental field study that is conducted

heading: Agricultural research study
paragraph: (a) on land that is cultivated with annual agricultural crops, such as corn and soybeans;

heading: Agricultural research study
paragraph: (b) on land that is cultivated with perennials or woody plants that do not have to be replanted for several years such as asparagus, grapevines, fruit trees, Christmas trees, ornamental trees and shrubs destined for nurseries and seedling trees destined for replanting in reforestation, conservation and restoration projects, excluding lands for forestry uses;

heading: Agricultural research study
paragraph: (c) on land that is used for five or more consecutive years to grow herbaceous forage crops that are either cultivated or growing wild; or

heading: Agricultural research study
paragraph: (d) inside a greenhouse that is not a contained facility.

heading: Information: Schedule 1
paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (6), a person who manufactures or imports a micro-organism must provide the information specified in Schedule 1.

heading: Exceptions: Information in Schedule 1
paragraph: (2) A person who manufactures or imports a micro-organism for introduction

heading: Exceptions: Information in Schedule 1
paragraph: (a) into an ecozone where it is not indigenous is not required to provide the information specified in paragraph 5(a) of Schedule 1, but must, in a separate notification for each ecozone, provide the other information specified in that Schedule as well as the identification of the ecozone of intended introduction and the data from tests conducted to determine the effects of the micro-organism on plant, invertebrate and vertebrate species likely to be exposed;

heading: Exceptions: Information in Schedule 1
paragraph: (b) in accordance with confinement procedures is not required to provide the information specified in paragraphs 5(a) and 6(c) and (d) of Schedule 1, but must provide the other information specified in that Schedule and a description of those confinement procedures and their effectiveness in restricting the exit or dispersal of the micro-organism from the locations of introduction; or

heading: Exceptions: Information in Schedule 1
paragraph: (c) into an ecozone to which the micro-organism is indigenous is not required to provide the information specified in subparagraphs 1(f)(i), (iii) and (iv) and paragraphs 1(i) and 5(a) of Schedule 1, but must, in a separate notification for each ecozone, provide the other information specified in that Schedule as well as the identification of the ecozone of intended introduction and the data that demonstrates that the micro-organism is indigenous to that ecozone.

heading: Introduction within 10 km of ecozone boundary
paragraph: (3) A person who manufactures or imports a micro-organism for introduction into an ecozone at a point within 10 km of the boundary of an ecozone referred to in paragraph (2)(a) or (c), as the case may be, may elect to have the introduction of the micro-organism considered to be in that ecozone and not into the actual ecozone of introduction, in which case the person must provide a notice in writing of the election and the information required by that paragraph.

heading: Information: Schedule 2
paragraph: (4) A person who manufactures in a contained facility or imports to a contained facility a micro-organism that is not for introduction outside the contained facility, or is for export only, is not required to provide the information specified in Schedule 1, but must provide the information specified in Schedule 2.

heading: Information: Schedule 3
paragraph: (5) A person who manufactures or imports a micro-organism for introduction in an experimental field study is not required to provide the information specified in Schedule 1, but must provide the information specified in Schedule 3.

heading: Information: Schedule 4
paragraph: (6) A person who manufactures a micro-organism at the site from which it was isolated, for introduction into the same site, is not required to provide the information specified in Schedule 1, but must provide the information specified in Schedule 4.

heading: Information: Schedule 5
paragraph: 4 A person who manufactures or imports an organism other than a micro-organism must provide the information specified in Schedule 5.

heading: Addition to Domestic Substances List - information
paragraph: 4.1 For the purposes of paragraph 112(1)(b) of the Act, a person who provides the information referred to in sections 3 and 4 must also provide - within 30 days after the day on which they manufactured or imported the organism - a notice confirming that manufacture or importation.

heading: Time limits
paragraph: 5 The information required under sections 3 and 4 must be provided as follows:

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (a) for the information required under

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (i) subsection 3(1), at least 120 days before the day on which the person manufactures or imports the micro-organism, and

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (ii) subsections 3(2) or (3), at least 120 days before the day on which the person manufactures or imports the micro-organism under conditions that trigger the requirement to provide the information;

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (b) for the information required under subsection 3(4) or (6), at least 30 days before the day on which the person manufactures or imports the micro-organism under conditions that trigger the requirement to provide the information;

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (c) for the information required under subsection 3(5), at least 90 days before the day on which the person manufactures or imports the micro-organism under conditions that trigger the requirement to provide the information; and

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (d) for the information required under section 4, at least 120 days before the day on which the person manufactures or imports the organism.

heading: Time limits
paragraph: 6 For the purposes of subsection 108(1) of the Act, the periods within which the Ministers must assess the information provided under sections 3 and 4 are as follows:

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (a) 120 days after receiving the information referred to in Schedule 1 or the other information required under subsection 3(2);

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (b) 30 days after receiving the information referred to in Schedule 2 or 4;

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (c) 90 days after receiving the information referred to in Schedule 3; and

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (d) 120 days after receiving the information referred to in Schedule 5.

heading: Five years
paragraph: 7 A person who is required to provide information to the Minister under these Regulations must keep a copy of that information and any supporting data at the person's principal place of business in Canada or at the principal place of business in Canada of a representative of that person. The information and the supporting data must be kept for a period of five years after the year in which the information is provided.

heading: Information and certification
paragraph: 8 (1) Any information to be provided to the Minister under these Regulations must include

heading: Information and certification
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and postal addresses and telephone number, as well as the fax number and e-mail address, if any, of the manufacturer or importer of the organism;

heading: Information and certification
paragraph: (b) the name, title, civic and postal addresses and telephone number, as well as the fax number and e-mail address, if any, of the person authorized to act on behalf of the manufacturer or importer of the organism, if any;

heading: Information and certification
paragraph: (c) the name, civic and postal addresses and telephone number, as well as the fax number and e-mail address, if any, of the head of the quality assurance unit of every laboratory that developed test data included in the information;

heading: Information and certification
paragraph: (d) an indication of whether the organism will be manufactured in or imported into Canada and the civic address of the site of manufacture in Canada of the organism or, if known, the port of entry into Canada of the organism, as the case may be; and

heading: Information and certification
paragraph: (e) a certification that the information is accurate and complete, dated and signed by the manufacturer or importer if they are resident in Canada or, if not, the person authorized to act on their behalf.

heading: Recipient
paragraph: (2) Two copies of any information provided under these Regulations must be sent in English or French to the Minister, care of the Substances Management Coordinator, Department of the Environment, Ottawa, Ontario K1A 0H3.

heading: Agent
paragraph: (3) If a person that provides the information under these Regulations is not resident in Canada, they must identify, under paragraph (1)(b), a person resident in Canada that is authorized to act on their behalf to whom any notice or correspondence may be sent and that is required to keep the information and any supporting data under section 7.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: 1 The following information in respect of the micro-organism:

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) its identification and the information substantiating its identification;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (b) its common and superseded names and any synonyms;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (c) its strain history;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (d) a description of any modifications to the micro-organism, including

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) the purpose of the modifications,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (ii) the methods and steps taken to make the modifications,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (iii) the phenotypic and genotypic changes that resulted from the steps referred to in subparagraph (ii),

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (iv) the stability of the changes referred to in subparagraph (iii), and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (v) the nature, source and function of any inserted genetic material;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (e) a description of the methods that can be used to distinguish and detect the micro-organism;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (f) a description of the biological and ecological characteristics of the micro-organism, including

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) its life cycle,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (ii) its infectivity, pathogenicity to non-human species, toxicity and toxigenicity,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (iii) its resistance to antibiotics and tolerance to metals and pesticides,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (iv) its involvement in biogeochemical cycling,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (v) the conditions required for, and conditions that limit, its survival, growth and replication, and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (vi) the mechanisms of its dispersal and the modes of interaction with any dispersal agents;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (g) a description of the mode of action in relation to the intended use;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (h) the identification of any patent or any application for a patent, as the case may be;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) the dispersal by gene transfer of traits of pathogenicity to non-human species, toxigenicity and resistance to antibiotics, including a description of

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) the genetic basis for pathogenicity to non-human species, toxigenicity and resistance to antibiotics,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (ii) the capability to transfer genes, and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (iii) the conditions that might select for dispersal of traits of pathogenicity to non-human species, toxigenicity and resistance to antibiotics, and whether the conditions are likely to exist at the locations of introduction or within the range of dispersal of the micro-organism; and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (j) a description of the geographic distribution of the micro-organism.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: 2 The following information in respect of the manufacture and importation of the micro-organism:

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) the identification of trade names and manufacturers, importers and vendors;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (b) the identification of locations of manufacture in Canada;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (c) the physical state of the formulation;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (d) the concentration of the micro-organism in the formulation;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (e) the identification and concentration of other ingredients and of any contaminants in the formulation;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (f) the viability of the micro-organism in the formulation;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (g) a description of any recommended storage and disposal procedures;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (h) an estimation of the quantity of the micro-organism that will be imported into or manufactured in Canada, as the case may be;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) a description of the equipment and methods of manufacture and of quality control and quality assurance procedures;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (j) a description of the location of manufacturing facilities in Canada;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (k) a description of the nature of potential releases of the micro-organism from the manufacturing facilities in Canada or from facilities to which the micro-organism will be imported, as the case may be, and the procedures to control releases; and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (l) a description of the procedures for the treatment and disposal of wastes containing the micro-organism from the manufacturing facilities in Canada.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: 3 The following information in respect of the introduction of the micro-organism:

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) the intended and potential uses;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (b) the history of use;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (c) a comparison of the natural habitat of the micro-organism to the habitat at the potential locations of its introduction, and the nature of the selection that may operate on the micro-organism at the potential locations of introduction;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (d) a description of the procedures for the introduction of the micro-organism, including

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) the method of application,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (ii) the quantity, frequency and duration of application, and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (iii) any activities associated with the introduction;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (e) a description of any contingency plans in the event of an accidental release; and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (f) a description of any recommended procedures for terminating the introduction of the micro-organism.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: 4 The following information in respect of the environmental fate of the micro-organism:

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) the identification of the plant and animal species likely to be exposed and, if infectivity, pathogenicity to non-human species, toxicity and toxigenicity have been identified under subparagraph 1(f)(ii), the identification of the receptor species likely to be exposed;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (b) a description of habitats where the micro-organism may persist or proliferate;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (c) the estimated quantities of the micro-organism in the air, water and soil at the points of introduction, and the estimated population trends; and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (d) any other information on the environmental fate of the micro-organism.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: 5 The following information in respect of the ecological effects of the micro-organism:

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) the data from tests conducted to determine the effects of the micro-organism on

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (i) aquatic plant, invertebrate and vertebrate species likely to be exposed to it, and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (ii) terrestrial plant, invertebrate and vertebrate species likely to be exposed to it;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (b) the involvement of the micro-organism in adverse ecological effects; and

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (c) the potential of the micro-organism to have adverse environmental impacts that could affect the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity.

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: 6 The following information in respect of the human health effects of the micro-organism:

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
paragraph: (a) any documented involvement of the micro-organism in adverse human health effects and a description of the characteristics of the micro-organism that distinguish it from known pathogens;

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Subsections 3(1) and (2) and paragraph 6(a))Information Required in Respect of Micro-organisms
