heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Oceans Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 In this Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: artificial island means any man-made extension of the seabed or a seabed feature, whether or not the extension breaks the surface of the superjacent waters; (ile artificielle)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Department means the Department of Fisheries and Oceans; (ministere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal laws includes Acts of Parliament, regulations as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Interpretation Act and any other rules of law within the jurisdiction of Parliament, but does not include laws of the Legislature of Yukon, of the Northwest Territories or for Nunavut; (droit)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: law, in respect of a province, includes a law or rule of law from time to time in force in the province, other than federal laws, and the provisions of any instrument having effect under any such law; (droit)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: marine installation or structure includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any ship and any anchor, anchor cable or rig pad used in connection therewith,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any offshore drilling unit, production platform, subsea installation, pumping station, living accommodation, storage structure, loading or landing platform, dredge, floating crane, pipelaying or other barge or pipeline and any anchor, anchor cable or rig pad used in connection therewith, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any other work or work within a class of works prescribed pursuant to paragraph 26(1)(a); (ouvrages en mer)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ship includes any description of vessel, boat or craft designed, used or capable of being used solely or partly for marine navigation without regard to method or lack of propulsion. (navire)

heading: Her Majesty
paragraph: 3 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Territorial sea of Canada
paragraph: 4 The territorial sea of Canada consists of a belt of sea that has as its inner limit the baselines described in section 5 and as its outer limit

heading: Territorial sea of Canada
paragraph: (a) subject to paragraph (b), the line every point of which is at a distance of 12 nautical miles from the nearest point of the baselines; or

heading: Territorial sea of Canada
paragraph: (b) in respect of the portions of the territorial sea of Canada for which geographical coordinates of points have been prescribed pursuant to subparagraph 25(a)(ii), lines determined from the geographical coordinates of points so prescribed.

heading: Determination of the baselines
paragraph: 5 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), the baseline is the low-water line along the coast or on a low-tide elevation that is situated wholly or partly at a distance not exceeding the breadth of the territorial sea of Canada from the mainland or an island.

heading: Geographical coordinates of points
paragraph: (2) In respect of any area for which geographical coordinates of points have been prescribed pursuant to subparagraph 25(a)(i) and subject to any exceptions in the regulations for

heading: Geographical coordinates of points
paragraph: (a) the use of the low-water line along the coast between given points, and

heading: Geographical coordinates of points
paragraph: (b) the use of the low-water lines of low-tide elevations that are situated wholly or partly at a distance not exceeding the breadth of the territorial sea of Canada from the mainland or an island,

heading: Geographical coordinates of points
paragraph: the baselines are straight lines interpreted as geodesics joining the consecutive geographical coordinates of points so prescribed.

heading: Baselines where historic title
paragraph: (3) In respect of any area not referred to in subsection (2), the baselines are the outer limits of any area, other than the territorial sea of Canada, over which Canada has a historic or other title of sovereignty.

heading: Low-tide elevations
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this section, a low-tide elevation is a naturally formed area of land that is surrounded by and above water at low tide but submerged at high tide.

heading: Internal waters of Canada
paragraph: 6 The internal waters of Canada consist of the waters on the landward side of the baselines of the territorial sea of Canada.

heading: Part of Canada
paragraph: 7 For greater certainty, the internal waters of Canada and the territorial sea of Canada form part of Canada.

heading: Rights of Her Majesty
paragraph: 8 (1) For greater certainty, in any area of the sea not within a province, the seabed and subsoil below the internal waters of Canada and the territorial sea of Canada are vested in Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Saving
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section abrogates or derogates from any legal right or interest held before February 4, 1991.

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: 9 (1) Subject to this section and to any other Act of Parliament, the laws of a province apply in any area of the sea

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: (a) that forms part of the internal waters of Canada or the territorial sea of Canada;

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: (b) that is not within any province; and

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: (c) that is prescribed by the regulations.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) Subject to any regulations made pursuant to paragraph 26(1)(d), subsection (1) does not apply in respect of any provision of a law of a province that

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (a) imposes a tax or royalty; or

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (b) relates to mineral or other non-living natural resources.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this section, the laws of a province shall be applied as if the area of the sea in which those laws apply under this section were within the territory of that province.

heading: Sums due to province
paragraph: (4) Any sum due under a law of a province that applies in an area of the sea under this section belongs to Her Majesty in right of the province.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (5) For greater certainty, this section shall not be interpreted as providing a basis for any claim, by or on behalf of a province, in respect of any interest in or legislative jurisdiction over any area of the sea in which a law of a province applies under this section or the living or non-living resources of that area, or as limiting the application of any federal laws.

heading: Contiguous zone of Canada
paragraph: 10 The contiguous zone of Canada consists of an area of the sea that has as its inner limit the outer limit of the territorial sea of Canada and as its outer limit the line every point of which is at a distance of 24 nautical miles from the nearest point of the baselines of the territorial sea of Canada, but does not include an area of the sea that forms part of the territorial sea of another state or in which another state has sovereign rights.

heading: Prevention in contiguous zone of infringement of federal laws
paragraph: 11 A person who is responsible for the enforcement of a federal law that is a customs, fiscal, immigration or sanitary law and who has reasonable grounds to believe that a person in the contiguous zone of Canada would, if that person were to enter Canada, commit an offence under that law may, subject to Canada's international obligations, prevent the entry of that person into Canada or the commission of the offence and, for greater certainty, section 25 of the Criminal Code applies in respect of the exercise by a person of any powers under this section.

heading: Enforcement in contiguous zone of federal laws
paragraph: 12 (1) Where there are reasonable grounds to believe that a person has committed an offence in Canada in respect of a federal law that is a customs, fiscal, immigration or sanitary law, every power of arrest, entry, search or seizure or other power that could be exercised in Canada in respect of that offence may also be exercised in the contiguous zone of Canada.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) A power of arrest referred to in subsection (1) shall not be exercised in the contiguous zone of Canada on board any ship registered outside Canada without the consent of the Attorney General of Canada.

heading: Exclusive economic zone of Canada
paragraph: 13 (1) The exclusive economic zone of Canada consists of an area of the sea beyond and adjacent to the territorial sea of Canada that has as its inner limit the outer limit of the territorial sea of Canada and as its outer limit

heading: Exclusive economic zone of Canada
paragraph: (a) subject to paragraph (b), the line every point of which is at a distance of 200 nautical miles from the nearest point of the baselines of the territorial sea of Canada; or

heading: Exclusive economic zone of Canada
paragraph: (b) in respect of a portion of the exclusive economic zone of Canada for which geographical coordinates of points have been prescribed pursuant to subparagraph 25(a)(iii), lines determined from the geographical coordinates of points so prescribed.

heading: Determination of the outer limit of the exclusive economic zone of Canada
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, paragraph (1)(a) applies regardless of whether regulations are made pursuant to subparagraph 25(a)(iv) prescribing geographical coordinates of points from which the outer limit of the exclusive economic zone of Canada may be determined.

heading: Sovereign rights and jurisdiction of Canada
paragraph: 14 Canada has

heading: Sovereign rights and jurisdiction of Canada
paragraph: (a) sovereign rights in the exclusive economic zone of Canada for the purpose of exploring and exploiting, conserving and managing the natural resources, whether living or non-living, of the waters superjacent to the seabed and of the seabed and its subsoil, and with regard to other activities for the economic exploitation and exploration of the exclusive economic zone of Canada, such as the production of energy from the water, currents and winds;

heading: Sovereign rights and jurisdiction of Canada
paragraph: (b) jurisdiction in the exclusive economic zone of Canada with regard to

heading: Sovereign rights and jurisdiction of Canada
paragraph: (i) the establishment and use of artificial islands, installations and structures,

heading: Sovereign rights and jurisdiction of Canada
paragraph: (ii) marine scientific research, and

heading: Sovereign rights and jurisdiction of Canada
paragraph: (iii) the protection and preservation of the marine environment; and

heading: Sovereign rights and jurisdiction of Canada
paragraph: (c) other rights and duties in the exclusive economic zone of Canada provided for under international law.

heading: Rights of Her Majesty
paragraph: 15 (1) For greater certainty, any rights of Canada in the seabed and subsoil of the exclusive economic zone of Canada and their resources are vested in Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Saving
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section abrogates or derogates from any legal right or interest held before February 4, 1991.

heading: Fishing zones of Canada
paragraph: 16 The fishing zones of Canada consist of areas of the sea adjacent to the coast of Canada that are prescribed in the regulations.

heading: Continental shelf of Canada
paragraph: 17 (1) The continental shelf of Canada is the seabed and subsoil of the submarine areas, including those of the exclusive economic zone of Canada, that extend beyond the territorial sea of Canada throughout the natural prolongation of the land territory of Canada

heading: Continental shelf of Canada
paragraph: (a) subject to paragraphs (b) and (c), to the outer edge of the continental margin, determined in the manner under international law that results in the maximum extent of the continental shelf of Canada, the continental margin being the submerged prolongation of the land mass of Canada consisting of the seabed and subsoil of the shelf, the slope and the rise, but not including the deep ocean floor with its oceanic ridges or its subsoil;

heading: Continental shelf of Canada
paragraph: (b) to a distance of 200 nautical miles from the baselines of the territorial sea of Canada where the outer edge of the continental margin does not extend up to that distance; or

heading: Continental shelf of Canada
paragraph: (c) in respect of a portion of the continental shelf of Canada for which geographical coordinates of points have been prescribed pursuant to subparagraph 25(a)(iii), to lines determined from the geographical coordinates of points so prescribed.

heading: Determination of the outer limit of the continental shelf of Canada
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) apply regardless of whether regulations are made pursuant to subparagraph 25(a)(iv) prescribing geographical coordinates of points from which the outer edge of the continental margin or other outer limit of the continental shelf of Canada may be determined.

heading: Sovereign rights of Canada
paragraph: 18 Canada has sovereign rights over the continental shelf of Canada for the purpose of exploring it and exploiting the mineral and other non-living natural resources of the seabed and subsoil of the continental shelf of Canada, together with living organisms belonging to sedentary species, that is to say, organisms that, at the harvestable stage, either are immobile on or under the seabed of the continental shelf of Canada or are unable to move except in constant physical contact with the seabed or the subsoil of the continental shelf of Canada.

heading: Rights of Her Majesty
paragraph: 19 (1) For greater certainty, any rights of Canada in the continental shelf of Canada are vested in Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Saving
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section abrogates or derogates from any legal right or interest held before February 4, 1991.

heading: Application of federal laws - continental shelf installations
paragraph: 20 (1) Subject to any regulations made pursuant to paragraph 26(1)(j) or (k), federal laws apply

heading: Application of federal laws - continental shelf installations
paragraph: (a) on or under any marine installation or structure from the time it is attached or anchored to the continental shelf of Canada in connection with the exploration of that shelf or the exploitation of its mineral or other non-living resources until the marine installation or structure is removed from the waters above the continental shelf of Canada;

heading: Application of federal laws - continental shelf installations
paragraph: (b) on or under any artificial island constructed, erected or placed on the continental shelf of Canada; and

heading: Application of federal laws - continental shelf installations
paragraph: (c) within such safety zone surrounding any marine installation or structure or artificial island referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) as is determined by or pursuant to the regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), federal laws shall be applied

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) as if the places referred to in that subsection formed part of the territory of Canada;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) notwithstanding that by their terms their application is limited to Canada; and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) in a manner that is consistent with the rights and freedoms of other states under international law and, in particular, with the rights and freedoms of other states in relation to navigation and overflight.

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: 21 (1) Subject to this section and to any other Act of Parliament, the laws of a province apply to the same extent as federal laws apply pursuant to section 20 in any area of the sea

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: (a) that forms part of the exclusive economic zone of Canada or is above the continental shelf of Canada;

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: (b) that is not within any province; and

heading: Application of provincial law
paragraph: (c) that is prescribed by the regulations.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (2) Subject to any regulations made pursuant to paragraph 26(1)(d), subsection (1) does not apply in respect of any provision of a law of a province that

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (a) imposes a tax or royalty; or

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (b) relates to mineral or other non-living natural resources.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this section, the laws of a province shall be applied as if the area of the sea in which those laws apply under this section were within the territory of that province.

heading: Sums due to province
paragraph: (4) Any sum due under a law of a province that applies in an area of the sea under this section belongs to Her Majesty in right of the province.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (5) For greater certainty, this section shall not be interpreted as providing a basis for any claim, by or on behalf of a province, in respect of any interest in or legislative jurisdiction over any area of the sea in which a law of a province applies under this section or the living or non-living resources of that area, or as limiting the application of any federal laws.

heading: Jurisdiction extended
paragraph: 22 (1) Subject to subsection (4) and to any regulations made pursuant to paragraph 26(1)(h), a court that would have jurisdiction in respect of any matter had the matter arisen in a province has jurisdiction in respect of any such matter involving a federal law that applies pursuant to this Act to the extent that the matter arises in whole or in part in any area of the sea that is not within any province and

heading: Jurisdiction extended
paragraph: (a) that area of the sea is nearer to the coast of that province than to the coast of any other province; or

heading: Jurisdiction extended
paragraph: (b) that province is prescribed by the regulations.

heading: Jurisdiction extended - provincial laws
paragraph: (2) Subject to any regulations made pursuant to paragraph 26(1)(h), a court that would have jurisdiction in respect of any matter had the matter arisen in a province has jurisdiction in respect of any such matter involving a law of the province that applies pursuant to this Act to the extent that the matter arises in whole or in part in any area of the sea to which the law of that province applies pursuant to this Act.

heading: Orders and powers
paragraph: (3) A court referred to in subsection (1) or (2) may make any order or exercise any power it considers necessary in respect of any matter referred to in that subsection.

heading: Criminal offences
paragraph: (4) The jurisdiction and powers of courts with respect to offences under any federal law are determined pursuant to sections 477.3, 481.1 and 481.2 of the Criminal Code.

heading: Saving
paragraph: (5) Nothing in this section limits the jurisdiction that a court may exercise apart from this Act.

heading: Definition of court
paragraph: (6) In this section, court includes a judge of a court and a justice of the peace.

heading: Certificate - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: 23 (1) In any legal or other proceedings, a certificate issued by or under the authority of the Minister of Foreign Affairs containing a statement that any geographic location specified in the certificate was, at any time material to the proceedings,

heading: Certificate - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (a) in the internal waters of Canada,

heading: Certificate - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (b) in the territorial sea of Canada,

heading: Certificate - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (c) in the contiguous zone of Canada,

heading: Certificate - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (d) in the exclusive economic zone of Canada, or

heading: Certificate - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (e) in or above the continental shelf of Canada

heading: Certificate - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: is conclusive proof of the truth of the statement without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have issued the certificate.

heading: Certificate - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (2) In any legal or other proceedings, a certificate issued by or under the authority of the Minister containing a statement that any geographic location specified in the certificate was, at any time material to the proceedings, within an area of the sea in which a law of the province named in the certificate applies under section 9 or 21 is conclusive proof of the truth of the statement without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have issued the certificate.

heading: Certificate cannot be compelled
paragraph: (3) A certificate referred to in subsection (1) or (2) is admissible in evidence in proceedings referred to in that subsection, but its production cannot be compelled.

heading: Saving
paragraph: 24 Nothing in this Part limits the operation that any Act, rule of law or instrument has apart from this Part.

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: 25 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs, make regulations

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (a) prescribing geographical coordinates of points from which

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (i) baselines may be determined under subsection 5(2) as straight lines interpreted as geodesics,

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (ii) in respect of a portion of the territorial sea of Canada prescribed in the regulations, an outer limit line may be determined, where, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, a portion of the territorial sea of Canada determined in accordance with paragraph 4(a) would conflict with the territorial sea of another state or other area of the sea in which another state has sovereign rights or would be unreasonably close to the coast of another state,

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (iii) in respect of a portion of the exclusive economic zone of Canada or the continental shelf of Canada prescribed in the regulations, an outer limit line may be determined, where, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, a portion of the exclusive economic zone of Canada or the continental shelf of Canada determined in accordance with paragraph 13(1)(a) or 17(1)(a) or (b) would conflict with the territorial sea of another state or other area of the sea in which another state has sovereign rights or would be unreasonably close to the coast of another state or is otherwise inappropriate, and

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (iv) the outer limit of the exclusive economic zone of Canada or the outer edge of the continental margin or other outer limit of the continental shelf of Canada may be determined; and

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Foreign Affairs
paragraph: (b) prescribing areas of the sea adjacent to the coast of Canada as fishing zones of Canada.

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: 26 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister of Justice, make regulations

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (a) prescribing a work or a class of works for the purpose of the definition marine installation or structure in section 2;

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (b) making any law of a province applicable in respect of any part of the area of the sea in which laws of the province apply under section 9 or 21, even though the law, by its own terms, is applicable only in respect of a particular area within the province;

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (c) restricting the application of subsection 9(1) or 21(1) to such laws of a province as are specified in the regulations;

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (d) making subsection 9(1) or 21(1) applicable, on the terms and conditions, if any, specified in the regulations, in respect of any laws of a province that impose a tax or royalty or relate to mineral or other non-living natural resources;

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (e) excluding any law of a province from the application of subsection 9(1) or 21(1);

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (f) determining or prescribing the method of determining the safety zone referred to in paragraph 20(1)(c);

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (g) prescribing an area of the sea and a province for the purposes of subsection 9(1), 21(1) or 22(1);

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (h) restricting the application of subsection 22(1), (2) or (3) to courts of a district or territorial division of a province;

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (i) prescribing, in respect of any area of the sea and for the purpose of subsection 22(1), the manner of determining the province that has the coast nearest to that area;

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (j) excluding any federal laws or laws of a province or any of their provisions from the application of subsection 20(1) or 21(1), as the case may be, in respect of any area in or above the continental shelf of Canada or in respect of any specified activity in any such area; and

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (k) making federal laws or laws of a province or any of their provisions applicable, in such circumstances as are specified in the regulations,

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (i) in the exclusive economic zone of Canada or in a portion of that zone,

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (ii) in or above the continental shelf of Canada or a portion of that shelf, or

heading: Recommendation - Minister of Justice
paragraph: (iii) in any area beyond the continental shelf of Canada, where that application is made pursuant to an international agreement or arrangement entered into by Canada.

heading: Restriction
paragraph: (2) A regulation made pursuant to subsection (1) in relation to a law of a province may be restricted to a specific area or place or to a specific provision of the law.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(j) and (k), federal laws and the laws of a province shall be applied

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) as if the places referred to in any regulations made pursuant to either of those paragraphs formed part of the territory of Canada;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) notwithstanding that by their terms their application is limited to Canada or a province; and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) in a manner that is consistent with the rights and freedoms of other states under international law and, in particular, with the rights and freedoms of other states in relation to navigation and overflight.

heading: Publication of proposed regulations
paragraph: 27 (1) A copy of each regulation that the Governor in Council proposes to make pursuant to paragraph 25(b) or section 26 shall be published in the Canada Gazette at least 60 days before its proposed effective date, and a reasonable opportunity shall be given to interested persons and provinces to make representations with respect to the proposed regulation.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) No proposed regulation that has been published pursuant to this section need again be published under this section, whether or not it has been altered.

heading: Part does not apply to inland waters
paragraph: 28 For greater certainty, this Part does not apply in respect of rivers and lakes.

heading: Development and implementation of strategy
paragraph: 29 The Minister, in collaboration with other ministers, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada, with provincial and territorial governments and with affected aboriginal organizations, coastal communities and other persons and bodies, including those bodies established under land claims agreements, shall lead and facilitate the development and implementation of a national strategy for the management of estuarine, coastal and marine ecosystems in waters that form part of Canada or in which Canada has sovereign rights under international law.

heading: Principles of strategy
paragraph: 30 The national strategy will be based on the principles of

heading: Principles of strategy
paragraph: (a) sustainable development, that is, development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs;

heading: Principles of strategy
paragraph: (b) the integrated management of activities in estuaries, coastal waters and marine waters that form part of Canada or in which Canada has sovereign rights under international law; and

heading: Principles of strategy
paragraph: (c) the precautionary approach, that is, erring on the side of caution.

heading: Integrated management plans
paragraph: 31 The Minister, in collaboration with other ministers, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada, with provincial and territorial governments and with affected aboriginal organizations, coastal communities and other persons and bodies, including those bodies established under land claims agreements, shall lead and facilitate the development and implementation of plans for the integrated management of all activities or measures in or affecting estuaries, coastal waters and marine waters that form part of Canada or in which Canada has sovereign rights under international law.

heading: Implementation of integrated management plans
paragraph: 32 For the purpose of the implementation of integrated management plans, the Minister

heading: Implementation of integrated management plans
paragraph: (a) shall develop and implement policies and programs with respect to matters assigned by law to the Minister;

heading: Implementation of integrated management plans
paragraph: (b) shall coordinate with other ministers, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada the implementation of policies and programs of the Government with respect to all activities or measures in or affecting coastal waters and marine waters;

heading: Implementation of integrated management plans
paragraph: (c) may, on his or her own or jointly with another person or body or with another minister, board or agency of the Government of Canada, and taking into consideration the views of other ministers, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada, provincial and territorial governments and affected aboriginal organizations, coastal communities and other persons and bodies, including those bodies established under land claims agreements,

heading: Implementation of integrated management plans
paragraph: (i) establish advisory or management bodies and appoint or designate, as appropriate, members of those bodies, and

heading: Implementation of integrated management plans
paragraph: (ii) recognize established advisory or management bodies; and

heading: Implementation of integrated management plans
paragraph: (d) may, in consultation with other ministers, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada, with provincial and territorial governments and with affected aboriginal organizations, coastal communities and other persons and bodies, including those bodies established under land claims agreements, establish marine environmental quality guidelines, objectives and criteria respecting estuaries, coastal waters and marine waters.

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: 33 (1) In exercising the powers and performing the duties and functions assigned to the Minister by this Act, the Minister

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (a) shall cooperate with other ministers, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada, with provincial and territorial governments and with affected aboriginal organizations, coastal communities and other persons and bodies, including those bodies established under land claims agreements;

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (b) may enter into agreements with any person or body or with another minister, board or agency of the Government of Canada;

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (c) shall gather, compile, analyse, coordinate and disseminate information;

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (d) may make grants and contributions on terms and conditions approved by the Treasury Board; and

heading: Cooperation and agreements
paragraph: (e) may make recoverable expenditures on behalf of and at the request of any other minister, board or agency of the Government of Canada or of a province or any person or body.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) In exercising the powers and performing the duties and functions mentioned in this Part, the Minister may consult with other ministers, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada, with provincial and territorial governments and with affected aboriginal organizations, coastal communities and other persons and bodies, including those bodies established under land claims agreements.

heading: Logistics support, etc.
paragraph: 34 The Minister may coordinate logistics support and provide related assistance for the purposes of advancing scientific knowledge of estuarine, coastal and marine ecosystems.

heading: Marine protected areas
paragraph: 35 (1) A marine protected area is an area of the sea that forms part of the internal waters of Canada, the territorial sea of Canada or the exclusive economic zone of Canada and has been designated under this section or section 35.1 for special protection for one or more of the following reasons:

heading: Marine protected areas
paragraph: (a) the conservation and protection of commercial and non-commercial fishery resources, including marine mammals, and their habitats;

heading: Marine protected areas
paragraph: (b) the conservation and protection of endangered or threatened marine species, and their habitats;

heading: Marine protected areas
paragraph: (c) the conservation and protection of unique habitats;

heading: Marine protected areas
paragraph: (d) the conservation and protection of marine areas of high biodiversity or biological productivity;

heading: Marine protected areas
paragraph: (e) the conservation and protection of any other marine resource or habitat as is necessary to fulfil the mandate of the Minister; and

heading: Marine protected areas
paragraph: (f) the conservation and protection of marine areas for the purpose of maintaining ecological integrity.

heading: Definition of ecological integrity
paragraph: (1.1) For the purpose of paragraph (1)(f), ecological integrity means a condition in which

heading: Definition of ecological integrity
paragraph: (a) the structure, composition and function of ecosystems are undisturbed by any human activity;

heading: Definition of ecological integrity
paragraph: (b) natural ecological processes are intact and self-sustaining;

heading: Definition of ecological integrity
paragraph: (c) ecosystems evolve naturally; and

heading: Definition of ecological integrity
paragraph: (d) an ecosystem's capacity for self-renewal and its biodiversity are maintained.

heading: Network of marine protected areas
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of integrated management plans referred to in sections 31 and 32, the Minister shall lead and coordinate the development and implementation of a national network of marine protected areas on behalf of the Government of Canada.

heading: Performance of duties and functions
paragraph: (2.1) In performing his or her duties and functions under subsection (2), the Minister shall ensure that:

heading: Performance of duties and functions
paragraph: (a) clearly identified objectives are set with regard to each marine protected area; and

heading: Performance of duties and functions
paragraph: (b) the network of marine protected areas covers diverse habitat types, biogeographic regions and environmental conditions.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (3) The Governor in Council, on the recommendation of the Minister, may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) designating marine protected areas;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) delineating zones within marine protected areas;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) prohibiting classes of activities within marine protected areas; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting any other matter consistent with the purpose of the designation.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 35.1 (1) The following definitions apply in this section.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: foreign national has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. (etranger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: foreign ship means a ship that is a foreign vessel, as defined in section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. (navire etranger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ongoing means, with respect to an activity in the area of the sea that is designated by an order made under subsection (2) as a marine protected area, that the activity

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) was lawfully carried out in the year immediately before the day on which the order comes into force and does not require an authorization, including a permit or licence, under any applicable federal laws or laws of a province;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) was lawfully carried out in the year immediately before the day on which the order comes into force and was authorized, including by a permit or licence, under any applicable federal laws or laws of a province; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) was not carried out before the day on which the order comes into force, but was authorized and continues to be authorized, including by a permit or licence, under any applicable federal laws or laws of a province. (en cours)

heading: Designation of marine protected area - Minister's order
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, by order, designate a marine protected area in any area of the sea that is not designated as a marine protected area under paragraph 35(3)(a), in a manner that is not inconsistent with a land claims agreement that has been given effect and has been ratified or approved by an Act of Parliament and, in that order, the Minister

heading: Designation of marine protected area - Minister's order
paragraph: (a) shall list the classes of activities that are ongoing activities in the marine protected area;

heading: Designation of marine protected area - Minister's order
paragraph: (b) shall prohibit, in the marine protected area, any activity that is not part of a class of activities set out in paragraph (a) and that disturbs, damages, destroys or removes from that marine protected area any unique geological or archeological features or any living marine organism or any part of its habitat or is likely to do so;

heading: Designation of marine protected area - Minister's order
paragraph: (c) may prohibit, in the marine protected area, any activity that is part of a class of activities set out in paragraph (a) and that is governed by an Act of Parliament under which the Minister is responsible for the management, conservation or protection of fisheries resources; and

heading: Designation of marine protected area - Minister's order
paragraph: (d) may exempt from the prohibition in paragraph (b) or (c), subject to any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate, any activity referred to in those paragraphs in the marine protected area by a foreign national, an entity incorporated or formed by or under the laws of a country other than Canada, a foreign ship or a foreign state.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (3) The prohibitions set out in an order made under subsection (2) do not apply to the following activities:

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a) activities that are carried out in response to an emergency situation or that are carried out by or on behalf of Her Majesty for the purpose of public safety, national defence, national security or law enforcement; and

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (b) marine scientific research activities that are consistent with the purpose of the designation of the marine protected area and that are authorized under federal laws or laws of a province, if required to be so authorized.

heading: Publication of report
paragraph: (4) If an order is made under subsection (2), the Minister shall publish, in any manner that the Minister considers appropriate, a report

heading: Publication of report
paragraph: (a) indicating the area of the sea designated in the order;

heading: Publication of report
paragraph: (b) summarizing the consultations undertaken prior to making the order; and

heading: Publication of report
paragraph: (c) summarizing the information that the Minister considered when making the order, which may include environmental, social, cultural or economic information.

heading: Powers, duties and functions
paragraph: 35.2 The Governor in Council and the Minister shall not use lack of scientific certainty regarding the risks posed by any activity that may be carried out in certain areas of the sea as a reason to postpone or refrain from exercising their powers or performing their duties and functions under subsection 35(3) or 35.1(2).

heading: Recommendation of Minister
paragraph: 35.3 (1) The Minister shall, not later than the fifth anniversary of the day on which an order under subsection 35.1(2) comes into force,

heading: Recommendation of Minister
paragraph: (a) recommend to the Governor in Council that the Governor in Council make a regulation under subsection 35(3) to designate a marine protected area covering at least part of the area of the sea that is designated by the order made under subsection 35.1(2); or

heading: Interim marine protected areas in emergency situations
paragraph: 36 (1) The Governor in Council, on the recommendation of the Minister, may make orders exercising any power under section 35 on an emergency basis, where the Minister is of the opinion that a marine resource or habitat is or is likely to be at risk to the extent that such orders are not inconsistent with a land claims agreement that has been given effect and has been ratified or approved by an Act of Parliament.

heading: Exemption from Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (2) An order made under this section is exempt from the application of sections 3, 5 and 11 of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Inconsistency
paragraph: (4) In the event of any inconsistency between an order made under subsection (1) and an order made under subsection 35.1(2), the order made under subsection (1) prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Enforcement officers
paragraph: 39 (1) The Minister may designate persons or classes of persons as enforcement officers for the purposes of the administration and enforcement of this Act and the regulations.

heading: Designation of provincial government employees
paragraph: (2) The Minister may not designate any person or class of persons employed by the government of a province unless that government agrees.

heading: Certificate of designation
paragraph: (3) Every enforcement officer must be provided with a certificate of designation as an enforcement officer in a form approved by the Minister and, on entering any place under this Act, the officer shall, if so requested, show the certificate to the occupant or person in charge of the place.

heading: Powers of peace officers
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this Act and the regulations, enforcement officers have all the powers of a peace officer, but the Minister may specify limits on those powers when designating any person or class of persons.

heading: Exemptions for law enforcement activities
paragraph: (5) For the purpose of investigations and other law enforcement activities under this Act, the Minister may, on any terms and conditions the Minister considers necessary, exempt enforcement officers who are carrying out duties or functions under this Act, and persons acting under their direction and control, from the application of any provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (6) When an enforcement officer is carrying out duties or functions under this Act or the regulations, no person shall

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (a) knowingly make any false or misleading statement either orally or in writing to the enforcement officer; or

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (b) otherwise wilfully obstruct the enforcement officer.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: 39.1 (1) For a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Act and the regulations, an enforcement officer may enter and inspect any place, including any conveyance, in which the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe, that there is any thing to which this Act or the regulations apply or any book, record, electronic data or other document relating to the application of this Act or the regulations, and the enforcement officer may, for that purpose,

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) open or cause to be opened any container that the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe contains that thing, book, record, electronic data or other document;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) examine the thing and take samples free of charge;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) require any person to produce the book, record, electronic data or other document for examination or copying, in whole or in part;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (d) use or cause to be used any computer system or data processing system at the place being inspected to examine any data contained in, or available to, the system;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (e) reproduce any record or cause it to be reproduced from the data in the form of a printout or other intelligible output and remove the printout or other output for examination or copying; and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (f) use or cause to be used any copying equipment at the place being inspected to make copies of any book, record, electronic data or other document.

heading: Disposition of samples
paragraph: (1.1) An enforcement officer may dispose of a sample taken under paragraph (1)(b) in any manner that the officer considers appropriate.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (1.2) For the purposes of subsection (1), the enforcement officer may seize any thing that the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (a) was used in the contravention of this Act or the regulations;

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (b) is something in relation to which this Act or the regulations have been contravened; or

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (c) was obtained by the contravention of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (1.3) The owner or the person in charge of the place, and every person found in the place, shall

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (a) give the enforcement officer all assistance that is reasonably required to enable the officer to exercise their powers or to perform their duties or functions under this section; and

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (b) provide the enforcement officer with any information or any book, record, electronic data or other document, and access to any data, that are reasonably required for that purpose.

heading: Conveyance
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of carrying out the inspection, the enforcement officer may stop a conveyance or direct that it be moved to any place, including in Canadian waters or the exclusive economic zone of Canada, where the inspection can be carried out.

heading: Passage through private property
paragraph: (2.1) An enforcement officer and any person accompanying them may enter and pass through private property, other than a dwelling-place, in order to gain entry to a place referred to in subsection (1). For greater certainty, neither person is liable for doing so.

heading: Passage through private property by authorized person
paragraph: (2.2) A person acting under the direction and control of an enforcement officer may, for the purposes of exercising the officer's powers or performing the officer's duties and functions under this section, enter and pass through private property, other than a dwelling-place, in order to gain entry to a marine protected area. For greater certainty, the person is not liable for doing so.

heading: Dwelling-place
paragraph: (3) The enforcement officer may not enter a dwelling-place except with the consent of the occupant or person in charge of the dwelling-place or under the authority of a warrant.

heading: Warrant
paragraph: (4) Where on ex parte application a justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Warrant
paragraph: (a) the conditions for entry described in subsection (1) exist in relation to a dwelling-place,

heading: Warrant
paragraph: (b) entry to the dwelling-place is necessary in relation to the administration of this Act or the regulations, and

heading: Warrant
paragraph: (c) entry to the dwelling-place has been refused or there are reasonable grounds for believing that entry will be refused,

heading: Warrant
paragraph: the justice may issue a warrant authorizing the enforcement officer to enter the dwelling-place subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant.

heading: Direction of ship to place
paragraph: 39.2 An enforcement officer may direct a ship to move to any place in Canadian waters or the exclusive economic zone of Canada if they have reasonable grounds to believe that the ship or a person on board the ship has committed, is committing or is about to commit an offence under this Act in Canadian waters or the exclusive economic zone of Canada and that the ship was, is being or is about to be used in connection with the commission of the offence.

heading: Detention order to ship
paragraph: 39.21 (1) An enforcement officer may make a detention order in relation to a ship if they have reasonable grounds to believe that the ship or a person on board the ship has committed an offence under this Act in Canadian waters or the exclusive economic zone of Canada and that the ship was used in connection with the commission of the offence.

heading: Order in writing
paragraph: (2) The detention order shall be in writing and addressed to all persons, at any port in Canada where the ship to which the order relates is or will be located, who are empowered to give a clearance in respect of the ship.

heading: Service of order
paragraph: (3) Notice of the detention order shall be served by delivering a copy of the notice personally to the master or another officer, the authorized representative, the owner or the operator of the ship, or if service cannot reasonably be effected personally, by posting a copy of the notice on any conspicuous part of the ship.

heading: Duty after service of order
paragraph: (4) Once notice of the detention order is served on any person referred to in subsection (3), the ship shall not move, other than in accordance with any conditions specified in the order, until the order has been rescinded.

heading: No clearance after receiving order
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), a person who has received the detention order shall not give clearance to the ship to which the order relates.

heading: When clearance may be given
paragraph: (6) A person who has received the detention order may give clearance to the ship to which the order relates if

heading: When clearance may be given
paragraph: (a) neither the ship nor any person is charged with the offence that gave rise to the making of the order within 30 days after the day on which the order is made;

heading: When clearance may be given
paragraph: (b) within 30 days after the day on which the order is made, the ship or a person is charged with the offence and every accused has appeared in Canada to answer to the charge;

heading: When clearance may be given
paragraph: (c) Her Majesty in right of Canada is given security, in a form determined by the Minister, for payment of the maximum fine that may be imposed as a result of a conviction of every accused and costs that might be incurred in proceedings in connection with the charge or charges, or payment of any lesser amount that is approved by the Minister;

heading: When clearance may be given
paragraph: (d) all proceedings in respect of the offence that gave rise to the making of the order are discontinued; or

heading: When clearance may be given
paragraph: (e) the order is rescinded by an enforcement officer.

heading: Compliance order
paragraph: 39.22 (1) If an enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that a person is committing an offence under this Act - or is about to commit an offence under this Act - the enforcement officer may issue a compliance order directing any person described in subsection (3) to take, at their own expense, any of the measures referred to in subsection (4) that the enforcement officer believes are reasonable in the circumstances, and consistent with the protection and preservation of the marine environment and with public safety, in order to cease the commission of the offence or to refrain from committing it.

heading: Order to ship
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), an order is deemed to have been given to the ship and is binding on it, if

heading: Order to ship
paragraph: (a) the order is given to the master or another officer, the authorized representative, the owner or the operator of the ship; or

heading: Order to ship
paragraph: (b) in the case of an order that cannot be given to any person referred to in paragraph (a) despite reasonable efforts having been made to do so, the order is posted on any conspicuous part of the ship.

heading: Persons subject to compliance order
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) applies to any person who causes or contributes to, or is likely to cause or contribute to, the offence.

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (4) The compliance order may require that the person to whom it is directed take one or more of the following measures:

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (a) do anything to comply with this Act or the regulations;

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (b) refrain from doing anything in contravention of this Act or the regulations;

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (c) cease any activity for a specified period or until the enforcement officer is satisfied that the activity is in compliance with this Act and the regulations;

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (d) move any conveyance to a location by the route and in the manner that the enforcement officer specifies;

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (e) unload or reload the contents of any conveyance; and

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (f) take any other reasonable measure that the enforcement officer considers necessary to facilitate compliance with the order - or to restore the components of the marine environment damaged by the offence or to protect the components of the marine environment that would be put at risk if the offence were committed - including

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (i) maintaining records on any relevant matter,

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (ii) reporting periodically to the enforcement officer, and

heading: Specific measures
paragraph: (iii) submitting to the enforcement officer any information, proposal or plan specified by the enforcement officer that sets out any action to be taken by the person with respect to the subject-matter of the order.

heading: Contents of compliance order
paragraph: (5) Subject to section 39.23, the compliance order shall be made in writing and shall set out

heading: Contents of compliance order
paragraph: (a) the name of the person or persons to whom it is directed;

heading: Contents of compliance order
paragraph: (b) the provisions of this Act or the regulations, or the order made under subsection 35.1(2) or 36(1), that has been or that is about to be contravened;

heading: Contents of compliance order
paragraph: (c) the relevant facts surrounding the offence described in subsection (1);

heading: Contents of compliance order
paragraph: (d) the measures to be taken; and

heading: Contents of compliance order
paragraph: (e) the time or the day when each measure is to begin or the period during which it is to be carried out.

heading: Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (6) A compliance order is not a statutory instrument for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Order given orally
paragraph: 39.23 (1) In the case of exigent circumstances, a compliance order may be given orally on the condition that it is followed, within seven days after the day on which the oral order was issued, by a written order issued in accordance with section 39.22.

heading: Exigent circumstances
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), exigent circumstances include circumstances in which the delay necessary to issue a written order that meets the requirements of subsection 39.22(5) would result in danger to human life or the marine environment.

heading: Compliance with compliance order
paragraph: 39.24 (1) A person to whom a compliance order is issued shall, immediately on receipt of the order or a copy of it, or on being given an order orally under subsection 39.23(1), comply with the order.

heading: No bar to proceedings
paragraph: (2) The issuance of, or compliance with, a compliance order is not a bar to any proceedings against the person under this or any other Act in relation to the offence described in subsection 39.22(1).

heading: Intervention by enforcement officer
paragraph: 39.25 (1) If a person to whom a compliance order is issued fails to take any measures specified in the order, an enforcement officer may take the measures or cause them to be taken.

heading: Access to property
paragraph: (2) An enforcement officer or other person authorized by an enforcement officer to take measures under subsection (1) may enter and have access to any place, other than a dwelling-place, and may do any reasonable thing that may be necessary in the circumstances.

heading: Personal liability
paragraph: (3) A person, other than a person described in subsection 39.22(3), who provides assistance or advice to the enforcement officer in taking the measures specified in an order or who takes any measures authorized or required by an enforcement officer under subsection (1) is not personally liable either civilly or criminally in respect of any act or omission in the course of providing assistance or advice or taking any measures under that subsection unless it is established that the person acted in bad faith.

heading: Recovery of reasonable costs and expenses by Her Majesty
paragraph: 39.26 (1) Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover the costs and expenses of, and any costs and expenses incidental to, any measures taken under subsection 39.25(1) from any person referred to in subsection 39.22(3).

heading: Costs reasonably incurred
paragraph: (2) The costs and expenses may be recovered only to the extent that they can be established to have been reasonably incurred in the circumstances.

heading: Liability
paragraph: (3) The persons referred to in subsection (1) are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for the costs and expenses referred to in that subsection.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (4) A claim under this section may be sued for and recovered by Her Majesty in right of Canada with costs in proceedings brought or taken in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Recourse or indemnity
paragraph: (5) This section does not limit or restrict any right of recourse or indemnity that a person may have against any other person.

heading: Limitation and prescription
paragraph: (6) If events giving rise to a claim under this section occur, proceedings in respect of the claim may be commenced not later than five years after the day on which the events occur.

heading: Custody of things seized
paragraph: 39.3 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (3.1), if an enforcement officer seizes a thing under this Act or under a warrant issued under the Criminal Code,

heading: Custody of things seized
paragraph: (a) sections 489.1 and 490 of the Criminal Code apply; and

heading: Custody of things seized
paragraph: (b) the enforcement officer, or any person that the officer may designate, shall retain custody of the thing, subject to any order made under section 490 of the Criminal Code.

heading: Forfeiture where ownership not ascertainable
paragraph: (2) Where the lawful ownership of or entitlement to the seized thing cannot be ascertained within thirty days after its seizure, the thing or any proceeds of its disposition are forfeited to

heading: Forfeiture where ownership not ascertainable
paragraph: (a) Her Majesty in right of Canada, if the thing was seized by an enforcement officer employed in the federal public administration; or

heading: Forfeiture where ownership not ascertainable
paragraph: (b) Her Majesty in right of a province, if the thing was seized by an enforcement officer employed by the government of that province.

heading: Perishable things
paragraph: (3) Where the seized thing is perishable, the enforcement officer may dispose of it or destroy it, and any proceeds of its disposition must be

heading: Perishable things
paragraph: (a) paid to the lawful owner or person lawfully entitled to possession of the thing, unless proceedings under this Act are commenced within ninety days after its seizure; or

heading: Perishable things
paragraph: (b) retained by the enforcement officer pending the outcome of the proceedings.

heading: Release of seized fish
paragraph: (3.1) The enforcement officer who seizes any fish as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Fisheries Act may, at the time of the seizure, return to the water any fish that they believe to be alive.

heading: Abandonment
paragraph: (4) The owner of the seized thing may abandon it to Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Disposition by Minister
paragraph: 39.4 Any thing that has been forfeited or abandoned under this Act must be dealt with and disposed of as the Minister may direct.

heading: Liability for costs
paragraph: 39.5 The lawful owner and any person lawfully entitled to possession of any thing seized, detained, abandoned or forfeited under this Act are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for all the costs of inspection, seizure, detention, abandonment, forfeiture or disposition incurred by Her Majesty in right of Canada in excess of any proceeds of disposition of the thing that have been forfeited to Her Majesty under this Act.

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: 39.6 (1) Every individual or corporation that contravenes subsection 39.21(5) or 39.24(1), a regulation made under paragraph 35(3)(c) or (d) or 52.1(a), or an order made under subsection 35.1(2) or 36(1) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (i) in the case of an individual,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $15,000 and not more than $1,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $30,000 and not more than $2,000,000,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a corporation, other than a corporation referred to in subparagraph (iii),

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $500,000 and not more than $6,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $1,000,000 and not more than $12,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (iii) in the case of a corporation that the court has determined to be a small revenue corporation,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $75,000 and not more than $4,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $150,000 and not more than $8,000,000; or

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (i) in the case of an individual,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $5,000 and not more than $300,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $10,000 and not more than $600,000,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a corporation, other than a corporation referred to in subparagraph (iii),

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $100,000 and not more than $4,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $200,000 and not more than $8,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (iii) in the case of a corporation that the court has determined to be a small revenue corporation,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $25,000 and not more than $2,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $50,000 and not more than $4,000,000.

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (2) Every ship that contravenes subsection 39.21(4) or 39.24(1), a regulation made under paragraph 35(3)(c) or (d) or 52.1(a), an order made under subsection 35.1(2) or 36(1) or a direction made under section 39.2 is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (i) in the case of a ship of 7 500 tonnes deadweight or more,

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $500,000 and not more than $6,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $1,000,000 and not more than $12,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a ship of less than 7 500 tonnes deadweight,

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $75,000 and not more than $4,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $150,000 and not more than $8,000,000; or

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (i) in the case of a ship of 7 500 tonnes deadweight or more,

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $100,000 and not more than $4,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $200,000 and not more than $8,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a ship of less than 7 500 tonnes deadweight,

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (A) for a first offence, to a fine of not less than $25,000 and not more than $2,000,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (B) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not less than $50,000 and not more than $4,000,000.

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (3) Every individual or corporation that contravenes subsection 39(6) or a regulation made under paragraph 52.1(b) or (c) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $500,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $1,000,000; or

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $100,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - persons
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $200,000.

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (4) Every ship that contravenes any regulation made under paragraph 52.1(b) or (c) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $500,000, and

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $1,000,000; or

heading: Offence and punishment - ship
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

paragraph: (i) for a first offence, to a fine of not more than $100,000, and
