paragraph: (ii) for a second or subsequent offence, to a fine of not more than $200,000.

heading: Small revenue corporation status
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of subsection (1), a court may determine a corporation to be a small revenue corporation if the court is satisfied that the corporation's gross revenues for the year immediately before the day on which the offence is committed - or, if the offence is committed on more than one day, for the year immediately before the first day on which the offence is committed - were not more than $5,000,000.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (6) The minimum amounts of fines set out in this section do not apply to any proceeding brought in accordance with subsection 39.93(1) or under the Contraventions Act.

heading: Liability of directors, officers or agents or mandataries
paragraph: 39.61 If a corporation or a ship owned or operated by a corporation commits an offence under section 39.6, any director, officer, agent or mandatary of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the penalty provided for by that section for an individual in respect of the offence committed by the corporation or the ship, whether or not the corporation or the ship has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Liability of owners, operators, masters and chief engineers of ships
paragraph: 39.62 If a ship commits an offence under section 39.6 and the owner, operator, master or chief engineer of the ship directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in the commission of the offence, the owner, operator, master or chief engineer, as the case may be, is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the penalty provided for by that section for an individual who commits an offence under that section, whether or not the ship has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 39.63 (1) A person shall not be found guilty of an offence under section 39.6, other than an offence consisting of a contravention of subsection 39(6), if the person establishes that they exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence.

heading: Defence - ship
paragraph: (2) If a ship is prosecuted for an offence, only the persons referred to in subsection 39.67(5) may establish, for the purposes of subsection (1), that they exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence.

heading: Contravention of unpublished order
paragraph: (3) A person shall not be found guilty of an offence consisting of a contravention of an order made under subsection 36(1) that, at the time of the alleged contravention, had not been published in the Canada Gazette unless it is proved that reasonable steps had been taken before that time to bring the purport of the order to the attention of those persons likely to be affected by it.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph: 39.64 (1) A person who commits or continues an offence on more than one day is liable to be convicted for a separate offence for each day on which the offence is committed or continued.

heading: Fines cumulative
paragraph: (2) If a person is convicted of an offence involving more than one animal, plant, other organism or object, the fine to be imposed in respect of that offence may be, despite section 39.6, the total of the fines that would have been imposed if each of the animals, plants, organisms or objects had been the subject of a separate information.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: (3) If a person is convicted of an offence and the court is satisfied that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any property, benefit or advantage, the court shall order them to pay an additional fine in an amount equal to the court's estimation of the value of that property, benefit or advantage. The additional fine may exceed the maximum amount of any fine that may otherwise be imposed under section 39.6.

heading: Deeming - second and subsequent offence
paragraph: (4) A conviction for a particular offence under section 39.6 is deemed to be a conviction for a second or subsequent offence if the court is satisfied that the person has been previously convicted - under any Act of Parliament or an Act of a provincial legislature that relates to environmental or wildlife protection or conservation - of a substantially similar offence.

heading: Application
paragraph: (5) Subsection (4) applies only to previous convictions on indictment, to previous convictions on summary conviction and to previous convictions under any similar procedure under an Act of a provincial legislature.

heading: Relief from minimum fine
paragraph: 39.65 The court may impose a fine that is less than the minimum amount provided for in section 39.6 if it is satisfied, on the basis of evidence submitted to the court, that the minimum fine would cause undue financial hardship to the person who has been convicted of an offence. The court shall provide reasons if it imposes a fine that is less than the minimum amount.

heading: Application of fines
paragraph: 39.66 (1) All fines received by the Receiver General in respect of the commission of an offence under this Act, other than fines collected under the Contraventions Act, are to be credited to the Environmental Damages Fund, an account in the accounts of Canada, and used for purposes related to the conservation, protection or restoration of marine protected areas, or for administering that Fund.

heading: Recommendations of court
paragraph: (2) The court imposing the fine may recommend to the Minister that all or a portion of the fine credited to the Environmental Damages Fund be paid to a person or an organization specified by the court for a purpose referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Application to ships
paragraph: 39.67 (1) The provisions of this Part - and those of any regulations or orders made under this Part or any regulations made under section 52.1 - relating to indictable or summary conviction offences that apply to persons also apply to ships, with any modifications that the circumstances require.

heading: Application of Criminal Code
paragraph: (2) The provisions of the Criminal Code relating to indictable or summary conviction offences that apply to persons also apply to ships, with any modifications that the circumstances require.

heading: Service
paragraph: (3) When a ship is charged with an offence under section 39.6, the summons may be served by leaving it with the master or another officer, the authorized representative, the owner or the operator of the ship, or if it cannot reasonably be left with any of those persons, by posting a copy of it on any conspicuous part of the ship.

heading: Appearance at trial
paragraph: (4) If a ship is charged with an offence under section 39.6, the ship may appear by counsel or representative before the court. Despite the Criminal Code, if the ship does not so appear, a court may, on proof of service of the summons, proceed to hold the trial.

heading: Proof of offence by ship
paragraph: (5) If a ship is prosecuted for an offence under section 39.6, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that the act or omission that constitutes the offence was committed by the master of the ship or any other person on board the ship, whether or not the person on board has been identified or has been prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Direction binding ship
paragraph: (6) For the purpose of prosecuting a ship for contravening a direction made under section 39.2, any direction made under that section that is given to the master or another officer, the authorized representative, the owner or the operator of the ship is deemed to have been given to the ship and is binding on it.

heading: Notice of detention order binding ship
paragraph: (7) For the purpose of prosecuting a ship for contravening of subsection 39.21(4), the notice of the detention order served in accordance with subsection 39.21(3) is deemed to have been served on the ship and is binding on it.

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: 39.68 (1) In addition to the principles and factors that the court is otherwise required to consider, including those set out in sections 718.1 to 718.21 of the Criminal Code, the court shall consider the following principles when sentencing a person who is convicted of an offence under this Act:

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (a) the amount of the fine should be increased to account for every aggravating factor associated with the offence, including the aggravating factors set out in subsection (2); and

heading: Sentencing principles
paragraph: (b) the amount of the fine should reflect the gravity of each aggravating factor associated with the offence.

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (2) The aggravating factors to be considered by the court in respect of a person convicted of an offence are the following:

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (a) the offence caused damage or a risk of damage to any marine resource, habitat or ecosystem;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (b) the offence caused damage or a risk of damage to any unique, rare, particularly important or vulnerable marine resource, habitat or ecosystem;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (c) the damage caused by the offence is extensive, persistent or irreparable;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (d) the person committed the offence intentionally or recklessly;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (e) the person failed to take reasonable steps to prevent the commission of the offence despite having the financial means to do so;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (f) by committing the offence or failing to take action to prevent its commission, the person increased revenue or decreased costs or intended to increase revenue or decrease costs;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (g) the person committed the offence despite having been warned by the Minister or an enforcement officer of the circumstances that subsequently became the subject of the offence;

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (h) the person has a history of non-compliance with an Act of Parliament or an Act of a provincial legislature that relates to environmental or wildlife protection or conservation; and

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) after committing the offence, the person

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (i) attempted to conceal its commission,

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (ii) failed to take prompt action to prevent, mitigate or remediate its effects, or

heading: Aggravating factors
paragraph: (iii) failed to take prompt action to reduce the risk of committing similar offences in the future.

heading: Absence of aggravating factor
paragraph: (3) The absence of an aggravating factor set out in subsection (2) is not a mitigating factor.

heading: Definition of damage
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of paragraphs (2)(a) to (c), damage includes loss of use value and non-use value.

heading: Reasons
paragraph: (5) If the court decides not to increase the amount of the fine despite being satisfied of the existence of one or more of the aggravating factors set out in subsection (2), the court shall provide reasons for that decision.

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: 39.7 (1) Where a person is convicted of an offence, the convicting court may, in addition to any punishment imposed, order that any seized thing by means of or in relation to which the offence was committed, or any proceeds of its disposition, be forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Return where no forfeiture ordered
paragraph: (2) Where the convicting court does not order the forfeiture, the seized thing, or the proceeds of its disposition, must be returned to its lawful owner or the person lawfully entitled to it.

heading: Retention or sale
paragraph: 39.8 Where a fine is imposed on a person convicted of an offence, any seized thing, or any proceeds of its disposition, may be retained until the fine is paid, or the thing may be sold in satisfaction of the fine and the proceeds applied, in whole or in part, in payment of the fine.

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: 39.9 (1) Where a person is convicted of an offence, the court may, in addition to any punishment imposed and having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that could, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (b) directing the person to take any action that the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to estuarine, coastal or ocean waters, or their resources that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (c) directing the person to publish, in any manner that the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (d) directing the person to pay the Minister or the government of a province compensation, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken by or on behalf of the Minister or that government as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (e) directing the person to perform community service in accordance with any reasonable conditions that may be specified in the order;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (f) directing the person to submit to the Minister, on application to the court by the Minister within three years after the conviction, any information respecting the activities of the person that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (g) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the person's good conduct and for preventing the person from repeating the offence or committing other offences;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (h) directing the person to post a bond or pay into court an amount of money that the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (i) directing the person to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount for monitoring the environmental effects of any activity or marine installation or structure on any marine resource, habitat or ecosystem in any marine protected area;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (j) directing the person to pay to Her Majesty in right of Canada an amount of money that the court considers appropriate for the purpose of promoting the conservation, protection or restoration of any marine protected area;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (k) directing the person to pay, in a manner specified by the court, an amount to enable research to be conducted with respect to the conservation, protection or restoration of any marine protected area;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (l) directing the person to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount to environmental or other groups to assist in their work related to marine protected areas; and

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (m) directing the person to pay, in the manner specified by the court, an amount to an educational institution including for scholarships for students enrolled in studies related to the environment.

heading: Debt due to Her Majesty
paragraph: (2) If the court makes an order under paragraph (1)(j) directing a person to pay an amount to Her Majesty in right of Canada, the amount constitutes a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Suspended sentence
paragraph: 39.91 (1) Where a person is convicted of an offence and the court suspends the passing of sentence pursuant to the Criminal Code, the court may, in addition to any probation order made on suspending the passing of that sentence, make an order containing one or more of the prohibitions, directions or requirements mentioned in section 39.9.

heading: Imposition of sentence
paragraph: (2) Where the person does not comply with the order or is convicted of another offence, within three years after the order was made, the court may, on the application of the prosecution, impose any sentence that could have been imposed if the passing of sentence had not been suspended.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 39.92 Proceedings by way of summary conviction in respect of an offence may be commenced not later than five years after the day on which the offence was committed.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: 39.93 (1) In addition to the procedures set out in the Criminal Code for commencing a proceeding, proceedings in respect of any offence prescribed by the regulations may be commenced by an enforcement officer

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (a) completing a ticket that consists of a summons portion and an information portion;

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (b) delivering the summons portion to the accused or mailing it to the accused at the accused's latest known address; and

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (c) filing the information portion with a court of competent jurisdiction before the summons portion has been delivered or mailed or as soon as is practicable afterward.

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (2) The summons and information portions of the ticket must

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (a) set out a description of the offence and the time and place of its alleged commission;

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (b) include a statement, signed by the enforcement officer who completes the ticket, that the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the accused committed the offence;

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (c) set out the amount of the fine prescribed by the regulations for the offence and the manner in which and period within which it may be paid;

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (d) include a statement that if the accused pays the fine within the period set out in the ticket, a conviction will be entered and recorded against the accused; and

heading: Content of ticket
paragraph: (e) include a statement that if the accused wishes to plead not guilty or for any other reason fails to pay the fine within the period set out in the ticket, the accused must appear in the court on the day and at the time set out in the ticket.

heading: Notice of forfeiture
paragraph: (3) Where a thing is seized under this Act and proceedings relating to it are commenced by way of the ticketing procedure, the enforcement officer who completes the ticket shall give written notice to the accused that, if the accused pays the fine prescribed by the regulations within the period set out in the ticket, the thing, or any proceeds of its disposition, will be immediately forfeited to Her Majesty.

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (4) Where an accused to whom the summons portion of a ticket is delivered or mailed pays the prescribed fine within the period set out in the ticket,

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (a) the payment constitutes a plea of guilty to the offence and a conviction must be entered against the accused and no further action may be taken against the accused in respect of that offence; and

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (b) notwithstanding section 39.3, any thing seized from the accused under this Act that relates to the offence, or any proceeds of its disposition, are forfeited to

heading: Consequences of payment
paragraph: (i) Her Majesty in right of Canada, if the thing was seized by an enforcement officer employed in the federal public administration, or

heading: Consequences of payment

heading: Powers, duties and functions of the Minister
paragraph: 40 (1) As the Minister responsible for oceans, the powers, duties and functions of the Minister extend to and include all matters over which Parliament has jurisdiction, not assigned by law to any other department, board or agency of the Government of Canada, relating to the policies and programs of the Government of Canada respecting oceans.

heading: Encouragement of activities
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), the Minister shall encourage activities necessary to foster understanding, management and sustainable development of oceans and marine resources and the provision of coast guard and hydrographic services to ensure the facilitation of marine trade, commerce and safety in collaboration with other ministers of the Government of Canada.

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: 41 (1) As the Minister responsible for coast guard services, the powers, duties and functions of the Minister extend to and include all matters over which Parliament has jurisdiction, not assigned by law to any other department, board or agency of the Government of Canada, relating to

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (a) services for the safe, economical and efficient movement of ships in Canadian waters through the provision of

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (i) aids to navigation systems and services,

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (ii) marine communications and traffic management services,

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (iii) ice breaking and ice management services, and

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (iv) channel maintenance;

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (b) the marine component of the federal search and rescue program;

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (c) response to wrecks and hazardous or dilapidated ships;

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (d) marine pollution response; and

heading: Coast guard services
paragraph: (e) the support of departments, boards and agencies of the Government of Canada through the provision of ships, aircraft and other marine services.

heading: Cost effective
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall ensure that the services referred to in subparagraphs (1)(a)(i) to (iv) are provided in a cost effective manner.

heading: Functions
paragraph: 42 In exercising the powers and performing the duties and functions assigned by paragraph 4(1)(c) of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Act, the Minister may

heading: Functions
paragraph: (a) collect data for the purpose of understanding oceans and their living resources and ecosystems;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (b) conduct hydrographic and oceanographic surveys of Canadian and other waters;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (c) conduct marine scientific surveys relating to fisheries resources and their supporting habitat and ecosystems;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (d) conduct basic and applied research related to hydrography, oceanography and other marine sciences, including the study of fish and their supporting habitat and ecosystems;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (e) carry out investigations for the purpose of understanding oceans and their living resources and ecosystems;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (f) prepare and publish data, reports, statistics, charts, maps, plans, sections and other documents;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (g) authorize the distribution or sale of data, reports, statistics, charts, maps, plans, sections and other documents;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (h) prepare in collaboration with the Minister of Foreign Affairs, publish and authorize the distribution or sale of charts delineating, consistently with the nature and scale of the charts, all or part of the territorial sea of Canada, the contiguous zone of Canada, the exclusive economic zone of Canada and the fishing zones of Canada and adjacent waters;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (i) participate in ocean technology development; and

heading: Functions
paragraph: (j) conduct studies to obtain traditional ecological knowledge for the purpose of understanding oceans and their living resources and ecosystems.

heading: Powers
paragraph: 43 Subject to section 4 of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Act respecting the powers, duties and functions of the Minister in relation to matters mentioned in that section over which Parliament has jurisdiction, the Minister

heading: Powers
paragraph: (a) is responsible for coordinating, promoting and recommending national policies and programs with respect to fisheries science, hydrography, oceanography and other marine sciences;

heading: Powers
paragraph: (b) in carrying out his or her responsibilities under this section, may

heading: Powers
paragraph: (i) conduct or cooperate with persons conducting applied and basic research programs and investigations and economic studies for the purpose of understanding oceans and their living resources and ecosystems, and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (ii) for that purpose maintain and operate ships, research institutes, laboratories and other facilities for research, surveying and monitoring for the purpose of understanding oceans and their living resources and ecosystems; and

heading: Powers
paragraph: (c) may provide marine scientific advice, services and support to the Government of Canada and, on behalf of the Government, to the governments of the provinces, to other states, to international organizations and to other persons.

heading: Marine scientific research by foreign ships
paragraph: 44 The Minister may

heading: Marine scientific research by foreign ships
paragraph: (a) request the Minister of Foreign Affairs to attach to a consent of the Minister of Foreign Affairs under paragraph 3(2)(c) of the Coasting Trade Act a condition that the foreign ship or non-duty paid ship supply the Minister with the results of the marine scientific research conducted by that ship in waters that form part of Canada or in which Canada has sovereign rights under international law; and

heading: Marine scientific research by foreign ships
paragraph: (b) establish guidelines, not inconsistent with Canada's international obligations, for use by foreign ships and non-duty paid ships in conducting marine scientific research in waters that form part of Canada or in which Canada has sovereign rights under international law.

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: 45 As the Minister responsible for hydrographic services, the powers, duties and functions of the Minister extend to and include all matters over which Parliament has jurisdiction, not assigned by law to any other department, board or agency of the Government of Canada, relating to

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (a) setting standards and establishing guidelines for use by hydrographers and others in collecting data and preparing charts on behalf of the Minister; and

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (b) providing hydrographic advice, services and support to the Government of Canada and, on behalf of the Government, to the governments of the provinces, to other states, to international organizations and to other persons.

heading: Entry on lands
paragraph: 46 A hydrographer may, for the purpose of conducting a hydrographic survey on behalf of the Minister, enter on or pass over the lands of any person, but shall take all reasonable precautions to avoid causing any damage in doing so.

heading: Fees for services or use of facilities
paragraph: 47 (1) The Minister may, subject to any regulations that the Treasury Board may make for the purposes of this section, fix the fees to be paid for a service or the use of a facility provided under this Act by the Minister, the Department or any board or agency of the Government of Canada for which the Minister has responsibility.

heading: Amount not to exceed cost
paragraph: (2) Fees for a service or the use of a facility that are fixed under subsection (1) may not exceed the cost to Her Majesty in right of Canada of providing the service or the use of the facility.

heading: Fees for products, rights and privileges
paragraph: 48 The Minister may, subject to any regulations that the Treasury Board may make for the purposes of this section, fix fees in respect of products, rights and privileges provided under this Act by the Minister, the Department or any board or agency of the Government of Canada for which the Minister has responsibility.

heading: Fees in respect of regulatory processes, etc.
paragraph: 49 (1) The Minister may, subject to any regulations that the Treasury Board may make for the purposes of this section, fix fees in respect of regulatory processes or approvals provided under this Act by the Minister, the Department or any board or agency of the Government of Canada for which the Minister has responsibility.

heading: Amount
paragraph: (2) Fees that are fixed under subsection (1) shall in the aggregate not exceed an amount sufficient to compensate Her Majesty in right of Canada for any reasonable outlays incurred by Her Majesty for the purpose of providing the regulatory processes or approvals.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: 50 (1) Before fixing a fee under this Act, the Minister shall consult with such persons or bodies as the Minister considers to be interested in the matter.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall, within 30 days after fixing a fee under this Act, publish the fee in the Canada Gazette and by such appropriate electronic or other means that the Treasury Board may authorize by regulation.

heading: Reference to Scrutiny Committee
paragraph: (3) Any fee fixed under this Act shall stand referred to the Committee referred to in section 19 of the Statutory Instruments Act to be reviewed and scrutinized as if it were a statutory instrument.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: 51 The Treasury Board may make regulations for the purposes of section 47, 48, 49 or 50.

heading: Review
paragraph: 52 (1) The administration of this Act shall, within three years after the coming into force of this section, be reviewed by the Standing Committee on Fisheries and Oceans.

heading: Report to Parliament
paragraph: (2) The Committee shall undertake a comprehensive review of the provisions and operation of this Act, including the consequences of its implementation, and shall, within a year after the review is undertaken or within such further time as the House of Commons may authorize, submit a report to Parliament thereon including a statement of any changes to this Act or its administration that the Committee would recommend.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 52.1 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, make regulations for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act and, in particular, but without restricting the generality of the foregoing, may make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing marine environmental quality requirements and standards;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the powers and duties of persons designated by the Minister as enforcement officers; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the implementation of provisions of agreements made under this Act.

paragraph: (b) the disturbance of known or suspected subsurface contamination, unless the project is located within a site that is classified as closed in the Federal Contaminated Sites Inventory but not including sites closed that require risk management measures;

heading: PART 7Structures in or Near Water
paragraph: (c) the use of vehicles or heavy machinery on the substrate of a water body; or

heading: PART 7Structures in or Near Water
paragraph: (d) the use of explosives

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agricultural land reserve" means land designated as agricultural land and established as an agricultural land reserve under section 11 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agricultural waste" means agricultural by-products within the meaning of the Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, except it does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) human or animal food waste that is diverted from residential, commercial or institutional sources,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) waste materials derived from non-agricultural operations, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) wood waste derived from land clearing, construction or demolition;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "biosolids" means stabilized municipal sewage sludge resulting from a municipal waste water treatment process or septage treatment process which has been sufficiently treated to reduce pathogen densities and vector attraction to allow the sludge to be beneficially recycled in accordance with the requirements of this regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "biosolids growing medium" means biosolids that meet the requirements of section 10;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Class A biosolids" means biosolids that meet the requirements of section 6;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Class B biosolids" means biosolids that meet the requirements of section 8;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Class A compost" means compost that meets the requirements of section 12;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Class B compost" means compost that meets the requirements of section 14;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "compost" means a product which is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a stabilized earthy matter having the properties and structure of humus,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) beneficial to plant growth when used as a soil amendment,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) produced by composting, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) only derived from organic matter;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "composting" means the controlled biological oxidation and decomposition of organic matter in accordance with the time and temperature requirements specified in Schedule 1;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "composting facility" means a facility that processes organic matter to produce compost;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "discharger" means any of the following responsible persons:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an owner of a composting facility;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an owner of a facility that produces managed organic matter for land application;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a registered owner of the land where managed organic matter is applied;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fertilizer" means an organic or inorganic material of natural or synthetic origin, other than liming material, that is added to a soil to supply one or more plant nutrients;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "foreign matter" means a contaminant that is not readily decomposed during the composting process, and includes demolition waste, metal, glass, plastic, rubber and leather, but does not include silt, sand, rocks or stones, or gravel less than 2.5 centimetres in diameter, or other similar mineral materials naturally found in soil;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "forest reserve land" means land designated as forest reserve land under section 10, 11 or 12 of the Forest Land Reserve Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land application" means the application to land, after biosolids treatment or composting, of managed organic matter;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "land application plan" means a plan for the land application of managed organic matter, prepared in accordance with section 5;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Land Reserve Commission" means the commission established under the Land Reserve Commission Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "leachate" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) effluent originating from organic matter being received, processed, composted, cured or stored at a composting facility,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) effluent originating from managed organic matter being stored or applied to land, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) precipitation, storm water, equipment wash water or other water which has come into contact with, or mixed with, organic matter or managed organic matter being received, processed, composted, cured or stored;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "managed organic matter" means Class A biosolids, Class B biosolids or Class B compost;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "organic matter" means those materials set out in Schedule 12 that are suitable for composting;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pathogen" means an organism capable of causing disease in humans, animals or plants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualified professional" means a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is registered in British Columbia with the person's appropriate professional association, acts under that professional association's code of ethics, and is subject to disciplinary action by that professional association, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) through suitable education, experience, accreditation and knowledge may be reasonably relied on to provide advice within the person's area of expertise as it relates to this regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "retail-grade organic matter" means biosolids growing medium or Class A compost;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "soil conditioner" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) managed organic matter that measurably improves specific chemical or physical characteristics of soil or chemical or physical processes for a given use, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a plant growth medium;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "vector" means a carrier organism that is capable of transmitting a pathogen from one facility, waste source, product or organism to another facility, waste source, product or organism;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "yard waste" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) clean and untreated wood waste, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) non-food vegetative matter resulting from gardening operations, landscaping and land clearing,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include wood waste derived from construction or demolition.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, neither

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) human or animal food waste that is diverted from residential, commercial or institutional sources, nor

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) manure,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: is yard waste.

heading: General application
paragraph: 2		  (1) For the purposes of the Act, compostable materials and recyclable materials continue to be a waste until dealt with in accordance with this regulation.

heading: General application
paragraph: (2) A person who produces or uses biosolids or compost is exempt from section 6 (2) and (3) of the Act if the person produces and uses the biosolids or compost only in accordance with this regulation.

heading: General application
paragraph: (3) This regulation applies in British Columbia to

heading: General application
paragraph: (a) the construction and operation of composting facilities, and

heading: General application
paragraph: (b) the production, distribution, storage, sale and use or land application of biosolids and compost.

heading: General application
paragraph: (4) The land application of retail-grade organic matter or managed organic matter, and the construction and operation of composting facilities, on an agricultural land reserve or on forest reserve land must

heading: General application
paragraph: (a) be in compliance with all applicable legislation of British Columbia including, without limitation, the Agricultural Land Commission Act and the Forest Land Reserve Act, and all applicable regulations under those enactments, and

heading: General application
paragraph: (b) be done in accordance with good agricultural practice.

heading: General application
paragraph: (5) Any discharge of waste into the environment, not otherwise authorized by this regulation, must be in compliance with the Act.

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: 3		  (1) In this section:

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: "agricultural composting processes" means the composting of agricultural by-products in accordance with the Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management;

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: "backyard composting" means the composting of food waste or yard waste, or both, at a site where

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (a) the food waste or yard waste is generated by the residents of a residential dwelling unit, and

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (b) the annual production of compost does not exceed 20 cubic metres.

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (2) This regulation does not apply to any of the following:

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (a) composting facilities

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (i)  authorized by a permit, approval or operational certificate, or

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  required by an order issued under the Act;

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (b) the land application of managed organic matter

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (i)  authorized by a permit, approval or operational certificate, or

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  in accordance with an order issued under the Act;

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (c) agricultural composting processes;

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (d) backyard composting;

heading: General exemptions
paragraph: (e) demonstration gardens for the composting of yard waste in quantities not exceeding 100 cubic metres per year.

heading: Permit required
paragraph:
3.1
		  (1) Section 2 (2) applies to a discharger in relation to a composting facility that processes food waste or biosolids and has a design production capacity of 5 000 tonnes or more of compost per year only if the discharger holds a permit for the composting facility, unless the discharger holds an approval or operational certificate for that composting facility.

heading: Permit required
paragraph: (2) Despite section 3 (2) (a) and (b), a discharger required under this section to hold a permit must comply with this regulation and the terms and conditions of the permit.

heading: Contaminated sites
paragraph:
4
		  A site is not a contaminated site with respect to a substance in the soil if

heading: Contaminated sites
paragraph: (a) the site has been used in accordance with this regulation for the application of managed organic matter or retail-grade organic matter,

heading: Contaminated sites
paragraph: (b) the site has not been used for any commercial or industrial purpose or activity listed in Schedule 2 of the Contaminated Sites Regulation, B.C. Reg. 375/96, and

heading: Contaminated sites
paragraph: (c) the site, before application of managed organic matter or retail-grade organic matter, was not a contaminated site as defined in section 11 (1) to (4) of the Contaminated Sites Regulation, B.C. Reg. 375/96.

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A discharger must have a qualified professional

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (a) prepare a land application plan for

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (i)  each site where managed organic matter is land applied, and

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (ii)  each occurrence that managed organic matter is land applied, and

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (b) sign the land application plan before its implementation.

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (2) The land application plan required by subsection (1) must provide the information specified in Schedule 7.

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (3) After land application of managed organic matter at any site, the discharger must obtain written certification from a qualified professional that the land application was done in accordance with the land application plan required by subsection (1).

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (4) The land application plan must be provided to the registered owner of the land and be made available, upon request, both before and after its implementation, to

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (a) a director, or

heading: Requirement for a land application plan
paragraph: (b) an official designated under the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: 6		  Biosolids that meet the requirements of all of the following are Class A biosolids:

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (a) Schedule 1, Pathogen Reduction Processes;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (b) Schedule 2, Vector Attraction Reduction;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (c) Schedule 3, Pathogen Reduction Limits;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (d) Section 3 of Schedule 4, Quality Criteria;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (e) Schedule 5, Sampling and Analyses - Protocols and Frequency;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (f) Schedule 6, Record-keeping.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph:
7
		  (1) Class A biosolids may be applied to land in accordance with subsection (2) or distributed in accordance with subsection (4).

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (2) When applied to land in quantities greater than 5 cubic metres per year per parcel of land, Class A biosolids must only be applied in accordance with

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (a) a land application plan for Class A biosolids, and

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (b) the soil substance concentrations specified in Schedule 10.1.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (3) The land application plan must, before land application of Class A biosolids, be made available to the registered owner of the land.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (4) Class A biosolids must only be distributed as follows:

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (a) in volumes that do not exceed 5 cubic metres per vehicle per day;

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (b) in sealed bags for retail purposes, each not to exceed 5 cubic metres, with no restrictions on the number of bags distributed per vehicle per day;

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (c) in volumes greater than 5 cubic metres to composting facilities or biosolids growing medium facilities.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph:
8
		  Biosolids that meet the requirements of all of the following are Class B biosolids:

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (a) Schedule 1, Pathogen Reduction Processes;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (b) Schedule 2, Vector Attraction Reduction;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (c) Schedule 3, Pathogen Reduction Limits;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (d) Column 3 of Schedule 4, Quality Criteria;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (e) Schedule 5, Sampling and Analyses - Protocols and Frequency;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (f) Schedule 6, Record-keeping.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Class B biosolids may be applied to land in accordance with subsection (2) or distributed in accordance with subsection (4).

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (2) Class B biosolids must only be applied to land in accordance with

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (a) a land application plan for Class B biosolids,

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (b) the methodology specified in Schedule 8, and

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (c) the soil substance concentrations specified in Schedule 10.1, or the site-specific criteria approved by a director.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (3) The land application plan must, before land application, be made available to the registered owner of the land.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (4) Class B biosolids may be distributed to composting facilities with no volume restriction.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (5) Class B biosolids that meet the pathogen reduction and vector attraction requirements for Class A biosolids specified in Schedules 1, 2 and 3 may be distributed to a biosolids growing medium facility with no volume restriction.

heading: Land application and distribution
paragraph: (6) Class B biosolids must not be land applied in a watershed used as a permitted water supply under the Drinking Water Protection Regulation, B.C. Reg. 200/2003.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph:
10
		  Biosolids that meet the requirements of all of the following are biosolids growing medium:

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (a) Column 2 of Schedule 4, Quality Criteria;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (b) Schedule 5, Sampling and Analyses - Protocols and Frequency;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (c) Schedule 6, Record-keeping;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (d) Schedule 11, Requirements for Biosolids Growing Medium.

heading: Distribution
paragraph:
11
		  Biosolids growing medium may be distributed with no volume restriction.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph:
12
		  (1) In this section, "untreated and unprocessed wood residuals" means clean wood from lumber manufacturing, and includes shavings, sawdust, chips, hog fuel, ground mill ends and land clearing waste which has been ground with the majority of the greenery removed and no soil present.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (2) Compost that is produced solely from yard waste or untreated and unprocessed wood residuals, or from both, and that meets the requirements of all of the following, is Class A compost:

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (a) Schedule 1, Pathogen Reduction Processes;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (b) Schedule 2, Vector Attraction Reduction;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (c) Column 1 of Schedule 4, Quality Criteria.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (3) Compost that is not solely produced from yard waste or from untreated and unprocessed wood residuals and that meets the requirements of all of the following is Class A compost:

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (a) the requirements of subsection (2) (a) to (c);

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (b) Schedule 3, Pathogen Reduction Limits;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (c) Schedule 5, Sampling and Analyses - Protocols and Frequency;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (d) Schedule 6, Record-keeping.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (4) Class A compost must be derived only from organic matter.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (5) Biosolids used as feedstock for the production of Class A compost must not exceed the standards for Class B biosolids set out in Column 3 of Schedule 4.

heading: Distribution
paragraph:
13
		  Class A compost may be distributed with no volume restriction.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph:
14
		  (1) Compost that meets the requirements of all of the following is Class B compost:

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (a) Schedule 1, Pathogen Reduction Processes;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (b) Schedule 2, Vector Attraction Reduction;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (c) Schedule 3, Pathogen Reduction Limits;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (d) Column 3 of Schedule 4, Quality Criteria;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (e) Schedule 5, Sampling and Analyses - Protocols and Frequency;

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (f) Schedule 6, Record-keeping.

heading: Process and quality criteria
paragraph: (2) Class B compost must be derived only from organic matter.

heading: Land application
paragraph:
15
		  (1) Class B compost must only be applied to land in accordance with

heading: Land application
paragraph: (a) a land application plan for Class B compost,

heading: Land application
paragraph: (b) the methodology specified in Schedule 8, and

heading: Land application
paragraph: (c) the soil substance concentrations specified in Schedule 10.1, or the site-specific numeric soil standards approved by a director.

heading: Land application
paragraph: (2) The land application plan must, before land application, be made available to the registered owner of the land.

heading: Land application
paragraph: (3) Class B compost must not be land applied in a watershed used as a permitted water supply under the Drinking Water Protection Regulation, B.C. Reg. 200/2003.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
16
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "precipitation" means precipitation as determined by the Canadian Atmospheric Environmental Service Reports of Environment Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "storage facility" means a structure for containing managed organic matter before its use under a land application plan, and includes a reservoir, lagoon, cistern, gutter, tank or bermed area but does not include a vehicle or any mobile equipment used for the transportation of managed organic matter;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "storage site" means a site for storing a temporary stock of managed organic matter which is ready to be drawn upon for use as a fertilizer or soil conditioner under a land application plan.

heading: Storage methods
paragraph:
17
		  (1) If managed organic matter, which is to be applied to land under a land application plan, is stored on a farm or at some other site, it must be stored

heading: Storage methods
paragraph: (a) in a storage facility in accordance with the requirements of section 18, or

heading: Storage methods
paragraph: (b) at a storage site in accordance with the requirements of section 19.

heading: Storage methods
paragraph: (2) Managed organic matter must only be stored on a farm if all of the managed organic matter is used on that farm.

heading: Storage facility
paragraph:
18
		  A storage facility must

heading: Storage facility
paragraph: (a) be of sufficient capacity to store all the managed organic matter to be used on the land application site for the period of time needed for its application as a fertilizer or soil conditioner,

heading: Storage facility
paragraph: (b) be located at least 15 metres from any watercourse and 30 metres from any source of water for domestic purposes, and

heading: Storage facility
paragraph: (c) be maintained in such a manner as to prevent the escape of managed organic matter.

heading: Storage site
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Managed organic matter may only be stored at a storage site as follows:

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (a) for not more than 2 weeks if it is

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (i)  used within 2 weeks, and

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (ii)  stored in a manner that prevents the escape of managed organic matter;

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (b) for more than 2 weeks if it is

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (i)  stored for no longer than 9 months,

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (ii)  located at least 30 metres from any watercourse or any source of water used for domestic purposes, and

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (iii)  stored in a manner that prevents the escape of managed organic matter.

heading: Storage site
paragraph: (2) Berms or other works must be constructed around the storage site if necessary to prevent the escape of managed organic matter.

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph:
20
		  (1) This section applies to

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: (a) Vancouver Island,

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: (b) the Fraser Valley, and

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: (c) any other area of British Columbia that receives a total average precipitation greater than 600 mm (24 inches) during the months of October to March inclusive.

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: (2) Managed organic matter that

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: (a) is to be applied to land under a land application plan,

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: (b) is stored at the land application site, and

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: (c) is not stored in a storage facility,

heading: Rainy season storage using a storage site
paragraph: must be covered from October 1 to March 31 of the next year to prevent the escape of managed organic matter.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
21
		  In this Division:

heading: Definition
paragraph: "medical health officer" means a medical health officer within the meaning of the Public Health Act who has jurisdiction within the geographic area in which managed organic matter is proposed to be applied;

heading: Definition
paragraph: "watershed" means a watershed used as a permitted water supply under the Drinking Water Protection Regulation, B.C. Reg. 200/2003.

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: 22		  (1) A discharger must, using the standardized form provided in Schedule 13, give notification of any proposed land application of managed organic matter in volumes greater than 5 cubic metres, as follows:

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (a) to a director at least 30 calendar days before the land application of managed organic matter;

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (b) to a medical health officer at least 30 calendar days before the land application of managed organic matter to agricultural land or in a watershed;

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (c) to the Land Reserve Commission at least 30 calendar days before the land application of managed organic matter within an agricultural land reserve or forest reserve land.

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (2) The director may, within 30 days after receipt of the information required by subsection (1) (a), request additional information.

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (3) If the information required by subsection (1) (a) or (2) indicates the need for site-specific standards or management practices respecting the land application of managed organic matter in order to protect human health and the environment, the director may, within 30 days after receipt of the information, require the discharger to meet the site-specific standards or management practices specified by the director.

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (4) A medical health officer may, within 30 days after receipt of the information required by subsection (1) (b), provide written directions to the discharger that the application of managed organic matter

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (a) must not proceed, or

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (b) may only proceed subject to conditions specified by the medical health officer.

heading: Discharger to give notice
paragraph: (5) If there is agreement between the discharger and the director and, in the case of land application to agricultural land or in a watershed, a medical health officer, the parties may agree to amend the time limit under subsection (3) or (4).

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph:
23
		  (1) This section applies, on and after the coming into force of this regulation, to a composting facility proposed to be

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (a) constructed with an existing or proposed annual production capacity of 20 000 tonnes or more,

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (b) expanded beyond an existing annual production capacity of 20 000 tonnes or more resulting in an increase in production capacity of more than 10 percent, or

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (c) expanded beyond an existing annual production capacity of less than 20 000 tonnes resulting in an annual production capacity of more than 20 000 tonnes.

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (2) A discharger must ensure that no organic matter is collected at, and no compost is distributed from, a composting facility unless a qualified professional conducts and completes an environmental impact study and produces an environmental impact study report acceptable to a director which includes, but is not limited to,

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (a) design of the composting facilities including buildings, works and other appurtances,

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (b) odour and leachate collection and treatment systems, and

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (c) site preparation for the composting facilities, buffer zones and plans to minimize the impact on adjacent lands.

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (3) A copy of the environmental impact study report required by subsection (2) must be submitted to the director at least 90 days before commencement of construction of a new composting facility or the modification of an existing composting facility.

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (4) The discharger must retain a copy of the completed environmental impact study report for inspection.

heading: Environmental impact study and report
paragraph: (5) The director may request additional information with respect to the environmental impact study that the director considers necessary for the protection of human health and the environment, and may specify particular concerns or questions that the impact study must address.

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph:
24
		  (1) A discharger must have a qualified professional prepare plans and specifications for

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (a) the construction and operation of a new composting facility, or

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (b) any modification of an existing composting facility that results in an increase in the annual production capacity of more than 10 percent or more than 20 000 cubic metres.

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (2) The plans and specifications required by subsection (1) must include, but are not limited to, all of the following:

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (a) all works to be constructed on the site;

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (b) design capacity of the composting facility;

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (c) a leachate management plan which stipulates how leachate generated from any and all stages of the composting process will be minimized, managed, treated or disposed;

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (d) an odour management plan which stipulates how air contaminants from the composting facility will be discharged in a manner that does not cause pollution;

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (e) an operating and closure plan for the composting facility.

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (3) The discharger must ensure that

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (a) the qualified professional

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (i)  affixes the qualified professional's professional seal or signature, or both, to the plans and specifications for the composting facility, and

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (ii)  makes a signed statement certifying that the composting facility has been constructed in accordance with the plans and specifications,

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (b) a copy of the plans and specifications for the composting facility are kept at the composting facility at all times, and are available for inspection at any time,

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (c) the plans and specifications are submitted to a director upon request, and

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (d) the composting facility is operated in compliance with the plans and specifications required by subsection (1).

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: (4) The director may request additional information with respect to the plans and specifications that the director considers necessary for the protection of human health and the environment, and may specify particular concerns or questions that the plans and specifications must address.

heading: Notification of operation
paragraph:
25
		  (1) The discharger must, at least 90 days before beginning the operation of a composting facility, give notice in writing to

heading: Notification of operation
paragraph: (a) a director, and

heading: Notification of operation
paragraph: (b) the Land Reserve Commission if the composting facility is in an agricultural land reserve or forest reserve land.

heading: Notification of operation
paragraph: (2) The notification required by subsection (1) must include

heading: Notification of operation
paragraph: (a) the composting facility location and design capacity, name of a contact person, type of waste received, and intended distribution of compost, and

heading: Notification of operation
paragraph: (b) a copy of a personnel training program plan that addresses the specific training needed to operate the composting facility in compliance with this regulation.

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph:
26
		  (1) In this section, "curing area" means an area where organic matter which has undergone the rapid initial stage of composting is further matured into a humus-like material.

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (2) The receiving, storage, processing and curing areas of a composting facility must comply with all of the following:

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (a) be located on asphalt, concrete or another similar impermeable surface that is capable of withstanding wear and tear from normal operations and that will prevent the release of leachate into the environment;

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (b) have a roof or cover, or a prepared surface, designed to prevent

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (i)  the surface collection of water around the base of organic matter and compost, and

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (ii)  run-off water from entering the receiving, storage, processing and curing areas;

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (c) have a leachate collection system designed, constructed, maintained and operated to reuse leachate, or to remove leachate, from the receiving, storage, processing and curing areas.

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (3) Leachate that is not collected and reused in the composting process must not be discharged into the environment unless authorized under the Act.

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (4) Despite subsections (2) and (3), an impermeable surface, roof, cover, prepared surface or leachate collection system is not necessary if a qualified professional can demonstrate through an environmental impact assessment that the environment will be protected and appropriate water quality criteria satisfied through the use of alternative leachate management processes.

heading: Composting facility requirements
paragraph: (5) A director may request additional information with respect to the environmental impact assessment that the director considers necessary for the protection of human health and the environment, and may specify particular concerns, questions, standards or monitoring that the assessment must address.

heading: Capacity for organic matter
paragraph:
27
		  The amount of organic matter in a composting facility must not at any time exceed the total design capacity of the facility.

heading: Capacity for compost
paragraph:
28
		  At least half of the compost stored at a composting facility must be removed annually from the facility beginning in the third year after facility start-up.

heading: Capacity for residuals
paragraph:
29
		  (1) Residuals from the composting process must

heading: Capacity for residuals
paragraph: (a) be stored so as to prevent vector attraction, and

heading: Capacity for residuals
paragraph: (b) be disposed of on a regular basis in accordance with the Act.

heading: Capacity for residuals
paragraph: (2) Residuals that are stored at a composting facility must not at any time exceed 15 cubic metres in total.

heading: Closure of a composting facility
paragraph:
30
		  Before the closure of a composting facility,

heading: Closure of a composting facility
paragraph: (a) all compost must be applied or distributed in accordance with this regulation, and

heading: Closure of a composting facility
paragraph: (b) all unprocessed organic matter must be removed from the facility and dealt with in accordance with the Act.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph:
31
		  (1) A person who contravenes a provision of this regulation, other than as set out in subsection (2), commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10 000.

heading: Offence and penalty
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes section 5 (1), 7 (2) or (4), 9 (2), 12 (4), or (5), 14 (2), 15 (1), 17 (1) or (2), 20 (2), 22 (1), 23 (2) or (3), 24 (1), 25 (1), 26 (2) or (3), 27, 28, 29 (1) or (2) or 30 commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $200 000.

heading: Spent
paragraph:
32
		  Spent.

heading: Transition - permit requirement under section 3.1

paragraph: (c) under section 5 (4) of the Public Notification Regulation, post the application on a billboard,

paragraph: (e) under section 6 (5) of the Public Notification Regulation, post the application in a post office.
