paragraph:
34
		  In respect of matters subject to approval or other consideration by a director under this regulation, if a person has submitted the required documentation in substantial compliance with this regulation before November 1, 2017, the director may apply to those matters the numeric soil standards that were in effect immediately before that date.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
1
		  The pathogen reduction requirements listed in section 2 (a) to (g) of this Schedule must be met before or at the same time as the vector attraction reduction requirements set out in sections 1 to 3 of Schedule 2.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
2
		  One of the following pathogen reduction methods is required for Class A biosolids or biosolids used to produce biosolids growing medium:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (a) the thermophilic aerobic digestion method consisting of an aerobic process whereby liquid biosolids are agitated with air or oxygen under a temperature of not less than 55° Celsius for 30 minutes or longer, and the temperature and time period are determined using the equation in paragraph (f). The process is to be configured (batch, plug flow, staged) to maintain sufficient retention time to ensure that pathogen and volatile solids destruction is reliably achieved;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (b) the thermophilic anaerobic digestion method consisting of a process whereby liquid biosolids are agitated in the absence of free oxygen (under negative Redox potential) at a temperature of not less than 50° Celsius for at least 10 consecutive days. The process must be configured (batch, plug flow, staged) to maintain sufficient retention time to ensure that pathogen and volatile solids destruction is reliably achieved;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (c) the heat treatment method such that when the percent solids of the biosolids is 7 percent or higher,

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (i)  the temperature of the biosolids must be 50° Celsius or higher,

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (ii)  the time period must be 20 minutes or longer, and

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (iii)  the minimum required time period must be determined using the following equation, except when small particles of biosolids are heated by either warmed gases or an immiscible liquid:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (d) the heat treatment method such that when the percent solids of the biosolids is 7 percent or higher and small particles of biosolids are heated by either warmed gases or an immiscible liquid,

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (i)  the temperature of the biosolids must be 50° Celsius or higher,

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (ii)  the time period must be 15 seconds or longer, and

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (iii)  the minimum required time period must be determined using the equation in paragraph (c);

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (e) the heat treatment method such that when the percent solids of the biosolids is less than 7 percent,

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (i)  the time period must be at least 15 seconds but less than 30 minutes, and

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (ii)  the minimum required time period must be determined using the equation in paragraph (c);

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (f) the heat treatment method such that when the percent solids of the biosolids is less than 7 percent,

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (i)  the temperature of the biosolids must be 50° Celsius or higher, and

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (ii)  the time period must be 30 minutes or longer, and

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (iii)  the minimum required time period must be determined using the following equation:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (g) the alkaline stabilization method consisting of maintaining the pH within the biosolids at above 12 for 72 hours with a temperature during the 72 hour period greater than 52° Celsius for 12 hours. After 72 hours at pH above 12, the biosolids must be air-dried to greater than 50 percent total solids.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
3
		  The pathogen reduction requirements for Class A compost listed in section 4 (a) to (c) of this Schedule must be met before the vector attraction reduction requirements listed in section 2 (a) and (b) of Schedule 2.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
4
		  One of the following pathogen reduction processes specified in paragraphs (a) to (c) is required to produce Class A compost:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (a) the windrow composting method whereby organic matter is processed in a windrow involving periodic aeration and mixing of the windrow, with a temperature of not less than 55° Celsius maintained for at least 15 days and not fewer than 5 turnings of the windrow made during the high temperature period to promote uniform exposure of the compost to thermophilic temperatures;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (b) the static aerated pile composting method consisting of a compost process involving mechanical aeration of the compost pile, with the compost pile insulated and a temperature of not less than 55° Celsius maintained throughout the compost pile for at least 3 consecutive days;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (c) the enclosed vessel method consisting of a confined compost process involving mechanical aeration of compost under controlled environmental conditions, with a temperature of not less than 55° Celsius maintained for at least 3 days during the composting process.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
5
		  To produce Class A compost from yard waste alone, a turning process can be used whereby the pile is turned on a periodic basis to aerate the yard waste, maintain optimum temperatures, and reduce pathogens.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
6
		  The director may provide approval for an alternative process on a specific basis if the director is satisfied that the alternative process in that case will provide a Class A compost equivalent in quality as that produced by the process described by section 4 (a) to (c).

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
7
		  For Class B biosolids and Class B compost a biosolids treatment or composting process must be used whereby fecal coliform are reduced to levels < 2 000 000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or one of the following processes must be used:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (a) the aerobic digestion process whereby Class B biosolids are agitated with air or oxygen to maintain aerobic conditions for a specific mean cell residence time at a specific temperature. Values for the mean cell residence time and temperature must be between 40 days at 20° Celsius and 60 days at 15° Celsius;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (b) the air-drying process whereby Class B biosolids are dried on sand beds or on paved or unpaved basins. The biosolids must dry for a minimum of 3 months. During 2 of the 3 months, the ambient average daily temperature must be above 0° Celsius;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (c) the anaerobic digestion process whereby Class B biosolids are treated in the absence of air for a specific mean cell residence time at a specific temperature. Values for the mean cell time and temperature must be between 15 days at 35° Celsius to 55° Celsius and 60 days at 20° Celsius;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (d) the compost process using either within-vessel, static aerated pile or windrow-composting methods whereby the temperature of the Class B compost is raised to 40° Celsius or higher and maintained for 5 days. For 4 hours during the 5-day period, the temperature in the compost pile must exceed 55° Celsius;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (e) the lime stabilization process whereby sufficient lime is added to the Class B biosolids to raise the pH of the biosolids to 12 after 2 hours of contact.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
1
		  One of the following vector attraction reduction processes is required for Class A biosolids or Class B biosolids used to produce biosolids growing medium:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (a) a digestion process (aerobic or anaerobic) resulting in the mass of volatile solids of the biosolids being reduced by more than 38 percent;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (b) when the 38 percent volatile solids reduction requirement in paragraph (a) cannot be met for an aerobically digested biosolids, vector attraction reduction can be demonstrated by digesting a portion of the previously digested biosolids that has a percent solids of two percent or less aerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 30 additional days at 20° Celsius. When, at the end of the 30 days, the volatile solids in the biosolids at the beginning of that period is reduced by less than 15 percent, vector attraction reduction is achieved;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (c) when the 38 percent volatile solids reduction requirement in paragraph (a) cannot be met for an anaerobically digested biosolids, vector attraction reduction can be demonstrated by digesting a portion of the previously digested biosolids anaerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 40 additional days at a temperature between 30° and 37° Celsius. When, at the end of the 40 days, the volatile solids in the biosolids at the beginning of that period is reduced by less than 17 percent, vector attraction reduction is achieved;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (d) the specific oxygen uptake rate (SOUR) for biosolids treated in an aerobic process shall be less than or equal to 1.5 milligrams of oxygen per hour per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) at a temperature of 20° Celsius;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (e) the pH of biosolids shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali, shall remain at 12 or higher for two hours and then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (f) the percent solids of biosolids generated in a wastewater treatment process must be equal to or greater than 90 percent based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials. The biosolids must thereafter be managed in such a way that the moisture content of the biosolids does not increase such that compliance with the 90 percent solids requirement is maintained until such time as the biosolids is land applied in accordance with section 7 (2) or distributed in accordance with 7 (4) of this regulation.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
2
		  One of the following vector attraction reduction processes are required for Class A compost:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (a) Class A compost must be treated in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer. During that time, the temperature of the compost must be higher than 40° Celsius and the average temperature of the compost must be higher than 45° Celsius. After the vector attraction reduction process is completed the carbon to nitrogen ratio of the compost must be greater than or equal to 15:1 and less than or equal to 35:1;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (b) Class A compost must be retained in curing piles for at least 21 days. After the 21 day period, the carbon to nitrogen ratio of the Class A compost must be greater than or equal to 15:1 and less than or equal to 35:1 and must not re-heat, upon standing, under the following conditions:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (i)  compost is aerated and formed into a pile no smaller than 3 metres in diameter and 2 metres high with compost having a moisture content between 35 percent and 60 percent;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (ii)  the pile must be formed in a location where the ambient temperature remains in the range of 5° to 30° Celsius;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (iii)  3 days after the pile has been formed, the temperature of the compost is measured at a depth of 60 cm into the pile from the outside surface of the pile;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (iv)  the compost must not re-heat upon standing to greater than 20° Celsius above ambient temperature.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
3
		  If one of the above vector attraction reduction methods cannot be met, then a test method or treatment process specified in protocols approved by the director, may be used as an alternative means of showing that vector attraction reduction has been achieved.

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph:
4
		  Class B biosolids must meet the vector attraction reduction processes specified in section 1 of this Schedule or meet one of the following alternatives:

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (a) if Class B biosolids, with fecal coliform levels determined to be < 2 000 000 MPN per gram of total solids, are injected into the soil, then the biosolids must be injected below the land surface within 8 hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process and no significant amount of biosolids must remain on the soil surface 1 hour after application;

heading: Transition - matters in progress
paragraph: (b) if Class B biosolids, with fecal coliform levels determined to be < 2 000 000 MPN per gram of total solids, are incorporated by tillage, then the biosolids must be incorporated within 8 hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process and no significant amount of biosolids must remain on the soil surface 6 hours after application.

heading: Issuance of Registration Cards, Registration Certificates and Licences
paragraph: 19 (1) The Minister may issue a fisher's registration card, a vessel registration certificate or a licence referred to in column I of an item of Part I of Schedule II upon application therefor and payment of the fee set out in column II of that item.

heading: Issuance of Registration Cards, Registration Certificates and Licences
paragraph: (2) Where, pursuant to subsection (1), the Minister issues a fisher's registration card to a person or a vessel registration certificate in respect of a vessel, that person or vessel is deemed to be registered with the Department.

heading: Issuance of Registration Cards, Registration Certificates and Licences
paragraph: (3) If an Indian or the Northern Native Fishing Corporation is issued a Category A licence in respect of a vessel, the Indian or the Corporation must elect to pay either the applicable fee set out in subitem 3(1) of Part I of Schedule II or the applicable fee set out in subitem 3(2) of that Part.

heading: Issuance of Registration Cards, Registration Certificates and Licences
paragraph: (4) Where a vessel in respect of which a Category A licence was issued after December 31, 1979 for the fee set out in subitem 3(2) of Part I of Schedule II is sold to a person other than an Indian or the Northern Native Fishing Corporation, the Category A licence is void.

heading: Registration Certificate Invalid
paragraph: 20 (1) A vessel registration certificate issued in respect of a vessel becomes invalid if the vessel is modified so that the tonnage or length of the vessel differs from that set out in the vessel registration certificate.

heading: Registration Certificate Invalid
paragraph: (2) Where a vessel registration certificate becomes invalid pursuant to subsection (1),

heading: Registration Certificate Invalid
paragraph: (a) the vessel registration certificate and all licences issued in respect of the vessel shall be returned to the Minister within seven days after the day on which the certificate becomes invalid; and

heading: Registration Certificate Invalid
paragraph: (b) no person shall use the vessel in commercial fishing until a new vessel registration certificate has been issued in respect of it.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: 22 (1) No person shall use a vessel, and no owner or lessee of a vessel shall permit the use of that vessel, in commercial fishing for any species of fish unless

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (a) subject to subsection (2), the vessel is registered; and

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (b) the use of the vessel to fish for that species of fish is authorized by a commercial fishing licence.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (2) A person may use an unregistered vessel in commercial fishing for roe herring with a gill net or when fishing in non-tidal waters.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: 23 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall use a vessel to process fish unless

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (a) the vessel is registered; and

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (b) a Category P licence has been issued in respect of the vessel.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of washing, eviscerating, icing or freezing fish, other than bivalve molluscs, on board the vessel that was used to catch the fish.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: 24 No person shall use a vessel to transport from fishing grounds fish that were taken in commercial fishing unless the vessel is registered and

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (a) is licensed to be used in commercial fishing; or

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (b) a Category D licence has been issued in respect of the vessel.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: 25 A person who is 16 years of age or older shall not engage in commercial fishing or be on board a vessel that is being used in commercial fishing unless they hold a fisher's registration card.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: 26 (1) Subject to subsection (2), no person shall fish except under the authority of a licence issued under these Regulations, the Fishery (General) Regulations or the Aboriginal Communal Fishing Licences Regulations.

heading: Registration and Licence Required
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who is registered and who is engaged in commercial fishing for a species of fish from a registered vessel that is authorized by a commercial fishing licence to be used in fishing for that species.

heading: Close Times
paragraph: 30 No person shall catch and retain a species of fish set out in column I of an item of Schedule III from the waters set out in column II of that item with the type of fishing gear set out in column III of that item during the close time set out in column IV of that item.

paragraph: 33 No person shall catch and retain a lingcod that is less than

heading: Lingcod
paragraph: (a) 58 cm in length, measured from the tip of the nose to the tip of the tail; or

heading: Lingcod

heading: Sablefish
paragraph: 34 (1) No person shall catch and retain a sablefish that is less than

heading: Sablefish
paragraph: (a) 55 cm in length, measured from the tip of the nose to the fork of the tail; or

heading: Sablefish
paragraph: (b) where the head has been removed, 39 cm in length, measured from the origin of the first dorsal fin to the fork of the tail.

heading: Smelt

heading: Smelt

heading: Smelt

heading: Smelt

paragraph: (b) a seine that

heading: Close Times
paragraph: 40 Where notified by a fishery officer or fishery guardian that a roe herring fishery is about to be opened in an area, a person who is operating a fishing vessel in that area shall, unless the vessel is authorized to be used in the roe herring fishery in that area pursuant to a Category H licence, remove the vessel from the area until the fishery has opened.

heading: Herring Spawning Grounds
paragraph: 41 (1) A fishery officer may designate an area as a herring spawning ground and establish the boundaries of the area and the period of time for which the area is designated as a herring spawning ground.

heading: Herring Spawning Grounds
paragraph: (2) Where an area is designated as a herring spawning ground under subsection (1), notice of the designation shall be given by the fishery officer to the persons affected or likely to be affected by the designation by one or more of the methods set out in respect of the variation of close times in section 7 of the Fishery (General) Regulations.

heading: Herring Spawning Grounds
paragraph: (3) No person shall, in an area designated as a herring spawning ground under subsection (1),

heading: Herring Spawning Grounds
paragraph: (a) transfer herring from one vessel to another; or

heading: Herring Spawning Grounds
paragraph: (b) anchor any fishing vessel or any other vessel used to assist in herring fishing.

heading: Herring Enclosures
paragraph: 44 (1) No person shall establish or operate a herring enclosure unless authorized to do so under a Category J or Z licence.

heading: Release of Herring from Herring Enclosure
paragraph: 45 (1) Where a fishery officer has evidence of excessive mortality of herring in a herring enclosure, the fishery officer may direct the operator of the enclosure to release all herring contained therein and, where the operator of the enclosure cannot be readily located, may release the herring from the enclosure.

heading: Release of Herring from Herring Enclosure
paragraph: (2) No person shall fail to comply with a direction given under subsection (1).

heading: Release of Herring from Herring Enclosure
paragraph: (3) Where a fishery officer releases herring from a herring enclosure under subsection (1), the fishery officer shall, as soon as practicable, notify the operator of the enclosure of the release.

heading: Herring Spawn on Kelp
paragraph: 47 No person shall transport herring spawn on kelp in any container that is not marked with the number of the licence under the authority of which the herring spawn on kelp was taken or collected.

heading: General
paragraph: 51 No person shall drive or attempt to drive salmon from one area of water to another.

heading: Salmon Fishing Boundaries
paragraph: 52 (1) A fishery officer may designate a salmon fishing boundary by erecting or causing to be erected

heading: Salmon Fishing Boundaries
paragraph: (a) in respect of tidal waters, not more than one nautical mile from the mouth of a river, creek or stream, two orange- or yellow-coloured triangular signs, each side of which is at least 1.5 m in length and 12 cm in width; and

heading: Salmon Fishing Boundaries
paragraph: (b) in respect of non-tidal waters, orange-coloured triangular signs, each side of which is at least 50 cm in length.

heading: Salmon Fishing Boundaries
paragraph: (2) No person shall fish for salmon

heading: Salmon Fishing Boundaries
paragraph: (a) in tidal waters within a circle, the diameter of which is the straight line between two orange-coloured signs erected under paragraph (1)(a);

heading: Salmon Fishing Boundaries
paragraph: (b) in tidal waters between the mouth of a river, creek or stream and the straight line between two yellow-coloured signs erected under paragraph (1)(a); or

heading: Salmon Fishing Boundaries
paragraph: (c) in any non-tidal waters other than waters bounded by orange-coloured signs erected under paragraph (1)(b).

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: 53 (1) No person shall fish in any waters set out in column I of an item of Part I of Schedule VI for the species of salmon set out in column II of that item with the type of fishing gear set out in column III of that item during the close time set out in column IV of that item.

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (2) No person shall troll in any waters set out in column I of an item of Part II of Schedule VI for the species of salmon set out in column II of that item using the type of vessel set out in column III of that item during the close time set out in column IV of that item.

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: 54 (1) Where a close time set out in Part I of Schedule VI is varied pursuant to section 6 of the Fishery (General) Regulations to permit salmon fishing by gill net, the notice referred to in section 7 of the Fishery (General) Regulations shall specify one of the gill net mesh sizes set out in column I, one of the maximum gill net depth limits set out in column II, one of the maximum gill net hang ratios set out in column III, one of the minimum corkline to web distances set out in column V and one of the maximum corkline to web distances set out in column VI of the table to this section.

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (2) Where a close time has been varied to permit salmon fishing with a gill net in accordance with subsection (1), no person shall fish for salmon with a gill net that has

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (a) any meshes that are not contiguous and uniform in size;

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (b) a mesh size other than that specified in the notice;

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (c) a depth greater than the maximum depth specified in the notice;

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (d) webbing with a total length, when compared to the length of the corkline to which it is hung, in a ratio greater than the maximum hang ratio specified in the notice; or

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (e) a corkline to web distance less than the minimum corkline to web distance or greater than the maximum corkline to web distance specified in the notice.

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (3) Where a close time set out in an item of Part I of Schedule VI is varied pursuant to section 6 of the Fishery (General) Regulations to permit salmon fishing with a purse seine, the notice referred to in section 7 of the Fishery (General) Regulations shall specify one of the minimum purse seine bunt mesh sizes set out in column IV of the table to this section.

heading: Salmon Close Times
paragraph: (4) Where a close time has been varied to permit salmon fishing with a purse seine in accordance with subsection (3), no person shall fish for salmon with a purse seine that has, in the final 18 m of the bunt, a mesh size that is less than the minimum bunt mesh size specified in the notice.

heading: PART VIIIMarine Plants

heading: PART VIIIMarine Plants

heading: PART VIIIMarine Plants
paragraph: (b) not later than the tenth day of every month during the term of the licence, and following the termination of the licence, make a written return to the Minister showing the quantity of each species of marine plants harvested under the authority of the licence during the previous month.

heading: Interpretation

paragraph: Commission means the International Pacific Halibut Commission established under the Convention between Canada and the United States of America for the Preservation of the Halibut Fishery of the Northern Pacific Ocean and Bering Sea, signed at Ottawa on March 2, 1953, and the Protocol amending that Convention, signed at Washington D.C. on March 29, 1979. heading: Close Time
paragraph: 74 (1) No person shall fish for or catch and retain halibut in any Subarea during the close time from 12:00 h October 31 to 12:00 h March 1.

heading: Close Time
paragraph: (2) No person fishing in any Subarea during the close time set out in subsection (1) shall possess halibut.

heading: Size Limits
paragraph: 75 No person shall catch and retain any halibut that is less than

heading: Size Limits
paragraph: (a) 81.3 cm in length, measured in a straight line from the tip of the lower jaw with the mouth closed and passing over the pectoral fin to the extreme end of the middle of the tail; or

heading: Size Limits
paragraph: (b) where the head has been removed, 61 cm in length, measured in a straight line from the base of the pectoral fin at its most anterior point to the extreme end of the middle of the tail.

heading: Gear Restrictions
paragraph: 76 (1) No person shall fish for or catch and retain halibut with any gear other than hook and line or trap.

heading: Gear Restrictions
paragraph: (2) No person shall possess halibut on board a vessel that is being used to fish with or is carrying a trawl net.

heading: Gear Restrictions
paragraph: (3) No person shall fish for halibut from a vessel that is equipped with or has on board an automated hook stripper.

heading: Gear Restrictions
paragraph: (4) No person shall possess halibut on a vessel that is equipped with or has on board an automated hook stripper.

heading: Retention of Tagged Halibut
paragraph: 77 Notwithstanding anything in these Regulations or the Fishery (General) Regulations, where a person at any time catches a halibut that bears a tag affixed by the Commission, the person may retain the halibut, if at the time of the landing of the halibut the person reports the landing to a fishery officer or a representative of the Commission and makes the halibut, with the tag still affixed, available for examination by a fishery officer or a representative of the Commission.
