heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "conservancy" means Crown land established or continued as a conservancy under this Act or the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Crown land" means land owned by the government;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "designated wildland area" means a roadless area in a park, conservancy or recreation area that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) retained in a natural condition for the preservation of its ecological environment and scenic features, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) designated or continued as a designated wildland area under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "minister" includes a person designated in writing by the minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "natural resources" means land, water and atmosphere, their mineral, vegetable and other components, and includes the flora and fauna on and in them;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "park" means Crown land established or continued as a park under this Act or the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "park officer" means a director, an officer or an employee appointed under section 4 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "park ranger" means a person appointed as a park ranger under section 4 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "park use permit" means a licence, issued under this Act, authorizing an activity or a course of behaviour or conduct, or the occupancy, use, development, exploitation or extraction of a natural resource on or in a park or conservancy;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permit", in sections 20 and 21, means a park use permit or a resource use permit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "recreation area" means Crown land reserved or set aside for public recreational use and established as a recreation area under this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "resource use permit" means a licence, issued under this Act, authorizing an activity or course of behaviour or conduct or the occupancy, use, development, exploitation or extraction of a natural resource on or in a recreation area.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: 2		  (1) This Act is subject to the Environment and Land Use Act, the Environmental Assessment Act, the Haida Nation Recognition Act, the Muskwa-Kechika Management Area Act, the Wildfire Act, except section 18 of that Act, and the Environmental Management Act, but otherwise, except as provided in this Act, this Act and the regulations are not subject to any other Act or regulation, whenever made, and a minister, ministry of government or agent of the Crown must not exercise any power granted under any other Act or regulation except in accordance with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (2) A bylaw or regulation of a municipality or regional district, or any provision of it, that is, in any manner, in conflict with, inconsistent with or repugnant to this Act or the regulations, is suspended and of no effect to the extent of the conflict, inconsistency or repugnancy.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (3) The Heritage Conservation Act applies in parks, conservancies and recreation areas.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (4) Subject to the regulations made under this Act, the Wildlife Act applies on any land, trail, path or waterway comprised in an order under section 6 (1) and in parks, conservancies and recreation areas.

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: 3		  (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the minister has jurisdiction over, and must manage and administer, all matters concerning parks, conservancies and recreation areas and public and private use and conduct in them, including all of the following:

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: (a) the rights, property and interests of the government in parks, conservancies and recreation areas;

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: (b) natural resources in parks, conservancies and recreation areas;

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: (c) wildlife and its habitats in parks, conservancies and recreation areas;

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: (d) the preservation, development, use and maintenance of parks, conservancies and recreation areas and natural resources in them;

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: (e) the regulation and control of public and private individuals in the use or exploitation of parks, conservancies and recreation areas and the natural resources in and on them, and of human activities, behaviour and conduct in parks, conservancies and recreation areas;

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: (f) all other matters under this Act.

heading: Duties and responsibilities of minister
paragraph: (2) The minister has, subject to an order under section 6, jurisdiction over and must manage and administer land or a trail, path or waterway comprised in an order under that section.

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph:
4
		  (1) The minister may appoint one or more directors and other officers and employees under the Public Service Act to assist the minister in the performance of duties and the exercise of powers under this Act.

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph: (2) The minister may appoint persons, or persons within a class of persons, to be park rangers.

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph: (3) Subject to the regulations and to any limitations, terms and conditions that may be imposed by the minister under subsection (4), a park ranger is responsible for enforcing compliance with

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph: (a) the Wildlife Act and the regulations under that Act, and

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph: (b) this Act, the regulations and other prescribed enactments within parks, conservancies, recreation areas and any land, trail, path or waterway comprised in an order under section 6 (1).

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph: (4) In appointing park rangers under subsection (2), the minister may

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph: (a) limit the powers and functions that the person or persons within the class of persons may exercise and perform, and

heading: Directors, officers, employees and park rangers
paragraph: (b) make the appointment subject to terms and conditions.

heading: Collaborative agreements
paragraph: 4.1		  The minister may enter into an agreement relating to the administration and management of matters and things referred to in section 3 or 6 with any of the following:

heading: Collaborative agreements
paragraph: (a) a government corporation;

heading: Collaborative agreements
paragraph: (b) a local government;

heading: Collaborative agreements
paragraph: (c) the government of Canada, the government of a province of Canada, the government of a jurisdiction outside Canada or an official or agency of any of those governments;

heading: Collaborative agreements
paragraph: (e) any other person or persons.

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph:
4.2
		  (1) The minister may enter into an agreement with a first nation respecting the first nation

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: (a) carrying out activities necessary for the exercise of aboriginal rights on, and

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: (b) having access for social, ceremonial and cultural purposes to,

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: land to which section 3 or 6 applies, and in respect of other topics relating to the management of matters and things referred to in section 3 or 6.

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: (2) An agreement entered into under subsection (1) is not a treaty or a land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), "first nation" includes

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: (a) a band, as defined in the Indian Act (Canada),

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: (b) another legal entity representing a first nation, or

heading: Relations with first nations
paragraph: (c) a person authorized by a band referred to in paragraph (a) or a legal entity referred to in paragraph (b).

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: 5		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (a) establish an area of Crown land as a Class A, Class B or Class C park, or as a conservancy or recreation area, or

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (b) designate land in a park, conservancy or recreation area as a designated wildland area,

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: and declare the name by which the park, conservancy, recreation area or designated wildland area is to be known.

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (2) Even though the power conferred on the Lieutenant Governor in Council by subsection (1) is expressed as being permissive, the Lieutenant Governor in Council must exercise that power to the extent and as often as may be necessary to ensure that the total area of parks and recreation areas

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (a) is not less than 7 300 000 hectares, and

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (b) will be not less than 10 000 000 hectares by January 1, 2000.

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (3) The Class A parks named and described in Schedules C and D of the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act are dedicated to the preservation of their natural environments for the inspiration, use and enjoyment of the public.

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (3.1) Conservancies are set aside

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (a) for the protection and maintenance of their biological diversity and natural environments,

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (b) for the preservation and maintenance of social, ceremonial and cultural uses of first nations,

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (c) for protection and maintenance of their recreational values, and

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (d) to ensure that development or use of their natural resources occurs in a sustainable manner consistent with the purposes of paragraphs (a), (b) and (c).

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, extend the boundaries of any park, or consolidate 2 or more of the parks, referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (6) Except as permitted by subsection (5), the boundaries of a park referred to in subsection (3) must not be affected except by an Act of the Legislature.

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (7) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by order, may extend the boundaries of any conservancy, or consolidate 2 or more of the conservancies, established or continued under the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act.

heading: Classification of parks, conservancies and recreation areas
paragraph: (8) Except as permitted under subsection (7), the boundaries of a conservancy established or continued under the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act must not be affected except by an Act of the Legislature.

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (a) an order has been made in respect of Crown land under the Environment and Land Use Act,

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (b) Crown land has been designated as green belt land under the Greenbelt Act,

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (c) Crown land is a heritage site under the Heritage Conservation Act,

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (d) land is leased to the government or to an agent of the government for public outdoor recreation,

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (e) land is owned by a person who has entered into an agreement with the government or with an agent of the government respecting the use of the land for outdoor recreation,

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (f) land is owned by a person who has entered into an agreement with the government or an agent of the government respecting the conservation, preservation or protection of the land or an amenity in relation to it,

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (g) a trail, path or waterway owned by the government is available for use by the public as a trail or path, or as a waterway for canoes or small boats, or

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (h) Crown land is established or continued as an ecological reserve under the Ecological Reserve Act or by the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act,

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order made under this and any other applicable Act, authorize the minister to manage and administer the land, or the trail, path or waterway, or the interest of the government in it.

heading: Additional powers for Crown land
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) that is also made under another Act must be consistent with that Act but, subject to that requirement, this Act applies to the land or to the trail, path or waterway to the extent specified in the order.

heading: Power to modify boundaries
paragraph: 7		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may cancel, reestablish or revise the boundaries of any park, conservancy or recreation area established under this Act to

heading: Power to modify boundaries
paragraph: (a) increase or decrease the area of the park, conservancy or recreation area,

heading: Power to modify boundaries
paragraph: (b) consolidate 2 or more parks, conservancies or recreation areas, or

heading: Power to modify boundaries
paragraph: (c) divide an existing park, conservancy or recreation area into 2 or more parks, conservancies or recreation areas.

heading: Power to modify boundaries
paragraph:
(2) 
          Subsection (1) does not apply to a park or conservancy continued under the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act.

heading: Official plan
paragraph: 7.1		  (1) For the purposes of this section, "official plan" means a plan that is

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (a) certified by the Surveyor General, by signature on the plan, to be an official plan, and

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (b) kept on deposit in the Crown land registry referred to in section 7 of the Land Act.

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (2) All or part of the boundary of a park, conservancy, designated wildland area or recreation area may be described by reference to

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (a) one or more official plans,

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (b) metes and bounds descriptions,

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (c) lot or parcel descriptions, or

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (d) any combination of the means referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c).

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (3) To the extent of any variance between the marked representation of the boundary on an official plan and the metes and bounds or other written descriptions on the official plan, the metes and bounds or other written descriptions prevail.

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (4) Copies of official plans must be available for public inspection in the Crown land registry during regular business hours, and a person may obtain a copy of an official plan on payment of a fee prescribed under section 6 (3) of the Land Act.

heading: Official plan
paragraph: (5) A copy of an official plan, that is certified by the Surveyor General to be a true copy, is admissible as evidence in a court without proof of the signature or official character of the Surveyor General.

heading: Publication in Gazette
paragraph: 7.2		  An order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council under this Act establishing or modifying a park, conservancy, designated wildland area or recreation area must be published in the Gazette.

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph:
8
		  (1) An interest in land in a Class A or Class C park must not be granted, sold, leased, pre-empted or otherwise alienated or obtained or made the subject of a licence except as authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit.

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph: (2) A park use permit referred to in subsection (1) must not be issued unless, in the opinion of the minister, to do so is necessary to preserve or maintain the recreational values of the park involved.

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph: (3) An interest in land in a Class B park must not be granted, sold, leased, pre-empted or otherwise alienated or obtained except as authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit.

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph: (4) A park use permit referred to in subsection (3) must not be issued unless, in the opinion of the minister, to do so is not detrimental to the recreational values of the park concerned.

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph: (5) Crown land in a recreation area

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph: (a) is reserved absolutely from sale, and title to that land is retained, in perpetuity, by the government, and

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph: (b) is reserved from lease or other disposal under the Land Act, except as may be approved by the minister.

heading: Restriction on alienation of interests
paragraph: (6) An interest in land in a conservancy must not be granted, sold, leased, pre-empted or otherwise alienated or made the subject of a licence except as authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: 9		  (1) A natural resource other than fish and wildlife taken, hunted or killed in accordance with the Wildlife Act and fish, game or wildlife stalked or pursued for observation or for photographic or study purposes, in a Class A or Class C park must not be granted, sold, removed, destroyed, damaged, disturbed or exploited except as authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (2) A park use permit referred to in subsection (1) must not be issued unless, in the opinion of the minister, it is necessary for the preservation or maintenance of the recreational values of the park involved.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (3) A natural resource other than fish and wildlife taken, hunted or killed in accordance with the Wildlife Act and fish, game or wildlife stalked or pursued for observation or for photographic or study purposes, in a Class B park must not be granted, sold, removed, destroyed, damaged, disturbed or exploited except as authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (4) A park use permit referred to in subsection (3) must not be issued unless, in the opinion of the minister, to do so is not detrimental to the recreational values of the park involved.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (5) A natural resource other than fish and wildlife taken, hunted or killed in accordance with the Wildlife Act and fish, game or wildlife stalked or pursued for observation or for photographic or study purposes, in a designated wildland area must not be granted, sold, removed, destroyed, damaged, disturbed or exploited.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (6) A natural resource other than fish and wildlife taken, hunted or killed in accordance with the Wildlife Act and fish, game or wildlife stalked or pursued for observation or for photographic or study purposes, in a recreation area must not be granted, sold, removed, destroyed, disturbed or damaged, exploited, developed, improved or utilized under any Act except as may be approved by the minister.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (6.1) A natural resource, other than fish and wildlife taken, hunted or killed in accordance with the Wildlife Act and fish, game or wildlife stalked or pursued for observation or for photographic or study purposes, in a conservancy must not be granted, sold, removed, destroyed, disturbed, damaged, exploited, developed, improved or utilized except as authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (7) A natural resource in a park of any class must not be granted, sold, removed, destroyed, disturbed, damaged or exploited unless, in the opinion of the minister, the development, improvement and use of the park in accordance with section 12 (3) will not be hindered by it.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (9) A natural resource in a conservancy must not be granted, sold, removed, destroyed, disturbed, damaged or exploited unless, in the opinion of the minister, the development, improvement and use of the conservancy in accordance with section 5 (3.1) will not be hindered by it.

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (10) A park use permit must not be issued to authorize the following activities in a conservancy:

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (a) commercial logging;

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (b) mining;

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (c) hydro electric power generation, other than local run-of-the-river projects;

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (d) any other activity unless, in the opinion of the minister, the activity will not restrict, prevent or inhibit the development, improvement or use of the conservancy in accordance with section 5 (3.1).

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (11) In subsection (10):

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: "commercial logging" means harvesting timber for the primary purpose of selling or trading the timber;

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: "local run-of-the-river projects", in relation to a conservancy, means run-of-the-river projects supplying power for use only

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (a) in the conservancy, or

heading: Natural resources protected
paragraph: (b) by communities, including first nation communities, that do not otherwise have access to hydro electric power.

heading: Resort and tourism development
paragraph: 9.1		  Nothing in section 8 (2) or 9 (2) prevents the issuance of a park use permit for an activity related to resort or tourism development if, in the minister's opinion, the activity and the development are consistent with or complementary to the recreational values of the park involved.

heading: Film production
paragraph:
9.2
		  Nothing in section 8 (2) or 9 (2) or (7) prevents the issuance of a park use permit for an activity related to film production, including commercial film production, if, in the minister's opinion, the activity is not detrimental to the recreational values of the park involved.

heading: Research
paragraph:
9.3
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Research
paragraph: "environmental assessment" means an assessment under the Environmental Assessment Act or an environmental assessment under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012;

heading: Research
paragraph: "feasibility study" means a study of the feasibility, including, without limitation, the feasibility of the location, design, construction, use, maintenance, improvement or deactivation, of one or more of the following:

heading: Research
paragraph: (a) a road or highway;

heading: Research
paragraph: (b) a pipeline;

heading: Research
paragraph: (c) a transmission line;

heading: Research
paragraph: (d) a telecommunications project;

heading: Research
paragraph: (e) a prescribed project or a project in a prescribed class of projects;

heading: Research
paragraph: (f) a structure, improvement or work related to a project described in any of paragraphs (a) to (e);

heading: Research
paragraph: "protected area" means a park or a conservancy;

heading: Research
paragraph: "purpose" means,

heading: Research
paragraph: (a) in relation to a park,

heading: Research
paragraph: (i)  the preservation of the park's natural environment for the inspiration, use and enjoyment of the public, and

heading: Research
paragraph: (ii)  if a category is specified for the park under section 12 (1), the purpose associated with the category, and

heading: Research
paragraph: (b) in relation to a conservancy, the purposes specified in section 5 (3.1) (a), (b) and (c).

heading: Research
paragraph: (2) Nothing in section 8 (2) or (4) or 9 (2), (4), (7), (9) or (10) (d) prevents the issuance of a park use permit for an activity related to research in a protected area if, in the opinion of the minister,

heading: Research
paragraph: (a) to do so is consistent with the purpose of the protected area,

heading: Research
paragraph: (b) the research relates to the improvement of public health or safety,

heading: Research
paragraph: (c) the research relates to an environmental assessment or a feasibility study, or

heading: Research
paragraph: (d) the research will inform a decision of the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the Legislature in relation to the boundaries of the protected area.

heading: Class C parks boards
paragraph: 10		  (1) Every Class C park must be under the jurisdiction of a separate park board appointed by the minister.

heading: Class C parks boards
paragraph: (2) A park board consists of not less than 3 and not more than 7 members and, on appointment of its members, is a corporation.

heading: Class C parks boards
paragraph: (3) A park board must conduct its proceedings and manage, administer, regulate and control the park under its jurisdiction in accordance with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph:
11
		  (1) For the purpose of establishing or enlarging any park, conservancy or recreation area, the minister, on behalf of the government, with the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, may do one or more of the following:

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (a) purchase or otherwise acquire, accept and take possession of land, improvements on land, timber, timber rights and other rights;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (b) grant, convey or transfer to any person, in exchange for land, improvements, or timber acquired under paragraph (a), other land, timber or rights of the government.

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of establishing or enlarging a park, conservancy or recreation area, the minister may expropriate

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (a) land,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (b) rights under a lease, as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act, of the recorded holder of the lease,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (c) rights under a claim, as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act, of the recorded holder of the claim,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (d) rights under a Crown granted 2 post claim of its owner, as defined in the Mineral Tenure Act,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (e) rights under a lease, as defined in the Coal Act, of the lessee under the lease,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (f) rights under a licence, as defined in the Coal Act, of the licensee, or

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (g) a road or improvement, or rights in relation to a road or improvement, if

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (i)  in the case of a road,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (A) the road is authorized under a road permit, or

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (B) the road is authorized, for a timber production purpose, under a special use permit,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of an improvement, the improvement is authorized, for a timber production purpose, under a special use permit, and

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (iii)  the road or improvement is on Crown land referred to in subsection (2.3).

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (2.1) An expropriation under subsection (2) (g) is effective on the date the park, conservancy or recreation area to which it relates is established or enlarged.

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (2.2) The holder of a right expropriated under subsection (2) is entitled to compensation

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (a) in relation to a right referred to in subsection (2) (b), (c) or (d), in accordance with section 17.1 of the Mineral Tenure Act,

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (b) in relation to a right referred to in subsection (2) (e) or (f), in accordance with section 4 of the Coal Act, and

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (2.21) If a road or improvement authorized under a road permit or special use permit is expropriated under subsection (2) (g), or if rights under the permit in relation to the road or improvement are expropriated under that subsection, the permit holder's entitlement to or eligibility for compensation and the compensation, if any, payable are to be determined under Part 18 of the Forest Act.

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (2.3) If the establishment or enlargement of a park, conservancy or recreation area requires Crown land in any of the following areas, the portion of the Crown land required is deleted from the area effective on the date the park, conservancy or recreation area is established:

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (a) a timber supply area;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (b) the licence area of a non-TFL timber licence entered into under the Forest Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (c) the licence area of an area-based licence entered into under the Forest Act.

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (2.4) If the holder of a forest tenure is affected by a deletion under subsection (2.3), the forest tenure holder's entitlement to or eligibility for compensation and the amount of compensation, if any, payable are to be determined under Part 18 of the Forest Act.

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (3) In this section:

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "area-based licence" has the same meaning as in the Forest Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "Crown granted 2 post claim" has the same meaning as in the Mineral Tenure Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "forest tenure" means any of the following licences or permits entered into under the Forest Act:

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (a) a forest licence;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (b) an area-based licence;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (c) a non-TFL timber licence within the meaning of section 180 of that Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (d) a forestry licence to cut;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (e) a timber sale licence;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: (f) a Christmas tree permit;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "licence area" has the same meaning as in the Forest Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "non-TFL timber licence" has the same meaning as in section 180 of the Forest Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "road permit" means a road permit issued under section 115 of the Forest Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "special use permit" means a special use permit referred to in section 2 of the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "timber production purpose" has the same meaning as in section 180 of the Forest Act;

heading: Minister's power to acquire land
paragraph: "timber supply area" has the same meaning as in the Forest Act.

heading: Park categories
paragraph: 12		  (1) The minister may specify a park to be in one of the following categories:

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (a) category 1, if the main purpose of the park is the preservation of its particular atmosphere, environment or ecology;

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (b) category 2, if the main purpose of the park is the preservation and presentation to the public of specific features of scientific, historic or scenic nature;

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (c) category 3, if the main purpose of the park is to offer enjoyment, convenience and comfort to the travelling public;

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (d) category 4, if the main purpose of the park is to offer recreational opportunity to the public of a particular community or area;

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (e) category 5, if the main purpose of the park is to offer opportunities to participate in a specific recreational activity;

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (f) category 6, if the park has 2 or more purposes.

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (2) The development and improvement of a park must be

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (a) if the park is in category 1, directed toward and limited to that necessary to the preservation, for public enjoyment, of the atmosphere, environment and ecology of the park,

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (b) if the park is in category 2, directed toward and limited to that necessary to the preservation, for public enjoyment, of the scientific, historic or scenic features of the park that are specified or described by the minister,

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (c) if the park is in category 3, directed toward and limited to those necessary to the beautification of the park and the provision of facilities necessary to the enjoyment, convenience and comfort of the travelling public,

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (d) if the park is in category 4, directed toward the provision of recreational opportunities for the community or communities specified or described by the minister,

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (e) if the park is in category 5, directed toward and limited to those necessary to the adaptation of the park to a single special use designated by the minister, and

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (f) if the park is in category 6, directed and limited in accordance with a zoning plan, which must be prepared by the director, allocating various lands of a single park to 2 or more of the purposes enumerated in subsection (1).

heading: Park categories
paragraph: (3) A person must not carry on, in any park, any activity that will restrict, prevent or inhibit the use of the park for its designated purpose.

heading: Private construction restricted
paragraph:
13
		  A person must not construct, install, erect or place any structure, improvement or work of any nature in a park, conservancy or recreation area, except under the authority of a valid and subsisting park use permit or resource use permit.

heading: Dumping prohibited
paragraph:
14
		  A person must not transport any garbage, refuse or domestic or industrial waste through, over, in or on any park, conservancy or recreation area or deposit any of that material in or on any park, conservancy or recreation area, except as may be authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit or resource use permit.

heading: Disposal of timber
paragraph:
15
		  All timber cut on or removed from any park, conservancy or recreation area must be disposed of in accordance with the Forest Act.

heading: Occupancy and use of land restricted
paragraph: 16		  Except as may be authorized by a valid and subsisting park use permit or resource use permit, a person must not do any of the following:

heading: Occupancy and use of land restricted
paragraph: (a) use or occupy land in a park, conservancy or recreation area for a log storage area, mill site, road, right of way, disposal area for tailings or waste or any other industrial purpose;

heading: Occupancy and use of land restricted
paragraph: (b) obtain any surface right or right to the use or occupancy of the surface of any land in a park, conservancy or recreation area;

heading: Occupancy and use of land restricted
paragraph: (c) exercise in a park, conservancy or recreation area any right under the Mineral Tenure Act, the Coal Act or the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act;

heading: Occupancy and use of land restricted
paragraph: (d) flood any part of a park, conservancy or recreation area, or impound, divert or distribute water in a park, conservancy or recreation area;

heading: Occupancy and use of land restricted
paragraph: (e) establish or carry on any work or improvement or any commercial or industrial activity or enterprise in a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: 17		  A director or any park officer acting on the director's behalf may do one or more of the following:

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: (a) enter on and inspect any land, road, structure or work in a park, conservancy or recreation area;

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: (b) order the repair, alteration, improvement, evacuation or removal of or addition to a structure or work in a park, conservancy or recreation area;

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: (c) order any person in any park, conservancy or recreation area to cease or refrain from an action, an omission or conduct that the director or park officer, in the director's or park officer's discretion, considers dangerous to life or property or detrimental to the public interest;

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: (d) require any person in any park, conservancy or recreation area to inform the director or officer of

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: (i)  the person's name, address and occupation,

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: (ii)  any fact or intention relating to the person's use of the park, conservancy or recreation area, and

heading: Authorities of director and officers
paragraph: (iii)  the person's conduct and activities in the park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Authority to carry out orders
paragraph:
18
		  If a lawful order of a director or a park officer under section 17 is not carried out or is only partially or imperfectly carried out,

heading: Authority to carry out orders
paragraph: (a) a director may authorize any person to carry out or complete the carrying out of the order,

heading: Authority to carry out orders
paragraph: (b) the expense to the government of carrying out or completing the carrying out of the order is a debt owing to the government by the person to whom the order was first given or directed, recoverable at the suit of the government in any court of competent jurisdiction, and

heading: Authority to carry out orders
paragraph: (c) the certificate of a director is proof in the absence of evidence to the contrary of the indebtedness and the amount of the debt.

heading: No rights acquired in contravention of this Act
paragraph:
19
		  (1) No person may

heading: No rights acquired in contravention of this Act
paragraph: (a) acquire any right or title to or interest in

heading: No rights acquired in contravention of this Act
paragraph: (i)  any natural resource removed, disturbed, destroyed, damaged or exploited in contravention of this Act, or

heading: No rights acquired in contravention of this Act
paragraph: (ii)  any structure, improvement or work constructed, installed, erected or placed in a park, conservancy or recreation area in contravention of this Act, or

heading: No rights acquired in contravention of this Act
paragraph: (b) acquire any lien on or in respect of, or any claim against any person or the government in respect of any work or expenditure done or incurred in connection with a natural resource, structure, improvement or work referred to in paragraph (a) (i) or (ii).

heading: No rights acquired in contravention of this Act
paragraph: (2) The minister or an authorized representative of the minister may seize any natural resource, structure, improvement or work referred to in subsection (1) and sell or otherwise dispose of it for the sole benefit of the government.

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph:
20
		  (1) Subject to this Act and only on receiving the prescribed application and administration fees, the minister may issue a permit, on the terms and conditions the minister may specify, authorizing a person to do anything for which a permit is required under this Act.

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (2) The minister may issue a permit under subsection (1) on receiving an application and with or without a public competition.

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (3) The minister may require that, before a public competition is held in respect of the issuance of a permit or a decision is made whether to issue a permit, the public be provided with an opportunity to review details and provide comments to the minister in respect of the proposed permit.

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (3.1) If the minister requires public consultation under subsection (3), the minister must publish in the prescribed manner details respecting the proposed permit, the period during which the minister will accept comments from the public and the address to which comments should be sent.

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (3.2) The terms and conditions specified in a permit issued under subsection (1) must include

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (a) the amounts, or a method for calculating the amounts, other than prescribed fees, payable in respect of the permit, and

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (b) when the amounts referred to in paragraph (a) must be paid.

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (3.3) The minister, in a permit, may waive payment of amounts referred to in subsection (3.2).

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (5) An application for a permit must be made in the form and manner approved by the minister.

heading: Issuing permits
paragraph: (6) Before issuing a permit under this Act, the minister may require that the permit be signed by the person to whom the permit is proposed to be issued.

heading: Permits authorizing road construction in a conservancy
paragraph:
20.1
		  Despite anything in this Act, the minister may issue a park use permit to a person for the construction, use or maintenance of a road in a conservancy if

heading: Permits authorizing road construction in a conservancy
paragraph: (a) the conservancy is named and described in Schedule F of the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act, and

heading: Permits authorizing road construction in a conservancy
paragraph: (b) the road is for the purpose of providing access to natural resources lying beyond the conservancy.

heading: Applications and assurances required for certain permits
paragraph: 21		  A permit may not be issued under section 20 to authorize the removal, destruction, disturbance, damage or exploitation of any natural resource or any work, occupancy, undertaking or activity incidental to it unless

heading: Applications and assurances required for certain permits
paragraph: (a) the person to whom the permit is proposed to be issued makes an application for the permit in accordance with section 20 (5), and

heading: Applications and assurances required for certain permits
paragraph: (b) the application is accompanied by a written undertaking, executed by the person to whom the permit is proposed to be issued, to pay to the government, in addition to any other sums that may be or become payable under any other Act,

heading: Applications and assurances required for certain permits
paragraph: (i)  the cost incurred by the government in surveying, cruising, examining and inspecting the area to be affected, and

heading: Applications and assurances required for certain permits
paragraph: (ii)  the prescribed fees for the permit.

heading: Restoration deposit may be required
paragraph:
22
		  Before issuing a park use permit or resource use permit, the minister or the minister's authorized agent may require the person to whom it is intended to issue the permit to pay to the government a sum that the minister or that agent considers sufficient to defray the cost of the restoration or repair of the park, conservancy or recreation area concerned necessitated by the use authorized by the permit.

heading: Permit not transferable
paragraph:
23
		  A park use permit or resource use permit is not transferable except with the approval of the minister and subject to conditions the minister may determine.

heading: Rights and interest vested in government
paragraph:
24
		  Every right, title and interest in any structure, improvement or installation in a park, conservancy or recreation area belongs to the government except as otherwise provided by a park use permit or resource use permit.

heading: No private rights except by permit
paragraph:
25
		  A person or party must not be permitted to acquire any property right in any park, conservancy or recreation area except under a park use permit or resource use permit as provided for in regulations.

heading: Occupiers of improvements on government land exempt from tax on those improvements
paragraph:
26
		  Lawful occupiers of improvements that are the property of the government in a park, conservancy or recreation area are exempt from taxes under any Act of British Columbia in respect of the improvements.

heading: Minister may accept gifts
paragraph:
27
		  (1) The minister, on behalf of the government, may accept gifts or bequests of money or other property for purposes of parks, conservancies, recreation areas, ecological reserves or areas protected under the Environment and Land Use Act and administered by the minister.

heading: Minister may accept gifts
paragraph: (2) Funds accepted under subsection (1) must be used at the direction of the minister in accordance with the terms of the gift or bequest.

heading: Minister may accept gifts
paragraph: (3) Subject to the terms of a gift or bequest under subsection (1), the minister may dispose of property, other than land, accepted under that subsection.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: 27.1		  (1) After providing a person with an opportunity to be heard, the minister may, in accordance with the regulations, impose an administrative penalty on the person if the minister is satisfied, on a balance of probabilities, that the person has

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of this Act or the regulations,

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with a term or condition of a permit issued under this Act, other than a permit issued by a park board, or

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) failed to wholly or perfectly comply with an order under section 17 or 33 (6).

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) An administrative penalty imposed under this section must be paid to the government within the prescribed time and in accordance with any other prescribed requirements.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) If, under this section, the minister imposes an administrative penalty on a person, a prosecution for an offence under this Act in respect of the same contravention may not be brought against the person.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) If a corporation contravenes a prescribed provision of the regulations or fails to comply with a term or condition of a permit or with an order, as described in subsection (1), an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure is liable for an administrative penalty under this section even if the corporation is liable for or pays an administrative penalty.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (5) All revenue the government derives from administrative penalties imposed under this section must be paid into the Park Enhancement Fund special account established by section 9.6 (2) of the Special Accounts Appropriation and Control Act.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: 27.2		  (1) Before the date an administrative penalty under section 27.1 is due, the minister may, in accordance with the regulations, enter into an agreement with the person who is liable for the administrative penalty.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (2) An agreement under subsection (1) may provide, in accordance with the regulations, for the reduction or cancellation of the administrative penalty subject to the terms and conditions the minister considers necessary or desirable.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (3) An agreement under subsection (1) must specify the time for performing any terms and conditions and, if the person fails to perform the terms and conditions by the date specified, the administrative penalty imposed under section 27.1 is due and payable on that date.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph:
27.3
		  (1) An administrative penalty under section 27.1 may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required under section 27.1, the minister may file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) must be signed by the minister and must contain the following information:

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the administrative penalty;

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) particulars of the administrative penalty;

heading: Recovery of administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the administrative penalty.

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph:
27.4
		  (1) In this section, "appeal board" means the Environmental Appeal Board continued under section 93 of the Environmental Management Act.

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) A person who is liable for an administrative penalty under section 27.1 may appeal the following decisions under this Act to the appeal board:

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) a decision of the minister, under section 27.1 (1), to impose the administrative penalty on the person;

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) a decision of the minister, under section 27.2 (3), that the person failed to perform a term or condition of an agreement under section 27.2 (1).

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) The following provisions of the Environmental Management Act apply in relation to an appeal under this section:

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) section 93.1 [application of Administrative Tribunals Act];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) section 94 [parties and witnesses];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) section 96 [decision of appeal board];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (d) section 97 [varying and rescinding orders of appeal board];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (e) section 98 [appeal board power to enter property];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (f) section 101 [time limit for commencing appeal];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (g) section 102 (2) [procedure on appeals - new hearing];

heading: Appeals in relation to administrative penalties
paragraph: (h) section 103 [powers of appeal board in deciding appeal].

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: 28		  (1) A person who contravenes any provision of this Act commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to $1 000 000 or a term of imprisonment of not more than one year or both.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes a regulation commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to $200 000.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (3) When a contravention of the Act or regulations continues for more than one day, the person is guilty of a separate offence for each day on which the contravention continues.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (4) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (4.1) A person who has been charged with an offence under this Act may not be subject to an administrative penalty in respect of the circumstances that gave rise to the charge.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (5) The time limit for laying an information for an offence under this Act is

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) 3 years after the date that the facts on which the information is based arose, or

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) if the minister issues a certificate described in subsection (6), 18 months after the date that the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Offences and penalties

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation, unless the context otherwise requires:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "Act" means the Park Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "backcountry" means an area in a park, conservancy or recreation area that is not frontcountry;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "camp" means to occupy a campsite, to set up a tent or other shelter or to remain overnight;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "campground" means one or more campsites managed by an operator or the ministry;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "campsite" means an area in a park, conservancy or recreation area developed by the ministry to accommodate persons who wish to camp;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "Canada" does not include a corporation

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) that is, under an enactment of Canada, an agent of Her Majesty in right of Canada,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) of which the government of Canada owns, directly or indirectly, more than 50% of the issued voting shares, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) that is controlled by the government of Canada, and for the purpose of this definition a corporation is controlled by the government of Canada when a majority of the members of the corporation or of its board of directors or board of management consists of either or both of the following:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (i)  persons appointed as members by the Governor in Council, by a minister of the government of Canada or by an enactment of Canada;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (ii)  public officers acting as such;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "cycle" means a device having any number of wheels that is propelled by human power and on which a person may ride;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "day use area" means an area in a park, conservancy or recreation area managed by an operator or the ministry for picnicking and other daytime activities;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "designated long-stay campsite" means a campsite in a park, conservancy or recreation area that has been designated as a campsite where a person may camp for more than 14 days in a calendar year;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "dock" means a structure connected to dry land and used for the purposes of mooring a vessel;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "domestic animal" means a vertebrate that has been domesticated;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "firearm" includes a rifle, shotgun, handgun, spring gun or any device that propels a projectile by means of an explosion, compressed gas or spring, but does not include a longbow or crossbow;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "frontcountry" means an area in a park, conservancy or recreation area within one kilometre of either side of the centreline of a park road or a highway;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "group" means 15 or more persons;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "guide" means a person who, for compensation or reward received or promised, accompanies, assists or provides a service to another person;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "hunt" means to shoot at, attract, search for, chase, pursue, follow after or on the trail of, stalk or lie in wait for wildlife, or to attempt to do any of those things, whether or not the wildlife is then or subsequently wounded, killed or captured,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) with the intention to capture the wildlife, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) while in possession of a firearm or other weapon;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "litter" means

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) garbage, refuse, rubbish or trash of any kind, including a container, package, bottle or can, or any part thereof, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) any abandoned or discarded article, product or item of manufacture,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: but does not include wastes of the primary processes of mining, logging, sawmilling, farming or manufacturing;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "operator" means a person authorized by a park use permit or resource use permit to operate facilities in any part of a park, conservancy or recreation area;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "park" includes any land, trail, path or waterway comprised in an order under section 6 (1) (a) to (g) of the Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "park road" means a road in a park, conservancy or recreation area that is designed and developed for the passage or parking of motor vehicles licensed under the Motor Vehicle Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "party" means up to 8 persons, of whom at least one, but no more than 4, are 16 years old or older, and who may have with them

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) one recreational vehicle,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) one non-recreational vehicle, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) one non-recreational vehicle and one legally towed trailer that is not a trailer primarily designed as temporary living quarters for recreational or travel use;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "Province" does not include a corporation

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) that is, under an Act, an agent of the Crown,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) of which the government owns, directly or indirectly, more than 50% of the issued voting shares, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) that is controlled by the government, and for the purpose of this definition a corporation is controlled by the government when a majority of the members of the corporation or of its board of directors or board of management consists of either or both of the following:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (i)  persons appointed as members by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, by a minister or by an Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (ii)  public officers acting as such;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "recreational vehicle" means a self-propelled vehicle or a trailer, primarily designed as temporary living quarters for recreational or travel use;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "snowmobile" means a snowmobile as defined in the Snowmobile Regulation, B.C. Reg. 65/72;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "trap" means to trap, snare, net or use any other device to take or capture wildlife;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "vessel" means a boat, canoe, kayak or other craft used, or capable of being used, for navigation on water;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "waste" means waste as defined in the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: "wildlife" means raptors, threatened species, endangered species, game or other species of vertebrates prescribed as wildlife under the Wildlife Act;

heading: Interpretation

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) undertaking a camping trip or day use trip organized for the group by a school, not-for-profit society or recreational centre operated by a municipality or regional district for the benefit of the members of the group who are 18 years of age or younger, and
