paragraph:
9
		  (1) A park ranger may order a person who does anything contrary to this regulation to leave a park, conservancy or recreation area, or a specified portion of it, within a period of time specified by the park ranger, and every person so ordered must comply with the order and leave the park, conservancy or recreation area, or the specified portion of it, within that specified period of time.

heading: Eviction
paragraph: (2) If no period of time is specified in an order issued under subsection (1), the order is effective immediately.

heading: Eviction
paragraph: (3) The order issued under subsection (1) must specify the period of time during which the order is to remain in effect, but in no case may it remain in effect for more than 72 hours from the time the order is issued.

heading: Eviction
paragraph: (4) A park ranger may use reasonable force to remove a person from the park, conservancy or recreation area, or the specified portion of it, if that person fails to comply with an order under subsection (1).

heading: Eviction
paragraph: (5) A person who is ordered to leave the park, conservancy or recreation area is not entitled to a refund of any fee which may have been paid by the party or group of which that person is a member.

heading: Signs
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A park officer may erect a sign or other device specifying an area in which specific activities are permitted, prohibited or restricted in a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Signs
paragraph: (2) Every person must observe and obey every prohibition and restriction announced by the sign or other device erected under subsection (1).

heading: Fires
paragraph:
11
		  (1) A person must not start or maintain a fire in a park, conservancy or recreation area in

heading: Fires
paragraph: (a) a campground,

heading: Fires
paragraph: (b) frontcountry, or

heading: Fires
paragraph: (c) backcountry that is less than 2 000 hectares in size,

heading: Fires
paragraph: unless the fire is

heading: Fires
paragraph: (d) in a fireplace provided by the ministry, and

heading: Fires
paragraph: (e) not more than 0.5 metres in diameter and 0.5 metres in height.

heading: Fires
paragraph: (2) A person must not use vegetation from a campground or from frontcountry to start or maintain a fire except

heading: Fires
paragraph: (a) vegetation that is specifically provided as firewood by the ministry or an operator, or

heading: Fires
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Fires
paragraph: (3) A person must not use vegetation from backcountry to start or maintain a fire except vegetation that is dead and lying on the ground.

heading: Fires
paragraph: (4) A person who starts or maintains a fire must extinguish the fire when that person leaves the campground, frontcountry or backcountry.

heading: Fires
paragraph: (5) A park officer may, at any time,

heading: Fires
paragraph: (a) prohibit a fire in a park, conservancy or recreation area,

heading: Fires
paragraph: (b) extinguish a fire, or

heading: Fires
paragraph: (c) require that a fire be contained within a device approved by the park officer.

heading: Tobacco and e-cigarettes
paragraph:
11.1
		  (1) In this section, "activated e-cigarette", "e-cigarette" and "tobacco" have the same meaning as in the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act.

heading: Tobacco and e-cigarettes
paragraph: (2) A person must not smoke tobacco, hold lighted tobacco, use an e-cigarette or hold an activated e-cigarette in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Tobacco and e-cigarettes
paragraph: (a) in an area as permitted by a sign or other device, or

heading: Tobacco and e-cigarettes
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Snow sliding devices
paragraph: 12		  Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not use or operate any snow sliding device in Mount Seymour Park, Cypress Park or E.C. Manning Park unless

heading: Snow sliding devices
paragraph: (a) in an area specifically designated and posted for such use, and

heading: Snow sliding devices
paragraph: (b) on a snow sliding device approved by a park officer.

heading: Responsibility for action of minors
paragraph:
13
		  A parent, guardian, custodian or person in charge of a minor must not permit the minor to do anything that is prohibited by the Act or this regulation.

heading: Exemption from this regulation
paragraph:
14
		  A person who is a peace officer, park officer or park ranger is exempt from this regulation while acting in that capacity.

heading: Obstruction of a park officer or park ranger
paragraph:
15
		  A person must not willfully obstruct a park officer or park ranger acting in that capacity.

heading: Bowron Lake Park special regulation
paragraph:
16
		  Except on Bowron Lake or as authorized by a park officer, not more than 6 persons may travel together on the circuit of lakes in Bowron Lake Park.

heading: Storage of equipment and supplies
paragraph:
17
		  (1) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not store, cache or leave equipment or supplies in a park, conservancy or recreation area for a period of more than 14 days in a calendar year.

heading: Storage of equipment and supplies
paragraph: (2) A person must not store, cache or leave equipment or supplies in a campground or day use area except

heading: Storage of equipment and supplies
paragraph: (a) in the campsite at which that person is registered, or

heading: Storage of equipment and supplies
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Horses prohibited
paragraph:
18
		  A person must not have a horse or other draught or riding animal in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Horses prohibited
paragraph: (a) in an area or on a trail as permitted by a sign or other device, or

heading: Horses prohibited
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not allow a domestic animal to enter or remain in any part of a park, conservancy or recreation area that is

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (a) a beach within a campground or day use area,

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (b) a public building or structure, or

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (c) an area in which domestic animals are prohibited by a sign or other device.

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a domestic animal that is used to guide a blind person.

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (3) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not allow a domestic animal to enter or remain in frontcountry or in backcountry that is less than 2 000 hectares in size unless the domestic animal is

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (a) restrained by a leash not longer than 2 metres, or

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (b) confined in a container, enclosure or motor vehicle.

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (4) A person must not allow a domestic animal in a park, conservancy or recreation area to

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (a) cause an annoyance,

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (b) injure a person,

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (c) damage property or vegetation, or

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (d) chase or molest wildlife.

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (5) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not allow a domestic animal to enter or remain in Bowron Lake Park or Garibaldi Park.

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (6) A person who has a domestic animal in a park, conservancy or recreation area must dispose of excrement from that domestic animal in a manner and at a location where the excrement will not cause a public inconvenience or annoyance.

heading: Control of domestic animals
paragraph: (7) A park officer may order a person who contravenes this section to remove the domestic animal from the park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Control of other animals
paragraph:
20
		  Except as authorized by a park officer, a person who owns or is responsible for an animal must not, in a park, conservancy or recreation area, allow that animal to

heading: Control of other animals
paragraph: (a) graze, browse or otherwise consume vegetation, or

heading: Control of other animals
paragraph: (b) roam at large.

heading: Explosives prohibited
paragraph:
21
		  A person must not have an explosive or an explosive substance in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Explosives prohibited
paragraph: (a) lawfully carried firearm ammunition, or

heading: Explosives prohibited
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Peace officer authority under Motor Vehicle Act
paragraph:
22
		  A park ranger has the powers and authority of a peace officer for the purposes of enforcement of the Motor Vehicle Act and control of traffic within a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: 23		  (1) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (a) stop or park a vehicle on the travelled portion of a park road, or

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (b) stop or park a vehicle in such a manner as to

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (i)  impede the proper use of a park road,

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (ii)  damage vegetation,

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (iii)  restrict or inhibit recreational use of the park, conservancy or recreation area, or

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (iv)  park a vehicle in the frontcountry without payment of the vehicle parking fee required by regulation.

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (2) A person must not, between the hours of 11 p.m. and 7 a.m. the following day, stop or park a vehicle in a campground, day use area or parking area of a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (a) at a campsite where that person is the member of a registered party, group or youth group,

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (b) in a parking area as permitted by a sign or other device, or

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (c) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (3) If a vehicle is stopped or parked in contravention of subsection (1) or (2), a park officer may remove the vehicle to a place of impoundment and any costs incurred by that removal are a debt of the owner of the vehicle payable to the party that removed and impounded the vehicle, which debt must be paid before removal of the vehicle from the place of impoundment.

heading: Illegal parking and tow away
paragraph: (4) A park officer removing a vehicle under subsection (3) must exercise reasonable care to avoid damage to the vehicle involved, but neither the Province nor any park officer is liable or accountable to the owner for damage to the vehicle being removed arising from that removal.

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph:
24
		  (1) A person must not use or operate a motor vehicle, motorcycle or other self-propelled vehicle in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph: (a) on a park road,

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph: (b) in an area as permitted by a sign or other device, or

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph: (c) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a self-propelled wheelchair or other similar conveyance used by a disabled person.

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph: (3) A person must not use or operate a snowmobile in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph: (a) in an area or on a trail as permitted by a sign or other device, or

heading: Motor vehicles and snowmobiles
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Cycles
paragraph:
25
		  A person must not ride a cycle in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Cycles
paragraph: (a) on a park road,

heading: Cycles
paragraph: (b) in an area or on a trail as permitted by a sign or other device, or

heading: Cycles
paragraph: (c) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Commercial vehicles prohibited
paragraph:
26
		  Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not have in a park, conservancy or recreation area a vehicle that displays advertising or is equipped with a public address system if that vehicle is being used to advertise, demonstrate or attract attention.

heading: Aircraft
paragraph:
27
		  (1) Subject to the Act and this section, a person may use an aircraft to arrive at or depart from a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Aircraft
paragraph: (2) A person must not use an aircraft to arrive at or depart from parks or parts of parks that are set out in Column 1 of Schedule A, except as may be provided for in the same row in Column 2 of that schedule.

heading: Possession of firearms, bows and crossbows
paragraph:
28
		  A person must not possess a firearm, bow or crossbow in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Possession of firearms, bows and crossbows
paragraph: (a) a firearm, bow or crossbow that is carried in a vehicle,

heading: Possession of firearms, bows and crossbows
paragraph: (b) during an open season specified under the Wildlife Act in those parks, conservancies and recreation areas listed in Schedule B,

heading: Possession of firearms, bows and crossbows
paragraph: (c) in Columbia Lake Park between September 10 and June 15 of the following year, or

heading: Possession of firearms, bows and crossbows
paragraph: (d) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Discharge of firearms, bows and crossbows prohibited
paragraph: 29		  (1) A person must not discharge a firearm, bow or crossbow in a park, conservancy or recreation area except

heading: Discharge of firearms, bows and crossbows prohibited
paragraph: (a) during an open season specified under the Wildlife Act in those parks, conservancies and recreation areas listed in Schedule B and only for the purposes of hunting, or

heading: Discharge of firearms, bows and crossbows prohibited
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Discharge of firearms, bows and crossbows prohibited
paragraph: (2) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not hunt or discharge a firearm, bow or crossbow in a park, conservancy or recreation area within 400 metres of either side of the centreline of a park road or highway.

heading: Feeding of wildlife
paragraph: 30		  A person must not feed wildlife in a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Seizure of hunting and fishing devices
paragraph:
31
		  (1) A park ranger may seize a firearm, bow, crossbow, fishing rod or other device used in a park, conservancy or recreation area to capture fish or wildlife if the park ranger finds that the firearm, bow, crossbow, fishing rod or other device is being used by or is in the possession of a person who

heading: Seizure of hunting and fishing devices
paragraph: (a) is in contravention of the Wildlife Act or section 28 or 29 of this regulation, or

heading: Seizure of hunting and fishing devices
paragraph: (b) fails upon request to exhibit a proper licence or permit issued under the Wildlife Act.

heading: Seizure of hunting and fishing devices
paragraph: (2) A firearm, bow, crossbow, fishing rod or other device that is seized under subsection (1) must be taken before a justice who, if satisfied that at the time of seizure it was being used or possessed in contravention of the Wildlife Act or section 28 or 29 of this regulation, may order it forfeited to the Crown.

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: 32		  (1) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: (a) damage or destroy any natural resource or property in a park, conservancy or recreation area,

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: (b) possess any natural resource or property of a park, conservancy or recreation area,

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: (c) remove any natural resource or property from a park, conservancy or recreation area,

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: (d) engage in any research or collection activity in a park, conservancy or recreation area,

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: (e) remove water from a park, conservancy or recreation area for purposes other than personal consumption, or

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: (f) deposit waste in a park, conservancy or recreation area or allow or cause waste to flow on or seep into any land or water or to be emitted into the air.

heading: Prohibited activity
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (a) to (c) does not apply to wildlife taken under this regulation.

heading: Litter only in receptacle provided
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A person must not deposit litter in a park, conservancy or recreation area except in a receptacle, pit or area provided for that purpose by the ministry or an operator.

heading: Litter only in receptacle provided
paragraph: (2) If a receptacle, pit or area is not provided for the deposit of litter, a person must not leave litter in a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Transporting litter into a park, conservancy or recreation area
paragraph:
34
		  A person must not bring domestic, commercial or industrial litter into a park, conservancy or recreation area for the purpose of disposal.

heading: Designated representative
paragraph:
35
		  (1) Every party, group or youth group using a park, conservancy or recreation area facility or service for which a fee is payable must designate one person to be the designated representative of that party, group or youth group.

heading: Designated representative
paragraph: (2) Except as authorized by a park officer, the designated representative must be 16 years of age or older.

heading: Designated representative
paragraph: (3) The designated representative must be responsible for

heading: Designated representative
paragraph: (a) the registration of the party, group or youth group,

heading: Designated representative
paragraph: (b) the payment of fees required to be paid by that party, group or youth group under this regulation, and

heading: Designated representative
paragraph: (c) the actions and conduct of each person in the party, group or youth group and each guest and visitor of that party, group or youth group while in the park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Registration required
paragraph:
36
		  The designated representative of a party, group or youth group that camps or uses facilities or services of a park, conservancy or recreation area for which the minister, by regulation or directive, has established a fee, must register with the ministry or an operator, as the case may be, by providing all of the following information:

heading: Registration required
paragraph: (a) the correct name of the designated representative;

heading: Registration required
paragraph: (b) the number of persons in the party, group or youth group;

heading: Registration required
paragraph: (c) the mode of transportation of the party, group or youth group;

heading: Registration required
paragraph: (d) any other information reasonably required to identify the party, group or youth group.

heading: Controlled public access
paragraph:
37
		  (1) A person must not, between the hours of 11 p.m. and 7 a.m. the following day, enter or remain in a campground except

heading: Controlled public access
paragraph: (a) a person who is the member of a registered party, group or youth group, or

heading: Controlled public access
paragraph: (b) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Controlled public access
paragraph: (2) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person must not, between the hours of 11 p.m. and 7 a.m. the following day, enter or remain in a day use area.

heading: Camping restrictions
paragraph:
38
		  (1) A person must not camp in

heading: Camping restrictions
paragraph: (a) frontcountry, or

heading: Camping restrictions
paragraph: (b) backcountry less than 2 000 hectares in size

heading: Camping restrictions
paragraph: except

heading: Camping restrictions
paragraph: (c) in a campsite, or

heading: Camping restrictions
paragraph: (d) as authorized by a park officer.

heading: Camping restrictions
paragraph: (2) If backcountry is 2 000 hectares or more in size, a park officer may restrict camping to a designated area, campground or campsite.

heading: Maximum length of stay
paragraph:
39
		  (1) A person may not camp in a park, conservancy or recreation area for more than 14 days except

heading: Maximum length of stay
paragraph: (a) as authorized by a park officer, or

heading: Maximum length of stay
paragraph: (b) in a designated long-stay campsite.

heading: Maximum length of stay
paragraph: (2) Except as authorized by a park officer, a person who owns a vessel or is responsible for a vessel must not allow that vessel to remain overnight in a park, conservancy or recreation area for more than 14 days in a calendar year.

heading: Limited occupancy or use
paragraph:
40
		  (1) A park officer may

heading: Limited occupancy or use
paragraph: (a) limit at any one time the number of persons, vehicles or vessels in a park, conservancy or recreation area or any part of a park, conservancy or recreation area, or

heading: Limited occupancy or use
paragraph: (b) close to public use a park, conservancy or recreation area or any part of a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Limited occupancy or use
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding section 39, a park officer may limit the length of stay of a person in a park, conservancy or recreation area.

heading: Second vehicles
paragraph:
40.1
		  (1) A party may not have more than one recreational vehicle on a campsite.

heading: Second vehicles
paragraph: (2) A party may have a second non-recreational vehicle on a campsite

heading: Second vehicles
paragraph: (a) if so authorized by a park officer and on payment of the fee established by regulation or directive of the minister, or

heading: Second vehicles
paragraph: (b) if the campsite is a designated long-stay campsite.

heading: Maximum number of persons on a campsite
paragraph:
40.2
		  No more than 8 persons may occupy a campsite, unless a park officer authorizes a different number.

heading: Fee collection period
paragraph:
41
		  (1) If fees established by the minister by regulation or directive are levied on an overnight basis, the overnight period commences at 12 noon and terminates at 12 noon the following day.

heading: Fee collection period
paragraph: (2) If fees established by the minister by regulation or directive are levied on a day basis, the day period commences and terminates at the times approved by a park officer between 7 a.m. and 11 p.m. on the same day.

heading: Payment of fees
paragraph:
42
		  The designated representative of a party, group or youth group that camps or uses a campsite or other authorized facility or area in a park, conservancy or recreation area must,

heading: Payment of fees
paragraph: (a) in respect of a campsite or other authorized facility or area managed by the minister, pay to the ministry the fees established by regulation or directive of the minister, or

heading: Payment of fees
paragraph: (b) in respect of a campsite or other authorized facility or area managed by an operator, pay to the operator the fees established by regulation or directive of the minister.

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph:
53
		  (1) A person applying for a park use permit or resource use permit for a purpose listed in Schedule K, Part 1, Column 1, must pay to the minister the application fee set out opposite that purpose in Column 2.

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (2) A permit holder must, for a request or requirement listed in Schedule K, Part 2, Column 1, pay to the minister the fee set out in Column 2 opposite that request or requirement.

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (3) A person to whom a permit listed in Schedule K, Part 3, Column 1 was issued before January 30, 2018 must pay to the minister the fee set out opposite that permit type in Column 2

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (a) in the case of a permit issued for a term of one year or less, when the permit is issued, and

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (b) in the case of a permit issued for a term of more than one year, when the permit is issued and, annually thereafter, before the anniversary date of the issue of the permit, until the end of the term.

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (4) No fee is payable under this section for a park use permit or resource use permit issued

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (a) to British Columbia or to Canada,

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (b) for the purposes of research,

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (c) for public telephones,

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (d) for the operation of campground and day facilities in a park, conservancy or recreation area,

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (e) for exploration and development work authorized by an approved reclamation permit issued under the Mines Act, being undertaken on a mineral claim in good standing in a recreation area designated under section 23 of the Mineral Tenure Act,

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (f) for a use for which, prior to April 1, 1988, no fee was payable, or

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (g) if the minister directs that payment is not required.

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsections (4) and (6), the fees payable under this section are in addition to and not instead of any other amount payable by an applicant or permit holder under the Act, this regulation, or another enactment.

heading: Park use permit and resource use permit fees
paragraph: (6) No fee listed in Parts 3 and 4 of Schedule K for a park use permit or resource use permit is payable if the permit is issued to a non-profit organization.

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph:
56
		  The following enactments are prescribed for purposes of section 4 (3) (b) of the Act:

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (a) regulations under the Ecological Reserve Act;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (b) sections 12 and 13 of the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (c) section 9 of the Firearm Act;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (d) Liquor Control and Licensing Act;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (d.1) Cannabis Control and Licensing Act;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (e) Motor Vehicle Act and regulations under that Act;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (f) Off-Road Vehicle Act and regulations under that Act;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (g) sections 2, 4, 5 and 6 of the Trespass Act.

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: 1		  (1) For the purposes of this Schedule,

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (a) measurements expressed in hectares must be rounded upwards to the next whole hectare and measurements expressed in square metres or cubic metres are rounded upwards to the next whole square metre or cubic metre, and

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (b) measurements expressed in square metres of any structure must be based on the outside dimensions including verandahs or porches.

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (2) In this Schedule:

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "base facility" means a facility that is the main location or one of the main locations for a commercial or industrial operation;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "defined" means an area specified in the park use permit or resource use permit for which the fee is payable;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "high-value film park" means any of the following parks:

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (a) Alice Lake Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (b) Brandywine Falls Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (c) Coquihalla Canyon Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (d) Cultus Lake Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (e) Cypress Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (f) E. C. Manning Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (g) Elk Falls Park, excluding the Elk Falls Protected Area;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (h) Garibaldi Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (i) Golden Ears Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (j) Goldstream Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (k) Gordon Bay Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (l) Juan de Fuca Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (m) MacMillan Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (n) Mount Seymour Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (o) Murrin Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (p) Peace Arch Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (q) Porteau Cove Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (r) Rathtrevor Beach Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (s) Sasquatch Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (t) Shannon Falls Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (u) Skaha Bluffs Park;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (v) Stawamus Chief Park, including the Stawamus Chief Protected Area;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "minor shoot" means commercial film production with no disturbance of the users or natural resources of a park, conservancy or recreation area;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "non-profit organization" means a club or association that is a society as defined in the Societies Act or a school board incorporated under the School Act, in which the use or activity undertaken is

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (a) of demonstrable benefit to the whole community, and

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: (b) consistent with the approved objectives of the park, conservancy or recreation area;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "satellite facility" means a facility with one permanent structure, excluding pit toilets, that is used for temporary accommodation, storage of supplies or fuel, or as an emergency shelter or an improved helicopter landing site;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "structure" means any building or permanent improvement constructed, placed or established on Park Act lands, excluding pit toilets;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "tent/spike camp" means a site with no permanent improvements or structures used on a non-exclusive basis for temporary tenting accommodation or the storage of supplies;

heading: Park ranger responsibilities
paragraph: "trapping cabin" means a cabin used for shelter and for storage of trapping supplies on a periodic but temporary basis in conjunction with the operation of a trapline.

paragraph: Schedules L and M

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Parks Canada Agency Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 (1) The definitions in this section apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Agency means the Parks Canada Agency established by section 3. (Agence)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Chief Executive Officer means the Chief Executive Officer appointed under section 10. (directeur general)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: employee means an employee appointed under subsection 13(1). (employe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: heritage protection programs includes programs that relate to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) heritage railway stations, heritage lighthouses and federal heritage buildings;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) Canadian heritage rivers and federal archaeology; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any other matters within the jurisdiction of the Minister that relate to areas of Canadian natural or historical significance that the Minister may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, specify for the purposes of this definition. (programmes de protection du patrimoine)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: national historic site means a place designated under subsection (2) or a national historic site of Canada to which the Canada National Parks Act applies. (lieu historique national)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: national marine conservation area means a marine conservation area or reserve as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada National Marine Conservation Areas Act. (aire marine nationale de conservation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: national park means a park or park reserve as defined in section 2 of the Canada National Parks Act. (parc national)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: other protected heritage areas includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) historic canals;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) historic museums that may be established by the Minister under the Historic Sites and Monuments Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b.1) the Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park established by section 5 of the Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b.2) the Rouge National Urban Park; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any other areas within the jurisdiction of the Minister that are of Canadian natural or historical significance and that the Minister may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, specify for the purposes of this definition. (autres lieux patrimoniaux proteges)

heading: Designation
paragraph: (2) The Minister may designate any historic place as defined in section 2 of the Historic Sites and Monuments Act as a national historic site for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Establishment
paragraph: 3 There is hereby established a body corporate to be called the Parks Canada Agency, that may exercise powers and perform duties and functions only as an agent of Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Minister responsible
paragraph: 4 (1) The Minister is responsible for the Agency and the powers, duties and functions of the Minister, in that capacity, extend to and include all matters over which Parliament has jurisdiction, not by law assigned to any other department, board or agency of the Government of Canada, relating to

heading: Minister responsible
paragraph: (a) areas of natural or historical significance to the nation, including national parks, national marine conservation areas, national historic sites, historic canals, historic museums established under the Historic Sites and Monuments Act, Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park and Rouge National Urban Park;

heading: Minister responsible
paragraph: (b) heritage railway stations, heritage lighthouses, federal heritage buildings, historic places in Canada, federal archaeology and Canadian heritage rivers; and

heading: Minister responsible
paragraph: (c) the design and implementation of programs that relate primarily to built heritage.

heading: Ministerial direction
paragraph: (2) The Minister has the overall direction of the Agency, which shall comply with any general or special direction given by the Minister with reference to the carrying out of its responsibilities.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Notwithstanding subsection (2), no direction may be given with respect to the matters referred to in section 13.

heading: Exercise of powers conferred on Minister
paragraph: 5 (1) Subject to any direction given by the Minister, the Agency may exercise the powers and shall perform the duties and functions that relate to national parks, national historic sites, national marine conservation areas, other protected heritage areas and heritage protection programs that are conferred on, or delegated, assigned or transferred to, the Minister under any Act or regulation.

heading: Officers and employees
paragraph: (2) An officer or employee of the Agency may exercise any power and perform any duty or function referred to in subsection (1) if the officer or employee is appointed to serve in the Agency in a capacity appropriate to the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty or function, and in so doing, shall comply with any general or special direction given by the Minister.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not include

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) any power, duty or function of the Minister under this Act, other than those referred to in subsection 4(1);

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) a power to make regulations under this or any other Act; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) a power to make designations or appointments under the Historic Sites and Monuments Act or the Heritage Railway Stations Protection Act.

heading: Non-application of Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: 5.1 A direction by the Minister referred to in sections 4 and 5 is not a statutory instrument for the purposes of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Responsibilities - subject-matter
paragraph: 6 (1) The Agency is responsible for the implementation of policies of the Government of Canada that relate to national parks, national historic sites, national marine conservation areas, other protected heritage areas and heritage protection programs.

heading: System plans
paragraph: (2) The Agency shall ensure that there are long-term plans in place for establishing systems of national parks, national historic sites and national marine conservation areas.

heading: New protected heritage areas
paragraph: (3) The Agency is responsible for negotiating, and recommending to the Minister, the establishment of new national parks, national marine conservation areas and other protected heritage areas and the acquisition of national historic sites.

heading: Responsibilities - Acts
paragraph: (4) The Agency is responsible for the administration and enforcement of the Acts listed in Part 1 of the schedule and any regulations made under those Acts and the regulations listed in Part 2 of the schedule.

heading: Other Acts and regulations
paragraph: 6.1 (1) If considerations of geography make it impractical for the body or minister responsible for administering and enforcing an Act listed in Part 3 of the schedule - or any regulation made under that Act - or any regulation listed in Part 4 of the schedule to do so in a part of Canada, the Agency may enter into an agreement with that body or minister under which the Agency may assist that body or minister in the administration and enforcement of the Act or regulation in that part of Canada.

heading: Park wardens
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of an agreement entered into under subsection (1), persons designated as park wardens under section 18 of the Canada National Parks Act may, with the Chief Executive Officer's approval,

heading: Park wardens
paragraph: (a) be designated under the Acts listed in Part 3 of the schedule to exercise powers set out in the designation in relation to the administration and enforcement of those Acts and any regulations made under them; and

heading: Park wardens
paragraph: (b) be designated under the Acts under which the regulations listed in Part 4 of the schedule are made to exercise powers set out in the designation in relation to the administration and enforcement of those regulations.

heading: Park wardens
paragraph: Meaning of part of Canada

heading: Park wardens
paragraph: (3) In this section, part of Canada means a part of Canada that is outside national parks, national historic sites, national marine conservation areas and other protected heritage areas.

heading: Additions to or deletions from the schedule
paragraph: 7 (1) The Governor in Council may, by order, add to or delete from the schedule any Act of Parliament or regulation or part of an Act or regulation that relates to national parks, national historic sites, national marine conservation areas or other protected heritage areas or heritage protection programs.

heading: Additions to or deletions from schedule
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 6.1, the Governor in Council may, by order, add to or delete from the schedule any Act of Parliament or regulation made under an Act of Parliament, or part of such an Act or regulation, that relates to the environment.

heading: Ancillary powers
paragraph: 8 The Agency may, in carrying out its responsibilities,

heading: Ancillary powers
paragraph: (a) enter into contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding or other arrangements with a department or agency of the Government of Canada, with any other government or any of its agencies or with any person or organization in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada or in its own name;

heading: Ancillary powers
paragraph: (b) acquire any property, including securities, by way of gift, bequest or other form of donation and, subject to the terms and conditions on which the property was acquired, hold, administer, expend, sell, exchange or otherwise dispose of the property;

heading: Ancillary powers
paragraph: (c) sell, exchange, loan or otherwise dispose of any personal property or moveables acquired, held or administered by the Agency;

heading: Ancillary powers
paragraph: (d) license, assign or otherwise make available any patent, copyright, industrial design, trademark, trade secret or other like property right held, controlled or administered by the Agency;

heading: Ancillary powers
paragraph: (e) publish, sell or otherwise disseminate studies, reports and other documents of the Agency; and

heading: Ancillary powers
paragraph: (f) do anything that is necessary or incidental to the furtherance of the purposes of the Agency.

heading: Convening round table
paragraph: 8.1 (1) The Minister shall, at least once every two years, convene a round table of persons interested in matters for which the Agency is responsible to advise the Minister on the performance by the Agency of its responsibilities under section 6.

heading: Response of Minister
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall respond within 180 days to any written recommendations submitted during a round table convened under subsection (1).

heading: Choice of goods and services providers
paragraph: 9 Notwithstanding section 9 of the Department of Public Works and Government Services Act, the Agency, with the approval given generally or in a specific case by the Governor in Council, on the recommendation of the Treasury Board, may procure goods and services, including legal services, from outside the federal public administration.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: 10 (1) The Governor in Council shall appoint an officer, to be called the Chief Executive Officer, to hold office during pleasure for a term of not more than five years, which term may be renewed for one or more further terms.

heading: Remuneration
paragraph: (2) The Chief Executive Officer shall be paid the remuneration that may be fixed by the Governor in Council.

heading: Absence or incapacity
paragraph: 11 In the event of the absence or incapacity of the Chief Executive Officer or a vacancy in that office, the Minister may appoint any person to exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the Chief Executive Officer, but no person may be so appointed for a term of more than ninety days without the approval of the Governor in Council.

heading: Role of Chief Executive Officer
paragraph: 12 (1) The Chief Executive Officer, under the direction of the Minister, has the control and management of the Agency and all matters connected with it.

heading: Rank of deputy head
paragraph: (2) The Chief Executive Officer has the rank and all the powers of a deputy head of a department.

heading: Guiding principles and operational policies
paragraph: (3) The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for preparing, for the Minister's approval, guiding principles and operational policies for matters within the Agency's responsibilities.

heading: Delegation
paragraph: (4) The Chief Executive Officer may delegate to any person any power, duty or function conferred on the Chief Executive Officer under this Act or any other Act or regulation.

heading: Personnel
paragraph: 13 (1) The Chief Executive Officer has exclusive authority to

heading: Personnel
paragraph: (a) appoint, lay-off or terminate the employment of the employees of the Agency; and

heading: Personnel
paragraph: (b) establish standards, procedures and processes governing staffing, including the appointment, lay-off or termination of employment otherwise than for cause, of employees.

heading: Right of employer
paragraph: (2) Nothing in the Federal Public Sector Labour Relations Act shall be construed to affect the right or authority of the Chief Executive Officer to deal with the matters referred to in paragraph (1)(b).

heading: Human resources management
paragraph: (3) Subsections 11.1(1) and 12(2) of the Financial Administration Act do not apply with respect to the Agency and the Chief Executive Officer may

heading: Human resources management
paragraph: (a) determine the organization of and classify the positions in the Agency;

heading: Human resources management
paragraph: (b) set the terms and conditions of employment, including termination of employment for cause, for employees and assign duties to them; and

heading: Human resources management
paragraph: (c) provide for any other matters that the Chief Executive Officer considers necessary for effective human resources management in the Agency.

heading: Political activities
paragraph: 14 (1) For the purposes of Part 7 of the Public Service Employment Act, the Chief Executive Officer is deemed to be a deputy head, and an employee is deemed to be an employee, within the meaning of subsection 2(1) of that Act.

heading: Services of the Public Service Commission
paragraph: (2) The Public Service Commission may, at the request of the Agency, provide any service to the Agency that it is authorized to provide to a department under the Public Service Employment Act or any other related service, and may recover from the Agency the costs incurred in providing the service, and the Commission is, for greater certainty, authorized to enter into arrangements with the Agency for those purposes.

heading: Negotiation of collective agreements
paragraph: 15 Notwithstanding section 112 of the Federal Public Sector Labour Relations Act, the Chief Executive Officer may, in accordance with the negotiating mandate approved by the President of the Treasury Board, enter into a collective agreement with the bargaining agent for a bargaining unit composed of employees that is applicable to employees in that bargaining unit.

heading: Charter for the Agency
paragraph: 16 (1) The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for establishing a charter for the Agency that sets out the values and principles governing

heading: Charter for the Agency
paragraph: (a) the provision of services by the Agency to the public; and

heading: Charter for the Agency
paragraph: (b) the management of the human resources of the Agency.

heading: Available to the public
paragraph: (2) The charter established under subsection (1) shall be made available to the public.

heading: Principal office
paragraph: 17 The principal office of the Agency shall be in the National Capital Region described in the schedule to the National Capital Act.

heading: Legal proceedings
paragraph: 18 (1) Actions, suits or other legal proceedings in respect of any right or obligation acquired or incurred by the Agency, whether in its own name or in the name of Her Majesty in right of Canada, may be brought or taken by or against the Agency in the name of the Agency in any court that would have jurisdiction if the Agency were not an agent of Her Majesty.

heading: Property
paragraph: (2) Property acquired by the Agency is the property of Her Majesty in right of Canada and title to it may be held in the name of Her Majesty or in the name of the Agency.

heading: Appropriations
paragraph: 19 (1) Money may be appropriated by Parliament from time to time by way of a vote in an appropriation Act or any other Act of Parliament for the purposes of making operating and capital expenditures of the Agency and providing financial assistance in the form of grants and contributions.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 20 (1) For the purposes of paragraphs (2)(b) and 21(2)(a), terms and expressions used in those paragraphs have the same meaning as in the Federal Real Property and Federal Immovables Act.

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (2) Notwithstanding subsection 29.1(1) of the Financial Administration Act, the Agency may, for the purposes referred to in subsection 19(1), spend amounts equal to revenues resulting from the conduct of its operations in that or subsequent fiscal years, including

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (a) proceeds from the sale, exchange, loan or other disposition or the licensing of any personal property or moveables acquired, held or administered by the Agency;

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (b) proceeds from any of the following transactions in respect of federal real property and federal immovables under the administration of the Minister for the purposes of the Agency:

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (i) the lease or giving of a licence,

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (ii) the transfer to Her Majesty in any right other than Canada of administration and control, otherwise than in perpetuity, and

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (iii) a disposition of any right or interest, other than a disposition referred to in paragraph 21(2)(a);

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (c) proceeds from, including fees paid under any Act of Parliament in respect of, the provision by the Agency of a service, of the use of a facility or of a product, right or privilege;

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (d) proceeds from any money recovered under section 29; and

heading: Operational revenues
paragraph: (e) any refund of expenditures made in previous fiscal years.

heading: Establishment of New Parks and Historic Sites Account
paragraph: 21 (1) There is hereby established an account in the accounts of Canada to be called the New Parks and Historic Sites Account.

heading: Amounts credited to Account
paragraph: (2) There shall be credited to the New Parks and Historic Sites Account money appropriated by Parliament from time to time by way of an appropriation Act or any other Act of Parliament for the purposes specified in subsection (3), and any revenues of the Agency resulting, including proceeds, from

heading: Amounts credited to Account
paragraph: (a) any of the following transactions in respect of federal real property and federal immovables under the administration of the Minister for the purposes of the Agency:

heading: Amounts credited to Account
paragraph: (i) the sale or any other disposition in perpetuity of any right or interest,

heading: Amounts credited to Account
paragraph: (ii) the transfer of administration to another minister or to an agent corporation, and

heading: Amounts credited to Account
paragraph: (iii) the transfer of administration and control in perpetuity to Her Majesty other than in right of Canada; and

heading: Amounts credited to Account
paragraph: (b) a gift, bequest or other form of donation made for the purposes of the Agency or for any purpose specified in subsection (3).

heading: Payments out of New Parks and Historic Sites Account
paragraph: (3) Despite any other Act of Parliament, amounts may be paid out of the New Parks and Historic Sites Account for the following purposes:

heading: Payments out of New Parks and Historic Sites Account
paragraph: (a) to acquire any historic place, or lands for historic museums, or any interest therein, for the purpose of paragraph 3(d) of the Historic Sites and Monuments Act;

heading: Payments out of New Parks and Historic Sites Account
paragraph: (b) to acquire any real property or immovables for the purpose of establishing, enlarging or designating, as the case may be, any national park, national historic site, national marine conservation area or other protected heritage area;

heading: Payments out of New Parks and Historic Sites Account
paragraph: (c) to develop or maintain any national park, national historic site, national marine conservation area or other protected heritage area that is being established, enlarged or designated, and to make any related contribution or other payment;

heading: Payments out of New Parks and Historic Sites Account
paragraph: (d) to implement a decision by the Minister to recommend the establishment of a national park, national historic site, national marine conservation area or other protected heritage area, or to commemorate a historic place under section 3 of the Historic Sites and Monuments Act, and to make any related contribution or other payment; and

heading: Payments out of New Parks and Historic Sites Account
paragraph: (e) to repay advances made under subsection 22(2).

heading: Statutory appropriation
paragraph: 22 (1) There is hereby appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund the amount of ten million dollars for the purpose of providing advances, from time to time, to the New Parks and Historic Sites Account.

heading: Advances to the Account
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Finance may, on the request of the Minister, authorize the making of advances to the New Parks and Historic Sites Account from the money appropriated under subsection (1) in accordance with any terms and conditions that have been approved by the Treasury Board.

heading: Credits to the Account
paragraph: (3) An advance made as authorized under subsection (2) must be credited to the New Parks and Historic Sites Account.

heading: Repayment of advances
paragraph: (4) The repayment of the principal amount of any advance made as authorized under subsection (2) shall, in accordance with any direction made by the Treasury Board, be charged to the New Parks and Historic Sites Account and credited to the balance outstanding of money appropriated under subsection (1), and the payment of any amount on account of interest payable on the advance may be made from money appropriated under an Act of Parliament as authorized under subsection 19(1).

heading: Amount may be changed
paragraph: (5) The amount of advances authorized under subsection (1) may be amended, from time to time, by an item in an appropriation Act.

heading: Fees for services and use of facilities
paragraph: 23 (1) The Minister may, subject to any regulations that the Treasury Board may make for the purposes of this section, fix the fees or the manner of calculating the fees to be paid for a service or the use of a facility provided by the Agency.

heading: Amount not to exceed cost
paragraph: (2) Fees for a service or the use of a facility that are fixed under subsection (1) may not exceed the cost to Her Majesty in right of Canada of providing the service or the use of the facility.

heading: Fees for products, rights and privileges
paragraph: 24 The Minister may, subject to any regulations that the Treasury Board may make for the purposes of this section, fix the fees or the manner of calculating fees in respect of products, rights or privileges provided by the Agency.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: 25 (1) Before fixing a fee under section 23 or 24, the Minister must consult with any persons and organizations that the Minister considers to be interested in the matter.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (2) The Minister must publish any fee fixed under section 23 or 24 in the Canada Gazette within thirty days after fixing it.

heading: Reference to Scrutiny Committee
paragraph: (3) A fee fixed under section 23 or 24 stands permanently referred to the Committee referred to in section 19 of the Statutory Instruments Act to be reviewed and scrutinized as if it were a statutory instrument.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 26 The Treasury Board may make regulations for the purposes of sections 23 and 24.

heading: Collection of fees
paragraph: 27 The Agency may enter into an agreement with any person respecting the collection of fees fixed under this Act or any other Act under which the Agency provides services, facilities, products, rights or privileges and, notwithstanding subsections 17(1) and (4) of the Financial Administration Act, authorizing that person to withhold amounts from those fees.

heading: Remission of fees
paragraph: 28 The Minister may remit or refund all or part of a fee fixed under section 23 or 24 or under any other Act under which the Agency provides services, facilities, products, rights or privileges, and the interest on it.

heading: Recovery of fees and costs
paragraph: 29 The Agency may recover, as a debt due to Her Majesty, any fee or charge fixed under this or any other Act, any costs incurred by the Agency, and any interest on those fees, charges or costs, that relate to providing a service, facility, product, right or privilege by the Agency under this or any other Act.

heading: Delegation
paragraph: 30 The Minister may delegate to the Agency any power, duty or function conferred on the Minister under sections 23 to 25 and 28.

heading: Report - heritage areas and programs
paragraph: 31 At least every five years, the Chief Executive Officer shall provide the Minister with a report, to be tabled in each House of Parliament, on the state of national parks, national historic sites, national marine conservation areas and other protected heritage areas and heritage protection programs, and on the Agency's performance in carrying out its responsibilities under section 6.

heading: Management plans
paragraph: 32. (1) In addition to the duties in relation to management plans under the Canada National Parks Act and the Canada National Marine Conservation Areas Act, the Chief Executive Officer shall, within five years after the establishment of a national historic site or other protected heritage area, other than the Rouge National Urban Park, or within five years after the coming into force of this section, whichever is later, provide the Minister with a management plan for that national historic site or other protected heritage area in respect of any matter that the Minister deems appropriate, including, but not limited to, commemorative and ecological integrity, resource protection or visitor use, and that plan shall be tabled in each House of Parliament.

heading: Review of management plans by Minister
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall review the management plan for each national historic site or other protected heritage area at least every 10 years and shall cause any amendments to the plan to be tabled in each House of Parliament.

heading: Report on human resources regime
paragraph: 35 (1) The Chief Executive Officer must, at least every five years, have prepared by a person or body, other than the Agency or any of its officers or employees, a report on the consistency of its human resources regime with the values and principles that are to govern the management of its human resources.

heading: Available to the public
paragraph: (2) The report prepared under subsection (1) shall be made available to the public.

heading: Official Languages Act applies
paragraph: 36.1 For greater certainty, the Official Languages Act applies to the Agency and the Agency has the duty, under section 25 of that Act, to ensure that, where services are provided or made available by another person or organization on its behalf, any member of the public in Canada or elsewhere can communicate with and obtain those services from that person or organization in either official language, in any case where those services, if provided by the Agency, would be required under Part IV of the Official Languages Act to be provided in either official language.

heading: Appropriation Act
paragraph: 37 The provisions made by any appropriation Act for the fiscal year in which this section comes into force or a subsequent fiscal year, based on the Estimates for that year, to defray the charges and expenses of the public service of Canada within the Parks Canada Sector of the Department of Canadian Heritage in relation to any matter for which the Agency is responsible by virtue of this Act are deemed to be an amount appropriated for defraying the charges and expenses of the Agency in the amount that the Treasury Board may, on the recommendation of the Minister, determine.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 38 The definitions in this section apply in sections 39 to 45.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: designated position has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Public Service Staff Relations Act. (poste designe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: employee means a person whose employment in the Department of Canadian Heritage is terminated under paragraph 11(2)(g.1) of the Financial Administration Act and who is appointed to the Agency following an offer of employment made by the Agency as a result of a transfer of any work, undertaking or business from the Department of Canadian Heritage to the Agency. (employe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: grievance has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Public Service Staff Relations Act. (grief)

heading: Pending competitions and appointments
paragraph: 39 A competition being conducted or an appointment being or about to be made under the Public Service Employment Act in respect of a position within the Department of Canadian Heritage the duties and functions of which are assigned to a position within the Agency, may continue to be conducted or made as if the Agency were a department for the purposes of that Act.

heading: Pending appeals
paragraph: 40 (1) An appeal made under section 21 of the Public Service Employment Act by any person against an appointment to a position within the Department of Canadian Heritage the duties and functions of which are assigned to a position within the Agency, and not finally disposed of on the assignment, must be dealt with and disposed of in accordance with that Act as if the Agency were a department for the purposes of that Act and the person continued to be an employee for the purposes of that Act.

heading: Other recourse
paragraph: (2) Any recourse commenced by an employee under the Public Service Employment Act that has not been finally dealt with on the appointment of the employee to the Agency must be dealt with and disposed of in accordance with that Act as if the Agency were a department for the purposes of that Act and the person continued to be an employee for the purposes of that Act.

heading: Employees on probation
paragraph: 41 (1) Every employee who was considered to be on probation under section 28 of the Public Service Employment Act immediately before being appointed to the Agency continues on probation with the Agency until the end of any period established by the Public Service Commission by regulation for that employee or a class of persons of which that employee is a member.

heading: Rejection
paragraph: (2) Subsection 28(2) of the Public Service Employment Act applies to an employee of the Agency who is on probation but the reference to deputy head in that subsection is to be read as a reference to the Chief Executive Officer.

heading: Designated positions
paragraph: 42 If an employee, immediately before being appointed to the Agency, occupied a position that was a designated position in the Department of Canadian Heritage, that employee is, on appointment to the Agency, deemed to occupy a designated position in the Agency.

heading: Pending grievances
paragraph: 43 (1) Any grievance commenced by an employee under the Public Service Staff Relations Act that has not been finally dealt with on the appointment of the employee to the Agency, must be dealt with and disposed of in accordance with that Act as if the employee's employment in the Department of Canadian Heritage had not been terminated.

heading: Implementation of decision
paragraph: (2) A final decision with respect to a grievance referred to in subsection (1) that provides for the reinstatement of or payment of money to a person must be implemented by the Agency as soon as practicable.

heading: Successor rights
paragraph: 44 For the purpose of section 48.1 of the Public Service Staff Relations Act, the Governor in Council may fix the date on which the Parks Canada Sector and any other portion of the Department of Canadian Heritage are deemed to be severed from the Department and to become a part of the Agency, and that date is to be used for the purposes of subsections 48.1(3), (6) and (7) of that Act.

heading: Conditional Amendment
paragraph: 61.1 [Amendment]

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: authorized facility means a facility, including a transfer site, that is authorized by the authorities of the jurisdiction in which it is located to process PCBs or products containing PCBs or to conduct laboratory analysis or research with PCBs or products containing PCBs. (installation agreee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: National Fire Code means the National Fire Code of Canada 2005, NRCC No. 47667, issued by the Canadian Commission on Building and Fire Codes, National Research Council of Canada, as amended from time to time. (Code national de prevention des incendies)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: PCB means any chlorobiphenyl described in item 1 of the List of Toxic Substances in Schedule 1 to the Act. (BPC)

heading: Concentration - several matrices
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of these Regulations, if a solid or a liquid containing PCBs is composed of several matrices, the concentration of PCBs is based on the mass of the matrix in which the PCBs are located.

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (3) Any analysis performed to determine the concentration of PCBs for the purposes of these Regulations must be performed by a laboratory that meets the following conditions at the time of the analysis:

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (a) it is accredited

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (i) under the International Organization for Standardization standard ISO/IEC 17025, entitled General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories, by an accrediting body that is a signatory to the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation Mutual Recognition Arrangement, or

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (ii) under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR, c. Q-2; and

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (b) the scope of its accreditation includes the analysis performed to determine the concentration of PCBs in the matrix in which the PCBs are located.

heading: Sampling method
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of these Regulations, other than section 13, the concentration of PCBs in a matrix is determined using a provincially, nationally or internationally recognized sampling method for PCBs in the matrix in which the PCBs are located.

heading: Sampling method - bulk solid products
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of section 13, the concentration of PCBs is determined using a sampling method for bulk solid products, which is set out in either federal or provincial legislation, as amended from time to time, or approved by the United States Environmental Protection Agency for compliance with the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act or with the regulations made under that Act, as amended from time to time.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2 (1) These Regulations apply to PCBs and to any products containing PCBs.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) These Regulations do not apply to the following:

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) the import and export of PCBs that are or are considered to be hazardous waste or hazardous recyclable material within the meaning of sections 2 to 5 of the Cross-border Movement of Hazardous Waste and Hazardous Recyclable Material Regulations;

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) the sale, importation or advertising of liquids containing PCBs for use in microscopy, including immersion oils but not including refractive index oils, which is prohibited under section 5 of the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act; and

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (c) the offer for sale, sale and use of land contaminated with PCBs or with products containing PCBs.

heading: Sale of property
paragraph: 3 Nothing in these Regulations shall be construed as preventing the sale of

heading: Sale of property
paragraph: (a) personal property or movables that contain PCBs, or real property or immovables that have PCBs or products containing PCBs, and that form part of the sale of the whole or part of a business, including a manufacturing or a processing business;

heading: Sale of property
paragraph: (b) real property or immovables that have products containing PCBs if the products continue to be used after the sale for the same purpose at the same place and are an integral part of the property or immovable; or

heading: Sale of property
paragraph: (c) real property or immovables on which a PCB storage site is located.

heading: Compliance
paragraph: 4 In addition to the persons who must comply with the requirements set out in these Regulations, a person who owns PCBs or products containing PCBs shall ensure that the requirements of these Regulations with respect to those PCBs or products are met.

heading: Release into the environment
paragraph: 5 (1) No person shall release PCBs into the environment, other than from the equipment referred to in subsection (2), in a concentration of

heading: Release into the environment
paragraph: (a) 2 mg/kg or more for a liquid containing PCBs; or

heading: Release into the environment
paragraph: (b) 50 mg/kg or more for a solid containing PCBs.

heading: Release from equipment
paragraph: (2) No person shall release more than one gram of PCBs into the environment from equipment referred to in section 16 that is in use or from equipment in use for which an extension has been granted under section 17.

heading: Prohibited activities
paragraph: 6 Except as provided in these Regulations, no person shall

heading: Prohibited activities
paragraph: (a) manufacture, export or import PCBs or a product containing PCBs in a concentration of 2 mg/kg or more;

heading: Prohibited activities
paragraph: (b) offer for sale or sell PCBs or a product containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more; or

heading: Prohibited activities
paragraph: (c) process or use PCBs or a product containing PCBs.

heading: Laboratory analysis
paragraph: 7 A person may manufacture, export, import, offer for sale, sell, process and use PCBs or products containing PCBs for the purpose of laboratory analysis if the analysis is conducted

heading: Laboratory analysis
paragraph: (a) in an authorized facility that is authorized for that purpose; or

heading: Laboratory analysis
paragraph: (b) in a facility that conforms to internationally recognized guidelines on best laboratory practices, if the authorities of the jurisdiction in which the facility is located do not have a mechanism in place to authorize the facility to conduct the analysis.

heading: Research
paragraph: 8 (1) A person may offer for sale or sell PCBs or products containing PCBs to be processed or used for the purpose of research to determine the effects of those PCBs or products on human health or on the environment, if the facility in which they are processed or used is

heading: Research
paragraph: (a) an authorized facility that is authorized for that purpose; or

heading: Research
paragraph: (b) a facility that conforms to internationally recognized guidelines on best laboratory practices, if the authorities of the jurisdiction in which the facility is located do not have a mechanism in place to authorize the facility to conduct the research.

heading: Processing and use
paragraph: (2) A person may process and use the PCBs or products containing PCBs for the purpose of the research referred to in subsection (1) at a facility that meets the requirement set out in paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

heading: Electrical capacitor
paragraph: 9 A person may offer for sale, sell and use an electrical capacitor containing PCBs if the electrical capacitor

heading: Electrical capacitor
paragraph: (a) is an integral part of a consumer product;

heading: Electrical capacitor
paragraph: (b) is fusion sealed; and

heading: Electrical capacitor
paragraph: (c) would be rendered inoperable and irreparable if the PCBs were removed from it.

heading: Aircraft, ships, trains and other vehicles
paragraph: 10 A person may export, import, offer for sale, sell and use for transportation purposes aircraft, ships, trains and other vehicles that contain PCBs only in their communication, navigation or electronic control equipment or cables.

heading: Colouring pigment
paragraph: 11 (1) A person may manufacture, export, import, offer for sale, sell, process and use a colouring pigment containing PCBs produced incidentally if the concentration of the PCBs is less than 50 mg/kg.

heading: Annual average concentration
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the annual average concentration of PCBs produced incidentally in colouring pigment that a person may manufacture, export, import, offer for sale, sell, process and use shall not exceed 25 mg/kg.

heading: Destruction
paragraph: 12 A person may process PCBs or products containing PCBs for the purpose of destroying PCBs or recovering PCBs for the purpose of destroying them in an authorized facility that is authorized for that purpose.

heading: Solid products
paragraph: 13 (1) A person may manufacture solid products containing PCBs in a concentration of less than 50 mg/kg using bulk solid products containing PCBs in a concentration of less than 50 mg/kg, and may use those solid products.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) only applies to the manufacture of the types of products that are manufactured before September 5, 2008.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) No person shall offer for sale or sell the products manufactured in accordance with subsection (1) unless the products are used in the course of a commercial or industrial activity.

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: 14 (1) A person may use the following products containing PCBs:

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: (a) cables, if they remain in place on September 5, 2008;

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: (b) pipelines that transport natural gas, petroleum or petroleum products and any associated equipment that is in contact with the natural gas, petroleum or petroleum products if the pipelines and the equipment remain in place on September 5, 2008;

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: (c) fusion sealed capacitors if they are used in relation to communication equipment or electronic control equipment; and

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: (d) the following equipment containing PCBs in a concentration of less than 50 mg/kg if the equipment is used for the purpose for which it was manufactured:

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: (i) electrical capacitors, light ballasts, electrical transformers and their auxiliary electrical equipment, including pole-top electrical transformers and their pole-top auxiliary electrical equipment,

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: (ii) electromagnets that are not used in the handling of food, feed or any additive to food or feed, and

heading: Cables, pipelines, electrical capacitors and other equipment
paragraph: (iii) heat transfer equipment, hydraulic equipment, vapour diffusion pumps and bridge bearings.

heading: Electrical capacitors
paragraph: (2) A person may import fusion sealed capacitors containing PCBs for use in relation to communication tactical equipment or electronic control tactical equipment.

heading: Liquids for servicing - concentration less than 2 mg/kg
paragraph: 15 (1) A person may use liquids containing PCBs in a concentration of less than 2 mg/kg for the purpose of servicing equipment containing PCBs.

heading: Liquids for servicing - concentration of 500 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (2) A person may use liquids containing PCBs in a concentration of 500 mg/kg or more for the purpose of servicing equipment containing PCBs in a concentration of 500 mg/kg or more until December 31, 2009.

heading: Equipment - subparagraphs 14(1)(d)(i) to (iii)
paragraph: 16 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (2.1), a person may use the equipment referred to in subparagraphs 14(1)(d)(i) to (iii) until the following dates if the equipment is in use on September 5, 2008:

heading: Equipment - subparagraphs 14(1)(d)(i) to (iii)
paragraph: (a) in the case of equipment containing PCBs in a concentration of 500 mg/kg or more, December 31, 2009; and

heading: Equipment - subparagraphs 14(1)(d)(i) to (iii)
paragraph: (b) in the case of equipment containing PCBs in a concentration of at least 50 mg/kg but less than 500 mg/kg,

heading: Equipment - subparagraphs 14(1)(d)(i) to (iii)
paragraph: (i) December 31, 2009, if the equipment is located at a drinking water treatment plant or food or feed processing plant, in a child care facility, preschool, primary school, secondary school, hospital or senior citizens' care facility or on the property on which the plant or facility is located and within 100 m of it, and

heading: Equipment - subparagraphs 14(1)(d)(i) to (iii)
paragraph: (ii) December 31, 2025, if the equipment is located at any other place.

heading: Light ballasts and pole-top electrical transformers
paragraph: (2) A person may use the following equipment containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more until December 31, 2025, if the equipment is in use on September 5, 2008:

heading: Light ballasts and pole-top electrical transformers
paragraph: (a) light ballasts; and

heading: Light ballasts and pole-top electrical transformers
paragraph: (b) pole-top electrical transformers and their pole-top auxiliary electrical equipment.

heading: Current transformers and other equipment
