paragraph: (2.1) A person may, from January 1, 2015 until December 31, 2025, use any current transformers, potential transformers, circuit breakers, reclosers and bushings that are located at an electrical generation, transmission or distribution facility and contain PCBs in a concentration of 500 mg/kg or more if that equipment is in use on September 5, 2008.

heading: Liquid - authorized concentration
paragraph: (3) A person may use a liquid containing PCBs in a concentration of 2 mg/kg or more but less than 50 mg/kg in equipment until the day on which the liquid is removed from the equipment.

heading: Extension of end-of-use date
paragraph: 17 (1) Despite subsection 15(2), paragraph 16(1)(a) and subparagraph 16(1)(b)(i), a person may use the equipment and the liquids used for servicing that equipment, referred to in those provisions, until the date set out in an extension granted by the Minister under subsection (2) for that equipment and those liquids.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall, on receiving a written application containing the information set out in subsection (3), grant an extension up to the date applied for but no later than December 31, 2014, if either of the following conditions are met:

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) the equipment is being replaced with equipment that is engineered to order, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) it is not technically feasible to replace the equipment on or before December 31, 2009,

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) the applicant is taking all necessary measures to minimize or eliminate any harmful effect of the PCBs in the equipment on the environment and on human health,

heading: Application
paragraph: (iii) a plan has been prepared, along with timelines, to end the use of the equipment by the date applied for,

heading: Application
paragraph: (iv) a plan has been prepared for inspecting the equipment on a monthly basis for the period of the extension for damage that could lead to the release of PCBs, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (v) the equipment bears the label required under section 29; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) the equipment is located at a facility that is scheduled for permanent closure on or before December 31, 2014, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) the applicant is taking all necessary measures to minimize or eliminate any harmful effect of the PCBs in the equipment on the environment and on human health,

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) a plan has been prepared, along with timelines, to end the use of the equipment by the date applied for,

heading: Application
paragraph: (iii) a plan has been prepared for inspecting the equipment on a monthly basis, for the period of the extension, for damage that could lead to the release of PCBs, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (iv) the equipment bears the label required under section 29.

heading: Information
paragraph: (3) The application shall contain the following:

heading: Information
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses, telephone number, fax number, if any, and e-mail address, if any, of the applicant and of any person authorized to act on the applicant's behalf;

heading: Information
paragraph: (b) a technical description of the equipment which is the subject of the application, including

heading: Information
paragraph: (i) the type and function of the equipment,

heading: Information
paragraph: (ii) the quantity of liquid containing PCBs that is in the equipment and the quantity of liquid needed for servicing that equipment, expressed in litres,

heading: Information
paragraph: (iii) the concentration of PCBs in the liquid, expressed in milligrams of PCBs per kilogram of liquid,

heading: Information
paragraph: (iv) the quantity of PCBs in the liquid that is in the equipment, expressed in kilograms, and

heading: Information
paragraph: (v) the name-plate description, if any, and the manufacturer's serial number, if any;

heading: Information
paragraph: (c) the unique identification number that is on the label required under section 29;

heading: Information
paragraph: (d) the name, if any, and civic address of the facility where the equipment is located, or, if there is no civic address, the location using the owner's site identification system, and the function and technical description of the facility;

heading: Information
paragraph: (e) information demonstrating that

heading: Information
paragraph: (i) it is not technically feasible to replace the equipment on or before December 31, 2009, or

heading: Information
paragraph: (ii) the facility where the equipment is located is scheduled for permanent closure on or before December 31, 2014;

heading: Information
paragraph: (f) information demonstrating that the applicant is taking all necessary measures to minimize or eliminate any harmful effect of the PCBs that are contained in the equipment on the environment and on human health;

heading: Information
paragraph: (g) the plan, along with timelines, for ending the use of the equipment; and

heading: Information
paragraph: (h) the plan for inspecting the equipment.

heading: Notice of change to information
paragraph: (4) The applicant shall notify the Minister in writing of any change to the information provided under subsection (3) within 30 days after the day on which the change occurs.

heading: False or misleading information
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall refuse to grant an extension if the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the applicant has provided false or misleading information in support of its application.

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (6) The Minister shall revoke the extension if

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (a) the requirements set out in subsection (2) are no longer met during the period of the extension; or

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (b) the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the applicant has provided false or misleading information to the Minister in support of its application.

heading: Reasons for revocation
paragraph: (7) The Minister shall not revoke the extension unless the Minister provides the applicant with

heading: Reasons for revocation
paragraph: (a) written reasons for the revocation; and

heading: Reasons for revocation
paragraph: (b) an opportunity to be heard, by written representation, in respect of the revocation.

heading: Application - concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: 18 (1) Subject to subsection (3), this Part applies to all solids and liquids containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more that are located at a particular site if the liquids or solids are present in a quantity greater than or equal to

heading: Application - concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (a) 100 L, in the case of liquids; and

heading: Application - concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (b) 100 kg, in the case of solids.

heading: Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), this Part also applies to all solids and liquids containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more that are located at a particular site in a quantity of less than 100 L, in the case of liquids, and 100 kg, in the case of solids, if the total quantity of PCBs contained in the liquids or the solids or in the liquids and solids combined, determined in accordance with the following formulas, as applicable, is 1 kg or more:

heading: Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
paragraph: (a) in the case of liquids,

heading: Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
paragraph: where

heading: Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
paragraph: (i) 0.9 kg/L, if the concentration of PCBs in the liquid is less than 10 000 mg/kg, and

heading: Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
paragraph: (ii) 1.5 kg/L, if the concentration of PCBs in the liquid is 10 000 mg/kg or more, and

heading: Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
paragraph: (b) in the case of solids,

heading: Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
Application - quantity of 1 kg or more
paragraph: where

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) This Part does not apply in respect of the following products containing PCBs:

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) solid or liquid products that are processed daily or used;

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) pipelines that transport natural gas, petroleum or petroleum products, and any associated equipment that is in contact with the natural gas, petroleum or petroleum products, if they remain in place on September 5, 2008; and

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (c) cables, if they remain in place on September 5, 2008.

heading: Requirement to store
paragraph: 19 (1) A person who owns, controls or possesses PCBs or products containing PCBs shall, within 30 days after the day on which those PCBs or products cease to be processed daily or used or after September 5, 2008, whichever is later, either

heading: Requirement to store
paragraph: (a) send them for destruction to an authorized facility that is authorized for that purpose; or

heading: Requirement to store
paragraph: (b) store them at a PCB storage site for the period during which they are not processed daily or used.

heading: Remote from or no access to roadway
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if the PCBs or products containing PCBs are remote from a roadway system or if there is no access to a roadway system, the person who owns, controls or possesses the PCBs or products may store them at a PCB storage site as soon as feasible but no later than one year after the day on which they are not processed daily or used or one year after September 5, 2008, whichever is later. That person shall use best management practices for them from the time that they cease to be processed daily or used until the time that they are stored at a PCB storage site.

heading: Prohibition against storage
paragraph: 20 (1) Effective September 5, 2009, no person shall store PCBs or products containing PCBs at the following plants or facilities or on the land on which those plants or facilities are located and within 100 m of them:

heading: Prohibition against storage
paragraph: (a) a drinking water treatment plant or a food or feed processing plant; or

heading: Prohibition against storage
paragraph: (b) a child care facility, preschool, primary school, secondary school, hospital, or senior citizens' care facility.

heading: Light ballasts
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to light ballasts.

heading: Maximum storage periods
paragraph: 21 (1) Despite any other provision in these Regulations and subject to section 22, no person shall store PCBs or products containing PCBs, other than those referred to in section 23, beyond the following time limits:

heading: Maximum storage periods
paragraph: (a) one year, beginning on the day on which their use is no longer permitted under these Regulations or the day on which they are no longer processed daily or used, whichever is sooner, if the PCBs or products are stored at a facility that is not referred to in paragraph (1)(b) or (c);

heading: Maximum storage periods
paragraph: (b) one year, if the PCBs or products are stored at an authorized facility that is a transfer site; and

heading: Maximum storage periods
paragraph: (c) two years, if the PCBs or products are stored at an authorized facility that is authorized to destroy them.

heading: Transfer sites
paragraph: (2) If the PCBs or products containing PCBs are sent from one transfer site to another, the period referred to in paragraph (1)(b) begins when they are received at the first transfer site.

heading: Destruction
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of the facility referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) shall send the PCBs or products containing PCBs for destruction to an authorized facility that is authorized for that purpose within the time limit set out in those paragraphs.

heading: Exceptions to maximum storage periods
paragraph: 22 (1) Section 21 does not apply to the storage of

heading: Exceptions to maximum storage periods
paragraph: (a) liquids referred to in subsection 15(2) or for which an extension has been granted under subsection 17; or

heading: Exceptions to maximum storage periods
paragraph: (b) for the duration of any environmental remediation work, solids and liquids containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more resulting from that work and stored on site for that duration, if the requirements set out in subsections (2) and (3) are complied with.

heading: Information to be provided
paragraph: (2) The owner of the land where the solids and liquids referred to in paragraph (1)(b) are located shall submit to the Minister at least 30 days before the storage of the solids or liquids or within 30 days after September 5, 2008, whichever is later, the following information:

heading: Information to be provided
paragraph: (a) the civic address of the remediation work site or if there is no civic address, the location using the Global Positioning System;

heading: Information to be provided
paragraph: (b) the date of commencement of the remediation work;

heading: Information to be provided
paragraph: (c) the anticipated date of completion of the remediation work; and

heading: Information to be provided
paragraph: (d) the anticipated date of the end of storage of the solids or liquids.

heading: Changes to information
paragraph: (3) The person referred to in subsection (2) shall notify the Minister in writing of the changes to be made at least 30 days before making any changes to the information provided under that subsection.

heading: PCBs or products containing PCBs stored on September 5, 2008
paragraph: 23 A person who owns, controls or possesses PCBs or products containing PCBs, other than liquids for which an extension has been granted under section 17, that are stored on September 5, 2008 may store them

heading: PCBs or products containing PCBs stored on September 5, 2008
paragraph: (a) until December 31, 2009 if they are sent by that date for destruction to an authorized facility that is authorized for that purpose; or

heading: PCBs or products containing PCBs stored on September 5, 2008
paragraph: (b) until December 31, 2011 if they are destroyed by that date, at the location where they are stored, in an authorized facility that is authorized for that purpose.

heading: PCB storage site
paragraph: 24 PCBs or products containing PCBs shall be stored at a site that is

heading: PCB storage site
paragraph: (a) a building, room, shipping container or other enclosed structure; or

heading: PCB storage site
paragraph: (b) an area that is enclosed by a woven mesh wire fence or any other fence or wall with similar security characteristics, and the fence or wall shall be at least 1.83 m high.

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: 25 The owner or operator of a PCB storage site shall

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (a) store all PCBs or products containing PCBs that are in liquid form in

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (i) sealed containers, other than drums, that are made of steel or other metals that provide sufficient durability and strength to prevent those PCBs or products from being affected by the weather or released, or

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (ii) drums that are

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (A) of a capacity not greater than 205 L,

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (B) a closed-head double-bung drum made of steel having a gauge of 16 or heavier, and

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (C) painted or treated to prevent rusting;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (b) store all PCBs or products containing PCBs that are in solid form in

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (i) containers, other than drums, that are made of steel or other materials that provide sufficient durability and strength to prevent those PCBs or products from being affected by the weather or released, or

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (ii) drums that are

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (A) of a capacity not greater than 205 L,

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (B) made of steel having a gauge of 18 or heavier,

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (C) equipped with a securely attached, removable steel lid and a gasket made of material that is resistant to the PCBs or the products containing PCBs that are stored in the drums, and

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (D) painted or treated to prevent rusting;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (c) store equipment containing PCB liquids in

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (i) containers, other than drums, that are made of steel or other materials that provide sufficient durability and strength to prevent the equipment from being affected by the weather and to prevent any PCB liquid that leaks from the equipment from being released, or

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (ii) drums described in subparagraph (b)(ii);

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (d) store all equipment that is not in a container, other than drained equipment, if that equipment contains PCB liquid, and all containers of PCB liquid, on a floor or surface that is made of steel, concrete or any other similar durable material and that is constructed with curbing or sides that are capable of containing

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (i) if one piece of equipment or one container is being stored, 125% of the volume of the PCB liquid in the equipment or container, and

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (ii) if more than one piece of equipment or more than one container is being stored, the greater of twice the volume of the PCB liquid in the largest piece of equipment or the largest container and 25% of the volume of all the PCB liquid stored on the floor or surface;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (e) if the material of the floor or surface or the curbing or sides referred to in paragraph (d) are capable of absorbing any PCB liquid or other product containing PCBs, seal the floor, surface, curbing or sides with an impervious, durable, PCB-resistant coating;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (f) ensure that all floor drains, sumps or other openings in the floor or surface referred to in paragraph (d) are

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (i) closed and sealed to prevent the release of liquids, or

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (ii) connected to a drainage system suitable for liquid dangerous goods that terminates at a location where any spilled liquids will be contained and recovered and where the spilled liquids will not create a fire hazard or a risk to public health or safety;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (g) place on skids or pallets all equipment containing PCBs and containers of PCBs or products containing PCBs that are not permanently secured to the floor or a surface;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (h) stack containers of PCBs and products containing PCBs, other than drums, only if the containers are designed for stacking, and stack containers of PCB liquid not more than two containers high;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (i) if drums containing PCBs or products containing PCBs are stacked, separate the drums from each other with pallets and, in the case of drums of PCB liquid, stack the drums not more than two drums high;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (j) store equipment containing PCBs, and containers of PCBs or products containing PCBs, in a manner that makes them accessible for inspection;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (k) store PCBs or products containing PCBs in a manner that prevents them from catching fire or being released;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (l) store PCBs or products containing PCBs together, and separate them from other stored materials;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (m) if reasonably practicable, equip any indoor PCB storage site having a mechanical exhaust system with heat or smoke sensory controls that stop the fan and close the intake and exhaust dampers in the event of a fire;

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (n) if equipment or containers of PCB liquid are stored outdoors, cover all PCB equipment that is not in a container, other than drained equipment, if that equipment contains PCB liquid, and all containers of PCB liquid, with a weatherproof roof or barrier that protects the equipment and containers and prevents rain or snow from entering the curbing and the sides of the floor and the surface under them; and

heading: Storage requirements
paragraph: (o) ensure that all drained PCB equipment and all containers of any PCB solid or PCB equipment are structurally sound and weatherproof if stored outdoors.

heading: Access to PCB storage site
paragraph: 26 The owner or operator of a PCB storage site shall keep all points of access to the PCB storage site locked or guarded.

heading: Inspection and maintenance of a PCB storage site
paragraph: 27 The owner or operator of a PCB storage site shall

heading: Inspection and maintenance of a PCB storage site
paragraph: (a) inspect all floors, curbing, sides, drains, drainage systems, weatherproof roofs and barriers, fences and walls of the PCB storage site, any fire alarm system, fire extinguishers and fire suppression system and all equipment containing PCBs, containers used for the storage of PCBs or products containing PCBs and materials for clean-up at the PCB storage site

heading: Inspection and maintenance of a PCB storage site
paragraph: (i) each month,

heading: Inspection and maintenance of a PCB storage site
paragraph: (ii) at intervals of more than one month, if the Minister, on the written request of the owner or operator, determines that it is not reasonably practicable to inspect the site each month, due to its remote location, or

heading: Inspection and maintenance of a PCB storage site
paragraph: (iii) at intervals of less than one month, if more frequent inspections are necessary for the safe operation of the site; and

heading: Inspection and maintenance of a PCB storage site
paragraph: (b) keep in good condition and, if damaged, immediately repair or replace the floors, curbing, sides, drains, drainage systems, weatherproof roofs or barriers, fences, walls, fire alarm system, fire extinguishers, fire suppression system, equipment containing PCBs and containers and immediately clean up any contaminated area.

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: 28 (1) The owner or operator of a PCB storage site shall

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (a) develop and implement at the PCB storage site a fire protection and emergency procedures plan and shall

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (i) update and test the plan once per year,

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (ii) keep a written copy of the latest plan at the PCB storage site and another at their principal place of business, and

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (iii) make the latest plan readily available to persons who implement the plan and to the local fire department or to the local officer appointed by the provincial Fire Marshall if there is no local fire department or to any other local authority responsible for fire protection;

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (b) ensure that all employees who are authorized to enter the PCB storage site are familiar with the contents of the latest plan;

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (c) equip the indoor PCB storage site with a fully operative fire alarm system that is maintained, inspected and tested in accordance with articles 6.3.1.1 and 6.3.1.2 of the National Fire Code and with

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (i) portable fire extinguishers that are selected and installed in accordance with article 2.1.5.1 of the National Fire Code and maintained, inspected and tested in accordance with article 6.2.1.1 of that Code, or

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (ii) an automatic fire suppression system that meets the requirements of article 3.2.7.9 of the National Fire Code, if required;

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (d) keep a copy of the records referred to in sections 43 and 44 at the PCB storage site and make a copy readily available to the local fire department and, if there is no local fire department, to the local officer appointed by the provincial Fire Marshall or to any other local authority responsible for fire protection;

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (e) ensure that all employees who are authorized to enter the PCB storage site are made aware of the hazards of PCBs and are familiar with the use of protective equipment and clothing and the clean-up procedures referred to in the Guidelines for the Management of Wastes Containing Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs), CCME-TS/WM-TRE008, September 1989, as amended from time to time, issued by the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment; and

heading: Fire protection and emergency procedures
paragraph: (f) store absorbent materials for clean-up near the PCB storage site.

heading: Shipping containers
paragraph: (2) Despite paragraph (1)(c), if the indoor PCB storage site is a shipping container, the owner or operator of the site does not have to equip that site with a fire alarm system.

heading: Equipment and liquids used for their servicing
paragraph: 29 (1) The owner of equipment referred to in section 16, other than equipment for which an extension has been applied for under section 17, or of a liquid used in its servicing referred to in subsection 15(2) shall affix a label in a readily visible location on the equipment or on the container of the liquid, no later than 30 days after the day on which it ceases to be used.

heading: Equipment for which extension applied for
paragraph: (2) The owner of equipment for which an extension has been applied under section 17 shall affix a label in a readily visible location on the equipment.

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a) equipment or containers of liquids that bear a label on September 5, 2008 that indicates the presence of PCBs; and

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (b) equipment that is too small, including light ballasts, to bear the label referred to in subsection (4).

heading: Containers for small equipment
paragraph: (3.1) The owner of the equipment referred to in paragraph (3)(b) that is stored shall affix the label referred to in subsection (4) in a readily visible location on the container in which the equipment is stored.

heading: Description
paragraph: (4) The label must

heading: Description
paragraph: (a) state "ATTENTION - contains 50 mg/kg or more of PCBs / contient 50 mg/kg ou plus de BPC" in black lettering on a white background, in a font size of no less than 36 points;

heading: Description
paragraph: (b) measure at least 150 mm by 150 mm or at least 76 mm by 76 mm in the case of capacitors; and

heading: Description
paragraph: (c) in the case of equipment for which an extension is applied for under section 17, state a unique identification number.

heading: Cables and pipelines
paragraph: 30 (1) The owner of a cable, a pipeline or equipment associated with a pipeline, referred to in paragraphs 14(1)(a) and (b), containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more that is in a room, a tunnel or a facility shall either

heading: Cables and pipelines
paragraph: (a) affix the label in the form set out in subsection 29(4) in a readily visible location on a part of the cable, pipeline or associated equipment that is accessible; or

heading: Cables and pipelines
paragraph: (b) place a notice in a readily visible location at the entrance of the room, tunnel or facility that states the information set out in paragraph 29(4)(a) and measures at least 150 mm by 150 mm.

heading: If dismantled
paragraph: (2) If a part of the cable, pipeline or associated equipment is dismantled, the owner of the cable, pipeline or associated equipment shall affix on each dismantled part the label in the form set out in subsection 29(4), no later than 30 days after the day on which it is dismantled.

heading: A facility other than transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: 31 (1) The owner or operator of a PCB storage site, other than the PCB storage site of an authorized facility that is a transfer site or that is authorized to destroy PCBs, shall affix a label in a readily visible location on any product containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more and that are stored at the PCB storage site, which

heading: A facility other than transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (a) is in the form referred to in subsection 29(4); and

heading: A facility other than transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (b) states "Date of Commencement of Storage / Date de debut de stockage" and the date on which the storage begins.

heading: Transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of the PCB storage site of an authorized facility that is a transfer site or that is authorized to destroy PCBs shall affix a label in the form set out in subsection 29(4) in a readily visible location on any container that is a fixed tank and that is used at the facility for the storage of PCBs or products containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of a PCB storage site shall place a notice in a readily visible location at the entrance of the site that states the information set out in paragraph 29(4)(a) and that measures at least 150 mm by 150 mm.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (4) Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply in respect of a product or container stored on September 5, 2008, if the product or the container

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) bore a label on September 5, 2008 that indicated the presence of PCBs and that stated "Date of Commencement of Storage" and the date on which the storage began; and

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) bears a label that states "Date of Commencement of Storage / Date de debut de stockage" and the date on which the storage began.

heading: Retention of labels
paragraph: 32 The person who is required to affix a label on a product or container in accordance with sections 29 to 31 shall ensure that it bears that label for the duration that the person possesses the product or container.

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: 33 (1) The owner of the equipment referred to in paragraph 16(1)(a) or subparagraph 16(1)(b)(i) - other than the equipment for which an extension is granted by the Minister in accordance with section 17 and the equipment referred to in subsection 16(2) or (2.1) - or of the liquids referred to in subsection 15(2) shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 of each calendar year in which the person owns the equipment or the liquids and that contains the following information:

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses, telephone number, fax number, if any, and e-mail address, if any, of the owner and any person authorized to act on the owner's behalf;

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (b) for each piece of equipment, the civic addresses of the facilities where the equipment and liquids are located or, if there is no civic address, their location using the owner's site identification system;

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (c) for each piece of equipment, the quantity of liquids containing PCBs in the equipment and of liquids, expressed in litres, the quantity of solids containing PCBs in the equipment, expressed in kilograms, and the concentration of PCBs in the liquids and solids, expressed in mg/kg,

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (i) that are in use on December 31,

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (ii) that are stored on December 31 at the person's PCB storage site,

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (iii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is a transfer site,

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (iv) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is authorized to destroy them, or

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (v) that are destroyed in that calendar year; and

heading: End of use of equipment and liquids - 2009
paragraph: (d) a certification that the information is accurate and complete and that is dated and signed by the owner or by a person authorized to act on the owner's behalf.

heading: Equipment and liquids with extension
paragraph: (2) The owner of the equipment referred to in paragraph 16(1)(a) or subparagraph 16(1)(b)(i) - other than the equipment referred to in subsection 16(2) or (2.1) - or of the liquids referred to in subsection 15(2) for which an extension is granted by the Minister in accordance with section 17 shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 of each calendar year in which the person owns the equipment or the liquids and that contains the following information for each piece of equipment or container of liquid:

heading: Equipment and liquids with extension
paragraph: (a) the information required under paragraphs (1)(a) and (d);

heading: Equipment and liquids with extension
paragraph: (b) the unique identification number that is on the label referred to in paragraph 29(4)(c);

heading: Equipment and liquids with extension
paragraph: (c) the civic address, function and technical description of the facility where the equipment or container of liquid is located or, if there is no civic address, its location using the owner's site identification system;

heading: Equipment and liquids with extension
paragraph: (d) the progress on the plan's implementation and the timelines for ending the use of the equipment;

heading: Equipment and liquids with extension
paragraph: (e) the measures taken to minimize or eliminate any harmful effect of the PCBs in the equipment on the environment and on human health; and

heading: Equipment and liquids with extension
paragraph: (f) the findings of the inspections of the equipment.

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (3) The owner of the equipment referred to in subparagraph 16(1)(b)(ii) and subsection 16(2) shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 of each calendar year in which the person owns the equipment and that contains the following information:

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (a) the information required under paragraphs (1)(a) and (d);

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (a.1) the civic addresses of the facilities where the equipment and liquids are located or, if there is no civic address, their location using the owner's site identification system; and

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (b) the quantity of liquids containing PCBs in the equipment, expressed in litres, the quantity of solids containing PCBs in the equipment, expressed in kilograms, and the concentration of PCBs in the liquids and the solids, expressed in mg/kg,

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (i) that are stored on December 31 at the person's PCB storage site,

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (ii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is a transfer site,

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (iii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is authorized to destroy them, or

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (iv) that are destroyed in that calendar year.

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (4) The owner of the equipment referred to in subsection 16(2.1) shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 of each calendar year in which the person owns the equipment and that contains the following information:

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (a) the information required under paragraphs (1)(a), (b) and (d); and

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (b) for each piece of equipment, the quantity of liquids containing PCBs in the equipment, expressed in litres, the quantity of solids containing PCBs in the equipment, expressed in kilograms, and the concentration of PCBs in the liquids and the solids, expressed in mg/kg,

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (i) that are in use on December 31,

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (ii) that are stored on December 31 at the person's PCB storage site,

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (iii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is a transfer site,

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (iv) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is authorized to destroy them, or

heading: End of use of equipment - 2025
paragraph: (v) that are destroyed in that calendar year.

heading: Research
paragraph: 34 The person who offers for sale, sells, processes or uses PCBs or products containing PCBs for the purpose of research in accordance with section 8 shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 in each calendar year in which the person offers for sale, sells, processes or uses those PCBs or products and that contains the following information:

heading: Research
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses, telephone number, fax number, if any, and e-mail address, if any, of the person and of any person authorized to act on that person's behalf;

heading: Research
paragraph: (b) an indication of whether the person offers for sale, sells, processes or uses the PCBs or products;

heading: Research
paragraph: (c) the quantity of the PCBs or of the products containing PCBs that are offered for sale, sold, processed or used in that calendar year; and

heading: Research
paragraph: (d) a certification that the information is accurate and complete and that is dated and signed by the person or by a person authorized to act on their behalf.

heading: Colouring pigment
paragraph: 35 The person who manufactures, exports or imports colouring pigment in accordance with section 11 shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 in each calendar year in which the person manufactures, imports or exports the colouring pigment and that contains the following information:

heading: Colouring pigment
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses, telephone number, fax number, if any, and e-mail address, if any, of the person and of any person authorized to act on that person's behalf;

heading: Colouring pigment
paragraph: (b) an indication of whether the person manufactures, exports or imports colouring pigment;

heading: Colouring pigment
paragraph: (c) the quantity of colouring pigment, expressed in kilograms, the maximum concentration of PCBs in the colouring pigment, expressed in mg/kg, and the average annual concentration of PCBs in the colouring pigment, expressed in mg/kg, that is manufactured, imported or exported in that calendar year;

heading: Colouring pigment
paragraph: (d) in the case of importing, the name, telephone number and civic and mailing addresses of the person from whom the colouring pigment is imported and, in the case of exporting, the name, telephone number and civic and mailing addresses of the person to whom the colouring pigment is exported; and

heading: Colouring pigment
paragraph: (e) a certification that the information is accurate and complete and that is dated and signed by the person or by a person authorized to act on their behalf.

heading: Solid products containing PCBs
paragraph: 36 The person who manufactures solid products containing PCBs in accordance with section 13 shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 in each calendar year in which the person manufactures the products and that contains the following information:

heading: Solid products containing PCBs
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses, telephone number, fax number, if any, and e-mail address, if any, of the person and of any person authorized to act on that person's behalf;

heading: Solid products containing PCBs
paragraph: (b) the quantity of solid products manufactured in that calendar year, expressed in kilograms, and the maximum concentration and average concentration of PCBs in the solid products, expressed in mg/kg, for that calendar year;

heading: Solid products containing PCBs
paragraph: (c) the name, telephone number and civic and mailing addresses of the person to whom the manufacturer sells the products; and

heading: Solid products containing PCBs
paragraph: (d) a certification that the information is accurate and complete and that is dated and signed by the person or by a person authorized to act on their behalf.

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: 37 The person who owns and stores PCBs or products containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more, other than the equipment and liquids referred to in section 33, and the owner of a facility who stores PCBs or products containing PCBs in a concentration of 50 mg/kg or more, other than the person referred to in section 38, shall each prepare a report that is current to December 31 in each calendar year in which the person stores the PCBs or products at their PCB storage site and that contains the following information:

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses, telephone number, fax number, if any, and e-mail address, if any, of the owner and of any person authorized to act on the owner's behalf;

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (b) the civic addresses of the PCB storage sites where the PCBs or products are located, or if there is no civic address, their location using the owner's site identification system;

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (c) the quantity of liquids containing PCBs in the products, expressed in litres, and the quantity of solids containing PCBs in the products, expressed in kilograms, and the concentration of PCBs in the liquids and the solids, expressed in mg/kg

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (i) that are stored on December 31 at the person's PCB storage site,

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (ii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is a transfer site,

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (iii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is authorized to destroy them, or

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (iv) that are destroyed in that calendar year; and

heading: Stored PCBs or products - PCB concentration of 50 mg/kg or more
paragraph: (d) a certification that the information is accurate and complete and that is dated and signed by the owner of the PCBs or products containing PCBs or by a person authorized to act on the owner's behalf.

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: 38 The owner of an authorized facility that is a transfer site or that is authorized to destroy PCBs or products containing PCBs and who stores them at their PCB storage site, other than the owner referred to in section 37, shall prepare a report that is current to December 31 in each calendar year and that contains the following information:

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses, telephone number, fax number, if any, and e-mail address, if any, of the owner and of any person authorized to act on the owner's behalf;

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (b) the civic addresses of the sites where the PCBs or products containing PCBs are stored, or if there is no civic address, the location of the sites using the owner's site identification system;

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (c) the quantity of liquids containing PCBs in the products, expressed in litres, or the quantity of solids containing PCBs in the products, expressed in kilograms, and the concentration of the PCBs in the liquids and the solids, expressed in mg/kg

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (i) that are stored on December 31 at the owner's PCB storage site,

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (ii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is a transfer site,

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (iii) that are sent, in that calendar year, to an authorized facility that is authorized to destroy them, or

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (iv) that are destroyed in that calendar year; and

heading: Stored PCBs or products - transfer site or destruction facility
paragraph: (d) a certification that the information is accurate and complete and that is dated and signed by the owner of the authorized facility or by a person authorized to act on the owner's behalf.

heading: Date of submission of report
paragraph: 39 (1) The person who is required to prepare a report in accordance with subsection 33(1), (2) or (4) or with any of sections 34 to 38 shall submit it to the Minister on or before March 31 of the calendar year following the calendar year for which the report is made.

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (2) The person who is required to prepare a report in accordance with subsection 33(3) shall submit it to the Minister

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (a) on or before March 31, 2010 for reports that are current to December 31 of the year that these Regulations come into force up to the year 2009;

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (b) on or before March 31, 2014 for reports that are current to December 31 of each of the years 2010 to 2013;

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (c) on or before March 31, 2018 for reports that are current to December 31 of each of the years 2014 to 2017;

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (d) on or before March 31, 2022 for reports that are current to December 31 of each of the years 2018 to 2021;

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (e) on or before March 31, 2026 for reports that are current to December 31 of each of the years 2022 to 2025;

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (f) on or before March 31, 2027 for reports that are current to December 31 of the year 2026; and

heading: Report made under subsection 33(3)
paragraph: (g) on or before March 31, 2030 for reports that are current to December 31 of each of the years 2027 to 2029.

heading: Release into the environment
paragraph: 40 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 95(1)(a) of the Act, where there occurs or is a likelihood of a release into the environment of PCBs in contravention of section 5, the person who is designated to be provided with a written report is the Regional Director, Environmental Enforcement Division, Enforcement Branch of the Department of the Environment in the region where the release occurs or is likely to occur.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The report shall include the following information:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) the name, civic and mailing addresses and telephone number of the person who owns or has the charge, management or control of the PCBs that are released into the environment;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) the date, time and location of the release;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) a description of the source of the release; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) the quantity of liquids containing PCBs released, expressed in litres, the quantity of solids containing PCBs released, expressed in kilograms, and the concentration of PCBs in the liquids and the solids that are released, expressed in mg/kg.

heading: Retention
paragraph: 41 Any person who is required to submit a report under these Regulations shall keep a copy of the report at their principal place of business in Canada for at least five years after the day on which the report is submitted.

heading: Method of submission
paragraph: 42 Each report referred to in sections 33 to 38 shall be submitted electronically in the format provided by the Department of the Environment, but the report shall be submitted in writing if

heading: Method of submission
paragraph: (a) no such format is provided; or

heading: Method of submission
paragraph: (b) it is, owing to circumstances beyond the control of the person required to submit the report, impracticable to submit the report electronically in the format provided.

heading: Records for permitted activities
paragraph: 43 The following persons shall maintain records containing information and documents that demonstrate that they manufacture, process, use, sell, offer for sale, store, import or export PCBs or products containing PCBs in accordance with the Act and these Regulations:

heading: Records for permitted activities
paragraph: (a) the owner of PCBs or products containing PCBs;

heading: Records for permitted activities
paragraph: (b) the person who is engaged in any of these activities; and

heading: Records for permitted activities
paragraph: (c) the owner or operator of a PCB storage site.

heading: Inspection record
paragraph: 44 (1) The owner or operator of a PCB storage site shall maintain a record of all inspections conducted at the PCB storage site under paragraph 27(a)

heading: Inspection record
paragraph: (a) listing all items that are inspected;

heading: Inspection record
paragraph: (b) describing any deficiency found;

heading: Inspection record
paragraph: (c) setting out the measures taken to remedy the deficiency; and

heading: Inspection record
paragraph: (d) specifying the dates of the inspections and the names of the inspectors.

heading: Owner of equipment - extension
paragraph: (2) The owner of equipment for which an extension of the end-of-use date is applied under section 17 shall maintain a record of all inspections conducted on the equipment that contains the information set out in paragraphs (1)(a) to (d).

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: 45 The person who is required to maintain a record under sections 43 and 44 shall retain it at their principal place of business in Canada or at the place where they conduct the activity for at least five years

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (a) after the destruction of the PCBs or the products containing PCBs that are the subject of the record, in the case of the owner of PCBs or products containing PCBs or the owner or operator of the PCB storage site where the PCBs or products containing PCBs are stored; or

heading: Retention of records
paragraph: (b) after the completion of an activity referred to in section 43, in the case of the person who is engaged in that activity.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Wildlife Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "government agency" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the government of Canada or an agency operated or maintained by that government,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the government of a province in Canada or an agency operated or maintained by a province, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the government of the United States of America, a state of the United States or an agency operated or maintained by the United States or a state of the United States;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licence year" means the period commencing April 1 in a calendar year and ending on March 31 of the following calendar year;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regional manager", except in sections 6 (2), 9 (1), 17 (1) and 23 (4) (c), includes a person authorized by a regional manager;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "shot" has the same meaning as in B.C. Reg. 76/84, the Closed Areas Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "youth hunting licence" has the same meaning as in the Hunting Licensing Regulation, B.C. Reg. 8/99;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "zoo" means a place or enclosure where animals are kept in captivity for public viewing or public display, but does not include a permitted rehabilitation facility or a business for the sale of live animals.

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: 2		  A regional manager may issue a permit in accordance with this regulation on the terms and for the period the regional manager specifies

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (a) authorizing a person to use land or resources in a wildlife management area in accordance with section 4 (4) of the Act,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (b) authorizing a resident to hunt, trap or kill wildlife on the resident's own property during the open or closed season, including by the use of poison, for the following purposes:

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (i)  agricultural crop protection;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (ii)  controlling wildlife populations,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (c) authorizing a person to hunt, trap or kill wildlife during the open or closed season for the following purposes:

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (i)  scientific purposes;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (ii)  educational purposes;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (iii)  if the regional manager considers it necessary for the proper management of the wildlife resource;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (iv)  on behalf of the government, to destroy wildlife that is dangerous to public safety;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (v)  on behalf of the government, to destroy wildlife that is so badly injured that prolonging the animal's life would result in the animal suffering unduly,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (d) authorizing a person to hunt, trap or kill wildlife in a wildlife sanctuary,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (e) authorizing a person to trap wildlife during the open or closed season with a trap that is prohibited by regulation,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (f) authorizing a person to traffic in

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (i)  legally taken wildlife meat,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (ii)  the person's possessory interest in wildlife legally held captive, or

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (iii)  the person's possessory interest in dead wildlife or wildlife parts,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (g) authorizing a person to allow a dog to pursue small game, excluding migratory game birds, during the open or closed season for the purpose of conducting field dog trials,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (h) authorizing a person to capture live wildlife,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (i) authorizing a person to discharge a firearm in a no shooting area,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (j) authorizing a person to possess live wildlife,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (k) authorizing

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (i)  a person to possess and dispose of dead wildlife or parts of wildlife for scientific or educational purposes, or

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (ii)  a person to possess and dispose of dead wildlife or parts of wildlife for a ceremonial or societal purpose,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (l) authorizing a licensed trapper or a person exempt from holding a trapping licence to set traps for and trap fur bearing animals on a trapline registered to another person,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (m) authorizing a person to transport or engage another person to transport live wildlife within British Columbia,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (n) authorizing a person to export from British Columbia

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (i)  wildlife,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (ii)  parts of wildlife, or

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (iii)  an egg of a wildlife species,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (o) authorizing a person to release an animal from captivity,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (p) transferring the right of property in dead wildlife or wildlife parts from the government to a person,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (q) authorizing an assistant guide to exercise the privileges and perform the duties of a guide outfitter under the Act and regulations,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (r) authorizing a person or association to organize or carry on an operation for the purpose of hunting game birds, excluding migratory game birds, on property the person or association owns or controls access to,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (s) authorizing an institution or non-profit organization directly concerned with physically or mentally disabled persons or persons under 19 years of age to undertake fishing programs in non-tidal waters of British Columbia and exempting the participants of the program from the requirement to hold an angling licence,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (t) authorizing a person, for the purpose of rehabilitating wildlife, to do any or all of the following:

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (i)  keep wildlife in captivity;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (ii)  capture wildlife;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (iii)  transport wildlife

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (A) to a rehabilitation facility, or

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (B) for the purpose of releasing the wildlife;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (iv)  release wildlife;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (v)  perform euthanasia on wildlife;

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (vi)  possess dead wildlife for the purpose of disposal,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (v) authorizing a person in need of sustenance to possess game meat for the purpose of providing sustenance for the person and the person's dependants,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (w) authorizing a food bank or similar non-profit organization to possess and distribute game meat to persons in need of sustenance,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (y) authorizing a person to possess dead wildlife or parts of wildlife if the documentation to prove ownership under section 2 (2) or 2 (3) of the Act has been lost or destroyed,

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (aa) subject to section 2.01, authorizing a physically disabled person to be assisted by having one or more hunting companions to, on the disabled person's behalf, track, kill and retrieve big game wounded by the disabled person, or

heading: Authorization by permit
paragraph: (bb) subject to section 2.01, authorizing a physically disabled person to be assisted by having one or more hunting companions, named on the permit, to shoot, track, kill and retrieve big game on the disabled person's behalf.

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph:
2.01
		  (1) The regional manager may only issue a permit

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph: (a) under section 2 (aa) if, because of a person's physical disability, the person to be assisted is unable to track or retrieve big game and would be unable, if on the initial shooting the big game is not killed, to track, kill or retrieve the wounded big game, or

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph: (b) under section 2 (bb) if, because of a person's physical disability, the person to be assisted is unable to discharge a firearm or crossbow.

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph: (2) The regional manager, in issuing a permit

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph: (a) under section 2 (aa) or (bb), must set as a condition of the permit that the permit holder and the hunting companion each has a hunting licence, and

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph: (b) under section 2 (bb), must set as conditions of the permit that the permit holder

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph: (i)  selects the animal to be hunted by the hunting companion, and

heading: Permits under section 2 (aa) and (bb)
paragraph: (ii)  remains in the presence of the hunting companion during the initial shooting of the animal by the hunting companion.

heading: Rainbow trout ponds
paragraph:
2.1
		  (1) In this section, "pond" means an artificially created pool of water

heading: Rainbow trout ponds
paragraph: (a) that is a closed-system for holding rainbow trout,

heading: Rainbow trout ponds
paragraph: (b) that is not connected to a natural watercourse,

heading: Rainbow trout ponds
paragraph: (c) from which rainbow trout can not escape to tidal or non-tidal waters if the pond overflows, and

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph:
3.1
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), a regional manager may issue a permit in accordance with this regulation on the terms and for the period the regional manager specifies authorizing a person to undertake one or more of the following activities prohibited by section 27 of the Act:

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (a) discharging a firearm or wounding or killing wildlife from a motor vehicle or from a boat that is propelled by a motor;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (b) hunting wildlife from an aircraft;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (c) using a helicopter to transport hunters or game, or while on a hunting expedition;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (d) herding or harassing wildlife with the use of a motor vehicle, aircraft, boat or other mechanical device.

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (2) A regional manager may not issue a permit under subsection (1) (a) unless

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (a) the activity to be undertaken under the permit is for one of the following purposes:

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (i)  a scientific purpose;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (ii)  an educational purpose;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (iii)  to destroy wildlife that is dangerous to public safety;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (iv)  to destroy wildlife that is so badly injured that prolonging the animal's life would result in the animal suffering unduly;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (v)  to address a matter of animal health among wildlife populations;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (vi)  to control wildlife populations;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (vii)  to accommodate hunting by a person with a physical disability, or

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (b) the regional manager considers that issuing the permit is necessary for the proper management of a wildlife resource.

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (3) A regional manager may not issue a permit under subsection (1) (b) or (d) unless

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (a) the regional manager is satisfied that the person who will be undertaking the activity under the permit has sufficient skill to undertake that activity, and

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (b) one the following applies:

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (i)  the activity to be undertaken under the permit is for a purpose referred to in any of subsection (2) (a) (i) to (vi);

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (ii)  the regional manager considers that issuing the permit is necessary for the proper management of a wildlife resource.

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (4) A regional manager may not issue a permit under subsection (1) (c) unless

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (a) the activity to be undertaken under the permit is for a purpose referred to in any of subsection (2) (i) to (vi),

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (b) the regional manager considers that exigent circumstances exist and use of the helicopter will assist in

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (i)  addressing a risk to the life or health of a person, or

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (ii)  retrieving property, including game that has been taken or killed, or

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (c) the regional manager considers that issuing the permit is necessary for the proper management of a wildlife resource.

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), a person who undertakes an activity in accordance with a permit issued under subsection (1) is exempt from the following:

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (a) section 35 (2) of the Act;

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (b) section 18 (1) (q) of the Hunting Regulation, B.C. Reg. 190/84.

heading: Permit for use of conveyance
paragraph: (6) The exemption under subsection (5) does not apply to a permit issued under subsection (1) (a) for the purpose referred to in subsection (2) (a) (vii).

heading: Director's permits
paragraph:
4
		  The director may issue a permit in accordance with this regulation on the terms and for the period the director specifies,

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (a) if satisfied that special circumstances exist, authorizing a non-resident or non-resident alien,

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (i)  to hunt game, or

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (ii)  to angle for fish,

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (b) authorizing a person to import into British Columbia

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (i)  live wildlife, or

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (ii)  the egg of a wildlife species,

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (c) authorizing an educational institution or non-profit organization that provides outdoor educational programs in British Columbia to undertake fishing programs in non-tidal waters of British Columbia and exempting the participants of the program from the requirement to hold an angling licence,

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (e) that will be awarded to the nominee of a person who holds a raffle or auction in accordance with a contract that person entered into with the government, authorizing a person to hunt game

paragraph: (i)  in an open or closed season, and

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (ii)  in excess of the bag limit for the species of game,

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (f) authorizing a person to possess a species individual of a controlled alien species if

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (i)  the species individual was in British Columbia on March 16, 2009,

heading: Director's permits
paragraph: (ii)  the person operates a zoo or is an educational or research institution, or

paragraph: (iii)  the director is satisfied that special circumstances exist,

paragraph: (g) authorizing a person who possesses a species individual of a controlled alien species and who operates a zoo or is an educational or research institution to allow that species individual to breed, or
