heading: Restrictions on issuing permits generally
paragraph:
5
		  (1) Before issuing a permit under section 2, 3 or 4 the regional manager or the director, as applicable, must be satisfied

heading: Restrictions on issuing permits generally
paragraph: (a) that the applicant meets the specific requirements, if any, for the permit as set out in this regulation, and

heading: Restrictions on issuing permits generally
paragraph: (b) that issuing the permit is not contrary to the proper management of wildlife resources in British Columbia.

heading: Restrictions on issuing permits generally
paragraph: (2) A permit must not be issued to a person

heading: Restrictions on issuing permits generally
paragraph: (a) who is under 10 years of age, or

heading: Restrictions on issuing permits generally
paragraph: (b) who is under 19 years of age unless a parent or guardian of the person has consented in writing to the application.

heading: Restrictions on issuing permits generally
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), a permit under section 4 (f) to (h) must not be issued to a person who is under 19 years of age.

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A regional manager must not issue

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (a) a permit under section 2 (j) or (p) if the wildlife or parts that are the subject of the permit were taken, captured, possessed, transported, hunted, trapped, imported or killed contrary to the Act or regulations,

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (b) a permit under section 2 (p) if the wildlife that is the subject of the permit was killed by accident, for a humane purpose or for the protection of life or property, unless the regional manager is satisfied that special circumstances exist,

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (c) a permit under section 2 (p) transferring a right of property in

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (i)  antlers, or

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (ii)  any of the following wildlife or parts of them:

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (A) eagles;

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (B) migratory insectivorous birds or migratory nongame birds both as defined in the Convention appended to the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 (Canada);

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (C) endangered species or threatened species;

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (D) grizzly bears, or

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (d) a permit under section 2 (p) for wildlife if the value of the wildlife or wildlife parts is greater than $200 unless

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (i)  the person applying for the permit will receive the dead wildlife or wildlife parts as compensation for conducting work or an activity on behalf of the government, or

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (ii)  the person applying for the permit is applying on behalf of a charitable organization in British Columbia.

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1) (d), the value of wildlife or wildlife parts is to be determined by the regional manager based on the average price the government receives at auction for wildlife or wildlife parts of the particular species, of similar size and in similar condition.

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), a regional manager may issue a permit under section 2 (j) or (p), as applicable, to an educational institution or a scientific organization or an agent of either

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (i) to authorize the possession of, or

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (ii) to transfer property rights in

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: wildlife or parts of wildlife for an educational or scientific purpose.

heading: Restrictions on permits providing possessory or property rights
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (1) (a), a regional manager may issue a permit under section 2 (p) with respect to dead wildlife or a part of wildlife to a person who finds and collects that wildlife or part and who was not a party to any of the activities referred to in subsection (1) (a) with respect that wildlife or part, other than transporting and possessing, if the person immediately notifies an officer that the person is in possession of that dead wildlife or part and applies for the permit.

heading: No permit to import certain wildlife
paragraph: 7		  (1) For the purpose of section 21 of the Act and section 4 (b) of this regulation, a permit must not be issued to authorize the importation of a species of wildlife listed in Schedule 1.

heading: No permit to import certain wildlife
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the director may issue a permit under section 4 (b) for a species of wildlife listed in Schedule 1 if the applicant is an educational institution or scientific organization or an agent of either and the director is satisfied that the importation will not be detrimental to native wildlife or wildlife habitat.

heading: General offence - failure to comply with permit
paragraph:
8
		  A person who holds a permit under the Act or this regulation commits an offence if the person fails to comply with a term of the permit.

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph:
9
		  (1) An application for a permit under section 2 (h) must be made to the regional manager in writing and must either contain the following information or specify when the applicant will provide the following information:

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (a) the name, address and date of birth of the applicant;

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (b) the species, age, sex and number of wildlife to be captured;

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (c) the location of the proposed capture;

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (d) the method of capture and transportation of the wildlife to be captured;

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (e) the standard of care for the wildlife to be captured;

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (f) the proposed use of the wildlife.

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (2) A person is not eligible for a permit under section 2 (h) if the person has been convicted of an offence

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (a) specified under section 84 (1) (a) of the Act, within the 5 year period immediately preceding the application for a permit, or

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (b) specified under section 84 (1) (b) of the Act, within the 3 year period immediately preceding the application for a permit.

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (3) A permit under section 2 (h) for the capture of a raptor for the purposes of falconry may be issued only to a resident.

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (4) The following are terms of every permit issued under section 2 (h):

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (a) the holder of the permit must notify the permit issuer in writing within 21 days after the capture of wildlife of

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (i)  the species, age, sex and number of the wildlife captured and whether alive or dead,

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (ii)  the date of capture of each animal,

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (iii)  the location of capture of each animal, and

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (iv)  the provisions instituted and maintained to ensure humane care of the wildlife;

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (b) if no wildlife is captured under the permit the holder of the permit must, within 21 days after the expiry date of the permit, notify the permit issuer in writing that no wildlife was captured under the permit;

heading: Live capture permits
paragraph: (c) if the holder of the permit is under 19 years of age, the holder of the permit may carry out the activities authorized by the permit only if accompanied by a resident who is 19 years of age or over.

heading: Sections 2 (j), (m), (n), (o) and 4 (b) permit requirements
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A regional manager or the director, as applicable, must not issue a permit with respect to live wildlife under section 2 (j), (m), (n), (o) or 4 (b) unless the applicant has submitted a plan with the applicant's permit application that demonstrates that public safety will not be jeopardized by any activity to be undertaken under the permit.

heading: Sections 2 (j), (m), (n), (o) and 4 (b) permit requirements
paragraph: (2) It is a term of every permit issued with respect to live wildlife under sections 2 (j), (m), (n) and (o) and 4 (b) that the permit holder comply with the plan submitted under subsection (1).

heading: Sections 2 (j), (m), (n), (o) and 4 (b) permit requirements
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to a permit respecting a raptor used for falconry purposes.

heading: Exemption - feeding dangerous wildlife
paragraph:
11
		  A person who holds a permit under section 2 (h), (j), (m), (n) or (o) or 4 (b) is exempt from section 33.1 of the Act for the purpose of feeding dangerous wildlife held under the permit.

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph:
12
		  A permit issued under section 2 (h), (j), (m) or (n) (i) or 4 (b) may include

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph: (a) terms and conditions respecting the location, dimensions, construction and maintenance of, and the materials to be used in constructing and maintaining, enclosures for wildlife, and

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph: (b) terms and conditions intended to

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph: (i)  protect against unnecessary suffering by the wildlife,

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph: (ii)  provide adequate protection and shelter for the wildlife,

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph: (iii)  facilitate safe and sanitary cleaning of the wildlife and enclosures,

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph: (iv)  prevent the escape of the wildlife, and

heading: Conditions attached to live wildlife permits
paragraph: (v)  prevent, by means of a secondary fence or barrier, members of the public from coming into personal contact with an enclosure.

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph:
13
		  The following are terms of every permit issued under section 2 (j):

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (a) the permit holder must maintain an accurate up to date record of the wildlife held under the permit which shows all additions and deletions from the record and which includes the following information:

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (i)  the common name of the wildlife;

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (ii)  the number, sex, maturity and condition of the wildlife;

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (iii)  the name and address of the person or organization who provided the wildlife;

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (iv)  the name and address of the person or organization to whom the wildlife was provided, if any;

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (v)  the number of the permit under which the wildlife was captured, transported or imported;

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (vi)  the manner, form, locations and date of marking of wildlife taken from the wild and the number and date of the official receipt for the capture fee;

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (b) the permit holder must submit a copy of the record referred to in paragraph (a) to the permit issuer within 21 days after the expiry date of the permit;

heading: Record of live wildlife held requirement
paragraph: (c) the permit holder must produce a copy of the record referred to in paragraph (a) on demand of an officer.

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph:
14
		  The following are terms of every permit issued under section 2 (b), (c) (i), (ii), (iv) or (v), (d), 3 (1) (a) or (d) or 3.1:

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (a) the permit holder must maintain an accurate up to date record of the wildlife hunted, trapped or killed under the permit, which includes the following information:

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (i)  the common name of the wildlife;

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (ii)  the location where the wildlife was taken;

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (iii)  the date the wildlife was hunted, trapped or killed;

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (iv)  the sex and age class of the wildlife taken;

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (v)  the bands or tags on the wildlife;

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (vi)  a description of all nests, dams or other structures destroyed or removed;

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (b) the permit holder must submit the original record referred to in paragraph (a) to the permit issuer within 21 days after the expiry date of the permit;

heading: Record of wildlife killed requirement
paragraph: (c) the permit holder must produce a copy of the record referred to in paragraph (a) on the demand of an officer.

heading: Application of section 33 (2) of the Act
paragraph:
15
		  (1) For the purposes of section 33 (2) of the Act, it is not an offence for a person to possess

heading: Application of section 33 (2) of the Act
paragraph: (a) antlers,

heading: Application of section 33 (2) of the Act
paragraph: (b) bird feathers, except feathers from migratory insectivorous birds or migratory nongame birds both as defined in the Convention appended to the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 (Canada),

paragraph: (e) wildlife or parts of wildlife that have been processed or manufactured into a product that no longer resembles the original dead wildlife or parts,

heading: Application of section 33 (2) of the Act

paragraph: (2) The burden of proving an entitlement under subsection (1) (d) is on the person claiming the exemption.

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: 16		  (1) To be eligible for a permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act an applicant must

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (a) be at least 19 years of age,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (b) be a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, and

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (c) have

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (i)  held a resident hunting licence and a species licence for big game for 3 of the 5 licence years immediately preceding the application for a permit, or

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (ii)  successfully completed the CORE program as defined in B.C. Reg. 53/98, the Hunter Safety Training Regulation, and have held a resident hunting licence and a species licence for big game for 2 of the 5 licence years immediately preceding the application for a permit.

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (2) A person is not eligible for a permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act if

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (a) another permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act has been issued to the person in the same licence year,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (b) either the applicant or the non-resident or non-resident alien to whom the permit would apply has been convicted of an offence

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (i)  specified under section 84 (1) (a) of the Act within the 5 year period immediately preceding the application for a permit, or

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (ii)  specified under

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (A) section 84 (1) (b) of the Act, or

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (B) the Firearm Act,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: within the 3 year period immediately preceding the application for a permit, or

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (c) another permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act has been issued for a different time period in the same licence year that applies to the non-resident or non-resident alien whom the person will accompany under the permit.

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (3) A permit must not be issued under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (a) for a period of more than 21 days,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (b) that applies to more than one region established by section 3 of B.C. Reg. 190/84, the Hunting Regulation,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (c) to allow the permit holder to accompany more than 2 non-residents or non-resident aliens, or

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (d) to allow the permit holder to accompany a non-resident alien who is not, in relation to the permit holder, a parent, sibling, child, parent's sibling, sibling's child, grandchild, grandparent, spouse, parent of a spouse, spouse of a child, sibling of a spouse or spouse of a sibling.

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (4) A person commits an offence if the person

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (a) hunts big game while in the company of a non-resident or non-resident alien who is hunting big game unless there is present a guide outfitter, an assistant guide or a person who holds a permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act that applies to that non-resident or non-resident alien,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (b) holds a permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and, while accompanying a non-resident or non-resident alien to which the permit applies,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (i)  is not a resident,

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (ii)  fails to hold a valid hunting licence, or

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (iii)  fails to hold an uncancelled species licence for the species being hunted, or

heading: Permits under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and offences
paragraph: (c) holds a permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act and fails to accompany the non-resident or non-resident alien to which the permit applies while that person is hunting big game unless a guide outfitter, an assistant guide or another person who holds a permit under section 70 (1) (a) of the Act that applies to the same non-resident or non-resident alien is accompanying that non-resident or non-resident alien.

paragraph: 2 (1) Any person applying for a permit under section 73 of the Act in relation to an activity affecting a listed wildlife species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals must submit an application to the competent minister in a form and manner that is satisfactory to that minister.

heading: Content - additional information
paragraph: (b) demonstrating that all feasible measures will be taken to minimize the impact of the activity on the species, its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals; and

heading: Content - additional information
paragraph: (c) describing any changes that the activity may cause to the listed wildlife species, its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals, the possible effects of those changes and the significance of those effects.

paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), the competent minister must either issue a permit or notify the applicant of the refusal to issue a permit within 90 days after the date of the notice indicating that the application has been received.

paragraph: (2) The time limit set out in subsection (1) is suspended if the application is incomplete. The suspension begins on the day on which the competent minister notifies the applicant in writing that the information provided is insufficient to allow the competent minister to issue or refuse to issue a permit and ends on the day on which the competent minister receives all of the missing information.

paragraph: (3) The time limit set out in subsection (1) is not applicable in the following circumstances:

paragraph: bioaccumulation factor means the ratio of the concentration of a substance in an organism to the concentration in water, based on uptake from the surrounding medium and food. (facteur de bioaccumulation)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: bioconcentration factor means the ratio of the concentration of a substance in an organism to the concentration in water, based only on uptake from the surrounding medium. (facteur de bioconcentration)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: half-life means the period it takes the concentration of a substance to be reduced by half, by transformation, in a medium. (demi-vie)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: octanol-water partition coefficient means the ratio of the concentration of a substance in an octanol phase to the concentration of the substance in the water phase of an octanol-water mixture. (coefficient de partage octanol-eau)

heading: Application
paragraph: 2 These Regulations apply to any substance, other than a living organism within the meaning of Part 6 of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999.

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: 3 A substance is persistent when it has at least one of the following characteristics:

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (a) in air,

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (i) its half-life is equal to or greater than 2 days, or

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (ii) it is subject to atmospheric transport from its source to a remote area;

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (b) in water, its half-life is equal to or greater than 182 days;

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (c) in sediments, its half-life is equal to or greater than 365 days; or

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (d) in soil, its half-life is equal to or greater than 182 days.

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: 4 A substance is bioaccumulative

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (a) when its bioaccumulation factor is equal to or greater than 5 000;

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (b) if its bioaccumulation factor cannot be determined in accordance with a method referred to in section 5, when its bioconcentration factor is equal to or greater than 5 000; and

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: (c) if neither its bioaccumulation factor nor its bioconcentration factor can be determined in accordance with a method referred to in section 5, when the logarithm of its octanol-water partition coefficient is equal to or greater than 5.

heading: Persistence and Bioaccumulation Determination
paragraph: 5 The determination of persistence and bioaccumulation with respect to a substance under sections 3 and 4 must be made in accordance with generally recognized methods of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) or of some other similar organisation or, if no such methods exist, in accordance with generally recognized methods within the scientific community and taking into account the intrinsic properties of the substance, the ecosystem under consideration and the conditions in the environment.

heading: Coming into Force
paragraph: 6 These Regulations come into force on March 31, 2000.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Pest Control Products Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 (1) The definitions in this subsection apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: active ingredient means a component of a pest control product to which the intended effects of the product are attributed and includes a synergist but does not include a solvent, diluent, emulsifier or other component that is not primarily responsible for those effects. (principe actif)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: advertise includes making a representation by any means for the purpose of directly or indirectly promoting the distribution of a pest control product. (publicite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: analyst means an individual who is appointed or designated as an analyst under section 45. (analyste)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: biological diversity means the variability among living organisms from all sources, including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, terrestrial and marine and other aquatic ecosystems and the ecological complexes of which they form a part and includes the diversity within and between species and of ecosystems. (diversite biologique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: biotechnology means the application of science and engineering in the direct or indirect use of living organisms or parts or products of living organisms in their natural or modified forms. (biotechnologie)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: conditions of registration means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any conditions specified by the Minister under paragraph 8(1)(a) or subsection 8(2) or when amending the registration of a pest control product under this Act; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any other requirements stated by this Act or the regulations to be conditions of registration. (conditions d'homologation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: confidential business information means information to which access may be refused under the Access to Information Act and that meets the requirements of subsection 43(4) or (5). (renseignements commerciaux confidentiels)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: confidential test data means test data to which access may be refused under the Access to Information Act. (donnees d'essai confidentielles)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: distribute means distribute in any way, whether or not for consideration, and includes sell, offer for sale or distribution, and expose, display or advertise for sale or distribution. (distribution)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: document means anything on which information that is capable of being understood by a person, or read by a computer or other device, is recorded or marked. (document)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ecosystem means a dynamic complex of plant, animal and micro-organism communities and their non-living environment interacting as a functional unit. (ecosysteme)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environment means the components of the Earth and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) air, land and water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) all layers of the atmosphere;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) all organic and inorganic matter and living organisms; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the interacting natural systems that include components referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c). (environnement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: environmental risk, in respect of a pest control product, means the possibility of harm to the environment, including its biological diversity, resulting from exposure to or use of the product, taking into account its conditions or proposed conditions of registration. (risque environnemental)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: formulant means any component of a pest control product that is added intentionally to the product and that is not an active ingredient. (formulant)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: government policy means the Toxic Substances Management Policy issued by the Government of Canada in June, 1995, as long as it remains in effect, and any other policies of the Government of Canada that are prescribed. (politique gouvernementale)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: health risk, in respect of a pest control product, means the possibility of harm to human health resulting from exposure to or use of the product, taking into account its conditions or proposed conditions of registration. (risque sanitaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inspector means an individual who is appointed or designated as an inspector under section 45. (inspecteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: label includes any written, printed or graphic matter

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) that is or is to be applied or attached to or included in, or that accompanies or is to accompany, a pest control product or a package; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) that belongs to a pest control product and is transmitted electronically, in accordance with the regulations. (etiquette)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: manufacture includes produce, formulate, package, label and prepare for distribution or use. (fabrication)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Health. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: package includes a container, wrapping, covering or holder in which a pest control product is wholly or partly contained, placed or packed. (emballage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: penalty means an administrative monetary penalty imposed under the Agriculture and Agri-Food Administrative Monetary Penalties Act for a violation. (penalite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: person means Her Majesty, an individual or an organization as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code. (personne)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pest means an animal, a plant or other organism that is injurious, noxious or troublesome, whether directly or indirectly, and an injurious, noxious or troublesome condition or organic function of an animal, a plant or other organism. (parasite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pest control product means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a product, an organism or a substance, including a product, an organism or a substance derived through biotechnology, that consists of its active ingredient, formulants and contaminants, and that is manufactured, represented, distributed or used as a means for directly or indirectly controlling, destroying, attracting or repelling a pest or for mitigating or preventing its injurious, noxious or troublesome effects;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an active ingredient that is used to manufacture anything described in paragraph (a); or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) any other thing that is prescribed to be a pest control product. (produit antiparasitaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: place includes a means of transport. (lieu)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed means prescribed by regulation. (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Register means the Register of Pest Control Products established and maintained under section 42. (Registre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: registrant means a person in whose name a pest control product is registered. (titulaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: test data means scientific or technical information respecting the health or environmental risks or the value of a pest control product. (donnees d'essai)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: threshold effect, in respect of a pest control product, means a harmful effect on human health for which the Minister is able to identify a level at which the product will not cause that effect. (effet de seuil)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: value, in respect of a pest control product, means the product's actual or potential contribution to pest management, taking into account its conditions or proposed conditions of registration, and includes the product's

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) efficacy;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) effect on host organisms in connection with which it is intended to be used; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) health, safety and environmental benefits and social and economic impact. (valeur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: violation means any of the following that may be proceeded with in accordance with the Agriculture and Agri-Food Administrative Monetary Penalties Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any contravention of any provision of this Act or of a regulation made under this Act; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any refusal or neglect to perform any duty imposed by or under this Act. (violation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: workplace means a place where an individual works for remuneration. (lieu de travail)

heading: Acceptable risks
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Act, the health or environmental risks of a pest control product are acceptable if there is reasonable certainty that no harm to human health, future generations or the environment will result from exposure to or use of the product, taking into account its conditions or proposed conditions of registration.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 3 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Primary objective
paragraph: 4 (1) In the administration of this Act, the Minister's primary objective is to prevent unacceptable risks to individuals and the environment from the use of pest control products.

heading: Ancillary objectives
paragraph: (2) Consistent with, and in furtherance of, the primary objective, the Minister shall

heading: Ancillary objectives
paragraph: (a) support sustainable development designed to enable the needs of the present to be met without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs;

heading: Ancillary objectives
paragraph: (b) seek to minimize health and environmental risks posed by pest control products and encourage the development and implementation of innovative, sustainable pest management strategies by facilitating access to pest control products that pose lower risks and by other appropriate measures;

heading: Ancillary objectives
paragraph: (c) encourage public awareness in relation to pest control products by informing the public, facilitating public access to relevant information and public participation in the decision-making process; and

heading: Ancillary objectives
paragraph: (d) ensure that only those pest control products that are determined to be of acceptable value are approved for use in Canada.

heading: Protection of future generations
paragraph: 4.1 For greater certainty, protection and consideration afforded to children in this Act shall also extend to future generations.

heading: Establishment
paragraph: 5 (1) In carrying out duties under this Act, the Minister may establish an advisory council of persons whose interests and concerns are affected by this Act, and may specify the functions of the council and the means by which it is to perform those functions.

heading: Report to Minister
paragraph: (2) The advisory council shall give any report that it makes, including its recommendations and the reasons for them, to the Minister, who shall place it in the Register.

heading: Unregistered pest control products
paragraph: 6 (1) No person shall manufacture, possess, handle, store, transport, import, distribute or use a pest control product that is not registered under this Act, except as otherwise authorized under subsection 21(5) or 41(1), section 48 or 51, any of sections 53 to 59 or the regulations.

heading: Conditions of registration
paragraph: (2) Except as otherwise authorized under section 53.3 or 54, no person shall manufacture, import, export or distribute a registered pest control product unless it conforms to the conditions of registration respecting its composition and the person complies with the other conditions of registration.

heading: Packaging and labelling
paragraph: (3) Except as otherwise authorized under section 53, 53.3 or 54, no person shall store, import, export or distribute a pest control product that is not packaged and labelled in accordance with the regulations and, if it is registered, the conditions of registration.

heading: Misuse of pest control products
paragraph: (5) No person shall handle, store, transport, use or dispose of a pest control product in a way that is inconsistent with

heading: Misuse of pest control products
paragraph: (a) the regulations; or

heading: Misuse of pest control products
paragraph: (b) if the product is registered, the directions on the label recorded in the Register, subject to the regulations.

heading: Packaging, labelling and advertisement
paragraph: (7) No person shall package, label or advertise a pest control product in a way that is false, misleading or likely to create an erroneous impression regarding its character, value, quantity, composition, safety or registration.

heading: Activities that endanger health, etc.
paragraph: (8) No person shall manufacture, possess, handle, store, transport, distribute, use or dispose of a pest control product in a way that endangers human health or safety or the environment.

heading: Alteration, destruction or falsification - required documents
paragraph: (8.1) No person shall alter, destroy or falsify a document that they are required under this Act to keep, maintain or provide.

heading: Alteration, possession or use - official documents
paragraph: (8.2) It is prohibited for a person to

heading: Alteration, possession or use - official documents
paragraph: (a) alter a document issued or made - or in any manner given - under this Act; or

heading: Alteration, possession or use - official documents
paragraph: (b) have in their possession, or use, a document issued or made - or in any manner given - under this Act that has been altered.

heading: Possession or use of documents that resemble official documents
paragraph: (8.3) It is prohibited for a person to have in their possession, or use, any document that has not been issued or made - or in any manner given - under this Act if the document so resembles a document issued or made - or in any manner given - under this Act that it is likely to be mistaken for such a document.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (9) A person who contravenes any provision of this section is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Application to Minister
paragraph: 7 (1) An application to register a pest control product or to amend the product's registration must be made to the Minister in the form and manner directed by the Minister and must include any information or other thing that is required by the regulations to accompany the application.

heading: Use of information provided by registrants
paragraph: (2) If the Minister determines that the active ingredient of the applicant's pest control product is equivalent to the active ingredient of a registered pest control product, the Minister shall, subject to and in accordance with the regulations, permit the applicant to use or rely on any information referred to in subsection (1) that has been provided by any registrant if the Minister is satisfied that the information

heading: Use of information provided by registrants
paragraph: (a) is relevant to the registered pest control product that contains the equivalent active ingredient; and

heading: Use of information provided by registrants
paragraph: (b) is necessary to support the application.

heading: Foreign review or evaluation
paragraph: (2.1) For the purposes of subsection (1), the applicant may include information that is available from a review or evaluation of a pest control product conducted by the government of another member country of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development if the proposed use of the pest control product in Canada would be under conditions similar to those under which the foreign review or evaluation was conducted.

heading: Evaluation of pest control product
paragraph: (3) If the Minister is satisfied that the application has been made in accordance with subsection (1), (2) or (2.1), the Minister shall

heading: Evaluation of pest control product
paragraph: (a) in accordance with the regulations, if any, conduct any evaluations that the Minister considers necessary with respect to the health or environmental risks or the value of the pest control product;

heading: Evaluation of pest control product
paragraph: (b) expedite evaluations with respect to a pest control product that may reasonably be expected to pose lower health or environmental risks; and

heading: Evaluation of pest control product
paragraph: (c) carry out any consultation required by section 28.

heading: Other information
paragraph: (4) The Minister may, by delivering a notice in writing, request an applicant to provide the Minister with other information in support of the application within the time and in the form specified in the notice.

heading: Denial of application
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall deny an application if the applicant does not comply with a notice under subsection (4).

heading: Burden of persuasion and consideration of information
paragraph: (6) During an evaluation,

heading: Burden of persuasion and consideration of information
paragraph: (a) the applicant has the burden of persuading the Minister that the health and environmental risks and the value of the pest control product are acceptable; and

heading: Burden of persuasion and consideration of information
paragraph: (b) the Minister shall consider the information provided by the applicant in support of the application and may consider additional information, but the Minister shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of the additional information before completing the evaluation.

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (7) In evaluating the health and environmental risks of a pest control product and in determining whether those risks are acceptable, the Minister shall

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (a) apply a scientifically based approach; and

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (b) in relation to health risks, if a decision referred to in paragraph 28(1)(a) or (b) is being made or has been made in relation to a pest control product,

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (i) among other relevant factors, consider available information on aggregate exposure to the pest control product, namely dietary exposure and exposure from other non-occupational sources, including drinking water and use in and around homes and schools, and cumulative effects of the pest control product and other pest control products that have a common mechanism of toxicity,

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (ii) apply appropriate margins of safety to take into account, among other relevant factors, the use of animal experimentation data and the different sensitivities to pest control products of major identifiable subgroups, including pregnant women, infants, children, women and seniors, and

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (iii) in the case of a threshold effect, if the product is proposed for use in or around homes or schools, apply a margin of safety that is ten times greater than the margin of safety that would otherwise be applicable under subparagraph (ii) in respect of that threshold effect, to take into account potential pre- and post-natal toxicity and completeness of the data with respect to the exposure of, and toxicity to, infants and children unless, on the basis of reliable scientific data, the Minister has determined that a different margin of safety would be appropriate.

heading: Government policy to be given effect in evaluation
paragraph: (8) In evaluating the health and environmental risks and the value of a pest control product, the Minister shall give effect to government policy.

heading: Comparative risk and value assessment
paragraph: (9) In determining whether the health and environmental risks and the value of a pest control product are acceptable, the Minister may, in accordance with the regulations, if any, take into account information regarding the risks and value of other pest control products that are registered for the same use.

heading: Representations
paragraph: (10) For the purposes of subsection (9), the Minister shall, before making the determination, give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of the information referred to in that subsection.

heading: Registration or amendment
paragraph: 8 (1) If the Minister considers that the health and environmental risks and the value of the pest control product are acceptable after any required evaluations and consultations have been completed, the Minister shall register the product or amend its registration in accordance with the regulations, if any, by

heading: Registration or amendment
paragraph: (a) specifying the conditions relating to its manufacture, handling, storage, transport, import, export, packaging, distribution, use or disposition, including conditions relating to its composition, and, subject to subsection (2), the conditions relating to its label;

heading: Registration or amendment
paragraph: (b) assigning a registration number to the product in the case of a new registration and, where the Minister considers it appropriate, in the case of an amendment; and

heading: Registration or amendment
paragraph: (c) specifying the period for which the registration or amended registration is valid, which period may be either finite or indefinite.

heading: Conditions relating to label
paragraph: (2) The Minister may specify conditions relating to the label of a pest control product, otherwise than in accordance with the regulations, if the Minister is satisfied that the purposes of this Act can be met by so doing.

heading: Provision of safety information to workplaces
paragraph: (3) Without limiting the generality of paragraph (1)(a), the Minister shall specify, as a condition of registration, the requirement for product safety information, including a material safety data sheet for the product, to be provided to workplaces where the pest control product is used or manufactured, in accordance with the regulations made under paragraph 67(1)(s).

heading: Denial of application
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall deny an application referred to in subsection 7(1) if the Minister does not consider that the health or environmental risks of a pest control product are, or its value is, acceptable.

heading: Sales data
paragraph: (5) A registrant of a pest control product shall, as a condition of registration, record, retain and report to the Minister information on sales of the product in the form and manner directed by the Minister and in accordance with the regulations made under paragraph 67(1)(u).

heading: Former registrants
paragraph: (6) The obligation under subsection (5) to retain and report sales information in respect of a pest control product continues to apply to a former registrant after that product ceases to be registered.

heading: Specification at time of registration decision
paragraph: 9 When making a decision regarding the registration of a pest control product, the Minister shall, if necessary, specify any maximum residue limits for the product or for its components or derivatives that the Minister considers appropriate in the circumstances.

heading: Specification for unregistered products and uses
paragraph: 10 (1) The Minister may specify maximum residue limits for an unregistered pest control product or its components or derivatives, or for a registered pest control product or its components or derivatives with respect to a use that is not provided for by its registration, whether or not an application under subsection (2) is made for that purpose.

heading: Application for specification
paragraph: (2) Any person may make an application to the Minister to specify maximum residue limits pursuant to subsection (1). Section 7, with any necessary modifications, applies to that application.

heading: Evaluation of health risks
paragraph: (3) When specifying maximum residue limits for a pest control product or its components or derivatives pursuant to subsection (1), the Minister shall evaluate only the health risks of the product or its components or derivatives.

heading: Health risks to be considered acceptable
paragraph: 11 (1) The health risks associated with maximum residue limits specified by the Minister under sections 9 and 10 must be considered to be acceptable by the Minister.

heading: Relevant factors
paragraph: (2) If a decision referred to in paragraph 28(1)(a) or (b) is being made or has been made in relation to a pest control product, the Minister shall, in evaluating and determining whether the health risks associated with maximum residue limits for that pest control product or its components or derivatives are acceptable under subsection (1),

heading: Relevant factors
paragraph: (a) among other relevant factors, consider available information on

heading: Relevant factors
paragraph: (i) aggregate exposure to the pest control product, namely dietary exposure and exposure from other non-occupational sources, including drinking water and use in and around homes and schools,

heading: Relevant factors
paragraph: (ii) cumulative effects of the pest control product and other pest control products that have a common mechanism of toxicity, and

heading: Relevant factors
paragraph: (iii) the different sensitivities to pest control products of major identifiable subgroups, including pregnant women, infants, children, women and seniors; and

heading: Relevant factors
paragraph: (b) in the case of a threshold effect, apply a margin of safety that is ten times greater than the margin of safety that would otherwise be applicable under subparagraph 7(7)(b)(ii) or 19(2)(b)(ii) in respect of that threshold effect, to take into account potential pre- and post-natal toxicity and completeness of the data with respect to the exposure of, and toxicity to, infants and children, unless, on the basis of reliable scientific data, the Minister has determined that a different margin of safety would be appropriate.

heading: Additional information
paragraph: 12 (1) The Minister may, by delivering a notice in writing, require a registrant

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (a) to compile information, conduct tests and monitor experience with the pest control product for the purpose of obtaining additional information with respect to its effects on human health and safety or the environment or with respect to its value; and

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (b) to report the additional information to the Minister within the time and in the form specified in the notice.

heading: Condition of registration
paragraph: (2) A requirement under subsection (1) is a condition of registration.

heading: Mandatory reporting
paragraph: 13 An applicant for registration of a pest control product, a person who makes an application under subsection 10(2) or a registrant shall report any prescribed information that relates to the health or environmental risks or the value of the pest control product to the Minister within the prescribed time and in the form and manner directed by the Minister.

heading: Determination by Minister
paragraph: 14 After considering any information reported under section 12 or 13, the Minister shall determine whether a special review of the registration of the pest control product should be initiated.

heading: Public availability
paragraph: 15 After considering any information reported under section 13, the Minister shall place his or her conclusions in the Register and shall make public those conclusions if, in the Minister's opinion,

heading: Public availability
paragraph: (a) the pest control product poses a significant health or environmental risk; or

heading: Public availability
paragraph: (b) it is in the public interest to do so.

heading: Minister's discretion to initiate re-evaluation
paragraph: 16 (1) The Minister may initiate the re-evaluation of a registered pest control product if the Minister considers that, since the product was registered, there has been a change in the information required, or the procedures used, for the evaluation of the health or environmental risks or the value of pest control products of the same class or kind.

heading: Minister required to initiate re-evaluation
paragraph: (2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1),

heading: Minister required to initiate re-evaluation
paragraph: (a) if a decision of a type referred to in paragraph 28(1)(a) or (b) was made in relation to a pest control product on or after April 1, 1995, the Minister shall initiate a re-evaluation of that product no later than one year after 15 years have elapsed since the most recent decision of that type; and

heading: Minister required to initiate re-evaluation
paragraph: (b) if the most recent decision of a type referred to in paragraph 28(1)(a) or (b) was made in relation to a pest control product before April 1, 1995, the Minister shall initiate a re-evaluation of that product no later than April 1, 2005 or the date that is one year after 15 years have elapsed since that decision, whichever date is later.

heading: Notice requesting information
paragraph: (3) Re-evaluation of a pest control product is initiated by the Minister delivering a notice in writing to the registrant explaining the reasons for initiating the re-evaluation and, if considered necessary by the Minister, requiring the registrant to provide information in the form and within the period specified in the notice.

heading: Request for information from departments and provinces
paragraph: (4) After the re-evaluation is initiated, the Minister shall deliver a notice to federal and provincial government departments and agencies whose interests and concerns are affected by the federal regulatory system requesting them to provide, in the form and within the period specified in the notice, information in respect of the health and environmental risks and the value of the product that is under re-evaluation.

heading: Provision of information if more than one registrant
paragraph: (5) If there is more than one registrant whose registered pest control products have active ingredients that the Minister has determined to be equivalent,

heading: Provision of information if more than one registrant
paragraph: (a) two or more registrants may provide the information required under subsection (3) or paragraph 19(1)(a) jointly; and

heading: Provision of information if more than one registrant
paragraph: (b) if the Minister is satisfied that the information required under subsection (3) or paragraph 19(1)(a) has been provided by one or more registrants, the Minister shall, subject to and in accordance with the regulations, permit another registrant to use or rely on that information to meet the requirements under that subsection or paragraph.

heading: If active ingredients not equivalent
paragraph: (5.1) If the active ingredients of the registered pest control product that is subject to the re-evaluation are not equivalent to the active ingredients in another registrant's registered pest control product, the Minister shall, subject to and in accordance with the regulations, permit the registrant whose product is subject to the re-evaluation to use or rely on information provided by the other registrant if the Minister is satisfied that the information is necessary for the re-evaluation.

heading: Evaluation of pest control product
paragraph: (6) After the re-evaluation is initiated, the Minister shall, in accordance with the regulations, if any, conduct any evaluations that the Minister considers necessary with respect to the health or environmental risks or the value of the pest control product and shall carry out the consultations required by section 28.

heading: Initiation of special review by Minister
paragraph: 17 (1) The Minister shall initiate a special review of the registration of a pest control product if the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the health or environmental risks of the product are, or its value is, unacceptable.

heading: Special review where OECD ban
paragraph: (2) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), when a member country of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development prohibits all uses of an active ingredient for health or environmental reasons, the Minister shall initiate a special review of registered pest control products containing that active ingredient.

heading: Special review where information from department or province
paragraph: (3) Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), the Minister shall initiate a special review of the registration of a pest control product if a federal or provincial government department or agency has provided information to the Minister that relates to the health or environmental risks or the value of the product and if, after considering the information provided, the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the health or environmental risks of the product are, or its value is, unacceptable.

heading: Request for special review
paragraph: (4) Any person may request a special review of the registration of a pest control product by making a request to the Minister in the form and manner directed by the Minister.

heading: Decision
paragraph: (5) Within a reasonable time after receiving a request, the Minister shall decide whether to initiate a special review and shall respond to the request with written reasons for the decision.

heading: Scope of special review
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of this section, the Minister shall initiate a special review only in relation to the aspect of the pest control product that prompted the special review.

heading: Addition of aspect
paragraph: (7) If the Minister has initiated a re-evaluation of, or a special review in relation to, a pest control product, the Minister may, at any time before the decision statement is made public under subsection 28(5), expand the scope of the re-evaluation or special review to include any aspect of the product that would otherwise prompt a new special review under subsection (1), (2) or (3).

heading: New or amended consultation statement
paragraph: (8) If the Minister expands the scope of a re-evaluation or special review under subsection (7) after the consultation statement relating to the re-evaluation or special review has been made public under subsection 28(2), the Minister shall make public a new or amended consultation statement under that subsection that takes into account the aspect referred to in subsection (7).

heading: Discretion of Minister - aspect already covered
paragraph: 17.1 (1) Despite section 17, the Minister may decide not to initiate a special review in relation to a pest control product if a re-evaluation of, or a special review in relation to, the product has already been initiated that includes the aspect of the product that would otherwise prompt a special review.

heading: Discretion of Minister - previous decision statement
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection 17(2), the Minister may decide not to initiate a special review of a registered pest control product under that subsection if

heading: Discretion of Minister - previous decision statement
paragraph: (a) the Minister made public under subsection 28(5) a decision statement respecting a re-evaluation of, or a special review in relation to, that product;

heading: Discretion of Minister - previous decision statement
paragraph: (b) the aspect of the product that would otherwise prompt a special review was addressed by the re-evaluation or special review referred to in paragraph (a); and

heading: Discretion of Minister - previous decision statement
paragraph: (c) the Minister determines that there is no additional information in relation to the health or environmental risks of the product that provides the Minister with reasonable grounds to believe that those risks are unacceptable.

heading: Duty to make decisions public
paragraph: 17.2 The Minister shall make public each of the following decisions and the reasons for it:

heading: Duty to make decisions public
paragraph: (a) a decision made under subsection 17(7) to expand the scope of a re-evaluation or special review to include an aspect that would otherwise prompt a new special review under subsection 17(2);

heading: Duty to make decisions public
paragraph: (b) a decision made under subsection 17.1(1) or (2) not to initiate a special review in relation to an aspect that would otherwise prompt such a review under subsection 17(2).

heading: Notice requesting information
paragraph: 18 (1) A special review of a pest control product is initiated by the Minister delivering a notice in writing to the registrant explaining the reasons for initiating the special review and, if considered necessary by the Minister, requiring the registrant to provide information in the form and within the period specified in the notice.

heading: Request for information from departments and provinces
paragraph: (2) After the special review is initiated, the Minister shall deliver a notice to federal and provincial government departments and agencies whose interests and concerns are affected by the federal regulatory system requesting them to provide, in the form and within the period specified in the notice, information in respect of the health and environmental risks and the value of the product that is under special review.

heading: Provision of information if more than one registrant
paragraph: (3) If there is more than one registrant whose registered pest control products have active ingredients that the Minister has determined to be equivalent,

heading: Provision of information if more than one registrant
paragraph: (a) two or more registrants may provide the information required under subsection (1) or paragraph 19(1)(a) jointly; and

heading: Provision of information if more than one registrant
paragraph: (b) if the Minister is satisfied that the information required under subsection (1) or paragraph 19(1)(a) has been provided by one or more registrants, the Minister shall, subject to and in accordance with the regulations, permit another registrant to use or rely on that information to meet the requirements under that subsection or paragraph.

heading: If active ingredients not equivalent
paragraph: (3.1) If the active ingredients of a registered pest control product that is subject to the special review are not equivalent to the active ingredients in another registrant's registered pest control product, the Minister shall, subject to and in accordance with the regulations, permit the registrant whose product is subject to the special review to use or rely on information provided by the other registrant if the Minister is satisfied that the information is necessary for the special review.

heading: Evaluation of pest control product
paragraph: (4) After the special review is initiated, the Minister shall, in accordance with the regulations, if any, evaluate only the aspects of the pest control product that are within the scope of the special review and shall carry out the consultations required by section 28.

heading: Burden of persuasion and consideration of information
paragraph: 19 (1) During an evaluation that is done in the course of a re-evaluation or special review,

heading: Burden of persuasion and consideration of information
paragraph: (a) the Minister may, by delivering a notice in writing, require the registrant to provide, in the form and within the period specified in the notice, additional information that the Minister considers necessary for the evaluation;

heading: Burden of persuasion and consideration of information
paragraph: (b) the registrant has the burden of persuading the Minister that the health and environmental risks and the value of the pest control product are acceptable; and

heading: Burden of persuasion and consideration of information
paragraph: (c) the Minister shall consider the information provided by the registrant in support of the product and may consider any additional information, but the Minister shall give the registrant a reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of the additional information before completing the evaluation.

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (2) In evaluating the health and environmental risks of a pest control product and in determining whether those risks are acceptable, the Minister shall

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (a) apply a scientifically based approach; and

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (b) in relation to health risks,

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (i) among other relevant factors, consider available information on aggregate exposure to the pest control product, namely dietary exposure and exposure from other non-occupational sources, including drinking water and use in and around homes and schools, and cumulative effects of the pest control product and other pest control products that have a common mechanism of toxicity,

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (ii) apply appropriate margins of safety to take into account, among other relevant factors, the use of animal experimentation data and the different sensitivities to pest control products of major identifiable subgroups, including pregnant women, infants, children, women and seniors, and

heading: Scientific approach
paragraph: (iii) in the case of a threshold effect, if the product is used in or around homes or schools, apply a margin of safety that is ten times greater than the margin of safety that would otherwise be applicable under subparagraph (ii) in respect of that threshold effect, to take into account potential pre- and post-natal toxicity and completeness of the data with respect to the exposure of, and toxicity to, infants and children, unless, on the basis of reliable scientific data, the Minister has determined that a different margin of safety would be appropriate.

heading: Government policy to be given effect in evaluation
paragraph: (3) In evaluating the health and environmental risks and the value of a pest control product, the Minister shall give effect to government policy.

heading: Comparative risk and value assessment
paragraph: (4) In determining whether the health and environmental risks and the value of a pest control product are acceptable, the Minister may, in accordance with the regulations, if any, take into account information regarding the risks and value of other pest control products that are registered for the same use.

heading: Representations
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of subsection (4), the Minister shall, before making the determination, give any registrant whose product is under re-evaluation or special review a reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of the information referred to in that subsection.

heading: Cancellation or amendment
paragraph: 20 (1) The Minister may cancel or amend the registration of a pest control product if

heading: Cancellation or amendment
paragraph: (a) the registrant fails to satisfy a requirement under subsection 16(3) or 18(1) or paragraph 19(1)(a); or

heading: Cancellation or amendment
paragraph: (b) in the course of a re-evaluation or special review, the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the cancellation or amendment is necessary to deal with a situation that endangers human health or safety or the environment, taking into account the precautionary principle set out in subsection (2).

heading: Precautionary principle
paragraph: (2) Where there are threats of serious or irreversible damage, lack of full scientific certainty shall not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures to prevent adverse health impact or environmental degradation.

heading: Rescission of action
paragraph: (3) The Minister may rescind any action taken under subsection (1) if the circumstances that prompted it cease to exist.

heading: Refusal to consider applications
paragraph: (4) If the registration of a pest control product is cancelled or amended under paragraph (1)(a), the Minister may, for a prescribed period, refuse to consider any application made in respect of that product by the registrant.

heading: Confirmation
paragraph: 21 (1) If the Minister considers that the health and environmental risks and the value of a pest control product are acceptable after any required evaluations and consultations have been completed, the Minister shall confirm the registration.

heading: Amendment or cancellation
paragraph: (2) If the Minister does not consider that the health or environmental risks or value of a pest control product are acceptable, the Minister shall

heading: Amendment or cancellation
paragraph: (a) amend the registration if the Minister considers that the health and environmental risks and value of the product would be acceptable after the amendment; or

heading: Amendment or cancellation
paragraph: (b) cancel the registration.

heading: Delay of effective date
paragraph: (3) The Minister may delay the effective date of the amendment or cancellation if

heading: Delay of effective date
paragraph: (a) no suitable alternative to the use of the pest control product is available; and

heading: Delay of effective date
paragraph: (b) the Minister considers that the health and environmental risks and value of the product are acceptable until the effective date of the amendment or cancellation.

heading: Conditions on delay
paragraph: (4) A delay is subject to any conditions that the Minister considers necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

heading: Continued possession, etc., of existing stocks
paragraph: (5) When cancelling the registration of a pest control product under this section or any other provision of this Act, the Minister may

heading: Continued possession, etc., of existing stocks
paragraph: (a) allow the continued possession, handling, storage, distribution and use of stocks of the product in Canada at the time of cancellation, subject to any conditions, including disposal procedures, that the Minister considers necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Act;

heading: Continued possession, etc., of existing stocks
paragraph: (b) require the registrant to recall and dispose of the product in a manner specified by the Minister; or

heading: Continued possession, etc., of existing stocks
paragraph: (c) seize and dispose of the product.

heading: Discontinuation of sale of product
paragraph: 22 (1) A registrant who intends to discontinue the sale of a pest control product for one or more uses for which it is registered shall notify the Minister of that intention in the form and manner directed by the Minister.

heading: Reasons for discontinuation
paragraph: (2) The Minister may deliver a notice in writing to the registrant requiring the registrant to explain the reasons for the discontinuation.

heading: Cancellation or amendment of registration
paragraph: (3) On receipt of notification under subsection (1), the Minister shall cancel or amend the registration, as the case may be, as of a date to be determined by the Minister and, pending that date, may impose any conditions that the Minister considers necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

heading: Non-payment of fees, fines, etc.
paragraph: 23 (1) If a registrant fails to pay a fee, fine, penalty, charge or cost that the registrant is liable to pay under or in relation to this Act, the Minister may

heading: Non-payment of fees, fines, etc.
paragraph: (a) cancel or amend any registration in the registrant's name; and

heading: Non-payment of fees, fines, etc.
paragraph: (b) refuse to consider any application made by the registrant under this Act.

heading: Representations
paragraph: (2) Before taking any action under subsection (1) in relation to charges or costs, the Minister shall give the registrant a reasonable opportunity to make representations.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) The Minister shall immediately give written notice to the registrant of any action taken under subsection (1) and of the reasons for the action.

heading: Amendment with consent
paragraph: 24 The Minister may, with the written consent of the registrant, amend the registration of a pest control product for the purpose of reducing its health or environmental risks or increasing its value.

heading: Breach of conditions
paragraph: 25 The Minister may cancel or amend the registration of a pest control product if the registrant does not comply with the conditions of registration.

heading: Violation or offence
paragraph: 26 If a person is found to have committed a violation or is convicted of an offence under this Act, the Minister may, having regard to the nature of the violation or offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission,

heading: Violation or offence
paragraph: (a) cancel or amend the registration of the pest control product that was involved in the violation or offence where the person who committed the violation or offence is the registrant;

heading: Violation or offence
paragraph: (b) cancel or amend the registration of any other pest control product in respect of which the person is the registrant; or

heading: Violation or offence
paragraph: (c) refuse to consider any application made under this Act by the person during any period that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Implementation of international agreement
paragraph: 27 The Governor in Council may, by order, cancel or amend the registration of a pest control product or a class of pest control products if the Governor in Council considers it necessary to do so to implement an international agreement.

heading: Minister to consult
paragraph: 28 (1) The Minister shall consult the public and federal and provincial government departments and agencies whose interests and concerns are affected by the federal regulatory system before making a decision

heading: Minister to consult
paragraph: (a) to grant or deny an application

heading: Minister to consult
paragraph: (i) to register a pest control product that is or contains an unregistered active ingredient, or

heading: Minister to consult
paragraph: (ii) to register, or amend the registration of, a pest control product if the Minister considers that registration or amendment of the registration may result in significantly increased health or environmental risks;

heading: Minister to consult
paragraph: (b) about the registration of a pest control product on completion of a re-evaluation or special review; or

heading: Minister to consult
paragraph: (c) about any other matter if the Minister considers it in the public interest to do so.

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (2) To initiate a consultation under subsection (1), the Minister shall make public a consultation statement and shall invite any person to send written comments on the proposed decision within the period specified in the statement.

heading: Consultation statement
paragraph: (3) The consultation statement shall include

heading: Consultation statement
paragraph: (a) a summary of any reports of the evaluation of the health and environmental risks and the value of the pest control product prepared or considered by the Minister;

heading: Consultation statement
paragraph: (b) the proposed decision and the reasons for it; and

heading: Consultation statement
paragraph: (c) any other information that the Minister considers necessary in the public interest.

heading: Consideration of comments
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall consider any comments received pursuant to subsection (2) before making a decision.

heading: Decision statement
paragraph: (5) After making a decision, the Minister shall make public a decision statement that shall include the decision, the reasons for it and a summary of any comments that the Minister received on the proposed decision.

heading: Confidential test data
paragraph: (6) A consultation statement referred to in subsection (2) and a decision statement referred to in subsection (5) shall contain any confidential test data that the Minister considers to be in the public interest.

heading: Failure to report information
paragraph: 29 (1) Every person who does not comply with section 13 is guilty of an offence.

heading: Non-compliance with requirement
paragraph: (2) A registrant who does not comply with a requirement in a notice referred to in subsection 16(3) or 18(1), paragraph 19(1)(a) or subsection 22(2) is guilty of an offence.

heading: False or misleading information
paragraph: 30 (1) Every person is guilty of an offence if they knowingly provide the Minister with false or misleading information

heading: False or misleading information
paragraph: (a) about the health or environmental risks or the value of a pest control product; or

heading: False or misleading information
paragraph: (b) in response to a notice delivered under this Act.

heading: False or misleading tests
paragraph: (2) Every person is guilty of an offence if they falsely claim to have conducted a test relating to the health or environmental risks or the value of a pest control product, knowingly conduct such a test that is misleading or knowingly provide false or misleading information about such a test.

heading: Non-compliance with conditions of registration
paragraph: 31 (1) A registrant who does not comply with the conditions of registration is guilty of an offence.

heading: Non-compliance with other conditions and requirements
paragraph: (2) A person who does not comply with a condition imposed under subsection 21(4), paragraph 21(5)(a) or subsection 22(3) or with a requirement under paragraph 21(5)(b) is guilty of an offence.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: 32 Every person who commits an offence under any of sections 29 to 31 is liable
