heading: Punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Export control list
paragraph: 33 (1) The Governor in Council may, by order, establish a Pest Control Products Export Control List consisting of pest control products that meet the prescribed criteria.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (2) No person shall export a pest control product that is on the Pest Control Products Export Control List, except as authorized under this Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: (3) An application for authorization to export a pest control product must be made to the Minister in the form and manner directed by the Minister.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (4) The Minister may authorize an applicant to export a pest control product to a specified country if

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (a) the applicant satisfies the Minister that the prescribed requirements for the authorization are or will be met; and

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (b) the proposed export is not prohibited under any other Act of Parliament.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (5) The authorization is subject to any conditions that the Minister considers necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (6) The Minister shall give public notice of the authorization.

heading: Offence and punishment - subsection (2)
paragraph: (7) Every person who contravenes subsection (2) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment - subsection (2)
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment - subsection (2)
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Offence and punishment - false or misleading information
paragraph: (8) Every person who knowingly provides false or misleading information in connection with an authorization is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment - false or misleading information
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment - false or misleading information
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: 34 (1) The Minister may amend, suspend or cancel an authorization to export a pest control product if the Minister

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (a) has reasonable grounds to believe that a prescribed requirement of the authorization is not or will not be met;

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (b) has reasonable grounds to believe that the conditions to which the authorization is subject have not been or will not be met; or

heading: Amendment, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (c) becomes aware of additional information about the health or environmental risks of the pest control product.

heading: Representations
paragraph: (2) Before amending or cancelling an authorization or after suspending one, the Minister shall give the authorized person a reasonable opportunity to make representations.

heading: Decision
paragraph: (3) After considering any representations that may be made by the authorized person, the Minister shall reinstate, amend or cancel the authorization.

heading: Public notice
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall give public notice of the amendment or cancellation of an authorization.

heading: Notice of objection to registration decisions
paragraph: 35 (1) Any person may file with the Minister, in the form and manner directed by the Minister, a notice of objection to a decision referred to in paragraph 28(1)(a) or (b) within 60 days after the decision statement referred to in subsection 28(5) is made public.

heading: Notice of objection to authorization decisions
paragraph: (2) Any person may file with the Minister, in the form and manner directed by the Minister, a notice of objection to a decision to authorize the export of a pest control product or to amend or cancel an authorization within 60 days after a notice referred to in subsection 33(6) or 34(4) is made public.

heading: Establishment of review panel
paragraph: (3) After receiving a notice of objection, the Minister may, in accordance with the regulations, if any, establish a panel of one or more individuals to review the decision and to recommend whether the decision should be confirmed, reversed or varied.

heading: Notice of review panel
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall give public notice of the establishment of a review panel.

heading: Reasons to be provided if panel not established
paragraph: (5) If the Minister does not establish a panel, the Minister shall provide written reasons without delay to the person who filed the notice of objection.

heading: Terms of reference and procedure
paragraph: (6) The Minister may determine the terms of reference of a review panel and the procedure for the review, and may at any time change them.

heading: Representations
paragraph: (7) A review panel shall give any person a reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of the decision under review, in accordance with the terms of reference.

heading: Public access
paragraph: (8) Subject to subsections 44(3) and (6), the hearings of a review panel shall be open to the public.

heading: Information to be placed in Register
paragraph: (9) A review panel shall give the information submitted to it to the Minister, who shall place it in the Register.

heading: No automatic suspension of decisions
paragraph: 36 The filing of a notice of objection or the establishment of a review panel does not suspend the decision under review, but the Minister may suspend the decision until a final decision is made on completion of the review or until the review panel is dissolved.

heading: Withdrawal of notice of objection
paragraph: 37 The Minister may dissolve a review panel if all notices of objection are withdrawn by the persons who filed them.

heading: Report
paragraph: 38 (1) As soon as possible after the conclusion of a review, the review panel shall submit to the Minister a report stating its recommendations and the reasons for them.

heading: Register
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall place the review panel's report in the Register.

heading: Confirmation, reversal or variation of decision
paragraph: 39 (1) After considering the recommendations of a review panel, the Minister shall confirm, reverse or vary the decision under review, but the confirmation, reversal or variation must not result in the registration, either initial or continued, of a pest control product unless the Minister considers that its health and environmental risks and its value are acceptable.

heading: Public notice of decision
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall make public the confirmation, reversal or variation of the decision, the reasons for confirmation, reversal or variation and a summary of the information considered by the Minister, including any confidential test data that the Minister considers to be in the public interest.

heading: False or misleading tests or information
paragraph: 40 (1) Every person is guilty of an offence if they

heading: False or misleading tests or information
paragraph: (a) knowingly provide a review panel with false or misleading information about the health or environmental risks or the value of a pest control product; or

heading: False or misleading tests or information
paragraph: (b) falsely claim to have conducted a test relating to the health or environmental risks or value of a pest control product, knowingly conduct such a test that is misleading or knowingly provide false or misleading information about such a test.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: 41 (1) The Minister may, in accordance with the regulations and subject to any conditions that the Minister may specify, authorize a person to use an unregistered pest control product for a specified purpose.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall authorize the use of a pest control product if the Minister considers that use of the product for the specified purpose in accordance with any conditions specified does not pose unacceptable health or environmental risks.

heading: Suspension
paragraph: (3) The Minister shall suspend an authorization if the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the conditions to which the authorization is subject have not been or will not be met or that the continuance of the authorization poses unacceptable health or environmental risks.

heading: Representations
paragraph: (4) After suspending an authorization, the Minister shall give the authorized person a reasonable opportunity to make representations.

heading: Decision
paragraph: (5) After considering any representations that may be made by the authorized person, the Minister shall reinstate, amend or cancel the authorization.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (6) Every person who fails to comply with the conditions of an authorization issued under this section is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Provision of safety information
paragraph: 41.1 A person who is authorized by the regulations to import an unregistered pest control product solely for the purpose of export or for a prescribed purpose and who imports such a product for that purpose shall provide, in accordance with the regulations, to workplaces where the pest control product is handled or stored, product safety information for the product that complies with the prescribed requirements.

heading: Register
paragraph: 42 (1) The Minister shall establish and maintain a Register of Pest Control Products in accordance with the regulations, if any, that contains information about pest control products, including information about applications, registrations, re-evaluations and special reviews.

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (2) The Register shall contain the following information:

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (a) for each application to register or amend the registration of a pest control product,

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (i) the active ingredient of the product, proposed new uses for it or any uses proposed to be withdrawn, and

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (ii) how the application was disposed of or whether it was withdrawn;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (b) the conditions of registration, registration number and registration validity period for each registered pest control product;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (c) information, in respect of each registered pest control product, that is provided by applicants and registrants

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (i) in support of an application for registration or for the amendment of a registration, or

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (ii) for the purposes of a re-evaluation or special review;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (d) information provided by applicants and registrants that is used to specify maximum residue limits;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (e) information, in respect of each registered pest control product, that is considered by the Minister under paragraphs 7(6)(b) and 19(1)(c);

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (f) any reports of the evaluation of the health and environmental risks and the value of registered pest control products prepared by the Minister;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (g) any advice from a person or body referred to in paragraph 44(1)(f), unless disclosure of the advice may be refused under section 23 or 23.1 of the Access to Information Act;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (h) the status, including cancelled status, of all registrations to which this Act applies;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (i) information provided to the Minister pursuant to subsection 8(5);

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (j) notices delivered under subsections 12(1), 16(3) and 18(1) and paragraph 19(1)(a);

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (k) conclusions of the Minister that were made public under section 15;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (l) consultation statements and decision statements made public under subsections 28(2) and (5), respectively;

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (m) notices of objection filed under subsections 35(1) and (2), public notices given under subsection 35(4) and the Minister's decisions and reasons under subsections 35(5) and 39(2);

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (n) authorizations under sections 33 and 41 and amendments and cancellations under sections 34 and 41; and

heading: Contents of Register
paragraph: (o) any other information required by this Act or the regulations to be included in the Register.

heading: Evaluation reports
paragraph: (3) An evaluation report referred to in paragraph (2)(f) shall contain a summary of the information considered and shall contain any confidential test data and confidential business information that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Public access to information in the Register
paragraph: (4) The Minister shall allow the public to have access to, and copies of, any information in the Register that

heading: Public access to information in the Register
paragraph: (a) is not confidential test data or confidential business information; or

heading: Public access to information in the Register
paragraph: (b) is confidential test data that has been made subject to public disclosure in accordance with the regulations made under paragraph 67(1)(m).

heading: Access to evaluation reports
paragraph: (5) The Minister shall allow the public to obtain a copy of any evaluation report in the Register, except for any confidential business information that it contains.

heading: Means of access to information in Register
paragraph: (6) Information in the Register that the public may obtain a copy of under this Act or the regulations shall be made available to the public in as convenient a manner as practicable.

heading: Electronic public registry
paragraph: (7) The Minister shall establish an electronic public registry, which shall include

heading: Electronic public registry
paragraph: (a) the information referred to in subsection (6), as soon as reasonably practicable;

heading: Electronic public registry
paragraph: (b) memoranda of understanding among federal government departments relating to the regulation of pest control products;

heading: Electronic public registry
paragraph: (c) reports of international harmonization activities relating to the regulation of pest control products;

heading: Electronic public registry
paragraph: (d) regulations and proposed regulations under this Act when published in the Canada Gazette; and

heading: Electronic public registry
paragraph: (e) policies, guidelines and codes of practice relating to the regulation of pest control products when proposed for public consultation, and their final texts when adopted.

heading: Consultation with public
paragraph: 42.1 The public shall be consulted as to policies, guidelines and codes of practice relating to the regulation of pest control products.

heading: Confidential test data
paragraph: 43 (1) A person who wishes to inspect confidential test data in the Register must submit to the Minister

heading: Confidential test data
paragraph: (a) an application in the form and manner directed by the Minister; and

heading: Confidential test data
paragraph: (b) an affidavit made under oath or a statutory declaration under the Canada Evidence Act made before a commissioner for oaths or for taking affidavits, stating

heading: Confidential test data
paragraph: (i) the purpose of the inspection, and

heading: Confidential test data
paragraph: (ii) that the person does not intend to use the test data, or make the test data available to others, in order to register a pest control product in Canada or elsewhere or to amend a registration.

heading: Right to inspection
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall permit the person to inspect confidential test data in the Register if the Minister is satisfied that the person does not intend to

heading: Right to inspection
paragraph: (a) use the test data in order to register a pest control product in Canada or elsewhere, or to amend a registration; or

heading: Right to inspection
paragraph: (b) make the test data available to others for the purpose of registering a pest control product in Canada or elsewhere, or of amending a registration.

heading: Notice to registrant
paragraph: (2.1) If the Minister permits a person to inspect confidential test data in the Register, the Minister shall make a reasonable effort to immediately notify any registrant who provided the data that the Minister has permitted a person to inspect the data.

heading: Denial of application
paragraph: (3) The Minister shall deny an application if the Minister is satisfied that

heading: Denial of application
paragraph: (a) the applicant intends to use the test data for a purpose referred to in subsection (2); or

heading: Denial of application
paragraph: (b) the applicant has used test data obtained from a prior inspection for a purpose referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Confidential business information
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsections (5) and (6), confidential business information is information provided under this Act that is designated as confidential business information by the person who provided it, or information provided under the Pest Control Products Act, chapter P-9 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985, and that concerns

heading: Confidential business information
paragraph: (a) manufacturing or quality control processes relating to a pest control product;

heading: Confidential business information
paragraph: (b) methods for determining the composition of a pest control product; or

heading: Confidential business information
paragraph: (c) the monetary value of sales of pest control products provided to the Minister pursuant to subsection 8(5) and other financial or commercial information provided to the Minister pursuant to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Formulants and contaminants
paragraph: (5) Unless otherwise excluded by the regulations, if any, made under paragraph 67(1)(n), confidential business information also includes information that

heading: Formulants and contaminants
paragraph: (a) is provided under this Act and is designated as confidential business information by the person who provided it or was provided under the Pest Control Products Act, chapter P-9 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1985; and

heading: Formulants and contaminants
paragraph: (b) contains the identity and concentration of the formulants and contaminants in a pest control product, other than those that the Minister considers to be of health or environmental concern and are identified on a list to be established and maintained by the Minister and made available to the public.

heading: Designation not satisfactory
paragraph: (6) If the Minister decides that information designated under subsection (4) or (5) does not meet the requirements of that subsection, the information is not confidential business information for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (7) If the Minister decides that designated information is not confidential business information, the Minister shall give written notice to the person who provided the information of the decision and the reasons for it.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (8) Nothing in this Act shall be construed as

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) preventing the Minister from refusing to disclose confidential test data or confidential business information under the Access to Information Act; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) entitling a person to make or obtain a copy of confidential test data, other than confidential test data to which the public has access

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (i) in documents referred to in subsections 28(6), 39(2) and 42(3), or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (ii) under the authority of the regulations made under paragraph 67(1)(m).

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (9) Every person who makes a false statement in an affidavit or a statutory declaration referred to in subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Permitted disclosure
paragraph: 44 (1) The Minister may, in accordance with the regulations, if any, disclose confidential test data or confidential business information that has been provided under this Act or is in the Register to

heading: Permitted disclosure
paragraph: (a) any person who provides services to Her Majesty in right of Canada for the purpose of protecting human health or safety or the environment;

heading: Permitted disclosure
paragraph: (b) an international organization or the government of a province or a country that is a party to an agreement with Her Majesty in right of Canada or an agent of Her Majesty, relating to the exchange of information about pest control products;

heading: Permitted disclosure
paragraph: (c) a medical professional who requests the information for the purpose of making a medical diagnosis or giving medical treatment to an individual;

heading: Permitted disclosure
paragraph: (d) a department or an agency of the federal or a provincial government that requests the information in order to respond to a situation that endangers human health or safety or the environment;

heading: Permitted disclosure
paragraph: (e) a review panel established by the Minister under subsection 35(3); or

heading: Permitted disclosure
paragraph: (f) any other person or body, including an advisory council established under subsection 5(1), from whom the Minister requests advice for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Protection of disclosed information
paragraph: (2) Before disclosing information under paragraph (1)(b), the Minister must be satisfied that the party to the agreement, other than Her Majesty in right of Canada or an agent of Her Majesty, can provide protection from unfair commercial use or disclosure of the information that is consistent with the protection provided under this Act.

heading: Prohibition against disclosure
paragraph: (3) No person shall disclose information obtained under subsection (1) unless authorized by the person who provided the information to the Minister or unless authorized under the Access to Information Act, this Act or the regulations.

heading: Prohibition against use
paragraph: (4) No person shall use information obtained under subsection (1) for any purpose other than the purpose for which it was obtained, unless authorized by the person who provided the information to the Minister.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (5) Every person who contravenes subsection (3) or (4) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Security measures
paragraph: (6) Every person who obtains information under subsection (1) shall comply with any prescribed security measures and take all reasonable precautions to avoid any prohibited disclosure of the information.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (7) Every person who contravenes subsection (6) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Appointment
paragraph: 45 (1) Subject to subsection (2), inspectors and analysts shall be appointed for the purposes of this Act and the regulations in accordance with the Public Service Employment Act.

heading: Designation of inspectors and analysts
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of the administration and enforcement of this Act, the Minister may designate individuals or classes of individuals as inspectors or analysts to exercise powers or perform duties or functions in relation to any matter referred to in the designation, but

heading: Designation of inspectors and analysts
paragraph: (a) no individual who is employed in a department other than the Department of Health may be designated without the approval of the minister responsible for the department in which the individual is employed; and

heading: Designation of inspectors and analysts
paragraph: (b) no individual who is employed by the government of a province may be designated without the approval of that government.

heading: Inspector's certificate of designation
paragraph: (3) An inspector shall be provided with a certificate in a form established by the Minister certifying the inspector's designation and, on entering any place under the authority of this Act, the inspector shall show the certificate to the person in charge of the place if the person requests proof of the designation.

heading: Obstruction of inspectors
paragraph: 46 (1) No person shall resist or obstruct an inspector or make a false or misleading statement either orally or in writing to an inspector who is exercising powers or performing duties or functions under this Act.

heading: Inspection of records
paragraph: (2) A person who is required by this Act or the regulations to keep records shall make them available to an inspector on request.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (3) Every person who contravenes this section is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Report of contravention
paragraph: 47 (1) A person who knows about a contravention of this Act or the regulations, or the reasonable likelihood of such a contravention, may report any information relating to the contravention to an inspector.

heading: Confidentiality
paragraph: (2) When making a report, the person may request that their identity and any information that could reasonably reveal their identity not be disclosed, and no person shall disclose or permit the disclosure of that identity or information unless the person who made the request authorizes the disclosure in writing.

heading: Protection of individual
paragraph: (3) Despite any other Act of Parliament, no person shall dismiss, suspend, demote, discipline, deny a benefit of employment to, harass or otherwise disadvantage an individual for having

heading: Protection of individual
paragraph: (a) made a report under subsection (1);

heading: Protection of individual
paragraph: (b) refused or stated an intention of refusing to do anything that the individual reasonably believed was or would be a contravention under this Act; or

heading: Protection of individual
paragraph: (c) done or stated an intention of doing anything that the individual reasonably believed was required by or under this Act.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (4) Every person who contravenes subsection (2) or (3) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: 48 (1) For a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with the provisions of this Act and the regulations, an inspector may

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (a) subject to section 49, at any reasonable time, enter and inspect any place, or stop any means of transport, in which the inspector believes on reasonable grounds there is a pest control product or other thing to which this Act or the regulations apply;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (b) open and examine any receptacle, package or other thing that the inspector believes on reasonable grounds contains a pest control product or other thing to which this Act or the regulations apply and take samples from it;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (c) order any person to present any pest control product or other thing for inspection in any manner and under any conditions that the inspector considers necessary to conduct an inspection;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d) order the owner or person having possession, care or control of a means of transport that the inspector intends to enter, to move it to a place where the inspector can enter it;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.1) examine or test, or take samples of, anything that is in the place being inspected;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.2) examine a document that is in the place being inspected, make copies of it or take extracts from it;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.3) order the owner or person having possession, care or control of a pest control product or other thing to which this Act or the regulations apply that is in the place being inspected to move it or, for any time that may be necessary, not to move it or to restrict its movement;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.4) use or cause to be used a computer or other device that is in the place being inspected to examine data that is contained in or available to a computer system or reproduce it or cause it to be reproduced in the form of a printout or other intelligible output and remove the output for examination or copying;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.5) use or cause to be used copying equipment that is in the place being inspected and remove the copies for examination;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.6) take photographs or make recordings or sketches;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.7) order any person in the place being inspected to establish their identity to the inspector's satisfaction;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.8) prohibit or limit access to all or part of the place being inspected or to anything that is in the place;

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (d.9) remove anything from the place being inspected for the purpose of examination, conducting tests or taking samples; and

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (e) conduct any tests or analyses or take any measurements.

heading: Persons accompanying inspector
paragraph: (2) An inspector may be accompanied by any person that they believe is necessary to help them exercise their powers or perform their duties or functions under this section.

heading: Entering private property
paragraph: (3) An inspector and any person accompanying them may enter and pass through private property, other than a dwelling house on that property, in order to gain entry to a place referred to in paragraph (1)(a).

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (4) Every person who fails to do anything the person was ordered to do by an inspector under paragraphs (1)(c), (d), (d.3) or (d.7) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Warrant required to enter dwelling-place
paragraph: 49 (1) An inspector may not enter a dwelling-place except with the consent of its occupant or under the authority of a warrant.

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (2) If on ex parte application a justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) the conditions for entry described in section 48 exist in relation to a dwelling-place,

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) entry to the dwelling-place is necessary for a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with the provisions of this Act and the regulations, and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (c) entry to the dwelling-place has been refused or there are reasonable grounds to believe that entry will be refused,

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: the justice may at any time sign and issue a warrant authorizing the inspector named in it to enter and inspect the dwelling-place, subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (3) An inspector who executes a warrant shall not use force unless he or she is accompanied by a peace officer and the use of force is specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Means of telecommunication
paragraph: (4) An application for a warrant under subsection (2) may be submitted, and the warrant may be issued, by a means of telecommunication and section 487.1 of the Criminal Code applies for those purposes with any necessary modifications.

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: 50 (1) The owner or the person in charge of a place entered by an inspector under section 48 or 49 and any person found in the place shall

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: (a) give the inspector all reasonable assistance in their power to enable the inspector to exercise powers or perform duties or functions under the provisions of this Act or the regulations; and

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: (b) provide the inspector with any information relevant to the administration of the provisions of this Act or the regulations that the inspector may reasonably require.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who contravenes subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Production of documents, information or samples
paragraph: 51 (1) An inspector may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with the provisions of this Act and the regulations, order a person to provide, on the date, at the time and place and in the manner specified by the inspector, any document, information or sample specified by the inspector.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who fails to do anything the person was ordered to do by an inspector under subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Inspector may seize
paragraph: 52 An inspector may seize and detain any pest control product or other thing that the inspector has reasonable grounds to believe

heading: Inspector may seize
paragraph: (a) was used in a contravention of a provision of this Act or the regulations;

heading: Inspector may seize
paragraph: (b) is something in relation to which a provision of this Act or the regulations was contravened; or

heading: Inspector may seize
paragraph: (c) was obtained by the contravention of a provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Storage, movement and disposition
paragraph: 53 (1) An inspector may, in respect of a pest control product or other thing seized under this Act,

heading: Storage, movement and disposition
paragraph: (a) on notice to its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure or to the owner or person responsible for the place where it was seized, store it or move it at the expense of the person to whom the notice is given;

heading: Storage, movement and disposition
paragraph: (b) order its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure or the owner or person responsible for the place where it was seized to store it or move it at the expense of the person being so ordered;

heading: Storage, movement and disposition
paragraph: (c) if the pest control product or other thing is perishable, order its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure to dispose of it at the expense of the person being so ordered or, on notice to its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure, dispose of it at the expense of the person to whom the notice is given; or

heading: Storage, movement and disposition
paragraph: (d) if the inspector is of the opinion that the pest control product or other thing endangers human health or safety or the environment and that its disposition is necessary to respond to the danger, order its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure to dispose of it, despite subsection 6(8), at the expense of the person being so ordered or, on notice to its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure, dispose of it, despite subsection 6(8), at the expense of the person to whom the notice is given.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) An order under paragraph (1)(c) or (d) shall be communicated by delivering a written notice to the owner or person and the notice

heading: Notice
paragraph: (a) must include a statement of the reasons for the order; and

heading: Notice
paragraph: (b) may specify the period within which and the manner in which the pest control product or other thing is to be disposed.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (3) Every person who fails to do anything the person was ordered to do by an inspector under paragraph (1)(b), (c) or (d) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Interference with seized things
paragraph: (4) Except with the authorization of an inspector, no person shall move, alter or interfere with a pest control product or other thing seized under this Act.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (5) Every person who contravenes subsection (4) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Release of seized thing
paragraph: 53.1 If an inspector is satisfied that the provisions of this Act and the regulations that apply with respect to a pest control product or other thing seized under this Act have been complied with, the product or thing must be released.

heading: Application for return
paragraph: 53.2 (1) Subject to subsection 55(1), if proceedings are instituted in relation to a pest control product or other thing seized under this Act, its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure may apply, in the case of a violation, to the Review Tribunal continued by subsection 27(1) of the Agriculture and Agri-Food Administrative Monetary Penalties Act or, in the case of an offence, to the court before which the proceedings are being held, for an order that the thing be returned.

heading: Order for return
paragraph: (2) If the Review Tribunal or court, as the case may be, is satisfied that sufficient evidence exists or may reasonably be obtained without the continued detention of the pest control product or other thing, the Tribunal or court may order it to be returned to the applicant, subject to any conditions the Tribunal or court may impose to ensure that it is preserved for any purpose for which it may subsequently be required.

heading: Unlawful imports
paragraph: 53.3 (1) An inspector who has reasonable grounds to believe that an imported pest control product does not meet the requirements of the regulations or was imported in contravention of a provision of this Act or the regulations may decide whether to give the owner or importer, or the person having possession, care or control of the product, the opportunity to take a measure in respect of it.

heading: Factors
paragraph: (2) In making a decision under subsection (1), the inspector shall consider, among other factors

heading: Factors
paragraph: (a) whether the pest control product endangers human health or safety or the environment; and

heading: Factors
paragraph: (b) any other prescribed factors.

heading: Duty of inspector
paragraph: (3) If the inspector decides under subsection (1) not to give the owner or importer or the person having possession, care or control of the pest control product the opportunity to take a measure in respect of it, the inspector shall exercise, in respect of the product, any of the powers conferred by the provisions of this Act, other than this section, or of the regulations.

heading: Measures that may be taken and notice
paragraph: (4) However, if the inspector decides under subsection (1) to give the owner or importer, or the person having possession, care or control of the pest control product the opportunity to take a measure in respect of it, the inspector, or any other inspector who is informed of the decision, shall decide whether the owner or importer, or the person having possession, care or control of it may remove it from Canada at their expense, consent to its forfeiture or take either of these measures, and shall notify or cause to be notified the owner or importer, or the person having possession, care or control of the product that they may take that measure within the period specified by the inspector or other inspector, as the case may be.

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: (5) If a person is notified under subsection (4) that they may consent to the forfeiture of the pest control product and the person consents to its forfeiture, the product is forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be disposed of, as the Minister may direct, at the person's expense.

heading: Removal or destruction of unlawful imports
paragraph: 54 (1) An inspector who has reasonable grounds to believe that an imported pest control product does not meet the requirements of the regulations or was imported in contravention of a provision of this Act or the regulations may, by written notice, whether the pest control product is seized or not, order its owner or importer, or the person having possession, care or control of it, to remove it from Canada at their expense or, if removal is not possible, to destroy it at their expense.

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: (2) If the pest control product is not removed from Canada, or destroyed, within the period specified in the notice - or, if no period is specified, within 90 days after the day on which the notice was delivered - it is, despite section 53.1, forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be disposed of, as the Minister may direct, at the expense of the person to whom the notice was delivered.

heading: Suspension of application of subsection (2)
paragraph: (3) An inspector may, for the period specified by the inspector, suspend the application of subsection (2) if the inspector is satisfied that

heading: Suspension of application of subsection (2)
paragraph: (a) the pest control product does not endanger human health or safety or the environment;

heading: Suspension of application of subsection (2)
paragraph: (b) the pest control product will not be sold within that period;

heading: Suspension of application of subsection (2)
paragraph: (c) the measures that should have been taken for the pest control product not to have been imported in contravention of a provision of this Act or the regulations will be taken within that period; and

heading: Suspension of application of subsection (2)
paragraph: (d) if the pest control product does not meet the requirements of the regulations, it will be brought into compliance with those requirements within that period.

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (4) An inspector may cancel the notice if the inspector is satisfied that

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (a) the pest control product does not endanger human health or safety or the environment;

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (b) the pest control product has not been sold within the period referred to in subsection (5);

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (c) the measures referred to in paragraph (3)(c) were taken within that period; and

heading: Cancellation
paragraph: (d) if the pest control product did not meet the requirements of the regulations when it was imported, it was brought into compliance with those requirements within that period.

heading: Period
paragraph: (5) The period for the purposes of subsection (4) is

heading: Period
paragraph: (a) if the application of subsection (2) was suspended under subsection (3), the period of the suspension; and

heading: Period
paragraph: (b) if the application of subsection (2) was not suspended, the period specified in the notice or, if no period was specified, the period of 90 days after the day on which the notice was delivered.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (6) Every person who fails to comply with an order in the notice is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Unclaimed pest control products or other things
paragraph: 54.1 (1) A pest control product or other thing seized under this Act is, at the Minister's election, forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada if

heading: Unclaimed pest control products or other things
paragraph: (a) within 60 days after the seizure, no person is identified in accordance with the regulations, if any, as its owner or as the person who is entitled to possess it; or

heading: Unclaimed pest control products or other things
paragraph: (b) its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure does not claim it within 60 days after the day on which they are notified that an inspector has released it.

heading: Proceedings instituted
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if proceedings are instituted for a violation or an offence that relates to the seized pest control product or other thing.

heading: Disposition
paragraph: (3) A seized pest control product or other thing that is forfeited under subsection (1) may be disposed of, as the Minister may direct, at the expense of its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure.

heading: Forfeiture on consent
paragraph: 55 (1) At the election of Her Majesty in right of Canada, a pest control product or other thing seized under this Act by an inspector is forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada if the owner consents to its forfeiture. The pest control product or other thing that is forfeited may be disposed of, as the Minister directs, at the owner's expense.

heading: Forfeiture by court order
paragraph: (2) If the Review Tribunal, continued by subsection 27(1) of the Agriculture and Agri-Food Administrative Monetary Penalties Act, decides that a person has committed a violation, or if an offender is convicted of an offence under this Act, the Tribunal or the court, as the case may be, may, in addition to imposing a penalty or punishment, order that the pest control product or other thing that was involved in the violation or offence be forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada, regardless of whether the product or thing was seized under this Act or not.

heading: Directions of Minister
paragraph: (3) A pest control product or other thing that is forfeited under subsection (2) may be disposed of as the Minister directs, at the expense of,

heading: Directions of Minister
paragraph: (a) if it was not seized, its owner; or

heading: Directions of Minister
paragraph: (b) if it was seized, its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure.

heading: Return of seized things
paragraph: 56 (1) A seized pest control product or other thing shall be returned to its owner or the person having possession, care or control of the product or thing at the time of its seizure if it has not been forfeited at the final conclusion of proceedings in respect of a violation or an offence under this Act.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A seized pest control product or other thing may be

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) detained pending the payment of any fine or penalty imposed on its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of seizure; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) sold in satisfaction of the fine or penalty.

heading: Forfeiture on application of inspector
paragraph: 56.1 (1) A judge of a superior court of the province in which a pest control product or other thing is seized under this Act may, on the application of an inspector, order that the pest control product or other thing be forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

heading: Notice and inquiry
paragraph: (2) The order may be made only if any notice to any persons that the judge directs was given and the judge finds, after making any inquiry that he or she considers necessary, that the pest control product or other thing is one by means of or in relation to which any of the provisions of this Act or the regulations have been contravened.

heading: Disposition
paragraph: (3) A pest control product or other thing that is forfeited under subsection (1) may be disposed of, as the Minister may direct, at the expense of its owner or the person having possession, care or control of it at the time of its seizure.

heading: Inspector may order measures
paragraph: 57 (1) If an inspector has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has contravened this Act or the regulations, he or she may order the person

heading: Inspector may order measures
paragraph: (a) to stop or shut down any activity or thing involved in the contravention; and

heading: Inspector may order measures
paragraph: (b) to take any other measures that the inspector considers necessary to prevent further contravention, including

heading: Inspector may order measures
paragraph: (i) modifying a pest control product or its labelling or disposing of the product so as to comply with this Act and the regulations, and

heading: Inspector may order measures
paragraph: (ii) manufacturing, handling, storing, transporting, importing, exporting, packaging, labelling, distributing or using a registered pest control product in accordance with the conditions of registration.

heading: Validity period
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) may apply for a specified period or until the inspector is satisfied that no further contravention is likely to take place.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) An order under subsection (1) shall be communicated by delivering a written notice to the registrant or, as the case may be, to the owner or person having possession, care or control of the pest control product, activity or thing that was involved in the contravention and the notice must be accompanied by a statement of the reasons for the order.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (4) Every person who fails to comply with an order in a notice delivered under subsection (3) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Prosecutions
paragraph: (5) An order under subsection (1) may be given whether or not the person has been charged with an offence relating to the contravention, but if the person is charged, the order may be confirmed, varied or rescinded by the court that tries the offence.

heading: Disposal of samples
paragraph: 58 A sample taken under this Act or the regulations may be disposed of as an inspector or analyst may direct.

heading: Inspectors may take measures to control risks
paragraph: 59 (1) Despite subsection 6(8), an inspector may take any measures described in subsection (2) if he or she has reasonable grounds to believe that there has been a contravention of this Act or the regulations and that a pest control product, or any other thing that has been treated or contaminated by a pest control product, poses a health or environmental risk that the Minister considers is unacceptable.

heading: Measures
paragraph: (2) The inspector may

heading: Measures
paragraph: (a) order an owner or a person having possession, care or control of the pest control product or other thing to dispose of it or do anything else that the inspector considers necessary to reduce or eliminate the risks it poses;

heading: Measures
paragraph: (b) dispose of the product or other thing or do anything else that the inspector considers necessary to reduce or eliminate the risks it poses, at the expense of its owner or the person having possession, care or control of the product or thing; or

heading: Measures
paragraph: (c) authorize any other person to exercise the powers described in paragraph (b).

heading: Notice
paragraph: (3) An order under paragraph (2)(a) shall be communicated by delivering a written notice to the owner or person having possession, care or control of the product or thing and the notice

heading: Notice
paragraph: (a) must include a statement of the reasons for the order; and

heading: Notice
paragraph: (b) may specify the period within which and the manner in which the required action must be taken.

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (4) Every person who fails to comply with an order in a notice delivered under subsection (3) is guilty of an offence and liable

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; or

heading: Offence and punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Request for review
paragraph: 60 (1) Subject to this section, an order in respect of which notice has been delivered under subsection 53(2), 57(3) or 59(3) shall be reviewed on the written request of the person to whom the notice was delivered.

heading: Contents of and time for making request
paragraph: (2) A request under subsection (1) shall state the grounds for the request and the decision that is requested and must be delivered to the Minister within 10 days after the date on which the notice referred to in that subsection was delivered to the person who made the request.

heading: Reviewer
paragraph: (3) A review requested under subsection (1) may be conducted by the inspector who delivered the notice or by any other inspector or official to whom the review is assigned.

heading: Refusal when grounds already considered
paragraph: (4) A review requested under subsection (1) may be refused if the request does not comply with subsection (2) or if the grounds stated in the request were presented to and considered by the inspector before the notice was delivered.

heading: Refusal in case of emergency
paragraph: (5) If the reasons in a notice referred to in subsection (1) include the existence of an emergency concerning risks to human health or safety or the environment, the reviewer may refuse to undertake the review until he or she is satisfied that there has been sufficient compliance with the order in the notice to address the emergency.

heading: Refusal not affected by inspector's prior knowledge of emergency
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of subsection (5), the reviewer may refuse to undertake the review no matter how long before delivery of the notice the inspector had known of the circumstances concerning the emergency.

heading: Reasons for refusal
paragraph: (7) A refusal under subsection (4) or (5) shall be communicated in writing to the person who made the request, with reasons for the refusal.

heading: Review initiated by inspector
paragraph: (8) An inspector who delivers a notice referred to in subsection (1), or any other inspector or official assigned to do so, may review the order included in the notice regardless of whether a request has been made under that subsection.

heading: Conduct of review
paragraph: (9) A review referred to in subsection (1) or (8) shall be conducted in accordance with the regulations, if any.

heading: Decision on completion of review
paragraph: (10) On completion of a review, the reviewer shall make a decision to confirm, amend, terminate or cancel the order.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (11) Written notice of the reviewer's decision under subsection (10), with reasons, shall be delivered to the person who made the request or, if there was no request, to the person to whom the notice referred to in subsection (1) was, or could have been, delivered.

heading: Delay in proceedings under section 61
paragraph: (12) An application shall not be made under section 61 in relation to an order until

heading: Delay in proceedings under section 61
paragraph: (a) the expiry of the 10-day period referred to in subsection (2) without a review having been requested under subsection (1);

heading: Delay in proceedings under section 61
paragraph: (b) a request for a review has been refused under subsection (4) or (5); or

heading: Delay in proceedings under section 61
paragraph: (c) a review that has been requested under subsection (1) and has not been refused under subsection (4) or (5), or a review that has been undertaken under subsection (8), has been completed and action has been taken under subsection (10).

heading: Effect of amendment
paragraph: (13) When the decision under subsection (10) is to amend an order, the notice of that decision under subsection (11) is deemed, for the purpose of section 61, to have been delivered under subsection 53(2), 57(3) or 59(3), as the case may be, and the amended order is subject to review under this section.

heading: Application for court order
paragraph: 61 If a person fails to comply with an order in respect of which notice has been delivered under subsection 53(2), 57(3) or 59(3), the Minister may apply to the Federal Court or any other court of competent jurisdiction for an order requiring the person to comply with the notice or authorizing an inspector to take any measures the court considers necessary to ensure compliance with the notice.

heading: Method of delivery
paragraph: 62 (1) Notices or other documents required or authorized to be delivered under this Act may be delivered by any method that provides proof of delivery or by any prescribed method.

heading: Representative in Canada
paragraph: (2) An applicant for registration of a pest control product or a registrant, who does not reside in Canada, shall

heading: Representative in Canada
paragraph: (a) designate a representative who resides in Canada to whom correspondence and any notices or documents referred to in subsection (1) can be sent; and

heading: Representative in Canada
paragraph: (b) inform the Minister in writing of the designation.

heading: Presumption
paragraph: (3) Any correspondence, notices or documents received by the representative designated under subsection (2) are deemed to have been received by the applicant or registrant who designated the representative.

heading: Requirement to communicate through designated representative
paragraph: (4) The Minister may require an applicant or registrant referred to in subsection (2) to conduct any communications with the Minister through the designated representative of the applicant or registrant.

heading: Refusal of communications
paragraph: (5) Despite any other provision of this Act, the Minister may refuse to receive or act on any communication that is not made in compliance with a requirement made by the Minister under subsection (4).

heading: Statutory Instruments Act does not apply
paragraph: (6) For greater certainty, the Statutory Instruments Act does not apply in respect of notices or other documents delivered under this Act.

heading: Recovery of fees
paragraph: 63 Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover, as a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada, any fee or charge that applies in relation to the administration of the provisions of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: 64 Her Majesty in right of Canada may recover, as a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada, any costs incurred by Her Majesty in right of Canada in relation to anything required or authorized under this Act, including

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (a) the inspection, treatment, testing or analysis of a place, pest control product or other thing or the storage, movement, seizure, detention, forfeiture, disposition or return of a pest control product or other thing;

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (b) any enforcement or risk-control measures taken by the Minister or an inspector under this Act.

heading: Time limit
paragraph: 64.1 Proceedings to recover a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada under this Act shall not be commenced later than five years after the debt became payable.

heading: Certificate of default
paragraph: 64.2 (1) Any debt that may be recovered under section 63 or 64 in respect of which there is a default of payment, or the part of any such debt that has not been paid, may be certified by the Minister.

heading: Judgment
paragraph: (2) On production to the Federal Court, a certificate made under subsection (1) shall be registered in that Court and, when registered, has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on the certificate, as if it were a judgment obtained in that Court for a debt of the amount specified in the certificate and all reasonable costs and charges attendant in the registration of the certificate.

heading: Her Majesty not liable
paragraph: 65 If a person must, by or under this Act or the regulations, do anything or permit an inspector to do anything, Her Majesty in right of Canada is not liable for any costs, loss or damage resulting from the compliance or to pay any fee, rent or other charge for what is done, provided, maintained or permitted.

heading: Agreements to determine compensation
paragraph: 66 (1) The Minister shall determine the terms and conditions of agreements to be entered into by applicants and registrants for the purposes of determining compensation payable for the right to use or rely on information provided by registrants to the Minister under this Act.

heading: Negotiation and arbitration
paragraph: (2) An agreement referred to in subsection (1) shall be entered into, and provide for the determination of compensation payable through negotiation and binding arbitration, in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Commercial Arbitration Act applies
paragraph: (3) Subject to this section, the Commercial Arbitration Act applies to an arbitration for the purposes of this section and the regulations.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (4) Subsection 5(2) of the Commercial Arbitration Act does not apply to an arbitration referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (5) Regulations made by the Minister of Justice under section 9 of the Commercial Arbitration Act apply to an arbitration referred to in subsection (3) unless the parties otherwise agree.

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: 67 (1) The Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (a) prescribing policies of the Government of Canada that are consistent with the objectives of this Act for the purposes of the definition government policy in section 2;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (b) prescribing the nomenclature of pests and pest control products for the purposes of this Act;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (c) respecting the information and other things that must accompany an application made under section 7 or 10;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (d) respecting standards of laboratory practice to be used in conducting tests to obtain information about pest control products, certification of compliance with those standards, inspection and audit of compliance and the consequences of a failure to comply;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (e) respecting the evaluation of the health or environmental risks or the value of pest control products;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (f) respecting the registration of pest control products, including the types of registration for classes of products, and, for each type,

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (i) the criteria and characteristics, and

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (ii) the period or maximum period for which the registration is valid, which periods may be either finite or indefinite;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (f.1) respecting minor uses of a pest control product and defining minor use for the purposes of this Act and the regulations;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (g) stating which requirements of the regulations are conditions of registration;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (h) respecting the circumstances and conditions under which information provided to the Minister by registrants may be used or relied upon in relation to applications or registrations of other persons, including distinctions among the rights of registrants based on the purposes for which the information was provided to the Minister;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (i) respecting the Pest Control Products Export Control List, authorizations to export pest control products and the amendment, suspension and cancellation of authorizations;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (j) respecting review panels, including their establishment, the selection and remuneration of panel members and the travel and living expenses to which they are entitled;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (k) respecting authorizations to use unregistered pest control products for specific purposes and the amendment, suspension and cancellation of authorizations;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (l) respecting the Register, including information that is to be included in the Register and public access to the information;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (m) respecting the public disclosure of confidential test data;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (n) prescribing information that is to be excluded in whole or in part from the application of subsection 43(5);

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (o) respecting the manufacture, possession, handling, storage, transport, import, export, distribution, use or disposition of pest control products;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (p) prescribing standards for pest control products, including standards relating to their form and composition;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (q) respecting the measures to be taken to facilitate the recognition of pest control products by a change in colouration or other means;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (r) respecting the packaging, labelling and advertising of pest control products;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (s) respecting pest control product safety information, including information related to product safety data sheets;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (t) respecting the keeping of records by registrants, manufacturers, importers, exporters, distributors and users of pest control products in relation to the products that they manufacture, store, import, export, distribute, use or dispose of and the requirements for making those records available to the Minister;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (u) respecting the recording by registrants of information on sales of pest control products, the retention and reporting to the Minister of such information by registrants and former registrants and the use of such information by the Minister;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (v) respecting the taking of samples and the conduct of analyses for the purposes of this Act;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (w) respecting the inspection and operation of establishments in which registered pest control products are manufactured;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (x) respecting the preservation, detention and forfeiture of pest control products and any other things seized by an inspector;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (y) respecting the destruction or disposition of pest control products or any other thing forfeited or authorized to be disposed of under this Act;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z) respecting reviews under section 60;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z.01) respecting the entering into of agreements and the determination of compensation payable through negotiations and binding arbitration, under section 66;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z.1) respecting the delivery or transmission of documents under this Act, including the transmission of documents in electronic form;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z.2) respecting fees and charges in relation to the administration of this Act or the regulations;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z.21) establishing classes of pest control products and any categories and subcategories of those classes;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z.3) respecting the implementation, in relation to pest control products, of international agreements that affect those products;

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z.4) exempting persons, activities or pest control products, including products that are imported solely for the purpose of export, from the application of all or any of the provisions of this Act or the regulations, and prescribing the conditions under which they are exempt; and

heading: Regulations - Governor in Council
paragraph: (z.5) prescribing anything that by this Act is to be prescribed and generally for carrying out the purposes and provisions of this Act.

heading: Incorporation by reference
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, regulations made under paragraph (1)(d) or (p) that incorporate a standard by reference may incorporate the standard as amended to a certain date or from time to time.

heading: Jointly produced documents
paragraph: (2.1) A regulation made under this Act may incorporate by reference documents that the Minister produces jointly with another government for the purpose of harmonizing the regulation with other laws.

heading: Internally produced standards
paragraph: (2.2) A regulation made under this Act may incorporate by reference technical or explanatory documents that the Minister produces, including

heading: Internally produced standards
paragraph: (a) specifications, classifications, illustrations, graphs or other information of a technical nature; and

heading: Internally produced standards
paragraph: (b) test methods, procedures, operational standards, safety standards or performance standards of a technical nature.

heading: Scope of incorporation
paragraph: (2.3) Documents may be incorporated by reference as they exist on a particular date or as they are amended from time to time.

heading: Regulations re WTO Agreement
paragraph: (3) Without limiting the authority conferred by subsection (1), the Governor in Council may make any regulations that the Governor in Council considers necessary for the purpose of implementing, in relation to pest control products, Article 39(3) of the Agreement on Trade-related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights set out in Annex 1C to the WTO Agreement.

heading: Definition of WTO Agreement
paragraph: (4) In subsection (3), WTO Agreement has the meaning assigned by the definition Agreement in subsection 2(1) of the World Trade Organization Agreement Implementation Act.

heading: Interim orders
paragraph: 67.1 (1) The Minister may make an interim order that contains any provision that may be contained in a regulation made under this Act if the Minister believes that immediate action is required to deal with a significant risk, direct or indirect, to health, safety or the environment.

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (2) An interim order has effect from the time that it is made but ceases to have effect on the earliest of

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (a) 14 days after it is made, unless it is approved by the Governor in Council,

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (c) the day on which a regulation made under this Act, that has the same effect as the interim order, comes into force, and

heading: Cessation of effect
paragraph: (d) one year after the interim order is made or any shorter period that may be specified in the interim order.

heading: Contravention of unpublished order
paragraph: (3) No person shall be convicted of an offence consisting of a contravention of an interim order that, at the time of the alleged contravention, had not been published in the Canada Gazette unless it is proved that, at the time of the alleged contravention, the person had been notified of the interim order or reasonable steps had been taken to bring the purport of the interim order to the notice of those persons likely to be affected by it.

heading: Exemption form Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (4) An interim order

heading: Exemption form Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (a) is exempt from the application of sections 3, 5 and 11 of the Statutory Instruments Act; and

heading: Exemption form Statutory Instruments Act
paragraph: (b) shall be published in the Canada Gazette within 23 days after it is made.

heading: Deeming
paragraph: (5) For the purpose of any provision of this Act other than this section, any reference to regulations made under this Act is deemed to include interim orders, and any reference to a regulation made under a specified provision of the Act is deemed to include a reference to the portion of an interim order containing any provision that may be contained in a regulation made under the specified provision.

heading: Tabling of order
paragraph: (6) A copy of each interim order must be tabled in each House of Parliament within 15 days after it is made.

heading: House not sitting
paragraph: (7) In order to comply with subsection (6), the interim order may be sent to the Clerk of the House if the House is not sitting.

heading: Contravention causing risk or harm
paragraph: 68 (1) Every person is guilty of an offence if, in contravening this Act or the regulations, they cause

heading: Contravention causing risk or harm
paragraph: (a) a risk of imminent death or serious bodily harm to another person;

heading: Contravention causing risk or harm
paragraph: (b) a risk of substantial harm to the environment; or

heading: Contravention causing risk or harm
paragraph: (c) harm to the environment.

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (2) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (a) on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than $200,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than six months, or to both; and

heading: Punishment
paragraph: (b) on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not more than $500,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than three years, or to both.

heading: Offence committed wilfully or recklessly
