paragraph: (b) in the case of compensable data in support of an application to amend the registration of a pest control product of the data holder, the day on which the Minister receives the application;

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (c) in the case of compensable data that is considered by the Minister during a re-evaluation or special review of a pest control product of the data holder, if the test data was provided by the data holder in response to a notice initiating the process under subsection 16(3) or 18(1) of the Act or a notice requiring additional information under paragraph 19(1)(a) of the Act, the day on which the Minister receives the data;

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (d) in the case of test data referred to in paragraph (1)(b), the day of registration referred to in subsection 17.03(1); or

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (e) in the case of test data referred to in paragraph (1)(c), the day on which the Minister initiates the re-evaluation or special review.

heading: Minister to identify test data
paragraph: 17.06 For the purpose of subsection 7(2) of the Act, the Minister must provide the applicant with a list of the test data referred to in subsection 17.05(1) for which compensation may be payable by the applicant and in respect of which an agreement is required to be entered into between the applicant and each data holder whose data the applicant wishes to use or rely on.

heading: Proposed agreement on test data
paragraph: 17.07 (1) On receipt of the list of test data, an applicant may deliver to each data holder a proposed agreement that specifies the test data that the applicant wishes to use or rely on.

heading: Agreement entered into
paragraph: (2) On receipt of the proposed agreement, the data holder must enter into the agreement with the applicant.

heading: Negotiation of compensation payable and settlement
paragraph: 17.08 (1) When the agreement is entered into, an applicant and a data holder must, in order to reach a settlement, begin to negotiate the compensation payable in respect of the test data that the applicant wishes to use or rely on.

heading: Period of negotiation and settlement of compensation payable
paragraph: (2) The applicant and the data holder must reach a negotiated settlement in respect of the compensation payable

heading: Period of negotiation and settlement of compensation payable
paragraph: (a) within 120 days after the day on which the data holder receives the proposed agreement; or

heading: Period of negotiation and settlement of compensation payable
paragraph: (b) by the end of any additional negotiation period, if the parties agree in writing to continue negotiating.

heading: Arbitration
paragraph: 17.09 (1) Despite subsection 17.08(2), in the absence of a negotiated settlement at the end of the negotiation and in accordance with the agreement entered into by the parties, the applicant may, by delivering to the data holder a written notice, submit the determination of the compensation payable to binding arbitration.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) The notice must contain the last offers of the applicant and the data holder, if they were presented in writing at the end of the negotiation.

heading: Arbitral award
paragraph: (3) The arbitrator must make an arbitral award within 120 days after the day on which the notice is delivered, unless

heading: Arbitral award
paragraph: (a) the parties agree to an extension before the end of that period and provide written notice to the arbitrator; or

heading: Arbitral award
paragraph: (b) the arbitrator provides written notice of an extension to the parties before the end of that period.

heading: Letter of access
paragraph: 17.1 (1) When a negotiated settlement is reached or an arbitral award is made, the data holder must provide the applicant with a letter of access, signed by the data holder, confirming that the applicant may use or rely on their test data.

heading: Failure to provide letter of access
paragraph: (2) If the data holder fails to provide the letter of access within the period specified in the negotiated settlement or arbitral award, the applicant may use or rely on the test data without having to continue to comply with the settlement or award.

heading: Early registration
paragraph: 17.11 (1) The applicant may, as soon as a notice referred to in subsection 17.09(1) has been delivered to the data holder, request that the Minister register their pest control product before obtaining a letter of access and may use or rely on the test data of the data holder if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (a) the applicant enters into an escrow agreement with a third party;

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (b) the third party is entitled under the laws of a province to receive and hold an amount of money on behalf of another person;

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (c) under the escrow agreement, the applicant deposits with the third party an amount of money equal to the data holder's last offer referred to in subsection 17.09(2);

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (d) the escrow agreement contains all of the following terms:

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (i) the third party holds the money until it becomes payable in accordance with the escrow agreement,

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (ii) on receipt of a copy of the registration certificate, the third party pays the data holder an amount of money equal to the applicant's last offer referred to in subsection 17.09(2),

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (iii) on receipt of a copy of the negotiated settlement or arbitral award, the third party pays the data holder the compensation payable as determined in the settlement or award, less the amount paid under subparagraph (ii),

heading: Early registration
paragraph: (iv) the third party pays any remaining balance to the applicant.

heading: Copy and proof to Minister
paragraph: (2) The applicant must send the Minister both a copy of the escrow agreement and proof that the applicant has deposited the money in accordance with paragraph (1)(c).

heading: When no last offer in writing
paragraph: (3) If the data holder's last offer was not made in writing at the end of the negotiation, the conditions set out in subsection (1) and subsection (2) do not apply.

heading: Conditions - use of or reliance on test data
paragraph: 17.12 (1) Subject to subsection 17.17(2), in the context of a re-evaluation or special review and on receipt of a notice initiating the process under subsection 16(3) or 18(1) of the Act or a notice requiring additional information under paragraph 19(1)(a) of the Act, a registrant may, in accordance with the agreement concluded with the data holder under subsection 17.14(2), use or rely on the following test data if they pay compensation to the data holder in accordance with the negotiated settlement or arbitral award for the period set out in subsection (2):

heading: Conditions - use of or reliance on test data
paragraph: (a) compensable data that the registrant wishes to use or rely on that is

heading: Conditions - use of or reliance on test data
paragraph: (i) provided to the Minister, in the context of the re-evaluation or special review, by the data holder in response to a notice initiating the process under subsection 16(3) or 18(1) of the Act or to a notice requiring additional information under paragraph 19(1)(a) of the Act, and

heading: Conditions - use of or reliance on test data
paragraph: (ii) relevant to the pest control product that is the subject of the re-evaluation or special review; and

heading: Conditions - use of or reliance on test data
paragraph: (b) test data that the Minister considers in support of the re-evaluation or special review decision in respect of the pest control product but that was not provided in response to one of the notices referred to in paragraph (a) and that is relevant to an active ingredient that is not equivalent to the active ingredient contained in the pest control product that is the subject of the re-evaluation or special review if

heading: Conditions - use of or reliance on test data
paragraph: (i) the test data is already compensable data, or

heading: Conditions - use of or reliance on test data
paragraph: (ii) the data holder already has exclusive rights in respect of the test data.

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (2) The period for which compensation is payable for the following test data by the registrant to the data holder commences on one of the following days and must not exceed 12 years, except in the case of the test data referred to in subparagraph (b)(ii) for which the period must not exceed the period provided for in section 17.03:

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (a) in the case of compensable data provided by the data holder under paragraph (1)(a), the day on which the Minister receives the data; or

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (b) in the case of test data referred to in paragraph (1)(b),

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (i) if the data is already compensable data, one of the days referred to in paragraph 17.05(2)(a), (b), (c) or (e), as the case may be, or

heading: Compensable period
paragraph: (ii) if the data holder already has exclusive rights in respect of the data, the day of registration referred to in subsection 17.03(1).

heading: Minister to identify test data
paragraph: 17.13 For the purposes of subsections 16(5) and (5.1) and 18(3) and (3.1) of the Act, the Minister must make available to data holders and other registrants, on the day on which the Minister makes public the decision statement referred to in subsection 28(5) of the Act, a list of the test data referred to in subsection 17.12(1) in respect of which compensation may be payable by any of those registrants and in respect of which an agreement is required to be entered into between the registrant and each data holder whose data the registrant wishes to use or rely on.

heading: Proposed agreement on test data
paragraph: 17.14 (1) Either the registrant or the data holder may deliver to the other party a proposed agreement that specifies the test data that the registrant wishes to use or rely on no later than 60 days after the day on which the decision statement referred to in subsection 28(5) of the Act is made public.

heading: Agreement entered into
paragraph: (2) The registrant or the data holder must, on receipt of the proposed agreement from the other party, enter into the agreement with the other party.

heading: Negotiation of compensation payable and settlement
paragraph: 17.15 (1) When the agreement is entered into, a registrant and a data holder must, in order to reach a settlement, begin to negotiate the compensation payable in respect of the test data that the registrant wishes to use or rely on.

heading: Period of negotiation and settlement
paragraph: (2) The registrant and the data holder must reach a negotiated settlement in respect of the compensation payable

heading: Period of negotiation and settlement
paragraph: (a) within 120 days after the day on which the decision statement referred to in subsection 28(5) of the Act is made public; or

heading: Period of negotiation and settlement
paragraph: (b) by the end of any additional negotiation period, if the parties agree in writing to continue negotiating.

heading: Arbitration
paragraph: 17.16 (1) Despite subsection 17.15(2), in the absence of a negotiated settlement at the end of the negotiation and in accordance with the agreement entered into by the parties, the registrant or the data holder may, by delivering to the other party a written notice, submit the determination of the compensation payable to binding arbitration.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (2) The notice must contain the last offers of the registrant and the data holder, if they were presented in writing at the end of the negotiation.

heading: Arbitral award
paragraph: (3) The arbitrator must make an arbitral award within 120 days after the day on which the notice is delivered, unless

heading: Arbitral award
paragraph: (a) the parties agree to an extension before the end of that period and provide written notice to the arbitrator; or

heading: Arbitral award
paragraph: (b) the arbitrator provides written notice of an extension to the parties before the end of that period.

heading: Letter of access
paragraph: 17.17 (1) When a negotiated settlement is reached or an arbitral award is made, the data holder must provide the registrant with a letter of access, signed by the data holder, confirming that the registrant may use or rely on their test data.

heading: Failure to provide letter of access
paragraph: (2) If the data holder fails to provide the letter of access within the period specified in the negotiated settlement or arbitral award, the registrant may use or rely on the test data without having to continue to comply with the settlement or award.

heading: Validity period and exemption
paragraph: 18 Despite section 13, if a pest control product is registered for, or the registration of a pest control product is amended to permit its use in, the emergency control of a seriously detrimental infestation,

heading: Validity period and exemption
paragraph: (a) the validity period must not be longer than three years and may not be extended;

heading: Validity period and exemption
paragraph: (b) subsections 28(1) and 35(1) and paragraphs 42(2)(c) to (f) of the Act do not apply; and

heading: Validity period and exemption
paragraph: (c) the registration may not be renewed.

heading: When required
paragraph: 20 If the physical properties of a pest control product are such that its presence may not be detected when it is used and as a result it could expose a person or domestic animal to a severe health risk, the pest control product must be denatured by means of colour, odour or any other means specified as a condition of registration by the Minister under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act to provide a signal or warning as to its presence.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 21 A word or an expression that states or implies that the Government of Canada or any of its departments or agencies promotes, endorses or recommends the use of a pest control product must not appear on the package of, or in any advertisement for, a pest control product.

heading: Official languages
paragraph: 22 (1) Subject to subsection (3), all information on a label must be in both English and French.

heading: Exception - products destined abroad
paragraph: (3) The information on the label of a registered pest control product that is not authorized to be manufactured, imported, sold or used in Canada may be in either English or French, or in both.

heading: Label - presentation
paragraph: 23 (1) All information that is required to be shown on a label must appear in a manner that is clearly legible and indelible.

heading: Label - presentation
paragraph: (2) Any written, printed or graphic matter on the marketplace label of the pest control product must not detract from or obscure the required information.

heading: Diseases of humans
paragraph: 24 (1) A label must not represent a pest control product as a treatment, preventive or cure for any disease, disorder or abnormal physical state listed in Schedule A.1 to the Food and Drugs Act.

heading: Diseases of domestic animals
paragraph: (2) A label must not represent a pest control product as a treatment, preventive or cure for any disease, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Health of Animals Act, that is required to be reported under that Act.

heading: Principal and secondary display panels
paragraph: 25 A registered pest control product must have a display panel consisting of a principal display panel and a secondary display panel.

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: 26 (1) The principal display panel of a registered pest control product must show the following information:

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (a) the product name of the pest control product, which may include a distinctive brand or trademark and the common chemical name of its active ingredient, if established;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (b) the product type of the pest control product, which must be descriptive of its purpose;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (c) the physical form of the pest control product;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (d) the product class designation of the pest control product as set out in section 5;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (e) information concerning the nature and degree of hazard inherent in the pest control product, which must identify the nature and degree of hazard by appropriate precautionary symbols and signal words selected from Schedule 3, together with a statement that indicates the nature of the primary hazard to which the symbol relates;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (f) the statement "READ THE LABEL BEFORE USING.";

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (g) if the pest control product has the product class designation "DOMESTIC", the statement "KEEP OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN.";

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (h) a statement, as follows:

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (i) the words "ACTIVE INGREDIENT:" or "ACTIVE INGREDIENTS:", as the case may be,

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (ii) the common chemical name of the active ingredient of the pest control product or, if it has no common chemical name, its chemical or other name,

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (iii) the concentration of the active ingredient, expressed, if the pest control product is

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (A) a liquid, as a percentage by mass, or as mass per unit volume, or both, as specified by the Minister in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act,

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (B) a dust, wettable powder or other dry formulation, as a percentage by mass, or

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (C) neither a liquid nor a dry formulation, in terms specified by the Minister in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act, and

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (iv) the viscosity, specific gravity, particle size or any other property or characteristic that the Minister may specify in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (i) the registration number of the pest control product, as follows: "REGISTRATION NO. (assigned registration number) PEST CONTROL PRODUCTS ACT" or "REG. NO. (assigned registration number) P.C.P. Act";

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (j) a declaration of net quantity of the product in the package, expressed

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (i) by volume, if the product is a liquid or gas or is viscous,

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (ii) by mass, if the product is a solid or pressure-packed, and

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (iii) in terms specified by the Minister in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act, in any other case;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (k) the registrant's name; and

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (l) the name, postal address and telephone number of a contact person in Canada to which public inquiries may be directed.

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (2) The secondary display panel of a registered pest control product must show the following information:

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (a) under the heading "DIRECTIONS FOR USE", the directions for the use of the pest control product, including application rates, timing and frequency of application, and any limitations on its use;

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (b) information that identifies any significant risk associated with the handling, storage, display, distribution and disposal of the pest control product, and instructions on procedures to reduce those risks and, if specified by the Minister in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act, instructions on decontamination procedures and disposal of the pest control product and its empty packages;

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (c) under the heading "PRECAUTIONS", information that identifies any significant risk to health, the environment or anything in connection with which the pest control product is to be used, and instructions on procedures to reduce that risk;

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (d) under the heading "PRECAUTIONS", the following statement:

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (i) if the pest control product does not have the product class designation "DOMESTIC": "KEEP OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN.", or

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (ii) if the pest control product is to be used only in the manufacture of another pest control product: "PREVENT ACCESS BY UNAUTHORIZED PERSONNEL.";

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (e) under the heading "FIRST AID", instructions that

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (i) set out the practical measures to be taken in the event of poisoning, intoxication or injury caused by the pest control product, and

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (ii) include the statement "Take the container label or product name and Pest Control Product Registration Number with you when seeking medical attention.";

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (f) under the heading "TOXICOLOGICAL INFORMATION", information that is essential to the treatment of persons who are poisoned, intoxicated or injured by the pest control product that includes all of the following:

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (i) antidotes and remedial measures or, if no specific antidote or remedial measure exists, the statement "Treat symptomatically.",

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (ii) a description of the symptoms of poisoning or intoxication, and

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (iii) a list of the components of the product, not including the active ingredient, that may affect the treatment; and

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (g) the following notice to users: "NOTICE TO USER: This pest control product is to be used only in accordance with the directions on the label. It is an offence under the Pest Control Products Act to use this product in a way that is inconsistent with the directions on the label."

heading: Outermost package
paragraph: (3) If a pest control product is contained in more than one package, the outermost package that is visible under normal conditions of storage, transportation or handling must bear a label that shows the following information:

heading: Outermost package
paragraph: (a) the information, as it appears on the approved label for the product, that is required under paragraphs (1)(a), (e), (h), (i), (k) and (l);

heading: Outermost package
paragraph: (b) the information, as it appears on the approved label for the product, that is required under paragraph (2)(b) and that is relevant if any significant risk referred to in that paragraph exists while the pest control product is contained in the outermost package; and

heading: Outermost package
paragraph: (c) the statement "For first aid instructions or the toxicological information essential for treatment, obtain and read the approved label from the registrant or phone the number indicated on this container.".

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not apply if the outermost package is transparent or otherwise allows the label on an inner package to be legible, and that label shows the information required under

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (a) subsection (3); or

heading: Exceptions
paragraph: (b) paragraphs (2)(e) and (f), and that information appears as it does on the approved label for the product, and paragraphs (3)(a) and (b).

heading: Brochures or leaflets
paragraph: 28 (1) If, under subsection 8(2) of the Act, the Minister specifies in the conditions of registration relating to the label that information required by these Regulations to be shown on the principal and secondary display panels may instead be shown in a brochure or leaflet that accompanies the pest control product, the following requirements must be met:

heading: Brochures or leaflets
paragraph: (a) the principal display panel must have prominently shown on it either the statement "READ ATTACHED BROCHURE (or LEAFLET) BEFORE USING." or the statement "READ ACCOMPANYING BROCHURE (or LEAFLET) BEFORE USING."; and

heading: Brochures or leaflets
paragraph: (b) the brochure or leaflet must contain all of the information that is to be shown on the principal and secondary display panels in addition to the specified information.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) The statement in paragraph (1)(a) does not need to appear on the container if, pursuant to subsection 31(1), a pest control product is transported in a railway tank car or a transport truck tanker-trailer and that tank car or tanker-trailer is the only container.

heading: Provided at distribution
paragraph: (3) Any brochure or leaflet referred to in subsection (1) must be provided to any user of the product at the time the product is distributed to them.

heading: Product class designation "RESTRICTED" - notice
paragraph: 29 (1) If the principal display panel shows the product class designation "RESTRICTED", the notice that is required by paragraph 26(2)(g) must appear prominently at the top of the secondary display panel, followed by the heading "RESTRICTED USES", followed by the directions for use, the application rates, the timing and frequency of application and the limitations on the use of the pest control product to which the restriction relates. All of the foregoing must be circumscribed by a line to set the information apart from all other information that is required to be shown on the secondary display panel.

heading: Product class designation "RESTRICTED" - brochure or leaflet
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if the principal display panel shows the product class designation "RESTRICTED", the directions for use, the application rates, the timing and frequency of application and the limitations on the use of the pest control product to which the restriction relates, together with the information required by paragraphs 26(1)(a) to (l) and (2)(a) and (c) may, if specified by the Minister in the conditions of registration relating to the label under subsection 8(2) of the Act, be shown instead in a brochure or leaflet that accompanies the pest control product.

heading: Schedule 1 devices
paragraph: 30 Despite subsections 26(1) and (2), the display panel of a registered pest control product that is a device of a type described in Schedule 1 must show

heading: Schedule 1 devices
paragraph: (a) on the principal display panel, the information set out in paragraphs 26(1)(i), (k) and (l); and

heading: Schedule 1 devices
paragraph: (b) on its secondary display panel, the information set out in paragraphs 26(2)(a) to (c).

heading: Unregistered device - display panel
paragraph: 30.1 (1) An ultraviolet radiation-emitting device referred to in paragraph 4(1)(c) must have a display panel consisting of a principal display panel and a secondary display panel.

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (2) The principal display panel and, if any, the operating manual of the device must show the following information:

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (a) its intended use;

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (b) if it is to be distributed primarily to the general public for personal use in or around their homes, the statement "KEEP OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN";

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (c) the statement

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (i) if there is an accompanying operating manual, "READ THE LABEL AND ANY OPERATING MANUAL BEFORE USING", and

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (ii) "READ THE LABEL BEFORE USING" in any other case; and

heading: Principal display panel
paragraph: (d) the name, postal address, telephone number and email address of a contact person in Canada to which public inquiries may be directed.

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (3) The secondary display panel of the device must show the following information:

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (a) under the heading "PRECAUTIONS", the statements

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (i) "WARNING - Ultraviolet radiation emitted from this device.",

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (ii) "Unintended use of the device, or damage to the housing, may result in exposure to ultraviolet radiation.",

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (iii) "Ultraviolet radiation may cause eye and skin irritation.", and

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (iv) "Avoid exposing eyes and skin to ultraviolet radiation.";

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (b) the statement "The use of this device is a supplement to and not a substitute for following best practices to control transmission of infections; users are to follow those best practices, including those related to the cleaning and disinfection of surfaces.";

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (c) under the heading "DIRECTIONS FOR USE", the directions for the use of the device, notably on how to operate the device, any limitation on its use and, if applicable, instructions on how users may replace the ultraviolet lamp or any other component that emits ultraviolet light without exposure to ultraviolet radiation, including instructions on the frequency required for those replacements; and

heading: Secondary display panel
paragraph: (d) other information that identifies any risk to health or the environment associated with the handling, storage, display, distribution, use or disposal of the device, or of any of its components, and instructions on procedures for reducing those risks.

heading: Insufficient space
paragraph: (4) If there is insufficient space to fit the information on the secondary display panel, that information must be shown in an accompanying operating manual and the secondary display panel must show

heading: Insufficient space
paragraph: (a) the information set out in paragraphs (2)(a) and (b); and

heading: Insufficient space
paragraph: (b) as much of the other information set out in subsection (2) as possible.

heading: Railway tank car or transport truck tanker-trailer
paragraph: 31 (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3) and to any condition specified by the Minister under subsection 8(2) of the Act relating to the label, if a pest control product is transported in a railway tank car or a transport truck tanker-trailer and that tank car or tanker-trailer is the only container, the information required under subsections 26(1) and (2) must be shown on the documents that accompany the shipment.

heading: Storing or dispensing product
paragraph: (2) If a pest control product is stored in a railway tank car or a transport truck tanker-trailer or if the tank car or tanker-trailer is being used to dispense the product directly, then the documents required under subsection (1) must be

heading: Storing or dispensing product
paragraph: (a) affixed to the tank car or tanker-trailer and readily available for review by all persons handling the product, the tank car or the tanker-trailer; and

heading: Storing or dispensing product
paragraph: (b) if applicable, within reach of and clearly visible to the person operating the control valve that is used for dispensing the product.

heading: Providing information
paragraph: (3) Subject to any condition specified by the Minister under subsection 8(2) of the Act relating to the label, if a pest control product referred to in subsection (1) is distributed directly to a user of the product, the information required under section 26 must be provided to the user at the time of distribution.

heading: Metric units
paragraph: 32 (1) Quantities shown on a label must be expressed in metric units.

heading: Decimal system
paragraph: (2) The declaration of net quantity must be shown in the decimal system to three figures, except that, if the net quantity is less than 100 g, 100 mL, 100 cm3, 100 cm2 or 100 cm, it may be shown truncated to two decimal figures, and, in either case, any final zero that appears to the right of the decimal point need not be shown.

heading: Net quantity less than one
paragraph: (3) A net quantity that is less than one must be shown in the decimal system, with a zero before the decimal point, or in words.

heading: Metric units
paragraph: (4) The metric units in the declaration of net quantity must be shown

heading: Metric units
paragraph: (a) in millilitres, if the net volume of the pest control product is less than 1 000 mL, except that 500 mL may be shown as 0.5 L;

heading: Metric units
paragraph: (b) in litres, if the net volume is 1 000 mL or more;

heading: Metric units
paragraph: (c) in grams, if the net mass is less than 1 000 g, except that 500 g may be shown as 0.5 kg; and

heading: Metric units
paragraph: (d) in kilograms, if the net mass is 1 000 g or more.

heading: Optional Canadian units of measurement
paragraph: (5) In addition to being expressed in accordance with subsection (1), quantities shown on a label may also be expressed in the Canadian units of measurement set out in Schedule II to the Weights and Measures Act.

heading: Packages
paragraph: 33 (1) The package of a pest control product must be constructed to contain the product safely under normal conditions of storage, display and distribution.

heading: Safe access to contents
paragraph: (2) Every package must be constructed to permit

heading: Safe access to contents
paragraph: (a) the withdrawal of any or all of the contents in a manner that is safe to the user; and

heading: Safe access to contents
paragraph: (b) the closing of the package in a manner that will contain the pest control product safely under normal storage conditions.

heading: Minimize degradation
paragraph: (3) Every package must be constructed to minimize the degradation or change of its contents.

heading: When package essential to safety
paragraph: (4) If the package is essential to the safe and effective use of the pest control product, it must be constructed to meet any specifications that the Minister may specify in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act.

heading: Storage, transportation and display
paragraph: (2) A pest control product must be stored or displayed in a separate room and transported in a separate compartment from any human food or animal feed or stored, displayed or transported in such a way as to avoid any possible contamination of the food or feed if the product bears the signal word "POISON" superimposed on the precautionary symbol for danger set out in item 2 of Schedule 3.

heading: Conditions on documents
paragraph: 35 When conditions of registration that relate to the distribution of a pest control product are specified by the Minister under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act, those conditions must be shown on the documents that accompany the shipment.

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: 36 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the importer of a pest control product - except a pest control product described in paragraph 4(1)(f) or (g) - must provide the Minister with a declaration at the time of the importation, in English or French, signed by the importer, that sets out

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (a) the shipper's name and postal address, along with their email address or telephone number;

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (b) the importer's name and address, along with their email address or telephone number;

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (c) the name of the pest control product, which may include a distinctive brand or trademark;

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (d) if applicable, the number of the pest control product's licence, certificate, permit, registration, foreign product use certificate, research authorization certificate or research notification certificate;

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (e) the quantity of the pest control product being imported, expressed

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (i) by volume, if the product is liquid, gaseous or viscous,

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (ii) by mass, if the product is a solid or pressure-packed,

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (iii) by number of units being imported, if the product is a device or a treated article, and

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (iv) in terms specified by the Minister in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act, in any other case;

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (f) if applicable, the chemical name, common chemical name or other name of each active ingredient of the pest control product, along with its quantity in the pest control product; and

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (g) the purpose of the importation of the pest control product, expressed as follows:

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (i) "For Distribution, Including Sale", if the product is being imported for distribution, including sale,

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (ii) "For Manufacturing Purposes", if the product is being imported for use in the manufacture of a registered pest control product,

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (iii) "For Research Purposes", if the product is being imported for research purposes,

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (iv) "For Grower Requested Own Use", if the product is being imported under a foreign product use certificate issued under subsection 41(3), and

heading: Declaration - general
paragraph: (v) "For (importer to specify the purpose)", in any other case.

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (2) The importer of treated seed must provide the Minister with a declaration at the time of the importation, in English or French, signed by the importer, that sets out

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (a) the shipper's name and postal address, along with their email address or telephone number;

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (b) the importer's name and address, along with their email address or telephone number;

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (c) the name of the kind or species of seed;

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (d) the country where the crop from which the seed is derived was grown;

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (e) if applicable, the number of the treated seed's licence, certificate, permit, registration, foreign product use certificate, research authorization certificate or research notification certificate;

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (f) the quantity of treated seed that is being imported, expressed by mass;

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (g) the chemical name, common chemical name or other name of each active ingredient of the pest control product that is incorporated into, or applied to, the seed, along with its quantity, expressed by mass or volume, as applicable, per 100 kg of seed;

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (h) the name of the treated seed, including any distinctive brand or trademark; and

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (i) the purpose of the importation of the treated seed, expressed as follows:

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (i) "For Distribution, Including Sale", if the seed is being imported for distribution, including sale,

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (ii) "For Manufacturing Purposes", if the seed is being imported for further manufacturing,

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (iii) "For Research Purposes", if the seed is being imported for research purposes,

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (iv) "For Grower Requested Own Use", if the seed is being imported under a foreign product use certificate issued under subsection 41(3), and

heading: Declaration - treated seed
paragraph: (v) "For (importer to specify the purpose)", in any other case.

heading: Retention
paragraph: (3) The importer must keep the information set out in a declaration for two years after the day on which the importation of the pest control product in respect of which the declaration was made.

heading: Procedure
paragraph: 37 For the purpose of subsection 41(1) of the Act, the following requirements must be met before the use of a foreign product may be authorized:

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (a) the Minister determines under section 38 that the foreign product is equivalent to a registered pest control product;

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (b) the Minister issues a certificate of equivalency under subsection 39(1) with respect to the foreign product;

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (c) the Minister approves the foreign product use label under section 40; and

heading: Procedure
paragraph: (d) the person who wishes to use the foreign product applies to the Minister for an authorization in accordance with subsections 41(1) and (2).

heading: Conditions
paragraph: 38 (1) Subject to subsection (4), the Minister may determine that a foreign product is equivalent to a registered pest control product if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (a) a grower or group of growers requests the Minister to make the determination;

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (b) four not-for-profit Canadian national grower associations support the request;

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (c) the person who makes the request provides the Minister with all of the information listed in subsection (4);

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (d) the foreign product meets the requirements of subsection (2); and

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (e) the registered pest control product meets the requirements of subsection (3).

heading: Eligibility - foreign products
paragraph: (2) A foreign product must meet all of the following requirements to be considered when making a determination of equivalency:

heading: Eligibility - foreign products
paragraph: (a) it is not an organism;

heading: Eligibility - foreign products
paragraph: (b) it is not under review in the foreign country where it is registered with respect to its health and environmental risks and is being sold in that country;

heading: Eligibility - foreign products
paragraph: (c) it does not contain an active ingredient that is under special review in Canada; and

heading: Eligibility - foreign products
paragraph: (d) it is manufactured by a person who is related to the registrant of the registered pest control product, within the meaning of the definition related persons in subsection 251(2) of the Income Tax Act, whether the related person is located in or outside Canada.

heading: Eligibility - registered pest control products
paragraph: (3) A registered pest control product must meet both of the following requirements to be considered when making a determination of equivalency:

heading: Eligibility - registered pest control products
paragraph: (a) it does not have the product class designation "RESTRICTED" described in paragraph 5(c); and

heading: Eligibility - registered pest control products
paragraph: (b) the test data referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b) of the definition exclusive rights in section 17.01 that were provided in support of its registration are no longer subject to exclusive rights within the meaning of that definition.

heading: Interpretation - test data
paragraph: (3.1) In subsection (3), test data has the same meaning as in section 17.01.

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (4) Before making the determination of equivalency, the Minister must first find that the foreign product and the registered pest control product are sufficiently similar so as to justify proceeding with the determination, based on the following preliminary information:

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (a) the name and registration number of the registered pest control product, the name and product identifier of the foreign product and the name of the country where the foreign product is registered;

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (b) the name of the registrant of the registered pest control product and the name of the holder of the registration of the foreign product;

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (c) the labels of both products;

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (d) the information described in subparagraphs 26(1)(h)(ii) and (iii) with respect to both products;

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (e) their type of formulation;

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (f) their type of package;

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (g) the health and environmental risks that were evaluated by the regulatory body that registered the foreign product; and

heading: Preliminary steps
paragraph: (h) the standard of acceptability of risk that was applied by that regulatory body.

heading: Further information
paragraph: (5) If the Minister finds that the foreign product is sufficiently similar to the registered pest control product, the Minister must so inform the registrant and request that they provide the Minister with the following information, in respect of both the registered pest control product and the foreign product:

heading: Further information
paragraph: (a) the composition of all formulations of the end-use products and of the technical grade active ingredients used in their manufacture, which, in the case of the registered pest control product and its active ingredient, must be the composition specified by the Minister in the conditions of registration under paragraph 8(1)(a) of the Act;

heading: Further information
paragraph: (b) the name of the manufacturer of the active ingredient that is used to manufacture each of the products and the address of the place where each active ingredient is manufactured;

heading: Further information
paragraph: (c) the name of the manufacturer of the formulation of each end-use product and the address of the place where each formulation is manufactured;

heading: Further information
paragraph: (d) the information described in subparagraph 26(1)(h)(iv); and

heading: Further information
paragraph: (e) product safety information relevant to their use in the workplace, if any.

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (6) If the information provided under subsection (5) with respect to the registered pest control product or the foreign product is insufficient to enable the Minister to make the determination, the Minister may request additional relevant information from the registrant in order to make the determination.

heading: Written consent of registrant
paragraph: (7) Instead of providing the information required by subsection (5), the registrant may provide their written consent to the Minister to use or rely on any information that they had previously provided to the Minister.

heading: Notice of no further action
paragraph: (8) If the Minister is unable to obtain the information from the registrant under subsection (5) or the consent of the registrant under subsection (7), the Minister must notify the person who made the request that no further steps will be taken by the Minister and place a copy of that notice in the Register.

heading: Resumption of request by any person
paragraph: (9) In the circumstances described in subsection (8), paragraph (2)(d) does not apply and any person may, within two years after the notice is placed in the Register, request that the Minister make the determination of equivalency and for that purpose must provide the Minister with either

heading: Resumption of request by any person
paragraph: (a) all of the following information:

heading: Resumption of request by any person
paragraph: (i) with respect to the registered pest control product, a detailed and comprehensive analysis with an accompanying description of methodology and analytical validation that permits the determination of the acceptability of procedures, results and conclusions concerning the composition of the product, including the identity and concentration of its active ingredient and formulants, and of any contaminants in the active ingredient, and

heading: Resumption of request by any person
paragraph: (ii) with respect to any foreign product, the information described in subsection (5); or

heading: Resumption of request by any person
paragraph: (b) with respect to both the registered pest control product and any foreign product, a detailed and comprehensive analysis with an accompanying description of methodology and analytical validation that permits the determination of the acceptability of procedures, results and conclusions concerning the composition of both products, including the identity and concentration of their active ingredients and formulants, and of any contaminants in the active ingredients.

heading: Additional information
paragraph: (10) If the information provided under subsection (9) is insufficient to enable the Minister to make the determination, the Minister may request additional relevant information from the person who made the request in order to make the determination.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 39 (1) If the Minister determines that a foreign product is equivalent to a registered pest control product, the Minister must issue a certificate of equivalency and place it in the Register.

heading: Validity
paragraph: (2) A certificate of equivalency is valid until December 31 in the second year after the year in which it is issued and may be reissued with respect to the same two products in accordance with the requirements of section 38. A certificate of equivalency ceases to be valid in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Validity
paragraph: (a) the basis on which the foreign product and the registered pest control product were determined to be equivalent no longer applies;

heading: Validity
paragraph: (b) any of the requirements set out in subsection 38(2) or (3) are no longer met;

heading: Validity
paragraph: (c) the registration of the registered pest control product is cancelled or expires and the sale and use of that product is no longer authorized under the Act; or

heading: Validity
paragraph: (d) the foreign product is no longer registered in the country referred to in paragraph 38(2)(b).

heading: Foreign product use label
paragraph: 40 (1) When the Minister issues a certificate of equivalency, she or he must also approve a foreign product use label.

heading: Brochures or leaflets
paragraph: (2) If the Minister permits the directions for use to be shown instead in a brochure or leaflet that must accompany the foreign product, the following requirements must be met:

heading: Brochures or leaflets
paragraph: (a) the label must have prominently shown on it the statement "READ ATTACHED BROCHURE (or LEAFLET) BEFORE USING."; and

heading: Brochures or leaflets
paragraph: (b) the brochure or leaflet must contain all of the information that is otherwise required to be shown on the label.

heading: Application for authorization
paragraph: 41 (1) A person who wishes to use a foreign product in respect of which a certificate of equivalency is in effect must apply to the Minister for an authorization under subsection 41(1) of the Act.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The application must include all of the following information:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) the person's name, address and signature;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) the name of the foreign product;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) the number of the applicable certificate of equivalency;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) a description of the intended use of the foreign product and the location where it will be used; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) the quantity of the foreign product required for that intended use for one growing season.

heading: Issuance of certificate
paragraph: (3) If the Minister authorizes the use of the foreign product, she or he must issue a foreign product use certificate that sets out all of the following information:

heading: Issuance of certificate
paragraph: (a) the identity of the certificate holder;

heading: Issuance of certificate
paragraph: (b) the amount of the foreign product that may be imported and used under the certificate; and

heading: Issuance of certificate
paragraph: (c) the location where the foreign product is to be used by the certificate holder.

heading: Validity
paragraph: (4) A foreign product use certificate is valid for only one importation and for the period specified in the certificate, which must not exceed one calendar year. It ceases to be valid if the applicable certificate of equivalency ceases to be valid.

heading: Not transferable
paragraph: (5) A foreign product use certificate is not transferable.

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: 42 (1) A person may import a foreign product whose use is authorized if all of the following conditions are met:

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (a) the person holds a foreign product use certificate in respect of that product;

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (b) that certificate holder purchases the product directly from the foreign source without the intervention of an agent or mandatary;

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (c) before the importation, the certificate holder provides the Minister with all of the following information:

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (i) the proposed date of the importation,

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (ii) the name of the person who will transport the foreign product into Canada, and

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (iii) the name of the entry point;

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (d) the certificate holder

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (i) affixes to each container of the foreign product, as soon as practicable after the importation of the product but in any case no later than upon its arrival either at the location of storage, or at the location of use specified in the foreign product use certificate, a copy of the approved foreign product use label in a way that the product identifier that relates to its registration outside Canada remains visible at all times, and

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (ii) ensures that a copy of any brochure or leaflet that sets out the directions for use accompanies the product; and

heading: Importation of foreign product
paragraph: (e) the quantity of the product imported does not exceed the amount set out in the foreign product use certificate.

heading: Pooled purchases
paragraph: (2) Two or more persons may together import in one shipment their authorized quantities of foreign products set out in their respective foreign product use certificates if the importation meets the conditions of subsection (1).

heading: Transport
paragraph: (3) The person who transports the foreign product into Canada must carry it to either the location of storage, or the location of use specified in the foreign product use certificate, and have the following documents in their possession:

heading: Transport
paragraph: (a) proof of purchase in respect of each quantity of foreign product in the shipment, including the name of the foreign source from whom it was purchased; and

heading: Transport
paragraph: (b) copies of all of the relevant foreign product use certificates.

heading: Information in Register
paragraph: 43 The Minister must place all of the following information in the Register with respect to every request for the determination of equivalency made under section 38:

heading: Information in Register
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who made the request and the date on which it was made;

heading: Information in Register
paragraph: (b) the name of the registered pest control product and its registration number;

heading: Information in Register
paragraph: (c) the name of the foreign product, its product identifier and the name of the country where it is registered; and

heading: Information in Register
paragraph: (d) the outcome of the request, including the reasons.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 44 (1) The holder of a foreign product use certificate must keep records that contain all of the following information in respect of each foreign product that they import and use:

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) a copy of the certificate;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) the name and quantity of the foreign product;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (c) the method of empty container disposal;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (d) the method of disposal of any unused foreign product;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (e) proof of purchase of the foreign product and the name of the foreign source from which it was purchased;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (f) the name of the person who transported the foreign product into Canada; and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (g) the date of importation.

heading: Retention
paragraph: (2) The records must be kept for five years after the end of the year in which the foreign product use certificate that relates to the product expires or ceases to be valid.

heading: Production of records
paragraph: (3) The records must be made available to the Minister on request.

heading: Non-application of subsection 6(1) of the Act
paragraph: 46 Subsection 6(1) of the Act does not apply to the manufacture of a pest control product that is for use only in conducting research under these Regulations.

heading: Application of certain provisions to research
paragraph: 47 Sections 48 to 50 and 56 to 68 apply to an authorization under subsection 41(1) of the Act to use an unregistered pest control product for the purpose of research.

heading: Application
paragraph: 48 A person who seeks permission for a research establishment to conduct research must apply to the Minister to obtain a research authorization.

heading: Contents
paragraph: 49 An application for a research authorization must include the information specified in subsections 6(1) and (3) in addition to all of the following:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) an electronic copy of the proposed experimental label;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) a copy of the research plan; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) any other information described in section 8 that the Minister may require to evaluate the health and environmental risks posed by the proposed research.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: 50 (1) Before the Minister authorizes the use of a pest control product under subsection 41(1) of the Act for the purpose of research, the Minister must consider the health and environmental risks and determine that the proposed experimental label meets the requirements of section 60.

heading: Issuance of research authorization certificate
paragraph: (2) When the Minister authorizes the use of a pest control product to conduct research, the Minister must issue a research authorization certificate to the research establishment that sets out the conditions specified under subsection 41(1) of the Act, including those that relate to the experimental label.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: 51 A research establishment is exempt from the application of subsection 6(1) of the Act and section 48 if the Minister confirms under section 54 that the proposed research meets all of the criteria set out in section 53.

heading: Notice and contents
paragraph: 52 A research establishment that wishes to obtain confirmation under section 54 must notify the Minister by providing the information specified in subsections 6(1) and (3) in addition to both of the following:

heading: Notice and contents
paragraph: (a) an electronic copy of the proposed experimental label; and

heading: Notice and contents
paragraph: (b) a copy of the research plan.

heading: Criteria
paragraph: 53 The following are the criteria referred to in section 51:

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (a) the research does not involve the use of a semiochemical;

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (b) in the case of research that involves the use of a chemical pest control product,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (i) it does not involve the use of an antimicrobial agent,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (ii) it does not involve aerial application,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (iii) it does not involve the application of a pest control product to water or to a place where runoff water may remove residues from the research site,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (iv) it does not involve the use of a pest control product in any of the following areas:

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (A) greenhouses,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (B) residential areas, including lawns, gardens and parks,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (C) industrial premises, and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (D) food-handling areas,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (v) it does not involve the use of a pest control product for either

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (A) structural pest control, or

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (B) fumigation,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (vi) it does not involve the use of a pest control product that contains a formulant that is on Part I of the List of Pest Control Product Formulants and Contaminants of Health or Environmental Concern or a contaminant that is on Part 3 of that List,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (vii) in the case of a pest control product that contains an unregistered active ingredient, the application of the product is carried out only by a researcher

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (A) on 5 to 50 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment, or

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (B) on 1 to 5 ha of land owned or operated by a cooperator, and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (viii) in the case of a pest control product that contains a registered active ingredient,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (A) the application of the pest control product is carried out by a researcher or cooperator on 10 to 50 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment or a cooperator, and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (B) there is a reasonable expectation that the research will not increase occupational exposure above the level that is expected when the pest control product is used in accordance with its conditions of registration; and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (c) in the case of research that involves the use of a microbial agent,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (i) it does not involve aerial application,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (ii) it does not involve the use of a pest control product that contains a formulant that is on Part 1 of the List of Pest Control Product Formulants and Contaminants of Health or Environmental Concern or a contaminant that is on Part 3 of that List,

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (iii) the micro-organism is indigenous to the area where it is intended to be used, and

heading: Criteria
paragraph: (iv) the application of the pest control product is carried out on a maximum of 10 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment or, in the case of an aquatic application, on a body of water that has a maximum of 1 ha of surface area and that is wholly contained on land owned or operated by a research establishment.

heading: Issuance of research notification certificate
paragraph: 54 If the Minister confirms that the proposed research meets the criteria set out in section 53 and the proposed experimental label meets the requirements of section 60, the Minister must issue a research notification certificate to the research establishment.

heading: Exemption - research solely in laboratory
paragraph: 55 (1) A research establishment is exempt from the application of subsection 6(1) of the Act and sections 48, 52 and 59 to 63 if the research is conducted solely in a laboratory.

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (2) A research establishment is exempt from the application of subsection 6(1) of the Act and sections 48 and 52 if all or part of the research is conducted outside a laboratory and meets all of the following criteria:

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (a) it does not involve the use of a microbial agent;

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (b) in the case of research that involves the use of a chemical pest control product,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (i) it does not involve the use of an antimicrobial agent,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (ii) it does not involve aerial application,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (iii) it does not involve the application of a pest control product to water or to a place where runoff water may remove residues from the research site,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (iv) it does not involve the use of a pest control product in any of the following areas:

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (A) greenhouses,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (B) residential areas, including lawns, gardens and parks,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (C) industrial premises, and

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (D) food-handling areas,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (v) it does not involve the use of a pest control product for either

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (A) structural pest control, or

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (B) fumigation,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (vi) it does not involve the use of a pest control product that contains a formulant that is on Part 1 of the List of Pest Control Product Formulants and Contaminants of Health or Environmental Concern or a contaminant that is on Part 3 of that List,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (vii) in the case of a pest control product that contains an unregistered active ingredient, the application of the product is carried out only by a researcher

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (A) on a maximum of 5 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment, or

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (B) in the case of land owned or operated by a cooperator, on a maximum of 1 ha or 5% of the total area of the crop under research, whichever is less, and

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (viii) in the case of a pest control product that contains a registered active ingredient,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (A) the application of the product is carried out by a researcher or cooperator on a maximum of 10 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment or a cooperator, or on a maximum of 20% of the total area of the crop under research, whichever is less, and

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (B) there is a reasonable expectation that the research will not increase occupational exposure above the level that is expected when the pest control product is used in accordance with its conditions of registration; and

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (c) in the case of research that involves the use of a semiochemical,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (i) it does not involve aerial application,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (ii) it does not involve the application of a pest control product to water,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (iii) it does not involve the use of a pest control product in any of the following areas:

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (A) greenhouses,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (B) residential areas, including lawns, gardens and parks,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (C) industrial premises, and

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (D) food-handling areas,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (iv) it does not involve the use of a pest control product for either

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (A) structural pest control, or

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (B) fumigation,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (v) it does not involve the use of a pest control product that contains a formulant that is on Part 1 of the List of Pest Control Product Formulants and Contaminants of Health or Environmental Concern or a contaminant that is on Part 3 of that List,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (vi) in the case of a pest control product that contains an unregistered active ingredient, other than an arthropod pheromone, the application of the product is carried out only by a researcher on a maximum of 5 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (vii) in the case of a pest control product that contains a registered active ingredient, other than an arthropod pheromone, the application of the product is carried out by a researcher or cooperator on a maximum of 10 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment or cooperator, and

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (viii) in the case of a pest control product that contains an active ingredient that is an arthropod pheromone,

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (A) the application of the product is carried out on a maximum of 100 ha of land owned or operated by a research establishment or cooperator and the maximum use rate does not exceed 375 g of active ingredient per hectare per year, and

heading: Exemption and criteria - research not solely in laboratory
paragraph: (B) if used in a food or feed crop, the pheromone is contained in an affixed solid matrix dispenser or in a retrievable-sized polymeric matrix dispenser, and the dispenser is not in direct contact with the crop.

heading: Expiry
paragraph: 56 A research authorization certificate and a research notification certificate expire on December 31 of the year in which they are issued, unless another expiry date is specified in the certificate.

heading: Not renewable
paragraph: 57 Neither a research authorization certificate nor a research notification certificate is renewable.

heading: Not transferable
paragraph: 58 Neither a research authorization certificate nor a research notification certificate is transferable.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 59 Unless otherwise specified as a condition by the Minister under subsection 41(1) of the Act, a research establishment must post signs at every research site that

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) show all of the following information:

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) the following primary message, in both English and French:

heading: Requirements
paragraph: "PEST CONTROL EXPERIMENTAL SITE / SITE D'EXPERIMENTATION DE LUTTE ANTIPARASITAIRE

heading: Requirements
paragraph: DO NOT ENTER WITHOUT AUTHORIZATION. / ACCES INTERDIT SANS AUTORISATION

heading: Requirements
paragraph: CONTACT (contact name) AT (phone number). / S'ADRESSER A (nom du responsable) AU (no de telephone).", and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) the research authorization certificate number or research notification certificate number, when there is one;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) are visible, legible, indelible and posted at every entrance to the research site on each side of the entrance;

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (c) are posted before treatment begins and remain posted until any treated food or feed crop is harvested or as long as data are being collected; and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (d) may include the name of the pest control product that is the subject of the research and the name and logo of its manufacturer, if they are printed smaller than the primary message.

heading: Requirement
paragraph: 60 (1) A research establishment must ensure that every pest control product that is used in research is accompanied by an experimental label.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) An experimental label must

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) show all of the information specified in section 26, except paragraphs 26(1)(d), (g), (i) and (k) and (2)(d);

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) show

heading: Contents
paragraph: (i) the following information on the principal display panel:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (A) the statement "EXPERIMENTAL USE ONLY",

heading: Contents
paragraph: (B) the research authorization certificate number or the research notification certificate number, when there is one, as follows:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (I) "RESEARCH AUTHORIZATION/NOTIFICATION NO. (assigned number) PEST CONTROL PRODUCTS ACT", or

heading: Contents
paragraph: (II) "RESEARCH AUTHORIZATION/NOTIFICATION NO. (assigned number) P.C.P. ACT",

heading: Contents
paragraph: (C) the statement "SALE PROHIBITED. NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION TO ANY PERSON OTHER THAN A RESEARCHER OR COOPERATOR.",

heading: Contents
paragraph: (D) the statement "KEEP OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN",

heading: Contents
paragraph: (E) the manufacturer's name and address, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (F) when the research involves the use of a pest control product that contains a formulant that is on Part 2 of the List of Pest Control Product Formulants and Contaminants of Health or Environmental Concern, the statement "Warning: contains the allergen (name of allergen)",

heading: Contents
paragraph: (ii) on the secondary display panel, when the research involves the use of an unregistered pest control product, in the instructions on decontamination procedures and disposal referred to in paragraph 26(2)(b), the statement "Any unused product must be returned to the manufacturer.", and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (iii) on the secondary display panel, despite paragraph (a), the statement set out in subparagraph 26(2)(e)(ii) amended to read as follows: "Take the experimental label with you when seeking medical attention."; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) represent the intended research as described in the research plan.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Despite paragraph (2)(a), when the research involves the use of a registered pest control product, the following information need not be shown on the experimental label if that label is used in conjunction with the approved label:

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) the net quantity referred to in paragraph 26(1)(j);

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) instructions on decontamination procedures and disposal referred to in paragraph 26(2)(b);

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) information that identifies any significant risk to the environment, and instructions on procedures to reduce those risks, referred to in paragraph 26(2)(c); and

heading: Exception
paragraph: (d) the notice to users referred to in paragraph 26(2)(g).

heading: Copies
paragraph: 61 A research establishment must

heading: Copies
paragraph: (a) supply to every researcher and cooperator involved in the research a copy of the experimental label, which must be the approved experimental label if a research authorization certificate or research notification certificate has been issued; and

heading: Copies
paragraph: (b) produce a copy of the experimental label to the Minister on request.

heading: Contents
paragraph: 63 A research establishment must maintain records that contain all of the following information for each research project, for five years after the end of the project:

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) the name and quantity of every pest control product used;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) the names of the researchers and cooperators;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) the locations of the research sites;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) a description of the application methods; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) the test data generated.

heading: Conditions for import
paragraph: 64 A research establishment may import an unregistered pest control product for the purpose of conducting research if

heading: Conditions for import
paragraph: (a) the product is imported in accordance with section 36; and

heading: Conditions for import
paragraph: (b) the quantity being imported is not more than that specified in a research authorization certificate or research notification certificate or that which is necessary to conduct the research for which a research establishment is exempt under section 55.

heading: Unregistered products
paragraph: 65 A research establishment must return to the manufacturer any unused unregistered pest control products.

heading: Registered products
paragraph: 66 A research establishment must return to the manufacturer any unused registered pest control product unless it is kept by the research establishment to be used by a researcher or cooperator involved in the research in a way that is consistent with the directions on the approved label.

heading: Researchers and cooperators only
paragraph: 67 A research establishment may not distribute a pest control product that is used in the conduct of research to any person that is not a researcher or cooperator involved in the research, except in accordance with section 65 or 66.

heading: Treated food and feed crops
paragraph: 68 When a research authorization certificate is issued, treated food and feed crops from research sites and meat (including meat by-products and fat), milk and eggs that may contain residues as a result of the research must not be sold unless

heading: Treated food and feed crops
paragraph: (a) written authorization to do so is set out on the certificate; and

heading: Treated food and feed crops
paragraph: (b) in the case of research that involves the use of a chemical pest control product, residues do not exceed an amount that would result in the sale of the food being prohibited under section 4 of the Food and Drugs Act.

heading: Research - section 53 criteria
paragraph: 69 In the case of research that meets the criteria set out in section 53 and for which a research notification certificate is issued,

heading: Research - section 53 criteria
