paragraph: (a) in the case of research that involves the use of a chemical pest control product, treated food and feed crops from research sites and meat (including meat by-products and fat), milk and eggs that may contain residues as a result of research must not be sold unless the residues do not exceed an amount that would result in the sale of the food being prohibited under section 4 of the Food and Drugs Act; and

heading: Research - section 53 criteria
paragraph: (b) in the case of research that involves the use of a microbial agent, other than one that contains Bacillus thuringiensis registered for use on agricultural crops, treated food and feed crops from research sites and meat (including meat by-products and fat), milk and eggs that may contain residues as a result of research must not be sold.

heading: Research - subsection 55(2) criteria
paragraph: 70 In the case of research that meets the criteria set out in subsection 55(2), treated food and feed crops from research sites and meat (including meat by-products and fat), milk and eggs that may contain residues as a result of research must not be sold unless

heading: Research - subsection 55(2) criteria
paragraph: (a) in the case of research that involves the use of a chemical pest control product, residues do not exceed an amount that would result in the sale of the food being prohibited under section 4 of the Food and Drugs Act; and

heading: Research - subsection 55(2) criteria
paragraph: (b) in the case of research that involves the use of a semiochemical, the research meets the criteria set out in subparagraph 55(2)(c)(viii).

heading: Representative samples
paragraph: 71 A sample of a pest control product that is taken by an inspector under paragraph 48(1)(b) of the Act must be representative of the lot from which it is taken and may consist of

heading: Representative samples
paragraph: (a) the entire package, in the case of a liquid packaged in containers of less than 5 L;

heading: Representative samples
paragraph: (b) the entire package, in the case of a dry material packaged in containers of less than 5 kg;

heading: Representative samples
paragraph: (c) the device, in the case of a device; and

heading: Representative samples
paragraph: (d) the treated article, in the case of a treated article.

heading: Detention tag
paragraph: 72 If a pest control product is seized under subsection 52(1) of the Act, the inspector must attach a detention tag to at least one package of the pest control product in the lot that is seized.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 These Regulations may be cited as the Petroleum Refinery Liquid Effluent Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2 (1) In these Regulations,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Act means the Fisheries Act; (Loi)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: actual deposit means the aggregate quantity, measured in pounds per day, of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) that is contained in all liquid effluent and once-through cooling water and that is actually deposited in any one day by a refinery; (rejet reel)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: ammonia nitrogen means the nitrogen in ammonia that results from the operation of a refinery, that is contained in liquid effluent or once-through cooling water from that refinery and that is determined to be present therein by the test method referred to in item 4 of the table to Schedule IV; (azote ammoniacal)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: authorized deposit means the aggregate quantity, measured in pounds per day, of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) that is contained in all liquid effluent and once-through cooling water and that may be deposited in any one day by a refinery under the authority of these Regulations; (rejet autorise)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: ballast water means water, carried in a vessel for stability and seaworthiness, that is discharged from the vessel to a refinery prior to loading the vessel and includes water used for cargo or ballast tank cleaning; (eau de ballast)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: crude oil means virgin or naturally occurring unrefined petroleum and any hydrocarbons or mixture of hydrocarbons similar in composition to petroleum brought into a refinery for processing, but does not include hydrocarbons and residual fuels brought into a refinery primarily to meet the fuel requirements of that refinery or primarily for direct blending into finished products; (petrole brut)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: day means a period of 24 consecutive hours; (jour)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: deposit means to deposit or permit the deposit in water frequented by fish; (rejeter)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: liquid effluent means, subject to subsection (3), waste water and includes process water, cooling tower blow-down, tank draining, ballast water, storm water, wastes from water treatment facilities and run-off from land used for the disposition of waste water and sludges associated with the operation of a refinery; (effluent)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment; (ministre)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: oil and grease means the oil and grease that results from the operation of a refinery, that is contained in liquid effluent or once-through cooling water from that refinery and that is determined to be present therein by the test method referred to in item 1 of the table to Schedule IV; (huiles et graisses)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: once-through cooling water means, subject to subsection (3), water that has been circulated once through heat exchangers, either singly or in series, for the purpose of removing heat from process streams and that is not intended to come into contact with the process streams; (eau de refroidissement non recyclee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: owner means the owner or operator of a refinery or his authorized representative; (proprietaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: phenols means the hydroxy derivatives of benzene and its condensed nuclei that result from the operation of a refinery, that are contained in liquid effluent or once-through cooling water from that refinery and that are determined to be present therein by the test method referred to in item 2 of the table to Schedule IV; (phenols)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: process water means water that is intended to come into contact with hydrocarbons or treating chemicals at a refinery; (eau de traitement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: reference crude rate means the quantity of crude oil, expressed in thousand barrels per day, that, in accordance with section 6, has been declared by the owner of a refinery to be the reference crude rate of the refinery; (taux de reference de brut)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: refinery means facilities intended primarily for the separation and conversion of crude oil into products, including liquified petroleum gas, gasolines, naphthas, heating oils, fuel oils, asphalts, lubricating oils and greases, benzene, toluene, xylene, hydrogen, sulphur and coke, and includes blending, shipping and packaging facilities located on the refinery property and all properties developed for the operation of those facilities, but does not include facilities associated with the processing of natural gas or the production of synthetic petroleum originating from coal or bituminous sands; (raffinerie)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: storm water means, subject to subsection (2), water run-off that results from precipitation of any kind that falls on a refinery and includes water run-off originating from outside the refinery that passes over or through the refinery; (eaux pluviales)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: stream day crude rate means the rate, in barrels per day, at which crude oil is processed in a refinery; (taux de brut par jour de fonctionnement effectif)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: sulfide means dissolved sulfide that results from the operation of a refinery that is contained in liquid effluent or once-through water from that refinery and that is determined to be present therein by the test method referred to in item 3 of the table to Schedule IV; (sulfures)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: total suspended matter means the non-filterable residue that results from the operation of a refinery, that is contained in liquid effluent or once-through cooling water from that refinery and that is determined to be present therein by the test method referred to in item 5 of the table to Schedule IV. (matieres en suspension de toute nature)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) When storm water is protected, in such manner as the Minister may approve in writing, from contamination by the deleterious substances prescribed in section 4 that originate from the refinery, the storm water shall be deemed not to be storm water for the purpose of these Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (3) When, prior to being deposited, liquid effluent or once-through cooling water has been treated, in such manner as the Minister may approve in writing, at a site outside a refinery for the purpose of removing therefrom the deleterious substances prescribed in section 4, the liquid effluent or once-through cooling water shall be deemed not to be liquid effluent or once-through cooling water for the purpose of these Regulations.

heading: Application
paragraph: 3 These Regulations apply to every refinery that has not commenced the processing of crude oil prior to November 1, 1973 and that commences the processing of crude oil on or after that date.

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: 4 For the purpose of paragraph (c) of the definition deleterious substance in subsection 33(11) of the Act, the following substances are prescribed as deleterious substances;

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (a) oil and grease;

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (b) phenols;

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (c) sulfide;

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (d) ammonia nitrogen;

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (e) total suspended matter; and

heading: Substances Prescribed as Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (f) any substance capable of altering the pH of liquid effluent or once-through cooling water.

heading: Authorized Deposit of a Deleterious Substance
paragraph: 5 (1) Subject to these Regulations, the owner of a refinery may deposit a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) if

heading: Authorized Deposit of a Deleterious Substance
paragraph: (a) the arithmetic mean of the actual deposits of each such substance during the month in which the deposit is made does not exceed the arithmetic mean of the authorized deposits of that substance in the same month for the refinery, as calculated in accordance with section 7;

heading: Authorized Deposit of a Deleterious Substance
paragraph: (b) the actual deposit of each such substance deposited in each day by the refinery does not exceed, for more than one day in each month, the authorized deposit of that substance for the refinery, as calculated in accordance with subsection 8(1); and

heading: Authorized Deposit of a Deleterious Substance
paragraph: (c) the actual deposit of each such substance deposited in each day by the refinery does not exceed the authorized deposit of that substance for the refinery as calculated in accordance with subsection 8(2).

heading: Authorized Deposit of a Deleterious Substance
paragraph: (2) Subject to these Regulations, the owner of a refinery may deposit the deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(f) if the pH of the liquid effluent or once-through cooling water is within the limits of 6.0 and 9.5.

heading: Authorized Deposit of a Deleterious Substance
paragraph: (3) Subject to these Regulations, the owner of a refinery may deposit a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b) or (e), if the aggregate quantity of that substance contained in storm water being deposited in any month does not exceed the limit of the deposit authorized of that substance in the same month for the refinery, as calculated in accordance with subsection 9(2).

heading: Reference Crude Rates
paragraph: 6 (1) When the owner of a refinery intends to deposit a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e), he shall, before making the deposit, sign, date and forward to the Minister a declaration, in such form as the Minister may prescribe, stating the reference crude rate of the refinery.

heading: Reference Crude Rates
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), the reference crude rate of a refinery is the maximum design stream day crude rate of the refinery, divided by 1,000.

heading: Reference Crude Rates
paragraph: (3) The owner of a refinery may revise the reference crude rate of the refinery at any time by signing, dating and forwarding to the Minister a declaration, in such form as the Minister may prescribe, stating the revised reference crude rate of the refinery.

heading: Reference Crude Rates
paragraph: (4) The owner of a refinery that deposits a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) shall revise the reference crude rate of the refinery if the arithmetic mean of the stream day crude rates during any two consecutive months, divided by 1,000, excluding days when crude rates have been reduced due to refinery maintenance, is less than 85 per cent of the last declared reference crude rate of the refinery and shall sign, date and forward a declaration, in such form as the Minister may prescribe, stating the revised reference crude rate of the refinery.

heading: Reference Crude Rates
paragraph: (5) For the purpose of subsection (3), the revised reference crude rate of a refinery is the arithmetic mean of stream day crude rates sustained in commercial operation for at least seven consecutive days, divided by 1,000.

heading: Reference Crude Rates
paragraph: (6) For the purpose of subsection (4), the revised reference crude rate of a refinery is the arithmetic mean of stream day crude rates sustained in commercial operation for at least 14 consecutive days, divided by 1,000.

heading: Reference Crude Rates
paragraph: (7) The revised reference crude rate of a refinery takes effect on the first day of the month in which it is declared.

heading: Calculation of Authorized Deposits
paragraph: 7 (1) For the purpose of paragraph 5(1)(a), the arithmetic mean of the authorized deposits for a refinery for a month shall be calculated using the amounts obtained in the calculations made under subsection (2).

heading: Calculation of Authorized Deposits
paragraph: (2) The authorized deposit for a refinery of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) shall, subject to section 9, be calculated for each day by multiplying the amount in Column II of an item of Schedule I for the deleterious substance set out in Column I of that item by the reference crude rate of the refinery for that month.

heading: Calculation of Authorized Deposits
paragraph: 8 (1) For the purpose of paragraph 5(1)(b), the authorized deposit for a refinery of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) shall, subject to section 9, be calculated by multiplying the amount set out in Column III of an item of Schedule I for the deleterious substance set out in Column I of that item by the reference crude rate of the refinery for that month.

heading: Calculation of Authorized Deposits
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of paragraph 5(1)(c), the authorized deposit for a refinery of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) shall, subject to section 9, be calculated by multiplying the amount set out in Column IV of an item of Schedule I for the deleterious substance set out in Column I of that item by the reference crude rate of the refinery for that month.

heading: Calculation of Authorized Deposits
paragraph: 9 (1) When storm water is deposited by a refinery in any day, the authorized deposit for the refinery of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b) or (e), calculated in accordance with sections 7 and 8, may be increased for that day by the amount set out in Column II of an item of Schedule II for the deleterious substance set out in Column I of that item for each 10,000 Canadian gallons of storm water that is deposited.

heading: Calculation of Authorized Deposits
paragraph: (2) The limit of the deposit authorized in pounds per month of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b) or (e) contained in storm water being deposited by a refinery in any month shall be calculated by multiplying the amount set out in Column III of an item of Schedule II for the deleterious substance set out in Column I of that item by the reference crude rate of the refinery for that month.

heading: Calculation of Actual Deposits
paragraph: 10 For the purposes of subsection 5(1), when the owner of a refinery deposits a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e), he shall, within 30 days after the end of the month in which the deposit is made, determine for that month the actual deposit of each substance deposited by the refinery by making the measurements and calculations in accordance with Schedule IV.

heading: Calculation of Actual Deposits
paragraph: 11 The owner of a refinery that deposits the deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(f) shall, every day in the month during which the deposit is made or when requested by the Minister, monitor the deposit for the purpose of subsection 5(2) by performing the test referred to in Schedule III.

heading: Reporting
paragraph: 12 (1) The owner of a refinery that has deposited a deleterious substance prescribed in section 4 in any month shall sign, date and forward to the Minister within 30 days after the end of that month or when requested by the Minister, a report, in such form as the Minister may prescribe, indicating

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (a) the arithmetic mean of the authorized deposits of that substance in that month for the refinery as calculated in accordance with section 7 and, where applicable, section 9;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (b) the authorized deposits of that substance in each day of that month for the refinery as calculated in accordance with sections 7 and 8 and, where applicable, section 9;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (c) the actual deposits of the deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) deposited in each day of that month by the refinery as calculated in accordance with Schedule IV;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (d) the arithmetic mean of the actual deposits of the deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) deposited in that month by the refinery as calculated in accordance with Schedule IV;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (e) the pH of composite samples measured in accordance with Schedule III;

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (f) the reference crude rate of the refinery in that month; and

heading: Reporting
paragraph: (g) such other information as may be requested by the Minister to enable him to determine whether the refinery is operating in compliance with the requirements of these Regulations.

heading: Reporting
paragraph: 13 The owner of a refinery that deposits a deleterious substance prescribed in section 4 shall install and maintain facilities including sampling connections and flow-measuring devices that are acceptable to the Minister to enable the Minister to determine whether the refinery is operating in compliance with the requirements of these Regulations.

paragraph: 2 (1) The concentration in milligrams per litre of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) in composite samples obtained from each liquid effluent outfall and from the once-through cooling water shall be determined every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, or as requested by the Minister, using

paragraph: (a) the quantity of liquid effluent or once-through cooling water that is collected continually during a sampling period of 24 hours at a rate in proportion to the flow rate of the liquid effluent or once-through cooling water;

paragraph: (b) the quantity of liquid effluent or once-through cooling water that is collected so that a minimum of 96 equal volumes of liquid are delivered into a receptacle at equal time intervals over a sampling period of 24 hours; or

paragraph: (3) For the purpose of this section, procedures pertaining to sampling, the preservation and storage of samples and the prevention of interference, as outlined in the general sections relating to the specific test methods set out in Column II of the table to this Schedule, should be adhered to.

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Sections 2, 10 and 12)Measurement and Calculation of Actual Deposit of a Deleterious Substance Prescribed in Paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) of Regulations
paragraph: 3 The actual deposit by a refinery of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) shall be calculated by using the amounts obtained under sections 1 and 2 of this Schedule for each day that the concentration of that deleterious substance has been determined.

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Sections 2, 10 and 12)Measurement and Calculation of Actual Deposit of a Deleterious Substance Prescribed in Paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) of Regulations
paragraph: 4 The arithmetic mean of the actual deposits referred to in paragraph 5(1)(a) of the Regulations shall be calculated using the amounts obtained under section 3 of this Schedule.

heading: SCHEDULE IV(Sections 2, 10 and 12)Measurement and Calculation of Actual Deposit of a Deleterious Substance Prescribed in Paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) of Regulations
paragraph: 5 For the purpose of subsection 5(3) of the Regulations, the actual quantity of a deleterious substance prescribed in paragraph 4(a), (b) or (e) of the Regulations contained in storm water deposited each month shall be calculated using the weighted average concentration, based on the quantity of storm water discharged for those days during which the concentration of that deleterious substance has been determined, and the total quantity of storm water discharged in that month.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1 (1) The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aerodrome has the same meaning as in subsection 3(1) of the Aeronautics Act. (aerodrome)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: area of mining operations means the area at ground level occupied by any open-pit or underground workings, mill complex or storage area for overburden, waste rock, tailings or ore. (aire d'exploitation miniere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: boundary water has the meaning assigned by the definition boundary waters in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Water Act. (eaux limitrophes)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: canal means a waterway constructed for navigation. (canal)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Class IA nuclear facility has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Class I Nuclear Facilities Regulations. (installation nucleaire de categorie IA)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: disposal at sea means disposal, as defined in subsection 122(1) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, but does not include any omission that constitutes a disposal in paragraph (g) of the definition of that term. (immersion)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: exploratory well has the same meaning as in subsection 101(1) of the Canada Petroleum Resources Act, but does not include a delineation well or development well as those terms are defined in that subsection. (puits d'exploration)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hazardous waste has the meaning assigned by paragraphs 1(a) to (e) of the definitions hazardous waste and hazardous recyclable material in sections 2 and 4, respectively, of the Cross-border Movement of Hazardous Waste and Hazardous Recyclable Material Regulations, but does not include nuclear substances, domestic waste water or anything collected from households in the course of regular municipal waste collection services. (dechets dangereux)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: international electrical transmission line has the meaning assigned by the definition international power line in section 2 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act. (ligne internationale de transport d'electricite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: marine terminal means a facility, including its areas, structures and equipment, that is used for berthing ships and that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) related to the movement of goods between ships and shore; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) used for the receiving, holding, regrouping, embarkation or landing of passengers transported by water. (terminal maritime)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: national marine conservation area means a marine conservation area or a reserve, as those terms are defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada National Marine Conservation Areas Act, or the Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park established under section 5 of the Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park Act. (aire marine nationale de conservation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: national park means a park or a park reserve as those terms are defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada National Parks Act. (parc national)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: navigable water has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canadian Navigable Waters Act. (eaux navigables)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: new right of way means land that is to be developed for an international electrical transmission line, a pipeline, as defined in section 2 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act, a railway line or an all-season public highway, and that is not alongside and contiguous to an area of land that was developed for an electrical transmission line, oil and gas pipeline, railway line or all-season public highway. (nouvelle emprise)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: nuclear substance has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Nuclear Safety and Control Act. (substance nucleaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: offshore means, except in respect of an offshore area, anything that is located in

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an area referred to in paragraph 3(d) or (e) of the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act in respect of which an authorization under that Act is required to conduct an activity that is related to the exploration and drilling for, or the production, conservation, processing or transportation of, oil or gas; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an area in respect of which an authorization under the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Act or the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation Act is required to conduct an activity that is related to the exploration and drilling for, or the production, conservation, processing or transportation of, oil or gas. (au large des cotes)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: offshore area has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act. (zone extracotiere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: oil and gas pipeline means a pipeline that is used, or is to be used, for the transmission of oil or gas alone or with any other commodity. (pipeline d'hydrocarbures)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: park community has the same meaning as in subsection 2(1) of the Canada National Parks Act. (collectivite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: uranium mill has the meaning assigned by the definition mill in section 1 of the Uranium Mines and Mills Regulations. (usine de concentration d'uranium)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: uranium mine has the meaning assigned by the definition mine in section 1 of the Uranium Mines and Mills Regulations. (mine d'uranium)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: water body means any body of water, including a canal, a reservoir, an ocean and a wetland, up to the high-water mark, but does not include a sewage or waste treatment lagoon or a mine tailings pond. (plan d'eau)

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 1 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment in a wildlife area, as defined in section 2 of the Wildlife Area Regulations, a migratory bird sanctuary, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Migratory Bird Sanctuary Regulations or a protected marine area established under subsection 4.1(1) of the Canada Wildlife Act, of one of the following:

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (a) a new electrical generating facility or electrical transmission line;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (b) a new structure for the diversion of water, including a new dam, dyke or reservoir;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (c) a new oil or gas facility or oil and gas pipeline;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (d) a new mine or mill;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (e) a new industrial facility;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (f) a new canal or lock;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (g) a new marine terminal;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (h) a new railway line;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (i) a new public road or parkway that is intended for the passage of motor vehicles;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (j) a new aerodrome or runway;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (k) a new waste management facility;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (l) a new aquaculture facility.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 2 The construction, in a national marine conservation area, of a new physical work if the construction is contrary to the management plan for that area tabled in or laid before each House of Parliament under subsection 9(1) of the Canada National Marine Conservation Areas Act or subsection 9(1) of the Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park Act.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 3 The disposal at sea, in a national marine conservation area, of waste or other matter as defined in subsection 122(1) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 at a new disposal at sea site or a new part of an existing disposal at sea site.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 4 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment, in a national marine conservation area, of a new pipeline for carrying a substance other than water.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 5 The construction, on land that is managed or administered by the Parks Canada Agency, of a new physical work, if the construction is

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (a) contrary to the management plan for that land that is tabled in each House of Parliament under subsection 32(1) of the Parks Canada Agency Act, subsection 11(1) of the Canada National Parks Act, or subsection 9(1) of the Rouge National Urban Park Act, or to a similar plan for the land that is approved by the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency; or

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (b) contrary to one of the following guidelines that is published by the Parks Canada Agency and that applies to that land:

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (i) the Marmot Basin Ski Area Site Guidelines for Development and Use dated February 2008,

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (ii) the Mt. Norquay Ski Area Site Guidelines for Development and Use dated July 2011,

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (iii) the Lake Louise Ski Area Site Guidelines for Development and Use dated July 2015,

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (iv) the Site Guidelines for Development and Use, Sunshine Village Ski Resort dated December 14, 2018.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 6 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment, in a national park, of a new dam or structure for the diversion of water for the purpose of supplying water outside the park, of recreation or of electrical power generation.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 7 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment, in a national park, of a structure that is required to implement a new agreement made under paragraph 10(2)(b) of the Canada National Parks Act.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 8 The expansion, in a national park, of the water supply capacity of a structure that was constructed to implement an agreement made under paragraph 10(2)(b) of the Canada National Parks Act by more than 20%.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 9 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment, in Yoho National Park of Canada, Kootenay National Park of Canada, Banff National Park of Canada or Jasper National Park of Canada, outside of a commercial ski area referred to in Schedule 5 to the Canada National Parks Act and of a park community, of a new commercial development that requires the disposal or occupation of land that was not previously disposed of for the purpose of a commercial development with the same or a similar purpose or occupied by such a commercial development, if that new commercial development has not been subject to strategic environmental assessment and public review as part of the park management plan tabled in each House of Parliament under subsection 11(1) of the Canada National Parks Act.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 10 The expansion, in Yoho National Park of Canada, Kootenay National Park of Canada, Banff National Park of Canada or Jasper National Park of Canada, outside of a commercial ski area referred to in Schedule 5 to the Canada National Parks Act and of a park community, of an existing commercial development that requires the disposal or occupation of land that was not previously disposed of for the purpose of a commercial development with the same or a similar purpose or occupied by such a commercial development, if that existing commercial development has not been subject to strategic environmental assessment and public review as part of a park management plan tabled in each House of Parliament under subsection 11(1) of the Canada National Parks Act.

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: 11 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment, in a national park, of either of the following:

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (a) a new railway line;

heading: National Parks and Protected Areas
paragraph: (b) a new public road or parkway that is intended for the passage of motor vehicles.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 12 The low-level flying of military fixed-wing jet aircraft, for more than 150 days in a calendar year, as part of a training program, at an altitude below 330 m above ground level on a route or in an area that was not established before October 7, 1994 by or under the authority of the Minister of National Defence or the Chief of the Defence Staff as a route or area set aside for low-level flying training.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 13 The construction and operation of a new military base or military station that is established for more than 12 consecutive months.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 14 The expansion of an existing military base or military station, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of the military base or military station of 50% or more.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 15 The decommissioning and abandonment of an existing military base or military station.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 16 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment, outside an existing military base, of a new military training area, range or test establishment for training or weapons testing that is established for more than 12 consecutive months.

heading: Defence
paragraph: 17 The testing of military weapons for more than five days in a calendar year in an area other than a training area, range or test establishment established before October 7, 1994 by or under the authority of the Minister of National Defence for the testing of weapons.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 18 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of one of the following:

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (a) a new coal mine with a coal production capacity of 5 000 t/day or more;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (b) a new diamond mine with an ore production capacity of 5 000 t/day or more;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (c) a new metal mine, other than a rare earth element mine, placer mine or uranium mine, with an ore production capacity of 5 000 t/day or more;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (d) a new metal mill, other than a uranium mill, with an ore input capacity of 5 000 t/day or more;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (e) a new rare earth element mine with an ore production capacity of 2 500 t/day or more;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (f) a new stone quarry or sand or gravel pit with a production capacity of 3 500 000 t/year or more.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 19 The expansion of an existing mine, mill, quarry or sand or gravel pit in one of the following circumstances:

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (a) in the case of an existing coal mine, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total coal production capacity would be 5 000 t/day or more after the expansion;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (b) in the case of an existing diamond mine if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total ore production capacity would be 5 000 t/day or more after the expansion;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (c) in the case of an existing metal mine, other than a rare earth element mine, placer mine or uranium mine, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total ore production capacity would be 5 000 t/day or more after the expansion;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (d) in the case of an existing metal mill, other than a uranium mill, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total ore input capacity would be 5 000 t/day or more after the expansion;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (e) in the case of an existing rare earth element mine if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total ore production capacity would be 2 500 t/day or more after the expansion;

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: (f) in the case of an existing stone quarry or sand or gravel pit if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total production capacity would be 3 500 000 t/year or more after the expansion.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 20 The construction, operation and decommissioning, outside the licensed boundaries of an existing uranium mine, of a new uranium mine with an ore production capacity of 2 500 t/day or more.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 21 The expansion of an existing uranium mine, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total ore production capacity would be 2500 t/day or more after the expansion.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 22 The construction, operation and decommissioning, outside the licensed boundaries of an existing uranium mill, of a new uranium mill with an ore input capacity of 2 500 t/day or more.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 23 The expansion of an existing uranium mill, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total ore input capacity would be 2 500 t/day or more after the expansion.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 24 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new oil sands mine with a bitumen production capacity of 10 000 m3/day or more.

heading: Mines and Metal Mills
paragraph: 25 The expansion of an existing oil sands mine, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of mining operations of 50% or more and the total bitumen production capacity would be 10 000 m3/day or more after the expansion.

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: 26 The construction, operation and decommissioning of one of the following:

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: (a) a new facility for the processing, reprocessing or separation of isotopes of uranium, thorium, or plutonium, with a production capacity of 100 t/year or more;

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: (b) a new facility for the manufacture of a product derived from uranium, thorium or plutonium, with a production capacity of 100 t/year or more;

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: (c) a new facility for the processing or use, in a quantity greater than 1015 Bq per calendar year, of nuclear substances with a half-life greater than one year, other than uranium, thorium or plutonium.

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: 27 The site preparation for, and the construction, operation and decommissioning of, one or more new nuclear fission or fusion reactors if

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: (a) that activity is located within the licensed boundaries of an existing Class IA nuclear facility and the new reactors have a combined thermal capacity of more than 900 MWth; or

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: (b) that activity is not located within the licensed boundaries of an existing Class IA nuclear facility and the new reactors have a combined thermal capacity of more than 200 MWth.

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: 28 The construction and operation of either of the following:

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: (a) a new facility for the storage of irradiated nuclear fuel or nuclear waste, outside the licensed boundaries of an existing nuclear facility, as defined in section 2 of the Nuclear Safety and Control Act, other than a facility for the on-site storage of irradiated nuclear fuel or nuclear waste associated with one or more new fission or fusion reactors that have a combined thermal capacity of less than 200 MWth;

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: (b) a new facility for the long-term management or disposal of irradiated nuclear fuel or nuclear waste.

heading: Nuclear Facilities, Including Certain Storage and Long-term Management or Disposal Facilities
paragraph: 29 The expansion of an existing facility for the long-term management or disposal of irradiated nuclear fuel or nuclear waste, if the expansion would result in an increase in the area of the facility, at ground level, of 50% or more.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 30 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new fossil fuel-fired power generating facility with a production capacity of 200 MW or more.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 31 The expansion of an existing fossil fuel-fired power generating facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in production capacity of 50% or more and a total production capacity of 200 MW or more.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 32 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new in situ oil sands extraction facility that has a bitumen production capacity of 2 000 m3/day or more and that is

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (a) not within a province in which provincial legislation is in force to limit the amount of greenhouse gas emissions produced by oil sands sites in the province; or

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (b) within a province in which provincial legislation is in force to limit the amount of greenhouse gas emissions produced by oil sands sites in the province and that limit has been reached.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 33 The expansion of an existing in situ oil sands extraction facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in bitumen production capacity of 50% or more and a total bitumen production capacity of 2 000 m3/day or more, if the facility is

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (a) not within a province in which provincial legislation is in force to limit the amount of greenhouse gas emissions produced by oil sands sites in the province; or

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (b) within a province in which provincial legislation is in force to limit the amount of greenhouse gas emissions produced by oil sands sites in the province and that limit has been reached.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 34 The drilling, testing and abandonment, in an area set out in one or more exploration licences issued in accordance with the Canada Petroleum Resources Act, the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Atlantic Accord Implementation Act or the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Resources Accord Implementation Act, of offshore exploratory wells in the first drilling program, as defined in subsection 1(1) of the Canada Oil and Gas Drilling and Production Regulations, SOR/2009-315.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 35 The construction, installation and operation of a new offshore floating or fixed platform, vessel or artificial island used for the production of oil or gas.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 36 The decommissioning and abandonment of an existing offshore floating or fixed platform, vessel or artificial island used for the production of oil or gas that is proposed to be disposed of or abandoned offshore or converted on site to another role.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 37 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of one of the following:

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (a) a new oil refinery, including a heavy oil upgrader, with an input capacity of 10 000 m3/day or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (b) a new facility for the production of liquid petroleum products from coal with a production capacity of 2 000 m3/day or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (c) a new sour gas processing facility with a sulphur inlet capacity of 2 000 t/day or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (d) a new facility for the liquefaction, storage or regasification of liquefied natural gas, with a liquefied natural gas processing capacity of 3 000 t/day or more or a liquefied natural gas storage capacity of 136 000 m3 or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (e) a new petroleum storage facility with a storage capacity of 500 000 m3 or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (f) a new natural gas liquids storage facility with a storage capacity of 100 000 m3 or more.

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: 38 The expansion of one of the following:

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (a) an existing oil refinery, including a heavy oil upgrader, if the expansion would result in an increase in input capacity of 50% or more and a total input capacity of 10 000 m3/day or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (b) an existing facility for the production of liquid petroleum products from coal, if the expansion would result in an increase in production capacity of 50% or more and a total production capacity of 2 000 m3/day or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (c) an existing sour gas processing facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in sulphur inlet capacity of 50% or more and a total sulphur inlet capacity of 2 000 t/day or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (d) an existing facility for the liquefaction, storage or regasification of liquefied natural gas, if the expansion would result in an increase in the liquefied natural gas processing or storage capacity of 50% or more and a total liquefied natural gas processing capacity of 3 000 t/day or more or a total liquefied natural gas storage capacity of 136 000 m3 or more, as the case may be;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (e) an existing petroleum storage facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in storage capacity of 50% or more and a total storage capacity of 500 000 m3 or more;

heading: Oil, Gas and Other Fossil Fuels
paragraph: (f) an existing natural gas liquids storage facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in storage capacity of 50% or more and a total storage capacity of 100 000 m3 or more.

heading: Electrical Transmission Lines and Pipelines
paragraph: 39 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of either of the following:

heading: Electrical Transmission Lines and Pipelines
paragraph: (a) a new international electrical transmission line with a voltage of 345 kV or more that requires a total of 75 km or more of new right of way;

heading: Electrical Transmission Lines and Pipelines
paragraph: (b) a new interprovincial power line designated by an order under section 261 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act.

heading: Electrical Transmission Lines and Pipelines
paragraph: 40 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new offshore oil and gas pipeline, other than a flowline as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Oil and Gas Installations Regulations.

heading: Electrical Transmission Lines and Pipelines
paragraph: 41 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new pipeline, as defined in section 2 of the Canadian Energy Regulator Act, other than an offshore pipeline, that requires a total of 75 km or more of new right of way.

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: 42 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of one of the following:

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: (a) a new hydroelectric generating facility with a production capacity of 200 MW or more;

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: (b) a new in-stream tidal power generating facility with a production capacity of 15 MW or more;

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: (c) a new tidal power generating facility that is not an in-stream tidal power generating facility.

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: 43 The expansion of one of the following:

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: (a) an existing hydroelectric generating facility if the expansion would result in an increase in production capacity of 50% or more and a total production capacity of 200 MW or more;

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: (b) an existing in-stream tidal power generating facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in production capacity of 50% or more and a total production capacity of 15 MW or more;

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: (c) an existing tidal power generating facility that is not an in-stream tidal power generating facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in production capacity of 50% or more.

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: 44 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment in an offshore area or in boundary water of a new wind power generating facility that has 10 or more wind turbines.

heading: Renewable Energy
paragraph: 45 The expansion in an offshore area or in boundary water of an existing wind power generating facility, if the expansion would result in an increase in production capacity of 50% or more and a total number of wind turbines of 10 or more.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 46 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of one of the following:

heading: Transport
paragraph: (a) a new aerodrome with a runway length of 1 000 m or more;

heading: Transport
paragraph: (b) a new aerodrome that is capable of serving aircraft of Aircraft Group Number IIIA or higher;

heading: Transport
paragraph: (c) a new runway at an existing aerodrome with a length of 1 000 m or more.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 47 The operation of an existing runway

heading: Transport
paragraph: (a) that was not capable of serving aircraft of Aircraft Group Number IIIA and becomes capable of serving aircraft of Aircraft Group Number IIIA or higher; or

heading: Transport
paragraph: (b) that was capable of serving aircraft of an Aircraft Group Number IIIA or higher and becomes capable of serving aircraft of any higher Aircraft Group Number.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 48 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of either of the following:

heading: Transport
paragraph: (a) a new international or interprovincial bridge or tunnel;

heading: Transport
paragraph: (b) a new bridge over the St. Lawrence Seaway.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 49 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of either of the following:

heading: Transport
paragraph: (a) a new canal;

heading: Transport
paragraph: (b) a new lock or associated structure that controls water levels in navigable water.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 50 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new permanent causeway with a continuous length of 400 m or more through navigable water.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 51 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new all-season public highway that requires a total of 75 km or more of new right of way.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 52 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new marine terminal designed to handle ships larger than 25 000 DWT.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 53 The expansion of an existing marine terminal, if the expansion requires the construction of a new berth designed to handle ships larger than 25 000 DWT and, if the berth is not a permanent structure in the water, the construction of a new permanent structure in the water.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 54 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of either of the following:

heading: Transport
paragraph: (a) a new railway line that is capable of carrying freight or of carrying passengers between cities and requires a total of 50 km or more of new right of way;

heading: Transport
paragraph: (b) a new railway yard with a total area of 50 ha or more.

heading: Transport
paragraph: 55 The expansion of an existing railway yard, if the expansion would result in an increase of its total area by 50% or more and a total area of 50 ha or more.

heading: Hazardous Waste
paragraph: 56 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new facility that is not more than 500 m from a natural water body and is used exclusively for the treatment, incineration, disposal or recycling of hazardous waste.

heading: Hazardous Waste
paragraph: 57 The expansion of an existing facility that is not more than 500 m from a natural water body and is used exclusively for the treatment, incineration, disposal or recycling of hazardous waste, if the expansion would result in an increase in hazardous waste input capacity of 50% or more.

heading: Water Projects
paragraph: 58 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new dam or dyke on a natural water body, if the new dam or dyke would result in the creation of a reservoir with a surface area that would exceed the annual mean surface area of the natural water body by 1 500 ha or more.

heading: Water Projects
paragraph: 59 The expansion of an existing dam or dyke on a natural water body, if the expansion would result in an increase in the surface area of the existing reservoir of 50% or more and an increase of 1 500 ha or more in the annual mean surface area of that reservoir.

heading: Water Projects
paragraph: 60 The construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of a new structure for the diversion of 10 000 000 m3/year or more of water from a natural water body into another natural water body.

heading: Water Projects
paragraph: 61 The expansion of an existing structure for the diversion of water from a natural water body into another natural water body, if the expansion would result in an increase in diversion capacity of 50% or more and a total diversion capacity of 10 000 000 m3/year or more.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assessor" means an assessor appointed under the Assessment Authority Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "board" has the same meaning as in the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "commission" has the same meaning as in the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "council" means the Private Managed Forest Land Council established under section 4;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "exit fee" includes interest that is calculated in accordance with the regulations;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "management commitment" means a management commitment that, as determined by the council, meets the applicable requirements of section 17 and includes any amendment made to the management commitment that, as determined by the council, meets the applicable requirements of section 17;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "owner" means the person registered in the records under the Land Title Act as owner of the land in respect of which there is a management commitment and that is classified as managed forest land under the Assessment Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "private managed forest land" means private land

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in respect of which there is a management commitment, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) that is classified as managed forest land under the Assessment Act.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2		  (1) Nothing in this Act restricts a person from carrying out fire suppression activities in accordance with the Wildfire Act and the regulations under that Act.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner does not contravene a provision of this Act or the regulations because of an activity that if carried out by the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner would be a contravention, if the activity is carried out by a person who is authorized under another enactment

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) to be on the owner's private managed forest land, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) to carry out the activity.

heading: Application
paragraph: 3		  This Act applies to private managed forest land other than land that is in a tree farm licence area, a woodlot licence area or a community forest agreement area.

heading: Council established
paragraph:
4
		  The Private Managed Forest Land Council is established as a corporation consisting of the members appointed under section 6.

heading: Object of council
paragraph:
5
		  The object of the council is to encourage forest management practices on private managed forest land, taking into account the social, environmental and economic benefits of those practices.

heading: Council members
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The minister must

heading: Council members
paragraph: (a) appoint 2 council members, and

heading: Council members
paragraph: (b) establish the terms of their appointment.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the owners must appoint 2 council members in accordance with the procedures set out in bylaws of the council and establish the terms of the appointment of those members.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (3) If the owners do not appoint the council members referred to in subsection (2), the council members may be appointed by the minister in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (4) Council members appointed by the minister or by the owners must be knowledgeable in matters relating to

heading: Council members
paragraph: (a) forest management practices, or

heading: Council members
paragraph: (b) local government.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (5) The council members appointed under this section must appoint an additional person as a member of the council and designate that person to be the chair of the council.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (6) If, within 60 days after the expiry of the term of the chair, the council members do not appoint a new chair, the minister may appoint an additional person to the council, designate that person to be the chair and set the terms of the chair's appointment, as long as

heading: Council members
paragraph: (a) the chair is selected from a list of persons provided by the remaining council members, and

heading: Council members
paragraph: (b) the appointment is for no longer than 6 months.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (7) If the minister considers it necessary or advisable

heading: Council members
paragraph: (a) a chair appointed under subsection (6) may be reappointed for a further period of 6 months, or

heading: Council members
paragraph: (b) another chair may be appointed, as long as subsection (6) (a) and (b) applies.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (8) The council must designate one of its members as vice chair.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (9) A council member or former council member may be reappointed to the council.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (10) A council member appointed by the owners may be removed in accordance with the procedures set out in bylaws of the council.

heading: Council members
paragraph: (11) The council members are the board of directors of the council.

heading: Staff of council
paragraph:
7
		  (1) The council may appoint employees necessary for its purposes and may determine their duties and remuneration.

heading: Staff of council
paragraph: (2) The council may retain consultants as it considers advisable and may set their remuneration.

heading: Staff of council
paragraph: (3) The Public Service Act, the Public Sector Pension Plans Act and the Public Service Labour Relations Act do not apply to the council or its employees.

heading: Operation of council
paragraph: 8		  (1) The council may pass resolutions and bylaws it considers necessary or advisable for the management and conduct of its affairs, the performance of its duties and the exercise of its powers.

heading: Operation of council
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (4), the council may refer a matter that is before the council to a panel established by the council consisting of one or more council members as determined by the council.

heading: Operation of council
paragraph: (3) A panel established under subsection (2) has all the powers and duties of the council and a decision of the panel is, for all purposes, a decision of the council.

heading: Operation of council
paragraph: (4) The council must not refer the making of a resolution, bylaw or regulation to a panel of the council.

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph:
9
		  (1) In this section, "bare land assessed value" means the value of managed forest land as determined under section 24 (4) (a) of the Assessment Act.

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (2) An owner must pay an annual administration fee to the council on or before the date established by regulation of the council for each year during which the owner's land is private managed forest land.

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (3) The council must set the rate of the annual administration fee payable under subsection (2) for each fiscal year

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (a) as a percentage of the bare land assessed value of private managed forest land, and

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (b) so that the total amount of the annual administration fee collected proportionally from all of the owners and any other revenue of the council are sufficient to fund the council's operations for that fiscal year.

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (4) If at any time during the fiscal year for which the annual administration fee has been calculated and collected, the total calculated and collected appears to the council to be insufficient to fund the council's operations for the months remaining in that fiscal year, the council

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (a) must notify the owners of, and provide information to the owners about, the insufficiency, and

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (b) may establish a levy to pay for the insufficiency.

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (5) A levy established by the council under subsection (4) (b) must be set as a percentage of the bare land assessed value of private managed forest land and collected proportionally from all of the owners.

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (6) If at the end of a fiscal year for which the annual administration fee or a levy has been collected there is a surplus, the council may do one or more of the following:

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (a) return the surplus or part of it to the owners who contributed to it, in proportion to their contributions;

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (b) set the surplus or part of it off from the total amount referred to in subsection (3) (b) for the following fiscal year;

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (c) retain the surplus or part of it and dispose of it to further the fulfillment of the council's object.

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (7) The council must, in accordance with the regulations of the council, notify the owners as soon as practicable of

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (a) the amount of the annual administration fee or a levy and the date by which the fee or levy must be paid, and

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (b) the following with respect to any surplus:

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (i)  the amount of the surplus;

heading: Annual administration fee, levy and surplus
paragraph: (ii)  the disposition of the surplus.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: 10		  (1) The fiscal year of the council begins on April 1 of each year and ends on March 31 of the following year.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (2) The council must publish an annual report for each year of operation of the council that contains information about the following:

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (a) the number of owners;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (b) the number of hectares subject to the Act;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (c) the number of management commitments withdrawn;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (d) the number and nature of inspections performed;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (e) the number and nature of consent agreements;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (f) the amount of penalties collected and the amount of penalties owing;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (g) the number and nature of remediation orders made;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (h) the number and nature of stop work orders made;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (i) new regulations enacted by the council;

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (j) any other information the council considers relevant to the fulfillment of its object or the exercise of its powers and performance of its functions and duties under this Act.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (3) The council must submit the report under subsection (2) to the minister and publish it.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), the Business Corporations Act does not apply to the council.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, declare that specified provisions of the Business Corporations Act apply to the council.

heading: Financial and corporate matters
paragraph: (6) The council may acquire and dispose of property and borrow and invest money for the purposes of fulfilling its object, exercising its powers and performing its functions and duties under this Act.

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: 11		  (1) The minister may order an independent audit by the board or other auditor, of the performance of the council in fulfilling its object or exercising its powers and performing its functions and duties under this Act.

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (2) The minister must provide terms of reference for the audit.

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (3) If requested by the auditor appointed under subsection (1), the council must submit records in its possession that are relevant to the audit.

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (4) Before an audit report is finalized, the auditor must provide to the council

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (a) a copy of the draft audit report, and

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (b) a reasonable opportunity to review and comment on the report.

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (5) As soon as practicable after completing an audit, the auditor must submit the final audit report and any comments of the council to

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (a) the minister, and

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (b) the council.

heading: Minister may order audit of council performance
paragraph: (6) The minister must publish the final audit report and any comments of the council.

heading: Soil conservation
paragraph:
12
		  The forest management objective for private managed forest land with respect to conservation of soil for areas where harvesting has been carried out is to protect soil productivity on those areas by minimizing the amount of area occupied by permanent roads, landings and excavated or bladed trails.

heading: Water quality
paragraph:
13
		  (1) The forest management objective for private managed forest land with respect to water quality is to protect human drinking water, both during and after harvesting.

heading: Water quality
paragraph: (2) Nothing in subsection (1) requires an owner to retain additional streamside trees or additional understory vegetation to address problems with water quality that originate outside of the owner's private managed forest land.

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph:
14
		  (1) The forest management objective for private managed forest land with respect to the protection of fish habitat, both during and after harvesting, is to retain sufficient streamside mature trees and understory vegetation to protect all of the following:

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (a) a natural variation in water temperatures;

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (b) sufficient cover for fish;

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (c) a continual source of large woody debris for stream channel stability purposes;

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (d) a vigorous mass of roots capable of controlling stream bank erosion;

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (e) a filter to prevent the transport of sediment into stream channels;

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (f) woody debris sufficient for in-stream habitat;

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (g) a source of nutrients to the stream through litter fall.

heading: Fish habitat
paragraph: (2) Nothing in subsection (1) requires an owner to retain additional streamside trees or additional understory vegetation to address problems with fish habitat that originate outside of the owner's private managed forest land.

heading: Critical wildlife habitat
paragraph:
15
		  The forest management objective for private managed forest land with respect to critical wildlife habitat is to facilitate the long term protection of that habitat by

heading: Critical wildlife habitat
paragraph: (a) providing a reasonable opportunity for a person designated in writing by the deputy minister to the minister responsible for the administration of the Wildlife Act to assess whether critical wildlife habitat is present on private managed forest land, and

heading: Critical wildlife habitat
paragraph: (b) fostering efforts of the government and the owners to enter into agreements for the protection of any critical wildlife habitat identified under paragraph (a).

heading: Reforestation
paragraph: 16		  The forest management objective for private managed forest land with respect to reforestation of areas where timber has been harvested or destroyed is to promptly regenerate the areas with a healthy, commercially valuable stand of trees that is not impeded by competition from plants or shrubs.

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph:
17
		  (0.1) In this section, "private land" does not include the treaty lands of a treaty first nation or Nisga'a Lands.

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (1) Before private land may be classified as private managed forest land under this Act or managed forest land under the Assessment Act, the landowner or owner must submit to the council a proposed management commitment that is in the prescribed form and contains

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (a) the legal description of the land to which the management commitment relates and any other information specified in regulations of the council, and

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (b) an acknowledgement of the requirements to

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (i)  pay the annual administration fee under section 9

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (ii)  pay the exit fee under section 19, if applicable, and

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (iii)  otherwise comply with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (2) An owner may at any time submit to the council an amendment to a management commitment that meets the applicable requirements of subsection (1) and the regulations of the council.

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (3) The council must

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (a) review the proposed management commitment or amendment to determine if it complies with the applicable requirements of subsection (1) and the regulations of the council, and

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (b) notify the landowner or owner of its determination under paragraph (a) and if the council concludes that the management commitment or amendment does not comply with the applicable requirements, provide reasons.

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (4) If the council determines that a proposed management commitment or amendment meets the applicable requirements of subsection (1) and complies with the regulations of the council, the council must notify the assessor and recommend to the assessor that the land that is the subject of the management commitment or amendment be classified as managed forest land under the Assessment Act.

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (5) After classifying land that is the subject of a management commitment as managed forest land under the Assessment Act, the assessor must notify the council and the owner.

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (6) A management commitment that the council determines meets the requirements of subsection (1) and the regulations is ineffective to the extent that

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (a) it contains information in addition to the information required under subsection (1), and

heading: Application for private managed forest land
paragraph: (b) the additional information conflicts with a provision of this Act or the regulations in effect on the date of the council's determination.

heading: Withdrawal of management commitment
paragraph: 18		  An owner may give written notice in the prescribed form and with the prescribed content to the council that the owner is withdrawing his or her management commitment.

heading: Exit fee
paragraph:
19
		  (1) Except when exempted by regulation or in prescribed circumstances, an owner must pay an exit fee in accordance with the regulations if the assessor declassifies the land under section 24 (3) (b) of the Assessment Act.

heading: Exit fee
paragraph: (2) If an owner from whom an exit fee is recoverable is an owner of property that is subject to property taxation under the Local Government Act, Taxation (Rural Area) Act or Vancouver Charter, the exit fee may be recovered as follows:

heading: Exit fee
paragraph: (a) in the case of property within a municipality, the council must file a notice of the amount of the exit fee with the municipality, which may collect the amount in the same manner as taxes against the property under the Local Government Act or the Vancouver Charter, as applicable;

heading: Exit fee
paragraph: (b) in the case of other property, the council must file a notice of the amount of the exit fee with the Surveyor of Taxes appointed under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, who may collect the amount in the same manner as taxes against the property under that Act.

heading: Exit fee
