paragraph: (3) If an amount is to be collected under subsection (2), the amount is deemed to be a municipal or Provincial tax, as applicable, and must be dealt with in the same manner as taxes against the property would be under the Local Government Act, Taxation (Rural Area) Act or Vancouver Charter, as applicable, and the following apply:

heading: Exit fee
paragraph: (a) in the case of property within a municipality, the municipality may retain the amount collected as though it were a tax against property;

heading: Exit fee
paragraph: (b) in the case of other property, the Surveyor of Taxes must deposit the amount collected in the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Exit fee
paragraph: (4) The minister must conduct a review of the manner in which the exit fee is calculated under the regulations at least once every 5 years.

heading: Annual declaration
paragraph: 20		  An owner must submit to the council on or before May 1 of each year, a declaration in the prescribed form that contains all of the following information with respect to the private managed forest land of the owner for the preceding operating season:

heading: Annual declaration
paragraph: (a) the location and size of areas where timber was harvested;

heading: Annual declaration
paragraph: (b) the location and size of areas where timber was destroyed and the cause or probable cause of the destruction;

heading: Annual declaration
paragraph: (c) the location and approximate length of roads constructed;

heading: Annual declaration
paragraph: (d) any other information prescribed by the council.

heading: Restriction on local government authority regarding uses of private managed forest land
paragraph:
21
		  (1) A local government must not do any of the following in respect of land that is private managed forest land if doing so would have the effect of restricting, directly or indirectly, a forest management activity:

heading: Restriction on local government authority regarding uses of private managed forest land
paragraph: (a) adopt a bylaw under any enactment;

heading: Restriction on local government authority regarding uses of private managed forest land
paragraph: (b) issue a permit under section 8 (3) (l) [authority in relation to buildings and other structures] of the Community Charter or Division 1 [Building Regulation] of Part 9 [Regional Districts: Specific Service Powers] of the Local Government Act;

heading: Restriction on local government authority regarding uses of private managed forest land
paragraph: (c) issue a permit under Part 14 [Planning and Land Use Management] of the Local Government Act.

heading: Restriction on local government authority regarding uses of private managed forest land
paragraph: (2) For certainty, this section applies if the bylaw or permit would have the effect described in subsection (1) even though the bylaw or permit does not directly apply to land referred to in that subsection.

heading: Production of records
paragraph: 22		  The council may require that an owner or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the owner submit records in that person's custody or control if the council considers it necessary in determining whether the owner or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the owner has contravened or is contravening a provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph:
23
		  (1) For any purpose related to the administration of this Act or the regulations, including administrative remedies under this Part, the council or a person authorized in writing by the council may enter on private managed forest land at any reasonable time if the council has reasonable grounds to believe that the private managed forest land is the site of an activity regulated under this Act.

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph: (2) A person who enters on private managed forest land under this section

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph: (a) may inspect any thing or activity that is reasonably related to the purpose for which the council entered on the private managed forest land,

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph: (b) may require production for inspecting or copying either or both of the following:

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph: (i)  an authorization to engage in the activity;

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph: (ii)  a record required to be kept in accordance with a provision of this Act or the regulations, and

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph: (c) on the request of the person who has apparent custody or control of the property or activity being inspected, must provide proof of identity to that person.

heading: Right of entry of council
paragraph: (3) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must admit the council or authorized person to all parts of the private managed forest land for the purposes of this section.

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph:
24
		  (1) For any purpose related to the management of critical wildlife habitat on private managed forest land, the minister responsible for the administration of the Wildlife Act or any person authorized in writing by the minister may enter on private managed forest land at any reasonable time if the minister has reasonable grounds to believe that critical wildlife habitat is present on private managed forest land.

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph: (2) The minister or authorized person who enters on private managed forest land under this section

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph: (a) may inspect any thing or activity that is reasonably related to the purpose for which the person entered on the private managed forest land,

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph: (b) may require production for inspecting or copying either or both of the following:

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph: (i)  an authorization to engage in the activity;

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph: (ii)  a record required to be kept in accordance with a provision of this Act or the regulations, and

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph: (c) on the request of the person who has apparent custody or control of the property or activity being inspected, must provide proof of identity to that person.

heading: Right of entry of government
paragraph: (3) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must admit the minister or authorized person to all parts of the private managed forest land for the purposes of this section.

heading: Consent agreements
paragraph: 25		  (1) If the council and an owner agree that the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner may have contravened or is contravening a provision of this Act or the regulations, the council and the owner may enter into a consent agreement under which

heading: Consent agreements
paragraph: (a) the owner agrees to

heading: Consent agreements
paragraph: (i)  carry out any remedial measures specified in the agreement,

heading: Consent agreements
paragraph: (ii)  take any measures specified in the agreement to prevent the contravention from continuing or a similar contravention occurring in the future, and

heading: Consent agreements
paragraph: (iii)  pay to the council a penalty, not greater than $5 000, that is specified in the agreement, and

heading: Consent agreements
paragraph: (b) the council agrees not to make any further determinations or orders under this Division with respect to the contravention unless the owner does not comply with the terms of the agreement.

heading: Consent agreements
paragraph: (2) An owner who enters into a consent agreement under subsection (1) must comply with the agreement.

heading: Penalties
paragraph:
26
		  (1) The council, after giving an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who is alleged to have contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations an opportunity to be heard, may determine whether the person has contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (2) After giving a person an opportunity to be heard under subsection (1), or after one month has elapsed after the date on which the person was given the opportunity, the council

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) if it determines that the person has contravened the provision,

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (i)  may levy an administrative penalty against the person in an amount that does not exceed $25 000, or

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (ii)  may refrain from levying an administrative penalty against the person if the council considers that the contravention is trifling, or

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) may determine that the person has not contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (3) If a corporation contravenes a provision of this Act or the regulations, a director or an officer of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention also commits the contravention.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (4) The time limit for levying a penalty against a person under subsection (2) is 2 years after the facts on which the penalty is based first came to the knowledge of a council member or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the council.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (5) Before the council levies a penalty under subsection (2), it must consider all of the following:

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) any previous contravention of a similar nature by the person if the contravention was the subject of

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (i)  a determination under this section in the previous 10 years, or

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (ii)  a consent agreement under section 25 in the previous 12 months;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) the gravity and magnitude of the contravention;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (c) whether the contravention was repeated or continuous;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (d) whether the contravention was deliberate;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (e) any economic benefit derived by the person from the contravention;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (f) the person's cooperation and efforts to remedy the contravention;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (g) the person's efforts to prevent the contravention;

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (h) whether relevant forest management objectives specified in Division 1 of Part 3 are being achieved despite the contravention.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (6) If the council levies a penalty under subsection (2), the council must give a notice of determination to the person, and the owner if the owner is not the person against whom the penalty is levied, and the notice must set out

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) the nature of the contravention,

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) the amount of the penalty,

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (c) the date by which the penalty must be paid,

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (d) the person's right to request that the council reconsider the penalty, and

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (e) the person's right to appeal the penalty to the commission.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (7) If the council levies a penalty under subsection (2), the council must give particulars of the penalty to the Minister of Finance as soon as practicable

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) if there is no appeal of the penalty, after the end of the appeal period, and

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) if there is an appeal of the penalty, after the person who is the subject of the penalty has no further right of appeal.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (8) The council must not levy a penalty under this section on an owner if the council has entered into a consent agreement under section 25 with the owner and the owner is complying with the agreement.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (9) An order under subsection (2) (a) (i) that is filed in the court registry has the same effect as an order of the court for the recovery of a debt in the amount stated in the order against the person named in it, and all proceedings may be taken as if the order were an order of the court.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph:
27
		  (1) The council, after giving an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who is alleged to have contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations an opportunity to be heard, or after one month has elapsed after the date on which the person was given the opportunity, may determine whether the person has contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (2) If the council determines that an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner has contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations, the council may order the person to remedy the contravention by

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) carrying out a requirement of this Act or the regulations that the person has failed to carry out, or

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) repairing or mitigating damage to private managed forest land caused by the contravention,

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: and the person must comply with the order.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (3) The time limit for making an order under subsection (2) is 2 years after the facts on which the order is based first came to the knowledge of a council member or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the council.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (4) If the council makes an order under subsection (2), the council must give a copy of the order to the person named in the order, and the owner if the owner is not the person named in the order, and the order must set out

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (a) the nature of the contravention,

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (b) the nature of the work to be done to remedy the contravention,

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (c) the date by which the work must be completed,

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (d) the person's right to request that the council reconsider the order, and

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (e) the person's right to appeal the order to the commission.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (5) An owner must not obstruct a person who is complying with a remediation order.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (6) If the council makes an order under subsection (2) against a person other than the owner of the private managed forest land, the owner may, on written notice to the council in the prescribed form and in the prescribed manner, assume responsibility for complying with the order and the order is deemed to be an order naming the owner instead of the other person.

heading: Remediation orders
paragraph: (7) If an owner gives written notice to the council under subsection (6), the council must serve notice on the person who is named in the order that the owner has assumed responsibility for complying with the order and the person named in the order is not responsible for complying with that order.

heading: Limitation on proceedings
paragraph:
28
		  (1) The council must not levy a penalty under section 26 for a contravention in respect of which the government has proceeded with a prosecution of the contravention under a regulation that provides the contravention is an offence.

heading: Limitation on proceedings
paragraph: (2) The government must, in accordance with the regulations, stay a proceeding for an administrative remedy under section 26 in respect of a contravention if the government has proceeded with a prosecution of the contravention under a regulation that provides the contravention is an offence.

heading: Defences to administrative proceedings
paragraph:
29
		  For the purposes of a determination of the council under sections 26 and 27, a person must not be found to have contravened a provision of this Act or the regulations if the person establishes that

heading: Defences to administrative proceedings
paragraph: (a) the person exercised all due diligence to prevent the contravention,

heading: Defences to administrative proceedings
paragraph: (b) the person reasonably and honestly believed in the existence of facts that if true would establish that the person did not contravene the provision, or

heading: Defences to administrative proceedings
paragraph: (c) the person's actions relevant to the provision were the result of an officially induced error.

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph:
30
		  (1) If the council or a person authorized in writing by the council considers that an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner is contravening a provision of this Act or the regulations, the council or authorized person may order that the contravention cease, or cease to the extent specified by the order.

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (2) An order under this section may be made to apply generally or to one or more owners or persons named in the order.

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (3) An order under this section must be in writing and include

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (a) the nature of the contravention,

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (b) the extent to which the contravention must cease, and

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (c) the date by which the requirement of paragraph (b) must be met,

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: and the person named in the order must comply with that order.

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), if the council or authorized person is of the opinion that the contravention is causing, or may imminently cause, serious damage to the environment, the council or authorized person may order that the contravention cease, or cease to a specified extent, and subject to subsection (5), the order need not be in writing.

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (5) Within 96 hours of making a stop work order under subsection (4), the council or authorized person must issue the order in writing, as specified in subsection (3), or the order ceases to be effective.

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (6) The council or authorized person may

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (a) rescind a stop work order if the council or authorized person determines that there were insufficient grounds for issuing the order, or

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (b) vary a stop work order

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (i)  on new information being provided, and

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (ii)  with the consent of the owner or person who is the subject of the order.

heading: Stop work orders
paragraph: (7) Despite subsection (6), the council or authorized person may not rescind or vary a stop work order that is the subject of a decision of the council under section 32.

heading: Notification to assessor
paragraph:
31
		  (1) The council may notify the assessor that an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner, in the course of carrying out the contract, employment or agency, has contravened or is contravening a provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Notification to assessor
paragraph: (2) On September 30 of each year the council must notify the assessor of

heading: Notification to assessor
paragraph: (a) the names of the owners and the legal descriptions of private managed forest land, and

heading: Notification to assessor
paragraph: (b) the names of the owners and the legal descriptions of land in respect of which a management commitment has been withdrawn under section 18 during the preceding 12 months.

heading: Power of the council to rescind or vary orders, decisions or determinations
paragraph:
32
		  (1) On the request of an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner, or on its own initiative, the council may rescind an order, a decision or a determination made by the council or an authorized person under this Act if the council determines that there were insufficient grounds for making the order, decision or determination.

heading: Power of the council to rescind or vary orders, decisions or determinations
paragraph: (2) On the request of an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner, or on its own initiative, the council may vary an order, a decision or a determination made by the council or authorized person under this Act

heading: Power of the council to rescind or vary orders, decisions or determinations
paragraph: (a) on new information being provided to the council, and

heading: Power of the council to rescind or vary orders, decisions or determinations
paragraph: (b) with the consent of the person who was the subject of the order, decision or determination.

heading: Power of the council to rescind or vary orders, decisions or determinations
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), the council may not rescind or vary an order, a decision or a determination that is the subject of an appeal under section 33 after the conclusion of the appeal.

heading: Power of the council to rescind or vary orders, decisions or determinations
paragraph: (4) If the council rescinds or varies an order, a decision or a determination under this section and the order, decision or determination is the subject of an appeal under section 33 that is not yet concluded, the council must notify the commission.

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A person who is the subject of an order, a decision or a determination of the council under section 26 (1), 27 (1) and (2), 30, 31 (1) or 32 may appeal the order, decision or determination to the commission in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph: (2) An order, a decision or a determination that may be appealed under this section, other than a stop work order, is stayed until the person who is the subject of the order, decision or determination has no further right to have the order, decision or determination appealed.

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph: (4) The appellant and the council are parties to the appeal and may be represented by counsel.

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph: (6) The commission may invite or permit any person who may be materially affected by the outcome of an appeal to take part in the appeal as an intervenor in the manner and to the extent permitted or ordered by the commission.

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph: (15) An appeal under this section to the commission is a new hearing and at the conclusion of the hearing, the commission may

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph: (a) by order, confirm, vary or rescind the order, decision or determination,

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph: (b) refer the matter back to the council or authorized person for reconsideration with or without directions, or

heading: Appeal to commission
paragraph: (d) make any other order the commission considers appropriate.

heading: Application of Part 8.1 of Forest and Range Practices Act
paragraph:
33.1
		  Part 8.1 of the Forest and Range Practices Act applies to an appeal under this Act.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
35
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide, by regulation, that

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) a contravention of a regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council or a regulation of the council is an offence, and

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) a person convicted of an offence contravening a regulation is liable to a fine not exceeding $500 000.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) The time limit for laying an information respecting an offence under the regulations is 2 years after the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of a council member or a contractor, an employee or an agent of the council.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) In a prosecution of an offence for contravention of the regulations, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by the defendant's employee or agent even if the employee or agent has not been identified or prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (4) If a corporation commits an offence for contravening the regulations, a director or an officer of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence also commits the offence.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (5) A proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under the regulations does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (6) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Court orders
paragraph: 36		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any other punishment that may be imposed, the court may order the person to do one or more of the following:

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (a) refrain from doing anything that may result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (b) take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment that may result from the act or omission that constituted the offence;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (c) publish, at the person's own cost, the facts relating to the conviction;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (d) pay court costs;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (e) pay costs of the investigation;

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (f) pay compensation to make restitution.

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (2) The court that convicts a person of an offence under this Act may increase a fine imposed on the person by an amount equal to the court's estimation of the amount of the economic benefit derived by the person as a result of having committed the offence.

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (3) A fine increase under subsection (2)

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (a) applies despite any enactment that provides for a maximum fine, and

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (b) is in addition to any other fine under this Act.

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (4) Nothing in this section prevents a court that is determining the amount of a fine from taking into consideration

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (a) the payment of an administrative penalty, or

heading: Court orders
paragraph: (b) actions taken by the person before, during and after the commission of the offence.

heading: Defences to a prosecution
paragraph:
37
		  The following are defences to the prosecution of a person under this Act:

heading: Defences to a prosecution
paragraph: (a) the person exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence;

heading: Defences to a prosecution
paragraph: (b) the person reasonably and honestly believed in the existence of facts that if true would establish that the person did not commit the offence;

heading: Defences to a prosecution
paragraph: (c) the person's actions relevant to the offence were the result of an officially induced error.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph:
38
		  The provisions of this Part are in addition to the provisions of any other enactment or rule of law under which

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: (a) a remedy or right of appeal is provided, or

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: (b) a procedure is provided for inquiry into or investigation of a matter,

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph: and nothing in this Act limits or affects that remedy, right or procedure.

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph:
39
		  Subject to section 28, the powers in this Act and the regulations for the council or the commission to

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: (a) make an order, a decision or a determination,

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: (b) impose a fine or penalty, or

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: (c) commence a proceeding

heading: Powers cumulative
paragraph: may be exercised separately, concurrently or cumulatively and do not affect the powers of the government under this or any other enactment.

heading: Service and receipt of documents
paragraph:
40
		  If this Act or the regulations require or authorize the council to serve a notice or other document on a person, the service may be effected in one of the following ways:

heading: Service and receipt of documents
paragraph: (a) by personal service, in which case service is effected when the person is served;

heading: Service and receipt of documents
paragraph: (b) by registered mail to the person's last known address, in which case service is deemed to be effected on the 14th day after the document was sent by registered mail;

heading: Service and receipt of documents
paragraph: (c) if the person or address is not known, by publication once in a newspaper having general circulation in the locality in which the private managed forest land is situated, in which case service is deemed to be effected on the 7th day after the date of publication.

heading: Penalties into the consolidated revenue fund
paragraph:
41
		  Penalties under sections 25 and 26 must be paid into the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
42
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing procedures for appointment of council members in accordance with section 6 (3);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting the custodianship and disposition of property held by the council, including revenue from annual administration fees and levies charged to and collected from owners, if the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it necessary or advisable;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) respecting the management of critical wildlife habitat on private managed forest land, and without limitation, including the following:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  identification of critical wildlife habitat;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  notification to prescribed persons;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iii)  limitation on an activity within critical wildlife habitat provided that the limitation on activity, unless otherwise agreed to by the owner, does not exceed

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (A) 1% of the total area of private managed forest land owned by that person, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (B) a period of one year;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) specifying

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  the manner in which an exit fee to be paid in accordance with section 19 is to be calculated,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  to whom notification of an exit fee and its amount must be given by the council and the manner in which the council must give the notification,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iii)  when the exit fee must be paid, and

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iv)  the rate of interest that may be charged on exit fees and the manner of calculating the interest;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (e) exempting an owner from paying an exit fee in accordance with section 19 or prescribing circumstances when an exit fee is not required to be paid;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (f) prescribing the form of notices and manner in which notice is given by an owner under section 27 (6);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting stays of proceedings under section 28 (2);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i) specifying records that must be transferred from the Provincial Agricultural Land Commission established under section 4 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act to the council for the purposes of this Act and when the records must be transferred;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (j) subject to subsection (3), providing that contravention of a regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council or of a regulation of the council is an offence.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council must not make a regulation under subsection (2) (j), unless regulations are also made or enacted respecting stays of proceedings referred to in section 28 (2).

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting matters that are

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) referred to in this Act as having to be in accordance with the regulations, or

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) indicated by this Act as being a matter for regulation.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make a regulation defining a word or expression used but not defined in this Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (6) In making a regulation under this Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may do one or more of the following:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) delegate a matter to a person;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) confer a discretion on a person;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) make different regulations for different persons, places, things, transactions or special concerns, or classes of persons, places, things or transactions.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (7) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations establishing criteria that a person must use when exercising a discretionary power conferred on the person by this Act or the regulations.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (8) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations exempting a person, place or thing, or class of persons, places or things, from a requirement of this Act or the regulations and may make the exemption subject to conditions.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (9) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the recovery of money that is required to be paid to the government under this Act.

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: 43		  (1) The council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing procedures and rules for notification to the owners about the amount of the annual administration fee, a levy or a surplus under section 9 and time limits for payment of a fee or levy;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting information that must be included in a management commitment under section 17 and the form of management commitments;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (c) prescribing the form and content of the notification of withdrawal under section 18;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (d) respecting information that must be included in an annual declaration under section 20 and prescribing the form and content of declarations;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (e) respecting requirements for and constraints on management of soil conservation, water quality and fish habitat on private managed forest land;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the requirement to reforest, including, without restriction,

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  the attributes, including species, density and distribution of crop trees, that must be attained by a crop of trees on an area before the area is considered to be reforested, and

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  the time period within which the area must be reforested;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (g) exempting a person, place or thing, or class of persons, places or things, from a requirement of the regulations under paragraph (e) or (f) and may make the exemption subject to conditions;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (h) prescribing circumstances in which regulations under paragraph (e) or (f) do not apply.

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (2) A regulation made by the council under subsection (1) (e), (f), (g) or (h) must not be inconsistent with the forest management objectives in Division 1 of Part 3 unless

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (a) the regulation is made under subsection (1) (g) or (h) to address the management of forest health factors,

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (b) the forest health factors must be managed in a unique manner in order to preserve resource values on private managed forest land or on surrounding land, and

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (c) the management of the forest health factors cannot be accomplished in a manner that is consistent with the forest management objectives in Division 1 of Part 3.

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (3) The council may make regulations concerning its practices and procedures for the purposes of section 32.

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (4) In making a regulation under this section, the council may do one or more of the following:

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (a) delegate a matter to a person;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (b) confer a discretion on a person;

heading: Power of council to make regulations
paragraph: (c) make different regulations for different persons, operations, places, things, transactions or special concerns, or classes of persons, operations, places, things or transactions.

heading: Transitional - existing managed forest land classification
paragraph:
45
		  (1) On the coming into force of this section, any land that was classified as managed forest land under section 24 of the Assessment Act, as it read immediately before its re-enactment by this Act, is deemed to be private managed forest land under this Act and managed forest land under the Assessment Act without the owner having to submit a management commitment under section 17 of this Act, and the owner must comply with this Act and the regulations.

heading: Transitional - existing managed forest land classification
paragraph: (2) If an owner referred to in subsection (1) notifies the council and the assessor that he or she is withdrawing his or her private managed forest land within one year of the coming into force of this section, the owner is not required to pay the exit fee under section 19.

heading: Transitional - council members
paragraph: 46		  (1) Despite section 6, this section applies for the first 6 months of operation of the council in respect of appointment of the council members.

heading: Transitional - council members
paragraph: (2) The minister must appoint a chair of the council for a term of no longer than 6 months and set the other terms of appointment of the chair.

heading: Transitional - council members
paragraph: (3) The minister may appoint council members for a term of no longer than 6 months and set the other terms of appointment of the council members.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 63		  This Act comes into force by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
1
		  For the purpose of the Act and this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Private Managed Forest              Land Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"clearing width" means an area that is cleared of standing trees for the
          purpose of constructing or maintaining a road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "domestic purpose" has the same meaning as under the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"ecoregion" means a geographical area of British Columbia set out in the          Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks 1996 publication entitled "An Introduction to the
          Ecoregions of British Columbia";

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "excavated or bladed trail" means a constructed trail that has

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an excavated or bladed width greater than 1.5 m, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a mineral soil cutbank height greater than 30 cm;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish habitat" means an area that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is a fish stream, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) provides habitat for specified species of fish;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish stream" means the portion of a stream that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is frequented by a specified species of fish, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b) has an average slope gradient of less than 20% for each 100 m of slope distance,
            unless

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(i)  a fish inventory, carried out in accordance with methods acceptable to the
              wildlife minister, shows that it is not frequented by a specified species of fish,
              or

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(ii)  the portion of the stream is located upstream of a proven barrier to
              fish;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"Interior" means that geographic area of British Columbia that is not the
          Coast;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licensed waterworks intake" means a water intake that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is to provide water for human consumption, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is licensed under the Water Sustainability Act for

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a waterworks purpose, if the licence is held by or is subject to the control              of a municipality, regional district or improvement district, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(ii)  a domestic purpose, if the licence is held by or is subject to the control of
              a water users' community incorporated under the Water Users' Communities Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "operating season" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) for the Coast, the 12 month period ending December 31, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for the Interior, the 12 month period ending March 31;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(a) any part of a tote road, pit, quarry, landing or waste area that is located            within the road's clearing width, that is used in conjunction with the road,
            and

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
(b) any bridges, culverts, fords and other structures associated with the
            road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"specified species of fish" means one or more of the following species of
          fish: anadromous salmonids, rainbow trout, cutthroat trout, brown trout, bull trout, Dolly
          Varden char, lake trout, brook trout, kokanee, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, mountain
          whitefish, lake whitefish, arctic grayling, burbot, white sturgeon, black crappie, yellow
          perch, walleye or northern pike;

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
"stream" means a watercourse, including a watercourse that is obscured by
          overhanging or bridging vegetation or soil mats, that contains water on a perennial or
          seasonal basis, is scoured by water or contains observable deposits of mineral alluvium,
          and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) has a continuous channel bed that is 100 m or more in length, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) flows directly into

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a fish stream or a fish-bearing lake or wetland, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a licensed waterworks intake;

heading: Definitions
Definitions
paragraph: "water users' community" has the same meaning as under the Water Users' Communities Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "waterworks purpose" has the same meaning as under the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife minister" means the minister responsible for the administration          of the Wildlife Act and includes a person authorized in writing          by that minister.

heading: Establishment of water quality objectives
paragraph:
2
		  (1) For the purpose of section 24 (3) (b) of the Private Managed Forest Land Council
          Regulation, the wildlife minister may establish water quality objectives for any part or
          all of a stream that is located upstream of a licensed waterworks intake.

heading: Establishment of water quality objectives
paragraph:
(2) Before establishing a water quality objective under subsection (1), the wildlife
          minister must consult with any affected owners.

heading: Establishment of water quality objectives
paragraph:
(3) If a water quality objective has been established under subsection (1),
          the wildlife minister may monitor to ascertain if the water quality in the stream is
          consistent with the water quality objective.

heading: Establishment of water quality objectives
paragraph:
(4) For the purposes of subsection (1) or (3), the wildlife minister may
          enter onto private managed forest land to access the stream.

heading: Establishment of water quality objectives
paragraph:
(5) The wildlife minister must notify the owner, in writing, at least 14 days before
          entering on land under subsection (4).

heading: Establishment of water quality objectives
paragraph:
(6) A water quality objective established under this section becomes effective on a
          date that is six months after the wildlife minister has notified the council that the
          water quality objective has been established.

heading:
Council not required to consider review request in specified
        circumstances
paragraph:
3
		  The council is exempt from the requirement under section 32 of the Act to consider a
        request from a person if the request is in respect of

heading:
Council not required to consider review request in specified
        circumstances
paragraph:
(a) the calculation of an annual administration fee under section 9 of the Act,
          or

heading:
Council not required to consider review request in specified
        circumstances
paragraph:
(b) the calculation of an exit fee under section 2 (3) of the Private Managed Forest
          Land Regulation.

heading: Owner assuming responsibility for remediation order
paragraph:
4
		  For the purpose of section 27 (6) of the Act, a written notice from an owner to the
        council in respect of assuming responsibility for complying with a remediation order
        must

heading: Owner assuming responsibility for remediation order
paragraph: (a) be in a form and manner acceptable to the council, and

heading: Owner assuming responsibility for remediation order
paragraph: (b) identify the order to which the notice relates.

heading:
Offences for contravening the Private Managed Forest Land Council
        Regulation
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A person who contravenes section 13, 14 (1), 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 (1) or (2), 21
          (1), (2) or (3), 22, 24 (1), (2) (3) or (4), 27 (1), 28 (1), 29 (1) or (3) or 30 (1) or
          (2) of the Private Managed Forest Land Council Regulation commits an offence and is liable
          on conviction to a fine not exceeding $500 000.

heading:
Offences for contravening the Private Managed Forest Land Council
        Regulation
paragraph:
(2) A person who contravenes section 11, 25 (2) (c), 27 (5), 28 (5) or 29 (4) of the
          Private Managed Forest Land Council Regulation commits an offence and is liable on
          conviction to a fine not exceeding $25 000.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "class A stream" means a stream with a riparian class A as determined under the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "class B stream" means a stream with a riparian class B as determined under the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "class C stream" means a stream with a riparian class C as determined under the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "class D stream" means a stream with a riparian class D as determined under the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "class E stream" means a stream with a riparian class E as determined under the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cutblock" means an area of private managed forest land in which timber is harvested, but does not include areas where timber is harvested for the purpose only of facilitating road construction;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "deactivated" means a road that has been treated in accordance with section 22;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "domestic purpose" has the same meaning as in the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "drinking water intake" means an intake of water from a stream in accordance with a license issued under the Water Sustainability Act, that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) used for a domestic purpose or for an industrial purpose, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is consumed by humans;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "industrial purpose" has the same meaning as in the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "logging trail" means a structure, other than a road, that is used to transport timber or equipment, and includes excavated or bladed trails;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "primary forest activity" means timber harvesting, road construction, maintenance or deactivation or silviculture treatments;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream channel" means the area between the outermost opposing stream banks measured at the point where rooted terrestrial vegetation begins;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream crossing" means a bridge, culvert or ford.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) Words and expressions not defined in this regulation have the meaning given to them in section 1 of the Private Managed Forest Land Council Matters Regulation.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2		  (1) Nothing in this regulation authorizes an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner of private managed forest land to make changes in and about a stream as that expression is defined in the Water Sustainability Act.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) Distances referred to in this regulation are horizontal distances except for the following references, which are slope distances:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) section 16 (1);

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) section 20 (2);

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) section 23;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (d) section 24;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) section 27 (1), (2) and (4);

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (f) section 28 (1), (2) and (4);

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (g) section 29 (1);

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (h) section 30 (1).

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (3) Widths of streams are determined as the average distance across the stream channel measured at right angles to stream flow.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (4) Diameters of trees are measured at a height of 1.3 m above the ground on the upslope side of the tree.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (5) Divisions 2 and 3 of Part 3 do not apply to land that is within 30 m of the high water mark of a reservoir used for generating hydroelectric power.

heading: Limited exemption from compliance
paragraph: 3		  (1) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner is exempt from a requirement of Part 3 to the extent that the requirement cannot be met due to the actions of a person who has been authorized to act by the government.

heading: Limited exemption from compliance
paragraph: (2) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner is exempt from a requirement of Part 3 to the extent necessary to conform to the requirements of the Workers Compensation Act or a regulation made under that Act.

heading: Limited exemption from compliance
paragraph: (3) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner is exempt from a requirement of Part 3 to the extent necessary to allow the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner to

heading: Limited exemption from compliance
paragraph: (a) prevent damage to the environment from occurring or continuing, or

heading: Limited exemption from compliance
paragraph: (b) protect the safety of the public.

heading: Council may make exemptions with or without conditions
paragraph: 4		  (1) The council, in a written notice given to an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of an owner, may exempt the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner, in whole or in part, from a requirement of Part 3 and may make the exemption with or without conditions.

heading: Council may make exemptions with or without conditions
paragraph: (2) The council may exempt an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of an owner under subsection (1) only if the council is satisfied that the exemption

heading: Council may make exemptions with or without conditions
paragraph: (a) is necessary in the interests of public safety, or

heading: Council may make exemptions with or without conditions
paragraph: (b) is not inconsistent with either of the following:

heading: Council may make exemptions with or without conditions
paragraph: (i)  the public interest;

heading: Council may make exemptions with or without conditions
paragraph: (ii)  the forest management objectives in Division 1 of Part 3 of the Act unless the exemption is necessary to address management of forest health factors.

heading: Council may make exemptions with or without conditions
paragraph: (3) If an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of an owner is the subject of an exemption or condition under this section, the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must comply with the exemption or condition.

heading: Powers of the council under section 32 of the Act
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A request referred to in section 32 (1) of the Act must

heading: Powers of the council under section 32 of the Act
paragraph: (a) be in writing,

heading: Powers of the council under section 32 of the Act
paragraph: (b) identify the order, decision or determination of the council that is the subject of the request, and

heading: Powers of the council under section 32 of the Act
paragraph: (c) specify the grounds of the request.

heading: Powers of the council under section 32 of the Act
paragraph: (2) A request referred to in subsection (1) must be submitted to the council.

heading: Powers of the council under section 32 of the Act
paragraph: (3) If the council receives a request under subsection (2), the council may require the person who made the request to provide written submissions in respect of the request.

heading: Powers of the council under section 32 of the Act
paragraph: (4) If the council requires a person to provide written submissions under subsection (3), the council is not required to consider the request under subsection (1) until the person complies with the requirement.

heading: Annual administration fee and levy
paragraph:
6
		  (1) For the purpose of section 9 (2) of the Act, the date by which an owner must pay an annual administration fee is March 15 of the calendar year to which the annual administration fee relates.

heading: Annual administration fee and levy
paragraph: (2) The notice referred to in section 9 (7) (a) of the Act must

heading: Annual administration fee and levy
paragraph: (a) be in writing, and

heading: Annual administration fee and levy
paragraph: (b) be served a minimum of 30 days before the date referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Disposition of surplus
paragraph:
7
		  If the council determines that there is a surplus referred to in section 9 (6) of the Act, the council must, within 30 days of making the determination, give written notice of the surplus to the owners.

heading: Notification of local government required
paragraph:
8
		  If the council receives a notice from an owner under section 18 of the Act, the council must notify the affected local government of the withdrawal within 60 days of receipt of the notice.

heading: Management commitments
paragraph:
9
		  (1) For the purpose of section 17 (1) (a) of the Act, a management commitment in respect of an area must contain the following information:

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (a) the size and location of the area;

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (b) a commitment to use the land for the production and harvesting of timber;

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (c) the long term forest management objectives for the owner's land;

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (d) the strategies that will be used to attain the long term forest management objectives described in paragraph (c);

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (e) a soil quality assessment for the purpose of section 24 (6) of the Assessment Act;

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (f) an inventory of existing roads that are 500 m or longer;

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (g) an inventory of forest cover;

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (h) the commercial species of trees that will be used during reforestation;

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (i) the signature or, with the permission of the council, the digital code of the owner or a person authorized to sign on behalf of the owner.

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of section 17 (2) of the Act, an owner who submits to the council an amendment to a management commitment must ensure that the amendment contains

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (a) all of the information referred to in subsection (1) to which the amendment relates, and

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (b) the signature or, with the permission of the council, a digital code of the owner or a person authorized to sign on behalf of the owner.

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (3) The council may specify the form with which a management commitment or amendment to a management commitment must conform.

heading: Management commitments
paragraph: (4) If a portion of private managed forest land is conveyed, transferred or otherwise disposed of, the owner must submit to the council within 60 days of the conveyance, transfer or disposition an amended management commitment in relation to the remaining portion of the private managed forest land.

heading: Notification of withdrawal of management commitment
paragraph: 10		  (1) For the purpose of section 18 of the Act, a notice that an owner is withdrawing the owner's management commitment in respect of an area must contain the following information:

heading: Notification of withdrawal of management commitment
paragraph: (a) the legal description of the land that is the subject of the notice;

heading: Notification of withdrawal of management commitment
paragraph: (b) the size and location of the area;

heading: Notification of withdrawal of management commitment
paragraph: (c) the signature or, with the permission of the council, a digital code of the owner or a person authorized to sign on behalf of the owner.

heading: Notification of withdrawal of management commitment
paragraph: (2) The council may specify the form with which a notice referred to in subsection (1) must conform.

heading: Notification of sale of private managed forest land
paragraph:
11
		  (1) If the holder of a management commitment under section 17 of the Act disposes of the land to which the management commitment applies, the holder must give notice to the council within 30 days of the disposal.

heading: Notification of sale of private managed forest land
paragraph: (2) A notice referred to in subsection (1) must be in writing and include all of the following:

heading: Notification of sale of private managed forest land
paragraph: (a) the date of completion of the sale;

heading: Notification of sale of private managed forest land
paragraph: (b) the name and address of the purchaser;

heading: Notification of sale of private managed forest land
paragraph: (c) the legal description of the property.

heading: Annual declarations
paragraph:
12
		  For the purpose of section 20 (c) and (d) of the Act, a declaration must contain all of the following:

heading: Annual declarations
paragraph: (a) the location of areas that were restocked under section 31 (3) (a);

heading: Annual declarations
paragraph: (b) the location of areas that were successfully regenerated under section 31 (3) (b);

heading: Annual declarations
paragraph: (c) the location of roads that were deactivated;

heading: Annual declarations
paragraph: (d) a description of the location and approximate length of any roads that are 500 m or longer and that were constructed during the preceding operating season;

heading: Annual declarations
paragraph: (e) sufficient maps and supporting documentation to enable the council to evaluate the declaration;

heading: Annual declarations
paragraph: (f) the signature or, with the permission of the council, the digital code of the owner or a person authorized to sign on behalf of the owner.

heading: Limits on areas that may be occupied by roads
paragraph:
13
		  An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who carries out timber harvesting in a cutblock must restrict the amount of productive forest land within the cutblock that is converted to roads to the minimum necessary for the safe and efficient conduct of timber harvesting operations.

heading: Limits on areas that may be occupied by logging trails
paragraph:
14
		  (1) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who carries out timber harvesting in a cutblock must restrict the amount of productive forest land within the cutblock that is converted to logging trails to the minimum necessary for the safe and efficient conduct of the timber harvesting operations.

heading: Limits on areas that may be occupied by logging trails
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who constructs logging trails when carrying out timber harvesting in a cutblock must rehabilitate the logging trails to the extent necessary to meet any reforestation requirements under section 31 for the cutblock.

heading: Limits on areas that may be occupied by logging trails
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply to logging trails that, at the time of the construction of the logging trail, are reasonably expected to provide access for timber harvesting and other activities that are not wholly contained in the cutblock.

heading: Protecting drinking water quality
paragraph:
14.1
		  (1) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who carries out a primary forest activity must not cause a material adverse effect on the quality of drinking water that may affect human health at the point of diversion of a drinking water intake.

heading: Protecting drinking water quality
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner if the drinking water intake

heading: Protecting drinking water quality
paragraph: (a) is owned by another person, and

heading: Protecting drinking water quality
paragraph: (b) has been constructed on the private managed forest land of the owner without the owner's written consent.

heading: Sediment transport or deposition
paragraph:
15
		  An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner carrying out a primary forest activity must not cause sediment or other material to be transported to, or deposited in, a stream if that sediment or material will have a material adverse effect on

heading: Sediment transport or deposition
paragraph: (a) fish habitat, or

heading: Sediment transport or deposition
paragraph: (b) water that is diverted by a licensed waterworks intake.

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph:
16
		  An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must not construct a road within

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (a) 30 m of a class A stream,

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (b) 30 m of a class B stream,

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (c) 10 m of a class C stream,

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (d) 10 m of a class D stream, or

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (e) 10 m of a class E stream

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: unless one or more of the following applies:

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (f) complying with paragraphs (a) to (e) would create a higher risk of sediment delivery to the stream than not complying with paragraphs (a) to (e);

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (g) there is no other practicable option for locating the road;

heading: Roads adjacent to streams
paragraph: (h) the road construction is part of a stream crossing.

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph:
17
		  (1) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who builds a stream crossing as part of a road or logging trail must locate, build and use the crossing in a manner that

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph: (a) protects the stream channel and stream bank immediately above and below the stream crossing, and

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph: (b) mitigates disturbance to the stream channel and stream bank at the crossing

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph: to the extent necessary to avoid causing a material adverse effect on fish habitat or water that is diverted by a licensed waterworks intake.

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph: (2) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who builds a stream crossing as part of a logging trail must remove the crossing when it is no longer required by the owner.

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph:
18
		  (1) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who constructs a road or logging trail must maintain natural surface drainage patterns in the surrounding area both during and after the construction to the extent necessary to avoid causing a material adverse effect on fish habitat or water that is diverted by a licensed waterworks intake.

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (2) If it is not practicable for an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner to comply with subsection (1), the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must make the altered surface drainage pattern compatible with the original natural surface drainage pattern, to the extent necessary to avoid causing a material adverse effect on fish habitat or water that is diverted by a licensed waterworks intake, by the earlier of

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (a) the end of the construction, or

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (b) the next freshet.

heading: Measures respecting exposed soils
paragraph:
19
		  If, during road construction or deactivation, an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner exposes soil on an area

heading: Measures respecting exposed soils
paragraph: (a) that is outside of the running surface of the road, and

heading: Measures respecting exposed soils
paragraph: (b) where it is reasonably foreseeable that the surface erosion of the soil would cause a material adverse effect on fish habitat or water that is diverted by a licensed waterworks intake,

heading: Measures respecting exposed soils
paragraph: the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must, within two years of the completion of the road construction or deactivation activity, revegetate the area or carry out other measures that will materially reduce the likelihood of surface soil erosion from the area.

heading: Protecting licensed waterworks intake
paragraph:
20
		  (1) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner carrying out a primary forest activity must ensure that the activity does not damage a licensed waterworks intake.

heading: Protecting licensed waterworks intake
paragraph: (2) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must not construct a road within a 100 m radius upslope of a licensed waterworks intake, unless

heading: Protecting licensed waterworks intake
paragraph: (a) the road construction will not increase sediment delivery to the licensed waterworks intake, or

heading: Protecting licensed waterworks intake
paragraph: (b) the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner obtains prior approval from the holder of the licence for that licensed waterworks intake.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph:
21
		  (1) An owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner who constructs or uses a road for a purpose related to timber harvesting must maintain the road in accordance with this section until the road is deactivated.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner uses for timber harvesting purposes a portion of a road that was constructed under another enactment, the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must maintain that portion of the road in accordance with this section for the period that the owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (a) uses the road for timber harvesting purposes, and

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (b) is the primary user of that portion of the road.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of this section, an owner or a contractor, employee or agent of the owner must maintain
