heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "applicant", in respect of a regulatory body, means a person who applies for

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) enrolment in the regulatory body's admission program for trainees, if applicable, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) admission or reinstatement as a registrant of the regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "board" means a board established under section 23 [board of regulatory body] for a regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "board member" means a board member referred to in section 23;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "bylaw" means a bylaw made under this Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "bylaw-making authority", in respect of a regulatory body, means the capacity of the board to make bylaws under this Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "citation" means a citation issued under section 66 (1) (d) [investigations authorized by board] or 72 (3) [reprimand or remedial action by consent];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "committee", in respect of a regulatory body, means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the nomination committee established under section 26 (1) [election of registrant board members],

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) the credentials committee established under section 44 (1) [credentials committee],

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) the audit and practice review committee established under section 63 (1) [audits and practice reviews],

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (d) the investigation committee established under section 64 [investigation committee],

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (e) the discipline committee established under section 75 (1) [discipline hearings], or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (f) another committee established under section 32 (3) [officers and committees];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "conduct unbecoming a registrant" means conduct of a registrant that

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) brings the regulatory body or its registrants into disrepute,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) undermines the standards, methods or principles that are the foundation of the profession, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (c) undermines the principle of holding paramount the safety, health and welfare of the public, including the protection of the environment and the promotion of health and safety in the workplace in the manner that reflects the stewardship of a given profession by each regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "confidential information" means information, whether written or oral, provided by a person to the superintendent or, in respect of a matter under Part 6 [Protection of the Public Interest With Respect to Professional Governance and Conduct], to an audit and practice review committee, an investigation committee or another committee with powers and duties in respect of an investigation, audit, hearing or other procedure under this Act

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) for the purpose of the investigation, audit, hearing or other procedure, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) under an agreement, express or implied, that the information will be kept confidential;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "declaration" means, as applicable,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a competence declaration made by a registrant under Division 2 of Part 6 [Competence Declarations and Conflict of Interest Declarations], or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) a conflict of interest declaration made by a registrant under Division 2 of Part 6;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "designated profession" means a profession that is designated by regulation under section 89 (1) [designation of profession];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "firm" means either of the following:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a government registrant;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) a legal entity or a combination of legal entities that is engaged in a regulated practice, whether the practice occurs solely within the firm or in the provision of services to a person or entity outside the firm, unless the legal entity or combination of legal entities is exempted from this Act by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "government registrant" means a ministry or agency of the government that the Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe by regulation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "incompetent", in relation to the performance of duties undertaken while engaged in a regulated practice, includes

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a lack of competence or fitness to engage in the regulated practice, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) an incapacity or impairment that prevents a registrant from engaging in the regulated practice with reasonable skill, competence and safety to the public;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "lay board member" means a board member described in section 23 (2) (b) [board of regulatory body];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "minister" means the minister responsible for the administration of this Act unless the context otherwise requires;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "office" means the office of the superintendent of professional governance established under section 4 [office of the superintendent of professional governance established], unless the context otherwise requires;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "profession" means a practice area in which a person exercises professional skill or judgment or provides a professional service;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "professional governance" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the regulation of professions, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) the superintendence by a regulatory body of registrants engaged in a regulated practice;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "professional misconduct" means misconduct by a registrant as a professional, relating to the performance of duties while engaged in a regulated practice, including a failure to comply with, or a breach of, this Act, the regulations or the bylaws;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "professional organization" means a corporation that

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) acts as an advocate for persons who practise a profession, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) is not a professional regulator;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "professional regulator" means a corporation that is responsible for the governance of a profession under an Act of British Columbia, another province or Canada;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "registrant" means the registrants specified in respect of each regulatory body in Schedule 1 to this Act, and includes, as applicable,

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) an individual who is a registered member of a regulatory body, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) a firm that is registered with the regulatory body, if firms may be registered in respect of that regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "registrant board member" means a board member described in section 23 (2) (a);

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "regulated practice" means the carrying on of a profession by a registrant of a regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "regulatory body" means a regulatory body set out in section 1 [regulatory bodies governed by Act] of Schedule 1 to this Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "relevant enactment" means an enactment that the Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe by regulation;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "reserved practice" means a regulated practice for which the right to practice is reserved for registrants of a regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "reserved title" means a title that is reserved for use by registrants of a regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "resolution", in respect of a regulatory body, board of the regulatory body or committee of the regulatory body, means a motion passed at a meeting of the regulatory body, board or committee;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "respondent" means a person whose conduct or competence is the subject of a discipline hearing under section 75 [discipline hearings];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "roster" means a roster of registrants designated by a minister and administered by the superintendent under section 17 [administration of rosters];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "roster member" means a registrant who is designated under section 17 as a member of a roster;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "specialist" means a registrant with a specialization;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "specialization" means a specialized area of practice with qualifications established by a regulatory body under section 43 (2) [restricted and specialized areas of practice];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "superintendent" means the superintendent of professional governance appointed under section 4 [office of the superintendent of professional governance established];

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "trainee", in respect of a regulated practice, means a person in training to engage in the regulated practice as a registrant.

paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Act, a reference to a professional regulator refers to a governing body other than a regulatory body listed in Schedule 1 to this Act.

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph:
7
		  (1) The superintendent must faithfully, honestly and impartially perform the duties of the superintendent and must not, except in the proper performance of those duties, disclose to a person any information obtained as a superintendent.

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (2) The superintendent is primarily responsible for the oversight of systemic or general matters relating to professional governance by regulatory bodies, including by doing the following:

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (a) superintending the governance by regulatory bodies of registrants in the regulatory bodies' respective regulated practices to ensure compliance by the regulatory bodies with their duties;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (b) conducting research and promoting or establishing policies on best practices with respect to the regulatory bodies, including

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (i)  monitoring regulatory bodies for consistency in governance of registrants and performance standards for registrants, and

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (ii)  promoting awareness among regulatory bodies to support reconciliation with Indigenous peoples in British Columbia, including supporting the implementation of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (c) providing for administrative matters that relate to regulatory bodies and are in the public interest, including

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (i)  overseeing the implementation and administration of this Act,

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (ii)  administering rosters,

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (iii)  receiving declarations, if they are required to be submitted to the superintendent in a regulation made under section 59 (d) [requirements for declarations may be prescribed],

paragraph: (iv)  advising the minister on matters related to the administration of this Act, and

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (v)  submitting reports in accordance with section 19 [reports to minister];

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (d) promoting professional governance by regulatory bodies or enforcing compliance with this Act, including

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (i)  publishing information and documents that the superintendent determines to be in the public interest,

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (ii)  providing information and advice to regulatory bodies, registrants, professional regulators and professional organizations,

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (iii)  establishing guidelines to promote compliance with this Act and the regulations,

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (iv)  conducting investigations and audits in respect of regulatory practices and compliance with this Act and the regulations or in relation to an offence under section 106 (1) [offences],

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (v)  issuing directives to ensure compliance with this Act and the regulations,

heading: General duty and responsibilities of superintendent
paragraph: (vii)  imposing administrative penalties in accordance with Division 1 [Enforcement Powers of Superintendent] of Part 8 [Enforcement of Act];

paragraph: (vi)  section 103 [no reprisals];

heading: Investigations and audits by superintendent
paragraph: (vii)  section 104 [obstruction].

heading: Investigations and audits by superintendent
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of an investigation or an audit under this section, the superintendent has the powers, privileges and protection set out in section 13 [power to compel persons to give evidence and order disclosure].

heading: Investigations and audits by superintendent
paragraph: (4) The superintendent may only investigate or conduct an audit in respect of a matter that relates to an individual registrant in the following cases:

heading: Investigations and audits by superintendent
paragraph: (a) an investigation or an audit of a general or systemic matter relating to the regulated practice;

heading: Investigations and audits by superintendent
paragraph: (b) an investigation in respect of a matter under a provision listed in subsection (2) (b).

heading: Investigations and audits by superintendent
paragraph: (5) In an investigation or an audit under this section, the superintendent may inquire into a matter that relates to one or more specific regulatory bodies.

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph:
11
		  (1) The superintendent may issue directives relating to the following:

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (a) that a board exercise its powers or perform its duties to better achieve the protection of the public interest with respect to professional governance;

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (b) that a board appoint an auditor to conduct an audit, in accordance with the directive and any applicable regulations, and provide an audit report to the superintendent;

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (c) for any matter the superintendent considers necessary in the public interest with respect to professional governance, including a directive that is

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (i)  consistent with any guidelines established under section 9, or

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (ii)  necessary to address issues arising out of an investigation or audit under section 10.

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (2) A directive of the superintendent takes effect immediately or on a later date specified in the directive.

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (3) A board must comply with a directive issued to it under this section.

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (4) The superintendent may require, by directive, a work, act, matter or thing to be performed or completed within a specified period.

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (5) If, in the superintendent's opinion, the circumstances of a case under subsection (4) so require, the superintendent may extend the specified period.

heading: Directives issued by superintendent
paragraph: (6) The superintendent must make accessible to the public any directives made under subsection (1).

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph:
12
		  (0.1) In this section, "regulatory authority" means a Schedule 2 regulatory authority as defined in section 1 of the International Credentials Recognition Act.

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph: (1) Without limiting sections 10 and 11, the superintendent may appoint a public administrator to discharge the powers and duties of a board under this Act or of a regulatory authority under the International Credentials Recognition Act if the superintendent considers this to be necessary in the public interest, whether or not the superintendent has exercised any other power under this Act or the International Credentials Recognition Act.

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph: (2) On the appointment of a public administrator, the board members cease to hold office unless otherwise ordered by the superintendent.

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph: (3) The superintendent may specify

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph: (a) the powers, duties and responsibilities of a public administrator appointed under this section, and

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph: (b) how a board will operate after the appointment of a public administrator has ended, including specifying whether a new board will be appointed under section 23 [board of regulatory body] as if the new board were the first board of a regulatory body.

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, within 45 days after an appointment of a public administrator under subsection (1), vary or rescind the appointment.

heading: Appointment of public administrator
paragraph: (5) The expenses incurred under this section by the government in respect of a regulatory body are a debt due and owing by the regulatory body to the government.

heading: Power to compel persons to give evidence and order disclosure
paragraph: 13		  (1) For the purposes of this Act, the superintendent may make an order requiring a person to do either or both of the following:

heading: Power to compel persons to give evidence and order disclosure
paragraph: (a) attend, in person or by electronic means, before the superintendent to answer questions on oath or affirmation or in any other manner;

heading: Power to compel persons to give evidence and order disclosure
paragraph: (b) produce for the superintendent a record or thing in the person's possession or control.

heading: Power to compel persons to give evidence and order disclosure
paragraph: (2) The superintendent may apply to the Supreme Court for an order directing

heading: Power to compel persons to give evidence and order disclosure
paragraph: (a) a person to comply with an order made under subsection (1), or

heading: Power to compel persons to give evidence and order disclosure
paragraph: (b) any directors and officers of a person to cause the person to comply with an order made under subsection (1).

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph:
14
		  The failure or refusal of a person summoned as a witness under section 13 (1) to do any of the following makes the person, on application to the court by the superintendent, liable to be committed for contempt as if in breach of an order or judgment of the court:

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph: (a) take an oath or affirmation;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph: (b) answer questions;

heading: Contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person
paragraph: (c) produce the records or things in the person's custody or possession.

heading: Referral of complaints
paragraph:
15
		  If a complaint is made to the superintendent that relates to a matter that is beyond the investigation power of the superintendent and the superintendent considers that there is another appropriate person or body having jurisdiction over the matter, the superintendent may

heading: Referral of complaints
paragraph: (a) with the consent of the person who made the complaint, refer that matter directly to an appropriate person or body having jurisdiction over the matter, or

heading: Referral of complaints
paragraph: (b) refer the person who made the complaint to an appropriate person or body having jurisdiction over that matter, or otherwise provide information that would permit the complaint to be made.

heading: Application of the Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph:
16
		  The following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the superintendent as if the superintendent were a tribunal, including the power of the superintendent to impose, and to consider responses to, administrative penalties under Division 1 [Enforcement Powers of Superintendent] of Part 8 [Enforcement of Act] of this Act:

heading: Application of the Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (a) section 44 [tribunal without jurisdiction over constitutional questions];

heading: Application of the Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (b) section 45 [tribunal without jurisdiction over Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms issues];

heading: Application of the Administrative Tribunals Act
paragraph: (c) section 46.3 [tribunal without jurisdiction to apply the Human Rights Code].

heading: Administration of rosters
paragraph: 17		  (1) A minister responsible for a relevant enactment may, by order, designate a registrant to be a roster member.

heading: Administration of rosters
paragraph: (2) The superintendent may administer rosters with roster members designated under subsection (1).

heading: Administration of rosters
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe, by regulation, any of the following in respect of the designation of roster members under subsection (1):

heading: Administration of rosters
paragraph: (a) the qualifications or other criteria required for designation as a roster member in respect of a relevant enactment;

heading: Administration of rosters
paragraph: (b) restricted activities that a registrant may carry out only if the registrant is a roster member;

heading: Administration of rosters
paragraph: (c) restrictions on carrying out activities by roster members.

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph:
18
		  (1) If the superintendent determines that it is in the public interest, the superintendent must, in accordance with regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, publish prescribed information or documents or classes of information or documents

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph: (a) that relate to, or were created by a registrant providing services under, a relevant enactment, or

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph: (b) that relate to

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph: (i)  a profession,

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph: (ii)  a regulated practice, or

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph: (iii)  a matter relevant to registrants under a relevant enactment.

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph: (2) If a minister responsible for a relevant enactment determines that it is in the public interest, that minister may order that the superintendent publish any information or documents, or classes of information or documents, described in subsection (1) of this section in accordance with regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Public interest disclosure
paragraph: (3) Personal information may not be published under this section that, if disclosed, would constitute an unreasonable invasion of personal privacy as described in section 22 (2) to (4) [disclosure harmful to personal privacy] of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act.

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: 19		  (1) The superintendent must, no later than May 31 in each year, submit to the minister an annual report in respect of the superintendent's activities under this Act in the preceding calendar year.

heading: Reports to minister
paragraph: (2) The superintendent must make the report submitted to the minister under subsection (1) available to the public on the superintendent's website.

heading: Superintendent to make recommendations
paragraph:
20
		  In addition to any other reports provided by the superintendent under this Act, on request of the minister, the superintendent must

heading: Superintendent to make recommendations
paragraph: (a) review this Act and recommend to the minister any amendments to this Act that the superintendent considers will better enable the superintendent to exercise or perform the superintendent's powers, duties and functions under this Act, and

heading: Superintendent to make recommendations
paragraph: (b) report to the minister on any other matter, as specified by the minister.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
21
		  In this Part, "lay committee member", in respect of a committee of a regulatory body, means a committee member who is not a registrant of the regulatory body.

heading: Corporate powers of regulatory body
paragraph:
21.1
		  (1) A regulatory body is a corporation consisting of

heading: Corporate powers of regulatory body
paragraph: (a) the board established under section 23 [board of regulatory body], and

heading: Corporate powers of regulatory body
paragraph: (b) the persons who are registrants of the regulatory body.

heading: Corporate powers of regulatory body
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of exercising its powers and performing its duties under this Act, a regulatory body has the powers and capacity of a natural person of full capacity, including the power to acquire and dispose of property.

heading: Corporate powers of regulatory body
paragraph: (3) The Business Corporations Act does not apply to a regulatory body unless the Lieutenant Governor in Council, by regulation, provides that specified provisions of that Act apply to the regulatory body, in which case the specified provisions apply.

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: 22		  (1) It is the general duty of a regulatory body at all times to

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (a) serve and protect the public interest with respect to the exercise of a profession, professional governance and the conduct of registrants in the registrants' regulated practice, and

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (b) exercise its powers and discharge its responsibilities in the public interest.

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (2) A regulatory body has the following responsibilities:

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (a) to superintend the regulated practice;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (b) to preserve and protect reserved titles or reserved practices, as applicable, in the public interest;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (c) to guard against the unlawful use of reserved titles or the unlawful practice of reserved practices;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (d) to govern the registrants of the regulatory body according to this Act, the regulations and the bylaws;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (e) to establish the conditions or requirements for registration of a person as a registrant of the regulatory body;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (f) to establish, monitor and enforce standards of practice to enhance the quality of practice so that registrants avoid

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (i)  professional misconduct,

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (ii)  conduct unbecoming a registrant, and

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (iii)  incompetent performance of duties undertaken while engaged in the regulated practice;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (g) to establish and maintain a continuing competency program to promote high practice standards amongst registrants;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (h) to establish, monitor and enforce standards of professional ethics amongst registrants;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (i) to establish and employ registration, investigation and discipline procedures that are transparent, objective, impartial and fair;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (j) to administer the affairs of the regulatory body and exercise its powers and perform its duties under this Act or other enactments;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (k) in the course of exercising the powers and performing the duties of the regulatory body under this Act or other enactments, to promote and enhance the following:

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (i)  collaborative relations with other regulatory bodies, post-secondary education institutions and the government;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (ii)  interprofessional collaborative practice between its registrants and persons practising another profession;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (iii)  the ability of its registrants to respond and adapt to changes in practice environments, advances in technology and other emerging issues;

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (l) any other responsibility that the Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe.

heading: General duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (3) A regulatory body may only act in an advocacy role in accordance with this Act and in accordance with rules, conditions or limits prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Annual fee
paragraph:
22.1
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Annual fee
paragraph: (a) requiring regulatory bodies to pay an annual fee, and

heading: Annual fee
paragraph: (b) setting annual fee amounts.

heading: Annual fee
paragraph: (2) A regulatory body must, within the prescribed period of time, pay any annual fee required to be paid in a regulation under subsection (1).

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph:
23
		  (1) Subject to section 84 [specified regulatory bodies continued as regulatory bodies under this Act], a board is established for each regulatory body in respect of that regulatory body.

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (2) The composition of a board consists of the following board members:

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (a) 7 registrant board members, including the board chair and board vice chair,

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (i)  who are registrants of the regulatory body, and

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (ii)  who are elected or temporarily appointed under section 26 [election of registrant board members];

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (b) 4 lay board members

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (i)  who are not registrants of the regulatory body, and

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (ii)  who are appointed under section 27 [appointment of board members];

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (c) the immediate past board chair of the regulatory body, who is a non-voting registrant board member.

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (3) The board members may act even if there is a vacancy on a board.

heading: Board of regulatory body
paragraph: (4) Subject to any exceptions prescribed by regulation, a board member may not be a member of a committee or panel established in respect of a regulatory body under this Act.

heading: Term limits
paragraph:
24
		  (1) Subject to subsection (5.1), the term for a board member to hold office is 3 years.

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (2) A registrant board member who serves successive terms is subject to the following limits:

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (a) subject to paragraph (b), the registrant board member may not serve for more than 6 consecutive years in each of the following offices:

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (i)  board chair of the regulatory body;

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (ii)  board vice chair of the regulatory body;

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (iii)  a board member other than the board chair and board vice chair of the regulatory body;

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (b) the registrant board member may not serve for more than 12 consecutive years from the date of the registrant board member's initial election or appointment, as applicable.

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (3) A regulatory body may set a term that is shorter than 3 years for the following offices:

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (a) board chair of the regulatory body;

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (b) board vice chair of the regulatory body.

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5.1), a lay board member may not serve successive terms for more than 6 consecutive years from the date of the lay board member's initial appointment.

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, set a term for an individual lay board member that is shorter than 3 years.

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (5.1) A lay board member whose term of office has expired may continue to hold office until a successor is appointed.

heading: Term limits
paragraph: (6) A person who has served the maximum number of consecutive years under this section is not eligible to serve as a board member until after a break in service of at least 3 years.

heading: Selection principles and criteria
paragraph:
25
		  (1) The selection of nominees to be registrant board members under section 26 (1) is to be conducted in accordance with the process and merit-based selection principles prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Selection principles and criteria
paragraph: (2) A board may

heading: Selection principles and criteria
paragraph: (a) subject to section 23 (2), establish different criteria or preferences for registrant board members in determining the board composition, and

heading: Selection principles and criteria
paragraph: (b) make recommendations to the Lieutenant Governor in Council in respect of different criteria or preferences for lay board members.

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph:
26
		  (1) The board of each regulatory body must, in accordance with section 23 (4), establish a nomination committee to administer the nomination of registrants who are qualified to be nominated for election to the board in accordance with the process and selection principles referred to in section 25 (1), the bylaws and applicable regulations.

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (2) Only a registrant who is nominated by the nomination committee under subsection (1) may be elected as a registrant board member.

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (3) An election of registrant board members is to be conducted in accordance with the bylaws made by the board and the regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), a board may temporarily appoint a registrant as a registrant board member until a successor is elected, in accordance with the process and selection principles referred to in section 25 (1), the bylaws and applicable regulations, if

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (a) an elected registrant fails to take the oath of office described in section 28,

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (b) an elected registrant board member dies, resigns or is incapable of performing the board member's duties under this Act,

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (c) an elected registrant board member is disqualified, or

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (d) there is a vacancy on the board because no registrant board member was elected.

heading: Election of registrant board members
paragraph: (5) A temporary appointment under subsection (4) may not be for a term that is longer than the remainder of the term of the registrant board member referred to in that subsection.

heading: Appointment of board members
paragraph:
27
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may appoint the lay board members for the board of each regulatory body after a merit-based process.

heading: Appointment of board members
paragraph: (2) If there is a vacancy in the office of a lay board member, the minister may temporarily appoint a lay board member for a term of not more than one year.

heading: Oath of office
paragraph:
28
		  (1) Before taking office as a board member or acting as a member of a committee in respect of a regulatory body, a person elected or appointed as a board member or to a committee must take and sign, by oath or solemn affirmation, an oath of office in the form and manner established by regulation.

heading: Oath of office
paragraph: (2) The registrar and the deputy registrars, if any, of each regulatory body may, for the purposes of this Act, administer oaths.

heading: Oath of office
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, provide for any exceptions in respect of the requirement to take and sign an oath of office.

heading: Required lay board members and quorum
paragraph:
29
		  (1) At least one lay board member must be present at any meeting, proceeding or hearing of the board under this Act unless there are no lay board members appointed in respect of the board on the date of the meeting, proceeding or hearing.

heading: Required lay board members and quorum
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (1), the majority of the voting board members of a board of a regulatory body constitutes a quorum.

heading: Required lay board members and quorum
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1) of this section and section 23 (2) [board of regulatory body],

heading: Required lay board members and quorum
paragraph: (a) the powers and duties of the board are not affected by a vacancy in the office of a lay board member, and

heading: Required lay board members and quorum
paragraph: (b) the acts done by a quorum of board are not invalid by reason only that the board is not at the time composed of the number of board members required under this Act.

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph:
30
		  (1) A registrant board member ceases to hold office

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (a) if the registrant board member

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (i)  contravenes a term of the oath of office required by section 28 (1),

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (ii)  contravenes a provision of this Act or the regulations, rules or bylaws,

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (iii)  contravenes a provision of another provincial or federal enactment, or

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (iv)  becomes bankrupt, and

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (b) if, after reasonable notice to the registrant board member, the board, by resolution passed by a vote of at least 2/3 of the other board members of the full board who are eligible to vote on the resolution, considers that the circumstance described in paragraph (a) is sufficiently serious to justify the board member's removal.

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (2) A registrant board member ceases to hold office if the registrant board member ceases to be a registrant.

heading: Disqualification and termination of board members
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, terminate the appointment of a lay board member.

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph:
31
		  (1) The board of each regulatory body must appoint a registrar and may appoint one or more deputy registrars for the regulatory body, each of whom holds office during the pleasure of the board.

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (2) The board may, by bylaw, authorize a deputy registrar or deputy registrars appointed under subsection (1) to exercise the powers and perform the duties of the registrar set out in the bylaws, subject to any limits or conditions specified in the bylaws.

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (3) The registrar must include in a register on a publicly available website maintained by or on behalf of the regulatory body, for every person granted registration or certification under this Act, the following information:

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (a) the person's name and whether the person is a registrant or a former registrant;

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (b) the category, subcategory or class of registrants in which the person is or was registered;

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (c) if the registrant is an individual, any limits or conditions imposed on the regulated practice under this Act;

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (d) if the registrant is a firm, any limits or conditions imposed on the regulated practice under this Act;

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (e) a notation of each cancellation or suspension of the person's registration, including any cancellation or suspension that

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (i)  occurred or was recorded before the coming into force of this section, or

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (ii)  was imposed by the regulatory body under an enactment that applied to the regulatory body before this section applied to the regulatory body;

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (f) any additional information

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (i)  specified under subsection (5) by

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (A) the credentials committee in respect of conditions or limitations on the registration, or

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (B) the discipline committee,

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (ii)  required under the bylaws of the regulatory body, or

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (iii)  prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (4) The registrar must cancel the registration of a registrant if

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (a) the registrant requests or consents in writing to the cancellation,

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (c) notification is received of the registrant's death, or

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (d) the registration of the registrant has been cancelled under Part 6 [Protection of the Public Interest With Respect to Professional Governance and Conduct].

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), either of the following may specify information that must be entered on the register:

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (a) the credentials committee, in respect of conditions or limitations on registration;

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (b) the discipline committee, in disposing of a matter under Part 6 in respect of a registrant.

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (6) Information required to be entered on the register in accordance with subsection (5) may be entered only after the final disposition of a matter.

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (7) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (a) prescribing a period of time, including a minimum period of time and a maximum period of time, during which a former registrant is to be included in a list of registrants made available under subsection (3), and

heading: Registrar and register for regulatory body
paragraph: (b) in respect of any exceptions to the application of this section.

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph:
32
		  (1) In addition to the registrar and any deputy registrars, a board may establish other offices and appoint other officers, including

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (a) an executive director, who must not be a board member, and

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (b) an officer other than the board chair and board vice chair, including an officer who may also be a board member.

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (2) A board may authorize the nomination committee, credentials committee, audit and practice review committee, investigation committee or discipline committee to exercise a power, authority or jurisdiction of the board under this Act, in addition to a power, authority or jurisdiction expressly referred to in this Act in connection with these committees, other than a bylaw-making authority.

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (3) Subject to section 23 (4) [board of regulatory body], a board may establish committees, in addition to the nomination committee, credentials committee, audit and practice review committee, investigation committee and discipline committee, for a purpose consistent with this Act.

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (4) A board may authorize a committee established under subsection (3) to exercise a power, authority or jurisdiction of the board under this Act, other than

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (a) a bylaw-making authority, or

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (b) a power, authority or jurisdiction expressly referred to in this Act in connection with the nomination committee, credentials committee, audit and practice review committee, investigation committee or discipline committee.

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (5) A board may authorize

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (a) an officer to exercise a power, authority or jurisdiction of the board, other than a bylaw-making authority, under this Act, and

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (b) a committee established by the board to delegate to an officer a power, authority or jurisdiction granted to the committee by the board.

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (6) A board may make bylaws in respect of the following:

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (a) the appointment and termination of officers other than the board chair and the board vice chair;

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (b) the appointment and termination of members of committees;

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (c) the conduct of committee meetings, including proceedings before a committee.

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (7) Subject to section 23 (4), each committee of a regulatory body established under this Act must

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (a) include at least one lay committee member,

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (b) have at least one lay committee member present at every meeting, proceeding or hearing of the committee under this Act, and

heading: Officers and committees
paragraph: (c) have a chair who is appointed in accordance with the selection principles referred to in section 25 (1) [selection principles and criteria].

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph:
33
		  (1) An annual general meeting of a regulatory body must be held, at the time and place appointed by the board of the regulatory body, at least once in every calendar year and not more than 15 months after the preceding annual meeting.

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (2) If an annual general meeting is not held as required under subsection (1), the superintendent, on application by a registrant, may call or direct the calling of an annual general meeting.

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (3) The board, at any time on its own motion, may call a general meeting of the regulatory body.

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (4) The board must call a general meeting of the regulatory body on the written request of

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (a) 5 board members, or

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (b) the greater of the following:

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (i)  50 registrants in good standing;

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (ii)  1% of the registrants.

heading: General meetings of regulatory bodies
paragraph: (5) Subject to this section, the board may make bylaws governing the calling and conduct of a general meeting of the regulatory body, including the annual general meeting.

heading: Implementing resolutions of general meetings
paragraph:
34
		  (1) A resolution of a general meeting of a regulatory body, including the annual general meeting, is not binding on the board of a regulatory body.

heading: Implementing resolutions of general meetings
paragraph: (4) The board must not implement a resolution if to do so would

heading: Implementing resolutions of general meetings
paragraph: (a) be inconsistent with this Act and the regulations made under it or otherwise constitute a breach of a statutory duty, or

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph:
35
		  (1) Subject to the requirements of this Act and any applicable regulations, the board of a regulatory body may make bylaws in respect of the following:

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (a) the duties of board members;

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (b) the removal of a registrant board member;

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (c) the temporary appointment of a registrant board member to fill a vacancy caused by the incapacity, resignation, removal or death of a registrant board member;

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (d) the duties of the board chair and the board vice chair of the board;

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (e) the temporary appointment of a board vice chair of the board to fill a vacancy caused by the incapacity, resignation, removal or death of a board vice chair;

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (f) for certainty, any other purpose contemplated as a bylaw-making authority of the regulatory body under this Act, including bylaws that may be made under this Part, Part 4 [Registrants] and Part 6 [Protection of the Public Interest With Respect to Professional Governance and Conduct];

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (g) the management, duties and purposes of the regulatory body.

heading: Bylaws of board
paragraph: (2) The board may make bylaws governing the conduct of the affairs of the board, including the conduct of board meetings and proceedings before the board.

heading: Provisions may be different in bylaws
paragraph:
36
		  Provisions in a bylaw under this Act may be different for

heading: Provisions may be different in bylaws
paragraph: (a) different classes of registrants, and

heading: Provisions may be different in bylaws
paragraph: (c) different matters, classes of persons, circumstances or categories prescribed by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph:
37
		  (1) Subject to subsection (3), a bylaw made by the board of a regulatory body under a bylaw-making authority

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (a) must be delivered, in accordance with any regulations respecting the form and manner of delivery of the bylaws, to the superintendent for filing with the minister,

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (b) must be filed by the superintendent with the minister within 45 days of delivery by the board unless the superintendent considers that the bylaw is unsuitable, in accordance with any criteria prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, and

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (c) has no effect unless it is delivered to the superintendent and filed with the minister.

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (2) A bylaw filed under subsection (1) comes into force on the date that is the number of days prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council after the date the bylaw is filed by the superintendent under subsection (1) unless

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (a) the superintendent declares, under section 38 (1) (a), that the bylaw comes into force on an earlier date,

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (b) the board withdraws the bylaw under section 38 (2), or

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (c) the superintendent disallows the bylaw under section 38 (3).

heading: Filing of bylaws
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, provide exceptions for the requirements of this section and section 38 in respect of bylaws made for different matters, classes of persons, circumstances or categories.

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph:
38
		  (1) If the superintendent considers it necessary or advisable to do so, the superintendent may, by order, within 45 days after the filing of a bylaw under section 37,

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (a) declare that the bylaw or a portion of the bylaw comes into force on a specified date that is earlier than the date it would otherwise come into force under section 37 (2), or

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (b) disallow a bylaw filed under section 37 or a portion of the bylaw in accordance with subsection (3) of this section.

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (2) The board may, by written notice delivered to the superintendent, withdraw a bylaw or a portion of a bylaw delivered under section 37 at any time before it would otherwise come into force or before it is disallowed.

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (3) The superintendent must disallow a bylaw filed under section 37 if the superintendent is not satisfied that appropriate provision has been made in respect of the following:

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (a) the appointment or election of board members of a regulatory body under

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (i)  section 23 [board of regulatory body],

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (ii)  section 26 [election of registrant board members], or

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (iii)  section 27 [appointment of board members];

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (b) the responsibilities referred to in section 22 [general duty and responsibilities of regulatory bodies];

heading: Disallowance of bylaws
paragraph: (c) the presence of required lay board members of a regulatory body in accordance with section 29 [required lay board members and quorum].

heading: Forms established by bylaws
paragraph:
39
		  (1) A bylaw made under a bylaw-making authority in this Act may authorize the registrar to establish a form that is required, under that bylaw, to be used by registrants.

heading: Forms established by bylaws
paragraph: (2) A form established by a registrar under subsection (1) is considered to be a bylaw made by the board of a regulatory body.

heading: Copies of bylaws
paragraph:
40
		  The board of each regulatory body must

heading: Copies of bylaws
paragraph: (a) maintain a complete and accurate record of the bylaws that are in effect for the regulatory body and provide a copy of those bylaws to each registrant,

heading: Copies of bylaws
paragraph: (b) make the bylaws available for inspection by any person, free of charge, at the office of the regulatory body at all reasonable times during regular business hours, and

heading: Copies of bylaws
paragraph: (c) post the bylaws on a publicly available website maintained by or on behalf of the regulatory body.

heading: Annual report to superintendent
paragraph:
41
		  The board of each regulatory body must, on or before April 1 each year, file with the superintendent an annual report of the general operations of the regulatory body in the form and manner established by the registrar with any information required by the superintendent and as may be prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council that is current to the preceding calendar year.

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph:
42
		  (1) A regulatory body may have categories of registrants established in accordance with a bylaw made under subsection (2) (a).

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (2) The board of a regulatory body may make bylaws to do the following:

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (a) establish categories of registrants, including firms and practising, non-practising, temporary, retired and honorary registrants;

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (b) establish subcategories within the categories of registrants referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (b.1) authorize registrants to provide services in respect of a regulated practice through limited liability partnerships as defined in section 83.1 [limited liability partnerships];

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (b.2) establish conditions, limitations and requirements for registrants to provide services in respect of a regulated practice through limited liability partnerships as defined in section 83.1;

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (c) subject to regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, determine the rights and privileges under this Act for each category of registrants referred to in paragraph (a), and for each subcategory of registrants established in accordance with a bylaw made under paragraph (b) of this subsection, including

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (i)  voting rights, and

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (ii)  use of titles, abbreviations or designations referred to in Part 5 [Reserved Titles and Reserved Practice];

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (d) establish requirements and procedures for the admission or reinstatement of registrants within a category established under paragraph (a);

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (e) set fees for registrants within a category established in accordance with a bylaw made under paragraph (a);

heading: Categories of registrants and bylaws for categories of registrants
paragraph: (f) determine whether a person is a registrant in good standing of the regulatory body.

heading: Restricted and specialized areas of practice
paragraph:
43
		  (1) Subject to regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the board of a regulatory body may make bylaws in respect of restricted areas of practice for the regulated practice as follows:

heading: Restricted and specialized areas of practice
paragraph: (a) designating restricted areas of practice;

heading: Restricted and specialized areas of practice
paragraph: (b) providing for the manner and extent to which a category of registrants referred to in section 42 (1), or a subcategory of registrants established in accordance with a rule made under section 42 (2) (b), may engage in a restricted area of practice.

heading: Restricted and specialized areas of practice
paragraph: (2) Subject to regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the board may make bylaws in respect of specialized areas of practice for the regulated practice as follows:

heading: Restricted and specialized areas of practice
paragraph: (a) designating specialized areas of practice;

heading: Restricted and specialized areas of practice
paragraph: (b) providing that registrants of the regulatory body must not hold themselves out as specialists in these areas unless they are practising registrants who have qualified in accordance with a bylaw made under paragraph (c);

heading: Restricted and specialized areas of practice
paragraph: (c) providing for the qualification of practising registrants as specialists in areas of practice designated under paragraph (a).

heading: Credentials committee
paragraph:
44
		  (1) The board of a regulatory body may, subject to section 23 (4) [board of regulatory body], establish a credentials committee to

heading: Credentials committee
paragraph: (a) advise the board on matters falling within the scope of this Division, and

heading: Credentials committee
paragraph: (b) carry out other functions consistent with this Division.

heading: Credentials committee
paragraph: (2) The board may authorize the credentials committee to exercise a power, authority or jurisdiction of the board under this Division, other than a bylaw-making authority.

heading: Application for enrolment, admission or reinstatement as registrant
paragraph:
45
		  (1) On receiving an application for enrolment, admission or reinstatement as a registrant of a regulatory body, the registrar of the regulatory body, or a committee authorized by the board of the regulatory body, may, in accordance with the bylaws,

heading: Application for enrolment, admission or reinstatement as registrant
paragraph: (a) grant the application,

heading: Application for enrolment, admission or reinstatement as registrant
paragraph: (b) grant the application subject to conditions or limitations on the registration, or

heading: Application for enrolment, admission or reinstatement as registrant
paragraph: (c) reject the application, with written reasons.

heading: Application for enrolment, admission or reinstatement as registrant
paragraph: (2) The board may vary conditions or limitations made under subsection (1) (b) if the applicant consents in writing to the variation.

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph:
46
		  (1) The board of a regulatory body may make bylaws to do the following:

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (a) establish requirements, including academic requirements, and procedures for the enrolment of trainees in the regulatory body's admission program for trainees;

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (b) set fees for enrolment;

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (c) establish, maintain or endorse an education program for trainees;

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (d) establish requirements for practising registrants to act as mentors or supervisors of trainees;

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (e) stipulate the duties of a practising registrant who acts as a mentor or supervisor of a trainee;

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (f) stipulate the duties of a trainee with respect to a practising registrant who acts as their mentor or supervisor.

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (2) Bylaws made under subsection (1) may do the following:

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (a) establish different requirements and procedures for enrolment, set different enrolment fees and establish, maintain or endorse different education programs for trainees with different specializations;

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (b) establish different requirements and stipulate different duties for practising registrants who act as mentors or supervisors for trainees with different specializations;

heading: Enrolment of trainees
paragraph: (c) stipulate different duties for trainees with different specializations with respect to practising registrants who act as their mentors or supervisors.

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph:
47
		  (1) The board of a regulatory body may make bylaws to do the following:

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (a) establish requirements, including academic requirements, and procedures for admission as a registrant;

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (b) set fees for admission;

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (c) establish requirements and procedures for the reinstatement of former registrants;

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (d) set fees for reinstatement;

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (e) provide for examinations to assess applicants for admission or reinstatement as registrants.

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (2) Bylaws made under subsection (1) may do either or both of the following:

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (a) establish different requirements and procedures, set different fees and provide for different examinations for the admission of registrants with different specializations in the regulatory body;

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (b) establish different requirements and procedures, set different fees and provide for different examinations for the reinstatement of registrants with different specializations in the regulatory body.

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (3) If, under the Labour Mobility Act or in accordance with a prescribed trade agreement, the board of a regulatory body is required to admit a person as a registrant, the board may admit the person as a registrant in accordance with

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (a) regulations that the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make in respect of the board, including any bylaws the board must make, and

heading: Admission and reinstatement of registrants
paragraph: (b) bylaws the board may make to administer the admission of the person as a registrant.

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: 48		  (1) Within 30 days of receiving notice of a decision in respect of an application in respect of a regulatory body, the applicant may apply in writing to the board of the regulatory body for a review on the record.

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (2) On receiving a request under subsection (1), the board or the credentials committee, if authorized by the board, may conduct a review of the record in accordance with the bylaws.

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), if, in the opinion of the board, there are special circumstances, the board may hear evidence that is not part of the record.

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (4) After conducting its review, the board may

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (a) confirm the decision in respect of the application, or

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (b) substitute a decision in respect of the application, including any conditions or limitations on the registration.

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (5) The board may make bylaws establishing

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (a) procedures and criteria for an application for review under this section, and

heading: Review on the record
paragraph: (b) the practice and procedure for proceedings before the board under this section, which may be different for reviews of different applications under section 45.

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph:
49
		  (1) The registrar of each regulatory body must issue to each registrant a certificate of registration and, on payment of the annual fee, confirmation that the registrant is in good standing and has complied with this Act and the bylaws.

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph: (2) A certificate or confirmation under subsection (1) purporting to contain the signature of the registrar stating that a person is, or was at the time specified in the certificate, a registrant in good standing is proof of that fact in the absence of evidence to the contrary.

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the board of the regulatory body may make bylaws

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph: (a) providing for the issuance of a seal to registrants in good standing, and

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph: (b) governing the use of the seal.

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, establish requirements in respect of the following:

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph: (a) bylaws made by the board under subsection (3);

heading: Certificate of registration and seal
paragraph: (b) the use of the seal by registrants.

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph:
50
		  The board of a regulatory body may make bylaws to do the following:

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (a) set the annual fee to be paid by registrants, which may be different for different specializations;

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (b) set fees, in addition to the annual fee referred to in paragraph (a), to be paid by registrants, trainees or applicants;

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (c) levy special assessments, for a purpose consistent with this Act, to be paid by registrants, trainees or applicants;

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (d) set the date by which a fee or a special assessment must be paid;

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (e) permit late payment of a fee or of a special assessment;

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (f) set a fee for late payment of a fee or of a special assessment;

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (g) determine the circumstances in which a full or partial refund of a fee or of a special assessment may be made;

heading: Fees and special assessments
paragraph: (h) waive payment of all or part of a fee or special assessment for a person whom the board wishes to honour.

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph:
50.1
		  (1) The board of a regulatory body may make bylaws authorizing the board to suspend or cancel the registration of a registrant of the regulatory body if the registrant fails to do any of the following:

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (a) pay, within the specified period of time, a fee or a special assessment that is set or levied under a bylaw made under section 50;

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (b) complete or provide proof of completion of, within the specified period of time, a continuing education program or requirements established in a bylaw made under section 57 (1) (e) or (f) [standards of conduct and competence];

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (c) provide, within the specified period of time, a continuing education program established in a bylaw made under section 57 (1) (g);

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (d) make or submit a declaration within the prescribed period of time, if required to do so in a regulation made under section 59 [requirements for declarations may be prescribed];

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (e) cooperate with a practice review authorized by a bylaw made under section 63 (4) [audits and practice reviews];

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (f) participate in an audit program established under a bylaw made under section 63 (7);

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (g) pay, within the specified period of time, a penalty imposed under section 75 [discipline hearings];

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (h) pay, within the specified period of time, costs required to be paid under section 81 [costs];

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (i) perform any other requirement under this Act that is prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (2) Bylaws under subsection (1) must establish the following:

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (a) procedures for the suspension or cancellation of a registration;

heading: Cancellation or suspension of registration
paragraph: (b) requirements and procedures for the reinstatement of a registrant whose registration has been suspended or cancelled under subsection (1).

heading: Exclusivity of reserved titles and right of practice of reserved practice
paragraph:
51
		  (1) Registrants of a regulatory body have, in accordance with regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council,

heading: Exclusivity of reserved titles and right of practice of reserved practice
paragraph: (a) the exclusive use of a reserved title as prescribed by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, if the regulatory body is listed in Schedule 2 to this Act, and

heading: Exclusivity of reserved titles and right of practice of reserved practice
paragraph: (b) the right of practice of a reserved practice as prescribed by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, if the regulatory body is listed in Schedule 3 to this Act.

heading: Exclusivity of reserved titles and right of practice of reserved practice
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, amend Schedules 2 and 3 to this Act.

heading: Exclusivity of reserved titles and right of practice of reserved practice
paragraph: (3) Despite this section, this Act does not apply to prevent a person from assuming a title or designation

heading: Exclusivity of reserved titles and right of practice of reserved practice
paragraph: (a) if registered as a registrant in more than one regulatory body under this Act, or

heading: Exclusivity of reserved titles and right of practice of reserved practice
paragraph: (b) as authorized by another enactment purporting to regulate another profession or occupation.

heading: Prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles
paragraph:
52
		  (1) If a regulation under section 51 (1) (a) or 89 (2) (b) [designation of profession] prescribes a title to be used exclusively by registrants of a regulatory body listed in Schedule 2 to this Act, a person other than a registrant of the regulatory body must not use the title, an abbreviation of the title or an equivalent of the title or abbreviation in another language

heading: Prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles
paragraph: (a) to describe the person's work,

heading: Prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles
paragraph: (b) in association with or as part of another title describing the person's work, or

heading: Prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles
paragraph: (c) in association with a description of the person's work.

heading: Prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles
paragraph: (2) If a regulation under section 51 (1) or 89 (2) (c) prescribes a limit or condition in respect of the use of a reserved title, the reserved title must not be used except in accordance with the regulation.

heading: Prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles
paragraph: (3) A person other than a registrant of a regulatory body must not use a reserved title or other name, title, description or abbreviation of a name or title, or an equivalent of a reserved title or other name or title in another language, in any manner that expresses or implies that the person is a registrant or associated with the regulatory body or is authorized to practice in a profession that is subject to a reserved title.

heading: Exceptions for use of reserved titles
paragraph:
53
		  Despite section 52 (1) and (2), but subject to subsection (3) of that section, a person's use of a title prescribed under section 51 (1) (a) or 89 (2) (b), an abbreviation of the title or an equivalent of the title or abbreviation in another language is not a contravention of section 52 (1) if the person

heading: Exceptions for use of reserved titles
paragraph: (a) is authorized by a body in another province or a foreign jurisdiction that regulates a profession in that other province or foreign jurisdiction to do so,

heading: Exceptions for use of reserved titles
paragraph: (b) indicates, in doing so,

heading: Exceptions for use of reserved titles
paragraph: (i)  whether the person is authorized to practise the profession in the other province or foreign jurisdiction, and

heading: Exceptions for use of reserved titles
paragraph: (ii)  the name of the other province or foreign jurisdiction, and

heading: Exceptions for use of reserved titles
paragraph: (c) uses the title only for the purpose of indicating whether the person is authorized to practise the profession in the other province or foreign jurisdiction.

heading: Prohibitions regarding reserved practice
paragraph:
54
		  (1) If a regulation under section 51 (1) (b) or 89 (2) (d) prescribes a service as a reserved practice that may only be provided by a registrant of a particular regulatory body,

heading: Prohibitions regarding reserved practice
