paragraph: (a) a person other than a registrant of the regulatory body must not provide the service, and

heading: Prohibitions regarding reserved practice
paragraph: (b) a person must not recover a fee or remuneration in respect of the provision of the service unless, at the time the service was provided, the person was a registrant of the regulatory body.

heading: Prohibitions regarding reserved practice
paragraph: (2) If a regulation under section 51 (1) (b) or 89 (2) (e) prescribes a service as a reserved practice that may only be provided by or under the supervision of a registrant of a particular regulatory body,

heading: Prohibitions regarding reserved practice
paragraph: (a) a person other than a registrant of the regulatory body must not provide the service unless the person does so under the supervision of such a registrant, and

heading: Prohibitions regarding reserved practice
paragraph: (b) a person other than a registrant of the regulatory body must not recover a fee or remuneration in respect of the provision of the service unless, at the time the service was provided, the person providing the service was supervised by such a registrant.

heading: Exceptions to prohibitions
paragraph:
55
		  Despite section 54, nothing in this Act, the regulations or the bylaws prohibits a person from practising a profession, discipline or other occupation in accordance with this Act, regulations made under this Act or another enactment.

heading: Traditional knowledge
paragraph:
55.1
		  (1) In this section, "Indigenous peoples" has the same meaning as in the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act.

heading: Traditional knowledge
paragraph: (2) Section 54 does not apply to a person exercising the rights of an Indigenous people, including the right to maintain, control, protect or develop any of the following with respect to the Indigenous people:

heading: Traditional knowledge
paragraph: (a) cultural heritage;

heading: Traditional knowledge
paragraph: (b) traditional knowledge;

heading: Traditional knowledge
paragraph: (c) traditional cultural expressions;

heading: Traditional knowledge
paragraph: (d) manifestations of sciences, technologies or cultures.

heading: Definition and application
paragraph: 56		  (1) In this Part, "registrant" includes a former registrant.

heading: Definition and application
paragraph: (2) In the case of a former registrant, the application of this Part is limited to the period of time when the former registrant was acting as a registrant.

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph:
57
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), the board of each regulatory body must make bylaws establishing the following:

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (a) standards of professional and ethical conduct for registrants, which standards may be different for different categories or subcategories of registrants;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (b) standards of competence for registrants, which standards may be different for different categories or subcategories of registrants or different areas of practices;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (c) aspects of practice that a registrant either may or must not

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (i)  delegate to a non-registrant to provide or perform, or

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (ii)  authorize a non-registrant to provide or perform under the supervision of a registrant;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (d) a program to assist registrants in dealing with professional or ethical issues;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (e) continuing education programs or requirements for qualified continuing education for individual registrants, which programs or requirements may be different for different specializations;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (f) continuing education programs or requirements that support reconciliation with Indigenous peoples in British Columbia;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (g) continuing education programs to be provided by registrants that are firms.

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (2) The bylaws made under subsection (1) must include a code of ethics that must include at least the following ethical principles:

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (a) hold paramount the safety, health and welfare of the public, including the protection of the environment and the promotion of health and safety in the workplace;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (b) practice only in those fields where training and ability make the registrant professionally competent;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (c) have regard for the common law and any applicable enactments, federal enactments or enactments of another province;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (d) have regard for applicable standards, policies, plans and practices established by the government or the regulatory body;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (e) maintain competence in relevant specializations, including advances in the regulated practice and relevant science;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (f) provide accurate information in respect of qualifications and experience;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (g) provide professional opinions that distinguish between facts, assumptions and opinions;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (h) avoid situations and circumstances in which there is a real or perceived conflict of interest and ensure conflicts of interest, including perceived conflicts of interest, are properly disclosed and necessary measures are taken so a conflict of interest does not bias decisions or recommendations;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (i) report to the regulatory body and, if applicable, any other appropriate authority, if the registrant, on reasonable and probable grounds, believes that the continued practice of a regulated practice by another registrant or other person, including firms and employers, might pose a risk of significant harm to the environment or to the health or safety of the public or a group of people;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (j) present clearly to employers and clients the possible consequences if professional decisions or judgments are overruled or disregarded;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (k) clearly identify each registrant who has contributed professional work, including recommendations, reports, statements or opinions;

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (l) undertake work and documentation with due diligence and in accordance with any guidance developed to standardize professional documentation for the applicable profession.

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (a) specifying further details about the code of ethics and ethical principles described in subsection (2),

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (b) prescribing additional ethical principles that the board of a regulatory body must establish in a code of ethics for registrants, and

heading: Standards of conduct and competence
paragraph: (c) prescribing ethical principles that apply to a class of registrants, including firms that are registrants, that a regulatory body must include in a code of ethics made under subsection (1).

heading: Duty to report
paragraph:
58
		  (1) In this section, "identified registrant" means a registrant of a regulatory body who is believed to be engaged in conduct described in subsection (2) (a) or (b).

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (2) If a registrant has reasonable and probable grounds to believe that an identified registrant is

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (a) engaged in the regulated practice in a manner that may pose a risk of significant harm to the environment or to the health or safety of the public or a group of people, or

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (b) engaged in a matter or conduct prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council,

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: the registrant must promptly report this to the registrar of the identified registrant's regulatory body.

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) applies even if the information on which the belief is based is confidential and its disclosure is prohibited under another Act.

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (4) If a person

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (a) terminates the employment of an identified registrant,

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (b) revokes, suspends or imposes restrictions on the privileges of the identified registrant, or

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (c) dissolves a partnership or association with the identified registrant,

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: based on a belief described in subsection (2), the person must promptly report this in writing to the registrar of the identified registrant's regulatory body.

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (5) If a person intended to act as described in subsection (4) (a), (b) or (c) but the identified registrant resigned, relinquished privileges or dissolved the partnership or association before the person acted, the person must report this in writing to the registrar of the identified registrant's regulatory body.

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (5.1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, exempt a class of persons from the requirements of this section.

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (6) On receiving a report under subsection (2), (4) or (5), the registrar must act under section 65 [complaints] as though the registrar had received a complaint under that section.

heading: Duty to report
paragraph: (7) Subject to the registrar's approval, the identified registrant, if ordered under this Act to cease or restrict the regulated practice as a registrant of the regulatory body, may employ another registrant of that regulatory body to carry on the regulated practice.

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph:
59
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (a) requiring registrants to make each of the following:

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (i)  a competence declaration;

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (ii)  a conflict of interest declaration, regarding conflicts of interest or perceived conflicts of interest in respect of the service to be provided;

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (b) prescribing the content of declarations under this Division;

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (c) prescribing a period of time within which registrants must make a declaration;

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (d) prescribing circumstances in which registrants must submit, within a prescribed period of time, declarations to the applicable regulatory body, to the superintendent or to a prescribed person or entity;

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (e) requiring registrants or regulatory bodies to keep records of declarations for a prescribed period of time;

heading: Requirements for declarations may be prescribed
paragraph: (f) providing an exception to a requirement in a regulation made under this section.

heading: Registrants must make declarations
paragraph:
60
		  If a regulation made under section 59 requires a registrant to make or submit a declaration, the registrant must do the following:

heading: Registrants must make declarations
paragraph: (a) make the declaration within the prescribed period of time and in the form established by the superintendent;

heading: Registrants must make declarations
paragraph: (b) submit the declaration to the applicable regulatory body, the superintendent or a prescribed person or entity, as the case may be, within the prescribed period of time.

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph:
63
		  (1) The board of a regulatory body may, subject to section 23 (4) [board of regulatory body], establish an audit and practice review committee to

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (a) advise the board on matters falling within the scope of this Division, and

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (b) carry out other functions consistent with this Division.

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (2) The board may authorize the audit and practice review committee to

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (a) exercise a power, authority or jurisdiction of the board under this section, other than a bylaw-making authority, and

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (b) appoint assessors for the purposes of an audit or practice review.

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (3) The board may authorize an audit to be conducted in accordance with the bylaws or an audit program as described in subsection (7).

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (4) The board may authorize a review of the practice of a registrant of the regulatory body to be carried out by an assessor, another officer or employee of the regulatory body or a contractor retained by the regulatory body for this purpose, if

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (a) there is reason to believe that the registrant might have

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (i)  contravened this Act, the regulations or the bylaws,

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (ii)  failed to comply with a standard, limit or condition imposed under this Act,

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (iii)  acted in a manner that constitutes professional misconduct or conduct unbecoming a registrant, or

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (iv)  acted in a manner that constitutes incompetent performance of duties undertaken while engaged in the registrant's regulated practice, or

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (b) the registrant consents.

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (5) If the board authorizes a practice review under subsection (4), the board may do the following:

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (a) by written notice, require a registrant of the regulatory body whose practice is being reviewed under this subsection to cooperate with the review, answer questions and provide access to information, files or records in the registrant's possession or control;

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (b) direct an assessor or other authorized person to prepare a report of the findings of the review, which, if prepared, must also be provided to the registrant whose practice was the subject of the review;

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (c) impose, in accordance with bylaws that the board may make, limits or conditions on the practice of the regulated practice by the registrant, including

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (i)  restricting the practice that may be engaged in by the registrant,

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (ii)  requiring that the registrant be overseen by another registrant when engaged in the regulated practice, and

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (iii)  requiring that the registrant undertake additional training;

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (d) refer a report required under paragraph (b) to an assessor, another officer or a committee with directions to

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (i)  consider whether or not the findings of the review might warrant action under section 66 [investigations authorized by board], and

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (ii)  advise the board or the investigation committee accordingly.

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (6) The board may make bylaws to do the following:

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (a) govern the initiation or conduct of a review referred to in subsection (4);

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (b) specify the nature and extent of the requirements that may be imposed on a registrant under subsection (5) (a);

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (c) govern the referral of a report under subsection (5) (d).

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (7) The board may make bylaws establishing an audit program to routinely or randomly assess the conduct or competence of registrants of the regulatory body.

heading: Audits and practice reviews
paragraph: (8) The confidentiality provisions set out under section 110 [confidentiality - committee matters] apply in respect of the audit and practice review committee.

heading: Investigation committee
paragraph:
64
		  The board of a regulatory body may, subject to section 23 (4), establish an investigation committee to

heading: Investigation committee
paragraph: (a) advise the board on matters falling within the scope of this Division, and

heading: Investigation committee
paragraph: (b) carry out other functions consistent with this Division.

heading: Complaints
paragraph:
65
		  (1) A person may make a complaint to the regulatory body, the board or an officer about a registrant of the regulatory body who may be

heading: Complaints
paragraph: (a) engaged in the registrant's regulated practice in an incompetent manner, or

heading: Complaints
paragraph: (b) guilty of professional misconduct, conduct unbecoming a registrant or a breach of this Act or the bylaws.

heading: Complaints
paragraph: (2) The board of the regulatory body may make bylaws governing the disposition of a complaint under subsection (1).

heading: Complaints
paragraph: (3) The registrar must advise the person who makes a complaint under subsection (1) of the disposition of the complaint.

heading: Complaints
paragraph: (4) The board, or an officer or a committee authorized to do so by the board, may, on the initiative of the board, the officer or the committee, or on receiving a complaint under subsection (1), authorize a practice review under section 63 or take action under section 66.

heading: Complaints
paragraph: (5) A registrant of the regulatory body who resigns before or after the beginning of a practice review, investigation, hearing or other proceeding under this Act remains subject to the jurisdiction of the regulatory body.

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph:
66
		  (1) The board of a regulatory body may do the following:

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (a) authorize an investigation into the conduct or competence of a registrant, to be carried out by a committee of the regulatory body, an officer or employee of the regulatory body, or a contractor retained by the regulatory body for this purpose, if there is reason to believe that the registrant may have been guilty of

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (i)  professional misconduct,

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (ii)  conduct unbecoming a registrant, or

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (iii)  incompetent performance of duties undertaken while engaged in the registrant's regulated practice;

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (b) if there is reason to believe that a registrant whose conduct or competence is being investigated under this subsection possesses any information, record or thing that is relevant to the investigation, issue a written notice requiring the registrant to

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (i)  cooperate with the investigation,

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (ii)  answer questions,

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (iii)  produce files, records or other evidence in the registrant's possession or control, and

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (iv)  provide explanations on request;

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (c) if there is reason to believe that the conduct or competence of a registrant may warrant action under this subsection, issue a written notice requiring the registrant to appear before the board or the investigation committee to discuss the conduct or competence of the registrant;

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (d) issue a citation ordering a discipline hearing under section 75 [discipline hearings] to inquire into the conduct or competence of a registrant;

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (e) rescind a citation issued under paragraph (d).

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (2) The board may make bylaws

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (a) authorizing the board to

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (i)  summarily suspend or cancel the registration of a registrant who has been convicted of an indictable offence, or

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (ii)  summarily reject the application of an applicant convicted of an indictable offence,

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (b) governing the initiation or conduct of an investigation referred to in subsection (1) (a),

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (c) specifying the nature and extent of the requirements that may be imposed on a registrant in a notice issued under subsection (1) (b),

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (d) governing the initiation or conduct of an appearance before the board or the investigation committee under subsection (1) (c), and

heading: Investigations authorized by board
paragraph: (e) governing the issuance or rescission of a citation.

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph:
67
		  (1) If the board of a regulatory body, or a discipline committee established under section 75 [discipline hearings], considers the action necessary in the public interest during an investigation under section 66 (1) (a) or pending a hearing under section 75, the board may, by order and without giving the registrant an opportunity to be heard,

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (a) impose limits or conditions on the practice of the regulated practice by the registrant, or

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (b) suspend the registration of the registrant.

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (2) An order of the board under subsection (1) must

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (a) be in writing,

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (b) include reasons for the order, and

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (c) be delivered to the complainant, if any, and to the registrant.

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (3) A decision under subsection (1) is not effective until the earlier of

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (a) the time the registrant receives the notice under subsection (2), and

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (b) 3 days after the notice is mailed to the registrant at the last address for the registrant recorded in the register of the regulatory body.

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (4) If the board determines that action taken under subsection (1) is no longer necessary to protect the public, it must cancel the limits, conditions or suspension and must notify the registrant in writing of the cancellation as soon as possible.

heading: Extraordinary action to protect public
paragraph: (5) After an order of the board is made under subsection (1), the registrar of the regulatory body must promptly notify the superintendent about the order.

heading: Investigators
paragraph:
68
		  (1) An investigation committee of a regulatory body may appoint persons as investigators for the regulatory body.

heading: Investigators
paragraph: (2) The registrar of a regulatory body is an investigator for the regulatory body.

heading: Investigators
paragraph: (3) The registrar may appoint a deputy registrar of the regulatory body as an investigator for the regulatory body.

heading: Powers and duties of investigators
paragraph:
69
		  (1) During regular business hours, an investigator under section 68 may, subject to any limits or conditions imposed on the investigator by the investigation committee, investigate, inquire into, inspect, observe or examine one or more of the following without a court order:

heading: Powers and duties of investigators
paragraph: (a) the premises, equipment and materials used by a registrant to engage in the regulated practice;

heading: Powers and duties of investigators
paragraph: (b) the records of the registrant relating to the registrant's regulated practice and may copy those records;

heading: Powers and duties of investigators
paragraph: (c) the regulated practice, as engaged in, performed by or under the supervision of the registrant.

heading: Powers and duties of investigators
paragraph: (2) The investigation committee may direct an investigator to act under subsection (1) or undertake any aspect of an investigation under section 66.

heading: Powers and duties of investigators
paragraph: (3) If an investigator acts under this section as a consequence of a direction given under subsection (2), the investigator must report the results of those actions in writing to the investigation committee.

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph:
70
		  (1) A person authorized by an investigation committee of a regulatory body may apply to the Supreme Court for an order that authorizes a person named in the order

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (a) to enter into the premises or land specified in the order at any reasonable time and conduct an inspection, examination or analysis,

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (b) to require the production of any record, property, assets or things and to inspect, examine or analyze them, and

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (c) on giving a receipt, to seize and remove any record, property, assets or things inspected, examined or analyzed under paragraph (a) or (b) for further inspection, examination or analysis.

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (2) Unless the court otherwise directs, an application under subsection (1) may be made without notice to any person and may be heard in private.

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (3) On application under subsection (1), the court may make an order under this section if satisfied on oath that there are reasonable grounds for believing that evidence may be found

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (a) that a person who is not a registrant of the regulatory body has contravened this Act, the regulations or the bylaws, or

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (b) that a person who is a registrant of the regulatory body has

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (i)  contravened this Act, the regulations or the bylaws,

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (ii)  failed to comply with a standard, limit or condition imposed under this Act,

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (iii)  acted in a manner that constitutes professional misconduct or conduct unbecoming a registrant, or

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (iv)  acted in a manner that constitutes incompetent performance of duties undertaken while engaged in the registrant's regulated practice.

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (4) In an order under this section, the court

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (a) must specify the premises or land to be entered and must generally describe any thing to be searched for and examined, audited or seized,

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (b) may include any limitations or conditions the court considers proper, including the time of entry, the disposition of things seized and the access by any person to the things seized, and

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (c) may direct that section 71 does not apply to a thing specified in the order if all limitations and conditions included under paragraph (b) are met.

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (5) Despite a court order made under subsection (4) (c), section 71 applies if the person who owned or controlled the thing at the time of the seizure requests in writing that section 71 be applied to the thing seized.

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (6) A request under subsection (5) of this section must be delivered to the investigation committee by personal service or registered mail no later than 21 days after the seizure.

heading: Search and seizure under court order
paragraph: (7) A person who, while conducting or attempting to conduct an entry or search under this section, finds any thing not described in the order that the person has reasonable grounds to believe will provide evidence in respect of a contravention of this Act, the regulations or the bylaws may seize and remove that thing.

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph:
71
		  (1) For the purposes of subsection (2), a person who makes a seizure under section 70 must report the seizure as soon as practicable to a judge of the Supreme Court, who must be the judge who issued the order under which the seizure was made unless this is not practicable.

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (2) On receiving a report under subsection (1), the judge must

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (a) order the thing that was seized returned to its owner or other person entitled to it unless satisfied that an order under paragraph (b) should be made, or

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (b) order the thing detained if satisfied that the detention is required for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (3) An investigator may make one or more copies of any record detained under subsection (2).

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (4) A document purporting to be certified by a representative of an investigation committee to be a true copy made under the authority of subsection (3) is evidence of the nature and content of the original document.

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (5) Subject to an order under section 70 (4) (b), the person from whom any thing is seized under this section or the owner of the thing, if that person is a different person, is entitled to inspect that thing at any reasonable time and, in the case of a record, to obtain one copy of the record at the expense of the regulatory body.

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (6) A record must not be detained under this section for a period longer than 3 months from the time of its seizure unless, before the expiration of the period, either

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (a) the person from whom the record was seized consents to the continued detention of the record, or

heading: Detention of things seized
paragraph: (b) the Supreme Court, on application and after being satisfied that the continued detention is justified, orders the continued detention of the record for a specified period of time.

heading: Reprimand or remedial action by consent
paragraph:
72
		  (1) In relation to a matter investigated under section 66 (1) (a) [investigations authorized by board], the investigation committee or the discipline committee of a regulatory body may request in writing that the registrant do one or more of the following:

heading: Reprimand or remedial action by consent
paragraph: (a) undertake not to repeat the conduct to which the matter relates;

heading: Reprimand or remedial action by consent
paragraph: (b) undertake educational courses specified by the audit and practice review committee;

heading: Reprimand or remedial action by consent
paragraph: (c) consent to a reprimand;

heading: Reprimand or remedial action by consent
paragraph: (d) undertake or consent to any other action specified by the audit and practice review committee.

heading: Reprimand or remedial action by consent
paragraph: (2) If a consent or undertaking given under subsection (1) relates to a complaint made under section 65 [complaints], the investigation committee or the discipline committee must, within 30 days of the consent or undertaking being given, deliver to the complainant a written summary of the consent or undertaking.

heading: Reprimand or remedial action by consent
paragraph: (3) If a registrant refuses to give an undertaking or consent requested under subsection (1), or if a registrant fails to comply with an undertaking or consent given in response to a request under subsection (1), the board may direct the registrar to issue a citation for a hearing by the discipline committee regarding the matter.

heading: Consent orders
paragraph:
73
		  (1) The investigation committee or the discipline committee of a regulatory body may, before the commencement of the discipline hearing, propose, in writing, to the person who is the subject of an investigation under section 66 (1) that a consent order be made for the voluntary resolution of one or more matters that may otherwise be dealt with at the discipline hearing.

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (2) A consent order is made if

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (a) the person who is the subject of an investigation under section 66 (1) accepts the proposal of the investigation committee or the discipline committee under subsection (1) of this section, or

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (b) an agreement is reached under section 74 (2) between the person who is the subject of an investigation under section 66 (1) and the investigation committee or the discipline committee.

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (3) A consent order made under subsection (2) (a) must contain

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (a) the terms set out in the proposal made by the investigation committee or discipline committee under subsection (1),

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (b) one or more admissions by the person who is the subject of the investigation in relation to one or more of the matters to be dealt with at the discipline hearing, and

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (c) one or more of the actions taken or penalties imposed in section 75 (3) to (7) [discipline hearings].

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (4) A consent order made under subsection (2) has the same effect as an action taken or penalty imposed under section 75.

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (5) After a consent order is made under subsection (2), no further action may be taken under this section and section 75 with respect to the matters contained in the consent order.

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (6) If the person to whom a proposal under subsection (1) is made rejects the proposal,

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (a) an investigation under section 66 in respect of the matters contained in the proposal must proceed as though the proposal had not been made, and

heading: Consent orders
paragraph: (b) the discipline committee conducting a hearing under section 75 must not consider the admissions contained in the proposal or the terms of the proposal in determining the matters or in taking an action or imposing a penalty in respect of the matters.

heading: Alternative complaint resolution
paragraph:
74
		  (1) At any time, a person who is the subject of an investigation under section 66 (1), the registrar of a regulatory body and the investigation committee or the discipline committee, as applicable, may agree that alternative complaint resolution, as provided in the bylaws, will commence between the person who is the subject of the investigation and the applicable committee in respect of one or more matters to be dealt with at the hearing.

heading: Alternative complaint resolution
paragraph: (2) If the person who is the subject of the investigation, the registrar and the investigation committee or the discipline committee, as applicable, reach an agreement in respect of one or more of the matters to be dealt with at the hearing, a consent order may be made under section 73 (2) (b) on the terms set out in the agreement.

heading: Alternative complaint resolution
paragraph: (3) No further action may be taken under this section and section 75 with respect to a matter referred to in subsection (1) of this section unless the registrar and the investigation committee or the discipline committee, as applicable, determine that an agreement in respect of the matter cannot be reached within a reasonable period of time.

heading: Alternative complaint resolution
paragraph: (4) If the registrar and the investigation committee or the discipline committee, as applicable, determine that an agreement in respect of a matter referred to in subsection (1) cannot be reached within a reasonable period of time,

heading: Alternative complaint resolution
paragraph: (a) an investigation under section 66 in respect of the matter must proceed, and

heading: Alternative complaint resolution
paragraph: (b) the discipline committee conducting a hearing under section 75 must not consider the information disclosed during the alternative complaint resolution process in determining the matters or in taking an action or imposing a penalty in respect of the matters.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph:
75
		  (1) The board of a regulatory body may, subject to section 23 (4) [board of regulatory body], establish a discipline committee to

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (a) advise the board on matters falling within the scope of this Division, and

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (b) carry out other functions consistent with the role of the discipline committee under this Division.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (2) This section applies to the hearing of a citation.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (3) A hearing must be conducted in accordance with section 77 [discipline committee to conduct hearings].

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (4) The discipline committee must

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (a) make determinations and take action according to this section,

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (b) give written reasons for a determination about the conduct or competence of the respondent and an action taken against the respondent, and

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (c) record in writing an order for costs.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (5) After a hearing, the discipline committee must do one of the following:

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (a) dismiss the citation;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (b) determine that the respondent has committed one or more of the following:

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (i)  professional misconduct;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (ii)  conduct unbecoming a registrant;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (iii)  incompetent performance of duties undertaken while engaged in the registrant's regulated practice.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (6) If, under subsection (5), an adverse determination is made against a respondent, other than a trainee, the discipline committee must do one or more of the following:

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (a) reprimand the respondent;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (b) impose a penalty on the respondent in an amount that is,

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (i)  in the case of an individual, not more than $100 000, and

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a firm, not more than $250 000;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (c) impose conditions on the respondent's registration as a registrant of the regulatory body;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (d) suspend the respondent's registration in the regulatory body

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (i)  for a specified period of time,

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (ii)  until the respondent complies with a requirement under paragraph (f), or

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (iii)  for a specified minimum period of time and until the respondent complies with a requirement under paragraph (f);

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (e) cancel the respondent's registration in the regulatory body;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (f) require the respondent to

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (i)  complete a remedial program to the satisfaction of the board or the audit and practice review committee, or

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (ii)  appear before a committee established by the board and satisfy the committee that the respondent is competent to practise the registrant's regulated practice.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (7) If, under subsection (5), an adverse determination is made against a trainee, the discipline committee may do one or more of the following:

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (a) require that the trainee undertake further training;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (b) reprimand the trainee;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (c) impose a penalty on the trainee in an amount not exceeding $2 000;

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (d) cancel the enrolment of the trainee.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (8) After a hearing, the registrar of the regulatory body must promptly

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (a) notify the superintendent about the disposition of the hearing,

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (b) update the online register maintained under section 31 [registrar and register for regulatory body], and

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (c) publish information about the disposition of the hearing on a website maintained by or on behalf of the regulatory body in the form and manner required by the superintendent or in accordance with regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (9) A penalty imposed under this Act may be recovered as a debt owing to the regulatory body and, when collected, is the property of the regulatory body.

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (10) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council makes regulations in respect of the publication of prescribed information about a hearing under this section, including publication of prescribed information about the hearing on a website maintained by or on behalf of the regulatory body, the regulatory body

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (a) must publish the prescribed information in the form, manner and time period required by the regulations, and

heading: Discipline hearings
paragraph: (b) may make bylaws in respect of the publication.

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph:
76
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: "conduct of concern" means, as applicable,

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) professional misconduct,

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) conduct unbecoming a registrant, or

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (c) incompetent performance of duties undertaken while engaged in the regulated practice;

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) a professional regulator or regulatory body other than the applicable regulatory body, or

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) a body, in a jurisdiction outside Canada, that regulates a profession in that jurisdiction.

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (2) A discipline committee of a regulatory body may make an order under section 75 (5) respecting a registrant without issuing a citation under section 66 (1) (d) [investigations authorized by board] or conducting a hearing under section 75 if the discipline committee learns that a different governing body has found, or the registrant has admitted to a different governing body, that the registrant committed an act that, in the opinion of the discipline committee, would constitute conduct of concern under this Act.

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (3) The discipline committee may take action under subsection (2)

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) regardless of whether the act referred to in that subsection was committed before or after the registrant was registered under Division 2 [Enrolment, Admission and Reinstatement] of Part 4 [Registrants], and

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) only after giving the registrant

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (i)  notice of the proposed action, in accordance with the bylaws,

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (ii)  a copy of the record of the relevant decision or findings made or action taken by the different governing body, and

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (iii)  an opportunity to be heard, which may be limited to a hearing in writing.

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (4) If the discipline committee makes an order under subsection (2), section 75 applies as if a determination had been made by the discipline committee under section 75 (4).

heading: Conduct in another jurisdiction
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of this section, a certified copy of a record of the decision or findings made or action taken by the different governing body in respect of a registrant is proof, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, of the findings made or the action taken, without proof of the signature of the person purporting to have signed on behalf of that different governing body.

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph:
77
		  (1) A discipline committee of a regulatory body may establish panels to conduct hearings under section 75 in accordance with the bylaws.

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (2) A panel established under subsection (1) must include at least one lay member, who is not a registrant, and may exercise any power or authority a discipline committee may exercise under this Act.

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (3) The board of the regulatory body may make bylaws

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (a) for the appointment and composition of panels,

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (b) for the practice and procedure for hearings, and

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (c) providing for oral or written hearings.

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (4) A discipline committee or panel may order an applicant or respondent who is the subject of a hearing under section 75 to do either or both of the following:

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (a) give evidence on oath or by affirmation;

heading: Discipline committee to conduct hearings
paragraph: (b) at any time before or during a hearing, produce all files, records or other information in the possession of that person that may be relevant to a matter under consideration.

heading: Failure to attend
paragraph:
78
		  (1) This section applies if an applicant or respondent fails to attend or remain in attendance at a discipline hearing under section 75.

heading: Failure to attend
paragraph: (2) If satisfied that the applicant or respondent has been notified of a hearing referred to in subsection (1), the discipline committee of a regulatory body or the panel, as applicable, may proceed with the hearing in the absence of the applicant or respondent and make any order that the discipline committee or panel could have made in the presence of the applicant or respondent.

heading: Right to counsel
paragraph:
79
		  (1) An applicant or respondent may appear with counsel at a discipline hearing under section 75.

heading: Right to counsel
paragraph: (2) The board, an employee or officer or a committee of a regulatory body may employ or retain legal or other assistance in exercising any power, authority or jurisdiction conferred under this Act, including the conduct of an audit, practice review or discipline investigation or the issuance of a citation, and may be represented by counsel at a discipline hearing under section 75.

heading: Right to counsel
paragraph: (3) A discipline committee or panel may employ or retain legal or other assistance in conducting a hearing.

heading: Witnesses
paragraph:
80
		  (1) For the purposes of a discipline hearing under section 75 of this Act, the following provisions of the Administrative Tribunals Act apply to the panel:

heading: Witnesses
paragraph: (a) section 34 (3) and (4) [power to compel witnesses and order disclosure];

heading: Witnesses
paragraph: (b) section 48 [maintenance of order at hearings];

heading: Witnesses
paragraph: (c) section 49 [contempt proceeding for uncooperative witness or other person].

heading: Witnesses
paragraph: (2) A regulatory body or a respondent may apply to the Supreme Court, without notice to anyone, for an order that a subpoena in the form set out in the Supreme Court Civil Rules be issued to compel the attendance of a person as a witness at a discipline hearing under section 75 of this Act.

heading: Witnesses
paragraph: (3) The Supreme Court Civil Rules in respect of the following apply to a person who is the subject of an order under subsection (2) of this section:

heading: Witnesses
paragraph: (a) the use of a subpoena to compel a person to attend at the trial of an action;

heading: Witnesses
paragraph: (b) failure to obey a subpoena or an order of the court.

heading: Costs
paragraph: 81		  (1) A discipline committee or panel, in the context of a discipline hearing under section 75, may require the respondent to pay the costs of one or both of the following:

heading: Costs
paragraph: (a) an investigation;

heading: Costs
paragraph: (b) the hearing under section 75.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (2) Costs assessed under subsection (1)

heading: Costs
paragraph: (a) must not exceed the actual costs incurred by the regulatory body during the course of the investigation and hearing, and

heading: Costs
paragraph: (b) may include the salary costs for employees or officers engaged in the investigation and hearing.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (3) The board may make bylaws governing the assessment of costs under subsection (1), including the following:

heading: Costs
paragraph: (a) the factors to be considered in assessing costs;

heading: Costs
paragraph: (b) the maximum amount of costs that may be assessed within the limits set out in subsection (2);

heading: Costs
paragraph: (c) the time allowed for payment of costs;

heading: Costs
paragraph: (d) the extension of time for payment of costs.

heading: Costs
paragraph: (4) The amount of costs assessed against a respondent under subsection (1) may be recovered as a debt owing to a regulatory body and, when collected, that amount is the property of the regulatory body.

heading: Time limit for judicial review
paragraph:
81.1
		  (1) In this section, "statutory power" means a statutory power as defined in the Judicial Review Procedure Act, other than a power to make a regulation or a bylaw.

heading: Time limit for judicial review
paragraph: (2) An application for judicial review of a decision in respect of the exercise of a statutory power under this Division or under section 48 [review on the record] must be brought within 60 days of the date the applicant receives written notice of the decision.

heading: Time limit for judicial review
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), either before or after expiration of the period of time in that subsection, the court may extend the period of time for bringing the application, on terms the court considers proper, if it is satisfied that

heading: Time limit for judicial review
paragraph: (a) there are serious grounds for relief,

heading: Time limit for judicial review
paragraph: (b) there is a reasonable explanation for the delay, and

heading: Time limit for judicial review
paragraph: (c) no substantial prejudice or hardship will result to a person affected by the delay.

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: 82		  (1) The board of each regulatory body must, in accordance with this section and any regulations made under subsection (4), make bylaws about information that is to be made publicly available by the regulatory body in respect of the following:

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (a) discipline hearings;

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (b) consent orders;

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (c) any other matter prescribed by regulation.

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (2) The information described in subsection (1) is to be made publicly available on a website maintained by or on behalf of the regulatory body and published in the form, manner and time period required by the bylaws.

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (3) Information that is to be made public must include the following:

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (a) if a registrant's conduct is at issue, the name of the registrant;

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (b) the fact that a citation is issued;

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (c) any other information prescribed by regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations in respect of

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (a) any exceptions in respect of the application of this section, and

heading: Information to be publicly available
paragraph: (b) any other matter relating to information that is to be made publicly available under this section.

heading: If registration of firm as registrant suspended or cancelled
paragraph:
83
		  (1) A decision to suspend or cancel, as applicable, the registration of a registrant of a regulatory body that is a firm under the following sections may, by order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, be rescinded, varied or substituted:

heading: If registration of firm as registrant suspended or cancelled
paragraph: (a) section 67 [extraordinary action to protect public];

heading: If registration of firm as registrant suspended or cancelled

heading: If registration of firm as registrant suspended or cancelled
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, impose limits or conditions on the regulated practice by a registrant that is a firm if the decision to suspend or cancel the firm's registration is rescinded, varied or substituted under subsection (1).

heading: If registration of firm as registrant suspended or cancelled
paragraph: (3) An order by the Lieutenant Governor in Council under this section

heading: If registration of firm as registrant suspended or cancelled
paragraph: (b) does not affect any other provisions under this Act that apply in respect of the registrant.

heading: Limited liability partnerships

heading: Limited liability partnerships
paragraph: (2) The liability of a registrant for the registrant's own professional negligence is not affected by the fact that the registrant is providing services in respect of a regulated practice through a limited liability partnership.

heading: Limited liability partnerships
paragraph: (3) The application of the provisions of this Act and the regulations and the bylaws of a regulatory body is not affected by a registrant's relationship to a limited liability partnership as a partner, employee or contractor.
