heading: Application for designation
paragraph: 85		  (1) A professional regulator or professional organization seeking designation of its profession under this Act must apply to the superintendent.

heading: Application for designation
paragraph: (2) An application under subsection (1) must be in the form and contain the information required by the superintendent and must be submitted with the fee prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Application for designation
paragraph: (3) On receiving an application under subsection (1), the superintendent may

heading: Application for designation
paragraph: (a) refuse the application without assessment, or

heading: Application for designation
paragraph: (b) conduct an assessment the superintendent considers necessary to determine whether the profession should be designated under this Act.

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph:
86
		  (1) The superintendent may, in the absence of an application under section 85 (1), conduct an assessment of a profession to determine whether it should be designated under this Act.

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (2) If the superintendent decides to conduct an assessment under subsection (1) or section 85 (3) (b) to determine whether a profession should be designated under this Act, the superintendent must give public notice of the assessment in the Gazette and on a website maintained by or on behalf of the superintendent.

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (3) Without limiting an assessment under this Act, other than an assessment under Division 3 [Amalgamation of Regulatory Bodies], the superintendent may do one or more of the following for the purposes of the assessment:

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (a) require the professional regulator or professional organization to provide further information;

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (b) examine the directors and officers of the professional regulator or professional organization;

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (c) seek the advice of other professional regulators, professional organizations or persons;

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (d) if the superintendent considers the action to be in the best interests of the professional regulator or professional organization or of the public, hold hearings the superintendent considers necessary in a manner the superintendent determines;

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (e) take other actions the superintendent considers necessary and incidental to the consideration of the application or matter.

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (4) If the superintendent holds a hearing under subsection (3) (d), the superintendent may order a person to

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (a) attend the hearing,

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (b) give evidence, and

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (c) produce records in the possession of or under the control of the person.

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (5) On application by the superintendent to the Supreme Court, a person who fails to attend or to produce records as required by an order under subsection (4) is liable to be committed for contempt as if in breach of an order or judgment of the Supreme Court.

heading: Assessment regarding possible designation
paragraph: (6) Subject to the regulations, the superintendent may charge to a professional regulator or professional organization part of the costs, including the administrative costs, incurred by the superintendent to conduct an assessment regarding the professional regulator's or professional organization's application under section 85 (1).

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph:
87
		  (1) If the superintendent conducts an assessment under section 85 (3) (b) [application for designation] or 86 (1) in respect of a profession, the superintendent must provide a report to the minister that includes the following:

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (a) a recommendation respecting whether the profession should be designated by regulation under section 89 (1) [designation of profession];

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (b) if the superintendent recommends that the profession be designated, a recommendation respecting which one of the following sections should apply:

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (i)  section 90.1 [new regulatory body established under this Act];

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (ii)  section 90.2 [continuation of professional regulator as regulatory body under this Act];

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (iii)  section 90.4 [existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession].

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (2) Before providing a report to the minister under subsection (1), the superintendent must do the following:

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (a) consider at least the following matters:

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (i)  the degree of risk to the environment and to the health or safety of the public from incompetent, unethical or impaired practice of the profession;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (ii)  the degree of supervision necessary or desirable in respect of a person practising the profession;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (iii)  the degree of supervision that a person practising the profession receives or is likely to receive with respect to that practice;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (iv)  the educational programs that exist in British Columbia or elsewhere for the proper education and training of persons with respect to the practice of the profession and the contents of those programs;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (v)  any information obtained during the assessment;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (vi)  any prescribed criteria respecting matters of public interest that must be considered by the superintendent;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (b) provide a copy of the report to the following, as applicable:

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (i)  the professional regulator or professional organization that made the application to the superintendent under section 85 (1);

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (ii)  the professional regulator that governs the profession in respect of which the superintendent conducted the assessment;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (iii)  a professional organization that, in the opinion of the superintendent, is closely associated with the profession in respect of which the superintendent conducted the assessment;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (c) give the applicable professional regulator or professional organization referred to in paragraph (b) an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (3) The minister must

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (a) consider the report provided to the minister under subsection (1),

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (b) decide whether it would be in the public interest to recommend to the Lieutenant Governor in Council that the profession be designated by regulation under section 89 (1), and

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (c) if the minister makes a recommendation to the Lieutenant Governor in Council under paragraph (b), include a recommendation respecting which one of the following sections should apply:

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (i)  section 90.1;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (ii)  section 90.2;

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (iii)  section 90.4.

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (4) The minister must, in relation to the minister's decision under subsection (3) (b) and, if applicable, the minister's recommendation under subsection (3) (c), provide written reasons to the applicable persons referred to in subsection (2) (b).

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (5) The superintendent must publish the minister's written reasons under subsection (4) on a publicly accessible website maintained by the superintendent.

heading: Assessment and recommendation respecting designation of profession
paragraph: (6) For certainty, if the minister decides not to make a recommendation to the Lieutenant Governor in Council that a profession be designated under section 89 (1), an application made to the superintendent under section 85 (1) in respect of the designation of the profession is deemed to have been refused.

heading: Regulations in respect of applications for designation
paragraph:
88
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations in respect of the following:

heading: Regulations in respect of applications for designation
paragraph: (a) fees, or rates or levels of fees, to be submitted with an application under section 85 (1);

heading: Regulations in respect of applications for designation
paragraph: (b) limits on the superintendent's authority to charge costs under section 86 (6).

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, designate a profession for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (1.1) In a regulation made under subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council must do one of the following:

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (a) specify

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (i)  that a new regulatory body is to be established under section 90.1 [new regulatory body established under this Act],

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (ii)  the date on which the establishment of the new regulatory body is to have effect,

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (iii)  the name that must be used by the new regulatory body, and

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (iv)  if applicable, the name of the professional regulator that, as of the date under subparagraph (ii), will cease to be responsible for the governance of the designated profession;

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (b) specify

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (i)  the professional regulator that is to be continued as a regulatory body under section 90.2 [continuation of professional regulator as regulatory body under this Act],

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (ii)  the date on which the continuation is to have effect, and

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (iii)  the name that must be used by the regulatory body, if the name is not the same as the name of the professional regulator;

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (c) specify

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (i)  the existing regulatory body that, under section 90.4 [existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession], is to be responsible for carrying out the objects of this Act in respect of the designated profession,

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (ii)  the date on which responsibility is to commence, and

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (iii)  if applicable, the name of the professional regulator that, as of the date under subparagraph (ii), will cease to be responsible for the governance of the designated profession.

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (2) In respect of a designated profession, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, prescribe the following matters:

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (b) one or more titles to be used exclusively by registrants in accordance with Part 5 [Reserved Titles and Reserved Practice];

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (c) limits or conditions in respect of the use of titles prescribed under paragraph (b) in accordance with Part 5;

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (d) services that may be provided only by registrants in accordance with Part 5;

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (e) services that may be provided under the supervision of a registrant by a person who is not a registrant;

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (f) services that may be provided by a registrant despite a limitation or prohibition, including a limitation or prohibition under another enactment;

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (g) restricted activities that may be performed by registrants in the course of providing services referred to in paragraphs (d) to (f) in accordance with section 43 (1) [restricted and specialized areas of practice];

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (h) limits or conditions on the performance of restricted activities referred to in paragraph (g);

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (i) requirements under this Act from which the regulatory body prescribed for the profession is exempted;

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (j) matters in respect of which the regulatory body prescribed for the profession may not make bylaws.

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (3) A designation under subsection (1) and regulations under subsection (2) may recognize that 2 or more professions are included in the designation.

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (4) If subsection (3) applies, this Act, the regulations or the bylaws of the regulatory body responsible for carrying out the objects of this Act in respect of the designated professions may be applied to

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (a) each designated profession separately, or

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (b) 2 or more designated professions jointly.

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (6) A notice under subsection (5) must be given to the regulatory body

heading: Designation of profession
paragraph: (b) if the Lieutenant Governor in Council prescribes a shorter notice period, within that shorter period.

heading: New regulatory body established under this Act
paragraph:
90.1
		  If a regulation under section 89 (1) [designation of profession] specifies that this section applies in respect of a designated profession,

heading: New regulatory body established under this Act
paragraph: (a) a corporation responsible for carrying out the objects of this Act is, on the date specified in the regulation, established as a regulatory body under this Act in respect of the designated profession,

heading: New regulatory body established under this Act
paragraph: (b) the regulatory body must, on the date specified in the regulation, assume responsibility for carrying out the objects of this Act, and

heading: New regulatory body established under this Act
paragraph: (c) if applicable, the professional regulator referred to in the regulation must, on the date specified in the regulation, cease to hold responsibility for carrying out the objects of this Act.

heading: Continuation of professional regulator as regulatory body under this Act
paragraph:
90.2
		  If a regulation under section 89 (1) [designation of profession] specifies that this section applies in respect of a designated profession, the specified professional regulator, effective on the date specified in the regulation, is

heading: Continuation of professional regulator as regulatory body under this Act
paragraph: (a) continued as a regulatory body under this Act, and

heading: Continuation of professional regulator as regulatory body under this Act
paragraph: (b) responsible for carrying out the objects of this Act in respect of the designated profession.

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph:
90.3
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: "affected professional regulator", in relation to a designated profession, means the professional regulator under section 89 (1.1) (b) (i) [designation of profession];

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: "pre-existing Act" means the Act, if any, under which an affected professional regulator is responsible for the governance of a profession.

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations in respect of any matters necessary for the following:

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (a) facilitating the establishment of a regulatory body under section 90.1 [new regulatory body established under this Act];

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (b) facilitating the continuation of an affected professional regulator as a regulatory body under section 90.2;

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (c) facilitating the transition from the operation of a pre-existing Act to the operation of this Act;

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (d) facilitating the cessation, by an affected professional regulator, of responsibility for the governance of the profession;

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (e) meeting or removing any difficulties encountered in respect of paragraphs (a), (b), (c) and (d), and for that purpose disapplying or varying any provision of

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (i)  this Act, or

heading: Regulations respecting establishment or continuation
paragraph: (ii)  a pre-existing Act.

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph:
90.4
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: "affected professional regulator", in respect of a designated profession, means a professional regulator under section 89 (1.1) (c) (iii) [designation of profession];

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: "pre-existing Act" means the Act, if any, under which an affected professional regulator is governed.

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (2) If a regulation under section 89 (1) specifies that an existing regulatory body is, under this section, to be responsible for carrying out the objects of this Act in respect of a designated profession,

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (a) the regulatory body must, on the date specified in the regulation, assume responsibility for carrying out the objects of this Act, and

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (b) if applicable, the affected professional regulator must, on the date specified in the regulation, cease to hold responsibility for carrying out the objects of this Act.

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations necessary for the following:

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (a) facilitating the assumption, by a regulatory body, of responsibility for carrying out the objects of this Act;

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (b) facilitating the cessation, by an affected professional regulator, of responsibility for the governance of a designated profession;

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (c) facilitating the transition from the operation of a pre-existing Act to the operation of this Act;

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (d) meeting or removing any difficulties encountered in respect of paragraphs (a), (b) and (c), and for that purpose disapplying or varying any provision of

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (i)  this Act, or

heading: Existing regulatory body to be responsible for designated profession
paragraph: (ii)  a pre-existing Act.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph:
91
		  (1) In this Division:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "amalgamated regulatory body" means the regulatory body that results from an amalgamation of 2 or more regulatory bodies or, if applicable, professional regulators or professional organizations, under this Division;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "amalgamation date" means, subject to subsection (2), the date on which the amalgamation of 2 or more regulatory bodies or, if applicable, professional regulators or professional organizations, under this Division occurs;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "former body", in relation to an amalgamated regulatory body, means a regulatory body or, if applicable, professional regulator or professional organization, that is amalgamating, or has amalgamated, under this Division with another regulatory body or, if applicable, professional regulator or professional organization, to form the amalgamated regulatory body;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "officer" means

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a registrar, deputy registrar or inspector, or

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) an assessor appointed in respect of an audit, a practice review or a similar quality assurance program.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Division, if a time is set under section 93 (1) (b) [amalgamation], a reference to the amalgamation date is to be read as a reference to that time on the amalgamation date.

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph:
92
		  (1) On request of the regulatory bodies to be amalgamated or on the initiative of the superintendent, the superintendent may determine whether 2 or more regulatory bodies should be amalgamated under this Division and the amalgamation may proceed with or without an investigation.

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (2) Without limiting an assessment under this Division, the superintendent may do one or more of the following for the purposes of an assessment:

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (a) require a regulatory body to provide information;

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (b) examine registrants of the board and the registrar of a regulatory body;

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (c) seek the advice of an organization or person;

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (d) do other things that the superintendent considers necessary and incidental to the consideration of the matter.

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (3) If the superintendent conducts an examination under subsection (2) (b), the superintendent may order a person to

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (a) attend the examination,

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (b) give evidence, and

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (c) produce records in the possession of or under the control of the person.

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (4) In determining whether 2 or more regulatory bodies should be amalgamated under this Division, the superintendent must

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (a) have regard to any information obtained through a request or an investigation made under subsection (1), and

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (b) make the determination in accordance with the prescribed criteria, if any.

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (5) If the superintendent determines that 2 or more regulatory bodies should be amalgamated under this Division, the superintendent must recommend amalgamation to the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (6) If the superintendent determines that 2 or more regulatory bodies should not be amalgamated under this Division, and if the superintendent received a request to amalgamate or acted under subsection (2) (a) or (b), the superintendent must refuse the request and provide reasons for the refusal to the regulatory body that made the request or was subject to the action.

heading: Determination of whether to amalgamate regulatory bodies
paragraph: (7) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations in respect of the criteria to be applied under subsection (4) (b).

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph:
93
		  (1) Subject to section 92 (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation,

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph: (a) specify that 2 or more regulatory bodies are amalgamated into one regulatory body, and

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph: (b) set the date and, if the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it necessary or advisable, the time of the amalgamation.

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph: (2) On amalgamation, the regulatory bodies specified under subsection (1) (a) of this section continue under this Act as one corporation consisting of

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph: (a) the board established under section 23 [board of regulatory body], and

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph: (b) the persons who are registrants of the amalgamated regulatory body.

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph: (4) A notice under subsection (3) must be given to the regulatory body

heading: Amalgamation
paragraph: (b) if the Lieutenant Governor in Council specifies a shorter notice period, within that shorter period.

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph:
94
		  (1) When regulatory bodies are amalgamated under this Division into an amalgamated regulatory body,

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (a) the amalgamated regulatory body may continue to exercise a power or perform a duty that a former body began to exercise or to perform, but did not complete, before the amalgamation date,

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (b) the property, rights and interests of each former body continue to be the property, rights and interests of the amalgamated regulatory body,

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (c) the records and confidential information in the possession of or under the control of a former body as of the amalgamation date are deemed to be the records and confidential information in the possession of or under the control of the amalgamated regulatory body,

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (d) a reference to a former body in any commercial paper, contract, lease, licence, certificate of authorization or other instrument or document is deemed to be a reference to the amalgamated regulatory body,

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (e) the amalgamated regulatory body continues to be liable for the obligations of each former body,

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (f) an existing cause of action, claim or liability to prosecution is unaffected,

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (g) a legal proceeding being prosecuted or pending by or against a former body may be prosecuted, or its prosecution may be continued, by or against the amalgamated regulatory body, and

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (h) a conviction against, or a ruling, order or judgment in favour of or against, a former body may be enforced by or against the amalgamated regulatory body.

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (2) An amalgamation does not constitute an assignment by operation of law, a transfer or any other disposition of the property, rights and interests of a former body to the amalgamated regulatory body.

heading: Property and obligations on amalgamation
paragraph: (3) A person does not contravene section 109 (1) [confidentiality - general] or 110 [confidentiality - committee matters] if the person discloses, to a person exercising powers or performing duties on behalf of an amalgamated regulatory body, matters or things that came to the first person's knowledge while that person was exercising similar powers or performing similar duties on behalf of a former body.

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph:
95
		  (1) When regulatory bodies are amalgamated under this Division into an amalgamated regulatory body, all of the following occur on the amalgamation date:

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (a) the board members for each former body cease to hold office;

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (b) the terms of the members of the first board for the amalgamated regulatory body begin;

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (c) the bylaws of each former body may be replaced by the bylaws for the amalgamated regulatory body;

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (e) subject to section 96 (2) to (4) and a bylaw made under section 96 (5),

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (i)  the officers for each former body cease to hold office, and

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (ii)  the committees for each former body are disestablished;

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (f) the registrar appointed under section 31 [registrar and register for regulatory body] begins to hold office.

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (2) Sections 37 (1) (c) [filing of bylaws] and 38 [disallowance of bylaw] do not apply for the purpose of making the initial bylaws described in subsection (1) (d) of this section but do apply for the purpose of amending or repealing those bylaws after they take effect.

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of providing an orderly transition from former bodies to an amalgamated regulatory body, the superintendent must appoint,

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (a) under section 23 [board of regulatory body], the members of the first board for the amalgamated regulatory body, and

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (b) the first registrar for the amalgamated regulatory body.

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of providing an orderly transition from former bodies to an amalgamated regulatory body,

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (a) the superintendent may, by order, appoint one or more persons to exercise the powers and perform the duties of a board of a former body, and

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (b) subject to any limit or condition set by the superintendent, a person appointed under paragraph (a)

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (i)  has all of the powers, duties, rights and obligations of the board for the former body, to the extent that those powers, duties, rights and obligations relate to the amalgamation, and

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (ii)  may, before the amalgamation date, exercise a power and perform a duty referred to in subparagraph (i).

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (5) On amalgamation of an amalgamated regulatory body under this Division, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation,

heading: Governance on amalgamation
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (6), address transitional matters related to the amalgamated regulatory body in accordance with the transitional regulation-making authority described in section 129 (1) and (2) [transitional regulations].

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph:
96
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), when regulatory bodies are amalgamated under this Division into an amalgamated regulatory body, the officers and committees for the amalgamated regulatory body may exercise any power and perform any duty under this Act that an officer holding the same title with, or a committee having the same mandate of, a former body

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (a) began to exercise or to perform, but did not complete, before the amalgamation date, or

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (b) could have exercised with respect to a discipline matter referred to in Division 3 [Audits, Practice Reviews and Discipline] of Part 6 [Protection of the Public Interest With Respect to Professional Governance and Conduct] that is alleged to have existed or occurred, but was not investigated, before the amalgamation date.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (2) If a discipline committee for a former body, or a committee of the former body with similar duties and powers, commenced a hearing before the amalgamation date, that committee is deemed to be a discipline committee for the amalgamated regulatory body for the purpose of continuing the hearing on and after the amalgamation date.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (3) If an investigation committee for a former body, or a committee of the former body with similar duties and powers, commenced an investigation before the amalgamation date, that committee is deemed to be an investigation committee for the amalgamated regulatory body for the purpose of continuing the investigation on and after the amalgamation date.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (4) If an audit and practice review committee for a former body, or a committee of the former body with similar duties and powers, commenced an assessment before the amalgamation date, that committee is deemed to be an audit and practice review committee for the amalgamated regulatory body for the purpose of continuing the assessment on and after the amalgamation date.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (5) The board of an amalgamated regulatory body may make a bylaw, subject to any limits or conditions the board considers necessary or advisable, authorizing an officer or a committee for a former body to continue to exercise a power or to perform a duty that the officer or the committee began to exercise or to perform, but did not complete, before the amalgamation date.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (6) If a bylaw is made under subsection (5), the authorized officer or committee is deemed to be an officer or a committee for the amalgamated regulatory body for the purpose of continuing to exercise a power or to perform a duty on and after the amalgamation date.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (7) If a bylaw described in subsection (5) takes effect on the amalgamation date,

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (a) the bylaw is deemed to have been made under a bylaw-making authority of the board under this Act, and

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (b) sections 37 (1) (c) [filing of bylaws] and 38 [disallowance of bylaws] do not apply for the purpose of making the bylaw but do apply for the purpose of amending or repealing the bylaw.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (8) If a bylaw described in subsection (5) is made after the amalgamation date, the bylaw is deemed to have been made under the applicable bylaw-making authority of the board under this Act if it is made in accordance with the applicable procedures for the bylaw.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (9) Confidential information may be disclosed by

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (a) an audit and practice review committee for a former body, or by an assessor appointed by that committee or a person acting on that committee's behalf, to the audit and practice review committee or an assessor for the amalgamated regulatory body as follows:

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (i)  for the purpose of carrying out the objectives of the audit or practice review;

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (ii)  to show that the registrant knowingly gave false information to the audit and practice review committee or an assessor for the amalgamated regulatory body, and

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (b) an investigation committee for a former body, or by an inspector appointed by that committee or a person acting on that committee's behalf, to the investigation committee or an inspector for the amalgamated regulatory body for the purpose of carrying out the investigation.

heading: Powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (10) An action taken under Part 6 with respect to an individual by an officer or a committee for a former body is deemed to be the action of an officer holding the same title with, or a committee having the same mandate of, the amalgamated regulatory body.

heading: Registrants and others on amalgamation
paragraph:
97
		  (1) When regulatory bodies are amalgamated under this Division into an amalgamated regulatory body, the persons who are, as of the amalgamation date, registrants or former registrants of each former body are deemed to be registrants or former registrants, as applicable, of the amalgamated regulatory body.

heading: Registrants and others on amalgamation
paragraph: (2) A person who applied, before the amalgamation date, to be a registrant of a former body but whose application has not, as of the amalgamation date, been granted or refused is deemed to have made the application to the amalgamated regulatory body.

heading: Registrants and others on amalgamation
paragraph: (3) Subject to the bylaws of the amalgamated regulatory body, if a bylaw made by a former body established a class or classes of registrants,

heading: Registrants and others on amalgamation
paragraph: (a) a person referred to in subsection (1) continues to be a member of the same class or a comparable class established by the bylaws of the amalgamated regulatory body, and

heading: Registrants and others on amalgamation
paragraph: (b) an applicant under subsection (2) is deemed to have applied to be a member of the same class or a comparable class established by the bylaws of the amalgamated regulatory body, as that stated in the application.

heading: Registrants and others on amalgamation
paragraph: (4) Subject to the bylaws of the amalgamated regulatory body, a limit or condition imposed under this Act before the amalgamation date on a registrant of a former body in respect of the registrant's regulated practice continues to apply until removed or varied in accordance with this Act.

heading: Firms on amalgamation
paragraph:
98
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), when regulatory bodies are amalgamated under this Division into an amalgamated regulatory body, a firm that is validly registered as a registrant by a former body

heading: Firms on amalgamation
paragraph: (a) is deemed to be validly registered by the amalgamated regulatory body, and

heading: Firms on amalgamation
paragraph: (b) continues to be subject to all limits and conditions, if any, provided by the former body.

heading: Firms on amalgamation
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations to provide for prescribed circumstances for the amalgamation, including if the amalgamated regulatory body is not authorized under section 3 [application to firms as registrants] to register firms in the amalgamated regulatory body as registrants, but the firm was validly registered as a registrant by a former body.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
99
		  (1) Subject to and in accordance with the regulations of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the superintendent may impose an administrative penalty on a person other than a regulatory body if the superintendent is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that the person has

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) contravened a prescribed provision of this Act or the regulations, or

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) failed to comply with an order under this Act.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (2) If the superintendent imposes an administrative penalty on a person in respect of a contravention or failure referred to in subsection (1), a prosecution for an offence under this Act in respect of the same contravention or failure may not be brought against the person.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (3) If a firm contravenes this Act or regulations made under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the firm who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure is also liable under this section even though the firm is liable for or pays an administrative penalty.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (4) An administrative penalty imposed under this Division must be paid within the prescribed time.

heading: Effect of charging an offence
paragraph:
100
		  A person who has been charged with an offence under this Act may not be subject to an administrative penalty in respect of the circumstances that gave rise to the charge.

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph:
101
		  (1) The following may be recovered in accordance with subsection (2) as a debt due to the government:

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (a) an administrative penalty imposed under section 99 [administrative penalties];

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (b) an annual fee required to be paid in a regulation made under section 22.1 [annual fee].

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative penalty as required under this Act or if a regulatory body fails to pay an annual fee required to be paid in a regulation made under section 22.1, the superintendent may file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on it, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2)

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (a) must be signed by the superintendent, and

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (b) must contain the following information:

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (i)  the name of the person who is liable for the administrative penalty or of the regulatory body that is liable for the annual fee;

heading: Recovery of penalties and other debts due
paragraph: (ii)  a statement of the amount of the administrative penalty or the annual fee under subsection (1).

heading: Limitation period
paragraph:
102
		  (1) The time limit for giving a notice imposing an administrative penalty is 3 years after the date on which the act or omission alleged to constitute the contravention first came to the attention of the superintendent.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: (2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the superintendent and certifying the date referred to in subsection (1) is proof of that date.

heading: No reprisals
paragraph:
103
		  A person must not evict, discharge, suspend, expel, intimidate, coerce, impose any pecuniary or other penalty on or otherwise retaliate against a registrant because that registrant

heading: No reprisals
paragraph: (a) has reported a matter as described in section 58 [duty to report] with respect to a registrant or other persons,

heading: No reprisals
paragraph: (b) complains or is named in a complaint under section 65 [complaints], or

heading: No reprisals
paragraph: (c) gives evidence or otherwise assists in respect of a prosecution, a complaint or another proceeding under this Act.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph:
104
		  (1) A person must not hinder, obstruct or interfere with, or attempt to hinder, obstruct or interfere with,

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (a) the superintendent exercising the power to conduct an assessment, inspection, investigation or audit under this Act or a person acting under the direction of the superintendent in an assessment, inspection, investigation or audit under this Act, or

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (b) an investigator for a regulatory body acting under section 69 [powers and duties of investigators].

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (2) A person must not provide false information to, or refuse or neglect to provide information to,

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (a) the superintendent exercising the power to conduct an assessment, inspection, investigation or audit under this Act or a person acting under the direction of the superintendent in an assessment, inspection, investigation or audit under this Act, or

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (b) an investigator for a regulatory body acting under section 69.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (3) A person must not withhold, destroy, tamper with, alter, conceal or refuse to produce anything requested for the purposes of an assessment, inspection, investigation or audit under this Act.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (4) A person must not obstruct a person acting under section 70 [search and seizure under court order] or 71 [detention of things seized] or under an order made under those sections.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
106
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) section 52 [prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) section 54 [prohibitions regarding reserved practice];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) section 58 [duty to report];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (e) section 67 [extraordinary action to protect public], in respect of an order made under that section;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (f) section 103 [no reprisals];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (g) section 104 [obstruction];

heading: Offences
paragraph: (1.1) A person who does either of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) provides false or misleading information when applying for enrolment, admission or reinstatement as a registrant of a regulatory body;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) provides false or misleading information when required under this Act to provide information.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (1.2) A person does not commit an offence under subsection (1.1) if, at the time the information was provided, the person did not know that the information was false or misleading and, with the exercise of reasonable diligence, could not have known that the information was false or misleading.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who commits an offence under subsection (1) or (1.1) is liable on conviction,

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) in the case of an individual, to a fine of not more than $200 000 or to a term of imprisonment of not more than 2 years, or both, and

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) in the case of a firm, to a fine of not more than $500 000.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) Section 5 [general offence] of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act, the regulations or any bylaws made under this Act.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (4) In any prosecution under this Act, it is sufficient to prove that the accused has committed a single act of unauthorized practice or has committed on one occasion any of the acts prohibited by this Act.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (5) If an offence under this Act is committed by a firm, each director, manager, secretary or other officer of that firm who assented to the commission of the offence is a party to that offence.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (6) Subject to subsection (7), an information alleging an offence against this Act may be laid

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) by the superintendent on oath or by affirmation, or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) in the name of a board of a regulatory body on oath or by affirmation of the board chair or a person authorized by the board.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (7) The time limit for laying an information, under subsection (6), to commence a prosecution for an offence is

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) 2 years after the date on which the act or omission that is alleged to constitute the offence occurred, or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) if the superintendent or, in respect of a board of a regulatory body, the board chair or person authorized by the board issues a certificate described in subsection (8), 2 years after the date on which the superintendent or the board learned of the act or omission referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Offences
paragraph: (8) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the superintendent or, in respect of a board of a regulatory body, the board chair or person authorized by the board certifying the date referred to in subsection (7) (b) is proof of that date.

heading: Injunction to restrain contravention
paragraph: 107		  (1) The superintendent, the board of a regulatory body or any other person may apply to the Supreme Court for an interim or permanent injunction to restrain a person from contravening a provision of this Act, the regulations or the bylaws.

heading: Injunction to restrain contravention
paragraph: (2) The court may grant an injunction sought under subsection (1) if satisfied there is reason to believe that there has been or will be a contravention of this Act, the regulations or the bylaws.

heading: Injunction to restrain contravention
paragraph: (3) A contravention may be restrained under subsection (1) whether or not a penalty or other remedy has been provided under this Act.

heading: Injunction to restrain contravention
paragraph: (4) The court may grant an interim injunction until the outcome of an action commenced under subsection (1).

heading: Contempt
paragraph:
108
		  On application of the superintendent, the board of a regulatory body or a person interested in the proceeding, the court in which a proceeding is brought may find the person in breach of section 52 [prohibition and limitation - use of reserved titles] or 54 [prohibitions regarding reserved practice] to be in contempt and punish that person accordingly.

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph:
109
		  (1) A person must preserve confidentiality with respect to all matters or things that come to the person's knowledge while exercising a power or performing a duty under this Act unless the disclosure is

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (a) necessary to exercise the power or to perform the duty, or

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (b) authorized as being in the public interest by, as applicable,

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (i)  the superintendent, or

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (ii)  the board of the regulatory body in relation to which the power or duty is exercised or performed.

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (2) Insofar as the laws of British Columbia apply, a person must not give, or be compelled to give, evidence in a court or in proceedings of a judicial nature concerning knowledge gained in the exercise of a power or in the performance of a duty under this Act unless

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (a) the proceedings are under this Act, or

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (b) disclosure of the knowledge is authorized under subsection (1) (b) or under the bylaws or regulations made under this Act.

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (3) Insofar as the laws of British Columbia apply, the records relating to the exercise of a power or the performance of a duty under this Act are not compellable in a court or in proceedings of a judicial nature unless

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (a) the proceedings are under this Act, or

heading: Confidentiality - general
paragraph: (b) disclosure of the knowledge is authorized under subsection (1) (b) or under the bylaws or regulations made under this Act.

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph:
110
		  (1) For the purpose of this section, "audit and practice review committee" includes an assessor appointed by the committee and a person acting on that committee's behalf.

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) to (6), unless it is for the purpose of carrying out a duty under this Act, an audit and practice review committee of a regulatory body must not disclose or provide the following to any other person, including another committee of the regulatory body:

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (a) records or information provided to the audit and practice review committee;

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (b) a self assessment prepared by a registrant for a practice review.

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), an audit and practice review committee may disclose information described in that subsection

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (a) to show that a person knowingly gave false information to the audit and practice review committee, or

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (b) to an appropriate authority for the purpose of reporting a risk of significant harm to the environment or to the health or safety of the public or a group of people.

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (4) If an audit and practice review committee has reasonable grounds to believe that a registrant's conduct constitutes

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (a) professional misconduct,

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (b) conduct unbecoming a registrant, or

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (c) incompetent performance of duties undertaken while engaged in the regulated practice,

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: that committee must, if it considers the action necessary to protect the public, notify the investigation committee, which must treat the matter as if it were a complaint under section 65 [complaints].

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (5) Records, information or a self assessment obtained through a breach of subsection (2) may not be used against a registrant except for the purposes of subsection (3).

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (6) Subject to subsection (3), records, information or a self assessment prepared for the purposes of an audit or practice review in respect of an audit and practice review committee may not be received as evidence

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (a) in a proceeding under this Act, or

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (b) in a civil proceeding.

heading: Confidentiality - committee matters
paragraph: (7) Subsection (2) applies despite the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, other than section 44 (2) or (3) [powers of commissioner in conducting investigations, audits or inquiries] of that Act.

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: 111		  (1) The superintendent, or a person acting on behalf of or under the direction of the superintendent, must not be required to testify or produce evidence in any proceeding about the reasons for which a conclusion was reached or a decision was made in the performance of duties under this Act.

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), the superintendent may be required by the Supreme Court to produce the record of a proceeding that is the subject of an application for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act.

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: (3) The production of government records of a public body may not be compelled under this Act unless

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: (a) the head of the public body consents,

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: (b) the production is a disclosure that is otherwise in accordance with the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act,

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: (c) the court orders, or

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: (d) the regulations of the Lieutenant Governor in Council otherwise allow.

heading: Compulsion protection
paragraph: (4) In subsection (3), "public body" means public body as defined in the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act.

heading: Personal liability protection - general
paragraph: 112		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), no legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against the superintendent, a board member, a regulatory body or a person acting on behalf of or under the direction of the superintendent, a board or a regulatory body because of anything done or omitted

heading: Personal liability protection - general
paragraph: (a) in the performance or intended performance of any duty under this Act, or

heading: Personal liability protection - general
paragraph: (b) in the exercise or intended exercise of any power under this Act.

heading: Personal liability protection - general
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person referred to in that subsection in relation to anything done or omitted by that person in bad faith.

heading: Personal liability protection - general
paragraph: (4) The board of a regulatory body may purchase and maintain insurance

heading: Personal liability protection - general
paragraph: (a) protecting the regulatory body and current and former board members, employees, officers and panel members against liability arising out of the operations or activities of the regulatory body, and

heading: Personal liability protection - general
paragraph: (b) providing for indemnity with respect to any claims arising out of acts done or omitted in good faith by those persons while acting or purporting to act on behalf of the regulatory body.

paragraph:
113
		  (1) No legal proceeding for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against a person for making a claim under this Act about a reprisal as described in section 103 [no reprisals].

heading: Personal liability protection - claims about reprisal
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person referred to in that subsection in relation to a claim made by that person in bad faith.

heading: Certificate as evidence
paragraph:
114
		  A certificate signed by a registrar or board member of a regulatory body is proof, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, of the matters stated in the certificate that relate to the records of the regulatory body.

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph:
115
		  (1) A notice or any document under this Act may be delivered to a person by personal service of a copy of the notice or document or by sending the copy by any of the following means:

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph: (a)  ordinary mail;

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph: (b) electronic transmission, including telephone transmission of a facsimile;

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph: (c) if specified in the superintendent's rules, another method that allows proof of receipt.

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph: (2) If the copy is sent by ordinary mail, it must be sent to the most recent address available of the person to be served and must be considered to be received on the fifth day after the day it is mailed, unless that day is a holiday, in which case the copy must be considered to be received on the next day that is not a holiday.

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph: (3) If the copy is sent by electronic transmission, it must be considered to be received on the day after it was sent, unless that day is a holiday, in which case the copy must be considered to be received on the next day that is not a holiday.

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph: (4) If the copy is sent by a method referred to in subsection (1) (c), the superintendent's rules govern the day on which the copy must be considered to be received.

heading: Service of notice or documents
paragraph: (5) If, through absence, accident, illness or other cause beyond the person's control, a person to be served who acts in good faith does not receive the copy until a later date than the date provided under subsection (2), (3) or (4), that subsection does not apply.

heading: When failure to serve does not invalidate proceeding
paragraph:
116
		  If a notice or document is not served in accordance with section 115, the proceeding is not invalidated if

heading: When failure to serve does not invalidate proceeding
paragraph: (a) the contents of the notice or document were known by the person to be served within the time allowed for service,

heading: When failure to serve does not invalidate proceeding
paragraph: (b) the person to be served consents, or

heading: When failure to serve does not invalidate proceeding
paragraph: (c) the failure to serve does not result in prejudice to the person, or any resulting prejudice can be satisfactorily addressed by an adjournment or other means.

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Act, a reference to "bylaws" in relation to an affected body includes the bylaws, rules or resolutions made under the affected Act by an affected board before the affected body is continued under this Act, unless the context otherwise requires.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 123.1		  In this Division,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) a reference to "board" must be read as including "council" if the provision in which the reference occurs relates to a board that was established as a council under an affected Act, and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) a reference to "board member" must be read as including "councillor" or "council member", as the case may be, if the provision in which the reference occurs relates to a board member who was a councillor or a council member under an affected Act.

heading: Interim elections to board
paragraph:
124
		  Despite any provisions in an affected Act or bylaws made under an affected Act, from the date of the coming into force of this section, each board member under the affected Act may only be elected to a board under the affected Act as follows:

heading: Interim elections to board
paragraph: (a) the board member, as applicable, must be nominated by a committee that, under the affected Act, has the purpose of nominating or selecting members for election;

heading: Interim elections to board
paragraph: (b) the committee must nominate qualified members in accordance with the process and selection principles referred to in section 25 [principles and criteria for board member selection] of this Act and bylaws of the board that are not inconsistent with this section.

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph:
124.1
		  (1) In this section, "affected member" means a person who pays fees for membership in an affected body under an affected Act.

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph: (2) For purposes relating to the administration of an affected body in respect of this Act, an affected board under an affected Act may, if the affected body is prescribed by regulation, make bylaws or pass resolutions to set or increase a fee that is payable by affected members, despite any requirement for ratification or other approval of bylaws or resolutions in respect of fees under the affected Act.

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph: (3) The authority of an affected board to make bylaws or pass resolutions to set or increase a fee under subsection (2) is subject to the following restrictions:

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph: (a) the fee that is payable in respect of a particular year may be either set or increased, but not both, only once;

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph: (b) if the amount of the fee or the rate of its increase is prescribed by regulation, the fee may be set or increased at an amount or rate that is not more than the prescribed amount or rate.

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (3), an affected board that makes bylaws or passes resolutions under this section may

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph: (a) set different fees for different categories or classes of affected members, and

heading: Interim authority - fees for transition to this Act
paragraph: (b) determine whether to set or increase fees if both the amount of the fee and the rate of its increase are prescribed by regulation.

heading: Inconsistent bylaws
paragraph:
125
		  Despite section 84 [specified regulatory bodies continued as regulatory bodies under this Act], if a regulatory body has bylaws made under an affected Act that are not continued due to inconsistency with this Act, the inconsistent bylaws may continue to be applicable for one year after the reference date and the board of the regulatory body must, as applicable, do the following:

heading: Inconsistent bylaws
paragraph: (a) consider any guidelines that may be established by the superintendent to provide guidance for ensuring that the regulatory body makes bylaws that are consistent with this Act;

heading: Inconsistent bylaws
paragraph: (b) comply with any directives of the superintendent made to address transitional matters arising from the inconsistent bylaws that are inconsistent with this Act;

heading: Inconsistent bylaws
paragraph: (c) act in accordance with regulations that may be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council to provide for the following:

heading: Inconsistent bylaws
paragraph: (i)  transitional matters arising from the application of this Act to the inconsistent bylaws;

heading: Inconsistent bylaws
paragraph: (ii)  matters governed by the inconsistent bylaws under the affected Act and, if so, the regulations apply to the matters.

paragraph:
126
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Continued boards and board members

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph:
127
		  (1) The officers and committees for a regulatory body may exercise any power and perform any duty under this Act that an officer holding the same title with, or a committee having the same mandate of, an affected body

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (a) began to exercise or to perform, but did not complete, before the reference date, or

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (b) could have exercised with respect to a discipline matter referred to in Division 3 [Audits, Practice Reviews and Discipline] of Part 6 [Protection of the Public Interest With Respect to Professional Governance and Conduct] that is alleged to have existed or occurred, but was not investigated, before the reference date.

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (2) If a discipline committee for an affected body, or a committee of the former body with similar duties and powers, commenced a hearing before the reference date, that committee is deemed to be a discipline committee for the regulatory body for the purpose of continuing the hearing on and after the reference date.

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (3) If an investigation committee for an affected body, or a committee of the affected body with similar duties and powers, commenced an investigation before the reference date, that committee is deemed to be an investigation committee for the regulatory body for the purpose of continuing the investigation on and after the reference date.

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (4) If an audit and practice review committee for an affected body, or a committee of the affected body with similar duties and powers, commenced an audit or a practice review, or an assessment, before the reference date, that committee is deemed to be an audit and practice review committee for the regulatory body for the purpose of continuing the audit or the practice review, or the assessment, on and after the reference date.

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (5) The board of a regulatory body may make a bylaw, in accordance with this Act and subject to any limits or conditions prescribed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council or that the board considers necessary or advisable, authorizing an officer or a committee for an affected body to continue to exercise a power or to perform a duty that the officer or the committee began to exercise or to perform, but did not complete, before the reference date.

heading: Transition - powers and duties in progress
paragraph: (6) If a bylaw is made under subsection (5), the authorized officer or committee is deemed to be an officer or a committee for the regulatory body for the purpose of continuing to exercise a power or to perform a duty on and after the reference date.

heading: Transitional regulations
paragraph:
129

paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for meeting or removing any difficulty arising out of the transition to this Act from the affected Acts, and for that purpose disapplying or varying any provision of this Act.
