heading: Application
paragraph: 1 Subject to sections 2 and 3, these Regulations apply to toxic substances that are both specified in the List of Toxic Substances in Schedule 1 to the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 and set out in either Schedule 1 or 2 to these Regulations.

heading: Non-application - substance
paragraph: 2 These Regulations do not apply to any toxic substance that

heading: Non-application - substance
paragraph: (a) is contained in a hazardous waste, hazardous recyclable material or non-hazardous waste to which Division 8 of Part 7 of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 applies;

heading: Non-application - substance
paragraph: (b) is contained in a pest control product as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Pest Control Products Act; or

heading: Non-application - substance
paragraph: (c) is present as a contaminant in a chemical feedstock that is used in a process from which there are no releases of the toxic substance and on the condition that the toxic substance is destroyed or completely converted in that process to a substance that is not a toxic substance set out in either Schedule 1 or 2.

heading: Non-application - use
paragraph: 3 (1) These Regulations, except for subsections (2) and (3), do not apply to any toxic substance or to any product containing it that is to be used in a laboratory for analysis, in scientific research or as a laboratory analytical standard.

heading: Information to Minister - more than 10 g
paragraph: (2) Every person must submit to the Minister in any calendar year the information set out in Schedule 3 for each toxic substance or a product containing it that they intend to use for a purpose referred to in subsection (1) as soon as feasible before the use of more than 10 g of the substance, by itself or in a product, in that calendar year. The information must be submitted only once in a calendar year in respect of each substance or product.

heading: Added substance - Schedule 2.1
paragraph: (3) Any person that is using a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Schedule 2.1 or a product containing it on the date set out in column 2 in respect of that substance, for a purpose referred to in subsection (1), must, if the quantity of the toxic substance used, by itself or in a product, exceeded 10 g in the calendar year in which that day occurs, submit to the Minister, within 60 days after that day, the information referred to in Schedule 3. The information must be submitted only once in a calendar year in respect of each substance or product.

heading: Toxic substance - Schedule 1
paragraph: 4 (1) Subject to sections 5 and 9, a person must not manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale or import a toxic substance set out in Schedule 1 or a product containing it unless the toxic substance is incidentally present.

heading: Non application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a product that is a manufactured item that is formed into a specific physical shape or design during its manufacture and that has, for its final use, a function or functions dependent in whole or in part on its shape or design, if a toxic substance set out in Part 2 of Schedule 1 is present in that product.

heading: Non-application - certain products
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to products other than those set out in column 2 of Part 3 of Schedule 1 that contain the toxic substance set out in column 1 of that Part.

heading: Exception - inventory of substance
paragraph: 4.1 (1) A person may use, sell or offer for sale a toxic substance set out in item 13 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 that was manufactured or imported before January 1, 2017.

heading: Exception - inventory of products
paragraph: (2) A person may use, sell, or offer for sale any product set out in column 2 of Part 3 of Schedule 1 that contains a toxic substance set out in item 13 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 if the product was manufactured or imported before January 1, 2017.

heading: Exception - manufactured or imported before March 14, 2013
paragraph: 5 (1) A person may use, sell or offer for sale a product containing a toxic substance set out in item 11 or 12 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 if the product was manufactured or imported before March 14, 2013.

heading: Exception - manufactured or imported before coming into force of subsection
paragraph: (2) A person may use, sell or offer for sale a product containing the toxic substance set out in item 5 of Part 2 of Schedule 1, with the molecular formula C12H(10-n)BrnO in which n=10, if the product was manufactured or imported before the day on which this subsection comes into force.

heading: Toxic substance - Schedule 2
paragraph: 6 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (2.5) and sections 7 and 9, a person must not manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale or import a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 1, 1.1, 1.2, 2, 3 or 3.1 of Schedule 2 or a product containing it unless the toxic substance is incidentally present.

heading: Permitted activities - Schedule 2
paragraph: (2) The prohibition to manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale or import a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 1, 2 or 3 of Schedule 2 or a product containing it does not apply if

heading: Permitted activities - Schedule 2
paragraph: (a) the toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 1 of Schedule 2 or the product containing it is designed for a use set out in column 2 in respect of that substance;

heading: Permitted activities - Schedule 2
paragraph: (b) the toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 2 of Schedule 2 or a product containing it is designed for a use set out in column 2 and that activity occurs before the date set out in column 3; or

heading: Permitted activities - Schedule 2
paragraph: (c) a product set out in column 2 of Part 3 of Schedule 2 contains the toxic substance set out in column 1 in a concentration less than or equal to that set out in column 3, including any incidental presence of the substance.

heading: Permitted use and import - Part 1.1 of Schedule 2
paragraph: (2.1) The prohibition to use or import a product containing a toxic substance set out in column 1 of item 1 of Part 1.1 of Schedule 2 does not apply to a product set out in column 2 of that item that contains that substance.

heading: Permitted activities - Part 1.1 of Schedule 2
paragraph: (2.2) The prohibition to use, sell, offer for sale or import a product containing a toxic substance set out in column 1 of any of items 2 to 5 of Part 1.1 of Schedule 2 does not apply to a product set out in column 2 of those items that contains that substance.

heading: Permitted use - Part 1.2 of Schedule 2
paragraph: (2.3) The prohibition to use a product containing a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 1.2 of Schedule 2 does not apply to a product set out in column 2 that contains that substance.

heading: Non-application - manufactured items
paragraph: (2.4) The prohibition to use, sell, offer for sale or import a product containing a toxic substance set out in column 1 of any of items 2 to 5 of Part 2 of Schedule 2 does not apply to a product that is a manufactured item that is formed into a specific physical shape or design during its manufacture and that has, for its final use, a function or functions dependent in whole or in part on its shape or design.

heading: Permitted use - Part 3.1 of Schedule 2
paragraph: (2.5) The prohibition to use a product containing a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 3.1 of Schedule 2 does not apply to a product set out in column 2 that contains the substance in a concentration less than or equal to that set out in column 3, including any incidental presence of the substance.

heading: Exception - incidental presence
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, the exception of the incidental presence referred to in subsection (1) does not apply in the case of a product described in paragraph (2)(c).

heading: Exception - personal use
paragraph: (4) Subsection (1) does not apply to the use or import of a product containing a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 2 of Schedule 2 if the product is used or intended to be used for a personal use.

heading: Exception - temporary permitted uses
paragraph: 7 (1) A person may use, sell, or offer for sale a product set out in column 2 of Part 2 of Schedule 2 containing a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 2 of Schedule 2 if the product is manufactured or imported before the expiry date set out in column 3 of Schedule 2.

heading: Exception - products
paragraph: (2) A person may use, sell or offer for sale a product

heading: Exception - products
paragraph: (a) containing a toxic substance that is set out in any of items 2 to 5 of Part 2 of Schedule 2, if the product was manufactured or imported before the coming into force of this subsection; or

heading: Exception - products
paragraph: (b) containing a toxic substance that is set out in item 2 of Part 3 of Schedule 2, if the product was manufactured or imported before March 14, 2013.

heading: Exception - manufactured items
paragraph: (3) A person may use, sell or offer for sale a product that was manufactured or imported before May 29, 2008 and that contains the toxic substance set out in item 1 of Part 3.1 of Schedule 2 if the product is a manufactured item that was formed into a specific physical shape or design during its manufacture and that has, for its final use, a function or functions dependent in whole or in part on its shape or design.

heading: Exception - manufacture or import under permit
paragraph: 8 A person may use, sell or offer for sale a toxic substance or a product containing it, if the substance or the product is manufactured or imported in accordance with a permit that is issued under section 10.

heading: Requirement for permit
paragraph: 9 (1) Any person that, on March 14, 2013, is a manufacturer or importer of a toxic substance or a product containing it that is prohibited under section 4 or 6 may continue to manufacture or import the substance or product if they have been issued a permit under section 10.

heading: Addition of substance
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), in the case of a toxic substance that, after March 14, 2013, is either added to Schedule 1 and prohibited under section 4 - other than the toxic substance set out in item 13 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 - or added to Schedule 2 and prohibited under section 6, any person that is a manufacturer or importer of the toxic substance or a product containing it on the date set out in column 2 of Schedule 2.1 in respect of that substance may continue to manufacture or import the substance or a product containing it if they have been issued a permit under section 10.

heading: Temporary permitted uses
paragraph: (3) Any person that, under paragraph 6(2)(b), manufactures or imports a toxic substance that is set out in Part 2 of Schedule 2 or a product containing it on the date set out in column 3 in respect of that substance may continue that activity if they have been issued a permit under section 10.

heading: Required information
paragraph: (4) An application for a permit must be submitted to the Minister and contain the information referred to in Schedule 4.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 10 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Minister must issue the permit if the following conditions are met:

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (a) there is no technically or economically feasible alternative or substitute available to the applicant at the time of the application, other than a substance regulated under these Regulations, for the toxic substance;

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (b) the applicant has taken the necessary measures to minimize or eliminate any harmful effect of the toxic substance on the environment and human health; and

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (c) a plan has been prepared respecting the toxic substance identifying the measures that will be taken by the applicant to comply with these Regulations, and the period within which the plan is to be implemented does not exceed three years after the day on which a permit is first issued to the applicant.

heading: Grounds for refusing permit
paragraph: (2) The Minister must refuse to issue a permit if

heading: Grounds for refusing permit
paragraph: (a) the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the applicant has provided false or misleading information in support of their application; or

heading: Grounds for refusing permit
paragraph: (b) information required under subsection 9(4) has not been provided or is insufficient to enable the Minister to process the application.

heading: Expiry and permit renewal
paragraph: (3) A permit expires 12 months after the day on which it is issued unless, at least 30 days before the day on which the permit expires, the applicant submits an application for renewal to the Minister that contains the information referred to in Schedule 4.

heading: Limits on renewal
paragraph: (4) A permit may only be renewed twice and subsections (1) and (2) apply to any renewal.

heading: Revocation
paragraph: 11 (1) The Minister must revoke a permit if the conditions set out in paragraphs 10(1)(a) to (c) are no longer met or if the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the permit holder has provided false or misleading information to the Minister.

heading: Conditions for revocation
paragraph: (2) The Minister must not revoke a permit unless the Minister has provided the permit holder with

heading: Conditions for revocation
paragraph: (a) written reasons for the revocation; and

heading: Conditions for revocation
paragraph: (b) an opportunity to be heard, by written representation, in respect of the revocation.

heading: Certain substances
paragraph: 12 Every person that manufactures or imports a toxic substance set out in column 1 of Part 4 of Schedule 2 or a product containing it, whether incidentally or not, must submit to the Minister a report that contains the information referred to in Schedule 5 by March 31 following the end of the calendar year during which either the toxic substance or a product containing it was manufactured or imported if, in that year

heading: Certain substances
paragraph: (a) the total annual quantity of the toxic substance manufactured or imported was equal to or greater than that set out in column 2, if any;

heading: Certain substances
paragraph: (b) the product imported contained the toxic substance in an annual weighted average concentration equal to or greater than that set out in column 3, if any; or

heading: Certain substances
paragraph: (c) the total annual quantity of the toxic substance contained in a product manufactured or imported and its annual weighted average concentration in the product were equal to or greater than those set out in column 4, if any.

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: 13 (1) Any analysis performed to determine the concentration of a toxic substance for the purposes of these Regulations must be performed by a laboratory that meets the following conditions at the time of the analysis:

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (a) it is accredited

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (i) under the International Organization for Standardization standard ISO/IEC 17025, entitled General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories, by an accrediting body that is a signatory to the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation Mutual Recognition Arrangement, or

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (ii) under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR, c. Q-2; and

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (2), the scope of its accreditation includes the analysis performed to determine the concentration of the toxic substance.

heading: Standards of good practice
paragraph: (2) If no method has been recognized by a standards development organization in respect of the analysis performed to determine the concentration of the toxic substance and the scope of the laboratory's accreditation does not therefore include that analysis, the analysis must be performed in accordance with standards of good scientific practice that are generally accepted at the time that it is performed.

heading: Certification
paragraph: 14 (1) Any information or an application for a permit required to be submitted to the Minister under these Regulations must bear the signature of the interested person or their authorized representative and be accompanied by a certification dated and signed by the interested person or the person authorized to act on their behalf, stating that the information is accurate and complete.

heading: Writing or electronic format
paragraph: (2) The information, application for a permit and certification may be submitted either in writing or in an electronic format that is compatible with the one that is used by the Minister.

heading: Records
paragraph: 15 (1) Every person that submits information to the Minister under these Regulations must keep a record containing a copy of that information, a copy of the certification and any documents supporting the information, including test data if applicable, for a period of at least five years beginning on the date of the submission of the information.

heading: Location
paragraph: (2) The records must be kept at the person's principal place of business in Canada or, on notification to the Minister, at any other place in Canada where the records can be inspected.

heading: Records moved
paragraph: (3) If the records are moved, the person must notify the Minister, in writing, of the civic address of the new location within 30 days after the day of the move.

heading: Activities prohibited under repealed regulations

heading: Three months after registration

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "special use permit" means a permit issued under section 9.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) Unless the context indicates otherwise, words and expressions not defined in this regulation have the meaning given to them in the Forest and Range Practices Act.

heading: Grandparented authorization under the Land Act or other enactments
paragraph: 2		  (1) In addition to the purposes set out in section 2 of the Act or under this regulation, Crown land in a Provincial forest, described in an agreement under the Range Act or described in a woodlot licence may be managed or used for any purpose authorized in an instrument granted or issued under the Land Act or any other enactment before the date this section comes into force.

heading: Grandparented authorization under the Land Act or other enactments
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), Crown land in a Provincial forest, described in an agreement under the Range Act or described in a woodlot licence may be managed or used for any purpose authorized in an instrument referred to in that subsection that is renewed or replaced before or after the date this section comes into force.

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: 3		  Crown land in a Provincial forest may be managed or used for any of the following purposes if carried out by the government or authorized in an instrument granted or issued under the Land Act:

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (a) agriculture;

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (b) if access to existing residences is not practicable, temporary residences for workers, including

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (i)  camps, and

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (ii)  individual residences;

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (c) sand pits, gravel pits, rock quarries and other quarries that provide materials for industrial, commercial or domestic use;

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (d) commercial recreation uses and facilities and ancillary improvements, including

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (i)  ski facilities,

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (ii)  hunting lodges,

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (iii)  fishing lodges, and

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (iv)  trails;

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (e) temporary commercial purposes;

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (f) navigational aids;

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (g) construction and maintenance of a road, including construction and maintenance of bridges and other drainage structures;

heading: Primary uses authorized under the Land Act
paragraph: (h) a utilities right-of-way, including

paragraph: (c) a drill site, well site, processing site, hydrocarbon collection system, core sampling site or other purpose including facilities and other improvements, that is ancillary to a use or occupation referred to in section 2 (4) of the Act;

paragraph: (d) any use of adjoining upland that is ancillary to the use of land covered by water authorized under the Land Act, including

paragraph: 5		  Crown land in a Provincial forest, described in an agreement under the Range Act or described in a woodlot licence may be managed or used for a purpose authorized under the Wildlife Act, and any ancillary purpose, including a trapline cabin, if carried out by the government or authorized in an instrument granted or issued under the Wildlife Act.

heading: Uses authorized under other enactments
paragraph: 6		  The following Crown land may be managed or used for the purposes provided for in the Coal Act, the Geothermal Resources Act, the Mineral Tenure Act and the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act:

paragraph: (a) subject to section 7 (2), Crown land in a Provincial forest or wilderness area;

paragraph: (b) Crown land described in an agreement under the Range Act or described in a woodlot licence.

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: 7		  (1) In addition to the purposes set out in section 2 of the Act and in this regulation, Crown land in a Provincial forest, Crown land described in an area-based licence as defined in section 1 (1) of the Forest Act or Crown range as defined in section 1 (1) of the Range Act may be managed or used for any of the purposes described in subsection (1.1) of this section if the purpose is

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (a) carried out by the government or authorized in a special use permit, and

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (b) ancillary to activities authorized under a licence, agreement, permit or authorization issued under an enactment other than the Land Act.

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (1.1) Crown land, or Crown range, described in subsection (1) may be managed or used in accordance with that subsection for the following purposes:

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (a) construction and maintenance of a road, including construction and maintenance of bridges and other drainage structures, for the following:

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (i)  a natural resource development purpose as defined in section 21.1 (1) of the Forest and Range Practices Act;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (ii)  the purposes of a permit issued under section 10 of the Mines Act;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (iii)  access to Crown land in respect of which another special use permit has been issued to the holder of the special use permit;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (b) sand pits, gravel pits, rock quarries and other quarries that provide materials for road construction, modification or maintenance authorized under the Forest Act or by a special use permit;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (c) a communications site to be used by the holder of an authorization under any of the following enactments:

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (i)  the Forest Act;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (ii)  the Range Act;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (iii)  the Mineral Tenure Act;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (iv)  the Coal Act;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (d) a short-term logging camp and associated facilities, including a waste disposal site;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (e) a log dump, or a dry land sort, above the natural boundary, as defined in section 1 of the Land Act, of a stream, as defined in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (f) disposal of organic debris from a remote log dump or dry land sort;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (g) a short-term timber processing site;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (h) a lookout;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (i) a weather station;

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (j) an airstrip, helipad or other air transportation landing site to be used by the holder of

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit

heading: Uses of a Provincial forest authorized by a special use permit
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), a holder of a woodlot licence is not required to have a special use permit to locate a temporary timber processing facility on Crown land described in a woodlot licence, if the use of the temporary processing facility is permitted under the woodlot licence.

heading: Application for special use permit
paragraph: 8		  A person may apply in writing to the district manager for a special use permit if the person

heading: Application for special use permit
paragraph: (a) wishes to use or manage either of the following:

heading: Application for special use permit
paragraph: (i)  for a purpose referred to in section 7 (1.1) or (1.2), a portion of Crown land, or Crown range, described in section 7 (1);

heading: Application for special use permit
paragraph: (ii)  for a purpose referred to in section 7 (2), a portion of Crown land in a Provincial forest or wilderness area, and

heading: Application for special use permit
paragraph: (b) has not been authorized under another enactment to use or manage the portion of Crown land in a manner described in paragraph (a).

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the district manager may issue a special use permit if

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (a) the applicant

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (i)  has applied in accordance with section 8, and

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (ii)  submitted a plan that sets out how the land will be used, and

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (b) the district manager is of the opinion that

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (i)  the issuance of the special use permit would not impair the proper management and conservation of forest resources on Crown land, and

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (ii)  any activity under the special use permit will not impair the ability of any affected holder of an agreement under the Forest Act or Range Act to exercise its rights or fulfill its obligations under the agreement.

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (2) The district manager may issue the special use permit subject to

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (a) a condition that the holder of the permit carry out the activity in accordance with the plan submitted under subsection (1),

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (b) any conditions the district manager determines necessary to conserve forest resources and the natural environment, including a condition

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (i)  restricting, regulating and prohibiting the building of or disposal of any chattel or fixture, and

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (ii)  requiring the clean up and restoration of the land under the permit to the satisfaction of the district manager on the expiry of the special use permit, and

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (c) a condition that the holder provide, in an amount specified in the permit, a deposit in the form of money or other securities acceptable to the district manager

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (i)  to ensure the conditions of the permit are met, or

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (ii)  if personal property owned by a person other than the holder or the government is situated on the land under the permit.

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (2.01) The holder of a special use permit must comply with the conditions of the permit, if any.

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (2.1) In issuing a special use permit, the district manager must specify its term, which must not exceed the following:

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (a) 4 years, if the special use permit is issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g);

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (b) 5 years, if the special use permit is issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (e), (f), (i), (j) (i) or (k) or (1.2) (b) or (c);

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (c) 10 years, if the special use permit is issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (a), (b), (c), (h) or (j) (ii) or (1.2) (a).

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (3) The district manager may use any or all of the deposit referred to in subsection (2) (c)

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (a) to satisfy a claim made by the owner of the personal property referred to in subsection (2) (c) (ii),

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (b) to cover the costs resulting from a failure of the holder to meet the conditions of the permit or

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (c) to cover the costs resulting from a failure of the holder to comply with an order under section 15 (1) (a) or (b).

heading: Issuance of special use permit
paragraph: (4) No later than 12 months after the date the special use permit expires or is cancelled, the remainder of the deposit must be returned to the holder of the permit.

paragraph: (2) The holder of a special use permit must pay the annual charge described in subsection (1) no later than,

heading: Annual charge
paragraph: (a) for the first year of the special use permit, 60 days after the date the permit is issued, and

heading: Annual charge
paragraph: (b) for all subsequent years, 60 days after the date an invoice is issued for the annual charge.

heading: Assignment prohibited
paragraph: 10		  A holder of a special use permit must not assign the special use permit to another person without the consent of the district manager.

heading: No exclusive rights to the use of the land
paragraph:
11
		  Rights granted under a special use permit are not exclusive and do not prevent the government from using the land or authorizing others to use the land in accordance with the Act or this regulation.

heading: Permit extension
paragraph:
12
		  (1) On application by the holder no less than 6 months before the expiry of a special use permit, the district manager may grant an extension of the term of the permit specified under section 9 (2.1) if the district manager is satisfied of all of the following:

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (a) the holder continues to hold a licence, agreement, permit or authorization to which the special use permit relates;

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (b) the holder has begun to exercise the rights granted under the special use permit;

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (c) the holder has performed the conditions of the special use permit;

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (d) the holder has paid all deposits and charges in relation to the special use permit;

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (e) the special use permit is not suspended at the time of application;

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (f) the conditions set out in section 9 (2) (b) will continue to be met;

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (g) the application demonstrates that an extension is necessary.

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (2) An extension under subsection (1)

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (a) may be granted once for a term not exceeding 2 years if the special use permit was issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g),

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (b) may be granted twice for terms not exceeding 5 years each if the special use permit was issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (e), (f), (i), (j) (i) or (k) or (1.2) (b) or (c), and

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (c) may be granted for terms not exceeding 10 years each if the special use permit was issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (a), (b) (c), (h) or (j)  (ii) or (1.2) (a).

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (3) If the maximum number of extensions described in subsection (2) (a) or (b) has been granted, the district manager may issue a replacement special use permit if the district manager is satisfied that the Crown land may not be managed or used under a tenure under the Land Act for the purpose authorized in the special use permit.

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (4) When granting an extension under subsection (1), the district manager may do one or both of the following:

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (a) require that the holder submit an updated plan described in section 9 (1) (a) (ii);

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (b) amend any of the conditions described in section 9 (2).

heading: Permit extension
paragraph: (5) If the district manager does not make a decision under subsection (1) before the expiry of the special use permit, the holder may continue to manage or use Crown land under the permit until a decision is made.

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: 13		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), sections 76, 76.1 and 77 of the Forest Act, except section 77 (5), apply to the cancellation or suspension of a special use permit under this section.

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (1.1) The district manager may suspend or cancel a special use permit if any of the following applies:

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (a) the holder of the special use permit

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (i)  has failed to provide a deposit described in section 9 (2) (c) or to pay the annual charge under section 9.1 by the required date, and

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (ii)  the deposit or annual charge has been in arrears for more than 6 months;

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (b) the holder of the special use permit has failed to comply with an order under section 15 (1);

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (c) 2 years after the date the permit is issued, the holder of the special use permit has not begun to exercise the rights granted under the special use permit;

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (d) the district manager

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (i)  has, for more than 6 months, not been able to locate or contact the holder of the special use permit, or

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (ii)  is satisfied that the holder of the special use permit no longer exists;

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (e) the district manager is satisfied that the holder of the special use permit is insolvent because the holder

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (i)  has filed for protection under the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act (Canada), or

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (ii)  is a bankrupt or insolvent person under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada).

heading: Cancellation and suspension
paragraph: (2) The district manager may cancel a special use permit without notice and without suspending the permit prior to cancellation if the holder contravenes section 10.

heading: Holder's obligations on permit expiry, surrender, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: 14		  On the expiry, surrender, suspension or cancellation of a special use permit, the holder or former holder of the special use permit must do all of the following:

heading: Holder's obligations on permit expiry, surrender, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (a) pay any outstanding charge or deposit the holder owes the government in respect of the special use permit;

heading: Holder's obligations on permit expiry, surrender, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (b) fulfill any outstanding obligation of the holder or former holder under the special use permit;

heading: Holder's obligations on permit expiry, surrender, suspension or cancellation
paragraph: (c) fulfill any outstanding obligation of the holder or former holder under the Act, the Forest and Range Practices Act, the Wildfire Act or any other enactment, in respect of any of the holder's activities under the special use permit.

heading: Deactivation and remediation orders
paragraph: 15		  (1) The minister may, by order, require the holder or former holder of a special use permit, including a special use permit that has expired or is surrendered, suspended or cancelled, to do one or both of the following:

heading: Deactivation and remediation orders
paragraph: (a) deactivate a road authorized in the special use permit;

heading: Deactivation and remediation orders
paragraph: (b) remediate the land that is the subject of the special use permit.

heading: Deactivation and remediation orders
paragraph: (2) An order under this section must include the following:

heading: Deactivation and remediation orders
paragraph: (a) a description of the location of the road to be deactivated or of the land to be remediated;

heading: Deactivation and remediation orders
paragraph: (b) the date by which the deactivation or remediation must be completed.

heading: Deactivation and remediation orders
paragraph: (3) A holder or former holder of a special use permit who receives an order under this section must comply with the order.

heading: Entry on Crown land
paragraph:
16
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the holder or former holder of a special use permit may enter onto Crown land for the purpose of fulfilling any of the obligations described in section 14 (b) and (c) or complying with an order under section 15 (1).

heading: Entry on Crown land
paragraph: (2) The district manager may impose on the holder or former holder of a special use permit who enters onto Crown land for a purpose described in subsection (1) any condition that the minister considers necessary or desirable.

heading: Entry on Crown land
paragraph: (3) A holder or former holder of a special use permit must comply with any conditions imposed by the minister under subsection (2).

heading: Existing special use permits
paragraph:
17
		  Sections 9.1, 9.2, 13 (1.1) and 14 to 16 apply to a special use permit issued before the date this Part comes into force.

heading: Transition - annual charge
paragraph:
18
		  The annual charge for a special use permit issued before the date this Part comes into force is, during the first year after the date this Part comes into force, the greater of

heading: Transition - annual charge
paragraph: (a) half of the annual charge determined in accordance with section 9.2 (3) (b), and

heading: Transition - annual charge
paragraph: (b) whichever of the following that applies:

heading: Transition - annual charge
paragraph: (i)  for a special use permit issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g) or (k), $675;

heading: Transition - annual charge
paragraph: (ii)  for a special use permit issued for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (h), (i) or (j), $500.

heading: Transition - replacement permit
paragraph:
19
		  (1) On the expiry of a special use permit issued before the date this Part comes into force for any purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) or (1.2), except a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g), the district manager may issue a replacement permit under section 12, as it read immediately before the date this Part comes into force, if, in addition to the matters set out in section 12, the district manager is satisfied of all of the following:

heading: Transition - replacement permit
paragraph: (a) the holder continues to hold a licence, agreement, permit or authorization to which the special use permit relates;

heading: Transition - replacement permit
paragraph: (b) the holder has begun to exercise the rights granted under the special use permit;

heading: Transition - replacement permit
paragraph: (c) the holder has paid all deposits and charges in relation to the special use permit;

heading: Transition - replacement permit
paragraph: (d) the special use permit is not suspended at the time of application;

heading: Transition - replacement permit
paragraph: (e) the holder has demonstrated that a replacement permit is necessary.

heading: Transition - replacement permit
paragraph: (2) The district manager may issue only one replacement permit for each special use permit.

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph:
20
		  (1) This section applies to a special use permit issued before the coming into force of this Part

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (a) for a purpose set out in section 7 (1.1) (d) or (g),

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (b) for a purpose other than a purpose set out in section 7, or

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (c) to a person who does not hold a licence, agreement, permit or authorization to which the special use permit relates.

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (2) A special use permit that expires before the date that is one year after the date this Part comes into force is extended for a term of one year from the date the special use permit expires.

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (3) If, before the expiry of the term referred to in subsection (2), the permit holder submits to the district manager proof of the holder's application for a licence, agreement, permit or authorization that would authorize the purpose for the special use permit, the district manager may grant an extension of the term of the special use permit

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (a) for up to 2 years, or

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (b) for up to 4 years if the district manager is satisfied that special circumstances exist.

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (4) If, before the expiry of a special use permit, the permit holder submits to the district manager proof of the holder's application, made no less than 6 months before the expiry of the special use permit, for tenure under another enactment that would authorize the purpose for the special use permit, the district manager may grant an extension of the term of the special use permit

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (a) for up to 2 years, or

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (b) for up to 4 years if the district manager is satisfied that special circumstances exist.

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (5) An extension granted under subsection (3) or (4) must include a condition that the permit holder notify the district manager of the decision made on the application for tenure under another enactment as soon as practicable after the permit holder is notified of the decision.

heading: Transition - permit extension
paragraph: (6) Once the district manager receives notification under subsection (5) that tenure has been granted to the permit holder, the district manager may cancel the special use permit whose term was extended under this section.

paragraph: effluent means

paragraph: (b) waste water from a mill, other than waste water from the treatment of intake water, including process water, gas scrubbing water, boiler blow-down water, wash-down water, cooling water, leachate from any site at the mill where solid residues generated by any mill are treated or disposed of, and leachate from any site at the mill where wood chips or hogfuel are stored; (effluent)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: finished product means pulp or a paper product that has completed the production process at a mill; (produit fini)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: mill means

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) a factory that is designed or used to produce pulp or paper products, or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) if a complex consists of factories that are owned by different owners and that are designed or used to produce pulp or paper products, all of those factories that discharge some or all of their effluent into a common treatment facility that is owned by one of those owners,

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: and includes any facility that is owned or operated by the owner of any of the factories referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) and that treats effluent; (fabrique)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: operator means the person who operates, has control or custody of or is in charge of a mill; (exploitant)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: outfall structure means a conduit or other structure through which effluent is conveyed from a mill to a location where it is deposited in water frequented by fish, or in any place from which it may enter such water, or a conduit or other structure through which effluent is conveyed from a mill to a wastewater system; (emissaire d'effluent)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: paper product means paper, coated paper, paperboard, hardboard, boxboard, linerboard, insulating board, building board, corrugating medium, tissue, moulded cellulose product and any other product directly derived from pulp, but does not include viscose, rayon, cellophane or any other cellulose derivative, or medium density fiberboard as defined in American National Standards Institute (ANSI) Standard A208.2-2002, published on May 13, 2002; (produit de papier)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Port Alberni Mill means the mill located in Port Alberni, British Columbia, that is owned by Norske Skog Canada Limited, its successors or assigns; (fabrique de Port Alberni)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: pulp means processed cellulose fibres that are derived from wood, other plant material or recycled paper products; (pate)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition means Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Effluents to Rainbow Trout (EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition), December 2000, published by the federal Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time; (methode de reference SPE 1/RM/13 Deuxieme edition)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition means Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Effluents to Daphnia magna (EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition), December 2000, published by the federal Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time; (methode de reference SPE 1/RM/14 Deuxieme edition)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: reference production rate means the daily production of finished product of a mill as determined under section 12; (rythme de production de reference)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: suspended solids means any solid matter that is present in effluent; (matieres en suspension)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: suspended solids test means the test to determine the presence and quantity of suspended solids in effluent referred to in section 4 of Schedule I; (essai de determination des matieres en suspension)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: treat, in respect of effluent, means to subject the effluent to physical, chemical or biological action, other than dilution, in order to reduce or eliminate deleterious substances; (traiter)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: wastewater system has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations. (systeme d'assainissement)

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: 3 For the purpose of the definition deleterious substance in subsection 34(1) of the Act, the following classes of substances from a mill are prescribed as deleterious substances:

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (a) acutely lethal effluent;

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (b) BOD matter; and

heading: Prescribed Deleterious Substances
paragraph: (c) suspended solids.

heading: Ministerial Orders
paragraph: 4 For the purpose of subsection 37(2) of the Act and in respect of mills, the Minister or a person designated by the Minister may issue an order under that subsection if the Minister or the person has reasonable grounds to believe that an offence under subsection 40(1) or (2) of the Act is being or is likely to be committed.

heading: Application
paragraph: 5 (1) This Part applies in respect of all mills except the Port Alberni Mill.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: 6 (1) For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of a mill may deposit, or permit the deposit of, BOD matter and suspended solids in any water or place other than a place referred to in subsection (3) or (4) if

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) the BOD of the BOD matter or the quantity of suspended solids, as the case may be, does not exceed the maximum quantities authorized by section 14; or

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) the deposit is made in accordance with an authorization to exceed the maximum quantities authorized by section 14.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of a mill may deposit, or permit the deposit of, any concentration of acutely lethal effluent, any BOD matter and any quantity of suspended solids into a wastewater system that is regulated by the Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of a factory that produces pulp or paper products may deposit, or permit the deposit of, any concentration of acutely lethal effluent, any BOD matter and any quantity of suspended solids into

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) a treatment facility that is owned or operated by the owner of the factory; or

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) if the factory is part of a complex, the common treatment facility for the factories that are part of the complex.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (5) The authority to deposit BOD matter and suspended solids conferred by subsections (1) and (2) does not confer any authority to deposit acutely lethal effluent.

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: 7 (1) The authority of the owner or operator of a mill under subsection 6(1) is conditional on the operator

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) installing, maintaining and calibrating monitoring equipment, and keeping records of that equipment, in accordance with section 8;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) monitoring effluent in accordance with Schedule II and submitting to the authorization officer a monthly report of the monitoring results and production information in accordance with subsections 9(1) and (3);

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (c) notifying an inspector, without delay, of any result of a test conducted in accordance with Schedule II and of any result of any additional test that was conducted on samples collected in accordance with the procedures specified in that Schedule, other than in the case of a deposit out of the normal course of events, that indicates a failure or non-compliance with these Regulations and reporting the test results in writing to the inspector within 10 days after the notification;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (d) submitting the identifying information to the authorization officer in accordance with subsections 10(1), (2) and (3);

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (e) preparing and updating annually a remedial plan describing the measures to be taken by the operator to eliminate all unauthorized deposits of deleterious substances in the case where effluent fails an acute lethality test conducted in accordance with Schedule II;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (f) preparing an emergency response plan in accordance with section 11 and making it readily available on site to persons who are to implement the plan;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (g) in the case of a mill, providing the authorization officer, in accordance with section 12, with

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (i) the reference production rate for all finished product, and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (ii) if an authorization has been issued to the owner or operator under subsection 16(2), the reference production rate for all finished product other than dissolving grade sulphite pulp and the reference production rate for dissolving grade sulphite pulp;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (h) in the case of a mill that treats, in addition to its own effluent, waste water from sources other than a mill, if an authorization has been issued to the owner or operator under subsection 16(1), submitting the values of Bo and So and the supporting data to the authorization officer in accordance with section 19;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (j) submitting the information on outfall structures to the authorization officer in accordance with section 27, and depositing effluent only through those outfall structures;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (k) complying with the requirements for environmental effects monitoring studies set out in sections 28 to 31; and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (l) keeping available for inspection

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (i) for at least five years, the information and data specified in section 8.2 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition and section 8.2 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition,

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (ii) for at least three years, the results of all pH level and electrical conductivity tests conducted in accordance with Schedule II,

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (iii) for at least five years, a remedial plan and every update of it,

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (iv) for at least five years, an emergency response plan and every update of it, and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (v) for at least six years, all records, reports and data collected or prepared for the purposes of an environmental effects monitoring study.

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (2) The authority of the owner or operator of a mill under subsection 6(1) is also conditional on the operator

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) not combining any treated effluent with water before the treated effluent is deposited; and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) not combining any treated effluent with any other effluent before the treated effluent is deposited, unless neither the treated effluent nor the other effluent is acutely lethal or unless combining the effluents is authorized pursuant to an authorization under section 17.

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (3) The authority of the owner or operator of a mill under subsection 6(3) is conditional on the operator

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) depositing effluent only into a wastewater system that is regulated by the Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) submitting the identifying information to the authorization officer in accordance with subsections 10(1.1) to (3); and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (c) preparing an emergency response plan in accordance with section 11, making it readily available on site to persons who are to implement the plan and keeping the plan and every update available for inspection for at least five years.

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (4) The authority of the owner of a mill under section 6 is, if the owner is not the same person as the operator, also conditional on the owner exercising all due diligence to ensure that the operator meets the applicable conditions specified in this section.

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: 8 (1) The monitoring equipment referred to in paragraph 7(1)(a) is equipment that is installed, maintained and calibrated so that it is capable of monitoring effluent in accordance with Schedule II, and includes the following:

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: (a) equipment that is capable of taking duplicate samples of effluent from each outfall structure, or a sufficient volume of effluent to obtain split samples, for the purpose of conducting BOD tests and suspended solids tests; and

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: (b) equipment that permits the determination of the volume of effluent that is deposited through each outfall structure using a method that accords with generally accepted engineering principles, such as a method described in the standards for the measurement of fluid flow in closed conduits and for the measurement of liquid flow in open channels, published by the International Organization for Standardization under International Classification for standards numbers 17.120.10 and 17.120.20, respectively, as amended from time to time.

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: (2) Flow monitoring equipment shall be calibrated to be accurate to within 10 per cent.

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: (3) The records of the monitoring equipment shall

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: (a) contain a description of the monitoring equipment, including the manufacturer's specifications and the year and model number of the equipment;

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: (b) contain the results of the calibration tests of the monitoring equipment; and

heading: Monitoring Equipment
paragraph: (c) be kept available for inspection for a period of at least three years.

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: 9 (1) Each monthly report of monitoring results and production information referred to in paragraph 7(1)(b) shall contain the following information and shall be submitted to the authorization officer no later than 30 days after the end of the month to which the report relates:

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (a) the data required by section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition and section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition for all tests that were conducted in accordance with Schedule II during the month, including any additional tests that were conducted on samples collected in accordance with the procedures specified in that Schedule;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (b) the results of all BOD tests and suspended solids tests that were conducted in accordance with Schedule II during the month, including any additional tests that were conducted on samples collected in accordance with the procedures specified in that Schedule;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (c) the average daily BOD of the BOD matter that was deposited during the month and the average daily quantity of suspended solids that was deposited during the month, calculated on the basis of the results referred to in paragraph (b);

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (d) the total BOD of the BOD matter that was deposited during the month and the total quantity of suspended solids that was deposited during the month, calculated by multiplying the number of days in the month during which effluent was deposited by the applicable daily average for that month referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (e) the volume of effluent that was deposited during each daily period in the month;

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (f) in the case of a mill at which, under the authority of an authorization, treated effluent is combined with other effluent before being deposited, the volume of each effluent that is to be treated and the volume of the treated effluent before it is combined, for any daily period during which samples of effluent are collected in accordance with section 15 of Schedule II; and

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (g) in the case of a mill, the quantity of finished product, measured in accordance with subsection 12(3), that was produced during each daily period that the mill was in operation during the month.

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (3) Each report referred to in this section shall be submitted electronically in the format provided by the federal Department of the Environment, but the report shall be submitted in writing if

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (a) no such format has been provided; or

heading: Reporting Monitoring Results
paragraph: (b) it is, owing to circumstances beyond the operator's control, impracticable to submit the report electronically in the format provided.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: 10 (1) The identifying information referred to in paragraph 7(1)(d) is as follows:

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (a) the name and address of both the owner and the operator of the mill;

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (b) the day referred to in subsection 30(1) after which the interpretive report is required to be submitted to the authorization officer; and

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (c) in the case of a mill that treats, in addition to its own effluent, waste water from sources other than a mill, the name and address of both the owner and the operator of each of those sources.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (1.1) The identifying information referred to in paragraph 7(3)(b) is as follows:

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (a) the name and address of both the owner and the operator of the mill; and

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (b) the name and address of both the owner and the operator of the wastewater system into which effluent is deposited.

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (2) The identifying information shall be submitted no later than

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (a) 30 days after the day on which this subsection comes into force; or

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (b) the day on which the mill becomes subject to these Regulations, if that day is after the period referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Identifying Information
paragraph: (3) Any change in the information previously submitted shall be submitted no later than 90 days after the change occurs.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: 11 (1) The emergency response plan referred to in paragraphs 7(1)(f) and (3)(c) shall describe the measures to be taken to prevent any deposit of a deleterious substance out of the normal course of events or to mitigate the effects of such a deposit. The plan shall include the following elements:

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (a) the identification of any deposit out of the normal course of events that can reasonably be expected to occur at the mill and that can reasonably be expected to result in damage or danger to fish habitat or fish or the use by man of fish, and the identification of the damage or danger;

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (b) a description of the measures to be used to prevent, prepare for and respond to a deposit identified under paragraph (a);

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (c) a list of the individuals who are to implement the plan in the event of a deposit out of the normal course of events, and a description of their roles and responsibilities;

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (d) the identification of the emergency response training required for each of the individuals listed under paragraph (c);

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (e) a list of the emergency response equipment included as part of the plan, and the equipment's location; and

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (f) alerting and notification procedures including the measures to be taken to notify members of the public who may be adversely affected by a deposit identified under paragraph (a).

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (2) The emergency response plan shall be prepared no later than

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (a) 30 days after the day on which this subsection comes into force; or

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (b) the day on which the mill becomes subject to these Regulations, if that day is after the period referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (3) An updated emergency response plan shall be prepared no later than January 31 of each calendar year.

heading: Emergency Response Plan
paragraph: (4) If a mill has not been subject to the requirements of these Regulations for more than one year, a new emergency response plan shall be prepared on the day on which the mill again becomes subject to these Regulations.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: 12 (1) The reference production rate of a mill for any year is equal to the highest value of the 90th percentiles of the daily production of finished product at the mill for any of the previous three years.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (2) The 90th percentile of the daily production of finished product at a mill for a year is the statistically derived value that is equal to the quantity of finished product, produced daily by the mill, that was exceeded on 10 per cent of the days that the mill operated in the year.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (3) The production of finished product shall be measured in tonnes, taking into account the following:

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (a) in the case of pulp,

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (i) if its moisture content exceeds 10%, the weight of the pulp shall be adjusted so that its moisture content does not exceed 10%, or

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (ii) if its moisture content is equal to or less than 10%, the weight of the pulp shall not be adjusted; and

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (b) in the case of a paper product, the weight of the paper product shall be its weight after it has been machine dried.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (4) The reference production rates referred to in paragraph 7(1)(g) shall be submitted for each calendar year to the authorization officer no later than January 31 of the following year.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: 13 (1) Where less than three years of data are available on which to calculate the reference production rate of a mill, the operator may use a reference production rate calculated on the basis of available data or may apply to the authorization officer for an interim reference production rate.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (2) If the 90th percentile of the daily production of finished product at a mill has increased or is expected to increase by more than 25%, in respect of any period of 100 consecutive days, from the reference production rate of the mill, the operator may apply to the authorization officer for an interim reference production rate.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (3) If the 90th percentile of the daily production of finished product at a mill has decreased or is expected to decrease by more than 25%, in respect of any period of 100 consecutive days, from the reference production rate of the mill, the operator shall apply to the authorization officer for an interim reference production rate no later than 31 days after the decrease occurs or after becoming aware of the expected decrease, as the case may be.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (4) An applicant for an interim reference production rate shall submit plans, specifications and other information on the design and capability of the mill's production process to the authorization officer and such further information as the authorization officer may subsequently require to assess the application.

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (5) If, in accordance with subsection (1), (2) or (3), the authorization officer assigns an interim reference production rate to a mill to be used for the purposes of section 14 instead of the reference production rate, the interim reference production rate shall be based on an estimation of what the 90th percentile of the daily production would be at that mill. The estimation shall be based on the information submitted in accordance with subsection (4).

heading: Reference Production Rate
paragraph: (6) The use of an interim reference production rate shall commence on the day the authorization officer may specify and expires at the end of the year.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: 15 (1) An application for an authorization may be made by one or more of

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (a) the owner or operator of a mill that treats, in addition to its own effluent, waste water from sources other than a mill and that commenced operations before November 3, 1971, who seeks an authorization to deposit, or to permit the deposit of, BOD matter or suspended solids in quantities that exceed the maximum quantities authorized by section 14;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (b) the owner or operator of a mill that commenced operations before November 3, 1971 and since that date treats effluent from the production of dissolving grade sulphite pulp, who seeks an authorization to deposit, or to permit the deposit of, BOD matter or suspended solids in quantities that exceed the maximum quantities authorized by section 14; or

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (d) the owner or operator of a mill who seeks an authorization to combine treated effluent with other effluent before the treated effluent is deposited.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (2) An application for an authorization shall contain the information specified in Schedule III and shall be submitted to the authorization officer.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: 16 (1) The authorization officer may issue to the owner or operator of a mill referred to in paragraph 15(1)(a) an authorization to deposit, or to permit the deposit of, BOD matter and suspended solids in quantities that exceed the maximum quantities authorized by section 14, if the quantities so authorized are the lowest that can be achieved and do not exceed the maximum quantities that may be authorized under section 19.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (2) The authorization officer may issue to the owner or operator of a mill referred to in paragraph 15(1)(b) an authorization to deposit, or to permit the deposit of, BOD matter and suspended solids in quantities that exceed the maximum quantities authorized by section 14, if the quantities so authorized are the lowest that can be achieved and do not exceed the maximum quantities that may be authorized under section 20.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (3) An authorization may not be issued under subsection (1) or (2) unless the owner or operator of the mill has taken all applicable preventative measures at the production stage to reduce the BOD of all BOD matter and the quantity of suspended solids in the effluent.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: 17 (1) The authorization officer may issue to the owner or operator of a mill referred to in paragraph 15(1)(d) an authorization to combine treated effluent with other effluent before the treated effluent is deposited if

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (a) the operator has taken all reasonable steps, before the effluent is treated, to reduce the BOD of the BOD matter, the quantity of suspended solids and the lethality in respect of the effluent to be treated;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (b) the operator has instituted or intends to institute a water conservation program at the mill that would so reduce the volume of the effluent requiring treatment that it would still be acutely lethal despite treatment;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (c) the treatment process removes at least 90 per cent of the BOD of all BOD matter in the effluent that is treated; and

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (d) the other effluent is not acutely lethal before being combined with the treated effluent.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (2) Treated effluent may not be combined with other effluent in accordance with an authorization under subsection (1) unless the operator institutes the water conservation program referred to in that subsection.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: 18 (1) No authorization shall be issued under section 16 or 17 if the authorization officer has data indicating that the quantity of the deleterious substances to be authorized has had or will have a significant effect on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish that is more adverse than if the quantities were the maximum quantities authorized under section 14.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (2) An authorization shall be issued in the form set out in Schedule IV.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (3) The authorization officer may amend or withdraw any authorization if

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (a) new data indicate that the quantity of the substances, authorized by the authorization officer, has had or will have a significant effect on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish that is more adverse than if the quantities were the maximum quantities authorized under section 14;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (b) any of the grounds on which the authorization was issued ceases to be true;

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (c) an owner or operator has not taken all applicable preventative measures at the production stage to reduce the BOD of the BOD matter, the quantity of suspended solids or the lethality in respect of the effluent to be treated; or

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (d) there is a change in any information provided under section 3, 4 or 5 of Schedule III.

heading: Authorizations
paragraph: (4) Before issuing, amending or withdrawing an authorization, the authorization officer shall consult with officials in the Department of Fisheries and Oceans and, if the authorization officer is a provincial official, with officials in the federal Department of the Environment. The authorization officer may also consult with any other person, body or group that has an interest in the authorization.

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: 27 (1) The information on outfall structures required by paragraph 7(1)(j) is as follows:

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: (a) a general description of each outfall structure, together with its plans and specifications; and

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: (b) a description of the portion of each outfall structure situated at the point at which effluent is deposited, as it pertains to the dispersion of deleterious substances, and more particularly a description of the design, location and maintenance of that portion.

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: (2) The information on each outfall structure shall be submitted no later than

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: (a) 30 days after the day on which this subsection comes into force; or

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
