heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 28 (1) The owner or operator of a mill shall conduct environmental effects monitoring studies of the potential effects of effluent on the fish population, on fish tissue and on the benthic invertebrate community.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (2) Environmental effects monitoring studies consist of the sublethal toxicity testing referred to in section 29 and the biological monitoring studies referred to in section 30.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (3) The studies shall be performed and their results recorded, interpreted and reported in accordance with generally accepted standards of good scientific practice at the time that the studies are performed.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator shall submit to the authorization officer reports of the results of the studies in writing and the supporting data in the electronic format provided by the federal Department of the Environment.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 29 (1) Sublethal toxicity testing shall be conducted in accordance with section 2 of Schedule IV.1, twice in each calendar year, on the aliquots of effluent samples collected in accordance with section 3 of Schedule II from the outfall structure that has potentially the most adverse environmental impact.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (2) A report on the sublethal toxicity tests shall be prepared twice in each calendar year and submitted to the authorization officer within three months after the completion of the tests.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), the owner or operator of a mill that deposits effluent from the outfall structure referred to in subsection (1) on fewer than 120 days in any calendar year is required to conduct and submit the report on the sublethal toxicity tests only once in respect of that calendar year.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (4) Despite subsections (1) to (3), the owner or operator of a mill is not required to conduct sublethal toxicity testing and submit a report on the sublethal toxicity tests if the mill has not produced pulp or paper products for at least eight consecutive months and has not resumed production.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 30 (1) Biological monitoring studies shall be conducted and an interpretive report shall be submitted to the authorization officer, in accordance with sections 3 to 12 of Schedule IV.1, within three years, after

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) the day on which a mill first becomes subject to these Regulations, which day shall not precede the coming into force of this section; or

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) the day on which a mill again becomes subject to these Regulations after having not produced pulp or paper products for at least eight consecutive months, which day shall not precede the coming into force of this section.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) to (5), subsequent biological monitoring studies shall be conducted and interpretive reports shall be submitted to the authorization officer within three years after the day on which the most recent interpretive report was required to be submitted.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (3) The time limit for conducting the subsequent biological monitoring study on the fish population, referred to in paragraph 3(a) of Schedule IV.1, and for submitting the interpretive report in relation to this study, is six years after the day on which the most recent interpretive report was required to be submitted if

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) according to the two most recent interpretive reports, the study has found no effects on the fish population; or

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) the most recent interpretive report indicates the solutions to eliminate the effects on the fish population.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (4) The time limit for conducting the subsequent biological monitoring study on the benthic invertebrate community, referred to in paragraph 3(c) of Schedule IV.1, and for submitting the interpretive report in relation to this study, is six years after the day on which the most recent interpretive report was required to be submitted if

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) according to the two most recent interpretive reports, the study has found no effects on the benthic invertebrate community; or

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) the most recent interpretive report indicates the solutions to eliminate the effects on the benthic invertebrate community.

heading: Environmental Effects Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (5) The owner or operator of a mill is not required to conduct biological monitoring studies if the mill has not produced pulp or paper products for at least eight consecutive months and has not resumed production.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: 32 (1) For the purpose of subsection 38(4) of the Act, the person occupying the position set out in column II of Schedule VI for the province, set out in column I, where the mill is located is a prescribed person.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (2) Any person required by subsection 38(4) of the Act to report the occurrence of a deposit of a deleterious substance out of the normal course of events shall, if a deposit has occurred, submit a written report to an inspector or the person referred to in subsection (1) as soon as possible in the circumstances, but at the latest 30 days after the day on which the deposit occurred.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of evaluating the effect of a deposit out of the normal course of events that has occurred from an outfall structure, the operator shall, in accordance with subsection 2(1) of Schedule II and as soon as possible in the circumstances,

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (a) collect a grab sample from the outfall structure through which the deposit occurred and subject the sample to

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (i) a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition, and

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (ii) a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition; and

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (b) subject another sample, collected from the outfall structure through which the deposit occurred in accordance with section 6 of Schedule II, to a BOD test.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (4) The collecting and testing of a sample under subsection (3) are not required if, for the purpose of monitoring effluent under paragraph 7(1)(b), the same sample has already been collected and the same test has been conducted whose result permits the determination of the effect of the deposit out of the normal course of events.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (5) The written report shall contain the following information:

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (a) the BOD of the BOD matter that was deposited, and the quantity of suspended solids that was deposited, that exceeded the maximum respective quantities authorized by section 14 or under an authorization or, if either of them cannot be determined, an estimate of that BOD or of that quantity of suspended solids, or both, along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived;

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (b) an estimate of the BOD of the BOD matter that was deposited during any period in which the monitoring equipment was malfunctioning, and of the quantity of suspended solids that was deposited during that period, along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived;

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (c) the volume or, if the volume cannot be determined, an estimate of the volume of acutely lethal effluent that was deposited and the results of the test that was conducted pursuant to subparagraph (3)(a)(i) or any test that meets the criteria of subsection (4);

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (d) the results of the test that was conducted pursuant to subparagraph (3)(a)(ii) or any test that meets the criteria of subsection (4);

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (e) the quantity of any deleterious substance that was deposited in any way other than through an outfall structure in respect of which a plan had been provided in accordance with paragraph 27(1)(a) or, if the quantity cannot be determined, an estimate of the quantity along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived;

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (f) the quantity of any deleterious substance that was deposited through an outfall structure through which untreated effluent is deposited or, if the quantity cannot be determined, an estimate of the quantity along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived; and

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (g) the circumstances of the deposit, the measures that were taken to mitigate the effects of the deposit and, if the emergency response plan prepared in accordance with section 11 was implemented, details concerning its implementation.

heading: Application
paragraph: 33 This Part applies in respect of the Port Alberni Mill.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: 34 (1) For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of the mill may deposit, or permit the deposit of, BOD matter in Alberni Inlet if the BOD of the BOD matter does not exceed

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) during any daily period, 5 641 kg; and

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) during any month, an average of 3 385 kg per daily period.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of the mill may deposit, or permit the deposit of, suspended solids in Alberni Inlet if the quantity of suspended solids does not exceed

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) during any daily period, 10 154 kg; and

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) during any month, an average of 6 092 kg per daily period.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (3) The authority to deposit BOD matter and suspended solids conferred by subsections (1) and (2) does not confer any authority to deposit acutely lethal effluent.

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of the mill may deposit, or permit the deposit of, any concentration of acutely lethal effluent, any BOD matter and any quantity of suspended solids into

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) a treatment facility that is owned or operated by the owner of the factory; or

heading: Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) if the factory is part of a complex, the common treatment facility for the factories that are part of the complex.

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: 35 (1) The authority of the owner or operator of the mill under section 34 is conditional on the operator

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) installing, maintaining and calibrating monitoring equipment, and keeping records of that equipment, in accordance with section 8;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) monitoring effluent in accordance with Schedule II and submitting to the authorization officer a monthly report of the monitoring results and production information in accordance with subsections 9(1) and (3), other than paragraphs (1)(d) and (f);

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (c) notifying an inspector, without delay, of any result of a test conducted in accordance with Schedule II and of any result of any additional test that was conducted on samples collected in accordance with the procedures specified in that Schedule, other than in the case of a deposit out of the normal course of events, that indicates a failure or non-compliance with these Regulations, and reporting the test results in writing to the inspector within 10 days after the notification;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (d) submitting the identifying information to the authorization officer in accordance with paragraph 10(1)(a) and subsections 10(2) and (3);

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (e) preparing and updating annually a remedial plan describing the measures to be taken by the operator to eliminate all unauthorized deposits of deleterious substances in the case where effluent fails an acute lethality test conducted in accordance with Schedule II;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (f) conducting a dissolved oxygen monitoring program in accordance with Schedule VII and submitting to the authorization officer data obtained from the program and reports in accordance with section 36;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (g) preparing an emergency response plan in accordance with section 11 and making it readily available on site to persons who are to implement the plan;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (h) submitting the information on outfall structures to the authorization officer in accordance with section 37, and depositing effluent only through those outfall structures;

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (i) complying with the requirements for environmental effects monitoring studies set out in sections 28 and 29 and conducting biological monitoring studies and submitting an interpretive report to the authorization officer, in accordance with sections 3 to 12 of Schedule IV.1, no later than April 1, 2007, and, with respect to subsequent biological monitoring studies and reports, complying with the requirements of subsections 30(2) and (3); and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (j) keeping available for inspection

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (i) for at least five years, the information and data specified in section 8.2 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition and section 8.2 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition,

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (ii) for at least three years, the results of all pH levels and electrical conductivity tests conducted in accordance with Schedule II,

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (iii) for at least five years, a remedial plan and every update of it,

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (iv) for at least five years, an emergency response plan and every update of it, and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (v) for at least six years, all records, reports and data collected or prepared for the purposes of an environmental effects monitoring study.

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (2) The authority of the owner or operator of the mill under section 34 is also conditional on the operator

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (a) not combining any treated effluent with water before the treated effluent is deposited; and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (b) not combining any treated effluent with any other effluent before the treated effluent is deposited, unless

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (i) neither the treated effluent nor the other effluent is acutely lethal, and

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (ii) the treated effluent and the other effluent are monitored in accordance with sections 17 to 19 of Schedule II before they are combined.

heading: Conditions Governing Authority to Deposit
paragraph: (3) The authority of the owner of the mill under section 34 is, if the owner is not the same person as the operator, also conditional on the owner exercising all due diligence to ensure that the operator meets the applicable conditions specified in this section.

heading: Submission of Data and Reports in Respect of the Dissolved Oxygen Monitoring Program
paragraph: 36 (1) The data obtained from the dissolved oxygen monitoring program referred to in paragraph 35(1)(f) shall be submitted to the authorization officer no later than 30 days after the end of the month in which the data are collected.

heading: Submission of Data and Reports in Respect of the Dissolved Oxygen Monitoring Program
paragraph: (2) An interpretive report that describes and evaluates the data obtained from the dissolved oxygen monitoring program in any calendar year shall be submitted to the authorization officer no later than March 31 following that calendar year.

heading: Submission of Data and Reports in Respect of the Dissolved Oxygen Monitoring Program
paragraph: (3) The data and the report shall be submitted electronically in the format provided by the federal Department of the Environment, but they shall be submitted in writing if

heading: Submission of Data and Reports in Respect of the Dissolved Oxygen Monitoring Program
paragraph: (a) no such format has been provided; or

heading: Submission of Data and Reports in Respect of the Dissolved Oxygen Monitoring Program
paragraph: (b) it is, owing to circumstances beyond the operator's control, impracticable to submit them electronically in the format provided.

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: 37 (1) The information on outfall structures required by paragraph 35(1)(h) is as follows:

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: (a) a general description of each outfall structure, together with its plans and specifications; and

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: (b) a description of the portion of each outfall structure situated at the point at which effluent is deposited, as it pertains to the dispersion of deleterious substances, and more particularly a description of the design, location and maintenance of that portion.

heading: Information on Outfall Structures
paragraph: (2) Information on any proposed change to an outfall structure shall be submitted at least 90 days before the change is made.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: 38 (1) For the purpose of subsection 38(4) of the Act, the person occupying the position set out in item 6, column II, of Schedule VI is a prescribed person.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (2) Any person required by subsection 38(4) of the Act to report the occurrence of a deposit of a deleterious substance out of the normal course of events shall, if a deposit has occurred, submit a written report to an inspector or the person referred to in subsection (1) as soon as possible in the circumstances, but at the latest 30 days after the day on which the deposit occurred.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of evaluating the effect of a deposit out of the normal course of events that has occurred from an outfall structure, the operator shall, in accordance with subsection 2(1) of Schedule II and as soon as possible in the circumstances,

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (a) collect a grab sample from the outfall structure through which the deposit occurred and subject the sample to

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (i) a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition, and

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (ii) a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition; and

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (b) subject another sample, collected from the outfall structure through which the deposit occurred in accordance with section 6 of Schedule II, to a BOD test.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (4) The collecting and testing of a sample under subsection (3) are not required if, for the purpose of monitoring effluent under paragraph 35(1)(b), the same sample has already been collected and the same test has been conducted whose result permits the determination of the effect of the deposit out of the normal course of events.

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (5) The written report shall contain the following information:

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (a) the BOD of the BOD matter that was deposited, and the quantity of suspended solids that was deposited, that exceeded the maximum respective quantities authorized by section 34 or, if either of them cannot be determined, an estimate of that BOD or of that quantity of suspended solids, or both, along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived;

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (b) an estimate of the BOD of the BOD matter that was deposited during any period in which the monitoring equipment was malfunctioning, and of the quantity of suspended solids that was deposited during that period along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived;

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (c) the volume or, if the volume cannot be determined, an estimate of the volume of acutely lethal effluent that was deposited and the results of the test that was conducted pursuant to subparagraph (3)(a)(i) or any test that meets the criteria of subsection (4);

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (d) the results of the test that was conducted pursuant to subparagraph (3)(a)(ii) or any test that meets the criteria of subsection (4);

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (e) whether any sample of effluent failed an acute lethality test or a Daphnia magna test conducted in accordance with sections 17 and 18 of Schedule II;

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (f) the quantity of any deleterious substance that was deposited in any way other than through an outfall structure in respect of which a plan had been provided in accordance with paragraph 37(1)(a) or, if the quantity cannot be determined, an estimate of the quantity along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived;

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (g) the quantity of any deleterious substance that was deposited through an outfall structure through which untreated effluent is deposited or, if the quantity cannot be determined, an estimate of the quantity along with information and supporting data on how the estimate was derived; and

heading: Reports of Deposits out of the Normal Course of Events
paragraph: (h) the circumstances of the deposit, the measures that were taken to mitigate the effects of the deposit and, if the emergency response plan prepared in accordance with section 11 was implemented, details concerning its implementation.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: 1 The test to determine the acute lethality of effluent is a test conducted in accordance with section 5 or 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: 2 (1) The test in respect of Daphnia magna is a test conducted in accordance with section 5 or 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/14 Second Edition.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (2) Effluent fails the Daphnia magna test when, at 100 per cent concentration, it kills more than 50 per cent of the Daphnia magna subjected to it during a 48-hour period.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: 3 (1) The test to determine the BOD of an effluent is a test conducted in accordance with one of the following standard five-day BOD test methods (BOD5):

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (a) the method described in subsections 5210A and 5210B of Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, 20th Edition, 1998, published jointly by the American Public Health Association, the American Water Works Association and the Water Environment Federation, as amended from time to time;

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (b) the method described in Method H.2, Determination of Biochemical Oxygen Demand, December 1991, published by the Technical Section of the Canadian Pulp and Paper Association (now the Pulp and Paper Technical Association of Canada), as amended from time to time; or

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (c) a test method equivalent to a method referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) that is required by or authorized under the law of the province where the mill is located.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (2) The quantity of BOD is measured in terms of an unfiltered sample.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), the test to determine the BOD of an effluent shall

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (a) commence within 48 hours of the sampling; and

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (b) be conducted on a sample that is of such concentration that the depletion of oxygen is equal to or greater than 30% but does not exceed 60%.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: 4 (1) The test to determine the presence and quantity of suspended solids in effluent is a test conducted in accordance with one of the following standard test methods for total suspended solids:

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (a) the applicable method described in subsections 2540A to 2540E of Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, 20th Edition, 1998, published jointly by the American Public Health Association, the American Water Works Association and the Water Environment Federation, as amended from time to time;

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (b) the method described in Method H.1, Determination of Solids Content of Pulp and Paper Mill Effluents, August 1993, published by the Technical Section of the Canadian Pulp and Paper Association (now the Pulp and Paper Technical Association of Canada), as amended from time to time; or

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (c) a test method equivalent to a method referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) that is required by or authorized under the law of the province where the mill is located.

heading: SCHEDULE I(Section 2)Test Methods
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of the suspended solids test, where a sample is difficult to filter, the bulk of the solids should be allowed to settle before the sample is filtered so that the upper portion of the sample can be filtered first.

heading: Required Monitoring
paragraph: 1 (1) Effluent from a mill other than the effluent from a mill that is deposited into a wastewater system, shall be monitored in accordance with this Schedule for

heading: Required Monitoring
paragraph: (a) the presence of acutely lethal effluent and the effect on Daphnia magna;

heading: Required Monitoring
paragraph: (b) the BOD of BOD matter;

heading: Required Monitoring
paragraph: (c) the quantity of suspended solids;

heading: Required Monitoring
paragraph: (d) volume; and

heading: Required Monitoring
paragraph: (e) pH levels and electrical conductivity.

heading: Location of Sampling
paragraph: 2 (1) The sampling of effluent from a mill, other than the effluent from a mill that is deposited into a wastewater system, that is required by this Schedule - except for sampling conducted in accordance with sections 14 and 15 or sections 18 and 19 - shall be conducted at any point of an outfall structure that is located upstream of the deposit point of the effluent and downstream of

heading: Location of Sampling
paragraph: (a) the treatment if the mill treats the effluent; and

heading: Location of Sampling
paragraph: (b) the combination point if the mill combines effluents before their deposit.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: 3 For the purpose of monitoring for the presence of acutely lethal effluent and the effect on Daphnia magna, a grab sample of effluent shall be collected from each outfall structure once a week when the mill is depositing effluent.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: 4 (1) Subject to section 5, the samples of effluent collected in accordance with section 3 shall be tested as follows:

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (a) each month, one of the samples collected during that month from each outfall structure in accordance with section 3 shall be subjected to an acute lethality test; and

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (b) each of the samples collected in accordance with section 3 shall be subjected to a Daphnia magna test.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (2) The following procedures apply in respect of an acute lethality test referred to in paragraph (1)(a):

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (a) the day on which a sample is to be collected for testing shall be selected by the operator, and notice of that day shall be given to the authorization officer, at least 30 days in advance;

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (b) the operator shall collect the sample on the selected day except if, owing to unforeseen circumstances, the operator cannot sample on that day, and in that case, shall do so as soon as possible after that day; and

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (c) a period of at least 21 days shall intervene between the collection of any two samples for testing.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: 5 (1) If a sample of effluent from an outfall structure fails a test conducted in accordance with paragraph 4(1)(a) of this Schedule or subparagraph 32(3)(a)(i) or 38(3)(a)(i) of these Regulations, each of the subsequent weekly samples collected from that outfall structure in accordance with section 3 shall be subjected to a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (2) If a sample of effluent from an outfall structure fails a test conducted in accordance with paragraph 4(1)(b), a grab sample of effluent shall be collected from that outfall structure without delay and subjected to a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if, at the time the sample that failed the test conducted in accordance with paragraph 4(1)(b) was collected, a sample of effluent was also collected from that outfall structure under subsection (1) or paragraph 4(1)(a) and subjected to a test in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (4) If a sample of effluent from an outfall structure fails a test conducted in accordance with subsection (2), each of the subsequent weekly samples collected from that outfall structure in accordance with section 3 shall be subjected to a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition.

heading: Acute Lethality and Effect on Daphnia Magna
paragraph: (5) The testing of samples of effluent shall continue as required by subsection (1) or (4), as applicable, until three consecutive tests are passed, after which testing may resume as required by section 4.

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: 6 (1) For the purpose of monitoring the BOD of BOD matter and the quantity of suspended solids in the case of a mill whose effluent is described in subsection 1(1), there shall be collected, from each outfall structure during each daily period that the mill is depositing effluent,

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: (a) a continuous sample of the effluent;

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: (b) equal samples of the effluent, collected at least every 15 minutes, for the preparation of a composite sample; or

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: (c) samples of the effluent in a quantity proportional to the effluent's volume, collected at least every 15 minutes, for the preparation of a composite sample.

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: (2) If effluent is deposited through an outfall structure for only a portion of a daily period, a sample of effluent shall be collected from that outfall structure during the period when that effluent is being deposited.

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: 7 The samples of effluent collected in accordance with section 6 shall be tested as follows:

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: (a) at least three of the samples collected from each outfall structure during each week shall be subjected to a BOD test; and

heading: BOD and Suspended Solids
paragraph: (b) each of the samples collected shall be subjected to a suspended solids test.

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: 10 (1) For the purpose of monitoring the volume of effluent in the case of a mill whose effluent is described in subsection 1(1), the volume of effluent that is deposited through each outfall structure during each daily period shall be determined using the monitoring equipment referred to in paragraph 8(1)(b) of these Regulations.

heading: Volume of Effluent
paragraph: (2) If the actual volume of effluent that is deposited cannot be determined because the monitoring equipment is malfunctioning, the volume shall be calculated based on flow rates that are estimated using generally accepted engineering principles.

heading: pH Levels and Electrical Conductivity
paragraph: 12 For the purpose of monitoring the pH levels and electrical conductivity of effluent, the effluent that is deposited through each outfall structure shall be tested continuously for pH levels and for electrical conductivity.

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: 13 If, under the authority of an authorization, treated effluent is combined with other effluent at a mill before being deposited, the effluent at the mill shall, in addition to being monitored in accordance with the other requirements of this Schedule, be monitored for the presence of acutely lethal effluent, for the BOD of BOD matter and for volume in accordance with sections 14 to 16.

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: 14 For the purpose of monitoring for the presence of acutely lethal effluent, a grab sample of the treated effluent and a grab sample of the other effluent shall be collected once a month upstream of the combination point, and each of the samples collected shall be subjected to an acute lethality test.

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: 15 (1) For the purpose of monitoring the BOD of BOD matter, the following samples of effluent shall be collected once every three months and subjected to a BOD test:

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (a) a sample of each effluent that is to be treated; and

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (b) a sample of the treated effluent upstream of the point where it is combined with the other effluent.

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (2) The samples shall be collected in accordance with section 6 using equipment that is installed, maintained and calibrated so that it is capable of taking duplicate samples of effluent or a sufficient volume of effluent to obtain split samples, or

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (a) in the case of effluent that is to be treated,

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (i) if there is only one effluent to be treated, by collecting grab samples of the effluent not more than six hours apart during a daily period and combining them as a composite sample, or

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (ii) if there is more than one effluent to be treated, by collecting grab samples of each effluent not more than six hours apart during a daily period and combining them, in proportion to the estimated flow rate of each of the effluents, as a composite sample; and

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (b) in the case of the treated effluent, by collecting grab samples of the effluent not more than six hours apart during a daily period and combining them as a composite sample.

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (3) If sampling is conducted using the equipment referred to in subsection (2), the requirements of subsections 8(2) and (3) of these Regulations apply in respect of that equipment.

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: 16 (1) For the purpose of monitoring the volume of effluent, the volume of each of the effluents referred to in section 15 shall, during each daily period that a sample is collected in accordance with that section, be determined as follows:

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (a) if samples are collected in accordance with section 6 using equipment referred to in subsection 15(2), by using equipment that is installed, maintained and calibrated so that it permits the determination of the volume of the effluent using a method that accords with generally accepted engineering principles, such as a method referred to in paragraph 8(1)(b) of these Regulations; and

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (b) if samples are collected in accordance with paragraph 15(2)(a) or (b), by using equipment referred to in paragraph (a) or by means of a calculation based on flow rates that are estimated using generally accepted engineering principles.

heading: Authorization to Combine
paragraph: (2) If the volume of effluent is determined using equipment referred to in subsection (1), the requirements of subsections 8(2) and (3) of these Regulations apply in respect of that equipment.

heading: Combination at Port Alberni Mill
paragraph: 17 If treated effluent is combined with other effluent at the Port Alberni Mill before being deposited, the effluent at that mill shall, in addition to being monitored in accordance with the other requirements of this Schedule, be monitored for the presence of acutely lethal effluent and the effect on Daphnia magna, and for pH levels and electrical conductivity, in accordance with sections 18 and 19.

heading: Combination at Port Alberni Mill
paragraph: 18 (1) For the purpose of monitoring for the presence of acutely lethal effluent and the effect on Daphnia magna, a grab sample of the treated effluent and a grab sample of the other effluent shall be collected once a week upstream of the combination point, and the samples collected shall be tested as follows:

heading: Combination at Port Alberni Mill
paragraph: (a) the samples collected during one week of each month shall be subjected to an acute lethality test; and

heading: Combination at Port Alberni Mill
paragraph: (b) each of the samples collected shall be subjected to a Daphnia magna test.

heading: Combination at Port Alberni Mill
paragraph: (2) If a sample of effluent fails a test conducted in accordance with paragraph (1)(b), a grab sample of that effluent shall be collected without delay and subjected to a test conducted in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition.

heading: Combination at Port Alberni Mill
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if, at the time the sample that failed the test conducted in accordance with paragraph (1)(b) was collected, a sample of effluent was also collected from that outfall under paragraph (1)(a) and subjected to a test in accordance with section 6 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition.

heading: Combination at Port Alberni Mill
paragraph: 19 For the purpose of monitoring the pH levels and electrical conductivity of effluent, the treated effluent and the other effluent shall be tested continuously for pH levels and for electrical conductivity upstream of the combination point.

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: 20 (1) The sampling and testing, other than testing for pH levels and electrical conductivity, of the effluent that is deposited through each outfall structure may be conducted at a reduced frequency of once a month, and the volume of effluent that is deposited through that outfall structure may be calculated based on flow rates that are estimated using generally accepted engineering principles, if either of the following conditions is met:

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (a) each sample of effluent from that outfall structure that was tested during the preceding month

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (i) was not acutely lethal,

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (ii) contained BOD matter having a BOD of less than 10 mg per litre of effluent,

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (iii) contained less than 10 mg of suspended solids per litre of effluent, and

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (iv) contained no other deleterious substance; or

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (b) the effluent from that outfall structure contains only water that has been used exclusively for non-contact cooling purposes.

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), the sampling of effluent from an outfall structure may be done by collecting a grab sample.

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (3) If monitoring of the effluent that is deposited through an outfall structure is being conducted in accordance with subsections (1) and (2) on the basis that the effluent met the conditions specified in paragraph (1)(a), monitoring may no longer be conducted in accordance with those subsections if the effluent

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (a) is acutely lethal;

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (b) contains BOD matter having a BOD of 10 mg or more per litre;

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (c) contains 10 mg or more of suspended solids per litre; or

heading: Reduced Monitoring
paragraph: (d) contains any other deleterious substance.

paragraph: Please refer to section 7 of the Pulp and Paper Effluent Regulations for conditions governing the authority to deposit. In addition, please note that this authorization may be amended or withdrawn in accordance with section 18 of those Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1 The following definitions apply in this Schedule.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effect on fish tissue means that the concentration of chlorinated dioxins and furans, expressed as toxic equivalents of 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-para-dioxin, exceeds 15 pg/g wet weight in muscle or 30 pg/g wet weight in liver or hepatopancreas in fish taken in the exposure area. (effet sur les tissus de poissons)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effect on the benthic invertebrate community means a statistical difference between data referred to in subparagraph 11(a)(ii) from a study respecting the benthic invertebrate community conducted in

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) an exposure area and a reference area; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) sampling areas within an exposure area where there are gradually decreasing effluent concentrations. (effet sur la communaute d'invertebres benthiques)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: effect on the fish population means a statistical difference between data relating to the indicators referred to in subparagraph 11(a)(i) from a study respecting fish population conducted in

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) an exposure area and a reference area; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) sampling areas within an exposure area where there are gradually decreasing effluent concentrations. (effet sur la population de poissons)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: exposure area means all fish habitat and waters frequented by fish that are exposed to effluent. (zone exposee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: fish means fish as defined in section 2 of the Fisheries Act, but does not include parts of fish, parts of shellfish, parts of crustaceans or parts of marine animals. (poissons)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: reference area means water frequented by fish that is not exposed to effluent and that has fish habitat that, as far as practicable, is most similar to that of the exposure area. (zone de reference)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: sampling area means the area within a reference or exposure area where representative samples are collected. (zone d'echantillonnage)

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: 2 (1) Sublethal toxicity testing shall be conducted by following the applicable methods referred to in subsections (2) and (3) and by recording the results for an invertebrate species and an algal species.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (2) In the case of effluent that is deposited into fresh waters, sublethal toxicity tests shall be conducted by using the following test methodologies, as amended from time to time, as applicable to each species:

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (b) in the case of an invertebrate species, Biological Test Method: Test of Reproduction and Survival Using the Cladoceran Ceriodaphnia dubia (Report EPS 1/RM/21 Second Edition), February 2007, published by the federal Department of the Environment; and

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (c) in the case of an algal species,

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (i) Biological Test Method: Growth Inhibition Test Using a Freshwater Alga (Report EPS 1/RM/25 Second Edition), March 2007, published by the federal Department of the Environment, or

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (ii) Determination de l'inhibition de la croissance chez l'algue Selenastrum capricornutum (Reference Method MA 500-S. cap.2.0), September 1997, published by the Centre d'expertise en analyse environnementale du Quebec.

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (3) In the case of effluent that is deposited into marine or estuarine waters, sublethal toxicity tests shall be conducted by using the following test methodologies, as amended from time to time, as applicable to each species:

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (a) in the case of an invertebrate species, Biological Test Method: Fertilization Assay Using Echinoids (Sea Urchins and Sand Dollars) (Report EPS 1/RM/27), December 1992, published by the federal Department of the Environment; and

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (b) in the case of algal species, one of the following test methodologies, as applicable, namely,

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (i) Short-term Methods for Estimating the Chronic Toxicity of Effluents and Receiving Waters to Marine and Estuarine Organisms (Third Edition) (Reference Method EPA/821/R/02-014), October 2002, published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, or

heading: Sublethal Toxicity Testing
paragraph: (ii) Short-term Methods for Estimating the Chronic Toxicity of Effluent and Receiving Waters to West Coast Marine and Estuarine Organisms (First Edition) (Reference Method EPA/600/R-95-136), August 1995, published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

heading: Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 3 Biological monitoring studies consist of

heading: Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) a study respecting the fish population, if the concentration of effluent in the exposure area is greater than 1% in the area located within 250 m of a point of deposit of the effluent in water;

heading: Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) a study respecting fish tissue if

heading: Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (i) since the submission of the most recent interpretive report, the effluent contained a measurable concentration of 2,3,7,8-TCDD or of 2,3,7,8-TCDF, within the meaning of the Pulp and Paper Mill Effluent Chlorinated Dioxins and Furans Regulations, or

heading: Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (ii) an effect on fish tissue was reported in the most recent interpretive report; and

heading: Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (c) a study respecting the benthic invertebrate community, if the concentration of effluent in the exposure area is greater than 1% in the area located within 100 m of a point of deposit of the effluent in water.

heading: Study Design
paragraph: 4 (1) At least six months before the commencement of sampling for biological monitoring studies, a study design shall be submitted to the authorization officer that, subject to subsections (2) to (4), consists of

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (a) the site characterization referred to in section 5;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (b) if a study respecting fish population is required under paragraph 3(a), a description of how the study will be conducted, that includes

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (i) the information referred to in paragraphs 6(a) to (d), and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (ii) how the study will determine whether the effluent has an effect on the fish population;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (c) if a study respecting fish tissue is required under paragraph 3(b), a description of how the study will be conducted that includes

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (i) the information referred to in paragraphs 6(a) to (d), and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (ii) how the study will determine whether the effluent has an effect on fish tissue;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (d) if the study referred to in paragraph 3(c) respecting the benthic invertebrate community is required, a description of how the study will be conducted, that includes

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (i) the information referred to in paragraphs 7(a) to (d), and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (ii) how the study will determine whether the effluent has an effect on the benthic invertebrate community;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (e) the dates when any samples will be collected;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (f) a description of the quality assurance and quality control measures that will be implemented to ensure the validity of the data that is collected;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (g) a summary of the results of any previous biological monitoring studies that were conducted respecting the fish population, fish tissue or the benthic invertebrate community; and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (h) if the two most recent interpretive reports indicate the same effect on the fish population, on fish tissue or on the benthic invertebrate community, a description of the magnitude and geographical extent of the effect.

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (2) If the most recent interpretive report indicates the magnitude and geographical extent of an effect on the fish population, on fish tissue or on the benthic invertebrate community, or that the cause of the effect has not been identified, the study design shall consist of the following:

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (a) the summary of results referred to in paragraph (1)(g); and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (b) a detailed description of the field and laboratory studies that will be used to determine the cause of the effect.

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (3) If the most recent interpretive report indicates the cause of the effect on the fish population, on fish tissue or on the benthic invertebrate community, or that the solutions have not been identified, the study design shall consist of a detailed description of the studies that will be used to identify the possible solutions to eliminate the effect.

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (4) If the most recent interpretive report indicates the solutions to eliminate the effect, the study design shall consist of the information referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Study Design
paragraph: 5 (1) The site characterization consists of

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (a) a description of the manner in which the effluent mixes within the exposure area, including an estimate of the concentration of effluent in water at 100 m and 250 m, respectively, from each point of deposit of the effluent in water;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (b) a description of the reference and exposure areas where the biological monitoring studies will be conducted that includes a mapped description of the sampling areas and information on the geological, hydrological, oceanographical, limnological, chemical and biological features of those areas;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (c) a description of any anthropogenic, natural or other factors that are not related to the effluent under study and that may reasonably be expected to contribute to any observed effect;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (d) the type of production process and treatment system used by the mill; and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (e) any additional information relevant to the site characterization.

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (2) If the information described in subsection (1) was submitted in a previous study design, it may be submitted in summary format, but it shall include a detailed description of any changes to that information since the submission of the most recent study design.

heading: Study Design
paragraph: 6 The information respecting the fish population and fish tissue studies shall include a description of and the scientific rationale for

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (a) the fish species selected, taking into account the abundance of the species most exposed to effluent;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (b) the sampling areas selected;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (c) the sample size selected; and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (d) the field and laboratory methodologies selected.

heading: Study Design
paragraph: 7 The information respecting the benthic invertebrate community studies shall include a description of and the scientific rationale for

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (a) the sampling areas selected, taking into account the benthic invertebrate diversity and the area most exposed to effluent;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (b) the sample size selected;

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (c) the sampling period selected; and

heading: Study Design
paragraph: (d) the field and laboratory methodologies selected.

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 8 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the biological monitoring studies shall be conducted in accordance with the study design submitted under section 4.

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (2) If it is impossible to follow the study design because of unusual circumstances, the owner or operator of a mill may deviate from the study design but shall inform the authorization officer without delay of those circumstances and of how the study was or will be conducted.

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 9 When studies respecting fish population or the benthic invertebrate community are conducted, water samples shall be collected from the sampling areas selected under paragraphs 6(b) and 7(a), and the following information shall be recorded:

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) water temperature;

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) depth;

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (c) concentration of dissolved oxygen;

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (d) in the case of effluent that is deposited into fresh water, pH levels, electrical conductivity, hardness, total phosphorus, total nitrogen and total organic carbon; and

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (e) in the case of effluent that is deposited into marine or estuarine waters, salinity.

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: 10 When studies respecting the benthic invertebrate community are conducted, sediment samples shall be collected from the sampling areas selected under paragraph 7(a), and the following information shall be recorded:

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (a) particle size distribution and total organic carbon; and

heading: Conducting Biological Monitoring Studies
paragraph: (b) in the case of effluent that is deposited into marine or estuarine waters, the ratio of carbon to nitrogen, redox potential (Eh) and sulphides.

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: 11 The data collected during the biological monitoring studies shall be used

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: (a) to calculate the mean, the standard deviation, the standard error and the minimum and maximum values in the sampling areas for

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: (i) in the case of a study respecting the fish population, and if it is possible to obtain data to establish the following indicators - indicators of growth, reproduction, condition and survival that include the length, total body weight and age of the fish, the weight of its liver or hepatopancreas and, if the fish are sexually mature, the egg weight, fecundity and gonad weight of the fish, and

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a study respecting the benthic invertebrate community - the total benthic invertebrate density, the evenness index, the taxa richness and the similarity index;

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: (b) to identify the sex of the fish sampled and the presence of any lesions, tumours, parasites or other abnormalities;

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: (c) to conduct an analysis of the results of the calculations under paragraph (a) and information identified under paragraph (b) to determine if there is a statistical difference between the sampling areas;

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: (d) to conduct a statistical analysis of the results of the calculations under paragraph (a) to determine the probability of correctly detecting an effect of a pre-defined size and the degree of confidence that can be placed in the calculations; and

heading: Assessment of Data Collected from Studies
paragraph: (e) to calculate the concentration of chlorinated dioxins and furans in fish tissue taken from the exposure area, which concentration is expressed as toxic equivalents of 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-para-dioxin.

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: 12 (1) After biological monitoring studies are conducted in accordance with sections 8 to 10, an interpretive report shall be prepared that, subject to subsections (2) and (2.1), contains the following information:

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (a) a description of any deviation from the study design that occurred while the biological monitoring studies were being conducted and any impact that the deviation had on the studies;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (b) the latitude and longitude of sampling areas in degrees, minutes and seconds and a description of the sampling areas sufficient to identify their location;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (c) the dates and times when samples were collected;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (d) the sample sizes;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (e) the results of the data assessment made under section 11 and any supporting raw data;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (f) based on the results referred to in paragraph (e), the identification of any effect on

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (i) the fish population,

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (ii) fish tissue, and

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (iii) the benthic invertebrate community;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (g) if the study design contains the information described in paragraph 4(1)(h), the magnitude and geographical extent of the effect on fish population, fish tissue or the benthic invertebrate community;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (h) the information referred to in sections 9 and 10;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (i) a description of any complaint within the three preceding years to the owner or operator of a mill about fish flavour or odour;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (j) the conclusions of the biological monitoring studies, based on the results of the statistical analysis conducted under paragraph 11(c), taking into account any of the following factors that may have affected those results:

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (i) the results of any previous biological monitoring studies,

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (ii) the presence of anthropogenic, natural or other factors that are not related to the effluent under study and that may reasonably be expected to contribute to any observed effect,

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (iii) any quality assurance or quality control results that may interfere with the reliability of the conclusions, and

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (iv) the exposure to effluent of the fish that were sampled;

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (k) a description of the impact of the results on the study design for subsequent biological monitoring studies; and

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (l) the date of the next biological monitoring studies.

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (2) If a study design is submitted under subsection 4(2), the interpretive report shall consist of only the cause of the effect on fish population, fish tissue or the benthic invertebrate community, and any supporting raw data and, if the cause was not determined, an explanation of why and a description of any steps that need to be taken in the next study to determine that cause.

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (2.1) If a study design is submitted under subsection 4(3), the interpretive report shall consist of only the studies that were used to identify possible solutions to eliminate the effect and the results of those solutions and, if no solutions were identified, an explanation of the reasons why and a description of any steps that need to be taken in the next study to identify the solutions.

heading: Interpretive Report
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(f), if a study on the fish population, on fish tissue or on the benthic invertebrate community is not required to be conducted under these Regulations, the effluent is considered to have no effect on the fish population, on fish tissue or on the benthic invertebrate community, respectively.
