paragraph: (2) A person who is required to publish a notice under section 17 must

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (a) consider any written comments received under subsection (1) that are relevant to the plan or authorization, and

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (b) submit to the district manager

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (i)  a copy of each written comment received under subsection (1), and

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (ii)  a description of any changes made to the plan or request for authorization as a result of the comments received under subsection (1).

heading: Advisory committee
paragraph:
19
		  The minister may establish an advisory committee referred to in section 37 (3) [approval of range use plan or range stewardship plan] of the Act consisting of at least 3 persons including

heading: Advisory committee
paragraph: (a) a person registered as an agrologist under the Professional Governance Act,

heading: Advisory committee
paragraph: (b) a person who holds a range use plan or a range stewardship plan, and

heading: Advisory committee
paragraph: (c) a representative of the government.

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: 20		  A range agreement holder who makes an amendment under section 40 [minor changes to range use plan or range stewardship plan] of the Act must provide the district manager with a copy of the amendment as soon as practicable.

heading: Minor amendment wrongly made
paragraph:
21
		  (1) If the minister determines that a decision made by a range agreement holder under section 40 [minor changes to range use plan or range stewardship plan] of the Act was wrongly made, the minister may

heading: Minor amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (a) declare the amendment to be without effect, and

heading: Minor amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (b) if the minister considers it appropriate, require the holder to suspend operations that are not authorized in the absence of the amendment.

heading: Minor amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (2) A range agreement holder referred to in subsection (1) will not be found to have contravened the Act or this regulation by carrying out, before the minister makes a determination under subsection (1), operations that are not authorized in the absence of the amendment if

heading: Minor amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (a) the minister is satisfied, or

heading: Minor amendment wrongly made
paragraph: (b) the holder establishes that the holder had reason to believe

heading: Minor amendment wrongly made
paragraph: that the amendment would have been approved under section 37 (1) [approval of range use plan or range stewardship plan] of the Act, had the amendment been properly submitted for approval.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph:
22
		  (1) For the purpose of section 38 (5) [mandatory amendments] of the Act, a range agreement holder must prepare and submit to the minister an amendment to the plan to take into account the following circumstances:

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) the establishment or amendment of an objective referred to in Division 2 [Objectives];

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) a change in the holder's agreement under the Range Act;

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (c) notice is given by the minister that an amendment is required in relation to

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (i)  plant communities,

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (ii)  range readiness criteria,

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (iii)  stubble height, or

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (iv)  issues identified by the minister under sections 33 (1) (c) [content of range use plan for grazing], 34 (1) (c) [content of range use plan for hay cutting] or 35 (1) (b) [content of range stewardship plan] of the Act.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (2) Section 13 (2) [content of range use plans] applies to a notice given by the minister under subsection (1) (c) in respect of range readiness criteria.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (3) A range agreement holder who prepares an amendment under section 38 of the Act must obtain the minister's approval of the amendment.

heading: Balancing objectives
paragraph: 23		  On request of a person who submits a range use plan or range stewardship plan for approval, the minister may balance objectives set by government, actions taken under the Government Actions Regulation, results, strategies or other plan content when making a determination under section 37 [approval of range use plan or range stewardship plan] of the Act.

heading: Extending term
paragraph:
24
		  For the purpose of section 36 (2) [term of range use plan and range stewardship plan] of the Act, the minister may extend the term of a range use plan or range stewardship plan if

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (a) the holder of the plan requests an extension, and

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (b) the minister is satisfied that the plan

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (i)  continues to be consistent with objectives set by government and actions taken under the Government Actions Regulation, or

heading: Extending term
paragraph: (ii)  will be amended so as to be consistent with the objectives and actions described in subparagraph (i).

heading: Range readiness
paragraph:
28
		  (1) Despite anything specified in a range use plan or range stewardship plan, a range agreement holder must not graze livestock on Crown range if the range readiness criteria specified in the plan are not met.

heading: Range readiness
paragraph: (2) A range agreement holder must not graze livestock on Crown range before the dates, if any, specified in a range use plan or range stewardship plan, unless

heading: Range readiness
paragraph: (a) written authorization is given by the minister, or

heading: Range readiness
paragraph: (b) the range readiness criteria specified in the range use plan or range stewardship plan are met.

heading: Removal from grazing
paragraph:
29
		  (1) Subject to section 36 [general wildlife measures], if a range agreement holder grazes livestock on an area of Crown range, the holder must remove the livestock on the first to occur of the following:

heading: Removal from grazing
paragraph: (a) the date specified in the holder's range use plan or range stewardship plan for the removal of livestock;

heading: Removal from grazing
paragraph: (b) the average stubble height on the area is the stubble height, if any, that is specified in the holder's plan;

heading: Removal from grazing
paragraph: (c) the average browse use level by livestock on that area is

heading: Removal from grazing
paragraph: (i)  the percentage of the current annual growth specified in the applicable plan, if any, or

heading: Removal from grazing
paragraph: (ii)  25% of the current annual growth, if subparagraph (i) does not apply.

heading: Removal from grazing
paragraph: (2) A range agreement holder who grazes livestock on Crown range must ensure that the grazing of herbaceous plants by the livestock does not occur in a manner that, if continued, will result in deterioration of plant communities located on the grazing area.

heading: Riparian areas
paragraph:
30
		  A range agreement holder must not carry out a range practice if it would result in a material adverse affect on the ability of the riparian area to

heading: Riparian areas
paragraph: (a) withstand normal peak flow events without accelerated soil loss, channel movement or bank movement,

heading: Riparian areas
paragraph: (b) filter runoff,

heading: Riparian areas
paragraph: (c) store and safely release water, and

heading: Riparian areas
paragraph: (d) conserve wildlife habitat values in the area.

heading: Upland areas
paragraph:
31
		  A range agreement holder must not carry out a range practice on an upland area if the range practice would result in a material adverse affect on the upland area by substantially

heading: Upland areas
paragraph: (a) accelerating the rate of soil loss from the area,

heading: Upland areas
paragraph: (b) diminishing infiltration of water on the area,

heading: Upland areas
paragraph: (c) reducing moisture storage on the area, or

heading: Upland areas
paragraph: (d) decreasing stability of the area.

heading: Protection of fish
paragraph:
32
		  (1) A range agreement holder who carries out a range practice must ensure that the range practice is conducted at a time and in a manner that is unlikely to

heading: Protection of fish
paragraph: (a) harm fish,

heading: Protection of fish
paragraph: (b) have a material adverse effect on fish passage, or

heading: Protection of fish
paragraph: (c) destroy, damage or harmfully alter fish habitat.

heading: Protection of fish
paragraph: (2) If satisfied that it is not practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to a particular area, the minister may exempt a range agreement holder, in relation to that area, from subsection (1).

heading: Protecting water quality
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A range agreement holder who carries out a range practice must ensure that the range practice does not cause material that is harmful to human health to be deposited in, or transported to, water that is diverted for human consumption by a licensed waterworks.

heading: Protecting water quality
paragraph: (2) A range agreement holder who carries out a range practice that could have a material adverse effect on a licensed waterworks must ensure that the range practice does not

heading: Protecting water quality
paragraph: (a) damage the licensed waterworks, or

heading: Protecting water quality
paragraph: (b) alter the vegetation, soil or terrain around the licensed waterworks, if the alteration could materially increase the risk of subsequent damage to the licensed waterworks.

heading: Protecting water quality
paragraph: (3) If satisfied that it is not practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to a particular area, the minister may exempt a range agreement holder, in relation to that area, from subsection (1) or (2).

heading: Water quality objective
paragraph:
34
		  (1) By January 1 following the establishment of a water quality objective for an area, a range agreement holder who carries out a range practice in the area must ensure that the range practice is consistent with the objective.

heading: Water quality objective
paragraph: (3) If a range agreement holder knows or ought to know that grazing livestock under the agreement in a portion of an area covered by a water quality objective would be inconsistent with the water quality objective, the holder must

heading: Water quality objective
paragraph: (a) remove the livestock from that portion, and

heading: Water quality objective
paragraph: (b) not allow livestock to enter that portion.

heading: Water quality objective
paragraph: (4) If the minister is satisfied that sufficient measures have been taken to prevent a failure to meet water quality objectives from recurring, the minister may exempt a range agreement holder from the requirement of subsection (3) (b).

heading: Removal of dead livestock
paragraph:
35
		  A range agreement holder must take reasonable steps to ensure that dead livestock belonging to the holder is

heading: Removal of dead livestock
paragraph: (a) not within 100 m of a stream in a community watershed, or

heading: Removal of dead livestock
paragraph: (b) removed to a distance of 100 m or more from a stream in a community watershed as soon as practicable after the holder becomes aware of the dead livestock.

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph:
36
		  (1) By January 1 following the establishment of a general wildlife measure for an area, a range agreement holder who carries out a range practice in the area must ensure that the range practice is consistent with

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (a) the general wildlife measure, or

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (b) a proposal approved under subsection (3).

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (3) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act may exempt a range agreement holder from subsection (1) if

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (a) the holder proposes an alternative to the general wildlife measure, and

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph: (b) that minister is satisfied that the proposed alternative is consistent with the general wildlife measure.

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: 36.1		  (1) By January 1 following the establishment of a general ecological community measure for an area, a range agreement holder who carries out a range practice in the area must ensure that the range practice is consistent with

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: (a) the general ecological community measure, or

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: (b) a proposal approved under subsection (2).

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act may exempt a range agreement holder from subsection (1) if

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: (a) the holder proposes an alternative to the general ecological community measure, and

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph: (b) that minister is satisfied that the proposed alternative is consistent with the general ecological community measure.

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: 37		  (1) A range agreement holder who carries out a range practice must ensure that the range practice does not damage or render ineffective a wildlife habitat feature.

heading: Wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (2) If satisfied that it is not practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to a particular area, the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act may exempt a range agreement holder, in relation to that area, from subsection (1).

heading: Resource features
paragraph: 38		  (1) A range agreement holder who carries out a range practice must ensure that the range practice does not damage or render ineffective a resource feature.

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (2) The minister may exempt a range agreement holder from the requirement of subsection (1), if satisfied that

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (a) there is no other practicable option for carrying out the range practice, and

heading: Resource features
paragraph: (b) the exemption is in the public interest.

heading: Restriction on range developments
paragraph:
39
		  (1) The minister may not grant an authorization under section 51 [range developments] of the Act if the range development is to be constructed within 50 m of a stream in a community watershed, unless satisfied that the construction and use of the range development is consistent with

heading: Restriction on range developments
paragraph: (a) the objective set by government for water as set out in section 8 [objectives set by government for water], and

heading: Restriction on range developments
paragraph: (b) water quality objectives, if any.

heading: Restriction on range developments
paragraph: (2) The minister may not grant an authorization under section 51 of the Act if the range development would alter vegetation, soil or terrain in a manner that, if the range development were a range practice, the person responsible for the range development would contravene section 30 [riparian areas], 31 [upland areas], 32 [protection of fish], 33 (2) [protecting water quality], 37 [wildlife habitat features] or 38 [resource features], unless satisfied that

heading: Restriction on range developments
paragraph: (a) there is no other practicable option for carrying out the construction of the range development, and

heading: Restriction on range developments
paragraph: (b) the vegetation, soil or terrain will be restored after the construction is completed to the extent that the person responsible for the range development would not, if the range development were a range practice, contravene section 30, 31, 32, 33 (2), 37 or 38.

heading: Maintenance of range developments
paragraph:
40
		  (1) A range agreement holder must maintain any range development located on an area that is subject to the agreement in an effective operating condition.

heading: Maintenance of range developments
paragraph: (2) The minister may exempt a range agreement holder from the requirement of subsection (1) if

heading: Maintenance of range developments
paragraph: (a) another person has obtained authorization from the minister under section 51 (2) [range developments] of the Act to maintain the range development,

heading: Maintenance of range developments
paragraph: (b) another person is required to maintain the range development and that person is not exempted under this subsection,

heading: Maintenance of range developments
paragraph: (c) another person has entered into an agreement referred to in section 118 (2) (a.1) [power to enter into agreements] of the Act, or

heading: Maintenance of range developments
paragraph: (d) the minister is satisfied that it is not in the public interest to maintain the range development.

heading: Revegetation
paragraph:
41
		  (1) A person who constructs a range development must ensure that any exposed soil is revegetated with ecologically suitable species within 2 years after the construction is completed.

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (2) The minister may exempt a person from the requirement of subsection (1) if the minister is satisfied that a failure to revegetate is consistent with the objective set by government for soils as set out in section 6 (c) [objectives set by government for soils].

heading: Tagging
paragraph:
42
		  (1) For the purpose of section 45 (2) (b) [general] of the Act, if the minister requires the range agreement holder to tag livestock, the minister must provide the tags to the holder.

heading: Tagging
paragraph: (2) A range agreement holder who is provided with tags under subsection (1) must

heading: Tagging
paragraph: (a) attach the tags to the holder's livestock in a time and in a manner specified by the minister, and

heading: Tagging
paragraph: (b) report the loss of any of the tags to the district manager.

heading: Authorization to cut Crown timber
paragraph:
43
		  For the purpose of section 52 (1) (e) [unauthorized timber harvesting] of the Act, a person is authorized to cut, damage or destroy Crown timber in the course of carrying out activities under

heading: Authorization to cut Crown timber
paragraph: (a) an authorization granted under section 51 [range developments] of the Act, or

heading: Authorization to cut Crown timber
paragraph: (b) a range use plan or range stewardship plan.

heading: Removal of livestock
paragraph:
44
		  (1) A range agreement holder who knows that grazing livestock under the agreement will cause significant interference with the establishment of a free growing stand under section 29 [free growing stands] of the Act, must

heading: Removal of livestock
paragraph: (a) remove the livestock from the area, and

heading: Removal of livestock
paragraph: (b) not allow livestock to enter the area.

heading: Removal of livestock
paragraph: (2) If the minister is satisfied that sufficient measures have been taken to prevent interference with the establishment of a free growing stand from recurring, the minister may exempt a range agreement holder from the requirement of subsection (1) (b).

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph:
45
		  (1) For the purpose of section 77 (1) [power of intervention: general] of the Act, an order given by the minister to a range agreement holder must specify

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph: (a) the measures or actions that must be taken,

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph: (b) the grounds for requiring the measures or action to be taken, and

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph: (c) whether or not the holder may recover all or part of the amount reasonably incurred in taking the specified measures or actions.

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph: (2) The minister may take action under section 77 (1) of the Act if an act or omission of a range agreement holder will likely result in a fundamental and adverse alteration of an ecosystem.

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of section 77 (3) and 77.1 (4) [power of intervention: first nations] of the Act, a range agreement holder may recover all or part of the amount reasonably incurred under that section if

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph: (a) the minister specifies in a notice under subsection (1) that the amount reasonably incurred in taking the required measures or actions is recoverable, and

heading: Intervention orders and payment of expenses
paragraph: (b) the minister is satisfied that the amounts claimed by the holder were, in fact, reasonably incurred.

heading: Annual reports
paragraph:
46
		  On or before December 31, the holder of a range stewardship plan must submit to the district manager a report respecting the following matters that occurred during the grazing season on the area to which the plan relates:

heading: Annual reports
paragraph: (a) the number of livestock released onto Crown range;

heading: Annual reports
paragraph: (b) the period when the livestock referred to in paragraph (a) occupied the Crown range;

heading: Annual reports
paragraph: (c) issues or events that affected or will affect the holder's ability to manage the area for which the plan relates in accordance with the Act, this regulation and the range stewardship plan.

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph:
47
		  (1) For the purposes of sections 67 [seizure of timber, chattels, hay, livestock, etc.] and 68 [forfeiture of livestock] of the Act, if livestock have been seized by an official the minister may sell the livestock

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (a) by public auction, or

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (b) if no bid is received at the public auction, by other means.

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (2) An official or other person who has worked for the government in seizing or selling the livestock may not buy the livestock at a sale under subsection (1).

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (3) Before livestock is sold under subsection (1) (a), the sale must be advertised in a newspaper, and the advertisement must

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (a) describe species, breed, age, colour and sex of the livestock,

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (b) if the livestock are branded, state all legible brands and their locations on the livestock,

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (c) if the livestock are not branded, state that fact and identify the livestock by tags, markings or other features identifying the livestock,

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (d) state the costs incurred for

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (i)  seizure of the livestock,

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (ii)  advertising, and

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (iii)  daily feed and care of the livestock,

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (e) state the name and address of a person from whom additional information may be obtained, and

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (f) state that unless the owner of the livestock in the meantime pays all costs referred to in paragraph (d), the livestock will, on a specified date and at a specified location, be offered for sale by public auction.

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (4) The specified date referred to in subsection (3) (f) must be a minimum of 10 clear days from the date of publication of the advertisement referred to in subsection (3).

heading: Sale of seized livestock
paragraph: (5) The official must make reasonable efforts to determine the identity of the owner of the livestock and notify the owner of the seizure and sale before the sale takes place.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
48
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of the following sections commits an offence:

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 28 [range readiness];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 29 [removal from grazing];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 30 [riparian areas];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 31 [upland areas];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 32 [protection of fish];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 33 [protecting water quality];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 34 (3) (a) and (b) [water quality objective];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 35 [removal of dead livestock];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 36 [general wildlife measures];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 36.1 [general ecological community measures];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 37 [wildlife habitat features];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 38 [resource features];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 40 [maintenance of range developments];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 41 [revegetation];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 42 (2) (a) and (b) [tagging];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 44 (1) (a) and (b) [removal of livestock];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 46 [annual reports].

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who commits an offence described in subsection (1) is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 6 months or to both.

heading: Offences
paragraph: Schedule

heading: Offences
paragraph: Range Readiness Criteria

heading: Offences
paragraph: The range readiness criteria that apply based on the desired plant community and preferred species are:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Range Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorized annual use" means the quantity of forage authorized to be used in a year in a licence or permit, expressed as

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) animal unit months of forage in the case of a grazing licence or grazing permit, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) tonnes of hay in the case of a hay cutting licence or hay cutting permit.

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: 2		  For the purposes of the definition of "animal unit month" in section 1 (1) of the Act, the amount of forage required by

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: (a) a yearling of the genus bos is 0.7 of an animal unit month,

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: (b) a bull of the genus bos is 1.5 animal unit months,

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: (c) a cow of the genus bos, by herself or together with her unweaned calf is one animal unit month,

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: (d) a horse is 1.25 animal unit months,

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: (e) a sheep is 0.2 of an animal unit month,

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: (f) a llama is 0.2 of an animal unit month, and

heading: Animal unit month
paragraph: (g) an alpaca is 0.1 of an animal unit month.

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph:
3
		  (1) The manner of giving public notice under section 9 (3) or 18 (3) of the Act of an invitation for applications for a licence or permit is

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (a) by advertisement in at least one issue of at least one newspaper circulating in or near the area proposed for the licence or permit, or

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (b) if there is no newspaper circulating as described in paragraph (a), by giving notice in one or more of the following ways:

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (i)  on a minister's ministry public computer bulletin board;

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (ii)  posted in a public place;

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (iii)  by radio or television broadcast received in or near the area proposed for the licence or permit.

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (2) An advertisement or notice referred to in subsection (1) must

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (a) contain an informal description of the Crown range proposed for the licence or permit and of the rights to be conferred by the licence or permit,

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (b) specify an address or place where persons may obtain details of the licence or permit and the application process, and

heading: Notice of application for licences and permits under section 9 or 18 of the Act
paragraph: (c) include an address to which applications or comments may be delivered, and the date and time by which they must be received in order to be considered.

heading: Applications for licence or permit in response to an invitation
paragraph:
4
		  Applications under section 9 of the Act for licences or permits, respectively, in conjunction with an invitation for applications under section 9 of the Act

heading: Applications for licence or permit in response to an invitation
paragraph: (a) may be made in writing or in electronic form and submitted to the minister, and

heading: Applications for licence or permit in response to an invitation
paragraph: (b) must contain or be accompanied by information required by the minister that the minister considers necessary for

heading: Applications for licence or permit in response to an invitation
paragraph: (i)  ascertaining the applicant's eligibility, and

heading: Applications for licence or permit in response to an invitation
paragraph: (ii)  evaluating the application,

heading: Applications for licence or permit in response to an invitation
paragraph: by reference to the criteria used under section 10 of the Act for the purpose of the invitation.

heading: Application for licence or permit by direct award - no public notice required
paragraph:
5
		  (1) An application under section 16 (1) of the Act for a licence in any of the circumstances referred to in that provision

heading: Application for licence or permit by direct award - no public notice required
paragraph: (a) may be made in writing or in electronic form and submitted to the minister, and

heading: Application for licence or permit by direct award - no public notice required
paragraph: (b) must contain or be accompanied by information required by the minister that the minister considers relevant, given the circumstances that, under paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d) or (e) of that provision, are applicable to the application.

heading: Application for licence or permit by direct award - no public notice required
paragraph: (2) An application under section 16 (2) or (4) of the Act for a permit

heading: Application for licence or permit by direct award - no public notice required
paragraph: (a) may be made in writing or in electronic form and submitted to the minister, and

heading: Application for licence or permit by direct award - no public notice required
paragraph: (b) must contain or be accompanied by information required by the minister that the minister considers relevant to the grazing permit or hay cutting permit applied for.

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph:
6
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: "company" has the same meaning as in the Business Corporations Act;

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: "extraprovincial company" has the same meaning as in the Business Corporations Act;

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: "society" has the same meaning as in the Societies Act.

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of paragraph (b) of the definition of "representative" in section 17 (1) of the Act, the minister must be satisfied that the person or other legal entity is

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (a) a company or an extraprovincial company that meets the requirements set out in subsection (3) of this section, or

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (b) a society that meets the requirements set out in subsection (4) of this section.

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2) (a), the first nation referred to in section 17 (1) (a) of the Act must own sufficient voting shares in the company or extraprovincial company to

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (a) elect more than 50% of the effective directors of that company or extraprovincial company, or

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (b) otherwise effectively control the operations and direction of that company or extraprovincial company.

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (2) (b),

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (a) holding a grazing or hay cutting permit or licence must be one of the purposes of the society, and

heading: Representative - direct award to or in respect of a first nation
paragraph: (b) the society must not be prohibited under section 2 (2) of the Societies Act from holding a grazing or hay cutting permit or licence.

heading: Application for special purpose licence or permit by direct award - public notice required
paragraph: 7		  (1) An application under section 18 (2) of the Act for a licence or permit

heading: Application for special purpose licence or permit by direct award - public notice required
paragraph: (a) may be made in writing or in electronic form and submitted to the minister, and

heading: Application for special purpose licence or permit by direct award - public notice required
paragraph: (b) must contain or be accompanied by information required by the minister that the minister considers appropriate in relation to

heading: Application for special purpose licence or permit by direct award - public notice required
paragraph: (i)  the ancillary, compensatory or exchange licence or permit that is the subject of the application, or

paragraph: 2 The power that is conferred by subsection 36(5.2) of the Act may be exercised by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans in relation to aquaculture, to aquatic species that are a pest to a fishery or to aquatic invasive species, if the following conditions are met:

heading: Aquaculture, pests and invasive species
paragraph: (a) the Minister is satisfied that the Regulations are required for the proper management and control of fisheries or the conservation and protection of fish; and

heading: Aquaculture, pests and invasive species

paragraph: (i) is a drug whose sale is permitted or otherwise authorized, or whose importation is not prohibited, under the Food and Drugs Act,

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: 3 The power that is conferred by subsection 36(5.2) of the Act may be exercised by the Minister of the Environment in relation to research activities if the persons authorized by the Regulations to deposit deleterious substances have processes in place or are subject to processes

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (a) to verify that

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (i) the research activities will contribute to the development of knowledge for the purpose of managing, conserving, protecting or restoring fish populations or waters frequented by fish,

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (ii) the research activities will be conducted under the supervision of a person who has expertise in conducting aquatic research under similar conditions, as evidenced by a substantial and relevant peer-reviewed publication record,

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (iii) the research activities will be designed so as to

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (A) avoid harmful effects on fish, fish habitat and the use by man of fish, other than the effects that are necessary to achieve results that are scientifically valid, and

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (B) confine any harmful effects on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish to the waters in respect of which the deposit is authorized, and

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (iv) if research activities render any waters frequented by fish unsuitable to sustain fish populations or render fish populations unsuitable for human consumption, no later than 20 years following the day on which the research activities are completed, the waters will be suitable to sustain fish populations and the fish populations will be suitable for human consumption;

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (b) to evaluate whether the research activities will be carried out in accordance with their design and to document any deviations from that design; and

heading: Aquatic research
paragraph: (c) to make research findings available to the public.

heading: Other subject matters
paragraph: 4 The power that is conferred by subsection 36(5.2) of the Act may be exercised by the Minister of the Environment in relation to any other subject matter if the following conditions are met:

heading: Other subject matters
paragraph: (a) the deleterious substance to be deposited, its deposit or the work, undertaking or activity that results in the deposit is authorized under federal or provincial law, or is subject to guidelines issued by the federal or provincial government, and is subject to an enforcement or compliance regime;

heading: Other subject matters
paragraph: (b) the federal or provincial law or guidelines set out conditions that result in a deposit that is not acutely lethal and contains a quantity or concentration of deleterious substance that when measured in the deposit, or in the relevant waters frequented by fish, satisfies

heading: Other subject matters
paragraph: (i) the recommendations of the Canadian Water Quality Guidelines for the Protection of Aquatic Life that were published in 1999 by the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment, as amended from time to time, or the recommendations that were derived from those guidelines on their site-specific application, as amended from time to time, or

heading: Other subject matters
paragraph: (ii) the recommendations of any peer-reviewed guidelines that are established for the purpose of protecting aquatic life and adopted by a federal or provincial body; and

heading: Other subject matters
paragraph: (c) the effects of such a deposit on fish, fish habitat and the use by man of fish have been evaluated in accordance with generally accepted standards of good scientific practice.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "foreshore" means land in tidal or non-tidal areas that, as a result of the rise and fall of the sea or water in an estuary or stream between the natural boundary and the ordinary low water mark, is periodically covered by salt water or fresh water and periodically exposed;

heading: How to calculate total waste discharge
paragraph:
2
		  (1) The total waste discharge for a project is the quantity of waste that is permitted under the Environmental Management Act to be discharged from the project.

heading: How to calculate total waste discharge
paragraph: (2) The total waste discharge for a project is calculated by adding the products obtained by multiplying the CWF for each permitted contaminant by the permitted discharge rate, in tonnes or other unit of measurement specified in Appendix 1, for that contaminant.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In the Act and this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "development" includes the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the addition, removal or alteration of soil, vegetation or a building or other structure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) without limiting paragraph (a), the addition, removal or alteration of works and services described in section 506 (1) [subdivision serving requirements] of the Local Government Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) subdivision as defined in section 455 [definitions in relation to Part 14] of the Local Government Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "natural features, functions and conditions" includes the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) large organic debris that falls in or around streams, including logs, snags and root wads;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) areas for channel migration, including active floodplains;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) side channels, intermittent streams, seasonally wetted contiguous areas and floodplains;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the multi-canopied forest and ground cover adjacent to streams that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  moderate water temperatures,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  provide a source of food, nutrients and organic matter to streams,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  establish root matrices that stabilize soils and stream banks, thereby minimizing erosion, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iv)  buffer streams from sedimentation and pollution in surface runoff;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a natural source of stream bed substrates;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) permeable surfaces that permit infiltration to moderate water volume, timing and velocity and maintain sustained water flows in streams, especially during low flow periods.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Riparian Areas Protection Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "active floodplain", in relation to a stream, means land that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) adjacent to the stream,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) inundated by the 1 in 5 year return period flow of the stream, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) capable of supporting plant species that are typical of inundated or saturated soil conditions and distinct from plant species on freely drained upland sites adjacent to the land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "allowable footprint" has the meaning given to it in section 11 (3) [undue hardship];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "area of human disturbance" means an area that is subject to enduring disturbance as a result of human occupation or activity and includes, without limitation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) footprints of buildings and other structures,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) areas where soil or vegetation has been added, removed or altered, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) without limiting paragraphs (a) and (b), the following areas:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  areas modified for agricultural use, including, without limitation, for crops, pasture, range, hayfields and normal farm practices;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  areas that are or have been used for resource extraction and have not been restored to their natural conditions;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  areas occupied by invasive plant species to an extent that precludes the unassisted reestablishment of native plant species;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assessment" means an assessment under section 12 [assessments];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "assessment report" means a report under section 14 [assessment reports];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "detailed assessment" means an assessment referred to in section 13 (b) [simple and detailed assessments];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "developable area", in relation to a site, means the area of the site other than

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the streamside protection and enhancement area, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the naturally and legally restricted areas of the site;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish habitat" means water frequented by fish and any other areas on which fish depend directly or indirectly to carry out their life processes, including spawning grounds and nursery, rearing, food supply and migration areas;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "footprint", in relation to a building or other structure, means the area covered by

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the structure, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a projection from the structure, whether or not the projection is in contact with the ground;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "legally restricted area", in relation to a site, means the area of the site that is unavailable for development because of restrictions imposed or rights granted under an enactment, including, without limitation, easements, rights of way, setback requirements and restrictive covenants;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local trust area" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Islands Trust Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "local trust committee" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Islands Trust Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "measure" has the meaning given to it in section 16 (b) [recommended measures];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "naturally restricted area", in relation to a site, means the area of the site that is unavailable for development because of natural features that preclude development;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "normal farm practice" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "parcel" means a lot, block or other area in which land is held or into which land is subdivided;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "planning and land use area",

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to a local government other than a local trust committee, means the area over which the local government has authority under section 456 [area of authority for municipalities and regional districts] of the Local Government Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to a local trust committee, means the local trust area or other part of the trust area in respect of which the local trust committee is a local trust committee;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "primary qualified environmental professional" has the meaning given to it in section 20 [primary qualified environmental professionals];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protected fish" means all life stages of

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) salmonids,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) game fish, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) fish that are listed in Schedule 1, 2 or 3 of the Species at Risk Act (Canada);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualified environmental professional" has the meaning given to it in section 21 [qualified environmental professionals];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ravine" means a narrow, steep-sided valley that is typically eroded by running water and has a slope grade greater than 3:1;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian assessment area" means the area around a stream that is determined in accordance with section 8 [riparian assessment area];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian development" means a development to which this regulation applies under section 3 [application to developments];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian protection standard" has the meaning given to it in section 10 [riparian protection standard];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "simple assessment" means an assessment referred to in section 13 (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "site", in relation to a proposed development, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the parcel on which the development is proposed to occur, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) if the development is proposed to occur on a strata lot, the strata lot;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "strata lot" has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) of the Strata Property Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a watercourse or body of water, whether or not usually containing water, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any of the following that is connected by surface flow to a watercourse or body of water referred to in paragraph (a):

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a ditch, whether or not usually containing water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a spring, whether or not usually containing water;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  a wetland;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream boundary", in relation to a stream, means whichever of the following is farther from the centre of the stream:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the visible high water mark of a stream where the presence and action of the water are so common and usual, and so long continued in all ordinary years, as to mark on the soil of the bed of the stream a character distinct from that of its banks, in vegetation, as well as in the nature of the soil itself;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the boundary of the active floodplain, if any, of the stream;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "streamside protection and enhancement area" has the meaning given to it in section 9 [streamside protection and enhancement area];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "streamside vegetation", in relation to a stream, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) riparian vegetation, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) upland vegetation that exerts an influence on the stream;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "subdivision" has the same meaning as in section 455 [definitions in relation to Part 14] of the Local Government Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "technical manual" means a manual published under section 13.1 (1) [technical manuals] of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "top of a ravine bank" means the first significant break in a ravine slope where

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the grade beyond the break is less than 3:1 for a minimum distance of 15 m measured perpendicularly from the break, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the break does not include a bench within the ravine that could be developed;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "trust area" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Islands Trust Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "undue hardship" has the meaning given to it in section 11;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wetland" means land that is inundated or saturated by surface water or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support, and that under normal conditions does support, plant species that are typical of inundated or saturated soil conditions, including swamps, marshes, bogs, fens, estuaries and similar areas that are not part of the active floodplain of a stream.

heading: Directive to local governments
paragraph: 4		  (1) This section is a directive under section 12 (1) [provincial directives on streamside protection] of the Act.

heading: Directive to local governments
paragraph: (2) A local government must have in force zoning or land use bylaws that ensure that a riparian development is subject to one of the following schemes:

heading: Directive to local governments

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister
paragraph:

		  (1) A qualified environmental professional may submit an assessment report to the minister in the manner and form required by the minister.

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister
paragraph: (2) On receiving an assessment report under subsection (1), the minister may

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister
paragraph: (a) provide a copy of the report to a local government, or

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister

heading: Administration of assessment reports by minister

heading: Riparian assessment area
paragraph:
8
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the riparian assessment area for a stream consists of a 30 m strip on each side of the stream, measured from the stream boundary.

heading: Riparian assessment area
paragraph: (2) If a stream is in a ravine, the riparian assessment area for the stream consists of the following areas, as applicable:

heading: Riparian assessment area
paragraph: (a) if the ravine is less than 60 m wide, a strip on each side of the stream that is measured from the stream boundary to a point that is 30 m beyond the top of the ravine bank;

heading: Riparian assessment area
paragraph: (b) if the ravine is 60 or more metres wide, a strip on each side of the stream that is measured from the stream boundary to a point that is 10 m beyond the top of the ravine bank.

heading: Streamside protection and enhancement area
paragraph:
9
		  (1) The streamside protection and enhancement area for a stream is the portion of the riparian assessment area for the stream that

heading: Streamside protection and enhancement area
paragraph: (a) includes the land, adjacent to the stream boundary, that

heading: Streamside protection and enhancement area
paragraph: (i)  links aquatic to terrestrial ecosystems, and

heading: Streamside protection and enhancement area
paragraph: (ii)  is capable of supporting streamside vegetation, and

heading: Streamside protection and enhancement area
paragraph: (b) in the case of a simple assessment, extends far enough upland from the stream that development outside the streamside protection and enhancement area will not result in any harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of natural features, functions and conditions in the area referred to in paragraph (a) that support the life processes of protected fish.

heading: Streamside protection and enhancement area
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1) (a) (ii), an area of human disturbance must be considered to be capable of supporting streamside vegetation if the area would be capable of supporting streamside vegetation were the area in a natural condition.

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph:
10
		  (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), a proposed development meets the riparian protection standard if the development

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (a) will not occur in the streamside protection and enhancement area, and

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (b) in the case of a detailed assessment, will not result in any harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of natural features, functions and conditions in the streamside protection and enhancement area that support the life processes of protected fish.

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), a proposed development on a site that is subject to undue hardship meets the riparian protection standard if

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (a) the development

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (i)  will not occur in the streamside protection and enhancement area, other than in a part of that area that is already an area of human disturbance,

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (ii)  will be situated and otherwise designed so as to minimize any encroachment into the streamside protection and enhancement area, and

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (iii)  in the case of a detailed assessment, will not result in any harmful alteration, disruption or destruction of natural features, functions and conditions in the streamside protection and enhancement area that support the life processes of protected fish, and

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (b) the areas of human disturbance on the site after the development is complete will not exceed the allowable footprint for the site.

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (3) Subsections (1) and (2) (a) do not require

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (a) a building or other structure that exists before the development occurs to be removed, if the structure will remain on its existing foundation and within its existing footprint, or

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (b) any other area of human disturbance that exists before the development occurs to be returned or allowed to return to a natural condition, if the area will not be extended and the type of the disturbance will not be changed.

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (4) A proposed development that involves a subdivision of a parcel or strata lot does not meet the riparian protection standard if the subdivision would create

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (a) a parcel that has a developable area that is less than the allowable footprint for that parcel, or

heading: Riparian protection standard
paragraph: (b) a strata lot that has a developable area that is less than the allowable footprint for that strata lot.

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph:
11
		  (1) In this section, "variance" means any of the following:

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (a) a variance that a board of variance may order to be permitted under section 542 [board powers on application] of the Local Government Act;

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (b) a variance that a local government may permit under section 498 [development variance permits] of the Local Government Act;

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (c) an amendment to a zoning bylaw.

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (2) A site is subject to undue hardship for the purposes of this regulation if

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (a) the site was created by subdivision in accordance with the laws in force in British Columbia at the time the site was created,

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (b) the developer has sought and received a decision on every variance that would reduce the legally restricted area of the site, and

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (c) the developable area of the site is less than the allowable footprint for the site.

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (3) The allowable footprint for a site subject to undue hardship is the following:

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (a) if the area of human disturbance on the site is less than or equal to 70% of the area of the site, the allowable footprint is 30% of the area of the site;

heading: Undue hardship
paragraph: (b) if the area of human disturbance on the site is greater than 70% of the area of the site, the allowable footprint is 40%.

heading: Assessments
paragraph: 12		  An assessment of a proposed development for the purposes of this regulation must be carried out

heading: Assessments
paragraph: (a) by one or more qualified environmental professionals, and

heading: Assessments
paragraph: (b) in accordance with

heading: Assessments
paragraph: (i)  section 13, and

heading: Assessments
paragraph: (ii)  the technical manuals.

heading: Simple and detailed assessments
paragraph:
13
		  An assessment must determine the streamside protection and enhancement area for a stream, in accordance with the technical manuals, using one of the following methods:

heading: Simple and detailed assessments
paragraph: (a) a method based on measurement from the stream boundary or, if the stream is in a ravine, from the top of the ravine bank;

heading: Simple and detailed assessments
paragraph: (b) a method based on the location of natural features, functions and conditions that support the life processes of protected fish.

heading: Assessment reports
paragraph:
14
		  An assessment report must be prepared

heading: Assessment reports
paragraph: (a) by or under the direction of a primary qualified environmental professional, and

heading: Assessment reports
paragraph: (b) in accordance with

heading: Assessment reports
paragraph: (i)  sections 15 to 19, and

heading: Assessment reports
paragraph: (ii)  the technical manuals.

heading: Description of assessment
paragraph:
15
		  (1) An assessment report must include

heading: Description of assessment
paragraph: (a) a description of the assessment activities carried out, and

heading: Description of assessment
paragraph: (b) a description of the results of the assessment.

heading: Description of assessment
paragraph: (2) A description under subsection (1) (b) must identify, in accordance with the technical manuals,

heading: Description of assessment
paragraph: (a) the riparian assessment area,

heading: Description of assessment
paragraph: (b) the streamside protection and enhancement area, and

heading: Description of assessment
paragraph: (c) in the case of a detailed assessment, any potential hazards posed by the proposed development to natural features, functions or conditions in the streamside protection and enhancement area that support the life processes of protected fish.

heading: Recommended measures
paragraph:
16
		  For each potential hazard identified under section 15 (2) (c), if applicable, an assessment report must

heading: Recommended measures
paragraph: (a) explain how the design of the proposed development will avoid the hazard, or

heading: Recommended measures
paragraph: (b) recommend measures to be taken to avoid the hazard.

heading: Opinion on development
paragraph:
17
		  An assessment report must set out the opinion of the primary qualified environmental professional by or under whose direction the report was prepared as to

heading: Opinion on development
paragraph: (a) whether the site of the proposed development is subject to undue hardship, and

heading: Opinion on development
paragraph: (b) whether the proposed development will meet the riparian protection standard if the development proceeds as proposed in the report and complies with the measures, if any, recommended in the report.

heading: Supporting information
paragraph:
18
		  (1) In this section, "contact details", in relation to a person, means the street address, mailing address, telephone number and, if any, email address of the person.

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), an assessment report must include the following information:

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (a) the legal name and contact details of the primary qualified environmental professional by or under whose direction the report was prepared;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (b) the legal name and contact details of every other qualified environmental professional who participated in carrying out the report;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (c) the following information about each individual named under paragraph (a) or (b):

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (i)  the profession of the individual under section 21 (2) (a) [qualified environmental professionals];

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (ii)  the professional association under section 21 (2) (b) for that profession and the number by which the individual is identified by that professional association;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (iii)  if the individual carried out functions in relation to the assessment or report as the employee of a company, the legal name of the company;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (iv)  with respect to the primary qualified environmental professional, whether the individual has taken and achieved a passing grade on a course of study referred to in section 20 (b) [primary qualified environmental professionals];

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (d) the legal name and contact details of the proponent of the proposed development;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (e) the following information about the proposed development:

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (i)  whether the development is a residential, commercial or industrial development;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (ii)  whether the development is a new development or a change to an existing development;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (iii)  the location of the development, set out as a street address, legal description and longitude and latitude;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (iv)  the names of the local governments in whose planning and land use areas the development is proposed to occur;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (v)  the code for the watershed in which the development is proposed to occur;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (vi)  for each riparian assessment area in which development is proposed to occur,

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (A) the official name of the affected stream or, if there is not an official name, a legal description of that stream, and

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (B) the length of the affected portion of the affected stream;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (vii)  the proposed start and completion dates for the development;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (f) final and complete design drawings for the proposed development;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (g) a clear and legible plan of the site of the proposed development that shows all of the following in accordance with the technical manuals:

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (i)  the riparian assessment area;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (ii)  the streamside protection and enhancement area;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (iii)  in the case of a detailed assessment, the areas in which natural features, functions and conditions that support the life processes of protected fish occur;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (iv)  an outline of the proposed development and any existing areas of human disturbance on the site;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (h) in the case of a detailed assessment, an orthophoto labelled as required by the technical manuals;

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (i) a plan to monitor the development, during construction, for the purposes of ensuring that the development is proceeding as proposed in the report and in accordance with any measures recommended in the report.

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (3) The following provisions do not apply in relation to a development that consists only in the subdivision of a parcel or strata lot:

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (a) subsection (2) (e) (ii) and (vii);

heading: Supporting information
paragraph: (b) subsection (2) (i).

heading: Signed statements
paragraph:
19
		  (1) An assessment report must include the following statements:

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (a) a statement of the primary qualified environmental professional by or under whose direction the report was prepared that

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (i)  the professional is qualified under section 20 to serve as a primary qualified environmental professional in relation to the assessment and report,

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (ii)  if the professional prepared part of the report, the professional is qualified under section 21 (2) to serve as a qualified environmental professional in relation to that part,

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (iii)  each other qualified environmental professional, if any, who carried out a part of the assessment is qualified under section 21 (2) to serve as a qualified environmental professional in relation to that part,

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (iv)  the assessment was carried out in accordance with section 12 [assessments], and

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (v)  the report was prepared in accordance with section 14 [assessment reports] and is complete;

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (b) a statement of each other qualified environmental professional, if any, who carried out a part of the assessment that

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (i)  the professional is qualified under section 21 (2) to serve as a qualified environmental professional in relation to that part,

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (ii)  the assessment as it relates to that part was carried out in accordance with section 12, and

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (iii)  the report as it relates to that part was prepared in accordance with section 14 and is complete;

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (c) if the developer is an individual, a statement of the developer that the developer has read the report;

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (d) if the developer is a corporation, a statement of an individual who is a director or officer of the corporation that the individual has read the report.

heading: Signed statements
paragraph: (2) A statement under subsection (1) must be signed by the person required to make the statement.

heading: Primary qualified environmental professionals
paragraph:
20
		  An individual may serve as a primary qualified environmental professional for the purposes of this regulation if the individual

heading: Primary qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (a) is a qualified environmental professional, and

heading: Primary qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (b) has completed and achieved a passing grade on a course of study, approved by the minister, relating to assessments and assessment reports.

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (2) An individual may serve as a qualified environmental professional for the purposes of carrying out part of an assessment under this regulation if

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (a) the individual is registered under the Professional Governance Act as any of the following professionals:

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (i)  an agrologist;

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (ii)  an applied science technologist or certified technician;

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (iii)  a registered professional biologist or registered biology technologist;

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (iv)  a professional engineer or professional licensee engineering;

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (v)  a professional forester or registered forest technologist;

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (vi)  a professional geoscientist or professional licensee geoscience,

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (b) the individual is in good standing with the regulatory body under that Act for the individual's profession, and

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (c) when carrying out that part of the assessment, the individual is acting

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (i)  within the individual's area of expertise,

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (ii)  within the scope of professional practice for the individual's profession, and

heading: Qualified environmental professionals
paragraph: (iii)  under the code of ethics of the regulatory body referred to in paragraph (b) and is subject to disciplinary action by that regulatory body.

heading: Strategies for monitoring, education and enforcement
paragraph: 22		  A local government must cooperate with the minister, and the federal Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, in developing strategies in relation to

heading: Strategies for monitoring, education and enforcement
paragraph: (a) monitoring and reporting on the effect of developments on riparian areas,

heading: Strategies for monitoring, education and enforcement
paragraph: (b) public education respecting the protection of riparian areas, and

heading: Strategies for monitoring, education and enforcement
paragraph: (c) the implementation of and compliance with recommendations in an assessment report.

heading: Transition - former regulations
paragraph:
23
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Transition - former regulations
paragraph: "2001 regulation" means the Streamside Protection Regulation, B.C. Reg. 10/2001;

heading: Transition - former regulations
paragraph: "2004 regulation" means the Riparian Areas Regulation, B.C. Reg. 376/2004.

heading: Transition - former regulations
paragraph: (2) This regulation does not apply in relation to a development that is proposed to occur in a riparian assessment area for a stream if

heading: Transition - former regulations

paragraph: (i)  in the case of amendments made on or after March 31, 2005 and before November 1, 2019, the resulting streamside protection and enhancement area was determined in accordance with the 2004 regulation;

paragraph:
24
		  (1) In this section:

paragraph: 1		  In this regulation, "Act" means the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Species at Risk Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 (1) The definitions in this subsection apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: action plan means an action plan included in the public registry under subsection 50(3) and includes any amendment to it included in the public registry under section 52. (plan d'action)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: alternative measures means measures, other than judicial proceedings, that are used to deal with a person who is alleged to have committed an offence. (mesures de rechange)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aquatic species means a wildlife species that is a fish, as defined in section 2 of the Fisheries Act, or a marine plant, as defined in section 47 of that Act. (espece aquatique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Attorney General means the Attorney General of Canada or, for the purposes of sections 108 to 113, an agent of the Attorney General of Canada. (procureur general)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council means the Council referred to in subsection 7(1). (Conseil canadien pour la conservation des especes en peril)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: competent minister means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency with respect to individuals in or on federal lands administered by that Agency;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans with respect to aquatic species, other than individuals mentioned in paragraph (a); and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the Minister of the Environment with respect to all other individuals. (ministre competent)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: conveyance means a vehicle, aircraft or water-borne craft or any other contrivance that is used to move persons or goods. (moyen de transport)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: COSEWIC means the Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada established by section 14. (COSEPAC)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: critical habitat means the habitat that is necessary for the survival or recovery of a listed wildlife species and that is identified as the species' critical habitat in the recovery strategy or in an action plan for the species. (habitat essentiel)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: emergency order means an order made under section 80. (decret d'urgence)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: endangered species means a wildlife species that is facing imminent extirpation or extinction. (espece en voie de disparition)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: extirpated species means a wildlife species that no longer exists in the wild in Canada, but exists elsewhere in the wild. (espece disparue du pays)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: federal land means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) land that belongs to Her Majesty in right of Canada, or that Her Majesty in right of Canada has the power to dispose of, and all waters on and airspace above that land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the internal waters of Canada and the territorial sea of Canada; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) reserves and any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band under the Indian Act, and all waters on and airspace above those reserves and lands. (territoire domanial)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: habitat means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in respect of aquatic species, spawning grounds and nursery, rearing, food supply, migration and any other areas on which aquatic species depend directly or indirectly in order to carry out their life processes, or areas where aquatic species formerly occurred and have the potential to be reintroduced; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in respect of other wildlife species, the area or type of site where an individual or wildlife species naturally occurs or depends on directly or indirectly in order to carry out its life processes or formerly occurred and has the potential to be reintroduced. (habitat)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: individual means an individual of a wildlife species, whether living or dead, at any developmental stage and includes larvae, embryos, eggs, sperm, seeds, pollen, spores and asexual propagules. (individu)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: land claims agreement means a land claims agreement within the meaning of section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982. (accord sur des revendications territoriales)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: List means the List of Wildlife Species at Risk set out in Schedule 1. (liste)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: listed means listed on the List. (inscrite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of the Environment. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: offence means an offence under this Act. (infraction)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: provincial minister means any minister of the government of a province who is responsible for the conservation and management of a wildlife species in that province. (ministre provincial)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: public registry means the registry established under section 120. (registre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: recovery strategy means a recovery strategy included in the public registry under subsection 43(2), and includes any amendment to it included in the public registry under section 45. (programme de retablissement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: residence means a dwelling-place, such as a den, nest or other similar area or place, that is occupied or habitually occupied by one or more individuals during all or part of their life cycles, including breeding, rearing, staging, wintering, feeding or hibernating. (residence)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sell includes to offer for sale or lease, have in possession for sale or lease or deliver for sale or lease. (vente)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: species at risk means an extirpated, endangered or threatened species or a species of special concern. (espece en peril)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: species of special concern means a wildlife species that may become a threatened or an endangered species because of a combination of biological characteristics and identified threats. (espece preoccupante)
