heading: Definitions
paragraph: status report means a report, prepared in accordance with the requirements of regulations made under subsection 21(2), that contains a summary of the best available information on the status of a wildlife species, including scientific knowledge, community knowledge and aboriginal traditional knowledge. (rapport de situation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: territorial minister means any minister of the government of a territory who is responsible for the conservation and management of a wildlife species in that territory. (ministre territorial)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: threatened species means a wildlife species that is likely to become an endangered species if nothing is done to reverse the factors leading to its extirpation or extinction. (espece menacee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: treaty means a treaty within the meaning of section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982. (traite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: wildlife management board means any board or other body established under a land claims agreement that is authorized by the agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species. (conseil de gestion des ressources fauniques)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: wildlife species means a species, subspecies, variety or geographically or genetically distinct population of animal, plant or other organism, other than a bacterium or virus, that is wild by nature and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is native to Canada; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has extended its range into Canada without human intervention and has been present in Canada for at least 50 years. (espece sauvage)

heading: Deeming
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of the definition wildlife species in subsection (1), a species, subspecies, variety or geographically or genetically distinct population is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, presumed to have been present in Canada for at least 50 years.

heading: Competent minister
paragraph: (3) A reference to a competent minister in any provision of this Act is to be read as a reference to the competent minister in respect of the wildlife species, or the individuals of the wildlife species, to which the provision relates.

heading: Sedentary living organisms
paragraph: 4 (1) This Act also applies to sedentary living organisms on or under the continental shelf of Canada outside the exclusive economic zone.

heading: Sedentary living organisms
paragraph: Meaning of sedentary

heading: Sedentary living organisms
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), a living organism is sedentary if it is, at the harvestable stage, either immobile on or under the seabed or is unable to move except in constant physical contact with the seabed or subsoil.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 5 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Purposes
paragraph: 6 The purposes of this Act are to prevent wildlife species from being extirpated or becoming extinct, to provide for the recovery of wildlife species that are extirpated, endangered or threatened as a result of human activity and to manage species of special concern to prevent them from becoming endangered or threatened.

heading: Composition
paragraph: 7 (1) The Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council consists of the Minister of the Environment, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and ministers of the government of a province or a territory who are responsible for the conservation and management of a wildlife species in that province or territory.

heading: Role
paragraph: (2) The role of the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council is to

heading: Role
paragraph: (a) provide general direction on the activities of COSEWIC, the preparation of recovery strategies and the preparation and implementation of action plans; and

heading: Role
paragraph: (b) coordinate the activities of the various governments represented on the Council relating to the protection of species at risk.

heading: Responsibility of Minister
paragraph: 8 (1) The Minister is responsible for the administration of this Act, except in so far as this Act gives responsibility to another minister.

heading: Delegation
paragraph: (2) The Minister, the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, after consultation with the other two ministers, delegate to any minister of the Crown in right of Canada or of a province or to any person who is employed by the Government of Canada, the government of a province or any other government in Canada any of that Minister's powers or functions under this Act, relating to its enforcement.

heading: Agreement and reporting obligation
paragraph: (3) The delegation must be the subject of an agreement between the delegating minister and the delegate and the agreement must provide that the delegate is to prepare an annual report for the delegating minister on the activities undertaken under the agreement. A copy of the agreement must be included in the public registry within 45 days after it is entered into, and a copy of every annual report must be included in the public registry within 45 days after it is received by the delegating minister.

heading: National Aboriginal Council on Species at Risk
paragraph: 8.1 The Minister shall establish a Council, to be known as the National Aboriginal Council on Species at Risk, consisting of six representatives of the aboriginal peoples of Canada selected by the Minister based upon recommendations from aboriginal organizations that the Minister considers appropriate. The role of the Council is to

heading: National Aboriginal Council on Species at Risk
paragraph: (a) advise the Minister on the administration of this Act; and

heading: National Aboriginal Council on Species at Risk
paragraph: (b) provide advice and recommendations to the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council.

heading: Advisory committees to assist Minister
paragraph: 9 (1) The Minister may, after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, establish one or more committees to advise the Minister on the administration of this Act.

heading: Advisory committees to assist Council
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans and the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council, establish one or more committees to advise the Council on matters related to the Council's role.

heading: Administrative agreements
paragraph: 10 A competent minister may, after consultation with every other competent minister, enter into an agreement with any government in Canada, organization or wildlife management board with respect to the administration of any provision of this Act for which that competent minister has responsibility, including the preparation and implementation of recovery strategies, action plans and management plans.

heading: Stewardship action plan
paragraph: 10.1 The Minister, after consultation with the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council, may establish a stewardship action plan that creates incentives and other measures to support voluntary stewardship actions taken by any government in Canada, organization or person. A copy of the stewardship action plan must be included in the public registry.

heading: Contents
paragraph: 10.2 The stewardship action plan must include, but is not limited to, commitments to

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) regularly examine incentives and programs that support actions taken by persons to protect species at risk;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) provide information and increase public awareness about species at risk;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) methods for sharing information about species at risk, including community and aboriginal traditional knowledge, that respect, preserve and maintain knowledge and promote their wider application with the approval of the holders of such knowledge, with other governments and persons;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) create awards and recognition programs;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) provide information respecting programs related to stewardship agreements, land conservation easements and other such agreements; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (f) provide information relating to the technical and scientific support available to persons engaged in stewardship activities.

heading: Conservation agreements - species at risk
paragraph: 11 (1) A competent minister may, after consultation with every other competent minister, and with the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council or any of its members if he or she considers it appropriate to do so, enter into a conservation agreement with any government in Canada, organization or person to benefit a species at risk or enhance its survival in the wild.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The agreement must provide for the taking of conservation measures and any other measures consistent with the purposes of this Act, and may include measures with respect to

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) monitoring the status of the species;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) developing and implementing education and public awareness programs;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) developing and implementing recovery strategies, action plans and management plans;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) protecting the species' habitat, including its critical habitat; or

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) undertaking research projects in support of recovery efforts for the species.

heading: Conservation agreements - other species
paragraph: 12 (1) A competent minister may, after consultation with every other competent minister, and with the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council or any of its members if he or she considers it appropriate to do so, enter into an agreement with any government in Canada, organization or person to provide for the conservation of a wildlife species that is not a species at risk.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The agreement may provide for the taking of conservation measures and any other measures consistent with the purposes of this Act, including measures with respect to

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) monitoring the status of the species;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) developing and implementing education and public awareness programs;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) protecting the species' habitat; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) preventing the species from becoming a species at risk.

heading: Funding agreements
paragraph: 13 (1) A competent minister may enter into an agreement with any government in Canada, organization or person to provide for the payment of contributions towards the costs of programs and measures for the conservation of wildlife species, including programs and measures under an agreement entered into under subsection 11(1) or 12(1).

heading: Provisions to be included
paragraph: (2) The agreement must specify

heading: Provisions to be included
paragraph: (a) the contribution towards the cost of the program or measure that is payable by any party and the time or times at which any amounts under the agreement will be paid;

heading: Provisions to be included
paragraph: (b) the authority or person who will be responsible for operating and maintaining the program or measure or any part of it;

heading: Provisions to be included
paragraph: (c) the proportions of any revenue from the program or measure that is payable to the parties; and

heading: Provisions to be included
paragraph: (d) the terms and conditions governing the operation and maintenance of the program or measure.

heading: Establishment
paragraph: 14 The Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada is hereby established.

heading: Functions
paragraph: 15 (1) The functions of COSEWIC are to

heading: Functions
paragraph: (a) assess the status of each wildlife species considered by COSEWIC to be at risk and, as part of the assessment, identify existing and potential threats to the species and

heading: Functions
paragraph: (i) classify the species as extinct, extirpated, endangered, threatened or of special concern,

heading: Functions
paragraph: (ii) indicate that COSEWIC does not have sufficient information to classify the species, or

heading: Functions
paragraph: (iii) indicate that the species is not currently at risk;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (b) determine when wildlife species are to be assessed, with priority given to those more likely to become extinct;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (c) conduct a new assessment of the status of species at risk and, if appropriate, reclassify or declassify them;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (c.1) indicate in the assessment whether the wildlife species migrates across Canada's boundary or has a range extending across Canada's boundary;

heading: Functions
paragraph: (d) develop and periodically review criteria for assessing the status of wildlife species and for classifying them and recommend the criteria to the Minister and the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council; and

heading: Functions
paragraph: (e) provide advice to the Minister and the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council and perform any other functions that the Minister, after consultation with that Council, may assign.

heading: Best information and knowledge
paragraph: (2) COSEWIC must carry out its functions on the basis of the best available information on the biological status of a species, including scientific knowledge, community knowledge and aboriginal traditional knowledge.

heading: Treaties and land claims agreements
paragraph: (3) COSEWIC must take into account any applicable provisions of treaty and land claims agreements when carrying out its functions.

heading: Composition
paragraph: 16 (1) COSEWIC is to be composed of members appointed by the Minister after consultation with the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council and with any experts and expert bodies, such as the Royal Society of Canada, that the Minister considers to have relevant expertise.

heading: Qualifications of members
paragraph: (2) Each member must have expertise drawn from a discipline such as conservation biology, population dynamics, taxonomy, systematics or genetics or from community knowledge or aboriginal traditional knowledge of the conservation of wildlife species.

heading: Term of appointment
paragraph: (3) The members are to be appointed to hold office for renewable terms of not more than four years.

heading: Not part of the public service of Canada
paragraph: (4) The members are not, because of being a member, part of the public service of Canada.

heading: Remuneration and expenses
paragraph: (5) The members may be paid remuneration and expenses for their services in amounts that the Minister may set.

heading: Discretion
paragraph: (6) Each member of COSEWIC shall exercise his or her discretion in an independent manner.

heading: Regulations and guidelines
paragraph: 17 The Minister may, after consultation with the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council and COSEWIC, establish regulations or guidelines respecting the appointment of members and the carrying out of COSEWIC's functions.

heading: Subcommittees
paragraph: 18 (1) COSEWIC must establish subcommittees of specialists to assist in the preparation and review of status reports on wildlife species considered to be at risk, including subcommittees specializing in groups of wildlife species and a subcommittee specializing in aboriginal traditional knowledge, and it may establish other subcommittees to advise it or to exercise or perform any of its functions.

heading: Membership
paragraph: (2) Each subcommittee must be presided over by a member of COSEWIC, but the subcommittee may include persons who are not members of COSEWIC.

heading: Aboriginal traditional knowledge subcommittee
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (2), the chairperson and members of the aboriginal traditional knowledge subcommittee must be appointed by the Minister after consultation with any aboriginal organization he or she considers appropriate.

heading: Rules
paragraph: 19 COSEWIC may make rules respecting the holding of meetings and the general conduct of its activities, including rules respecting

heading: Rules
paragraph: (a) the selection of persons to chair its meetings; and

heading: Rules
paragraph: (b) the meetings and activities of any of its subcommittees.

heading: Staff and facilities
paragraph: 20 The Minister must provide COSEWIC with any professional, technical, secretarial, clerical and other assistance, and any facilities and supplies, that, in his or her opinion, are necessary to carry out its functions.

heading: Status reports
paragraph: 21 (1) COSEWIC's assessment of the status of a wildlife species must be based on a status report on the species that COSEWIC either has had prepared or has received with an application.

heading: Content
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, after consultation with COSEWIC, the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations establishing the content of status reports.

heading: Applications
paragraph: 22 (1) Any person may apply to COSEWIC for an assessment of the status of a wildlife species.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) The Minister may, after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans and the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council, make regulations respecting the making of applications to COSEWIC under subsection (1) and the dealing with of those applications by COSEWIC.

heading: Time for assessment
paragraph: 23 (1) COSEWIC must assess the status of a wildlife species within one year after it receives a status report on the species, and it must provide reasons for its assessment.

heading: Notification of applicant
paragraph: (2) If the assessment results from an application, COSEWIC must notify the applicant of the assessment and the reasons.

heading: Review of classifications
paragraph: 24 COSEWIC must review the classification of each species at risk at least once every 10 years, or at any time if it has reason to believe that the status of the species has changed significantly.

heading: Copies to Minister and Council
paragraph: 25 (1) When COSEWIC completes an assessment of the status of a wildlife species, it must provide the Minister and the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council with a copy of the assessment and the reasons for it. A copy of the assessment and the reasons must also be included in the public registry.

heading: COSEWIC list
paragraph: (2) COSEWIC must annually prepare a complete list of every wildlife species it has assessed since the coming into force of this section and a copy of that list must be included in the public registry.

heading: Report on response
paragraph: (3) On receiving a copy of an assessment of the status of a wildlife species from COSEWIC under subsection (1), the Minister must, within 90 days, include in the public registry a report on how the Minister intends to respond to the assessment and, to the extent possible, provide time lines for action.

heading: Annual reports
paragraph: 26 COSEWIC must annually provide a report on its activities to the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council and a copy of that report must be included in the public registry.

heading: Power to amend List
paragraph: 27 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, by order amend the List in accordance with subsections (1.1) and (1.2) by adding a wildlife species, by reclassifying a listed wildlife species or by removing a listed wildlife species, and the Minister may, by order, amend the List in a similar fashion in accordance with subsection (3).

heading: Decision in respect of assessment
paragraph: (1.1) Subject to subsection (3), the Governor in Council, within nine months after receiving an assessment of the status of a species by COSEWIC, may review that assessment and may, on the recommendation of the Minister,

heading: Decision in respect of assessment
paragraph: (a) accept the assessment and add the species to the List;

heading: Decision in respect of assessment
paragraph: (b) decide not to add the species to the List; or

heading: Decision in respect of assessment
paragraph: (c) refer the matter back to COSEWIC for further information or consideration.

heading: Statement of reasons
paragraph: (1.2) Where the Governor in Council takes a course of action under paragraph (1.1)(b) or (c), the Minister shall, after the approval of the Governor in Council, include a statement in the public registry setting out the reasons.

heading: Pre-conditions for recommendation
paragraph: (2) Before making a recommendation in respect of a wildlife species or a species at risk, the Minister must

heading: Pre-conditions for recommendation
paragraph: (a) take into account the assessment of COSEWIC in respect of the species;

heading: Pre-conditions for recommendation
paragraph: (b) consult the competent minister or ministers; and

heading: Pre-conditions for recommendation
paragraph: (c) if the species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of a wildlife species, consult the wildlife management board.

heading: Amendment of List by Minister
paragraph: (3) Where the Governor in Council has not taken a course of action under subsection (1.1) within nine months after receiving an assessment of the status of a species by COSEWIC, the Minister shall, by order, amend the List in accordance with COSEWIC's assessment.

heading: Applications for assessment of imminent threat
paragraph: 28 (1) Any person who considers that there is an imminent threat to the survival of a wildlife species may apply to COSEWIC for an assessment of the threat for the purpose of having the species listed on an emergency basis under subsection 29(1) as an endangered species.

heading: Information to be included in application
paragraph: (2) The application must include relevant information indicating that there is an imminent threat to the survival of the species.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (3) The Minister may, after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans and the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council, make regulations respecting the making of applications to COSEWIC under subsection (1) and the dealing with of those applications by COSEWIC.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (4) COSEWIC must provide the applicant, the Minister and the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council with a copy of its assessment. A copy of the assessment must be included in the public registry.

heading: Emergency listing
paragraph: 29 (1) If the Minister is of the opinion that there is an imminent threat to the survival of a wildlife species, the Minister must, on an emergency basis, after consultation with every other competent minister, make a recommendation to the Governor in Council that the List be amended to list the species as an endangered species.

heading: Formation of opinion
paragraph: (2) The Minister may arrive at that opinion on the basis of his or her own information or on the basis of COSEWIC's assessment.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (3) If a recommendation is made under subsection (1), subsection 27(2) does not apply to any order that is made under subsection 27(1) on the basis of that recommendation, and the order is exempt from the application of section 3 of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Review
paragraph: 30 (1) As soon as possible after an order is made on the basis of a recommendation referred to in subsection 29(1), COSEWIC must have a status report on the wildlife species prepared and, within one year after the making of the order, COSEWIC must, in a report in writing to the Minister,

heading: Review
paragraph: (a) confirm the classification of the species;

heading: Review
paragraph: (b) recommend to the Minister that the species be reclassified; or

heading: Review
paragraph: (c) recommend to the Minister that the species be removed from the List.

heading: Copy of report
paragraph: (2) Within 30 days after the report is received by the Minister, a copy of the report must be included in the public registry.

heading: Recommendation to amend List
paragraph: 31 If COSEWIC makes a recommendation under paragraph 30(1)(b) or (c), the Minister may make a recommendation to the Governor in Council with respect to amending the List.

heading: Killing, harming, etc., listed wildlife species
paragraph: 32 (1) No person shall kill, harm, harass, capture or take an individual of a wildlife species that is listed as an extirpated species, an endangered species or a threatened species.

heading: Possession, collection, etc.
paragraph: (2) No person shall possess, collect, buy, sell or trade an individual of a wildlife species that is listed as an extirpated species, an endangered species or a threatened species, or any part or derivative of such an individual.

heading: Deeming
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), any animal, plant or thing that is represented to be an individual, or a part or derivative of an individual, of a wildlife species that is listed as an extirpated species, an endangered species or a threatened species is deemed, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, to be such an individual or a part or derivative of such an individual.

heading: Damage or destruction of residence
paragraph: 33 No person shall damage or destroy the residence of one or more individuals of a wildlife species that is listed as an endangered species or a threatened species, or that is listed as an extirpated species if a recovery strategy has recommended the reintroduction of the species into the wild in Canada.

heading: Application - certain species in provinces
paragraph: 34 (1) With respect to individuals of a listed wildlife species that is not an aquatic species or a species of birds that are migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994, sections 32 and 33 do not apply in lands in a province that are not federal lands unless an order is made under subsection (2) to provide that they apply.

heading: Order
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, by order, provide that sections 32 and 33, or either of them, apply in lands in a province that are not federal lands with respect to individuals of a listed wildlife species that is not an aquatic species or a species of birds that are migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994.

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (3) The Minister must recommend that the order be made if the Minister is of the opinion that the laws of the province do not effectively protect the species or the residences of its individuals.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (4) Before recommending that the Governor in Council make an order under subsection (2), the Minister must consult

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (a) the appropriate provincial minister; and

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (b) if the species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, the wildlife management board.

heading: Application - certain species in territories
paragraph: 35 (1) Sections 32 and 33 apply in each of the territories in respect of a listed wildlife species only to the extent that the Governor in Council, on the recommendation of the Minister, makes an order providing that they, or any of them, apply.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) in respect of individuals of aquatic species and their habitat or species of birds that are migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) on land under the authority of the Minister or the Parks Canada Agency.

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (3) The Minister must recommend that the order be made if the Minister is of the opinion that the laws of the territory do not effectively protect the species or the residences of its individuals.

heading: Pre-conditions for recommendation
paragraph: (4) Before recommending that an order be made under subsection (1), the Minister must

heading: Pre-conditions for recommendation
paragraph: (a) consult the appropriate territorial minister; and

heading: Pre-conditions for recommendation
paragraph: (b) if the species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, consult the wildlife management board.

heading: Prohibitions re provincial and territorial classifications
paragraph: 36 (1) If a wildlife species that is not listed has been classified as an endangered species or a threatened species by a provincial or territorial minister, no person shall

heading: Prohibitions re provincial and territorial classifications
paragraph: (a) kill, harm, harass, capture or take an individual of that species that is on federal lands in the province or territory;

heading: Prohibitions re provincial and territorial classifications
paragraph: (b) possess, collect, buy, sell or trade an individual of that species that is on federal lands in the province or territory, or any part or derivative of such an individual; or

heading: Prohibitions re provincial and territorial classifications
paragraph: (c) damage or destroy the residence of one or more individuals of that species that is on federal lands in the province or territory.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only in respect of the portions of the federal lands that the Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the competent minister, by order, specify.

heading: Preparation - endangered or threatened species
paragraph: 37 (1) If a wildlife species is listed as an extirpated species, an endangered species or a threatened species, the competent minister must prepare a strategy for its recovery.

heading: More than one competent minister
paragraph: (2) If there is more than one competent minister with respect to the wildlife species, they must prepare the strategy together and every reference to competent minister in sections 38 to 46 is to be read as a reference to the competent ministers.

heading: Commitments to be considered
paragraph: 38 In preparing a recovery strategy, action plan or management plan, the competent minister must consider the commitment of the Government of Canada to conserving biological diversity and to the principle that, if there are threats of serious or irreversible damage to the listed wildlife species, cost-effective measures to prevent the reduction or loss of the species should not be postponed for a lack of full scientific certainty.

heading: Cooperation with others
paragraph: 39 (1) To the extent possible, the recovery strategy must be prepared in cooperation with

heading: Cooperation with others
paragraph: (a) the appropriate provincial and territorial minister for each province and territory in which the listed wildlife species is found;

heading: Cooperation with others
paragraph: (b) every minister of the Government of Canada who has authority over federal land or other areas on which the species is found;

heading: Cooperation with others
paragraph: (c) if the species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, the wildlife management board;

heading: Cooperation with others
paragraph: (d) every aboriginal organization that the competent minister considers will be directly affected by the recovery strategy; and

heading: Cooperation with others
paragraph: (e) any other person or organization that the competent minister considers appropriate.

heading: Land claims agreement
paragraph: (2) If the listed wildlife species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, the recovery strategy must be prepared, to the extent that it will apply to that area, in accordance with the provisions of the agreement.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) To the extent possible, the recovery strategy must be prepared in consultation with any landowners and other persons whom the competent minister considers to be directly affected by the strategy, including the government of any other country in which the species is found.

heading: Determination of feasibility
paragraph: 40 In preparing the recovery strategy, the competent minister must determine whether the recovery of the listed wildlife species is technically and biologically feasible. The determination must be based on the best available information, including information provided by COSEWIC.

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: 41 (1) If the competent minister determines that the recovery of the listed wildlife species is feasible, the recovery strategy must address the threats to the survival of the species identified by COSEWIC, including any loss of habitat, and must include

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (a) a description of the species and its needs that is consistent with information provided by COSEWIC;

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (b) an identification of the threats to the survival of the species and threats to its habitat that is consistent with information provided by COSEWIC and a description of the broad strategy to be taken to address those threats;

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (c) an identification of the species' critical habitat, to the extent possible, based on the best available information, including the information provided by COSEWIC, and examples of activities that are likely to result in its destruction;

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (c.1) a schedule of studies to identify critical habitat, where available information is inadequate;

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (d) a statement of the population and distribution objectives that will assist the recovery and survival of the species, and a general description of the research and management activities needed to meet those objectives;

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (e) any other matters that are prescribed by the regulations;

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (f) a statement about whether additional information is required about the species; and

heading: Contents if recovery feasible
paragraph: (g) a statement of when one or more action plans in relation to the recovery strategy will be completed.

heading: Contents if recovery not feasible
paragraph: (2) If the competent minister determines that the recovery of the listed wildlife species is not feasible, the recovery strategy must include a description of the species and its needs, an identification of the species' critical habitat to the extent possible, and the reasons why its recovery is not feasible.

heading: Multi-species or ecosystem approach permissible
paragraph: (3) The competent minister may adopt a multi-species or an ecosystem approach when preparing the recovery strategy if he or she considers it appropriate to do so.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (4) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations for the purpose of paragraph (1)(e) prescribing matters to be included in a recovery strategy.

heading: Proposed recovery strategy
paragraph: 42 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the competent minister must include a proposed recovery strategy in the public registry within one year after the wildlife species is listed, in the case of a wildlife species listed as an endangered species, and within two years after the species is listed, in the case of a wildlife species listed as a threatened species or an extirpated species.

heading: First listed wildlife species
paragraph: (2) With respect to wildlife species that are set out in Schedule 1 on the day section 27 comes into force, the competent minister must include a proposed recovery strategy in the public registry within three years after that day, in the case of a wildlife species listed as an endangered species, and within four years after that day, in the case of a wildlife species listed as a threatened species or an extirpated species.

heading: Comments
paragraph: 43 (1) Within 60 days after the proposed recovery strategy is included in the public registry, any person may file written comments with the competent minister.

heading: Finalization of recovery strategy
paragraph: (2) Within 30 days after the expiry of the period referred to in subsection (1), the competent minister must consider any comments received, make any changes to the proposed recovery strategy that he or she considers appropriate and finalize the recovery strategy by including a copy of it in the public registry.

heading: Existing plans
paragraph: 44 (1) If the competent minister is of the opinion that an existing plan relating to a wildlife species meets the requirements of subsection 41(1) or (2), and the plan is adopted by the competent minister as the proposed recovery strategy, he or she must include it in the public registry as the proposed recovery strategy in relation to the species.

heading: Incorporation of existing plans
paragraph: (2) The competent minister may incorporate any part of an existing plan relating to a wildlife species into a proposed recovery strategy for the species.

heading: Reporting
paragraph: 46 The competent minister must report on the implementation of the recovery strategy, and the progress towards meeting its objectives, within five years after it is included in the public registry and in every subsequent five-year period, until its objectives have been achieved or the species' recovery is no longer feasible. The report must be included in the public registry.

heading: Preparation
paragraph: 47 The competent minister in respect of a recovery strategy must prepare one or more action plans based on the recovery strategy. If there is more than one competent minister with respect to the recovery strategy, they may prepare the action plan or plans together.

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: 48 (1) To the extent possible, an action plan must be prepared in cooperation with

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (a) the appropriate provincial and territorial minister of each province and territory in which the listed wildlife species is found;

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (b) every minister of the Government of Canada who has authority over federal land or other areas on which the species is found;

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (c) if the species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, the wildlife management board;

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (d) every aboriginal organization that the competent minister considers will be directly affected by the action plan; and

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (e) any other person or organization that the competent minister considers appropriate.

heading: Land claims agreement
paragraph: (2) If the listed wildlife species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, an action plan must be prepared, to the extent that it will apply to that area, in accordance with the provisions of the agreement.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) To the extent possible, an action plan must be prepared in consultation with any landowners, lessees and other persons whom the competent minister considers to be directly affected by, or interested in, the action plan, including the government of any other country in which the species is found.

heading: Contents
paragraph: 49 (1) An action plan must include, with respect to the area to which the action plan relates,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) an identification of the species' critical habitat, to the extent possible, based on the best available information and consistent with the recovery strategy, and examples of activities that are likely to result in its destruction;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) a statement of the measures that are proposed to be taken to protect the species' critical habitat, including the entering into of agreements under section 11;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) an identification of any portions of the species' critical habitat that have not been protected;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d) a statement of the measures that are to be taken to implement the recovery strategy, including those that address the threats to the species and those that help to achieve the population and distribution objectives, as well as an indication as to when these measures are to take place;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (d.1) the methods to be used to monitor the recovery of the species and its long-term viability;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (e) an evaluation of the socio-economic costs of the action plan and the benefits to be derived from its implementation; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (f) any other matters that are prescribed by the regulations.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations for the purpose of paragraph (1)(f) prescribing matters to be included in an action plan.

heading: Proposed action plan
paragraph: 50 (1) The competent minister must include a proposed action plan in the public registry.

heading: Comments
paragraph: (2) Within 60 days after the proposed action plan is included in the public registry, any person may file written comments with the competent minister.

heading: Finalization of action plan
paragraph: (3) Within 30 days after the expiry of the period referred to in subsection (2), the competent minister must consider any comments received, make any changes to the proposed action plan that he or she considers appropriate and finalize the action plan by including a copy of it in the public registry.

heading: Summary if action plan not completed in time
paragraph: (4) If an action plan is not finalized in the time set out in the recovery strategy, the competent minister must include in the public registry a summary of what has been prepared with respect to the plan.

heading: Existing plans
paragraph: 51 (1) If the competent minister is of the opinion that an existing plan relating to a wildlife species meets the requirements of section 49, and the plan is adopted by the competent minister as a proposed action plan, he or she must include it in the public registry as a proposed action plan in relation to the species.

heading: Incorporation of existing plans
paragraph: (2) The competent minister may incorporate any part of an existing plan relating to a wildlife species into a proposed action plan for the species.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 53 (1) The competent minister must, with respect to aquatic species, species of birds that are migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994, regardless of where they are located, or with respect to any other wildlife species on federal lands, make any regulations that are necessary in the opinion of the competent minister for the purpose of implementing the measures included in an action plan, but, if the measures relate to the protection of critical habitat on federal lands, the regulations must be made under section 59.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect a reserve or any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band under the Indian Act, he or she must consult the Minister of Indigenous Services and the band before making the regulation.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, he or she must consult the wildlife management board before making the regulation.

heading: Incorporation by reference
paragraph: (4) The regulations may incorporate by reference any legislation of a province or territory, as amended from time to time, insofar as the regulations apply in that province or territory.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (5) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect land in a territory, he or she must consult the territorial minister before making the regulation.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (6) Subsection (5) does not apply

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) in respect of individuals of aquatic species and their habitat or species of birds that are migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 and their habitat; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) in respect of land under the authority of the Minister or the Parks Canada Agency.

heading: Use of powers under other Acts
paragraph: 54 For the purpose of implementing the measures included in an action plan, the competent minister may use any powers that he or she has under any other Act of Parliament.

heading: Monitoring and reporting
paragraph: 55 The competent minister must monitor the implementation of an action plan and the progress towards meeting its objectives and assess and report on its implementation and its ecological and socio-economic impacts five years after the plan comes into effect. A copy of the report must be included in the public registry.

heading: Codes of practice, national standards or guidelines
paragraph: 56 The competent minister may, after consultation with the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council and any person whom he or she considers appropriate, establish codes of practice, national standards or guidelines with respect to the protection of critical habitat.

heading: Purpose
paragraph: 57 The purpose of section 58 is to ensure that, within 180 days after the recovery strategy or action plan that identified the critical habitat referred to in subsection 58(1) is included in the public registry, all of the critical habitat is protected by

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (a) provisions in, or measures under, this or any other Act of Parliament, including agreements under section 11; or

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (b) the application of subsection 58(1).

heading: Destruction of critical habitat
paragraph: 58 (1) Subject to this section, no person shall destroy any part of the critical habitat of any listed endangered species or of any listed threatened species - or of any listed extirpated species if a recovery strategy has recommended the reintroduction of the species into the wild in Canada - if

heading: Destruction of critical habitat
paragraph: (a) the critical habitat is on federal land, in the exclusive economic zone of Canada or on the continental shelf of Canada;

heading: Destruction of critical habitat
paragraph: (b) the listed species is an aquatic species; or

heading: Destruction of critical habitat
paragraph: (c) the listed species is a species of migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994.

heading: Protected areas
paragraph: (2) If the critical habitat or a portion of the critical habitat is in a national park of Canada named and described in Schedule 1 to the Canada National Parks Act, the Rouge National Urban Park established by the Rouge National Urban Park Act, a marine protected area under the Oceans Act, a migratory bird sanctuary under the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 or a national wildlife area under the Canada Wildlife Act, the competent Minister must, within 90 days after the recovery strategy or action plan that identified the critical habitat is included in the public registry, publish in the Canada Gazette a description of the critical habitat or portion that is in that park, area or sanctuary.

heading: Application
paragraph: (3) If subsection (2) applies, subsection (1) applies to the critical habitat or the portion of the critical habitat described in the Canada Gazette under subsection (2) 90 days after the description is published in the Canada Gazette.

heading: Application
paragraph: (4) If all of the critical habitat or any portion of the critical habitat is not in a place referred to in subsection (2), subsection (1) applies in respect of the critical habitat or portion of the critical habitat, as the case may be, specified in an order made by the competent minister.

heading: Obligation to make order or statement
paragraph: (5) Within 180 days after the recovery strategy or action plan that identified the critical habitat is included in the public registry, the competent minister must, after consultation with every other competent minister, with respect to all of the critical habitat or any portion of the critical habitat that is not in a place referred to in subsection (2),

heading: Obligation to make order or statement
paragraph: (a) make the order referred to in subsection (4) if the critical habitat or any portion of the critical habitat is not legally protected by provisions in, or measures under, this or any other Act of Parliament, including agreements under section 11; or

heading: Obligation to make order or statement
paragraph: (b) if the competent minister does not make the order, he or she must include in the public registry a statement setting out how the critical habitat or portions of it, as the case may be, are legally protected.

heading: Habitat of migratory birds
paragraph: (5.1) Despite subsection (4), with respect to the critical habitat of a species of bird that is a migratory bird protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 that is not on federal land, in the exclusive economic zone of Canada, on the continental shelf of Canada or in a migratory bird sanctuary referred to in subsection (2), subsection (1) applies only to those portions of the critical habitat that are habitat to which that Act applies and that the Governor in Council may, by order, specify on the recommendation of the competent minister.

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (5.2) The competent minister must, within 180 days after the recovery strategy or action plan that identified the critical habitat that includes habitat to which the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 applies is included in the public registry, and after consultation with every other competent minister,

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (a) make the recommendation if he or she is of the opinion there are no provisions in, or other measures under, this or any other Act of Parliament, including agreements under section 11, that legally protect any portion or portions of the habitat to which that Act applies; or

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (b) if the competent minister does not make the recommendation, he or she must include in the public registry a statement setting out how the critical habitat that is habitat to which that Act applies, or portions of it, as the case may be, are legally protected.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (6) If the competent minister is of the opinion that an order under subsection (4) or (5.1) would affect land in a territory that is not under the authority of the Minister or the Parks Canada Agency, he or she must consult the territorial minister before making the order under subsection (4) or the recommendation under subsection (5.2).

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (7) If the competent minister is of the opinion that an order under subsection (4) or (5.1) would affect a reserve or any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band under the Indian Act, he or she must consult the Minister of Indigenous Services and the band before making the order under subsection (4) or the recommendation under subsection (5.2).

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (8) If the competent minister is of the opinion that an order under subsection (4) or (5.1) would affect an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, he or she must consult the wildlife management board before making the order under subsection (4) or the recommendation under subsection (5.2).

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (9) If the competent minister is of the opinion that an order under subsection (4) or (5.1) would affect land that is under the authority of another federal minister, other than a competent minister, he or she must consult the other federal minister before making the order under subsection (4) or the recommendation under subsection (5.2).

heading: Regulations re federal lands
paragraph: 59 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the competent minister after consultation with every other competent minister, make regulations to protect critical habitat on federal lands.

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (2) The competent minister must make the recommendation if the recovery strategy or an action plan identifies a portion of the critical habitat as being unprotected and the competent minister is of the opinion that the portion requires protection.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (3) The regulations may include provisions requiring the doing of things that protect the critical habitat and provisions prohibiting activities that may adversely affect the critical habitat.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (4) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect land in a territory that is not under the authority of the Minister or the Parks Canada Agency, he or she must consult the territorial minister before recommending the making of the regulation.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (5) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect a reserve or any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band under the Indian Act, he or she must consult the Minister of Indigenous Services and the band before recommending the making of the regulation.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (6) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, he or she must consult the wildlife management board before recommending the making of the regulation.

heading: Provincial and territorial classifications
paragraph: 60 (1) If a wildlife species has been classified as an endangered species or a threatened species by a provincial or territorial minister, no person shall destroy any part of the habitat of that species that the provincial or territorial minister has identified as essential to the survival or recovery of the species and that is on federal lands in the province or territory.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only to the portions of the habitat that the Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the competent minister, by order, specify.

heading: Destruction of critical habitat
paragraph: 61 (1) No person shall destroy any part of the critical habitat of a listed endangered species or a listed threatened species that is in a province or territory and that is not part of federal lands.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (1.1) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) an aquatic species; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the critical habitat of a species of bird that is a migratory bird protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 that is habitat referred to in subsection 58(5.1).

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies only to the portions of the critical habitat that the Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister, by order, specify.

heading: Power to make recommendation
paragraph: (3) The Minister may make a recommendation if

heading: Power to make recommendation
paragraph: (a) a provincial minister or territorial minister has requested that the recommendation be made; or

heading: Power to make recommendation
paragraph: (b) the Canadian Endangered Species Conservation Council has recommended that the recommendation be made.

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (4) The Minister must make a recommendation if he or she is of the opinion, after consultation with the appropriate provincial or territorial minister, that

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (a) there are no provisions in, or other measures under, this or any other Act of Parliament that protect the particular portion of the critical habitat, including agreements under section 11; and

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (b) the laws of the province or territory do not effectively protect the critical habitat.

heading: Expiry and renewal of order
paragraph: (5) An order made under subsection (2) expires five years after the day on which it is made or renewed, unless the Governor in Council, by order, renews it.

heading: Acquisition of lands
paragraph: 62 A competent minister may enter into an agreement with any government in Canada, organization or person to acquire any lands or interests in land for the purpose of protecting the critical habitat of any species at risk.

heading: Progress reports on unprotected portions of critical habitat
paragraph: 63 If in the opinion of the Minister any portion of the critical habitat of a listed wildlife species remains unprotected 180 days after the recovery strategy or action plan that identified the critical habitat was included in the public registry, the Minister must include in that registry a report on the steps taken to protect the critical habitat. The Minister must continue to report with respect to every subsequent period of 180 days until the portion is protected or is no longer identified as critical habitat.

heading: Compensation
paragraph: 64 (1) The Minister may, in accordance with the regulations, provide fair and reasonable compensation to any person for losses suffered as a result of any extraordinary impact of the application of

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (a) section 58, 60 or 61; or

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (b) an emergency order in respect of habitat identified in the emergency order that is necessary for the survival or recovery of a wildlife species.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) The Governor in Council shall make regulations that the Governor in Council considers necessary for carrying out the purposes and provisions of subsection (1), including regulations prescribing

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) the procedures to be followed in claiming compensation;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) the methods to be used in determining the eligibility of a person for compensation, the amount of loss suffered by a person and the amount of compensation in respect of any loss; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) the terms and conditions for the provision of compensation.

heading: Preparation of management plan
paragraph: 65 If a wildlife species is listed as a species of special concern, the competent minister must prepare a management plan for the species and its habitat. The plan must include measures for the conservation of the species that the competent minister considers appropriate and it may apply with respect to more than one wildlife species.

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: 66 (1) To the extent possible, the management plan must be prepared in cooperation with

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (a) the appropriate provincial and territorial minister of each province and territory in which the listed wildlife species is found;

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (b) every minister of the Government of Canada who has authority over federal land or other areas on which the species is found;

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (c) if the species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, the wildlife management board;

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (d) every aboriginal organization that the competent minister considers will be directly affected by the management plan; and

heading: Cooperation with other ministers and governments
paragraph: (e) any other person or organization that the competent minister considers appropriate.

heading: Land claims agreement
paragraph: (2) If the listed wildlife species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, the management plan must be prepared, to the extent that it will apply to that area, in accordance with the provisions of the agreement.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) To the extent possible, the management plan must be prepared in consultation with any landowners, lessees and other persons whom the competent minister considers to be directly affected by, or interested in, the management plan, including the government of any other country in which the species is found.

heading: Multi-species or ecosystem approach permissible
paragraph: 67 The competent minister may adopt a multi-species or an ecosystem approach when preparing the management plan if he or she considers it appropriate to do so.

heading: Proposed management plan
paragraph: 68 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the competent minister must include a proposed management plan in the public registry within three years after the wildlife species is listed as a species of special concern.

heading: First listed species
paragraph: (2) With respect to a wildlife species that is set out in Schedule 1 as a species of special concern on the day section 27 comes into force, the competent minister must include a proposed management plan in the public registry within five years after that day.

heading: Comments
paragraph: (3) Within 60 days after the proposed management plan is included in the public registry, any person may file written comments with the competent minister.

heading: Finalization of management plan
paragraph: (4) Within 30 days after the expiry of the period referred to in subsection (3), the competent minister must consider any comments received, make any changes to the proposed management plan that he or she considers appropriate and finalize the management plan by including a copy of it in the public registry.

heading: Existing plans
paragraph: 69 (1) If the competent minister is of the opinion that an existing plan relating to a wildlife species includes adequate measures for the conservation of the species and the competent minister adopts the existing plan as the proposed management plan, he or she must include a copy of it in the public registry as the proposed management plan in relation to the species.

heading: Incorporation of existing plans
paragraph: (2) The competent minister may incorporate any part of an existing plan relating to a wildlife species into a proposed management plan for the species.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 71 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the competent minister, make any regulations with respect to aquatic species or species of birds that are migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994, regardless of where they are located, or with respect to any other wildlife species on federal lands, that the Governor in Council considers appropriate for the purpose of implementing the measures included in the management plan.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (2) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect a reserve or any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band under the Indian Act, he or she must consult the Minister of Indigenous Services and the band before recommending the making of the regulation.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, he or she must consult the wildlife management board before recommending the making of the regulation.

heading: Incorporation by reference
paragraph: (4) The regulations may incorporate by reference any legislation of a province or territory, as amended from time to time, insofar as the regulations apply in that province or territory.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (5) If the competent minister is of the opinion that a regulation would affect land in a territory, he or she must consult the territorial minister before recommending the making of the regulation.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (6) Subsection (5) does not apply

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) in respect of individuals of aquatic species and their habitat or species of birds that are migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 and their habitat; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) in respect of land under the authority of the Minister or the Parks Canada Agency.

heading: Monitoring
paragraph: 72 The competent minister must monitor the implementation of the management plan and must assess its implementation five years after the plan is included in the public registry, and in every subsequent five-year period, until its objectives have been achieved. The report must be included in the public registry.

heading: Powers of competent minister
paragraph: 73 (1) The competent minister may enter into an agreement with a person, or issue a permit to a person, authorizing the person to engage in an activity affecting a listed wildlife species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals.

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (2) The agreement may be entered into, or the permit issued, only if the competent minister is of the opinion that

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (a) the activity is scientific research relating to the conservation of the species and conducted by qualified persons;

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (b) the activity benefits the species or is required to enhance its chance of survival in the wild; or

heading: Purpose
paragraph: (c) affecting the species is incidental to the carrying out of the activity.

heading: Pre-conditions
paragraph: (3) The agreement may be entered into, or the permit issued, only if the competent minister is of the opinion that

heading: Pre-conditions
paragraph: (a) all reasonable alternatives to the activity that would reduce the impact on the species have been considered and the best solution has been adopted;

heading: Pre-conditions
paragraph: (b) all feasible measures will be taken to minimize the impact of the activity on the species or its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals; and

heading: Pre-conditions
paragraph: (c) the activity will not jeopardize the survival or recovery of the species.

heading: Explanation in public registry
paragraph: (3.1) If an agreement is entered into or a permit is issued, the competent minister must include in the public registry an explanation of why it was entered into or issued, taking into account the matters referred to in paragraphs (3)(a), (b) and (c).

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (4) If the species is found in an area in respect of which a wildlife management board is authorized by a land claims agreement to perform functions in respect of wildlife species, the competent minister must consult the wildlife management board before entering into an agreement or issuing a permit concerning that species in that area.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (5) If the species is found in a reserve or any other lands that are set apart for the use and benefit of a band under the Indian Act, the competent minister must consult the band before entering into an agreement or issuing a permit concerning that species in that reserve or those other lands.

heading: Terms and conditions
paragraph: (6) The agreement or permit must contain any terms and conditions governing the activity that the competent minister considers necessary for protecting the species, minimizing the impact of the authorized activity on the species or providing for its recovery.

heading: Date of expiry
paragraph: (6.1) The agreement or permit must set out the date of its expiry.

heading: Review of agreements and permits
paragraph: (7) The competent minister must review the agreement or permit if an emergency order is made with respect to the species.

heading: Amendment of agreements and permits
paragraph: (8) The competent minister may revoke or amend an agreement or a permit to ensure the survival or recovery of a species.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (10) The Minister may, after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations respecting the entering into of agreements, the issuance of permits and the renewal, revocation, amendment and suspension of agreements and permits.

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (11) The regulations may include provisions

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (a) respecting time limits for issuing or renewing permits, or for refusing to do so;

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (b) specifying the circumstances under which any of those time limits does not apply; and

heading: Time limits
paragraph: (c) authorizing the competent minister to extend any of those time limits or to decide that a time limit does not apply, when the competent minister considers that it is appropriate to do so.

heading: Competent minister acting under other Acts
paragraph: 74 An agreement, permit, licence, order or other similar document authorizing a person or organization to engage in an activity affecting a listed wildlife species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals that is entered into, issued or made by the competent minister under another Act of Parliament has the same effect as an agreement or permit under subsection 73(1) if

heading: Competent minister acting under other Acts
paragraph: (a) before it is entered into, issued or made, the competent minister is of the opinion that the requirements of subsections 73(2) to (6.1) are met; and

heading: Competent minister acting under other Acts
paragraph: (b) after it is entered into, issued or made, the competent minister complies with the requirements of subsection 73(7).

heading: Adding terms and conditions
paragraph: 75 (1) A competent minister may add terms and conditions to protect a listed wildlife species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals to any agreement, permit, licence, order or other similar document authorizing a person to engage in an activity affecting the species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals that is entered into, issued or made by the competent minister under another Act of Parliament.

heading: Amending terms and conditions
paragraph: (2) A competent minister may also revoke or amend any term or condition in any of those documents to protect a listed wildlife species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals.

heading: Treaties and land claims agreements
paragraph: (3) The competent minister must take into account any applicable provisions of treaty and land claims agreements when carrying out his or her powers under this section.

heading: Exemption for existing agreements, permits, etc.
paragraph: 76 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of a competent minister, by order, provide that section 32, 33, 36, 58, 60 or 61, or any regulation made under section 53, 59 or 71, does not apply, for a period of up to one year from the date of listing of a wildlife species, to agreements, permits, licences, orders or other similar documents authorizing persons to engage in an activity affecting the listed wildlife species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals that were entered into, issued or made under another Act of Parliament before the species was listed.

heading: Licences, permits, etc., under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: 77 (1) Despite any other Act of Parliament, any person or body, other than a competent minister, authorized under any Act of Parliament, other than this Act, to issue or approve a licence, a permit or any other authorization that authorizes an activity that may result in the destruction of any part of the critical habitat of a listed wildlife species may enter into, issue, approve or make the authorization only if the person or body has consulted with the competent minister, has considered the impact on the species' critical habitat and is of the opinion that

heading: Licences, permits, etc., under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: (a) all reasonable alternatives to the activity that would reduce the impact on the species' critical habitat have been considered and the best solution has been adopted; and

heading: Licences, permits, etc., under other Acts of Parliament
paragraph: (b) all feasible measures will be taken to minimize the impact of the activity on the species' critical habitat.

heading: Application of section 58
paragraph: (2) For greater certainty, section 58 applies even though a licence, a permit or any other authorization has been issued in accordance with subsection (1).

heading: Agreements and permits under other provincial and territorial Acts
paragraph: 78 (1) An agreement, permit, licence, order or other similar document authorizing a person to engage in an activity affecting a listed wildlife species, any part of its critical habitat or the residences of its individuals that is entered into, issued or made under an Act of the legislature of a province or a territory by a provincial or territorial minister with whom a competent minister has entered into an agreement under section 10 has the same effect as an agreement or permit under subsection 73(1) if

heading: Agreements and permits under other provincial and territorial Acts
paragraph: (a) before it is entered into, issued or made, the provincial or territorial minister determines that the requirements of subsections 73(2), (3), (6) and (6.1) are met;

heading: Agreements and permits under other provincial and territorial Acts
paragraph: (b) after it is entered into, issued or made, the provincial or territorial minister complies with the requirements of subsection 73(7).

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1), the references to "competent minister" in subsections 73(2), (3), (6) and (7) are to be read as references to "provincial minister" or "territorial minister", as the case may be.

heading: Clarification - renewals
paragraph: 78.1 For greater certainty, a reference in any of sections 73 to 78 to the entering into, issuing, making or approving of any agreement, permit, licence, order or other similar document or authorization, includes renewing it, and a reference in any of those sections or in paragraph 97(1)(c) to any such document or authorization includes one that has been renewed.

heading: Notification of Minister
paragraph: 79 (1) Every person who is required by or under an Act of Parliament to ensure that an assessment of the environmental effects of a project is conducted, and every authority who makes a determination under paragraph 82(a) or (b) of the Impact Assessment Act in relation to a project, must, without delay, notify the competent minister or ministers in writing of the project if it is likely to affect a listed wildlife species or its critical habitat.

heading: Required action
paragraph: (2) The person must identify the adverse effects of the project on the listed wildlife species and its critical habitat and, if the project is carried out, must ensure that measures are taken to avoid or lessen those effects and to monitor them. The measures must be taken in a way that is consistent with any applicable recovery strategy and action plans.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (3) The following definitions apply in this section.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: person includes an association, an organization, a federal authority as defined in section 2 of the Impact Assessment Act, and any body that is set out in Schedule 4 to that Act. (personne)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: project means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a designated project as defined in section 2 of the Impact Assessment Act or a project as defined in section 81 of that Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a project as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Yukon Environmental and Socio-economic Assessment Act; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a development as defined in subsection 111(1) of the Mackenzie Valley Resource Management Act. (projet)

heading: Emergency order
paragraph: 80 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the competent minister, make an emergency order to provide for the protection of a listed wildlife species.

heading: Obligation to make recommendation
paragraph: (2) The competent minister must make the recommendation if he or she is of the opinion that the species faces imminent threats to its survival or recovery.

heading: Consultation
paragraph: (3) Before making a recommendation, the competent minister must consult every other competent minister.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (4) The emergency order may

heading: Contents
paragraph: (a) in the case of an aquatic species,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (i) identify habitat that is necessary for the survival or recovery of the species in the area to which the emergency order relates, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (ii) include provisions requiring the doing of things that protect the species and that habitat and provisions prohibiting activities that may adversely affect the species and that habitat;

heading: Contents
paragraph: (b) in the case of a species that is a species of migratory birds protected by the Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (i) on federal land or in the exclusive economic zone of Canada,

heading: Contents
