paragraph: (A) identify habitat that is necessary for the survival or recovery of the species in the area to which the emergency order relates, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (B) include provisions requiring the doing of things that protect the species and that habitat and provisions prohibiting activities that may adversely affect the species and that habitat, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (ii) on land other than land referred to in subparagraph (i),

heading: Contents
paragraph: (A) identify habitat that is necessary for the survival or recovery of the species in the area to which the emergency order relates, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (B) include provisions requiring the doing of things that protect the species and provisions prohibiting activities that may adversely affect the species and that habitat; and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (c) with respect to any other species,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (i) on federal land, in the exclusive economic zone of Canada or on the continental shelf of Canada,

heading: Contents
paragraph: (A) identify habitat that is necessary for the survival or recovery of the species in the area to which the emergency order relates, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (B) include provisions requiring the doing of things that protect the species and that habitat and provisions prohibiting activities that may adversely affect the species and that habitat, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (ii) on land other than land referred to in subparagraph (i),

heading: Contents
paragraph: (A) identify habitat that is necessary for the survival or recovery of the species in the area to which the emergency order relates, and

heading: Contents
paragraph: (B) include provisions prohibiting activities that may adversely affect the species and that habitat.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (5) An emergency order is exempt from the application of section 3 of the Statutory Instruments Act.

heading: Equivalent measures
paragraph: 81 Despite subsection 80(2), the competent minister is not required to make a recommendation for an emergency order if he or she is of the opinion that equivalent measures have been taken under another Act of Parliament to protect the wildlife species.

heading: General exceptions
paragraph: 83 (1) Subsections 32(1) and (2), section 33, subsections 36(1), 58(1), 60(1) and 61(1), regulations made under section 53, 59 or 71 and emergency orders do not apply to a person who is engaging in

heading: General exceptions
paragraph: (a) activities related to public safety, health or national security, that are authorized by or under any other Act of Parliament or activities under the Health of Animals Act and the Plant Protection Act for the health of animals and plants; or

heading: General exceptions
paragraph: (b) activities authorized under section 73, 74 or 78 by an agreement, permit, licence, order or similar document.

heading: Authorization of activities under other Acts
paragraph: (2) A power under an Act described in paragraph (1)(a) may be used to authorize an activity prohibited by subsection 32(1) or (2), section 33, subsection 36(1), 58(1), 60(1) or 61(1), a regulation made under section 53, 59 or 71 or an emergency order only if the person exercising the power

heading: Authorization of activities under other Acts
paragraph: (a) determines that the activity is necessary for the protection of public safety, health, including animal and plant health, or national security; and

heading: Authorization of activities under other Acts
paragraph: (b) respects the purposes of this Act to the greatest extent possible.

heading: Exceptions - land claims agreements
paragraph: (3) Subsections 32(1) and (2), section 33, subsections 36(1), 58(1), 60(1) and 61(1) and regulations made under section 53, 59 or 71 do not apply to a person who is engaging in activities in accordance with conservation measures for wildlife species under a land claims agreement.

heading: Exemptions for permitted activities
paragraph: (4) Subsections 32(1) and (2), section 33 and subsections 36(1), 58(1), 60(1) and 61(1) do not apply to a person who is engaging in activities that are permitted by a recovery strategy, an action plan or a management plan and who is also authorized under an Act of Parliament to engage in that activity, including a regulation made under section 53, 59 or 71.

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (5) Subsection 32(2) and paragraph 36(1)(b) do not apply to a person who possesses an individual of a listed extirpated, endangered or threatened species, or any part or derivative of such an individual, if

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (a) it was in the person's possession when the species was listed;

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (b) it is used by an aboriginal person for ceremonial or medicinal purposes, or it is part of ceremonial dress used for ceremonial or cultural purposes by an aboriginal person;

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (c) the person acquired it legally in another country and imported it legally into Canada;

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (d) the person acquired it by succession from someone who was entitled to possess it under this Act;

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (e) the person acquired it under circumstances that would afford them a defence under section 100 and the person possesses it only for as long as is necessary to donate it to a museum, a zoo, an educational institution, a scientific society or a government;

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (f) the person is, or is acting on behalf of, a museum, zoo, educational institution, scientific society or government and the person acquired it from someone who was entitled to possess it under this Act; or

heading: Additional possession exceptions
paragraph: (g) it or the person is otherwise exempt by the regulations.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 84 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations for the purpose of paragraph 83(5)(g).

heading: Enforcement officers
paragraph: 85 (1) A competent minister may designate any person or person of a class of persons to act as enforcement officers for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Designation of provincial or territorial government employees
paragraph: (2) The competent minister may not designate any person or person of a class of persons employed by the government of a province or a territory unless that government agrees.

heading: Certificate of designation
paragraph: (3) An enforcement officer must be provided with a certificate of designation as an enforcement officer in a form approved by the competent minister and, on entering any place under this Act, the officer must, if so requested, show the certificate to the occupant or person in charge of the place.

heading: Powers
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of this Act, enforcement officers have all the powers of a peace officer, but the competent minister may specify limits on those powers when designating any person or person of a class of persons to act as enforcement officers.

heading: Exemptions for law enforcement activities
paragraph: (5) For the purpose of investigations and other law enforcement activities under this Act, a competent minister may, on any terms and conditions that he or she considers necessary, exempt from the application of any provision of this Act, the regulations or an emergency order enforcement officers whom the competent minister has designated and who are carrying out duties or functions under this Act and persons acting under the direction and control of such enforcement officers.

heading: Inspections
paragraph: 86 (1) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with any provision of this Act, the regulations or an emergency order, an enforcement officer may, subject to subsection (3), at any reasonable time enter and inspect any place in which the enforcement officer believes, on reasonable grounds, there is any thing to which the provision applies or any document relating to its administration, and the enforcement officer may

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (a) open or cause to be opened any container that the enforcement officer believes, on reasonable grounds, contains that thing or document;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (b) inspect the thing and take samples free of charge;

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (c) require any person to produce the document for inspection or copying, in whole or in part; and

heading: Inspections
paragraph: (d) seize any thing by means of or in relation to which the enforcement officer believes, on reasonable grounds, the provision has been contravened or that the enforcement officer believes, on reasonable grounds, will provide evidence of a contravention.

heading: Conveyance
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of carrying out the inspection, the enforcement officer may stop a conveyance or direct that it be moved to a place where the inspection can be carried out.

heading: Dwelling-place
paragraph: (3) The enforcement officer may not enter a dwelling-place except with the consent of the occupant or person in charge of the dwelling-place or under the authority of a warrant.

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (4) On an ex parte application, a justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, may issue a warrant, subject to any conditions specified in it, authorizing an enforcement officer to enter a dwelling-place, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (a) the conditions for entry described in subsection (1) exist in relation to the dwelling-place;

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (b) entry to the dwelling-place is necessary for the purposes of the administration of this Act, the regulations or an emergency order; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of dwelling-place
paragraph: (c) entry to the dwelling-place has been refused or there are reasonable grounds for believing that entry will be refused.

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (5) On an ex parte application, a justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, may issue a warrant, subject to any conditions specified in it, authorizing an enforcement officer to enter a place other than a dwelling-place, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (a) the conditions for entry described in subsection (1) exist in relation to that place;

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (b) entry to that place is necessary for the purposes of the administration of this Act, the regulations or an emergency order;

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (c) entry to that place has been refused, the enforcement officer is not able to enter without the use of force or the place was abandoned; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant for inspection of non-dwellings
paragraph: (d) subject to subsection (6), all reasonable attempts were made to notify the owner, operator or person in charge of the place.

heading: Waiving notice
paragraph: (6) The justice may waive the requirement to give notice referred to in subsection (5) if the justice is satisfied that attempts to give the notice would be unsuccessful because the owner, operator or person in charge is absent from the jurisdiction of the justice or that it is not in the public interest to give the notice.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (7) In executing a warrant issued under subsection (4) or (5), an enforcement officer may not use force unless the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant.

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (8) In carrying out an inspection of a place under this section, an enforcement officer may

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (a) use or cause to be used any computer system at the place to examine any data contained in or available to the computer system;

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (b) reproduce any record or cause it to be reproduced from the data in the form of a printout or other intelligible output;

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (c) take a printout or other output for examination or copying; and

heading: Operation of computer system and copying equipment
paragraph: (d) use or cause to be used any copying equipment at the place to make copies of the record.

heading: Duty of person in possession or control
paragraph: (9) Every person who is in possession or control of a place being inspected under this section must permit the enforcement officer to do anything referred to in subsection (8).

heading: Custody of things seized
paragraph: 87 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), if an enforcement officer seizes a thing under this Act or under a warrant issued under the Criminal Code,

heading: Custody of things seized
paragraph: (a) sections 489.1 and 490 of the Criminal Code apply; and

heading: Custody of things seized
paragraph: (b) the enforcement officer, or any person that the officer may designate, must retain custody of the thing subject to any order made under section 490 of the Criminal Code.

heading: Forfeiture if ownership not ascertainable
paragraph: (2) If the lawful ownership of or entitlement to the seized thing cannot be ascertained within 30 days after its seizure, the thing or any proceeds of its disposition are forfeited to Her Majesty in right of Canada, if the thing was seized by an enforcement officer employed in the public service of Canada or by the government of a territory, or to Her Majesty in right of a province, if the thing was seized by an enforcement officer employed by the government of that province.

heading: Perishable things
paragraph: (3) If the seized thing is perishable, the enforcement officer may dispose of it or destroy it, and any proceeds of its disposition must be paid to the lawful owner or person lawfully entitled to possession of the thing, unless proceedings under this Act are commenced within 90 days after its seizure, in which case the proceeds must be retained by the enforcement officer pending the outcome of the proceedings.

heading: Release of individual
paragraph: (4) An enforcement officer who seizes an individual of a species at risk may, at the time of the seizure, return the individual to the wild if the enforcement officer believes the individual to be alive.

heading: Abandonment
paragraph: (5) The owner of the seized thing may abandon it to Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Disposition by competent minister
paragraph: 88 Any thing that has been forfeited or abandoned under this Act is to be dealt with and disposed of as the competent minister may direct.

heading: Liability for costs
paragraph: 89 The lawful owner and any person lawfully entitled to possession of any thing seized, forfeited or abandoned under this Act and who has been convicted of an offence under this Act in relation to that thing, are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for all the costs of inspection, seizure, abandonment, forfeiture or disposition incurred by Her Majesty in excess of any proceeds of disposition of the thing that have been forfeited to Her Majesty under this Act.

heading: Right of passage
paragraph: 90 An enforcement officer may, while carrying out powers, duties or functions under this Act, enter on and pass through or over private property without being liable for trespass or without the owner of the property having the right to object to that use of the property.

heading: Assistance
paragraph: 91 The owner or the person in charge of a place entered by an enforcement officer under section 86, and every person found in the place, must

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (a) give the enforcement officer all reasonable assistance to enable the enforcement officer to carry out duties and functions under this Act; and

heading: Assistance
paragraph: (b) provide the enforcement officer with any information in relation to the administration of this Act, the regulations or an emergency order that the enforcement officer may reasonably require.

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: 92 While an enforcement officer is exercising powers or carrying out duties or functions under this Act, no person shall

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (a) knowingly make any false or misleading statement, either orally or in writing, to the enforcement officer; or

heading: Obstruction
paragraph: (b) otherwise obstruct or hinder the enforcement officer.

heading: Application for investigation
paragraph: 93 (1) A person who is a resident of Canada and at least 18 years of age may apply to the competent minister for an investigation of whether an alleged offence has been committed or whether anything directed towards its commission has been done.

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (2) The application must be in a form approved by the competent minister and must include a solemn affirmation or declaration containing

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the applicant;

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (b) a statement that the applicant is at least 18 years old and a resident of Canada;

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (c) a statement of the nature of the alleged offence and the name of each person alleged to be involved;

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (d) a summary of the evidence supporting the allegations;

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (e) the name and address of each person who might be able to give evidence about the alleged offence, together with a summary of the evidence that the person might give, to the extent that information is available to the applicant;

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (f) a description of any document or other material that the applicant believes should be considered in the investigation and, if possible, a copy of the document; and

heading: Statement to accompany application
paragraph: (g) details of any previous contact between the applicant and the competent minister about the alleged offence.

heading: Investigation
paragraph: 94 (1) The competent minister must acknowledge receipt of the application within 20 days after receiving it and, subject to subsections (2) and (3), investigate all matters that he or she considers necessary to determine the facts relating to the alleged offence.

heading: Frivolous or vexatious applications
paragraph: (2) No investigation is required if the competent minister decides that the application is frivolous or vexatious.

heading: Notice of decision
paragraph: (3) If the competent minister decides not to conduct an investigation, he or she must, within 60 days after the application for investigation is received, give notice of the decision, with reasons, to the applicant.

heading: When notice need not be given
paragraph: (4) The competent minister need not give the notice if an investigation in relation to the alleged offence is ongoing apart from the application.

heading: Competent minister may send evidence to Attorney General
paragraph: 95 At any stage of the investigation, the competent minister may send any documents or other evidence to the Attorney General for a consideration of whether an offence has been or is about to be committed, and for any action that the Attorney General may wish to take.

heading: Suspension or conclusion of investigation
paragraph: 96 (1) The competent minister may suspend or conclude the investigation if he or she is of the opinion that the alleged offence does not require further investigation or the investigation does not substantiate the alleged offence or any other offence.

heading: Report if investigation suspended
paragraph: (2) If the investigation is suspended, the competent minister must prepare a written report describing the information obtained during the investigation and stating the reasons for its suspension and the action, if any, that the competent minister has taken or proposes to take and send a copy of the report to the applicant. The competent minister must notify the applicant if the investigation is subsequently resumed.

heading: Report when investigation concluded
paragraph: (3) When the investigation is concluded, the competent minister must prepare a written report describing the information obtained during the investigation and stating the reasons for its conclusion and the action, if any, that the competent minister has taken or proposes to take and send a copy of the report to the applicant and to each person whose conduct was investigated.

heading: Personal information not to be disclosed
paragraph: (4) A copy of the report sent to a person whose conduct was investigated must not disclose the name or address of the applicant or any other personal information about him or her.

heading: When report need not be sent
paragraph: (5) If another investigation in relation to the alleged offence is ongoing apart from the application, the competent minister need not send copies of a report described in subsection (2) or (3) until the other investigation is suspended or concluded.

heading: Offences
paragraph: 97 (1) Every person commits an offence who

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) contravenes subsection 32(1) or (2), section 33, subsection 36(1), 58(1), 60(1) or 61(1) or section 91 or 92;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) contravenes a prescribed provision of a regulation or an emergency order;

heading: Offences
paragraph: (c) fails to comply with a term or condition of a permit issued under subsection 73(1); or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (d) fails to comply with an alternative measures agreement that the person has entered into under this Act.

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (1.1) Every person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (a) on conviction on indictment,

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (i) in the case of a corporation, other than a non-profit corporation, to a fine of not more than $1,000,000,

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a non-profit corporation, to a fine of not more than $250,000, and

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (iii) in the case of any other person, to a fine of not more than $250,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than five years, or to both; or

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (b) on summary conviction,

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (i) in the case of a corporation, other than a non-profit corporation, to a fine of not more than $300,000,

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a non-profit corporation, to a fine of not more than $50,000, and

heading: Penalty
paragraph: (iii) in the case of any other person, to a fine of not more than $50,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than one year, or to both.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (1.2) Paragraph (1)(c) does not apply in respect of the failure to comply with any term or condition of any agreement, permit, licence, order or other similar document referred to in section 74 or subsection 78(1).

heading: Prescription of provisions
paragraph: (2) A regulation or emergency order may prescribe which of its provisions may give rise to an offence.

heading: Subsequent offence
paragraph: (3) For a second or subsequent conviction, the amount of the fine may, despite subsection (1.1), be double the amount set out in that subsection.

heading: Continuing offence
paragraph: (4) A person who commits or continues an offence on more than one day is liable to be convicted for a separate offence for each day on which the offence is committed or continued.

heading: Fines cumulative
paragraph: (5) A fine imposed for an offence involving more than one animal, plant or other organism may be calculated in respect of each one as though it had been the subject of a separate information and the fine then imposed is the total of that calculation.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: (6) If a person is convicted of an offence and the court is satisfied that monetary benefits accrued to the person as a result of the commission of the offence, the court may order the person to pay an additional fine in an amount equal to the court's estimation of the amount of the monetary benefits, which additional fine may exceed the maximum amount of any fine that may otherwise be imposed under this Act.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: Definition of non-profit corporation

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of subsection (1.1), non-profit corporation means a corporation, no part of the income of which is payable to, or is otherwise available for, the personal benefit of any proprietor, member or shareholder of the corporation.

heading: Officers, etc., of corporations
paragraph: 98 If a corporation commits an offence, any officer, director or agent or mandatary of the corporation who directed, authorized, assented to, or acquiesced or participated in, the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the punishment provided for the offence, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Offences by employees or agents or mandataries
paragraph: 99 In any prosecution for an offence, the accused may be convicted of the offence if it is established that it was committed by an employee or an agent or mandatary of the accused, whether or not the employee, agent or mandatary has been prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Due diligence
paragraph: 100 Due diligence is a defence in a prosecution for an offence.

heading: Venue
paragraph: 101 A prosecution for an offence may be instituted, heard and determined in the place where the offence was committed, the subject-matter of the prosecution arose, the accused was apprehended or the accused happens to be or is carrying on business.

heading: Sentencing considerations
paragraph: 102 A court that imposes a sentence shall take into account, in addition to any other principles that it is required to consider, the following factors:

heading: Sentencing considerations
paragraph: (a) the harm or risk of harm caused by the commission of the offence;

heading: Sentencing considerations
paragraph: (b) whether the offender was found to have committed the offence intentionally, recklessly or inadvertently;

heading: Sentencing considerations
paragraph: (c) whether the offender was found by the court to have been negligent or incompetent or to have shown a lack of concern with respect to the commission of the offence;

heading: Sentencing considerations
paragraph: (d) any property, benefit or advantage received or receivable by the offender to which, but for the commission of the offence, the offender would not have been entitled;

heading: Sentencing considerations
paragraph: (e) any evidence from which the court may reasonably conclude that the offender has a history of non-compliance with legislation designed to protect wildlife species; and

heading: Sentencing considerations
paragraph: (f) all available sanctions that are reasonable in the circumstances, with particular attention to the circumstances of aboriginal offenders.

heading: Forfeiture
paragraph: 103 (1) If a person is convicted of an offence, the convicting court may, in addition to any punishment imposed, order that any seized thing by means of or in relation to which the offence was committed, or any proceeds of its disposition, be forfeited to Her Majesty.

heading: Return if no forfeiture ordered
paragraph: (2) If the convicting court does not order the forfeiture, the seized thing, or the proceeds of its disposition, must be returned to its lawful owner or the person lawfully entitled to it.

heading: Retention or sale
paragraph: 104 If a fine is imposed on a person convicted of an offence, any seized thing, or any proceeds of its disposition, may be retained until the fine is paid or the thing may be sold in satisfaction of the fine and the proceeds applied, in whole or in part, in payment of the fine.

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: 105 If a person is convicted of an offence, the court may, in addition to any punishment imposed and having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order having any or all of the following effects:

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that could, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (b) directing the person to take any action that the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to any wildlife species that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (c) directing the person to have an environmental audit conducted by a person of a class and at the times specified by the court and directing the person to remedy any deficiencies revealed during the audit;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (d) directing the person to publish, in any manner that the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (e) directing the person to perform community service in accordance with any conditions that the court considers reasonable;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (f) directing the person to submit to the competent minister, on application to the court by the competent minister within three years after the conviction, any information about the activities of the person that the court considers appropriate;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (g) directing the person to pay a competent minister or the government of a province or a territory an amount for all or any of the cost of remedial or preventive action taken, or to be taken, by or on behalf of the competent minister or that government as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (h) directing the person to pay, in the manner prescribed by the court, an amount for the purpose of conducting research into the protection of the wildlife species in respect of which the offence was committed;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (i) directing the person to pay, in the manner prescribed by the court, an amount to an educational institution for scholarships for students enrolled in environmental studies;

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (j) directing the person to post a bond or pay to the court an amount that the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section; and

heading: Orders of court
paragraph: (k) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the person's good conduct and for preventing the person from repeating the offence or committing other offences.

heading: Suspended sentence
paragraph: 106 (1) If a person is convicted of an offence and the court suspends the passing of sentence under paragraph 731(1)(a) of the Criminal Code, the court may, in addition to any probation order made under that Act, make an order containing one or more of the prohibitions, directions or requirements mentioned in section 105.

heading: Imposition of sentence
paragraph: (2) If the person does not comply with the order or is convicted of another offence, within three years after the order is made, the court may, on the application of the prosecution, impose any sentence that could have been imposed if the passing of sentence had not been suspended.

heading: Limitation period
paragraph: 107 (1) Proceedings by way of summary conviction in respect of an offence may be commenced at any time within, but not later than, two years after the day on which the subject-matter of the proceedings became known to the competent minister.

heading: Competent minister's certificate
paragraph: (2) A document appearing to have been issued by the competent minister, certifying the day on which the subject-matter of any proceedings became known to the competent minister, is admissible in evidence without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the document and is proof of the matter asserted in it.

heading: References to the competent minister
paragraph: (3) A reference to the competent minister in this section includes a provincial or territorial minister if the competent minister has delegated responsibility for the enforcement of this Act, the regulations or an emergency order in the province or territory to the provincial or territorial minister and the offence is alleged to have been committed in the province or territory.

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: 108 (1) Alternative measures may be used to deal with a person who is alleged to have committed an offence, but only if it is not inconsistent with the purposes of this Act to do so and the following conditions are met:

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (a) the measures are part of a program of alternative measures authorized by the Attorney General, after consultation with the competent minister;

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (b) an information has been laid in respect of the offence;

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (c) the Attorney General, after consultation with the competent minister, is satisfied that the alternative measures would be appropriate, having regard to the nature of the offence, the circumstances surrounding its commission and the following factors, namely,

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (i) the protection of species at risk,

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (ii) the person's history of compliance with this Act,

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (iii) whether the offence is a repeated occurrence,

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (iv) any allegation that information is being or was concealed or other attempts to subvert the purposes and requirements of this Act are being or have been made, and

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (v) whether any remedial or preventive action has been taken by or on behalf of the person in relation to the offence;

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (d) the person applies, in accordance with regulations made under paragraph 119(a), to participate in the alternative measures after having been informed of them;

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (e) the person and the Attorney General have concluded an agreement respecting the alternative measures within 180 days after the person has, with respect to the offence, been served with a summons, been issued an appearance notice or a release order or entered into an undertaking;

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (f) before consenting to participate in the alternative measures, the person has been advised of the right to be represented by counsel;

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (g) the person accepts responsibility for the act or omission that forms the basis of the offence;

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (h) there is, in the opinion of the Attorney General, sufficient evidence to proceed with the prosecution of the offence; and

heading: When alternative measures may be used
paragraph: (i) the prosecution of the offence is not barred at law.

heading: Restriction on use
paragraph: (2) Alternative measures may not be used to deal with a person who

heading: Restriction on use
paragraph: (a) denies participation or involvement in the commission of the alleged offence; or

heading: Restriction on use
paragraph: (b) expresses the wish to have any charge against them dealt with by the court.

heading: Admissions not admissible in evidence
paragraph: (3) No admission, confession or statement accepting responsibility for a given act or omission made by a person as a condition of being dealt with by alternative measures is admissible in evidence against the person in any civil or criminal proceedings.

heading: Dismissal of charge
paragraph: (4) A court must dismiss a charge laid against a person in respect of an offence if alternative measures have been used to deal with the person in respect of the alleged offence and

heading: Dismissal of charge
paragraph: (a) the court is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that the person has totally complied with the agreement; or

heading: Dismissal of charge
paragraph: (b) the court is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that the person has partially complied with the agreement and, in the opinion of the court, the prosecution of the charge would be unfair, having regard to the circumstances and the person's performance with respect to the agreement.

heading: No bar to proceedings
paragraph: (5) The use of alternative measures in respect of a person who is alleged to have committed an offence is not a bar to any proceedings against the person under this Act.

heading: Laying of information, etc.
paragraph: (6) This section does not prevent any person from laying an information, obtaining the issue or confirmation of any process, or proceeding with the prosecution of any offence, in accordance with law.

heading: Terms and conditions in agreement
paragraph: 109 (1) An alternative measures agreement may contain any terms and conditions, including

heading: Terms and conditions in agreement
paragraph: (a) terms and conditions having any or all of the effects set out in section 105 or any other terms and conditions having any of the effects prescribed by regulations that the Attorney General, after consultation with the competent minister, considers appropriate; and

heading: Terms and conditions in agreement
paragraph: (b) terms and conditions relating to the costs associated with ensuring compliance with the agreement.

heading: Supervision of compliance
paragraph: (2) Any governmental organization may supervise compliance with the agreement.

heading: Duration of agreement
paragraph: 110 An alternative measures agreement comes into effect on the day on which it is concluded or on any later day that is specified in the agreement and continues in effect for a period of not more than three years.

heading: Filing in court for purpose of public access
paragraph: 111 (1) The Attorney General must consult the competent minister before concluding an alternative measures agreement and, subject to subsection (5), must have the agreement filed with the court in which the information was laid within 30 days after the agreement is concluded. The agreement is to be filed as part of the court record of the proceedings to which the public has access.

heading: Reports
paragraph: (2) A report relating to the administration of, and compliance with, the agreement must be filed with the same court by the Attorney General immediately after all the terms and conditions of the agreement have been complied with or the charges in respect of which the agreement was entered into have been dismissed.

heading: Third party information
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), if any of the following information is to be part of the agreement or the report, it must be set out in a schedule to the agreement or to the report:

heading: Third party information
paragraph: (a) trade secrets of any person;

heading: Third party information
paragraph: (b) financial, commercial, scientific or technical information that is confidential information and is treated consistently in a confidential manner by any person;

heading: Third party information
paragraph: (c) information the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to result in material financial loss or gain to any person, or could reasonably be expected to prejudice the competitive position of any person; or

heading: Third party information
paragraph: (d) information the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to interfere with contractual or other negotiations of any person.

heading: Agreement on information to be in schedule
paragraph: (4) The parties to the agreement must agree on which information that is to be part of the agreement or the report is information that meets the requirements of paragraphs (3)(a) to (d).

heading: How schedule is to be kept secret
paragraph: (5) The schedule is confidential and must not be filed with the court.

heading: Prohibition of disclosure
paragraph: (6) The competent minister must not disclose any information set out in a schedule to the agreement or to the report, except as authorized by section 117 or the Access to Information Act.

heading: Stay of proceedings
paragraph: 112 (1) Despite section 579 of the Criminal Code, the Attorney General must, on filing an alternative measures agreement, stay the proceedings in respect of the alleged offence, or apply to the court for an adjournment of the proceedings, for a period of not more than one year after the expiry of the agreement.

heading: Recommencement of proceedings
paragraph: (2) Proceedings stayed under subsection (1) may be recommenced without laying a new information or preferring a new indictment, as the case may be, by the Attorney General giving notice of the recommencement to the clerk of the court in which the stay of the proceedings was entered. If no such notice is given within one year after the expiry of the agreement, the proceedings are deemed to have never been commenced.

heading: Application to vary agreement
paragraph: 113 (1) Subject to subsections 111(2) and (3), the Attorney General may vary the terms and conditions of an alternative measures agreement on application by the person bound by the agreement and after consultation with the competent minister. The Attorney General must be of the opinion that the variation is desirable because of a material change in the circumstances since the agreement was concluded or last varied. The variation may include

heading: Application to vary agreement
paragraph: (a) decreasing the period for which the agreement is to remain in force; and

heading: Application to vary agreement
paragraph: (b) relieving the person of compliance with any condition that is specified in the agreement, either absolutely or partially or for any period that the Attorney General considers desirable.

heading: Filing varied agreement
paragraph: (2) An agreement that has been varied must be filed in accordance with section 111 with the court in which the original agreement was filed.

heading: Application of provisions dealing with records
paragraph: 114 Sections 115 to 117 apply only in respect of persons who have entered into an alternative measures agreement, regardless of the degree of their compliance with the terms and conditions of the agreement.

heading: Disclosure of information by peace officer or enforcement officer
paragraph: 115 Where it is necessary in the conduct of an investigation of an offence, a peace officer or enforcement officer may disclose to a department or agency of a government in Canada any information in a record relating to an offence alleged to have been committed by a person, including the original or a copy of any fingerprints or photographs of the person.

heading: Government records
paragraph: 116 (1) The competent minister, any enforcement officer and any department or agency of a government in Canada with which the competent minister has entered into an agreement under section 10 may keep records and use information obtained as a result of the use of alternative measures to deal with a person

heading: Government records
paragraph: (a) for the purposes of an inspection under this Act or an investigation of an offence alleged to have been committed by a person;

heading: Government records
paragraph: (b) in proceedings against a person under this Act;

heading: Government records
paragraph: (c) for the purpose of the administration of alternative measures programs; or

heading: Government records
paragraph: (d) otherwise for the administration of this Act.

heading: Private records
paragraph: (2) Any person or organization may keep records of information obtained by them as a result of supervising compliance with an alternative measures agreement and use the information for the purpose of supervising such compliance.

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: 117 (1) A record or information referred to in section 115 or 116 may be made available to

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (a) any judge or court for any purpose with respect to proceedings relating to offences under this or any other Act committed or alleged to have been committed by the person to whom the record relates;

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (b) any peace officer, enforcement officer or prosecutor

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (i) for the purpose of investigating an offence under this or any other Act that the person is suspected on reasonable grounds of having committed, or in respect of which the person has been arrested or charged, or

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (ii) for any purpose related to the administration of the case to which the record relates;

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (c) any member of a department or agency of a government in Canada, or any agent of such a government, that is

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (i) engaged in the administration of alternative measures in respect of the person, or

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (ii) preparing a report in respect of the person under this Act; or

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (d) any other person who is deemed, or any person within a class of persons that is deemed, by a judge of a court to have a valid interest in the record, to the extent directed by the judge, if

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (i) the judge is satisfied that the disclosure is desirable in the public interest for research or statistical purposes or in the interest of the proper administration of justice, and

heading: Disclosure of records
paragraph: (ii) the person gives a written undertaking not to subsequently disclose the information except in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Subsequent disclosure for research or statistical purposes
paragraph: (2) If a record is made available for inspection to any person under paragraph (1)(d) for research or statistical purposes, that person may subsequently disclose information contained in the record, but may not disclose the information in any form that would reasonably be expected to identify the person to whom it relates.

heading: Information, copies
paragraph: (3) A person to whom a record is authorized to be made available under this section may be given any information contained in the record and may be given a copy of any part of the record.

heading: Evidence
paragraph: (4) This section does not authorize the introduction into evidence of any part of a record that would not otherwise be admissible in evidence.

heading: Exception for public access to court record
paragraph: (5) For greater certainty, this section does not apply in respect of an alternative measures agreement, a varied alternative measures agreement or a report that is filed with the court in accordance with section 111.

heading: Information exchange agreements
paragraph: 118 The competent minister may enter into an agreement with a department or agency of a government in Canada respecting the exchange of information for the purpose of administering alternative measures or preparing a report in respect of a person's compliance with an alternative measures agreement.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 119 The competent minister may make regulations respecting the alternative measures that may be used for the purposes of this Act including regulations respecting

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) the form and manner in which and the period within which an application to participate in the alternative measures is to be made, and the information that must be contained in or accompany the application;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) the manner of preparing and filing reports relating to the administration of and compliance with alternative measures agreements;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) the types of costs, and the manner of paying the costs, associated with ensuring compliance with alternative measures agreements; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (d) the terms and conditions that may be included in an alternative measures agreement and the effects of those terms and conditions.

heading: Public registry
paragraph: 120 The Minister must establish a public registry for the purpose of facilitating access to documents relating to matters under this Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 121 The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister after consultation with the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations respecting the form of the public registry, the keeping of the public registry and access to it.

heading: Protection from proceedings
paragraph: 122 Despite any other Act of Parliament, no civil or criminal proceedings may be brought against Her Majesty in right of Canada, the Minister, the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or any person acting on behalf of or under the direction of any of them for the full or partial disclosure in good faith of any notice or other document through the public registry or any consequences of its disclosure.

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: 123 The public registry shall contain every document required to be included in the public registry by this Act and the following documents, or a copy of the following documents:

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (a) regulations and orders made under this Act;

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (b) agreements entered into under section 10;

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (c) COSEWIC's criteria for the classification of wildlife species;

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (d) status reports on wildlife species that COSEWIC has had prepared or has received with an application;

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (e) the List of Wildlife Species at Risk;

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (f) codes of practice, national standards or guidelines established under this Act;

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (g) agreements and reports filed under section 111 or subsection 113(2) or notices that those agreements or reports have been filed in court and are available to the public; and

heading: Documents to be in public registry
paragraph: (h) every report made under sections 126 and 128.

heading: Restriction
paragraph: 124 The Minister, on the advice of COSEWIC, may restrict the release of any information required to be included in the public registry if that information relates to the location of a wildlife species or its habitat and restricting its release would be in the best interests of the species.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: 125 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister and the President of the Treasury Board, after the Minister has consulted the Minister responsible for the Parks Canada Agency and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, make regulations

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing the fees and charges, or the manner of determining them, that may be charged for agreements or permits under section 73, for amendments to or for the renewal of such agreements or permits, for copies of documents in the public registry and for the inclusion of a document in the public registry;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) exempting any person or class of persons from the requirement to pay any of those fees or charges; and

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) generally, in respect of any condition or any other matter in relation to the payment of those fees or charges.

heading: Recovery of fees
paragraph: (2) A fee or charge required by the regulations to be paid constitutes a debt due to Her Majesty in right of Canada and may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: 126 The Minister must annually prepare a report on the administration of this Act during the preceding calendar year and must have a copy of the report tabled in each House of Parliament within the first 15 days that it is sitting after the completion of the report. The report must include a summary addressing the following matters:

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: (a) COSEWIC's assessments and the Minister's response to each of them;

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: (b) the preparation and implementation of recovery strategies, action plans and management plans;

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: (c) all agreements made under sections 10 to 13;

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: (d) all agreements entered into or renewed under section 73, all permits issued or renewed under that section and all agreements and permits amended under section 75 or exempted under section 76;

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: (e) enforcement and compliance actions taken, including the response to any requests for investigation;

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: (f) regulations and emergency orders made under this Act; and

heading: Annual report to Parliament
paragraph: (g) any other matters that the Minister considers relevant.

heading: Convening round table
paragraph: 127 (1) The Minister must, at least once every two years, convene a round table of persons interested in matters respecting the protection of wildlife species at risk in Canada to advise the Minister on those matters.

heading: Recommendations to be in public registry
paragraph: (2) Any written recommendations from the round table must be included in the public registry.

heading: Response of Minister
paragraph: (3) The Minister must respond to any written recommendations from the round table within 180 days after receiving them and a copy of the Minister's response must be included in the public registry.

heading: Reports on status of wildlife species
paragraph: 128 Five years after this section comes into force and at the end of each subsequent period of five years, the Minister must prepare a general report on the status of wildlife species. The Minister must have the report tabled in each House of Parliament within the first 15 days that it is sitting after the completion of the report.

heading: Parliamentary review of Act
paragraph: 129 Five years after this section comes into force, a committee of the House of Commons, of the Senate or of both Houses of Parliament is to be designated or established for the purpose of reviewing this Act.

heading: Assessment of status
paragraph: 130 (1) COSEWIC must assess the status of each wildlife species set out in Schedule 2 or 3, and, as part of the assessment, identify existing and potential threats to the species and

heading: Assessment of status
paragraph: (a) classify the species as extinct, extirpated, endangered, threatened or of special concern;

heading: Assessment of status
paragraph: (b) indicate that COSEWIC does not have sufficient information to classify the species; or

heading: Assessment of status
paragraph: (c) indicate that the species is not currently at risk.

heading: Time for assessment - Schedule 2
paragraph: (2) In the case of a species set out in Schedule 2, the assessment must be completed within 30 days after section 14 comes into force.

heading: Deemed classification
paragraph: (3) If an assessment of a wildlife species set out in Schedule 2 is not completed within the required time or, if there has been an extension, within the extended time, COSEWIC is deemed to have classified the species as indicated in Schedule 2.

heading: Time for assessment - Schedule 3
paragraph: (4) In the case of a species set out in Schedule 3, the assessment must be completed within one year after the competent minister requests the assessment. If there is more than one competent minister with respect to the species, they must make the request jointly.

heading: Extension
paragraph: (5) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Minister after consultation with the competent minister or ministers, by order, extend the time provided for the assessment of any species set out in Schedule 2 or 3. The Minister must include a statement in the public registry setting out the reasons for the extension.

heading: Provisions apply
paragraph: (6) Subsections 15(2) and (3) and 21(1) and section 25 apply with respect to assessments under subsection (1).

heading: Recent reports
paragraph: (7) In making its assessment of a wildlife species, COSEWIC may take into account and rely on any report on the species that was prepared in the two-year period before this Act receives royal assent.

heading: Section 27 applies
paragraph: 131 Section 27 applies in respect of a wildlife species referred to in section 130 that COSEWIC classifies as extinct, extirpated, endangered, threatened or of special concern or that is deemed to have been so classified.

heading: Time for recovery strategy
paragraph: 132 If a wildlife species is added to the List by the Governor in Council as the result of an assessment under section 130, the recovery strategy for the species must be prepared within three years after the listing in the case of an endangered species, and within four years in the case of a threatened species.

heading: Time for management plan
paragraph: 133 If a wildlife species is added to the List by the Governor in Council as a species of special concern as the result of an assessment under section 130, the management plan for the species must be prepared within five years after the listing.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
1		  
          In this regulation, "Act" means the Community Charter.

heading: Definitions for Part 2
paragraph: 1.1		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions for Part 2
paragraph: "alien invasive species" means the species listed in sections 1 and 2 of the Schedule;

heading: Definitions for Part 2
paragraph: "dangerous wildlife" has the same meaning as in the Wildlife Act;

heading: Definitions for Part 2
paragraph: "excluded pesticide" has the same meaning as in the Integrated Pest Management Regulation, B.C. Reg. 604/2004.

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: 2		  (1) For the purposes of section 9 (4) (a) (i) of the Act, a municipality may,

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (a) under section 8 (3) (j) of the Act, regulate, prohibit and impose requirements in relation to polluting or obstructing, or impeding the flow of, a stream, creek, waterway, watercourse, waterworks, ditch, drain or sewer, whether or not it is located on private property,

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (b) regulate, prohibit and impose requirements in relation to,

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (i)  under section 8 (3) (j) of the Act, the sale of wild flowers,

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (ii)  subject to subsection (2), under section 8 (3) (j) of the Act, the application of pesticides, except excluded pesticides, for the purpose of maintaining outdoor trees, shrubs, flowers, other ornamental plants and turf on a parcel or a part of a parcel if the parcel or part is used for residential purposes, or on land vested in the municipality,

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (iii)  under section 8 (3) (j) and (k) of the Act, the control and eradication of alien invasive species, and

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (iv)  under section 8 (3) (k) of the Act, the control of wildlife species listed in Schedule B or C to the Designation and Exemption Regulation, B.C. Reg. 168/90, and

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (c) under section 8 (3) (k) of the Act, regulate, prohibit and impose requirements respecting the feeding or attracting of dangerous wildlife or members of the family Cervidae.

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 9 (4) (b) of the Act, a municipality may not exercise the authority under subsection (1) (b) (ii) of this regulation in relation to the application of pesticides

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (a) for the management of pests that transmit human diseases or impact agriculture or forestry,

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (b) on the residential areas of farms,

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (c) to buildings or inside buildings, or

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (d) on land used for agriculture, forestry, transportation, public utilities or pipelines unless the public utility or pipeline is vested in the municipality.

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection 9 (4) (b) of the Act, the exercise of the authority under subsection (1) (c) is subject to the condition that the bylaw must exempt from its application all the following:

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (a) a person who is engaging in hunting or trapping wildlife in accordance with the Wildlife Act and its regulations;

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (b) a farm operation, as defined in section 1 of the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act, that

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (i)  is conducted on, in or over land anywhere in British Columbia, and

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (ii)  meets the requirements set out in section 2 (2) (a) and (c) of that Act;

heading: Municipal jurisdiction in relation to the environment and wildlife
paragraph: (c) a facility for the disposal of waste that is operated in accordance with the Environmental Management Act by a municipality, a regional district, an improvement district that has as an object the disposal of sewage or refuse or the provision of a system for the disposal of sewage or refuse or the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District.

paragraph: 3		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph:

            a commodity or product, whether by wholesale or retail;

heading: Definitions for Part 3

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (a) an assisted living residence as defined in section 1 of the Community Care              and Assisted Living Act;

heading: Definitions for Part 3

heading: Definitions for Part 3

heading: Definitions for Part 3

"customer" includes a person to whom a commodity or product is distributed for
            free;

heading: Definitions for Part 3

heading: Definitions for Part 3

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (b) a beverage cup sleeve;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (c) a condiment;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (d) a drinking straw;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (e) a garnish;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (f) a napkin;

heading: Definitions for Part 3

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (h) a wet wipe;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (a) who, in the ordinary course of business, prepares and serves food or              beverages to individuals, or

heading: Definitions for Part 3
Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: "food service ware" means any of the following types of container or packaging:

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (a) a bowl;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (b) a box or carton, including an egg carton;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (c) a cup;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (d) a hinged or lidded container;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (e) a plate;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (f) a platter;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (g) a tray;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: (h) film wrap;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
Definitions for Part 3
paragraph:
"packaging", except in section 9 (4) (b), means packaging as defined in section 1 (1)
            of the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph: "plastic" includes any type of compostable plastic and any type of biodegradable            plastic;

heading: Definitions for Part 3

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph:
(a) cook, slice, chop, mix, brew, squeeze or otherwise make ready to eat or

heading: Definitions for Part 3
paragraph:
(b) remove from a container or packaging and place or repackage in a different
              container or package;

heading: Definitions for Part 3

"single-use", when used in reference to an item, means the item is ordinarily

heading: Authority of municipality
paragraph:

		  For the purposes of section 9 (4) (a) (i) of the Act, a municipality may, under section 8 (3) (j) of the Act, regulate, prohibit and impose requirements in relation to the protection of the natural environment in accordance with this Part.

paragraph:

paragraph:
(2) For the purposes of section 9 (4) (b) of the Act, the exercise of the authority under

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
7
		  (1) A municipality may do any of the following:

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(a) prohibit a business operator from distributing or selling a shopping bag
              other than a recycled paper bag or reusable bag;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(b) require that a business operator report to the municipality respecting the
              sale or distribution of shopping bags.

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(2) For the purposes of section 9 (4) (b) of the Act, the exercise of the authority under
            subsection (1) (a) is subject to the following conditions:

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(a) the bylaw must permit a business operator to provide a recycled paper bag
              or reusable bag on payment of a charge for the bag, as follows:

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph: (i)  at least $0.25 for each recycled paper bag;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph: (ii)  at least $2 for each reusable bag;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(b) the bylaw must include an exemption from the payment of the charge if any
              of the following apply:

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph: (i)  the bag is a used bag;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph: (ii)  the bag is a paper bag that is less than 15 cm by 20 cm when flat;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(iii)  the bag is a recycled paper bag and is distributed to facilitate the
                transport of any of the following:

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(A) a drug specified in Schedule I, IA, II or III of the Drug
                  Schedules Regulation;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph: (B) a device as defined in the Pharmaceutical Services Act;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(iv)  the business operator is a food service provider, and the bag is a                recycled paper bag that is distributed for any of the following
                purposes:

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(A) to facilitate the transport of food or beverages that are prepared
                  by the business operator and purchased for delivery;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(B) to contain prepared food or beverages served to a customer
                  through a window at a drive-through restaurant;

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph: (v)  the bag

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph: (A) is a recycled paper bag, reusable bag or used bag, and

heading: Shopping bags
paragraph:
(B) contains food, beverages or personal hygiene products that are
                  to be provided directly or indirectly to an individual for free or
                  at reduced cost by a society or by a registered charity as defined
                  in section 248 (1) of the Income Tax Act (Canada).

heading: Bag charge not a fee payable to municipality
paragraph:
8		  An amount referred to in section 7 (2) (a) must not be collected by the municipality as
          a fee payable to the municipality.

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph:
(a) food service ware that is wholly composed of paper or a plant fibre material
              and lined with compostable plastic;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material

(b) food or beverages intended for sale or distribution to a person outside
              British Columbia;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph: (c) film wrap that is wholly composed of polyvinyl chloride.

paragraph:
(3) For the purposes of section 9 (4) (b) of the Act, the exercise of the authority under

            subsections (5) and (6), exclude from its application all of the following:

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph:
(a) food or beverages intended for sale or distribution to a person outside
              British Columbia;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph: (b) film wrap that is wholly composed of polyvinyl chloride;

              of the following types of food, whether fresh or frozen:

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph: (i)  raw meat;

paragraph: (ii)  raw poultry;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph: (iii)  raw fish in a state not ready to be eaten.

paragraph:
(4) For the purposes of section 9 (4) (b) of the Act, the exercise of the authority under
            subsection (1) (c) is subject to the condition that the bylaw must, subject to
            subsections (5) and (6), exclude from its application all of the following:

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph:
(a) food service ware intended for sale or distribution to a person outside
              British Columbia;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph: (c) film wrap that is wholly composed of polyvinyl chloride;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph: (i)  raw meat;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material
paragraph: (ii)  raw poultry;

heading: Food service ware composed of specified material

heading: Single-use food service accessories
paragraph:
10
		  (1) A municipality may prohibit a food service provider from distributing or selling
            a single-use food service accessory.

heading: Single-use food service accessories
paragraph:
