heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "3-year period", in relation to a spill contingency plan, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the period of 3 calendar years beginning with the calendar year immediately after the calendar year in which the plan is first prepared, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) each subsequent period of 3 calendar years;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "breakout tank" means a tank, attached to a pipeline, used to relieve surges in the pipeline and store the substance being transported for reinsertion into the pipeline;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "contact information", in relation to a person, means the address, telephone number and, if any, email address of the person;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "discussion-based test" means an exercise or drill, based on a simulated spill of a regulated substance, that is not an operations-based test;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "disposal", in relation to waste, includes the treatment, recycling, storage and destruction of the waste;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "heritage feature" means a heritage site or heritage object designated under section 9 (1) [heritage designation] of the Heritage Conservation Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "highway" has the same meaning as in the Transportation Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "highway transporter" means a regulated person referred to in section 2 (1) (b) (ii) [regulated person] of the Spill Preparedness, Response and Recovery Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "means of containment" has the same meaning as in the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992 (Canada);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "operations-based test" means an exercise or drill, based on a simulated spill of a regulated substance, that involves

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the deployment of equipment, personnel and other resources, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the implementation of spill response procedures;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pipeline" has the same meaning as in the Spill Preparedness, Response and Recovery Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pipeline transporter" means a regulated person referred to in section 2 (1) (a) of the Spill Preparedness, Response and Recovery Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protected area" means an area of land set out in Column 1 of the Schedule that is established, named, designated or otherwise prescribed under the Act listed opposite in Column 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "railway transporter" means a regulated person referred to in section 2 (1) (b) (i) of the Spill Preparedness, Response and Recovery Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regulated substance", in relation to a regulated person or the regulated person's spill contingency plan, means the substance in respect of which the regulated person is a regulated person;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "specified quantity" has the meaning set out in section 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "spill response equipment" has the same meaning as in the Spill Preparedness, Response and Recovery Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "spill response planning zone", in relation to a regulated person and a regulated substance, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the area in which the person transports the substance, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the surrounding area that could be affected by the worst case scenario of a spill of the specified quantity of the substance at a location within the area described in paragraph (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife" means any of the following, including eggs and juvenile stages, but excluding controlled alien species as defined in the Wildlife Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any of the following, as defined in the Wildlife Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  raptors;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  threatened species;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  endangered species;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iv)  game;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) species of vertebrates prescribed as wildlife under the Wildlife Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) fish from or in the non-tidal waters of British Columbia;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "worst-case-scenario test" means an operations-based test that is based on a simulation of the worst case scenario of a spill of the specified quantity of a regulated substance.

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: 2		  (1) The specified quantity in relation to the transportation of a regulated substance is the following, as applicable:

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (a) in the case of transportation through a pipeline, the greatest of

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (i)  the quantity of the largest historic spill from the pipeline,

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (ii)  the volume of the largest breakout tank, or battery of breakout tanks, without a secondary containment system, and

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (iii)  the quantity calculated in accordance with subsection (2);

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (b) in the case of transportation by railway, the greater of

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (i)  the maximum quantity that could be transported by a single rail car operated by the regulated person, and

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (ii)  20% of the maximum quantity that could be transported by a train operated by the regulated person;

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (c) in the case of transportation on a highway, the maximum quantity that could be transported by a single motor vehicle, including trailers, if any, attached to the motor vehicle operated by the regulated person.

heading: Specified quantity
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1) (a) (iii), the quantity is to be calculated as follows:

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph:
3
		  For the purposes of section 91.11 (1) (a) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act, a spill contingency plan must address the worst case scenario of a spill of the specified quantity of the regulated substance and must contain all of the following:

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the regulated person;

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) a declaration that the spill contingency plan is true, accurate and complete, signed by any of the following, as applicable:

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (i)  if the regulated person is an individual, the regulated person;

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (ii)  if the regulated person is a corporation, a director or officer of the regulated person;

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (iii)  if the regulated person is a partnership,

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (A) a partner who is an individual, or

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (B) a director or officer of a partner that is a corporation;

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (c) the information required by the following sections:

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (i)  section 4 [hazard assessment];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (ii)  section 5 [spill response planning map];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (iii)  section 6 [equipment, personnel and other resources];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (iv)  section 7 [incident command system];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (v)  section 8 [human health and safety];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (vi)  section 9 [communication procedures];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (vii)  section 10 [waste management];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (viii)  section 11 [wildlife];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (ix)  section 12 [spill response procedures];

heading: Contents of spill contingency plan
paragraph: (x)  section 13 [training].

heading: Hazard assessment
paragraph:
4
		  (1) The spill contingency plan must contain the following information about the regulated substance:

heading: Hazard assessment
paragraph: (a) a description of the properties of the substance that are relevant to its potential to cause adverse effects to the environment, human health or infrastructure;

heading: Hazard assessment
paragraph: (b) a description of the types and sizes of the means of containment used

heading: Hazard assessment
paragraph: (i)  to transport the substance, and

heading: Hazard assessment
paragraph: (ii)  if the regulated person is a pipeline transporter, to store the substance incidentally to its transportation;

heading: Hazard assessment
paragraph: (c) an assessment of the magnitude of the risk to the environment, human health and infrastructure that would result from the worst case scenario of a spill of the specified quantity of the substance.

heading: Hazard assessment
paragraph: (2) The assessment referred to in subsection (1) (c) must identify the aspects of the environment, human health and infrastructure that are at risk of being adversely affected by that spill.

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph:
5
		  (1) If the regulated person is a pipeline transporter or railway transporter, the spill contingency plan must contain a map of the spill response planning zone for the regulated substance that shows all of the following:

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (a) the corridors along which the substance is transported;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (b) the facilities used in or related to the transportation of the substance;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (c) roads;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (d) evacuation routes;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (e) topographical features relevant to the movement of or response to a spill of the substance;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (f) potential response staging sites and potential spill control points;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (g) locations of all of the following, as applicable:

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (i)  bodies of water;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (ii)  wetlands;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (iii)  protected areas;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (iv)  heritage features;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (v)  key infrastructure, including, without limitation, dams and major public and industrial water intakes;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (vi)  areas of human habitation and recreation activities and areas that include hospitals, schools and other public facilities.

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (2) If the regulated person is a highway transporter, the spill contingency plan must contain a map of the area in which the regulated person regularly transports the regulated substance that shows all of the following:

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (a) if the regulated person uses a regular route, the roads along which the regulated person regularly transports the regulated substance;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (b) topographical features relevant to the movement of or response to a spill of the substance;

heading: Spill response planning map
paragraph: (c) bodies of water.

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The spill contingency plan must contain the following information:

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (a) a list of the equipment, personnel and other resources that the regulated person intends to use in responding to and cleaning up the worst case scenario of a spill of the specified quantity of the regulated substance;

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (b) for each piece of spill response equipment listed for the purposes of paragraph (a) that is maintained by or on behalf of the regulated person,

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (i)  a copy of records evidencing the inspection and maintenance of the equipment, or

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (ii)  a copy of any agreement under which a person other than the regulated person agrees

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (A) to be responsible for the inspection and maintenance of the equipment, and

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (B) to maintain, and produce to the minister on request, records evidencing the inspection and maintenance of the equipment.

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1) (a), the list must include equipment, personnel and other resources to be used for the following purposes, if applicable:

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (a) if the regulated substance is flammable, firefighting;

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (b) if the regulated substance is harmful to human health, first aid;

heading: Equipment, personnel and other resources
paragraph: (c) if the regulated substance is volatile and harmful to human health, air-quality monitoring.

heading: Incident command system
paragraph:
7
		  (1) If the regulated person is a pipeline transporter or railway transporter, the spill contingency plan must identify the following:

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (a) the roles in the incident command system, which must include at least the following:

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (i)  incident commander;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (ii)  information officer;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (iii)  liaison officer;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (iv)  safety officer;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (v)  chiefs of the following sections:

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (A) administration / finance;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (B) logistics;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (C) operations;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (D) planning;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (b) for each of those roles, the job titles of one primary and 2 alternate individuals who are to fill the role.

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (2) If the regulated person is a highway transporter, the spill contingency plan must identify the following:

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (a) the roles in the incident command system, which must include at least the following:

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (i)  incident commander;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (ii)  information officer;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (iii)  liaison officer;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (iv)  safety officer;

heading: Incident command system
paragraph: (b) for each of the roles, the job titles of one primary and one alternate individual who are to fill the role.

heading: Human health and safety
paragraph:
8
		  The spill contingency plan must include procedures for

heading: Human health and safety
paragraph: (a) protecting the health and safety of individuals involved in spill response actions, and

heading: Human health and safety
paragraph: (b) controlling access to and ensuring safety at locations where spill response actions are carried out.

heading: Communication procedures
paragraph:
9
		  (1) The spill contingency plan must include procedures for

heading: Communication procedures
paragraph: (a) communications among spill response personnel, and

heading: Communication procedures
paragraph: (b) communications with the public about the spill, including, without limitation, procedures for

heading: Communication procedures
paragraph: (i)  providing information to the public, and

heading: Communication procedures
paragraph: (ii)  gathering information from the public.

heading: Communication procedures
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (b) does not apply in relation to a highway transporter.

heading: Waste management
paragraph:
10
		  (1) The spill contingency plan must include waste management procedures for waste resulting from a spill of the regulated substance that identify all of the following:

heading: Waste management
paragraph: (a) locations at which the waste might be stored temporarily before being transported to a facility referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Waste management
paragraph: (b) persons who might transport the waste;

heading: Waste management
paragraph: (c) facilities at which the waste might be received for disposal.

heading: Waste management
paragraph: (2) If the waste resulting from a spill of the regulated substance is likely to be hazardous waste,

heading: Waste management
paragraph: (a) the persons identified for the purposes of subsection (1) (b) must include persons licensed under the Act to transport the waste, and

heading: Waste management
paragraph: (b) the facilities identified for the purposes of subsection (1) (c) must include facilities authorized under the Act to receive the waste for disposal.

heading: Waste management
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) (a) does not apply in relation to a highway transporter.

heading: Wildlife
paragraph:
11
		  (1) If the assessment referred to in section 4 (1) (c) [hazard assessment] identifies potential adverse effects to wildlife, the spill contingency plan must describe the following:

heading: Wildlife
paragraph: (a) procedures to deter the wildlife from the spill site, reduce attractants to the wildlife at the spill site or otherwise reduce the presence of the wildlife at, or manage the access of the wildlife to, the spill site;

heading: Wildlife
paragraph: (b) potential sites at which the wildlife could be tended to;

heading: Wildlife
paragraph: (c) persons with relevant expertise who could be called on to assist with tending to the wildlife.

heading: Wildlife
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (b) does not apply in relation to a highway transporter.

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph:
12
		  (1) The spill contingency plan must, in accordance with this section, include spill response procedures that address the following topics:

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (a) initial assessment of the spill;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (b) notification of persons about the spill;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (c) spill response actions;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (d) monitoring and documenting of

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (i)  the spill, and

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (ii)  actions described in paragraphs (a) to (c).

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (2) Procedures for initial assessment of the spill must include procedures for the following:

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (a) identifying and evaluating the immediate risks to and impacts on the environment, human health and infrastructure;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (b) classifying spills, which must be based on at least the following factors:

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (i)  the substance spilled;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (ii)  the quantity of the substance spilled;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (iii)  the location and circumstances of the spill;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (c) assessing

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (i)  what is to be done to protect the safety of spill response personnel and the public, and

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (ii)  whether evacuation is necessary.

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (3) Procedures for notifying persons about the spill must

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (a) identify the following:

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (i)  the obligation to report the spill to the Provincial Emergency Program under section 4 (1) [initial report] of the Spill Reporting Regulation and the telephone number specified in that section for reporting;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (ii)  directors, officers, employees and contractors of the regulated person who are to be notified, the order in which they are to be notified and their contact information;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (iii)  governments and other public agencies that are to be notified and their contact information, and

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (b) include procedures for notifying persons who might need to take protective action in relation to the spill.

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (4) Procedures for spill response actions must include procedures for the following:

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (a) identifying and documenting the location and movement of, and the area covered by, the spill;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (b) assessing the current and potential adverse effects of the spill on the environment, human health and infrastructure;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (c) mobilizing, deploying and maintaining the ongoing sufficiency of equipment, personnel and other resources;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (d) establishing the incident command post;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (e) controlling the source of the spill;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (f) stabilizing, containing, removing and cleaning up the spill and waste resulting from the spill or spill response actions;

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (g) protecting the aspects of the environment, human health and infrastructure

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (i)  referred to in section 5 (1) (g) or (2) (c) [spill response planning map], or

heading: Spill response procedures
paragraph: (ii)  identified in the assessment referred to in section 4 (1) (c) [hazard assessment] as at risk of being adversely affected by a spill.

heading: Training
paragraph:
13
		  (1) The spill contingency plan must describe the training that will be provided to the following individuals on the following topics and how frequently that training will be provided:

heading: Training
paragraph: (a) each individual who holds a job title identified for the purposes of section 7 (1) (a) or (2) (a) [incident command system], on the individual's role in the incident command system;

heading: Training
paragraph: (b) each individual referred to in subsection (2) who might be involved in responding to a spill, on the procedures, referred to in the following sections, that are relevant to the involvement of that individual:

heading: Training
paragraph: (i)  section 8 [human health and safety];

heading: Training
paragraph: (ii)  section 9 [communication procedures];

heading: Training
paragraph: (iii)  section 10 [waste management];

heading: Training
paragraph: (iv)  section 11 [wildlife];

heading: Training
paragraph: (v)  section 12 [spill response procedures].

heading: Training
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (b) applies in relation to the following individuals:

heading: Training
paragraph: (a) if the regulated person is an individual, the regulated person;

heading: Training
paragraph: (b) an individual employed or retained by the regulated person.

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph:
14
		  (1) For the purposes of section 91.11 (1) (b) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act, a regulated person who has a spill contingency plan must, at the frequency required by subsection (2) of this section, review the plan and make updates, if necessary, to

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) correct deficiencies in the plan, or

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) adjust the plan to reflect changed circumstances.

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (2) The regulated person must review and update the spill contingency plan

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) at least once each calendar year, and

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) within one month after any of the following events occur:

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (i)  a change in the regulated substances, or the quantities of the regulated substances, transported by the regulated person that could result in a material increase to the magnitude of the risk referred to in section 91.11 (2) of the Act;

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (ii)  a vacancy in one of the jobs that is noted by title in the plan for the purposes of section 7 (1) (a) or (2) (a) [incident command system];

heading: Reviewing and updating spill contingency plan
paragraph: (iii)  spill response equipment noted in the plan is no longer available.

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph:
15
		  (1) For the purposes of section 91.11 (1) (b) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act, a regulated person who has a spill contingency plan must test the plan, in accordance with this section, every 3-year period by conducting

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) at least one worst-case-scenario test, and

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) in every calendar year in the 3-year period that is not a calendar year in which the regulated person conducts a worst-case-scenario test,

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (i)  at least one discussion-based test, and

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (ii)  at least one operations-based test.

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (2) The tests conducted for the purposes of this section must

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) cover, in each 3-year period, at least the components of the plan that are referred to in section 16, so as to ensure that the plan demonstrates that the regulated person has the capability to effectively respond to a spill,

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) involve individuals who, in the event of a spill, would be deployed or otherwise involved in implementing the components of the plan that are being tested but need not involve more than the minimum number of those individuals necessary to implement those components, and

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (c) in the case of a worst-case-scenario test, be conducted in British Columbia.

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (3) A regulated person who has a spill contingency plan must, on request of the director,

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) inform the director of the dates of the tests that the regulated person has conducted, or plans to conduct, for the purposes of this section in the current 3-year period,

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) give to the director information or records relating to the tests referred to in paragraph (a), and

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (c) allow the director, or an individual authorized by the director, to observe any test that the regulated person plans to conduct for the purposes of this section.

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (1) (a), a highway transporter is not required to conduct a worst-case-scenario test.

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (5) Despite subsections (1) and (2) (a), a regulated person is not required

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) to test a component of the plan in a 3-year period that was implemented in response to an actual spill in the 3-year period, or

heading: Testing spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) to carry out a worst-case-scenario test in a 3-year period if the regulated person suffers the worst case scenario of a spill of the specified quantity of the regulated substance in the 3-year period.

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph:
16
		  The components of a spill contingency plan to be tested for the purposes of section 15 (2) (a) are the following:

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (a) section 12 (3) [notification];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (b) section 12 (4) (c) [mobilization, deployment and ongoing sufficiency] as it relates to the mobilization and deployment of spill response equipment and spill response personnel;

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (c) section 12 (4) (c) as it relates to maintaining the ongoing sufficiency of equipment, personnel and other resources;

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (d) sections 7 [incident command system] and 12 (4) (d) [incident command post];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (e) section 12 (4) (e) [source control];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (f) section 12 (2) and (4) (b) [initial and ongoing assessments];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (g) section 12 (4) (f) [stabilizing, containing, removing and cleaning up];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (h) section 12 (4) (g) [protection of aspects of environment, human health and infrastructure];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (i) section 12 (1) (d) [monitoring and documentation];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (j) section 9 [communication];

heading: Components to be tested
paragraph: (k) section 10 [waste management].

heading: Availability of spill contingency plan to employees
paragraph:
17
		  For the purposes of section 91.11 (1) (c) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act, a regulated person who is a highway transporter and has a spill contingency plan must ensure that each motor vehicle used by the regulated person to transport the regulated substance contains a copy of the parts of the plan that address

heading: Availability of spill contingency plan to employees
paragraph: (a) the procedures referred to in section 12 (2) [initial assessment],

heading: Availability of spill contingency plan to employees
paragraph: (b) the procedures referred to in section 12 (3) [notification], and

heading: Availability of spill contingency plan to employees
paragraph: (c) the procedures referred to in section 12 (4) [spill response actions] in which a driver might be involved.

paragraph: Schedule

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "highway" has the same meaning as in the Transportation Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Indian reserve" has the same meaning as "reserve" in the Indian Act (Canada);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "listed substance" means a substance identified by a standard set out in Column 2 of the Schedule, or any combination of those substances, but does not include hazardous waste;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "national park" has the same meaning as "park" in the Canada National Parks Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "national park reserve" has the same meaning as "park reserve" in the Canada National Parks Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "pipeline" includes a facility used to

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) transport a substance through a pipeline, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) store a substance incidentally to its transportation through a pipeline;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "spill response equipment" means equipment used directly in responding to a spill, including, without limitation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) personal protective equipment, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) equipment used to stabilize, contain, remove or clean up a spill or waste resulting from the spill or spill response actions.

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: 2		  (1) For the purposes of the definition of "regulated person" in section 91.1 [definitions] of the Act, the following substances in the following quantities are prescribed:

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (a) a listed substance in any quantity, in the case of a person who transports the substance through a pipeline;

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (b) a listed substance in a quantity of 10 000 litres or more, in the case of

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (i)  a person who transports the substance by railway, or

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (ii)  a person who transports the substance on a highway.

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a person is not a regulated person in respect of the transportation of a substance in the following circumstances:

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (a) the substance is being transported through a pipeline at a facility that

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (i)  uses, produces or refines the substance, or

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (ii)  stores the substance other than incidentally to its transportation through a pipeline;

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (b) the substance is in a fuel tank of a train or motor vehicle and is being used, or intended to be used, to propel the train or motor vehicle;

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (c) the substance is being transported only within the area of an airport, Indian reserve, military installation, national park or national park reserve;

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (d) the substance is being transported by a railway that is operated only within an area of land on which is located industrial infrastructure, including, without limitation,

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (i)  facilities for manufacturing or processing, and

heading: Regulated person
paragraph: (ii)  mines, well sites, equipment yards and other facilities for or ancillary to energy production or resource extraction.

heading: Deadline to prepare spill contingency plan
paragraph:
3
		  (1) For the purposes of section 91.11 (1) (a) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act, a regulated person must have a spill contingency plan by the following date:

heading: Deadline to prepare spill contingency plan
paragraph: (a) for a regulated person referred to in section 2 (1) (a) or (b) (i), April 30, 2018;

heading: Deadline to prepare spill contingency plan
paragraph: (b) for a regulated person referred to in section 2 (b) (ii), October 30, 2018.

heading: Deadline to prepare spill contingency plan
paragraph: (2) On application by a person referred to in subsection (1), the minister may specify a later date, that is not more than 6 months later than the applicable date under subsection (1) (a) or (b), by which the regulated person must have a spill contingency plan.

heading: Exemption in relation to energy resource permits
paragraph:
4
		  A person who holds a permit to carry out an energy resource activity to which the Emergency Management Regulation, B.C. Reg. 204/2013, applies is exempt from section 91.11 [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act.

heading: Recovery of costs of government spill response
paragraph:
5
		  (1) If the government incurs costs referred to in section 91.4 (3) [government spill response] of the Act that total less than $175, those costs are deemed to be $175.

heading: Recovery of costs of government spill response
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 91.4 (4) (b) of the Act, the prescribed percentage is 25% of the costs referred to in section 91.4 (3) of the Act.

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A responsible person who is ordered under section 91.2 (4) [responsible persons - spill response] of the Act to prepare a recovery plan in relation to a spill must include all of the following information in the plan:

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (a) the substance spilled;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (b) the amount of the substance spilled;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (c) a description of the properties of the substance spilled that are relevant to its potential to cause adverse effects to the environment, human health or infrastructure;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (d) an assessment, prepared in accordance with subsection (2), of the potential impacts on the environment of the spill and the spill response actions carried out in relation to the spill;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (e) an assessment, prepared in accordance with subsection (2), of the actual impacts on the environment of the spill and the spill response actions carried out in relation to the spill;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (f) a description of the environment in the area affected by the spill, as that environment was before the spill;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (g) a description of the environment in the area affected by the spill, as that environment will be after the recovery plan is implemented, that identifies, in accordance with subsection (3), quantifiable targets for recovery;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (h) a description of the recovery actions proposed to meet the targets referred to in paragraph (g) and an analysis, prepared in accordance with subsection (3), in support of those recovery actions that identifies and weighs alternatives;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (i) a summary of engagement and consultation with any of the following that might be directly affected by the proposed recovery actions or have knowledge about that area:

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (i)  a local government;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (ii)  a first nation government;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (iii)  a resident;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (iv)  a business;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (v)  a recreational organization;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (j) a description of the process for communicating with the persons referred to in paragraph (i) during the implementation of the plan;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (k) a schedule for the implementation of the plan.

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (2) An assessment under subsection (1) (d) or (e) must

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (a) describe and quantify the severity and geographical extent of the impacts on the environment of the spill and the spill response actions carried out in relation to the spill, and

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (b) identify all of the following:

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (i)  the contaminants introduced into or created in the environment by the spill or the spill response actions carried out in relation to the spill;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (ii)  the flora, fauna and human populations that could be adversely affected by those contaminants;

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (iii)  the pathways by which those contaminants could move through the environment to cause adverse effects to those flora, fauna and human populations.

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (3) The identification of quantifiable targets for recovery referred to in subsection (1) (g) and the proposal of recovery actions and analysis of alternatives referred to in subsection (1) (h) must be based on the principle that the impacts of a spill on the environment are to be restored to the greatest extent that is consistent with the limits set out in section 91.21 (1) (a) (i), (ii) and (iii) [when restoration not reasonably achievable] of the Act.

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (1) (i) and without limiting that subsection,

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (a) a first nation government must be considered to be directly affected if the proposed recovery actions are likely to affect a culturally sensitive site or a site used for food gathering,

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (b) a resident must be considered to be directly affected if the proposed recovery actions are likely to affect the health or livelihood or require the relocation of the resident, and

heading: Contents of recovery plan
paragraph: (c) a business must be considered to be directly affected if the proposed recovery actions are likely to affect the profitability or require the relocation of the business.

heading: Report on conclusion of recovery process
paragraph:
7
		  A responsible person who is required by section 91.2 (6) (c) [responsible persons - spill response] of the Act to submit a report at the conclusion of a recovery process must include all of the following information in the report:

heading: Report on conclusion of recovery process
paragraph: (a) a declaration that the recovery plan has been carried out;

heading: Report on conclusion of recovery process
paragraph: (b) the date on which carrying out of the recovery plan was completed;

heading: Report on conclusion of recovery process
paragraph: (c) a description of the recovery actions carried out;

heading: Report on conclusion of recovery process
paragraph: (d) a description of the environment at the conclusion of the recovery process;

heading: Report on conclusion of recovery process
paragraph: (e) a record of sampling, testing, monitoring and assessing carried out, the data generated that demonstrates that the recovery plan has been carried out and a summary of that data.

heading: Records relating to hazard assessments
paragraph:
8
		  For the purposes of section 91.11 (3) (a) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act, the period during which a regulated person must ensure that records respecting investigations, tests and surveys referred to in section 91.11 (2) of the Act are kept is the period during which the person has a spill contingency plan to which the records relate.

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph:
9
		  (1) A regulated person who has a spill contingency plan must maintain the following records:

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (a) a record of changes to the plan that shows, for each change, the date the change was made and the reason for the change;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (b) a record in relation to the spill response equipment listed in the plan that shows

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (i)  the dates on which each item on the list was inspected and whether the item was ready for use on each date, and

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (ii)  the dates on which each item on the list was maintained or repaired;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (c) a record of the training referred to in section 13 (1) [training] of the Spill Contingency Planning Regulation that includes the following for each course of training provided:

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (i)  the dates of the training;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (ii)  a description of the training;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (iii)  the person who provided the training;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (iv)  the roles and procedures, as applicable, on which the training was provided;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (v)  the names and job titles of the individuals to whom the training was provided;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (d) a record of the tests conducted by the regulated person for the purposes of section 15 [testing spill contingency plans] of the Spill Contingency Planning Regulation that shows the following for each test:

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (i)  the date of the test;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (ii)  a description of the test;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (iii)  whether the test is a discussion-based test, an operations-based test or a worst-case-scenario test;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (iv)  the components of the spill contingency plan tested;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (v)  the records generated by the individuals who participated in the test;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (vi)  an evaluation of the components tested that identifies any deficiencies in the components revealed by the test or changes to the components suggested by the test;

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (vii)  if applicable, the changes made to the spill contingency plan in response to the test and the dates on which those changes were made.

heading: Records relating to spill contingency plans
paragraph: (2) The regulated person must keep each record referred to in subsection (1) for at least 5 years.

heading: Records relating to service arrangements
paragraph:
10
		  If a regulated person enters into an arrangement with another person respecting the use of the other person's services to meet obligations of the regulated person under Division 2.1 [Spill Preparedness, Response and Recovery] of Part 7 of the Act in relation to spill contingency planning or spill response actions, the regulated person must keep any records relating to the arrangement for at least 5 years after that arrangement comes to an end.

heading: Requirement to produce records to minister
paragraph:
11
		  A regulated person who is required by section 91.11 (3) (a) [regulated persons - spill contingency planning] of the Act or this regulation to keep a record must produce the record to the minister on request.

heading: Report to the Legislative Assembly
paragraph:
12
		  A report under section 91.7 [report to the Legislative Assembly] of the Act is to be laid before the Legislative Assembly

heading: Report to the Legislative Assembly
paragraph: (a) for the period beginning on the date section 91.7 of the Act comes into force, on or before October 30, 2019, and

heading: Report to the Legislative Assembly
paragraph: (b) thereafter, annually.

heading: Report to the Legislative Assembly
paragraph: Schedule

heading: Interpretation
paragraph:
1
		  A reference in this Schedule to a standard is a reference to that standard as amended from time to time.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "body of water" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a stream, as defined in the Water Sustainability Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an aquifer, as defined in the Water Sustainability Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) fish habitat, as defined in the Water Sustainability Regulation, B.C. Reg. 36/2016, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) any of the following that could drain or empty directly into a body of water:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a naturally formed pool of water other than one referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a ditch;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "contact information", in relation to a person, means the address, telephone number and, if any, email address of the person;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "emergency response completion date", in relation to a spill, has the meaning given in section 8 [emergency response completion date];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "listed quantity", in relation to a listed substance, means the quantity listed in Column 2 of the Schedule opposite the listed substance or, if more than one quantity is listed, the highest of those quantities;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "listed substance" means a substance listed in Column 1 of the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Provincial Emergency Program" has the same meaning as in the Emergency Program Act.

heading: Reportable spills
paragraph: 2		  This regulation applies for the purposes of section 91.2 (1) (a) [responsible persons - spill response] of the Act in relation to a spill of a listed substance, other than natural gas, if

heading: Reportable spills
paragraph: (a) the spill enters, or is likely to enter, a body of water, or

heading: Reportable spills
paragraph: (b) the quantity of the substance spilled is, or is likely to be, equal to or greater than the listed quantity for the listed substance.

heading: Reportable spills of natural gas
paragraph:
3
		  This regulation applies for the purposes of section 91.2 (1) (a) [responsible persons - spill response] of the Act in relation to a spill of natural gas if

heading: Reportable spills of natural gas
paragraph: (a) the spill is caused by a break in a pipeline or fitting operated above 100 psi that results in a sudden and uncontrolled release of natural gas, and

heading: Reportable spills of natural gas
paragraph: (b) the quantity of natural gas spilled is, or is likely to be, equal to or greater than the listed quantity for natural gas.

heading: Initial report
paragraph:
4
		  (1) If a spill occurs or is at imminent risk of occurring, a responsible person must ensure that the actual or potential spill is immediately reported to the Provincial Emergency Program by calling 1-800-663-3456.

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (2) A report under this section must include, to the extent practicable, the following information:

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (a) the contact information for

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (i)  the individual making the report,

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (ii)  the responsible person in relation to the spill, and

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (iii)  the owner of the substance spilled;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (b) the date and time of the spill;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (c) the location of the spill site;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (d) a description of the spill site and the surrounding area;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (e) a description of the source of the spill;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (f) the type and quantity of the substance spilled;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (g) a description of the circumstances, cause and adverse effects of the spill;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (h) details of action taken or proposed to comply with section 91.2 (2) [responsible persons - spill response] of the Act;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (i) the names of the government, federal government, local government and first nation government agencies at the spill site;

heading: Initial report
paragraph: (j) the names of other persons or government, federal government, local government or first nation government agencies advised about the spill.

heading: Updates to minister
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A responsible person for a spill that occurs on or after October 30, 2018 must, until the emergency response completion date, submit written reports on the spill to the minister in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Updates to minister
paragraph: (2) A report under subsection (1) must be made

heading: Updates to minister
paragraph: (a) as soon as practicable on request of the minister,

heading: Updates to minister
paragraph: (b) at least once every 30 days after the date the spill began, and

heading: Updates to minister
paragraph: (c) at any time the responsible person has reason to believe that information previously reported by the responsible person under section 4 or this section was or has become inaccurate or incomplete.

heading: Updates to minister
paragraph: (3) A report under this section must be made in the manner and form specified by the minister and must include, to the extent practicable, the information set out in section 6 (2).

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The responsible person for a spill that occurs on or after October 30, 2018 must submit a written report on the spill to the minister within 30 days after the emergency response completion date for that spill.

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (2) A report under this section must be made in the manner and form specified by the minister and must include the following information:

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (a) the contact information of

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (i)  the responsible person, and

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (ii)  the owner of the substance spilled;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (b) the date, time and duration of the spill;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (c) the location of the spill site, which must be specified by

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (i)  its address, if any, and

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (ii)  its latitude and longitude;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (d) a description of the spill site and sites affected by the spill;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (e) a description of the source of the spill;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (f) the type and quantity of the substance spilled;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (g) a description of the circumstances, cause and adverse effects of the spill, including, without limitation, a description of the following:

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (i)  the activity during which the spill occurred (e.g., transportation, transfer of cargo, fuelling, cleaning, maintenance);

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (ii)  the incident leading to the spill (e.g., tank rupture, overfill, collision, rollover, derailment, fire, explosion);

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (iii)  the underlying cause of the spill (e.g., human error, external conditions, organizational or management failure);

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (iv)  the adverse effects of the spill to human health, which must specify

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (A) the number of injuries,

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (B) the number of fatalities, and

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (C) the number of evacuees;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (v)  the adverse effects of the spill to the environment and infrastructure at the spill site and the area surrounding the spill, which description must specify

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (A) the size of the area adversely affected by the spill,

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (B) the biological and other resources adversely affected by the spill, including, without limitation,

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (I) bodies of water,

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (II) flora and fauna, and

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (III) animal, fish and plant habitat;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (h) details of action taken to comply with section 91.2 [responsible persons - spill response] of the Act;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (i) how and where waste from the spill was disposed of;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (j) a copy of data from and reports of sampling, testing, monitoring and assessing carried out during spill response actions;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (k) a map of the spill site and the area surrounding the spill and photographs of the spill;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (l) the names of agencies on the scene;

heading: End-of-spill report
paragraph: (m) the names of other persons or agencies advised about the spill.

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph:
7
		  (1) A director may order a responsible person in relation to a spill of a listed substance to submit a written report on the spill to the director.

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (2) An order under subsection (1) must be made in writing and within 6 months after the emergency response completion date for the spill.

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (3) A responsible person to whom an order under subsection (1) is directed must submit the report to the director in the manner and form specified by the director and must include

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (a) a description of the effectiveness of the spill response actions,

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (b) a description of actions taken to prevent future spills and improve response to future spills,

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (c) if the responsible person is a regulated person,

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (i)  a description of any changes that the person intends to make to the person's spill contingency plan to improve response to future spills,

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (ii)  if the spill occurred in a geographic response area, a description of any changes that the person considers should be made to the related geographic response plan to improve response to future spills, and

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (iii)  if spill response actions were carried out by a PRO, a description of any changes that the person considers should be made to the PRO's area response plan to improve response to future spills, and

heading: Lessons-learned report
paragraph: (d) responses to any specific questions the director asks in the order.

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph:
8
		  For the purposes of this regulation, the emergency response completion date for a spill is the date on which all of the following criteria are met:

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (a) the incident command post is disestablished;

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (b) the source of the spill is under control and is neither spilling nor at imminent risk of spilling;

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (c) emergency actions to stabilize, contain and remove the spill have been taken;

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (d) the waste removed from the spill site has been

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (i)  received at a facility for disposal, or

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (ii)  received for transportation to a facility for disposal;

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (e) if applicable, all notices respecting evacuation from the spill site have expired or been rescinded;

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (f) all equipment, personnel and other resources used in emergency spill response actions have been removed from the spill site, other than equipment, personnel or other resources required for

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (i)  sampling, testing, monitoring or assessing at the spill site, or

heading: Emergency response completion date
paragraph: (ii)  recovery or restoration of the spill site.

heading: Application to energy resource permit holders
paragraph:
9
		  The following sections do not apply to a person who holds a permit to carry out an energy resource activity to which the Emergency Management Regulation, B.C. Reg. 204/2013, applies:

heading: Application to energy resource permit holders
paragraph: (a) section 5 [updates to minister];

heading: Application to energy resource permit holders
paragraph: (b) section 6 [end-of-spill report];

heading: Application to energy resource permit holders
paragraph: (c) section 7 [lessons-learned report].
