paragraph: Schedule

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
1
		  In this Schedule, "Federal Regulations" means the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations made under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992 (Canada).

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1 The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: aboveground tank means a tank that operates at atmospheric pressure and that has all of its volume either above ground or encased within an unfilled secondary containment. (reservoir hors sol)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: allied petroleum product means a product set out in Schedule 1. (produit apparente)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: CCME Code of Practice means the Environmental Code of Practice for Aboveground and Underground Storage Tank Systems Containing Petroleum and Allied Petroleum Products published by the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment in 2003. (Code de recommandations techniques du CCME)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: certification mark means the mark, such as a tag, label, plate or embossing, on or affixed to a tank or a component of a storage tank system, certifying that the tank or component conforms to the standards of a certification organization accredited by the Standards Council of Canada or conforms to the standards of the American Petroleum Institute or of the ASTM International. (marque de certification)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: corrosion expert means a professional engineer experienced in corrosion protection or a person recognized by NACE International as a corrosion specialist. (expert en corrosion)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: free oil means the non-soluble, non-emulsified petroleum product or allied petroleum product layer that accumulates in an oil-water separator. (huile libre)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: partially buried tank means a tank that has part of its volume above ground and part of its volume below ground, unless all of the tank volume is encased within an unfilled secondary containment. (reservoir partiellement enfoui)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: petroleum product means, other than an allied petroleum product, a single hydrocarbon or a mixture of at least 70% hydrocarbons by volume, refined from crude oil, with or without additives, that is used or could be used as a fuel, lubricant or power transmitter, and includes used oil, but does not include propane, paint and solvents. (produit petrolier)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: piping means pipes and tubing, including fittings and valves, that are for the handling and storage of petroleum products and allied petroleum products. (raccordement)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: secondary containment means containment that prevents liquids that leak from a storage tank system from reaching outside the containment area and includes double-walled tanks, piping, liners and impermeable barriers. (confinement secondaire)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: separated solids means the particulate material that settles at the bottom of an oil-water separator. (solide separe)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: storage tank system means a tank or commonly connected tanks and all piping, vents, pumps, sumps, diking, overfill protection devices, spill containment devices and oil-water separators. In the case of a system located at an airport, the system ends at the pump discharge. (systeme de stockage)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: tank means a closed container with a capacity of more than 230 L that is designed to be installed in a fixed location. (reservoir)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: transfer area means the area around the connection point between a delivery truck, railcar, aircraft or vessel and a storage tank system in which the tanks have an aggregate capacity of more than 2 500 L. (aire de transfert)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: underground tank means a tank that operates at atmospheric pressure and that has all of its storage volume below ground and completely surrounded by fill. (reservoir souterrain)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: used oil means oil - other than oils derived from animal or vegetable fats, other than crude oil or recovered fuel oils spilled onto land or into water and other than wastes from petroleum refining operations - that has become unsuitable for its original purpose due to the presence of impurities or the loss of original properties, including

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) lubricating oil for use in engines, turbines, or gears;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) hydraulic fluid, including transmission fluid; and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) insulating oil. (huile usee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 1.1 (1) A method or standard that is incorporated by reference into these Regulations is incorporated as amended from time to time.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of interpreting documents that are incorporated by reference into these Regulations, "should" must be read to mean "must" and any recommendation or suggestion must be read as an obligation.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2 (1) These Regulations apply to any storage tank system located in Canada in which petroleum products or allied petroleum products are stored and

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) that is operated by a federal department, board or agency, or belongs to Her Majesty in right of Canada;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) that is operated to provide a service to, or belongs to, a federal work or undertaking that is

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) a port authority set out in the schedule to the Canada Marine Act,

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) an airport within the meaning of subsection 3(1) of the Aeronautics Act, or

heading: Application
paragraph: (iii) a railway;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) that is located on federal land or aboriginal land; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) that is operated by a Crown corporation, as defined in subsection 83(1) of the Financial Administration Act, or that belongs to such a corporation.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) These Regulations do not apply to

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) storage tank systems located in a building that provides secondary containment equivalent to a maximum hydraulic conductivity of 1 x 10-6 cm/s, on a continuous basis;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) storage tank systems containing unprocessed petroleum products resulting from or used during oil or natural gas exploration;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) storage tank systems that have aboveground tanks in which the aggregate capacity of the tanks is 2 500 L or less and the systems are connected to a heating appliance or emergency generator; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) storage tank systems regulated under the National Energy Board Act or the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 2.1 (1) A person must not release - or permit or cause any release of - a petroleum product or allied petroleum product, in liquid form in the environment, from a storage tank system.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if the released product does not reach outside the secondary containment of the storage tank system.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (3) A person must not release - or permit or cause any release of - a petroleum product or allied petroleum product, in liquid form in the environment, during the transfer of the product to or from a storage tank system.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not apply if the released product does not reach outside the transfer area of the storage tank system and if that transfer area is designed in accordance with subsection 15(1).

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 3 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), the owner or operator of a storage tank system that leaks a liquid must, without delay, temporarily withdraw from service, in accordance with section 43, either

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (a) the leaking component, if it can be isolated from the system; or

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (b) in any other case, the system.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: The owner or operator may only return the system or component, as the case may be, to service if they have made the necessary repairs to ensure that it no longer leaks.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (4), the owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has single-walled underground tanks that leak a liquid must, without delay, permanently withdraw those tanks and their components from service in accordance with section 44 and, within two years after the later of  June 12, 2008 and the day on which the owner or operator becomes aware of the leak,

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (a) in the case of a storage tank system that has vertically-oriented underground tanks, remove any piping and other components that are outside the tanks in accordance with section 45; or

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (b) in any other case, remove the single-walled underground tanks and their components in accordance with section 45.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has single-walled underground piping and which piping leaks a liquid must, without delay,

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (a) temporarily withdraw that system from service in accordance with section 43, permanently withdraw that piping from service in accordance with section 44, remove it in accordance with section 45 and replace it in accordance with section 14; or

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (b) permanently withdraw that system from service in accordance with section 44 and, within two years after the later of June 12, 2008 and the day on which the owner or operator becomes aware of the leak,

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (i) in the case of a storage tank system that has shop-fabricated aboveground tanks or underground tanks, other than vertically-oriented underground tanks, remove the system in accordance with section 45, and

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a storage tank system that has field-erected aboveground tanks or vertically-oriented underground tanks, remove all piping and other components that are outside the tanks in accordance with section 45.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (4) If circumstances make it impossible to comply with subsection (1), (2) or (3), the owner or operator must, without delay, take necessary measures to minimize the immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment and danger to human life or health until it becomes possible to comply with that subsection, and must, without delay, inform the Minister, in writing, of those circumstances and the measures that will be taken. For greater certainty, a petroleum product or allied petroleum product must not be transferred into the system until it becomes possible to comply with that subsection.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 4 The owner or operator of a storage tank system that permanently withdraws the system from service but that is not required to do so under subsection 3(2) or (3) must

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (a) in the case of a storage tank system that has shop-fabricated aboveground tanks or underground tanks, other than vertically-oriented underground tanks, remove the system in accordance with section45; and

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (b) in the case of a storage tank system that has field-erected aboveground tanks or vertically-oriented underground tanks, remove any piping and other components that are outside the tanks in accordance with section 45.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 5 The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has tanks designed to be installed above ground that were installed before June 12, 2008 below ground or encased within a filled secondary containment must, by June 12, 2012, permanently withdraw that system from service in accordance with section 44 and remove it in accordance with section 45.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 6 The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has tanks designed to be installed underground that were installed before June 12, 2008 above ground or encased within an unfilled secondary containment must, by June 12, 2012, permanently withdraw that system from service in accordance with section 44 and remove it in accordance with section 45.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 7 The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has a partially buried tank must, within four years after June 12, 2008, permanently withdraw that system from service in accordance with section 44 and remove it in accordance with section 45.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 8 A person must not install a storage tank system that has either partially buried or single-walled underground tanks to store petroleum products or allied petroleum products.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 9 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has single-walled underground tanks, other than those described in subsection3(2), must, within four years after June 12, 2008, permanently withdraw those tanks and their components from service in accordance with section 44 and remove them in accordance with section 45 unless, on June 12, 2008, those tanks have

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (a) in the case of steel tanks, cathodic protection and leak detection, groundwater monitoring wells or vapour monitoring wells; and

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (b) in any other case, leak detection, groundwater monitoring wells or vapour monitoring wells.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (2) In respect of any single-walled underground tank other than a steel tank or a reinforced plastic tank, the owner or operator must, within one year after June 12, 2008, provide the Minister with a declaration, dated after June 12, 2008 and signed by a professional engineer, stating that the tank has normal and emergency venting, the walls of the tank and its floor are impervious to the passage of petroleum product or allied petroleum product, the tank's structural integrity is maintained and the tank is suitable for the storage of petroleum products or allied petroleum products.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 10 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the owner or operator of a storage tank system that has single-walled underground piping, other than one described in subsection 3(3), that is installed before June 12, 2008 must, within four years after June 12, 2008,

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (a) temporarily withdraw that system from service in accordance with section 43, permanently withdraw that piping from service in accordance with section 44, remove it in accordance with section 45 and replace it in accordance with section 14; or

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (b) permanently withdraw that system from service in accordance with section 44, and

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (i) in the case of a storage tank system that has shop-fabricated aboveground tanks or underground tanks, other than vertically-oriented underground tanks, remove the system in accordance with section 45, and

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a storage tank system that has field-erected aboveground tanks or vertically-oriented underground tanks, remove all piping and other components that are outside the tanks in accordance with section 45.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator is not required to comply with subsection (1) if, on June 12, 2008, that piping has

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (a) in the case of steel piping, cathodic protection and leak detection, groundwater monitoring wells, vapour monitoring wells, single vertical check valves or mechanical line leak detection devices; and

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: (b) in the case of non-metallic or copper piping, leak detection, groundwater monitoring wells, vapour monitoring wells, single vertical check valves or mechanical line leak detection devices.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 11 The owner or operator of a storage tank system must ensure compatibility between any petroleum products and allied petroleum products to be stored in that system and the material used in the construction of the system.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 12 The owner or operator of a storage tank system must not store petroleum products or allied petroleum products in a tank of the system unless a fill pipe and vent line have been installed in that tank and all of the tank's other openings have been sealed or connected to piping.

heading: General Requirements
paragraph: 13 A person must not use a secondary containment area for storage purposes.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: 14 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system that installs the system or any component of the system on or after June 12, 2008 must ensure that the system or the component conforms to the applicable requirements set out in the following provisions of the CCME Code of Practice:

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (a) Part 3, subject to the following:

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (i) excluding Section 3.2, Clause 3.3.1(1)(c), Article 3.3.2, Clause 3.4.1(1)(c), Article 3.4.3, Clauses 3.5.1(1)(a) and 3.6.1(1)(l), Section 3.7, Clause 3.9.2(2)(a), Articles 3.9.4 and 3.10.1, and

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (ii) in Subclause 3.9.2(1)(a)(ii), the reference to "Aboveground Secondary Containment Tanks" must be read as a reference to "Secondary Containments for Aboveground Flammable and Combustible Liquid Storage Tanks";

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (c) Part 5, subject to the following:

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (i) excluding Sentence 5.2.1(1), Articles 5.2.4 to 5.2.6, Clause 5.4.2(1)(b), Sentence 5.4.3(1) and Section 5.5, and

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (ii) in Clauses 5.4.4(1)(a) to (c), the references to standards must be read as references to ULC/ORD-C971, Nonmetallic Underground Piping for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, or to CAN/ULC-S660, Standard for Nonmetallic Underground Piping for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, whichever is in effect at the time the system or component is manufactured; and

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (d) Section 8.6 and Article 8.7.2.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has aboveground tanks that installs those tanks on or after June 12, 2008 must ensure that those tanks are equipped with a spill containment device that bears a certification mark certifying conformity with ULC/ORD-C142.19, Spill Containment Devices for Aboveground Flammable and Combustible Liquid Storage Tanks, or with CAN/ULC-S663, Standard for Spill Containment Devices for Flammable and Combustible Liquid Aboveground Storage Tanks, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured, unless

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (a) the tank is filled remotely and its remote fill is equipped with a spill containment device that bears a certification mark certifying conformity with ULC/ORD-C142.19, Spill Containment Devices for Aboveground Flammable and Combustible Liquid Storage Tanks, or with CAN/ULC-S663, Standard for Spill Containment Devices for Flammable and Combustible Liquid Aboveground Storage Tanks, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured; or

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (b) the tank bears a certification mark certifying conformity with one of the following standards:

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (i) CAN/ULC-S652:2016, Standard For Tank Assemblies for the Collection, Storage and Removal Of Used Oil,

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (ii) CAN/ULC-S653:2016, Standard for Aboveground Horizontal Steel Contained Tank Assemblies for Flammable and Combustible Liquids,

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (iii) ULC/ORD-C142.5, Concrete Encased Steel Aboveground Tank Assemblies for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, or CAN/ULC-S677, Standard for Fire Tested Aboveground Tank Assemblies for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured,

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (iv) ULC/ORD-C142.18, Rectangular Steel Aboveground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, or CAN/ULC-S601, Standard for Shop Fabricated Steel Aboveground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured,

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (v) ULC/ORD-C142.21, Aboveground Used Oil Systems, or

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (vi) ULC/ORD-C142.22, Contained Vertical Steel Aboveground Tank Assemblies for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, or CAN/ULC-S601, Standard for Shop Fabricated Steel Aboveground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has underground tanks that installs those tanks on or after June 12, 2008 must ensure that those tanks bear a certification mark certifying conformity with one of the following standards:

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (a) for underground steel tanks

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (i) if used for storing used oil, CAN/ULC-S652:2016, Standard For Tank Assemblies for the Collection, Storage and Removal Of Used Oil, and

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (ii) if used for storing other petroleum products or allied petroleum products

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (A) CAN/ULC-S603-14, Standard for Steel Underground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, excluding Section 5 and clause 8.3.3.1, or

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (B) CAN/ULC-S603.1:2017, Standard for External Corrosion Protection Systems for Steel Underground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids;

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (b) for underground reinforced plastic tanks

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (i) if used for storing used oil, CAN/ULC-S652:2016, Standard For Tank Assemblies for the Collection, Storage and Removal Of Used Oil, and

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (ii) if used for storing other petroleum products or allied petroleum products, CAN/ULC-S615-14, Standard for Fibre Reinforced Plastic Underground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids; and

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (c) for underground tanks that are double containment linings, ULC/ORD-C58.4, Double Containment Fibre Reinforced Plastic Linings for Flammable and Combustible Liquid Storage Tanks, or CAN/ULC-S669, Standard for Internal Retrofit Systems for Underground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has steel underground tanks that installs those tanks on or after June 12, 2008 must ensure that those tanks are protected from corrosion as follows:

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (a) those tanks must bear a certification mark certifying conformity with CAN/ULC-S603.1:2017, External Corrosion Protection Systems for Steel Underground Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquids; or

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (b) those tanks must have a cathodic protection system designed by a corrosion expert.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (5) The owner or operator of a storage tank system that installs piping on or after June 12, 2008 must ensure that

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (a) the piping does not have buried or concealed mechanical joints; and

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (b) any piping other than copper piping bears a certification mark certifying conformity with

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (i) one of the standards referred to in Clauses 5.2.1(1)(a) to (c) or (g) of the CCME Code of Practice, or

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (ii) ULC/ORD-C971, Nonmetallic Underground Piping for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, or CAN/ULC-S660, Standard for Nonmetallic Underground Piping for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (6) Any reference to a standard in this section is a reference to the version of that standard that is in effect at the time the storage tank system's component is erected or manufactured, as applicable.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (7) The owner or operator of a storage tank system must comply with the applicable requirements before any petroleum products or allied petroleum products are first transferred into that system.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: 15 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system must ensure that petroleum product and allied petroleum product transfer areas are designed to contain any releases in liquid form in the environment that occur during the transfer process.

heading: Compliance with Requirements
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies to storage tank systems installed before June 12, 2008 four years after June 12, 2008.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 16 The owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has single-walled underground tanks must test those tanks using a tank precision leak detection test in accordance with section 21 within two years after June 12, 2008 and after that test they must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) immediately

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (i) use automatic tank gauging in accordance with section 18, or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (ii) use continuous in-tank leak detection in accordance with section 20; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) annually perform a tank precision leak detection test in accordance with section 21.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 17 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has single-walled underground piping must test that piping using a piping precision leak detection test in accordance with section 24 within two years after June 12, 2008 and after that test they must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) immediately

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (i) use continuous external underground pipe leak monitoring,

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (ii) use automatic tank gauging in accordance with section 18, or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (iii) use continuous in-tank leak detection in accordance with section 20; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) annually perform a piping precision leak detection test in accordance with section 24.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (2) The continuous external underground pipe leak monitoring must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) be carried out using a sensor cable system designed for installation adjacent to the piping and within the same pipe trench;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) be capable of detecting a leak rate of at least 0.38 L/h within 96 hours after the onset of the leak at the lowest expected soil temperature at the site where the sensor cable system is installed;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) be capable of locating the leak with an accuracy of +/- 1 m;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (d) be capable of continuously monitoring sensor cable system integrity; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (e) have an alarm located at a place of work where it can be readily heard and seen.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 18 Any reference to a standard in this section is a reference to the version of that standard that is in effect at the time of the certification. Equipment used for automatic tank gauging referred to in subparagraphs 16(a)(i) and 17(1)(a)(ii) must have an alarm located at a place of work where it can be readily heard and seen and must bear a certification mark certifying conformity with

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) ULC/ORD-C58.12, Leak Detection Devices (Volumetric Type) for Underground Flammable Liquid Storage Tanks, or CAN/ULC-S675.1, Standard for Volumetric Leak Detection Devices for Underground and Aboveground Storage Tanks for Flammable and Combustible Liquid, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) ULC/ORD-C58.14, Nonvolumetric Leak Detection Devices for Underground Flammable Liquid Storage Tanks, or CAN/ULC-S675.2, Standard for Nonvolumetric Precision Leak Detection Devices for Underground and Aboveground Storage Tanks and Piping for Flammable and Combustible Liquids, whichever is in effect at the time the storage tank system is manufactured.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 19 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has horizontal aboveground tanks without secondary containment must visually inspect the walls of those tanks within two years after June 12, 2008 to determine if the tank is leaking and after that inspection they must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) visually inspect the walls of those tanks at least once per month and perform an inventory reconciliation in accordance with subsection (2);

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) immediately

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (i) use continuous in-tank leak detection in accordance with section 20, or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (ii) use continuous external horizontal aboveground tank leak monitoring; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) annually perform a tank precision leak detection test in accordance with section 21.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (2) The inventory reconciliation must include

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) the measurement of the level of water and the combined level of water and petroleum product or allied petroleum product in every storage tank of the storage tank system at least every seven days unless the storage tank system is located at a fuel dispensing station, in which case the levels must be measured each day the station is in operation; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) a comparison of the measurements with readings of any meters that measure the volume of liquid transferred and the calculation of any gain or loss of liquid each time the measurements are taken.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (3) The continuous external horizontal aboveground tank leak monitoring must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) be carried out using a sensor cable system designed for installation beneath the horizontal aboveground tank and surrounding its perimeter dripline in order that any leak will be detected before any liquid moves beyond the tank's perimeter;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) be capable of detecting a leak rate of at least 0.38 L/h within 30 days after the onset of the leak at the lowest expected air temperature at the site where the sensor cable system is installed;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) be capable of locating the leak with an accuracy of +/- 1 m;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (d) be capable of continuously monitoring sensor cable system integrity; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (e) have an alarm located at a place of work where it can be readily heard and seen.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 20 Continuous in-tank leak detection referred to in subparagraphs 16(a)(ii), 17(1)(a)(iii), 19(1)(b)(i) and 22(1)(a)(i) must conform to the requirements set out in Article 6.2.6 of the CCME Code of Practice and have an alarm located at a place of work where it can be readily heard and seen.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 21 The tank precision leak detection test referred to in section 16 and paragraphs 19(1)(c), 26(a) and 43(b) must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) be capable of measuring the level of water in the tank to within 3 mm with a probability of 0.95 or greater;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) if a volumetric method is used, be capable of measuring the level of liquid in the tank to within 3 mm with a probability of 0.99 or greater;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) be capable of detecting a leak rate of at least 0.38 L/h within a 24 hour period with a probability of detection of 0.95 or greater and a probability of false alarm of 0.05 or less, accounting for variables such as vapour pockets, thermal expansion and contraction, evaporation and condensation, temperature stratification, groundwater level and tank deformation; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (d) be performed, using a documented and validated method, by an individual trained in the maintenance and use of the test equipment.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 22 (1) Subject to subsections (5) and (6), the owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has vertical aboveground tanks without secondary containment must, within two years after June 12, 2008, inspect those tanks or the floor of those tanks, and after that inspection they must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) immediately

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (i) use continuous in-tank leak detection in accordance with section 20, or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (ii) use continuous external vertical aboveground tank leak monitoring for each of those tanks; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) once every ten years, inspect those tanks or the floor of those tanks.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (2) The inspection of the vertical aboveground tanks must be performed in accordance with the version of API Standard 653, Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction that is in effect at the time of the inspection.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (3) The inspection of the floor of the vertical aboveground tank must be performed

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) using one of the following testing methods, namely, ultrasonic, magnetic particle, videographic or vacuum; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) using a documented and validated method by an individual trained in the maintenance and use of the test equipment.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (4) The continuous external vertical aboveground tank leak monitoring must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) be a sensor cable system designed for installation beneath the floor plate of the vertical aboveground tank in order to detect any leak into the soil beneath the tank floor and immediately surrounding the tank's perimeter;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) be capable of detecting a leak rate of at least 0.38 L/h within 30 days after the onset of the leak at the lowest expected soil temperature at the site where the sensor cable system is installed;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) be capable of locating the leak with an accuracy of +/- 1 m;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (d) be capable of continuously monitoring sensor cable system integrity; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (e) have an alarm located at a place of work where it can be readily heard and seen.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (5) If, within eight years before June 12, 2008, the owner or operator has inspected the vertical aboveground tanks without secondary containment in accordance with the version of API Standard 653, Tank Inspection, Repair, Alteration, and Reconstruction that existed at the time of the inspection, they must perform a new inspection in accordance with subsection (2) at least every ten years after the day on which that inspection was performed.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (6) If, within eight years before June 12, 2008, the owner or operator has inspected the floor of the vertical aboveground tanks without secondary containment as set out in subsection (3), they must perform a new inspection in accordance with that subsection at least every ten years after the day on which that inspection was performed.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 23 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system installed before June 12, 2008 that has aboveground piping without secondary containment must visually inspect the walls of that piping within two years after June 12, 2008 to determine if the piping is leaking and after that inspection they must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) immediately

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (i) use continuous external aboveground pipe leak monitoring for that piping, or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (ii) implement a corrosion analysis program for that piping, developed and conducted by a corrosion expert, that includes at least an annual inspection;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) once each month, visually inspect that piping; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) annually perform a piping precision leak detection test of that piping in accordance with section 24.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (2) The continuous external aboveground pipe leak monitoring must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) be carried out using a sensor cable system designed either for installation on the bottom of the piping or for placement on the ground underneath the piping;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) be capable of detecting a leak rate of at least 0.38 L/h within 96 hours after the onset of the leak at the lowest expected soil temperature at the site where the sensor cable system is installed;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) be capable of locating the leak with an accuracy of +/- 1 m;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (d) be capable of continuously monitoring sensor cable system integrity; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (e) have an alarm located at a place of work where it can be readily heard and seen.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 24 The piping precision leak detection test referred to in section 17 and paragraphs 23(1)(c) and 26(d) must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) be capable of detecting a leak rate of at least 0.38 L/h within a 24 hour period at a line pressure of 310 kPa with a probability of detection of 0.95 or greater and a probability of false alarm of 0.05 or less, accounting for variables such as vapour pockets, thermal expansion and contraction, static head pressure, temperature differential and piping compressibility; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) be performed, using a documented and validated method, by an individual trained in the maintenance and use of the test equipment.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 25 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has turbine, transition, dispenser or pump sumps must, by June 12, 2010, visually inspect those sumps to determine if they are leaking and after that inspection they must either

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) immediately use continuous sump leak monitoring for those sumps; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) visually inspect those sumps annually.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (2) The continuous sump leak monitoring must

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) use a petroleum product probe capable of detecting 1 mm of petroleum product or allied petroleum product on a concrete surface or 1 mm of petroleum product or allied petroleum product floating on the water within the sump; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) have a probe that is capable of reporting the presence of petroleum product or allied petroleum product at the probe location within two hours of contact with that product at the lowest expected air temperature at the site where the probe is installed.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 26 In the case of a storage tank system that is not equipped with continuous leak monitoring, if the owner or operator of the storage tank system has reasonable grounds to believe that any of the following components of the system is leaking, they must test or inspect the component as follows:

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) in the case of an underground tank, they must test that tank using the tank precision leak detection test in accordance with section 21;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) in the case of an aboveground vertical tank, they must inspect the tank in accordance with subsection 22(2) or the floor of that tank in accordance with subsection 22(3);

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) in the case of an aboveground horizontal tank, they must visually inspect the walls of that tank to determine if the tank is leaking;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (d) in the case of underground piping, they must test that piping using the piping precision leak detection test in accordance with section 24;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (e) in the case of aboveground piping, they must visually inspect the walls of that piping to determine if the piping is leaking; or

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (f) in the case of a turbine, transition, dispenser or pump sump, they must perform a static liquid media leak detection test that respects the following conditions:

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (i) the test has a duration of at least one hour,

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (ii) the level of the test liquid exceeds the elevation of the sump's piping and of other points of entry into the sump, and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (iii) there is no measurable loss of liquid in the sump.

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: 27 The owner or operator of a storage tank system that has tested or inspected any component of the system for leaks under sections 16 to 26 must keep a record that includes the following information:

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (a) the test or inspection date;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (b) the storage tank system identification number;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (c) the allied petroleum product or the type of petroleum product stored in the system;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (d) the test or inspection results;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (e) the testing method;

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (f) the name and address of the individual and, if applicable, the company that performed the test or inspection; and

heading: Leak Detection
paragraph: (g) the components of the corrosion analysis program referred to in subparagraph 23(1)(a)(ii).

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: 28 (1) The owner of a storage tank system that is installed before June 12, 2008 must identify the system by submitting to the Minister, in writing, the information set out in Schedule 2

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (a) by June 12, 2009; or

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (b) by June 12, 2010 if they submit to the Minister a storage tank system identification progress report containing the information set out in Schedule 3 by June 12, 2009.

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (2) The owner of a storage tank system that is installed on or after June 12, 2008 must identify the system by submitting to the Minister, in writing, the information set out in Schedule 2 before the day on which the first transfer of petroleum products or allied petroleum products into any tank of the system occurs.

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (3) The Minister must issue an identification number for the storage tank system for which the information was submitted and inform the owner of the identification number and its date of issuance.

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator must display the identification number in a readily visible location on or near the storage tank system for which the number was issued.

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (5) The owner or operator must update the information submitted under subsection (1) or (2) and submit to the Minister, in writing, any changed information within 60 days after the change.

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (6) A person must not operate a storage tank system unless an identification number has been issued for that system. In the case of a storage tank system referred to in subsection (1), this subsection applies beginning June 12, 2010.

heading: Identification of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (7) The person that is required to submit information under subsection (1), (2) or (5) must also submit to the Minister, in writing, a certification that the information is accurate and complete, dated and signed by the person or a person authorized to act on their behalf.

heading: Delivery of Petroleum Products or Allied Petroleum Products
paragraph: 29 A person that delivers petroleum products or allied petroleum products must comply with the following requirements:

heading: Delivery of Petroleum Products or Allied Petroleum Products
paragraph: (a) they must immediately notify the operator of the storage tank system of any release in liquid form in the environment that occurs during the transfer or any evidence observed of a leak or of any release in liquid form; and

heading: Delivery of Petroleum Products or Allied Petroleum Products
paragraph: (b) beginning two years after June 12, 2008,

heading: Delivery of Petroleum Products or Allied Petroleum Products
paragraph: (i) they must not transfer petroleum products or allied petroleum products into any storage tank system unless the storage tank system identification number is visible, and

heading: Delivery of Petroleum Products or Allied Petroleum Products
paragraph: (ii) they must keep a record of the storage tank system identification number.

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: 30 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system must prepare an emergency plan taking into consideration the following factors:

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (a) the properties and characteristics of each petroleum product or allied petroleum product stored in each tank of the system and the maximum expected quantity of the petroleum product or allied petroleum product to be stored in the system at any time during any calendar year; and

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (b) the characteristics of the place where the system is located and of the surrounding area that may increase the risk of harm to the environment or of danger to human life or health.

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (2) The emergency plan must include

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (a) a description of the factors considered under subsection (1);

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (b) a description of the measures to be used to prevent, warn of, prepare for, respond to and recover from any emergency that may cause harm to the environment or danger to human life or health;

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (c) a list of the individuals who are required to carry out the plan and a description of their roles and responsibilities;

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (d) the identification of the training required for each of the individuals listed under paragraph (c);

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (e) a list of the emergency response equipment included as part of the plan, and the equipment's location; and

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (f) the measures to be taken to notify members of the public who may be adversely affected by the harm or danger referred to in paragraph (b).

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of a storage tank system must ensure that the emergency plan is ready to be implemented

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (a) in the case of a storage tank system that is installed before June 12, 2008, no later than two years after June 12, 2008; and

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (b) in any other case, before the day on which the first transfer of petroleum products or allied petroleum products into any tank of the storage tank system occurs.

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: 31 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system must keep the emergency plan up-to-date and keep a copy of it readily available for the individuals who are required to carry it out, as well as a copy at the place where the storage tank system is located if that place is a place of work.

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator must notify the Minister of the civic address of each location where the emergency plan is kept.

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: 32 (1) If the owner or operator of a storage tank system has prepared an emergency plan with respect to the system on a voluntary basis or for another government or under an Act of Parliament and the plan meets the requirements of subsections 30(1) and (2), they may use that plan for the purposes of meeting those requirements.

heading: Emergency Plan
paragraph: (2) If the plan does not meet all of the requirements of subsections 30(1) and (2), the owner or operator may use the plan if they amend it so that it meets all of those requirements.

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: 33 (1) The owner of a storage tank system must have the system installed by a person approved to do so by the province in which the system is to be installed. If no person has been approved in the province where the storage tank system is to be installed, the installation must be supervised by a professional engineer.

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator must keep a record establishing that the storage tank system was installed by an approved person or that the installation was supervised by a professional engineer.

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: 34 (1) For the installation of any storage tank system, the owner of the system must use design plans, drawings and specifications of the system that bear the stamp and signature of a professional engineer.

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (2) Upon the installation and before the first transfer of any petroleum products or allied petroleum products into any tank of the storage tank system, the owner of the system must ensure that as-built drawings are prepared, bear the stamp and signature of a professional engineer and show

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (a) the outline of all tanks;

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (b) the centreline of all piping;

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (c) the centreline of all underground electrical power and monitor sensor conduits;

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (d) the building foundation outlines;

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (e) the property lines; and

heading: Installation of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (f) the secondary containment systems.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: 35 (1) If the owner or operator of a storage tank system uses an oil-water separator in the operation of the system, the operator must

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (a) each month, measure, as close to the baffle as possible, the thickness of the free oil layer and the separated solids layer and keep a record of those measurements with the date of measurement; or

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (b) use an oil-water separator that is electronically monitored.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (2) If the owner or operator becomes aware of a leak in the storage tank system or a release in liquid form in the environment, they must, without delay, measure the thickness of the free oil layer and the separated solids layer in the oil-water separator and keep a record of that measurement.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: 36 (1) If the owner or operator of a storage tank system uses an oil-water separator in the operation of the system, the operator must ensure that the oil-water separator's free oil layer is removed

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (a) continuously by an automatic skimmer; or

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (b) in a manner such that the thickness of the layer does not exceed 50 mm.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator must ensure that disposal of the free oil removed occurs in a manner such that there will be no immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment and the disposal will not constitute a danger to human life or health, and must keep a record of the quantity disposed of, the disposal method and the place where the free oil was disposed of.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: 37 (1) If the owner or operator of a storage tank system uses an oil-water separator in the operation of the system, the operator must ensure that the oil-water separator's separated solids layer is removed

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (a) by an automatic removal device; or

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (b) in a manner such that the thickness of the layer does not exceed 150 mm.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator must ensure that disposal of the separated solids removed occurs in a manner such that there will be no immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment and the disposal will not constitute a danger to human life or health, and must keep a record of the quantity disposed of, the disposal method and the place where the separated solids were disposed of.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: 38 If the owner or operator of a storage tank system uses an oil-water separator in the operation of the system, the operator must ensure that the oil-water separator's water is discharged in a manner such that there will be no immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment and will not constitute a danger to human life or health.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: 39 The owner or operator of a storage tank system must not use centrifugal-type pumps to transfer oil-contaminated water from dikes or sumps to the oil-water separator.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: 40 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system must ensure that disposal of water that accumulates in the bottom of any tank of the system occurs in a manner such that there will be no immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment and the disposal will not constitute a danger to human life or health.

heading: Operation and Maintenance
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of the storage tank system must keep a record of the quantity of any tank bottom water removed, the date of its removal, the name and address of the individual and, if applicable, the company removing it, the disposal method and the place where it was disposed of.

heading: Release Report
paragraph: 41 (1) For the purposes of paragraph 212(1)(a) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, the written report must contain the following information:

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (a) the names of both the owner and the operator of the storage tank system;

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (b) the identification number of the storage tank system;

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (c) the date on which any release in liquid form in the environment occurred;

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (d) each allied petroleum product or type of petroleum product that is the subject of the report;

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (e) the quantity of each petroleum product or allied petroleum product that is the subject of the report or, if the quantity cannot be determined, an estimate of that quantity;

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (f) a description of the circumstances of any release in liquid form in the environment and any mitigating measures taken; and

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (g) a description of the measures taken following any release in liquid form in the environment to prevent a subsequent occurrence.

heading: Release Report
paragraph: (2) In the event of a release in the environment of less than 100 L of a petroleum product or an allied petroleum product, in liquid form, the report under paragraph 212(1)(a) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 is not required.

heading: Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: 42 The owner or operator of a storage tank system may withdraw the system or any component of it from service

heading: Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (a) temporarily, if the withdrawal lasts less than two years; or

heading: Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (b) permanently.

heading: Temporary Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: 43 The owner or operator of a storage tank system that temporarily withdraws the system or any component of it from service must keep a record of the date on which they withdrew the system or component from service and must ensure that

heading: Temporary Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (a) if the system is equipped with a cathodic protection system, the cathodic protection system is maintained and operated during the withdrawal;

heading: Temporary Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (b) if the system has either underground tanks, other than vertically-oriented underground tanks, or shop-fabricated aboveground tanks and the system or its component has been out of service for more than one year, those tanks are tested for leaks using a tank precision leak detection test in accordance with section 21 before the system or component is returned to service;

heading: Temporary Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (c) if the system has field-erected aboveground tanks or vertically-oriented underground tanks and the system or its component has been out of service for more than one year, an inspection of the floor of those tanks using one of the following testing methods, namely, ultrasonic, magnetic particle, videographic or vacuum, is performed before the system or component is returned to service; and

heading: Temporary Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (d) a label is affixed to the system's fill pipe stating that the system is temporarily out of service.

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: 44 (1) The owner or operator of a storage tank system that permanently withdraws the system or any component of it from service must have the system or component withdrawn by a person approved to do so by the province in which the system or component is located. If no person has been approved in the province where the storage tank system or component is located, the withdrawal must be supervised by a professional engineer.

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator must keep a record that includes the date on which they withdrew the system or component from service and that establishes that the storage tank system or component was withdrawn by an approved person or that the withdrawal was supervised by a professional engineer.

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of the storage tank system must ensure that

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (a) all liquids and sludge are removed and disposed of;

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (b) if a tank is being withdrawn from service, the tank is purged of vapours to less than 10% of the lower flammability limit and the presence of vapours is checked with a combustible gas meter; and

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (c) the withdrawal is done in a way such that there will be no immediate or long-term harmful effect on the environment and it will not constitute a danger to human life or health.

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator of the storage tank system must affix a label to the system's fill pipe stating that the system is permanently out of service.

heading: Permanent Withdrawal from Service
paragraph: (5) The owner or operator must notify the Minister, in writing, of the permanent withdrawal from service of a storage tank system or any component of a storage tank system within 60 days after the day on which it is permanently withdrawn from service.

heading: Removal of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: 45 (1) If a storage tank system or any component of a storage tank system is required to be removed under these Regulations, the owner of the system must have the system or the component removed by a person approved to do so by the province in which the system is located. If no person has been approved in the province where the storage tank system is located, the owner must have the removal supervised by a professional engineer.

heading: Removal of Storage Tank Systems
paragraph: (2) The owner must keep a record establishing that the storage tank system or the component was removed by an approved person or that the removal was supervised by a professional engineer.

heading: Record Keeping
paragraph: 46 (1) Subject to subsection (2) and section 31, the owner or operator of a storage tank system that is required to keep a record under these Regulations must keep the record at the owner's or operator's place of work nearest to the system for five years after the day on which that record was made.

heading: Record Keeping
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of a storage tank system must keep the following records and documents until the system is removed:

heading: Record Keeping
paragraph: (a) the record referred to in section 27

heading: Record Keeping
paragraph: (i) in respect of an inspection performed under section 22, or

heading: Record Keeping
paragraph: (ii) that includes the information referred to in paragraph 27(g); and

heading: Record Keeping
paragraph: (b) the record referred to in subsection 33(2) and the documents referred to in section 34.

heading: Coming into Force
paragraph: 48 These Regulations come into force on the day on which they are registered.

heading: Short Title
paragraph: 1 This Order may be cited as the Territorial Sea Geographical Coordinates Order.

heading: Interpretation

heading: Interpretation

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Area, followed by a number, includes all islands and low-tide elevations adjacent to the Area followed by that number; (region)

heading: General
paragraph: 3 The lists of geographical coordinates of points set out in Schedules I, II and III are hereby issued as lists of geographical coordinates of points from which baselines may be determined pursuant to the Act in respect of the Areas to which the Schedules relate.

heading: General
paragraph: 4 (1) In respect of the portions of Areas 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 for which the geographical coordinates of points are listed in Schedule I, the baselines are straight lines joining the points so listed.

heading: General
paragraph: (2) In respect of the portion of Area 2 for which the geographical coordinates of points are listed in Schedule II, the baseline is the low-water line along the coast joining the points so listed.

heading: General
paragraph: (3) In respect of the portions of Areas 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 consisting of the islands named and the low-tide elevations described in Schedule III, the baselines are the low-water lines of the islands and of the low-tide elevations.

heading: General
paragraph: 5 The list of geographical coordinates of points set out in Parts I and II of Schedule IV is hereby issued as a list of geographical coordinates of points from which, in respect of the portion of Area 3 to which that Schedule relates, the territorial sea outer limit line may be determined, in substitution for the territorial sea outer limit line described in subsection 3(1) of the Act,

heading: General
paragraph: (a) by straight lines joining the points set out in Part I thereof; and

heading: General
paragraph: (b) by the geodesic line joining the points set out in Part II thereof.

heading: Right to hunt and fish
paragraph:
1
		  A person has the right to hunt and fish in accordance with the law.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act, "Tla'amin Final Agreement" means the Tla'amin Final Agreement among the Tla'amin Nation, Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada and Her Majesty the Queen in right of British Columbia set out in the Schedule, and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) that agreement as it is given effect by an Act of Canada, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) amendments to that agreement made in accordance with it.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) Words and expressions used in this Act have the same meanings as they have in the Tla'amin Final Agreement, unless the context requires otherwise.

heading: Treaty and land claims agreement
paragraph:
2
		  The Tla'amin Final Agreement is a treaty and a land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Tla'amin Final Agreement
paragraph: 3		  (1) The Tla'amin Final Agreement is approved, given effect and declared valid and has the force of law.

heading: Tla'amin Final Agreement
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a person or body

heading: Tla'amin Final Agreement
paragraph: (a) has the powers, rights, privileges and benefits conferred, and

heading: Tla'amin Final Agreement
paragraph: (b) must perform the duties and is subject to the liabilities imposed

heading: Tla'amin Final Agreement
paragraph: on the person or body by the Tla'amin Final Agreement.

heading: Tla'amin Final Agreement
paragraph: (3) Nothing in this Act that provides for a matter that is already provided for in the Tla'amin Final Agreement in any way limits this section.

heading: Authorization to sign Tla'amin Final Agreement
paragraph:
4
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may authorize a member of the Executive Council to sign the Tla'amin Final Agreement.

heading: Tla'amin Final Agreement binding and can be relied on
paragraph:
5
		  The Tla'amin Final Agreement is binding on, and can be relied on by, all persons.

heading: Relationship between final agreement and legislation
paragraph:
6
		  (1) As set out in paragraph 10 of Chapter 2 [General Provisions] of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, the Tla'amin Final Agreement prevails to the extent of an inconsistency or a Conflict with Provincial Law.

heading: Relationship between final agreement and legislation
paragraph: (2) As set out in paragraph 12 of Chapter 2 of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, Provincial Settlement Legislation prevails over other Provincial Laws to the extent of a Conflict.

heading: Tla'amin Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph:
7
		  (1) In this section, "estate in fee simple" means the estate in fee simple within the meaning of the Tla'amin Final Agreement.

heading: Tla'amin Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (2) On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation owns the estate in fee simple in the following lands:

heading: Tla'amin Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (a) Tla'amin Lands, as identified in paragraph 1 of Chapter 3 [Lands] of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, except the Lund Hotel Parcels;

heading: Tla'amin Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (b) Other Tla'amin Lands, as identified in paragraph 2 of Chapter 3 of the Tla'amin Final Agreement.

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph:
8
		  (1) As provided in paragraph 40 of Chapter 26 [Dispute Resolution] of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, if, in any judicial or administrative proceeding, an issue arises in respect of

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (a) the interpretation or validity of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, or

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (b) the validity or applicability of Settlement Legislation or a Tla'amin Law,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: the issue must not be decided until the party raising the issue has properly served notice on the Attorney General of British Columbia, the Attorney General of Canada and the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (2) The notice required under subsection (1) must

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (a) describe the judicial or administrative proceeding in which the issue arises,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (b) state whether the issue arises in respect of the matters referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (b) or both,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (c) state the day on which the issue is to be argued,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (d) give particulars necessary to show the point to be argued, and

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (e) be served at least 14 days before the day of argument unless the court or tribunal authorizes a shorter notice.

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (3) As provided in paragraph 41 of Chapter 26 of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, in a judicial or administrative proceeding to which subsection (1) applies, the Attorney General of British Columbia, the Attorney General of Canada and the Tla'amin Nation may appear and participate in the proceeding as parties with the same rights as any other party to the proceeding.

heading: Agricultural Land Reserve
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Despite sections 2 and 16 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act, on the Effective Date, agricultural land, as defined in the Agricultural Land Commission Act, that is identified in Appendix E as "Former Agricultural Land Reserve" is excluded from the agricultural land reserve.

heading: Agricultural Land Reserve
paragraph: (2) Despite section 2 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act, on the Effective Date, the Provincial Agricultural Land Commission must amend the land reserve plan in accordance with subsection (1) of this section and provide notice to the Tla'amin Nation and the registrar of titles that the amendment has been made.

heading: Agricultural Land Reserve
paragraph: (3) Despite section 2 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act, section 21 of that Act does not apply in relation to a subdivision plan of Tla'amin Lands deposited in the land title office on the Effective Date for the purposes of registering those lands in the name of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Tla'amin Nation participation in regional hospital district
paragraph: 10		  If, on the Effective Date, the letters patent of the Powell River Regional Hospital District have not been amended to include and designate the treaty lands of the Tla'amin Nation as a member of the district, those letters patent are deemed amended for that purpose.

heading: Authorization to enter into agreements
paragraph:
11
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may authorize a member of the Executive Council to enter into, on behalf of Her Majesty the Queen in right of British Columbia, an agreement that is contemplated by the Tla'amin Final Agreement.

heading: Tax treatment agreement
paragraph:
12
		  (1) In this section, "tax treatment agreement" means the tax treatment agreement referred to in paragraphs 22 and 23 of Chapter 21 [Taxation] of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, which agreement

heading: Tax treatment agreement
paragraph: (a) is substantially in the form approved by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, and

heading: Tax treatment agreement
paragraph: (b) has been signed by the parties and published by the minister in the Gazette,

heading: Tax treatment agreement
paragraph: and includes an amendment to the tax treatment agreement made in accordance with the terms of the tax treatment agreement if the agreement amending the tax treatment agreement satisfies both paragraphs (a) and (b) of this subsection.

heading: Tax treatment agreement
paragraph: (2) The tax treatment agreement is given effect and declared valid and its provisions have the force of law during the period they are in effect.

heading: Tax treatment agreement
paragraph: (3) The minister charged with the administration of the Financial Administration Act is authorized to enter into the tax treatment agreement, or an agreement amending the tax treatment agreement, and may sign the tax treatment agreement or agreement amending the tax treatment agreement before or after it has been approved by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Tax treatment agreement

paragraph: (2.1) If a person is convicted of an offence against a Tla'amin Law enacted under law-making authority delegated to the Tla'amin Nation in the foreshore agreement, in addition to any penalty provided for in the Tla'amin Law, on application by the Tla'amin Nation, the court may make an order

heading: Foreshore agreement
paragraph: (2.3) A person who fails to comply with an order under subsection (2.1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $10 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 6 months, or to both.

heading: Foreshore agreement
paragraph: (2.4) For the purposes of section 169 of Chapter 15 [Governance] of the Tla'amin Final Agreement, a fine imposed in a prosecution of an offence under subsection (2.3) is deemed to be a fine imposed for a violation of a Tla'amin Law.

heading: Foreshore agreement
paragraph: (2.5) If a person is convicted of an offence against a law referred to in subsection (2.1), on application by the Tla'amin Nation for compensation, the court must give consideration to the application and, in addition to any penalty imposed, may order the convicted person

paragraph: (a) to pay to the Tla'amin Nation compensation, in an amount that is not more than the monetary limit specified under the Small Claims Act, for any damage or loss sustained by the Tla'amin Nation because of the commission of the offence, and

paragraph: (b) in accordance with the schedule of costs prescribed under section 132 (2) (h) of the Offence Act, if any, to pay to the Tla'amin Nation the costs incurred by the Tla'amin Nation in investigating and prosecuting the person.

paragraph: (2.6) In the case of a dispute, the amount of compensation payable under subsection (2.5) (a) must be proven on a balance of probabilities by the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Schedule to the Tla'amin Final Agreement Act

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TABLE OF CONTENTS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PREAMBLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: WHEREAS:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: A. The Tla'amin Nation is an aboriginal people of Canada;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: B. The Tla'amin Nation asserts that it has used, occupied and governed its traditional territory from time immemorial;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: C. The Tla'amin Nation has never entered into a treaty or land claims agreement with the Crown;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: D. Section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 recognizes and affirms the existing aboriginal and treaty rights of the aboriginal peoples of Canada and the courts have stated that aboriginal rights include aboriginal title;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: E. The Tla'amin Nation's existing aboriginal rights are recognized and affirmed by the Constitution Act, 1982;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: F. The courts have stated that reconciliation of the prior presence of aboriginal people and the assertion of sovereignty by the Crown is best achieved through negotiation and agreement rather than through litigation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: G. The Parties have negotiated this Agreement to provide a basis for this reconciliation and the establishment of a new relationship on a government-to-government basis;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: H. The negotiations of this Agreement have been conducted in an atmosphere of mutual respect and openness;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: I. The Parties have negotiated this Agreement under the British Columbia treaty process;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: J. The Parties desire certainty in respect of the Tla'amin Nation's ownership and use of lands and resources, the Tla'amin Nation's law-making authority and the relationship of Federal Law, Provincial Law and Tla'amin Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: K. The Parties have negotiated this Agreement to provide certainty by agreeing to the continuation of the Tla'amin Nation's existing aboriginal rights as treaty rights set out in this Agreement, rather than by extinguishment of those rights;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: L. Tla'amin people are Coast Salish people who speak the Tla'amin language and who assert that their heritage, history and culture, including their language and religion, are tied to the lands and waters surrounding the northern Gulf of Georgia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: M. It is an important objective of the Tla'amin Nation to preserve, protect and enhance Tla'amin heritage, language and culture;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: N. The Tla'amin Nation asserts that it has an inherent right to self-government, and the Government of Canada has negotiated self-government in this Agreement based on its policy that the inherent right to self-government is an existing aboriginal right within the meaning of section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: O. This Agreement provides for Tla'amin Government and sets out authorities exercisable by the Tla'amin Nation through Tla'amin Government;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NOW THEREFORE THE PARTIES AGREE AS FOLLOWS:
