heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Crown" means Canada or British Columbia, as the case may be;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Cultural Purposes" means the use of Monumental Cedar and Cypress for a purpose that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. was integral to Tla'amin culture before contact;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. is primarily for totem poles, dugout canoes or long beams or posts to build longhouses, community halls or similar community structures; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. is not carried out for profit, commercial purpose, Trade and Barter, individual or community gain, residential building construction, structures associated with a residential building or for providing firewood for individual needs;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Designated Migratory Bird Population" means a population of a species of Migratory Birds that has been designated by the Minister in accordance with paragraph 45 of the Migratory Birds Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Direct" has the same meaning, for the purposes of distinguishing between a direct tax and an indirect tax, as in class 2 of section 92 of the Constitution Act, 1867;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Director" means an individual designated as director by the Minister under the Child, Family and Community Service Act or the Adoption Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Disagreement" means a dispute or negotiation to which the Dispute Resolution Chapter applies as described in paragraph 6 of that Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Domestic Purposes" means food, social and ceremonial purposes;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Effective Date" means the date, agreed to by the Parties, on which this Agreement takes effect;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Eligible Voter" means an individual who:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. is eligible to vote in accordance with paragraph 8 of the Ratification Chapter; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. votes under paragraph 9 and whose vote is counted under paragraph 10 of the Ratification Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Enhancement Initiative" means an initiative that is intended to result in an increase in the abundance or variety of a species or stock of Fish through:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the creation of, or artificial improvement to, Fish habitat; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the application of Fish culture technology;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Enrolment Appeal Board" means the board established under paragraph 21 of the Eligibility and Enrolment Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Enrolment Committee" means the committee established under paragraph 12 of the Eligibility and Enrolment Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Environment" means the components of the Earth and includes:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. air, land and water, including all layers of the atmosphere;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. all organic and inorganic matter and living organisms; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the interacting natural systems that include components referred to in subparagraphs a and b;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Environmental Emergency" means an uncontrolled, unplanned or accidental release, or release in contravention of laws or regulations, of a substance into the Environment, or the reasonable likelihood of such a release into the Environment, that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. has or may have an immediate or long term harmful effect on the Environment;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. constitutes or may constitute a danger to the Environment on which human life depends; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. constitutes or may constitute a danger in Canada to human life or health;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Federal Expropriating Authority" means a federal department or agency or any person with the authority to expropriate land or an interest in land under Federal Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Federal and Provincial Law" means Federal Law and Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Federal Law" includes federal statutes, regulations, ordinances, orders-in-council and the common law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Federal or Provincial Law" means Federal Law or Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Federal Project" means a "project", as defined in the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, that is subject to an environmental assessment under that Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Federal Settlement Legislation" means the Act of Parliament that gives effect to this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "First Nation Government in British Columbia" means the government of a First Nation in British Columbia that has a treaty or a land claims agreement in effect with Canada and British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Fiscal Financing Agreement" means an agreement negotiated among the Parties in accordance with the Fiscal Relations Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Fish" means:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. fish, shellfish, crustaceans and marine animals excluding cetaceans;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the parts of fish, shellfish, crustaceans and marine animals excluding cetaceans; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the eggs, sperm, spawn, larvae, spat, juvenile stages and adult stages of fish, shellfish, crustaceans and marine animals excluding cetaceans;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Fish Fund" has the meaning ascribed to it in the initial Fiscal Financing Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Foreshore" means land between the high water mark and the low water mark;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Forest Practices" means timber harvesting, road construction, road maintenance, road use, road deactivation, silviculture treatments and other related activities, including grazing for the purposes of brushing, botanical forest product collecting and fire use, but does not include timber marking or scaling, manufacture of timber or export of timber;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Forest Resources" means all Timber Resources and Plants, but does not include Aquatic Plants;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Former Kahkaykay Indian Reserve No. 6" means the Former Sliammon Indian Reserve described in Part 1 of Appendix C-1 and identified for illustrative purposes in Map 6, Part 2 of Appendix C-1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Former Sliammon Indian Reserve No. 1" means the Former Sliammon Indian Reserve described in Part 1 of Appendix C-1 and identified for illustrative purposes in Map 1, Part 2 of Appendix C-1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Former Sliammon Indian Reserves" means the lands that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. were, on the day before the Effective Date, Indian Reserves set apart for the use and benefit of the Sliammon Indian Band; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. are described in Part 1 of Appendix C-1 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix C-1 as "Former Sliammon Indian Reserves";

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Former Tokenatch Indian Reserve No. 5" means the Former Sliammon Indian Reserve described in Part 1 of Appendix C-1 and identified for illustrative purposes in Map 5, Part 2 of Appendix C-1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Former Toquana Indian Reserve No. 4" means the Former Sliammon Indian Reserve described in Part 1 of Appendix C-1 and identified for illustrative purposes in Map 4, Part 2 of Appendix C-1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Fossils" means remains, traces or imprints of animals or Plants that have been preserved in rocks, and includes bones, shells, casts and tracks;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Framework Agreement on First Nation Land Management" means the agreement entered into between Canada and thirteen First Nations in 1996 in respect of First Nation land management as amended;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Geothermal Resources" means the natural heat of the Earth and all substances that derive thermal energy from it, including steam, water and water vapour heated by the natural heat of the earth and all substances dissolved in the steam, water and water vapour, but does not include:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. water that has a temperature less than 80°C at the point where it reaches the surface; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. hydrocarbons;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Groundwater" means water below the surface of the ground;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Heritage Site" means a site of archaeological, historical or cultural significance and includes graves and burial sites;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Implementation Committee" means the committee established under paragraph 4 of the Implementation Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Implementation Plan" means the plan described in paragraph 2 of the Implementation Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Independent Regulatory Agency" means a federal statutory body, including the National Energy Board and the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission, which, in the exercise of regulatory or licensing powers, is not subject to specific control or direction by the federal government notwithstanding that it may be subject to general direction whether by guidelines, regulations or directives, or that its decisions may be subject to approval, variance or rescission by Canada;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Indian" means an "Indian" as defined in the Indian Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Indian Band" means a "band" as defined in the Indian Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Indian Reserve" means a "reserve" as defined in the Indian Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Intellectual Property" includes any intangible property right resulting from intellectual activity in the industrial, scientific, literary or artistic fields, including any rights relating to patents, copyrights, trademarks, industrial designs or plant breeders' rights;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "International Legal Obligation" means an obligation binding on Canada under international law, including those that are in force before, on or after the Effective Date;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "International Treaty" means an agreement governed by international law and concluded in written form:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. between states; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. between one or more states and one or more international organizations,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: whether that agreement is embodied in a single instrument or in two or more related instruments and whatever its particular designation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "International Tribunal" means any international court, committee, treaty body, tribunal, arbitral tribunal or other international mechanism or procedure which has jurisdiction to consider the performance of Canada with regard to the International Legal Obligation in question;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Intertidal Bivalves" means Manila clams, littleneck clams, butter clams, horse clams, softshell clams, varnish clams, blue mussels, California mussels, cockles and oysters;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Joint Fisheries Committee" means the committee established under paragraph 85 of the Fisheries Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Land Title Office" means the Land Title Office, as established and described in the Land Title Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Local Government" means a "local government" as defined in the Local Government Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Logs" means logs of all species of wood which are controlled under Canada's Export Control List, Group 5, Item number 5101, pursuant to section 3 (1) (e) of the Export and Import Permits Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Lois Harvest Area" means the area identified as "Lois Harvest Area" in Appendix Q;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Lund Hotel Parcels" means the lands described in Part 1 of Appendix C-3 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix C-3 as the "Lund Hotel Parcels";

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Marine Protected Area" means a marine protected area as described in subsection 35 (1) of the Oceans Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Migratory Bird Sanctuary" means an area described in the schedule to the Migratory Bird Sanctuary Regulations;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Migratory Birds" means "migratory birds" as defined under Federal Law enacted further to international conventions and, for greater certainty, includes their eggs and inedible byproducts such as feathers and down;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Mineral" means an ore of metal or natural substance that can be mined and includes:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. rock and other materials from mine tailings, dumps and previously mined deposits of minerals;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. dimension stone; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. precious and base minerals;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Minister" means the federal or provincial minister having responsibility for the exercise of powers in relation to the matter in question and any individual with authority to act in respect of the matter in question;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Monumental Cedar and Cypress" means a Thuja plicata (western red cedar) or a Chamaecyparis nootkatensis (cypress or yellow cedar) that is:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. approximately 250 years or older; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. at least 100 centimetres diameter at 1.3 meters above germination point;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "National Historic Site" means a site, building or other place of national historic interest or significance that is commemorated under section 3 of the Historic Sites and Monuments Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "National Marine Conservation Area" means lands and water areas named and described in the schedules to the Canada National Marine Conservation Areas Act and includes a national marine conservation area reserve;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "National Park" means lands and waters named and described in the schedules to the Canada National Parks Act and includes a national park reserve;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "National Wildlife Area" means a national wildlife area as defined under Federal Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Natural Gas" means all fluid hydrocarbons that are not defined as Petroleum, and includes coalbed gas and hydrogen sulphide, carbon dioxide and helium produced from a well;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Neutral" means an individual appointed to assist the Parties to resolve a Disagreement and, except in subparagraph 23.e of the Dispute Resolution Chapter, includes an arbitrator;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Neutral Appointing Authority" means the British Columbia International Commercial Arbitration Centre or, where the Centre is unavailable to make a required appointment, any other independent and impartial body or individual acceptable to the Parties;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Non-Allocated Species" means a species of Fish or Aquatic Plant for which a Tla'amin Fish Allocation has not been established under this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Non-Member" means an individual who has reached the age of majority under Provincial Law, is ordinarily resident on Tla'amin Lands and is not a Tla'amin Citizen;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Official Voters List" means the list of Eligible Voters prepared by the Ratification Committee under paragraph 7 of the Ratification Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Other Tla'amin Lands" means the lands described in Part 1 of Appendix D and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix D as "Other Tla'amin Lands";

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Parties" means the Tla'amin Nation, Canada and British Columbia and "Party" means any one of them;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Payment Date" means each of the first 50 anniversaries of the Effective Date of this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Periodic Review Date" means the 15th anniversary of the Effective Date or a date that occurs every 15 years after that date;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Person" for the purposes of the Taxation Chapter, includes an individual, a partnership, a corporation including a Crown corporation, a trust, an unincorporated association or other entity or government or any agency or political subdivision thereof, and their heirs, executors, administrators and other legal representatives;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Petroleum" means crude petroleum and all other hydrocarbons, regardless of specific gravity, that are or can be recovered in liquid form from a pool or that are or can be recovered from oil sand or oil shale;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Placer Mineral" means an ore of metal, including all base and precious metals, and every natural substance that can be mined and that is either loose, or found in fragmentary or broken rock that is not talus rock and occurs in loose earth, gravel and sand, and includes rock or other materials from placer mine tailings, dumps and previously mined deposits of placer minerals;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Plants" means all flora and fungi, but does not include Aquatic Plants or Timber Resources except for the bark, branches, burls, cones, foliage and roots of Timber Resources;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Powell-Daniels Harvest Area" means the area identified as "Powell-Daniels Harvest Area" in Appendix Q;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Private Lands" means land that is not Crown land;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Protected Area" means provincial Crown land established or designated as a provincial park, ecological reserve, conservancy or protected area under Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Provincial Crown Roads" means a road under the administration and control of British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Provincial Expropriating Authority" means a provincial ministry or agency or any person with the authority to expropriate land or an interest in land under Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Provincial Law" includes provincial statutes, regulations, ordinances, orders-in-council and the common law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Provincial Project" means a "reviewable project", as defined in the British Columbia Environmental Assessment Act, that is subject to an environmental assessment under that Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Provincial Public Planning Process Area" means the area set out in Appendix S;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Provincial Settlement Legislation" means the Act of the Legislature that gives effect to this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Public Planning Process" means a public planning process established by British Columbia to develop:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. regional or strategic land or resource use management plans or guidelines, including land and resource management plans, landscape unit plans and integrated watershed plans;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Protected Areas and their management plans; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. public plans or guidelines for specific sectors such as commercial recreation and agriculture, but not operational plans that give specific direction to government staff;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Public Utility" means a person, or the person's lessee, trustee, receiver or liquidator that owns or operates in British Columbia equipment or facilities for the:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. production, gathering, generating, processing, storage, transmission, sale, supply, distribution or delivery of petroleum (including petroleum products or byproducts), gas (including natural gas, natural gas liquids, propane and coalbed gas), electricity, steam, water, sewage, or any other agent for the production of light, heat, cold or power; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. emission, conveyance, transmission or reception of information, messages or communications by guided or unguided electromagnetic waves, including systems of cable, microwave, optical fibre or radio communications, if that service is offered to the public for compensation,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: and for the purposes of this definition, "person" includes a partnership and a corporation, including a Crown corporation or agent of the Crown;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Railway" means a company, established under Federal or Provincial Law, authorized to construct and operate a railway. For greater certainty, railway, as used in this definition, includes:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. all branches, extensions, sidings, stations, depots, wharves, rolling stock, equipment, works, property and works connected with the railway and all railway bridges, tunnels or other structures connected with the railway; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. communications or signalling systems and related facilities and equipment used for railway purposes;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Range Practices" means:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. grazing of livestock;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. cutting of hay;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. activities relating to grazing of livestock or cutting of hay; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. activities related to constructing, modifying or maintaining a structure, an excavation, a livestock trail or an improvement to forage quality or quantity for purposes of range development;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Ratification Committee" means the committee established under paragraph 5 of the Ratification Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Ratification Votes" means the votes conducted by the Ratification Committee for the ratification of the Tla'amin Constitution and this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Registrar" means a "registrar" as defined in the Land Title Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Resource Revenue Payment" means a resource revenue payment calculated in accordance with the formula set out in the Resource Revenue Sharing Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Review Period" means a time period beginning on a Periodic Review Date and ending on a date six months later or another date as the Parties may agree;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Right of Way" means a defined portion of Tla'amin Lands on which a grant is given by the Tla'amin Nation for a specified use, including use for a public or private road, or a Public Utility;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Safety and Well-Being of Children" includes the principle that the cultural identity of aboriginal children should be preserved and those other guiding principles under section 2 of the Child, Family and Community Service Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Sales Tax Collection Agreement" means the Sales Tax Collection Agreement entered into between Canada and the Sliammon Indian Band on August 23, 1999 as amended from time to time;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Sliammon Indian Band" means the Sliammon Indian Band which was, on the day before the Effective Date, a "band" as defined in the Indian Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Specific Claim Settlement" means any sum paid by Canada in settlement of a claim brought under the Specific Claims Policy or the Specific Claims Tribunal Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Specific Claims Policy" means the policy described in Canada's Specific Claims Policy and Process Guide (2009);

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "State of Title Certificate" means a certificate issued under the Land Title Act as evidence of a registered interest in Tla'amin Lands in the form set out in Document 1 of Appendix F-6;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Stewardship Activities" means activities conducted for the assessment, monitoring, protection and management of Fish and Fish habitat;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Stream" means a natural watercourse or source of water supply, whether usually containing water or not, and a lake, river, creek, spring, ravine, swamp and gulch, but does not include Groundwater;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Submerged Lands" means land below the "natural boundary" as that term is defined in the Land Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Subsurface Resources" include the following:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. earth, including diatomaceous earth, soil, peat, marl, sand and gravel;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. slate, shale, argillite, limestone, marble, clay, gypsum, volcanic ash and rock;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. Minerals, including Placer Minerals;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. coal, Petroleum and Natural Gas;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. Fossils; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. Geothermal Resources;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Sunshine Coast Trail" means the unofficial footpath as it exists on the Effective Date and which is identified for illustrative purposes in Part 1 of Appendix K;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Surrendered Lands" means "surrendered lands" as defined in the Indian Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Theodosia Harvest Area" means the area identified as the "Theodosia Harvest Area" in Appendix Q;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Timber Resources" means trees whether standing, fallen, living, dead, limbed, bucked or peeled;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Annual Fishing Plan" means a fishing plan described in the Fisheries Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Archaeological Human Remains" means Archaeological Human Remains that are determined to be of Tla'amin ancestry;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Area" means the area set out in Appendix A;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Artifact" means any object created by, traded to, commissioned by or given as a gift to a Tla'amin individual or Tla'amin community, or that originated from a Tla'amin community, and that has past and ongoing importance to Tla'amin culture or spiritual practices, but does not include any object traded to, commissioned by or given as a gift to another aboriginal group or person;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Capital" means all land, cash and other assets transferred to, or recognized as owned by, the Tla'amin Nation under this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Child" means a Child who is a Tla'amin Citizen;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Citizen" means an individual who is enrolled under this Agreement in accordance with the Eligibility and Enrolment Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Constitution" means the constitution of the Tla'amin Nation described in the Governance Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Corporation" means a corporation that is incorporated under Federal or Provincial Law, all of the shares of which, except any qualifying shares that directors are required to own under Federal or Provincial Law, are owned, directly or indirectly, legally and beneficially by:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. one or more trusts that is resident in Canada and is for the sole benefit of the Tla'amin Nation; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. any combination of the persons set out in subparagraphs a and b;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Family" means a family where one or both parents or guardians live together with one or more Children and:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. at least one of the parents or guardians is a Tla'amin Citizen; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. at least one of the Children is a Tla'amin Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Fish Allocation" means in respect of a right to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a defined harvest quantity or quota;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a formula defining a harvest quantity or quota; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a defined harvest area within the Tla'amin Fishing Area;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Fishing Area" means:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. for all species of Fish and Aquatic Plants other than herring, the area described in Part 1 of Appendix N-1 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix N-1 as the "Tla'amin Fishing Area"; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. for herring, the area described in Part 1 of Appendix N-2 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix N-2 as the "Tla'amin Herring Fishing Area";

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Fishing Right" means the right to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants set out in paragraph 1 of the Fisheries Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Government" means the government of the Tla'amin Nation referred to in paragraph 2 of the Governance Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Harvest Document" means any fishing licence, permit or document, or amendment thereto, issued by the Minister under Federal or Provincial Law in respect of the Tla'amin Fishing Right;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Institution" means Tla'amin Government or a Tla'amin Public Institution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Lands" means the lands set out in Appendix C;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Law" means a law made pursuant to the Tla'amin Nation law-making authority set out in this Agreement and includes the Tla'amin Constitution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Nation" means the collectivity of those individuals eligible to be enrolled under this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Nation Certificate" means a certificate issued by the Tla'amin Nation as described under subparagraph 13.b of the Land Title Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin People" means those individuals who are eligible to be enrolled under this Agreement in accordance with the Eligibility and Enrolment Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Plant Gathering Area" means the area set out in Appendix T;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Private Lands" means those Tla'amin Lands designated as Tla'amin Private Lands by the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Project" means a project on Tla'amin Lands that is subject to an environmental assessment under Tla'amin Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Public Institution" means a body, board, commission or any other similar entity established under Tla'amin Law, including a school board or health board, but for greater certainty does not include Tla'amin Government;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Public Lands" means Tla'amin Lands other than Tla'amin Private Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Public Officer" means:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. an officer or employee of the Tla'amin Nation or a Tla'amin Institution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a member, commissioner, director or trustee of a Tla'amin Public Institution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a director, officer or employee of a Tla'amin Corporation whose principal function is to provide programs or services reasonably similar to those provided by federal, provincial or municipal governments, rather than to engage in commercial activities;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. a volunteer who participates in the delivery of programs or services by a body referred to in subparagraph b, under the supervision of a director, officer or employee of that body; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. an election official within the meaning of Tla'amin Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Records" means records including any correspondence, memoranda, books, plans, maps, drawings, diagrams, pictorial or graphic work, photographs, films, microforms, sound recordings, videotape, machine readable records and any other documentary material regardless of physical form or characteristics and any copy thereof that document Tla'amin culture;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Right to Gather Plants" means the right to gather Plants set out in paragraph 14 of the Tla'amin Role Outside Tla'amin Lands Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Right to Harvest Migratory Birds" means the right to harvest Migratory Birds set out in paragraph 1 of the Migratory Birds Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Right to Harvest Wildlife" means the right to harvest Wildlife set out in paragraph 1 of the Wildlife Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Road" means any road on Tla'amin Lands under the administration and control of the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Section 35 Rights" means the rights, anywhere in Canada, of the Tla'amin Nation, that are recognized and affirmed by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Total Allowable Migratory Bird Harvest" means the maximum number of a Designated Migratory Bird Population that may be harvested in a specified period of time;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Trade and Barter" does not include sale;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Transaction Tax" includes a tax imposed under:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Carbon Tax Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the Consumption Tax Rebate and Transition Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the Hotel Room Tax Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. section 4 of the Insurance Premium Tax Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. the Motor Fuel Tax Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. the Property Transfer Tax Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. the Social Service Tax Act (except those sections pertaining to alcohol);

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. the Tobacco Tax Act; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. Part IX of the Excise Tax Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Water Licence" means a licence, approval or other authorization under Provincial Law for the storage, diversion, extraction or use of water, and for the construction, maintenance and operation of works;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Wildfire Suppression Agreement" means an agreement entered into by Canada, British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation under paragraph 15 of the Forest Resources Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Wildlife" means:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. all vertebrate and invertebrate animals, including mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the eggs, juvenile stages and adult stages of all vertebrate and invertebrate animals,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: but does not include Fish or Migratory Birds; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Wildlife and Migratory Birds Harvest Area" means the area identified as the "Wildlife and Migratory Birds Harvest Area" in Appendix P of this Agreement, but does not include lands that are owned by Canada or lands that are administered or occupied by the Minister of National Defence, or areas temporarily being used for military training from the time that notice has been given to the Tla'amin Nation until the temporary use is completed.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 2 - GENERAL PROVISIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NATURE OF THIS AGREEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. This Agreement is a treaty and a land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: AGREEMENT IS BINDING

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. This Agreement is binding on the Parties and all persons.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. The Parties and all persons are entitled to rely on this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. Canada and British Columbia will recommend to Parliament and the Legislature, respectively, that Federal Settlement Legislation and Provincial Settlement Legislation provide that this Agreement is approved, given effect, declared valid and has the force of law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. The Tla'amin Nation represents and warrants to Canada and British Columbia that, in relation to the matters dealt with in this Agreement, it has the authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of all individuals who, based on their identity as Tla'amin People, may exercise any aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, in Canada, or may make any claims to those rights.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Canada and British Columbia represent and warrant to the Tla'amin Nation that, in relation to the matters dealt with in this Agreement, they have the authority to enter into this Agreement within their respective authorities.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CONSTITUTION OF CANADA

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. This Agreement does not alter the Constitution of Canada, including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the distribution of powers between Canada and British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the identity of the Tla'amin Nation as an aboriginal people of Canada within the meaning of the Constitution Act, 1982; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, including section 25, applies to the Tla'amin Nation in respect of all matters within its authority.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHARACTER OF TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. There are no "Lands reserved for the Indians" within the meaning of the Constitution Act, 1867 for the Tla'amin Nation and there are no Indian Reserves for the use and benefit of the Tla'amin Nation. For greater certainty, Tla'amin Lands are not "Lands reserved for the Indians" within the meaning of the Constitution Act, 1867 and are not Indian Reserves.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: APPLICATION OF FEDERAL AND PROVINCIAL LAW

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. This Agreement prevails to the extent of an inconsistency or a Conflict with Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. Federal Settlement Legislation prevails to the extent of a Conflict with other Federal Laws.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Provincial Settlement Legislation prevails to the extent of a Conflict with other Provincial Laws.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. Federal and Provincial Law apply to the Tla'amin Nation, Tla'amin Institutions, Tla'amin Corporations, Tla'amin Citizens, Tla'amin Lands and Other Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. Where an authority or obligation of British Columbia referred to in this Agreement is based on a delegation of authority from Canada, the reference to British Columbia will be deemed to be a reference to Canada if:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a superior court of a province, the Federal Court of Canada or the Supreme Court of Canada finally determines that the delegation of that authority is invalid.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. Where an authority or obligation of Canada referred to in this Agreement is based on a delegation of authority from British Columbia, the reference to Canada will be deemed to be a reference to British Columbia if:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a superior court of a province, the Federal Court of Canada or the Supreme Court of Canada finally determines that the delegation of that authority is invalid.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Any licence, permit, tenure or other authorization to be issued by Canada or British Columbia as a result of this Agreement will be issued under Federal or Provincial Law, as the case may be, and will not be part of this Agreement. This Agreement prevails to the extent of an inconsistency with any such licence, permit, tenure or other authorization.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. For greater certainty, paragraph 16 does not limit the obligation of the Minister to issue a Tla'amin Harvest Document under paragraph 76 of the Fisheries Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: RELATIONSHIP OF LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Notwithstanding any other rule of priority in this Agreement, Federal or Provincial Law prevails over Tla'amin Law to the extent of any Conflict involving a provision of a Tla'amin Law that has a double aspect with or an incidental impact on:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. any area of federal or provincial jurisdiction for which the Tla'amin Nation does not have any law-making authority; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. any area of jurisdiction for which Federal or Provincial Law prevails.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. For greater certainty, the Tla'amin Nation law-making authority under this Agreement does not extend to criminal law and procedure, Intellectual Property, official languages of Canada, aeronautics, navigation and shipping, or labour relations and working conditions.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Notwithstanding any other rule of priority in this Agreement, Federal Law prevails over Tla'amin Law to the extent of any Conflict involving a provision of a Tla'amin Law that Conflicts or is inconsistent with Federal Law in relation to peace, order and good government, criminal law, human rights, the protection of health and safety of all Canadians, or other matters of overriding national importance.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. Canada will recommend to Parliament that Federal Settlement Legislation include a provision that, to the extent a Provincial Law does not apply of its own force to the Tla'amin Nation, Tla'amin Institutions, Tla'amin Corporations, Tla'amin Citizens, Tla'amin Lands or Other Tla'amin Lands, the Provincial Law will, subject to Federal Settlement Legislation and any other Act of Parliament, apply in accordance with this Agreement to the Tla'amin Nation, Tla'amin Institutions, Tla'amin Corporations, Tla'amin Citizens, Tla'amin Lands and Other Tla'amin Lands, as the case may be.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Unless otherwise provided in this Agreement, Tla'amin Law does not apply to Canada or British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. Tla'amin Law is of no force or effect to the extent of an inconsistency or Conflict with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: INTERNATIONAL LEGAL OBLIGATIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. After the Effective Date, before consenting to be bound by a new International Treaty that would give rise to a new International Legal Obligation that may adversely affect a right of the Tla'amin Nation under this Agreement, Canada will Consult with the Tla'amin Nation in relation to the International Treaty either separately or through a forum that Canada determines is appropriate.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. Where Canada informs the Tla'amin Nation that it considers that a Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government causes Canada to be unable to perform an International Legal Obligation, the Tla'amin Nation and Canada will discuss remedial measures to enable Canada to perform the International Legal Obligation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Subject to paragraph 27, the Tla'amin Nation will remedy the Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government to the extent necessary to enable Canada to perform the International Legal Obligation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. Subject to paragraph 29, where Canada and the Tla'amin Nation disagree over whether a Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government causes Canada to be unable to perform an International Legal Obligation, the dispute will be finally determined by arbitration under the Dispute Resolution Chapter, and:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. where the arbitrator, having taken into account all relevant considerations, including any reservations and exceptions taken by Canada, determines that the Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government does not cause Canada to be unable to perform the International Legal Obligation, or that the remedial measures are sufficient to enable Canada to perform the International Legal Obligation, Canada will not take any further action for this reason aimed at changing the Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where the arbitrator, having taken into account all relevant considerations, including any reservations and exceptions available to Canada, determines that the Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government causes Canada to be unable to perform the International Legal Obligation, or that the remedial measures are insufficient to enable Canada to perform the International Legal Obligation, the Tla'amin Nation will remedy the Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government to the extent necessary to enable Canada to perform the International Legal Obligation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. Canada will Consult with the Tla'amin Nation in relation to the development of positions taken by Canada before an International Tribunal where a Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government has given rise to an issue concerning the performance of an International Legal Obligation of Canada and Canada's positions before the International Tribunal will take into account the commitment of the Parties to the integrity of this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. Where there is a finding of an International Tribunal of non-performance of an International Legal Obligation of Canada attributable to a Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government, the Tla'amin Nation will, at the request of Canada, remedy the Tla'amin Law or other exercise of power by the Tla'amin Government to enable Canada to perform the International Legal Obligation consistent with the compliance of Canada or British Columbia, as applicable, with that International Legal Obligation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: APPLICATION OF THE INDIAN ACT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. Subject to the Transition Chapter, the Indian Act does not apply to the Tla'amin Nation, Tla'amin Institutions, Tla'amin Citizens, Tla'amin Lands and Other Tla'amin Lands, except for:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the purpose of determining whether an individual is an "Indian"; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. section 87 of that Act in respect of Tla'amin Citizens prior to the dates set out in paragraph 16 of the Taxation Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. Subject to paragraph 6 of the Transition Chapter, the Framework Agreement on First Nation Land Management, the First Nations Land Management Act and the Sliammon First Nation Land Code have no application to the Tla'amin Nation, Tla'amin Institutions, Tla'amin Citizens or Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. For so long as the First Nations Land Management Act is in force, Canada will indemnify the Tla'amin Nation, and the Tla'amin Nation will indemnify Canada, in relation to Former Sliammon Indian Reserves, in the same manner and under the same conditions as would be the case if that Act applied to those lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: OTHER RIGHTS, BENEFITS AND PROGRAMS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. Tla'amin Citizens who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents of Canada continue to be entitled to all of the rights and benefits for which they would otherwise be eligible as Canadian citizens or permanent residents of Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. Subject to paragraph 36, nothing in this Agreement affects the ability of the Tla'amin Nation, Tla'amin Institutions, Tla'amin Corporations or Tla'amin Citizens to participate in, or benefit from, programs established by Canada or British Columbia for aboriginal people, registered Indians or other Indians in accordance with criteria established for those programs from time to time.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. Nothing in this Agreement affects the ability of the Tla'amin Nation, Tla'amin Institutions, Tla'amin Corporations or Tla'amin Citizens to apply for or bid on any commercial, economic or other activity or project for which they would otherwise be eligible.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. Tla'amin Citizens are eligible to participate in programs established by Canada or British Columbia and to receive public services from Canada or British Columbia, in accordance with general criteria established for those programs or public services from time to time, to the extent that the Tla'amin Nation has not assumed responsibility for those programs or public services under a Fiscal Financing Agreement or other funding agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: COURT DECISIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. Where a superior court of a province, the Federal Court of Canada or the Supreme Court of Canada finally determines that any provision of this Agreement is invalid or unenforceable:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Parties will make best efforts to amend this Agreement to remedy or replace the provision; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the provision will be severable from this Agreement to the extent of the invalidity or unenforceability and the remainder of this Agreement will be construed, to the extent possible, to give effect to the intent of the Parties.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 38. No Party will challenge, or support a challenge to, the validity of any provision of this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 39. A breach of this Agreement by a Party does not relieve any Party from its obligations under this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CERTAINTY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Full and Final Settlement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 40. This Agreement constitutes the full and final settlement with respect to the Tla'amin Nation's aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, in Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Exhaustively Sets Out Rights

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 41. This Agreement exhaustively sets out Tla'amin Section 35 Rights, the attributes and the geographic extent of those rights, and the limitations to those rights, to which the Parties have agreed, and those rights are:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation's aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, in Canada, modified as a result of this Agreement, in and to Tla'amin Lands and other lands and resources in Canada;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the jurisdictions, authorities and rights of the Tla'amin Nation and Tla'amin Government; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the other Tla'amin Section 35 Rights.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Modification

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 42. Notwithstanding the common law, as a result of this Agreement and the Federal Settlement Legislation and Provincial Settlement Legislation, the Tla'amin Nation's aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, as they existed anywhere in Canada before the Effective Date, including the attributes and the geographic extent of those rights, are modified, and continue as modified, as set out in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 43. For greater certainty, the Tla'amin Nation's aboriginal title as it existed anywhere in Canada before the Effective Date, including its attributes and geographic extent, is modified and continues as the estates in fee simple to those areas identified in this Agreement as Tla'amin Lands and Other Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Purpose of Modification

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 44. The purpose of the modification referred to in paragraph 42 is to ensure that as of the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation has, and can exercise, Tla'amin Section 35 Rights as set out in this Agreement, including the attributes and geographic extent of those rights, and the limitations to those rights, to which the Parties have agreed;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Canada, British Columbia and all other persons can exercise their rights, authorities, jurisdictions and privileges in a manner consistent with this Agreement; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. Canada, British Columbia and all other persons do not have any obligations in relation to any of the Tla'amin Nation's aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, to the extent that they might be in any way other than, or different in attributes or geographic extent from, Tla'amin Section 35 Rights as set out in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 45. For greater certainty, any aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, that the Tla'amin Nation may have are not extinguished, but are modified and continue as modified as set out in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Release of Past Claims

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 46. The Tla'amin Nation releases Canada, British Columbia and all other persons from all claims, demands, actions or proceedings, of whatever kind, whether known or unknown, that the Tla'amin Nation ever had, now has or may have in the future, relating to or arising from any act or omission before the Effective Date that may have affected, interfered with or infringed any of the Tla'amin Nation's aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, in Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Indemnities

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 47. The Tla'amin Nation will indemnify and save harmless Canada or British Columbia, as the case may be, from any:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. costs, excluding fees and disbursements of solicitors and other professional advisors;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. damages;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. losses; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. liabilities

heading: Commencement
paragraph: that Canada or British Columbia, respectively, may suffer or incur in connection with, or as a result of, any claims, demands, actions or proceedings relating to or arising out of any act or omission before the Effective Date that may have affected or infringed any of the Tla'amin Nation's aboriginal rights, including aboriginal title, in Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 48. The Tla'amin Nation will indemnify and save harmless Canada or British Columbia, as the case may be, from any:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. costs, excluding fees and disbursements of solicitors and other professional advisors;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. damages;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. losses; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. liabilities

heading: Commencement
paragraph: that Canada, or British Columbia, respectively, may suffer or incur in connection with or as a result of any claims, demands, actions or proceedings relating to or arising out of the existence of any aboriginal right, including aboriginal title, of the Tla'amin Nation in Canada that is other than, or different in attributes or geographical extent from, Tla'amin Section 35 Rights as set out in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 49. A Party who is the subject of a claim, demand, action or proceeding that may give rise to a requirement to provide payment to that Party under an indemnity under this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. will vigorously defend the claim, demand, action or proceeding; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. will not settle or compromise the claim, demand, action or proceeding except with the consent of the Party who has granted that indemnity, which consent will not be arbitrarily or unreasonably withheld or delayed.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: SPECIFIC CLAIMS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 50. Nothing in this Agreement precludes the Tla'amin Nation from pursuing any claims, including any claims respecting Teeskwat, that fall within the scope of Canada's Specific Claims Policy, in accordance with that policy, the Specific Claims Tribunal Act or in court. For greater certainty, if the Tla'amin Nation pursues a specific claim in court, Canada reserves the right to plead all defenses available to it including limitation periods, laches and lack of admissible evidence.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 51. For greater certainty, the Tla'amin Nation's claims referred to in paragraph 50 will not result in any land being declared to be, or being set aside as, "Lands reserved for the Indians" within the meaning of the Constitution Act, 1867 for the Tla'amin Nation or an Indian Reserve for the use and benefit of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: OTHER ABORIGINAL PEOPLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 52. Nothing in this Agreement affects, recognizes or provides any rights under section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 for any aboriginal people other than the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 53. Where a superior court of a province, the Federal Court of Canada or the Supreme Court of Canada finally determines that any aboriginal people, other than the Tla'amin Nation, have rights under section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 that are adversely affected by a provision of this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the provision will operate and have effect to the extent that it does not adversely affect those rights; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where the provision cannot operate and have effect in a way that it does not adversely affect those rights, the Parties will make best efforts to amend this Agreement to remedy or replace the provision.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 54. Where Canada or British Columbia enters into a treaty or a land claims agreement, within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982, with another aboriginal people, and that treaty or land claims agreement adversely affects Tla'amin Section 35 Rights as set out in this Agreement, Canada or British Columbia, or both, as the case may be, will provide the Tla'amin Nation with additional or replacement rights or other appropriate remedies.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 55. At the request of the Tla'amin Nation, the Parties will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on the provision of those additional or replacement rights or other appropriate remedies under paragraph 54.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CONSULTATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 56. Neither Canada nor British Columbia has any obligation to Consult with the Tla'amin Nation except:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. as provided for in this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. as provided for in Federal or Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. as provided for in an agreement with the Tla'amin Nation other than this Agreement; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. as may be required at common law in relation to an infringement of a Tla'amin Section 35 Right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 57. Nothing in this Agreement, nor any action or authority taken, exercised or carried out by Canada or British Columbia in accordance with this Agreement will be, or will be interpreted to be, an infringement of a Tla'amin Section 35 Right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PERIODIC REVIEW

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 58. The Parties recognize and acknowledge that this Agreement provides a foundation for an ongoing relationship amongst the Parties and commit to conducting a periodic review of this Agreement in accordance with paragraphs 59 to 65.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 59. At least sixty days before each Periodic Review Date, each Party will provide the other Parties with written notice if the Party wishes to discuss a matter contemplated by paragraph 60, and if no notice is provided by any Party, the Parties will forego engaging in a review for that Review Period.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 60. The purpose of the periodic review is to provide an opportunity for the Parties to meet and discuss:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the practicability of the harmonization of the Tla'amin Nation's legal and administrative systems, including law-making authorities that are being exercised by the Tla'amin Nation, with those of Canada and British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the practicability of processes established by the Parties under this Agreement; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. other matters in relation to the implementation of this Agreement as may be agreed to by the Parties in writing.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 61. Unless the Parties otherwise agree, the discussion under paragraph 60 will take place on the Periodic Review Date and such other dates as the Parties agree, but will not exceed the applicable Review Period. Within 60 days of the end of that discussion each Party will provide the other Parties with its written response on any matter discussed during that Review Period.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 62. The periodic review under paragraphs 58 to 65 and all discussions and information relating to the periodic review are without prejudice to the legal positions of the Parties, unless the Parties otherwise agree. Nothing made or done in relation to a periodic review, including the discussions or the responses provided by the Parties, except for any amendments made pursuant to paragraph 64, creates any legally binding rights or obligations.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 63. Except for the Parties' commitment to meet and provide written responses under paragraph 61, neither the periodic review process under paragraphs 58 to 65, nor the decisions or actions of the Parties relating in any way to the periodic review process, is:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. subject to the Dispute Resolution Chapter; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. reviewable by a court or in any other forum.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 64. For greater certainty:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. no Party is required to agree to amend this Agreement or any agreement contemplated by this Agreement as a result of the periodic review under paragraphs 58 to 65;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where the Parties agree to amend this Agreement, any such amendment will be made in accordance with the Amendment Chapter; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. where the Parties agree to amend an agreement contemplated by this Agreement, the agreement will be amended in accordance with its terms.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 65. Each of the Parties will be responsible for its own costs in relation to the periodic review process.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: INFORMATION AND PRIVACY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 66. For the purposes of federal and provincial access to information and privacy legislation, information that the Tla'amin Nation provides to Canada or British Columbia in confidence is deemed to be information received or obtained in confidence from another government.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 67. Where the Tla'amin Nation requests disclosure of information from Canada or British Columbia, the request will be evaluated as if it were a request by a province for disclosure of that information, but Canada and British Columbia are not required to disclose to the Tla'amin Nation information that is only available to a particular province or particular provinces, or that is not available to any provinces.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 68. The Parties may enter into agreements in relation to any one or more of the collection, protection, retention, use, disclosure and confidentiality of personal, general or other information in accordance with any applicable legislation, including federal and provincial access to information and privacy legislation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 69. Canada or British Columbia may provide information to the Tla'amin Nation in confidence if the Tla'amin Nation has made a law or has entered into an agreement with Canada or British Columbia, as the case may be, under which the confidentiality of the information will be protected.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 70. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Canada and British Columbia are not required to disclose any information that they are required or authorized to withhold under Federal or Provincial Law, including under sections 37 to 39 of the Canada Evidence Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where Federal or Provincial Law allows the disclosure of certain information only if specified conditions for disclosure are satisfied, Canada and British Columbia are not required to disclose that information unless those conditions are satisfied; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the Parties are not required to disclose any information that may be withheld under a privilege at law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: OBLIGATION TO NEGOTIATE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 71. Where the Parties are obliged under this Agreement to negotiate and attempt to reach agreement all Parties will participate in the negotiations, unless the Parties otherwise agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 72. Where this Agreement provides that the Parties, or any two of them, "will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement", those negotiations will be conducted as set out in the Dispute Resolution Chapter, but no Party is obliged to proceed to arbitration under Stage Three unless, in a particular case, they are required to do so under paragraph 27 of the Dispute Resolution Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 73. Where this Agreement provides that a dispute will be "finally determined by arbitration", the dispute will be referred to arbitration under paragraph 27 of the Dispute Resolution Chapter, unless none of the Parties directly engaged in the Disagreement delivers notice to all Parties under Appendix X-6.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENTIRE AGREEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 74. This Agreement is the entire agreement among the Parties in respect of the subject matter of this Agreement and, except as set out in this Agreement, there is no representation, warranty, collateral agreement, condition, right or obligation affecting this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 75. The Schedules and Appendices to this Agreement form part of this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NO IMPLIED WAIVER

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 76. Any waiver of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a provision of this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the performance by a Party of an obligation under this Agreement; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a default by a Party of an obligation under this Agreement,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: will be in writing and signed by the Party or Parties giving the waiver and will not be a waiver of any other provision, obligation or subsequent default.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ASSIGNMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 77. Unless the Parties otherwise agree, this Agreement may not be assigned, either in whole or in part, by any Party.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENUREMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 78. This Agreement will enure to the benefit of and be binding upon the Parties and their respective permitted assigns.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: MINOR CHANGES AND CORRECTIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 79. After ratification of this Agreement by the Tla'amin Nation, but before the Parties sign this Agreement, the Chief Negotiators on behalf of Canada, British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation may agree to minor changes to this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 80. Before the Effective Date, the Chief Negotiators for Canada, British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation may agree to amendments to this Agreement and the Appendices to update information or correct any editing, grammatical or typographical errors. Any updated information or corrections may be incorporated in the printing of this Agreement and the Appendices after the Effective Date.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: INTERPRETATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 81. The provisions of this Chapter prevail over the provisions in the other Chapters, the Schedules to the other Chapters and the Appendices to the extent of an inconsistency.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 82. No agreement, plan, guideline or other document made or issued by a Party or Parties that is referred to or contemplated by this Agreement, including an agreement that is reached as a result of negotiations that are required or permitted by this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. is part of this Agreement; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. is a treaty or land claims agreement, or creates, recognizes or affirms any aboriginal or treaty rights, within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 83. There will be no presumption that doubtful expressions, terms or provisions in this Agreement are to be resolved in favour of any Party.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 84. In this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. "will" denotes an obligation that, unless this Agreement provides otherwise or otherwise clear from the context, must be carried out as soon as practicable after the Effective Date or the event that gives rise to the obligation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. "may" is to be construed as permissive and empowering;

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. "harvest" includes attempts to harvest and "gather" includes attempts to gather;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. "provincial" means relating to the province of British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. a reference in a Chapter of this Agreement to a "paragraph", "subparagraph" or "Schedule" means a paragraph, subparagraph or schedule of that Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. a reference to a "Chapter", "paragraph", "subparagraph", "Schedule" or "Appendix" means a Chapter, paragraph, subparagraph, schedule or appendix of this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. headings and subheadings are for convenience only, do not form a part of this Agreement and in no way define, limit, alter or enlarge the scope or meaning of any provision of this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the use of the singular includes the plural and the use of the plural includes the singular;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: j. where a word is defined, other parts of speech and grammatical forms of the same word have corresponding meanings; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: k. a reference to a statute will include every amendment to it, every regulation made under it, every amendment made to a regulation made under it and any law enacted in substitution for, or in replacement of, it.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 85. The Parties acknowledge that the Official Languages Act applies to this Agreement, including the execution of this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 86. Notwithstanding paragraph 2, this Agreement is not intended to bind provinces, other than British Columbia, or territories, on matters within their jurisdiction without their consent.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NOTICE

paragraph: 87. In paragraphs 88 to 93, "communication" includes a notice, document, request, response, confirmation, approval, authorization or consent.

heading: Commencement

paragraph: c. where delivered by any method for which confirmation of delivery is provided, when receipt is acknowledged by the addressee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 90. The Parties may agree to give, make or deliver a communication by means other than those set out in paragraph 88.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 91. The Parties will provide to each other addresses for delivery of communications under this Agreement and, subject to paragraph 92, will deliver a communication to the address provided by each Party.

paragraph: 92. If no other address for delivery of a particular communication has been provided by a Party, a communication will be delivered to, mailed to the address or transmitted to the fax number of, the intended recipient as set out below:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 3 - LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. On the Effective Date, Tla'amin Lands consist of the following:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. 1,917 hectares, more or less, of Former Sliammon Indian Reserves subject to paragraph 24;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. 6,405 hectares, more or less, of provincial Crown land identified for illustrative purposes in Part 1 of Appendix C-2 and described in Part 2 of Appendix C-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. 0.968 hectares, more or less, of lands identified as the Lund Hotel Parcels subject to the Tla'amin Nation meeting the conditions under paragraph 25; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. 0.393 hectares, more or less, of lands described in Part 1 of Appendix C-4 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix C-4 as "Oyster Plant Upland Parcel",

heading: Commencement
paragraph: including Subsurface Resources referred to in paragraph 67.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. On the Effective Date, Other Tla'amin Lands consist of 0.38 hectares, more or less, described in Part 1 of Appendix D and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix D as "Other Tla'amin Lands".

heading: Commencement
paragraph: OWNERSHIP OF TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation owns Tla'amin Lands in fee simple except for those lands identified as the Lund Hotel Parcels.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. The Tla'amin Nation's fee simple ownership of Tla'amin Lands is not subject to any condition, proviso, restriction, exception or reservation set out in the Land Act, or any comparable limitation under Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. All methods of acquiring a right in or over land by prescription or by adverse possession, including the common law doctrine of prescription and the doctrine of the lost modern grant, are abolished in relation to Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Where, at any time, any parcel of Tla'amin Lands, or any estate or interest in a parcel of Tla'amin Lands, finally escheats to the Crown, the Crown will transfer, at no charge, that parcel, estate or interest to the Tla'amin Nation and it will form part of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. Paragraphs 4, 5 and 6 will apply notwithstanding the registration of Tla'amin Lands under the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LIMITATIONS ON SEIZURE OF TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. An estate, interest, reservation or exception held by the Tla'amin Nation or by a Tla'amin Public Institution in any parcel of Tla'amin Lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the title to which is not registered in the Land Title Office; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. in respect of which title no application for registration in the Land Title Office has been made,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: is not subject to attachment, charge, seizure, distress, execution or sale under a writ of execution, order for sale or other process unless the attachment, charge, seizure, distress, execution or sale under a writ of execution, order for sale or other process is:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. made or issued for the purpose of enforcing, in accordance with its terms, a security instrument granted by the Tla'amin Nation or by a Tla'amin Public Institution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. allowed under Tla'amin Law; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. made or issued for the purpose of enforcing a lien in favour of Canada or British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. An estate, interest, reservation or exception held by the Tla'amin Nation or by a Tla'amin Public Institution in any parcel of Tla'amin Lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the title to which is registered in the Land Title Office; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. in respect of which title an application for registration in the Land Title Office has been made,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: is not subject to seizure or sale under a writ of execution, order for sale or other process unless the writ of execution, order for sale or other process is:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. made or issued for the purpose of enforcing, in accordance with its terms, a security instrument granted by the Tla'amin Nation or by a Tla'amin Public Institution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. allowed under Tla'amin Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. made or issued for the purpose of enforcing a lien in favour of Canada or British Columbia; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. by leave of the Supreme Court of British Columbia under paragraph 192 of the Governance Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CREATION AND DISPOSITION OF ESTATES AND INTERESTS IN TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. In accordance with this Agreement, the Tla'amin Constitution and Tla'amin Law, the Tla'amin Nation may without the consent of Canada or British Columbia:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. dispose of its fee simple estate in any parcel of Tla'amin Lands to any person; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. from its fee simple estate, or its interest in any parcel of Tla'amin Lands, create or dispose of any lesser estate or interest to any person, including Rights of Way and covenants similar to those in sections 218 and 219 of the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. Where the Tla'amin Nation disposes of a fee simple estate in a parcel of Tla'amin Lands under an agreement with Canada, at the time of the transfer of ownership, those lands will no longer be Tla'amin Lands and Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Subject to paragraph 11, section 14 of Appendix J-1 and section 18 of Appendix J-2, or the agreement of the Parties, a parcel of Tla'amin Lands does not cease to be Tla'amin Lands as a result of any change in ownership of an estate or interest in that parcel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. Where the Tla'amin Nation wishes to dispose of a fee simple estate in a parcel of Tla'amin Lands it will, prior to the disposition, register the indefeasible title to that parcel under the Land Title Act in accordance with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. Where the Tla'amin Nation disposes of a fee simple estate in a parcel of Tla'amin Lands to any person, other than a Tla'amin Institution, a Tla'amin Corporation or a Tla'amin Citizen, expropriation of any interest in that parcel will occur in accordance with Federal or Provincial Law and is not subject to paragraphs 122 to 128 or Appendices J-1 and J-2, except section 14 of Appendix J-1 and section 18 of Appendix J-2.

heading: Commencement
