paragraph: 15. The Tla'amin Nation may remove a fee simple estate from Tla'amin Lands with the consent of Canada and British Columbia. In considering whether to consent to the removal of the parcel from Tla'amin Lands, Canada and British Columbia may consider:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. necessary jurisdictional, administrative and servicing arrangements;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the views of any affected Local Governments and neighbouring First Nations;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. whether removal of the land will have an impact on fiscal arrangements negotiated between the Tla'amin Nation and either or both of Canada and British Columbia; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. whether its removal will create legal or financial exposure to Canada or British Columbia; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. any other matters Canada or British Columbia consider relevant.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Where Canada and British Columbia consent to the removal of a parcel of land from Tla'amin Lands then, upon the Tla'amin Nation's receipt of Canada and British Columbia's written consent:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation will register the parcel of land in the Land Title Office, if it is not registered;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the parcel will cease to be Tla'amin Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PRE-EFFECTIVE DATE LAND TRANSFERS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. Before the Effective Date, some or all of the following lands may be transferred by British Columbia to one or more corporations or societies designated by the Sliammon Indian Band subject, where applicable, to the continuing interests set out in Part 1 of Appendix F-3 and on such other terms and conditions as British Columbia and the Sliammon Indian Band may agree:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the lands identified as the "Oyster Plant Parcel" in Map 4a, Part 2 of Appendix C-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. DL 5176, DL 5182 and DL 5186, Group 1, New Westminster District within the municipal boundaries identified in Map 8, Part 2 of Appendix C-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the lands identified as the "Lund Filled Foreshore Parcels" in Map 10, Part 2 of Appendix C-2; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the lands identified as the "Wharf Street Parcel" in Map 1, Part 2 of Appendix D.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. The entity designated under paragraph 17 may not dispose of the fee simple interest in the lands referred to in paragraph 17, but may grant a lesser interest provided that the entity will, prior to doing so, advise the intended charge or encumbrance holder in writing that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. on the Effective Date, the land will be transferred to the Tla'amin Nation and will become Tla'amin Lands or Other Tla'amin Lands, as the case may be; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where applicable, the land is subject to the interests set out in Part 1 of Appendix F-3.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation and entity designated under paragraph 17 will register, or cause to be registered, any lands transferred under paragraph 17 in the name of the Tla'amin Nation in accordance with paragraph 2 of the Land Title Chapter subject, where applicable, to the continuing interests set out in Part 1 of Appendix F-3 and any other encumbrances described in or permitted under the land transfer agreement between British Columbia and the Sliammon Indian Band under paragraph 17.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. For greater certainty:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. any lands transferred under subparagraphs 17.a to 17.c will form part of Tla'amin Lands on the Effective Date; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. any lands transferred under subparagraph 17.d will form part of Other Tla'amin Lands on the Effective Date.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. For the purposes of paragraphs 17 to 20, the Sliammon Indian Band or the Tla'amin Nation, as the case may be, will indemnify and save harmless Canada and British Columbia from any costs, damages, losses or liabilities that Canada or British Columbia may suffer or incur in connection with, or as a result of, any claims, demands, actions or proceedings relating to or arising out of any charge or encumbrance of any of the lands, the transfer of the lands to the Tla'amin Nation or the inclusion of the lands as Tla'amin Lands or Other Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Nothing in paragraphs 17 to 20 creates or implies any financial or other obligations or service responsibility on the part of Canada nor are they intended to have, or to be interpreted as having, the effect of establishing any of the lands transferred as an Indian Reserve or as "Lands reserved for the Indians" within the meaning of subsection 91 (24) of the Constitution Act, 1867.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ROADS TRANSFERRED TO BRITISH COLUMBIA ON THE EFFECTIVE DATE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. Before the Effective Date, British Columbia will survey:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. that portion of Plummer Creek Road, being a 30 metre corridor illustrated as "Road Transferred to British Columbia on the Effective Date" on Map 5, Part 2 of Appendix C-1, located on Former Tokenatch Indian Reserve No. 5; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. that portion of Southview Road, being a corridor illustrated as "Road Transferred to British Columbia on the Effective Date" on Map 1, Part 2 of Appendix C-1, located on Former Sliammon Indian Reserve No. 1.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation will transfer ownership of those portions of Plummer Creek Road and Southview Road referred to in paragraph 23, including the Subsurface Resources, to British Columbia whereupon they will be Provincial Crown Roads and, for greater certainty, will not be Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LUND HOTEL PARCELS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. On the Effective Date, the lands identified as the Lund Hotel Parcels will be Tla'amin Lands subject to the continuing interests set out in Part 3 of Appendix C-3 and the Tla'amin Nation providing to Canada and British Columbia on or before the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. certificates, in substantially the form set out in Documents 1A and 1B, Part 4 of Appendix C-3, certifying that on the date of the certificate the person named as the owner in fee simple is the owner of the estate in fee simple of the lands legally described in the certificate and consents to the inclusion of those lands in Tla'amin Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where applicable, written consent, in substantially the form set out in Document 2, Part 4 of Appendix C-3, signed by the holder of a charge or encumbrance stipulating that, on the date of the consent, the holder of the charge or encumbrance consents to the inclusion of the lands legally described in the document in Tla'amin Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. releases, in substantially the form set out in Documents 3A and 3B, Part 4 of Appendix C-3, signed by the person named as the owner in fee simple releasing Canada and British Columbia, as of the Effective Date, from any damages, losses, liabilities or costs that Canada or British Columbia may suffer or incur in connection with or as a result of any claims, demands, actions or proceedings relating to or arising out of the inclusion of the lands legally described in the release in Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Subject to the Tla'amin Nation meeting the conditions in paragraph 25, on the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. section 50 of the Land Act ceases to apply in respect of the Lund Hotel Parcels; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the interests, rights, privileges, titles and estates described in subsections 50 (1) (a), (b) and (c) of the Land Act that were excluded from the original disposition of Crown land vest in the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. The Tla'amin Nation will indemnify and save harmless Canada and British Columbia from any damages, losses, liabilities or costs, excluding fees and disbursements of solicitors and other professional advisors, that Canada or British Columbia may suffer or incur in connection with or as a result of any claims, demands, actions or proceedings relating to or arising out of the inclusion of the Lund Hotel Parcels in Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LANDS NEAR THE POWELL RIVER AIRPORT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. No development on DL 5127, Group 1, New Westminster District may affect the safe operation of the Powell River Airport and NAV CANADA facilities.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. Prior to authorizing any development on DL 5127, Group 1, New Westminster District, the Tla'amin Nation will discuss with representatives of the Powell River Airport and NAV CANADA the proposed development in order to identify and avoid any potential adverse impacts of the proposed development on the safe operation of the Powell River Airport and NAV CANADA facilities related to the Powell River Airport.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: AGRICULTURAL LAND RESERVE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. On the Effective Date the Tla'amin Lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. identified as "Former Agricultural Land Reserve" in Appendix E are excluded from the designation as an agricultural land reserve under the Agricultural Land Commission Act; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. identified as "Current Agricultural Land Reserve" in Appendix E retain the designation as an agricultural land reserve under the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. Any lands designated as an agricultural land reserve which are added to Tla'amin Lands in accordance with this Agreement will retain the designation as an agricultural land reserve under the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. The designation of areas of Tla'amin Lands as an agricultural land reserve may be removed by the Provincial Agricultural Land Commission in accordance with the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. Notwithstanding paragraph 118, the Agricultural Land Commission Act prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tla'amin Law under paragraph 116 in relation to Tla'amin Lands that retain the designation as an agricultural land reserve under subparagraph 30.b and paragraph 31.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. For Tla'amin Lands that retain the designation as an agricultural land reserve, the Provincial Agricultural Land Commission will explore with the Tla'amin Nation opportunities to include the Tla'amin Nation in the Provincial Agricultural Land Commission processes with respect to those Tla'amin Lands, including the delegation of decision-making under section 26 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. After the Effective Date, any part of Tla'amin Lands that is not designated as an agricultural land reserve will not be designated as an agricultural land reserve without the consent of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: SUBMERGED LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. Other than as provided in paragraphs 37 to 40:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Submerged Lands do not form part of Tla'amin Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. nothing in this Agreement affects British Columbia's ownership of Submerged Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. The Submerged Lands which are part of Former Sliammon Indian Reserves form part of Tla'amin Lands, including the lands beneath the following water bodies:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Okeover Creek;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. water bodies on Ahgykson (Harwood Island); and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. Kwehtums Kahkeeky (creek that runs into Grace Harbour).

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 38. For greater certainty, the following Submerged Lands are not part of Former Sliammon Indian Reserves:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. lands beneath Theodosia River and its tidal channels; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the Foreshore and lands beneath tidal waters.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 39. The Submerged Lands of Sliammon Creek within Former Sliammon Indian Reserve No. 1, excluding the Submerged Lands beneath Highway 101, form part of Tla'amin Lands. For greater certainty, the Submerged Lands that form part of Tla'amin Lands include Blocks C and D of District Lot 390.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 40. A parcel of Tla'amin Lands does not cease to be Tla'amin Lands where a fishway, Fish bypass channel or Fish spawning channel is constructed on that parcel as an Enhancement Initiative in accordance with paragraph 137 of the Fisheries Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 41. The Tla'amin Nation's ownership of Submerged Lands does not include:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. property rights in Fish;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the exclusive right to fish; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the right to allocate Fish.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 42. British Columbia will not authorize any use or disposition in relation to Sliammon Lake, Little Sliammon Lake or Submerged Lands within Tla'amin Lands without the consent of the Tla'amin Nation, which consent will not be unreasonably withheld. In deciding whether to grant or withhold its consent, the Tla'amin Nation may take into account that Sliammon Lake is the major source of water for Former Sliammon Indian Reserve No. 1.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 43. Paragraph 42 does not affect the riparian rights of the upland owners of Tla'amin Lands adjacent to Submerged Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 44. British Columbia will not authorize any use or disposition of the Foreshore around Ahgykson without the consent of the Tla'amin Nation, which consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 45. Paragraph 44 does not apply to temporary non-commercial recreational use or temporary non-commercial occupation of the Foreshore around Ahgykson.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ACCRETIONS TO TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 46. The Tla'amin Nation will own lawful accretions to Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 47. Where the Tla'amin Nation provides to Canada and British Columbia a certificate issued by the Surveyor General of British Columbia confirming that there has been lawful accretion to Tla'amin Lands, upon receipt of the certificate by Canada and British Columbia, the accreted land will become Tla'amin Lands and Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DELEGATION AGREEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 48. On the Effective Date, British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation will enter into an agreement in accordance with paragraph 46 of the Governance Chapter to provide the Tla'amin Nation with law-making authority in accordance with paragraph 49.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 49. The agreement under paragraph 48 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. identify the area extending through and beyond the Foreshore where the agreement applies;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provide the Tla'amin Nation with law-making authority in relation to the area in subparagraph 49.a; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. provide that Federal Law or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tla'amin Law made in accordance with the agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 50. Before concluding an agreement in accordance with paragraph 48, British Columbia will Consult with Canada regarding the proposed agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: INTERESTS ON TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 51. On the Effective Date, the title of the Tla'amin Nation to Tla'amin Lands is free and clear of all interests, except:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the following interests on Former Sliammon Indian Reserves which will be replaced on the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the certificates of possession and other interests referred to in Part 1 of Appendix F-1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. the Klahanie interests referred to in Part 2 of Appendix F-1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. the Southview interests referred to in Part 3 of Appendix F-1; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. the Public Utility distribution works and other interests referred to in Part 4 of Appendix F-1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the following interests on former provincial Crown land which will be replaced on the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the Public Utility distribution works referred to in Part 1 of Appendix F-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. the permits to occupy provincial Crown land, associated with Water Licences, referred to in Part 2 of Appendix F-2; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. the licences of occupation for pit toilet purposes, associated with the float home tenures, referred to in Part 3 of Appendix F-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the following interests on Tla'amin Lands that will continue in accordance with Provincial Law and with the terms and conditions of that interest existing on the Effective Date, modified where appropriate to reflect ownership of the lands by the Tla'amin Nation:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the licence of occupation issued to the Powell River Regional District relating to the sewer main and outfall under the Land Act and referred to in Part 1 of Appendix F-3;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. the Subsurface Tenure referred to in Part 2 of Appendix F-3;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. the Water Licences issued under the Water Act referred to in Part 3 of Appendix F-3; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. the guide outfitter certificates issued under the Wildlife Act referred to in Part 4 of Appendix F-3; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the following interests on Tla'amin Lands that will be created on the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. Tla'amin Nation upland owner consent to interference with the Tla'amin Nation's right of upland access issued to British Columbia and associated with the float home tenures referred to in Part 1 of Appendix F-4 and identified for illustrative purposes on the map set out in Part 2 of Appendix F-4;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. in relation to shellfish aquaculture tenures:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (1) licences of occupation to shellfish aquaculture tenures to occupy Tla'amin Lands for temporary storage purposes referred to in Part 3 of Appendix F-4;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (2) Tla'amin Nation upland owner consent to interference with the Tla'amin Nation's right of upland access issued to British Columbia and associated with the aquaculture shellfish tenures referred to in Part 4 of Appendix F-4;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. private road easements over Tla'amin Lands issued to the parties referred to in Parts 5 and 6 of Appendix F-4;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. the Public Utility distribution works referred to in Part 7 of Appendix F-4; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: v. licences of occupation for the forest research plots described in Part 8 of Appendix F-4 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 9 of Appendix F-4.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 52. On the Effective Date, every interest, other than those referred to in paragraphs 18, 25 and 51 that encumbered or applied to the lands that are Tla'amin Lands before the Effective Date, ceases to exist.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Replacement of Certificates of Possession and Other Interests

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 53. On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation will grant to each holder or joint holder of a certificate of possession or other interest identified in Part 1 of Appendix F-1 a fee simple estate or a joint fee simple estate that is free and clear of all interests except:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. any condition, proviso, restriction, including restrictions on alienation, exception or reservation that may be set out in Tla'amin Law; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. any applicable Public Utility or other interests referred to in Part 4 of Appendix F-1,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: and the certificate of possession or other interest held by that individual or individuals will cease to exist.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 54. For greater certainty, any Tla'amin Law made under paragraph 116 applies in respect of Tla'amin Lands including a fee simple estate granted under paragraph 53.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Replacement and Creation of Interests

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 55. On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Public Institution or a Tla'amin Corporation, as applicable and where they have the authority to grant the interest, will execute documents to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. grant to each person holding the interest referred to in Appendices F-1 and F-2 an interest replacing that person's interest set out in those Appendices; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. create new interests by granting to each person referred to in Appendix F-4 the interest set out in that Appendix.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 56. Documents referred to in paragraph 55 will be in the applicable form, if any, set out in Appendix F-5 and will include any modifications agreed upon in writing before the Effective Date by the applicable grantor and the interest holder.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 57. Documents referred to in paragraph 55 will be deemed to have legal effect on the Effective Date as though they had been prepared, executed and delivered by the grantor and by the applicable person named in Appendices F-1, F-2 and F-4 on that date.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 58. After the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation will deliver the applicable document:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. to each person referred to in paragraph 55; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. upon notice to the Tla'amin Nation by Canada or British Columbia before the Effective Date, to any other person identified as the person who should instead receive the replacement interest for any reason, including death, any form of transfer, error or operation of law and the applicable Appendix will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter to reflect the change.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 59. Where Canada or British Columbia notifies the Tla'amin Nation after the Effective Date that an interest granted under paragraph 55:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. is in the name of a person who was not actually entitled to the interest on the Effective Date; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. contains a clerical error or a wrong description of a material fact,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: the appropriate Parties will take reasonable measures to rectify the error.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 60. Any Right of Way of the nature described in section 218 of the Land Title Act that is granted by the Tla'amin Nation under this Agreement is legally binding and enforceable notwithstanding that Tla'amin Lands to which the Right of Way applies may not be subject to the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: SHELLFISH AQUACULTURE TENURES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 61. Subject to paragraph 62, the upland tenures associated with the shellfish aquaculture tenures set out in Appendix G will remain provincial Crown land.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 62. Where a shellfish aquaculture tenure set out in Appendix G ceases to exist, or is acquired by the Tla'amin Nation or a Tla'amin Corporation, British Columbia will transfer to the Tla'amin Nation the provincial Crown land that is covered by the associated upland tenure and, upon completion of the transfer, at the request of the Tla'amin Nation, the land will become Tla'amin Lands and Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TLA'AMIN SHELLFISH AQUACULTURE TENURES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 63. The shellfish aquaculture tenures issued to the Tla'amin Nation set out in Part 1 of Appendix H, or that may be acquired by the Tla'amin Nation, will continue as provincial tenures in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law and federal and provincial policy and procedures.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 64. The map reserves designated for use compatible with shellfish aquaculture listed in Part 2 of Appendix H will continue in accordance with Provincial Law, provincial policy and procedures.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 65. British Columbia will establish a reservation on the map reserves described in Part 2 of Appendix H for 25 years during which time the Tla'amin Nation may apply for shellfish aquaculture tenures and the diligent use provisions will not apply.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 66. British Columbia will establish a reservation on the map reserve described in Part 3 of Appendix H to enable the Tla'amin Nation to apply for authorization for the interest described in Part 3 of Appendix H.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TLA'AMIN SUBSURFACE RESOURCES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 67. The Tla'amin Nation owns Subsurface Resources on or under Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 68. The Tla'amin Nation's ownership of Subsurface Resources is subject to the subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 69. As owner of the Subsurface Resources, the Tla'amin Nation has exclusive authority to set, collect and receive fees, rents, royalties and charges other than taxes for the exploration, development, extraction and production of Subsurface Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 70. Paragraph 69 does not limit British Columbia from collecting and receiving fees or other payments for administering under Provincial Law the exploration, development, extraction and production of Subsurface Resources from Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 71. The Tla'amin Nation may act through Tla'amin Government in exercising its authority under paragraph 69.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 72. Nothing in this Agreement confers authority on the Tla'amin Nation to make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the development, production, use or application of nuclear energy and atomic energy;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the exploration, development, production, possession or use, for any purpose, of nuclear substances and prescribed substances; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the development, production, possession or use, for any purpose, of associated prescribed equipment and prescribed information.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 73. Nothing in this Agreement confers authority on the Tla'amin Nation to make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. spacing and target areas related to Petroleum and Natural Gas or conservation and allocation of Petroleum and Natural Gas among parties having interests in the same reservoir;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. occupational health and safety and labour standards, in respect of Subsurface Resources exploration, development, production, extraction and site reclamation; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. subsurface tenures or the Subsurface Resources which are subject to the subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 74. Notwithstanding paragraph 118, Federal or Provincial Law in respect of Subsurface Resources prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Tla'amin Law under paragraph 116.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Provincial Subsurface Resource Tenure

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 75. The subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3 will continue and the tenure and the Subsurface Resources under the tenure will be administered by British Columbia in accordance with Provincial Law and this Agreement as if the Subsurface Resources were vested in or reserved to British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 76. The subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3 is not subject to paragraph 2 of the Environmental Assessment and Environmental Protection Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 77. For the purposes of paragraph 75, British Columbia may grant any related extensions, renewals or replacements or issue any further related rights as the Subsurface Resources are developed.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 78. Notwithstanding paragraph 69, the Tla'amin Nation does not have the authority to establish fees, rents, royalties or other charges in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the exploration, development, extraction or production of Subsurface Resources under that tenure.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 79. British Columbia will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. ensure that any rents and royalties applicable to the subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3 and the Subsurface Resources under that tenure, and any interest earned on those rents and royalties, are paid to the Tla'amin Nation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. retain any fees or other payments for administering the subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3 and the Subsurface Resources under that tenure.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 80. British Columbia will notify the Tla'amin Nation before changing or eliminating any rents or royalties applicable to Subsurface Resources in British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 81. Tla'amin Lands will be treated as private lands under Provincial Law for the purposes of resolving any access issues or compensation rights associated with any proposed entrance, occupation or use of Tla'amin Lands by the holder of the subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 82. Any dispute under paragraph 81 may be resolved under Provincial Law respecting access and compensation disputes involving Subsurface Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Termination of Provincial Subsurface Resource Tenures

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 83. Where the subsurface tenure listed in Part 2 of Appendix F-3 is forfeited, cancelled or expires and is not restored under Provincial Law, Tla'amin Lands will no longer be subject to the subsurface tenure.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: INDEMNITIES FOR OMISSIONS AND ERRORS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 84. British Columbia will indemnify and save harmless the Tla'amin Nation from any damages, losses, liabilities or costs, excluding fees and disbursements of solicitors and other professional advisors, that the Tla'amin Nation may suffer or incur in connection with or as a result of any claims, demands, actions or proceedings relating to or arising out of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the omission from Appendix F of the name of a person who, on the day before the Effective Date, had an interest in Tla'amin Lands that had been granted by British Columbia; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the incorrect naming of a person in Appendix F as a person entitled to an interest, where another person was actually entitled, on the day before the Effective Date, to the interest in Tla'amin Lands that had been granted by British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ADDITIONS TO TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: General Additions of Lands

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 85. At any time after the Effective Date, at the Tla'amin Nation's request and with the agreement of Canada and British Columbia, the Tla'amin Nation may add parcels of land to Tla'amin Lands which are:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. within the Tla'amin Area;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. outside the boundaries of a municipality incorporated under the Local Government Act, or within municipal boundaries if the municipality consents; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. owned in fee simple by the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 86. Where the Tla'amin Nation wishes to add a parcel of land under paragraph 85 which is subject to a purchase agreement conditional only on the agreement of Canada and British Columbia to its addition to Tla'amin Lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the federal Minister will advise the Tla'amin Nation in a timely manner whether the Minister would agree to recommend to the Governor-in-Council the addition of that parcel, once acquired by the Tla'amin Nation, to Tla'amin Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the provincial Minister will advise the Tla'amin Nation in a timely manner whether the Minister would agree to recommend to the Lieutenant-Governor-in-Council the addition of that parcel, once acquired by the Tla'amin Nation, to Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 87. When making a decision under paragraph 85:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Canada will require the parcel of lands to be in areas free from overlap with another First Nation unless that First Nation consents; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Canada and British Columbia may take into account other matters that Canada or British Columbia consider relevant.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 88. Canada and British Columbia will notify the Tla'amin Nation once a decision has been made under paragraph 85 and, where Canada and British Columbia agree to the addition of the parcel of land to Tla'amin Lands, Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter upon the Tla'amin Nation's receipt of the notices.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Non-Crown Lands Surrounded by Tla'amin Lands

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 89. Where, at any time, the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Institution, a Tla'amin Corporation or a Tla'amin Citizen becomes the registered owner of the fee simple estate to a parcel of land set out in Map 1, Part 1 of Appendix I, the Tla'amin Nation may add the parcel to Tla'amin Lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. with the written consent of the owner and the registered holder of any financial charge or encumbrance on that parcel; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. upon notice to Canada and British Columbia identifying the parcel and attaching the written consents required under subparagraph 89.a.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 90. Upon receipt by Canada and British Columbia of a notice under subparagraph 89.b, the parcel of land will become Tla'amin Lands and Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Crown Lands Surrounded by Tla'amin Lands

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 91. Where, at any time:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. British Columbia determines that any parcel of provincial Crown land set out in Maps 2 and 3, Part 1 of Appendix I is not of use to British Columbia; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the parcel of provincial Crown land set out in Map 4, Part 1 of Appendix I ceases to be subject to the woodlot licence existing on the Effective Date,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: British Columbia will offer to sell the fee simple estate to the parcel of land to the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 92. Where the Tla'amin Nation wishes to purchase the parcel of land offered for sale under paragraph 91, British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on a purchase price that reflects the fair market value for the parcel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 93. Where the Tla'amin Nation purchases any parcel of land under paragraph 91, the Tla'amin Nation may add the parcel to Tla'amin Lands upon written notice to Canada and British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 94. Upon receipt by Canada and British Columbia of notice under paragraph 93, the parcel of land will become Tla'amin Lands and Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Future Acquisition Lands

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 95. On the Effective Date, British Columbia will for a period of ten years withdraw the parcels of provincial Crown land set out in Part 2 of Appendix I from disposition under Section 16 of the Land Act and establish for those lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a mineral reserve under the Mineral Tenures Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a coal land reserve under the Coal Act; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a no disposition notation under the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 96. Where, within the ten year period under paragraph 95, the Tla'amin Nation notifies British Columbia that it wishes to purchase the fee simple estate to any parcel of land under paragraph 95, British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on a purchase price that reflects the fair market value for the parcel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 97. Where the Tla'amin Nation purchases a parcel of land under paragraph 96, the Tla'amin Nation may add the parcel to Tla'amin Lands upon notice to Canada and British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 98. Upon receipt by Canada and British Columbia of notice under paragraph 97, the parcel will become Tla'amin Lands and Appendix C will be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Interests on Added Lands

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 99. Any parcel of land that is added to Tla'amin Lands under paragraphs 85 to 98 will be subject to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. where the parcel is not registered in the Land Title Office, any interest granted by British Columbia that is not discharged at the time of purchase, or any replacement or modification of that interest agreed to in writing by the Tla'amin Nation and the interest holder; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where the parcel is registered in the Land Title Office, any registered charge or registered encumbrance subject to their discharge under the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 100. The Tla'amin Nation will own the Subsurface Resources on lands that are added to Tla'amin Lands where:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the fee simple title includes ownership of the Subsurface Resources; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. British Columbia owns the Subsurface Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 101. For the purposes of subparagraph 100.b, unless otherwise agreed by British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation any Subsurface Resources tenures and the Subsurface Resources subject to those tenures will be administered by British Columbia in accordance with paragraphs 75 to 80.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Transaction Costs and Registration of Additions to Tla'amin Lands

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 102. Nothing in paragraphs 85 and 89 obligates Canada or British Columbia to pay any costs associated with the addition of lands to Tla'amin Lands, including costs for the purchase or transfer of the lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 103. For the purposes of paragraphs 93 and 97:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation will be responsible for all transaction costs that are normally the responsibility of a purchaser of provincial Crown land; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. British Columbia will provide the Tla'amin Nation with an instrument transferring the indefeasible title or, where applicable, the registered title to the parcel to the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 104. Where the Tla'amin Nation wishes to register a parcel of land added to Tla'amin Lands which is not at the time registered in the Land Title Office, the Tla'amin Nation and British Columbia will, as appropriate, file such plans, certificates, instruments and other documents in the Land Title Office as may be required under the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: EXTERIOR BOUNDARY SURVEYS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 105. No new survey will be required for a parcel of Tla'amin Lands where the Surveyor General of British Columbia determines that an Adequate Survey of the exterior boundary exists for that parcel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 106. Before or as soon as practicable after the Effective Date, in those cases where Adequate Surveys do not already exist, Adequate Surveys of exterior boundaries of Tla'amin Lands will be carried out by:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Canada in respect of Former Sliammon Indian Reserves; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. British Columbia in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. former provincial Crown land identified for illustrative purposes in Part 1 of Appendix C-2 and described in Part 2 of Appendix C-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. the Lund Hotel Parcels; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. lands described in Part 1 of Appendix C-4 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix C-4 as "Oyster Plant Upland Parcel",

heading: Commencement
paragraph: in accordance with instructions to be issued by the Surveyor General of British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 107. The priority and timing of exterior boundary surveys not completed by the Effective Date will be set out in a survey and registration protocol agreed to between British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation prior to the Effective Date having regard to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation's priorities;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. efficiency and economy, including the availability of British Columbia Land Surveyors; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the necessity to clarify the boundaries because of imminent public or private development on adjacent lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 108. Canada and British Columbia will, as agreed between them, pay the cost of surveys of the exterior boundaries of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: INTERIOR BOUNDARY SURVEYS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 109. Interior boundary surveys of parcels or interests within Tla'amin Lands will meet the requirements of the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: OTHER TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 110. On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation owns Other Tla'amin Lands in fee simple.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 111. The Tla'amin Nation does not own the Subsurface Resources on or under Other Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 112. The Tla'amin Nation's fee simple ownership of Other Tla'amin Lands is subject to the conditions, provisos, restrictions, exceptions and reservations set out in the Land Act, or any comparable limitation under Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: SITE REMEDIATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 113. The transfer of the Former Sliammon Indian Reserves to the Tla'amin Nation in accordance with this Agreement will not, in and of itself, result in British Columbia being liable in respect of any Contamination of such lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 114. To the best of British Columbia's knowledge, the provincial Crown land transferred to the Tla'amin Nation in accordance with this Agreement has not been used for a prescribed industrial or commercial purpose or any other purpose or activity prescribed under the Environmental Management Act, and British Columbia is not required to prepare or provide a site profile under the Environmental Management Act for those lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 115. Nothing in this Agreement precludes the Tla'amin Nation from recovering the costs incurred in the inspection or remediation of any Contaminated Sites on the lands referred to in paragraph 114 from British Columbia or any other person who may be determined to be a responsible person under the Environmental Management Act in respect of the Contamination of that site.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LAW-MAKING AUTHORITY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 116. The Tla'amin Nation may make laws with respect to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the use of Tla'amin Lands, including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. management; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. planning, zoning and development;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the creation, allocation, ownership and disposition of estates or interests in Tla'amin Lands, including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. fee simple estates or any lesser estate or interest;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. mortgages;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. leases, licences, permits, easements and Rights of Way, including Rights of Way and covenants similar to those in sections 218 and 219 of the Land Title Act; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. any conditions, provisos, restrictions, including restrictions on alienation, exceptions or reservations on such estates or interests;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the establishment and operation of a Tla'amin Nation land title or land registry system for Tla'amin Lands that are not registered in the Land Title Office; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the expropriation by the Tla'amin Nation of estates or interests in Tla'amin Lands for public purposes and public works other than:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. estates or interests granted or continued on the Effective Date or thereafter replaced under this Agreement, unless specifically provided for in this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. estates or interests expropriated or otherwise acquired by a Federal Expropriating Authority or a Provincial Expropriating Authority; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. any other interests upon which the Parties have agreed in this Agreement,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: where the Tla'amin Nation provides fair compensation to the owner of the estate or interest and the expropriation is for the smallest estate or interest necessary for the public purpose or public work.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 117. Notwithstanding subparagraph 116.d.i, the Tla'amin Nation may expropriate for public purposes and public works a fee simple estate or a lesser interest in a fee simple estate granted under paragraph 53 where the Tla'amin Nation provides fair compensation to the owner of the interest and the expropriation is for the smallest interest necessary for the public purpose or public work.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 118. Subject to paragraph 119 and paragraph 10 of the Land Title Chapter, Tla'amin Law under paragraph 116 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 119. Notwithstanding paragraph 118, Federal or Provincial Law in respect of the division of matrimonial real property prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Tla'amin Law in respect of the division of matrimonial real property made under subparagraph 116.b. For greater certainty, Tla'amin Law that may restrict the disposition of real property to a Tla'amin Citizen is not Tla'amin Law in respect of the division of matrimonial real property.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 120. For the purposes of subparagraph 116.b. the Tla'amin Nation may make laws with respect to estates or interests in Tla'amin Lands that are:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. not recognized under Federal or Provincial Law; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. recognized under Federal or Provincial Law provided that they are consistent with Federal or Provincial Law with respect to those estates or interests.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 121. For greater certainty, a Tla'amin Law under subparagraph 116.b.iv in respect of a fee simple estate granted under paragraph 53 is not inconsistent with common law principles.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LIMITS ON PROVINCIAL EXPROPRIATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 122. British Columbia acknowledges that it is of fundamental importance to maintain the size and integrity of Tla'amin Lands and, therefore, as a general principle interests in Tla'amin Lands will not be expropriated under Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 123. Where a Provincial Expropriating Authority has determined that it requires an estate or interest in Tla'amin Lands, the Provincial Expropriating Authority will make reasonable efforts to acquire the estate or interest through agreement with the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 124. Notwithstanding paragraph 122 and 123, and paragraph 2 of the Environmental Assessment and Environmental Protection Chapter, a Provincial Expropriating Authority may expropriate Tla'amin Lands in accordance with Appendix J-1 and Provincial Law and with the consent and by the order of the Lieutenant-Governor-in-Council.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 125. Notwithstanding paragraph 122, Subsurface Resources owned by the Tla'amin Nation on Tla'amin Lands may not be expropriated by Local Government.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 126. An expropriation of Tla'amin Lands by a Provincial Expropriating Authority will be the most limited estate or interest in Tla'amin Lands necessary and will be expropriated for the shortest time possible.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LIMITS ON FEDERAL EXPROPRIATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 127. Canada acknowledges that it is of fundamental importance to maintain the size and integrity of Tla'amin Lands and, therefore, as a general principle interests in Tla'amin Lands will not be expropriated under Federal Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 128. Notwithstanding paragraph 127, any interest in Tla'amin Lands may be expropriated by a Federal Expropriating Authority in accordance with Appendix J-2 and Federal Law and with the consent and by the order of the Governor-in-Council.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 129. Nothing in this Agreement affects or limits the application of the Emergencies Act to Tla'amin Lands and that Act will continue to apply on Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 4 - LAND TITLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: FEDERAL TITLE REGISTRATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Federal land title and land registry laws, other than laws with respect to the survey and recording of interests or estates that are owned by Canada and are in Tla'amin Lands, do not apply to any parcel of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: REGISTRATION OF INDEFEASIBLE TITLE AND INTERESTS ON EFFECTIVE DATE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. On the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. an indefeasible title in the name of the Tla'amin Nation to those parcels of Tla'amin Lands identified as:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. Former Sliammon Indian Reserves;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. Blocks A and B of District Lot 390, Group 1, New Westminster District, shown on Plan 7TU842 recorded in the British Columbia Crown Land Registry;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. Sliammon Road being firstly, that portion of a road Right of Way shown on Plan RD2566 CLSR lying immediately south of Lund Road (Highway 101) as shown on Plan 51177 CLSR, and secondly, a road Right of Way shown outlined in green on Plan 51177 CLSR, lying immediately south of Lund Road as shown on Plan 51177 CLSR; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. the Old Lund Highway being a strip of land 66 feet wide with the centreline shown on Plan RD2208 CLSR, lying immediately north of Lund Road (Highway 101) as shown on Plan 52926 CLSR;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. an indefeasible title in the name of the Tla'amin Nation to those parcels of Tla'amin Lands described in:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. Map 4a, Part 2 of Appendix C-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. Map 8, Part 2 of Appendix C-2;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. Map 10, Part 2 of Appendix C-2; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. Part 1 of Appendix C-4 and identified for illustrative purposes in Part 2 of Appendix C-4 as "Oyster Plant Upland Parcel";

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. an indefeasible title to the Lund Hotel Parcels as follows:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. in the name of "593035 B.C. Ltd." to Lot 2, District Lot 1612, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 17853, except part subdivided by Plan LMP26444 and Lot 4, District Lot 1612, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 11021; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. in the name of "Sliammon Development Corporation Inc. No. 491626" to Block 3, District Lot 1612, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 10681;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. an indefeasible title in the name of the Tla'amin Nation to Other Tla'amin Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. the interests referred to in Part 3 of Appendix C-3 in accordance with paragraph 25 of the Lands Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. the interests referred to in Part 1 of Appendix F-1 in accordance with paragraph 51.a.i of the Lands Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. the interests referred to in Parts 2 and 3 of Appendix F-1 in accordance with paragraph 55 of the Lands Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. the interests referred to in Part 1 of Appendix F-2 in accordance with paragraph 55 of the Lands Chapter, unless that person has agreed in writing that the interest does not need to be granted;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. any other interests in Tla'amin Lands already registered in the Land Title Office; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: j. any other interests agreed to by the Parties,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: will be registered or will remain registered in the Land Title Office in accordance with this Agreement and the requirements of the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. On registration of the indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands referred to in subparagraphs 2.a and 2.b, the Registrar will make a notation on the indefeasible title that the parcel is Tla'amin Lands and may be subject to conditions, provisos, restrictions, exceptions and reservations, in favour of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. On the Effective Date, subject to the Tla'amin Nation meeting the conditions under paragraph 25 of the Lands Chapter, the Registrar will make a notation on the indefeasible title of the parcels referred to in subparagraph 2.c that the parcels are Tla'amin Lands and are subject to the conditions, provisos, restrictions, exceptions and reservations set out in paragraph 26 of the Lands Chapter, in favour of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: REGISTRATION OF INDEFEASIBLE TITLE AND INTERESTS AFTER EFFECTIVE DATE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. After the Effective Date:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. an indefeasible title in the name of the Tla'amin Nation to those parcels of Tla'amin Lands described in Appendix C-2, except those parcels registered on the Effective Date under subparagraph 2.b; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the interests of the Tla'amin Nation in those Tla'amin Lands that the Tla'amin Nation determines need to be registered,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: as set out in and determined by the survey and registration protocol described in paragraph 107 of the Lands Chapter, will be registered in the Land Title Office in accordance with this Agreement and the requirements of the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LAND TITLE FEES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Notwithstanding any provision contained in the Land Title Act, or any other Provincial Law, no land title fees, including the provision of a State of Title Certificate and any fees associated with the issuance of survey instructions, parcel designation, plan confirmation, and final survey plan examination and recording, are payable by any Party or the holder of an interest referred to in paragraph 2 on or after the Effective Date in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the first registration of indefeasible title to any portion of land described in subparagraphs 1.a, 1.b and 1.d of the Lands Chapter in the name of the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the designation of the Lund Hotel Parcels as Tla'amin Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the first registration of indefeasible title to Other Tla'amin Lands in the name of the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. a reference or subdivision plan accompanying an application, under subparagraph 6.a, for registration under Sections 25 or 26 of Schedule 1 of the Land Title Act;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. the first registration of any interests referred to in paragraph 51 of the Lands Chapter, including any related plans, but excluding any interests in favour of a Public Utility;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. the first registration of indefeasible title to, or first registration of the transfer of, any lands which are transferred by British Columbia to the Tla'amin Nation under section 19 of Appendix J-1 and are added to Tla'amin Lands under section 20;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. the first registration of indefeasible title to, or first registration of the transfer of any lands which are transferred by Canada to the Tla'amin Nation under section 10 of Appendix J-2 and are added to Tla'amin Lands under section 22;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. the first registration of indefeasible title to, or first registration of the transfer of, any lands which are transferred by a Provincial Expropriating Authority to the Tla'amin Nation under section 21 of Appendix J-1 and are added to Tla'amin Lands under section 23;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the first registration of indefeasible title to, or first registration of the transfer of, any lands which are transferred by a Federal Expropriating Authority to the Tla'amin Nation under section 23 of Appendix J-2 and are added to Tla'amin Lands under section 25;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: j. the first registration of indefeasible title to, or first registration of the transfer of, any lands which are transferred by British Columbia to the Tla'amin Nation under subparagraph 16.a of the Roads and Rights of Way Chapter and are added to Tla'amin Lands under subparagraph 16.b of that Chapter;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: k. the first registration of indefeasible title to, or first registration of the transfer of, lands for which the Tla'amin Nation has received approval under paragraph 88 or provided notice under paragraphs 90, 94 or 98 of the Lands Chapter to add those lands to Tla'amin Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: l. the transfer of a parcel of Tla'amin Lands that has been expropriated by a Provincial Expropriation Authority or Federal Expropriation Authority; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: m. the filing of a certificate under Section 29 of Schedule 1 of the Land Title Act in respect of the addition or removal of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: APPLICATION OF LAND TITLE SYSTEM

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. The Land Title Act applies to all parcels of Tla'amin Lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. registered on the Effective Date under this Agreement; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. for which the Tla'amin Nation applies for registration under that Act in accordance with this Agreement, from the time of application and until the application has been withdrawn or rejected, or the indefeasible title is cancelled.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The Land Title Act does not apply to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands for which:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. no application has been made under that Act in accordance with this Agreement for the registration of an indefeasible title;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. an application has been made under that Act in accordance with this Agreement for the registration of an indefeasible title and that application has been withdrawn or rejected; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the indefeasible title under that Act has been cancelled in accordance with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. No title adverse to, or in derogation of, the title of the registered owner of a parcel of Tla'amin Lands under the Land Title Act will be acquired by length of possession and, for greater certainty, subsection 23 (4) of the Land Title Act does not apply in respect of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. Notwithstanding paragraph 118 of the Lands Chapter, where the Land Title Act applies to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands, that Act prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Tla'amin Law under paragraph 116 of the Lands Chapter in respect of that parcel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. When the Land Title Act applies to Tla'amin Lands:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the jurisdiction of the Tla'amin Nation is not diminished, except to the extent set out in this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the powers, rights, privileges, capacities, duties and obligations of the Tla'amin Nation under this Agreement in respect of Tla'amin Lands under that Act are analogous to those of the Crown in relation to Crown land or a Local Government in relation to Local Government lands under that Act; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the status and treatment of Tla'amin Lands under that Act are analogous to that of municipal lands or rural area, as the case may be, under that Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: APPLICATION FOR REGISTRATION OF INDEFEASIBLE TITLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. The Tla'amin Nation, and no other person, may apply under the Land Title Act for the registration of an indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands for which no indefeasible title is registered at the time of application, and such application may be made in the name of the Tla'amin Nation or on behalf of another person.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. When applying for the registration of an indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands under paragraph 12 the Tla'amin Nation will provide to the Registrar:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a plan of the parcel that has been prepared by a Land Surveyor and signed by the Surveyor General of British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a Tla'amin Nation Certificate certifying the person named as the owner of the fee simple estate is the owner of the fee simple estate of the parcel as of the date of the certificate and certifying that the certificate sets out all:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. subsisting conditions, provisos, restrictions, including restrictions on alienation, exceptions and reservations, including royalties, contained in the original or any other conveyance or disposition from the Tla'amin Nation that are in favour of the Tla'amin Nation, or that are in favour of another person;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. interests or estates; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. charges, including charges in respect of debts owed to the Tla'amin Nation,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: to which the fee simple estate of the parcel is subject; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. registrable instruments necessary to register all of the items referred to in subparagraph 13.b.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. A Tla'amin Nation Certificate expires where:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. within seven days of the date of the Tla'amin Nation Certificate the Tla'amin Nation has not applied for registration of an indefeasible title to the parcel referred to in the Tla'amin Nation Certificate, unless otherwise provided for under the Land Title Act; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. an application under paragraph 12 has been made but that application has been withdrawn or rejected under the Land Title Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. Where the Tla'amin Nation makes an application for the registration of indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands under paragraph 12 and the Registrar is satisfied that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a good safe holding and marketable title in fee simple for the parcel has been established by the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the boundaries of the parcel are sufficiently defined by the plan provided by the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. all of the estates, interests and other charges set out in the Tla'amin Nation Certificate are registrable under the Land Title Act; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the Tla'amin Nation Certificate complies with the Land Title Act,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: then the Registrar will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. register the indefeasible title to the parcel in the name of the person named in the Tla'amin Nation Certificate;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. make a note on the indefeasible title that the parcel is Tla'amin Lands and may be subject to conditions, provisos, restrictions, exceptions and reservations in favour of the Tla'amin Nation or another person; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. register as charges the estates and interests set out in subparagraph 13.b.ii and the other charges set out in subparagraph 13.b.iii.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. The Registrar is entitled to rely on, and is not required to make any inquiries with respect to, the matters certified in the Tla'amin Nation Certificate.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. A person deprived of an estate, interest, condition, proviso, restriction, exception or reservation, in or to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands as a result of the reliance by the Registrar on the Tla'amin Nation Certificate, and the issuance by the Registrar of an indefeasible title based on the Tla'amin Nation Certificate, will have no recourse, at law or in equity, against the Registrar, the assurance fund under the Land Title Act, British Columbia or Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Upon registration under paragraphs 2 and 5 the Parties, where necessary, will amend Appendix C and, where applicable, Appendix L in accordance with paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter, to reflect any adjustments to the boundaries of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. Subject to this Agreement, to the extent that the following instruments are applicable to a parcel of land registered under paragraphs 2 and 5, the Parties will present the instruments for registration in the following order of priority:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. any Right of Way in favour of the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. any distribution Rights of Way in favour of British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. any distribution Rights of Way in favour of TELUS Communications Inc.;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. any Rights of Way in favour of other Public Utilities; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. any other instruments.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Upon the request of the Parties and with the appointee's agreement, each holder of an interest referred to in paragraph 19 may appoint the Tla'amin Nation, Canada or British Columbia, as applicable, as its agent for the purpose of making such changes to the instruments, whether executed or not, as may be necessary in order to ensure that the instruments are in registrable form.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CANCELLATION OF INDEFEASIBLE TITLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. The Tla'amin Nation, and no other person, may apply under the Land Title Act in accordance with this Chapter for cancellation of the registration of an indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. When applying for the cancellation of the registration of an indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands, the Tla'amin Nation will provide to the Registrar an application for cancellation of registration and will deliver to the Registrar any duplicate indefeasible title that may have been issued with respect to that parcel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. Upon receiving an application from the Tla'amin Nation under paragraphs 21 and 22, the Registrar will cancel the registration of the indefeasible title where:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the registered owner of the fee simple estate to the parcel is the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Corporation or a Tla'amin Public Institution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provides written consent; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the indefeasible title to the parcel is free and clear of all charges, except those in favour of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: SUBSEQUENT REGISTRATION OF CANCELLED INDEFEASIBLE TITLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. Where the indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands has been cancelled by the Registrar under paragraph 23, the Tla'amin Nation, and no other person, may subsequently apply under the Land Title Act for the registration of an indefeasible title to that parcel of Tla'amin Lands and such application may be made in the name of the Tla'amin Nation or on behalf of another person.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. Paragraphs 13 to 17 apply when the Tla'amin Nation applies for the registration of indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands under paragraph 24.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Where the Tla'amin Nation makes an application for the registration of indefeasible title to a parcel of Tla'amin Lands under paragraph 24, then, effective from the time of application and until the application has been withdrawn or rejected, or the indefeasible title for that parcel is cancelled, the Land Title Act applies to the parcel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 5 - ACCESS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Except as modified by this Agreement, the Tla'amin Nation as owner of Tla'amin Lands has the same rights and obligations in respect of public access to Tla'amin Lands as other owners of estates in fee simple have in respect of public access to their land.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. Except as modified by paragraphs 30 and 31, the Tla'amin Nation's liability for public access to Tla'amin Public Lands is comparable to the liability of the provincial Crown for public access to unoccupied provincial Crown land.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DESIGNATIONS OF TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. Ahgykson is designated as Tla'amin Private Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. The Tla'amin Nation may designate portions of Tla'amin Lands as Tla'amin Private Lands where the Tla'amin Nation authorizes a use or disposition of those portions that is incompatible with public access.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Before making a designation under paragraph 4, or changing the boundaries of Tla'amin Private Lands, the Tla'amin Nation will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. provide reasonable notice to Canada, British Columbia and the public of the proposed designation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. consider views advanced by Canada, British Columbia or the public in respect of the proposed designation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Where the designation of Tla'amin Lands as Tla'amin Private Lands has or will have the effect of preventing public access to an area or location to which there is a public right of access under Federal or Provincial Law, such as navigable waters or Provincial Crown Roads, the Tla'amin Nation will provide reasonable alternative means of public access to that area or location.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. For greater certainty, paragraph 6 will not apply where British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation agree that a reasonable alternative means of public access across provincial Crown land already exists.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PUBLIC ACCESS ON TLA'AMIN PUBLIC LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The Tla'amin Nation will allow reasonable public access on Tla'amin Public Lands for temporary recreational and non-commercial purposes, including reasonable access for the public to hunt and fish on Tla'amin Public Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. Public access under paragraph 8 will be in accordance with Tla'amin Law respecting public access to Tla'amin Public Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. Public access to Tla'amin Public Lands does not include:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the harvesting or extraction of resources owned by the Tla'amin Nation unless authorized by the Tla'amin Nation or as set out in this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. causing mischief or nuisance;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. causing damage to Tla'amin Public Lands or resources owned by the Tla'amin Nation; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. interfering with other uses authorized by the Tla'amin Nation or interfering with the ability of the Tla'amin Nation to authorize uses or dispose of Tla'amin Public Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. Any hunting or fishing on Tla'amin Public Lands by the public will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TLA'AMIN PUBLIC ACCESS PERMITS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. For the purpose of monitoring and regulating public access under paragraph 8, the Tla'amin Nation may require persons other than Tla'amin Citizens to obtain a permit or licence or to sign a waiver.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. The Tla'amin Nation will make any permits, licences or waivers which may be required under paragraph 12 reasonably available at a reasonable fee taking into account the administrative and other costs of monitoring and regulating public access.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NOTICE OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF PUBLIC ACCESS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. The Tla'amin Nation will take reasonable measures to notify the public of the terms and conditions respecting public access on Tla'amin Public Lands, including any requirement under paragraph 12.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. The Tla'amin Nation will notify Canada and British Columbia of any proposed Tla'amin Law that would significantly affect public access on Tla'amin Public Lands. Upon request, the Tla'amin Nation will discuss the proposed law with Canada or British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PUBLIC RIGHT OF NAVIGATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Nothing in this Agreement affects the public right of navigation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LAW-MAKING AUTHORITY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. The Tla'amin Nation may make laws regulating public access on Tla'amin Lands for:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the prevention of harvesting or extracting of resources owned by the Tla'amin Nation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the protection of Heritage Sites.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Tla'amin Law under paragraph 17 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. The Tla'amin Nation may make laws regulating public access on Tla'amin Lands for:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the purposes of public safety;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the prevention of nuisance or damage, including forest fire prevention; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the protection of sensitive habitat.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Tla'amin Law under paragraph 19.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ACCESS TO TENURES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. The Tla'amin Nation will allow reasonable access at no cost to any tenure located on or beneath Tla'amin Lands, consistent with the terms and conditions of those tenures.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Where no other reasonable access exists across Crown land, the Tla'amin Nation will allow reasonable access at no cost across Tla'amin Lands to any tenure located on or beneath lands adjacent or in close proximity to Tla'amin Lands, consistent with the terms and conditions of those tenures.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. For greater certainty, nothing in paragraph 21 or 22 obligates the Tla'amin Nation to pay any costs associated with access to a tenure referred to in those paragraphs.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ACCESS TO ESTATES IN FEE SIMPLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. The Tla'amin Nation will allow reasonable access to the fee simple estates listed in Part 6 of Appendix F-4 in accordance with subparagraph 51.d.iii of the Lands Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. Where no other reasonable access exists across Crown land, the Tla'amin Nation will allow reasonable access at no cost across Tla'amin Lands to any fee simple estate adjacent or in close proximity to Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. For greater certainty, nothing in paragraph 24 or 25 obligates the Tla'amin Nation to pay any costs associated with access to a fee simple estate referred to in those paragraphs.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: SUNSHINE COAST TRAIL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. The Tla'amin Nation will allow reasonable public access to and use of those portions of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands for temporary recreational purposes subject to the conditions set out in paragraph 10.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. The Tla'amin Nation is not responsible for the management or maintenance of those portions of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands or any other portion of the Sunshine Coast Trail.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. On the Effective Date, the Tla'amin Nation and the Powell River Parks and Wilderness Society will enter into an agreement in substantially the form set out in Part 2 of Appendix K relating to the management and maintenance of the Sunshine Coast Trail.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. For the purposes of paragraph 27, the Tla'amin Nation has no duty of care to an individual in respect of risks willingly assumed by that individual other than a duty not to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. create a danger with intent to do harm to the individual or damage to the individual's property; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. act with reckless disregard to the safety of the individual or the integrity of the individual's property.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. An individual using the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands is deemed to have willingly assumed all risks.
