The Tla'amin Nation is subject only to the duty of care set out in paragraph 30 where the Tla'amin Nation receives no payment or other consideration for the use or activity, other than a payment or other consideration from a government, government agency or a non-profit recreational club or association.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CROWN ACCESS TO TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. Agents, employees, contractors and other representatives of Canada, British Columbia or Public Utilities, and members of the Canadian Armed Forces and peace officers, will have access to Tla'amin Lands, at no cost, in order to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. enforce laws;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. carry out duties under Federal and Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. carry out inspections;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. respond to emergencies and natural disasters;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. deliver programs and services; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. carry out other specified purposes as set out in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. Any access under paragraph 32 will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law, including the payment of compensation for any damage to Tla'amin Lands where required by Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. If at any time a Railway runs through or adjacent to Tla'amin Lands, paragraph 32 shall be read to also apply to agents, employees, contractors and other representatives of Railways.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. The Department of National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces will have access to Tla'amin Lands for military training with the agreement of the Tla'amin Nation. Failing agreement on conditions for the exercise of that access, the Minister of National Defence may refer the dispute for resolution under the Dispute Resolution Chapter but the Department of National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces may not exercise that access until the dispute has been resolved.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. Nothing in this Agreement limits the authority of the Minister of National Defence under section 257 of the National Defence Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. This Agreement does not affect the ability of individuals acting in an official capacity pursuant to lawful authority to have access to Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 38. Unless otherwise agreed, Canada or British Columbia, as the case may be, will provide reasonable notice of entry onto Tla'amin Lands under paragraph 32 to the Tla'amin Nation:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. before the entry, if it is practicable to do so; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. as soon as practicable after the entry.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 39. The requirement to provide reasonable notice under paragraph 38 does not apply to peace officers, investigators, or federal or provincial law enforcement officers carrying out duties under Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TLA'AMIN ACCESS OFF TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 40. Agents, employees, contractors and other representatives of the Tla'amin Nation may have access off Tla'amin Lands, at no cost, in order to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. enforce laws;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. carry out inspections;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. respond to emergencies and natural disasters;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. deliver programs and services; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. carry out other specified purposes as set out in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 41. Any access under paragraph 40 will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law, including the payment of compensation for any damage where required by Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 42. Unless otherwise agreed, the Tla'amin Nation will provide reasonable notice of entry onto Crown land under paragraph 40 to Canada or British Columbia, as the case may be:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. before the entry if it is practicable to do so; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. as soon as practicable after the entry.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 43. Tla'amin Citizens will have reasonable access to the Tla'amin Fishing Area, Wildlife and Migratory Birds Harvest Area and the Tla'amin Plant Gathering Area to allow for the exercise of the Tla'amin Nation's rights set out in this Agreement, subject to Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 44. Where an authorized use or disposition of provincial Crown land would deny the Tla'amin Nation reasonable access to Tla'amin Lands, British Columbia will allow reasonable access across provincial Crown land.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 6 - ROADS AND RIGHTS OF WAY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LAW-MAKING AUTHORITY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. The Tla'amin Nation may make laws in respect of traffic, transportation, parking and highways on Tla'amin Lands to the same extent as municipal governments in British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Tla'amin Law under paragraph 1.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENTRY ON TLA'AMIN LANDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. In addition to the provisions of the Access Chapter, British Columbia, a Public Utility or a Local Government and their agents, employees, contractors and other representatives may have access to Tla'amin Lands, including Tla'amin Roads, at no cost, for the purpose of undertaking works, including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. constructing drainage works;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. maintaining slope stability;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. removing dangerous trees or other hazards;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. carrying out vegetation management;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. carrying out normal repairs; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. carrying out emergency repairs,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: where this is necessary for constructing, operating, maintaining, repairing, replacing, removing or protecting Provincial Crown Roads, Rights of Way, municipal roads or works located on Provincial Crown Roads, Rights of Way or municipal roads or works that are on or adjacent to Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: WORK PLANS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. Before commencing any work referred to in paragraph 3, British Columbia, a Public Utility or a Local Government will notify and, at the Tla'amin Nation's request, deliver to the Tla'amin Nation a written work plan describing the effect and extent of the proposed work on Tla'amin Lands. The Tla'amin Nation will, within 30 days of receipt of the work plan, notify British Columbia, the Public Utility or the Local Government, as the case may be, as to whether or not it approves the work plan, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Where the Tla'amin Nation does not approve a work plan prepared by British Columbia under paragraph 4, the dispute will be finally determined by arbitration under the Dispute Resolution Chapter without having to proceed through Stages One and Two.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: UNDERTAKING OF WORKS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. In undertaking works referred to in paragraph 3, British Columbia, a Public Utility or a Local Government, as the case may be, will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. minimize the damage to, and time spent on, Tla'amin Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. pay compensation to the Tla'amin Nation for any interference with, or damage to, Tla'amin Lands resulting from the works.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. Where British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation do not agree on compensation under subparagraph 6.b with respect to the works undertaken by British Columbia, the dispute will be finally determined by arbitration under the Dispute Resolution Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. Paragraph 6.b is subject to the terms of any grant issued by the Tla'amin Nation or any agreement between the Tla'amin Nation and the person undertaking works referred to in paragraph 3.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: EMERGENCY WORKS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, British Columbia, a Public Utility or a Local Government, as the case may be, may undertake works and take steps on Tla'amin Lands that are urgently required in order to protect works constructed on Provincial Crown Roads, Rights of Way or municipal roads to protect persons or vehicles using Provincial Crown Roads, Rights of Way or municipal roads.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. British Columbia, a Public Utility or a Local Government, as the case may be, will notify the Tla'amin Nation that it has undertaken works on Tla'amin Lands under paragraph 9.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PROVINCIAL CROWN ROADS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. Provincial Crown Roads and lands set aside for use as a Provincial Crown Road identified in Appendix L are not part of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. British Columbia is responsible for the maintenance and repair of Provincial Crown Roads.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. British Columbia will Consult with the Tla'amin Nation regarding new uses for or major road construction of Provincial Crown Roads on or adjacent to Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: REALIGNMENT OF PROVINCIAL CROWN ROADS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. Where British Columbia acquires by agreement or expropriates an estate or interest in a parcel of Tla'amin Lands for the purpose of realigning all or a portion of a Provincial Crown Road:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. at the request of the Tla'amin Nation, British Columbia will transfer to the Tla'amin Nation that portion of the Provincial Crown Road on or adjacent to Tla'amin Lands that is no longer required for road, highway or Public Utility purposes and that land will become Tla'amin Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the estate or interest transferred to or expropriated by British Columbia for the purpose of such realignment will be the same as the estate or interest held by British Columbia in the pre-existing Provincial Crown Road; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. upon completion of any transfers or expropriation under this paragraph, Appendices C and L will, where appropriate, be amended in accordance with the process set out in paragraph 9 of the Amendment Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. Where the Tla'amin Nation does not request a transfer under subparagraph 14.a:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. British Columbia will not transfer its interest in the pre-existing Provincial Crown Road to the Tla'amin Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the Tla'amin Nation will transfer any Tla'amin Lands between the pre-existing Provincial Crown Road and the new Provincial Crown Road to British Columbia; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. British Columbia will compensate the Tla'amin Nation for the value of the land retained by and transferred to British Columbia under subparagraphs 15.a and 15.b.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CLOSURE OF PROVINCIAL CROWN ROADS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Where a Provincial Crown Road adjacent to Tla'amin Lands is closed and is no longer required for road, highway or Public Utility purposes:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. British Columbia will provide the Tla'amin Nation with a right of first refusal to acquire, on mutually acceptable terms, that portion of the land adjacent to Tla'amin Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. where the Tla'amin Nation acquires the land under subparagraph 16.a, it may request the addition of the land to Tla'amin Lands under paragraph 85 of the Lands Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TLA'AMIN ROADS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. Tla'amin Roads are part of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. The Tla'amin Nation is responsible for the maintenance and repair of Tla'amin Roads.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. Tla'amin Roads are open to the public unless designated otherwise by the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Subject to this Agreement, the Tla'amin Nation may temporarily or permanently close Tla'amin Roads.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. Before the Tla'amin Nation permanently closes a Tla'amin Road, the Tla'amin Nation will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. provide public notice and an opportunity for affected persons to make representations to the Tla'amin Nation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. notify Public Utilities whose facilities or works may be affected.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PUBLIC UTILITIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. The Tla'amin Nation will issue interests to the Public Utilities identified in Part 4 of Appendix F-1, Part 1 of Appendix F-2 and Part 7 of Appendix F-4 as provided for under paragraph 55 of the Lands Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. With the prior written approval of the Tla'amin Nation, a Public Utility may extend or locate and install new works on Tla'amin Lands on substantially the same terms and conditions as the applicable form of document in Appendix F-5 where it is necessary to meet demand for service on or off Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. The Tla'amin Nation will not unreasonably withhold approval for works referred to in paragraph 23.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. Nothing in paragraph 23 requires a Public Utility to obtain the approval of the Tla'amin Nation for usual service extensions or connections to Public Utility works or to deliver and manage services to customers of a Public Utility.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Tla'amin Law will not apply to the regulation of the business of a Public Utility or the planning, development, construction, repair, maintenance, operation or decommissioning of a Public Utility's authorized works.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. Without limiting the generality of paragraph 26, Tla'amin Law and the Tla'amin Nation's use or occupation of Tla'amin Lands will not impair or frustrate:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a Public Utility's authorized use or occupation of its interest issued under this Agreement; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a Public Utility's authorized use or occupation of Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. An interest of a Public Utility established after the Effective Date on or adjacent to Tla'amin Lands will be subject to this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ACCESS AND SAFETY REGULATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. Nothing in this Agreement limits the authority of British Columbia to regulate all matters in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the location and design of intersecting roads giving access to or from Provincial Crown Roads, including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. regulating or requiring signs, signals or other traffic control devices;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. regulating and requiring merging lanes, on ramps and off ramps; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. requiring contributions to the cost of the matters referred to in subparagraphs 29.a.i and 29.a.ii; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the height and location of structures on Tla'amin Lands adjacent to Provincial Crown Roads to the extent reasonably required to protect the safety of the users of the Provincial Crown Road or the functional capacity of the Provincial Crown Road.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. British Columbia will provide the Tla'amin Nation with any licence, permit or approval required under Provincial Law to join or intersect a Provincial Crown Road with a Tla'amin Road where:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the application for the required licence, permit or approval complies with Provincial Law, including the payment of any prescribed fees; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the joining or intersecting Tla'amin Road complies with standards established under Provincial Law for equivalent Provincial Crown Roads.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. Where the Tla'amin Nation and British Columbia fail to agree on the location of a joining or intersecting Tla'amin Road, the Tla'amin Nation or British Columbia may refer the dispute for resolution under the Dispute Resolution Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. The Tla'amin Nation will Consult with British Columbia on land use decisions relating to the development of Tla'amin Lands adjacent to Provincial Crown Roads.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CONSULTATION REGARDING TRAFFIC REGULATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. Upon the Tla'amin Nation's request, British Columbia will Consult with the Tla'amin Nation with respect to existing regulation of traffic and transportation on a Provincial Crown Road that is adjacent to a settled area on Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 7 - WATER

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Storage, diversion, extraction or use of water and Groundwater will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. The Tla'amin Nation may only sell water in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law that permit the sale of water.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. This Agreement does not alter Federal or Provincial Law in respect of proprietary interests in water.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. Notwithstanding paragraph 1, the Water Utility Act does not apply to the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Public Institution or a Tla'amin Corporation for the provision of services on Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: WATER RESERVATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. On the Effective Date, British Columbia will establish a water reservation under the Water Act in favour of the Tla'amin Nation of 11,225 cubic decametres of water per year from Streams set out in Schedule 1 for all purposes under the Water Act including domestic, agricultural and industrial uses, but excluding those purposes set out in paragraphs 25 to 27.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Any water reservation for the Tla'amin Nation established under paragraph 5 will have priority over all Water Licences other than:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Water Licences for the Sliammon Creek watershed issued:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. before June 6, 2003;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. pursuant to an application made before June 6, 2003; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. pursuant to water reservations established before June 6, 2003; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Water Licences other than for the Sliammon Creek watershed issued:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. before February 27, 2008;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. pursuant to an application made before February 27, 2008; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. pursuant to water reservations established before February 27, 2008.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: WATER LICENCES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. The Tla'amin Nation or, with the consent of the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Public Institution, Tla'amin Corporation or Tla'amin Citizen may apply to British Columbia for Water Licences for volumes of flow to be applied against the Tla'amin Nation's water reservation under paragraph 5.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The total volume of flow under the Water Licences to be applied against the Tla'amin Nation's water reservation under paragraph 5 may not exceed the monthly percentage of the Available Flow of each Stream listed in Schedule 1.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. Where the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Public Institution, Tla'amin Corporation or Tla'amin Citizen applies to British Columbia for a water licence under paragraph 7, British Columbia will approve the application and issue a Water Licence if:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation has consented to the application;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the application conforms to provincial regulatory requirements;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. there is sufficient unrecorded volume of flow in the Tla'amin Nation's water reservation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the application is for a volume of flow that, together with the total volume of flow licensed for that Stream under this Agreement, does not exceed a percentage of Available Flow for that Stream as set out in this Agreement; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. where required, the application includes provisions for storage where the monthly Available Flow during periods of low flow is insufficient to meet proposed demand.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. The volume of flow approved in a Water Licence issued under paragraph 9 will be deducted from the unrecorded volume of flow in the Tla'amin Nation's water reservation under paragraph 5.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. A Water Licence issued under paragraph 9, for use on Tla'amin Lands, will not be subject to any rentals, fees or other charges except taxes by British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Where a Water Licence issued under paragraph 9 is cancelled, expires or otherwise terminates, the volume of flow in that Water Licence will be added back to the unrecorded volume of flow in the Tla'amin Nation's water reservation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. This Agreement does not preclude the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Public Institution, Tla'amin Corporation or Tla'amin Citizen from applying for additional Water Licences under Provincial Law not provided for under the water reservation under paragraph 5.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: WATER LICENCE ACCESS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. Where the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Public Institution, Tla'amin Corporation or Tla'amin Citizen has a Water Licence issued under paragraph 9 or obtains a Water Licence under paragraph 13 and reasonably requires access across, or an interest in, provincial Crown land for the construction, maintenance, improvement or operation of works authorized under the licence, British Columbia will grant the access or interest on reasonable terms in accordance with Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. Where a person other than the Tla'amin Nation, a Tla'amin Public Institution, Tla'amin Corporation or Tla'amin Citizen has a Water Licence and reasonably requires access across, or an interest in, Tla'amin Lands for the construction, maintenance, improvement, or operation of works authorized under the licence, the Tla'amin Nation may not unreasonably withhold consent to, and will take reasonable steps to ensure, that access or the granting of that interest where the licence holder offers fair compensation to the owner of the estate or interest affected.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. For greater certainty, paragraph 15 does not apply to works, or access to works, on Tla'amin Lands which continue as provincial permits of occupation in accordance with Provincial Law or are replaced by the Tla'amin Nation under paragraph 55 of the Lands Chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. British Columbia will Consult with the Tla'amin Nation respecting applications for Water Licences made after the Effective Date where the applicant may reasonably require access across, or an interest in, Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LAW-MAKING AUTHORITY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. The Tla'amin Nation may make laws in relation to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the consent of the Tla'amin Nation under paragraph 7; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the supply and use of water from a Water Licence issued under paragraph 9.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. Tla'amin Law under subparagraph 18.a prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Federal of Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with Tla'amin Law under subparagraph 18.b.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GROUNDWATER

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. Where:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. British Columbia brings into force Provincial Law regulating the volume of Groundwater under Tla'amin Lands which may be extracted and used; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Groundwater is reasonably available,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on the volume of Groundwater that may be extracted and used for domestic, agricultural and industrial purposes by the Tla'amin Nation on Tla'amin Lands for as long as such Provincial Law is in effect.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. For the purposes of paragraph 21, British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. determine the volume of flow of Groundwater that can reasonably be withdrawn from the Groundwater aquifer under consideration while maintaining the sustainability and quality of the Groundwater from the aquifer;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. determine the existing and reasonable future needs for Groundwater of the Tla'amin Nation and Tla'amin Citizens on Tla'amin Lands, as well as the existing and future needs of other users in the area; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. take into account any applicable requirement under Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. Where British Columbia and the Tla'amin Nation fail to agree under paragraph 21, the dispute will be finally determined by arbitration under the Dispute Resolution Chapter without having to proceed through Stages One and Two.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. Access to Tla'amin Lands to extract Groundwater under Tla'amin Lands requires the consent of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: HYDRO POWER RESERVATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. In addition to the Tla'amin Nation's water reservation under paragraph 5, on the Effective Date British Columbia will establish a water reservation under the Water Act in favour of the Tla'amin Nation of the unrecorded water from Sliammon Creek, Appleton Creek and Theodosia River for 5 years to enable the Tla'amin Nation to investigate the suitability of those Streams for hydro power purposes, including related storage purposes.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Where:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tla'amin Nation applies for a Water Licence for hydro power purposes and any related storage purposes for a volume of flow to be applied against the water reservation under paragraph 25;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the proposed hydro power project conforms with Federal and Provincial Law; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. there is sufficient Available Flow in the Stream that is subject to the water reservation,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: British Columbia will grant the Water Licence.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. Where British Columbia issues a Water Licence under paragraph 26, the water reservation established under paragraph 25 will terminate in respect of that Stream.

paragraph: 2 As of the date of this Certificate, 593035 B.C. Ltd. is the registered owner in fee simple of the lands illustrated in Part 2 of Appendix C-3 of the Tla'amin Final Agreement and legally described as:

paragraph: a. Lot 2, District Lot 1612, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 17853, except part subdivided by Plan LMP26444; and

Ltd., on behalf of itself and its successors and assigns (the "Releasing Parties"), and in consideration of the agreement of Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada ("Canada") and Her Majesty the Queen in right of the Province of British Columbia ("British Columbia") to the inclusion in Tla'amin Lands of the lands legally described as:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Lot 2, District Lot 1612, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 17853, except part subdivided by Plan LMP26444; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: the sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, does hereby, as of the Effective Date of the Tla'amin Final Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. release, acquit and forever discharge each of Canada and British Columbia, including their respective employees, servants, agents, officers, directors, members, successors and assigns (the "Released Parties") of and from any and all damages, losses, liabilities or costs that the Released Parties may suffer or incur in connection with or as a result of any claims, demands, actions, or proceedings of whatsoever kind and howsoever arising, whether known or unknown, and which any of the Releasing Parties now have, have had or at any time hereafter can, shall or may have, in any way resulting from, arising from, or related to, the inclusion of the above lands in Tla'amin Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1.1 In this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) "Affiliate" will have the meaning ascribed to it in the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, as amended or replaced from time to time and, in the case of TELUS, includes an affiliate (as defined in that Act) of TELUS and any partnership or other unincorporated association in which TELUS or any affiliate (as defined in that Act) of TELUS has a controlling interest;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) "Agreement" means the General Instrument and the Filed Terms and all schedules attached to either of them;

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (d) "Effective Date" means the date upon which the Final Agreement will take effect;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (e) "Environment" means all the components of the earth including, without limitation, all layers of the atmosphere, air, land (including, without limitation, all underground spaces and cavities and all lands submerged under water), soil, water (including, without limitation, surface and underground water), organic and inorganic matter and living organisms, the interacting natural systems that include the foregoing and all other external conditions or influences under which humans, animals and plants live or are developed;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (f) "Excluded Right of Way Area" means any right of way area or corridor that is not part of the Lands but in whole or in part passes through the Lands or is adjacent to such Lands;

paragraph: (g) "Filed Terms" means these filed standard charge terms;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (h) "Final Agreement" means the Tla'amin Final Agreement among the Grantor, Canada and British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (i) "General Instrument" means the Form C General Instrument - Part 1 which refers to these Filed Terms and any other pages attached thereto;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (j) "Grantor" means the person named as the transferor in item 5 of the General Instrument;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (k) "Hydro" means British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (l) "Lands" means the lands and premises as are legally described in item 2 of the General Instrument;

paragraph: (m) "Right of Way Area" means those portions of the Lands more particularly described in Section 3 of this Agreement, as may be modified under this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (n) "TELUS" means TELUS Communications Inc.; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (o) "Works" means:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (i) as it relates to the rights and responsibilities of Hydro, all things and components, using any type of technology from time to time, necessary or convenient for the purposes of transmitting and distributing electricity and for the purpose of telecommunications, including: poles, towers, antennae (except for monopole free standing antennae), guy wires, brackets, crossarms, insulators, above ground or underground transformers, anchors, attachments, lines, access nodes and cables, including underground or fibre optic cables, underground conduits, lines and pipes of every kind, cabinets, all ancillary appliances and fittings, reasonably required associated protective installations and related works such as fencing for safety or security, devices and identifying colours for aircraft warning, and utility services for the operation of any of the foregoing;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (ii) as it relates to the rights and responsibilities of TELUS, all things and components, using any type of technology from time to time, necessary or convenient for the purpose of telecommunications, including: poles, towers, guy wires, brackets, crossarms, insulators, transformers, anchors, attachments, lines, access nodes and cables, including fibre optic cables, in whole or in part and underground conduits, lines and pipes of every kind, underground cables, including fibre optic cables, together with all ancillary appliances, fittings and cabinets and above ground or underground equipment shelters.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1.2 With respect to any obligation on the part of Hydro or TELUS under this Agreement, any reference to Hydro or TELUS includes their respective servants, officers, employees, agents, contractors, sub-contractors, invitees, licensees, successors, permitted assigns, and those for whom either or both of them is responsible in law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GRANT OF RIGHT OF WAY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2.1 The Grantor grants over the Lands separately to each of Hydro and TELUS and their respective employees, representatives, contractors, agents, licensees, successors and assigns, for so long as required, the uninterrupted right, liberty and right of way to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) use the Right of Way Area as follows:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (i) excavate for, construct, install, erect, abandon, replace, extend, upgrade, operate, maintain, alter, remove and repair the Works on, over, in, under, across and through the Right of Way Area; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (ii) clear the Right of Way Area and keep it cleared (including pruning or removal) of any trees or growth at any time located therein;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) use the Area of the Works as follows:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (i) enter, work, pass and repass upon, on, and along the Area of the Works;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (ii) maintain, repair, replace and use trails, roads, lanes, and bridges on the Area of the Works including, in addition, any portions reasonably required adjacent to the Area of the Works for the sake of continuity, with or without equipment, machinery and materials to such extent as may reasonably be required by Hydro or TELUS in relation to this Agreement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (iii) clear the Area of the Works and keep it cleared of all or any part of any obstruction, improvement or other matter which, in the reasonable opinion of Hydro or TELUS, does or might interfere with or endanger the Works, disrupt service to Hydro's or TELUS's customers, or pose a hazard to persons or property in relation to the Works; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (iv) clear the Area of the Works and keep it cleared (including pruning or removal) of all or any part of any trees or growth which do or might, in the opinion of Hydro or TELUS, interfere with or endanger the Works, disrupt service to Hydro's or TELUS's customers, or pose a hazard to persons or property in relation to the Works;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (c) to enjoy further rights as follows:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (i) Hydro and TELUS may, with the prior approval of the Grantor and any party with a registered interest in the affected areas, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned, cut trees or growth outside the Area of the Works, if in the reasonable opinion of Hydro or TELUS such trees or growth might interfere with or endanger the Works (whether on or off the Lands) or pose a hazard to persons or property in relation to the Works;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (ii) Hydro and TELUS may pass and repass over, and maintain, repair replace and use, all roads, lanes and bridges on the Lands outside of the Area of the Works with or without equipment, machinery and materials to such extent as may reasonably be required by Hydro or TELUS in relation to this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (iii) if there are no suitable roads, lanes or bridges under paragraph 2.1 (c) (ii), Hydro and TELUS may either:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: A. construct, maintain, repair, replace and pass and repass over roads, lanes or bridges on the Lands; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: B. pass and repass over the Lands elsewhere than on roads, lanes and bridges, with or without equipment, machinery and materials to such extent as may reasonably be required by Hydro or TELUS in relation to this Agreement, subject to prior approval of the route by the Grantor, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Hydro and TELUS do not require such approval if there is an emergency or a reasonably apprehended emergency or for the determination of electricity consumption, but will act reasonably and report to the Grantor the purpose and extent of the access as soon as practicable;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (iv) to conduct vegetation management upon the Area of the Works, such as the planting of vegetation compatible with the undertakings of Hydro or TELUS, and the application of herbicides and pesticides with the consent of the Grantor, provided that Hydro and TELUS will not conduct any aerial application of herbicides or pesticides on the Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (v) to install, maintain and use gates in all fences which are now or hereafter shall be on the Right of Way Area and in fences affecting access to the Area of the Works;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (vi) to ground any structures, installation or things, by whomsoever owned, from time to time situated anywhere on the Right of Way Area or adjacent Lands where, in the reasonable opinion of Hydro and TELUS, such grounding will eliminate or reduce hazards to persons or property in relation to the Works;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (vii) Hydro and TELUS may enter onto the Lands outside the Area of the Works for the purpose of undertaking works to protect any Works located within the Lands or within an Excluded Right of Way Area or to protect persons or property that may be at risk from such Works, provided that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: A. Hydro or TELUS will before commencing such works deliver to the Grantor for approval a written work plan describing the proposed work on the Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: B. the Grantor will not unreasonably withhold, condition or delay approval of such work plan, and shall take into consideration the effect of the proposed work, the cost of the proposed work compared to the cost of alternate solutions and the extent of the risk of not undertaking the work. If Hydro or TELUS, as the case may be, and the Grantor cannot agree on a work plan requested by Hydro or TELUS within 30 days of receipt by the Grantor of the proposed work plan, then either party may refer the disagreement to dispute resolution under section 18 of this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: C. Hydro or TELUS, as the case may be, will pay compensation for any damage to the Lands resulting from the implementation of the work plan;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: D. if Hydro or TELUS, as the case may be, determines in its reasonable judgment that an emergency situation exists or there are imminent safety concerns, Hydro and TELUS may, without approval of the Grantor, undertake works and take such steps on the Lands as are reasonably required to be taken immediately in order to protect the Works, or to protect persons or property that may be at risk from the Works, and in that event Hydro or TELUS will as soon as reasonably possible thereafter notify the Grantor; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (d) generally, do all such other acts or things as may reasonably be necessary or incidental to the business of Hydro or TELUS in connection with any of the above.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: RIGHT OF WAY AREA

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3.1 The Right of Way Area consists of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) all portions of the Lands reasonably required for the following:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (i) those Works existing at the date of this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (ii) any additional Works constructed adjacent to, along the sides of or across any roads, lanes or bridges from time to time existing on or through the Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (iii) any additional Works that provide service to any lands adjacent to any roads, lanes, or bridges from time to time existing on or through the Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (iv) any additional Works that provide service to any lands or customers where the landowners of any intervening parcels consent to the installation of any such Works; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) any such other portions of the Lands as may from time to time be consented to in writing by the Grantor, or by any delegate appointed by the Grantor.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3.2 Hydro and TELUS agree to provide the Grantor on request with an updated sketch of the Works from time to time, if the Works have been extended in the previous calendar year, unless such information is available to the Grantor on-line. The Parties confirm that this Agreement, and all of its terms and provisions, shall apply to such new works in their entirety.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3.3 Nothing in this Part 3.0 is intended to affect the rights of Hydro or TELUS to make arrangements directly with a person in legal possession of any lands for the construction, operation and maintenance of the Works and all matters incidental thereto.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NON-EXCLUSIVE USE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4.1 Notwithstanding anything else in this Agreement, Hydro and TELUS acknowledge and agree that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) this Agreement does not grant a fee simple interest in the Lands, but rather grants a non-exclusive use over the Area of the Works; and

heading: Commencement

paragraph: 6.1 Hydro and TELUS each covenant separately with the Grantor to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) keep the portions of the Lands used by Hydro or TELUS under this Agreement in a safe, clean and sanitary condition to the extent the condition relates to the use or occupation by Hydro or TELUS of such Lands, as the case may be, provided that Hydro and TELUS have no obligation to keep any roads within the Area of the Works suitable for use by anyone except Hydro and TELUS;

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (d) if any human remains, burial pit or grave are unearthed or discovered on the Lands by either Hydro or TELUS immediately notify the Grantor, cease any further activity that could affected the site until permitted by the Grantor to resume activity and take such reasonable steps and precautions to protect the site as may be directed by the Grantor;

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (f) not bury debris or rubbish of any kind on the Lands in excavations or backfill, and to remove shoring and similar temporary structures as backfilling proceeds; and

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) Hydro or TELUS, as the case may be, will, before undertaking any work, deliver a sketch plan to the Grantor indicating the contemplated relocation of the Works for approval by the Grantor, which approval will not be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) Hydro or TELUS, as the case may be, will take into account any likely material effect of the relocated Works on adjacent lands, and the Grantor will take into account the cost efficiencies of the location selected by Hydro or TELUS for the relocated Works in relation to alternative locations;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (c) the relocated Works will be covered by the terms and conditions of this Agreement; and

heading: Commencement

paragraph: 13.1 When a portion of the Right of Way Area is no longer required for the Works, Hydro or TELUS, as the case may be, will restore the ground surface of the affected portion of the Right of Way Area, as near as is reasonably practicable to its condition prior to the installation of the Works, including the removal of any above ground Works, underground transformers and, where practicable and at the request of the Grantor, any cables located within underground ducts in such portion of the Right of Way Area.

paragraph: (iii) may by its operation, use, maintenance or existence on the Area of the Works create or increase any hazard to persons or property in relation to the Works;

paragraph: COMPENSATION FOR DAMAGES

paragraph: 16.1 Hydro and TELUS covenant with the Grantor that if, contrary to the terms of this Agreement, they damage any structures, buildings, fixtures, improvements, or chattels, or damage any crops, merchantable timber, livestock, drains, ditches, culverts, fences, trails, bridges, or roads on the Lands, or contaminate the Lands in the exercise of its vegetation management under paragraph 2.1 (c) (vi), and such damage is not caused as a result of the Grantor's breach of the terms of this Agreement or the negligence or willful act of the Grantor or its contractors, agents or permittees, then Hydro or TELUS, as the case may be, will:

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement

paragraph: (a) to use the Permit Area as follows:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (i) to construct, install, remove, operate, maintain, repair and replace the Facilities under, over, in, on and through the Permit Area for the purpose of Shaw's telecommunication business and undertaking;

paragraph: (d) to trim, cut back or remove any trees or shrubs in the Permit Area which because of overhanging branches or extensive root growth causes or are likely to cause interference with the Facilities or with their installation, operation, maintenance, or removal. paragraph: 8.0 ENVIRONMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8.1 Should the Facilities or any action by Shaw on the Permit Area pursuant to this Agreement contribute to any detrimental environmental changes for which remedial action is necessary in accordance with regulations and standards established by applicable Tla'amin, federal and/or provincial legislation, Shaw will immediately undertake, at its own cost, the required remedial action to the extent of its contribution.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8.2 Shaw acknowledges and agrees that, notwithstanding any rule of law to the contrary, any Hazardous Substances, which are located, stored or incorporated in or on the Permit Area or any part of the Lands as a result of any action or inaction on behalf of Shaw will remain the sole and exclusive property of Shaw and will not become the property of Tla'amin regardless of any degree of affixation of the Hazardous Substances to the Permit Area or the Lands. This section will survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, save only that, to the extent that the performance of any obligation pertaining to it requires access to or entry upon the Permit Area after the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, Shaw will have entry and access to the Permit Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8.3 Notwithstanding any provision contained hereunder to the contrary, Shaw shall not be responsible for any Hazardous Substances that are or were present in or on the Permit Area and/or the Lands prior to the work by or on behalf of Shaw with respect to its Facilities or if such Hazardous Substance was brought by any person for whom Shaw is not responsible for at law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9.0 DEBRIS REMOVAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9.1 Shaw will remove all garbage and debris deposited by it from or at the Permit Area as construction of the Facilities progresses and will maintain the Permit Area free and clear of garbage and debris.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10.0 ARTIFACTS AND SURVEY MONUMENTS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10.1 Shaw will immediately notify Tla'amin of any Artifact or human remains unearthed or discovered by it in the course of its operations on or at the Permit Area and will cease any further activity that could affect the site until permitted by Tla'amin to resume activity, so as to avoid any and all further damage, injury or destruction to such Artifact or remains, ensuring the preservation of the same. Tla'amin retains the exclusive right to take possession of said Artifact and move or relocate it as Tla'amin deems appropriate. If the human remains turn out to be Tla'amin ancestral remains, Tla'amin retains the exclusive right to remove or re-bury the remains according to Tla'amin laws and traditions.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10.2 Shaw will ensure that all legal control survey monuments are protected and not disturbed, damaged or destroyed during any construction or maintenance which is undertaken by it or on its behalf on the Permit Area. Should any monuments be disturbed, damaged or destroyed, Shaw, at its own expense, will replace such monuments by a duly qualified Land Surveyor to the satisfaction of Tla'amin, acting reasonably.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11.0 FENCING AND USE OF THE PERMIT AREA

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11.1 Shaw will not fence the Permit Area, without the prior consent of Tla'amin.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11.2 Tla'amin will not:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) make, place, erect or maintain any building, structure, excavation, pile of material or obstruction or plant any growth on the Permit Area which, in the reasonable opinion of Shaw might interfere with or endanger the construction, operation, maintenance or removal of the Facilities or might obstruct access by Shaw to the Facilities; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) do any act or thing which might, in the reasonable opinion of Shaw interfere with or damage the Facilities or create or increase any hazards to persons.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12.0 INSPECTIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12.1 Shaw will keep the Facilities in good repair and it will be lawful for Tla'amin at all reasonable times to enter upon the Permit Area for the purposes of examining the Permit Area and the Facilities.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13.0 INSURANCE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13.1 Shaw shall, at its own expense, obtain and maintain insurance, or provide reasonable evidence of insurance, in the amount of not less than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000.00) for each occurrence against claims for personal injury, death, property damage and loss which may arise under this Agreement, including, but not limited to, the construction, maintenance or operation of the Facilities or any act or omission of Shaw.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13.2 All insurance policies will be on the following terms:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) Tla'amin shall be an additional insured;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) the policy will contain an agreement by the insurer that it will not cancel or alter the policy without first giving Tla'amin at least thirty (30) days prior written notice; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (c) the policy will include protective liability for acts performed by Shaw and/or its contractors or their subcontractors, employer's liability (or contingent employer's liability where workers' compensation insurance applies), and unlicensed and specially licensed vehicle liability coverage.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13.3 Shaw, including its contractors and sub-contractors, shall make and maintain all required workers' compensation insurance payments.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14.0 NUISANCE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14.1 Where, as a result of any act or omission by Shaw relative to this Agreement, a nuisance exists, Tla'amin may, by written notice, order Shaw to abate the nuisance. If Shaw fails to do so within a reasonable time, Tla'amin may take whatever steps may be necessary to abate the nuisance and Shaw will be liable for the direct cost thereof; PROVIDED, however, that the existence or the use of the Facilities on the Permit Area will not constitute a nuisance.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15.0 QUIET ENJOYMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15.1 Subject to performing and observing all the covenants and conditions on its part to be performed and observed, Shaw will peaceably hold and enjoy the Permit Rights without hindrance, molestation or interruption on the part of Tla'amin.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16.0 ASSIGNMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16.1 This Agreement and the Permit Rights may:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (a) not be assigned or otherwise transferred without the prior written consent of Tla'amin which consent will not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: (b) be assigned or otherwise transferred to an Affiliate or to a purchaser of all or substantially all of Shaw's assets located in the Permit Area,

heading: Commencement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17.0 INDEMNITY AND INTEREST

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17.1 Each party (the "Indemnifying Party") agrees that it shall be liable to the other party, its officers, employees, servants and agents (collectively, the "Indemnified Party") for all losses, costs, expenses (including all reasonable legal and other professional fees and disbursements) and damages whatsoever which the Indemnified Party may suffer, sustain, pay or incur and shall indemnify and hold harmless the Indemnified Party from and against all actions, proceedings, claims and demands whatsoever which may be brought or made against the Indemnified Party or suffered or incurred by the Indemnified Party, by reason of any damage to property, including property of Indemnified Party, or injury, including injury resulting in death, to persons, including the employees, servants, agents, licensees and invitees of the Indemnified Party, whether in contract, tort or otherwise, by reason of or arising out of or attributable to any act or omission of the Indemnifying        Party under this Agreement and/or relating to the Lands and the Permit Area except where any losses, costs, expenses (including all reasonable legal and other professional fees and disbursements) and damages are due to the wrongful act, omission, default or negligence of the Indemnified Party and/or by those for whom it is in law responsible.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17.2 Notwithstanding any provision contained in this Agreement to the contrary, neither party shall be liable to the other party in any way for indirect or consequential losses or damages, or damages for pure economic loss, howsoever caused or contributed to or in connection with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18.0 BREACH

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18.1 If Shaw fails to perform or observe any material covenant contained in this Agreement, Tla'amin will be entitled to give Shaw notice of breach of covenant and if Shaw fails to rectify the breach to the reasonable satisfaction of Tla'amin within ninety (90) days of receipt of such notice, or if the breach is one which cannot reasonably be remedied within ninety (90) days, within such further period as Shaw may request and Tla'amin may approve, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed, it will be lawful for Tla'amin to authorize the rectification of such breach in any manner Tla'amin deems appropriate at the sole expense of Shaw which expense will be expeditiously paid to Tla'amin upon demand.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19.0 DISPUTE RESOLUTION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19.1 The parties shall attempt to settle any dispute arising out of or pursuant to this Agreement through good-faith negotiations among the parties.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19.2 Failing a negotiated agreement, the parties may then refer the matter to mediation, arbitration or other alternative to court dispute resolution mechanisms by mutual written consent. Absent such consent or failing the resolution of the matter through these means, the matter may be referred to a court or regulatory authority of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19.3 During any stages in this dispute resolution process, the parties will continue to perform their obligations under this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19.4 Any resolution of the dispute will be in accordance with the applicable Laws of Tla'amin and the Province of British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20.0 WAIVER

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20.1 No waiver on behalf of any party of any breach will take place or be binding unless it is expressed in writing and any waiver will not be deemed to be a general waiver or to limit or affect the rights of any such party with respect to any other future breach.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21.0 NOTICE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21.1 Any notice or demand required or permitted to be given hereunder or any tender or delivery of documents may be sufficiently given by personal delivery or by facsimile or other electronic transmission (receipt confirmed) to the parties at the following addresses:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21.2 Any notice may also be given by prepaid registered mail and such notice shall be effective on the third day following the date of mailing, except in the event that there is a disruption in postal services at the date of mailing in which case notice may be effected by courier or by personal delivery or a facsimile transmission as stated above. Any notice so given shall be deemed to have been received on the date on which is was delivered in person or, if transmitted by facsimile, on the date it was transmitted. Tla'amin and Shaw may change their respective addresses by notice in writing to each other.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22.2 This Agreement will be binding upon and enure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, successors, and permitted assigns and this Agreement will be binding upon any residents, users, or occupiers of any portion of the Permit Area from time to time.

heading: Commencement

paragraph: 1.1 In this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Agreement" means this agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Effective Date" means the date on which the Tla'amin Final Agreement takes effect;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Parties" means the parties to this Agreement; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: "Tla'amin Final Agreement" means the Tla'amin Final Agreement signed on behalf of Canada, British Columbia and Tla'amin Nation on ..........................., 20....., and includes any amendments from time to time.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2.0 SUNSHINE COAST TRAIL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2.1 For the purposes of this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. an overview map of Tla'amin Lands is attached to this Agreement as Schedule 1;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. an overview map of the Sunshine Coast Trail is attached to this Agreement as Schedule 2; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. an overview map of that portion of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands is attached to this Agreement as Schedule 3.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2.2 PRPAWS will have access to Tla'amin Lands for the purposes of this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3.0 MAINTENANCE OF SUNSHINE COAST TRAIL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3.1 PRPAWS will be responsible for the management and maintenance of those portions of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3.2 PRPAWS will notify the Tla'amin Nation prior to undertaking any trail maintenance on those portions of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4.0 TLA'AMIN NATION LAND MANAGEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4.1 The Tla'amin Nation land management plans will take into consideration continued public access to and use of those portions of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4.2 The Tla'amin Nation will notify and, if requested by PRPAWS, discuss with PRPAWS any land management plan or proposed use of Tla'amin Lands that may affect public access to or use of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4.3 In the event that the Tla'amin Nation's use of Tla'amin Lands prevents continued public access to or use of those portions of the Sunshine Coast Trail on Tla'amin Lands, the Tla'amin Nation and PRPAWS will develop a work plan which identifies:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. alternative locations for the Sunshine Coast Trail; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. costs and responsibilities of each Party pertaining to trail relocation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5.0 ENTIRE AGREEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement between the Parties in respect of the subject matter of this Agreement and, except as set out in this Agreement, there is no representation, warranty, collateral agreement, condition, right or obligation affecting this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6.0 AMENDMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6.1 The Parties agree to review this Agreement and its effectiveness from time to time as may be requested by either Party.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6.2 Any amendments to this Agreement will require the written consent of both Parties, and will take effect on the date designated in the amendment.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7.0 TERM AND TERMINATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7.1 This Agreement will take effect upon the date that it is signed by the authorized signatories of the Parties.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7.2 PRPAWS may terminate this Agreement on sixty (60) days notice in writing to the Tla'amin Nation or a date mutually agreed upon by the Parties.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8.0 ASSIGNMENT AND ENUREMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8.1 This Agreement may be assigned by PRPAWS, either in whole or in part, without the consent of the Tla'amin Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8.2 This Agreement will enure to the benefit of and be binding upon the Parties and their respective permitted assigns.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9.1 Unless otherwise provided, notice must be in writing and delivered personally or by courier, transmitted by fax or mailed by prepaid registered post.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9.2 Notice will be considered to have been given, made, or delivered, and received:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. if delivered personally or by courier, at the start of business on the next business day after the business day on which it was received by the addressee or a responsible representative of the addressee;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. if mailed by prepaid registered post in Canada, when the postal receipt is acknowledged by the addressee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9.3 If a fax number has not been provided by a Party, notice will be delivered or mailed to the address appearing on the first page of this Agreement.
