heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "analyst" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person designated under section 6 (2), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a member of a class of persons designated under section 6 (2);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "container" includes equipment that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is carried on a chassis,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is strong enough to be suitable for repeated use, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) is designed to facilitate the transportation of goods without intermediate reloading,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include packaging, a road vehicle or a rail vehicle;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "dangerous goods" means any product, substance or organism included by its nature or by the regulations in any of the classes listed in the Schedule;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "facility" includes an installation, plant, factory or place where goods are or may be handled;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "federal Act" means the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act (Canada);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "handling" means loading, packing or placing, unloading, unpacking or removing or reloading, repacking or replacing dangerous goods in or from any container, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle or at any facility for the purposes of, in the course of or following transportation and includes storing dangerous goods in the course of transportation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "highway" means a highway as defined in the Motor Vehicle Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "inspector" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person designated under section 6 (1), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a member of a class of persons designated under section 6 (1);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "packaging" means a receptacle or enveloping material used to contain or protect dangerous goods, but does not include a container, road vehicle or rail vehicle;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "rail vehicle" means a vehicle that is drawn, propelled or driven on rails by means other than by muscular power;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "road vehicle" means a vehicle as defined in the Motor Vehicle Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "safety mark" includes a design, symbol, device, sign, label, placard, letter, word, number, abbreviation or any combination of these that is to be displayed on dangerous goods or containers, packaging, road vehicles or rail vehicles used in the handling or transportation of dangerous goods;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "safety requirements" means requirements for

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the handling or transportation of dangerous goods,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the reporting of handling or transportation of dangerous goods,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the training of persons engaged in the handling or transportation of dangerous goods, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the inspection of the handling or transportation of dangerous goods;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "safety standards" means standards regulating the design, construction, equipping, functioning or performance of containers, packaging, road vehicles or rail vehicles used in the handling or transportation of dangerous goods;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "shipping document" means a document that accompanies dangerous goods being handled or transported and that describes or contains information relating to the goods and, without restricting the generality of this definition, includes a bill of lading, cargo manifest, shipping order and waybill;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transportation" means transportation by a road vehicle or a rail vehicle or both.

heading: Application
paragraph: 2		  This Act does not apply to the handling or transportation of dangerous goods if the dangerous goods are deemed under the regulations to be handled or transported or both under the sole direction or control of the Minister of National Defence for Canada.

heading: Conflicting provisions
paragraph:
3
		  (1) In the event of a conflict between

heading: Conflicting provisions
paragraph: (a) a regulation made under this Act, or a permit issued under this Act, and

heading: Conflicting provisions
paragraph: (b) a regulation made under another Act,

heading: Conflicting provisions
paragraph: the regulation made under this Act and the terms of the permit issued under this Act prevail to the extent of the conflict.

heading: Conflicting provisions
paragraph:
(2) 
            Subsection (1) does not apply to a regulation made under the Environmental Management Act.

heading: Exemption by permit
paragraph: 4		  (1) The minister, or a person designated by the minister, may issue a permit exempting a person or dangerous goods from one or more provisions of this Act.

heading: Exemption by permit
paragraph: (2) A permit issued under this section may contain any terms that the minister, or a person designated by the minister, considers appropriate.

heading: Safety requirements
paragraph:
5
		  A person must not handle or transport dangerous goods unless

heading: Safety requirements
paragraph: (a) all applicable prescribed safety requirements are complied with, and

heading: Safety requirements
paragraph: (b) all containers, packaging, road vehicles and rail vehicles comply with the applicable prescribed safety standards and display the applicable prescribed safety marks.

heading: Inspectors and analysts
paragraph:
6
		  (1) If the minister is of the opinion that a person or the members of a class of persons are qualified to act in the capacity of dangerous goods inspector under this Act, the minister may designate the person or class.

heading: Inspectors and analysts
paragraph: (2) If the minister is of the opinion that a person or the members of a class of persons are qualified to act in the capacity of analyst under this Act, the minister may designate the person or class.

heading: Inspector to show certificate of designation
paragraph:
7
		  (1) An inspector must be provided with a certificate, in the prescribed form, of the inspector's designation showing the purposes, classes of dangerous goods, road vehicles or rail vehicles and the buildings or places for which the inspector has been designated.

heading: Inspector to show certificate of designation
paragraph: (2) On entering or inspecting any building, place, container, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle an inspector must, if so required, produce the certificate to the person in charge of the thing or material being entered or inspected.

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph:
8
		  (1) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this Act, regulations under it or a permit under section 4 and within the scope of the inspector's certificate of designation, an inspector may, at any reasonable time,

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (a) enter and inspect any building, place, road vehicle or rail vehicle where the inspector believes, on reasonable and probable grounds, that dangerous goods are being handled or transported, and

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (b) request the opening and inspection of, or open and inspect any container, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle that the inspector believes, on reasonable and probable grounds, is being used for the handling or transportation of dangerous goods.

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (2) In the course of an inspection under subsection (1), an inspector may

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (a) for the purpose of analysis, take samples of anything found in the building, place, container, package, road vehicle or rail vehicle being inspected if the inspector believes, on reasonable and probable grounds, the substance or thing to be dangerous goods, and

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (b) examine and remove, for the purpose of making copies and extracts of, any books, records, shipping documents or other documents or papers that the inspector believes, on reasonable and probable grounds, contain information relevant to the administration or enforcement of this Act and the regulations.

heading: Powers of inspectors
paragraph: (3) If an inspector is satisfied, on reasonable and probable grounds, that any dangerous goods are being handled or transported other than in compliance with the applicable prescribed safety marks, safety requirements, safety standards and shipping documents, the inspector must, wherever possible, request the taking of, or take, any measures necessary to remedy the failure to comply.

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph:
9
		  (1) An inspector may exercise the powers under this section if satisfied, on reasonable and probable grounds, that

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (a) there is occurring or has occurred a discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods from any container, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle by means of which the dangerous goods are being handled or transported,

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (b) there exists a serious and imminent danger of a discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods by reason of any condition occurring during the handling or transportation of the dangerous goods, or

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (c) a provision of this Act or the regulations or a term of a permit is being or has been contravened.

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (2) In circumstances referred to in subsection (1) the inspector may do one or more of the following:

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (a) take measures that the inspector considers necessary in order to prevent or reduce any serious and imminent danger to life, health, property or the environment;

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (b) detain any dangerous goods, container, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle that the inspector believes, on reasonable and probable grounds, to be related to the discharge, emission or escape or condition that has arisen or is related to the contravention that has occurred;

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (c) remove or direct the removal of the detained goods, container, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle to an appropriate place.

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (3) Any property detained under this section must be released after

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (a) the provisions of this Act, the regulations and the terms of a permit, if any, have, in the opinion of the inspector, been complied with, or

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (b) the danger to life, health, property or the environment has, in the opinion of the inspector, been prevented or adequately reduced, as the case may be,

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: whichever occurs first.

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (4) All costs and charges of the detention of a road vehicle or rail vehicle under subsection (2) are a lien on the road vehicle or rail vehicle, as the case may be, and any of the rights and remedies under Part 6 of the Commercial Liens Act may be exercised in respect of the lien.

heading: Inspector's power to detain and remove
paragraph: (5) Neither the government nor any person acting under the authority of this section is liable for loss or damage arising from the detention of goods, containers, packaging, a road vehicle or a rail vehicle or the destruction or deterioration of anything detained under this section.

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: 10		  A person must not, while an inspector is exercising powers or carrying out duties and functions under this Act, do any of the following:

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: (a) fail to comply with any reasonable request of the inspector;

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: (b) knowingly make any false or misleading statement either verbally or in writing to the inspector;

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: (c) unless authorized by the inspector, remove, alter or interfere in any way with anything removed, being inspected or detained by the inspector;

heading: Assistance to inspectors
paragraph: (d) otherwise obstruct or hinder the inspector.

heading: Certificate of inspection, detention or sampling
paragraph:
11
		  If an inspector inspects, detains or takes a sample of anything under this Act the inspector must, on request, provide the person in charge of it with a certificate, in the prescribed form, evidencing the inspection, detention or taking of the sample, as the case may be.

heading: Analyst's certificate or report as evidence
paragraph:
12
		  Subject to sections 14 and 15, a certificate or report appearing to have been signed by an inspector or an analyst stating that the inspector or analyst has inspected, analyzed or examined any road vehicle, rail vehicle, packaging, container, shipping document, product, substance or organism and stating the results of the inspection, analysis or examination

heading: Analyst's certificate or report as evidence
paragraph: (a) is admissible in evidence in a prosecution for an offence under this Act without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the certificate or report, and

heading: Analyst's certificate or report as evidence
paragraph: (b) in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, is proof of the statements contained in the certificate or report.

heading: Copies or extracts of certificate or report as evidence
paragraph:
13
		  Subject to sections 14 and 15, a copy or an extract of a certificate or report made by an inspector or analyst and appearing to have been certified under an inspector's or analyst's signature as a true copy or extract

heading: Copies or extracts of certificate or report as evidence
paragraph: (a) is admissible in evidence in a prosecution for an offence under this Act without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the copy or extract of a certificate or report, and

heading: Copies or extracts of certificate or report as evidence
paragraph: (b) in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, has the same probative force as the original document would have if it had been proved in the ordinary way.

heading: Cross examination of inspector may be permitted by court
paragraph:
14
		  The party against whom a certificate or report is produced under section 12 or against whom a copy or extract is produced under section 13 may, with leave of the court, require the attendance of the inspector or analyst who signed or appears to have signed the certificate, report, copy or extract for the purpose of a cross-examination.

heading: Notice of intention to introduce evidence
paragraph:
15
		  A certificate, report, copy or extract referred to in section 12 or 13 must not be received in evidence unless the party intending to produce it has served on the party against whom it is intended to be produced a notice of this intention together with a duplicate of the certificate, report, copy or extract.

heading: Penalties
paragraph:
16
		  (1) A person who contravenes section 5 or the terms of a permit issued under section 4 commits an offence.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (2) A person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) on a first conviction, to a fine of not more than $50 000 or to a term of imprisonment of not more than 2 years, or both, and

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) on a subsequent conviction, to a fine of not more than $100 000 or to a term of imprisonment of not more than 2 years, or both.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (3) A person who contravenes section 10 or 21 (1) or (2) commits an offence.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (4) A person who commits an offence under subsection (3) is liable on conviction to a fine of not more than $10 000 or to a term of imprisonment of not more than one year, or both.

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may provide in regulations that a person, who is guilty of an offence established under the regulations to this Act, is liable to

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (a) a fine of a prescribed amount not greater than $10 000,

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (b) a prescribed term of imprisonment of not longer than one year, or

heading: Penalties
paragraph: (c) both a prescribed fine and term of imprisonment that does not exceed the maximum amount and term specified in paragraphs (a) and (b).

heading: Defence of due diligence
paragraph:
17
		  Subject to section 18, in a prosecution for an offence against this Act or the regulations, it is a defence for the person charged to prove that the person took all reasonable measures to comply with this Act.

heading: Offence by employee or agent
paragraph:
18
		  In a prosecution for an offence against this Act or the regulations, it is sufficient proof of the offence to establish that it was committed by an employee or agent of the accused, whether or not the employee or agent is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence, unless the accused establishes that the offence was committed without the accused's consent and that the accused took all reasonable measures to prevent its commission.

heading: Officers, directors and agents of corporation guilty of offence by corporation
paragraph:
19
		  An officer, director or agent of a corporation, who directs, authorizes, assents to, acquiesces in or participates in the commission of an offence, is a party to and guilty of the offence and is liable on conviction to the punishment provided for the offence, whether or not the corporation has been prosecuted or convicted.

heading: Time limit for bringing prosecution
paragraph:
20
		  No prosecution for an offence against this Act or the regulations may be commenced more than 2 years after the day the alleged offence was committed.

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph:
21
		  (1) If a discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods from any container, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle occurs, the person who, at that time, has the charge, management or control of the dangerous goods must, in the manner and the circumstances established by the regulations, report the discharge, emission or escape.

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph: (2) If a person is required to make a report under subsection (1), the person must, as soon as possible, take all reasonable emergency measures consistent with public safety to repair or remedy a dangerous condition or to reduce or mitigate danger to life, health, property or the environment that results or may reasonably be expected to result from the discharge, emission or escape.

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph: (3) If an inspector is satisfied, on reasonable and probable grounds, that

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph: (a) a discharge, emission or escape referred to in subsection (1) has occurred or might occur, and

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph: (b) immediate action is necessary in order to carry out any reasonable emergency measures referred to in subsection (2),

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph: the inspector may take the emergency measures or request that the emergency measures be taken by a person the inspector considers qualified to do so.

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph: (4) Any inspector or other person required, requested or authorized to take reasonable emergency measures under subsection (2) or (3) may enter and have access to any place or property and may do all reasonable things in order to comply with either or both of those subsections.

heading: Duty to report discharge, emission or escape of dangerous goods
paragraph: (5) A person requested to act under subsection (3) is not personally liable for any damage in respect of any act or omission in the course of complying with the request, unless it is shown that the person did not act reasonably in the circumstances.

heading: Evidence of financial responsibility
paragraph:
22
		  The minister may require any person who engages in or who proposes to engage in the transportation of dangerous goods to provide evidence of financial responsibility in a form of insurance, an indemnity bond or any other form satisfactory to the minister.

heading: Local government control of transport on highways
paragraph:
23
		  (1) A municipality may make bylaws with respect to highways under its direction, control and management

heading: Local government control of transport on highways
paragraph: (a) designating the route and time of travel of road vehicles transporting dangerous goods, and

heading: Local government control of transport on highways
paragraph: (b) prohibiting the carrying of dangerous goods on the highways specified in the bylaw.

heading: Local government control of transport on highways
paragraph: (2) A bylaw under subsection (1) does not come into force until it is approved by the minister.

heading: Agreements with Canada
paragraph:
24
		  (1) With the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister may enter into agreements with the government of Canada with respect to the administration and enforcement of

heading: Agreements with Canada
paragraph: (a) this Act and the regulations or any provision of this Act or the regulations, and

heading: Agreements with Canada
paragraph: (b) the federal Act, or any provision of that Act or the regulations made under it.

heading: Agreements with Canada
paragraph: (2) An agreement entered into under subsection (1) may provide for any matters necessary for or incidental to the implementation, administration or enforcement agreed on, or for the apportionment of any costs, expenses or revenues arising from the agreement.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
25
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (a) specifying products, substances and organisms to be included in the classes listed in the Schedule;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (b) establishing divisions, subdivisions and groups of dangerous goods and classes of dangerous goods;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (c) specifying, for each product, substance and organism prescribed under paragraph (a), the class listed in the Schedule and the division, subdivision or group into which it falls;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (d) determining or providing a manner of determining the class listed in the Schedule and the division, subdivision or group into which any dangerous goods not prescribed under paragraph (a) falls;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (e) exempting from the application of this Act, the regulations or a provision of this Act or the regulations, the handling or transportation of dangerous goods

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i)  in specified quantities or concentrations,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (ii)  in specified circumstances,

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iii)  for specified purposes, or

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (iv)  in specified containers, packaging, road vehicle or rail vehicle;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (f) respecting the manner of identifying the quantities or concentrations of dangerous goods exempted under paragraph (e);

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (g) respecting the circumstances in which any dangerous goods are deemed to be under the sole direction or control of the Minister of National Defence for Canada;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (h) respecting the manner of applying for a permit;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (i) respecting circumstances in which the handling or transportation of dangerous goods is prohibited;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (j) specifying dangerous goods that must not be handled or transported in any circumstances;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (k) respecting safety marks, safety requirements and safety standards of general or particular application;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (l) respecting shipping and other documents to be used in the handling or transportation of dangerous goods, the information to be included in those documents and the persons by whom and the manner in which these documents are to be used and retained;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (m) establishing circumstances in which fees are or are not payable for inspections or permits under this Act and determining the amount of those fees;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (n) prescribing the forms of the certificates referred to in sections 7 and 11;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (o) establishing the manner of reporting and the information to be included in the report under section 21 (1) and the circumstances in which a report need not be made under that section;

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (p) providing for the appeal of a decision to issue or a refusal to issue a permit and establishing rules and procedures respecting that appeal.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under this section may adopt by reference, in whole or in part and with any changes the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers necessary, any code, standard or rule, as amended from time to time.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "arterial highway" means any of the following that has not ceased to be an arterial highway under section 45 (1) (b):

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any land that becomes an arterial highway under section 44.1;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any land, improvement or highway that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  is designated as an arterial highway under section 45 (1) (a), or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  becomes an arterial highway under section 56 (2) (a);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authority" means the BC Transportation Financing Authority continued under section 25;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "concession agreement" has the same meaning as in the Transportation Investment Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "concession highway" has the same meaning as in the Transportation Investment Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "concessionaire" has the same meaning as in the Transportation Investment Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "controlled access highway" means a highway designated as a controlled access highway under section 48;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "documented item" means a thing that has been seized under this Act if

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a record of the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia identifies the owner of the thing, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) there is, in the personal property registry or in or on the thing, evidence identifying the owner of the thing or a person who holds an interest in the thing;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "ferry" means any vessel

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) by which individuals or goods may be transported over water, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) that is part of the provincial public highway system,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a ferry to which the Coastal Ferry Act applies, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a ferry that is part of the regional transportation system as defined in the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "furnish" means furnish in accordance with section 82;

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) deposit of a subdivision, reference or explanatory plan in a land title office under section 107 of the Land Title Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a public expenditure to which section 42 applies;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a common law dedication made by the government or any other person;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) declaration, by notice in the Gazette, made before December 24, 1987;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) in the case of a road, colouring, outlining or designating the road on a record in such a way that section 13 or 57 of the Land Act applies to that road;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) an order under section 56 (2) of this Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) any other prescribed means;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "improvement" includes a structure or work;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipal highway" means a highway within a municipality that is not an arterial highway;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipality" means, as applicable,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the corporation into which the residents of an area are incorporated as a municipality under Part 2 of the Local Government Act, under the Vancouver Charter or under any other Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the geographic area of the municipal corporation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "personal property registry" means the registry referred to in section 42 of the Personal Property Security Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "provincial public highway" means any highway that is a rural highway, an arterial highway or a highway referred to in section 35 (2) (f) of the Community Charter;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "provincial public undertaking" means any improvement or other work of public utility that relates to transportation, including, without limitation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) ferries,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a.1) terminals,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a.2) transit systems,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) provincial public highways,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) hydraulic powers created by the construction of highways or works of public utility, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) canals, ditches, drains, drainage, irrigation works and earthworks required for the planning, design, acquisition, holding, construction, use, operation, upgrading, alteration, expansion, extension, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, protection, removal, discontinuance, closure and disposal of highways and public works;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regional district" has the same meaning as in the Local Government Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "rural highway" means a highway that is not within a municipality;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "scenic highway" means a highway designated as a scenic highway under section 54;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "terminal" means the buildings, fixtures, docks, wharves, ramps, landings, approaches, ways, offices and other improvements and facilities, other than land or a ferry, necessary for or incidental to the operation of ferry, shipping and related services;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transit system" means a system for the transportation of passengers and goods and any works or undertakings ancillary to the system, including, without limiting the ancillary works or undertakings,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) links to private or public transportation services, including stops, stands, lanes, loops and parking for buses and taxis,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) parking facilities,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) areas in stations for the provision of services and amenities to passengers,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) employee facilities,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) walkways, overpasses and other means of ingress to and egress from stations and vehicles,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) undertakings for the relocation, enhancement and upgrading of utility services and related poles, wires, pipes and apparatus,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) adjacent roadway enhancements,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) power distribution systems, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) operating facilities and facilities for storage, maintenance and repair of vehicles, parts, signage and related items;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transportation" includes transportation by land, water or air;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "undocumented item" means a thing that has been seized under this Act if

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) there is no record of ownership of the thing in the records of the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) there is no evidence in the personal property registry of the ownership of the thing or of any interest held in the thing, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) there is not, in or on the thing, any evidence of the identity of the owner of the thing or of any person who may have an interest in the thing;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "vehicle" has the same meaning as in the Motor Vehicle Act, and, in Division 3 of Part 5 of this Act, includes a disabled vehicle.

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: 2		  (1) Without limiting any other rights, powers or advantages of the minister under this or any other enactment, the minister may do whatever is or may be necessary to do any or all of the following:

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (a) plan, design, acquire, hold, construct in any manner and in any place the minister considers appropriate, use, operate, upgrade, alter, expand, extend, maintain, repair, rehabilitate, protect, remove, discontinue, close and dispose of provincial public undertakings and related improvements;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (b) acquire, carry on or dispose of any business or commercial or industrial enterprise that relates to transportation;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (c) grant franchises and licences, and enter into agreements, to operate any ferry services on terms and conditions set by the minister, including, without limitation,

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (i)  terms and conditions respecting fares or rates that may be charged for those services, and

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (ii)  authorizing one or more providers of ferry services to charge and retain fares or rates;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (d) make grants and contributions;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (e) enter into arrangements or agreements, including, without limitation, arrangements or agreements for the exchange of information, or for the payment or sharing of the cost of anything related to provincial public undertakings or to transportation, with any person, including, without limitation, any of the following:

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (i)  the government of Canada, the government of a province or territory within Canada or the government of a jurisdiction outside of Canada, or an agent, agency, department or official of any of those governments;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (ii)  a local government body, educational body or health care body, as those terms are defined in the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (iii)  a first nation;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (iv)  any other body prescribed by regulation as a public authority for the purposes of one or more provisions of this Act;

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (f) name and rename provincial public highways.

heading: Rights, powers and advantages of minister
paragraph: (2) If the minister changes the name of a provincial public highway, the minister must publish notice of the change in the prescribed manner.

heading: Power to contract
paragraph: 3		  Without limiting any other power the minister has under this or any other enactment, the minister may enter into contracts for, or otherwise provide for the carrying out of, any activity or service relating to transportation, including, without limitation, the planning, design, acquisition, holding, construction, use, operation, upgrading, alteration, expansion, extension, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, protection, removal, closure and disposition of provincial public undertakings and related improvements.

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph:
4
		  (1) Before awarding a contract to any person in relation to the construction or repair of a provincial public highway, the minister must invite tenders in any manner that will make the invitation for tenders reasonably available to the public.

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (2) The minister need not invite tenders for a project referred to in subsection (1) if

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (a) delay would be injurious to the public interest,

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (b) the project is to be carried out by officers or employees of the government,

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (c) the minister believes that an alternative contracting process will result in a competitively established cost for the project,

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (d) the project must be completed to meet a condition of or other requirement for subdivision approval, whether completion of the project precedes or follows that approval,

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (e) the project must be completed to meet a condition imposed

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (i)  by the minister in relation to an authorization under section 51,

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (ii)  in an agreement referred to in section 52 (2),

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (iii)  by the minister in relation to an approval of a bylaw under section 52, or

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (iv)  by the minister in relation to an approval of a site plan under section 505 of the Local Government Act, or

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (f) the minister is, in relation to the project, relieved from that obligation by order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (3) For each tender received in response to an invitation for tenders under subsection (1), the minister must cause the tender price and the name of the person tendering to be published in any manner set out in the invitation to tender.

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (4) For each contract awarded in the circumstances described in subsection (2) (c), the minister must make available to any person, on request, the name of the person to whom the contract is awarded and the price of the contract.

heading: Competitive processes
paragraph: (5) If, in the case of any project in relation to which the minister must, under subsection (1), invite tenders, the minister believes that it is not expedient to award the project to the lowest tenderer, the minister must report to and obtain the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council before passing by the lowest tender, unless delay would be injurious to the public interest.

heading: Security for performance
paragraph: 5		  (1) If any project referred to in section 4 (1) is to be performed under a contract awarded under this Division,

heading: Security for performance
paragraph: (a) the minister may require that security be provided

heading: Security for performance
paragraph: (i)  to the government, and

heading: Security for performance
paragraph: (ii)  in the form and amount the minister believes will provide reasonable assurance that the project will be completed in the manner and within the time specified in the contract,

heading: Security for performance
paragraph: (b) the contract must be signed by all parties to it before any money is paid, or any work is performed, under the contract, and

heading: Security for performance
paragraph: (c) unless the contract provides otherwise, the security, if any, referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection must be provided before any money is paid, or any work is performed, under the contract.

heading: Security for performance
paragraph: (2) The minister may, at any time, release or surrender all or part of any security provided under subsection (1) (a).

heading: Disputes arising from contracts
paragraph:
6
		  (1) If the minister enters into a contract under section 3, a provision in that contract that stipulates a drawback, penalty or amount of liquidated damages for failing to perform, fulfill or comply with a term, condition, covenant or promise of the contract must not be construed as punitive, but as importing by mutual consent an assessment of the damages that would be caused by the failure.

heading: Disputes arising from contracts
paragraph: (2) If a claim is made under a contract entered into under section 3,

heading: Disputes arising from contracts
paragraph: (a) no compensation is payable to the claimant if the claim is founded on the ground that the cost to the claimant of performing the contract was greater than the contract price, and

heading: Disputes arising from contracts
paragraph: (b) no interest is payable on any money awarded or paid in response to the claim unless the contract in relation to which the claim is made expressly provides for payment of such interest.

heading: Acquisition
paragraph:
7
		  The minister may acquire, hold and maintain land.

heading: Entry
paragraph:
8
		  (1) Without limiting Division 4, the minister may, without consent, for any of the purposes in subsection (2) of this section,

heading: Entry
paragraph: (a) enter, remain on and use land, and

heading: Entry
paragraph: (b) do one or more of the following:

heading: Entry
paragraph: (i)  take possession of or use timber, stone, gravel, sand, clay and other materials on the land;

heading: Entry
paragraph: (ii)  place or store anything on the land;

heading: Entry
paragraph: (iii)  construct temporary roads or improvements;

heading: Entry
paragraph: (iv)  provide, remove or repair access from the land to a provincial public undertaking and, for that purpose, take possession of, use or move anything on the land.

heading: Entry
paragraph: (2) The minister may exercise the rights, powers and advantages granted under subsection (1) to

heading: Entry
paragraph: (a) acquire, hold, construct, use, operate, upgrade, alter, expand, extend, maintain, repair, rehabilitate or protect any improvement or other work of public utility, including, without limitation, improvements or works referred to in paragraphs (a) to (d) of the definition of "provincial public undertaking" in section 1,

heading: Entry
paragraph: (b) remove, discontinue, close or dispose of a provincial public undertaking,

heading: Entry
paragraph: (c) protect any animal, bird, fish or plant species or habitat, or the environment, from the effects of a provincial public undertaking, or

heading: Entry
paragraph: (d) carry out work connected with planning or designing a provincial public undertaking.

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Except as provided in subsection (4), the Expropriation Act does not apply to an entry on land under section 8 of this Act or to any other activity undertaken by the minister under section 8.

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (5) of this section, if any entry or other activity of the minister under section 8 causes any damage, the minister must

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (a) remedy the damage, or

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (b) if the minister chooses not to remedy the damage, pay compensation for the damage.

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (3) If the minister takes possession of or uses any thing under section 8 (1) (b), the minister

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (a) must, subject to subsection (5) of this section, pay compensation for the thing, or

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (b) may pay compensation for the thing, in an amount determined by the minister, if the minister took possession of or used the thing under the authority of this or any other Act or under a reservation, in a Crown grant relating to the land, that provides the right to take possession of or use the thing without compensation.

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (4) If the minister and a person entitled to compensation under subsection (2) (b) or (3) (a) of this section fail to agree on the amount of compensation payable, the amount must be determined by the Supreme Court.

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (5) The minister is not required to pay compensation for any entry onto land under section 8 of this Act, or for any other thing done under section 8, including, without limitation, any activity or taking of possession of or using any thing, if the entry, activity, taking possession or use was to deal with a situation that

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (a) directly interferes with the minister's ability to exercise the rights, powers and advantages granted under this Act, and

heading: Compensation for entry
paragraph: (b) was created or condoned by the owner or occupier of the land.

heading: Expropriation
paragraph: 10		  The minister may expropriate land for any of the purposes in section 8 (2) (a) or (c).

heading: Compensation for expropriation
paragraph:
11
		  If the minister exercises the power under section 10 to expropriate land, the minister must pay compensation as agreed with the owner of the land or, if there is no agreement, in accordance with the Expropriation Act.

heading: Injurious affection
paragraph: 12		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), but despite any other enactment or the common law, no action lies and no proceeding may be brought against the government, the minister or any other person for compensation or damages resulting from injurious affection to land resulting from the exercise of a power provided to, or the performance of a duty imposed on, the minister under this Act or any predecessor Act.

heading: Injurious affection
paragraph: (2) If the minister expropriates part of the land of an owner, subsection (1) does not apply in relation to the minister if and to the extent that injurious affection results to the unexpropriated remainder of that land.

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph:
13
		  (1) The minister may dispose of land.

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1) and despite Part 3, the minister may

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (a) dispose of the whole or any part of a provincial public highway by lease for any purpose, including, without limitation, a commercial purpose, and

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (b) if a provincial public highway is discontinued and closed, dispose of the whole or any part of the land over which the provincial public highway was discontinued and closed.

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (3) If the minister wishes to sell land that is not a provincial public highway, the minister must, in selecting the person to whom the sale is to be made, use a public competitive process unless,

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (a) in the case of a disposition referred to in subsection (2) (b), the disposition is

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (i)  to the authority or the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority,

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (ii)  to a municipality or regional district for consideration determined by the minister,

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (iii)  in exchange for other land, with or without additional consideration, or

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (iv)  to an owner of land adjacent to the land over which the provincial public highway was discontinued and closed, or

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (b) in the case of any other disposition of land, the disposition is one referred to in paragraph (a) (i), (ii) or (iii) of this subsection.

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (4) If the minister wishes to dispose of land that is not a provincial public highway by lease, the minister must, in selecting the person to whom the lease is to be granted, use a public competitive process unless the lease is for at least market rent or is to

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (a) an agency, board or commission of the government,

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (b) the authority or the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority,

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (c) a municipality or regional district,

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (d) a corporation

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (i)  established by an Act of the Legislature of British Columbia or by an Act of the Parliament of Canada, and

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (ii)  of which the majority of shares are owned by the government of British Columbia or the government of Canada, or

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (e) any other person if

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (i)  special circumstances exist, and

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (ii)  the lease arrangements are approved by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Disposition of land
paragraph: (5) The proceeds of every disposition of land referred to in this section must be paid to the government.

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph:
14
		  (1) The minister may furnish a notice under this section in respect of an improvement in either of the following circumstances:

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (a) the minister has entered into an agreement with an owner of land under which the owner agrees to maintain the improvement in accordance with the agreement, and the minister believes that the improvement is not being maintained in accordance with the agreement;

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (b) the minister has attempted to negotiate an agreement referred to in paragraph (a) in relation to the improvement but, in the minister's opinion, it will not be possible to reach such an agreement with the owner within a reasonable time, and the minister believes that the improvement

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (i)  has been constructed by the minister under this or any other enactment,

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (ii)  relates to a provincial public undertaking, and

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (iii)  is primarily for the benefit of the owner.

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (2) If, under subsection (1), the minister furnishes a notice to an owner of land in respect of an improvement on the land, the owner must, at the owner's expense, keep the improvement in good repair.

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (3) A notice under subsection (1) must

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (a) require the owner to keep the improvement in good repair, and

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (b) indicate that, if the improvement is not kept in good repair, the minister may, at the owner's expense, enter the land and carry out any action considered by the minister to be necessary for that purpose.

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (4) The minister may refrain from furnishing a notice under subsection (1) or may revoke a notice furnished under that subsection if the minister believes that the notice obligation would cause undue hardship to the owner.

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (5) If the minister believes that the owner to whom a notice has been furnished under subsection (1) in respect of an improvement has not kept the improvement in good repair, the minister may

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (a) enter the land on which the improvement is located, and

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (b) carry out any repairs or other remedial actions considered by the minister to be appropriate.

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (6) If the minister enters land or performs any remedial actions under subsection (5), the minister may demand, from the owner of the land, payment of

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (a) the expenses incurred as a result of any entry and remedial actions by the minister under subsection (5),

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (b) interest on the amount referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection, and

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (c) the expenses incurred in recovering the amounts referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b).

heading: Owner's responsibility to maintain
paragraph: (7) An amount demanded by the minister from an owner of land under subsection (6) is due, owing and payable by the owner to the minister on the owner's receipt of the demand and, without limiting section 76, may, if the land is outside a municipality, be recovered as delinquent taxes in the same manner as delinquent taxes may be recovered under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act.

heading: Definition
paragraph: 15		  In this Division, "responsible person" means a person to whom a notice is furnished under section 16 (1) that requires the person to take some remedial action.

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph:
16
		  (1) Subject to section 22, the minister may furnish a notice under this section to the owner or occupier of land if the minister believes that there is on the land, whether or not that land is near a provincial public undertaking, equipment or a tree, fence, sign, building, vehicle, device, object or situation that, in the minister's opinion,

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (a) creates a need to act to protect

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (i)  a provincial public undertaking,

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (ii)  any land or improvement related to a provincial public undertaking, or

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (iii)  any thing that is or may be on or near a provincial public undertaking,

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (b) might affect the safety of any person who is or might be on or near

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (i)  a provincial public undertaking, or

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (ii)  any land or improvement related to a provincial public undertaking,

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (c) is causing or might cause the accumulation of snow, water, debris or any other potentially hazardous material on or near a provincial public undertaking or on or near any land or improvement related to a provincial public undertaking, or

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (d) is a nuisance that might distract the operator of a vehicle on or near a provincial public undertaking or impair the operator's ability to drive safely.

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) must

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (a) specify the remedial actions the minister requires,

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (b) specify the time or date on or before which the remedial actions must be completed, and

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (c) indicate that if the specified remedial actions are not completed by the specified time or date, the minister may carry out remedial actions at the expense of the responsible person.

heading: Minister may require remedial action
paragraph: (3) The minister may extend the time for completion of a required remedial action whether or not a previously specified time limit has expired.

heading: Notice to other affected persons
paragraph:
17
		  If a notice is furnished under section 16 (1), a copy of the notice must be sent, by ordinary mail, to the last known address, if any, of

heading: Notice to other affected persons
paragraph: (a) the occupier, if the responsible person is the owner, and

heading: Notice to other affected persons
paragraph: (b) the owner, if the responsible person is the occupier.

heading: Action by minister on failure to comply
paragraph:
18
		  If the remedial actions specified in a notice furnished under section 16 (1) have not been completed by the time or date set in the notice for completion, the minister may

heading: Action by minister on failure to comply
paragraph: (a) subject to section 23, enter any place or premises on the land where the action was required to be taken, and

heading: Action by minister on failure to comply
paragraph: (b) carry out any remedial actions considered by the minister to be appropriate, including, without limitation,

heading: Action by minister on failure to comply
paragraph: (i)  seizing or impounding any thing the minister believes caused or contributed to the situation for which the remedial actions were required,

heading: Action by minister on failure to comply
paragraph: (ii)  constructing, upgrading, altering, expanding, extending, repairing, rehabilitating and removing any improvement as the minister considers necessary, and

heading: Action by minister on failure to comply
paragraph: (iii)  subject to section 19, disposing of any thing seized under subparagraph (i) of this paragraph.

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph:
19
		  (1) A documented item must not be disposed of by the minister under section 18 (b) (iii) unless

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (a) notice in writing is furnished to

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (i)  the person, if any, shown as the current owner of the documented item in the records of the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia, and

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (ii)  any other person who is shown in the personal property registry, or in or on the documented item, as being an owner of the documented item or as having an interest in the documented item, and

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (b) 14 days have elapsed since the date of the notice and no person has, within the 14 days, established ownership, paid the expenses recoverable under subsection (3) of this section and taken custody of the documented item.

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (2) An undocumented item must not be disposed of by the minister under section 18 (b) (iii) unless

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (a) 7 days have elapsed since the seizure, and

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (b) no person has, within the 7 days, established ownership, paid the expenses recoverable under subsection (3) of this section and taken custody of the undocumented item.

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (3) The expenses incurred in entering any land under section 18 (a) and carrying out any remedial actions under section 18 (b), including, without limitation, seizing, removing, impounding or disposing of any thing under section 18 (b), are recoverable by the minister from the responsible person.

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph:
20
		  (1) If the minister gives or sells any thing under section 18 (b) (iii),

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (a) the person to whom the thing is given or sold takes it free and clear of any encumbrances, including, without limitation, any right, title or interest of the person who was its owner before the disposition but excluding any right, title or interest retained by the minister by the disposition, and

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (b) the minister must apply any proceeds realized from that disposition to the expenses recoverable under section 19 (3).

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (2) If, after the proceeds realized from a disposition are applied to the expenses recoverable under section 19 (3), a balance of proceeds remains that is in excess of $10, the minister must,

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (a) if the thing that was disposed of is a documented item, furnish a notice of that balance and of the person to whom, under subparagraph (ii) of this paragraph, that balance is to be paid to every person to whom notice of disposition was furnished under section 19 (1) and

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (i)  pay the balance in accordance with any court order received by the minister within 14 days after the date of the notice under this subsection, or

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (ii)  if no court order is received by the minister within that 14 day period, pay the balance to the person who is shown as the owner of the documented item in the records of the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia or, if no person is shown as the owner in those records, to the person who is shown as the owner of the documented item in the personal property registry or in or on the documented item, or

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (b) if the thing that was disposed of is an undocumented item and no person has, within 14 days after the disposition, satisfied the minister as to that person's ownership of the undocumented item, pay the balance to the administrator under the Unclaimed Property Act.

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (3) Money paid to the administrator under subsection (2) (b) of this section is deemed to be an unclaimed money deposit under the Unclaimed Property Act.

heading: Recovery of expenses
paragraph: 21		  (1) The minister may demand, from the responsible person, payment of

heading: Recovery of expenses
paragraph: (a) the expenses recoverable under section 19 (3) that have not been satisfied under section 20 (1) (b),

heading: Recovery of expenses
paragraph: (b) interest on the amount referred to in paragraph (a) of this subsection, and

heading: Recovery of expenses
paragraph: (c) the expenses incurred in recovering the amounts referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b).

heading: Recovery of expenses
paragraph: (2) An amount demanded by the minister under subsection (1) is due, owing and payable by the responsible person to the minister on the responsible person's receipt of the demand and, without limiting section 76, may, if the responsible person is the owner of the land referred to in section 18 (a) and that land is outside a municipality, be recovered as delinquent taxes in the same manner as delinquent taxes may be recovered under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act.

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: 22		  (1) If the minister believes that the circumstances referred to in section 16 (1) create an urgent need for remedial action, the minister may

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (a) subject to section 23, enter any place or premises on the land without notice to or the consent of the owner or occupier of the land, and

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (b) carry out any remedial actions considered by the minister to be appropriate, including, without limitation,

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (i)  seizing, removing or impounding any thing the minister believes caused or contributed to the situation for which the remedial actions are required,

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (ii)  constructing, upgrading, altering, expanding, extending, repairing, rehabilitating and removing any improvement as the minister considers necessary, and

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (iii)  subject to section 19, disposing of any thing seized under subparagraph (i) of this paragraph.

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3) of this section, section 9 (1) to (4) applies to any entry or activity of the minister under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (3) The minister is not required to pay compensation for any entry onto the land under subsection (1) of this section, or for anything done under subsection (1) in connection with any entry onto the land, including, without limitation, any activity or taking of possession of or using any thing, if the situation that created the urgent need was created or condoned by the owner or occupier of the land.

heading: Minister may act without notice in emergency
paragraph: (4) Sections 19, 20 and 21 apply to any disposition of a thing under subsection (1) (b) (iii) of this section and, for that purpose, a reference to "the responsible person" in those provisions as they apply for the purposes of this section is deemed to be a reference to the owner or occupier of the land.

heading: Search of residence under warrant
paragraph:
23
		  (1) Subject to this section, the power to enter premises under section 18 (a) or 22 (1) (a) must not be used to enter a dwelling occupied as a residence without the consent of the occupier.

heading: Search of residence under warrant
paragraph: (2) Without limiting any other rights, powers or advantages of the minister under this or any other enactment, the minister may, for the purposes referred to in section 18 (b) or 22 (1) (b), as the case may be, enter a dwelling occupied as a residence, without the consent of the occupier, under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (3) of this section.

heading: Search of residence under warrant
paragraph: (3) A justice may issue a warrant authorizing a person named in the warrant and, if appropriate, any peace officer that the named person may call on for assistance to enter a dwelling occupied as a residence in accordance with the warrant, for the purposes referred to in section 18 (b) or 22 (1) (b), if the justice is satisfied by evidence on oath that the entry is required for those purposes.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
24
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "board" means the board of directors of the authority;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "director" means a member of the board.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transit station" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a bus exchange, passenger rail station or prescribed transit facility, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a planned bus exchange, passenger rail station or prescribed transit facility;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transit-oriented development" means a development, including, without limitation, a commercial, industrial, institutional, recreational or residential development, that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) intended to support use of public transit, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) located within the prescribed distance from a transit station.

heading: Authority continued
paragraph:
25
		  (1) The BC Transportation Financing Authority is continued as a corporation consisting of a board of directors made up of the minister and not more than 4 other members appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Authority continued
paragraph: (2) The minister is the chair of the board.

heading: Purpose of the authority
paragraph:
26
		  The purpose of the authority is

heading: Purpose of the authority
paragraph: (a) to, throughout British Columbia, acquire, construct, hold, improve or operate, or cause to be constructed, improved or operated,

heading: Purpose of the authority
paragraph: (i)  transportation infrastructure, other than infrastructure related to municipal highways,

heading: Purpose of the authority
paragraph: (ii)  provincial public undertakings, and

heading: Purpose of the authority
paragraph: (iii)  transit-oriented developments, and

heading: Purpose of the authority
paragraph: (b) to do such other things as the Lieutenant Governor in Council may authorize.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph:
27
		  (1) The authority is an agent of the government.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (2) Subject to this Act and the regulations, the authority has the power and capacity of an individual of full capacity.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (2) but subject to this Part and the regulations, the authority may do one or more of the following for the purposes of this Part:

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (a) acquire, construct, hold, improve or operate, or cause to be constructed, improved or operated,

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (i)  transportation infrastructure,

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (ii)  provincial public undertakings, or

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (iii)  transit-oriented developments;

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (b) acquire or expropriate land;

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (c) hold and maintain land acquired or expropriated under paragraph (b);

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (d) subject to paragraph (d.1), dispose of land acquired or expropriated under paragraph (b);

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (d.1) with the approval of the Minister of Finance, dispose of land by lease for less than market rent;

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (e) with the approval of the Minister of Finance, provide financial assistance by way of grant, contribution, loan or guarantee;

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (f) enter into agreements with the government of Canada, the government of a province or territory within Canada or the government of a jurisdiction outside Canada, or with an agency, department or official of any of those governments;

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (g) create subsidiary corporations to carry out the purposes of the authority;

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (g.1) exercise within a municipality in or through which a transit system is acquired, constructed, held, improved or operated, or caused to be constructed, improved or operated, all the powers that a municipality authorized to lay out, construct and maintain highways may exercise in carrying out that authorization;

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (h) do such other things as the Lieutenant Governor in Council may authorize.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (3.1) The authority has, for the purposes of acquiring, constructing, holding, improving or operating a transit system on a highway in a municipality, or causing the transit system to be constructed, improved or operated,

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (a) all the rights, powers and advantages conferred by any enactment on the municipality with respect to the highway, and

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (b) the right to enjoy and exercise any right of way, easement or licence owned, enjoyed or exercised by the municipality in connection with or for the purposes of its operation of the highway,

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: and the authority may exercise those rights, powers and advantages and enjoy and exercise that right of way, easement or licence in the same manner and to the same extent as the municipality might have done if the highway had not become part of a transit system.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (3.2) If a municipality or proposed operator fails or refuses to enter into an agreement that the authority considers necessary for the purposes of a transit system, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the authority, establish the contents of the agreement and order that the agreement be binding on the parties named in it.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (3.3) Despite any other Act, on the making of an order under subsection (3.2), the persons named in the agreement as parties are bound by that agreement.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (4) The authority has the same immunities in relation to property of the authority as the government has in relation to property of the government.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), but despite any other enactment or law, no action lies and no proceeding may be brought against the authority, the government, the minister or any other person for compensation or damages resulting from injurious affection to land resulting from the exercise of a power provided to, or the performance of a duty imposed on, the authority under this Act or any predecessor Act.

heading: Powers, capacity and immunities
paragraph: (6) If the authority expropriates part of the land of an owner, subsection (5) does not apply in relation to the authority if and to the extent that injurious affection results to the unexpropriated remainder of that land.

heading: Meetings and quorum
paragraph:
28
		  (1) A majority of the directors holding office constitutes a quorum at meetings of the board.

heading: Meetings and quorum
paragraph: (2) Without limiting section 29 (5), the affirmative votes of the majority of the directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present are sufficient to pass a resolution of the board.

heading: Powers of board
paragraph:
29
		  (1) The directors must manage the affairs of the authority or supervise the management of those affairs.

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: (2) The directors may

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: (a) exercise the rights, powers and advantages conferred on them under this Part,

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: (b) exercise the rights, powers and advantages of the authority on behalf of the authority, and

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: (c) delegate the exercise or performance of any right, power, advantage or duty conferred or imposed on them to the chief executive officer of the authority or to a person employed by the authority.

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: (3) The directors may pass the resolutions they consider necessary or advisable for the management and conduct of the affairs of the authority, the exercise of their rights, powers and advantages or the performance of their duties.

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: (4) Without limiting subsection (3), the directors may pass resolutions respecting the procedure to be followed at meetings of the board.

heading: Powers of board
paragraph: (5) A resolution of the board that is approved by directors, whether present in person or approving by telex, telegraph, electronic mail, facsimile, telephone or any other similar means of communication confirmed in writing or other graphic communication, is as valid as if it had been passed at a meeting of the directors properly called and constituted.

heading: Board remuneration
paragraph:
30
		  The authority may pay to a director

heading: Board remuneration
paragraph: (a) an allowance for reasonable travelling and incidental expenses necessarily incurred in carrying out the business of the authority, and

heading: Board remuneration
paragraph: (b) if the director is not a member of the Legislative Assembly or a public servant, remuneration at rates set by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Officers and employees
paragraph:
31
		  (1) The board may appoint a chief executive officer of the authority.

heading: Officers and employees
paragraph: (2) The chief executive officer must carry out those functions and perform those duties that are specified in the resolutions of the board.

heading: Officers and employees
paragraph: (3) The chief executive officer, to the extent authorized by the board, may appoint officers and employees of the authority necessary to carry on the business and operations of the authority and may define their duties and determine their remuneration.

heading: Officers and employees
paragraph: (4) The Public Service Act and the Public Service Labour Relations Act apply to the authority and the officers and employees of the authority.

heading: Benefits
paragraph: 32		  (1) The Public Service Benefit Plan Act applies to the officers and employees of the authority.

heading: Benefits
paragraph: (2) The Public Service Pension Plan, continued under the Public Sector Pension Plans Act, applies to the authority and the officers and employees of the authority.

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: 33		  (1) The authority must

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (a) establish and maintain an accounting system satisfactory to the Minister of Finance, and

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (b) whenever required by that minister, render detailed accounts of its revenues and expenditures for the period or to the day that minister designates.

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (2) All records of the authority must at all times be open for inspection by the Minister of Finance or a person designated by that minister.

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Finance may direct the Comptroller General to examine and report to the Treasury Board on any or all of the financial and accounting operations of the authority.

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (4) Unless the Auditor General is appointed in accordance with the Auditor General Act as the auditor of the authority, the Lieutenant Governor in Council must appoint an auditor to audit the accounts of the authority at least once each year.

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (4.1) The costs of the audit referred to in subsection (4) must be paid by the authority.

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (5) The accounts referred to in subsection (4) must be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.

heading: Financial administration
paragraph: (6) The Minister of Finance is the fiscal agent of the authority.

heading: Revenue from gasoline tax
paragraph: 34		  (1) If a regulation is made under subsection (2), the Minister of Finance must pay to the authority out of the consolidated revenue fund, without an appropriation other than this section, amounts equivalent to the net revenue under section 13 of the Motor Fuel Tax Act in the prescribed area.

heading: Revenue from gasoline tax
paragraph: (2) On request by resolution of the board, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation for the purposes of this Part,

heading: Revenue from gasoline tax
