paragraph: (a) bring into force section 13 of the Motor Fuel Tax Act in a prescribed area of British Columbia, and

heading: Revenue from gasoline tax
paragraph: (b) prescribe the tax to be collected under that section in the prescribed area.

heading: Revenue from additional tax on lease of passenger vehicle
paragraph:
35.1
		  In each calendar month, the Minister of Finance must pay to the authority out of the consolidated revenue fund, without an appropriation other than this section, 1/12 of the amount estimated under section 229.1 (a) of the Provincial Sales Tax Act for the fiscal year that includes the calendar month.

heading: Tolls and charges
paragraph: 36		  (1) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the authority may establish a system of tolls or charges to be paid to the authority in respect of the use of a provincial public highway.

heading: Tolls and charges
paragraph: (2) If a system of tolls or charges has been established by the authority under this section in respect of the use of a provincial public highway, a person must not take or operate a vehicle on the provincial public highway without paying the toll or charge applicable to the vehicle.

heading: Investment powers
paragraph:
37
		  Subject to the approval of the Minister of Finance, the authority may invest or loan any money of the authority that is not otherwise required for the purposes of the authority in investments or loans authorized by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph:
38
		  (1) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council and the Minister of Finance, the authority may borrow the sums of money it considers necessary or advisable for the purpose of carrying out any right, power, advantage or duty conferred or imposed on it under this or any other Act, and may issue securities in relation to that borrowing in the form and on the terms and conditions determined by the Minister of Finance at or before the time the securities are issued.

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (2) By resolution, the board may delegate any of its rights, powers and advantages or the powers of the authority under this section to any director or officer of the authority.

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (3) A recital or declaration in a resolution of the board authorizing the issue of securities, to the effect that the issue of the securities authorized under subsection (1) is being made for the purposes of the authority and that the amount is necessary to realize the net sum required for those purposes, is conclusive evidence of the fact.

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (4) Subject to the approval of the Lieutenant Governor in Council and the Minister of Finance, the authority, on terms it considers necessary or advisable, may

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (a) dispose of securities of the authority, either at par value or at less or more than par value, and

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (b) charge, pledge, hypothecate, deposit or otherwise deal with the securities as collateral security.

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (5) The securities of the authority, other than notes, together with any coupons attached, must bear the signatures of

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (a) the chair and another director or officer, or

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (b) those directors or officers of the authority or officers of the Ministry of Finance as the authority may determine.

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (6) As the fiscal agent of the authority, the Minister of Finance may arrange all details and do, transact and execute all deeds, matters and things that are required during the negotiation of a loan or for the purpose of placing a loan.

heading: Borrowing powers
paragraph: (7) The mechanically reproduced signature of a person authorized under subsection (5) is for all purposes valid and binding on the authority, even if the person whose signature is reproduced has ceased to hold office before the date of the security or before its issue.

heading: Sinking funds
paragraph:
39
		  If required to do so by the Minister of Finance, the authority must, on terms and conditions specified by that minister,

heading: Sinking funds
paragraph: (a) establish one or more sinking fund accounts, or

heading: Sinking funds
paragraph: (b) make other arrangements for the repayment of securities issued by the authority.

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph:
39.1
		  (1) For the purpose of the construction, acquisition or operation of a transit system, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, establish tax exemptions under any or all of the Acts referred to in subsection (5) in respect of land or improvements, or both, or a portion of land or improvements, or both.

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (2) A tax exemption under subsection (1) may be made with respect to land or improvements, or both, or a portion of land or improvements, or both, that is

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (a) described in the order, or

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (b) within a category described in the order.

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), a tax exemption under subsection (1) applies to the extent, for the period and subject to the terms and conditions specified by the Lieutenant Governor in Council.

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (4) A tax exemption under subsection (1) applies only to the extent that the land or improvements, or both, or the portion of land or improvements, or both, is held, used or occupied for the purpose set out in that subsection.

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (5) A tax exemption under subsection (1) may be provided under any or all of the following Acts:

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (a) the Assessment Authority Act;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (b) the Community Charter;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (c) the Hospital District Act;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (d) the Local Government Act;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (e) the Municipal Finance Authority Act;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (f) the Police Act;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (g) the School Act;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (h) the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority Act;

heading: Power to exempt
paragraph: (i) the Vancouver Charter.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph:
41
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), the Business Corporations Act does not apply to the authority.

heading: Application of other Acts
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, declare that certain provisions of the Business Corporations Act apply to the authority.

heading: Travelled roads becoming highways
paragraph: 42		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), if public money is spent on a travelled road that is not a highway, the travelled road is deemed and declared to be a highway.

heading: Travelled roads becoming highways
paragraph:
(2) 
              Subsection (1) does not apply to any road or class of roads, or to any expenditure or class of expenditures, that is prescribed by the regulations.

heading: Dedicated land becoming provincial public highways
paragraph:
43
		  If a person agrees under section 3 (1) of the Expropriation Act or otherwise to dedicate land to the government to become a highway, the minister may, for the purposes of section 107 of the Land Title Act, prepare and deposit with the registrar of the applicable land title office an explanatory plan showing that land as highway, and, in that event,

heading: Dedicated land becoming provincial public highways
paragraph: (a) section 107 (1) (c) and (d) and (3) of the Land Title Act applies, and

heading: Dedicated land becoming provincial public highways
paragraph: (b) the dedicated land becomes a provincial public highway.

heading: Definition
paragraph: 44		  In this Division, "affected municipality", in relation to an arterial highway, means the municipality in which the arterial highway is located.

heading: Arterial highway created on deposit of plan
paragraph:
44.1
		  (1) The deposit in a land title office of a subdivision, reference or explanatory plan that shows land as an arterial highway operates to make that land an arterial highway if the land surveyor who signed the plan certifies on the plan, in the prescribed form, that the land surveyor was authorized by the minister to show that land as an arterial highway.

heading: Arterial highway created on deposit of plan
paragraph: (2) After a plan referred to in subsection (1) is deposited in a land title office, the minister must publish, in the prescribed manner, notice of the deposit of the plan and of the creation of the arterial highway effected by that deposit.

heading: Designation of highways as arterial
paragraph:
45
		  (1) Without limiting section 44.1, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by order, on the recommendation of the minister,

heading: Designation of highways as arterial
paragraph: (a) designate as an arterial highway all or any part of

heading: Designation of highways as arterial
paragraph: (i)  any land or improvement in a municipality that has been expropriated or otherwise acquired by the government,

heading: Designation of highways as arterial
paragraph: (ii)  a municipal highway that has been resumed under section 35 of the Community Charter, or

heading: Designation of highways as arterial
paragraph: (iii)  any land or improvement in a municipality referred to in section 35 (2) (a) to (f) and (j) of the Community Charter, and

heading: Designation of highways as arterial
paragraph: (b) order that all or any part of any land, improvement or highway referred to in the definition of "arterial highway" cease to be an arterial highway.

heading: Designation of highways as arterial
paragraph: (2) After an order is made under subsection (1), the minister must publish notice of the order in the prescribed manner.

heading: Consultation with municipality
paragraph: 46		  Before making a recommendation referred to in section 45 (1) in relation to any land, improvement or highway, the minister must consult with the municipal council of the municipality in which the land, improvement or highway or a part of it is located.

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph:
47
		  In addition to any other rights, powers and advantages held by the minister in relation to an arterial highway under this Act, the minister

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (a) has, and may exercise, in relation to the arterial highway, all of the rights, powers and advantages to plan, design, acquire, hold, construct, use, operate, upgrade, alter, expand, extend, maintain, repair, rehabilitate, protect, remove, discontinue, close and dispose of the arterial highway that,

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (i)  in the case of an arterial highway referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of "arterial highway" in section 1, the affected municipality had before the arterial highway was designated as such under this Act, or

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of any other arterial highway, the affected municipality would have were the highway not an arterial highway,

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (b) has, and may exercise, in relation to any improvement on, under, over or related to the arterial highway, all of the rights, powers and advantages to plan, design, acquire, hold, construct, use, operate, upgrade, alter, expand, extend, maintain, repair, rehabilitate, protect, remove, discontinue, close and dispose of the improvement that,

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (i)  in the case of an arterial highway referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of "arterial highway" in section 1, the affected municipality had before the arterial highway was designated as such under this Act, or

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of any other arterial highway, the affected municipality would have were the highway not an arterial highway,

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (c) has, and may exercise, all of the rights, powers and advantages under any contract relating to the arterial highway or any related improvement that,

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (i)  in the case of an arterial highway referred to in paragraph (b) of the definition of "arterial highway" in section 1, the affected municipality had before the arterial highway was designated as such under this Act, or

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of any other arterial highway, the affected municipality would have were the highway not an arterial highway, and

heading: Minister has municipality's rights, powers and advantages
paragraph: (d) may sue in the name of the minister to enforce any of the rights, powers or advantages referred to in this section.

heading: Controlled access highways
paragraph:
48
		  (1) The minister may, by order,

heading: Controlled access highways
paragraph: (a) designate all or any part of a provincial public highway as a controlled access highway, and

heading: Controlled access highways
paragraph: (b) remove the designation of "controlled access highway" from all or any part of a highway.

heading: Controlled access highways
paragraph: (2) If a provincial public highway designated as a controlled access highway under subsection (1) was, before that designation, a rural highway, an arterial highway or a scenic highway, the provisions of this or any other enactment that apply to rural, arterial or scenic highways, as the case may be, continue to apply to the controlled access highway for so long as it is a rural highway, an arterial highway or a scenic highway.

heading: Controlled access highways
paragraph: (3) After an order is made under subsection (1), the minister must publish notice of the order in the prescribed manner.

heading: Restrictions on access
paragraph:
49
		  (1) A person must not,

heading: Restrictions on access
paragraph: (a) without the authorization of the minister, construct or reopen, or allow the construction or reopening of, any means of access to or from a controlled access highway, or

heading: Restrictions on access
paragraph: (b) obtain access to or from any controlled access highway other than by way of an access point

heading: Restrictions on access
paragraph: (i)  constructed by the minister, or

heading: Restrictions on access
paragraph: (ii)  authorized by the minister under paragraph (a).

heading: Restrictions on access
paragraph: (2) An authorization under subsection (1) must be in writing unless the authorization is provided to a person who is to engage in the authorized activity within the course of the person's employment as a public officer.

heading: Unauthorized access
paragraph:
50
		  (1) If the minister believes that there is a location at or through which unauthorized access to or from a controlled access highway may be obtained, the minister may furnish a notice to the owner or occupier of the land to or from which that access may be obtained requiring the person to seal off the access point in the manner and within the time specified by the minister.

heading: Unauthorized access
paragraph: (2) Division 4 of Part 2 applies to a notice under subsection (1).

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph:
51
		  (1) The minister may, on terms and conditions the minister considers appropriate, provide to a person an authorization to construct or reopen, or allow the construction or reopening of, any means of access to or from a controlled access highway.

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (2) Without limiting other terms and conditions the minister may impose in relation to an authorization under this section, the minister may, as part of the terms and conditions on which an authorization may be provided, do one or more of the following:

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (a) establish the location and form of the authorized access;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (b) require the person to whom the authorization is provided to construct, upgrade, alter, expand, extend, repair, rehabilitate or protect any improvement that the minister considers necessary to facilitate the required access;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (c) establish terms and conditions relating to the planning, design, acquisition, holding, construction, use, operation, upgrading, alteration, expansion, extension, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, protection, removal, discontinuance, closure and disposition of the access, including, without limitation, the standards to which that work is to be completed;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (d) impose limitations on the authorized access;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (e) charge and collect a fee for the authorization in the amount prescribed.

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (3) The minister may amend or terminate an authorization given in relation to a controlled access highway under subsection (1) in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (a) the minister believes that the amendment or termination is necessary to protect the health or safety of a person who is or may be using, or who is near to, a provincial public undertaking;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (b) the minister believes that there is an urgent public need to amend or terminate the authorization;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (c) the minister believes that the amendment or termination is necessary to

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (i)  protect or preserve the integrity of the controlled access highway, or

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (ii)  operate the controlled access highway in the most efficient and effective manner;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (d) the minister believes that the authorization has resulted in an unreasonable impediment to the minister's ability to exercise one or more of the minister's rights, powers or advantages under this Act;

heading: Authorization for constructing or reopening access
paragraph: (e) the holder of the authorization has breached any of the terms and conditions on which the authorization was granted.

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph:
52
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: "controlled area" means, in relation to an intersection of a controlled access highway with any other highway, land and improvements within a radius of 800 metres from the intersection;

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: "zoning bylaw" means

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (a) a zoning bylaw under the Local Government Act, or

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (b) for a community planning area, a zoning bylaw under the Local Services Act.

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (2) The minister may enter into an agreement under this section with the municipality or regional district in which a controlled area is located.

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (3) A zoning bylaw of a municipality or regional district does not apply to a controlled area unless

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (a) the bylaw has been approved in writing by the minister or any person designated in writing by the minister before its adoption, or

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (b) the bylaw is in compliance with the terms of an agreement referred to in subsection (2) between the minister and the municipality or regional district.

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (4) If the minister enters into an agreement referred to in subsection (2) with a municipality or regional district,

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (a) a zoning bylaw is in compliance with that agreement, for the purposes of subsection (3) (b), if and for so long as

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (i)  development within the controlled area complies with a plan that forms part of or is identified in the agreement, and

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (ii)  the municipality or regional district complies with the terms of the agreement, and

heading: Development near controlled access highway
paragraph: (b) a zoning bylaw that is not in compliance with the agreement must be submitted to the minister for approval in writing under subsection (3) (a).

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 53		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "garbage" includes rubbish, ashes, filth, discarded materials and the bodies or parts of vehicles or machinery;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "roadside land" means land within 150 metres of the centre line of a scenic highway.

heading: Designation
paragraph:
54
		  (1) The minister may, by order,

heading: Designation
paragraph: (a) designate a highway or part of a highway as a scenic highway, or

heading: Designation
paragraph: (b) remove the designation of a highway as a scenic highway.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (2) If a scenic highway under subsection (1) is also a rural highway, a controlled access highway or an arterial highway, the provisions of this or any other enactment that apply to rural, controlled access or arterial highways, as the case may be, continue to apply to the scenic highway for so long as it is a rural highway, a controlled access highway or an arterial highway.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (3) After an order is made under subsection (1), the minister must publish notice of the order in the prescribed manner.

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph:
55
		  (1) If satisfied that there is, on roadside land, garbage that is likely to be unsightly or offensive to the public travelling on the scenic highway, the following may furnish to the owner or occupier of the roadside land a notice under this section, requiring the owner or occupier, as the case may be, to remove the garbage or to take such other remedial actions as may be specified in the notice:

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (a) if the roadside land is within a municipality, the municipal council;

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (b) if the roadside land is within a regional district but not within a municipality, the board of the regional district;

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (c) if the roadside land is not within a municipality or a regional district, the minister.

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (2) Division 4 of Part 2 applies to a notice furnished under subsection (1) of this section, and, for that purpose, a reference to "minister" in that Division, as it applies for the purposes of a notice referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (b) of this section, is deemed to be a reference to the applicable municipality or regional district, as the case may be.

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (2),

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (a) Division 14 of Part 7 of the Community Charter applies to an amount recoverable by a municipality under section 21 of this Act as it applies under subsection (2) of this section, and

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (b) section 399 of the Local Government Act applies to an amount recoverable by a regional district under section 21 of this Act as it applies under subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Garbage removal remedial action
paragraph: (4) Nothing in this section limits any other powers of the minister, a municipality or a regional district under this or any other enactment.

heading: Forest service roads
paragraph: 56		  (1) In this section, "forest service road" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Forest Act.

heading: Forest service roads
paragraph: (2) Without limiting any right or power the minister responsible for the administration of the Ministry of Forests and Range Act may have in relation to forest service roads, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, with the consent of the minister and the minister responsible for the administration of the Ministry of Forests and Range Act, order that a forest service road cease to be a forest service road for the purposes of the Forest Act and become, for the purposes of this Act,

heading: Forest service roads
paragraph: (a) if and to the extent it is located in a municipality, an arterial highway, or

heading: Forest service roads
paragraph: (b) in any other case, a rural highway.

heading: Forest service roads
paragraph: (3) Without limiting any right or power the minister may have to close a provincial public highway, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, with the consent of the minister and the minister responsible for the administration of the Ministry of Forests and Range Act, order that a provincial public highway cease to be a provincial public highway and become a forest service road for the purposes of the Forest Act, and, in that event, the provincial public highway is deemed to be closed and discontinued at the time it becomes a forest service road.

heading: Forest service roads
paragraph: (4) Before an order is made under subsection (2) (a) in relation to a forest service road, the minister must consult with the municipal council of the municipality in which the forest service road or a part of it is located.

heading: Soil and freehold of provincial public highways vested in government
paragraph: 57		  Unless otherwise provided for in this Act, the soil and freehold of every provincial public highway is vested in the government.

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph:
58
		  (1) In this section, "provincial public highway" does not include

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (a) a ferry landing,

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (b) a highway on land leased to the government unless that highway is a bridge, or

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (c) a highway that is part of the major road network within the meaning of the South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority Act.

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (5), the authority

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (a) holds all of the government's right and title in and to the soil and freehold of every provincial public highway in British Columbia, and

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (b) acquires all of the government's right and title in and to the soil and freehold of every provincial public highway that comes into being.

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (3) This section does not affect any powers, duties, functions and liabilities, in relation to highways, of the government, the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister or ministry, another minister or ministry or another authority under

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (a) this Act or any other enactment,

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (b) any contract, licence or permit, or

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (c) the law.

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (4) The authority, in relation to a provincial public highway referred to in subsection (2), does not hold, because of subsection (2), any of the powers, duties, functions and liabilities referred to in subsection (3), except for the purpose of accounting for the provincial public highways, and does not have, and has not had, since acquiring the right and title referred to in subsection (2), any of those powers, duties, functions and liabilities except for that purpose.

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (5) The authority may transfer to the government the authority's right and title in and to the soil and freehold of any provincial public highway and, in that event, subsection (2) does not apply to that provincial public highway.

heading: Transfers of highways and other land
paragraph: (6)               Subsection (2) does not operate to constitute the authority as an occupier, within the meaning of the Occupiers Liability Act, of a provincial public highway.

heading: Transfers to Canada
paragraph: 59		  (1) Subject to the terms, reservations and restrictions the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers advisable, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, despite section 58, transfer the administration, control and benefit of any provincial public highway to the government of Canada, in the same manner and with the same effect as if the transfer were a transfer of Crown land under the Land Act, either in perpetuity or for a specified period, and with or without consideration.

heading: Transfers to Canada
paragraph: (2) Except to the extent that it so provides, a transfer under subsection (1) is not subject to section 50 of the Land Act.

heading: Power to close a highway permanently
paragraph: 60		  (1) In this section, "surplus highway" means a provincial public highway or part of a provincial public highway that is not considered necessary in the public interest.

heading: Power to close a highway permanently
paragraph: (2) The minister may discontinue and close a surplus highway by publishing in the prescribed manner a notice in a form, and containing the particulars, the minister considers appropriate.

heading: Power to close a highway permanently
paragraph: (3) If, in the opinion of the minister, no highway that is an alternative to a surplus highway exists or will be provided, the minister must, before publication of the notice referred to in subsection (2), give notice of the intention to discontinue and close the surplus highway by notice published, in a manner and with a frequency prescribed by the regulations, over 4 consecutive weeks.

heading: Power to close a highway permanently
paragraph: (4) A surplus highway to which a notice referred to in subsection (2) is published ceases to be a highway on the date specified in the notice.

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph:
61
		  (1) Without limiting section 60, the minister may close a provincial public highway under this section for any reason, including, without limitation, if the minister believes that the closure is necessary

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: (a) for the planning, design, acquisition, holding, construction, use, operation, upgrading, alteration, expansion, extension, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, protection, removal, discontinuance, closure or disposition of a provincial public undertaking or any related land or improvement,

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: (b) for the protection of the health or safety of a person who is or may be using, or who is near to, the provincial public undertaking or any related land or improvement, or

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: (c) to enable traffic that is allowed to access the provincial public highway to be handled safely and expeditiously.

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: (2) The minister may close a provincial public highway under subsection (1)

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: (a) at a time,

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: (b) for a period of time, and

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: (c) for any or all classes of traffic or use,

heading: Power to close a highway temporarily
paragraph: that the minister considers appropriate.

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph:
62
		  (1) A person must not use or occupy, including do anything to or cause any thing to be constructed or deposited on, a provincial public highway or any land or improvement related to a provincial public highway, unless the person is authorized to do so under this Part, under another enactment, by a lease entered into under section 13 (2) (a) or at law.

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (2) The minister may, on terms and conditions the minister considers appropriate, authorize any person to use or occupy, in any manner and for any purpose, including a commercial purpose, the whole or any part of a provincial public highway, or land or improvements related to a provincial public highway, and, in that event, the person may engage in the authorized activity despite any other provision of this Act.

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (3) Without limiting any other terms and conditions the minister may impose in relation to an authorization under this section, the minister may, as part of the terms and conditions on which an authorization is provided, do one or more of the following:

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (a) establish the period during which the authorization remains effective;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (b) provide for termination of the authorization on the occurrence of an event or condition specified by the minister;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (c) limit, regulate or prohibit access to or entry on the provincial public highway, land or improvement in relation to which the authorization is given;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (d) charge and collect a fee for the authorization in an amount approved by the Lieutenant Governor in Council or, if the authorization is in the nature of a licence, charge not less than a market rent for that licence.

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (4) An authorization under subsection (2) must be in writing unless the authorization is provided to a person who is to engage in the authorized activity within the course of the person's employment as a public officer.

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (5) The minister may amend or terminate an authorization given under subsection (2) in relation to a provincial public highway, land or an improvement in any of the following circumstances:

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (a) the minister believes that the amendment or termination is necessary to protect the health or safety of a person using or near the provincial public highway, land or improvement;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (b) the minister believes that there is an urgent public need to amend or terminate the authorization;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (c) the minister believes that the amendment or termination is necessary to

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (i)  protect and preserve the integrity of the provincial public highway, land or improvement, or

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (ii)  operate the provincial public highway in the most efficient and effective manner;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (d) the minister believes that the authorization has resulted in an unreasonable impediment to the minister's ability to exercise one or more of the minister's rights, powers or advantages under this Act;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (e) the holder of the authorization has breached any of the terms and conditions on which the authorization was granted.

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (6) In addition to the minister's ability to give authorizations under subsection (2), the minister may

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (a) prescribe one or more general authorizations under which all persons or specified classes of persons are authorized to use or occupy one or more of the following:

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (i)  any or all provincial public highways;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (ii)  one or more classes of provincial public highways;

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (iii)  any other land or improvement, or class of land or improvements, related to a provincial public highway, and

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (b) in relation to any authorization prescribed under this subsection, prescribe terms and conditions applicable to that authorization, including, without limitation, terms and conditions respecting the manner in which and the purpose for which the provincial public highway, land or improvement referred to in the regulation may be used or occupied.

heading: Authorization of use or occupation of provincial public highways
paragraph: (7) A person to whom a regulation referred to in subsection (6) applies may use or occupy the provincial public highways, land or improvements to which the regulation applies in the manner and for the purposes provided in the regulation without obtaining an individual authorization from the minister under subsection (2).

heading: Unauthorized use
paragraph:
63
		  (1) The minister may furnish a notice to any person who the minister believes is contravening or has contravened section 62 (1).

heading: Unauthorized use
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1)

heading: Unauthorized use
paragraph: (a) must require the person to stop any contravention the minister believes is ongoing, and

heading: Unauthorized use
paragraph: (b) may require the person to take specified remedial actions.

heading: Unauthorized use
paragraph: (3) If a notice under subsection (1) includes a requirement under subsection (2) (b), Division 4 of Part 2 applies.

heading: Interference with provincial public undertakings
paragraph:
64
		  (1) A person must not

heading: Interference with provincial public undertakings
paragraph: (a) directly or indirectly interfere with or obstruct the planning, design, acquisition, holding, construction, use, operation, upgrading, alteration, expansion, extension, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, protection, removal, discontinuance or closure of a provincial public undertaking, or of any related land or improvement, that is authorized under this Act, another enactment or at law, or

heading: Interference with provincial public undertakings
paragraph: (b) moor or attach a vessel or other floating object to a bridge or other structure that forms part of a provincial public undertaking, other than a terminal.

heading: Interference with provincial public undertakings
paragraph:
(2) 
              Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who does anything referred to in subsection (1) if the thing done is within the course of the person's employment as a public officer.

heading: Minister may furnish notice
paragraph:
65
		  (1) The minister may furnish a notice to any person who the minister believes is contravening or has contravened section 64 (1).

heading: Minister may furnish notice
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) of this section

heading: Minister may furnish notice
paragraph: (a) must require the person to stop any contravention the minister believes is ongoing, and

heading: Minister may furnish notice
paragraph: (b) may require the person to take specified remedial actions.

heading: Minister may furnish notice
paragraph: (3) If a notice under subsection (1) includes a requirement under subsection (2) (b), Division 4 of Part 2 applies.

heading: Extraordinary traffic
paragraph:
66
		  (1) In this section, "extraordinary traffic" includes the carriage of goods or persons over a provincial public highway, whether in vehicles drawn by animal power or propelled by other means, that in conjunction with the nature or existing condition of the provincial public highway is so extraordinary or improper

heading: Extraordinary traffic
paragraph: (a) in the quality or quantity of the goods or the number of persons carried,

heading: Extraordinary traffic
paragraph: (b) in the mode or time of use of the provincial public highway, or

heading: Extraordinary traffic
paragraph: (c) in the speed at which the vehicles are driven or operated,

heading: Extraordinary traffic
paragraph: as, in the opinion of the minister, substantially alters or increases the burden imposed on the provincial public highway through its proper use by ordinary traffic, and causes damage and expense to the provincial public highway beyond what is reasonable or ordinary.

heading: Extraordinary traffic
paragraph: (2) If the minister believes that a provincial public highway is liable to damage through extraordinary traffic, the minister may limit, prohibit or make directions respecting the use of the provincial public highway by a person operating or in charge of the extraordinary traffic or owning the goods carried by it or the vehicles used in it.

heading: Extraordinary traffic
paragraph: (3) Any person to whom this section might otherwise apply may, with the approval of the minister, enter into an agreement for the payment to the government of compensation for the damage or expense that may, in the opinion of the minister, be caused by the extraordinary traffic, and, in that event, the person may use the provincial public highway in the manner contemplated by the agreement despite any limitation, prohibition or direction of the minister under subsection (2) that would otherwise affect that use.

heading: Definition
paragraph:
67
		  In this Division, "seized item" means a vehicle or other thing seized under section 68 (5) or (6).

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph:
68
		  (1) A person must not abandon a vehicle or other thing on a highway.

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (2) If the minister believes that a vehicle or other thing has been abandoned on a provincial public highway, the minister may furnish a notice to the owner or, if known, to any other person who is responsible for abandoning the vehicle or thing on the provincial public highway.

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (3) A notice under subsection (2) must

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (a) require the person to whom it is furnished to remove the vehicle or thing from the provincial public highway,

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (b) specify the time or date before which the vehicle or thing must be removed, and

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (c) indicate that if the removal is not completed by the specified time or date, the minister may effect the removal at the expense of the person to whom the notice was furnished.

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (4) The minister may extend the time for removal whether or not a previously specified time limit has expired.

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (5) The minister may seize a vehicle or thing that the minister believes has been abandoned on a provincial public highway if

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (a) the vehicle or thing is the subject of a notice under subsection (2) and the notice has not been complied with in the time specified, or

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (b) the minister believes that the vehicle or thing has been abandoned for more than 72 hours.

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (6) Without limiting subsection (5), the minister and any member of the provincial police service or a municipal police department may seize any vehicle or thing on a provincial public highway if

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (a) the vehicle interferes with the normal flow of traffic on the provincial public highway,

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (b) the vehicle interferes with the maintenance of the provincial public highway by equipment for that purpose, or

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (c) the vehicle or thing is causing, or might cause, a danger or inconvenience to persons using the provincial public highway.

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph:
69
		  (1) The minister may, in respect of a seized item,

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (a) remove it from the provincial public highway,

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (b) relocate it,

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (c) impound it, or

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (d) subject to subsection (4), dispose of it by sale, destruction or otherwise.

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (2) The expenses incurred in seizing, removing, impounding and disposing of, as the case may be, a seized item, less the proceeds, if any, realized from a disposition of the seized item, are recoverable by the minister from the person who abandoned or left, or authorized the abandonment or leaving, of the seized item.

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (3) In the case of a vehicle seized under section 68 (5) (b) or (6), in the absence of proof to the contrary, the last person whose name appears as owner of the vehicle in the records of the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia is, for the purposes of subsection (2) of this section, deemed to have abandoned or left, or authorized the abandonment or leaving, of the vehicle.

heading: Disposition of seized items
paragraph: (4) Section 19 (1) and (2) applies to a disposition under subsection (1) (d) of this section.

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph:
70
		  (1) If the minister gives or sells any thing under section 69 (1) (d),

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (a) the person to whom the thing is given or sold takes it free and clear of any encumbrances, including, without limitation, any right, title or interest of the person who was its owner before the disposition but excluding any right, title or interest retained by the minister by the disposition, and

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (b) the minister must apply any proceeds realized from that disposition to the expenses recoverable under section 69 (2).

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (2) If, after the proceeds realized from a disposition are applied to the expenses recoverable under section 69 (2), a balance of proceeds remains that is in excess of $10, the minister must,

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (a) if the thing that was disposed of is a documented item, furnish a notice of that balance and of the person to whom, under subparagraph (ii) of this paragraph, that balance is to be paid to every person to whom notice of disposition was furnished under section 19 (1), as it applies for the purposes of section 69, and

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (i)  pay the balance in accordance with any court order received by the minister within 14 days after the date of the notice, or

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (ii)  if no court order is received by the minister within that 14 day period, pay the balance to the person who is shown as the owner of the documented item in the records of the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia or, if no person is shown as the owner in those records, to the person who is shown as the owner of the documented item in the personal property registry or in or on the documented item, or

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (b) if the thing that was disposed of is an undocumented item and no person has, within 14 days after the disposition, satisfied the minister as to that person's ownership of the undocumented item, pay the balance to the administrator under the Unclaimed Property Act.

heading: Proceeds on disposition
paragraph: (3) Money paid to the administrator under subsection (2) (b) of this section is deemed to be an unclaimed money deposit under the Unclaimed Property Act.

heading: Application
paragraph: 71		  (1) Without limiting section 6 (3) of the Transportation Investment Act, this Division applies to a concessionaire unless the concession agreement provides otherwise.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) If a concession highway is also a rural highway, an arterial highway, a controlled access highway or a scenic highway, the provisions of this or any other enactment that apply to rural, arterial, controlled access or scenic highways, as the case may be, continue to apply to the concession highway for so long as it is a rural highway, an arterial highway, a controlled access highway or a scenic highway.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: 72		  (1) A person must not use or occupy, including do anything to or cause any thing to be constructed or deposited on, a concession highway unless the person is authorized to do so under this section or at law.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a person must not cause or allow equipment or a tree, fence, sign, building, vehicle, device, object or situation to exist on land that, in the concessionaire's opinion,

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (a) creates a need to act to protect

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (i)  the concession highway,

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (ii)  any land or improvement related to the concession highway, or

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (iii)  any property that is or may be on or near the concession highway,

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (b) might affect the safety of any person who is or might be on or near

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (i)  the concession highway, or

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (ii)  any land or improvement related to the concession highway,

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (c) is causing or might cause the accumulation of snow, water, debris or any other potentially hazardous material on or near the concession highway or on or near any land or improvement related to the concession highway, or

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (d) is a nuisance that might distract the operator of a vehicle on or near the concession highway or impair the operator's ability to drive safely.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (3) The concessionaire may, if and only to the extent that the concessionaire is expressly allowed to do so by the concession agreement, authorize any person, on terms and conditions the concessionaire considers appropriate, to use or occupy, in any manner and for any purpose, including a commercial purpose, the whole or any part of the concession highway, and, in that event, the person may engage in the authorized activity despite any other provision of this Act.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (4) Section 62 (3), (4) and (5) (a) to (c) and (e) applies to a concession highway and, for that purpose, a reference in those provisions, as they apply for the purposes of this section,

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (a) to "minister" is deemed to be a reference to the concessionaire, and

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (b) to "provincial public highway" is deemed to be a reference to the concession highway.

heading: Interference with concession highways
paragraph:
73
		  
            Section 64 applies to a concession highway and, for that purpose, a reference to "provincial public undertaking" in that provision, as it applies for the purposes of this section, is deemed to be a reference to the concession highway.

heading: Remedial action
paragraph:
74
		  (1) The concessionaire may furnish a notice to any person who the concessionaire believes is contravening or has contravened

heading: Remedial action
paragraph:
(a) 
                section 72, or

heading: Remedial action
paragraph:
(b) 
                section 64 as it applies to a concession highway under section 73.

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) of this section

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (a) must require the person to stop any contravention the concessionaire believes is ongoing, and

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (b) may require the person to take specified remedial actions.

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (3) If the remedial actions specified in a notice furnished under subsection (2) have not been completed by the time or date set in the notice for completion, the concessionaire may,

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (a) if and to the extent that remedial actions may be performed on the concession highway, undertake whichever of those remedial actions the concessionaire considers appropriate, and sections 18 to 21 apply, or

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (b) if and to the extent that remedial actions are required as a result of a breach of section 72 (2), refer the matter to the minister.

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (4) If a matter referred to in subsection (3) is referred to the minister under subsection (3) (b), the minister may

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (a) subject to section 23, as it applies for the purposes of subsection (6) of this section, enter any place or premises on the land where the action was required to be taken, and

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (b) carry out any remedial actions considered by the minister to be appropriate, including, without limitation,

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (i)  seizing or impounding any thing the minister believes caused or contributed to the situation for which the remedial actions were required,

heading: Remedial action

heading: Remedial action

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (5) Sections 18 to 21 apply to any action taken by the concessionaire under subsection (3) (a) and, for that purpose, a reference to "minister" in those provisions, as they apply for the purposes of this section, is deemed to be a reference to the concessionaire.

heading: Remedial action
paragraph: (6) Sections 18 to 23 apply to any action taken by the minister under subsection (4).

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph:
75

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things

heading: Abandoned vehicles and things
paragraph: (b) to "highway" or to "provincial public highway" is deemed to be a reference to the concession highway.

heading: Recovery of money due
paragraph:
76
		  (1) Any money due to or recoverable by the minister under this Act may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of money due
paragraph: (2) The rights, powers and advantages provided to the government under subsection (1) are in addition to any other rights, powers and advantages the government or the minister may have under this or any other enactment or at law to collect the money referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Interest on money due
paragraph:
77
		  Interest on any money due to or recoverable by the minister or the government under this Act is payable and must be calculated

heading: Interest on money due
paragraph: (a) at the rate prescribed under section 20 (1) of the Financial Administration Act, and

heading: Interest on money due
paragraph: (b) in the manner prescribed in the regulations.

heading: Offence Act
paragraph: 78		  Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: Offences
paragraph: 79		  (1) A person commits an offence who

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) contravenes section 36 (2), 49, 62 (1), 64 (1) or 68 (1),

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with a notice furnished to the person under section 16 (1), 50 (1), 55 (1), 63 (1), 65 (1) or 68 (2),

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 In this Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: compliance mark means a symbol, device, sign, label, placard, letter, word, number or abbreviation, or any combination of those things, that is to be displayed on a means of containment used or intended to be used in importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting dangerous goods to indicate compliance with a safety standard that applies under the regulations; (indication de conformite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: dangerous goods means a product, substance or organism included by its nature or by the regulations in any of the classes listed in the schedule; (marchandises dangereuses)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: dangerous goods mark means a symbol, device, sign, label, placard, letter, word, number or abbreviation, or any combination of those things, that is to be displayed to indicate the presence or nature of danger on dangerous goods, or on a means of containment or means of transport used in importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting dangerous goods; (indication de marchandises dangereuses)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: handling means loading, unloading, packing or unpacking dangerous goods in a means of containment for the purposes of, in the course of or following transportation and includes storing them in the course of transportation; (manutention)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inspector means a person designated as an inspector under subsection 10(1); (inspecteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: means of containment means a container or packaging, or any part of a means of transport that is or can be used to contain goods; (contenant)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: means of transport means a road or railway vehicle, aircraft, vessel, pipeline or any other contrivance that is or can be used to transport persons or goods; (moyen de transport)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means the Minister of Transport; (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: organization has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Criminal Code; (organisation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: person means an individual or an organization; (personne)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed means prescribed by regulations of the Governor in Council; (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: public safety means the safety of human life and health and of property and the environment; (securite publique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: release means, in relation to dangerous goods,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a discharge, emission, explosion, outgassing or other escape of dangerous goods, or any component or compound evolving from dangerous goods, from a means of containment being used to handle or transport the dangerous goods, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) an emission, from a means of containment being used to handle or transport dangerous goods, of ionizing radiation that exceeds a level or limit established under the Nuclear Safety and Control Act; (rejet)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: safety mark means a dangerous goods mark or a compliance mark; (indication de securite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: safety requirement means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a requirement for persons engaged in importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting dangerous goods,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a requirement for persons engaged in designing, manufacturing, repairing, testing or equipping a means of containment used or intended to be used in importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting dangerous goods, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a requirement for reporting by persons referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b) or a requirement for their training or registration; (regle de securite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: safety standard means a standard for a means of containment used or intended to be used in importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting dangerous goods, including standards for the means of containment's design, manufacture, repair, testing, equipping, functioning, use or performance; (norme de securite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: security requirement means a requirement for persons engaged in importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting dangerous goods established under regulations made under section 27.1; (regle de surete)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: shipping record means a record that relates to dangerous goods being imported, offered for transport, handled or transported and that describes or contains information relating to the goods, and includes electronic records of information; (registre d'expedition)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: standardized means of containment means a means of containment to which a safety standard applies under the regulations; (contenant normalise)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vessel has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. (batiment)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 2.1 For the purposes of this Act, a person who is named in a shipping record accompanying dangerous goods or a means of containment on entry into Canada as the person in Canada to whom the dangerous goods or the means of containment is to be delivered is deemed to be importing the dangerous goods or means of containment.

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 3 (1) This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) In addition to its application in Canada, this Act applies to vessels and aircraft outside Canada that are registered in Canada.

heading: Exceptions - regulations and certificates
paragraph: (3) This Act does not apply to the extent that its application is excluded by a regulation made under paragraph 27(1)(e) or by a certificate issued under section 31.

heading: Other exceptions
paragraph: (4) This Act does not apply in relation to

heading: Other exceptions
paragraph: (a) any activity or thing under the sole direction or control of the Minister of National Defence, including in circumstances in which the regulations provide that it is under that Minister's sole direction or control;

heading: Other exceptions
paragraph: (b) commodities transported by a pipeline governed by the Canadian Energy Regulator Act, the Canada Oil and Gas Operations Act or the law of a province; or

heading: Other exceptions
paragraph: (c) dangerous goods confined only by the permanent structure of a vessel.

heading: Agreement with provinces
paragraph: 4 (1) The Minister may

heading: Agreement with provinces
paragraph: (a) with the approval of the Governor in Council, enter into an agreement with one or more provincial governments with respect to the administration of this Act; and

heading: Agreement with provinces
paragraph: (b) subject to such terms and conditions as the Governor in Council may specify in the approval, agree to amendments to the agreement.

heading: Publication
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall make the agreement public.

heading: General prohibition
paragraph: 5 No person shall import, offer for transport, handle or transport any dangerous goods unless

heading: General prohibition
paragraph: (a) the person complies with all safety requirements and security requirements that apply under the regulations;

heading: General prohibition
paragraph: (b) the goods are accompanied by all documents that are required under the regulations;

heading: General prohibition
paragraph: (c) a means of containment is used for the goods that is required or permitted under the regulations; and

heading: General prohibition
paragraph: (d) the means of containment and means of transport comply with all safety standards that apply under the regulations and display all applicable safety marks in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Prohibition - means of containment
paragraph: 5.1 No person shall design, manufacture, repair, test or equip a means of containment used or intended to be used in importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting dangerous goods unless the person complies with all safety requirements that apply under the regulations.

heading: Prohibition - compliance mark
paragraph: 6 No person shall affix or display on a means of containment a compliance mark that is required or permitted under the regulations - or another mark that is likely to be mistaken for such a mark - in respect of the manufacture, repair or testing of the means of containment, unless the manufacture, repair or testing was done in compliance with all safety requirements and safety standards applicable to that compliance mark.

heading: Prohibition - dangerous goods mark
paragraph: 6.1 No person shall affix or display on dangerous goods, a means of containment or a means of transport a dangerous goods mark that is required or permitted under the regulations - or another mark that is likely to be mistaken for such a mark - if the mark is misleading as to the presence of danger or the nature of any danger.

heading: Emergency response assistance plan
paragraph: 7 (1) No person shall import, offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods in a quantity or concentration that is specified by regulation - or that is within a range of quantities or concentrations that is specified by regulation - unless the person has an emergency response assistance plan that is approved under this section before

heading: Emergency response assistance plan
paragraph: (a) importing the dangerous goods;

heading: Emergency response assistance plan
paragraph: (b) offering the dangerous goods for transport; or

heading: Emergency response assistance plan
paragraph: (c) handling or transporting the dangerous goods, in the case where no other person is required to have an emergency response assistance plan under paragraph (a) or (b) in respect of that handling or transporting.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The plan shall outline what is to be done to respond to an actual or anticipated release of the dangerous goods in the course of their handling or transporting that endangers, or could endanger, public safety.

heading: Approval
paragraph: (3) The Minister may approve the plan for a specified period, if the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that it can be implemented and will be effective in responding to such a release.

heading: Interim approval
paragraph: (4) The Minister may grant an interim approval of the plan for a specified period before finishing the investigation of the matters to be considered under subsection (3) if the Minister has no reason to suspect that the plan cannot be implemented or will be ineffective in responding to such a release.

heading: Revocation of approval
paragraph: (5) The Minister may revoke an approval of an emergency response assistance plan if

heading: Revocation of approval
paragraph: (a) in the case of an interim approval, the Minister subsequently believes on reasonable grounds that the plan cannot be implemented or will be ineffective in responding to such a release;

heading: Revocation of approval
paragraph: (b) the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that the plan can no longer be implemented or will no longer be effective in responding to such a release;

heading: Revocation of approval
paragraph: (c) the Minister has requested changes to the plan that the Minister believes on reasonable grounds are needed to make it effective in responding to such a release and the changes have not been made within a reasonable time or have been refused;

heading: Revocation of approval
paragraph: (d) the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that there has been a release of dangerous goods to which the plan applies - or that such a release has been anticipated - and that the plan was not used to respond to the actual or anticipated release; or

heading: Revocation of approval
paragraph: (e) a direction made in respect of the plan under paragraph 7.1(a) has not been complied with.

heading: Direction and permission
paragraph: 7.1 The Minister may, if the Minister believes that doing so is necessary for the protection of public safety,

heading: Direction and permission
paragraph: (a) direct a person with an approved emergency response assistance plan to implement the plan, within a reasonable time as specified in the direction, in order to respond to an actual or anticipated release of dangerous goods to which the plan applies; or

heading: Direction and permission
paragraph: (b) authorize a person with an approved emergency response assistance plan to implement the plan in order to respond to an actual or anticipated release of dangerous goods if the Minister does not know the identity of any person required under subsection 7(1) to have an emergency response assistance plan in respect of the release.

heading: Compensation
paragraph: 7.2 (1) The Minister shall compensate, in accordance with the regulations, any person who is authorized to implement an approved emergency response assistance plan under paragraph 7.1(b) for expenses authorized to be compensated under the regulations that are incurred by that person as a result of implementing the plan.

heading: Payment out of C.R.F.
paragraph: (2) The compensation shall be paid out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

heading: Security plan
paragraph: 7.3 (1) No prescribed person shall import, offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods in a quantity or concentration that is specified by regulation - or that is within a range of quantities or concentrations that is specified by regulation - before the person has undergone security training in accordance with the regulations, has a security plan that meets the requirements of subsection (2) and has implemented the plan in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Contents
paragraph: (2) The plan shall, in accordance with the regulations, set out measures to prevent the dangerous goods from being stolen or otherwise unlawfully interfered with in the course of the importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting.

heading: Improper means of containment
paragraph: 8 No person shall sell, offer for sale, deliver, distribute, import or use a standardized means of containment unless it displays all applicable safety marks in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Supply records
paragraph: 9 (1) A manufacturer or importer of standardized means of containment shall keep records of the persons to whom the manufacturer or importer supplies the means of containment.

heading: Notice of defective construction or recall
paragraph: (2) If the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that any standardized means of containment is unsafe as supplied by the manufacturer or as imported for handling or transporting dangerous goods, the Minister may direct the manufacturer or importer to issue a notice of defective construction or recall to the person to whom it was supplied.

heading: Notice of defective repair or defective testing
paragraph: (3) The Minister may direct a person who repaired or tested a standardized means of containment to issue a notice of defective repair or defective testing, as the case may be, to the person for whom it was repaired or tested, or to publish the notice in a manner such that the notice is likely to come to that person's attention, if the Minister believes on reasonable grounds that the person who repaired or tested the standardized means of containment

heading: Notice of defective repair or defective testing
paragraph: (a) failed to comply with an applicable safety requirement or safety standard; and

heading: Notice of defective repair or defective testing
paragraph: (b) affixed to the standardized means of containment - or did not remove from it - the safety mark that indicates that the safety requirement or safety standard had been complied with.

heading: Designation of inspectors
paragraph: 10 (1) The Minister may designate persons or classes of persons whom the Minister considers qualified to act as inspectors for any of the purposes of this Act, and may revoke such a designation.

heading: Certificate of designation
paragraph: (2) The Minister shall give every inspector a certificate of designation showing the matters in respect of which the inspector is designated, including the purposes, classes of dangerous goods, means of containment, means of transport and places for which the inspector is designated.

heading: Certificate to be shown
paragraph: (3) On entering any place or inspecting anything, an inspector shall show the certificate to the person in charge of the place or thing if the person requests proof of the inspector's designation.

heading: Obstruction of inspectors
paragraph: 13 (1) When an inspector is exercising powers or carrying out duties and functions under this Act, no person shall

heading: Obstruction of inspectors
paragraph: (a) fail to comply with any reasonable request of the inspector;

heading: Obstruction of inspectors
paragraph: (b) knowingly make any false or misleading statement either orally or in writing to the inspector;

heading: Obstruction of inspectors
paragraph: (c) except with the authority of the inspector, remove, alter or interfere in any way with anything detained or removed by or under the direction of the inspector; or

heading: Obstruction of inspectors
paragraph: (d) otherwise obstruct or hinder the inspector.

heading: Obstruction of qualified person
paragraph: (2) When a qualified person is exercising powers under subsection 15(3), no person shall

heading: Obstruction of qualified person
paragraph: (a) fail to comply with any reasonable request of the qualified person;

heading: Obstruction of qualified person
paragraph: (b) knowingly make any false or misleading statement either orally or in writing to the qualified person; or

heading: Obstruction of qualified person
paragraph: (c) otherwise obstruct or hinder the qualified person.

heading: Financial responsibility
paragraph: 14 (1) No person shall import, offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods, or manufacture or import standardized means of containment, unless the person is financially responsible in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Proof of financial responsibility
paragraph: (2) A person who carries on any of those activities shall provide to an inspector on request the proof that is required under the regulations of financial responsibility.

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply to Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province or to the entities named in Schedules II and III to the Financial Administration Act.

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: 15 (1) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this Act, an inspector may, subject to section 16 but at any reasonable time, stop any means of transport for which the inspector is designated and enter and inspect any place, or any such means of transport, if the inspector believes on reasonable grounds that in or on the place or means of transport there are

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (a) dangerous goods being offered for transport, handled or transported;

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (b) means of containment being manufactured, repaired or tested on which a compliance mark is displayed or will be affixed;

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (c) standardized means of containment;

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (d) books, shipping records, emergency response assistance plans, security plans or other documents that contain any information relevant to the purposes of this Act; or

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (e) computer systems, data processing systems or any other electronic devices or media that contain information relevant to the purposes of this Act, or that have such information available to them.

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (2) In the course of carrying out an inspection under subsection (1), an inspector may

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (a) open and inspect, or request the opening and inspection of, any means of containment for which the inspector is designated, including any closures, valves, safety release devices or other appurtenances that are essential to the use of the means of containment to contain dangerous goods, if the inspector believes on reasonable grounds that it is being used to handle or transport dangerous goods or to contain dangerous goods offered for transport;

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (b) open and inspect, or request the opening and inspection of, any means of containment described in paragraph (1)(b) or (c), including any closures, valves, safety release devices or other appurtenances that are essential to the use of the means of containment to contain dangerous goods;

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (c) for the purpose of analysis, take, or request the taking of, a reasonable quantity of anything the inspector believes on reasonable grounds to be dangerous goods;

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (d) examine, or request the examining of, information described in paragraph (1)(d) or (e) that the inspector believes on reasonable grounds is relevant to the purposes of this Act and make, or request the making of, copies of any of it; and

heading: Powers of inspector
paragraph: (e) ask questions of any person for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Authorized person
paragraph: (3) An inspector may, in accordance with the regulations, authorize any qualified person to enter any place or means of transport that the inspector may enter under subsection (1) and to exercise any of the powers set out in subsection (2).

heading: Warrant required to enter dwelling-place
paragraph: 16 (1) An inspector may not enter a dwelling-place except with the consent of the occupant or under the authority of a warrant.

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (2) Where on ex parte application a justice, as defined in section 2 of the Criminal Code, is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) the conditions for entry described in section 15 exist in relation to a dwelling-place,

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) entry is necessary for the purposes of this Act, and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (c) entry has been refused or there are reasonable grounds for believing that entry will be refused,

heading: Authority to issue warrant
