heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1.4 The following definitions apply in these Regulations.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Act means the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992. (Loi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: adsorbed gas means a gas that when packaged for transport is adsorbed onto a solid porous material resulting in an internal receptacle pressure of less than 101.3 kPa at 20°C and less than 300 kPa at 50°C. (gaz adsorbe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aerosol container means an article consisting of any non-refillable means of containment that contains a substance under pressure and that is fitted with a self-closing device that allows the contents to be ejected as

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) solid or liquid particles in suspension in a gas;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a foam, paste or powder; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a liquid or gas. (bombe aerosol)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: aircraft means any machine capable of deriving support in the atmosphere from reactions of the air, other than a machine designed to derive support in the atmosphere from reactions against the earth's surface of air expelled from the machine, and includes a rocket. (aeronef)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: biological product means a product that is derived from living organisms and that is used to prevent, treat or diagnose disease in humans or animals or for development, experiment or investigation purposes and includes finished or unfinished products, live vaccines or attenuated live vaccines. (produit biologique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: CANUTEC means the Canadian Transport Emergency Centre of the Department of Transport. (CANUTEC)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: capacity means, for a means of containment used to contain

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a liquid or a gas, the maximum volume of water, normally expressed in litres, that the means of containment can hold at 15°C and at an absolute pressure of 101.325 kPa; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) dangerous goods other than a liquid or a gas, the maximum volume, normally expressed in cubic metres, that the means of containment can hold. (capacite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: cargo aircraft means an aircraft, other than a passenger carrying aircraft, that is carrying goods or property. (aeronef cargo)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: carrier means a person who, whether or not for hire or reward, has possession of dangerous goods while they are in transport. (transporteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Category A means an infectious substance that is transported in a form such that, when it is released outside of its means of containment and there is physical contact with humans or animals, it is capable of causing permanent disability or life-threatening or fatal disease to humans or animals. (categorie A)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Category B means an infectious substance that does not meet the criteria for inclusion in Category A. (categorie B)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: class means, when the word "class" is followed by

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) one digit, the class of dangerous goods listed in the schedule to the Act; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) two digits separated by a point, the class of dangerous goods listed in the schedule to the Act and its division. (classe)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: classification means, for dangerous goods, as applicable, the shipping name, the primary class, the compatibility group, the subsidiary class, the UN number, the packing group, and the infectious substance category. (classification)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: compatibility group means one of the 13 groups of explosives described in Appendix 2 of Part 2 (Classification). (groupe de compatibilite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: consignment means a quantity of dangerous goods transported at the same time in one or more means of containment from one consignor at one location to one consignee at another location. (envoi)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: consignor means a person in Canada who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is named in a shipping document as the consignor;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) imports or who will import dangerous goods into Canada; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) if paragraphs (a) and (b) do not apply, has possession of dangerous goods immediately before they are in transport. (expediteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: consolidation bin means a bin that is used in a road vehicle

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) to secure one or more small means of containment so that, under normal conditions of transport, they will not shift in a way that might compromise their integrity; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) to allow small means of containment to be added or removed during transport. (conteneur de groupage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: culture means the result of a process by which pathogens in a specimen are intentionally propagated. This definition does not include specimens taken from a human or animal patient and that are intended to be processed in a laboratory. (culture)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: cylinder means a small means of containment, other than an aerosol container, that is cylindrical or spherical in shape and that is capable of withstanding an internal absolute pressure of 275 kPa. (bouteille a gaz)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: drum means a flat-ended or convex-ended cylindrical means of containment made of metal, fibreboard, plastic or other similar material, with a maximum capacity of 450 L, or for a drum made of plywood, a maximum capacity of 250 L. This definition includes means of containment of other shapes such as pail-shaped or round with a tapered neck, but does not include a wood barrel or jerrican (that is, a means of containment of rectangular or polygonal cross-section). (fut)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: dust means a mixture of solid particles and air in which 90% or more of the solid particles have a diameter less than or equal to 10 µm. (poussiere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: emergency means an immediate danger to public safety

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) requiring the use of dangerous goods to avert or mitigate the danger; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) arising directly or indirectly from dangerous goods. (urgence)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: employer means a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) employs one or more individuals; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) provides the services of one or more individuals and from whom the individuals receive their remuneration. (employeur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ERAP means an emergency response assistance plan. (PIU)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: farmer means a person engaged in farming in Canada for commercial purposes. (agriculteur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: farming means the production of field-grown crops, cultivated and uncultivated and horticultural crops, the raising of livestock, poultry and fur-bearing animals, the production of eggs, milk, honey, maple syrup, tobacco, fibre and fodder crops, but does not include aquaculture. (agriculture)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fire point means the lowest temperature at which a substance will ignite and will continue to burn for at least 5 seconds. (point d'inflammation)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: flash point means the lowest temperature at which the application of an ignition source causes the vapours of a liquid to ignite near the surface of the liquid or within a test vessel. (point d'eclair)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fuel cell means an electrochemical device that converts the chemical energy of a fuel to electrical energy, heat and reaction products. (pile a combustible)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fuel cell cartridge means an article that stores fuel for discharge into a fuel cell through one or more valves that control the discharge of the fuel into the fuel cell. (cartouche pour pile a combustible)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: fuel cell engine means a device that is used to power equipment and that consists of a fuel cell and its fuel supply, whether integrated with or separate from the fuel cell, and includes all appurtenances necessary to fulfil its function. (moteur pile a combustible)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: gas means a substance that at 50°C has a vapour pressure greater than 300 kPa or that is completely gaseous at 20°C at an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa and that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) compressed (other than in solution) so that when it is packaged under pressure for transport it remains entirely gaseous at 20°C;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) liquefied so that when it is packaged for transport it is partially liquid at 20°C;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) refrigerated so that when it is packaged for transport it is made partially liquid because of its low temperature; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) in solution so that when it is packaged for transport it is dissolved in a solvent. (gaz)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: gross mass means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) for a means of containment, the mass of the means of containment and all of its contents; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for a quantity of dangerous goods, the gross mass of all minimum required means of containment used to contain the dangerous goods. (masse brute)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: infectious substance means a substance known or reasonably believed to contain viable micro-organisms such as bacteria, viruses, rickettsia, parasites, fungi and other agents such as prions that are known or reasonably believed to cause disease in humans or animals and that are listed in Appendix 3 to Part 2 (Classification) or that exhibit characteristics similar to a substance listed in Appendix 3. (matiere infectieuse)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: inland voyage has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations. (voyage en eaux internes)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: in standard means that a means of containment meets the requirements set out in section 5.2 of Part 5 (Means of Containment). (en regle)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: in transport means that a person has possession of dangerous goods for the purposes of transportation or for the purposes of storing them in the course of transportation. (en transport)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: large means of containment means a means of containment with a capacity greater than 450 L. (grand contenant)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: LC50 means the lowest concentration of gas, vapour, mist or dust that, when administered by continuous inhalation to both male and female young adult albino rats for one hour, results in the death within 14 days of one half of the animals. (CL50)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: LD50 (dermal) means the lowest amount of a substance that, when administered by continuous contact with the bare skin of both male and female young adult albino rabbits for 24 hours, results in the death within 14 days of one half of the animals. (DL50 (absorption cutanee))

heading: Definitions
paragraph: LD50 (oral) means the lowest amount of a substance that, when administered by mouth to both male and female young adult albino rats, results in the death within 14 days of one half of the animals. (DL50 (ingestion))

heading: Definitions
paragraph: liquid means a substance that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) has a melting point less than or equal to 20°C at an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is a viscous substance for which a specific melting point cannot be determined but that is determined to be a liquid in accordance with ASTM D 4359. (liquide)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: lithium content means the mass of lithium in the anode of a lithium metal or lithium alloy cell. (quantite de lithium)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: mist means a mixture of liquid particles and air in which 90% or more of the liquid particles have a diameter not greater than 10 µm. (brouillard)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: net explosives quantity means the net mass of explosives, excluding the mass of any means of containment. (quantite nette d'explosifs)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: neutron radiation detector means a device that detects neutron radiation and includes a device in which a gas may be contained in a hermetically sealed electron tube transducer that converts neutron radiation into a measureable electric signal. (detecteur de rayonnement neutronique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: offer for transport means, for dangerous goods not in transport, to select or allow the selection of a carrier to transport the dangerous goods, to prepare or allow the preparation of the dangerous goods so that a carrier can take possession of them for transport or to allow a carrier to take possession of the dangerous goods for transport. (demande de transport)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: overpack means an enclosure that is used by a single consignor to consolidate one or more small means of containment for ease of handling but that is not a minimum required means of containment. This definition does not include a large means of containment or a unit load device, as defined in the ICAO Technical Instructions, that is intended for transport by aircraft. (suremballage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: packing group means a group in which dangerous goods are included based on the inherent danger of the dangerous goods; Packing Group I indicates great danger, Packing Group II indicates medium danger and Packing Group III indicates minor danger. (groupe d'emballage)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: passenger means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) for a vessel, a passenger within the meaning of section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001; and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or an aircraft, a person carried on board the means of transport but does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) a crew member,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) a person who is accompanying dangerous goods or other cargo,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii) an operator, owner or charterer of the means of transport,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iv) an employee of the operator, owner or charterer of the means of transport, who is acting in the course of employment, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (v) a person carrying out inspection or investigation duties under an Act of Parliament or of a provincial legislature. (passager)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: passenger carrying aircraft means an aircraft that is carrying one or more passengers. (aeronef de passagers)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: passenger carrying railway vehicle means a railway vehicle that is carrying one or more passengers. (vehicule ferroviaire de passagers)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: passenger carrying road vehicle means a road vehicle that is carrying one or more passengers. (vehicule routier de passagers)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: passenger carrying vessel means a vessel that is carrying one or more passengers. (batiment a passagers)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: primary class means the first class shown in column 3 of Schedule 1. (classe primaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: protective direction means a direction issued under section 32 of the Act to cease an activity or to conduct other activities to reduce any danger to public safety. (ordre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: radiation detection system means an apparatus that contains a radiation detector as a component. (systeme de detection des rayonnements)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: railway vehicle means any vehicle that is designed to be drawn or propelled on rails by any power other than muscle power and that is being prepared for use or being used on rails. (vehicule ferroviaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: residue means the dangerous goods remaining in a means of containment after its contents have been emptied to the maximum extent feasible and before the means of containment is either refilled or cleaned of dangerous goods and purged to remove any vapours. (residu)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: road vehicle means any vehicle that is designed to be drawn or propelled on land, including on ice roads, by any power other than muscle power and includes a machine designed to derive support in the atmosphere from reactions against the earth's surface of air expelled from the machine, but does not include a railway vehicle that operates exclusively on rails. (vehicule routier)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: ro-ro ship has the same meaning as in section 1.2.1 of the IMDG Code. (navire roulier)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sheltered waters voyage has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations. (voyage en eaux abritees)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: shipping document means a document that relates to dangerous goods that are being offered for transport, handled or transported and that contains the information required by Part 3 relating to the goods but does not include an electronic record. (document d'expedition)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: shipping name means an entry in upper case letters (capitals) in column 2 of Schedule 1, but does not include any lower case descriptive text except for the purpose of determining the classification of dangerous goods. (appellation reglementaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: small means of containment means a means of containment with a capacity less than or equal to 450 L. (petit contenant)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: solid means a substance that is not a liquid or a gas. (solide)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: special provision means an item of Schedule 2 referred to in column 5 of Schedule 1. (disposition particuliere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: subsidiary class means a class shown in parentheses in column 3 of Schedule 1. (classe subsidiaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: substance includes an article. (matiere)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: technical name means the chemical name or another name currently used in a scientific or technical handbook, journal or text but does not include a trade name. (appellation technique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: train means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a train, as defined in the Canadian Rail Operating Rules, published by The Railway Association of Canada and approved by the Minister under the Railway Safety Act on January 16, 1990, as amended to July 1, 2000; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a number of railway vehicles coupled together moving at a velocity exceeding 24 km/h (15 mph) with at least one railway vehicle providing propulsion and at least one railway vehicle containing dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be displayed in accordance with Part 4. (train)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: transport index has the same meaning as determined under the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015. (indice de transport)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: tube means a large means of containment that is cylindrical in shape and that is capable of withstanding an internal absolute pressure of 12.4 MPa. (tube)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Type P620 means of containment means a means of containment that is in compliance with the requirements of CGSB-43.125 for Type P620 packaging or, if it is manufactured outside Canada, is in compliance with the requirements of Chapter 6.3 and Packing Instruction P620 of the UN Recommendations and the national regulations of the country of manufacture. (contenant de type P620)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Type P650 means of containment means a means of containment that is in compliance with the requirements of CGSB-43.125 for Type P650 packaging or, if it is manufactured outside Canada, is in compliance with the requirements of Packing Instruction P650 of the UN Recommendations and the national regulations of the country of manufacture. (contenant de type P650)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: UN number means an entry in column 1 of Schedule 1. (numero UN)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: UN standardized means of containment means a means of containment that meets the requirements set out in section 5.6 of Part 5 (Means of Containment). (contenant normalise UN)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vapour means the dispersion in air of imperceptible particles of a substance that is liquid or solid in its normal state. (vapeur)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: watt-hour or Wh the electrical energy developed by a power of 1 watt (W) during 1 hour (h) and expressed as watt-hour (Wh). (wattheure ou Wh)

heading: Applicability of the Regulations
paragraph: 1.5 Unless otherwise stated in sections 1.15 to 1.48 of this Part or in Schedule 1 or 2, dangerous goods must be handled, offered for transport or transported in accordance with these Regulations.

heading: Schedule 2: Special Provisions
paragraph: 1.5.1 (1) When there is a special provision in Schedule 2 for dangerous goods, that special provision applies.

heading: Schedule 2: Special Provisions
paragraph: (2) When there is a conflict between a special provision in Schedule 2 and other provisions in these Regulations, the special provision applies.

heading: Schedule 2: Special Provisions
paragraph: (3) The UN numbers set out in italics after a special provision of Schedule 2 indicate the dangerous goods in respect of which the special provision applies. They are for information only and are not part of the Regulations.

heading: Schedules 1 and 3: Forbidden Dangerous Goods
paragraph: 1.5.2 (1) When the word "Forbidden" is shown for dangerous goods in column 3 of Schedule 1 or column 2 of Schedule 3, a person must not handle, offer for transport or transport the dangerous goods.

heading: Schedules 1 and 3: Forbidden Dangerous Goods
paragraph: (2) When the word "Forbidden" is shown for dangerous goods in column 8 or 9 of Schedule 1, a person must not offer for transport or transport the dangerous goods by the means of transport set out in the heading of that column.

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: 1.6 (1) When there is a number shown in column 8 of Schedule 1, that number is a quantity limit per means of containment for the corresponding dangerous goods in column 2. A person must not load onto a passenger carrying vessel, or transport on a road vehicle or a railway vehicle on board a passenger carrying vessel, dangerous goods that exceed the quantity limit. Dangerous goods exceed the quantity limit if

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (a) in the case of a solid, they have a mass that is greater than the number when that number is expressed in kilograms;

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (b) in the case of a liquid, they have a volume that is greater than the number when that number is expressed in litres;

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (c) in the case of a gas, including a gas in a liquefied form, they are contained in a means of containment the capacity of which is greater than the number when that number is expressed in litres; and

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (d) in the case of an explosive

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (i) not subject to special provision 85 or 86, they have a net explosives quantity that is greater than the number when that number is expressed in kilograms, or

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (ii) subject to special provision 85 or 86, they exceed 100 articles.

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (2) When there is a number shown in column 9 of Schedule 1, that number is a quantity limit per means of containment for the corresponding dangerous goods in column 2. A person must not offer for transport or transport by passenger carrying road vehicle or passenger carrying railway vehicle dangerous goods that exceed the quantity limit. Dangerous goods exceed the quantity limit if

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (a) in the case of a solid, they have a mass that is greater than the number when that number is expressed in kilograms;

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (b) in the case of a liquid, they have a volume that is greater than the number when that number is expressed in litres;

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (c) in the case of a gas, including a gas in a liquefied form, they are contained in a means of containment the capacity of which is greater than the number when that number is expressed in litres; and

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (d) in the case of an explosive

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (i) not subject to special provision 85 or 86, they have a net explosives quantity that is greater than the number when that number is expressed in kilograms, or

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (ii) subject to special provision 85 or 86, they exceed 100 articles.

heading: Schedule 1: Quantity Limits in Columns 8 and 9
paragraph: (3) If a quantity limit in column 8 or 9 of Schedule 1 conflicts with any other quantity limit in these Regulations, other than a quantity limit in special provisions, the quantity limit in that column takes precedence.

heading: Safety Requirements, Documents and Safety Marks
paragraph: 1.7 As provided for in section 5 of the Act, a person must not import, offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods unless

heading: Safety Requirements, Documents and Safety Marks
paragraph: (a) the person complies with all applicable prescribed safety requirements;

heading: Safety Requirements, Documents and Safety Marks
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods are accompanied by all applicable prescribed documents; and

heading: Safety Requirements, Documents and Safety Marks
paragraph: (c) the means of containment and transport comply with all applicable prescribed safety standards and display all applicable prescribed safety marks.

heading: Prohibition: Explosives
paragraph: 1.8 A person must not handle, offer for transport or transport dangerous goods by any means of transport if the dangerous goods are explosives and

heading: Prohibition: Explosives
paragraph: (a) are in direct contact with a large means of containment, except when the explosives are to be transported by road vehicle in quantities that are allowed for explosives in section 9.5, Part 9 (Road), in Schedule 1 or in any special provision in Schedule 2; or

heading: Prohibition: Explosives
paragraph: (b) are also radioactive materials.

heading: Requirements Respecting the Transportation of Dangerous Goods on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: 1.10 (1) The requirements of these Regulations respecting the transportation of dangerous goods other than explosives on board a passenger carrying vessel apply to a passenger carrying vessel that is transporting more than 25 passengers or more than one passenger for each 3 m of the length of the vessel.

heading: Requirements Respecting the Transportation of Dangerous Goods on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (2) The requirements of these Regulations respecting the transportation of dangerous goods that are explosives on board a passenger carrying vessel apply to a passenger carrying vessel that is transporting more than 12 passengers.

heading: Use of 49 CFR for Non-Regulated Dangerous Goods
paragraph: 1.11 When a substance is regulated in the United States by 49 CFR but is not regulated in Canada by these Regulations, a person may transport the substance between Canada and the United States by road vehicle or railway vehicle in accordance with all or part of 49 CFR.

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: 1.15 (1) Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of Containment), Part 6 (Training) and Part 8 (Reporting Requirements) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage if

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (a) in the case of

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more small means of containment in compliance with the requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of Containment), except that, in the case of dangerous goods that are UN1950, AEROSOLS, or UN2037, GAS CARTRIDGES, the requirement in section 8.1.7 of CGSB-43.123 that aerosol containers and gas cartridges be tightly packed in a strong outer packaging does not apply, or

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) dangerous goods not included in Class 2, they are in one or more small means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (b) except for dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, the dangerous goods are contained in one or more means of containment each of which has a gross mass less than or equal to 30 kg;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (c) the gross mass of all dangerous goods

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) transported on the road vehicle or the railway vehicle is less than or equal to 150 kg, and

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) transported on the vessel on a domestic voyage is less than or equal to 150 kg, excluding dangerous goods in a road vehicle or railway vehicle being transported on the vessel; and

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (d) the dangerous goods are in a quantity or concentration available to the general public and are transported

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) by a user or purchaser of the dangerous goods, or

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) by a retailer to or from a user or purchaser of the dangerous goods.

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to dangerous goods that

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (a) are in a quantity or concentration that requires an ERAP;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (b) require a control or emergency temperature;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (c) are included in Class 1, Explosives, except for UN numbers UN0012, UN0014, UN0044, UN0055, UN0105, UN0131, UN0161, UN0173, UN0186, UN0191, UN0197, UN0276, UN0312, UN0323, UN0335 if classified as a consumer firework, UN0336, UN0337, UN0351, UN0373, UN0378, UN0404, UN0405, UN0431, UN0432, UN0454, UN0499, UN0501, UN0503, UN0505 to UN0507, UN0509 and UN0510;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (d) are included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, and are in a cylinder with a capacity greater than 46 L;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (e) are included in Class 2.3, Toxic Gases;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (f) are included in Class 4, Flammable Solids; Substances Liable to Spontaneous Combustion; Substances that on Contact with Water Emit Flammable Gases (Water-reactive Substances); and in Packing Group I;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (g) are included in Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, unless they are allowed to be transported as limited quantities in accordance with section 1.17 and column 6(a) of Schedule 1;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (h) are liquids included in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, and Packing Group I;

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) are included in Class 6.2, Infectious Substances; or

heading: 150 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (j) are included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, and are required to be licensed by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: 1.16 (1) Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) and Part 5 (Means of Containment) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage if

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (a) in the case of

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more small means of containment in compliance with the requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of Containment), or

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) dangerous goods not included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more means of containment

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (A) each of which has a gross mass less than or equal to 30 kg and that is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety, or

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (B) that are drums in compliance with the requirements of section 5.12 of Part 5 (Means of Containment), for transporting dangerous goods in drums;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (b) the gross mass of all dangerous goods

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) transported on the road vehicle or the railway vehicle is less than or equal to 500 kg, and

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) transported on the vessel on a domestic voyage is less than or equal to 500 kg, excluding the dangerous goods in a road vehicle or railway vehicle being transported on the vessel;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (c) each means of containment has displayed on one side, other than a side on which it is intended to rest or to be stacked during transport,

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) the dangerous goods safety marks required by Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), or

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) for dangerous goods, other than dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, the shipping name of the dangerous goods and the marks required for them in one of the following Acts and regulations, as long as those marks are legible and visible during handling and transporting in the same manner as dangerous goods safety marks:

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (A) the Pest Control Products Act and its regulations,

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (B) the Hazardous Products Act and its regulations, or

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (C) the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act and its regulations;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (d) the dangerous goods are accompanied by a shipping document or document that is located, for a road or railway vehicle or a vessel, in accordance with the requirements for location of a shipping document in sections 3.7 to 3.9 of Part 3 (Documentation); and

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (e) any document referred to in paragraph (d), other than a shipping document, includes the following information in the following order:

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) the primary class of the dangerous goods, following the word "Class" or "Classe", and

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) the total number of means of containment, on which a dangerous goods safety mark is required to be displayed, for each primary class, following the words "number of means of containment" or "nombre de contenants".

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to dangerous goods that

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (a) are in a quantity or concentration that requires an ERAP;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (b) require a control or emergency temperature;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (c) are included in Class 1, Explosives, except for

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) explosives included in Class 1.4S, or

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (ii) UN numbers UN0191, UN0197, UN0276, UN0312, UN0336, UN0403, UN0431, UN0453 and UN0493;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (d) are included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, and are in a cylinder with a capacity greater than 46 L;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (e) are included in Class 2.3, Toxic Gases;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (f) are included in Class 4, Flammable Solids; Substances Liable to Spontaneous Combustion; Substances that on Contact with Water Emit Flammable Gases (Water-reactive Substances); and in Packing Group I;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (g) are included in Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, unless they are allowed to be transported as limited quantities in accordance with section 1.17 and column 6(a) of Schedule 1;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (h) are liquids included in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, and Packing Group I;

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (i) are included in Class 6.2, Infectious Substances; or

heading: 500 kg Gross Mass Exemption
paragraph: (j) are included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, and are required to be licensed by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: 1.17 (1) A quantity of dangerous goods, other than explosives, is a limited quantity if

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are in one or more means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety; and

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) each outer means of containment has a gross mass that is less than or equal to 30 kg and

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (i) if the dangerous goods are a solid or a liquid, the goods in each inner means of containment are in a quantity that is less than or equal to the number shown in column 6(a) of Schedule 1, or

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (ii) if the dangerous goods are a gas, including a gas in a liquefied form, each means of containment in which they are contained has a capacity less than or equal to the number shown in column 6(a) of Schedule 1.

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (2) Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of Containment), Part 6 (Training), Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan) and Part 8 (Reporting Requirements) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of limited quantities of dangerous goods on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage if each means of containment is legibly and durably marked on one side, other than a side on which it is intended to rest or to be stacked during transport, with the mark illustrated in subsection (5).

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (3) When a limited quantity of dangerous goods is in a means of containment that is inside another means of containment, the inner means of containment is not required to be marked if

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the gross mass of the outer means of containment is less than or equal to 30 kg;

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) the outer means of containment is not intended to be opened during transport; and

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (c) the outer means of containment is legibly and visibly marked, on a contrasting background, with the mark illustrated in subsection (5).

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (4) When a limited quantity of dangerous goods is in a means of containment that is inside an overpack, the following information must be displayed on the overpack unless the marks on the small means of containment are visible through the overpack:

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the word "Overpack" or "Suremballage" or ; and

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) the mark illustrated in subsection (5), legibly and visibly marked on a contrasting background.

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (5) The mark is a square on point, and the line forming the square on point must be at least 2 mm wide. The top and bottom portions must be black and the central portion must be white or a contrasting colour. Each side of the mark must be at least 100 mm long. The letter "Y" may be displayed in the centre of the mark if the limited quantity is in compliance with the ICAO Technical Instructions. If the size of the means of containment so requires, the length of each side may be reduced to not less than 50 mm, provided that the mark remains clearly visible.

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (6) Until December 31, 2020, instead of being marked with the mark illustrated in subsection (5), a means of containment may have displayed on it

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the words "Limited Quantity" or "quantite limitee";

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) the abbreviation "Ltd. Qty." or "quant. ltee";

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (c) the words "Consumer Commodity" or "bien de consommation"; or

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (d) the UN number of each limited quantity of dangerous goods placed within a square on point.

heading: Limited Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of paragraph (6)(d), the line forming the square on point must be black and be at least 2 mm wide. If the dangerous goods have different UN numbers, the square on point must be large enough to include each UN number, but in any case each side must be not less than 50 mm long. The UN numbers must be at least 6 mm high. The line and UN numbers must be on a contrasting background.

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: 1.17.1 (1) A quantity of dangerous goods, other than explosives, is an excepted quantity if

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are in an inner means of containment and an outer means of containment that are designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) any of the dangerous goods in the inner means of containment,

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (i) if solids, have a mass that is less than or equal to the number shown in column 1 of the table to subsection (2) for the corresponding alphanumeric code in column 6(b) of Schedule 1, when that number is expressed in grams,

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (ii) if liquids, have a volume that is less than or equal to the number shown in column 1 of the table to subsection (2) for the corresponding alphanumeric code in column 6(b) of Schedule 1, when that number is expressed in millilitres, or

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (iii) if gases, including a gas in a liquefied form, are contained in one or more means of containment each of which has a capacity less than or equal to the number shown in column 1 of the table to subsection (2) for the corresponding alphanumeric code in column 6(b) of Schedule 1, when that number is expressed in millilitres; and

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (c) any of the dangerous goods in the outer means of containment,

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (i) if solids, have a mass that is less than or equal to the number shown in column 2 of the table to subsection (2) for the corresponding alphanumeric code in column 6(b) of Schedule 1, when that number is expressed in grams,

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (ii) if liquids, have a volume that is less than or equal to the number shown in column 2 of the table to subsection (2) for the corresponding alphanumeric code in column 6(b) of Schedule 1, when that number is expressed in millilitres, or

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (iii) if gases, including a gas in a liquefied form, are contained in one or more means of containment each of which has a capacity less than or equal to the number shown in column 2 of the table to subsection (2) for the corresponding alphanumeric code in column 6(b) of Schedule 1, when that number is expressed in millilitres.

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (2) When dangerous goods in excepted quantities for which different alphanumeric codes are assigned are together in an outer means of containment, the total quantity of dangerous goods must not exceed the lowest maximum net quantity per outer means of containment that is set out in column 2 of the table to this subsection for any of the dangerous goods.
