heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (3) Parts 3 to 8 and 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of dangerous goods in excepted quantities if each means of containment is marked on one side, other than a side on which it is intended to rest or to be stacked during transport, with the excepted quantities mark illustrated below.

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: Excepted Quantities Mark

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (4) When dangerous goods in excepted quantities are in a means of containment that is inside an overpack, the following information must be displayed on the overpack, unless that information is on the means of containment and is visible through the overpack:

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the word "Overpack" or "Suremballage"; and

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) the mark illustrated in subsection (3).

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (5) The number of outer means of containment containing dangerous goods in excepted quantities on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or an intermodal container must not exceed 1 000.

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (6) When dangerous goods in excepted quantities are in an inner means of containment that is inside an outer means of containment, the inner means of containment is not required to be marked in accordance with subsection (3) if

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the outer means of containment is not intended to be opened during transport; and

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) the outer means of containment is marked, legibly and visibly on a contrasting background, with the mark illustrated in that subsection.

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (7) If a shipping document or any other document accompanies dangerous goods in excepted quantities, the document must include the words "dangerous goods in excepted quantities" or "marchandises dangereuses en quantites exceptees" and must indicate the number of outer means of containment.

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (8) These Regulations, except for Parts 1 and 2, do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transport of dangerous goods in excepted quantities that are assigned to alphanumeric codes E1, E2, E4 and E5 in column 6(b) of Schedule 1 if

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (a) the net quantity of the dangerous goods per inner means of containment is less than or equal to 1 g for solids or 1 mL for liquids and gases; and

heading: Excepted Quantities Exemption
paragraph: (b) the net quantity of the dangerous goods per outer means of containment is less than or equal to 100 g for solids or 100 mL for liquids and gases.

heading: Medical Device or Article
paragraph: 1.18 These Regulations do not apply to the transport on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage of

heading: Medical Device or Article
paragraph: (a) a medical device, wheelchair or medical article if

heading: Medical Device or Article
paragraph: (i) the medical device is attached to or implanted in an individual or an animal, or

heading: Medical Device or Article
paragraph: (ii) the wheelchair or medical article is in transport and is intended for the personal use of a specific individual;

heading: Medical Device or Article
paragraph: (b) a radio-pharmaceutical that has been injected in or ingested by an individual or an animal.

heading: Samples for Inspection or Investigation Exemption
paragraph: 1.19 These Regulations do not apply to samples of goods, including forensic samples, that are reasonably believed to be dangerous goods if, for the purposes of inspection or investigation duties under an Act of Parliament or of a provincial legislature, the samples are

heading: Samples for Inspection or Investigation Exemption
paragraph: (a) in transport under the direct supervision of a federal, provincial or municipal government employee acting in the course of employment; and

heading: Samples for Inspection or Investigation Exemption
paragraph: (b) in one or more means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety.

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: 1.19.1 Parts 2 to 7 and 17 do not apply to samples of goods that the consignor reasonably believes to be dangerous goods whose classification or exact chemical composition is unknown and cannot be readily determined if

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (a) in the case of

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (i) samples that are reasonably believed to be a gas, including a gas in a liquefied form, they are in one or more means of containment in compliance with the requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of Containment), or

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (ii) samples that are reasonably believed not to be a gas, they are in one or more means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (b) the samples are in transport for the purposes of classifying, analysing or testing;

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (c) the samples are believed not to contain explosives, infectious substances or radioactive materials;

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (d) the dangerous goods are contained in one or more means of containment each of which has a gross mass less than or equal to 10 kg;

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (e) the samples are accompanied by a document that includes the name and address of the consignor and the words "test samples" or "echantillons d'epreuve"; and

heading: Samples Classifying, Analysing or Testing Exemption
paragraph: (f) each means of containment has marked on it the words "test samples" or "echantillons d'epreuve" and the words are legible and displayed on a contrasting background.

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: 1.19.2 Parts 3, 4 and 17 do not apply to samples of dangerous goods if

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (a) in the case of

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (i) samples included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more means of containment in compliance with the requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of Containment), or

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (ii) samples not included in Class 2, they are in one or more means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (b) the samples are in transport for demonstration purposes;

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (c) the samples are in the custody of an agent of the manufacturer or distributor who is acting in the course of employment;

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (d) the samples are not for sale;

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (e) the samples are not transported in a passenger carrying road vehicle, passenger carrying railway vehicle, passenger carrying aircraft or passenger carrying vessel other than a passenger carrying vessel that operates over the most direct water route between two points that are not more than 5 km apart;

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (f) the dangerous goods are contained in one or more means of containment each of which has a gross mass less than or equal to 10 kg; and

heading: Samples Demonstration Exemption
paragraph: (g) each means of containment has marked on it the words "demonstration samples" or "echantillons de demonstration" and the words are legible and displayed on a contrasting background.

heading: National Defence
paragraph: 1.20 For the purposes of paragraph 3(4)(a) of the Act, any activity or thing related to the transportation of dangerous goods is under the sole direction or control of the Minister of National Defence if the dangerous goods are in or on a means of transport

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (a) owned and operated by the Department of National Defence or operated on behalf of the Department of National Defence by

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (i) an employee of the Department of National Defence,

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (ii) a member of the Canadian Forces, or

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (iii) civilian personnel who are not employed by the Department of National Defence if the means of transport is accompanied at all times by, and is under the direct responsibility of, an employee of the Department of National Defence or a member of the Canadian Forces;

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (b) owned and operated by the military establishment of a member country of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization or operated on behalf of such an establishment by

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (i) military or civilian personnel of that establishment, or

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (ii) civilian personnel who are not employed by that establishment if the means of transport is accompanied at all times by, and is under the direct responsibility of, military or civilian personnel of that establishment; or

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (c) owned and operated by the military establishment of another country under an agreement with the Department of National Defence or operated on behalf of such an establishment by

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (i) military or civilian personnel of that establishment, or

heading: National Defence
paragraph: (ii) civilian personnel who are not employed by that establishment if the means of transport is accompanied at all times by, and is under the direct responsibility of, military or civilian personnel of that establishment.

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: 1.21 (1) Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of Containment) and Part 6 (Training) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods on a road vehicle licensed as a farm vehicle if

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (a) in the case of

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (i) dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more means of containment in compliance with the requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of Containment), or

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (ii) dangerous goods not included in Class 2, they are in one or more means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (b) the gross mass of all dangerous goods on the road vehicle is less than or equal to 1 500 kg;

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (c) the dangerous goods are to be or have been used by a farmer for farming purposes;

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (d) the dangerous goods are transported solely on land and the distance on public roads is less than or equal to 100 km; and

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (e) the dangerous goods do not include

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (i) Class 1, Explosives, other than explosives included in Class 1.4S,

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (ii) Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, in a cylinder with a capacity greater than 46 L,

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (iii) Class 2.3, Toxic Gases,

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (iv) Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, or

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (v) Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

heading: Agriculture: 1 500 kg Gross Mass Farm Vehicle Exemption
paragraph: (2) Despite the exemption from Part 3 (Documentation) in subsection (1), when an ERAP is required under Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan), the dangerous goods for which the plan is required must be accompanied by a shipping document.

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: 1.22 (1) Parts 3 to 5 and 17 do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods on a road vehicle if

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (a) in the case of

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (i) dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more means of containment in compliance with the requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of Containment), or

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (ii) dangerous goods not included in Class 2, they are in one or more means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods are transported solely on land between a retail place of purchase and place of destination and the distance on public roads is less than or equal to 100 km;

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (c) the gross mass of all dangerous goods on the road vehicle is less than or equal to 3 000 kg;

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (d) the dangerous goods are to be or have been used by a farmer for farming purposes; and

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (e) the dangerous goods do not include

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (i) Class 1, Explosives, other than explosives included in Class 1.4S,

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (ii) Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, in a cylinder with a capacity greater than 46 L,

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (iii) Class 2.3, Toxic Gases,

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (iv) Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, or

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (v) Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

heading: Agriculture: 3 000 kg Gross Mass Farm Retail Exemption
paragraph: (2) Despite the exemption from Part 3 (Documentation) in subsection (1), when an ERAP is required under Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan) the dangerous goods for which the plan is required must be accompanied by a shipping document.

heading: Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption
paragraph: 1.23 (1) Part 3 (Documentation), the requirements for the display of a UN number in section 4.15 of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) and Part 6 (Training) do not apply to a solution of pesticides in transport on a road vehicle if

heading: Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are transported solely on land for a distance less than or equal to 100 km;

heading: Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods are in a large means of containment that

heading: Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption
paragraph: (i) has a capacity that is less than or equal to 6 000 L, and

heading: Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption
paragraph: (ii) is used to prepare the dangerous goods for application or to apply the dangerous goods; and

heading: Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption
paragraph: (c) only one large means of containment containing the solution of pesticides is in transport on the road vehicle.

heading: Agriculture: Pesticide Exemption
paragraph: (2) Despite the exemption for documentation in subsection (1), when an ERAP is required under Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan), the dangerous goods must be accompanied by a shipping document.

heading: Agriculture: Anhydrous Ammonia Exemption
paragraph: 1.24 Part 3 (Documentation) and Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan) do not apply to UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA, if it is

heading: Agriculture: Anhydrous Ammonia Exemption
paragraph: (a) in transport solely on land and the distance on public roads is less than or equal to 100 km; and

heading: Agriculture: Anhydrous Ammonia Exemption
paragraph: (b) in a large means of containment with a capacity that is less than or equal to 10 000 L and is used for the field application of anhydrous ammonia.

heading: Transportation within a Facility
paragraph: 1.25 These Regulations do not apply to dangerous goods that are transported solely within a manufacturing or processing facility to which public access is controlled.

heading: Emergency Response Exemption
paragraph: 1.26 These Regulations do not apply to dangerous goods that are in quantities necessary to respond to an emergency that endangers public safety and that are in transport in a means of transport that is dedicated to emergency response, unless the dangerous goods are forbidden for transport in Schedule 1, Schedule 3 or, for transport by aircraft, the ICAO Technical Instructions.

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: 1.27 (1) These Regulations do not apply to dangerous goods on a means of transport that are required for

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (a) the propulsion of the means of transport and that are

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (i) intended to remain on the means of transport until used, and

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (ii) contained in a fuel tank permanently installed on the means of transport;

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (b) the safety of individuals on board the means of transport;

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (c) the operation or safety of the means of transport including, while installed in the means of transport and used or likely to be used for purposes related to transport, air bags, air brakes, flares, lighting, shock absorbers or fire extinguishers; or

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (d) ventilation, refrigeration or heating units that are necessary to maintain environmental conditions within a means of containment in transport on the means of transport and are intended to remain with the units or on the means of transport until used.

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (2) The exemption in subsection (1) does not apply to

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (a) ammunition; or

heading: Operation of a Means of Transport or a Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (b) dangerous goods being delivered to a destination and from which a portion is drawn off during transport for propulsion of the means of transport.

heading: Transportation between Two Properties
paragraph: 1.28 These Regulations do not apply to dangerous goods, other than Class 1, Explosives, or Class 7, Radioactive Materials, that are in transport on a road vehicle between two properties owned or leased by the manufacturer, producer or user of the dangerous goods if

heading: Transportation between Two Properties
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are transported a distance less than or equal to 3 km on a public road;

heading: Transportation between Two Properties
paragraph: (b) the road vehicle has displayed on it

heading: Transportation between Two Properties
paragraph: (i) the placard for the primary class of each of the dangerous goods, or

heading: Transportation between Two Properties
paragraph: (ii) the DANGER placard;

heading: Transportation between Two Properties
paragraph: (c) the dangerous goods are in one or more means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety; and

heading: Transportation between Two Properties
paragraph: (d) the local police are advised, in writing, of the nature of the dangerous goods no more than 12 months in advance of the transport.

heading: Ferry Exemption
paragraph: 1.30 Paragraph 3.6(3)(a) of Part 3 (Documentation), and subsection 4.16(3) and paragraph 4.16.1(2)(d) of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) do not apply to dangerous goods in transport on a road vehicle or railway vehicle that is being transported on board a vessel that is operating over the most direct water route between two points that are not more than 5 km apart.

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: 1.30.1 Subsection 1.6(1) and paragraph 3.6(3)(a) do not apply to dangerous goods that are UN1203, GASOLINE, or UN1978, PROPANE, that are in a highway tank that is being transported by a tank truck on board a passenger carrying vessel that is operating over the most direct water route between two points that are not more than 5 km apart if the following conditions are met:

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (a) no more than two tank trucks transporting dangerous goods that are UN1203, GASOLINE or UN1978, PROPANE are on board the passenger carrying vessel;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (b) before the tank truck is placed on board the passenger carrying vessel, the highway tank is visually inspected by its driver for dents or evidence of leakage;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (c) the tank truck is located on an open deck;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (d) a safety perimeter of at least 1 m is established around the tank truck while it is on board the passenger carrying vessel;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (e) the tank truck's parking brakes are set securely throughout the journey until the passenger carrying vessel has completed docking;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (f) the tank truck's engine is either left running at all times or is shut off and not restarted until the passenger carrying vessel has completed docking;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (g) the tank truck's driver remains with the tank truck while it is on board the passenger carrying vessel;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (h) notices prohibiting smoking, the use of an open flame and the use of spark-producing equipment on the passenger carrying vessel are placed in full view of passengers;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (i) fixed extinguishing equipment, including foam cannon units that are capable of reaching the highway tank, is installed on board the passenger carrying vessel;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (j) absorbent material that is compatible with flammable liquids is available on board the passenger carrying vessel;

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (k) a flammable gas detector is available on board the passenger carrying vessel; and

heading: Propane and Gasoline in Highway Tanks on Board Passenger Carrying Vessels
paragraph: (l) the passenger carrying vessel's master ensures that the tank truck is constantly monitored by a crew member while it is on board the passenger carrying vessel.

heading: Class 1, Explosives, Exemption
paragraph: 1.31 Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 6 (Training), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting on a road vehicle or a railway vehicle dangerous goods included in Class 1, Explosives, if

heading: Class 1, Explosives, Exemption
paragraph: (a) the quantity of each explosive in the road vehicle or railway vehicle that is not subject to special provision 85 or 86 is less than or equal to the number shown in column 6(a) of Schedule 1 for that explosive;

heading: Class 1, Explosives, Exemption
paragraph: (b) the quantity of each explosive in the road vehicle or railway vehicle that is subject to special provision 85 or 86 is less than or equal to the number shown in special provision 85 or 86 for that explosive;

heading: Class 1, Explosives, Exemption
paragraph: (c) each means of containment has displayed on it the class, compatibility group and UN number of the explosives contained inside it; and

heading: Class 1, Explosives, Exemption
paragraph: (d) a placard is displayed in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) if the explosives are included in Class 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 or 1.5

heading: Class 1, Explosives, Exemption
paragraph: (i) in any quantity exceeding 10 kg net explosives quantity, or

heading: Class 1, Explosives, Exemption
paragraph: (ii) in any number of articles exceeding 1 000 for explosives subject to special provision 85 or 86.

heading: Class 2, Gases, or Ammonia Solutions (Class 8) in Refrigerating Machines Exemption
paragraph: 1.32 Parts 3 to 10 and 17 do not apply to UN2857, REFRIGERATING MACHINES, and refrigerating machine components containing gases included in Class 2.2 or UN2672, AMMONIA SOLUTION, if the quantity of gas has a mass that is less than or equal to 12 kg and the quantity of ammonia solution is less than or equal to 12 L.

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: 1.32.1 (1) The following dangerous goods may be identified by the UN number UN1075 and the shipping name LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES instead of the UN number and shipping name identified for them:

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (a) UN1011, BUTANE;

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (b) UN1012, BUTYLENE;

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (c) UN1055, ISOBUTYLENE;

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (d) UN1077, PROPYLENE;

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (e) UN1969, ISOBUTANE; and

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (f) UN1978, PROPANE.

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (2) The shipping name of the dangerous goods listed in paragraphs (1)(a) to (f) may be shown on the shipping document, in parentheses, following the words "LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES".

heading: Class 2, Gases, that May Be Identified as UN1075, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
paragraph: (3) If either UN1077, PROPYLENE, or UN1978, PROPANE, is to be transported on a road vehicle or railway vehicle on board a vessel and is identified as LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES on the shipping document in accordance with subsection (1), the shipping name PROPYLENE or PROPANE, as appropriate, must be shown on the shipping document, in parentheses, following the words "LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES".

heading: Class 2, Gases, Absolute Pressure between 101.3 kPa and 280 kPa
paragraph: 1.32.2 Gases that are at an absolute pressure between 101.3 kPa and 280 kPa at 20°C, other than gases included in Class 2.1 or Class 2.3, may be handled, offered for transport or transported on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage as Class 2.2, Non-flammable, Non-toxic gas. In that case, the requirements of these Regulations that relate to gases included in Class 2.2 must be complied with.

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: 1.32.3 Part 3 (Documentation) and Part 6 (Training) do not apply to dangerous goods that are transported in one or more small means of containment on a road vehicle solely on land if

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (i) UN1001, ACETYLENE, DISSOLVED,

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (ii) UN1002, AIR, COMPRESSED,

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (iii) UN1006, ARGON, COMPRESSED,

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (iv) UN1013, CARBON DIOXIDE,

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (v) UN1060, METHYLACETYLENE AND PROPADIENE MIXTURE, STABILIZED,

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (vi) UN1066, NITROGEN, COMPRESSED,

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (vii) UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED, or

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (viii) UN1978, PROPANE;

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods are contained in no more than five small means of containment;

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (c) the gross mass of the dangerous goods is less than or equal to 500 kg; and

heading: Class 2, Gases, in Small Means of Containment Exemption
paragraph: (d) the labels displayed on the small means of containment can be seen from outside the road vehicle.

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids: General Exemption
paragraph: 1.33 Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of Containment), Part 6 (Training), Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage if the dangerous goods

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids: General Exemption
paragraph: (a) have no subsidiary class;

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids: General Exemption
paragraph: (b) are included in Packing Group III and have a flash point greater than 37.8°C; and

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids: General Exemption
paragraph: (c) are in one or more small means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety.

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Flash Point Greater Than 60°C but Less Than or Equal to 93°C
paragraph: 1.34 Despite section 6.1 of the Act and section 4.2 of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) of these Regulations, substances that have a flash point greater than 60°C but less than or equal to 93°C may be transported on a road vehicle, on a railway vehicle or on a vessel on a domestic voyage as Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Packing Group III. In that case, the requirements of these Regulations, except paragraph 7.2(1)(f) of Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan), that relate to flammable liquids that have a flash point less than or equal to 60°C must be complied with.

heading: UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, or UN1203, GASOLINE, Exemption
paragraph: 1.35 Part 3 (Documentation), the UN number requirements in sections 4.12 and 4.15.2 of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) and Part 6 (Training) do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting on a road vehicle of dangerous goods that are UN1202, DIESEL FUEL or UN1203, GASOLINE, if

heading: UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, or UN1203, GASOLINE, Exemption
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are in one or more means of containment, each of which is visible from outside the road vehicle and each of which has displayed on it

heading: UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, or UN1203, GASOLINE, Exemption
paragraph: (i) the label or placard required for the dangerous goods by Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), or

heading: UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, or UN1203, GASOLINE, Exemption
paragraph: (ii) if a side or end of the means of containment is not visible from outside the road vehicle, the label or placard required for the dangerous goods by Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) on a side or end that is visible from outside the road vehicle;

heading: UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, or UN1203, GASOLINE, Exemption
paragraph: (b) each means of containment is secured to the road vehicle so that the required label or at least one of the required placards displayed on it is visible from outside the road vehicle during transport; and

heading: UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, or UN1203, GASOLINE, Exemption
paragraph: (c) the total capacity of all the means of containment is less than or equal to 2 000 L.

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: 1.36 Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of Containment), Part 6 (Training), Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan), Part 8 (Reporting Requirements), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage of

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: (a) an alcoholic beverage if the alcoholic beverage

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: (i) contains alcohol that is less than or equal to 24% by volume,

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: (ii) is included in Packing Group II and is in a means of containment with a capacity that is less than or equal to 5 L, or

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: (iii) is included in Packing Group III and is in a means of containment with a capacity that is less than or equal to 250 L; or

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: (b) an aqueous solution of alcohol if the aqueous solution has a flash point greater than 23°C and

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: (i) contains alcohol that is less than or equal to 50% by volume and at least 50% by volume of a substance that is not dangerous goods, and

heading: Class 3, Flammable Liquids, Alcoholic Beverage and Aqueous Solution of Alcohol Exemption
paragraph: (ii) is contained in a small means of containment.

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: 1.38 Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), Part 5 (Means of Containment), Part 6 (Training), Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan), Part 8 (Reporting Requirements), Part 9 (Road) and Part 10 (Rail) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of a polyester resin kit that consists of a substance included in Class 3, Packing Group II or III and a substance included in Class 5.2, Type D, E or F that does not require temperature control if

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (a) the kit is in transport on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage;

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (b) the gross mass of the kit is less than or equal to 30 kg;

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (c) the quantity of Class 3 substance in the kit is less than or equal to

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (i) 1 L for Packing Group II substances, and

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (ii) 5 L for Packing Group III substances; and

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (d) the quantity of Class 5.2 substance in the kit is less than or equal to

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (i) 125 mL for liquids, and

heading: Polyester Resin Kit Exception
paragraph: (ii) 500 g for solids.

heading: Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B Exemption
paragraph: 1.39 Parts 3 and 4, except section 4.22.1, and Part 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of infectious substances that are included in Category B if

heading: Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B Exemption
paragraph: (a) one external surface of the means of containment for the substances measures at least 100 mm * 100 mm;

heading: Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B Exemption
paragraph: (b) the means of containment is in compliance with Part 5 (Means of Containment) and has displayed on the external surface

heading: Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B Exemption
paragraph: (i) the mark illustrated in Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) for infectious substances included in Category B, and

heading: Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B Exemption
paragraph: (ii) the shipping name, on a contrasting background, next to the mark in letters at least 6 mm high; and

heading: Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B Exemption
paragraph: (c) the 24-hour telephone number required under paragraph 3.5(1)(f) is displayed next to the shipping name on the means of containment.

heading: Biological Products Exemption
paragraph: 1.41 Parts 3 to 8 and 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of biological products if they

heading: Biological Products Exemption
paragraph: (a) are prepared in accordance with the requirements set out under the Food and Drugs Act;

heading: Biological Products Exemption
paragraph: (b) are in a means of containment that is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety; and

heading: Biological Products Exemption
paragraph: (c) are in a means of containment that is marked with the words "Biological Product" or "Produit biologique" in black letters at least 6 mm high on a contrasting background.

heading: Human or Animal Specimens Believed Not to Contain Infectious Substances Exemption
paragraph: 1.42 (1) Parts 3 to 8 and 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of human or animal specimens that are reasonably believed not to contain infectious substances.

heading: Human or Animal Specimens Believed Not to Contain Infectious Substances Exemption
paragraph: (2) The human or animal specimens referred to in subsection (1) must be in a means of containment that is marked with the words "Exempt Human Specimen" or "specimen humain exempte" or "Exempt Animal Specimen" or "specimen animal exempte" and that is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the specimen.

heading: Tissues or Organs for Transplant Exemption
paragraph: 1.42.1 These Regulations do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transport of tissues or organs for transplant.

heading: Blood or Blood Components Exemption
paragraph: 1.42.2 (1) Parts 3 to 8 and 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of blood or blood components that are intended for transfusion or for the preparation of blood products and are reasonably believed not to contain infectious substances.

heading: Blood or Blood Components Exemption
paragraph: (2) The blood or blood components referred to in subsection (1) must be in a means of containment that is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the blood or blood components.

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste
paragraph: 1.42.3 Part 3, sections 4.10 to 4.12 and Parts 5 to 8 and 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of dangerous goods that are medical waste or clinical waste if

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are UN3291, (BIO) MEDICAL WASTE, N.O.S.;

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods are in a means of containment that is in compliance with CGSB-43.125; and

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste
paragraph: (c) the following information is displayed on the means of containment:

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste
paragraph: (i) the biohazard symbol; and

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste
paragraph: (ii) the word "BIOHAZARD" or "BIORISQUE".

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Materials, Exemption
paragraph: 1.43 Parts 3 to 7, 9 to 12 and 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of dangerous goods included in Class 7 if the dangerous goods

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Materials, Exemption
paragraph: (a) satisfy the conditions in the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations to be transported in an excepted package;

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Materials, Exemption
paragraph: (b) are in an excepted package; and

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Materials, Exemption
paragraph: (c) are accompanied by a document that includes the shipping name and UN number of the radioactive materials.

heading: Residue of Dangerous Goods in a Drum Exemption
paragraph: 1.44 Part 2 (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), and Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan) do not apply to a residue of dangerous goods contained in a drum that is in transport on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage, except for dangerous goods included in Packing Group I or contained in a drum otherwise requiring a label for Class 1, 4.3, 6.2 or 7, if

heading: Residue of Dangerous Goods in a Drum Exemption
paragraph: (b) the drum is being transported for the purpose of reconditioning or reuse in accordance with section 5.12 of Part 5 (Means of Containment);

heading: Residue of Dangerous Goods in a Drum Exemption
paragraph: (c) when more than 10 drums are on the road vehicle or on the railway vehicle, the road vehicle or railway vehicle has displayed on it the DANGER placard in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks); and

heading: Residue of Dangerous Goods in a Drum Exemption
paragraph: (d) the drums are accompanied by a document that includes the following information:

heading: Residue of Dangerous Goods in a Drum Exemption
paragraph: (i) the primary class of each residue and the words "Residue Drum(s)" or "fut(s) de residu" when the primary class can be reasonably determined, preceded by the number of drums containing dangerous goods with that primary class, and

heading: Residue of Dangerous Goods in a Drum Exemption
paragraph: (ii) the words "Residue Drum(s) - Content(s) Unknown" or "fut(s) de residu - contenu inconnu" if there are any residues for which the primary class cannot be reasonably determined, preceded by the number of drums containing the residues.

heading: Fumigation of Means of Containment
paragraph: 1.45 These Regulations, except for subsection 3.5(3) of Part 3 (Documentation) and section 4.21 of Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), do not apply to a means of containment, or the contents of a means of containment, that is being fumigated with dangerous goods and that is in transport if the fumigant is the only dangerous goods in transport in the means of containment.

heading: Marine Pollutants Exemption
paragraph: 1.45.1 Part 3 (Documentation) and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) do not apply to substances that are classified as marine pollutants in accordance with section 2.43 of Part 2 (Classification) if they are in transport solely on land by road vehicle or railway vehicle. However, substances may be identified as marine pollutants on a shipping document and the required dangerous goods safety marks may be displayed when they are in transport by road or railway vehicle.

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: 1.46 These Regulations do not apply to the following dangerous goods:

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (a) ammoniating fertilizer solutions with an absolute pressure of ammonia less than or equal to 276 kPa at 41°C;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (b) antimony oxides and antimony sulphides with 0.5% or less arsenic by mass;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (c) charcoal or carbons that are

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (i) non-activated carbon blacks of mineral origin,

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (ii) carbons made by a steam activation process, or

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (iii) activated or non-activated carbons that pass the self-heating test for carbon in section 33.3.1.3.3 of the Manual of Tests and Criteria;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (d) cinnabar;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (e) cyclohexanone peroxides with 70% or more inert inorganic solid, by mass;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (f) Di-4-chlorobenzoyl peroxide or p-chlorobenzoyl peroxide with 70% or more inert inorganic solid, by mass;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (g) 1,3-Di-(2-tert-butylperoxyisopropyl) benzene or 1,4-Di-(2-tert-butylperoxyisopropyl) benzene, or mixtures of both, 60% or more, by mass, of which consists of an inert solid, if the substance is in a means of containment in a total quantity less than or equal to 200 kg;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (h) dibenzoyl peroxide or benzoyl peroxide that is in a concentration less than 35.5%, by mass, with finely ground starch, calcium sulphate dihydrate or dicalcium phosphate dihydrate, or that is in a concentration less than 30%, by mass, with 70% or more, by mass, inert solid;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (i) dicumyl peroxide with 60% or more inert inorganic solid, by mass;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (j) ferricyanides and ferrocyanides;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (k) fish-meal that is acidified and is wetted with 40% or more water, by mass;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (n) sodium dichloroisocyanurate dihydrate;

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (o) solvent extracted soya bean meal free of flammable solvent and containing 1.5% or less oil, by mass, and 11% or less moisture, by mass; or

heading: Miscellaneous Special Cases
paragraph: (p) wood or wood products treated with wood preservatives.

heading: UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, Exemption
paragraph: 1.47 Subsections 5.10(1) and (2) and Part 17 do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transporting of UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, if the fire extinguishers

heading: UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, Exemption
paragraph: (a) do not contain dangerous goods included in Class 2.3, Class 6.1 or Class 8;

heading: UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, Exemption
paragraph: (b) are contained in an outer means of containment;

heading: UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, Exemption
paragraph: (c) have a capacity less than 18 L or, if they contain liquefied gas, a capacity less than 0.6 L;

heading: UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, Exemption
paragraph: (d) have an internal pressure less than or equal to 1 650 kPa at 21°C; and

heading: UN1044, FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, Exemption
paragraph: (e) are manufactured, tested, maintained, marked and used in accordance with ULC Standard S504, ULC Standard S507, ULC Standard S512 or ULC Standard S554.

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: 1.48 These Regulations, except for Part 8 (Reporting Requirements), do not apply to dangerous goods required for patient care on an aircraft if

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: (a) the aircraft is configured as an air ambulance and is used only as an air ambulance;

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: (b) the transport of the dangerous goods is not forbidden in Schedule 1, Schedule 3 or the ICAO Technical Instructions;

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: (c) the dangerous goods are under the control of a health care professional or a person who is trained in accordance with Part 6 (Training);

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: (d) in the case of

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: (i) dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more small means of containment in compliance with the requirements for transporting gases in Part 5 (Means of Containment), or

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: (ii) dangerous goods not included in Class 2, Gases, they are in one or more small means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety; and

heading: Air Ambulance Exemption
paragraph: (e) the means of containment are secured to prevent unintended movement during transport.

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: 1.49 (1) Subsection 5.1(1) and Section 5.10 of Part 5 (Means of Containment) do not apply to the handling, offering for transport or transporting of dangerous goods in a cylinder on a road vehicle or an aircraft if

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (a) the cylinder is from or for a vessel or an aircraft;

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (b) the cylinder is transported solely for the purpose of refilling, exchanging or requalification;

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (c) the cylinder is accompanied by a shipping document that includes the words "Cylinder in transport for purpose of refilling, exchanging or requalification in compliance with section 1.49 of the TDGR" or "Bouteille a gaz en transport aux fins de remplissage, d'echange ou de requalification en conformite avec l'article 1.49 du RTMD";

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (d) the cylinder is closed and secured so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (e) in the case of a cylinder from or for a vessel that is a Canadian vessel as defined in section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, the cylinder conforms, as applicable, to

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (ii) the Life Saving Equipment Regulations,

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (iii) the Large Fishing Vessel Inspection Regulations,

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (iv) the Fishing Vessel Safety Regulations,

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (v) the Small Vessel Regulations, and

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (vi) the Vessel Fire Safety Regulations;

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (f) in the case of a cylinder from or for a vessel that is a foreign vessel as defined in section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and that is a Safety Convention vessel as defined in that section, the cylinder is used for a purpose related to the operation or navigation of the vessel, including a life-saving or emergency purpose; and

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (g) in the case of a cylinder from or for an aircraft, a flight authority, as defined in subsection 101.01(1) of the Canadian Aviation Regulations, has been issued in respect of the aircraft and the cylinder serves an aeronautical purpose, including a life-saving or emergency purpose.

heading: Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (2) When the cylinder has been requalified or filled, the exemption set out in subsection (1) applies only if the cylinder was requalified in accordance with clause 6.5.1(b) of CSA B340 and filled in compliance with clause 6.5.1(c) of CSA B340.

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: 1.50 (1) Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.5 and subsection 5.10(1) do not apply to the offering for transport, handling or transport of UN1978, PROPANE, in a cylinder on a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a ship on a domestic voyage if

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (a) the cylinder is for use in a hot air balloon and is marked clearly and visibly, in letters at least 5 mm high, with the words "FOR USE IN HOT AIR BALLOONS ONLY" or "POUR UTILISATION DANS LES BALLONS SEULEMENT";

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (b) a flight authority, as defined in subsection 101.01(1) of the Canadian Aviation Regulations, has been issued in respect of the hot air balloon;

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (c) the cylinder is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (d) subject to paragraph (e), the cylinder

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (i) is manufactured, selected and used in accordance with CSA B340, except clause 5.3.1.4 of that standard,

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (ii) is manufactured, selected and used in accordance with CSA B342,

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (iii) is manufactured, selected and used in accordance with 49 CFR and, in the case of a requalified cylinder, is marked with the requalification markings required by CSA B339 or 49 CFR,

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (iv) is manufactured and selected in accordance with the ADR, is marked with the symbol π (Pi) in accordance with the TPED and is used in accordance with clauses 4.1.1.2, 4.1.3, 4.1.4, 4.2, 4.3.1, 4.3.2, 4.3.7, 4.3.8, 4.3.9, 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.1.3(b) to (e), 5.1.8 and 5.3.1.1 of CSA B340, or

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (v) was manufactured before January 1, 2017, and is used in accordance with clauses 4.1.1.2, 4.1.3, 4.1.4, 4.2, 4.3.1, 4.3.2, 4.3.7, 4.3.8, 4.3.9, 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.1.3(b) to (e), 5.1.8 and 5.3.1.1 of CSA B340; and

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (e) the liquid phase of the propane is less than or equal to 85% of the capacity of the cylinder at 15°C.

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subparagraph (1)(d)(iv), ADR means the European Agreement concerning the International Carriage of Dangerous Goods by Road, published by the United Nations, as amended from time to time and TPED means the Transportable Pressure Equipment Directive, Directive 2010/35/EU, June 16, 2010, published by the Council of the European Union.

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), a cylinder referred to in subparagraph (1)(d)(iv) or (v) must be requalified within

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (a) 10 years after its date of manufacture; or

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (b) 10 years after its most recent requalification date as marked on the cylinder.

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (4) A cylinder that must be requalified on or before January 1, 2018 may be requalified within a 12-month grace period that starts on the day on which this section comes into force.

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (5) When it is requalified, a cylinder referred to in subparagraph (1)(d)(iv) or (v) must

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (a) be requalified with a proof pressure retest and an internal and external visual inspection in accordance with clause 24 of CSA B339 by a facility that holds a valid certificate of registration referred to in clause 25.3 of CSA B339; or

heading: Hot Air Balloon Cylinder Exemption
paragraph: (b) be subjected to a periodic inspection and test in accordance with clause 19 of CSA B341.

heading: Determining When Substances Are Dangerous Goods
paragraph: 2.1 A substance is dangerous goods when

heading: Determining When Substances Are Dangerous Goods
paragraph: (a) it is listed by name in Schedule 1 and is in any form, state or concentration that meets the criteria in this Part for inclusion in at least one of the nine classes of dangerous goods; or

heading: Determining When Substances Are Dangerous Goods
paragraph: (b) it is not listed by name in Schedule 1 but meets the criteria in this Part for inclusion in at least one of the nine classes of dangerous goods.

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: 2.2 (1) Before allowing a carrier to take possession of dangerous goods for transport, the consignor must determine the classification of the dangerous goods in accordance with this Part.

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (2) When importing dangerous goods into Canada, the consignor must ensure that they have the correct classification before they are transported in Canada.

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (3) A consignor must use the following classifications:

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (a) for substances included in Class 1, Explosives, the classification determined in accordance with the Explosives Act; and

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (b) for radioactive materials, the classification determined in accordance with the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations.

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (3.1) For substances included in Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, a consignor may use a classification determined by the Public Health Agency of Canada or the Canadian Food Inspection Agency.

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (4) A consignor may use the appropriate classification in the ICAO Technical Instructions, the IMDG Code or the UN Recommendations to transport dangerous goods within Canada by a road vehicle, a railway vehicle or a vessel on a domestic voyage if these Regulations or the document from which the classification is taken does not forbid their transport.

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (5) If an error in classification is noticed or if there are reasonable grounds to suspect an error in classification, the consignor must not allow a carrier to take possession of the dangerous goods for transport until the classification has been verified or corrected.

heading: Responsibility for Classification
paragraph: (6) A carrier who notices an error in classification or has reasonable grounds to suspect an error in classification while the dangerous goods are in transport must advise the consignor and must stop transporting the dangerous goods until the consignor verifies or corrects the classification. The consignor must immediately verify or correct the classification and ensure that the carrier is provided with the verified or corrected classification.

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: 2.2.1 (1) A consignor who allows a carrier to take possession of dangerous goods for transport or who imports dangerous goods into Canada must, during a five-year period that begins on the date that appears on the shipping document, make a proof of classification available to the Minister on reasonable notice given by the Minister.

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this section, a proof of classification is

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (a) a test report;

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (b) a lab report; or

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (c) a document that explains how the dangerous goods were classified.

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (3) A proof of classification must include the following information:

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (a) the date on which the dangerous goods were classified;

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (b) if applicable, the technical name of the dangerous goods;

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (c) the classification of the dangerous goods; and

heading: Proof of Classification
paragraph: (d) if applicable, the classification method used under this Part or under Chapter 2 of the UN Recommendations.

heading: Classifying Substances That Are Listed by Name in Schedule 1
paragraph: 2.3 If a name of dangerous goods is shown as a shipping name in column 2 of Schedule 1, that name must be used as the shipping name. That shipping name and the corresponding data for that shipping name in columns 1, 3 and 4 of Schedule 1 must be used as the classification of the dangerous goods.

heading: Classifying Substances That Are Included in Only One Class and One Packing Group
paragraph: 2.4 If, in accordance with the criteria and tests in this Part, a substance is included in only one class and one packing group, the substance is dangerous goods and the shipping name in column 2 of Schedule 1 that most precisely describes the dangerous goods and that is most consistent with the class and the packing group determined by the criteria and tests must be selected as the shipping name. That shipping name and the corresponding data for that shipping name in columns 1, 3 and 4 of Schedule 1 must be used as the classification of the dangerous goods.

heading: Classifying Substances That Are Included in More Than One Class or Packing Group
paragraph: 2.5 If, in accordance with the criteria and tests in this Part, a substance meets the criteria for inclusion in more than one class or packing group, the substance is dangerous goods and its classification is determined in the following manner:

heading: Classifying Substances That Are Included in More Than One Class or Packing Group
paragraph: (a) the classes in which the dangerous goods are included are ranked in order of precedence in accordance with section 2.8 to determine the primary class and the potential subsidiary class or classes;

heading: Classifying Substances That Are Included in More Than One Class or Packing Group
paragraph: (b) the potential packing group is the one with the lowest roman numeral;

heading: Classifying Substances That Are Included in More Than One Class or Packing Group
paragraph: (c) the shipping name in column 2 of Schedule 1 that most precisely describes the dangerous goods and for which the corresponding data in columns 1, 3 and 4 are the most consistent with the primary class, the potential subsidiary class or classes and the potential packing group is selected; and

heading: Classifying Substances That Are Included in More Than One Class or Packing Group
paragraph: (d) the shipping name and the corresponding data in columns 1, 3 and 4 of Schedule 1 are used as the classification of the dangerous goods.

heading: Descriptive Text Following a Shipping Name
paragraph: 2.5.1 When applying section 2.4 or 2.5, the descriptive text written in lower case letters following a shipping name must be used in determining the shipping name that most precisely describes the dangerous goods.

heading: Classifying a Mixture or Solution
paragraph: 2.6 A mixture or solution of substances that are not dangerous goods and one substance that is dangerous goods and that is listed by name in Schedule 1 has the classification shown for the dangerous goods in that Schedule if the mixture or solution is still dangerous goods in accordance with paragraph 2.1(a) and the mixture or solution is not identified by a shipping name in Schedule 1. However, if the classification for the dangerous goods does not precisely describe the mixture or solution but the mixture or solution meets the criteria in this Part for inclusion in at least one of the nine classes of dangerous goods, then sections 2.4 and 2.5 must be used to determine its classification.

heading: Marine Pollutants
paragraph: 2.7 (1) A substance is a marine pollutant if

heading: Marine Pollutants
paragraph: (a) the letter "P" (marine pollutant) is set out in column 4 of Schedule 3 for the substance; or

heading: Marine Pollutants
paragraph: (b) the substance meets the criteria for classification as a marine pollutant in accordance with section 2.9.3 or chapter 2.10 of the IMDG Code.

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: 2.8 (1) When dangerous goods meet the criteria for inclusion in more than one class but meet the criteria for inclusion in only one of the following classes, that one class is the primary class. The classes are

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (a) Class 1, Explosives, except for the following dangerous goods for which Class 1 is a subsidiary class:

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (i) UN3101, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, LIQUID,

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (ii) UN3102, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, SOLID,

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (iii) UN3111, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, LIQUID, TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED,

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (iv) UN3112, ORGANIC PEROXIDE TYPE B, SOLID, TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED,

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (v) UN3221, SELF-REACTIVE LIQUID TYPE B,

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (vi) UN3222, SELF-REACTIVE SOLID TYPE B,

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (vii) UN3231, SELF-REACTIVE LIQUID TYPE B, TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED, and

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (viii) UN3232, SELF-REACTIVE SOLID TYPE B, TEMPERATURE CONTROLLED;

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (b) Class 2, Gases, and within this class, Class 2.3, Toxic Gases, takes precedence over Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, and Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, takes precedence over Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases;

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (c) Class 4.1, Flammable Solids, desensitized explosives included in Packing Group I or self-reactive substances;

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (d) Class 4.2, Substances Liable to Spontaneous Combustion, pyrophoric solids or liquids included in Packing Group I;

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (e) Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides;

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (f) Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, that are included in Packing Group I, due to inhalation toxicity;

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (g) Class 6.2, Infectious Substances; and

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (h) Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (2) Despite paragraph (1)(f), Class 8 is the primary class when a substance meets the criteria for inclusion in

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (a) Class 8, Corrosives;

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (b) Packing Group I due to inhalation toxicity of dusts or mists; and

heading: Precedence of Classes
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III due to oral or dermal toxicity.
