heading: General
paragraph: 2.9 Substances are included in Class 1, Explosives, if they are

heading: General
paragraph: (a) capable, by chemical reaction, of producing gas at a temperature, pressure and speed that would damage the surroundings; or

heading: General
paragraph: (b) designed to produce an explosive or pyrotechnic effect by heat, light, sound, gas or smoke or a combination of those means as a result of non-detonative, self-sustaining exothermic chemical reactions.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: 2.10 Class 1, Explosives, has six divisions:

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (a) Class 1.1, mass explosion hazard;

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (b) Class 1.2, projection hazard but not a mass explosion hazard;

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (c) Class 1.3, fire hazard and either a minor blast hazard or a minor projection hazard or both but not a mass explosion hazard;

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (d) Class 1.4, no significant hazard beyond the package in the event of ignition or initiation during transport;

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (e) Class 1.5, very insensitive substances with a mass explosion hazard; and

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (f) Class 1.6, extremely insensitive articles with no mass explosion hazard.

heading: Compatibility Groups
paragraph: 2.11 Explosives are divided into 13 compatibility groups as described in Appendix 2, Description of Compatibility Groups, Class 1, Explosives, to this Part.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: 2.12 Explosives are included in Packing Group II.

heading: General
paragraph: 2.13 A substance is included in Class 2, Gases, if it is

heading: General
paragraph: (a) a gas included in one of the three divisions set out in section 2.14;

heading: General
paragraph: (b) a mixture of gases;

heading: General
paragraph: (c) a mixture of one or more gases with one or more vapours of substances included in other classes;

heading: General
paragraph: (d) an article charged with a gas;

heading: General
paragraph: (e) tellurium hexafluoride; or

heading: General
paragraph: (f) an aerosol.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: 2.14 Class 2, Gases, has three divisions:

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (a) Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, which consists of gases that, at 20°C and an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (i) are ignitable when in a mixture of 13% or less by volume with air, or

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (ii) have a flammability range with air of at least 12 percentage points determined in accordance with tests or calculations in ISO 10156;

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (b) Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases, which consists of gases that are transported at an absolute pressure greater than or equal to 280 kPa at 20°C, or as refrigerated liquids, and that are not included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, or Class 2.3, Toxic Gases; and

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (c) Class 2.3, Toxic Gases, which consists of gases that

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (i) are known to be toxic or corrosive to humans according to CGA P-20, ISO Standard 10298 or other documentary evidence published in technical journals or government publications, or

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (ii) have an LC50 value less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m3.

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: 2.14.1 (1) Dangerous goods contained in an aerosol container must be transported under UN1950, AEROSOLS.

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: (2) The dangerous goods are included

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: (a) in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, if the dangerous goods contain at least 85% by mass of flammable components and the chemical heat of combustion is greater than or equal to 30 kJ/g; or

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: (b) in Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases, if the dangerous goods contain not more than 1% by mass of flammable components and the heat of combustion is less than 20 kJ/g.

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: (3) The dangerous goods must be classified in accordance with section 31 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria.

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: (4) The dangerous goods must not contain gases included in Class 2.3, Toxic Gases.

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: (5) The dangerous goods must have a subsidiary class of 6.1, Toxic Substances, or Class 8, Corrosive Substances, if the dangerous goods - other than the propellant to be ejected from the aerosol container - are included in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, Packing Groups II or III, or Class 8, Corrosive Substances, Packing Groups II or III.

heading: Aerosols
paragraph: (6) The dangerous goods are forbidden for transport when they are included in Packing Group I for toxicity or corrosiveness.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (a) in foodstuffs, including carbonated beverages other than UN1950;

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (b) in balls intended for use in sports;

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (c) in tires; or

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (d) in light bulbs.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (2) The exemption set out in paragraph (1)(d) applies only if the light bulbs are packaged so that any pieces of a ruptured bulb are contained by the packaging.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: 2.15 There are no packing groups for Class 2, Gases.

heading: Determination of LC50
paragraph: 2.16 LC50 values for a single or pure gas or for a mixture of gases must be determined

heading: Determination of LC50
paragraph: (a) by using LC50 values published in CGA P-20, ISO Standard 10298, technical journals or government publications;

heading: Determination of LC50
paragraph: (b) in accordance with paragraphs 2.2.3(b) and (c) of Chapter 2.2 of the UN Recommendations; or

heading: Determination of LC50
paragraph: (c) for a mixture of gases, in accordance with section 2.17.

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: 2.17 To determine the LC50 of a mixture of gases when the LC50 of each of the gases is known, use 5 000 mL/m3 as the toxic limit and,

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: (a) if the mixture contains only one gas with an LC50 less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Gas A"), use the following calculation:

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: LC50 of the mixture = (LC50 of Gas A) / (fraction by volume of Gas A in the mixture)

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: or

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: (b) if the mixture contains more than one gas with an LC50 less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Gas A", "Gas B", etc.),

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: (i) determine the contributing number (CN) of each of the gases with an LC50 less than or equal to the toxic limit using the formula

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: CN Gas A = (LC50 of Gas A) / (fraction by volume of Gas A in the mixture)

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: (ii) combine the contributing numbers (CN) of each gas with an LC50 less than or equal to the toxic limit using the formula

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: T = 1 / (CN Gas A) + 1 / (CN Gas B) + (as needed)

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: and

heading: Determination of LC50 of a Mixture of Gases
paragraph: (iii) obtain the LC50 of the mixture by dividing 1 by the number T (LC50 of the mixture = 1 / T).

heading: General
paragraph: 2.18 (1) Substances that are liquids or liquids containing solids in solution or suspension are included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, if they

heading: General
paragraph: (a) have a flash point less than or equal to 60ºC using the closed-cup test method referred to in Chapter 2.3 of the UN Recommendations; or

heading: General
paragraph: (b) are intended or expected to be at a temperature that is greater than or equal to their flash point at any time while the substances are in transport.

heading: General
paragraph: (2) Despite paragraph (1)(a), liquids that have a flash point greater than 35°C are not included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, if they

heading: General
paragraph: (a) do not sustain combustion, as determined in accordance with the sustained combustibility test referred to in section 2.3.1.3 of Chapter 2.3 of the UN Recommendations;

heading: General
paragraph: (b) have a fire point greater than 100°C, as determined in accordance with ISO 2592; or

heading: General
paragraph: (c) are water-miscible solutions with a water content greater than 90% by mass.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: 2.19 (1) Flammable liquids included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if they have an initial boiling point of 35°C or less at an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa and any flash point;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if they have an initial boiling point greater than 35°C at an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa and a flash point less than 23°C; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III, if the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or II are not met.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), for dangerous goods included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) when the packing group is unknown, the consignor may include the dangerous goods in Packing Group I; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) when the packing group is reasonably believed or is known to be Packing Group II or III, the consignor may include the dangerous goods in Packing Group II but, if the substance has the same characteristics as UN1203, GASOLINE, it may also be transported as Packing Group II.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (3) Despite paragraph (1)(b), a viscous flammable liquid that has a flash point less than 23°C may be included in Packing Group III if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) the liquid or any separated solvent does not meet the criteria for inclusion in Class 6.1 or Class 8;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) less than 3% of the clear solvent layer separates when the solvent separation test set out in subsection 32.5.1 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria is carried out;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) the viscosity and flash-point of the liquid are in accordance with the table to this subsection; and

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (d) the viscosity test is carried out in accordance with the procedure set out in subsection 32.4 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria or the procedure set out in ISO 2431.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (3.1) If a liquid referred to in subsection (3) is a non-Newtonian substance or a flow cup method of viscosity determination is unsuitable, a variable shear-rate viscometer must be used to determine the dynamic viscosity coefficient of the liquid, at 23°C, at a number of shear rates. The values obtained must be plotted against shear rate and then extrapolated to zero shear rate. The dynamic viscosity value thus obtained, divided by the density, gives the apparent kinematic viscosity at near-zero shear rate.

heading: General
paragraph: 2.20 Substances are included in Class 4 if they are flammable solids, substances liable to spontaneous combustion or substances that on contact with water emit flammable gases (water-reactive substances) and meet the criteria for inclusion in one of the divisions and packing groups of Class 4.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: 2.21 (1) Class 4 has three divisions:

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (a) Class 4.1, Flammable Solids, which consists of substances that are

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (i) readily combustible, as determined in accordance with section 2.4.2.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (ii) under normal conditions of transport, liable to cause fire through friction,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (iii) solid desensitized explosives, which are solid explosives desensitized through wetting with water or alcohols or diluted with other substances to form a homogeneous solid mixture to suppress their explosive properties so that they are not included in Class 1, Explosives,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (iv) self-reactive substances that are liable to undergo a strongly exothermic decomposition even without the participation of oxygen (air), as determined in accordance with section 2.4.2.3 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations, but Class 4.1 does not include substances that have

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (A) a primary class of Class 1, Explosives, Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, or Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (B) a heat of decomposition less than 300 J/g, or

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (C) a self-accelerating decomposition temperature (SADT) that is greater than 75°C for a 50 kg means of containment, as determined in accordance with section 2.4.2.3.4 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (iv.1) polymerizing substances that, without stabilization, are liable to undergo a strongly exothermic reaction resulting in the formation of larger molecules or resulting in the formation of polymers under conditions normally encountered in transport,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (v) identified by one of the following UN numbers: UN2956, UN3241, UN3242 or UN3251, or

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (vi) are in the list of currently assigned self-reactive substances in section 2.4.2.3.2.3 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations;

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (b) Class 4.2, Substances Liable to Spontaneous Combustion, which consists of

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (i) pyrophoric substances that spontaneously ignite within 5 minutes after coming into contact with air, as determined in accordance with section 2.4.3.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations, and

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (ii) self-heating substances that, when in large amounts (kilograms), spontaneously ignite on contact with air after long periods (hours or days), as determined in accordance with section 2.4.3.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations; and

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (c) Class 4.3, Water-reactive Substances, which consists of substances that, in tests performed in accordance with section 2.4.4.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations, emit a flammable gas at a rate greater than 1 L/kg of substance per hour or spontaneously ignite at any step in the test procedure.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subparagraph (1)(a)(iv.1), a substance is considered to be a polymerizing substance of Class 4.1 if it

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (a) has a self-accelerating polymerization temperature (SAPT) that is less than or equal to 75°C under the conditions in which the substance or mixture is to be transported, with or without chemical stabilization as offered for transport, and in the means of containment in which the substance or mixture is to be transported;

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (b) exhibits a heat of reaction of more than 300 J/g; and

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (c) does not meet any other criteria for inclusion in Classes 1 to 8.

heading: Polymerizing Substances
paragraph: 2.21.1 A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport the following polymerizing substances unless they are stabilized by temperature control:

heading: Polymerizing Substances
paragraph: (a) polymerizing substance that is in a small means of containment prescribed by TP 14850 or Chapter 6.1 of the UN Recommendations or in an intermediate bulk container (IBC) and whose self-accelerating polymerization temperature (SAPT) is 50°C or less in the small means of containment or IBC; and

heading: Polymerizing Substances
paragraph: (b) a polymerizing substance that is in a large means of containment that is not an IBC and whose SAPT is 45°C or less in the large means of containment.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: 2.22 (1) Substances included in Class 4.1, Flammable Solids, are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if the substances meet the criterion in subparagraph 2.21(1)(a)(iii), except that substances that have one of the following UN numbers are included in Packing Group II: UN2555, UN2556, UN2557, UN2907, UN3270, UN3319 or UN3344;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) the substances meet the criteria for inclusion in Class 4.1 in subparagraph 2.21(1)(a)(iv) or (v), except that substances that have one of the following UN numbers are included in Packing Group III: UN2956, UN3241 or UN3251,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria for readily combustible solids, excluding metal powders, the burning time of the substances is less than 45 seconds and the flame passes the wetted zone, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (iii) in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria, for readily combustible solids that are powders of metals or metal alloys, the zone of reaction of the substances spreads over the whole length of the sample in 5 minutes or less; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria, for readily combustible solids, excluding metal powders, the burning time of the substances is less than 45 seconds and the wetted zone stops the flame propagation for at least 4 minutes,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) in tests referred to in section 33.2.1 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria, for readily combustible solids that are powders of metals or metal alloys, the zone of reaction of the substances spreads over the whole length of the sample in more than 5 minutes but not more than 10 minutes, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (iii) the substances are solids that are liable to cause fire through friction.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (2) Substances included in Class 4.2, Substances Liable to Spontaneous Combustion, are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if the substances are pyrophoric solids or liquids;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if the substances are self-heating substances that give a positive result, as determined in accordance with section 2.4.3.2 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations using a 25 mm sample cube at 140°C; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III for all other substances.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (3) Substances included in Class 4.3, Water-reactive Substances, are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if the substances

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) react vigorously with water at ambient temperatures and demonstrate a tendency for the gas produced to ignite spontaneously, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) react readily with water at ambient temperatures so that the rate of evolution of flammable gas is greater than or equal to 10 L/kg of substance over any one minute;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) the substances react readily with water at ambient temperatures so that the rate of evolution of flammable gas is greater than or equal to 20 L/kg of substance per hour, and

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I are not met; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) the substances react slowly with water at ambient temperatures so that the rate of evolution of flammable gas is greater than or equal to 1 L/kg of substance per hour, and

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or II are not met.

heading: General
paragraph: 2.23 Substances are included in Class 5 if they are oxidizing substances or organic peroxides and meet the criteria for inclusion in one of the divisions of Class 5.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: 2.24 Class 5 has two divisions:

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (a) Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, which consists of substances that yield oxygen thereby causing or contributing to the combustion of other material, as determined in accordance with section 2.5.2 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations; and

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (b) Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, which consists of substances that

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (i) are thermally unstable organic compounds that contain oxygen in the bivalent "-O-O-" structure, as determined in accordance with section 2.5.3 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (ii) are liable to undergo exothermic self-accelerating decomposition,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (iii) have one or more of the following characteristics:

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (A) they are liable to explosive decomposition,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (B) they burn rapidly,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (C) they are sensitive to impact or friction,

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (D) they react dangerously with other substances, or

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (E) they cause damage to the eyes, or

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (iv) are in the list of currently assigned organic peroxides in section 2.5.3.2.4 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: 2.25 (1) The packing group for a substance that is included in Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, must be determined by using a test sample of the substance that

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) in the case of a solid, is prepared in accordance with section 2.5.2.2 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations; and

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) in the case of a liquid, is prepared in accordance with section 2.5.2.3 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (2) In the case of a solid substance included in Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, the test procedure set out in either subsection 34.4.1 (test O.1) or subsection 34.4.3 (test O.3) of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria must be carried out on the test sample. The substance is included in

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if the test sample exhibits an average burning time that is

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) less than the mean burning time of a 3:2 potassium bromate/cellulose mixture by mass when test O.1 is used, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) greater than the mean burning rate of a 3:1 calcium peroxide/cellulose mixture by mass when test O.3 is used;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if the criteria for Packing Group I are not met and the test sample exhibits an average burning time that is

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) less than or equal to the mean burning time of a 2:3 potassium bromate/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.1 is used, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) equal to or greater than the mean burning rate of a 1:1 calcium peroxide/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.3 is used; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III, if the criteria for Packing Groups I and II are not met and the test sample exhibits an average burning time that is

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) less than or equal to the mean burning time of a 3:7 potassium bromate/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.1 is used, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) equal to or greater than the mean burning rate of a 1:2 calcium peroxide/cellulose mixture by mass, when test O.3 is used.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (2.1) In the case of a liquid substance included in Class 5.1, Oxidizing Substances, the test procedure set out in sub-section 34.4.2 (test O.2) of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria must be carried out on the test sample. The substance is included in

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if the test sample in a 1:1 mixture by mass of substance and cellulose spontaneously ignites or the mean pressure rise time is less than that of a 1:1 mixture by mass of 50% perchloric acid and cellulose;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if the mean pressure rise time is less than or equal to the mean pressure rise time of a 1:1 mixture by mass of 40% aqueous sodium chlorate solution and cellulose and the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I are not met; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III, if the mean pressure rise time is less than or equal to the mean pressure rise time of a 1:1 mixture by mass of 65% aqueous nitric acid solution and cellulose and the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or II are not met.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (3) Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, are included in Packing Group II.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (4) The type, B to F, of organic peroxides must be determined in accordance with section 2.5.3.3 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations.

heading: General
paragraph: 2.26 Substances are included in Class 6 if they are

heading: General
paragraph: (a) liable to cause death or serious injury or to harm human health if swallowed or inhaled or if they come into contact with human skin; or

heading: General
paragraph: (b) infectious substances.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: 2.27 Class 6 has two divisions:

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (a) Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, which consists of substances that are liable to cause death or serious injury or to harm human health if swallowed or inhaled or if they come into contact with human skin; and

heading: Divisions
paragraph: (b) Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, which consists of infectious substances.

heading: Criteria for Inclusion in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances
paragraph: 2.28 A substance is included in Class 6.1

heading: Criteria for Inclusion in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances
paragraph: (a) due to oral toxicity if its LD50 (oral) is less than or equal to 300 mg/kg;

heading: Criteria for Inclusion in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances
paragraph: (b) due to dermal toxicity if its LD50 (dermal) is less than or equal to 1 000 mg/kg; or

heading: Criteria for Inclusion in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances
paragraph: (c) due to inhalation toxicity

heading: Criteria for Inclusion in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances
paragraph: (i) by dust or mist if dust or mist is likely to be produced in a transport accident and its LC50 (inhalation) is less than or equal to 4 mg/L, or

heading: Criteria for Inclusion in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances
paragraph: (ii) by vapour if its LC50 (inhalation) is less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m3.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: 2.29 (1) When a substance is known to be included in Class 6.1 and that knowledge is based on documentary evidence published in technical journals or government publications and testing is not done to determine the packing group, the substance must be included in Packing Group I.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (2) Substances that are included in Class 6.1 due to

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) oral toxicity are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) Packing Group I, if the LD50 (oral) is less than or equal to 5 mg/kg,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) Packing Group II, if the LD50 (oral) is greater than 5 mg/kg but less than or equal to 50 mg/kg, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (iii) Packing Group III, if the LD50 (oral) is greater than 50 mg/kg but less than or equal to 300 mg/kg;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) dermal toxicity are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) Packing Group I if the LD50 (dermal) is less than or equal to 50 mg/kg,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) Packing Group II if the LD50 (dermal) is greater than 50 mg/kg but less than or equal to 200 mg/kg, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (iii) Packing Group III if the LD50 (dermal) is greater than 200 mg/kg but less than or equal to 1 000 mg/kg;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) inhalation toxicity by dust or mist are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) Packing Group I if the LC50 (inhalation) is less than or equal to 0.2 mg/L,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) Packing Group II if the LC50 (inhalation) is greater than 0.2 mg/L but less than or equal to 2 mg/L, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (iii) Packing Group III if the LC50 (inhalation) is greater than 2 mg/L but less than or equal to 4 mg/L; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (d) inhalation toxicity by vapour are included in one of the following packing groups, where "V" is the saturated vapour concentration in millilitres per cubic metre of air at 20°C and at 101.3 kPa:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) Packing Group I, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (A) V is greater than or equal to 10 multiplied by the LC50, and

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (B) the LC50 is less than or equal to 1 000 mL/m3,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) Packing Group II, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (A) V is greater than or equal to the LC50,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (B) the LC50 is less than or equal to 3 000 mL/m3, and

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (C) the criteria for Packing Group I are not met, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (iii) Packing Group III, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (A) V is greater than or equal to 0.2 multiplied by the LC50,

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (B) the LC50 is less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m3, and

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (C) the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or II are not met.

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal)
paragraph: 2.30 LD50 (oral or dermal) values for solid or liquid substances or for a mixture of solid or liquid substances must be determined

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal)
paragraph: (a) by using the LD50 values published in technical journals or in government publications;

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal)
paragraph: (b) in accordance with section 2.6.2.3 of Chapter 2.6 of the UN Recommendations; or

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal)
paragraph: (c) for a mixture of solid or liquid substances, in accordance with section 2.31.

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: 2.31 To determine the LD50 of a mixture of solid or liquid substances when the LD50 of each of the substances is known, use 1 000 mg/kg as the toxic limit and

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: (a) if the mixture contains only one substance with an LD50 less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Substance A"), use the following calculation:

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: LD50 of the mixture = (LD50 of Substance A) / (fraction by mass of Substance A in the mixture)

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: or

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: (b) if the mixture contains more than one substance with an LD50 less than or equal to the toxic limit (called "Substance A", "Substance B", etc.),

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: (i) determine the lowest LD50 of all substances, assign that LD50 to all substances whose actual LD50 is less than or equal to the toxic limit, then use the calculation in paragraph (a) using that assigned LD50 and taking as the mass of Substance A in the formula the total of the masses of all substances whose actual LD50 is less than or equal to the toxic limit, or

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: (ii) use the following calculations:

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: (A) determine the contributing number (CN) of each of the substances with an LD50 less than or equal to the toxic limit using the formula

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: CN for Substance A= (LD50 of Substance A) / (fraction by mass of Substance A in the mixture)

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: (B) combine the contributing numbers (CN) of each substance with an LD50 less than or equal to the toxic limit as

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: T = 1 / (CN Substance A) + 1 / (CN Substance B) + (as needed)

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: and

heading: Determination of LD50 (oral or dermal) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: (C) obtain the LD50 of the mixture by dividing 1 by the number T (LD50 of the mixture = 1 / T).

heading: Determination of LC50 (dust, mist or vapour)
paragraph: 2.32 LC50 values for a substance in the form of a dust, mist or vapour or for a mixture of substances in the form of a dust, mist or vapour must be determined

heading: Determination of LC50 (dust, mist or vapour)
paragraph: (a) by using the LC50 values published in technical journals or in government publications;

heading: Determination of LC50 (dust, mist or vapour)
paragraph: (b) in accordance with sections 2.6.2.2.4.2 to 2.6.2.2.4.7 of Chapter 2.6 of the UN Recommendations; or

heading: Determination of LC50 (dust, mist or vapour)
paragraph: (c) for a mixture of substances, in accordance with section 2.33.

heading: Determination of LC50 (dust, mist or vapour) of a Mixture of Substances
paragraph: 2.33 To determine the LC50 of a mixture of substances that are in the form of a dust, mist or vapour, when the LC50 of each of the substances is known, make the determination in accordance with section 2.17, except that for a dust use 10 mg/L as the toxic limit and for a mist use 2 mg/L as the toxic limit. For a substance in the form of vapour the toxic limit is the same as for a gas, which is 5 000 mL/m3.

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: 2.34 (1) The first step in determining the packing group of a mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity by vapour when one or more of the substances has an LC50 (vapour) less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m3, and the LC50 of each substance is known, is to determine the following data:

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (a) determine the LC50 (vapour) for the mixture in accordance with section 2.33;

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (b) where Pi is the vapour pressure of the ith substance in kPa at 20°C and an absolute pressure of 101.3 kPa, determine the volatility, Vi, of each substance in the mixture as

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: Vi = Pi multiplied by 106 then divided by 101.3;

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (c) determine the ratio of the volatility of a substance to its LC50 for each substance with an LC50 less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m3 as

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: Ri = Vi divided by the LC50 of the ith substance;

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: and

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (d) set R equal to the sum of the Ri for each of the substances with an LC50 less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m3 as

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: R = R1 + R2 + ... + (as needed).

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (2) Using the data determined in accordance with subsection (1), the mixture is included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (i) R is greater than or equal to 10, and

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (ii) the LC50 (mixture) is less than or equal to 1 000 mL/m3;

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (i) R is greater than or equal to 1,

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (ii) the LC50 (mixture) is less than or equal to 3 000 mL/m3, and

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (iii) the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I are not met; or

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III, if

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (i) R is greater than or equal to 0.2,

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (ii) the LC50 (mixture) is less than or equal to 5 000 mL/m3, and

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity by Vapour
paragraph: (iii) the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or II are not met.

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: 2.35 (1) A mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity and an unknown LC50 is included in Packing Group I if it meets the following criteria:

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (a) when a sample of the mixture is vapourized and diluted with air to create a test atmosphere of 1 000 mL/m3 and 10 young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation period; and

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (b) when a sample of the vapour in equilibrium with the mixture at 20°C is diluted with 9 equal volumes of air to form a test atmosphere and 10 young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation period.

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (2) A mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity and an unknown LC50 is included in Packing Group II if it meets the following criteria and the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I are not met:

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (a) when a sample of the mixture is vapourized and diluted with air to create a test atmosphere of 3 000 mL/m3 and 10 young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation period; and

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (b) when a sample of the vapour in equilibrium with the mixture at 20°C is used to form a test atmosphere and 10 young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation period.

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (3) A mixture of liquids with an inhalation toxicity and an unknown LC50 is included in Packing Group III if it meets the following criteria and the criteria for inclusion in Packing Group I or II are not met:

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (a) when a sample of the mixture is vapourized and diluted with air to create a test atmosphere of 5 000 mL/m3 and 10 young adult albino rats (5 male and 5 female) are exposed to the test atmosphere for 1 hour and observed for 14 days, the result is the death of 5 or more of the animals within the 14-day observation period; and

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (b) when the vapour pressure of the mixture is measured, the vapour concentration is greater than or equal to 1 000 mL/m3.

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (4) If only LC50 data relating to 4-hour exposures to dust or mist are available, those figures can be multiplied by 4 and the result taken as the LC50 data for 1 hour, that is LC50 4 hours (dust or mist) multiplied by 4 is equivalent to LC50 1 hour.

heading: Determination of the Packing Group of a Mixture of Liquids with an Inhalation Toxicity and an Unknown LC50
paragraph: (5) If only LC50 data relating to 4-hour exposures to vapour are available, those figures can be multiplied by 2 and the result taken as the LC50 data for 1 hour, that is LC50 4 hours (vapour) multiplied by 2 is equivalent to LC50 1 hour.

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste

paragraph: (b) under UN3291, if they contain Category B infectious substances; or

heading: Medical or Clinical Waste
paragraph: (c) under UN3291, if the shipper has reasonable grounds to believe that they have a low probability of containing infectious substances.

heading: General
paragraph: 2.37 Substances defined as Class 7, Radioactive Materials in the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations are included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: 2.38 There are no divisions for Class 7.

paragraph: 2.39 There are no packing groups for Class 7.

heading: General
paragraph: 2.40 Substances are included in Class 8, Corrosives, if they

heading: General
paragraph: (a) are known to cause full thickness destruction of human skin, that is, skin lesions that are permanent and destroy all layers of the outer skin through to the internal tissues;

heading: General
paragraph: (b) cause full thickness skin destruction, as determined in accordance with OECD Guideline 430 or OECD Guideline 431; or

heading: General
paragraph: (c) do not cause full thickness destruction of skin, but exhibit a corrosion rate that exceeds 6.25 mm per year at a test temperature of 55°C, as determined in accordance with section 37 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria.

heading: Divisions
paragraph: 2.41 There are no divisions for Class 8.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: 2.42 (1) If a substance is known to be included in Class 8, Corrosives, and that knowledge is based on documentary evidence published in technical journals or government publications and testing is not done to determine the packing group, the substance must be included in Packing Group I.

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (2) Class 8, Corrosives, are included in one of the following packing groups:

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (a) Packing Group I, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) they are known to cause full thickness destruction of human skin, that is, skin lesions that are permanent and that destroy all layers of the outer skin through to the internal tissues, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) full thickness destruction of intact skin tissue occurs within an observation period of 60 minutes after an exposure time of 3 minutes or less, as determined in accordance with OECD Guideline 404 or OECD Guideline 435;

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (b) Packing Group II, if full thickness destruction of skin occurs within an observation period of 14 days after an exposure time of more than 3 minutes but not more than 60 minutes, as determined in accordance with OECD Guideline 404 or OECD Guideline 435; or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (c) Packing Group III, if

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (i) full thickness destruction of intact skin tissue occurs within an observation period of 14 days after an exposure time of more than 60 minutes but not more than 4 hours, as determined in accordance with OECD Guideline 404 or OECD Guideline 435, or

heading: Packing Groups
paragraph: (ii) they exhibit a corrosion rate that exceeds 6.25 mm per year at a test temperature of 55°C on steel or aluminum surfaces as determined in accordance with subparagraph 2.8.2.5(c)(ii) of the UN Recommendations.

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: 2.43.1 (1) A person must not handle, offer for transport or transport lithium cells and batteries under any of the following shipping names unless the cells and batteries meet the conditions set out in subsection (2):

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (a) UN3090, LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES;

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (b) UN3091, LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES CONTAINED IN EQUIPMENT or LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES PACKED WITH EQUIPMENT;

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (c) UN3480, LITHIUM ION BATTERIES; or

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (d) UN3481, LITHIUM ION BATTERIES CONTAINED IN EQUIPMENT or LITHIUM ION BATTERIES PACKED WITH EQUIPMENT.

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (2) The conditions are as follows:

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (a) the cell or battery type passes each test set out in subsection 38.3 of Part III of the Manual of Tests and Criteria;

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (b) each cell or battery has a safety venting device or is designed to prevent a violent rupture under normal conditions of transport;

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (c) each cell or battery is equipped to prevent external short circuits; and

heading: Lithium Cells and Batteries
paragraph: (d) each battery containing cells or a series of cells connected in parallel is equipped with diodes, fuses or other devices that prevent dangerous reverse current flow.
