heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: 3.1 (1) Before allowing a carrier to take possession of dangerous goods for transport, the consignor must prepare and give to that carrier a shipping document or, if the carrier agrees, an electronic copy of the shipping document.

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: (2) When dangerous goods are imported into Canada, the consignor must, before the dangerous goods are transported in Canada, ensure that the carrier has a shipping document or, with the agreement of the carrier, an electronic copy of the shipping document that contains the information required by these Regulations.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: 3.2 (1) A carrier must not take possession of dangerous goods for transport unless the carrier has the shipping document for the dangerous goods.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (2) A carrier who accepts an electronic copy of a shipping document must produce a shipping document from the electronic copy before taking possession of the dangerous goods for transport.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (3) Dangerous goods in transport are in the possession of a carrier from the time the carrier takes possession of them for transport until another person takes possession of them.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (4) While the dangerous goods are in transport and in the possession of a carrier, the carrier must keep the shipping document in the location specified by sections 3.7 to 3.10.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (5) At or before the time another carrier takes possession of the dangerous goods, the carrier must give the shipping document or a copy of the shipping document to that other carrier or, with that other carrier's agreement, an electronic copy of it.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (6) At or before the time a person, other than another carrier, takes possession of the dangerous goods, the carrier of the dangerous goods must give to that person a document that identifies the dangerous goods or, with that person's agreement, an electronic copy of a document that identifies the dangerous goods.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (7) A carrier may replace a shipping document provided by the consignor with a new shipping document or with a copy of the shipping document in a different format.

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: 3.3 (1) When a train includes a railway vehicle containing dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be displayed in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), the person in charge of the train must prepare and give a consist to a member of the train crew. The information on the consist must be kept up to date by the train crew and kept with the shipping document.

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (2) The consist must include, for each railway vehicle containing dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be displayed in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks),

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (a) the numerical location of the railway vehicle in the train, numbering the first vehicle at the head of the train as 1, the next vehicle as 2 and so on, excluding the locomotive or locomotives wherever they are located in the train;

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (b) the reporting mark of the railway vehicle;

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (c) for a tank car, the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous goods in the tank car; and

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (d) for a railway vehicle other than a tank car,

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (i) the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous goods, if the railway vehicle contains only dangerous goods with the same shipping name and UN number, or

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (ii) the words "Dangerous Goods" or "Marchandises dangereuses", if the railway vehicle contains dangerous goods that have different shipping names or UN numbers.

heading: Consist for Transport by Rail
paragraph: (3) A carrier must be able to immediately provide to CANUTEC a copy of a consist whenever the train to which the consist applies is in operation or is involved in an accident.

heading: Legibility and Language
paragraph: 3.4 (1) The information required on a shipping document and on a consist must be easy to identify, legible, in indelible print and in English or French.

heading: Legibility and Language
paragraph: (2) When the information related to dangerous goods is on the same shipping document with information related to non-dangerous goods, the dangerous goods information must be shown

heading: Legibility and Language
paragraph: (a) before the information related to the non-dangerous goods and under the heading "Dangerous Goods" or "Marchandises dangereuses";

heading: Legibility and Language
paragraph: (b) printed or highlighted in a colour that contrasts with the print or highlight used for the information related to the non-dangerous goods; or

heading: Legibility and Language
paragraph: (c) following the letter "X" opposite the UN number in a column under the heading "DG" or "MD".

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: 3.5 (1) The following information must be included on a shipping document:

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the place of business in Canada of the consignor;

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (b) the date the shipping document or an electronic copy of it was prepared or was first given to a carrier;

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (c) the description of each of the dangerous goods, in the following order:

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (i) the UN number,

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (ii) the shipping name and, immediately after the shipping name unless it is already part of it,

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (A) for dangerous goods that are subject to special provision 16, the technical name, in parentheses, of at least one of the most dangerous substances that predominantly contributes to the danger or dangers posed by the dangerous goods, and

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (B) for a liquefied petroleum gas that has not been odorized, the words "Not Odourized" or "Not Odorized" or "Sans odorisant",

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (iii) the primary class, which may be shown as a number only or under the heading "Class" or "Classe" or following the word "Class" or "Classe",

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (iv) for dangerous goods with a primary class of Class 1, Explosives, the compatibility group letter following the primary class,

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (v) the subsidiary class or classes, in parentheses, which may be shown as a number only or under the heading "subsidiary class" or "classe subsidiaire" or following the words "subsidiary class" or "classe subsidiaire", except that, for transport by aircraft or by vessel, the subsidiary class or classes may be shown after the information required by this paragraph,

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (vi) the packing group roman numeral, which may be shown under the heading "PG" or "GE" or following the letters "PG" or "GE" or following the words "Packing Group" or "Groupe d'emballage", and

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (vii) for dangerous goods that are subject to special provision 23, the words "toxic by inhalation" or "toxic - inhalation hazard" or "toxique par inhalation" or "toxicite par inhalation";

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (d) for each shipping name, the quantity of dangerous goods and the unit of measure used to express the quantity which, on a shipping document prepared in Canada, must be a unit of measure included in the International System of Units (SI) or a unit of measure acceptable for use under the SI system, except that for dangerous goods included in Class 1, Explosives, the quantity must be expressed in net explosives quantity or, for explosives with UN numbers subject to special provision 85 or 86, in number of articles or net explosives quantity;

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (e) for dangerous goods in one or more small means of containment that require a label to be displayed on them in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), the number of small means of containment for each shipping name; and

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (f) the words "24-Hour Number" or "Numero 24 heures", or an abbreviation of these words, followed by a telephone number, including the area code, at which the consignor can be reached immediately for technical information about the dangerous goods in transport, without breaking the telephone connection made by the caller.

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (2) The telephone number of a person who is not the consignor, such as CANUTEC, but who is competent to give the technical information required by paragraph (1)(f) in English or in French may be used. However, to use CANUTEC's telephone number, the consignor must receive permission, in writing, from CANUTEC. A consignor who uses the telephone number of an organization or agency other than CANUTEC must ensure that the organization or agency has current, accurate information on the dangerous goods the consignor offers for transport and, if the organization or agency is located outside Canada, the telephone number must include the country code and, if required, the city code.

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (3) A means of containment, or the contents of a means of containment, that is being fumigated with dangerous goods and that is in transport must be accompanied by a shipping document that, despite subsections (1) and (5) and section 3.6, includes the following information if the fumigant is the only dangerous goods in transport in the means of containment:

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (a) the shipping name, "FUMIGATED CARGO TRANSPORT UNIT" or "ENGIN DE TRANSPORT SOUS FUMIGATION";

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (b) the class, Class 9;

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (c) the UN number, UN3359;

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (d) the quantity of the fumigant;

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (e) the date of fumigation; and

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (f) instructions for the disposal of residues of the fumigant or fumigation device.

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (4) Despite paragraph (1)(d), if the means of containment contains a residue, the words "Residue - Last Contained" or "Residu - dernier contenu" may be added before or after the description of the dangerous goods. These words must not, however, be used for dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, that are in a small means of containment or for dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

heading: Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (5) If the quantity of dangerous goods required on a shipping document under paragraph (1)(d) or the number of small means of containment required under paragraph (1)(e) changes during transport, the carrier must show those changes on the shipping document or on a document attached to the shipping document.

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: 3.6 (1) In addition to the information required by subsection 3.5(1), the shipping document for dangerous goods for which an approved ERAP is required under subsection 7(1) of the Act must include

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (a) the ERAP reference number issued by Transport Canada, preceded or followed by the letters "ERAP" or "PIU"; and

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (b) the ERAP telephone number required under paragraph 7.3(2)(f).

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (2) If the 24-hour number required by paragraph 3.5(1)(f) and the ERAP telephone number are the same, that number may be shown on the same line on the shipping document.

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (3) In addition to the information required by subsection 3.5(1), the following information must be included on a shipping document:

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (a) for dangerous goods in transport by vessel,

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (i) the flash point for dangerous goods included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, and

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (ii) for dangerous goods that are marine pollutants under section 2.7 of Part 2 (Classification), the words "marine pollutant" or "polluant marin" and, for a pesticide that is a marine pollutant, the name and concentration of the most active substance in the pesticide;

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (b) for dangerous goods included in Class 4.1, Flammable Solids, the control and emergency temperatures shown in section 2.4.2.3.2.3 of Chapter 2.4 of the UN Recommendations, if applicable;

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (c) for dangerous goods included in Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, the control and emergency temperatures shown in section 2.5.3.2.4 of Chapter 2.5 of the UN Recommendations, if applicable; and

heading: Additional Information on a Shipping Document
paragraph: (d) for dangerous goods included in Class 7, the additional information required for transport documents under the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015.

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: 3.6.1 (1) A shipping document must include, after the information required under section 3.5, one of the following certifications:

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: (a) "I hereby declare that the contents of this consignment are fully and accurately described above by the proper shipping name, are properly classified and packaged, have dangerous goods safety marks properly affixed or displayed on them, and are in all respects in proper condition for transport according to the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations.";

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: (b) the certification set out in section 172.204 of 49 CFR;

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: (c) the certification set out in section 5;4.1.6 of the ICAO Technical Instructions;

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: (d) the certification set out in section 5.4.1.6 of the IMDG Code; or

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: (e) the certification set out in section 5.4.1.6 of the UN Recommendations.

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: (2) The certification must be made by an individual who is the consignor or by an individual acting on behalf of the consignor and must set out that individual's name.

heading: Consignor's Certification
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply in respect of a large means of containment that contains a residue.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Road
paragraph: 3.7 The driver of a power unit that is attached to or is part of the cargo unit of a road vehicle transporting dangerous goods must ensure that a copy of the shipping document is kept, as follows:

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Road
paragraph: (a) if the driver is in the power unit, in a pocket mounted on the driver's door or within the driver's reach; or

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Road
paragraph: (b) if the driver is out of the power unit, in a pocket mounted on the driver's door, on the driver's seat or in a location that is clearly visible to anyone entering through the driver's door.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document and Consist: Rail
paragraph: 3.8 The person in charge of a train transporting dangerous goods must ensure that a copy of the shipping document and, when a consist is required, a copy of the consist are kept,

heading: Location of a Shipping Document and Consist: Rail
paragraph: (a) when one or more members of the train crew are present, in the possession of one of them; or

heading: Location of a Shipping Document and Consist: Rail
paragraph: (b) when no member of the train crew is present, in the first locomotive.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Marine
paragraph: 3.9 (1) The master of a vessel containing dangerous goods or the master in control of a vessel containing dangerous goods must have readily available on or near the bridge of the vessel a paper copy or electronic copy of

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Marine
paragraph: (a) the shipping document; or

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Marine
paragraph: (b) a list that includes the classification of the dangerous goods.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Marine
paragraph: (2) If dangerous goods are transported by vessel on board a road vehicle that is accompanied by one or more drivers or a railway vehicle that is accompanied by one or more members of the train crew, a driver or a member of the train crew must notify the master of the vessel or the marine carrier of the presence of the dangerous goods and make available to the master a copy of the shipping document. However, the shipping document must be kept, for the road vehicle, in accordance with section 3.7 and, for the railway vehicle, in the possession of a member of the train crew.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: 3.10 (1) A carrier must ensure that a shipping document is placed in a waterproof receptacle that is securely attached to or near the means of containment containing the dangerous goods, at a readily identifiable and accessible location, when the dangerous goods are in transport if

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (a) they are left in an unsupervised area

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (i) after being unloaded from a means of transport,

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (ii) after the cargo unit of a road vehicle containing them has been disconnected from the power unit, or

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (iii) when the railway vehicle containing them is no longer part of a train; and

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (b) possession of the dangerous goods has not been transferred to another person.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (2) When dangerous goods in transport are left in a supervised area, the person in charge of the supervised area is considered to have taken possession of the dangerous goods. The carrier must leave a copy of the shipping document with that person, who must keep it and give it to the next person who takes possession of the dangerous goods.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (3) When the person in charge of a supervised area is absent from the area, that person must ensure that the copy of the shipping document is

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (a) placed in a waterproof receptacle securely attached to or near the means of containment containing the dangerous goods, at a readily identifiable and accessible location; or

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (b) left in the possession of an employee who is present in the supervised area and is designated for this purpose by the person in charge of the supervised area.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (4) Despite the locations specified in subsections (1) to (3), when dangerous goods that are in transport by road vehicle, railway vehicle or vessel are stored in a supervised or unsupervised area, the shipping document or an electronic copy of it may be left at the office of a person referred to in one of the following paragraphs if the conditions in subsections (5) and (6) are complied with:

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (a) the rail dispatcher for the area in which the railway vehicle is located;

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (b) the person responsible for the port at which the dangerous goods are located; or

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (c) the marine terminal manager at the terminal where the dangerous goods are located.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (5) When a shipping record is left at the office of a person referred to in subsection (4),

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (a) use of the telephone number of that office must be approved in accordance with subsection (6); and

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (b) that person or that person's representative must provide immediately, at the request of a federal, provincial or municipal official including a member of a fire department, a facsimile or electronic copy of the shipping record or, if requested, a voice description of the information on the shipping record.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (6) The telephone number of the office of a person referred to in subsection (4) must not be used to comply with subsection (5), unless that person gives CANUTEC the following information and receives approval, in writing, from CANUTEC to use that telephone number:

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the person;

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (b) the telephone number of the office of the person;

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (c) the physical area to which the telephone number applies and, in the case of a port or a marine terminal, evidence that public access to the area is controlled;

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (d) the period of time, not to exceed 5 years, for which CANUTEC's approval is requested; and

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (e) the dangerous goods to which the approval applies.

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (7) The Minister may revoke, in writing, the approval to use a telephone number if

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (a) the person referred to in subsection (4), or that person's representative, does not answer the telephone;

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (b) the person referred to in subsection (4), or that person's representative, does not provide immediately, at the request of a federal, provincial or municipal official including a member of a fire department, a facsimile or an electronic copy of the shipping record or, if requested, a voice description of the information on the shipping record; or

heading: Location of a Shipping Document: Storage in the Course of Transportation
paragraph: (c) public access to a port or marine terminal is not controlled.

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: 3.11 (1) A consignor must be able to produce a copy of any shipping document

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (a) for two years after the date the shipping document or an electronic copy of it was prepared or given to a carrier by the consignor;

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (b) for dangerous goods imported into Canada, for two years after the date the consignor ensured that the carrier, on entry into Canada, had a shipping document or an electronic copy of one; and

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (c) within 15 days after the day on which the consignor receives a written request from an inspector.

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (2) When dangerous goods are no longer in transport, each carrier who transported the dangerous goods must be able to produce a copy of the shipping document that related to the dangerous goods and was required to be in the possession of that carrier while the dangerous goods were in transport

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (a) for two years after the date the dangerous goods are no longer in transport; and

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (b) within 15 days after the day on which the carrier receives a written request from an inspector.

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply to a carrier who transported dangerous goods

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (a) from a place outside Canada, through Canada to a place outside Canada or for a portion of such transportation; or

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (b) entirely outside Canada

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (i) on board a vessel, or

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (ii) on board an aircraft that is registered in Canada and leased to a foreign carrier.

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (4) Subsection (2) does not apply to a carrier who is involved only in handling the dangerous goods, including storing them in the course of transport.

heading: Keeping Shipping Document Information
paragraph: (5) The shipping documents referred to in this section may be kept as electronic copies.

heading: Requirements for Dangerous Goods Safety Marks
paragraph: 4.1 A person must not offer for transport, transport or import a means of containment that contains dangerous goods unless each dangerous goods safety mark required by this Part and illustrated in the appendix to this Part, or illustrated in Chapter 5.2 or 5.3 of the UN Recommendations, is displayed on it in accordance with this Part.

heading: Voluntary Display of a Placard
paragraph: 4.1.1 When a person transports dangerous goods in or on a road vehicle or railway vehicle and the person voluntarily displays a placard on the vehicle, the following provisions apply:

heading: Voluntary Display of a Placard
paragraph: (a) section 4.2;

heading: Voluntary Display of a Placard
paragraph: (b) sections 4.6 and 4.7;

heading: Voluntary Display of a Placard
paragraph: (c) subsection 4.9(2);

heading: Voluntary Display of a Placard
paragraph: (d) sections 4.14 to 4.15.1;

heading: Voluntary Display of a Placard
paragraph: (e) paragraphs 4.15.3(a) and (b); and

heading: Voluntary Display of a Placard
paragraph: (f) section 4.16.

heading: Misleading Dangerous Goods Safety Marks
paragraph: 4.2 (1) As provided for in section 6.1 of the Act, a person must not display a dangerous goods safety mark on a means of containment or a means of transport if the mark is misleading as to the presence or nature of any danger.

heading: Misleading Dangerous Goods Safety Marks
paragraph: (2) As provided for in section 6.1 of the Act, a person must not display a mark other than a dangerous goods safety mark on a means of containment or a means of transport if the other mark is likely to be mistaken for a dangerous goods safety mark or is misleading as to the presence or nature of any danger.

heading: Display of Dangerous Goods Safety Marks Before Loading or Packing a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.3 A person must not load or pack dangerous goods into a large means of containment for transport unless, immediately before the loading or packing, the large means of containment has displayed on it the dangerous goods safety marks that will be required when the loading or packing is complete.

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: 4.4 (1) Before importing dangerous goods or allowing a carrier in Canada to take possession of dangerous goods for transport, the consignor must

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: (a) display or ensure the display of the required dangerous goods marks on each small means of containment that contains the dangerous goods;

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: (b) display or ensure the display of the required dangerous goods marks on each large means of containment that contains the dangerous goods; and

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: (c) provide to the carrier the dangerous goods marks for the dangerous goods that the consignor is importing or offering for transport and that are to be transported in a large means of containment.

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: (2) The consignor is not required to provide the dangerous goods marks referred to in paragraph (1)(c) if they

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: (a) are already displayed on the large means of containment; or

heading: Consignor Responsibilities
paragraph: (b) are not the correct ones to display because of the presence of other dangerous goods in the large means of containment.

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: 4.5 The carrier of dangerous goods must

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (a) ensure that the required dangerous goods safety marks remain displayed on the small means of containment while the dangerous goods are in transport;

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (b) display the required dangerous goods safety marks on the large means of containment, unless they are already displayed on it, and ensure that they remain displayed while the dangerous goods are in transport; and

heading: Carrier Responsibilities
paragraph: (c) provide and display, or remove, the dangerous goods safety marks if the requirements for dangerous goods safety marks change while the dangerous goods are in transport.

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: 4.6 Dangerous goods safety marks must be

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (a) visible, legible and displayed against a background of contrasting colour;

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (b) made of durable and weather-resistant material that will withstand the conditions to which they will be exposed without substantial detachment or deterioration of their colour, symbols, letters, text or numbers; and

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (c) displayed in the colours specified in

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (i) the appendix to this Part, which colours must conform to the following standards in the PANTONE (R) Formula Guide, published by Pantone Inc., 590 Commerce Boulevard, Carlstadt, New Jersey 07072-3098, United States:

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (A) for blue, PANTONE 285,

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (B) for green, PANTONE 335,

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (C) for orange, PANTONE 151,

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (D) for red, PANTONE 186, and

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (E) for yellow, PANTONE 109,

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (ii) Part 172 of 49 CFR, or

heading: Visibility, Legibility and Colour
paragraph: (iii) Chapters 5.2 and 5.3 of the UN Recommendations.

heading: Labels and Placards: Size and Orientation
paragraph: 4.7 (1) Labels and placards must be displayed on a means of containment as they are illustrated in the appendix to this Part, that is, a square on a point.

heading: Labels and Placards: Size and Orientation
paragraph: (2) Each side of a label must be at least 100 mm in length with a line running 5 mm inside the edge. However, except for dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, if that size label, together with the shipping name, technical name and UN number, cannot be displayed because of the irregular shape or size of the small means of containment, each side of the label may be reduced in length by the same amount to the point where the label, together with the shipping name, technical name and UN number, will fit that small means of containment, but must not be reduced to less than 30 mm.

heading: Labels and Placards: Size and Orientation
paragraph: (3) Each side of a placard must be at least 250 mm in length and, except for the DANGER placard, have a line running 12.5 mm inside the edge. However, except for dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, if that size placard cannot be displayed because of the irregular shape or size of the large means of containment, each side of the placard may be reduced in length by the same amount to the point where the placard will fit that large means of containment, but must not be reduced to less than 100 mm.

heading: Labels and Placards: Size and Orientation
paragraph: (4) If the size of a label or a placard is reduced, every symbol, letter and number required on that label or placard must be reduced proportionately.

heading: Labels and Placards: Size and Orientation
paragraph: (5) If a large means of containment contains dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, and a Class 7 placard is required to be displayed in accordance with this Part, the means of containment must have displayed on it the Class 7 placard required or the appropriate optional Class 7 placard illustrated in the appendix to this Part.

heading: Ways to Display a UN Number
paragraph: 4.8 (1) A UN number that is required by this Part to be displayed on a small means of containment or on a tag attached to it must be displayed in one of the following ways:

heading: Ways to Display a UN Number
paragraph: (a) next to the primary class label for the dangerous goods; or

heading: Ways to Display a UN Number
paragraph: (b) within a white rectangle located on the primary class label for the dangerous goods, without the prefix "UN", but it must not obscure the symbol, class number, compatibility group letter or text on the label.

heading: Ways to Display a UN Number
paragraph: (2) A UN number that is required by this Part to be displayed on a large means of containment must be displayed in black numerals not less than 65 mm high in one of the following ways:

heading: Ways to Display a UN Number
paragraph: (a) on an orange panel placed next to the primary class placard for the dangerous goods, without the prefix "UN"; or

heading: Ways to Display a UN Number
paragraph: (b) within a white rectangle located on the primary class placard for the dangerous goods, without the prefix "UN", but it must not obscure the symbol, class number, compatibility group letter or text on the placard.

heading: Removal or Change of Dangerous Goods Safety Marks
paragraph: 4.9 (1) When the conditions that required the display of dangerous goods safety marks change, the person having the charge, management or control of the means of containment must determine, as a result of the new conditions, whether the dangerous goods safety marks must be changed or removed.

heading: Removal or Change of Dangerous Goods Safety Marks
paragraph: (2) The person who neutralizes the contents of the means of containment or who unloads, unpacks, cleans or purges the means of containment must cover or remove the dangerous goods safety mark when the danger indicated by the dangerous goods safety mark is no longer present in the means of containment.

heading: Removal or Change of Dangerous Goods Safety Marks
paragraph: (3) When the DANGER placard is permitted to be displayed on a large means of containment, a person may continue to display that placard, in place of any other placard, until the large means of containment no longer contains any of the dangerous goods identified by that placard.

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.10 (1) One label must be displayed on a small means of containment for the primary class and one for each subsidiary class set out in column 3 of Schedule 1 for each of the dangerous goods in transport in the small means of containment, except that

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) a label is not required to be displayed on a small means of containment that is inside another small means of containment if the other small means of containment has a label displayed on it and is not opened during loading or unloading or while the dangerous goods are in transport;

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) the oxidizing gas label, illustrated in the appendix to this Part, must be displayed on a small means of containment for the following dangerous goods:

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (i) UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED,

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (ii) UN1073, OXYGEN, REFRIGERATED LIQUID,

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (iii) UN3156, COMPRESSED GAS, OXIDIZING, N.O.S., and

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (iv) UN3157, LIQUEFIED GAS, OXIDIZING, N.O.S.;

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (b.1) the Class 9, lithium battery label, illustrated in the appendix to this Part, must be displayed on a small means of containment for the following dangerous goods:

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (i) UN3090, LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES,

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (ii) UN3091, LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES CONTAINED IN EQUIPMENT or LITHIUM METAL BATTERIES PACKED WITH EQUIPMENT,

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (iii) UN3480, LITHIUM ION BATTERIES, and

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (iv) UN3481, LITHIUM ION BATTERIES CONTAINED IN EQUIPMENT or LITHIUM ION BATTERIES PACKED WITH EQUIPMENT;

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (c) if the dangerous goods are included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, two labels must be displayed on the small means of containment for the primary class; and

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (d) when the dangerous goods are included in Class 2, Gases, and are contained in a combination of cylinders each with a capacity greater than 225 L that are a single unit as a result of being interconnected through a piping arrangement, and are permanently mounted on a structural frame for transport, and have a combined capacity exceeding 450 L, the combination of cylinders may be placarded as one large means of containment.

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) For the subsidiary class of Class 1, the label to be displayed is the label for Class 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 illustrated in the appendix to this Part.

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (3) When a label is required to be displayed, it must be displayed

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) on any side of the outer surface of a small means of containment other than the side on which it is intended to rest or to be stacked during transport;

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) on or near the shoulder of a cylinder containing dangerous goods; or

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (c) in the case of a label for dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, on two opposite sides of the outer surface of a small means of containment, other than the side on which it is intended to rest or to be stacked during transport.

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), a label with sides that are reduced to 30 mm in length in accordance with subsection 4.7(2) may be displayed on a tag that is securely attached to a small means of containment.

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (5) Despite subsection (1), a label is not required to be displayed on a small means of containment that contains a radioactive material if the shipping name and UN number of the radioactive material are displayed on the small means of containment and

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) the radioactive material is contained in an exposure device, as defined in the Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices Regulations, and the small means of containment is marked in accordance with paragraph 16(5)(a) of the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations; or

heading: Labels on a Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) the radioactive material is LSA-I material, as defined in subsection 1(1) of the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, and the small means of containment is marked in accordance with paragraph 16(5)(c) of the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations.

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: 4.10.1 (1) When a dangerous goods mark is required by this Part to be displayed on a small means of containment and the small means of containment is inside an overpack, the person who prepares the overpack must display

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (a) the word "Overpack" or "Suremballage", in letters that are at least 12 mm high on a contrasting background, on at least one side of the overpack;

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (b) the information required by subsection (3) on one side of the overpack, if its capacity is less than 1.8 m3 (64 cubic feet); and

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (c) the information required by subsection (3) on two opposite sides of the overpack, if its capacity is greater than or equal to 1.8 m3 (64 cubic feet).

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if a safety mark for each class of dangerous goods inside the overpack is visible through the overpack.

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (3) The following information must be displayed on the overpack:

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (a) the primary class label and each subsidiary class label for each of the dangerous goods contained in the overpack, except that only one label is required for dangerous goods that are included in the same class; and

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (b) the shipping name and UN number of the dangerous goods.

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on an Overpack
paragraph: (4) When dangerous goods included in Class 7 are transported in an overpack and a label is required to be displayed by this Part, the overpack must be prepared in accordance with section 28 of the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015.

heading: Dangerous Goods Marks on a Consolidation Bin
paragraph: 4.10.2 When a label is required by this Part to be displayed on a small means of containment that is inside a consolidation bin, an indication of each class of dangerous goods contained in the consolidation bin must be clearly and legibly marked on a tag or fixed display device that is attached to the bin.

heading: Shipping Name and Technical Name on a Small Means of Containment or on a Tag
paragraph: 4.11 (1) When dangerous goods in transport are in a small means of containment on which a primary class label for the dangerous goods must be displayed, the shipping name of the dangerous goods must be displayed next to the primary class label.

heading: Shipping Name and Technical Name on a Small Means of Containment or on a Tag
paragraph: (2) When dangerous goods in transport are subject to special provision 16 and are in a small means of containment on which the shipping name is displayed, the technical name of at least one of the most dangerous substances that predominantly contributes to the hazard or hazards posed by the dangerous goods must be displayed, in parentheses, following the shipping name.

heading: Shipping Name and Technical Name on a Small Means of Containment or on a Tag
paragraph: (3) When the primary class label for dangerous goods in transport is displayed on a tag in accordance with subsection 4.10(4), the shipping name and, when required by subsection (2), the technical name of the dangerous goods must also be displayed on the tag.

heading: UN Numbers on a Small Means of Containment or on a Tag
paragraph: 4.12 (1) When dangerous goods in transport are in a small means of containment on which the primary class label for the dangerous goods is displayed, the UN number for the dangerous goods must be displayed on or next to the primary class label.

heading: UN Numbers on a Small Means of Containment or on a Tag
paragraph: (2) When the primary class label for dangerous goods in transport is displayed on a tag in accordance with subsection 4.10(4), the UN number must also be displayed on the tag on or next to the primary class label.

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Material
paragraph: 4.14 (1) For dangerous goods included in Class 7, the label or placard required to be displayed by this Part must be determined in accordance with the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015.

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Material
paragraph: (2) For dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Material, the following information must be determined in accordance with the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, and must be displayed on the primary class label for the dangerous goods:

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Material
paragraph: (a) the name or symbol of the radionuclide, except that if there is a mixture of radionuclides, the name or symbol of the most restrictive of the radionuclides in the mixture; and

heading: Class 7, Radioactive Material
paragraph: (b) the activity and the transport index of the dangerous goods.

heading: Placards on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.15 (1) The primary class placard for each of the dangerous goods contained in a large means of containment, other than a vessel or an aircraft, must be displayed on each side and on each end of the large means of containment.

heading: Placards on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) If two or more dangerous goods have different UN numbers but are identified by the same placard or placards, the placard or placards are required to be displayed only once on each side and on each end of a large means of containment.

heading: Subsidiary Class Placards on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.15.1 A subsidiary class placard for dangerous goods must be displayed, next to the primary class placard for the dangerous goods, on each side and on each end of a large means of containment if the dangerous goods require an ERAP and

heading: Subsidiary Class Placards on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) have a subsidiary class of Class 1, Explosives, in which case the placard is the one illustrated for Class 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 in the appendix to this Part;

heading: Subsidiary Class Placards on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) have a subsidiary class of Class 4.3, Water-reactive Substances, in which case the placard is the one illustrated for Class 4.3 in the appendix to this Part;

heading: Subsidiary Class Placards on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (c) have a subsidiary class of Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, and are included in Packing Group I due to inhalation toxicity, in which case the placard is the one illustrated for Class 6.1 in the appendix to this Part; or

heading: Subsidiary Class Placards on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (d) have a subsidiary class of Class 8, Corrosives, and are UN2977, RADIOACTIVE MATERIAL, URANIUM HEXAFLUORIDE, FISSILE, or UN2978, RADIOACTIVE MATERIAL, URANIUM HEXAFLUORIDE, non-fissile or fissile excepted, in which case the placard is the one illustrated for Class 8 in the appendix to this Part.

heading: UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.15.2 UN numbers, except UN numbers for dangerous goods included in Class 1, Explosives, must be displayed on a large means of containment in accordance with subsection 4.8(2) if the dangerous goods

heading: UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) are in a quantity or concentration for which an ERAP is required; or

heading: UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) are a liquid or a gas in direct contact with the large means of containment.

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.15.3 A placard, or a placard and UN number, must be displayed on each side and on each end of a large means of containment, except that

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) in the case of a large means of containment that is permanently connected to a frame, such as a truck frame or a supporting frame for the means of containment, the placard, or the placard and UN number, may be displayed on the frame if the resulting position of the placard, or the placard and UN number, is equivalent on each side and on each end of the means of containment;

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) in the case of a large means of containment that is a trailer unit, the placard, or the placard and UN number, may be displayed on the front of the vehicle that is attached to the trailer unit rather than on the leading end of the trailer unit; and

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (c) in the case of a large means of containment that is an intermediate bulk container (IBC) with a capacity greater than 450 L but less than or equal to 3 000 L,

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (i) a placard and UN number may be displayed on two opposite sides of the IBC, or

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (ii) a label for each primary and subsidiary class as well as a UN number and a shipping name may be displayed on two opposite sides of the IBC.

heading: Visibility of Labels, Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.15.4 (1) When a large means of containment that has labels or placards displayed on it is inside another large means of containment and those labels or placards are not visible, the placards required by this Part must be displayed on the outer large means of containment. The UN numbers that are required by this Part must also be displayed on the outer large means of containment.

heading: Visibility of Labels, Placards and UN Numbers on a Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) When a large means of containment that has labels, placards, labels and UN numbers, or placards and UN numbers, displayed on it is loaded onto another large means of containment and those labels, placards, labels and UN numbers, or placards and UN numbers, are visible, the placards, or placards and UN numbers, are not required to be displayed on the other large means of containment.

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: 4.16 (1) Except in the case of the dangerous goods listed in subsection (2) or a flammable gas referred to in subsection (3), a DANGER placard is permitted to be displayed on a large means of containment instead of any other placard required by section 4.15, if

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (a) the large means of containment contains two or more dangerous goods that require different placards; and

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods loaded into the large means of containment are contained in two or more small means of containment.

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (2) The DANGER placard referred to in subsection (1) must not be displayed on a large means of containment for

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (a) dangerous goods that have a gross mass greater than 1 000 kg, are included in the same class and are offered for transport by one consignor;

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (b) dangerous goods that require an ERAP;

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (c) dangerous goods included in Class 1, Explosives;

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (d) dangerous goods included in Class 2.3, Toxic Gases;

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (e) dangerous goods included in Class 4.3, Water-reactive Substances;

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (f) dangerous goods included in Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, Type B, liquid or solid, that require a control or emergency temperature;

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (g) dangerous goods included in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, that are subject to special provision 23; and

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (h) dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, that require a Category III - Yellow label.

heading: DANGER Placard
paragraph: (3) If a road vehicle or railway vehicle to be transported by vessel contains a flammable gas, the flammable gas placard illustrated in the appendix to this Part must be displayed on the road vehicle or railway vehicle.

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: 4.16.1 (1) Except in the case of the dangerous goods listed in subsection (2), a placard is not required to be displayed on a road vehicle or railway vehicle if the dangerous goods in or on the road vehicle or railway vehicle have a gross mass that is less than or equal to 500 kg.

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (2) The exemption set out in subsection (1) does not apply to dangerous goods

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (a) requiring an ERAP;

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (b) requiring the display of a subsidiary class placard in accordance with section 4.15.1;

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (c) included in Class 1, Explosives, except for

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (i) explosives referred to in subsection 4.17(1), and

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (ii) explosives included in Class 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 or 1.5, if

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (A) the explosives are not subject to special provision 85 or 86 and have a net explosives quantity that is less than or equal to 10 kg, or

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (B) the explosives are subject to special provision 85 or 86 and the number of articles of explosives is less than or equal to 1 000;

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (d) included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, if the road vehicle or railway vehicle is to be transported by vessel;

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (e) included in Class 2.3, Toxic Gases;

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (f) included in Class 4.3, Water-reactive Substances;

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (g) included in Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, Type B, liquid or solid, that require a control or emergency temperature;

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (h) included in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, that are subject to special provision 23; or

heading: Placarding Exemption for Dangerous Goods Having a Gross Mass of 500 kg or Less
paragraph: (i) included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, that require a Category III - Yellow label.

heading: Class 1, Explosives
paragraph: 4.17 (1) Despite section 4.15, a placard is not required to be displayed for explosives that are included in

heading: Class 1, Explosives
paragraph: (a) Class 1.4, except for UN0301, AMMUNITION, TEAR-PRODUCING, and are in a quantity that is less than or equal to 1 000 kg net explosives quantity; or

heading: Class 1, Explosives
paragraph: (b) Class 1.4S and are in any quantity.

heading: Class 1, Explosives
paragraph: (2) Despite section 4.15, only the placard for the explosives with the lowest division number is required to be displayed for explosives that are included in more than one division and are in a large means of containment, except in the following cases:

heading: Class 1, Explosives
paragraph: (a) when explosives included in Class 1.2 and Class 1.5 are transported together, the placard for Class 1.1 must be displayed; and

heading: Class 1, Explosives
paragraph: (b) when explosives included in Class 1.4 and Class 1.5 are transported together, the placard for Class 1.5 must be displayed.

heading: Options for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: 4.18 Despite section 4.15, if a road vehicle transporting toxic gases, flammable gases or oxygen, or gases included in Class 2.2, Non-Flammable and Non-toxic Gases, is placarded with the Toxic Gases placard, the following placards are not required to be displayed on the road vehicle:

heading: Options for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (a) the Flammable Gases placard;

heading: Options for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (b) the Oxidizing Gases placard; and

heading: Options for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (c) the Non-Flammable and Non-toxic Gases placard.

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for Oxidizing Gases
paragraph: 4.18.1 When dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, and contained in a large means of containment are oxidizing gases, the oxidizing gas placard illustrated in the appendix to this Part must be displayed on the large means of containment for the following dangerous goods instead of the placard required by section 4.15, but if an ERAP is required for the dangerous goods the UN number must also be displayed:

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for Oxidizing Gases
paragraph: (a) UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED;

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for Oxidizing Gases
paragraph: (b) UN1073, OXYGEN, REFRIGERATED LIQUID;

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for Oxidizing Gases
paragraph: (c) UN3156, COMPRESSED GAS, OXIDIZING, N.O.S.; and

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for Oxidizing Gases
paragraph: (d) UN3157, LIQUEFIED GAS, OXIDIZING, N.O.S.

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA
paragraph: 4.18.2 When UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA, is contained in a large means of containment, the large means of containment must have displayed on it

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA
paragraph: (a) the Class 2.3 placard and a UN number; or

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA
paragraph: (b) the anhydrous ammonia placard and, on at least two sides, the words "Anhydrous Ammonia, Inhalation Hazard" or "Ammoniac anhydre, dangereux par inhalation" in letters

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA
paragraph: (i) at least 6 mm wide and 100 mm high in the case of a tank car,

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA
paragraph: (ii) at least 4 mm wide and 25 mm high in the case of a portable tank, and

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for UN1005, ANHYDROUS AMMONIA
paragraph: (iii) at least 6 mm wide and 50 mm high in the case of all other large means of containment.

heading: Class 2, Gases: Placards for Tube Trailers
paragraph: 4.18.3 When dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, are contained in a combination of tubes that are a single unit as a result of being interconnected through a piping arrangement and are permanently mounted on a structural frame for transport, the combination of tubes may be placarded as if it were one large means of containment.

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Compartmentalized Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 4.19 (1) When dangerous goods included in different primary classes are transported in different compartments of a compartmentalized large means of containment,

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Compartmentalized Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) the primary class placard and the UN number for the dangerous goods in each compartment must be displayed on each side of that compartment; and

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Compartmentalized Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) each placard and UN number displayed in accordance with paragraph (a) must be displayed on each end of the compartmentalized large means of containment but each specific placard need only be displayed once on each end.

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Compartmentalized Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) When all compartments in a compartmentalized large means of containment contain dangerous goods included in the same primary class,

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Compartmentalized Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) the primary class placard must be displayed on each side and on each end of the compartmentalized large means of containment; and

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Compartmentalized Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) the UN number of the dangerous goods in a compartment must be displayed on each side of that compartment and on each end of the compartmentalized large means of containment, except that, if all the dangerous goods are included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, only the UN number of the dangerous goods with the lowest flash point is required to be displayed on each side and on each end of the compartmentalized large means of containment.

heading: Placards and UN Numbers on a Compartmentalized Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (3) Despite paragraph (2)(b), if a compartmentalized large means of containment contains UN3475, ETHANOL AND GASOLINE MIXTURE, the UN number for ETHANOL AND GASOLINE MIXTURE must be displayed, in addition to the UN number of the dangerous goods with the lowest flash point, on each side and on each end of the compartmentalized large means of containment.

heading: Elevated Temperature Sign
paragraph: 4.20 (1) In addition to the requirements for placards and UN numbers in section 4.15, the elevated temperature sign must be displayed for dangerous goods that are contained in a large means of containment and that are offered for transport or transported at a temperature greater than or equal to

heading: Elevated Temperature Sign
paragraph: (a) 100°C if the dangerous goods are in a liquid state; and

heading: Elevated Temperature Sign
paragraph: (b) 240°C if the dangerous goods are in a solid state.

heading: Elevated Temperature Sign
paragraph: (2) The elevated temperature sign must be displayed on each side and on each end of the large means of containment next to each primary class placard for the dangerous goods or, if there is a subsidiary class placard, next to the subsidiary class placard.

heading: Fumigation Sign
paragraph: 4.21 (1) If the fumigation of a large means of containment is done using dangerous goods, the fumigation sign must be displayed at or next to each entryway through which a person can enter into the large means of containment. The consignor must ensure that the fumigation sign is displayed by the person in charge of the fumigation process and that the sign has displayed on it the name of the fumigant, the date and time the fumigant was applied and the date of ventilation.

heading: Fumigation Sign
paragraph: (2) The fumigation sign must continue to be displayed on a large means of containment that has been fumigated until

heading: Fumigation Sign
paragraph: (a) the large means of containment has been ventilated to remove harmful concentrations of the fumigant; and

heading: Fumigation Sign
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods that were in the large means of containment during the fumigation have been unloaded.

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: 4.22 (1) In addition to the requirements for placards and UN numbers in section 4.15, the marine pollutant mark must be displayed in the following locations, for dangerous goods that are marine pollutants in transport by vessel:

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (a) on a small means of containment, next to the primary class label for the dangerous goods or, if there is a subsidiary class label, next to the subsidiary class label; and

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (b) on each side and each end of a large means of containment next to the placard that is required to be displayed for the dangerous goods.

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (2) The marine pollutant mark is not required to be displayed when marine pollutants are

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (a) on board a road vehicle or railway vehicle on a ro-ro ship; or

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (b) contained in

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (i) a small means of containment and are in a quantity that is less than or equal to 5 L for a liquid marine pollutant or 5 kg for a solid marine pollutant, or

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (ii) a large means of containment and

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (A) are in a quantity that is less than or equal to 500 kg,

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (B) are transported by vessel on a domestic voyage, and

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (C) the large means of containment does not contain Class 1, Explosives, other than explosives included in Class 1.4, Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, or Class 7, Radioactive Materials.

heading: Marine Pollutant Mark
paragraph: (3) The placard and UN number are not required to be displayed for substances identified as marine pollutants in subparagraph 2.43(b)(ii) when the marine pollutant mark is not required to be displayed in accordance with subsection (2).

heading: Category B Mark
paragraph: 4.22.1 The Category B mark illustrated in the appendix to this Part must be displayed, instead of the Class 6.2, Infectious Substances label, on a small means of containment containing infectious substances included in UN3373, BIOLOGICAL SUBSTANCE, CATEGORY B.

heading: Toxic - Inhalation Hazard
paragraph: 4.23 A person must not import, offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods that are included in Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, in accordance with paragraph 2.28(c) of Part 2 (Classification) or Class 2.3, Toxic Gases, in accordance with paragraph 2.14(c) of Part 2 (Classification), unless the words "inhalation hazard" or "dangereux par inhalation" are displayed

heading: Toxic - Inhalation Hazard
paragraph: (a) in the case of a small means of containment, in letters at least 12 mm high, next to the shipping name, unless these words are already part of the shipping name; and

heading: Toxic - Inhalation Hazard
paragraph: (b) in the case of a large means of containment, on two opposite sides of the large means of containment, in addition to any placard or placard and UN number required by this Part, in letters

heading: Toxic - Inhalation Hazard
paragraph: (i) at least 6 mm wide and 100 mm high in the case of a tank car,

heading: Toxic - Inhalation Hazard
paragraph: (ii) at least 4 mm wide and 25 mm high in the case of a portable tank or an intermediate bulk container (IBC), and

heading: Toxic - Inhalation Hazard
paragraph: (iii) at least 6 mm wide and 50 mm high in the case of all other large means of containment.

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: 4.24 (1) For the purposes of special provision 34, the lithium battery mark, illustrated in the appendix to this Part, must indicate

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (a) "UN3090" for lithium metal cells or batteries;

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (b) "UN3480" for lithium ion cells or batteries; and

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (c) "UN3091" or "UN3481", as appropriate, for lithium cells or batteries that are contained in, or packed with, equipment.

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (2) When a means of containment contains lithium cells or batteries assigned to different UN numbers, all applicable UN numbers must be indicated on one or more marks.

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the mark must be at least 120 mm wide * 110 mm high and the hatching must be at least 5 mm wide.

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (4) The dimensions of the mark may be reduced for a means of containment that is an irregular shape or size if

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (a) the mark is at least 105 mm wide * 74 mm high; and

heading: Lithium Battery Mark
paragraph: (b) every symbol, letter and number required on the mark is reduced proportionately.

heading: Selecting and Using Means of Containment
paragraph: 5.1.1 (1) A person must not import, offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods in a means of containment unless the means of containment is required or permitted by this Part to be used for the transportation of the dangerous goods.

heading: Selecting and Using Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods in a standardized means of containment unless the standardized means of containment is in standard.

heading: Selecting and Using Means of Containment
paragraph: (3) A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods in a means of containment that is required or permitted by this Part unless the means of containment is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety.

heading: Requirements for a Standardized Means of Containment to Be in Standard
paragraph: 5.2 A standardized means of containment is in standard with a specific safety standard if

heading: Requirements for a Standardized Means of Containment to Be in Standard
paragraph: (a) it has displayed on it the compliance marks required by the standard;

heading: Requirements for a Standardized Means of Containment to Be in Standard
paragraph: (b) it was in compliance with the requirements of the standard when each compliance mark was first displayed; and

heading: Requirements for a Standardized Means of Containment to Be in Standard
paragraph: (c) it remains in compliance with the requirements of the standard that had to be complied with when each compliance mark was first displayed.

heading: Compliance Marks on a Means of Containment
paragraph: 5.3 Any mark required by a safety standard is a compliance mark and must be visible and legible when it is displayed on a means of containment.

heading: Loading and Securing
paragraph: 5.4 A person must load and secure dangerous goods in a means of containment and must load and secure the means of containment on a means of transport in such a way as to prevent, under normal conditions of transport, damage to the means of containment or to the means of transport that could lead to a release of the dangerous goods.

heading: Filling Limits
paragraph: 5.5 (1) A person filling a means of containment with dangerous goods must not exceed the maximum quantity limit specified in a safety standard or safety requirement applicable to that means of containment.

heading: Filling Limits
paragraph: (2) If the maximum quantity limit for a means of containment is not specified in a safety standard or safety requirement, the person filling the means of containment with dangerous goods

heading: Filling Limits
paragraph: (a) must not exceed the maximum quantity limit established by the manufacturer for the means of containment; and

heading: Filling Limits
paragraph: (b) must ensure that the means of containment could not become liquid full at any temperature that is less than or equal to 55°C.

heading: UN Standardized Means of Containment
paragraph: 5.6 A means of containment is a UN standardized means of containment if it has displayed on it the applicable UN marks illustrated in Chapter 6.1, Chapter 6.3 and Chapter 6.5 of the UN Recommendations and

heading: UN Standardized Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) it is in compliance with

heading: UN Standardized Means of Containment
paragraph: (i) sections 2 and 3 and Part I of CGSB-43.125 for a Type P620 means of containment,

heading: UN Standardized Means of Containment
paragraph: (ii) sections 2 and 3 and Part I of CGSB-43.146, or

heading: UN Standardized Means of Containment
paragraph: (iii) sections 2 and 3 and Part 1 of TP 14850; or

heading: UN Standardized Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) it was manufactured outside Canada in compliance with Chapter 6.1, 6.3 or 6.5 of the UN Recommendations and with the national regulations of the country of manufacture.

heading: Compatibility Groups
paragraph: 5.7 (1) A person must not load or transport with other explosives in the same means of transport, except for a vessel, explosives that have a compatibility group letter listed in column 1 of a row in the following table unless the compatibility group letter of the other explosives is listed in column 2 of the same row:

heading: Compatibility Groups
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Compatibility Groups
paragraph: (2) For a mixed load of two or more explosives with compatibility groups C, D, E, N or S, the compatibility group of the mixed load is the first compatibility group of E, D, C, N or S present in the mixed load.

heading: Compatibility Groups
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), detonators in compatibility group B may be loaded or transported in the same road vehicle with explosives in compatibility group D or N. The compatibility group of the mixed load is D.

heading: Compatibility Groups
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (1), explosive articles included in compatibility group G, except for fireworks with UN number UN0333, UN0334, UN0335 or UN0336, may be loaded or transported in the same road vehicle together with explosive articles included in compatibility group C, D or E. The compatibility group of the mixed load is E.

heading: Compatibility Groups
paragraph: (5) For a mixed load of two explosives with one of the compatibility groups being S, the compatibility group of the mixed load is that of the other compatibility group.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 1, Explosives
paragraph: 5.8 A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods included in Class 1, unless they are in a means of containment that is selected and used in accordance with CGSB-43.151.

paragraph: 5.10 (1) A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods included in Class 2, Gases, in a means of containment unless the means of containment is manufactured, selected and used in accordance with

paragraph: (a) for transport by road vehicle,

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (i) CGSB-43.123, if the gas is included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases or Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases,

paragraph: (iv) CSA B622, except clause 4.3 of that standard, and, despite any indication to the contrary in CSA B620, Annex B of CSA B620,

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (vi) TP 14877, if the means of containment is a ton container;

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (b) for transport by railway vehicle,

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (i) CGSB-43.123, if the gas is included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases or Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases,

paragraph: (iv) CSA B342, or

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (v) CSA B625;

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (c) for transport by aircraft,

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (i) CGSB-43.123, if the gas is included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases or Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases,

paragraph: (ii) CSA B340, or

paragraph: (d) for transport by vessel,

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (i) CGSB-43.123, if the gas is included in Class 2.1, Flammable Gases or Class 2.2, Non-flammable and Non-toxic Gases,

paragraph: (iii) CSA B340,

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (iv) CSA B342,

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (v) CSA B622, except clause 4.3 of that standard, and, despite any indication to the contrary in CSA B620, Annex B of CSA B620, or

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (vi) CSA B625.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of this section, the following requirements apply in respect of a report of requalification, repair, reheat treatment or rebuilding that is referred to in clause 24.7 of CSA B339:

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (a) the person who prepares the report must give a copy of it to the owner of the means of containment;

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (b) the person who prepares the report and the owner must each keep a copy of the report for 10 years; and

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (c) the owner must, during the 10-year period, give a copy of the report to any person to whom ownership of the means of containment is transferred.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (11) For the purposes of this section, a person who uses a standardized means of containment in accordance with CSA B622 must use a means of containment that

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (a) is manufactured in accordance with CSA B620 if it was manufactured in Canada on or after August 31, 2008; and

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (b) is tested and inspected in accordance with CSA B620 if its most recent periodic re-test or periodic inspection was performed in Canada on or after August 31, 2008.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (12) Despite paragraph 11(a), a standardized means of containment that is a TC 51 portable tank and that is used in accordance with CSA B622 may be manufactured in accordance with CSA B620-09.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
paragraph: (13) For the purposes of subsection (12), the following requirements of CSA B622 do not apply:

heading: Means of Containment for Class 2, Gases
