paragraph: (b) the requirement in the footnote respecting TC 51 portable tanks after Table 1 to clause 4.4.3.

heading: UN1950, AEROSOLS, and UN2037, GAS CARTRIDGES
paragraph: 5.11 Despite section 5.10, a person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods that are UN1950, AEROSOLS, or UN2037, GAS CARTRIDGES, unless they are contained in a means of containment that is manufactured, selected and used in accordance with CGSB-43.123.

heading: Small Means of Containment
paragraph: 5.12 (1) A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods included in Class 3, 4, 5, 6.1, 8 or 9 in a small means of containment unless it is a means of containment that is selected and used in accordance with Part II of CGSB-43.146 or a means of containment that is selected and used in accordance with sections 2 and 3 and with Part 2 of TP 14850.

heading: Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) A person must not reuse a steel or plastic drum with a capacity greater than or equal to 150 L to handle, offer for transport or transport dangerous goods that are liquid and are included in Class 3, 4, 5, 6.1, 8 or 9 unless

heading: Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) for a steel drum, the requirements for the reconditioning, remanufacturing and repair in Part II of CGSB-43.126 are complied with and the drum reconditioning, remanufacturing and repair facility is registered with Transport Canada in accordance with the requirements of Appendix A of CGSB-43.126; or

heading: Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) for a plastic drum, the requirements for the reconditioning, remanufacturing and repair in Part III of CGSB-43.126 are complied with and the drum reconditioning, remanufacturing and repair facility is registered with Transport Canada in accordance with the requirements of Appendix A of CGSB-43.126.

heading: Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (3) The manufacturer or subsequent distributor of a UN standardized small means of containment manufactured in Canada must provide a notice to the initial user in accordance with section 4.4 of TP 14850. The manufacturer or subsequent distributor of a UN standardized intermediate bulk container (IBC) manufactured in Canada must provide a notice to the initial user in accordance with clause 4.8 of CGSB-43.146.

heading: Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (4) A person must not reuse an IBC for liquids, or an IBC for solids, that is filled or discharged under pressure to offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods that are included in Class 3, 4, 5, 6.1, 8 or 9 unless it has been leak tested and inspected in accordance with clause 12.6 of CGSB-43.146.

heading: Small Means of Containment
paragraph: (5) In addition to the requirements set out in subsection (1), a person who uses a means of containment that is required under CGSB-43.146 for the offering for transport of dangerous goods must follow the requirements of clauses 12.2, 12.3 and 12.4 of CGSB-43.146.

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: 5.14 (1) A person must not handle, offer for transport or transport dangerous goods included in Class 3, 4, 5, 6.1, 8 or 9 in a large means of containment unless it is manufactured, selected and used in accordance with

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) for transport by road vehicle,

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (i) the requirements of Part II of CGSB-43.146, if the means of containment is a UN standardized means of containment,

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (ii) CSA B621, except clause 8.2(b), and, despite any indication to the contrary in CSA B620, Annex B of CSA B620,

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (iii) CSA B625, or

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (iv) TP 14877, if the means of containment is a ton container;

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) for transport by railway vehicle,

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (i) the requirements of Part II of CGSB-43.146, if the means of containment is a UN standardized means of containment,

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (ii) TP 14877, or

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (iii) CSA B625;

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (c) for transport by aircraft, Part 12 (Air) of these Regulations; and

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (d) for transport by vessel,

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (i) the requirements of Part II of CGSB-43.146, if the means of containment is a UN standardized means of containment,

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (iii) CSA B621, except clause 8.2(b), and, despite any indication to the contrary in CSA B620, Annex B of CSA B620, or

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (iv) CSA B625.

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) In addition to the requirements of subparagraphs (1)(a)(ii) and (d)(iii), a person who uses a standardized means of containment that is required by CSA B621 to offer for transport dangerous goods included in Class 3, 4, 5, 6.1, 8 or 9 must use a means of containment

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) manufactured in accordance with CSA B620 if the means of containment was manufactured in Canada on or after August 31, 2008; and

heading: Large Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) tested and inspected in accordance with CSA B620 when the most recent periodic re-test or periodic inspection is performed in Canada on or after August 31, 2008.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 6.2, Infectious Substances
paragraph: 5.16 (1) A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods included in Category A or Category B of Class 6.2, Infectious Substances, unless the dangerous goods are in a means of containment that is manufactured, selected and used in accordance with CGSB-43.125.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 6.2, Infectious Substances
paragraph: (2) If the means of containment is made available as a kit, the packaging manufacturer and subsequent distributor must provide the packaging information required under section 4.4 of CGSB-43.125 to the packaging purchaser at each initial purchase and to a packaging user upon request.

heading: Means of Containment for Class 7, Radioactive Materials
paragraph: 5.17 A person must not offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods included in Class 7 in a means of containment unless the means of containment is in compliance with the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations, 2015.

heading: Consolidation Bins
paragraph: 5.18 A person must not use a consolidation bin to handle or transport dangerous goods in a road vehicle unless

heading: Consolidation Bins
paragraph: (a) the capacity of the consolidation bin is less than or equal to 1.8 m3 (64 cubic feet);

heading: Consolidation Bins
paragraph: (b) the consolidation bin is reusable and constructed of plastic, wood or metal; and

heading: Consolidation Bins
paragraph: (c) the consolidation bin is blocked or braced within the road vehicle.

heading: Training Certificate Requirements
paragraph: 6.1 (1) A person who handles, offers for transport or transports dangerous goods must

heading: Training Certificate Requirements
paragraph: (a) be adequately trained and hold a training certificate in accordance with this Part; or

heading: Training Certificate Requirements
paragraph: (b) perform those activities in the presence and under the direct supervision of a person who is adequately trained and who holds a training certificate in accordance with this Part.

heading: Training Certificate Requirements
paragraph: (2) An employer must not direct or allow an employee to handle, offer for transport or transport dangerous goods unless the employee

heading: Training Certificate Requirements
paragraph: (a) is adequately trained and holds a training certificate in accordance with this Part; or

heading: Training Certificate Requirements
paragraph: (b) performs those activities in the presence and under the direct supervision of a person who is adequately trained and who holds a training certificate in accordance with this Part.

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: 6.2 A person is adequately trained if the person has a sound knowledge of all the topics listed in paragraphs (a) to (m) that relate directly to the person's duties and to the dangerous goods the person is expected to handle, offer for transport or transport:

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (a) the classification criteria and test methods in Part 2 (Classification);

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (b) shipping names;

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (c) the use of Schedules 1, 2 and 3;

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (d) the shipping document and train consist requirements in Part 3 (Documentation);

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (e) the dangerous goods safety marks requirements in Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks);

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (f) the certification safety marks requirements, safety requirements and safety standards in Part 5 (Means of Containment);

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (g) the ERAP requirements in Part 7 (Emergency Response Assistance Plan);

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (h) the report requirements in Part 8 (Reporting Requirements);

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (i) safe handling and transportation practices for dangerous goods, including the characteristics of the dangerous goods;

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (j) the proper use of any equipment used to handle or transport the dangerous goods;

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (k) the reasonable emergency measures the person must take to reduce or eliminate any danger to public safety that results or may reasonably be expected to result from an accidental release of the dangerous goods;

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (l) for air transport, the aspects of training set out in Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions for the persons named in that Chapter and the requirements in Part 12 (Air) of these Regulations; and

heading: Adequate Training
paragraph: (m) for marine transport, the requirements of the IMDG Code and the requirements of Part 11 (Marine) of these Regulations.

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: 6.3 (1) An employer who has reasonable grounds to believe that an employee is adequately trained and will perform duties to which the training relates must issue a training certificate to the employee that includes the following information:

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the place of business of the employer;

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (b) the employee's name;

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (c) the date the training certificate expires, preceded by the words "Expires on" or "Date d'expiration"; and

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (d) the aspects of handling, offering for transport or transporting dangerous goods for which the employee is trained, including the specific topics set out in section 6.2.

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (2) A self-employed person who has reasonable grounds to believe that he or she is adequately trained and who will perform duties to which the training relates must issue to himself or herself a training certificate that includes the information required by subsection (1).

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (3) The training certificate must be signed

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (a) by the employee and by the employer or another employee acting on behalf of the employer; or

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (b) in the case of a self-employed person, by that person.

heading: Issuance and Contents of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (1), if the employer of a person who is a member of a vessel's complement has reasonable grounds to believe that the person's certificate of competency issued in accordance with the Marine Certification Regulations is acceptable evidence that the person is adequately trained, the employer is not required to issue the training certificate. The certificate of competency is a valid training certificate for the purposes of these Regulations when the certificate of competency is valid in Canada.

heading: Foreign Carriers
paragraph: 6.4 (1) A document that is issued to a driver of a road vehicle licensed in the United States or to a member of the crew of a train subject to 49 CFR for the transportation of dangerous goods and that indicates that the driver or the crew member is trained in accordance with sections 172.700 to 172.704 of 49 CFR is a valid training certificate for the purposes of these Regulations when that document is valid in the United States.

heading: Foreign Carriers
paragraph: (2) A document that is issued to a foreign member of the flight crew of an aircraft registered in a country that is a Member State of the International Civil Aviation Organization and that indicates that the crew member is trained to transport dangerous goods by air is a valid training certificate for the purposes of these Regulations, in accordance with Article 33 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation, when that document is valid in the Member State.

heading: Foreign Carriers
paragraph: (3) A document that is issued to a foreign member of the crew of a vessel registered in a country that is a Member State of the International Maritime Organization and that indicates that the crew member is trained to transport dangerous goods by vessel is a valid training certificate for the purposes of these Regulations when that document is valid in the Member State.

heading: Expiry of a Training Certificate
paragraph: 6.5 A training certificate expires

heading: Expiry of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (a) for transport by aircraft, 24 months after its date of issuance; and

heading: Expiry of a Training Certificate
paragraph: (b) for transport by road vehicle, railway vehicle or vessel, 36 months after its date of issuance.

heading: Keeping Proof of Training: Employer's and Self-Employed Person's Responsibility
paragraph: 6.6 An employer or a self-employed person must keep a record of training or a statement of experience, as well as a copy of a training certificate, in electronic or paper form, beginning on the date the training certificate is issued and continuing until two years after the date it expires.

heading: Showing Proof of Training: Employer's and Self-Employed Person's Responsibility
paragraph: 6.7 Within 15 days after the date of a written request by an inspector, the employer of a person who holds a training certificate or a self-employed person must provide a copy of the training certificate to the inspector and, if applicable, a copy of the record of training or the statement of experience and a description of the training material used in the person's training.

heading: Showing Proof of Training: Trained Person's Responsibility
paragraph: 6.8 A person who handles, offers for transport or transports dangerous goods, or who directly supervises another person engaged in these activities, must give his or her training certificate, or a copy of it, to an inspector immediately on request.

heading: Application
paragraph: 7.1 This Part sets out

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) the requirement to have an approved ERAP;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) the approval of an ERAP;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) the authorization to use an approved ERAP;

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) the implementation of an approved ERAP; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (e) the compensation for the authorized implementation of an approved ERAP.

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: 7.2 (1) For the purposes of subsection 7(1) of the Act, an approved ERAP is required for

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) dangerous goods that have the same UN number and that are contained in a single means of containment, if the quantity of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of Schedule 1;

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) dangerous goods, in a road vehicle or a railway vehicle, that have the same UN number and that are contained in more than one means of containment, if the total quantity of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of Schedule 1 and are included in one of the following classes:

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (i) Class 3, Flammable Liquids, with a subsidiary class of Class 6.1, Toxic Substances,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (ii) Class 4, Flammable Solids; Substances Liable to Spontaneous Combustion; Substances That on Contact with Water Emit Flammable Gases (Water-reactive substances),

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (iii) Class 5.2, Organic Peroxides, that are Type B or Type C,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (iv) Class 6.1, Toxic Substances, that are included in Packing Group I;

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (c) dangerous goods, in a road vehicle or a railway vehicle, that have the same UN number, and that are contained in more than one large means of containment, if the total quantity of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of Schedule 1;

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (d) dangerous goods, in a road vehicle or a railway vehicle, that are included in Class 1, Explosives, and that are contained in one or more means of containment, if the total quantity of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of Schedule 1 for the explosives with the lowest index number in that column;

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (e) dangerous goods that are included in Class 2, Gases, that have the same UN number, that are contained in more than one means of containment - each of which has a capacity greater than 225 L - that are a single unit as a result of being interconnected through a piping arrangement and that are permanently mounted on a structural frame for transport, if the total quantity of those dangerous goods exceeds the ERAP index in column 7 of Schedule 1;

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (f) any of the following dangerous goods that are transported by rail in a tank car, if the quantity of those dangerous goods in the tank car exceeds 10 000 L:

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (i) UN1170, ETHANOL with more than 24% ethanol, by volume, ETHANOL SOLUTION with more than 24% ethanol, by volume, ETHYL ALCOHOL with more than 24% ethanol, by volume, or ETHYL ALCOHOL SOLUTION with more than 24% ethanol, by volume,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (ii) UN1202, DIESEL FUEL, GAS OIL, or HEATING OIL, LIGHT,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (iii) UN1203, GASOLINE, MOTOR SPIRIT, or PETROL,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (iv) UN1267, PETROLEUM CRUDE OIL,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (v) UN1268, PETROLEUM DISTILLATES, N.O.S., or PETROLEUM PRODUCTS, N.O.S.,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (vi) UN1863, FUEL, AVIATION, TURBINE ENGINE,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (vii) UN1987, ALCOHOLS, N.O.S.,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (viii) UN1993, FLAMMABLE LIQUID, N.O.S.,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (ix) UN3295, HYDROCARBONS, LIQUID, N.O.S.,

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (x) UN3475, ETHANOL AND GASOLINE MIXTURE, with more than 10% ethanol, ETHANOL AND MOTOR SPIRIT MIXTURE, with more than 10% ethanol, or ETHANOL AND PETROL MIXTURE, with more than 10% ethanol, and

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (xi) UN3494, PETROLEUM SOUR CRUDE OIL, FLAMMABLE, TOXIC; and

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (g) any quantity of dangerous goods that are Risk Group 4 human pathogens within the meaning of the Human Pathogens and Toxins Act.

heading: Requirement to Have an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (2) Any substance that would require an ERAP if its classification were determined in accordance with Part 2 (Classification) requires an approved ERAP if its appropriate classification in the ICAO Technical Instructions, the IMDG Code or the UN Recommendations is to be used under subsection 2.2(4).

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: 7.3 (1) A person must apply to the Minister in writing for the approval of an ERAP.

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (2) The application for approval must be signed by the applicant and must include a copy of the ERAP and the following information:

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the applicant;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (b) a description of the applicant's operations;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (c) the name and contact information of any third party who assisted in the preparation of the application;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (d) the classification of the dangerous goods to which the ERAP relates and the mode of transport used;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (e) for each mode of transport used,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (i) the frequency of the transportation of the dangerous goods,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (ii) the type and specification of the means of containment used to transport the dangerous goods, and

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iii) the geographical area in which the dangerous goods are transported;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (f) the ERAP telephone number, including the area code, at which a person identified in the ERAP can be reached at any time while the dangerous goods are handled or transported;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (g) a description of the communications systems that will be available at the location of a release or anticipated release of dangerous goods;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (h) the name and contact information of any third-party emergency responders, their role and a copy of the agreement between the applicant and the third party;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (i) the following information regarding the ERAP response equipment:

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (i) a detailed list of the equipment,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (ii) the location of the equipment,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iii) the name of the person responsible for the operation of the equipment at each location,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iv) for each location, the dangerous goods in respect of which the equipment is to be used during emergency measures, and

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (v) the geographical areas where the equipment at each location is to be used;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (j) the following information respecting the ERAP response personnel, including technical advisors, team leaders and response teams:

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (i) their names and contact information,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (ii) their responsibilities,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iii) any training they have taken, and

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iv) description of their knowledge and experience in respect of the dangerous goods;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (k) the response capability in respect of the dangerous goods, including

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (i) the measures that can be taken in response to the release or anticipated release,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (ii) the persons responsible for taking the measures referred to in subparagraph (i), and

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iii) the ERAP equipment that will be used to take those measures;

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (l) an estimate of the time required for the response personnel and equipment to reach the location of the release or anticipated release and a description of the mobilization and deployment steps in respect of the response personnel and equipment; and

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (m) a potential incident analysis, including

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (i) the following scenarios:

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (A) an anticipated release of dangerous goods,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (B) the release of less than 1% of the dangerous goods in a means of containment,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (C) the release of more than 50% of the dangerous goods in a means of containment, and

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (D) the exposure to fire of a means of containment that contains dangerous goods,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (ii) the possible consequences of the release or anticipated release for each scenario,

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iii) the measures, organized by tier in accordance with section 7.8, to be taken in response to the release or anticipated release for each scenario, and

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP
paragraph: (iv) the identification of the persons responsible for taking the measures referred to in subparagraph (iii).

heading: Application for Approval of an ERAP - Emergency Response Contractors
paragraph: 7.4 A person who is not required to have an approved ERAP under subsection 7(1) of the Act, but who is able to take measures to respond to a release or anticipated release of dangerous goods for the purposes of paragraph 7.1(b) of the Act, may apply to the Minister in writing for the approval of an ERAP. The application must include a copy of the ERAP and the information referred to in paragraphs 7.3(2)(a), (b), (d), (g) and (i) to (l).

heading: Application for Approval of Changes to Approved ERAP
paragraph: 7.5 (1) A person with an approved ERAP must, as soon as possible, apply to the Minister in writing for an approval of changes if any of the information referred to in paragraphs 7.3(2)(a) to (l) has changed since its approval.

heading: Application for Approval of Changes to Approved ERAP
paragraph: (2) The application referred to in subsection (1) must be signed by the applicant and include

heading: Application for Approval of Changes to Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) a copy of the ERAP; and

heading: Application for Approval of Changes to Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) the information referred to in paragraphs 7.3(2)(a) to (l) that has changed.

heading: Request for Review of Decision
paragraph: 7.6 (1) A person may request a review of the decision to refuse an application for approval of an ERAP or to revoke an ERAP approval within 30 days after being notified of the decision.

heading: Request for Review of Decision
paragraph: (2) The request must be made to the Minister in writing and must include the reasons why the decision should be revised.

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: 7.7 (1) A person who is required to have an ERAP under subsection 7(1) of the Act may use, as an authorized user, the ERAP of another person who received approval for the ERAP if

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) the authorized user is not the producer of the dangerous goods to which the ERAP relates;

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) the ERAP applies to the dangerous goods, the mode of transport, the means of containment and the geographical area in which the dangerous goods will be in transport;

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (c) the person who received approval for the ERAP agrees to take measures to respond to a release or anticipated release of the dangerous goods to which the ERAP relates; and

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (d) the person who received approval for the ERAP provides a written authorization to the authorized user before the information referred to in subsection 3.6(1) is entered on the shipping document.

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (2) The authorized user must be able to produce a copy of the authorization referred to in paragraph (1)(d)

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) for two years after the day on which the authorization is no longer in effect; and

heading: Authorization to Use an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) within 15 days after the day on which the authorized user receives a written request from the Minister.

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: 7.8 (1) A person with an approved ERAP must implement it to tier 1 or tier 2 in response to a release or anticipated release of dangerous goods.

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (2) A person who implements an approved ERAP to tier 1 must

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) provide technical or emergency response advice as soon as possible after a request for the advice; and

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) remotely monitor the response to the release or anticipated release.

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (3) A person who implements an approved ERAP to tier 2 must

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) provide technical or emergency response advice as soon as possible after a request for the advice;

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) monitor the response to the release or anticipated release; and

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (c) send ERAP emergency response resources to the location of the release or anticipated release.

heading: Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (4) A person must not prevent another person who has an approved ERAP from taking emergency measures in response to a release or anticipated release.

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: 7.9 (1) If a person implements an approved ERAP in accordance with paragraph 7.1(b) of the Act, the following expenses are authorized for the purposes of compensation under section 7.2 of the Act:

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) expenses related to the death, disability or injury of the person or to the death, disability or injury of any of the person's employees or contractors if

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (i) the person, the employee or the contractor is killed, disabled or injured during the implementation of the ERAP, and

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (ii) the death, disability or injury is the result of an act or omission that was committed by the person in good faith and without negligence;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) the cost of the person's employees or contractors who are reasonably required to implement the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (c) the cost of using the person's tools and other equipment, such as vehicles, pumps, hoses and generators, that are reasonably required to implement the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (d) travel expenses, such as those incurred for meals, accommodation, fuel, oil and flights, for persons who are reasonably required to implement the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (e) rental fees for heavy equipment, such as cranes, bulldozers, pumps, compressors and generators, that are reasonably required to implement the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (f) other overhead costs that can reasonably be attributed to the implementation of the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (g) the cost of repairing tools and other equipment that are damaged during the implementation of the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (h) the cost of replacing

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (i) single-use equipment and supplies, such as packaging, personal protective equipment, personal protective clothing, chemicals and other consumables, that are reasonably required to implement the ERAP,

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (ii) tools and other equipment that are lost during the implementation of the ERAP, and

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (iii) tools and other equipment that are damaged beyond repair during the implementation of the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (i) the cost of repairing or replacing personal property or movables or real property or immovables that have to be damaged to implement the ERAP;

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (j) the cost of defending any legal action for which there is no personal liability under paragraph 20(c) of the Act; and

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (k) the cost of cleaning up after an incident, including handling and disposal costs for dangerous goods and contaminated materials.

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (2) The following expenses are not authorized for the purposes of compensation under section 7.2 of the Act:

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (a) the cost of purchasing new equipment to implement the approved ERAP; and

heading: Compensation for the Authorized Implementation of an Approved ERAP
paragraph: (b) the cost of lost business or production during the implementation of the approved ERAP.

heading: Compensation Limits
paragraph: 7.10 (1) Compensation under paragraph 7.9(1)(a) is limited to the compensation that would be paid in relation to the dead, disabled or injured person if the person were insured under

heading: Compensation Limits
paragraph: (a) the Public Service Management Insurance Plan;

heading: Compensation Limits
paragraph: (b) the Public Service Health Care Plan, with hospital coverage at level III; and

heading: Compensation Limits
paragraph: (c) the Public Service Dental Care Plan.

heading: Compensation Limits
paragraph: (2) Compensation under paragraph 7.9(1)(h) in relation to the replacement of the items listed in subparagraphs 7.9(1)(h)(i), (ii) and (iii) is limited to the cost of an item of equivalent capability and quality.

heading: Compensation Limits
paragraph: (3) Compensation under paragraph 7.9(1)(i) in relation to damaged property is limited to the fair market value of the property immediately before it is damaged by the person who implements the approved ERAP.

heading: Claims for Compensation
paragraph: 7.11 Claims for compensation must be submitted with supporting documentation to the Minister no later than three months after completion of the emergency response work.

heading: Application and Interpretation
paragraph: 8.1 This Part applies in respect of

heading: Application and Interpretation
paragraph: (a) the release or anticipated release of dangerous goods that are being offered for transport, handled or transported by road vehicle, railway vehicle or vessel;

heading: Application and Interpretation
paragraph: (b) the release or anticipated release of dangerous goods that are being offered for transport, handled or transported by aircraft;

heading: Application and Interpretation
paragraph: (c) undeclared and misdeclared dangerous goods that are being offered for transport, handled or transported by aircraft;

heading: Application and Interpretation
paragraph: (d) the loss or theft of dangerous goods; and

heading: Application and Interpretation
paragraph: (e) unlawful interference with dangerous goods.

heading: Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: 8.2 A person who is required by subsection 18(1) of the Act to report a release or anticipated release of dangerous goods that are being offered for transport, handled or transported by road vehicle, railway vehicle or vessel must, as soon as possible after a release or anticipated release, make an emergency report to any local authority that is responsible for responding to emergencies at the geographic location of the release or anticipated release if the dangerous goods are, or could be, in excess of the quantity set out in the following table:

heading: Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: 8.3 An emergency report referred to in section 8.2 must include the following information:

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (b) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the release;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (c) in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led to the anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (d) the mode of transport used;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (e) the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (f) the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means of containment before the release or anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (g) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released; and

heading: Information To Be Included in an Emergency Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (h) if applicable, the type of incident leading to the release or anticipated release, including a collision, roll-over, derailment, overfill, fire, explosion or load-shift.

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: 8.4 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person who has made an emergency report referred to in section 8.2 must, as soon as possible after making it, make a report to the persons listed in subsection (4).

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the person is not required to make a report referred to in subsection (1) if the release or anticipated release did not result in

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (a) the death of a person;

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (b) a person sustaining injuries that required immediate medical treatment by a health care provider;

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (c) an evacuation of people or their shelter in place; or

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (d) the closure of

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (i) a facility used in the loading and unloading of dangerous goods, or

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (ii) a road, a main railway line or a main waterway.

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (3) The person is required to make a report referred to in subsection (1) if

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (a) a means of containment has been damaged to the extent that its integrity is compromised; or

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (b) the centre sill or stub sill of a tank car is broken or there is a crack in the metal equal to or greater than 15 cm (6 in.).

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsection (1), the persons to whom a report must be made are

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (b) the consignor of the dangerous goods;

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (c) in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission; and

heading: Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (d) in the case of a vessel, a Vessel Traffic Services Centre or a Canadian Coast Guard radio station.

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: 8.5 A release or anticipated release report referred to in section 8.4 must include the following information:

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (b) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (c) in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led to the anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (d) the mode of transport used;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (e) the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (f) the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means of containment before the release or anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (g) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (h) if applicable, the type of incident leading to the release or anticipated release, including a collision, rollover, derailment, overfill, fire, explosion or load-shift;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (i) if applicable, the name and geographic location of any road, main railway line or main waterway that was closed;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (j) a description of the means of containment containing the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (k) if applicable, an estimate of the number of people evacuated or sheltered in place; and

heading: Information To Be Included in a Release or Anticipated Release Report - Road, Rail or Marine
paragraph: (l) if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of persons who sustained injuries that required immediate medical treatment by a health care provider.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: 8.6 A person who has made a report referred to in section 8.4, or the person's employer, must make a follow-up report in writing to the Minister within 30 days after the day on which the report was made.

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: 8.7 A follow-up report referred to in section 8.6 must include the following information:

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (b) the names and contact information of the consignor, consignee and carrier;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (c) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (d) in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led to the anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (e) the mode of transport used;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (f) the classification of the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (g) the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means of containment before the release or anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (h) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (i) a description of the means of containment containing the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (j) if applicable, a description of any failure of or damage to the means of containment;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (k) information about the events leading to the release or anticipated release of dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (l) information as to whether there was an explosion or fire;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (m) the name and geographic location of any facility used in the loading or unloading of the dangerous goods that was closed, and the duration of the closure;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (n) the name and geographic location of any road, main railway line or main waterway that was closed, and the duration of the closure;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (o) if applicable, an estimate of the number of people evacuated or sheltered in place and the duration of the evacuation or shelter in place;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (p) if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of persons who sustained injuries that required immediate medical treatment by a health care provider;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (q) the ERAP reference number, if applicable, and

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (i) the name of the person who was required to have the ERAP under subsection 7(1) of the Act, and

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (ii) the date and time that the ERAP incident report referred to in section 8.20 was made;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (r) the date on which the report referred to in section 8.4 was made; and

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (s) an estimate of any financial loss incurred as a result of the release or anticipated release, and any emergency response cost or remediation costs related to it.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report - Notice and Retention of Report
paragraph: 8.8 (1) A person who has made a follow-up report referred to in section 8.6 must, as soon as possible, notify the Minister of any change to the information referred to in paragraph 8.7(f), (i), (j), (k), (l), (p) or (s) that occurs within one year after the day on which the follow-up report was made.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report - Notice and Retention of Report
paragraph: (2) The person must keep a copy of the report for two years after the day on which it is made.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report - Notice and Retention of Report
paragraph: (3) The person must make the report available to an inspector within 15 days after the day on which the person receives a written request from the inspector.

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: 8.9 (1) Subject to subsection (3), a person who is required by subsection 18(1) of the Act to report a release or anticipated release of dangerous goods that are being offered for transport, handled or transported at an aerodrome, at an air cargo facility or by aircraft must as soon as possible after a release or anticipated release, make a report if the dangerous goods are, or could be, in excess of the quantity set out in the following table:

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: TABLE

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (2) The report referred to in subsection (1) must be made to CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or 613-996-6666, and, in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, to the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (3) The person is not required to make the report referred to in subsection (1) if the release or anticipated release does not result in any of the following:

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (a) the death or injury of a person;

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (b) damage to property or to the environment;

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (c) signs that the integrity of a means of containment has been compromised, including signs of fire, of breakage or of fluid or radiation leakage;

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (d) serious jeopardy to persons on an aircraft or to the aircraft itself;

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (e) an evacuation of people or their shelter in place; or

heading: Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (f) the closure of an aerodrome, air cargo facility or runway.

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: 8.10 A report referred to in section 8.9 must include the following information:

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (b) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (c) in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led to the anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (d) the name of the aircraft operator, aerodrome or air cargo facility;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (e) the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (f) the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means of containment before the release or anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (g) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (h) if applicable, the type of incident leading to the release or anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (i) a description of the means of containment containing the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (j) if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of persons who sustained injuries; and

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Accident or Incident Report - Air
paragraph: (k) if applicable, an estimate of the number of people evacuated or sheltered in place.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: 8.11 A person who has made a report referred to in section 8.9, or the person's employer, must make a follow-up report in writing to the Minister within 30 days after the day on which the report was made.

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: 8.12 A follow-up report referred to in section 8.11 must include the following information:

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (b) the names and contact information of the consignor, consignee and aircraft operator;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (c) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (d) in the case of an anticipated release of dangerous goods, the date, time and geographic location of the incident that led to the anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (e) the classification of the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (f) the quantity of dangerous goods that was in the means of containment before the release or anticipated release;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (g) in the case of a release of dangerous goods, the quantity of dangerous goods estimated to have been released;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (h) a description of the means of containment containing the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (i) if applicable, a description of any failure of or damage to the means of containment;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (j) information about the events leading to the release or anticipated release of dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (k) information as to whether there was an explosion or fire;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (l) the name and geographic location of any aerodrome, air cargo facility or runway that was closed, and the duration of the closure;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (m) if applicable, an estimate of the number of people evacuated or sheltered in place, and the duration of the evacuation or shelter in place;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (n) if applicable, the number of deaths and the number of persons who sustained injuries;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (o) if applicable, the ERAP reference number;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (p) the date on which the report referred to in section 8.9 was made;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (q) an estimate of any financial loss incurred as a result of the release or anticipated release, and any emergency response costs or remediation costs related to it;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (r) a description of the route by which the dangerous goods were to be transported, including the names of any aerodromes along the route;

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (s) a description of any serious jeopardy to persons on any aircraft or to the aircraft itself; and

heading: Information To Be Included in a 30-Day Follow-up Report
paragraph: (t) a description of any damage to property or to the environment.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report - Notice and Retention of Report
paragraph: 8.13 (1) A person who has made a follow-up report referred to in section 8.11 must, as soon as possible, notify the Minister of any change to the information referred to in paragraph 8.12(e), (h), (i), (k), (n) or (q) that occurs within one year after the day on which the follow-up report was made.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report - Notice and Retention of Report
paragraph: (2) The person must keep a copy of the report for two years after the day on which it is made.

heading: 30-Day Follow-up Report - Notice and Retention of Report
paragraph: (3) The person must make the report available to an inspector within 15 days after the day on which the person receives a written request from the inspector.

heading: Undeclared or Misdeclared Dangerous Goods Report
paragraph: 8.14 A person must make a report to CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or 613-996-6666, as soon as possible after discovering, at an aerodrome or air cargo facility or on board an aircraft, dangerous goods that are not accompanied by the documentation or dangerous goods marks set out for the dangerous goods in Parts 1 to 6 and 8 of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

heading: Information To Be Included in an Undeclared or Misdeclared Dangerous Goods Report
paragraph: 8.15 A report referred to in section 8.14 must include the following information:

paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Undeclared or Misdeclared Dangerous Goods Report
paragraph: (b) the name of the aircraft operator, aerodrome or air cargo facility;

heading: Information To Be Included in an Undeclared or Misdeclared Dangerous Goods Report
paragraph: (c) the names and contact information of the consignor and consignee;

paragraph: (d) the date of the discovery of the dangerous goods;

paragraph: (g) the gross mass or capacity of the means of containment and, if applicable, the total number of means of containment; and

paragraph: (h) a description of the route by which the dangerous goods were to be transported, including the names of any aerodromes along the route.

paragraph: 8.15.1 A person must make a dangerous goods occurrence report (ICAO) to the Minister within seven days after discovering, at an aerodrome or air cargo facility or on board an aircraft, dangerous goods that have been transported on board an aircraft without

paragraph: (a) being loaded, segregated or secured in accordance with Chapter 2 of Part 7 of the ICAO Technical Instructions; or

heading: Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: 8.15.2 A dangerous goods occurrence report (ICAO) referred to in section 8.15.1 must be in writing and include the following information:

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (b) the name of the aircraft operator, aerodrome or air cargo facility;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (c) the names and contact information of the consignor and consignee;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (d) the date of the discovery of the occurrence referred to in paragraph 8.15.1(a) or (b);

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (e) the shipping name or UN number of the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (f) a description of the means of containment containing the dangerous goods;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (g) the gross mass or capacity of the means of containment and, if applicable, the total number of means of containment;

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (h) a description of the route by which the dangerous goods were, or were to be, transported, including the names of any aerodromes along the route; and

heading: Information To Be Included in a Dangerous Goods Occurrence Report (ICAO)
paragraph: (i) a detailed description of the circumstances that led to the discovery of the occurrence referred to in paragraph 8.15.1(a) or (b), as the case may be.

paragraph: 8.16 (1) A person who is required by subsection 18(3) of the Act to report the loss or theft of dangerous goods must, as soon as possible after the loss or theft, report it by telephone to the persons listed in subsection (3) if the lost or stolen dangerous goods are in excess of the quantity set out in subsection (2).

heading: Unlawful Interference Report
paragraph: 8.18 (1) If there has been unlawful interference with dangerous goods while they were being imported, offered for transport, handled or transported, the person who had the charge, management or control of the goods must, as soon as possible after the discovery of the unlawful interference, report it by telephone to the persons listed in subsection (2).

heading: Unlawful Interference Report
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), the persons to whom the unlawful interference must be reported are

heading: Unlawful Interference Report
paragraph: (b) in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 1, Explosives, or referred to in paragraph 8.16(2)(a) or subparagraph 8.16(2)(b)(i) or (c)(i), a Natural Resources Canada inspector, at 613-995-5555; and

heading: Unlawful Interference Report
paragraph: (c) in the case of dangerous goods included in Class 7, Radioactive Materials, the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

heading: Information To Be Included in an Unlawful Interference Report
paragraph: 8.19 A report referred to in section 8.18 must include the following information:

paragraph: (a) the name and contact information of the person making the report;

paragraph: (b) the names and contact information of the consignor, the consignee and the carrier;

paragraph: 8.20 A person who is required under subsection 18(1) of the Act to report a release or anticipated release of dangerous goods in respect of which an approved ERAP is required under subsection 7(1) of the Act must, as soon as possible after the release or anticipated release, make an ERAP incident report by telephone to the person at the ERAP telephone number required to be included on the shipping document under paragraph 3.6(1)(b), if the dangerous goods are, or could be, in excess of the quantity set out in the following table:

paragraph: (l) if applicable, the type of incident leading to the release or anticipated release, including a collision, rollover, derailment, overfill, fire, explosion or load-shift.

heading: ERAP Implementation Report
paragraph: 8.22 Each time a person implements an approved ERAP to tier 1 or tier 2, the person must, as soon as possible, make an ERAP implementation report to CANUTEC, at 1-888-CANUTEC (1-888-226-8832) or 613-996-6666.

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: 9.1 (1) Despite the requirements in Part 2 (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation) and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), a person may handle or transport dangerous goods by road vehicle from a place in the United States to a place in Canada or from a place in the United States through Canada to a place outside Canada in accordance with the classification, marking, labelling, placarding and documentation requirements of 49 CFR, if

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (a) the information required on the shipping document is easy to identify, legible, in indelible print, in English or French and includes

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (i) when dangerous goods are transported to a place in Canada, the name and address of the place of business in Canada of the consignor,

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (ii) when dangerous goods are transported from a place in the United States through Canada to a place outside Canada, the name and the address of the place of business of each consignor, except that in this case the name and address may be shown on a separate document attached to the shipping document and is required only while that person is the consignor,

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (iii) the classification in Schedule 1 or in the UN Recommendations, for dangerous goods that have the letter "D" assigned to them in column 1 of the table to section 172.101 of 49 CFR, except for dangerous goods with the shipping name "Consumer commodity", and

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (iv) if applicable, the information relating to the approved ERAP referred to in subsection 3.6(1);

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (b) the person complies with the following sections in Part 3 (Documentation):

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (i) section 3.2, Carrier responsibilities,

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (ii) section 3.7, Location of a shipping document: road, and

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (iii) section 3.10, Location of a shipping document: storage in the course of transportation; and

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (c) on or after August 31, 2008, the labels and placards displayed for dangerous goods included in Class 2.3 or Class 6.1 are the labels and placards required in these Regulations for the dangerous goods. The labels and placards may be displayed before August 31, 2008.

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to dangerous goods that

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (a) are forbidden for transport by these Regulations;

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (b) are not regulated by 49 CFR but are regulated by these Regulations; or

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (d) are given dangerous goods safety mark or packaging exceptions in 49 CFR that are not permitted by these Regulations.

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (3) A person who handles or transports dangerous goods by road vehicle in accordance with an exemption issued under Subpart B of Part 107 of 49 CFR may do so from a place in the United States to a place in Canada or from a place in the United States through Canada to a place outside Canada if the exemption number appears on the shipping document.

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods from the United States into or through Canada
paragraph: (4) If there is a conflict between the requirements of Part 2 (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks) or Part 5 (Means of Containment) and an exemption referred to in subsection (3), the exemption prevails to the extent of the conflict.

paragraph: 9.2 (1) Despite the requirements in Part 2 (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), if transport has been or is to be by aircraft, a person may handle or transport dangerous goods by road vehicle to or from an aircraft, an aerodrome or an air cargo facility in accordance with the classification, marking, labelling, and documentation requirements of the ICAO Technical Instructions, if

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from an Aircraft, an Aerodrome or an Air Cargo Facility
paragraph: (a) the information required on the shipping document is easy to identify, legible, in indelible print, in English or French and includes, if applicable, the information relating to the approved ERAP referred to in subsection 3.6(1); and

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from an Aircraft, an Aerodrome or an Air Cargo Facility
paragraph: (b) the person complies with the following provisions in Part 3 (Documentation):

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from an Aircraft, an Aerodrome or an Air Cargo Facility

paragraph: (iv) section 3.10, Location of a shipping document: storage in the course of transportation.

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from an Aircraft, an Aerodrome or an Air Cargo Facility
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if these Regulations forbid the transport of the dangerous goods or if the dangerous goods are not regulated by the ICAO Technical Instructions but are regulated by these Regulations.

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from an Aircraft, an Aerodrome or an Air Cargo Facility
paragraph: (3) When dangerous goods are transported to or from an aircraft, an aerodrome or an air cargo facility, by a road vehicle, the road vehicle, or any means of containment visible from outside the road vehicle, must have placards displayed on it in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks).

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from a Vessel, a Port Facility or a Marine Terminal
paragraph: 9.3 (1) Despite the requirements in Part 2 (Classification), Part 3 (Documentation), and Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), if transport has been or is to be by vessel, a person may handle or transport by road vehicle an international consignment of dangerous goods to or from a vessel, a port facility or a marine terminal in accordance with the classification, marking, labelling, placarding and documentation requirements of the IMDG Code if

paragraph: (b) the person complies with the following provisions in Part 3 (Documentation):

paragraph: (iii) section 3.7, Location of a shipping document: road, and

paragraph: (iv) section 3.10, Location of a shipping document: storage in the course of transportation.

heading: Transporting Dangerous Goods to or from a Vessel, a Port Facility or a Marine Terminal

heading: Coupling of Railway Vehicles
paragraph: 10.7 (1) A person must not couple a railway vehicle with another railway vehicle at a relative coupling speed greater than 9.6 km/h (6 mph) if either of the railway vehicles that make contact on coupling contains dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be displayed in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks).

heading: Coupling of Railway Vehicles
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a person may couple a single railway vehicle moving under its own momentum at a relative coupling speed less than or equal to 12 km/h (7.5 mph) when the ambient temperature is above -25ºC.

heading: Coupling of Railway Vehicles
paragraph: (3) If a person couples a tank car that contains dangerous goods for which a placard is required to be displayed in accordance with Part 4 (Dangerous Goods Safety Marks), with another railway vehicle and the three conditions in any one of the four rows set out in the table to this subsection apply, the person must

paragraph: (b) report, in writing, to the owner of the tank car within 10 days after the coupling and include a copy of the text of this section and information about any damage that compromises the integrity of the underframe assembly or draft gear of the tank car discovered as a result of the inspection.
