paragraph: (f) the explosives are placed in an inner means of containment that is a box, in metal or plastic clips or in partitions that fit snugly in an outer means of containment that is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety;

heading: Explosives, Class 1.4S
paragraph: (g) the primers are protected from accidental initiation; and

heading: Explosives, Class 1.4S
paragraph: (h) each of the outer means of containment is marked with the gross mass in kilograms and the words "Explosives - Excepted" or "Explosifs - Exceptes", in letters at least 25 mm high and in a colour that contrasts with the background colour of the means of containment.

heading: Explosives, Class 1.4S
paragraph: (2) Despite the restrictions that apply to item 19 of Table 8-1 to Chapter 1, Provisions for dangerous goods carried by passengers or crew, of Part 8, Provisions Concerning Passengers and Crew, of the ICAO Technical Instructions, ammunition, or ammunition loaded in a firearm, with the UN number and shipping name UN0012, CARTRIDGES FOR WEAPONS, INERT PROJECTILE or UN0012, CARTRIDGES, SMALL ARMS or UN0014, CARTRIDGES FOR WEAPONS, BLANK or UN0014, CARTRIDGES, SMALL ARMS, BLANK or UN0014, CARTRIDGES FOR TOOLS, BLANK, may be transported on board an aircraft by a peace officer as defined in section 3 of the Canadian Aviation Security Regulations, 2012, by a Canadian in-flight security officer or by a person described in item 22, column 1, of the table to subsection 78(2) of the Canadian Aviation Security Regulations, 2012.

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: 12.5 (1) A person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within Canada explosives that are forbidden for transport in any of columns 10 to 13 of Table 3-1, Dangerous Goods List, in Chapter 2, Arrangement of the dangerous goods list (Table 3-1), of Part 3, Dangerous Goods List, Special Provisions and Limited and Excepted Quantities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions if

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (a) the person complies with

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (i) paragraphs 12.1(1)(a) to (j),

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (ii) the quantity limits and the packing instructions set out in columns 10 to 13 of Table S-3-1, Supplementary Dangerous Goods List, in Chapter 2, Supplementary Dangerous Goods List (Class 1), of Part S-3, Dangerous Goods List, Special Provisions and Quantity Limitations, of the Supplement to the ICAO Technical Instructions, and

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (iii) the requirements of the ICAO Technical Instructions;

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (b) the explosives are

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (i) UN0030, DETONATORS, ELECTRIC for blasting,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (ii) UN0042, BOOSTERS without detonator,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (iii) UN0059, CHARGES, SHAPED without detonator,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (iv) UN0065, CORD, DETONATING, flexible,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (v) UN0081, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE A,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (vi) UN0082, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE B,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (vii) UN0083, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE C,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (viii) UN0084, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE D,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (ix) UN0241, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE E,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (x) UN0331, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING, TYPE B; or AGENT, BLASTING, TYPE B,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (xi) UN0332, EXPLOSIVE, BLASTING TYPE E; or AGENT, BLASTING, TYPE E, or

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (xii) UN0360, DETONATOR ASSEMBLIES, NON-ELECTRIC for blasting;

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (c) the explosives

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (i) are not included in compatibility group A,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (ii) have not deteriorated or been damaged,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (iii) do not have an active means of initiation and are not primed for use, and

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (iv) are in a means of containment that is required for them by the packing instructions set out in Chapter 3, Class 1 - Explosives, of Part S-4, Packing Instructions, of the Supplement to the ICAO Technical Instructions; and

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (d) there are no other dangerous goods transported on board the aircraft at the same time as the explosives.

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (2) The consignor of the explosives must

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (a) notify the air carrier, in writing, of the shipping name, UN number, primary class and compatibility group of the explosives at least 48 hours before the explosives are loaded on the aircraft;

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (b) keep a copy of the notification to the air carrier for two years after the date the notification is sent to the air carrier; and

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (c) notify the consignee at least 24 hours before the explosives are transported of the expected time of transport unless the consignor and the air carrier agree that the air carrier will notify the consignee of the expected time of transport when the air carrier gives the consignor written agreement to transport the explosives.

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (3) The air carrier must, at least 24 hours before transporting the explosives,

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (a) give the consignor written agreement to transport the explosives and keep a copy of this agreement for two years after the date the notification referred to in paragraph (2)(a) is sent to the consignor; and

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (b) notify each aerodrome operator listed on the flight plan of the intended time of departure, arrival and technical stops, if any.

heading: Forbidden Explosives
paragraph: (4) The notification referred to in paragraph (2)(a) and the agreement referred to in paragraph (3)(a) are valid for any subsequent transport of the explosives for two years beginning on the date that the notification and the agreement were made unless any of the information required in them changes.

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: 12.8 (1) A person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within Canada dangerous goods that are aerosols included in Class 2.1 or 2.2, are UN3175, SOLIDS CONTAINING FLAMMABLE LIQUID, N.O.S., or are included in Class 3 and Packing Group II or III or in Class 6.1 and Packing Group III, if

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (ii) the ICAO Technical Instructions, other than Chapter 2, Markings, Chapter 3, Labelling, and Chapter 4, Documentation, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, and paragraphs (j) and (l) of Packing Instruction Y963 of Chapter 11, Class 9 - Miscellaneous dangerous goods, of Part 4, Packing Instructions;

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (b) when the dangerous goods are liquid,

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (i) the quantity for Class 3, Packing Group II, is less than or equal to

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (A) 1 L in a metal inner means of containment, except for UN1263, PAINT or PAINT RELATED MATERIAL, in which case the quantity may be less than or equal to 5 L, or

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (B) 500 mL in a glass, earthenware or plastic inner means of containment, and

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (ii) the quantity for Class 3, Packing Group III, and for Class 6.1, Packing Group III, is less than or equal to

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (A) 5 L in a metal inner means of containment, or

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (B) 500 mL in a glass, earthenware or plastic inner means of containment; and

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (c) when the dangerous goods are solid, the quantity is less than or equal to 5 kg in an inner means of containment.

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (2) The person who offers for transport the dangerous goods must, on each small means of containment that contains the dangerous goods,

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (a) mark the words "Air Transport, 12.8, Consumer commodity" or "Transport aerien, 12.8, produit de consommation" in letters at least 25 mm high and in a colour that contrasts with the background colour of the means of containment; and

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (b) for liquids, except flammable liquids in a quantity less than or equal to 120 mL, display on two opposite sides of the means of containment a package orientation label illustrated in Figure 5-29 of Chapter 3, Labelling, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

heading: Packing Instruction Y963
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), the dangerous goods safety marks that are required by that subsection to be marked or displayed on a small means of containment are not required to be marked or displayed on a small means of containment that is inside another small means of containment if the other small means of containment is not opened during loading or unloading or while the dangerous goods are in transport.

paragraph: (i) transported by cargo aircraft or passenger carrying aircraft referred to in Subpart 4 of Part VI and Subparts 1 to 4 of Part VII of the Canadian Aviation Regulations,

paragraph: (d) when the dangerous goods are Class 2.1, Flammable Gases, or Class 3, Flammable Liquids, smoking is prohibited on board the aircraft and the aircraft and each area or compartment of the aircraft containing the dangerous goods is ventilated to prevent the accumulation of vapours;

paragraph: (2) The requirements in subsections (3) to (6) apply to dangerous goods that are included in Class 3, Flammable Liquids, and that are

paragraph: (f) UN1863, FUEL, AVIATION, TURBINE ENGINE, Packing Groups II and III only.

paragraph: (3) When the Class 3, Flammable Liquids, referred to in subsection (2) are

heading: Limited Access
paragraph: (a) contained in a small means of containment that is a drum, the drum must be securely closed and marked with one of the following manufacturer's permanent markings when the drum has a capacity greater than 25 L and less than or equal to 230 L: TC, CTC, DOT, ICC 5A, 5B, 5C, 17C, 17E, TC-34, CTC-34, DOT-34, UN 1A1, UN 1B1, UN 1H1 or UN 6HA; or

heading: Limited Access
paragraph: (i) the body of the drum or jerrican is not faded, discoloured, gouged, cracked or distorted to the extent that the integrity of the drum or jerrican is compromised,

paragraph: (i) neither the body nor the bottom chimes of the tank is damaged by wear, scoring, dents or corrosion to the extent that the integrity of the tank is compromised,

paragraph: (5) When the Class 3, Flammable Liquids, referred to in subsection (2) are contained in a large means of containment, that large means of containment must be

paragraph: (b) Packing Instruction 950 of Chapter 11, Class 9 - Miscellaneous dangerous goods, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, in the case of

paragraph: (i) UN3166, VEHICLE, FLAMMABLE GAS POWERED, or

paragraph: (d) Packing Instruction 378 of Chapter 5, Class 3 - Flammable liquids, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, in the case of

paragraph: (i) UN3528, ENGINE, INTERNAL COMBUSTION, FLAMMABLE LIQUID POWERED,

paragraph: (ii) the following packing instructions of Chapter 10, Class 8 - Corrosives, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, of the ICAO Technical Instructions, except that, when the aircraft is not a pressurized aircraft, section 1.1.6 of Chapter 1, General packing requirements, of Part 4, Packing Instructions, of the ICAO Technical Instructions does not apply:

heading: Limited Access
paragraph: (15) An air carrier must produce a record, notice or report required by subsection (1) within 15 days after the day on which a written request is received from an inspector.

heading: Private Aircraft
paragraph: 12.10 A person may handle or transport dangerous goods within Canada by small aircraft or helicopter registered as private aircraft under sections 202.16 and 202.17 of the Canadian Aviation Regulations if the dangerous goods

heading: Private Aircraft
paragraph: (a) are intended for non-commercial recreational use; and

heading: Private Aircraft
paragraph: (b) are not forbidden for transport by Schedule 1 or Schedule 3 to these Regulations or by the ICAO Technical Instructions.

heading: Geological Core Samples
paragraph: 12.11 A person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within Canada dangerous goods that are contained in geological core samples less than or equal to 100 mm in diameter if

heading: Geological Core Samples
paragraph: (a) when the consignor is not the air carrier, the consignor notifies the air carrier of the presence of the core samples before offering them for transport;

heading: Geological Core Samples
paragraph: (b) the core samples are transported in wooden core sample boxes that are wrapped in a sealed plastic or polyethylene bag or in a means of containment that is equally leak-proof;

heading: Geological Core Samples
paragraph: (c) the core samples as well as the means of containment are secured to prevent movement during transport; and

heading: Geological Core Samples
paragraph: (d) where the core samples contain radioactive material, they are contained in a means of containment in accordance with the Packaging and Transport of Nuclear Substances Regulations.

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: 12.12 (1) A person may handle, offer for transport or transport dangerous goods by aircraft within Canada if the dangerous goods are being used at the location where the following aerial work takes place:

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (a) active fire suppression;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (b) aerial cloud seeding;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (c) aerial drip torching;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (d) agriculture;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (e) avalanche control;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (f) forestry;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (g) horticulture;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (h) hydrographic or seismographic work; or

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (i) pollution control.

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (2) The dangerous goods must be contained in a means of containment that is

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (a) a tank, a container or an apparatus that is an integral part of the aircraft or that is attached to the aircraft in accordance with the Certificate of Airworthiness issued under the Canadian Aviation Regulations;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (b) a cylindrical collapsible rubber drum that is transported in or suspended from an aircraft and that is constructed, tested, inspected and used in accordance with MIL-D-23119G;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (c) a collapsible fabric tank that is transported suspended from a helicopter and that is constructed of material and seamed in accordance with MIL-T-52983G; or

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (d) a small means of containment designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety.

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (3) The air carrier must ensure that

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (a) the person who loads and secures the dangerous goods on board the aircraft is trained, or works under the direct supervision of a person who is trained, in accordance with Part 6 (Training) of these Regulations and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (b) if the dangerous goods are handled or transported by a person other than an employee of the air carrier, that person is trained in accordance with Part 6 (Training) of these Regulations and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (c) the air carrier complies with Part 8 (Reporting Requirements) of these Regulations;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (d) if the pilot-in-command of the aircraft does not load or directly supervise the loading of the dangerous goods, the person who loads and secures the dangerous goods gives the pilot-in-command, in writing, the following information for each of the dangerous goods:

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (i) its shipping name, UN number and class, and

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (ii) the gross mass of the dangerous goods and, in the case of explosives, the net explosives quantity;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (e) smoking is prohibited on board the aircraft and each area or compartment of the aircraft containing dangerous goods is ventilated to prevent the accumulation of vapour;

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (f) when an in-flight emergency occurs and circumstances permit, the pilot-in-command complies with section 4.3, Information to be provided by the pilot-in-command in case of in-flight emergency, of Chapter 4, Provision of information, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions; and

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (g) the person who loads and secures or directly supervises the loading and securing of dangerous goods on board the aircraft

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (i) complies with section 3.1, Inspection for damage or leakage, of Chapter 3, Inspection and decontamination, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions, and

heading: Aerial Work
paragraph: (ii) segregates the means of containment that contain dangerous goods that could react dangerously with one another in case of a release, in accordance with Table 7-1, "Segregation between packages", of Chapter 2, Storage and loading, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: 12.13 A person may handle or transport by aircraft within Canada a measuring instrument that contains dangerous goods if

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (a) the person who is responsible for the measuring instrument

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (i) ensures that the measuring instrument or its means of containment has displayed on it labels in accordance with Chapter 3, Labelling, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions,

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (ii) before transporting the measuring instrument on the aircraft, has the written agreement of the air carrier to use or transport the measuring instrument on board the aircraft, and

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (iii) is trained in accordance with Part 6 (Training) of these Regulations and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions and complies with all laws applicable to the measuring instrument;

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (b) the measuring instrument is placed or used in a location in the aircraft that is known to the pilot-in-command and the flight crew; and

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (c) when the measuring instrument contains radioactive materials,

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (i) the radiation level at 100 mm from any point of the external surface of the instrument is less than or equal to 100 µSv/h (10 millirems per hour), and

heading: Measuring Instruments
paragraph: (ii) the activity of the measuring instrument does not exceed the applicable exception limit set out in the column entitled "Item limits" in Table 2-14, "Activity limits for excepted packages", of Chapter 7, Class 7 - Radioactive material, of Part 2, Classification of Dangerous Goods, of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: 12.14 (1) A person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within Canada dangerous goods, other than Class 2, Gases, if

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods will be used or part of the dangerous goods have been used for a person who will require or who has required medical aid during flight;

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (b) the transport of the dangerous goods is not forbidden by Schedule 1 or Schedule 3 of these Regulations or the ICAO Technical Instructions;

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (c) before the dangerous goods are loaded, the person who offers them for transport receives the agreement of the air carrier to transport the dangerous goods on board the aircraft;

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (d) the air carrier

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (i) directly supervises the loading and securing of the dangerous goods on board the aircraft so that they do not move during transport,

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (ii) complies with section 3.1, Inspection for damage or leakage, of Chapter 3, Inspection and decontamination, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions, and

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (iii) provides to the pilot-in-command, in writing, the shipping name, the UN number and the class of the dangerous goods and their location on board the aircraft;

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (f) in the event of a change of aircraft or flight crew, the pilot-in-command communicates the information required by subparagraph (d)(iii) to the next pilot-in-command;

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (g) the air carrier's employees are trained, or work under the direct supervision of a person who is trained, in accordance with Part 6 (Training) of these Regulations and Chapter 4, Training, of Part 1, General, of the ICAO Technical Instructions; and

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (h) the air carrier complies with Part 8 (Reporting Requirements) of these Regulations.

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (2) The air carrier and the person who offers the dangerous goods for transport must ensure that

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (a) the dangerous goods are contained in a means of containment that is designed, constructed, filled, closed, secured and maintained so that under normal conditions of transport, including handling, there will be no accidental release of the dangerous goods that could endanger public safety; and

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (b) the means of containment has displayed on it the package markings and labels required by Chapter 2, Marking, and Chapter 3, Labelling, of Part 5, Shipper's Responsibilities, of the ICAO Technical Instructions.

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (3) A person may handle, offer for transport or transport by aircraft within Canada UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED, if

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (a) the air carrier and the person who offers the dangerous goods for transport comply with the requirements of subsection (1) and paragraph (2)(b);

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (b) the dangerous goods are in a cylinder that is in compliance with section 5.10 of Part 5 (Means of Containment) of these Regulations;

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (c) each cylinder contains a quantity of UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED, that is less than or equal to 850 L or 30 ft3;

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (d) the number of cylinders containing UN1072, OXYGEN, COMPRESSED, does not exceed 6 owned by the air carrier and one additional cylinder for each passenger who needs the oxygen at destination; and

heading: Medical Aid
paragraph: (e) the pilot-in-command is advised of the number of cylinders loaded on board the aircraft.

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: 12.17 A person may handle or transport within Canada, by an aircraft that does not have a Class B, Class C or Class D cargo compartment, dangerous goods other than those included in Class 4.3, Water Reactive Substances, if

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: (a) the person complies with

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: (i) paragraphs 12.1(1)(a) to (j), and

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: (ii) the ICAO Technical Instructions, other than section 2.1, Loading restrictions on flight deck and for passenger aircraft, of Chapter 2, Storage and loading, of Part 7, Operator's Responsibilities;

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: (b) a certificate was issued for the aircraft under Subpart 4 of Part VI or Subpart 3 or 4 of Part VII of the Canadian Aviation Regulations;

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: (c) transport of the dangerous goods is not forbidden by Schedule 1 or Schedule 3 of these Regulations or the ICAO Technical Instructions;

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: (d) transport of the dangerous goods is not restricted by the ICAO Technical Instructions to cargo aircraft only; and

heading: Flight Deck Loading Restrictions
paragraph: (e) the dangerous goods are loaded and transported in a compartment that is accessible during flight so that the dangerous goods and any other cargo can be readily reached by a crew member using, if necessary, a hand-held fire extinguisher.

heading: Effective Date and Expiry of a Protective Direction
paragraph: 13.1 (1) A protective direction takes effect on the date on which it is signed by the Minister or at a later date indicated in the protective direction. However, after the effective date of the protective direction, any non-compliance with it must not be enforced against a person unless the person has received the original signed protective direction or an electronic copy of it, or reasonable steps have been taken to make the person aware of the protective direction.

heading: Effective Date and Expiry of a Protective Direction
paragraph: (2) A protective direction expires on the expiry date specified in it. If no expiry date is specified in the protective direction, it expires 12 months after the date on which it is signed.

heading: Requesting a Review of a Protective Direction
paragraph: 13.2 (1) A person may request a review of a protective direction at any time after it is signed.

heading: Requesting a Review of a Protective Direction
paragraph: (2) The request must be made, in writing, to the Minister and must include the following information:

heading: Requesting a Review of a Protective Direction
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the place of business of the person requesting the review;

heading: Requesting a Review of a Protective Direction
paragraph: (b) the result the person expects from the review; and

heading: Requesting a Review of a Protective Direction
paragraph: (c) all the information necessary to support the request for the review.

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: 14.1 A person must apply to the Minister in writing for an equivalency certificate and must include the following information:

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (a) if the applicant is an individual, the name of the individual;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (b) if the applicant is a company or an association, the name of the company or association and each association member, as the names appear in letters patent, articles of incorporation or any other document that shows the legal identity of the company or the association and each association member;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (c) the address of the place of business of the applicant;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (d) the telephone number, including the area code, and, if applicable, the electronic mailing address and the facsimile number of the applicant;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (e) if a person submits an application on behalf of a company or an association, the person's name and position and the telephone number, including the area code, and address of the person's place of business;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (f) the classification of the dangerous goods and, if the dangerous goods are in a solution or mixture, the composition and percentage (specified by volume, mass or net explosives quantity) of each chemical;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (g) the method of packaging the dangerous goods, including a description of the means of containment and the quantity of dangerous goods in each means of containment;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (h) whether the equivalency certificate is requested for transport by road vehicle, railway vehicle, aircraft or vessel;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (i) a description of the proposal for an equivalency certificate, including

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (i) the requirements of the Act or these Regulations that the applicant proposes not to comply with,

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (ii) the manner in which the activity will be carried out and how that manner will provide a level of safety at least equivalent to that provided by compliance with the Act and these Regulations, and

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (iii) drawings, plans, calculations, procedures, test results and any other information necessary to support the proposal;

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (j) the length of time or the schedule of activities for which the equivalency certificate is requested; and

heading: Applying for an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (k) the name, position and business telephone number, including the area code, of the person who can be contacted regarding the application for an equivalency certificate and who is authorized by the applicant to speak on the applicant's behalf.

heading: Issuance or Refusal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: 14.2 If an application for an equivalency certificate is refused, the Minister must notify the applicant, in writing, of the refusal and the reasons for the refusal.

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: 14.3 A person must apply to the Minister in writing to renew an equivalency certificate and must include the following information:

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (a) if the applicant is an individual, the name of the individual;

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (b) if the applicant is a company or an association, the name of the company or association and each association member, as the names appear in letters patent, articles of incorporation or any other document that shows the legal identity of the company or the association and each association member;

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (c) the address of the place of business of the applicant;

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (d) the telephone number, including the area code, and, if applicable, the electronic mailing address and the facsimile number of the applicant;

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (e) if a person submits an application on behalf of a company or an association, the person's name and position and the telephone number, including the area code, and address of the person's place of business;

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (f) certification that the information provided in the original application in accordance with paragraphs 14.1(f) to (i) is still applicable and complete;

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (g) the length of time or the schedule of activities for which the renewal is requested; and

heading: Applying for Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (h) the name, position and business telephone number, including the area code, of the person who can be contacted regarding the application for a renewal and who is authorized by the applicant to speak on the applicant's behalf.

heading: Renewal or Refusal of a Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: 14.4 (1) The Minister may renew an equivalency certificate if the Minister is satisfied, on the basis of the information available and the information submitted with the application for a renewal, that the activity authorized by the equivalency certificate will provide a level of safety at least equivalent to that provided by compliance with the Act and these Regulations.

heading: Renewal or Refusal of a Renewal of an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (2) If an application for a renewal is refused, the Minister must notify the applicant, in writing, of the refusal and the reasons for the refusal.

heading: Revoking an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: 14.5 The Minister must notify a person, in writing, of the revocation of an equivalency certificate under subsection 31(6) of the Act and the reasons for the revocation.

heading: Requesting a Review of a Decision to Refuse or Revoke an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: 14.6 (1) A person may request a review of a decision to refuse or revoke an equivalency certificate within 30 days after the day on which the notification of the decision is received.

heading: Requesting a Review of a Decision to Refuse or Revoke an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (2) The request must be made in writing to the Minister and must include the following information:

heading: Requesting a Review of a Decision to Refuse or Revoke an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the place of business of the person requesting the review;

heading: Requesting a Review of a Decision to Refuse or Revoke an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (b) the reasons why the decision should be reversed; and

heading: Requesting a Review of a Decision to Refuse or Revoke an Equivalency Certificate
paragraph: (c) all of the information necessary to support the request for the review.

heading: Notification of a Decision
paragraph: 14.8 The Minister must notify, in writing, the person who made the request for a review of the decision and the reasons for the decision.

heading: Payment of Money for Research
paragraph: 15.1 A person who is subject to a court order that requires payment of an amount of money under paragraph 34(1)(d) of the Act to be used to conduct programs of research must

heading: Payment of Money for Research
paragraph: (a) provide a summary of the order, in writing, to the Minister within 30 days after the day on which the order is made; and

heading: Payment of Money for Research
paragraph: (b) give to the Minister the amount in the form of a certified cheque, money order or bank draft, payable to the Receiver General for Canada, within the period established by the court or, if no period is established, within 90 days after the day on which the order is made.

heading: Certificate of Designation
paragraph: 16.1 A certificate of designation issued to an inspector under subsection 10(2) of the Act must be in the following form:

heading: Certificate of Designation
paragraph: Photograph

heading: Certificate of Designation
paragraph: Photographie

heading: Certificate of Designation
paragraph: 3.8 cm x 3.2 cm

heading: Certificate of Designation
paragraph: 3,8 cm x 3,2 cm

heading: Inspection Certificate
paragraph: 16.2 An inspection certificate provided under subsection 11(1) of the Act when an inspector opens anything for inspection or takes a sample of anything that is sealed or closed up must be in the following form:

heading: Inspection Certificate
paragraph: Name / Signature / Certificate Number of Inspector

heading: Inspection Certificate
paragraph: Nom / Signature / Numero du certificat de l'inspecteur

heading: Inspection Certificate
paragraph: Date

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: 16.3 (1) When an inspector detains dangerous goods or a means of containment under subsection 17(1) or (2) of the Act, the inspector must deliver a Detention Notice in the form following this section to the person who has charge, management or control of the dangerous goods or of the means of containment at the time they are detained.

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: (2) The inspector must sign and date the Notice.

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: (3) The detention takes effect when the Notice is signed and dated by the inspector. However, any non-compliance with the detention must not be enforced against a person until the person has received the Notice or a copy of it or a reasonable attempt has been made to give the person the Notice or a copy of it.

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: (5) A person may request a review of the detention at any time after it takes effect and the Notice is delivered to the person who has charge, management or control of the dangerous goods or of the means of containment. The request must be made in writing to the Minister or the Director General and must include the following information:

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the place of business of the person requesting the review;

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: (b) a copy of the Notice;

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: (d) all of the information necessary to support the request for the review.

heading: Detention of Dangerous Goods or Means of Containment
paragraph: (6) The Minister or the Director General must notify the person, in writing, of the decision made and the reasons for the decision.

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: 16.4 (1) When an inspector directs a person, under subsection 17(3) of the Act, to take necessary measures to remedy non-compliance with the Act and these Regulations, the inspector must deliver to that person a Notice of Direction to Remedy Non-compliance in the form following this section.

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (2) The inspector must sign and date the Notice.

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (3) The Notice must also be signed and dated by one of the following designated persons before it is delivered to the person directed by the inspector to take the necessary measures: the Director, Compliance and Response, the Chief, Response Operations, or the Chief, Enforcement, of the Transport Dangerous Goods Directorate, Department of Transport.

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (4) The direction takes effect when the Notice is signed and dated in accordance with subsections (2) and (3). However, any non-compliance with the direction must not be enforced against a person until the person has received the Notice or a copy of it or a reasonable attempt has been made to give the person the Notice or a copy of it.

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (6) A person may request a review of the direction at any time after it takes effect and the Notice is delivered to the person who has charge, management or control of the dangerous goods or means of containment. The request must be made in writing to the Minister or the Director General and must include the following information:

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the place of business of the person requesting the review;

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (b) a copy of the Notice;

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (d) all of the information necessary to support the request for the review.

heading: Direction to Remedy Non-compliance
paragraph: (7) The Minister or the Director General must notify the person, in writing, of the decision made and the reasons for the decision.

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: 16.5 (1) When an inspector directs, under subsection 17(4) of the Act, a person who has charge, management or control of dangerous goods or means of containment that the dangerous goods or means of containment not be imported into Canada or, if they are already in Canada, that they be returned to their place of origin, the inspector must deliver to that person a Notice of Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin in the form following this section.

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: (2) The inspector must sign and date the Notice.

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: (3) The direction takes effect when the Notice is signed and dated by the inspector. However, any non-compliance with the direction must not be enforced against a person until the person has received the Notice or a copy of it or a reasonable attempt has been made to give the person the Notice or a copy of it.

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: (5) A person may request a review of the direction at any time after it takes effect and the Notice is delivered to the person who has charge, management or control of the dangerous goods or means of containment. The request must be made in writing to the Minister or the Director General and must include the following information:

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: (a) the name and address of the place of business of the person requesting the review;

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: (b) a copy of the Notice;

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: (d) all of the information necessary to support the request for the review.

heading: Direction Not to Import or to Return to Place of Origin
paragraph: (6) The Minister or the Director General must notify the person, in writing, of the decision made and the reasons for the decision.

heading: Definition
paragraph: 17.1 In this Part, site means a permanent location where dangerous goods are imported, offered for transport, handled or transported and are in the direct possession of a person conducting these activities, but does not include a location where dangerous goods are used only in the scope of a person's work or as raw materials in products that they manufacture.

heading: Application
paragraph: 17.2 (1) Subject to subsection (2), this Part applies to a person who imports, offers for transport, handles or transports dangerous goods at a site located in Canada that they own or operate.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a person who imports, offers for transport, handles or transports dangerous goods originating from outside Canada and passing through Canada to a destination outside Canada without any handling being done in Canada;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) a person conducting cross-border movements who does not have a headquarters in Canada or who does not operate a site in Canada where importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting activities take place;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) a person who offers for transport, handles or transports dangerous goods at a site that are in quantities necessary for a federal, provincial or municipal officer to carry out their duties with respect to the enforcement of federal, provincial or municipal law; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) a person operating one or more oil wells.

heading: Registration
paragraph: 17.3 (1) A person must not import, offer for transport, handle or transport dangerous goods at a site that they own or operate in Canada unless they are registered in the registration database relating to dangerous goods on the Department of Transport website in accordance with subsection (2) and comply with sections 17.4 and 17.5.

heading: Registration
paragraph: (2) A person registers in the database by providing the following information:

heading: Registration
paragraph: (a) the business number assigned to them by the Canada Revenue Agency, if any;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (b) their name and the address of their headquarters;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (c) the phone numbers and email addresses of both a contact person and their replacement when absent;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (d) the addresses of all sites where dangerous goods are imported, offered for transport, handled or transported;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (e) the mode of transport of dangerous goods used at each site;

heading: Registration
paragraph: (f) for each site, the classes and divisions of dangerous goods that were imported, offered for transport, handled or transported within the previous fiscal year, if any; and

heading: Registration
paragraph: (g) for each site, the importing, offering for transport, handling or transporting activities that were undertaken in the previous fiscal year, if any.

heading: Renewal
paragraph: 17.4 A person must renew their registration annually within 30 days of the anniversary date of their initial registration by validating or, if applicable, updating the information referred to in subsection 17.3(2) in the registration database relating to dangerous goods on the Department of Transport website.

heading: Changes to Information
paragraph: 17.5 A person must update the information in the registration database relating to dangerous goods on the Department of Transport website within 60 days after the day on which any change occurs to the information that they provided under paragraphs 17.3(2)(a) to (e) on their initial registration or annual renewal.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act, "Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement" means the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement among the Tsawwassen First Nation, Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada and Her Majesty the Queen in right of British Columbia set out in the Schedule, and includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) that agreement as it is given effect by an Act of Canada, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) amendments to that agreement made in accordance with it.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) Words and expressions used in this Act have the same meanings as they have in the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement, unless the context requires otherwise.

heading: Treaty and land claims agreement
paragraph:
2
		  The Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement is a treaty and a land claims agreement within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement
paragraph: 3		  (1) The Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement is approved, given effect and declared valid and has the force of law.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a person or body

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement
paragraph: (a) has the powers, rights, privileges and benefits conferred, and

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement
paragraph: (b) must perform the duties and is subject to the liabilities imposed

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement
paragraph: on the person or body by the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement
paragraph: (3) Nothing in this Act that provides for a matter that is already provided for in the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement in any way limits this section.

heading: Authorization to sign Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement
paragraph:
4
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may authorize a member of the Executive Council to sign the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement binding and can be relied on
paragraph:
5
		  The Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement is binding on, and can be relied on by, all persons.

heading: Relationship between final agreement and legislation
paragraph:
6
		  (1) As set out in clause 27 of Chapter 2 [General Provisions] of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement, the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement prevails to the extent of an inconsistency with Provincial Law.

heading: Relationship between final agreement and legislation
paragraph: (2) As set out in clause 28 of Chapter 2 [General Provisions] of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement, Provincial Settlement Legislation prevails over other Provincial Law to the extent of a Conflict.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph:
7
		  (1) In this section, "estate in fee simple" means the estate in fee simple within the meaning of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (2) On the Effective Date, the Tsawwassen First Nation owns the estate in fee simple in the following lands:

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (a) Tsawwassen Lands as identified in clause 1 of Chapter 4 [Lands] of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement;

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (b) Other Tsawwassen Lands as identified in clause 18 a. of that chapter.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (3) On the Effective Date, the soil and freehold of

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (a) the highways described in paragraphs a. and b. of the definition of "Local Road" in the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement,

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (b) the highways described in paragraph a. of the definition of "Local Boundary Road" in that agreement, and

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (c) the highway known as Eagle Way and legally described as Road Plan CLSR RD1801,

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: excluding any portion of those highways that was located within the Former Tsawwassen Reserve, are, without compensation to any person, transferred to and vested in the government.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (4) The transfer and vesting under subsection (3) are conclusively deemed to have occurred before the registration of Tsawwassen Lands under section 25 of Schedule 1 of the Land Title Act.

heading: Tsawwassen First Nation's ownership of lands
paragraph: (5) Section 35 of the Community Charter does not apply in relation to land vested in the government under subsection (3) of this section except any portion of that land that is not, on the Effective Date, registered in the land title office in the name of the Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: 8		  (1) As provided in clause 40 of Chapter 22 [Dispute Resolution] of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement, if, in any judicial or administrative proceeding, an issue arises in respect of

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (a) the interpretation or validity of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement, or

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (b) the validity or applicability of Settlement Legislation or a Tsawwassen Law,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: the issue must not be decided until the party raising the issue has properly served notice on the Attorney General of British Columbia, the Attorney General of Canada and the Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (2) The notice required under subsection (1) must

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (a) describe the judicial or administrative proceeding in which the issue arises,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (b) state whether the issue arises in respect of the matters referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (b) or both,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (c) state the day on which the issue is to be argued,

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (d) give particulars necessary to show the point to be argued, and

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (e) be served at least 14 days before the day of argument unless the court or tribunal authorizes a shorter notice.

heading: Judicial or administrative proceedings
paragraph: (3) As provided in clause 41 of Chapter 22 [Dispute Resolution] of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement, in a judicial or administrative proceeding to which subsection (1) applies, the Attorney General of British Columbia, the Attorney General of Canada and the Tsawwassen First Nation may appear and participate in the proceeding as parties with the same rights as any other party to the proceeding.

heading: Agricultural land reserve
paragraph:
9
		  (1) Despite sections 2 and 16 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act, the following lands are excluded from the agricultural land reserve:

heading: Agricultural land reserve
paragraph: (a) the lands described in clause 32 of Chapter 4 [Lands] of the Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement;

heading: Agricultural land reserve
paragraph: (b) agricultural land, as defined in the Agricultural Land Commission Act, that is within the Former Tsawwassen Reserve.

heading: Agricultural land reserve
paragraph: (2) Despite section 2 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act, on the Effective Date, the Agricultural Land Commission must amend the land reserve plan in accordance with subsection (1) and provide notice to the Tsawwassen First Nation and the registrar of titles that the amendment has been made.

heading: Agricultural land reserve
paragraph: (3) Despite section 2 of the Agricultural Land Commission Act, section 21 of that Act does not apply in relation to a subdivision plan of Tsawwassen Lands deposited in the land title office on the Effective Date for the purposes of registering those lands in the name of the Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: 10		  (1) In this section:

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: "Board", "Corporation" and "District" have the same meanings as in section 2 of the Greater Vancouver Water District Act;

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: "minister" means the minister charged with the administration of the Greater Vancouver Water District Act;

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: "Tsawwassen Indian Band" means the band, as defined in the Indian Act (Canada), named the Tsawwassen Indian Band.

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: (2) The membership of the Tsawwassen First Nation in the Corporation and the provision of water to the Tsawwassen First Nation by the Corporation must be

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: (a) on the terms and conditions that, despite the Greater Vancouver Water District Act, may be mutually agreed upon between the Board, on the recommendation of the Commission under that Act, and the Tsawwassen Indian Band, or

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: (b) if the Board and the Tsawwassen Indian Band cannot reach agreement under paragraph (a), on the terms and conditions as may be ordered by the minister under subsection (3).

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: (3) If the Board and the Tsawwassen Indian Band fail to agree on the terms and conditions under subsection (2) (a), the Tsawwassen Indian Band may appeal to the minister and the minister has full power and authority to settle, by order, the terms and conditions upon which Tsawwassen Lands will be added to the District and water will be provided to the Tsawwassen First Nation by the Corporation, and the order, on becoming effective under subsection (4), is final and binding upon the Tsawwassen First Nation and the Corporation.

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: (4) An agreement under subsection (2) or an order under subsection (3) becomes effective to add the Tsawwassen Lands to the District on the date that both the following have occurred:

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: (a) the Tsawwassen First Nation has, by Tsawwassen Law, confirmed the agreement or order;

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: (b) a regulation under subsection (5) is in effect,

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District
paragraph: and the Corporation must provide water to the Tsawwassen First Nation on the terms and conditions agreed or ordered, as the case may be.

heading: Power to add Tsawwassen First Nation to Greater Vancouver Water District

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PREAMBLE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: WHEREAS:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: A. Tsawwassen First Nation are Coast Salish, an aboriginal people, and speak a dialect of the Hun'qum'i'num language;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: B. Tsawwassen First Nation claim aboriginal rights based on their assertion of a unique, current and historical, cultural connection and use, since time immemorial, to the lands, waters and resources surrounding those areas of Roberts Bank, the Fraser River, the Fraser River estuary, Pitt Lake, the Pitt River, the Serpentine River, the Nicomekl River, Boundary Bay and the Gulf Islands, that comprise Tsawwassen Territory in Canada;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: C. The Constitution Act, 1982 recognizes and affirms the existing aboriginal and treaty rights of the aboriginal peoples of Canada, and the courts have stated that aboriginal rights include aboriginal title;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: D. Tsawwassen First Nation asserts that it has an inherent right to self-government, and the Government of Canada has negotiated self-government in this Agreement based on its policy that the inherent right to self-government is an existing aboriginal right within section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: E. Tsawwassen First Nation has never entered into a treaty or land claims agreement with the Crown;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: F. Canada established Tsawwassen Indian Reserve for the benefit of the Tsawwassen Indian Band;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: G. Tsawwassen First Nation and Canada are signatories to the Framework Agreement on First Nation Land Management, and Canada transferred to Tsawwassen First Nation land management authority for Tsawwassen Indian Reserve;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: H. Tsawwassen First Nation's existing aboriginal rights are recognized and affirmed by the Constitution Act, 1982, and the Parties have negotiated this Agreement under the British Columbia Treaty Commission process to provide certainty in respect of those rights and to allow them to continue and to have the effect and be exercised as set out in this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: I. Canada and British Columbia acknowledge the perspective of Tsawwassen First Nation that harm and losses in relation to its aboriginal rights have occurred in the past and express regret if any acts or omissions of the Crown have contributed to that perspective, and the Parties rely on this Agreement to move them beyond the difficult circumstances of the past;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: J. Canada and British Columbia acknowledge the aspiration of Tsawwassen First Nation to preserve, promote and develop the culture, heritage, language and economy of Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: K. Canada and British Columbia acknowledge the aspiration of Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen people to participate more fully in the economic, political, cultural and social life of British Columbia in a way that preserves and enhances the collective identity of Tsawwassen people as Tsawwassen First Nation, and to evolve and flourish in the future as a self-sufficient and sustainable community; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: L. The Parties are committed to the reconciliation of the prior presence of Tsawwassen First Nation and of the sovereignty of the Crown through the negotiation of this Agreement which will establish a new government to government relationship based on mutual respect;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NOW THEREFORE THE PARTIES AGREE AS FOLLOWS:

heading: Commencement
