heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 9 FISHERIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to harvest for Domestic Purposes:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Fish and Aquatic Plants in the Tsawwassen Fishing Area; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Intertidal Bivalves in the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: in accordance with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. The Tsawwassen Fishing Right is limited by measures necessary for conservation, public health or public safety.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. The Tsawwassen Fishing Right is held by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen First Nation may not Dispose of that right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members have the right to Trade and Barter Fish and Aquatic Plants harvested under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right, among themselves or with other aboriginal people of Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Harvesting of Fish and Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right will be conducted in accordance with the provisions of Tsawwassen Harvest Documents.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Unless otherwise provided for in a Tsawwassen Harvest Document, the Tsawwassen Fishing Right will be exercised within:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tsawwassen Fishing Area, in respect of all species of Fish and Aquatic Plants; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area, in respect of Intertidal Bivalves.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. Harvesting of Intertidal Bivalves under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right in areas where the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area overlaps with a National Park or National Marine Conservation Area will be conducted in accordance with the terms and conditions for harvesting in National Parks and National Marine Conservation Areas.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The Tsawwassen Fishing Right will be exercised in a manner that does not interfere with authorized uses or Dispositions of provincial Crown land existing on the Effective Date or authorized in accordance with clause 9.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. British Columbia may authorize uses of or Dispose of provincial Crown land and any authorized use or Disposition may affect the methods, times and locations of the harvest of Fish and Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right, provided that British Columbia ensures that those authorized uses or Dispositions do not deny Tsawwassen First Nation the reasonable opportunity to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants in the Tsawwassen Fishing Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. Upon six months notice by either Party, Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on a process to evaluate uses and Dispositions of provincial Crown land that have the potential to deny Tsawwassen First Nation the reasonable opportunity to harvest under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right in the Tsawwassen Fishing Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. British Columbia may authorize uses of or Dispose of provincial Crown land and any authorized use or Disposition:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. may affect the methods, times and locations of the harvest of Intertidal Bivalves under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right in the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. may, because of the location of the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area, result in Tsawwassen First Nation having no meaningful opportunity to harvest Intertidal Bivalves in the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. The harvest of Intertidal Bivalves under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right in the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area will be exercised in a manner that does not interfere with authorized uses or Dispositions of provincial Crown land existing on the Effective Date or authorized in accordance with clause 11.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. British Columbia has no obligation to Consult in respect of authorized uses or Dispositions of provincial Crown land made under clause 11.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. The Minister retains authority for managing and conserving Fish, Aquatic Plants, and Fish habitat and will exercise that authority in a manner that is consistent with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. The Tsawwassen Fishing Right may be exercised by those individuals who are designated by Tsawwassen First Nation to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Any vessel used to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right will be a vessel that has been designated by Tsawwassen First Nation. For greater certainty, this Agreement does not alter the application of Federal or Provincial Law in respect of foreign fishing vessels in Canadian waters.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. Neither Canada nor British Columbia will require an individual, designated by Tsawwassen First Nation, to have a licence for the harvesting of Fish and Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Neither Canada nor British Columbia will charge a fee for a Tsawwassen Harvest Document, or any management fee or landing fee in respect of fisheries authorized by a Tsawwassen Harvest Document.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. Fish and Aquatic Plants harvested under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right may not be sold.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. This Agreement does not alter Federal or Provincial Law in respect of property in Fish or Aquatic Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. Nothing in this Agreement precludes:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Tsawwassen Members from harvesting Fish and Aquatic Plants under a licence, permit or other document issued under Federal or Provincial Law, or as otherwise authorized under Federal or Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Tsawwassen First Nation from concluding agreements that are in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law with other aboriginal groups with respect to designations to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. Tsawwassen Members from being designated by another aboriginal group to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants under federal or provincial arrangements with that aboriginal group.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Tsawwassen First Nation will provide catch data and other information related to Fish and Aquatic Plants harvested under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right as required by Tsawwassen Harvest Documents or Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN ALLOCATIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. The Tsawwassen Allocations for Fish and Aquatic Plants are set out in Appendix J-2.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. In any year in which the Minister determines, in respect of a stock or species of Fish or Aquatic Plants for which there is a Tsawwassen Allocation expressed as a fixed number, that the quantity of that stock or species that is available for harvest is not sufficient to meet all anticipated allocations from that stock or species for food, social or ceremonial purposes, the Minister may reduce any one or more of the allocations for that year.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. Where, under clause 24, the Minister wishes to reduce a Tsawwassen Allocation, the Minister will inform the Joint Fisheries Committee of the proposed reduction and, if time permits, will take into account any written recommendations on the proposed reduction received from the Joint Fisheries Committee before implementing the reduction.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Where under clause 24, the Minister reduces a Tsawwassen Allocation, the Minister will give reasons in writing for the reduction to Tsawwassen First Nation and the Joint Fisheries Committee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: OVERAGES AND UNDERAGES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. The Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation will endeavour to minimize any overages or underages for Tsawwassen Allocations in each year and to minimize the accumulation of overages and underages through adjustments to the Tsawwassen First Nation annual harvest in successive years.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. The Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines describe the process, timing and data sources for calculating overages and underages.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. Unless Canada and Tsawwassen First Nation agree otherwise, the determination of overages and underages described in the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines will be consistent with the principles described in Appendix J-3.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. Overages and underages will not be applied to non-salmon Fish species harvested under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right and managed by British Columbia as of the Effective Date.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NON-ALLOCATED SPECIES - CRAB

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. Any Tsawwassen Harvest Document for Tsawwassen First Nation to harvest crab under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right will authorize the harvest to be carried out using the number of traps proposed by Tsawwassen First Nation in the Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan for the harvest if:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the number of traps does not exceed 50 traps per vessel;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the traps meet the requirements for traps for harvesting crab as set out in the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a Tsawwassen Allocation for crab has not been established under this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PROCESS FOR NON-ALLOCATED SPECIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. For the purposes of this chapter,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. "Non-Allocated Species" means a species of Fish or Aquatic Plant for which a Tsawwassen Allocation has not been established under this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. "Basic Harvest Entitlement" for a Non-Allocated Species means Tsawwassen First Nation average annual harvest, expressed as:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. a defined harvest quantity or quota;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. a harvest quantity or quota determined by the use of a formula; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. a harvest quantity or quota determined by the use of a formula with respect to a defined harvest area within the Tsawwassen Fishing Area or the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: for that species for Domestic Purposes, over the Base Period for that Non-Allocated Species, as may be determined by arbitration under clauses 40 through 49;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. "Base Period" for a Non-Allocated Species means a period of 10 calendar years immediately preceding the date of a proposal made under clause 34 for the establishment of a Tsawwassen Allocation for the Non-Allocated Species, or such other period as the Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation may agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. Non-Allocated Species may be harvested for Domestic Purposes under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right in accordance with Tsawwassen Harvest Documents.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. Subject to clause 35, the Minister or Tsawwassen First Nation may propose the establishment of a Tsawwassen Allocation for a Non-Allocated Species by providing the other Parties with a written proposal and providing a copy of the proposal to the Joint Fisheries Committee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. The Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation will propose the establishment of a Tsawwassen Allocation for crab under clause 34 in the twelfth year after the Effective Date or such other date as the Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation may agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. Where, under clause 34, the Minister or Tsawwassen First Nation proposes the establishment of a Tsawwassen Allocation for a Non-Allocated Species under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right, the Joint Fisheries Committee will consider the proposal, taking into account:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Base Period information on the harvests by Tsawwassen First Nation of that Non-Allocated Species for Domestic Purposes;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. measures necessary for conservation, including the impact of those measures on the harvests by Tsawwassen First Nation of that Non-Allocated Species for Domestic Purposes;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. harvests for management of that Non-Allocated Species;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. other harvests of that Non-Allocated Species for food, social or ceremonial purposes;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. the impact of commercial and recreational fisheries on harvests by Tsawwassen First Nation of that Non-Allocated Species for Domestic Purposes; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. other relevant information.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. Where all representatives of the Joint Fisheries Committee agree, the Joint Fisheries Committee may recommend to the Parties that studies, in respect of the information referred to in clause 36, be conducted to assist the representatives in reaching agreement on a recommendation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 38. Where all representatives of the Joint Fisheries Committee agree on a recommendation for a Tsawwassen Allocation for a Non-Allocated Species, the Joint Fisheries Committee will notify the Parties of that recommendation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 39. Where, six months after receipt of a proposal under clause 34, the Joint Fisheries Committee has not agreed on recommendations for a Tsawwassen Allocation, the Joint Fisheries Committee will notify the Parties that they are unable to agree on a recommendation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ARBITRATED TSAWWASSEN ALLOCATON

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 40. Where a proposal is made under clause 34 to establish a Tsawwassen Allocation for a Non-Allocated Species and the Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation have not agreed to a Tsawwassen Allocation for that Non-Allocated Species within one year after the proposal, the Basic Harvest Entitlement for that Non-Allocated Species will be finally determined by arbitration, under the Dispute Resolution chapter, without proceeding through Stages One and Two.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 41. Where the Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation agree with the recommendation of the Joint Fisheries Committee for studies, the Parties may agree to extend the time period referred to in clause 39 or 40 to allow for the completion of the studies referred to in clause 37.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 42. The Minister or Tsawwassen First Nation may request that an arbitrator describe a Basic Harvest Entitlement for a Non-Allocated Species under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right as a defined harvest quantity or quota, or a harvest quantity or quota determined by the use of a formula, or a harvest quantity or quota determined by the use of a formula in respect of a defined harvest area within the Tsawwassen Fishing Area or Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 43. In an arbitration referred to in clause 40, the arbitrator will take into account the factors set out in clause 36.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 44. In an arbitration referred to in clause 40, the arbitrator will determine the Basic Harvest Entitlement within a period of not more than one year.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 45. An arbitrator may extend the time period referred to in clause 44 to allow for the completion of studies referred to in clause 37.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 46. Where an arbitrator determines the Basic Harvest Entitlement for a species, the Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation will, as soon as practicable, negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on the Tsawwassen Allocation for that species.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 47. If, six months after an arbitrator provides a decision to the Parties under clause 40, the Parties have not agreed on the Tsawwassen Allocation for that Non-Allocated Species, the Tsawwassen Allocation for that Non-Allocated Species is the Basic Harvest Entitlement times 1.25.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 48. In the case of crab, where an arbitrator determines the Basic Harvest Entitlement for crab under clause 40, the Parties will use that Basic Harvest Entitlement as the Tsawwassen harvest level for crab until the Parties reach agreement on a Tsawwassen Allocation under clause 46 or until a Tsawwassen Allocation is established under clause 49.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 49. In the case of crab, if 30 months after an arbitrator provides a decision under clause 40, the Parties have not agreed on the Tsawwassen Allocation, the Tsawwassen Allocation is the Basic Harvest Entitlement times 1.25.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: AMENDMENT TO THE FINAL AGREEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 50. Where the Minister and Tsawwassen First Nation agree in writing to the Tsawwassen Allocation for a Non-Allocated Species, or a Tsawwassen Allocation for a Non-Allocated Species is determined under clause 47 or 49, the Parties will amend this Agreement, in accordance with clause 11 of the Amendment chapter, to include the Tsawwassen Allocation in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: POWER TO MAKE LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 51. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the designation of individuals and vessels to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the distribution among Tsawwassen Members of Fish and Aquatic Plants harvested under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 52. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 51 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 53. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the designation of individuals and vessels by Tsawwassen First Nation to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants under fishing licences that are issued to Tsawwassen First Nation but that are not Tsawwassen Harvest Documents;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the documentation of individuals and vessels designated by Tsawwassen First Nation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the Trade and Barter by Tsawwassen Members of Fish and Aquatic Plants harvested under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 54. A Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 53.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DESIGNATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 55. Where a Tsawwassen Allocation for a species of Fish or Aquatic Plants has been established under this Agreement, Tsawwassen First Nation may designate Tsawwassen Members and other individuals to harvest that species of Fish or Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 56. Tsawwassen First Nation may not designate individuals who are not Tsawwassen Members to harvest a species of Fish or Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right where no Tsawwassen Allocation for that species has been established under this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DOCUMENTATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 57. Where Tsawwassen First Nation designates an individual or a vessel, Tsawwassen First Nation will issue written documentation to the individual or vessel to evidence the designation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 58. Documentation issued under clause 57 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. be in the English language, which version is authoritative and, at the discretion of Tsawwassen First Nation, in the Hun'qum'i'num language;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. in the case of an individual, include the name and address of the individual; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. meet any requirements set out in the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines and Tsawwassen Harvest Documents.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN HARVEST DOCUMENTS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 59. Each year, or periodically for those fisheries matters managed by British Columbia, the Minister will issue one or more Tsawwassen Harvest Documents to Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of the Tsawwassen Fishing Right. A Tsawwassen Harvest Document will be consistent with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 60. Tsawwassen First Nation will inform those individuals who are designated by Tsawwassen First Nation to harvest Fish and Aquatic Plants under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right of the provisions of the Tsawwassen Harvest Documents.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 61. Where the Minister issues a Tsawwassen Harvest Document, the Minister will take into account:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. conservation measures and the availability of fisheries resources;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the recommendations on the provisions of Tsawwassen Harvest Documents that the Minister has received in a timely way from the Joint Fisheries Committee;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. utilization of the fisheries resources for the benefit of all Canadians;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. efficient and effective harvesting of fisheries resources;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. requirements for integration and efficient management of all fisheries;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. accepted scientific procedures for management of fisheries resources; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. any other matters that the Minister considers relevant.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 62. The Minister will provide written reasons to Tsawwassen First Nation and the Joint Fisheries Committee if the provisions of a Tsawwassen Harvest Document differ significantly from:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the provisions that the Joint Fisheries Committee recommended to the Minister for inclusion in the Tsawwassen Harvest Document; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a written recommendation in respect of the Tsawwassen Harvest Document under clause 77.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 63. Where the Minister amends a Tsawwassen Harvest Document, the Minister will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. give notice to;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provide written reasons to; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. where practicable, discuss those amendments in advance with

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen First Nation and the Joint Fisheries Committee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 64. Where special circumstances make it impracticable to discuss an amendment with Tsawwassen First Nation or the Joint Fisheries Committee under clause 63, the Minister:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. may amend the Tsawwassen Harvest Document without receiving recommendations from the Joint Fisheries Committee; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. will notify the Joint Fisheries Committee and Tsawwassen First Nation as soon as practicable of the amendment and the reasons for the amendment.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN ANNUAL FISHING PLAN

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 65. Every year, Tsawwassen First Nation will develop a Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan for the harvest under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right of Non-Allocated Species of Fish and Aquatic Plants, and species for which there is a Tsawwassen Allocation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 66. A Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan will include, as appropriate, Tsawwassen First Nation preferences as to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the stocks or species of Fish and Aquatic Plants to be harvested and, where appropriate, the amounts;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a description of the Fish and Aquatic Plants to be harvested;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the species, locations and timing of the harvest of Intertidal Bivalves;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the location and timing of harvests;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. access to specific run timing groups;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. the method of harvest, the size, type, identification, marking, and quantity of fishing gear and the manner in which it may be used;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. the monitoring of harvests, including notification, catch monitoring, identification and reporting of harvest;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. the distribution and transportation of Fish and Aquatic Plants harvested under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. Tsawwassen First Nation enforcement activities;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: j. other matters as may be required for Tsawwassen Harvest Documents; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: k. other matters in respect of Tsawwassen fisheries.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 67. Each year, Tsawwassen First Nation will provide a Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan to the Joint Fisheries Committee in a timely way.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: JOINT FISHERIES COMMITTEE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 68. On the Effective Date, the Parties will establish a Joint Fisheries Committee to facilitate cooperative assessment, planning, and management of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the exercise of the Tsawwassen Fishing Right;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Enhancement Initiatives and Stewardship Activities by Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. monitoring and enforcement activities in respect of Tsawwassen First Nation fisheries; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. other matters as the Parties may agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 69. Subject to federal and provincial access to information and privacy legislation, the Parties will provide each other with access to publicly available information necessary to enable the Joint Fisheries Committee to carry out its functions and activities.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 70. The Joint Fisheries Committee will consist of one representative from each Party, but additional individuals may participate in meetings to support or assist a representative.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 71. Canada may choose not to attend Joint Fisheries Committee meetings on fisheries matters managed by British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 72. British Columbia may choose not to attend Joint Fisheries Committee meetings on fisheries matters managed by Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 73. In facilitating cooperative activities and functions under clause 68, the Joint Fisheries Committee may:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. discuss publicly available information for proposed new emerging commercial fisheries and other fisheries that may be conducted in Tsawwassen Territory or that could significantly affect the Tsawwassen Fishing Right;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. discuss publicly available information that is related to measures necessary for conservation, public health or public safety that could significantly affect the Tsawwassen Fishing Right;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. discuss publicly available information related to proposed Enhancement Initiatives in the Tsawwassen Fishing Area or Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. arrange for the collection and exchange of publicly available data on fisheries;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. discuss possible provisions for a Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan or Tsawwassen Harvest Documents before Tsawwassen First Nation develops a Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. review a Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. review proposals by Tsawwassen First Nation for Enhancement Initiatives;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. communicate with other advisory bodies in respect of matters of mutual interest;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. exchange publicly available information on issues related to international arrangements that could significantly affect the Tsawwassen Fishing Right; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: j. carry out other functions and activities as the Parties may agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 74. The Joint Fisheries Committee may discuss and make recommendations to the Parties in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Tsawwassen First Nation fisheries for Non-Allocated Species and Tsawwassen Allocations;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the management and harvesting of Fish in the Tsawwassen Fishing Area and the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the management and harvesting of Fish outside the Tsawwassen Fishing Area and the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area that could significantly affect harvesting under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the management and protection of Fish habitat;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. Enhancement Initiatives and Stewardship Activities conducted by Tsawwassen First Nation in Tsawwassen Territory;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. overages and underages;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. in-season amendments to Tsawwassen Harvest Documents;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. the provisions for Tsawwassen Harvest Documents, taking into account, among other things, provisions related to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. matters set out in a Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan, where Tsawwassen First Nation gives the Tsawwassen Annual Fishing Plan to the Joint Fisheries Committee in a timely way;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. measures for establishing harvest amounts for a Non-Allocated Species in any given year;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. access to a specific stock; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. other measures for the harvest and management of Fish;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. procedures for the identification of surplus Salmon and terms and conditions for harvests of surplus Salmon;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: j. the size and disposition of surplus Salmon;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: k. the harvest of surplus Salmon; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: l. other matters that could significantly affect harvesting under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 75. The Joint Fisheries Committee will establish its own operating procedures and the Parties will set them out in the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 76. The Joint Fisheries Committee representatives will seek to operate by consensus. The representatives of the Joint Fisheries Committee representing the Tsawwassen First Nation and Canada are responsible for functions and activities in respect of fisheries matters managed by Canada. The representatives of the Joint Fisheries Committee representing the Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia are responsible for functions and activities in respect of fisheries matters managed by British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 77. If the Joint Fisheries Committee has not been able to reach agreement on a recommendation or is unable to convene due to special circumstances, any Party may submit its written recommendations to the Minister and will provide a copy to the other Parties.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 78. If special circumstances make it impracticable for the Minister to receive recommendations from the Joint Fisheries Committee, the Minister:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. may make the decision or take the action that the Minister considers necessary, without receiving recommendations from the Joint Fisheries Committee; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. for the matters described in the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines, will provide written reasons to the Joint Fisheries Committee, as soon as practicable, of the special circumstances and the decision made or action taken.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN FISHERIES OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 79. The Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines set out the operational principles, procedures and guidelines to assist the Parties to implement this chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 80. The Parties will update and maintain the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines document as required.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: REGIONAL FISHERIES COMMITTEE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 81. Where a regional fisheries committee is proposed or established for aboriginal fisheries in an area that includes all or part of the Tsawwassen Fishing Area or Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area and that committee has functions and activities similar to those of the Joint Fisheries Committee, the Parties will determine which functions or activities of the Joint Fisheries Committee can be addressed more effectively by a regional fisheries committee, and will discuss the mechanism for participation by Tsawwassen First Nation in the regional fisheries committee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 82. Any Party may request that a function or activity of the Joint Fisheries Committee be performed by the regional fisheries committee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 83. In determining which functions or activities of the Joint Fisheries Committee can be addressed more effectively by a regional fisheries committee under clause 81, no Party will unreasonably withhold consent to a request made by another Party.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 84. Where the Parties agree that a function or activity of the Joint Fisheries Committee will be carried out by a regional fisheries committee:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Parties will update the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines document, as required, to reflect the change; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a reference in this Agreement to the Joint Fisheries Committee will be read as a reference to the regional fisheries committee for that function or activity.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 85. Where a regional fisheries committee performs a function or activity of the Joint Fisheries Committee:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. any Party may request that a function or activity that is not effectively addressed or efficiently coordinated by the regional fisheries committee be resumed by the Joint Fisheries Committee; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the Parties will update the Tsawwassen Fisheries Operational Guidelines document, as required, to reflect the change.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 86. In determining which functions or activities of the regional fisheries committee can be resumed by the Joint Fisheries Committee, under subclause 85.a, no Party will unreasonably withhold its consent to a request made by another Party.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 87. If a regional fisheries committee is terminated and is not replaced by another process, the Joint Fisheries Committee will resume its original functions or activities.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 88. The Parties will, from time to time, review and discuss the effectiveness of the Joint Fisheries Committee and the regional fisheries committee that carries out a function or activity of the Joint Fisheries Committee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PUBLIC FISHERIES MANAGEMENT ADVISORY PROCESS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 89. Where Canada or British Columbia proposes to establish a public fisheries management advisory process for an area of the Fraser River watershed that includes any part of the Tsawwassen Fishing Area or Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area, Canada or British Columbia will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation in developing that public fisheries management advisory process and, if appropriate, will provide for participation by Tsawwassen First Nation on the same basis as other First Nations.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 90. Neither a public fisheries management advisory process referred to in clause 89 nor a regional fisheries committee referred to in clause 81 is an international fisheries advisory process.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 91. The design, establishment and termination of public fishery advisory management processes are at the discretion of the Minister.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENFORCEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 92. The Parties may negotiate agreements in respect of the enforcement of Federal and Provincial Laws and Tsawwassen Laws in respect of fisheries.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 93. Tsawwassen Laws made under this chapter may be enforced by persons authorized to enforce, in British Columbia, Federal Law, Provincial Law or Tsawwassen Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: STEWARDSHIP AND ENHANCEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 94. With the approval of the Minister and in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law, Tsawwassen First Nation may conduct Enhancement Initiatives and Stewardship Activities in Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 95. Canada and Tsawwassen First Nation may negotiate agreements in respect of Tsawwassen First Nation activities related to Enhancement Initiatives and Stewardship Activities.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN FISHERIES FUND

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 96. On the Effective Date, Canada will pay to Tsawwassen First Nation one million dollars ($1,000,000) to establish a Tsawwassen Fisheries Fund.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 97. The Tsawwassen Fisheries Fund may be used for:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. promoting the conservation and protection of Fish and Aquatic Plants and Fish habitat in Tsawwassen Territory;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. facilitating the sustainable management of Fish and Fish habitat in Tsawwassen Territory; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. promoting and supporting participation by Tsawwassen First Nation in the stewardship of Fish and Fish habitat in Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 98. In pursuing the uses of the Tsawwassen Fisheries Fund, Tsawwassen First Nation may seek and consider recommendations from the Joint Fisheries Committee.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: MARINE PROTECTED AREAS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 99. Canada will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation when Canada proposes to establish, terminate, or change the boundaries of a Marine Protected Area that is wholly or partially within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 100. Tsawwassen First Nation may recommend in writing that Canada establish, terminate or change the boundaries of a Marine Protected Area that is wholly or partially within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 101. Where Tsawwassen First Nation makes a written recommendation under clause 100 to establish, terminate or change the boundaries of a Marine Protected Area that is wholly or partially within Tsawwassen Territory, Canada will review the recommendation and provide a written response.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 102. On the Effective Date, Canada, British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation will enter into a Tsawwassen First Nation Harvest Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 103. For greater certainty, as provided for under clause 58 of the General Provisions chapter, a Tsawwassen First Nation Harvest Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. is not part of this Agreement; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. is not a treaty or land claims agreement and does not create, recognize or affirm aboriginal or treaty rights within the meaning of sections 25 and 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 104. A Party may terminate a Tsawwassen First Nation Harvest Agreement and it will recompense the Tsawwassen First Nation in accordance with the terms of that agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 105. For purposes of increasing the commercial fishing capacity of Tsawwassen First Nation, on the Effective Date, Canada will provide to Tsawwassen First Nation amounts, to be paid in accordance with clause 1 of the Capital Transfer and Negotiation Loan Repayment chapter, to establish:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a Tsawwassen Commercial Fish Fund; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a Tsawwassen Commercial Crab Fund.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: The values in 2006 of the amounts referred to in subclauses 105.a and 105.b are approximately $1,155,000 and $450,000, respectively.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NEW EMERGING COMMERCIAL FISHERIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 106. Where the Minister proposes to establish a new emerging commercial fishery within Pacific Fishery Management Areas 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 28 or 29, the Minister will advise Tsawwassen First Nation of the proposal to establish the fishery and will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation on a process for participants to enter the fishery and for how the fishery should be allocated among participants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 107. Any participation by Tsawwassen First Nation in any new emerging commercial fishery authorized by the Minister will be determined in accordance with the process established by the Minister.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: AQUACULTURE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 108. Tsawwassen First Nation may give notice to British Columbia within ten years of the Effective Date that it wishes to negotiate a shellfish aquaculture tenure within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 109. A notice from Tsawwassen First Nation under clause 108 will include written confirmation that Tsawwassen First Nation has addressed any issues arising from claims of other aboriginal groups to specific shellfish aquaculture tenure sites proposed by Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 110. Upon receiving notice from Tsawwassen First Nation under clause 109, British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on a shellfish aquaculture tenure under Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Schedule

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 10 WILDLIFE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to harvest Wildlife for Domestic Purposes in the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area in accordance with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife is limited by measures necessary for conservation, public health or public safety.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife is held by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen First Nation may not Dispose of that right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members have the right to Trade and Barter Wildlife or Wildlife parts, including meat and furs, harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife, among themselves or with other aboriginal people of Canada resident in British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Tsawwassen First Nation may sell Wildlife or Wildlife parts, including meat and furs, harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife if the sale is permitted under Federal and Provincial Law, and any such sale will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law and any Tsawwassen Law made under subclause 22.b.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. British Columbia may authorize uses of or Dispose of provincial Crown land, including Provincial Parks and Protected Areas, and any authorized use or Disposition:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. may affect the methods, times and locations of the harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. having regard to the location of the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area within and adjacent to a heavily urbanized area with limited Wildlife habitat, may result in Tsawwassen First Nation being without any meaningful opportunity to harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife will be exercised in a manner that does not interfere with authorized uses or Dispositions of provincial Crown land, including Provincial Parks and Protected Areas, existing on the Effective Date or authorized in accordance with clause 6.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia may meet, at the request of either Party, to discuss the harvest of Wildlife, including harvest for Domestic Purposes, or the development of a Wildlife Harvest Plan.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. In compensation for the limited existing opportunity to harvest Wildlife and the likely future diminution or loss of any meaningful opportunity to harvest Wildlife in the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area, on the Effective Date, Canada will provide to Tsawwassen First Nation an amount, to be paid in accordance with clause 1 of the Capital Transfer and Negotiation Loan Repayment chapter, for the purpose of establishing a Wildlife Fund. The value in 2006 of that amount is approximately $50,000. No additional compensation will be payable by Canada or British Columbia at any time to Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of the limited opportunity or diminution or loss of any meaningful opportunity to harvest Wildlife in the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. British Columbia has no obligation to Consult in respect of its authorized uses or Dispositions of Crown land made under clause 6, other than as set out in clauses 34 and 35 of the Provincial Parks and Gathering chapter.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. Tsawwassen First Nation may exercise the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife on Private Lands, if the owner or occupant of that land agrees to provide access.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Tsawwassen First Nation may exercise the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife on a Reserve if the Indian Band for whom the Reserve is set aside agrees to provide access.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. This Agreement does not preclude Tsawwassen First Nation from entering into an agreement with a federal department or agency in respect of access and harvesting by Tsawwassen Members on land owned or in use by that department or agency in accordance with that agreement and Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. Tsawwassen First Nation may exercise the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife within Burns Bog Ecological Conservancy Area if harvesting of Wildlife is permitted on the lands, and any such harvesting will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law, and Local Government bylaws.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. The Minister retains authority for managing and conserving Wildlife and Wildlife habitat and will exercise that authority in a manner that is consistent with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Neither Canada nor British Columbia will require a Tsawwassen Member to have a licence or to pay a fee or royalty for harvesting Wildlife under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. Nothing in this Agreement affects the application of Federal or Provincial Law in respect of the possession, use or regulation of firearms.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. This Agreement does not alter Federal or Provincial Law in respect of property in Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. This Agreement does not preclude Tsawwassen Members from harvesting Wildlife in Canada under:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Federal or Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. an agreement, that is in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law, between Tsawwassen First Nation and other aboriginal people; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. an arrangement between other aboriginal people and Canada or British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: POWER TO MAKE LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the designation of Tsawwassen Members to harvest Wildlife under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the distribution among Tsawwassen Members of Wildlife harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the Trade and Barter of Wildlife harvested by Tsawwassen Members under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. methods, timing, and location of the harvest of Wildlife by Tsawwassen Members under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. the identification of which Wildlife and Wildlife parts, harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife, may be transported by an undocumented First Nation citizen or by an aboriginal trading partner who is not a First Nation citizen.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 20 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the management of Wildlife habitat on Tsawwassen Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the sale of Wildlife and Wildlife parts, including meat and furs, harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the documentation of Tsawwassen Members who have been designated.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. A Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 22.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DOCUMENTATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. Tsawwassen First Nation will issue documentation to identify individuals who are authorized by Tsawwassen First Nation to harvest Wildlife under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. When harvesting under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife an individual is required to produce, at the request of a person authorized to enforce Federal Law, Provincial Law or Tsawwassen Law in respect of Wildlife, the documentation referred to in clause 24.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Documentation issued under clause 24 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. be in the English language, which version is authoritative and, at the discretion of Tsawwassen First Nation, in the Hun'qum'i'num language; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. include the name and address of the individual.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DESIGNATED WILDLIFE SPECIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. If the Minister determines that, in order to address a conservation risk to a Wildlife species within the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area, there should be a Total Allowable Wildlife Harvest established for that species, the Minister may designate that species as a Designated Wildlife Species.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. Tsawwassen First Nation or British Columbia may recommend to the Minister whether a Wildlife species should be, or continue to be, a Designated Wildlife Species.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. The Minister may determine that a Wildlife species is no longer a Designated Wildlife Species if the Minister determines that the conservation risk to that Wildlife species within the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area no longer exists.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TOTAL ALLOWABLE WILDLIFE HARVEST

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. If the Minister establishes a Designated Wildlife Species, the Minister will determine the maximum number of the Designated Wildlife Species that may be harvested by all harvesters in the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area in each year as the Total Allowable Wildlife Harvest.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. The Minister will request and consider recommendations from Tsawwassen First Nation before determining the Total Allowable Wildlife Harvest for a Designated Wildlife Species.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. In determining the Total Allowable Wildlife Harvest for a Designated Wildlife Species, the Minister will take into account the population of the Designated Wildlife Species within, and outside, the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ALLOCATION OF DESIGNATED WILDLIFE SPECIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. If the Minister establishes a Designated Wildlife Species, British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on the Tsawwassen Allocation of that Designated Wildlife Species.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. In determining a Tsawwassen Allocation, the Minister will take into account the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife, and all relevant information presented by British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation and, in particular, information in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Total Allowable Wildlife Harvest for the Designated Wildlife Species;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. current and past harvest by Tsawwassen Members for Domestic Purposes;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. changes in Tsawwassen First Nation harvesting effort; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. harvest by individuals who are not Tsawwassen Members.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. British Columbia or Tsawwassen First Nation may, at any time, request a review to vary a Tsawwassen Allocation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. The Party requesting a review of a Tsawwassen Allocation has the onus of establishing that the Tsawwassen Allocation should be varied.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. A negotiation to vary a Tsawwassen Allocation will take into account the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife and all relevant information presented by British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation and, in particular, information in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Total Allowable Wildlife Harvest for the Designated Wildlife Species;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. current and past harvest by Tsawwassen Members for Domestic Purposes;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. changes in Tsawwassen First Nation harvesting effort;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. harvest by individuals who are not Tsawwassen Members;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. changes in the status of the Designated Wildlife Species; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. changes in conservation requirements.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 38. If Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia fail to agree on a Tsawwassen Allocation under clause 33 or 37, the Tsawwassen Allocation or a variation to the Tsawwassen Allocation will be finally determined by arbitration under the Dispute Resolution chapter. In making a determination, the arbitrator will take into account the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife and the information referred to in clause 34 or 37, as the case may be.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: WILDLIFE HARVEST PLAN

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 39. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife in respect of a Designated Wildlife Species will be exercised in accordance with an approved Wildlife Harvest Plan.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 40. Tsawwassen First Nation will develop a proposed Wildlife Harvest Plan for the harvest of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a Designated Wildlife Species; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a Wildlife species proposed by Tsawwassen First Nation or British Columbia for inclusion in a Wildlife Harvest Plan in order to adequately manage and conserve the resource.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 41. A proposed Wildlife Harvest Plan will include, as necessary, provisions in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. documentation of harvesters authorized by Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. methods, timing and locations of harvesting by Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the number, sex and age composition of the harvest of Designated Wildlife Species and other Wildlife Species;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. method of identifying harvested Wildlife;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. method of monitoring and reporting harvested Wildlife;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. process for in-season adjustment and amendment to the Wildlife Harvest Plan;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. the term of the Wildlife Harvest Plan;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. management concerns identified by the Minister; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. other matters agreed to by British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 42. Tsawwassen First Nation will submit the proposed Plan to the Minister for approval.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 43. In considering a proposed Wildlife Harvest Plan the Minister will take into account:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. conservation requirements and availability of Wildlife resources including, as applicable, any Tsawwassen Allocation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. public health and public safety;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. any Tsawwassen First Nation preferences set out in the proposed Wildlife Harvest Plan in respect of harvest locations, methods, or times;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. requirements for the integration and efficient harvest of the overall Wildlife resources;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. scientific and local information, and aboriginal traditional knowledge brought forward by Tsawwassen First Nation, with respect to Wildlife populations, numbers, health, distribution and methods for managing Wildlife;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. harvesting by individuals who are not Tsawwassen Members; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. other relevant considerations.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 44. After reviewing the Wildlife Harvest Plan, the Minister may, in a timely way:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. advise Tsawwassen First Nation of any questions regarding the Wildlife Harvest Plan;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. give Tsawwassen First Nation an opportunity to respond to those questions;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. consider the response of Tsawwassen First Nation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. modify, adjust and make additions or deletions to the Wildlife Harvest Plan.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 45. The Minister may approve a method of harvesting that differs from those methods permitted under Federal or Provincial Law if the Minister is satisfied that the method is consistent with public safety.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 46. The Minister will, in a timely way, subject to the factors referred to in clause 43, approve, or vary and approve, the Wildlife Harvest Plan.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 47. A Wildlife Harvest Plan will come into effect when it is approved by the Minister.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 48. The Wildlife Harvest Plan will be reviewed at such times as proposed by either Tsawwassen First Nation or British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 49. An approved Wildlife Harvest Plan prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: REGIONAL WILDLIFE PLANNING

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 50. Tsawwassen First Nation will be invited to participate in any public regional wildlife advisory management process established by British Columbia for an area that includes any portion of the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area. The Minister may request recommendations resulting from the process before determining:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. whether a Wildlife Species will be or continue to be a Designated Wildlife Species; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the Total Allowable Wildlife Harvest for any Designated Wildlife Species.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 51. Tsawwassen First Nation will be invited to participate in any First Nation regional wildlife harvest advisory body established by British Columbia for an area that includes any part of Tsawwassen Territory in the Lower Mainland region.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENFORCEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 52. Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia may negotiate agreements in respect of the enforcement of Provincial Laws, or Tsawwassen Laws in respect of Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 53. Tsawwassen Laws made under this chapter may be enforced by persons authorized to enforce Federal Law, Provincial Law, or Tsawwassen Law in respect of Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 54. Tsawwassen Government will make laws to require:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Tsawwassen Members to comply with a Wildlife Harvest Plan; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. all individuals who harvest Wildlife or transport Wildlife or Wildlife parts under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife to carry documentation issued by Tsawwassen First Nation and to produce that documentation on request by an authorized person.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TRAINING

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 55. Tsawwassen First Nation may establish programs, consistent with provincial programs, to require training for Tsawwassen Members who harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. conservation and safety; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. methods of harvesting and handling Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 56. In the absence of any program established by Tsawwassen First Nation under clause 55, the provincial training program will apply to Tsawwassen Members who harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 57. If a Tsawwassen Member required under Provincial Law to take training has taken that training under a program established by Tsawwassen First Nation under clause 55, the Tsawwassen Member will not be obliged to take that training under a provincial program.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Schedule

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 11 MIGRATORY BIRDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to harvest Migratory Birds for Domestic Purposes in the Tsawwassen Migratory Bird Harvest Area throughout the year in accordance with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds is limited by measures necessary for conservation, public health or public safety.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds is held by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen First Nation may not Dispose of that right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members have the right to Trade and Barter Migratory Birds harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds, among themselves or with other aboriginal people of Canada resident in British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Tsawwassen First Nation may sell inedible by-products, including down, of Migratory Birds harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds, in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law and a Tsawwassen Law made under subclause 20.e.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Tsawwassen First Nation may sell Migratory Birds harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds if the sale of Migratory Birds is permitted under Federal and Provincial Law, and any such sale will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law and a Tsawwassen Law made under subclause 22.c.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. This Agreement does not preclude Tsawwassen First Nation from entering into an agreement with a federal department or agency in respect of access and harvesting by Tsawwassen Members on land owned or in use by that department or agency in accordance with that agreement and Federal and Provincial Laws.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds will be exercised in a manner that does not interfere with authorized uses or Dispositions of provincial Crown land existing as at the Effective Date or authorized in accordance with clause 9.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. British Columbia may authorize uses of or Dispose of provincial Crown land and any authorized use or Disposition may affect the methods, times and locations of the harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds, provided that British Columbia ensures that those authorized uses or Dispositions do not deny to Tsawwassen First Nation the reasonable opportunity to harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. Upon six months notice by either Party, Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on a process to evaluate uses and Dispositions of provincial Crown land that have the potential to deny to Tsawwassen First Nation the reasonable opportunity to harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. Tsawwassen First Nation may exercise the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds on Private Lands, if the owner or occupant of that land agrees to provide access.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Tsawwassen First Nation may exercise the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds on a Reserve, if the Indian Band for whom the Reserve is set aside agrees to provide access.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. Tsawwassen First Nation may exercise the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds on lands contained within a National Wildlife Area if Canada agrees to provide access, and any such harvest will be in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. The transport and export by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members of Migratory Birds or their inedible by-products, including down, harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds are subject to Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. The Minister retains authority for managing and conserving Migratory Birds and Migratory Bird habitat and will exercise that authority in a manner that is consistent with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Neither Canada nor British Columbia will require a Tsawwassen Member to have a licence or to pay a fee or royalty for harvesting Migratory Birds under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. Nothing in this Agreement affects the application of Federal or Provincial Law in respect of the possession, use or regulation of firearms.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. This Agreement does not alter Federal or Provincial Law in respect of property in Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. This Agreement does not preclude Tsawwassen Members from harvesting Migratory Birds in Canada under:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Federal or Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. an agreement, that is in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law, between Tsawwassen First Nation and other aboriginal people; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. an arrangement between other aboriginal people and Canada or British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: POWER TO MAKE LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the designation of Tsawwassen Members to harvest Migratory Birds under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the distribution among Tsawwassen Members of Migratory Birds harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the methods, timing, and location of the harvest of Migratory Birds by Tsawwassen Members under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the Trade and Barter of Migratory Birds harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. the sale of inedible by-products, including down, of Migratory Birds harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 20 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the management of Migratory Birds and Migratory Bird habitat on Tsawwassen Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the establishment and administration of licensing requirements for the harvest of Migratory Birds under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds, including the issuance of documentation to identify individuals designated by Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of that harvest; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the sale of Migratory Birds harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. A Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 22.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DOCUMENTATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. Tsawwassen First Nation will issue documentation to identify individuals who are authorized by Tsawwassen First Nation to harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. When harvesting under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds, an individual is required to produce, at the request of a person authorized to enforce Federal Law, Provincial Law or Tsawwassen Law in respect of Migratory Birds, the documentation referred to in clause 24.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Documentation issued under clause 24 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. be in the English language, which version is authoritative and, at the discretion of Tsawwassen First Nation, in the Hun'qum'i'num language; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. include the name and address of the individual.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENFORCEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. The Parties may negotiate and attempt to reach agreements in respect of the enforcement of Federal Law, Provincial Law, and Tsawwassen Law in respect of Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. Tsawwassen Laws made under this chapter may be enforced by persons authorized to enforce Federal Law, Provincial Law, or Tsawwassen Law in respect of Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CONSERVATION MEASURES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Designated Migratory Bird Population

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. At the request of Tsawwassen First Nation or the Minister, the Parties will share information in respect of conservation for Migratory Bird populations, including activities related to harvesting under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. Where, in the opinion of a Party, there is a conservation risk to a Migratory Bird population, that Party may make recommendations to the Minister for the designation of that population as a Designated Migratory Bird Population.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. After Consulting with Tsawwassen First Nation, the Minister may designate a Migratory Bird population as a Designated Migratory Bird Population if the Minister determines that, in order to address a conservation risk to that population, a Total Allowable Migratory Bird Harvest of that Migratory Bird population is necessary.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. The Minister, in determining the Total Allowable Migratory Bird Harvest for a Designated Migratory Bird Population, will take into account, among other things, the following:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. recommendations from Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the best available knowledge about the Designated Migratory Bird Population, including aboriginal traditional knowledge;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. continental and local conservation requirements; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. Canada's international commitments in respect of Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. In making an allocation for Tsawwassen First Nation from the Total Allowable Migratory Bird Harvest for a Designated Migratory Bird Population, the Minister will take into account the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds and, among other things, the following:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Total Allowable Migratory Bird Harvest for that population;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. current and past food, social or ceremonial needs, and harvesting practices of Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of that population; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. other harvests of that population for food, social or ceremonial purposes.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. On the recommendation of a Party, the Minister may determine that there is no longer a conservation risk to a Designated Migratory Bird Population and remove the designation from that population.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Migratory Bird Agreements

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. The Parties may enter into an agreement on the conservation or management of Migratory Birds, including a range of activities related to achieving Migratory Bird population and habitat conservation objectives, such as inventory, monitoring, assessment, research, harvest allocation, regulation, compliance and enforcement, creation and management of protected areas, stewardship, restoration, enhancement, outreach and education on best practices.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CONSULTATION ON INTERNATIONAL NEGOTIATIONS ON MIGRATORY BIRDS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. Canada will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation on the development of Canada's positions in respect of international discussions or negotiations that may adversely affect the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.
