heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 12 NATIONAL PARKS AND NATIONAL MARINE CONSERVATION AREAS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to harvest Renewable Resources for Domestic Purposes:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. in National Parks that are wholly or partly within Tsawwassen Territory; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. in National Marine Conservation Areas that are wholly or partly within Tsawwassen Territory, if any are established,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: in accordance with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. Harvesting of Intertidal Bivalves under the Tsawwassen Fishing Right in areas where the Tsawwassen Intertidal Bivalve Fishing Area overlaps with a National Park or National Marine Conservation Area will be conducted in accordance with the terms and conditions for harvesting in National Parks and National Marine Conservation Areas in this chapter, as if Intertidal Bivalves were included in the definition of Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources is limited by measures necessary for conservation, public health or public safety.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. The Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources is held by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen First Nation may not Dispose of that right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members have the right to Trade and Barter Renewable Resources harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources, among themselves or with other aboriginal people of Canada resident in British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. For ceremonial purposes, Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members may exchange regalia or traditional or artistic objects, made from Renewable Resources harvested in accordance with this chapter, among themselves or with other Coast Salish people.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. The transport and export by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members of Renewable Resources harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources are subject to Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The Minister retains authority for the management, administration and control of National Parks and National Marine Conservation Areas, and any other protected areas that are owned by Canada and administered by the Parks Canada Agency, and will exercise that authority in a manner that is consistent with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. Neither Canada nor British Columbia will require a Tsawwassen Member to have a licence or to pay a fee or royalty for harvesting Renewable Resources under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. Canada will not charge a fee for a Tsawwassen Member to enter or gain access to a National Park or National Marine Conservation Area to harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources, but may charge for the use of visitor facilities or other services for which fees are normally charged.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. Nothing in this Agreement affects the application of Federal or Provincial Law in respect of the possession, use or regulation of firearms.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. This Agreement does not alter Federal or Provincial Law in respect of property in Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. This Agreement does not preclude Tsawwassen Members from gathering Plants on federal Crown lands other than federal protected areas, subject to Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: POWER TO MAKE LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the designation of Tsawwassen Members to harvest Renewable Resources under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the distribution among Tsawwassen Members of Renewable Resources harvested under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 14 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of the documentation of Tsawwassen Members who have been designated to harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. A Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 16.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DOCUMENTATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Tsawwassen First Nation will issue documentation to identify individuals who are authorized to harvest under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. When harvesting under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources, an individual is required to produce, at the request of a person authorized to enforce Federal Law, Provincial Law or Tsawwassen Law in respect of Renewable Resources, the documentation referred to in clause 18.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Documentation issued under clause 18 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. be in the English language, which version is authoritative, and, at the discretion of Tsawwassen First Nation, in the Hun'qum'i'num language;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. include the name and address of the individual; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. meet any requirements set out in a Renewable Resource Harvesting Document.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: RENEWABLE RESOURCE HARVESTING

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. Each year, or as otherwise agreed, Canada and Tsawwassen First Nation will meet to develop terms and conditions for harvesting under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources and will make reasonable efforts to reach consensus using a collaborative process.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. In developing the terms and conditions referred to in clause 21, Canada and Tsawwassen First Nation will take into account:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the preferences of Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of the quantity, methods, timing and locations for harvesting;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the requirements for conservation and ecological integrity and the availability of the Renewable Resources to which the terms and conditions would apply;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the use of the relevant National Park or National Marine Conservation Area for the benefit and enjoyment of all Canadians;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. other authorized uses of the National Park or National Marine Conservation Area;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. requirements for the management of the National Park or National Marine Conservation Area;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. opportunities for similar harvesting activities outside of National Parks and National Marine Conservation Areas, as provided for in other chapters of this Agreement;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. other harvests of Renewable Resources for food, social or ceremonial purposes; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. any other matter that Canada or Tsawwassen First Nation considers relevant.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. Subject to clause 24, after receiving and considering any terms and conditions developed under clause 21, the Minister will, in a timely way, issue a Renewable Resource Harvest Document to Tsawwassen First Nation that sets out the terms and conditions for harvesting under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. Where Canada and Tsawwassen First Nation do not agree on terms and conditions under clause 21, the Minister may take the action, including issuing a Renewable Resource Harvesting Document, that the Minister considers necessary.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. The Minister may issue or amend a Renewable Resource Harvesting Document:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. at the request of Tsawwassen First Nation; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. in order to respond to exceptional circumstances where it is not practicable to engage in the process referred to in clause 21.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Where the Minister takes action under clause 24 or 25, the Minister will advise Tsawwassen First Nation as soon as practicable of the action taken and the reasons for it.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. Tsawwassen First Nation will exercise the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources in accordance with:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the applicable Tsawwassen Renewable Resource Harvesting Document; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the management plan for the relevant National Park or National Marine Conservation Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. Tsawwassen First Nation will provide to the Minister, on request, information in respect of harvesting by Tsawwassen Members under the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. Canada will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of any proposed new legislation or regulation, or amendment thereto, for harvesting of Renewable Resources in any National Park or National Marine Conservation Area that is wholly or partly within Tsawwassen Territory to the extent that the new legislation or regulation, or amendment thereto, may reasonably be expected to affect the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Renewable Resources.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. After Consultation with Tsawwassen First Nation, the Minister may close to harvesting an area in a National Park or National Marine Conservation Area, for as long as necessary, for purposes of park or marine conservation area management including ecosystem research, protection of representative ecosystems and protection of species or habitats.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CONSERVATION MEASURES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. Canada will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the need for additional conservation measures within the relevant National Park or National Marine Conservation Area in Tsawwassen Territory during the term of a Renewable Resource Harvesting Document; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the development and implementation of such additional conservation measures where the Minister decides that the measures are necessary.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. After the Consultation referred to in clause 31, the Minister may amend a Renewable Resource Harvesting Document to the extent required to bring into effect the conservation measures referred to in clause 31.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PARK ESTABLISHMENT AND BOUNDARY CHANGES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. Canada will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation before establishing or changing the boundaries of any National Park or National Marine Conservation Area that is wholly or partly within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CO-OPERATION IN PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. In respect of a National Park or National Marine Conservation Area that is wholly or partly within Tsawwassen Territory, Canada will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation on:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the role of Tsawwassen First Nation in interim planning and management planning;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the role of Tsawwassen First Nation in the research and protection of Cultural Heritage Sites of significance to Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the role of Tsawwassen First Nation in the identification, protection, interpretation and presentation of Tsawwassen Artifacts and heritage where applicable, including the use of the Hun'qum'i'num language in signage and interpretation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the traditional ecological knowledge of Tsawwassen First Nation being considered in the natural history and management of any National Park or National Marine Conservation Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. At the request of Tsawwassen First Nation, Canada and Tsawwassen First Nation will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on arrangements for Tsawwassen First Nation to provide advice on matters affecting Tsawwassen First Nation in any National Park or National Marine Conservation Area that is wholly or partly within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. An agreement referred to in clause 35 will take the place of any Consultation referred to in clause 34.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. An agreement referred to in clause 35 may provide for the following:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. representation in an advisory process;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. procedures for an advisory process, including a consensual approach and a dispute resolution process;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. procedures for cooperation on appropriate cultural activities and the management of Renewable Resource Harvesting;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. identification of the interests of Tsawwassen Members in economic, employment or training opportunities in or associated with any National Park or National Marine Conservation Area; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. any other matters as agreed by Canada and Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 38. In respect of a National Park or National Marine Conservation Area that is wholly or partly within Tsawwassen Territory, Tsawwassen First Nation will make reasonable efforts to cooperate with others who harvest Renewable Resources for food, social or ceremonial purposes.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 13 PROVINCIAL PARKS AND GATHERING

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to gather Plants for Domestic Purposes in those areas set out in Appendix M-2 in accordance with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. If any additional Provincial Park, Protected Area or Wildlife Management Area is established in Tsawwassen Territory, the Parties will amend Appendices M-1 and M-2 to include the area, in accordance with clause 11 of the Amendment chapter, unless the Parties agree otherwise.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. The Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants is limited by measures necessary for conservation, public health or public safety.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. The Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants is held by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen First Nation may not Dispose of that right.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members have the right to Trade and Barter Plants gathered under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants, among themselves or with other aboriginal people of Canada resident in British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. For ceremonial purposes, Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members may exchange regalia or traditional or artistic objects, made from Plants gathered under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants, among themselves and with other Coast Salish people.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. The Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants will be exercised in a manner that does not interfere with authorized uses or Dispositions existing on the Effective Date or with uses, Dispositions or boundary modifications authorized in accordance with clause 8.

paragraph: 8. British Columbia may authorize uses of, Dispose of, or make boundary modifications to the areas set out in Appendix M-2 and any authorized use, Disposition or boundary modification may affect the methods, times and locations of gathering under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants provided that British Columbia ensures that those authorized uses, Dispositions or boundary modifications do not deny to Tsawwassen First Nation the reasonable opportunity to gather under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. Upon six months notice by either Party, Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on a process to evaluate uses and Dispositions of provincial Crown land that have the potential to deny to Tsawwassen First Nation the reasonable opportunity to gather under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. The transport and export by Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Members of Plants gathered under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants are subject to Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. The Minister retains authority for managing, administering and controlling Provincial Parks, Protected Areas and Wildlife Management Areas and will exercise that authority in a manner that is consistent with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Neither Canada nor British Columbia will require a Tsawwassen Member to have a licence or to pay a fee or royalty for gathering Plants under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. Tsawwassen Members will have access, without a fee being charged, for entrance to and within areas set out in Appendix M-2, except where fees are charged to a Tsawwassen Member for use of visitor facilities and services for which fees are normally charged.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. This Agreement does not alter Federal or Provincial Law in respect of property in Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. This Agreement does not preclude Tsawwassen Members from gathering Plants on provincial Crown lands, subject to Federal and Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: POWER TO MAKE LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the designation of Tsawwassen Members to gather Plants under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the distribution among Tsawwassen Members of Plants gathered under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the Trade and Barter of Plants gathered under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 16 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of the documentation of Tsawwassen Members who have been designated to gather Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. A Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 18.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DOCUMENTATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Tsawwassen First Nation will issue documentation to individuals who are authorized by Tsawwassen First Nation to gather under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. When gathering under the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants, an individual is required to produce, at the request of a person authorized to enforce Federal Law, Provincial Law, or Tsawwassen Law in respect of Plants, the documentation referred to in clause 20.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Documentation issued under clause 20 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. be in the English language, which version is authoritative and, at the discretion of Tsawwassen First Nation, in the Hun'qum'i'num language;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. include the name and address of the individual; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. meet any requirements set out in the approved gathering plan.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GATHERING PLANTS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. The Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants will be exercised in accordance with an approved gathering plan.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. Tsawwassen First Nation will develop a proposed gathering plan, consistent with the applicable management plan, if any, for areas set out in Appendix M-2 and submit it to the Minister for approval.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. The Minister will consult with the Greater Vancouver Regional District before approving a gathering plan that includes provincial Crown land within the Burns Bog Ecological Conservancy Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Any approved gathering plan that includes provincial Crown land within the Burns Bog Ecological Conservancy Area will be consistent with the Burns Bog Management Agreement between Canada, British Columbia, the Greater Vancouver Regional District and the Corporation of Delta, dated March 23, 2004.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. At the request of the Minister or Tsawwassen First Nation, or on or before the expiry of the approved gathering plan, Tsawwassen First Nation, in collaboration with British Columbia, will submit a new or revised proposed gathering plan.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. The Minister may issue or amend an approved gathering plan:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. at the request of Tsawwassen First Nation; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. in order to respond to exceptional circumstances where it is impracticable to engage in discussions with Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. Tsawwassen First Nation will provide to the Minister, on request, information concerning the activities of Tsawwassen Members related to the exercise of the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PLANNING AND CO-OPERATION IN MANAGEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation may enter into an agreement in respect of the development of a cooperative working relationship in the Fraser River estuary, including the South Arm Marshes Wildlife Management Area, and Roberts Bank south to the United States border.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. Where a public management planning process is established for a Provincial Park, Protected Area or Wildlife Management Area that is wholly or partially within Tsawwassen Territory, Tsawwassen First Nation may participate in the planning process on the same basis as other participants.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. The participation of Tsawwassen First Nation in the planning processes referred to in clause 31 may include providing input on Tsawwassen First Nation culture and history, including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. protection of Heritage Resources of significance to Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. interpretation and presentation of Tsawwassen culture in interpretive signage; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. Tsawwassen traditional ecological knowledge.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. British Columbia may proceed with any Provincial Park, Protected Area or Wildlife Management Area public management planning process whether or not Tsawwassen First Nation participates in that process.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. British Columbia will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the establishment of new Provincial Parks, Protected Areas or Wildlife Management Areas;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the Disposition of or modification of boundaries of existing Provincial Parks, Protected Areas or Wildlife Management Areas; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. changes in the use or designation of existing Provincial Parks, Protected Areas or Wildlife Management Areas;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: that may affect the Tsawwassen Right to Gather Plants, the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife or the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Migratory Birds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. British Columbia will Consult with Tsawwassen First Nation on the closure of opportunities for the exercise of the Tsawwassen Right to Harvest Wildlife in Provincial Parks and Protected Areas within the Tsawwassen Wildlife Harvest Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. Nothing in this Agreement obliges British Columbia to establish any new Provincial Park, Protected Area or Wildlife Management Area or to maintain the designation of any Provincial Park, Protected Area, Wildlife Management Area or the Burns Bog Ecological Conservancy Area.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. At the request of either Party, British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation will meet to discuss and exchange written information about maintenance, construction, research and operations opportunities available for competitive bid within any Provincial Park, Protected Area or Wildlife Management Area set out in Appendix M-2.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 14 CULTURE AND HERITAGE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GENERAL

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to practise the culture of Tsawwassen First Nation, and to use the Hun'qum'i'num language, in a manner that is consistent with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: POWER TO MAKE LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the preservation, promotion and development of the culture of Tsawwassen First Nation and the Hun'qum'i'num language on Tsawwassen Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the conservation and protection of and access to Heritage Resources on Tsawwassen Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. archaeological sites on Tsawwassen Lands and archaeological material found after the Effective Date on Tsawwassen Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. Tsawwassen Artifacts owned by Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. Archaeological Human Remains found after the Effective Date on Tsawwassen Lands and any Archaeological Human Remains that come into the possession of Tsawwassen First Nation from Canada or British Columbia after the Effective Date; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. the devolution of Cultural Property of a Tsawwassen Member who dies without a valid will.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 2 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. For the purposes of subclause 2.a, the culture of Tsawwassen First Nation includes its history, feasts, ceremonies, symbols, songs, dances, stories and traditional naming practices. For greater certainty, and in accordance with clause 22 of the General Provisions chapter, Tsawwassen Government does not have the power to make laws in respect of Intellectual Property or the official languages of Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Tsawwassen First Nation has standing in any judicial proceeding in which:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the validity of the will of a Tsawwassen Member; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the devolution of Cultural Property of a Tsawwassen Member,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: is in issue, including any proceeding to vary a will.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Tsawwassen First Nation may commence, and has standing to intervene in, an action under provincial legislation in relation to wills variation in respect of the will of a Tsawwassen Member that provides for the devolution of Cultural Property.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. In a proceeding to which clause 5 or clause 6 applies, the court will consider, among other matters, any evidence or representations in respect of Tsawwassen Law and Tsawwassen First Nation customs dealing with the devolution of Cultural Property.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. The participation of Tsawwassen First Nation in proceedings referred to in clause 5 or clause 6 will be in accordance with the applicable rules of court and will not affect the ability of the court to control its process.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: BEACH GROVE PARCELS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. As of the Effective Date, in respect of the Beach Grove Parcels, unless Tsawwassen First Nation agrees otherwise, British Columbia will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. retain ownership;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. not permit any activity under the Heritage Conservation Act; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. not permit any activity with respect to heritage objects.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia may negotiate and attempt to reach agreement for a delegated management arrangement over the Beach Grove Parcels, but there will be no associated financial obligations.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN ARTIFACTS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. After the Effective Date, if a Tsawwassen Artifact comes into the permanent possession or under the control of the Royal British Columbia Museum, Tsawwassen First Nation and the Royal British Columbia Museum may negotiate a custodial arrangement for the Tsawwassen Artifact.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Tsawwassen First Nation and the Royal British Columbia Museum may negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on arrangements outside this Agreement in respect of cultural artifacts in the possession of either Tsawwassen First Nation or the Royal British Columbia Museum, in accordance with their respective policies and procedures.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. On the Effective Date, British Columbia will pay to Tsawwassen First Nation one million dollars ($1,000,000) to establish a Cultural Purposes Fund.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. Tsawwassen First Nation owns a Tsawwassen Artifact discovered, after the Effective Date, on Tsawwassen Lands in an archaeological context.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. If a Tsawwassen Artifact, discovered off Tsawwassen Lands, comes into the permanent possession or under the control of Canada, Canada may lend or transfer that Tsawwassen Artifact to Tsawwassen First Nation in accordance with an agreement negotiated between Tsawwassen First Nation and Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. At the request of Tsawwassen First Nation, the Royal British Columbia Museum will share, in accordance with Federal and Provincial Law, any information it has about Tsawwassen Artifacts or Tsawwassen Archaeological Human Remains in other public collections in Canada.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. At the request of Tsawwassen First Nation, Canada will use reasonable efforts to facilitate access by Tsawwassen First Nation to Tsawwassen Artifacts or Archaeological Human Remains of Tsawwassen ancestry that are held in Canadian public collections.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: HERITAGE RESOURCES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Before the Effective Date, Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia may negotiate and attempt to reach agreement to provide for the meaningful participation of Tsawwassen First Nation in the identification, conservation, interpretation, management and protection of heritage sites that are:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. of significance to Tsawwassen First Nation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. outside Tsawwassen Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia may negotiate and attempt to reach agreement to provide for cooperative management of Heritage Resources that are:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. of significance to Tsawwassen First Nation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. on provincial Crown land within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Nothing in this Agreement precludes Tsawwassen First Nation from providing to Canada information in respect of the presence on federal Crown land of artifacts, Archaeological Human Remains or Heritage Resources of significance to Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. Where British Columbia establishes a public or First Nation process in respect of Heritage Resources found on provincial Crown land within Tsawwassen Territory, Tsawwassen First Nation may participate in that process on the same basis as any other First Nation or other participant.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Where Canada establishes a public or First Nation process in respect of artifacts or Archaeological Human Remains found on federal Crown land within Tsawwassen Territory, Tsawwassen First Nation may participate in that process on the same basis as any other First Nation or other participant.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. Where Tsawwassen First Nation provides to British Columbia information on an archaeological site within Tsawwassen Territory, in a format that meets the standards of the provincial archaeological site inventory, British Columbia will record that information in the provincial archaeological site inventory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation may exchange information in respect of newly discovered archaeological sites and heritage objects within Tsawwassen Territory as they are identified.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. Where British Columbia determines that a site within Tsawwassen Territory that is listed in the provincial archaeological site inventory is an archaeological site confirmed through archaeological investigation to no longer exist, or is a type of site not protected under Provincial Law, British Columbia will provide to Tsawwassen First Nation information on that site.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ARCHAEOLOGICAL HUMAN REMAINS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. Subject to clause 27, at the request of Tsawwassen First Nation, Canada or British Columbia, as applicable, will transfer to Tsawwassen First Nation, in accordance with Federal or Provincial Law and policy, Archaeological Human Remains or Associated Burial Objects that:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. come into the possession of Canada or British Columbia after the Effective Date; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. that can be demonstrated to be linked to Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. If there are competing aboriginal claims to the Archaeological Human Remains or Associated Burial Objects referred to in clause 26, Tsawwassen First Nation will provide to Canada or British Columbia, as applicable, written confirmation that the claim has been resolved before the transfer proceeds.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. British Columbia will inform Tsawwassen First Nation where British Columbia becomes aware of a site that contains Archaeological Human Remains off Tsawwassen Lands and within Tsawwassen Territory.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PLACE NAMES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. On the Effective Date, British Columbia will add the place names proposed by Tsawwassen First Nation, set out in Appendix O-4, to the British Columbia Geographical Names Database.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. After the Effective Date, Tsawwassen First Nation may propose that British Columbia name, rename or add a place name to a geographic feature in accordance with Federal or Provincial Law and policy.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Schedule

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 15 ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: POWER TO MAKE LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen Government may make laws applicable on Tsawwassen Lands to manage, protect, preserve and conserve the Environment including laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the prevention, mitigation and remediation of pollution and the degradation of the Environment;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. waste management, including solid wastes and wastewater;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. protection of local air quality, but such laws will include standards that meet or exceed the standards set by the Greater Vancouver Regional District in bylaws in respect of the protection of local air quality; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. response to an Environmental Emergency.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. A Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 1.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. Within Tsawwassen Territory, Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to participate in provincial Environmental processes and to receive referrals on Environmental matters from British Columbia on the same basis as Local Governments or other First Nations.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. If a proposed Federal Project may reasonably be expected to adversely affect Tsawwassen Lands or Tsawwassen First Nation rights set out in this Agreement:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Canada will ensure that Tsawwassen First Nation is provided with timely notice of the Environmental Assessment and information describing the Federal Project in sufficient detail to permit Tsawwassen First Nation to determine whether it is interested in participating in the Environmental Assessment;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. if Tsawwassen First Nation confirms that it is interested in participating in the Environmental Assessment of the Federal Project, Canada will provide Tsawwassen First Nation with an opportunity to comment on the Environmental Assessment conducted under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the scope of the Federal Project;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. the environmental effects of the Federal Project;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. any mitigation measures to be implemented; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iv. any follow-up programs to be implemented;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. during the course of the Environmental Assessment conducted under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, Canada will give full and fair consideration to any comments provided by Tsawwassen First Nation under subclause 4.b, and will respond to the comments, before taking any decision to which those comments pertain; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. Canada will provide to Tsawwassen First Nation access to information in Canada's possession related to the Environmental Assessment of the Federal Project, in accordance with the public registry provisions in the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. For greater certainty, clause 4 also applies where the Federal Project referred to in that clause is also a Provincial Project and is subject to a harmonized Environmental Assessment process.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. If a proposed Federal Project that is referred to a panel under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act may reasonably be expected to adversely affect Tsawwassen Lands or Tsawwassen First Nation rights set out in this Agreement, Canada will provide Tsawwassen First Nation with:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the opportunity to propose to the Minister a list of names that the Minister may consider for appointment to the panel, unless the panel is a decision-making body such as the National Energy Board, or Tsawwassen First Nation is a proponent of the Federal Project; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. formal standing before that panel.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. If a proposed Provincial Project is located within the area of land that as at the Effective Date comprises the Greater Vancouver Regional District, or is otherwise located within Tsawwassen Territory, and may reasonably be expected to adversely affect Tsawwassen Lands, residents of Tsawwassen Lands or Tsawwassen First Nation rights set out in this Agreement, British Columbia will ensure that Tsawwassen First Nation:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. receives timely notice of, and relevant available information on, the Provincial Project and the potential adverse environmental effects;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. is Consulted regarding the environmental effects of the Provincial Project; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. receives an opportunity to participate in any Environmental Assessment of that Provincial Project.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. British Columbia will give full and fair consideration to the comments received from Tsawwassen First Nation under subclauses 7.b and 7.c, and will respond to those comments during the Environmental Assessment process, before making a decision that would have the effect of enabling the Provincial Project to be carried out in whole or in part.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. Despite any decision made by Canada or British Columbia in respect of a Federal Project or a Provincial Project, no Federal Project or Provincial Project may proceed on Tsawwassen Lands without the consent of Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. Where a proposed development referred to in subclause 1.h of the Land Management chapter is a Federal Project or a Provincial Project that is subject to the administrative procedures referred to in clause 12 of that chapter, the Parties will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement to harmonize their respective procedures.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ENVIRONMENTAL EMERGENCIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. As the owner of, or decision-maker in respect of, Tsawwassen Lands, Tsawwassen First Nation has responsibility for the prevention of, preparedness for, timely response to and recovery from Environmental Emergencies that originate on Tsawwassen Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Any Party may respond to an Environmental Emergency on Crown land or Tsawwassen Lands or the bodies of water immediately adjacent to Tsawwassen Lands if the Person who has primary responsibility for responding has not responded, or is unable to respond, in a timely way.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. If possible, in advance of taking action, a Party responding as described in clause 12, will notify the Person who has primary responsibility, but in any case, will notify that Person as soon as practicable after responding.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. The Parties may negotiate and attempt to reach agreement in respect of the prevention of, preparedness for, response to, and recovery from Environmental Emergencies occurring on Tsawwassen Lands, which agreement will include a definition of the roles and responsibilities of each Party.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Schedule

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen First Nation Final Agreement

heading: Commencement
paragraph: CHAPTER 16 GOVERNANCE

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN FIRST NATION SELF-GOVERNMENT

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 1. Tsawwassen First Nation has the right to self-government, and the authority to make laws, as set out in this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 2. Tsawwassen Government, as provided for under the Tsawwassen Constitution and this Agreement, is the government of Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 3. The rights, powers, privileges and authorities of Tsawwassen First Nation will be exercised in accordance with Tsawwassen Laws, including the Tsawwassen Constitution, and with this Agreement.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 4. For greater certainty, the authority of Tsawwassen Government to make laws in respect of a subject matter as set out in this Agreement includes the authority to make laws and do other things as may be necessarily incidental to exercising that authority.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 5. Tsawwassen First Nation will act through Tsawwassen Government in exercising its rights, powers, privileges and authorities, and in carrying out its duties, functions and obligations.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 6. Subject to requirements to make laws under this Agreement, Tsawwassen First Nation may exercise the law-making authorities set out in this Agreement over time.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: LEGAL STATUS AND CAPACITY

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 7. Tsawwassen First Nation is a legal entity with the capacity, rights, powers, and privileges of a natural person including the ability to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. enter into contracts and agreements;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. acquire and hold property or an interest in property, and sell or otherwise Dispose of that property or interest;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. raise, spend, invest and borrow money;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. sue and be sued; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. do other things ancillary to the exercise of its rights, powers and privileges.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN CONSTITUTION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 8. Tsawwassen First Nation will have a Constitution, consistent with this Agreement, which will provide:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. for a democratic Tsawwassen Government, including its duties, composition and membership;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. that Tsawwassen Government will be democratically accountable with elections at least every five years;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. that a majority of members of Tsawwassen Government will be elected;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. that Tsawwassen Government may include elements of traditional governance;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. for the role of advisory bodies in Tsawwassen Government;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. that this Agreement sets out the authority of the Tsawwassen Government to make laws;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. for a system of financial administration with standards comparable to those generally accepted for governments in Canada, through which Tsawwassen Government will be financially accountable to Tsawwassen Members;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: h. for conflict of interest rules comparable to those generally accepted for governments of similar size in Canada;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. for recognition and protection of rights and freedoms of Tsawwassen Members;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: j. that every individual who is enrolled under this Agreement is entitled to be a Tsawwassen Member;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: k. for a process for the enactment of laws by Tsawwassen Government;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: l. for a process for challenging the validity of laws enacted by Tsawwassen Government;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: m. that any law enacted by Tsawwassen Government that is inconsistent with the Tsawwassen Constitution is, to the extent of the inconsistency, of no force or effect;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: n. for the establishment of Tsawwassen Public Institutions;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: o. for conditions under which Tsawwassen First Nation may Dispose of land or interests in land;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: p. for a process for the removal from office of members of Tsawwassen Government;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: q. for a process for the amendment of the Tsawwassen Constitution; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: r. for other provisions.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 9. The Tsawwassen Constitution, once ratified in accordance with this Agreement, comes into force on the Effective Date.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: GOVERNANCE TRANSITION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 10. The individuals who were the Chief Councillor and Councillors of the Tsawwassen First Nation band council under the Indian Act on the day immediately before the Effective Date are the chief and legislative members, respectively, of Tsawwassen Government from the Effective Date until the office holders elected in the first election for Tsawwassen Government take office.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN ELECTIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 11. The first election for Tsawwassen Government will be held no later than six months after the Effective Date.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 12. Elections for members of Tsawwassen Government will be held in accordance with the Tsawwassen Constitution and other Tsawwassen Laws.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: APPEAL AND REVIEW OF ADMINISTRATIVE DECISIONS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 13. Tsawwassen First Nation will establish procedures for appeal or review of administrative decisions made by Tsawwassen First Nation or a Tsawwassen Public Institution and, if those procedures provide for a right of appeal to a court for a decision made under a Tsawwassen Law, the Supreme Court of British Columbia has jurisdiction to hear those appeals.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 14. An application may be made to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review of an administrative decision made by Tsawwassen First Nation or a Tsawwassen Public Institution under a Tsawwassen Law, and the Supreme Court of British Columbia has jurisdiction to hear any such application, but no such application may be brought until all procedures for appeal or review provided by Tsawwassen First Nation under clause 13, and applicable to that decision, have been exhausted.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 15. The Judicial Review Procedure Act applies to an application for judicial review under clause 14, and Provincial Settlement Legislation will provide that the Judicial Review Procedure Act is amended to include Tsawwassen Law in the definition of enactment.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: REGISTRY OF LAWS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 16. Tsawwassen Government will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. maintain a public registry of Tsawwassen Laws in the English language which version is authoritative and, at the discretion of Tsawwassen First Nation, in the Hun'qum'i'num language;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provide Canada and British Columbia with copies of Tsawwassen Laws as soon as practicable after they are enacted, unless otherwise agreed by the Parties; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. establish procedures for determining the coming into force and providing for the publication of Tsawwassen Laws.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: PARTICIPATION OF NON-MEMBERS

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 17. Tsawwassen First Nation will provide that Tsawwassen Institutions will Consult with Non-Members in respect of decisions of Tsawwassen Institutions that directly and significantly affect those Non-Members.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 18. Tsawwassen First Nation will provide that Non-Members may participate in the decision-making processes of a Tsawwassen Public Institution if the activities of that Tsawwassen Public Institution directly and significantly affect Non-Members.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 19. The means of participation under clause 18 will include:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. if members of a Tsawwassen Public Institution are elected, an opportunity for Non-Members to vote for and stand for election as a member of the Tsawwassen Public Institution with the ability to participate in discussions and to vote on matters that directly and significantly affect Non-Members;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. if members of a Tsawwassen Public Institution are not elected, at least one member of the Tsawwassen Public Institution will be a Non-Member selected by Non-Members with the ability to participate in discussions and to vote on matters that directly and significantly affect Non-Members; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. other comparable measures.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 20. Despite clause 19, Tsawwassen First Nation may provide that a majority of the members of the Tsawwassen Public Institution must be Tsawwassen Members.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 21. Tsawwassen First Nation will establish the means of participation under clause 18 by law at the same time that it establishes a Tsawwassen Public Institution whose activities may directly and significantly affect Non-Members.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 22. Tsawwassen First Nation will provide Non-Members with access to the appeal and review procedures established under clause 13 in respect of activities that directly and significantly affect Non-Members.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NOTIFICATION OF TSAWWASSEN LAW-MAKING

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 23. Before Tsawwassen Government brings into force any Tsawwassen Law in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. adoption;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Child Protection Services;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. health services;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. social services;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. Child Care services; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. kindergarten to grade 12 education,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen Government will give at least six months written notice of the proposed Tsawwassen Law to Canada and British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 24. Despite clause 23, after giving the notice referred to in clause 23, Tsawwassen Government may bring into force the Tsawwassen Law within the six month period if Canada and British Columbia agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 25. The Parties may negotiate and attempt to reach agreements in respect of any of the matters set out in clause 26 or 27, but an agreement under those clauses is not a condition precedent to the exercise of law-making authority by Tsawwassen Government, and such authority may be exercised immediately following the six month notice period referred to in clause 23.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 26. If Canada or British Columbia makes a request in writing within three months of being given notice under clause 23, Tsawwassen First Nation will Consult with Canada or British Columbia, as the case may be, in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. options the Parties could take to address the interests of Tsawwassen First Nation through methods other than law-making;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. immunity of individuals providing services or exercising authority under Tsawwassen Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. readiness and quality assurance; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. other matters as the Parties may agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 27. At the written request of any Party within three months of notice being provided under clause 23, the relevant Parties will discuss:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. any transfer of cases and related documentation from federal or provincial institutions to Tsawwassen Institutions, including any confidentiality and privacy considerations;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. any transfer of assets from federal or provincial institutions to Tsawwassen Institutions;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. any appropriate amendments to Federal or Provincial Laws; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. other matters as the Parties may agree.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 28. If, in the notice referred to in clause 23, Tsawwassen First Nation advises that it is proposing a Tsawwassen Law for reasons of emergency, Canada and British Columbia will respond as soon as practicable.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: NOTIFICATION OF CHANGES TO PROVINCIAL LEGISLATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 29. Subject to clause 35 or an agreement under clause 32, before British Columbia introduces legislation in the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia, or before the Lieutenant Governor in Council approves a regulation, British Columbia will notify, in writing, Tsawwassen First Nation if:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. this Agreement provides for Tsawwassen Government law-making authority in respect of the subject matter of the legislation or regulation;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the legislation or regulation may affect the protections, immunities, limitations in respect of liability, remedies over, or rights referred to in clauses 163 and 164; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the legislation or regulation may affect the rights, powers, duties, obligations, or the protections, immunities, limitations in respect of liability, remedies over, or rights referred to in clause 113;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: except where this cannot be done for reasons of emergency or confidentiality.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 30. If British Columbia does not notify Tsawwassen First Nation under clause 29 for reasons of emergency or confidentiality, British Columbia will notify, in writing, Tsawwassen First Nation, as soon as practicable, that it has introduced legislation in the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia, or deposited a regulation with the Registrar of Regulations.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 31. Notifications under clauses 29 and 30 will include:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the nature and purpose of the proposed legislation or regulation; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the date that the proposed legislation or regulation is anticipated to take effect, if it has not already done so.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 32. Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia may negotiate and attempt to reach agreements establishing alternatives to the obligations that would otherwise apply under clauses 29, 30, 31 and 33.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 33. Subject to clauses 34 and 35, or an agreement under clause 32, if Tsawwassen First Nation makes a written request to British Columbia, then British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation will discuss the effect, if any, of the legislation or regulation on:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a Tsawwassen Law; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the matters referred to in subclauses 29.b and 29.c.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 34. If British Columbia establishes a process providing for collective discussions with First Nation Governments in British Columbia concerning matters referred to in clause 33, Tsawwassen First Nation will participate in that process and the process will satisfy the obligations of British Columbia under clause 33.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 35. If Tsawwassen First Nation is a member of a representative body and British Columbia has entered into an agreement with the body that provides for consultation in respect of matters referred to in clause 29, 30, 31, and 33, then consultations between British Columbia and that representative body in respect of a particular matter will satisfy the obligations on British Columbia to provide notice under clauses 29 and 30 and discussion under clause 33.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 36. Unless British Columbia agrees otherwise, Tsawwassen First Nation will retain the information provided under clauses 29 through 35 in strict confidence until such time, if ever, the proposed legislation is given first reading in the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia or the regulation is deposited with the Registrar of Regulations, as applicable.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 37. The Parties acknowledge that nothing in clauses 29 through 35 is intended to interfere with the legislative process of British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 38. Despite any other provision of this Agreement, to the extent that provincial legislation or a regulation referred to in clause 29 affects the validity of a Tsawwassen Law, the Tsawwassen Law will be valid for a period of six months or until it is amended, whichever is the shorter period, after the coming into force of the provincial legislation or regulation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: DELEGATION

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 39. Any law-making authority of Tsawwassen Government under this Agreement may be delegated by a Tsawwassen Law to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. a Tsawwassen Public Institution;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. another First Nation Government in British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a public institution established by one or more First Nation Governments in British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. Canada;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: f. a Local Government; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: g. a legal entity as agreed by the Parties,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: if the delegation and the exercise of any law-making authority is in accordance with this Agreement and the Tsawwassen Constitution.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 40. Any authority of Tsawwassen First Nation under this Agreement other than a law-making authority may be delegated by a Tsawwassen Law to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. any body set out in clause 39; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a legal entity in Canada

heading: Commencement
paragraph: if the delegation and the exercise of any delegated authority is in accordance with this Agreement and the Tsawwassen Constitution.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 41. Any delegation under subclauses 39.b through 39.g or clause 40 requires the written consent of the delegate.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 42. Tsawwassen First Nation may receive a delegated authority by agreement, including a law-making authority.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: TSAWWASSEN FIRST NATION LAW-MAKING AUTHORITIES

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen Government

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 43. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of the election, administration, management and operation of Tsawwassen Government including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the establishment of Tsawwassen Public Institutions, including their respective powers, duties, composition and membership, but the registration or incorporation of the Tsawwassen Public Institution must be under Federal or Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the powers, duties, responsibilities, remuneration and indemnification of members, officials, employees and appointees of Tsawwassen Institutions;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. the establishment of a Tsawwassen Corporation, but the registration or incorporation of the Tsawwassen Corporation must be under Federal or Provincial Law;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. the financial administration of Tsawwassen First Nation and Tsawwassen Institutions; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: e. elections, by-elections and referenda.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 44. In accordance with clause 22 of the General Provisions chapter, nothing in clause 43 confers authority on Tsawwassen Government to make laws in respect of labour relations and working conditions.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 45. Tsawwassen Government will make laws to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. provide Tsawwassen Members with reasonable access to information in the custody or control of a Tsawwassen Institution; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provide Persons other than Tsawwassen Members with reasonable access to information in the custody or control of a Tsawwassen Institution regarding matters that directly and significantly affect those Persons.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 46. For greater certainty, a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 45 need not provide access to information of a kind that is generally unavailable under Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 47. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 43 or 45 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law, except that a Federal or Provincial Law in respect of the protection of personal information prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 43 or 45.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen Membership

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 48. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of membership in Tsawwassen First Nation.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 49. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 48 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 50. The conferring of membership in Tsawwassen First Nation does not:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. confer or deny rights of entry into Canada, Canadian citizenship, or the right to be registered as an Indian under the Indian Act; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. except as set out in this Agreement or in Federal or Provincial Law, impose any obligation on Canada or British Columbia to provide rights or benefits.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Tsawwassen Assets

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 51. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of the use, possession, management and Disposition of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. assets located on Tsawwassen Lands;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. assets located off Tsawwassen Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. Other Tsawwassen Lands as an asset,

heading: Commencement
paragraph: of Tsawwassen First Nation, a Tsawwassen Corporation or a Tsawwassen Public Institution.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 52. For greater certainty, the law-making authority in clause 51 does not include the authority to make laws in respect of creditors' rights and remedies.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 53. A Tsawwassen Law made under subclause 51.a prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 54. A Federal or Provincial Law prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Tsawwassen Law made under subclause 51.b or 51.c.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Adoption

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 55. In determining a Child's best interests, all relevant factors will be considered including those factors that must be considered under the Adoption Act.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 56. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. adoption of Tsawwassen Children in British Columbia;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. adoption in British Columbia by Tsawwassen Members of Children who reside on Tsawwassen Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. adoption in British Columbia of Children of Tsawwassen Members in accordance with clause 60.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 57. Tsawwassen Laws under clause 56 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. expressly provide that the best interests of the Child are the paramount consideration in determining whether an adoption will take place; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provide for the consent of individuals whose consent to a Child's adoption is required under Provincial Law, subject to the power of the court to dispense with such consent under Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 58. If Tsawwassen Government makes laws under clause 56, Tsawwassen First Nation will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. develop operational and practice standards that promote the best interests of the Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. participate in British Columbia's information management systems, or establish an information management system that is compatible with British Columbia's information management systems, concerning the management, storage and disposal of adoption records and the safeguarding of personal adoption information; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. provide British Columbia and Canada with a record of all adoptions occurring under Tsawwassen Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 59. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 56 applies to the adoption of a Tsawwassen Child residing off Tsawwassen Lands if:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the Tsawwassen Child has not been placed for adoption under the Adoption Act, and all of the following consent to the application of Tsawwassen Law to the adoption:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the parents of the Tsawwassen Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. if the Tsawwassen Child has reached the age where consent to adoption is required under the Adoption Act, the Tsawwassen Child; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. if the Tsawwassen Child is not under the guardianship of a Director, the guardian of the Tsawwassen Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a Director designated under the Child, Family and Community Service Act is guardian of the Tsawwassen Child, and the Director consents in accordance with subclauses 62.c and 62.d; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a court dispenses with the requirement for the consent referred to in subclause 59.a, in accordance with the criteria that would be used by that court in an application to dispense with the requirement for a parent's or guardian's consent to an adoption under Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 60. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 56 applies to the adoption of a Child of a Tsawwassen Member or a Child residing on Tsawwassen Lands who is not a Tsawwassen Child if:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. before the Child is placed for adoption under Tsawwassen Law, all of the following consent to the application of Tsawwassen Law to the adoption:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: i. the parents of the Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: ii. if the Child has reached the age where consent to adoption is required under the Adoption Act, the Child; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: iii. if the Child is not under the guardianship of a Director, the guardian of the Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. a Director designated under the Child, Family and Community Service Act is guardian of the Child and the Director consents to the application of Tsawwassen Law to the adoption of that Child provided that it is in the best interests of the Child; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. a court dispenses with the requirement for the consent referred to in subclause 60.a, in accordance with the criteria that would be used by that court in an application to dispense with the requirement for a parent's or guardian's consent to an adoption under Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 61. The Parties will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement on the information that will be included in the record provided under subclause 58.c.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 62. If a Director designated under the Child, Family and Community Service Act, or a successor to that position, becomes the guardian of a Tsawwassen Child, the Director will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. provide notice to Tsawwassen First Nation that the Director is the guardian of the Tsawwassen Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provide notice to Tsawwassen First Nation when the Director applies for a continuing custody order for the Tsawwassen Child, provide Tsawwassen First Nation with a copy of the continuing custody order once the order is made and make reasonable efforts to involve Tsawwassen First Nation in planning for the Tsawwassen Child;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. if requested by Tsawwassen First Nation, consent to the application of Tsawwassen Law to the adoption of the Tsawwassen Child provided that it is in the best interests of the Tsawwassen Child; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. in determining the best interests of the Tsawwassen Child under subclause 62.c., the Director will consider the importance of preserving the Tsawwassen Child's cultural identity.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 63. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 56 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 64. Before placing a Tsawwassen Child for adoption, an adoption agency must make reasonable efforts to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. obtain information about the Tsawwassen Child's cultural identity; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. discuss with the designated representative of Tsawwassen First Nation, the placement of the Tsawwassen Child.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 65. Subclause 64.b does not apply if the Tsawwassen Child has reached the age where consent to adoption is required under the Adoption Act and the Tsawwassen Child objects to the discussion taking place, or if the birth parent or other guardian of the Tsawwassen Child who requested that the Tsawwassen Child be placed for adoption objects to the discussion taking place.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 66. Nothing in this Agreement prevents Tsawwassen First Nation from sharing information with any Person in respect of an adoption occurring under Tsawwassen Law, with the written permission of the adoptive parents, birth parents and the adoptee if over the age of majority under Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Child Custody

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 67. Tsawwassen First Nation has standing in any judicial proceedings in British Columbia in which custody of a Tsawwassen Child is in dispute and the court will take judicial notice of Tsawwassen Law and will consider any evidence and representations in respect of Tsawwassen Law and Tsawwassen First Nation customs in addition to any other matters it is required by law to consider.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 68. The participation of Tsawwassen First Nation in proceedings referred to in clause 67 will be in accordance with the applicable rules of court and will not affect the ability of the court to control its process.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Child Protection Services

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 69. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of Child Protection Services on Tsawwassen Lands with respect to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Tsawwassen Children; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Children who are not Tsawwassen Children, subject to an agreement under clause 75 between Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 70. Tsawwassen Laws under clause 69 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. expressly provide that the Tsawwassen Law will be interpreted and administered such that the Safety and Well-Being of Children are the paramount considerations; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. not preclude the reporting under Provincial Law of a Child in Need of Protection.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 71. If Tsawwassen Government makes laws under clause 69, Tsawwassen First Nation will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. develop operational and practice standards intended to ensure the Safety and Well-Being of Children;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. participate in British Columbia's information management systems, or establish an information management system that is compatible with British Columbia's information management systems, concerning Children in Need of Protection and Children in Care;

heading: Commencement
paragraph: c. allow for mutual sharing of information with British Columbia concerning Children in Need of Protection and Children in Care; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: d. establish and maintain a system for the management, storage and disposal of Child Protection Service records and the safeguarding of personal Child Protection Services information.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 72. Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia acknowledge that the information shared under subclause 71.c is personal information, as defined in federal and provincial privacy and access to information legislation, and agree to protect that personal information from subsequent disclosures to the extent possible under law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 73. Despite a Tsawwassen Law made under clause 69, if there is an emergency in which a Child on Tsawwassen Lands is a Child in Need of Protection, British Columbia may act to protect the Child and, in those circumstances, unless British Columbia and Tsawwassen First Nation agree otherwise in writing, British Columbia, as appropriate, will refer the matter to Tsawwassen First Nation after the emergency.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 74. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 69 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 75. At the request of Tsawwassen First Nation, Tsawwassen First Nation and British Columbia will negotiate and attempt to reach agreements in respect of Child Protection Services for:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. Tsawwassen Children who do not reside on Tsawwassen Lands; or

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Children who reside on Tsawwassen Lands who are not Tsawwassen Children.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 76. Where the Director becomes the guardian of a Tsawwassen Child, the Director will make reasonable efforts to include Tsawwassen First Nation in planning for the Tsawwassen Child, including adoption planning.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Education

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 77. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of education in the culture of Tsawwassen First Nation and the Hun'qum'i'num language provided by a Tsawwassen Institution or a person appointed by Tsawwassen First Nation on Tsawwassen Lands including:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. the certification and accreditation of teachers of the culture of Tsawwassen First Nation and the Hun'qum'i'num language; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. the development of the curriculum for teaching the culture of Tsawwassen First Nation and the Hun'qum'i'num language.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 78. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of kindergarten to grade 12 education provided by a Tsawwassen Institution on Tsawwassen Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 79. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 78 will:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. establish curriculum, examination, and other standards that permit students to transfer between school systems at a similar level of achievement and permit students to enter the provincial post-secondary education systems; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. provide for the certification and accreditation of teachers, by a Tsawwassen Public Institution, or by a body recognized by British Columbia, in accordance with standards comparable to standards applicable to individuals who teach in public or provincially-funded independent schools in British Columbia.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 80. Tsawwassen Government may make laws in respect of kindergarten to grade 12 home education of Tsawwassen Members on Tsawwassen Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 81. A Tsawwassen Law made under clause 77, 78 or 80 prevails to the extent of a Conflict with a Federal or Provincial Law.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: 82. If Tsawwassen Government makes a Law under clause 78, at the request of Tsawwassen First Nation or British Columbia, those Parties will negotiate and attempt to reach agreement concerning the provision of kindergarten to grade 12 education to:

heading: Commencement
paragraph: a. individuals, other than Tsawwassen Members, residing on Tsawwassen Lands; and

heading: Commencement
paragraph: b. Tsawwassen Members residing off Tsawwassen Lands.

heading: Commencement
paragraph: Post-Secondary Education and Training

heading: Commencement
