paragraph: (d) the discharge does not contain chemicals or any other substances introduced for the purpose of circumventing the detection of concentrations of oil that exceed the oil content limits specified in subparagraph (c)(iii).

heading: Alarms
paragraph: (2) The alarm required for the purposes of clause (1)(c)(iii)(A) must meet the requirements of section 13 and the alarm required for the purposes of clause (1)(c)(iii)(B) must meet the requirements of regulation 14 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: 31 (1) For the purposes of section 187 of the Act and section 29, an oily mixture may be discharged from a vessel in Section II waters or a Canadian vessel in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction if

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (a) the vessel is en route;

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (b) in the case of an oil tanker, none of the oily mixture

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (i) originates in cargo pump room bilges, or

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (ii) is mixed with oil cargo residues;

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (c) the discharge is processed through oil filtering equipment that

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (i) meets the requirements of regulation 14 of Annex I to MARPOL, and

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (ii) produces an undiluted effluent that has an oil content of not more than 15 ppm; and

heading: Authorized discharge - Section II waters and seaward
paragraph: (d) the discharge does not contain chemicals or any other substances introduced for the purpose of circumventing the detection of concentrations of oil that exceed the oil content limit specified in subparagraph (c)(ii).

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 187 of the Act and section 29, an oily mixture from cargo spaces may be discharged from a vessel in Section II waters or a Canadian vessel in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction if

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (a) the vessel is en route;

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (b) the vessel is more than 50 nautical miles from the nearest land;

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (c) the instantaneous rate of discharge of the oil that is in the oily mixture does not exceed 30 L per nautical mile;

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (d) the total quantity of oil discharged does not exceed

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (i) 1/15,000 of the cargo of which the oily mixture forms part, in the case of a vessel that was put into service on or before December 31, 1979,

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (ii) 1/30,000 of the cargo of which the oily mixture forms part, in the case of a vessel that is put into service after December 31, 1979, or

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (iii) despite subparagraph (i), 1/30,000 of the cargo of which the oily mixture forms part, in the case of a Canadian vessel whose registration is transferred to the Register after February 15, 1993; and

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (e) the oil discharge monitoring and control system is in operation and can stop the discharge of

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (i) any effluent having an oil discharge rate greater than that allowed under paragraph (c), or

heading: Authorized discharge from cargo spaces
paragraph: (ii) any oil in a quantity greater than that allowed under paragraph (d).

heading: Application
paragraph: 32 (1) This Subdivision applies in respect of vessels only when they are in waters under Canadian jurisdiction.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) Sections 33 and 37 and paragraphs 38(1)(b) to (d) and (f) to (j) do not apply in respect of oil tankers of less than 150 gross tonnage or other vessels of less than 400 gross tonnage.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) Sections 33, 34 and 37 and paragraphs 38(1)(b) to (d) and (g) to (i) do not apply in respect of an oil tanker without a master or crew and from which oil is being unloaded if the tanker is not attended by a vessel with a master or crew and the tanker is in a location that makes it infeasible to meet the requirements of those provisions.

heading: Application in waters that are not Canadian waters
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (1),

heading: Application in waters that are not Canadian waters
paragraph: (a) paragraph 38(1)(l) also applies in respect of Canadian vessels in waters other than waters under Canadian jurisdiction; and

heading: Application in waters that are not Canadian waters
paragraph: (b) section 39.1 also applies in respect of Canadian vessels in the territorial sea or the exclusive economic zone of a foreign state that is a party to MARPOL.

heading: Communications
paragraph: 33 If a vessel or a handling facility engages in a transfer operation, the vessel's master and the operator of the facility must, before and during the transfer operation, have the means for two-way voice communication on a continuing basis that enables the supervisor on board the vessel and the supervisor at the facility or on board the other vessel

heading: Communications
paragraph: (a) to communicate immediately as the need arises; and

heading: Communications
paragraph: (b) to direct the immediate shutdown of the transfer operation in case of an emergency.

heading: Lighting
paragraph: 34 (1) If a vessel or a handling facility engages in a transfer operation between sunset and sunrise, the vessel's master and the operator of the facility must ensure that illumination is provided that has

heading: Lighting
paragraph: (a) a lighting intensity of not less than 54 lx at each transfer connection point of the vessel or facility; and

heading: Lighting
paragraph: (b) a lighting intensity of not less than 11 lx at each transfer operation work area around each transfer connection point of the vessel or facility.

heading: Measurement
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), lighting intensity is to be measured on a horizontal plane 1 m above the walking surface of the facility or the working deck of the vessel, as applicable.

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: 35 (1) A person must not use a transfer conduit in a transfer operation unless the conduit

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: (a) has a bursting pressure of not less than four times its maximum design pressure;

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: (b) is clearly marked with its maximum design pressure; and

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: (c) has successfully passed, during the year before its use, a hydrostatic test to a pressure equal to one and one-half times its maximum design pressure.

heading: Test certificates
paragraph: (2) If a transfer conduit used in a transfer operation is part of a vessel's equipment, the vessel's master must keep on board the test certificate for the hydrostatic test.

heading: Manufacturer's specifications
paragraph: (3) The owner of a transfer conduit that is used in a transfer operation must ensure that the conduit is used, maintained, tested and replaced in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications.

heading: Leaks
paragraph: (4) If a transfer conduit or a connection leaks during a transfer operation, the supervisor on board the vessel and the supervisor at the handling facility or on board the other vessel must, as soon as feasible, slow down or stop the operation to remove the pressure from the conduit or connection.

heading: Reception facility - standard discharge connections
paragraph: 36 The owner of a reception facility that receives oily residues from a vessel's machinery space bilges or sludge oil tanks must equip the reception facility with a piping system that, at its vessel side end, is fitted with a standard discharge connection that meets the requirements of regulation 13 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Overall advisory control of transfers between oil tankers
paragraph: 36.1 (1) The authorized representative of an oil tanker of 150 gross tonnage or more must ensure that a transfer operation to which section 27.1 applies is under the overall advisory control of a person who meets the qualifications set out in section 6.2.1.2 of the Manual on Oil Pollution, Section I - Prevention, published by the IMO.

heading: Duties
paragraph: (2) The person must carry out the duties set out in section 6.2.1.3 of the Manual.

heading: Requirements for transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: 37 The authorized representative of a vessel that engages in a transfer operation must ensure that it is supervised on board the vessel by a person who is required to be part of the complement of the vessel

heading: Requirements for transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (a) in the case of a Canadian vessel, by paragraph 207(3)(a), (b) or (c) or subparagraph 207(3)(d)(i) of the Marine Personnel Regulations; and

heading: Requirements for transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (b) in the case of a foreign vessel, by paragraph 241(a), subparagraph 241(b)(ii) or (iii) or paragraph 241(d) of the Marine Personnel Regulations.

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: 38 (1) The supervisor of a transfer operation on board a vessel must ensure that

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (a) the vessel is secured, having regard to the weather and the tidal and current conditions, and the mooring lines are tended so that the movement of the vessel does not damage the transfer conduit or its connections;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (b) transfer procedures are established with the concurrence of the supervisor of the transfer operation at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be, with respect to

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (i) the rates of flow and pressures for the transferred liquid,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (ii) the reduction of rates of flow and pressures, where required to avoid an overflow of the tanks,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iii) the time required to stop the transfer operation under normal conditions,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iv) the time required to shut down the transfer operation under emergency conditions, and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (v) the communication signals for the transfer operation, including

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (A) stand by to start transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (B) start transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (C) slow down transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (D) stand by to stop transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (E) stop transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (F) emergency stop of transfer, and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (G) emergency shutdown of transfer;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (c) the supervisor of the transfer operation at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be, has reported readiness for the commencement of the transfer operation;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (d) the person who is on duty on board the vessel in respect of the transfer operation is fully conversant with the communication signals, maintains watch over the vessel's tanks to ensure that they do not overflow, and maintains continuous communication with that person's counterpart at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (e) the manifold valves and tank valves on the vessel are not closed until the relevant pumps are stopped, if the closing of the valves would cause dangerous over-pressurization of the pumping system;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (f) the rate of flow is reduced when the tanks are being topped off;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (g) the supervisor of the transfer operation at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be, is given sufficient notice of the stopping of the transfer operation to permit them to take the necessary action to reduce the rate of flow or pressure in a safe and efficient manner;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (h) the following measures are taken to prevent the discharge of oil:

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (i) all cargo and bunker manifold connections that are not being used in the transfer operation are securely closed and fitted with blank flanges or other equivalent means of closure,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (ii) all overboard discharge valves are securely closed and marked to indicate that they are not to be opened during the transfer operation, and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iii) all scuppers are plugged;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (i) a supply of peat moss or other absorbent material is readily available near every transfer conduit to facilitate the cleanup of any minor spillage of oil that may occur on the vessel or on the shore;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (j) all transfer conduits that are used in the transfer operation are supported to prevent the conduits and their connections from being subjected to any strain that might cause damage to them or cause the conduits to become disconnected;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (k) all reasonable precautions are taken to avoid the discharge of oil; and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (l) the vessel's STS operations Plan is implemented, if the vessel is of 150 gross tonnage or more and section 27.1 applies to the transfer operation.

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (2) The supervisor of a transfer operation at a handling facility must ensure that

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (a) the supervisor of the transfer operation on board the vessel has reported readiness for the transfer operation to begin;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (b) continuous communication is maintained with the supervisor on board the vessel; and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (c) the manifold valves and the tank valves at the handling facility are not closed until the relevant pumps are stopped, if the closing of the valves would cause dangerous over-pressurization of the pumping system.

heading: Emergency
paragraph: 39 In the event of an emergency during a transfer operation, the master of a vessel and the operator of a handling facility engaged in the operation must take all necessary measures to rectify or minimize the emergency's effects.

heading: Notification of transfers between oil tankers
paragraph: 39.1 (1) The master of an oil tanker of 150 gross tonnage or more must ensure that the tanker does not engage in a transfer operation to which section 27.1 applies unless, at least 48 hours before the transfer operation begins, the master gives notice in accordance with regulation 42.2 of Annex I to MARPOL to

heading: Notification of transfers between oil tankers
paragraph: (a) if the transfer operation is in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, a marine communications and traffic services officer; and

heading: Notification of transfers between oil tankers
paragraph: (b) if the transfer operation is in the territorial sea or the exclusive economic zone of a foreign state that is a party to MARPOL, the appropriate official of the foreign state.

heading: Information not available 48 hours before transfer
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), information that is specified in regulation 42.2 of Annex I to MARPOL and that is not, because of exceptional circumstances, available 48 hours before the transfer operation begins, does not need to be included with the notice. The master of an oil tanker that is planning to unload oil or an oily mixture must ensure that the tanker does not engage in the transfer operation unless the information that was not available is provided at the earliest opportunity to the marine communications and traffic services officer or the appropriate official, as the case may be.

heading: Change in estimated arrival time
paragraph: (3) If the estimated time of arrival of an oil tanker at the location for the transfer operation changes by more than six hours, the master of the tanker must ensure that it does not engage in the transfer operation unless a revised estimated time of arrival is provided at the earliest opportunity to the marine communications and traffic services officer or the appropriate official, as the case may be.

heading: Oil Record Books - Part I
paragraph: 40 (1) Every oil tanker of 150 gross tonnage or more, and every other vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more that carries oil as cargo or as fuel, must keep on board an Oil Record Book, Part I (Machinery Space Operations) in the form set out in appendix III to Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Oil Record Books - Part II
paragraph: (2) Every oil tanker of 150 gross tonnage or more must keep on board an Oil Record Book, Part II (Cargo/Ballast Operations) in the form set out in appendix III to Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Entries - Part I - officer in charge
paragraph: (3) The officer in charge of a machinery space operation set out in regulation 17.2 of Annex I to MARPOL that takes place on a vessel referred to in subsection (1) must

heading: Entries - Part I - officer in charge
paragraph: (a) ensure that the operation is recorded without delay in the Oil Record Book, Part I (Machinery Space Operations); and

heading: Entries - Part I - officer in charge
paragraph: (b) sign the recorded entry.

heading: Entries - Part I - master
paragraph: (4) The master of a vessel referred to in subsection (1) must

heading: Entries - Part I - master
paragraph: (a) ensure that

heading: Entries - Part I - master
paragraph: (i) the circumstances of and reasons for any discharge referred to in paragraph 5(a) or (b), or any other accidental or exceptional discharge to which paragraph 5(c) does not apply, of oil or an oily mixture are recorded without delay in the Oil Record Book, Part I (Machinery Space Operations), and

heading: Entries - Part I - master
paragraph: (ii) any failure of the oil filtering equipment is recorded without delay in the Oil Record Book, Part I (Machinery Space Operations);

heading: Entries - Part I - master
paragraph: (b) ensure that each entry recorded in the Oil Record Book, Part I (Machinery Space Operations) is signed by the officer in charge of the operation; and

heading: Entries - Part I - master
paragraph: (c) sign each page of the Oil Record Book, Part I (Machinery Space Operations) after the page is completed.

heading: Language - Part I
paragraph: (5) An entry in the Oil Record Book, Part I must be written

heading: Language - Part I
paragraph: (a) in English or French, in the case of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft; and

heading: Language - Part I
paragraph: (b) in English, French or Spanish, in the case of a foreign vessel or a foreign pleasure craft.

heading: Entries - Part II - officer in charge
paragraph: (6) The officer in charge of a cargo/ballast operation set out in regulation 36.2 of Annex I to MARPOL that takes place on a vessel referred to in subsection (2) must

heading: Entries - Part II - officer in charge
paragraph: (a) ensure that the operation is recorded without delay in the Oil Record Book, Part II (Cargo/Ballast Operations); and

heading: Entries - Part II - officer in charge
paragraph: (b) sign the recorded entry.

heading: Entries - Part II - master
paragraph: (7) The master of a vessel referred to in subsection (2) must

heading: Entries - Part II - master
paragraph: (a) ensure that

heading: Entries - Part II - master
paragraph: (i) the circumstances of and reasons for any discharge referred to in paragraph 5(a) or (b), or any other accidental or exceptional discharge, of oil or an oily mixture are recorded without delay in the Oil Record Book, Part II (Cargo/Ballast Operations), and

heading: Entries - Part II - master
paragraph: (ii) any failure of the oil discharge monitoring and control system is recorded without delay in the Oil Record Book, Part II (Cargo/Ballast Operations);

heading: Entries - Part II - master
paragraph: (b) ensure that each entry recorded in the Oil Record Book, Part II (Cargo/Ballast Operations) is signed by the officer in charge of the operation; and

heading: Entries - Part II - master
paragraph: (c) sign each page of the Oil Record Book, Part II (Cargo/Ballast Operations) after the page is completed.

heading: Language - Part II
paragraph: (8) An entry in the Oil Record Book, Part II must be written

heading: Language - Part II
paragraph: (a) in English or French, in the case of a Canadian vessel; and

heading: Language - Part II
paragraph: (b) in English, French or Spanish, in the case of a foreign vessel.

heading: Three years
paragraph: (9) A vessel referred to in subsection (1) or (2) must keep the Oil Record Book, Part I and, if applicable, the Oil Record Book, Part II on board for three years after the day on which the last entry was made.

heading: Official log book
paragraph: (10) The Oil Record Book, Part I and, if applicable, the Oil Record Book, Part II may be part of the vessel's official log book.

heading: Reception facility receipts
paragraph: 41 (1) The master of a vessel must obtain from the owner or operator of a reception facility that receives oily residues from the vessel a receipt or certificate that sets out the type and amount of oily residues received and the date and time that they were received.

heading: One year
paragraph: (2) The master must keep the receipt or certificate on board for one year after the day on which it was issued.

heading: Recording device for bilge alarms
paragraph: 42 If an alarm on a vessel is required under paragraph 12(1)(e) or (f) or subsection 30(2) to be fitted with a recording device to meet the specifications of Part 2 of the Annex to Resolution MEPC.107(49), the vessel must keep on board the data that those specifications require to be recorded (the date, the time, the alarm status of the alarm and the operating status of the oil filtering equipment) for 18 months after the data is recorded.

heading: STS operations Plan - Records
paragraph: 42.1 (1) The master of an oil tanker of 150 gross tonnage or more that is required by section 27.1 to keep on board an STS operations Plan must ensure that the records required by the Plan are made.

heading: Three years
paragraph: (2) The oil tanker must keep each record on board for three years after it is made.

heading: Application
paragraph: 43 (1) This section applies in respect of an oil tanker

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) for which the building contract is placed after July 5, 1993;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) that is constructed after January 5, 1994, in the absence of a building contract;

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) that is first delivered after July 5, 1996; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (d) that undergoes a major conversion

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) for which the building contract is placed after July 5, 1993,

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) for which the construction work begins after January 5, 1994, in the absence of a building contract, or

heading: Application
paragraph: (iii) that is completed after July 5, 1996.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of an oil tanker must ensure that it

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) meets the design and construction requirements of regulations 19.3 and 19.4 of Annex I to MARPOL, or of regulation 19.6 of that Annex if applicable, unless the tanker is designed and constructed in accordance with the requirements of regulation 19.5 of that Annex; and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) is designed and constructed to facilitate the inspection and maintenance of wing and double bottom tanks or spaces.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 44 (1) In this section, Category 2 oil tanker and Category 3 oil tanker have the same meaning as in regulations 20.3.2 and 20.3.3, respectively, of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) This section applies in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a foreign vessel that is an oil tanker referred to in regulation 20.1.1 of Annex I to MARPOL; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) a Canadian vessel that is a Category 2 oil tanker or Category 3 oil tanker and that holds an International Oil Pollution Prevention Certificate.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply in respect of

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) an oil tanker in respect of which section 43 applies;

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) an oil tanker to which regulation 20.1.3 of Annex I to MARPOL applies and that, if applicable, meets the alternative requirements set out in that regulation;

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (c) an oil tanker that is entitled to fly the flag of the United States; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (d) an oil tanker that is engaged in the coasting trade as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Coasting Trade Act.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsections (5) to (7), the authorized representative of an oil tanker must ensure that it meets the requirements of subsection 43(2).

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (5) A Category 2 oil tanker, or a Category 3 oil tanker, that is a Canadian vessel fitted with double hull spaces that are not used for the carriage of oil and extend over the entire cargo tank length but do not fulfil the conditions specified in regulation 20.1.3 of Annex I to MARPOL, or fitted with only double bottoms or double sides that are not used for the carriage of oil and extend over the entire cargo tank length, may continue to operate if

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (a) it was in service on July 1, 2001;

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (b) its specifications set out in this subsection remain unchanged; and

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (c) its continued operation does not go beyond the day in the year 2015 that is the anniversary of the date of its delivery or the day on which it reaches 25 years of age, whichever is the earlier day.

heading: Continued operation dependent on Condition Assessment Scheme
paragraph: (6) A Category 2 oil tanker, or Category 3 oil tanker, that is a Canadian vessel may continue to operate if

heading: Continued operation dependent on Condition Assessment Scheme
paragraph: (a) the Board determines that the results of the Condition Assessment Scheme referred to in regulation 20.6 of Annex I to MARPOL indicate that the tanker is fit to continue to operate; and

heading: Continued operation dependent on Condition Assessment Scheme
paragraph: (b) the tanker's continued operation does not go beyond the day in the year 2015 that is the anniversary of the date of its delivery or the day on which it reaches 25 years of age, whichever is the earlier day.

heading: Foreign vessels operating under regulation 20.5 or 20.7
paragraph: (7) Subject to subsection (8), a Category 2 oil tanker, or a Category 3 oil tanker, that is a foreign vessel may operate if the government of the state whose flag the tanker is entitled to fly has allowed it to continue to operate under regulation 20.5 or 20.7 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Prohibited to enter ports or offshore terminals
paragraph: (8) A Category 2 oil tanker, or a Category 3 oil tanker, that is a foreign vessel and is continuing to operate under regulation 20.5 of Annex I to MARPOL after the anniversary in the year 2015 of the date of its delivery must not enter a port or an offshore terminal in waters under Canadian jurisdiction.

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: (9) For the purposes of this section,

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: (a) the date of delivery of a tanker is the day on which it is first delivered; and

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: (b) the age of a tanker is determined from the day on which it is first delivered.

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: Definition of heavy grade oil

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: 45 (1) In this section, heavy grade oil has the same meaning as in regulation 21.2 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) This section applies in respect of an oil tanker of 600 tonnes deadweight or more that is carrying heavy grade oil as cargo.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply in respect of

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) an oil tanker that is a Canadian vessel and engages only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) an oil tanker to which regulation 21.1.2 of Annex I to MARPOL applies and that, if applicable, meets the alternative requirements set out in that regulation.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsections (5) to (8), the authorized representative of an oil tanker must ensure that

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) if it is of 5 000 tonnes deadweight or more, it meets the requirements of subsection 43(2); and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) if it is of 600 tonnes deadweight or more but less than 5 000 tonnes deadweight, it meets the requirements of subsection 43(2) or is fitted with

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) double bottom tanks or spaces that meet the requirements of regulation 19.6.1 of Annex I to MARPOL, and

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) wing tanks or spaces arranged in accordance with regulation 19.3.1 of Annex I to MARPOL that meet the requirement for distance, w, referred to in regulation 19.6.2 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (5) An oil tanker that is a Canadian vessel of 5 000 tonnes deadweight or more fitted with double hull spaces that are not used for the carriage of oil and extend over the entire cargo tank length but do not fulfil the conditions specified in regulation 21.1.2 of Annex I to MARPOL, or fitted with only double bottoms or double sides that are not used for the carriage of oil and extend over the entire cargo tank length, may continue to operate if

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (a) it was in service on December 4, 2003;

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (b) its specifications set out in this subsection remain unchanged; and

heading: Continued operation dependent on fittings
paragraph: (c) its continued operation does not go beyond the day in the year 2015 that is the anniversary of the date of its delivery or the day on which it reaches 25 years of age, whichever is the earlier day.

heading: Continued operation dependent on Condition Assessment Scheme
paragraph: (6) An oil tanker that is a Canadian vessel of 5 000 tonnes deadweight or more that is carrying crude oil having a density at 15°C that is higher than 900 kg/m3 but lower than 945 kg/m3 may continue to operate if

heading: Continued operation dependent on Condition Assessment Scheme
paragraph: (a) the Board determines, taking into consideration the tanker's size, age, operational area and structural conditions, that the results of the Condition Assessment Scheme referred to in regulation 20.6 of Annex I to MARPOL indicate that it is fit to continue to operate; and

heading: Continued operation dependent on Condition Assessment Scheme
paragraph: (b) its continued operation does not go beyond the day in the year 2015 that is the anniversary of the date of its delivery or the day on which it reaches 25 years of age, whichever is the earlier day.

heading: Continued operation - heavy grade oil
paragraph: (7) An oil tanker that is a Canadian vessel of 600 tonnes deadweight or more but less than 5 000 tonnes deadweight and that does not meet the requirements of paragraph (4)(b) may continue to operate if

heading: Continued operation - heavy grade oil
paragraph: (a) the Board determines, taking into consideration the tanker's size, age, operational area and structural conditions, that it is fit to continue to operate; and

heading: Continued operation - heavy grade oil
paragraph: (b) its continued operation does not go beyond the day on which it reaches 25 years of age.

heading: Foreign vessels
paragraph: (8) An oil tanker that is a foreign vessel may operate if the government of the state whose flag the tanker is entitled to fly has allowed the tanker to continue to operate under regulation 21.5, 21.6.1 or 21.6.2 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: (9) For the purposes of this section,

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: (a) the date of delivery of a tanker is the day on which it is first delivered; and

heading: Delivery and age
paragraph: (b) the age of a tanker is determined from the day on which it is first delivered.

heading: Application
paragraph: 46 (1) This section applies in respect of any oil tanker in respect of which sections 43 to 45 do not apply.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) This section does not apply in respect of

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) an oil tanker to which regulation 20.1.3 of Annex I to MARPOL applies and that, if applicable, meets the alternative requirements set out in that regulation; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) an oil tanker that does not have mechanical means of propulsion and

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (i) is of less than 2 000 gross tonnage,

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (ii) has no cargo tanks that exceed 200 m3 capacity, and

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (iii) engages only on voyages on

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (A) the Mackenzie River,

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (B) the waters contiguous to the Mackenzie River that are not within shipping safety control zone 12, or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (C) the rivers, streams or lakes that feed into the Mackenzie River.

heading: Oil tankers of less than 5 000 gross tonnage
paragraph: (3) The authorized representative of an oil tanker of less than 5 000 gross tonnage must ensure that it has a double hull or a double containment system determined by the Minister to be as effective as a double hull for the prevention of a discharge of oil. However, this requirement does not apply before January 1, 2015.

heading: Oil tankers of 5 000 gross tonnage or more
paragraph: (4) The authorized representative of an oil tanker of 5 000 gross tonnage or more must ensure that it meets the requirements of subsection 43(2).

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (5) Subsection (4) does not apply before January 1, 2015 in respect of an oil tanker that has either double sides or double bottoms that are contiguous with cargo spaces and meet the applicable design and construction requirements of regulation 19.3 or 19.4, as the case may be, of Annex I to MARPOL, and

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) is of less than 30 000 gross tonnage and less than 30 years of age; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) is of 30 000 gross tonnage or more and less than 28 years of age.

heading: Age
paragraph: (6) For the purposes of subsection (5), the age of an oil tanker is determined from the later of

heading: Age
paragraph: (a) the day on which it is first delivered, and

heading: Age
paragraph: (b) the day on which a major conversion is completed, if the conversion is completed before July 6, 1996.

heading: Height of double bottom
paragraph: 47 Despite paragraph 43(2)(a), subsection 45(3), paragraph 45(4)(b) and subsection 46(4), in the case of an oil tanker that is a Canadian vessel of less than 5 000 tonnes deadweight that does not have mechanical means of propulsion and engages only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction within 40 nautical miles from the nearest land, the height of its double bottom must in no location be less than the width calculated for its wing tanks in accordance with the formula in regulation 19.6.2 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Board
paragraph: 48 (1) The Board may, in respect of Canadian vessels and Canadian pleasure craft, exercise the powers of the Administration conferred by regulations 3 and 5 of Annex I to MARPOL.

heading: Foreign governments
paragraph: (2) In the case of a foreign vessel or a foreign pleasure craft, the requirements of this Division are subject to the exercise of the powers conferred by regulations 3 and 5 of Annex I to MARPOL by the government of the state whose flag the vessel is entitled to fly.

heading: Limited application - foreign vessels
paragraph: 49 This Division applies in respect of foreign vessels in waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada only in respect of pollution.

heading: Liquid substances
paragraph: 50 (1) The authorized representative and the master of a vessel must ensure that the vessel does not carry a liquid substance in bulk unless the substance

heading: Liquid substances
paragraph: (a) is listed in chapter 17 or 18 of the IBC Code; or

heading: Liquid substances
paragraph: (b) is provisionally assessed under regulation 6.3 of Annex II to MARPOL.

heading: Non-application to oil
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of oil.

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: 51 On application, the Minister must approve plans and specifications with respect to a Canadian vessel or a vessel that is recorded under the Act if the matters described in the plans and specifications meet the applicable requirements of this Subdivision.

heading: NLS tankers - Annex II to MARPOL
paragraph: 52 (1) The authorized representative of an NLS tanker must ensure that

heading: NLS tankers - Annex II to MARPOL
paragraph: (a) the requirements of regulation 12 of Annex II to MARPOL relating to the pumping, piping and unloading arrangements, the location and size of underwater discharge outlets, and the slop tanks or other arrangements are met; and

heading: NLS tankers - Annex II to MARPOL
paragraph: (b) if the tanker uses ventilation procedures referred to in regulation 13.3 of Annex II to MARPOL to remove cargo residues from a tank, the tanker has ventilation equipment that can produce an air jet that reaches the tank bottom.

heading: IBC Code
paragraph: (2) Any of the following vessels that were constructed on or after July 1, 1986, or that are Canadian vessels that were constructed before that date and first registered or listed in Canada after February 15, 1993, must meet the applicable design, construction, equipment and systems requirements of the IBC Code:

heading: IBC Code
paragraph: (a) vessels that carry a noxious liquid substance in bulk that is listed in chapter 17 of the IBC Code or is provisionally assessed under regulation 6.3 of Annex II to MARPOL as falling into Category X, Y or Z in the Pollution Category column of that chapter; and

heading: IBC Code
paragraph: (b) chemical tankers that have means of self-propulsion.

heading: BCH Code
paragraph: (3) Any of the following vessels that were constructed before July 1, 1986, other than Canadian vessels that were first registered or listed in Canada after February 15, 1993, must meet the applicable design, construction, equipment and systems requirements of the BCH Code:

heading: BCH Code
paragraph: (a) vessels that carry a noxious liquid substance in bulk that is listed in chapter 17 of the IBC Code or is provisionally assessed under regulation 6.3 of Annex II to MARPOL as falling into Category X, Y or Z in the Pollution Category column of that chapter; and

heading: BCH Code
paragraph: (b) chemical tankers that have means of self-propulsion.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of subsections (2) and (3), a vessel converted to a chemical tanker, irrespective of the date of its construction, is considered to be a chemical tanker constructed on the date on which the conversion commenced unless the vessel

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) was constructed before July 1, 1986; and

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) was, when the conversion commenced, certified under the BCH Code to carry only those products identified by the Code as substances with pollution hazards only.

heading: Offshore support vessels
paragraph: (5) Offshore support vessels may meet the applicable design, construction, equipment and systems requirements of Resolution A.673(16) instead of the requirements referred to in subsection (2) or (3).

heading: Containers or enclosed deck areas - NLS tankers
paragraph: 53 (1) The authorized representative of an NLS tanker must ensure that each noxious liquid substance cargo manifold and each cargo transfer connection point on the tanker is fitted with a container or has an enclosed deck area that

heading: Containers or enclosed deck areas - NLS tankers
paragraph: (a) can retain noxious liquid substances that might leak or spill during transfer operations;

heading: Containers or enclosed deck areas - NLS tankers
paragraph: (b) has a means for the removal of the noxious liquid substances retained in it; and

heading: Containers or enclosed deck areas - NLS tankers
paragraph: (c) does not adversely affect the stability of the tanker or the safety of its crew.

heading: Volume
paragraph: (2) If the largest conduit serving a noxious liquid substance cargo manifold or a cargo transfer connection point on an NLS tanker has an inside diameter set out in column 1 of the table to subsection 15(2), the tanker's authorized representative must ensure that the container or enclosed deck area, under even-keel conditions, has the volume set out in column 2.

heading: Issuance
paragraph: 54 (1) On application by the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel and subject to paragraphs 16(4)(b) to (d) of the Act, the Minister must issue

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (a) a Canadian Noxious Liquid Substance Certificate to the vessel if the applicable requirements of this Division are met;

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (b) an International Pollution Prevention Certificate for the Carriage of Noxious Liquid Substances in Bulk to the vessel if the applicable requirements of Annex II to MARPOL are met;

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (c) an International Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk to the vessel if the applicable requirements of the IBC Code are met;

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (d) a Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk to the vessel if the applicable requirements of the BCH Code are met; or

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (e) a Certificate of Fitness for an Offshore Support Vessel to the vessel if the applicable requirements of Resolution A.673(16) are met.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (2) The Minister must, on the basis of the applicable requirements that are met, specify on the certificates issued under subsection (1) the particular substances or products that the vessel is certified to carry.

heading: Endorsement of Canadian NLS certificates
paragraph: 55 (1) The authorized representative of a vessel that holds a Canadian Noxious Liquid Substance Certificate must ensure that the certificate is endorsed by the Minister, within three months before or after each anniversary date of the issuance of the certificate, to indicate that the requirements for the issuance of the certificate are met.

heading: Endorsement of international NLS certificates
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a vessel that holds an International Pollution Prevention Certificate for the Carriage of Noxious Liquid Substances in Bulk must ensure that the certificate is endorsed as required by regulations 8.1.3, 8.1.4 and 9.2 of Annex II to MARPOL.

heading: Endorsement of IBC Code certificates of fitness
paragraph: (3) The authorized representative of a vessel that holds an International Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk must ensure that the certificate is endorsed as required by chapter 1 of the IBC Code.

heading: Endorsement of BCH Code certificates of fitness
paragraph: (4) The authorized representative of a vessel that holds a Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk must ensure that the certificate is endorsed as required by chapter 1 of the BCH Code.

heading: Endorsement of certificates of fitness for offshore support vessels
paragraph: (5) The authorized representative of a vessel that holds a Certificate of Fitness for an Offshore Support Vessel must ensure that the certificate is endorsed as required by section 1.5.4 of Resolution A.673(16).

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (6) If the construction, arrangement, equipment, fittings, installations or systems of a vessel that holds a certificate issued under section 54 are changed as a result of an accident, the discovery of a defect, a repair or a major conversion that affects the requirements that were met when the certificate was issued, the authorized representative of the vessel must ensure that the Minister inspects the vessel as soon as feasible to ensure that the requirements continue to be met.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (7) Subsection (6) does not apply in respect of minor repairs or the direct replacement of equipment or fittings that meet the requirements of the certificate.

heading: Certificates
paragraph: 56 (1) Every NLS tanker and every chemical tanker must hold and keep on board

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (a) a Canadian Noxious Liquid Substance Certificate, if the tanker is a Canadian vessel that engages only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction and carries noxious liquid substances in bulk but not dangerous chemicals in bulk;

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (b) an International Pollution Prevention Certificate for the Carriage of Noxious Liquid Substances in Bulk that is in the form set out in appendix 3 to Annex II to MARPOL, if the tanker

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (i) is a Canadian vessel that does not engage only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction and carries noxious liquid substances in bulk but not dangerous chemicals in bulk, or

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (ii) is entitled to fly the flag of a foreign state that is a party to MARPOL and carries noxious liquid substances in bulk but not dangerous chemicals in bulk;

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (c) a certificate of compliance certifying that the tanker meets the applicable requirements of Annex II to MARPOL, if the tanker is entitled to fly the flag of a state that is not a party to MARPOL and carries noxious liquid substances in bulk but not dangerous chemicals in bulk;

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (d) an International Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk or a Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk that is in the form set out in the IBC Code or the BCH Code, as the case may be, if the tanker

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (i) is a Canadian vessel that carries dangerous chemicals in bulk, or

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (ii) is entitled to fly the flag of a foreign state that is a party to MARPOL and carries dangerous chemicals in bulk; or

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (e) a certificate of compliance certifying that the tanker meets the applicable requirements of the IBC Code or the BCH Code, as the case may be, if the tanker is entitled to fly the flag of a state that is not a party to MARPOL and carries dangerous chemicals in bulk.

heading: Offshore support vessels
paragraph: (2) An offshore support vessel may hold and keep on board a Certificate of Fitness for an Offshore Support Vessel instead of a Certificate required by subsection (1).

heading: Procedures and arrangements manual
paragraph: (3) Every NLS tanker must keep on board a procedures and arrangements manual that meets the requirements of regulation 14 of Annex II to MARPOL. In the case of a Canadian vessel, the expression "the requirements of this Annex" in regulation 14.2 of that Annex includes the requirements of section 67.

heading: IBC or BCH Codes
paragraph: (4) Every chemical tanker must keep on board the IBC Code or the BCH Code, as the case may be.

heading: Emergency plan
paragraph: 57 (1) Subject to subsection (2), an NLS tanker of 150 gross tonnage or more must keep on board a shipboard marine pollution emergency plan for noxious liquid substances that meets the requirements of regulation 17.2 of Annex II to MARPOL.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) If subsection 27(1) applies, the shipboard marine pollution emergency plan for noxious liquid substances may be combined with the shipboard oil pollution emergency plan, in which case the title of the plan must be the "shipboard marine pollution emergency plan".

heading: Display
paragraph: 58 The master of an NLS tanker or chemical tanker must ensure that

heading: Display
paragraph: (a) permanent notices are displayed in conspicuous places on board, indicating the areas in which smoking and naked lights are prohibited;

heading: Display
paragraph: (b) while the tanker is in a port, the following notices are displayed near every access to the tanker, as appropriate:

heading: Display
paragraph: (i) "NO NAKED LIGHTS / PAS DE FLAMMES NUES",

heading: Display
paragraph: (ii) "NO SMOKING / DEFENSE DE FUMER", and

heading: Display
paragraph: (iii) "NO UNAUTHORIZED PERSONS / ACCES INTERDIT AUX PERSONNES NON AUTORISEES"; and

heading: Display
paragraph: (c) while the tanker is in a port and the cargo being handled presents a health hazard, the notice "WARNING HAZARDOUS CHEMICALS / ATTENTION PRODUITS CHIMIQUES DANGEREUX" is displayed near every access to the tanker.

heading: Operational requirements - NLS tankers
paragraph: 59 The master of an NLS tanker must ensure that the operational procedures with respect to cargo handling, tank cleaning, slops handling and cargo tank ballasting and deballasting are carried out in accordance with the tanker's procedures and arrangements manual and with this Subdivision.

heading: Operational requirements - IBC Code
paragraph: 60 (1) The master of a chemical tanker that was constructed on or after July 1, 1986, or that is a Canadian vessel that was constructed before that date and first registered or listed in Canada after February 15, 1993, must ensure that the operational requirements of the IBC Code are met.

heading: Section 16.2.2 of the IBC Code
paragraph: (2) The master of a chemical tanker referred to in subsection (1) must refuse any cargo mentioned in section 16.2.2 of the IBC Code if the analysis of the cargo has not been certified by its manufacturer or a marine chemist.

heading: Operational requirements - BCH Code
paragraph: (3) The master of a chemical tanker that is not referred to in subsection (1) must ensure that the operational requirements of chapter V of the BCH Code are met.

heading: Offshore support vessels
paragraph: (4) The master of an offshore support vessel that holds a Certificate of Fitness for an Offshore Support Vessel may ensure that the operational requirements of chapter 6 of Resolution A.673(16) are met instead of the requirements referred to in subsection (1) or (3).

heading: Tank prewash operations
paragraph: 61 The tank prewash operations referred to in sections 63 and 64 must be carried out

heading: Tank prewash operations
paragraph: (a) in accordance with the requirements of appendix 6 to Annex II to MARPOL; and

heading: Tank prewash operations
paragraph: (b) in such a way that the effluent resulting from the washing

heading: Tank prewash operations
paragraph: (i) is transferred to a reception facility that can receive the effluent in an environmentally safe manner, and

heading: Tank prewash operations
paragraph: (ii) is not discharged.

heading: Stripping operations
paragraph: 62 (1) If cargo stripping operations that involve a Category Y noxious liquid substance are carried out at a handling facility, the operator of the facility must ensure that it can receive the cargo at an average flow rate of 6 m3 per hour without creating back pressure of more than 100 kPa at the vessel's manifold.

heading: Vessel's manifold
paragraph: (2) The vessel's manifold must not be more than 3 m above the waterline at low mean tide.

heading: Cargo hoses and piping systems
paragraph: (3) A cargo hose or piping system that contains a noxious liquid substance must not be drained back into the vessel after the completion of a cargo stripping operation.

heading: Procedures - Category X
paragraph: 63 (1) A tank from which a Category X noxious liquid substance has been unloaded must undergo a tank prewash operation before the vessel leaves the port of unloading unless the vessel has been granted an exemption from a tank prewash operation.

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (2) On request by the master of a vessel, a marine safety inspector may grant an exemption from a tank prewash operation if the inspector is satisfied that

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (a) the unloaded tank will be reloaded with the same substance or another substance compatible with the previous one and will not be washed or ballasted prior to loading;

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (b) the unloaded tank will not be washed or ballasted at sea and the vessel's master has given written notice to the Department of Transport Marine Safety Office nearest to the vessel that the tank will undergo a tank prewash operation at another port and that this other port has confirmed in writing that it has a reception facility that is available and adequate for such a purpose; or

heading: Exemption
paragraph: (c) the cargo residues will be removed from the tank by a ventilation procedure.

heading: Transfer of effluent
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), the tank prewash operation must be carried out by washing the tank and transferring the effluent to a reception facility that can receive the effluent in an environmentally safe manner until the concentration of the substance in the effluent has fallen to 0.1% by weight, and then by continuing to transfer the remaining effluent to the facility until the tank is empty.

heading: If not feasible
paragraph: (4) If it is not feasible to measure the concentration of the substance to ensure that it falls within the limit specified in subsection (3) without causing undue delay to the vessel, the tank prewash operation must be carried out by washing the tank and transferring the effluent to a reception facility in accordance with subparagraph 61(b)(i).

heading: Marine safety inspector
paragraph: (5) The tank prewash operation must be carried out in the presence of a marine safety inspector who endorses the appropriate entries in the vessel's Cargo Record Book required by subsection 79(1).

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 64 (1) The following definitions apply in this section.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: high-viscosity substance means a noxious liquid substance in Category X or Y with a viscosity equal to or greater than 50 mPa·s at the unloading temperature. (substance a viscosite elevee)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: solidifying substance means a noxious liquid substance that at the time of unloading is

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) at a temperature of less than 5°C above its melting point, in the case of a substance with a melting point below 15°C; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) at a temperature of less than 10°C above its melting point, in the case of a substance with a melting point of 15°C or higher. (substance qui se solidifie)

heading: Procedures - Categories Y and Z
paragraph: (2) A tank from which a Category Y or Z noxious liquid substance has been unloaded must undergo a tank prewash operation before the vessel leaves the port of unloading if

heading: Procedures - Categories Y and Z
paragraph: (a) the unloaded substance is a Category Y noxious liquid substance that is a high-viscosity substance or a solidifying substance; or

heading: Procedures - Categories Y and Z
paragraph: (b) the unloading operation is not carried out in accordance with the vessel's procedures and arrangements manual.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) the unloaded tank will be reloaded with the same substance or another substance compatible with the previous one and will not be washed or ballasted prior to loading;

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) the unloaded tank will not be washed or ballasted at sea and the vessel's master has given written notice to the Department of Transport Marine Safety Office nearest to the vessel that the tank will undergo a tank prewash operation at another port and that this other port has confirmed in writing that it has a reception facility that is available and adequate for such a purpose; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (c) the cargo residues will be removed from the tank by a ventilation procedure.

heading: Ventilation procedures
paragraph: 65 A ventilation procedure must not be used to remove cargo residues for the purposes of paragraph 63(2)(c) or 64(3)(c) unless

heading: Ventilation procedures
paragraph: (a) the noxious liquid substance that was unloaded has a vapour pressure greater than 5 kPa at 20°C; and

heading: Ventilation procedures
paragraph: (b) the ventilation is carried out in accordance with sections 2 and 4 of appendix 7 to Annex II to MARPOL.

heading: Application
paragraph: 66 This subdivision does not apply in respect of vessels in a shipping safety control zone or of Canadian vessels in an area in respect of which subsection 7(2) applies.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 67 (1) A person or vessel must not discharge a noxious liquid substance carried in bulk except

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (a) in accordance with sections 68 to 71, in the case of a discharge from an NLS tanker in Section II waters or from a Canadian vessel that is an NLS tanker in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction; or

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (b) in the circumstances set out in section 5 that apply in respect of the discharge.

heading: Offshore support vessels
paragraph: (2) Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply in respect of a vessel that holds a Certificate of Fitness for an Offshore Support Vessel.

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: 68 For the purposes of section 67, ballast water that contains a Category X noxious liquid substance only because the ballast water was introduced into a tank that last contained that substance may be discharged if

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: (a) the tank underwent a tank prewash operation in accordance with subsection 63(3);

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: (b) the vessel is en route at a speed of at least 7 knots, if it is self-propelled, or at least 4 knots, if it is not self-propelled; and

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: (c) the discharge is made

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: (i) in accordance with the vessel's procedures and arrangements manual,

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: (ii) below the waterline through an underwater discharge outlet at a rate that does not exceed the maximum rate for which the underwater discharge outlet was designed,

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: (iii) at a distance of at least 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, and

heading: Authorized discharge - Category X
paragraph: (iv) into waters whose depth is at least 25 m.

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Y
paragraph: 69 For the purposes of section 67, a Category Y noxious liquid substance may be discharged if

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Y
paragraph: (a) the vessel is en route at a speed of at least 7 knots, if it is self-propelled, or at least 4 knots, if it is not self-propelled; and

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Y
paragraph: (b) the discharge is made

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Y
paragraph: (i) in accordance with the vessel's procedures and arrangements manual,

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Y
paragraph: (ii) below the waterline through an underwater discharge outlet at a rate that does not exceed the maximum rate for which the underwater discharge outlet was designed,

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Y
paragraph: (iii) at a distance of at least 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, and

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Y
paragraph: (iv) into waters whose depth is at least 25 m.

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Z
paragraph: 70 For the purposes of section 67, a Category Z noxious liquid substance may be discharged if

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Z
paragraph: (a) the vessel is en route at a speed of at least 7 knots, if it is self-propelled, or at least 4 knots, if it is not self-propelled; and

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Z
paragraph: (b) the discharge is made

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Z
paragraph: (i) in accordance with the vessel's procedures and arrangements manual,

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Z
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a vessel constructed after December 31, 2006, below the waterline through an underwater discharge outlet at a rate that does not exceed the maximum rate for which the underwater discharge outlet was designed;

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Z
paragraph: (iii) at a distance of at least 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, and

heading: Authorized discharge - Category Z
paragraph: (iv) into waters whose depth is at least 25 m.

heading: Authorized discharge - ballast water
paragraph: 71 (1) For the purposes of section 67, a Category Y or Z noxious liquid substance in ballast water that is introduced into a cargo tank that last carried the substance and has been washed to such an extent that the ballast water contains less than 1 ppm of the noxious liquid substance may be discharged without regard to the discharge rate, vessel speed and discharge outlet location if the discharge is made at a distance of at least 12 nautical miles from the nearest land and into waters whose depth is at least 25 m.

heading: NLS tankers constructed before July 1, 1994
paragraph: (2) In the case of an NLS tanker constructed before July 1, 1994, the ballast water is considered to contain less than 1 ppm of the noxious liquid substance previously carried if the cargo tank

heading: NLS tankers constructed before July 1, 1994
paragraph: (a) is washed in accordance with the requirements of Part A of appendix 6 to Annex II to MARPOL and subsequently washed with a complete cycle of the cleaning machine; or

heading: NLS tankers constructed before July 1, 1994
paragraph: (b) is washed with a water quantity not less than that required by paragraph 20 of Part B of appendix 6 to Annex II to MARPOL, using a k factor of 1.0 in the formula set out in that paragraph.

heading: Other vessels
paragraph: (3) In the case of an NLS tanker other than one referred to in subsection (2), the ballast water is considered to contain less than 1 ppm of the noxious liquid substance previously carried if the cargo tank is washed in accordance with the requirements of Part B of appendix 6 to Annex II to MARPOL.

heading: Application
paragraph: 72 This Subdivision applies in respect of vessels only when they are in waters under Canadian jurisdiction or, if a transfer operation to which this Subdivision applies does not involve a noxious liquid substance, only when they are in Canadian waters.

heading: Communications
paragraph: 73 If a vessel or a handling facility engages in a transfer operation, the vessel's master and the operator of the facility must, before and during the transfer operation, have the means for two-way voice communication on a continuing basis that enables the supervisor on board the vessel and the supervisor at the facility or on board the other vessel

heading: Communications
paragraph: (a) to communicate immediately as the need arises; and

heading: Communications
paragraph: (b) to direct the immediate shutdown of the transfer operation in case of an emergency.

heading: Lighting
paragraph: 74 (1) If a vessel or a handling facility engages in a transfer operation between sunset and sunrise, the vessel's master and the operator of the facility must ensure that illumination is provided that has

heading: Lighting
paragraph: (a) a lighting intensity of not less than 54 lx at each transfer connection point of the vessel or facility; and

heading: Lighting
paragraph: (b) a lighting intensity of not less than 11 lx at each transfer operation work area around each transfer connection point of the vessel or facility.

heading: Measurement
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), lighting intensity is to be measured on a horizontal plane 1 m above the walking surface of the facility or the working deck of the vessel, as applicable.

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: 75 (1) A person must not use a transfer conduit in a transfer operation unless the conduit

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: (a) has a bursting pressure of not less than five times its maximum design pressure;

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: (b) is clearly marked with its maximum design pressure; and

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: (c) has successfully passed, during the year before its use, a hydrostatic test to a pressure equal to one and one-half times its maximum design pressure.

heading: Test certificates
paragraph: (2) If a transfer conduit used in a transfer operation is part of a vessel's equipment, the vessel's master must keep on board the test certificate for the hydrostatic test.

heading: Manufacturer's specifications
paragraph: (3) The owner of a transfer conduit that is used in a transfer operation must ensure that the conduit is used, maintained, tested and replaced in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications.

heading: Leaks
paragraph: (4) If a transfer conduit or a connection leaks during a transfer operation, the supervisor on board the vessel and the supervisor at the handling facility or on board the other vessel must, as soon as feasible, slow down or stop the operation to remove the pressure from the conduit or connection.

heading: Requirements for transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: 76 The authorized representative of a vessel that engages in a transfer operation must ensure that it is supervised on board the vessel by a person who is required to be part of the complement of the vessel

heading: Requirements for transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (a) in the case of a Canadian vessel, by paragraph 207(3)(a), (b) or (c) or subparagraph 207(3)(d)(i) of the Marine Personnel Regulations; and

heading: Requirements for transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (b) in the case of a foreign vessel, by paragraph 241(a), subparagraph 241(b)(ii) or (iii) or paragraph 241(d) of the Marine Personnel Regulations.

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: 77 (1) The supervisor of a transfer operation on board a vessel must ensure that

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (a) the vessel is secured, having regard to the weather and the tidal and current conditions, and the mooring lines are tended so that the movement of the vessel does not damage the transfer conduit or its connections;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (b) transfer procedures are established with the concurrence of the supervisor of the transfer operation at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be, with respect to

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (i) the rates of flow and pressures for the transferred liquid,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (ii) the reduction of rates of flow and pressures where required to avoid an overflow of the tanks,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iii) the time required to stop the transfer operation under normal conditions,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iv) the time required to shut down the transfer operation under emergency conditions, and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (v) the communication signals for the transfer operation, including

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (A) stand by to start transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (B) start transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (C) slow down transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (D) stand by to stop transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (E) stop transfer,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (F) emergency stop of transfer, and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (G) emergency shutdown of transfer;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (c) the supervisor of the transfer operation at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be, has reported readiness for the commencement of the transfer operation;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (d) the person who is on duty on board the vessel in respect of the transfer operation is fully conversant with the communication signals, maintains watch over the vessel's tanks to ensure that they do not overflow, and maintains continuous communication with that person's counterpart at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (e) the manifold valves and tank valves on the vessel are not closed until the relevant pumps are stopped, if the closing of the valves would cause dangerous over-pressurization of the pumping system;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (f) the rate of flow is reduced when the tanks are being topped off;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (g) the supervisor of the transfer operation at the handling facility or on board the other vessel, as the case may be, is given sufficient notice of the stopping of the transfer operation to permit them to take the necessary action to reduce the rate of flow or pressure in a safe and efficient manner;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (h) the following measures are taken to prevent the discharge of a noxious liquid substance or dangerous chemical:

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (i) all cargo manifold connections that are not being used in the transfer operation are securely closed and fitted with blank flanges or other equivalent means of closure,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (ii) all overboard discharge valves are securely closed and marked to indicate that they are not to be opened during the transfer operation, and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iii) all scuppers are plugged;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (i) a supply of absorbent material is readily available near every transfer conduit to facilitate the clean-up of any minor spillage of noxious liquid substances or dangerous chemicals that may occur on the vessel or on the shore;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (j) all transfer conduits that are used in the transfer operation are supported to prevent the conduits and their connections from being subjected to any strain that might cause damage to them or cause the conduits to become disconnected;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (k) all systems, equipment, personnel and information necessary for the safety of the transfer are in readiness before the transfer operation begins;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (l) towing-off wires are positioned fore and aft and are ready for use without adjustment if it is necessary to tow the vessel away;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (m) the transfer of a flammable cargo and the gas-freeing that follows the unloading of a flammable cargo is stopped when an electrical storm is in the immediate vicinity of the vessel;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (n) no work is carried out in the cargo tank area without the authorization of the vessel's master;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (o) the valves in the vent system are checked for the correct setting and the flame arresters are examined for cleanliness and proper installation;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (p) articulated loading booms, if used, are checked for undue strain;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (q) the pump room ventilation is running and all precautions for that area are observed;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (r) a tank that is required to be kept in an inert state (a state in which the oxygen content of the tank must be below a specified level), and to maintain a small positive pressure at all times, has a supply of inert gas available to maintain its inert state during the transfer operation;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (s) during loading,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (i) the tank concerned is free of flammable or toxic vapours or residues,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (ii) the free end of the loading hose is securely lashed to the inside of the tank to prevent movement,

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iii) all flanges and gaskets are suitable for the purpose, and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (iv) all tank openings, other than those that are in use, are closed; and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - vessels
paragraph: (t) all reasonable precautions are taken to avoid the discharge of a noxious liquid substance or dangerous chemical.

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (2) The supervisor of a transfer operation at a handling facility must ensure that

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (a) the supervisor of the transfer operation on board the vessel has reported readiness for the transfer operation to begin;

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (b) continuous communication is maintained with the supervisor on board the vessel; and

heading: Duties of supervisors of transfer operations - facilities
paragraph: (c) the manifold valves and the tank valves at the handling facility are not closed until the relevant pumps are stopped, if the closing of the valves would cause dangerous over-pressurization of the pumping system.

heading: Emergencies
paragraph: 78 In the event of an emergency during a transfer operation, the master of a vessel and the operator of a handling facility engaged in the operation must take all necessary measures to rectify or minimize the emergency's effects.

heading: Cargo Record Books for NLS tankers
paragraph: 79 (1) Every NLS tanker must keep on board a Cargo Record Book in the form set out in appendix 2 to Annex II to MARPOL.

heading: Entries - officer in charge
paragraph: (2) The officer in charge of an operation set out in appendix 2 to Annex II to MARPOL that takes place on an NLS tanker must

heading: Entries - officer in charge
paragraph: (a) ensure that the operation is recorded without delay in the Cargo Record Book; and

heading: Entries - officer in charge
paragraph: (b) sign the recorded entry.

heading: Entries - master
paragraph: (3) The vessel's master must

heading: Entries - master
paragraph: (a) ensure that the circumstances of and reasons for any discharge referred to in paragraph 5(a) or (b), or any other accidental or exceptional discharge, of a noxious liquid substance carried in bulk are recorded without delay in the Cargo Record Book;

heading: Entries - master
paragraph: (b) ensure that each entry recorded in the Cargo Record Book is signed by the officer in charge of the operation; and

heading: Entries - master
paragraph: (c) sign each page of the Cargo Record Book after the page is completed.

heading: Language
paragraph: (4) An entry in the Cargo Record Book must

heading: Language
paragraph: (a) in the case of a Canadian vessel, be written in English or French; and

heading: Language
paragraph: (b) in the case of a foreign vessel, be written in English, French or Spanish.

heading: Three years
paragraph: (5) The vessel must keep the Cargo Record Book on board for three years after the day on which the last entry was made.

heading: Official log book
paragraph: (6) The Cargo Record Book may be part of the vessel's official log book.

heading: Reception facility receipts
paragraph: 80 (1) The master of a vessel must obtain from the owner or operator of a reception facility that receives noxious liquid substance residues or mixtures from the vessel a receipt or certificate that sets out the type and amount of noxious liquid substance residues or mixtures received and the date and time that they were received.

heading: One year
paragraph: (2) The master must keep the receipt or certificate on board for one year after the day on which it was issued.

heading: Board
