paragraph: 81 (1) The Board may, in respect of Canadian vessels, exercise the powers of the Administration conferred by regulations 4 and 5 of Annex II to MARPOL.

heading: Foreign governments
paragraph: (2) In the case of a foreign vessel, the requirements of this Division are subject to the exercise of the powers conferred by regulations 4 and 5 of Annex II to MARPOL, section 1.4 of the IBC Code, section 1.5 of the BCH Code and section 1.4 of Resolution A.673(16) by the government of the state whose flag the vessel is entitled to fly.

heading: Discharge prohibited
paragraph: 82 (1) A person or vessel must not discharge a marine pollutant that is not carried in bulk except in accordance with subsection (2) or in the circumstances set out in section 5 that apply in respect of the discharge.

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), a leakage of a marine pollutant that is not carried in bulk and is not kept as ships' stores may be discharged if any of the spillage schedules to The EmS Guide: Emergency Response Procedures for Ships Carrying Dangerous Goods, published by the IMO, sets out procedures in respect of the leakage and those procedures are followed.

heading: Jettisoning
paragraph: (3) A person or vessel must not jettison a marine pollutant that is carried in packaged form unless it is necessary to do so for the purpose of saving lives, securing the safety of a vessel or preventing the immediate loss of a vessel.

heading: Limited application - pleasure craft
paragraph: (4) This section applies in respect of pleasure craft that are not Canadian vessels only when they are in Canadian waters.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 83 The following definitions apply in this Division.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: designated sewage area means an area set out in Schedule 2. (zone designee pour les eaux usees)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: holding tank means a tank that is used solely for the collection and storage of sewage or sewage sludge and includes a tank that is an integral part of a toilet. (citerne de retenue)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: inland waters of Canada means all the rivers, lakes and other navigable fresh waters within Canada, and includes the St. Lawrence River as far seaward as a straight line drawn from Pointe-au-Pere to Orient Point. (eaux internes du Canada)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Definition of existing vessel

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 84 (1) In this section, existing vessel means a vessel

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) for which the building contract was placed before May 3, 2007;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) in the absence of a building contract, the keel of which was laid or that was at a similar stage of construction before May 3, 2007; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) the delivery of which was before May 3, 2010.

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) This Division does not apply before May 3, 2012 in respect of an existing vessel that

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) is of less than 400 gross tonnage, is not certified to carry more than 15 persons and is engaged on an international voyage; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) is not engaged on an international voyage.

heading: Discharge requirements
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2),

heading: Discharge requirements
paragraph: (a) Subdivision 2, section 95 and paragraph 96(1)(a) apply on the coming into force of this section in respect of all vessels that are in the Great Lakes, their connecting or tributary waters, or the St. Lawrence River as far east as the lower exit of the St. Lambert Lock at Montreal, Quebec; and

heading: Discharge requirements
paragraph: (b) Subdivision 2, section 95 and paragraph 96(1)(b) apply on the coming into force of this section in respect of all vessels that are in a designated sewage area.

heading: Plans and specifications
paragraph: 85 On application, the Minister must approve plans and specifications with respect to a Canadian vessel or a vessel that is recorded under the Act if the matters described in the plans and specifications meet the applicable requirements of this Subdivision.

heading: Vessels with toilet facilities
paragraph: 86 (1) Subject to subsections (3) and (4), the authorized representative of a vessel in Section I waters or Section II waters that has a toilet must ensure that the vessel is fitted with a holding tank or a marine sanitation device that meets the requirements of section 88 or 90, as the case may be.

heading: Temporary storage of sewage
paragraph: (2) The vessel's authorized representative must ensure that it is fitted with facilities for the temporary storage of sewage if the vessel

heading: Temporary storage of sewage
paragraph: (a) is fitted with a marine sanitation device that meets the requirements of paragraph 90(1)(d) only; or

heading: Temporary storage of sewage
paragraph: (b) is in a designated sewage area and is fitted with a marine sanitation device that does not meet the requirements of paragraph 90(1)(b).

heading: Limitation
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of meeting the requirement of subsection (1), a Canadian vessel or Canadian pleasure craft must not be fitted with a marine sanitation device referred to in paragraph 90(1)(d).

heading: Exception
paragraph: (4) A vessel referred to in subsection (1) that is of less than 15 gross tonnage, is not certified to carry more than 15 persons and is not operating in the inland waters of Canada or designated sewage areas may be fitted with facilities for the temporary storage of sewage instead of meeting the requirements of subsection (1) if it is not feasible to meet those requirements and the vessel has measures in place to ensure that no discharge is made otherwise than in accordance with section 96.

heading: Securing toilets
paragraph: 87 The authorized representative of a vessel must ensure that any toilet fitted on the vessel is secured in a manner that ensures its safe operation in any environmental conditions likely to be encountered.

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: 88 For the purposes of subsection 86(1), a holding tank must

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (a) be constructed so that it does not compromise the integrity of the hull;

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (b) be constructed of structurally sound material that prevents the tank contents from leaking;

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (c) be constructed so that the potable water system and other systems cannot become contaminated;

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (d) be resistant to corrosion by sewage;

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (e) have an adequate volume for the amount of sewage that could be reasonably expected to be produced on a voyage in waters where the discharge of sewage is not authorized by section 96;

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (f) be provided with a discharge connection and piping system for the removal of the tank contents at a reception facility;

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (g) be designed so that the level of sewage in the tank can be determined without the tank being opened and without contacting or removing any of the tank contents, or be equipped with a device that allows the determination to be made;

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (h) in the case of a vessel, other than a pleasure craft, that operates solely on the Great Lakes and their connecting waters, be equipped with an alarm that indicates when the tank is 75% full by volume; and

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (i) be equipped with a ventilation device that

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (i) has its outlet located on the exterior of the vessel and in a safe location away from ignition sources and areas usually occupied by people,

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (ii) prevents the build-up within the tank of pressure that could cause damage to the tank,

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (iii) is designed to minimize clogging by the contents of the tank or by climatic conditions such as snow or ice,

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (iv) is constructed of material that cannot be corroded by sewage, and

heading: Holding tanks
paragraph: (v) has a flame screen of non-corrosive material fitted to the vent outlet.

heading: Transfer conduits
paragraph: 89 (1) A person must not use a transfer conduit for the purpose of removing sewage or sewage sludge from a holding tank or a temporary means of storage on a vessel to a reception facility unless it is used, maintained and secured in a manner that minimizes risk to the marine environment from a discharge of sewage or sewage sludge.

heading: Leaks
paragraph: (2) If a transfer conduit or a connection leaks during the removal of sewage or sewage sludge from a holding tank or a temporary means of storage on a vessel to a reception facility, the vessel's master must, as soon as feasible, ensure that the removal operation is slowed down or stopped to remove the pressure from the conduit or connection.

heading: Marine sanitation devices
paragraph: 90 (1) For the purposes of subsection 86(1), a marine sanitation device must meet

heading: Marine sanitation devices
paragraph: (a) the requirements of regulation 9.1.1 of Annex IV to MARPOL for a sewage treatment plant;

heading: Marine sanitation devices
paragraph: (b) requirements substantially similar to the requirements referred to in paragraph (a) except that the standards referred to in regulation 9.1.1 include the effluent standard set out in paragraph 96(1)(b);

heading: Marine sanitation devices
paragraph: (c) the design, construction and testing requirements of Title 33, Part 159, Subpart C of the Code of Federal Regulations of the United States for a Type II marine sanitation device; or

heading: Marine sanitation devices
paragraph: (d) the requirements of regulation 9.1.2 of Annex IV to MARPOL for a sewage comminuting and disinfecting system.

heading: Grandfathering
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a marine sanitation device that was approved as an approved device under the Great Lakes Sewage Pollution Prevention Regulations and continues to meet the requirements of those Regulations as they read on May 2, 2007 may continue to be used as a marine sanitation device.

heading: Issuance of International Sewage Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: 91 On application by the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft and subject to paragraphs 16(4)(b) to (d) of the Act, the Minister must issue an International Sewage Pollution Prevention Certificate to the vessel if the applicable requirements of Annex IV to MARPOL are met.

heading: Inspection
paragraph: 92 (1) If the construction, arrangement, equipment, fittings, installations or systems of a vessel that holds a certificate issued under section 91 are changed as a result of an accident, the discovery of a defect, a repair or a major conversion that affects the requirements that were met when the certificate was issued, the authorized representative of the vessel must ensure that the Minister inspects the vessel as soon as feasible to ensure that the requirements continue to be met.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of minor repairs or the direct replacement of equipment or fittings that meet the requirements of the certificate.

heading: Certificates
paragraph: 93 (1) Every vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more and every vessel that is certified to carry more than 15 persons must hold and keep on board

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (a) an International Sewage Pollution Prevention Certificate in the form set out in the appendix to Annex IV to MARPOL, if the vessel

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (i) is a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft and does not engage only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, or

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (ii) is entitled to fly the flag of a foreign state that is a party to Annex IV to MARPOL; or

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (b) a certificate of compliance certifying that the vessel meets the applicable requirements of Annex IV to MARPOL, if the vessel is entitled to fly the flag of a state that is not a party to Annex IV to MARPOL.

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (2) Every vessel that is fitted with a marine sanitation device in order to meet the requirements of subsection 86(1) must keep on board a certificate of type approval

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (a) in the case of a device referred to in subsection 90(1), certifying that the device meets the applicable requirements referred to in that subsection; and

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (b) in the case of a device referred to in subsection 90(2), certifying that the device was approved as an approved device under the Great Lakes Sewage Pollution Prevention Regulations and bearing the approval number.

heading: Operation and maintenance manual
paragraph: (3) Every vessel that is fitted with a marine sanitation device in order to meet the requirements of subsection 86(1) and is of 400 gross tonnage or more or certified to carry more than 15 persons must keep on board a manual that sets out the operational and maintenance procedures for the device.

heading: Sewage effluent records
paragraph: (4) Every vessel must keep on board for 12 months an English or French version of

heading: Sewage effluent records
paragraph: (a) a record of the results of any tests required by subsection 97(2); or

heading: Sewage effluent records
paragraph: (b) the records required by subsection 97(4).

heading: Application
paragraph: 94 This Subdivision does not apply in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) vessels in a shipping safety control zone; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) pleasure craft that are not Canadian vessels and that are in waters in the exclusive economic zone of Canada.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 95 A person or vessel must not discharge sewage or sewage sludge except in accordance with section 96 or in the circumstances set out in section 5 that apply in respect of the discharge.

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: 96 (1) For the purposes of section 95, sewage may be discharged if

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (a) in the case of a vessel in an area other than a designated sewage area, the discharge is passed through a marine sanitation device and the effluent has a fecal coliform count that is equal to or less than 250/100 mL;

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (b) in the case of a vessel in a designated sewage area, the discharge is passed through a marine sanitation device and the effluent has a fecal coliform count that is equal to or less than 14/100 mL;

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (c) in the case of a vessel that is in Section I waters or Section II waters, but not in the inland waters of Canada or a designated sewage area, and that is of 400 gross tonnage or more or is certified to carry more than 15 persons,

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (i) the discharge is made at a distance of at least 12 nautical miles from shore and, if it is made from a holding tank or from facilities for the temporary storage of sewage, at a moderate rate while the vessel is en route at a speed of at least 4 knots, or

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (ii) the sewage is comminuted and disinfected using a marine sanitation device and the discharge is made at a distance of at least 3 nautical miles from shore;

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (d) in the case of a Canadian vessel that is in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction, other than the Antarctic area, and that is of 400 gross tonnage or more or is certified to carry more than 15 persons,

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (i) the discharge is made at a distance of at least 12 nautical miles from the nearest land and, if it is made from a holding tank or from facilities for the temporary storage of sewage, at a moderate rate while the vessel is en route at a speed of at least 4 knots, or

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (ii) the sewage is comminuted and disinfected using a marine sanitation device and the discharge is made at a distance of at least 3 nautical miles from the nearest land; or

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (e) in the case of a vessel that is in Section I waters or Section II waters but not in the inland waters of Canada or a designated sewage area, and that is of less than 400 gross tonnage and is not certified to carry more than 15 persons,

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (i) the sewage is comminuted and disinfected using a marine sanitation device and the discharge is made at a distance of at least 1 nautical mile from shore,

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (ii) the discharge is made at a distance of at least 3 nautical miles from shore while the vessel is en route at the fastest feasible speed, or

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (iii) if it is not feasible to meet the requirements of subparagraph (ii) because the vessel is located in waters that are less than 6 nautical miles from shore to shore, the discharge is made while the vessel is en route at a speed of at least 4 knots or, if the discharge is not feasible at that speed, the discharge is made

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (A) during an ebb tide, while the vessel is en route at the fastest feasible speed and into the deepest waters that are located the farthest from shore, or

heading: Authorized discharge
paragraph: (B) while the vessel is en route at the fastest feasible speed and into the deepest and fastest moving waters that are located the farthest from shore.

heading: Paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) and subparagraphs (1)(c)(ii), (d)(ii) and (e)(i)
paragraph: (2) In addition to the circumstances set out in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) and subparagraphs (1)(c)(ii), (d)(ii) and (e)(i), the sewage may be discharged only if it does not contain any visible solids and the discharge does not cause

heading: Paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) and subparagraphs (1)(c)(ii), (d)(ii) and (e)(i)
paragraph: (a) a film or sheen to develop on the water;

heading: Paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) and subparagraphs (1)(c)(ii), (d)(ii) and (e)(i)
paragraph: (b) a discoloration of the water or its shorelines; or

heading: Paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) and subparagraphs (1)(c)(ii), (d)(ii) and (e)(i)
paragraph: (c) sewage sludge or an emulsion to be deposited beneath the surface of the water or on its shorelines.

heading: Subparagraphs (1)(c)(i), (d)(i) and (e)(ii) and (iii)
paragraph: (3) In addition to the circumstances set out in subparagraphs (1)(c)(i), (d)(i) and (e)(ii) and (iii), the sewage may be discharged only if the discharge does not cause visible solids to be deposited on the shoreline.

heading: Subparagraph (1)(e)(iii)
paragraph: (4) Subparagraph (1)(e)(iii) does not apply if a reception facility that can receive the sewage in an environmentally safe manner is available to receive it.

heading: Definition of moderate rate
paragraph: (5) In this section, moderate rate means a rate that on average over any 24-hour or shorter period of discharge is not greater than the maximum permissible discharge rate calculated in accordance with section 3.1 of the Annex to the Recommendation on Standards for the Rate of Discharge of Untreated Sewage from Ships, IMO Resolution MEPC.157(55), and that over any hourly period is not more than 20% greater than that rate.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 97 (1) The following definitions apply in this section.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: biochemical oxygen demand means the quantity of oxygen determined to be used in the biochemical oxidation of organic matter during a five-day period when the organic matter is tested in accordance with the method described in section 5210 B of the Standard Methods. (demande biochimique en oxygene)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: suspended solids means the total suspended solid matter determined to be in or on a liquid when it is tested in accordance with the method described in section 2540 D of the Standard Methods. (matieres solides en suspension)

heading: Testing of effluent
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a vessel that discharges effluent from a marine sanitation device into Section I waters must, if the Minister determines that it is necessary to do so in order to ascertain whether the effluent meets the specifications on the device's certificate of type approval, ensure that samples of the effluent are tested in accordance with the Standard Methods to determine each of the following that is relevant to those specifications:

heading: Testing of effluent
paragraph: (a) the fecal coliform count of the samples;

heading: Testing of effluent
paragraph: (b) the total suspended solids content of the samples;

heading: Testing of effluent
paragraph: (c) the 5-day biochemical oxygen demand of the samples; and

heading: Testing of effluent
paragraph: (d) in the case of chlorine used as a disinfectant, the total residual chlorine content of the samples.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if the marine sanitation device is fitted with instrumentation that meets the requirements of subsection (4).

heading: Automatic continuous record
paragraph: (4) The instrumentation referred to in subsection (3) must indicate the performance of the device by providing an automatic continuous record while the device is in operation of

heading: Automatic continuous record
paragraph: (a) the suspended matter;

heading: Automatic continuous record
paragraph: (b) the residual disinfectant content, in the case of disinfection by chlorine; and

heading: Automatic continuous record
paragraph: (c) the disinfection efficiency, in the case of disinfection by any other method.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 98 The following definitions apply in this Division.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Lake Superior Special Protection Area means the area enclosed by rhumb lines connecting the following coordinates, beginning at the northernmost point and proceeding clockwise:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (e) 47°18.1' N, 86°05.0' W. (zone de protection speciale du lac Superieur)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: Six Fathom Scarp Mid-Lake Special Protection Area means the area enclosed by rhumb lines connecting the following coordinates, beginning at the northernmost point and proceeding clockwise:

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (k) 44°54' N, 82°40' W. (zone de protection speciale du milieu du lac Six Fathom Scarp)

heading: Application
paragraph: 99 This Division does not apply in respect of vessels in a shipping safety control zone or Canadian vessels in an area in respect of which subsection 7(3) applies.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 100 A Canadian vessel in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction, and a person on such a vessel, must not discharge garbage except in accordance with section 101 or in the circumstances set out in section 5 that apply in respect of the discharge.

heading: Authorized discharge - garbage
paragraph: 101 (1) For the purposes of section 187 of the Act and section 100, garbage may be discharged from a vessel in Section II waters or a Canadian vessel in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction if

heading: Authorized discharge - garbage
paragraph: (a) in the case of dunnage, lining material or packing material that does not contain plastics and can float, the discharge is made as far as feasible from the nearest land and in any case at least 25 nautical miles from the nearest land;

heading: Authorized discharge - garbage
paragraph: (b) subject to paragraph (c), in the case of garbage other than plastics or garbage that is referred to in paragraph (a), the discharge is made as far as feasible from the nearest land and in any case at least 12 nautical miles from the nearest land;

heading: Authorized discharge - garbage
paragraph: (c) in the case of garbage that is referred to in paragraph (b) and has been passed through a comminuter or grinder such that the comminuted or ground garbage can pass through a screen with openings not greater than 25 mm, the discharge is made as far as feasible from the nearest land and in any case at least 3 nautical miles from the nearest land; and

heading: Authorized discharge - garbage
paragraph: (d) in the case of cargo residues, the discharge is made after all reasonable efforts have been made to empty the cargo hold of the cargo residues and to reclaim any cargo residues that are on the vessel.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a vessel that is alongside or within 500 m of a fixed or floating platform located more than 12 nautical miles from the nearest land and engaged in the exploration, exploitation and associated offshore processing of seabed mineral resources unless the garbage is food wastes that have been passed through a comminuter or grinder such that the comminuted or ground food wastes can pass through a screen with openings not greater than 25 mm.

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: 102 (1) For the purposes of section 187 of the Act, subject to subsections (2) to (4), cargo residues that are garbage may be discharged

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (a) from a vessel in Lake Ontario, or in Lake Erie east of a line that runs due south from Point Pelee, if the discharge is made

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (i) at a distance of more than 12 nautical miles from shore, or

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (ii) in the case of iron ore cargo residues, at a distance of more than 5.2 nautical miles from shore;

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (b) from a vessel in Lake Erie, in the dredged navigation channels running between Toledo Harbor Light and Detroit River Light, if the vessel loaded cargo from a Lake Erie port immediately after unloading iron ore, coal or salt at that port and the cargo residues are residues of the unloaded iron ore, coal or salt;

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (c) from a vessel in Lake Huron, other than in the Six Fathom Scarp Mid-Lake Special Protection Area, if the discharge is made

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (i) at a distance of more than 12 nautical miles from shore, or

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (ii) in the case of iron ore cargo residues, at a distance of more than 5.2 nautical miles from shore;

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (d) from a vessel in Lake Huron, other than in the Six Fathom Scarp Mid-Lake Special Protection Area, if

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (i) the vessel is upbound along the Thumb of Michigan between 5.04 nautical miles northeast of entrance buoys 11 and 12 and the track line turn abeam of Harbor Beach, and

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (ii) the cargo residues are iron ore, coal or salt and the discharge is made at a distance of more than 2.6 nautical miles from shore;

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (e) from a vessel in Lake Superior, other than the Lake Superior Special Protection Area, if

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (i) the discharge is made from the vessel at a distance of more than 12 nautical miles from shore, and

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (ii) in the case of iron ore cargo residues, the discharge is made from the vessel at a distance of more than 5.2 nautical miles from shore;

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (f) from a vessel in Lake Ontario, Lake Erie, Lake Huron, other than in the Six Fathom Scarp Mid-Lake Special Protection Area, or Lake Superior, other than the Lake Superior Special Protection Area, or in any of the connecting and tributary waters of those lakes, if the cargo residues are limestone or other clean stone;

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (g) from a vessel in the St. Lawrence River west of Les Escoumins, if the vessel is en route and the cargo residues are not cargo sweepings;

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues
paragraph: (h) from a vessel in the inland waters of Canada in the St. Lawrence River east of Les Escoumins, if the vessel is en route and the discharge is made at a distance of more than 6 nautical miles from shore; and

heading: Authorized discharge - cargo residues

paragraph: (b) the use of equipment or materials or the carrying out of procedures; and

heading: Washwater from exhaust gas cleaning systems
paragraph: (a) any exhaust gas cleaning system residues are delivered to an onshore reception facility that is licensed by the jurisdiction where the facility is located; and

heading: Washwater from exhaust gas cleaning systems
paragraph: (b) if one or more of the vessels operate an exhaust gas cleaning system that has been certified in accordance with Resolution MEPC.184(59), the washwater from the operation of the system, as well as the monitoring and recording of the washwater, meets the requirement of section 10 of the Resolution.

heading: Report - the manner in which vessels will be managed
paragraph: (8) The vessels' authorized representative must provide the Minister with a revised report as soon as feasible if

heading: Report - the manner in which vessels will be managed
paragraph: (a) after a report is provided under paragraph (1)(b), the manner in which any of the vessels are managed in order to meet the requirements of subsection (4) or (6) changes; or

heading: Report - the manner in which vessels will be managed
paragraph: (b) after a report is provided under paragraph (2)(b), the manner in which any of the vessels are managed in order to meet the requirements of subsection (5) or (6) changes.

heading: Interim report - the manner in which vessels are being managed
paragraph: (9) The vessels' authorized representative must, during the period beginning on June 1 and ending on September 30 of any year in respect of which an election is made under subsection (1) or (2), provide the Minister with an interim report that describes how each of the vessels is being managed in order to meet the requirements of subsection (4), (5) or (6) for that year.

heading: Report - how vessels were managed
paragraph: (10) The vessels' authorized representative must

heading: Report - how vessels were managed
paragraph: (a) if an election is made under subsection (1) in respect of a period or year, provide the Minister, on or before March 1 of the year following the period or year, with a report that describes the manner in which each of the vessels was managed in order to meet the requirements of subsection (4) or (6) for that period or year; or

heading: Report - how vessels were managed
paragraph: (b) if an election is made under subsection (2), provide the Minister, on or before March 1 of each year starting in 2014 and ending in 2021, with a report that describes the manner in which each of the vessels was managed in order to meet the requirements of subsection (5) or (6) for

heading: Report - how vessels were managed
paragraph: (i) the period that begins on the day on which this section comes into force and ends on December 31, 2013, in the case of a report made in 2014, or

heading: Report - how vessels were managed
paragraph: (ii) the year before the report is made, in any other case.

heading: Auditing
paragraph: (11) The reports referred to in subsection (10) must be audited for accuracy by a person who has knowledge of the methods of conducting audits and is independent of the authorized representative.

heading: Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: (12) Despite paragraph 122(1)(a), if an election is made under paragraph (1)(a) or (2)(a) in respect of a vessel, the vessel

heading: Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: (a) must hold and keep on board a Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificate; and

heading: Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: (b) is not required to hold and keep on board an International Air Pollution Prevention Certificate, unless the vessel operates in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction and are not within the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence waters.

heading: Documentation if exhaust gas cleaning system is operated
paragraph: 111.2 If a vessel operates an exhaust gas cleaning system referred to in paragraph 111(4)(a) or 111.1(6)(a) or (c),

heading: Documentation if exhaust gas cleaning system is operated
paragraph: (a) the vessel must hold and keep on board a certificate of type approval certifying that the system meets the applicable requirements referred to in Resolution MEPC.184(59);

heading: Documentation if exhaust gas cleaning system is operated
paragraph: (b) the vessel must keep on board an EGC System Technical Manual "Scheme A" that meets the requirements of section 4.2.2 of Resolution MEPC.184(59) or an EGC System Technical Manual "Scheme B" that meets the requirements of section 5.6 of Resolution MEPC.184(59);

heading: Documentation if exhaust gas cleaning system is operated
paragraph: (c) the vessel must keep on board a SOx Emissions Compliance Plan that meets the requirements of section 9.1.1 of Resolution MEPC.184(59);

heading: Documentation if exhaust gas cleaning system is operated
paragraph: (d) the authorized representative must ensure that the information required by Resolution MEPC.184(59) respecting the operation, maintenance, servicing, adjustments and monitoring of the system is recorded as required by the Resolution; and

heading: Documentation if exhaust gas cleaning system is operated
paragraph: (e) the vessel must keep on board the information referred to in paragraph (d) in the form and manner required by Resolution MEPC.184(59).

heading: New diesel engines
paragraph: 111.3 (1) The authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft must ensure that any new diesel engine that has a displacement of 7 L or more per cylinder but less than 30 L per cylinder, and that is installed on the vessel for its propulsion, has been certified

heading: New diesel engines
paragraph: (a) by the United States Environmental Protection Agency as meeting the requirements of Title 40, section 1042.101, of the Code of Federal Regulations of the United States for Category 2 engines; or

heading: New diesel engines
paragraph: (b) by the government of another state as meeting requirements for emissions of particulate matter, nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons that are equivalent to the requirements referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Deferred application
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply before January 1, 2016.

heading: Vapour collection systems
paragraph: 112 (1) The authorized representative of an oil tanker, an NLS tanker or a gas carrier that uses a vapour collection system for volatile organic compounds must ensure that the vessel is fitted with a vapour collection system that meets the requirements of regulation 15.5 of Annex VI to MARPOL.

heading: Application to gas carriers
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) applies in respect of a gas carrier only if the type of loading and containment systems used by the carrier allow safe retention of non-methane volatile organic compounds on board or their safe return ashore.

heading: VOC management plan
paragraph: (3) The authorized representative of a crude oil tanker must ensure that a volatile organic compounds management plan that meets the requirements of regulation 15.6 of Annex VI to MARPOL is implemented.

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: 113 A person must not incinerate any of the following substances on a vessel:

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (a) oil cargo residues, noxious liquid substance cargo residues and marine pollutants;

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (b) polychlorinated biphenyls;

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (c) garbage containing more than traces of heavy metals;

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (d) refined petroleum products containing halogen compounds;

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (e) sewage sludge and sludge oil that are not generated on board the vessel; and

heading: Prohibition
paragraph: (f) exhaust gas cleaning system residues.

heading: Prohibition unless in a shipboard incinerator
paragraph: 114 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person must not incinerate a substance on a vessel unless the incineration is in a shipboard incinerator.

heading: Sewage sludge or sludge oil
paragraph: (2) Sewage sludge or sludge oil generated during the normal operation of a vessel may be incinerated in the main or auxiliary power plant or the boilers on the vessel if the incineration does not take place inside ports, harbours or estuaries.

heading: Polyvinyl chlorides
paragraph: (3) A person must not incinerate polyvinyl chlorides on a vessel unless the incineration is in a shipboard incinerator that meets the requirements of regulation 16.6.1 of Annex VI to MARPOL.

heading: Shipboard incinerators
paragraph: 115 (1) This section applies in respect of a shipboard incinerator that is installed

heading: Shipboard incinerators
paragraph: (a) after December 31, 1999

heading: Shipboard incinerators
paragraph: (i) on a Canadian vessel that does not engage only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, or

heading: Shipboard incinerators
paragraph: (ii) on a foreign vessel; or

heading: Shipboard incinerators
paragraph: (b) after May 2, 2007 on a Canadian vessel that engages only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction.

heading: Regulation 16.6.1 of Annex VI to MARPOL
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a vessel must ensure that every shipboard incinerator installed on the vessel meets the requirements of regulation 16.6.1 of Annex VI to MARPOL.

heading: Operating personnel
paragraph: (3) The authorized representative of a vessel must ensure that the personnel responsible for the operation of a shipboard incinerator are trained and capable of implementing the guidance provided in the manufacturer's operating manual.

heading: Monitoring
paragraph: (4) The master of a vessel must ensure that

heading: Monitoring
paragraph: (a) the combustion flue gas outlet temperature of a shipboard incinerator is monitored at all times; and

heading: Monitoring
paragraph: (b) waste or other matter is not fed into a continuous-feed shipboard incinerator when the temperature is below 850°C.

heading: Batch-loaded shipboard incinerators
paragraph: (5) The authorized representative of a vessel on which a batch-loaded shipboard incinerator is installed must ensure that it is designed so that the temperature in the combustion chamber reaches 600°C within five minutes after start-up and stabilizes at not less than 850°C.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 116 (1) The authorized representative of a vessel must ensure that fuel oil used on board the vessel for combustion purposes does not contain inorganic acid and meets the following requirements:

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) in the case of fuel oil derived from petroleum refining, the fuel oil must be a blend of hydrocarbons, with or without the incorporation of small amounts of additives that are intended to improve performance, and must not contain any added substance or chemical waste that

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) jeopardizes the vessel's safety,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) jeopardizes the safety or health of the vessel's personnel,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (iii) adversely affects the performance of the vessel's machinery, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (iv) contributes overall to additional air pollution; or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) in the case of fuel oil derived by methods other than petroleum refining, the fuel oil must not

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (i) jeopardize the vessel's safety,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (ii) jeopardize the safety or health of the vessel's personnel,

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (iii) adversely affect the performance of the vessel's machinery, or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (iv) contribute overall to additional air pollution.

heading: Limited application
paragraph: (2) Subparagraphs (1)(a)(ii) and (iii) and (b)(ii) and (iii) apply in respect of foreign vessels, and pleasure craft that are not Canadian vessels, only when they are in Canadian waters.

heading: Canadian vessels and Canadian pleasure craft
paragraph: 116.1 (1) If a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft cannot, while voyaging in accordance with its voyage plan, obtain fuel oil that meets the requirements of this Division, its master must notify the Minister and, if its port of destination is not in Canada, the competent authority of that port.

heading: Foreign vessels and foreign pleasure craft
paragraph: (2) If a foreign vessel or a foreign pleasure craft whose port of destination is in Canada cannot, while voyaging in accordance with its voyage plan, obtain fuel oil that meets the requirements of this Division, its master must notify the Minister.

heading: Contents of notification
paragraph: (3) The notification must include

heading: Contents of notification
paragraph: (a) the vessel's name and, if applicable, the vessel's IMO ship identification number;

heading: Contents of notification
paragraph: (b) the vessel's port of origin and port of destination;

heading: Contents of notification
paragraph: (c) details of the attempts that were made to obtain fuel oil that meets the requirements of this Division, including the names and addresses of the fuel oil suppliers contacted, and the dates on which contact was made;

heading: Contents of notification
paragraph: (d) the sulphur content of the fuel oil that was obtained; and

heading: Contents of notification
paragraph: (e) the measures that will be taken to obtain, as soon as feasible, fuel oil that meets the requirements of this Division.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: 116.2 (1) The following definitions apply in this section.

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: bulk carrier means a vessel that is intended primarily to carry dry cargo in bulk, but does not include combination carriers. (vraquier)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: combination carrier means a vessel designed to carry liquid or dry cargo in bulk. (transporteur mixte)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: container vessel means a vessel designed exclusively for the carriage of containers. (porte-conteneurs)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: existing vessel means a vessel that is not a new vessel. (batiment existant)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: gas carrier means a cargo vessel constructed or adapted, and used, for the carriage in bulk of any liquefied gas. (transporteur de gaz)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: general cargo vessel means a vessel with a multi-deck or single deck hull designed primarily for the carriage of general cargo, but does not include livestock carriers, barge carriers, heavy load carriers, yacht carriers or nuclear fuel carriers. (batiment pour marchandises diverses)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: new vessel means a vessel

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (a) for which the building contract is placed after June 30, 2013;

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (b) that is constructed after June 30, 2013, in the absence of a building contract; or

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: (c) that is delivered 30 months or more after June 30, 2015. (batiment neuf)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: refrigerated cargo carrier means a vessel designed exclusively for the carriage of refrigerated cargoes in holds. (transporteur de cargaisons refrigerees)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: ro-ro cargo vessel means a vessel designed for the carriage of cargo transportation units. (batiment de charge roulier)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: ro-ro cargo vessel (vehicle carrier) means a multi-deck ro-ro cargo vessel designed for the carriage of empty cars and trucks. (batiment de charge roulier (transporteur de vehicules))

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: ro-ro passenger vessel means a passenger vessel with ro-ro cargo spaces. (batiment roulier a passagers)

heading: Interpretation
paragraph: tanker means a chemical tanker, NLS tanker or oil tanker. (batiment-citerne)

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) Subsections (3) and (4) do not apply in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) a Canadian vessel that engages only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction or in the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence waters; or

paragraph: (b) a vessel that has a diesel-electric propulsion, turbine propulsion or hybrid propulsion system.

heading: Attained Energy Efficiency Design Index
paragraph: (3) In the case of a vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more that is a bulk carrier, combination carrier, container vessel, gas carrier, general cargo vessel, passenger vessel, refrigerated cargo carrier, ro-ro cargo vessel, ro-ro cargo vessel (vehicle carrier), ro-ro passenger vessel or tanker, the authorized representative of the vessel must ensure that the requirements of regulation 20 of Annex VI to MARPOL are met if

heading: Attained Energy Efficiency Design Index
paragraph: (a) the vessel is a new vessel; or

paragraph: (b) the vessel is an existing vessel and is considered to be a newly constructed vessel for the purposes of chapter 4 of Annex VI to MARPOL.

paragraph: (4) In the case of a vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more that is a bulk carrier, combination carrier, container vessel, gas carrier, general cargo vessel, refrigerated cargo carrier or tanker, the authorized representative of the vessel must ensure that the requirements of regulation 21 of Annex VI to MARPOL are met if

heading: Required Energy Efficiency Design Index
paragraph: (a) the vessel is a new vessel; or

paragraph: (b) the vessel is an existing vessel and is considered to be a newly constructed vessel for the purposes of chapter 4 of Annex VI to MARPOL.

paragraph: (5) In the case of a foreign vessel, the requirements of subsections (3) and (4) are subject to the exercise of the power conferred by regulation 19.4 of Annex VI to MARPOL by the government of the state whose flag the vessel is entitled to fly.

heading: Application
paragraph: 117 (1) This Subdivision applies only in respect of vessels in Canadian waters within 1 nautical mile from shore.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (2) This Subdivision does not apply in respect of vessels during the start-up or maintenance of smoke-producing systems.

heading: Density of black smoke
paragraph: 118 (1) For the purposes of this section and section 119, the smoke chart to be used in determining the density of black smoke is the Department of Transport Smoke Chart set out in Schedule 3 or a comparable chart on which fine black dots or lines, evenly spaced on a white ground space, are so arranged as to indicate

heading: Density of black smoke
paragraph: (a) density number 1, by having approximately 20% of the space black;

heading: Density of black smoke
paragraph: (b) density number 2, by having approximately 40% of the space black;

heading: Density of black smoke
paragraph: (c) density number 3, by having approximately 60% of the space black;

heading: Density of black smoke
paragraph: (d) density number 4, by having approximately 80% of the space black; and

heading: Density of black smoke
paragraph: (e) density number 5, by having approximately 100% of the space black.

heading: Visual observation
paragraph: (2) The density of black smoke is to be determined by visual observation, by

heading: Visual observation
paragraph: (a) holding a smoke chart at arm's length;

heading: Visual observation
paragraph: (b) viewing the smoke at approximately right angles to the line of travel of the smoke; and

heading: Visual observation
paragraph: (c) matching the shade of the smoke to the shade of smoke density that it most closely resembles on the smoke chart.

heading: Closest resemblance
paragraph: (3) When a determination of the density of black smoke is made in accordance with subsections (1) and (2), the black smoke is considered to be of the density and to have the density number indicated by the shade of smoke density that it most closely resembles on the smoke chart.

heading: Other smoke
paragraph: (4) Smoke that is not black smoke is considered to be of the same density and to have the same density number as black smoke that is of approximately the same degree of opacity.

heading: Other smoke
paragraph: Definition of black smoke

heading: Other smoke
paragraph: (5) In this section, black smoke means smoke that appears black or blackish.

heading: Limits of smoke emission - general
paragraph: 119 (1) Subject to subsection (2), a person must not operate on a vessel a fuel-burning installation that does not utilize hand-fired boilers and that is emitting smoke of a density greater than density number 1.

heading: Relaxation of limit
paragraph: (2) A fuel-burning installation that does not utilize hand-fired boilers may emit smoke of density number 2 for an aggregate of not more than 4 minutes in any 30-minute period.

heading: Limits of smoke emission - hand-fired boilers
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), a person must not operate on a vessel a fuel-burning installation that utilizes hand-fired boilers and that is emitting smoke of a density greater than density number 2.

heading: Relaxation of limit
paragraph: (4) A fuel-burning installation that utilizes hand-fired boilers may

heading: Relaxation of limit
paragraph: (a) while in the Detroit River, emit smoke of a density not greater than density number 3 for an aggregate of not more than 9 minutes in any 30-minute period; and

heading: Relaxation of limit
paragraph: (b) while elsewhere than in the Detroit River, emit smoke

heading: Relaxation of limit
paragraph: (i) of a density not greater than density number 3 for an aggregate of not more than 9 minutes in any 30-minute period, and

heading: Relaxation of limit
paragraph: (ii) of a density not greater than density number 4 for an aggregate of not more than 3 minutes in any 30-minute period.

heading: Issuance of Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: 120 (1) On application by the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft, and subject to paragraphs 16(4)(b) to (d) of the Act, the Minister must issue a Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificate to the vessel if the applicable requirements of this Division, other than those of section 116.2, are met.

heading: Issuance of International Air Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: (2) On application by the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft, and subject to paragraphs 16(4)(b) to (d) of the Act, the Minister must issue an International Air Pollution Prevention Certificate to the vessel if the applicable requirements of chapter 3 of Annex VI to MARPOL are met.

heading: Issuance of International Energy Efficiency Certificate
paragraph: (3) On application by the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft, and subject to paragraphs 16(4)(b) to (d) of the Act, the Minister must issue an International Energy Efficiency Certificate to the vessel if the applicable requirements of chapter 4 of Annex VI to MARPOL are met.

heading: Endorsement of Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: 121 (1) The authorized representative of a vessel that holds a Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificate must ensure that the certificate is endorsed by the Minister, within three months before or after each anniversary date of the issuance of the certificate, to indicate that the requirements for the issuance of the certificate are met.

heading: Endorsement of International Air Pollution Prevention Certificates
paragraph: (2) The authorized representative of a vessel that holds an International Air Pollution Prevention Certificate must ensure that the certificate is endorsed as required by regulations 5.1.3, 5.1.4 and 6.3 of Annex VI to MARPOL.

heading: Inspection
paragraph: (3) If the construction, arrangement, equipment, fittings, installations or systems of a vessel that holds a certificate issued under section 120 are changed as a result of an accident, the discovery of a defect, a repair or a major conversion that affects the requirements that were met when the certificate was issued, the authorized representative of the vessel must ensure that the Minister inspects the vessel as soon as feasible to ensure that the requirements continue to be met.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (4) Subsection (3) does not apply in respect of minor repairs or the direct replacement of equipment or fittings that meet the requirements of the certificate.

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: 122 (1) Every vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more must

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (a) hold and keep on board

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (i) a Canadian Air Pollution Prevention Certificate, or an International Air Pollution Prevention Certificate in the form set out in appendix I to Annex VI to MARPOL, if the vessel is a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft and engages only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction or in the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence waters,

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (ii) an International Air Pollution Prevention Certificate in the form set out in appendix I to Annex VI to MARPOL, if the vessel

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (A) is a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft and does not engage only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, or

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (B) is entitled to fly the flag of a foreign state that is a party to Annex VI to MARPOL, or

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (iii) a certificate of compliance certifying that the vessel meets the applicable requirements of Annex VI to MARPOL, if the vessel is entitled to fly the flag of a state that is not a party to Annex VI to MARPOL; and

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (b) keep on board

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (i) if the vessel has a marine diesel engine in respect of which any of sections 110.1 to 110.3 apply, an applicable certificate of type approval and a Technical File that meets the requirements of section 2.3.4 of the NOx Technical Code,

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (ii) if the vessel has a shipboard incinerator in respect of which section 115 applies, a certificate of type approval and an equipment operation manual that specifies how to operate the incinerator within the limits set out in paragraph 2 of appendix IV to Annex VI to MARPOL, and

heading: Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (iii) if the vessel is referred to in subparagraph (a)(ii) or (iii), a list, in the form set out in Appendix I to Annex VI to MARPOL, of equipment that contains ozone depleting substances, other than equipment referred to in subsection 109(5).

heading: VOC management plan
paragraph: (2) Every crude oil tanker must keep on board the volatile organic compounds management plan referred to in subsection 112(3).

heading: International Energy Efficiency Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (3) Every vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more must hold and keep on board

heading: International Energy Efficiency Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (a) an International Energy Efficiency Certificate in the form set out in appendix VIII to Annex VI to MARPOL, if the vessel

heading: International Energy Efficiency Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (i) is a Canadian vessel and does not engage only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, or

heading: International Energy Efficiency Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (ii) is entitled to fly the flag of a foreign state that is a party to Annex VI to MARPOL; or

heading: International Energy Efficiency Certificates, etc.
paragraph: (b) a certificate of compliance certifying that the vessel meets the applicable requirements of Annex VI to MARPOL, if the vessel is entitled to fly the flag of a state that is not a party to Annex VI to MARPOL.

paragraph: (4) Every vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more that does not engage only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, and every Canadian vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more that engages only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, must keep on board a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan that meets the requirements of regulation 22 of Annex VI to MARPOL. The Plan may form part of the vessel's Safety Management System, if the vessel has one.

heading: Non-application - U.S. vessels
paragraph: (5) Subsections (3) and (4) do not apply in respect of a vessel that is entitled to fly the flag of the United States.

heading: Record book of engine parameters
paragraph: 123 A vessel that is fitted with a marine diesel engine in respect of which any of sections 110.1 to 110.3 apply must keep on board a record book of engine parameters and maintain it in accordance with section 6.2.2 of the NOx Technical Code.

heading: Bunker delivery notes
paragraph: 124 (1) The master of a vessel referred to in subparagraph 122(1)(a)(ii) or (iii) must ensure that the details of fuel oil delivered to and used on board the vessel for combustion purposes are recorded in a bunker delivery note that contains at least the information specified in appendix V to Annex VI to MARPOL.

heading: Keep on board
paragraph: (2) The vessel's master must keep the bunker delivery note on board for three years after the day on which the fuel oil was delivered on board.

heading: Fuel oil samples
paragraph: (3) The vessel's master must ensure that the requirements of regulation 18.8.1 of Annex VI to MARPOL, respecting a representative sample of the fuel oil delivered that must accompany the bunker delivery note, are met.

heading: Ozone Depleting Substances Record Book
paragraph: 124.1 (1) Every vessel referred to in subparagraph 122(1)(a)(ii) or (iii) that has a rechargeable system containing ozone depleting substances, other than any system or equipment referred to in subsection 109(5), must maintain an Ozone Depleting Substances Record Book and keep it on board.

heading: Entries
paragraph: (2) The vessel's master must ensure that entries are made without delay in the Ozone Depleting Substances Record Book in respect of the following:

heading: Entries
paragraph: (a) the repair or maintenance of equipment containing ozone depleting substances;

heading: Entries
paragraph: (b) the recharge, full or partial, of equipment containing ozone depleting substances;

heading: Entries
paragraph: (c) any emission of ozone depleting substances;

heading: Entries
paragraph: (d) the transfer of ozone depleting substances to land-based reception facilities; and

heading: Entries
paragraph: (e) the supply of ozone depleting substances to the vessel.

heading: Mass of ozone depleting substances
paragraph: (3) The entries must include the mass of the ozone depleting substances that are involved in a recharge of equipment or that are emitted, transferred or supplied, as the case may be.

heading: Board
paragraph: 125 (1) The Board may, in respect of Canadian vessels and Canadian pleasure craft, exercise the powers of the Administration conferred by regulations 3.2 and 4 of Annex VI to MARPOL.

heading: Foreign governments
paragraph: (2) In the case of a foreign vessel or a foreign pleasure craft, the requirements of this Division are subject to the exercise of the powers conferred by regulations 3.2 and 4 of Annex VI to MARPOL by the government of the state whose flag the vessel is entitled to fly.

heading: Discharge prohibited
paragraph: 126 (1) A vessel in waters under Canadian jurisdiction, and a person on such a vessel, must not discharge, except in accordance with subsection (2) or in the circumstances set out in section 5 that apply in respect of the discharge, a substance listed in Schedule 1 that is not

heading: Discharge prohibited
paragraph: (a) carried in packaged form; or

heading: Discharge prohibited
paragraph: (b) carried in a cargo container, a road vehicle, a trailer, a portable tank, a railway vehicle or a tank mounted on a chassis.

heading: Authorized discharge - noxious liquid substances
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of subsection (1), a noxious liquid substance may be discharged from a vessel in Section II waters if the discharge is made in accordance with any of sections 68 to 71.

heading: Authorized discharge - chlorine
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (1), chlorine that is in sewage effluent may be discharged from a vessel if

heading: Authorized discharge - chlorine
paragraph: (a) the discharge is made as a result of the chlorine being used in a marine sanitation device to disinfect sewage; and

heading: Authorized discharge - chlorine
paragraph: (b) when the vessel is in Section I waters or at a distance of less than three nautical miles from shore in Section II waters, the total residual chlorine content in the effluent is equal to or less than 0.5 mg/L.

heading: Limited application - pleasure craft
paragraph: (4) This section applies in respect of pleasure craft that are not Canadian vessels only when they are in Canadian waters.

heading: Organotin compounds
paragraph: 127 (1) The authorized representative of a vessel must ensure that it does not have an anti-fouling system that contains any organotin compound that acts as a biocide.

heading: If applied before January 1, 2008
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an organotin compound applied before January 1, 2008 that has a coating that forms a barrier preventing the compound from leaching.

heading: Issuance of International Anti-fouling System Certificates
paragraph: 128 On application by the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft and subject to paragraphs 16(4)(b) to (d) of the Act, the Minister must issue an International Anti-fouling System Certificate to the vessel if the applicable requirements of Annex 1 to the Anti-fouling Systems Convention are met.

heading: Endorsement
paragraph: 129 The authorized representative of a vessel that holds an International Anti-fouling System Certificate must ensure that the certificate is endorsed as required by regulation 1(1)(b) of Annex 4 to the Anti-fouling Systems Convention.

heading: Certificates
paragraph: 130 Every vessel of 400 gross tonnage or more must hold and keep on board

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (a) an International Anti-fouling System Certificate in the form set out in appendix 1 to Annex 4 to the Anti-fouling Systems Convention, if the vessel

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (i) is a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft, or

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (ii) is entitled to fly the flag of a foreign state that is a party to the Anti-fouling Systems Convention; or

heading: Certificates
paragraph: (b) a certificate of compliance certifying that the vessel meets the applicable requirements of the Anti-fouling Systems Convention, if the vessel is entitled to fly the flag of a state that is not a party to the Anti-fouling Systems Convention.

heading: Certificates
paragraph: Definition of length

heading: Certificates
paragraph: 131 (1) In this section, length has the same meaning as in article 2(8) of the International Convention on Load Lines, 1966, as modified by the Protocol of 1988 relating to the Convention.

heading: Anti-fouling Systems Declaration
paragraph: (2) A vessel that is 24 m or more in length but of less than 400 gross tonnage and does not engage only on voyages in waters under Canadian jurisdiction must keep on board a declaration confirming that the anti-fouling system applied to the vessel meets the applicable requirements of Annex 1 to the Anti-fouling Systems Convention.

heading: Signing
paragraph: (3) The declaration must be signed by the authorized representative, in the case of a Canadian vessel, and the owner, in the case of any other vessel.

heading: Language
paragraph: (4) The declaration must be in the form set out in Schedule 4. It must

heading: Language
paragraph: (a) in the case of a Canadian vessel or a Canadian pleasure craft, be written in English or French; and

heading: Language
paragraph: (b) in the case of a foreign vessel or a foreign pleasure craft, be written in English, French or Spanish.

heading: Endorsement
paragraph: (5) The declaration must be accompanied by appropriate documentation, such as a paint receipt or a contractor invoice, or contain an appropriate endorsement of the system applied to the vessel.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 131.1 (1) The following definitions apply in this section.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: greywater means drainage from sinks, laundry machines, bath tubs, shower-stalls or dishwashers. It does not include sewage, or drainage from machinery spaces or workshop areas. (eaux grises)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: new passenger vessel means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a passenger vessel that is constructed on or after the day on which this section comes into force;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a passenger vessel that, on or after the day on which this section comes into force, undergoes a conversion that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) substantially alters the dimensions or carrying capacity of the vessel, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) is intended to substantially prolong the life of the vessel; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a vessel that, on or after the day on which this section comes into force, is converted into a passenger vessel. (batiment a passagers neuf)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: release includes spilling, leaking, pumping, pouring, emitting, emptying, throwing and dumping. (liberation)

heading: Application
paragraph: (2) This section applies in respect of vessels in waters under Canadian jurisdiction other than arctic waters.

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (3) This section does not apply in respect of a release of greywater that

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (a) is necessary for the purpose of saving lives, securing the safety of a vessel or preventing the immediate loss of a vessel; or

heading: Non-application
paragraph: (b) occurs as a result of an accident of navigation in which a vessel or its equipment is damaged, unless the accident occurs as a result of an action that is outside the ordinary practice of seafarers.

heading: Solids in water and sheen on water prohibited
paragraph: (4) The authorized representative of a vessel must ensure that any release of greywater by or from the vessel into the water does not result in the deposit of solids in the water or leave a sheen on the water.

heading: New passenger vessels
paragraph: (5) The authorized representative of a new passenger vessel that is carrying more than 500 passengers must ensure that any release of greywater by or from the vessel into the water

heading: New passenger vessels
paragraph: (a) is passed through a marine sanitation device that meets the requirements of section 90; or

heading: New passenger vessels
paragraph: (b) is made at a distance of at least three nautical miles from shore.

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (6) Every vessel that is fitted with a marine sanitation device in order to meet the requirements of paragraph (5)(a) must keep on board

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (a) a certificate of type approval

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (i) in the case of a device referred to in subsection 90(1), certifying that the device meets the applicable requirements referred to in that subsection, and

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (ii) in the case of a device referred to in subsection 90(2), certifying that the device was approved as an approved device under the Great Lakes Sewage Pollution Prevention Regulations and bearing the approval number; and

heading: Certificates of type approval
paragraph: (b) a manual that sets out the operational and maintenance procedures for the device.

heading: Vessels in waters under Canadian jurisdiction
paragraph: 132 (1) The master of a vessel in waters under Canadian jurisdiction must report any discharge or anticipated discharge from the vessel if the discharge or anticipated discharge is

heading: Vessels in waters under Canadian jurisdiction
paragraph: (a) prohibited by section 187 of the Act or by these Regulations; or

heading: Vessels in waters under Canadian jurisdiction
paragraph: (b) authorized by paragraph 5(a), (b), (d) or (e).

heading: Canadian vessels in other waters
paragraph: (2) The master of a Canadian vessel in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction must report any discharge or anticipated discharge from the vessel of oil, a noxious liquid substance carried in bulk or a marine pollutant that is not carried in bulk if the discharge or anticipated discharge is

heading: Canadian vessels in other waters
paragraph: (a) prohibited by section 187 of the Act or by these Regulations; or

heading: Canadian vessels in other waters
paragraph: (b) authorized by paragraph 5(a), (b), (d) or (e).

heading: When report is to be made
paragraph: (3) The master must make the report

heading: When report is to be made
paragraph: (a) as soon as a discharge occurs or is anticipated; or

heading: When report is to be made
paragraph: (b) as soon as feasible after a discharge occurs or is anticipated, if the master is unable to make the report under paragraph (a) because he or she is involved in activities relating to

heading: When report is to be made
paragraph: (i) saving lives,

heading: When report is to be made
paragraph: (ii) securing the vessel's safety or preventing its immediate loss,

heading: When report is to be made
paragraph: (iii) preventing or mitigating damage to the vessel or its equipment, or

heading: When report is to be made
paragraph: (iv) preventing or mitigating damage to the environment.

heading: If report not made in accordance with paragraph (3)(a)
paragraph: (4) If the authorized representative of a Canadian vessel, or the owner of any other vessel, is not on board the vessel and has knowledge that a report has not been made in accordance with paragraph (3)(a), the authorized representative or owner must make the report immediately.

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (5) Every report must be made in accordance with sections 2 and 3.1 to 3.3 of the appendix to the Annex to the General Principles for Ship Reporting Systems and Ship Reporting Requirements, Including Guidelines for Reporting Incidents Involving Dangerous Goods, Harmful Substances and/or Marine Pollutants, IMO Resolution A.851(20), and must include the following information:

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (a) the identity of every vessel involved;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (b) the date, time and location of the discharge or the estimated date, time and location of the anticipated discharge;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (c) the nature of the discharge or anticipated discharge, including the type and estimated quantity of pollutant involved; and

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (d) in the case of a discharge, a description of the assistance and salvage measures employed.

heading: Vessels rendering assistance or undertaking salvage
paragraph: (6) The master of a vessel must report the particulars of any action taken in rendering assistance to or undertaking salvage of another vessel whose master is required under subsection (1) or (2) to report a discharge or an anticipated discharge.

heading: To whom reports are made
paragraph: (7) A report required by subsection (1), (2), (4) or (6) must be made to

heading: To whom reports are made
paragraph: (a) a marine safety inspector or a marine communications and traffic services officer, in the case of a discharge or anticipated discharge in waters under Canadian jurisdiction; or

heading: To whom reports are made
paragraph: (b) an appropriate official of the nearest coastal state, in the case of a discharge or anticipated discharge from a Canadian vessel in waters that are not waters under Canadian jurisdiction.

heading: Supplementary reports
paragraph: (8) A person who makes a report must, whenever there is further information relating to the incident and essential for the protection of the marine environment, submit to the person to whom the report was made a supplementary report with as much of that information as possible.

heading: Language
paragraph: (9) Despite the requirement in the IMO Resolution referred to in subsection (5) that the languages used in reports include English where language difficulties may exist, a report made to a marine safety inspector or a marine communications and traffic services officer may be made in English or French.

heading: Oil handling facilities
paragraph: 133 (1) The operator of an oil handling facility who is required to have an oil pollution emergency plan under paragraph 168(1)(d) of the Act must, as soon as feasible,

heading: Oil handling facilities
paragraph: (a) report any discharge or anticipated discharge of oil to the federal emergency telephone number identified in the oil pollution emergency plan; and

heading: Oil handling facilities
paragraph: (b) report in writing any discharge or anticipated discharge of oil to the Department of Transport Marine Safety Office nearest to the facility.

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (2) The report must include the following information:

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (a) the identity of any vessel involved;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (b) the name and address of the oil handling facility;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (c) the name and position of the person who is responsible for implementing and coordinating the oil pollution emergency plan;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (d) the date, time and location of the discharge or the estimated date, time and location of the anticipated discharge;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (e) the nature of the discharge or anticipated discharge, including the type and estimated quantity of oil involved;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (f) a description of the response actions to be taken;

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (g) on-scene conditions; and

heading: Contents of report
paragraph: (h) any other relevant information.
