(egout unitaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: composite sample means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a composite sample as defined by the government of the province where the wastewater system is located, or under an Act of Parliament, if the definition applies to the wastewater system;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a quantity of effluent consisting of not less than three equal volumes or three volumes proportionate to the rate of flow that have been collected at approximately equal time intervals over

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) the period during which effluent is deposited, if effluent is deposited only during part of the day, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) a sampling period of not less than seven hours and not more than 24 hours, if effluent is deposited throughout the day; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a quantity of effluent collected continuously at a constant rate or at a rate proportionate to the rate of flow of the effluent over

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i) the period during which effluent is deposited, if effluent is deposited only during part of the day, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii) a sampling period of not less than seven hours and not more than 24 hours, if effluent is deposited throughout the day. (echantillon composite)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: effluent means wastewater that is deposited from a wastewater system. (effluent)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: final discharge point means any point of a wastewater system, other than an overflow point, beyond which the owner or operator of the system no longer exercises control over the quality of the wastewater before it is deposited as effluent in water or a place. (point de rejet final)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: greywater means used water, other than blackwater, from sanitary appliances or from other appliances in a kitchen or laundry. (eaux grises)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hydraulic retention time, in relation to a wastewater system, means the average period during which wastewater is retained for treatment and storage prior to release from that system. (temps de retention hydraulique)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: influent means wastewater entering a wastewater system. (affluent)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: licensed professional means a licensed member of an engineering or scientific professional organization who has technical expertise in the field in question. (professionnel agree)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: overflow point means a point of a wastewater system via which excess wastewater may be deposited in water or a place and beyond which its owner or operator no longer exercises control over the quality of wastewater before it is deposited as effluent. (point de debordement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: point of entry, in relation to the final discharge point or an overflow point of a wastewater system, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the point where effluent is deposited in water frequented by fish via the final discharge point or the overflow point, as the case may be; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any point where the effluent enters that water from the place where it was deposited via the final discharge point or the overflow point, as the case may be. (point d'entree)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: previous calendar year, in respect of a given period and a wastewater system, means the most recent calendar year during which effluent was deposited via the system's final discharge point that ended before the given period. (annee civile precedente)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: previous month, in respect of a given period and a wastewater system, means the most recent month during which effluent was deposited via the system's final discharge point that ended before the given period. (mois precedent)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: previous quarter, in respect of a given period and a wastewater system, means the most recent quarter during which effluent was deposited via the system's final discharge point that ended before the given period. (trimestre precedent)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Procedure for pH Stabilization EPS 1/RM/50 means the Procedure for pH Stabilization During the Testing of Acute Lethality of Wastewater Effluent to Rainbow Trout (EPS 1/RM/50), March 2008, published by the Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time. (Procedure de stabilisation du pH SPE 1/RM/50)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: protected aquatic species means an aquatic species as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Species at Risk Act that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a species at risk as defined in that subsection or a species that is listed in Schedule 1 to that Act; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a species that is protected - or classified as an endangered species or threatened species as defined in that subsection - under the laws of a province. (espece aquatique protegee)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: quarter, in respect of a year, means a period of three months that begins on the first day of January, April, July or October. (trimestre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 means the Biological Test Method: Reference Method for Determining Acute Lethality of Effluents to Rainbow Trout (EPS 1/RM/13 Second Edition), December 2000 with May 2007 amendments, published by the Department of the Environment, as amended from time to time. (Methode de Reference SPE 1/RM/13)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: sanitary sewer means a sewer that is designed to collect wastewater referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (c) of the definition wastewater or any combination of wastewater referred to in those paragraphs. (egout sanitaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: suspended solids or SS means any solid matter contained in effluent that is retained on a filter that has a nominal pore size of 1.5 micrometres or smaller. (matieres en suspension ou MES)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: total residual chlorine means the sum of free chlorine and combined chlorine, including inorganic chloramines. (chlore residuel total)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: wastewater means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) blackwater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) greywater that is mixed with blackwater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) used water - other than blackwater and greywater - from an industrial, commercial or institutional facility that is mixed with blackwater; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) surface runoff and stormwater that is mixed with blackwater. (eaux usees)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: wastewater system means any work or undertaking, at least part of which is located on land, that is used for the collection and deposit of wastewater, whether or not the wastewater is treated, and includes a site that contains a wastewater lagoon. (systeme d'assainissement)

heading: Application
paragraph: 2 (1) These Regulations apply in respect of a wastewater system that, when it deposits effluent via one or more final discharge points, deposits a deleterious substance prescribed in section 5 in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act and that

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) is designed to collect an average daily volume of 100 m3 or more of influent; or

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) during any calendar year, collects an average daily volume of 100 m3 or more of influent.

heading: Annual exceptions
paragraph: (2) Despite paragraph (1)(a), these Regulations do not, for the subsequent calendar year, apply in respect of a wastewater system referred to in that paragraph that, during a calendar year, collected an average daily volume of less than 100 m3 of influent.

heading: Non-applica-tion - areas
paragraph: (3) These Regulations do not apply in respect of a wastewater system located

heading: Non-applica-tion - areas
paragraph: (a) in the Northwest Territories;

heading: Non-applica-tion - areas
paragraph: (b) in Nunavut; or

heading: Non-applica-tion - areas
paragraph: (c) north of the 54th parallel in Quebec or Newfoundland and Labrador.

heading: Non-applica-tion - industrial, commercial or institutional influent
paragraph: (4) These Regulations do not apply in respect of a wastewater system that is located on the site of an industrial, commercial or institutional facility if the wastewater system is designed to collect influent whose volume consists of less than 50% blackwater and greywater combined.

heading: Non-applica-tion - pulp and paper mills
paragraph: (5) These Regulations do not apply in respect of a mill as defined in section 2 of the Pulp and Paper Effluent Regulations.

heading: Types of wastewater systems
paragraph: 3 For the purpose of these Regulations, there are two types of wastewater systems, as follows:

heading: Types of wastewater systems
paragraph: (a) an intermittent wastewater system, namely, one with a hydraulic retention time of at least 90 days that deposits effluent via its final discharge point during at most four periods per calendar year, each of which is separated from every other period by at least seven clear days during which no deposit occurs; and

heading: Types of wastewater systems
paragraph: (b) a continuous wastewater system, namely, any wastewater system other than an intermittent wastewater system.

heading: Consolidated wastewater systems
paragraph: 4 (1) If an owner of at least two original wastewater systems - none of which treats its wastewater in a manner that would permit the deposit of effluent, via its final discharge points, that meets the condition set out in paragraph 6(1)(a) or (b) - plans to consolidate those original wastewater systems into a future consolidated wastewater system, the original wastewater systems that will be consolidated constitute a fictional consolidated wastewater system during the period beginning on the day on which a consolidation plan that meets the requirements of subsection (3) is received by an authorization officer and ending on the day on which the future consolidated wastewater system is put into service.

heading: Final discharge point
paragraph: (2) The final discharge point of the fictional consolidated wastewater system is considered to be the final discharge point of the original wastewater systems that is allocated the greatest number of points under the table to Schedule 2.

heading: Consolidation plan
paragraph: (3) The consolidation plan must contain a description of the modifications to be made to each of the original wastewater systems, including a description of the modifications to be made to their processes, so that the effluent deposited via the final discharge point of the future consolidated wastewater system will not be acutely lethal and will meet the conditions for authorization set out in subsection 6(1), along with a schedule for implementation of the plan.

heading: Prescribed deleterious substances
paragraph: 5 For the purpose of the definition deleterious substance in subsection 34(1) of the Act, the following substances or classes of substances are prescribed as deleterious substances:

heading: Prescribed deleterious substances
paragraph: (a) carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demanding matter;

heading: Prescribed deleterious substances
paragraph: (b) suspended solids;

heading: Prescribed deleterious substances
paragraph: (c) total residual chlorine; and

heading: Prescribed deleterious substances
paragraph: (d) un-ionized ammonia.

heading: Authorization to deposit
paragraph: 6 (1) For the purpose of paragraph 36(4)(b) of the Act, the owner or operator of a wastewater system may - during a given calendar year, quarter or month, as determined in accordance with subsection (2) - deposit or permit the deposit of effluent that contains any of the deleterious substances prescribed in section 5 of these Regulations via each of the system's final discharge points in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act if the effluent is not acutely lethal as determined in accordance with section 15, the maximum concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the effluent is less than 1.25 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N), at 15˚C +/- 1˚C, and - during the previous calendar year, previous quarter or previous month, as the case may be - the effluent met the following conditions:

heading: Authorization to deposit
paragraph: (a) the average carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand due to the quantity of CBOD matter in the effluent did not exceed 25 mg/L;

heading: Authorization to deposit
paragraph: (b) the average concentration of suspended solids in the effluent did not exceed 25 mg/L; and

heading: Authorization to deposit
paragraph: (c) the average concentration of total residual chlorine in the effluent did not exceed 0.02 mg/L, if chlorine, or one of its compounds, was used in the treatment of wastewater.

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (2) The maximum concentration and the averages referred to in subsection (1) must be determined on the following basis:

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (a) each calendar year, if the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all of the final discharge points during the previous calendar year was

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (i) less than or equal to 17 500 m3, for an intermittent wastewater system, and

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (ii) less than or equal to 2 500 m3, for a continuous wastewater system with a hydraulic retention time of five or more days or for a continuous wastewater system that is the subject of a transitional authorization;

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (b) each quarter, if the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all of the final discharge points during the previous calendar year was

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (i) greater than 2 500 m3 and less than or equal to 17 500 m3, for a continuous wastewater system with a hydraulic retention time of five or more days, and

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (ii) less than or equal to 17 500 m3, for any other continuous wastewater system; and

heading: Averaging periods
paragraph: (c) each month, if the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all of the final discharge points during the previous calendar year was greater than 17 500 m3.

heading: Determination of averages
paragraph: (3) The averages referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) must be determined

heading: Determination of averages
paragraph: (a) for an intermittent wastewater system, based on samples of effluent referred to in subsection 10(1) and, if applicable, subsection 10(2), in accordance with subsection 10(6); and

heading: Determination of averages
paragraph: (b) for a continuous wastewater system, based on samples of effluent referred to in, as the case may be, subsection 10(3) or (4), in accordance with subsection 10(6).

heading: Determinations for additional samples
paragraph: (4) The determination of averages made in accordance with subsection (3) must take into account the results of the determination, by a laboratory referred to in section 16, of the elements referred to in subsection 10(6) for any sample in excess of the number of samples required by subsections 10(1) to (4).

heading: Average of SS during certain months
paragraph: (5) For an intermittent wastewater system or a continuous wastewater system with a hydraulic retention time of five or more days, the determination of the average referred to in paragraph (1)(b) is not to take into account the result of any determination of the concentration of suspended solids in a sample of effluent referred to in paragraph 10(6)(b) that was taken during any four months during the period beginning on May 1 and ending on November 30, if that result is greater than 25 mg/L and is caused by a bloom of algae or proliferation of aquatic invertebrates.

heading: SS average deemed 0 mg/L
paragraph: (6) If subsection (5) applies to every sample referred to in paragraph (3)(a) or (b) that is used to determine the average referred to in paragraph (1)(b), that average is deemed to be 0 mg/L.

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (7) The authorization granted to an owner or operator under subsection (1) is conditional on the owner or operator

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (a) determining the average daily volume of effluent deposited annually via the final discharge point in accordance with section 7;

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (b) for an intermittent wastewater system, either installing, maintaining and calibrating the monitoring equipment referred to in subparagraph 7(2)(a)(i) or establishing a method of estimation referred to in subparagraph 7(2)(a)(ii) and applying and updating it in accordance with subsection 7(4);

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (c) for a continuous wastewater system, either installing, maintaining and calibrating the monitoring equipment referred to in subparagraph 7(2)(b)(i) or establishing a method of estimation referred to in subparagraph 7(2)(b)(ii) and applying and updating it in accordance with subsection 7(4);

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (d) monitoring effluent in accordance with sections 10 and 11 and sending a monitoring report in accordance with section 19;

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (e) keeping the record required under section 17;

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (f) sending an identification report in accordance with section 18;

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (g) sending the overflow report, if applicable, required under section 20 in accordance with subsections 19(4) and (5); and

heading: Conditions
paragraph: (h) installing, operating and maintaining a dechlorination system - if chlorine, or one of its compounds, is being used in the treatment of wastewater - so that the concentration of total residual chlorine in a grab sample of effluent does not exceed 0.10 mg/L when measured using a total residual chlorine instrument or test in accordance with standards of good scientific practice that are generally accepted at the time of the sampling.

heading: Average daily volume deposited annually
paragraph: 7 (1) The owner or operator of a wastewater system must, for each calendar year, calculate the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all of the system's final discharge points by

heading: Average daily volume deposited annually
paragraph: (a) determining, in accordance with subsection (2), for each day during that calendar year when effluent was deposited, the volume of effluent deposited via each of the final discharge points, expressed in m3;

heading: Average daily volume deposited annually
paragraph: (b) calculating the sum of the daily volumes of effluent of all of the discharge points referred to in paragraph (a); and

heading: Average daily volume deposited annually
paragraph: (c) dividing that sum by the number of days in that calendar year.

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (2) The volume of effluent during each day referred to in paragraph (1)(a) must be determined

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (a) for an intermittent wastewater system,

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (i) by using monitoring equipment referred to in section 9 that provides

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (A) a continuous measure of the volume of influent, or effluent deposited via the final discharge point, during that day, or

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (B) a measure of the rate of flow of the influent or that effluent upon which that daily volume may be estimated, or

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (ii) by using a method of estimation in accordance with subsection (4);

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (b) for a continuous wastewater system,

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (i) by using monitoring equipment referred to in section 9 that provides

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (A) a continuous measure of the volume of influent, or effluent deposited via the final discharge point, during that day, if the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all final discharge points during the previous calendar year was more than 2 500 m3, or

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (B) a continuous measure of the volume of influent or effluent deposited over this day, or a measure of the rate of flow of that influent or effluent, that allows for the daily volume of effluent to be estimated, if the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all final discharge points during the previous calendar year was 2 500 m3 or less, or

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (ii) by using a method of estimation in accordance with subsection (4) if

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (A) a transitional authorization has been issued under subsection 26(1) in respect of the continuous wastewater system, and

heading: Daily volumes
paragraph: (B) the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all final discharge points during the previous calendar year was less than 2 500 m3.

heading: Daily volume estimate - rate of flow
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of paragraph (1)(a), if the owner or operator estimates the daily volume of effluent deposited via the final discharge point based on the measured rate of flow referred to in clause (2)(a)(i)(B) or (b)(i)(B), the estimation is to be done as follows:

heading: Daily volume estimate - rate of flow
paragraph: (a) measure the rate of flow of influent, or effluent deposited via the final discharge point, in any chosen unit of volume for any chosen unit of time; and

heading: Daily volume estimate - rate of flow
paragraph: (b) calculate that volume based on that rate of flow for the duration of the deposits of effluent made on that day and, if applicable, convert it to m3.

heading: Method of estimation
paragraph: (4) The owner or operator of a wastewater system who has established a method of estimation of the volume of effluent must ensure that it is based on generally accepted engineering practices and use it to estimate the daily volume of effluent deposited via the final discharge point with a margin of error of +/-15%.

heading: Default measurement
paragraph: 8 (1) If the average daily volume of effluent deposited via the final discharge point of a wastewater system for a previous calendar year cannot be determined under paragraph 7(2)(a) or (b), as the case may be, that average daily volume must be determined on the basis of the system's average design rate of flow of influent.

heading: One-time use of default measurement
paragraph: (2) If subsection (1) has been applied in respect of a wastewater system for a calendar year, it is not to be applied in respect of the wastewater system for any subsequent calendar year.

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 9 (1) The owner or operator of a wastewater system must install monitoring equipment that provides a continuous measure of the daily volume or of the rate of flow of the influent or effluent.

heading: Maintenance
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator must maintain the monitoring equipment so that it may be used to determine the volume of effluent deposited via the final discharge point.

heading: Calibration
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator must calibrate the monitoring equipment in accordance with the recommendations of the manufacturer or licensed professional or, in the absence of such recommendations, must calibrate the equipment at least once in every calendar year and at least five months after the most recent calibration.

heading: Accuracy
paragraph: (4) The monitoring equipment must determine the volume or rate of flow with a margin of error of +/-15%.

heading: Taking of samples - intermittent wastewater system
paragraph: 10 (1) The owner or operator of an intermittent wastewater system must, during each period referred to in paragraph 3(a), take at each of the system's final discharge points a grab or composite sample of effluent at the following minimum frequencies:

heading: Taking of samples - intermittent wastewater system
paragraph: (a) if the period is more than 30 days, every two weeks, at least seven days after the previous sample; and

heading: Taking of samples - intermittent wastewater system
paragraph: (b) if the period is 30 days or less, once.

heading: Taking of samples prior to deposit
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if a grab or composite sample of effluent has been collected at a sampling location referred to in subsection (5) within two weeks of the period referred to in paragraph 3(a) for the government of the province where the wastewater system is located or under an Act of Parliament, and if the determinations referred to in subsection (6) and, if applicable, paragraph 38(b) were made, the owner or operator of a system is not required to take a sample during the first 30 days of deposit and may use the results of the determinations made on the sample of effluent collected prior to deposit.

heading: Taking of samples - continuous wastewater system
paragraph: (3) The owner or operator of a continuous wastewater system must take at each of the system's final discharge points, during each calendar year, a sample of effluent of the type set out in column 2 of the table to this subsection that corresponds to the average daily volume of effluent set out in column 1 that is deposited via all final discharge points during the previous calendar year and must do so at the frequency set out in column 3.

heading: Sampling and frequency - exception
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), the owner or operator of a continuous wastewater system with a hydraulic retention time of five or more days, or of a continuous wastewater system that is the subject of a transitional authorization, may

heading: Sampling and frequency - exception
paragraph: (a) take a grab or composite sample at each of the system's final discharge points; and

heading: Sampling and frequency - exception
paragraph: (b) reduce the minimum sampling frequency to quarterly, with each sample taken at least 60 days after the previous sample, if the system deposited via all of its final discharge points an average daily volume of less than or equal to 2 500 m3 of effluent during the previous calendar year.

heading: Taking of samples - other sampling location
paragraph: (5) Despite subsections (1) and (4), the owner or operator of an intermittent wastewater system, or of a continuous wastewater system with a hydraulic retention time of five or more days, may take a grab or composite sample of effluent at a sampling location other than the final discharge point if the sampling location yields a representative sample as if the sample had been collected at the final discharge point and if the sampling location and sampling procedure are determined by a licensed professional.

heading: Determination - certain deleterious substances
paragraph: (6) The owner or operator must, for each sample referred to in subsection (1) to (4), determine or cause the determination of the following elements:

heading: Determination - certain deleterious substances
paragraph: (a) the carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand due to the quantity of CBOD matter in the effluent, in accordance with section 12; and

heading: Determination - certain deleterious substances
paragraph: (b) the concentration of suspended solids in the effluent, in accordance with section 13.

heading: Taking of samples - intermittent wastewater system
paragraph: 11 (1) The owner or operator of an intermittent wastewater system must take at each of the system's final discharge points, for each period referred to in paragraph 3(a) during each calendar year, a grab sample of effluent on the day a deposit begins if the average daily volume of effluent deposited via all of the final discharge points during the previous calendar year was more than 2 500 m3.

heading: Taking of samples - continuous wastewater system
paragraph: (2) The owner or operator of a continuous wastewater system must take at each of the system's final discharge points, during each calendar year, a grab sample of effluent at the minimum sampling frequency set out in column 2 of the table to this subsection that corresponds to the average daily volume of effluent set out in column 1 deposited via all of the system's final discharge points during the previous calendar year.

heading: Acute lethality
paragraph: (3) For each sample taken under subsection (1) or (2), the owner or operator must determine or cause the determination of whether it is acutely lethal in accordance with section 15.

heading: Additional tests
paragraph: (4) If a sample is determined to be acutely lethal, the owner or operator must take a grab sample without delay, and then subsequently once every two weeks, but at least seven days after the previous sample, and determine or cause the determination of whether it is acutely lethal in accordance with section 15.

heading: Consecutive samples - not acutely lethal
paragraph: (5) If three consecutive samples taken in accordance with subsection (4) are determined not to be acutely lethal, subsections (1) to (3) apply to subsequent samples.

heading: Subsequent samples
paragraph: (6) For greater certainty, subsection (4) applies to any subsequent sample referred to in subsection (5) that is determined to be acutely lethal when tested under subsection (3).

heading: Change in sampling frequency
paragraph: (7) The minimum sampling frequency set out in column 2 of the table to subsection (2) is reduced

heading: Change in sampling frequency
paragraph: (a) for item 1, to yearly, but at least six months after any other sample, if samples were taken under subsection (2) for each of four consecutive quarters and those samples were tested under subsection (3) and determined not to be acutely lethal; and

heading: Change in sampling frequency
paragraph: (b) for item 2, to quarterly, but at least 60 days after any other sample, if samples were taken under subsection (2) for each of 12 consecutive months and those samples were tested under subsection (3) and determined not to be acutely lethal.

heading: CBOD matter
paragraph: 12 The demand due to the quantity of carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demanding matter in the effluent must be determined in accordance with a five-day biochemical oxygen demand test with nitrification inhibition.

heading: Suspended solids
paragraph: 13 The concentration of suspended solids in the effluent must be determined in accordance with a total suspended solids test.

heading: Un-ionized ammonia
paragraph: 14 (1) The concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the effluent must be determined in accordance with the following formula:

heading: Un-ionized ammonia
paragraph: total ammonia * 1 / (1 +109.56 - pH)

heading: Un-ionized ammonia
paragraph: where

heading: Concentration of total ammonia
paragraph: (2) The concentration of total ammonia in the effluent must be determined by using an aliquot of the same sample of effluent from which the pH of the effluent was determined and testing it in accordance with a total ammonia test.

heading: pH
paragraph: (3) The pH of the effluent must be determined by using an aliquot of the same sample of effluent from which the concentration of total ammonia of the effluent was determined and testing it in accordance with a pH test.

heading: Acute lethality
paragraph: 15 The acute lethality of the effluent must be determined in accordance with

heading: Acute lethality
paragraph: (a) Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 using the procedure set out in section 5 or 6 of that Method; or

paragraph: (b) paragraph (a) using the Procedure for pH Stabilization EPS 1/RM/50.

paragraph: 16 Any determination referred to in subsection 10(6) or 11(3) or (4) or paragraph 34(1)(a) or (b) or subsection 34(4) and any other determination necessary to make any of those determinations - other than the determination of the pH of water necessary to make the determination referred to in subsection 34(3) - must be performed by a laboratory that meets the following conditions at the time of the determination:

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (a) the laboratory is accredited

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (i) under the International Organization for Standardization standard ISO/IEC 17025, entitled General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories, by an accrediting body that is a signatory to the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation Mutual Recognition Arrangement, or

paragraph: (ii) under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR, c. Q-2; and

heading: Accredited laboratory
paragraph: (b) the scope of the accreditation of the laboratory includes the parameters that are determined.

paragraph: 17 The owner or operator of a wastewater system must keep the report on each determination made by an accredited laboratory referred to in section 16 and a record that contains the following information:

paragraph: (a) for any final discharge point,

paragraph: (iv) the average daily volume of effluent deposited annually, expressed in m3, determined in accordance with subsection 8(1), if applicable;

paragraph: (b) for each combined sewer overflow point via which effluent is deposited because of precipitation, including the melting of snow or ice, that resulted in excess wastewater in the wastewater system,

paragraph: (A) the daily volume of the effluent deposited, expressed in m3, if that volume is yielded by a continuous measure, and

heading: Information to be recorded
paragraph: (B) the estimated daily volume of the effluent deposited, expressed in m3, in any other case,

heading: Information to be recorded
paragraph: (c) for any monitoring equipment referred to in section 9,

paragraph: (i) a description, including its type,
