paragraph: (b) implement the plan referred to in subsection 4(1) or paragraphs 25(1)(f) or (s) or, if applicable, the amended plan referred to in subsection (3) - in accordance with its schedule for implementation.

heading: Progress reports
paragraph: (2) The holder of a transitional authorization must, within 90 days before the following dates, send to the authorization officer a progress report on the steps taken to implement the plan referred to in subsection 4(1) or paragraph 25(1)(f) or (s), as the case may be:

heading: Progress reports
paragraph: (a) July 1 of 2026, 2028 and 2030, if the period of authorization ends on December 31, 2030; and

heading: Progress reports
paragraph: (b) July 1 of 2026, 2028, 2030, 2032, 2034, 2036, 2038 and 2040, if the period of authorization ends on December 31, 2040.

heading: Compliance obligations - amended plan
paragraph: (3) The progress report must include amendments to the plan referred to in subsection 4(1) or paragraph 25(1)(f) or (s), as the case may be, along with a schedule to implement the plan.

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: 30 A transitional authorization must be in the form set out in Schedule 4 and contain the following information:

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (a) the information referred to in paragraphs 25(1)(a) and (c);

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (b) the latitude and longitude of the final discharge point;

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (c) the date of issuance;

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (d) the period of authorization; and

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (e) the following averages and maximum concentration of the deleterious substances prescribed in section 5 that are authorized to be contained in effluent that is deposited via the final discharge point during a given calendar year, quarter or month referred to in subsection 28(1):

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (i) for the average carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand due to the quantity of CBOD matter, the average referred to in, as the case may be, subparagraph 28(1)(a)(i) or (ii),

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (ii) for the average concentration of suspended solids, the average referred to in, as the case may be, subparagraph 28(1)(b)(i) or (ii),

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (iii) for the average concentration of total residual chlorine, the average referred to in paragraph 28(1)(c), and

heading: Content of transitional authorization
paragraph: (iv) for the maximum concentration of un-ionized ammonia, the maximum concentration referred to in, as the case may be, subparagraph 28(1)(d)(i) or (ii).

heading: Correction of information
paragraph: 31 (1) If the owner or operator of a wastewater system becomes aware that the information provided in their application for a transitional authorization contains errors or if the information provided in the transitional authorization is incorrect, they must, without delay, send a notice to the authorization officer that indicates the reason for the incorrect information and any corrections made, along with a corrected statement referred to in paragraph 25(1)(t).

heading: Corrected transitional authorization
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a notice that provides corrections that, if provided with the application, would have affected the scope of the information referred to in section 30 contained in the transitional authorization, the authorization officer must issue a corrected transitional authorization as if the corrections together with the remaining information originally provided in the application were an application under section 25.

heading: Change in ownership
paragraph: (3) A new owner or operator of a wastewater system must, no later than 30 days after the day on which the ownership of the wastewater system is transferred, send a notice to the authorization officer that indicates the date on which the transfer occurred and any updates to the information referred to in paragraphs 25(1)(a) to (c), along with a corrected statement referred to in paragraph 25(1)(t) signed and dated by the new owner or operator or their authorized representative.

heading: Amended transitional authorization
paragraph: (4) On receipt of a notice referred to in subsection (3), the authorization officer must issue an amended transitional authorization with the updates to the information referred to in paragraphs 30(a) and (c).

heading: Revocation
paragraph: 32 (1) The authorization officer may revoke a transitional authorization if

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (a) the information referred to in subsection 25(1) or (2), as the case may be, contained in the application or the information provided in a progress report referred to in subsection 29(2) is false or misleading in a material respect;

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (b) the holder has, during the period of authorization, failed to comply with any condition set out in section 28 or any provision referred to in subsection 29(1);

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (c) new information indicates that a deposit authorized under section 28 has had or is likely to have an effect on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish that is more adverse than the worst of the effects that were anticipated when that authorization was issued;

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (d) the holder has not sent a progress report in accordance with subsection 29(2); or

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (e) the authorization officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the plan referred to in subsection 4(1) or paragraph 25(1)(f) or (s) or subsection 29(3), as the case may be, cannot be fully implemented before the end of the period of authorization.

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (2) When determining whether to revoke a transitional authorization, the authorization officer must consider, as applicable, whether the holder of a transitional authorization

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (a) has a history of non-compliance with any condition or provision referred to in paragraph (1)(b);

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (b) has provided a reasonable justification for not sending a progress report in accordance with subsection 29(2); or

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (c) has carried out, or signed an undertaking to carry out, specified corrective measures to ensure compliance with any condition or provision referred to in paragraph (1)(b) or to prevent or mitigate a more adverse effect referred to in paragraph (1)(c).

heading: Representations
paragraph: (3) The authorization officer is not permitted to revoke a transitional authorization unless they have provided the holder with

heading: Representations
paragraph: (a) written reasons for the proposed revocation; and

heading: Representations
paragraph: (b) an opportunity to be heard, by written representation, in respect of the proposed revocation.

heading: Transitional authorization - termination
paragraph: 33 (1) Despite subsections 24(2) and 26(2), the authorization officer may terminate a transitional authorization at the end of a given calendar year, quarter or month determined in accordance with subsection 6(2), if the effluent deposited via the final discharge point of the wastewater system was not acutely lethal and if it met the conditions for the authorization set out in paragraphs 6(1)(a) and (b) during

heading: Transitional authorization - termination
paragraph: (a) that given calendar year;

heading: Transitional authorization - termination
paragraph: (b) that given quarter and the three quarters immediately before that given quarter during which effluent was deposited via the final discharge point; or

heading: Transitional authorization - termination
paragraph: (c) that given month and each of the 11 months immediately before that given month during which effluent was deposited via the final discharge point.

heading: Expiry of temporary authorization - notice
paragraph: (2) If the modifications to be made to a wastewater system are completed in accordance with the plan referred to in subsection 4(1) or paragraph 25(1)(f) or (s) or subsection 29(3), as the case may be, the owner or operator of the wastewater system must send a notice to the authorization officer that indicates the date on which the modifications were completed and certifies that the identification report has been updated in accordance with subsection 18(6).

heading: Requirements
paragraph: 34 (1) The owner or operator of a wastewater system whose effluent deposited via its final discharge point is acutely lethal because of the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in it may apply to an authorization officer for a temporary authorization to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia via the final discharge point if the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water, determined in accordance with subsection (3), at all points that are 100 m downstream from the point of entry where effluent is deposited in that water via the final discharge point is less than or equal to 0.016 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N), and if

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (a) the acute lethality of the effluent - as determined in accordance with Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 using the procedure set out in section 6 of that Method and the Procedure for pH Stabilization EPS 1/RM/50 - is primarily because of the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the effluent; or

heading: Requirements
paragraph: (b) the effluent is acutely lethal because the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the effluent deposited via the final discharge point is greater than or equal to 1.25 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N) at 15°C +/- 1°C, determined in accordance with section 14.

heading: Samples
paragraph: (2) The determination referred to in paragraph (1)(b) must

heading: Samples
paragraph: (a) for an intermittent wastewater system, be based on at least one sample of effluent; and

heading: Samples
paragraph: (b) for a continuous wastewater system, be based on at least two samples of effluent taken 7 days apart.

heading: Determination of NH3 concentration in water
paragraph: (3) The concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water referred to in subsection (1) must be determined in accordance with the following formula:

heading: Determination of NH3 concentration in water
paragraph: total ammonia * 1 / (1 +10pKa - pH)

heading: Determination of NH3 concentration in water
paragraph: where

heading: Determination of concentration of total ammonia in water
paragraph: (4) The concentration of total ammonia in the water referred to in subsection (3) must be determined using a total ammonia test.

heading: Periods for application
paragraph: (5) An initial application for a temporary authorization to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia must be made within 30 days after, as the case may be, the determination referred to in paragraph (1)(a) or (b) has been made. Applications to extend the temporary authorization must be made at least 90 days before the expiry of the authorization.

heading: Required information
paragraph: 35 An application for a temporary authorization to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia in respect of a wastewater system must contain the following information:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the owner's and the operator's name, civic and postal addresses, telephone number and, if any, email address and fax number;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the name, title, civic and postal addresses, telephone number and, if any, email address and fax number, of a contact person;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (c) if any, the wastewater system's name and civic address;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (d) the latitude and longitude of the final discharge point expressed in decimal degrees in accordance with subsection 18(3);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (e) in relation to the determination of the acute lethality of the effluent

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) if that determination is the one referred to in paragraph 34(1)(a),

heading: Required information
paragraph: (A) the result of that determination, including, for each sample on which that determination was based, the information referred to in section 8.1 of Reference Method EPS 1/RM/13 and section 3 of the Procedure for pH Stabilization EPS 1/RM/50, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (B) information establishing that, when that determination was made, any acute lethality of the effluent was primarily because of the concentration of the un-ionized ammonia in the effluent, or

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii) if that determination is the one referred to in paragraph 34(1)(b), the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in each of the samples referred to in subsection 34(2);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (f) information that establishes that, at the time the application was made, the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water, determined in accordance with subsection 34(3), at any point that is 100 m downstream from the point of entry where effluent is deposited in that water via the final discharge point was less than or equal to 0.016 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N); and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (g) a statement signed and dated by the owner or operator or their authorized representative that certifies that the information provided in the application is true, accurate and complete

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) in the case of information that was prepared by the owner or operator, to the best of the owner's or operator's information and belief, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii) in the case of information that was prepared by other persons with sufficient knowledge to evaluate that information, to the best of the owner's or operator's information and belief, based on representations made to them by those persons.

heading: Required information
paragraph: 36 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the authorization officer must issue the temporary authorization to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia for a period of three years beginning on the date of issuance, if

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the application contains the information required under section 35;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the information referred to in paragraph 35(e) has established that the effluent was, at the time of the application, acutely lethal because of the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in it; and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (c) the information referred to in paragraph 35(f) has established that the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water, determined in accordance with subsection 34(3), at any point that is 100 m downstream from the point of entry where effluent was deposited in that water via the final discharge point was less than or equal to 0.016 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N).

heading: Refusal
paragraph: (2) The authorization officer must refuse to issue the temporary authorization if they have reasonable grounds to believe that the information contained in, or provided in support of, the application is false or misleading in a material respect.

heading: Authorized deposits
paragraph: 37 A holder of a temporary authorization to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia in respect of a wastewater system is authorized to deposit, via the final discharge point, effluent

heading: Authorized deposits
paragraph: (a) that satisfies the conditions set out in paragraphs 6(1)(a) to (c); and

heading: Authorized deposits
paragraph: (b) that results in a concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water that is less than or equal to 0.016 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N), determined in accordance with subsection 34(3), at all points that are 100 m downstream from the point of entry where effluent is deposited in that water via the final discharge point.

heading: General requirements
paragraph: 38 The holder of a temporary authorization to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia must, at the final discharge point, during the period of authorization

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (a) comply with sections 7 to 10, 12 to 14, 16 to 22 and 48;

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (b) for each sample as referred to in subsection 10(1) to (4), determine, or cause the determination of, the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the effluent, in accordance with section 14; and

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (c) once each August, determine, or cause the determination of, the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water referred to in paragraph 37(b).

heading: Period and content
paragraph: 39 A temporary authorization, and any extension of it, to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia must be in the form set out in Schedule 5 and contain the following information:

heading: Period and content
paragraph: (a) the information referred to in paragraphs 35(a) and (c);

heading: Period and content
paragraph: (b) the latitude and longitude of the final discharge point;

heading: Period and content
paragraph: (c) the date of issuance of the temporary authorization and of any extension of it;

heading: Period and content
paragraph: (d) the period of authorization; and

heading: Period and content
paragraph: (e) a statement that the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water must be less than or equal to 0.016 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N), determined in accordance with subsection 34(3), at all points that are 100 m downstream from the point of entry where effluent is deposited in that water via the final discharge point.

heading: Extension
paragraph: 40 (1) A temporary authorization may, on application, be extended for successive periods of three years. If that application is based on a determination of the acute lethality of effluent referred to in paragraph 34(1)(a), it must contain the information referred to in subparagraph 35(e)(i).

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (2) The authorization officer must - based on the information contained in the application for the extension, the monitoring reports sent under subsection 19(1) and the original application for the temporary authorization referred to in section 35 - extend the authorization if it is established that, when the application for an extension was made,

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (a) the effluent was acutely lethal because of the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in it; and

heading: Issuance
paragraph: (b) the concentration of un-ionized ammonia in the water, determined in accordance with subsection 34(3), at any point that is 100 m downstream from the point of entry where effluent was deposited in that water via the final discharge point was less than or equal to 0.016 mg/L, expressed as nitrogen (N).

heading: Correction of information
paragraph: 41 (1) If the owner or operator becomes aware that the information provided in an application for a temporary authorization, or for an extension of a temporary authorization, contains errors, they must, without delay, send a notice to the authorization officer, which indicates the reason for the errors and provides corrections, and make the certification under paragraph 35(g) with respect to the corrected application.

heading: Corrected temporary authorization
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a notice that provides corrections that, if provided with the application, would have affected the scope of the information referred to in section 39, the authorization officer must issue a corrected temporary authorization or corrected extension of a temporary authorization, as the case may be, as if the corrections together with the remaining information originally provided in the application were an application under section 35 or 40.

heading: Revocation
paragraph: 42 (1) The authorization officer may revoke a temporary authorization, or an extended temporary authorization, to deposit effluent that contains un-ionized ammonia if

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (a) the information contained in, as the case may be, the application for the temporary authorization referred to in section 35 or the application for the extended temporary authorization referred to in 40 is false or misleading in a material respect;

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (b) the holder has, during the period of authorization, failed to comply with paragraph 37(a) or (b), any section referred to in paragraph 38(a), or paragraph 38(b) or (c); or

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (c) new information indicates that a deposit under the temporary authorization or the extended temporary authorization has had or is likely to have an effect on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish that is more adverse than the worst of those effects that were anticipated when that authorization was issued.

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (2) When determining whether to revoke a temporary authorization or an extended temporary authorization, the authorization officer must consider, as applicable, whether the holder

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (a) has a history of non-compliance with any provision referred to in paragraph (1)(b); or

heading: Considerations
paragraph: (b) has carried out, or signed an undertaking to carry out, specified corrective measures to ensure compliance with any provision referred to in paragraph (1)(b) or to prevent or mitigate a more adverse effect referred to in paragraph (1)(c).

heading: Representations
paragraph: (3) The authorization officer is not permitted to revoke a temporary authorization or an extended temporary authorization unless they have provided the holder with

heading: Representations
paragraph: (a) written reasons for the proposed revocation; and

heading: Representations
paragraph: (b) an opportunity to be heard, by written representation, in respect of the proposed revocation.

heading: Deposit without or with partial treatment
paragraph: 43 (1) An owner or operator of a wastewater system may apply to an authorization officer for a temporary authorization to bypass at least one of the treatment processes normally applied to wastewater in the system and, as a result, to deposit effluent that contains any deleterious substance prescribed in section 5.

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (2) An application for a temporary bypass authorization is not to be made unless

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (a) the requirement to bypass those treatment processes arises from

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (i) construction work to make changes to the system,

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (ii) the maintenance of the system, or

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (iii) the response to an anticipated event that is beyond the control of the owner or operator of the system;

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (b) the bypass is designed, within the constraints of technical and economic feasibility, to minimize the volume of effluent deposited and the concentration of deleterious substances prescribed in section 5 in the effluent deposited;

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (c) notice of the proposed bypass has been given to members of the public and to any community or Indigenous governing body, if the owner or operator has reasonable grounds to believe that the member, community or governing body could be affected by the bypass or may have used or may use the receiving environment before, during or after the bypass; and

heading: Conditions precedent
paragraph: (d) notice of the proposed bypass has been given to the National Manager of the Shellfish Water Classification Program, Department of the Environment, if the proposed bypass will result in the deposit of effluent in open marine waters or marine port waters, as defined in Schedule 2, or a shellfish harvesting area or within a radius of 20 km of such an area or such waters.

heading: Period for application
paragraph: (3) An application for a temporary bypass authorization must be made at least

heading: Period for application
paragraph: (a) 21 days before the day on which the requirement referred to in paragraph (2)(a) is to arise, if the bypass is a Category 1 bypass as determined in accordance with sections 43.2 to 43.4;

heading: Period for application
paragraph: (b) 45 days before the day on which the requirement referred to in paragraph (2)(a) is to arise, if the bypass is a Category 2 bypass as determined in accordance with sections 43.2 to 43.4; or

heading: Period for application
paragraph: (c) 90 days before the day on which the requirement referred to in paragraph (2)(a) is to arise, if the bypass is a Category 3 bypass as determined in accordance with sections 43.2 to 43.4.

heading: Bypass Categories for Temporary Bypass Authorizations
paragraph: Physical or biological treatment

heading: Bypass Categories for Temporary Bypass Authorizations
paragraph: 43.1 For the purposes of sections 43.2 and 43.3, physical or biological treatment means any treatment process, other than preliminary treatment, applied to wastewater for the purpose of removing suspended solids or CBOD matter, or both, from the influent.

heading: Bypass category determination - physical or biological treatment
paragraph: 43.2 (1) If the effluent deposited during the proposed bypass has undergone a physical or biological treatment, the determination of the bypass category for the purpose of obtaining a temporary bypass authorization is made in accordance with subsections (2) to (4).

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (2) The bypass is a Category 1 bypass if

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (a) the estimated volume of the deposits is equal to or less than 25 000 m3 and the approximate duration referred to in paragraph 44(1)(g) is equal to or less than 240 hours; and

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (b) the bypass is at a final discharge point or at one or more overflow points, and all of those points of entry are in a water or place that regularly receives wastewater during normal conditions.

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (3) The bypass is a Category 3 bypass if

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (a) the estimated volume of the deposits is greater than 500 000 m3 or the approximate duration referred to in paragraph 44(1)(g) is greater than 2 160 hours; and

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (b) any of the following conditions apply:

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (i) a shellfish harvesting area is within 1 500 m of any point of entry where effluent is deposited during the bypass via any final discharge point or one or more overflow points, or

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (ii) an identified critical habitat for species referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition protected aquatic species is within 500 m of any point of entry where effluent is deposited during the bypass via any final discharge point or one or more overflow points.

heading: Category 2 bypass
paragraph: (4) The bypass is a Category 2 bypass if it does not meet the requirements set out in subsection (2) or (3).

heading: Bypass category determination - no physical or biological treatment
paragraph: 43.3 (1) If the effluent deposited during the proposed bypass has not undergone a physical or biological treatment, the determination of the bypass category for the purpose of obtaining a temporary bypass authorization is made in accordance with subsections (2) to (4).

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (2) The bypass is a Category 1 bypass if

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (a) the estimated volume of the deposits is equal to or less than 2 500 m3 or the approximate duration referred to in paragraph 44(1)(g) is equal to or less than 48 hours;

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (b) the bypass is at a final discharge point or at one or more overflow points, and all of those points of entry are in a water or place that regularly receives wastewater during normal conditions; and

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (c) the bypass does not qualify as a category 3 bypass.

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (3) The bypass is a Category 3 bypass if

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (a) the estimated volume of the deposits is greater than 50 000 m3 or the approximate duration referred to in paragraph 44(1)(g) is greater than 720 hours; or

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (b) the estimated volume of the deposits is greater than 25 000 m3 or the approximate duration referred to in paragraph 44(1)(g) is greater than 360 hours, and any of the following conditions apply:

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (i) a shellfish harvesting area is within 1 500 m of any point of entry where effluent is deposited during the bypass via any final discharge point or one or more overflow points, or

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (ii) an identified critical habitat for species referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition protected aquatic species is within 500 m of any point of entry where effluent is deposited during the bypass via any final discharge point or one or more overflow points.

heading: Category 2 bypass
paragraph: (4) The bypass is a Category 2 bypass if it does not meet the requirements set out in subsection (2) or (3).

heading: Category 2 bypass
paragraph: Precipitation event

heading: Category 2 bypass
paragraph: 43.4 (1) For the purposes of this section, precipitation event means an accumulation of precipitation, other than from melting snow or ice, that causes a temporary surcharge in the wastewater system because of a reduced capacity due to the construction work, the maintenance of the system or the response referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a) and results in a deposit of untreated wastewater mixed with surface runoff and stormwater.

heading: Bypass category determination - precipitation events during period of reduced capacity
paragraph: (2) If the effluent deposited during the proposed bypass is caused by one or more precipitation events that occur during a period of reduced capacity of the wastewater system, the determination of the bypass category for the purpose of obtaining a temporary bypass authorization is made in accordance with subsections (3) to (5).

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (3) The bypass is a Category 1 bypass if

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (a) the estimated volume of the deposits is equal to or less than 5 000 m3 or the period referred to in paragraph 44(1)(f) is equal to or less than 96 hours;

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (b) the bypass is at a final discharge point or at one or more overflow points, and all of those points of entry are in a water or place that regularly receives wastewater during normal conditions; and

heading: Category 1 bypass
paragraph: (c) the bypass does not qualify as a category 3 bypass.

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (4) The bypass is a Category 3 bypass if

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (a) the estimated volume of the deposits is greater than 100 000 m3 or the period referred to in paragraph 44(1)(f) is greater than 1 440 hours; and

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (b) any of the following conditions apply:

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (i) a shellfish harvesting area is within 1 500 m of any point of entry where effluent is deposited during the bypass via any final discharge point or one or more overflow points, or

heading: Category 3 bypass
paragraph: (ii) an identified critical habitat for species referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition protected aquatic species is within 500 m of any point of entry where effluent is deposited during the bypass via any final discharge point or at one or more overflow points.

heading: Category 2 bypass
paragraph: (5) The bypass is a Category 2 bypass if it does not meet the requirements set out in subsection (3) or (4).

heading: Required information
paragraph: 44 (1) An application for a temporary bypass authorization must contain the following information:

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the owner's and the operator's name, civic and postal addresses, telephone number and, if any, email address and fax number;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the name, title, civic and postal addresses, telephone number and, if any, email address and fax number, of a contact person;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (c) if any, the wastewater system's name and civic address;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (c.1) a description of the construction work, the maintenance of the system or the response referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a), as well as

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) an explanation that demonstrates why it is necessary to bypass at least one of the treatment processes normally applied to the wastewater in the system, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii) in the case of an application by an owner or operator who had to confirm the existence of a plan referred to in paragraph 45.2(3)(f) for a previous authorization, an explanation that demonstrates how the bypass meets the requirements of that plan and any amendments to that plan since it was created;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (d) an explanation of how the bypass is designed to minimize the volume of effluent deposited and the concentration of deleterious substances prescribed in section 5 in the effluent deposited during the construction work, the maintenance of the system or the response referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a), including a description of, and a schedule for, all steps that are to be taken to achieve that minimization;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (e) the latitude and longitude, expressed in decimal degrees in accordance with subsection 18(3), of

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) any final discharge points, if the bypass results in the deposit of effluent via one or more of the system's final discharge points, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii) any overflow points, if the bypass results or may result in wastewater being diverted for deposit in any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (e.1) a description of any water or place referred to in subsection 36(3) of the Act into which effluent is deposited, including

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) the use, if any, of the water or place,

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii) the name, if any, of the water or place and, in the case of water, the name, if any, of the body of water that includes the water, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (iii) for an overflow point, a statement indicating whether the water or place regularly receives wastewater under normal conditions;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (f) the period for which the bypass is required in order to allow for the construction work, for the maintenance of the system or for the response referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (g) the approximate duration, expressed in hours, of the deposits referred to in subparagraph (e)(i) or (ii) or both;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (h) the estimated volume, expressed in m3, of those deposits, and an explanation of how the estimation was made;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (h.1) a description of the treatment, if any, that will be applied to effluent prior to deposit and whether deposits will be caused by precipitation events occurring during a period of reduced capacity of the wastewater system, as defined in subsection 43.4(1);

heading: Required information
paragraph: (h.2) a list of the measures that will be implemented to avoid or mitigate the adverse effects of the bypass on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish, including the choice of appropriate timing for the proposed work to reduce the risk of harm;

heading: Required information
paragraph: (h.3) a description and the results of notifications to and engagement with any members of the public, communities, or Indigenous governing bodies that may be impacted by the proposed bypass; and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) a statement signed and dated by the owner or operator or their authorized representative that certifies that the information provided in the application is true, accurate and complete

heading: Required information
paragraph: (i) in the case of information that was prepared by the owner or operator, to the best of the owner's or operator's information and belief, and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (ii) in the case of information that was prepared by other persons with sufficient knowledge to evaluate that information, to the best of the owner's, operator's or authorized representative's information and belief, based on representations made to them by those persons.

heading: Additional information - risk level
paragraph: (2) In addition to the information referred to in subsection (1), an application for a temporary bypass authorization must contain the following information:

heading: Additional information - risk level
paragraph: (a) for a Category 2 bypass, a detailed description of the measures referred to in paragraph (1)(h.2);

heading: Additional information - risk level
paragraph: (b) for a Category 3 bypass,

heading: Additional information - risk level
paragraph: (i) a detailed description of the measures referred to in paragraph (1)(h.2),

heading: Additional information - risk level
paragraph: (ii) an assessment of the methods that were considered but not retained to avoid or minimize the bypass, including their technical feasibility and an estimate of costs,

heading: Additional information - risk level
paragraph: (iii) an assessment of the geographical scope where the effluent mixes with the receiving environment and where there is a distinguishable difference from the ambient water conditions, as well as a description of the methodologies used to prepare the assessment, and

heading: Additional information - risk level
paragraph: (iv) a detailed description of the monitoring of the effluent or of the receiving environment based on the assessment of the geographical scope referred to in subparagraph (iii) that will be implemented to assess the effectiveness of the measures referred to in paragraph (1)(h.2), including a detailed plan and schedule for monitoring before, during and after the bypass occurs.

heading: Additional information - on demand
paragraph: (3) The authorization officer may request additional information from an applicant if that information is required to assess the potential adverse effects of the bypass on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish.

heading: Additional information - written notice
paragraph: (4) In accordance with subsection (3), the authorization officer must provide the applicant with a written notice setting out the information to be provided and the timeline for providing it.

heading: Required information
paragraph: 45 (1) Subject to subsection (3), the authorization officer must issue a temporary bypass authorization if

heading: Required information
paragraph: (a) the authorization officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the conditions set out in subsection 43(2) are met; and

heading: Required information
paragraph: (b) the application contains the information required under subsection 44(1) and, if applicable, subsections 44(2) and (3).

heading: Duration of temporary bypass authorization
paragraph: (2) The temporary bypass authorization is to be issued for the period that, in the authorization officer's opinion,

heading: Duration of temporary bypass authorization
paragraph: (a) is required in order to allow for the construction work, for the maintenance of the system or for the response referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a); and

heading: Duration of temporary bypass authorization
paragraph: (b) will mitigate any adverse effects on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish to the extent possible given the requirement referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a) for which the bypass authorization arises.

heading: Refusal - adverse effects
paragraph: (3) The authorization officer may refuse to issue the temporary authorization if they have reasonable grounds to believe that its issuance, for any period, would result in adverse effects on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish that cannot be mitigated.

heading: Refusal - false or misleading information
paragraph: (4) The authorization officer must refuse to issue the temporary authorization if they have reasonable grounds to believe that the information contained in, or provided in support of, the application is false or misleading in a material respect.

heading: Authorized deposit
paragraph: 45.1 A holder of a temporary bypass authorization in respect of a wastewater system is authorized to deposit effluent if the mitigation and monitoring measures referred to in paragraphs 44(1)(h.1) and (h.2) and subparagraph 44(2)(b)(iv), as applicable, are implemented.

heading: General requirements
paragraph: 45.2 (1) An owner or operator of a wastewater system who holds a temporary bypass authorization must, during the period of authorization, comply with,

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (a) if the bypass occurs only at one or more overflow points,

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (i) sections 5 to 19, 21, 22 and 48 for the effluent deposited via all the final discharge points of the wastewater system; and

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (ii) paragraph 17(b) and section 20 for the effluent deposited via all the combined sewer overflow points of the wastewater system,

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (b) if the bypass occurs at at least one final discharge point,

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (i) sections 7 to 10, subsections 11(1) to (3) and (7), sections 12 to 19, 21, 22 and 48 for the effluent deposited via all the final discharge points of the wastewater system; and

heading: General requirements
paragraph: (ii) paragraph 17(b) and section 20 for the effluent deposited via all the combined sewer overflow points of the wastewater system.

heading: Exemption - daily volume
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if, during the period of authorization, the volume or rate of flow of the influent or effluent cannot be measured in accordance with section 9, the holder of a temporary authorization may determine the daily volume of effluent by using a method of estimation in accordance with subsection 7(4).

heading: Final report
paragraph: (3) The holder of a temporary bypass authorization must, within 90 days after the last day of the period of the authorization, send to the authorization officer a final report on the temporary bypass that includes the following information, as applicable:

heading: Final report
paragraph: (a) the actual duration of the deposits;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (b) the actual or estimated volume of the deposits;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (c) a description of any actual treatment applied to effluent;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (d) a description of how the mitigation and monitoring measures referred to in paragraphs 44(1)(h.1) and (h.2) have been implemented;

heading: Final report
paragraph: (e) the results of any monitoring referred to in subparagraph 44(2)(b)(iv) conducted during the bypass period; and

heading: Final report
paragraph: (f) for a Category 2 bypass as determined in accordance with sections 43.3 or 43.4 or a Category 3 bypass as determined in accordance with sections 43.2 to 43.4, a confirmation of the existence of a plan that describes modifications to be made to the wastewater system and any other measures to be taken to reduce the need for future temporary bypass authorizations and to limit any adverse effects on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish when performing work referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a), including a schedule for implementation of the plan.

heading: Examination
paragraph: (4) The holder of a temporary bypass authorization must ensure that the plan referred to in paragraph (3)(f) is available for examination by the public.

heading: Content of authorization
paragraph: 46 A temporary bypass authorization is to be issued for a period that is sufficient to allow for the construction work, for the maintenance of the system or for the response referred to in paragraph 43(2)(a) and the authorization must be in the form set out in Schedule 6.

heading: Correction of information
paragraph: 47 (1) If the holder of the temporary authorization becomes aware that the information provided in their application for a temporary bypass authorization contains errors, they must, without delay, send a notice to the authorization officer that indicates the reason for the errors and provides corrections, along with a corrected statement referred to in paragraph 44(1)(i).

heading: Corrected authorization
paragraph: (2) On receipt of the notice and the corrections, the authorization officer may only issue a corrected temporary bypass authorization if

heading: Corrected authorization
paragraph: (a) the corrected bypass category, as determined in accordance with sections 43.2 to 43.4, remains the same as that of the original application; or,

heading: Corrected authorization
paragraph: (b) the corrected bypass category, as determined in accordance with sections 43.2 to 43.4, changes from that in the original application as a result of the corrections, and the additional information required under the corrected bypass application has been provided.

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (3) The authorization officer may revoke a temporary bypass authorization if

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (a) the information contained in the application referred to in subsections 44(1) to (3), as the case may be, is false or misleading in a material respect;

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (b) during the period of authorization, the holder has failed to comply with the conditions set out in section 45.1 or any obligation set out in subsection 45.2(1); or

heading: Revocation
paragraph: (c) new information indicates that a deposit under the temporary bypass authorization has had or is likely to have an effect on fish, fish habitat or the use by man of fish that is more adverse than the worst of the effects that were anticipated when the authorization was issued.

heading: Representation
paragraph: (4) The authorization officer must not revoke a temporary authorization unless they have provided the holder with

heading: Representation
paragraph: (a) written reasons for the proposed revocation; and

heading: Representation
paragraph: (b) an opportunity to make written representations in respect of the proposed revocation.

heading: Electronic applications
paragraph: 48 (1) An application for a transitional authorization or a temporary authorization must be sent electronically in the form and format specified by the Minister of the Environment and must bear the electronic signature of the owner or operator or their authorized representative.

heading: Application on paper
paragraph: (2) If the Minister of the Environment has not specified an electronic form and format or if it is not feasible to send the application electronically in accordance with subsection (1) because of circumstances beyond the control of the owner or operator, or their authorized representative, the application must be sent on paper, signed by the owner or operator, or their authorized representative, and in the form and format specified by that Minister.

heading: On registration
paragraph: 50 (1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), these Regulations come into force on the day on which they are registered.

heading: January 1, 2013
paragraph: (2) Subsections 6(2) to (6), sections 7, 8, 10, 12 to 14 and 16, paragraphs 17(a), (b) and (d) to (g) and sections 18 to 20, 23 to 27, 30, 31, 34 to 36, 39, 41, 48 and 49 come into force on January 1, 2013.

paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), paragraphs 6(1)(c) and 28(1)(c) come into force on January 1, 2021 in relation to an owner or operator of a wastewater system that has, on the day on which these Regulations are registered, an average daily volume of effluent deposited annually via its final discharge point of less than 5 000 m3, determined on the basis of its average design rate of flow of influent.

heading: Purpose
paragraph: 2		  The purpose of this Act is to foster sustainable use of British Columbia's water resources in continuation of the objectives of conserving and protecting the environment.

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph:
4
		  (1) Except for a registered licence, no authorization, change approval or permit under the Water Sustainability Act or a former Act, whether issued before, on or after the date this section comes into force, confers any right

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph: (a) to drill for, divert or use water for removal from British Columbia,

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph: (b) to dispose of or sell water to a person for removal from British Columbia,

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph: (c) to convey or transport water for removal from British Columbia,

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph: (d) to remove water from British Columbia, or

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph: (e) of property in respect of water removed or intended to be removed from British Columbia.

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph: (2) A person who, in British Columbia, diverts unrecorded water does not have, and does not by diverting the water acquire, any of the rights described in subsection (1) (a) to (e).

heading: B.C. water removal restriction
paragraph: (3) Despite any other enactment, a person who acquires water originating in British Columbia from another person, whether directly or indirectly, does not, by that acquisition, acquire any of the rights described in subsection (1) (a) to (e).

heading: Prohibition against B.C. water removal
paragraph: 5		  A person must not remove water from British Columbia unless the person

heading: Prohibition against B.C. water removal
paragraph: (a) is a registrant under a registered licence that remains in effect and complies with the registered licence,

heading: Prohibition against B.C. water removal
paragraph: (c) removes the water in containers of 20 litres capacity or less, of water that has been packaged in British Columbia, or

heading: Prohibition against B.C. water removal
paragraph: (d) obtained the water outside British Columbia and, at the time of the removal, is in possession of evidence satisfactory to the comptroller to that effect.

heading: Prohibition against large scale transfers between major watersheds
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A person must not construct or operate a large scale project capable of transferring water from one major watershed to another major watershed.

heading: Prohibition against large scale transfers between major watersheds
paragraph: (2) A person must not modify a project capable of diverting water if the modification results in, or if completed would result in, the project having the capability of transferring water at a peak instantaneous flow of 10 m3 or more a second from one major watershed to another major watershed.

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph:
7
		  (1) Despite the Water Sustainability Act and the regulations under that Act, but subject to subsection (2), the comptroller or a water manager must not issue an authorization, change approval or permit that allows a person to

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (a) remove water from British Columbia,

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (b) divert water for removal to an area outside British Columbia,

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (c) construct or operate a large scale project capable of transferring water from one major watershed to another major watershed, or

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (d) modify a project contrary to section 6 (2).

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to the issuance of a licence under

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (a) section 25 [transition - unlicensed registrants] of this Act, or

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (b) the Water Sustainability Act in substitution for a registered licence.

heading: No further authorizations for B.C. water removal
paragraph: (3) An authorization, change approval or permit issued contrary to subsection (1) has no effect.

heading: Exception for water to be used in transit
paragraph: 8		  Nothing in this Act prohibits the removal of water from British Columbia in the ordinary course of carrying the water in vehicles, vessels or aircraft for the use of persons or animals while the persons or animals, as the case may be, are being transported in the vehicles, vessels or aircraft.

heading: Register for continuing water removal
paragraph:
9
		  (1) The comptroller must maintain for the purposes of this Act a register and must record in the register

heading: Register for continuing water removal
paragraph: (a) the name and address of each registrant,

heading: Register for continuing water removal
paragraph: (b) for each registrant, a copy of the relevant registered licence, and

heading: Register for continuing water removal
paragraph: (c) other information that the Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe.

heading: Register for continuing water removal
paragraph: (2) The comptroller must publish the register by posting the register on a publicly accessible website or in another manner that ensures accessibility to the public.

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph:
11
		  (0.1) The comptroller must amend the register, and make the changes in registration that the comptroller considers appropriate, in order to reflect

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (a) an amendment under the Water Sustainability Act of a registered licence, or a substitution under that Act of another licence for a registered licence, other than as provided for under subsection (1) or (2) of this section, or

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (b) the suspension, cancellation, abandonment or expiry under the Water Sustainability Act of a registered licence.

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (1) On the disposition to any person of the whole or any part of any land, mine or undertaking to which a registered licence has been made appurtenant under the Water Sustainability Act, the comptroller must,

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (a) in the case of a disposition of the whole, cancel the registration of the person making the disposition, and register the other person as the registrant in respect of that registered licence, or

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (b) in the case of a partial disposition, amend the registration of the person making the disposition to reflect the disposition and register the other person as a registrant in respect of the part disposed of to that other person.

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (2) On any transfer or apportionment, under the Water Sustainability Act, by the comptroller of the whole or part of the rights and obligations under a registered licence,

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (a) the comptroller must amend the register as the comptroller considers appropriate in order to reflect the transfer or apportionment, as the case may be, and

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (b) if the transfer or apportionment effects a transfer from the registrant to another person of the whole or part of the rights related to the registration of that registrant, the comptroller must,

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (i)  in the case of a transfer of the whole of those rights, cancel the registration of the registrant and register the other person as the registrant in respect of that registered licence, or

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of a partial transfer of those rights, amend the registration of the registrant to reflect the transfer of rights and register the other person as a registrant in respect of the part transferred to that other person.

heading: Amendments to register
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, nothing in this section affects the application of any provision of the Water Sustainability Act to or in respect of any licence under that Act that is a registered licence under this Act.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
17
		  (1) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or to the regulations.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence who

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) contravenes section 5 or 6 (1) or (2), or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) makes a statement in a record filed or provided under this Act that is false or misleading with respect to a material fact or that omits to state a material fact the omission of which makes the statement false or misleading.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) A person does not commit an offence under subsection (2) (b) if at the time of the statement the person did not know that the statement was false or misleading and, exercising due diligence, could not have known that the statement was false or misleading.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (4) A person who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) to a fine of not more than $200 000, and

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) if the offence is a continuing one, to a fine of not more than $200 000 for each day the offence is continued

heading: Offences
paragraph: or to imprisonment not exceeding 12 months, or to both a fine and imprisonment.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (5) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence notwithstanding that the corporation is convicted.

heading: Offences
paragraph: (6) An information for or in respect of any offence against this Act or the regulations must be laid before the expiration of one year from the time of the happening of the offence.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: 18		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under section 17 and the court is satisfied that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any monetary benefits or that monetary benefits accrued to the person, the court may order the person to pay a fine equal to the court's estimation of the amount of those monetary benefits.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: (2) A fine under subsection (1) is in addition to and not in place of a fine under section 17.

heading: Remedies preserved
paragraph:
19
		  A conviction or penalty for an offence under this Act does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Power to stop and search vehicles, vessels and aircraft
paragraph:
20
		  An officer may

heading: Power to stop and search vehicles, vessels and aircraft
paragraph: (a) stop a person, including a person who is operating a vehicle, vessel or aircraft,

heading: Power to stop and search vehicles, vessels and aircraft
paragraph: (b) require the person to produce proof of identity, and

heading: Power to stop and search vehicles, vessels and aircraft
paragraph: (c) without warrant, search the vehicle, vessel or aircraft,

heading: Power to stop and search vehicles, vessels and aircraft
paragraph: if the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the person is contravening or has contravened this Act, and, at the request of the person, the officer must produce proof of the officer's identity.

heading: Duty to stop
paragraph:
21
		  A person must stop, and a person who is operating a vehicle, vessel or aircraft must stop the vehicle, vessel or aircraft, when required to do so by an officer who is acting under section 20 and who

heading: Duty to stop
paragraph: (a) is in uniform,

heading: Duty to stop
paragraph: (b) displays the officer's official badge, or

heading: Duty to stop
paragraph: (c) is in or near a vehicle that is readily identifiable as a ministry vehicle, police car, police motorcycle or other official vehicle.

heading: Duty to disclose identity
paragraph:
22
		  A person must provide proof of the person's identity when required to do so by an officer who is acting under section 20 and who displays the officer's official badge or produces other proof of the officer's identity.

heading: Orders for compliance
paragraph:
23
		  (1) If the minister considers that a person is not complying or has not complied with this Act, the minister may apply to the Supreme Court for either or both of the following:

heading: Orders for compliance
paragraph: (a) an order requiring the person to comply with this Act or restraining the person from violating this Act;

heading: Orders for compliance
paragraph: (b) an order requiring the directors and officers of the person to cause the person to comply with or to cease violating this Act.

heading: Orders for compliance
paragraph: (2) On application by the minister under this section, the Supreme Court may make an order it considers appropriate.

heading: Transition - licensed registrants
paragraph:
24
		  A person who, immediately before the date this section comes into force, is recorded in the register in the "licensed" category in respect of a licence is, on and after that date, conclusively deemed to be a registrant in respect of that licence.

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph:
25
		  (1) In this section, "successor registrant" means a person

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (a) to whom the registration of an unlicensed registrant passes, under section 13 (1) and (2) [unlicensed category - dispositions, transfers and apportionment], as that section applies under subsection (3) of this section, on a disposition of the whole or a part of the land, mine or undertaking to which the unlicensed registrant's registration is appurtenant, or

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (b) to whom the whole or a part of the rights and obligations associated with the registration of an unlicensed registrant is transferred, under section 13 (3) and (4), as that section applies under subsection (3) of this section, on a transfer or apportionment referred to in that section.

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (2) Unless a contrary intention appears, words and expressions used in this section have the same meaning as in this Act as it read immediately before this section comes into force.

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (3) Despite the amendments made to this Act by the Water Sustainability Act, this Act, as it read immediately before this section comes into force, continues to apply in relation to a person who was an unlicensed registrant at that time, or any person who, after that time, becomes a successor registrant,

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (a) if the person applies for an authorization within the period provided in subsection (4) of this section, until the date a decision is made on the application, and

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (b) if the person fails to apply for an authorization within that period, on the expiry of that period.

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (4) Despite section 140 (2) of the Water Sustainability Act, a person who, immediately before the date this section comes into force, is recorded in the register under this Act in the "unlicensed" category must, within 180 days of that date, apply to the comptroller for a licence authorizing the diversion and use of the maximum annual volume of groundwater specified in the report of the comptroller under section 14 of this Act, from the well or wells the locations of which are described in that report, as amended, if applicable, under section 16 (4) of this Act, as those sections apply under subsection (3) of this section, from the aquifer the location of which is described in that register in relation to the person.

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (5) Despite this Act, the comptroller must issue the licence applied for to a person who is required to apply and who applies in accordance with subsection (4), subject to prescribed terms and conditions and the terms and conditions the comptroller considers advisable.

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (6) A licence issued under subsection (5) has precedence for the purposes of section 22 (1) or (4) of the Water Sustainability Act from the person's date of first use, as defined in section 1 (1) of that Act, of groundwater from the aquifer and for the water use purpose to which the licence relates.

heading: Transition - unlicensed registrants
paragraph: (7) A person to whom subsection (4) applies is liable for the applicable fees, rentals or charges for the water diverted and used by the person on and after the date this section comes into force as if a licence were issued to the person on that date.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "agricultural land reserve" has the same meaning as in the Agricultural Land Commission Act;

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) undertake a structural change to a well related to the well's depth, diameter or screen assembly,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) install a surface seal in a well that does not have one, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) hydrofracture a well to enhance groundwater supply from the well;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "appeal board" means the Environmental Appeal Board continued under section 93 of the Environmental Management Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "applicant" means a person applying for

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an authorization, an amendment to an authorization, a transfer of the appurtenancy of an authorization or an apportionment of the rights under a licence,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a change approval, an amendment to a change approval or the transfer of the appurtenancy of a change approval,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a drilling authorization, an amendment to a drilling authorization or the transfer of the appurtenancy of a drilling authorization,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) the transfer of an application for an authorization, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) the abandonment of all or some of the person's rights under an authorization;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquatic ecosystem", in relation to a stream, means the natural environment of the stream, including

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the stream channel, the vegetation in the stream and the water in the stream, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) fish, wildlife and other living organisms insofar as their life processes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  are carried out in the stream, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  depend on the natural environment of the stream;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "aquifer" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a geological formation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a group of geological formations, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a part of one or more geological formations

heading: Definitions
paragraph: that is groundwater bearing and capable of storing, transmitting and yielding groundwater;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorization", except in references to drilling authorization, means a licence or use approval;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "beneficial use",

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to a use of water under an authorization, means using the water

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  as efficiently as practicable,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  in accordance with any applicable regulations, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  for the water use purposes, in the manner and in the period or at the times, authorized by the authorization, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to a use of water other than under an authorization, means using the water for a water use purpose

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  as efficiently as practicable,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  in accordance with any applicable regulations, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (iii)  in accordance with the provisions of this Act or the regulations that apply in relation to the use of water without an authorization;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "beneficial use declaration" means a declaration described in section 30 (2) [beneficial use];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "change approval" means an approval, to make changes in and about a stream, issued under section 11 (1) [changes in and about a stream] or a similar approval issued under a former Act;

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) any modification to the nature of a stream, including any modification to the land, vegetation and natural environment of a stream or the flow of water in a stream, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any activity or construction within a stream channel that has or may have an impact on a stream or a stream channel;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) drill the well,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) alter the well,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) develop the well,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) repair or maintain the well,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) inject water or any other substance into the well, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) construct, install, replace, repair, alter or remove works that relate to groundwater or the well;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "date of first use", in relation to a use of groundwater from an aquifer for a water use purpose, means the date from which the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer is satisfied in accordance with the regulations that groundwater from the aquifer has been used

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) regularly and beneficially on an ongoing basis,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) for the water use purpose, and

paragraph: "deactivate", in relation to works, means take the works out of service temporarily;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "debris" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) clay, silt, rock or similar material, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) any material, natural or otherwise, from construction or demolition;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "decision maker", in relation to a decision under this Act, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the person authorized to make the decision, and

heading: Definitions

paragraph: "development district" has the same meaning as "district" in section 58 [definitions] of the Drainage, Ditch and Dike Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to water in a stream, cause the water to leave the stream channel, whether to cause the water to flow into another stream channel or a reservoir or otherwise, and

paragraph: "drill", in relation to a well, means make the well by drilling, boring, driving, jetting or excavating;

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "drinking water officer" has the same meaning as in section 1 [definitions] of the Drinking Water Protection Act;

paragraph: "engineer", except in the definition of "professional" in section 48 [definitions for Division 3 of Part 3], means a person designated as an engineer under section 114 (5) [administration];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "farm use", subject to the regulations, has the same meaning as in section 1 (1) [definitions] of the Agricultural Land Commission Act;

paragraph: (a) the minister,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the provincial health officer appointed under the Public Health Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a prescribed minister, or

paragraph: (e) a prescribed government corporation;

paragraph: (ii)  that is either loose, or found in fragmentary or broken rock that is not talus rock and occurs in loose earth, gravel and sand, and includes rock or other materials from placer mine tailings, dumps and previously mined deposits of placer minerals, or

paragraph: (b) coal,

paragraph: "order" includes a decision or direction, whether or not the decision or direction is given in writing, but does not include a request;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "owner", in relation to land, a mine or an undertaking in British Columbia, means a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is entitled to possession of the land, mine or undertaking, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has a substantial interest in the land, mine or undertaking;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permit" means a permit issued under section 24 [permits over Crown land] or an authority, issued under a former Act, to flood, or to construct, maintain or operate works on, Crown land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "personal information" has the same meaning as in Schedule 1 of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "plan area" means the area designated under section 65 [order designating area for planning process] for the development of a water sustainability plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "precedence", in relation to rights to divert and use water, means the precedence of those rights in accordance with section 22 [precedence of rights];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "private dwelling" means a structure, or a part of a structure, that is occupied as a private residence;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "production casing", in relation to a well, means the innermost pipe, tubing or other material installed in the well to support the sides of the well, but does not include a well liner or surface casing;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "prospecting for a mineral" means searching for a mineral

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) using hand-held tools in a manner that does not involve mechanical disturbance of the surface, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in a prescribed manner;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protected fish population", in relation to a sensitive stream, means the population of fish in relation to which the stream has been designated as a sensitive stream;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "public officer" includes a member of the executive council, a public service employee and any other person, other than a judicial officer, who, under an enactment, has authority to make a decision affecting the rights of another person;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "public personal information" means any of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the name, address, telephone number and other personal information of a subscriber that appears in a telephone directory, in either printed or electronic form, or is available through a directory assistance service, if

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the directory or the directory assistance service is available to the public, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the subscriber is permitted to refuse to have the subscriber's personal information included in the directory or made available by the directory assistance service;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) personal information that appears in a professional or business directory, listing or notice that is available to the public, if the individual is permitted to refuse to have the individual's personal information included in the directory, listing or notice;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) personal information appearing in a registry to which the public has lawful access, if the personal information is collected under the authority of an enactment, the laws of the government of Canada or a province of Canada, or the bylaws of a municipality or other similar local authority in Canada;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) personal information that appears in a printed or electronic publication that is available to the public, including a magazine, book or newspaper in printed or electronic form, unless

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a court has prohibited the publication or continued publication of the personal information by the source, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the Information and Privacy Commissioner has made an order stating that the information was published contrary to the Personal Information Protection Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "public service employee" has the same meaning as "employee" in section 1 [definitions] of the Public Service Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualifying agricultural land" means all or the part of a plan area, to which a regulation under section 82 (1) [plan regulations - dedicated agricultural water] applies, that is

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in the agricultural land reserve, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) zoned to permit the use of the land for farm use under

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  a municipal or regional district bylaw under Divisions 5 and 12 to 14 of Part 14 [Planning and Land Use Management] of the Local Government Act or Part XXVII [Planning and Development] of the Vancouver Charter, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  a bylaw made by a local trust committee under section 29 [land use and subdivision regulation] of the Islands Trust Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "qualifying agricultural use" means the use of water for

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an irrigation purpose,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a prescribed industrial purpose, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a storage purpose associated with a purpose described in paragraph (a) or (b);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "recorded water" means water the right to the diversion or use of which is held under an authorization or another enactment;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "registrar", in relation to land, means the registrar appointed under the Land Title Act for the land title district in which the land is located;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sensitive stream" means a stream designated by regulation as a sensitive stream;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a natural watercourse, including a natural glacier course, or a natural body of water, whether or not the stream channel of the stream has been modified, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a natural source of water supply,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: including, without limitation, a lake, pond, river, creek, spring, ravine, gulch, wetland or glacier, whether or not usually containing water, including ice, but does not include an aquifer;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "stream channel", in relation to a stream, means the bed of the stream and the banks of the stream, both above and below the natural boundary and whether or not the channel has been modified, and includes side channels of the stream;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "take action",

heading: Definitions
