paragraph: (b) the gravity and magnitude of the contravention or failure;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (c) the extent of adverse impacts to the environment or the rights of other persons resulting from the contravention or failure;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (d) whether the contravention or failure was repeated or continuous;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (e) whether the contravention or failure was deliberate;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (f) any economic benefit derived by the person from the contravention or failure;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (g) the person's efforts to prevent and correct the contravention or failure;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (h) prescribed matters.

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (4) A person served with an administrative monetary penalty notice under subsection (2) is subject to an administrative monetary penalty as follows:

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (a) if the person admits, in writing, the contravention or failure as determined by the comptroller, the penalty indicated in the notice is imposed at the time of that admission;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (b) if the time for appealing the determination of a contravention or failure under Division 3 [Appeals] has elapsed and no appeal has been commenced, the penalty indicated in the notice is imposed at the end of the time for appealing;

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (c) if the determination of contravention or failure is appealed and, under the final determination of the appeal, the person is subject to an administrative monetary penalty, the penalty specified in the final determination is imposed at the time of that final determination.

heading: Administrative monetary penalties
paragraph: (5) An administrative monetary penalty under this section must be paid to the government within the prescribed period after the penalty is imposed and in accordance with any other prescribed requirements.

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph:
100
		  (1) Before delivering an administrative monetary penalty notice under section 99 (2), the comptroller must

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (a) deliver to the person a notice of intent to impose an administrative monetary penalty, and

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (b) provide the person with an opportunity to be heard.

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (2) An opportunity to be heard for the purposes of this section may be provided, as the comptroller considers appropriate in the circumstances, in writing, electronically or in person or by any combination of written, electronic or in-person hearings and if the comptroller decides to hold a hearing orally, either in person or electronically, sections 95 [inquiry powers], 96 [maintenance of order at hearings] and 97 [contempt proceeding for uncooperative person] apply.

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (3) A notice of intent to impose an administrative monetary penalty must set out

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (a) the alleged contravention or failure, including the provision of this Act or the regulations, the term or condition of the order or the term or condition of the authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization the person is alleged to have contravened and the circumstances of that contravention,

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (b) an estimate of the amount of the administrative monetary penalty to be imposed and the particulars under section 99 (3) on which the estimate is based, and

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (c) the time, date, place and manner of the oral hearing or the due date for written submissions.

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (4) A notice of intent to impose an administrative monetary penalty must be delivered to the person not less than 21 days before the date of a hearing or the due date of a submission under subsection (3) (c).

heading: Notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (5) On application, the comptroller may change a time, date, place or manner of hearing specified under subsection (3) (c).

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph:
101
		  (1) An administrative monetary penalty imposed under this Division may be recovered as a debt due to the government.

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to pay an administrative monetary penalty as required under this Act, the comptroller may file a certificate in a court that has jurisdiction and, on filing, the certificate has the same force and effect, and all proceedings may be taken on the certificate, as if it were a judgment of the court with which it is filed.

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (3) A certificate under subsection (2) must be signed by the comptroller and must contain

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (a) the name of the person who is liable for the penalty,

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (b) particulars of the administrative monetary penalty, and

heading: Recovery of penalties
paragraph: (c) the amount of the administrative monetary penalty.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph:
102
		  (1) The comptroller, in accordance with any applicable regulations, may enter into an agreement with a person

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (a) after the person has received a notice of intent to impose an administrative monetary penalty and made admissions in respect of one or more of the contraventions or failures in respect of which the notice was sent, or

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (b) after the person has received an administrative monetary penalty notice and made admissions in respect of one or more of the contraventions or failures in respect of which the administrative monetary penalty was imposed, but before the date the administrative monetary penalty is due under section 99 (5) [administrative monetary penalties].

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (2) An agreement under this section may provide, in accordance with the regulations, for the suspension of the notice of intent or for the reduction or suspension of the penalty, as applicable, subject to the terms and conditions the comptroller considers advisable, including, without limitation,

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (a) requiring compliance with this Act, the regulations, an order or the terms and conditions of an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization,

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (b) requiring remediation of adverse impacts that resulted from the contravention or failure in respect of which the administrative monetary penalty is imposed, or

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (c) if the comptroller considers the adverse impacts referred to in paragraph (b) cannot be remediated, or cannot be fully remediated, requiring compensatory mitigation measures, in place of or supplemental to the remediation of those adverse impacts, on a different part of the stream or aquifer in respect of which the contravention or failure occurred, or with the consent of the person, on a different stream or aquifer.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (3) An agreement under this section must specify the time for performing the terms and conditions, and if the person fails to perform those terms and conditions by the date specified,

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (a) if the notice of intent to impose an administrative monetary penalty under section 100 was suspended, the comptroller may deliver an administrative monetary penalty notice under section 99 for the contraventions or failures in respect of which an admission was made, and the penalty is due and payable upon delivery of the administrative monetary penalty notice, and

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (b) if an administrative money penalty was reduced or suspended, the administrative monetary penalty specified in the administrative monetary penalty notice under section 99 for any contraventions or failures in respect of which an admission was made is restored and is due and payable immediately upon a breach of the agreement.

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (4) The following decisions are final and may not be appealed to the appeal board:

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (a) the comptroller's decision whether to enter into a compliance agreement;

heading: Compliance agreements
paragraph: (b) the comptroller's decision as to the terms and conditions of a compliance agreement.

heading: Effect of imposing administrative monetary penalty
paragraph:
103
		  (1) If the comptroller issues a notice of intent to impose an administrative monetary penalty under section 100 [notice of intent to impose administrative monetary penalty] to a person in respect of a contravention or failure referred to in section 99 (1) [administrative monetary penalties], a prosecution for an offence under this Act in respect of the same contravention or failure may not be brought against the person.

heading: Effect of imposing administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (2) If a corporation

heading: Effect of imposing administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (a) contravenes a provision of this Act or the regulations prescribed under section 99 (1) (a), or

heading: Effect of imposing administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: (b) fails to comply with an order or the terms and conditions of an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization, as described under section 99 (1) (b) or (c), as applicable,

heading: Effect of imposing administrative monetary penalty
paragraph: an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the contravention or failure is also liable for an administrative monetary penalty whether or not an administrative monetary penalty is assessed against the corporation in relation to the contravention or failure.

heading: Effect of charging offence
paragraph:
104
		  A person who has been charged with an offence under this Act, unless the charge was commenced by an information laid by a private individual and was later stayed by the Crown, may not be subject to an administrative monetary penalty in respect of the circumstances that gave rise to the charge.

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph:
105
		  (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, an order resulting from an exercise of discretion of the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer may be appealed to the appeal board by any of the following:

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (a) the person who is subject to the order;

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (2), an owner whose land is or is likely to be physically affected by the order;

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (c) the owner of the works that are the subject of the order;

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (d) the holder of an authorization, a riparian owner or an applicant for an authorization who considers that the holder's, owner's or applicant's rights are or will be prejudiced by the order.

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (2) In the case of the issuance of a drilling authorization, a person whose consent has been given for the purposes of section 62 (4) (c) [drilling authorizations] has no right of appeal unless the order respecting the drilling authorization in respect of which the consent was given is inconsistent with that consent.

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (3) The time limit for a person to commence an appeal is 30 days after the date on which notice of the order being appealed is delivered to the person.

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (4) Subject to this Act, Division 1 of Part 8 of the Environmental Management Act applies to an appeal under this Act.

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (5) The appeal board may conduct an appeal by way of a new hearing.

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (6) On an appeal, the appeal board may

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (a) send the matter back, with directions, to the comptroller, water manager or engineer who made the order being appealed,

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (b) confirm, reverse or vary the order being appealed, or

heading: Appeals to appeal board
paragraph: (c) make any order that the person whose order is being appealed could have made and that the board considers appropriate in the circumstances.

heading: General offences
paragraph: 106		  (1) Section 5 of the Offence Act does not apply to this Act or the regulations.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (2) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) wilfully hinders or interrupts

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i)  the holder of an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization, or

heading: General offences
paragraph: (ii)  a person acting on behalf of a person referred to in subparagraph (i)

heading: General offences
paragraph: in the lawful exercise of a right granted by this Act or the regulations or under an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) without lawful authority,

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i)  diverts water from a stream or aquifer,

heading: General offences
paragraph: (ii)  makes changes in and about a stream,

heading: General offences
paragraph: (iii)  wilfully destroys, damages or interferes with the works of an authorization holder, a change approval holder, a person who holds a drilling authorization or a person who is authorized to construct and has constructed works in accordance with the regulations,

heading: General offences
paragraph: (iii.1)  alters, defaces or removes a sign that is required under the regulations to be posted in respect of a dam,

heading: General offences
paragraph: (iv)  for the purpose of connecting with the works of an authorization holder, lays or causes to be laid a pipe or constructs or causes to be constructed a ditch or other conduit,

heading: General offences
paragraph: (v)  constructs, maintains, operates or uses works,

heading: General offences
paragraph: (vi)  opens or closes a hydrant used for fire protection, or obstructs free access to or damages a fire hydrant stop cock or fire hydrant accessory, or

heading: General offences
paragraph: (vii)  engages in the business of operating works to carry water for others;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (c) wilfully destroys a notice posted by an applicant, an engineer, an officer or a water bailiff;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (d) fails to do anything in accordance with applicable regulations that is required under this Act to be done in accordance with the regulations;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (e) destroys, injures or tampers with

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i)  works, or

heading: General offences
paragraph: (ii)  a gauge, weir, measuring device, structure, appliance, cable, boat, instrument or tool

heading: General offences
paragraph: belonging to or placed in position by an applicant, authorization holder, change approval holder or a person acting on behalf of the government of British Columbia or Canada.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (3) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) diverts or uses water contrary to section 6 (1) [use of water] except under section 6 (2), (3) or (4) or an order;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) contravenes section 6 (2) (a) [use of water - firefighting] by failing to restore the stream flow to its stream channel;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (c) without holding an authorization to do so, diverts recorded water from an aquifer or a stream for prospecting for a mineral or from a stream for domestic purpose other than essential household use as defined in section 22 (11) [precedence of rights], unless the diversion is authorized by the regulations;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (d) diverts unrecorded water from an aquifer or a stream for prospecting for a mineral or from a stream for domestic purpose other than essential household use, as defined in section 22 (11), when prohibited by regulations under section 135 [regulations closing or restricting access to water source];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (e) diverts or stores water from an aquifer under section 6 (4) [use of water - excluded groundwater users] when that section does not apply to the person by regulation under section 135 or 136 [regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (f) diverts, stores or uses water under the regulations when prohibited by a regulation under section 135;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (g) diverts more water than the person is authorized to divert under a licence or use approval;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (h) diverts water for a water use purpose not specified in the person's licence or use approval;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i) diverts water when the person is prohibited by the person's authorization from diverting water;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (j) constructs, operates or uses works for diverting, storing or using water, which works

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i)  are not authorized by the person's licence, use approval, change approval, permit or drilling authorization, or by another enactment, or

heading: General offences
paragraph: (ii)  are not constructed, operated or used in accordance with any applicable regulations;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (k) fails to comply with a term or condition of an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization other than an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization in relation to a sensitive stream;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (l) fails to provide the information, plans, specifications or reports of assessments at the time directed for the purposes of a 30-year licence review under section 23;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (m) fails to provide the information, plans, specifications or reports of assessments directed under section 23 (3);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (n) floods Crown land or constructs, operates or maintains works on Crown land without holding a permit or permission under another enactment authorizing the flooding, construction, operation or maintenance;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (o) fails to give notice of a conveyance or other disposition of land, a mine or an undertaking as required under section 25 [transfer of authorization, change approval or permit];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (p) contravenes section 29 (2) [rights and responsibilities of applicants and holders] by failing to inspect, maintain or repair works as required by that section;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (q) fails to ensure that works are deactivated or decommissioned when or as required under section 29 (3);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (r) fails to make beneficial use of water diverted by the person.

heading: General offences
paragraph: (4) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) fails to submit a beneficial use declaration at the time directed to do so under section 30 (2) [beneficial use];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) fails to provide the information or results of a water conservation audit under section 30 (3) or (4);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (c) fails to take measures as and when required to do so under section 30 (5);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (d) fails to provide information as and when directed under section 30 (6);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (e) fails to provide the information or results of a water conservation audit at the time specified in the direction;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (f) fails to comply with the terms and conditions on which an abandonment of the person's rights under an authorization is approved under section 31 [abandonment of rights under an authorization];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (g) interferes with the works of a licensee, or prevents the licensee from maintaining, operating, using or improving works, located on land owned by the person after the licensee has commenced and is diligently prosecuting expropriation of that land, contrary to section 32 (5) [licensee's right to expropriate land];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (h) fails to give notice in accordance with section 34 [owner to give notice before interfering with works] before altering, moving, filling in or otherwise interfering with works constructed or used under an authorization;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i) fails to take steps to expropriate land when required to do so under section 35 (3) [entry on land in case of urgency];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (j) fails to jointly construct works or permit joint use of the person's works as required by an order under section 36 [joint construction or use of works may be ordered];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (k) fails to comply with the terms and conditions of an order under section 36;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (l) fails to comply with the terms and conditions under which an extension of rights has been authorized under section 37 [power to authorize extension of rights under licence];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (m) fails to pay amounts owing under section 38 (5) [appointment of water bailiffs] by the person to a water bailiff in the amount or at the time specified under that section;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (n) contravenes section 46 (1) [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into stream];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (o) performs an activity in relation to a well, well pump or wellhead for which qualifications are required under this Act without holding the required qualifications;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (p) fails to comply with section 49 (4) [restrictions on constructing or decommissioning wells and related activities] after penetrating an aquifer;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (q) fails to comply with the applicable regulations in relation to

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i)  constructing, decommissioning, deactivating or disinfecting a well, or

heading: General offences
paragraph: (ii)  installing, maintaining, repairing, removing or testing a well pump or wellhead, conducting a flow test of a well or disinfecting a well pump;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (r) fails to provide proof of qualifications as required under section 51 (1) or (3) [proof of qualifications and insurance];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (s) fails to carry the amount of liability insurance required under section 51 (2);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (t) fails to provide proof of liability insurance as required under section 51 (1) or (3).

heading: General offences
paragraph: (5) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) fails to stop or bring artesian flow under control, or give notice, as and when required under section 52 [controlling artesian flow during construction];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) fails to comply with section 53 [controlling flowing artesian well] by failing to engage a well driller with the required qualifications or a professional, or by failing to ensure that the well driller or professional stops the flow of the artesian well or brings that flow under control;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (c) fails to secure a well cap or well cover in accordance with section 54 [well caps or well covers] or removes a well cap or well cover other than for an activity referred to in section 54 (3);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (d) fails to replace a well cap or well cover when required to do so under section 54 (4);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (e) fails to attach an identification plate to a well or wellhead or to remove an identification plate from a well or wellhead when required to do so under section 55 [well identification];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (f) destroys, injures or tampers with an identification plate attached to a well or wellhead;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (g) fails to decommission or deactivate a well when required under section 56 [decommissioning or deactivating well];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (h) fails to maintain, retain, produce or submit a well report when required to do so under section 57 [well reports];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (i) operates a well contrary to section 58 [well operation];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (j) performs an activity for which a drilling authorization is required without holding a drilling authorization;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (k) contravenes section 59 (1) [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into well];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (l) fails to take and cause to be analyzed a groundwater sample when required to do so under section 63 [water analyses for new or altered wells];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (m) tampers with a groundwater sample required to be taken under section 63;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (n) fails to submit the results of an analysis of groundwater as and when required under section 63;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (o) contravenes, other than wilfully, an order of the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer whether given directly or through an officer or a water bailiff;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (p) fails to keep information or records required to be kept under section 116 (1) [records and reporting];

heading: General offences
paragraph: (q) fails to keep information or records for the prescribed period contrary to section 116 (1);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (r) fails to produce records when required under section 116 (2) (a);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (s) fails to provide records to a person to whom the records must be provided under section 116 (2) (b);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (t) fails to install works, prepare reports or submit reports contrary to section 116 (3);

heading: General offences
paragraph: (u) knowingly contravenes section 116 (5).

heading: General offences
paragraph: (6) A person who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction to the following:

heading: General offences
paragraph: (a) in the case of an offence that is not a continuing offence, a fine of not more than $200 000 or imprisonment for not longer than 6 months, or both;

heading: General offences
paragraph: (b) in the case of a continuing offence, a fine of not more than $200 000 for each day the offence is continued or imprisonment for not longer than 6 months, or both.

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: 107		  (1) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (a) fails to comply with a term or condition of an authorization, change approval or permit issued in relation to a sensitive stream or with a term or condition of a drilling authorization imposed for the protection of a sensitive stream;

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (b) constructs a bank-to-bank dam contrary to section 45 [no new dams on protected rivers];

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (c) fails to comply with an order under section 47 (1) or (2) [remediation orders in relation to foreign matter in stream];

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (d) fails to comply with an order under section 60 (1), (2) (3) or (4) [remediation orders in relation to foreign matter in well];

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (e) contravenes a fish population protection order under section 88 [fish population protection orders];

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (f) constructs, places, maintains or makes use of an obstruction in the channel of a stream without authority to do so under this or another enactment;

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (g) drills a well, makes an alteration to a well, installs a well pump or conducts a flow test of a well when the activity is prohibited under this Act;

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (h) interferes with, delays, obstructs or otherwise impedes the comptroller, a water manager, an engineer, an officer or a water bailiff in the performance of a duty or the exercise of a power under this Act;

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (i) wilfully contravenes an order of the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer, whether given directly or through an officer or a water bailiff;

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (j) wilfully interferes with any works in respect of which the comptroller, a water manager, an engineer, an officer or a water bailiff has taken action.

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (2) A person who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction to the following:

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (a) in the case of an offence that is not a continuing offence, a fine of not more than $1 000 000 or imprisonment for not longer than one year, or both;

heading: High penalty offences
paragraph: (b) in the case of a continuing offence, a fine of not more than $1 000 000 for each day the offence is continued or imprisonment for not longer than one year, or both.

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph:
108
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, the court may increase a fine imposed on the person by an amount equal to the court's estimation of the amount of the monetary benefit acquired by or that accrued to the person as a result of the commission of the offence.

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (2) A fine increased under subsection (1)

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (a) applies despite any provision that provides for a maximum fine, and

heading: Penalty for monetary benefit
paragraph: (b) is in addition to any other fine under this Act.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph:
109
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any punishment imposed, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (b) directing the person to take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (c) directing the person to pay the government an amount of money as compensation, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken by or caused to be taken on behalf of the government as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (d) directing the person to perform community service;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (e) directing the person to pay an amount of money the court considers appropriate to the trustee under Part 3 [Habitat Conservation Trust] of the Wildlife Act for inclusion in the trust property as defined in section 118 [definitions] of that Act;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (f) directing the person to post a bond or pay into court an amount of money the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (g) directing the person to submit to the minister, on application by the minister within 3 years after the date of the conviction, any information respecting the activities of the person that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (h) directing the person to publish, in any manner the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (i) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the person's good conduct and for preventing the person from repeating the offence or committing other offences under this Act.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (2) The person against whom an order under subsection (1) is made, or the Attorney General, may apply for a variation to the court that made the original order.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (3) Before hearing an application under subsection (2), the court may order the applicant to give notice of the application in accordance with the directions of the court.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (4) On an application under subsection (2), if the court considers a variation appropriate because of a change in the circumstances, the court may make an order doing one or more of the following:

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (a) changing the original order or any conditions specified in the order;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (b) relieving the person against whom the order was made absolutely or partially from compliance with all or part of the original order;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (c) reducing the period for which the original order is to remain in effect;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (d) extending the period for which the original order is to remain in effect, subject to the limit that the extension must not be longer than one year.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (5) If an application under subsection (2) has been heard by a court, no other application may be made in respect of the original order, or the order as varied under subsection (2), except with leave of the court.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (6) If a person fails to comply with an order referred to in subsection (1) (h) directing the person to publish the facts relating to the commission of an offence, the minister may publish those facts and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (7) If

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (a) an order under this section directs a person to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose, or

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (b) the minister incurs publication costs under subsection (6),

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: the amount and any interest payable on that amount are a debt due to the government of the person directed to pay and may be recovered by filing a certificate in accordance with section 101 [recovery of penalties] as if the amount and interest were an administrative monetary penalty imposed under section 99 [administrative monetary penalties].

heading: Breach of creative sentencing order
paragraph: 110		  (1) A person who contravenes an order under section 109 commits an offence.

heading: Breach of creative sentencing order
paragraph: (2) A person who commits an offence under subsection (1) is liable on conviction to the penalties provided for the offence in relation to which the order under section 109 was made.

heading: Liability of individuals for offences committed by a corporation
paragraph:
111
		  If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the offence commits the offence whether or not the corporation is prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph:
112
		  (1) The time limit for laying an information to commence a prosecution for an offence under this Act is as follows:

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (a) 3 years after the date on which the act or omission that is alleged to constitute the offence occurred:

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) if the minister completes a certificate described in subsection (2), 3 years after the date on which the minister learned of the act or omission referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (2) A certificate purporting to have been issued by the minister, certifying the date referred to in subsection (1) (b), is proof of that date.

heading: Other liabilities remain
paragraph:
113
		  Subject to sections 103 [effect of imposing administrative penalty] and 104 [effect of charging offence], a proceeding, conviction or penalty for an offence under this Act does not relieve a person from any other liability.

heading: Administration
paragraph:
114
		  (1) The minister may designate a public service employee as the Comptroller of Water Rights to exercise the powers and perform the duties of the Comptroller of Water Rights under this or another enactment.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (2) The minister may designate a public service employee or an employee of a government corporation as a Deputy Comptroller of Water Rights and authorize the employee to exercise the powers and perform the duties of the comptroller that are specified in the designation.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (3) The minister may designate

heading: Administration
paragraph: (a) a public service employee or an employee of a government corporation as a water manager, or

heading: Administration
paragraph: (b) a class of public service employee or a class of employee of a government corporation as water managers, the members of which class are

heading: Administration
paragraph: to exercise the powers and perform the duties of a water manager under this or another enactment.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (4) The minister may designate

heading: Administration
paragraph: (a) a public service employee or an employee of a government corporation as an assistant water manager, or

heading: Administration
paragraph: (b) a class of public service employee or a class of employee of a government corporation as assistant water managers

heading: Administration
paragraph: and authorize the employees or employees in the class to exercise the powers and perform the duties of a water manager as may be restricted in the designation.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (5) The comptroller may designate as an engineer for the purposes of this Act

heading: Administration
paragraph: (a) a public service employee, or

heading: Administration
paragraph: (b) an employee of a government corporation

heading: Administration
paragraph: who is a professional engineer, a professional geoscientist as defined in the Engineers and Geoscientists Act or a holder of limited licence under the Engineers and Geoscientists Act acting within the scope of the limited licence.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (6) The comptroller may designate for the purposes of this Act

heading: Administration
paragraph: (a) a public service employee or an employee of a government corporation as an officer, or

heading: Administration
paragraph: (b) a class of public service employee or a class of employee of a government corporation as officers the members of which class are

heading: Administration
paragraph: to exercise the powers and perform the duties of an officer.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (7) A designation under this section must be in writing.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (8) The comptroller may exercise any power or perform any duty given under this Act to a water manager, an engineer or an officer.

heading: Administration
paragraph: (9) A water manager may exercise any power or perform any duty given under this Act to an engineer or an officer.

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: 115		  (1) The minister may establish advisory boards to provide advice in relation to

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (a) establishing water objectives,

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (b) methods for determining environmental flow needs or critical environmental flow thresholds,

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (c) qualifications of well drillers and well pump installers, and competencies of professionals, as defined in section 48 [definitions for Division 3 of Part 3], generally and in relation to specific activities,

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (d) standards and best practices in respect of the diversion and use of water,

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (e) standards and best practices in respect of activities in relation to wells and groundwater protection,

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (f) standards and best practices in respect of activities in relation to artesian flow,

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (g) methods for estimating amounts of water diverted or used, or

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (h) any other matter under this Act.

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (2) The chair and members of an advisory board are to be appointed by the minister.

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (3) A person appointed to an advisory board, may, as directed by the minister,

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (a) be reimbursed in accordance with the directives of Treasury Board for reasonable travelling and out-of-pocket expenses necessarily incurred in discharging the person's duties under this Act, and

heading: Advisory boards
paragraph: (b) be paid remuneration in accordance with the directives of Treasury Board unless the person is a public service employee, in which case no remuneration may be paid.

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph:
116
		  (1) A person must keep for the prescribed period

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (a) any information or records required to be obtained, prepared or retained by the person under this Act,

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (b) the prescribed information and records, and

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (c) any other information or records that the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer directs.

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (2) A person who is required under this Act to retain records must

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (a) produce those records for inspection when required by the comptroller, a water manager, an engineer, an officer or a water bailiff, and

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (b) if the person holds an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization, provide the records referred to in subsection (1) in relation to the authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization to a person to whom

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (i)  the holder transfers, as described in section 25 [transfer of authorization, change approval or permit], the land, mine or undertaking to which the authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization is appurtenant, or

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (ii)  the appurtenancy of the authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization is transferred under section 27 [transfer of appurtenancy].

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (3) The prescribed persons must, for the purposes of measuring water use, water quantity and water quality,

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (a) install the prescribed works,

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (b) prepare the prescribed reports, and

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (c) submit those reports to the prescribed persons and at the times required by this Act or the regulations.

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (4) The comptroller, a water manager or an engineer may collect public personal information and government water records for the purposes of verifying information provided by a person under this Act.

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (5) A person must not record, retain or submit false or misleading information

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (a) in a record the person is required under this Act to retain, or

heading: Records and reporting
paragraph: (b) in an application, declaration, log or another record the person is required or authorized under this Act to submit to the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer.

heading: Delivery and publication of documents and information
paragraph:
117
		  (1) Unless specifically provided otherwise, a notice or other document that under this Act must or may be given or delivered to a person may be given or delivered in any of the following manners:

heading: Delivery and publication of documents and information
paragraph: (a) by leaving a copy with the person;

heading: Delivery and publication of documents and information
paragraph: (b) by sending a copy by ordinary mail or registered mail to the address on file with the comptroller for the person or provided to the comptroller for that purpose;

heading: Delivery and publication of documents and information
paragraph: (c) by leaving a copy at the person's residence with an adult who apparently resides with the person or, if the person is a business, by leaving a copy at the address at which the person carries on business with a person apparently employed in the business;

heading: Delivery and publication of documents and information
paragraph: (d) by leaving a copy in a mailbox or mail slot for the address at which the person resides or, if the person carries on a business, for the address at which the person carries on business;

heading: Delivery and publication of documents and information

heading: Fees, rentals and charges
paragraph:

heading: Fees, rentals and charges

heading: Protection of officials
paragraph:
119
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2), no legal proceedings for damages lies or may be commenced or maintained against the comptroller, a water manager, an engineer, an officer, a registrar, a water bailiff or a person authorized under section 18 (7) [quick licensing procedures] for anything done or omitted

heading: Protection of officials

paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person referred to in that subsection in relation to anything done or omitted by the person in bad faith.

heading: Restriction on proceedings respecting decisions under Act
paragraph:
120
		  Except as otherwise provided in this Act or on a question of law,

heading: Restriction on proceedings respecting decisions under Act
paragraph: (a) a hearing, investigation or proceeding of the comptroller, a water manager, an engineer, an officer or a water bailiff must not be questioned, reviewed or restrained by any process or proceeding in any court, and

heading: Restriction on proceedings respecting decisions under Act
paragraph: (b) an order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister, the comptroller, a water manager or an engineer is final and must not be questioned, reviewed or restrained by any process or proceeding in any court.

heading: No compensation
paragraph:
121
		  (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Act or by regulation, no compensation is payable by, and no legal proceedings may be commenced or maintained against, the government or any other person for or in relation to loss or damages arising from an effect on

heading: No compensation
paragraph: (a) an application under this or another enactment,

heading: No compensation
paragraph: (b) rights under a licence or use approval,

heading: No compensation
paragraph: (c) permission given under a change approval, permit, drilling authorization or order,

heading: No compensation
paragraph: (d) permission given under another enactment,

heading: No compensation
paragraph: (e) resource rights conferred by Crown grant, or

heading: No compensation
paragraph: (f) rights and privileges in relation to land and resources

heading: No compensation
paragraph: resulting under the provisions of this Act, the regulations or an order from any of the following:

paragraph: (g) a change in precedence of water rights;

heading: No compensation
paragraph: (h) a restriction or prohibition on the exercise of rights or a permission provided under this Act or a former Act;

paragraph: (l) a change of or the imposition of new terms and conditions on an authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization.

heading: No compensation

heading: Liability of owner for damage remains
paragraph:
122
		  The abandonment, suspension, termination or cancellation of all or part of the rights held under an authorization or change approval, or all or part of the permission held under a change approval, permit or drilling authorization, does not relieve any of the following persons of liability for damage resulting from the works owned, operated or maintained by the person, or from a defect, insufficiency or failure of those works:

paragraph: (a) the owner of the land, mine or undertaking to which the authorization, change approval, permit or drilling authorization is or was appurtenant;

heading: Authorization or permit as evidence
paragraph:
123
		  The production of an order, licence, use approval, change approval, permit or drilling authorization or a copy of any of them certified to be a copy by the comptroller or other person authorized by the minister to certify copies, is, without further proof, evidence in a court of the matters and things set out in the order, licence, use approval, change approval, permit or drilling authorization.

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph:
124
		  (1) For the purpose of making regulations authorized under this Act to be made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of making regulations authorized under this Act to be made by the minister, the minister may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (3) The authority under another provision of this Act to make regulations does not limit subsection (1) or (2).

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (4) A regulation of the Lieutenant Governor in Council or the minister under this Act may do one or more of the following:

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (a) specify who is responsible for meeting a prescribed requirement;

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (b) exempt from a requirement of this Act or the regulations, on specified terms and conditions, in specified circumstances or at specified times, a person, including the Crown, an entity, an activity, a stream, an aquifer, an area, a water sustainability plan, a water use purpose, an authorization, a change approval, a permit, a drilling authorization, a watershed, a natural resource, a work, a contaminant, a matter or a substance;

paragraph: (c) make different regulations for different classes of water, persons, entities, activities, streams, aquifers, areas, water sustainability plans, water use purposes, circumstances, authorizations, change approvals, permits, drilling authorizations, appurtenances, times or periods of time, watersheds, natural resources, works, contaminants, matters or substances, and establish classes for that purpose;

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (d) designate an area by any method that adequately describes the area, including, without limitation, by name, map, plan or legal description or by reference to a stream, watershed, aquifer or other geological formation, part of a geological formation or depth or other dimension of a geological formation, or by any combination of these methods;

paragraph: (e) require a person to engage a person with prescribed qualifications to perform audits, studies and assessments and make reports required under this Act;

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (f) establish criteria for audits, studies, assessments, including methods of assessment, and reports referred to in paragraph (e);

paragraph: (g) confer a discretion or delegate a matter to the comptroller, a water manager, an engineer, an officer or a person in a class of official prescribed for the purposes of section 126 (1) (c) [regulations respecting administration and governance];

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (h) provide that the contravention of a regulation is an offence;

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (i) prescribe for a contravention of a regulation, as the Lieutenant Governor in Council or minister, as applicable, considers appropriate,

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (i)  a penalty not exceeding the penalty authorized under section 106 (6) [general offences], or

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (ii)  a penalty not exceeding the penalty authorized under section 107 (2) [high penalty offences].

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (a) defining words or phrases used but not defined in this Act, and

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (b) respecting any matter for which regulations, other than regulations of the minister, are contemplated by this Act.

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (6) Regulations made under this Act may

heading: General regulation-making powers
paragraph: (a) adopt, in whole or in part, codes or standards published by a provincial, national or international standards association, including adoption of amendments to the codes or standards published before or after the making of the regulations,

paragraph: (b) in adopting the codes or standards under paragraph (a), grant powers to and establish functions and duties of public officers that the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers necessary for the public officer to administer the codes or standards adopted, and

paragraph: (c) exempt persons from all or part of the codes or standards adopted.
