paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations authorizing a person or entity to divert or use, including store, unrecorded water for a period of up to 24 months without holding an authorization authorizing the diversion or use, including, without limitation, the following regulations:

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (a) requiring notice to the comptroller or a water manager and specifying when notice must be given and the required content of the notice;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (b) respecting the duties of a person or entity that diverts or uses water;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (c) applying provisions of this Act or the regulations in relation to the diversion or use of water;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (d) prescribing the water use purposes for which water may be diverted or used;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (e) respecting the works that may be used to divert or use water;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (f) respecting the timing and circumstances in which the person or entity may start or continue, or must stop, diverting or using water;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (g) prescribing the maximum quantity of water that may be diverted or used;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (h) imposing terms and conditions on the diversion or use of water.

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (3) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations authorizing a person to make changes in and about a stream without holding an authorization or change approval authorizing the changes in and about the stream, including, without limitation, the following regulations:

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (a) requiring notice to the comptroller or a water manager and specifying when notice must be given and the required content of the notice;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (b) establishing requirements, procedures and standards applicable to persons who undertake any works or changes in and about a stream;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (c) respecting the timing and circumstances in which the person or entity may start or continue, or must stop, any activity that causes, directly or indirectly, changes in and about a stream;

heading: Regulations respecting licensing, diversion and use of water and related matters
paragraph: (d) prescribing the maximum quantity of water that may be diverted or used, including stored, in making changes in and about a stream.

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph:
128
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting sensitive streams, including, without limitation, regulations

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (a) designating a stream, including specified tributaries and specified aquifers the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers are reasonably likely to be connected to the stream or a tributary of the stream, as a sensitive stream if the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers the designation will contribute to the protection of a fish population whose sustainability is at risk because of damage to the aquatic ecosystem of the stream,

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (b) prescribing the plans, specifications, reports of assessments or other information that must be provided by an applicant for an authorization, a change approval or an amendment to an authorization or change approval in relation to a sensitive stream,

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (c) establishing criteria that a decision maker must apply in making a decision on an application for an authorization, a change approval or an amendment to an authorization or change approval in relation to a sensitive stream, and

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (d) prescribing terms and conditions that apply to an authorization or change approval in relation to a sensitive stream, including, without limitation, terms and conditions respecting

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (i)  mitigation measures,

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (ii)  diversion and use of water, and

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (iii)  monitoring and reporting.

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (a) the sustainability of the protected fish population is no longer at risk,

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (b) the implementation of a water sustainability plan will reduce the risk to the protected fish population so that the designation is no longer required, or

heading: Regulations respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (c) removal of the designation is in the public interest.

heading: Regulations respecting streams and stream protection
paragraph:
129
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations respecting streams and stream protection
paragraph: (a) amending the Schedule to designate a stream as a protected river,

heading: Regulations respecting streams and stream protection
paragraph: (b) prescribing for the purposes of section 46 (2) [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into stream] other activities, practices or substances, including activities or practices to which this or another enactment applies,

heading: Regulations respecting streams and stream protection
paragraph: (c) establishing requirements, procedures, standards or codes in respect of the use, construction, operation, maintenance, alteration, abandonment, deactivation, decommissioning or inspection of works, and

heading: Regulations respecting streams and stream protection
paragraph: (d) respecting the use of a stream for floating timber and the construction, maintenance, operation, alteration and removal of booms and other installations in a stream, and the duties of persons who float timber in a stream with respect to the segregation and sorting of the timber.

heading: Regulations respecting streams and stream protection
paragraph: (2) A stream designated by regulation under subsection (1) remains a protected river until the Schedule is amended by an Act to delete the stream from the Schedule.

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph:
130
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of Division 3 [Wells and Groundwater Protection] of Part 3 [Protecting Water Resources], including, without limitation, the following regulations:

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (a) prescribing the purposes or classes of artificial openings in the ground that are not included in the definition of "well";

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (b) respecting well drillers, well pump installers and professionals, as defined in section 48 (1) [definitions], including, without limitation,

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i)  establishing the qualifications that well drillers and well pump installers are required to have to perform or supervise specified activities, and

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ii)  requiring well drillers, well pump installers or professionals to carry not less than a prescribed amount of liability insurance;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (c) establishing requirements, procedures, standards or codes in respect of any aspect of the following:

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i)  siting wells;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ii)  constructing wells;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (iii)  installing well pumps;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (iv)  designing, testing, operating, disinfecting, floodproofing, capping or covering wells;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (v)  deactivating or decommissioning wells;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (vi)  conducting flow tests of wells;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (vii)  works, including the design, construction, installation, testing, operation, alteration, maintenance, repair, disinfection, removal or replacement of works relating to the use, testing or monitoring of wells and groundwater;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (viii)  stopping or controlling the flow of flowing artesian wells;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ix)  any other activities respecting wells for which the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers it necessary or advisable for purposes of the protection of an aquifer or groundwater to establish requirements, procedures, standards or codes;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (d) respecting the identification of wells, including, without limitation, specifying

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i)  the form, content, placement and manner of attachment of identification plates,

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ii)  alterations to a well that require that an identification plate be attached, and

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (iii)  classes of water supply systems that must have an identification plate attached;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (e) establishing the periods of time after which a well that is not being used

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i)  is considered not to be in service, which may be different in specified circumstances, or

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ii)  must be permanently decommissioned;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (f) specifying the circumstances in which a well is considered not to be in service;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (g) establishing a register of well drillers or well pump installers who are qualified in respect of specified matters, including, without limitation,

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i)  specifying the person responsible for the register,

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ii)  specifying the information, which may include contact information, that well drillers or well pump installers must provide to that person, and

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (iii)  requiring that the register be published;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (h) establishing requirements for the protection of aquifers from activities that are capable of causing a significant adverse impact on

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i)  the quality of groundwater in an aquifer, water in a stream that is recharged by the aquifer or groundwater in a well that draws from the aquifer, or

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ii)  the existing uses made of groundwater from any well that draws from that aquifer or water in a stream that is recharged by that aquifer;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i) prescribing matters or substances for the purposes of section 59 (1) (f) or [prohibition on introducing foreign matter into well];

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (j) authorizing individual variations on requirements, procedures, standards or codes established under paragraph (c) on application to a prescribed official;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (k) respecting well reports and logs, including, without limitation, specifying

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (i)  the records required,

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (ii)  the form of logs, records and reports,

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (iii)  the frequency and timing of reports,

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (iv)  activities in relation to a well that require that a well report be submitted, and

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (v)  the manner of delivering well reports to the comptroller;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (l) specifying the circumstances in which logs, records and reports respecting wells must be kept and produced, and the period for which they must be retained.

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting sampling and analyzing groundwater for new or altered wells, including, without limitation, the following regulations:

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (a) specifying the class of laboratory that may carry out the analyses;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (b) specifying the nature or the parameters of the analyses;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (c) prescribing alterations, activities or circumstances for the purposes of section 63 (1) [water analyses for new or altered wells];

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (d) specifying requirements for the timing, collection, quality, storage, handling and transportation of groundwater samples;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (e) specifying the purpose, timing and technical requirements for groundwater sample analyses;

heading: Regulations respecting groundwater and groundwater works
paragraph: (f) specifying the content, frequency and timing of reports and the method and form used for reporting relating to groundwater sampling and analyses.

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph:
131
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations requiring measurement and testing in relation to the diversion or use of water under this Act, including, without limitation, the following regulations:

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (a) requiring specified persons who are diverting or using water under this Act to install or use specified works for the purposes of measuring, monitoring and testing the quality or quantity of water diverted and the quality or quantity of water available for diversion and use;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (b) requiring specified persons who are diverting or using water under this Act to calculate the quantity of water diverted or used in accordance with a prescribed formula;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (c) respecting the installation, operation, maintenance or use of works described in paragraph (a);

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (d) requiring persons described in paragraph (a) to measure the quantities of water diverted or used for a water use purpose;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (e) requiring persons described in paragraph (a) or (b) to test for specified parameters water in a stream or aquifer or water diverted or used from a stream or aquifer;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (f) prescribing methods and standards for specified measurements, calculations or tests;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (g) specifying the manner and frequency of testing or calculating.

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (2) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations respecting records and reporting by persons who are diverting or using water under this Act, including, without limitation, the following regulations:

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (a) prescribing the records and the information the records must contain that must be retained by a person who is diverting or using water under this Act, and the period for which the records must be retained;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (b) prescribing reports a person who is diverting or using water under this Act must prepare or have prepared;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (c) prescribing the records, the information the records must contain and the reports that must be submitted, to whom the records and reports must be submitted and the manner and time of submission;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (d) authorizing or requiring a person to whom a record or report must be submitted under the regulation to publish the record or report;

heading: Regulations respecting measuring, testing and reporting
paragraph: (e) requiring that records be kept and submissions be made in a form approved by the comptroller.

heading: Regulations respecting water sustainability plans
paragraph:
132
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of Division 4 [Water Sustainability Plans] of Part 3 [Protecting Water Resources] respecting the preparation of proposed water sustainability plans, as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting water sustainability plans
paragraph: (a) setting minimum requirements for the organizational structure supporting the development of a proposed plan, including, without limitation, steering committees, planning teams and technical advisory committees;

heading: Regulations respecting water sustainability plans
paragraph: (b) setting minimum requirements for public and stakeholder communications and consultations in relation to the development of a proposed plan;

heading: Regulations respecting water sustainability plans
paragraph: (c) setting requirements for notification of potentially affected persons under section 71 [notice to affected persons].

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph:
133
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of Division 2 [Administrative Penalties] of Part 4 [Enforcement] as follows:

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) prescribing provisions of this Act and the regulations in relation to the contravention of which an administrative monetary penalty may be imposed;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) prescribing

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (i)  a schedule of administrative monetary penalties that may be imposed and any additional matters that must be considered by the comptroller in establishing the amount of an administrative monetary penalty, or

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (ii)  a maximum or minimum amount of an administrative monetary penalty that may be imposed generally, or for specified contraventions or failures, or the manner of calculating those amounts;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (c) prescribing a limitation period for imposing an administrative monetary penalty and evidentiary matters in relation to that period;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (d) prescribing procedures to be applied by the comptroller in making a determination of contravention or non-compliance;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (e) authorizing administrative monetary penalties to be imposed on a daily basis for continuing contraventions or failures;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (f) prohibiting the comptroller from serving an administrative monetary penalty notice on a person who has demonstrated to the satisfaction of the comptroller that the person exercised due diligence to prevent the specified contravention or failure;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (g) respecting the time limit, manner and process for paying an administrative monetary penalty;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (h) prescribing the consequences of failing to pay an administrative monetary penalty which may include, but are not limited to, imposing additional administrative monetary penalties;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (i) authorizing or requiring the comptroller to publish compliance agreements;

heading: Regulations respecting administrative penalties
paragraph: (j) respecting compliance agreements.

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph:
134
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations for the purposes of section 121 [no compensation] respecting the payment of compensation by the government, including, without limitation,

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph: (a) respecting circumstances in which compensation may be payable or must not be paid to a person by the government,

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph: (b) providing for applications for compensation and prescribing the information that must be provided in an application for compensation, which may include, but is not limited to, information respecting and proof of loss or damage,

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph: (c) respecting the assessment of loss or damage and the matters in respect of which compensation may be paid,

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph: (d) respecting the calculation of compensation, including, without limitation, prescribing methods of evaluating loss or damage and maximum amounts of compensation that may be paid,

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph: (e) respecting the manner and timing of paying compensation,

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph: (f) requiring that disputes in respect of compensation be resolved in a prescribed manner or using a prescribed method, including by specifying a person or tribunal who may hear and decide disputes, and

heading: Regulations respecting compensation
paragraph: (g) providing that decisions in relation to the payment of compensation by the government or of specified persons or tribunals are final and prohibiting appeals in relation to such decisions.

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph:
135
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: "eligible applicant",

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (a) in respect of a water reservation under section 39 [water reservations], means a person authorized under section 39 (4) (a), (b) or (d) in relation to the water reserved,

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (b) in respect of a water reservation under section 40 [treaty first nation water reservations], means a person authorized by the applicable treaty first nation to acquire rights to the water reserved, and

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (c) in respect of a water reservation under section 41 [Nisga'a water reservation], means a person authorized by the Nisga'a Nation to acquire rights to the water reserved;

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: "new authorization" does not include

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (a) an amendment of an existing authorization under section 26 [amendment or substitution of authorization, change approval or permit],

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (b) a transfer of appurtenancy in relation to an existing authorization under section 27 [transfer of appurtenancy],

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (c) an apportionment of rights under an existing licence under section 28 [apportionment of rights under licences], and

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (d) a partial abandonment of rights under an existing authorization under section 31 [abandonment of rights under an authorization].

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), if the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers that there is not sufficient unrecorded water in a specified stream or aquifer to warrant the issuance of any new authorizations in relation to the stream or aquifer, or if recommended in a water sustainability plan, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the comptroller and the water managers from accepting or considering applications for new authorizations in relation to the stream or aquifer, or

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (b) restricting the applications that may be accepted or considered by the comptroller and the water managers in relation to the stream or aquifer.

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (3) A regulation under subsection (2) may not prohibit the comptroller and the water managers from accepting or considering applications for new authorizations in relation to a specified aquifer from

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (a) a person to whom a regulation under section 136 (2) applies in relation to the aquifer,

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (b) a person to whom a regulation under section 140 (1) [transition - groundwater licensing] applies in relation to that aquifer,

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (c) a person to whom section 25 (4) [transition - unlicensed registrants] of the Water Protection Act applies in relation to that aquifer, or

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (d) a person who, at the time the regulation under subsection (2) comes into force, has drilled a well into that aquifer to divert water for domestic purpose but, at that time

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (i)  the well is not yet in use, and

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (ii)  the well owner is not yet required under section 56 [decommissioning or deactivating well] to decommission the well.

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (4) A regulation under subsection (2) may not prohibit the comptroller and the water managers from accepting or considering applications for new authorizations

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (a) from an eligible applicant for water reserved under section 39, 40 or 41, or

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (b) for dedicated agricultural water for a qualifying agricultural use on qualifying agricultural land.

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (5) A regulation under subsection (2) in relation to a specified stream may also do either or both of the following:

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (a) prohibit or restrict the diversion or use of water from the stream under section 6 (1) (b) [use of water under the regulations];

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (b) provide that section 6 (3) [use of water - at sufferance] applies only to a person who, before the date on which the regulation takes effect, has diverted water from the stream under that provision.

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (6) A regulation under subsection (2) in relation to a specified aquifer may also do one or more of the following:

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (a) prohibit or restrict the diversion or use of water from the aquifer under section 6 (1) (b);

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (b) prohibit or restrict the drilling of wells for the purpose of diverting water from that aquifer;

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (c) provide that section 6 (4) [use of water - excluded groundwater users] applies only to one or more of the following:

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (i)  a person who is diverting water from that aquifer under that section immediately before the date on which the regulation comes into force;

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (ii)  a person who, before the date on which the regulation comes into force, drilled a well for the purpose of diverting water from that aquifer for domestic purpose but on the date on which the regulations comes into force

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (A) the well is not yet in use, and

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (B) the well owner is not yet required under section 56 to decommission the well.

heading: Regulations closing or restricting access to water source
paragraph: (7) A regulation under this section applies despite any other provision of this Act or the regulations.

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: 136		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations providing that section 6 (4) [use of water - excluded groundwater users] does not apply in relation to a specified aquifer or the aquifers in a specified area

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (a) if the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers that the regulation is warranted to protect the specified aquifer, a specified stream the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers is reasonably likely to be hydraulically connected to the aquifer or the aquifers in the specified area, or

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (b) if recommended in a water sustainability plan.

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (2) A regulation under subsection (1) must contain transitional provisions in respect of persons who, on the date on which the regulation comes into force, are diverting, storing or using water from the specified aquifer or an aquifer in the specified area in the quantity and for the purposes described in section 6 (4), permitting those persons to continue to divert, store and use water from that aquifer in that quantity and for that purpose,

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (a) subject to any requirements, restrictions and conditions set out in the regulation, and

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (b) until,

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (i)  if the person applies for an authorization on or before the date that applies to the person by regulations under subsection (1), the date an authorization is issued to the person, and

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (ii)  if the person fails to apply for an authorization on or before the date that applies to the person by regulations under subsection (2), that date.

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (3) Despite sections 12 [application and decision maker initiative procedures], 13 [objections to applications and decision maker initiatives], 14 [powers respecting applications and decision maker initiatives], 17 [sensitive stream mitigation] and 18 [quick licensing procedures], a regulation under subsection (1) of this subsection may

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (a) establish application procedures and requirements for persons described in subsection (2),

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (b) establish, for the purposes of section 22 [precedence of rights], the method for determining precedence of an authorization issued to a person described in subsection (2), and

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (c) provide for the application of the provisions of Part 2 [Licensing, Diversion and Use of Water] to persons described in subsection (2) at different times for different areas or aquifers.

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (4) Despite any effect on the precedence of the rights under authorizations in effect on the date a person is issued an authorization in accordance with regulations under this section, the method for determining the precedence date of an authorization for the purposes of subsection (3) may provide for the rights under the authorization to have precedence from the person's date of first use of water from the aquifer.

heading: Regulations requiring authorizations for domestic use of groundwater
paragraph: (5) On and after the date a regulation under subsection (1) provides that section 6 (4) does not apply in relation to an aquifer, a person diverting water under section 6 (4) from the aquifer is liable for the applicable fees, rentals or charges for the water diverted and used by the person as if an authorization were issued to the person on that date.

heading: Minister's regulations restricting groundwater activities
paragraph:
137
		  (1) The minister, by regulation applicable to an area designated in the regulation, may restrict one or more of the following or may impose requirements on a person doing one or more of the following:

heading: Minister's regulations restricting groundwater activities
paragraph: (a) constructing wells;

heading: Minister's regulations restricting groundwater activities
paragraph: (b) installing well pumps;

heading: Minister's regulations restricting groundwater activities
paragraph: (c) conducting flow tests;

heading: Minister's regulations restricting groundwater activities
paragraph: (d) another activity in relation to a well or groundwater.

heading: Minister's regulations restricting groundwater activities
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), a restriction in a regulation under that subsection may require that a person hold a drilling authorization in order to carry out one or more of the activities referred to in section 62 (1) [drilling authorizations].

heading: Minister's regulations restricting groundwater activities
paragraph: (3) A regulation under subsection (1) must set out the purpose of the regulation.

heading: Transition - power purposes
paragraph:
138
		  (1) A person who, on the date section 19 [licences for power purposes] of this Act comes into force, holds a licence issued under section 12.2 [licences for power purposes] of the Water Act may apply to the comptroller or a water manager, within one year after that date, for an extension of the term of the licence of up to 10 years to account for any project development term, as defined in section 19, that occurred under the licence.

heading: Transition - power purposes
paragraph: (2) Section 19 (6) does not apply in relation to an application authorized under subsection (1) of this section.

heading: Transition - water use purposes
paragraph: 139		  (1) On and after the date section 2 [water use purposes] comes into force, a reference in a licence issued under a former Act authorizing the use of water for an industrial - oil field injection purpose is conclusively deemed to be a reference to an oil and gas purpose.

heading: Transition - water use purposes
paragraph: (2) On and after the date section 2 comes into force, a reference in a licence issued under a former Act authorizing the use of water for a mineral trading purpose is conclusively deemed to be a reference to a mineralized water purpose.

heading: Transition - water use purposes
paragraph: (3) On and after the date section 2 comes into force, a reference in a licence issued under a former Act authorizing the use of water for a river improvement purpose is conclusively deemed to be a reference to the applicable industrial purpose established by regulations.

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph:
140
		  (1) Despite section 6 (1) [use of water], a person who, on the date section 6 comes into force, is diverting or using, including storing, water, other than as described in section 6 (4) [use of water - excluded groundwater users], from an aquifer for a water use purpose may continue to divert, store and use water from that aquifer for that purpose as follows:

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (a) if the person applies for an authorization on or before the date that applies to the person by regulations under subsection (2) (c), until the date a decision is made on the application;

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (b) if the person fails to apply for an authorization on or before the date that applies to the person by regulations under subsection (2) (c), until that date.

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (2) Despite sections 12 [application and decision maker initiative procedures], 13 [objections to applications and decision maker initiatives], 14 [powers respecting applications and decision maker initiatives], 17 [sensitive stream mitigation], 18 [quick licensing procedures] and 22 [precedence of rights], the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (a) establishing application procedures and requirements for persons described in subsection (1),

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (b) establishing for the purposes of section 22 the method for determining the precedence date of an authorization issued to a person described in subsection (1) (a), and

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (c) providing for the application of the provisions of Part 2 [Licensing, Diversion and Use of Water] to persons described in subsection (1) at different times for different areas, aquifers, water use purposes or quantities of water diverted.

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (3) Despite any effect on the precedence of the rights under authorizations in effect on the date a person is issued an authorization in accordance with regulations under this section, the method for determining the precedence date of an authorization for the purposes of subsection (2) may provide for the rights under the authorization to have precedence from the person's date of first use for a specified water use purpose of a specified amount of water from the aquifer.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "application" means an application of an applicant;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "dry hydrant" means works, typically constructed of metal pipes, strainers, fittings and concrete, that are

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) for diverting water,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) not pressurized, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) accessible by a fire truck;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "erosion" means the wearing away by the action of water of the stream channel or the materials used in works;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish habitat" means the areas of an aquatic ecosystem on which fish depend, directly or indirectly, in order to carry out their life processes, including areas for spawning grounds, nurseries, rearing, food supply and migration;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "legal instrument" means a record that transfers, charges or otherwise deals with or affects land, or evidences title to the land;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "location description", in relation to land, works, streams, aquifers or other geographical features, means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in the case of land registered in a land title office, the description on the title to the land, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in any other case, a description of the location of the land, works or feature that is sufficient to clearly identify that location;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "official name" in relation to a place or a geographical feature means the name given to the place or feature in the Gazetteer of British Columbia;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "point of diversion" means,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) in relation to a stream, the location on the stream channel where water is diverted from the stream, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) in relation to an aquifer, the location of a well from which water is diverted from the aquifer;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "well tag number" means the file number assigned in the government's records to the records in relation to a particular well;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "worksite" means an area used for the construction of works.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) In the Act and the regulations:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "extinguish" includes to contain and control the spread of a fire;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licensee", in relation to a licence, means the owner of the land, mine or undertaking to which the licence is appurtenant, and includes the holder of an authorization if the authorization is a licence.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of the definition of "groundwater" in section 1 (1) of the Act, "naturally occurring" means occurring otherwise than in a pipe, cistern or other structure placed in the ground.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of paragraph (d) of the definition of "government water record" in section 1 (1) of the Act, the following ministers are prescribed as prescribed ministers:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the minister responsible for the administration of the Environment and Land Use Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the minister responsible for the administration of the Ministry of Environment Act.

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph:
3
		  (1) An application to a decision maker for an authorization must include all the following information, as applicable:

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (a) the full name of the applicant and a mailing address, a telephone number and, if available, an email address at which the applicant or the applicant's agent may be contacted;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (b) the official name of the stream or aquifer that is the proposed source of the water, or, if there is no official name, a location description of that stream or aquifer;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (c) if the application relates to water in a stream, the official name of the stream into which the proposed source of the water discharges or is immediately tributary, or, if there is no official name for the stream, a location description of that stream;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (d) if the application relates to water in an aquifer, the official names of each stream or other aquifer known to the applicant to be reasonably likely to be hydraulically connected to the source aquifer, or, if there is no official name, a location description of that stream or aquifer;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (e) if water is to be stored under the authorization, the official name of the proposed reservoir, or, if there is no official name, a location description of that reservoir;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (f) the water use purposes for which the water is to be used;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (g) the quantity of water proposed to be diverted or stored for each water use purpose identified under paragraph (f), and, in the case of a power purpose, the amount of power proposed to be generated;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (h) if the water is not to be diverted or used throughout the year, the periods in the year during which the water will be diverted or used;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (i) a location description of the land, mine or undertaking to which the authorization is to be appurtenant or a general description of the project or scheme of water use;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (j) if the land described in paragraph (i), (l) or (n) is Crown land, proof of the applicant's authority to occupy the Crown land, proof that an application for a disposition of the Crown land has been made or the applicant's request for a permit in relation to that Crown land;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (k) if the water use purposes of the authorization include an irrigation purpose, the measurements of the area of land to be irrigated;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (l) an identification of the location of the point of diversion, or diversion and storage, if applicable, either by location description or by reference to the location of a known feature;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (m) a detailed description of the proposed works for the proposed diversion or use, including, without limitation, in relation to a well, the depth of the well or proposed well and, if available, any well report that has been prepared in respect of the well and the well identification plate number or well tag number;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (n) a location description of

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (i)  the land on which the applicant proposes to construct works, and

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (ii)  any land that is likely to be physically affected by the proposed works;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (o) the applicant's title to or other interest in the appurtenancy referred to in paragraph (i) and the name of the owner of any land described in paragraph (l) or (n) that is not owned by the applicant;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (p) an accurate labelled drawing, to scale, showing all the following:

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (i)  the location and boundaries of the appurtenancy and the location within the appurtenancy where the water is to be used;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (ii)  the approximate location of the proposed works;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (iii)  the boundaries of any land that is likely to be physically affected by the proposed works;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (iv)  if the water source is an aquifer, streams and other water bodies, whether natural or otherwise, other wells that are diverting water from the aquifer and other water features in the area shown in the drawing, if known to the applicant;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (v)  if the water source is a stream, the location of the stream and the direction of flow.

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (2) A decision maker must not authorize in a use approval water storage by a dam to which Part 2 of the Dam Safety Regulation applies unless the dam is authorized by a licence.

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (3) An application for a licence or, subject to subsection (2), a use approval, that proposes the storage of water by a dam must include all the following information, as applicable:

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (a) the height or proposed height of the dam;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (b) the length or proposed length of the dam;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (c) the crest width or proposed crest width of the dam;

heading: Applications for licences and use approvals
paragraph: (d) the maximum volume of water proposed to be stored by the dam.

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph:
4
		  An application for a change approval must include all the following information, as applicable:

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (a) the information specified in section 3 (1) (a);

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (b) the official name of the stream in respect of which the changes in and about a stream are proposed, or, if there is no official name, a location description of the stream;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (c) a location description of the place on the stream at which the changes in and about the stream are proposed to occur and, if available, the street address of that location;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (d) a location description of the land or undertaking, if any, to which the change approval is to be appurtenant;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (e) a drawing as described in section 3 (1) (p) showing the relevant boundaries and locations in relation to the application;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (f) the proposed start and finish dates for making the changes in and about the stream and constructing any proposed works;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (g) a description of the activities and works to be constructed in relation to the proposed changes in and about the stream and that may affect the stream;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (h) if the land described in paragraph (c) or (d) is owned by a person other than the applicant, the written consent of the land owner to the use of the person's land for any works or construction of any works;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (i) if the land described in paragraph (c) or (d) is Crown land, proof of the applicant's authority to occupy the Crown land, proof that an application for a disposition of the Crown land has been made or the applicant's request for a permit in relation to that Crown land;

heading: Applications for change approvals
paragraph: (j) if the proposed changes in and about the stream will be carried out, or proposed works related to the change in and about the stream will be constructed, by a person other than the applicant, the person's name, professional affiliation, if any, and a mailing address and telephone number at which the person may be contacted.

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph:
5
		  An application for a drilling authorization referred to in section 62 [drilling authorizations] of the Act must include all the following:

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (a) the information specified in section 3 (1) (a) [applications for licences and use approvals] of this regulation;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (b) the official name of the aquifer in respect of which the activity authorized by the drilling authorization is to occur, or, if there is no official name, a location description of the aquifer;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (c) the restricted activity referred to in section 62 (1) of the Act to which the application relates;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (d) a location description of the land on which the activity referred to in paragraph (c) will occur, including an accurate description of where on that land that activity will be carried out;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (e) the class of well and the water use purpose, if any, the water is or will be used for;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (f) the reason for the activity referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (g) the proposed start and finish dates for the activity referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (h) the name of the well driller, well pump installer or professional who will perform or supervise the activity referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (i) a description of the works or equipment to be used in respect of the activity referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (j) a description of the manner in which the activity referred to in paragraph (c) is proposed to be carried out;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (k) if the application relates to an existing well,

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (i)  the number assigned to any authorization issued in relation to the well,

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (ii)  the well identification plate number and well tag number of the well, if known,

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (iii)  any well reports that have been prepared in relation to the well, and

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (iv)  the results of any flow tests that have been conducted in relation to the well;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (l) if the application relates to a proposed new well,

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (i)  details of the proposed well, including, without limitation, the drilling method, well diameter and construction materials to be used, and

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (ii)  the target depth of the well;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (m) if the land described in paragraph (d) is owned by a person other than the applicant, the written consent of the land owner to the use of the person's land for any works or construction of any works;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (n) if the land described in paragraph (d) is Crown land, proof of the applicant's authority to occupy the Crown land, proof that an application for a disposition of the Crown land has been made or the applicant's request for a permit in relation to that Crown land;

heading: Applications for drilling authorizations
paragraph: (o) a drawing as described in section 3 (1) (p) showing the relevant boundaries and locations in relation to the application.

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph:
6
		  (1) An application for an amendment referred to in section 26 [amendment or substitution of authorization, change approval or permit] of the Act must include

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (a) the information specified in section 3 (1) (a) [applications for licences and use approvals] of this regulation,

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act

paragraph: (iii)  a location description of any land that is likely to be physically affected by the proposed works,

paragraph: (iv)  the name of the owner of any land described in subparagraph (ii) or (iii) that is not owned by the applicant,

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (v)  if the land described in subparagraph (ii) is Crown land, proof of the applicant's authority to occupy the Crown land, proof that an application for a disposition of the Crown land has been made by the applicant or the applicant's request for a permit in relation to that Crown land, and

paragraph: (vi)  a drawing as described in section 3 (1) (p) showing the relevant boundaries and the location of the proposed works,

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (f) if the application is under section 26 (1) (e) of the Act, identification of the error,

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (g) if the application is under section 26 (1) (f) of the Act, identification of the inconsistency,

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (h) if the application is under section 26 (1) (g) of the Act,

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (i)  the proposed new water use purposes and the quantities of water requested for each, and

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (ii)  the water use purposes to be deleted, if any, from the authorization and the quantities of water associated with those purposes, and

paragraph: (i) if the application is under section 26 (1) (i) of the Act, an explanation of how the error occurred.

paragraph: (a) the information described in subsection (1) (a), (b) and (c) of this section, and

heading: Applications for amendments under sections 26 and 62 (7) of Act
paragraph: (3) If an amendment proposed to a drilling authorization includes a change in the location of activities or works, the application must include

paragraph: (a) a location description of the land where the activities are proposed to take place or works are to be constructed,

paragraph: (b) in the case of privately owned land, the written consent of the owner of that land, unless the holder of the drilling authorization is the owner of the land,

paragraph: (a) signed by the applicant or the applicant's agent, and

heading: Applications must be signed, filed and include consents
paragraph: (b) filed with the decision maker.

heading: Applications must be signed, filed and include consents
paragraph: (2) An application under section 12 of the Act, other than an application for an apportionment referred to in section 28 [apportionment of rights under licence], must include the written consents, in a form acceptable to the decision maker, of each person described in paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection, as applicable, if the application is made by one person on the person's own behalf and on behalf of one or more other persons and the application will result in

heading: Applications must be signed, filed and include consents
paragraph: (a) one or more of those other persons co-holding the authorization, change approval or drilling authorization with the applicant, or

heading: Applications must be signed, filed and include consents
paragraph: (b) the issuance of authorizations, change approvals or drilling authorizations to one or more of those other persons.

heading: Applications must be signed, filed and include consents
paragraph: (3) If an application under section 12 of the Act, other than an application for an apportionment referred to in section 28 of the Act, relates to an existing authorization, change approval, drilling authorization or permit that is held by more than one person, the application must include the written consents of each co-holder to the application being made by the applicant on the co-holder's behalf.

heading: Notice requirements and objections
paragraph:
14
		  (1) A decision maker in respect of an application may require that notice of the application be given under section 13 (1) or (9) [objections to applications and decision maker initiatives] of the Act, and the decision maker may give notice under section 13 (14) of the Act, by publication, once each week for 3 consecutive weeks, in a printed or electronic newspaper that

heading: Notice requirements and objections
paragraph: (a) is published and circulates in the area in which the stream or aquifer to which the licence, use approval or change approval that is the subject of the application applies or is to apply, or

heading: Notice requirements and objections
paragraph: (b) is approved by the decision maker.

heading: Notice requirements and objections
paragraph: (2) At any time before a licence, use approval, change approval or amendment has been issued in respect of an application, a person may request that the decision maker in respect of the application give the person notice under section 13 (14) of the Act if the person

heading: Notice requirements and objections
paragraph: (a) is a person referred to in section 13 (1) (a) or (b) of the Act in relation to the application, and

heading: Notice requirements and objections
paragraph: (b) has not been given notice of the application under section 13 (1), (9) or (14) of the Act.

heading: Notice requirements and objections
paragraph: (3) A person given notice under section 13 (1), (9) or (14) of the Act may deliver the person's objection to the application within 30 days after the date the notice is given in accordance with section 117 (2) [delivery and publication of documents and information] of the Act.

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph:
15
		  (1) For the purposes of satisfying a decision maker as to a person's date of first use of groundwater from an aquifer, the person must provide all the following information to the decision maker:

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (a) the official name, if known, and otherwise a location description of the location of the aquifer that is the source of the groundwater;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (b) the location of each well from which the person diverts groundwater, either by location description or by reference to the location of a known feature, and the well identification plate number and well tag number of each well, if known;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (c) the water use purposes for which the person diverts groundwater from the aquifer;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (d) the land, mine or undertaking to which the water use is appurtenant and a location description of its location;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (e) the history of the use of groundwater in relation to the appurtenancy described in paragraph (d) from the aquifer, including, without limitation,

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (i)  the date from which, to the person's knowledge, any person made beneficial use of the groundwater in relation to that appurtenancy,

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (ii)  the quantity of water beneficially used by the person for each water use purpose identified under paragraph (c) in each year since the person owned the appurtenancy, and, to the extent known, the quantity of groundwater beneficially used for each water use purpose identified under paragraph (c) in each year of the period from the date referred to in subparagraph (i) to the date the person became the owner,

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (iii)  an explanation for any significant increases or decreases in the quantities referred to in subparagraph (ii) that occurred since the date referred to in subparagraph (i), and

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (iv)  any changes in the appurtenancy of the water use or the water use purposes of the water diverted from the aquifer that occurred since the date referred to in subparagraph (i) and a description of the changes.

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (2) A person must submit to the decision maker evidence of the information provided under subsection (1), which evidence may include, but is not limited to, the following:

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (a) well reports submitted under section 57 [well reports] of the Act, or a former Act, in respect of a well referred to in subsection (1) (b) of this section;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (b) in relation to beneficial use of groundwater referred to in subsection (1) (e),

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (i)  the results of water quality tests and the date of the tests,

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (ii)  the results of flow tests and the date of the tests,

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (iii)  pumping records,

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (iv)  in the case of a waterworks purpose, the number of connections to the waterworks, when the connections were established and the size of the population served under the waterworks licence,

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (v)  in the case of an irrigation purpose, the area of land, type of soil and type of crops irrigated, and

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (vi)  in the case of an industrial livestock and animal purpose, the number and type of livestock watered;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (c) invoices in relation to the construction or testing of the well or the installation of a well pump;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (d) copies of any of the following required in relation to the water use purpose for which the groundwater is diverted:

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (i)  a certificate of public convenience and necessity under the Utilities Commission Act;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (ii)  an environmental assessment certificate under the Environmental Assessment Act or a predecessor to that Act or a decision statement issued under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012 or a predecessor to that Act;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (iii)  a construction permit or an operating permit issued under the Drinking Water Protection Act;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (iv)  a building permit, occupancy permit, business licence, inspection report or other document issued by a municipality or regional district;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (v)  a licence of occupation or other privilege issued in relation to the use of Crown land;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (vi)  an approval under the Land Title Act of a subdivision plan;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (e) if the applicant is registered under the Water Protection Act, the registration number and evidence of the registration;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (f) signed statements from persons having information or knowledge respecting the person's beneficial use of water;

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (g) other evidence the person considers relevant or that is requested by the decision maker.

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (3) A person submitting information or evidence to a decision maker in relation to the person's date of first use of groundwater must include the person's signed declaration as to the origins of documents and the accuracy of information submitted.

heading: Evidence - date of first use
paragraph: (4) Despite this section, for the purpose of making orders or taking action in relation to water or works, an engineer may determine the date of first use of a person to whom section 6 (4) [use of water - unlicensed domestic user of groundwater] of the Act applies based on the records available to the engineer at the time of making the order or taking the action, including, without limitation, records related to the construction of a well or test results respecting the quantity or quality of water in a well.

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: 16		  For the purposes of section 15 (1) of the Act, a decision maker need not consider the environmental flow needs of a stream in relation to the following applications:

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (a) an application for a new authorization for a domestic purpose;

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (b) an application for a change approval;

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (c) an application for a drilling authorization in relation to an aquifer that is not hydraulically connected to the stream;

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (d) an application under section 26 [amendment or substitution of authorization, change approval or permit], 27 [transfer of appurtenancy] or 31 [abandonment of rights under an authorization] of the Act unless granting the application would result in

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (i)  a change in the point of diversion,

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  an increase in the rate of diversion, or

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (iii)  a change in the timing of water use;

heading: Environmental flow needs - exemptions
paragraph: (e) an application for a final licence.

heading: Sensitive streams designated
paragraph:
17
		  The streams named and described in Schedule B are designated as sensitive streams.

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph:
18
		  The decision maker considering an application for an authorization in respect of a sensitive stream may require that the applicant provide the following information:

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (a) a fish inventory of the stream;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (b) a flow or runoff analysis of the stream, including additional flow measurements for correlation of data;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (c) seasonal distribution of water demand from the stream, including for irrigation purposes;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (d) if there is a tributary or aquifer designated with the sensitive stream,

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (i)  the contribution to the sensitive stream of water from the tributary or aquifer, and

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (ii)  the seasonal distribution of water demand from the tributary or aquifer;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (e) an assessment of the fish habitat at the point of diversion, or proposed point of diversion, on the stream and in the area of the stream affected or that will be affected;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (f) the design of proposed works, including diversion structure and balancing and storage reservoirs;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (g) if appropriate, any specific water conservation measures that the applicant will use to minimize the amount of water used;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (h) whether material is to be removed from the stream or stream channel in connection with the works;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (i) proposed measures for the protection of natural materials and vegetation that contribute to the fish habitat of the stream and the stability of the stream channel;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (j) whether substances, sediment, debris or other material is to be deposited in the stream or stream channel in connection with the works;

heading: Applications respecting sensitive streams
paragraph: (k) a proposal for restoration of the worksite after the works have been completed.

heading: Mitigation requirements
paragraph:
19
		  It is a term and condition of a licence issued in respect of a sensitive stream that the holder implement mitigation measures to ensure that no significant adverse impact on a protected fish population or the aquatic ecosystem of the stream will occur or compensatory mitigation measures, as defined in section 21 [compensatory mitigation measures], that provide full compensation for any significant adverse impact on a protected fish population or the aquatic ecosystem of the stream.

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph:
20
		  (1) For the purposes of section 17 (2) [sensitive streams mitigation] of the Act, the mitigation measures that must be proposed under that subsection must include all the following in relation to the worksite for each of the project planning, design, construction and operational phases:

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (a) strategies relating to the timing for the construction of any proposed works;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (b) practices to be undertaken to ensure stream bank and channel stability;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (c) practices to be undertaken to provide for satisfactory fish migration;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (d) practices to be undertaken to ensure that fish are not injured and their migration is not hindered by structures, pumping devices or construction activities;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (e) practices and procedures to be undertaken to maintain water quality in the stream;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (f) measures to be undertaken to restore the stream channel to the state that exists before the work proposed by the application begins;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (g) measurement and reporting of water use;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (h) measures to be undertaken in respect of water conservation.

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (2) If, for the purposes of section 17 (3) of the Act, the decision maker imposes a term or condition on the authorization or change approval, or amendment to the authorization or change approval, that the holder implement mitigation measures, it is a term and condition of the authorization, change approval or amendment that the holder ensure that the following are monitored, by a person whose qualifications are acceptable to the decision maker, to ensure that they are performed and maintained in accordance with the Act, the regulations and the authorization, change approval or amendment:

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (a) the construction of the works authorized under the authorization, change approval or amendment;

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (b) the implementation of the mitigation measures required under the authorization, change approval or amendment.

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (3) It is a term and condition of an authorization, change approval or amendment referred to in subsection (2) that the monitoring required under that subsection may be discontinued only if

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (a) the person whose qualifications are acceptable to the director under subsection (2) certifies in writing that all works have been completed and are functioning as required, and

heading: Mitigation measures
paragraph: (b) the holder of the authorization or change approval is relieved of the monitoring and maintenance requirement by the comptroller or a water manager or, in the case of a change approval, by an engineer.

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph:
21
		  (1) In this section, "compensatory mitigation measures" means compensatory mitigation measures described in section 17 (3) (a) (iii) [sensitive streams mitigation] of the Act.

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (2) If a decision maker considers that mitigation measures proposed under section 17 (2) of the Act in relation to an application respecting a sensitive stream would not satisfy the requirements of that section, the decision maker may require that the applicant submit a proposal for compensatory mitigation measures that complies with this section.

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (3) The measures proposed for compensatory mitigation must

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (a) be in relation to the same species of fish as the fish population whose sustainability is at risk,

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (b) provide the same type of fish habitat as the fish habitat used by the fish population whose sustainability is at risk, and

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (c) result in an area of fish habitat that is at least the size of the fish habitat that will be lost.

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (4) A proposal for compensatory mitigation for fish habitat in a sensitive stream must provide for mitigation measures to be taken at the following locations in the following order of priority until the proposal satisfies subsection (3):

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (a) at a different location on the sensitive stream;

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (b) within the watershed in which the sensitive stream is located;

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (c) within another area immediately adjacent to that watershed that has similar physiography and macroclimate as that watershed.

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
