paragraph: (5) If, for the purposes of section 17 (3) of the Act, the decision maker imposes a term or condition on the authorization or change approval, or amendment to the authorization or change approval, that the holder implement compensatory mitigation measures, it is a term and condition of the authorization, change approval or amendment that the holder ensure the following are monitored, by a person whose qualifications are acceptable to the decision maker, to ensure that they are performed and maintained in accordance with the Act, the regulations and the authorization, change approval or amendment:

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (a) the construction of the works authorized under the authorization, change approval or amendment;

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (b) the implementation of the compensatory mitigation measures required under the authorization, change approval or amendment.

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (6) It is a term and condition of an authorization, change approval or amendment referred to in subsection (5) that the monitoring required under that subsection may be discontinued only if

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (a) the person whose qualifications are acceptable to the director under subsection (5) certifies in writing that all works have been completed and are functioning as required, and

heading: Compensatory mitigation measures
paragraph: (b) the holder of the authorization or change approval is relieved of the monitoring and maintenance requirement by the comptroller or a water manager or, in the case of a change approval, by an engineer.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
22
		  (1) In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "affected land" means land expropriated or proposed to be expropriated under section 32 [licensee's right to expropriate land] of the Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "benefiting land" means the land, mine or undertaking to which a licence referred to in section 32 (1), (2) or (3) of the Act is appurtenant;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "court" means the Supreme Court.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) In sections 32 and 33 [licensee's rights when owner refuses compensation] of the Act, and in this Division, "land" includes an easement over land.

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council consent to flood
paragraph:
23
		  A licensee requiring consent for an expropriation under section 32 (3) of the Act may petition the Lieutenant Governor in Council by submitting to the minister a request that sets out, in a form acceptable to the minister,

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council consent to flood
paragraph: (a) details of the proposed expropriation,

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council consent to flood
paragraph: (b) the reason for the proposed expropriation,

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council consent to flood
paragraph: (c) the potential benefits of the expropriation to the licensee, and

heading: Lieutenant Governor in Council consent to flood
paragraph: (d) an assessment of the potential impacts of the expropriation on the affected land.

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph:
24
		  (1) A licensee, including a licensee referred to in section 23, who has a right under section 32 of the Act to expropriate land, may commence expropriation proceedings if the licensee intends to exercise the right and is unable to reach agreement with the owners of the affected land as to

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (a) the land reasonably required to be expropriated,

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (b) the amount of compensation, or

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (c) the terms of the required conveyance or other legal instrument.

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (2) A licensee may commence expropriation proceedings by filing with the comptroller and the registrar, and by personally serving on each owner of affected land, the following documents:

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (a) a notice of intent to acquire the affected land;

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (b) a plan showing the area the licensee wishes to acquire;

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (c) a draft of the legal instrument necessary to vest in the licensee the title to or right over that land, which legal instrument includes

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (i)  legal descriptions of the affected land and the benefiting land, and

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (ii)  a description of the works to be constructed, maintained, improved or operated within the affected land;

heading: Commencement of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (d) a statement of the amount of compensation offered.

heading: Substituted service
paragraph:
25
		  If the comptroller is satisfied that an expropriating licensee has been unable, after reasonable efforts, to effect personal service on an owner of affected land, the comptroller may order substituted service of the documents referred to in section 24 (2) in accordance with the order.

heading: Amendment of documents after commencement
paragraph:
26
		  (1) At any time before an application is made under section 28 [applications to Supreme Court], the expropriating licensee may amend the documents referred to in section 24 (2) [commencement of expropriation proceedings].

heading: Amendment of documents after commencement
paragraph: (2) If an expropriating licensee makes an amendment under subsection (1), the expropriating licensee must refile and personally serve the amended documents in accordance with section 24 (2) or 25, as applicable.

heading: Owner may refuse or accept offer of compensation
paragraph:
27
		  If an owner of affected land intends to accept the compensation offered and execute the legal instrument referred to in section 24 (2) (c), the owner must notify the expropriating licensee and the comptroller of that intention within 30 days after being served under section 24 (2) or 25, as applicable.

heading: Applications to Supreme Court
paragraph:
28
		  When the 30-day period referred to in section 27 expires, the expropriating licensee or an owner of the affected land may commence an action in the court for a determination of any matter referred to in section 24 (1) (a), (b) or (c).

heading: Procedures on application and method and basis of compensation
paragraph:
29
		  (1) On application under section 28, the court must determine the matters referred to in that section and, for that purpose, subject to subsection (2), the court has all powers of the court under the Expropriation Act.

heading: Procedures on application and method and basis of compensation
paragraph: (2) Section 26 (1) (b), as it relates to section 19 (4), and sections 26 (1) (d), 27, 31 to 44 and 50 of the Expropriation Act apply in respect of a proceeding commenced under section 28 of this regulation, and, for that purpose, a reference in those sections to a term set out in Column 1 of the following table has the meaning set out opposite in Column 2:

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: 30		  (1) Subject to subsections (3) to (5) and (8), the owner of affected land that is expropriated is entitled to be paid costs necessarily incurred by the owner for the purpose of asserting the owner's claim for compensation or damages.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (2) If the court makes an order for compensation or damages to which a person is entitled, the court must also determine the reasonable costs of the expropriation proceedings in accordance with this section.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (3) If the compensation awarded to the owner of affected land is greater than 115% of the amount of compensation, as set out in the statement referred to in section 24 (2) (d) [commencement of expropriation proceedings], offered by expropriating licensee, the court must award costs to the owner of the affected land and include the costs in the award of compensation.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (4) If the compensation awarded to the owner of affected land is greater than 100% but not greater than 115% of the amount of compensation, as set out in the statement referred to in section 24 (2) (d), offered by the expropriating licensee, the court may award all or part of the owner's costs to the owner of the affected land and the court must, if it awards any costs to the owner, include the amount of the costs in the award of compensation.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (5) If the compensation awarded to the owner of affected land is 100% or less of the amount of compensation offered to the owner, as set out in the statement referred to in section 24 (2) (d), the court may award costs to

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (a) the owner of the affected land and include the costs in the award of compensation, or

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (b) the expropriating licensee.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (6) If the court awards costs to the expropriating licensee under subsection (5), the court must deduct the amount of costs from the award of compensation.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (7) The costs payable under subsection (3), (4) or (5) are the costs described in section 45 (7) (a) and (b) of the Expropriation Act.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (8) Section 45 (6) and (8) of the Expropriation Act applies for the purposes of this section.

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (9) In a determination of the amount of costs to be paid, the following considerations apply:

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (a) the degree of success of the party, taking into account the determination of the issues;

heading: Costs of expropriation proceedings
paragraph: (b) the manner in which the case was prepared and conducted.

heading: Exemption - corridor drainage
paragraph: 31		  (1) In this section, "corridor ditch" means a ditch constructed alongside a road or a railway line, for the purpose of draining surface runoff from the road surface or railway bed or to divert water from an aquifer to lower the water table, to protect the road or railway line.

heading: Exemption - corridor drainage
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion of water from an aquifer using a corridor ditch if

heading: Exemption - corridor drainage
paragraph: (a) there is no use of the water for a water use purpose between the time the water enters the corridor ditch and the time that water is discharged from the corridor ditch, and

heading: Exemption - corridor drainage
paragraph: (b) that water is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph:
32
		  (1) In this section and section 34:

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: "drainage works" means works belonging to or used by a local government to drain surface runoff, or to divert water from an aquifer to lower the water table, to prevent a nuisance;

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: "local government" means

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: (a) a municipality,

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: (b) a regional district that operates drainage works as a service, or

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: (c) an improvement district that operates drainage works under its letters patent.

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: (2) A local government is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion of water from an aquifer using drainage works if

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: (a) there is no use of the water for a water use purpose between the time the water enters the drainage works and the time that water is discharged from the drainage works, and

heading: Exemption - local government drainage works
paragraph: (b) that water is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Exemption - agricultural drainage
paragraph:
33
		  (1) In this section, "agricultural drainage works" means ditches or subsurface drain pipes or other conduits used to drain surface runoff or to divert water from an aquifer to lower the water table to improve the productivity of agricultural land.

heading: Exemption - agricultural drainage
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion of water from an aquifer using agricultural drainage works if

heading: Exemption - agricultural drainage
paragraph: (a) there is no use of the water for a water use purpose between the time the water enters the agricultural drainage works and the time the water is discharged from the agricultural drainage works, and

heading: Exemption - agricultural drainage
paragraph: (b) that water is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Exemption - building perimeter drainage
paragraph:
34
		  (1) In this section, "perimeter drainage works" means works, including, without limitation, curtain or French drains and sumps, that are constructed around the perimeter of a building to convey surface runoff and groundwater away from the foundation of the building.

heading: Exemption - building perimeter drainage
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion of water from an aquifer using perimeter drainage works if

heading: Exemption - building perimeter drainage
paragraph: (a) there is no use of the water for a water use purpose between the time the water enters the perimeter drainage works and the time that water is discharged from the perimeter drainage works, and

heading: Exemption - building perimeter drainage
paragraph: (b) that water is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Exemption - mine drainage works
paragraph:
34.1
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Exemption - mine drainage works
paragraph: "mine" has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Mines Act;

heading: Exemption - mine drainage works
paragraph: "mine drainage works" means works, including a drainage well as defined in section 35, located in or at a mine and used or intended to be used for diverting groundwater by discharging the groundwater from the mine to prevent interference with the operation of the mine and protect the mine.

heading: Exemption - mine drainage works
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion of groundwater from an aquifer using mine drainage works if

heading: Exemption - mine drainage works
paragraph: (a) there is no use of the groundwater for a water use purpose between the time the groundwater is diverted and the time the groundwater is discharged, and

heading: Exemption - mine drainage works
paragraph: (b) that groundwater is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Definitions - mineral exploration
paragraph: 34.2		  In this section and sections 34.3 to 34.5:

heading: Definitions - mineral exploration
paragraph: "mineral exploration activities" means activities, described in paragraph (a) of the definition of "mining activity" in section 1 of the Mines Act, performed in relation to minerals other than placer minerals;

heading: Definitions - mineral exploration
paragraph: "Mines Act permit" means a permit issued under section 10 of the Mines Act in relation to mineral exploration activities or placer mining activities;

heading: Definitions - mineral exploration
paragraph: "placer mining activities" means activities, described in the definition of "mining activity" in section 1 of the Mines Act, performed in relation to placer minerals and that involve the processing of less than 2 000 m3 of pay dirt per year.

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: 34.3		  (1) Subject to section 34.4 [rules for exemptions], a person who holds a Mines Act permit is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion and use of water for

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: (a) mineral exploration activities or placer mining activities, and

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: (b) a camp that

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: (i)  is operated and maintained in relation to activities conducted under the permit, and

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: (ii)  provides living quarters for no more than 20 people.

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: (2) Subject to section 34.4, a person who is exempt from the requirement to hold a Mines Act permit is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion and use of water for mineral exploration activities if

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: (a) the activities are conducted using only mechanical hand drills or mechanical rock saws, and

heading: Exemptions - mineral exploration
paragraph: (b) the tools referred to in paragraph (a) are designed to be carried and used by a single person only.

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: 34.4		  (1) A person who is exempt under section 34.3 [exemptions - mineral exploration] must comply with this section.

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (2) A person must not, under section 34.3, divert or use recorded water.

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (3) A person must not, under section 34.3, divert or use unrecorded water from any of the following:

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (a) a stream or aquifer in respect of which there is a water reservation under section 40 [treaty first nation water reservations] or 41 [Nisga'a water reservation] of the Act;

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (b) a sensitive stream;

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (c) a point of diversion on a stream if the point of diversion is within the boundaries of a protected area, as defined in section 46;

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (d) a stream to which a regulation under section 82 [plan regulations - dedicated agricultural water] of the Act applies;

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (e) a stream to which an order under section 86 [declarations of significant water shortage] or 87 [critical environmental flow protection orders] of the Act applies or an aquifer affected by such an order;

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (f) a stream or aquifer to which an order under section 88 [fish population protection orders] of the Act applies.

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (4) A person who, under section 34.3, diverts or uses water from a stream must not construct, install or place any permanent or semi-permanent works in the stream channel.

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (5) A person who, under section 34.3, diverts or uses water from a stream must

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (a) remove from the stream channel any pump, equipment or material constructed, installed or placed by that person in diverting or using water from the stream,

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (b) ensure that the intake line or other device for diverting water is equipped with a screen, or otherwise modified, to

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (i)  prevent potential loss of fish due to entrainment or impingement, and

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  minimize disturbance of, or removal of sand and gravel from, the stream channel, and

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (c) ensure that

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (i)  any disturbance of a stream channel or of the stable natural materials and vegetation in and about the stream is minimized when gaining access to water from the stream,

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  any water that is diverted is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property,

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (iii)  the water supply and works of persons who are lawfully diverting or using water under the Act are not adversely affected, and

heading: Rules for exemptions
paragraph: (iv)  the diversion or use of water, whether from a stream or aquifer, does not cause a risk of significant harm to fish, wildlife or the aquatic ecosystem of a stream.

heading: Exception to exemptions
paragraph:
34.5
		  (1) In this section, "related aquifer" means an aquifer that an engineer considers is reasonably likely to be hydraulically connected to a stream.

heading: Exception to exemptions
paragraph: (2) Despite section 34.3, an engineer may require that an application for an authorization be made for the diversion or use of water for mineral exploration activities or placer mining activities, or for a camp described in section 34.3 (1) (b), if the engineer considers that a diversion or use of water from a stream or related aquifer

heading: Exception to exemptions
paragraph: (a) may have a significant adverse impact on

heading: Exception to exemptions
paragraph: (i)  the stream, including the flow of water within the stream, or

heading: Exception to exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  other authorized water users, or

heading: Exception to exemptions
paragraph: (b) may have an adverse impact on a cultural heritage resource within the meaning of the Mineral Tenure Act.

heading: Exception to exemptions
paragraph: (3) If an engineer imposes a requirement under subsection (2), section 34.3 does not apply to the diversion or use of water from the stream or related aquifer for the mineral exploration activities, placer mining activities or camp, as applicable.

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: 35		  (1) In this section:

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: "drainage well" has the same meaning as in the Groundwater Protection Regulation;

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: "remediation well" has the same meaning as in the Groundwater Protection Regulation.

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: (2) A person is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) [use of water] of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion of groundwater using a remediation well if

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: (a) there is no use of the groundwater for a water use purpose between the time the groundwater is diverted through the remediation well and the time that water is discharged, and

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: (b) that groundwater is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: (3) A person is exempt from the requirement under section 6 (1) of the Act to hold an authorization for the diversion of groundwater from a drainage well if

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: (a) there is no use of the groundwater for a water use purpose between the time the groundwater is diverted and the time that groundwater is discharged, and

heading: Exemption - wells
paragraph: (b) that groundwater is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Diversion and use of water for firefighting
paragraph:
35.1
		  A fire department may divert and use, including store, water without holding an authorization for the diversion and use if the diversion and use is for activities related to preparation for firefighting, including

heading: Diversion and use of water for firefighting
paragraph: (a) maintaining and testing fire equipment, and

heading: Diversion and use of water for firefighting
paragraph: (b) training firefighters,

heading: Diversion and use of water for firefighting
paragraph: and does not

heading: Diversion and use of water for firefighting
paragraph: (c) adversely affect the water supply or works of other persons who are diverting water with lawful authority under the Act,

heading: Diversion and use of water for firefighting
paragraph: (d) cause risk of significant harm to fish, wildlife or the aquatic ecosystem of the stream, or

heading: Diversion and use of water for firefighting
paragraph: (e) cause a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
36
		  (1) In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "acid-generating rock" means rock that when ground to paste has a paste pH of less than 4.5;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorized changes" means the changes in and about a stream described in section 39 (1), (2), (3) or (5) [authorized changes];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "clear span bridge" means a single span structure without piers that spans a stream channel from top of bank to top of bank with the bridge abutments outside the stream channel;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "culvert" means one or more pipes, pipe arches or structures, covered with soil and lying below the land surface, used to carry water, but does not include log structures;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "embankment" means a structure made of earth, gravel or similar material raised above the surrounding land surface;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "engineering professional" means a person who is registered under the Professional Governance Act as a professional engineer or professional licensee engineering;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "fish-bearing", in relation to a stream, means that the stream has a fish population present at some time during the year;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "habitat officer" means a public service employee or an employee of a government corporation designated in writing by the comptroller as a habitat officer for the purposes of this Part;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "public utility" has the same meaning as in the Utilities Commission Act and includes a similar utility regulated by Canada.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) A habitat officer has the powers of an officer under section 89 [right of access to land and premises by authorized persons] of the Act for the purpose of exercising powers and performing duties assigned to the habitat officer under this Part.

heading: Authority to make changes in and about a stream
paragraph: 37		  (1) A person may make an authorized change without holding an authorization or change approval authorizing the changes if

heading: Authority to make changes in and about a stream
paragraph: (a) the person satisfies the requirements in relation to making changes in and about a stream that are imposed by this Part, and

heading: Authority to make changes in and about a stream
paragraph: (b) the changes in and about a stream are made in accordance with this Part, including, if applicable, the terms and conditions specified by a habitat officer under section 44 [protection of aquatic ecosystem].

heading: Authority to make changes in and about a stream
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if an engineer considers that an authorized change may have a significant adverse impact on the nature of the stream, including the flow of water in the stream, or the stream channel, the engineer may require that an application for a change approval or an authorization be made in connection with the change.

heading: Authority to make changes in and about a stream
paragraph: (3) If an engineer imposes a requirement under subsection (2), the authorized change may not be carried out under this Part.

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph:
38
		  (1) A person proposing to make an authorized change, other than an authorized change described in section 39 (1) (o) to (s), (2) and (5), must

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (a) provide a notice, signed by the person or the person's agent, to a habitat officer of the particulars of the proposal at least 45 days before beginning the authorized change, and

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (b) obtain from a habitat officer a statement of the terms and conditions described in section 44 (2) [protection of aquatic ecosystem] on which the authorized change can proceed.

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) must

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (a) be in a form approved by the comptroller, and

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (b) include the information specified in section 4 [applications for change approvals].

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (3) Section 12 [consents respecting personal information] applies in relation to a notice under this section.

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (1), if a person who has given notice under that subsection is not contacted by a habitat officer within 45 days after the notice is received by a habitat officer, the person may proceed with the authorized change that is the subject of the notice.

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (5) A person who makes an authorized change described in section 39 (1) (o) or (p) must

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (a) report the authorized change to a habitat officer within 72 hours after making the change, and

heading: Notice to habitat officer
paragraph: (b) comply with the terms and conditions, if any, specified by a habitat officer in relation to matters described in section 44 (2).

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph:
39
		  (1) The following changes in and about a stream are authorized changes:

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (a) the installation, maintenance or removal of a culvert for crossing a stream for the purposes of a road, trail or footpath, if all the following conditions are met:

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  the equipment used for site preparation, or for installation, construction, maintenance or removal of the culvert, is situated in a dry stream channel or operated from the top of the bank;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  if the stream is fish-bearing, the culvert allows fish in the stream to pass up or down stream under all flow conditions;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iii)  the culvert inlet and outlet incorporate measures to protect the structure and the stream channel against erosion;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iv)  debris can pass through the culvert;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (v)  the installation, maintenance or removal of the culvert does not destabilize the stream channel;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (vi)  the culvert and its approach roads do not produce a backwater effect or increase the head of the stream;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (vii)  the culvert capacity is equivalent to the hydraulic capacity of the stream channel or is capable of passing the 1 in 200 year maximum daily flow without the water level at the culvert inlet exceeding the top of the culvert;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (viii)  the culvert has a minimum equivalent diameter of 600 mm;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ix)  if the culvert has an equivalent diameter of 2 m or greater, or has a design capacity to pass a flow of more than 6 m3 per second, the culvert is designed by an engineering professional and constructed in conformance with that design;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (x)  the culvert is installed in a manner that permits the removal of obstacles and debris within the culvert and at the culvert ends;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (xi)  if the changes in and about the stream are related to a right of way, the stream channel, except the portion within the right of way, is not altered;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (xii)  embankment fill materials do not, and are unlikely to, encroach on culvert inlets and outlets;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (xiii)  the culvert has a depth of fill cover that is at least 300 mm or as required by the culvert manufacturer's specifications;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (xiv)  the maximum fill heights above the top of the culvert do not exceed 2 m;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (xv)  the culvert is made of materials that meet the applicable standards of the Canadian Standards Association;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (b) the construction, maintenance or removal of a clear span bridge, if all the following conditions are met:

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  the equipment used for site preparation, or for construction, maintenance or removal of the bridge is situated in a dry stream channel or operated from the top of the bank;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  the bridge and its approach roads do not produce a back water effect or increase the head of the stream;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iii)  the hydraulic capacity of the bridge is equivalent to the hydraulic capacity of the stream channel, or is capable of passing the 1 in 200 year maximum daily flow;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iv)  the height of the underside of the bridge is adequate to provide free passage of flood debris and ice flows;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (v)  the bridge is made of materials that meet the applicable standards of the Canadian Standards Association;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (c) the construction or maintenance of a pipeline crossing of a stream, if either of the following conditions is met:

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  the pipeline and associated works are installed in a dry stream channel at a depth so that the top of the pipe is at least 1 m below the lowest elevation of the bed of the stream;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of an aerial crossing, the crossing is constructed in accordance with the conditions of paragraph (b) for clear span bridges;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (d) the construction, maintenance or removal of a pier or wharf in a stream, if the ebb and flow of water and the movement of material under the influence of waves or currents is not obstructed;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (e) the construction, maintenance or removal by the Crown in right of either Canada or British Columbia of a flow or water level measuring device in a stream;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (f) the construction or removal by the Crown in right of either Canada or British Columbia of a fish fence, fish screen or fish or game guard across a stream if the fence, screen or guard is designed, constructed, maintained and used in a manner that does not obstruct the flow of water in the stream;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (g) the restoration or maintenance of a stream channel by the government;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (h) the restoration or maintenance of a stream channel by a municipality or regional district;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i) the mechanical or manual cutting of annual vegetation within a stream channel;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (j) the restoration or maintenance of fish habitat by the Crown in right of either Canada or British Columbia;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (k) the repair or maintenance of existing dikes or existing erosion protection works to their original state, if the dikes or works were functional during the previous year;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (l) the construction or maintenance of storm sewer outfalls, if both the following conditions are met:

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  the storm sewer outfall is designed by an engineering professional;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  the storm sewer outfall is constructed, maintained and used in a manner that does not obstruct the flow of water in the stream or cause erosion of the stream channel;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (m) the mechanical or manual control of Eurasian watermilfoil and other invasive species of aquatic vegetation by a land owner, a municipality, a regional district or the Greater Vancouver Water District, or an improvement district or other body, established or continued under an enactment, that has jurisdiction in relation to the control of invasive aquatic vegetation;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (n) the construction or maintenance of ice bridges, winter fords or snowfills if,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  in the cases of ice bridges, winter fords or snowfills, only clean ice and snow are used in the construction or maintenance and are removed from the stream channel before ice breakup, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  in the case of ice bridges, any logs, timber and other structural materials used are removed, before ice breakup, without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (o) the construction or placement, under the direction of the Crown in right of British Columbia, a municipality or a regional district, or an agent of any of them, of erosion protection works or flood protection works during any of the following that involves flooding:

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  a declaration of a state of local emergency, as defined in section 175 of the Emergency and Disaster Management Act;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  a declaration of a state of provincial emergency, or a declaration of a state of local emergency, made under the Emergency and Disaster Management Act;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (p) the clearing of an obstruction from a bridge or culvert by the Crown in right of British Columbia, a municipality or a regional district during a flood, if the obstruction is causing or has the potential to cause a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (q) the installation or cleaning of drainage outlets;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (r) the repair or maintenance of the superstructure of a bridge, other than the bridge's foundation;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (s) the installation, repair, maintenance or removal of a fence, if the fencing materials

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  are not in the stream channel,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  do not block debris in the stream channel, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iii)  do not interfere with navigation of the stream;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (t) maintenance of a minor and routine nature by a public utility of its works;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (u) the removal of a beaver dam under section 9 of the Wildlife Act, if the removal is carried out in such a manner that downstream flooding and erosion do not occur;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (v) the construction of a temporary ford for vehicular traffic across a stream, if

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  the construction occurs at a time in the year during which the construction can occur without causing a risk of significant harm to fish, wildlife or the aquatic ecosystem of the stream,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  the 1 in 10 year maximum daily flow over the ford is accommodated without the loss of the ford and without eroding the stream channel,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iii)  any culvert is designed and installed to pass the average low flow for the period of use,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iv)  the stream channel is protected against any anticipated erosion

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (A) for the period of construction and use of the ford, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (B) after the ford is removed,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (v)  sediment from approach ditches does not enter the stream,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (vi)  the driveable running surface is erosion-free,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (vii)  the stream remains in its channel,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (viii)  channel debris will pass over the ford, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ix)  the ford is removed at the end of the period of use at a time when the removal can proceed without causing a risk of significant harm to fish, wildlife or the aquatic ecosystem of the stream;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (w) the construction of a temporary diversion around or through a worksite for the purposes of constructing or maintaining bridge abutments, constructing or maintaining piers other than bridge piers, maintaining bridge piers or constructing works authorized under this section, if

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  the size of the worksite is minimized,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  any pumps, pipes or conduits used to divert water around or through the worksite are sized to divert the 1 in 10 year maximum daily flow for the period of construction,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iii)  any pump or intake withdrawing water from a fish-bearing stream is screened to prevent potential loss of fish due to entrainment or impingement,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (iv)  any cofferdams used to isolate successive parts of the construction occurring at the worksite are designed by an engineering professional and constructed in accordance with that design,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (v)  the natural channel remaining outside of any cofferdams is adequate to pass the 1 in 10 year maximum daily flow for the period of construction,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (vi)  the flow of water diverted around the worksite using ditches remains within the stream channel,

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (vii)  any ditches used to divert the flow of water around the worksite are designed and constructed to divert the 1 in 10 year maximum daily flow around or through the worksite and are protected from any anticipated erosion for the period of construction and use of the ditch, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (viii)  any ditches are completely backfilled and the area returned as closely as possible to the state that existed before the changes in and about the stream were made;

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (x) the construction and maintenance of a dry hydrant in a stream if

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  the dry hydrant is designed by an engineering professional, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  the dry hydrant is constructed, maintained and used in a manner that does not cause erosion of the stream channel or sedimentation in the stream.

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (2) A change in and about a stream to which a standard or regulation under the Forest and Range Practices Act applies is an authorized change if

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (a) the change is made by

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  a municipality, a regional district or another person who

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (A) holds an agreement or road use permit under the Forest Act, an agreement under the Range Act or a special use permit under the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act, or

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (B) is authorized under the Coal Act, the Geothermal Resources Act, the Mining Right of Way Act or the Petroleum and Natural Gas Act to construct or modify a road, or

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  the Crown in right of British Columbia, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (b) the person making the change complies with the Forest and Range Practices Act and the regulations and standards established under that Act.

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (3) A change in and about a stream is an authorized change if

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (a) the change is made by a person who holds a permit under section 10 of the Mines Act, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (b) the person making the change complies with

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  Part 9 of the Health, Safety and Reclamation Code for Mines in British Columbia, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  the conditions included in the permit respecting changes in and about the stream.

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of section 38, an application for a permit to carry out exploration activities under section 10 of the Mines Act constitutes notice of the change.

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (5) A change in and about a stream is an authorized change if

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (a) the activities in relation to which the change in and about the stream is to be made are authorized by a permit issued under the Energy Resource Activities Act, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (b) the change in and about the stream is made in accordance with

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (i)  applicable regulations under the Energy Resource Activities Act, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (ii)  the conditions respecting changes in and about the stream included in the permit.

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (6) If a person making changes in and about a stream under subsection (5) causes damage to an aquatic ecosystem, which damage is not authorized under the Energy Resource Activities Act or the permit referred to in that subsection, the person must

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (a) report the damage to the British Columbia Energy Regulator within 72 hours after the damage is caused, and

heading: Authorized changes
paragraph: (b) take any action ordered under the Energy Resource Activities Act by an official, as defined in that Act, to repair the damage and restore the aquatic ecosystem.

heading: Limitation on making authorized changes under this Part
paragraph: 40		  A person must not, for any purpose related to making an authorized change in accordance with this Part, enter onto any private land or premises, or use any privately owned works, unless the person has the written consent of the owner of the land, premises or works.

heading: Obligations of persons making authorized changes under this Part
paragraph:
41
		  (1) A person making or proposing to make an authorized change, other than an authorized change described in section 39 (5) [authorized changes], in accordance with this Part must, on request of an engineer, officer or habitat officer, provide the information that the engineer, officer or habitat officer requires to assess the impact of the authorized changes on the nature of the stream or stream channel.

heading: Obligations of persons making authorized changes under this Part
paragraph: (2) A person making an authorized change in accordance with this Part must, once the person begins making the change, complete the authorized change without delay unless the delay is necessary to preserve the nature of the stream or stream channel.

heading: Obligations of persons making authorized changes under this Part
paragraph: (3) A person making an authorized change in accordance with this Part must ensure that the authorized change is designed, constructed and maintained so that the change does not pose a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Failure to comply with this Part when making authorized change
paragraph:
42
		  (1) If a person purporting to make an authorized change in accordance with this Part fails to comply with this Part, the person must

heading: Failure to comply with this Part when making authorized change
paragraph: (a) report the non-compliance to the closest regional office of the minister's ministry within 72 hours after the non-compliance,

heading: Failure to comply with this Part when making authorized change
paragraph: (b) take the measures, if any, specified by an engineer to remedy the effects of the non-compliance, and

heading: Failure to comply with this Part when making authorized change
paragraph: (c) comply with the terms and conditions, if any, specified by a habitat officer in relation to matters described in section 44 (2) [protection of aquatic ecosystem] to remedy the effects of the non-compliance.

heading: Failure to comply with this Part when making authorized change
paragraph: (2) Compliance with subsection (1) does not relieve a person of any other consequences that may be imposed under the Act for non-compliance.

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph:
43
		  (1) A person making an authorized change in accordance with this Part must ensure that

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph: (a) making the authorized change does not cause a significant adverse impact on the ambient water quality of the stream,

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph: (b) there is no disturbance or removal of stable natural materials and vegetation in and about the stream that contribute to stream channel stability except as authorized under this Part and in accordance with any terms and conditions specified by a habitat officer under section 44 (2) [protection of aquatic ecosystem],

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph: (c) temporary material, fill, bridges, culverts, pumps, pipes, conduits, ditches or other structures used to assist in the construction of any works are constructed and maintained only for the period of construction and are removed on completion of the works,

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph: (d) all cast-in-place concrete and grouting is completely separated from fish-bearing waters for a minimum of 48 hours,

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph: (e) rock from acid-generating rock formations is not used for construction, and

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph: (f) on completion of the authorized change the stream is restored to the state that existed before the authorized change was made.

heading: Protection of water quality
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (c) does not apply in relation to a person making an authorized change described in section 39 (5) [authorized changes].

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph:
44
		  (1) In this section, "timing window", in relation to a stream, means a period of the calendar year, specified under this section by a habitat officer, during which changes in and about the stream can be made without causing a risk of significant harm to fish, wildlife or the aquatic ecosystem of the stream.

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (2) A habitat officer may provide to a person carrying out or proposing to carry out an authorized change in accordance with this Part, for the protection of an aquatic ecosystem, a written statement containing terms and conditions applicable to the person in relation to the following:

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (a) the timing window during which the change may be made;

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (b) the minimum instream flow or the minimum flow of water that must remain in the stream while the change is being made;

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (c) the removal of material from the stream or stream channel in connection with the change;

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (d) the addition of a substance, sediment, debris or material to the stream or stream channel in connection with the change;

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (e) the salvage or protection of fish or wildlife while the change is being made or after the change has been made;

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (f) the protection of natural materials and vegetation that contribute to the aquatic ecosystem or stream channel stability;

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (g) the restoration of the worksite after the change has been made.

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (3) If a person making an authorized change in accordance with this Part, other than an authorized change described in section 39 (5) [authorized changes], causes damage to an aquatic ecosystem, the person must

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (a) report the damage to a habitat officer within 72 hours after the damage is caused, and

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (b) repair the damage and restore the aquatic ecosystem to the state that existed before the damage was caused, or as directed by the habitat officer.

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (4) Compliance with subsection (3) does not relieve a person of any other consequences that may be imposed under the Act in relation to the damage.

heading: Protection of other water users
paragraph:
45
		  (1) A person making an authorized change in accordance with this Part, other than a change described in section 39 (1) (o) to (s), (2) or (5) [authorized changes], must ensure that the water supply and works of persons who are lawfully diverting or using water under the Act will not be adversely affected.

heading: Protection of other water users
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if the water supply of persons who are lawfully diverting or using water under the Act may be adversely affected by making the authorized change, the person proposing to make the authorized change, other than a change described in section 39 (1) (o) to (s), (2) or (5), must

heading: Protection of other water users
paragraph: (a) give 3 days' notice to those persons before starting to make the change, and

heading: Protection of other water users
paragraph: (b) provide an adequate supply of water to those persons while making the change, if required by those persons.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
46
		  (1) In the Act and this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "develop", in relation to a well, has the same meaning as in the Groundwater Protection Regulation;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "protected area" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a park as defined in the Park Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a conservancy as defined in the Park Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a recreation area as defined in the Park Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) an ecological reserve established or continued under the Ecological Reserve Act, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) a park dedicated or reserved under section 29 or 30 of the Community Charter.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorized person" means a person authorized under section 47 (2) to divert and use water in accordance with this Part;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "rehabilitate", in relation to a well, has the same meaning as in the Groundwater Protection Regulation.

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph: 47		  (1) This Part applies to a professional or a well driller included in the register referred to in section 7 (a) (i) of the Groundwater Protection Regulation, or a person supervised by either, who diverts and uses water for the industrial purpose of drilling, altering, developing, rehabilitating or decommissioning a well.

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph: (2) A person referred to in subsection (1) may divert and use water in accordance with this Part without holding an authorization for the diversion and use.

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), if an engineer considers that a diversion or use of water from a stream, or an aquifer the engineer considers is reasonably likely to be hydraulically connected to a stream, may have a significant adverse impact on the stream, including the flow of water within the stream, the engineer may require that an application for an authorization be made for that diversion or use of water.

heading: Application of this Part
paragraph: (4) If an engineer imposes a requirement under subsection (3), the diversion or use of water may not be carried out under this Part.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph:
48
		  (1) An authorized person must not, for the purposes of diverting or using water in accordance with this Part, enter onto any private land or premises, or use any privately owned works, unless the person has the written consent of the owner of the land, premises or works.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (2) An authorized person must not, under this Part,

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (a) divert water from any one location on a stream or aquifer for more than 5 successive days,

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (b) divert water from a stream or aquifer for more than 10 days in any calendar month, or

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (c) divert more than 10 m3 of water per day from a stream or aquifer.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (3) An authorized person must not, under this Part, divert or use water from

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (a) a wetland,

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (b) a point of diversion on a stream if the point of diversion is within the boundaries of a protected area,

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (c) a stream, other than a lake, unless the width of the flowing water in the stream channel is at least 5 m at surface level, or

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (d) a lake, unless the surface area of the lake is at least one hectare.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (4) An authorized person must not, under this Part, divert or use recorded water.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (5) An authorized person must not, under this Part, divert or use unrecorded water from

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (a) a stream or aquifer in respect of which there is a water reservation under section 39 [water reservations], 40 [treaty first nation water reservations] or 41 [Nisga'a water reservation] of the Act,

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (b) a sensitive stream,

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (c) a stream to which a regulation under section 82 [plan regulations - dedicated agricultural water] of the Act applies,

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (d) a stream to which an order under section 86 [declarations of significant water shortage] or 87 [critical environmental flow protection orders] of the Act applies or an aquifer affected by such an order, or

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (e) a stream or aquifer to which an order under section 88 [fish population protection orders] of the Act applies.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (6) An authorized person who, under this Part, diverts or uses water from a stream must not construct, install or place any permanent or semi-permanent works in the stream channel.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (7) An authorized person who, under this Part, diverts or uses water from a stream must remove from the stream channel any pump, equipment or material constructed, installed or placed by that person in diverting or using water from the stream.

heading: Limitations on diversion under this Part
paragraph: (8) An authorized person may divert and use groundwater under this Part only if the diversion is carried out using existing works that are either authorized under the Act or do not require authorization under the Act.

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph:
49
		  (1) An authorized person must not, under this Part, divert water from a stream at any time or in any period when the diversion or use would cause a risk of significant harm to fish, wildlife or the aquatic ecosystem of the stream.

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (2) An authorized person who, under this Part, diverts water from a stream must ensure that the intake line or other device for diverting the water is equipped with a screen, or otherwise modified, to

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (a) prevent potential loss of fish due to entrainment or impingement, and

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (b) minimize disturbance of, or removal of sand and gravel from, the stream channel.

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (3) An authorized person who, under this Part, diverts or uses water from a stream must ensure that

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (a) any disturbance of the stream channel or of the stable natural materials and vegetation in and about the stream is minimized when gaining access to water from the stream, and

heading: Protection of aquatic ecosystem
paragraph: (b) any water that is diverted from the stream but is not used for the purpose of drilling, altering, developing, rehabilitating or decommissioning a well is discharged without causing a significant risk of harm to public safety, the environment, land or other property.

heading: Protection of other water users
paragraph:
50
		  An authorized person who, under this Part, diverts or uses water from a stream or an aquifer must ensure that the water supply and works of persons who are lawfully diverting or using water under the Act are not adversely affected.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
51
		  In this Part:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "base of fish scales marker" is a stratum of the earth's surface, within the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin, that demarcates the boundary between the sedimentary rocks of the Lower Cretaceous Age from the sedimentary rocks of the Upper Cretaceous Age and is characterized by

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the presence of abundant fish scales and skeletal material,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a high concentration of organic carbon, and

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) groundwater that is found in the subject area

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  below the base of fish scales marker, or if there is no base of fish scales marker, below strata that are older than the base of fish scales marker, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  at a depth greater than 300 m below the earth's surface;

paragraph: "group" has the same meaning as in the Petroleum and Natural Gas Grid Regulation;

paragraph: "subject area" means the areas described, by reference to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Grid Regulation, in the following table:

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph:
52
		  (1) A person may divert from a water source well and use deep groundwater in accordance with this Part without holding an authorization.

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph: (2) A person must not divert deep groundwater under this Part unless

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph: (a) the use is an oil and gas purpose,

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph: (b) the person holds a well permit, as defined in the Drilling and Production Regulation, in relation to the well,

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph: (c) the deep groundwater that is diverted is unrecorded water,

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph: (d) the diversion and use are in the subject area, and

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph: (e) the diversion does not adversely affect the water supply or works of a person lawfully diverting and using water from the same aquifer, another aquifer or a stream.

heading: Conditions on diversion and use of deep groundwater
paragraph: (3) Deep groundwater may be diverted and used in accordance with this Part in any quantity and at any time of the year.

heading: When diversion and use must stop
paragraph:
53
		  (1) A water manager may order a person to stop diverting and using deep groundwater under this Part if the water manager considers on reasonable grounds that

heading: When diversion and use must stop
paragraph: (a) the diversion of deep groundwater from the well is having an adverse impact on the rights of a person who is lawfully diverting and using water from the same aquifer, another aquifer or a stream, or

heading: When diversion and use must stop
paragraph: (b) there is a significant and imminent risk that the continued diversion of deep groundwater from the well will have an adverse impact on the rights of a person who is lawfully diverting and using water from the same aquifer, another aquifer or a stream.

heading: When diversion and use must stop
paragraph: (2) This Part ceases to apply to a person, and the person must immediately stop the diversion and use,

heading: When diversion and use must stop
paragraph: (a) in the circumstances described in subsection (1) (a), or

heading: When diversion and use must stop
paragraph: (b) if a water manager makes an order under subsection (1)

heading: When diversion and use must stop
paragraph: until the person holds an authorization for the diversion and use or, in the case of an order under subsection (1), the order is rescinded.

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph:
54
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences and penalties

paragraph: (j) section 43 (1) (c);

paragraph: (k) section 44 (3) (a) [protection of aquatic ecosystem];

paragraph: (l) section 44 (3) (b);

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (m) section 45 (1) [protection of other water users];

heading: Offences and penalties

heading: Offences and penalties

paragraph: (p) section 35.1 (c) [diversion and use of water for firefighting];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (q) section 35.1 (d);

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (r) section 35.1 (e).

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (2) An authorized person, as defined in section 46 [definitions], who contravenes any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) section 48 (7) [limitations on diversion under this Part];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) section 49 (1) [protection of aquatic ecosystem];

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (c) section 49 (3) (a);

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (d) section 49 (3) (b);

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (e) section 50 [protection of other water users].

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (3) The owner of a well being used under Part 5 [Use of Deep Groundwater] who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (a) diverts or uses deep groundwater under section 52 contrary to a condition set out in section 52 (2) (a) to (e);

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (b) fails to terminate the diversion and use of deep groundwater when required under section 53 (2) (a) or (b).

heading: Offences and penalties
paragraph: (4) A person who commits an offence under this section is liable on conviction to the penalties set out in section 106 (6) [general offences] of the Act.

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A person to whom section 140 (1) of the Act applies must apply on or before March 1, 2022 for an authorization authorizing the person's diversion and use of water from an aquifer.

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (2) Subject to this section, the Act and the regulations apply in relation to an application under subsection (1).

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (3) Despite section 12 (1) (b) (ii) [application and decision maker initiative procedures] of the Act, if an application under subsection (1) of this section is received on or before March 1, 2022, the applicant is exempt from the requirement to pay an application fee.

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (4) Applications under subsection (1) are exempt from section 15 (1) [environmental flow needs] of the Act.

heading: Transition - groundwater licensing
paragraph: (5) For the purposes of section 22 (1) [precedence of rights] of the Act, the date set out in an authorization issued in relation to an application under subsection (1) of this section is to be the person's date of first use in relation to the diversion and use of water from the aquifer.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "compensation" means a rate, remuneration, gain or reward of any kind paid, payable, promised, demanded, received or expected, directly or indirectly, and includes a promise or undertaking by a water utility to provide service as consideration for, or as part of, a proposal or contract to dispose of land or any interest in it;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "comptroller" means the person designated as the Comptroller of Water Rights under section 114 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "service" includes

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the use and accommodation provided, and a product or commodity furnished, by a water utility, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the plant, equipment, apparatus, appliances, property and facilities employed by or in connection with a water utility in providing service or in furnishing a product or commodity for the purposes in which the water utility is engaged and for the use and accommodation of the public;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "tenant" does not include a lessee for a term of more than 5 years;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "water utility" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a person who owns or operates in British Columbia equipment or facilities for the diverting, developing, pumping, impounding, distributing or furnishing of water, for compensation,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  to or for more than the prescribed number of persons or, if no number is prescribed, 5 or more persons, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  to a corporation, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the lessee, trustee, receiver or liquidator of a person referred to in paragraph (a),

heading: Definitions
paragraph: but does not include

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a municipality in respect of services furnished by the municipality,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (d) a person who furnishes services or commodity only to the person, the person's employees or tenants, if the service or commodity is not resold to or used by others,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (e) the Greater Vancouver Water District under the Greater Vancouver Water District Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f) an improvement district as defined in section 1 (1) of the Water Sustainability Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (f.1) a water users' community as defined in section 1 (1) of the Water Users' Communities Act,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (g) a regional district under the Local Government Act in respect of the service of the supply of water

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  in bulk to a municipality or electoral area participating in that service, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (h) a person who supplies water by tanker truck,

heading: Definitions
