heading: Definitions
paragraph: (j) a strata corporation, if the comptroller is satisfied that the owner developers within the meaning of the Strata Property Act have ceased to own a majority of the strata lots in the strata plan.

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: 2		  (1) This Act applies only to water utilities that are subject to the legislative authority of British Columbia.

heading: Application of Act
paragraph: (2) If a water utility furnishes a class of service in respect of which the water utility is not subject to the legislative authority of British Columbia, nothing in this section operates to make this Act inapplicable to the water utility in respect of another class of service furnished in respect of which the water utility is subject to the legislative authority of British Columbia.

heading: Jurisdiction of comptroller
paragraph:
3
		  A water utility is subject to the regulation and control of the comptroller.

heading: Utilities Commission Act to apply
paragraph:
4
		  The duties, responsibilities and restraints to which a water utility is subject are the same as are imposed on a public utility under the Utilities Commission Act and the powers and jurisdiction of the comptroller in respect of a water utility are the same as are vested in the British Columbia Utilities Commission under the Utilities Commission Act, in respect of a public utility, and for these purposes

heading: Utilities Commission Act to apply
paragraph: (a) the water utility is deemed to be a public utility, and

heading: Utilities Commission Act to apply
paragraph: (b) the Utilities Commission Act, other than sections 2.1 (b), (c) and (k) to (m), 21.1, 28, 29, 44.1, 44.2, 45 (2), (3), (5) and (6), 58 (2.1) to (2.4), 58.1, 125.1 and 125.2, applies.

heading: Cancellation of certificate
paragraph: 5		  If the comptroller determines that public convenience and necessity do not or will not require the construction or operation of a plant or system by a water utility, the comptroller may cancel the certificate of public convenience and necessity issued to the water utility for that plant or system.

heading: Regulations
paragraph:
6
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (a) prescribing a number for the purposes of paragraph (a) of the definition of "water utility";

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (b) for the purpose of recovering the expenses arising out of the administration of this Act, prescribing fees, levies or other charges payable by water utilities and other persons;

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (c) exempting, or authorizing the comptroller to exempt, a water utility or other person, or a class of either of them, from the payment of a fee, levy or other charge.

heading: Regulations
paragraph: (3) Fees, levies and charges prescribed under this section may be different for different classes of water utility, different water utilities and different classes of persons.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "council" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the council of a municipality, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the board of a regional district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "inspector" means a person appointed by the minister under section 3, and includes a weed control officer appointed by a council under section 10;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "minister" includes a person designated in writing by the minister;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "municipality" includes a regional district;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "notice" means a notice issued by an inspector under section 4;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "noxious weed" means a weed designated by regulation to be a noxious weed, and includes the seeds of the noxious weed;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "occupier" means a person who

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is in physical possession of land, premises or property, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is responsible for, and has control over, the condition of, the activities conducted on and the persons allowed to enter or use, land, premises or property.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (2) For this Act

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) there may be more than one occupier of land, premises or property,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) a municipality may be an occupier of land, premises or property, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) the government may be an occupier of land, premises or property.

heading: Duty to control noxious weeds
paragraph:
2
		  In accordance with the regulations, an occupier must control noxious weeds growing or located on land and premises, and on any other property located on land and premises, occupied by that person.

heading: Appointment and powers of inspectors
paragraph:
3
		  (1) The minister may appoint inspectors for this Act under the Public Service Act.

heading: Appointment and powers of inspectors
paragraph: (2) At any time during daylight hours, an inspector may enter any land, premises, except a residence, and property for any purpose relating to the administration or enforcement of this Act or the regulations, and may inspect and examine the land, premises and property.

heading: Appointment and powers of inspectors
paragraph: (3) An inspector who enters land, premises or property under subsection (2) may require an occupier of the land, premises or property

heading: Appointment and powers of inspectors
paragraph: (a) to give the inspector all reasonable assistance in connection with the entry, inspection and examination,

heading: Appointment and powers of inspectors
paragraph: (b) to answer all proper questions relating to the inspection and examination, and

heading: Appointment and powers of inspectors
paragraph: (c) for the purposes of paragraphs (a) and (b), to attend at the land, premises or property with the inspector.

heading: Notice to control noxious weeds
paragraph: 4		  (1) An inspector may serve a notice directing an occupier, in accordance with the notice, to control noxious weeds growing or located on land, premises or property occupied by the occupier.

heading: Notice to control noxious weeds
paragraph: (2) If a notice is served on an occupier the occupier must promptly bring the notice to the attention of the owner of the land, premises or property that is the subject of the notice.

heading: Noxious weed control regulations
paragraph:
5
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations

heading: Noxious weed control regulations
paragraph: (a) to control noxious weeds on land, premises, property or a class of land, premises, or property, or

heading: Noxious weed control regulations
paragraph: (b) respecting a process or a class of process

heading: Noxious weed control regulations
paragraph: considered particularly susceptible to noxious weeds or to the injurious distribution or effect of noxious weeds.

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A notice must be in the prescribed form and contain the information required under the regulations.

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (2) A notice

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (a) may be served personally on the occupier to whom it is directed,

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (b) may be sent by registered mail addressed to the occupier to whom it is directed, or

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (c) may be left with any person who is, in the opinion of the inspector leaving the notice,

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (i)  over the age of 16 years, and

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (ii)  occupying residential or business premises on the land that is the subject of the notice.

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (3) If an inspector

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (a) is unable to serve a notice under subsection (2) and the inspector believes that the occupier to whom the notice is directed is evading service,

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (b) is unable to ascertain any occupier of the land, premises or property that is the subject of the notice, or

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: (c) is of the opinion that it is unreasonable or impractical to serve under subsection (2) the occupier to whom the notice is directed,

heading: Form of notice and method of service
paragraph: the inspector may serve the notice by posting it in a conspicuous place on the land, premises or property that is the subject of the notice, and the notice is served for the purposes of this Act at the expiration of 3 days immediately following the date that the notice was posted.

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (a) a notice is served under section 6 and, in the opinion of an inspector, noxious weeds are not controlled

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (i)  within the time, which must not be less than 5 days, specified in the notice, or

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (ii)  in the manner specified in the notice, or

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (b) an inspector is of the opinion that, in order to prevent the injurious distribution and effect of noxious weeds, it is necessary to immediately control the noxious weeds,

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: an inspector may, without notice, take the action considered necessary to enter on any land, premises or property and control noxious weeds.

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (2) If an inspector controls noxious weeds under subsection (1), the inspector must prepare a signed statement setting out the costs of the control and send the signed statement,

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (a) if the noxious weeds were controlled on land, premises or property in a municipality, other than a regional district, to the designated municipal officer, and

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (b) if the noxious weeds were controlled on land, premises or property other than that referred to in paragraph (a), to the minister.

heading: Control of noxious weeds by inspector
paragraph: (3) If the municipal officer or minister to whom a signed statement is sent under subsection (2) issues a certificate in respect of the amount of the signed statement, every occupier of the land, premises or property on which or in which the noxious weeds were controlled is jointly and severally liable to pay the amount specified in the certificate to the municipality or the minister.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph:
8
		  (1) If the amount specified in a certificate issued under section 7 is not paid, the municipal officer or minister who issued the certificate may,

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (a) if the noxious weeds were controlled on land or an improvement in a municipality, other than a regional district, send a certificate containing

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (i)  a legal description of the land,

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (ii)  a description of the improvement and legal description of the land on which it is located,

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (iii)  the name of the owner of the land or improvement, and

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (iv)  the total amount of the money owing,

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: to the duly appointed collector of taxes for that municipality, or

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (b) if the noxious weeds were controlled on land or an improvement, as defined in the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, which are not located in a municipality, other than a regional district, send the certificate referred to in paragraph (a) to the Surveyor of Taxes appointed under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act.

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (2) On receipt of a certificate referred to in subsection (1), the municipal collector or the Surveyor of Taxes must enter in the tax roll the amount set out in the certificate in respect of the land or improvement referred to in it, and the amount is then deemed for all purposes to be, as applicable,

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (a) taxes in arrear of the municipality under the Community Charter, or

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: (b) delinquent taxes under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act,

heading: Recovery of costs
paragraph: and the provisions for collection and recovery of taxes contained in those Acts apply to those amounts.

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: 9		  (1) The council of a municipality may establish one or more weed control committees, each consisting of

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (a) one member of the council appointed by the council,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (b) one resident in the municipality appointed by the council,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (c) one member of the ministry appointed by the minister,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (d) one member in good standing, appointed by the council, of a society, as defined in the Societies Act, that has as a primary purpose the protection of the environment or the encouragement of anti-pollution measures, and

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (e) one member appointed by the minister responsible for the Public Health Act.

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (2) A member of a weed control committee holds office for a period of one year.

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (3) If a council establishes a weed control committee under subsection (1), that council

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (a) must notify the minister in writing of the names of the persons appointed,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (b) must provide secretarial or clerical assistance for the weed control committee,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (c) must designate the member of the weed control committee appointed by council to be chair, and

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (d) may provide for the payment of expenses to weed control committee members.

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (4) A weed control committee must, with respect to its municipality,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (a) advise the minister and the council on all matters relating to noxious weeds and noxious weed control,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (b) compile a list of weeds that it considers to be noxious and to require control, and submit the list to the minister and the council,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (c) advise the council on the appointment of weed control officers, and supervise weed control officers,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (d) assist in the organization and administration of weed control programs,

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (e) not later than October 1 in each year, submit to the minister and the council an annual report, and estimates for the next year, respecting weed control matters, and

heading: Weed control committees
paragraph: (f) perform other duties the Lieutenant Governor in Council prescribes.

heading: Weed control officers
paragraph: 10		  (1) A council may appoint one or more inspectors and weed control officers to enforce and administer this Act in the municipality.

heading: Weed control officers
paragraph: (2) If an inspector is appointed by a council, it must notify the minister in writing of the name of the inspector.

heading: Weed control officers
paragraph: (3) If the minister is of the opinion that additional inspectors or weed control officers are required in a municipality for the purpose of effectively enforcing and administering this Act and the regulations in the municipality, the minister may appoint one or more inspectors for that purpose.

heading: Weed control agreements
paragraph:
11
		  (1) The councils of 2 or more municipalities may enter into an agreement respecting noxious weed control and an agreement respecting the costs of noxious weed control in all or part of those municipalities.

heading: Weed control agreements
paragraph: (2) On behalf of the government the minister may enter into an agreement with the council of a municipality for noxious weed control and the costs of noxious weed control in all or part of

heading: Weed control agreements
paragraph: (a) that municipality, or

heading: Weed control agreements
paragraph: (b) land, premises and property that are not within, but adjoin, the boundaries of that municipality.

heading: Highways
paragraph:
12
		  (1) In this section, "highway" means a highway as defined in the Transportation Act.

heading: Highways
paragraph: (2) If a highway is owned by the government, but is in the possession of a municipality, other than a regional district, that municipality is the occupier of that highway.

heading: Highways
paragraph: (3) If a highway is owned by the government and is not in the possession of a municipality, the occupier of that highway is the minister responsible for the administration of the Transportation Act on behalf of the government.

heading: Highways
paragraph: (4) If a new highway is constructed, or an existing highway is rerouted, within the boundaries of a municipality, other than a regional district, by or under the direction of the government, the minister responsible for the administration of the Transportation Act, on behalf of the government, is the occupier of that highway while it is being constructed or rerouted.

heading: Crown land
paragraph: 13		  If unoccupied land is owned by the government, the occupier of that Crown land is that member of the Executive Council designated by the minister to be the occupier on behalf of the government.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph:
14
		  (1) If, in the opinion of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, an area of British Columbia not in a municipality, other than a regional district, is waste land or sparsely populated land, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may exempt that area from this Act.

heading: Exemptions
paragraph: (2) If, in the opinion of the council of a municipality, other than a regional district, an area of British Columbia in the municipality is waste land or sparsely populated land, the council of that municipality may, by bylaw and with the consent of the minister, exempt that area from this Act.

heading: Offence
paragraph:
15
		  A person commits an offence who knowingly

heading: Offence
paragraph: (a) contravenes this Act,

heading: Offence
paragraph: (b) contravenes a regulation made under section 5,

heading: Offence
paragraph: (c) obstructs an inspector in the lawful exercise of the inspector's duties under this Act,

heading: Offence
paragraph: (c.1) provides information that is false or misleading with respect to a material fact contained in a signed statement under this Act, or

heading: Offence
paragraph: (d) refuses or neglects to comply with a notice served on the person.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph:
16
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Power to make regulations
paragraph: (2) Regulations in respect of methods used to control noxious weeds must not be made under subsection (1) unless the Environment and Land Use Committee established under the Environment and Land Use Act approves the methods.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Weed Control Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "area" means a portion of a regional district or of a municipality;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "implement of husbandry" has the same meaning as in the Motor Vehicle Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "screenings" means seeds and other material removed in the process of cleaning or grading cereal, forage or oilseed crops.

heading: Designation of noxious weeds
paragraph: 2		  (1) The weeds set out in Part I of Schedule A of this regulation are designated as noxious weeds throughout British Columbia.

heading: Designation of noxious weeds
paragraph: (2) A weed listed in Part II of Schedule A of this regulation is a noxious weed in the regions of British Columbia listed to the right of that weed.

heading: Notice to control noxious weeds
paragraph:
3
		  For the purpose of section 4 of the Act, a notice issued by an inspector shall be in the form of Schedule B.

heading: Screenings
paragraph:
4
		  (1) No person shall transport, keep for sale, offer to buy or sell, or buy or sell any screenings containing seeds of a noxious weed unless

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (a) the screenings are graded as No. 1 or No. 2 feed screenings under section 17 of the Off Grades of Grain and Grades of Screenings Order established by SOR 71-91 under the Canada Grain Act,

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (b) the person holds a valid and subsisting

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (i)  permit for removal of screenings in the form of Schedule C, or

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (ii)  feeder's permit in the form of Schedule D

heading: Screenings
paragraph: issued by the minister, and the permit holder complies with the terms and conditions set out in the permit, or

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (c) the screenings have been treated so as to devitalize any weed seeds.

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (2) Nothing in the section prevents

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (a) a farmer transporting from a grain elevator, mill or warehouse to the farmer's farm screenings that have been removed from grain grown on that farm, or

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (b) a person keeping or selling for export from the Province any screenings from grain that is recleaned in the Province.

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (3) On the sale of any screenings, the person who sells the screenings shall file with the minister a report specifying

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (a) the quantity of screenings sold,

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (b) the date and place of shipment, and

heading: Screenings
paragraph: (c) the person within the Province to whom the screenings are to be shipped.

heading: Transportation of grain, screenings, etc.
paragraph: 5		  No person shall transport on a highway grain, screenings or other material that contains, or is likely to contain, seeds of a noxious weed unless

heading: Transportation of grain, screenings, etc.
paragraph: (a) the grain, screenings or other material is transported in a covered container, or

heading: Transportation of grain, screenings, etc.
paragraph: (b) the horse trailer, recreational vehicle or other vehicle in which the grain, screenings or other material is transported is constructed so that no weed seeds can escape from the vehicle.

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph:
6
		  No person shall move on a highway

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph: (a) any vehicle that has any knapweed on it, or

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph: (b) any

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph: (i)  agricultural equipment or implement of husbandry,

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph: (ii)  construction machinery,

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph: (iii)  recreational vehicle, or

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph: (iv)  horse trailer

heading: Movement of machinery or vehicles
paragraph: that has any noxious weed on it.

heading: Cleaning of agricultural equipment
paragraph:
7
		  No person shall remove any agricultural equipment or implement of husbandry from any premises on which the equipment or implement has been operated unless it has first been cleaned and is free of any noxious weeds or seeds of a noxious weed.

heading: Seeds, fertilizer, etc.
paragraph:
8
		  Where a noxious weed is not established in an area, no person shall

heading: Seeds, fertilizer, etc.
paragraph: (a) within that area

heading: Seeds, fertilizer, etc.
paragraph: (i)  sow any grain or other seed that is intermixed with seeds of the noxious weed, or

heading: Seeds, fertilizer, etc.
paragraph: (ii)  apply fertilizer, lime, topsoil or other substance that contains the noxious weed or seeds of the noxious weed, or

heading: Seeds, fertilizer, etc.
paragraph: (b) sell for delivery within that area any fertilizer, lime, topsoil or other substance that contains the noxious weed or seeds of the noxious weed.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 1.01		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "permanent identification number" means a unique number assigned under the authority of the director to a person who passes an assistant guide examination approved or established by the director;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "written authorization" means an authorization issued by a guide outfitter to an assistant guide.

heading: Age requirement for guides
paragraph:
1.01.01
		  For the purposes of section 51 (1) (a) (iii) of the Wildlife Act, a regional manager may not issue a guide outfitter licence to a person unless the person is 19 years of age or older.

heading: Public liability insurance
paragraph: 1.01.1		  (1) For the purposes of section 51 (1) (a) (ii) of the Wildlife Act, a regional manager may issue a guide outfitter licence to a person if the person has public liability insurance as follows:

heading: Public liability insurance
paragraph: (a) the amount of the insurance must be at least $2 million;

heading: Public liability insurance
paragraph: (b) the insurance must be applicable to the guide outfitter's guiding business;

heading: Public liability insurance
paragraph: (c) the insurance must cover the guiding activities of each assistant guide employed by the guide outfitter as permitted under section 48 (1.1) of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Public liability insurance
paragraph: (2) A guide outfitter must continue to have public liability insurance as described in subsection (1) while the guide outfitter is licensed.

heading: Offence
paragraph: 1.02		  Where a guide outfitter guides, the guide outfitter commits an offence unless, at the time the guide outfitter

heading: Offence
paragraph: (a) guides, or

heading: Offence
paragraph: (b) employs an assistant guide to guide on the guide outfitter's behalf,

heading: Offence
paragraph: the guide outfitter is insured under a policy of public liability insurance as described in section 1.01.1.

heading: Guide outfitter licence with quota
paragraph:
1.04
		  Where a regional manager issues a guide outfitter licence which attaches a quota as a condition of licence, the regional manager may specify

heading: Guide outfitter licence with quota
paragraph: (a) species of game and their age, sex, horn or antler classification, and numbers of each class or classification of game that may be harvested,

heading: Guide outfitter licence with quota
paragraph: (b) the area or areas within which the harvest may occur,

heading: Guide outfitter licence with quota
paragraph: (c) the time period within which the game may be harvested, or

heading: Guide outfitter licence with quota
paragraph: (d) the number of hunters or a class of hunters that may hunt a species in a defined time and area.

heading: Guide outfitter licence term and condition
paragraph:
1.041
		  (1) It is a term and condition of every guide outfitter licence that the holder must not block or damage a road, trail, airstrip or watercourse or other real or personal property while providing services under a guide outfitter licence.

heading: Guide outfitter licence term and condition
paragraph: (2) Without limiting section 16.01 (i) of the Wildlife Act General Regulation, a holder of a guide outfitter licence who contravenes the term and condition referred to in subsection (1) of this section commits an offence.

heading: Guide outfitter licence term and condition
paragraph: (3) An offence under subsection (2) of this section is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (b) (ii) of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Offence
paragraph: 1.05		  (1) A guide outfitter or assistant guide commits an offence if, while guiding for big game, the guide outfitter or assistant guide

heading: Offence
paragraph: (a) guides more than 2 hunters at one time, or

heading: Offence
paragraph:
(b) fails to accompany a hunter the guide outfitter or
              assistant guide is guiding.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (2) A guide outfitter commits an offence if the guide outfitter

heading: Offence
paragraph: (a) guides a hunter outside the guide outfitter's guiding area, or

heading: Offence
paragraph: (b) allows an assistant guide employed by the guide outfitter to guide a hunter outside the guide outfitter's guiding area.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (3) An assistant guide employed by a guide outfitter commits an offence if the assistant guide guides a hunter outside the guide outfitter's guiding area.

heading: Offence
paragraph: (4) An offence under subsection (2) or (3) of this section is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (b) (ii) of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Delivery of guide report
paragraph: 1.05.1		  (0.1) In this section, "guide report" means a guide report referred to in section 55 (1) of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Delivery of guide report
paragraph: (1) A guide outfitter must do one of the following within 30 days after a hunt is concluded:

heading: Delivery of guide report
paragraph: (a) submit to the regional manager the original of the completed guide report that relates to the hunt;

heading: Delivery of guide report
paragraph: (b) submit to the regional manager, in the form and manner specified by the director, the information in the completed guide report that relates to the hunt.

heading: Delivery of guide report
paragraph: (2) A guide outfitter who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Royalties
paragraph: 1.06		  (1) For the purpose of section 69 of the Wildlife Act, royalties shall be submitted to a regional manager, not later than March 31 of the year following the calendar year in which the animals were taken, in the amount provided in Schedule 1.06.

heading: Royalties
paragraph: (3) A guide outfitter is exempt from the application of section 69 of the Wildlife Act in relation to animals taken on or after April 1, 2005 by a resident guided by or on behalf of the guide outfitter.

heading: Guide outfitter licence fees
paragraph:
1.10
		  (1) The guide outfitter licence fee payable for a guide outfitter licence issued for a term

heading: Guide outfitter licence fees
paragraph: (a) up to and including 12 months is set out in Schedule 1.10 (1), and

heading: Guide outfitter licence fees
paragraph: (b) greater than 12 months is set out in Schedule 1.10 (1.1).

heading: Guide outfitter licence fees
paragraph: (2) The guide outfitter licence fee described in subsection (1) must be paid on or before the first day of the term of the guide outfitter licence.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
1.11
		  An applicant for a guide outfitter licence commits an offence if the applicant

heading: Offences
paragraph: (a) fails to pay

heading: Offences
paragraph: (i)  the guide outfitter licence fee in accordance with section 1.10 (2),

heading: Offences
paragraph: (ii)  the surcharge in accordance with section 1.14 (2), or

heading: Offences
paragraph: (iii)  both the fee and surcharge referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii), and

heading: Offences
paragraph: (b) guides, or employs an assistant guide to guide on the applicant's behalf.

heading: Fees
paragraph:
1.12
		  (1) An applicant for a guide outfitter licence who has not previously held a guide outfitter licence must, at the time the applicant submits the application to the regional manager, pay the fee set out in Schedule 1.10 (3).

heading: Surcharge
paragraph:
1.14
		  (1) The surcharge payable for a guide outfitter licence issued for a term

heading: Surcharge
paragraph: (a) up to and including 12 months is set out in Schedule 1.10 (1), and

heading: Surcharge
paragraph: (b) greater than 12 months is set out in Schedule 1.10 (1.1).

heading: Surcharge
paragraph: (2) The surcharge described in subsection (1) must be paid on or before the first day of the term of the guide outfitter licence.

heading: Qualifications of assistant guides
paragraph:
1.16
		  For the purposes of section 48 (1.1) (a) and (2.1) (a) of the Wildlife Act, the prescribed qualifications for a person to guide for game as an assistant guide are as follows:

heading: Qualifications of assistant guides
paragraph: (a) the person passes an assistant guide examination approved or established by the director;

heading: Qualifications of assistant guides
paragraph: (b) the person pays any fees approved by the director for the examination;

heading: Qualifications of assistant guides
paragraph: (c) the person may lawfully work in British Columbia as an assistant guide.

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: 1.17		  For the purposes of section 48 (1.2) of the Wildlife Act, the written authorization that a guide outfitter issues to an assistant guide must be legible and contain the following information:

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (a) the name, birth date and permanent address of the assistant guide;

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (b) the permanent identification number of the assistant guide;

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (c) the name of the guide outfitter;

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (d) the number of the guide outfitter's licence;

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (e) the date the written authorization is issued;

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (f) the date the term of the guide outfitter's licence ends;

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (g) the statement: "(name of assistant guide) has been hired as an assistant guide.";

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (h) any restrictions on the assistant guide when guiding for game on behalf of the guide outfitter contained in the contract between the guide outfitter and the assistant guide, such as restrictions relating to seasons, areas or species;

heading: Written authorizations
paragraph: (i) a signed statement by the guide outfitter that, to the best of the guide outfitter's knowledge, the information contained in the written authorization is true, accurate and complete.

heading: Issuing new written authorizations
paragraph: 1.18		  For the purposes of section 48 (1.2) (b) of the Wildlife Act, the prescribed circumstances are as follows:

heading: Issuing new written authorizations
paragraph: (a) the original written authorization is lost or destroyed;

heading: Issuing new written authorizations
paragraph: (b) the information referred to in section 1.17 (a), (c), (d), (f) or (h) changes.

heading: Age requirement for assistant guides
paragraph: 1.19		  For the purposes of section 48 (2.1) (h) of the Wildlife Act, the prescribed requirement that a person must meet to guide for game as an assistant guide is that the person must be 18 years of age or older.

heading: Records
paragraph: 1.20		  (1) For the purposes of section 48 (1.3) (a) of the Wildlife Act, the required records are a copy of every written authorization the guide outfitter issues.

heading: Records
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of section 48 (1.3) (b) of the Wildlife Act, a copy of a written authorization must be kept for a period of 7 years from the date the authorization is issued.

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (1) For the purpose of section 71 of the Wildlife Act, a taxidermist, tanner, licensed fur trader, meatcutter or an operator of a cold storage plant must, immediately upon receiving wildlife or wildlife parts, record what was received, whether directly or through an agent, describing

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (a) the total number of wildlife or parts of them of each species acquired,

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (b) the date of receipt of the wildlife or parts of them,

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (c) the name and address of the person from whom wildlife or parts of them were acquired, and

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (d) the legal authority that the person claims to have to possess the wildlife or parts of them.

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (1.1) For the purpose of section 71 of the Wildlife Act, in addition to the requirements of subsection (1) of this section, a meatcutter or an operator of a cold storage plant must, immediately upon receiving the wildlife or wildlife parts referred to in that subsection, record

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (a) the species and sex of the wildlife or wildlife parts, and

heading: Records to be kept
paragraph: (b) the Management Unit from which the wildlife or wildlife parts were taken.

heading: Reports relating to grizzly bears
paragraph: 2.01.1		  (1) A taxidermist or tanner who receives a grizzly bear or a part of a grizzly bear must submit a report to the director within 10 days after receipt of the bear or part.

heading: Reports relating to grizzly bears
paragraph: (2) A report under subsection (1) must include

heading: Reports relating to grizzly bears
paragraph: (a) the information set out in section 2.01 (1) (a) to (d), and

heading: Reports relating to grizzly bears
paragraph: (b) if the bear or part is acquired from an individual, the address of the primary residence of the individual.

heading: Reports relating to grizzly bears
paragraph: (3) A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Fees and surcharges
paragraph:
2.02
		  (1) The fees and surcharges payable for a trapping licence or fur trader's licence shall be those in Schedule 2.02.

heading: Fees and surcharges
paragraph: (2) A duplicate copy of a licence may be issued if the holder of the licence

heading: Fees and surcharges
paragraph: (a) completes a statement of loss in the form specified by the director, and

heading: Fees and surcharges
paragraph: (b) pays the fee set out in Schedule 2.02.

heading: Term of annual licence
paragraph:
2.04
		  An annual trapping licence, fur trader's licence or fur trader's (transient) licence is valid from and including the later of

heading: Term of annual licence
paragraph: (a) July 1 of the year in which it is issued, or

heading: Term of annual licence
paragraph: (b) the date on which it is issued

heading: Term of annual licence
paragraph: to the following June 30.

heading: Term of five year trapping licence
paragraph:
2.04.1
		  A five year trapping licence is valid from and including the later of

heading: Term of five year trapping licence
paragraph: (a) July 1 of the year in which it is issued, or

heading: Term of five year trapping licence
paragraph: (b) the date on which it is issued

heading: Term of five year trapping licence
paragraph: to June 30 of the year 5 years after the year in which the licence was issued.

heading: Offence
paragraph:
2.05
		  Where a person possesses more than one current trapping licence, the person commits an offence.

heading: Licensed fur trader to make return
paragraph:
2.06
		  (1) For the purpose of section 71 (2) (b) of the Wildlife Act, a licensed fur trader must, for each calendar month, make a full and complete return on the form contained in Schedule 2.06 of all wildlife or wildlife parts that have been received during that calendar month for processing, manufacturing, curing, selling or trading.

heading: Licensed fur trader to make return
paragraph: (2) A return under this section must be submitted within 30 days after the last day of the month to which the report relates.

heading: Licensed fur trader to make return
paragraph: (3) A person who contravenes this section commits an offence.

heading: Lynx pelt measurements to be submitted
paragraph: 2.07		  (1) A licensed fur trader shall measure each lynx pelt that the licensed fur trader acquires and shall submit all measurements taken as specified on the form and in the manner authorized by the director.

heading: Lynx pelt measurements to be submitted
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Bear parts prohibitions - general
paragraph:
2.08
		  (1) A person commits an offence by possessing any of the following parts of a bear:

heading: Bear parts prohibitions - general
paragraph: (a) a gall bladder or bile;

heading: Bear parts prohibitions - general
paragraph: (b) male genitalia separated from the carcass and the hide.

heading: Bear parts prohibitions - general
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), a person who possesses a gall bladder or bile of a bear does not commit an offence under subsection (1) (a) if

heading: Bear parts prohibitions - general
paragraph: (a) the gall bladder is attached to the carcass,

heading: Bear parts prohibitions - general
paragraph: (b) the bile has not been extracted from the gall bladder, and

heading: Bear parts prohibitions - general

paragraph: (2) A person who kills a fur bearing animal under the authority of a licence to hunt wildlife is exempt from paying a royalty in relation to the pelt or skin of that animal, unless the person intends to offer the pelt or skin for sale.

heading: Fur royalty
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (2), a person who kills a fur bearing animal under the authority of a licence to hunt wildlife is exempt from paying a royalty in relation to the pelt or skin if the person sells the pelt or skin to a licensed fur trader.

paragraph: (4) If the person did not kill a fur bearing animal under the licence during the trapping year, the report must

paragraph: (a) state that no fur bearing animals were killed, and

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (b) be submitted on or before July 31 of the following trapping year.

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (5) If the person killed one or more fur bearing animals under the licence during the trapping year, the report must include all of the following information for each fur bearing animal killed:

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (a) the management unit in which the fur bearing animal was killed and either

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (i)  the trapline number, or

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (ii)  a statement that the kill occurred on private property;

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (b) the month in which the fur bearing animal was killed;

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (c) the fur bearing animal's species and sex.

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (6) The information required under subsection (5)

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (a) may be submitted, with respect to one or more fur bearing animals killed during the trapping year, at any time during the trapping year, and

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (b) must be submitted, with respect to all fur bearing animals killed during the trapping year, on or before July 31 of the following trapping year.

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (7) For greater certainty, the reporting requirements under this section are in addition to those imposed under section 3.16.

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (8) A person commits an offence if the person fails to make a report as required under this section with respect to

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (a) the trapping year that begins July 1, 2022, and

heading: Compulsory report of fur bearing animals killed
paragraph: (b) each subsequent trapping year.

heading: Trapping on private property
paragraph: 3.17		  (1) A person must not trap on private property that is not within the boundaries of a registered trapline area unless

heading: Trapping on private property
paragraph: (a) the person possesses a valid trapping licence, and

heading: Trapping on private property
paragraph: (b) the person has obtained the written permission of the property owner.

heading: Trapping on private property
paragraph: (2) A person who violates subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Registration of trapline
paragraph:
3.18
		  A regional manager may, by public auction or sealed tender from persons who qualify under section 42 of the Wildlife Act, select the successful applicant for registration of a trapline.

heading: Trapline registration transfer fee
paragraph: 3.19		  Where the rights to a registered trapline are transferred to a person or group of persons, that person or group of persons shall pay a transfer fee of $50.00.

heading: Quotas and bag limits
paragraph:
3.20
		  Notwithstanding sections 10 and 11 of the Hunting Regulation (B.C. Reg. 190/84), a licensed trapper commits an offence if, by authority of a trapping licence, the licensed trapper takes more than

heading: Quotas and bag limits
paragraph: (a) two black bear in one licence year.

heading: Use of nails or spikes
paragraph:
3.21
		  A person who lawfully sets a trap for fur bearing animals under a licence, permit or exemption from the requirement for a licence or permit is authorized to make reasonable use of a nail or spike to secure the trap to any timber in the area in which a trap may be lawfully set by that person.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
5.01
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licence activity report" means the form prescribed in Appendix 2;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "transporter" means a person who, for money or other compensation, transports a hunter to, from or between locations so that the hunter can hunt but does not include a person who operates a scheduled commercial flight or a chartered aircraft unless the person also provides ground transportation, accommodation or other ground services to the hunter.

heading: Transporter licence
paragraph:
5.02
		  (1) A person must not act as a transporter unless the person holds a transporter licence issued under section 15 of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Transporter licence
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Transporter licence
paragraph: (2.1) An offence under this section is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (b) (ii) of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Transporter licence
paragraph: (3) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who is licensed as a guide outfitter.

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: 5.03		  (1) A person is eligible for a transporter licence only if

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (a) the person

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (i)  is a citizen or permanent resident of Canada,

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (ii)  carries public liability insurance in an amount of not less than $2 million that is

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (A) applicable to the person's transporting business,

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (B) in effect at the time of the application for a transporter licence, and

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (C) effective for the term of the transporter licence,

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (iii)  satisfies the director that the person has a good working knowledge of the Wildlife Act and regulations by achieving a passing grade on an examination set by the director for that purpose, and

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (iv)  submits to the director a transporter licence application and management plan, in the form and with the information required by the instructions set out in Appendix 1, along with the application fee under Schedule 5.05 (2), and

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (b) based on the applicant's application and management plan, the director is satisfied that the person's transporter activities are unlikely to have a significant negative impact on wildlife.

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (2) An applicant for a transporter licence must submit the application fee, and the transporter licence application and management plan, required under subsection (1) (a) (iv) at least 3 months before the date the licence is required.

heading: Eligibility for transporter licence
paragraph: (3) The director need not make a decision on an application submitted under this section for 3 months after the date on which the director is in receipt of the application fee, application and management plan.

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: 5.04		  (1) The following are terms and conditions of every transporter licence:

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: (a) a holder of a transporter licence must not block or damage a road, trail, airstrip or watercourse or other real or personal property while providing transporter services under a transporter licence;

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: (c) a holder of a transporter licence must maintain the public liability insurance required under section 5.03 for the term of the licence.

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: (2) The director may make anything set out in the transporter licence application or management plan submitted under section 5.03 a term or condition of the licence issued on the basis of that application and management plan.

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: (3) Without limiting section 16.01 (m) of the Wildlife Act General Regulation, a holder of a transporter licence who contravenes either of the following commits an offence:

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: (a) a term and condition referred to in subsection (1) (a) of this section;

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: (b) a term or condition imposed by the director under subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Transporter licence conditions
paragraph: (4) An offence under subsection (3) of this section is prescribed as an offence for the purposes of section 84 (1) (b) (ii) of the Wildlife Act.

heading: Transporter licence fees
paragraph: 5.05		  (1) The fee and surcharge payable for a transporter licence are those set out in Schedule 5.05 (1).

heading: Transporter licence fees
paragraph: (2) A transporter licence fee and surcharge must be paid on or before April 1.

heading: Transporter licence fees
paragraph: (3) If an applicant for a transporter licence fails to pay the fee and surcharge in the time specified under subsection (2), the holder must pay the late payment fee set out in Schedule 5.05 (3) with the amount required under subsection (2).

heading: Transporter licence fees
paragraph: (4) A duplicate copy of a transporter licence may be issued if the licence holder

heading: Transporter licence fees
paragraph: (a) signs a declaration affirming that the licence has been lost, stolen or destroyed, and

heading: Transporter licence fees
paragraph: (b) pays the fees under Schedule 5.05 (4) and (5) for a duplicate transporter licence and declaration.

heading: Transporter licence reporting requirement
paragraph:
5.05.1
		  (1) A holder of a transporter licence must file in accordance with subsection (2) a completed licence activity report setting out the information required by the form of that report in relation to the holder's transporting activities for the year.

heading: Transporter licence reporting requirement
paragraph: (2) A licence activity report must be filed

heading: Transporter licence reporting requirement
paragraph: (a) with the regional manager indicated on the transporter licence, and

heading: Transporter licence reporting requirement
paragraph: (b) by December 31 of each year.

heading: Transporter licence reporting requirement
paragraph: (3) A holder of a transporter licence who fails to file a licence activity report in accordance with this section commits an offence.

heading: Non-renewal of licence: non-use of area
paragraph:
5.06
		  If the holder of a transporter licence has not applied for a new licence by the expiry date of the licence, the director

heading: Non-renewal of licence: non-use of area
paragraph: (a) must review the transporter's operation, and

heading: Non-renewal of licence: non-use of area
paragraph: (b) after affording the transporter an opportunity to be heard, may advise that the person is not eligible for a transporter licence for the new licence year,

heading: Non-renewal of licence: non-use of area
paragraph: and, if the director so advises, the person is not eligible for a transporter licence for that year whether or not they satisfy the requirements in section 5.03 (1).

paragraph: 1		  In this Appendix, "FWID number" has the same meaning as in the Wildlife Act General Regulation.

heading: Licence activity report
paragraph:
2
		  The following form is prescribed for the purposes of section 5.05.1 (1):

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
1.001
		  In this regulation:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "Act" means the Wildlife Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "FWID number", in relation to a person, means a unique number assigned to the person by the director as that person's fish and wildlife identification number.

heading: Falconry exemption
paragraph: 1.01		  Where a person is legally in possession of a raptor and the person uses the bird for the purposes of falconry, the person is for those purposes exempted from section 77 (2) of the Act.

heading: Native non-wildlife exemption
paragraph:
1.02
		  Where a person keeps an animal that

heading: Native non-wildlife exemption
paragraph: (a) is not designated as wildlife, and

heading: Native non-wildlife exemption
paragraph: (b) is native to the Province or occurs naturally in the wild in the Province

heading: Native non-wildlife exemption
paragraph: and releases the animal in an area of the Province where it naturally occurs, the person is for that purpose exempted from section 77 (2) of the Act.

heading: Captive game bird exemption - private land
paragraph:
1.04
		  A person who releases on private land a pheasant, quail, partridge or wild turkey which is hatched and raised in captivity is for that purpose exempt from section 77 of the Act.

heading: Form of information
paragraph:
3.01
		  An information for the purposes of section 92 of the Act may be in the form provided as Form 1 in the Schedule to the Offence Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 4.001		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "authorization" means a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "licence year" has the same meaning as in the Hunting Licensing Regulation, B.C. Reg. 8/99, or the Angling and Scientific Collection Regulation, B.C. Reg. 125/90, as applicable.

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph:
4.002
		  For the purposes of sections 4.01 and 4.07, a person may demonstrate that the person held an authorization by

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (a) producing the authorization, or

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (b) except with respect to an authorization described in section 20.05 (2),

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (i)  producing a legible copy of the authorization, or

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (ii)  stating the person's FWID number, if the authorization is one of the following:

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (A) a hunting licence issued with respect to a licence year that began on or after April 1, 2017;

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (B) a special area licence required by Part 2 or 3 of the Hunting Licensing Regulation issued with respect to a licence year that began on or after April 1, 2017;

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (C) an upland game bird licence issued with respect to a licence year that began on or after April 1, 2018;

heading: Demonstrating that authorizations were held
paragraph: (D) a limited entry hunting authorization issued with respect to an open season that began on or after April 1, 2017.

heading: Transport by person who killed or took wildlife or fish
paragraph:
4.01
		  (1) For the purposes of section 37 of the Act, a person may ship or transport wildlife or fish or parts of them where the person

heading: Transport by person who killed or took wildlife or fish
paragraph: (a) has killed or taken them,

heading: Transport by person who killed or took wildlife or fish
paragraph: (b) personally accompanies them, and

heading: Transport by person who killed or took wildlife or fish
paragraph: (c) is able to demonstrate, while shipping or transporting the wildlife, fish or parts, that the person held all authorizations that that person was required under the Act to hold in order to kill or take the wildlife or fish lawfully.

heading: Transport by person who killed or took wildlife or fish
paragraph: (2) In addition to the requirement under subsection (1) (c), a person must carry, while shipping or transporting wildlife or parts, all species licences for the species of wildlife or parts being shipped or transported, whether cancelled or not, issued to the person for the current licence year if

heading: Transport by person who killed or took wildlife or fish
paragraph: (a) the person is required to hold a species licence for that species, and

heading: Transport by person who killed or took wildlife or fish
paragraph: (b) the wildlife was killed or taken in the current licence year.

heading: Transport for another person
paragraph:
4.02
		  For the purposes of section 37 of the Act, a person may offer to ship or transport, or engage another person to ship or transport, wildlife or fish or parts of them where they are lawfully in the first person's possession or in the possession of the person on whose behalf the first person offers to ship or transport or engages another person to ship or transport them.

heading: Transport with record of receipt
paragraph:
4.03
		  For the purposes of section 37 of the Act, a person may ship or transport wildlife or fish killed or taken by another person or parts of them where the first person has in the first person's immediate possession a record of receipt of the wildlife or fish or parts of them showing

heading: Transport with record of receipt
paragraph: (a) the date and place of receipt,

heading: Transport with record of receipt
paragraph: (b) the name, address and, if one has been issued to the person, FWID number of the person who killed or took the wildlife or fish or from whom the wildlife or fish or parts of them were acquired,

heading: Transport with record of receipt
paragraph: (c) the type and number of each authorization that the person who killed or took the wildlife or fish was required under the Act to hold in order for the wildlife or fish to be killed or taken lawfully,

heading: Transport with record of receipt
paragraph: (d) the name and address of the person to whom the wildlife or fish or parts are to be delivered, and

heading: Transport with record of receipt
paragraph: (e) the species and sex of the animal if it is a big game animal.

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph:
4.04
		  For the purposes of section 37 of the Act,

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (a) a person who holds a trapping licence or fur traders licence,

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (b) a taxidermist, or

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (c) a tanner

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: may ship or transport wildlife or fish or parts of them lawfully in the licence holder, taxidermist or tanner's possession where

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (d) the licence holder, taxidermist or tanner personally accompanies them, or

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (e) the licence holder, taxidermist or tanner identifies each package with the licence holder, taxidermist or tanner's name and address and completes a written declaration that accompanies the shipment stating

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (i)  the contents of the shipment,

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (ii)  the number of packages in the shipment,

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (iii)  the name and address of the consignee, and

heading: Transport by trapper, trader, taxidermist or tanner
paragraph: (iv)  the royalty fur export permit number or game export permit number as appropriate.

heading: Other transport
paragraph:
4.05
		  For the purposes of section 37 of the Act, a person, other than

heading: Other transport
paragraph: (a) a fur trader,

heading: Other transport
paragraph: (b) a taxidermist, or

heading: Other transport
paragraph: (c) a tanner

heading: Other transport
paragraph: engaged in the person's calling, may ship or transport, or offer to ship or transport, dead wildlife or fish or parts of them

heading: Other transport
paragraph: (d) that have been tanned or processed into manufactured items, or

heading: Other transport
paragraph: (e) obtained from a licensed commercial outlet.

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph:
4.07
		  (1) For the purposes of section 37 of the Act, a supervising hunter may ship or transport wildlife if

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph: (a) the wildlife was killed or taken by the person the supervising hunter accompanied for the purposes of the Act,

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph: (b) the supervising hunter personally accompanies the wildlife, and

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph: (c) the supervising hunter is able to demonstrate, while shipping or transporting the wildlife, that the supervising hunter held all authorizations that the supervising hunter was required under the Act to hold in order for the wildlife to be killed or taken lawfully.

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph: (1.1) In addition to the requirement under subsection (1) (c), the supervising hunter must carry, while shipping or transporting wildlife or its parts, all species licences for the species of wildlife being shipped or transported, whether cancelled or not, issued to the supervising hunter for the current licence year, if

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph: (a) the supervising hunter is required to hold a species licence for that species, and

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph: (b) the wildlife was killed or taken in the current licence year.

heading: Transport by supervising hunter
paragraph: (2) In this section "supervising hunter" has the same meaning as in the Hunting Licensing Regulation.

heading: Transport of animal parts outside M.U.s 4-1 to 4-8 and 4-20 to 4-25
paragraph:
4.08
		  A person who kills or takes a deer, elk or moose within M.U.s 4-1 to 4-8 and 4-20 to 4-25 must not ship or transport, or engage another person to ship or transport, the following parts of the animal outside those M.U.s:

paragraph:

heading: Definition

heading: Prescribed offences
paragraph:

		  (1) It is a second or subsequent offence for the purpose of section 24 (8) (e) of the Act to commit an offence under the regulations made under the Act, or under the Act and not listed in section 24 (8) (a) to (d) of the Act, within 2 years from conviction for an offence under the Firearm Act, the Act or the regulations made under the Act.

heading: Prescribed offences
paragraph: (3) It is a second or subsequent offence for the purpose of section 24 (10) (c) of the Act to commit an offence under the regulations made under the Act, or under the Act and not listed in section 24 (10) (a) to (b) of the Act, within 2 years from conviction for an offence under the Firearm Act, the Act or the regulations made under the Act.

heading: Calculation of a period of ineligibility

paragraph: (b) the date a court makes a disposition under the Young Offenders (British Columbia) Act.

heading: Calculation of a period of ineligibility
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if a person is convicted of offences that result in more than one period of ineligibility under this Division, those periods run consecutively.

heading: Calculation of a period of ineligibility
paragraph: (3) Despite subsection (1), if a person is ineligible to hold a licence on the date referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (b), the period of ineligibility described in section 7.04 runs consecutively with the person's current period of ineligibility.

paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (1), a person is ineligible to obtain a hunting licence for one year, if

heading: Periods of ineligibility for a licence
paragraph: (b) the person has within the 2 years prior to the conviction been convicted of an offence under the Firearm Act, under the Act, or under regulations made under the Act.

heading: Periods of ineligibility for a licence

paragraph: (a) the person is convicted of an offence under the Act, or under regulations made under the Act, relating to angling or an angling licence, and

heading: Periods of ineligibility for a licence
paragraph: (b) the person has within the 2 years prior to the conviction been convicted of an offence under the Firearm Act, under the Act, or under regulations made under the Act.

paragraph: (6) Despite subsections (1) to (5), if a person is convicted of

heading: Periods of ineligibility for a licence
paragraph: (a) an offence listed in Column 1 of the Table in this section and the person has within 2 years prior to the conviction been convicted of an offence under the Firearm Act, under the Act, or under regulations made under the Act, not relating to angling or an angling licence, the person is ineligible to obtain a hunting licence for 3 years,

heading: Periods of ineligibility for a licence
paragraph: (b) an offence listed in Column 2 of the Table in this section and the person has within 2 years prior to the conviction been convicted of an offence under the Act, or under regulations made under the Act, relating to angling or an angling licence, the person is ineligible to obtain an angling licence for 3 years, and

heading: Periods of ineligibility for a licence
paragraph: (7) Despite subsections (1) to (6), if a person is convicted of an offence under section 26 (1) (a), (e) or (g) of the Act and the person has within 2 years prior to the conviction been convicted under the Firearm Act, under the Act, or under regulations made under the Act, not relating to angling or an angling licence, the person is ineligible to obtain a hunting licence for 5 years.

heading: Licence under Fur Farm Regulation exemption
paragraph:

paragraph: (2) A person who holds a licence for a particular species of fur bearing animal under the Fur Farm Regulation and who imports or exports live fur bearing animals of that species from or to another province, is exempt from section 21 (1) of the Act.

heading: Circus exemption
paragraph:

		  (1) A person who imports wildlife from, and exports that same wildlife to, another province, as part of a circus whose main place of business is outside British Columbia, is exempt from section 21 (1) of the Act.

heading: Circus exemption
paragraph: (2) A person who imports wildlife in the circumstances described in subsection (1) is exempt from sections 33 (1) and 37 of the Act.

heading: Residency exemptions
paragraph:
11.01
		  A person who

heading: Residency exemptions
paragraph: (a) is a member of the armed services of Her Majesty raised by Canada and enrolled in continuing full time military service who has made the person's permanent residence in British Columbia for 30 consecutive days immediately before making an application under the Act or doing another thing relevant to the operation of the Act,

heading: Residency exemptions
paragraph: (b) is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada, who leaves British Columbia to attend a recognized educational institution, and who returns to British Columbia on completion of studies at the institution concerned, or

paragraph: (c) is under 18 years of age, has resided with a parent or guardian in another province and returns to British Columbia to reside with another parent or guardian who is a resident,

heading: Definition
paragraph:
12.01
		  In this Division, "main portion" means,

heading: Definition
paragraph: (a) in relation to big game, the edible meat of the four quarters, loins, neck and ribs, and

heading: Definition
paragraph: (b) in relation to a game bird, the edible meat of both breasts.

heading: Exemption - small game
paragraph:
12.02
		  A person who hunts and kills small game, other than a game bird or a fur bearing animal, is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed.

heading: Exemption - game taken for hide
paragraph:
12.03
		  A person who hunts and kills game that is a fur bearing animal other than a black bear and removes the hide to any of the following is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed:

heading: Exemption - game taken for hide
paragraph: (a) a dwelling place of the person;

heading: Exemption - game taken for hide
paragraph: (b) a taxidermist, tanner, fur trader or the owner or operator of a cold storage plant.

heading: Exemption - game taken for food
paragraph:
12.04
		  A person who hunts and kills a game bird or big game and makes every reasonable effort to remove the main portions to any of the following is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed:

heading: Exemption - game taken for food
paragraph: (a) the person's normal dwelling place;

heading: Exemption - game taken for food
paragraph: (b) a meatcutter or the owner or operator of a cold storage plant.

heading: Exemption - transfers of game
paragraph:
12.05
		  A person who hunts and kills game and transfers the game killed to another person is exempt from section 35 (2) (b) of the Act in relation to the game killed if

heading: Exemption - transfers of game
paragraph: (a) the game is a fur bearing animal other than a black bear and the other person removes the hide to a dwelling place of the other person or to a person described in section 12.03 (b) of this regulation, or

heading: Exemption - transfers of game
paragraph: (b) the other person makes every reasonable effort to remove the edible portions or, in the case of a game bird or big game, the main portions to the other person's normal dwelling place or to a person described in section 12.04 (b) of this regulation.

paragraph:
15.01
		  (1) A person under the age of 10 years may not hunt wildlife.

heading: Minimum hunting age
paragraph: (2) A person who causes or allows a person under the age of 10 years to hunt wildlife commits an offence.

16.011

heading: Sale of birds held under permit

paragraph: (a) section 22 of the Act, and

heading: Failure to submit reports

heading: Failure to submit reports

paragraph: (a) section 13 (1) (b) of the Angling and Scientific Collection Regulation and, if applicable, section 13 (3) (c) of that regulation;

heading: Failure to submit reports

paragraph: (b.1) sections 16 (5), 16.1 (1) and 16.11 (1) of the Hunting Regulation;

heading: Failure to submit reports

paragraph:
21.01
		  (1) For the purposes of section 97 (2) (b) and (4) (b) of the Act, the following photo identification is prescribed:

paragraph: (a) in the case of a person who is a resident or a non-resident, valid photo identification issued to the person by any of the following:

heading: Proof of authorization

heading: How to give notice
paragraph:
22.02
		  A notice to which this Division applies must be given to a person in one of the following methods:

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (a) by leaving a copy with the person;

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (b) by sending a copy by ordinary mail or registered mail to the last known address of the person or, if the person carries on a business, to the address at which the person carries on business;

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (c) by leaving a copy in a mailbox or mail slot for the last known address of the person or, if the person carries on a business, for the address at which the person carries on business;

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (d) by attaching a copy to a door or other conspicuous place at the last known address of the person or, if the person carries on a business, at the address at which the person carries on business;

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (e) by fax to a number, or by email to an email address, provided by the person;

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (f) by sending a copy to an online account held by the person on a website that

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (i)  is maintained by or on behalf of the minister, and

heading: How to give notice
paragraph: (ii)  immediately sends an email notification to an email address provided by that person.

heading: When notice must be considered received
paragraph:
22.03
		  A notice given in accordance with section 22.02 is deemed to be received as follows:

heading: When notice must be considered received
paragraph: (a) if given by sending a copy by ordinary mail or registered mail, the 14th day after it is mailed;

heading: When notice must be considered received
paragraph: (b) if given by leaving a copy in a mailbox or mail slot, the 3rd day after it is left;

heading: When notice must be considered received
paragraph: (c) if given by attaching a copy to a door or other conspicuous place, the 3rd day after it is attached;

heading: When notice must be considered received
paragraph: (d) if faxed or emailed, the 3rd day after it is sent;

heading: When notice must be considered received
paragraph: (e) if given by sending a copy to an online account on a website that also sends an email notification, the 3rd day after it is sent to the account.

heading: Definitions for this Division
paragraph:
23.01
		  In this Division:

heading: Definitions for this Division
paragraph: "bait" means anything, including meat, cereal, cultivated crops, a restrained animal or any manufactured product or material, that may attract wildlife, but does not include a decoy;

heading: Definitions for this Division
paragraph: "management unit" or "M.U." means an area designated as a management unit by the Management Unit Regulation, B.C. Reg. 64/96;

heading: Definitions for this Division
paragraph: "Region 1" means the area within M.U.s 1-1 to 1-15;

heading: Definitions for this Division
paragraph: "Region 4" means the area within M.U.s 4-1 to 4-9 and 4-14 to 4-40;

heading: Definitions for this Division
paragraph: "Region 5" means the area within M.U.s 5-1 to 5-15.

heading: No baiting or feeding - Region 1
paragraph:
23.011
		  A person commits an offence if the person intentionally baits or feeds a turkey or an ungulate within 200 m of a dwelling, school yard or playground in Region 1.

heading: No baiting or feeding - Region 4
paragraph:
23.02
		  A person who, in Region 4, intentionally baits or feeds a turkey or an ungulate commits an offence.

heading: No baiting or feeding - Region 5 and M.U.s 6-12 and 6-13
paragraph:
23.03
		  A person commits an offence if the person intentionally baits or feeds an ungulate within 200 m of a dwelling, school yard or playground in Region 5 or in M.U.s 6-12 and 6-13.

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: 1		  (1) In this Act:

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "accompany" means to remain in the company of the other person, able to see the other person without the aid of any device other than ordinary corrective lenses and able to communicate by unamplified voice with that person;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "amphibian" means a vertebrate of the class Amphibia and includes the eggs and other developmental life stages;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "angler day" is a unit representing one person angling during any part of a day and is used to determine the extent to which a stream, lake or area specified under section 53 may be used for angling, for example, "a limit of 1 000 angler days" means that the total obtained by adding together the number of anglers using the stream, lake or area on each day of a specified period must not exceed 1 000;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "angler day quota" means the number of angler days allocated by the regional manager to an angling guide for the use of the angling guide's clients, or a class of those clients, during a period specified under section 53;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "angling" means catching or attempting to catch fish with a hook and line, with or without a rod, and includes

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (a) spear fishing or attempting to spear fish, and

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: (b) catching or attempting to catch crayfish;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
paragraph: "angling guide" means a person licensed as an angling guide under this Act;

heading: Definitions and interpretation
