heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: 2		  (1) Ownership in all wildlife in British Columbia is vested in the government.

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: (2) A person does not acquire a right of property in any wildlife except in accordance with a permit or licence issued under this Act or the Animal Health Act or as provided in subsection (3) of this section.

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: (3) A person who lawfully kills wildlife and complies with all applicable provisions of this Act and the regulations acquires the right of property in that wildlife.

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: (4) If a person by accident or for the protection of life or property kills wildlife, that wildlife, despite subsection (3), remains the property of the government.

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: (5) Despite anything in this Act, no right of action lies, and no right of compensation exists, against the government for death, personal injury or property damage caused by

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: (a) wildlife,

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: (a.1) controlled alien species described in paragraph (a) of the definition of "species", or

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: (b) an animal that escapes or is released from captivity or is abandoned

heading: Property in wildlife
paragraph: in British Columbia.

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: 3		  The minister, for the purpose of access to or the management or protection of wildlife, may

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (a) acquire and administer land, improvements on land and timber, timber rights and other rights on private land, and

heading: Minister's powers
paragraph: (b) enter into and carry out an agreement with a person, association or other body.

heading: Power to designate wildlife management areas
paragraph:
4
		  (1) In this section, "park", "conservancy" and "recreation area" have the same meanings as in the Park Act.

heading: Power to designate wildlife management areas
paragraph: (2) With the consent of the Lieutenant Governor in Council, the minister may, by regulation, designate as a wildlife management area land that is under the minister's administration and is not in a park, a conservancy or a recreation area.

heading: Power to designate wildlife management areas
paragraph: (3) The designation of land under subsection (2) does not affect any rights granted before the designation.

heading: Power to designate wildlife management areas
paragraph: (4) Despite any other enactment, a person may not use land or resources in a wildlife management area without the written permission of the regional manager.

heading: Critical wildlife areas and wildlife sanctuaries
paragraph: 5		  (1) If the minister requires land for habitat for a species of wildlife designated as an endangered species or threatened species, the minister may, by regulation, designate land in a wildlife management area as a critical wildlife area.

heading: Critical wildlife areas and wildlife sanctuaries
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by regulation, designate land in a wildlife management area as a wildlife sanctuary.

heading: Endangered and threatened species
paragraph:
6
		  (1) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers that a species of wildlife is threatened with imminent extinction throughout all or a significant portion of its range in British Columbia because of the action of humans, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, designate the species as an endangered species.

heading: Endangered and threatened species
paragraph: (2) If the Lieutenant Governor in Council considers that a species of wildlife is likely to become endangered in British Columbia if the factors affecting its vulnerability are not reversed, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, designate the species as a threatened species.

heading: Designation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph:
6.4
		  If the minister considers that a non-native species described in paragraph (a) or (b) of the definition of "species" poses a risk to the health or safety of any person or poses a risk to property, wildlife or wildlife habitat, the minister may make regulations designating the species as

heading: Designation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (a) a controlled alien species, or

heading: Designation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (b) a controlled alien species that is an aquatic invasive species.

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph:
6.5
		  (1) The minister may, by regulation, regulate, prohibit and impose requirements in relation to the following:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (a) the possession of a species individual of a controlled alien species;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (b) the breeding of controlled alien species;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (c) the release of a species individual of a controlled alien species;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (d) trafficking in species individuals of a controlled alien species;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (e) the shipping or transporting in British Columbia of, or the engaging of another person to ship or transport in British Columbia, a species individual of a controlled alien species.

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (2) The minister may, by regulation, regulate, prohibit and impose requirements in relation to any of the following for the purposes of preventing aquatic invasive species from entering into or spreading in British Columbia:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (a) the driving, operating, shipping or transporting in British Columbia of, or the engaging of another person to drive, operate, ship or transport in British Columbia, any of the following:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (i)  a motor vehicle or other vehicle;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (ii)  an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (iii)  a boat;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (b) the shipping or transporting in British Columbia of, or the engaging of another person to ship or transport in British Columbia, any of the following:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (i)  a boat trailer;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (ii)  any item used for fishing;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (iii)  a wharf or dock;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (iv)  any item used for water-based activities;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (v)  any equipment associated with, and any component of, an aircraft designed to land on water, a boat or a thing referred to in this paragraph.

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (3) The minister may make the following regulations in relation to inspections for the purposes of preventing aquatic invasive species from entering into or spreading in British Columbia:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (a) establishing a specified period or a specified event before which there must be an inspection, in accordance with section 95.1, of a vehicle, aircraft, boat, trailer, item, wharf, or dock, or any equipment, referred to in subsection (2);

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (b) requiring the creation or retention of records, including, without limitation, a requirement for the retention of records related to the inspection or decontamination of a vehicle, aircraft, boat, trailer, item, wharf, or dock, or any equipment, referred to in subsection (2).

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (4) In making regulations under this section, the minister may do one or more of the following:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (a) define classes of the following:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (i)  controlled alien species;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (ii)  vehicles, aircrafts, boats, trailers, items, wharves, docks or equipment referred to in subsection (2);

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (b) make different regulations for the following:

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (i)  different controlled alien species or classes of controlled alien species;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (ii)  different vehicles, aircrafts, boats, trailers, items, wharves, docks or equipment referred to in subsection (2) or classes of vehicles, aircrafts, boats, trailers, items, wharves, docks or equipment referred to in subsection (2);

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (c) exclude a person or a vehicle, aircraft, boat, trailer, item, wharf, or dock, or any equipment, referred to in subsection (2) or classes of persons or vehicles, aircrafts, boats, trailers, items, wharves, docks or equipment referred to in subsection (2);

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (d) delegate a matter to a person;

heading: Regulation of controlled alien species and aquatic invasive species
paragraph: (e) confer a discretion on a person.

heading: Application of this Act to controlled alien species
paragraph:
6.6
		  (1) Sections 3, 82 (4), 89, 93, 94 (1), 95, 95.3 and 107 (2) apply in relation to controlled alien species as if those species were wildlife.

heading: Financial responsibility

heading: Hunting and trapping

heading: Hunting and trapping

heading: Hunting and trapping

paragraph: (1.1) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person under 18 years of age on whose behalf the parent or guardian holds a hunting licence.

heading: Angling licences
paragraph:
12
		  A person commits an offence if the person angles in the non-tidal waters of British Columbia unless the person is

heading: Angling licences
paragraph: (a) the holder of

heading: Angling licences

heading: Angling licences
paragraph: (ii)  any other licence or permit that is required by regulation,

paragraph: (b) an Indian residing in British Columbia, or

heading: Angling licences
paragraph: (c) exempt by regulation.

heading: Licences as prescribed
paragraph:
13
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may prescribe other licences required in addition to any licence required by this Act.

heading: Number of licences limited
paragraph:
14
		  A person commits an offence if the person obtains or holds more licences or limited entry hunting authorizations than the number prescribed by regulation.

heading: Issue of licences
paragraph:
15
		  (1) The director, or a person authorized by the director, may issue and authorize the issue of licences with the conditions, and valid for the term, the director, or a person authorized by the director, specifies.

heading: Issue of licences
paragraph: (2) A licence issued under this Act must be issued in a manner and form, if any, specified by the director.

heading: Licence applications
paragraph:
15.1
		  An application for a licence under this Act must be made in a manner and form, if any, specified by the director.

heading: Limited entry hunting authorization
paragraph:
16
		  (1) The minister, by regulation, may

heading: Limited entry hunting authorization
paragraph: (a) limit hunting for a species of wildlife in an area of British Columbia,

heading: Limited entry hunting authorization
paragraph: (b) provide for limited entry hunting authorizations to be issued by means of a lottery or other method of random selection among applicants,

heading: Limited entry hunting authorization
paragraph: (b.1) provide for exceptions that the minister considers appropriate to the random selection among applicants in conducting a lottery or other method of random selection among applicants under paragraph (b), and

heading: Limited entry hunting authorization
paragraph: (c) do other things necessary for the purposes of this section.

heading: Limited entry hunting authorization
paragraph: (2) An application fee collected under a lottery or other method referred to in subsection (1) must be paid into the general fund of the consolidated revenue fund.

heading: Limited entry hunting authorization
paragraph: (3) In making regulations under subsection (1), the minister may define classes of applicants and make different regulations for different classes of applicants.

heading: Examinations
paragraph:
17
		  (1) A person may not apply for or be issued a hunting licence unless the person has successfully completed examinations, approved by the director, about conservation, outdoor recreation and safety.

heading: Examinations
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to a non-resident, or a non-resident alien, who is to be accompanied by

heading: Examinations
paragraph: (a) a guide outfitter,

heading: Examinations

heading: Examinations
paragraph: (c) a person who holds a permit issued under section 70 (1) (a) that authorizes the person to accompany the non-resident or non-resident alien.

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph:
17.1
		  (1) A hunting licence must not be issued to, or on behalf of, a person who is under 18 years of age unless a parent or guardian applies for the licence and signs a written undertaking that the parent or guardian will not allow the child or ward to hunt or carry a firearm unless he or she is accompanied by and under the close personal supervision of a person who

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (a) is 18 years of age or older,

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (b) holds a hunting licence, other than an initiation hunting licence, or is exempted from holding a hunting licence, and

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (c) meets the prescribed qualifications.

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (2) Despite section 17 (1) but subject to this section, a parent or guardian who complies with the regulations may apply for and be issued a hunting licence on behalf of a child or ward who is at least 10 years of age, but less than 18 years of age.

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (3) A person commits an offence if the person

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (a) is 18 years of age or older,

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (b) is accompanied by another person who is under 18 years of age and who is carrying a firearm, and

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (c) either

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (i)  does not hold a hunting licence other than an initiation hunting licence and is not exempted from holding a hunting licence, or

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (ii)  does not meet the prescribed qualifications.

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (3.1) Subsection (3) does not apply if the younger person is accompanied by and under the close personal supervision of a person, other than the person described in subsection (3), who

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (a) is 18 years of age or older,

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (b) holds a hunting licence other than an initiation hunting licence or is exempted from holding a hunting licence, and

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (c) meets the prescribed qualifications.

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (4) A parent or guardian commits an offence if he or she gives permission to his or her child or ward, who is under 18 years of age and with respect to whom the parent or guardian has signed a written undertaking under subsection (1), to

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (a) hunt, or

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (b) be in possession of a firearm

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: unless the child or ward is accompanied by and under the close personal supervision of a person who

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (c) is 18 years of age or older,

paragraph: (d) holds a hunting licence, other than an initiation hunting licence, or is exempted from holding a hunting licence, and

heading: Hunting licences for persons under 18 years of age
paragraph: (e) meets the prescribed qualifications.

paragraph:

		  (1) Despite section 17 (1), a person who

paragraph: (a) is a resident,

heading: Initiation hunting licence
paragraph: (b) is 18 years of age or older,

paragraph: (c) has never held a hunting licence issued under this Act, other than a hunting licence issued to a parent or guardian on his or her behalf, and

paragraph: (d) complies with the regulations

heading: Initiation hunting licence

paragraph: (2) A person who holds an initiation hunting licence commits an offence if the person hunts unless the person is accompanied by and under the close personal supervision of a person who

paragraph: (3) A person who

paragraph: (a) is 18 years of age or older, and

paragraph: (c) is 18 years of age or older, and

paragraph: (d) meets the prescribed qualifications.

heading: Prescribed course of training
paragraph:
18
		  The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Prescribed course of training
paragraph: (a) requiring that a person, before being entitled to hunt or to receive a hunting licence, successfully complete examinations on conservation, outdoor recreation and safety approved by the director;

heading: Prescribed course of training
paragraph: (b) prescribing fees for any examinations required under this Act;

heading: Prescribed course of training
paragraph: (c) designating the persons required to pay the fees;

heading: Prescribed course of training
paragraph: (d) respecting the conduct of examinations.

heading: Permits
paragraph:
19
		  (1) A regional manager or a person authorized by a regional manager may, to the extent authorized by and in accordance with regulations made by the Lieutenant Governor in Council, by the issue of a permit, authorize a person

heading: Permits
paragraph: (a) to do anything that the person may do only by authority of a permit or that the person is prohibited from doing by this Act or the regulations, or

heading: Permits
paragraph: (b) to omit to do anything that the person is required to do by this Act or the regulations,

heading: Permits
paragraph: subject to and in accordance with those conditions, limits and period or periods the regional manager may set out in the permit and, despite anything contained in this Act or the regulations, that person has that authority during the term of the permit.

heading: Permits
paragraph: (2) A permit issued under this Act must be issued in a manner and form, if any, and with the conditions, if any, specified by the director.

heading: Permits
paragraph: (3) If a regional manager issues a permit respecting the use of firearms, the regional manager may exempt a person from the requirements of section 9 of the Firearm Act and may specify the conveyance or type of conveyance for which the permit is limited.

heading: Permits
paragraph: (4) The regional manager or the person authorized by the regional manager may amend the conditions of a permit as determined by him or her and issued under this section, but the amendment is not effective until the permittee has notice of it.

heading: Permit applications and fees
paragraph: 20		  (1) An application for a permit under this Act must be made in a manner and form, if any, specified by the director.

heading: Permit applications and fees
paragraph: (2) If the director issues a permit to a non-resident or non-resident alien for a period of 14 days or less, the director may waive a prescribed fee.

heading: Import and export of wildlife
paragraph:
21
		  (1) Except as authorized by a permit issued under this Act or under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, a person commits an offence if the person

heading: Import and export of wildlife
paragraph: (a) imports into British Columbia live wildlife, or the egg of a wildlife species, or

heading: Import and export of wildlife
paragraph: (b) exports out of British Columbia wildlife or parts of them, or the egg of a wildlife species.

heading: Trafficking in wildlife
paragraph:
22
		  A person who traffics in live wildlife or wildlife meat, except as authorized by regulation or a permit, commits an offence.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph:
24
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: "convicted" includes the granting of an absolute or conditional discharge;

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: "date of sentencing" includes

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (a) the date that the passing of sentence is suspended,

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (b) the date that an absolute or a conditional discharge is granted, or

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (c) the date that a court

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (i)  imposes a sentence under the Youth Justice Act, or

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (2) After providing an opportunity for the person to be heard, the director may, for any cause considered sufficient by the director, do any of the following:

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (a) prohibit, for a period within prescribed limits, the person from hunting, angling or carrying a firearm;

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (b) cancel or suspend, for a period within prescribed limits, any limited entry hunting authorization or licence that is issued to the person under this Act.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (5) If a licence or limited entry hunting authorization is cancelled, the director may order that the person is ineligible to obtain or renew a licence or limited entry hunting authorization for a period, within the prescribed limits, and the director must inform the person of the period of ineligibility.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (6) If the licence or limited entry hunting authorization held by a person has been suspended, the person commits an offence if during the period of suspension

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (a) of the licence or limited entry hunting authorization, he or she applies for or in any way obtains a new licence or limited entry hunting authorization,

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (b) of a hunting licence, he or she hunts, or

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (d) of an angling licence, he or she angles.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (7) A person who does any of the following commits an offence:

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (a) while ineligible to obtain a licence or limited entry hunting authorization, the person applies for or obtains a licence or limited entry hunting authorization;

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (b) the person hunts while ineligible to obtain a hunting licence;

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (c) the person angles while ineligible to obtain an angling licence.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (8) A hunting licence or limited entry hunting authorization issued to a person under this Act is cancelled automatically from the date of sentencing if the person is convicted of

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (a) an offence under section 22, 26 (1) (a), (e), (f) or (g),

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (b) an offence under subsection (6), (7) or (14) of this section or section 28 with respect to hunting,

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (c) an offence under section 81 or 82 with respect to a hunting licence or limited entry hunting authorization,

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (d) an offence under section 3 of the Firearm Act, or

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (e) a second or subsequent offence as prescribed within 2 years.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (10) An angling licence issued to a person under this Act is cancelled automatically from the date of sentencing if the person is convicted of

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (a) an offence under subsection (6), (7) or (14) of this section with respect to angling,

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (b) an offence under section 81 or 82 with respect to an angling licence, or

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (c) a second or subsequent offence as prescribed within 2 years.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (12) If a person to whom subsection (2) would otherwise apply does not hold a licence or limited entry hunting authorization or is exempted from holding one, the director may prohibit the person for a period, within any prescribed limits, from doing the thing for which a licence or limited entry hunting authorization would ordinarily be required.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (13) If a person to whom subsection (8) or (10) otherwise applies does not hold a licence or limited entry hunting authorization or is exempted from holding one, the person is automatically prohibited, from the date of sentencing, from doing the thing for which a licence or limited entry hunting authorization would ordinarily be required, and subsection (5) applies.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (14) A person commits an offence if the person, during a period of prohibition under subsection (2), (12) or (13),

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (a) applies for or in any way obtains a licence or limited entry hunting authorization that he or she is prohibited from obtaining, or

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (b) while prohibited from

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (i)  hunting, hunts,

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (ii)  carrying a firearm, carries a firearm, or

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (iii)  angling, angles.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (15) The sanctions provided for in this section apply in addition to any fines, penalties, additional fines, prohibitions, directions or requirements that may be imposed under section 84, 84.1, 84.2 or 84.3 and whether or not they are requested or ordered at the time of sentencing for an offence.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of licences
paragraph: (16) If a person who has obtained a licence or limited entry hunting authorization for which residence in British Columbia is a prerequisite ceases to be a resident, the person's licence or limited entry hunting authorization is suspended for as long as he or she is not a resident.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of permits
paragraph: 25		  (1) A regional manager, for any cause he or she considers sufficient, and after providing an opportunity for the person to be heard, may suspend or cancel a permit held by a person, may order that the person is ineligible to obtain or renew a permit for a period and, if he or she does make an order, must inform the person of the period of ineligibility.

heading: Suspension and cancellation of permits
paragraph: (2) An officer may, without the necessity of holding a hearing, exercise the powers of a regional manager under this section to suspend a permit and, if a permit is suspended by an officer, the matter must be referred to the regional manager, who may confirm, reduce, extend or terminate the suspension.

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph:
26
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person hunts, takes, traps, wounds or kills wildlife

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (a) that is an endangered species or threatened species,

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (b) in a wildlife sanctuary,

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (c) at a time not within the open season,

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (d) with a firearm or a bow during the prohibited hours,

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (e) by the use or with the aid of a light or illuminating device,

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (f) with poison,

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (g) with a set gun, or

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (h) with a pump, repeating or auto loading shotgun unless the magazine contains a plug that is incapable of removal except by disassembling the gun, and that makes the magazine incapable of holding more than 2 cartridges.

heading: Hunting, trapping and firearm prohibitions
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) (c), (d), (e) and (h) does not apply to a person who hunts or traps wildlife that is on the person's property and is a menace to a domestic animal or bird.

heading: Use of conveyance
paragraph:
27
		  (1) A person who discharges a firearm or wounds or kills wildlife from a motor vehicle or from a boat that is propelled by a motor commits an offence.

heading: Use of conveyance
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if the person

heading: Use of conveyance
paragraph: (a) hunts wildlife from an aircraft, or

heading: Use of conveyance
paragraph: (b) uses a helicopter for the purposes of transporting hunters or game, or while on a hunting expedition,

heading: Use of conveyance
paragraph: except as authorized by regulation.

heading: Use of conveyance
paragraph: (3) A person who herds or harasses wildlife with the use of a motor vehicle, aircraft, boat or other mechanical device commits an offence.

heading: Use of conveyance
paragraph: (4) A person who hunts game within 6 hours after being airborne in an aircraft, other than a regularly scheduled commercial aircraft, commits an offence.

heading: Dangerous hunting or trapping
paragraph:
28
		  A person who hunts or traps without reasonable consideration for the lives, safety or property of other persons commits an offence.

heading: Attempt to capture wildlife
paragraph:
29
		  Except as authorized by this Act, the regulations or a permit, a person who attempts to capture wildlife commits an offence.

heading: Swimming wildlife
paragraph:
30
		  Except as provided under section 35, a person who hunts, takes, wounds or kills big game while it is swimming commits an offence.

heading: Shooting across highway
paragraph:
31
		  A person who discharges a firearm on or across the travelled portions of a highway prescribed under section 108 commits an offence.

heading: No shooting area
paragraph:
32
		  A person who discharges a firearm in a no shooting area commits an offence.

heading: Possession of wildlife
paragraph:
33
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person has live wildlife in his or her personal possession except as authorized under a licence or permit or as provided by regulation.

heading: Possession of wildlife
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if the person has dead wildlife or a part of any wildlife in his or her possession except as authorized under a licence or permit or as provided by regulation.

heading: Possession of wildlife
paragraph: (3) Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to a person who possesses wildlife under a licence or permit under the Animal Health Act.

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: 33.1		  (1) A person must not

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (a) intentionally feed or attempt to feed dangerous wildlife, or

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (b) provide, leave or place an attractant in, on or about any land or premises with the intent of attracting dangerous wildlife.

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (2) A person must not leave or place an attractant in, on or about any land or premises where there are or where there are likely to be people, in a manner in which the attractant could

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (a) attract dangerous wildlife to the land or premises, and

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (b) be accessible to dangerous wildlife.

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (5) and (6), a person who contravenes subsection (1) or (2) commits an offence.

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (4) If an offence under this section continues for more than one day, separate fines, each not exceeding the maximum fine for that offence, may be imposed for each day the offence continues.

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (5) A person does not contravene subsection (1) (b) or (2) by providing, leaving or placing an attractant in, on or about any land or premises for the purposes of hunting or trapping wildlife in accordance with all other applicable provisions of this Act and the regulations.

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (6) A person does not contravene subsection (2)

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (a) by conducting a farm operation, as defined in section 1 of the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act, if the person

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (i)  conducts the farm operation on, in or over land anywhere in British Columbia, and

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (ii)  meets the requirements set out in section 2 (2) (a) and (c) of that Act, or

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (b) by operating a facility for the disposal of waste, that is operated in accordance with the Environmental Management Act by a municipality, as defined in section 1 (1) of that Act.

heading: Attracting dangerous wildlife
paragraph: (7) For the purposes of this section, "leave", in relation to a person who is an owner, tenant or occupant of land or premises, includes to fail to remove an attractant from or to allow an attractant to remain in, on or about that land or those premises.

heading: Birds, nests and eggs
paragraph: 34		  A person commits an offence if the person, except as provided by regulation, possesses, takes, injures, molests or destroys

heading: Birds, nests and eggs
paragraph: (a) a bird or its egg,

heading: Birds, nests and eggs
paragraph: (b) the nest of an eagle, peregrine falcon, gyrfalcon, osprey, heron or burrowing owl, or

heading: Birds, nests and eggs
paragraph: (c) the nest of a bird not referred to in paragraph (b) when the nest is occupied by a bird or its egg.

heading: Retrieval of wildlife killed
paragraph:
35
		  (1) In this section, "dwelling place" does not include a temporary or seasonal camp.

heading: Retrieval of wildlife killed
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if the person hunts wildlife and kills or injures that wildlife and fails to make every reasonable effort to

heading: Retrieval of wildlife killed
paragraph: (a) retrieve the wildlife, and if it is alive to kill it and include it in his or her bag limit, and

heading: Retrieval of wildlife killed
paragraph: (b) remove the edible portions of the carcass of game to the person's normal dwelling place or to a meatcutter or the owner or operator of a cold storage plant,

heading: Retrieval of wildlife killed
paragraph: unless exempted by regulation.

heading: Possession of carcass
paragraph:
36
		  (1) A person who possesses the carcass of any wildlife, whether or not the carcass has been divided, without leaving attached the parts required by regulation to be left attached, commits an offence.

heading: Possession of carcass
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) only applies until the earlier of the following:

heading: Possession of carcass
paragraph: (a) the carcass is given to a meatcutter or the owner or operator of a cold storage plant to be recorded in accordance with section 71,

heading: Possession of carcass
paragraph: (b) the carcass arrives at the person's normal dwelling place and is butchered and stored there for consumption on the premises, or

heading: Possession of carcass
paragraph: (c) the carcass is presented to an employee of the ministry for which the minister is responsible or other person specified by the Lieutenant Governor in Council for inspection.

heading: Transportation of wildlife
paragraph:
37
		  A person who ships or transports in British Columbia, or engages another person to ship or transport in British Columbia, wildlife or fish or parts of them, except as provided by regulation, commits an offence.

heading: Failure to provide information
paragraph:
38
		  A person who fails, on the request of an officer, to state correctly the locality where and the date on which wildlife or fish in the person's possession was killed, taken or caught by the person or came into his or her possession, commits an offence.

heading: Agricultural and cleared land
paragraph:
39
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person, without the consent of the owner, lessee or occupier of land,

heading: Agricultural and cleared land
paragraph: (a) hunts over or traps in or on cultivated land, or

heading: Agricultural and cleared land
paragraph: (b) hunts over Crown land that is subject to a grazing lease while the land is occupied by livestock.

heading: Agricultural and cleared land
paragraph: (2) This section does not affect the Trespass Act.

heading: Power to prohibit hunting or trapping
paragraph: 40		  (1) Despite anything in this Act or the regulations or the privileges conferred by a licence or limited entry hunting authorization, the minister may, by regulation, prohibit a person or a class of persons from

heading: Power to prohibit hunting or trapping
paragraph: (a) hunting or trapping, or

heading: Power to prohibit hunting or trapping
paragraph: (b) using a method of hunting or trapping

heading: Power to prohibit hunting or trapping
paragraph: in a defined area for a period the minister considers necessary for the proper management of wildlife in that area.

heading: Power to prohibit hunting or trapping
paragraph: (2) Despite anything in this Act or the regulations, the minister may, by regulation, allow a person or a class of persons to hunt or trap in a defined area for a period the minister considers necessary for the proper management of wildlife in that area.

heading: Issue of trapping licence
paragraph:
40.1
		  A regional manager may issue a trapping licence to a person who is a citizen of Canada or a permanent resident of Canada.

heading: Prohibition within a trapline
paragraph:
41
		  A person commits an offence if the person sets a trap for, hunts, kills, takes or captures a fur bearing animal in an area of British Columbia unless the person

heading: Prohibition within a trapline
paragraph: (a) is a registered holder of the trapline for that area,

heading: Prohibition within a trapline
paragraph: (b) has written permission of a registered holder of the trapline for that area,

heading: Prohibition within a trapline
paragraph: (c) is the owner or occupier of the land,

heading: Prohibition within a trapline
paragraph: (d) has written permission from the owner or occupier of the land, or

heading: Prohibition within a trapline
paragraph: (e) holds a permit to trap that is required by regulation.

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph:
42
		  (1) A regional manager, or a person authorized by the regional manager, may grant registration of a trapline on Crown land to a person who is, or to a group of persons each of whom is,

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (a) 19 years of age or older, and

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (b) a citizen of Canada or a permanent resident of Canada.

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (2) A person or group of persons must not be granted registration of more than one trapline unless

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (a) the traplines are contiguous,

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (b) the person or group of persons has submitted to the regional manager a fur management plan, and

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (c) the regional manager has approved the fur management plan.

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (3) Registration of a trapline or traplines in the name of more than one person creates a tenancy in common.

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (4) If a holder of the traplines for which a fur management plan was submitted does not observe the undertakings given in the plan, the regional manager may take action under section 61.

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (5) Registration of a trapline does not

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (a) give the holder of the trapline any proprietary rights in wildlife, or

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (b) restrict the rights of another person

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (i)  to hunt, or

heading: Registration of traplines
paragraph: (ii)  to capture wildlife if authorized by the regulations or a permit.

heading: Use of trapline
paragraph:
43
		  (1) A person must not hold a registered trapline unless the person complies with the regulations and the conditions of his or her licence.

heading: Use of trapline
paragraph: (2) Despite a regulation or a condition of a licence requiring the holder of a trapline to carry on active trapping, the regional manager may authorize the holder of a registered trapline to temporarily discontinue the use or part of the use of the trapline for a period not exceeding 2 years.

heading: Leaving traps set
paragraph:
44
		  A person who leaves a trap set after the last day of the open season for the trapping of fur bearing animals commits an offence.

heading: Disputes
paragraph:
45
		  If a dispute arises as to priority of rights respecting any trapline, the matter must, at the request of a party to the dispute, be determined by the regional manager, who may alter, eliminate or reassign part or all of a trapline.

heading: Interference with traps
paragraph:
46
		  A person who knowingly damages or interferes with a lawfully set trap commits an offence.

heading: Non-residents and big game
paragraph:
47
		  A person commits an offence if the person hunts big game unless he or she

heading: Non-residents and big game
paragraph: (a) is a resident, or

heading: Non-residents and big game
paragraph: (b) is accompanied by

heading: Non-residents and big game
paragraph: (i)  a guide licensed under this Act,

heading: Non-residents and big game
paragraph: (i.1)  an assistant guide issued a written authorization under section 48 (1.2), or

heading: Non-residents and big game
paragraph: (ii)  a person who holds a permit under section 70 (1) (a) allowing him or her to accompany the hunter.

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph:
48
		  (1) A person, other than a person who guides for game as an assistant guide in accordance with this Act, commits an offence if the person acts as a guide for game, or offers to act as a guide for game, unless the person

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (a) holds a guide outfitter licence,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (c) holds another licence to guide for game, or

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (d) accompanies or assists a person to hunt game birds or small game on land other than Crown land.

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (1.1) A guide outfitter may employ a person as an assistant guide to guide for game on behalf of the guide outfitter only if the guide outfitter ensures that

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (a) the person meets the prescribed qualifications, if any,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (b) the person is not prohibited under this Act from applying for employment as an assistant guide,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (c) the person is not prohibited under this Act from guiding as an assistant guide, and

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (d) the terms of employment are consistent with any conditions or restrictions imposed under this Act on the person and any prescribed requirements referred to in subsection (2.1) (h).

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (1.2) A guide outfitter must promptly issue to an assistant guide written authorization, in the prescribed manner and form and with the prescribed content,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (a) on employing the assistant guide under subsection (1.1), and

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (b) whenever a change in prescribed circumstances occurs.

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (1.3) A guide outfitter must, in relation to assistant guides employed by the guide outfitter under subsection (1.1),

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (a) create and maintain any records required by the regulations,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (b) keep any records referred to in paragraph (a) for a prescribed period, and

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (c) provide any records referred to in paragraph (a) to an officer on request.

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (2) A person who holds a guide outfitter licence commits an offence if the person employs an assistant guide to guide for game and contravenes any of the provisions of subsections (1.1) to (1.3).

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (2.1) A person must not guide for game as an assistant guide unless the person

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (a) meets the prescribed qualifications, if any,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (b) is employed under subsection (1.1) as an assistant guide by a guide outfitter,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (c) has been issued written authorization under subsection (1.2) by the guide outfitter referred to in paragraph (b) of this subsection,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (d) at all times when guiding for game as an assistant guide, carries

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (i)  the written authorization referred to in paragraph (c), and

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (ii)  any other prescribed documentation that is issued, in the prescribed manner and form and with the prescribed content, to the assistant guide,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (e) produces the written authorization referred to in paragraph (c) and other documentation referred to in paragraph (d) (ii) on the request of an officer or a person the assistant guide is guiding for game,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (f) is not prohibited under this Act from guiding as an assistant guide,

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (g) complies with any conditions or restrictions imposed under this Act on the assistant guide, and

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (h) meets the prescribed requirements, if any.

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (2.2) A person guiding for game as an assistant guide commits an offence if the person fails to meet any of the requirements under subsection (2.1).

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (2.3) Subsections (1.1) to (1.3) and (2) to (2.2) do not apply in respect of a person who guides as an assistant guide if the person accompanies or assists another person to hunt game birds or small game on land other than Crown land.

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (3) A guide outfitter must be present in his or her guiding area during a majority of the time when his or her assistant guides are guiding for game.

heading: Requirements and offences for guide outfitters and assistant guides
paragraph: (4) If a guide outfitter fails to comply with subsection (3), a regional manager may take action under section 61.

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph:
49
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person acts as a guide for fish, or offers to act as a guide for fish, unless the person

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (a) holds an angling guide licence, or

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (b) holds an assistant angling guide licence.

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (2) A person who holds an angling guide licence commits an offence if the person employs another person to guide for fish and that other person does not hold an assistant angling guide licence.

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (3) An angling guide must

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (a) be present in one of the regions specified in the angling guide's licence, or

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (b) if specific waters or a specific area is authorized in the angling guide's licence, be present on or near those waters or in that area, in the manner specified on the angling guide's licence

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: during substantially all of the times when assistant angling guides employed by the angling guide are guiding for fish.

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (4) If an angling guide fails to comply with subsection (3), a regional manager may take action under section 61.

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (5) An angling guide who guides for fish elsewhere than on the waters or in the area authorized by the angling guide's licence commits an offence.

heading: Compulsory angling guide licence
paragraph: (6) An assistant angling guide who guides for fish elsewhere than on the waters or in the area authorized by the licence of the angling guide employing the assistant angling guide commits an offence.

heading: Applicants to know Act
paragraph:
50
		  An applicant for a guide outfitter licence must satisfy a regional manager that he or she possesses a working knowledge of this Act and the regulations.

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph:
51
		  (1) A regional manager

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph: (a) may issue a guide outfitter licence to a person if all of the following apply:

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph: (i)  the person is a citizen of Canada or a permanent resident of Canada;

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph: (ii)  the person has public liability insurance prescribed by regulation;

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph: (iii)  the person has other qualifications prescribed by regulation, and

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph: (b) must issue a guide outfitter licence to a person if the person is a person to whom the regional manager is obliged under the Labour Mobility Act to issue a guide outfitter licence.

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph: (2) A guide outfitter licence authorizes the holder to guide persons to hunt only for those species of game and in the area described in the licence.

heading: Issue of guide outfitter licence
paragraph: (3) If an area is part of a guiding territory assigned in a guiding territory certificate, the regional manager may not issue a guide outfitter licence under subsection (1) authorizing a person to guide in the area unless the person provides proof, satisfactory to the regional manager, that the person has the consent of the holder of the guiding territory certificate.

heading: Issue of angling guide licences
paragraph: 52		  (1) A regional manager may issue an angling guide licence to a person who

heading: Issue of angling guide licences
paragraph: (a) is a citizen of Canada or a permanent resident of Canada,

heading: Issue of angling guide licences
paragraph: (b) has public liability insurance and other qualifications prescribed by regulation, and

heading: Issue of angling guide licences
paragraph: (c) has submitted an angling guide operating plan that has been approved by the regional manager.

heading: Issue of angling guide licences
paragraph: (2) If the holder of an angling guide licence does not observe the undertakings given by the holder in an angling guide operating plan, the regional manager may take action under section 61.

heading: Issue of angling guide licences
paragraph: (3) Until the publication by the Recreational Fisheries Branch of a plan for managing guiding for fish and angling on a stream or lake or in an area of British Columbia, the minister may order the regional manager to restrict the issue of angling guide licences or endorsements for that stream, lake or area to persons who, on the date of the order, hold an angling guide licence or endorsement for that stream, lake or area.

heading: Issue of angling guide licences
paragraph: (4) If a plan referred to in subsection (3) for a stream, lake or area specified in an order of the minister is not published within the period of 18 months after the date of the order, the order ceases to have any effect on the expiry of that period.

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph:
53
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, by regulation, may do one or more of the following:

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (a) limit the number of angling guides permitted to guide for fish on a stream or lake or in an area of British Columbia during a specified period;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (b) limit the number of angler days on which members of a class of persons may be guided for fish on a stream or lake or in an area of British Columbia during a specified period;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (c) limit the number of

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (i)  clients an angling guide may guide for fish, and

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (ii)  assistant angling guides an angling guide may employ

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: on a stream or lake or in an area of British Columbia on any day during a specified period;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (d) limit the number of angler days on which members of a class of persons may angle without a guide on a stream or lake or in an area of British Columbia during a specified period;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (e) provide for the selection of applicants for angler days by a lottery or a booking system or by any other means;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (f) provide for the issue of licences specifying the number of days on which a person may angle on a stream or lake or in an area of British Columbia;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (g) provide for the allocation of angler day quotas to and among angler guides and for the disposal of angler day quotas by auction or tender or any other means;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (h) provide for the suspension, cancellation or variation of an angler day quota;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (i) prohibit or regulate the transfer of an angling licence or angler day quota or both;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (j) prescribe the information and undertakings to be included in an angling guide operating plan;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (k) impose or provide for requirements respecting the use of angler day quotas to ensure that the use of an angler day quota is not restricted to a club or other group of persons;

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (l) prohibit or regulate in relation to the periods of time during which members of a class of persons may angle on a stream or lake or in an area of British Columbia, including prescribing different periods for different classes, including, without limitation, classes based on age.

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of subsection (1) (e), (g), (h), (i), (j), (k) and (l), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make different regulations for different classes of streams or lakes or for different areas of British Columbia.

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (3) A regulation made under this section may

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (a) provide for the attachment of an angler day quota to, or for the reduction or cancellation of an angler day quota attached to, an angling guide licence issued before or after this section or the regulation comes into force, and

heading: Restrictions on guiding for fish and angling
paragraph: (b) impose limitations, restrictions and requirements relating to guiding for fish on an angling guide, even though the angling guide's licence was issued before this section or the regulation comes into force.

heading: Issue of assistant angling guide licence
paragraph:
54
		  (1) The regional manager or the regional manager's designate may issue an assistant angling guide licence to a person if all of the following apply:

heading: Issue of assistant angling guide licence
paragraph: (a) the person is a citizen of Canada or a permanent resident of Canada;

heading: Issue of assistant angling guide licence
paragraph: (b) the person is 19 years of age or older;

heading: Issue of assistant angling guide licence
paragraph: (c) the person has other qualifications prescribed by regulation.

heading: Issue of assistant angling guide licence
paragraph: (2) An assistant angling guide licence is valid only while the holder of the licence carries a record, signed by an angling guide, that indicates that the angling guide employs the holder as an assistant angling guide.

heading: Guide reports
paragraph:
55
		  (1) A guide outfitter must

heading: Guide reports
paragraph: (a) immediately after a hunt is concluded, complete and sign a guide report in the form specified by the director, and

heading: Guide reports
paragraph: (b) immediately after signing the completed guide report, give a copy of the report to each hunter guided on the hunt.

heading: Guide reports
paragraph: (2) A guide outfitter who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Guide reports
paragraph: (3) A guide outfitter may comply with subsection (1) by having an agent of the guide outfitter complete and sign the guide report, and give a copy of that report, on behalf of the guide outfitter.

heading: Guiding unlicensed hunters and anglers
paragraph:
56
		  (1) A guide who guides a hunter for game commits an offence unless the hunter holds a hunting licence and any other required licence.

heading: Guiding unlicensed hunters and anglers
paragraph: (2) A person who guides an angler for fish commits an offence unless the angler holds an angling licence and any other required licence.

heading: Non-use of waters or area by angling guide
paragraph:
58
		  If an angling guide does not guide or states that he or she does not intend to guide anglers in a year,

heading: Non-use of waters or area by angling guide
paragraph: (a) the angling guide may apply to the regional manager for permission to temporarily discontinue or partially discontinue the use of the waters or area authorized by his or her angling guide licence, or

heading: Non-use of waters or area by angling guide
paragraph: (b) the regional manager may review the angling guide's operation and, after affording him or her an opportunity to be heard, the regional manager may suspend, cancel or refuse to renew the angling guide's licence.

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph:
59
		  (1) A regional manager may issue a guiding territory certificate to a person who, or to a group of persons each of whom,

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (b) in the case of an individual, is 19 years of age or older, and

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (c) has the qualifications prescribed by regulation, if any.

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (2) A guiding territory certificate issued under this Act must be issued in a manner and form, if any, and with the conditions, if any, specified by the director.

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (3) Subject to a permit issued under section 70 (1) (b), a guiding territory certificate grants to the holder the exclusive control over guiding privileges in the area described in the certificate for the period stated in the certificate, which may not exceed 25 years.

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (4) The issuance of a guiding territory certificate to more than one person creates a tenancy in common in the rights granted by the certificate.

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (5) If a guiding territory certificate is issued to more than one person, the guiding territory certificate must

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (a) identify a person as the agent of the holders of the certificate, and

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (b) specify the interest held in the certificate by each holder of the certificate.

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (6) A regional manager may rely on information provided in an application or submission made by the agent identified in the guiding territory certificate as if that information were provided or that application or submission were made by all the holders of the certificate.

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (7) A regional manager may, on application by the holder of the guiding territory certificate, issue a new guiding territory certificate for a period not exceeding 25 years if

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (a) more than 5 years have elapsed since the date of issue of a guiding territory certificate issued before this subsection comes into force, or

heading: Guiding territory certificate
paragraph: (b) more than 3/5 of the period of a guiding territory certificate issued after this subsection comes into force has elapsed.

heading: Non-use of guiding territory
paragraph:
59.1
		  (1) On application by the holder of a guiding territory certificate who does not intend to consent to guiding in a year in the guiding territory described in the guiding territory certificate, the regional manager may give permission for the temporary or partial discontinuance of the use of that guiding territory for guiding.

heading: Non-use of guiding territory
paragraph: (2) If, in the opinion of the regional manager, there is no guiding in a year in a guiding territory described in a guiding territory certificate,

heading: Non-use of guiding territory
paragraph: (a) the regional manager may review the operation of the holder of the guiding territory certificate, and

heading: Non-use of guiding territory
paragraph: (b) after affording the holder an opportunity to be heard, the regional manager may suspend, cancel or refuse to renew the guiding territory certificate.

heading: Quotas
paragraph:
60
		  (1) If a regional manager issues a guide outfitter licence, the regional manager may attach a quota as a condition of the licence and may vary the quota for a subsequent licence year.

heading: Quotas
paragraph: (2) If a guide outfitter has a quota assigned as a condition of his or her guide outfitter licence and allows his or her clients to kill game to the extent that the number killed exceeds the quota assigned to the guide outfitter, the regional manager may reduce or take away his or her quota for a period and may take action under section 61.

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph:
61
		  (1) If a person holds, held within the last year or applies to renew, a guide outfitter's licence, guiding territory certificate or another licence to guide for game, angling guide licence, assistant angling guide licence, trapping licence, fur trader's licence or registration of a trapline and the person is convicted of an offence under this Act or does not comply with the conditions contained in or restrictions imposed on his or her licence, certificate or registration, or for another cause that the regional manager considers reasonable, the regional manager may conduct a hearing to determine whether the person should continue to enjoy the privileges afforded him or her by the licence or certificate or by having the registration and may do one or more of the following:

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (a) suspend, cancel or refuse to issue or renew the person's licence, certificate or registration;

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (b) amend the licence, certificate or registration to specify a different area in which the person may operate;

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (c) in the case of a guide outfitter,

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (i)  amend the licence to further limit the numbers, age and sex of game in respect of which the person may guide,

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (ii)  prohibit the person from guiding as an assistant guide for a period of time the regional manager specifies,

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (iii)  specify an area in which the person may not guide as an assistant guide for a period of time the regional manager specifies, and

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (iv)  impose conditions or restrictions on the person, in respect of guiding as an assistant guide, that the regional manager considers appropriate for a period of time the regional manager specifies;

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (d) amend the licence, certificate or registration to require the person to meet other conditions or restrictions that the regional manager considers appropriate;

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (e) in the case of an angling guide, reduce or cancel an angler day quota attached to that person's licence.

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (1.1) If a person is guiding as an assistant guide or was guiding as an assistant guide in the past year and the person is convicted of an offence under this Act, or for another cause that the regional manager considers reasonable, the regional manager may conduct a hearing to determine whether the person should be allowed to continue to guide as an assistant guide and may do one or more of the following:

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (a) prohibit the person from guiding as an assistant guide for a period of time the regional manager specifies;

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (b) specify an area in which the person may not guide as an assistant guide for a period of time the regional manager specifies;

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (c) impose conditions or restrictions on the person, in respect of guiding as an assistant guide, that the regional manager considers appropriate for a period of time the regional manager specifies.

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (2) The person in respect of whom the hearing under subsection (1) or (1.1) is to be conducted must be given reasonable notice of the time and place for the hearing.

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (3) A hearing conducted under subsection (1) or (1.1) must be held in public unless the minister orders that the hearing be held in private.

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (4) If notice of a hearing under subsection (1) is given to the holder of a licence, certificate or registered trapline and the licence or certificate expires or the registration ceases before the regional manager conducts the hearing or makes a determination under that subsection, the regional manager

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (a) may proceed to hear and determine the matter, and

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (b) is not obliged to renew or consider renewal of the licence or certificate or grant registration of the trapline until the earlier of the following:

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (i)  the end of the 30 day period immediately after the licence or certificate expires or the registration ceases;

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (ii)  the regional manager makes the determination after the hearing is held.

heading: Action if conditions of licence, certificate or registration not fulfilled
paragraph: (5) Despite subsection (4), if the hearing is delayed at the request of the holder of the licence, certificate or registered trapline, the regional manager is not obliged to consider renewing the licence or certificate or granting the registration of the trapline until the regional manager makes the determination after the hearing is held.

heading: Transfers
paragraph:
62
		  (1) The following may not be transferred without the authorization of the regional manager:

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (a) the privileges conferred in a guide outfitter licence;

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (b) the privileges conferred in a portion of the guiding area described in a guide outfitter licence.

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (2) The following may not be transferred except in accordance with and subject to the regulations:

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (a) the privileges conferred in a guiding territory certificate;

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (b) the privileges conferred in a portion of the guiding territory held under a guiding territory certificate;

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (c) a guiding territory certificate or an interest in a guiding territory certificate.

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty, none of the following constitutes a transfer for the purposes of subsection (2):

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (a) the granting of a security interest in a guiding territory certificate or in an interest in a guiding territory certificate by the holder of the certificate or interest;

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (b) the transmission of a privilege, certificate or interest referred to in subsection (2) (a), (b) or (c) to

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (i)  a trustee in bankruptcy of the holder of the privilege, certificate or interest, or

heading: Transfers
paragraph: (ii)  a personal representative of the holder of the privilege, certificate or interest, in the event of the holder's death.

heading: Certificate or licence is part of estate
paragraph:
64
		  (1) An interest in a guiding territory certificate is part of the estate of the holder of that interest and, subject to section 62 (2), the heirs or administrators of a deceased holder may transfer, within 2 years of the holder's death, the holder's interest in the guiding territory certificate to a person who qualifies under section 59 (1).

heading: Certificate or licence is part of estate
paragraph: (1.1) If an interest in a guiding territory certificate is not transferred in accordance with subsection (1) after the death of a holder, the deceased holder's interest in the guiding territory certificate is forfeited to the government.

heading: Certificate or licence is part of estate
paragraph: (2) An angling guide licence, including any angler day quota attached to it, is part of the estate of the angling guide and, subject to the regulations, the heirs or administrators of a deceased angling guide may transfer, within 2 years after the angling guide's death, the privileges conferred by the angling guide licence and any angler day quota attached to it.

heading: Certificate or licence is part of estate
paragraph: (3) If an annual fee for an angling guide licence becomes due in the interval between the death of the licence holder and the date of a transfer under this section, no annual fee is payable.

heading: Certificate or licence is part of estate
paragraph: (4) If privileges conferred by an angling guide licence are not transferred in accordance with this section, the heirs or administrators must surrender the angling guide licence to the regional manager.

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph:
64.1
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may, by regulation, do one or more of the following:

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (a) impose or provide for requirements respecting applications for guiding territory certificates and prescribing qualifications of applicants for guiding territory certificates;

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (b) prohibit or regulate the transfer of a guiding territory certificate and any privilege or interest referred to in section 62 (2) (a), (b) or (c), including, without limitation, prohibiting the transfer without the authorization of the regional manager;

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (c) prescribe fees for the transfer of a guiding territory certificate and any privilege or interest referred to in section 62 (2) (a), (b) or (c);

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (d) prohibit or regulate in relation to control of and changes to control of a corporation that holds an interest in a guiding territory certificate, including, without limitation, the following:

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (i)  prescribing circumstances that constitute control of and changes to control of the corporation;

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (ii)  imposing or providing for requirements respecting control of and changes to control of the corporation, including, without limitation, requiring the corporation to give notice of a change to, an acquisition of or a disposition of control of the corporation in the prescribed manner and form, within the prescribed time and accompanied by any information or documents required by the regulations;

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (iii)  authorizing the regional manager to, after affording the corporation an opportunity to be heard, do one or more of the following:

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (A) by order in writing, require the corporation to transfer, subject to section 62 (2), that corporation's interest in the guiding territory certificate to another person qualified to hold a guiding territory certificate within the period specified in the order;

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (B) amend, suspend or cancel a guiding territory certificate that is held by the corporation;

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (C) any other thing prescribed by regulation.

heading: Regulation of guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this section, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make different regulations for different persons, guiding territory certificates or privileges or interests in guiding territory certificates, or for different classes of persons, guiding territory certificates or privileges or interests in guiding territory certificates.

heading: Disposal of guiding territories and interests in guiding territory certificates
paragraph:
65
