		  (1) If exclusive control over guiding privileges in an area is not assigned in a guiding territory certificate, the regional manager may designate the area as a guiding territory.

heading: Disposal of guiding territories and interests in guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (2) If

heading: Disposal of guiding territories and interests in guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (a) the regional manager designates a new guiding territory, or

heading: Disposal of guiding territories and interests in guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (b) a guiding territory certificate is cancelled or surrendered or forfeited to the government and the regional manager considers that the exclusive control over guiding privileges in the guiding territory described in the guiding territory certificate should be reassigned,

heading: Disposal of guiding territories and interests in guiding territory certificates
paragraph: the exclusive control over guiding privileges in that guiding territory must be advertised for sale by the regional manager and sold by tender or by any other prescribed means to a person qualified to hold a guiding territory certificate.

heading: Disposal of guiding territories and interests in guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (3) If the exclusive control over guiding privileges in an area is not assigned in a guiding territory certificate and the regional manager considers that the area is not by itself suitable for designation as a guiding territory, the regional manager may assign, by amendment to a guiding territory certificate and on payment of the prescribed charge, the exclusive control over guiding privileges in all or part of that area to the holder of the guiding territory certificate in respect of a guiding territory adjoining that area.

heading: Disposal of guiding territories and interests in guiding territory certificates
paragraph: (4) If an interest in a guiding territory certificate is forfeited to the government under section 64 (1.1), the interest in that certificate must be advertised for sale by the regional manager and sold by tender or by any other prescribed means to a person qualified to hold a guiding territory certificate.

heading: No proprietary rights in wildlife
paragraph:
67
		  A guiding territory certificate or angling guide's licence does not

heading: No proprietary rights in wildlife
paragraph: (a) give the holder any proprietary rights in wildlife or fish, or

heading: No proprietary rights in wildlife
paragraph: (b) restrict the rights of a resident to hunt or fish.

heading: No cancellation for park
paragraph:
68
		  The regional manager must not cancel a guide outfitter's licence, a guiding territory certificate or an angling guide's licence because of the establishment of a park under the Park Act, the  Protected Areas of British Columbia Act, the Community Charter or the Local Government Act in the area described in the licence or certificate.

heading: Royalties
paragraph: 69		  A guide outfitter commits an offence if the guide outfitter fails to pay to the Minister of Finance a royalty on an animal taken by a person guided by the guide outfitter, or guided on his or her behalf, in the amount and within the time prescribed by regulation.

heading: Permit in guide area
paragraph:
70
		  (1) The regional manager may, by issuing a permit containing conditions the regional manager considers suitable, authorize

heading: Permit in guide area
paragraph: (a) a resident, who holds a hunting licence and meets the prescribed qualifications, to accompany

heading: Permit in guide area
paragraph: (i)  a non-resident, or

heading: Permit in guide area
paragraph: (ii)  a non-resident alien

heading: Permit in guide area
paragraph: as provided in the regulations, while hunting big game, if no remuneration is requested by, offered to or accepted by the permittee, or

heading: Permit in guide area
paragraph: (b) a guide outfitter or angling guide to guide in an area other than that endorsed on his or her guide outfitter licence or angling guide licence.

heading: Permit in guide area
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if the person, without a permit issued under subsection (1), accompanies a non-resident or a non-resident alien referred to in subsection (1) (a) (i) or (ii) while the non-resident or the non-resident alien hunts for big game.

heading: Sheltering agreements
paragraph:
70.1
		  (1) In this section and section 70.2:

heading: Sheltering agreements
paragraph: "guest" means a member of a first nation who, under a sheltering agreement, hunts in the traditional territory of the host first nation;

heading: Sheltering agreements
paragraph: "host first nation" means the first nation whose governing body enters into a sheltering agreement under subsection (2) of this section;

heading: Sheltering agreements
paragraph: "sheltering agreement" means an agreement referred to in subsection (2) of this section.

heading: Sheltering agreements
paragraph: (2) The minister and the governing body of a first nation may enter into an agreement respecting hunting in the traditional territory of that first nation by members of other first nations.

heading: Sheltering agreements
paragraph: (3) A sheltering agreement may include parties in addition to those referred to in subsection (2), including the governing body of the first nation of which a guest is a member.

heading: Authorizations in relation to hunting under sheltering agreements
paragraph:
70.2
		  (1) Subject to subsection (2) and without limiting the matters that may be addressed in a sheltering agreement, a sheltering agreement may include provisions that do one or more of the following:

heading: Authorizations in relation to hunting under sheltering agreements
paragraph: (a) in respect of hunting in the traditional territory of the host first nation, authorize a guest to

heading: Authorizations in relation to hunting under sheltering agreements
paragraph: (i)  do anything that is prohibited under this Act, or

heading: Authorizations in relation to hunting under sheltering agreements
paragraph: (ii)  omit to do anything that is required to be done under this Act;

heading: Authorizations in relation to hunting under sheltering agreements
paragraph: (b) set out conditions or limits that a guest must comply with in relation to an authority provided for under paragraph (a).

heading: Authorizations in relation to hunting under sheltering agreements
paragraph: (2) A provision included in a sheltering agreement under subsection (1) is not effective unless the Lieutenant Governor in Council, by regulation, approves the provision.

heading: Authorizations in relation to hunting under sheltering agreements
paragraph: (3) Despite any other provision of this Act or the regulations, a guest who acts in accordance with the provisions included in a sheltering agreement under subsection (1) has the authority provided for under subsection (1) (a).

heading: Requirement to keep records
paragraph:
71
		  (1) A taxidermist, a tanner, a fur trader, a meatcutter or an owner or operator of a cold storage plant commits an offence if

heading: Requirement to keep records
paragraph: (a) he or she fails to keep, in the prescribed manner, a record of the receipt of wildlife or fish or a part of either, or

heading: Requirement to keep records
paragraph: (b) having received wildlife or fish or a part of either, he or she fails to keep the record referred to in paragraph (a) for a period of 2 years from the time he or she gives up possession of the wildlife or fish or a part of either.

heading: Requirement to keep records
paragraph: (2) A taxidermist, a tanner, a fur trader, a meatcutter or an owner or operator of a cold storage plant commits an offence if he or she fails

heading: Requirement to keep records
paragraph: (a) to produce for inspection, on demand by an officer, all wildlife and records in his or her possession, or

heading: Requirement to keep records
paragraph: (b) to make a full and complete return, as prescribed by regulation, of all wildlife that has been or is in his or her possession for processing, manufacturing, curing, selling or trading.

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph:
72
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person engages in the business of fur trading unless he or she holds a fur trader's licence.

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (2) A regional manager may issue a fur trader's licence to a person who is a citizen of Canada or a permanent resident of Canada.

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (3) If a fur trader has more than one established place of business in British Columbia for the purpose of buying, selling or trading in pelts or skins, the fur trader commits an offence if he or she fails to obtain a separate fur trader's licence for each place of business.

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (4) A person is not, for the purposes of subsection (1), engaged in the business of fur trading, if the activity as a fur trader is confined to any of the following:

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (a) the buying of furs at wholesale from licensed fur traders at public auction;

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (b) the buying of pelts of animals raised in captivity from persons lawfully engaged in carrying on the business of breeding fur bearing animals;

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (c) selling pelts taken by the person as

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (i)  the holder of a trapping licence, or

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (ii)  a person exempted from holding a trapping licence;

heading: Fur trader's licence
paragraph: (d) buying pelts for personal use.

heading: Royalties for fur
paragraph:
73
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person, having in possession a pelt or skin of a fur bearing animal not raised in captivity and on which a royalty has not already been paid under this section, fails to pay to the Minister of Finance a royalty, as prescribed by regulation, on each pelt and skin in his or her possession.

heading: Royalties for fur
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to

heading: Royalties for fur
paragraph: (a) the holder of a trapping licence, or

heading: Royalties for fur
paragraph: (b) a person exempted from holding a trapping licence

heading: Royalties for fur
paragraph: when selling pelts, lawfully taken by him or her, to the holder of a fur trader's licence.

heading: Seizure of pelt or skin
paragraph:
74
		  A conservation officer or constable may seize a pelt or skin on which he or she believes on reasonable grounds that the royalty payable under section 73 has not been paid.

heading: Accidental killing of wildlife
paragraph:
75
		  (1) A person who kills or wounds wildlife, other than prescribed wildlife, either by accident or for the protection of life or property, must promptly report to an officer

heading: Accidental killing of wildlife
paragraph: (a) the killing or wounding, and

heading: Accidental killing of wildlife
paragraph: (b) the location of the wildlife.

heading: Accidental killing of wildlife
paragraph: (2) A person who fails to report as required under subsection (1) commits an offence.

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph:
76
		  (1) On the escape from captivity or the release or abandonment of an animal that is not a domestic animal, the government acquires the ownership of that animal.

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if a fur farm animal or a game farm animal escapes from the premises of an owner,

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph: (a) the application of subsection (1) is suspended for the prescribed period,

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph: (b) the owner retains ownership of the animal during the prescribed period, and

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph: (c) if the owner does not recapture the animal within the prescribed period, subsection (1) applies as though the animal had escaped at the end of the prescribed period.

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of subsection (2):

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph: "fur farm animal" and "game farm animal" have the same meaning as in a regulation made under the Animal Health Act;

heading: Escape, etc., of captive animal
paragraph: "prescribed period" means the period prescribed for this purpose under the Animal Health Act, subject to any discretion conferred, for this purpose, on the chief veterinarian under that Act.

heading: Release or escape of animals
paragraph: 77		  (1) A person who releases or abandons an animal or from whose captivity an animal escapes

heading: Release or escape of animals
paragraph: (a) is, despite section 11 (4) of the Livestock Act, liable to the government for loss or damage to wildlife or wildlife habitat caused by the animal, and for all costs incurred by the government in pursuing, recovering, holding or destroying it, and

heading: Release or escape of animals
paragraph: (b) is not entitled to any compensation from the government if the animal is destroyed under section 79.

heading: Release or escape of animals
paragraph: (2) If a person releases or abandons an animal, other than a domestic animal, the person commits an offence.

heading: Release or escape of animals
paragraph: (3) If an animal, other than a domestic animal, escapes from the possession of a person, the person commits an offence if he or she fails to make every reasonable effort to recover the animal.

heading: Release or escape of animals
paragraph: (4) This section does not apply if the person is authorized by the regional manager to release the animal.

heading: Dogs hunting game
paragraph: 78		  A person commits an offence if the person causes or allows a dog to hunt or pursue

heading: Dogs hunting game
paragraph: (a) wildlife or an endangered species or threatened species, or

heading: Dogs hunting game
paragraph: (b) game, except in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Destruction of animals
paragraph:
79
		  (1) An officer may kill an animal, other than a domestic animal, that is at large and is likely to harm persons, property, wildlife or wildlife habitat.

heading: Destruction of animals
paragraph: (2) An officer may kill a dog that is

heading: Destruction of animals
paragraph: (a) at large in a wildlife management area, or

heading: Destruction of animals
paragraph: (b) at large and harassing wildlife.

heading: Destruction of animals
paragraph: (3) An officer may kill a cat at large where wildlife is usually found.

heading: Obstructing licensed persons
paragraph:
80
		  A person commits an offence if the person interferes with or obstructs a person licensed or permitted to capture wildlife or to hunt, fish, guide or trap while that person is lawfully so engaged.

heading: Documents not transferable
paragraph:
81
		  Except as authorized by regulation or as otherwise provided under this Act, a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization is not transferable, and a person commits an offence if the person

heading: Documents not transferable
paragraph: (a) allows his or her licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization to be used by another person, or

heading: Documents not transferable
paragraph: (b) uses another person's licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization.

heading: False statements
paragraph:
82
		  (1) A person commits an offence if the person knowingly makes a false statement

heading: False statements
paragraph: (a) in order to obtain a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization,

heading: False statements
paragraph: (b) on a licence or permit issued by him or her under this Act,

heading: False statements
paragraph: (c) in a book, record, certificate, report or return made, kept or furnished under this Act, or

heading: False statements
paragraph: (d) to an officer engaged in the discharge of his or her duties under this Act, if the person is required to provide information under this Act.

heading: False statements
paragraph: (2) A licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization is void if it is issued contrary to this Act.

heading: False statements
paragraph: (3) A person commits an offence if the person, without lawful authority, changes or alters a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization issued under this Act.

heading: False statements
paragraph: (4) A person commits an offence if the person obliterates, alters, imitates or duplicates a stamp, tag, seal, brand, mark or signature that is placed on wildlife or a part of wildlife under this Act.

heading: False statements
paragraph: (5) A person commits an offence if the person makes a false statement in an application that the person makes on behalf of another person.

heading: False statements
paragraph: (6) A person is not guilty of an offence under subsection (5) if at the time of the statement the person did not know that the statement was false and, exercising due diligence, could not have known that the statement was false.

heading: Posting signs and notices
paragraph:
83
		  (1) An officer may post signs or notices the officer considers necessary or advisable in order to carry out the provisions of this Act.

heading: Posting signs and notices
paragraph: (2) A person who without lawful authority removes, alters, destroys or defaces a sign, notice or traffic control device posted or erected under this Act commits an offence.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph:
84
		  (1) For the purpose of determining the fines and penalties to which a person is subject on conviction for an offence under this Act,

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (a) subsections (2) and (2.1) apply in relation to an offence

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (ii)  prescribed under section 108 (3) (l) (i),

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (b) subsections (3) and (4) apply in relation to an offence

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (i.1)  under section 48 (2) respecting the contravention of any of the provisions of section 48 (1.1),

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (i.2)  under section 48 (2.2) respecting the failure to meet a requirement under section 48 (2.1) (c) or (f),

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (i.3)  under section 97 (6) respecting the contravention of section 97 (2) (a) or (b) or (4) (a) or (b), or

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (ii)  prescribed under section 108 (3) (l) (ii), and

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (c) subsections (5) and (6) apply in relation to any offence under this Act that is not referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (2) A person who commits an offence referred to in subsection (1) (a) is liable,

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (a) on a first conviction, to a fine set out in subsection (2.1) or to a term of imprisonment not exceeding 2 years, or both, and

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (b) on each subsequent conviction for the same offence or another offence referred to in subsection (1) (a), to a fine of not more than $500 000 and not less than $5 000 or to a term of imprisonment not exceeding 3 years, or both.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (2.1) For the purposes of subsection (2) (a), the person referred to in that subsection is liable,

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (a) if the first conviction is for an offence under section 82 (1) (a) or (5), to a fine of not more than $250 000, and

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (b) in any other case, to a fine of not more than $250 000 and not less than $2 500.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsection (4), a person who commits an offence referred to in subsection (1) (b) is liable,

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (a) on a first conviction, to a fine of not more than $100 000 or to a term of imprisonment not exceeding one year, or both, and

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (b) on each subsequent conviction for the same offence or another offence referred to in subsection (1) (b), to a fine of not more than $200 000 and not less than $2 000 or to a term of imprisonment not exceeding 2 years, or both.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3) (a), if the person referred to in that subsection has previously been convicted of an offence referred to in subsection (1) (a), the person is liable to the punishment set out in subsection (3) (b).

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), a person who commits an offence referred to in subsection (1) (c) is liable,

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (a) on a first conviction, to a fine of not more than $50 000 or to a term of imprisonment not exceeding 6 months, or both, and

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (b) on each subsequent conviction for the same offence or another offence referred to in subsection (1) (c), to a fine of not more than $100 000 and not less than $1 000 or to a term of imprisonment not exceeding one year, or both.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (6) Despite subsection (5) (a), if the person referred to in that subsection has previously been convicted of an offence referred to in subsection (1) (a) or (b), the person is liable to the punishment set out in subsection (5) (b).

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (6.1) In subsections (6.2) to (6.4), "wildlife" includes a part of wildlife.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (6.2) If a thing, other than wildlife, has been seized in relation to an offence under this Act or the Firearm Act, the court may

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (a) order the thing forfeited to the government, if the court is satisfied that the thing was used in the commission of the offence or possessed in contravention of this Act, the Firearm Act or their regulations, or

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (b) deal with the thing in accordance with section 24.2 (4) of the Offence Act and for this purpose section 24.2 (2) and (3) of the Offence Act do not apply.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (6.3) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act or the Firearm Act, the court must order returned to the government any wildlife seized in relation to that offence that has not already been disposed of under section 97.2, 97.3 or 97.6 if the wildlife was

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (a) obtained by or used in the commission of that offence, or

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (b) possessed in contravention of this Act, the Firearm Act or their regulations.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (6.4) Wildlife returned to the government under subsection (6.3) is to be disposed of as the minister directs.

heading: Fines and penalties
paragraph: (7) Nothing in this section limits the application of sections 24 and 84.1 to 84.3 or any other sanctions provided for in this Act or the regulations under this Act.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: 84.1		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act, in addition to any punishment imposed, the court may, having regard to the nature of the offence and the circumstances surrounding its commission, make an order containing one or more of the following prohibitions, directions or requirements:

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (a) prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity that may, in the opinion of the court, result in the continuation or repetition of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (b) directing the person to take any action the court considers appropriate to remedy or avoid any harm to the environment or any wildlife, endangered species or threatened species, that resulted or may result from the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (c) directing the person to pay the government an amount of money as compensation, in whole or in part, for the cost of any remedial or preventive action taken by or caused to be taken on behalf of the government as a result of the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (d) directing the person to perform community service;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (e) directing the person to pay an amount of money the court considers appropriate to

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (ii)  the trustee under Part 3 for inclusion in the trust property, as that term is defined in section 118, or

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (iii)  the Grizzly Bear Trust Fund established and administered by the government;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (f) directing the person to post a bond or pay into court an amount of money the court considers appropriate for the purpose of ensuring compliance with any prohibition, direction or requirement under this section;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (g) directing the person to submit to the minister, on application by the minister within 3 years after the date of the conviction, any information respecting the activities of the person that the court considers appropriate in the circumstances;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (h) directing the person to publish, in any manner the court considers appropriate, the facts relating to the commission of the offence;

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (i) requiring the person to comply with any other conditions that the court considers appropriate for securing the person's good conduct and for preventing the person from repeating the offence or committing other offences under this Act.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (2) If a person fails to comply with an order referred to in subsection (1) (h) directing the person to publish the facts relating to the commission of an offence, the minister may publish those facts and recover the costs of publication from the person.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (3) If

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (a) an order under this section or section 84.2 directs a person to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose, or

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (b) the minister incurs publication costs under subsection (2) of this section,

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: the amount and any interest payable on that amount constitute a debt due to the government and may be recovered as such in any court of competent jurisdiction.

heading: Creative sentencing
paragraph: (4) A person who contravenes an order under this section or section 84.2 commits an offence and is liable to the penalties provided for the offence in relation to which the order was made.

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph:
84.2
		  (1) An application for variation of an order under section 84.1 may be made to the court that made the order by

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (a) the Attorney General, or

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (b) the person against whom the order under section 84.1 was made.

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (2) Before hearing an application under subsection (1), the court may order the applicant to give notice of the application in accordance with the directions of the court.

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (3) On an application under subsection (1), if the court considers variation appropriate because of a change in circumstances, the court may make an order doing one or more of the following:

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (a) changing the original order or any conditions specified in it;

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (b) relieving the person referred to in subsection (1) (b) absolutely or partially from compliance with all or part of the original order;

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (c) reducing the period for which the original order is to remain in effect;

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (d) extending the period for which the original order is to remain in effect, subject to the limit that this extension must not be longer than one year.

heading: Variation of section 84.1 orders
paragraph: (4) If an application under subsection (1) has been heard by a court, no other application may be made in respect of the order under section 84.1 except with leave of the court.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph:
84.3
		  (1) If a person is convicted of an offence under this Act and the court is satisfied that, as a result of the commission of the offence, the person acquired any monetary benefits or that monetary benefits accrued to the person, the court may order the person to pay a fine equal to the court's estimation of the amount of those monetary benefits.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: (2) If a person is convicted of an offence under section 22 or an offence prescribed under section 108 (3) (l) (iii) and the court is satisfied that the person was engaged in a commercial enterprise in relation to the commission of the offence and that monetary benefits could have accrued as a result of the commission of that offence, the court may order the person to pay a fine equal to the court's estimation of the amount of those monetary benefits.

heading: Additional fine
paragraph: (3) A fine under subsection (1) or (2) is in addition to and not in place of a fine under section 84 or an order under section 84.1 or 84.2 directing a person to pay an amount of money as compensation or for any other purpose.

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph:
85
		  (1) This section applies if a person

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (a) fails to pay, within the time required by law, a fine imposed as a result of the person's conviction for an offence under this Act or the Firearm Act, and

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (b) has been served with notice of this section.

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (2) In the circumstances referred to in subsection (1),

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (a) the person's right to apply for or obtain a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization under this Act is suspended immediately and automatically on the failure to pay the fine,

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (b) all licences, permits and limited entry hunting authorizations issued to that person under this Act are cancelled immediately and automatically on the failure to pay the fine,

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (b.1) the person must not apply for employment as an assistant guide,

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (b.2) the person must not guide as an assistant guide, and

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (c) the person commits an offence if, before that fine is paid, the person

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (i)  applies for, or in any way obtains, a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization under this Act,

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (ii)  does anything for which a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization under this Act is required,

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (iii)  applies for employment as an assistant guide, or

heading: Failure to pay fine
paragraph: (iv)  guides as an assistant guide.

heading: Officers exempted
paragraph: 86		  The offence provisions of this Act and the regulations and section 9 of the Firearm Act do not apply to an officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties.

heading: Arrest
paragraph: 87		  A conservation officer or constable may, without a warrant, arrest a person he or she finds committing an offence against this Act or the regulations.

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph:
88
		  (1) A conservation officer or constable may, if he or she has reasonable and probable grounds to believe that by reason of consumption of alcohol a person who is hunting or carrying a firearm is affected in his or her ability to hunt or handle a firearm safely and responsibly, request that person to surrender any firearms in his or her possession.

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (2) A conservation officer or constable may, if he or she has reasonable and probable grounds to believe that a person who is hunting or carrying a firearm is affected by a drug in his or her ability to hunt or handle a firearm safely and responsibly, request that person to surrender any firearms in his or her possession.

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (3) On a request being made under subsection (1),

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (a) the hunting licence, if any, of the person is suspended and the person must not hunt or carry a firearm, and

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (b) the person must immediately surrender to the conservation officer or constable all firearms in the person's possession.

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (4) A conservation officer or constable must return the firearms surrendered under subsection (3) to the person on

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (a) the person promptly undergoing a test that indicates his or her blood contains less than 50 mg of alcohol to 100 ml of blood,

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (b) the expiration of 24 hours after the surrender, or

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (c) the production by the person to the conservation officer or constable of a certificate made by a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner after the suspension and certifying that the blood of the person contains less than 50 mg of alcohol to 100 ml of blood,

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: and the suspension and prohibitions referred to in subsection (3) (a) are terminated on the person satisfying the requirements of paragraph (a), (b) or (c).

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (5) On a request being made under subsection (2), subsections (3) and (4) (b) apply.

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (6) If a person to whom subsection (2) applies satisfies a conservation officer or constable having charge of the matter that his or her ability to hunt or handle a firearm safely and responsibly is not affected by a drug other than alcohol, the suspension and prohibitions referred to in subsection (3) (a) are terminated and the firearms must be returned to the person.

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (8) A person commits an offence if the person, during the period of the suspension and prohibitions referred to in subsection (3) (a),

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (a) applies for or in any way obtains a new hunting licence,

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (b) hunts, or

heading: Surrender of firearms
paragraph: (c) carries a firearm.

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph:
88.1
		  (1) In this section, "private dwelling" means a structure used solely as a private residence or a residential accommodation within any other structure.

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (2) If a conservation officer believes on reasonable grounds that dangerous wildlife is or may be attracted to any land or premises other than a private dwelling, the conservation officer may, without a warrant, enter and search the land or premises.

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (3) If a conservation officer believes on reasonable grounds that the existence or location of an attractant in, on or about any land or premises, other than in a private dwelling, poses a risk to the safety of any person because the attractant is attracting or could attract dangerous wildlife to the land or premises, the conservation officer may issue a dangerous wildlife protection order directing an owner, occupier or person in charge of that land or premises to contain, move or remove the attractant within a reasonable period of time specified in the order.

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), a dangerous wildlife protection order may not be made in respect of any of the following:

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (a) a farm operation, as defined in section 1 of the Farm Practices Protection (Right to Farm) Act, that

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (i)  is conducted on, in or over land anywhere in British Columbia, and

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (ii)  meets the requirements set out in section 2 (2) (a) and (c) of that Act;

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (b) a person who is engaging in trapping in accordance with all other applicable provisions of this Act and the regulations;

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (c) a facility for the disposal of waste, that is operated in accordance with the Environmental Management Act by a municipality, as defined in section 1 (1) of that Act.

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (5) A person to whom an order under subsection (3) is expressed to apply must comply with the order within the period of time specified in that order.

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (6) For the purpose of ensuring that an order issued under subsection (3) is being, or has been, complied with, a conservation officer may, without a warrant, enter and search the land or premises other than a private dwelling that is affected by the order.

heading: Dangerous wildlife protection order
paragraph: (7) A person commits an offence if the person neglects or refuses to comply with an order in accordance with subsection (5).

heading: Entering premises
paragraph: 89		  (1) For the purpose of ensuring that this Act and the regulations are being complied with, an officer may enter and inspect any premises or enclosure in which live wildlife or live fish is kept but, at the request of the owner or occupier, the officer must produce proof of identity.

heading: Entering premises
paragraph: (2) Despite the Trespass Act, an officer exercising duties under this Act may enter any land, whether enclosed or not but, at the request of the owner or occupier of the land, the officer must produce proof of identity.

heading: Inspection of firearms
paragraph: 90		  (1) A person, when requested to do so, for the purposes of this Act or the Firearm Act, by a conservation officer or constable, must immediately produce and permit inspection of a firearm in his or her possession.

heading: Inspection of firearms
paragraph: (2) A conservation officer or constable may, for the purposes of this Act or the Firearm Act, inspect a firearm found in or on a vehicle or boat.

heading: Inspection of camps
paragraph: 91		  An officer may inspect a camp occupied by a hunter or angler.

heading: Search warrants
paragraph:
92
		  On information in the prescribed form and on oath that there is reasonable ground to believe that an animal or fish, or a portion of an animal or fish, killed, taken or possessed in violation of this Act or the regulations, or about to be illegally exported, is located in or on a building or premises, a justice may by a warrant authorize and direct a conservation officer or constable to enter and search the building or premises and to seize and remove an animal or fish, or a portion of it, found, and it may be disposed of as provided in this Act.

heading: Search without warrant
paragraph:
93
		  A conservation officer or constable may, without a warrant,

heading: Search without warrant
paragraph: (a) search a person whom he or she believes on reasonable grounds has in his or her possession any wildlife or fish killed, taken or possessed in violation of this Act or the regulations, or about to be illegally exported,

heading: Search without warrant
paragraph: (b) stop and search a motor vehicle, private or chartered aircraft, boat or other conveyance, in or on which he or she believes on reasonable grounds that wildlife or fish is being carried by a person, and

heading: Search without warrant
paragraph: (c) enter and search a shop, public market, storehouse, garage, restaurant, hotel, eating house or camp, in or on which he or she believes on reasonable grounds that wildlife or fish is located.

heading: Seizure
paragraph:
94
		  (1) A conservation officer or constable may seize wildlife or fish or parts of either wildlife or fish, anything referred to in paragraph (b) and anything found in, on or about a place, building or premises, or in the possession of a person, that might afford evidence of the commission of an offence under this Act, if the conservation officer or constable

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (a) finds in the possession of a person, or in, on or about a place or thing referred to in section 93, wildlife or fish that the conservation officer or constable believes on reasonable grounds was killed, taken or possessed in violation of this Act, or is about to be illegally exported, or

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (b) finds firearms, ammunition, decoys, traps, fishing rods or other devices or materials, implements or appliances for hunting or trapping wildlife or for catching fish, that the conservation officer or constable believes on reasonable grounds were held, kept or used for or in connection with a violation of this Act.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (2) A conservation officer may seize wildlife or fish, or parts of either wildlife or fish, in a person's possession if the conservation officer believes on reasonable grounds that the right of property in that wildlife is with the government or remains in the government.

heading: Seizure
paragraph: (3) Sections 23 to 24.2 of the Offence Act do not apply in respect of wildlife or fish, or parts of either wildlife or fish, seized under this Act.

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: 95		  (1) In this section and sections 95.1 to 95.3:

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: "aircraft" means a private or chartered aircraft;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: "specified person" means a person in possession of any of the following:

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (a) an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (b) a boat;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (c) any water-related equipment;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: "vehicle" means a motor vehicle or other vehicle;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: "water-related equipment" means any of the following:

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (a) a boat trailer;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (b) any item used for fishing;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (c) a wharf or dock;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (d) any item used for water-based activities;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (e) any equipment associated with, and any component of, an aircraft designed to land on water, a boat or a thing referred to in paragraphs (a) to (d) of this definition.

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (2) An officer may, for the purposes of this Act, stop a person who is driving or operating a vehicle, aircraft or boat to determine whether or not the driver, operator or occupants have been hunting, trapping or angling, and to obtain information about wildlife or game fish possessed by them.

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (3) An officer may, for the purposes of preventing aquatic invasive species from entering into or spreading in British Columbia, stop any of the following persons to obtain any of the records or information referred to in subsection (4):

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (a) the driver or operator of a vehicle transporting

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (i)  an aircraft designed to land on water,

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (ii)  a boat, or

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (iii)  any water-related equipment;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (b) the operator of an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (c) the operator of a boat;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (d) a specified person.

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (4) The following records or information may be obtained under subsection (3):

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (a) information from the driver or operator, any occupant or a specified person in relation to the use of the vehicle, aircraft, boat or water-related equipment in water-based activities;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (b) information from the driver or operator, any occupant or a specified person in relation to the exposure of the vehicle, aircraft, boat or water-related equipment to water;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (c) records or information in relation to the vehicle, aircraft, boat or water-related equipment, including, without limitation, any of the following:

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (i)  vehicle, aircraft or boat registration;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (ii)  boating records;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (iii)  inspection or decontamination records;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (iv)  prescribed records or information;

heading: Power to stop and obtain information
paragraph: (d) any other information in relation to aquatic invasive species.

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph:
95.1
		  (1) For the purposes of preventing aquatic invasive species from entering into or spreading in British Columbia, an officer may, without a warrant, stop any of the following persons to conduct an inspection in accordance with subsection (2):

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (a) the driver or operator of a vehicle transporting

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (i)  an aircraft designed to land on water,

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (ii)  a boat, or

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (iii)  any water-related equipment;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (b) the operator of an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (c) the operator of a boat;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (d) a specified person.

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of preventing aquatic invasive species from entering into or spreading in British Columbia, an officer may, without a warrant, do any of the following:

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (a) inspect an aircraft designed to land on water, a boat or any water-related equipment, including, without limitation, any of the following:

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (i)  the interior or exterior of the aircraft, boat or equipment;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (ii)  bait buckets;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (iii)  ballast tanks;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (iv)  bilge areas;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (v)  compartments;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (vi)  through-hull fittings;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (b) inspect the exterior of a vehicle transporting any of the following:

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (i)  an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (ii)  a boat;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (iii)  any water-related equipment;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (c) enter the interior of a vehicle in which a boat or any water-related equipment is contained and inspect the boat or water-related equipment if

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (i)  the vehicle contains a boat or any equipment that was exposed to water, and

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (ii)  the boat or equipment cannot reasonably be removed from the vehicle.

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (3) An officer who is conducting an inspection under this section may do any of the following for the purposes of the inspection:

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (a) require the driver or operator or an occupant of a vehicle, aircraft designed to land on water or boat or a specified person to facilitate access to the vehicle, aircraft or boat, or any equipment, including, without limitation, by uncovering or unlocking an area to be inspected;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (b) take samples of water, aquatic invasive species or suspected aquatic invasive species and perform analyses and tests;

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (c) take photographs of

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (i)  a vehicle,

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (ii)  an aircraft designed to land on water,

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (iii)  a boat,

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (iv)  any water-related equipment, or

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (v)  water, aquatic invasive species or suspected aquatic invasive species that are in or on a vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment referred to in subparagraphs (i) to (iv);

heading: Power to stop and inspect
paragraph: (d) make copies of relevant records.

heading: Sign or traffic control device to stop vehicle
paragraph:
95.2
		  For the purposes of stopping a person under section 95 or 95.1, an officer may post or erect a sign or traffic control device directing that any of the following persons must stop as indicated on the sign or device:

heading: Sign or traffic control device to stop vehicle
paragraph: (a) a person driving or operating a vehicle, aircraft or boat;

heading: Sign or traffic control device to stop vehicle
paragraph: (b) a specified person.

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph:
95.3
		  (1) An officer must be wearing an officer's official uniform or displaying an officer's official identification for the purposes of enforcing an offence under this section.

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (2) A person commits an offence if, when signalled or requested by an officer under section 95 or 95.1, the person fails to stop.

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (3) A person commits an offence under section 95 if the person does any of the following:

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (a) being the driver or operator of a motor vehicle, in or on which there is wildlife or game fish or an article or device that may be used for hunting, trapping or fishing, fails, refuses or neglects to stop the motor vehicle when signalled or requested to stop by an officer;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (b) fails to identify themselves when requested to do so by an officer;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (c) refuses to give information respecting hunting, trapping or fishing, when requested to do so by an officer;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (d) fails to give information relating to the person's use of any of the following in water-based activities, when requested to do so by an officer:

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (i)  a vehicle;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (ii)  an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iii)  a boat;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iv)  any water-related equipment;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (e) fails to give information relating to an exposure to water of any of the following, when requested to do so by an officer:

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (i)  a vehicle;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (ii)  an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iii)  a boat;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iv)  any water-related equipment;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (f) fails to provide a record or information specified in section 95 (4) (c), when requested to do so by an officer.

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (4) A person commits an offence under section 95.1 if the person does any of the following:

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (a) fails to allow an officer to inspect any of the following:

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (i)  a vehicle;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (ii)  an aircraft designed to land on water;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iii)  a boat;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iv)  any water-related equipment;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (b) fails to facilitate access for an officer for the purposes of an inspection;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (c) fails to allow an officer to take samples of water, aquatic invasive species or suspected aquatic invasive species;

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (d) fails to allow an officer to take photographs of

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (i)  a vehicle,

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (ii)  an aircraft designed to land on water,

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iii)  a boat,

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (iv)  any water-related equipment, or

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (v)  water, aquatic invasive species or suspected aquatic invasive species that are in or on a vehicle, aircraft, boat or equipment referred to in subparagraphs (i) to (iv);

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (e) fails to allow an officer to make copies of relevant records.

heading: Offences under sections 95, 95.1 and 95.2
paragraph: (5) A person, including a specified person, commits an offence if the person fails to stop as indicated on a sign or traffic control device posted or erected under section 95.2.

heading: Obstructing officers
paragraph:
96
		  (1) A person who resists or obstructs an officer from exercising his or her duty under this Act commits an offence.

heading: Obstructing officers
paragraph: (2) An officer is, for the purposes of this Act, a peace officer.

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph:
97
		  (1) In this section, "authorization" means a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization issued under this Act.

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (5), a person who is required to hold an authorization must, on the request of an officer,

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (a) state the person's name and address,

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (b) produce prescribed photo identification, and

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (c) demonstrate in accordance with subsection (3) that the person holds the authorization.

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (3) A person may demonstrate that the person holds an authorization by

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (a) producing the authorization, or

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (b) unless the regulations require that the original authorization be produced,

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (i)  producing a legible copy of the authorization, or

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (ii)  if authorized by the regulations, stating a number assigned to the person by the director as an identification number for the person.

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (4) Subject to subsection (5), a person who would be required to hold a licence or permit issued under this Act were the person not exempt under section 11 (9) or 12 (b) must, on the request of an officer,

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (a) state the person's name and address, and

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (b) produce prescribed photo identification.

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (5) Subsections (2) (b) and (4) (b) do not apply to a person in a prescribed class of persons.

heading: Proof of identity and authorization
paragraph: (6) A person who contravenes subsection (2) or (4) commits an offence.

heading: Definitions
paragraph:
97.1
		  In sections 97.2 to 98.1:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "responsible official" has the same meaning as in section 24 (1) of the Offence Act;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife" includes a part of wildlife.

heading: If live wildlife seized
paragraph: 97.2		  Despite anything else in this Act, if live wildlife is seized under this Act, a conservation officer may dispose of the wildlife, or have the wildlife disposed of, by returning it to the natural environment if the conservation officer believes on reasonable grounds that the live wildlife is capable of surviving after release.

heading: If perishable wildlife seized
paragraph:
97.3
		  Despite anything else in this Act, if wildlife is seized under this Act and a conservation officer believes on reasonable grounds that the wildlife may rot, spoil or otherwise perish, the conservation officer may dispose of the wildlife, or have the wildlife disposed of, as the minister directs.

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph:
97.4
		  (1) Subject to sections 97.2 and 97.3, wildlife seized under this Act may be detained by the responsible official for no longer than 12 months from the day of seizure unless

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (a) a trial, inquiry or hearing under this Act is instituted before the end of that period and the wildlife may be required in that trial, inquiry or hearing,

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (b) an order authorizing the continued detention is made on application under subsection (2), or

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (c) section 97.6 applies.

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (2) On application by the responsible official on at least 3 days' notice to the person from whom the wildlife was seized, a Provincial Court judge may order the continued detention of the wildlife for a specified period, subject to any conditions the judge considers appropriate, if satisfied that

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (a) the continued detention might reasonably be required for the purpose of an investigation, trial, inquiry or hearing under this Act, and

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (b) it is in the interests of justice to make the order.

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (3) If an application under subsection (2) has been made but is not yet decided, the period authorized for detention of the wildlife extends until the application is decided.

heading: Detention of seized wildlife
paragraph: (4) A person aggrieved by an order under this section may appeal the order to the Supreme Court and, for the purposes of the appeal, sections 103 to 114 of the Offence Act apply.

heading: Access to wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: 97.5		  (1) On at least 3 days' notice to the minister, a person may apply to a Provincial Court judge for an order under subsection (2) that the person be permitted to examine wildlife detained under section 97.4.

heading: Access to wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (2) The judge may make an order that the applicant or a representative of the applicant be permitted to examine the wildlife, but must make the order on terms that the judge considers necessary or desirable to ensure that the wildlife is safeguarded and preserved for any purpose for which it may subsequently be required.

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph:
97.6
		  (1) This section applies in respect of wildlife detained under section 97.4 if a responsible official determines that the wildlife is not required for law enforcement purposes and gives notice of that determination to the person from whom the wildlife was seized.

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (2) The person from whom the wildlife was seized may make an application to a justice on at least 3 days' notice to the minister.

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (3) An application under subsection (2) must be made within 30 days from the date that the person receives notice referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (4) On the hearing of an application under subsection (2), the justice must order that the wildlife be returned

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (a) to the person from whom it was seized, if satisfied that the person is lawfully entitled to the wildlife,

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (b) to another person, if

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (i)  satisfied that the person from whom the wildlife was seized is not lawfully entitled to the wildlife but that the other person is, and

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (ii)  this other person is known, or

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (c) if neither paragraph (a) nor (b) apply, to the government to be disposed of as the minister directs.

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (5) A person aggrieved by an order under this section may appeal the order to the Supreme Court and, for the purposes of the appeal, sections 103 to 114 of the Offence Act apply.

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (6) Despite anything in this section, wildlife must not be returned or disposed of under this section until the later of the following:

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (a) 30 days after an order under subsection (4);

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (b) if the order under subsection (4) is appealed, 30 days after the decision on the appeal has been given.

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (7) If

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (a) a person does not make an application within the time limit under subsection (3), or

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: (b) wildlife is ordered returned to a person under subsection (4) (a) or (b) and the person does not, within 60 days of that order, take possession of that wildlife,

heading: Disposition of wildlife seized and detained as evidence
paragraph: the wildlife is returned to the government or forfeited to the government, as the case may be, to be disposed of as the minister directs.

heading: Seizure or destruction of controlled alien species
paragraph: 97.7		  (1) A conservation officer or constable may seize a species individual of a controlled alien species if the person in possession of the species individual

heading: Seizure or destruction of controlled alien species
paragraph: (a) is prohibited from possessing that species individual,

heading: Seizure or destruction of controlled alien species
paragraph: (b) contravenes the person's permit in relation to the species individual, or

heading: Seizure or destruction of controlled alien species
paragraph: (c) contravenes a regulation respecting controlled alien species.

heading: Seizure or destruction of controlled alien species
paragraph: (2) A conservation officer or constable may seize or destroy a species individual of a controlled alien species if, in the opinion of the conservation officer or constable, the species individual presents an imminent danger to the health or safety of a person or to property, wildlife or wildlife habitat.

heading: Seizure or destruction of controlled alien species
paragraph: (3) If a constable seizes a species individual under subsection (1) or (2), the constable must, as soon as practicable, deliver the species individual to a conservation officer or to a person designated by the minister.

heading: Seizure or destruction of controlled alien species
paragraph: (4) Sections 23 to 24.2 of the Offence Act do not apply in respect of a species individual of a controlled alien species seized under this Act.

heading: Disposition of seized controlled alien species
paragraph: 97.71		  (1) If a species individual of a controlled alien species is seized under section 97.7 (1) or (2), the government may destroy, sell or otherwise dispose of the species individual 14 days after the regional manager or a person designated by the minister has given notice to the owner of the species individual.

heading: Controlled alien species is property of new owner
paragraph:
97.72
		  If a species individual of a controlled alien species is sold or otherwise disposed of under section 97.71, all rights and interests in the species individual

heading: Controlled alien species is property of new owner
paragraph: (a) vest in the person to whom it has been sold or otherwise disposed of, and

heading: Controlled alien species is property of new owner
paragraph: (b) the former owner ceases to have any of those rights and interests.

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph:
97.73
		  (1) If a species individual of a controlled alien species is seized or destroyed under this Act, the director may

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (a) issue a certificate

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (i)  setting out the reasonable costs incurred under this Act by the government with respect to the species individual,

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (ii)  identifying one or more persons who own the species individual, and

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (iii)  specifying all or part of those costs as payable by one or more of the persons identified in the certificate, and

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (b) by serving notice of the certificate on a person identified in it, require the person to pay all or part of the costs as specified in the certificate.

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (3) If 2 or more persons are identified in a certificate, those persons are jointly and separately liable to pay the costs as specified in the certificate.

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (4) If notice of a certificate is served under subsection (1) (b),

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (a) the amount certified as being payable by a person is a debt due to the government by the person, and

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (b) on filing in the Supreme Court, the certificate has the same effect and is subject to the same proceedings as a judgment of the court for the recovery of a debt in the amount stated in the certificate against the person named in it.

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (5) The government may require the owner to pay the costs that the owner is required to pay under subsection (1) before returning the species individual to the owner.

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (6) Subject to subsection (7), the government may retain the proceeds of a sale or other disposition of a species individual of a controlled alien species under section 97.71.

heading: Costs and proceeds of disposition of controlled alien species
paragraph: (7) If the proceeds of a sale or other disposition of a species individual of a controlled alien species exceed the costs referred to in subsection (1), the owner of the species individual that was seized may, within 6 months of the date of seizure, claim the balance from the government.

heading: Disposition of other property seized
paragraph:
98
		   If property, other than wildlife, that is seized in relation to an offence under this Act or the Firearm Act is ordered returned to a person under section 24.2 (4) (a) or (b) of the Offence Act and the person does not, within 6 months after receiving notice from the responsible official of that order, remove the property from the place specified in the notice, the property is forfeited to the government, to be disposed of as the minister directs.

heading: Detention of other property seized until fine paid
paragraph: 98.1		  (1) This section applies if

heading: Detention of other property seized until fine paid
paragraph: (a) a person is convicted of an offence under this Act or the Firearm Act,

heading: Detention of other property seized until fine paid
paragraph: (b) property, other than wildlife, is ordered returned to that person under section 24.2 (4) (a) or (b) of the Offence Act, and

heading: Detention of other property seized until fine paid
paragraph: (c) a fine is imposed on the person by the court.

heading: Detention of other property seized until fine paid
paragraph: (2) Despite the order under section 24.2 (4) (a) or (b) of the Offence Act, the responsible official must deliver the property referred to in subsection (1) (b) of this section to the minister and the minister may detain the property until the fine is paid.

heading: Detention of other property seized until fine paid
paragraph: (3) If the fine is not paid within the time for payment set by the court, the property is forfeited to the government, to be disposed of as the minister directs.

heading: Detention of other property seized until fine paid
paragraph: (4) Proceeds of a disposition under subsection (3) must be applied towards payment of the fine referred to in subsection (1) (c).

heading: Powers of director
paragraph:
100
		  (1) In addition to other powers given under this Act, the director may do an act or thing that a regional manager is empowered to do.

heading: Powers of director
paragraph: (2) If the regional manager is satisfied that special circumstances exist, the regional manager may,

heading: Powers of director
paragraph: (a) if an applicant for an assistant angling guide licence or the registration of a trapline meets all the requirements except the age of eligibility, issue or authorize the issue of the licence or the registration of the trapline to the applicant, and

heading: Powers of director
paragraph: (b) if an applicant for a guide outfitter licence meets all the requirements of section 51 (1) except a requirement prescribed for the purposes of this section, issue or authorize the issue of a guide outfitter licence to the applicant.

heading: Submission of reports and other records
paragraph:
100.1
		  Subject to the regulations, a report or other record required to be submitted under this Act, other than Part 3, must be submitted in a manner and form, if any, specified by the director.

heading: Indigenous knowledge
paragraph:
100.2
		  For certainty, in making a decision under this Act, the director, the assistant director and a regional manager must consider relevant Indigenous knowledge provided to the director, assistant director or regional manager, as applicable.

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph:
100.3
		  (1) Any Indigenous knowledge of a first nation that is provided in confidence by the first nation to a person engaged in the administration of this Act may be

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) used only for the purposes for which the Indigenous knowledge is provided, and

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) disclosed only as authorized under subsection (2).

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (2) Indigenous knowledge referred to in subsection (1) may be disclosed as follows:

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) with the written consent of the governing body of the first nation;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) if the Indigenous knowledge is publicly available;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (c) to a person engaged in the administration of this Act if the Indigenous knowledge is necessary for the performance of that person's duties as they relate to the purpose for which the Indigenous knowledge was provided;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (d) to the Attorney General or legal counsel for the government for the purposes of obtaining legal advice;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (e) by order of the court;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (f) by order of the appeal board in accordance with section 34 (3) of the Administrative Tribunals Act;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (g) by a person who has authority under this Act to make a decision if

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (i)  the decision relates to a matter under this Act for which the Indigenous knowledge was provided, and

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (ii)  the person considers that the disclosure is necessary for the purposes of procedural fairness;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (h) in prescribed circumstances.

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (3) Before disclosing Indigenous knowledge under any of the following provisions, a person must give written notice of the contemplated disclosure to the governing body of the first nation that provided the knowledge:

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) subsection (2) (e), (f) or (g);

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) if required by regulation, subsection (2) (h).

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (4) The following persons may impose conditions on the further disclosure of Indigenous knowledge by the person to whom it is disclosed under subsection (2):

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (a) a justice, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (e);

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (b) the appeal board, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (f);

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (c) the person referred to in subsection (2) (g), if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under that provision;

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (d) a prescribed person, if the Indigenous knowledge is disclosed under subsection (2) (h).

heading: Confidentiality of Indigenous knowledge
paragraph: (5) If the holder of a licence, certificate or registration referred to in section 61 (1) or an assistant guide contravenes a condition imposed under subsection (4) of this section, a regional manager may take action under section 61.

heading: Reasons for and notice of decisions
paragraph: 101		  (1) The regional manager or the director, as applicable, must give written reasons for a decision that affects

heading: Reasons for and notice of decisions
paragraph: (a) a licence, permit, registration of a trapline or guiding territory certificate held by a person, or

heading: Reasons for and notice of decisions
paragraph: (b) an application by a person for anything referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Reasons for and notice of decisions
paragraph: (1.1) The regional manager must give written reasons for a decision made under section 61 (1.1) (a) or (b).

heading: Reasons for and notice of decisions
paragraph: (2) Notice of a decision referred to in subsection (1) or (1.1) must be given to the affected person.

heading: Reasons for and notice of decisions
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of applying this section to a decision that affects a guiding territory certificate, if notice of a decision referred to in subsection (1) is given in accordance with this section to the agent identified in the guiding territory certificate, the notice is deemed to have been given to the holders of the guiding territory certificate as if the agent were an affected person.

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph:
101.1
		  (1) The affected person referred to in section 101 (2) may appeal the decision to the Environmental Appeal Board continued under the Environmental Management Act.

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (2) The time limit for commencing an appeal is 30 days after notice is given

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (a) to the affected person under section 101 (2), or

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (b) in accordance with the regulations.

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (3) Subject to this Act, Division 1 of Part 8 of the Environmental Management Act applies to an appeal under this Act.

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (4) The appeal board may conduct an appeal by way of a new hearing.

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (5) On an appeal, the appeal board may

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (a) send the matter back to the regional manager or director, with directions,

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (b) confirm, reverse or vary the decision being appealed, or

heading: Appeals to Environmental Appeal Board
paragraph: (c) make any decision that the person whose decision is appealed could have made, and that the board considers appropriate in the circumstances.

heading: Commercial vendors of licences
paragraph: 102		  Despite the Financial Administration Act, the Lieutenant Governor in Council may

heading: Commercial vendors of licences
paragraph: (a) authorize a commercial vendor of licences to retain a prescribed fee or commission for issuing licences, and

heading: Commercial vendors of licences
paragraph: (b) prescribe a different fee or commission for different licences.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: 103		  (1) The time limit for laying an information in respect of an offence under this Act is

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (a) 3 years after the date that the facts on which the information is based arose, or
