heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) if the minister completes a certificate described in subsection (2), 18 months after the date that facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the minister.

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (2) A document purporting to have been issued by the minister, certifying the date that the facts on which the information is based first came to the knowledge of the minister,

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (a) is admissible without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed the certificate, and

heading: Time limit for prosecuting offence
paragraph: (b) is proof of the certified matters.

heading: Liability for offence by employee
paragraph:
104
		  (1) In a prosecution of a person for an offence under this Act, if it is proved that the offence was committed by an employee or agent of the person, whether or not the employee or agent is identified or has been prosecuted for the offence, the person is a party to the offence and is liable to the penalties prescribed for the offence as a principal offender unless the person establishes that the offence was committed without his or her knowledge or consent or that he or she exercised all due diligence to prevent its commission.

heading: Liability for offence by employee
paragraph: (2) Nothing in this section relieves the person who actually committed the offence from liability for it.

heading: Liability of employee, agent, etc.
paragraph:
104.1
		  (1) If a corporation commits an offence under this Act, an employee, officer, director or agent of the corporation who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the commission of the offence also commits that offence.

heading: Liability of employee, agent, etc.
paragraph: (2) If an individual who holds an interest in a guiding territory certificate commits an offence under this Act, an employee or agent of the individual who authorized, permitted or acquiesced in the commission of the offence also commits that offence.

heading: Liability of employee, agent, etc.
paragraph: (3) Subsections (1) and (2) apply whether or not the corporation or the individual who holds an interest in the certificate, as applicable, is prosecuted for the offence.

heading: Proof of citizenship or residence
paragraph:
105
		  In a prosecution for an offence under this Act, if it is alleged that the defendant was not a Canadian citizen or a resident, the onus is on the defendant to prove that he or she was a Canadian citizen or a resident at the time of the offence.

heading: Wildlife hunted or fish taken in British Columbia
paragraph:
106
		  In a prosecution under this Act, wildlife or fish found in British Columbia is presumed, unless the contrary is proved, to have been hunted or taken in British Columbia.

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph:
107
		  (1) In a proceeding under this Act in which proof is required with regard to

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (a) the issue, non renewal, suspension or cancellation of or the suspension of the right to obtain a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization,

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (b) the person who is the licensee or permittee named in a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization,

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (c) the appointment or authority of an officer, or

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (d) the delivery, service, mailing or giving of a notice or document by an official of the government,

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: a certificate signed by a regional manager certifying as to a matter referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d) is admissible and is proof of the facts stated in the certificate and of the authority of the regional manager without further proof of his or her appointment or signature.

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (2) In a proceeding under this Act, a certificate signed by a regional manager stating that wildlife or fish

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (a) has been examined by a person qualified to judge and classify wildlife or fish, and

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (b) is of a certain species or sex or is in a certain condition

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: is proof of the facts stated in the certificate and of the authority of the regional manager without further proof of his or her appointment or signature.

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (3) The fact that the person charged in an information laid in respect of an offence under this Act has the same name as the person who is referred to as being the holder of a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization in a certificate issued under subsection (1) (b) is proof that the person charged in the information is the holder of the licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization.

heading: Certificate evidence and presumptions
paragraph: (4) In a proceeding under this Act, a certificate relating to the analysis of a thing or a sample, signed by a person who is in charge of a laboratory operated, maintained, supported or certified by the government of Canada, a province, the United States of America or a state of it, is proof of the facts stated in the certificate and of the authority of the person signing the certificate without further proof of his or her appointment or signature.

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph:
108
		  (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations referred to in section 41 of the Interpretation Act.

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (a) respecting threatened species or endangered species;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (b) respecting the use and occupation of a wildlife management area;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (b.1) respecting identification numbers that may be assigned to persons by the director, including, without limitation,

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i)  establishing classes of identification numbers,

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (ii)  for the purposes of section 97 (3) (b) (ii), prescribing authorizations for which an identification number may be stated,

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (iii)  authorizing the director to issue identification cards, and

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (iv)  making different regulations for different classes of identification numbers;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (c) respecting applications for licences, permits and limited entry hunting authorizations, specifying conditions of eligibility for them including proof of financial responsibility or insurance for third party liability and discriminating among classes of applicants for them whether or not the classes are specified in this Act;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (c.1) prescribing the manner, form and content of written authorizations issued under section 48 (1.2), which may be different for different people, events, areas or circumstances;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (c.2) prescribing the circumstances that, if changed, require a new written authorization to be issued under section 48 (1.2);

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (c.3) prescribing the documentation that an assistant guide who is guiding for game must carry and the manner, form and content of that documentation, which may be different for different types of documentation;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (d) prescribing conditions of eligibility including proof of financial responsibility or insurance for third party liability for different classes of licence applicants and for different licences, permits and limited entry hunting authorizations;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (e) prescribing the conditions of a licence and conditions that the director or a regional manager may attach to a licence when he or she issues it to a person;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (f) limiting the number and types of licences and limited entry hunting authorizations that may be held by a person;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (f.1) requiring that the original copy of a licence, permit or limited entry hunting authorization issued in paper form be produced for the purposes of section 97 (3) (b);

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (g) prescribing surcharges, royalties and fees, including fees for applications, licences, permits, limited entry hunting authorizations and identification cards and for the transfer of a trapline registration, and establishing different surcharges or fees for different classes including, without limitation, classes based on the following:

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i)  age;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (ii)  residence;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (iii)  the nature of the activity;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (iv)  the manner of collection of the surcharge or fee;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (v)  the person entitled to collect the surcharge or fee;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (vi)  in the case of a licence, permit, limited entry hunting authorization or identification card, the manner in which it is provided to the applicant;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (h) prohibiting or regulating the trafficking or possession in British Columbia of wildlife or fish or parts of either;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i) prescribing exceptions to requirements for guides and for guides for fish, defining classes of and prescribing qualifications of guides and guides for fish, prescribing rules and conditions that a regional manager may attach to a guide outfitter licence, angling guide licence or assistant angling guide licence and prescribing penalties, including the prohibition of a person from guiding or guiding for fish, for contravention of this Act or the regulations;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i.2) prescribing qualifications that a person must meet to guide for game as an assistant guide, including, without limitation, requiring that the person

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i)  pass an examination approved or established by the director, and

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (ii)  pay any fees approved by the director for the examination;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i.3) prescribing requirements that a person must meet to guide for game as an assistant guide;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i.4) respecting the records guide outfitters are required to create or maintain with respect to assistant guides who are guiding for game;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i.5) prescribing the period of time the records referred to in paragraph (i.4) must be kept, which may be different for different types of records;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (j) providing for the disposal of guide areas to licensed guide outfitters;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (k) exempting persons or classes of persons from the application of provisions of this Act or the regulations;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (l) prescribing bag limits for wildlife by species, type, sex, age, circumstances or physical features of the wildlife and by periods of time;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (l.01) in respect of a regulation under paragraph (l), requiring that wildlife taken or killed by a person be included in the bag limit of another person;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (l.1) prescribing, by species, type, sex, age or physical features of the wildlife, the maximum number of wildlife that a person may possess and respecting the circumstances in which a person may possess a prescribed number of wildlife;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (l.2) respecting the circumstances in which a person may take, kill or possess wildlife;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (m) constituting a portion of British Columbia as a wildlife unit, area, district or region with a distinctive name or number;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (n) designating no shooting areas;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (o) regulating or prohibiting the types and calibres of firearms or types of projectiles that may be discharged in a prescribed area;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (p) providing for cancellation or suspension of, periods of ineligibility for and periods of suspension of licences for specified offences or combinations of offences, and specifying what is a second or subsequent offence;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (q) specifying lakes, streams or areas of British Columbia for the purpose of requiring a member of a class of persons to hold a licence issued under section 53 (1) (f) to engage in angling in that lake, stream or area;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (r) respecting how notice of a decision may be given for the purposes of section 101.1 (2) (b);

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (r.1) respecting the manner in which a notice under this Act may or must be given and when a notice given in a specified manner, whether actually received or not, must be considered to have been received;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (s) prohibiting or regulating methods and devices for hunting, trapping, capturing or taking wildlife and respecting safety in those activities;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (t) requiring specified parts to be left attached to a wildlife carcass;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (u) providing for the reporting and recording

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i)  by taxidermists, tanners, meatcutters and operators of cold storage plants of wildlife or fish processed or prepared by them or in their possession, and

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (ii)  by holders of licences, permits and limited entry hunting authorizations of any matters or activities relating to their licences, permits or authorizations,

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: and prescribing exceptions to reporting requirements;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (v) requiring wildlife, whether alive or dead, or a part of wildlife to be permanently marked or tagged;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (w) prohibiting or regulating the keeping of wildlife in captivity, and specifying the conditions under which wildlife may be released from captivity;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (x) requiring that a person who captures or kills wildlife take that wildlife or a part of it to a place and report to a member of the staff of the ministry or a person specified by the Lieutenant Governor in Council;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (y) prohibiting or regulating field trials of hunting and gun dogs;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (z) prohibiting or regulating the causing or allowing of a dog to hunt or pursue wildlife.

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsection (1), the Lieutenant Governor in Council may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (a) controlling the transportation in British Columbia of wildlife or fish or parts of either;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (b) defining methods and devices for trapping and the conditions under which and areas in which trapping may be carried on by a licensed trapper;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (e) prescribing open seasons or closed seasons, or both, for

paragraph: (i)  wildlife by species, type, sex, age, circumstances or physical features of the wildlife, or

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i) respecting the information and undertakings to be included in fur management plans and requirements for the renewal and amendment of fur management plans;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (j) prescribing licences, permits or stamps that, in addition to an angling licence, must be held to angle for or to catch and retain a designated species of fish or to angle in a designated area of British Columbia;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (k) prescribing tags that must be attached in the prescribed manner to fish caught by angling;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (l) prescribing an offence under a specified provision of this Act, or a regulation under this Act, as an offence for the purposes of

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i)  section 84 (1) (a) (ii),

paragraph: (ii)  section 84 (1) (b) (ii), or

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (iii)  section 84.3 (2);

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (m) prescribing a species of wildlife as dangerous wildlife;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (n) for any purpose contemplated by this Act;

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (o) prohibiting or regulating in relation to

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (i)  hunting by a person who is under 18 years of age or who holds an initiation hunting licence, and

heading: Regulations by Lieutenant Governor in Council
paragraph: (ii)  persons in the company of a person referred to in subparagraph (i) while he or she hunts,

paragraph: (4) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may delegate a power under subsection (2) or (3) to the minister.

paragraph: (5) The Lieutenant Governor in Council, despite anything in this Act, may make regulations respecting the issue of permits.

heading: Regulations by the minister
paragraph: 109		  (1) The minister may make regulations as follows:

heading: Regulations by the minister
paragraph: (a) designating employees of the government, by name or by their positions, as officers;

heading: Regulations by the minister
paragraph: (b) prohibiting, restricting or allowing access by members of the public to designated areas of British Columbia, for the purposes of wildlife management;

heading: Regulations by the minister
paragraph: (c) with the approval of the minister responsible for the highway or road, for the temporary closure of or for the imposition of restrictions on vehicular access to a highway or road, or part of either, for the purpose of protecting wildlife;

heading: Regulations by the minister
paragraph: (d) providing, for a regulation made by the minister, that its contravention constitutes an offence;

heading: Regulations by the minister

heading: Transition - assistant guide licences
paragraph: 110.1		  (1) On the date this section comes into force, all assistant guide licences are deemed to expire.

heading: Transition - assistant guide licences
paragraph: (2) If, on the date immediately before the date this section comes into force, an assistant guide licence is subject to a suspension or a refusal to issue or renew, the person who held the assistant guide licence is prohibited from guiding as an assistant guide for a period of time that ends on the date the suspension or refusal to issue or renew would have ended.

heading: Transition - assistant guide licences
paragraph: (3) If, on the date immediately before the date this section comes into force, an assistant guide licence is subject to a condition or restriction imposed under this Act, any written authorization issued under section 48 (1.2) to the person who held the assistant guide licence is deemed to be subject to the same condition or restriction as the assistant guide licence, for the same period of time as would have applied to the assistant guide licence.

heading: Transition - assistant guide licences
paragraph: (4) If, on the date immediately before the date this section comes into force, a person is subject to an order of the court prohibiting the person from obtaining an assistant guide licence, the person is prohibited from guiding as an assistant guide for the same period of time the person would have been prohibited from obtaining an assistant guide licence.

heading: Definitions

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) for private land subject to the woodlot licence where a woodlot licence holder harvests timber without authorization, the date the timber harvesting begins;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "cutblock" means an area within which a woodlot licence holder is authorized to harvest timber, as identified in a cutting permit;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "free growing date" means the date, measured from the commencement date, by which a free growing stand must be established on an area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "harvesting of bark beetle infested timber" means harvesting timber that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is infested with larvae or adult bark beetles,

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) has been recently killed by bark beetles, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) must be removed incidentally to facilitate the removal of timber described in paragraphs (a) and (b);

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "intermediate cuttings" means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) the harvesting of timber if

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (i)  the harvesting takes place before the final harvest or regeneration cut, and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (ii)  the majority of the pre-harvest stand volume is not removed, or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) the harvesting of bark beetle infested timber by harvesting scattered trees, small clumps of trees or for access trails required to harvest the timber;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "net area to be reforested" means, for the purpose of section 29 (3) [free growing stands] of the Act, the portion of a cutblock in which harvesting has occurred that is not occupied by permanent access structures;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "regeneration date" means the date, measured from the commencement date, by which a stand being established on the net area to be reforested must conform to the requirements of section 35 (1) [conforming to stocking standards];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian class" means the riparian class of a stream, wetland or lake as determined under Division 3 [Riparian areas] of Part 3 [Practice requirements];

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian management zone" means an area described under Division 3 [Riparian areas] of Part 3 [Practice requirements] that is established to protect the riparian reserve zone;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "riparian reserve zone" means an area described under Division 3 [Riparian areas] of Part 3 [Practice requirements] that is established to conserve riparian values within the area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "sensitive soil" means an area with one or both of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a slope of greater than 60%;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) indicators of potential slope instability;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "single tree selection" means a silvicultural system in which age classes are created or maintained by the removal, uniformly throughout the stand, of individual trees of all size classes;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "soil disturbance" means an area within a cutblock that is occupied by one or more of the following:

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) an unrehabilitated temporary access structure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) gouges, ruts or scalps that are outside of a temporary access structure;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) a compacted area;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "wildlife tree retention area" means an area for retention of wildlife trees specified in a woodlot licence plan;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: "woodlot licence holder" means a person who holds a woodlot licence issued under the Forest Act.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: 2		  (1) Subject to section 82 [government assumption of obligations], this regulation applies only to a woodlot licence holder, and the holder's employee, agent, contractor or subcontractor, who is carrying out an activity on or in relation to

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the area for which the woodlot licence has been issued, or

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (b) an area identified in a road permit that provides access to the area referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (2) This regulation does not apply to a person who is authorized to carry out a forest practice that is

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (a) funded under a vote as defined in section 1 [definitions] of the Financial Administration Act, and

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (b) administered under the Forest Investment Account, under the Financial Administration Act.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (3) Unless this regulation specifically provides otherwise, the Forest Planning and Practices Regulation, except for section 1.2, does not apply to a person referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (4)  Division 6 [General] of Part 3 [Practice requirements] and section 41 [lakeshore management zones] do not apply to any forest practice carried out on an area that is subject to a cutting permit or road permit that was in effect on the date the feature, objective, site, trail or measure under that Division or section was identified or established.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (5) Subject to subsection (6), the following sections do not apply to private land in a woodlot licence area that is subject to a woodlot licence issued before June 15, 1995:

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (a) the sections referred to in subsection (4);

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (b)  section 52 [wildlife tree retention];

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (c)  section 54 [coarse woody debris].

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (6) If the management plan for a woodlot licence issued before June 15, 1995 contains commitments respecting the subject matter described in subsection (5), the provision of this regulation that applies to that subject matter applies to the private land.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (7) A reference to distance in respect to riparian management zones and riparian reserve zones, and in Division 4 [Watersheds] of Part 3 [Practice requirements], is a reference to the slope distance.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (8) A power or duty of a minister under this regulation must be exercised in accordance with section 86 [process respecting orders and exemptions], including where reference is made to an order of a minister.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (9) A person is exempt from

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (a) a requirement of Parts 3 and 4 of this regulation, or

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (b) an obligation under section 29, 47 or 48 of the Act

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: as necessary to allow the person to conform to the Workers Compensation Act and the regulations under that Act.

heading: Application and interpretation
paragraph: (10) Until June 1, 2005, this regulation and the standards and objectives made under it apply immediately, despite section 16 (2) of the Act, to a woodlot licence plan.

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: 3		  (1) For the purpose of section 46 (1) and (1.1) [protection of the environment] of the Act, "damage" means any of the following that adversely alters an ecosystem:

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (a) a landslide;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (b) a gully process on the Coast;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (c) a fan destabilization on the Coast;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (d) soil disturbance;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (e) the deposit into a stream, wetland or lake of

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (i)  a petroleum product,

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (ii)  a fluid used to service industrial equipment, or

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (iii)  any other similar harmful substance;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (f) a debris torrent that enters a fish stream;

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (g) changes to soil.

heading: Damage to the environment
paragraph: (2) A person who is carrying out fire control or suppression in accordance with an enactment is exempt from section 46 of the Act.

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph:
4
		  (1) This regulation is a prescribed enactment for the purposes of section 52 (1) (e) (ii) of the Act.

heading: Authorization to cut
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder may cut, damage or destroy Crown timber as necessary for the purpose of carrying out silviculture treatments, stand tending treatments or forest health treatments.

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph:
5
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder is exempt from the requirement under section 12 [woodlot licence plan required] of the Act to prepare a woodlot licence plan if timber harvesting or road construction is

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) limited to a purpose described in section 4 (1) [exemption from forest stewardship plans] of the Act, or

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) authorized under another enactment, or is ancillary to the carrying out of an activity that is authorized under another enactment.

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (2) The minister may exempt a woodlot licence holder from the requirement under section 12 of the Act to prepare a woodlot licence plan if the minister is satisfied that timber harvesting or road construction is consistent with the objectives set by government.

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of section 12 (3) of the Act, the minister may authorize a woodlot licence holder to obtain a cutting permit, a road permit, or both, to enable the holder to harvest timber

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) damaged by natural causes, or

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) to address conditions created by persons other than the woodlot licence holder.

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (4)  Section 17 [review and comment] does not apply to a woodlot licence holder who

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) is exempt under subsection (1),

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) has been exempted under subsection (2), or

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (c) has been authorized under subsection (3).

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (5) The minister may, by written notice, require a woodlot licence holder to

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) publish a notice in a newspaper, in a form acceptable to the minister,

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) provide a copy of a map describing the nature and extent of the proposed harvesting or road construction to any persons specified by the minister, and

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (c) after a period of at least 5 days from the date of publication under paragraph (a), submit to the minister

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (i)  a copy of any written comments received in respect of the notice and map described in paragraphs (a) and (b), and

heading: Exemptions from woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (ii)  any changes to the proposed timber harvesting or road construction the woodlot licence holder intends to make as a result of the written comments.

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph:
6
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder who prepares a woodlot licence plan is exempt from the requirement of a 10 year term under section 14 (1) (a) [term of woodlot licence plan] of the Act, if

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) the remaining term of the woodlot licence is less than 10 years, or

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) the minister is satisfied that the woodlot licence holder cannot reasonably plan for a period of 10 years due to reasons beyond the control of the holder.

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (2) Despite the expiry of a woodlot licence plan, a woodlot licence holder must

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) establish a free growing stand on a cutblock in accordance with the plan as if it had not expired, and

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) otherwise act in accordance with the plan as if it had not expired, if the holder

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (i)  is issued a cutting permit or a road permit before the expiry, and

heading: Term of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (ii)  harvests timber from an area under the permit.

heading: Woodlot licence plan area
paragraph:
7
		  A woodlot licence holder must ensure that the holder's woodlot licence plan addresses the entire woodlot licence area, unless the minister is satisfied that a smaller area is sufficient because no timber harvesting or road construction will take place on the area not being addressed.

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph:
8
		  (1) Unless exempted under subsection (2), a woodlot licence holder must include in the holder's woodlot licence plan, for the area required to be addressed in the plan under section 7 [woodlot licence plan area], information and maps that describe or identify the following:

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (a) the forest cover;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (b) topography;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (c) the location and riparian class of streams, wetlands and lakes shown on government-endorsed

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (i)  forest cover maps,

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (ii)  terrain resource inventory maps, and

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (iii)  fish and fish habitat inventory maps;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (d) any of the streams identified in paragraph (c) that are fish streams;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (e) the biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification of the area, to the subzone level;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (f) public utilities on Crown land including

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (i)  transmission lines,

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (ii)  gas and oil pipelines, and

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (iii)  railways;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (g) resource management zones, landscape units and sensitive areas that are continued or established under the Land Act;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (h) wildlife habitat areas;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (i) scenic areas;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (j) ungulate winter ranges;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (k) community watersheds or fisheries sensitive watersheds;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (l) community and domestic water supply intakes that are licensed under the Water Sustainability Act and any related water supply infrastructures;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (m) contiguous areas of sensitive soils;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (n) existing roads;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (o) temporary or permanent barricades to restrict vehicle access;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (p) private property within or adjacent to the woodlot licence area;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (q) resource features other than wildlife habitat features, archaeological sites, and domestic water supply intakes licensed under the Water Sustainability Act.

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (2) The minister may exempt a woodlot licence holder from subsection (1) (b), (e) or (h).

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder must describe in the holder's woodlot licence plan areas where timber harvesting will be avoided or modified during the term of the plan for the following reasons:

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (a) to protect resource features;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (b) to address the interests of private property owners or aboriginal peoples;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (c) to manage resource values including specifying retention of trees in riparian management zones;

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (d) to address areas described in subsection (1) (g) to (k).

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (4) If a stream, wetland or lake was not identified or was incorrectly classified in subsection (1) (c), the riparian reserve zone and riparian management area have widths as determined under Division 3 [Riparian areas] of Part 3 [Practice requirements].

heading: Mapping and information
paragraph: (5) If a biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification was not identified or was incorrectly classified in subsection (1) (e), the biological ecosystem classification is as described in the Ministry of Forests' publication, Biogeoclimatic Ecosystem Classification Codes and Names, as amended from time to time.

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: 9		  (1) For the purpose of section 13 (1) (b) (i) [content of woodlot licence plan] of the Act, the objectives set by government are as follows:

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (a) maintaining or enhancing an economically valuable supply of commercial timber from the woodlot licence area;

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (b) conserving the productivity and the hydrologic function of soils;

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (c) conserving within riparian areas, at the landscape level, water quality, fish habitat, wildlife habitat and biodiversity;

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (d) conserving and protecting cultural heritage resources that are

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (i)  the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people that is of continuing importance to that people, and

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (ii)  not regulated under the Heritage Conservation Act;

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (e) subject to section 52 (1) [wildlife tree retention], any land use objective.

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of section 13 (1) (b) (ii) of the Act, the following objectives apply:

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (a) any fisheries sensitive watershed objective or water quality objective established for a watershed within which the woodlot licence area is located;

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (b) subject to subsection (3), conserving sufficient wildlife habitat in terms of amount of area and distribution of areas, and attributes of those areas for

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (i)  the winter survival of specified ungulate species,

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (ii)  the survival of a species at risk, and

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (iii)  the survival of a species of regionally important wildlife.

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder required to prepare a woodlot licence plan must act in a manner consistent with the objective stated under subsection (2) (b) only if the minister responsible for the Wildlife Act notifies the holder of the applicable

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (a) species referred to in subsection (2) (b), and

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (b) indicators of the amount, distribution and attributes of necessary wildlife habitat described in subsection (2) (b).

heading: Established objectives
paragraph: (4) On or after December 31, 2004, a notice described in subsection (3) must be given at least 4 months before the woodlot licence plan is submitted for approval.

heading: Results or strategies not required
paragraph: 10		  For the purpose of section 13 (1) (b) [content of woodlot licence plan] of the Act, a woodlot licence holder is not required to specify a result or strategy in relation to the following:

heading: Results or strategies not required
paragraph: (a) any objective listed in section 9 (1) or (2) [established objectives], except that described in section 9 (1) (d);

heading: Results or strategies not required
paragraph: (b) an objective for an interpretive forest site, recreation site or recreation trail;

heading: Results or strategies not required
paragraph: (c) a wildlife habitat area objective;

heading: Results or strategies not required
paragraph: (d) an ungulate winter range objective;

heading: Results or strategies not required
paragraph: (e) a lakeshore management zone objective;

heading: Results or strategies not required
paragraph: (f) a visual quality objective.

heading: Wildlife tree retention strategy required
paragraph:
11
		  For the purpose of section 52 (2) [wildlife tree retention], a woodlot licence holder must specify in the holder's woodlot licence plan a wildlife tree retention strategy that describes

heading: Wildlife tree retention strategy required
paragraph: (a) generally, the species and characteristics of individual wildlife trees,

heading: Wildlife tree retention strategy required
paragraph: (b) generally, the forest cover attributes of wildlife tree retention areas,

heading: Wildlife tree retention strategy required
paragraph: (c) the conditions under which individual wildlife trees may be removed,

heading: Wildlife tree retention strategy required
paragraph: (d) the conditions under which trees may be removed from within a wildlife tree retention area, and

heading: Wildlife tree retention strategy required
paragraph: (e) how trees removed under subparagraphs (c) and (d) will be replaced.

heading: Stocking information for specified areas
paragraph:
12
		  A woodlot licence holder must specify in the holder's woodlot licence plan stocking standards for areas referred to in section 34 (3) [free growing stands].

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph:
13
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder may propose in a woodlot licence plan an alternative performance requirement that specifies in relation to the plan

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (a) an amount of soil disturbance for the purposes of section 24 (1) (a),

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (b) an area for occupation by permanent access structures for the purposes of sections 25 (1) (a), (2) (a) or (3) (a),

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (c) the stocking standards, regeneration date and free growing date for the purposes of section 35 (1) (a),

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (d) the minimum riparian management area width, riparian reserve zone width and riparian management zone width for the purposes of one or more of section 36 (4) (a), 37 (3) (a) or 38 (2) (a),

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (e) the circumstances in which cutting, modification or removal of trees may occur in a riparian reserve zone for the purposes of section 39 (1),

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (f) the circumstances in which road construction may occur in a riparian management zone for the purposes of section 40 (1) (a),

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (g) the proportion of the woodlot licence area that may consist of wildlife tree retention areas for the purposes of section 52 (1) (b),

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (h) the quantity of logs to be retained for the purposes of section 54 (1) (a), and

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (i) the measures that relate to resource features for the purposes of section 56 (1) (a).

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (2) In proposing an alternative performance requirement under subsection (1), a woodlot licence holder must

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (a) specify in the holder's woodlot licence plan the provision to which the alternative performance requirement relates,

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (b) specify in the holder's woodlot licence plan the location to which the alternative performance requirement is applicable, and

heading: Alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (c) submit to the minister a rationale for how the alternative performance requirement is consistent with the criteria described in section 9, if any, to which the alternative performance requirement relates.

heading: Invasive plants
paragraph:
14
		  For the purpose of section 47 [invasive plants] of the Act, a woodlot licence holder must, subject to section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemption], specify measures in the holder's woodlot licence plan to prevent the introduction or spread of species of plants prescribed in the Invasive Plants Regulation, if the introduction or spread is likely to be the result of the holder's forest practices.

heading: Natural range barriers
paragraph:
15
		  For the purpose of section 48 [natural range barriers] of the Act, a woodlot licence holder must, subject to section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], specify measures in the holder's woodlot licence plan to mitigate the effect of removing or rendering ineffective natural range barriers.

heading: Signature
paragraph:
16
		  Despite section 13 (4) [content of woodlot licence plan] of the Act, a woodlot licence plan may be signed by a person who is authorized by the woodlot licence holder to sign the plan on behalf of the holder.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph:
17
		  (1) For the purpose of section 18 [review and comment] of the Act, before submitting a woodlot licence plan for approval, a woodlot licence holder must

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (a) publish a notice in a newspaper, in a form acceptable to the minister, and

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (b) if required by the minister, refer a copy of the plan, or a portion of the plan, to

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (i)  any agency of government,

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (ii)  any agency of the Government of Canada, or

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (iii)  a person specified by the minister.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (2) In respect to an amendment for which an approval is required under section 15 [amendments to a woodlot licence plan] or 16 [approval of woodlot licence plan or amendment] of the Act, the minister may exempt a woodlot licence holder from the requirement to publish a notice under subsection (1) (a) if the minister is satisfied that the proposed amendment will not affect others in a material way.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder who publishes a notice or refers a copy of the plan under subsection (1) must provide opportunity for review and comment to persons interested or affected by operations under the plan for a period of

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (a) if the plan is to address an emergency, at least 5 days from the first date of publication,

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (b) if the minister determines that a period of more than 30 days is required to provide adequate opportunity for review, the time specified by the minister, or

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (c) in any other case, 30 days from the first date of publication.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (3.1) A woodlot licence holder who publishes a notice or refers a copy of the plan under subsection (1) must, for the period referred to in subsection (3), make reasonable efforts to meet with first nation groups affected by the plan to discuss the plan or amendment.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (4) A woodlot licence holder must review all written comments in respect of the holder's plan received during the period of review specified under subsection (3), and make any revisions to the plan that the holder considers appropriate.

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (5) A woodlot licence holder who submits a woodlot licence plan to the minister for approval must submit with the plan

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (a) a copy of the notice published under subsection (1) (a),

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (b) a copy of each written comment received during the period of review specified in subsection (3),

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (c) a description of any changes made to the plan as a result of the comments received, and

heading: Review and comment
paragraph: (d) a description of the efforts made to comply with the requirements of subsection (3.1).

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph:
18
		  (1) If, in preparing an alternative performance requirement under section 13 [alternative performance requirements] or stocking standards under section 12 [stocking information for specified areas], a woodlot licence holder satisfies the minister that the holder took into consideration only those factors contained in Schedule 1, the minister must not require the holder to consider other factors.

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (2) The minister may request information under section 16 (2.1) [approval of woodlot licence plan or amendment] of the Act in respect of an alternative performance requirement or stocking standard if the information is

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) relevant to the factors in Schedule 1 that were addressed, if any,

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) relevant to any factor that the holder addressed that is not a factor listed in Schedule 1, and

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (c) either available to the holder or in the control or possession of the holder.

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (3) The minister must approve an alternative performance requirement in respect of regeneration date, free growing date and stocking standards, and a stocking standard described under section 12 [stocking information for specified areas], if the minister is satisfied that the alternative performance requirement or stocking standard will result in the area being stocked with or retaining, as applicable, ecologically suitable species that address immediate and long-term forest health issues on the area, to a density or to a basal area that, in either case, is consistent with

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a)  section 9 (1) (a) [established objectives], and

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) the timber supply projections and forest management assumptions that apply to the area covered by the plan on the date that the plan is submitted for approval.

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (4) The minister must not refuse to approve an alternative performance requirement solely on the basis that performance of the alternative performance requirement

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (a) would result in an outcome that is outside of the range of natural variation that is characteristic of a season, an area or a forest resource,

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (b) would cause or contribute to an adverse impact on a forest resource, if that impact would be consistent with the objectives described in section 8 [mapping and information],

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (c) proposes an innovative means of meeting the intent of the requirement to which the alternative performance requirement relates, or

heading: Minister's consideration of woodlot licence plan
paragraph: (d) is based on a factor other than one specified in Schedule 1.

heading: Emergency approval
paragraph:
19
		  For the purpose of section 17 of the Act, the prescribed circumstances in relation to a woodlot licence plan are those described in that section.

heading: Minor amendments that require approval
paragraph:
20
		  For the purpose of section 20 (1) [minor amendments] of the Act, an amendment to a woodlot licence plan requires the approval of the minister if the amendment would add or vary an alternative performance requirement.

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph:
21
		  (1) For the purpose of section 20 (1) (b) [minor amendments] of the Act, a proposed amendment to a woodlot licence plan does not require approval of the minister if the proposed amendment is in respect to

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (a) correcting a mapping or non-substantive data entry referred to in section 8 [mapping and information], that will not

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (i)  decrease the area where harvesting will be avoided or constrained, or

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (ii)  increase the adverse impact on forest resources,

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (b) the reclassification of a stream, wetland or lake, or

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (c) the wildlife tree retention strategy prepared under section 11 [wildlife tree retention strategy required], that will not decrease the nature or quality of wildlife trees or wildlife tree retention areas.

heading: Minor amendments that do not require approval
paragraph: (2) An amendment that does not require the approval of the minister takes effect when it is signed in accordance with section 13 (4) [content of woodlot licence plan] of the Act or section 16 [signature].

heading: Minor amendments wrongly made
paragraph:
22
		  (1) Under section 20 (3) [minor amendments] of the Act, if the minister determines that a decision made by a woodlot licence holder under section 20 (1) of the Act was wrongly made, the minister may

heading: Minor amendments wrongly made
paragraph: (a) declare the amendment to be without effect, and

heading: Minor amendments wrongly made
paragraph: (b) if the minister considers it appropriate, require the holder to suspend operations that are not authorized in the absence of the amendment.

heading: Minor amendments wrongly made
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder referred to in subsection (1) will not be found to have contravened the Act or this regulation by carrying out, before the minister makes a determination under subsection (1), operations that are not authorized in the absence of the amendment if

heading: Minor amendments wrongly made
paragraph: (a) the minister is satisfied, or

heading: Minor amendments wrongly made
paragraph: (b) the holder establishes that the holder had reason to believe

heading: Minor amendments wrongly made
paragraph: that the amendment would have been approved under section 16 (1.1) [approval of woodlot licence or amendment] of the Act, had the amendment been properly submitted for approval.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph:
23
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder who knows or ought reasonably to know that performing the operations specified in a woodlot licence plan will not achieve the results specified in the plan or the requirements of this regulation

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) must submit to the minister an amendment to the plan, and

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) must not carry out any operation that would be materially affected by the amendment submitted under paragraph (a) until the amendment has been approved.

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (2) If the requirements of the woodlot licence plan cannot be met as a result of the woodlot licence holder carrying out, or failing to carry out, a forest practice on the area covered by the plan, or the occurrence of a natural event, the holder must

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (a) notify the minister, and

heading: Mandatory amendments
paragraph: (b) if an amendment to the plan is required, not carry out any operation that would be materially affected by the proposed amendment until the amendment has been approved.

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph:
24
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder must not cause the amount of soil disturbance on the net area to be reforested to exceed

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) the amount specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) 8%, if there is no amount specified in paragraph (a).

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder must not cause soil disturbance on any portion of the net area to be reforested to be concentrated in a manner that would be inconsistent with the objective set out in section 9 (1) (b) [established objectives].

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder may exceed the limit set out in subsection (1), if

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (a) the holder is removing infected stumps or salvaging windthrow, and

heading: Soil disturbance limits
paragraph: (b) the additional disturbance is the minimum necessary.

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph:
25
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder must ensure that the maximum amount of the total area within a cutblock that is 5 ha or greater in size that is occupied by permanent access structures is

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (a) the amount specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (b) 7%, if there is no amount specified in paragraph (a).

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder must ensure that the maximum amount of the total area within a cutblock that is less than 5 ha in size that is occupied by permanent access structures is

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (a) the amount specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (b) 10%, if there is no amount specified in paragraph (a).

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (3) Without limiting subsections (1) and (2), a woodlot licence holder must ensure that the maximum amount of the woodlot licence area that is occupied by permanent access structures is

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (a) the amount specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Permanent access structure limits
paragraph: (b) 7%, if there is no amount specified in paragraph (a).

heading: Landslides
paragraph:
26
		  A woodlot licence holder who carries out a primary forest activity must ensure that the primary forest activity does not cause a landslide that has a material adverse effect on a matter referred to in section 149 (1) [objectives set by government] of the Act.

heading: Gully processes
paragraph:
27
		  A woodlot licence holder who carries out a primary forest activity on the Coast must ensure that the primary forest activity does not cause a gully process that has a material adverse effect on a matter referred to in section 149 (1) [objectives set by government] of the Act.

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph:
28
		  (1) If a woodlot licence holder constructs a temporary access structure or a permanent access structure on an area, the holder must maintain natural surface drainage patterns on the area both during and after construction.

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), if it is not practicable for a woodlot licence holder to maintain natural surface drainage patterns during the construction of a temporary access structure or permanent access structure, the holder must ensure the altered surface drainage pattern is compatible with the original natural surface drainage pattern by the earlier of

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (a) the end of the construction, and

heading: Natural surface drainage patterns
paragraph: (b) the next freshet.

heading: Revegetation
paragraph:
29
		  A woodlot licence holder who constructs or deactivates a road must ensure that soil exposed by the construction or deactivation is revegetated within two years after the construction or deactivation is completed if it is reasonably foreseeable that

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (a) the erosion of the soil would cause

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (i)  sediment to enter a stream, wetland or lake, or

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (ii)  a material adverse effect on a matter referred to in section 149 (1) [objectives set by government] of the Act, and

heading: Revegetation
paragraph: (b) revegetation would materially reduce the likelihood of erosion.

heading: Modification of insect behaviour
paragraph:
30
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who uses trap trees or pheromones to concentrate insect populations must ensure that the insect brood is destroyed before the insects emerge.

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph:
31
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], if a woodlot licence holder who is required to establish a free growing stand uses livestock for site preparation or brush control, the woodlot licence holder must ensure that all necessary measures are taken to

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph: (a) control the location and movement of the livestock to minimize conflict with wildlife that could prey on the livestock,

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph: (b) prevent the transmission of disease from the livestock to wildlife, and

heading: Use of livestock
paragraph: (c) maintain the health of the livestock.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph:
32
		  (1) In this section, "transfer" means the process by which seed is selected and used, based on the origin of the seed and its genetic suitability for the site on which trees grown from the seed are to be planted.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (2) The chief forester may make standards for matters referred to in section 169 (1) (a) (i) to (v) [chief forester standards for forest practices] of the Act if the chief forester considers such standards to be necessary or appropriate for the purpose of regulating the use, registration, storage, selection or transfer of seed to be used in the establishment of free growing stands.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (3) The chief forester may authorize a person to exercise a discretion of the chief forester described in subsection (5), (6) or (7).

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (4) Unless an alternative is approved under subsection (6), a woodlot licence holder who plants trees while establishing a free growing stand must use only seed registered, stored, selected and transferred in accordance with the standards, if any, established by the chief forester.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (5) A woodlot licence holder referred to in subsection (4) may submit to the chief forester for approval an alternative to any standard established by the chief forester under subsection (2).

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (6) The chief forester may approve an alternative submitted under subsection (5) if the chief forester considers that the alternative is consistent with achieving the intent of the standard.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (7) If the chief forester approves an alternative submitted under subsection (5), the woodlot licence holder who submitted the alternative

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (a) is exempt from the requirement of subsection (4) for which the alternative has been approved, and

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (b) must comply with the alternative.

heading: Use of seed
paragraph: (8) A woodlot licence holder who is required to establish a free growing stand must keep a record of the registration numbers of the seed that is used, if any, and a map of the location where the trees grown from the seed are planted.

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph:
33
		  (1) The chief forester may establish standards for the purpose of this section.

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph: (2) Before a woodlot licence holder harvests timber from an area where the holder is required to establish a free growing stand, the holder must prepare a map for the area according to the standards set under subsection (1), showing

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph: (a) the biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification, including the site series listed within that classification, for the area, and

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph: (b) the stocking standards that apply to the area.

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder must make the map referred to in subsection (2) available to the district manager, or a person authorized by the district manager, on request.

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph: (4) A woodlot licence holder must retain the map referred to in subsection (2) until the holder

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph: (a) has produced a free growing stand on the area, or

heading: Pre-harvest mapping
paragraph: (b) has been relieved under section 107 [limitation on liability of person to government] or 108 [government may fund extra expense or waive obligation] of the Act of the requirement to establish a free growing stand on the area.

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph:
34
		  (1) Unless exempted under subsection (2) or section 78 (2) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder must establish, in accordance with this Division, a free growing stand on

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (a) the net area to be reforested,

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (b) areas where timber was harvested by the holder in contravention of section 52 [unauthorized timber harvesting] of the Act,

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (c) private land subject to the woodlot licence where timber was harvested by the holder without authorization, and

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (d) areas where the minister requires the holder to establish a free growing stand when the holder is authorized to obtain a cutting permit under section 12 (3) [woodlot licence plan required] of the Act.

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder is exempt from the requirements of section 29 (3) [free growing stands] of the Act in respect of an area if timber harvesting is limited to one or more of the following:

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (a) harvesting timber to eliminate a safety hazard;

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (b) harvesting timber to facilitate the collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha;

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (c) removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way;

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (d) commercial thinning, removal of individual trees, or a similar type of intermediate cutting;

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (e) harvesting special forest products.

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder who harvests timber for the reasons referred to in subsection (2) (d) or (e) must ensure that, for a period of 12 months after completion of harvest, the area on which timber harvesting was carried out conforms to the stocking standards specified in section 12 [stocking information for specified areas] for the area.

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of the definition of "commencement date", the minister may give written authorization for a specified commencement date if

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (a) harvesting of bark beetle infested timber or timber damaged by wind occurs before harvesting the majority of the cutblock volume, or

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (b) all of the following apply:

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (i)  harvesting in areas that are in close proximity has taken place over one or more seasons;

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (ii)  the holder has proposed to amalgamate the areas into a single unit;

heading: Free growing stands
paragraph: (iii)  the minister is satisfied that the amalgamation will simplify future management of the areas.

heading: Conforming to stocking standards
paragraph:
35
		  (1) In subsection (2), the applicable stocking standards, regeneration date and free growing date are those specified for the applicable silvicultural system in

heading: Conforming to stocking standards
paragraph: (a) the woodlot licence holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Conforming to stocking standards
paragraph: (b) the Ministry of Forests' publication, Reference Guide for Forest Development Plan Stocking Standards, as amended from time to time, if the stocking standards, regeneration date or free growing date are not specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan.

heading: Conforming to stocking standards
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder who is required to establish a free growing stand on an area must,

heading: Conforming to stocking standards
paragraph: (a) by the applicable regeneration date, establish a stand that conforms to the stocking standards that relate to the biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification for the area, and

heading: Conforming to stocking standards
paragraph: (b) by the applicable free growing date, establish a free growing stand that conforms to the stocking standards that relate to the biogeoclimatic ecosystem classification for the area.

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph:
35.1
		  (1) Subject to section 108 of the Act, a woodlot licence holder who

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (a) is required to establish a free growing stand under section 34 of this regulation, and

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (b) knows that the requirements of sections 34 and 35 of this regulation cannot be met

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: must

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (c) give notice to the minister that the requirements to establish a free growing stand cannot be met, giving the reasons, and

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (d) submit to the minister a proposal for establishing a free growing stand on the area, including the stocking standards, the free growing height and the latest date by which the stocking standards and free growing height will be achieved.

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (2) The minister must approve a proposal submitted under subsection (1) if the minister considers that the proposal is consistent with section 18 (3).

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (3) The minister must give notice to the holder who submitted the proposal if the proposal has been approved or rejected and, if rejected, must provide written reasons.

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (4) A rejection under subsection (3) is reviewable as set out in sections 80 and 81 of the Act and those sections and sections 82 to 84 of the Act apply in respect of the review.

heading: Requirements if free growing stand cannot be established
paragraph: (5) A holder who is notified under subsection (3) that the proposal has been approved must ensure that a free growing stand is established that conforms to the approved proposal.

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph:
36
		  (1) In this section, "active flood plain" means the level area with alluvial soils, adjacent to streams, that is flooded by stream water on a periodic basis and is at the same elevation as areas showing evidence of

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (a) flood channels free of terrestrial vegetation,

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (b) rafted debris or fluvial sediments, recently deposited on the surface of the forest floor or suspended on trees or vegetation, or

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (c) recent scarring of trees by material moved by flood waters.

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (2) A stream that is a fish stream or is located in a community watershed has the following riparian class:

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (a) S1A, if the stream averages, over a one km length, either a stream width or an active flood plain width of 100 m or greater;

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (b) S1B, if the stream width is greater than 20 m but the stream does not have a riparian class of S1A;

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (c) S2, if the stream width is not less than 5 m and not more than 20 m;

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (d) S3, if the stream width is not less than 1.5 m but is less than 5 m;

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (e) S4, if the stream width is less than 1.5 m.

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (3) A stream that is not a fish stream and is located outside of a community watershed has the following riparian class:

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (a) S5, if the stream width is greater than 3 m;

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (b) S6, if the stream width is 3 m or less.

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (4) Unless subsection (5) or (6) applies, for each riparian class of stream, the minimum riparian management area width, riparian reserve zone width and riparian management zone width, on each side of the stream, are

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (a) as specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (b) if widths are not specified in a woodlot licence plan, as follows:

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (5) If the width of the active flood plain of a stream exceeds the specified width for the riparian management zone, the width of the riparian management zone extends to the outer edge of the active flood plain.

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (6) The minister may specify a riparian reserve zone for a stream with a riparian class of S1-A if the minister considers that a riparian reserve zone is required.

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (7) The riparian reserve zone for a stream begins at the edge of the stream channel bank and extends to the width specified in subsection (4) or (6).

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (8) The riparian management zone for a stream begins at

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (a) the outer edge of the riparian reserve zone, or

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: (b) if there is no riparian reserve zone, the edge of the stream channel bank,

heading: Stream riparian classes
paragraph: and extends out to the widths specified in subsection (4) or (5).

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph:
37
		  (1) Wetlands have the following riparian classes:

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (a) W1, if the wetland is greater than 5 ha in size;

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (b) W2, if the wetland is not less than 1 ha and not more than 5 ha in size and is in one of the following biogeoclimatic zones or subzones:

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (i)  Ponderosa Pine;

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (ii)  Bunch Grass;

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (iii)  Interior Douglas-fir, very dry hot, very dry warm or very dry mild;

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (iv)  Coastal Douglas-fir;

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (v)  Coastal Western Hemlock, very dry maritime, dry maritime or dry submaritime;

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (c) W3, if the wetland is not less than 1 ha and not more than 5 ha in size and is in a biogeoclimatic zone or subzone other than one referred to in paragraph (b);

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (d) W4, if the wetland is

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (i)  not less than 0.25 ha and not more than 1 ha in size and is in a biogeoclimatic zone or subzone referred to in paragraph (b) (i), (ii) or (iii), or

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (ii)  not less than 0.5 ha and not more than 1 ha in size and is in a biogeoclimatic zone or subzone referred to in paragraph (b) (iv) or (v).

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (2) Despite subsection (1), an area is to be treated as a single wetland with a riparian class of W5 if

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (a) the area contains

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (i)  two or more W1 wetlands located within 100 m of each other,

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (ii)  a W1 wetland and one or more W2, W3 or W4 wetlands, all of which are within 80 m of each other, or
