heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (iii)  two or more W2, W3 or W4 wetlands located within 60 m of each other, and

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (b) the combined size of the wetlands, excluding the upland areas, is 5 ha or larger.

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (3) Unless subsection (4) or (5) applies, for each riparian class of wetland, the minimum riparian management area width, riparian reserve zone width and riparian management zone width for the wetland are

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (a) as specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (b) if no widths are specified in a woodlot licence plan, as follows:

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (4) No riparian reserve zone or riparian management zone extends onto any enclosed upland areas of a W1 wetland if the wetland is

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (a) located in a boreal, subboreal or hyper-maritime climate, and

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (b) greater than 1 000 ha in size.

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (5) If the minister considers it necessary for a riparian reserve zone or riparian management zone to extend onto an enclosed upland area, the minister may require either or both of the following:

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (a) a riparian reserve zone of a width of 10 m or less;

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (b) a riparian management zone with a width of 40 m or less.

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (6) The riparian reserve zone for a wetland begins at the edge of the wetland and extends to the width described in subsection (3) or (5).

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (7) The riparian management zone for a wetland begins at

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (a) the outer edge of the riparian reserve zone, or

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: (b) if there is no riparian reserve zone, the edge of the wetland,

heading: Wetland riparian classes
paragraph: and extends to the width specified in subsection (3) or (5).

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph:
38
		  (1) Lakes have the following riparian classes:

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (a) L1-A, if the lake is 1 000 ha or greater in size;

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (b) L1-B, if

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (i)  the lake is greater than 5 ha but less than 1 000 ha in size, or

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (ii)  the minister designates the lake as L1-B;

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (c) L2, if the lake is not less than 1 ha and not greater than 5 ha in size and is in a biogeoclimatic zone or subzone that is

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (i)  Ponderosa Pine,

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (ii)  Bunch Grass,

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (iii)  Interior Douglas-fir, very dry hot, very dry warm or very dry mild,

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (iv)  Coastal Douglas-fir, or

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (v)  Coastal Western Hemlock, very dry maritime, dry maritime or dry submaritime;

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (d) L3, if the lake is not less than 1 ha and not more than 5 ha in size and is in a biogeoclimatic zone or subzone other than one referred to in paragraph (c);

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (e) L4, if the lake is

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (i)  not less than 0.25 ha and not more than 1 ha in size and is in a biogeoclimatic zone or subzone referred to in paragraph (c) (i), (ii) or (iii), or

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (ii)  not less than 0.5 ha and not more than 1 ha in size and is in a biogeoclimatic zone or subzone referred to in paragraph (c) (iv) or (v).

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (2) Unless subsection (3) applies, for each riparian class of lake, the minimum riparian management area width, riparian reserve zone width and riparian management zone width are

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (a) as specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (b) if no widths are specified in a woodlot licence plan, as follows:

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (3) If the minister considers it necessary, the minister may specify a riparian management area and a riparian reserve zone for a lake with a riparian class of L1-A.

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (4) The riparian reserve zone for a lake begins at the edge of the lake and extends to the width specified in subsection (2) or (3).

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (5) The riparian management zone for a lake begins at

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (a) the outer edge of the riparian reserve zone, or

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: (b) if there is no riparian reserve zone, the edge of the lake,

heading: Lake riparian classes
paragraph: and extends to the width specified in subsection (2) or (3).

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph:
39
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder must not cut, modify or remove trees in a riparian reserve zone, unless it has been specified in a woodlot licence plan or it is limited to one of the following purposes:

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (a) felling or modifying a tree that is a safety hazard, if there is no other practicable option for addressing the safety hazard;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (b) topping or pruning a tree that is not wind firm;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (c) constructing a stream crossing;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (d) creating a corridor for full suspension yarding;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (e) creating guyline tiebacks;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (f) carrying out a sanitation treatment;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (g) felling or modifying a tree that has been windthrown or has been damaged by fire, insects, disease or other causes, if the felling or modifying will not have a material adverse impact on the riparian reserve zone;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (h) felling or modifying a tree for the purpose of establishing or maintaining an interpretive forest site, recreation site, recreation facility or recreation trail.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder who fells, tops, prunes or modifies a tree under subsection (1) may remove the tree only if the removal will not have a material adverse affect on the riparian reserve zone.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (2.1) A woodlot licence holder must not construct a road in a riparian reserve zone in a cutblock unless the construction has been specified in a woodlot licence plan.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (3) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder must not carry out the following silviculture treatments in a riparian reserve zone:

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (a) grazing or broadcast herbicide applications for the purpose of brushing;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (b) mechanized site preparation or broadcast burning for the purpose of site preparation;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian reserve zone
paragraph: (c) spacing or thinning.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph:
40
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder must not construct a road in a riparian management zone in a cutblock, unless one of the following applies:

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (a) the construction of the road is provided for in the woodlot licence plan;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (b) locating the road outside the riparian management zone would create a higher risk of sediment delivery to the stream, wetland or lake to which the riparian management zone applies;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (c) there is no other practicable option for locating the road;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (d) the road is required as part of a stream crossing.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (2) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], if a road is constructed within a riparian management zone, a woodlot licence holder must not carry out road maintenance activities beyond the clearing width of the road, except as necessary to maintain a stream crossing.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (3) Unless exempted under section 78 (1), a woodlot licence holder who constructs, maintains or deactivates a road must not remove gravel or other fill from within a riparian management zone, unless

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (a) the gravel or fill is within a road prism,

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (b) the gravel or fill is at a stream crossing, or

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (c) there is no other practicable option.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (4) Unless exempted under section 78 (1), a woodlot licence holder who cuts, modifies or removes trees within a riparian management zone for an S4, S5 or S6 stream that has trees that contribute significantly to the maintenance of stream bank or channel stability, must retain enough trees adjacent to the stream to maintain the stream bank or channel stability, if the stream

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (a) is a direct tributary to an S1, S2 or S3 stream,

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (b) flows directly into the ocean, at a point near to or where one or more of the following is located:

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (i)  a herring spawning area;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (ii)  a shellfish bed;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (iii)  a saltwater marsh area;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (iv)  an aquaculture site;

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (v)  a juvenile salmonid rearing area or an adult salmon holding area, or

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (c) flows directly into the ocean at a point near to the location of an area referred to in paragraph (b) and failure to maintain stream bank or channel stability will have a material adverse impact on that area.

heading: Restrictions in a riparian management zone
paragraph: (5) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder must cut, modify or remove trees within a riparian management zone only as described in section 8 (3) [mapping and information].

heading: Lakeshore management zones
paragraph:
41
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], if a lakeshore management zone objective applies to Crown land in a woodlot licence area, a woodlot licence holder must carry out forest practices in the area only in a manner that is consistent with the lakeshore management zone objective.

heading: Temperature sensitive streams
paragraph:
42
		  Unless exempted under section 79 (1), a woodlot licence holder who fells, modifies or removes trees within a riparian reserve zone or riparian management zone adjacent to a temperature sensitive stream, or a stream that is a direct tributary to a temperature sensitive stream, must retain either or both of the following in an amount sufficient to prevent the temperature of the temperature sensitive stream from increasing to an extent that would have a material adverse impact on fish:

heading: Temperature sensitive streams
paragraph: (a) streamside trees whose crowns provide shade to the stream;

heading: Temperature sensitive streams
paragraph: (b) understory vegetation that provides shade to the stream.

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph:
43
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1), a woodlot licence holder who builds a stream crossing as part of a temporary access structure or permanent access structure must locate, build and use the crossing in a manner that

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph: (a) protects the stream channel and stream bank immediately above and below the stream crossing, and

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph: (b) mitigates disturbance to the stream channel and stream bank at the crossing.

heading: Stream crossings
paragraph: (2) Unless exempted under section 78 (1), a woodlot licence holder who builds a stream crossing as part of a temporary access structure must remove the crossing when it is no longer required by the holder.

heading: Fish passage
paragraph:
44
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who carries out a primary forest activity must ensure that the primary forest activity does not have a material adverse effect on fish passage in a fish stream.

heading: Fish passage
paragraph: (2) Unless exempted under section 78 (1), a woodlot licence holder who maintains a fish stream crossing built after June 15, 1995, must ensure that the crossing does not have a material adverse effect on fish passage.

heading: Fish passage
paragraph: (3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), a woodlot licence holder may temporarily have a material adverse effect on fish passage to construct, maintain or deactivate a road, including a stream crossing, if

heading: Fish passage
paragraph: (a) fish are not migrating or spawning, and

heading: Fish passage
paragraph: (b) the source of the material adverse effect is removed immediately on completion of the construction, maintenance or deactivation.

heading: Protection of fish and fish habitat
paragraph:
45
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who carries out a primary forest activity must conduct the primary forest activity at a time and in a manner that is unlikely to harm fish or destroy, damage or harmfully alter fish habitat.

heading: Use of livestock in riparian areas
paragraph:
46
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who uses livestock for site preparation or brush control for the purpose of carrying out a silviculture treatment must not do either of the following:

heading: Use of livestock in riparian areas
paragraph: (a) construct a livestock corral

heading: Use of livestock in riparian areas
paragraph: (i)  within a riparian management zone or riparian reserve zone,

heading: Use of livestock in riparian areas
paragraph: (ii)  on an area that drains directly into a fish stream or a fish-bearing wetland or lake, or

heading: Use of livestock in riparian areas
paragraph: (iii)  on an area within a community watershed that drains directly into a potable water source;

heading: Use of livestock in riparian areas
paragraph: (b) use the livestock within a riparian management zone or riparian reserve zone that is located within a community watershed.

heading: Protecting water quality
paragraph:
47
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who carries out a primary forest activity must ensure that the primary forest activity does not cause material that is harmful to human health to be deposited in, or transported to, water that is diverted for human consumption by a licensed waterworks.

heading: Licensed waterworks
paragraph:
48
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who carries out a primary forest activity must ensure that the primary forest activity does not damage a licensed waterworks.

heading: Licensed waterworks
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder must not harvest timber or construct a road within a community watershed if the timber harvesting or road construction is within a 100 m radius upslope of a licensed waterworks where the water is diverted for human consumption, unless the timber harvesting or road construction will not increase sediment delivery to the intake.

heading: Excavated or bladed trails
paragraph:
49
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1), a woodlot licence holder who

heading: Excavated or bladed trails
paragraph: (a) carries out timber harvesting, and

heading: Excavated or bladed trails
paragraph: (b) constructs an excavated or bladed trail in a community watershed,

heading: Excavated or bladed trails
paragraph: must ensure that doing so does not cause sediment delivery that would be harmful to human health to enter a stream, wetland or lake from which water is being diverted for human consumption by a licensed waterworks.

heading: Roads in a community watershed
paragraph:
50
		  (1) To prevent interference with the subsurface flow path of a drainage area that contributes to a spring that is a source of water for a licensed waterworks, the minister may

heading: Roads in a community watershed
paragraph: (a) identify a spring in a community watershed,

heading: Roads in a community watershed
paragraph: (b) specify a distance from the spring within which a person who constructs a road must not locate the road, and

heading: Roads in a community watershed
paragraph: (c) permit a person who constructs a road to locate the road closer to the spring than the distance specified under paragraph (b).

heading: Roads in a community watershed
paragraph: (2) If the minister does not specify a distance under subsection (1) (b), subject to an exemption granted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who constructs a road must not locate the road closer than a 100 m radius upslope of the spring identified under subsection (1) (a), unless the construction does not interfere with the subsurface flow path of a drainage area that contributes to the spring.

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph:
51
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who applies fertilizer within a community watershed for the purpose of carrying out a silviculture treatment must not apply fertilizer

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: (a) closer than a 100 m radius upslope of a licensed waterworks, or

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: (b) within 10 m of a perennial stream that is observable from an aircraft used to apply the fertilizer,

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: that results in

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: (c) if measured immediately below the area where the fertilizer is applied, nitrate nitrogen levels in the stream exceeding 10 parts per million, or

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: (d) chlorophyll levels in the stream exceeding

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: (i)  two micrograms per litre in a lake into which the stream drains, or

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: (ii)  50 milligrams per square metre in the stream.

heading: Use of fertilizers
paragraph: (2)  Subsection (1) does not apply if the use of fertilizer is restricted to spot applications.

heading: Wildlife tree retention
paragraph:
52
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder must ensure that the proportion of the woodlot licence area that is occupied by wildlife tree retention areas is no less than the least of the following:

heading: Wildlife tree retention
paragraph: (a) the proportion specified for the area in a land use objective;

heading: Wildlife tree retention
paragraph: (b) the proportion specified for the area in the holder's woodlot licence plan;

heading: Wildlife tree retention
paragraph: (c) 8% of the woodlot licence area.

heading: Wildlife tree retention
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder must not cut, damage or remove wildlife trees or trees within a wildlife tree retention area except in accordance with the wildlife tree retention strategy prepared under section 11 [wildlife tree retention strategy required].

heading: Restriction on harvesting
paragraph:
53
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder must not harvest timber in areas identified under section 8 (3) [mapping and information] as areas where harvesting will be avoided during the term of the woodlot licence plan.

heading: Restriction on harvesting
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder must harvest timber in areas described in section 8 (3) as areas where harvesting will be modified during the term of the woodlot licence plan in accordance with the modifications described in the plan.

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph:
54
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who is required to establish a free growing stand on an area must retain logs on the area consistent with

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph: (a) the amount specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, or

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph: (b) if no amount is specified in the woodlot licence plan,

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph: (i)  if the area is on the Coast, a minimum of 4 logs per hectare, each being a minimum of 5 m in length and 30 cm in diameter at one end, and

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph: (ii)  if the area is in the Interior, a minimum of 4 logs per hectare, each being a minimum of 2 m in length and 7.5 cm in diameter at one end.

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder is exempt from the requirements of subsection (1) if

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph: (a) the holder's agreement or an enactment requires the holder to act in a manner contrary to that set out in subsection (1), or

heading: Coarse woody debris
paragraph: (b) the holder carries out a controlled burn on the cutblock that is authorized under an enactment.

heading: General wildlife measures
paragraph:
55
		  Unless exempted under section 79 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], if a general wildlife measure is established for a woodlot licence area, a woodlot licence holder who carries out primary forest activities in the area must comply with each general wildlife measure that applies to the area.

heading: General ecological community measures
paragraph:
55.1
		  Unless exempted under section 79 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], if a general ecological community measure is established for a woodlot licence area, a woodlot licence holder who carries out primary forest activities in the area must comply with each general ecological community measure that applies to the area.

heading: Resource features and wildlife habitat features
paragraph:
56
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who carries out a forest practice that could affect a resource feature must

heading: Resource features and wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (a) carry out the measures specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan that relate to the resource feature, or

heading: Resource features and wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (b) if no measures are specified in the holder's woodlot licence plan, ensure that the forest practice does not damage or render ineffective a resource feature.

heading: Resource features and wildlife habitat features
paragraph: (2) Unless exempted under section 79 (2) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who carries out a forest practice that could affect a wildlife habitat feature must not damage or render ineffective the wildlife habitat feature.

heading: Fisheries sensitive watershed objectives
paragraph:
57
		  Unless exempted under section 79 (2) [minister may grant exemptions], if a fisheries sensitive watershed objective applies to a woodlot licence area, a woodlot licence holder must carry out primary forest activities in the area only in a manner that is consistent with the fisheries sensitive watershed objective.

heading: Protection of fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph:
57.1
		  (1) In this section, "fisheries sensitive watershed" means an area identified in Schedule 2

heading: Protection of fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (a) with significant downstream fisheries values continued under section 180 (f) of the Act and significant watershed sensitivity continued under section 180 (g) of the Act, and

heading: Protection of fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (b) for which there is no fisheries sensitive watershed objective.

heading: Protection of fish habitat in fisheries sensitive watersheds
paragraph: (2) Until December 31, 2005, the holder of a woodlot licence must ensure that the cumulative hydrological effects of primary forest activities in any part of a fisheries sensitive watershed that is in the woodlot licence area do not result in a material adverse impact on the habitat of the fish species for which the fisheries sensitive watershed was established.

heading: Water quality objectives
paragraph:
58
		  Unless exempted under section 79 (2) [minister may grant exemptions], if a water quality objective applies to a woodlot licence area, a woodlot licence holder must carry out primary forest activities in the area only in a manner that is consistent with the water quality objective.

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph:
58.1
		  (1) In this section, "community watershed" means a community watershed

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (a) that is continued under section 180 (e) of the Act, and

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (b) for which a water quality objective has not been

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (i)  continued under section 181 of the Act, or

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (ii)  established under the Government Actions Regulation.

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (2) If water is being diverted for human consumption through a licensed waterworks in a community watershed, the holder of a woodlot licence must ensure that the cumulative hydrological effects of primary forest activities within any part of the community watershed that is in the woodlot licence area do not result in

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (a) a material adverse effect on the quantity of water or the timing of the flow of the water from the licensed waterworks, or

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (b) the water from the licensed waterworks having a material adverse impact on human health that cannot be addressed by water treatment required under

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (i)  an enactment, or

heading: Safeguards for water through licensed waterworks in community watersheds
paragraph: (ii)  the licence pertaining to the waterworks.

heading: Visual quality objectives
paragraph:
59
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], if a visual quality objective applies to a woodlot licence area, a woodlot licence holder must carry out primary forest activities in the area only in a manner that is consistent with the visual quality objective.

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph:
59.1
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: "scenic area" means an area of land established as a scenic area under the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act on or before October 24, 2002 and continued as a scenic area under section 180 (c) of the Act;

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: "visual sensitivity class" means a visual sensitivity class established on or before October 24, 2002, particulars of which are publicly available in the Land and Resource Data Warehouse maintained by the minister responsible for the Land Act.

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (2) If a woodlot licence holder carries out a primary forest activity in a scenic area, that

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (a) on or before October 24, 2002 was established by the district manager, and

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (b) for which there is no visual quality objective

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: the holder must ensure that the primary forest activities in the area are consistent with an altered forest landscape for the scenic area that

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (c) in visual sensitivity class 1 is in either the preservation or retention category,

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (d) in visual sensitivity class 2 is in either the retention or partial retention category,

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (e) in visual sensitivity class 3 is in either the partial retention or modification category,

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (f) in visual sensitivity class 4 is in either the partial retention or modification category, and

heading: Objectives set by government for visual quality
paragraph: (g) in visual sensitivity class 5 is in either the modification or maximum modification category.

heading: Recreation objectives
paragraph: 60		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], if an objective for a recreation site, recreation trail or interpretive forest site applies to a woodlot licence area, a woodlot licence holder must carry out primary forest activities in the area only in a manner that is consistent with the objective.

heading: Roads and associated structures
paragraph:
61
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who constructs or maintains a road must ensure that the road and the bridges, culverts, fords and other structures associated with the road are structurally sound and safe for use by industrial users.

heading: Design of bridges
paragraph:
62
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who builds a bridge for the purpose of constructing or maintaining a road must ensure that the design and fabrication of the bridge

heading: Design of bridges
paragraph: (a) meets or exceeds standards applicable to roads at the time the design or fabrication is done, in respect of

heading: Design of bridges
paragraph: (i)  bridge design, established by the Canadian Standards Association, Canadian Highway Bridge Design Code, CAN/CSA-S6, and

heading: Design of bridges
paragraph: (ii)  soil properties, as they apply to bridge piers and abutments, established by the Canadian Foundation of Engineering Manual, and

heading: Design of bridges
paragraph: (b) takes into account the effect of logging trucks with unbalanced loads and off-centre driving.

heading: Peak flow
paragraph:
63
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder who builds a bridge across a stream or installs a culvert in a stream for the purpose of constructing or maintaining a road must ensure that the bridge or culvert is designed to pass the highest peak flow of the stream that can reasonably be expected within the return periods specified below for the length of time it is anticipated the bridge or culvert will remain on the site:

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder may build a bridge that will not conform to the requirements of subsection (1) if

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (a) the bridge will pass the flow that will occur during the period the bridge remains on the site,

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (b) the construction of the bridge occurs during a period of low flow, and

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (c) the bridge, or a component of the bridge that is vulnerable to damage by high flow, is removed before any period of high flow begins.

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder may install a culvert that will not conform to the requirements of subsection (1) if

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (a) the installation is temporary and the woodlot licence holder does not expect to subsequently install a replacement culvert at that location,

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (b) the stream in which the culvert is being installed is not a fish stream,

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (c) the culvert will pass the flow that will occur during the period the culvert remains on the site,

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (d) the installation of the culvert occurs during a period of low flow, and

heading: Peak flow
paragraph: (e) the culvert is removed before any period of high flow begins.

heading: Structural defects
paragraph:
64
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who builds a bridge for the purpose of constructing or maintaining a road must do one or more of the following if a structural defect or deficiency occurs:

heading: Structural defects
paragraph: (a) correct the defect or deficiency to the extent necessary to protect

heading: Structural defects
paragraph: (i)  industrial users of the bridge, and

heading: Structural defects
paragraph: (ii)  downstream property, improvements or forest resources that could be affected if the bridge fails;

heading: Structural defects
paragraph: (b) close, remove or replace the bridge;

heading: Structural defects
paragraph: (c) restrict traffic loads to a safe level;

heading: Structural defects
paragraph: (d) place a sign, on each bridge approach, stating the maximum load capacity of the bridge.

heading: Culvert fabrication
paragraph:
65
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who builds a culvert for the purpose of constructing or maintaining a road must fabricate all permanent culvert materials according to

heading: Culvert fabrication
paragraph: (a) culvert fabrication standards, as established by the Canadian Standards Association, Corrugated Steel Pipe Products, CSA G401 and Plastic Nonpressure Pipe Compendium, section B182.8 of the B1800 Series, that are applicable to roads at the time of the fabrication, or

heading: Culvert fabrication
paragraph: (b) standards that ensure at least the same strength and durability as the standards referred to in paragraph (a).

heading: Retaining information
paragraph:
66
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder who builds a bridge or major culvert for the purpose of constructing or maintaining a road must do all of the following:

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (a) prepare or obtain

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (i)  pile driving records,

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (ii)  for new materials used to build the bridge or major culvert, mill test certificates, in-plant steel fabrication drawings, and concrete test results,

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (iii)  soil compaction results, and

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (iv)  other relevant field and construction data;

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (b) prepare as-built drawings of the bridge or major culvert;

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (c) retain the information referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b) until the earlier of the date that

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (i)  the bridge or major culvert is removed, and

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (ii)  the holder is no longer required to maintain the road.

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), a woodlot licence holder responsible for maintaining a road must retain a copy of inspection records for a bridge or major culvert associated with the road for at least one year after the bridge or major culvert is removed from the site.

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (3) Unless the road has been deactivated, a woodlot licence holder must submit to the district manager the documents, drawings and records described in subsections (1) and (2) in respect of a road if the woodlot licence holder is no longer required to maintain the road because the district manager

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (a) cancels a road permit, road use permit or special use permit for a road, and

heading: Retaining information
paragraph: (b) does not require the road to be deactivated.

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph:
67
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who constructs or maintains a road must ensure clearing widths are of the minimum width necessary to accommodate the road, having regard to all of the following:

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (a) the safety of industrial users;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (b) the topography of the area;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (c) the drainage of water in the area;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (d) the stability of terrain in the area;

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (e) operational requirements, including

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (i)  the placement of pits, quarries, landings or waste areas,

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (ii)  the storage of bridge or culvert material,

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (iii)  the amount of area required to operate equipment within the clearing width, including equipment turnaround sites,

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (iv)  snow removal, and

heading: Clearing widths
paragraph: (v)  fencing and other ancillary structures.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph:
68
		  (1) Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder who is authorized to construct a road must maintain the road, including bridges, culverts, fords and other structures associated with the road, until

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (a) the road is deactivated,

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (b) the district manager notifies the woodlot licence holder that the road should not be deactivated due to use or potential use of the road by others,

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (c) a road permit or special use permit for the road is issued to another person, or

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (d) the road is declared a forest service road under the Forest Act.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (2) Subject to subsection (3), the government must maintain a forest service road, including bridges, culverts, fords and other structures associated with the road, until the road is deactivated.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (3) The district manager may order a woodlot licence holder who holds a road use permit that authorizes the use of a forest service road to assume all or part of the responsibility to maintain the road, including bridges, culverts, fords and other structures associated with the road.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (4) A woodlot licence holder who is the subject of an order referred to in subsection (3) must, in maintaining the road, comply with the provisions of this regulation respecting the maintenance of a road, including those provisions that refer to carrying out a primary forest activity.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (5) A woodlot licence holder required to maintain a road must ensure all of the following:

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (a) the structural integrity of the road prism and clearing width are protected;

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (b) the drainage systems of the road are functional;

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (c) the road can be used safely by industrial users.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (6) A woodlot licence holder required to maintain a forest service road under subsection (3), on giving the district manager at least 30 days notice, may do one or more of the following in respect of the forest service road:

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (a) build a bridge;

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (b) install a major culvert;

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (c) install a culvert in a fish stream.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (7) Within 30 days of receiving a notice referred to in subsection (6), the district manager may impose requirements respecting a bridge or culvert referred to in that subsection, and the holder of the road use permit must comply with those requirements.

heading: Road maintenance
paragraph: (8) If the district manager does not impose requirements under subsection (7), the woodlot licence holder may proceed in accordance with the notice given under subsection (6).

heading: Requirements where exempted
paragraph: 69		  For the purpose of section 22.1 (6) [industrial use of a road] of the Act, a woodlot licence holder exempted under section 22.1 (4) of the Act must comply with the provisions of this regulation respecting maintenance of a road, including those provisions that refer to carrying out a primary forest activity.

heading: Wilderness roads
paragraph:
70
		  Despite section 22.2 [non-industrial use of a road] of the Act and section 68 [road maintenance], if a woodlot licence holder is required to maintain a forest service road, or a road authorized under a road permit, a cutting permit or a woodlot licence, and the road is not being used by industrial users,

heading: Wilderness roads
paragraph: (a) section 68 (5) (a) and (b) apply to that road only to the extent necessary to ensure there is no material adverse effect on a forest resource, and

heading: Wilderness roads
paragraph: (b)  section 68 (5) (c) does not apply to that road.

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph:
71
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder who deactivates a road must do the following:

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (a) barricade the road surface width in a clearly visible manner to prevent access by motor vehicles, other than all-terrain vehicles;

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (b) remove bridge and log culvert superstructures and stream pipe culverts;

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (c) remove bridge and log culvert substructures, if the failure of these substructures would have a material adverse effect on downstream property, improvements or forest resources;

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (d) stabilize the road prism or the clearing width of the road if the stabilization is necessary to reduce the likelihood of a material adverse effect in relation to one or more of the subjects listed in section 149 (1) of the Act.

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder may submit to the district manager, in writing, a request for an exemption from the requirements of subsection (1) if

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (a) the woodlot licence holder has not begun deactivating the road, and

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (b) the road does not contain any bridges or major culverts.

heading: Road deactivation
paragraph: (3) The minister, in a notice given to a woodlot licence holder who submits a request under subsection (2), may exempt the holder if the minister is satisfied that the effectiveness of the works described in subsection (1) will not be negatively impacted by motor vehicle use.

heading: Hazard warning
paragraph:
72
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], a woodlot licence holder must at all times during a period that a road is being deactivated have a sign posted that will warn users of the deactivation.

heading: Notice - road in community watershed
paragraph:
73
		  Unless exempted under section 78 (1) [minister may grant exemptions], at least 48 hours before commencement of road construction or deactivation in a community watershed, a woodlot licence holder must notify affected water licensees or their representatives.

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph:
74
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder must notify the district manager before

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (a) beginning

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (i)  timber harvesting in a cutblock that comprises more than one hectare, or

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (ii)  construction of a road that is a permanent access structure, and

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (b) re-starting the activities described in paragraph (a) (i) and (ii) in a cutblock that comprises more than one hectare after an inactive period of 3 months or more.

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (2) A notice under subsection (1) must specify

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (a) the location of the timber harvesting or road, including any administrative identifier that relates to the location,

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (b) a contact name and contact information, and

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (c) the projected date for beginning timber harvesting or road construction.

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder is exempt from the requirements of subsection (1) if

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (a) the timber harvesting or road construction is necessary to reduce or remove a safety hazard,

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (b) the timber harvesting is limited to felling trap trees, or

heading: Notification of timber harvesting or road construction
paragraph: (c) the timber harvesting is limited to felling trees to facilitate the collection of seed, leaving an opening not greater than 1 ha.

heading: Surveys
paragraph:
75
		  (1) If required by the minister, a woodlot licence holder must carry out a survey of the nature and extent of

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (a) the total area of the cutblock that is occupied by permanent access structures, and

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (b) soil disturbance within the net area to be reforested.

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (2) If the minister reasonably believes that a woodlot licence holder has not met a requirement under section 35 [conforming to stocking standards] on an area, the minister may require the holder to carry out a survey to ascertain if the requirements have been met.

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder must carry out a survey for the net area to be reforested, on or before the free growing date, identifying all of the following:

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (a) the area for which the free growing stocking requirements have been met;

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (b) the number of healthy, well spaced free growing trees per hectare of preferred and acceptable species, as those species are described under section 35;

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (c) the number of healthy, well spaced free growing trees per hectare of the preferred species as those species are described under section 35;

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (d) for any areas for which the free growing stocking requirements have not been met, both the areas that are and are not satisfactorily stocked;

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (e) the forest cover inventory.

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (4) Despite subsection (3), the minister may exempt a woodlot licence holder from the requirement to carry out a free growing survey on an area if

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (a) the minister is satisfied that a free growing stand has been established on the area, and

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (b) the holder has provided the information referred to in subsection (3) (a) to (e) for that area.

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (5) A woodlot licence holder who has carried out intermediate cuttings must carry out a survey, between 1 and 3 years after the completion of harvesting on the area, that identifies

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (a) the area,

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (b) the forest cover inventory, and

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (c) damage to trees by insects, disease or other factors affecting forest health.

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (6) Despite subsection (5), the minister may exempt a woodlot licence holder from the requirement to carry out a survey on an area of intermediate cuttings if

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (a) the area is too small to warrant the survey, or

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (b) the extent of harvesting does not significantly change the inventory label.

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (7) A woodlot licence holder must

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (a) carry out other surveys and assessments according to the direction of the minister,

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (b) amend any survey or assessment prepared under this section, if required by the minister,

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (c) keep a record of each survey or assessment prepared under this section, and

heading: Surveys
paragraph: (d) provide a copy of the records under paragraph (c) to the minister when submitting the annual report for the year in which the survey or assessment was carried out, unless the minister requires the copy at a different time.

heading: Annual report
paragraph:
76
		  (1) In this section, "reporting period", in respect of an annual report required under subsection (2), means the 12-month period that begins on January 1 of the year immediately preceding the year in which the annual report must be submitted.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder must, on or before May 31 each year, submit to the minister, in accordance with the requirements of subsections (3) and (4), an annual report respecting activities completed within the reporting period.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder must, unless the information was previously provided to the minister, include with an annual report the following:

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (a) a copy of any amendment made under section 20 (1) of the Act during the reporting period;

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (b) the approximate location of any resource feature or wildlife habitat feature, in or contiguous to a cutblock or road, that the holder became aware of during the reporting period, if the order establishing the resource feature or wildlife habitat feature requires the location of the resource feature or wildlife habitat feature to be included in the annual report required under subsection (2);

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (c) any other information specified by the chief forester.

heading: Annual report
paragraph: (4) The information required under subsection (3) (c) to be included in an annual report must be provided in an electronic format or another format satisfactory to the chief forester.

heading: Limited exemption from compliance
paragraph:
77
		  A woodlot licence holder is exempt from the requirements of section 21 (1) [compliance with plans] of the Act to the extent that results cannot be achieved or strategies cannot be carried out due to the actions of a person who has been authorized to act by the government.

heading: Minister may grant exemptions
paragraph:
78
		  (1) If the minister is satisfied that it is not practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to a particular area, the minister may exempt a woodlot licence holder from

heading: Minister may grant exemptions
paragraph: (a) one or more of the following sections of the Act: 29; 29.1, or

heading: Minister may grant exemptions
paragraph: (b) one or more of the following sections of this regulation: 14; 15; 30; 31; 39 (3); 40 (2), (3) and (4); 41; 42; 43 to 52; 54; 56 (1); 59 to 62; 64; 65; 67; 68; 72 to 74.

heading: Minister may grant exemptions
paragraph: (2) The minister may exempt a woodlot licence holder from section 29 (3) of the Act and section 34 or 35 of this regulation, in relation to a specific area, if all of the following apply:

heading: Minister may grant exemptions
paragraph: (a) the timber to be harvested is in danger of being significantly reduced in value, lost or destroyed;

heading: Minister may grant exemptions
paragraph: (b) the volume will not exceed 500 m3;

heading: Minister may grant exemptions
paragraph: (c) the area, when taken together with adjoining areas, will not result in a clearcut exceeding 1 ha, unless the adjoining area is occupied by a free growing stand.

heading: Exemptions by minister responsible for Wildlife Act
paragraph:
79
		  (1) The minister responsible for the  Wildlife Act may exempt a person from section 55 of this regulation in relation to a general wildlife measure or section 55.1 of this regulation in relation to a general ecological community measure, if satisfied that

heading: Exemptions by minister responsible for Wildlife Act
paragraph: (a) the intent of the general wildlife measure or general ecological community measure will be achieved, or

heading: Exemptions by minister responsible for Wildlife Act
paragraph: (b) compliance with that provision is not practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to a particular area.

heading: Exemptions by minister responsible for Wildlife Act
paragraph: (2) The minister responsible for the Wildlife Act may exempt a person from section 56 (2), 57 or 58 of this regulation if satisfied that compliance with that provision is not practicable, given the circumstances or conditions applicable to a particular area.

heading: Payment of expenses
paragraph: 80		  (1) Expenses incurred by a woodlot licence holder in carrying out measures under sections 26 (9) [control of insects, disease, animals or abiotic factors], 27 (5) [forest health emergency] and 77.1 (4) [power of intervention: first nations] of the Act must be paid by the government, if the minister is satisfied that the expenses were reasonably incurred.

heading: Payment of expenses
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of section 77 (3) [power of intervention: general] of the Act, a woodlot licence holder may recover all or part of the amount reasonably incurred under that section if

heading: Payment of expenses
paragraph: (a) the minister specifies in a notice under section 87 (1) [intervention orders] that the amount reasonably incurred in taking the required measures or actions is recoverable, and

heading: Payment of expenses
paragraph: (b) the minister is satisfied that the amounts claimed by the holder were, in fact, reasonably incurred.

heading: Transfer of obligations
paragraph:
81
		  (1) For the purpose of section 29.1 (1) (b) or (3) (b) of the Act, a woodlot licence holder may transfer an obligation to establish a free growing stand if the minister is satisfied that the person to whom the obligation is to be transferred

heading: Transfer of obligations
paragraph: (a) is likely to meet the obligation, and

heading: Transfer of obligations
paragraph: (b) has provided security to the minister in a form and in an amount specified by the minister.

heading: Transfer of obligations
paragraph: (2) If the minister approves an agreement under section 29.1 (1) (c) or (3) (c) of the Act, the minister must return to the person who transferred the obligation any security deposit provided by that person specifically for that obligation.

heading: Transfer of obligations
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the stocking standards referred to in section 29.1 (5) of the Act are the stocking standards that were in effect for the transferred obligation immediately before the transfer became effective.

heading: Transfer of obligations
paragraph: (4) The minister may approve stocking standards other than those referred to in subsection (3) if satisfied that the stocking standards are consistent with section 26.

heading: Transfer of obligations
paragraph: (5) A person to whom an obligation is transferred under section 29.1 of the Act must comply with Part 3 and section 75 of this regulation.

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph:
82
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: "affiliate"  has the same meaning as "affiliate" in section 1 (1) of the Forest Act;

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: "associated with" means being associated with another person in a business activity whether by partnership, joint venture, contract or otherwise, and includes the contractual relationship between a licence holder and a person to whom the licence holder is contractually obliged to supply, directly or indirectly, some or all of the timber harvested under the licence holder's agreement.

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (2) For the purpose of section 30 (1) (d) [free growing stands for non-replaceable licences] of the Act, a "licence holder" means a person who

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (a) does not hold a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut of greater than 10 000 m3, and

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (b) unless the minister is satisfied that it is in the public interest that this paragraph not apply,

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (i)  does not hold shares of any type in a corporation that holds

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (A) a replaceable tree farm licence or forest licence, or

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (B) a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut greater than 10 000 m3,

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (ii)  is not affiliated with a corporation that holds shares of any type in

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (A) a replaceable tree farm licence or forest licence, or

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (B) a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut greater than 10 000 m3, and

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (iii)  is not associated with a holder of

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (A) a replaceable tree farm licence or forest licence, or

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (B) a replaceable timber sale licence that has an allowable annual cut greater than 10 000 m3.

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of section 30 (3) of the Act, the prescribed period for giving a notice under that section to a licence holder is one year.

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (4) For the purpose of section 30 (3) (d) of the Act, the following requirements must be met before a district manager may assume a licence holder's responsibility for establishing a free growing stand:

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (a) the licence holder requests that the district manager assume responsibility for establishing a free growing stand on all cutblocks that are harvested under the licence holder's agreement under the Forest Act, as and when the requirements referred to in section 30 (3) (a) to (c) of the Act are met in respect of those cutblocks;

heading: Government assumption of obligations
paragraph: (b) the request referred to in paragraph (a) is made by the licence holder as part of the licence holder's first application under the Forest Act for a cutting permit for the agreement.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: 83		  (1) For the purpose of section 108 (0.1) (a) (ii) [government may fund extra expense or waive obligation] of the Act, a woodlot licence holder must not be relieved from the requirements of section 26 [landslides], 27 [gully processes], 28 [natural surface drainage patterns] or 29 [revegetation], unless the minister is satisfied that

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (a) extraordinary circumstances exist which, due to their nature, would make it unjust if the woodlot licence holder were not relieved, and

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (b) granting the relief is in the public interest.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (1.1) For the purpose of section 108 (1) and (6) of the Act, "an event causing damage", in relation to an area in which a person has an obligation to establish a free growing stand, means

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (a) an occurrence of wildfire, or

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (c) another event that renders the area ill-suited for the establishment of a free growing stand.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (2) A woodlot licence holder who applies, under section 108 (0.1) (a) or (b) of the Act, for relief from an obligation referred to in that section must submit the following to the minister:

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (a) a description of

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (i)  the area to which the obligation relates, and

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (ii)  the area, within the area referred to in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, in which the damage has occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (b) a description of the extent to which the obligation had been met at the time the damage occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (c) the reasons the obligation cannot be met in the area referred to in paragraph (a) (ii) of this subsection without significant extra expense than would have been the case if the damage had not occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (d) the signature of the woodlot licence holder or of a person authorized to sign on behalf of the woodlot licence holder;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (e) the date on which the application is signed.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (2.1) A woodlot licence holder who applies for funding under section 108 (0.1) (b) of the Act must submit the following to the minister:

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (a) a description of

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (i)  the area to which the obligation referred to in section 108 (0.1) (b) of the Act relates, and

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (ii)  the area, within the area referred to in subparagraph (i) of this subsection, in which the damage has occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (b) a description of the extent to which the obligation had been met at the time the damage occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (c) a proposal for restoring the stand

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (i)  to the stage the stand had reached at the time the damage occurred, or

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (ii)  to the stage that is consistent with an agreement between the woodlot licence holder and the minister;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (d) an estimate of the expense to be incurred in implementing the proposal described in paragraph (c) of this subsection;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (e) the signature of the woodlot licence holder or of a person authorized to sign on the holder's behalf;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (f) the date on which the application is signed.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (2.2) An application under section 108 (0.1) of the Act must be submitted no later than 2 years after December 31 of the year in which the event causing damage began, unless an application submission plan is submitted under section 83.1 of this regulation.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (2.3) An application under section 108 (0.1) of the Act that relates to an event causing damage that began before the date this subsection comes into force must be submitted no later than 2 years after that date.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (2.4) A woodlot licence holder who applies, under section 108.3 (1) of the Act, for relief from an obligation referred to in that section must submit the following to the minister:

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (a) a description of

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (i)  the area to which the obligation relates, and

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (ii)  the area, within the area referred to in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph, in which the catastrophic damage has occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (b) a description of the extent to which the obligation had been met at the time the catastrophic damage occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (c) the reasons it is not practicable for the woodlot licence holder to fulfill the obligation given the circumstances or conditions of the area to which the obligation relates;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (d) an estimate of the expense that will be incurred in restoring the stand to the stage the stand had reached at the time the catastrophic damage occurred;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (e) the signature of the woodlot licence holder or of a person authorized to sign on the holder's behalf;

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (f) the date on which the application is signed.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (2.5) An application under section 108.3 (1) of the Act must be submitted no later than 2 years after December 31 of the year in which the order designating the area of catastrophic damage that overlaps with the area referred to in subsection (2.4) (a) (i) of this section was made, unless an application submission plan is submitted under section 83.1 of this regulation.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (3) If the minister is satisfied that relief or funding is required, the minister must, within one year of receiving the information referred to in subsection (2),

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (a) grant the relief,

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (b) determine whether or not to provide the funds necessary for the proposal under subsection (2.1) (c), or

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (c) provide and fund an alternate course of action to that proposed under subsection (2.1) (c), if the minister determines that

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (i)  the obligation to establish a free growing stand should continue, and

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (ii)  either

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (A) the woodlot licence holder has not provided a proposed course of action under subsection (2.1) (c), or

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (B) the proposed course of action under subsection (2.1) (c) is unacceptable.

heading: Relief or funding
paragraph: (4) During the period of one year described in subsection (3), a person who makes a request is not required to meet a requirement of the Act or this regulation that relates to the request.

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph:
83.1
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder may, pending the submission of an application for relief or funding under section 108 (0.1) or 108.3 (1) of the Act, submit an application submission plan to the minister for approval, if circumstances exist that limit the holder's ability to submit the application for relief or funding by the date described in section 83 (2.2) or (2.5), as applicable, of this regulation.

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (2) An application submission plan must include the following:

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (a) a description of the circumstances referred to in subsection (1) and how they limit the ability of the woodlot licence holder to submit the application for relief or funding by the date described in section 83 (2.2) or (2.5), as applicable;

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (b) a description of the activities the woodlot licence holder must undertake, in response to the circumstances referred to in subsection (1);

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (c) a timeline for completing the activities referred to in paragraph (b);

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (d) the date by which the woodlot licence holder proposes to submit the application for relief or funding;

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (e) the signature of the woodlot licence holder or of a person authorized to sign on the holder's behalf;

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (f) the date on which the application is signed.

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (3) An application submission plan must be submitted no later than 90 days before the date, referred to in subsection (1), by which the application for relief or funding must be submitted.

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (4) The minister must give notice to the woodlot licence holder who submitted the application submission plan of the minister's approval or rejection of the plan, and, if the plan is rejected, must provide written reasons for the rejection.

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (5) If the minister approves the application submission plan, the minister must

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (a) determine the date by which the application for relief or funding must be submitted, and

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (b) inform the woodlot licence holder who submitted the plan of the date determined under paragraph (a).

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (6) If the minister rejects the application submission plan, the woodlot licence holder who submitted the plan must submit the application for relief or funding no later than 60 days after the date the holder was notified of the rejection.

heading: Application submission plans
paragraph: (7) Sections 80 to 84 of the Act apply in relation to a decision by the minister under this section.

heading: Declarations
paragraph:
84
		  (1) A woodlot licence holder may make a declaration under section 107 [limitation on liability of persons to government] of the Act that a free growing stand has been established on a cutblock at any time before the date referred to in section 34 [free growing stands] if the stand

heading: Declarations
paragraph: (a) has met the free growing height that relates to the area, and

heading: Declarations
paragraph: (b) is not under threat from

heading: Declarations
paragraph: (i)  competing plants, shrubs or other trees established on the area, or

heading: Declarations
paragraph: (ii)  insects, disease or other factors adverse to forest health in the area.

heading: Declarations
paragraph: (2) A person may make a declaration under section 107 [limitation on liability of persons to government] of the Act in respect of a cutblock referred to in section 35 (2) [conforming to stocking standards] no earlier than 12 months after the completion of harvesting on the area.

heading: Declarations
paragraph: (3) A woodlot licence holder who makes a declaration under section 107 of the Act that the requirements for the regeneration date or free growing date on an area have been met must include with the declaration a forest cover inventory for the area to which the declaration applies.

heading: Declarations
paragraph: (4) The prescribed period for giving a notice to a woodlot licence holder under section 107 (3) of the Act is 15 months.

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph:
86
		  (1) An order or exemption under this regulation must

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (a) be in writing,

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (b) specify the matter to which it relates,

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (c) specify when the order or exemption comes into effect,

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (d) be delivered to the woodlot licence holder to whom the order or exemption applies, and

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (e) be filed with the district office for the forest district in which the area or thing to which the order or exemption applies is located.

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (2) An order or exemption referred to in subsection (1) takes effect on the later of the date

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (a) specified in the order or exemption, or

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (b) the order or exemption is received by the woodlot licence holder to whom the order or exemption applies.

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (3) For the purpose of subsection (2) (b), an order or exemption is received

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (a) on the date it is delivered, if it is delivered in person to

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (i)  the woodlot licence holder to whom it applies or that holder's representative, or

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (ii)  the place of business of the woodlot licence holder to whom it applies,

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (b) on the eighth day after it is mailed, if it is delivered by registered mail, or

heading: Process respecting orders and exemptions
paragraph: (c) on the date referred to in a confirmation of delivery, if it is delivered electronically or by facsimile transmission.

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph:
88
		  (1) For the purpose of section 77 (1) [power of intervention: general] of the Act, an order given by the minister must specify

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph: (a) the measures or actions that must be taken,

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph: (b) the grounds for requiring the measures or actions to be taken, and

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph: (c) whether or not the holder may recover all or part of the amount reasonably incurred in taking the specified measures or actions.

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph: (2) The minister may act under section 77 (1) or (2) of the Act if the act or omission of the holder will likely result in

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph: (a) a significant failure in meeting the stocking requirements described in section 35 [conforming to stocking standards],

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph: (b) a significant delay in meeting the stocking requirements by the dates described in section 35, or

heading: Intervention orders
paragraph: (c) a fundamental and adverse alteration of an ecosystem.

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph:
89
		  For the purpose of section 71 (5) (g) [administrative penalties] of the Act, before levying an administrative penalty in respect of a contravention by a woodlot licence holder, the minister may

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (a) request recommendations in respect of the contravention and penalty from any interested group, and

heading: Administrative penalties
paragraph: (b) if a request under paragraph (a) is made, act on any recommendation received from the group to which the request was made.

heading: Offences
paragraph:
90
		  (1) A person who contravenes any of the following sections commits an offence and is liable, on conviction, to a fine not exceeding $500 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 2 years or to both:

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 24 (1) or (2) [soil disturbance limits];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 26 [landslides];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 34 (1) or (3) [free growing stands];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 35 (2) [conforming to stocking standards];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 39 [restrictions in a riparian reserve zone];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 40 [restrictions in a riparian management zone];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 41 [lakeshore management zones];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 42 [temperature sensitive streams];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 43 [stream crossings];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 44 [fish passage];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 45 [protection of fish and fish habitat];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 46 [use of livestock in riparian areas];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 47 [protecting water quality];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 48 [licensed waterworks];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 49 [excavated or bladed trails];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 50 [roads in a community watershed];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 51 (1) [use of fertilizers];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 52 [wildlife tree retention];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 53 [restriction on harvesting];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 55 [general wildlife measures];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 55.1 [general ecological community measures];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 56 [resource features and wildlife habitat features];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 57 [fisheries sensitive watershed objectives];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 58 [water quality objectives];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 61 [roads and associated structures];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 62 [design of bridges];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 63 (1) [peak flow];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 64 [structural defects];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 65 [culvert fabrication];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 66 (1) (a) [retaining information];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 68 (7) [road maintenance];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 71 (1) (a), (b) or (c) [road deactivation];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 72 [hazard warning];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 87 (1) [intervention orders].

heading: Offences
paragraph: (2) A person who contravenes any of the following sections commits an offence and is liable, on conviction, to a fine not exceeding $100 000 or to imprisonment for not more than one year or to both:

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 28 [natural surface drainage patterns];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 29 [revegetation];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 30 [modification of insect behaviour];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 59 [visual quality objectives];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 59.1 [visual quality: transition];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 60 [recreation objectives];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 66 (1) (b) or (c) or (3) [retaining information];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 68 (1), (4) or (5) [road maintenance];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 71 (1) (d) [road deactivation].

heading: Offences
paragraph: (3) A person who contravenes any of the following sections commits an offence and is liable, on conviction, to a fine not exceeding $5 000 or to imprisonment for not more than 6 months or to both:

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 25 [permanent access structure limits];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 31 [use of livestock];

heading: Offences
paragraph: section 32 (4) or (7) (b) [use of seed];
