heading: Offences respecting alternative performance requirements
paragraph:
91
		  (1) If a woodlot licence holder fails to comply with an alternative performance requirement for which the holder has received approval under section 13 [alternative performance requirements], the holder commits an offence and is liable, on conviction, to the fine or imprisonment, or both, that is applicable to the provision to which the alternative performance requirement relates.

heading: Offences respecting alternative performance requirements
paragraph: (2) Section 87 (2) [fines] of the Act does not apply to a woodlot licence holder who is liable under subsection (1).

heading: Application of Code to forest development plans
paragraph:
97
		  The Code and the Code regulations apply to a forest development plan described in section 199 of the Act and to a forest development plan prepared under section 200 (1) of the Act.

heading: Factors relating to land use objectives
paragraph:
1
		  Information contained in land use plans approved under the Land Act may be used as factors to determine if a woodlot licence plan is consistent with the objective described in section 9 (1) (e) [established objectives].

heading: Factors relating to biodiversity
paragraph:
2
		  The following factors may be used for the purpose of developing a comprehensive wildlife tree retention strategy referred to in section 11 [wildlife tree retention strategy required]:

heading: Factors relating to biodiversity
paragraph: (a) the size, structure, amount, location and other characteristics of trees that

heading: Factors relating to biodiversity
paragraph: (i)  make the trees suitable for wildlife habitat, and

heading: Factors relating to biodiversity
paragraph: (ii)  have ecological attributes that contribute to stand level biodiversity;

heading: Factors relating to biodiversity
paragraph: (b) the extent to which wildlife habitat areas, ungulate winter ranges, riparian management zones, riparian reserve zones, scenic areas and other areas established to manage forest resources

heading: Factors relating to biodiversity
paragraph: (i)  provide suitable wildlife habitat, and

heading: Factors relating to biodiversity
paragraph: (ii)  assist in the conservation of stand level biodiversity.

heading: Factors relating to objective set by government for soils
paragraph:
3
		  The following factors may be used to determine if a woodlot licence plan is consistent with the objective set out in section 9 (1) (b) [established objectives]:

heading: Factors relating to objective set by government for soils
paragraph: (a) the amount of productive forest land base that will be occupied by permanent access structures;

heading: Factors relating to objective set by government for soils
paragraph: (b) the amount of soil disturbance within the net area to be reforested, having regard to

heading: Factors relating to objective set by government for soils
paragraph: (i)  the classification of soils based on their biological, physical and chemical properties, including their sensitivity to displacement, surface erosion and compaction,

heading: Factors relating to objective set by government for soils
paragraph: (ii)  the kinds of disturbance that are detrimental to productivity and hydrological function,

heading: Factors relating to objective set by government for soils
paragraph: (iii)  the amount of detrimental disturbance that can occur without unduly compromising productivity or hydrological function, and

heading: Factors relating to objective set by government for soils
paragraph: (iv)  the extent to which rehabilitation efforts can mitigate the effects of detrimental disturbance.

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph:
4
		  The following factors may be used to determine if a woodlot licence plan is consistent with the objective set out in section 9 (1) (c) [established objectives]:

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph: (a) the type of management regime that is required for a riparian area, having regard to

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph: (i)  the need to buffer the aquatic ecosystem of a stream, wetland or lake from the introduction of materials that are deleterious to water quality or fish habitat,

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph: (ii)  the role played by trees and understory vegetation in conserving water quality, fish habitat, wildlife habitat and biodiversity,

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph: (iii)  the need to maintain stream bank and stream channel integrity, and

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph: (iv)  the relative importance and sensitivity of different riparian classes of streams, wetlands and lakes in conserving water quality, fish habitat, wildlife habitat and biodiversity;

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph: (b) the type, timing or intensity of forest practices that can be carried out within the context of a management regime referred to in paragraph (a);

heading: Factors relating to water, fish, wildlife and biodiversity in riparian areas
paragraph: (c) the role of forest shading in controlling an increase in temperature within a temperature sensitive stream, if the increase might have a deleterious effect on fish or fish habitat.

heading: Factors relating to cultural heritage resources
paragraph:
5
		  The following factors may be used to determine if a woodlot licence plan is consistent with the objective set out in section 9 (1) (d) [established objectives]:

heading: Factors relating to cultural heritage resources
paragraph: (a) the relative value or importance of a particular cultural heritage resource to a traditional use by an aboriginal people;

heading: Factors relating to cultural heritage resources
paragraph: (b) the relative abundance or scarcity of a cultural heritage resource that is the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people;

heading: Factors relating to cultural heritage resources
paragraph: (c) the historical extent of a traditional use by an aboriginal people of a cultural heritage resource;

heading: Factors relating to cultural heritage resources
paragraph: (d) the impact on government granted timber harvesting rights of conserving or protecting a cultural heritage resource that is the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people;

heading: Factors relating to cultural heritage resources
paragraph: (e) options for mitigating the impact that a forest practice might have on a cultural heritage resource that is the focus of a traditional use by an aboriginal people.

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph:
6
		  (1) In this section:

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: "even-aged stand" means a stand of trees consisting of only one or two age classes;

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: "uneven-aged stand" means a stand of trees consisting of three or more age classes.

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (2) The following factors apply to the development of stocking standards generally:

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (a) the long term forest health risks that are relevant to species selection for the purposes of establishing a free growing stand under section 29 [free growing stands] of the Act;

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (b) the occurrence and extent of forest health factors.

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (3) The following factors apply to the development of stocking standards under section 35 [conforming to stocking standards]:

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (a) for an area that is managed as an even-aged stand,

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (i)  the types of commercially valuable and ecologically suitable species that should be established on the area, and

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (ii)  the numbers and the distribution of healthy trees of a species referred to in subparagraph (i) that are required to adequately stock a free growing stand established on the area;

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (b) for an area that is managed as an uneven-aged stand,

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (i)  the factors referred to in paragraph (a) that are applicable to those parts of the area that will be reforested,

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (ii)  the types of commercially valuable and ecologically suitable species that should be retained on the area, and

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (iii)  the characteristics, quantity and distribution of retained trees referred to in subparagraph (ii).

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (4) The following factors apply to developing stocking standards under section 12 [stocking information for specific areas]:

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (a) the types of commercially valuable and ecologically suitable species that should be retained on the area;

heading: Factors relating to stocking specifications
paragraph: (b) the characteristics, quantity and distribution of retained trees of a species referred to in paragraph (a) that are required to ensure the area will remain adequately stocked.

heading: Short title
paragraph: 1 This Act may be cited as the Wrecked, Abandoned or Hazardous Vessels Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 2 The following definitions apply in this Act.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: authorized representative has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. (representant autorise)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian vessel, except in Part 1, means a vessel that is not registered, listed, recorded or licensed in a foreign state. (batiment canadien)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: master has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. (capitaine)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Minister means, subject to section 89, the Minister of Transport. (ministre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: owner, except in Part 1, means, in relation to a vessel, a person that

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is a registered owner of the vessel;

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is a holder of a pleasure craft licence; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (c) has, either by law or by contract, the rights of an owner of the vessel in respect of its possession and use. (proprietaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: person includes a partnership, an unincorporated organization, an association and a trust. (personne)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: person in charge means, in relation to a vessel or a wreck, the owner, master or authorized representative of the vessel, and any person that is or appears to be in command, control or charge of the vessel or that has management of the vessel, but does not include a licensed pilot, as defined in section 1.1 of the Pilotage Act, while the pilot is exercising their powers or performing their duties or functions under that Act. (responsable)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: pleasure craft has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. (embarcation de plaisance)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: prescribed means prescribed by the regulations.‍ (Version anglaise seulement)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Transportation Appeal Tribunal means the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada established by subsection 2(1) of the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada Act.‍ (Tribunal d'appel des transports)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vessel, except in Part 1, means any boat, ship or craft of any kind designed, used or capable of being used solely or partly for navigation in, on, through or immediately above water, without regard to method or lack of propulsion or to whether it is under construction or being re-purposed or dismantled. It also includes a floating object that is designated to be a vessel by the regulations. (batiment)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Wreck Removal Convention means the Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007, signed at Nairobi on May 18, 2007 and set out in Schedule 1. (Convention sur l'enlevement des epaves)

heading: Binding on Her Majesty
paragraph: 3 This Act is binding on Her Majesty in right of Canada or a province.

heading: Purpose of Act
paragraph: 4 The purpose of this Act is to promote the protection of the public, of the environment, including coastlines and shorelines, and of infrastructure by, among other things, regulating wrecks and vessels posing hazards, prohibiting vessel abandonment, and recognizing the responsibility and liability of owners for their vessels.

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: 5 (1) Except as otherwise provided by regulations made under paragraph 130(1)(c) or subsection 131(1) and despite subsection (3), this Act does not apply in respect of a vessel or aircraft that belongs to the Canadian Forces or a foreign military force or in respect of any other vessel or aircraft that is under the command, control or direction of the Canadian Forces.

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (2) Except as otherwise provided by regulations made under subsection 131(1), this Act, other than Parts 3 and 4, does not apply in respect of

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (a) a vessel that is owned or operated by Her Majesty in right of Canada or of a province or by a foreign state while that vessel is being used exclusively for non-commercial governmental purposes; and

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: (b) vessels that are on location for the purposes of engaging in the exploration, exploitation or production of mineral resources or that, as a result of an accident or incident, have drifted from that location.

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: (3) Except as otherwise provided by regulations made under subsection 131(1), this Act, other than Parts 3 and 4, does not apply in respect of wrecks considered as having heritage value under an Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province.

heading: Agreements or arrangements
paragraph: 6 (1) The Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, with respect to that Minister's powers, duties and functions under this Act, enter into agreements or arrangements for carrying out the purposes of this Act and authorize any person, including a provincial government, a local authority and a government, council or other entity authorized to act on behalf of an Indigenous group, with whom an agreement or arrangement is entered into to exercise the powers - other than the power to make an order under section 11 - or perform the duties or functions under this Act that are specified in the agreement or arrangement.

heading: Guidelines
paragraph: (2) The Minister may issue guidelines for the purposes of this Act.

heading: Delegation - Minister
paragraph: 7 (1) The Minister may delegate any of his or her powers, duties or functions under this Act to the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans for any period and under any terms and conditions that the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Delegation - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may delegate any of his or her powers, duties or functions under this Act to the Minister for any period and under any terms and conditions that the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans considers appropriate.

heading: Obligation to consult - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: 8 (1) For the purposes of this Act, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may determine whether a vessel or wreck poses, or may pose, a hazard and, in exercising that power, may consult with any person that he or she considers appropriate, and is to consult with the Minister to the extent that it is possible to do so.

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (2) The consultation with the Minister is to include the following matters:

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (a) any proposed salvage plans; and

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (b) if relevant, whether the vessel or wreck poses, or may pose, a hazard

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (i) to navigation,

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (ii) to a public port or public port facility, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Marine Act, or

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (iii) to transportation infrastructure in respect of which Parliament has jurisdiction.

heading: Obligation to consult - Minister
paragraph: 9 (1) For the purposes of this Act, if the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans has, under subsection 7(2), delegated his or her power to the Minister to determine whether a vessel or wreck poses, or may pose, a hazard, the Minister, in exercising that power, may consult with any person that he or she considers appropriate, and is to consult with the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans to the extent that it is possible to do so.

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (2) The consultation with the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is to include, if relevant, whether the vessel or wreck poses, or may pose, a hazard

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (a) to the environment;

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (b) to aquatic wildlife or their habitat and ecosystems;

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (c) to fisheries and aquaculture; or

heading: Consultation - matters
paragraph: (d) to a scheduled harbour, as defined in section 2 of the Fishing and Recreational Harbours Act.

heading: Validity of determination not affected
paragraph: 10 The failure to comply with the obligation under section 8 or 9 does not affect the validity of the determination of the Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans.

heading: Exclusion
paragraph: 11 Subject to any conditions that the Minister considers appropriate, he or she may, by order, exclude a vessel or wreck that is specified in the order from the application of all or part of this Act, if the Minister is of the opinion that it would be in the public interest to do so.

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to issue or renew
paragraph: 12 (1) The Minister or the Chief Registrar or a registrar referred to in the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 may suspend, cancel or refuse to issue or renew any document, including a certificate, licence or permit, that may be issued under that Act, if the applicant or the holder of the document

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to issue or renew
paragraph: (a) has contravened a direction given under this Act;

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to issue or renew
paragraph: (b) has not paid a fine or penalty imposed on them under this Act; or

heading: Suspension, cancellation and refusal to issue or renew
paragraph: (c) has not reimbursed the Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans for any costs and expenses incurred in respect of measures taken under any of subsections 21(2) and (3), section 22, paragraphs 30(3)(a) to (c), sections 35 and 36 and subsection 37(3).

heading: Corporation
paragraph: (2) If the applicant or the holder of the document referred to in subsection (1) is a corporation, the Minister or the Chief Registrar or a registrar referred to in the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 may take the measures referred to in that subsection if a director, officer, agent or mandatary of the corporation

heading: Corporation
paragraph: (a) has contravened a direction given under this Act;

heading: Corporation
paragraph: (b) has not paid a fine or penalty imposed on them under this Act; or

heading: Corporation
paragraph: (c) has not reimbursed the Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans for any costs and expenses incurred in respect of measures taken under any of subsections 21(2) and (3), section 22, paragraphs 30(3)(a) to (c), sections 35 and 36 and subsection 37(3).

heading: Disclosure by Minister or Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: 13 (1) The Minister and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, on their own initiative or on request, disclose to each other, to an enforcement officer or to any person authorized to exercise powers or perform duties or functions under this Act any information collected or obtained under this Act, the Fishing and Recreational Harbours Act, the Canadian Navigable Waters Act, the Canada Marine Act or the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, to the extent that the disclosure is necessary for the administration of this Act.

heading: Disclosure by enforcement officer or authorized person
paragraph: (2) An enforcement officer and any person authorized to exercise powers or perform duties or functions under this Act may, on their own initiative or on request, disclose to each other, to the Minister or to the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans any information collected or obtained under this Act, to the extent that the disclosure is necessary for the administration of this Act.

heading: Disclosure to Chief Registrar, registrar or authorized person
paragraph: 14 (1) The Minister, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, an enforcement officer or any person authorized to exercise powers or perform duties or functions under this Act may, on their own initiative or on request, disclose to the Chief Registrar or a registrar referred to in the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 or to any person authorized to exercise powers or perform duties or functions under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 any information collected or obtained under this Act relating to the identity and contact information of an owner of a vessel, to the extent that the disclosure is necessary for the administration or enforcement of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Disclosure to Minister
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, an enforcement officer or any person authorized to exercise powers or perform duties or functions under this Act may, on their own initiative or on request, disclose to the Minister any information collected or obtained under this Act relating to the identity and contact information of an owner of a vessel, to the extent that the disclosure is necessary for the administration or enforcement of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 15 (1) The following definitions apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Canadian vessel means a vessel that is registered, listed, recorded or licensed under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. (batiment canadien)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: owner, in relation to a vessel, has the meaning assigned by the definition registered owner in Article 1 of the Wreck Removal Convention. (proprietaire)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: vessel has the meaning assigned by the definition ship in Article 1 of the Wreck Removal Convention, but includes non-seagoing vessels. (batiment)

heading: Words and expressions defined
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of this Part, unless otherwise provided, words and expressions used in this Part have the same meaning as in the Wreck Removal Convention.

heading: Extended meaning of expression
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of the application of the Wreck Removal Convention, in cases where Canada is the affected State, the definition Convention area in Article 1 of that Convention is to be read as including Canada.

heading: Clarification
paragraph: (4) For the purposes of the application of the Wreck Removal Convention, any reference to a "State Party" in the provisions of that Convention referred to in section 16 is, for greater certainty, to be read as including Canada.

heading: Force of law
paragraph: 16 Article 1, paragraphs 1 and 3 of Article 3, paragraphs 1, 2 and 4 of Article 4, paragraph 2 of Article 5, Article 6, paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 9, Articles 10 and 11, paragraphs 1 to 3, 5 to 10 and 13 of Article 12 and Article 13 of the Wreck Removal Convention have the force of law in Canada.

heading: Inconsistency
paragraph: 17 In the event of any inconsistency between this Part and the Wreck Removal Convention, this Part prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Application
paragraph: 18 This Part applies in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) vessels in Canadian waters or in the exclusive economic zone of Canada;

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) Canadian vessels, wherever they are; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (c) wrecks

heading: Application
paragraph: (i) that are located in the Convention area of a State Party to the Wreck Removal Convention, and

heading: Application
paragraph: (ii) that are the result of a maritime casualty.

heading: Obligation to report
paragraph: 19 (1) Subject to subsection (2), if a vessel - other than a vessel that is registered, listed, recorded or licensed in a state that is not a party to the Wreck Removal Convention and that is located in the exclusive economic zone of Canada - is involved in a maritime casualty that resulted in a wreck, the master and the operator of the vessel must, without delay and in accordance with Article 5 of that Convention, provide a report containing the information referred to in paragraph 2 of that Article to a marine communications and traffic services officer designated under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, unless another person has been designated by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, in which case it must be provided to that person. To the extent that either the master or the operator complies with the obligation, the other is not required to provide a report.

heading: Canadian vessels abroad
paragraph: (2) If the vessel referred to in subsection (1) is a Canadian vessel located in the Convention area of a State Party to the Wreck Removal Convention other than Canada, the report under subsection (1) must be made to the government of that state, unless another person has been designated by that state, in which case it must be made to that person.

heading: Designation
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may designate persons or classes of persons for the purposes of subsection (1).

heading: Marking
paragraph: 20 Unless otherwise directed by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, the owner of a vessel - other than a vessel that is registered, listed, recorded or licensed in a state that is not a party to the Wreck Removal Convention and that is located in the exclusive economic zone of Canada - that was involved in a maritime casualty that resulted in a wreck that poses a hazard must ensure that all reasonable steps are taken without delay to mark the wreck with markings that conform to the internationally accepted system of buoyage in use in the area where the wreck is located.

heading: Direction - locating, marking and removal
paragraph: 21 (1) If the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is of the opinion that a wreck poses a hazard, he or she may direct the owner of the vessel that was involved in the maritime casualty that resulted in the wreck, within the time that he or she specifies, to

heading: Direction - locating, marking and removal
paragraph: (a) take all measures that that Minister considers practicable to establish the precise location of the wreck; and

heading: Direction - locating, marking and removal
paragraph: (b) take all measures that that Minister considers proportionate to the hazard to mark or remove the wreck.

heading: Measures - Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: (2) If the measures referred to in subsection (1) are not taken within the period specified by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, he or she may take the measures.

heading: Measures - owner cannot be contacted
paragraph: (3) If the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is of the opinion that a wreck poses a hazard and the owner of the vessel that was involved in the maritime casualty that resulted in the wreck cannot be contacted, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may take the measures referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Immediate action required
paragraph: 22 If the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is of the opinion that a wreck poses a hazard and that a measure referred to in subsection 21(1) must be taken immediately, he or she may take the measure.

heading: Owner
paragraph: 23 Subject to any limit set out in the Marine Liability Act, the liability of the owner of a vessel for the purposes of Article 10 of the Wreck Removal Convention also includes

heading: Owner
paragraph: (a) the costs and expenses incurred by any person in Canada or any person in a state, other than Canada, that is a party to that Convention, including those incurred by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans in determining whether a wreck poses a hazard, if he or she determined that it posed one; and

heading: Owner
paragraph: (b) any loss or damage caused by the measures taken in accordance with this Act.

heading: Absence of certificate
paragraph: 24 (1) Unless a vessel of 300 gross tonnage and above carries a certificate described in paragraph 2 of Article 12 of the Wreck Removal Convention and issued in accordance with subsection 25(1), the vessel must not

heading: Absence of certificate
paragraph: (a) enter or leave a port in Canadian waters or in the exclusive economic zone of Canada or arrive at or leave an offshore facility in Canadian waters or in the exclusive economic zone of Canada; or

heading: Absence of certificate
paragraph: (b) operate, if it is a Canadian vessel.

heading: Certificate to be produced on request
paragraph: (2) Unless, in accordance with paragraph 13 of Article 12 of the Wreck Removal Convention, the certificate is not required to be carried on board the vessel, the master, a crew member or any person on board who is, or appears to be, in charge of the vessel must produce the certificate and give details of it at the request of an enforcement officer or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans.

heading: By whom certificate must be issued
paragraph: 25 (1) The certificate must be issued

heading: By whom certificate must be issued
paragraph: (a) if the vessel is a Canadian vessel, by the Minister;

heading: By whom certificate must be issued
paragraph: (b) if the vessel is registered, listed, recorded or licensed in a state, other than Canada, that is a party to the Wreck Removal Convention, by or under the authority of the government of that state; or

heading: By whom certificate must be issued
paragraph: (c) if the vessel is registered, listed, recorded or licensed in a state that is not a party to the Wreck Removal Convention, by the Minister or by or under the authority of the government of a state, other than Canada, that is a party to that Convention.

heading: Designation by Minister
paragraph: (2) The Minister may designate persons or classes of persons to issue, refuse or revoke a certificate on the Minister's behalf.

heading: Issuance of certificate by Minister
paragraph: (3) Subject to the regulations, on an application to the Minister for a certificate in respect of a Canadian vessel or a vessel registered, listed, recorded or licensed in a state that is not a party to the Wreck Removal Convention, the Minister must issue the certificate to the owner of the vessel - in printed or electronic form, or both - if he or she is satisfied that a contract of insurance or other financial security satisfying the requirements of Article 12 of that Convention will be in force in respect of the vessel throughout the period for which the certificate is issued.

heading: When Minister may refuse certificate
paragraph: (4) Subject to the regulations, if the Minister is of the opinion that the insurer or guarantor will be unable to meet their obligations under the contract of insurance or other financial security referred to in Article 12 of the Wreck Removal Convention, or that the contract of insurance or other financial security will not satisfy the requirements of that Article, the Minister may refuse to issue the certificate.

heading: When Minister may revoke certificate
paragraph: (5) Subject to the regulations, the Minister may revoke the certificate issued by him or her if the Minister is of the opinion that the insurer or guarantor is unable to meet their obligations under the contract of insurance or other financial security referred to in Article 12 of the Wreck Removal Convention, or that the contract of insurance or other financial security does not satisfy the requirements of that Article.

heading: Towing
paragraph: 26 (1) Subject to the regulations, the Minister may, on any terms and conditions that he or she considers necessary, exempt a vessel that is not registered, listed, recorded or licensed from the application of section 24, for the period during which it is being towed, if he or she is satisfied that a contract of insurance or other financial security in an amount equal to that set out in paragraph 1 of Article 12 of the Wreck Removal Convention will be in force in respect of the vessel while it is being towed and the insurer or guarantor will be able to meet their obligations under the contract of insurance or other financial security.

heading: Proof to be produced on request
paragraph: (2) The master, a crew member or any person on board who is, or appears to be, in charge of the vessel that is towing a vessel that has been exempted under subsection (1) must produce proof of the exemption and give details of it at the request of an enforcement officer or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 27 The following definitions apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: dilapidated vessel means a vessel that meets any prescribed criteria and

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) is significantly degraded or dismantled; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) is incapable of being used for safe navigation. (batiment delabre)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: hazard means any condition or threat that may reasonably be expected to result in harmful consequences to the environment, coastlines, shorelines, infrastructure or any other interest, including the health, safety, well-being and economic interests of the public. It does not include harmful consequences that are excluded by the regulations. (danger)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: wreck means

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (a) a vessel, or part of a vessel, that is sunk, partially sunk, adrift, stranded or grounded, including on the shore; or

heading: Definitions
paragraph: (b) equipment, stores, cargo or any other thing that is or was on board a vessel and that is sunk, partially sunk, adrift, stranded or grounded, including on the shore. (epave)

heading: Application
paragraph: 28 Unless otherwise provided, this Part applies in respect of

heading: Application
paragraph: (a) wrecks and Canadian vessels in Canadian waters and in the exclusive economic zone of Canada; and

heading: Application
paragraph: (b) all other vessels in Canadian waters.

heading: Exclusions
paragraph: 29 This Part does not apply in respect of vessels that are less than 5.5 m in length and are designed to be primarily human-powered or wind-powered, including those that have become wrecks.

heading: Dilapidated vessel
paragraph: 30 (1) It is prohibited for an owner of a dilapidated vessel to leave it stranded, grounded, including on the shore, anchored or moored in the same location - or within a radius of three nautical miles of, or, if a radius is prescribed, within that prescribed radius of that location - for a period of 60 consecutive days or, if a number of consecutive days is prescribed, that number of consecutive days.

heading: Exception - consent
paragraph: (2) An owner of a dilapidated vessel does not contravene subsection (1) if they obtain the express consent to leave the vessel, at each location where the vessel is situated during the period referred to in that subsection, of a person that has the authority to give that consent as owner, manager or lessee of the location. The onus of proving that consent is on the owner of the dilapidated vessel.

heading: Measures
paragraph: (3) If subsection (1) has been contravened, the Minister may

heading: Measures
paragraph: (a) take the measures that he or she considers necessary in respect of the dilapidated vessel or its contents, including repairing, securing, moving or removing the vessel or its contents or selling, dismantling, destroying or otherwise disposing of them;

heading: Measures
paragraph: (b) monitor the measures taken by any person in respect of the dilapidated vessel or its contents; and

heading: Measures
paragraph: (c) if he or she considers it necessary to do so, direct any person or vessel to take measures referred to in paragraph (a) or to refrain from doing so.

heading: Vessel adrift
paragraph: 31 It is prohibited for an owner of a vessel to leave it adrift for a period of 48 hours without taking measures to secure it.

heading: Abandoned vessel
paragraph: 32 (1) It is prohibited for an owner of a vessel to abandon it.

heading: Presumption - abandonment
paragraph: (2) An owner of a vessel is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, presumed to have abandoned it if they leave the vessel unattended for a period of two years.

heading: For greater certainty
paragraph: (3) For greater certainty and despite subsection (2), it is not necessary for an owner to leave a vessel unattended for a period of two years for the owner to be found to have contravened subsection (1).

heading: Exception
paragraph: (4) An owner of a vessel who abandons it does not contravene subsection (1) if

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) the abandonment is in accordance with a Canadian permit, as defined in subsection 122(1) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, authorizing the disposal of the vessel;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) the abandonment is in accordance with any other Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) the abandonment is temporary and necessary to avert a danger to human life; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (d) it is a wreck, as defined in Article 1 of the Wreck Removal Convention, and its owner complies with Part 1.

heading: Vessel becoming wreck
paragraph: 33 It is prohibited for an owner of a vessel to let it become a wreck by reason of failing to maintain it.

heading: Sinking, stranding or grounding vessel
paragraph: 34 (1) It is prohibited for a person in charge of a vessel to knowingly cause it to sink or partially sink or to be stranded or grounded, including on the shore.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) A person in charge of a vessel that knowingly causes it to sink or partially sink or to be stranded or grounded, including on the shore, does not contravene subsection (1) if

heading: Exception
paragraph: (a) they do so in accordance with any other Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province;

heading: Exception
paragraph: (b) they cause it to sink in accordance with a Canadian permit, as defined in subsection 122(1) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, authorizing the disposal of the vessel; or

heading: Exception
paragraph: (c) they cause it to be stranded or grounded so as to avert a danger to human life.

heading: Sale, destruction or other disposition
paragraph: 35 The Minister may sell, destroy or otherwise dispose of a vessel that is abandoned.

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - general powers
paragraph: 36 If the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans has reasonable grounds to believe that a vessel or wreck poses, or may pose, a hazard, he or she

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - general powers
paragraph: (a) may take the measures that he or she considers necessary to prevent, mitigate or eliminate the hazard, including by repairing, securing, moving or removing of the vessel, the wreck or their contents or selling, dismantling, destroying or otherwise disposing of them;

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - general powers
paragraph: (b) may monitor the measures taken by any person to prevent, mitigate or eliminate the hazard; and

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - general powers
paragraph: (c) if he or she considers it necessary to do so, may direct any person or vessel to take measures referred to in paragraph (a) or to refrain from doing so.

heading: Power related to dilapidated vessel
paragraph: 37 (1) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may direct the authorized representative of a dilapidated vessel or, in the absence of an authorized representative, its owner, to repair, secure, move, remove, dismantle or destroy it or its contents in accordance with that Minister's directions if the vessel is

heading: Power related to dilapidated vessel
paragraph: (a) in a scheduled harbour, as defined in section 2 of the Fishing and Recreational Harbours Act; or

heading: Power related to dilapidated vessel
paragraph: (b) on any property belonging to Her Majesty in right of Canada for which the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is responsible.

heading: Power related to dilapidated vessel
paragraph: (2) The Minister may direct the authorized representative of a dilapidated vessel or, in the absence of an authorized representative, its owner, to repair, secure, move, remove, dismantle or destroy it or its contents in accordance with the Minister's directions if the vessel is

heading: Power related to dilapidated vessel
paragraph: (a) located in a public port or public port facility, as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Canada Marine Act; or

heading: Power related to dilapidated vessel
paragraph: (b) on any property belonging to Her Majesty in right of Canada, other than a scheduled harbour or property referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Failure to comply with direction
paragraph: (3) If the measures referred to in subsection (1) or (2) are not taken in accordance with the directions given, the Minister who gave them

heading: Failure to comply with direction
paragraph: (a) may take the measures that he or she considers necessary, including repairing, securing, moving or removing the vessel or its contents or selling, dismantling, destroying or otherwise disposing of them;

heading: Failure to comply with direction
paragraph: (b) may monitor the measures taken by any person in respect of the dilapidated vessel or its contents; and

heading: Failure to comply with direction
paragraph: (c) if he or she considers it necessary to do so, may direct any person or vessel to take measures referred to in paragraph (a) or to refrain from doing so.

heading: Authorized representative or owner unknown or not located
paragraph: (4) If the authorized representative or, in the absence of an authorized representative, the owner, is unknown or cannot be located, the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans or the Minister, as the case may be, may take any of the measures referred to in paragraphs (3)(a) to (c).

heading: Authorization to take possession
paragraph: 38 (1) If any vessel or other thing is wrecked, sunk, partially sunk, stranded, grounded, including on the shore, or abandoned in Canadian waters, the Minister may, for a purpose that he or she specifies and subject to any conditions that he or she considers appropriate, authorize any person to take possession of all or part of the vessel or thing, for the benefit of that person or the public.

heading: Notification
paragraph: (2) The Minister must not authorize a person to take possession of all or part of the vessel or thing under subsection (1) unless the person has given 30 days' notice, in the form and manner specified by the Minister, of their intention to do so

heading: Notification
paragraph: (a) to its owner; or

heading: Notification
paragraph: (b) to the public, if its owner is unknown or cannot be located.

heading: Consent not required
paragraph: (3) A person that is authorized to take possession of a vessel under subsection (1) is not required to obtain the consent of its owner to register the vessel or obtain a pleasure craft license for it under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: 39 The Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may sell, dismantle, destroy or otherwise dispose of a vessel, a wreck or their contents under paragraph 30(3)(a), section 35, paragraph 36(a) or 37(3)(a) or subsection 37(4) only if

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (a) 30 days have elapsed after the day on which notice of his or her intention to dispose of it was given to

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (i) the public,

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (ii) the authorized representative of the vessel or, in the absence of an authorized representative, its owner, if known,

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (iii) the owner of the wreck or the contents, if known,

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (iv) the holder of any mortgage or hypothec against the vessel that is registered on the register in which the vessel is recorded,

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (v) the holder of any maritime lien against the vessel or the holder of any similar interest or right, if known, and

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (vi) the holder of any lien against the contents or the holder of any similar interest or right, if known;

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (b) the vessel, the wreck or their contents are, in his or her opinion, likely to deteriorate rapidly; or

heading: Disposition of vessel, wreck or contents
paragraph: (c) the disposition is made under paragraph 36(a) and the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans is of the opinion that it must be made in a period of less than 30 days to prevent, mitigate or eliminate the hazard.

heading: At risk, cost and expense of owner
paragraph: 40 The disposition is at the risk, cost and expense of the owner of the vessel, wreck or contents.

heading: Payment of proceeds
paragraph: 41 If a vessel, a wreck or their contents are disposed of under paragraph 30(3)(a), section 35, paragraph 36(a) or 37(3)(a) or subsection 37(4), any surplus remaining from the proceeds of the disposition after deducting the costs and expenses incurred in respect of the disposition must be paid to the Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, in respect of all costs and expenses incurred in taking any other measures under subsection 30(3), section 35 or 36 or subsection 37(3) or (4), and to the holders, if known at the time of the disposition, of any mortgages, hypothecs, maritime liens or other interests or rights that are in existence at the time of the disposition, and any amount that remains must be paid to the owner of the vessel, the wreck or their contents or, if proceedings have been commenced under this Act, must be retained by the Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, as the case may be, pending the outcome of the proceedings.

heading: Federal Court directions
paragraph: 42 The Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may apply to the Federal Court for directions as to the allocation of the surplus referred to in section 41.

heading: Clear title
paragraph: 43 When a vessel, a wreck or their contents are sold or otherwise disposed of under paragraph 30(3)(a), section 35, paragraph 36(a) or 37(3)(a) or subsection 37(4), the Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may give the person acquiring it a valid title to the vessel, the wreck or their contents free from any mortgage, hypothec, maritime lien or other interest or right that is in existence at the time of the disposition.

heading: Compensation
paragraph: 44 Compensation must be paid by Her Majesty in right of Canada to any vessel or person that has complied with a direction issued under paragraph 30(3)(c), 36(c) or 37(3)(c) or subsection 37(4), other than

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (a) an owner that contravened subsection 30(1);

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (b) an authorized representative or owner that was the subject of a direction under subsection 37(1) or (2); or

heading: Compensation
paragraph: (c) a vessel or wreck that was the subject of measures under section 36 or subsection 37(3) or (4), or the person in charge of that vessel or wreck.

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: 45 (1) The owner of a vessel or wreck is liable for the costs and expenses incurred by

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (a) the Minister

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (i) in respect of measures taken under paragraph 30(3)(a), section 35, paragraph 37(3)(a) or subsection 37(4) and any loss or damage caused by those measures,

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (ii) in respect of any monitoring under paragraph 30(3)(b) or 37(3)(b) or subsection 37(4),

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (iii) in relation to any direction given under paragraph 30(3)(c) or 37(3)(c) or subsection 37(4), and

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (iv) in relation to the use of property under subsection 86(5);

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (b) the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (i) in respect of measures taken under paragraph 36(a) (including any costs and expenses incurred by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans in determining whether a vessel or wreck poses a hazard, if he or she determined that it posed one) or 37(3)(a) or subsection 37(4) and any loss or damage caused by those measures,

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (ii) in respect of any monitoring under paragraph 36(b) or 37(3)(b) or subsection 37(4),

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (iii) in relation to any direction given under paragraph 36(c) or 37(3)(c) or subsection 37(4), and

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (iv) in relation to the use of property under subsection 86(5); and

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (c) any other person, in cases where no compensation is paid by Her Majesty in right of Canada,

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (i) in respect of the measures that they were directed to take or to refrain from taking under paragraph 30(3)(c), 36(c) or 37(3)(c) or subsection 37(4) and any loss or damage caused by those measures, and

heading: Liability of owner
paragraph: (ii) in respect of any loss or damage caused by the use of property under subsection 86(5).

heading: Limitation or prescription period
paragraph: (2) No action lies in respect of the liability referred to in subsection (1) if it is commenced more than six years after the day on which the first measure was taken in respect of the vessel or wreck under any of paragraphs 30(3)(a) to (c), section 35, paragraphs 36(a) to (c) and 37(3)(a) to (c) and subsections 37(4) and 86(5).

heading: Liability for costs and expenses
paragraph: (3) If there is more than one owner of a vessel or wreck, the owners are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable for the costs and expenses referred to in subsection (1).

heading: Direction to vessel
paragraph: 46 For the purposes of this Part, a direction is deemed to have been given to the vessel and is binding on it if

heading: Direction to vessel
paragraph: (a) the direction is given to the authorized representative or a person in charge of the vessel; or

heading: Direction to vessel
paragraph: (b) in the case of a direction that cannot be given to any person referred to in paragraph (a) despite reasonable efforts having been made to do so, a copy of it is posted on any conspicuous part of the vessel.

heading: Inconsistency - Part 1
paragraph: 47 (1) In the event of any inconsistency between Part 1 and this Part, Part 1 prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Inconsistency - directions
paragraph: (2) Any direction under this Part that is inconsistent with a direction under any other Act of Parliament is void to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: 48 (1) The following definitions apply in this Part.

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Crown vessel means a vessel that is owned by or is in the exclusive possession of Her Majesty in right of Canada. (batiment appartenant a Sa Majeste)

heading: Definitions
paragraph: Salvage Convention means the International Convention on Salvage, 1989, signed at London on April 28, 1989 and set out in Part 1 of Schedule 2. (Convention sur l'assistance)

heading: Clarification
paragraph: (2) For the purposes of the application of the Salvage Convention, any reference to a "State Party" in the provisions referred to in subsection 50(1) is, for greater certainty, to be read as including Canada.

heading: Vessels
paragraph: 49 This Part applies in respect of vessels registered, listed, recorded or licensed under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, wherever they are, and in respect of all other vessels in Canadian waters.

heading: Salvage Convention
paragraph: 50 (1) Subject to the reservations that Canada made and that are set out in Part 2 of Schedule 2, Articles 1 to 9, paragraphs 1 and 3 of Article 10 and Articles 11 to 26 of the Salvage Convention have the force of law in Canada.

heading: Inconsistent laws
paragraph: (2) In the event of any inconsistency between the Salvage Convention and this Act or the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 or the regulations made under those Acts, the Convention prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

heading: When salvage services may be claimed
paragraph: 51 (1) In the case of salvage services rendered by or with the aid of a Crown vessel, Her Majesty in right of Canada and the master and crew members of the Crown vessel may claim salvage for salvage services only if the Crown vessel is a tug or is specially equipped with a salvage plant.

heading: Rights and limitations
paragraph: (2) In respect of salvage services that may be claimed under subsection (1),

heading: Rights and limitations
paragraph: (a) Her Majesty and the master and crew members have the same rights and remedies in respect of salvage services as any other salvor would have had if the vessel had belonged to that other salvor; and

heading: Rights and limitations
paragraph: (b) no claim for salvage services by the master or a crew member of a Crown vessel may be finally adjudicated unless the consent of the Governor in Council to the institution of proceedings in respect of the claim is proved.

heading: Time for giving consent
paragraph: (3) For the purposes of paragraph (2)(b), the consent of the Governor in Council may be given at any time before final adjudication.

heading: Evidence of consent
paragraph: (4) Any document that purports to give the consent of the Governor in Council for the purposes of paragraph (2)(b) is evidence of that consent.

heading: Claim dismissed if no consent
paragraph: (5) If proceedings in respect of a claim are instituted by the master or a crew member and the consent of the Governor in Council is not proved, the claim must be dismissed with costs.

heading: Governor in Council may accept offers of settlement
paragraph: 52 (1) The Governor in Council may, on the recommendation of the Attorney General of Canada, accept, on behalf of Her Majesty in right of Canada and the master or a crew member, offers of settlement made with respect to claims for salvage services rendered by Crown vessels.

heading: Distribution
paragraph: (2) The proceeds of a settlement made under subsection (1) must be distributed in the manner that the Governor in Council specifies.

heading: Proceedings within two years
paragraph: 53 (1) No action in respect of salvage services may be commenced more than two years after the date that the salvage services were rendered.

heading: Extension of period by court
paragraph: (2) The court having jurisdiction to deal with an action to which this section relates may, in accordance with the rules of court, extend the period described in subsection (1) to the extent and on the conditions that it considers appropriate.

heading: Aircraft treated as if vessel
paragraph: 54 The provisions of this Part with respect to salvage apply in respect of aircraft on or over Canadian waters as they apply in respect of vessels, with any modifications that the circumstances require.

heading: Salvage
paragraph: 55 Compliance with section 130, 131 or 132 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 does not affect the right of a master or of any other person to salvage.

heading: Definition of wreck
paragraph: 56 In this Part, wreck includes

heading: Definition of wreck
paragraph: (a) jetsam, flotsam, lagan and derelict and any other thing that was part of or was on a vessel wrecked, stranded or in distress; and

heading: Definition of wreck
paragraph: (b) aircraft wrecked in waters and anything that was part of or was on an aircraft wrecked, stranded or in distress in waters.

heading: Designation
paragraph: 57 (1) The Minister may designate persons or classes of persons as receivers of wreck.

heading: Authorization
paragraph: (2) A receiver of wreck may authorize any person or class of persons to exercise any of their powers or perform any of their duties or functions.

heading: Obligation to report
paragraph: 58 (1) A person must report a wreck whose owner is unknown or cannot be located to a receiver of wreck, in the form and manner specified by the receiver of wreck,

heading: Obligation to report
paragraph: (a) as soon as feasible after taking possession of it under paragraph (3)(a);

heading: Obligation to report
paragraph: (b) before taking possession of it, other than under paragraph (3)(a), if the wreck was found in Canada; or

heading: Obligation to report
paragraph: (c) as soon as feasible, if the person brings the wreck into Canada.

heading: Exception
paragraph: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a wreck that is a thing that could not reasonably be expected to be identified as having been part of or on a vessel or aircraft.

heading: Finding wreck
paragraph: (3) It is prohibited for a person that finds a wreck in Canada whose owner is unknown or cannot be located to take possession of it unless

heading: Finding wreck
paragraph: (a) the wreck is in danger and the possession is necessary to secure or otherwise protect it; or

heading: Finding wreck
paragraph: (b) that person has been authorized to do so by the receiver of wreck under paragraph (4)(a).

heading: Powers of receiver of wreck
paragraph: (4) On receipt of a report referred to in subsection (1), a receiver of wreck may

heading: Powers of receiver of wreck
paragraph: (a) authorize the person that made the report to take possession of the wreck;

heading: Powers of receiver of wreck
paragraph: (b) direct the person that made the report to

heading: Powers of receiver of wreck
paragraph: (i) provide any additional information that the receiver specifies,

heading: Powers of receiver of wreck
paragraph: (ii) take the measures with respect to the wreck - other than selling, dismantling, destroying or otherwise disposing of it - that the receiver specifies, including delivering it to the receiver or keeping it in their possession, in accordance with his or her instructions, and

heading: Powers of receiver of wreck
paragraph: (iii) take the measures that the receiver specifies to determine the owner of the wreck, including giving notice that the wreck was reported, in the form and manner that the receiver considers appropriate; and

heading: Powers of receiver of wreck
paragraph: (c) take, or authorize any other person to take, the measures with respect to the wreck - other than selling, dismantling, destroying or otherwise disposing of it - that the receiver considers appropriate.

heading: Salvage award
paragraph: 59 (1) The following persons are entitled to a salvage award to be determined by the receiver of wreck:

heading: Salvage award
paragraph: (a) a person that took possession of a wreck and that was authorized to do so under paragraph 58(4)(a); and

heading: Salvage award
paragraph: (b) a person that reported a wreck under paragraph 58(1)(a) or (c).

heading: Nature of award
paragraph: (2) The salvage award may consist of the wreck, part of the wreck or all or part of the proceeds of its disposition.

heading: Reimbursement of costs and expenses
paragraph: (3) A person that has complied with a direction given to them under subparagraph 58(4)(b)(iii) or that has taken a measure under paragraph 58(4)(c) is entitled to the reimbursement of any costs and expenses incurred by them in doing so from the person that pays them under paragraph 61(d) or, if no payment is made under that paragraph, from the receiver of wreck.

heading: Prohibition - selling, dismantling, etc.
paragraph: 60 (1) Except as authorized under this Part, it is prohibited for a person to sell, dismantle, destroy or otherwise dispose of a wreck that was required to be reported under subsection 58(1).

heading: Prohibition - concealing or disguising
paragraph: (2) It is prohibited for a person to conceal a wreck, or use any means to disguise or conceal the fact that anything is a wreck, if the person knows that it has not been reported to a receiver of wreck under subsection 58(1).

heading: Claim to wreck
paragraph: 61 A receiver of wreck must release a wreck or pay the proceeds of its disposition under subsection 63(1) to a person that claims ownership of the wreck and that

heading: Claim to wreck
paragraph: (a) submits, in the form and manner specified by the Minister, a claim to the receiver within 30 days after the day on which notice was given under paragraph 63(1)(a);

heading: Claim to wreck
paragraph: (b) establishes their claim to the satisfaction of the receiver;

heading: Claim to wreck
paragraph: (c) pays to the receiver the receiver's costs and expenses and the prescribed fees;

heading: Claim to wreck
paragraph: (d) pays to the person entitled to a reimbursement under subsection 59(3) the costs and expenses referred to in that subsection; and

heading: Claim to wreck
paragraph: (e) pays to the person entitled to the salvage award under subsection 59(1) the salvage award determined by the receiver.

heading: Interpleader in case of wreck
paragraph: 62 (1) If two or more persons claim a wreck or proceeds of the disposition of a wreck, or if a person disputes the amount or value of the salvage award determined by the receiver of wreck, any court having jurisdiction in civil matters to the value or amount in question may hear and determine the matter.

heading: Maximum award
paragraph: (2) A salvage award that a court makes under subsection (1) must not exceed the value of the wreck.

heading: When wrecks may be disposed of
paragraph: 63 (1) A receiver of wreck may sell, dismantle, destroy or otherwise dispose of a wreck that was the subject of a report referred to in subsection 58(1), or authorize its disposition, only if

heading: When wrecks may be disposed of
paragraph: (a) 30 days have elapsed after the day on which notice was given that the wreck was reported; or

heading: When wrecks may be disposed of
paragraph: (b) in the opinion of the receiver, the wreck is likely to deteriorate rapidly.

heading: Proceeds held by receiver of wreck
paragraph: (2) The proceeds, if any, of a disposition under subsection (1) must be held by the receiver of wreck for not less than 30 days after the day on which the disposition occurred.

heading: Payment to Receiver General
paragraph: (3) The proceeds of a disposition under subsection (1) must be paid, less the amounts described in paragraphs 61(c) to (e), to the Receiver General

heading: Payment to Receiver General
paragraph: (a) if no claim has been submitted in accordance with paragraph 61(a); or

heading: Payment to Receiver General
paragraph: (b) if a claim to the wreck has not been established within the period that the receiver of wreck considers appropriate.

heading: Consent not required
paragraph: 64 A person that has been awarded all or part of a wreck under section 59 or that obtains a wreck under section 63 is not required to obtain the consent of its owner to register it as a vessel or obtain a pleasure craft licence for it under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

heading: Unpaid salvage award, fees, etc.
paragraph: 65 If a person has established a claim to a wreck, but has not paid the salvage award or the costs and expenses described in paragraphs 61(c) to (e) within 30 days after the day on which the receiver of wreck notified the person that the amounts were due, the receiver may sell, dismantle, destroy or otherwise dispose of all or part of the wreck and, if it is disposed of, must pay, from the proceeds of the disposition, the expenses of the disposition and the award and the costs and expenses described in paragraphs 61(c) to (e), and release whatever remains of the wreck and pay any amount that remains from the proceeds to that person.

heading: Prosecutions or violations
paragraph: 66 In any proceeding related to a contravention of this Part, it is not necessary to identify the wreck as the property of a particular person or as coming from a particular vessel.

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - authority to enter
paragraph: 67 (1) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, in exercising the powers referred to in sections 21, 22 and 36 or for the purposes of determining whether a vessel or wreck poses, or may pose, a hazard, enter a place, including a vessel or wreck.

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, in exercising those powers or for that purpose,

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (a) examine the place and anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (b) use any means of communication or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (c) use any computer system or data processing system, or cause it to be used, to examine data contained in or available to it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (d) prepare or cause to be prepared any record, in the form of a printout or other intelligible output, from the data;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (e) direct any person to produce for inspection, or for the purposes of making copies or taking extracts, any document;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (f) use any copying equipment or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (g) conduct tests or analyses;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (h) take measurements or samples;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (i) take photographs or make recordings or sketches;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (j) remove anything for the purposes of examination, testing or copying;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (k) direct any person to put anything into operation or to cease operating it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (l) prohibit or limit access to all or part of the place or to anything in the place; and

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (m) direct any person to establish their identity to his or her satisfaction.

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (3) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, in exercising the powers referred to in sections 21, 22 and 36 or for the purposes of determining whether a vessel or wreck poses, or may pose, a hazard, may

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (a) direct any person to provide any information; and

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (b) direct the vessel, if it is about to enter or is within Canadian waters or in the exclusive economic zone of Canada,

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (i) to stop,

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (ii) to provide any information,

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (iii) to proceed through those waters or to the place that he or she may specify within those waters, by the route and in the manner that he or she may specify, and to moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that he or she may specify,

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (iv) to proceed out of those waters, by the route and in the manner that he or she may specify, or

heading: Minister of Fisheries and Oceans - other powers
paragraph: (v) to remain outside those waters.

heading: Emergency zone
paragraph: (4) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may, if he or she has reasonable grounds to believe that a vessel or wreck poses a hazard that is grave and imminent, declare an emergency zone, the size of which is reasonable with regard to the seriousness of the situation, and

heading: Emergency zone
paragraph: (a) direct any vessel within that emergency zone to report its position to him or her;

heading: Emergency zone
paragraph: (b) direct any person or vessel to leave or not to enter the emergency zone or any vessel not to leave the emergency zone; and

heading: Emergency zone
paragraph: (c) direct any vessel within the emergency zone in respect of routes, speed limits and pilotage and equipment requirements.

heading: Exclusive economic zone
paragraph: (5) Every power that may be exercised in Canada under this section may be exercised in the exclusive economic zone of Canada.

heading: Disposition of samples
paragraph: 68 (1) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may dispose of a sample taken under paragraph 67(2)(h) in any manner that he or she considers appropriate or may submit it for analysis or examination to any person that he or she considers appropriate.

heading: Certificate or report
paragraph: (2) A person that has made an analysis or examination under subsection (1) may issue a certificate or report that sets out the results of the analysis or examination.

heading: Return of anything removed
paragraph: 69 (1) Anything removed under paragraph 67(2)(j) must be returned as soon as feasible after it is no longer required for the purpose for which it was taken unless

heading: Return of anything removed
paragraph: (a) the thing, in the opinion of the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, is no longer useful; or

heading: Return of anything removed
paragraph: (b) the owner is unknown or cannot be located.

heading: Thing not returned
paragraph: (2) The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may dispose of anything that is not returned under subsection (1), in the manner that he or she considers appropriate, and any proceeds realized from the disposition are to be paid to the Receiver General.

heading: Interference
paragraph: 70 Unless authorized by the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, it is prohibited for a person to knowingly move, alter or interfere in any way with a sample taken under paragraph 67(2)(h) or anything removed under paragraph 67(2)(j).

heading: Designation by Minister
paragraph: 71 The Minister may designate persons or classes of persons as enforcement officers for the purposes of the administration and enforcement of all or part of this Act - other than subsection 19(1), section 20, subsection 21(1), paragraph 36(c), subsection 37(1), paragraphs 67(2)(e), (k) and (m), subsections 67(3) and (4) and section 70 - and may limit in any manner that he or she considers appropriate the powers that the officers may exercise under this Act.

heading: Designation by Minister of Fisheries and Oceans
paragraph: 72 The Minister of Fisheries and Oceans may designate persons or classes of persons as enforcement officers for the purposes of the administration and enforcement of all or part of subsection 19(1), section 20, subsection 21(1), paragraph 36(c), subsection 37(1), paragraphs 37(3)(c), 67(2)(e), (k) and (m), subsections 67(3) and (4) and sections 70, 87 and 88 and may limit in any manner that he or she considers appropriate the powers that the officers may exercise under this Act.

heading: Certificate of designation
paragraph: 73 The Minister or the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, as the case may be, must provide every enforcement officer with a certificate of their designation and, if the officer's powers are limited under section 71 or 72, the certificate must specify the powers that the officer may exercise.

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: 74 (1) An enforcement officer may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Act, enter a place, including a vessel or wreck, in which the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: (a) there is anything to which this Act applies;

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: (b) there has been carried on, is being carried on or is likely to be carried on any activity in respect of which this Act applies; or

heading: Authority to enter
paragraph: (c) there is any book, record, electronic data or other document relating to the application of this Act.

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (2) The enforcement officer may, for that purpose,

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (a) examine the place and anything in the place;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (b) use any means of communication or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (c) use any computer system or data processing system, or cause it to be used, to examine data contained in or available to it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (d) prepare or cause to be prepared any record, in the form of a printout or other intelligible output, from the data;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (e) direct any person to produce for inspection, or for the purposes of making copies or taking extracts, any document;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (f) use any copying equipment or cause it to be used;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (g) conduct tests or analyses;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (h) take measurements or samples;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (i) take photographs or make recordings or sketches;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (j) remove anything for the purposes of examination, testing or copying;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (k) direct any person to put anything into operation or to cease operating it;

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (l) prohibit or limit access to all or part of the place or to anything in the place; and

heading: Powers on entry
paragraph: (m) direct any person to establish their identity to the enforcement officer's satisfaction.

heading: Powers - direction to provide information
paragraph: (3) An enforcement officer may, for a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Act,

heading: Powers - direction to provide information
paragraph: (a) direct any person to provide any information; and

heading: Powers - direction to provide information
paragraph: (b) direct a vessel, if it is about to enter or is within Canadian waters or in the exclusive economic zone of Canada, to provide any information.

heading: Powers - direction to vessel
paragraph: (4) If an enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to believe that an offence under this Act has been committed, they may direct a vessel that is about to enter or is within Canadian waters or in the exclusive economic zone of Canada

heading: Powers - direction to vessel
paragraph: (a) to stop;

heading: Powers - direction to vessel
paragraph: (b) to proceed through those waters or to the place within those waters that they may specify, by the route and in the manner that they may specify, and to moor, anchor or remain there for any reasonable period that they may specify;

heading: Powers - direction to vessel
paragraph: (c) to proceed out of those waters, by the route and in the manner that they may specify; or

heading: Powers - direction to vessel
paragraph: (d) to remain outside those waters.

heading: Exclusive economic zone
paragraph: (5) Every power that may be exercised in Canada under this section may be exercised in the exclusive economic zone of Canada.

heading: Entering living quarters
paragraph: 75 (1) An enforcement officer must not enter living quarters under subsection 74(1) without the consent of the occupant except under the authority of a warrant issued under subsection (2), unless they have reasonable grounds to believe that the living quarters are not being lived in or are located on an abandoned vessel.

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (2) On ex parte application, a justice of the peace may issue a warrant authorizing an enforcement officer to enter living quarters, subject to any conditions that may be specified in the warrant, if the justice is satisfied by information on oath that

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (a) the living quarters are a place referred to in subsection 74(1);

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (b) entry to the living quarters is necessary for a purpose related to verifying compliance or preventing non-compliance with this Act; and

heading: Authority to issue warrant
paragraph: (c) entry was refused by the occupant or there are reasonable grounds to believe that entry will be refused by, or that consent to entry cannot be obtained from, the occupant.

heading: Use of force
paragraph: (3) In executing a warrant to enter living quarters, an enforcement officer may use force only if the use of force has been specifically authorized in the warrant and they are accompanied by a peace officer.

heading: Means of telecommunication
paragraph: (4) An application for a warrant under subsection (2) may be submitted, and the warrant may be issued, by a means of telecommunication and section 487.1 of the Criminal Code applies for those purposes with any necessary modifications.

heading: Disposition of samples
paragraph: 76 (1) An enforcement officer who takes a sample under paragraph 74(2)(h) may dispose of it in any manner that they consider appropriate or may submit it for analysis or examination to any person the Minister considers appropriate.

heading: Certificate or report
paragraph: (2) A person that has made an analysis or examination under subsection (1) may issue a certificate or report that sets out the results of the analysis or examination.

heading: Certificate or report admissible in evidence
paragraph: (3) Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the certificate or report is admissible in evidence in any proceeding related to a contravention of this Act and, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, is proof of the statements contained in it without proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have signed it.

heading: Attendance of person
paragraph: (4) The party against whom the certificate or report is produced may, with leave of the court or of the Transportation Appeal Tribunal, require for the purposes of cross-examination the attendance of the person that issued it.

heading: Notice
paragraph: (5) The certificate or report may be admitted in evidence only if the party who intends to produce it has given to the party against whom it is intended to be produced reasonable notice of that intention, together with a copy of the certificate or report.

heading: Return of anything removed
