heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2)Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007
paragraph: THE STATES PARTIES TO THE PRESENT CONVENTION,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2)Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007
paragraph: CONSCIOUS of the fact that wrecks, if not removed, may pose a hazard to navigation or the marine environment,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2)Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007
paragraph: CONVINCED of the need to adopt uniform international rules and procedures to ensure the prompt and effective removal of wrecks and payment of compensation for the costs therein involved,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2)Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007
paragraph: NOTING that many wrecks may be located in States' territory, including the territorial sea,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2)Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007
paragraph: RECOGNIZING the benefits to be gained through uniformity in legal regimes governing responsibility and liability for removal of hazardous wrecks,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2)Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007
paragraph: BEARING IN MIND the importance of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, done at Montego Bay on 10 December 1982, and of the customary international law of the sea, and the consequent need to implement the present Convention in accordance with such provisions,

heading: SCHEDULE 1(Section 2)Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007
paragraph: HAVE AGREED as follows:

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: For the purposes of this Convention:

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 1 Convention area means the exclusive economic zone of a State Party, established in accordance with international law or, if a State Party has not established such a zone, an area beyond and adjacent to the territorial sea of that State determined by that State in accordance with international law and extending not more than 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of its territorial sea is measured.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 2 Ship means a seagoing vessel of any type whatsoever and includes hydrofoil boats, air-cushion vehicles, submersibles, floating craft and floating platforms, except when such platforms are on location engaged in the exploration, exploitation or production of seabed mineral resources.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 3 Maritime casualty means a collision of ships, stranding or other incident of navigation, or other occurrence on board a ship or external to it, resulting in material damage or imminent threat of material damage to a ship or its cargo.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 4 Wreck, following upon a maritime casualty, means:

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (a) a sunken or stranded ship; or

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (b) any part of a sunken or stranded ship, including any object that is or has been on board such a ship; or

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (c) any object that is lost at sea from a ship and that is stranded, sunken or adrift at sea; or

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (d) a ship that is about, or may reasonably be expected, to sink or to strand, where effective measures to assist the ship or any property in danger are not already being taken.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 5 Hazard means any condition or threat that:

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (a) poses a danger or impediment to navigation; or

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (b) may reasonably be expected to result in major harmful consequences to the marine environment, or damage to the coastline or related interests of one or more States.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 6 Related interests means the interests of a coastal State directly affected or threatened by a wreck, such as:

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (a) maritime coastal, port and estuarine activities, including fisheries activities, constituting an essential means of livelihood of the persons concerned;

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (b) tourist attractions and other economic interests of the area concerned;

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (c) the health of the coastal population and the wellbeing of the area concerned, including conservation of marine living resources and of wildlife; and

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (d) offshore and underwater infrastructure.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 7 Removal means any form of prevention, mitigation or elimination of the hazard created by a wreck. "Remove", "removed" and "removing" shall be construed accordingly.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 8 Registered owner means the person or persons registered as the owner of the ship or, in the absence of registration, the person or persons owning the ship at the time of the maritime casualty. However, in the case of a ship owned by a State and operated by a company which in that State is registered as the operator of the ship, "registered owner" shall mean such company.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 9 Operator of the ship means the owner of the ship or any other organization or person such as the manager, or the bareboat charterer, who has assumed the responsibility for operation of the ship from the owner of the ship and who, on assuming such responsibility, has agreed to take over all duties and responsibilities established under the International Safety Management Code, as amended.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 10 Affected State means the State in whose Convention area the wreck is located.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 11 State of the ship's registry means, in relation to a registered ship, the State of registration of the ship and, in relation to an unregistered ship, the State whose flag the ship is entitled to fly.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 12 Organization means the International Maritime Organization.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: 13 Secretary-General means the Secretary-General of the Organization.

heading: ARTICLE 2Objectives and general principles
paragraph: 1 A State Party may take measures in accordance with this Convention in relation to the removal of a wreck which poses a hazard in the Convention area.

heading: ARTICLE 2Objectives and general principles
paragraph: 2 Measures taken by the Affected State in accordance with paragraph 1 shall be proportionate to the hazard.

heading: ARTICLE 2Objectives and general principles
paragraph: 3 Such measures shall not go beyond what is reasonably necessary to remove a wreck which poses a hazard and shall cease as soon as the wreck has been removed; they shall not unnecessarily interfere with the rights and interests of other States including the State of the ship's registry, and of any person, physical or corporate, concerned.

heading: ARTICLE 2Objectives and general principles
paragraph: 4 The application of this Convention within the Convention area shall not entitle a State Party to claim or exercise sovereignty or sovereign rights over any part of the high seas.

heading: ARTICLE 2Objectives and general principles
paragraph: 5 States Parties shall endeavour to co-operate when the effects of a maritime casualty resulting in a wreck involve a State other than the Affected State.

heading: ARTICLE 3Scope of application
paragraph: 1 Except as otherwise provided in this Convention, this Convention shall apply to wrecks in the Convention area.

heading: ARTICLE 3Scope of application
paragraph: 2 A State Party may extend the application of this Convention to wrecks located within its territory, including the territorial sea, subject to Article 4, paragraph 4. In that case, it shall notify the Secretary-General accordingly, at the time of expressing its consent to be bound by this Convention or at any time thereafter. When a State Party has made a notification to apply this Convention to wrecks located within its territory, including the territorial sea, this is without prejudice to the rights and obligations of that State to take measures in relation to wrecks located in its territory, including the territorial sea, other than locating, marking and removing them in accordance with this Convention. The provisions of articles 10, 11 and 12 of this Convention shall not apply to any measures so taken other than those referred to in articles 7, 8 and 9 of this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 3Scope of application
paragraph: 3 When a State Party has made a notification under paragraph 2, the "Convention area" of the Affected State shall include the territory, including the territorial sea, of that State Party.

heading: ARTICLE 3Scope of application
paragraph: 4 A notification made under paragraph 2 above shall take effect for that State Party, if made before entry into force of this Convention for that State Party, upon entry into force. If notification is made after entry into force of this Convention for that State Party, it shall take effect six months after its receipt by the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 3Scope of application
paragraph: 5 A State Party that has made a notification under paragraph 2 may withdraw it at any time by means of a notification of withdrawal to the Secretary-General. Such notification of withdrawal shall take effect six months after its receipt by the Secretary-General, unless the notification specifies a later date.

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall not apply to measures taken under the International Convention relating to Intervention on the High Seas in Cases of Oil Pollution Casualties, 1969, as amended, or the Protocol relating to Intervention on the High Seas in Cases of Pollution by Substances other than Oil, 1973, as amended.

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: 2 This Convention shall not apply to any warship or other ship owned or operated by a State and used, for the time being, only on Government non-commercial service, unless that State decides otherwise.

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: 3 Where a State Party decides to apply this Convention to its warships or other ships as described in paragraph 2, it shall notify the Secretary-General, thereof, specifying the terms and conditions of such application.

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: 4 (a) When a State Party has made a notification under article 3, paragraph 2, the following provisions of this Convention shall not apply in its territory, including the territorial sea:

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: (i) Article 2, paragraph 4;

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: (ii) Article 9, paragraphs 1, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10; and

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: (iii) Article 15.

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: (b) Article 9, paragraph 4, insofar as it applies to the territory, including the territorial sea of a State Party, shall read:

heading: ARTICLE 4Exclusions
paragraph: Subject to the national law of the Affected State, the registered owner may contract with any salvor or other person to remove the wreck determined to constitute a hazard on behalf of the owner. Before such removal commences, the Affected State may lay down conditions for such removal only to the extent necessary to ensure that the removal proceeds in a manner that is consistent with considerations of safety and protection of the marine environment.

heading: ARTICLE 5Reporting wrecks
paragraph: 1 A State Party shall require the master and the operator of a ship flying its flag to report to the Affected State without delay when that ship has been involved in a maritime casualty resulting in a wreck. To the extent that the reporting obligation under this article has been fulfilled either by the master or the operator of the ship, the other shall not be obliged to report.

heading: ARTICLE 5Reporting wrecks
paragraph: 2 Such reports shall provide the name and the principal place of business of the registered owner and all the relevant information necessary for the Affected State to determine whether the wreck poses a hazard in accordance with article 6, including:

heading: ARTICLE 5Reporting wrecks
paragraph: (a) the precise location of the wreck;

heading: ARTICLE 5Reporting wrecks
paragraph: (b) the type, size and construction of the wreck;

heading: ARTICLE 5Reporting wrecks
paragraph: (c) the nature of the damage to, and the condition of, the wreck;

heading: ARTICLE 5Reporting wrecks
paragraph: (d) the nature and quantity of the cargo, in particular any hazardous and noxious substances; and

heading: ARTICLE 5Reporting wrecks
paragraph: (e) the amount and types of oil, including bunker oil and lubricating oil, on board.

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: When determining whether a wreck poses a hazard, the following criteria should be taken into account by the Affected State:

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (a) the type, size and construction of the wreck;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (b) depth of the water in the area;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (c) tidal range and currents in the area;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (d) particularly sensitive sea areas identified and, as appropriate, designated in accordance with guidelines adopted by the Organization, or a clearly defined area of the exclusive economic zone where special mandatory measures have been adopted pursuant to article 211, paragraph 6, of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (e) proximity of shipping routes or established traffic lanes;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (f) traffic density and frequency;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (g) type of traffic;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (h) nature and quantity of the wreck's cargo, the amount and types of oil (such as bunker oil and lubricating oil) on board the wreck and, in particular, the damage likely to result should the cargo or oil be released into the marine environment;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (i) vulnerability of port facilities;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (j) prevailing meteorological and hydrographical conditions;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (k) submarine topography of the area;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (l) height of the wreck above or below the surface of the water at lowest astronomical tide;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (m) acoustic and magnetic profiles of the wreck;

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (n) proximity of offshore installations, pipelines, telecommunications cables and similar structures; and

heading: ARTICLE 6Determination of hazard
paragraph: (o) any other circumstances that might necessitate the removal of the wreck.

heading: ARTICLE 7Locating wrecks
paragraph: 1 Upon becoming aware of a wreck, the Affected State shall use all practicable means, including the good offices of States and organizations, to warn mariners and the States concerned of the nature and location of the wreck as a matter of urgency.

heading: ARTICLE 7Locating wrecks
paragraph: 2 If the Affected State has reason to believe that a wreck poses a hazard, it shall ensure that all practicable steps are taken to establish the precise location of the wreck.

heading: ARTICLE 8Marking of wrecks
paragraph: 1 If the Affected State determines that a wreck constitutes a hazard, that State shall ensure that all reasonable steps are taken to mark the wreck.

heading: ARTICLE 8Marking of wrecks
paragraph: 2 In marking the wreck, all practicable steps shall be taken to ensure that the markings conform to the internationally accepted system of buoyage in use in the area where the wreck is located.

heading: ARTICLE 8Marking of wrecks
paragraph: 3 The Affected State shall promulgate the particulars of the marking of the wreck by use of all appropriate means, including the appropriate nautical publications.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 1 If the Affected State determines that a wreck constitutes a hazard, that State shall immediately:

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: (a) inform the State of the ship's registry and the registered owner; and

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: (b) proceed to consult the State of the ship's registry and other States affected by the wreck regarding measures to be taken in relation to the wreck.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 2 The registered owner shall remove a wreck determined to constitute a hazard.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 3 When a wreck has been determined to constitute a hazard, the registered owner, or other interested party, shall provide the competent authority of the Affected State with evidence of insurance or other financial security as required by article 12.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 4 The registered owner may contract with any salvor or other person to remove the wreck determined to constitute a hazard on behalf of the owner. Before such removal commences, the Affected State may lay down conditions for such removal only to the extent necessary to ensure that the removal proceeds in a manner that is consistent with considerations of safety and protection of the marine environment.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 5 When the removal referred to in paragraphs 2 and 4 has commenced, the Affected State may intervene in the removal only to the extent necessary to ensure that the removal proceeds effectively in a manner that is consistent with considerations of safety and protection of the marine environment.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 6 The Affected State shall:

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: (a) set a reasonable deadline within which the registered owner must remove the wreck, taking into account the nature of the hazard determined in accordance with article 6;

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: (b) inform the registered owner in writing of the deadline it has set and specify that, if the registered owner does not remove the wreck within that deadline, it may remove the wreck at the registered owner's expense; and

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: (c) inform the registered owner in writing that it intends to intervene immediately in circumstances where the hazard becomes particularly severe.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 7 If the registered owner does not remove the wreck within the deadline set in accordance with paragraph 6(a), or the registered owner cannot be contacted, the Affected State may remove the wreck by the most practical and expeditious means available, consistent with considerations of safety and protection of the marine environment.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 8 In circumstances where immediate action is required and the Affected State has informed the State of the ship's registry and the registered owner accordingly, it may remove the wreck by the most practical and expeditious means available, consistent with considerations of safety and protection of the marine environment.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 9 States Parties shall take appropriate measures under their national law to ensure that their registered owners comply with paragraphs 2 and 3.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 10 States Parties give their consent to the Affected State to act under paragraphs 4 to 8, where required.

heading: ARTICLE 9Measures to facilitate the removal of wrecks
paragraph: 11 The information referred to in this article shall be provided by the Affected State to the registered owner identified in the reports referred to in article 5, paragraph 2.

heading: ARTICLE 10Liability of the owner
paragraph: 1 Subject to article 11, the registered owner shall be liable for the costs of locating, marking and removing the wreck under articles 7, 8 and 9, respectively, unless the registered owner proves that the maritime casualty that caused the wreck:

heading: ARTICLE 10Liability of the owner
paragraph: (a) resulted from an act of war, hostilities, civil war, insurrection, or a natural phenomenon of an exceptional, inevitable and irresistible character;

heading: ARTICLE 10Liability of the owner
paragraph: (b) was wholly caused by an act or omission done with intent to cause damage by a third party; or

heading: ARTICLE 10Liability of the owner
paragraph: (c) was wholly caused by the negligence or other wrongful act of any Government or other authority responsible for the maintenance of lights or other navigational aids in the exercise of that function.

heading: ARTICLE 10Liability of the owner
paragraph: 2 Nothing in this Convention shall affect the right of the registered owner to limit liability under any applicable national or international regime, such as the Convention on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims, 1976, as amended.

heading: ARTICLE 10Liability of the owner
paragraph: 3 No claim for the costs referred to in paragraph 1 may be made against the registered owner otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of this Convention. This is without prejudice to the rights and obligations of a State Party that has made a notification under article 3, paragraph 2, in relation to wrecks located in its territory, including the territorial sea, other than locating, marking and removing in accordance with this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 10Liability of the owner
paragraph: 4 Nothing in this article shall prejudice any right of recourse against third parties.

heading: ARTICLE 11Exceptions to liability
paragraph: 1 The registered owner shall not be liable under this Convention for the costs mentioned in article 10, paragraph 1 if, and to the extent that, liability for such costs would be in conflict with:

heading: ARTICLE 11Exceptions to liability
paragraph: (a) the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage, 1969, as amended;

heading: ARTICLE 11Exceptions to liability
paragraph: (b) the International Convention on Liability and Compensation for Damage in Connection with the Carriage of Hazardous and Noxious Substances by Sea, 1996, as amended;

heading: ARTICLE 11Exceptions to liability
paragraph: (c) the Convention on Third Party Liability in the Field of Nuclear Energy, 1960, as amended, or the Vienna Convention on Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage, 1963, as amended; or national law governing or prohibiting limitation of liability for nuclear damage; or

heading: ARTICLE 11Exceptions to liability
paragraph: (d) the International Convention on Civil Liability for Bunker Oil Pollution Damage, 2001, as amended;

heading: ARTICLE 11Exceptions to liability
paragraph: provided that the relevant convention is applicable and in force.

heading: ARTICLE 11Exceptions to liability
paragraph: 2 To the extent that measures under this Convention are considered to be salvage under applicable national law or an international convention, such law or convention shall apply to questions of the remuneration or compensation payable to salvors to the exclusion of the rules of this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 1 The registered owner of a ship of 300 gross tonnage and above and flying the flag of a State Party shall be required to maintain insurance or other financial security, such as a guarantee of a bank or similar institution, to cover liability under this Convention in an amount equal to the limits of liability under the applicable national or international limitation regime, but in all cases not exceeding an amount calculated in accordance with article 6(1)(b) of the Convention on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims, 1976, as amended.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 2 A certificate attesting that insurance or other financial security is in force in accordance with the provisions of this Convention shall be issued to each ship of 300 gross tonnage and above by the appropriate authority of the State of the ship's registry after determining that the requirements of paragraph 1 have been complied with. With respect to a ship registered in a State Party, such certificate shall be issued or certified by the appropriate authority of the State of the ship's registry; with respect to a ship not registered in a State Party it may be issued or certified by the appropriate authority of any State Party. This compulsory insurance certificate shall be in the form of the model set out in the annex to this Convention, and shall contain the following particulars:

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (a) name of the ship, distinctive number or letters and port of registry;

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (b) gross tonnage of the ship;

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (c) name and principal place of business of the registered owner;

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (d) IMO ship identification number;

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (e) type and duration of security;

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (f) name and principal place of business of insurer or other person giving security and, where appropriate, place of business where the insurance or security is established; and

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (g) period of validity of the certificate, which shall not be longer than the period of validity of the insurance or other security.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 3 (a) A State Party may authorize either an institution or an organization recognized by it to issue the certificate referred to in paragraph 2. Such institution or organization shall inform that State of the issue of each certificate. In all cases, the State Party shall fully guarantee the completeness and accuracy of the certificate so issued and shall undertake to ensure the necessary arrangements to satisfy this obligation.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (b) A State Party shall notify the Secretary-General of:

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (i) the specific responsibilities and conditions of the authority delegated to an institution or organization recognized by it;

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (ii) the withdrawal of such authority; and

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (iii) the date from which such authority or withdrawal of such authority takes effect.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: An authority delegated shall not take effect prior to three months from the date on which notification to that effect was given to the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: (c) The institution or organization authorized to issue certificates in accordance with this paragraph shall, as a minimum, be authorized to withdraw these certificates if the conditions under which they have been issued are not maintained. In all cases the institution or organization shall report such withdrawal to the State on whose behalf the certificate was issued.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 4 The certificate shall be in the official language or languages of the issuing State. If the language used is not English, French or Spanish, the text shall include a translation into one of these languages and, where the State so decides, the official language(s) of the State may be omitted.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 5 The certificate shall be carried on board the ship and a copy shall be deposited with the authorities who keep the record of the ship's registry or, if the ship is not registered in a State Party, with the authorities issuing or certifying the certificate.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 6 An insurance or other financial security shall not satisfy the requirements of this article if it can cease for reasons other than the expiry of the period of validity of the insurance or security specified in the certificate under paragraph 2 before three months have elapsed from the date on which notice of its termination is given to the authorities referred to in paragraph 5 unless the certificate has been surrendered to these authorities or a new certificate has been issued within the said period. The foregoing provisions shall similarly apply to any modification, which results in the insurance or security no longer satisfying the requirements of this article.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 7 The State of the ship's registry shall, subject to the provisions of this article and having regard to any guidelines adopted by the Organization on the financial responsibility of the registered owners, determine the conditions of issue and validity of the certificate.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 8 Nothing in this Convention shall be construed as preventing a State Party from relying on information obtained from other States or the Organization or other international organizations relating to the financial standing of providers of insurance or financial security for the purposes of this Convention. In such cases, the State Party relying on such information is not relieved of its responsibility as a State issuing the certificate required by paragraph 2.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 9 Certificates issued and certified under the authority of a State Party shall be accepted by other States Parties for the purposes of this Convention and shall be regarded by other States Parties as having the same force as certificates issued or certified by them, even if issued or certified in respect of a ship not registered in a State Party. A State Party may at any time request consultation with the issuing or certifying State should it believe that the insurer or guarantor named in the certificate is not financially capable of meeting the obligations imposed by this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 10 Any claim for costs arising under this Convention may be brought directly against the insurer or other person providing financial security for the registered owner's liability. In such a case the defendant may invoke the defences (other than the bankruptcy or winding up of the registered owner) that the registered owner would have been entitled to invoke, including limitation of liability under any applicable national or international regime. Furthermore, even if the registered owner is not entitled to limit liability, the defendant may limit liability to an amount equal to the amount of the insurance or other financial security required to be maintained in accordance with paragraph 1. Moreover, the defendant may invoke the defence that the maritime casualty was caused by the wilful misconduct of the registered owner, but the defendant shall not invoke any other defence which the defendant might have been entitled to invoke in proceedings brought by the registered owner against the defendant. The defendant shall in any event have the right to require the registered owner to be joined in the proceedings.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 11 A State Party shall not permit any ship entitled to fly its flag to which this article applies to operate at any time unless a certificate has been issued under paragraphs 2 or 14.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 12 Subject to the provisions of this article, each State Party shall ensure, under its national law, that insurance or other security to the extent required by paragraph 1 is in force in respect of any ship of 300 gross tonnage and above, wherever registered, entering or leaving a port in its territory, or arriving at or leaving from an offshore facility in its territorial sea.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 13 Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 5, a State Party may notify the Secretary-General that, for the purposes of paragraph 12, ships are not required to carry on board or to produce the certificate required by paragraph 2, when entering or leaving a port in its territory, or arriving at or leaving from an offshore facility in its territorial sea, provided that the State Party which issues the certificate required by paragraph 2 has notified the Secretary-General that it maintains records in an electronic format, accessible to all States Parties, attesting the existence of the certificate and enabling States Parties to discharge their obligations under paragraph 12.

heading: ARTICLE 12Compulsory insurance or other financial security
paragraph: 14 If insurance or other financial security is not maintained in respect of a ship owned by a State Party, the provisions of this article relating thereto shall not be applicable to such ship, but the ship shall carry a certificate issued by the appropriate authority of the State of registry, stating that it is owned by that State and that the ship's liability is covered within the limits prescribed in paragraph 1. Such a certificate shall follow as closely as possible the model prescribed by paragraph 2.

heading: ARTICLE 13Time limits
paragraph: Rights to recover costs under this Convention shall be extinguished unless an action is brought hereunder within three years from the date when the hazard has been determined in accordance with this Convention. However, in no case shall an action be brought after six years from the date of the maritime casualty that resulted in the wreck. Where the maritime casualty consists of a series of occurrences, the six-year period shall run from the date of the first occurrence.

heading: ARTICLE 14Relationship to other conventions and international agreements
paragraph: 1 At the request of not less than one-third of States Parties, a conference shall be convened by the Organization for the purpose of revising or amending this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 14Relationship to other conventions and international agreements
paragraph: 2 Any consent to be bound by this Convention, expressed after the date of entry into force of an amendment to this Convention, shall be deemed to apply to this Convention, as amended.

heading: ARTICLE 15Settlement of disputes
paragraph: 1 Where a dispute arises between two or more States Parties regarding the interpretation or application of this Convention, they shall seek to resolve their dispute, in the first instance, through negotiation, enquiry, mediation, conciliation, arbitration, judicial settlement, resort to regional agencies or arrangements or other peaceful means of their choice.

heading: ARTICLE 15Settlement of disputes
paragraph: 2 If no settlement is possible within a reasonable period of time not exceeding twelve months after one State Party has notified another that a dispute exists between them, the provisions relating to the settlement of disputes set out in Part XV of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982, shall apply mutatis mutandis, whether or not the States party to the dispute are also States Parties to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982.

heading: ARTICLE 15Settlement of disputes
paragraph: 3 Any procedure chosen by a State Party to this Convention and to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982, pursuant to Article 287 of the latter, shall apply to the settlement of disputes under this article, unless that State Party, when ratifying, accepting, approving or acceding to this Convention, or at any time thereafter, chooses another procedure pursuant to Article 287 for the purpose of the settlement of disputes arising out of this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 15Settlement of disputes
paragraph: 4 A State Party to this Convention which is not a Party to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982, when ratifying, accepting, approving or acceding to this Convention or at any time thereafter shall be free to choose, by means of a written declaration, one or more of the means set out in Article 287, paragraph 1, of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982, for the purpose of settlement of disputes under this Article. Article 287 shall apply to such a declaration, as well as to any dispute to which such State is party, which is not covered by a declaration in force. For the purpose of conciliation and arbitration, in accordance with Annexes V and VII of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982, such State shall be entitled to nominate conciliators and arbitrators to be included in the lists referred to in Annex V, Article 2, and Annex VII, Article 2, for the settlement of disputes arising out of this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 15Settlement of disputes
paragraph: 5 A declaration made under paragraphs 3 and 4 shall be deposited with the Secretary-General, who shall transmit copies thereof to the States Parties.

heading: ARTICLE 16Relationship to other conventions and international agreements
paragraph: Nothing in this Convention shall prejudice the rights and obligations of any State under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982, and under the customary international law of the sea.

heading: ARTICLE 17Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall be open for signature at the Headquarters of the Organization from 19 November 2007 until 18 November 2008 and shall thereafter remain open for accession.

heading: ARTICLE 17Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (a) States may express their consent to be bound by this Convention by:

heading: ARTICLE 17Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (i) signature without reservation as to ratification, acceptance or approval; or

heading: ARTICLE 17Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (ii) signature subject to ratification, acceptance or approval, followed by ratification, acceptance or approval; or

heading: ARTICLE 17Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (iii) accession.

heading: ARTICLE 17Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (b) Ratification, acceptance, approval or accession shall be effected by the deposit of an instrument to that effect with the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 18Entry into force
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall enter into force twelve months following the date on which ten States have either signed it without reservation as to ratification, acceptance or approval or have deposited	instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession with the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 18Entry into force
paragraph: 2 For any State which ratifies, accepts, approves or accedes to this Convention after the conditions in paragraph 1 for entry into force have been met, this Convention shall enter into force three months following the date of deposit by such State of the appropriate instrument, but not before this Convention has entered into force in accordance with paragraph 1.

heading: ARTICLE 19Denunciation
paragraph: 1 This Convention may be denounced by a State Party at any time after the expiry of one year following the date on which this Convention comes into force for that State.

heading: ARTICLE 19Denunciation
paragraph: 2 Denunciation shall be effected by the deposit of an instrument to that effect with the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 19Denunciation
paragraph: 3 A denunciation shall take effect one year, or such longer period as may be specified in the instrument of denunciation, following its receipt by the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall be deposited with the Secretary General.

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: 2 The Secretary-General shall:

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: (a) inform all States which have signed or acceded to this Convention of:

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: (i) each new signature or deposit of an instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession, together with the date thereof;

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: (ii) the date of entry into force of this Convention;

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: (iii) the deposit of any instrument of denunciation of this Convention, together with the date of the deposit and the date on which the denunciation takes effect; and

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: (iv) other declarations and notifications received pursuant to this Convention;

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: (b) transmit certified true copies of this Convention to all States that have signed or acceded to this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 20Depositary
paragraph: 3 As soon as this Convention enters into force, a certified true copy of the text shall be transmitted by the Secretary-General to the Secretary-General of the United Nations, for registration and publication in accordance with Article 102 of the Charter of the United Nations.

heading: ARTICLE 21Languages
paragraph: This Convention is established in a single original in the Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish languages, each text being equally authentic.

heading: ARTICLE 21Languages
paragraph: DONE IN NAIROBI this eighteenth day of May two thousand and seven.

heading: ARTICLE 21Languages
paragraph: IN WITNESS WHEREOF the undersigned, being duly authorized by their respective Governments for that purpose, have signed this Convention.

heading: PART 1International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: THE STATES PARTIES TO THE PRESENT CONVENTION,

heading: PART 1International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: RECOGNIZING the desirability of determining by agreement uniform international rules regarding salvage operations,

heading: PART 1International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: NOTING that substantial developments, in particular the increased concern for the protection of the environment, have demonstrated the need to review the international rules presently contained in the Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules of Law relating to Assistance and Salvage at Sea, done at Brussels, 23 September 1910,

heading: PART 1International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: CONSCIOUS of the major contribution which efficient and timely salvage operations can make to the safety of vessels and other property in danger and to the protection of the environment,

heading: PART 1International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: CONVINCED of the need to ensure that adequate incentives are available to persons who undertake salvage operations in respect of vessels and other property in danger,

heading: PART 1International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: HAVE AGREED as follows:

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: For the purpose of this Convention:

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (a) Salvage operation means any act or activity undertaken to assist a vessel or any other property in danger in navigable waters or in any other waters whatsoever.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (b) Vessel means any ship or craft, or any structure capable of navigation.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (c) Property means any property not permanently and intentionally attached to the shoreline and includes freight at risk.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (d) Damage to the environment means substantial physical damage to human health or to marine life or resources in coastal or inland waters or areas adjacent thereto, caused by pollution, contamination, fire, explosion or similar major incidents.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (e) Payment means any reward, remuneration or compensation due under this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (f) Organization means the International Maritime Organization.

heading: ARTICLE 1Definitions
paragraph: (g) Secretary-General means the Secretary-General of the Organization.

heading: ARTICLE 2Application of the Convention
paragraph: This Convention shall apply whenever judicial or arbitral proceedings relating to matters dealt with in this Convention are brought in a State Party.

heading: ARTICLE 3Platforms and drilling units
paragraph: This Convention shall not apply to fixed or floating platforms or to mobile offshore drilling units when such platforms or units are on location engaged in the exploration, exploitation or production of sea-bed mineral resources.

heading: ARTICLE 4State-owned vessels
paragraph: 1 Without prejudice to article 5, this Convention shall not apply to warships or other non-commercial vessels owned or operated by a State and entitled, at the time of salvage operations, to sovereign immunity under generally recognized principles of international law unless that State decides otherwise.

heading: ARTICLE 4State-owned vessels
paragraph: 2 Where a State Party decides to apply the Convention to its warships or other vessels described in paragraph 1, it shall notify the Secretary-General thereof specifying the terms and conditions of such application.

heading: ARTICLE 5Salvage operations controlled by public authorities
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall not affect any provisions of national law or any international convention relating to salvage operations by or under the control of public authorities.

heading: ARTICLE 5Salvage operations controlled by public authorities
paragraph: 2 Nevertheless, salvors carrying out such salvage operations shall be entitled to avail themselves of the rights and remedies provided for in this Convention in respect of salvage operations.

heading: ARTICLE 5Salvage operations controlled by public authorities
paragraph: 3 The extent to which a public authority under a duty to perform salvage operations may avail itself of the rights and remedies provided for in this Convention shall be determined by the law of the State where such authority is situated.

heading: ARTICLE 6Salvage contracts
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall apply to any salvage operations save to the extent that a contract otherwise provides expressly or by implication.

heading: ARTICLE 6Salvage contracts
paragraph: 2 The master shall have the authority to conclude contracts for salvage operations on behalf of the owner of the vessel. The master or the owner of the vessel shall have the authority to conclude such contracts on behalf of the owner of the property on board the vessel.

heading: ARTICLE 6Salvage contracts
paragraph: 3 Nothing in this article shall affect the application of article 7 nor duties to prevent or minimize damage to the environment.

heading: ARTICLE 7Annulment and modification of contracts
paragraph: A contract or any terms thereof may be annulled or modified if:

heading: ARTICLE 7Annulment and modification of contracts
paragraph: (a) the contract has been entered into under undue influence or the influence of danger and its terms are inequitable; or

heading: ARTICLE 7Annulment and modification of contracts
paragraph: (b) the payment under the contract is in an excessive degree too large or too small for the services actually rendered.

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: 1 The salvor shall owe a duty to the owner of the vessel or other property in danger:

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: (a) to carry out the salvage operations with due care;

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: (b) in performing the duty specified in subparagraph (a), to exercise due care to prevent or minimize damage to the environment;

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: (c) whenever circumstances reasonably require, to seek assistance from other salvors; and

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: (d) to accept the intervention of other salvors when reasonably requested to do so by the owner or master of the vessel or other property in danger; provided however that the amount of his reward shall not be prejudiced should it be found that such a request was unreasonable.

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: 2 The owner and master of the vessel or the owner of other property in danger shall owe a duty to the salvor:

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: (a) to co-operate fully with him during the course of the salvage operations;

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: (b) in so doing, to exercise due care to prevent or minimize damage to the environment; and

heading: ARTICLE 8Duties of the salvor and of the owner and master
paragraph: (c) when the vessel or other property has been brought to a place of safety, to accept redelivery when reasonably requested by the salvor to do so.

heading: ARTICLE 9Rights of coastal States
paragraph: Nothing in this Convention shall affect the right of the coastal State concerned to take measures in accordance with generally recognized principles of international law to protect its coastline or related interests from pollution or the threat of pollution following upon a maritime casualty or acts relating to such a casualty which may reasonably be expected to result in major harmful consequences, including the right of a coastal State to give directions in relation to salvage operations.

heading: ARTICLE 10Duty to render assistance
paragraph: 1 Every master is bound, so far as he can do so without serious danger to his vessel and persons thereon, to render assistance to any person in danger of being lost at sea.

heading: ARTICLE 10Duty to render assistance
paragraph: 2 The States Parties shall adopt the measures necessary to enforce the duty set out in paragraph 1.

heading: ARTICLE 10Duty to render assistance
paragraph: 3 The owner of the vessel shall incur no liability for a breach of the duty of the master under paragraph 1.

heading: ARTICLE 11Co-operation
paragraph: A State Party shall, whenever regulating or deciding upon matters relating to salvage operations such as admittance to ports of vessels in distress or the provisions of facilities to salvors, take into account the need for co-operation between salvors, other interested parties and public authorities in order to ensure the efficient and successful performance of salvage operations for the purpose of saving life or property in danger as well as preventing damage to the environment in general.

heading: ARTICLE 12Conditions for reward
paragraph: 1 Salvage operations which have had a useful result give right to a reward.

heading: ARTICLE 12Conditions for reward
paragraph: 2 Except as otherwise provided, no payment is due under this Convention if the salvage operations have had no useful result.

heading: ARTICLE 12Conditions for reward
paragraph: 3 This chapter shall apply, notwithstanding that the salved vessel and the vessel undertaking the salvage operations belong to the same owner.

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: 1 The reward shall be fixed with a view to encouraging salvage operations, taking into account the following criteria without regard to the order in which they are presented below:

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (a) the salved value of the vessel and other property;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (b) the skill and efforts of the salvors in preventing or minimizing damage to the environment;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (c) the measure of success obtained by the salvor;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (d) the nature and degree of the danger;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (e) the skill and efforts of the salvors in salving the vessel, other property and life;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (f) the time used and expenses and losses incurred by the salvors;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (g) the risk of liability and other risks run by the salvors or their equipment;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (h) the promptness of the services rendered;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (i) the availability and use of vessels or other equipment intended for salvage operations;

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: (j) the state of readiness and efficiency of the salvor's equipment and the value thereof.

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: 2 Payment of a reward fixed according to paragraph 1 shall be made by all of the vessel and other property interests in proportion to their respective salved values. However, a State Party may in its national law provide that the payment of a reward has to be made by one of these interests, subject to a right of recourse of this interest against the other interests for their respective shares. Nothing in this article shall prevent any right of defence.

heading: ARTICLE 13Criteria for fixing the reward
paragraph: 3 The rewards, exclusive of any interest and recoverable legal costs that may be payable thereon, shall not exceed the salved value of the vessel and other property.

heading: ARTICLE 14Special compensation
paragraph: 1 If the salvor has carried out salvage operations in respect of a vessel which by itself or its cargo threatened damage to the environment and has failed to earn a reward under article 13 at least equivalent to the special compensation assessable in accordance with this article, he shall be entitled to special compensation from the owner of that vessel equivalent to his expenses as herein defined.

heading: ARTICLE 14Special compensation
paragraph: 2 If, in the circumstances set out in paragraph 1, the salvor by his salvage operations has prevented or minimized damage to the environment, the special compensation payable by the owner to the salvor under paragraph 1 may be increased up to a maximum of 30 % of the expenses incurred by the salvor. However, the tribunal, if it deems it fair and just to do so and bearing in mind the relevant criteria set out in article 13, paragraph 1, may increase such special compensation further, but in no event shall the total increase be more than 100 % of the expenses incurred by the salvor.

heading: ARTICLE 14Special compensation
paragraph: 3 Salvor's expenses for the purpose of paragraphs 1 and 2 means the out-of-pocket expenses reasonably incurred by the salvor in the salvage operation and a fair rate for equipment and personnel actually and reasonably used in the salvage operation, taking into consideration the criteria set out in article 13, paragraph 1(h), (i) and (j).

heading: ARTICLE 14Special compensation
paragraph: 4 The total special compensation under this article shall be paid only if and to the extent that such compensation is greater than any reward recoverable by the salvor under article 13.

heading: ARTICLE 14Special compensation
paragraph: 5 If the salvor has been negligent and has thereby failed to prevent or minimize damage to the environment, he may be deprived of the whole or part of any special compensation due under this article.

heading: ARTICLE 14Special compensation
paragraph: 6 Nothing in this article shall affect any right of recourse on the part of the owner of the vessel.

heading: ARTICLE 15Apportionment between salvors
paragraph: 1 The apportionment of a reward under article 13 between salvors shall be made on the basis of the criteria contained in that article.

heading: ARTICLE 15Apportionment between salvors
paragraph: 2 The apportionment between the owner, master and other persons in the service of each sailing vessel shall be determined by the law of the flag of that vessel. If the salvage has not been carried out from a vessel, the apportionment shall be determined by the law governing the contract between the salvor and his servants.

heading: ARTICLE 16Salvage of persons
paragraph: 1 No remuneration is due from persons whose lives are saved, but nothing in this article shall affect the provisions of national law on this subject.

heading: ARTICLE 16Salvage of persons
paragraph: 2 A salvor of human life, who has taken part in the services rendered on the occasion of the accident giving rise to salvage, is entitled to a fair share of the payment awarded to the salvor for salving the vessel or other property or preventing or minimizing damage to the environment.

heading: ARTICLE 17Services rendered under existing contracts
paragraph: No payment is due under the provisions of this Convention unless the services rendered exceed what can be reasonably considered as due performance of a contract entered into before the danger arose.

heading: ARTICLE 18The effect of salvor's misconduct
paragraph: A salvor may be deprived of the whole or part of the payment due under this Convention to the extent that salvage operations have become necessary or more difficult because of fault or neglect on his part or if the salvor has been guilty of fraud or other dishonest conduct.

heading: ARTICLE 19Prohibition of salvage operations
paragraph: Services rendered notwithstanding the express and reasonable prohibition of the owner or master of the vessel or the owner of any other property in danger which is not and has not been on board the vessel shall not give rise to payment under this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 20Maritime lien
paragraph: 1 Nothing in this Convention shall affect the salvor's maritime lien under any international convention or national law.

heading: ARTICLE 20Maritime lien
paragraph: 2 The salvor may not enforce his maritime lien when satisfactory security for his claim, including interest and costs, has been duly tendered or provided.

heading: ARTICLE 21Duty to provide security
paragraph: 1 Upon the request of the salvor a person liable for payment due under this Convention shall provide satisfactory security for the claim, including interest and costs of the salvor.

heading: ARTICLE 21Duty to provide security
paragraph: 2 Without prejudice to paragraph 1, the owner of the salved vessel shall use his best endeavours to ensure that the owners of the cargo provide satisfactory security for the claims against them including interest and costs before the cargo is released.

heading: ARTICLE 21Duty to provide security
paragraph: 3 The salved vessel and other property shall not, without the consent of the salvor, be removed from the port or place at which they first arrive after the completion of the salvage operations until satisfactory security has been put up for the salvor's claim against the relevant vessel or property.

heading: ARTICLE 22Interim payment
paragraph: 1 The tribunal having jurisdiction over the claim of the salvor may, by interim decision, order that the salvor shall be paid on account such amount as seems fair and just, and on such terms including terms as to security where appropriate, as may be fair and just according to the circumstances of the case.

heading: ARTICLE 22Interim payment
paragraph: 2 In the event of an interim payment under this article the security provided under article 21 shall be reduced accordingly.

heading: ARTICLE 23Limitation of actions
paragraph: 1 Any action relating to payment under this Convention shall be time-barred if judicial or arbitral proceedings have not been instituted within a period of two years. The limitation period commences on the day on which the salvage operations are terminated.

heading: ARTICLE 23Limitation of actions
paragraph: 2 The person against whom a claim is made may at any time during the running of the limitation period extend that period by a declaration to the claimant. This period may in the like manner be further extended.

heading: ARTICLE 23Limitation of actions
paragraph: 3 An action for indemnity by a person liable may be instituted even after the expiration of the limitation period provided for in the preceding paragraphs, if brought within the time allowed by the law of the State where proceedings are instituted.

heading: ARTICLE 24Interest
paragraph: The right of the salvor to interest on any payment due under this Convention shall be determined according to the law of the State in which the tribunal seized of the case is situated.

heading: ARTICLE 25State-owned cargoes
paragraph: Unless the State owner consents, no provision of this Convention shall be used as a basis for the seizure, arrest or detention by any legal process of, nor for any proceedings in rem against, non-commercial cargoes owned by a State and entitled, at the time of the salvage operations, to sovereign immunity under generally recognized principles of international law.

heading: ARTICLE 26Humanitarian cargoes
paragraph: No provision of this Convention shall be used as a basis for the seizure, arrest or detention of humanitarian cargoes donated by a State, if such State has agreed to pay for salvage services rendered in respect of such humanitarian cargoes.

heading: ARTICLE 27Publication of arbitral awards
paragraph: States Parties shall encourage, as far as possible and with the consent of the parties, the publication of arbitral awards made in salvage cases.

heading: ARTICLE 28Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall be open for signature at the Headquarters of the Organization from 1 July 1989 to 30 June 1990 and shall thereafter remain open for accession.

heading: ARTICLE 28Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: 2 States may express their consent to be bound by this Convention by:

heading: ARTICLE 28Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (a) signature without reservation as to ratification, acceptance or approval; or

heading: ARTICLE 28Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (b) signature subject to ratification, acceptance or approval, followed by ratification, acceptance or approval; or

heading: ARTICLE 28Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: (c) accession.

heading: ARTICLE 28Signature, ratification, acceptance, approval and accession
paragraph: 3 Ratification, acceptance, approval or accession shall be effected by the deposit of an instrument to that effect with the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 29Entry into force
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall enter into force one year after the date on which 15 States have expressed their consent to be bound by it.

heading: ARTICLE 29Entry into force
paragraph: 2 For a State which expresses its consent to be bound by this Convention after the conditions for entry into force thereof have been met, such consent shall take effect one year after the date of expression of such consent.

heading: ARTICLE 30Reservations
paragraph: 1 Any State may, at the time of signature, ratification, acceptance, approval or accession, reserve the right not to apply the provisions of this Convention:

heading: ARTICLE 30Reservations
paragraph: (a) when the salvage operation takes place in inland waters and all vessels involved are of inland navigation;

heading: ARTICLE 30Reservations
paragraph: (b) when the salvage operations take place in inland waters and no vessel is involved;

heading: ARTICLE 30Reservations
paragraph: (c) when all interested parties are nationals of that State;

heading: ARTICLE 30Reservations
paragraph: (d) when the property involved is maritime cultural property of prehistoric, archaeological or historic interest and is situated on the sea-bed.

heading: ARTICLE 30Reservations
paragraph: 2 Reservations made at the time of signature are subject to confirmation upon ratification, acceptance or approval.

heading: ARTICLE 30Reservations
paragraph: 3 Any State which has made a reservation to this Convention may withdraw it at any time by means of a notification addressed to the Secretary-General. Such withdrawal shall take effect on the date the notification is received. If the notification states that the withdrawal of a reservation is to take effect on a date specified therein, and such date is later than the date the notification is received by the Secretary-General, the withdrawal shall take effect on such later date.

heading: ARTICLE 31Denunciation
paragraph: 1 This Convention may be denounced by any State Party at any time after the expiry of one year from the date on which this Convention enters into force for that State.

heading: ARTICLE 31Denunciation
paragraph: 2 Denunciation shall be effected by the deposit of an instrument of denunciation with the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 31Denunciation
paragraph: 3 A denunciation shall take effect one year, or such longer period as may be specified in the instrument of denunciation, after the receipt of the instrument of denunciation by the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 32Revision and amendment
paragraph: 1 A conference for the purpose of revising or amending this Convention may be convened by the Organization.

heading: ARTICLE 32Revision and amendment
paragraph: 2 The Secretary-General shall convene a conference of the States Parties to this Convention for revising or amending the Convention, at the request of eight States Parties, or one fourth of the States Parties, whichever is the higher figure.

heading: ARTICLE 32Revision and amendment
paragraph: 3 Any consent to be bound by this Convention expressed after the date of entry into force of an amendment to this Convention shall be deemed to apply to the Convention as amended.

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: 1 This Convention shall be deposited with the Secretary-General.

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: 2 The Secretary-General shall:

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: (a) inform all States which have signed this Convention or acceded thereto, and all Members of the Organization, of:

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: (i) each new signature or deposit of an instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession together with the date thereof;

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: (ii) the date of the entry into force of this Convention;

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: (iii) the deposit of any instrument of denunciation of this Convention together with the date on which it is received and the date on which the denunciation takes effect;

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: (iv) any amendment adopted in conformity with article 32;

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: (v) the receipt of any reservation, declaration or notification made under this Convention;

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: (b) transmit certified true copies of this Convention to all States which have signed this Convention or acceded thereto.

heading: ARTICLE 33Depositary
paragraph: 3 As soon as this Convention enters into force, a certified true copy thereof shall be transmitted by the Depositary to the Secretary-General of the United Nations for registration and publication in accordance with Article 102 of the Charter of the United Nations.

heading: ARTICLE 34Languages
paragraph: This Convention is established in a single original in the Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish languages, each text being equally authentic.

heading: ARTICLE 34Languages
paragraph: IN WITNESS WHEREOF the undersigned being duly authorized by their respective Governments for that purpose have signed this Convention.

heading: ARTICLE 34Languages
paragraph: DONE AT LONDON this twenty-eighth day of April one thousand nine hundred and eighty-nine.

heading: ATTACHMENT 1Common Understanding concerning Articles 13 and 14 of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: It is the common understanding of the Conference that, in fixing a reward under article 13 and assessing special compensation under article 14 of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989 the tribunal is under no duty to fix a reward under article 13 up to the maximum salved value of the vessel and other property before assessing the special compensation to be paid under article 14.

heading: ATTACHMENT 2Resolution requesting the amendment of the York-Antwerp Rules, 1974
paragraph: THE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON SALVAGE, 1989,

heading: ATTACHMENT 2Resolution requesting the amendment of the York-Antwerp Rules, 1974
paragraph: HAVING ADOPTED the International Convention on Salvage, 1989,

heading: ATTACHMENT 2Resolution requesting the amendment of the York-Antwerp Rules, 1974
paragraph: CONSIDERING that payments made pursuant to article 14 are not intended to be allowed in general average,

heading: ATTACHMENT 2Resolution requesting the amendment of the York-Antwerp Rules, 1974
paragraph: REQUESTS the Secretary-General of the International Maritime Organization to take the appropriate steps in order to ensure speedy amendment of the York-Antwerp Rules, 1974, to ensure that special compensation paid under article 14 is not subject to general average.

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: THE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON SALVAGE, 1989,

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: IN ADOPTING the International Convention on Salvage, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as "The Convention"),

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: CONSIDERING IT DESIRABLE that as many States as possible should become Parties to the Convention,

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: RECOGNIZING that the entry into force of the Convention will represent an important additional factor for the protection of the marine environment,

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: CONSIDERING that the international publicizing and wide implementation of the Convention is of the utmost importance for the attainment of its objectives,

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: I RECOMMENDS:

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: (a) that the Organization promote public awareness of the Convention through the holding of seminars, courses or symposia;

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: (b) that training institutions created under the auspices of the Organization include the study of the Convention in their corresponding courses of study.

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: II REQUESTS:

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: (a) Members States to transmit to the Organization the text of the laws, orders, decrees, regulations and other instruments that they promulgate concerning the various matters falling within the scope of application of the Convention;

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: (b) Member States, in consultation with the Organization, to promote the giving of help to those States requesting technical assistance for the drafting of laws, orders, decrees, regulations and other instruments necessary for the implementation of the Convention; and

heading: ATTACHMENT 3Resolution on international co-operation for the implementation of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989
paragraph: (c) the Organization to notify Member States of any communication it may receive under paragraph II(a).

heading: PART 2Canada's Reservations
paragraph: The Government of Canada reserves the right not to apply the provisions of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989 when the property involved is maritime cultural property of prehistoric, archaeological or historic interest and is situated on the seabed.
